abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing energy-efficient, high-performance embedded systems for IoT and edge computing applications, which require balancing computational throughput with strict power and thermal constraints. Current design approaches for such systems rely on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-intensive and fails to account for the complex interdependencies between hardware-software co-design parameters. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing a scalable simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model heterogeneous embedded architectures integrating custom FPGA-based accelerators, low-power microcontrollers, and machine learning inference engines. The computational approach will combine hardware-in-the-loop emulation via Verilog/VHDL simulations with multi-objective optimization algorithms to explore design trade-offs across power consumption, latency, and resource utilization. Large-scale parameter sweeps will be parallelized across HPC nodes to evaluate thousands of hardware configurations and neural network quantization strategies efficiently. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for rapid prototyping of energy-aware embedded systems, a dataset mapping architectural choices to performance metrics, and open-source tools to automate design space exploration. This work will directly support industry partners in reducing development cycles for IoT devices while advancing curricular case studies in computer engineering technology programs. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the computationally intensive nature of cycle-accurate hardware simulations and the need to process terabytes of telemetry data from parallelized experiments. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for designing next-generation embedded systems that meet escalating demands for real-time processing within sustainable power envelopes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical inefficiencies in prehospital emergency medical decision-making during mass casualty incidents (MCIs). While EMT paramedics are trained to prioritize patient care under extreme time constraints, existing triage protocols rely on static algorithms that fail to dynamically adapt to real-time variables such as fluctuating resource availability, evolving patient conditions, and complex environmental factors. This limitation often leads to suboptimal resource allocation, delayed interventions, and preventable mortality. To resolve this, we propose developing a machine learning-driven decision support system that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including vital signs, injury patterns, geospatial data, and resource inventories—into adaptive triage recommendations. The computational workflow involves three phases: (1) Agent-based modeling of MCI scenarios to simulate patient trajectories, EMT workflows, and logistical constraints; (2) Training deep reinforcement learning models on synthetic and historical EMS datasets to optimize dynamic resource allocation; and (3) Validating predictions against multi-center MCI registries using Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (>10^6 simulated scenarios), parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations for outcome prediction, and reducing latency in model retraining cycles. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time triage optimization, validated against gold-standard triage protocols, with measurable targets of 15-20% improvement in predicted survival rates across simulated MCIs. This interdisciplinary integration of computational epidemiology, operations research, and prehospital emergency medicine fills a critical gap in health sciences by translating theoretical modeling into actionable tools for frontline EMT personnel, ultimately enhancing disaster response efficacy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the remote supervision of physicians, to recognize, assess, and manage medical emergencies in prehospital settings and to supervise Ambulance personnel. Includes instruction in basic, intermediate, and advanced EMT procedures; emergency surgical procedures; medical triage; rescue operations; crisis scene management and personnel supervision; equipment operation and maintenance; patient stabilization, monitoring, and care; drug administration; identification and preliminary diagnosis of diseases and injuries; communication and computer operations; basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: Ophthalmic dispensing relies on precise measurements and personalized adaptations of corrective eyewear to optimize visual outcomes and patient comfort. However, current methods for lens design and fitting—particularly for complex prescriptions, irregular corneal topography, or multifocal needs—often depend on static anatomical data and generalized optical models. This can lead to suboptimal visual acuity, discomfort, or prolonged adaptation periods, especially in cases involving high astigmatism, keratoconus, or post-surgical prosthetics. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing dynamic, patient-specific computational models of light interaction with ocular structures and corrective lenses under real-world conditions, such as eye movement, ambient lighting variations, and tear film dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate these multi-physics phenomena at scale, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for biomechanical interactions between contact lenses and corneal tissue, Monte Carlo ray-tracing for light propagation through progressive lenses, and machine learning to correlate simulated optical outcomes with patient-reported comfort metrics. The computational pipeline will process high-resolution 3D ocular surface scans, pupillometry data, and material properties of modern lens polymers, requiring parallelized workflows to handle terabytes of input data and iterative optimization cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for identifying optimal lens geometries and materials for individual patients, reducing trial-and-error in clinical fittings. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated optical performance under diverse physiological conditions, advancing education in ophthalmic dispensing. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to bridge gaps between optical theory, manufacturing precision, and clinical practice, ultimately improving accessibility to personalized vision correction solutions in underserved populations with complex ocular needs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: Understanding the mechanisms governing earthquake nucleation and propagation remains a critical challenge in geophysics, with significant implications for seismic hazard assessment. Current models struggle to resolve the multi-scale physics of fault zones, where granular interactions at micrometer scales influence kilometer-scale stress accumulation and rupture dynamics. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations of fault systems using advanced computational methods. The research will focus on the San Andreas Fault system, integrating geodetic, seismologic, and laboratory-derived friction data to constrain models of stress transfer and rupture propagation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the non-linear coupling of thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes across spatial scales (nanometers to kilometers) and temporal scales (seconds to millennia). Numerical methods will include adaptive mesh refinement finite element modeling to capture localized deformation and machine learning algorithms to optimize parameter space exploration. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers and GPU acceleration to manage the high dimensionality of the problem. Expected outcomes include new insights into the role of fluid-rock interactions in modulating earthquake recurrence intervals and the identification of precursory stress patterns detectable through geodetic monitoring. By bridging laboratory-scale friction laws with field-scale fault behavior, this work will advance physics-based seismic hazard models, directly informing infrastructure resilience planning. The requested computing resources will enable ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainties, a critical step toward operational earthquake forecasting. This project underscores the necessity of HPC in modern geophysical research, where data-intensive, multi-physics simulations are indispensable for decoding Earth’s complex mechanical systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physics of solids and its application to the study of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in gravimetric, seismology, earthquake forecasting, magnetrometry, electrical properties of solid bodies, plate tectonics, active deformation, thermodynamics, remote sensing, geodesy, and laboratory simulations of geological processes.

abstract: This project seeks to advance geothermal reservoir modeling and optimization by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical gaps in simulating subsurface thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical interactions at scale. Geothermal energy systems require precise characterization of heterogeneous rock formations, fluid flow dynamics, and heat exchange processes to maximize energy extraction and ensure long-term reservoir viability. Current models often oversimplify multi-physics couplings or lack the spatial resolution needed to predict system behavior under dynamic operational conditions, limiting their utility for real-world design and decision-making. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) simulation framework using finite element methods optimized for parallel computation. The model will integrate geophysical data from field sites to represent complex fracture networks, variable permeability zones, and temperature-dependent material properties. HPC resources will enable high-resolution 3D simulations of heat transfer and fluid migration across decade-long operational timelines, with sensitivity analyses to evaluate drilling configurations, injection rates, and energy recovery strategies. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters against historical production data and identify optimal operating conditions. Outcomes will include validated workflows for predicting reservoir efficiency and longevity, reducing exploration risks, and informing sustainable management practices. By providing scalable computational tools to unravel subsurface complexity, this work aims to lower barriers to geothermal adoption, enhance energy output per well, and support the transition to low-carbon power systems. The requested allocation will directly enable large-scale simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, accelerating progress toward cost-effective, reliable geothermal energy technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze dialectal variation and linguistic evolution in Spanish across geographic and temporal contexts. The research addresses a critical gap in Hispanic linguistics: the lack of large-scale, computationally driven studies that systematically map phonetic, syntactic, and lexical shifts in regional Spanish dialects, particularly in underdocumented areas of Latin America. Current methodologies rely on manual corpus analysis, limiting the scope and granularity of findings. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining dialectometry, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning (ML) to process multilingual text corpora, digitized historical documents, and spoken language datasets. Key tasks include training transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants) on dialect-specific corpora to detect syntactic patterns, implementing phonetic alignment algorithms for comparative audio analysis, and applying spatial-temporal clustering techniques to visualize linguistic change. The scale of data—spanning 20 regional dialects, 15 million words of text, and 2,000 hours of speech—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a geolocated database of dialectal features traceable from early modern Castilian to present-day variants, (2) quantitative models identifying sociolinguistic drivers of language change, and (3) open-access tools for automated dialect classification. This work will advance scholarly understanding of Spanish linguistic diversity while providing methodological frameworks applicable to minority language preservation and computational philology. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with traditional humanistic inquiry, the project bridges gaps between computational linguistics and Hispanic studies, offering replicable models for resource-constrained language research in the humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Spanish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Castilan; Latin American and regional Spanish dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Medical imaging technologies, such as high-resolution MRI and CT, generate complex three-dimensional datasets critical for diagnosing neurological and oncological conditions. However, current computational tools struggle to process these datasets in real-time, limiting their utility in time-sensitive clinical environments. This project proposes the development of a scalable deep learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to enable rapid, automated analysis of volumetric medical images. The research will focus on architecting convolutional neural networks (CNNs) tailored for 3D spatial data, leveraging parallelized training across GPU clusters to reduce processing times. Additionally, the project will implement dynamic load-balancing algorithms to efficiently distribute computational workloads, addressing bottlenecks in memory-intensive operations. By integrating multi-institutional imaging datasets—comprising over 50,000 annotated scans—the framework will be validated for accuracy in detecting cerebral aneurysms and early-stage tumors against radiologist assessments. The expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for real-time medical image analysis, reducing diagnostic delays in emergency care, and a computational pipeline adaptable to emerging imaging modalities. This work bridges gaps between computational science and clinical medicine, offering a template for deploying HPC resources to enhance diagnostic precision while maintaining interoperability with existing hospital systems.
cip_definition: Any program in medicine, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design of adaptive engineering systems that integrate heterogeneous subsystems with conflicting operational requirements. Such systems—common in smart infrastructure, reconfigurable robotics, and modular industrial platforms—require balancing dynamic adaptability with structural or functional efficiency, a challenge compounded by the absence of unified design methodologies. Current approaches rely on sequential optimization of individual subsystems, leading to suboptimal global performance when interdependent variables are not co-evolved. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach coupled with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to simulate and iteratively refine system-wide design parameters under uncertainty. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parallelize thousands of design simulations, each modeling interactions between mechanical, control, and human-in-the-loop decision-making subsystems. Computational workflows will integrate physics-based simulations (e.g., finite element analysis for structural integrity) with stochastic agent-based models to evaluate emergent system behaviors. Key innovations include a conflict-resolution metric space to quantify trade-offs between subsystem requirements and a co-evolutionary algorithm to identify Pareto-optimal configurations. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated framework for cross-domain system design that reduces iterative prototyping costs by 30-50% in early-stage engineering, (2) benchmark datasets for adaptive system performance under multi-physics constraints, and (3) open-source tools enabling modular integration of domain-specific simulators. This work advances computational engineering design by formalizing methods to manage complexity in next-generation systems where flexibility, resilience, and interdisciplinary coordination are critical to success. Case studies will focus on validating the approach for modular energy harvesting platforms and reconfigurable aerospace testbeds, though the methodology is generalizable to broader applications.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to engineering problems involving marrying or coordinating multiple dissimilar systems to carry out single functions or achieve common purposes, organizing system components for maximum flexibility and utility, planning engineering projects involving multiple tasks and design solutions, planning design testing and evaluation procedures, resolving specification and requirement conflicts, and choosing among competing theoretical solutions. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 14.2901.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize adaptive decision-making in multi-stakeholder business ecosystems under dynamic, uncertain conditions. The research problem centers on improving resilience in urban supply chains, where interdependent actors (e.g., retailers, logistics providers, municipal systems) must respond to real-time disruptions such as demand shocks, infrastructure failures, or environmental events. Traditional business analytics methods struggle to model the nonlinear feedback loops, competitive-cooperative incentives, and spatial-temporal heterogeneities inherent in such systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid approach integrating agent-based modeling, game-theoretic reinforcement learning, and high-resolution geospatial simulations. The computational workflow will leverage distributed graph neural networks to capture entity interactions, federated learning to preserve stakeholder data privacy, and multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to balance competing priorities like cost efficiency, equity, and sustainability. High-performance computing resources are critical for scaling simulations across millions of agent decisions per epoch, processing real-time sensor data streams from IoT networks, and conducting parameter sensitivity analyses across probabilistic disaster scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for scenario-based supply chain stress-testing, novel convergence criteria for multi-agent coordination under partial information, and policy insights for public-private resource allocation during crises. By bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and complex systems science, this work aims to advance predictive analytics for interconnected urban challenges while establishing computational benchmarks for decentralized, ethics-aware decision architectures. The requested resources will enable latency-sensitive experiments across 10,000+ core-hour simulations, with datasets and models designed for interoperability across business analytics platforms and urban digital twin initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to solve business challenges. Includes instruction in machine learning, optimization methods, computer algorithms, probability and stochastic models, information economics, logistics, strategy, consumer behavior, marketing, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural narratives across transnational communities using advanced computational methods, integrating perspectives from digital humanities, computational social science, and ethnographic studies. The research addresses the challenge of analyzing large-scale, unstructured datasets—including multilingual texts, visual media, and oral histories—to identify patterns in narrative formation, propagation, and adaptation. A central problem is the lack of scalable frameworks to systematically analyze how cultural narratives evolve in response to sociopolitical events, migration, and digital media, particularly in contexts where data is sparse, heterogeneous, or linguistically complex. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, machine learning models for cross-modal data integration (text, image, audio), and network analysis to map narrative diffusion across communities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential due to the computational demands of training transformer-based models on multilingual corpora, processing high-resolution multimedia data, and simulating large-scale narrative networks. The proposed work will leverage parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, GPU-accelerated model training, and distributed computing for network simulations. Expected outcomes include a novel interdisciplinary methodology for cultural narrative analysis, open-source tools for multimodal data integration, and empirical insights into how marginalized communities preserve cultural identity through adaptive storytelling. These results will advance scholarly understanding of narrative resilience in globalized contexts and provide actionable frameworks for policymakers and cultural organizations. The project’s computational demands—requiring terabytes of storage, multi-node processing, and sustained GPU capacity—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve scalability, reproducibility, and timely completion.
cip_definition: A program that derives from two or more distinct programs and that is integrated around a unifying theme or topic that cannot be subsumed under a single discipline or occupational field.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive mechanisms underlying dynamic decision-making in uncertain environments using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral datasets. A core challenge in experimental psychology lies in disentangling how individuals integrate probabilistic feedback, adjust strategies over time, and exhibit inter-individual variability in adaptive learning. Traditional behavioral methods lack the granularity to model nonlinear interactions between cognitive parameters (e.g., learning rates, exploration-exploitation trade-offs) and task dynamics. To address this, we propose a hierarchical Bayesian framework coupled with reinforcement learning (RL) models to simulate and analyze decision trajectories across parametrically varied uncertainty conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) Parallelized parameter estimation across 10,000+ synthetic and empirical trial sequences, (2) Comparative model evidence calculations using nested Monte Carlo sampling for 15 competing cognitive architectures, and (3) Population-level hierarchical inference to quantify individual differences in cognitive flexibility. The empirical dataset comprises behavioral responses from N = 300 participants completing a novel multi-stage decision task with shifting reward contingencies, generating ~4.5 million data points. Without HPC, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for model comparison would exceed 6 months of computation time due to high-dimensional parameter spaces and cross-validated likelihood evaluations. Expected outcomes include identifying latent cognitive profiles predictive of adaptation speed, validating a computational account of uncertainty-driven strategy switching, and releasing open-source tools for efficient RL model fitting in psychology. This work advances methodological capabilities for studying complex decision processes while providing theoretical insights into how humans navigate volatile environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in research and experimental psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The development of advanced drug formulations with optimized therapeutic efficacy and patient-specific adaptability remains a critical challenge in pharmaceutics. Traditional experimental approaches to evaluate drug stability, release kinetics, and host interactions are resource-intensive, time-consuming, and limited in their ability to capture complex biological variability. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to accelerate the design of novel nanoscale drug delivery systems targeting chronic inflammatory diseases. The research will employ multi-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model drug-polymer interactions, self-assembly mechanisms of nanoparticle carriers, and drug release profiles under physiologically relevant conditions. Machine learning models will be integrated to predict formulation stability, bioavailability, and pharmacokinetic properties from simulation-derived datasets. Key objectives include elucidating the role of polymer chemistry in modulating drug-carrier binding affinities and simulating host immune responses to nanoparticle surfaces. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational demands of large-scale MD systems (≥1 million atoms), long simulation timescales (µs-ms), and high-throughput screening of 500+ formulation candidates. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for optimizing drug loading efficiency and release kinetics, validated against in vitro dissolution and cell culture experiments. The project aims to establish a translatable pipeline for rational formulation design, reducing reliance on iterative trial-and-error experimentation. By correlating computational predictions with experimental data, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of formulation-biology interactions and support the development of personalized therapeutics with enhanced targeting and reduced off-target effects. The requested computing infrastructure will enable unprecedented resolution of dynamic processes in drug delivery systems, directly contributing to the program’s mission of bridging pharmaceutical sciences with computational innovation.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the formulation of medicinal substances into product vehicles capable of being stored, transported, and then introduced into the patient and behaving in ways optimal to therapeutic interaction. Includes instruction in statistics, biopharmaceutics, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, physical pharmacy, pharmacological analysis, drug design and development, pharmacological biotechnology, chemical separations, spectroscopy, drug-host interactions, immunology, quantitative drug measurement, enzymatic transformations, and metabolic excretion.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize clinical decision-making workflows for licensed practical nurses (LPNs) in acute care settings, where dynamic patient conditions and resource constraints necessitate rapid, evidence-based interventions. A critical challenge in LPN training and practice is the lack of personalized, real-time tools to simulate and evaluate the impact of care prioritization strategies under variable clinical workloads. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-patient care scenarios. The ABM component will integrate anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data to generate synthetic patient cohorts with diverse acuity levels, while reinforcement learning algorithms will train decision agents to prioritize tasks such as vital sign monitoring, medication administration, and wound care. Computational experiments will evaluate how different task sequences and staffing ratios affect patient outcomes, including preventable complications and response times. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these simulations to thousands of parallelized scenarios, capturing rare but high-stakes clinical events. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated simulation platform for LPN educators to prototype competency-based training modules and (2) data-driven guidelines for balancing patient loads in resource-limited settings. By quantifying trade-offs in care prioritization, this work aims to reduce cognitive overload for trainees and improve adherence to sterile technique and safety protocols during high-pressure interventions. The resulting tools will be disseminated to nursing programs to bridge gaps between theoretical instruction and clinical practice, directly aligning with the program’s mission to prepare LPNs for dynamic healthcare environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in providing general nursing care under the direction of a registered nurse, physician or dentist. Includes instruction in taking patient vital signs, applying sterile dressings, patient health education, and assistance with examinations and treatment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance personalized motor rehabilitation strategies for individuals with acquired neurological injuries (e.g., stroke, spinal cord injury). Current approaches to optimizing brain-computer interface (BCI)-assisted therapies are limited by variability in user-specific neurophysiological responses and insufficient computational power to model complex neural-motor interactions in real time. The research aims to address this gap by integrating multimodal neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), biomechanical motion capture data, and machine learning to predict individualized neuroplasticity patterns and optimize rehabilitation protocols. A computational pipeline will be developed to analyze large-scale neural datasets, simulate motor recovery trajectories using biologically plausible neural network models, and dynamically adapt BCI parameters to enhance sensorimotor retraining. Key challenges include processing high-dimensional neurophysiological data streams, resolving time-sensitive feedback loops for therapeutic BCIs, and validating models against clinical outcome measures. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of neuroimaging datasets, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for temporal pattern recognition), and large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal stimulation protocols. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive framework for personalizing neuromodulation strategies, open-source tools for real-time BCI adaptation, and quantitative biomarkers linking neurodynamic changes to functional recovery. This work bridges computational neuroscience, rehabilitation engineering, and clinical therapeutics, offering potential to transform post-injury care by enabling data-driven, precision rehabilitation paradigms that adapt to patients’ evolving neural states.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with people who have learning disabilities, mental illness, and physical disabilities in a clinical, educational, or institutional setting. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, assistive technology, case management, counseling techniques, cultural diversity, disability assessment and measurement, ethics, psychological and physiological aspects of disability, rehabilitation services, rehabilitation science, and vocational counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the spatial dynamics of informal knowledge networks in urban environments, focusing on how transient populations (e.g., migrants, seasonal workers, and digital nomads) influence the diffusion of localized skills and practices across cities. While traditional social science frameworks emphasize formal institutions or economic drivers, this research addresses a gap by analyzing ephemeral, place-based interactions that shape cultural and technical innovation. The study integrates high-resolution geolocated social media data, anonymized mobile device movement records, and ethnographic field annotations to model knowledge transfer pathways at metropolitan scales. A core computational challenge involves resolving spatiotemporal mismatches between heterogeneous datasets (spanning seconds to years and meters to kilometers) while preserving the granularity required to detect micro-scale social behaviors. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel execution of agent-based simulations that test hypotheses about network formation under varying urban design constraints, coupled with graph neural networks trained to identify latent patterns in multi-modal data. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for quantifying informal knowledge diffusion in transient populations, (2) scalable algorithms for fusing real-time sensor data with qualitative inputs in socio-spatial models, and (3) evidence-based insights for policymakers seeking to foster inclusive innovation ecosystems in hyper-mobile societies. By advancing computational methods to analyze human-environment interactions at the intersection of mobility and knowledge economies, this work contributes to an emerging subfield of geography focused on non-institutional social dynamics in rapidly urbanizing contexts.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in geography, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time decision-making in complex, dynamic Command and Control (C2) environments, where traditional systems struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams and maintain operational coherence under uncertainty. The core challenge lies in balancing rapid situational analysis with robust resource allocation across distributed, contested networks—a problem exacerbated by the scale of modern multi-domain operations and adversarial cyber-physical threats. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, graph-theoretic network analysis, and adaptive reinforcement learning to simulate C2 workflows under varying threat scenarios. Computational experiments will focus on emulating multi-echelon decision processes, incorporating real-world constraints such as bandwidth limitations, sensor noise, and partial observability. Key innovations include the development of a modular simulation architecture capable of ingesting operational data from live systems, coupled with metaheuristic optimization techniques to identify resilient resource distribution patterns. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for system latency, decision accuracy, and fault tolerance under stress conditions, as well as open-source tools for scenario generation and performance benchmarking. This work directly addresses gaps in current C2 modernization efforts by providing a testbed for evaluating emergent technologies like AI-assisted planning and decentralized coordination protocols. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to theater-level complexity, enabling parametric studies of infrastructure hardening strategies, and validating probabilistic models of human-machine teaming behaviors. By bridging theoretical models with operational constraints, this research aims to inform next-generation C2 system design principles and enhance interoperability standards across joint military networks.
cip_title: Command & Control (C3, C4I) Systems and Operations (MILITARY)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational use of information and decision systems in support of battlefield, theatre, and global strategic operations. Includes instruction in applied mathematics and statistics, computer systems, real-time analysis and decision systems, surveillance and navigation systems, information and communications technology, information security, situational awareness, system integration, joint operations and applications to specific command problems and services.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the theoretical understanding of algebraic structures, particularly in the classification and analysis of high-dimensional Lie algebras and their representations, which remain central challenges in modern algebra. The computational complexity of these problems arises from the exponential growth of structural invariants and the need to solve large systems of polynomial equations to identify isomorphism classes or decompose representations. Traditional methods, limited by serial processing and memory constraints, fail to scale beyond low-dimensional cases. This work proposes a hybrid computational approach combining symbolic computation, numerical linear algebra, and distributed-memory parallelism to address these limitations. Key objectives include developing optimized algorithms for Gröbner basis calculations over finite fields, parallelizing cohomology computations to classify extensions of Lie algebras, and implementing tensor decomposition techniques for irreducible representation analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as storing and manipulating sparse matrices with dimensions exceeding 10^6, and for executing massively parallelized searches across parameter spaces governing algebraic relations. The project will leverage MPI-based frameworks for distributed computation and GPU acceleration for dense linear algebra operations. Success in this endeavor will yield new conjectures and theorems in structural algebra, explicit classifications for families of Lie algebras in dimensions previously intractable, and open-source software tools tailored for algebraic computations. These outcomes will provide foundational insights into the hierarchy of algebraic structures, with implications for adjacent fields such as algebraic geometry and mathematical physics. By scaling theoretical algebra into the computational frontier, this research aims to establish reproducible pipelines for future investigations while enhancing the interoperability of mathematical software in HPC environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on algebraic structures and linear algebra.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the impact of leadership decision-making frameworks on organizational adaptability in dynamic environments. While leadership strategies are well-studied in static contexts, there is a critical gap in understanding how computational models can simulate and predict the efficacy of different leadership approaches during periods of rapid change, such as market disruptions or internal crises. The study will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate organizational behavior under varying leadership styles, including hierarchical, distributed, and hybrid decision-making structures. These models will incorporate variables such as communication latency, resource allocation efficiency, and team cohesion dynamics, calibrated using empirical data from case studies of technology firms and non-profit organizations. HPC resources are essential to run large-scale, parallel simulations that capture the nonlinear interactions between leadership decisions, environmental stressors, and workforce responses. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to identify patterns in successful adaptive strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to guide leaders in selecting optimal decision-making structures under uncertainty, as well as actionable insights into mitigating bottlenecks in organizational resilience. This work bridges computational social science and leadership theory, offering a novel methodology for evaluating leadership efficacy in complex systems. By quantifying the relationship between leadership practices and adaptive outcomes, the project aims to advance evidence-based strategies for organizational sustainability, directly contributing to the Business Administration and Management field’s understanding of computational leadership analytics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative coalition formation and policy outcomes in the U.S. Congress through advanced computational modeling. The research problem centers on understanding how partisan polarization, interest group networks, and procedural rules interact to shape the passage of major legislation. Traditional methods, limited by small datasets and static models, struggle to capture the complexity of these interactions across time and institutional contexts. To address this, we propose a multi-method approach combining large-scale text analysis of congressional hearings and legislative texts (1990–2024) with dynamic network simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process over 10 million pages of legislative documents using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for topic detection and sentiment analysis. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate coalition-building processes under varying procedural scenarios (e.g., filibuster rules, committee structures), requiring thousands of parallelized iterations to assess stability and predictive accuracy. The integration of empirical text data with computational experiments will enable novel tests of theories regarding institutional constraints on bipartisan cooperation. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of linguistic markers in legislative debates that signal coalitional shifts before critical votes, (2) quantification of rule-based versus ideology-based barriers to consensus, and (3) open-source tools for simulating institutional reforms. This work contributes to political science by advancing computational methods to study legislative behavior while providing evidence-based insights into contemporary governance challenges. The requested resources—particularly GPU nodes for NLP training and high-memory CPUs for network simulations—are necessary to handle the project’s data volume (12+ TB) and real-time modeling demands, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of United States political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in American political theory, political parties and interest groups, state and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) is critical for preventing neurological injury during surgeries, yet existing systems face challenges in real-time processing of complex neurophysiological data and predictive modeling of adverse events. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing advanced computational tools to enhance the speed, accuracy, and interpretability of IONM systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to analyze multimodal data streams—including high-density EEG, EMG, and somatosensory evoked potentials—to detect subtle neural changes indicative of surgical risk. The computational approach integrates parallelized signal processing algorithms for noise reduction and feature extraction, coupled with machine learning models trained on retrospective surgical datasets to predict intraoperative neurological compromise. A key innovation involves simulating real-world surgical scenarios using finite element modeling to map how mechanical or ischemic perturbations propagate through neural networks, enabling the creation of patient-specific risk profiles. The HPC environment is essential for managing the scale of data (terabytes per case), optimizing deep learning architectures via distributed training, and reducing latency in real-time analytics to sub-second thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive IONM signal interpretation, validated against clinical outcomes from 500+ historical cases, and a predictive dashboard to guide surgical decision-making. This work will establish computational benchmarks for neuromonitoring accuracy, directly addressing gaps in current clinical practice where delayed or ambiguous interpretations contribute to preventable complications. By enabling rapid, data-driven insights, the project aims to improve surgical safety standards and provide a scalable platform for training future neuromonitoring professionals in computational methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in understanding how interdisciplinary humanities training influences ethical decision-making patterns among healthcare professionals during high-stakes clinical scenarios. Traditional medical education often siloes ethics and humanities content, limiting opportunities to model their dynamic integration into real-world practice. To bridge this divide, we propose developing a novel computational framework that combines natural language processing (NLP), multi-agent reinforcement learning, and immersive virtual environment simulations. The research will analyze 15,000+ historical clinical ethics case records and contemporaneous educational materials using transformer-based models to identify latent patterns in ethical reasoning development. Concurrently, we will build parameterized simulations of complex care scenarios (e.g., end-of-life decisions, resource triage) within a high-fidelity virtual platform, training agent models on heterogeneous ethical frameworks derived from philosophical, legal, and cultural perspectives. By implementing distributed deep learning across GPU-accelerated nodes, the system will simulate over 100,000 provider-patient interaction variants while tracking decision trajectories under competing ethical constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping relationships between humanities education content and observed clinical ethical behaviors, 2) validated predictive models of educational intervention impacts on decision-making quality, and 3) an open-source simulation environment for stress-testing ethics curricula against emergent biomedical challenges. This work directly advances priorities in health professions education by creating scalable computational tools to optimize the integration of humanistic principles into clinical training, ultimately aiming to reduce moral injury among providers and improve patient outcomes through ethically informed care. The project's HPC requirements center on large-scale language model fine-tuning, massively parallel simulation runs, and real-time rendering of immersive ethical dilemma scenarios.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of narrative structures and stylistic patterns in British and Commonwealth literature from the early modern period to the 21st century using computational text analysis. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on close reading to identify shifts in narrative form and rhetorical strategies, the scale and complexity of cross-temporal, transnational comparisons necessitate scalable computational methods. The research problem centers on mapping large-scale trends in literary innovation—such as the emergence of free indirect discourse, the persistence of oral storytelling conventions in postcolonial texts, or the relationship between genre hybridity and cultural exchange—across a corpus of over 50,000 primary texts, including novels, plays, and poetry. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process this multilingual, diachronic corpus, which spans four centuries and includes digitized rare materials from Commonwealth archives. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for syntactic parsing, sentiment analysis, and semantic role labeling, alongside transformer-based models fine-tuned to detect stylistic features (e.g., metaphor density, focalization patterns). Network analysis will trace intertextual influences among authors, while clustering algorithms will identify latent genre categories. The project’s outcomes will produce 1) a quantitative framework for periodizing narrative techniques in Anglophone literatures, 2) open-access datasets linking formal innovations to historical contexts of empire and globalization, and 3) visualizations of transnational literary networks. By integrating computational rigor with literary hermeneutics, this work aims to advance debates about canon formation, aesthetic adaptation, and the digital humanities’ capacity to enrich traditional scholarship. The requested HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale text collections, the training of custom language models, and the iterative testing of hypotheses across heterogeneous subcorpora—tasks infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literatures and literary developments of the English-speaking peoples of the British Isles and the British Commonwealth, from the origins of the English language to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, country and regional specializations, literary criticism, and the study of folkloric traditions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and interpret the evolving dynamics of cultural production and consumption in the digital age, with a focus on arts journalism and criticism. The research problem centers on the challenges of processing and contextualizing vast, heterogeneous datasets—including multimedia content (film, music, visual art), social media discourse, and archival journalism—to identify patterns in cultural representation, bias, and public engagement. Traditional analytical methods struggle to scale with the volume and complexity of digital cultural data, limiting journalists’ ability to critically assess trends or hold cultural institutions accountable. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and network analysis to examine (1) how cultural narratives are constructed across platforms, (2) disparities in coverage of underrepresented artists or genres, and (3) the impact of algorithmic curation on arts journalism. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including decades of digitized criticism, live social media streams, and audiovisual archives, while training machine learning models to detect stylistic, thematic, and demographic trends. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for multimodal cultural analysis, open-source tools to support investigative arts reporting, and data-driven insights into the ethical and aesthetic challenges facing contemporary cultural journalism. By integrating computational methods with humanistic critique, this work aims to empower journalists and critics to address systemic inequities in cultural coverage and enhance public understanding of the arts’ role in society. The requested allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data storage, and parallelized analysis of time-sensitive cultural datasets, which are critical for maintaining relevance in fast-moving media environments.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to be journalists who critically examine current culture as expressed through the visual and performing arts, design, film, music, radio, television, dance, theater, and written text. Includes instruction in arts criticism, art and entertainment reporting, cultural critique, investigative reporting, newspaper reporting, photojournalism, and writing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate emergent collective dynamics in hybrid biological-physical systems, integrating principles from soft matter physics, nonlinear biochemistry, and network theory. The focus lies on modeling light-responsive microbial communities interfaced with synthetic colloidal matrices—a novel class of systems where biological activity couples to tunable physical forces, enabling programmable self-organization. Current limitations in simulating such systems stem from the need to resolve multi-scale interactions: atomistic details of microbial sensing pathways, mesoscale colloidal dynamics, and population-level signaling networks. Existing frameworks either oversimplify biochemical coupling or lack scalability for 3D, time-dependent simulations. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational strategy combining lattice Boltzmann methods for fluid-structure interactions, agent-based modeling of microbial populations, and graph neural networks to capture adaptive signaling. The HPC implementation will optimize parallelization across spatial decomposition (fluid dynamics) and distributed graph architectures (signaling networks), with validation against experimental collaborator data on optogenetically engineered bacteria and photocatalytic colloids. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for designing biohybrid materials with controlled pattern formation, (2) identification of critical parameters governing stability in living-physical composites, and (3) open-source tools bridging continuum, discrete, and network-based simulation paradigms. This work establishes a computational foundation for engineering biologically integrated responsive matter, with applications ranging from sustainable bioremediation to adaptive photonic materials. The scale of parameter space exploration—requiring ~2 million core-hours—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to manage stochastic sampling across physicochemical conditions and system sizes. Success will provide both fundamental insights into non-equilibrium coupling across biological and abiotic components and a pipeline for accelerating the design of multifunctional living materials.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to science, mathematics, and engineering practice. Includes instruction in applied mathematics and statistics, data science, numerical analysis and scientific computing, computational mechanics and physics, parallel computing and computer architecture, and mathematical modeling.

abstract: Structural biology faces a critical challenge in resolving the dynamic, multi-scale interactions of biomolecular systems, particularly those involving large macromolecular assemblies and transient states that evade conventional experimental techniques. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform atomic-level molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and hybrid modeling of key structural processes, including the assembly mechanisms of viral capsid proteins and the conformational dynamics of membrane-bound receptors. Current computational limitations restrict the timescales and system sizes that can be feasibly modeled, hindering insights into allosteric regulation, ligand-binding pathways, and structural transitions central to cellular function. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-tiered computational approach integrating enhanced sampling techniques (e.g., metadynamics, replica exchange) with coarse-grained modeling to map free-energy landscapes of protein folding and aggregation. Large-scale MD simulations will utilize GPU-optimized software (AMBER, GROMACS) to achieve microsecond-to-millisecond timescales for systems exceeding 1 million atoms, including explicit solvent and membrane environments. Concurrently, cryo-EM density maps and X-ray crystallography data will inform flexible fitting algorithms to refine structural models of disordered regions in cytoskeletal proteins. The requested HPC allocation will enable parallel processing of ensemble-based simulations, machine learning-aided analysis of conformational clusters, and validation against experimental biophysical data (SAXS, FRET). Expected outcomes include atomic-resolution models of metastable intermediate states in chaperone-mediated folding, predictive frameworks for mutational impacts on protein stability, and mechanistic insights into how microtubule-associated proteins regulate polymerization kinetics. These results will advance fundamental understanding of molecular recognition and assembly principles, with direct implications for targeting structural vulnerabilities in neurodegenerative diseases and viral pathogenesis. By bridging computational and experimental structural biology, this work will establish scalable protocols for simulating multi-component cellular machinery, fostering collaboration across biochemistry and biophysics disciplines.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of submolecular and molecular components and assemblies of living systems and how they are organized into functional units such as cells and anatomic tissues. Includes instruction in glycoprotein, carbohydrate, protein, and nucleic acid structures and chemistry; cytoskeletal structure; nuclear and intracellular structures; molecular recognition; molecular chaperones; transcription and folding; multicellular organization; microtubules and microfilaments; cell differentiation; immunophysics; and DNA sequencing.

abstract: The design and optimization of industrial piping and automatic fire protection systems present significant challenges due to the complex interplay of fluid dynamics, thermal stresses, and regulatory compliance. Traditional design methods often rely on simplified models or iterative physical testing, which can lead to suboptimal performance, material inefficiencies, and safety risks. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models for simulating multiphase fluid flow, pressure transients, and thermal expansion in large-scale piping networks. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA), the research will evaluate system behavior under extreme operating conditions, including high-temperature steam distribution and emergency fire suppression scenarios. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize pipe routing and sprinkler head placement, minimizing pressure losses while ensuring compliance with NFPA standards and local building codes. The computational demands of these simulations—particularly the need to resolve turbulent flow patterns in three-dimensional geometries and perform parametric studies across diverse configurations—require parallel processing capabilities and large-scale memory allocation available only in HPC environments. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for pipe stress analysis, data-driven design guidelines to reduce installation costs, and open-source tools for simulating sprinkler coverage in complex architectural layouts. By integrating computational rigor with industry-specific requirements, this research aims to advance technical education in pipefitting disciplines and provide practitioners with methodologies to enhance system reliability and safety in critical infrastructure applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, install, and test industrial and commercial piping systems and automatic fire and exposure protection systems. Includes instruction in water systems, steam systems, heating and cooling systems, lubricating systems, piping materials, installation tools operation and maintenance, valve installation and repair, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This research project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies and latent risks in medication administration workflows performed by Medication Aides (MAs), a critical yet understudied component of patient safety. Despite rigorous training protocols, preventable errors—such as incorrect dosages, timing discrepancies, or documentation oversights—persist due to dynamic variables like fluctuating patient loads, heterogeneous care environments, and cognitive fatigue. Current quality improvement strategies rely on retrospective audits or self-reported data, which lack the granularity to model real-world complexity. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate MA workflows under diverse clinical scenarios and predict error-prone conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallelization of ABM simulations, incorporating stochastic patient acuity profiles, temporal workload distributions, and environmental interruptions (e.g., urgent requests, equipment availability). Concurrently, ML models trained on multimodal datasets—including anonymized electronic health records, time-motion studies, and biometric sensor data from MAs—will identify latent risk factors and validate simulation outcomes. The resulting hybrid models will quantify the impact of proposed interventions, such as dynamic task prioritization algorithms or redes shift rotation schedules, on error reduction. By bridging healthcare operations research, human factors engineering, and computational analytics, this project will generate actionable insights for optimizing MA training protocols and institutional workflow policies. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for healthcare educators and evidence-based guidelines for mitigating systemic risks, ultimately enhancing patient safety in long-term care and residential clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed medications; observe and report patient reactions and side effects; and perform related emergency and recording duties under the supervision of nurses and/or physicians. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, common medications and their effects, taking vital signs, oxygen administration, medication administration and application, record-keeping, and patient observation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of predicting and mitigating the impacts of climate change on culturally significant heritage sites through the integration of multidisciplinary data and computational modeling. Cultural heritage sites, which include archaeological landmarks, historical structures, and indigenous landscapes, face increasing threats from environmental stressors such as temperature fluctuations, extreme weather events, and soil degradation. Current risk assessment frameworks often lack the resolution and interdisciplinary scope required to account for complex interactions between environmental, geographical, and material factors. To bridge this gap, this research proposes a computational framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to synthesize climate projections, geospatial data, and material science models into a unified predictive system. The project will employ high-resolution regional climate models (RCMs) to simulate localized environmental changes over decadal timescales, coupled with machine learning algorithms to analyze site-specific vulnerability patterns derived from historical preservation datasets. Geospatial analytics will map risk hotspots, while agent-based modeling will simulate human intervention strategies under varying climate scenarios. By integrating these methods, the project aims to generate actionable insights into preservation prioritization and adaptive management. The computational demands of processing terabytes of climate data, running parallelized simulations, and training predictive models necessitate access to HPC resources for storage, scalability, and processing speed. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision-support tool for heritage conservators, a publicly available repository of risk projection datasets, and a methodological framework for interdisciplinary climate-cultural research. This work advances the intersection of environmental science, computational social science, and heritage studies, offering a replicable model for addressing complex, systems-level challenges through multidisciplinary collaboration.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated program that includes instruction in the general arts, general science, or unstructured studies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of electrical and electronic systems design, where traditional computer-aided drafting (CAD) tools struggle to efficiently model large-scale or high-frequency circuits, integrated embedded systems, and multi-domain interactions (e.g., electromagnetic interference, thermal dispersion). The computational limitations of conventional workflows often lead to oversimplified simulations, prolonged iteration cycles, and increased risk of post-fabrication design flaws. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enhanced CAD framework tailored for advanced electrical/electronics drafting applications. The research will leverage parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms to simulate high-fidelity models of power distribution networks, mixed-signal circuits, and IoT-enabled embedded systems. Key computational tasks include distributed parameter extraction for RF/microwave components, transient analysis of multi-layer PCBs under thermal stress, and topology optimization for energy-efficient circuit layouts. By deploying these workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to reduce simulation times by orders of magnitude while maintaining sub-1% error margins against physical prototypes. The project will also integrate GPU-accelerated rendering tools to enable real-time visualization of electromagnetic field distributions and 3D thermal maps within CAD environments. Outcomes will include an open-source plugin module compatible with industry-standard CAD software, validated through case studies on smart grid components and wearable electronics. This work will directly enhance the precision and scalability of electrical drafting education, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-aided design workflows while bridging gaps between academic training and industry demands for high-complexity system modeling. The requested computing resources will support large-scale parametric sweeps, dataset generation for AI/ML training, and collaborative cross-institution benchmarking efforts.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Drafting and Electrical/ Electronics CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working schematics and representations in support of electrical/electronic engineers, computer engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic electronics, electrical systems and computer layouts; electrode-mechanical drafting; manufacturing circuitry; computer-aided drafting (CAD); and electrical systems specification interpretation.

abstract: Aerospace medicine faces critical challenges in understanding and mitigating the physiological and psychological stressors experienced by crew members and passengers during prolonged air and space missions. Extended exposure to microgravity, radiation, circadian disruption, and confined environments contributes to multisystem degradation, including cardiovascular deconditioning, muscle atrophy, neurocognitive deficits, and immune dysfunction. Current countermeasures remain insufficient for long-duration missions, such as crewed Mars expeditions, necessitating advanced predictive models to optimize interventions. This project proposes a computational physiology framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate integrated human responses to aerospace environments and evaluate targeted countermeasures. Multiscale biomechanical models will couple cardiovascular fluid dynamics, musculoskeletal adaptations, and neural control systems under microgravity conditions, informed by astronaut biometric data from orbital missions. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze multi-omics datasets (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) to identify biomarkers of resilience and predict individualized health risks. HPC resources are essential for resolving the spatiotemporal complexity of whole-body simulations, enabling real-time modeling of autonomic regulation during extravehicular activities and high-G maneuvers. The computational pipeline will also test virtual interventions, including optimized exercise protocols, artificial gravity profiles, and pharmacological strategies, through probabilistic risk assessment workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to personalize countermeasure regimens, reduce mission-critical health failures, and inform next-generation vehicle life-support systems. By bridging clinical data with systems-level computational models, this work aims to establish scalable frameworks for maintaining human performance in extreme environments, directly supporting the development of evidence-based medical standards for emerging commercial spaceflight and deep-space exploration programs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the health care of operating crews, support personnel, and passengers of air and space vehicles. Includes instruction in special conditions of physical and psychological stress, emergency medical procedures, adaptive systems and artificial environments. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize maternal and neonatal outcomes during the perinatal period using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Despite advances in prenatal care, complications such as preeclampsia, preterm labor, and postpartum hemorrhage remain significant contributors to maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in underserved populations. Current risk assessment tools lack precision due to the complex interplay of biological, socioeconomic, and environmental factors. This research will leverage large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets from diverse clinical settings, integrating variables such as longitudinal vital sign trends, genetic markers, and geospatial health disparities. Machine learning models, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, will be trained to identify high-risk patients and recommend personalized intervention timelines. Computational challenges include processing multi-terabyte EHR repositories, managing heterogeneous data types, and iteratively optimizing model architectures—tasks requiring parallelized computing and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for perinatal complications with improved sensitivity over existing clinical scores, (2) open-source tools for real-time risk stratification adaptable to resource-limited settings, and (3) novel insights into modifiable risk factors through explainable AI techniques. By enabling rapid analysis of complex, multidimensional data, HPC resources will directly support the project’s goal of advancing evidence-based midwifery care through computational innovation. Results will be disseminated via midwifery clinical guidelines and collaborations with maternal health informatics networks, bridging gaps between computational science and nursing practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to independently deliver babies and treat mothers in the prenatal, delivery, and post-delivery periods. Includes instruction in pre-delivery screening, physician referral, and the care of infants during the delivery and immediate post-delivery phases.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of English as a Second Language (ESL) acquisition through large-scale computational analysis of learner linguistic patterns. The central research problem lies in identifying and modeling the nuanced relationships between instructional interventions, learner backgrounds, and proficiency outcomes in diverse ESL populations. Current studies often rely on small datasets or simplified metrics, limiting their ability to account for the complex interplay of sociolinguistic, cognitive, and pedagogical factors. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with longitudinal statistical modeling. The project will process multilingual corpora of learner writing samples, speech recordings, and demographic data using transformer-based models fine-tuned for error pattern detection and proficiency classification. Parallelized simulations will test hypotheses about optimal intervention timing and language feature sequencing across different learner subgroups. HPC resources are essential for training custom neural architectures on terabyte-scale datasets, running ensemble models to account for variability in learning trajectories, and performing real-time analysis of multimodal interaction data from digital learning platforms. Expected outcomes include (1) empirically validated frameworks for personalized ESL curriculum adaptation, (2) open-source tools for automated proficiency assessment aligned with Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) standards, and (3) novel insights into cross-linguistic transfer patterns among understudied language pairs. By enabling analysis at previously impractical scales, this research will directly inform evidence-based pedagogical strategies and contribute computational methodologies to the broader field of applied linguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: The intensifying challenges of climate variability and soil degradation necessitate advanced strategies to optimize crop resilience and nutrient efficiency. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational model to simulate genotype-environment-management (GxExM) interactions in staple crops under dynamic soil conditions, with a focus on nitrogen and phosphorus cycling. Current models lack the granularity to resolve root-soil-microbe feedbacks at scale, limiting their utility for precision agriculture. We propose a hybrid approach integrating mechanistic soil biogeochemistry models with machine learning (ML) to predict crop performance across heterogeneous field environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable (1) large-scale parameterization of partial differential equation systems describing nutrient transport and root exudation dynamics, (2) ensemble simulations of crop growth responses under 10^4 distinct soil-climate scenarios derived from historical and projected weather data, and (3) training of deep neural networks on the resultant datasets to identify optimal fertilization strategies. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for soil hydrology and parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification. Validation will utilize multi-year field trial data from collaborating institutions, incorporating hyperspectral imagery and rhizosphere microbiome sequencing. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive nutrient management and novel biomarkers for root efficiency traits.
