By elucidating nonlinear relationships between soil heterogeneity, microbial communities, and crop productivity, this work will directly inform breeding programs and reduce fertilizer waste in row-crop systems. The requested HPC allocation is critical for achieving biologically realistic spatiotemporal resolutions in simulations, which cannot be processed on local clusters due to memory constraints and the combinatorial complexity of GxExM interactions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the chemical, physical, and biological relationships of crops and the soils nurturing them. Includes instruction in the growth and behavior of agricultural crops, the development of new plant varieties, and the scientific management of soils and nutrients for maximum plant nutrition, health, and productivity.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing resilient supply chain networks under dynamic disruptions, such as material shortages, transportation delays, and demand volatility. Modern supply chains face increasing complexity due to globalization, climate risks, and geopolitical uncertainties, yet traditional analytical models struggle to balance cost efficiency with robustness at scale. The research problem centers on creating adaptive decision-support tools that integrate real-time data streams, stochastic demand forecasting, and multi-objective optimization to mitigate cascading disruptions. The proposed computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate supplier-customer interactions, mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) for inventory and routing optimization, and machine learning (ML) to predict disruption propagation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale parallel simulations across diverse scenarios, including regional crises and supplier failures, while training ML models on historical supply chain data. The project will utilize graph theory to map multi-tier supplier networks and reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust safety stock levels. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for evaluating trade-offs between cost, carbon footprint, and service-level targets during disruptions. This work will advance academic understanding of network resilience in logistics management and provide actionable insights for industries adopting just-in-time or lean supply chain strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the models will handle datasets with over 10,000 nodes, representing global supplier networks, to generate policy recommendations for contingency planning and resource allocation. The results will be validated against case studies from automotive and pharmaceutical supply chains, where delayed component deliveries incur high costs. This research aligns with the program’s focus on logistics planning and resource allocation, offering methodological innovations for sustainable supply chain management education and practice.
cip_title: Logistics, Materials, and Supply Chain Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and coordinate all logistical functions in an enterprise, ranging from acquisitions to receiving and handling, through internal allocation of resources to operations units, to the handling and delivery of output. Includes instruction in acquisitions and purchasing, inventory control, storage and handling, just-in-time manufacturing, logistics planning, shipping and delivery management, transportation, quality control, resource estimation and allocation, and budgeting.

abstract: The rapid expansion of online education necessitates evidence-based frameworks to optimize instructional design and learner engagement in virtual environments. While existing research identifies key factors in online pedagogy, the dynamic interplay of multimodal interaction data—including discussion forum text, video engagement metrics, and real-time assessment patterns—remains underexplored due to computational limitations. This project seeks to develop machine learning models that analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets from learning management systems (LMS) to identify predictive signatures of student success and instructor effectiveness in asynchronous online courses. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process natural language from discussion forums (via transformer-based architectures), temporal patterns in video-watching behaviors (using recurrent neural networks), and multimodal fusion of these features with assessment outcomes. Computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale LMS datasets spanning 50,000+ learners, optimizing transformer fine-tuning for domain-specific pedagogical discourse, and developing attention mechanisms to interpret model decisions for educator stakeholders. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for early identification of at-risk online learners, (2) evidence-based recommendations for temporal sequencing of multimedia content in course design, and (3) open-source tools to help instructors visualize interaction patterns relative to learning objectives. By enabling analysis of previously intractable datasets, this work will advance computational approaches to studying online pedagogy while directly addressing the practical needs of educators designing courses in hybrid and fully virtual programs. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data storage for deidentified learner interactions, and parallel processing of multimodal feature extraction pipelines.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various academic levels through online instructional technologies. Includes instruction in andragogy, pedagogy, assessment, instructional design and technology, and learning science.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance polymers with tailored properties necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize synthesis and processing parameters. Current experimental approaches in plastics engineering are time-intensive and costly, particularly when exploring the complex relationships between polymer microstructure, processing conditions, and final material performance. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale computational framework for predicting the behavior of novel polymer systems under industrial manufacturing conditions. The research will focus on simulating polymerization kinetics, melt flow dynamics during extrusion/injection molding, and long-term thermal stability of engineering-grade plastics. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model chain-level interactions and crosslinking phenomena, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict bulk material behavior during processing. Machine learning techniques will be employed to identify correlations between molecular architecture, processing parameters, and mechanical/thermal properties. The computational workflow requires parallelized simulations of systems containing >1 million atoms (MD) and coupled thermomechanical models with nonlinear viscoelastic material definitions (FEA). Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing screw design in extrusion systems, reducing thermal degradation in processing, and accelerating the development of recyclable polymer formulations. The results will provide critical insights into structure-property relationships that are experimentally inaccessible, enabling data-driven design of sustainable plastic materials. This work directly addresses industry needs for reduced trial-and-error prototyping and supports academic research in advanced polymer characterization. The proposed HPC resources are essential for handling the memory-intensive simulations and iterative parameter optimization required to establish this computational framework.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using industrial polymers. Includes instruction in the principles of macromolecular chemistry, polymerization and plastic manufacturing processes and equipment, design and operational testing procedures, equipment maintenance and repair procedures, safety procedures, applications to specific products, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of radiation therapy planning, diagnostic imaging optimization, and radiopharmaceutical dosimetry demands advanced computational tools to address unresolved challenges in clinical radiologic physics. Current limitations in modeling radiation-tissue interactions, particularly for heterogeneous anatomies and emerging modalities like MRI-guided radiotherapy and alpha-emitting radionuclides, restrict the precision of treatment delivery and diagnostic accuracy. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity, multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate radiation transport, energy deposition, and biological effect prediction across therapeutic, diagnostic, and nuclear medicine applications. The research will implement GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations (using Geant4/GATE toolkits) coupled with finite element biomechanical models to account for patient-specific tissue heterogeneity and dynamic motion (e.g., respiratory shifts, cardiac cycles). Machine learning architectures will be trained on simulated and clinical datasets to optimize real-time adaptive radiotherapy dose calculations and reduce uncertainties in SPECT/CT quantitative imaging. A dedicated focus will address the computational bottlenecks in modeling short-range alpha-particle interactions for targeted radionuclide therapy, requiring massively parallelized track structure simulations. The HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10^6+ beam configurations, 4D anatomical phantoms, and radiobiological models incorporating DNA damage repair kinetics. Expected outcomes include validated open-source modules for clinical translation, reducing systematic errors in tumor control probability calculations by ≥15% compared to current commercial algorithms. The work will directly inform safety protocols for FLASH proton therapy and improve dosimetric accuracy for pediatric nuclear medicine patients, addressing critical gaps in personalized radiologic care. By integrating HPC-driven insights into clinical workflows, this project aims to establish scalable computational standards for next-generation radiologic physics applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on that branch of physics which includes the physical aspects of radiation therapy, radiologic diagnosis, and/or nuclear medicine. Radiologic physicists must specialize in at least one of the three subspecialty areas: therapeutic radiological physics, diagnostic radiological physics, and/or medical nuclear physics.

abstract: Theatrical production management involves complex logistical, financial, and operational challenges that require dynamic decision-making under uncertainty. Current approaches to resource allocation—such as budgeting, scheduling, and risk assessment—often rely on static models or historical data, limiting adaptability to real-time variables like fluctuating ticket demand, labor availability, and supply chain disruptions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation in theatre production planning using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-variable scenarios and generate adaptive management strategies. Leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM), the research will simulate interactions between production elements (e.g., design teams, vendors, marketing departments) and external factors (e.g., economic trends, audience demographics). Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical production data and real-time inputs (e.g., social media engagement, ticket pre-sales) to predict outcomes such as cost overruns, labor bottlenecks, or revenue shortfalls. Monte Carlo methods will assess risk probabilities across thousands of simulated production timelines, enabling probabilistic resource allocation recommendations. HPC resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of these models, particularly for large-scale productions involving hundreds of interdependent variables. Expected outcomes include a toolkit for theatre managers to dynamically adjust budgets, staffing, and marketing strategies during pre-production and active runs, reducing financial waste and improving artistic outcomes. The project will also contribute a publicly accessible dataset of anonymized production metrics to support computational research in arts management. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with theatre operations, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for resource optimization in the visual and performing arts, with potential applications to grant allocation, venue scheduling, and sustainable arts ecosystem modeling.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business management principles to the management of theatres and production corporations. Includes instruction in theatrical production, theatre design and planning, fund-raising and promotion, investment strategies, human resources management, theatre operations management, marketing, public relations, financial management and insurance, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize resource efficiency and resilience amid climate variability and evolving pest-disease pressures. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating multi-scale interactions between crop genotypes, management practices, and environmental stressors to identify sustainable intensification strategies. We propose integrating high-resolution soil sensor data, climate projections, and genomic information into a coupled modeling system that combines process-based crop growth models with machine learning architectures. The core computational challenge involves parameterizing genotype-environment-management (G×E×M) relationships across spatial scales from individual plants to production fields, requiring iterative simulations of >10^6 possible scenario combinations. High-performance computing resources are essential for three components: 1) Parallelized execution of modified DSSAT-CROPGRO modules with custom stress response algorithms, 2) Training convolutional neural networks on hyperspectral imagery and LiDAR data to detect subfield nutrient deficiencies, and 3) Bayesian optimization of irrigation/nutrient application schedules using 10-year regional climate model ensembles. Initial pilot studies on soybean systems have demonstrated model feasibility but were constrained by 48-hour simulation bottlenecks when evaluating 50,000+ parameter sets. The requested allocation would enable daily canopy-scale resolution across 500ha virtual fields through GPU-accelerated cellular automata models, representing a 40× scalability improvement. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools for precision nitrogen management and genomic selection indices for drought-adaptive root architecture traits. By quantifying tradeoffs between yield stability and input costs under climate uncertainty, this work directly addresses priority gaps in digital agriculture infrastructure while adhering to FAIR data principles. The computational pipelines developed will provide transferable frameworks for optimizing diverse cropping systems, with particular relevance to row crop operations in water-limited environments.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural production operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Professional diving operations face significant challenges in safety, efficiency, and environmental adaptability due to the dynamic, high-risk nature of underwater environments. Current approaches to equipment design, decompression protocols, and emergency response planning rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the complexities of real-world diving scenarios, including turbulent flow interactions, physiological responses to hyperbaric conditions, and equipment failure modes. This project proposes a computational framework to address these limitations by developing high-resolution simulations of diver-environment systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Multiphysics models will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for water-current interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for equipment stress testing under extreme pressures, and machine learning (ML) to predict decompression risks based on diver physiology and environmental variables. These simulations will be validated against empirical data from controlled diving trials and sensor-equipped gear. The HPC infrastructure is essential to resolve microsecond-scale fluid-structure interactions in turbulent flows, optimize neural networks for real-time risk assessment, and perform Monte Carlo analyses of rare but critical failure events. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for decompression sickness mitigation, evidence-based protocols for salvage and rescue operations, and digital twins of diving systems to test novel equipment configurations. The results will advance safety standards in commercial and scientific diving while providing immersive simulation modules for diver training programs. By openly sharing optimized computational workflows, this project will establish a foundation for data-driven innovation in underwater technical operations, benefiting both academic research and industry practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as professional deep-water or scuba divers, diving instructors, or diving support personnel. Includes instruction in the use of diving equipment and related specialized gear; diving safety procedures; operation and maintenance of underwater life-support systems; underwater communication systems; decompression systems; underwater salvage; exploration, rescue, and photography; and installation and fitting of underwater mechanical systems and their maintenance, repair or demolition.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of theological concepts across key Christian traditions, with a focus on doctrinal debates, scriptural interpretations, and their cultural intersections. The central challenge lies in processing and correlating vast, multilingual textual corpora spanning early Christian writings, medieval scholastic works, Reformation-era polemics, and modern theological discourses. These sources—often digitized in heterogeneous formats—require advanced computational methods to map doctrinal shifts, identify patterns in theological argumentation, and contextualize them within broader intellectual histories. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for ancient Greek, Latin, and early modern vernacular texts, combined with network analysis to trace the development of contested concepts (e.g., grace, salvation, ecclesiology) across denominational boundaries. Computational theology methods will be adapted to detect semantic nuances in exegetical traditions, while machine learning models will classify rhetorical strategies in inter-confessional dialogues. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on niche theological lexicons, running large-scale comparative analyses of synodal documents, and simulating the diffusion of ideas through historical communities. Expected outcomes include a quantitative framework for assessing doctrinal continuity/discontinuity, visualizations of theological influence networks across eras, and open-access datasets linking creedal formulations to their philosophical underpinnings. By bridging computational humanities with historical theology, this work aims to provide new methodologies for understanding how Christian thought has negotiated cultural change while addressing contemporary interdisciplinary questions about religion’s role in shaping ethical systems. The resource request supports both the development of custom analytical pipelines and the preservation of computational outputs for reuse in religious studies scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy and teachings of Jesus Christ and his apostles, and the subsequent intellectual and cultural movements and institutions based on Christianity. Includes instruction in Christian sacred scripture, Christian literature and philosophy, and studies of one or more of the main branches of the faith and their cultural context including Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism, Protestantism, Evangelicalism, and others.

abstract: Dental restorative materials are critical for managing structural defects caused by trauma, decay, or congenital disorders, yet their long-term performance is limited by interfacial failures and microbial colonization. This project addresses the computational design of next-generation bioactive dental composites optimized for interfacial stress distribution and antimicrobial resistance. Current experimental approaches struggle to predict microscale biomechanical interactions at the material-tooth interface or model dynamic microbial biofilm formation under oral cavity conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and agent-based modeling (ABM). High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable atomistic MD simulations to characterize adhesive bonding dynamics between composite resins and dentinal collagen, while FEA models will resolve stress concentrations across hierarchical tooth-composite interfaces under masticatory loads. Concurrently, ABM will simulate spatial biofilm development influenced by material surface topography and chemical leaching. Machine learning algorithms will iteratively optimize composite formulations by correlating simulation outputs with experimental data from in vitro microbial assays and mechanical testing. The project’s computational demands arise from the need to process terabyte-scale datasets from parallelized simulations, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for designing composites with enhanced mechanical durability and biofilm-resistant properties, reducing secondary caries and restoration failures. This interdisciplinary approach bridges materials science, microbiology, and biomechanics, offering a paradigm shift in dental biomaterial development with potential applications in personalized restorative therapies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the work advances computational methodologies for health sciences, addressing a critical niche in dental innovation beyond conventional experimental paradigms.
cip_title: Dental Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dental services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Public health research increasingly relies on complex computational models to address multifaceted challenges in disease prevention, health equity, and policy evaluation. Existing approaches often struggle to integrate high-resolution demographic, environmental, and behavioral data at scale, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making. This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling framework to simulate the spread of emerging infectious diseases in urban environments while accounting for heterogeneous population mobility, socioeconomic disparities in healthcare access, and dynamic public health interventions. The computational demands of simulating millions of individual agents with time-varying interactions, coupled with the integration of multi-terabyte geospatial and electronic health record datasets, necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will parallelize model components using MPI and OpenMP to optimize scalability across thousands of CPU cores, enabling stochastic parameter sweeps to quantify uncertainty in outbreak trajectories. Machine learning methods will be applied to reduce dimensionality in parameter calibration, leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for training neural networks on synthetic epidemic scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive disease transmission modeling, (2) policy-relevant projections of intervention efficacy under varying resource allocation strategies, and (3) novel metrics quantifying equity impacts of containment measures. By enabling rapid scenario testing at unprecedented spatial granularity, this work will advance capacity to prioritize targeted vaccination campaigns and mobility restrictions during emerging outbreaks. The requested HPC allocation directly supports public health agencies’ need for computationally intensive models that reflect real-world complexity, ultimately strengthening evidence-based pandemic preparedness in diverse urban settings.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public health, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the safety, efficacy, and innovation of nail care practices through computational modeling and data-driven analysis. While nail technology is traditionally a hands-on field, emerging challenges—such as optimizing sterilization protocols, predicting allergenicity of novel cosmetic formulations, and modeling the biomechanical interactions between nail products and natural nail structures—require sophisticated computational approaches. Current training and practice rely heavily on empirical knowledge, with limited tools to systematically evaluate risks or design evidence-based solutions. This research addresses gaps in understanding microbial persistence under salon conditions, chemical stability of hybrid gel polishes, and stress distribution in artificial nail extensions. Computational methods will include finite element analysis to simulate mechanical forces on nail architectures, molecular dynamics to study polymer-curing processes, and machine learning models trained on microbial genomic data to predict pathogen survival post-sterilization. Additionally, agent-based models will evaluate contamination risks in salon workflows. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights for improving sanitization standards, reducing occupational hazards, and guiding product development. Outcomes will include open-access datasets on material properties and microbial thresholds, predictive tools for allergy risk assessment, and simulation frameworks for training nail technicians in virtual environments. This work bridges the technical-artisanal divide, positioning computational research as a transformative force in a field where empirical tradition and modern scientific rigor intersect.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the challenge of analyzing high-dimensional longitudinal data in clinical trials, where traditional statistical methods face computational limitations due to increasing data complexity and scale. Clinical trials increasingly incorporate frequent measurements of biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes, and digital health metrics, generating datasets with high temporal resolution and numerous covariates. Existing software and algorithms struggle with the computational demands of fitting mixed-effects models or performing variable selection in such settings, leading to oversimplified analyses or impractical runtime. This project aims to develop a scalable, parallelized computational framework for Bayesian hierarchical models that efficiently handle high-dimensional longitudinal data. The approach will leverage Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling techniques, optimized for graphics processing unit (GPU) architectures, to accelerate posterior inference. Key innovations include adaptive preconditioning strategies for ill-conditioned covariance matrices and sparse matrix operations to reduce memory overhead. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to benchmark the method against existing approaches using simulated datasets with varying dimensionality (10³–10⁶ observations, 10²–10⁴ covariates) and to apply the framework to an ongoing Phase III trial evaluating a novel immunotherapy for autoimmune diseases. The trial’s data include weekly multi-omics measurements, electronic health record covariates, and irregularly sampled patient-generated health data. Successful implementation will provide the biostatistics community with open-source software optimized for distributed HPC environments, enabling rigorous analysis of complex trial data without resorting to dimensionality reduction. Anticipated outcomes include improved identification of treatment-effect heterogeneity, more accurate characterization of temporal biomarker trajectories, and actionable insights for adaptive trial designs. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for advancing computational infrastructure in clinical research and has broad applicability to precision medicine initiatives requiring real-time analysis of high-resolution biomedical data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of descriptive and inferential statistics to biomedical research and clinical, public health, and industrial issues related to human populations. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, modeling, clinical trials methodology, disease and survival analysis, longitudinal analysis, missing data analysis, spatial analysis, computer tomography, biostatistics consulting, and applications to such topics as genetics, oncology, pharmacokinetics, physiology, neurobiology, and biophysics.

abstract: Wildfire behavior prediction remains a critical challenge in fire protection, with existing models often failing to integrate real-time environmental variables, fuel dynamics, and fire-atmosphere interactions at sufficient spatial-temporal resolution. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance coupled fire-atmosphere modeling with embedded machine learning for adaptive wildfire spread prediction. The research will develop multi-scale simulations using physics-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models such as Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS) and the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF)-Fire framework, enhanced by deep learning architectures to assimilate real-time sensor data from IoT networks, satellite imagery, and weather stations. Key computational challenges include resolving turbulent combustion processes at meter-scale resolutions across kilometer-scale domains, optimizing data assimilation workflows, and training neural networks on heterogeneous wildfire datasets. The HPC implementation will employ parallelized simulations using MPI and OpenMP across thousands of CPU cores, coupled with GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines for feature extraction from multispectral imagery. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated wildfire prediction system with 20-30% improved accuracy over operational models in complex terrain, (2) quantitative risk assessment tools integrating building vulnerability metrics with fire spread projections, and (3) open-source computational workflows for real-time data fusion in fire emergencies. This work directly addresses critical gaps in fire protection science by enabling high-fidelity simulation of coupled fire-fuel-weather interactions while maintaining computational feasibility for operational timeframes. The requested resources will support ensemble simulations across historical fire scenarios, sensitivity analyses of mitigation strategies, and development of AI-driven early warning systems with potential applications in community evacuation planning and adaptive resource allocation for fire agencies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing prevalence of sports-related concussions and the variability in recovery trajectories present a critical challenge in athletic training. Current return-to-play protocols rely on generalized guidelines that fail to account for individual neurophysiological differences, leading to suboptimal outcomes and potential long-term health risks. This project seeks to develop personalized rehabilitation frameworks by integrating high-resolution neuroimaging data, biomechanical sensor outputs, and dynamic biomarkers of cerebral metabolism. The research will employ computational modeling to simulate the effects of graded physical and cognitive exertion on brain recovery processes in concussed athletes. A hybrid approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating intracranial pressure dynamics and machine learning (ML) algorithms for pattern recognition in multimodal datasets will be implemented. High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabyte-scale diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) sequences, compute real-time fluid-structure interactions in FEA, and train deep neural networks on heterogeneous data streams from wearable sensors and clinical assessments. Expected outcomes include a predictive model that maps individual recovery thresholds to specific exertion modalities, enabling data-driven adjustments to rehabilitation protocols. The computational tools developed will be open-sourced as modular pipelines, facilitating translation to clinical practice. By bridging neurobiology, biomechanics, and computational analytics, this work aims to advance evidence-based standards in concussion management while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources in specialized athletic healthcare domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work in consultation with, and under the supervision of physicians to prevent and treat sports injuries and associated conditions. Includes instruction in the identification, evaluation, and treatment of athletic injuries and illnesses; first aid and emergency care; therapeutic exercise; anatomy and physiology; exercise physiology; kinesiology and biomechanics; nutrition; sports psychology; personal and community health; knowledge of various sports and their biomechanical and physiological demands; and applicable professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision in radiation dose optimization for computed tomography (CT) imaging through the development of patient-specific, anatomy-aware exposure protocols. While modern CT systems employ automated exposure control, these tools rely on generalized patient models and lack the resolution to account for fine-scale variations in tissue composition, organ geometry, or pathological anomalies. This gap poses risks of overexposure in vulnerable populations—particularly pediatric and oncologic patients—and undermines image quality in complex anatomical regions. We propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations with deep learning-based organ segmentation to generate dynamic, adaptive exposure parameters tailored to individual patient anatomy. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train 3D convolutional neural networks on a curated dataset of 15,000 anonymized pediatric and adult CT studies, with voxel-level annotations for 27 tissue types. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations (Geant4-based) will model photon interactions across 10^6 unique anatomical configurations, incorporating variable beam energies, collimation strategies, and iterative reconstruction algorithms. Computational outputs will be validated against physical phantom measurements and clinical image quality assessments conducted by certified radiographers. Anticipated outcomes include a deployable software module for real-time exposure adaptation and an open-access dataset correlating simulated dose distributions with patient-specific image noise metrics. This work bridges radiologic science, computational physics, and machine learning to address a critical need in medical imaging: minimizing ionizing radiation risks while preserving diagnostic fidelity. Successful implementation could reduce effective dose variability by 30-50% in heterogeneous patient populations, directly enhancing safety protocols in radiologic practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical imaging services to patients and attending health care professionals. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, patient positioning, radiographic technique, radiation biology, safety and emergency procedures, equipment operation and maintenance, quality assurance, patient education, and medical imaging/radiologic services management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale textual datasets in English literature, addressing gaps in understanding how narrative structures evolve across genres and periods. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically track patterns in syntax, metaphor, and discourse coherence across thousands of texts. Our research focuses on a corpus of 18th- to 20th-century British and American novels, letters, and essays to identify latent stylistic and thematic shifts that correlate with socio-cultural transformations. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models for semantic role labeling and dependency parsing, with graph-theoretical analysis to map narrative networks. These methods require parallelized processing of terabytes of text, necessitating HPC infrastructure for efficient tokenization, embedding generation, and graph traversal. Key challenges include optimizing memory usage for heterogeneous document formats and scaling community detection algorithms to trace recurring character archetypes or plot motifs. Expected outcomes include (1) a quantitative framework for classifying narrative innovation in understudied literary subgenres, (2) open-access tools for visualizing temporal shifts in rhetorical strategies, and (3) evidence-based hypotheses about the relationship between linguistic complexity and historical readership trends. By enabling systematic comparisons across 50,000+ texts, this work will advance digital humanities scholarship by demonstrating how computational rigor can complement qualitative interpretation. The requested resources—particularly GPU nodes for fine-tuning BERT-based models and high-memory CPUs for graph analytics—are critical to handling the project’s scale. Results will be disseminated through an interactive web repository, peer-reviewed publications on computational literary analysis, and workshops for literature researchers adopting HPC methodologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in English language literature, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models for optimizing the design and manufacturing processes of fiber-reinforced polymer composites, which are critical to advancing performance and sustainability in automotive, marine, and renewable energy applications. A key challenge in composite materials technology lies in understanding the nonlinear interactions between matrix materials, reinforcement fibers, and manufacturing variables (e.g., curing temperatures, pressure cycles). Traditional trial-and-error approaches are resource-intensive and limit the exploration of novel material combinations. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating multiscale finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate composite behavior across fabrication and operational phases. The FEA models will resolve micromechanical stress distributions at fiber-matrix interfaces, while CFD simulations will optimize resin infusion processes in mold-based manufacturing. An ML pipeline trained on simulation datasets will predict optimal curing parameters and failure thresholds under cyclic loading. The HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across diverse material configurations (carbon/glass fibers, thermoset/thermoplastic matrices) and stochastic defect scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated models for rapid prototyping of composites with tailored stiffness-to-weight ratios and enhanced environmental resistance, directly applicable to wind turbine blade design and lightweight automotive components. By reducing reliance on physical testing, this computational approach aims to accelerate the development of cost-effective, durable composites while minimizing material waste—advancing both industrial innovation and sustainability goals in engineering technology.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and use of composite materials in aircraft technology, automotive technology, boats, medical prostheses, and wind turbines. Includes instruction in computer-aided design and drafting, composite materials and processes, composite maintenance, composite manufacturing, composite repair, material science, and mold manufacturing and production.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to address systemic biases in consumer credit risk models, leveraging high-dimensional transactional data and alternative behavioral indicators. Traditional credit scoring systems often rely on historical financial metrics that disproportionately exclude marginalized demographics while inadequately capturing real-time economic behaviors. The project aims to integrate dynamic, non-traditional data streams—such as gig economy participation, digital payment patterns, and supply chain dependencies—into ensemble machine learning models to improve predictive fairness without sacrificing accuracy. The central computational challenge involves processing terabyte-scale datasets with complex temporal dependencies while simultaneously optimizing multiple conflicting objectives: default prediction accuracy, regulatory compliance, and demographic parity across protected classes. High-performance computing resources are required to implement parallelized Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning across competing fairness-accuracy trade-offs, coupled with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to stress-test model robustness under evolving macroeconomic conditions. The proposed framework will employ hybrid architectures combining graph neural networks to map inter-business relationships with transformer-based time series analysis for individual behavioral trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source algorithmic toolkit for fairness-aware credit scoring validated against EU GDPR and US ECOA standards, (2) quantitative evidence informing policy frameworks for alternative data usage in financial services, and (3) scalability benchmarks for ethical AI deployment in regulated industries. By bridging computational statistics, regulatory tech, and consumer finance, this work aims to establish new methodological standards for equity-conscious business analytics in emerging data economies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to advance data-driven advertising strategies through the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for real-time optimization of multi-platform ad campaigns. The research problem centers on the escalating complexity of digital advertising ecosystems, where fragmented consumer touchpoints, dynamic audience behaviors, and high-dimensional data streams (e.g., social media interactions, programmatic bidding logs, and cross-device engagement metrics) overwhelm traditional analytical tools. Current methods struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets at scale or adapt bidding and creative strategies in near-real time, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and diminished campaign efficacy. To address this, we propose a computational architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for cross-platform audience modeling, reinforcement learning (RL) agents for adaptive bidding, and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for creative sentiment analysis. These components will be co-optimized using distributed training across GPU clusters to handle terabyte-scale datasets spanning paid search, social media, and connected TV platforms. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across thousands of concurrent simulations, enabling rapid iteration of scenario-based campaign forecasts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for audience segmentation prediction (with privacy-preserving federated learning modules) and a decision support system that reduces computational latency in campaign adjustments by 40-60% compared to industry benchmarks. By demonstrating scalable methods to synthesize behavioral, contextual, and creative data streams, this work will provide both scholarly and practical contributions to computational advertising research, particularly in resource-constrained environments where marginal gains in targeting precision directly impact return on ad spend. The requested resources will support model training, large-scale A/B testing simulations, and storage of anonymized interaction datasets from partner advertising platforms.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in high-volume, complex document processing workflows by developing and optimizing computational models for next-generation word processing systems. While conventional word processors excel at basic tasks, they struggle with scalability, real-time collaboration on large documents, and integration of advanced features such as context-aware formatting or AI-driven content optimization—particularly in technical domains requiring precise formatting (e.g., code documentation, engineering reports, or mathematical manuscripts). To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize and accelerate core word processing operations, including dynamic rendering of multi-user edits, automated semantic analysis for error detection, and large-scale template optimization. Our approach combines distributed computing frameworks with machine learning models trained on technical document corpora to enable real-time processing of documents exceeding 1,000 pages with embedded multimedia, cross-references, and collaborative annotations. Key computational challenges include minimizing latency during concurrent editing sessions, optimizing memory allocation for heterogeneous document elements, and developing GPU-accelerated natural language processing pipelines for style consistency checks. By simulating user interaction patterns and document complexity scenarios on HPC clusters, we aim to create a proof-of-concept architecture that reduces processing delays by 40–60% compared to existing solutions while maintaining sub-millisecond response times for critical operations. The outcomes will directly benefit technical fields requiring robust documentation tools, such as software development and academic publishing, while providing a framework for integrating AI-assisted writing features without compromising performance. This work will also generate open-source benchmarks for evaluating computational efficiency in word processing systems, addressing a significant gap in language-driven HPC applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing artificial intelligence (AI) integration in clinical decision support systems (CDSS). As AI tools become pervasive in healthcare, their deployment raises novel legal questions related to liability, algorithmic bias, compliance with privacy statutes (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR), and the interpretation of "standard of care" in malpractice litigation. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically evaluate the vast, heterogeneous datasets required to model these interactions, including court opinions, regulatory guidance, insurance claims, and simulated patient outcomes. This project proposes a computational legal analytics framework combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling, and probabilistic graph networks to map how emerging case law and regulatory actions intersect with technical system performance. Legal texts and healthcare incident reports will be processed using transformer-based models fine-tuned for semantic extraction of legal predicates and causal reasoning patterns. Concurrently, stochastic simulations of CDSS-patient interactions will generate synthetic datasets to quantify how variations in algorithmic transparency and regulatory constraints correlate with litigation risk profiles. By integrating these pipelines on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to identify critical thresholds in system accuracy, explainability, and compliance that influence judicial outcomes and policy reform. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for predicting legal exposure in AI-driven healthcare innovation and a policy optimization model to balance liability frameworks with equitable technology adoption. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational law, health policy, and ethical AI, offering a paradigm to proactively address legal uncertainties in rapidly evolving medical technologies.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies and regulations affecting the health care industry, health professions, health services and insurance industries, and patients.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the rhetorical dynamics of large-scale digital writing communities through computational text analysis, a novel approach in writing studies that demands high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While prior research has examined localized case studies of online discourse, the scale and complexity of multimodal, cross-platform digital writing—such as collaborative knowledge-building on wikis, argumentation in public comment forums, and genre-blending in social media—remain understudied due to computational limitations. The central research problem lies in mapping how rhetorical strategies (e.g., ethos construction, counterargument patterns, multimodal persuasion) evolve across diverse digital spaces and timeframes, requiring analysis of terabytes of unstructured text, image metadata, and temporal interaction logs. The project will employ transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for rhetorical feature detection, network analysis of co-occurring persuasive moves, and GPU-accelerated topic modeling to trace genre hybridity in cross-platform corpora. These methods necessitate HPC resources to manage distributed processing of heterogeneous data, parallelized model training across writing domains, and real-time visualization of rhetorical networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for computational rhetoric analysis applicable to emerging digital writing contexts, (2) empirical insights into how platform architectures shape collective persuasion strategies, and (3) open-access tools for writing researchers to analyze rhetorical patterns at unprecedented scale. By bridging computational methods with writing studies’ theoretical foundations, this work advances disciplinary understanding of 21st-century digital literacy practices while demonstrating how HPC infrastructure can expand humanities scholars’ capacity to engage complex, born-digital texts. The results will inform pedagogy for teaching adaptive rhetorical strategies in technologically mediated environments and provide benchmarks for interdisciplinary studies of large-scale discourse.
cip_title: Rhetoric and Composition/ Writing Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rhetoric and composition/writing studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance construction efficiency and structural resilience through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of modular building systems. Modular construction, while promising for reducing costs and timelines, faces challenges in optimizing material use, assembly sequencing, and load distribution across diverse environmental conditions. Traditional physical prototyping and empirical methods are time-intensive and fail to account for the complex, interdependent variables influencing modular performance. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), discrete event simulation, and machine learning (ML) to model modular assemblies at scale. FEA will evaluate stress distribution, thermal performance, and seismic resilience across 3D-printed and prefabricated components, while ML algorithms will iteratively optimize material allocation and assembly workflows based on simulated outcomes. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of thousands of design permutations, incorporating real-world data on material properties, climate stressors, and supply chain constraints. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate on-site labor dynamics to identify bottlenecks in construction workflows. Validation will occur through comparison with physical prototype testing and historical project data. Expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying cost-optimal modular configurations under variable constraints, a decision-support tool for trade-offs between material durability and project timelines, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated structural performance metrics. This work will directly contribute to reducing material waste in construction projects by up to 20% in simulated scenarios, while improving the scalability of modular techniques for affordable housing applications. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the high-resolution spatial datasets and computationally intensive multiphysics simulations required for industry-grade accuracy. By bridging computational engineering with construction trades, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven building practices in vocational technical education.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the building, inspecting, and maintaining of structures and related properties. May include instruction in masonry, carpentry, electrical and power transmission installation, building/construction finishing, management, inspection and other construction-related applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational workflows in architectural design, specifically addressing the integration of generative algorithms, real-time simulation, and multi-objective optimization within immersive digital design environments. Contemporary architectural practice faces a critical challenge in balancing design innovation, material efficiency, and environmental performance, particularly as projects grow in scale and complexity. While parametric modeling and digital fabrication have transformed design possibilities, existing tools struggle to synthesize real-time feedback across structural, thermal, and occupant-centric datasets during iterative design exploration. This research proposes a computational framework that unifies physics-based simulations, machine learning-assisted topology optimization, and augmented reality (AR) interfaces to enable architects to interactively explore high-dimensional design spaces. The HPC infrastructure will support parallelized evaluation of thousands of design variants through finite element analysis (FEA) for structural performance, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for microclimate modeling, and reinforcement learning agents trained to propose material-efficient geometries. A novel aspect involves developing distributed computing pipelines to bridge discrete architectural software ecosystems (e.g., BIM platforms, game engines) with scientific simulation tools, requiring customized containerization and GPU-accelerated rendering for AR visualization. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source middleware prototype for cross-platform interoperability, validated through case studies on adaptive reuse projects requiring rapid performance evaluation of heritage structures under climate stress scenarios. By reducing latency between design iteration and performance feedback from days to minutes, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for computationally augmented decision-making in architecture, with broader implications for resource-efficient urban retrofitting strategies. The requested resources will enable scaling from single-building analyses to district-level simulations, addressing critical gaps in tools for sustainable architectural practice.
cip_definition: An advanced program of study for architects and related professionals that focuses on theoretical and practical issues in architecture and integrates digital technologies into architectural design, fabrication, and construction. Includes instruction in architectural history and urban theory, 3-D digital technologies, construction, design and fabrication methods, and sustainable practices in architecture.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing executive coaching strategies in complex organizational ecosystems. While executive coaching is a critical tool for leadership development and organizational change, current methodologies often rely on qualitative, anecdotal approaches that struggle to account for the dynamic interplay of individual behaviors, team dynamics, and systemic organizational variables. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven models to predict how tailored coaching interventions propagate through hierarchical and cross-functional networks, particularly in large, geographically dispersed organizations. To address this gap, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate multi-level organizational interactions, integrating behavioral datasets (e.g., psychometric assessments, 360-degree feedback) with real-time communication metadata (e.g., email, Slack networks) to map decision-making cascades. HPC resources will enable the parallelization of thousands of scenario simulations, varying parameters such as leadership styles, communication latency, and team cohesion thresholds. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks, will be applied to identify latent patterns in coaching efficacy across diverse organizational cultures. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for quantifying the second-order effects of coaching interventions, such as their impact on innovation cycles or conflict resolution pathways. This work aims to establish a novel, computationally rigorous paradigm for designing adaptive coaching protocols that balance individual executive growth with enterprise-wide strategic objectives. By bridging computational social science with leadership development, the project will provide actionable insights for optimizing human capital investments in rapidly evolving business environments, with potential applications in merger integration, digital transformation initiatives, and crisis leadership preparedness.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on assisting individuals achieve career goals or assisting business leaders achieve organizational change. Includes instruction in executive coaching, group dynamics, leadership, management, organizational behavior, organizational communication, and team building.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interplay between host immune responses and microbiome metabolic activity in chronic inflammatory disorders, with a focus on diseases lacking robust diagnostic biomarkers. Current clinical approaches often fail to account for the bidirectional, multiscale interactions between human cellular signaling pathways and microbial community functions, particularly in conditions such as post-infectious inflammatory syndromes. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to integrate multi-omic datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and single-cell transcriptomic) from patient-derived samples with mechanistic computational models of immune-microbial crosstalk. A hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, network inference, and Bayesian hierarchical methods will be employed to simulate spatial and temporal shifts in microbial metabolite production and their immunomodulatory effects on mucosal tissues. The computational pipeline will prioritize scalability to handle heterogeneous datasets from longitudinal cohorts while maintaining interpretability for clinical translation. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved microbial metabolic signatures predictive of disease flares and the generation of testable hypotheses about host-microbe feedback loops amenable to therapeutic intervention. By bridging systems biology and clinical phenomenology, this work aims to address critical gaps in personalized management of inflammation-driven pathologies, offering a paradigm shift from current symptom-focused approaches to mechanism-based stratification. The requested computing resources will enable the iterative refinement of models through parallelized parameter space exploration and validation against experimental data from collaborator labs, ultimately supporting the development of open-source tools for clinical researchers investigating host-microbe interactions.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated clinical science program that prepares clinicians to conduct clinical and translational research in various areas. Note: programs that prepare clinicians to conduct research in specific scientific fields should report under the relevant CIP code series (e.g., Series 26 Biological and Biomedical Sciences).

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in clinical workflow optimization by developing a machine learning (ML) framework to predict and mitigate patient no-show risks and procedural bottlenecks in outpatient care settings. Medical assistants (MAs) play a critical role in managing patient flow, coordinating pre-examination protocols, and ensuring timely resource allocation, yet clinics often lack predictive tools to adapt dynamically to operational uncertainties. The research problem centers on the gap between static scheduling systems and the variable demands of patient behavior, clinic staffing, and equipment availability. To resolve this, we propose a computational approach leveraging historical patient data (demographics, appointment records, clinical metrics) and real-time clinic operation logs to train ensemble ML models capable of forecasting no-show probabilities and optimizing MA task prioritization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning diverse clinical variables, perform hyperparameter tuning for time-series forecasting models (e.g., transformer-based architectures), and simulate clinic workflows via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include a deployable decision-support system that reduces idle time for clinical staff and diagnostic equipment by 15–20%, as validated through retrospective analysis of pilot data from partner clinics. Additionally, the project will generate novel benchmarks for operational analytics in outpatient care, bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational logistics. By focusing on the intersection of healthcare operations and predictive analytics, this work advances an understudied niche in health sciences, directly enhancing the efficacy of medical assistants while avoiding overlap with traditional clinical or public health domains. The computational pipeline developed here will be open-sourced to support scalability in resource-constrained care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical office administrative services and perform clinical duties including patient intake and care, routine diagnostic and recording procedures, pre-examination and examination assistance, and the administration of medications and first aid. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology; medical terminology; medical law and ethics; patient psychology and communications; medical office procedures; and clinical diagnostic, examination, testing, and treatment procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing sustainable tourism flows in high-density urban destinations through advanced computational modeling. As global tourism rebounds post-pandemic, cities face escalating pressures from overcrowding, resource strain, and conflicting stakeholder priorities. Traditional demand forecasting models fail to capture the dynamic interplay between real-time visitor behavior, localized infrastructure capacities, and environmental constraints. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale tourism ecosystems, integrating heterogeneous data streams including mobile device mobility patterns, transit network performance metrics, attraction capacity thresholds, and climate impact indicators. The computational model will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate millions of individual tourist decision pathways under varying policy scenarios, while machine learning components will predict emergent crowd behaviors and system tipping points. This approach requires significant HPC resources for both the calibration of hyperparameters across multidimensional datasets (including 5 years of geotagged visitor data from 12 global cities) and the execution of real-time "digital twin" simulations for adaptive management applications. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of testing interventions such as dynamic pricing architectures, congestion-based routing recommendations, and carbon-aware itinerary optimization at metropolitan scales. The research aims to establish new methodologies for computational tourism ecosystem management, providing destination managers and policymakers with evidence-based tools to balance economic objectives with carrying capacity limits. By advancing predictive analytics for complex tourism environments, this work contributes to an emerging interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of computational social science, urban resilience planning, and sustainable travel systems engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage travel-related enterprises and related convention and/or tour services. Includes instruction in travel agency management, tour arranging and planning, convention and event planning, travel industry operations and procedures, tourism marketing and promotion strategies, travel counseling, travel industry law, international and domestic operations, and travel and tourism policy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of autonomous cargo transport systems in dynamic environments necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize real-time decision-making, route planning, and resource allocation. Current approaches for coordinating multi-agent fleets in mixed-traffic settings (e.g., ports, warehouses, and urban delivery networks) struggle to balance efficiency, safety, and scalability due to the combinatorial explosion of variables in large-scale systems. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity simulation framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize heterogeneous transportation networks involving autonomous ground and aerial vehicles, human-operated equipment, and fluctuating demand patterns. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to evaluate scenarios such as congestion mitigation, energy-efficient pathfinding, and failure recovery under uncertainty. By leveraging parallel computing architectures, we will train adaptive control policies on synthetic and real-world datasets, scaling to networks with over 10,000 interacting agents—a magnitude beyond current single-node simulation capabilities. Key outcomes include quantifiable performance benchmarks for hybrid human-autonomous systems, open-source optimization tools tailored for materials-moving applications, and predictive models for infrastructure stress testing. The research directly supports the development of safer, more resilient logistics networks while reducing the computational barriers to deploying AI-driven coordination in industrial settings. Results will be validated against operational data from partner freight hubs, ensuring practical relevance. This work fills a critical gap in transportation informatics by enabling large-scale, real-time analysis of emergent interactions in next-generation supply chains, with implications for energy consumption reduction, accident prevention, and infrastructure investment prioritization.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in transportation and materials moving, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven decision-making in corrections policy through the development of predictive models for evaluating rehabilitation program efficacy. Despite significant investments in offender rehabilitation, outcomes remain inconsistent, and existing analytical tools often fail to account for the complex interplay of sociodemographic, behavioral, and systemic variables influencing recidivism. This research addresses this gap by integrating heterogeneous datasets—including historical criminal records, program participation metrics, and longitudinal post-release surveys—into a unified computational framework. Agent-based modeling will simulate individual and cohort-level trajectories under varying intervention scenarios, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract qualitative insights from parole officer notes and rehabilitative program feedback. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, necessitating scalable GPU clusters for training deep learning architectures and stochastic optimization of intervention parameters. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for quantifying program risk-benefit ratios and a policy dashboard to visualize cost-per-success metrics across demographic strata. By enabling real-time scenario testing and bias auditing, this work aims to reduce over-reliance on heuristic approaches in corrections management, offering a paradigm shift toward adaptive, evidence-based resource allocation. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—spanning computational social science, public policy, and criminology—highlights the transformative potential of HPC in addressing systemic challenges within understudied niches of criminal justice research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in corrections and criminal justice, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent patterns in biological systems through large-scale simulations of organismal interactions, aiming to uncover fundamental principles underlying collective behaviors in diverse taxa. While collective phenomena—such as flocking, swarming, or synchronized signaling—are observed across biological scales, the general rules driving these behaviors remain poorly understood, particularly in non-model organisms and under variable environmental conditions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling with empirical data on movement, communication, and resource utilization from field studies of arthropods, avian groups, and marine invertebrates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating populations of >10^5 agents across parameter spaces that capture habitat heterogeneity, stochastic disturbances, and interspecific variability. Each agent will follow dynamically updated rules informed by species-specific biological constraints (e.g., sensory thresholds, energy budgets), with parallelized simulations running on GPU clusters to optimize scaling. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved interaction motifs that promote robust collective outcomes despite phylogenetic and ecological differences, and (2) predictive models of how environmental stressors disrupt or amplify self-organization. By focusing on cross-taxa principles rather than molecular or ecosystem-level mechanisms, this work bridges gaps between subdisciplines in general biology while avoiding domain-specific assumptions. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will enable researchers to test hypotheses about behavioral adaptation and resilience in biologically realistic virtual environments, advancing our capacity to study complexity in underexplored species. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential given the iterative nature of parameter optimization and the need for high-resolution, multi-generational simulations across proposed scenarios.
cip_definition: A general program of biology at the introductory, basic level or a program in biology or the biological sciences that is undifferentiated as to title or content. Includes instruction in general biology and programs covering a variety of biological specializations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biomedical systems, particularly in medical imaging and diagnostic technologies, demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in accuracy, scalability, and real-time processing. Current methods for analyzing high-resolution medical images, such as MRI and CT scans, struggle with processing latency and precision when handling large datasets, limiting their utility in time-sensitive clinical environments. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize deep learning models capable of rapid, automated analysis of multi-modal medical imaging data. The research will focus on training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures on distributed GPU clusters to enhance anomaly detection in neurological and oncological imaging. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive 3D volumetric data, optimizing parallel processing workflows, and validating models against diverse patient cohorts to ensure generalizability. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce model training times by an order of magnitude while achieving sub-millimeter precision in lesion localization. Outcomes will include open-source software tools for scalable image processing and a validated framework for integrating AI-driven diagnostics into clinical workflows. The successful implementation of this work has the potential to accelerate the adoption of precision medicine by enabling real-time, high-accuracy analysis of complex biomedical data, directly supporting advancements in early disease detection and personalized treatment planning. This project aligns with the Biomedical Technology program’s emphasis on engineering-driven solutions for medical systems, bridging computational innovation with practical healthcare applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing personalized therapeutic interventions in occupational therapy. Occupational Therapist Assistants (OTAs) face challenges in efficiently designing patient-specific treatment plans due to the complex interplay of factors such as individual motor function, cognitive capacity, psychosocial context, and response variability to therapeutic activities. Traditional approaches rely heavily on manual assessment and iterative adjustments, which can delay progress and reduce intervention efficacy.
