To address this, we propose a computational framework that integrates clinical data, wearable sensor metrics, and patient-reported outcomes to model treatment pathways. The research will employ machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, to analyze multi-modal datasets spanning demographics, therapy session performance, and longitudinal recovery patterns. These models will predict optimal activity sequences, duration, and intensity adjustments to maximize functional gains while minimizing patient fatigue or disengagement. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (e.g., motion capture data, electronic health records) and training computationally intensive models with hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simulated patient trajectories. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that enables OTAs to rapidly prototype and validate treatment plans using evidence-based simulations. The project will also generate novel insights into motor learning patterns across diverse populations, advancing the precision of occupational therapy practices. By reducing trial-and-error in clinical workflows, this work aims to enhance patient adherence, accelerate skill acquisition, and improve resource allocation in rehabilitation settings. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other therapeutic domains within allied health professions, fostering interdisciplinary innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Russian linguistic and literary corpora, with a focus on diachronic and synchronic patterns in dialectal variation and literary style. Despite the growing digitization of Russian texts—spanning classical literature, Soviet-era publications, and contemporary digital media—existing tools for large-scale textual analysis remain underdeveloped for the specific morphological and syntactic complexities of Russian. Current methods, optimized for English or other languages, often fail to capture the nuances of Russian inflectional morphology, aspectual verb systems, and dialect-specific lexical shifts, limiting the scope of philological and literary research. This project will address these gaps by developing and deploying computationally intensive models tailored to Russian language data. Using a corpus of over 10 million words—including regional dialect archives, 19th-century novels, and modern social media texts—we will apply transformer-based neural networks (e.g., BERT architectures) fine-tuned for Russian to automate the identification of grammatical, lexical, and stylistic features. Parallelized processing will enable the comparison of linguistic patterns across temporal, geographic, and sociocultural dimensions, while clustering algorithms will map literary genre evolution and dialectal boundaries. HPC resources are critical for training these models, given the computational demands of tokenizing highly inflected forms, processing Cyrillic embeddings, and iterating hyperparameters for optimal performance. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access tools for Russian corpus linguistics, (2) quantitative insights into the relationship between sociohistorical events (e.g., Soviet language reforms) and literary style shifts, and (3) datasets annotating understudied Russian dialects. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to redefine methodologies in Slavic studies, enabling scalable analysis of textual phenomena previously constrained by manual approaches. The results will support interdisciplinary collaborations in digital humanities, computational linguistics, and regional studies, with applications in language preservation and educational resource development.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Russian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized surgical instrument design using biomechanical simulations and machine learning, addressing variability in patient-specific tissue responses that limit the efficacy of standard surgical tools. Current approaches to instrument selection rely on surgeon experience and population-level data, leading to suboptimal outcomes in complex cases involving atypical anatomy or pathological tissue properties. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate real-time intraoperative data with patient-specific biomechanics to recommend instrument parameters, such as grip geometry or force distribution, tailored to individual procedural contexts. The computational approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating tissue-instrument interactions with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to iteratively optimize designs under physiological constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling multidomain simulations across heterogeneous tissue types (e.g., fibrotic vs. healthy liver parenchyma) and processing high-resolution intraoperative imaging datasets. Parallelized FEA workflows will model nonlinear tissue deformation, while graph neural networks will map spatial stress distributions to instrument performance metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for adaptive surgical tool optimization and validated prototypes tested against ex vivo porcine models. This work bridges gaps in precision surgery and medical device innovation by enabling data-driven instrument customization, with potential to reduce operative times, tissue trauma, and revision rates in hepatobiliary and oncologic surgeries. The computational infrastructure developed will also provide a template for integrating real-time sensor data into procedural planning systems, advancing broader efforts in adaptive surgical robotics and AI-enhanced operative decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to innovate solutions and lead change within a healthcare organization. Includes instruction in innovation management, medical device development, evidence-based practice, systems thinking, information technology, healthcare policy and finance, organizational change, and leadership.

abstract: Pharmaceutical research increasingly relies on advanced computational methods to model drug-target interactions, predict pharmacokinetic properties, and optimize therapeutic compounds. However, pre-pharmacy students often lack exposure to cutting-edge computational tools that bridge foundational coursework with modern drug discovery pipelines. This project proposes the development of a research-driven educational framework utilizing high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural dynamics of understudied membrane transporters implicated in drug absorption and resistance. The central research problem focuses on understanding how conformational changes in P-glycoprotein (P-gp), a critical efflux transporter, influence multidrug resistance patterns across diverse patient populations. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will model P-gp’s structural flexibility in complex with chemotherapeutic agents and common adjuvant medications. The computational workflow integrates enhanced sampling techniques (metadynamics, replica exchange MD) with machine learning-assisted analysis of free energy landscapes to identify transport mechanisms and potential binding inhibitors. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations across multiple ligand-receptor systems while maintaining the temporal resolution required to capture nanosecond-scale conformational shifts. Expected outcomes include: (1) atomistic insights into polypharmacy interactions affecting P-gp activity, (2) predictive models of transporter-mediated drug resistance applicable to personalized medication management, and (3) open-access simulation datasets for integration into pre-pharmacy curricula. This dual research-educational initiative will advance computational pharmacology literacy among future pharmacy professionals while contributing quantitative data to ongoing efforts in rational drug design. The requested computing allocation will support 12 months of GPU-accelerated simulations through a cloud-based HPC platform, processing an estimated 250,000 core-hours across 15 distinct drug-transporter systems. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and modular case studies adaptable for undergraduate laboratory instruction in pharmaceutical sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in private security operations, addressing inefficiencies in traditional static deployment models. Current security service management relies heavily on historical data and manual risk assessments, leading to suboptimal personnel and technology deployment in rapidly evolving threat environments. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based simulations and reinforcement learning algorithms that model complex, real-world security scenarios. These simulations will integrate multi-source data streams, including geospatial threat patterns, client facility layouts, personnel skill sets, and real-time incident reports, to generate adaptive resource allocation strategies. Computational methods will focus on balancing competing priorities such as cost efficiency, response latency, and risk mitigation across heterogeneous client portfolios. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of predicting optimal security team compositions, patrol routes, and technology placements under variable threat conditions. The framework will be validated against historical security breach data from corporate campus environments and high-value asset transportation case studies. By bridging operations management principles with computational modeling in a security-specific context, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for proactive security resource optimization. Successful implementation could reduce operational costs by 15-25% in simulated environments while maintaining or improving protection levels, offering transformative potential for an industry increasingly challenged by cyber-physical threats and budget constraints. The project’s computational demands—particularly parallel processing for Monte Carlo simulations and neural network training on multi-terabyte security incident datasets—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve practical runtime performance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and supervise services providing private security protection for people and property and related investigative and consulting functions. Includes instruction in security and loss prevention services, private security and investigation techniques, security technologies, personnel management, business operations, marketing, applicable law and regulations, and client relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the neural and biomechanical underpinnings of speech motor control in individuals with acquired communication disorders, such as post-stroke aphasia and traumatic brain injury. A critical barrier in understanding these disorders lies in modeling the complex interactions between cortical activity, sensorimotor pathways, and articulatory dynamics, which generate high-dimensional datasets spanning neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), motion capture, and acoustic signals. Traditional computational tools lack the capacity to integrate these multimodal data streams at scale, limiting insights into individualized recovery patterns and precision therapy design. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework that combines dynamical systems modeling, machine learning, and large-scale simulations to map disrupted communication pathways. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of neuroimaging data to identify lesion-specific functional connectivity deficits, GPU-accelerated training of deep neural networks for real-time analysis of speech kinematics, and finite element simulations of vocal tract biomechanics under varying neuromotor constraints. By unifying these approaches, the project aims to establish predictive models linking neural reorganization to speech output variability, enabling hypothesis-driven testing of intervention strategies in silico. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for automated, high-resolution assessment of speech motor deficits and a computational pipeline to optimize neuromodulation protocols or prosthetic device parameters in patient-specific contexts. This work will directly inform clinical translation by bridging gaps between neurocomputational theory and rehabilitative practice, while advancing scalable methodologies for analyzing heterogeneous communication sciences data. The requested resources are essential to manage the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, computationally intensive simulations, and iterative model training, which exceed the capabilities of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: Developmental-behavioral disorders in children arise from complex interactions between genetic, neurobiological, and environmental factors, yet current diagnostic and intervention frameworks often lack precision due to heterogeneous data and limited integrative analysis. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to predict developmental-behavioral trajectories and optimize personalized intervention strategies. Leveraging multimodal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomic profiles, and longitudinal behavioral assessments—we aim to identify biomarkers and environmental modifiers associated with developmental delays, autism spectrum disorder, and family dysfunction. The scale and complexity of these datasets, which encompass millions of clinical variables and high-resolution neuroimaging data, necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources for efficient processing, integration, and analysis. We will employ ensemble machine learning methods to handle data heterogeneity, coupled with graph neural networks to model dynamic interactions between biological and psychosocial factors. Bayesian hierarchical models will further quantify uncertainty in predictive outcomes across diverse populations. Computational workflows will parallelize feature extraction from neuroimaging pipelines, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and natural language processing (NLP) of clinical notes. HPC infrastructure is critical to meet the memory and processing demands of these tasks, particularly for training deep learning architectures on clustered GPUs and conducting large-scale simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for early risk stratification, a computational framework for evaluating intervention efficacy, and open-source tools to assist clinicians in personalizing care plans. By integrating multidimensional data at unprecedented scale, this work will advance translational research in developmental-behavioral pediatrics, offering new pathways to mitigate disparities in diagnostic access and improve long-term developmental outcomes for children and families.
cip_definition: Research on how to assist in the prevention, diagnosis, and management of developmental difficulties and problematic behaviors in children, and in the family dysfunctions that compromise children's development; and to foster understanding and promotion of optimal development of children and families through research, education, clinical care, and advocacy efforts.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze dynamic, large-scale economic systems characterized by heterogeneous agents, nonlinear interactions, and evolving network structures. Traditional econometric methods struggle to capture the emergent behaviors and equilibrium dynamics in such systems, particularly when scaling to real-world data sizes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized agent-based models (ABMs) and Bayesian estimation techniques for high-dimensional parameter spaces. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) simulating decentralized market equilibria under asymmetric information and strategic learning, and (2) estimating spillover effects in production networks using granular firm-level data covering 10 million+ economic entities. Computational challenges include solving systems of stochastic differential equations with adaptive time-stepping, maintaining consistency across distributed-memory simulations, and optimizing Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers for hierarchical Bayesian models. The HPC architecture will enable efficient scaling through MPI-based parallelism for ABMs and GPU-accelerated tensor operations for gradient-based inference. Expected outcomes include new insights into resilience thresholds for supply chain disruptions, empirically grounded policy scenarios for mitigating systemic risk, and open-source computational tools for economic complexity analysis. This work addresses critical gaps in modeling modern, interconnected economies while advancing methodological capacity for data-intensive economic research. The requested resources will support sustained GPU-node allocations for neural network surrogate modeling, large-memory nodes for network analysis, and high-throughput computing capabilities for Monte Carlo sensitivity testing. Results will contribute to both theoretical economics and applied policy analysis, with particular relevance to understanding cascading failures in financial and industrial ecosystems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in economics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The genetic architecture underlying complex phenotypic traits often involves intricate interactions between regulatory elements, epigenetic modifications, and non-coding genomic regions. However, resolving these interactions at scale remains challenging due to limitations in computational frameworks capable of integrating multi-omics data while accounting for population-level variation. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to analyze the combinatorial effects of regulatory variants, chromatin accessibility, and three-dimensional genome organization on gene expression dynamics. Leveraging whole-genome sequencing, ATAC-seq, and Hi-C data from a diverse cohort of 5,000 individuals, we will employ graph-based algorithms to model spatial interactions between enhancers, promoters, and structural chromatin domains. Parallelized Bayesian inference methods will quantify how allelic heterogeneity in non-coding regions influences transcriptional networks across cell types. A second aim focuses on simulating evolutionary trajectories of regulatory landscapes using forward-time population genetics models optimized for GPU acceleration. These simulations will test hypotheses about selection pressures shaping cis-regulatory architectures in humans compared to non-human primates. The computational workflow will utilize containerized environments for reproducibility and integrate with existing genomic databases through federated querying. By enabling simultaneous analysis of regulatory variant effects, chromatin topology, and evolutionary conservation patterns, this resource-intensive approach will provide novel insights into the hierarchical organization of gene regulation. Anticipated outcomes include identifying functionally coordinated regulatory hubs associated with developmental disorders and establishing predictive models for pleiotropic effects of non-coding variants. The developed tools will be disseminated as open-source packages, enhancing community capacity to interrogate multidimensional genomic datasets. This work directly advances foundational genetics research by bridging mechanistic studies of gene regulation with population-scale genomic analyses.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the organization, recombination, function, regulation, and transmission of heritable information in biological organisms at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in Mendelian genetics, mechanisms of gene regulation, chromosome structure and replication, epigenetic phenomena, DNA repair and recombination, sex determination, genetic interactions between genomes, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of lithospheric dynamics and crustal deformation processes through high-resolution 3D numerical modeling, with a focus on regions experiencing complex tectonic interactions. The research addresses critical gaps in predicting strain localization and fault network evolution during continental rifting and intraplate deformation, challenges that stem from the nonlinear interplay of thermomechanical rock properties, fluid-rock interactions, and inherited structural heterogeneity. Current models often oversimplify these multiscale processes, limiting their ability to reconcile geodetic observations with long-term geologic records. To bridge this gap, we propose a coupled finite element approach integrating visco-elasto-plastic rheologies, fracture propagation algorithms, and stochastic representations of basement structures. The models will assimilate field-derived fault maps, seismic velocity profiles, and stress orientation datasets from target regions in active rift systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve meter- to kilometer-scale deformation features across domain sizes exceeding 500 km, requiring iterative parallel simulations with adaptive mesh refinement. Each simulation will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for efficient computation of coupled thermal-mechanical-fluid flow equations across 10⁶–10⁷ degrees of freedom. Anticipated outcomes include a quantitative framework linking short-term geodetic signals to million-year tectonic evolution, with direct applications to seismic hazard assessment in extensional terranes. The computational infrastructure will enable probabilistic analysis of fault interaction scenarios, providing uncertainty-constrained forecasts of strain partitioning. By advancing the spatiotemporal resolution of geodynamic models, this work will refine predictions of crustal stress evolution during resource extraction and inform paleoseismic interpretations in complex fault zones. The requested allocation of 750,000 node-hours on HPC clusters will support parameter space exploration across 50+ model configurations, with data products made publicly available through community repositories to catalyze cross-disciplinary research in structural geology and seismology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and relationships between the solids, liquids and gases comprising it.

abstract: The integration of alternative and complementary medicine (ACM) modalities with conventional biomedical frameworks remains a significant challenge due to the complex, multi-target nature of interventions such as herbal formulations and mind-body therapies. This project seeks to address the lack of mechanistic understanding of synergistic interactions in multi-herb botanical formulations using computational approaches. Specifically, we aim to model the polypharmacological effects of traditional herbal combinations on inflammatory pathways, which are implicated in chronic conditions like arthritis and neurodegenerative diseases. The research problem centers on the inability of traditional reductionist methods to capture the dynamic, systems-level behavior of these formulations, which involve hundreds of bioactive compounds acting on multiple molecular targets. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven strategy combining molecular dynamics simulations, network pharmacology, and machine learning to map compound-target-pathway relationships. The computational workflow will integrate phytochemical databases with human proteome data to construct interaction networks, followed by multi-scale simulations of key protein-ligand complexes under varying stoichiometric conditions reflective of herbal combination ratios. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical synergistic nodes in inflammation-related pathways, (2) predictive models for optimizing herbal formulation efficacy, and (3) a computational framework adaptable to other ACM modalities such as acupuncture meridian systems. The HPC resources are essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-herb systems, requiring simultaneous simulation of >50,000 compound-target pairs and tera-scale data analysis. Results will provide unprecedented insights into the systems pharmacology of traditional medicine, bridging ACM practices with molecular biomedicine. This work aligns with growing interest in evidence-based integration of alternative therapies while addressing computational challenges unique to multi-target, whole-system interventions.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of biomechanical forces in tumor progression and metastasis using multiscale computational modeling, with a focus on integrating tissue-level mechanical stress dynamics with cancer cell signaling pathways. While genetic and molecular drivers of cancer are well-studied, the contribution of physiological forces—such as interstitial fluid pressure, shear stress, and extracellular matrix stiffness—to tumor aggressiveness and treatment resistance remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for organ-scale mechanical stress modeling with agent-based cellular simulations of tumor cell migration and proliferation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, particularly in simulating dynamic feedback between tissue deformation, hypoxia-driven angiogenesis, and metastatic potential across clinically relevant timescales (weeks to months). The model will incorporate experimental data from collaborator labs, including tissue-specific mechanical properties from murine mammary carcinoma models and single-cell RNA sequencing profiles of mechanosensitive pathways. Expected outcomes include identifying mechanical biomarkers predictive of metastatic risk and optimizing simulated therapeutic interventions targeting tumor microenvironments. This work will advance integrative pathobiology by bridging physiological mechanics with cancer biology, offering a platform to test hypotheses about mechanotransduction in disease progression. By leveraging HPC capabilities, we aim to generate predictive models that inform personalized treatment strategies for solid tumors, ultimately reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in oncology. The computational pipeline developed here will be shared openly to support interdisciplinary research at the intersection of physiology and cancer systems biology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanisms underlying human disease. Includes instruction in the causes and nature of disease processes in animals and humans at the molecular, cellular, tissue, organ and organ systems level, tissue structure and function, cellular mechanisms of disease and organ systems response to disease.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling and intervention analysis in forensic social work, addressing systemic gaps in evaluating outcomes for justice-involved individuals with co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders. Current approaches to risk assessment and program evaluation rely on fragmented datasets and static statistical models, limiting their ability to account for dynamic social, behavioral, and institutional factors. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data sources—including criminal justice records, clinical histories, and community service utilization patterns—to develop computational models that better predict recidivism, treatment adherence, and long-term stabilization. The proposed work combines machine learning techniques with agent-based modeling to simulate individual and systemic interactions across legal, healthcare, and social service domains. Computational workflows will process de-identified datasets from partner agencies, employing natural language processing to analyze unstructured case notes and temporal network analysis to map service access barriers. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble models on multi-modal data while preserving privacy through distributed computation frameworks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for forensic social workers to optimize case planning through dynamic risk stratification and resource allocation scenarios. The project also aims to identify policy-relevant thresholds for intervention efficacy in diversion programs and trauma-informed care pathways. By enabling large-scale analysis of cross-system interactions, this work addresses urgent needs in forensic social work practice, offering data-driven strategies to reduce cyclical incarceration and improve health equity for marginalized populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as social workers in correctional facilities, mental health hospitals, the justice system, substance abuse treatment programs, and victim assistance. Includes instruction in forensic social work, criminal justice administration, domestic violence, ethics, juvenile justice systems, mental illness and crime, program evaluation, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance geography teacher education by developing computational tools to model and simulate dynamic geographic processes for use in classroom instruction. A critical challenge in geography education is the limited accessibility of scalable, interactive resources that allow pre-service teachers to engage with real-world spatial data and complex systems (e.g., climate change, urbanization, or hydrological cycles) in pedagogically meaningful ways. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to generate and analyze large-scale geospatial datasets, create agent-based models of geographic phenomena, and design immersive virtual environments for teaching practice. The computational workflow will integrate geospatial machine learning techniques to process satellite imagery, demographic data, and environmental sensor outputs, transforming them into customizable teaching modules. These modules will simulate region-specific scenarios, enabling educators to tailor content to diverse student contexts. HPC resources are essential due to the computational intensity of processing high-resolution spatial data, running parallelized simulations of interacting geographic variables, and rendering 3D visualizations for classroom use. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of adaptable geographic simulation tools, coupled with evidence-based frameworks for integrating computational modeling into teacher training curricula. This work will directly support geography educators in fostering spatial reasoning and systems thinking skills among K-12 students, while advancing research on technology-enhanced pedagogies in geography education. The project’s computational outputs will be validated through partnerships with teacher preparation programs, ensuring alignment with classroom needs and educational standards. By bridging geospatial computation and teacher education, this initiative aims to democratize access to advanced geographic analysis tools, ultimately improving the quality of geography instruction across diverse learning environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational modeling of neurochemical interactions underlying the behavioral effects of psychoactive compounds. A key challenge in psychopharmacology is disentangling how dynamic drug-receptor interactions, neural circuit modulation, and individual variability collectively drive behavioral outcomes. Traditional experimental methods often struggle to capture the multiscale, nonlinear relationships between molecular mechanisms and organism-level responses. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of ligand-receptor binding, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, and spiking neural network models of cortico-striatal circuits. The MD component will simulate high-resolution interactions between neurotransmitters (e.g., dopamine, serotonin) and receptors under varying drug occupancy conditions, while neural network models will map these perturbations to behavioral phenotypes such as reward processing or cognitive flexibility. The project will utilize existing behavioral datasets from rodent studies of antidepressants, antipsychotics, and stimulants to parameterize and validate models. HPC resources are critical for scaling MD simulations across thousands of ligand-receptor configurations, optimizing neural network topologies via evolutionary algorithms, and conducting sensitivity analyses to identify critical neuropharmacological thresholds. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for estimating dose-response relationships and behavioral side effect profiles of novel compounds, reducing reliance on iterative in vivo testing. The models will also generate testable hypotheses about understudied mechanisms, such as allosteric modulation effects on decision-making circuits. By making computational workflows openly accessible, this work aims to establish a community resource for hypothesis-driven psychopharmacology research, bridging molecular neurochemistry and behavioral neuroscience through scalable computational methods.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the behavioral effects of medications, drugs, nutrients, and chemicals (including natural and artificial toxins) in laboratory and clinical settings. Includes instruction in pharmacology, behavioral toxicology and pharmacology, neuroscience, physiology, clinical psychopharmacology, substance abuse treatments and antidotes, neurochemical mechanisms, epidemiology of chemicals and substances, biochemical interactions, and psychoactive drugs.

abstract: Securing critical infrastructure against emerging threats requires advanced predictive models capable of analyzing complex, multi-scale interactions between physical and cyber systems. Current approaches often rely on simplified simulations or static risk assessments, which fail to capture dynamic adversarial behaviors, cascading failures, or real-time interdependencies in modern infrastructure networks. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to model threat propagation across interconnected energy, transportation, and communication systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based simulations integrating stochastic adversarial decision-making algorithms, physics-informed neural networks for infrastructure component degradation modeling, and graph-theoretic analyses of cascading impacts. The computational workflow will employ hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization to scale simulations across millions of agent interactions while maintaining sub-second resolution for cyber-physical event tracking. Key challenges include optimizing memory usage for heterogeneous data structures representing both discrete cyber events and continuous physical processes, as well as validating models against real-world incident datasets through Bayesian calibration techniques. Expected outcomes include a novel risk quantification metric that dynamically weights threat likelihood against consequence severity across infrastructure sectors, validated through comparative analysis with historical attack patterns. The resulting framework will provide decision-support capabilities for infrastructure operators and security agencies, enabling proactive vulnerability mitigation and resource allocation. By advancing computational methods for security science, this work aims to establish new standards for infrastructure resilience modeling while demonstrating how HPC-enabled complex systems analysis can transform threat anticipation in homeland security applications.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing biomechanical interventions for chronic foot disorders, specifically focusing on diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) recurrence and progressive plantar fascia degradation. Despite advances in podiatric care, mechanistic insights into tissue stress distribution during gait and its relationship to microtrauma remain poorly quantified, limiting personalized treatment strategies. To bridge this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating patient-specific imaging, wearable sensor data, and biomechanical modeling to simulate dynamic foot-loading patterns under varying orthotic and surgical interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-resolution 3D reconstructions of foot anatomy from MRI/CT datasets, perform finite element analysis (FEA) of tissue strain distributions at micron-scale resolution, and train machine learning models predicting optimal intervention parameters. The workflow involves three phases: (1) automated segmentation of clinical imaging data to generate anatomically accurate computational meshes; (2) GPU-accelerated FEA simulations incorporating viscoelastic tissue properties and nonlinear contact mechanics during gait cycles; (3) reinforcement learning optimization of orthotic geometries and surgical correction angles using output from 10^5+ simulated loading scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for identifying high-risk DFU recurrence profiles and a generative AI tool for designing patient-specific orthotics. By correlating simulation results with longitudinal clinical outcomes from 200+ enrolled patients, this work will establish computational biomarkers for early intervention in podiatric care. The resource-intensive nature of modeling transient tissue responses at clinical cohort scales necessitates access to parallelized computing architectures with large memory nodes and high-throughput GPU clusters. Successful implementation could redefine standards for precision podiatry, reducing preventable amputations and healthcare costs associated with chronic foot morbidity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of podiatric medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and injuries to the foot and lower extremities. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, anatomy of the lower extremity, functional orthopedics, foot biomechanics, podiatric radiology, dermatology, podiatric surgery, podopediatrics, sports medicine, physical diagnosis, emergency medicine and traumatology, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of personalized dietary intervention optimization by investigating the complex interplay between host metabolism, gut microbiota dynamics, and nutritional inputs. Current clinical nutrition frameworks often rely on population-level recommendations, which fail to account for individual variations in microbial community structure, metabolic pathways, and nutrient processing efficiency. We propose to develop a computational platform integrating multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and proteomic profiles) with physiological parameters to model personalized nutrient-microbiome-host interactions. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify predictive biomarkers of dietary response variability and agent-based modeling to simulate microbial community shifts under different nutritional regimes. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (>10 TB of multi-omics data from clinical cohorts), training deep neural networks to recognize nonlinear relationships between dietary components and metabolic outcomes, and running parallelized simulations of gut ecosystem dynamics across diverse virtual patient profiles. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-source predictive tool for optimizing clinical nutrition strategies in metabolic disorders, identification of microbial taxa associated with differential nutrient absorption efficiency, and novel insights into temporal patterns of microbiome-mediated food compound transformation. This work bridges computational biology, systems nutrition, and clinical dietetics, offering a transformative approach to precision nutrition that could inform therapeutic dietary interventions for conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and micronutrient deficiency syndromes. The computational framework developed will enable real-time adjustment of dietary recommendations based on individual microbial and metabolic signatures, advancing the field beyond current one-size-fits-all paradigms in clinical nutrition practice.
cip_title: Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dietetics and clinical nutrition services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of customer service operations in multichannel environments necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize resource allocation, predict service demand, and enhance customer satisfaction. This project seeks to address the challenge of dynamically managing customer service resources—such as agent scheduling, real-time query routing, and sentiment-driven prioritization—in large-scale, data-rich call centers and digital support platforms. Traditional heuristic methods often fail to adapt to rapidly changing customer behavior patterns, leading to inefficiencies in service delivery and elevated operational costs. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning-driven framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze historical interaction data, real-time customer sentiment, and operational performance metrics. The computational approach will integrate agent-based modeling to simulate service workflows, reinforcement learning to optimize decision-making under uncertainty, and natural language processing (NLP) to classify and prioritize customer inquiries from text and voice data. Large-scale datasets from partner organizations—including call logs, chat transcripts, customer surveys, and CRM records—will be processed to train and validate models. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high dimensionality of interaction data (spanning millions of records) and enabling parallelized hyperparameter tuning for time-sensitive predictive tasks. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system capable of recommending real-time adjustments to staffing levels, channel-specific resource distribution, and personalized response strategies. This research will contribute novel methodologies to the field of customer service management by bridging gaps between operational theory, computational scalability, and practical implementation. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and open-source toolkits to support evidence-based management practices in service-oriented organizations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and monitor customer service performance and manage frontline customer support services, call centers/help desks, and customer relations. Includes instruction in customer behavior, specialized information technology and systems management, developing and using customer service databases, user surveys and other feedback mechanisms, strategic and performance planning and analysis, operations management, personnel supervision, and communications and marketing skills.

abstract: The development of novel pharmaceutical compounds faces persistent challenges in efficiency, cost, and predictive accuracy, particularly when balancing therapeutic efficacy, manufacturability, and safety. Traditional approaches to drug synthesis, pharmacokinetic profiling, and quality control remain resource-intensive, with high attrition rates during clinical and industrial phases. This project proposes an integrated computational framework to address these bottlenecks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) for multi-scale modeling and machine learning. We aim to optimize drug candidate selection and production workflows through three synergistic objectives: (1) simulating protein-ligand interactions and binding dynamics for lead compounds using molecular dynamics (MD) with enhanced sampling techniques, (2) training graph neural networks on structural and bioactivity data to predict ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) properties, and (3) deploying discrete event simulation models to streamline biomanufacturing processes under quality-by-design (QbD) constraints. The MD simulations will employ GPU-accelerated workflows to resolve time-dependent conformational changes in target proteins, while federated learning architectures will aggregate data from distributed pharmaceutical partners to improve model generalizability without compromising proprietary data. Industrial application components will focus on optimizing bioreactor parameters and purification steps to minimize batch variability. Anticipated outcomes include a validated pipeline for prioritizing synthesis targets with >50% reduced computational cost compared to existing virtual screening methods, predictive models for early-stage toxicity flags (targeting 85% accuracy), and dynamic production protocols that adapt to raw material variability. By unifying computational drug discovery with scalable process analytics, this work seeks to demonstrate a translatable paradigm for accelerating therapeutic development while maintaining regulatory compliance. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the terabyte-scale simulation outputs, parallelized ML training across heterogeneous datasets, and real-time optimization of multivariate production models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific application of pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and industrial management to the development, production, marketing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Includes instruction in industrial microbiology, plasmids, expression vectors, protein chemistry, assay and evaluation, drug synthesis and purification, quality control, industrial management, production security, patent procedures, intellectual property regulations and issues, patent enforcement and defense, and research design and testing.

abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical laboratory data, including high-dimensional omics, digital pathology imaging, and real-time diagnostic instrument outputs, presents a critical challenge in translating raw data into actionable insights for precision medicine. Current analytical pipelines lack the scalability to integrate heterogeneous datasets while maintaining the speed required for clinical decision-making. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multi-modal data integration and predictive modeling in Laboratory Medicine. We propose to leverage GPU-accelerated machine learning to analyze large-scale genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets alongside whole-slide pathology images and longitudinal electronic health record data. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, employing containerized environments to ensure reproducibility across research and clinical infrastructure. Key methodological innovations include the implementation of graph neural networks to model biomarker interactions across biological scales and federated learning architectures to enable multi-institutional collaboration while preserving data privacy. The proposed resource allocation will support the training of deep learning models on annotated datasets from 15,000+ retrospective cases of hematologic malignancies, with validation across three academic medical centers. Anticipated outcomes include (1) novel algorithms for early detection of treatment-resistant disease subtypes, (2) a validated computational pipeline for automated quality control in high-throughput diagnostic systems, and (3) open-source tools for real-time data harmonization across laboratory instruments. By overcoming current computational bottlenecks, this work will establish a paradigm for resource-efficient translational research in Laboratory Medicine, directly addressing the growing need for HPC-supported infrastructure in clinical biomarker discovery and diagnostic optimization. The developed framework will be disseminated through CLIA-certified laboratory partnerships, bridging the gap between research computing capabilities and clinical laboratory operations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied medical research and related techniques, equipment, data systems, and research design. Includes instruction in the management of medical laboratories in research and healthcare facilities.

abstract: The sustainable intensification of livestock production systems requires advanced tools to optimize animal health, feed efficiency, and environmental outcomes. Current models for predicting livestock productivity and emissions often lack resolution to account for complex interactions between genetics, microbiome dynamics, and nutrient utilization. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate metabolic networks in ruminants, evaluate disease resilience traits, and predict methane mitigation strategies. The research will integrate multi-omics data (genomic, metagenomic, metabolomic) with agent-based modeling to analyze host-microbiome interactions under varying dietary and management scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets, run iterative simulations of rumen microbial communities, and train machine learning models to identify biomarkers for feed efficiency. Key computational tasks include genome-scale metabolic reconstructions of microbial consortia, probabilistic risk modeling of zoonotic disease transmission in livestock populations, and 3D molecular dynamics simulations of enzyme interactions in feed substrates. The project will leverage parallelized workflows for parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses across diverse livestock genotypes and environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for precision feeding protocols, genetic selection indices for low-emission traits, and decision-support systems for disease outbreak mitigation. By bridging gaps between molecular-scale processes and herd-level outcomes, this work aims to advance data-driven livestock management strategies that align productivity gains with climate resilience. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable scaling to global livestock genomic datasets and real-time adaptive modeling, which are computationally prohibitive with existing institutional resources. Results will inform stakeholder frameworks for sustainable protein production and contribute open-source models to the agricultural sciences community.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of livestock animals and the production and handling of meat and other products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, range science, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: Pediatric pathologies, particularly those arising during fetal development and early childhood, present unique diagnostic challenges due to the dynamic interplay of growth processes and disease mechanisms. Current approaches to diagnosing rare or complex pediatric disorders often rely on fragmented analyses of histopathological, genomic, and clinical data, limiting the ability to uncover multifactorial etiologies. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omics datasets (including single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and proteomics) with high-resolution histopathology imaging to model disease pathways in developmental anomalies and childhood cancers. The primary computational challenge lies in processing and analyzing terabyte-scale datasets while resolving cellular-level interactions across heterogeneous modalities. To achieve this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled pipeline leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) to map spatial relationships between cell populations and machine learning classifiers to correlate molecular signatures with clinical outcomes. Custom algorithms will be developed to harmonize temporal data from longitudinal patient samples, accounting for developmental trajectories. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model pathogenic variants in growth-related proteins to assess their mechanistic roles. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of image analysis, reduce runtime for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) from weeks to days, and support the training of deep learning models on annotated whole-slide imaging repositories. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking cellular microenvironment features to disease progression in congenital anomalies, (2) identification of novel biomarkers for early detection of pediatric solid tumors, and (3) open-source computational tools for integrative pediatric pathology analysis. This work will enhance diagnostic precision in understudied childhood conditions and provide a framework for computationally driven discovery in developmental pathology. The requested resources are critical given the exponential growth of multi-omics datasets in our ongoing cohort studies and the infeasibility of local computing infrastructure for these analyses.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory diagnosis of diseases that occur during fetal growth, infancy, and child development, based on knowledge of general pathology, normal growth and development, and pediatric medicine.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in obstetrics and gynecology by addressing critical gaps in predicting and managing adverse maternal-fetal outcomes. The clinical complexity of conditions such as preeclampsia, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes arises from multifactorial interactions between genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, and environmental factors. Current predictive models lack the resolution to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale, limiting their utility in risk stratification and personalized intervention. To overcome this, we propose developing a unified computational framework that synthesizes multi-omics data (genome-wide association studies, methylation arrays, single-cell RNA sequencing) with real-world clinical data from electronic health records. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify predictive biomarkers and model dynamic risk trajectories across pregnancy. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of genomic data, optimizing hyperparameters in high-dimensional spaces, and running simulations to validate model robustness against demographic and clinical variability. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel biomarker panels for early detection of preeclampsia, a risk prediction tool deployable in clinical settings, and foundational insights into shared molecular pathways underlying disparate obstetric complications. By enabling large-scale integration of biological and clinical data, this work will accelerate translational discoveries, reduce health disparities through equitable risk modeling, and inform targeted therapeutic strategies. The requested computing infrastructure will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multi-institutional datasets, and parallelized pipeline execution to meet the computational demands of this initiative.
cip_definition: Research focused on Obstetrics and Gynecology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale digital humanities investigation into the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in Ukraine, with emphasis on underrepresented regional and gender perspectives. The research problem centers on analyzing vast, unstructured datasets—including digitized folklore archives, Soviet-era periodicals, post-independence media, and contemporary social media—to identify patterns in how cultural symbols, linguistic markers, and collective memory have been negotiated across Ukraine’s contested historical landscapes. Current methodologies in cultural studies lack scalable tools to systematically process multimodal Ukrainian-language materials spanning five centuries while accounting for dialectal diversity, shifting political terminologies, and erasures in archival records. Our computational approach integrates transformer-based language models fine-tuned on historical Ukrainian texts, geospatial network analysis of cultural production centers, and semi-supervised clustering algorithms to map discursive continuities and fractures across time, space, and sociocultural groups. The workflow requires parallelized processing of 12TB of text and image data, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for graph-based analyses of regional cultural networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of persistent subnational narrative frameworks in border regions like Slobozhanshchyna and Bukovyna; (2) quantitative models tracing the impact of 20th-century state policies on gendered representations in folk traditions; (3) an open-access annotated corpus of Ukrainian cultural discourse from 1600–2023. By enabling computationally intensive analysis at unprecedented temporal and geographical granularity, this project will provide new empirical foundations for understanding cultural resilience and adaptation in Ukraine while developing transferable pipelines for non-Anglocentric digital humanities research. The requested resources directly address the computational barriers that have historically constrained large-scope cultural studies in under-resourced linguistic contexts.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: The development of stable and efficacious pharmaceutical formulations requires precise understanding of molecular interactions between active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and excipients, yet empirical screening remains time- and resource-intensive. Challenges in predicting long-term stability, optimizing dissolution profiles, and mitigating phase separation in complex formulations hinder rapid product development. This project proposes a computational framework to model drug-excipient compatibility, stability under stress conditions, and microstructure evolution in solid dispersions and semi-solid cosmetic matrices. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to quantify API-excipient binding affinities, diffusion coefficients, and amorphous system thermodynamics, complemented by finite element analysis (FEA) of heat and mass transfer during manufacturing processes. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets to predict degradation kinetics and identify formulation "design rules." The scale of these simulations—particularly for multicomponent systems requiring >1 million atoms or mesoscale modeling of emulsion stability—exceeds the capacity of local computing resources. HPC access will enable parallelized parameter sweeps across temperature, humidity, and composition variables, as well as neural network training on high-dimensional data (e.g., spectral time-series, X-ray microtomography). Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for accelerated excipient selection, stability risk assessment, and optimization of topical drug delivery systems. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of formulation failures while reducing experimental costs by prioritizing high-risk candidates computationally. By integrating computational pharmaceutics with industrial practice, the project aims to streamline development pipelines for both conventional dosage forms and novel cosmeceutical products, directly addressing industry demands for agile, data-driven formulation strategies.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between tumor microenvironment remodeling and therapy resistance in solid malignancies, with a focus on pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Despite advances in oncology, PDAC remains intractable due to its complex stromal architecture, heterogeneous cell populations, and adaptive molecular pathways that collectively drive treatment failure. Current experimental models inadequately capture the spatiotemporal evolution of these interactions, limiting mechanistic insights. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multiscale agent-based modeling (ABM) with patient-derived histopathological and transcriptomic datasets. The ABM platform will simulate stromal-tumor crosstalk, incorporating biomechanical constraints, hypoxia-driven signaling, and chemotherapy-induced selection pressures. Cellular agents will encode phenotypic plasticity rules informed by single-cell RNA sequencing data from pre- and post-treatment biopsies. HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10^4 simulated tumor nodules (each comprising >10^6 interacting agents) to identify critical thresholds in extracellular matrix density, immune infiltration patterns, and metabolic adaptation trajectories that predict therapeutic vulnerability. Parallelized model fitting will utilize clinical imaging timelines and survival data through Bayesian optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive signatures of early therapy resistance detectable through radiomic correlates, novel combinatorial stromal modulation strategies, and a publicly accessible simulation engine for prioritizing organ-specific metastasis interventions. This systems pathology approach bridges tissue-scale pathophysiology with subcellular adaptation mechanisms, directly aligning with the program’s mission to decode disease progression through molecularly informed computational models. The requested resources are essential for handling memory-intensive 3D microenvironment reconstructions and achieving statistical power in simulating rare, high-impact cellular transitions central to PDAC lethality.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the expression, initiation, maintenance and progression of tissue injury and disease, including death, and the relationship of pathogenesis to fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms. Includes instruction in immunology, microbiology, gene expression, inflammation, cell injury, apoptosis, immunopathology, molecular markers of disease and toxins, neoplasia, growth regulation, and organ- and system-specific investigations.

abstract: The proposed research aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the diagnosis and treatment of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain by integrating multimodal data analysis and biomechanical modeling. Despite the high prevalence of TMD, clinical decision-making remains challenging due to the heterogeneous etiologies of pain and dysfunction, which span biomechanical, neurological, and psychosocial factors. Current diagnostic frameworks lack precision, and treatment outcomes for intraoral appliances (e.g., for sleep apnea or occlusal stabilization) vary widely. This project addresses these gaps by developing computational models to simulate temporomandibular joint (TMJ) biomechanics under diverse physiological and pathological conditions, correlate these dynamics with patient-specific clinical and imaging data, and identify biomarkers predictive of treatment response. High-resolution 3D imaging datasets (CBCT, MRI) and electromyographic recordings from a longitudinal cohort of 500 patients will be processed to construct finite element models of TMJ loading, soft tissue strain, and intraoral appliance interactions. Machine learning pipelines will integrate these biomechanical outputs with electronic health record data, including pain phenotypes, neurophysiological assessments, and treatment histories, to classify subtypes of TMD and orofacial pain. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of large imaging datasets, iterative optimization of biomechanical parameters, and training of deep neural networks for pattern recognition—tasks that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. Access to HPC resources will enable rapid simulation of complex TMJ dynamics, validation of model predictions against clinical outcomes, and development of open-source tools for personalized therapeutic planning. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework to stratify patients by underlying pathophysiology, optimize appliance design via virtual testing, and reduce trial-and-error in clinical management. This work bridges computational biomechanics and clinical practice, offering a scalable approach to improve precision in diagnosing and treating complex orofacial pain disorders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to evaluate, diagnose, and treat of a wide variety of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain disorders as well as the treatment of sleep apnea and snoring with intraoral appliances. Includes instruction in head and neck anatomy, physical diagnosis and evaluation, orofacial pain, neurobiology of pain and analgesia, and diagnostic radiography.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the complex interplay between cultural dietary practices, nutritional outcomes, and community health resilience in understudied populations. Traditional nutritional research often prioritizes universal dietary guidelines, yet fails to account for the dynamic role of culturally embedded food practices—such as seasonal rituals, heritage crop cultivation, or communal meal traditions—in shaping health trajectories. The computational challenges of modeling these multidimensional, context-dependent relationships, which integrate qualitative ethnographic data with longitudinal health metrics, remain underexplored. This project will develop a novel computational framework to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including community-sourced dietary narratives, agricultural biodiversity records, metabolomic profiles, and public health surveillance data from three distinct Indigenous foodways. Machine learning models will identify patterns linking cultural food practices to micronutrient adequacy and metabolic health markers, while agent-based simulations will evaluate how disruptions to traditional food systems (e.g., climate shifts, supply chain failures) propagate through community health networks. By employing GPU-accelerated natural language processing to interpret oral histories and HPC-enabled phylogenetic analysis of traditional crop varieties, the study bridges computational gastronomy, nutritional anthropology, and resilience theory. Expected outcomes include a scalable methodology for culturally grounded nutritional modeling, predictive insights into food system vulnerabilities, and actionable frameworks for designing community-specific nutritional interventions that honor cultural heritage. This work fills a critical gap in transdisciplinary nutrition research, offering computational tools to address health inequities while preserving biocultural diversity in food practices. The requested resources will enable the integration of terabyte-scale datasets, parallelized model training, and real-time sensitivity analyses, which are computationally prohibitive without advanced HPC infrastructure.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foods, nutrition, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project addresses critical challenges in optimizing the design and operational efficiency of advanced electromechanical systems, which integrate complex mechanical, electrical, and thermal interactions. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the nonlinear dynamics and multi-physics coupling inherent in these systems, leading to suboptimal performance, reduced reliability, and increased energy consumption. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a high-fidelity computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven optimization. The study focuses on hybrid electromechanical actuators for renewable energy applications, where variable loads and harsh environmental conditions exacerbate system inefficiencies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-scale phenomena, including electromagnetic field interactions, heat dissipation in compact geometries, and fatigue analysis under cyclic loading. Parallelized simulations will enable parametric studies across thousands of design configurations, while neural networks trained on HPC-generated datasets will identify optimal material compositions and control strategies. Key outcomes include predictive models for lifetime estimation, actuator designs with 15–20% improved energy density, and an open-source toolkit for coupled electromechanical simulation. These advancements will directly support the development of robust, sustainable energy systems and smart manufacturing infrastructure. The requested computing resources are indispensable for handling memory-intensive simulations and iterative optimization loops, which exceed the capacity of local workstations. By bridging gaps in multi-physics modeling and data-driven design, this work aims to establish new methodologies for electromechanical innovation, with applications in wind turbine pitch control, electric vehicle drivetrains, and industrial automation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electromechanical technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical pharmacogenomics aims to optimize drug therapy by leveraging genetic variability, yet challenges persist in predicting individual drug response due to the polygenic nature of traits, epistatic interactions, and environmental influences. Current models often fail to account for the complexity of multi-omic datasets, limiting their clinical utility. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic profiles, and electronic health record data to predict drug efficacy and adverse events in diverse patient populations. The research will employ machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to model gene-drug interactions while addressing population stratification and confounding variables. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of genomic data, performing genome-wide association studies (GWAS) at scale, and training deep learning models with millions of parameters. Key computational steps include parallelized variant annotation, haplotype phasing, and polygenic risk score optimization across heterogeneous cohorts. Molecular dynamics simulations will supplement these analyses to characterize functional impacts of prioritized genetic variants on protein-drug binding affinities. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for warfarin dosing, clopidogrel response, and statin-induced myopathy, with generalizable methods for other therapeutics. The project will produce open-source tools for real-time pharmacogenomic decision support, enabling clinicians to integrate genetic data into prescribing workflows. By elucidating novel gene-drug associations and refining dose prediction algorithms, this work aims to reduce adverse drug reactions, improve therapeutic outcomes, and advance the implementation of precision medicine in routine care. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable the analysis of datasets spanning 50,000+ individuals, ensuring statistical power to detect rare variant effects and accelerate translation of findings into clinical guidelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Pharmacogenomics

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and dynamic determinants of enzyme catalytic efficiency in metalloenzymes using advanced computational simulations. Despite extensive biochemical characterization of metalloenzymes such as zinc-dependent hydrolases and iron-containing oxidoreductases, the atomic-level mechanisms by which metal cofactors modulate reaction energetics and transition state stabilization remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental techniques struggle to capture transient intermediates and metal-ligand coordination dynamics on biologically relevant timescales. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations, molecular dynamics (MD) sampling, and free energy calculations to model catalytic cycles in two model systems: a hydrolytic enzyme implicated in neurotransmitter regulation and a redox-active enzyme involved in cellular detoxification pathways. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable iterative QM/MM optimizations of active-site geometries, microsecond-scale MD trajectories to sample conformational ensembles, and umbrella sampling calculations to reconstruct free energy landscapes for rate-limiting steps. These simulations will integrate experimentally derived constraints from X-ray crystallography and kinetic isotope effect measurements. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of metal coordination geometries that lower activation barriers for substrate transformation, (2) characterization of protein motions that facilitate proton transfer and intermediate stabilization, and (3) predictive models linking metal ion speciation to catalytic turnover rates. The computational demands of this work—particularly the need to simulate multi-nanosecond trajectories for 200,000-atom solvated systems with hybrid QM/MM potentials—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory processors. Results will advance fundamental understanding of metalloenzyme catalysis while providing mechanistic insights applicable to the design of metal-targeted inhibitors and biomimetic catalysts. This work aligns with the biochemistry program's emphasis on enzymology and bioanalytical chemistry by bridging molecular-level simulations with experimentally testable hypotheses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemistry of living systems, their fundamental chemical substances and reactions, and their chemical pathways and information transfer systems, with particular reference to carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.
