Includes instruction in bio-organic chemistry, protein chemistry, bioanalytical chemistry, bioseparations, regulatory biochemistry, enzymology, hormonal chemistry, calorimetry, and research methods and equipment operation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges of optimizing integrated electromechanical systems for advanced manufacturing applications, where dynamic interactions between mechanical, thermal, and electrical components often lead to inefficiencies and reliability issues. Current design approaches struggle to predict system-level behavior under real-world operating conditions, particularly when accounting for multi-physics couplings, transient thermal loads, and nonlinear control responses. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate electromechanical systems at unprecedented fidelity. The research will employ coupled finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and thermal dynamics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cooling systems, and circuit simulation tools to capture embedded electronics behavior. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to optimize control algorithms for automated processes, targeting energy efficiency and operational stability. Key computational challenges include resolving microsecond-scale electrical transients alongside minute-long thermal cycles in hybrid manufacturing environments, necessitating parallelized solvers and adaptive meshing strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive models for electromechanical component degradation, validated control strategies for precision automation, and a digital twin framework for rapid system prototyping. This work will directly support the development of next-generation smart manufacturing systems with improved energy efficiency, reduced maintenance costs, and enhanced adaptability to complex production demands. The requested HPC resources are critical to handle the computational intensity of multi-scale, multi-physics simulations, enabling parameter sweeps across mechanical, thermal, and electrical domains that would otherwise be infeasible on local computing infrastructure. Successful implementation will provide methodological advances for electromechanical integration challenges while offering open-source simulation tools to the broader engineering community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the problems associated with combining electrical and mechanical components with special emphasis on manufacturing and automated processes. Includes instruction in applied mechanics, instrumentation and monitoring, machine design, automated control techniques, fluid and thermal dynamics, circuit analysis, and solid state electronics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Arabic linguistic and literary corpora. Arabic’s rich morphological complexity, dialectal diversity, and the historical breadth of its textual traditions present unique obstacles to large-scale analysis. Existing computational tools often inadequately handle Classical Arabic’s inflectional systems or fail to account for regional dialect variations, limiting the scalability of research on language evolution, stylistic patterns, and sociolinguistic dynamics. This project proposes the development and deployment of advanced natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to Arabic’s linguistic features, enabling the systematic study of multi-genre corpora spanning pre-Islamic poetry, medieval philosophical texts, Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) media, and contemporary dialectal speech. Computational methods will include the training of transformer-based models for dialect identification, graph-based algorithms for morphological parsing, and neural architectures for cross-period semantic shift detection. These workflows require HPC capabilities to process terabytes of text data, optimize deep learning models, and run parallelized analyses across heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible annotated corpus of Classical and MSA texts with dialectal annotations, (2) quantitative insights into syntactic and lexical changes between historical and modern Arabic registers, and (3) open-source tools for dialect-aware machine translation. By enabling unprecedented scale and precision in Arabic linguistic research, this project aims to advance scholarly understanding of the language’s development while supporting practical applications in language education, digital humanities, and region-specific NLP technologies. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive processing demands and reduce training times for complex models, which are infeasible with standard academic infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Arabic language. Includes instruction in philology; Classical Arabic; Modern Standard Arabic; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling of dynamic consumer decision-making under economic uncertainty, with a focus on heterogeneous household behaviors in response to fluctuating commodity prices and service accessibility. Traditional consumer economics models often rely on aggregate data or simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to capture granular, real-world complexities such as intertemporal trade-offs, spatial disparities in resource access, and the interaction of behavioral biases with market shocks. The research addresses this gap by developing a microsimulation framework that integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with high-dimensional econometric estimation, enabling the analysis of individualized consumption patterns across diverse demographic and geographic strata. Computational challenges include scaling Bayesian hierarchical models to process terabytes of transactional, geospatial, and survey data while maintaining probabilistic rigor in parameter estimation. The HPC environment will facilitate parallelized Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty quantification, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning surrogates to approximate costly utility maximization routines, and large-scale sensitivity analyses across synthetic populations. Expected outcomes include novel insights into the resilience of low-income households to energy price volatility, the distributional impacts of subscription-based service economies, and empirically grounded policy scenarios for mitigating consumption inequality. By bridging computational scalability gaps in consumer economics, this work aims to establish a replicable infrastructure for next-generation behavioral microsimulation, with applications to regulatory testing, targeted welfare program design, and private-sector demand forecasting. The requested resources will specifically support the deployment of containerized model pipelines across clustered nodes, memory-intensive dataset merging, and runtime optimizations for ABM ensembles simulating 10^6+ agent households over multi-year horizons.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of micro- and macro-economic theory to consumer behavior and individual and family consumption of goods and services. Includes instruction in modeling, economic forecasting, indexing, price theory, and analysis of individual commodities and services and/or groups of related commodities and services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, safety, and maintenance of recreational vehicles (RVs) by addressing gaps in current industry practices, which rely heavily on physical prototyping and reactive repair strategies. As RVs integrate increasingly complex systems—such as hybrid electrical-propane power systems, adaptive towing dynamics, and lightweight composite structures—traditional methods struggle to efficiently predict performance, failure modes, or long-term durability. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-physics simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model interactions between mechanical, thermal, electrical, and fluid systems in RV operation. Key focuses include stress analysis of welded chassis frames under dynamic loads, thermal-fluid simulations of propane appliance efficiency in extreme climates, and predictive machine learning models for diagnosing electrical system faults. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and time-series anomaly detection algorithms trained on synthetic and experimental datasets. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to generate high-resolution insights into system interdependencies, enabling proactive design improvements and failure prevention protocols. Expected outcomes include validated digital twins of critical RV subsystems, optimized maintenance schedules informed by predictive analytics, and open-source simulation templates for educational use in RV technician training programs. This work will provide the RV industry with scalable tools to reduce development costs, enhance safety standards, and accelerate the adoption of sustainable technologies, while equipping technicians with data-driven diagnostic skills. The requested computing resources will directly support the generation of large-scale simulation datasets, enabling iterative model refinement and real-world validation through partnerships with RV manufacturers and service centers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to build, test, inspect, repair, service and maintain recreational vehicles, systems, and interior and exterior components. Includes instruction in brake, hydraulic, and towing systems; electrical systems; propane systems and propane and electric appliances; carpentry; plumbing; welding; and structural frames.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize diagnostic accuracy in clinical laboratory workflows by addressing pre-analytical variability—a critical yet understudied factor contributing to diagnostic errors. While clinical laboratory assistants (CLAs) perform standardized procedures for specimen collection, handling, and preparation, subtle variations in technique, environmental conditions, or equipment interactions may introduce biases that propagate through downstream analyses. Current quality assurance protocols lack granular, data-driven tools to identify and mitigate these pre-analytical confounders. We propose a computational framework integrating high-resolution sensor data from laboratory equipment, environmental monitors, and wearable devices with machine learning to model how CLA workflows influence specimen integrity. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process multimodal datasets (e.g., pneumatic tube system vibration profiles, centrifuge temperature fluctuations, phlebotomy grip pressure patterns) to identify latent correlations between procedural microvariations and analyte stability. Agent-based modeling will simulate how individual operator behaviors interact with laboratory systems under diverse operational constraints. The computational pipeline will employ neural networks trained on synthetic datasets generated via physics-informed digital twins of laboratory devices, validated against experimental measurements of hemolysis rates, platelet clumping, and other pre-analytical artifacts in blood samples. Outcomes will include predictive models to flag high-risk workflow deviations in real time and adaptive training modules for CLAs, tailored to individual learning patterns. This work bridges human factors engineering, laboratory medicine, and computational analytics to advance precision in pre-analytical processes—a niche with direct implications for diagnostic reliability but limited prior integration of HPC-driven approaches. By mapping the "hidden variables" of laboratory workflows, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for error reduction in specimen-dependent diagnostics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians or laboratory scientists or technologists, to perform waived testing procedures (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988), phlebotomy, and other duties in support of laboratory teams. Includes instruction in clinical procedures, various laboratory tests, laboratory mathematics, computer technology, equipment operation and maintenance, sterilization and safety, communications skills, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze syntactic and morphological evolution in German dialects from the Early Modern period to the present, addressing gaps in large-scale comparative studies of regional language variation. While existing scholarship has documented isolated dialect features, the systematic tracking of structural changes across time and geography remains computationally prohibitive due to the fragmented nature of historical texts, non-standardized orthographies, and the need for context-sensitive morphological analysis. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will process a corpus of 15,000+ digitized texts—including sermons, letters, and municipal records—from archives in Bavaria, Saxony, and Westphalia. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to handle regional grapheme-phoneme conversions, while graph neural networks will map syntactic dependencies across divergent dialect structures. Parallelized pipelines will enable comparative analysis of feature diffusion patterns, correlating linguistic shifts with sociohistorical data on migration and trade routes. The computational workflow integrates dialectometric visualization tools to render multidimensional language change across temporal and spatial axes. Anticipated outcomes include the first quantitative model of grammatical convergence in Central German dialects, a publicly accessible web interface for interactive dialect mapping, and machine-learning architectures adaptable to other low-resource historical languages. By scaling traditional philological methods through HPC, this research will provide new insights into language contact dynamics while establishing replicable practices for computational dialectology. The resource demands—particularly GPU-accelerated training of attention models on heterogeneous historical data and large-memory processing of syntactic graphs—necessitate specialized infrastructure beyond current institutional capacities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the German language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for identifying students at risk of behavioral challenges and evaluating the efficacy of school-based interventions. School psychologists face growing demands to deliver timely, data-driven support, yet existing tools for analyzing complex, multi-source student data (e.g., academic performance, behavioral observations, socio-emotional surveys) remain limited in scalability and precision. Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture nonlinear interactions between risk factors or adapt to longitudinal datasets spanning diverse student populations. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and network analysis to model dynamic relationships between individual, classroom, and systemic variables influencing behavioral outcomes. The project will utilize large-scale datasets from partnered K–12 districts, including anonymized records of academic assessments, disciplinary referrals, intervention logs, and teacher-reported behavioral metrics. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble ML models (e.g., gradient-boosted decision trees, recurrent neural networks) to identify patterns predictive of escalating behavioral concerns and to simulate intervention scenarios across heterogeneous student subgroups. Additionally, graph-based algorithms will map how risk factors (e.g., attendance gaps, social skill deficits) co-evolve over time, enabling personalized recommendations for tiered support strategies. By parallelizing computationally intensive tasks such as hyperparameter optimization and cross-validation across thousands of cases, HPC infrastructure will reduce processing times from weeks to days, accelerating iterative model refinement. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for school psychologists to prioritize interventions based on real-time risk profiles and resource availability, as well as novel insights into how school climate variables moderate intervention success. This work aligns with the broader goal of enhancing equity in psychological service delivery through scalable, evidence-based computational methods.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of health system pharmacy operations, driven by expanding patient populations, diverse medication regimens, and dynamic resource constraints, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize clinical and administrative decision-making. This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time, data-driven management of pharmacy workflows, medication safety surveillance, and resource allocation within large healthcare systems. Current methodologies often rely on static protocols or retrospective analyses, which lack the scalability and adaptability required for modern, high-volume clinical environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating machine learning (ML) and discrete-event simulation (DES) models. These models will analyze multi-source data—including electronic health records, pharmacy dispensing logs, and supply chain metrics—to predict medication demand, identify latent risks of drug shortages or adverse events, and simulate the impact of operational interventions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization of DES parameters to reflect real-world variability in patient arrivals, staffing patterns, and facility-specific constraints. Key computational challenges include training ensemble ML algorithms on imbalanced clinical outcomes data and achieving sub-second latency for scenario testing in mission-critical applications. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for proactive inventory management, risk-stratified workload balancing across pharmacy teams, and dynamic scheduling algorithms to minimize medication turnaround times. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for health system pharmacy leaders to evaluate operational trade-offs, mitigate risks, and allocate finite resources with precision. The resulting frameworks will be disseminated as open-source modules to support reproducibility and adoption across diverse clinical settings, ultimately advancing the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of medication use systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on Health System Pharmacy Administration

abstract: Mental health disorders present complex, multifactorial challenges that require innovative approaches to improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment personalization, and service delivery. Current methodologies in mental health research often struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as electronic health records, neuroimaging, genomic data, and social determinants of health—limiting the ability to model interactions between biological, psychological, and environmental factors. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to analyze high-dimensional datasets and predict treatment outcomes for individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD). The primary research problem centers on identifying dynamic biomarkers and psychosocial predictors of intervention efficacy, which remain poorly characterized due to the computational demands of multi-modal data integration. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, capable of processing temporally resolved clinical data, structural/functional MRI scans, and polygenic risk scores. These models will be trained on a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 MDD patients, with validation across diverse demographic subgroups. Computational workflows will prioritize scalability, enabling iterative optimization of hyperparameters and cross-validation protocols to mitigate overfitting. The project also includes simulating population-level intervention scenarios via agent-based modeling to assess how resource allocation strategies impact mental health service accessibility. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for individualized treatment matching, (2) actionable insights into modifiable social factors influencing recovery trajectories, and (3) open-source tools for reproducible analysis of mental health datasets. By elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment response variability, this work aims to advance precision psychiatry and inform policy decisions to reduce disparities in mental healthcare access. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing memory-intensive computations and enabling rapid iteration across model architectures, which would be infeasible with standard clinical workstations.
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of large-scale, biologically plausible neural network models that simulate dynamic interactions within cortical microcircuits. A critical challenge in computational neuroscience lies in bridging the gap between microscale neuronal dynamics and macroscale cognitive functions, such as working memory and decision-making. Current models often simplify synaptic connectivity or neglect spatiotemporal heterogeneity due to computational constraints, limiting their ability to replicate experimental data or generate testable predictions. To address this, we propose constructing a multi-layered spiking neural network (SNN) incorporating empirically derived synaptic plasticity rules, spatially structured connectivity, and stochastic ion channel variability. The SNN will be implemented using the NEST simulator, with parallelization strategies to manage the computational load of simulating 100,000+ neurons with millisecond temporal resolution. Key computational challenges include optimizing memory allocation for synaptic weight matrices, implementing adaptive time-stepping algorithms for stiff differential equations governing ion channel dynamics, and conducting parameter sweeps to identify regimes that reproduce in vivo electrophysiological patterns. HPC resources will enable rapid iteration across network architectures and plasticity mechanisms while maintaining biological fidelity. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available model framework for simulating cortical circuit dysfunction in neuropsychiatric disorders, 2) novel predictions about how dendritic computation shapes population-level oscillations during memory tasks, and 3) benchmarks for neuromorphic hardware design. This work directly supports the development of biologically grounded theories of cognition while providing computational tools to interpret high-density neural recordings from collaborating experimental labs. Successful implementation will require sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory systems for large-scale parameter optimization and data storage.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to the nervous system and neuroscience-related technologies. Includes instruction in neural network modeling, neural dynamics, sensory, motor, and cognitive modeling, statistical modeling, sensory prosthesis, brain-machine interfaces, neuroinformatics, neuromorphic engineering, and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Tamil language and literature, addressing critical gaps in large-scale textual analysis and dialect modeling. Tamil’s rich literary history, spanning classical Sangam poetry to modern digital texts, presents unique challenges due to its diglossic nature, morphological complexity, and dialectal diversity. Existing computational tools for Tamil remain limited in scalability and accuracy, particularly for pre-modern texts and understudied regional dialects. Our research aims to develop machine learning models and NLP pipelines tailored to Tamil’s linguistic structure, enabling systematic analysis of syntactic patterns, semantic shifts, and sociolinguistic variation across genres and historical periods. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models on curated corpora of digitized manuscripts, deploying graph-based algorithms to map dialect continua, and simulating language change through agent-based models. The HPC infrastructure will support intensive tasks such as parallel processing of terabyte-scale text repositories, hyperparameter optimization for deep learning architectures, and probabilistic clustering of phonetic data from oral narratives. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for Tamil philology, annotated datasets linking literary features to sociohistorical contexts, and dynamic visualizations of dialect boundaries in collaboration with regional archives. By bridging computational methods with traditional literary scholarship, this work will facilitate novel insights into Tamil’s evolution as a literary and cultural medium while establishing scalable frameworks for under-resourced Dravidian languages. The requested resources will directly address the computational bottlenecks of processing non-Latin scripts, managing sparse data in historical corpora, and validating models against interdisciplinary benchmarks in linguistics and digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Tamil language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Classical and Modern Tamil; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and simulating the evolution of interactive narrative structures in digital media, a niche area intersecting computational storytelling, dynamic user interaction modeling, and high-performance simulation. While narrative generation has been explored in limited contexts, existing tools struggle with scalability when handling multi-threaded, user-influenced stories that adapt in real time to complex inputs (e.g., collaborative audiences, sensor-driven environments). The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in representing and optimizing branching narrative graphs with probabilistic dependencies, where traditional tree-based models become intractable for stories exceeding 10^4 decision nodes. Using a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks and discrete-event simulation, the project will implement a distributed memory framework to parallelize narrative state updates and user intent predictions. High-performance computing resources are critical for training models on synthetically generated interaction datasets (simulating 10^5+ user pathways) and for benchmarking real-time inference capabilities under variable concurrency loads. Expected outcomes include a novel partitioning algorithm to decompose narrative graphs across GPU nodes while preserving temporal consistency, as well as a publicly available toolkit for prototyping large-scale adaptive stories. This work advances computational media applications by enabling previously infeasible narrative complexity in domains such as immersive theater, collaborative world-building platforms, and AI-augmented educational simulations. The results will be evaluated against industry-standard interactive storytelling engines, with performance metrics targeting a 40% reduction in latency for stories with dynamically inserted user content. By addressing both algorithmic and systems-level challenges, this project bridges gaps between computational creativity, human-computer interaction, and distributed systems, fostering new research avenues in emergent media design.
cip_title: Computer Software and Media Applications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer software and media applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Phlebotomy, a critical yet understudied component of diagnostic medicine, faces persistent challenges in procedural success rates and sample integrity, particularly in patients with complex vascular anatomy or comorbidities. Current training paradigms rely heavily on static anatomical models and subjective skill transfer, contributing to variability in outcomes. This project proposes a computational approach to optimize venipuncture protocols and training methodologies by modeling dynamic interactions between needle insertion techniques, vascular biomechanics, and blood sample stability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop multiscale simulations integrating patient-specific vascular geometry (derived from anonymized ultrasound datasets), real-time hemodynamic parameters, and biomechanical tissue response. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and clinical datasets to predict optimal venipuncture sites and angles while minimizing hemolysis risk. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate how procedural variables (e.g., needle gauge, aspiration rate) influence cellular stress thresholds in blood samples, informing evidence-based handling protocols. The computational framework will be validated against experimental data from phantom models and retrospective clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for personalized venipuncture strategies, quantitative metrics for assessing trainee proficiency in virtual reality environments, and optimized sample collection guidelines to reduce preanalytical errors. By bridging clinical phlebotomy practice with computational biomechanics and data science, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for procedural optimization in blood collection, with potential applications in rare disease diagnostics and pediatric care where conventional approaches often prove inadequate. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project's large-scale simulations, which require parallel processing of 3D vascular models at submillimeter resolution and ensemble machine learning across heterogeneous clinical datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Turfgrass systems play a critical role in agricultural sustainability, urban landscapes, and recreational industries, yet optimizing their resilience to biotic and abiotic stressors remains a persistent challenge. Current approaches to cultivar development and management practices often rely on resource-intensive field trials, which are limited in scalability and fail to capture complex genotype-environment interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model turfgrass responses to environmental variables, disease pressures, and management regimes at unprecedented resolution. We propose a two-phase computational approach. First, genomic and phenotypic data from diverse turfgrass varieties will be integrated into machine learning frameworks to identify genetic markers associated with drought tolerance, disease resistance, and nutrient use efficiency. Second, agent-based models will simulate turfgrass growth dynamics under varying climate scenarios, incorporating soil microbiomes, irrigation patterns, and maintenance practices. These models will be parameterized using multi-omics datasets and validated against experimental field data from controlled trials. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale genomic datasets, training deep neural networks, and running iterative simulations necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with parallel processing capabilities and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for accelerating the development of climate-resilient turfgrass cultivars and data-driven recommendations for precision turf management. By reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches, this research aims to decrease water and pesticide use in turf systems while maintaining functional performance—a critical advancement for agricultural sustainability. The resulting computational pipelines will be shared as open-source resources to support broader innovation in plant sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on turfgrasses and related groundcover plants and prepares individuals to develop ornamental or recreational grasses and related products; plant, transplant, and manage grassed areas; and to produce and store turf used for transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable plant sciences, genetics of grasses, turf science, use analysis, turf management, and related economics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of moral reasoning and collective decision-making in heterogeneous societies using computational models grounded in philosophy, political science, and behavioral economics. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how diverging ethical frameworks—such as utilitarianism, deontology, and virtue ethics—interact with socioeconomic inequalities and institutional structures to shape policy preferences and coalition formation. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback between individual moral cognition, group deliberation, and systemic outcomes, particularly at scale. To overcome this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework augmented by machine learning techniques, simulating populations of agents with distinct ethical reasoning algorithms, socioeconomic profiles, and political affiliations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and run large-scale simulations (N ≈ 10^6 agents) that incorporate multi-level game-theoretic interactions, evolutionary learning mechanisms, and dynamic network structures. The computational pipeline includes Monte Carlo sampling for sensitivity analysis, graph neural networks to detect emergent coalition patterns, and Bayesian inference to calibrate model outputs against historical datasets of legislative decision-making and public opinion shifts. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of conditions under which moral pluralism enhances or destabilizes policy consensus, (2) predictive metrics for ethical conflict escalation in polarized societies, and (3) open-source tools for simulating value-laden governance scenarios. By integrating normative philosophy with computational social science, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for institutions navigating deeply divided moral landscapes, offering novel insights into the coevolution of ethics, power, and resource allocation in complex human systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on philosophical foundations, political institutions, collective behavior, economic theory, and economic influences. Includes instruction in econometrics, logic, metaphysics, moral responsibility, philosophy of language, philosophy of perception, philosophy through history, reasoning and persuasion, and social epistemology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between social connectivity, cognitive health, and environmental factors in aging populations, with a focus on identifying scalable interventions to mitigate late-life social isolation. While gerontology traditionally intersects with health sciences, this study adopts a computational social science lens, integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with longitudinal social network analysis to simulate how age-related changes in mobility, communication habits, and community infrastructure influence social engagement over time. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding non-linear cascades of social withdrawal—a multidimensional phenomenon shaped by psychological thresholds, spatial accessibility, and digital literacy. Computational demands arise from simulating millions of agent interactions across heterogeneous urban and rural environments, parameterized using geospatial data, census microdata, and biomarkers from aging cohort studies. GPU-accelerated simulations will test hypotheses about tipping points in community support systems, while machine learning pipelines will identify high-impact intervention targets from simulated outcomes. Expected outputs include a novel open-source framework for simulating lifecourse social dynamics, validated against longitudinal datasets from transnational aging studies. By quantifying how localized policy decisions (e.g., transportation subsidies, telehealth adoption) propagate through aging social networks, this work aims to provide actionable insights for reducing isolation-related health disparities. The project’s computational scale—encompassing 10^6+ agent-time steps with real-world parameter uncertainty—necessitates parallelized workflows and large-memory nodes to manage stochastic ensemble experiments. Findings will advance methodological integration in gerontology while addressing a pressing societal challenge through computationally rigorous, policy-relevant social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences, psychology and the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic structural adaptations of musculoskeletal tissues during aging, with a focus on how cellular organization and extracellular matrix remodeling contribute to functional decline. A critical gap exists in understanding the multiscale biomechanical relationships between cellular-scale dynamics (e.g., myocyte cytoskeletal rearrangements, osteocyte lacunar morphology) and tissue-level mechanical integrity in aging. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating high-resolution 3D histology datasets with biomechanical modeling, requiring advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Image stacks from aged murine and human cadaveric samples (muscle-bone interfaces, tendon insertions) will be processed using custom segmentation algorithms to extract cellular and matrix features. These data will inform finite element models simulating load distribution across hierarchical tissue structures under physiologically relevant stresses. Agent-based models will concurrently simulate age-related changes in cellular communication (e.g., mechanosensitive signaling between osteocytes and myocytes) and their impact on tissue adaptation. The HPC environment is essential for managing petabyte-scale image datasets, parallelizing computationally intensive simulations across multiple nodes, and applying machine learning classifiers to identify predictive structural biomarkers of tissue vulnerability. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of critical cellular-scale failure points preceding age-related tissue degradation, (2) quantitative maps of stress concentration patterns correlated with histological evidence of microdamage, and (3) predictive models linking subcellular architecture to organ-level biomechanical performance. This work will establish computational tools for analyzing anatomical systems at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution, directly informing strategies to mitigate age-related functional decline in musculoskeletal tissues. Results will be disseminated through open-source modeling pipelines adaptable to broader anatomical research on tissue dynamics in disease and development.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of organ systems, tissue structures, and whole bodies together with their cellular and structural components and dynamics. Includes instruction in cell biology and histology, structural biology, molecular mechanics, regional and gross anatomy, embryology, neuroanatomy, endocrinology and secretory dynamics, and applications to such topics as aging and disease conditions.

abstract: Pediatric emergency care requires tailored approaches due to the unique physiological and developmental characteristics of infants and children, yet clinical decision-making in acute settings often relies on protocols adapted from adult medicine. This project seeks to address critical gaps in evidence-based pediatric emergency management by developing predictive computational models that account for age-specific physiological variability, drug metabolism, and injury response patterns. The research problem centers on optimizing time-sensitive interventions—such as fluid resuscitation, airway management, and medication dosing—while mitigating risks of adverse outcomes in diverse pediatric populations. To achieve this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating machine learning with mechanistic modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable analysis of multimodal clinical data (retrospective EHRs, vital sign waveforms, and pharmacokinetic datasets) to identify predictors of decompensation and treatment response. Agent-based modeling will simulate clinical scenarios across developmental stages, while parallelized pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic models will evaluate drug safety and efficacy under dynamic physiological conditions. Federated learning techniques will be employed to preserve data privacy across participating pediatric trauma centers. The computational outputs will be validated against prospective observational data from pediatric emergency departments. Expected outcomes include risk stratification algorithms for early recognition of critical illness, personalized dosing recommendations for emergency medications, and simulated clinical workflows to optimize resource allocation during mass casualty events. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process complex, high-dimensional datasets and perform real-time simulations, this work aims to generate actionable tools for clinicians, reducing variability in pediatric emergency care and improving outcomes for acutely ill children. The resulting open-source models and datasets will serve as a foundation for future research in precision emergency medicine.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage emergencies in infants and children.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the behavioral dynamics of emergency responders during high-stress, multi-threat incidents, with a focus on improving real-time decision-making protocols in homeland security and protective services. Current training simulations and incident response strategies often rely on static scenarios or simplified psychological models, which fail to capture the complex interplay of cognitive load, environmental variables, and team coordination under rapidly evolving conditions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale agent-based simulations that integrate psychophysiological data, threat dispersion patterns, and adaptive communication networks. The computational model will utilize machine learning techniques to process biometric datasets (e.g., heart rate variability, situational awareness metrics) from field exercises, coupled with geospatial incident data, to simulate thousands of scenario permutations. These simulations will quantify how stress cascades affect decision latency, resource allocation accuracy, and cross-agency interoperability during crises such as active shooter events or chemical hazard responses. Expected outcomes include the identification of critical thresholds in responder performance degradation, predictive tools for optimizing team composition under specific threat profiles, and evidence-based protocols for dynamically reallocating personnel during extended operations. By bridging computational neuroscience, operational analytics, and crisis management, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for enhancing responder resilience and mission effectiveness in scenarios that defy conventional training frameworks. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the concurrent processing of high-dimensional behavioral data, real-time physics-based threat modeling, and ensemble machine learning workflows required to advance this interdisciplinary research niche.
cip_title: Homeland Security, Law Enforcement, Firefighting and Related Protective Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, law enforcement, firefighting, and related protective services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational modeling of phonological and syntactic structures in understudied Southeast Asian languages, with a focus on the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families. Despite their typological diversity and sociolinguistic significance, many languages in this region remain underrepresented in computational linguistics due to sparse digital corpora and the complexity of their morphological systems. The research problem centers on overcoming these barriers by developing scalable methods for automated analysis of tone, syllable structure, and clause alignment in low-resource languages, which are critical for understanding language contact, historical change, and regional dialect continua. The computational approach integrates machine learning techniques—including transformer-based models for unsupervised phonological segmentation and graph-based algorithms for syntactic dependency parsing—with traditional comparative linguistic methods. Large-scale parallel processing will be employed to train models on heterogeneous datasets spanning transcribed oral narratives, legacy lexical databases, and newly digitized texts from fieldwork archives. Key challenges include managing noise in non-standardized orthographies, addressing data sparsity through transfer learning across related languages, and optimizing memory usage for processing agglutinative morphologies. Expected outcomes include (1) the creation of open-access, annotated corpora for at least five languages with limited digital resources (e.g., Shan, Lahu, Javanese); (2) computational models that improve automated transcription accuracy for tonal languages by ≥20% compared to existing benchmarks; and (3) phylogenetic network visualizations tracing contact-induced changes in argument-marking systems across mainland and insular Southeast Asia. By enabling resource-intensive analyses of cross-linguistic patterns at unprecedented scale, this work will contribute new methodologies for documenting endangered languages while advancing theoretical debates about areal typology and language change in one of the world’s most linguistically diverse regions.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the modern languages spoken in mainland Southeast Asia and the Indonesian and Philippines Archipelagoes, including, but not limited to, members of the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time personalization of financial service offerings in multi-channel digital environments, addressing the challenge of balancing customer privacy preferences with dynamic marketing efficiency. Financial institutions increasingly rely on AI-driven tools to tailor services, yet existing models struggle to integrate real-time behavioral data, regulatory constraints, and cross-platform coordination at scale—a gap that limits both customer satisfaction and operational profitability. The project will employ multi-agent reinforcement learning systems to simulate decentralized decision-making across marketing touchpoints (mobile apps, chatbots, and advisor interfaces), incorporating heterogeneous customer privacy tolerance levels derived from anonymized transaction histories and interaction logs. High-performance computing resources are critical for training ensemble models on synthetic datasets representing 10M+ customer agents, each with dynamically evolving financial profiles and communication channel preferences. The computational architecture will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to test optimal incentive structures under evolving regulatory scenarios, while federated learning techniques preserve data localization constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated protocol for ethical real-time service personalization that reduces customer churn by ≥15% in simulation benchmarks, alongside open-source tools for privacy-preserving recommendation systems in financial operations. By advancing computational methods at the intersection of behavioral economics, distributed systems, and financial marketing operations, this work aims to establish new performance standards for responsive service design while informing regulatory frameworks for AI-enhanced financial ecosystems.
cip_title: Business and Personal/ Financial Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and operational tasks associated with the provision of personal and financial services. Includes instruction in banking, marketing research, advertising, promotional campaign organization, insurance, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic analysis of Bulgarian textual heritage, with a focus on diachronic syntactic evolution and dialectal variation. While Bulgarian’s complex morphology and historical development from Old Church Slavonic have been studied extensively through traditional philological methods, large-scale quantitative analysis remains limited due to the computational demands of processing heterogeneous, unstructured texts spanning medieval manuscripts to modern digital corpora. The primary research problem centers on identifying patterns of syntactic change and regional linguistic variation that are not easily discernible through manual analysis, particularly in under-resourced historical and dialectal texts. Computational methods will include the development of customized NLP pipelines for automated morphological tagging, dependency parsing, and syntactic feature extraction across temporally and geographically diverse Bulgarian texts. These pipelines will integrate transformer-based language models fine-tuned on pre-modern Bulgarian variants, requiring distributed training across GPU nodes to handle low-resource scenarios. Concurrently, graph-based algorithms will analyze syntactic network structures to model language change, while clustering techniques will map dialectal features. The project will utilize existing digitized collections and newly processed materials from regional archives, comprising approximately 15TB of text and metadata. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive diachronic syntactic corpus of Bulgarian, public computational tools for Slavic philology, and quantitative models tracing the relationship between literary standardization and regional vernaculars. By enabling systematic analysis at unprecedented scale, this work will provide novel insights into Balkan Sprachbund dynamics and inform preservation strategies for endangered dialectal forms. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive corpus processing, parallelized model training, and large-scale comparative simulations across linguistic variables.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bulgarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing agricultural data governance, with a focus on the intersection of intellectual property, privacy, and sustainability in precision agriculture. As digital tools such as IoT sensors, drones, and AI-driven analytics become integral to farming practices, legal disputes over data ownership, cross-jurisdictional compliance, and ethical use have surged. Traditional legal research methods struggle to map the rapid proliferation of case law, statutes, and international agreements in this domain or model their systemic impacts. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) to process large-scale legal text corpora—including court opinions, legislative documents, and trade agreements—paired with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate how conflicting regulatory regimes influence stakeholder behavior (e.g., farmers, agribusinesses, policymakers). Computational legal analytics will identify latent trends in judicial reasoning, while ABM experiments will test hypothetical policy interventions under scenarios such as climate-driven resource scarcity or supply chain disruptions. By integrating legal text mining with complex systems simulation, this project aims to generate actionable insights into balancing innovation incentives, data sovereignty, and equitable access in agricultural technology. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on multilingual legal texts, scaling ABM parameters to reflect global agricultural ecosystems, and conducting sensitivity analyses across diverse policy environments. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated legal decisions, predictive frameworks for regulatory risk assessment, and policy recommendations to address fragmentation in agricultural data law. This work bridges computational social science and legal informatics, offering a novel methodology for addressing 21st-century governance challenges in non-traditional STEM domains.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in food and agriculture.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance understanding of how adaptive social-emotional learning (SEL) interventions impact academic engagement and outcomes in K–12 students from diverse backgrounds. A critical challenge in educational psychology is modeling the dynamic, non-linear interactions between individual differences (e.g., cognitive development, cultural context), intervention components, and longitudinal academic behaviors. Traditional statistical methods struggle to account for these multidimensional, time-dependent relationships at scale. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate student trajectories under varying SEL strategies. The ABM component will parameterize agents using real-world datasets—including demographic, behavioral, and psychometric data from 10,000+ students—to replicate classroom ecosystems, while ML pipelines will identify intervention optimization pathways. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing large-scale parameter sweeps across diverse virtual cohorts and iteratively training predictive models on simulated interaction data. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model of SEL intervention efficacy across developmental stages and cultural contexts, (2) actionable guidelines for personalizing intervention timing and delivery modes, and (3) open-source tools for simulating equity-focused educational strategies. By quantifying how systemic factors moderate intervention impacts, this work will inform scalable, culturally responsive counseling practices and reduce trial-and-error in program design. The computational demands of simulating high-fidelity educational environments—including real-time adaptation algorithms and multi-level outcome analyses—necessitate cluster-based processing and GPU acceleration unavailable in local infrastructure. This project bridges counseling psychology and computational education research, offering novel methodologies to study complex person-environment interactions in learning ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of healthcare data present significant challenges in medical records management, particularly in integrating heterogeneous data sources, ensuring real-time processing, and maintaining security. Traditional computational methods often lack the scalability and efficiency required for modern clinical datasets. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced data integration frameworks and predictive analytics models. The research will employ distributed computing techniques to manage large-scale electronic health records (EHRs) and unstructured clinical notes, utilizing natural language processing (NLP) libraries such as spaCy and NLTK for text analysis. Machine learning algorithms, implemented via TensorFlow and PyTorch, will be optimized for parallel processing to enable real-time predictive analytics for patient outcomes and resource allocation. Additionally, the project will investigate cryptographic protocols and federated learning architectures to enhance data security and privacy compliance. Expected outcomes include a scalable infrastructure for rapid EHR processing, validated predictive models with clinical applicability, and a secure data-sharing framework adhering to regulatory standards. The successful implementation of this research will provide critical tools for improving data-driven decision-making in healthcare, optimizing resource utilization, and supporting the integration of emerging technologies such as AI-driven diagnostics and telemedicine. By addressing computational bottlenecks and advancing methodological innovations in health informatics, this project aims to contribute significantly to the evolution of robust, scalable solutions in medical records technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: Aging populations face complex health challenges due to the interplay of chronic conditions, polypharmacy, and physiological decline, yet clinical guidelines for geriatric patients often lack specificity for these multifaceted scenarios. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of health outcomes in elderly patients with multimorbidity. The research will analyze electronic health records (EHRs) from geriatric populations, incorporating variables such as comorbidities, medication regimens, biomarkers, and psychosocial factors. Machine learning techniques, including ensemble models and deep neural networks, will be employed to identify patterns in disease progression, adverse drug events, and care utilization. A parallel computational workflow will simulate pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions in polypharmacy scenarios, accounting for age-related changes in drug metabolism. Additionally, agent-based models will test hypothetical care coordination strategies to optimize interventions for patients with cognitive impairment or functional limitations. The scale of data—spanning millions of patient encounters—and the computational complexity of modeling nonlinear biological interactions necessitate HPC infrastructure for efficient processing. Expected outcomes include risk stratification tools for clinicians, personalized medication optimization frameworks, and evidence-based recommendations for revising geriatric care protocols. By quantifying the impact of specific nursing interventions on long-term health trajectories, this work aims to reduce hospital readmissions, mitigate adverse drug reactions, and improve quality of life for aging populations. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to support future gerontological nursing research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time adaptive behavior in large-scale, multi-user virtual environments (VEs) through the integration of predictive human-performance modeling and distributed resource allocation. Current VE systems struggle to balance immersive interactivity with computational efficiency, particularly as user populations scale or environmental complexity increases. Traditional approaches prioritize either rendering fidelity or network latency reduction, often neglecting the dynamic interplay between human behavioral variance and system resource constraints. Our research addresses this gap by coupling stochastic models of user interaction patterns—derived from eye-tracking, gesture recognition, and biometric feedback—with a reinforcement learning system that dynamically allocates computational resources (GPU, memory, network bandwidth) across distributed nodes. The core computational challenge involves training neural surrogates to predict region-of-interest shifts and interaction criticality across thousands of concurrent users, then using these predictions to guide just-in-time resource redistribution in a cloud-based simulation architecture. High-performance computing resources are essential for both the offline training phase (requiring massive parallelism for Monte Carlo simulations of heterogeneous user cohorts) and the online deployment phase (demanding low-latency communication across GPU clusters to maintain synchronization tolerances below 20ms). Expected outcomes include a validated open-source middleware capable of sustaining >10,000 concurrent users in photorealistic VEs with sub-percentile latency outliers, alongside new metrics quantifying the trade-space between perceptual realism and computational load. This work bridges human-factors engineering with distributed systems optimization, offering foundational insights for next-generation applications in remote collaborative training, virtual healthcare delivery, and crowd-behavior analysis in smart city simulations.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles of applied visual simulation technology and the application of quantitative analyses to human-computer interaction. Includes instruction in object-oriented programming, artificial intelligence, computer communications and networks, computer graphics, virtual worlds and simulation systems, probability, statistics, stochastic modeling, data analysis, human-performance evaluation, and human-behavior modeling.

abstract: Emerging and re-emerging pathogens in veterinary populations present complex challenges requiring advanced computational approaches to model host-microbe interactions and predict therapeutic outcomes. This project addresses critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms driving antimicrobial resistance (AMR) evolution in *Pasteurella multocida* and related veterinary pathogens associated with bovine respiratory disease. Current clinical interventions face limitations due to rapid pathogen adaptation and incomplete characterization of resistance pathways across diverse bacterial lineages. We propose an integrative computational framework combining comparative pangenomics, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of target protein-ligand interactions, and machine learning-driven prediction of resistance phenotypes from whole genome sequences. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets encompassing 15,000+ microbial genomes, perform nanoseconds-scale MD simulations of mutant penicillin-binding proteins, and train deep neural networks on heterogeneous data types (genomic, proteomic, and clinical metadata). The computational workflow will identify conserved structural motifs in resistance determinants, predict epistatic interactions between resistance mutations, and model population-level transmission dynamics under different treatment protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive atlas of AMR-associated genetic signatures validated against in vitro susceptibility testing, (2) mechanistic models of β-lactam antibiotic target evolution, and (3) optimized treatment guidelines incorporating genomic surveillance data. This resource will enable clinical veterinarians to implement genotype-guided antimicrobial selection, reducing treatment failures in livestock while preserving drug efficacy. The computational framework developed will be adaptable to other veterinary pathogens of concern, supporting proactive management of zoonotic disease threats at the human-animal interface. Successful implementation requires dedicated GPU nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory CPU allocations for population genomic analyses exceeding 1.5TB RAM per job.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: The integration of traditional herbal medicine into modern health sciences faces a critical challenge: understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of complex plant-derived compounds, which often act synergistically rather than in isolation. While ethnobotanical knowledge provides a foundation, the lack of systematic computational frameworks to model multi-compound interactions, bioavailability, and target pathways hinders the validation and optimization of herbal therapies. This project seeks to address this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze the polypharmacology of herbal formulations, focusing on their interactions with human proteomes and microbiomes. Leveraging a curated database of 10,000+ phytochemicals from 300 medicinal plants used in Western and Indigenous traditions, we will combine molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven binding affinity prediction, and network pharmacology to map compound-target-pathway relationships. HPC resources will enable large-scale virtual screening of phytochemical libraries against disease-relevant proteins (e.g., inflammatory cytokines, neuroreceptors) and simulate time-dependent interactions in multi-compound systems. Concurrently, metagenomic datasets from clinical studies on herbal interventions will be analyzed to model microbiome-mediated metabolic activation of botanicals. The computational pipeline will integrate these layers to predict synergistic formulations and potential adverse herb-host-microbiome interactions. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel bioactive synergists, validation of ethnobotanical use cases through mechanistic insights, and the development of an open-access predictive platform for herbal therapy optimization. This work bridges traditional knowledge systems with computational biology, offering a paradigm to enhance the precision, safety, and efficacy of herbal medicine while addressing understudied aspects of plant-human-microbiome co-evolution in health maintenance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to utilize the materia medica and clinical practices of Western, Native American, African, Australasian, and other herbal medicine traditions to prevent and cure illness and temporary physical disorders. Includes instruction in basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; nutrition; terminology and materia medica; therapeutic herbalism; herbal pharmacy; botanicals and ethnobotany; wildcrafting and harvesting; labeling and dispensing phytotherapy; counterindications; practice management; consultation skills; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational legal analytics framework aimed at modeling the evolution of judicial reasoning in U.S. appellate courts. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically analyze the growing volume and complexity of case law, particularly in identifying subtle patterns in judicial argumentation, citation networks, and the interplay between legal doctrine and sociopolitical context. By integrating natural language processing (NLP), temporal graph analysis, and transformer-based language models, this research will process a corpus of 10 million judicial opinions (1790–present) to trace doctrinal shifts, quantify the influence of non-legal factors on decision-making, and simulate the propagation of legal concepts across jurisdictions. The computational pipeline will involve entity recognition for legal constructs, dynamic network modeling of precedent hierarchies, and attention-based classification of rhetorical strategies in majority and dissenting opinions. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific legal language models, conducting large-scale graph traversals to map precedent cascades, and running Monte Carlo simulations to assess the stability of inferred doctrinal patterns. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph of legal reasoning trajectories, predictive models of judicial outcomes under hypothetical policy scenarios, and methodological innovations in applying computational social science techniques to legal texts. This work bridges gaps between legal theory, computational linguistics, and complex systems analysis, offering pre-law scholars tools to study law as a dynamic, data-driven system. Results will inform curricular advancements in legal education, particularly in teaching students to navigate rapidly evolving areas like algorithmic accountability and digital rights, while providing a foundation for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of law, ethics, and emergent technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional study of law at the post-baccalaureate level.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance speech-language pedagogy by developing computational models that analyze patterns in student speech development and inform adaptive teaching strategies. Current methods for evaluating speech acquisition and language arts proficiency in K–12 classrooms rely heavily on manual observation, which limits scalability and real-time feedback. To address this gap, we propose training machine learning models on multimodal datasets—including audio recordings of student speech, demographic metadata, and longitudinal performance metrics—to identify predictive markers of language development challenges. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of speech data using parallelized acoustic feature extraction (e.g., formant analysis, prosody quantification) and transformer-based natural language processing to evaluate semantic complexity. These pipelines will be optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters to handle real-time inference demands. A secondary aim involves simulating classroom discourse scenarios via agent-based modeling, where synthetic student avatars interact with proposed teaching interventions, enabling rapid iteration of pedagogical strategies. Outcomes will include open-source tools for automated speech proficiency assessment and a framework for personalizing language arts instruction based on computational insights. By bridging speech science, educational practice, and HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to equip educators with empirically validated, scalable methods to address heterogeneous student needs. The requested resources will directly support model training, large-scale simulations, and the development of cloud-based interfaces for teacher training programs, ultimately contributing to more equitable and data-informed speech education practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach speech and language arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Dental implant success relies on the biomechanical integration of implants with bone and soft tissues, yet variability in patient anatomy, bone density, and occlusal forces complicates predictable outcomes. Current clinical methods for implant planning and design optimization lack the resolution to model complex, patient-specific biomechanical interactions at scale, leading to suboptimal load distribution and risks of failure. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate multiscale biomechanical responses in dental implants, enabling data-driven personalization of implant design and surgical placement. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to execute finite element analysis (FEA) models integrating patient-derived CT/CBCT data, material properties of bone and implants, and dynamic occlusal force patterns. These models will simulate stress-strain distributions under physiological and parafunctional loading conditions across thousands of virtual implant configurations. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze retrospective clinical datasets to identify predictive biomechanical and anatomical features associated with osseointegration success or complications. The integration of simulation outputs and predictive analytics will generate patient-specific risk profiles and design recommendations. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for FEA solvers, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models on high-dimensional clinical data, and real-time optimization algorithms for surgical planning. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for implant stability, optimized implant geometries for heterogeneous bone qualities, and a decision-support tool for clinicians to preempt biomechanical failure risks. This work aims to reduce implant failure rates, improve functional outcomes in patients with compromised bone anatomy, and establish a paradigm for computational biomechanics in implantology. The scalability of this approach, enabled by HPC resources, will facilitate future translation to broader populations and complex craniofacial reconstruction cases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the surgical and restorative aspects of implant dentistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision nutrition interventions by modeling the dynamic interactions between dietary components, gut microbiota, and individual metabolic responses. Current dietary planning frameworks often rely on generalized population data, limiting their efficacy in addressing heterogeneous patient needs. Dietetic technicians, who operationalize nutrition plans, require tools to predict patient-specific outcomes of dietary modifications, particularly for individuals with complex metabolic conditions or atypical responses to standard interventions. The research problem centers on the computational limitations of existing models, which cannot simultaneously integrate high-resolution data on nutrient composition, microbial community dynamics, and host physiology at scale. To address this, we propose developing a multi-scale computational platform that combines agent-based modeling of gut microbial ecosystems with machine learning-driven analysis of clinical biomarkers and dietary intake patterns. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of microbiome sequencing data (metagenomic and metabolomic), real-time simulation of nutrient-microbiota interactions, and probabilistic forecasting of metabolic outcomes.
