Computational workflows will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of patients with type 2 diabetes and irritable bowel syndrome, conditions where diet-microbiota crosstalk significantly influences treatment efficacy. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for simulating personalized dietary interventions, predictive algorithms to guide meal planning, and quantitative metrics linking microbial diversity to nutrient absorption efficiency. This work directly supports dietetic technicians in transitioning from standardized protocols to data-driven, patient-specific care while contributing novel computational methodologies to the emerging field of precision nutrition. By bridging gaps between clinical dietetics, systems biology, and computational modeling, the project aims to establish scalable infrastructure for optimizing therapeutic diets in metabolic and gastrointestinal disorders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of registered dietitians and nutritionists, to implement nutritional and dietetic plans and provide direct client and patient services. Includes instruction in human nutrition, client interviewing and record keeping, dietary planning, food preparation and safety, food worker supervision, food service establishment monitoring and inspection, and applicable procedures and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in fitting complex Bayesian hierarchical models to large-scale spatial and temporal datasets, a critical bottleneck in modern statistical research. Such models are increasingly used in epidemiology, environmental science, and public policy to capture dependencies across multiple scales and integrate heterogeneous data sources. However, their implementation is hindered by the computational intensity of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, particularly when applied to high-dimensional parameter spaces and massive datasets. The research will develop and optimize scalable algorithms for Bayesian inference, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize MCMC sampling across multiple nodes, implement GPU-accelerated gradient-based variational inference, and exploit sparse matrix techniques for efficient handling of spatial covariance structures. Key computational innovations include hybrid sampling schemes that combine Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with adaptive Metropolis-Hastings steps, distributed memory parallelism for hierarchical model components, and memory-efficient data partitioning strategies. The project will validate these methods through case studies analyzing multi-decadal climate model outputs paired with satellite-derived environmental data, as well as epidemiological datasets tracking disease spread across urban networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly available open-source software package optimized for HPC environments, benchmarks demonstrating order-of-magnitude improvements in sampling efficiency for common model classes, and novel statistical insights into spatiotemporal processes underlying climate extremes and infectious disease transmission. By enabling the practical application of richly structured Bayesian models to real-world problems at unprecedented scales, this work will advance statistical methodology while providing actionable tools for interdisciplinary researchers grappling with complex, data-intensive challenges. The requested computing resources are essential for testing algorithmic scalability, conducting large-scale simulations, and ensuring reproducibility across diverse application domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mathematics and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the structural-functional relationships of animal anatomical systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale biological processes. Veterinary anatomy research increasingly relies on integrating cellular, tissue, and organ-level data—from electron microscopy, molecular dynamics, and 3D imaging—to decode mechanisms underlying diseases such as degenerative neuromuscular disorders or developmental anomalies. However, existing computational tools lack the capacity to resolve spatial and temporal complexities across these scales, particularly in large animal models. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework for multi-modal data integration and simulation. This framework will combine machine learning-driven segmentation of histological and ultrastructural datasets with biomechanical modeling of tissue systems, enabling predictive analyses of how molecular or cellular disruptions propagate to organ dysfunction. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of terabyte-scale imaging datasets, GPU-accelerated finite element modeling of musculoskeletal dynamics, and agent-based simulations of neural network adaptations in disease states. HPC resources will be critical for scaling these workflows to species-specific anatomies (e.g., equine, bovine) with high-resolution precision. Anticipated outcomes include new open-source tools for mapping disease pathways in veterinary contexts, validated against experimental electrophysiology and histopathology data. This work will directly advance translational applications, such as optimizing surgical interventions or therapeutic regimens, while establishing a computational anatomy pipeline adaptable to emerging imaging and omics technologies. By resolving structural drivers of pathology in diverse species, the project aligns with broader agricultural science goals of improving animal health and productivity.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of small and large animal cellular, organ, tissue, and body systems and their relation to physiologic function, disease, and therapeutic treatment. Includes instruction in histology, ultrastructure, molecular biology, biochemistry, developmental biology, neuroscience, electrophysiology, electron microscopy, computer imaging, and applications to specific species.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are critical for global carbon sequestration, biodiversity, and sustainable resource provision, yet optimizing their management under climate uncertainty remains a complex, data-intensive challenge. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model forest growth dynamics, harvest scheduling, and ecological trade-offs across heterogeneous landscapes. The research addresses two core gaps: (1) limited integration of spatially explicit climate projections, species-specific growth patterns, and economic constraints in existing forest management tools, and (2) the computational infeasibility of running multi-decadal simulations at fine spatial scales (<1 km² resolution) using conventional methods. We propose a hybrid machine learning and process-based modeling approach, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to parallelize simulations across 10,000+ landscape units while incorporating real-time LiDAR data assimilation. Key computational components include a deep neural network trained on historical growth data from 50+ forest stands, an agent-based model for harvesting equipment interactions, and a Monte Carlo framework to evaluate climate scenarios from CMIP6 datasets. The HPC resources will enable parameter optimization across 15+ tree species, simultaneous evaluation of 200+ management strategies, and uncertainty quantification through 10,000+ ensemble runs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that identifies harvest schedules maximizing timber yield while maintaining 90% of baseline carbon storage capacity, alongside species transplantation guidelines to enhance climate resilience. By scaling analyses to entire watersheds rather than individual stands, this work will provide forestry managers with actionable insights into landscape-level resource allocation, particularly in mixed-use regions where agroforestry interfaces with industrial timber production. The computational framework will be开源ly released to support adaptive management across boreal and temperate forests globally.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of forestry principles to the production, harvesting, and processing of forest resources and that prepares individuals to perform associated technical and managerial functions. Includes instruction in forest production and utilization, industrial forestry, agroforestry, transplantation, timber harvesting, selection and identification of trees, processing technologies and systems, equipment operations and maintenance, and related management skills.

abstract: The increasing demand for German language education across diverse learner populations necessitates innovative pedagogical tools that address individualized learning needs. Current approaches to assessing language proficiency and designing adaptive instructional materials often rely on static frameworks, which may not account for the dynamic interplay of linguistic, cognitive, and cultural factors influencing second language acquisition. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational model to analyze learner interactions and predict proficiency trajectories, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale multilingual datasets. The research problem centers on optimizing real-time adaptive assessment tools for German language learners, particularly in classroom settings where teachers must balance heterogeneous skill levels. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based architectures, the project will process spoken and written learner corpora to identify patterns in syntactic complexity, lexical diversity, and pragmatic accuracy. These datasets, drawn from anonymized student interactions across proficiency levels (A1–C1), will be enriched with contextual metadata such as task type, error frequency, and corrective feedback responses. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of machine learning models to classify learner errors, simulate language development pathways, and generate personalized feedback recommendations. The computational workflow will integrate fine-tuned BERT models for German-specific error detection and graph-based algorithms to map interlanguage development. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for German language instructors, offering dynamic proficiency analytics and evidence-based strategies for differentiated instruction. By modeling the variability in learner outcomes at scale, this project aims to advance the integration of computational linguistics into teacher education, equipping future German language educators with data-driven methodologies to enhance curricular design and classroom practice. The scalability of this approach, enabled by HPC infrastructure, will support replication across less commonly taught languages, fostering equity in language education resource development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach German language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize decision-making processes for adaptive logistics networks in contested military environments. Modern military operations face dynamic challenges due to rapidly evolving threats, resource constraints, and the need for real-time coordination across distributed units. Traditional linear planning tools struggle to account for the unpredictability of adversarial actions, environmental disruptions, and multi-domain interdependencies. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based and reinforcement learning approach to simulate complex logistics scenarios under asymmetric constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to incorporate thousands of interacting agents—representing personnel, autonomous systems, and supply nodes—while integrating real-world geospatial, meteorological, and threat intelligence datasets. The computational model will train adaptive decision policies under stochastic conditions, testing resilience against cascading failures and adversarial machine learning attacks. Outcomes will include a suite of open-source tools for evaluating trade-offs between speed, security, and resource efficiency in mission-critical supply chains. By leveraging parallelized optimization and probabilistic risk analysis, this work aims to advance computational methods for military logistics planning, offering a template for human-AI collaboration in high-stakes, resource-constrained environments. The results will directly inform training protocols and contingency planning frameworks, with broader implications for crisis response systems in non-military sectors requiring robust decentralized coordination.
cip_title: Military Technologies and Applied Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military technologies and applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Maternal morbidity and adverse pregnancy outcomes remain significant challenges in women’s health, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations. Current approaches to risk stratification and intervention planning often rely on generalized guidelines that inadequately account for the complex interplay of physiological, pharmacological, and sociodemographic factors unique to individual patients. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a predictive computational framework to optimize personalized care strategies for obstetric and gynecological patients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-modal datasets—including electronic health records, longitudinal biomarker profiles, pharmacogenomic data, and patient-reported outcomes—to construct machine learning models capable of forecasting individualized risks for conditions such as preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, and postpartum hemorrhage. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian hierarchical modeling to address data sparsity in underrepresented groups and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate tailored intervention pathways. The models will further incorporate pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations to evaluate drug efficacy and safety across pregnancy stages, accounting for dynamic physiological changes. By enabling real-time analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, HPC resources are critical to achieving the resolution and speed required for these simulations. The anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools to guide nurse-led interventions, reducing preventable complications and advancing equity in women’s health care. This work aligns with nursing science priorities by translating computational insights into actionable clinical practices, ultimately strengthening evidence-based, patient-centered care models in obstetrics and gynecology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: Mental health challenges are increasingly complex, requiring interventions tailored to individual biopsychosocial profiles. Current methods for predicting treatment outcomes or optimizing personalized counseling strategies are limited by the multidimensional nature of client data, which includes psychometric assessments, session transcripts, behavioral logs, and physiological markers. Traditional statistical approaches struggle to model nonlinear interactions among these variables, hindering the development of actionable clinical insights. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build machine learning models capable of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets in mental health counseling. The research will integrate anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), natural language processing (NLP) of session transcripts, and longitudinal outcome data from 5,000+ clients across diverse demographic groups. Computational workflows will include ensemble methods to identify predictors of treatment adherence, deep learning architectures to detect latent patterns in counselor-client interactions, and agent-based simulations to model the impact of intervention timing on recovery trajectories. HPC resources are essential for training these models efficiently, given the need for parallel processing of high-dimensional data (e.g., NLP features from 50,000+ session notes) and hyperparameter optimization across thousands of iterations. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for matching clients to optimal counseling modalities, (2) quantifiable thresholds for risk stratification based on dynamic behavioral markers, and (3) open-source tools for real-time clinical decision support. This work will advance precision mental health care while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for data privacy. By elucidating computational pathways between counseling techniques and client outcomes, the project aims to establish empirically grounded guidelines for resource allocation in community mental health systems, ultimately improving accessibility and efficacy of short-term therapeutic interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide evaluations, referrals, and short-term counseling services to help people prevent or remediate personal problems, conflicts, and emotional crises. Includes instruction in human development, psychopathology, individual and group counseling, personality theory, career assessment, patient screening and referral, observation and testing techniques, interviewing skills, professional standards and ethics, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of integrating heterogeneous biomedical data streams into dynamic, interpretable visual models for precision medicine applications. Specifically, the study focuses on neurodegenerative disorders, where the interplay between neuroimaging data, molecular biomarkers, and patient-specific clinical trajectories remains poorly visualized and computationally intractable at scale. Current tools struggle to synthesize high-dimensional datasets—such as diffusion tensor imaging, single-cell transcriptomics, and longitudinal electronic health records—into cohesive representations that clinicians can intuitively navigate. The project proposes developing a novel computational pipeline that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to create adaptive 3D visualizations of disease progression. These models will be trained on multi-institutional neuroimaging repositories and multi-omics datasets, requiring distributed training across GPU clusters to manage memory-intensive operations. Key computational challenges include optimizing tensor decomposition for real-time rendering of probabilistic disease pathways and implementing federated learning protocols to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source visualization platform that enables clinicians to interactively explore patient-specific neurodegenerative patterns against population-level biomarkers. The HPC infrastructure will facilitate processing petabytes of imaging data while maintaining sub-second latency for model inference during surgical planning scenarios. By bridging medical illustration principles with advanced informatics architectures, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven clinical decision support systems, with potential applications in oncology and rare disease management. The resource allocation will directly support the scaling of hybrid voxel-graph neural networks and validation studies using synthetic patient cohorts generated via differential privacy-preserving GANs.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in medical illustration and informatics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interdependencies between municipal debt instruments, climate risk exposure, and fiscal resilience in U.S. local governments. As climate-related shocks increasingly strain public budgets, traditional linear budgeting frameworks fail to capture the nonlinear feedback loops linking environmental stressors, credit market reactions, and service delivery costs. We propose developing an agent-based computational model that integrates 1) climate projection data (e.g., flood risks, heatwave frequency), 2) municipal bond market microstructures, and 3) adaptive policymaking processes across 10,000+ simulated jurisdictions. The model will parameterize heterogeneous local governments with varying debt portfolios, insurance mechanisms, and infrastructure adaptation strategies, subjecting them to stochastic climate events and investor behavior shifts. Computational challenges include managing high-dimensional optimization spaces for multi-objective fiscal policies (revenue stabilization, credit rating preservation, capital project viability) and processing terabyte-scale historical datasets on municipal defaults, disaster expenditures, and bond issuance patterns. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool quantifying the cascading budgetary impacts of climate scenarios under different refinancing strategies and intergovernmental aid frameworks. By bridging computational economics, climate science, and public finance theory, this work aims to establish new metrics for "climate-debt vulnerability" that could inform bond rating methodologies and federal risk-sharing programs. The HPC environment is critical for achieving the necessary scale and resolution to model rare but catastrophic fiscal tipping points while maintaining computational tractability across decade-long policy horizons.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of analyzing cultural phenomena in journalism, where traditional methods struggle to process vast, heterogeneous datasets spanning visual arts, performing arts, digital media, and textual discourse. As cultural journalism increasingly intersects with data-driven storytelling, there is a critical need for advanced computational tools to analyze multimodal content—such as video, audio, social media, and archival texts—at scale. The research aims to develop a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to systematically examine cultural trends, biases, and narratives across media, enabling journalists to uncover nuanced insights and produce evidence-based critiques. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for textual criticism, computer vision algorithms for visual and performance art analysis, and audio signal processing for music and broadcast media. These methods will be deployed in parallel on HPC clusters to handle large-scale datasets, including decades of arts reporting, film archives, and social media interactions. Machine learning models, such as transformer-based architectures and multimodal neural networks, will be trained to identify patterns in cultural representation, track the evolution of artistic movements, and detect disparities in media coverage across demographics. The project also explores ethical AI frameworks to mitigate biases in automated analysis. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for cultural journalists to analyze multimedia content efficiently, alongside scholarly articles examining computational methods’ role in enhancing critical journalism. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to bridge computational scalability with qualitative cultural critique, empowering journalists to address systemic inequities in arts coverage and enrich public discourse on contemporary culture.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to be journalists who critically examine current culture as expressed through the visual and performing arts, design, film, music, radio, television, dance, theater, and written text. Includes instruction in arts criticism, art and entertainment reporting, cultural critique, investigative reporting, newspaper reporting, photojournalism, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in dynamic print production workflows, a critical challenge in the graphic and printing equipment operations field. Traditional methods for optimizing job scheduling, color calibration, and material usage in commercial printing rely on static heuristics or manual adjustments, leading to suboptimal resource allocation, increased waste, and delays under variable demand. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a computational framework that integrates real-time data from digital printing systems, environmental sensors, and customer specifications to model and simulate production scenarios. The core computational challenge lies in processing heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution image files, substrate behavior models, and machine performance metrics—to generate adaptive scheduling algorithms and predictive maintenance protocols. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of finite element analysis (FEA) simulations for substrate deformation under different printing conditions, as well as training machine learning models to correlate historical job data with optimal ink-volume profiles. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that reduces material waste by 15-20% in testbed environments and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated print production scenarios for educational use. The project aligns with the Communication and Journalism field’s growing emphasis on sustainable media production by bridging technical operations research with practical workforce training. Results will directly inform curriculum updates in graphic equipment operation courses, ensuring students engage with data-driven methodologies that reflect industry advancements. This work fills a critical gap in non-STEM computational applications by demonstrating how HPC can transform traditionally manual trade processes into precision-oriented, digitally integrated systems.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in digital textual studies by addressing the challenge of analyzing large-scale, multilingual historical archives through computational methods. Current approaches to textual criticism and archival analysis often struggle to process the volume and complexity of digitized historical texts, particularly those spanning multiple languages, scripts, and temporal periods. This limitation hinders the ability to uncover patterns in textual transmission, semantic shifts, or cross-cultural influences at scale. To bridge this gap, the project proposes a computational pipeline integrating machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis. The workflow will involve preprocessing digitized manuscripts (OCR correction, tokenization, metadata alignment), training multilingual transformer models for semantic and stylistic feature extraction, and applying graph-based algorithms to model textual relationships. HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of training transformer models on terabytes of text data, running parallelized analyses across distributed corpora, and storing intermediate outputs. The project will utilize GPU clusters for model training and CPU nodes for large-scale text alignment tasks. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for cross-temporal and cross-linguistic textual analysis, open-source tools for digital humanities scholars, and new insights into the circulation of medieval legal texts across European and Mediterranean archives. By enabling the study of textual networks at unprecedented scale, this work aims to demonstrate how computational methods can reshape traditional philological research while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between humanities scholars and computer scientists. The requested resources will support both the development of reproducible workflows for textual data and the exploration of ethical considerations in applying AI to culturally sensitive materials.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on digital textual editing, archiving, and publishing, and on the study of new media and computing platforms from the perspectives of the humanities and computer science. Includes instruction in archiving, computer programming, cultural studies, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced signal processing algorithms to enhance the detection and classification of stealth submarines in complex underwater environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges unique to military acoustics. Modern undersea warfare requires overcoming significant limitations in existing sonar systems, particularly in cluttered coastal regions where multipath interference, biologics, and anthropogenic noise degrade detection accuracy. Traditional methods, optimized for open-ocean scenarios, struggle to adapt to these dynamic conditions, necessitating novel computational approaches. The research will focus on simulating high-fidelity acoustic propagation models under diverse environmental parameters (e.g., bathymetry, salinity gradients, sediment layers) and integrating machine learning (ML) techniques to isolate target signatures from confounding noise. HPC resources will enable large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to train deep neural networks on synthetic and experimentally validated datasets, optimizing robustness against adversarial conditions such as echo-reduction coatings or decoy deployment. Key computational tasks include finite element modeling of transient acoustic wave interactions, parallelized processing of multi-static sonar array data, and real-time classification algorithm development. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for adaptive sonar signal processing, validated against classified field data, capable of improving detection probabilities in contested littoral zones. This work bridges gaps between theoretical acoustics, computational engineering, and tactical military requirements, offering a pathway to next-generation antisubmarine warfare systems. The HPC component is critical due to the exponential computational demands of 3D wave propagation modeling and ML training, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters. By advancing both algorithmic efficiency and physical modeling accuracy, this project aims to deliver actionable tools for undersea domain awareness while contributing open-source computational methodologies to the broader acoustics community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of acoustics and signals processing to undersea and antisubmarine warfare. Includes instruction in acoustics; electrical engineering; the generation, propagation and reception of underwater sound waves; military applications of underwater sound; and acoustic signal processing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the socio-spatial dynamics of ancient maritime networks in the Mediterranean Basin (3000–500 BCE), integrating archaeological, environmental, and textual data to model how seafaring communities navigated ecological and political uncertainties. Traditional approaches to maritime interaction have relied on static distribution maps of artifacts or isolated site analyses, limiting our understanding of how transient phenomena—such as seasonal trade winds, shifting political alliances, or episodic resource scarcity—shaped collective decision-making. The research problem centers on reconstructing adaptive strategies that enabled resilience in premodern seafaring societies, with a focus on computational modeling of multi-scalar interactions between environmental variables, material exchanges, and social networks. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate sailor decision-making under variable constraints, geospatial network analysis to map connectivity patterns from amphora distribution data, and natural language processing (NLP) to extract temporal and relational cues from fragmented textual sources (e.g., Linear B tablets, Phoenician trade records). HPC resources are critical for iteratively running large-scale ABM simulations with high-resolution paleoenvironmental datasets (e.g., sea-level reconstructions, paleoclimate proxies) and processing 3D artifact scans from 40+ coastal sites. Expected outcomes include a dynamic, open-access visualization platform that synthesizes archaeological and environmental data into interactive spatiotemporal models, revealing how decentralized knowledge-sharing practices mitigated systemic risks in ancient maritime economies. The project advances interdisciplinary methodologies in computational archaeology while contributing to broader social science debates on human adaptation to environmental volatility, offering analogical insights for contemporary discussions on sustainable resource distribution and decentralized governance. By situating archaeological data within a computational social science framework, this work bridges humanities-focused material analysis with quantitative models of collective behavior, establishing a template for HPC-driven research in understudied niches of social complexity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures with a focus on the humanistic aspects of archaeology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized, real-time biomechanical models for optimizing assistive mobility devices in patients with neuromuscular impairments. Current assistive devices, such as orthoses and exoskeletons, often rely on static, population-averaged biomechanical parameters, leading to suboptimal fit, reduced patient adherence, and incomplete functional recovery. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating dynamic motion capture data, electromyography (EMG) signals, and finite element modeling to simulate patient-specific neuromuscular responses under diverse movement conditions. The research problem centers on the computational scalability required to process high-dimensional datasets (e.g., terabyte-scale motion/EMG time series) and resolve complex, nonlinear interactions between device mechanics and biological tissues in real time. Our approach combines GPU-accelerated finite element analysis for simulating tissue-device stress distributions with machine learning algorithms trained to predict adaptive device configurations based on individualized motor patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized optimization of device parameters across thousands of simulated scenarios, reducing iterative design cycles from months to days. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific device blueprints and a predictive model linking neuromuscular variability to optimal assistive torque profiles. This work bridges computational biomechanics, embedded systems design, and clinical rehabilitation, offering a transformative tool for allied health practitioners to prescribe dynamically adaptive assistive technologies. Successful implementation could reduce device abandonment rates by 30–40% in target populations while establishing a scalable computational methodology applicable to other personalized medical devices.
cip_title: Allied Health and Medical Assisting Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health and medical assisting services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives across East Asian diasporic communities through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in area studies: the lack of systematic, computationally driven frameworks to trace how collective identities and transnational cultural practices are negotiated in diaspora-produced media, including literature, film, and digital archives. Traditional methods struggle to process the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources, which span Chinese, Japanese, and Korean diaspora communities and incorporate mixed-language texts, visual symbolism, and multimedia elements. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for classical and modern East Asian languages, alongside computer vision techniques to detect recurring visual motifs in film and art. Custom transformer-based architectures will be trained to identify cross-cultural thematic shifts in multilingual corpora, while graph neural networks will map the diffusion of narratives across temporal and geographic boundaries. Computational demands include parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, fine-tuning multilingual embeddings, and simulating cultural transmission dynamics. Outcomes will include an open-access repository of annotated diasporic media, a computational toolkit for interdisciplinary cultural analysis, and new theoretical insights into the interplay of tradition and adaptation in East Asian diasporas. By integrating HPC-driven methods with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to establish a replicable model for data-intensive area studies research, bridging qualitative scholarship and scalable computational approaches. The requested resources will enable processing of historically fragmented materials at unprecedented resolution, advancing both regional studies and methodological innovation in digital humanities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of East Asia, defined as including China, Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Taiwan, Tibet, related borderlands and island groups, and including the study of the East Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize operational efficiency and emissions control in fossil fuel and nuclear power plants, with a focus on addressing thermal stress dynamics in turbine systems and real-time pollutant mitigation. Power plant operations require precise balancing of energy output, equipment longevity, and regulatory compliance, yet existing models often oversimplify transient thermal gradients in turbine blades or rely on static assumptions about combustion byproduct dispersion. The research will employ multiphysics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization to characterize heat transfer, material fatigue, and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system performance under variable load conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve 3D transient simulations of turbine blade erosion patterns, coupled with reactor core thermal-hydraulic interactions in nuclear systems, at timescales spanning milliseconds to operational cycles. A parallelized workflow will combine OpenFOAM for turbulent flow modeling, MOOSE Framework for thermomechanical stress analysis, and custom Python-based optimizers to identify operating thresholds that minimize NOx/SOx emissions while maintaining grid stability. Datasets from three operational power plants will validate model outputs. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms for turbine assemblies, dynamic SCR control templates to reduce reagent waste by 15-20%, and generalized thermal stress mitigation protocols applicable to next-generation reactor designs. This work directly supports workforce training in power plant instrumentation and industrial controls by generating open-access simulation case studies for academic use. The requested computing allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ core-hour simulations, which are infeasible on local clusters due to memory-intensive meshing requirements for rotating machinery geometries. Results will advance scalable computational tools for power generation infrastructure, aligning with national priorities for grid reliability and emissions reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: Traditional methods for designing and testing structural iron components rely heavily on physical prototyping and empirical data, leading to prolonged development cycles and increased costs. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models for simulating the behavior of iron structures under diverse mechanical and environmental conditions. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) models to predict stress distribution, deformation, and failure points in complex structural configurations, including welded joints and ornamental designs, and (2) employing machine learning algorithms to optimize material usage and structural efficiency while adhering to safety codes and standards. The computational workflows will integrate multiphysics simulations, accounting for dynamic loads such as wind, seismic activity, and thermal expansion, as well as material heterogeneity introduced during fabrication processes. By utilizing parallel computing architectures, the project aims to reduce simulation times from weeks to hours, enabling rapid iterative design improvements. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for structural performance, data-driven guidelines for reinforcing critical junctions, and open-source tools tailored for ironworking professionals to simulate designs prior to fabrication. This research will directly enhance the precision and sustainability of ironworking practices, reducing material waste and improving compliance with evolving safety regulations. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the scale of parametric studies and high-resolution simulations required to achieve these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to make and install structural, ornamental, and reinforcing metal structures and supports. Includes instruction in drafting, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, welding, riveting, beam placement, ornamental design, structural reinforcement, crane operation, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize operational decision-making in multi-location restaurant enterprises through advanced computational modeling, addressing the challenge of dynamically balancing resource allocation, supply chain logistics, and labor management across geographically distributed operations. Traditional management approaches often struggle to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating consumer demand, perishable inventory constraints, and staff scheduling conflicts at scale. The project will develop a high-performance computing (HPC) framework integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to simulate complex operational scenarios. Agent-based models will represent individual restaurant units, suppliers, and customer behavior patterns, while discrete-event simulations will map cross-location interactions and resource flows. Machine learning components will analyze historical sales data, weather patterns, and local event calendars to predict demand surges and inventory requirements. The computational intensity of simultaneously modeling hundreds of interconnected agents and supply chain networks necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing food waste through just-in-time inventory systems, adaptive staffing algorithms that comply with labor regulations across jurisdictions, and scenario-testing capabilities for emergency preparedness (e.g., supply chain disruptions). The research will produce an open-source computational toolkit tailored for culinary management applications, bridging gaps between operations research and hospitality-specific constraints. By enabling data-driven decision-making at enterprise scale, this work aims to establish computational modeling as a transformative methodology in culinary management, with potential applications in sustainability initiatives and crisis response planning for the food service industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage food and beverage preparation and service operations, restaurant facilities, and catering services.  Includes instruction in food/beverage industry operations, cost control, purchasing and storage, business administration, logistics, personnel management, culinary arts, restaurant and menu planning, executive chef functions, event planning and management, health and safety, insurance, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision pharmacotherapy by optimizing drug dosing and therapeutic outcomes in complex clinical populations. A critical challenge in clinical pharmacy is the interindividual variability in drug response, driven by factors such as genetic polymorphisms, comorbidities, polypharmacy, and organ dysfunction. Traditional pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models often fail to account for these multidimensional interactions, leading to suboptimal dosing recommendations and increased risks of adverse events or therapeutic failure. To address this, we propose the development of a machine learning-enhanced, multi-scale modeling framework integrating real-world patient data from electronic health records (EHRs), genomic datasets, and dynamic physiological parameters. The computational workflow will involve (1) natural language processing (NLP) of unstructured clinical notes to extract medication histories and comorbidities, (2) Bayesian hierarchical modeling to quantify covariate effects on drug disposition, and (3) neural network architectures predicting individualized dosing thresholds based on simulated patient trajectories. Large-scale parallelization will be required for parameter estimation across heterogeneous virtual patient cohorts and sensitivity analyses of dosing protocols under diverse physiological scenarios. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate drug-receptor interactions in patients with rare genetic variants affecting drug metabolism. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this project aims to generate validated, adaptive dosing algorithms for high-risk medications such as anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, and oncology therapies. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for model-informed precision dosing, risk stratification dashboards for clinical pharmacists, and a computational framework adaptable to emerging therapeutics. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the integration of multi-omics data with real-time PK simulations—necessitates access to high-memory nodes and GPU clusters to achieve clinically actionable timelines. Successful implementation will directly support safer, more effective medication management in hospital and managed care settings while establishing scalable methodologies for computational pharmacy research.
cip_title: Clinical, Hospital, and Managed Care Pharmacy
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to deliver specialized pharmacy services and produce pharmaceutical products in clinical settings in conjunction with other health care professionals. Includes instruction in biostatistics; clinical pharmacokinetics; biopharmaceutics; neuropharmacology; pharmacodynamics; drug metabolism; clinical sampling and research design; drug delivery systems; chemotherapy; pharmacotherapy; clinical pharmacy management; medical and research ethics; and applications to nuclear, nutrition support, oncology, psychiatric, and therapeutic pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in modeling large-scale, algorithmically generated musical compositions and analyzing their structural coherence. Current approaches to automated music generation and analysis often rely on simplified harmonic or rhythmic models, which struggle to capture the complexity of human-composed works—particularly in advanced domains such as polyphonic counterpoint, spectral harmony, or real-time improvisation systems. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework that integrates symbolic AI (for rule-based tonal and formal structures) with machine learning models (trained on diverse corpora of 20th-21st century art music) to simulate and evaluate compositional processes. The core research problem involves optimizing these models to operate across multiple temporal scales, from micro-level timbral manipulations to macro-formal development, while maintaining auditive plausibility and stylistic consistency. HPC resources will be critical for three components: (1) parallelized training of transformer-based architectures on high-resolution MIDI and audio datasets encompassing complex orchestral textures; (2) real-time rendering of physically modeled instrument interactions in virtual ensembles; and (3) evolutionary algorithms for stress-testing harmonic progressions against psychoacoustic constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational music theory research, a repository of algorithmically generated works demonstrating previously undocumented harmonic-contrapuntal configurations, and quantitative metrics for assessing computational creativity in music systems. By enabling the synthesis and analysis of music at unprecedented complexity levels, this work aims to advance both pedagogical tools for composition students and methodological frameworks for studying emergent musical structures through computational means.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the principles of sound manipulation as applied to the creation of music, and the techniques of creating and arranging music. Includes instruction in aural theory, melody, counterpoint, complex harmony, modulation, chromatics, improvisation, progressions, musical writing, instrumentation, orchestration, electronic and computer applications, studies of specific musical styles, and development of original creative ability.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing multiphysics systems in advanced manufacturing processes, where concurrent thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamics phenomena create complex, nonlinear interactions. Traditional simulation tools struggle to resolve these coupled processes at industrially relevant scales due to prohibitive computational costs, limiting the design and operational efficiency of systems such as additive manufacturing platforms, composite material curing systems, and energy-intensive thermal processing units. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a parallelized finite element method (FEM) solver enhanced with adaptive mesh refinement and machine learning-driven surrogate models. The solver will integrate open-source libraries, including PETSc and Deal.II, to exploit distributed-memory architectures for large-scale simulations. Machine learning components will accelerate parameter space exploration by predicting optimal mesh configurations and reducing the need for full-order model evaluations. Key computational challenges include managing memory bottlenecks during multiphysics data transfers, optimizing load balancing across >10,000 CPU cores, and validating results against experimental datasets from collaborative industry partners. The outcomes will enable high-fidelity simulations of manufacturing systems with sub-millimeter spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution, a 50–100x improvement over current capabilities. This will directly support the design of energy-efficient industrial processes, reducing material waste and carbon footprints in sectors such as aerospace and renewable energy component fabrication. The resulting open-source tools will be disseminated to academic and industrial users, fostering broader adoption of HPC-driven optimization in engineering. Resource requests include 200,000 node-hours on a GPU-accelerated cluster for solver development and 50 TB of storage for managing multiphysics datasets and surrogate model training.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical laboratory science faces growing challenges in integrating multi-dimensional datasets—including genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and clinical data—to advance precision diagnostics and therapeutic monitoring. Current analytical workflows struggle to process these heterogeneous, high-volume datasets efficiently, limiting real-time insights for critical applications such as sepsis prediction, autoimmune disorder stratification, or therapeutic drug monitoring. This project seeks to address these bottlenecks by developing scalable computational pipelines optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The research will focus on creating machine learning models to identify biomarkers from multi-omics data and clinical laboratory parameters, coupled with dynamic simulations of disease progression pathways. Computational methods will include parallelized feature selection algorithms, GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for temporal lab data), and agent-based modeling of host-pathogen interactions. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from consortium partnerships with three academic medical centers, reducing analysis times from weeks to hours compared to current workstation-based approaches. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for early detection of sepsis in ICU patients using longitudinal lab metrics, (2) a publicly accessible containerized workflow for clinical omics integration, and (3) mechanistic insights into metabolic dysregulation patterns in autoimmune diseases. By leveraging distributed memory architectures and optimized resource allocation strategies, this work will establish a framework for resource-efficient analysis of complex laboratory datasets. The resulting tools and models will be disseminated through CLIA-certified laboratory partnerships, directly informing clinical decision support systems and broadening access to advanced computational methods in routine diagnostic practice. This project underscores the critical role of HPC in bridging translational gaps between laboratory medicine research and real-world clinical implementation.
cip_title: Clinical/ Medical Laboratory Science and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical/medical laboratory science and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the computational modeling of advanced materials for next-generation engineering applications, with a focus on optimizing performance under extreme thermal and mechanical conditions. Traditional experimental approaches to material design are time-intensive and costly, particularly when targeting multifunctional composites or high-entropy alloys. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) calculations. These methods will enable atomic-resolution analysis of stress distribution, phase transitions, and defect propagation in candidate materials, while machine learning algorithms will accelerate the identification of optimal compositional profiles from terabyte-scale datasets. The computational workflow integrates open-source tools (LAMMPS, Quantum ESPRESSO) with custom Python-based analysis pipelines to correlate microstructural features with macroscopic properties. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for DFT benchmarks and distributed-memory CPU clusters for MD simulations exceeding 10 million atoms. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for two novel material systems: (1) lightweight ceramic-metal composites for hypersonic vehicle thermal protection and (2) radiation-resistant alloys for nuclear fusion reactor components. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error prototyping, this work will directly advance the development of materials capable of operating in extreme environments while establishing reproducible computational protocols for the broader engineering community. The requested resources will also support the training of undergraduate researchers in parallel computing techniques through hands-on participation in simulation campaigns and data visualization tasks. Results will be disseminated through three peer-reviewed publications and integrated into a public database of material property predictions to inform future experimental studies.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical and neuromuscular mechanisms underlying human movement pathologies, with applications to injury prevention, rehabilitation, and performance optimization. Current computational models of musculoskeletal dynamics often lack the resolution to capture multiscale interactions between tissue-level mechanics, neural control strategies, and real-world movement variability. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing high-fidelity simulations of human motion using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate subject-specific biomechanical data (motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging) with multibody dynamics modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate complex movements under diverse physiological conditions. A key focus will be modeling impaired motor control in populations with neurological disorders or musculoskeletal injuries, as well as optimizing exercise interventions for rehabilitation. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to assess sensitivity of movement outcomes to variations in muscle activation patterns, joint loading, and environmental constraints, as well as the training of neural networks to predict optimal therapeutic exercise parameters. Expected outcomes include novel computational frameworks for personalized rehabilitation protocol design, improved predictive models of injury risk during dynamic tasks, and mechanistic insights into motor adaptation processes. This work will directly support the development of evidence-based therapeutic tools and contribute to advancing precision medicine in kinesiology. The requested computing resources are essential given the computational intensity of solving inverse dynamics problems across thousands of simulated trials, processing high-resolution tissue deformation datasets, and running parallelized optimization algorithms for movement pattern identification. By bridging gaps between theoretical biomechanics and clinical practice, this research aligns with the program’s mission to innovate diagnostic and rehabilitative methodologies through advanced analytical approaches.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized oral health interventions for geriatric patients, who often present with complex comorbidities, polypharmacy, and age-related physiological changes that complicate treatment outcomes. Current clinical decision-making frameworks lack robust computational tools to integrate multi-dimensional data—such as electronic health records, intraoral imaging, genomic profiles, and longitudinal behavioral data—into predictive models tailored for aging populations. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models and biomechanical simulations that account for the interplay between systemic health, oral microbiome dynamics, and therapeutic efficacy. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) large-scale data harmonization and feature extraction from heterogeneous clinical datasets using natural language processing and deep learning-based image analysis; (2) ensemble ML model training to predict risks of post-procedural complications, caries recurrence, and periodontal disease progression; and (3) finite element simulations to assess biomechanical stress distribution in geriatric-specific dental restorations under varying bone density and occlusal load conditions. These simulations will inform material selection and procedural adaptations for fragile dentition. By utilizing HPC capabilities for parallelized model training, hyperparameter optimization, and high-fidelity biomechanical modeling, this work aims to generate actionable clinical tools that enhance preventive strategies, reduce iatrogenic risks, and improve long-term oral health outcomes in geriatric patients. The expected outcomes include open-source predictive algorithms validated against multi-center geriatric dental cohorts and simulation-derived guidelines for restorative procedures in atrophic jaw environments. This research will directly contribute to advancing precision geriatric dentistry, reducing healthcare costs associated with trial-and-error treatments, and establishing scalable computational frameworks for aging-related oral health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of geriatric patients. Includes instruction in aging, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, geriatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and patient management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of durable, energy-efficient roofing systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of material performance under dynamic environmental conditions. Current roofing systems face challenges in balancing structural resilience, thermal efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, particularly as climate extremes intensify. While field testing remains critical, computational modeling can accelerate the evaluation of novel materials (e.g., advanced polymer composites, reflective coatings) and structural designs by simulating decades of weather exposure, load stresses, and thermal cycling in reduced timeframes. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution across roofing layers under wind, hail, and snow loads, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to assess water drainage efficiency and wind uplift resistance. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs and real-world failure datasets to predict degradation pathways and optimize material configurations. A key innovation is the integration of multi-physics simulations to evaluate how thermal expansion mismatches between roofing components accelerate fatigue. HPC resources are essential to resolve these multi-scale interactions, which involve millions of mesh elements and require parallelized solvers for transient analyses. Expected outcomes include validated models correlating simulated performance with empirical data from partner roofing manufacturers, a decision-support framework for material selection based on regional climate risks, and prototype designs for modular roofing assemblies with embedded sensor data points. The project will contribute open-access datasets on material failure thresholds, supporting updates to industry standards (e.g., ASTM International) and vocational training modules. By reducing trial-and-error in roofing system development, this work aims to lower building lifecycle costs, improve urban climate resilience, and inform code-compliant retrofitting strategies for aging infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare, install, and maintain exterior roofing materials and roofs. Includes instruction in building materials, flashing, lag bolts, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, layering, site preparation, basic internal structural design, finishing, waterproofing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The development of advanced polymeric materials with tailored properties for sustainable applications remains a critical challenge in plastics and polymer engineering. Current experimental approaches to optimize polymer formulations and processing parameters are time-intensive and lack the resolution to predict nanoscale interactions that govern macroscopic material behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model polymer systems at multiple scales, enabling the rational design of materials with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and environmental performance. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) simulating polymerization kinetics and chain dynamics using molecular dynamics (MD) and coarse-grained Monte Carlo methods to predict molecular weight distributions and branching behavior, and (2) employing finite element analysis (FEA) to model polymer melt flow during extrusion and injection molding processes under varying thermal and shear conditions. These computational studies will be validated against experimental data from collaborator laboratories, including rheological measurements and spectroscopic characterization. The scale of simulations—involving systems with over 10^6 particles and multi-physics coupling—necessitates access to parallelized computing architectures and GPU-accelerated nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for structure-process-property relationships in industrial polymers, with direct applications to biodegradable packaging materials and high-strength recyclable composites. By reducing trial-and-error prototyping, this work aims to accelerate the development of sustainable polymer technologies while minimizing resource consumption. The generated datasets and open-source simulation tools will be shared with the broader polymer engineering community to foster collaborative innovation in material science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using industrial polymers. Includes instruction in the principles of macromolecular chemistry, polymerization and plastic manufacturing processes and equipment, design and operational testing procedures, equipment maintenance and repair procedures, safety procedures, applications to specific products, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of mechanical systems demands advanced computational tools to optimize design accuracy and efficiency in mechanical drafting and CAD/CADD workflows. Current simulation methods for multi-physics systems—such as thermally stressed components or fluid-structure interactions—often face scalability limitations due to high computational costs, restricting the resolution, realism, and iterative potential of virtual prototypes. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges by enabling large-scale, high-fidelity simulations critical for next-generation mechanical design. The research will focus on developing a parallelized computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model multi-physics scenarios inherent in industrial applications, such as aerospace components or energy systems. Custom algorithms will automate mesh refinement and parameter optimization across distributed computing nodes, while machine learning models trained on simulation data will predict optimal geometric tolerancing strategies to reduce manual iterations. The HPC environment will allow for parametric studies at unprecedented scales, evaluating thousands of design variants under dynamic loading conditions to identify failure-prone configurations and improve compliance with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) standards. Expected outcomes include a reduction in computational time for complex assemblies by 40–60% compared to single-node workflows, validated through case studies involving turbine blade and heat exchanger designs. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular code templates to bridge gaps between academic CAD training and industry HPC practices. By enhancing the precision and scalability of virtual prototyping, this work aims to accelerate innovation in mechanical systems, reduce physical testing costs, and equip students with skills in high-performance computational drafting, aligning educational outcomes with emerging industry needs.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing resource allocation in early childhood education (ECE) programs through advanced computational modeling. ECE administrators face complex decisions in balancing budgetary constraints, staffing needs, facility utilization, and regulatory compliance while maintaining program quality and accessibility. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating enrollment, evolving policy requirements, and socioeconomic disparities. This research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to model multi-dimensional resource allocation scenarios across diverse ECE settings. The computational approach will integrate demographic data, funding structures, staff qualifications, and facility capacities into agent-based models that simulate program operations under varying constraints. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical program outcomes to identify patterns in resource utilization efficiency and predict the impact of administrative decisions on equity metrics. By leveraging parallel processing, the platform will enable rapid scenario testing for large-scale program networks, including sensitivity analyses of policy changes and disaster preparedness planning. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for administrators to visualize trade-offs between fiscal responsibility, regulatory adherence, and educational quality, with particular emphasis on underserved communities. The project will also generate scalable frameworks for evaluating state-level funding distribution models and workforce development investments. This work advances the field of education leadership by introducing computational social science methodologies to early childhood administration, offering empirically grounded strategies to enhance program sustainability and equitable access. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational complexity of simulating thousands of interdependent variables across heterogeneous program environments while maintaining the fidelity required for policy-relevant conclusions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on early childhood educational program administration and prepares individuals to serve as a principal or director of an early childhood educational program. Includes instruction in early childhood education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, early childhood growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing equitable, culturally responsive instructional strategies in multilingual K-12 classrooms through advanced computational modeling. Current approaches to curriculum adaptation for culturally diverse learners often rely on static frameworks that inadequately capture the dynamic interplay of language acquisition, cultural identity, and individualized learning trajectories. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) simulating classroom interactions across diverse cultural and linguistic profiles. These models will integrate anonymized student performance data, sociolinguistic surveys, and ethnographic classroom observations from partner school districts serving predominantly immigrant and refugee populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to account for complex variables, including code-switching patterns, cross-cultural communication dynamics, and the impact of culturally grounded pedagogical interventions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive relationships between instructional strategies and learning outcomes across simulated student subgroups. The computational pipeline will also leverage natural language processing to analyze multilingual student writing samples, enabling real-time feedback systems for teachers. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating data-driven, adaptive lesson plans that respond to classroom cultural composition, as well as evidence-based guidelines for deploying educational technologies in linguistically diverse settings. By modeling how cultural context mediates learning processes at scale, this work aims to advance teacher preparation programs’ capacity to address systemic inequities in multicultural education. The requested HPC resources will support parallelized simulation runs, large-scale sentiment analysis of student narratives, and optimization of hybrid human-AI teaching frameworks tailored to underrepresented cultural groups.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, and implementation of instructional and advising services for culturally diverse learning populations. Includes instruction in cultural diversity, at-risk populations, multilingual and ESL education, program and curriculum design, instructional technology, information resources, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling and communicating with multicultural populations, law and regulations, and applications to specific cultural groups, educational services, and research issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to enhance the real-time fusion and analysis of multi-modal signals intelligence (SIGINT) and geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) data streams in contested electromagnetic environments. Modern military operations increasingly rely on integrating disparate sensor inputs—including radar, acoustic arrays, and overhead synthetic aperture systems—to detect and characterize adversarial threats. However, existing processing pipelines struggle with latency, scalability, and adaptability when handling heterogeneous data types across distributed, low-bandwidth networks. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in time-critical signal exploitation, particularly in scenarios involving spectral congestion, adaptive adversary waveforms, and degraded sensor conditions. The proposed approach combines graph-based sensor fusion architectures with machine learning models trained on synthetic and operational datasets to enable autonomous signal prioritization, anomaly detection, and probabilistic source attribution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be leveraged to 1) simulate multi-domain electromagnetic battlefields using wave propagation models, 2) optimize parallelized processing chains for GPU-accelerated tensor operations, and 3) validate adaptive algorithms through large-scale synthetic aperture radar (SAR) coherence analysis and multi-static signal triangulation experiments.
