Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for dynamic resource allocation in edge computing environments, improved temporal resolution in wide-area persistent surveillance workflows, and quantifiable reductions in decision latency for electromagnetic order-of-battle assessments. By advancing computational methods for joint SIGINT/GEOINT correlation under constrained bandwidth conditions, this work aims to establish new paradigms for resilient intelligence processing architectures that align with emerging joint all-domain command and control requirements. The resulting frameworks will be stress-tested against operational datasets representing contested logistics corridors and dense urban signal environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational aspects of collecting, processing and exploiting remote-sensed, radar, acoustic and other forms of signals intelligence. Includes instruction in applied physics, wave propagation and capture, radar systems, acoustics and underwater systems, infrared systems, synthetic aperture systems, collection and processing systems, signal phenomenology, signal analysis and exploitation, and applications to specific intelligence problems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic resource allocation for large-scale construction projects, where traditional heuristic methods fail to account for real-time disruptions, multi-stakeholder interactions, and sustainability constraints. The central challenge lies in optimizing labor, equipment, and material flows under stochastic variables such as weather delays, supply chain volatility, and evolving regulatory requirements. To overcome computational limitations of existing commercial project management software, we propose developing an adaptive decision-support framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The model will integrate agent-based simulations to capture subcontractor behaviors, Monte Carlo methods to quantify cascading risks, and reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine allocation strategies across parallelized scenarios. Key innovations include embedding carbon-cost trade-off analytics into optimization objectives and incorporating real-time IoT data streams from construction sites to enable responsive replanning. The HPC environment will facilitate processing of high-dimensional datasets (e.g., 4D BIM models, supplier lead times, OSHA incident reports) while maintaining computational feasibility for projects exceeding 10,000 interdependent tasks. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for quantifying the financial and operational impacts of dynamic resource policies, predictive models for bottleneck mitigation, and open-source tools compatible with existing construction management platforms. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resource allocation that balances economic, safety, and sustainability KPIs in complex projects, with potential applications in disaster recovery infrastructure and net-zero building initiatives. By bridging computational engineering and operations research within the construction management domain, the project addresses a critical gap in business-oriented decision tools for the built environment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches for managing complex, multimorbid conditions in adult patients within general internal medicine. Despite the prevalence of chronic diseases such as diabetes, heart failure, and autoimmune disorders, optimizing individualized treatment plans remains challenging due to the high-dimensional interactions between patient-specific factors (e.g., genetic predispositions, comorbidities, polypharmacy, and behavioral patterns). Traditional statistical methods often fail to model these nonlinear relationships or dynamically adjust recommendations based on evolving clinical data. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) with mechanistic physiological models to predict treatment responses and adverse event risks. The project will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 250,000+ patients, including longitudinal lab results, medication histories, and patient-reported outcomes, alongside genomic and proteomic datasets where available. Deep neural networks will be trained to identify latent patterns in treatment efficacy, while reinforcement learning algorithms will simulate adaptive decision-making strategies for escalating or de-escalating therapies. Graph-based models will map interactions between coexisting conditions and medications to quantify risk-benefit tradeoffs. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for hyperparameter optimization, Monte Carlo simulations to address clinical uncertainty, and real-time inference capabilities for eventual integration into clinical decision support tools. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for 3-5 high-burden disease clusters, open-source tools for dynamic treatment regimen optimization, and novel insights into modifiable behavioral factors influencing therapeutic success. By enabling data-driven personalization of care plans, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error prescribing, mitigate adverse drug events, and improve quality-of-life metrics for medically complex patients. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational scale, speed, and reproducibility for translating these models into clinically actionable solutions.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of general medical services to adult patients with a wide range of non-surgical clinical problems. May included related research in behavioral aspects of diseases, patient and family counseling and practice management.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable water management systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize wastewater treatment and recycling processes. Current challenges include accurately modeling complex biological and chemical interactions within treatment systems, predicting contaminant removal efficiency under variable operational conditions, and scaling laboratory-derived process parameters to full-scale implementations. This project proposes to develop a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through three primary objectives: (1) simulating hydrodynamic behavior and mass transfer in membrane filtration systems using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with adaptive mesh refinement, (2) parameterizing biofilm growth and nutrient degradation kinetics in bioreactors via agent-based modeling coupled with machine learning optimization, and (3) validating predictive models for emerging contaminant removal through ensemble molecular dynamics simulations of adsorption processes. The computational workflow will integrate open-source solvers (OpenFOAM, LAMMPS) with custom Python-based analytics pipelines to process terabyte-scale simulation outputs. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution for capturing microscale biofilm dynamics (μm-scale over 100+ hours) while maintaining system-scale predictive capability. Expected outcomes include optimized membrane module designs reducing energy consumption by 15-20%, validated operational thresholds for biofilm-based nutrient recovery systems, and predictive tools for selecting adsorbent materials targeting pharmaceutical residues in recycled water. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation treatment plants with enhanced recycling capacity, addressing critical gaps in water scarcity mitigation. The developed models and datasets will be made available through a public repository to support workforce training in computational water quality management.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: Critically ill patients with acute life-threatening conditions often exhibit complex, dynamic physiological derangements that challenge conventional predictive models. Current approaches to risk stratification and treatment optimization in critical care lack the computational power to integrate high-dimensional data streams—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biosensor data, medical imaging, and multi-omics profiles—into actionable clinical insights. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for real-time, multi-organ failure prediction and personalized therapeutic decision support. Leveraging machine learning techniques such as ensemble models and recurrent neural networks, combined with mechanistic modeling using differential equations, we will analyze heterogeneous datasets from ICU patients to identify early signatures of clinical deterioration. HPC resources will be essential for training deep learning architectures on terabyte-scale data, simulating organ-system interactions via computationally intensive numerical solvers, and optimizing treatment protocols through parallelized in silico trials. The resulting models aim to predict the onset of sepsis-associated organ dysfunction, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and circulatory shock with greater accuracy than existing scores, while dynamically recommending individualized fluid, vasopressor, and ventilator strategies. Validation will occur through retrospective cohort analysis and prospective pilot implementation in a tertiary care ICU. This research has the potential to establish a new paradigm for data-driven critical care that adapts to patient trajectories at temporal resolutions previously unattainable, ultimately reducing mortality through earlier intervention. The computational infrastructure developed may serve as a template for other complex clinical decision-making environments requiring massive data integration and real-time analytics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the management of care for patients with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. Includes instruction in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures and post-discharge care of former critical care patients.

abstract: The increasing complexity of public infrastructure projects necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize design validation and material performance analysis in civil engineering technologies. Current empirical methods for evaluating composite materials, such as fiber-reinforced polymers (FRPs) used in bridge retrofitting, struggle to account for heterogeneous stress distributions and long-term environmental degradation. This project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model FRP-concrete interfacial behavior under multifactorial loading conditions, including thermal cycling and moisture ingress. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) coupling, we will simulate microscale material interactions across representative volume elements, scaling to full structural components through parallelized solvers. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning surrogates trained on experimental datasets to accelerate parameter optimization for bond strength and fatigue resistance. By leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times by 70% compared to existing commercial software, enabling probabilistic analysis of failure mechanisms across diverse climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for civil engineering technologists, capable of informing ASTM-compliant testing protocols and reducing physical prototyping costs by 40–60%. This work will directly enhance the precision of infrastructure rehabilitation plans, particularly for aging transportation systems in environmentally sensitive regions. The resource request supports 200,000 core-hours for initial model calibration and scalability testing, with iterative refinement cycles aligned with ongoing laboratory validations at our materials testing facility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of civil engineers engaged in designing and executing public works projects such as highways, dams, bridges, tunnels and other facilities. Includes instruction in site analysis, structural testing procedures, field and laboratory testing procedures, plan and specification preparation, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale textual and multimedia datasets documenting cultural expressions and identity formation within Southeast Asian diasporic communities. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital platforms mediate the preservation and transformation of intangible cultural heritage—such as oral traditions, performative arts, and vernacular narratives—among transnational populations. Existing studies lack computational tools to systematically trace the interplay between digital content creation, linguistic hybridity, and evolving notions of belonging across dispersed communities. By integrating computational text analysis, network mapping, and machine learning, this study will process multilingual corpora (including social media, digital archives, and community-generated repositories) to identify patterns of cultural adaptation and hybridity. Methods include training transformer-based models on low-resource Southeast Asian languages (e.g., Cham, Tetum, and minority Philippine languages) to detect semantic shifts in diasporic discourse, alongside graph-based analyses to visualize transnational knowledge-sharing networks. The computational workflow will utilize distributed processing for metadata-rich multimedia files and GPU-accelerated model training to handle non-Latin scripts and code-mixing phenomena. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated datasets, computational models tailored to underrepresented languages, and visual analytics tools for mapping cultural transmission pathways. This work will advance methodological innovation in area studies by bridging humanistic inquiry with scalable computational frameworks, offering new insights into how digital technologies shape cultural resilience in diaspora contexts. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the project’s data volume (estimated at 150 TB of unstructured text, audio, and video) and for executing computationally intensive tasks within feasible timeframes, enabling rigorous analysis of complex sociocultural dynamics at unprecedented scale.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Southeast Asia, defined as including Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, The Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Viet Nam; related borderlands and island groups; and including the study of migration patterns and overseas diasporas.

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and disorders, such as acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), exhibit complex molecular heterogeneity that complicates diagnosis, risk stratification, and therapeutic targeting. While multi-omics approaches (genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic) have expanded our understanding of these diseases, integrating large-scale datasets to identify clinically actionable patterns remains computationally prohibitive with standard infrastructure. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of disease progression and treatment response in AML/MDS by analyzing multi-modal data from 1,200 patients in the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Hematologic Malignancy Database. The computational workflow will employ machine learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) to integrate whole-exome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility profiles, and clinical outcomes data. Molecular dynamics simulations (using GROMACS and Amber) will model protein-DNA interactions for recurrent mutations in splicing factors (SF3B1, U2AF1) to assess their structural impact on RNA processing. Additionally, GPU-accelerated network analysis (Cytoscape, custom CUDA scripts) will reconstruct dysregulated signaling pathways driving clonal evolution. A key innovation is the development of a federated learning pipeline to securely incorporate data from three external medical centers without transferring sensitive patient records. The HPC environment is critical for managing the project’s estimated 450 TB of raw data, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks, and reducing model training times from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include (1) validated biomarkers for early detection of AML transformation in MDS, (2) a open-access computational toolkit for predicting patient-specific vulnerabilities to targeted therapies, and (3) mechanistic insights into how splicing factor mutations alter hematopoietic differentiation. These results will directly inform two planned clinical trials at our institution and provide a scalable framework for data-driven precision hematology. The requested resources will enable transformative analysis of datasets that are currently inaccessible with local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the mechanisms and therapy of diseases of the blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lymph, including patient management, diagnostic tests, biopsies, and other procedures.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable livestock production systems necessitates advanced genomic tools to optimize traits such as disease resistance, feed efficiency, and reproductive performance. While next-generation sequencing technologies have generated vast datasets linking genetic variation to phenotypic outcomes in livestock species, existing analytical workflows lack the computational scalability to integrate multi-omics data, environmental variables, and longitudinal production records. This project seeks to address this bottleneck by developing and deploying high-performance computing (HPC) pipelines to enable genome-to-phenome prediction models in cattle and swine populations. Leveraging existing whole-genome sequencing data from 10,000 animals and corresponding phenotype records, we will implement distributed computing frameworks to parallelize Bayesian mixed-model analyses and deep learning architectures. These models will quantify genotype-by-environment interactions and epistatic effects influencing complex traits, with iterative validation using independent datasets. The computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and MPI-based parallelization for variance component estimation in mixed models. Successful implementation will yield predictive algorithms capable of identifying optimal breeding candidates under diverse management scenarios, reducing the computational time for genomic evaluations from weeks to days. This work directly supports translational goals in precision livestock breeding, enabling data-driven strategies to enhance animal health and resource-efficient production. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the memory-intensive processing of terabyte-scale genomic datasets and the concurrent execution of thousands of stochastic simulations to quantify model uncertainty. Outcomes will be disseminated through open-source software packages and collaborative partnerships with agricultural extension networks, ensuring broad applicability across animal sciences research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the animal sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of traditional herbal medicine with modern molecular science remains underexplored, despite its widespread global use and potential for novel therapeutic discovery. This project addresses the critical gap in understanding the polypharmacological mechanisms of multi-herb formulations used in Traditional East Asian Medicine (TEAM) systems. While clinical studies suggest efficacy for conditions such as chronic inflammation and metabolic disorders, the combinatorial effects of phytochemical ensembles on cellular signaling networks remain computationally intractable with conventional methods. We propose a multi-scale computational framework to model herb-herb-target-pathway interactions using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Molecular docking simulations will screen 8,000+ phytochemicals from a curated database of 120 TEAM formulations against 320 human protein targets implicated in immunometabolic regulation. Network pharmacology analyses will map synergistic and antagonistic relationships between compounds, followed by dynamic simulations of prioritized multi-target systems using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) to characterize binding stability and conformational changes. A machine learning pipeline will then identify predictive patterns linking traditional formulation principles (e.g., herb pairing rules) to measurable bioactivity profiles. The computational workflow leverages GPU-accelerated docking (AutoDock-GPU), distributed MD (NAMD), and ensemble learning architectures (PyTorch), requiring 1.2 million core-hours and 40 TB of temporary storage for parallel batch processing. Expected outcomes include 1) the first quantitative map of cross-herb target modulation networks, 2) validated predictive models for formulation bioactivity, and 3) a public database of simulated herb-target interaction kinetics. This work establishes a computational bridge between empirical traditional medicine knowledge and systems biology, enabling data-driven optimization of integrative treatment strategies while preserving historical therapeutic paradigms. Results will directly inform ongoing preclinical studies of formulation safety and biomarker responses.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and optimize adaptive language learning systems for English and French as second languages (ESL/FSL), with a focus on addressing individual learner variability in under-resourced pedagogical contexts. While adaptive tutoring tools show promise in personalizing instruction, existing systems often lack the capacity to model nuanced, real-time interactions between learner error patterns, multilingual transfer effects, and instructional scaffolding strategies—particularly for learners from diverse linguistic backgrounds. The research problem centers on bridging this gap through advanced computational modeling of longitudinal learner data. The project will employ transformer-based neural architectures to process multimodal datasets (text, speech, and interaction logs) from ESL/FSL classrooms, coupled with reinforcement learning to simulate optimal feedback mechanisms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training multi-modal models on heterogeneous data streams while maintaining the temporal resolution required to track micro-level learning progressions. Computational experiments will compare the efficacy of dynamic parameterization approaches for error correction algorithms across phonology, syntax, and discourse-level challenges. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating adaptive lesson plans informed by learner-specific error trajectories and cross-linguistic interference profiles. This work aims to advance teacher education by providing empirically grounded computational methods to (1) diagnose persistent acquisition barriers and (2) automate the customization of pedagogical content in mixed-proficiency language classrooms. The requested resources will enable large-scale validation of models across six documented learner language corpora, totaling approximately 12TB of annotated interaction data. By integrating computational linguistics with second language acquisition theory, the project intends to establish new benchmarks for data-driven language pedagogy while addressing scalability challenges in teacher training programs serving multilingual populations.
cip_title: Teaching English or French as a Second or Foreign Language, Other
cip_definition: Any program in teaching English or French as a second or foreign language, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities investigation into the cultural dynamics of Francophone communities, with a focus on the interplay between colonial legacies and contemporary identity formation in French-speaking regions outside Europe. The research problem centers on analyzing vast, multilingual corpora of textual and visual materials—including colonial-era administrative records, post-independence literature, and digital media from Francophone Africa and the Caribbean—to trace how cultural hybridity and resistance are articulated across time and space. Traditional methods struggle to process the scale and linguistic diversity of these materials, which include digitized archives, social media datasets, and oral history transcripts in French, Creole, and Indigenous languages. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for low-resource languages, network analysis to map transnational cultural exchanges, and computer vision tools to study visual motifs in protest art and public memorials. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based language models on non-standard French variants, running large-scale topic modeling across century-spanning texts, and simulating the diffusion of cultural narratives through multilayer network algorithms. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative framework for measuring linguistic creolization in administrative documents, geotemporal visualizations of diasporic cultural memory, and open-access tools for decolonial text analysis. By computationally bridging historical and contemporary Francophone expressions, this work aims to reshape scholarly understandings of cultural survival in postcolonial contexts while centering marginalized voices in digital archives. The project directly contributes to French Studies’ interdisciplinary mission by innovating methodologies for analyzing power, identity, and representation at scales previously unattainable in humanities research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of France, other Francophone countries inside and outside Europe, and the French colonial experience and the associated French minorities around the world.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate computational modeling and simulation into the creation and analysis of complex metal artworks, addressing the challenge of optimizing material behavior, structural integrity, and aesthetic outcomes in advanced metalworking processes. Traditional methods in metal arts—such as casting, welding, and electroforming—rely heavily on iterative physical experimentation, which is time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in its ability to predict nuanced material interactions. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to develop predictive models for thermomechanical stresses during casting, electrochemical dynamics in anodizing and electroforming, and microstructural evolution in alloys under varying fabrication conditions. These simulations will employ finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning algorithms trained on empirical data from studio experiments. The project also explores generative design algorithms to iteratively refine 3D-printed metal sculptures, balancing geometric complexity with manufacturability constraints. Outcomes will include a library of open-source computational tools tailored to metal arts practitioners, enabling data-driven decision-making in studio practice. Additionally, the research will produce a series of hybrid digital-physical artworks that demonstrate the integration of computational insights with traditional craftsmanship. By bridging gaps between material science, computational engineering, and artistic practice, this work aims to expand the technical and expressive possibilities of metal arts while reducing material waste and energy consumption. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large-scale simulations of multi-physics processes and training neural networks on high-resolution imaging data of metal surfaces. This interdisciplinary approach positions computational methods as a transformative force in visual arts pedagogy and creative practice, fostering new dialogues between technology and handcrafted materiality.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of individual artistic expression and technical skills necessary for fabricating refined metal works. Includes instruction in aesthetics, anodizing, art history, casting, design, electroforming, enameling, metalsmithing, sculpture, two and three-dimensional design, wax carving, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of personalizing rehabilitation protocols for individuals with musculoskeletal impairments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Current approaches often apply generalized treatment plans, which fail to account for individual variability in anatomy, movement patterns, and tissue healing, leading to suboptimal recovery outcomes. To overcome this limitation, we propose a computational framework that combines patient-specific biomechanical simulations with predictive analytics to optimize rehabilitation strategies. Motion capture data, electromyography (EMG) recordings, and clinical imaging will inform finite element models of musculoskeletal dynamics, simulating the biomechanical effects of therapeutic exercises across diverse patient cohorts. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze longitudinal clinical data to identify predictors of recovery success. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations and the processing of high-dimensional datasets. The integration of these computational outputs will generate adaptive rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual biomechanical profiles and recovery trajectories. Expected outcomes include validated models that predict patient-specific responses to therapy, a decision-support tool for rehabilitation aides, and a deeper understanding of mechanobiological factors influencing recovery. This research bridges computational biomechanics and clinical rehabilitation, offering a novel paradigm to enhance precision in rehabilitative care. By reducing trial-and-error in therapy design, the project has the potential to accelerate functional recovery, minimize complications, and improve resource allocation in rehabilitation settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other therapeutic professionals, and to perform routine functions in support of rehabilitation. Includes instruction in roles and responsibilities of rehabilitation providers, basic function of the human body, disabling conditions, therapeutic skills, client management, and communication skills.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between Indigenous knowledge systems and colonial-era documentation across Pacific Island communities through large-scale computational analysis of multilingual archival materials. Existing research struggles to systematically trace how oral traditions, ecological practices, and artistic motifs were represented—and often distorted—in European administrative records, missionary accounts, and early anthropological collections. By employing high-performance computing resources, this study will process over 500,000 pages of digitized texts, images, and audio recordings from 19th- and 20th-century archives using transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource Pacific languages. Semantic segmentation algorithms will identify patterns of cultural translation and omission in colonial documents, while comparative network analysis will map the persistence of Indigenous conceptual frameworks related to land stewardship and kinship. A novel multimodal approach will correlate textual references with digitized tapa cloth designs and canoe schematics from museum collections, training vision-language models to detect symbolic continuities disrupted by colonial governance systems. The computational workflow requires GPU-accelerated processing for cross-lingual embeddings, graph-based knowledge representation, and probabilistic matching of oral narrative structures with written records. Outcomes will include an open-source repository of machine-readable cultural metadata, a visualization platform for tracking epistemic shifts, and methodological frameworks for ethically computationalizing Indigenous heritage materials. This work advances Pacific Studies by enabling systematic analysis of cultural representation across previously inaccessible archival scales while centering Indigenous perspectives on digital stewardship. The resource demands stem from parallelized processing of heterogeneous data types and iterative model training accommodating community feedback loops.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Australasia and the Pacific Ocean, related island groups and bordering coastal regions, and including pre- and post-colonial migration patterns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of cinematic form and its historical evolution across global film traditions. A central challenge in film and media studies is the systematic analysis of visual and narrative patterns at scale, particularly when examining large, heterogeneous corpora spanning decades or regions. Traditional close-reading methods, while foundational, struggle to quantify stylistic trends or map the diffusion of techniques across cultures and time. This research proposes a computational framework combining computer vision, deep learning, and spatial-temporal data modeling to analyze over 10,000 digitized films from archival collections, focusing on features such as shot composition, lighting, color dynamics, and editorial rhythm. Custom neural networks will be trained to detect and classify visual motifs, while graph-based models will trace the influence of specific techniques through director networks and production contexts. The scale of data—petabytes of high-resolution video requiring frame-level processing—demands HPC capabilities for parallelized training, distributed storage, and GPU-accelerated feature extraction. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking cinematic techniques to sociohistorical metadata, new quantitative models of stylistic evolution, and visualization tools for comparative media analysis. This work aims to bridge humanities scholarship and computational methods, offering film historians a dynamic platform to test theoretical claims about technological, aesthetic, and cultural exchange while preserving material at risk of degradation. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across previously unmanageable datasets, the project will expand methodologies in digital media studies and provide open-source tools for interdisciplinary research on visual culture.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program in the visual arts that focuses on the study of the history, development, theory, and criticism of the film/media arts, as well as the basic principles of filmmaking and film production.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative design frameworks for adaptive architectural systems that integrate cultural, environmental, and structural data. Traditional architectural design tools often prioritize static solutions or rely on simplified simulations, limiting their ability to address dynamic, context-specific challenges such as climate resilience, heritage preservation, and evolving urban needs. By situating this work within architectural sciences and technology, the research occupies an interdisciplinary niche bridging computational design, cultural analytics, and building performance optimization—areas not fully captured by conventional engineering or social science domains. The core problem lies in creating scalable algorithms capable of iterating through complex design spaces while balancing competing parameters: material efficiency, energy use, spatial functionality, and socio-cultural relevance. Computational methods will combine agent-based modeling to simulate human-building interactions, finite element analysis for structural and thermal dynamics, and machine learning to identify patterns in region-specific architectural heritage datasets. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing thousands of design iterations across variable climate scenarios and cultural constraints, enabling real-time multi-objective optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational workflow for generating context-adaptive architectural prototypes, validated against case studies in historically significant urban areas undergoing climate-driven transitions. The project aims to demonstrate how HPC-enabled generative design can expand architectural practice beyond reactive problem-solving toward proactive, data-informed creation of built environments that simultaneously address technical performance and cultural continuity. By formalizing methods to quantify and operationalize intangible cultural factors in computational design, this work contributes to emerging discourses on equitable technocultural transitions in architecture. Resource requests focus on GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning components and high-memory nodes for large-scale 3D parametric model evaluations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven computational framework to model and optimize pedagogical strategies for cosmetology and barbering education, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in instructor training methodologies. Current cosmetology instructor programs rely on generalized pedagogical frameworks that inadequately account for the dynamic, skill-based nature of hands-on grooming instruction. The research problem centers on the absence of adaptive, evidence-based models for teaching tactile techniques (e.g., precision haircutting, chemical texture services, nail artistry) that align with diverse student learning patterns and rapidly evolving industry standards. The computational approach integrates three components: (1) agent-based modeling of instructor-student interactions in simulated classroom/clinic environments, (2) machine learning analysis of longitudinal student performance data from accredited programs, and (3) discrete-event simulations of curriculum sequencing efficacy. High-resolution datasets will include motion-capture recordings of technical demonstrations, biometric feedback during practical assessments, and historical licensure outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of multimodal data streams (visual, kinetic, cognitive) while training neural networks to identify optimal instructional interventions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for personalizing teaching methods based on student skill progression rates, quantitative benchmarks for competency-based assessment, and generative AI tools to create adaptive lesson plans addressing regional licensing requirements. By establishing computational links between pedagogical strategies, psychomotor skill acquisition, and professional outcomes, this work aims to transform cosmetology instructor development through precision education models. The resulting open-access toolkit will support accredited programs in reducing attrition rates and improving licensure pass percentages while maintaining compliance with evolving state board regulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares cosmetologists, barbers, stylists, nail technicians, and other grooming specialists to teach their specializations in licensed and accredited schools of cosmetology and barbering, and to prepare for licensure as instructors.  Includes instruction in cosmetology arts and sciences teaching principles; student learning styles; professional curricula development; instructional planning; instructional methods and aids; student counseling and career assistance; test development; and classroom/clinic management.

abstract: Hematologic and coagulation disorders present complex diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, heterogeneous molecular profiles, and dynamic interactions between genetic, proteomic, and cellular pathways. Current laboratory methods for analyzing hematologic data—including genomic sequencing, flow cytometry, and coagulation assays—generate high-dimensional datasets that exceed the processing capacity of conventional computing infrastructure. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced computational models for multi-omics integration, predictive biomarker discovery, and dynamic simulation of coagulation cascades. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to identify subtype-specific genomic and proteomic signatures in leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and inherited bleeding disorders, and (2) employing molecular dynamics simulations to model aberrant protein interactions in thrombotic and hemorrhagic conditions. The computational workflows will integrate bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry-based proteomics, and clinical laboratory parameters using scalable data fusion algorithms. By deploying GPU-accelerated architectures, we will optimize time-intensive processes such as variational autoencoder training for dimensionality reduction and Markov state models for simulating fibrin polymerization kinetics. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, stratification algorithms for patient-specific anticoagulation management, and predictive models for laboratory test utilization optimization. This work addresses critical gaps in translating complex hematologic data into clinically actionable insights, with direct implications for diagnostic accuracy, treatment personalization, and resource efficiency in hematopathology laboratories. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale datasets, reducing computational bottlenecks in ensemble modeling, and enabling real-time analytics integration with institutional electronic health records.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory and analytical procedures for studying all facets of hematologic and coagulation disorders. May included related research in the management of hematology laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision nutrition by modeling the dynamic interplay between dietary interventions, metabolic heterogeneity, and gut microbiome-host interactions. Current nutrition guidelines often rely on population-level data, limiting their applicability to individuals with unique genetic, metabolic, or microbial profiles. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational tools to predict personalized responses to dietary patterns, particularly in complex chronic conditions like post-bariatric surgery nutrient malabsorption or inherited metabolic disorders. Using a multi-omics approach, we will integrate genomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic datasets from clinical cohorts to build agent-based models simulating nutrient processing across biological scales—from microbial community dynamics to systemic metabolic fluxes. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to identify predictive signatures of dietary responsiveness, incorporating longitudinal data on micronutrient status, inflammation markers, and microbiome resilience. The computational workflow requires HPC capabilities for large-scale parameter optimization, parallelized simulation of stochastic microbiome-nutrient interactions, and real-time adaptation of models using federated learning frameworks. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for simulating personalized dietary interventions, validated against clinical trial data, that enables dietitians to anticipate nutrient deficiencies or intolerances in vulnerable populations. This work will establish a foundation for computational dietetics—a novel interdisciplinary niche bridging systems biology and clinical nutrition—with potential to transform care paradigms in metabolic health, gerontology, and precision therapeutics. The scalability of the models will also inform institutional food service design for medically tailored meals, addressing a critical gap in healthcare infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to integrate and apply the principles of the food and nutrition sciences, human behavior, and the biomedical sciences to design and manage effective nutrition programs in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in human nutrition; nutrient metabolism; the role of foods and nutrition in health promotion and disease prevention; planning and directing food service activities; diet and nutrition analysis and planning; supervision of food storage and preparation; client education; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address a critical gap in the optimization of personalized neuromuscular rehabilitation protocols for individuals with movement disorders resulting from neurological injury or degenerative disease. While kinesiotherapy emphasizes therapeutic exercise tailored to individual needs, current protocols often rely on generalized guidelines that fail to account for the complex interplay of patient-specific biomechanical constraints, neural adaptation dynamics, and real-world functional demands. This project aims to develop a computational framework to model neuromuscular recovery pathways, enabling the design of adaptive, precision interventions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate multiscale biomechanical simulations with neural network-driven predictive analytics to resolve two challenges: (1) identifying optimal exercise parameters (intensity, frequency, movement patterns) that maximize neuroplasticity while minimizing injury risk, and (2) predicting longitudinal recovery trajectories based on individualized sensorimotor profiles. Computational methods will include finite element modeling of musculoskeletal stress distribution during therapeutic exercises, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms trained on synthetic and clinical datasets (motion capture, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes). Agent-based models will simulate neural adaptation processes across motor cortex reorganization and peripheral neuromuscular junction recovery. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-dimensional data from wearable sensors, scaling simulations across diverse anatomical variants, and iterating optimization algorithms within clinically relevant timeframes. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive toolset for clinicians to generate dynamically adjusted rehabilitation plans, validated through a virtual patient cohort representing heterogeneous pathologies (e.g., stroke, multiple sclerosis). This work will advance the evidence base for precision kinesiotherapy, reduce trial-and-error in rehabilitation design, and establish a computational paradigm for bridging neurorehabilitation theory with individualized therapeutic practice. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated workloads for deep learning components and parallelized biomechanical simulations across 10,000+ core-hours annually.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the direction of physicians, to treat the effects of disease, injury, and congenital disorders through therapeutic exercise and education. Includes instruction in human anatomy, human physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, therapeutic exercise and adapted physical education, human growth and development, motor learning and performance, testing and measurement, first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, psychology, rehabilitation procedures, patient assessment and management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of biomechanical dysfunction in diabetic foot syndrome (DFS), a leading cause of lower extremity morbidity. Current clinical assessments for DFS rely on static imaging and simplified gait models, which inadequately capture the dynamic, multiscale interactions between tissue degeneration, altered foot kinematics, and abnormal pressure distribution. We propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific finite element modeling (FEM) of foot architecture with machine learning-driven analysis of real-world inertial measurement unit (IMU) data from wearable sensors. The FEM component will simulate three-dimensional stress-strain distributions across plantar tissues under varying gait patterns, incorporating hyperelastic material properties derived from MRI-based tissue segmentation. Concurrently, unsupervised clustering algorithms will process longitudinal IMU datasets (sampled at 200 Hz) from 500 patients to identify latent movement patterns predictive of ulceration risk. HPC resources are essential for scaling the FEM meshing to submillimeter resolution across 10,000+ elements per simulation and enabling parallel processing of high-frequency sensor data. Expected outcomes include a predictive model correlating microstructural tissue strain with macroscale kinematic biomarkers, validated against prospective ulcer incidence data. This work will establish a novel computational paradigm for pre-emptive intervention in DFS, with potential applications to personalized orthotic design and surgical planning. By quantifying previously intractable relationships between localized mechanical loading and systemic disease progression, the project aims to reduce the 23% annual recurrence rate of diabetic foot ulcers while advancing computational podiatry as a distinct interdisciplinary research domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of podiatric medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and injuries to the foot and lower extremities. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, anatomy of the lower extremity, functional orthopedics, foot biomechanics, podiatric radiology, dermatology, podiatric surgery, podopediatrics, sports medicine, physical diagnosis, emergency medicine and traumatology, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and generating large-scale generative art and interactive media installations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations in processing complex visual datasets and real-time rendering. Contemporary digital art practices increasingly rely on computationally intensive processes, such as training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on high-resolution imagery, simulating dynamic particle systems for immersive installations, or optimizing 3D-printable designs through iterative topological algorithms. However, existing consumer-grade hardware struggles with the scale and latency demands of these workflows, particularly when handling multi-modal inputs (e.g., motion capture, environmental sensors) or generating ultra-high-definition outputs for public installations. The proposed research will deploy parallelized rendering pipelines using GPU clusters to accelerate neural style transfer algorithms, optimize fluid dynamics simulations for real-time projection mapping, and train custom diffusion models on terabyte-scale archives of historical and contemporary visual art. A key innovation involves hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to balance memory-intensive tasks like voxel-based 3D modeling with rapid inference of generative models. Outcomes will include open-source tools for artists to prototype computationally demanding projects, a benchmark dataset quantifying performance gains in HPC-accelerated creative workflows, and a series of public exhibitions demonstrating scalable applications of these methods. This work addresses critical gaps in accessible computational infrastructure for visual arts research, enabling novel forms of data-driven artistic expression while contributing to interdisciplinary dialogues about the role of HPC in creative practice. Resource allocation will specifically support large-batch training jobs, distributed rendering nodes, and sustained memory bandwidth for multi-week generative design experiments.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in visual and performing arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic purchasing decisions in Merchandising and Buying Operations, addressing the challenge of real-time alignment between volatile consumer preferences, supplier constraints, and inventory sustainability. Traditional purchasing models often rely on historical data and static assumptions, inadequately capturing the interdependencies between emerging trends (e.g., viral social media demand), supply chain disruptions, and multi-tier negotiation dynamics. The project proposes an agent-based simulation platform powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex buyer-supplier-consumer ecosystems, integrating real-time data streams from social sentiment analysis, supplier pricing APIs, and inventory telemetry. Machine learning submodules will predict short-term demand shifts using transformer-based natural language processing applied to trend-driven text and image data, while reinforcement learning agents will simulate negotiation strategies under stochastic supply conditions. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about adaptive bulk purchasing thresholds, ethical sourcing trade-offs, and crisis-responsive inventory buffers across 10,000+ simulated scenarios, varying parameters such as geopolitical risk levels and consumer trend decay rates. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations of multi-echelon supply networks and training deep reinforcement learning models on high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for retail buyers, reducing overstock losses by 12–18% in simulated fast-fashion and electronics retail environments, as well as novel metrics for quantifying "trend agility" in purchasing workflows. By bridging computational social science, operations research, and merchandising practice, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-intensive, resilience-focused buying strategies in hyperdynamic retail markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional buyers of resale products and product lines for stores, chains, and other retail enterprises. Includes instruction in product evaluation, merchandising, applicable aspects of brand and consumer research, principles of purchasing, and negotiation skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of non-coding regulatory elements in shaping phenotypic diversity across natural populations of *Arabidopsis thaliana*, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic and transcriptomic datasets. While protein-coding regions have been extensively studied, the contribution of cis-regulatory variation to complex traits—particularly in non-model plant systems—remains poorly resolved. The research addresses this gap by integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with allele-specific expression (ASE) data to identify regulatory variants influencing adaptive traits such as flowering time and drought response. A key challenge is the computational demand of analyzing population-scale whole-genome sequencing data (>1,000 accessions) alongside RNA-seq profiles from diverse tissue types and stress conditions. Our approach employs graph-based genome representations to efficiently map structural variants in non-coding regions, paired with machine learning models trained on epigenetic features (e.g., chromatin accessibility, histone modifications) to prioritize functional regulatory mutations. These analyses will be coupled with forward genetic simulations to quantify the evolutionary constraints on regulatory versus coding regions. The project requires HPC resources for 1) parallelized processing of terabyte-scale genomic datasets using containerized workflows, 2) GPU-accelerated training of deep neural networks for variant effect prediction, and 3) stochastic simulations of selection dynamics across simulated populations. Expected outcomes include a comprehensive atlas of regulatory variants linked to ecologically relevant traits, novel algorithms for cis-regulatory network inference, and quantitative models of how regulatory evolution contributes to local adaptation. This work will advance foundational knowledge in plant genetics while developing computational frameworks applicable to other species with complex, non-Mendelian inheritance patterns. By clarifying the mechanisms by which regulatory variation shapes phenotypic diversity, the project has broad implications for evolutionary genetics and crop improvement strategies.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the organization, recombination, function, regulation, and transmission of heritable information in biological organisms at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in Mendelian genetics, mechanisms of gene regulation, chromosome structure and replication, epigenetic phenomena, DNA repair and recombination, sex determination, genetic interactions between genomes, and molecular evolution.

abstract: Students with diverse learning needs require highly personalized educational interventions, yet designing effective strategies remains challenging due to the complex interplay of cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors. Traditional analytical approaches often struggle to model these multidimensional interactions at scale. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from special education settings, including student performance metrics, behavioral observations, and physiological sensor data. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns predictive of intervention success, while agent-based simulations will model classroom dynamics under varying instructional scenarios. The computational demands of processing heterogeneous data streams and running iterative simulations necessitate parallelized workflows and substantial memory allocation. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to guide educators in tailoring interventions to individual learner profiles and (2) optimized simulation environments for testing the scalability of adaptive teaching strategies. By integrating computational modeling with special education pedagogy, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in teacher preparation programs, ultimately supporting more equitable learning outcomes for students with disabilities. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable rapid prototyping of models, real-time analysis of complex datasets, and validation of intervention efficacy across simulated and real-world classroom contexts. This project bridges gaps between computational innovation and special education practice, offering transformative potential for teacher training and individualized instruction.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in special education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural semantic alignment in global corporate communication networks using advanced natural language processing (NLP) and graph analytics. As multinational corporations increasingly rely on decentralized, AI-driven communication platforms, mismatches in context-specific meaning—particularly in idioms, metaphors, and culturally embedded terminology—create operational risks and stakeholder misinterpretations. Traditional approaches to localization fail to address real-time semantic drift across distributed teams, necessitating computational methods to model how meaning evolves in multilingual organizational ecosystems. The study will analyze 12+ terabytes of multi-modal corporate communications data (emails, meeting transcripts, internal social media, and press releases) across six languages from three multinational enterprises. A hybrid transformer-graph neural network architecture will be developed to map semantic networks across languages, identifying high-risk zones of conceptual divergence and latent alignment opportunities. High-performance computing resources are essential for training cross-lingual embeddings on industry-specific corpora, running large-scale graph traversals to detect emergent semantic patterns, and simulating communication cascade effects under cultural adaptation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for predictive semantic risk assessment, adaptive retraining protocols for enterprise language models, and evidence-based guidelines for structuring multicultural communication teams. By bridging computational linguistics with organizational communication theory, this work aims to reduce cross-cultural friction in global operations while establishing new metrics for evaluating semantic coherence as a business continuity factor. The computational artifacts developed will be open-sourced to support research at the intersection of AI ethics, decentralized collaboration systems, and intercultural business practices.
cip_definition: Any program in business or corporate communications, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyberterrorism and digitally enabled criminal networks demands advanced forensic tools capable of analyzing encrypted communications, identifying covert malware, and reconstructing fragmented digital evidence at scale. Current methods struggle with the computational intensity of decrypting modern cryptographic algorithms, parsing terabytes of network traffic, and detecting AI-generated obfuscation patterns in real time. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy scalable forensic frameworks for counterterrorism applications. Key objectives include optimizing parallelized decryption workflows for distributed GPU clusters, training deep learning models to identify steganographic payloads in multimedia files, and simulating attacker behavior in virtualized network environments to preemptively map intrusion vectors. Computational methods will integrate forensic disk imaging, memory analysis, and blockchain transaction tracing, with a focus on automating evidence correlation across heterogeneous datasets. HPC resources will enable rapid processing of petabyte-scale case data, reduce brute-force decryption times for law enforcement, and improve detection accuracy for zero-day exploits through ensemble machine learning. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for forensic analysts, validated benchmarks for cloud-based incident response systems, and novel methodologies for tracing cross-platform terrorist communications. By accelerating the analysis of encrypted devices and dark web artifacts, this research aims to strengthen proactive cyber counterterrorism operations, support judicial processes with court-admissible digital evidence, and inform policy frameworks for managing emerging threats in decentralized systems. The project’s computational demands necessitate dedicated HPC access to ensure scalability, reproducibility, and secure handling of sensitive operational datasets.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques used to identify, search, seize and analyze digital media and to conduct cyber investigations against criminal and terrorist activity. Includes instruction in computer boot processes and drives, jumper setting, file access and reconstruction, hacking, network systems, cryptography, programming, investigative techniques, forensic imagery, web-based investigation methods, cyberterrorism, and applicable laws and administrative procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize precision anesthetic dosing through the development of a machine learning (ML) framework integrating genetic, physiological, and clinical data to predict individual responses to anesthetic agents. Current dosing protocols rely on population-level pharmacokinetic models that inadequately account for genetic polymorphisms affecting drug metabolism (e.g., CYP450 variants) or dynamic intraoperative variables such as hemodynamic fluctuations and tissue oxygenation. The resulting dosing inaccuracies contribute to adverse outcomes, including postoperative delirium and prolonged recovery. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models on retrospective electronic health records (n ≈ 50,000 surgical cases), genomic datasets from pre-anesthesia testing, and high-frequency intraoperative biosensor data. Recurrent neural networks will process temporal physiological signals, while transformer-based architectures will analyze heterogeneous inputs (genetic variants, comorbidities, drug histories) to predict real-time drug effect-site concentrations. Parallelized pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations will generate synthetic training data to address clinical dataset sparsity. The computational workflow requires GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and large-memory nodes for genome-wide association analysis. Successful validation could yield a clinical decision support system that dynamically adjusts dosing recommendations based on evolving patient states, reducing complications by an estimated 15–20%. This work bridges artificial intelligence and translational anesthesiology, advancing personalized perioperative care while establishing scalable methods for integrating multi-omics data into real-time clinical workflows. The requested HPC resources are essential given the computational intensity of processing terabyte-scale biosensor streams and performing genome-phenome association studies across diverse anesthetic scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the cultural and linguistic dynamics of non-clinical pastoral counseling sessions across diverse communities, addressing a critical gap in understanding how sociocultural variables influence care outcomes. While pastoral counseling integrates theological frameworks with psychological principles, current training models lack robust tools to systematically evaluate how factors like dialect, metaphor, and narrative structures—shaped by ethnicity, gender, or regional identity—affect counselor-client rapport and intervention efficacy. The research will compile a novel corpus of anonymized pastoral counseling transcripts (n≈10,000 sessions) from interfaith organizations, enriched with metadata on participants’ cultural backgrounds. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for HPC environments, including transformer-based models (e.g., BERT, GPT-3) fine-tuned on theological and counseling-specific lexicons, the project will quantify patterns in language use, emotional valence, and thematic focus across demographic cohorts. Parallelized sentiment analysis and topic modeling will identify disparities in communication efficacy, while network graphs will map how counselors adapt theological concepts to clients’ cultural frameworks. The computational workflow will integrate ethical AI guardrails to mitigate bias in language analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for culturally responsive pastoral training, (2) open-access datasets annotated with sociolinguistic features, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing theological discourse in multicultural contexts. By bridging computational linguistics, pastoral theology, and intercultural studies, this work advances a neglected frontier in digital humanities: the rigorous, data-driven study of spiritual care practices as socially embedded phenomena. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional text data and training domain-specific AI models, enabling insights that traditional qualitative methods cannot feasibly generate.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and principles of pastoral care and prepares ordained clergy to provide non-clinical pastoral counseling to individuals and groups. Includes instruction in pastoral leadership, counseling psychology; crisis intervention; individual and group procedures; theological and spiritual counseling; pastoral care; and applications to specific types of ministry.

abstract: The oral microbiome plays a critical role in the development of dental caries, periodontal disease, and systemic health conditions, yet the complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and environmental factors remain poorly understood. Traditional laboratory methods face limitations in modeling these dynamic systems at scale, hindering the identification of predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This project proposes a computational approach to analyze multi-omics datasets and simulate microbial community behaviors to advance precision dentistry strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate metagenomic sequencing data from dental plaque samples with host transcriptomic and proteomic profiles to construct agent-based models of oral biofilm formation. These models will simulate spatial-temporal interactions under varying conditions, including pH fluctuations, nutrient availability, and antimicrobial treatments. Machine learning algorithms will then identify keystone microbial species and genetic pathways associated with dysbiosis and disease progression. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will characterize the structural stability of enamel proteins under acidic stress, informed by atomic-level data from crystallography studies. The computational workload requires parallel processing capabilities for large-scale parameter optimization and real-time visualization of 3D biofilm architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking specific microbial consortia to early caries risk, (2) mechanistic insights into enamel demineralization dynamics, and (3) a publicly accessible database of simulated treatment responses for educational use in preclinical dental training. By elucidating microenvironmental drivers of oral disease, this work will support the development of personalized preventive care protocols and biomimetic restorative materials, directly aligning with pre-dentistry competencies in evidence-based practice. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the terabytes of heterogeneous data and computationally intensive simulations central to this translational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in dentistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance early childhood education (ECE) by modeling and optimizing individualized teaching strategies for diverse learners aged 0–8 years. A critical challenge in ECE is designing scalable, adaptive pedagogical approaches that account for variability in developmental trajectories, learning styles, and socioemotional needs. Traditional observational and survey-based methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multivariate interactions between instructional practices, child behavior, and learning outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom environments and predict the efficacy of teaching interventions. Large-scale datasets—including longitudinal assessments, video-recorded classroom interactions, and physiological response metrics (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate)—will be analyzed using deep neural networks to identify patterns in engagement and skill acquisition. Concurrently, ABM will simulate hypothetical teaching scenarios, varying parameters such as lesson pacing, group composition, and multimodal instruction (e.g., tactile vs. visual tools). These simulations will generate probabilistic outcomes for skill mastery and socioemotional growth, enabling data-driven recommendations for personalized teaching practices. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, training complex ML models, and running thousands of parallelized ABM iterations to ensure statistical robustness. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of computational models linking teaching strategies to learner profiles, (2) evidence-based guidelines for adapting curricula in real-time classroom settings, and (3) a pipeline for translating simulated insights into teacher training modules. By bridging computational analytics and ECE pedagogy, this work aims to equip educators with scalable tools to enhance equity and efficacy in early learning environments.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students ranging in age from infancy through eight years (grade three), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: Gene therapies hold transformative potential for treating genetic disorders, yet their development is hindered by challenges in optimizing delivery systems, predicting off-target effects, and personalizing treatments. This project seeks to address these barriers by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the interactions of viral and nonviral gene delivery vectors with host genomes, tissues, and immune systems. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of current vector design pipelines, which rely heavily on trial-and-error experimental approaches that are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to simulate complex biological systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven genome editing prediction, and multi-omics data analysis. MD simulations will model structural dynamics of adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids and lipid nanoparticles to identify modifications that enhance tissue-specific targeting and evade immune detection. Concurrently, neural networks trained on CRISPR-Cas9 editing outcomes and single-cell RNA-seq datasets will predict gene expression profiles following therapeutic interventions, enabling in silico screening of candidate therapies. These workflows will be scaled using GPU-accelerated nodes to handle systems with >10^6 atoms (for MD) and terabyte-scale genomic datasets (for ML/omics integration). The expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for vector-host interactions, (2) optimized vector designs with improved efficacy and safety profiles, and (3) a computational platform for patient-specific therapy simulation. By reducing reliance on low-throughput experimental methods, this work aims to accelerate the translation of gene therapies into clinical practice while addressing critical bioethical concerns around off-target risks. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary computational granularity and throughput, which cannot be supported by local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies.
