Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for vessel efficiency under climate change scenarios, decision-support tools for crew training and operational logistics, and open-source computational frameworks tailored to maritime applications. By bridging gaps between naval architecture, marine engineering, and data science, this research will advance sustainable practices in commercial shipping, enhance safety protocols for extreme conditions, and inform policy development for maritime environmental stewardship. The results will directly benefit merchant marine education by integrating computational tools into training curricula, preparing future officers to leverage HPC-driven solutions in real-world operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as captains, executive officers, engineers and ranking mates on commercially licensed inland, coastal and ocean-going vessels. Includes instruction in maritime traditions and law, maritime policy, economics and management of commercial marine operations, basic naval architecture and engineering, shipboard power systems engineering, crew supervision, and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address challenges in optimizing additive manufacturing processes for high-performance metallic alloys, where traditional trial-and-error methods lead to excessive material waste and suboptimal mechanical properties. The research aims to develop a computational framework that integrates multiphysics simulations with machine learning (ML) to predict and control process parameters such as laser power, scan speed, and thermal gradients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the coupled thermal-structural-fluid dynamics inherent in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processes, which involve micron-scale melt pool dynamics and rapid solidification phenomena. Large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model heat transfer, residual stress formation, and defect generation across varying temporal and spatial scales. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze simulation outputs to identify parameter combinations that minimize porosity and distortion while maximizing tensile strength. The computational workload necessitates parallelized solvers, distributed memory architectures, and GPU acceleration to handle datasets exceeding 10^6 degrees of freedom per simulation. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for LPBF parameter optimization, reducing experimental iterations by 40-60% while achieving target material properties. This work will directly benefit aerospace and biomedical industries by enabling faster development of complex, defect-free components. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will also serve as a resource for advancing digital twin technologies in additive manufacturing, contributing to sustainable practices through reduced material waste and energy consumption.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the role of dysregulated intracellular calcium signaling in cancer cell migration and metastasis, a critical yet underexplored aspect of tumor progression in epithelial cancers. Despite established links between calcium homeostasis and cytoskeletal dynamics, the precise mechanisms by which oncogenic mutations alter calcium-dependent signaling networks to drive invasive behavior remain poorly resolved. We propose to develop a multiscale computational model integrating stochastic simulations of ion channel dynamics, spatial modeling of calcium diffusion, and mechanochemical coupling to actin remodeling. The model will parameterize experimental data from live-cell imaging of calcium transients and traction force microscopy in breast cancer cell lines, enabling quantitative predictions of how oncogenic drivers (e.g., HER2 amplification) rewire calcium handling to enhance motility. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of calcium microdomains near membrane protrusions, simulate probabilistic channel gating at submillisecond resolution, and perform ensemble analyses across physiologically relevant parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical control points in calcium-regulated migration pathways, (2) predictive maps of how channelopathies synergize with oncogenic signaling to accelerate metastasis, and (3) candidate targets for microenvironment-specific therapies disrupting mechanical adaptation in tumors. By bridging cell-scale physiology to tissue-level cancer biology, this work will advance mechanistic strategies to inhibit metastatic competence while avoiding broad-spectrum calcium modulation, which carries systemic toxicity risks. The computational framework will be shared as an open-access tool for testing therapeutic perturbations in silico, accelerating translational research in precision oncology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of physiological processes operating within and among cells, and intracellular communication and behavior, in the context of larger systems and whole organisms. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology, molecular physiology, cell cycle control, signal transduction, protein structure, membrane biochemistry and structure, ion channel physics, cell respiration and digestion, secretory functions, cell adhesion and communication, information encoding and decoding, and the relation of cell physiology to tissue, organ, and organismic functioning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in precision nutrition and dietetic care planning, addressing the critical challenge of efficiently personalizing dietary interventions for diverse populations. Current methods for analyzing complex interactions between dietary patterns, health outcomes, and individual variables (e.g., genetics, metabolic markers, socio-economic factors) are limited by the scalability of traditional computational tools. We propose to develop machine learning models and agent-based simulations to optimize dietary recommendations and predict long-term health impacts. These models will integrate multi-modal datasets, including electronic health records, dietary intake logs, biomarker data, and public health databases, to identify patterns and generate tailored nutrition plans. Computational workflows will involve parallel processing of large datasets to train predictive algorithms, simulate population-level dietary scenarios, and assess compliance with clinical and regulatory guidelines. HPC resources are essential to handle the high dimensionality of data, reduce runtime for iterative model refinement, and enable real-time adjustments during client consultations. Expected outcomes include scalable frameworks for dynamic meal planning, risk stratification tools for diet-related chronic diseases, and evidence-based insights into the cost-effectiveness of community nutrition programs. This work will directly enhance the capacity of dietetic technicians to deliver data-driven care, support interdisciplinary collaboration with public health and computational researchers, and inform policy updates in nutritional services. By bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational innovation, the project aims to establish a foundation for AI-enhanced decision support systems in dietetics education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of registered dietitians and nutritionists, to implement nutritional and dietetic plans and provide direct client and patient services. Includes instruction in human nutrition, client interviewing and record keeping, dietary planning, food preparation and safety, food worker supervision, food service establishment monitoring and inspection, and applicable procedures and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance geothermal energy system design and operational efficiency by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex subsurface-plant interactions. Current geothermal installations face challenges in optimizing heat extraction, managing geological variability, and minimizing long-term performance degradation due to dynamic subsurface conditions. Traditional design tools often rely on simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to predict system behavior under heterogeneous geological formations or variable thermal loads. To address this, the research will develop a coupled computational framework integrating 3D finite element modeling of subsurface heat transfer, fluid dynamics simulations of borehole heat exchangers, and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive maintenance algorithms. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations to resolve multiphysics interactions at high spatial resolution across multi-year operational timelines. Key objectives include quantifying the impact of rock fracturing patterns on heat exchange efficiency, optimizing borehole field configurations for urban-scale installations, and training ML models to detect early signs of equipment wear using synthetic sensor data generated from simulations. The computational workflow will utilize open-source tools (e.g., FEniCS, OpenFOAM) and custom Python-based ML pipelines, with validation against field data from active geothermal sites in partnership with industry collaborators. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for site-specific system design, reducing installation costs by 15–20% through optimized resource targeting; (2) a publicly accessible dataset of simulated fault scenarios to inform technician training protocols; and (3) predictive maintenance templates adaptable to diverse geothermal hardware configurations. By bridging computational innovation with practical technician training needs, this work aims to accelerate the deployment of resilient, cost-effective geothermal systems while enhancing educational resources for next-generation technicians.
cip_title: Geothermal Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance biomechanical modeling of foot pathologies in patients with diabetes, a critical area of podiatric medicine. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a leading cause of lower extremity amputations, driven by complex interactions between tissue mechanics, neuropathy, and vascular dysfunction. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict ulcer formation in heterogeneous tissue environments, limiting early intervention strategies. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating molecular-scale collagen degradation, cellular-scale inflammatory responses, and macroscopic foot biomechanics. The model will incorporate patient-specific data from 3D gait analysis, MRI-derived tissue morphology, and proteomic profiles of diabetic skin. Finite element simulations will map mechanical stress distributions across the plantar surface under dynamic loading, while agent-based modeling will simulate inflammatory cell migration and collagen remodeling in response to localized strain. Machine learning algorithms will identify high-risk stress-cytokine interaction patterns predictive of ulcer onset. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of coupling these models at scale, particularly for optimizing parallelized solvers handling >10^6 degrees of freedom in tissue deformation analyses and training deep neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets of clinical and simulated outcomes. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for stratifying DFU risk at submillimeter spatial resolutions, validated against a longitudinal cohort of 200 patients. This work will establish a paradigm for personalized podiatric interventions targeting biomechanical and molecular drivers of tissue failure, with potential applications in orthotic design and surgical planning. By bridging computational biomechanics and diabetic pathophysiology, the project addresses an unmet need in podiatric research while demonstrating how HPC can transform management of complex foot disorders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of podiatric medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and injuries to the foot and lower extremities. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, anatomy of the lower extremity, functional orthopedics, foot biomechanics, podiatric radiology, dermatology, podiatric surgery, podopediatrics, sports medicine, physical diagnosis, emergency medicine and traumatology, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly threatened by climate change, invasive species, and anthropogenic disturbances, necessitating advanced predictive models to inform sustainable management strategies. Current approaches often fail to capture the multi-scale interactions between forest dynamics, soil biogeochemistry, and microclimate variability due to computational limitations in resolving fine-grained ecological processes across large spatial and temporal domains. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, process-based computational model integrating forest growth, hydrology, and soil nutrient cycling using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The model will simulate forest responses to climate scenarios (RCP 4.5 and 8.5) at a 1 km² resolution across heterogeneous landscapes in the Pacific Northwest, incorporating species-specific traits, disturbance regimes, and edaphic factors. Key computational challenges include parallelizing agent-based tree population dynamics, coupling hydrological and biogeochemical submodels via scalable numerical solvers, and assimilating multi-source remote sensing data (LiDAR, hyperspectral) for parameterization. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations spanning decadal timescales, sensitivity analyses, and Bayesian calibration against long-term forest inventory datasets. Anticipated outcomes include identifying resilient forest compositions under climate stress, quantifying carbon sequestration trade-offs in managed versus unmanaged stands, and mapping drought-induced mortality risks. This work will directly support regional conservation planning and climate adaptation policies by providing actionable projections of forest health and ecosystem services. By open-sourcing the model framework and workflows, the project will also establish a replicable computational platform for interdisciplinary forest research, bridging gaps between empirical ecology and predictive modeling. The requested resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in scaling ecological simulations, ensuring robust uncertainty quantification essential for stakeholder decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of one or more forest-related sciences to the study of environmental factors affecting forests and the growth and management of forest resources. Includes instruction in forest biology, forest hydrology, forest mensuration, silviculture, forest soils, water resources, environmental science, forest resources management, and wood science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a machine learning (ML)-driven decision support system to optimize clinical workflows for medical assistants (MAs) managing complex, multi-morbid patients in outpatient settings. Despite their critical role in patient triage, data collection, and preliminary assessments, MAs often face challenges in prioritizing tasks when managing patients with overlapping chronic conditions, leading to inefficiencies and potential delays in care. The research problem centers on the lack of adaptive, real-time tools to guide MAs in dynamically adjusting workflows based on evolving patient data, clinic demands, and provider priorities. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train ensemble ML models on heterogeneous datasets, including de-identified electronic health records (EHRs), real-time vital sign streams from wearable sensors, and clinic operational logs. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing for clinician note analysis, time-series forecasting for patient deterioration risk, and graph neural networks to model task interdependencies. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data across 50,000+ simulated patient-clinician interactions and validation against a 3-year longitudinal MA workflow dataset. Expected outcomes include a prototype system that reduces task redundancy by ≥25% in simulated environments while maintaining 95% clinical priority adherence, as well as novel metrics for quantifying MA decision burden. This work addresses an understudied nexus of clinical operations, predictive analytics, and human factors engineering within health sciences, with potential to establish computational frameworks for adaptive workflow management in resource-constrained care settings. Successful implementation could inform new standards for MA training programs and intelligent health IT system design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical office administrative services and perform clinical duties including patient intake and care, routine diagnostic and recording procedures, pre-examination and examination assistance, and the administration of medications and first aid. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology; medical terminology; medical law and ethics; patient psychology and communications; medical office procedures; and clinical diagnostic, examination, testing, and treatment procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of complex interactions between alternative medical therapies and biological systems. Despite growing interest in complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) modalities such as herbal medicine, acupuncture, and mind-body interventions, their mechanisms of action at molecular and systemic levels remain poorly characterized. This gap limits evidence-based integration with conventional medical frameworks. To address this, we propose a computational study combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, network pharmacology, and machine learning (ML) to model the multi-scale effects of CAM therapies. Key objectives include simulating the binding dynamics of bioactive herbal compounds to target proteins, mapping the polypharmacological networks of naturopathic formulations, and analyzing longitudinal clinical datasets to identify biomarkers associated with mind-body therapy outcomes. The computational pipeline will integrate publicly available phytochemical databases, proteomic datasets, and electronic health records (EHRs) from CAM clinical trials. MD simulations will employ all-atom and coarse-grained models to capture time-dependent interactions, while graph neural networks will elucidate system-level responses. This work requires HPC resources due to the scale of molecular simulations (10^6–10^7 atom systems), the complexity of multi-omics data integration, and the need for hyperparameter optimization in ML models. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for herbal compound synergies, mechanistic insights into acupuncture’s neuromodulatory effects, and validated computational tools for optimizing CAM treatment protocols. By bridging computational biomedicine and CAM research, this project aims to generate translatable evidence for holistic health interventions, potentially informing clinical guidelines and personalized integrative medicine strategies.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: Osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) leverages the interdependence of the musculoskeletal system and systemic health, yet the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain insufficiently characterized. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to simulate OMT-induced physiological responses, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the complexity of integrated anatomical, biomechanical, and cellular datasets. The research problem centers on quantifying how targeted manual interventions influence tissue remodeling, neural signaling, and inflammatory pathways, which are critical for optimizing evidence-based OMT protocols. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining finite element modeling of musculoskeletal stress-strain dynamics, agent-based simulations of cellular responses (e.g., fibroblast activation, cytokine diffusion), and machine learning analysis of clinical OMT outcomes data. These models will integrate anonymized patient data from motion capture systems, electronic health records, and molecular assays (e.g., proteomic profiles pre/post-OMT). The HPC infrastructure is essential for running large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal intervention parameters (e.g., force, angle, duration) and for validating model predictions against experimental data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific OMT techniques to quantifiable changes in tissue repair kinetics and autonomic nervous system modulation, with implications for treating chronic pain, post-surgical recovery, and inflammatory conditions. This work will also establish open-source simulation tools for the osteopathic research community, enabling reproducible investigations into mechanotransduction pathways and holistic health outcomes. By elucidating the systems-level effects of OMT, this project aims to advance personalized osteopathic care and strengthen the integration of computational methodologies into musculoskeletal medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of osteopathic medicine, involving a combination of medical principles and procedures and osteopathic principles of holistic medicine and the relationship of the musculoskeletal system to general health. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, preventive medicine, family and community medicine, medical informatics, disease systems, organ and physiologic systems, osteopathic principles and practice, osteopathic manipulative treatment, musculoskeletal and skin systems, clinical specialty rotations, medical ethics, and professional standards and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize the design and operational efficiency of multi-component industrial systems, with a focus on applications in manufacturing and infrastructure monitoring. Engineering technologies often rely on integrating heterogeneous systems—such as sensor networks, control units, and mechanical actuators—but current approaches to modeling these interactions lack the resolution and adaptability needed for dynamic, real-world environments. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in simulating system-wide behavior under variable physical constraints (e.g., thermal stress, material fatigue) and operational demands. To address this, we propose a hybrid methodology combining finite element analysis (FEA) for localized stress-strain modeling, agent-based simulations for subsystem interactions, and machine learning to predict failure thresholds. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parallelize these computationally intensive tasks, enabling large-scale parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses across diverse scenarios. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for FEA and distributed computing frameworks to manage agent-based simulations, with validation against experimental data from collaborative industry partners. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for system resilience prediction, reduced computational overhead for multi-physics simulations, and actionable insights into maintenance scheduling for aging industrial assets. This work will directly advance the capability of engineering technologists to model complex systems at scale, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical implementation. By prioritizing resource efficiency and interoperability, the project aligns with broader goals of sustainable industrial practices and adaptive infrastructure management. Successful implementation will provide a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into applied engineering workflows, benefiting sectors such as advanced manufacturing, energy distribution, and smart infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in a wide variety of projects. Includes instruction in various engineering support functions for research, production, and operations, and applications to specific engineering specialties.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in health information system interoperability and data integration by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous medical records. The fragmentation of health data across disparate systems—ranging from electronic health records (EHRs) to wearable device outputs—hinders efficient clinical decision-making, population health analytics, and personalized care delivery. Current methods for harmonizing these datasets struggle with scalability, real-time processing, and maintaining data integrity across formats. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework that combines machine learning (ML) models with graph-based data structures to map, standardize, and query multi-modal health information at scale. The project will utilize distributed computing paradigms to process petabytes of de-identified patient data from partner health systems, including structured EHR entries, unstructured clinical notes, and imaging metadata. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for clinical concept normalization, implementing parallelized entity-resolution algorithms across distributed nodes, and simulating network architectures for optimal data federation. HPC resources are essential to support the iterative refinement of privacy-preserving federated learning approaches, which will enable cross-institutional analytics without raw data sharing. Expected outcomes include optimized algorithms for real-time data harmonization, benchmarks for scalable health information system design, and open-source tools to automate metadata tagging across diverse clinical repositories. By addressing computational bottlenecks in data integration, this work aims to provide health information administrators with evidence-based strategies for managing next-generation health systems while ensuring compliance with evolving interoperability standards. The project’s scalability assessments will directly inform national efforts to modernize health data infrastructure, reducing latency in critical care scenarios and enabling longitudinal research on underrepresented patient populations.
cip_title: Health Information/ Medical Records Administration/ Administrator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage systems, processes, and facilities used to collect, store, secure, retrieve, analyze, and transmit medical records and other health information used by clinical professionals and health care organizations. Includes instruction in the principles and basic content of the biomedical and clinical sciences, information technology and applications, data and database management, clinical research methodologies, health information resources and systems, office management, legal requirements, and professional standards.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic administrative workflow optimization within modern office environments, particularly focusing on the integration of unstructured communication data and real-time task prioritization. As clerical roles increasingly intersect with data-driven decision-making, traditional tools for managing emails, scheduling, and document workflows struggle to adapt to variable workloads, hybrid work models, and multi-channel communication patterns. The project will develop a computational framework to model and simulate office workflows using natural language processing (NLP) and reinforcement learning, analyzing how semantic content in communications (e.g., emails, chat logs) correlates with task urgency, resource allocation bottlenecks, and operational latency. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process large-scale anonymized communication datasets (>10 TB) from corporate archives, train transformer-based models for contextual task classification, and run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of workflow scenarios under stochastic demand conditions. Key innovations include a graph-based representation of ad-hoc task dependencies derived from unstructured text and a multi-agent simulation environment to test adaptive scheduling policies. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for workload redistribution, validated protocol recommendations for hybrid office environments, and open-source tools to optimize legacy systems like shared calendars and ticketing platforms. By bridging computational linguistics and operations research, this work aims to reduce cognitive load on clerical staff while improving service-level compliance in administrative support roles, with implications for workforce training and resource planning in the AI-augmented office of the future.
cip_title: General Office Occupations and Clerical Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide basic administrative support under the supervision of office managers, administrative assistants, secretaries, and other office personnel. Includes instruction in typing, keyboarding, filing, general business correspondence, office equipment operation, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize floriculture supply chain management and improve post-harvest longevity of cut flowers through advanced computational modeling and machine learning. The floriculture industry faces critical challenges in balancing perishable inventory with dynamic market demand, minimizing waste, and maintaining product quality across global distribution networks. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to logistics and preservation lack the scalability to account for multivariate factors such as temperature fluctuations, ethylene sensitivity, transportation delays, and cultivar-specific deterioration rates. To address this, we propose developing agent-based supply chain simulations that integrate real-world data from IoT-enabled cold chain sensors, historical sales patterns, and genomic databases of flower senescence traits. Concurrently, machine learning models will be trained on hyperspectral imaging datasets to predict vase life outcomes under varying storage conditions. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets, running parallelized genomic association studies (GWAS) to identify genetic markers linked to extended longevity, and optimizing neural networks for real-time decision support in inventory routing. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for reducing floral waste by 15–30% in test markets, dynamic pricing algorithms tied to quality metrics, and genotype-to-phenotype insights for breeding resilient cultivars. By bridging computational science with floriculture operations, this work aims to establish scalable, data-driven protocols that enhance profitability for growers and retailers while reducing the environmental footprint of floral distribution networks.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage commercial and contract florist enterprises, supply and delivery services, and flower catering services. Includes instruction in the applicable principles of plant science; purchasing, storage, and delivery systems; floral design and arranging; and principles of business management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to analyze the efficacy of mathematics teaching strategies in diverse classroom settings, with the goal of informing teacher education practices. A critical challenge in mathematics teacher preparation is understanding how instructional choices interact with variables such as student prior knowledge, engagement patterns, and problem-solving approaches. While classroom studies provide valuable insights, they struggle to systematically isolate the effects of specific pedagogical decisions across varied scenarios. To address this gap, we propose creating large-scale agent-based simulations that model student-teacher interactions during mathematics instruction. The simulations will incorporate cognitive architectures for student agents, calibrated using empirical data from classroom observations and student assessments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations representing different teaching strategies, classroom compositions, and mathematical content areas (e.g., algebra, geometry). Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to identify strategy patterns that optimally balance conceptual understanding, skill development, and equity considerations. Additionally, we will develop visualization tools to help teacher educators explore causal relationships between instructional decisions and student outcomes. The computational framework will be validated through collaborations with mathematics teacher preparation programs, comparing model predictions with observed classroom outcomes. This work aims to produce two key contributions: (1) evidence-based guidelines for tailoring mathematics teaching methods to specific learning contexts, and (2) an open-access simulation platform for use in teacher professional development. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges computational modeling and mathematics education praxis, offering novel methods to enhance teacher preparation at scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach mathematics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address disparities in preventable chronic disease outcomes across underserved communities by developing a predictive modeling framework to optimize resource allocation for local public health interventions. Chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension disproportionately affect marginalized populations, yet current intervention strategies often rely on static, population-wide approaches that fail to account for dynamic social determinants, environmental factors, and community-specific behavioral patterns. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data sources—including electronic health records, geospatial environmental exposures, socioeconomic indicators, and community health surveys—into a unified computational model capable of simulating intervention impacts at hyper-local scales. The proposed approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling (ABM) combined with machine learning techniques, enabling the simulation of millions of individual agents interacting with spatially explicit social and environmental conditions. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution geospatial data, training ensemble models on multi-modal datasets, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in intervention outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will facilitate parallelized parameter sweeps to identify optimal combinations of preventive strategies tailored to specific community profiles, while graph neural networks will analyze social network effects on health behavior adoption. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for health departments to prioritize interventions based on predicted cost-effectiveness and equity impacts. By enabling real-time adaptation to evolving community needs, this work aims to advance precision public health practices, reduce wasteful spending, and improve health equity. The computational framework will be validated using retrospective data from three regional health districts, with prospective implementation planned in partnership with local agencies. This project directly aligns with community health priorities by translating complex multi-scale data into actionable strategies for preventive care delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to plan and manage health services in local community settings, including the coordination of related support services, government agencies, and private resources. Includes instruction in public health, community health services and delivery, health behavior and cultural factors, local government operations, human services, health communication and promotion, health services administration in local settings, environmental health, preventive and comparative medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, family and community health, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Plant stems exhibit remarkable mechanical resilience, balancing flexibility and rigidity to withstand dynamic environmental stresses. However, the relationship between vascular bundle arrangement—a critical anatomical feature—and biomechanical performance remains poorly quantified. This project seeks to resolve how spatially heterogeneous distributions of vascular tissues influence stress distribution, deformation, and failure resistance in stems across diverse plant species. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models parameterized with micro-computed tomography (μCT) scans of vascular anatomy from herbaceous and woody plants. These models will simulate mechanical responses to multidirectional loads mimicking wind, gravitational bending, and torsional forces. HPC resources are essential to accommodate the computational intensity of nonlinear, anisotropic material properties and high-resolution 3D meshes required for anatomically accurate simulations. By iteratively modifying vascular geometries in silico, we will identify configurations that optimize strain energy dissipation and minimize structural fatigue. Parallelized workflows will enable statistical comparisons across phylogenetic lineages and environmental adaptations. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking vascular architecture to biomechanical trade-offs, offering insights into plant evolutionary strategies and informing the design of bioinspired materials with graded stiffness. Additionally, this work will establish a computational pipeline for mechano-anatomical analysis applicable to other plant organs, advancing foundational knowledge in plant structural biology. The requested resources will directly support the generation of large-scale simulation datasets, which will be made publicly available to foster interdisciplinary collaborations in materials science, paleobotany, and agricultural engineering.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plants, related microbial organisms, and plant habitats and ecosystem relations. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and structure, phytochemistry, cytology, plant genetics, plant morphology and physiology, plant ecology, plant taxonomy and systematics, paleobotany, and applications of biophysics and molecular biology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in gastrointestinal and hepatic diseases, focusing on the integration of multi-omics data with clinical variables to predict disease progression and therapeutic responses. Chronic liver diseases and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) exhibit marked heterogeneity in outcomes, yet current clinical tools inadequately stratify risk or personalize treatment. A critical barrier is the computational complexity of analyzing high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data—to identify biomarkers and mechanistic pathways. To address this, we propose developing a scalable computational framework using machine learning (ML) and network-based approaches. Deep learning models will be trained on multimodal data from multicenter cohorts of patients with cirrhosis and IBD to predict decompensation events, treatment resistance, or malignancy. Concurrently, Bayesian network inference will map disease-specific molecular interactions, prioritizing nodes for therapeutic targeting. These workflows require HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (≥100 TB), iterative model training, and the need for real-time parallel processing in simulating dynamic biological networks. GPU-accelerated clusters will enable rapid hyperparameter optimization for neural networks, while large-memory nodes will support genome-wide association studies (GWAS) combined with single-cell RNA-seq integration. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for clinical deployment, novel biomarkers for early disease detection, and mechanistic insights into microenvironment-driven fibrosis. By unifying HPC-driven analytics with translational hypotheses, this work aims to bridge the gap between molecular discovery and clinical decision-making, offering a template for data-driven management of complex gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary disorders. The requested resources will directly support these computationally intensive tasks, which are infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology and Hepatology

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in autonomous agricultural machinery systems by developing computational models to optimize real-time decision-making under variable field conditions. Current systems struggle to adapt to dynamic environmental factors (e.g., soil heterogeneity, crop density fluctuations, and weather variability), leading to suboptimal resource use and energy expenditure. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating multi-agent simulations, machine learning, and sensor data fusion to model adaptive machinery behaviors at scale. The computational approach will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate thousands of field scenarios across diverse geographies, crop types, and machinery configurations. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms will then train autonomous systems to minimize fuel consumption, soil compaction, and crop damage while maximizing operational speed and precision. A key innovation involves developing hybrid models that combine physics-based simulations of soil-tool interactions with real-time LiDAR and multispectral data streams. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the computational intensity of 3D terrain modeling at sub-centimeter resolutions and processing terabytes of sensor data from field trials. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated optimization algorithms for adaptive path planning and implement control, (2) open-source simulation tools for agricultural robotics benchmarking, and (3) predictive models linking machinery parameters to sustainability metrics. This work will directly advance precision agriculture by enabling machinery that dynamically balances productivity with environmental stewardship. The requested computing resources will support scaling from single-machine simulations to full fleet coordination analyses, addressing a critical gap in agricultural cyber-physical systems research. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with extension services and agricultural equipment manufacturers to accelerate technology transfer.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural mechanization, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize sustainable and ergonomic interior design solutions through advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. The research problem centers on the challenge of balancing aesthetic, functional, and environmental factors in interior spaces, particularly as design complexity grows with evolving demands for energy efficiency, occupant well-being, and adaptive reuse of materials. Current manual and software-assisted workflows struggle to efficiently integrate real-time analysis of multidimensional variables such as thermal comfort, acoustic performance, spatial ergonomics, and material lifecycle impacts. To address this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale parametric modeling, finite element analysis, and generative adversarial networks (GANs). Computational methods will include parallelized simulations of lighting distribution using ray-tracing algorithms, acoustic propagation modeling in complex geometries, and predictive analytics for material wear patterns under varying occupancy scenarios. Machine learning models trained on historical design datasets will propose optimized layouts that minimize resource use while adhering to building codes and accessibility standards. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated design validation, capable of rapidly iterating through thousands of spatially coherent solutions that satisfy competing constraints. This work will advance computational design methodologies in the visual arts by demonstrating how HPC-powered workflows can reduce trial-and-error prototyping cycles, lower carbon footprints through predictive material optimization, and establish quantifiable metrics for occupant comfort in diverse interior typologies. The resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated rendering of high-fidelity virtual environments and distributed processing of sensor data from IoT-equipped prototype spaces, enabling previously infeasible scale in analyzing human-environment interactions. Results will directly inform curriculum development in digital design integration and provide case studies for sustainable commercial retrofitting strategies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional planning, designing, equipping, and furnishing of residential and commercial interior spaces. Includes instruction in computer applications, drafting, and graphic techniques; principles of interior lighting, acoustics, systems integration, and color coordination; furniture and furnishings; textiles and their finishing; the history of interior design and period styles; basic structural design; building codes and inspection regulations; and applications to office, hotel, factory, restaurant and housing design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision engineering and material science applications in horology and jewelry fabrication. A critical challenge in these fields lies in optimizing the microscale mechanical behavior of components—such as watch movements, gemstone settings, and soldered joints—while balancing durability, aesthetic integrity, and manufacturability. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict complex interactions between materials, thermal stresses, and microstructural evolution during fabrication. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to model the nonlinear dynamics of micro-engineered systems. FEA will simulate macro-scale stresses in gear trains and jewelry structures under operational loads, while MD simulations will resolve atomistic interactions in soldered joints and crystalline materials (e.g., gemstones, alloys) to predict fracture mechanics and wear patterns. ML models, trained on experimental datasets from laser engraving and casting processes, will optimize toolpath generation and thermal management strategies to minimize defects. The HPC environment is essential for handling the multiscale, multiphysics nature of these simulations, which involve billions of degrees of freedom and require parallelized computation across GPU and CPU nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive models for component lifespan, data-driven guidelines for material selection in micro-casting, and generative algorithms for structurally sound jewelry designs. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in the Watchmaking and Jewelrymaking program, providing students with access to cutting-edge computational tools that bridge traditional craftsmanship with modern engineering principles. By reducing material waste and prototyping costs, this work also aims to enhance sustainability in small-scale manufacturing, benefiting both artisanal industries and advanced horology enterprises.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make repairs, and maintain timepieces, time-measuring devices, and jewelry items. Includes instruction in mechanical timekeeping systems, digital timekeeping systems, timesetting, casting, engraving, polishing, stonesetting, soldering, fine microscopic work, equipment and tool maintenance, redesign and restyling techniques, and customer relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model and predict physiological and environmental factors influencing labor outcomes in out-of-hospital birth settings, a critical yet underexplored area within Direct Entry Midwifery (DEM). While DEM emphasizes low-intervention, patient-centered care, current risk assessment tools lack granularity to integrate real-time, multi-modal data—such as maternal biosignals, fetal heart rate variability, and environmental stressors—into dynamic decision-making frameworks. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing a computational pipeline to synthesize heterogeneous datasets, enabling predictive analytics for labor progression and emergent complication risks. Using anonymized data from wearable biosensors, electronic health records, and geospatial environmental monitors, we will train machine learning models (e.g., convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks) to identify latent patterns associated with adverse outcomes, such as prolonged labor or neonatal distress. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle high-dimensional time-series data and stochastic simulations of birth scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool to assist midwives in preemptive clinical decision-making, reducing preventable transfers to hospital settings. Additionally, this work will establish a scalable framework for integrating ambulatory monitoring technologies into DEM practice, advancing evidence-based protocols for underserved populations seeking community-based maternity care. By aligning computational innovation with the ethical and practical priorities of direct-entry midwifery, this project aims to enhance safety and personalization in out-of-hospital births while contributing novel methodologies to computational perinatal health research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide pre-natal, natural birth, and immediate postpartum care to pregnant women in jurisdictions licensing direct (non-nursing) training for midwives. Includes instruction in basic obstetrics, women's health, fetal development, childbirth education, maternal nutrition and health, labor support, natural childbirth, postpartum support, prebirth counseling and risk screening, management of obstetric emergencies, patient referral, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Vascular neurology research faces significant challenges in modeling the complex, multifactorial pathophysiology of cerebrovascular diseases, which involve dynamic interactions between hemodynamic forces, thrombus formation, endothelial injury, and neural tissue vulnerability. Current clinical tools often inadequately capture these spatially and temporally evolving processes, limiting personalized risk prediction and therapeutic optimization. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models integrating patient-specific neuroimaging, hemodynamic simulations, and machine learning to advance the study of acute ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage. The research will utilize 3D vessel geometry extracted from clinical CT/MRI angiography to simulate cerebral blood flow dynamics via finite element analysis, coupled with agent-based modeling of clot formation and dissolution under varying anticoagulation regimens. Concurrently, diffusion tensor imaging and perfusion data will inform finite element models of penumbral tissue viability under hypoxic stress. Deep learning architectures will be trained on multi-institutional neuroimaging datasets to predict hemorrhage expansion risk and optimize blood pressure management thresholds. These parallel computational workflows require substantial GPU-accelerated nodes for fluid-structure interaction simulations and distributed training of neural networks on large-scale imaging datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for real-time thrombolytic dosing, individualized blood pressure targets in hemorrhagic stroke, and dynamic biomarkers of salvageable brain tissue. By bridging spatially resolved biophysical models with clinically actionable decision support tools, this work aims to address critical gaps in cerebrovascular disease management. The requested HPC resources will enable computationally intensive simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, directly supporting translational objectives to reduce disability from stroke through precision medicine approaches. All models and pipelines will be made available to the clinical research community via open-source platforms.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation, prevention, treatment, and recovery from vascular diseases of the nervous system resulting from a large number of causes, such as ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, spinal cord ischemia, and spinal cord hemorrhage.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of diagnostic ambiguity in complex, multi-parametric clinical laboratory data, which often leads to delayed or inaccurate interpretations in conditions such as autoimmune disorders, rare metabolic diseases, and polymicrobial infections. Traditional analysis methods struggle to integrate high-dimensional data from diverse laboratory modalities—including flow cytometry, mass spectrometry-based proteomics, and automated urinalysis—limiting their ability to detect subtle pathological patterns. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop an adaptive computational framework that unifies machine learning (ML) and topological data analysis (TDA) for enhanced diagnostic decision support. The research will utilize raw instrument outputs and longitudinal patient data from clinical chemistry, immunology, and hematology laboratories to train ensemble ML models capable of identifying cross-modal biomarkers, while TDA will map nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional parameter spaces. HPC resources will enable rapid processing of terabyte-scale datasets, parallelized model training, and real-time simulation of diagnostic scenarios through agent-based modeling. Anticipated outcomes include a validated pipeline for automated pattern recognition in heterogeneous laboratory data, predictive algorithms for early disease stratification, and open-source tools for clinical laboratory integration. This interdisciplinary approach bridges clinical laboratory science with advanced computational analytics, offering transformative potential to reduce diagnostic latency, optimize test utilization, and uncover novel pathophysiological signatures in understudied diseases. Successful implementation could redefine analytical workflows in medical laboratories, advancing precision diagnostics beyond current manual interpretation paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists/medical technologists, to perform routine medical laboratory procedures and tests and to apply preset strategies to record and analyze data. Includes instruction in general laboratory procedures and skills; laboratory mathematics; medical computer applications; interpersonal and communications skills; and the basic principles of hematology, medical microbiology, immunohematology, immunology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop advanced computational models to simulate fire dynamics and suppression systems in complex built environments, addressing critical gaps in predicting fire behavior and optimizing mitigation strategies. Current fire protection system designs rely on simplified empirical models that struggle to account for the coupled interactions of turbulent combustion, heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and structural response in real-world scenarios. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations using FireFOAM and FDS frameworks, validated against experimental fire test data. These simulations will resolve multi-scale phenomena, including flame spread in heterogeneous fuels, smoke transport in ventilation systems, and the efficacy of water-based suppression agents under varying hydraulic conditions. Parametric studies will assess fire risks in diverse building configurations, such as high-rises with compartmentalized spaces and industrial facilities with hazardous material storage. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify optimal sensor placement and suppression system activation thresholds. The computational demands of these simulations—requiring terabytes of memory, thousands of CPU cores for parallel processing, and GPU acceleration for reduced time-to-solution—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation. Outcomes will include predictive models for fire growth in modern construction materials, data-driven guidelines for retrofitting legacy fire protection systems, and scalable frameworks for real-time decision support during fire emergencies. This work will directly inform fire code revisions, equipment standardization, and training protocols, enhancing community resilience against escalating fire risks associated with urbanization and climate change.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and practice of firefighting systems, building construction and related resources as applied to fire prevention, control, and mitigation. Includes instruction in fire hydraulics and dynamics, fire protection structures and systems design, fire behavior and combustion, fire protection hydraulics and water supply, fire protection equipment and systems, building construction for fire protection, and fire apparatus.

abstract: Maternal morbidity and mortality remain significant public health challenges, with persistent disparities in outcomes linked to clinical, social, and biological factors. This project seeks to develop a predictive computational model to identify high-risk pregnancies and optimize care pathways for midwifery patients by analyzing complex interactions between prenatal health indicators, labor progression patterns, and postpartum recovery metrics. Current risk stratification tools lack granularity to process high-dimensional clinical data streams, including continuous fetal monitoring signals, longitudinal biomarker profiles, and socioenvironmental determinants captured in electronic health records (EHRs). We propose a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate heterogeneous data types (time-series sensor data, imaging-derived biometrics, and structured EHR fields) at scale. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models for temporal data and graph neural networks for relational health factors, will be trained on a de-identified dataset of 85,000 midwifery-managed births from a multi-site health system. Computational experiments will focus on (1) predicting unexpected labor complications requiring obstetric intervention and (2) modeling individualized postpartum hemorrhage risk trajectories. The workflow requires distributed training of 3D convolutional networks on ultrasound video data and parallel processing of physiological time series at 1Hz resolution across 72-hour labor epochs. Successful implementation depends on GPU-accelerated nodes for model optimization and large-memory instances for feature engineering across 250+ clinical variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source risk prediction toolkit validated against current clinical standards, with interpretability modules to support shared decision-making. This work aims to advance computational midwifery science by enabling data-driven care personalization while preserving the low-intervention philosophy central to midwifery practice. Results will inform national guidelines on predictive analytics in perinatal care and establish computational infrastructure for future maternal health equity research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to independently deliver babies and treat mothers in the prenatal, delivery, and post-delivery periods. Includes instruction in pre-delivery screening, physician referral, and the care of infants during the delivery and immediate post-delivery phases.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for individuals with neuromotor impairments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize adaptive human-device interfaces. Current assistive technologies, such as robotic exoskeletons and neural prostheses, often rely on generalized control algorithms that fail to account for dynamic physiological changes in users, leading to suboptimal performance and user abandonment. The research problem centers on the lack of real-time, patient-specific computational frameworks capable of integrating multimodal biosignals (e.g., electromyography, inertial sensor data, and cortical activity) to adaptively refine device behavior. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining dynamical systems modeling, deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and Bayesian optimization to iteratively predict and adjust device parameters in response to user-state variability. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of biomechanical simulations, training of DRL agents across heterogeneous datasets (spanning ~10,000 hours of anonymized patient biosignal records), and real-time optimization of control policies under physiological constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive human-device interaction, validated through in silico trials and pilot testing with a cohort of 20 participants with spinal cord injuries. This work bridges gaps in rehabilitation engineering, computational neuroscience, and machine learning, with potential to transform the design of assistive technologies by prioritizing responsiveness to individual neurophysiological states. The scalability of the proposed methods will also lay groundwork for future applications in telerehabilitation and brain-computer interface systems, directly addressing unmet needs in allied health diagnostics and intervention.
cip_title: Allied Health Diagnostic, Intervention, and Treatment Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health diagnostic, intervention, and treatment professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cross-cultural ethical frameworks through computational analysis of philosophical and religious texts spanning diverse traditions. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in moral reasoning that transcend geographic, historical, and doctrinal boundaries, a task complicated by the scale and linguistic complexity of primary sources. Traditional comparative methods struggle to systematically analyze the thousands of digitized manuscripts, commentaries, and liturgical texts required to map ethical concepts across traditions such as Buddhist sutras, Abrahamic scriptures, and Hellenistic philosophy. To address this, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) models on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to perform semantic similarity analysis, concept clustering, and temporal sentiment tracking across multilingual corpora in Sanskrit, Pali, Greek, Arabic, and Classical Chinese. Custom transformer-based architectures will be trained to handle low-resource ancient languages and domain-specific terminology, while graph neural networks will model the diffusion of ethical arguments through annotated textual networks. The computational demands of processing tera-scale tokenized datasets, training multilingual embeddings, and running iterative simulations of conceptual convergence/divergence necessitate GPU-accelerated parallel processing and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping transnational ethical concept flows, 2) quantitative evidence for or against universalist claims in moral philosophy, and 3) new computational methods for interdisciplinary humanities research. By revealing previously undetectable correlations between religious narratives and philosophical systems, this work aims to reshape debates about cultural particularism while demonstrating how HPC resources can advance humanistic inquiry at scale.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in philosophy and religion, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform media content dissemination and its impact on public discourse, addressing the challenge of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets in communication research. Contemporary media ecosystems are characterized by the rapid proliferation of multimodal content—text, images, video—across social networks, news outlets, and digital platforms, necessitating advanced computational tools to unravel complex patterns of information flow. The research employs a mixed-methods approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and network analysis to examine how media frames evolve and propagate across platforms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training deep learning models for multimodal sentiment and thematic analysis, and simulating information diffusion networks in real-time scenarios. By leveraging parallelized workflows and distributed computing frameworks, the project aims to map temporal and spatial variations in media framing, identify amplification mechanisms driven by algorithmic curation, and assess the role of influencer networks in shaping discursive trajectories. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework for cross-platform media analysis, empirical insights into the interdependencies between content modality and virality, and theoretical contributions to understanding digital publics in fragmented media environments. The findings will advance methodological capabilities in communication studies, offering tools for researchers to address pressing questions about misinformation, polarization, and collective sensemaking in the digital age. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in enabling data-driven, interdisciplinary inquiry within non-STEM fields, bridging gaps between computational scalability and theoretical innovation in media scholarship.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication and media studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven pedagogical tools for multilingual classrooms. A critical challenge in bilingual education lies in designing instruction that dynamically responds to learners’ evolving linguistic proficiencies, cultural backgrounds, and cognitive loads. Current approaches often rely on static curricular frameworks or generalized assessments, which fail to account for the complex interplay of sociolinguistic, cognitive, and instructional variables in real-world classrooms. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating longitudinal classroom interaction datasets—including speech, writing samples, and engagement metrics—with cognitive models of bilingual language acquisition. Large-scale natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze multilingual discourse patterns across 10,000+ hours of annotated classroom recordings in Spanish-English and Mandarin-English contexts. Concurrently, neural network architectures will simulate the impact of code-switching frequency, vocabulary complexity, and instructional scaffolding on learning outcomes. These models require HPC resources to process terabytes of multimodal data, train deep learning architectures with cross-lingual embeddings, and run parallelized simulations of instructional scenarios under diverse sociolinguistic parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for optimizing language allocation (L1/L2) in content-based instruction, (2) evidence-based thresholds for cognitive load in simultaneous literacy development, and (3) open-source tools for generating differentiated bilingual lesson plans. By quantifying how specific instructional strategies interact with individual learner trajectories, this work will directly inform teacher preparation programs on data-supported practices for heterogeneous multilingual classrooms. The computational infrastructure will enable scaling to underrepresented language pairs and low-resource educational contexts in subsequent phases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to bilingual/bicultural children or adults, and/or the design and implementation of educational programs having the goal of producing bilingual/bicultural individuals. Includes preparation to serve as teachers and administrators in bilingual/bicultural education programs.

abstract: Audiovisual communication technologies face growing demands for processing high-resolution, multimodal data in real-time applications, yet existing computational infrastructures struggle to balance latency, quality, and scalability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a novel framework for adaptive streaming and immersive audiovisual synthesis using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on optimizing dynamic resource allocation for parallelized encoding/decoding pipelines, leveraging machine learning models to predict and prioritize bandwidth-intensive visual and auditory elements in heterogeneous network environments. Computational workflows will integrate GPU-accelerated neural networks for real-time video super-resolution and spatial audio rendering, paired with distributed computing strategies to synchronize multi-channel data streams. The project will utilize HPC clusters to simulate large-scale user interactions in virtual environments, stress-testing latency thresholds under variable load conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for efficient bitrate adaptation in 4K/8K streaming, validated benchmarks for QoS (Quality of Service) in cloud-based audiovisual production, and a scalable architecture for low-latency telepresence systems. By advancing computational methods tailored to audiovisual workflows, this work aims to directly benefit remote collaboration tools, interactive media platforms, and accessibility technologies—domains critical to modern communication and journalism. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of video/audio datasets, training deep learning models on temporal-spatial features, and emulating global-scale user networks to ensure practical applicability. This research bridges a gap in non-STEM computational innovation, demonstrating how HPC can drive progress in understudied areas of audiovisual technology while adhering to ethical standards for data privacy and inclusive design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in audiovisual communications technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neuroimmunological mechanisms underlying stress-induced alterations in decision-making processes, integrating biophysical modeling of neuro-glial interactions with behavioral data analysis. Chronic stress is known to impair cognitive flexibility and promote maladaptive decision-making, but the role of dynamic neuroimmune signaling—particularly cytokine-mediated modulation of synaptic plasticity in prefrontal-limbic circuits—remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining 1) agent-based modeling of microglial-neuronal crosstalk during stress hormone exposure, 2) network-level simulations of noradrenaline-cortisol-cytokine interactions using coupled differential equations, and 3) machine learning analysis of longitudinal behavioral datasets from stress-challenge paradigms. The computational pipeline will integrate empirical data from multiplex cytokine assays, fMRI-based functional connectivity maps, and behavioral task performance metrics across multiple species. High-performance computing resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of immune-neural parameter spaces, simulating emergent network dynamics across temporal scales (milliseconds to weeks), and performing high-dimensional pattern recognition in heterogeneous biological-behavioral datasets. Expected outcomes include identification of critical thresholds in neuroimmune signaling that predict decision-making deficits, characterization of stress-phase-dependent rewiring in corticostriatal circuits, and predictive models of individual differences in stress vulnerability. This interdisciplinary approach bridges molecular psychiatry, systems immunology, and computational neuroscience to advance our understanding of biopsychological linkages in stress pathophysiology. The resulting models will establish a computational testbed for evaluating theoretical frameworks of mind-body interactions while providing clinically relevant insights into biomarkers for stress-related cognitive disorders.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological and psychological linkages, especially the linkages between biochemical and biophysical activity and the functioning of the central nervous system.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of European social and institutional networks during the Thirty Years’ War (1618–1648), a critical period of state formation and societal fragmentation. The research problem centers on understanding how localized conflicts escalated into a continent-wide crisis, with a focus on the interplay between economic resource distribution, military logistics, and environmental stressors. Traditional historiography relies on qualitative analysis of fragmented archival sources, but this project proposes a computational approach to synthesize disparate datasets—including tax records, grain price fluctuations, troop movement logs, and climate data—into a unified analytical framework. The scale and complexity of these datasets, spanning over 30,000 digitized records across seven modern-day countries, necessitate HPC capabilities to manage data integration, perform spatiotemporal mapping, and run probabilistic simulations. Machine learning models will identify patterns in resource allocation and conflict propagation, while agent-based modeling will simulate decision-making processes of key institutional actors (e.g., mercenary armies, urban councils, and monarchies) under varying constraints. Expected outcomes include a dynamic, open-access geospatial database of war-related socioeconomic metrics and a series of network analyses quantifying the role of logistical bottlenecks in prolonging hostilities. By integrating computational methods with archival scholarship, this project aims to resolve longstanding debates about the war’s geographic unevenness and its legacy for early modern statecraft. The resource allocation request prioritizes GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale network simulations, ensuring scalability as additional datasets are incorporated. Results will provide a template for computational humanities research on premodern European institutions, with implications for interdisciplinary studies of conflict resilience and resource governance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of European society, culture, and institutions from the origins to the present. Includes instruction in European historiography, European history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: Current word processing tools often lack adaptive capabilities to optimize user efficiency and accuracy, particularly when handling large-scale documents or complex formatting tasks.
