This research project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and enhance text processing workflows. The core challenge lies in analyzing real-time user interactions, predicting formatting requirements, and minimizing errors without compromising processing speed—a task that demands significant computational power for parallelizable tasks such as keystroke pattern analysis, automated style optimization, and dynamic error correction. Using machine learning algorithms trained on large datasets of user-generated documents and interaction logs, the project will create predictive models to anticipate formatting adjustments and streamline document assembly processes. HPC clusters will enable rapid iteration of these models across diverse scenarios, including multi-user collaborative environments and high-volume batch processing. Additionally, the research will simulate stress-testing scenarios to evaluate system performance under extreme document sizes (e.g., >10^6 words) or concurrent user loads. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for intelligent document automation, benchmarks for computational efficiency in word processing tasks, and insights into human-computer interaction patterns that can inform future software design. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with user-centric design principles, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for computational tools in text processing, with potential applications in education, technical writing, and enterprise document management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dynamic data ecosystems—spanning heterogeneous sources, evolving schemas, and multi-modal formats—poses critical challenges for scalable integration and real-time analytics. Traditional data warehousing frameworks struggle to adapt to such environments due to rigid architectures, latency in schema harmonization, and inefficiencies in processing high-dimensional, sparsely correlated datasets. This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for autonomous, context-aware data integration and warehousing, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability bottlenecks in semantic mapping, schema evolution, and distributed query optimization. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) designing adaptive graph-based models to represent dynamic metadata relationships across federated data sources, (2) implementing a parallelized engine for probabilistic schema alignment and ontology-driven data fusion, and (3) optimizing in-memory caching strategies for high-throughput ETL (extract, transform, load) workflows in multi-tenant environments. Computational methods will combine large-scale graph neural networks for metadata inference, distributed constraint-solving algorithms for schema consistency, and GPU-accelerated simulations to evaluate partitioning strategies under variable load conditions. The project will utilize HPC resources to train models on synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., IoT sensor networks, cross-institutional biomedical repositories) simulating terabyte-scale ingestion rates and complex query workloads. Expected outcomes include a modular toolkit for self-organizing data warehouses, benchmarks for elasticity in schema-agnostic environments, and novel metrics for evaluating trade-offs between consistency, latency, and resource allocation in hybrid cloud-edge architectures. By enabling efficient integration of disparate, evolving data streams, this work aims to advance capabilities in domains such as precision agriculture, decentralized clinical trials, and smart infrastructure, where rapid data harmonization is critical for decision-making. The computational infrastructure requested will directly support iterative model training, large-scale graph processing, and validation of real-time ingestion pipelines, addressing gaps in current data warehousing paradigms.
cip_title: Data Modeling/ Warehousing and Database Administration
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and manage the construction of databases and related software programs and applications, including the linking of individual data sets to create complex searchable databases (warehousing) and the use of analytical search tools (mining). Includes instruction in database theory, logic, and semantics; operational and warehouse modeling; dimensionality; attributes and hierarchies; data definition; technical architecture; access and security design; integration; formatting and extraction; data delivery; index design; implementation problems; planning and budgeting; and client and networking issues.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computing systems demands innovative approaches to optimize hardware performance, energy efficiency, and reliability. This project addresses the critical challenge of designing next-generation computer hardware architectures capable of supporting emerging computational workloads, such as AI-driven edge computing and heterogeneous processing. Current simulation tools and methodologies struggle to model the interplay between nanoscale circuit behavior, thermal dynamics, and system-level performance at the scale required for cutting-edge hardware development. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a multi-physics computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and optimize hardware designs. The approach integrates finite-element analysis for thermal-electrical co-design, machine learning-driven circuit optimization, and large-scale verification of fault-tolerant architectures. Key objectives include developing adaptive algorithms for power distribution network analysis, automating layout optimization under thermal constraints, and validating reliability models for 3D-integrated circuits. HPC resources are essential to parallelize computationally intensive tasks, including Monte Carlo simulations for process variation analysis, transient modeling of chip-scale power delivery, and topology exploration for reconfigurable computing fabrics. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for hardware designers to rapidly prototype energy-efficient systems, reduce design iteration cycles, and mitigate risks associated with physical prototyping. The project will directly contribute to advancing domestic capabilities in high-performance computing hardware, addressing bottlenecks in semiconductor innovation, and enabling sustainable technology scaling. By bridging gaps between device physics and system-level requirements, this work aims to establish methodologies for co-optimizing performance, manufacturability, and resilience in post-Moore’s Law computing environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and evaluation of computer hardware and related peripheral equipment. Includes instruction in computer circuit and chip design, circuitry, computer systems design, computer equipment design, computer layout planning, testing procedures, and related computer theory and software topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing computational pedagogy training for pre-service computer science educators by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While computer teacher education programs emphasize foundational programming and instructional design, current training frameworks struggle to systematically model the dynamic interactions between teaching strategies, student cognitive load, and learning outcomes in diverse classroom environments. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to simulate and evaluate the efficacy of pedagogical approaches for teaching computational thinking across varied learner demographics. To resolve this, we propose developing an agent-based modeling platform to simulate classroom ecosystems under different instructional scenarios. The computational approach will involve parallelized simulations of student-teacher interactions using parameterized models of learner behavior, curriculum complexity, and instructional pacing. Machine learning methods will then analyze emergent patterns from simulation outputs to identify pedagogical strategies that maximize engagement and skill retention. HPC resources are essential to process the high-dimensional data generated by these simulations, which involve thousands of concurrent agents representing students with distinct learning profiles. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive framework for optimizing lesson plans based on simulated classroom dynamics, 2) quantitative metrics for assessing the cognitive accessibility of programming concepts across age groups, and 3) open-source training modules that integrate these insights into teacher education curricula. By enabling large-scale analysis of pedagogical effectiveness, this work will advance evidence-based practices in computer teacher preparation, particularly for underserved populations where standardized approaches often fail. The resulting models and tools will provide teacher educators with actionable guidance for tailoring instruction to heterogeneous classrooms while maintaining computational rigor.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach computer education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on early literacy development and intervention strategies for K–3 students with reading difficulties. A critical challenge in language and literacy education is identifying individualized instructional pathways for learners who struggle with decoding, fluency, or comprehension, particularly when such challenges stem from complex interactions between cognitive, linguistic, and sociocultural factors. Current diagnostic frameworks often rely on static assessments, limiting educators’ ability to model dynamic learning trajectories or predict responses to targeted interventions. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating longitudinal student performance data, eye-tracking metrics, and natural language processing (NLP) outputs to simulate and analyze reading development patterns. The project will employ machine learning models—including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer-based architectures—to process multimodal datasets encompassing over 10,000 anonymized student records, audiovisual recordings of reading sessions, and standardized assessment results. HPC resources are essential for training these models at scale, enabling parallelized processing of high-dimensional data and iterative optimization of parameters. Key objectives include (1) identifying latent predictors of reading progress using unsupervised clustering techniques, (2) simulating the efficacy of intervention strategies through agent-based modeling, and (3) developing an open-access tool for educators to visualize probabilistic learning pathways. Outcomes will advance theoretical understanding of atypical reading development while providing actionable frameworks for data-driven literacy instruction. By quantifying how specific instructional inputs correlate with growth in phonological awareness or vocabulary acquisition, this work directly supports teacher education programs in designing adaptive curricula. The computational infrastructure requested will ensure robust validation of models across diverse demographic subgroups, addressing equity gaps in literacy education research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach language and literacy subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in language development, typical and atypical reading development, and diagnosing reading difficulties.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize personalized mental health intervention strategies for college students, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal student data. Student counseling services face growing demand, yet traditional methods for matching interventions to individual needs rely on manual assessments and static protocols, which may fail to account for dynamic, interconnected factors such as academic stress, social engagement, and longitudinal mental health trends. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating anonymized student records (e.g., counseling session transcripts, academic performance, campus activity logs) with psychometric survey data. Natural language processing (NLP) will be applied to unstructured session notes to quantify emotional states and therapeutic themes, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) will model temporal and relational patterns in student behavior. The HPC environment is critical for training these models at scale, given the anticipated dataset of 50,000+ student profiles and the computational intensity of processing high-dimensional time-series data. Sensitivity analyses will evaluate model robustness across demographic subgroups to mitigate bias risks. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated tool for recommending tailored counseling approaches based on predictive risk stratification, (2) insights into how academic and social stressors co-evolve with mental health outcomes, and (3) open-source code for ethical AI applications in student services. This work advances education research by demonstrating how computational methods can enhance decision-making in student support systems while preserving human-centered care principles. Results will inform training programs for counselors and institutional policies on scalable mental health resource allocation.
cip_title: Student Counseling and Personnel Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in student counseling and personnel services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic research on Turkish language evolution and dialectal variation across historical and modern contexts. The primary research problem centers on the challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous text corpora spanning pre-modern Ottoman Turkish (using Perso-Arabic script) and modern Turkish (Latin script), which exhibit significant grammatical, lexical, and orthographic shifts. Traditional manual methods are insufficient for identifying patterns in phonology, morphology, and semantic change across these variants, particularly when analyzing understudied dialects or non-standard texts from regional archives. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for cross-script alignment, neural machine translation for historical text normalization, and graph-based algorithms to map dialectal features. Computational philological workflows will be developed to automate the analysis of morphological segmentation in agglutinative structures and detect loanword integration from Arabic, Persian, and European languages. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning models on multi-terabyte corpora, parallelizing comparative analyses across temporal and geographic axes, and running computationally intensive simulations of language change. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for Ottoman Turkish NLP, a diachronic corpus annotated for linguistic features, and quantitative models tracing syntactic simplification trends from the 15th to 21st centuries. These resources will enable novel research on language contact phenomena in Anatolian dialects and accelerate the digitization of endangered vernacular texts. By bridging computational methods with Turkological scholarship, this project aims to establish a scalable framework for studying lesser-resourced languages with complex historical trajectories, while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Turkish language in either or both of its pre-modern and modern variants. Includes instruction in philology; Ottoman Turkish; Modern Turkish; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) systems face critical challenges in dynamically allocating resources across unpredictable, high-acuity environments, particularly during mass casualty incidents (MCIs) and disasters. Current strategies for optimizing pre-hospital care delivery, responder deployment, and patient routing often rely on static protocols or historical data, which inadequately address real-time variables such as fluctuating incident severity, geographic constraints, and resource scarcity. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate EMS operations under diverse crisis scenarios, enabling data-driven improvements in system design, medical oversight, and clinical outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) integrating real-world geospatial data, patient injury patterns, and EMS logistics to simulate interactions between responders, patients, and infrastructure. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze historical EMS datasets, identifying predictors of operational bottlenecks and patient outcomes, while Monte Carlo methods will assess uncertainty in disaster response workflows. The simulations will evaluate interventions such as dynamic ambulance repositioning, adaptive triage protocols, and multi-agency coordination strategies. By scaling these computationally intensive models across HPC clusters, we aim to generate granular insights into system resilience, response time optimization, and resource utilization during MCIs. Outcomes will include validated decision-support tools for EMS administrators, predictive analytics frameworks for medical directors, and evidence-based recommendations for wilderness EMS and disaster planning. This work directly advances the clinical and operational rigor of pre-hospital care systems, with potential to reduce mortality in time-sensitive emergencies and enhance preparedness for large-scale public health crises.
cip_definition: Research focused on the leadership and medical oversight of pre- and out-of-hospital emergency care systems with advanced competencies in Emergency Medical System (EMS) system design, administration, and clinical care. Includes instruction in clinical aspects of EMS, medical oversight of EMS, mass casualty management, disaster planning and operations, wilderness EMS systems, and quality management and research.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze cross-cultural musical transmission and innovation through large-scale comparative analysis of audio recordings and symbolic music data. Current research in musicology and ethnomusicology lacks scalable methods to systematically identify patterns of melodic, rhythmic, and timbral evolution across diverse cultural contexts, particularly when examining understudied oral traditions and non-Western repertoires. The research will employ high-performance computing resources to process and analyze multimodal datasets encompassing field recordings, historical transcriptions, and contemporary performances from 15 distinct global traditions, including Balinese gamelan, West African drumming, and Appalachian folk music. Machine learning models—including transformer-based architectures for sequence modeling and contrastive learning networks for timbral similarity detection—will be trained to detect latent structural relationships within and between musical traditions. Computational musicological methods will be augmented by phylogenetic analysis adapted from biological sciences to model potential genealogies of musical influence. The workflow requires distributed computing for feature extraction across 50,000+ audio segments and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models with cross-modal attention mechanisms. Expected outcomes include a quantitative taxonomy of cross-cultural musical convergences in post-colonial contexts, computational tools for automated style analysis in endangered traditions, and novel methodologies for modeling non-linear transmission pathways in oral music cultures. By integrating HPC capabilities with ethnomusicological domain knowledge, this project aims to establish new paradigms for studying musical globalization while addressing critical gaps in the preservation and analysis of intangible cultural heritage. The resource-intensive nature of processing heterogeneous audio archives and training complex models on multi-terabyte datasets necessitates specialized computing infrastructure beyond typical academic workstations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the forms and methods of music art, and the functions of music, in Western and non-Western societies and cultures. Includes instruction in music theory, musicological research methods, and studies of specific cultural styles such as jazz, folk music, rock, ethnic musical traditions, and the music of non-Western cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable numerical methods for solving high-dimensional, nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in multiscale fluid-structure interaction problems, with applications to biomedical engineering and renewable energy systems. The core challenge lies in efficiently resolving coupled dynamics across disparate spatial and temporal scales while maintaining numerical stability, particularly for problems involving complex geometries or stochastic boundary conditions. Traditional discretization techniques struggle with the computational cost of resolving fine-scale features in three-dimensional domains, necessitating advanced algorithmic strategies. The proposed approach combines adaptive finite element methods with parallelized model reduction frameworks, leveraging tensor-train decompositions to compress high-dimensional solution manifolds. Key innovations include hybrid CPU-GPU implementations of iterative solvers for ill-conditioned linear systems and dynamic load-balancing algorithms to optimize resource utilization during mesh adaptation cycles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for benchmarking these methods against established solvers on large-scale test cases, including pulsatile blood flow in deformable arterial networks and turbulent wake interactions in offshore wind turbine arrays. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for parameter-sensitive preconditioning and data-driven reduced-order modeling, validated on O(10^4) core-hour simulations using petascale-ready codebases. The project will quantify trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost for problems with >10^8 degrees of freedom, providing guidelines for HPC-driven PDE solver design. Successful implementation will advance predictive modeling capabilities for multiphysics systems while contributing new methodological insights at the intersection of numerical analysis and computational science. Resource requests focus on allocations for memory-intensive computations (>1 TB per node) and sustained access to multi-node GPU clusters to profile weak scaling performance up to 16,384 cores.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of culinary precision and innovation through computational modeling of complex gastronomic processes. The research focuses on optimizing cooking techniques and ingredient interactions in large-scale food production, addressing challenges such as inconsistent texture, flavor degradation, and energy inefficiency in commercial kitchens. Current empirical approaches to recipe scaling and equipment calibration lack predictive accuracy, particularly for novel cooking methods (e.g., sous-vide, flash-freezing) or alternative protein matrices. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning to model heat and mass transfer phenomena during cooking. High-fidelity simulations will analyze time-temperature profiles in heterogeneous food systems, predict protein denaturation pathways, and quantify nutrient retention under varying processing conditions. A parallelized workflow will process tera-scale datasets capturing ingredient physicochemical properties, equipment performance metrics, and sensory outcome correlations from partnered culinary institutes. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from controlled cooking trials, with iterative model refinement using neural networks trained on heterogeneous data streams (thermal imaging, spectroscopy, sensory panels). Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing cooking parameters in industrial kitchens, reducing energy consumption by 15–20% through dynamic equipment scheduling algorithms, and enabling data-driven design of plant-based meat analogs with improved palatability. This work establishes a novel computational paradigm for culinary science, merging food chemistry, thermodynamics, and data analytics to address pressing challenges in sustainable food systems and global foodservice operations. By transcending traditional trial-and-error methodologies, the project aims to catalyze innovation in culinary arts education and industrial practice through quantitatively grounded, computation-first approaches.
cip_title: Cooking and Related Culinary Arts, General.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of the cooking and related culinary arts, and that may prepare individuals for a variety of jobs within the food service industry.  Includes instruction in food preparation, cooking techniques, equipment operation and maintenance, sanitation and safety, communication skills, applicable regulations, and principles of food service management.

abstract: Coastal ecosystems are increasingly threatened by interacting stressors such as warming, acidification, and hypoxia, yet the nonlinear feedbacks between these processes and marine microbial communities remain poorly quantified. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of how microbial-driven biogeochemical cycles modulate coastal ecosystem resilience under multiparameter environmental change. We propose a high-resolution, coupled physical-biogeochemical modeling approach to simulate microbial metabolism, nutrient fluxes, and dissolved oxygen dynamics across estuarine gradients. The computational framework will integrate hydrodynamic data from regional ocean models with genome-informed trait-based representations of microbial functional groups, requiring iterative parameter optimization and ensemble simulations at scales from meters to kilometers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale turbulence-particle interactions, run parallelized sensitivity analyses across decadal time series, and assimilate observational data from autonomous sensors and multi-omics datasets. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated simulations for machine learning-based parameterization of microbial growth kinetics and hybrid modeling techniques to bridge molecular-scale processes with ecosystem-level emergent properties. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source model capable of predicting tipping points in coastal oxygen budgets, quantitative assessments of how archaeal methanogenesis and bacterial sulfur cycling respond to concurrent stressors, and improved forecasts of carbon sequestration potential in eutrophic estuaries. By elucidating microbial mediation of coastal biogeochemical resilience, this work will directly inform management strategies for water quality and climate adaptation. The requested allocation of 1.2 million CPU-core hours and 200 TB of dedicated storage will enable the scaling of these computationally intensive simulations across heterogeneous coastal zones while maintaining the resolution required to capture microbial niche partitioning and redox threshold dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of biology, chemistry, geology and physics applied to marine, estuarine and coastal environments. Includes instruction in marine biogeochemistry, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, coastal ecology, coastal ocean processes, microbial ecology, marine ecosystem modeling, and polar microbiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of generative design and real-time environmental simulation within architectural technology. The central challenge lies in optimizing complex building systems for energy efficiency, structural resilience, and spatial functionality under dynamic environmental conditions—a task requiring iterative analysis of multi-physics interactions that exceed the capabilities of conventional architectural software. Current workflows in architectural practice rely on compartmentalized simulations (e.g., static thermal models or isolated structural analyses), leading to suboptimal solutions when addressing interconnected design parameters. This project proposes a computational framework that unifies parametric modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization into a cohesive HPC pipeline. By parallelizing simulations across climate zones, material properties, and usage scenarios, the system will enable rapid exploration of design alternatives that balance competing priorities such as embodied carbon reduction, passive heating/cooling performance, and adaptive reuse potential. Key computational methods include GPU-accelerated physics engines for real-time feedback, graph-based optimization algorithms to navigate high-dimensional design spaces, and uncertainty quantification to assess robustness against climate variability. The research will utilize existing architectural datasets and generate new synthetic training data for predictive models. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scalable architectural performance analysis, validated through case studies on mixed-use urban structures in climatically diverse regions. By democratizing access to HPC-driven design exploration, this work aims to bridge the gap between academic research and practical architectural workflows, empowering practitioners to create buildings that proactively respond to environmental challenges while maintaining aesthetic and functional rigor. Success will be measured by computational efficiency gains over industry-standard tools, quantitative improvements in energy performance predictions, and the toolkit’s adoption in pedagogical settings for architectural technology programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist architects in developing plans and related documentation and in performing architectural office services. Includes instruction in architectural drafting, computer-assisted drafting and design, construction methods and materials, environmental systems, building codes and standards, structural principles, cost estimation, planning documentation, visual communication skills, display production, and architectural office management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance voice writing technology by addressing critical gaps in real-time transcription accuracy and adaptability across diverse linguistic and acoustic environments. Voice writing systems—essential for live captioning, media accessibility, and transcription services—often struggle with variability in speech patterns, background noise, speaker accents, and domain-specific terminology, leading to errors that hinder communication access. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to train and optimize adaptive neural speech recognition models capable of processing multimodal inputs (audio, contextual metadata, and user corrections) while maintaining low latency for real-time applications. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models and dynamic acoustic adaptation algorithms, to improve contextual awareness and robustness. Large-scale datasets of spoken shorthand, live event recordings, and annotated corrections will be used to simulate challenging real-world conditions, enabling iterative model refinement. Computational workflows will prioritize parallel processing to reduce training times for resource-intensive tasks such as noise-invariant feature extraction and speaker diarization. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source voice writing toolkit with enhanced accuracy (targeting <5% word error rate in noisy environments) and adaptive personalization features for professional captioners and journalists. This work will directly benefit accessibility initiatives, media production workflows, and remote communication platforms by reducing barriers to high-quality transcription. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s data volume (estimated at 50TB of audio-text pairs) and computational demands, enabling rapid experimentation with model architectures that would otherwise be infeasible on local infrastructure. By bridging computational linguistics with user-centered design, this project aims to set new benchmarks for equitable access to voice-driven communication technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to use voice writing computer software and speak a verbal shorthand language to create transcripts and screen captioning of live or recorded events intended for the public or a specific audience in a variety of media (e.g., digital, film, print, television) as well as for conferences, conversations, interviews, and meetings. Includes instruction in screen captioning, speed building, spoken shorthand, transcription, and voice input writing.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the role of mechanical forces in cancer progression within solid tumor microenvironments, with a focus on biomechanical interactions between tumors and surrounding tissues. Despite growing evidence that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness and cellular stress influence tumor growth, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, the multiscale mechanical mechanisms driving these processes remain poorly quantified. This project aims to develop high-resolution computational models of tumor-ECM systems to analyze how spatially heterogeneous mechanical forces regulate cellular behaviors such as proliferation, migration, and apoptosis. A central challenge lies in simulating dynamic, three-dimensional tissue environments at physiologically relevant scales while capturing subcellular mechanotransduction pathways. To address this, we propose a hybrid finite element modeling (FEM) framework integrating continuum-level tissue mechanics with agent-based cellular responses, calibrated using experimental data from in vitro tumor models subjected to controlled mechanical loading. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the nonlinear, time-dependent interactions across multiple spatial scales (µm to mm) and temporal domains (seconds to days). Simulations will leverage parallelized solvers for large-scale matrix computations and GPU acceleration for real-time visualization of force propagation. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of stress distribution in tumors under varying mechanical conditions, identification of critical thresholds for ECM remodeling, and correlations between localized strain patterns and metastatic potential. This work will advance understanding of biomechanical regulation in oncology, potentially informing strategies to disrupt force-mediated cancer progression. The computational pipeline developed will also serve as a adaptable platform for future studies on mechanobiological phenomena in other physiological systems. Resource allocation will directly support 20+ concurrent simulations, each requiring 48-72 hours of runtime on 128-core nodes with 256 GB RAM, necessitating access to HPC clusters with advanced numerical libraries and capacity for petascale data output.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, anatomical, and mechanical structure and function of the mechanical aspects of biological systems. Includes courses in anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, mechanics, measurement and instrumentation, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis and generative modeling of large-scale visual art datasets, with a focus on resolving challenges in pattern recognition, stylistic evolution, and interactive digital art creation. A central research problem lies in the limitations of existing tools for processing high-resolution, multidimensional visual data—such as 3D scans of historical artworks, dynamic digital media installations, or cross-cultural visual corpora—which require advanced computational power to analyze and synthesize effectively. The project will employ machine learning frameworks, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), to map stylistic features, predict aesthetic trends, and simulate complex material interactions in virtual environments. Additionally, real-time rendering pipelines will be optimized using parallel computing to enable collaborative, interactive art creation in immersive platforms. By integrating HPC-driven simulations with art historical datasets and contemporary digital practices, this research aims to produce scalable tools for artists and scholars, facilitating novel insights into the relationship between technological innovation and visual expression. Expected outcomes include open-source software for artifact preservation, a publicly accessible database of computationally analyzed stylistic patterns, and proof-of-concept interactive installations that demonstrate the potential of HPC in democratizing access to advanced visual design tools. The project bridges computational scalability with artistic experimentation, offering a framework for interdisciplinary collaboration in digital humanities and media studies while addressing critical gaps in resource-intensive visual arts research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the visual and performing arts and that may prepare individuals in any of the visual artistic media or performing disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize school-level administrative decision-making processes in K-7 educational settings, with a focus on resource allocation, emergency response planning, and student outcome forecasting. School administrators face complex challenges in balancing finite resources—such as staffing, budgets, and facility usage—with dynamic variables including fluctuating enrollment, safety protocols, and evolving pedagogical needs. Traditional decision-support tools often lack the capacity to simulate multi-variable scenarios or account for longitudinal data on student development. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate school operations under diverse constraints. These models will integrate anonymized demographic data, historical budget records, and facility blueprints from partner school districts, alongside synthetically generated datasets representing hypothetical scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify patterns in administrative efficiency and predict the downstream effects of policy decisions on student performance metrics. A key innovation involves coupling discrete-event simulations of daily school operations with geospatial analyses to optimize emergency evacuation routes and resource deployment during crisis events. The computational intensity of running thousands of parallel simulations across multi-year timescales necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with robust GPU acceleration and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit for school leaders, empirically validated strategies for equitable resource distribution, and evidence-based protocols for crisis management. By bridging computational modeling with practical administrative needs, this work aims to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and equity in elementary and middle school settings while maintaining strict adherence to ethical standards for data privacy and educational equity.
cip_title: Elementary and Middle School Administration/ Principalship
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the elementary and middle school (K-7) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of elementary and middle schools. Includes instruction in elementary and/or middle school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, childhood and pre-adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the classification and structural properties of high-dimensional algebraic structures, particularly focusing on the cohomology and representation theory of Lie algebras and their associated modules. A central challenge in modern algebraic research lies in resolving the combinatorial and geometric complexity inherent to these structures, especially as their dimensionality increases. Traditional computational methods often fail to address the scale of these problems due to exponential growth in memory and processing requirements, necessitating advanced high-performance computing (HPC) solutions. The research aims to develop and implement parallelized algorithms for computing invariants such as Ext-groups, Betti numbers, and decomposition matrices in graded Lie algebra modules, which are critical for advancing classification conjectures in non-associative algebra and representation theory. Key computational tasks include the symbolic manipulation of large tensor products, Gröbner basis computations for ideals in universal enveloping algebras, and homology calculations via distributed-memory chain complex resolutions. These methods will leverage MPI-based parallelization to distribute workloads across multiple nodes, optimizing memory usage and reducing computation times for tasks exceeding the limits of single-node systems. The project will utilize existing open-source algebraic software (e.g., GAP, Singular) while extending their functionality through custom C++ and Python modules for HPC integration. Expected outcomes include the resolution of open questions regarding the stability of cohomology dimensions in certain Lie algebra families, as well as new algorithms for efficient module decomposition. Results will contribute foundational insights to algebraic geometry and mathematical physics, with potential applications in the study of symmetries in high-energy particle models. By enabling large-scale algebraic computations, this work will provide a framework for future research in pure algebra, bridging theoretical advances with computational innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on algebraic structures and linear algebra.

abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is a critical intervention for conditions such as decompression sickness, non-healing wounds, and carbon monoxide poisoning. However, optimizing treatment protocols—particularly balancing therapeutic efficacy with risks of oxygen toxicity and barotrauma—remains challenging due to the complex interplay of physiological, environmental, and patient-specific variables. This project seeks to develop patient-specific computational models to simulate tissue oxygenation dynamics, inert gas exchange, and decompression stress under varied hyperbaric conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these multi-physics processes at clinically relevant spatiotemporal scales. Using finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics, we will construct 3D models of human anatomy integrated with physiological parameters (e.g., perfusion rates, metabolic demand) derived from anonymized patient data. These models will simulate gas diffusion in tissues during hyperbaric exposures, predict oxygen radical formation linked to toxicity, and evaluate decompression trajectories to minimize microbubble formation. Machine learning techniques will be applied to clinical datasets to identify predictors of adverse events and refine model inputs. The computational workflow will leverage parallel processing to perform parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated treatment scenarios, enabling probabilistic risk assessment and protocol optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to personalize pressure-time profiles, reduce complications, and improve adherence to hyperbaric safety standards. By elucidating mechanisms of tissue injury and resilience, this work will advance fundamental understanding of hyperbaric physiology while directly addressing a translational need in clinical practice. The resulting open-source framework will provide a scalable platform for future research in hyperbaric medicine, enhancing both patient outcomes and operational safety in chamber management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to operate hyperbaric (recompression) chambers for the treatment of disease. Includes instruction in patient assessment and management, hyperbaric safety, physics of hyperbaric and hypobaric exposures, physiology, hyperbaric chamber operation, and air decompression procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized educational interventions for students with intellectual disabilities (ID), leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of personalizing learning strategies at scale. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual, qualitative assessments, which are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict the long-term efficacy of pedagogical strategies across diverse cognitive and behavioral profiles. To overcome these barriers, we propose a data-driven approach integrating multimodal student data—including academic performance, behavioral observations, and sensor-based engagement metrics—with computational models of learning progression. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and simulated datasets to identify patterns in skill acquisition, predict barriers to learning, and recommend adaptive instructional strategies tailored to individual needs. HPC resources are critical for processing large datasets, running complex simulations of intervention outcomes, and optimizing parameters for heterogeneous learner populations. The project will also employ agent-based modeling to simulate classroom dynamics, enabling the testing of intervention scalability under varying resource constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators to generate evidence-based IEP recommendations, validated through partnerships with K-12 special education programs. By bridging computational analytics and special education praxis, this work aims to empower teachers with actionable insights, reduce disparities in educational access, and improve functional and academic outcomes for students with ID. The scalability of the proposed models will also inform policy discussions on equitable resource allocation in special education.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with intellectual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with intellectual disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising mentally handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Groundwater systems are critical for sustaining freshwater resources, yet their responses to climate variability and anthropogenic stressors remain poorly quantified at regional scales. This project addresses the urgent need to advance predictive modeling of coupled surface-subsurface hydrological processes under changing climatic and land-use conditions. Current models often oversimplify heterogeneous aquifer structures or decouple surface and groundwater interactions, leading to uncertainties in projecting water availability and contamination risks. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-resolution, three-dimensional integrated hydrologic model leveraging parallel computing to simulate dynamic feedbacks between precipitation, evapotranspiration, surface runoff, and groundwater flow. The computational framework combines finite element discretization for variably saturated porous media with GPU-accelerated solvers for efficient simulation of large domains. Key innovations include stochastic parameterization of subsurface heterogeneity using geostatistical borehole data and assimilation of remote sensing-derived soil moisture and groundwater level measurements via ensemble Kalman filtering. The model will be applied to a drought-prone agricultural basin in the southwestern U.S., where groundwater overdraft and nitrate contamination threaten long-term water security. Simulations will quantify recharge dynamics under projected climate scenarios (RCP 4.5/8.5) and evaluate managed aquifer recharge strategies. The HPC resources requested are essential to achieve the required spatial resolution (≤100 m grid cells) and multi-decadal temporal scales, with an estimated 250,000 core-hours needed for ensemble runs and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) improved mechanistic understanding of how aquifer heterogeneity modulates climate impacts on groundwater resilience, (2) open-source release of optimized simulation workflows for community use, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for conjunctive water management policies. By bridging gaps between process hydrology and computational scalability, this work will provide actionable science for stakeholders addressing water scarcity challenges in semi-arid regions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the occurrence, circulation, distribution, chemical and physical properties, and environmental interaction of surface and subsurface waters, including groundwater. Includes instruction in geophysics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, chemical physics, geomorphology, mathematical modeling, hydrologic analysis, continental water processes, global water balance, and environmental science.

abstract: This project investigates the psychological dynamics of collective decision-making in augmented reality (AR) environments, focusing on how spatially embedded digital interfaces alter group cognition and consensus formation. While traditional social psychology examines face-to-face or virtual group interactions, the integration of persistent AR overlays—digital artifacts anchored to physical spaces—introduces novel cognitive-perceptual challenges. The research problem centers on quantifying how multi-sensory AR cues (e.g., geolocated data visualizations, shared holographic objects) modulate attention allocation, information prioritization, and conflict resolution strategies in time-sensitive collaborative tasks. Using a custom Unity-based AR platform integrated with eye-tracking and motion capture, we will simulate urban planning scenarios requiring groups of participants to negotiate competing priorities under resource constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) real-time rendering of complex 3D environments with physics-based interactions across multiple AR headsets, (2) computational modeling of emergent decision patterns through agent-based simulations (NetLogo) to test intervention strategies, and (3) machine learning analysis (PyTorch) of multimodal behavioral datasets (gaze patterns, gesture sequences, vocal prosody) to identify predictors of optimal vs. suboptimal group outcomes. Expected outcomes include a framework for AR-mediated group cognition that advances theoretical understanding of distributed situational awareness in hybrid physical-digital spaces. The computational models will inform design principles for next-generation collaborative interfaces, with potential applications in crisis management training and participatory urban design. By bridging environmental psychology, human-computer interaction, and complex systems science, this work establishes a foundation for studying embodied collective intelligence in emerging mixed-reality ecosystems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical and physiological dynamics of human lactation through advanced computational modeling. Despite the clinical importance of breastfeeding, current approaches to managing lactation challenges—such as inefficient milk transfer, maternal pain, or infant latch anomalies—rely on observational assessments and generalized protocols. A mechanistic understanding of the interplay between mammary tissue mechanics, infant oral motor patterns, and milk flow dynamics remains understudied, limiting evidence-based interventions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing high-resolution, multi-scale computational models of the lactating breast and infant feeding biomechanics. These models will integrate anatomical data from 3D ultrasound imaging, material properties of mammary tissues, and fluid-structure interaction simulations to map stress distributions during milk ejection and infant suckling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the complex, nonlinear interactions between viscoelastic tissues, transient pressure gradients, and non-Newtonian milk flow at physiologically relevant spatiotemporal scales. Machine learning techniques will be applied to parameterize model inputs using clinical datasets from lactation consultations, including infant intraoral pressure measurements and maternal symptom reports. The resulting simulations will identify biomechanical risk factors for common lactation complications and predict the efficacy of positioning or device-based interventions. Outcomes will provide the first quantitative framework for personalized lactation support, enabling consultants to tailor strategies based on biomechanical profiling. This work also lays the foundation for virtual training tools to enhance clinical education. By leveraging HPC to decode the biophysics of lactation, the project advances an emerging niche at the intersection of maternal-infant health, biomechanics, and computational physiology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide lactation management services and breastfeeding support to women, and to work as a Lactation Consultant in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology of lactation, nutrition, breastfeeding techniques and technologies, common concerns and solutions, management of special situations, breastfeeding instruction, professional and legal concerns, and advocacy.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes in emergency and trauma nursing through the development of predictive computational models for acute care scenarios. Trauma patients often present with complex, dynamic physiological states requiring rapid intervention, yet existing protocols struggle to account for multivariate interactions between injury patterns, pharmacogenomic factors, and time-sensitive treatment pathways. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning-driven approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets. These include retrospective electronic health records (EHRs) from Level I trauma centers, real-time vital sign streams, pharmacodynamic data, and imaging-derived biomarkers. Computational workflows will integrate feature engineering for variables such as injury severity scores, fluid resuscitation responses, and coagulopathy indicators, while reinforcement learning techniques will simulate optimal intervention sequences under time constraints. The HPC environment is critical for training ensemble models on terabyte-scale datasets, executing parallelized parameter sweeps, and validating predictions against synthetic trauma scenarios generated via agent-based simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) risk stratification algorithms for early identification of patients at high risk of sepsis, hemorrhagic shock, or multi-organ failure, and (2) adaptive decision-support tools to guide nurse-driven interventions in resource-constrained emergency departments. By quantifying nonlinear relationships between trauma mechanisms, physiological resilience, and treatment timing, this research aims to reduce preventable complications and inform precision nursing practices. The computational framework will be shared as open-source modules to facilitate replication in diverse clinical settings, advancing both emergency nursing education and translational trauma informatics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver advanced, direct patient care in emergency and trauma settings. Includes instruction in advanced health assessment, pharmacology, physiology, emergency management, trauma conditions, trauma assessments and acute care.

abstract: This research project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual and conceptual analysis of early Christian theological debates and their development across denominational traditions. The primary research problem lies in the complexity of tracing doctrinal evolution within Christianity, particularly the interplay between scriptural interpretation, philosophical frameworks, and cultural contexts in foundational texts from the first five centuries CE. Manual analysis of these interconnected dynamics is hindered by the vast corpus of multilingual patristic writings, conciliar documents, and apocryphal literature, necessitating computational methods to identify patterns, semantic shifts, and cross-referential networks. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Koine Greek, Latin, and Coptic texts to analyze theological terminology, argumentative structures, and citation practices across approximately 10,000 digitized documents. Machine learning models will be trained to classify doctrinal positions, map conceptual relationships, and detect intra-textual influences, while graph-based algorithms will visualize the diffusion of ideas among early Christian communities. Computational demands include parallel processing for corpus-wide topic modeling, GPU-accelerated transformer training for low-resource ancient languages, and large-scale semantic similarity calculations. Expected outcomes include a searchable database of cross-denominational theological linkages, quantitative maps of doctrinal development timelines, and interactive tools for comparative analysis of exegetical strategies. These resources will provide scholars with novel methodologies to investigate understudied connections between scriptural hermeneutics and philosophical reasoning in formative Christian thought, offering empirical insights into how cultural and intellectual contexts shaped core theological concepts. The project aligns with contemporary interdisciplinary approaches in religious studies, bridging traditional hermeneutics with computational humanities to deepen understanding of Christianity’s intellectual heritage.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy and teachings of Jesus Christ and his apostles, and the subsequent intellectual and cultural movements and institutions based on Christianity. Includes instruction in Christian sacred scripture, Christian literature and philosophy, and studies of one or more of the main branches of the faith and their cultural context including Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism, Protestantism, Evangelicalism, and others.

abstract: The analysis of complex chemical systems, such as multicomponent environmental samples or dynamic biological matrices, presents significant challenges in achieving high-resolution, real-time characterization of molecular interactions and reaction pathways. Current experimental methods in analytical chemistry, including chromatography and spectroscopy, often require complementary computational modeling to resolve overlapping signals, predict emergent behaviors, and optimize detection protocols. However, existing computational tools struggle to balance accuracy with the scalability needed for large datasets or systems involving thousands of interacting species. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations, machine learning-driven spectral deconvolution algorithms, and multiscale kinetic modeling frameworks. The computational workflows will integrate density functional theory (DFT) for electronic structure analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) for solvation effects, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to identify latent patterns in high-dimensional spectral and chromatographic data. These methods will be validated against experimental datasets from laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) studies of environmental pollutants and pharmaceutical intermediates. By enabling atomistic resolution of intermolecular interactions and rapid processing of terabyte-scale analytical datasets, this work aims to establish predictive models for signal optimization, reduce false positives in trace analyte detection, and uncover kinetic bottlenecks in catalytic systems. The outcomes will directly enhance the precision of analytical workflows in contaminant monitoring, drug impurity profiling, and metabolomics. Access to HPC resources is critical due to the parallelizable nature of ensemble simulations, the memory demands of training deep learning models on spectral libraries, and the need for real-time computational support during time-sensitive experimental campaigns. This project will advance the integration of computational chemistry with analytical instrumentation, fostering a paradigm shift toward data-driven, hypothesis-generating laboratory practices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of techniques for analyzing and describing matter, including its precise composition and the interrelationships of constituent elements and compounds. Includes instruction in spectroscopy, chromatography, atomic absorption, photometry, chemical modeling, mathematical analysis, laboratory analysis procedures and equipment maintenance, and applications to specific research, industrial and health problems.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation faces significant challenges in optimizing therapeutic interventions for children with neuromuscular impairments, such as cerebral palsy or spinal cord injuries. Current clinical approaches rely on sparse, heterogeneous datasets and simplified biomechanical models, limiting their ability to predict individualized treatment outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to analyze high-dimensional movement data, simulate neuromuscular responses to interventions, and identify personalized rehabilitation strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including motion capture, electromyography, and neuroimaging—from a cohort of 500+ pediatric patients. Computational workflows will integrate musculoskeletal modeling, finite element simulations of tissue adaptation, and machine learning algorithms to predict functional outcomes under varying therapeutic conditions. A key innovation involves coupling patient-specific neural control models with biomechanical simulations to quantify how motor learning protocols influence long-term recovery trajectories. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across diverse patient subgroups, enabling real-time parameter optimization in complex simulations, and training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models of motor recovery, (2) computationally optimized intervention parameters for distinct impairment profiles, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive clinical decision support. This work will provide the first quantitative framework linking neuroplasticity mechanisms to functional gains in pediatric rehabilitation, addressing a critical gap in evidence-based practice. By enabling large-scale simulation of intervention strategies, the project aims to reduce trial-and-error in clinical care while establishing computational benchmarks for personalized rehabilitation protocols. The requested allocation supports GPU-accelerated workloads, parallelized simulation jobs, and secure storage for sensitive clinical data, which are essential for achieving statistically robust results within clinically relevant timescales.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Rehabilitation

abstract: Pediatric radiology faces unique challenges in diagnostic imaging due to the dynamic anatomical and physiological changes across developmental stages, coupled with the need to minimize radiation exposure and invasive procedures in young patients. Current imaging protocols and diagnostic tools are often adapted from adult studies, which may not account for pediatric-specific pathologies, size variations, or motion artifacts. This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize pediatric imaging workflows, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and enable personalized risk-stratified protocols. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning algorithms on multimodal pediatric imaging datasets (MRI, CT, and ultrasound) from diverse age groups and pathologies, including congenital anomalies, oncology, and trauma. Computational pipelines will integrate image segmentation, artifact correction, and feature extraction tailored to pediatric anatomy, with a focus on minimizing radiation dose in CT through synthetic image generation and dose simulation. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be employed to augment limited pediatric datasets, addressing data scarcity while preserving demographic and pathological diversity. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-resolution 3D/4D imaging data, running iterative simulations, and validating models across multi-institutional cohorts. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated pediatric image analysis, validated age-specific imaging protocols, and predictive models linking imaging biomarkers to clinical outcomes. This work aims to establish a computational framework that improves diagnostic precision, reduces procedural risks, and supports evidence-based imaging guidelines for pediatric populations. By prioritizing scalability and interoperability, the resulting resources will foster collaboration across pediatric radiology networks, ultimately advancing equitable access to high-quality diagnostic care for children worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on all forms of diagnostic imaging as it pertains to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases in the newborn, infant, child, and adolescent.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving complexity of human resources (HR) legal frameworks and their operational impacts on organizations. The research addresses the challenge of systematically interrogating large-scale, unstructured legal datasets—including court rulings, labor legislation, regulatory guidance, and corporate compliance records—to identify patterns in legal risk, compliance gaps, and policy interpretation. Traditional legal analysis struggles to process the volume and interdependencies of these documents, particularly as jurisdictions increasingly digitize legal systems and generate dynamic, text-based regulatory updates. The project employs computational legal analytics, combining natural language processing (NLP), graph-based network modeling, and machine learning (ML) to map relationships between legal provisions, judicial outcomes, and organizational responses. Custom NLP pipelines will classify text from heterogeneous sources (e.g., case law databases, HR policy manuals) to train models predicting compliance vulnerabilities and litigation trends. Network analysis will visualize how specific legal clauses propagate across jurisdictions or industries, while ML-driven simulations will stress-test hypothetical HR policies against historical litigation data. By deploying these methods on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in training large language models on legal corpora and running parallelized simulations of regulatory scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access toolkit for quantifying HR legal risk and a framework for real-time monitoring of regulatory changes. This work bridges computational social science and legal informatics, offering organizations data-driven strategies to navigate compliance and contributing foundational insights into how algorithmic methods can advance the study of law beyond traditional doctrinal analysis. The results will inform interdisciplinary scholarship on the scalability of legal systems in digital economies and establish precedents for HPC applications in non-STEM professional disciplines.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting human resources.

abstract: Women’s health nursing requires evidence-based approaches to address complex, multifactorial conditions that disproportionately or uniquely affect women, such as maternal mortality, preterm birth, and gynecologic cancers. Current clinical decision-making often relies on generalized risk models that fail to account for dynamic interactions between biological, social, and environmental factors. This project seeks to develop predictive models for adverse pregnancy outcomes and optimize pharmacotherapeutic protocols for women with comorbid conditions (e.g., gestational diabetes and hypertension) using high-performance computing (HPC). The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and social determinants of health—to identify individualized risk profiles and treatment responses. Existing computational tools lack the scalability to process these data at clinically relevant resolutions or timeframes. The proposed work will apply machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate physiological pathways, patient trajectories, and intervention impacts. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of EHRs from 500,000+ pregnancies, genomic variant analysis, and multiscale modeling of drug interactions in diverse patient subgroups. Key computational steps include federated learning to preserve data privacy across institutions, graph neural networks to map comorbidity networks, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic simulations to evaluate sex-specific drug efficacy. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for preeclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage, (2) optimized dosing guidelines for high-risk obstetric populations, and (3) open-source tools for real-time risk stratification in clinical settings. This work will advance precision nursing by bridging gaps between population-level data and individualized care, directly addressing disparities in women’s health outcomes. The scale and complexity of these analyses necessitate HPC infrastructure to manage terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local servers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: Architectural design increasingly relies on computational tools to address complex challenges in sustainability, structural efficiency, and spatial optimization. However, current architectural drafting and CAD workflows struggle to perform high-fidelity simulations at scale due to computational limitations, particularly when analyzing large structures or integrating multiple performance criteria. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable advanced simulations and generative design processes that transcend the capabilities of standalone workstations. The research will focus on three computational domains: 1) parallelized finite element analysis for evaluating structural integrity under dynamic environmental loads, 2) machine learning-driven energy modeling that incorporates real-time climate data and material properties, and 3) multi-objective optimization algorithms for space planning and building systems integration. By distributing these compute-intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce simulation times from days to hours while improving model resolution by an order of magnitude. Expected outcomes include novel methodologies for integrating HPC capabilities into mainstream architectural CAD workflows, validated through case studies of mid-rise mixed-use buildings. The results will advance the precision of performance-based design in architectural practice, enable data-driven material optimization strategies, and establish scalable frameworks for collaborative design iteration. This work will directly enhance instructional resources in architectural CAD/CADD programs by providing students with access to cutting-edge computational design techniques, while contributing to broader efforts in sustainable building practices through optimized energy and structural solutions.
cip_title: Architectural Drafting and Architectural CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations for architectural and related construction projects. Includes instruction in basic construction and structural design, architectural rendering, architectural-aided drafting (CAD), layout and designs, architectural blueprint interpretation, building materials, and basic structural wiring diagramming.

abstract: Vascular neurology encompasses complex, multifactorial diseases requiring integrative analysis of diverse datasets to optimize patient outcomes. Current limitations in predicting treatment responses and long-term recovery trajectories stem from inadequate computational frameworks capable of handling high-dimensional clinical, imaging, and molecular data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of cerebrovascular injury progression and therapeutic efficacy in acute ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage. We will integrate multi-omic data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with dynamic neuroimaging biomarkers (4D flow MRI, perfusion-weighted imaging) and real-world clinical outcomes from a longitudinal cohort of 1,200 patients. Machine learning architectures, including graph neural networks and transformer-based models, will be deployed to identify interaction networks between vascular risk factors, thrombus composition profiles, and neuroinflammatory cascades. Concurrently, finite element modeling of cerebral hemodynamics will simulate blood flow alterations under varying degrees of arterial stenosis and collateral circulation patterns. These simulations will inform personalized thrombolytic therapy windows and recanalization strategies. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale neuroimaging datasets, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models with >10⁷ parameters, and large-scale genomic association studies. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated predictive algorithms for hemorrhagic transformation risk following reperfusion therapies, (2) mechanistic maps linking endothelial dysfunction biomarkers to penumbral salvage capacity, and (3) open-source simulation tools for optimizing endovascular intervention protocols. By establishing computational infrastructure tailored to cerebrovascular pathophysiology, this work will enable precision medicine approaches that account for individual variations in clot biology, neurovascular anatomy, and systemic comorbidities. The requested HPC resources are essential for overcoming current bottlenecks in multimodal data integration and real-time hemodynamic modeling, ultimately advancing evidence-based guidelines for stroke care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation, prevention, treatment, and recovery from vascular diseases of the nervous system resulting from a large number of causes, such as ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, spinal cord ischemia, and spinal cord hemorrhage.
