abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the optimization of personalized dietary supplements for cognitive enhancement by integrating multi-omics data with computational modeling of metabolic pathways. While traditional approaches to nutritional interventions rely on population-level data, individual variability in metabolism, gut microbiota composition, and genetic polymorphisms often lead to suboptimal outcomes. This project addresses the challenge of predicting person-specific responses to micronutrient combinations, a problem requiring high-dimensional data integration and large-scale simulation beyond the capacity of standard computing infrastructure. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop a multi-scale model that links molecular-level nutrient interactions (simulated via molecular dynamics) to systemic physiological effects (modeled using ordinary differential equation networks). Machine learning algorithms will be trained on heterogeneous datasets, including gut metagenomic sequences, host genomic variants, and longitudinal cognitive performance metrics from a cohort of 1,200 healthy adults. The computational workflow will optimize supplement formulations through iterative in silico trials, accounting for dynamic nutrient competition, epigenetic modulation, and blood-brain barrier permeability. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for precision nutrition design and validated predictive biomarkers of cognitive response variability. This work bridges nutritional biochemistry, computational systems biology, and cognitive neuroscience, offering a novel paradigm for personalized health optimization. The resulting models and tools will additionally serve as educational resources for pre-pharmacy students, demonstrating advanced computational approaches to understanding biochemical interactions—a critical foundation for future studies in pharmacodynamics and personalized medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: Military information systems require rapid, secure processing of heterogeneous data streams in dynamic, resource-constrained environments. Current architectures struggle to balance real-time decision support with evolving cybersecurity threats, particularly when integrating legacy systems with modern AI-driven analytics. This project proposes the development of adaptive computational frameworks to optimize mission-critical workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-domain battlefield networks under variable constraints. The research focuses on two interconnected challenges: 1) modeling latency-tolerant resource allocation for distributed edge computing nodes in contested electromagnetic environments, and 2) validating neural-symbolic AI architectures that combine machine learning with rule-based systems for explainable decision support. Computational methods will include discrete-event simulations of network topologies using parallelized NS-3 modifications, coupled with multi-objective optimization algorithms to evaluate tradeoffs between processing speed, energy efficiency, and cybersecurity postures. A novel contribution involves implementing quantum-resistant encryption protocols within containerized microservices to assess their performance impact on real-time sensor fusion tasks. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter space exploration across synthetic operational scenarios, including stress-testing hybrid cloud-edge architectures under simulated adversarial conditions. Expected outcomes include quantifiable benchmarks for resilient system design, open-source simulation modules for military IoT integration, and probabilistic models of infrastructure degradation during prolonged cyber-physical attacks. This work directly addresses the DoD's need for agile, survivable command-and-control systems while advancing computational techniques for security-aware resource management in non-standard network environments. Results will inform both tactical system upgrades and strategic planning for next-generation defense information infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, design and application of computer and networking technology to the military environment. Includes instruction in planning; program development; graphical user interfaces; rapid prototyping; program construction; data types, operations; control flow; arrays; records; file I/O; database access; event-driven OOP structures; and enabling global-networked communications, including databases, systems analysis and design, decision support systems, and network security.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance protocols for legacy military hardware systems, addressing gaps in current methodologies that struggle to adapt to dynamic operational environments and aging equipment constraints. While traditional maintenance models prioritize fixed schedules or reactive repairs, they often fail to account for real-time sensor data, supply chain variability, and human operational factors unique to military contexts. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including equipment telemetry, maintenance logs, and simulated stress-test scenarios—into a multi-scale decision support system. Machine learning techniques, specifically ensemble models combining survival analysis and gradient-boosted trees, will be trained to predict failure risks across mechanical, electrical, and software subsystems. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model technician workflows and resource allocation under simulated deployment conditions, enabling scenario testing for maintenance prioritization. The computational intensity stems from processing high-frequency sensor streams (sampled at 10 kHz across 200+ channels) and optimizing millions of parameter combinations in hybrid simulation-optimization workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for adaptive maintenance scheduling that reduces unplanned downtime by ≥25% in modeled scenarios while maintaining compatibility with legacy systems’ technical constraints. This work fills a critical niche at the intersection of operational logistics, human factors engineering, and data-driven systems management—domains not fully addressed by conventional engineering or public administration approaches. By quantifying interdependencies between hardware degradation patterns and organizational decision-making processes, the project aims to establish new benchmarks for sustainment strategies in military technology ecosystems with limited modernization pathways. Results will be disseminated through tailored decision support tools for maintenance planners and foundational methodologies applicable to other high-stakes, resource-constrained operational environments.
cip_title: Military Systems and Maintenance Technology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military systems and maintenance technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling and optimization of enzymatic bioreactor systems for sustainable biochemical production. A critical challenge in biochemical engineering lies in scaling laboratory-scale enzymatic processes to industrial volumes while maintaining catalytic efficiency, substrate specificity, and product yield. Traditional experimental approaches to reactor design are resource-intensive and limited in their ability to resolve the multi-scale interactions between fluid dynamics, enzyme kinetics, and mass transfer. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning-driven parameter optimization. The CFD models will resolve reactor-scale hydrodynamics and substrate gradients, while atomistic MD simulations will characterize enzyme conformational stability under shear stress and pH gradients observed in large-scale systems. A hybrid neural network will iteratively optimize operational parameters (e.g., agitation rate, feed concentration) by linking reactor-scale simulations with enzyme-level performance metrics. This multi-scale approach requires parallelized simulations across spatial and temporal domains, necessitating HPC capabilities for handling O(10^6)-node CFD meshes, µs-scale MD trajectories, and high-dimensional optimization loops. Expected outcomes include predictive models for enzyme deactivation kinetics under industrial conditions, validated against experimental bioreactor data from collaborating partners, and an open-source optimization toolkit for scalable bioprocess design. The results will directly inform the development of energy-efficient bioreactors for pharmaceutical intermediates and bio-based chemical synthesis, aligning with global priorities in sustainable manufacturing. By bridging molecular-scale enzyme behavior with macro-scale transport phenomena, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for computational bioprocess engineering that reduces reliance on iterative physical prototyping.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the study of biochemical processes in living organisms, properties of biological materials, and processes using biochemical agents such as cells, enzymes, and antibodies. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, bioprocesses, and chemical engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in resource-constrained edge computing environments, where dynamic workloads and heterogeneous hardware complicate real-time task offloading and system reliability. Current heuristic-based approaches struggle to adapt to fluctuating network conditions, hardware variability, and latency-sensitive applications, leading to suboptimal resource utilization. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an adaptive computational framework that integrates machine learning (ML) with high-fidelity simulations to optimize task scheduling and resource allocation in edge systems. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models on large-scale simulations of edge architectures, emulating diverse network topologies, hardware configurations, and workload scenarios. These simulations will model edge nodes as multi-agent systems with varying computational capabilities, energy constraints, and communication latencies. The DRL agents will learn dynamic offloading policies that minimize end-to-end latency while balancing energy consumption and hardware utilization. Concurrently, we will validate the framework against real-world edge computing benchmarks and IoT datasets. The computational intensity of training DRL models across thousands of simulated edge environments necessitates HPC support for parallelized training workflows and distributed hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a generalizable framework for intelligent edge resource management, benchmark datasets for edge computing research, and insights into scalability challenges in distributed ML-driven systems. This work will directly benefit applications in smart infrastructure, industrial IoT, and autonomous systems, where adaptive edge computing is critical. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the project’s scale, enabling rapid iteration of complex models that would otherwise be infeasible on local hardware.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize staffing and resource allocation in long-term care (LTC) facilities using high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic interactions between resident needs, workforce constraints, and regulatory requirements. LTC facilities face persistent challenges in balancing personalized care delivery with operational efficiency, exacerbated by fluctuating resident acuity levels, staff turnover, and complex compliance demands. Traditional scheduling tools often fail to account for real-time variability in care requirements or cascading impacts of staffing decisions on care quality and burnout. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with machine learning (ML) to simulate facility operations under diverse scenarios. The ABM will incorporate anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), staff workflow data, and environmental sensors to represent resident-staff interactions, while ML algorithms trained on historical outcomes will predict optimal staffing ratios and task prioritization. HPC resources are critical to process large-scale datasets (spanning 5+ years from 15 partner facilities) and execute parallel simulations testing thousands of parameter combinations. Key outputs include predictive models linking staffing patterns to clinical outcomes (e.g., falls, pressure injuries) and an open-source optimization toolkit for administrators. This work bridges healthcare management and computational science, offering a novel methodology to enhance decision-making in aging populations’ care. Expected outcomes include evidence-based strategies to reduce staff workload variance by 20–30% while maintaining compliance with care standards, directly addressing workforce sustainability challenges in LTC. By leveraging HPC to model emergent behaviors in complex care systems, this project aims to advance scalable solutions for an understudied yet critical area of health sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of nursing homes, assisted living facilities, adult day care, home health services, and other long term care settings and agencies serving the elderly and disabled. Includes instruction in social and clinical aspects of aging, health care delivery systems, nursing home administration, assisted living administration, aging policy and government programs, ethics, business management, financial management, human resource management, marketing, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical need for advanced computational tools in enhancing pedagogical strategies for Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) teacher education. Current methods for training FCS educators lack robust frameworks to model the complex, dynamic interactions between instructional techniques, student engagement, and learning outcomes in home economics contexts, such as nutrition science, textile design, and household resource management. Traditional experimental or observational approaches struggle to account for the multivariate nature of these educational environments, limiting the scalability and generalizability of teacher training programs. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate diverse classroom scenarios, incorporating variables such as student demographics, socio-economic backgrounds, and differentiated learning styles. Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical datasets of student performance and teaching evaluations to identify patterns in effective instructional strategies. The computational models will further test hypothetical interventions, such as virtual labs for culinary arts or adaptive learning modules for financial literacy education, to predict their efficacy across varied educational settings. By integrating these computational outputs with empirical data from partner FCS teacher training programs, the project aims to generate evidence-based guidelines for optimizing curriculum design and instructional delivery. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable, open-access toolkit for FCS educators to simulate and refine teaching practices, thereby improving preparedness for real-world classroom challenges. This work aligns with national priorities to modernize vocational education through data-driven innovation, ultimately contributing to a more skilled workforce in home economics disciplines. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required computational throughput for parallelized simulations and large-scale data analytics, enabling real-time feedback loops for iterative model refinement.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Home Economics Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational home economics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Sleep disorders, such as obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), insomnia, and circadian rhythm dysregulation, are pervasive yet mechanistically complex conditions with poorly understood interactions between genetic, neurological, and physiological factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks often rely on phenotypic classifications that inadequately capture heterogeneity, limiting personalized interventions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including polysomnography (PSG) time series, genomic profiles, and electronic health records (EHRs) from a cohort of 15,000 patients. The primary research problem focuses on identifying latent biomarkers and causal pathways underlying sleep disorder subtypes using computational methods that require intensive parallel processing. A hybrid approach integrating deep neural networks (DNNs) and Bayesian hierarchical modeling will be employed to disentangle temporal dependencies in PSG signals, correlate them with genetic variants, and predict treatment responses. Additionally, computational simulations of neural circuit dynamics will model interactions between orexinergic pathways and sleep-wake transitions, utilizing differential equations solved over high-dimensional parameter spaces. These analyses demand significant memory allocation (~2 TB RAM), multi-node GPU clusters for DNN training, and scalable storage for iterative model validation. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel subtype-specific biomarkers, predictive algorithms for therapeutic efficacy, and mechanistic insights into neurotransmitter dysregulation in sleep disorders. The computational workflows will be open-sourced to enable reproducibility, and results will directly inform three ongoing clinical trials targeting genotype-guided interventions for OSA. By enabling the integration of heterogeneous data at unprecedented scale, this project aims to advance precision sleep medicine, reduce trial-and-error treatment paradigms, and provide a template for computationally driven clinical research in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Sleep Medicine

abstract: Respiratory care management for patients with acute or chronic pulmonary conditions relies heavily on optimizing ventilator settings and therapeutic interventions. However, current clinical protocols often depend on generalized guidelines that may not account for individual patient variability in lung mechanics, disease progression, or response to treatment. This project seeks to address this gap by developing patient-specific computational models to simulate respiratory mechanics and predict optimal ventilator parameters. The research problem centers on the lack of personalized, data-driven tools to guide respiratory therapists in dynamically adjusting care plans, particularly in critical care settings where rapid decision-making is essential. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to create multi-scale models integrating clinical data—such as airflow resistance, lung compliance, and gas exchange metrics—with biomechanical simulations of pulmonary function. These models will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to analyze airway pressure gradients and machine learning algorithms to correlate real-time patient monitoring data with historical outcomes. The computational workflow will require parallel processing to handle large datasets from electronic health records and high-resolution imaging, as well as iterative simulations to test hypothetical interventions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for identifying patient-specific ventilation strategies that minimize barotrauma and hypoxia risks while improving weaning success rates. This project will also generate open-source tools for respiratory therapy education, enabling technicians to explore simulated clinical scenarios. The results have the potential to enhance evidence-based practice, reduce trial-and-error in ventilator management, and improve care quality for patients with respiratory failure. Successful implementation of this research hinges on access to HPC resources capable of managing complex simulations and large-scale data integration within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer general respiratory care procedures under the supervision of respiratory therapists in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in patient data collection and monitoring, airway management, installation of nebulizers and other respiratory assistance devices, application and monitoring of breathing gases, equipment operation and maintenance, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in digital humanities and textual studies, focusing on the analysis and preservation of large-scale, heterogeneous textual corpora. A central challenge in the field lies in processing and interpreting vast collections of digitized historical manuscripts, modern digital texts, and born-digital media, which often exist in fragmented, multilingual, or non-standardized formats. Traditional computational methods struggle to manage the scale and complexity of these datasets, particularly when integrating semantic analysis, network-based modeling of textual relationships, and machine learning-driven pattern detection across temporal and cultural contexts. The proposed research will develop and deploy scalable computational workflows to address these challenges, including natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical language variants, graph-based models to trace intertextual networks across centuries of literature, and AI-assisted tools for automated collation of variant texts in critical editions. These methods require parallelized computing architectures to handle memory-intensive tasks such as training transformer models on low-resource languages, conducting high-resolution optical character recognition (OCR) corrections for degraded archival materials, and simulating textual dissemination patterns in dynamic cultural landscapes. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to produce novel frameworks for analyzing textual evolution, cultural exchange, and epistemic shifts in ways previously constrained by computational limitations. Anticipated outcomes include publicly accessible digital editions of understudied texts, interoperable datasets for cross-disciplinary humanities research, and open-source tools tailored for archival institutions and scholars. This work will directly contribute to preserving vulnerable cultural heritage materials while enabling new forms of humanistic inquiry at the intersection of computational scalability and interpretative rigor. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for petabyte-scale textual repositories, and real-time collaboration platforms for international scholarly networks engaged in critical editing projects.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on digital textual editing, archiving, and publishing, and on the study of new media and computing platforms from the perspectives of the humanities and computer science. Includes instruction in archiving, computer programming, cultural studies, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision agriculture through the development of an adaptive decision-support framework for autonomous agricultural machinery, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize equipment performance in dynamic field environments. Current agricultural machinery systems face challenges in real-time decision-making due to variable soil conditions, crop heterogeneity, and weather unpredictability, leading to suboptimal resource use and energy inefficiencies. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline integrating multi-modal sensor data (e.g., LiDAR, hyperspectral imaging, IoT soil sensors) with machine learning models to simulate and predict equipment responses under diverse operational scenarios. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of mechanized workflows, including soil tillage dynamics, variable-rate seeding, and irrigation system performance, using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and discrete element method (DEM) models. Additionally, reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to optimize path planning and implement control for autonomous tractors, reducing fuel consumption and soil compaction risks. The project will validate models against empirical data from partner farms in the Midwest US, focusing on corn and soybean production systems. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for equipment performance prediction, a benchmark dataset for agricultural machinery AI applications, and scalable protocols to reduce the computational burden of real-time control systems. By enhancing the precision and adaptability of mechanized operations, this work aims to directly contribute to sustainable intensification goals in agriculture, bridging critical gaps between theoretical automation potential and field-scale implementation. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the high-dimensional parameter space of agricultural environments and achieve the resolution required for generalizable insights.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to sell, select, and service agricultural or agribusiness technical equipment and facilities, including computers, specialized software, power units, machinery, equipment structures, and utilities. Includes instruction in agricultural power systems, planning and selecting materials for the construction of support facilities, mechanical practices associated with irrigation and water conservation, erosion control, and agricultural data processing systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the systemic risk dynamics of decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems using high-frequency network analysis and agent-based simulations. DeFi platforms, which operate via blockchain-based smart contracts, have introduced novel financial instruments (e.g., automated liquidity pools, algorithmic stablecoins) that exhibit complex, non-linear interactions under market stress. Traditional risk models, designed for centralized systems, fail to account for real-time interdependencies and cascading failures in these permissionless, globally interconnected protocols. The study will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of on-chain transaction data, reconstruct dynamic network topologies of liquidity flows, and simulate stress scenarios across multiple DeFi protocols (e.g., lending markets, decentralized exchanges). Computational methods will combine graph neural networks for anomaly detection with Monte Carlo simulations to quantify contagion risks under varying volatility regimes. A custom agent-based model will emulate heterogeneous participant behavior (e.g., arbitrage bots, collateral liquidators) interacting with protocol-specific incentive mechanisms. Expected outcomes include a risk propagation framework capable of identifying critical leverage feedback loops and liquidity choke points in real time, as well as stress-testing benchmarks for cross-protocol exposure. Results will inform the development of early warning systems for regulators and protocol designers, addressing a critical gap in managing systemic stability within this $100B+ asset class. The scale of data processing (10M+ daily transactions across 20+ blockchains) and the computational intensity of multi-agent simulations necessitate parallelized GPU computing and distributed memory architectures to achieve actionable latency thresholds. This work bridges quantitative finance, distributed systems theory, and computational economics, advancing risk management paradigms for next-generation financial infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and analyze the financial and monetary aspects and performance of business enterprises, banking institutions, or other organizations. Includes instruction in principles of accounting, financial instruments, capital planning, funds acquisition, asset and debt management, budgeting, financial analysis, and investments and portfolio management.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of consumer decision-making in omnichannel retail environments, where fragmented data and dynamic interactions across physical, digital, and mobile platforms challenge traditional merchandising strategies. Retailers struggle to predict and optimize resource allocation—such as inventory distribution, personalized promotions, and channel-specific advertising—due to the nonlinear, context-dependent nature of consumer behavior. Current analytical tools lack the capacity to model real-time, multi-channel interactions at scale, limiting the industry’s ability to balance profitability with customer experience. To bridge this gap, this project proposes the development of a high-fidelity agent-based simulation framework powered by machine learning (ML) and high-performance computing (HPC). The framework will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including transaction histories, geolocation patterns, social media sentiment, and in-store IoT sensor data, to parameterize millions of synthetic consumer agents with empirically grounded behavioral profiles. These agents will interact within a dynamic virtual retail ecosystem simulating diverse merchandising scenarios, such as flash sales, supply chain disruptions, or seasonal demand shifts. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to explore the cascading effects of strategic interventions—like pricing adjustments or loyalty programs—across channels and demographic segments. Computational outputs will be analyzed using cluster computing techniques to identify optimal resource allocation policies and quantify trade-offs between customer engagement metrics and operational costs. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for retailers to test merchandising strategies in silico, reducing financial risks associated with trial-and-error implementations. The project will also contribute methodological advances in applying agent-based modeling to consumer analytics, offering a template for data-driven, ethical personalization in retail. By leveraging HPC to resolve the computational bottlenecks of large-scale consumer simulations, this work aims to enhance the agility of merchandising management in an increasingly competitive and digitally mediated marketplace.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on product and service promotion from the perspective of individual and family consumers and that prepares individuals to function as consumer management and marketing consultants in for-profit and non-profit enterprises. Includes instruction in applied market research, consumer behavior, product sourcing and distribution, profitability, customer feedback and evaluation methods, promotion and retailing campaign development, and applications to specific domestic and international consumer markets.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized neuromuscular rehabilitation protocols through computational modeling of dynamic movement patterns in patients recovering from stroke or traumatic brain injury. Current clinical protocols in kinesiotherapy rely on generalized exercise frameworks, which often fail to account for individual variability in neuromuscular control, biomechanical constraints, and adaptive motor learning processes. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating patient-specific simulations that predict optimal therapeutic exercise parameters, including intensity, joint loading, and motor task complexity, while minimizing injury risk. The computational approach integrates multibody biomechanical modeling with machine learning algorithms trained on high-resolution motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and force plate data collected from diverse patient cohorts. Finite element analysis will be applied to simulate soft tissue responses during therapeutic exercises, while reinforcement learning frameworks will optimize exercise sequences based on real-time feedback loops mimicking neuroplastic adaptation. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabytes of kinematic and physiological data, running parallelized simulations across heterogeneous movement scenarios, and iterating predictive models with clinically relevant latency. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for generating adaptive rehabilitation prescriptions and a quantitative framework for assessing neuromuscular recovery trajectories. This work aims to transform kinesiotherapy practice by shifting from static, population-based exercise regimens to dynamic, patient-driven interventions, potentially reducing rehabilitation durations by 20-30% in pilot populations. The computational models developed may also inform the design of next-generation assistive devices and virtual reality-based therapeutic environments, positioning kinesiotherapy at the intersection of precision medicine and neuromotor engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the direction of physicians, to treat the effects of disease, injury, and congenital disorders through therapeutic exercise and education. Includes instruction in human anatomy, human physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, therapeutic exercise and adapted physical education, human growth and development, motor learning and performance, testing and measurement, first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, psychology, rehabilitation procedures, patient assessment and management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Francophone cultural narratives across colonial and postcolonial contexts through large-scale textual and visual data. While traditional methods in French Studies have relied on close reading of limited corpora, the scale and complexity of digitized archives—including colonial administrative records, Francophone periodicals, and postcolonial literary works—require advanced computational tools to identify patterns in language, representation, and discourse across time and geography. The research addresses two interconnected gaps: (1) the lack of systematic, transnational studies on how French colonial ideologies were reproduced or contested in Francophone cultural production, and (2) the underutilization of computational methods in humanities-driven area studies. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on historical French texts, to trace semantic shifts in key concepts (e.g., “civilisation,” “assimilation”) across 20th-century sources from France, North Africa, and the Caribbean. Concurrently, computer vision methods will analyze visual materials such as colonial-era propaganda posters and contemporary Francophone graphic novels to map iconographic continuities and ruptures. These parallel workflows will integrate via dimensionality reduction and network analysis to reveal intersections between textual and visual discourse networks. The computational demands—particularly for training domain-specific language models, processing high-resolution image datasets, and running iterative simulations of cultural influence—necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Francophone cultural artifacts, new methodologies for interdisciplinary area studies, and scholarly insights into how decolonial narratives have reconfigured Franco-global cultural identities. By bridging computational scalability with humanistic critique, this work aims to redefine the scope of French Studies in analyzing transnational cultural systems.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of France, other Francophone countries inside and outside Europe, and the French colonial experience and the associated French minorities around the world.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the longitudinal outcomes of mental health interventions in diverse populations, addressing the critical challenge of predicting patient-specific treatment efficacy in real-world settings. Mental health disorders exhibit significant heterogeneity in symptom presentation, treatment response, and social determinants, yet existing clinical decision-support tools lack the capacity to integrate multi-modal data at scale. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging datasets, and socio-environmental data from public health repositories. Machine learning models—including ensemble methods and graph neural networks—will be trained to identify dynamic patterns linking biological, psychological, and social variables to intervention outcomes. A key innovation involves natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract latent psychosocial features from unstructured clinical notes, enabling the synthesis of qualitative clinician observations with quantitative biomarkers. Computational demands arise from the need to process terabytes of multi-temporal data, optimize hyperparameters across competing model architectures, and perform permutation-based significance testing to mitigate overfitting in high-dimensional datasets. Anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide personalized treatment selection for depression and anxiety disorders, (2) an open-source software package for adaptive intervention modeling, and (3) population-level insights into how systemic factors (e.g., access disparities, community support networks) modulate treatment effectiveness. By enabling rapid iteration of complex, data-driven hypotheses, HPC resources will directly support the translation of computational psychiatry research into actionable clinical tools. This work bridges a critical gap between traditional psychosocial intervention research and emerging computational methodologies, with potential to inform both precision mental healthcare delivery and public health policy.
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Developmental-behavioral pediatrics faces a critical challenge in identifying early biomarkers and heterogeneous risk pathways for childhood developmental and behavioral disorders (DBDs), such as autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Current diagnostic frameworks rely on subjective assessments and late-stage clinical markers, limiting opportunities for timely, personalized interventions. This project proposes to address this gap by integrating multi-modal clinical, neuroimaging, and genomic datasets to model developmental trajectories and predict disorder risk. We will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) from 50,000+ children, high-resolution functional MRI data from 2,000 participants, and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify dynamic interactions between genetic susceptibility, neural circuit maturation, and environmental exposures. Computational workflows will include deep learning architectures for time-series EHR analysis, Bayesian network models to infer causal pathways in neurodevelopmental processes, and GPU-accelerated population-scale simulations of intervention outcomes. A key innovation is the development of a federated learning framework to harmonize data across eight pediatric research networks while preserving patient privacy. The scale of these datasets and the complexity of modeling non-linear developmental interactions necessitate parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and high-throughput storage systems. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to stratify DBD risk during infancy, (2) mechanistic insights into how family dynamics modulate genetic and neural risk factors, and (3) optimized resource allocation strategies for early intervention programs. By elucidating critical periods for therapeutic efficacy, this work will directly inform clinical guidelines and public health policies aimed at reducing lifelong disability burdens. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to advance precision medicine in developmental pediatrics.
cip_definition: Research on how to assist in the prevention, diagnosis, and management of developmental difficulties and problematic behaviors in children, and in the family dysfunctions that compromise children's development; and to foster understanding and promotion of optimal development of children and families through research, education, clinical care, and advocacy efforts.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying energy-based therapies, specifically the effects of biofield modulation (e.g., Qi Gong, Therapeutic Touch) on cellular redox homeostasis and mitochondrial function. While such therapies are increasingly integrated into holistic health practices, their molecular and systemic effects remain poorly characterized, hindered by the complexity of modeling low-energy bioelectromagnetic interactions and nonlinear cellular responses. The research problem centers on developing a multiscale computational framework to simulate how externally applied biofields interact with endogenous bioelectric networks, influencing reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and metabolic regulation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the dual challenges of scale: quantum mechanical modeling of putative electromagnetic field interactions with ion channels (timescales <1 ns) and systems biology simulations of ROS-mediated signaling cascades across tissues (timescales >1 hr). The computational approach integrates 1) molecular dynamics simulations using polarized force fields to assess field-induced conformational changes in voltage-gated channels, 2) finite element modeling of endogenous bioelectric gradients perturbed by external fields, and 3) stochastic reaction-diffusion models of ROS propagation and antioxidant responses. Machine learning will be employed to parameterize models using sparse experimental data from coupled in vitro electrophysiology and metabolomics studies. Expected outcomes include the first predictive map of biofield intensity/duration thresholds that transition ROS signaling from physiological to pathological regimes, identification of critical intervention windows for metabolic synchronization, and optimization of treatment parameters for specific mitochondrial dysfunction phenotypes. This work will establish a computational foundation for evidence-based protocol design in energy therapies, bridging biophysical theory with clinical applications in managing chronic inflammatory and metabolic disorders. By resolving mechanistic uncertainties, the project aims to catalyze interdisciplinary collaboration between systems biology, quantum biophysics, and integrative medicine communities.
cip_title: Energy and Biologically Based Therapies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative, complementary, and somatic health and therapeutic services not elsewhere classified (bioenergetics, cranio-sacral therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Qi Gong, and others).

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in applied and professional ethics, specifically addressing the challenge of modeling complex ethical decision-making scenarios in multi-stakeholder environments. Traditional ethical analysis often relies on qualitative case studies or simplified theoretical frameworks, which struggle to account for dynamic interactions, large-scale data, and the probabilistic outcomes inherent in real-world dilemmas. Our research aims to bridge this gap by developing computational models that simulate ethical decision-making processes across diverse professional contexts, including healthcare triage, corporate governance, and environmental policy. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques, we will simulate interactions between stakeholders with competing values, resource constraints, and institutional pressures. The models will integrate empirical datasets (e.g., public policy records, organizational ethics reports) with normative ethical frameworks (e.g., utilitarianism, deontology) to evaluate how different decision-making algorithms affect moral outcomes under uncertainty. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to reflect real-world complexity, enabling parallelized scenario testing, high-dimensional parameter exploration, and real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible library of modular ethical decision-making models tailored to specific professions, (2) quantitative insights into systemic biases and trade-offs in resource allocation ethics, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for improving institutional ethics protocols. By combining computational social science methods with philosophical rigor, this project will provide novel tools for anticipating ethical risks in emerging technologies and socio-technical systems while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in applied ethics research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the design of adaptive underwater energy harvesters for low-velocity ocean currents, a critical challenge in sustainable marine energy systems. Existing devices struggle with efficiency in dynamic, low-flow coastal environments due to complex fluid-structure interactions and transient turbulence patterns. Leveraging Ocean Engineering principles, the research integrates multiphysics modeling of hydrodynamic loads, material fatigue in corrosive conditions, and bio-inspired morphing geometries to enhance energy capture. The core computational challenge involves resolving millimeter-scale vortex shedding around deformable structures at realistic oceanic scales—a task requiring parallelized, transient simulations of coupled fluid-structure systems. The proposed approach combines immersed boundary methods for fluid-structure interaction with tensor-based machine learning to predict optimal geometry adjustments in real-time flow conditions. High-performance computing resources will enable large-eddy simulations across parameter spaces encompassing Reynolds numbers (10^3–10^5), structural elasticity, and tidal phase variations. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for harvester performance under unsteady flows, a machine learning-accelerated design optimization pipeline, and open-source tools for marine energy system simulation. This work directly addresses the energy resilience needs of coastal communities while advancing fundamental knowledge about nonlinear interactions in marine renewable infrastructure. The requested computational allocation will support parametric studies across 50+ geometric configurations at temporal resolutions below the Kolmogorov timescale, significantly exceeding the capabilities of current institutional clusters. Successful implementation could increase energy conversion efficiency by 30–40% in field-tested prototypes, accelerating the viability of low-impact underwater energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to monitor, control, manipulate and operate within coastal or ocean environments, such as underwater platforms, flood control systems, dikes, hydroelectric power systems, tide and current control and warning systems, and communications equipment; the planning and design of total systems for working and functioning in water or underwater environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as the action of water properties and behavior on physical systems and people, tidal forces, current movements, and wave motion.

abstract: Zoonotic infectious diseases present complex challenges at the intersection of animal and human health, requiring advanced tools to unravel pathogen-host-environment interactions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and epidemiological drivers of emerging veterinary pathogens, with a focus on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dynamics in livestock-associated bacterial communities. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale genomic datasets and simulating multi-host transmission networks hinder progress in predicting outbreaks and optimizing intervention strategies. We propose an integrated computational approach combining metagenomic sequencing data from cattle populations with spatially explicit epidemiological models. Machine learning pipelines will identify AMR gene clusters and their mobility across microbial populations, while agent-based models will simulate pathogen spread under varying agricultural practices and climate scenarios. These models will incorporate high-resolution environmental data, host movement patterns, and pathogen mutation rates derived from comparative genomic analyses. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of sequencing data, running parallelized evolutionary simulations to trace resistance gene origins, and optimizing neural networks for predicting cross-species transmission risks. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of key genomic markers associated with zoonotic potential in livestock pathogens, (2) predictive maps of AMR hotspots under different management policies, and (3) open-source tools for real-time monitoring of resistance gene transfer. By leveraging computational power to bridge molecular and population-level analyses, this work will advance targeted vaccine development, inform antimicrobial stewardship in agriculture, and strengthen One Health frameworks for disease prevention. The requested resources will directly support 15+ researchers analyzing complex datasets that are infeasible to process through conventional computing, accelerating progress toward sustainable solutions for veterinary and public health challenges.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of zoonotic infectious diseases, disease mechanisms, and prevention and treatment strategies. Includes instruction in disease pathogenesis, vector biology, mycobacterial infection, blood parasites, retroviruses, food-borne diseases, new infectious agents, ecotoxicology, mechanisms of disease transfer, antibody resistance, comparative pathology, communicable diseases, and disease prevention and eradication.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-domain cognitive processes through the development of a multi-scale computational model integrating neural, behavioral, and environmental data. While existing approaches often isolate cognitive functions like memory, perception, or decision-making, real-world cognition involves continuous interaction between these domains, shaped by contextual and physiological constraints. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how such interactions scale across biological and situational variables, particularly in neurodiverse populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to simulate a hybrid architecture combining spiking neural networks with reinforcement learning frameworks, calibrated against empirical neuroimaging and eye-tracking datasets. The model will dynamically map how sensory inputs are gated through attentional mechanisms, integrated with prior knowledge, and transformed into adaptive behaviors under varying cognitive loads. Key computational challenges include real-time synchronization of modular network components, parameter optimization across 10^6+ possible configurations, and probabilistic inference under noisy input conditions—all requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows. Outcomes will generate predictive insights into individual differences in cognitive flexibility, with applications to personalized neuroeducational interventions and assistive technologies. By bridging computational neuroscience, developmental psychology, and machine learning, this work advances methodological frameworks for studying cognition as a complex adaptive system rather than a collection of isolated modules. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving biologically plausible temporal resolutions in whole-brain simulations while maintaining ecological validity through embedded virtual environments. Successful implementation will produce open-source tools for scalable cognitive modeling, addressing reproducibility challenges in interdisciplinary research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the mind and the nature of intelligence from the interdisciplinary perspectives of computer science, philosophy, mathematics, psychology, neuroscience, and other disciplines. Includes instruction in mathematics and logic, cognitive process modeling, dynamic systems, learning theories, brain and cognition, neural networking, programming, and applications to topics such as language acquisition, computer systems, and perception and behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of next-generation hypersonic aerospace vehicles through advanced computational modeling of aerothermal-structural interactions. Current limitations in predicting turbulent boundary layer behavior, shock-wave interactions, and thermal protection system performance under extreme Mach number regimes (Mach 5–20) hinder progress toward reliable, efficient vehicles capable of sustained atmospheric flight. The research will employ high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with thermo-structural finite element analysis to resolve multi-physics phenomena across disparate temporal and spatial scales. Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) and wall-modeled Large Eddy Simulation (LES) approaches will be implemented to capture turbulence-chemistry interactions in high-enthalpy flows, while adaptive mesh refinement techniques will optimize resource allocation for localized phenomena such as boundary layer transition and shock impingement. The computational framework will integrate open-source solvers (e.g., SU2, OpenFOAM) with custom-developed algorithms for conjugate heat transfer and material ablation modeling. Access to high-performance computing resources is essential to achieve the required spatial resolution (sub-millimeter scale) and temporal sampling across multi-second flight trajectories, with anticipated simulations exceeding 10 million core-hours. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for surface heat flux distribution, boundary layer stability criteria, and thermally induced structural deformation, directly informing the design of actively cooled leading edges and scramjet combustor configurations. Results will advance fundamental understanding of hypersonic flow physics while providing industry-applicable tools to reduce reliance on empirical correlations and costly experimental testing. The developed workflows will also contribute scalable parallelization strategies for exascale-ready aerospace simulations, benefiting broader scientific efforts in multi-physics modeling.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aeronautics/ Aviation/ Aerospace Science and Technology, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of aviation and the aviation industry, including in-flight and ground support operations. Includes instruction in the technical, business, and general aspects of air transportation systems.

abstract: Perioperative nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to optimize patient outcomes and surgical efficiency. However, variability in intraoperative workflows, patient responses, and surgical team dynamics presents challenges in standardizing care and predicting complications. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex perioperative environments and develop predictive tools for real-time clinical support. We will integrate multimodal data streams—including electronic health records, real-time vital signs, surgical instrument telemetry, and nurse documentation—to create dynamic simulations of surgical workflows. Machine learning models will be trained on retrospective datasets to identify patterns associated with adverse events (e.g., hypothermia, surgical site infections) and inefficiencies in instrument handling or team communication. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further analyze airflow patterns in operating rooms to optimize sterile field maintenance. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-frequency sensor data and iterative refinement of neural networks to account for rare but critical events. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for early complication detection, evidence-based recommendations for workflow redesign, and interactive training modules for perioperative nurses using synthetic surgical scenarios. By quantifying relationships between nursing interventions and surgical outcomes at scale, this work aims to advance precision in perioperative practice while maintaining focus on the human factors essential to patient-centered care. The requested computing resources will directly support the development of open-source tools adaptable to diverse surgical settings, ultimately contributing to safer, more efficient operating room environments through enhanced nursing decision-support systems.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, yet its biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely characterized, limiting evidence-based optimization of clinical protocols. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets and simulate OMT’s effects on neuromusculoskeletal systems. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the integration of high-resolution imaging, motion-capture biomechanics, electrophysiological signals, and patient-reported outcomes—key to modeling the complex, dynamic interactions underlying OMT efficacy. We propose a computational framework combining finite element modeling (FEM), machine learning (ML), and network analysis to quantify how OMT-induced mechanical forces propagate through tissue structures, modulate neural signaling, and correlate with clinical outcomes. FEM will simulate real-time tissue deformation and stress distribution during OMT maneuvers, informed by 3D musculoskeletal anatomy derived from patient-specific MRI/CT data. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify predictive patterns in heterogeneous clinical datasets (n=850 retrospective cases; prospective n=120), including electromyography, gait analysis, and inflammatory biomarkers. Graph-based network models will map functional connectivity shifts in sensorimotor and autonomic pathways post-OMT. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses: biomechanical simulations require parallelized solvers for ultra-high-resolution meshes (>10^6 elements), while ML workflows demand GPU acceleration to train deep neural networks on terabyte-scale multimodal data. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into OMT’s impact on proprioceptive feedback loops, validated predictive models for treatment personalization, and open-source computational tools for the osteopathic research community. By bridging clinical observations with multiscale computational modeling, this work aims to establish a robust framework for advancing OMT research, ultimately enhancing therapeutic precision in neuromusculoskeletal care.
cip_definition: Research focused on osteopathic neuromusculoskeletal diagnosis and Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT).

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing construction finishing processes, quality management, and defect inspection through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Current methods for predicting material performance, detecting finishing defects, and managing dynamic construction workflows are limited by the inability to process multi-scale, multi-physics interactions in real time. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to overcome these limitations by enabling large-scale simulations of material behavior under diverse environmental and operational conditions, coupled with machine learning-driven analysis of inspection data. The project will develop a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating stress distribution, thermal dynamics, and moisture diffusion in finishing materials, such as coatings, tiles, and composite panels. Concurrently, deep learning models trained on high-resolution image datasets of surface defects (e.g., cracks, delamination) will be deployed to automate inspection workflows. These models will leverage distributed computing to process terabytes of LiDAR, drone-captured imagery, and IoT sensor data from active construction sites. The HPC infrastructure will also support agent-based simulations of construction management scenarios, optimizing resource allocation and scheduling under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for material failure thresholds, a real-time defect detection system with 95%+ accuracy, and adaptive project management protocols to reduce delays and waste. By advancing computational capabilities in this domain, the project aims to enhance the durability of building finishes, improve regulatory compliance, and reduce costs associated with rework. The proposed work will provide open-source software modules for the construction technology community, fostering broader adoption of HPC-driven solutions in an industry traditionally reliant on empirical methods.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of violence risk and intervention outcomes in forensic psychology, with a focus on improving equity and accuracy in legal decision-making. Current risk assessment tools often rely on static, demographic-heavy datasets, which can perpetuate systemic biases and fail to account for dynamic psychological and contextual factors. The research problem centers on developing computational models that integrate longitudinal behavioral data, neuropsychological profiles, and situational variables to predict individualized risk trajectories and treatment responsiveness. Using anonymized datasets from forensic counseling evaluations, criminal justice records, and intervention outcome studies, the project will apply machine learning techniques—including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods—to model complex interactions between cognitive-behavioral patterns, environmental stressors, and therapeutic interventions. HPC resources are critical for processing multimodal data (e.g., text-based clinical notes, neuroimaging-derived features, and time-series behavioral metrics) and optimizing hyperparameters in computationally intensive models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for dynamic risk prediction that reduces reliance on demographic proxies, (2) identification of neurocognitive and psychosocial markers most predictive of successful intervention in secure settings, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing risk trajectories to support forensic counseling practitioners. By enabling large-scale analysis of heterogeneous data, this work aims to address gaps in equitable risk assessment while advancing applied psychological practices at the intersection of mental health and legal systems. The computational pipeline will be designed for scalability to inform future studies on tailored forensic treatment protocols, with implications for policy and ethical standards in psychological service delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical, counseling, school, and neuropsychology skills to the provision of psychological services within the criminal justice and civil legal systems, including consultation, assessment, and interventions. Includes instruction in the epidemiology of mental/behavioral disorders, risk factors for violence and criminality, profiling and patterning, psychological testing, prediction and intervention measurement, forensic assessment, criminal and civil law and procedures, secure environments, forensic treatment and intervention skills, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The industrial production of specialty chemicals requires precise control over reaction kinetics and transport phenomena to optimize yield, minimize waste, and ensure operational safety. However, experimental approaches to scale-up reactor designs and process parameters are often costly and time-intensive, particularly when addressing complex multiphase systems or novel catalytic materials. This project seeks to address these challenges through advanced computational modeling leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose a multiscale framework integrating quantum mechanical simulations (density functional theory) for catalyst surface interactions, kinetic Monte Carlo methods for reaction network evolution, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model transport effects at the reactor scale. These coupled simulations will enable the prediction of optimal operating conditions, catalyst configurations, and reactor geometries under industrially relevant flow rates and temperatures. The HPC environment is critical for handling the computational complexity of bridging time and length scales spanning 10 orders of magnitude, as well as for conducting high-throughput screening of potential catalytic materials. Expected outcomes include validated models for ethylene oxide synthesis, optimized reactor designs to reduce energy consumption by 15–20%, and guidelines for mitigating hazardous intermediate formation during scale-up. The results will provide a template for computationally driven process intensification in chemical manufacturing, aligning with industry priorities around sustainability and decarbonization. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, this work aims to accelerate the development of efficient, scalable, and safer chemical production systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the reliability and efficacy of law enforcement investigative interviewing through advanced computational modeling and analysis. Current practices in tactical interviewing rely heavily on subjective interpretation of verbal and nonverbal cues, which can introduce biases, inconsistencies, and legal risks. To address these challenges, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets of interview transcripts, audio-visual recordings, and case outcomes. The research will integrate natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to identify patterns in interviewer strategies, suspect responses, and contextual factors that correlate with successful investigative outcomes. Agent-based models will simulate dynamic interactions between interviewers and subjects under varying psychological and situational conditions, incorporating principles from cognitive psychology and behavioral economics. Additionally, multimodal data analysis (speech, facial expressions, and physiological signals) will be conducted to assess stress, deception, and cognitive load in real-time scenarios. The computational demands of processing terabytes of unstructured data, training deep neural networks, and running parallelized simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based protocols for optimizing questioning techniques, (2) predictive tools to flag high-risk interactions requiring intervention, and (3) a training module for law enforcement that uses generative AI to create adaptive, scenario-based learning environments. By bridging computational science and investigative practices, this work aims to reduce wrongful convictions, improve evidentiary quality, and establish standardized, empirically validated methods for ethical suspect engagement. The resulting open-source toolkit will provide agencies with scalable solutions to address evolving challenges in criminal justice.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, procedures, techniques, legal concerns, and problems associated with a criminal investigation. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, courtroom evidence management and preparation, case presentation and court testimony, description and identification, state and federal criminal law and procedures, informant and suspect rights, officer liability, informant and witness management, victim awareness, tactical interviewing, psychology, criminal investigation methods and procedures, report writing and documentation, investigative techniques, and case management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance evidence-based design methodologies for healthcare environments, focusing on optimizing spatial configurations to enhance patient healing and staff efficiency. Current healthcare design practices often rely on static post-occupancy evaluations or anecdotal frameworks, limiting the ability to model dynamic interactions between environmental variables (e.g., lighting, acoustics, spatial flow) and physiological or behavioral outcomes in real time. The proposed work addresses this gap by developing computational models to simulate how design interventions impact stress reduction, patient mobility, and care delivery workflows across diverse populations and clinical contexts. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project integrates spatial analytics, real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled clinical environments, and machine learning techniques to predict how architectural features influence biometric markers (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels) and operational metrics (e.g., staff fatigue, patient wait times). Agent-based modeling will simulate patient and staff movement patterns under varying design scenarios, while deep learning architectures will analyze multimodal datasets to identify non-linear relationships between environmental variables and health outcomes. Parametric modeling tools will iteratively test design permutations, optimizing for variables such as infection control, accessibility, and sensory comfort. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of large-scale 3D spatial datasets and real-time simulation of complex human-environment interactions—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to evaluate design prototypes prior to physical implementation, reducing costly retrofits and improving scalability of patient-centered solutions. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven healthcare design, with open-source tools and benchmarks for the architecture and healthcare communities. By bridging computational science and environmental design, the project will contribute foundational insights into how built environments can be dynamically tailored to support healing processes, operational resilience, and health equity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize technology education curricula for K-12 classrooms, with a focus on integrating emerging industrial tools such as additive manufacturing, robotics, and IoT systems. A critical challenge in technology teacher education is the rapid evolution of industrial technologies, which creates gaps between available training resources and the skills needed to teach modern tools effectively. Traditional curriculum design relies on qualitative assessments and small-scale pilot studies, limiting scalability and adaptability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate classroom technology integration scenarios, evaluate pedagogical outcomes, and generate adaptive curriculum recommendations. Agent-based models will simulate student interactions with industrial tools under varying instructional conditions, while machine learning classifiers trained on historical student performance data will predict skill acquisition patterns. Computational fluid dynamics methods will be adapted to model resource allocation challenges in classroom makerspaces. The simulations will require parallel processing to manage large parameter spaces encompassing tool availability, student ability distributions, and safety constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying curriculum bottlenecks, a decision-support tool for technology resource investments in schools, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated classroom-technology interaction trajectories. This work will advance industrial arts education by providing data-driven strategies to align teacher training with real-world technological demands, directly supporting the preparation of educators to foster STEM competencies in diverse student populations.
cip_title: Technology Teacher Education/ Industrial Arts Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach technology education/industrial arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to advance nuclear reactor safety and operational efficiency by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate complex thermal-hydraulic and neutronic phenomena in nuclear systems. Current models for predicting coolant flow behavior, heat transfer dynamics, and fuel performance under transient or accident conditions—such as loss-of-coolant accidents (LOCAs) or reactivity insertion events—rely on simplified assumptions that limit their accuracy. These limitations hinder the optimization of safety protocols and the design of next-generation reactors, including small modular reactors (SMRs). To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multi-physics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), neutron transport theory, and structural mechanics. High-resolution 3D models of reactor cores and primary cooling systems will be developed using open-source frameworks like OpenFOAM and MOOSE, coupled with Monte Carlo N-Particle (MCNP) codes for radiation transport. Parallel computing techniques will enable the resolution of fine-scale turbulence, phase changes in coolant, and localized stress-strain responses in fuel cladding under extreme conditions. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to accelerate uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analyses, identifying critical parameters influencing system stability. The project will validate simulations against experimental data from integral effect test facilities and operational reactor datasets.
