Outcomes will include validated predictive tools for accident progression, optimized emergency response strategies, and insights into material performance limits. These results will directly support regulatory decision-making, safety training programs, and the development of advanced reactor designs with enhanced inherent safety features. By addressing computational bottlenecks through HPC scalability, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical models and real-world nuclear system behavior, contributing to safer and more efficient nuclear energy technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering, knowledge and technical skills in support of engineer and other professionals operating nuclear facilities and engaged in nuclear applications and safety procedures. Includes instruction in physics, nuclear science, nuclear systems, nuclear plant and systems design, radiological safety, radiological applications, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) leverages pressurized oxygen environments to treat conditions such as non-healing wounds, radiation injury, and decompression sickness. However, optimizing treatment protocols remains challenging due to variability in patient-specific physiological responses and the complex interplay between oxygen dynamics, tissue perfusion, and cellular metabolism under hyperbaric conditions. Current protocols rely on generalized pressure-duration frameworks, which may not account for individual differences in vascular anatomy, tissue oxygenation capacity, or mitochondrial function. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating multi-scale physiological modeling and machine learning to predict personalized HBOT outcomes and mitigate risks such as oxygen toxicity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the simulation of oxygen transport across vascular, interstitial, and cellular compartments using 3D fluid dynamics models parameterized by patient-specific imaging and hemodynamic data. Concurrently, neural networks trained on clinical datasets—including hyperbaric chamber metrics, real-time biosensor outputs, and post-treatment biomarkers—will identify patterns linking protocol variables to therapeutic efficacy and adverse events. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine simulations using machine learning-derived correlations, creating adaptive models that account for dynamic physiological feedback during hyperbaric exposure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for optimizing pressure profiles, session duration, and oxygenation targets tailored to individual patients. This work addresses a critical gap in hyperbaric medicine by bridging mechanistic insights from computational physiology with data-driven clinical decision support. Successful implementation could reduce trial-and-error in protocol design, enhance safety margins, and improve therapeutic precision for complex cases. The project also establishes a foundation for real-time adaptive control systems in hyperbaric technology, leveraging HPC to advance personalized medicine in an emerging interdisciplinary niche.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to operate hyperbaric (recompression) chambers for the treatment of disease. Includes instruction in patient assessment and management, hyperbaric safety, physics of hyperbaric and hypobaric exposures, physiology, hyperbaric chamber operation, and air decompression procedures.

abstract: Concrete finishing practices are critical to the structural integrity, durability, and aesthetics of modern infrastructure, yet current methods for optimizing concrete mixtures and curing processes remain largely empirical. This project seeks to address the inefficiencies and material waste associated with trial-and-error approaches by developing a computational framework to model the physicochemical behavior of concrete mixtures during placement, curing, and finishing. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale interactions between cement hydration, aggregate distribution, and environmental factors (e.g., temperature, humidity) that influence mechanical properties and surface quality. Molecular dynamics simulations will elucidate nanoscale binding mechanisms, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict macroscale stress distribution and cracking tendencies under varying curing conditions. Machine learning models, trained on experimental and simulated datasets, will identify optimal mixture proportions and finishing protocols for targeted performance metrics, such as compressive strength, workability, and resistance to environmental degradation. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of cores to manage the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and stochastic variability in material behavior. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for designing sustainable, high-performance concrete mixes tailored to site-specific constraints, reducing reliance on resource-intensive physical testing. This work will advance the integration of computational materials science into construction technology, offering novel strategies to mitigate carbon footprints, enhance infrastructure longevity, and improve safety in concrete finishing operations. By bridging empirical tradecraft with data-driven modeling, the project aims to establish a paradigm shift in vocational training programs, equipping future concrete professionals with decision-support systems rooted in computational innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to prepare, construct, and finish buildings, components, and related structures using compound masonry mixtures of stone, gravel, sand, cement, and water. Includes instruction in site preparation, applied mathematics, mixing formulas and applications, job estimation, concrete design, finishing techniques, mold preparation, reinforcement installation, site safety, and equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: Ophthalmic diseases, such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration, require early and accurate diagnosis to prevent irreversible vision loss. Current diagnostic workflows in clinical settings rely heavily on manual interpretation of imaging data, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fundus photography, which can introduce variability and delay. This project seeks to develop an automated, high-throughput computational pipeline to enhance the precision and efficiency of ophthalmic diagnostics by leveraging machine learning (ML) models trained on multimodal imaging data. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing large-scale ophthalmic datasets, which are often heterogeneous, high-resolution, and require real-time analysis in clinical workflows. We propose a hybrid approach combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and graph-based models to capture structural relationships in retinal layers, alongside federated learning to address data privacy concerns in multi-institutional collaborations. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage parallelized training of deep learning architectures, optimize hyperparameters at scale, and validate models against diverse, annotated datasets spanning demographic and disease subgroups. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated lesion detection, quantitative biomarkers for disease progression, and a cloud-based interface to assist ophthalmic technicians in prioritizing high-risk cases. By reducing diagnostic latency and inter-observer variability, this work aims to improve clinical decision-making and expand access to vision-saving interventions, particularly in resource-limited settings. The computational framework will also serve as an educational resource for training ophthalmic technologists in emerging AI-driven diagnostic technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist ophthalmologists and optometrists in examining and treating patients with vision problems, vision disorders, and eye diseases. Includes instruction in taking patient histories, administering directed treatments and topical medications, diagnostic test procedures and equipment operation, anatomical and functional ocular measurements, patient care and instruction, ophthalmic and surgical equipment maintenance, safety and sterilization procedures, and office administrative procedures.

abstract: Plant diseases caused by fungal pathogens pose significant threats to global food security, yet the dynamic interplay between pathogen-secreted effector proteins and plant cell wall remodeling during early infection remains poorly understood. This project seeks to unravel the structural and biophysical mechanisms underlying enzymatic degradation of plant cell wall polysaccharides by *Fusarium graminearum*, a devastating wheat pathogen, using multiscale computational modeling. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture real-time, atomic-level interactions due to the complexity and transient nature of cell wall–effector interfaces. We propose an integrated computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-enhanced free energy calculations, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to elucidate how effector enzymes dynamically reconfigure cellulose microfibrils and hemicellulose networks during host penetration. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale MD simulations of effector-cellulose binding trajectories under varying pH and ionic conditions, informed by experimental crystallography data. ML algorithms will predict energy landscapes for enzyme-substrate complexes, while ABM will simulate population-level enzyme activity across heterogeneous cell wall architectures. This approach will identify critical molecular determinants of enzymatic efficiency and plant resistance mechanisms, offering insights into pathogen adaptability. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of effector-cell wall interactions, identification of novel targets for engineered disease resistance, and a publicly accessible database of simulated enzyme dynamics. By bridging gaps between structural biology, soft matter physics, and phytopathology, this work will advance strategies for developing next-generation antifungal treatments and inform the design of pathogen-resistant crop varieties through computational-guided agricultural innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms from an agricultural perspective. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance driver and safety education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the efficacy of instructional strategies in reducing traffic incidents. Traditional driver education programs often rely on static curricula that inadequately address the dynamic, high-risk scenarios novice drivers face. The complexity of human behavior, environmental variables, and real-time decision-making in driving necessitates a computational approach to evaluate how pedagogical methods translate to safer driving outcomes. Current tools lack the capacity to simulate these multifactorial interactions at scale, limiting evidence-based improvements to training frameworks. The proposed study will employ HPC resources to run agent-based simulations that integrate cognitive learning models, traffic pattern data, and risk perception metrics. These simulations will replicate diverse driving scenarios (e.g., adverse weather, distracted driving) while testing variations in teaching methodologies, such as virtual reality training, hazard anticipation drills, and feedback mechanisms. Machine learning techniques will analyze simulation outputs to identify correlations between instructional approaches, skill retention, and collision avoidance behaviors. Additionally, large-scale datasets from state driver licensing agencies and in-vehicle telematics will be processed to validate simulation findings against real-world outcomes. The computational demands of modeling millions of scenario iterations, coupled with high-dimensional data analysis, require the parallel processing and storage capabilities of HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify the impact of specific teaching interventions on safety metrics, enabling the design of adaptive, personalized training programs. This work will directly inform curriculum updates for driver education instructors, prioritizing strategies proven to mitigate risks for diverse learner populations. By bridging computational modeling and teacher education, this project aims to reduce traffic fatalities and improve instructional standards in a critical public health domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach driver and safety education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to advance physics education research by developing computational models to analyze and predict the efficacy of instructional strategies in overcoming persistent student misconceptions. Despite decades of pedagogical innovation, learners across educational levels continue to struggle with fundamental physics concepts such as force interactions, energy conservation, and quantum phenomena. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create large-scale simulations of concept acquisition processes, integrating cognitive science principles with physics education datasets. Agent-based modeling techniques will simulate diverse classroom environments, capturing interactions between instructional methods, student prior knowledge, and problem-solving behaviors. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to multi-institutional datasets containing longitudinal student performance metrics, video analysis of classroom discourse, and digital learning platform interactions. These computational approaches will enable systematic exploration of how variations in curriculum sequencing, technology-enhanced learning tools, and teacher feedback mechanisms influence conceptual mastery. The project will produce (1) predictive models identifying optimal intervention timing for specific misconceptions, (2) evidence-based frameworks for personalizing physics instruction in mixed-ability classrooms, and (3) open-access simulation tools for teacher education programs. By quantifying relationships between pedagogical choices and learning outcomes at unprecedented scale, this research will directly inform the design of teacher training modules and adaptive learning systems. The requested computing resources are essential for handling complex multivariate analyses across terabyte-scale educational datasets and running ensemble simulations that account for the heterogeneous nature of learning environments. Outcomes will strengthen the empirical foundation for physics education practices while demonstrating how computational methods can address persistent challenges in STEM teacher preparation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The rising complexity of pharmacoeconomic evaluations necessitates advanced computational methods to model the multifaceted interactions between pharmaceutical interventions, healthcare systems, and patient outcomes. Current approaches often rely on simplified assumptions due to limitations in handling large-scale datasets, dynamic patient populations, and stochastic variables inherent in real-world drug utilization. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to optimize cost-effectiveness analyses and policy simulations for novel therapeutics. The research will integrate agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations to capture heterogeneous patient behaviors, time-dependent treatment effects, and system-level healthcare costs. Key objectives include parameterizing models with real-world claims data, genomic datasets, and clinical trial outcomes; evaluating the impact of drug pricing policies on health equity; and simulating long-term budget impacts under varying formulary adoption scenarios. Computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to iteratively refine models across thousands of simulations, incorporating sensitivity analyses for variables such as adherence rates, generic/biosimilar entry, and value-based contracting structures. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space and enabling rapid scenario testing unachievable with standard computing resources. Expected outcomes include an open-source pharmacoeconomic modeling toolkit validated against retrospective outcomes data, policy briefs on cost containment strategies for specialty pharmaceuticals, and predictive frameworks to assess the value of precision medicine initiatives. By enhancing the granularity and accuracy of economic evaluations, this work aims to directly inform formulary decision-making, payer negotiations, and regulatory policies while maintaining focus on pharmaceutical-specific applications distinct from broader health systems or public health research. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale data integration, and cloud-based collaboration features for multidisciplinary research teams in pharmacy and health economics.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics and policy analysis to the study of the relationship of pharmacy services and pharmaceutical processes and products to the health care system and their impact on health care organizations. Includes instruction in health economics, pharmacoeconomics, health care systems, health care organization and management, statistics and biostatistics, outcomes research, health care policy, pharmacy services, and pharmaceutical industry operations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational linguistic research on under-documented South Asian languages, focusing on syntactic, morphological, and phonetic patterns in languages such as Sindhi, Maithili, and Tulu. These languages, though spoken by millions, lack robust digital corpora and tools for large-scale analysis, hindering advances in both theoretical linguistics and language preservation. The research problem centers on overcoming computational limitations in processing complex morphosyntactic structures and low-resource speech data, which traditional single-threaded workflows cannot efficiently handle. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable pipelines for corpus construction, automated morphological parsing, and cross-dialect phonetic modeling. Neural transformer architectures will be fine-tuned using distributed training on GPU clusters to analyze syntactic trees and phoneme distributions across diverse speech samples. Phonetic data, including tonal and aspirated consonant features, will undergo parallelized acoustic analysis using Python-based signal processing libraries optimized for HPC environments. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, annotated multilingual corpus for these languages, machine learning models for morphosyntactic prediction, and phonetic maps highlighting dialectal variations. These resources will enable quantitative testing of historical linguistics hypotheses about language contact in South Asia while providing tools for educators and preservation initiatives. The project’s computational demands—such as processing terabytes of audio-text paired data and training transformer models on non-standard orthographies—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve timely results. By integrating computational linguistics with area studies, this work aims to set a precedent for ethically grounded, technology-driven research in under-resourced language contexts, with implications for NLP applications and interdisciplinary scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: South Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in South Asian languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing pedagogical strategies for social science teacher education through large-scale analysis of classroom interaction data and simulation modeling. A critical challenge in teacher preparation is understanding how novice educators internalize and adapt discipline-specific teaching practices—such as facilitating discussions on complex sociohistorical issues or integrating primary sources—amidst diverse classroom contexts. While prior studies have relied on small-scale qualitative coding or self-reported data, this project will computationally analyze multimodal datasets spanning video recordings of classroom instruction, longitudinal student performance metrics, and demographic context data from 200+ secondary social science classrooms. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, we will model discourse patterns and instructional scaffolding in teacher-student interactions. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how variations in pedagogical training approaches propagate through early-career teaching behaviors. These computationally intensive methods require HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train deep learning models for multimodal analysis, and run parallelized simulations across diverse parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying high-impact teaching practices correlated with improved student engagement in social science disciplines, (2) developing predictive models of how teacher training experiences translate into classroom implementation, and (3) generating actionable frameworks for teacher educators to tailor instruction around equity-focused, inquiry-based pedagogy. By scaling analysis beyond traditional observational methodologies, this work aims to address systemic gaps in preparing educators to teach socially charged topics effectively. The requested computing resources will enable processing of unstructured data (e.g., video, free-response evaluations) and iterative model refinement that would be infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure. Findings will directly inform curriculum updates in partner teacher preparation programs, with broader implications for advancing evidence-based practices in social science education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific social science subjects and programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Behavioral disorders in companion animals present complex challenges that intersect biological, environmental, and psychological factors. Current approaches to diagnosing and treating these conditions—such as anxiety, aggression, or compulsive behaviors—rely heavily on observational assessments and trial-and-error applications of behavior modification techniques. However, the interplay between neurological, genetic, and environmental variables remains poorly quantified, limiting the personalization and efficacy of interventions. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing computational models that predict behavioral outcomes and optimize treatment strategies. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets, including longitudinal behavioral assessments, electronic health records, neuroimaging data, and genomic profiles from companion animals (primarily dogs and cats). Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify biomarkers of specific disorders, classify subtypes of behavioral pathologies, and simulate the effects of behavior modification protocols under varying physiological conditions. Agent-based modeling will further simulate owner-pet interactions to evaluate how environmental adjustments influence treatment trajectories. Additionally, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) models will be developed to predict dose-response relationships for psychoactive medications, accounting for interspecies and individual metabolic differences. The computational intensity of integrating these heterogeneous datasets—particularly when handling high-resolution neuroimaging or whole-genome sequences—necessitates scalable HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide clinicians in selecting targeted therapies, reducing reliance on generic protocols, and minimizing adverse drug reactions. By elucidating the systems-level mechanisms underlying behavioral disorders, this work aims to advance evidence-based veterinary behavioral medicine, improve animal welfare, and reduce the economic and emotional burdens on pet owners. The resulting models and pipelines will be disseminated as open-source resources to foster collaboration across veterinary and computational research communities.
cip_definition: Research on how to understand and treat the behavioral problems of animals, primarily through the application of behavior modification techniques to companion animals; may also involve diagnosis of medical conditions that can affect a pet's behavior, and the use of medication in conjunction with behavior modification therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance precision in large animal surgical and medical interventions through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address high morbidity rates linked to postoperative complications in food animals and equines. Despite advancements in veterinary care, variability in patient outcomes persists due to complex interactions between species-specific anatomy, metabolic demands, and disease pathophysiology. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, which inadequately account for individual biomechanical, physiological, and genomic factors. To bridge this gap, we propose developing species-specific multiscale models integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for biomechanical stress prediction during surgical procedures, machine learning (ML)-enabled risk stratification using retrospective electronic health records (n > 50,000 cases), and genomic variant analysis to identify biomarkers associated with recovery trajectories. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of high-resolution imaging data (CT/MRI), whole-genome sequencing datasets, and real-time sensor data from wearable monitoring devices deployed in perioperative care. Computational workflows will be optimized using GPU-accelerated frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) for ML model training and ANSYS for FEA simulations. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing surgical planning (e.g., orthopedic implant design in equines, cesarean section protocols in dairy cattle) and personalized analgesia/anesthesia regimens. This work will establish open-access computational pipelines tailored to veterinary applications, directly addressing critical gaps in food animal and equine medicine. By reducing complication rates through data-driven precision, the project aims to improve welfare in production and sport animals while mitigating economic losses linked to prolonged recovery. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the computational burden of multimodal data integration and deliver scalable, translatable solutions for clinical veterinary practice.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Large Animal/ Food Animal and Equine Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of herd, work, sport, and food animals. Includes instruction in equine medicine, swine and dairy medicine, food animal medicine, pathophysiology, large animal diseases, large animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: The cultivation of ornamental plants faces increasing challenges due to climate variability, pest pressures, and consumer demand for novel aesthetic traits. Traditional breeding approaches are often constrained by the complex genetic architectures underlying ornamental traits such as flower morphology, pigmentation, and stress resilience, leading to prolonged development cycles. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the identification of genetic markers and optimize trait prediction models for ornamental species, including roses, orchids, and ornamental grasses. We will integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic datasets from controlled greenhouse trials and field experiments to construct machine learning models that correlate genetic variation with traits of commercial and ecological interest. Key computational tasks include genome-wide association studies (GWAS), population genomic simulations, and deep learning-based image analysis of floral and foliar phenotypes. These analyses demand large-scale parallel processing to handle multidimensional data (e.g., terabyte-scale sequencing files, high-resolution imagery) and iterative model training. HPC resources will also enable the simulation of genotype-environment interactions under projected climate scenarios to prioritize resilient cultivars. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes for marker-assisted breeding, predictive frameworks for trait introgression, and optimized growth protocols tailored to regional climatic conditions. By reducing the trial-and-error phase of breeding programs, this work aims to enhance the efficiency of developing commercially viable ornamental varieties with improved adaptability, thereby supporting the horticulture industry’s economic and environmental sustainability. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to advance precision horticulture research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on domesticated plants and plant materials used for decorative and recreational applications and prepares individuals to breed, grow, and utilize ornamental plant varieties for commercial and aesthetic purposes. Includes instruction in applicable plant science subjects, the environmental design and artistic aspects of horticultural product usage, and the management of horticultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of information operations (IO) and psychological warfare (PSYWAR) in contemporary conflict environments, with a focus on modeling the interplay between military media strategies, adversarial disinformation campaigns, and public perception. As digital platforms accelerate the spread of narratives and erode traditional boundaries between civilian and combatant information spaces, military planners require predictive tools to assess how IO tactics influence strategic outcomes. Current models often lack the computational granularity to simulate multi-domain information ecosystems—spanning social media, state-aligned media, and covert influence networks—while accounting for cultural, linguistic, and behavioral variables. The research proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling (ABM), and network science to analyze real-time information flows and forecast the efficacy of counter-messaging strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing petabytes of multilingual social media data, training transformer-based models to detect emerging narrative patterns, and running large-scale simulations of population-level cognitive responses to IO campaigns. The project will leverage existing military doctrine documents, historical PSYWAR case studies, and live data streams from conflict zones to validate models. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for optimizing media engagement timelines, identifying vulnerabilities in adversarial information networks, and quantifying the second-order effects of narrative interventions. By bridging computational social science with defense-specific operational requirements, this work aims to advance the empirical foundations of information warfare while addressing ethical considerations in AI-driven influence analytics. Results will inform policy frameworks for responsible military-civilian media coordination in contested information environments.
cip_title: Information/ Psychological Warfare and Military Media Relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the support of military and strategic operations and policy via the use of information as a tool of statecraft and warfighting. Includes instruction in information technology and systems, information security, command and control, satellite communications, global information dissemination, communications and media management, intelligence, psychological warfare, strategic planning, security policy and doctrine, and applications to specific operations, services, and scenarios.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in educational assessment by developing advanced computational models to analyze complex, multidimensional assessment data at scale. Traditional psychometric methods often struggle to account for dynamic learning processes, contextual biases, and high-dimensional interaction patterns inherent in modern digital learning platforms and adaptive testing systems. The research will employ machine learning architectures and Bayesian hierarchical models to (1) detect latent skill trajectories across heterogeneous student populations, (2) quantify differential item functioning in culturally diverse contexts, and (3) optimize automated scoring systems for constructed-response assessments. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on longitudinal response data from 2.5 million learners across 14 state assessment systems, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate measurement invariance, and implementing parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithms for large-scale item response theory parameter estimation. Computational challenges include managing sparse, nested data structures across multiple assessment modalities (e.g., game-based tasks, multimedia stimuli) while maintaining interpretability for educational decision-making. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time diagnostic assessment analytics, improved detection of biased test items through neural network attribution methods, and optimized algorithms for adaptive test assembly that reduce computational latency by 40% compared to current industry standards. By enhancing the scalability and precision of measurement models, this work will directly inform the design of fairer, more responsive assessment systems while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of psychometrics and computational education research.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for designing, developing, implementing and evaluating tests and other mechanisms used to measure learning, evaluate student progress, and assess the performance of specific teaching tools, strategies and curricula. Includes instruction in psychometric measurement, instrument design, test implementation techniques, research evaluation, data reporting requirements, and data analysis and interpretation.

abstract: Dental caries and periodontal diseases remain prevalent global health challenges, driven by complex microbial biofilm communities in the oral cavity. Traditional experimental approaches to studying these biofilms face limitations in resolving spatial-temporal dynamics, interspecies interactions, and substrate adhesion mechanisms at micron and sub-second scales. This project proposes a computational framework to model oral biofilm formation, structural evolution, and response to antimicrobial agents using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will employ hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to capture multiscale processes, from molecular-level interactions between bacterial adhesins and tooth enamel hydroxyapatite to population-level biofilm expansion under varying oral environments. The ABM component will integrate empirical data from microbial culturing assays to parameterize species-specific growth rates, metabolic cooperation, and quorum sensing behaviors, while MD simulations will elucidate atomic-scale binding affinities critical for early biofilm adhesion. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across thousands of microbial agents and billions of molecular interactions, particularly when modeling clinically relevant timeframes (24-72 hours) at high spatial resolution. Expected outcomes include identification of key molecular targets for disrupting biofilm initiation, predictive models of pH-dependent antimicrobial efficacy, and optimization of topical treatment delivery kinetics. These results will directly inform preclinical studies in caries prevention strategies and provide a computational platform for testing novel biomaterials in restorative dentistry. By bridging gaps between molecular mechanisms and ecological biofilm behavior, this work aims to advance personalized preventive dentistry frameworks while demonstrating how computational modeling can accelerate translational research in oral health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in dentistry.

abstract: Radiation therapy treatment planning requires precise modeling of radiation interactions with biological tissues to maximize tumor control while minimizing damage to healthy structures. Current approaches often rely on simplified computational models that inadequately capture tissue heterogeneity, dynamic physiological processes, and secondary particle effects, leading to suboptimal dose predictions. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, patient-specific radiation transport framework using advanced Monte Carlo methods accelerated by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will address two interconnected challenges: (1) the prohibitive computational cost of modeling multi-scale radiation interactions across anatomically complex geometries, and (2) the integration of real-time biological response data into dose optimization pipelines. Leveraging GPU-accelerated versions of established Monte Carlo codes (e.g., TOPAS, Geant4), we will implement parallelized simulations of proton and photon beam interactions at cellular resolution, incorporating 4D CT datasets and spatially resolved radiobiological parameters. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated data to enable rapid sensitivity analyses of treatment parameters. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental microdosimetry data and clinical outcomes from retrospective patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive radiotherapy planning that accounts for intra-fractional anatomical changes and patient-specific radiosensitivity, potentially reducing normal tissue complication probabilities by 15–20% compared to conventional methods. Additionally, the developed models will enable novel investigations into low-dose radiation effects relevant to public health, including secondary cancer risks from scatter radiation and environmental exposure scenarios. This work directly aligns with the Health/Medical Physics program’s emphasis on computational applications in therapeutic processes and radiation protection, while providing a scalable infrastructure for future studies in personalized cancer care and epidemiological risk modeling. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the petabyte-scale datasets and trillion-particle simulations required to achieve clinically relevant statistical precision.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics, nuclear science, and engineering physics to diagnostic, treatment, and therapeutic processes and public health protection. Includes instruction in radiation biophysics, biophysics, health effects of natural and artificially induced radiation, hazard evaluation, environmental radioactivity, nuclear physics, engineering physics, radiobiology, medical radiology, calibration and dosage theory, computer applications and medical informatics, and specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the safety, precision, and personalization of permanent cosmetics and therapeutic tattooing through advanced computational modeling. Despite the growing demand for these procedures in aesthetic and clinical contexts (e.g., scar camouflage, areola restoration), practitioners lack evidence-based tools to predict pigment behavior in heterogeneous skin types or optimize outcomes for diverse anatomical regions. Current methods rely on heuristic experience, risking suboptimal results, prolonged healing, or adverse reactions. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model pigment dispersion, tissue interaction, and long-term retention. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of needle-skin mechanics across micron-resolution 3D skin models derived from clinical imaging data, incorporating variables such as epidermal thickness, melanin distribution, and scar tissue biomechanics. ML algorithms trained on longitudinal clinical datasets will correlate simulation outputs with observed pigment migration and fading patterns, while CFD models will assess the role of needle geometry and injection parameters in intracellular pigment deposition. The resulting predictive platform will quantify procedural risks (e.g., granuloma formation) and optimize pigment selection, needle configurations, and insertion angles for individual patient profiles. By establishing the first computational pipeline for this understudied domain, this work aims to reduce procedural complications, standardize training protocols, and inform regulatory frameworks for emerging techniques like semi-permanent makeup removal via laser-tissue interaction modeling. Outcomes will be disseminated through open-access tools for practitioners and partnerships with licensing boards to integrate computational insights into safety guidelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to prepare and apply permanent markings, color, and cosmetic products to the face and body for aesthetic or clinical purposes; to remove unwanted markings; and to function as licensed permanent makeup artists and tattooists.  Includes instruction in client consultation; sterilization and sanitation; skin anatomy, diseases, and disorders; skin preparation and anesthetics; color theory; machine theory and operation; needle selection; applications such as eyebrows, eyeliners, lips, lipliners, beauty marks, and blemish/mark removal; after care; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized orthotic and prosthetic (O&P) device design through computational biomechanical modeling and machine learning, addressing critical limitations in traditional fabrication methods. Current O&P practices rely on static anatomical measurements and qualitative assessments, often resulting in suboptimal device fit, discomfort, and secondary complications such as pressure injuries or compensatory gait patterns. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework to simulate dynamic interactions between custom devices and patient-specific musculoskeletal tissues under real-world loading conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable finite element analysis of tissue-device interface stresses, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms trained on biomechanical datasets to optimize device geometry, material distribution, and compliance. Input data will integrate 3D anatomical reconstructions from clinical imaging, sensor-derived gait kinetics/kinematics, and tissue property measurements from indentation testing. The computational pipeline will iteratively predict pressure hotspots, energy expenditure during mobility, and long-term tissue adaptation risks, generating design recommendations that balance structural integrity with physiological compatibility. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting device efficacy prior to fabrication, reducing trial-and-error adjustments during clinical fitting. This work bridges gaps between clinical O&P practice and computational engineering, with potential to establish new standards for data-driven assistive device personalization. Successful implementation could significantly improve functional outcomes for patients with limb loss or neuromuscular impairment while reducing healthcare costs associated with device-related complications. The scale of biomechanical simulations and machine learning training—requiring parallel processing of high-resolution meshes and terabyte-scale motion capture datasets—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically relevant turnaround times.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: The proposed research addresses inverse problems arising in partial differential equation (PDE) models of physical systems, with applications to nondestructive material evaluation and biomedical imaging. Many such problems involve reconstructing spatially varying parameters from sparse boundary measurements—a computationally intensive task requiring high-resolution discretization of multiscale domains and iterative optimization over high-dimensional spaces. Current approaches struggle with the ill-posed nature of these reconstructions and the computational expense of repeatedly solving forward models. This project develops a hybrid computational framework combining asymptotic analysis, adaptive finite element methods, and Bayesian-inspired optimization to regularize and accelerate parameter identification. The methodology leverages asymptotic expansions to derive reduced-order models that inform preconditioning strategies for large-scale PDE-constrained optimization. Adaptive mesh refinement will target regions of high solution sensitivity identified through adjoint-based error indicators. We propose implementing parallelized optimization algorithms using PETSc and FEniCS, exploiting high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the O(10^6)-degree-of-freedom systems generated by three-dimensional multiphysics simulations. The computational demands stem from (1) ensemble evaluations for uncertainty quantification across parameter space, (2) distributed linear algebra operations for Newton-Krylov optimization steps, and (3) memory-intensive sparse direct solvers required for ill-conditioned forward problems. Expected outcomes include new provably convergent algorithms for inverse medium problems with quantified reconstruction uncertainties, validated through applications to photoacoustic tomography and composite material characterization. The developed methods will advance computational inverse problem techniques in applied mathematics by bridging asymptotic analysis with data-driven optimization, while the HPC implementation strategies will provide template architectures for resource-aware parameter estimation in industrial-scale models. Successful execution requires dedicated allocation for sustained parallel workloads, including GPU-accelerated linear algebra and distributed memory systems to handle the dual challenges of numerical precision and algorithmic scalability.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as engineering and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in natural phenomena modeling continuum mechanics, reaction-diffusion, wave propagation, dynamic systems, numerical analysis, controlled theory, asymptotic methods, variation, optimization theory, inverse problems, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: Livestock diseases significantly threaten global food security, animal welfare, and agricultural economies. A critical challenge in veterinary medicine is the rapid identification of genetic and molecular factors influencing disease susceptibility and treatment efficacy, particularly in species such as cattle, swine, and poultry. While advances in genomics and molecular modeling offer promising tools, the scale and complexity of multi-omics data—combined with the need for precise, species-specific pharmacological insights—exceed the capabilities of conventional computing systems. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps through two interconnected aims. First, we will conduct large-scale genomic analyses to identify signatures of disease resistance in livestock populations, integrating whole-genome sequencing data with machine learning models to prioritize candidate genes for zoonotic pathogens such as *Salmonella* and avian influenza. Second, molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to model interactions between veterinary therapeutics and pathogen-specific targets, enabling rapid in silico screening of drug candidates. These computational workflows will require parallelized processing of terabytes of genomic data, GPU-accelerated simulations, and high-memory nodes to manage complex phylogenetic and structural datasets. The outcomes will provide actionable insights into breeding strategies for disease-resistant livestock and accelerate the development of targeted therapies, directly benefiting veterinary practice and agricultural sustainability. By establishing scalable pipelines for veterinary genomics and drug discovery, this project will also create educational resources for pre-veterinary trainees, fostering proficiency in computational tools critical to modern animal health research. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to overcoming current bottlenecks in data analysis and simulation, ensuring timely translation of results to clinical and agricultural settings.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in veterinary medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurochemical mechanisms underlying behavioral responses to psychoactive compounds using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral data analysis. A key challenge in psychopharmacology is resolving how molecular interactions between drugs, receptors, and neural circuits translate to quantifiable behavioral outcomes across varying biological contexts. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the multi-scale complexity of these interactions, particularly when accounting for individual differences in neurophysiology or combinatorial effects of polypharmacy. To address this gap, we propose developing biophysically grounded neural network models that integrate pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic principles with behavioral outcome data from preclinical studies. The models will simulate dose-response dynamics across three levels: (1) molecular-scale binding kinetics of neurotransmitters and drugs (e.g., SSRIs, NMDA antagonists) derived from molecular dynamics simulations, (2) circuit-level neural population dynamics modeled through coupled differential equations, and (3) behavioral readouts mapped via reinforcement learning frameworks trained on experimental rodent behavioral datasets. High-performance computing resources are essential for several components: GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulations of drug-receptor binding (using AMBER and GROMACS), parallelized parameter sweeps across neurophysiological conditions, and large-scale optimization of neural circuit models against behavioral datasets encompassing >10^6 data points from open-source repositories. Expected outcomes include predictive models of substance-induced behavioral variability based on individual neurochemical profiles, identification of novel targets for behavioral modulation, and quantitative frameworks for assessing polypharmacy risks. These results will advance computational psychopharmacology by establishing open-source tools for simulating drug-behavior interactions while reducing reliance on exploratory animal testing. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scaling of in silico experiments across neurochemical parameter spaces, directly supporting NIH initiatives to develop alternatives to conventional behavioral pharmacology paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the behavioral effects of medications, drugs, nutrients, and chemicals (including natural and artificial toxins) in laboratory and clinical settings. Includes instruction in pharmacology, behavioral toxicology and pharmacology, neuroscience, physiology, clinical psychopharmacology, substance abuse treatments and antidotes, neurochemical mechanisms, epidemiology of chemicals and substances, biochemical interactions, and psychoactive drugs.

abstract: Forklift operations are integral to material handling across industries, yet workplace accidents persist due to complex interactions between human operators, equipment dynamics, and environmental variables. Traditional safety training and operational protocols often lack empirical validation under diverse, high-risk scenarios, limiting their effectiveness. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate forklift operations in dynamic environments, enabling data-driven optimization of safety practices. The research problem centers on understanding how operator behavior, load physics, and workspace layouts contribute to accident risks—factors difficult to isolate in real-world studies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose an agent-based modeling approach combined with machine learning to simulate multi-agent interactions (e.g., forklifts, pedestrians, inventory systems) in virtual warehouses. High-resolution sensor data from real forklifts will inform physics-based models of load stability and equipment kinematics, while reinforcement learning algorithms will train adaptive operator agents under stochastic conditions. The simulations will test scenarios such as narrow-aisle navigation, blind-spot collisions, and emergency braking, quantifying risk probabilities across variables like operator fatigue, load asymmetry, and floor surface friction. By scaling these simulations to thousands of parallelized trials via HPC, we aim to identify critical risk thresholds and generate predictive models for accident prevention. Expected outcomes include actionable strategies for workspace design, real-time safety alert systems, and personalized training modules informed by risk-prediction analytics. This work will advance vocational education by integrating computational safety analysis into forklift operator training curricula while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in technical fields traditionally reliant on empirical methods. The computational datasets and models will be shared publicly to support further innovation in industrial safety research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate forklifts in a variety of work environments. Includes instruction in accident prevention, forklift operation, materials handling, and worksite safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in automated medical transcription systems by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to enhance the accuracy, adaptability, and security of speech-to-text technologies in clinical environments. Current automated speech recognition (ASR) systems struggle with domain-specific challenges, including rapid speaker turnover, overlapping dialogue in multidisciplinary team meetings, and highly specialized medical terminology across subdisciplines (e.g., rare disease nomenclature in genetic counseling sessions). The research will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures to train multimodal transformer-based models that concurrently process audio waveforms, contextual speaker metadata, and real-time terminology validation from federated clinical knowledge bases. A hybrid approach combining contrastive learning for accent-agnostic acoustic modeling and few-shot adaptation for emerging terminology will be implemented, requiring distributed training across terabytes of de-identified clinical dictations spanning 15 medical specialties. Privacy-preserving techniques, including differential privacy and on-the-fly audio redaction, will be integrated to meet healthcare data compliance standards. Anticipated outcomes include a deployable ASR pipeline capable of sub-500ms latency with <5% word error rate in complex clinical scenarios, validated against gold-standard human transcriptions. The computational infrastructure will also enable large-scale analysis of temporal patterns in clinician dictation behaviors, informing usability improvements for EHR-integrated transcription tools. By bridging computational linguistics, clinical informatics, and edge computing, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for AI-assisted medical documentation that reduces cognitive burdens on healthcare professionals while maintaining rigorous accuracy and privacy standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to execute verbatim medical conference minutes, medical reports, and medical orders. Includes instruction in dictation and simultaneous recording, analysis of notes and visual evidence, medical terminology, data processing applications and skills, formal medical report and correspondence formats, professional standards, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Palliative care nursing requires the integration of complex, multimodal data—including clinical, psychosocial, and behavioral metrics—to optimize patient-centered care for individuals with life-limiting illnesses. However, existing approaches often struggle to synthesize these heterogeneous datasets in real time, limiting the ability to predict symptom trajectories, personalize interventions, or model the impact of care strategies on patient and family outcomes. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and computational frameworks tailored to palliative care contexts. Using de-identified electronic health records, patient-reported outcomes, and qualitative data from caregiver interviews, we will employ machine learning techniques to identify patterns in symptom clusters, treatment responses, and quality-of-life indicators. Natural language processing will be applied to analyze unstructured clinical notes and interview transcripts, enabling the integration of narrative data into predictive analytics. Agent-based modeling will simulate patient-provider interactions to evaluate the potential impact of care delivery modifications. These computationally intensive tasks demand parallel processing capabilities and large-scale data storage, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the creation of dynamic risk-stratification tools to guide early intervention for pain and symptom crises, as well as decision-support systems to tailor care plans to individual patient values and contextual factors. By elucidating the interplay between biological, psychological, and social determinants of palliative outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in symptom management and bereavement support. The resulting computational pipelines will be shared as open-source tools to strengthen research capacity in palliative care nursing, ultimately contributing to improved quality of life for patients and families facing serious illness.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide a combination of active and compassionate therapies intended to comfort and support patients and their families who are living with life-threatening illness. Includes instruction in pathophysiology, palliative care processes, pain management, pharmacology, loss, grief, death, and bereavement.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dental restorative procedures demands precise, patient-specific approaches to optimize clinical outcomes and material longevity. Current methods for predicting biomechanical performance of dental restorations—such as crowns, bridges, and implants—rely on simplified models that fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between restorative materials, oral tissues, and occlusal forces. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and predict the biomechanical behavior of dental restorations under clinically relevant conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct patient-specific 3D models derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and intraoral scans, integrating material properties, mastication dynamics, and temporal degradation factors. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to model stress distribution, fatigue failure, and interfacial interactions between restorations and biological tissues. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze large datasets of clinical outcomes to identify predictive patterns linking restoration design parameters to long-term success rates. The computational workflow will be validated against in vitro experiments and retrospective clinical data. This project requires HPC capabilities to manage the high-resolution meshing, multi-physics simulations, and iterative optimization processes inherent to modeling complex oral biomechanics. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for optimizing restoration design, reducing clinical failure rates, and informing material selection guidelines. By bridging computational engineering and clinical dentistry, this work aims to advance personalized treatment planning, reduce costs associated with restorative failures, and contribute foundational insights into the biomechanical adaptation of dental materials. The proposed resource allocation will enable scalable, parallelized simulations that are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure, directly supporting innovation in evidence-based dental practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of dental clinical techniques and dental practice issues. Includes instruction in subjects such as the history of dentistry, advanced dental practice management, dental ethics and jurisprudence, social and behavioral science studies of dentistry, advanced restorative dentistry, oral medicine, oral radiology, advanced clinical procedures and technology, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and functional integration of implantable biosensors for real-time monitoring of physiological biomarkers. A critical challenge in biomedical device engineering lies in balancing sensor sensitivity, biocompatibility, and long-term stability within dynamic biological environments. Current experimental approaches are limited in resolving multiscale interactions between sensor materials, biofluids, and host tissue responses. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model sensor-tissue interfaces across spatial and temporal scales. MD will simulate atomic-level interactions between sensor coatings and proteins to predict fouling risks, while FEA will model mechanical strain distributions and electrochemical signal stability under physiological conditions. A neural network trained on these datasets will identify optimal sensor geometries and material compositions. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the need for parallelized MD trajectories (10⁶–10⁷ atoms) over microsecond timescales, coupled with multiphysics FEA simulations incorporating fluid-structure interactions and diffusion-reaction kinetics. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking sensor design parameters to in vivo performance metrics, validated against experimental data from collaborator labs. This work will establish an open-source toolkit for accelerated biosensor prototyping, reducing iterative animal trials and enabling patient-specific device customization. By addressing computational bottlenecks in multiscale biointerface modeling, the project aims to advance translational biomedical engineering while fostering HPC-enabled innovation in medical technology development.
detailed_field: Biological/ biosystems engineering and biomedical technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Pediatric dermatological disorders, such as congenital ichthyoses, vascular anomalies, and severe atopic dermatitis, present unique therapeutic challenges due to their complex pathophysiology and the vulnerability of developing tissues. Current treatment protocols often rely on limited evidence from adult studies, underscoring the need for pediatric-specific mechanistic insights. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model disease pathways, predict treatment responses, and optimize therapeutic strategies tailored to pediatric populations. The research focuses on three computational aims: (1) integrating multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) from pediatric skin biopsies to identify age-specific molecular drivers of disease; (2) developing machine learning models to simulate drug interactions within pediatric skin microenvironments, prioritizing compounds with minimal off-target effects on growth pathways; and (3) employing agent-based modeling to map immune cell dynamics in inflammatory skin conditions, such as juvenile psoriasis, under varying therapeutic regimens. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale biomedical datasets (≥100 TB), running parallelized molecular dynamics simulations to assess drug efficacy, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized treatment selection, novel biomarkers for disease progression, and mechanistic insights into pediatric-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. By bridging computational innovation with clinical dermatology, this work aims to establish a framework for precision medicine in pediatric skin disease, reducing trial-and-error prescribing and improving long-term outcomes for patients. The requested computing infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models, validation against institutional electronic health records, and open sharing of computational tools via pediatric dermatology research consortia.
cip_definition: Research focused on the treatment of specific skin disease categories, with emphasis on those diseases which predominate in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized neuromotor rehabilitation protocols for individuals with rare neuromuscular disorders, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome current limitations in real-time biosignal processing and adaptive modeling. Current rehabilitation strategies for conditions such as hereditary sensory-motor neuropathies or focal dystonias often rely on generalized therapeutic approaches, which fail to account for the high inter-individual variability in neuromuscular pathophysiology and real-time biomechanical responses. The research problem centers on the lack of dynamic, patient-specific models that integrate electromyographic (EMG), inertial measurement unit (IMU), and neuroimaging data to predict optimal therapeutic interventions. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational pipeline combining finite element modeling of muscle-tendon dynamics with machine learning-driven analysis of neural activation patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of multimodal data streams (sampled at 2 kHz across 16 channels) during simulated therapeutic tasks, coupled with GPU-accelerated training of recurrent neural networks to identify latent biomarkers of motor adaptation. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for generating patient-specific rehabilitation profiles, capable of predicting optimal resistance levels, movement trajectories, and neurofeedback timing in simulated environments. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and clinical rehabilitation by establishing a scalable platform for precision therapeutics in underserved neuromuscular populations. The requested resources will specifically support the parameterization of multi-scale musculoskeletal models, real-time data assimilation, and validation against a longitudinal dataset of 120 patients across five rare disorder subtypes. Successful implementation could redefine therapeutic paradigms for rare neuromuscular conditions while providing a template for HPC-enabled adaptive rehabilitation across broader health contexts.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rehabilitation and therapeutic professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize hydraulic fracturing and reservoir management in unconventional petroleum systems. The research addresses the critical challenge of predicting fluid flow and fracture propagation in heterogeneous subsurface formations, where existing models struggle to account for multiscale geological complexities, multiphase flow dynamics, and coupled geomechanical effects. Current approaches often oversimplify fracture networks or rely on coarse grid resolutions, leading to inaccurate production forecasts and suboptimal well-completion strategies. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated workflow combining three-dimensional discrete fracture network modeling, coupled fluid-solid interaction simulations, and machine learning-driven parameter upscaling. The computational approach leverages parallelized finite element methods for fracture propagation and hybrid finite volume/discontinuous Galerkin schemes for multiphase flow simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the required spatial discretization (10^8–10^9 grid cells) and temporal resolution across multiple physical domains. The workflow will be implemented using MPI-OpenMP hybrid parallelism, with adaptive mesh refinement to concentrate computational resources on dynamically evolving fracture fronts. Validation will employ field data from Permian Basin well logs and microseismic monitoring arrays. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source simulation package capable of predicting production yields with <15% error relative to field measurements, compared to current industry-standard tools exhibiting 30–40% errors. The research will directly inform strategies to maximize hydrocarbon recovery while minimizing water usage and environmental footprint through optimized fracture spacing and fluid injection protocols. Results will be disseminated through three peer-reviewed publications and a workshop for industry partners, potentially reducing operational costs by $2–4 million per well through improved completion designs. This work bridges critical gaps in petroleum engineering by enabling physics-based, data-informed decision-making at field scales.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mining and petroleum engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders represent a leading cause of global disability, yet diagnostic imaging approaches for early detection and personalized treatment planning remain limited by conventional analytic methods. This project seeks to address the critical need for advanced computational tools to improve the accuracy and predictive capacity of musculoskeletal radiology in characterizing degenerative joint diseases, traumatic injuries, and metabolic bone disorders. We propose developing a multimodal artificial intelligence framework integrating high-resolution MRI, CT, and clinical data to enable automated tissue segmentation, biomechanical modeling, and biomarker discovery. The computational workflow will employ deep learning architectures—including 3D convolutional neural networks and graph-based models—to analyze spatial relationships in imaging data while accounting for patient-specific factors such as age, activity history, and comorbidities. A key innovation involves coupling these models with finite element simulations to predict load-dependent tissue degeneration patterns in osteoarthritic joints. Successful implementation requires access to high-performance computing resources to manage the processing of multi-terabyte imaging datasets, parallelized training of memory-intensive neural networks, and iterative biomechanical simulations across diverse anatomical geometries. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms for automated detection of subclinical musculoskeletal pathology, (2) predictive models of disease progression in weight-bearing joints, and (3) quantitative imaging biomarkers correlating with histopathological and biomechanical ground truth data. This work will directly enhance diagnostic radiology practice by enabling earlier intervention in degenerative conditions and data-driven surgical planning for complex fractures. By leveraging scalable computational infrastructure, the project establishes a foundation for translating research insights into clinical decision support systems that improve patient outcomes while reducing healthcare costs associated with delayed diagnoses.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders or injuries of the joints, bones, muscles, and spine in adults and children.

abstract: Welding processes involve complex, multi-physics interactions between thermal, mechanical, and metallurgical phenomena that are challenging to model with conventional experimental or computational methods. This project seeks to advance the understanding of welding dynamics through high-fidelity simulations enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on the need to predict and mitigate defects such as porosity, residual stress, and microstructural inhomogeneity in high-strength alloys used in critical applications like aerospace and automotive manufacturing. Current analytical models lack the resolution to capture transient heat transfer, molten metal flow, and phase transformations at the scales necessary to optimize welding parameters. This work proposes a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and phase-field modeling to simulate multi-pass arc welding and laser beam welding processes. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of 3D weld pools, solidification behavior, and stress evolution at micron-level resolution, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify parameter sets that minimize defects while maximizing joint efficiency. By correlating simulated thermal histories with experimental metallography and mechanical testing data, the models will be validated against physical benchmarks. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for tailoring welding procedures to specific material combinations, reducing trial-and-error in process development, and improving the reliability of welded structures. The computational workflows developed will also serve as educational resources for training welding technology students in advanced numerical methods. Access to HPC resources is critical due to the memory-intensive nature of multi-scale simulations and the need for rapid iteration across diverse welding scenarios. This project bridges gaps between empirical welding practice and computational materials science, with potential impacts on industrial standards and the design of next-generation welding systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to join or cut metal surfaces. Includes instruction in arc welding, resistance welding, brazing and soldering, cutting, high-energy beam welding and cutting, solid state welding, ferrous and non-ferrous materials, oxidation-reduction reactions, welding metallurgy, welding processes and heat treating, structural design, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical phonological evolution of North Germanic languages using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on understudied sound shifts in regional Scandinavian dialects from the Viking Age to the early modern period.
