Includes instruction in data analysis, data-driven decision-making, data mining, higher education administration and organization, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: The effective preparation of health occupations educators requires innovative approaches to address complex pedagogical challenges in vocational training environments. Current limitations in traditional teacher education models stem from an inability to dynamically simulate clinical learning scenarios, analyze multimodal student performance data at scale, and personalize instruction for diverse healthcare specializations. This project proposes the development of an artificial intelligence-driven instructional design platform requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance health occupations pedagogy. The research will employ deep learning architectures to process heterogeneous educational datasets—including simulated patient interactions, skills competency assessments, and biometric feedback from virtual reality training sessions—to identify patterns in instructional effectiveness. Monte Carlo methods will be implemented to model the outcomes of different teaching strategies across varied learner populations and healthcare disciplines (e.g., nursing, radiology, physical therapy). The computational intensity of training transformer-based models on multimodal educational data, coupled with real-time analysis of high-fidelity clinical simulations, necessitates distributed computing capabilities and GPU-accelerated processing. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a predictive framework for optimizing health-specific lesson plans based on learner analytics, 2) generative AI tools for creating adaptive clinical scenarios, and 3) computational evidence supporting competency-based assessment protocols. By enabling large-scale analysis of vocational teaching practices and their downstream impacts on healthcare workforce readiness, this work will establish a new paradigm for data-driven teacher development in critical health professions education. The requested HPC resources will directly support the creation of open-access pedagogical tools designed to enhance instructional quality across accredited health occupations programs nationwide.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational health occupations programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for neuromusculoskeletal disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex biomechanical, physiological, and clinical interactions. Current rehabilitation protocols often rely on population-level data, which inadequately address individual variability in injury etiology, comorbidities, and recovery trajectories. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific data—including motion capture, electromyography, medical imaging, and electronic health records—to simulate rehabilitation outcomes under diverse therapeutic conditions. The core computational challenge involves multi-scale modeling of neuromuscular activation patterns, tissue healing dynamics, and biomechanical load redistribution during rehabilitation exercises. HPC resources are critical for running iterative, high-fidelity finite element analyses and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms to identify patient-specific intervention parameters. These simulations will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 200 patients with spinal cord injuries or post-stroke motor impairments. The anticipated outcomes include predictive models that quantify the impact of rehabilitation variables (e.g., exercise intensity, assistive device design) on functional recovery rates, enabling data-driven personalization of treatment plans. By elucidating mechanistic links between intervention parameters and recovery outcomes, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, improve resource allocation in rehabilitation teams, and establish computational biomarkers for monitoring progress. The resulting open-source tools will provide a scalable platform for simulating novel rehabilitation strategies, directly addressing the program’s focus on evidence-based innovation in physical medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, etiology, treatment, prevention and rehabilitation of neuromusculo-skeletal, cardiovascular, pulmonary and other system disorders common to patients of both sexes and all ages. May included related research in physical examinations, design and prescription of rehabilitation strategies and the supervision of rehabilitation teams.

abstract: The safe and effective administration of anesthesia requires precise pharmacological decision-making under dynamic physiological conditions. However, current protocols for anesthetic dosing and perioperative monitoring rely on population-level models that inadequately account for interpatient variability in drug metabolism, comorbid risk factors, and acute pathophysiological shifts. This project seeks to develop patient-specific pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models to predict individualized responses to anesthetic and analgesic agents, with the goal of reducing adverse events such as intraoperative awareness, hemodynamic instability, and postoperative delirium. Using anonymized electronic health record data from 15,000+ surgical cases, we will implement a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling of drug-receptor interactions, machine learning (ML)-driven feature extraction from multimodal physiological time-series data, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to quantify uncertainty in rare-event scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of anesthetic drug distributions across heterogeneous tissue compartments, (2) training recurrent neural networks on high-frequency vital sign waveforms (200 Hz sampling rate), and (3) real-time sensitivity analyses during model validation against prospective cases. The resulting framework will enable probabilistic forecasting of drug effects at 30-second intraoperative intervals while integrating emergent covariates such as blood loss or allergic response. Anticipated outcomes include clinically validated decision support tools for nurse anesthetists, optimized dosing algorithms for special populations (e.g., obese patients, geriatrics), and open-source simulation modules for anesthesia training programs. By addressing the computational barriers to personalized dynamic modeling in perioperative care, this work directly aligns with the program’s focus on advancing evidence-based practice through technological innovation in patient assessment and crisis management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: The management of fine and studio arts organizations faces growing challenges in balancing operational sustainability with equitable access to cultural resources. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model complex variables, such as fluctuating community needs, dynamic funding landscapes, and evolving digital engagement metrics. This project proposes the development of a computational modeling platform to optimize resource allocation strategies for galleries, museums, and arts nonprofits. By integrating high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to analyze multi-source datasets—including visitor analytics, donor behavior patterns, and spatial utilization metrics—to simulate the long-term impacts of financial, curatorial, and outreach decisions. Computational methods will combine network analysis to map stakeholder relationships, Monte Carlo simulations to forecast budget scenarios under uncertainty, and computer vision algorithms to assess the relationship between exhibition design and audience retention. The scale of these datasets, which encompass geospatial, temporal, and visual information, necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated machine learning workflows only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that enables arts administrators to visualize trade-offs between fiscal responsibility, programmatic scope, and community impact. This research advances the integration of computational social science methodologies into arts management, offering empirically grounded strategies to address systemic inequities in cultural resource distribution. Results will be disseminated through interactive workshops for arts professionals and a pilot implementation with three regional galleries, establishing a replicable model for data-informed stewardship in the visual arts sector.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage fine and studio art organizations, operations, and facilities. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; public relations and arts advocacy; arts law; and applications to specific arts activities such as galleries, museums, studios, foundations, and community organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the detection and classification of precancerous and malignant cellular anomalies in cytological samples, addressing critical bottlenecks in manual screening processes. Current cytotechnological methods rely heavily on labor-intensive microscopic evaluation by trained professionals, which can lead to variability in diagnostic accuracy, particularly in early-stage or borderline cases. To mitigate these challenges, we propose a machine learning-driven approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze high-resolution digitized cytology slides. The research will focus on creating deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs), trained on multi-institutional datasets of cervical, thyroid, and urinary tract cytology samples. These models will be optimized to identify subtle cellular and nuclear features—such as hyperchromasia, chromatin patterns, and nuclear membrane irregularities—that correlate with dysplastic or malignant transformations. Computational workflows will include preprocessing pipelines for stain normalization and artifact removal, followed by multi-scale feature extraction and ensemble classification. HPC resources are essential to manage the terabyte-scale image datasets, accelerate model training through parallelized GPU computing, and validate results against gold-standard pathologist annotations. Successfully validating these models is expected to yield three outcomes: (1) a reproducible open-source tool for augmenting cytotechnologists’ workflow by prioritizing high-risk cases, (2) quantitative benchmarks linking computational predictions to diagnostic confidence metrics, and (3) insights into understudied morphological precursors of malignancy. By integrating computational pathology with traditional cytotechnology, this work aims to reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve inter-observer consistency, and ultimately support earlier intervention for patients with neoplastic diseases. The scalability of the proposed methods will also provide a foundation for adapting the framework to other cytological subfields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with pathologists to detect changes in body cells that may indicate, and permit diagnosis of, the early development of cancers and other diseases. Includes instruction in biochemistry, microbiology, applied mathematics, microscopy, slide preparation, identification of cellular structures and abnormalities, and laboratory procedures and safety.

abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is a critical intervention for conditions such as non-healing wounds, radiation injury, and decompression sickness. However, current treatment protocols rely on generalized pressure and oxygenation parameters, which may not account for individual patient variability in tissue perfusion, metabolic demand, or gas diffusion dynamics. This project seeks to address the lack of personalized HBOT regimens by developing a computational framework to model oxygen transport and tissue response under hyperbaric conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale physiological interactions—from systemic circulation to cellular metabolism—under varying hyperbaric exposures. A hybrid approach integrating fluid dynamics simulations, finite element analysis, and machine learning will be employed. Fluid dynamics models will predict oxygen distribution in heterogeneous tissues, while patient-specific data (e.g., vascular geometry, hemoglobin levels, and mitochondrial density) will refine simulations. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data will identify patterns linking treatment parameters to clinical outcomes. These models will be iteratively validated against experimental data from hyperbaric chamber trials measuring tissue oxygenation and biomarker responses. The anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms to optimize pressure-duration-oxygen concentration profiles for individual patients and pathological contexts. This work will establish a foundational platform for precision hyperbaric medicine, potentially reducing treatment times, mitigating adverse effects such as oxygen toxicity, and improving recovery rates. By bridging computational biophysics, clinical data science, and hyperbaric technology, the project advances an emerging niche in therapeutic optimization, offering a template for integrating HPC-driven modeling into procedural medicine. The resulting tools and datasets will be shared via open-access repositories to accelerate innovation in understudied areas of hyperbaric research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to operate hyperbaric (recompression) chambers for the treatment of disease. Includes instruction in patient assessment and management, hyperbaric safety, physics of hyperbaric and hypobaric exposures, physiology, hyperbaric chamber operation, and air decompression procedures.

abstract: Aerospace medicine faces critical challenges in understanding and mitigating the health risks posed by extreme physiological and psychological stressors in air and space environments. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to predict and address these risks, with a focus on optimizing medical protocols for crew health during long-duration missions. The primary research problem involves the dynamic interplay of microgravity, rapid pressure changes, and high-G forces on human physiology, particularly their cumulative effects on cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, and neurovestibular systems. Current clinical datasets lack resolution to capture real-time adaptive responses during critical mission phases, necessitating advanced simulation approaches. The proposed work will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-scale biomechanical models integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cerebral and cardiovascular responses, finite element analysis (FEA) for bone density loss under microgravity, and machine learning algorithms trained on astronaut biometric datasets. These models will simulate emergency scenarios such as rapid decompression events and sustained hypergravity during re-entry, predicting physiological thresholds for medical intervention. A parallel computational framework will evaluate the efficacy of artificial gravity countermeasures and pharmacological protocols through in silico clinical trials. The anticipated outcomes include predictive analytics tools for decompression sickness risk stratification, optimized exercise regimens for muscle atrophy prevention, and adaptive medical decision-support systems for deep-space missions. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process terabytes of multimodal physiological data from existing spaceflight studies, this research aims to establish evidence-based standards for aerospace medical operations while reducing reliance on Earth-based analog experiments. The computational infrastructure will enable near real-time simulation of crewed mission profiles, significantly advancing the field's capacity to safeguard human health in next-generation space exploration initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on the health care of operating crews, support personnel, and passengers of air and space vehicles. Includes instruction in special conditions of physical and psychological stress, emergency medical procedures, adaptive systems and artificial environments. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize personalized anesthetic dosing protocols using high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific responses to anesthetic agents. Current protocols rely on population-level averages, leading to variability in drug efficacy and adverse events such as intraoperative awareness or hemodynamic instability. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, machine learning, and multi-omic data analysis. The research will leverage anonymized electronic health records, genomic data, and intraoperative physiological monitoring datasets from a cohort of 2,500 patients undergoing diverse surgical procedures. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelized simulations of drug distribution and metabolism across virtual patient populations, accounting for genetic polymorphisms in drug-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYP2B6, pseudocholinesterase), body composition metrics, and comorbidities. Machine learning models will be trained to predict individualized dose-response curves and adverse event risks, with validation against clinical outcomes. The computational pipeline will also incorporate real-time optimization algorithms to guide dynamic dosing adjustments during simulated surgical scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for precision anesthetic administration, reducing postoperative complications by an estimated 15-20% in pilot data. This work aligns with the growing emphasis on personalized perioperative care in nurse anesthesia practice, offering a scalable method to enhance patient safety and recovery trajectories. By elucidating genotype-phenotype interactions in anesthetic response, the project will further contribute foundational knowledge to nursing science regarding biological determinants of interpatient variability. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the computational burden of multi-parametric modeling and achieving clinically actionable processing speeds for complex datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: Beekeeping faces critical challenges from environmental stressors, pathogens, and management practices that threaten colony health and agricultural pollination. This project seeks to develop predictive models of honey bee colony dynamics to identify intervention strategies that enhance resilience and productivity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate multi-scale datasets—including hive sensor metrics (temperature, humidity, brood patterns), genomic profiles of Varroa mite resistance, and regional pesticide exposure maps—into an agent-based simulation framework. This framework will model individual bee behavior, colony-level resource allocation, and pathogen transmission under varying environmental and management scenarios. Key computational challenges include parameterizing interactions between 10,000+ agents, optimizing differential equations for disease spread, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations across diverse climatic conditions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of these stochastic models, reducing runtime from months to days. Expected outcomes include identifying hive management practices that mitigate Varroa destructor infestations, optimizing queen-rearing schedules to align with floral resource availability, and predicting colony survival rates under pesticide exposure gradients. The models will be validated against longitudinal field data from 200 apiaries across three agroecological zones. By quantifying trade-offs between honey production, pollination efficiency, and colony health, this work will provide evidence-based guidelines for adaptive beekeeping protocols. The resulting open-source tools will empower apiculturists to simulate management decisions in silico, reducing costly trial-and-error approaches. This project directly addresses the agricultural sector’s need for data-driven strategies to sustain pollinator populations, which underpin $15 billion annually in U.S. crop production.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on improving the beekeeping industry, promoting pollination of fruits and vegetables, and bee colony expansion and maintenance. Includes instruction in apiary behavior, apiary equipment and supplies, beekeeping, bee pests and parasites, handling bees, hive set up and care, queen rearing, and seasonal management practices.

abstract: The development of advanced ceramic materials with tailored properties requires a comprehensive understanding of atomic-scale processes, microstructural evolution, and defect dynamics under thermomechanical and chemical stressors. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve these phenomena across relevant length and time scales, particularly for complex systems such as ceramic superconductors or high-entropy abrasives. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multi-scale simulations of ceramic synthesis, degradation mechanisms, and performance optimization. Using molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT), we will model atomic interactions during sintering processes, interfacial reactions in composite ceramics, and crack propagation under extreme thermal gradients. Mesoscale phase-field methods will simulate microstructural evolution in polycrystalline systems, while machine learning models trained on simulation data will predict optimal processing parameters for defect minimization. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated codes (e.g., LAMMPS, Quantum ESPRESSO) to handle systems exceeding 10^6 atoms and long-timescale reactive events via enhanced sampling techniques. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into pore coalescence during sintering, interfacial stability in ceramic-metal composites, and phase transformation kinetics in zirconia-based thermal barrier coatings. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation ceramics with enhanced fracture toughness, thermal stability, and wear resistance for energy storage and high-temperature applications. The generated datasets and validated force fields will be disseminated to the ceramic engineering community, establishing a computational framework to accelerate materials discovery. By integrating HPC-driven simulations with experimental validation, this work addresses critical gaps in processing-structure-property relationships for non-metallic inorganic materials, advancing the foundational knowledge required to meet industrial demands for sustainable, high-performance ceramics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of inorganic non-metallic materials, such as porcelains, cements, industrial ceramics, ceramic superconductors, abrasive, and related materials and systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for non-profit and public organizations operating in dynamic, resource-constrained environments. Non-profit entities face unique challenges in balancing mission-driven priorities with operational efficiency, particularly under fluctuating funding, shifting policy landscapes, and complex stakeholder demands. Existing decision-support tools often lack the capacity to model multi-objective trade-offs at scale or incorporate real-time data on donor behavior, community needs, and regulatory constraints. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale agent-based simulations and stochastic optimization models. These computational methods will simulate diverse organizational scenarios—including funding volatility, program scalability, and workforce constraints—while integrating machine learning techniques to predict donor retention rates and community impact metrics. The project will extend established operations research frameworks by embedding ethical and equity considerations as computational constraints, enabling non-profits to evaluate allocation strategies through both efficiency and social justice lenses. By parallelizing thousands of scenario iterations across HPC nodes, we aim to identify robust decision policies that maintain organizational resilience across uncertainty ranges exceeding conventional modeling capabilities. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive resource allocation, validated through case studies with partner organizations in education and public health sectors. This work will advance computational social science methodologies while providing practical decision-support infrastructure for mission-driven organizations. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space and real-world data integration required to capture the complexity of non-profit management ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the business affairs of non-profit corporations, including foundations, educational institutions, associations, and other such organizations, and public agencies and governmental operations. Includes instruction in business management, principles of public administration, principles of accounting and financial management, human resources management, taxation of non-profit organizations, and business law as applied to non-profit organizations.

abstract: The efficient allocation of healthcare resources remains a critical challenge in health services administration, particularly as systems face evolving demands from population health trends, emergent public health crises, and disparities in care access. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for regional healthcare networks, with a focus on balancing cost, equity, and clinical outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models simulating patient care pathways, facility workflows, and resource utilization patterns under diverse demographic and crisis scenarios (e.g., pandemic surges, rural service gaps). These models will integrate real-world data from electronic health records, insurance claims, and public health datasets to parameterize multi-objective optimization algorithms. Key computational challenges include managing large-scale simulations across thousands of synthetic populations, parallelizing mixed-integer programming for resource scheduling, and applying machine learning to predict demand fluctuations. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of policy-sensitive variables—such as staffing ratios, facility capacity thresholds, and telehealth adoption rates—while quantifying trade-offs between competing priorities. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide administrators in preemptively redistricting service areas, dynamically scaling emergency response capacity, and minimizing care delays for high-risk populations. By open-sourcing validated model components, this work aims to establish a reproducible platform for evaluating equity-focused allocation policies, directly supporting the program's emphasis on evidence-based health systems management. The computational infrastructure developed will also serve as a template for scaling similar analyses to national or global health systems, enhancing decision-making in both public and private sector contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of policy analysis, public administration, business management, and communications to the planning and management of health services delivery systems in the public and private sectors, and prepares individuals to function as health services administrators and managers. Includes instruction in health systems planning, public health organization and management, pubic health policy formulation and analysis, finance, business and operations management, economics of health care, organizational and health communications, marketing, human resources management, and public health law and regulations.

abstract: Ophthalmic diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, and glaucoma represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss globally. Early diagnosis and personalized treatment planning are hindered by the complexity of ocular imaging data, variability in disease progression, and limitations in conventional analytical methods. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing advanced computational models to analyze multimodal ophthalmic imaging data and simulate disease mechanisms, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets and computationally intensive workflows. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) training deep learning architectures to automate the detection of pathological features in optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fundus imaging datasets, (2) integrating generative AI models to synthesize synthetic ocular images for augmenting limited clinical datasets, and (3) employing biomechanical simulations to model intraocular pressure dynamics in glaucoma and their impact on optic nerve integrity. These efforts will utilize HPC clusters to process over 50,000 high-resolution images, optimize three-dimensional convolutional neural networks, and run parallelized finite element simulations of ocular tissues. The computational pipeline will be validated against multi-institutional clinical data to ensure generalizability across diverse patient populations. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of open-source tools for automated lesion quantification, predictive biomarkers for disease progression, and mechanistic insights into pressure-induced retinal ganglion cell loss. By enabling rapid, large-scale analysis of heterogeneous data, this project aims to advance precision medicine in ophthalmology, reduce diagnostic delays, and inform the development of targeted therapies. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory and processing limitations inherent in local workstations, ensuring scalable, reproducible, and clinically translatable results.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders, and ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in eye surgery.

abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens represents a critical threat to global public health, necessitating novel approaches to understand resistance mechanisms and identify therapeutic vulnerabilities. This project seeks to investigate the structural and functional dynamics of bacterial efflux pumps—key drivers of antibiotic resistance—in clinically relevant Gram-negative pathogens, including *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* and *Acinetobacter baumannii*. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve the real-time conformational changes of these membrane protein complexes, which are essential for substrate binding and transport. To address this gap, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model efflux pump behavior under varying physiological conditions, including antibiotic exposure and membrane stress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to perform microsecond-to-millisecond timescale simulations across multiple replicates, leveraging GPU-accelerated workflows for enhanced sampling and all-atom resolution. These simulations will integrate experimentally derived parameters, such as lipid bilayer composition and ion gradients, to improve biological fidelity. Concurrently, we will apply machine learning-driven analysis to identify conserved structural motifs and transient binding pockets that could serve as targets for efflux pump inhibitors. The computational pipeline will be validated using existing cryo-EM structures and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) data from clinical isolates. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic models of efflux pump activation cycles, (2) predictive maps of inhibitor binding sites, and (3) a publicly accessible database of simulation trajectories annotated with phenotypic resistance data. By elucidating mechanistic links between efflux pump dynamics and resistance phenotypes, this work will directly inform the design of next-generation antimicrobial adjuvants. The requested HPC allocation will enable the first comprehensive computational exploration of efflux-mediated resistance at biologically relevant timescales, bridging critical gaps between structural biology and clinical bacteriology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of pathogenic bacteria that are significant factors in causing or facilitating human disease. Includes instruction in the pathogenesis of bacterial diseases, bacterial genetics and physiology, bacterial anatomy and structure, antigens, bacterial reproduction, bacterial adhesion, phagocytes, and the identification of new or mutated bacteria and bacterial agents.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize individualized educational strategies for junior high/middle school students in special education programs. A critical challenge in this domain is the dynamic, multifaceted nature of student needs, which requires educators to balance diverse factors—including cognitive abilities, behavioral patterns, and curriculum standards—when designing personalized learning plans. Traditional methods often rely on qualitative assessments and static heuristics, limiting scalability and real-time adaptability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model student learning trajectories, simulate instructional interventions, and identify data-driven strategies tailored to individual profiles. The project will integrate anonymized student datasets (e.g., academic performance records, individualized education program [IEP] benchmarks, and behavioral logs) with machine learning techniques to train predictive models that correlate specific teaching methods with learning outcomes. Computational simulations will test hypothetical classroom scenarios, evaluating how variations in curriculum pacing, assistive technologies, and multisensory instructional approaches impact student engagement and skill acquisition. By parallelizing these simulations across HPC clusters, we aim to rapidly explore high-dimensional parameter spaces and derive actionable insights for educators. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating adaptive IEP recommendations, validated through collaboration with practicing special education teachers. This work will advance the precision of middle school special education practices by enabling computationally informed decision-making, reducing trial-and-error in classroom strategies, and fostering equitable outcomes for neurodiverse learners. The scalability of this approach also lays groundwork for future studies on AI-assisted pedagogy in K–12 special education contexts.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Junior High/ Middle School Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in junior high/middle school. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for middle school special education; and principles of middle school instruction in specific subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the precision and efficiency of postmortem tissue analysis in forensic and clinical pathology through automated histomorphometric feature extraction and machine learning-driven pattern recognition. Pathologist Assistants (PAs) routinely process complex tissue specimens for diagnostic evaluation, yet current workflows rely heavily on manual microscopic assessment, which is time-intensive and subject to interobserver variability. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating scalable tools to quantify subtle morphological patterns in digitized histopathology slides, particularly in cases of ambiguous cause-of-death determination or early-stage disease. The computational approach integrates high-throughput image analysis pipelines with deep learning models (e.g., convolutional neural networks) trained on annotated datasets of postmortem tissues from diverse etiologies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale whole-slide imaging data, optimization of three-dimensional reconstructions from serial tissue sections, and parallelized model training to detect microarchitectural anomalies predictive of specific pathologies. Methods include validation against gold-standard autopsy reports and clinical histories, with iterative feedback from practicing PAs to ensure clinical relevance. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated tissue classification, anomaly detection algorithms optimized for postmortem artifacts, and quantitative biomarkers linking morphological signatures to molecular autopsy findings. This work aims to augment PA decision-making in complex cases, reduce diagnostic turnaround times, and establish a foundation for data-driven forensic pathology. The HPC infrastructure is critical given the computational demands of multi-scale image analysis and the need for robust generalizability across heterogeneous tissue types and staining protocols. Successful implementation could transform autopsy workflows while advancing the integration of computational pathology into PA education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational challenges of modeling and optimizing decentralized financial ecosystems (DeFi) under dynamically shifting regulatory and market conditions. Traditional financial systems rely on centralized intermediaries, but the rapid growth of blockchain-based DeFi platforms introduces novel complexities, including multi-layered smart contract interactions, cross-chain liquidity flows, and emergent systemic risks. Current analytical frameworks struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback loops between protocol design, user behavior, and regulatory interventions at scale. The project proposes developing an adaptive simulation environment leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model DeFi networks as complex adaptive systems. Agent-based modeling techniques will simulate heterogeneous actors (liquidity providers, arbitrage bots, regulators) across multiple blockchain layers, while graph neural networks will analyze contagion risks in real-time transaction networks. Monte Carlo methods will stress-test protocol parameterizations against regulatory scenarios, including sudden compliance rule changes or black swan market events. The computational workload requires parallelized execution across GPU clusters for near-real-time simulation of month-long market periods at sub-block time resolution. Expected outcomes include: 1) A dynamic risk-scoring framework for cross-protocol exposures, 2) Evolutionary algorithms for automated compliance rule optimization, and 3) Predictive metrics for liquidity fragmentation thresholds in multi-chain environments. By enabling high-resolution analysis of decentralized financial infrastructures, this research aims to provide actionable insights for designing resilient DeFi architectures while informing adaptive regulatory approaches. The requested HPC resources are critical for maintaining simulation fidelity across the target scale of 10^6 autonomous agents interacting through 100+ simulated protocols—a computational complexity exceeding conventional cloud infrastructure capabilities.
cip_title: Finance and Financial Management Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in financial management and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of global film style evolution and its sociocultural implications across the 20th and 21st centuries. While traditional film studies methodologies have relied on qualitative close readings of select works, the scale of digitized archival material—including over 50,000 publicly available films, production documents, and paratextual sources—now enables large-scale quantitative inquiry. However, processing this data poses significant technical challenges: multimodal analysis of audiovisual content requires computationally intensive tasks such as frame-level feature extraction, shot-boundary detection, and dynamic narrative pattern recognition across heterogeneous datasets. The research will develop and deploy custom machine learning pipelines to analyze visual style (e.g., lighting, composition, editing rhythms), auditory patterns (dialogue density, sound design), and narrative structures at scale. Computational models will be trained to identify stylistic signatures across genres, national cinemas, and historical periods, while graph-based network analyses will map the diffusion of techniques through production networks and cultural exchanges. A key innovation involves simulating hypothetical "style trajectories" using generative adversarial networks (GANs) to model counterfactual historical developments in film form, informed by sociopolitical metadata. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks for vision tasks and distributed computing for cross-regional comparative analyses. Outcomes will include the first longitudinal dataset tracking cinematic technique adoption rates, interactive visualizations of style networks, and new theoretical models linking technological change to aesthetic innovation. By bridging computational methods with media historiography, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of cultural globalization while establishing scalable technical workflows for digital humanities research. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing petabytes of audiovisual data and training complex multimodal models that cannot feasibly run on local infrastructure.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program in the visual arts that focuses on the study of the history, development, theory, and criticism of the film/media arts, as well as the basic principles of filmmaking and film production.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for the analysis of Slovak dialectal variation, a phenomenon increasingly threatened by linguistic homogenization. Traditional methods, limited in scale and granularity, have struggled to systematically document and model the phonetic, lexical, and syntactic diversity across Slovakia’s regional dialects. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), this study will process and analyze a corpus comprising over 10,000 hours of spoken dialect recordings and corresponding textual transcripts, spanning six major dialect groups. Computational workflows will integrate speech-to-text conversion, machine learning-based phonetic feature extraction, and geospatial clustering algorithms to map linguistic features across geographic and sociocultural contexts. The HPC environment is essential for handling the dataset’s size (≈50 TB), parallelizing feature extraction across thousands of audio files, and training neural networks for dialect classification. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated Slovak dialect data, interactive visualization tools for dialect boundaries, and quantitative models correlating linguistic variation with historical migration patterns. By enabling large-scale, data-driven approaches to Slovak philology, this project aims to preserve endangered linguistic heritage while advancing methodologies for digital dialectology in under-resourced languages. Resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multilingual corpora, and high-throughput processing of audio-text alignments.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Slovak language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized therapeutic exercise protocols for patients with mobility impairments due to neurological or musculoskeletal conditions. Current rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual variability in biomechanics, physiology, and pathology. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create patient-specific simulations that model the biomechanical and physiological effects of therapeutic exercises. The research problem centers on identifying how individualized parameters—such as joint kinematics, muscle activation patterns, and tissue load distribution—interact during rehabilitation, and how these factors influence functional recovery outcomes. The computational approach integrates musculoskeletal modeling, machine learning, and dynamic simulations to predict optimal exercise intensity, duration, and modality for diverse patient profiles. Multiscale models will simulate neuromuscular responses to therapeutic movements using open-source biomechanics software (e.g., OpenSim), while machine learning algorithms will analyze clinical datasets (e.g., gait analysis, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes) to identify predictive biomarkers of rehabilitation success. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across large patient cohorts and high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool to guide kinesiotherapists in designing adaptive, evidence-based interventions for conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injury, and osteoarthritis. This work will advance precision rehabilitation by bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational biomechanics, potentially reducing trial-and-error in therapy design and improving patient adherence. The resulting open-access models and datasets will serve as a resource for interdisciplinary research in rehabilitation science, motor control, and assistive technology development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the direction of physicians, to treat the effects of disease, injury, and congenital disorders through therapeutic exercise and education. Includes instruction in human anatomy, human physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, therapeutic exercise and adapted physical education, human growth and development, motor learning and performance, testing and measurement, first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, psychology, rehabilitation procedures, patient assessment and management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize grooming protocols for domestic animals by modeling the biomechanical and physiological interactions between grooming tools, animal anatomy, and coat characteristics. Current grooming practices rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for individual variations in species, breed-specific skin elasticity, fur density, or stress responses. The lack of data-driven, personalized protocols can lead to suboptimal outcomes, including skin irritation, incomplete coat maintenance, or undue animal stress. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate grooming processes across a diverse array of biological and tool-based parameters. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model tool-skin interactions under varying pressure, motion, and temperature conditions, while agent-based simulations will predict stress responses in animals based on physiological metrics such as heart rate variability and thermal regulation. Machine learning algorithms will integrate empirical data from veterinary studies, groomer-reported outcomes, and sensor-derived biometrics (collected via wearable devices during grooming sessions) to generate adaptive, breed-specific grooming recommendations. The computational pipeline will also evaluate the efficacy of novel grooming tool designs through virtual prototyping, reducing reliance on iterative physical testing. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of simulated grooming scenarios, predictive models for stress-minimized workflows, and evidence-based guidelines for tool selection and maintenance. By bridging computational biomechanics, ethology, and cosmetology, this work aims to advance animal welfare standards while supporting innovation in a historically practice-driven industry. The scale of multi-parametric simulations and real-time data assimilation necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve the resolution required for actionable insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework for generating real-time, patient-specific 3D anatomical visualizations to enhance surgical planning and medical education. Current medical illustration workflows rely on pre-rendered models or generic datasets, limiting their adaptability to individual patient anatomy and dynamic clinical scenarios. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution medical imaging data (e.g., CT, MRI) into interactive, deformable 3D models that can simulate tissue behavior and pathological variations. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize segmentation, mesh generation, and biomechanical simulation tasks across GPU-accelerated nodes. The computational pipeline will integrate deep learning architectures for automated feature extraction from imaging data with finite element analysis to model soft tissue dynamics. A key innovation involves developing adaptive resolution algorithms that balance model fidelity with rendering speed, enabling clinicians to manipulate complex anatomical structures in virtual reality (VR) environments with sub-millisecond latency. The project will validate outputs against intraoperative data from collaborating neurosurgeons and anatomists, assessing geometric accuracy and biomechanical predictive value. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating patient-specific surgical simulations and a novel dataset linking imaging features to tissue deformation patterns. This work bridges gaps between computational biomechanics, medical imaging, and interactive visualization, offering translational potential for personalized surgical training platforms and intraoperative augmented reality systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling datasets exceeding 100GB per patient case and achieving the iterative processing speeds required for clinical usability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles and techniques of art and computer-assisted imaging, graphics, and animation to create visual materials to facilitate the recording and dissemination of biomedical knowledge for educational, research, and clinical purposes. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, histology, embryology, neuroanatomy, medical terminology, artistic media and techniques, illustration techniques, three-dimensional modeling, prosthetics, data display design, exhibit design and production, medical photography, multimedia, computer graphics and animation, digital imaging, business management, production technology, and instructional design.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of neuromuscular disorders necessitates advanced methodologies to optimize rehabilitation strategies for patients undergoing physical therapy. Current clinical protocols rely on generalized biomechanical models that inadequately capture individual variability in musculoskeletal dynamics, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to design personalized therapeutic interventions by modeling patient-specific neuromuscular responses to rehabilitation exercises. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to integrate high-resolution motion capture data, electromyography (EMG), and medical imaging into multiscale biomechanical simulations that predict tissue stress distributions, motor unit recruitment patterns, and energy expenditure during task-specific movements. The computational pipeline will employ finite element analysis to simulate soft tissue deformation, coupled with agent-based modeling of motor neuron activation, to create dynamic, patient-adaptive digital twins. Machine learning techniques will be applied to iteratively refine these models using real-world clinical outcome data, enabling the identification of movement patterns that maximize functional recovery while minimizing injury risk. Challenges include managing the computational complexity of real-time feedback loops between sensor data and model parameters, which requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a deployable tool for clinicians to virtually test and compare rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual biomechanical constraints. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation science, offering a novel paradigm for precision physical therapy. Successful implementation could reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, accelerate recovery timelines, and inform the development of next-generation assistive devices. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the intensive memory and processing demands of multiscale simulations, enabling parameter optimization at unprecedented resolution across anatomical hierarchies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physical therapist, to implement physical therapy treatment care plans, train patients, conduct treatment interventions, use equipment, and observe and record patient progress. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, behavioral sciences, biomechanics, clinical documentation, clinical pathology, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize the electrochemical interactions underlying modern electrology treatments, with the goal of improving treatment efficacy, safety, and accessibility. Despite advances in electrolysis technology, practitioners lack evidence-based guidelines for selecting electrical parameters (e.g., current intensity, pulse duration, probe geometry) tailored to diverse biological tissues and patient-specific factors. Current protocols rely on heuristic adjustments, risking suboptimal outcomes such as incomplete hair removal, tissue damage, or prolonged recovery. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model electrochemical dynamics during probe-tissue interactions. The computational framework integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for localized current distribution and Joule heating effects with agent-based models of follicular response to thermal and electrochemical stressors. Machine learning techniques will be applied to correlate simulated outcomes with clinical datasets, enabling predictive optimization of treatment parameters across skin types, hair densities, and anatomical regions. The HPC environment is critical for resolving the spatiotemporal complexity of coupled electrical-thermal-biological processes, which involve microsecond-scale electrical pulses interacting with millimeter-scale tissue structures over treatment durations of minutes. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models quantifying the relationships between electrical settings, tissue damage thresholds, and clinical efficacy, (2) an open-access parameter optimization toolkit for practitioners, and (3) foundational data for developing adaptive electrotherapy systems capable of real-time feedback. By bridging computational electrochemistry and clinical electrology, this work aims to establish a quantitative paradigm for personalized hair removal therapies while reducing the trial-and-error burden on practitioners and patients. The computational infrastructure will additionally support virtual training environments for electrolysis students, enhancing educational access in this specialized healthcare field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to permanently remove hair from the human scalp, face, and body using specialized charged solid needle probes, and to function as licensed electrologists and electrolysis technicians.  Includes instruction in direct current electrolysis, alternating current/high frequency thermolysis, blend/dual modality treatments, equipment theory and operation, safety and sanitation, client evaluation and care, laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Medical Family Therapy (MedFT) by modeling the dynamic interplay of biopsychosocial-spiritual factors influencing family resilience during chronic illness management. Families navigating chronic illnesses face complex, interdependent challenges that span emotional, relational, and systemic domains. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear, time-dependent interactions among these variables, limiting the development of tailored therapeutic interventions. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating longitudinal clinical data (e.g., therapy session transcripts, electronic health records, and patient-reported outcomes) with agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques. HPC resources will enable the creation of high-fidelity simulations of family systems, incorporating variables such as communication patterns, coping strategies, disease progression, and cultural contexts. These simulations will be calibrated using ML-driven analysis of real-world datasets to identify critical tipping points in family adaptation and maladaptation. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze therapy session transcripts to quantify emotional tone, relational alliances, and thematic shifts over time, providing empirical validation for the ABM outputs. The computational intensity of training ML models on multimodal data (text, structured clinical metrics) and running large-scale, stochastic ABM simulations necessitates distributed computing and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying families at risk of poor therapeutic outcomes, (2) actionable insights into optimal intervention timing and modalities, and (3) an open-source framework for simulating family-system dynamics in chronic illness contexts. This work will directly inform the development of evidence-based, systemic treatment protocols, advancing MedFT’s capacity to address health disparities and improve holistic care for medically complex families.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with patients and their families who are experiencing emotional, physical, relational and spiritual difficulties related to acute and chronic illnesses. Includes instruction in cultural context, ethics, family dynamics, family therapy, gender, human development, marriage counseling, psychopathology, research design and methods, sexuality, and systems thinking.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing strategies in the hospitality sector by integrating real-time, unstructured data streams—such as social media sentiment, localized event dynamics, and hyperlocal weather patterns—into predictive revenue management systems. Traditional pricing models in hospitality rely on historical occupancy rates and structured market data, often failing to adapt to rapidly shifting consumer behavior or external disruptions. This gap limits revenue potential and customer satisfaction, particularly in contexts like boutique hotels, event-based accommodations, or crisis-affected tourism markets. To address this, we propose developing a high-dimensional computational model that synthesizes natural language processing (NLP), time-series forecasting, and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to simulate pricing decisions under volatile conditions. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of real-time social media text, geospatial event data, and IoT-derived environmental inputs, training MARL agents to optimize pricing policies across diverse market scenarios. Computational workflows will include parallelized sentiment analysis pipelines, graph-based event impact simulations, and ensemble learning to quantify uncertainty in demand forecasts. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for adaptive pricing that balances profit margins with customer retention metrics, validated against historical crisis datasets (e.g., pandemic travel restrictions). The results will advance decision-support tools for niche hospitality sectors requiring rapid responsiveness to unstructured external factors, while contributing novel methods to the emerging field of computational hospitality analytics. This work necessitates HPC infrastructure due to the concurrent processing of heterogeneous data streams, the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent simulations, and the need for sub-hourly model retraining in operational deployments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in hospitality service management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The study addresses the computational challenges in analyzing under-resourced Semitic and Middle/Near Eastern languages, which exhibit complex morphological structures, dialectal diversity, and limited digital resources. Despite rich textual traditions spanning ancient inscriptions, medieval manuscripts, and modern vernaculars, computational tools for automated parsing, semantic analysis, and dialect classification remain underdeveloped, hindering large-scale comparative studies. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models for processing non-concatenative morphology in languages such as Akkadian, Classical Arabic, and Ge'ez, while analyzing contact phenomena in regional pidgins and creoles. Computational methods will include transformer-based architectures for cross-dialectal semantic role labeling, graph neural networks for modeling historical sound changes, and distributed training of multilingual embeddings across heterogeneous corpora. The research will utilize HPC capabilities to process terabytes of digitized texts—including OCR outputs from fragmentary manuscripts—and run parallelized simulations of language evolution under varying sociolinguistic constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for morphological disambiguation in Semitic languages, probabilistic models of syntactic convergence in Mesopotamian contact varieties, and annotated corpora supporting diachronic studies of grammaticalization patterns. These resources will advance philological research by enabling quantitative analysis of literary and epigraphic materials at previously infeasible scales, while contributing methodological innovations to low-resource NLP. The project directly supports interdisciplinary scholarship on language preservation, cultural heritage, and the diffusion of literary traditions across the Near East, addressing critical gaps in both computational linguistics and area studies. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with traditional philological expertise, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying non-Western language systems in the digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Middle/ Near Eastern and Semitic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages of the ancient and modern Middle/Near East, Western Asia, North Africa, and Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The study of quantum many-body systems far from equilibrium presents fundamental challenges in modern physics, with implications ranging from quantum information science to condensed matter phenomena. While analytical methods provide limited insight into complex, interacting systems out of equilibrium, numerical simulations remain computationally prohibitive for large system sizes or long time scales. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate dynamical phase transitions and thermalization processes in one- and two-dimensional quantum spin lattices. The research will employ tensor network methods, including time-dependent variational principles (TDVP) and matrix product operator (MPO) techniques, to simulate real-time evolution under tunable Hamiltonians with disorder and long-range interactions. Key objectives include characterizing the stability of many-body localized phases, quantifying entanglement growth, and identifying universal features of prethermalization in systems with approximate conservation laws. The computational workload involves iterative diagonalization, singular value decompositions at scale, and parallelized parameter sweeps across disorder realizations, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory capacity. Expected outcomes include predictive models for nonequilibrium critical behavior, validated against recent ultracold atom experiments, and optimized algorithms for simulating open quantum systems. Results will advance the understanding of how isolated quantum systems approach thermal equilibrium—a cornerstone problem in statistical mechanics—while providing open-source code frameworks to bridge numerical and experimental efforts in quantum simulation. This work directly supports the broader physics community by addressing computational bottlenecks in simulating emergent phenomena, with potential applications in error mitigation strategies for quantum computing architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and safety assessment of load-bearing structures under extreme dynamic loads, such as those induced by earthquakes, hurricanes, and blast events. Current structural engineering practices rely on simplified analytical models that often fail to capture the complex nonlinear behavior of modern composite materials, soil-structure interactions, and progressive collapse mechanisms. To address these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multiscale structural responses across varying temporal and spatial domains. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) with explicit time integration, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify critical failure modes and optimize retrofitting strategies. Key computational challenges include resolving contact dynamics in fractured materials, modeling stochastic environmental loads, and handling the high dimensionality of design parameter spaces. HPC resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations at unprecedented scales, reducing wall-clock time for ensemble analyses from months to days. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for structural resilience, open-source tools for probabilistic risk assessment, and data-driven design guidelines for next-generation infrastructure. These results will directly inform codes for disaster-resistant construction in seismic and coastal zones, with applications to bridges, high-rise buildings, and offshore energy platforms. By integrating computational mechanics with AI-driven analytics, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in structural safety while advancing the sustainable use of advanced materials in civil engineering. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated workloads, large-scale eigenvalue solvers, and distributed memory operations for terabyte-scale datasets, enabling transformative insights into structural performance under multi-hazard scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and systems used in building load-bearing structures for various purposes and in different environments, including buildings, roads, rail lines, bridges, dams, conduits, offshore platforms and work stations, and other structural shells; and the analysis of structural problems such as, failure, fabrication, safety, and natural hazards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Ukrainian linguistics, focusing on the analysis of dialectal variation and historical text corpora. While Ukrainian dialects and literary evolution have been studied through traditional philological methods, large-scale quantitative analyses remain limited due to the computational demands of processing unstructured textual data spanning diverse regions and time periods. The research problem centers on mapping phonetic, morphological, and lexical features across digitized dialect recordings (20th–21st centuries) and early modern literary texts (16th–18th centuries) to identify patterns of language change and regional influences. Computational methods will include training transformer-based models for automated morphological tagging of non-standardized orthographies, implementing phonetic alignment algorithms for speech corpora, and conducting cluster analyses of lexical distributions across geographic and temporal dimensions. The HPC environment is critical for managing the project's scale: initial datasets comprise approximately 15 TB of text and audio recordings, requiring parallel processing for feature extraction and comparative modeling. Expected outcomes include the first open-access database of annotated Ukrainian dialect features, machine learning tools optimized for historical Ukrainian texts, and quantitative models tracing the relationship between literary standardization and spoken language variants. These resources will enable novel research in Ukrainian sociolinguistics, support educational applications in language preservation, and provide methodological frameworks for under-resourced Slavic languages. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, this project aims to address gaps in digital Ukrainian studies while demonstrating how HPC capabilities can transform research paradigms in lesser-studied languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Ukrainian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for enhancing the detection and analysis of systemic risk patterns in real-time auditing processes. Traditional auditing methodologies often struggle to integrate dynamic, high-volume transactional data with contextual operational variables, leading to delayed risk identification and reactive compliance measures. The proposed work addresses this gap by constructing a multi-agent simulation environment that models complex interactions between financial transactions, regulatory constraints, and organizational behavior across decentralized supply chains. The computational approach combines graph-based anomaly detection algorithms with reinforcement learning to identify latent risk pathways and simulate audit scenarios under varying regulatory conditions. Key challenges include processing heterogeneous datasets (e.g., blockchain-ledger transactions, IoT-enabled operational logs, and unstructured compliance documents) and maintaining temporal consistency in risk assessments at enterprise scale. HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in audit outcomes while training deep learning models on historical audit findings across multiple industries. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predictive audit analytics, capable of generating probabilistic risk heatmaps and optimizing resource allocation for audit teams. The research will specifically examine applications in cross-jurisdictional cryptocurrency transactions and AI-driven financial reporting systems, areas where current auditing standards lack computational rigor. By enabling real-time, data-driven audit prioritization, this work aims to reduce compliance costs by an estimated 15–20% in pilot sectors while establishing a foundation for adaptive regulatory frameworks in emerging digital economies. The computational infrastructure developed will be scalable to public auditing entities and private firms managing multi-tiered compliance requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including certified accountants, to perform independent internal and external appraisals to evaluate organizational financial and operational activities, ensure compliance with laws and policies, safeguard assets, and promote effective planning and resource allocation. Includes instruction in advanced accounting, audit tools and techniques, sampling, risk and control, audit planning, audit function management, law and regulations, environmental auditing, information technology applications, professional standards and ethics, and specific industry and service sector problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how disruptions in cortico-basal ganglia-thalamic circuit dynamics contribute to motor and cognitive deficits in Parkinson’s disease (PD). While dopaminergic degeneration is a hallmark of PD, the mechanisms linking synaptic-level dysfunction to network-level oscillations and behavioral impairments remain poorly understood. We propose a computational approach combining biologically detailed spiking neural network models with behavioral task simulations to bridge this gap. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale networks (>100,000 neurons) incorporating dopaminergic modulation, synaptic plasticity, and inter-regional connectivity derived from primate neuroanatomical data. Models will be validated against in vivo electrophysiological recordings from PD rodent models and human behavioral datasets. Key computational challenges include parallelization of multi-timescale simulations (from millisecond spikes to hours of task performance), parameter space exploration to identify critical transition points in network stability, and machine learning-driven analysis of high-dimensional neural activity patterns. Expected outcomes include a mechanistic framework linking dopaminergic depletion to aberrant beta oscillations and decision-making deficits, with translational implications for adaptive deep brain stimulation protocols. This work directly addresses NIH priorities in computational neuroscience and neurotechnology by developing open-source tools for simulating neurodegenerative circuit pathology. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across clinically relevant conditions (e.g., dopamine levels, stimulation patterns) that are infeasible with local computing resources, significantly accelerating hypothesis testing. By integrating cellular-level mechanisms with behavioral outputs, this project advances fundamental understanding of how distributed neural circuits generate—and lose—control of motor and cognitive functions.
