cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates as it relates to control of behavior. Includes instruction in neuronal systems and circuits, higher level studies of behavior and cognition, computational neurobiology, and behavioral manifestations of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing wind energy systems through advanced computational modeling of wind turbine arrays and atmospheric interactions. Current wind farm design practices often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the complex, multi-scale fluid dynamics governing turbine wakes, terrain effects, and turbulence. These limitations hinder the development of layouts that maximize energy output while minimizing structural fatigue and maintenance costs. To overcome these barriers, we propose a coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning framework to simulate wind farm performance under realistic atmospheric conditions. The HPC workflow will integrate large-eddy simulations (LES) using open-source solvers like OpenFOAM and NREL’s SOWFA to resolve turbulent airflow at meter-scale resolution across multi-turbine arrays. Concurrently, neural networks trained on simulation data will identify patterns linking turbine placement, wind regimes, and power generation, enabling rapid optimization of farm configurations. The computational demand is substantial, requiring thousands of core-hours to resolve time-dependent flow features and validate models against field data from existing wind farms. Expected outcomes include high-fidelity predictive tools to mitigate wake losses, extend turbine lifespans, and improve energy yield by 10–15% in complex terrains. These advances will directly inform next-generation wind farm design standards and operational strategies, supporting global decarbonization goals. Additionally, the project will train students in HPC-driven renewable energy research, fostering workforce readiness in computational modeling for sustainable technology. By bridging high-resolution simulations with data-driven optimization, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for accelerating wind energy deployment in diverse geographic and climatic settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing wind-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in wind energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Sleep disorders present complex diagnostic challenges due to the multidimensional nature of polysomnographic data, which includes electroencephalographic (EEG), electrooculographic (EOG), electromyographic (EMG), and cardiorespiratory signals. Current clinical workflows rely on manual scoring of sleep stages and events, a time-intensive process prone to inter-rater variability and limited in its capacity to detect subtle physiological patterns predictive of disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy, or parasomnias. This project proposes the development of automated, high-resolution analysis pipelines leveraging machine learning (ML) and signal processing to improve the accuracy and efficiency of sleep disorder diagnostics. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on large-scale polysomnography datasets, encompassing diverse patient demographics and pathologies. Computational workflows will integrate time-frequency analysis for noise reduction, feature extraction from multichannel biosignals, and ensemble modeling to classify sleep stages and pathological events. A key innovation involves the synthesis of spatially resolved EEG dynamics with cardiorespiratory variability metrics to identify novel biomarkers of sleep disruption. HPC capabilities are critical for managing the computational load of processing terabytes of high-density physiological data, optimizing hyperparameters for convolutional and recurrent neural networks, and conducting large-scale validation across heterogeneous cohorts. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated polysomnography scoring, validated ML models with clinical interpretability, and new insights into the physiological signatures of understudied sleep disorders. By enhancing the granularity and reproducibility of sleep data analysis, this work aims to advance personalized treatment strategies, reduce diagnostic latency, and establish scalable infrastructure for translational sleep research. The requested resources will directly support iterative model training, real-time simulation of biosignal processing pipelines, and benchmarking against gold-standard clinical assessments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: Agricultural and food product processing involves complex, dynamic interactions between biological materials and processing parameters that influence final product quality, safety, and sustainability. Current challenges in optimizing these processes—such as balancing nutrient retention, microbial safety, energy efficiency, and waste reduction—require advanced computational modeling to account for multi-scale, nonlinear relationships. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multiscale simulation frameworks for agricultural processing systems, with a focus on thermal treatment, drying, and enzymatic modification of plant-based foods. We propose integrating molecular dynamics simulations to model nutrient degradation kinetics and microbial inactivation at the microstructural level, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to predict bulk heat and mass transfer during industrial-scale operations. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to optimize processing parameters across these scales while minimizing computational expense. Key datasets include hyperspectral imaging of nutrient profiles, time-resolved microbial survival data, and industrial sensor logs from pilot-scale processing equipment. The HPC environment is critical for managing large parameter spaces, parallelizing multiphysics simulations, and training neural networks on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide the design of energy-efficient processing protocols, reduce post-harvest losses, and enhance the nutritional quality of shelf-stable foods. This work will directly support the development of scalable, data-driven decision tools for agri-food industries, addressing global challenges in food security and sustainable production. By bridging molecular-level insights with system-level engineering constraints, the project advances computational methodologies unique to agricultural processing sciences, fostering innovation in a sector traditionally reliant on empirical trial-and-error approaches. Resource allocation will enable parameter sensitivity analyses, validation against experimental datasets, and the creation of open-access simulation templates for broader academic and industry use.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, inspect, store, process, and package agricultural products in the form of human food consumables, animal or plant food, or other industrial products. Includes instruction in the nutrient and industrial properties of various agricultural products; logistics and storage procedures; chemical and mechanical processing operations; packaging; safety and health requirements; and related technical and business principles.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory management in multi-location restaurant franchises, a critical yet underexplored challenge at the intersection of food services operations, computational economics, and real-time data analytics. Traditional pricing and inventory models fail to account for the hyper-localized variability in demand drivers—such as seasonal tourism patterns, regional supply chain disruptions, and localized competitor activity—that impact perishable food inventory across geographically dispersed franchises. The project proposes a novel computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate spatially distributed consumer behavior, supplier networks, and cross-location inventory transfers. By deploying parallelized simulations across HPC clusters, the model will iteratively optimize pricing and redistribution strategies for perishable goods under constraints including shelf life, transportation costs, and franchise-specific profit-sharing agreements. The computational workflow will process real-time sales data, weather forecasts, and social media sentiment metrics to dynamically adjust parameters, requiring distributed memory architectures for low-latency updates across thousands of simulated franchise nodes. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of reducing food waste by 12–18% and improving margin resilience during supply shocks, as validated against historical data from a participating franchise network. This work advances computational methods in food services by formalizing the interdependencies between micro-localized demand signals and macro-scale inventory logistics, offering a transferable paradigm for perishable goods industries. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the granularity, speed, and parallelization required for both training RL policies and operationalizing real-time recommendations across complex, multi-stakeholder systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market restaurants, food services in hospitality establishments, food service chains and franchise networks, and restaurant supply operations. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, food services management, wholesale logistics and distribution, franchise operations, business networking, personnel management, culinary arts, business planning and capitalization, food industry operations, marketing and retailing, business law and regulations, finance, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) methodologies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve critical bottlenecks in processing, analyzing, and modeling multidimensional spatial-temporal data for security and intelligence applications. Current GEOINT workflows struggle to integrate real-time, heterogeneous datasets—including satellite imagery, social media geotags, and sensor networks—at scales necessary to predict emergent threats or model complex human-environment interactions. Traditional tools lack the computational capacity to handle the volume, velocity, and variety of modern geospatial data, limiting their utility for proactive decision-making. To address this gap, the research will develop a scalable computational framework combining machine learning, spatial statistics, and agent-based modeling (ABM) optimized for parallelized HPC environments. The framework will be tested on two use cases: (1) simulating population displacement patterns during geopolitical crises using fused satellite imagery and open-source intelligence (OSINT), and (2) identifying anomalous activity in urban environments by correlating real-time sensor data with historical movement patterns. Key computational challenges include optimizing raster/vector data fusion for GPU architectures, reducing latency in streaming data ingestion, and implementing spatially explicit ABMs at metropolitan scales. Outcomes will include open-source algorithms for geospatial data parallelism, validated predictive models for threat detection, and benchmarks for HPC resource allocation in GEOINT applications. By enhancing the speed and accuracy of large-scale geospatial analysis, this work aims to provide intelligence analysts with actionable insights into dynamic security landscapes while establishing computational best practices for emerging GEOINT research domains. The project’s interdisciplinary approach bridges technical gaps between geographic information science, data-intensive computing, and security studies, offering a template for resource-efficient innovation in non-traSTEM fields reliant on spatial reasoning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to analyze security and intelligence problems using a geographic perspective by relating human actions to cultural, political, economic, social, and physical landscapes. Includes instruction in aerial photography analysis, cartography, geographic information systems (GIS), physical geography, remote sensing, spatial programming, and quantitative methods in geographic research.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive maintenance strategies for complex mechanical systems through high-fidelity computational modeling, addressing a critical gap in current diagnostic methodologies that rely on reactive or rule-based approaches. Traditional repair and maintenance frameworks often fail to account for dynamic operational stresses, environmental variability, and material degradation interactions, leading to unplanned downtime and costly inefficiencies in industries reliant on specialized machinery. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-physics simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model wear patterns, fatigue behavior, and failure modes in heterogeneous mechanical assemblies. The computational approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution mapping, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and fluid interaction modeling, and machine learning algorithms trained on synthetic failure datasets generated through parameterized simulations. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the project will enable real-time sensitivity analyses of component interactions under diverse operating conditions, including extreme temperature gradients and variable load cycles. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework capable of identifying subcritical failure signatures with 85-90% accuracy across simulated scenarios, validated against empirical data from industrial partners. The resulting models will inform optimized maintenance schedules and repair protocols while reducing computational expense through adaptive meshing techniques. This work directly supports workforce development in emerging repair technologies by providing open-source simulation tools for training technicians in failure analysis and system diagnostics. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling simulations to industrial-grade mechanical systems, as single-node computing cannot accommodate the memory and processing demands of multi-scale, coupled physics models. Successful implementation will bridge a critical gap between computational mechanics and applied repair technologies, fostering innovation in sustainable equipment lifecycle management.
cip_title: Mechanic and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanic and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced graphic design workflows, particularly in the creation of high-fidelity, interactive, and generative visual media. Current design tools struggle to efficiently process real-time rendering of complex 3D environments, AI-driven generative asset creation, and large-scale dynamic simulations—tasks critical to pushing the boundaries of digital art, user experience design, and immersive media. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test novel computational pipelines that integrate machine learning models, physics-based simulations, and parallelized rendering techniques. Key objectives include optimizing neural networks for style transfer at scale, accelerating fluid dynamics simulations for procedural animation, and enabling multi-user collaborative design in virtual reality environments with low-latency rendering. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated frameworks for training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on terabyte-scale visual datasets, distributed computing for real-time iteration on 4K/8K multimedia projects, and cloud-based rendering farms for iterative design validation. Expected outcomes include new methodologies for computationally intensive design processes, open-source tools to democratize access to advanced rendering capabilities, and case studies demonstrating HPC-enabled workflows in commercial design applications. By bridging gaps between artistic intent and technical feasibility, this research aims to expand creative possibilities in data-driven visual storytelling, interactive installations, and adaptive branding systems while establishing best practices for computational resource allocation in design education and practice. The project’s findings will directly benefit visual arts curricula, industry partnerships, and interdisciplinary research at the intersection of aesthetic innovation and computational scalability.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic and computer techniques to the interpretation of technical and commercial concepts. Includes instruction in computer-assisted art and design, printmaking, concepts sketching, technical drawing, color theory, imaging, studio technique, still and life modeling, multimedia applications, communication skills and commercial art business operations.

abstract: The increasing frequency of extreme weather events under climate change highlights critical gaps in understanding multiscale interactions between atmospheric and oceanic processes. Traditional models often treat these systems separately or use coarse parameterizations, limiting predictive accuracy for high-impact phenomena such as tropical cyclones and marine heatwaves. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a novel coupled modeling framework that integrates stochastic mathematics, high-resolution ocean-atmosphere dynamics, and machine learning-driven parameterizations. The research will employ advanced numerical methods to capture nonlinear feedback mechanisms across spatial and temporal scales, with a focus on improving the representation of boundary layer processes and mesoscale eddy interactions. High-performance computing resources are essential to conduct large-scale ensemble simulations, enabling probabilistic assessments of extreme event formation under varying climate scenarios. Key computational challenges include solving coupled partial differential equations with adaptive grid refinement, assimilating heterogeneous observational datasets, and training neural networks to predict subgrid-scale fluxes. The expected outcomes include a validated open-source model capable of simulating compound extreme events with unprecedented resolution, new insights into the role of ocean stratification in modulating storm intensification, and scalable algorithms for uncertainty quantification in Earth system models. By uniting applied mathematics, fluid dynamics, and climate science, this work will provide actionable data for coastal resilience planning while advancing foundational knowledge about cross-scale interactions in the climate system.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to atmospheric and oceanic problems. Includes instruction in chemistry, physics, atmospheric/ocean dynamics, climatology, weather simulation, climate modeling, mathematics, oceanography, and atmospheric science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance decision-support frameworks for next-generation military command, control, and intelligence operations. Modern multi-domain operations generate vast, heterogeneous data streams—from satellite imagery and sensor telemetry to unstructured human-generated reports—that challenge traditional analytical workflows. Current systems struggle to integrate these datasets in real time while accounting for adversarial deception tactics, resource constraints, and rapidly evolving mission parameters. To address this gap, we propose developing an adaptive computational architecture combining agent-based modeling, graph-based anomaly detection, and reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate contested information environments and optimize decision pathways. The project will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to model probabilistic outcomes of command choices under varying threat scenarios, while transformer-based natural language processing will automate the extraction of tacit insights from unstructured intelligence documents. A key innovation involves coupling these components through a dynamic knowledge graph that updates in near real time, enabling HPC-powered scenario testing to identify vulnerabilities in proposed strategies before deployment. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for simulating multi-echelon command decisions under asymmetric information conditions, (2) quantifiable metrics for assessing the resilience of proposed courses of action against adversarial counter-strategies, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing decision trade-offs across temporal, spatial, and organizational dimensions. By enabling rapid iteration through complex what-if scenarios, this work aims to reduce cognitive overload in high-stakes environments while maintaining human oversight. The computational demands—particularly the need for distributed training of RL agents across thousands of concurrent simulations and real-time fusion of terabyte-scale sensor data—necessitate specialized HPC infrastructure. Successful implementation will provide a foundation for enhancing interoperability in joint operations and inform future investments in AI-assisted command systems.
cip_title: Intelligence, Command Control and Information Operations, Other (MILITARY)
cip_definition: Any instructional program in intelligence, command control and information operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for analyzing cross-jurisdictional legal reasoning patterns, specifically tailored to support foreign lawyers navigating U.S. case law. The challenge lies in the vast, unstructured nature of U.S. judicial opinions, which contain implicit reasoning frameworks, cultural assumptions, and citation networks that are often opaque to those trained in non-Common Law systems. Traditional legal education tools struggle to systematically decode these patterns at scale, creating barriers for foreign legal professionals. This project proposes an interdisciplinary approach combining computational linguistics, graph theory, and comparative legal analysis to map doctrinal evolution and argumentation structures within U.S. appellate decisions. Using transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal corpora, we will process ~500,000 federal and state court opinions to identify latent reasoning templates, citation dynamics, and rhetorical strategies characteristic of U.S. jurisprudence. Graph neural networks will then model precedent hierarchies and temporal influence patterns across jurisdictions. The computational workflow requires distributed training of large language models across GPU nodes, parallel processing of heterogeneous legal texts, and iterative visualization of multidimensional legal concept spaces. Expected outcomes include an open-access analytical platform that visually surfaces implicit reasoning norms, predicts jurisprudential trends, and generates comparative syntheses between U.S. and non-U.S. legal approaches. This resource will directly enhance pedagogical tools for foreign lawyers by providing data-driven insights into the contextual logic of U.S. legal arguments, while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational social science and legal education. The project’s scale demands HPC capabilities to manage memory-intensive model training, real-time querying of massive legal graphs, and dynamic simulation of hypothetical legal scenarios based on historical reasoning patterns.
cip_definition: A program that prepares lawyers educated outside the United States to understand U. S. or Canadian law and jurisprudence.

abstract: Climate change and escalating anthropogenic pressures necessitate robust economic strategies to optimize conservation efforts and sustainable resource management. However, existing approaches often fail to account for the dynamic, non-linear interactions between ecological systems and socioeconomic factors, leading to suboptimal policy outcomes. This project addresses this gap by developing an integrated computational framework to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of conservation policies under environmental and market uncertainties. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to implement a spatially explicit, dynamic stochastic model that combines agent-based simulations of resource user behavior with biophysical models of ecosystem services. Key computational tasks include Bayesian calibration of ecological-economic parameters, Monte Carlo simulations to assess climate scenario uncertainties, and parallelized optimization algorithms to identify Pareto-efficient resource allocation strategies across heterogeneous landscapes. The model integrates high-resolution datasets on land use, biodiversity, and regional economic indicators, requiring large-scale data processing and real-time sensitivity analyses. By quantifying trade-offs between conservation investments, agricultural productivity, and long-term ecosystem resilience, this project aims to generate actionable insights for designing adaptive management policies. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for policymakers to prioritize interventions in critical habitats while balancing equity and efficiency goals. The computational framework will also advance methodological innovation in environmental economics by enabling granular, systems-level analysis of coupled human-natural systems, which is infeasible with conventional computing resources. This work directly contributes to global sustainability targets by bridging gaps between economic theory, ecological complexity, and computational scalability.
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Economics (NATURAL RESOURCES/ CONSERVATION SCIENCES)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic concepts and methods to the analysis of issues such as air and water pollution, land use planning, waste disposal, invasive species and pest control, conservation policies, and related environmental problems. Includes instruction in cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, evaluation and assessment of alternative resource management strategies, policy evaluation and monitoring, and descriptive and analytic tools for studying how environmental developments affect the economic system.

abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders represent a leading cause of disability globally, with surgical interventions such as joint replacements and fracture repairs often exhibiting variable outcomes due to patient-specific biomechanical, anatomical, and biological factors. A critical challenge in orthopedics is optimizing surgical planning and implant design to improve long-term functionality while minimizing complications. This project seeks to address this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific computational models that predict postoperative biomechanical behavior and tissue remodeling. The research will integrate clinical imaging data (CT, MRI), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate load distribution, bone-implant interface stresses, and osseointegration dynamics across diverse patient cohorts. Multiscale modeling frameworks will bridge molecular pathways influencing bone healing with macroscale mechanical responses, enabling the identification of biomarkers linked to implant failure or delayed recovery. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution imaging datasets, execute parallelized FEA simulations under physiologically realistic loading conditions, and train ML algorithms on multi-modal clinical data (demographic, genomic, biomechanical). Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide implant selection, surgical technique customization, and postoperative rehabilitation protocols. By correlating simulation results with longitudinal clinical outcomes, this work aims to establish a validated computational platform for personalized orthopedic care. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—requiring terabytes of data storage, GPU-accelerated computations, and large-scale parameter optimization—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Success in this project could reduce revision surgery rates, enhance functional recovery timelines, and provide a template for data-driven innovation in orthopedic clinical research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in reconstructing and interpreting fragmented ancient texts, a critical barrier in classical and ancient studies. Thousands of papyri, inscriptions, and manuscript fragments from Greco-Roman, Near Eastern, and early medieval contexts remain unreadable due to physical degradation, disordering, or linguistic ambiguities. Traditional manual reconstruction methods are labor-intensive and limited in scalability, particularly for cross-referencing multilingual corpora or detecting patterns across vast spatiotemporal contexts. This project proposes a computational pipeline integrating machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), and image analysis to automate fragment reassembly and contextual analysis. Neural networks will be trained on digitized text corpora (e.g., the Papyri.info database, epigraphic archives) and 3D-scanned artifact datasets to identify linguistic, stylistic, and material features that signal fragment relationships. Parallelized algorithms will map syntactic structures and semantic networks across languages (e.g., Greek, Latin, Coptic), while probabilistic models simulate plausible textual reconstructions. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution multispectral imaging data, train deep learning models on heterogeneous datasets (textual, visual, and archaeological), and run large-scale simulations of fragment alignment hypotheses. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for fragment analysis, newly reconstructed texts with confidence metrics, and interactive visualizations of textual networks. These results will advance understanding of cultural exchange, administrative practices, and literary transmission in antiquity, while establishing methodological frameworks for interdisciplinary collaboration between computational sciences and humanities. The project’s open-source tools and datasets will provide a foundation for future research in digital philology, reducing barriers to studying fragmentary heritage. By addressing computational bottlenecks in data integration and model training, this work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in unlocking inaccessible dimensions of ancient history.
cip_definition: Any program in classical and ancient studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making in horticultural business operations through advanced modeling of plant-environment interactions and supply chain dynamics. Horticultural enterprises face challenges in balancing productivity, resource efficiency, and profitability due to the complex interplay of biological systems, environmental variability, and market demands. Current analytical tools often lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale data, such as genomic traits, real-time sensor data from controlled environments, and fluctuating market variables. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build predictive models that synthesize these heterogeneous datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and experimental data to identify genotype-by-environment interactions that maximize crop yield and quality under resource constraints. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate supply chain scenarios to evaluate the economic and logistical impacts of production decisions, such as planting schedules or greenhouse energy use. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities to manage large parameter spaces and stochastic simulations. The outcomes will include open-access tools for growers to predict optimal crop selections, resource allocation strategies, and market timing, thereby reducing waste and improving profitability. By bridging biological insights with business analytics, this work aims to advance precision horticulture while supporting scalable, data-driven practices for an industry critical to food security and agricultural sustainability. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training, and real-time optimization analyses, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Applied Horticulture/ Horticultural Business Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in horticultural service operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The growing complexity of vendor-specific software ecosystems and the rapid evolution of proprietary technologies have created critical gaps in scalable, automated methods for validating certification workflows. Current approaches to software product certification rely heavily on manual testing and static compliance checks, which are resource-intensive, error-prone, and ill-suited for adaptive systems or heterogeneous deployment environments. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to automate the simulation and validation of vendor-certified software installation, configuration, and maintenance processes. By leveraging containerized environments and dynamic dependency analysis, the research will model multi-vendor interoperability scenarios across distributed systems, focusing on edge cases arising from hardware variability, security policy conflicts, and versioning inconsistencies. Computational workflows will integrate graph-based anomaly detection and probabilistic failure forecasting to identify certification risks in complex dependency chains. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated clusters to parallelize large-scale simulations of installation sequences, training machine learning models on synthetic and vendor-provided datasets to predict certification outcomes under constrained resource conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolchain for certifying cross-platform software deployments, optimized performance benchmarks for vendor-specific runtime environments, and novel metrics quantifying the resilience of certified configurations to adversarial system states. This work addresses an urgent need in industry-academia collaboration by bridging the gap between proprietary certification requirements and reproducible computational validation methods, with potential applications in healthcare IT, industrial control systems, and cloud-native infrastructure auditing. The HPC resources will enable the iterative refinement of predictive models and the validation of results against ground-truth certification data from participating technology partners.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to fulfill the requirements set by vendors for professional qualification as certified installation, customization, and maintenance engineers for specific software products and/or processes. Includes training in specific vendor-supported software products and their installation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social communication patterns and cognitive resilience in older adults, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model longitudinal changes in social network structures and their neuropsychological correlates. As aging populations grow, understanding how digitally mediated interactions (e.g., video calls, messaging platforms) influence cognitive health has become critical, yet existing studies lack the computational tools to analyze multi-modal, time-series data at scale. The research addresses this gap by integrating psycholinguistic analysis of communication content, dynamic network modeling of social ties, and machine learning–driven predictions of cognitive trajectories using neuroimaging and behavioral data. A cohort of 500 adults aged 65+ will provide anonymized digital communication logs, quarterly cognitive assessments, and functional MRI scans over three years. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing (NLP) to quantify emotional tone and semantic complexity in communications, graph theory algorithms to map evolving social network properties, and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to identify bidirectional relationships between network dynamics and domain-specific cognitive decline (e.g., memory, executive function). HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of text and neuroimaging data, running parallelized simulations of network evolution, and training predictive models with cross-validated temporal parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for modeling how technology-mediated social engagement buffers against age-related cognitive decline, (2) identification of linguistic and network signatures predictive of resilience, and (3) open-source tools for personalized intervention design, such as optimizing communication frequency or content to bolster cognitive health. By bridging geropsychology, computational linguistics, and network neuroscience, this work advances translational insights into how digital ecosystems shape aging trajectories, with implications for designing age-inclusive technologies and community support systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the characteristics of aging populations and the needs of older individuals in family and institutional settings. Includes instruction in the biological and psychological stages of aging; the provision of dependent care; serving the social, economic, and psychological needs of aging adults; related public policy issues; and adult community resources.

abstract: Radionuclide therapy faces a critical challenge in achieving patient-specific dose optimization due to complex interactions between radiopharmaceutical biodistribution, tissue heterogeneity, and dynamic metabolic processes. Current clinical protocols rely on population-averaged pharmacokinetic models, which often fail to account for individual variations in tumor biology, vascularization, and organ function. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC) framework integrating multi-scale biomechanical modeling and machine learning to predict patient-specific radiopharmaceutical dynamics and optimize therapeutic radiation doses. The computational approach combines finite-element simulations of tracer diffusion through vascular and interstitial spaces with Monte Carlo radiation transport models, calibrated using dynamic SPECT/CT imaging data and genomic profiles of tumor radiosensitivity. Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical patient datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of spatial dose deposition patterns. By leveraging parallelized GPU-accelerated computing, the framework will generate real-time, adaptive dosimetry maps accounting for temporal changes in tracer uptake and clearance. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for personalized activity administration and novel computational tools for intra-therapeutic dose modulation. This work will directly address variability in treatment response observed in neuroendocrine and prostate cancer therapies, potentially reducing off-target toxicity by 20-30% while maintaining tumor control rates. The developed platform will establish a paradigm shift toward adaptive, precision radionuclide therapy, bridging gaps between molecular imaging, systems biology, and therapeutic dosimetry. Access to HPC resources is essential for handling the >10^6-core-hour simulations and petabyte-scale multimodal data integration required for clinical translation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to employ radioactive and stable nuclides in diagnostic evaluations and therapeutic applications while monitoring for patient health and safety. Includes instruction in nuclear physics, health physics, instrumentation and statistics, biochemistry, immunology, radiopharmacology, radiation biology, clinical nuclear medicine, radionuclide therapy, computer applications, safety regulations, equipment operation, quality control, laboratory procedures, taking patient histories, patient evaluation and monitoring, emergency first aid, administration and record-keeping, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize multi-modal transportation networks under dynamic urban demand and climate resilience constraints. Rapid urbanization and shifting mobility patterns have strained existing infrastructure, leading to inefficiencies in traffic flow, increased congestion, and heightened vulnerability to extreme weather events. Traditional analytical models struggle to integrate real-time traffic data, heterogeneous traveler behavior, and infrastructure degradation scenarios at metropolitan scales. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and parallelized simulation to evaluate infrastructure interventions across spatial and temporal domains. The computational workflow will integrate terabytes of traffic sensor data, GPS trajectories, and climate projections to calibrate a city-scale digital twin. Reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively test adaptive traffic signal control policies, emergency evacuation routing, and infrastructure retrofit scenarios under stochastic demand and flood risk conditions. The HPC environment is critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of these simulations, which require millions of CPU-hours to resolve interactions between 10^6+ agent decisions, network-wide congestion effects, and probabilistic hazard exposures. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for prioritizing cost-effective infrastructure upgrades, reducing peak-hour congestion by 15-25% in testbed cities, and improving evacuation route resilience during flood scenarios. By quantifying trade-offs between mobility efficiency, equity, and climate adaptation, this work will provide transportation agencies with actionable insights for sustainable infrastructure investment. The resulting open-source codebase will enable scalable replication of the framework across diverse urban contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems for the physical movement of people, materials and information, including general network design and planning, facilities planning, site evaluation, transportation management systems, needs projections and analysis, and analysis of costs.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and behavioral dynamics of decentralized decision-making in ephemeral digital communities, a phenomenon increasingly prevalent in hybrid work and social platforms but underexplored in computational social science. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how transient, algorithmically mediated groups develop shared mental models despite lacking traditional organizational structures, and how these processes are shaped by real-time feedback loops between platform architectures and user behaviors. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose to develop a novel agent-based modeling framework integrating cognitive architectures with dynamic network analysis to simulate multi-scale interactions across heterogeneous digital environments. The computational model will incorporate empirical data from API-driven platform monitoring, including temporal interaction patterns and content diffusion metrics, to parameterize agents with empirically grounded decision heuristics. Key methodological challenges include scaling neural-symbolic hybrid agents to populations exceeding 10^5 nodes while maintaining cognitive plausibility, and resolving time-dependent network effects across multiple temporal granularities (millisecond-scale interface interactions to week-long community lifespans). Expected outcomes include 1) a validated simulation framework for studying emergent coordination in unstructured digital groups, 2) quantitative insights into critical thresholds where interface design features amplify or suppress collective intelligence, and 3) open-source tools for ethical AI-assisted moderation systems. The computational demands necessitate parallelized parameter space exploration across GPU-accelerated clusters, particularly for evolutionary optimization of agent learning rules and large-scale sensitivity analyses. By bridging cognitive science, human-computer interaction, and complex systems theory, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying digitally native social phenomena while informing the design of adaptive platforms that support sustainable decentralized collaboration.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in social sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern printing press operations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize complex variables in real-time press workflows. Despite advancements in digital printing technologies, operators face persistent challenges in balancing speed, material conservation, and color accuracy, particularly for high-volume or specialized print runs. Current trial-and-error calibration methods result in significant material waste, energy overuse, and production delays. This research proposes a computational approach to simulate press dynamics under diverse conditions, integrating sensor data from industrial presses with machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict optimal parameter configurations. Key computational tasks include finite element analysis of mechanical stress on press components, fluid dynamics modeling of ink distribution, and neural network training using historical performance data from partner printing facilities. The HPC environment is critical for handling large-scale simulations of multi-physics interactions and iterative ML training across heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include a predictive optimization toolkit that recommends pressure, temperature, and alignment settings for specific substrate-ink combinations, reducing setup time by an estimated 30-50% and waste by 15-25% in initial pilot tests. By establishing a computational framework tailored to non-scientific domains, this work aims to bridge gaps between industrial practices and data-driven decision-making in vocational printing education. The resource request supports the creation of adaptable digital twins for training purposes while advancing sustainable practices in communication industries reliant on physical media production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate, and maintain printing presses.

abstract: The increasing diversity of learning needs among students with disabilities necessitates innovative approaches to developing personalized educational strategies. Current methods for designing individualized education plans (IEPs) often rely on manual analysis of behavioral, academic, and sensory data, which limits scalability and real-time adaptability. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to create predictive models that optimize IEP development by integrating heterogeneous datasets, including longitudinal academic performance records, physiological sensor data, and unstructured behavioral observations. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in analyzing multi-modal data streams to identify patterns that correlate with optimal learning outcomes for students with neurodevelopmental disabilities (e.g., autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia). Using parallelized machine learning pipelines, we will train ensemble models on anonymized student datasets encompassing 50,000+ IEP trajectories from national repositories. Computational experiments will focus on (1) clustering students by multidimensional learning profiles using graph neural networks, (2) simulating intervention impacts through agent-based modeling of classroom dynamics, and (3) optimizing natural language processing (NLP) tools to automate analysis of teacher narratives and speech therapy transcripts. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of high-frequency sensor data (eye-tracking, wearable devices) and video recordings at scale, facilitating temporal pattern recognition inaccessible to traditional statistical methods. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating data-driven IEP recommendations, validated through partnerships with 12 special education schools. This work aims to establish computational foundations for precision special education while maintaining strict ethical standards for student data privacy. By reducing IEP development time by 30-50% while improving outcome correlation metrics, the project could transform resource-constrained special education classrooms through scalable AI-assisted decision support.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical vulnerabilities in healthcare data privacy and security posed by evolving cyber threats and the increasing complexity of modern health information systems. Current encryption and access control mechanisms often fail to adequately protect sensitive patient data, particularly when integrating emerging technologies such as genomic databases, IoT-enabled medical devices, and AI-driven diagnostics. The research problem centers on developing scalable, adaptive computational models to safeguard multi-modal healthcare data while maintaining compliance with ethical and legal frameworks like HIPAA and GDPR. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design and simulate advanced privacy-preserving algorithms, including federated learning architectures, homomorphic encryption protocols, and real-time anomaly detection systems. Computational workflows will involve large-scale simulations of cyber-attack scenarios on synthetic healthcare datasets, optimization of machine learning models for threat prediction, and benchmarking of cryptographic techniques under varying data-sharing conditions. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC clusters, the team will quantify trade-offs between data utility, privacy guarantees, and computational overhead in diverse clinical contexts. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for dynamic risk assessment in healthcare networks, open-source tools for privacy-aware data anonymization, and performance benchmarks for next-generation security protocols. The project’s significance lies in its potential to mitigate ransomware attacks, unauthorized data breaches, and insider threats in healthcare systems, directly supporting the program’s mission to train professionals in implementing robust security infrastructures. Results will be disseminated through a public repository of simulated attack datasets and modular codebases tailored for healthcare IT administrators, advancing both theoretical and applied research in health information assurance.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and performance of composite materials for aerospace, renewable energy, and medical applications. Composite materials’ heterogeneous, multiscale structures present significant challenges in predicting mechanical behavior, failure modes, and environmental durability. Traditional experimental approaches are costly and time-intensive, while existing simulations often lack the resolution to capture interactions between fibers, matrices, and interfaces across atomic, micro-, and macro-scales. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating multiscale modeling, machine learning, and finite element analysis (FEA). Molecular dynamics simulations will resolve atomic-scale interactions in polymer matrices and fiber coatings, while mesoscale FEA models will predict stress distribution and damage propagation in laminated structures. A machine learning pipeline trained on simulation data will identify optimal material configurations (e.g., fiber orientation, resin chemistry) under constraints such as weight, thermal stability, and fatigue resistance. These workflows require HPC resources to manage large parameter spaces, parallelize computationally intensive simulations, and process high-dimensional data. Expected outcomes include predictive models for novel carbon-fiber-reinforced polymers with 15–20% improved strength-to-weight ratios for aircraft components, fatigue-resistant wind turbine blades, and bio-compatible composites for prosthetics. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular code for the composites community, reducing barriers to computational material design. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping, this work aims to shorten development cycles by 30–50% and support sustainable material innovation in critical industries. The requested computing resources will directly sustain GPU-accelerated simulations, data storage for terabyte-scale outputs, and distributed training of deep neural networks, ensuring scalability as model complexity grows.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and use of composite materials in aircraft technology, automotive technology, boats, medical prostheses, and wind turbines. Includes instruction in computer-aided design and drafting, composite materials and processes, composite maintenance, composite manufacturing, composite repair, material science, and mold manufacturing and production.

abstract: Ophthalmic lens fabrication requires precise optimization of optical, material, and ergonomic parameters to address diverse visual impairments, yet current methods for designing complex prescriptions—such as those for high myopia, irregular corneas, or multifocal needs—rely heavily on iterative manual adjustments. These processes are time-intensive, costly, and may not fully account for patient-specific anatomical variations or dynamic visual demands. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to automate and enhance the design of precision ophthalmic lenses using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of traditional lens fabrication workflows by integrating optical ray-tracing simulations, finite element analysis (FEA) of lens stress distribution, and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization algorithms. Computational models will simulate light propagation through candidate lens geometries under varying pupil dynamics and gaze conditions, while FEA will evaluate mechanical durability during edging and mounting. Concurrently, ML models trained on historical prescription data, patient biometrics, and material performance metrics will predict optimal lens parameters. HPC resources are critical to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize simulations across thousands of design iterations, and process multimodal datasets (optical, structural, clinical) at scale. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific lens designs that minimize optical aberrations, improve comfort, and reduce production waste. The project also aims to establish a database correlating computational predictions with real-world fabrication outcomes, enabling iterative refinement of models. By bridging computational optics and ophthalmic technology, this work has the potential to advance personalized eyewear solutions, reduce turnaround times for complex prescriptions, and provide a scalable platform for educating future practitioners in data-driven lens design methodologies. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and partnerships with clinical training programs to align laboratory practices with emerging computational techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving dynamics of labor solidarity networks in gig economy platforms using large-scale network analysis and agent-based modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how decentralized, algorithmically mediated work environments influence collective action among workers, particularly in regions with weak traditional labor protections. By integrating anonymized gig worker interaction data (from public forums, protest coordination platforms, and unionization efforts) with simulated economic shock scenarios, the project will model emergent patterns of labor mobilization under varying platform governance structures. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale temporal network datasets spanning multiple countries, running parallelized simulations of worker decision-making algorithms, and training graph neural networks to identify latent organizational structures within fragmented digital labor communities. The computational workflow will combine natural language processing of worker-generated text, dynamic network community detection, and game-theoretic equilibrium analysis to map how information cascades and resource constraints shape solidarity-building processes. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting labor movement scalability in platform economies, actionable insights for designing algorithmic tools that support worker agency, and policy-relevant metrics quantifying the relationship between platform architecture and collective bargaining potential. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, labor economics, and human-computer interaction studies while advancing methodological innovation in analyzing digital labor phenomena at unprecedented scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of various aspects of work, labor organization and policy, and labor movements from the perspective of the social sciences and history. Includes instruction in labor history; political and ideological issues; worker movements and social organizations; civil rights; labor law and policy studies; labor economics; international and comparative labor studies; and applications to specific industries, groups, locations, and time periods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the design and control of integrated electromechanical systems for advanced manufacturing applications. A critical challenge in this domain lies in balancing real-time responsiveness with energy efficiency in systems where dynamic mechanical loads interact with embedded power electronics and sensor networks. Traditional decoupled simulations often fail to capture the nonlinear coupling between solid-state circuitry, thermal-fluid effects in actuators, and mechanical vibrations, leading to suboptimal designs or unstable control strategies. To address this gap, we propose a multi-physics modeling approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) for structural dynamics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management, and circuit simulation tools, all tightly coupled through co-simulation techniques. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the temporal and spatial scales required for accurate system-level predictions, particularly when analyzing high-frequency switching in power electronics alongside millisecond-scale mechanical transients. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers for distributed parameter systems and employ machine learning algorithms to accelerate design space exploration for robotic assembly cells and automated material handling systems. Expected outcomes include validated digital twins for three industrial use cases: (1) energy-regenerative linear actuators, (2) thermally stable motor-drive units for CNC machinery, and (3) adaptive vibration damping systems with embedded power electronics. By enabling concurrent optimization of electrical and mechanical subsystems, this research will provide new methodologies to reduce prototyping costs by 30-50% while improving system efficiency metrics. The resulting open-source simulation tools will directly support workforce development in smart manufacturing, aligning with Industry 4.0 priorities for electromechanical engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the problems associated with combining electrical and mechanical components with special emphasis on manufacturing and automated processes. Includes instruction in applied mechanics, instrumentation and monitoring, machine design, automated control techniques, fluid and thermal dynamics, circuit analysis, and solid state electronics.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for individuals with sensorimotor impairments by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to model neuromuscular adaptation during assistive device training. Current clinical approaches to prescribing robotic exoskeletons or prosthetics rely on generalized biomechanical models, which often fail to account for patient-specific neurophysiological variability, leading to suboptimal outcomes in mobility restoration. This project addresses the critical gap in understanding how neural control systems dynamically interact with assistive technologies during rehabilitation, particularly in populations with stroke or spinal cord injury. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate multiscale datasets—including electromyography, motion capture, and neuroimaging—to simulate corticospinal reorganization and muscle synergy recalibration in response to device use. Computational models will employ hybrid agent-based and finite element methods to capture individual neuromuscular dynamics at resolutions impractical for conventional systems. Machine learning pipelines will optimize parameter estimation across heterogeneous patient cohorts, while sensitivity analyses will identify biomarkers predictive of rehabilitation success. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable, open-source platform for simulating patient-device interactions, validated against longitudinal clinical data, which will enable clinicians to tailor device configurations and training protocols to individual neuro-mechanical profiles. By bridging computational neuroscience and rehabilitation engineering, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift toward precision rehabilitation, reducing trial-and-error in device prescription and improving functional recovery timelines. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize stochastic simulations of neural plasticity, and deploy federated learning architectures to protect patient privacy during multi-institution collaborations. This interdisciplinary approach not only advances rehabilitation science but also provides a template for integrating HPC-driven modeling into clinical decision-making for complex, understudied populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human function, disability, and rehabilitation from the perspectives of the health sciences, social sciences, psychology, engineering, and related fields. Includes instruction in psychological, social, and cultural aspects of disability and rehabilitation; sensory and motor function and dysfunction; biomechanics and kinesiology; assistive technology; rehabilitation instrumentation and methodology; statistics; and health and rehabilitation policy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems necessitates advanced methods to optimize equipment reliability, maintenance protocols, and failure prediction. Traditional approaches to equipment diagnostics and repair often rely on reactive strategies, leading to unplanned downtime and inefficiencies in industrial and commercial settings. This project proposes a computational research initiative to develop predictive maintenance frameworks and fault-detection algorithms tailored to electrical and electronic systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the study will simulate diverse operational scenarios—including voltage fluctuations, thermal stress, and component degradation—to model failure mechanisms in power distribution systems, industrial control circuits, and consumer electronics. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic and real-world sensor data to identify early warning signs of equipment malfunction. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will further analyze heat dissipation patterns in densely packed circuits, informing design improvements for enhanced longevity. The scale of these simulations, requiring parallel processing of multi-physics interactions and large datasets, mandates access to HPC infrastructure for feasible execution. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms capable of reducing equipment downtime by 20–30%, optimized maintenance schedules validated through probabilistic risk assessment models, and data-driven guidelines for component redesign. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops for repair technicians and open-access datasets to bridge gaps between computational research and applied repair practices. This work directly supports the educational mission of Electrical/Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair programs by integrating computational tools into technician training, fostering a workforce adept at leveraging advanced analytics in equipment maintenance. The project’s computational outputs will provide a scalable framework for adaptive repair strategies in evolving smart grid and IoT-enabled environments.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: Dairy cattle production systems face critical challenges in optimizing feed efficiency, animal health, and environmental sustainability. Current models for predicting rumen microbiota dynamics and their metabolic interactions with host physiology lack resolution to account for strain-level microbial diversity, host-genetic variation, and real-time environmental inputs. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating multi-omics data (metagenomics, metabolomics, host transcriptomics) to model microbial community behavior in the dairy cow rumen and its systemic impacts on milk production, methane emissions, and nutrient utilization. The research will employ machine learning architectures, including graph neural networks and attention-based models, to identify key microbial taxa and functional pathways associated with feed efficiency phenotypes across diverse cattle genotypes. Agent-based modeling will simulate microbial population dynamics under varying dietary regimes, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize enzymatic interactions in fiber degradation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of sequencing data, train predictive models on heterogeneous datasets, and run computationally intensive simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible predictive platform for optimizing feed formulations, a ranked list of microbial biomarkers for selective breeding programs, and mechanistic insights into methane mitigation strategies. By linking microbial ecology to dairy production metrics, this work will advance precision nutrition tools, reduce the environmental footprint of dairy operations, and provide a template for integrating systems biology approaches in agricultural sciences. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for genome assembly, and parallelized simulations across 10,000+ core-hours to achieve statistically robust results within biologically relevant timescales.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: Neurologic disorders in children, including epilepsy, cerebral palsy, and genetic neurodevelopmental conditions, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their etiological heterogeneity, dynamic developmental trajectories, and complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors. Current clinical approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multi-modal datasets—such as high-resolution neuroimaging, whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), and wearable sensor data—limiting the ability to identify predictive biomarkers or personalize interventions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps by enabling large-scale integrative analyses of heterogeneous pediatric neurology data. We will develop computational workflows to harmonize and process multi-site neuroimaging (e.g., MRI, fMRI, DTI) and multi-omics data, leveraging machine learning models to uncover subtype-specific patterns in conditions like neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and autism spectrum disorder. HPC resources will facilitate genome-wide association studies (GWAS) paired with deep learning-based image analysis to identify genotype-phenotype correlations, as well as dynamic simulations of neurodevelopmental trajectories using patient-derived neural organoid models. Additionally, federated learning frameworks will be deployed to train predictive models on distributed EHR data while preserving privacy. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, stratification of patients into treatment-responsive subgroups, and open-source tools for scalable analysis of pediatric neurodevelopmental data. This work will directly inform clinical trial design and therapeutic targeting, ultimately reducing diagnostic delays and improving outcomes for children with neurologic disorders. The requested computing resources are critical to managing the computational load of these analyses, which involve terabytes of imaging data, millions of genetic variants, and complex longitudinal modeling.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of neurologic disorders of the neonatal period, infancy, early childhood, and adolescence. Requires training in neurology with additional training in child neurology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to evaluate the multi-dimensional impacts of urban housing policies, a critical public policy challenge characterized by complex interactions between regulatory environments, demographic shifts, and resource allocation dynamics. Traditional policy analysis tools often struggle to integrate real-time heterogeneous datasets—such as zoning records, housing affordability metrics, and infrastructure utilization patterns—while accounting for nonlinear feedback effects across stakeholders. To address this gap, the research employs agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate decision-making processes among policymakers, developers, and residents under varying policy scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations that capture granular spatial and temporal interactions across millions of agents, incorporating dynamic datasets from municipal APIs, census microdata, and geospatial repositories. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess policy robustness under uncertainty, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will identify emergent inequities in housing access. The computational pipeline will be validated against historical policy outcomes in three U.S. metropolitan regions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating housing policy trade-offs, with open-source modules for sensitivity analysis and equity impact scoring. This work will provide policymakers with evidence-based insights into optimizing housing supply interventions while mitigating displacement risks. The requested HPC resources will enable iterative model calibration, reduce runtime for parameter-space exploration from weeks to days, and support the integration of high-resolution urban datasets that exceed the memory limits of standard computing infrastructure. By advancing computational methods for policy simulation, this project aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven decision-making in complex public policy domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues and decision processes. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, microeconomic analysis of policy issues, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in optimizing healthcare delivery systems through advanced computational modeling and data analytics. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies in resource allocation, operational workflows, and policy evaluation within complex healthcare environments, which are exacerbated by dynamic patient populations, fluctuating demand, and heterogeneous regulatory landscapes. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the interdependencies among these factors, limiting the ability to predict outcomes or design scalable interventions. To overcome these limitations, this study will develop large-scale simulation models integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning techniques to analyze multi-source data, including electronic health records, insurance claims, and public health datasets. These models will simulate scenarios such as hospital capacity planning, workforce distribution, emergency response coordination, and the impact of reimbursement policies on service accessibility. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of parallelized simulations, real-time optimization of stochastic parameters, and training predictive algorithms on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into cost-effective resource allocation strategies, predictive tools for mitigating service bottlenecks, and evidence-based frameworks for evaluating the equity and sustainability of health policies. The results will directly inform healthcare administrators and policymakers, enabling data-driven decisions to enhance system resilience, reduce disparities, and improve population health outcomes. This work aligns with the Health Services Administration program’s emphasis on integrating management, policy, and operational analytics to advance healthcare delivery.
