cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of policy analysis, public administration, business management, and communications to the planning and management of health services delivery systems in the public and private sectors, and prepares individuals to function as health services administrators and managers. Includes instruction in health systems planning, public health organization and management, pubic health policy formulation and analysis, finance, business and operations management, economics of health care, organizational and health communications, marketing, human resources management, and public health law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how leadership development programs in educational institutions influence organizational climate and equity outcomes using large-scale computational modeling. While leadership training frameworks are widely implemented to foster inclusive environments, traditional evaluations often rely on self-reported data or localized case studies, limiting insights into systemic, long-term impacts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate organizational dynamics across diverse institutional contexts. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to represent interactions among leaders, staff, and stakeholders, incorporating variables such as decision-making hierarchies, resource allocation patterns, and communication networks. Longitudinal datasets from public K-12 districts and higher education systems—including employee surveys, retention metrics, and policy implementation records—will be integrated to parameterize and validate models. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) techniques will analyze unstructured data from leadership training materials, meeting transcripts, and institutional communications to identify latent biases or alignment with equity-focused practices. The computational demands of simulating thousands of organizational scenarios, coupled with NLP processing across multi-terabyte text corpora, necessitate parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated inference. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of leadership behaviors most strongly correlated with equitable resource distribution and employee satisfaction, (2) predictive models to assess how training interventions scale across institutions of varying sizes and demographics, and (3) open-source tools for simulating policy impacts on organizational development. By elucidating the computational signatures of effective educational leadership, this work aims to provide evidence-based strategies for designing adaptive professional development programs and advancing equity in administrative decision-making. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the iterative model calibration, sensitivity analyses, and large-scale data integration required to generalize findings beyond isolated cases.
cip_title: Education and Human Resource Studies/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize operational decision-making in salon and beauty salon management through advanced data analytics and simulation. The beauty industry faces unique challenges, including dynamic customer preferences, high staff turnover, and the need for real-time inventory and service customization, yet traditional management tools often lack the granularity to address these complexities. Our research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to model salon ecosystems at scale, integrating heterogeneous datasets—such as customer booking patterns, stylist performance metrics, supply chain logistics, and regional beauty trends—into a unified simulation environment. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate stylist-client interactions, machine learning (ML) for demand forecasting, and discrete-event simulation (DES) to evaluate resource allocation strategies under varying operational scenarios. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve real-time optimization of staffing schedules, inventory procurement, and service pricing while accounting for stochastic variables like seasonal demand shifts and emerging beauty trends. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for salon managers to simulate “what-if” scenarios, predict revenue impacts of operational changes, and identify inefficiencies in service workflows. The project bridges a critical gap in non-STEM business analytics by applying computational rigor to a specialized service sector, offering scalable solutions that could redefine small-business management practices in the beauty industry. Results will be validated against real-world salon performance data, with a focus on generalizability across diverse business sizes and geographic markets. This work highlights the transformative potential of HPC in niche service industries, advancing both academic understanding and practical tools for understudied, high-impact domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares cosmetologists, hairstylists, and other personal grooming specialists to manage beauty parlors, shops, and full-service or specialized salons and to prepare for licensure as professional salon owners and operators.  Includes instruction in cosmetic services marketing and retailing; advertising and promotion; salon management; the cosmetic and salon supply industries; hiring, supervision, and labor relations; applicable business and professional laws and regulations; professional standards and image; and customer service.

abstract: This project proposes a novel computational investigation into the biophysical mechanisms underlying Reiki therapy, an energy-based healing practice, to evaluate its potential physiological impacts at the cellular and molecular levels. Despite anecdotal reports of Reiki’s therapeutic benefits, a lack of empirical models explaining its interaction with biological systems limits its integration into evidence-based health frameworks. The research problem centers on identifying quantifiable, energy-mediated interactions between Reiki practices and cellular processes, particularly in contexts of stress response and tissue repair. To address this, we will develop multiscale computational models simulating biofield dynamics—hypothesized low-level electromagnetic or quantum-vibrational fields associated with Reiki—and their influence on ion channels, protein conformations, and redox signaling pathways. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the complexity of these simulations, which integrate molecular dynamics (GROMACS), finite element analysis for electromagnetic field propagation (COMSOL), and machine learning-driven pattern recognition (PyTorch) to analyze perturbations in simulated cellular environments. Parallelized workflows will optimize parameter space exploration across varying Reiki "attunement" protocols (e.g., symbol sequences, practitioner intent metrics). Experimental data from in vitro models of human fibroblasts under oxidative stress, treated by certified Reiki practitioners, will validate computational predictions via comparative transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework linking Reiki’s energy manipulation to mechanistically plausible biological effects, (2) identification of candidate biomarkers for non-thermal biofield-cell interactions, and (3) predictive models for optimizing Reiki protocols in targeted clinical scenarios, such as post-operative recovery. By bridging energy medicine and systems biology, this work aims to establish a foundational toolkit for studying subtle energy therapies within rigorous computational health science paradigms, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue and informing future translational studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical, emotional, and spiritual balance and healing through the manipulation of the body's energy field to increase healing energy. Includes instruction in the history and philosophy of Usui Reiki, attunement, empowerment, self-treatment, direct and distance healing techniques, healing symbols, aura clearing, Reiki meditation, practice management, and related Reiki systems such as Lightarian, Urevia, and Magnified Healing.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing predictive maintenance strategies for complex industrial machinery through advanced computational modeling and machine learning techniques. Industrial systems such as marine propulsion units, refinery pipelines, and high-pressure hydraulic equipment are subject to multifaceted degradation mechanisms, including thermal stress, corrosion, and mechanical wear. Traditional maintenance schedules often rely on generalized heuristics or reactive protocols, leading to unnecessary downtime, inefficient resource allocation, and elevated failure risks. This research will develop physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) coupled with high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to predict equipment lifespan under variable operational conditions. The computational workflow will integrate real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled machinery with material science models of fatigue behavior, enabling dynamic risk assessment at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep learning models on heterogeneous datasets spanning vibration spectra, thermal imaging, and lubrication analysis while simultaneously resolving multiphysics simulations of component failure modes. Expected outcomes include a framework for condition-based maintenance prioritization that reduces unplanned downtime by ≥30% in testbed industrial environments, validated against empirical wear measurements from CNC machining centers and centrifugal pump systems. The research will further produce open-source tools for anomaly detection in time-series equipment data, tailored to workforce training applications in industrial maintenance programs. By leveraging parallel computing architectures to handle complex optimization landscapes and large-scale parameter sweeps, this work aims to bridge the gap between academic predictive maintenance theories and deployable solutions for small-to-medium manufacturing enterprises. The computational infrastructure will also support student-led projects in digital twin development, enhancing workforce readiness in emerging Industry 4.0 maintenance paradigms.
cip_title: Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair and maintain industrial machinery and equipment such as cranes, pumps, engines and motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, production machinery, marine deck machinery, and steam propulsion, refinery, and pipeline-distribution systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of enzyme-responsive biomaterials for targeted drug delivery, addressing the challenge of achieving precise spatiotemporal control in therapeutic release. Current experimental approaches to engineer these systems are limited by the complexity of modeling enzyme-substrate interactions, molecular-level assembly dynamics, and degradation kinetics under physiological conditions. We propose to integrate atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with coarse-grained kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) methods to bridge time- and length-scale gaps inherent in traditional modeling approaches. The MD simulations will characterize interfacial binding energetics and conformational changes in protease-sensitive peptide linkers, while the kMC framework will predict bulk degradation behavior of polymeric nanoparticles as a function of linker chemistry and matrix topology. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation data to identify design rules linking molecular descriptors to release profiles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the >10^6-atom systems in explicit solvent, microsecond-scale MD trajectories, and parameterization of multi-fidelity models across 10^4+ combinatorial material variants. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for rational biomaterial design, reducing costly iterative experimentation in drug carrier development. The computational pipeline will be generalized to other enzyme-driven systems, advancing applications in personalized cancer therapeutics and programmable biomanufacturing. This work aligns with the molecular biotechnology focus of chemical engineering by connecting nanoscale phenomena to process-relevant performance metrics, with broader impacts on biopharmaceutical innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems at the interface of chemical engineering and biology, with an emphasis at the molecular level, such as biopharmaceutical processes, protein engineering, metabolic engineering, gene therapy, biomaterials, cell and tissue engineering, and drug delivery. Includes instruction in chemical engineering, thermodynamics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, momentum and heat transfer, cellular and molecular biotechnology, process design, and chemical reactor design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transmission and transformation of Jewish philosophical thought across multilingual textual corpora spanning antiquity to the early modern period. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of influence, adaptation, and debate within Jewish philosophical works written in Hebrew, Judeo-Arabic, and Aramaic, which remain understudied due to the computational challenges of processing non-Latin scripts, morphological complexity in Semitic languages, and the intertextual nature of religious-philosophical discourse. Traditional methods of close reading struggle to systematically track conceptual developments across vast textual networks or quantify linguistic shifts in philosophical terminology over time. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) adapted for historical Semitic languages, graph-based network analysis of citation patterns, and transformer models fine-tuned on philosophical texts. HPC resources will enable processing of ~15,000 digitized manuscripts and early printed works from the Open Genizah Project, Sefaria database, and partner libraries, requiring significant memory allocation for parallelized text normalization and morphological disambiguation across heterogeneous sources. Network analysis will map relationships between philosophical concepts (e.g., divine providence, free will) and their evolution through key nodes such as Maimonides' *Guide for the Perplexed* and subsequent commentaries. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for cross-lingual analysis of Jewish philosophical corpora, 2) quantitative evidence challenging periodization boundaries in medieval Jewish thought, and 3) open-access visualization tools for tracing argumentative trajectories. This computational approach will advance Judaic studies by revealing previously obscured intellectual networks while demonstrating how HPC can address fundamental humanities questions about cultural transmission in religious-philosophical traditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people. Includes instruction in Jewish religious heritage, sacred texts, and law; Jewish philosophy and intellectual history; Jewish life and culture, both in Israel and the Jewish Diaspora; historical Jewish minority cultures such as the Yiddish, Sephardic, and other; anti-Semitism, gentile relations and Shoa; Zionism; and modern developments within Judaism.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance the detection and analysis of complex fraud patterns in government contracting and grant systems, a critical component of suspension and debarment investigations. Current investigative methods often rely on manual audits and fragmented data analysis, which struggle to scale with the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of modern procurement data. This limitation impedes the identification of subtle fraud networks, cross-jurisdictional anomalies, and emergent money-laundering tactics. To address this gap, the project proposes developing computational models that integrate structured transactional data with unstructured legal, contractual, and communications records. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to extract entities and relationships from legal documents and correspondence, while graph-based machine learning algorithms will map interdependencies among contractors, subcontractors, and grantees. These models will be supplemented by anomaly detection frameworks trained on historical case data to flag high-risk behaviors. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of federal procurement datasets (spanning billions of transactions), the complexity of temporal network analyses, and the iterative nature of training domain-specific NLP models. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for forensic auditors and investigators, optimized to identify collusion patterns, resource misallocation, and jurisdictional overlaps in near-real time. The project also aims to establish benchmarks for algorithmic fairness in investigative AI systems, addressing potential biases in case prioritization. By bridging computational social science and administrative law, this work will advance proactive fraud mitigation strategies while informing policy frameworks for ethical AI adoption in regulatory contexts. Results will be validated against active investigations in collaboration with oversight agencies, ensuring practical applicability to public integrity preservation.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for investigating criminal behavior among government contractors and grantees at different levels. Includes instruction in financial fraud and money-laundering, auditing, computer investigations, legal concepts and applications, procurement law, non-procurement debarment, jurisdiction and lead agency, analytical methods, suspension, parallel proceedings, evidence protection, equitable considerations, investigative techniques, administrative and global solutions, case management and preparation.

abstract: Public agencies face increasing challenges in optimizing resource allocation for social services amid growing demand, fiscal constraints, and complex socioeconomic interdependencies. Traditional analytical tools often fail to account for dynamic system-wide interactions, stochastic variables, and large-scale datasets, limiting evidence-based policymaking. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating the impacts of public resource allocation strategies across interconnected policy domains, including healthcare access, housing assistance, and workforce development programs. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct an agent-based model integrating demographic, economic, and service utilization data from municipal, state, and federal sources. The model will simulate how variations in funding thresholds, eligibility criteria, and administrative coordination affect both equity outcomes and operational efficiency across multiple policy timelines. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters using historical program performance data, while Monte Carlo methods will assess policy resilience under diverse economic scenarios. Computational demands arise from the need to process terabyte-scale linked datasets, execute parallelized simulations across thousands of policy permutations, and perform sensitivity analyses on high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of identifying allocation strategies that balance equity, cost-effectiveness, and administrative feasibility under uncertainty. This work will advance methodological approaches in public administration by demonstrating how computational social science techniques can address gaps in conventional policy analysis frameworks. Results will provide actionable insights for improving multi-program resource coordination and establish scalable modeling protocols for public agencies. The project aligns with the program’s focus on enhancing governance through innovative applications of technology in public decision-making processes.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Administration and Public Policy and with an emphasis the administration and management of public policies. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; research methods; role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation; and resource allocation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making processes within joint military command and control (C3/C4I) systems under conditions of dynamic, multi-domain operational complexity. Current C3/C4I architectures often struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams—ranging from sensor feeds to human-generated intelligence—into actionable insights at scales and speeds demanded by modern multi-theater operations. The research problem centers on developing adaptive computational frameworks capable of simulating and analyzing decision pathways in contested environments where adversarial actions, resource constraints, and communication latency introduce nonlinear uncertainties. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this project will model large-scale, scenario-driven simulations of joint task force operations, incorporating machine learning (ML) techniques to predict adversarial behavior patterns and evaluate resilience of command networks. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling of multi-echelon decision hierarchies, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic risk assessment, and graph-theoretic analyses of communication network robustness under cyber-physical attacks. Key innovations involve the integration of federated learning architectures to preserve data security across distributed command nodes and the use of evolutionary algorithms to optimize resource allocation in bandwidth-constrained environments. Expected outcomes include a validated suite of predictive models for identifying systemic vulnerabilities in C3/C4I workflows, as well as actionable metrics for balancing automation with human oversight in high-stakes scenarios. By enabling rapid stress-testing of command protocols against synthetically generated multi-domain threats, this work aims to advance adaptive planning capabilities for joint forces while informing next-generation C3/C4I system design. The computational intensity of simulating thousands of concurrent entities across geographically dispersed nodes necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with parallel processing capabilities, distributed memory architectures, and low-latency interconnects to achieve militarily relevant temporal resolutions.
cip_title: Joint Command/ Task Force (C3, C4I) Systems (MILITARY)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and operational use of command and control (C3, C4I) systems as applied to joint and combined military operations involving unified commands. Includes instruction in information technology, communications systems, network systems and architecture, systems engineering, C3 and C4I doctrine and policy, C3 and C4I systems management, intelligence, operational and strategic planning, interagency operations, operational security and deception.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze patterns in legal document complexity and procedural inefficiencies within high-volume litigation contexts, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in paralegal workflows. Legal assistants routinely manage vast datasets of case files, motions, and discovery materials, where manual review processes delay timelines and increase the risk of oversight. The research problem centers on identifying systemic bottlenecks—such as recurrent ambiguities in contractual language or inconsistent citation practices—that prolong case preparation and compromise resource allocation in legal practices. Using natural language processing (NLP) methods tailored to legal text, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on case law corpora, the project will automate semantic analysis of document clusters to classify complexity levels and predict procedural delays. Graph-based algorithms will map temporal and relational dependencies between case components (e.g., motions, evidence chains, judicial rulings) to simulate workflow optimizations. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across millions of documents from publicly accessible legal databases and anonymized firm repositories, enabling rapid iteration of ensemble models and hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for prioritizing document review tasks, flagging high-risk procedural dependencies, and generating templated recommendations for workflow adjustments. By integrating computational rigor with paralegal domain expertise, this work aims to establish a precedent for data-driven decision-making in legal operations, reducing administrative burdens and enhancing the strategic allocation of human resources. The interdisciplinary approach bridges legal informatics and computational logistics, offering a template for similar resource-constrained, document-intensive fields outside traditional science and engineering domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform research, drafting, investigatory, record-keeping and related administrative functions under the supervision of an attorney or court. Includes instruction in legal research, drafting legal documents, appraising, pleading, courthouse procedures, and legal specializations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern engineering design challenges necessitates advanced computational tools to enable high-fidelity simulations and optimization. Traditional drafting and design methodologies often struggle with the computational demands of multi-physics modeling, real-time collaborative design iterations, and generative topology optimization, particularly when applied to large-scale or intricate systems. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy scalable computational frameworks tailored for drafting and design engineering applications. The research will focus on implementing parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers to accelerate simulation workflows, alongside machine learning algorithms for predictive design optimization. By integrating distributed computing architectures, the proposed methods aim to reduce simulation times for complex assemblies by an order of magnitude, enabling rapid design iteration cycles. Additionally, the project will investigate GPU-accelerated rendering techniques to support real-time collaborative design environments, facilitating simultaneous multi-user engagement with high-resolution 3D models. The expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools that bridge gaps between HPC capabilities and mainstream computer-aided design (CAD) software, thereby democratizing access to advanced simulation resources for educational and industrial practitioners. This work is anticipated to significantly enhance the efficiency of design validation processes, reduce material waste through optimized structural configurations, and contribute to sustainable engineering practices by enabling data-driven design decisions. The requested computing resources will be critical in handling the large-scale datasets and iterative computations inherent to these objectives, ensuring robust validation of the proposed methodologies across diverse use cases in mechanical, aerospace, and civil infrastructure design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in drafting/design engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to evaluate the equity and efficiency of public resource allocation strategies in multi-stakeholder policy environments, with a focus on urban infrastructure planning. Traditional policy evaluation methods often struggle to account for dynamic interactions between demographic shifts, competing budgetary priorities, and evolving regulatory constraints. The research problem centers on creating scalable models that can simulate thousands of policy scenarios while integrating real-time data from municipal records, environmental sensors, and public feedback systems. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling techniques to represent diverse stakeholder decision-making processes and system dynamics across transportation, housing, and public health domains. The computational approach combines parallelized Monte Carlo simulations with machine learning-driven sensitivity analysis to identify policy configurations that optimize multiple equity metrics under uncertainty. Key challenges include processing terabyte-scale datasets of historical policy outcomes and resolving complex constraints through mixed-integer optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that enables policymakers to visualize trade-offs between competing objectives and assess the long-term resilience of allocation strategies. This work will advance computational social science methodologies in public administration by establishing new benchmarks for modeling polycentric governance systems. Successful implementation could inform evidence-based revisions to municipal capital improvement processes, particularly in regions facing rapid urbanization and climate adaptation pressures. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution in simulations, as preliminary tests on local clusters show prohibitive runtime requirements when modeling city-scale systems beyond five-year horizons.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Policy and Public Administration with an emphasis on issues related to public policy. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, principles of public administration; the management of public policy; and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing energy-efficient signal processing in next-generation distributed wireless communication systems, with a focus on dynamically reconfigurable networks operating in non-stationary environments. Current methods for real-time beamforming and resource allocation in massive MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) architectures struggle to balance computational complexity, latency, and energy consumption under rapidly changing channel conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with parallelizable stochastic optimization algorithms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to 1) train multi-scale PINN models on terahertz channel propagation datasets generated via finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulations, 2) implement distributed consensus optimization across simulated network nodes using MPI-based parallelization, and 3) validate adaptive beamforming strategies through large-scale digital twin simulations incorporating real-world mobility patterns. The computational intensity arises from simultaneously solving coupled partial differential equations for wave propagation, training neural networks with 10^8+ parameters, and simulating network dynamics across 1000+ virtual user equipment nodes. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms capable of reducing energy consumption by 30-40% compared to conventional methods while maintaining sub-millisecond latency targets for 6G applications. Results will advance the design of environmentally sustainable communication infrastructure and provide open-source tools for joint electromagnetic-optimization modeling. The requested GPU-accelerated computing resources are essential for achieving the required simulation scale and training throughput within practical timeframes.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronics, and Communications Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The construction and repair of wooden boats rely on empirical techniques and artisanal knowledge, which, while historically effective, lack integration with modern computational methods to optimize structural performance, material efficiency, and environmental resilience. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to address critical challenges in wooden boatbuilding, including predictive analysis of hull integrity under dynamic loads, hydrodynamic efficiency optimization, and sustainable material selection. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution across complex wooden joinery and planking systems, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model hydrodynamic interactions of traditional hull designs, and machine learning algorithms to correlate historical construction data with long-term durability outcomes. These simulations will integrate 3D-scanned geometries of heritage vessels and parametric variations of modern hybrid designs, requiring parallel processing to manage iterative optimization tasks across millions of mesh elements and time-step resolutions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive frameworks for identifying failure-prone joints under climatic stressors, data-driven recommendations for material combinations balancing strength and sustainability, and hydrodynamic profiles reducing drag by 10–20% in common maritime conditions. By digitizing and extending traditional craftsmanship through computational validation, this work aims to advance the technical precision of wooden boatbuilding while preserving its cultural legacy. The project will also generate open-source simulation tools and case studies, enabling educators to train technicians in computational literacy, thereby fostering interdisciplinary innovation at the intersection of heritage techniques and modern engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to construct and repair traditional and modern wooden boats. Includes instruction in budgeting, drafting, fairing, lofting, joinery, planking, spars and rigging, and woodworking.

abstract: Psychiatric comorbidities in medically ill patients present complex diagnostic and treatment challenges due to the bidirectional interactions between physiological, psychological, and social factors. Current approaches often lack the capacity to integrate multi-system data at scale, limiting predictive accuracy and personalized intervention strategies. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to predict psychiatric outcomes and optimize treatment plans in consultation-liaison psychiatry. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze multimodal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomic profiles, and real-time biometric sensor data—from a cohort of 15,000 patients with comorbid psychiatric and medical conditions. Machine learning methods, such as graph neural networks and ensemble models, will be employed to identify dynamic risk factors, biomarker signatures, and treatment-response patterns across heterogeneous subpopulations. A federated learning framework will enable secure, cross-institutional data analysis while preserving patient privacy. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract psychosocial and symptom-related features from unstructured clinical notes. Computational simulations will model the systemic effects of psychiatric interventions on medical outcomes, such as hospital readmission rates or treatment adherence. The anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to stratify patients by risk of psychiatric decompensation during medical treatment, algorithms to recommend personalized pharmacotherapy regimens, and mechanistic insights into neuroimmune pathways linking chronic medical illness to depression and anxiety. This work will provide a scalable framework for integrating multi-omics and clinical data in consultation-liaison psychiatry, with direct applications in clinical decision support systems. By elucidating the computational drivers of psychiatric morbidity in medically complex populations, the project aims to advance precision psychiatry and reduce the burden of treatment-resistant symptoms in this vulnerable patient group.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of psychiatric disorders and symptoms in complex medically ill patients. This includes treatment of patients with acute or chronic medical, neurological, obstetrical, or surgical illness in which psychiatric illness is affecting their medical care and/or quality of life, and patients who have a psychiatric disorder that is the direct consequence of a primary medical condition, a somatoform disorder, or psychological factors affecting a general medical condition.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the transmission of Tibetan religious and cultural narratives across digital archives, with a focus on understudied texts produced in diaspora communities. While Tibetan Studies has increasingly engaged digital humanities methods, the scale and complexity of multilingual textual corpora—spanning classical Tibetan, modern vernaculars, and exile community publications—present computational challenges that exceed the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in doctrinal adaptation, lexical shifts, and cross-regional knowledge exchange within these texts, which are critical to understanding how Tibetan cultural identity is reconstituted in transnational contexts. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will apply transformer-based language models fine-tuned for classical Tibetan and Himalayan languages to perform semantic similarity analyses, temporal topic modeling, and network mapping of textual references across 15,000 digitized manuscripts, pamphlets, and periodicals. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing on GPU clusters to handle non-Latin script tokenization, low-resource language alignment, and sparse-data training scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for cross-temporal and cross-community textual analysis in Tibetan Studies, (2) quantitative evidence of narrative preservation versus innovation in post-1959 exile literature, and (3) open-access visualization tools mapping doctrinal linkages between pre-modern and contemporary sources. By enabling large-scale interrogation of cultural production mechanisms, this work will provide new empirical foundations for theorizing resilience in diasporic knowledge systems while directly supporting the preservation priorities of Tibetan archival institutions. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets and train domain-specific models that account for Tibetan Buddhism’s unique lexico-conceptual structures, which mainstream NLP tools frequently misrepresent.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: Cardiopulmonary dysfunction often presents as a complex interplay between cardiovascular and respiratory systems, yet existing diagnostic models frequently treat these systems in isolation, limiting predictive accuracy for patients with comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and concurrent heart failure. This project proposes the development of an integrated multiscale computational model to simulate cardiopulmonary interactions in real time, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the prohibitive computational demands of coupled hemodynamic and respiratory mechanics simulations. The research will utilize patient-specific data from echocardiography, pulmonary function tests, and arterial blood gas analyses to parameterize a hybrid model combining finite element analysis (FEA) for pulmonary tissue mechanics and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cardiovascular flow. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective clinical datasets to optimize model calibration and reduce runtime without sacrificing physiological fidelity. Key challenges include resolving time-scale disparities between cardiac pulsatility (milliseconds) and respiratory cycles (seconds) and ensuring robust data integration across heterogeneous clinical inputs. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution imaging data, iterative optimization of boundary conditions, and large-scale sensitivity analyses to identify critical biomarkers of decompensation. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for identifying patients at risk of acute cardiopulmonary failure and a framework for simulating interventions such as ventilator adjustments or inotropic drug responses. This work bridges a critical gap in personalized cardiopulmonary diagnostics, offering a platform for future clinical decision-support systems and advancing the mechanistic understanding of system-level interactions in complex disease states. The computational workflows developed here will be disseminated as open-source tools to foster collaboration in this emerging interdisciplinary niche.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to perform both cardiovascular and pulmonary diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Includes instruction in cardiopulmonary pharmacology; anatomy and physiology of the heart, peripheral vascular system, and lungs; pulmonary and cardiovascular disease and dysfunction; peripheral vascular Doppler procedures; invasive and non-invasive cardiology; pulmonary function tests; blood gas analysis; echocardiograph procedures; bronchoscopy; patient management; patient history taking and record-keeping; applications to clinical research; and emergency procedures.

abstract: Understanding the interplay between ecological dynamics and evolutionary processes across spatial and temporal scales is critical for predicting biodiversity responses to rapid environmental change. This project seeks to address how species interactions and dispersal limitations mediate adaptive evolution in fragmented landscapes under climate warming scenarios, using a combination of individual-based simulations and empirical data integration. Current models often oversimplify either ecological complexity or evolutionary mechanisms, limiting their predictive power. We propose developing a high-resolution, spatially explicit framework that couples eco-evolutionary dynamics with landscape genetics, parameterized using field data from montane plant communities in biodiversity hotspots. The computational approach will integrate agent-based population models with genomic-informed trait evolution algorithms, simulating >10^6 individuals across heterogeneous environments over 500-year horizons. Each simulation iteration requires tracking multi-trait selection gradients, gene flow between metapopulations, and stochastic disturbance events while maintaining genomic-resolution inheritance patterns. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core components: 1) Parallel execution of parameter sweeps across climate projection ensembles (CMIP6), 2) Bayesian calibration of hybrid models using fossil pollen records and contemporary range shift observations, and 3) Variance partitioning analysis of evolutionary versus ecological contributions to range dynamics. Expected outcomes include quantifying thresholds of climate velocity beyond which evolutionary rescue becomes unlikely, identifying landscape configurations that enhance adaptive capacity, and generating testable predictions about phylogenetic turnover patterns in warming mountain ecosystems. By bridging microevolutionary processes with macroecological patterns, this work will advance fundamental theory while providing actionable insights for conservation prioritization. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scaling of eco-evolutionary models to realistic landscape extents, establishing an open-source framework for predicting biodiversity responses to anthropogenic change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions across levels of biological organization--genes and genomes, organisms, species, and ecosystems--and how these change over time, including the origins and history of species, the processes by which biodiversity has evolved, and the ecological context in which this evolution takes place. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize mineral extraction processes and enhance safety protocols in underground mining environments using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. A critical challenge in mining technology is balancing operational efficiency with environmental and safety constraints, particularly when processing heterogeneous mineral deposits under dynamic geological conditions. Traditional physical testing and small-scale simulations often fail to account for the complex interplay of variables such as rock stress distribution, airflow dynamics, and real-time equipment performance. To address this, the research will employ 3D finite element modeling and discrete element method (DEM) simulations to replicate large-scale mining operations, integrating geological survey data, equipment sensor inputs, and historical incident datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to predict optimal blasting patterns, ventilation system configurations, and equipment deployment strategies, reducing energy consumption and mitigating collapse risks. Additionally, agent-based models will simulate emergency response scenarios to evaluate evacuation protocols under varying failure modes. The computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to handle high-resolution spatial datasets and stochastic uncertainty analyses, which are infeasible on local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for resource allocation during mine planning, dynamic risk assessment dashboards for operational oversight, and data-driven guidelines for regulatory compliance. By quantifying trade-offs between extraction rates, energy use, and safety margins, this work aims to advance sustainable practices in mineral processing while reducing the reliance on costly trial-and-error approaches. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the required scale, resolution, and statistical rigor for these simulations, directly supporting the program’s mission to integrate engineering principles with operational innovation in mining technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Emerging infectious diseases in livestock present significant threats to global food security and agricultural economies. Traditional experimental approaches to understanding host-pathogen interactions and transmission dynamics are often limited in scalability, particularly when analyzing complex genomic datasets or modeling multispecies epidemiological networks. This project proposes an integrative computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical gaps in predicting and mitigating zoonotic disease risks in veterinary populations. We will develop agent-based models to simulate disease spread across heterogeneous livestock populations, incorporating genomic, environmental, and husbandry variables derived from poultry and cattle production systems. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate structural variations in key viral fusion proteins associated with cross-species infectivity. These simulations will utilize existing whole-genome sequencing data from clinical isolates of avian influenza and bovine coronaviruses, requiring large-scale parallel processing to analyze evolutionary patterns across >10^6 genomic sequences. Machine learning pipelines will integrate multi-omics data (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) from infected hosts to identify biomarkers for early disease detection. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing petabyte-scale datasets, executing complex phylogenetic reconstructions, and training deep neural networks with >100 million parameters. Expected outcomes include predictive models of outbreak trajectories, novel insights into molecular determinants of host specificity, and computational tools for rapid risk assessment of emerging variants. This work will directly inform vaccine development strategies and biosecurity protocols, advancing veterinary clinical sciences through enhanced capacity to address 21st-century agricultural health challenges. By bridging computational innovation with applied veterinary medicine, the project aims to establish a paradigm shift in proactive disease management for livestock systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the systemic interplay of biological processes underlying multifactorial diseases through the development of integrative computational models. Despite advances in understanding individual biological components, there remains a critical gap in elucidating how dysregulations across diverse systems—such as metabolic, immune, and developmental pathways—coalesce to drive complex pathologies like autoimmune disorders or chronic inflammatory conditions. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture these multidimensional interactions, necessitating advanced computational frameworks. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to construct large-scale, dynamic models that synthesize heterogeneous datasets, including longitudinal clinical records, proteomic profiles, and population-level health data. These models will employ parallelized agent-based simulations and systems of differential equations to map cross-system signaling cascades and feedback loops under varying physiological conditions. Key computational challenges include optimizing scalability for real-time simulation of millions of interacting cellular agents and implementing adaptive algorithms to handle high-dimensional parameter spaces. By deploying these models on HPC clusters, we aim to identify emergent network behaviors and critical regulatory nodes that are inaccessible through reductionist methodologies. Expected outcomes include the discovery of previously unrecognized biomarkers predictive of disease progression and the prioritization of therapeutic targets that modulate system-wide stability rather than isolated pathways. This work will establish a scalable computational platform for hypothesis generation in multifactorial disease research, bridging gaps between molecular observations and clinical phenotypes. The requested resources will support iterative model refinement, validation against experimental datasets, and simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts, ultimately advancing translational strategies for personalized intervention in systemic diseases.
cip_definition: A general, program that focuses on the integrative scientific study of biological issues related to health and medicine, or a program in one or more of the biomedical sciences that is undifferentiated as to title. Includes instruction in any of the basic medical sciences at the research level; biological science research in biomedical faculties; and general studies encompassing a variety of the biomedical disciplines.

abstract: Cytotechnological analysis of cellular samples remains a critical yet labor-intensive component of early cancer detection, requiring manual microscopic evaluation of morphological features by trained professionals. While this approach is effective, it is inherently limited by inter-observer variability, processing delays, and the growing volume of screening demands in aging populations. This project proposes to develop an AI-driven computational framework to augment cytotechnologists’ workflow by automating the detection of pre-malignant and malignant cellular abnormalities in digitized cytology slides. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate deep learning models on a multi-institutional dataset of over 50,000 annotated whole-slide images of cervical, thyroid, and urinary tract specimens. Computational methods will include the implementation of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) optimized for patch-based analysis of high-resolution gigapixel images, with parallelized preprocessing pipelines for stain normalization, artifact removal, and multi-scale feature extraction. A key innovation will be the integration of spatial attention mechanisms to mimic cytotechnologists’ hierarchical inspection patterns, prioritizing regions of interest while maintaining diagnostic context. Model training will utilize distributed computing frameworks to manage memory-intensive operations, with iterative validation against pathologist-annotated ground truth and existing clinical outcomes data. Successful implementation is expected to yield a scalable decision-support tool that reduces slide review time by 30–40% while maintaining diagnostic accuracy above 98% compared to manual screening. The open-source release of optimized models and computational workflows will provide a foundation for future research in computational cytopathology, addressing workforce shortages and improving early detection rates for cancers with high prognostic sensitivity to timely diagnosis. This work directly aligns with national priorities in precision medicine and AI-driven healthcare innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with pathologists to detect changes in body cells that may indicate, and permit diagnosis of, the early development of cancers and other diseases. Includes instruction in biochemistry, microbiology, applied mathematics, microscopy, slide preparation, identification of cellular structures and abnormalities, and laboratory procedures and safety.

abstract: The increasing complexity of medical imaging data and the growing demand for rapid, accurate diagnostic support necessitate advanced computational tools tailored to radiologist assistants (RAs). This project seeks to develop a machine learning (ML) framework to enhance the efficiency and precision of RAs in analyzing cross-sectional imaging studies, such as CT and MRI, while integrating patient-specific clinical data. A critical challenge lies in processing high-resolution volumetric images and correlating them with heterogeneous datasets—including patient histories, lab results, and prior imaging—to generate actionable insights within clinically feasible timeframes. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models capable of simultaneous image segmentation, anomaly detection, and risk stratification. The computational workflow will involve three stages: (1) preprocessing multi-modal data (DICOM images, structured EHR entries) using GPU-accelerated pipelines to handle terabyte-scale datasets; (2) training 3D convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms to localize pathologies while accounting for anatomical variability; and (3) implementing ensemble models to predict diagnostic urgency based on fused imaging and clinical features. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive operations, hyperparameter optimization across thousands of concurrent trials, and validating models against multi-institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated ML pipeline that reduces time-to-preliminary-report generation by ≥40% compared to manual workflows, while maintaining diagnostic sensitivity >95% for critical findings. This resource will be integrated into a prototype decision-support platform for RAs, designed to prioritize cases, highlight relevant comparative imaging, and flag discrepancies in initial observations. By augmenting RA capabilities in initial image assessment and patient management, this research aims to improve workflow efficiency in radiology departments, reduce physician burnout, and ultimately enhance patient outcomes through earlier intervention. The developed models and computational strategies will be disseminated as open-source tools to support broader applications in medical imaging education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to perform patient assessment, patient management, selected imaging procedures and to make initial observations of diagnostic images. Includes instruction in radiologic procedures and techniques, cross sectional anatomy, pharmacology, pathophysiology, patient assessment, patient care and management, and radiation biology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and organizational principles governing cellular compartments during dynamic processes such as differentiation and stress response, with a focus on understanding how disruptions in spatial organization contribute to pathological states. A critical gap exists in mapping the 3D architecture of organelles and cytoskeletal networks in live cells under physiologically relevant conditions, particularly in the context of tissue-specific microenvironments. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline integrating high-resolution live-cell imaging datasets with physics-based modeling to simulate organelle interactions and cytoskeletal remodeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale 4D microscopy data (XYZ-time) acquired through lattice light-sheet imaging, followed by deep learning-based segmentation of membraneless organelles and mitochondria. Agent-based models will simulate force propagation during cytoskeletal rearrangements, while finite element analysis will predict mechanical stresses influencing organelle positioning. These computational approaches will be validated against experimental perturbations of microtubule dynamics and nuclear envelope integrity. The anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework linking subcellular spatial patterns to functional outcomes in epithelial and mesenchymal cell types, with direct relevance to tissue degeneration and fibrosis. By resolving how spatial misregulation of organelles impacts cellular homeostasis, this work will provide foundational insights into structural determinants of cell health, offering new avenues for targeting architectural vulnerabilities in disease. The developed tools will be shared as open-source packages to advance quantitative cell biology methodologies.
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cells, cellular systems, and the molecular basis of cell structure and function. Includes instruction in cell biology, cell chemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, and structural biology.

abstract: This project proposes a computational investigation into the linguistic and structural evolution of Jewish liturgical poetry (piyyutim) across medieval Mediterranean communities, integrating textual analysis with cultural history. While piyyutim served as central vehicles for theological and communal expression, their adaptation patterns remain understudied due to the scale of manuscripts, dialectal diversity in Hebrew/Aramaic hybrid texts, and nonlinear transmission paths. The research will develop machine learning models to analyze 8,000+ digitized piyyut texts from Cairo Genizah fragments and European manuscripts (8th–15th centuries), employing HPC resources for three parallel workflows: 1) neural OCR refinement of challenging Judeo-Arabic scribal hands using vision transformers, 2) multilingual semantic segmentation to disentangle Hebrew liturgical formulae from vernacular glosses and meta-commentary, and 3) phylogenetic network modeling of poetic meter variations correlated with diaspora migration routes. Custom transformer architectures will be trained to detect intertextual references to Talmudic vs. contemporary philosophical sources, testing hypotheses about liturgical acculturation. The computational pipeline requires large-scale GPU clusters for training domain-specific language models on non-standard Hebrew morphosyntax and CPU-intensive Monte Carlo simulations for textual phylogenetics. Outcomes will include the first comprehensive digital typology of piyyutim genres linked to historical contexts, a publicly accessible analysis toolkit for liturgical studies, and quantitative evidence reevaluating the role of women’s oral traditions in preserving poetic variants. This interdisciplinary methodology advances both Jewish cultural heritage preservation and computational humanities approaches to ritual texts, offering new paradigms for studying how liturgical forms negotiate religious authority and communal identity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as Rabbis. Includes instruction in Talmud, Halacha, Liturgy and Rituals, Rabbinical Thought, Jewish Ethics, Jewish Education, Pastoral Counseling and Homiletics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in agricultural business decision-making caused by fragmented and heterogeneous data streams. Modern agricultural operations generate vast datasets from precision farming sensors, supply chain logistics, market price fluctuations, and climate models, yet integrating these datasets for actionable insights remains computationally prohibitive for small-to-medium agribusinesses. Our research focuses on developing a scalable computational framework to unify these disparate data sources, enabling real-time analytics for crop yield optimization, cost forecasting, and risk mitigation. The proposed work combines machine learning (ML) models—including transformer-based architectures for time-series market data and convolutional neural networks for satellite imagery analysis—with agent-based simulations of agricultural supply chains. Key computational challenges include processing high-resolution geospatial datasets (10-100 TB scale), training multi-modal ML models with asynchronous data inputs, and simulating stochastic market-climate interactions across parametric scenarios. HPC resources are critical to parallelize model training, optimize hyperparameter searches, and run ensemble simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-source analytics platform tailored for agricultural cooperatives, validated against case studies in Midwestern U.S. soybean and livestock operations. This work will provide empirically grounded tools to improve resource allocation decisions, reduce operational waste, and enhance profitability for agribusinesses operating in climate-volatile regions. By quantifying the economic value of integrated data systems, the project also aims to inform policy incentives for technology adoption in underserved agricultural communities. The computational workflows developed will be documented for reuse in similar agricultural technology applications, fostering broader innovation in the sector.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized support functions related to agricultural business offices and operations and to operate agricultural office equipment, software, and information systems. Includes instruction in basic agricultural business principles, office management, equipment operation, standard software, and database management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, three-dimensional modeling framework to assess the long-term impacts of anthropogenic groundwater extraction on regional aquifer stability and land subsidence in sedimentary basin environments. The research problem centers on the urgent need to predict how prolonged groundwater depletion—driven by agricultural, industrial, and urban demands—interacts with heterogeneous subsurface geology to exacerbate soil compaction, infrastructure damage, and irreversible aquifer capacity loss. Current models lack the spatial granularity and computational scalability to resolve fine-scale lithological variations or simulate multi-decadal feedbacks between fluid dynamics and sediment mechanics. To address this gap, we propose a coupled hydrogeomechanical approach using finite element modeling (FEM) integrated with stochastic lithology distributions derived from borehole and geophysical datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations at basin scales (1–10 km resolution) while preserving meter-scale geological heterogeneity across 10^6–10^7 grid elements. Machine learning workflows will be implemented to optimize parameterization of sediment compressibility and hydraulic conductivity fields, reducing computational overhead. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of high-risk zones where subsurface heterogeneity amplifies subsidence rates, (2) probabilistic forecasts of aquifer degradation under climate and demand scenarios, and (3) open-source tools for regulatory agencies to evaluate sustainable extraction limits. By quantifying the coupled impacts of geological complexity and human activity on groundwater systems, this work will directly inform hazard mitigation strategies, water resource policies, and infrastructure resilience planning in vulnerable regions. The computational framework will also advance broader capabilities in environmental geosciences by enabling scalable, physics-based assessments of human-geosphere interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the environmental implications of geological processes and human activities on Earth. Includes instruction in environmental/natural resource management, geographic information systems (GIS), geology, hydrology, regulatory agency compliance, hazard identification and mitigation, environmental law, environmental policy, and sustainability studies.

abstract: Nuclear medicine faces critical challenges in optimizing radiopharmaceutical design, tracer kinetic modeling, and radiation dose quantification due to the complex interplay between molecular targeting, physiological variability, and stochastic radiation interactions. Current computational approaches often rely on simplified compartmental models or static anatomical phantoms, limiting their ability to capture patient-specific biodistribution patterns or predict therapeutic responses accurately. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating dynamic multiscale modeling of radiopharmaceutical transport, time-resolved Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations, and machine learning-driven parameter optimization. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated platforms to simulate tracer kinetics across vascular, tissue, and cellular scales while accounting for inter-patient anatomical variations derived from clinical PET/CT datasets. A key innovation involves coupling agent-based modeling of tumor microenvironment heterogeneity with full-body photon/particle transport to quantify dose-response relationships in targeted alpha therapy. The project will validate models against prospective clinical data from [Institution]'s radiopharmacy program, including time-activity curves from ⁶⁸Ga-PSMA and ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for personalized dosimetry, predictive biomarkers for treatment response in neuroendocrine tumors, and optimized radiopharmaceutical dosing protocols that minimize off-target radiation exposure. By enabling submillimeter-scale resolution in whole-body simulations with temporal sampling under one second, the requested HPC resources will address critical bottlenecks in modeling short-lived isotopes and rapid tracer redistribution. This work directly advances the clinical translation of novel theranostic agents while establishing computational nuclear medicine as a quantitative framework for precision radiopharmaceutical development.
cip_definition: Research focused on the tracer principle, most often with radiopharmaceuticals, to evaluate molecular, metabolic, physiologic and pathologic conditions of the body for the purposes of diagnosis, therapy and research. Includes instruction in tracer kinetics, the biologic effects of radiation exposure, the fundamentals of the physical sciences, and the principles and operation of radiation detection and imaging systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to elucidate the mechanisms underlying phenotypic plasticity and metabolic adaptation in therapy-resistant neoplasms, with a focus on solid tumors exhibiting paradoxical progression post-treatment. A critical gap persists in understanding how dynamic interactions between tumor cell populations, stromal components, and hypoxia-driven signaling networks drive pathological tissue remodeling. We propose an integrative computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and continuum-scale biophysical simulations to reconstruct evolving tumor microenvironments across clinically relevant timescales. The ABM framework will simulate individual cell decision-making processes—including proliferation, apoptosis, and metabolic state transitions—governed by intracellular oxygen tension, nutrient gradients, and paracrine signaling. Continuum models will then extrapolate these interactions to tissue-scale patterns of vascular collapse and necrosis. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the emergent behavior of >10^7 cellular agents while concurrently solving reaction-diffusion equations for oxygen, glucose, and lactate dynamics across millimeter-scale domains. Model parameters will be constrained by longitudinal histopathology data from murine xenograft models and clinical biopsy specimens. Expected outcomes include identification of spatial patterning rules that predict regions of latent treatment resistance and quantification of microenvironmental selection pressures driving aggressive phenotypic transitions. This multiscale approach will establish a predictive platform for evaluating stromal-targeted adjuvant therapies, directly addressing the program’s mission to connect molecular pathogenesis with tissue-level disease manifestations. The computational framework and validated models will be disseminated as modular, open-source tools for investigating organ-specific pathophysiological progression in experimental pathology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the expression, initiation, maintenance and progression of tissue injury and disease, including death, and the relationship of pathogenesis to fundamental molecular and cellular mechanisms. Includes instruction in immunology, microbiology, gene expression, inflammation, cell injury, apoptosis, immunopathology, molecular markers of disease and toxins, neoplasia, growth regulation, and organ- and system-specific investigations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive simulation framework for optimizing proactive policing strategies in urban environments. The research addresses the challenge of dynamically modeling crime patterns influenced by complex socio-spatial factors—such as transient demographics, infrastructure layouts, and real-time event data—which traditional analytical tools struggle to capture. By integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning techniques, the project aims to simulate interactions between civilian populations, law enforcement patrols, and environmental variables at city-scale resolution. The computational approach will utilize anonymized historical crime datasets, geospatial information systems (GIS) layers, and crowd-sourced incident reports to parameterize simulations, enabling the testing of hypothetical scenarios, including targeted patrol allocations, community engagement interventions, and emergency response protocols. HPC resources are critical to manage the high dimensionality of spatiotemporal data, execute parallelized simulations across varying urban contexts, and train deep reinforcement learning models to identify adaptive policing policies. Expected outcomes include a validated, open-source simulation platform for evaluating the long-term efficacy of crime prevention strategies under resource constraints, as well as actionable insights into balancing reactive enforcement with community trust-building measures. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational social science and criminal justice practice, offering a novel tool for law enforcement agencies to mitigate urban crime while addressing systemic biases in patrol deployment. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated through partnerships with municipal police departments and policy research institutes, prioritizing ethical AI frameworks to ensure transparency in algorithmic recommendations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing construction resource allocation and scheduling in large-scale building projects, with a focus on minimizing delays and cost overruns caused by supply chain variability and workforce availability. Current manual and rule-based approaches struggle to account for the dynamic interactions between material procurement, equipment logistics, labor productivity, and site-specific constraints such as weather or code compliance. To address this gap, the research will implement agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES) techniques to create a high-fidelity digital twin of construction workflows. The computational model will integrate real-world data streams from IoT sensors, supplier databases, and historical project records to simulate scenarios under uncertainty. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the parallel processing required for Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of potential resource allocation strategies across multiple project phases. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that predicts optimal material delivery schedules, equipment deployment patterns, and crew size configurations while maintaining compliance with safety standards and building codes. The research will validate the framework using case studies from mid-rise commercial construction projects, comparing simulated results against actual project timelines and budgets. Successful implementation could reduce average project delays by 15-20% through proactive risk mitigation, directly supporting the Construction Engineering Technology program's mission to advance data-driven construction management practices. This work will also establish a template for integrating computational modeling into construction education, enabling students to analyze complex resource allocation challenges through cloud-based HPC platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cytogenetic and molecular genetic data, driven by high-resolution imaging techniques and large-scale genomic sequencing, poses significant challenges for timely and accurate analysis in clinical diagnostics and research.
