Current workflows in cytogenetic technologies—such as fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), chromosomal microarray analysis, and karyotyping—generate vast datasets, including high-resolution photomicrographs and multidimensional genomic data. Conventional computational tools struggle to efficiently process, integrate, and interpret these data, limiting diagnostic precision and hindering research into genetic disorders, cancer genomics, and transplant compatibility. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy advanced computational pipelines tailored for cytogenetic and clinical genetic applications. The proposed work will focus on three areas: (1) optimizing machine learning models for automated detection of chromosomal abnormalities and structural variants in FISH and karyotype imaging data, (2) accelerating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and variant prioritization algorithms to identify pathogenic mutations in rare genetic diseases, and (3) simulating spatial interactions of chromosomal territories to predict genomic instability in cancer and post-transplant scenarios. Computational methods will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks, distributed processing of whole-genome sequencing data, and molecular dynamics simulations to model chromatin organization. Outcomes will include open-source tools for automated cytogenetic analysis, validated predictive models for clinical variant interpretation, and scalable workflows for integrating multi-omics data into diagnostic pipelines. By enhancing the resolution, speed, and reproducibility of genetic analyses, this work will directly support precision medicine initiatives, improve diagnostic turnaround times for malignancies and congenital disorders, and advance research into mechanisms of genomic rearrangements. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive tasks inherent to modern cytogenetics, ensuring clinically actionable results within feasible timeframes.
cip_title: Cytogenetics/ Genetics/ Clinical Genetics Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform analyses of the human genome and chromosomes for the research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes instruction in chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: The rapid evolution of computing demands necessitates innovative approaches to optimize hardware architectures for performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. Current challenges in computer hardware design—such as mitigating thermal bottlenecks, enhancing parallelism in multi-core processors, and improving reliability in emerging memory technologies—require computationally intensive modeling and simulation that surpass the capabilities of standard laboratory resources. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in next-generation computer hardware design, focusing on the development and validation of novel architectures for heterogeneous computing systems. The research will employ large-scale finite-element simulations to model thermal and electrical behaviors in advanced processor designs, coupled with discrete-event simulations to evaluate system-level performance under varying workloads. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be integrated to automate design optimization, enabling rapid exploration of parameter spaces for components such as cache hierarchies, interconnect fabrics, and near-memory computing units. The computational workflows will leverage parallel computing frameworks (e.g., MPI and OpenCL) to maximize resource utilization. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal configurations for reducing power consumption in high-density server processors, predictive models for failure rates in non-volatile memory systems, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated hardware benchmarks. These results will directly inform the design of energy-efficient data center infrastructure and edge computing devices, addressing critical gaps in sustainable technology development. By enabling large-scale, multi-physics simulations, the requested HPC allocation will accelerate the prototyping cycle for hardware innovations while reducing reliance on physical fabrication during early design stages. The project aligns with industry priorities for scalable computing solutions and will provide foundational insights for academic curricula in computer architecture and embedded systems engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens presents a critical challenge to global health, necessitating advanced approaches to unravel the molecular and ecological drivers of resistance. This project focuses on *Staphylococcus aureus*, a priority pathogen with rapidly evolving resistance mechanisms, to investigate how genetic variability and host-microbe interactions shape AMR trajectories. Traditional experimental methods are limited in capturing the dynamic interplay between microbial evolution, population heterogeneity, and immune system pressures. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of bacterial populations with multi-omics data analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of *S. aureus* populations under varied antibiotic regimens and host immune conditions, incorporating genomic diversity, gene expression dynamics, and metabolic constraints. Machine learning algorithms will identify key genetic signatures and regulatory networks associated with resistance emergence. Additionally, spatial models of biofilm formation will explore how microbial community structures influence resistance dissemination. This approach bridges molecular-scale mechanisms with population-level adaptation, providing a systems-level understanding of AMR. The expected outcomes include identifying high-risk genetic combinations predisposing to resistance, characterizing microenvironmental triggers of resistance gene transfer, and evaluating the efficacy of combination therapies. These insights will directly inform the development of targeted antimicrobial strategies and immune-modulating interventions, aligning with global health priorities to combat drug-resistant infections. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project addresses a critical bottleneck in AMR research, offering scalable methodologies applicable to other priority pathogens.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biological, social, and behavioral factors contributing to the cause and spread of infectious diseases. Includes instruction in research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, disease mechanisms, antimicrobial resistance, immunology, and bioterrorism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the systemic implications of evolving regulatory frameworks in global financial markets, with a focus on algorithmic compliance and risk modeling in securities law. As financial markets grow increasingly reliant on machine learning-driven trading systems and decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, regulators face challenges in anticipating cascading risks arising from complex, non-linear interactions between automated trading behaviors and fragmented legal jurisdictions. Traditional legal research methods lack the capacity to model these dynamics at scale, necessitating computational approaches to simulate market responses to regulatory interventions. The research will develop agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate real-world regulatory datasets—including SEC enforcement actions, EU Market Abuse Regulation filings, and cross-border merger filings—with synthetic market data to simulate how algorithmic trading systems adapt to proposed regulatory changes. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing (NLP) to parse regulatory texts and legal precedents into structured parameters for market simulations, followed by Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic outcomes. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, the project aims to quantify latent systemic risks in scenarios such as the introduction of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) or sudden shifts in antitrust enforcement priorities. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for stress-testing regulatory proposals against emergent market behaviors, with applications to compliance strategy optimization and legislative impact assessments. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational legal studies with financial mathematics, offering policymakers data-driven insights into the stability of regulatory ecosystems in an era of AI-driven finance. The scale of required computations—involving millions of agent interactions across heterogeneous regulatory environments—necessitates HPC resources to achieve statistically robust results within operationally relevant timeframes.
cip_title: Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law and process related to the regulation of businesses and the financial services industry. Includes instruction in corporate law, antitrust law, securities law and regulation, negotiation, incorporation, partnerships, trusts, and related topics

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial automation systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize their design, control, and reliability. Current simulation approaches for multi-domain systems—integrating programmable logic controllers (PLCs), hydraulic/pneumatic actuators, and sensor networks—often lack the scalability to model large-scale, real-time interactions between hardware and control algorithms. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity digital twin framework for industrial automation systems, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected challenges: (1) modeling the dynamic behavior of heterogeneous components (e.g., PLC logic, fluid power systems, robotic manipulators) under variable operating conditions, (2) optimizing control parameters to minimize energy consumption while maintaining system stability, and (3) predicting fault propagation across electromechanical subsystems. Computational methods will include parallelized finite element analysis for fluid-structure interactions in pneumatic circuits, discrete-event simulations for PLC code validation, and machine learning techniques to identify nonlinear relationships in sensor data streams. The HPC environment will allow simultaneous execution of multi-physics simulations at production-scale resolution, reducing reliance on physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include a modular simulation platform capable of emulating facility-wide automation systems, validated against experimental data from a pilot-scale manufacturing testbed. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing downtime in automated assembly lines and improving the sustainability of industrial processes through energy-aware control strategies. The resource request supports both algorithm development and large-scale parametric studies, with results disseminated through open-source tools and case studies tailored to workforce training in automation engineering. By bridging gaps between theoretical models and real-world system behavior, this project aims to advance the design and maintenance of next-generation automation infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, installing, calibrating, modifying and maintaining automated systems. Includes instruction in computer systems; electronics and instrumentation; programmable logic controllers (PLCs); electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control systems; actuator and sensor systems; process control; robotics; applications to specific industrial tasks; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing adaptive pedagogical strategies for International Baccalaureate (IB) classrooms, where educators must navigate diverse cultural, linguistic, and cognitive student backgrounds. While culturally responsive teaching frameworks exist, there is a critical gap in scalable tools to analyze and model the dynamic interplay of instructional methods, student engagement, and learning outcomes across global contexts. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop large-scale simulations of classroom interactions and train machine learning models on multimodal educational datasets. The computational approach will integrate three components: (1) agent-based modeling to simulate student-teacher interactions under varying cultural and pedagogical conditions, (2) natural language processing (NLP) of multilingual classroom discourse and IB curriculum materials, and (3) predictive analytics linking instructional strategies to longitudinal student performance data from IB schools worldwide. These methods require parallelized computation to process terabytes of anonymized classroom recordings, student assessments, and demographic metadata while preserving privacy standards. The simulations will test hypotheses about how specific teaching practices—such as translanguaging techniques or inquiry-based lesson structures—affect equitable participation and conceptual mastery in heterogeneous classrooms. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for optimizing IB-aligned pedagogy, actionable metrics for teacher self-reflection, and open-source tools to help educators visualize cultural biases in instructional materials. By enabling rapid analysis of cross-cultural educational dynamics that would otherwise require decades of classroom observation, this work aims to advance evidence-based teacher training for international schools while maintaining fidelity to IB’s mission of fostering intercultural understanding. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational complexity of modeling thousands of concurrent interaction variables and ensuring robust, generalizable results across educational contexts.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach in schools that are implementing or proposing to implement the International Baccalaureate curriculum. Includes instruction in culturally-responsive classrooms, cross-cultural awareness, foundations of international education, human learning, human development, international teaching and learning, and pedagogy.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in public resource allocation during large-scale social crises, such as natural disasters or pandemics, where equitable and rapid distribution of services is critical but often hindered by fragmented data systems and static planning models. Current approaches lack the dynamic computational tools needed to simulate complex, evolving scenarios involving intersecting variables like population mobility, resource availability, and real-time demand shifts. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an adaptive decision-support framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-agent interactions, optimize resource distribution networks, and predict service gaps under uncertainty. The project will employ a combination of agent-based modeling, graph theory, and machine learning techniques to analyze geospatial, demographic, and historical crisis response datasets. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data from municipal records, satellite imagery, and IoT-enabled supply chain sensors, enabling parallelized simulations of crisis scenarios across diverse urban and rural contexts. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for public agencies to (1) dynamically reroute emergency supplies based on real-time needs, (2) identify structural vulnerabilities in existing social service infrastructure, and (3) stress-test allocation policies against synthetic crisis trajectories. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with participatory governance principles, this work aims to advance evidence-based crisis management strategies while maintaining transparency in algorithmic decision-making. The resulting models and open-source simulation modules will be validated through partnerships with three regional emergency management agencies, offering transferable insights for improving equity in disaster response systems globally. This project underscores the transformative potential of computational social science in public administration, particularly in enhancing the adaptive capacity of institutions tasked with social service delivery during systemic shocks.
cip_title: Public Administration and Social Service Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public administration and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of spiritual resilience and interpersonal trust in non-clinical pastoral counseling contexts, an understudied area within Humanities-focused pastoral studies. While traditional pastoral care research relies on qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, this project addresses the computational complexity of modeling multilayered interactions between counselors, congregants, and community networks, particularly in culturally diverse or crisis-driven scenarios. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how spiritual narratives, emotional responses, and sociocultural factors co-evolve during counseling sessions, which existing analytical frameworks struggle to capture due to data dimensionality and nonlinear relationships. Using anonymized session transcripts, ethnographic field notes, and longitudinal congregational surveys (totaling ~15 TB of unstructured/textual data), we propose a hybrid computational approach combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of spiritual metaphors, agent-based modeling to simulate counselor-congregant dyads under stress scenarios, and network science to map how trust dynamics propagate through religious communities. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of cross-modal datasets, large-scale sentiment-temporal analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations testing intervention strategies across synthetic populations. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for quantifying spiritual resilience markers in pastoral interactions, 2) predictive models to optimize counselor training protocols for multicultural contexts, and 3) open-source tools enabling faith organizations to ethically implement computational social science methods. By bridging pastoral theology, counseling psychology, and computational humanities, this work aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for evaluating the efficacy of non-clinical spiritual care while demonstrating HPC's transformative potential in under-resourced Humanities domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and principles of pastoral care and prepares ordained clergy to provide non-clinical pastoral counseling to individuals and groups. Includes instruction in pastoral leadership, counseling psychology; crisis intervention; individual and group procedures; theological and spiritual counseling; pastoral care; and applications to specific types of ministry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize decision-making processes for equitable resource allocation in urban K-12 school systems. Urban educational leaders face complex challenges in distributing limited resources—such as funding, personnel, and programmatic support—across schools with divergent needs, often under dynamic socioeconomic and demographic conditions. Traditional analytical methods struggle to account for the multidimensional interactions between policy variables, community needs, and systemic inequities. To address this gap, the project will develop a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate resource allocation scenarios across diverse urban school districts. The ABM component will represent stakeholders (e.g., administrators, teachers, students, families) and their behavioral patterns, while ML algorithms will analyze historical equity outcomes and predict the impacts of allocation strategies under varying constraints (e.g., budget fluctuations, shifting enrollment, policy mandates). Large-scale datasets from public school systems, including student performance metrics, funding histories, and community health indices, will be processed to parameterize models. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational intensity of parallel simulations, which will evaluate thousands of allocation permutations to identify strategies that maximize equity and academic outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for urban educational leaders, enabling data-driven prioritization of resources to schools and student subgroups most affected by systemic disparities. The project aligns with the program’s focus on urban educational leadership by bridging computational innovation with practical strategies for addressing inequity, ultimately contributing to frameworks for justice-oriented administrative practices in metropolitan contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on issues and problems specific to the educational needs of populations and communities located in metropolitan, inner city, and related areas and prepares individuals to provide educational services and administrative leadership in urban contexts. Includes instruction in multicultural education, at-risk studies, urban sociology, multilingual education, urban studies and planning, human services, health services and nutrition, cross-cultural communication, diversity studies, safety and security, and urban educational administration and leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address interdisciplinary questions about the development and interaction of ancient civilizations through large-scale spatial, environmental, and cultural datasets. A key challenge in Ancient Studies is synthesizing fragmented archaeological records, climatic reconstructions, and textual sources to model how environmental pressures, resource distribution, and trade networks shaped societal trajectories across regions such as the Mediterranean, Mesopotamia, and the Indus Valley. Current methodologies often lack the computational capacity to integrate multi-modal datasets—including LiDAR surveys, sediment core analyses, epigraphic corpora, and artifact distributions—at the spatiotemporal resolutions required to test complex hypotheses about cross-cultural exchange or collapse dynamics. This project will employ geospatial agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques to simulate human-environment interactions over millennial scales, incorporating paleoclimate proxies, hydrologic data, and archaeological site distributions. Parallelized computation will enable parameter sweeps across hypothesized variables such as agricultural productivity thresholds, trade route viability, and demographic carrying capacities. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to analyze multilingual ancient texts (e.g., cuneiform tablets, Linear B inscriptions) for semantic patterns linked to material culture shifts. The HPC environment is critical for managing terabyte-scale datasets, running iterative simulations, and training transformer models on low-resource ancient languages. Expected outcomes include 1) reconstructions of decision-making processes in ancient resource management, 2) identification of understudied climatic or economic catalysts for cultural change, and 3) open-access tools for aligning textual and archaeological chronologies. By bridging computational scalability gaps in traditional humanities methods, this work aims to establish new frameworks for analyzing antiquity’s “big data,” with implications for heritage preservation and comparative civilizational studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Western and Non-Western cultures and related topics in the periods of Pre-history and Antiquity. Includes such disciplines as ancient languages, archeology, history, art history, geography, population studies, environmental studies, religious studies, and the social sciences.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) necessitates scalable, evidence-based strategies for designing personalized educational interventions. Current approaches to developing individualized education plans (IEPs) for students with autism rely heavily on manual observation and trial-and-error adjustments, which are time-intensive and lack predictive precision. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model learning behaviors and predict optimal intervention strategies for students with ASD, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale data synthesis and real-time analytics. The research problem centers on bridging the gap between heterogeneous behavioral data—drawn from classroom interactions, sensory processing assessments, and communication logs—and actionable pedagogical recommendations. We will employ machine learning techniques, including multimodal deep learning and reinforcement learning, to analyze longitudinal datasets encompassing video recordings, biometric sensor outputs, and academic performance metrics from 500+ students across diverse educational settings. Computational models will be trained to identify patterns in skill acquisition trajectories, sensory overload triggers, and social communication barriers, with parallelized simulations testing hypothetical intervention scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-dimensional data (e.g., 30,000+ hours of annotated video), optimizing hyperparameters across neural architectures, and running ensemble models that integrate domain knowledge from special education frameworks. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to recommend IEP components with quantified success probabilities, (2) generative models of student-teacher interaction dynamics to inform adaptive teaching strategies, and (3) open-source code for behavior pattern recognition tailored to low-resource school districts. By computationally encoding evidence-based practices in autism education, this work aims to empower educators with data-driven decision-support systems, ultimately improving the scalability and efficacy of specialized instruction for neurodiverse learners.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance molecular pharmacology research by elucidating the mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions at atomic resolution. A critical challenge in drug discovery lies in predicting how small molecules dynamically engage with target proteins, particularly G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and ion channels, which mediate diverse physiological responses. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve transient binding intermediates or allosteric modulation events that dictate drug efficacy and selectivity. To address this, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations paired with enhanced sampling techniques to map free-energy landscapes of ligand binding, conformational changes in receptor activation, and the impact of genetic variants on drug response. These simulations will integrate structural data from cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography to model full-length receptors in membrane-embedded systems, capturing lipid interactions and solvent effects critical to pharmacological activity. Additionally, virtual screening of >1 million compounds against dynamic receptor conformations will identify novel leads with improved specificity. The computational workflow will employ free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to refine binding affinity predictions and machine learning models trained on simulation-derived features to classify off-target risks. This project directly addresses unmet needs in rational drug design by revealing molecular determinants of biased signaling and polypharmacology, with applications to cardiovascular and neurological therapies. Successful execution requires HPC resources to manage the petabytes of trajectory data generated and the parallelized processing of quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations. Outcomes will include predictive frameworks for optimizing drug-receptor kinetics, reducing attrition in preclinical development, and guiding personalized therapeutic strategies based on patient-specific receptor variants. The work aligns with molecular pharmacology’s focus on therapeutic innovation through mechanistic insights into drug action at the molecular scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biochemical and biophysical characteristics of drugs at the molecular level and their interaction with, and effects on, biological macromolecules and cellular structures and processes. Includes instruction in molecular biology and biophysics; pharmacology of signal transduction, transmitters, and protein synthesis and release; receptors, protein interaction and binding; drug discovery and recognition; molecular toxicology; drug design; pharmacodynamics; developmental genetics; and studies of therapeutic strategies.

abstract: Emergent phenomena in biological systems arise from complex interactions across organizational scales, yet integrative computational frameworks to study these dynamics remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a multiscale modeling platform to investigate how organismal physiology interfaces with population-level ecological processes under environmental stressors. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models that simulate individual physiological responses (e.g., metabolic adaptation, stress signaling) alongside collective behaviors influencing population resilience. The computational framework will integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning physiological time-series, environmental gradients, and demographic trends, requiring scalable architectures for parallelized parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses. Key challenges include resolving feedback loops between individual adaptive mechanisms and group-level survival outcomes under dynamic resource availability. By employing GPU-accelerated simulations and machine learning-driven pattern detection, the project aims to identify critical thresholds and nonlinear dependencies governing system stability. Expected outcomes include predictive models of stress propagation across biological scales, validated against empirical data from model organisms in controlled ecosystems. This work will advance interdisciplinary methodologies in systems biology, providing tools to anticipate cascading effects of environmental change on biodiversity. The requested HPC allocation will enable computationally intensive iterations essential for robust statistical inference and the exploration of high-dimensional parameter spaces, which are intractable on conventional systems.
cip_title: Integrative/ Interdisciplinary Biology, Biosciences, and Biomedical Sciences
cip_definition: A program that crosses multiple specializations within the biological and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in general biological research and variety of specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of relational dynamics in therapeutic contexts, specifically within Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT). Traditional MFT research relies heavily on qualitative analysis or small-scale quantitative studies, limiting the ability to model complex, nonlinear interactions within family systems or predict long-term outcomes of therapeutic interventions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), multilevel agent-based modeling (ABM), and network analysis to analyze longitudinal therapy session transcripts and simulate family interaction patterns. The research problem centers on identifying critical thresholds in communication dynamics that correlate with therapeutic success or relapse, particularly in cases involving intergenerational trauma or chronic mental health conditions. Using anonymized session datasets (audio transcripts and clinician notes) from a multi-site cohort study, NLP pipelines will extract semantic, emotional, and relational features, while ABM simulations will map how micro-level interactions propagate through family networks over time. Computational demands include training transformer-based models for context-aware dialogue analysis, running ensemble simulations to account for psychosocial variability, and optimizing graph neural networks to detect latent relational patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model of intervention efficacy based on early-session communication features, (2) a generative toolkit for clinicians to explore "what-if" scenarios in treatment planning, and (3) novel metrics for quantifying resilience in family systems. By bridging computational social science with clinical practice, this work aims to establish an evidence base for personalized, data-informed MFT strategies while addressing scalability challenges in relational health research. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high dimensionality of interaction data, enabling real-time simulation of complex adaptive systems, and ensuring reproducibility across diverse demographic subgroups.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of marriage and family therapy, involving the diagnosis of cognitive, affective, and behavioral domain disorders, both mental and emotional, within the context of marriage and family systems and the application of short- and long-term therapeutic strategies in family group contexts. Includes instruction in psychotherapy, family systems and studies, small group intervention and therapy, marital problems, depression, identification of psychopathologies and behavioral disorders, holistic health care, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in translating complex human sciences concepts into accessible, evidence-based communication strategies for diverse audiences. Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) communication bridges technical subject matter—such as nutrition science, financial literacy, and family dynamics—with public-facing media, yet existing tools lack the capacity to model how heterogeneous audiences process multimodal information across evolving digital platforms. The research problem centers on optimizing message design and delivery by analyzing large-scale, unstructured datasets (e.g., social media interactions, multimedia content, and user engagement metrics) to identify patterns in comprehension gaps, cultural biases, and behavioral outcomes. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to dissect semantic structures in FCS content, network analysis to map information diffusion pathways, and agent-based modeling to simulate audience responses under varying media formats and sociocultural contexts. These approaches require HPC resources to manage the volume and velocity of data, parallelize sentiment and thematic analyses across multilingual corpora, and iteratively train machine learning models to predict engagement efficacy. Expected outcomes include a framework for dynamically adapting FCS messaging to align with audience needs, literacy levels, and platform-specific behaviors, thereby enhancing the reach and impact of consumer education initiatives. The project also aims to establish scalable computational workflows for real-time feedback integration, enabling practitioners to refine campaigns proactively. By advancing the methodological toolkit for human sciences communication, this work addresses a critical gap in non-STEM domains reliant on data-driven public outreach, with implications for improving health equity, economic resilience, and intergenerational knowledge transfer in underserved communities.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Communication
cip_definition: A program that focuses on communication of human sciences subject matter and related consumer information to a variety of audiences through print and non-print media.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize clinical workflows and improve diagnostic accuracy in dental assisting through advanced analysis of dental radiographs and patient care data. Despite the critical role of dental assistants in managing radiography and patient preparation, current protocols for interpreting imaging data and predicting procedural outcomes rely heavily on manual, time-intensive methods. This limits scalability and introduces variability in clinical decision-making. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on large-scale datasets of dental radiographs, patient histories, and procedural outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automate the detection of common pathologies—such as caries, periodontal bone loss, and impacted teeth—from radiographic images, alongside natural language processing (NLP) models to extract insights from unstructured clinical notes. A key innovation involves simulating real-world dental clinic environments via agent-based modeling to identify bottlenecks in patient flow and resource allocation, enabling data-driven optimization of scheduling and equipment use. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of high-resolution imaging data, running parallelized model training, and performing iterative simulations under diverse clinic configurations. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for rapid radiograph analysis, predictive models to guide pre-operative patient preparation, and evidence-based recommendations for clinic workflow improvements. By enhancing the precision and efficiency of dental assisting tasks, this research aims to reduce procedural delays, improve patient outcomes, and inform educational curricula for dental assistants. The project will collaborate with three regional dental clinics to validate models against real-world data, ensuring translational relevance to the health professions community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide patient care, take dental radiographs (x-ray photographs), prepare patients and equipment for dental procedures, and discharge office administrative functions under the supervision of dentists and dental hygienists. Includes instruction in medical record-keeping, general office duties, reception and patient intake, scheduling, equipment maintenance and sterilization, basic radiography, pre- and post-operative patient care and instruction, chairside assisting, taking tooth and mouth impressions, and supervised practice.

abstract: The dynamical evolution of small-body populations in the outer solar system remains poorly understood, particularly the origins of resonant Kuiper Belt objects (KBOs) and their relationship to Neptune’s migration history. Current models struggle to reconcile the observed orbital distributions of resonant KBOs with proposed planetary migration scenarios, limiting our ability to reconstruct the solar system’s dynamical past. This project seeks to address this gap by conducting high-resolution N-body simulations of Neptune’s migration and its gravitational interactions with primordial KBOs. We will employ the REBOUND code with the WHFast integrator to model the solar system’s evolution over 100 Myr timescales, incorporating constraints from recent observational surveys and varying parameters such as migration speed, planetary eccentricities, and initial disk conditions. These simulations require high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the need for fine temporal resolution, large particle counts (>10^5 test particles), and ensemble runs to quantify statistical outcomes. Additionally, we will implement Monte Carlo methods to assess collisional probabilities within the migrating disk, providing insights into the role of fragmentation in shaping present-day KBO size distributions. The expected outcomes include a refined timeline of Neptune’s migration, predictions for the orbital architecture of undiscovered resonant populations, and constraints on the primordial trans-Neptunian disk’s mass and structure. Results will directly inform the interpretation of data from upcoming observational campaigns (e.g., Rubin Observatory) and missions to KBOs, while advancing computational techniques for simulating gravitational many-body systems. This work will bridge critical gaps in planetary formation theory and enhance our understanding of how giant planet dynamics sculpted the solar system’s small-body reservoirs. Successful completion of this project relies on access to HPC resources for parallelized simulations, large-scale data storage, and post-processing workflows, which are unavailable on local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the acoustical properties of woodwind instruments, with a focus on optimizing performance techniques and instrument design. While traditional pedagogical methods for woodwind performance emphasize empirical practice and subjective feedback, the complex interactions between airflow, mechanical resonance, and player biomechanics remain poorly quantified. Current challenges include predicting how subtle variations in embouchure, finger technique, or instrument geometry affect tonal quality, intonation, and dynamic control. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate air-column vibrations, pressure distributions, and energy transfer within instrument bodies under performance conditions. High-resolution 3D scans of instruments (e.g., clarinet, oboe) will inform geometrically accurate models, while motion-capture data of performer interactions will parameterize boundary conditions. Machine learning algorithms will then identify patterns linking computational outputs to perceptual audio metrics derived from professional performance recordings. The scale of these simulations—requiring millions of mesh elements and iterative solvers for transient multiphysics problems—necessitates parallelized HPC workflows. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models to guide pedagogical strategies for embouchure development, quantitative frameworks for evaluating instrument modifications, and data-driven insights into historical performance practices. By bridging computational engineering and performing arts, this work aims to establish reproducible methodologies for studying woodwind acoustics, offering conservatories and instrument makers tools to enhance artistic training and design innovation. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated computations, large-scale data storage for time-series simulations, and collaborative visualization platforms for interdisciplinary analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a woodwind instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and historical narratives of the African diaspora in North America and the Caribbean through large-scale textual and spatial analysis. Despite rich archival holdings of African-American literature, newspapers, slave narratives, and oral histories, traditional humanities methods struggle to systematically analyze patterns across vast, multilingual corpora or map transnational intellectual networks over time. Our research addresses this gap by employing computational text mining, natural language processing (NLP), and geospatial modeling to interrogate three interconnected problems: (1) the evolution of resistance rhetoric in Black literary and political texts from the 19th century to the present; (2) the circulation of abolitionist ideologies between Caribbean, U.S., and Canadian communities; and (3) the relationship between migratory patterns and cultural production in diaspora communities. Datasets include digitized archives from the Schomburg Center, the Caribbean Newspaper Digital Library, and the Early Caribbean Digital Archive, alongside georeferenced maps of historical migration routes. Computational workflows will apply transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) for semantic analysis of themes like liberation and belonging, network analysis tools (Gephi, NetworkX) to trace transnational publishing linkages, and spatial-temporal visualization (QGIS, Kepler.gl) to correlate demographic shifts with literary output. The scale of data (10+ TB of unstructured text and images) and complexity of training custom multilingual NLP models necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of diaspora intellectual history, annotated corpora highlighting underrepresented voices, and computational frameworks for analyzing intersectional identity in historical contexts. This work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of diasporic cultural resilience while establishing scalable methodologies for humanities-centered HPC applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: Understanding the evolutionary origins of complex behavioral phenotypes requires integrating neurophysiological mechanisms with species-specific ecological pressures. This project investigates how social learning strategies diverge across phylogenetically distinct species, with a focus on identifying conserved and derived neural circuits underlying these behaviors. A key challenge lies in modeling dynamic interactions between genetic, neurophysiological, and environmental variables at evolutionary timescales—a task demanding computational resources beyond standard laboratory infrastructure. We propose a multi-scale computational approach combining agent-based modeling of population-level behavioral dynamics with machine learning analysis of cross-species neuroimaging datasets. Agent-based simulations will incorporate empirical data on synaptic plasticity, dopaminergic reinforcement mechanisms, and ecological constraints to test hypotheses about adaptive value in different social learning strategies. Concurrently, deep neural networks will process comparative fMRI datasets from primates, corvids, and cetaceans to identify conserved functional connectivity patterns associated with social information processing. Phylogenetic comparative methods will then map these neural and behavioral traits onto evolutionary trees. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage 1) large-scale parameter space exploration in evolutionary simulations (10⁶+ agent generations), 2) three-dimensional convolutional neural network training on multispecies neuroimaging repositories (>500 TB), and 3) Bayesian phylogenetic inference across behavioral-neural trait matrices. Expected outcomes include a computational framework linking neurophysiological adaptations to macroevolutionary patterns in social cognition, with implications for comparative neuropsychology and evolutionary reinforcement learning theory. By characterizing how natural selection operates on brain-behavior relationships, this work aims to establish predictive models of cognitive evolution while advancing methodology for cross-species neuroscience research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the behavior of members of particular species or groups and the relationship of the behaviors of the species or group to their evolutionary origins. Includes instruction in differential psychology, experimental and physiological psychology, psychopharmacology, psychology of individual differences, reinforcement theory, and neurophysiology.

abstract: Occupational therapy interventions often rely on personalized, contextually rich activities to improve functional outcomes, yet current methods for predicting patient-specific motor learning trajectories or optimizing task complexity remain limited by static clinical models. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate sensorimotor learning processes during occupation-based interventions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic interactions between individual biomechanical constraints, task demands, and neural plasticity. The research problem centers on the inability of traditional assessment tools to capture real-time adaptive behaviors in variable environments, which hinders the design of precision interventions for patients with neuromotor impairments. Using motion capture data from occupational therapist assistant-led sessions, we will train agent-based models to replicate patient interactions with adaptive tasks (e.g., virtual reality simulations of daily activities). HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds for task progression and fatigue management across diverse patient phenotypes. A hybrid approach combining mechanistic neural network models and reinforcement learning will simulate how motor strategies evolve under different therapeutic scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool to recommend task modifications based on real-time performance metrics, validated against clinical data from stroke survivors undergoing upper extremity rehabilitation. The computational platform will also generate synthetic datasets to train occupational therapy assistants in recognizing subtle markers of skill acquisition or compensatory behaviors. By bridging computational neuroscience and rehabilitation science, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for dynamically adaptive intervention design, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice while providing a scalable infrastructure to study motor learning principles in health sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of precision tools and safety protocols within the nail technician industry—a specialized, practice-driven field intersecting cosmetology, material science, and microbiology. Current practices in nail care rely on empirical knowledge and standardized protocols, yet lack robust computational frameworks to address emerging challenges such as microbial contamination risks, long-term durability of nail coatings, and ergonomic tool design. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study analyzing (1) the biomechanical interactions between nail coatings (e.g., gels, acrylics) and natural nail substrates under varying environmental conditions, and (2) the efficacy of sanitation practices against fungal and bacterial pathogens in salon settings. Molecular dynamics simulations will model adhesive and stress behaviors of coatings, incorporating humidity, temperature, and mechanical wear variables. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate microbial survival and transmission under different sterilization workflows. High-resolution finite element analysis will further evaluate strain distribution in natural nails during filing procedures to optimize tool geometries. These simulations require HPC resources due to the multi-scale complexity of interactions (atomic-level material properties to macro-level tool dynamics) and the need for iterative, parameter-rich scenario testing. Outcomes will yield data-driven guidelines for coating formulations, sanitation protocols, and ergonomic tool adjustments, reducing occupational hazards for technicians and improving client outcomes. By integrating computational rigor into a traditionally practice-based domain, this project establishes a novel framework for evidence-driven innovation in cosmetology, with potential spillover applications to dermatology and biomedical device design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the emergence and evolution of legal norms in decentralized digital ecosystems, such as blockchain networks and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). As these systems operate outside traditional jurisdictional boundaries, they present novel challenges in understanding how self-governing communities develop enforceable rules without centralized legal authority. The research will employ large-scale network analysis and agent-based modeling to map decision-making patterns across distributed ledger transactions and on-chain governance protocols. Machine learning techniques will be applied to a curated dataset of 10+ million smart contract interactions and community governance proposals to identify recurrent conflict resolution strategies and consensus-forming behaviors. The computational models will simulate how pseudo-legal frameworks emerge from repeated interactions, incorporating game-theoretic principles to assess stability under varying economic incentives. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of decentralized governance archetypes, predictive metrics for detecting systemic vulnerabilities in self-executing legal agreements, and a benchmarking tool for evaluating compliance with hybrid (digital-traditional) legal standards. By requiring simultaneous processing of cryptographic transaction logs, natural language governance debates, and cross-chain metadata, the project demands high-performance computing resources capable of maintaining sub-second latency during complex event processing across petabyte-scale datasets. This work aims to establish foundational computational methods for studying algorithmic legal systems while providing practical tools for regulators and developers operating in Web3 environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of law, for taking state and national bar examinations, and for advanced research in jurisprudence. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of the legal system, including the statutory, administrative, and judicial components of civil and criminal law.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze patterns in large-scale health insurance claims data, with the goal of identifying systemic inefficiencies, potential fraud, and disparities in claims processing. The increasing complexity of medical claims—driven by evolving regulations, heterogeneous data sources, and sophisticated fraudulent tactics—requires advanced analytical tools beyond traditional manual review. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets encompassing structured claims records, unstructured clinical notes, and regulatory documents. Our approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to extract features from textual data, graph analytics to map provider-patient interaction networks, and machine learning models to classify anomalous claims. Parallelized workflows will be implemented to handle federated data across distributed storage systems while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy standards. The computational pipeline will also simulate regulatory scenarios to assess the impact of policy changes on claims adjudication efficiency. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for real-time claims evaluation, predictive models to flag high-risk cases for audit, and evidence-based insights into regulatory bottlenecks. This work directly aligns with the Health/Medical Claims Examiner program’s emphasis on analytical rigor, ethical oversight, and regulatory adherence. By enabling rapid analysis of claims at scale, the project aims to reduce administrative costs, enhance fraud detection accuracy, and support equitable access to care. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing memory-intensive graph traversals, training deep learning models on heterogeneous data, and ensuring reproducibility across diverse insurance ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized investigatory, analytical, evaluative, and consultative functions related to health/medical insurance operations and their regulation. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes and procedures, health insurance law and regulations, health care industry law, record-keeping, analytic and investigatory techniques, evaluation methods, field operations methods, office procedures, related software applications, oral and written communications skills, interviewing techniques, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the neural and computational mechanisms underlying language recovery in individuals with post-stroke aphasia. Aphasia, a communication disorder caused by brain damage, disrupts speech, comprehension, and social interaction, yet recovery trajectories remain poorly understood due to the complex interplay of neuroplasticity, lesion characteristics, and behavioral factors. Current clinical tools lack the precision to predict recovery or optimize personalized rehabilitation, highlighting a critical gap in both scientific and translational domains. To address this, we propose a computational modeling framework integrating multimodal neuroimaging (fMRI, DTI), longitudinal behavioral data, and machine learning (ML) to map dynamic brain-network reorganization and its relationship to language outcomes. Large-scale datasets from 200+ participants—including structural/functional brain scans, speech samples, and cognitive assessments—will be analyzed using deep learning architectures (3D CNNs, graph neural networks) to identify biomarkers of recovery. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will quantify syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic features in patient speech, enabling fine-grained correlations with neural connectivity patterns. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of neuroimaging data, training computationally intensive ML models, and running parallelized simulations of lesion-induced network disruptions. Expected outcomes include predictive models of recovery trajectories, data-driven stratification of patient subtypes, and the development of open-source tools for clinicians to tailor therapies based on individual neural profiles. This work will significantly advance the understanding of neuroplasticity in aphasia, bridge gaps between computational neuroscience and clinical practice, and establish scalable methodologies for future studies in communication disorders. By harnessing HPC capabilities, the project aims to transform aphasia rehabilitation into a precision medicine paradigm, ultimately improving quality of life for affected individuals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate complex household decision-making dynamics under economic stress, a critical yet underexplored area within Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Traditional studies in FCS rely on survey-based or qualitative methods, which struggle to model the nonlinear interactions of financial, social, and psychological factors shaping resource allocation decisions in families. The research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate multi-agent household systems, integrating behavioral economics, psychosocial stressors, and real-world economic datasets. The primary objective is to model how households prioritize competing needs—such as healthcare, education, nutrition, and debt management—during prolonged economic instability, such as that induced by global crises or localized recessions. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques, the project will simulate decision trees influenced by variables including income volatility, cultural norms, policy interventions, and intergenerational resource transfer. HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize simulations across diverse demographic profiles, and validate models against longitudinal datasets from public health and economic databases. Expected outcomes include identifying resilience strategies adopted by households in different socioeconomic contexts, quantifying the cascading effects of delayed financial decisions, and generating predictive insights into crisis-driven behavioral shifts. The results will inform policymakers and FCS practitioners in designing targeted interventions to mitigate economic vulnerability. Additionally, the project aims to establish a scalable computational methodology for human sciences, bridging gaps between empirical social research and data-driven systems modeling. By advancing the use of HPC in non-traditional domains, this work will demonstrate the transformative potential of computational social science in addressing real-world challenges at the intersection of family well-being and economic sustainability.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of climate-driven shifts in vector-pathogen coevolution dynamics in understudied tropical arboviruses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex biological and environmental interactions. Emerging arboviral diseases in tropical regions—such as Oropouche virus and Mayaro virus—are increasingly linked to climate variability, yet the mechanisms driving pathogen adaptation within mosquito vectors under changing thermal and hydrological conditions remain poorly characterized. Current models lack granularity in integrating genomic, entomological, and microclimatic data at spatiotemporal scales relevant to transmission hotspots. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining agent-based modeling of vector population dynamics with machine learning-driven phylogenetic prediction. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10^6+ mosquito cohorts under projected climate scenarios, incorporating high-resolution temperature and precipitation data from regional Earth system models. Concurrently, we will apply Bayesian inference and neural networks to analyze time-series viral genomic datasets (∼50 TB) from field isolates, identifying signatures of thermal adaptation in structural proteins and untranslated regions. This dual approach will quantify how temperature fluctuations alter viral mutation rates in vectors and modulate transmission efficiency. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of arboviral emergence risks under IPCC climate pathways and mechanistic insights into thermal tolerance thresholds for viral replication in *Culicidae* vectors. The work directly supports targeted surveillance and the design of thermostable vaccines, addressing critical gaps in tropical disease resilience. By bridging computational genomics, ecological modeling, and climate science, this project establishes a template for interdisciplinary research on climate-sensitive zoonoses, with deliverables aligned with global health priorities for neglected tropical diseases.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of syntactic and morphological variation across understudied Germanic dialects, with a focus on Low German (Plattdeutsch) and Frisian varieties. While historical and comparative Germanic linguistics has long relied on manual textual analysis, the increasing digitization of regional archives, oral histories, and dialect dictionaries presents an opportunity—and challenge—to systematically analyze patterns of language change, contact, and divergence at unprecedented scales. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict researchers to small corpora or simplified models, neglecting complex interdependencies between phonological shifts, syntactic structures, and sociolinguistic factors. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid computational pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) tools optimized for non-standardized orthographies, transformer-based models for diachronic feature extraction, and graph-based network analyses to map cross-dialectal influences. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale multilingual corpora spanning 19th- to 21st-century texts, phonetic transcriptions, and speaker metadata. Key outcomes will include 1) a probabilistic atlas of syntactic isoglosses in Northwestern Germanic varieties, 2) quantitative models tracing the diffusion of morphological innovations under language contact scenarios, and 3) open-access tools for dialectometric analysis adaptable to other minority languages. By bridging computational methods with philological expertise, this work aims to redefine the scale at which linguistic variation can be studied while preserving the granularity required for rigorous historical reconstruction. The resource demands—particularly for GPU-accelerated training of custom tokenizers and runtime-intensive phylogenetic simulations—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve these objectives within a humanities research framework typically constrained by local computing limitations.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Germanic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Germanic languages of Western, Central, and Northern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing the design and operational efficiency of next-generation autonomous systems in dynamic environments, with a focus on applications in robotics, smart infrastructure, and precision agriculture. Current approaches to modeling these systems face critical limitations in handling real-time sensor fusion, multi-physics interactions, and uncertainty quantification at scale, particularly when addressing safety-critical constraints. To address these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized simulations combining agent-based modeling, finite element analysis, and Monte Carlo methods. The computational workflow will integrate machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets—including LiDAR, thermal imaging, and IoT sensor streams—to predict system behaviors under variable environmental conditions. Key innovations include the development of adaptive mesh refinement techniques for multi-scale simulations and GPU-accelerated optimization routines to reduce time-to-solution for complex design parameter spaces. The project will validate these methods using case studies in autonomous agricultural machinery navigation and energy-aware drone swarm coordination. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for simulating safety-compliant autonomous systems, along with benchmarks quantifying trade-offs between computational accuracy and resource allocation. Outcomes will directly inform the development of industry standards for verifying autonomous system reliability while advancing computational methods applicable to broader engineering challenges in robotics and smart manufacturing. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to manage memory-intensive workloads involving terabyte-scale datasets and to achieve the required throughput for ensemble-based uncertainty analysis. This work bridges critical gaps in engineering-related technologies by enabling high-fidelity, real-time simulation capabilities previously constrained by conventional computing resources.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of diagnosing and managing multi-factorial diseases in veterinary internal medicine necessitates advanced computational tools to integrate heterogeneous clinical data and model biological systems. Current challenges include analyzing large-scale datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, genomics, and wearable sensors in companion animals, particularly for chronic conditions such as renal disease, endocrine disorders, and age-related pathologies. Traditional statistical methods lack the capacity to resolve non-linear interactions or simulate dynamic disease progression. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework to identify diagnostic biomarkers, predict treatment responses, and model disease trajectories in domestic animals. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-modal data from 10,000+ anonymized canine and feline EHRs, including longitudinal lab results, imaging metadata, and owner-reported behavioral metrics. Deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models and graph neural networks, will be trained to detect subtle patterns in temporal clinical data and correlate them with histopathological findings. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate protein-ligand interactions for drug repurposing candidates targeting feline chronic kidney disease. A secondary aim involves agent-based modeling of hospital-acquired infection risks in veterinary referral centers using real-world admission data. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early disease detection, optimized therapeutic protocols for geriatric patients, and open-source tools for veterinary EHR analysis. The computational demands of training large models, running parallelized simulations, and managing distributed data storage require dedicated HPC infrastructure with GPU acceleration and scalable memory. This work will advance precision veterinary medicine by bridging clinical observations with systems biology approaches, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment personalization for non-surgical conditions. Results will be disseminated through veterinary informatics platforms to support evidence-based decision-making in general practice and specialty care settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of general medical services to animals with a wide range of non-surgical clinical problems. May included related research in behavioral aspects of diseases, animal diagnosis, animal aging, and referral procedures.

abstract: Mental health care faces a critical challenge in personalizing treatment plans for patients with complex, comorbid psychiatric conditions, where conventional trial-and-error approaches prolong recovery and increase costs. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to predict individualized responses to psychotropic medication combinations and psychosocial interventions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multifactorial interactions between genetic, neurophysiological, and behavioral data. The research focuses on patients under the care of psychiatric technicians, prioritizing populations with treatment-resistant mood disorders who frequently cycle through acute care settings. Current predictive models in psychiatry remain limited by unidimensional analyses that fail to capture nonlinear relationships between polypharmacy effects, symptom trajectories, and social determinants of health. We will employ federated learning techniques on aggregated electronic health records (EHRs) from partner institutions, incorporating time-series data from wearable biosensors and natural language processing of clinical progress notes documented by psychiatric technicians. Graph neural networks will map patient-specific neurochemical pathways against known pharmacodynamic profiles, while reinforcement learning algorithms simulate optimized intervention sequences. Computational demands include large-scale parameter optimization for hybrid machine learning architectures and privacy-preserving data integration across heterogeneous formats (genomic VCFs, EHR structured fields, unstructured clinician notes). Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool that identifies high-risk medication interactions and prioritizes behavioral interventions aligned with patients' evolving social contexts, directly aiding technicians in care coordination. This work bridges computational psychiatry and frontline mental health services, offering a novel paradigm to reduce iatrogenic harm and improve resource allocation in crisis-oriented care systems. Successful validation could establish scalable methods for real-time treatment personalization in resource-constrained clinical environments.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses, and other mental health care professionals, to provide direct patient care services, assist in developing and implementing treatment plans, administer medications, and perform related administrative functions. Includes instruction in mental health theory, applied psychopathology, patient communication and management, crisis intervention, psychotropic medication, mental health treatment procedures, substance abuse, record-keeping, clinical administrative skills, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic merchandising strategies in omnichannel retail environments through advanced computational modeling. As consumer interactions increasingly span online platforms, physical stores, and hybrid touchpoints, traditional rule-based merchandising systems struggle to adapt to real-time demand signals, spatial constraints, and behavioral heterogeneity. The project will develop a high-fidelity simulation framework using agent-based modeling and deep reinforcement learning to analyze how multi-source data—including real-time foot traffic, basket composition patterns, and micro-location contextual factors—can inform adaptive product placement decisions. High-performance computing resources are required to process terabytes of transactional logs, IoT sensor data, and computer vision-derived customer movement patterns across 12 simulated retail formats.
