The computational architecture will integrate graph neural networks to model cross-category product affinities with transformer-based demand forecasting, enabling the system to propose layout adjustments that balance revenue goals, inventory turnover, and experiential metrics. Validation will occur through A/B testing simulations comparing model-driven strategies against historical control periods across three multinational retailers' datasets. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of generating spatially optimized merchandising plans under constrained floor space, along with quantitative insights into how localized cultural preferences and seasonal demand shifts influence optimal category adjacency rules. This work aims to establish computational merchandising as a distinct interdisciplinary domain at the intersection of operations research, behavioral economics, and spatial analytics, with potential applications in automated planogram generation and crisis-responsive inventory allocation.
cip_title: General Merchandising, Sales, and Related Marketing Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in merchandising, sales, and related marketing operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Nuclear medicine research relies on the development and optimization of radiopharmaceuticals to enable precise diagnostic imaging and targeted radionuclide therapies. Current challenges include modeling complex tracer kinetics in heterogeneous biological systems, optimizing radiation dosimetry for patient-specific therapies, and accelerating the design of novel radiopharmaceuticals with improved targeting and pharmacokinetic properties. These tasks demand computationally intensive simulations that exceed the capabilities of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address three interrelated aims: (1) multi-scale modeling of tracer transport and binding dynamics using spatially resolved pharmacokinetic models informed by clinical PET/CT data; (2) Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations to refine organ- and voxel-level dosimetry estimates for alpha- and beta-emitting therapeutic isotopes; and (3) machine learning-driven virtual screening of ligand libraries for next-generation theranostic agents targeting oncologic and neurodegenerative diseases. The computational workflow will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of ligand-receptor interactions, finite-element methods for tissue-scale biodistribution modeling, and neural networks trained on experimental radiochemistry datasets. HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across physiologically relevant scales (10^−9 to 10^−2 m) and time domains (10^−12 to 10^4 seconds), while distributed memory parallelism will manage the stochastic nature of Monte Carlo dose calculations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for tracer behavior in pathologic tissues, optimized dosing protocols for emerging targeted radionuclide therapies, and prioritized candidate molecules for preclinical evaluation. By bridging spatial and temporal scales that are currently analyzed in isolation, this resource-intensive approach aims to reduce empirical optimization cycles in radiopharmaceutical development and provide quantitative tools for personalizing diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in oncology, cardiology, and neurology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the tracer principle, most often with radiopharmaceuticals, to evaluate molecular, metabolic, physiologic and pathologic conditions of the body for the purposes of diagnosis, therapy and research. Includes instruction in tracer kinetics, the biologic effects of radiation exposure, the fundamentals of the physical sciences, and the principles and operation of radiation detection and imaging systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the spatiotemporal dynamics of soilborne fungal pathogen emergence in agroecosystems under climate variability. Plant pathogens in soil ecosystems present unique challenges due to complex interactions between microbial communities, host root exudates, and abiotic factors like soil moisture and temperature fluctuations. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the nonlinear, multiscale feedbacks driving pathogen resilience and outbreak patterns. We propose a hybrid computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of fungal hyphal networks with partial differential equations (PDEs) governing solute transport and soil microclimate. The ABM component will simulate pathogen growth strategies (saprotrophic vs. parasitic phases) in response to dynamic carbon allocation patterns from host plants, while PDEs model diffusion of antimicrobial root exudates and water potential gradients. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated simulations to enable probabilistic forecasting of disease hotspots under projected climate scenarios. The computational workflow requires massive parallelization for parameter sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous soil profiles and 3D root architecture datasets derived from X-ray tomography. Expected outcomes include identification of critical thresholds in soil carbon-to-water ratios that trigger pathogenic phase transitions, as well as predictive maps of regional pathogen adaptability under drought-heatwave regimes. This work addresses a critical gap in translating microbial-scale interactions to field-scale disease risk assessment, providing actionable insights for climate-resilient crop rotation schemes and precision biocontrol strategies. By bridging microbial ecology, soil physics, and plant immunology through computational synthesis, the project establishes a novel paradigm for proactive management of emergent soilborne diseases in agricultural systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms from an agricultural perspective. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern diesel engines, coupled with stringent emissions regulations and demands for higher fuel efficiency, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize engine design, diagnostics, and maintenance strategies. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate diesel engine combustion dynamics, emissions formation, and component wear under diverse operating conditions. Current experimental approaches are limited by cost, scalability, and the inability to isolate variables in real-world systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address these gaps through large-scale parametric studies of fuel injection patterns, turbocharger performance, and aftertreatment system interactions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will leverage open-source solvers (e.g., OpenFOAM) to model multiphase combustion processes, while machine learning frameworks will analyze sensor data from engine testbeds to predict failure modes in critical components like fuel injectors and piston rings. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of core-hours, integrating 3D engine geometries and real-world duty-cycle data from industrial partners. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing combustion efficiency under transient loads, digital twins for proactive maintenance of fleet vehicles, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated engine performance scenarios. This work will directly support curriculum modernization in Diesel Mechanics Technology programs by providing students with exposure to computational diagnostics tools, bridging traditional hands-on training with Industry 4.0 methodologies. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops for diesel technicians and collaborations with manufacturers to validate models against engine dynamometer tests. The project addresses a critical need for data-driven decision-making in diesel engine maintenance and design, with potential impacts on reducing operational downtime, lowering emissions, and extending engine service life in transportation and energy sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain diesel engines in vehicles such as automobiles, buses, ships, trucks, railroad locomotives, and construction equipment; as well as stationary diesel engines in electrical generators and related equipment.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenges of optimizing digital audience engagement and resource distribution for visual arts organizations in an increasingly data-driven cultural landscape. As galleries, digital art platforms, and media collectives navigate evolving consumption patterns—particularly with the rise of immersive technologies and decentralized content ecosystems—there is a critical need to model complex interactions between artistic content, platform algorithms, and viewer behavior. Current analytical frameworks lack the capacity to process multimodal data (including high-resolution visual assets, user interaction logs, and cross-platform engagement metrics) at scales required for actionable insights. To bridge this gap, we propose deploying high-performance computing resources to implement machine learning architectures specifically adapted for cultural analytics. Computational methods will include 1) transformer-based natural language processing to analyze audience sentiment across social media and critique platforms, 2) vision transformers (ViTs) trained on curated art historical datasets to identify stylistic trends influencing engagement, and 3) graph neural networks modeling the flow of digital artworks through hybrid physical-virtual exhibition networks. These models will be integrated into an agent-based simulation framework to test resource allocation strategies under varying market conditions. The project’s outcomes aim to establish predictive metrics for artwork visibility in algorithmically mediated environments while providing arts managers with computational tools to balance artistic integrity with operational sustainability. By processing terabytes of heterogeneous cultural data—including 4K/8K video streams from virtual exhibitions—the requested computing infrastructure will enable unprecedented granularity in mapping how technical constraints, aesthetic values, and economic pressures intersect in contemporary visual media ecosystems. Results will be disseminated through an open-access dashboard for small-to-midsize arts organizations, accompanied by computational workflows tailored for non-technical cultural practitioners.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Arts, Entertainment, and Media Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage various aspects of the visual arts, performing arts, and entertainment media industries. Includes instruction in business and financial management, marketing and fund-raising, labor relations for the arts, event promotion and management, product and artist management, and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dispersion and health impacts of airborne contaminants in urban environments, integrating dynamic interactions between human mobility, built infrastructure, and atmospheric conditions. Current models often treat indoor and outdoor environments as separate systems, creating gaps in assessing real-world exposure risks exacerbated by climate change and urbanization. Our research addresses this by coupling agent-based simulations of pedestrian movement with high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to predict contaminant transport across interconnected microenvironments. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale scenarios, including pollutant infiltration into buildings, ventilation efficacy in transit hubs, and population-level exposure disparities during extreme heat or pollution events. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in uncertainty quantification, enabling sensitivity analyses across diverse urban morphologies and meteorological conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize emergency response protocols, urban design guidelines for pollution mitigation, and evidence-based policies to reduce environmental health inequities. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling large-scale simulations involving 10^6–10^7 grid cells for CFD, parallelized stochastic agent models, and integration with real-world sensor data from municipal air quality networks. By advancing coupled human-environment system modeling, this work will support resilient infrastructure planning and improve public health interventions for vulnerable populations. The computational workflows developed will also serve as a template for future studies on emerging contaminants and climate adaptation strategies in environmental engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for personalized rehabilitation interventions in individuals with neuromusculoskeletal disabilities. A critical challenge in rehabilitation science is the integration of multi-modal data—including biomechanical, neurophysiological, and patient-reported outcomes—to optimize interventions that account for individual variability in motor recovery, pain perception, and functional adaptation. Current approaches often rely on simplified models or small datasets, limiting their clinical applicability. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining musculoskeletal simulations, machine learning (ML), and large-scale data fusion to model the interactions between neuromuscular control, tissue mechanics, and behavioral outcomes. The project will utilize open-source biomechanical software (e.g., OpenSim) to simulate movement dynamics across diverse patient populations, augmented by ML algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets (kinematic, electromyography, and wearable sensor data). HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations to thousands of virtual subjects, enabling parameter sweeps to identify critical biomechanical and physiological factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. Additionally, graph neural networks will be employed to model patient-specific functional networks derived from brain imaging and sensorimotor performance data, requiring distributed training across GPU nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational pipeline for predicting optimal rehabilitation protocols based on individual biomechanical and neural profiles, (2) open-access datasets of simulated movement pathologies, and (3) novel insights into the role of motor variability in recovery trajectories. This work directly addresses the NIH’s emphasis on precision rehabilitation and has implications for improving assistive device design, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice, and informing policy on resource allocation for rehabilitation technologies. The requested computing resources will support iterative model refinement, large-scale sensitivity analyses, and the integration of real-world data from ongoing clinical trials in stroke and spinal cord injury rehabilitation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human function, disability, and rehabilitation from the perspectives of the health sciences, social sciences, psychology, engineering, and related fields. Includes instruction in psychological, social, and cultural aspects of disability and rehabilitation; sensory and motor function and dysfunction; biomechanics and kinesiology; assistive technology; rehabilitation instrumentation and methodology; statistics; and health and rehabilitation policy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, multi-channel digital marketing campaigns under dynamic consumer behavior and platform constraints. Current models for cross-channel attribution and budget allocation struggle to account for nonlinear interactions between social media, search engines, and e-commerce platforms, particularly as emerging technologies like generative AI alter content consumption patterns. We propose developing a computational framework that integrates stochastic consumer journey simulation with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to identify adaptive resource allocation strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets spanning clickstream logs, contextual advertising bids, and synthetic consumer persona data generated through large language models. Key computational challenges include parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations of 10^6+ hypothetical buyer journeys across variable platform algorithms and solving high-dimensional optimization problems with time-dependent constraints. The project will implement a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks (to model channel interdependencies) with transformer-based temporal models (to forecast shifting platform policies). Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for testing allocation strategies under combinatorial uncertainty, validated against live campaign data from partner organizations. This work aims to advance marketing computational economics by quantifying the value of adaptive resource partitioning in decentralized digital ecosystems while establishing performance benchmarks for emerging "always-on" campaign paradigms. Results will be disseminated through open-source libraries for marketing operations research and privacy-preserving synthetic data replicas to support reproducibility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop a digital marketing plan and integrate marketing, advertising, sales, and logistics across physical and digital channels. Includes instruction in digital marketing, e-commerce, online consumer psychology, search engine optimization, social media marketing, and web analytics.

abstract: The preservation and revitalization of the Hawaiian language (‘ōlelo Hawaiʻi) face critical challenges due to the scarcity of digitized linguistic resources and advanced analytical tools tailored to its unique phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures. Existing computational methods, often designed for Indo-European languages, inadequately capture the complexities of Hawaiian, including its vowel-rich phonology, verb-noun ambiguities, and dialectal variations across historical and contemporary texts. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a scalable computational framework for analyzing Hawaiian language corpora, enabling large-scale philological research and dialectological mapping. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) constructing a parallelized pipeline for processing and annotating digitized historical manuscripts, oral histories, and modern publications using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for Polynesian languages; (2) implementing machine learning models to identify and classify dialectal features across temporal, geographic, and sociolinguistic dimensions; and (3) simulating phonetic shifts through agent-based modeling to trace the evolution of regional speech patterns. HPC resources will be critical for handling the terabytes of textual and audio data, training deep neural networks on rare morphological patterns, and running computationally intensive phylogenetic analyses of language change. Expected outcomes include the first open-access repository of computationally annotated Hawaiian texts, interactive visualization tools for educators and cultural practitioners, and empirically grounded insights into language contact dynamics between Hawaiian and colonial languages. By integrating computational linguistics with Indigenous knowledge systems, this project aims to empower Hawaiian language revitalization efforts while advancing methodological innovations for under-resourced languages globally. The requested computing infrastructure will directly support graduate student researchers in developing technical skills aligned with both linguistic scholarship and community-driven language preservation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hawaiian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the historical evolution of medical practices and disease management across the 19th and 20th centuries, with a focus on the interplay between socio-economic factors and public health interventions. The primary research problem centers on the lack of large-scale, quantitative studies examining how regional disparities in wealth, infrastructure, and governance influenced the adoption of medical technologies and the outcomes of epidemic responses. Traditional historiographical methods, reliant on manual analysis of fragmented archival sources, struggle to synthesize heterogeneous datasets—including digitized patient records, public health reports, trade logs, and demographic surveys—into cohesive models of long-term trends. To address this, the project will employ computational text mining, geospatial network analysis, and agent-based modeling to process over 10 terabytes of multilingual archival materials from repositories in Europe, North America, and Asia. Custom natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract temporal and thematic patterns from medical journals and governmental correspondence, while network simulations will reconstruct the diffusion of therapies and public health policies across trade and colonial routes. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on historical medical terminology, running parallelized simulations of disease spread under varying socio-economic conditions, and handling high-resolution geospatial data. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized correlations between infrastructural investment and mortality rates, a publicly accessible database of annotated historical medical texts, and methodological frameworks for integrating computational analysis into historiography. By bridging quantitative and qualitative approaches, this work aims to advance the history of medicine as a data-rich discipline capable of informing contemporary debates on health equity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution and socio-economic context of medical theories, education, practices, and technologies; and on the history of diseases, therapeutics, patients, and healers. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of the historiography of medicine; the history of science, medicine, and technology; and of research methods in the history of medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the operational dynamics and socio-cultural impacts of large-scale military campaigns across multiple historical eras. Traditional historical methods face challenges in systematically processing vast datasets—including troop movements, supply logistics, correspondence archives, and geopolitical records—to identify patterns in decision-making, resource allocation, and institutional adaptation under conflict conditions. The research will focus on three case studies: 17th-century European sieges, 20th-century mechanized warfare, and Cold War-era proxy conflicts, integrating multi-lingual primary sources, geospatial data, and quantitative records. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling to simulate battlefield logistics and morale outcomes, natural language processing (NLP) to analyze command hierarchies in archival communications, and network analysis to map alliances and supply chains. Parallelized simulations will test hypotheses about the relationship between technological adoption (e.g., artillery, radar) and tactical flexibility, while machine learning classifiers will identify cultural narratives in soldier diaries and propaganda materials. The scale of datasets—spanning over 10TB of digitized records—necessitates HPC infrastructure for distributed data processing, GPU-accelerated NLP tasks, and high-memory nodes for geospatial rendering. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking military operational data to socio-political contexts, validated models of logistical efficiency under resource constraints, and visualizations of decision-making timelines in crises. This work will advance historiographical debates about institutional learning in military organizations while demonstrating methodologies for computational humanities research. By quantifying interactions between technology, culture, and strategy, the project aims to provide a framework for interdisciplinary analysis of warfare’s long-term societal impacts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the history of warfare and military institutions in their operational, politico-economic and socio-cultural contexts; including airpower history, naval history, and military history. Includes instruction in military organization, military operations, the history of technology, leadership and biography, military psychology and behavior, international relations and politics, economics, aspects of general and regional history, cultural history and anthropology, historiography, and applicable quantitative methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic, real-time pricing and inventory allocation strategies for omnichannel retail environments, integrating localized demand forecasting with supply chain resilience metrics. The rise of hybrid shopping models (e.g., buy-online-pickup-in-store, ship-from-store) has introduced unprecedented complexity in balancing perishable inventory across physical and digital channels while maintaining price competitiveness. Traditional rule-based systems fail to account for hyperlocal variables such as microseasonal demand shifts, competitor price fluctuations detected via web scraping, or last-mile logistics disruptions. The research will employ reinforcement learning (RL) models trained on multi-agent simulations of customer behavior, supplier networks, and store-level operational constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to handle three core components: 1) Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of demand scenarios incorporating geospatial weather data and social media sentiment analysis, 2) Neural architecture search for optimizing RL reward functions that simultaneously maximize margin and minimize waste, and 3) Real-time validation against a synthetic retail ecosystem mirroring the scale of national retail chains (10,000+ SKUs across 500+ locations). Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive pricing elasticity measurement and a decision-support system that reduces perishable inventory write-offs by ≥15% in simulated environments. The computational intensity arises from processing high-dimensional time-series data streams (IoT shelf sensors, POS systems) while maintaining sub-minute latency for price updates—a requirement that necessitates GPU-accelerated training and distributed memory architectures. This work bridges operations research, behavioral economics, and computational logistics, offering a novel paradigm for resource allocation in spatially distributed retail networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations associated with retail sales in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in over-the-counter and other direct sales operations in business settings, basic bookkeeping principles, customer service, team/staff leadership and supervision, floor management, and applicable technical skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory challenges surrounding generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the global entertainment industry. As generative AI tools rapidly transform content creation in music, film, and digital media, unresolved questions persist regarding copyright attribution, derivative work classification, and jurisdictional inconsistencies in liability frameworks. Traditional legal research methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of AI-generated content datasets, international case law variations, and real-time policy developments across creative sectors. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) to map precedent patterns in transnational copyright disputes involving AI outputs, train machine learning models on synthetic media detection in trademark infringement cases, and simulate multi-jurisdictional regulatory scenarios using agent-based modeling. By integrating legal text corpora, audiovisual metadata from AI platforms, and policy documents from 50+ jurisdictions, the computational approach aims to identify systemic gaps in existing intellectual property frameworks and quantify risks for content producers. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for assessing litigation probabilities in AI-assisted creative works and a comparative analysis of proposed regulatory models’ economic impacts on entertainment markets. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational legal analytics with arts industry needs, offering empirically grounded insights to inform contract drafting standards, legislative proposals, and ethical AI deployment guidelines for creative professionals. The scale of multimodal data analysis and iterative policy simulations necessitates HPC capabilities to process terabyte-level datasets while maintaining low-latency performance for real-time model refinement. Results will advance scholarship at the intersection of entertainment law and emergent technologies while providing actionable frameworks for legal practitioners navigating AI’s disruptive effects on artistic production.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for integrating heterogeneous medical data sources—including electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic datasets—to enable precision medicine applications in clinical decision-making. A critical challenge in medical informatics lies in synthesizing high-dimensional, multi-modal data to generate actionable insights while preserving patient privacy and data integrity. Current methods struggle with computational inefficiency when processing terabytes of imaging data, harmonizing unstructured clinical notes, and identifying biomarkers from genome-wide associations. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline leveraging distributed deep learning, federated learning architectures, and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze de-identified EHRs, radiology images, and sequencing data from [Institution]’s clinical research repositories. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated clusters for training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on 3D medical imaging data, parallelized NLP models for extracting phenotypic features from clinical narratives, and privacy-preserving federated learning to integrate insights across institutions without raw data sharing. The HPC environment is essential to manage memory-intensive tasks, such as whole-slide image analysis, and to reduce model training times from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for early detection of [specific disease/complication, e.g., sepsis, cancer progression] using multi-modal data fusion, (2) an open-source toolkit for federated analysis of sensitive medical datasets, and (3) benchmarks demonstrating scalability to petabyte-scale data. This work will advance medical informatics infrastructure by enabling efficient, secure analysis of large-scale clinical data, directly supporting translational research in personalized treatment planning and real-time decision support systems. The requested computing resources will ensure rigorous validation of these methods, fostering reproducibility and deployment in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to medical research and clinical information technology support, and the development of advanced imaging, database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in computer science, health information systems architecture, medical knowledge structures, medical language and image processing, quantitative medical decision modeling, imaging techniques, electronic medical records, medical research systems, clinical decision support, and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of multi-pollutant exposure effects on respiratory health outcomes in urban populations. Environmental health research faces a critical challenge in disentangling the synergistic impacts of complex air pollution mixtures—including particulate matter (PM₂.₅), ozone, and volatile organic compounds—on vulnerable communities, where traditional statistical models often fail to account for dynamic spatial-temporal interactions and confounding socioeconomic variables. We propose a computational framework integrating large-scale environmental sensor data, electronic health records, and high-resolution atmospheric modeling to quantify exposure-risk relationships. Machine learning algorithms, including ensemble neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models, will be deployed to analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning air quality monitoring networks, satellite remote sensing, and anonymized clinical diagnoses. Agent-based modeling will simulate population mobility patterns and inhalation rates under varying pollution scenarios, while GPU-accelerated toxicology simulations will predict biological responses to pollutant mixtures. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing parallelized processing of heterogeneous data streams, optimizing model hyperparameters, and conducting Monte Carlo-based uncertainty analyses. Expected outcomes include high-resolution risk maps identifying pollution hotspots linked to asthma exacerbations and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) incidence, as well as policy-relevant metrics for prioritizing emission control strategies. This work will provide a scalable framework for assessing environmental justice disparities in exposure burdens, directly supporting regulatory decision-making under the Clean Air Act. By elucidating mechanistic pathways through which multi-pollutant interactions drive health inequities, the project aims to advance precision public health interventions while establishing computational methods transferable to other environmental health challenges, such as wildfire smoke exposure and climate-related disease surveillance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of environmental sciences, public health, the biomedical sciences, and environmental toxicology to the study of environmental factors affecting human health, safety, and related ecological issues, and prepares individuals to function as professional environmental health specialists. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, toxicology, public policy analysis, public management, risk assessment, communications, environmental law, occupational health and safety emergency response, and applications such as air quality, food protection, radiation protection, solid and hazardous waste management, water quality, soil quality, noise abatement, housing quality, and environmental control of recreational areas.

abstract: This research project investigates the sociotechnical dynamics of algorithmic decision-making in public health surveillance systems, focusing on the ethical and policy implications of machine learning models used to predict disease outbreaks. As governments and institutions increasingly deploy predictive analytics to allocate resources during health crises, concerns about algorithmic bias, transparency, and equity have emerged. These systems often integrate heterogeneous data streams—including mobility patterns, clinical records, and socioeconomic indicators—raising questions about how computational choices in model design propagate systemic disparities in marginalized communities. Using a mixed-methods approach grounded in Science and Technology Studies (STS), this work combines large-scale computational simulations with qualitative policy analysis to evaluate how technical architectures interact with social values. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the construction of agent-based models simulating disease spread across synthetic populations with granular demographic and geographic variation. Parallelized sensitivity analyses will test how algorithmic assumptions about risk thresholds, data completeness, and spatial prioritization affect equity outcomes in simulated resource allocation scenarios. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze historical policy documents and public health communications to identify patterns in how technical uncertainties are framed to stakeholders. By iteratively coupling computational experiments with discourse analysis, the project aims to develop framework metrics for auditing the societal impacts of predictive public health tools. Expected outcomes include open-source software for simulating bias propagation in population-scale models, evidence-based guidelines for participatory model design, and a typology of governance challenges at the intersection of computational epidemiology and health justice. This work addresses critical gaps in understanding how interdisciplinary teams can operationalize ethical principles in societally consequential AI systems while meeting the technical demands of emergency response infrastructures.
detailed_field: History/ philosophy of science, technology, and society
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the contemporary social and public policy ramifications of science and technology, the interrelationship of science and engineering with the public policy process, and the social and ethical dimensions of scientific and technological enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic treatment personalization for complex, multi-system disorders by integrating high-dimensional clinical, genomic, and metabolomic data. Current approaches to precision medicine often rely on static models that fail to account for temporal variations in patient physiology, heterogeneous data streams, and the nonlinear interactions between biomarkers. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning architecture leveraging time-series analysis, graph neural networks (GNNs), and federated learning to model patient trajectories and predict individualized therapeutic adjustments in real time. The research will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 15,000 patients with autoimmune-inflammatory conditions, paired with longitudinal multi-omics datasets, to train models that identify critical inflection points in disease progression and recommend intervention strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing petabytes of raw EHR data, training GNNs on dynamically evolving patient graphs, and simulating virtual cohorts to validate model robustness under diverse clinical scenarios. Key computational challenges include managing sparse, irregularly sampled data streams, ensuring privacy-preserving federated learning across institutional partners, and scaling ensemble methods to accommodate thousands of concurrent simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive treatment optimization, validated against retrospective clinical outcomes, and a novel biomarker interaction network revealing previously unrecognized therapeutic targets. This work bridges translational gaps by enabling clinicians to operationalize complex, data-driven insights at the point of care, directly supporting the program’s focus on integrating computational innovation into clinical practice. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parallelized simulations, and secure data federation infrastructure, advancing both methodological rigor and practical applicability in next-generation clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares medical and health clinicians to combine knowledge from scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge, improve medical education, and bridge laboratory and clinical science into clinical practice. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, medical education and scientific writing.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in livestock-associated pathogens pose critical challenges to veterinary medicine, public health, and sustainable agriculture. Current gaps in understanding the genomic and epidemiological drivers of AMR in veterinary clinical settings limit effective intervention strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic and clinical datasets from livestock pathogens, with a focus on cattle and poultry populations in intensive agricultural systems. The research will integrate whole-genome sequencing data from resistant and susceptible bacterial isolates (e.g., *Escherichia coli*, *Staphylococcus aureus*) with clinical metadata, including treatment histories, farm management practices, and animal health outcomes. Computational methods will include phylogenetic reconstruction to trace resistance gene transmission, machine learning models to predict resistance phenotypes from genomic features, and agent-based simulations to evaluate the impact of proposed mitigation strategies under diverse farming scenarios. The scale of data—spanning terabytes of sequence data and millions of clinical records—necessitates parallelized processing, advanced statistical modeling, and optimized storage solutions, all of which require HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include identifying high-risk resistance pathways, validating genomic markers for rapid AMR diagnostics, and generating evidence-based recommendations for stewardship protocols tailored to veterinary clinical practice. By elucidating the interplay between pathogen evolution, treatment practices, and host-environment interactions, this work will directly inform veterinary decision-making, reduce antimicrobial misuse in livestock systems, and contribute to global efforts to curb AMR. The proposed computational framework will also establish a scalable platform for future studies on emerging zoonotic diseases and precision veterinary medicine.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Sciences/ Veterinary Clinical Sciences, General
cip_definition: An integrated program of study in one or more of the veterinary medical or clinical sciences or a program undifferentiated as to title.

abstract: Veterinary medicine faces critical challenges in understanding the complex dynamics of zoonotic disease transmission, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) evolution, and host-pathogen interactions at scale. Current limitations in computational resources hinder the ability to model these systems with sufficient resolution, particularly when integrating multi-omics data, epidemiological variables, and environmental factors across diverse animal populations. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of pathogen spread and treatment outcomes in veterinary contexts. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) frameworks to simulate disease transmission across heterogeneous livestock populations, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on high-throughput genomic and metagenomic datasets to identify AMR gene transfer patterns. Molecular dynamics simulations will further elucidate mechanisms of drug resistance in priority veterinary pathogens, such as *Streptococcus suis* and avian influenza viruses. These computational approaches require parallel processing capabilities to manage large parameter spaces, optimize stochastic models, and analyze real-time sensor data from livestock monitoring systems. Expected outcomes include actionable models for predicting outbreak hotspots, evaluating intervention strategies, and informing precision veterinary protocols to reduce antibiotic overuse. By leveraging HPC, this work will address scalability gaps in existing veterinary informatics tools, enabling rapid, data-driven decision-making for animal health management. The results will directly contribute to national biosecurity frameworks and provide open-access computational pipelines for the broader agricultural research community. This project aligns with global One Health initiatives by enhancing interoperability between veterinary and public health datasets, ultimately mitigating risks of zoonotic spillover and promoting sustainable livestock practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of veterinary medicine, involving the diagnosis, treatment, and health care management of animals and animal populations and the prevention and management of zoonosis. Includes instruction in the veterinary basic sciences, infectious and noninfectious disease, diagnostic procedures, veterinary clinical medicine, obstetrics, radiology, anesthesiology, surgery, toxicology, animal health and preventive medicine, clinical nutrition, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Sleep disorders present complex challenges in diagnosis and management, often requiring the integration of multimodal physiological data. Traditional polysomnographic analysis relies on manual scoring of sleep stages and events, a process limited by subjectivity, time-intensive protocols, and an inability to capture dynamic interactions between neurophysiological signals, cardiorespiratory patterns, and environmental factors. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model sleep architecture and disorder phenotypes using large-scale polysomnography datasets. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process and analyze terabytes of multichannel recordings (EEG, EMG, EOG, respiratory effort, SpO2) from 5,000+ clinical sleep studies, integrating concurrent actigraphy, environmental sensor data, and electronic health records. Machine learning pipelines will be optimized to identify latent patterns in sleep-wake transitions, autonomic instability during REM sleep, and microstructural biomarkers of neurodegenerative comorbidity. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model upper airway collapse mechanisms in obstructive sleep apnea, correlating real-time pressure gradients with anatomical imaging data. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of signal decomposition tasks, GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for event detection, and large-scale validation of predictive algorithms across heterogeneous patient subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) automated tools for quantifying sleep continuity disturbances with sub-second precision, (2) novel metrics linking sleep microstructure to cognitive decline trajectories, and (3) personalized airflow collapse risk profiles derived from biomechanical simulations. By advancing computational methods in polysomnography, this work aims to establish scalable infrastructure for precision sleep medicine, reducing diagnostic latency for rare parasomnias and improving prognostic accuracy in complex cases where sleep pathology intersects with neurological, metabolic, and cardiovascular disease states.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: Reproductive cancers, particularly ovarian and endometrial malignancies, present complex challenges due to their dynamic interaction with hormonal cycles and tissue-specific microenvironmental factors. A critical gap exists in understanding how cyclical hormonal fluctuations and mechanical forces within reproductive tissues collectively influence tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational model integrating hormonal signaling pathways, tissue biomechanics, and tumor growth dynamics to identify microenvironment-driven mechanisms of cancer resilience. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate three-dimensional tissue architectures under hormonally dynamic conditions, parameterized by clinical imaging data and ex vivo biomechanical measurements from patient-derived samples. The computational framework will employ finite element analysis to model tissue deformation during menstrual or estrous cycles, coupled with agent-based modeling of cancer cell proliferation and invasion. Parallelized parameter optimization will be conducted to calibrate the model against longitudinal clinical outcomes, while machine learning approaches will identify predictive biomechanical and endocrine biomarkers of metastatic potential. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational platform for simulating hormone-responsive reproductive cancers, (2) mechanistic insights into how cyclic mechanical stress synergizes with estrogen receptor signaling to drive therapy-resistant phenotypes, and (3) predictive biomarkers for risk stratification in patients with early-stage disease. This work will directly inform targeted therapeutic strategies that account for reproductive system physiology, advancing precision oncology in hormonally driven cancers. The scale of spatial-temporal simulations (10^6+ cellular agents across 100+ cycle iterations) and integration of high-resolution imaging datasets (>50 TB) necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically relevant resolution within tractable timeframes.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of reproductive processes and biogenesis in animals and human beings. Includes instruction in reproductive ecology and behavior, reproductive system physiology, endocrinology, developmental biology, neuroendocrinology, evolution and types of reproductive systems, reproductive genetics, physiopathology of reproductive processes, and applications of molecular biology and biophysics to the study of reproductive physiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the role of computational hermeneutics in modeling the ethical decision-making frameworks of pre-ministerial students during simulated pastoral care scenarios. While theological training traditionally emphasizes qualitative, text-based methods, this study proposes an interdisciplinary approach integrating moral philosophy, sociocultural analytics, and machine learning to systematically examine how emerging religious leaders navigate complex interpersonal dilemmas. The central research problem revolves around the lack of empirically grounded, scalable tools for assessing and enhancing situational ethics training in pre-seminary education. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the project will develop agent-based models simulating diverse congregational environments, with neural language processing architectures trained on interfaith dialogue corpora and historical pastoral case studies. These models will generate dynamic interaction scenarios that adapt to trainees’ evolving responses, enabling granular analysis of decision patterns through graph-based ethical reasoning networks. The computational framework aims to identify latent biases, cultural competency gaps, and contextual heuristics in simulated ministry contexts while preserving the nuanced spiritual dimensions of pastoral care. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for theological educators to create culturally tailored training modules and a novel evaluation metric for ethical agility in ministerial formation. By bridging computational social science with applied theology, this research contributes to understudied intersections of artificial intelligence and religious vocation training, offering scalable methods to address 21st-century ministerial challenges while maintaining humanistic rigor.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to enter a seminary or other program leading to religious ordination, or a related religious vocation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the mathematical characterization of non-perturbative regimes in quantum field theories (QFTs) using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While perturbative methods dominate studies of weakly coupled systems, many phenomena—such as confinement in Yang-Mills theories or vacuum structure in strongly interacting models—require non-perturbative solutions. Current analytical tools face fundamental limitations in these regimes, necessitating numerical approaches to resolve high-dimensional functional integrals and operator spectra. The research will employ lattice field theory techniques combined with Monte Carlo sampling and tensor network algorithms to approximate path integrals and extract ground-state properties of selected QFTs. Key targets include (1) mapping phase transitions in 3+1D SU(2) gauge theories with matter couplings, (2) quantifying entanglement entropy scaling near critical points in 2D conformal field theories deformed by relevant operators, and (3) analyzing topological contributions to partition functions in supersymmetric models. These objectives demand large-scale parallel computations due to the exponential scaling of state spaces and the need for finite-volume extrapolations. The proposed HPC resources will enable simulations on lattices up to 32^4 sites, with iterative diagonalization routines optimized via GPU-accelerated linear algebra libraries. Expected outcomes include high-precision determinations of critical coupling constants, universal data for conformal bootstrap programs, and insights into the mathematical consistency of non-Lagrangian QFTs. Results will be disseminated through open-source code releases and publications, providing foundational data for theoretical studies of quantum gravity, holography, and emergent spacetime geometries. The computational infrastructure will also support training initiatives in numerical relativity and advanced quantum dynamics for graduate researchers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and mathematical formulation and evaluation of the physical laws governing, and models describing, matter-energy phenomena, and the analysis of related experimental designs and results. Includes instruction in classical and quantum theory, relativity theory, field theory, mathematics of infinite series, vector and coordinate analysis, wave and particle theory, advanced applied calculus and geometry, analyses of continuum, cosmology, and statistical theory and analysis.

abstract: Pediatric urological disorders, encompassing congenital anomalies, neurogenic bladder dysfunction, and pediatric urinary tract malignancies, present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneous pathophysiology and the unique anatomical considerations of developing patients. Current management strategies are often generalized, lacking precision tools to predict disease progression, optimize surgical interventions, or tailor therapies to individual patients. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets and develop predictive models for personalized care. The research will integrate clinical data from electronic health records (EHRs), longitudinal imaging studies, genomic profiles, and urinary biomarkers to identify patterns associated with disease severity, postoperative outcomes, and therapeutic response. Machine learning (ML) algorithms, including deep neural networks, will be employed to classify congenital anomalies, predict renal functional decline in neurogenic bladder patients, and stratify risk in pediatric urothelial tumors. Additionally, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model urinary flow in complex anatomical reconstructions to optimize surgical planning for obstructive uropathies. These analyses require HPC resources due to the volume of imaging data (>10,000 high-resolution scans), the computational intensity of CFD simulations, and the need for real-time processing of streaming EHR data. The expected outcomes include validated predictive models for clinical deployment, open-source tools for pediatric urological CFD applications, and novel biomarkers derived from multi-omic integration. By enhancing the precision of diagnostics and interventions, this work aims to reduce invasive procedures, improve long-term renal and urological health in pediatric patients, and establish a scalable computational framework for future research in congenital genitourinary disorders. The requested computing resources are critical to managing data complexity and ensuring robust, reproducible analyses in this high-dimensional research space.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals in the study, prevention, and management of congenital, childhood-acquired, and overlapping adolescent anomalies of the genitourinary tract, including problems, diseases, tumors, and traumas.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid quantum-classical communication networks presents critical challenges in optimizing resource allocation and ensuring secure data transmission across heterogeneous infrastructures. While classical networking frameworks have matured, the integration of emerging quantum communication nodes—such as entanglement distribution channels and quantum key distribution (QDD) relays—introduces dynamic resource contention, non-standard latency profiles, and novel attack surfaces that existing protocols cannot adequately address. This project seeks to develop adaptive resource orchestration algorithms capable of managing hybrid networks by modeling multi-objective optimization across quantum bandwidth, classical throughput, and security constraints. The research employs a two-tier computational approach: first, large-scale network simulations using parameterized quantum-classical topologies to profile performance degradation patterns under varying entanglement rates and decoherence effects; second, the training of graph neural networks (GNNs) on these simulations to predict optimal resource partitioning strategies in real-time configurations. High-performance computing resources are essential for both simulating photonic quantum network components at physically accurate noise levels and processing the high-dimensional optimization space inherent to hybrid networks. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for quantum-aware software-defined networking (SDN) controllers, quantitative guidelines for capacity planning in transitional quantum networks, and vulnerability assessments of proposed resource allocation protocols against superposition-based attack models. This work aims to bridge the gap between quantum information theory and practical network engineering, providing foundational tools for next-generation infrastructure that must seamlessly integrate classical and quantum communication paradigms. The computational results will directly inform standardization efforts in post-quantum telecommunications and support the design of fault-tolerant network architectures for distributed quantum computing applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of linked systems of computers, peripherals, and associated software to maximize efficiency and productivity, and that prepares individuals to function as network specialists and managers at various levels. Includes instruction in operating systems and applications; systems design and analysis; networking theory and solutions; types of networks; network management and control; network and flow optimization; security; configuring; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the impact of cultural and linguistic dynamics on consumer decision-making in cross-border e-commerce platforms. While international marketing strategies increasingly rely on algorithmic recommendations and personalized content, existing models inadequately account for the nonlinear interactions between cultural variables (e.g., regional idioms, symbolism, and social norms) and real-time purchasing behavior. The computational complexity of simulating these interactions across multilingual datasets—spanning 50+ countries and 10,000+ product categories—exceeds the capacity of standard analytical tools. This project proposes the development of a hybrid agent-based model (ABM) integrated with transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) to simulate how micro-level cultural cues propagate through global digital marketplaces. The ABM will simulate heterogeneous consumer agents with culturally embedded preference structures, while NLP pipelines will process unstructured data from social media, product reviews, and localized advertising campaigns to train dynamic sentiment layers. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing agent interactions across diverse cultural contexts and scaling transformer models to analyze low-resource languages prevalent in emerging markets. Expected outcomes include a framework to predict demand volatility caused by cultural misalignment in automated marketing systems, with applications to adaptive pricing, crisis communication, and brand localization. Results will be validated against real-world datasets from a multinational retail partner, focusing on instances where algorithmic recommendations triggered unintended cultural backlash. By quantifying the relationship between cultural granularity and market penetration, this work aims to advance computational social science methodologies in international business while addressing a critical gap in data-driven global marketing strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing activities in enterprises primarily engaged in exporting or importing goods and services in world markets. Includes instruction in international trade controls, foreign trade operations, locating markets, negotiation practices, monetary issues, and international public relations.

abstract: Public sector decision-making increasingly relies on complex, data-driven analyses to optimize resource allocation during crises, yet existing computational tools often fail to address the dynamic interdependencies between infrastructure systems, population behavior, and institutional constraints. This project seeks to develop an adaptive simulation framework for evaluating emergency response strategies in multi-hazard urban environments, with a focus on equity in service delivery. The research employs high-performance computing to integrate agent-based modeling of citizen mobility patterns, Monte Carlo simulations of hazard cascades (e.g., concurrent extreme weather and power grid failures), and multi-objective optimization algorithms that balance response efficiency with distributional fairness metrics. Key computational challenges include real-time processing of heterogeneous datasets (satellite imagery, IoT sensor networks, and social services records) and parallel execution of scenario ensembles across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations. By leveraging GPU-accelerated graph neural networks, the framework will model spatial dependencies in critical infrastructure networks at metropolitan scales, while differential privacy techniques will safeguard sensitive health and demographic information embedded in synthetic population models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated decision-support system for municipal governments to stress-test contingency plans under competing priorities, (2) quantitative benchmarks for equitable resource distribution during simultaneous crises, and (3) open-source modules for vulnerability assessment compatible with existing geospatial information systems. This work directly addresses gaps in computational social policy design by enabling rapid scenario prototyping that accounts for both systemic risks and socioeconomic disparities—a capability currently limited by conventional workstation capacities. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for over 150 U.S. cities participating in the National Emergency Management Association’s resilience planning initiative.
cip_definition: Any program in public administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical nurse leaders (CNLs) face complex challenges in optimizing patient outcomes through evidence-based interventions, particularly when managing dynamic care environments with high-acuity patients. A critical barrier is the inability to rapidly analyze large-scale, heterogeneous clinical datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biosensor data, and longitudinal care coordination metrics—to inform decision-making. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that identify early risk factors for preventable adverse events (e.g., sepsis, medication errors) and simulate intervention strategies for CNL-led teams. Leveraging a de-identified dataset of 250,000+ patient encounters from three tertiary care centers, we will employ parallelized machine learning (ML) frameworks, including ensemble classifiers and recurrent neural networks, to model temporal patterns in patient deterioration and care process inefficiencies. Computational workflows will integrate structured EHR data, unstructured nursing notes (processed via natural language processing), and high-frequency vital sign streams. Sensitivity analyses will evaluate how staffing ratios, care pathway adjustments, and interdisciplinary communication protocols affect outcomes in agent-based simulations. HPC resources are essential for training ML models on multi-terabyte datasets, running computationally intensive simulations across diverse scenarios, and enabling real-time model validation. Expected outcomes include (1) risk prediction tools with ≥85% accuracy for adverse events, integrated into CNL workflows via a dashboard; (2) evidence-based recommendations for care team configurations under varying clinical demands; and (3) an open-source computational framework for nursing researchers to simulate care delivery models. By bridging high-performance analytics with frontline nursing practice, this work will empower CNLs to proactively mitigate risks, allocate resources efficiently, and demonstrate the translational impact of computational nursing science on patient safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the documentation and analysis of understudied languages in Southeast Asia and the Pacific, focusing on their morphosyntactic diversity, historical development, and sociolinguistic vitality. Many languages in these regions remain under-documented, with limited digital corpora, and are at risk of endangerment due to shifting linguistic ecologies. Traditional methods of manual analysis are insufficient for processing the growing volume of digitized recordings, texts, and metadata, necessitating scalable computational approaches. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply machine learning models for automated phonetic alignment, syntactic parsing, and cross-linguistic comparison. A key focus is the creation of language-specific NLP pipelines for Austronesian and Papuan languages, which present challenges such as complex clause chaining, tonal variation, and non-concatenative morphology. These pipelines will integrate transformer-based models fine-tuned on newly digitized field recordings and legacy texts, combined with phylogenetic algorithms to model language contact and divergence. Additionally, HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of language shift scenarios, informed by sociodemographic data, to assess preservation strategies. Expected outcomes include open-access corpora for 10+ endangered languages, a comparative database of grammatical structures, and methodological advancements in computational linguistics for low-resource contexts. The project will directly support collaborative revitalization efforts with Indigenous communities while advancing theoretical frameworks for understanding linguistic diversity in the region. By leveraging parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workflows, this work addresses computational bottlenecks in handling terabytes of multimodal data, enabling analyses previously infeasible on standard infrastructure. Results will inform both academic research and community-based language preservation initiatives, contributing to global efforts to safeguard intangible cultural heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian and Australasian/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of pharmacy operations, driven by advances in personalized medicine and high-volume dispensing workflows, necessitates novel computational tools to optimize medication safety and operational efficiency. This project addresses critical gaps in real-time error detection and workflow modeling within pharmacy technician workflows, which remain underexplored despite their direct impact on patient outcomes. Current rule-based systems for identifying dispensing errors or inventory mismatches lack adaptability to dynamic clinical contexts, while human-centric workflow analyses fail to account for multi-variable interactions in large-scale pharmacy environments. We propose the development of a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets spanning electronic health records, medication dispensing logs, and sensor-derived technician motion patterns. A hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) and temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) will be implemented to model complex relationships between drug properties, patient-specific factors, and operational constraints. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-resolution time-series data from 150+ institutional pharmacies, encompassing over 2.5 million annual transactions. Computational experiments will focus on two key areas: (1) probabilistic forecasting of context-dependent error risks during high-throughput dispensing tasks, and (2) agent-based simulation of workflow modifications under evolving regulatory and therapeutic paradigms. Validation will employ synthetic control methods comparing model predictions against prospective observational data from partner community hospitals. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive workflow optimization and a real-time error prevention API capable of processing 10,000+ concurrent transactions with <50ms latency. This work will provide unprecedented quantitative insights into latent risk factors in medication preparation workflows while establishing computational methods tailored to pharmacy technicians' evolving roles in precision medicine ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pharmacists, to prepare medications, provide medications and related assistance to patients, and manage pharmacy clinical and business operations. Includes instruction in medical and pharmaceutical terminology, principles of pharmacology and pharmaceutics, drug identification, pharmacy laboratory procedures, prescription interpretation, patient communication and education, safety procedures, record-keeping, measurement and testing techniques, pharmacy business operations, prescription preparation, logistics and dispensing operations, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of real-time image management for organizations navigating volatile digital media environments. Public relations professionals increasingly face complex, data-driven scenarios—such as crisis communications, misinformation spread, or reputation shifts—that require rapid analysis of massive multimedia datasets across social platforms, news outlets, and stakeholder networks. Traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to process these multimodal, high-velocity data streams while accounting for contextual factors like cultural nuance, platform-specific communication norms, and emergent narrative patterns. We propose developing a computational framework leveraging natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning to model reputation dynamics at scale. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on cross-platform communication datasets (text, image, video metadata), simulate information diffusion patterns through multiplex network models, and run ensemble forecasting systems to predict perception shifts. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of heterogeneous media data, maintaining low-latency analysis for real-time monitoring, and executing parallelized simulations of stakeholder response scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for automated sentiment tracking with contextual awareness of platform-specific semiotics, (2) probabilistic models identifying reputation risk thresholds in crisis situations, and (3) validation of network intervention strategies through large-scale agent-based simulations. By enabling precise measurement of communication impact across digital ecosystems, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in strategic message design while establishing computational social science methodologies tailored to public relations research. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the spatial-temporal complexity of global media landscapes and achieving the project’s goal of developing actionable, AI-enhanced frameworks for organizational image management.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories and methods for managing the media image of a business, organization, or individual and the communication process with stakeholders, constituencies, audiences, and the general public; and that prepares individuals to function as public relations assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in public relations theory; related principles of advertising, marketing, and journalism; message/image design; image management; special event management; media relations; community relations; public affairs; and internal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nursing education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize clinical training scenarios. A persistent gap exists in scalable, evidence-based methods for preparing nursing educators to design and evaluate clinical instruction, particularly in resource-constrained or high-demand settings. Traditional approaches to clinical education rely heavily on in-person placements, which are limited by capacity, variability in patient encounters, and inconsistent access to rare or high-risk scenarios. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates diverse clinical learning environments, predicts student competency outcomes, and identifies optimal instructional strategies. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning, we will create dynamic, data-driven simulations of clinical decision-making scenarios. These simulations will integrate anonymized electronic health record data, student performance metrics, and educator feedback to generate synthetic patient cases and learner interactions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of thousands of simulated training sessions, allowing us to test variables such as instructor-student ratios, case complexity, and intervention timing. Additionally, natural language processing will be applied to analyze qualitative feedback from nursing educators, identifying patterns in instructional effectiveness.
