The outcomes will include (1) a validated predictive model linking instructional design choices to competency development, (2) an open-access toolkit for generating adaptive clinical training modules, and (3) recommendations for balancing simulation-based and traditional clinical hours in nursing curricula. By quantifying relationships between educational inputs and learner outcomes, this work will directly inform accreditation standards and faculty development programs, ultimately enhancing the capacity of nursing educators to train clinicians capable of addressing complex healthcare needs. The scale and interdependencies of the datasets necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust, generalizable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to teach in academic and clinical settings, including staff development. Includes instruction in advanced nursing practice, nursing role development, curriculum and instruction, program and course design, clinical instruction, and evaluation of learning.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of modern security systems, which integrate IoT devices, machine learning-driven analytics, and multi-sensor networks, by developing computational tools to optimize their design, reliability, and real-time performance. Current industry practices for installing, inspecting, and maintaining these systems rely heavily on manual testing and static configurations, which struggle to adapt to dynamic environments or predict cascading failures in interconnected components. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale security networks under diverse threat and environmental scenarios, enabling data-driven insights into system vulnerabilities and performance thresholds. Agent-based modeling will simulate intrusion attempts and equipment malfunctions across virtual representations of commercial and residential spaces, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will assess environmental interference (e.g., temperature, airflow) on sensor accuracy. Parallelized machine learning frameworks will train anomaly detection models on heterogeneous datasets comprising sensor logs, video feeds, and historical breach records. These models will predict equipment degradation and recommend preemptive maintenance schedules. Additionally, combinatorial optimization algorithms will iteratively test security system layouts to minimize blind spots and latency in threat response. The computational workload demands scalable storage for petabyte-scale simulation outputs and GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time inference tasks. Outcomes include open-source tools for technicians to visualize system performance metrics, predictive maintenance protocols to reduce downtime, and evidence-based guidelines for configuring adaptive security networks. By bridging computational modeling with practical technician training, this project aims to elevate industry standards for security system resilience, reducing false alarms and critical failures by an estimated 30–40% in simulated scenarios. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in security technology programs, ensuring graduates are prepared to deploy next-generation, computation-aware solutions.
cip_title: Security System Installation, Repair, and Inspection Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair household, business, and industrial security alarms, sensors, video and sound recording devices, identification systems, protective barriers, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of contaminant transport and transformation in heterogeneous environmental systems. A critical challenge in environmental chemistry lies in understanding the coupled physical, chemical, and biological processes governing pollutant fate across scales—from molecular interactions at mineral-water interfaces to plume-scale reactive transport in soils and groundwater. Current models often oversimplify these dynamics due to computational constraints, limiting their utility for remediation planning or risk assessment. To address this gap, we propose multiscale simulations integrating quantum mechanical calculations, molecular dynamics (MD), and reactive transport modeling (RTM) to investigate the behavior of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and heavy metal complexes in iron oxide-rich soils. Quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT) will parameterize adsorption energetics and degradation pathways at mineral surfaces, while MD simulations resolve interfacial solvation dynamics. These outputs will inform continuum-scale RTM frameworks implemented in open-source codes (e.g., PFLOTRAN), simulating field-relevant scenarios with spatially variable hydrology and redox conditions. The HPC environment is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of reactive species, stochastic parameterization of heterogeneous media, and ensemble runs quantifying uncertainty. Anticipated outcomes include (1) mechanistically grounded rate laws for PFAS transformation under iron-reducing conditions, (2) scalable reactive transport workflows linking nanoscale interactions to macroscopic predictions, and (3) open-access datasets informing regulatory thresholds for co-contaminated sites. By resolving cross-scale feedbacks between pollutant chemistry and environmental matrices, this work aims to advance predictive tools for contaminant mitigation while establishing computational protocols adaptable to emerging contaminants of concern.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of natural systems (air, water, and soil) through the use of chemical techniques and instrumentation, with an emphasis on the movement and fate of pollutants and chemical aspects of contaminant remediation. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; aquatic, soil, and atmospheric chemistry; environmental engineering; environmental toxicology; and analytical methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the quantitative analysis of doctrinal and cultural evolution within the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS). While qualitative methods dominate Mormon Studies, the growing availability of digitized primary sources—including sermons, theological treatises, and organizational records spanning two centuries—presents an opportunity to systematically map shifts in religious thought, institutional priorities, and community identity. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational limitations of analyzing unstructured text corpora (e.g., 300,000+ pages of journals, conference addresses, and curriculum materials) and modeling complex socioreligious networks. Proposed work combines natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based analytics to (1) identify semantic patterns in theological discourse across time, (2) trace the diffusion of doctrinal interpretations through leadership hierarchies, and (3) correlate textual changes with sociopolitical events. Transformer models (e.g., BERT) will be fine-tuned to recognize Mormon-specific terminology, while distributed computing frameworks (Apache Spark) will enable large-scale topic modeling and sentiment analysis. Network graphs will map citation patterns and institutional influence using temporal graph neural networks. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus, interactive visualization tools for scholarly use, and quantitative frameworks to test hypotheses about religious adaptation. This computational approach addresses gaps in understanding how doctrinal flexibility intersects with institutional stability in the LDS tradition. The project’s scalability—dependent on HPC resources for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated model training—will set precedents for data-driven methodologies in religious studies while preserving disciplinary grounding in theological nuance. Results will inform broader interdisciplinary dialogues on religion’s role in shaping cultural resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on beliefs, practices, culture, and history of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormon). Includes instruction in Mormon culture, history, literature, philosophy, sociology, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the discovery and mechanistic analysis of bioactive natural products with therapeutic potential. Despite the rich diversity of compounds in plants, microbes, and marine organisms, identifying those with medicinal value remains labor-intensive and constrained by limitations in traditional experimental screening. Computational approaches can accelerate this process, but the scale of chemical space in natural product libraries and the complexity of modeling interactions between compounds and biological targets demand significant computational power. This project aims to address these challenges through two integrated computational workflows. First, molecular docking and virtual screening will be performed on a curated library of 500,000+ natural product structures to predict binding affinities for disease-relevant targets, including inflammatory enzymes and antimicrobial resistance proteins. Second, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will characterize the stability and conformational dynamics of top candidate complexes at atomic resolution, with simulations extending to the microsecond scale. These workflows will be complemented by machine learning models trained on existing bioactivity data to predict ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) properties, prioritizing compounds with viable pharmacokinetic profiles. The HPC environment is critical for managing the parallelized processing of large ligand/target datasets, long-timescale MD simulations requiring GPU acceleration, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel lead compounds for experimental validation, structural insights into target engagement mechanisms, and predictive frameworks to guide future bioprospecting efforts. By integrating computational chemistry with ethnobotanical knowledge and experimental data from collaborators (e.g., mass spectrometry, bioassay results), this work will enhance the efficiency of natural product drug discovery and contribute to the understanding of structure-activity relationships in medicinal chemistry. The requested resources will directly support these computationally intensive tasks, enabling workflows that are infeasible on standard laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into clinical dental research is critical for addressing complex challenges in diagnosis, treatment planning, and outcomes prediction. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale computational models that simulate biomechanical interactions in dental structures, analyze large-scale clinical datasets, and optimize treatment protocols for heterogeneous patient populations. The research problem centers on the limitations of conventional analytical tools in handling the nonlinear dynamics of dental materials, the variability of patient anatomy, and the integration of multi-modal data (e.g., radiographs, intraoral scans, electronic health records) required for personalized care. Using HPC clusters, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution in restored teeth under functional loads, machine learning algorithms to predict long-term outcomes of prosthodontic interventions, and agent-based simulations to evaluate practice management strategies in diverse clinical scenarios. The computational workflows will integrate anonymized patient datasets, including 3D imaging and longitudinal treatment records, to ensure clinical relevance. By parallelizing these processes, we aim to reduce simulation timescales from weeks to hours, enabling rapid iteration of treatment parameters. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for implant failure risk, data-driven guidelines for material selection in complex restorations, and scalable frameworks for optimizing clinical workflows. This work will directly advance evidence-based practices in advanced general dentistry, offering translational insights into precision care while reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical decision-making. The requested computing resources are essential to manage the project’s terabyte-scale data processing demands and computationally intensive simulations, which exceed the capacity of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of dental clinical techniques and dental practice issues. Includes instruction in subjects such as the history of dentistry, advanced dental practice management, dental ethics and jurisprudence, social and behavioral science studies of dentistry, advanced restorative dentistry, oral medicine, oral radiology, advanced clinical procedures and technology, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize meal planning for individuals with complex dietary needs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability and precision challenges in clinical dietetics. Current manual methods for designing personalized meal plans are labor-intensive and often struggle to balance dynamic variables such as nutritional requirements, allergen restrictions, cultural preferences, budgetary constraints, and real-time ingredient availability. The proposed research will construct a machine learning model trained on multi-source datasets, including national nutritional databases, electronic health records, and regional food cost and supply-chain data. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of these heterogeneous datasets to identify optimal ingredient combinations, portion sizes, and meal sequences while adhering to evidence-based dietary guidelines. The model will integrate constraint satisfaction algorithms to navigate trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., maximizing nutrient density while minimizing cost) and simulate longitudinal outcomes for chronic disease management scenarios. Validation will involve retrospective comparison against dietitian-created plans from clinical records and prospective testing through a pilot study with dietitian assistants. Successful implementation will yield an open-source tool that generates actionable, patient-specific meal recommendations in seconds—a process that currently takes hours. This tool aims to reduce cognitive workload for dietetic teams, improve adherence through culturally tailored options, and enhance scalability of nutrition interventions in underserved populations. The project’s computational demands—including large-scale matrix operations for nutrient optimization and Monte Carlo simulations for cost variability analysis—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically relevant throughput. Outcomes will advance both applied dietetics and computational methods in healthcare optimization, with potential integration into telehealth platforms and dietitian training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the long-term environmental and socioeconomic impacts on cultural heritage sites, integrating multidisciplinary datasets to inform preservation policy and management strategies. Cultural heritage systems face compounding threats from climate change, urbanization, and tourism, yet existing decision-making frameworks often rely on fragmented or static data. This research addresses the critical gap in predictive, scalable tools capable of simulating dynamic interactions between environmental stressors, policy interventions, and community engagement outcomes. By developing agent-based models (ABMs) and geospatial simulations, the project will quantify risks to archaeological sites, historic structures, and intangible cultural practices under varying climate and policy scenarios. Computational workflows will fuse remote sensing data, ethnographic records, material degradation metrics, and socioeconomic indicators to parameterize models. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution geospatial inputs, run Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty analysis, and optimize machine learning algorithms that identify vulnerable regions or artifacts. Anticipated outcomes include a modular, open-source platform for simulating preservation trade-offs (e.g., tourism revenue vs. site degradation) and policy impact visualizations to support stakeholder negotiations. The project advances interdisciplinary methodology by bridging computational archaeology, policy informatics, and heritage economics, offering scalable tools for agencies managing UNESCO World Heritage sites and other at-risk locales. Results will be disseminated through a public dashboard for policymakers and peer-reviewed modules integrating with existing cultural resource management software. This work underscores the role of computational social science in sustaining cultural heritage amid 21st-century global challenges.
cip_title: Cultural Resource Management and Policy Analysis
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of cultural studies, public policy analysis, and management skills to planning, promoting, and implementing programs to preserve and protect cultural heritage sites and artifacts. Includes instruction in historical preservation and conservation, business management, policy analysis, applied economics, public relations, applied history, historical archaeology, and environmental impact studies.

abstract: Acoustic wave propagation in complex, heterogeneous media presents significant challenges for predictive modeling, particularly in environments where material properties, boundaries, and external conditions interact nonlinearly. This project seeks to advance computational methods for simulating broadband acoustic phenomena in two key domains: underwater sound transmission in dynamically varying oceanographic conditions and ultrasound scattering in biologically realistic tissue models for diagnostic applications. The research employs high-resolution 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations coupled with stochastic parameterization of environmental variables, requiring parallelized computation at scale. Key objectives include resolving wave interactions with anisotropic seabed sediments (incorporating viscoelastic attenuation and poroelastic effects) and quantifying uncertainty in medical ultrasound predictions due to tissue microstructure variability. The computational framework integrates GPU-accelerated solvers for the acoustic wave equation with adjoint-based optimization to infer material properties from synthetic aperture scattering data. Memory-intensive simulations will model domains spanning 10–100 wavelengths, with grid resolutions fine enough to capture sub-wavelength geometric features and dispersion effects. Expected outcomes include validated numerical benchmarks for multi-physics acoustic environments, open-source tools for parameter sensitivity analysis, and improved inversion algorithms for reconstructing hidden interfaces in cluttered media. These results will address critical gaps in predictive capability for sonar performance in climate-impacted oceans and ultrasound-based tumor margin detection, where existing ray-tracing and linear scattering approximations prove inadequate. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential to handle O(10^12)-degree-of-freedom problems, Monte Carlo parameter ensembles, and data assimilation workflows that exceed the capacity of local cluster infrastructure. By advancing scalable computational acoustics methods, this work aims to bridge theoretical wave physics with applied challenges in environmental sensing and biomedical diagnostics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of sound, and the properties and behavior of acoustic wave phenomena under different conditions. Includes instruction in wave theory, the acoustic wave equation, energy transformation, vibration phenomena, sound reflection and transmission, scattering and surface wave phenomena, singularity expansion theory, ducting, and applications to specific research problems such as underwater acoustics, crystallography, and health diagnostics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to enhance the security and reliability of mechanical and electronic locking systems, addressing critical vulnerabilities in modern safe and lock designs. Traditional locksmithing methods rely heavily on physical testing and iterative manual adjustments, which are time-consuming, costly, and insufficient for addressing increasingly sophisticated security threats. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex lock mechanisms, analyze material stress under forced entry attempts, and optimize combination algorithms for electronic safes. The research will focus on three primary areas: (1) finite element analysis (FEA) of lock components under mechanical stress to identify failure points and improve durability, (2) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of thermal attacks on safes to evaluate insulation performance, and (3) machine learning-driven simulations to predict vulnerabilities in digital lock systems against brute-force and side-channel attacks. These computational approaches will integrate multi-physics simulations and probabilistic risk assessment frameworks, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle large datasets and iterative optimization tasks. The outcomes will include predictive models for lock and safe failure modes, validated against empirical data from industry partners, and open-source tools for designing next-generation security systems. By bridging computational engineering with traditional locksmithing practices, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive security system development, reducing reliance on reactive repairs. The requested HPC resources will enable scalability in simulating diverse attack scenarios and material behaviors, which are infeasible with local computing infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops for locksmithing professionals and peer-reviewed publications, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational scientists and security technology experts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, modify, and open locks; to make keys; to enter and change lock and safe combinations; and install and repair safes.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation spacecraft thermal protection systems (TPS) for high-speed atmospheric entries, a critical challenge in planetary exploration and crewed spaceflight. Current TPS materials and configurations face extreme aerothermal loads during hypersonic deceleration, but existing predictive models lack the resolution to capture coupled thermochemical ablation, turbulent boundary layer transitions, and microscale material responses under real flight conditions. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining direct numerical simulation (DNS) of reactive hypersonic flows with finite element modeling of anisotropic carbon composite degradation. The approach leverages high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFS3D-HyCAP) and material response (CHAR) codes, coupled through a novel implicit boundary data transfer algorithm to resolve bidirectional fluid-structure interactions. Simulations will utilize adaptive mesh refinement to track ablation fronts and localized heating spikes while maintaining computational tractability. The research requires access to high-performance computing resources for three primary workloads: 1) petascale DNS of turbulent reacting boundary layers (10^8-10^9 grid points), 2) ensemble-based parameter optimization of TPS layup configurations using Monte Carlo methods, and 3) machine learning surrogate model training on multi-terabyte simulation datasets. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for TPS performance under Venusian and Martian entry profiles, identification of optimal porous material architectures for heat flux mitigation, and open-source release of optimized coupling libraries for the aerospace community. This work directly supports NASA’s Moon-to-Mars objectives by enabling lighter, more reliable thermal protection systems, with potential performance improvements of 15-20% in mass-specific heat rejection capacity compared to current Artemis-era designs.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any program in aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, or space engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance genomic and phenotypic prediction models for optimizing crop resilience and yield under climate variability. A critical challenge in plant sciences is bridging the gap between genomic data and field-scale outcomes to accelerate the development of stress-tolerant cultivars. Traditional breeding approaches struggle to integrate multi-omics datasets, environmental variables, and complex genotype-by-environment interactions efficiently. We propose a computational framework combining machine learning, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and mechanistic crop models to predict plant responses to abiotic stressors such as drought and heat. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of genomic data from diverse germplasm collections, high-resolution climate projections, and sensor-derived phenotypic data. Key tasks include training neural networks to identify stress-responsive genetic markers, simulating crop growth under projected climate scenarios using modified Agricultural Production Systems sIMulator (APSIM) modules, and optimizing genomic selection pipelines via distributed computing. The integration of these methods will facilitate the discovery of candidate genes and metabolic pathways linked to stress tolerance while quantifying their agronomic impact. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for breeders, validated gene-editing targets for experimental validation, and scalable models to prioritize crop varieties for specific environments. By reducing computational bottlenecks in analyzing terabyte-scale datasets, this work will directly support climate-resilient crop development, aligning with global food security priorities. The requested resources will ensure timely processing of complex datasets, enabling iterative model refinement and collaboration with experimental labs to translate computational insights into field applications.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding, cultivation, and production of agricultural plants, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural plant products. Includes instruction in the plant sciences, crop cultivation and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal analysis within the domain of international law, specifically focusing on the automated identification and predictive modeling of treaty compliance patterns. The research addresses a critical gap in legal scholarship: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to analyze the complex interplay between treaty text, state behavior, and compliance outcomes across vast temporal and jurisdictional scales. Traditional legal methods struggle to process the growing volume of multilateral agreements, case law, and compliance reports, which now span decades and involve thousands of actors. To overcome this, the project will develop a novel computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based network analysis to map obligations, reservations, and compliance triggers embedded in treaty texts. These outputs will be integrated with historical state practice data to train machine learning models capable of predicting compliance risks under varying geopolitical scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing multilingual legal corpora (e.g., UN treaty collections, ICJ rulings), running parallelized semantic analysis of treaty clauses, and simulating multi-agent interactions in hypothetical dispute scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access repository of computationally annotated treaty networks, 2) a predictive compliance risk dashboard for use by legal practitioners and policymakers, and 3) new interdisciplinary methodologies for quantifying ambiguity in treaty language. By bridging computational science and international legal theory, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-intensive legal research while providing actionable insights into the design of more enforceable international agreements. The resource request aligns with strategic priorities in legal informatics, where computational scalability is increasingly vital to addressing global governance challenges in a multipolar world.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law affecting relations between nations, the behavior of international organizations, and the international activities of private citizens and organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance pharmacoeconomic and policy analyses critical to optimizing medication access, pharmacy service delivery, and regulatory decision-making. A key challenge in pharmacy administration is modeling the multi-faceted impacts of drug pricing policies, insurance reimbursement structures, and healthcare system constraints on patient outcomes and costs. Existing approaches often oversimplify dynamic interactions between stakeholders (e.g., patients, providers, payers, manufacturers) or fail to account for large-scale real-world data, limiting predictive accuracy and policy relevance. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework integrating electronic health records, insurance claims, and drug supply chain data to model the cascading effects of policy changes on medication utilization, health disparities, and system-wide expenditures. Computational demands arise from simulating millions of agent interactions across diverse demographic and geographic scenarios, requiring parallelized parameter sweeps and machine learning-driven sensitivity analyses. Additionally, we will apply natural language processing to analyze regulatory documents and public comment databases, identifying trends in policy implementation barriers and stakeholder concerns. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets and reduce runtime for iterative model calibration from months to days. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source policy simulation toolkit for evaluating proposed legislation, plus evidence-based recommendations to streamline drug approval processes and reduce administrative burdens in pharmacy practice. By quantifying trade-offs between cost containment and equitable access, this work will directly inform state and federal agencies, healthcare organizations, and pharmacy leaders in designing data-driven policies that balance economic sustainability with patient-centered care.
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) with architectural heritage preservation, addressing the challenge of dynamically modeling and simulating culturally significant built environments at scale. While computational tools are increasingly used in architectural design, their application to heritage contexts remains limited by the complexity of encoding intangible cultural narratives, adaptive reuse scenarios, and multi-temporal degradation patterns into predictive models. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework that synthesizes architectural typology analysis, material decay simulations, and socio-spatial behavior modeling to generate adaptive preservation strategies for historic urban districts. The proposed methodology employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to map relationships between architectural elements and cultural values across historical datasets, coupled with physics-informed reinforcement learning to simulate material weathering and intervention outcomes under varying climate scenarios. High-fidelity agent-based modeling will further assess how preservation measures impact community engagement and spatial use patterns. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the project aims to overcome current limitations in processing lidar-scanned heritage site data (≥10TB), running multi-parameter optimization for conservation plans, and rendering interactive 3D visualizations of temporal change. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for heritage-driven urban planning, validated through case studies on UNESCO World Heritage sites, that bridges architectural conservation theory with scalable AI-driven simulation. This work positions HPC as critical infrastructure for preserving cultural memory in rapidly urbanizing contexts while establishing new computational paradigms at the intersection of architectural history, materials science, and community-centered design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of architecture and to conduct research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in architectural design, history, and theory; building structures and environmental systems; project and site planning; construction; professional responsibilities and standards; and related cultural, social, economic, and environmental issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interactions of pigments, binders, and solvents in acrylic and oil painting techniques, addressing gaps in understanding how material behaviors influence artistic outcomes. While traditional painting research relies on empirical experimentation, the chemical complexity of modern media—such as acrylic polymer suspensions or oxidized oil binders—creates nonlinear relationships between application methods, drying kinetics, and final visual properties. Current analytical tools struggle to predict outcomes for novel hybrid techniques or non-traditional substrates. To bridge this gap, we propose multiscale simulations combining molecular dynamics (MD) to model pigment-binder interactions at atomic scales, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for brushstroke-level paint deposition, and machine learning (ML) to correlate simulation data with empirical colorimetry and texture metrics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the MD simulations’ nanosecond-scale trajectories (requiring ~1M CPU-hours) and train physics-informed neural networks on heterogeneous datasets spanning quantum chemistry calculations, hyperspectral imaging of historical paintings, and 3D microscopy of experimental samples. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for paint formulation effects on opacity, sheen, and crack propagation, as well as an open-access database linking computational parameters to perceptual art metrics. This work will provide painters with evidence-based guidance for innovating techniques while preserving material longevity, benefiting conservation science and educational practices in the visual arts. By integrating computational materials science with aesthetic inquiry, the project establishes a paradigm for data-driven artistic research, expanding the tools available for both technical and conceptual explorations in painting.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by the application of paints and related chemical color substances to canvases or other materials. Includes instruction in color and color mixing, surface preparation, composition, oil and acrylic media, watercolor media, painting techniques, and personal style development.

abstract: Speech-language disorders significantly impact communication, necessitating timely and accurate assessment. Current clinical methods rely on manual analysis of speech samples, which is labor-intensive and subject to variability. This project seeks to develop computational tools leveraging machine learning to automate the analysis of speech patterns, enhancing diagnostic precision and treatment personalization. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process and analyze large datasets of audio recordings from individuals with disorders such as aphasia, dysarthria, and childhood apraxia of speech. Computational methods include deep neural networks for acoustic feature extraction, natural language processing to evaluate linguistic structures, and ensemble models to classify disorder subtypes. Additionally, simulations of language processing networks will model neurophysiological underpinnings of speech pathologies. The scale of data (thousands of hours of speech samples) and complexity of models require parallelized computing for efficient training and validation. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for automated speech analysis, validated against clinician assessments, and computational frameworks to predict treatment responses based on individual profiles. These tools will support speech-language pathology assistants in streamlining screenings, optimizing therapy plans, and contributing to research datasets. By integrating computational advancements with clinical expertise, this project aims to improve access to high-quality care, particularly in resource-limited settings, while providing SLPA students with hands-on experience in data-driven methodologies. The requested resources are critical to managing the computational demands of multimodal data integration and ensuring reproducible, scalable solutions for the speech-language pathology community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: Hemodialysis efficiency is critically dependent on the dynamic interactions between blood, dialysate, and membrane materials within dialyzers. However, current empirical methods for optimizing treatment parameters—such as flow rates, membrane pore geometries, and anticoagulant distribution—fail to capture the multiscale, nonlinear fluid-structure interactions that govern solute clearance and clotting risk. This project proposes a computational approach to model these phenomena at unprecedented resolution, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to advance personalized dialysis protocols. The primary research problem centers on the lack of predictive frameworks to guide individualized dialyzer operation, particularly for patients with atypical vascular access or heightened thrombotic susceptibility. To address this, we will develop multiphysics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), solute transport modeling, and machine learning-driven parameter optimization. These simulations will resolve 3D spatiotemporal variations in shear stress, solute concentration gradients, and fibrinogen-membrane binding kinetics across clinically relevant dialyzer geometries and flow conditions. Validation will utilize anonymized patient data, including pressure transients and biomarker levels from dialysis sessions. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational load, as each simulation involves ~10^8 mesh elements and iterative solvers for coupled Navier-Stokes and advection-diffusion equations. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for thrombosis risk and urea/phosphorus clearance rates under variable operational parameters, enabling the derivation of patient-specific optimization strategies. By identifying non-intuitive relationships between flow modulation and solute extraction efficiency, this work could reduce treatment-related complications (e.g., clotting, hypotension) by an estimated 15-20% in modeled cohorts. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will provide renal technologists with a novel decision-support platform, bridging the gap between theoretical transport principles and real-world clinical constraints. This interdisciplinary integration of biomedical engineering, computational mathematics, and renal therapy represents a transformative approach to dialysis technology development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Fire dynamics in complex urban and industrial environments present critical challenges for firefighter safety, structural preservation, and emergency response efficiency. Current predictive models often lack the resolution to account for multi-scale interactions between turbulent combustion, heat transfer, and suppression system performance, particularly in large-scale or geometrically intricate scenarios. This project proposes an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to advance fire behavior prediction and mitigation strategy optimization. Using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis, we will simulate fire spread, structural degradation, and suppression agent dispersion at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Large eddy simulations (LES) will resolve turbulent combustion dynamics, while machine learning models trained on HPC-generated datasets will identify optimal nozzle configurations and water droplet size distributions for varied fuel loads and ventilation conditions. The research will also model thermal-induced failure thresholds of modern construction materials under combined mechanical and fire stresses. By parallelizing Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS) workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to achieve real-time predictive capabilities for incident commanders during evolving emergencies. Anticipated outcomes include validated protocols for adaptive ventilation tactics in high-rise fires, predictive tools for wildfire-urban interface scenarios, and quantitative guidelines for retrofitting fire protection systems in energy storage facilities. These advancements will directly enhance firefighter operational decision-making, improve building code recommendations, and reduce collateral damage in complex fire events. The computational datasets and open-source model extensions produced will serve as critical resources for both academic research and industrial fire safety engineering applications within the homeland security ecosystem.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: Public works systems are critical to community well-being, yet municipalities face persistent challenges in optimizing infrastructure maintenance, resource distribution, and operational resilience under constrained budgets. This project seeks to develop a computational decision-support framework to model public works management scenarios, with a focus on balancing fiscal responsibility, equity, and long-term infrastructure performance. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to simulate the interdependencies between aging infrastructure networks, climate stressors, and dynamic population needs—a gap that limits evidence-based policymaking. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models to simulate infrastructure degradation patterns, workforce allocation dynamics, and budget trade-offs across multiple urban systems (e.g., transportation, water, utilities). Computational workflows will integrate geospatial data, historical maintenance records, and demographic projections to evaluate "what-if" scenarios under varying funding levels and policy interventions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify non-linear relationships between maintenance investments and service outcomes, while optimization algorithms will propose resource allocation strategies that minimize lifecycle costs and maximize equity metrics. The project will validate models against case studies from three midsized U.S. cities, calibrating parameters through partnerships with municipal agencies. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for public works planners, a comparative analysis of management strategies under fiscal constraints, and a cost-benefit framework for prioritizing infrastructure upgrades. By quantifying the long-term impacts of budgetary decisions on service quality and community resilience, this work aims to advance operational standards in public administration while providing scalable computational methods for resource-limited jurisdictions. The HPC environment is essential to process high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets and run parallelized simulations at metropolitan scales, enabling insights that traditional analytical tools cannot capture.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: Dental pulp vitality is critical to tooth longevity, yet current diagnostic methods for early pulp inflammation lack sensitivity, often leading to delayed intervention and irreversible necrosis. This project addresses the challenge of identifying molecular biomarkers predictive of reversible versus irreversible pulpitis through computational modeling of pulp tissue microenvironment dynamics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data from clinical pulp samples with spatially resolved biomechanical models of intrapulpal pressure changes during inflammatory progression. A multiscale computational framework will be developed to simulate cell-cell signaling networks (Notch, Wnt) under varying inflammatory cytokine gradients, coupled with finite element analysis of fluid dynamics within the confined pulp chamber geometry. Machine learning classifiers will then identify biomarker combinations that correlate with transition thresholds between recoverable and non-recoverable states. The HPC environment is essential for processing 10+ TB of spatial transcriptomic data, running agent-based inflammatory cascade simulations (>10⁶ cellular agents), and iteratively training predictive models across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital twin platform for in silico testing of diagnostic strategies and a ranked biomarker panel validated against longitudinal clinical data. This work bridges computational biology and dental pathophysiology to enable precision endodontics, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving early intervention accuracy. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulation workflows, large-scale parallelized parameter optimization, and secure HIPAA-compliant data integration from clinical partners.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the morphology, physiology, and pathology of human dental pulp and periradicular tissues, and prepares dentists to diagnose and treat internal diseases and injuries of teeth. Includes instruction in theory and practice of endodontics; pulpal disease; relationship of endodontic conditions to other dental/oral health issues; endodontic operative technique; and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of designing next-generation composite materials with tailored thermal and mechanical stability for extreme environment applications, such as energy-efficient industrial manufacturing systems and high-temperature processing equipment. Current experimental approaches to optimize material microstructures and interfacial properties are time-intensive and costly, limiting rapid innovation. To overcome this, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating quantum-mechanical simulations, phase-field modeling, and machine learning (ML) to predict the evolution of material behavior under thermomechanical stress. Density functional theory (DFT) will model atomic-scale interactions in ceramic-metal composites, while phase-field methods will simulate mesoscale grain growth and crack propagation at elevated temperatures. An ML surrogate model, trained on this multiscale data, will accelerate the exploration of processing parameters (e.g., sintering temperatures, particle size distributions) to optimize interfacial adhesion and thermal shock resistance. The proposed work requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the computational intensity of concurrent DFT calculations (VASP), large-scale phase-field simulations (MOOSE/FEniCS), and neural network training across diverse parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for composite design, identification of three candidate material systems with ≥20% improved high-temperature durability over existing alloys, and open-access datasets linking processing conditions to microstructure-property relationships. This research directly supports the Materials Engineering program’s mission by advancing computational tools for efficient materials development, reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, and addressing industry needs for robust materials in harsh operational environments. Results will inform experimental synthesis campaigns and provide foundational data for curriculum modules on computational materials design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and materials science principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and related processes used in manufacturing in a wide variety of settings; the synthesis of new industrial materials, including marrying and bonding composites; analysis of materials requirements and specifications; and related problems of system design dependent on materials factors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in holistic and integrative health by addressing the challenge of modeling complex, multidimensional interactions among biological, behavioral, and environmental factors that influence wellness. Holistic health emphasizes the interconnectedness of physical, psychological, and environmental systems, yet existing analytical tools often struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as genomic, microbiome, lifestyle, and clinical data—while accounting for dynamic, nonlinear relationships. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning, network analysis, and agent-based modeling to simulate how interventions like mindfulness, herbal medicine, or nutrition interact with individual biopsychosocial profiles. The project will aggregate longitudinal datasets from clinical studies on stress management, microbiome diversity, and metabolic health, applying ensemble learning methods to identify predictive biomarkers of wellness outcomes. Network models will map how perturbations in one domain (e.g., gut microbiota) propagate through interconnected systems (e.g., immune function, mental health). Agent-based simulations will test personalized intervention strategies under varying environmental conditions. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses, as the computational demands of training multi-modal models, handling high-dimensional data, and running stochastic simulations exceed the capacity of local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide individualized holistic care plans, (2) mechanistic insights into synergies between conventional and complementary therapies, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic health system modeling. By elucidating the systems-level effects of integrative interventions, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in preventive health and chronic disease management while demonstrating the transformative role of computational science in holistic health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the holistic interconnectedness of physical, psychological, social, spiritual, and environmental well-being and that integrates aspects of alternative, complementary, and conventional medicine to alleviate illness and promote, maintain, and optimize wellness. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, alternative diagnostic and healing methods, aromatherapy, biofeedback, energy medicine, environmental psychology, ethics, health coaching, herbal medicine, mind-body medicine, mindfulness, nutrition, somatic bodywork, and stress management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize prehospital emergency response protocols through advanced simulation and predictive analytics, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Prehospital care delivery in dynamic, high-stakes environments requires rapid decision-making under uncertainty, yet current protocols often rely on static guidelines that inadequately account for real-time variables such as patient acuity, resource availability, and logistical constraints. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale modeling approach integrating agent-based simulations, machine learning, and geospatial analytics. Agent-based models will simulate EMT workflows, patient interactions, and resource allocation across diverse emergency scenarios (e.g., multi-casualty incidents, mass casualty events). Machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized historical dispatch data, patient outcomes, and environmental factors (e.g., traffic patterns, weather) will predict optimal resource deployment strategies. Geospatial models will map response times and coverage gaps across urban and rural regions. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive models, enabling parallel processing of large datasets (e.g., regional EMS records, real-time telemetry feeds) and iterative scenario testing. The computational pipeline will be validated against retrospective case data and piloted in partnership with regional EMS agencies. Anticipated outcomes include data-driven protocols for dynamic triage prioritization, predictive tools for ambulance dispatch routing, and simulated training environments for EMT personnel. This work aims to reduce critical time-to-interval metrics (e.g., on-scene arrival, definitive care access) by 15–20% in modeled scenarios, directly addressing systemic inefficiencies in prehospital care. By bridging computational science and emergency medicine, this project will provide a scalable platform for improving evidence-based practices in EMT education and operational decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the remote supervision of physicians, to recognize, assess, and manage medical emergencies in prehospital settings and to supervise Ambulance personnel. Includes instruction in basic, intermediate, and advanced EMT procedures; emergency surgical procedures; medical triage; rescue operations; crisis scene management and personnel supervision; equipment operation and maintenance; patient stabilization, monitoring, and care; drug administration; identification and preliminary diagnosis of diseases and injuries; communication and computer operations; basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing computational demands of real-time, high-fidelity 3D rendering and interactive media production in graphic communications. As digital storytelling and immersive journalism increasingly rely on photorealistic visualizations, traditional rendering pipelines struggle to balance quality, interactivity, and scalability. The core challenge lies in optimizing complex rendering workflows—including ray tracing, dynamic lighting, and multi-user synchronization—for time-sensitive applications in virtual production and augmented reality environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a distributed rendering framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will implement parallelized rendering algorithms using GPU-accelerated nodes, coupled with machine learning models for predictive resource allocation during scene preprocessing. Computational experiments will benchmark rendering times, frame rate consistency, and energy efficiency across varying node configurations and scene complexities using industry-standard assets from Unreal Engine and Unity workflows. A secondary focus involves simulating networked collaboration scenarios to test latency thresholds in multi-user creative environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive rendering resource management and performance guidelines for HPC-supported graphic communication systems. This work will directly benefit media production pipelines requiring rapid iteration of high-resolution visual content while maintaining artistic control. By quantifying the relationship between computational resource allocation and perceptual quality metrics, the research aims to establish best practices for deploying HPC infrastructure in graphic communications education and professional workflows, particularly for emerging applications in immersive journalism and virtual set design. Results will be validated through case studies with partner media organizations, measuring productivity gains in collaborative 3D content creation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in graphic communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Critical illness in surgical patients, particularly trauma victims and those with multi-organ dysfunction, presents complex clinical challenges requiring rapid, data-driven decisions. Current predictive models for outcomes such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and mortality lack sufficient granularity to account for dynamic interactions between organ systems, limiting their clinical utility. This project proposes to develop multi-scale computational models integrating real-time physiological data, electronic health records, and biomarker profiles to predict clinical trajectories in critically ill surgical patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process high-dimensional datasets from 4,500+ trauma ICU patients, including continuous vital sign streams, laboratory results, and radiographic imaging metadata. Machine learning approaches (recurrent neural networks, gradient-boosted decision trees) will be combined with mechanistic models of systemic inflammation and organ crosstalk to simulate patient-specific pathophysiology. Computational workflows will require parallel processing of time-series data at 5-second resolutions across 72-hour clinical windows, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework identifying early signatures of clinical deterioration 6-12 hours before current diagnostic thresholds, (2) mechanistic insights into multi-organ failure pathways, and (3) open-source tools for simulating individualized treatment responses. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive analyses of petabyte-scale datasets and executing ensemble modeling approaches across parameter spaces. Successful implementation could transform resource allocation in surgical ICUs by enabling proactive interventions, optimizing trial designs for critical care therapies, and establishing a template for computationally augmented clinical decision-making in acute care settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares surgeons in the diagnosis, treatment, and support of critically ill and injured patients, particularly trauma victims and patients with multiple organ dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of data-driven diagnostic tools for reading difficulties, a critical challenge in reading teacher education. Current methods for diagnosing and addressing reading challenges often rely on static assessments or qualitative analysis, which may overlook complex interactions between linguistic, cognitive, and socio-environmental factors. To address this gap, the research proposes a computational approach integrating large-scale datasets of student reading performance, eye-tracking metrics, phonological processing assessments, and demographic variables. Machine learning models—including ensemble methods and neural networks—will be trained to identify patterns predictive of specific reading difficulties, such as dyslexia or comprehension deficits. These models will also simulate the efficacy of targeted instructional strategies under varied learner profiles. The scale and dimensionality of the data (spanning thousands of students, multilingual corpora, and high-frequency temporal data from eye-tracking sensors) necessitate HPC resources for efficient preprocessing, parallelized model training, and hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks to classify reading challenges with higher accuracy than existing tools, (2) generative models to propose individualized intervention plans, and (3) interactive visualization tools to help educators interpret model outputs. By bridging computational analytics and reading pedagogy, this work aims to equip teacher education programs with scalable, evidence-based resources for training reading specialists. The resulting tools will be validated through partnerships with K-12 literacy clinics, ensuring translational impact. This project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in addressing heterogeneous educational needs while adhering to ethical AI practices in teacher preparation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose reading difficulties and to teach reading programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing wine program management in hospitality settings, addressing the intersection of sensory science, supply chain logistics, and consumer behavior analytics. While traditional sommelier training emphasizes experiential knowledge, the increasing complexity of global wine markets, climate-driven variability in vintage quality, and shifting consumer preferences demand data-driven decision-making tools. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including regional climate records, biochemical profiles of wines, historical sales data, and real-time consumer feedback—to model dynamic strategies for inventory selection, pricing, and food pairing recommendations. Computational challenges arise from the need to process high-dimensional sensory data (e.g., mass spectrometry outputs for tannin structures), simulate long-term aging outcomes under variable storage conditions, and apply natural language processing to unstructured reviews or pairing descriptions. The proposed methodology combines graph neural networks to map relationships between terroir characteristics and flavor profiles, agent-based modeling to forecast regional market trends, and reinforcement learning to adapt inventory strategies under supply chain uncertainties. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across HPC nodes, the project will quantify risk metrics for rare wine investments and evaluate preservation protocols under stochastic environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for sommeliers to visualize region-specific climate impacts on emerging vintages, optimize cellar configurations via digital twin simulations, and dynamically adjust menu pairings using real-time sentiment analysis. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between enology, computational logistics, and hospitality analytics, offering a novel paradigm for data-informed wine stewardship while maintaining alignment with traditional sensory evaluation frameworks. The scalability of models developed through this work may later extend to broader applications in perishable goods management and experiential retail analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage wine selection, purchasing, storage, sales, and service for a variety of establishments in the hospitality industry. Includes instruction in wine production, wine regions of the world, wine tasting, food and wine matching, service techniques, and wine program management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance wind energy technology by optimizing the design and operational efficiency of wind turbine systems through high-fidelity computational modeling. Wind energy systems face persistent challenges in maximizing energy capture, minimizing structural fatigue under dynamic loads, and mitigating wake interference effects in wind farms—all of which are governed by complex, multiscale fluid-structure interactions. Current empirical and low-resolution modeling approaches struggle to resolve these coupled phenomena with sufficient accuracy, limiting predictive capabilities for turbine performance and longevity. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled study coupling large-eddy simulations (LES) of atmospheric boundary layer turbulence with finite element analysis (FEA) of turbine structural dynamics. The LES framework will resolve sub-meter-scale turbulent flow structures around turbine blades and across wind farm arrays, while FEA models will simulate stress distributions and material responses in rotor components under transient loads. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify patterns in the multivariate data and accelerate parametric optimization of blade geometries and farm layouts. The computational workload demands scalable HPC resources due to the high spatial-temporal resolution required for turbulence modeling, the coupled multi-physics simulations, and the iterative nature of design optimization. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for turbine performance under realistic operating conditions, data-driven guidelines for wake management in clustered turbine arrays, and optimized blade designs that balance energy efficiency with fatigue resistance. By enabling these advances, the project aims to reduce levelized costs of wind energy, extend turbine service lifetimes, and inform next-generation wind farm deployment strategies. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and collaborations with industry partners to accelerate the translation of computational insights into practical engineering solutions for renewable energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing wind-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in wind energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: The efficient allocation of social services remains a critical challenge in public administration, particularly in addressing disparities among vulnerable populations. Traditional policy evaluation methods often rely on simplified models that fail to capture the dynamic interactions between socioeconomic factors, institutional constraints, and individual behaviors. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate the impact of social service interventions on heterogeneous populations, enabling data-driven decision-making. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct an agent-based model integrating multi-source data—including census records, service utilization histories, and real-time socioeconomic indicators—to emulate decision-making processes at individual, community, and institutional levels. The computational approach will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess policy scenarios under varying demographic and economic conditions, coupled with machine learning techniques to identify latent patterns in service access barriers. By scaling these analyses across millions of synthetic agents, the project aims to quantify trade-offs between resource allocation strategies, predict unintended consequences of policy changes, and optimize service delivery networks. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the memory-intensive datasets and computationally demanding iterative simulations, which exceed the capacity of local computing resources. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible policy simulation toolkit for municipal planners, evidence-based recommendations for reducing service disparities, and methodological advances in computational social science applications within public administration. This work directly supports the program’s mission to enhance societal well-being through innovative administrative strategies grounded in rigorous, scalable analytical frameworks.
cip_title: Public Administration and Social Service Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public administration and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Radiation-induced genomic instability (RIGI) is a delayed biological phenomenon where cellular damage manifests generations after initial exposure, posing significant challenges for accurate risk assessment in low-dose radiation environments. Current models, predominantly linear-no-threshold (LNT)-based, fail to capture non-linear dynamics and intercellular signaling pathways implicated in RIGI, limiting predictive accuracy for occupational and environmental exposure scenarios. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate RIGI mechanisms by integrating multi-scale models of DNA repair processes, bystander effects, and systemic immune responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to track radiation-induced double-strand breaks (DSBs) across spatial and temporal scales, coupled with stochastic simulations of error-prone repair pathways. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will parameterize DSB repair fidelity under varying radiation qualities (e.g., alpha particles vs. gamma rays), while graph neural networks (GNNs) will map intercellular communication networks driving bystander effects. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from human lymphocyte cultures exposed to chronic low-dose radiation (0.1–100 mGy), with single-cell RNA sequencing used to refine model training. By parallelizing simulations across GPU clusters, we aim to resolve time-delayed genomic destabilization patterns over simulated timescales equivalent to 5–10 years post-exposure. Outcomes will include predictive biomarkers for RIGI susceptibility, probabilistic risk models for radiation workers, and a publicly accessible HPC-optimized codebase for simulating delayed radiation effects. This work addresses critical gaps in radiation protection paradigms by enabling real-time, systems-level analysis of low-dose risks, directly informing safety protocols for nuclear medicine technicians, decontamination workflows, and spaceflight radiation monitoring systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health physicists, occupational safety and health specialists, and public health officials, to monitor and control radiation exposure and implement preventive measures in health care, work, and natural environments. Includes instruction in radiation physics, environmental radioactivity, radiological instrumentation, electronics of radiation detection equipment, radioactive waste management and control, safety and handling procedures, decontamination procedures, radioactivity testing and analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cytopathological data, driven by advances in high-resolution digital imaging and molecular profiling, presents significant challenges in analyzing cellular alterations for disease diagnosis and prognosis. Current computational workflows struggle to efficiently process and integrate multi-modal datasets—including gigapixel whole-slide images, single-cell RNA sequencing, and proteomic profiles—while maintaining diagnostic rigor. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable, AI-driven frameworks for cytopathological analysis. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating deep learning models optimized for automated detection of rare malignant cells in large-scale cytology screenings, and (2) establishing computational pipelines to correlate cellular morphometric features with molecular alterations across diverse cancer types. The computational approach will utilize convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms for image analysis, graph-based algorithms for spatial feature extraction, and federated learning architectures to handle distributed datasets while preserving patient privacy. HPC resources will be critical for training complex models on terabyte-scale imaging repositories, performing hyperparameter optimization at scale, and conducting molecular dynamics simulations to investigate protein interactions underlying observed cytomorphological changes. Expected outcomes include validated computational tools for standardized, high-throughput cytological analysis, predictive models linking cellular phenotypes to therapeutic vulnerabilities, and open-source software packages optimized for clinical research workflows. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in precancerous lesion characterization, enable discovery of novel biomarkers through integrated multi-omics analysis, and provide a template for resource-efficient computational cytopathology. By bridging cellular imaging data with molecular mechanisms through advanced computing, the project aims to advance personalized disease management strategies in clinical cytopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals to study, prevent, and manage human diseases manifested in cells. Includes instruction in laboratory procedures, laboratory management, quality assurance, screening, specimen collection, cytopreparation, cytometric and image analysis, and related immunological and molecular techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of conflict dynamics in fragile states, integrating sociopolitical, economic, and environmental data to predict escalation pathways and evaluate de-escalation strategies. Contemporary peace studies lack scalable frameworks to analyze the nonlinear interactions between diverse conflict drivers—such as resource scarcity, ethnic polarization, and external intervention—in real-world scenarios. Current models often oversimplify feedback loops or fail to account for spatial-temporal heterogeneity, limiting their utility for policymakers.
