To address this, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) coupled with machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate multi-actor decision-making under conditions of uncertainty, incorporating geospatial data, historical conflict datasets, and ethnographic case studies. The ABM will parameterize state and non-state actors (e.g., governments, insurgent groups, NGOs) with adaptive behavioral rules derived from game-theoretic principles and empirical observations, while ML components will identify latent patterns in historical escalation events to refine model accuracy. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale parallel simulations across diverse parameter spaces, enabling sensitivity analyses of intervention strategies (e.g., aid distribution protocols, ceasefire negotiation timing) under stochastic conditions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for conflict forecasting, validated against historical cases (e.g., post-2011 Syria, Lake Chad Basin crises), and policy-reducible insights into resilience-building mechanisms. By bridging computational social science and peace studies, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven conflict resolution, offering granular risk assessments and scenario-testing capabilities to practitioners working in complex, evolving crises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of international and inter-group conflicts. Includes instruction in peace research methods and related social scientific and psychological knowledge bases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the relationship between artistic expression and psychological states, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance methodological innovation in pre-art therapy research. Art therapy relies on qualitative interpretation of visual artifacts to assess emotional and cognitive processes, but current approaches lack scalable, data-driven tools to quantify patterns in artistic creation. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by establishing reproducible computational methods to decode artistic elements (e.g., color use, composition, symbolic content) and correlate them with psychometric data. This requires processing large datasets of digitized artwork—spanning diverse demographics and clinical profiles—while integrating multimodal inputs such as self-reported emotional states and behavioral annotations. The computational approach combines computer vision techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction, with graph-based models to map temporal changes in artistic output during therapeutic interventions. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning models on high-resolution image datasets and running iterative simulations to validate associations between artistic features and psychological metrics. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for quantifying stylistic and thematic elements in art therapy applications, (2) predictive models linking specific visual patterns to mental health indicators (e.g., anxiety, trauma resilience), and (3) a scalable pipeline for analyzing longitudinal art therapy datasets. By enabling large-scale, granular analysis of artistic expression, this work will strengthen evidence-based practices in art therapy training programs, inform personalized therapeutic strategies, and provide pre-art therapy students with interdisciplinary computational skills. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in expanding empirical rigor within creative arts therapies while maintaining the human-centered ethos of the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced cinematographic techniques, particularly in the integration of real-time, high-fidelity rendering with AI-driven post-production workflows. While emerging tools in virtual production, dynamic lighting simulation, and neural network-based image processing offer transformative potential for visual storytelling, their adoption is constrained by the limitations of consumer-grade hardware. Current workflows struggle to manage the latency, scalability, and data intensity required for photorealistic virtual environments or frame-accurate AI enhancements in 4K/8K resolution pipelines. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test a scalable framework for hybrid cinematography workflows. The computational approach combines physics-based light transport simulations using Monte Carlo path-tracing algorithms with distributed neural network training for style transfer and automated color grading. Key challenges include optimizing memory bandwidth for multi-camera volumetric video processing (up to 16 synchronized 8K streams) and implementing low-latency frame buffering for director-led interactive editing of GPU-rendered scenes. The project will benchmark distributed rendering across GPU clusters using open-source tools like Blender Cycles and NVIDIA Omniverse, while custom CUDA kernels will accelerate machine learning models for temporal coherence in AI-generated visual effects. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for HPC-accelerated virtual production that reduces render times for complex scenes by 60-80% compared to local workstations, enabling practical experimentation with computationally intensive techniques like neural radiance fields (NeRFs) for dynamic background replacement. This work will contribute methodological frameworks for computational cinematography while demonstrating how shared HPC infrastructure can democratize access to cutting-edge production tools previously limited to high-budget studios. Resulting workflows and performance data will be disseminated through academic workshops and integrated into film production curricula, fostering new research directions at the intersection of visual arts and computational media.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the making and producing of films and videos. Includes instruction in theory of film, film technology and equipment operation, film production, film directing, film editing, cinematographic art, film audio, techniques for making specific types of films and/or videos, media technologies, computer image making, multi-media production, and the planning and management of film/video operations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, real-time flight simulation framework to enhance pilot training efficacy and safety by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current flight training simulations often lack the computational resolution to model complex aerodynamic interactions, multi-system failures, or extreme environmental conditions with sufficient accuracy, limiting their utility in preparing pilots for rare but critical scenarios. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating a dynamic, physics-based simulation environment capable of replicating high-risk flight conditions—such as engine failures, severe weather, or aerodynamic stalls—while integrating real-time pilot inputs and physiological responses. The computational approach combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airflow over aircraft surfaces, finite element analysis (FEA) to assess structural stresses during maneuvers, and machine learning algorithms to predict system-level interactions under emergent conditions. These methods will be parallelized across HPC clusters to enable rapid, high-resolution simulations that adapt to trainee decisions, providing instantaneous feedback. The project will also incorporate anonymized flight data from existing aircraft recorders to validate and refine simulation parameters. Expected outcomes include a scalable simulation platform that reduces reliance on physical flight hours for high-risk training, thereby lowering costs and risks. The framework will enable instructors to design personalized training modules, quantify trainee performance metrics, and identify latent skill gaps. By advancing the fidelity of virtual flight environments, this work aims to improve pilot readiness for atypical scenarios, contribute to evidence-based updates in FAA training standards, and inform future aircraft design through simulated stress-testing. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational load of coupled multiphysics models and achieving real-time performance for immersive training applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the training of pilots or navigators, to prepare them to fly and/or navigate commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue aircraft, and fixed or rotary wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications and navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to administer the FAA commercial air crew examinations.

abstract: Pediatric dental caries remains a leading chronic disease in children, with disparities in prevalence linked to complex interactions between microbial, genetic, environmental, and behavioral factors. Current clinical risk-assessment tools lack precision in predicting caries progression, particularly in diverse populations, due to oversimplified models that fail to capture nonlinear dynamics. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to model caries etiology and progression in pediatric populations, integrating longitudinal clinical data, microbial metagenomics, and socio-environmental variables. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate spatial-temporal interactions within oral biofilms under varying dietary and hygiene conditions, coupled with machine learning (ML) to identify critical risk thresholds and optimize personalized prevention strategies. The ABM will incorporate strain-level microbial genomic data from pediatric saliva samples (n=1,200) to simulate pH dynamics, biofilm maturation, and enamel demineralization processes. Parallelized ML pipelines will analyze multi-omic datasets (16S rRNA sequencing, host transcriptomics, geospatial data) to stratify patients by risk trajectories. Computational demands include large-scale parameter space exploration (>10,000 simulated patient-years), real-time adaptation of ML models to heterogeneous data streams, and validation against a 5-year clinical cohort. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive tool for early caries intervention, mechanistic insights into resilience phenotypes in high-risk populations, and optimized preventive protocols tailored to genetic and socioeconomic profiles. This work will advance precision pedodontics by bridging gaps between microbial ecology, behavioral science, and clinical decision-making, with direct implications for reducing oral health disparities. The computational infrastructure will also establish a scalable platform for future studies on pulp therapy outcomes and dental trauma management in pediatric populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize venipuncture procedural outcomes by integrating computational biomechanics with real-time clinical data to model vascular access dynamics in diverse patient populations. Phlebotomy, while foundational to diagnostic medicine, faces challenges in first-attempt success rates due to anatomical variability, particularly in pediatric, geriatric, and chronically ill patients. Traditional training relies on heuristic approaches, but variability in vessel elasticity, hematocrit levels, and subcutaneous tissue composition remains poorly quantified. We propose developing a high-fidelity finite element model (FEM) simulating needle-tissue interactions across heterogeneous physiological conditions. The model will integrate anonymized patient data (ultrasound imaging, demographic variables, and hematologic parameters) from a retrospective cohort of 15,000 phlebotomy encounters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve multiscale tissue deformation, hemodynamic responses, and needle trajectory predictions at submillimeter spatial resolution. Machine learning pipelines will then correlate simulated outcomes with clinical success metrics to identify predictive biomarkers for difficult venous access. A secondary aim involves creating a real-time decision support tool using federated learning to adapt simulations to emerging procedural data from partner clinics. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework to guide needle insertion strategies, reduce complications (hematomas, hemolysis), and inform adaptive training modules for phlebotomists. By bridging biomechanical modeling with clinical phlebotomy workflows, this work advances precision in a ubiquitous yet understudied clinical procedure while establishing computational methods as a novel paradigm for procedural skill optimization in allied health sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance trauma counseling research by modeling neurobiological, psychological, and social dynamics of trauma response and recovery. A critical challenge in trauma care is understanding heterogeneous treatment outcomes, particularly how individual differences in neurobiological stress pathways interact with therapeutic interventions. Current clinical models lack the computational power to integrate multimodal data—such as neuroimaging, physiological biomarkers, and behavioral assessments—at the scale necessary to predict personalized treatment trajectories. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that combines dynamical systems modeling, machine learning, and network analysis to simulate trauma-related neural circuits and their modulation during therapy. The project will utilize HPC clusters to train deep learning models on anonymized datasets spanning fMRI scans, heart rate variability metrics, and patient-reported outcomes from trauma survivors (N ≈ 2,500). Parallelized simulations will map how perturbations in amygdala-prefrontal cortex interactions correlate with symptom reduction in PTSD cases. Additionally, agent-based models will explore how relational trauma propagates in social networks, informing crisis intervention strategies. The computational workflow will require GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time analysis of high-dimensional data and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive biomarkers for trauma resilience, (2) optimized protocols for timing therapeutic interventions based on neurodynamic states, and (3) open-source tools for trauma clinicians to simulate patient-specific treatment scenarios. By bridging computational neuroscience and counseling practice, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven, precision approaches in trauma care, reducing trial-and-error in clinical settings and improving accessibility to evidence-based interventions. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the project’s iterative modeling demands, enabling rapid hypothesis testing and translation of findings into scalable counseling frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on understanding elements of traumatic exposure, trauma-sensitive care, and crisis intervention. Includes instruction in disaster response, grief and loss counseling, crisis intervention and management, trauma counseling, neurobiology of trauma, PTSD and combat-related trauma, relational trauma and treatment of trauma-related disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Urdu language research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale textual and linguistic datasets. Urdu, with its rich literary history and complex Perso-Arabic script, presents unique challenges for automated processing, including dialectal diversity, non-standardized orthography in historical texts, and limited digital corpora. Current tools for Urdu computational linguistics are underdeveloped compared to those for major global languages, hindering advances in areas such as dialectology, stylistic evolution, and cross-regional linguistic variation. This research aims to develop and apply computational models to (1) construct a unified, annotated corpus of classical and modern Urdu texts spanning diverse genres and dialects; (2) train machine learning algorithms for syntactic parsing, semantic analysis, and dialect classification; and (3) map phonetic and lexical shifts across temporal and geographic contexts using comparative algorithms. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of digitized manuscripts, newspapers, and contemporary media, enabling parallelized text normalization, neural network training on GPU clusters, and large-scale sentiment analysis across sociolinguistic registers. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for Urdu NLP, quantitative insights into the linguistic impact of post-colonial sociopolitical changes, and interoperable datasets for cross-disciplinary humanities research. By bridging computational methods with Urdu philology, this project will empower scholars to interrogate textual traditions at unprecedented scale while preserving endangered dialectal forms. The resources will also support practical applications in language education, speech recognition systems, and archival digitization initiatives across South Asia.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Urdu language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Urdu; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize anesthetic drug dosing strategies to improve perioperative outcomes and reduce adverse events in diverse patient populations, including those undergoing complex surgeries or managing chronic pain. Current dosing guidelines often fail to account for dynamic patient-specific factors such as comorbidities, genetic polymorphisms, and real-time physiological variability, leading to suboptimal therapeutic efficacy or toxicity. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) modeling, machine learning, and high-fidelity simulations of drug interactions under varying clinical scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal data—including electronic health records, intraoperative vital sign streams, and genomic profiles—and to parameterize multi-scale models that predict patient responses to anesthetic agents. The project will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in drug metabolism pathways and Bayesian inference to refine dosing recommendations adaptively. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic cohorts generated via computational physiology models to identify risk signatures for hypotension, respiratory depression, or prolonged recovery. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for personalized anesthesia regimens, open-source simulation modules for drug interaction testing, and clinically actionable thresholds for dose adjustments in vulnerable subgroups (e.g., geriatric, obese, or critically ill patients). These advancements will directly inform precision dosing protocols, enhance intraoperative safety, and reduce healthcare costs associated with postoperative complications. The scale of data integration and the need for real-time parameter optimization in high-dimensional models necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with GPU acceleration and large-memory nodes. By bridging computational innovation with clinical anesthesiology, this work aims to establish a paradigm for dynamically tailored therapies in acute and chronic pain management.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical patient care, and the care of pain problems. Includes instruction in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern automotive systems, including electrified powertrains, autonomous driving components, and lightweight structural designs, demands advanced computational tools to optimize performance, safety, and sustainability. Physical prototyping and experimental testing remain costly and time-intensive, particularly when evaluating multi-physics interactions under diverse operational conditions. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable simulation framework for next-generation vehicle systems. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) multi-physics modeling of battery thermal management systems for electric vehicles, integrating electrochemical, thermal, and fluid dynamics simulations; (2) machine learning-enhanced crashworthiness analysis using high-fidelity finite element models to predict material behavior under impact loads; and (3) real-time aerodynamics optimization for autonomous vehicle platooning scenarios. Computational workflows will employ parallelized solvers, coupled with data-driven surrogate models, to reduce simulation times while maintaining accuracy. Validation will occur through targeted physical tests on prototype subsystems. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, transient analyses with microsecond resolution, and ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainties in complex operating environments. Expected outcomes include predictive design guidelines for battery cooling systems, lightweight energy-absorbing structures, and coordinated aerodynamic profiles that reduce energy consumption in connected vehicles. By bridging high-fidelity simulation with experimental validation, this work aims to accelerate development cycles for sustainable transportation technologies while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. The resulting methodologies will be disseminated to industry partners and integrated into advanced automotive engineering curricula, strengthening the pipeline for workforce-ready computational engineers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive learning systems for diverse adult learners in continuing education contexts, where heterogeneous backgrounds, learning objectives, and engagement patterns complicate the design of effective, personalized instruction. While adaptive platforms increasingly leverage learner data to tailor content, existing models often fail to account for the complex interplay between adult learners’ situational factors (e.g., work obligations, prior knowledge gaps) and pedagogical strategies. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate and evaluate millions of learner-instructor interaction pathways, enabling data-driven insights into personalized teaching practices. The research will utilize anonymized longitudinal datasets from adult basic education and workforce development programs, including demographic profiles, learning analytics, and outcome metrics. Computational workflows will integrate recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model temporal learning behaviors, graph-based algorithms to map knowledge acquisition trajectories, and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to simulate adaptive teaching strategies in dynamic virtual environments. These methods require parallelized processing of high-dimensional data and iterative optimization cycles that exceed the capacity of standard computing infrastructure. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters and distributed memory systems, the project aims to identify optimal instructional decision points, predict at-risk learner profiles, and generate actionable frameworks for competency-based adult education. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for instructors to design adaptive lesson plans, validated strategies for balancing flexibility and structure in adult learning environments, and a scalable computational model for evaluating equity in personalized education. This work will directly support educators in addressing the unique needs of adult learners while advancing the integration of computational pedagogy in teacher training programs.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_title: Adult and Continuing Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach adult students in various settings, including basic and remedial education programs, continuing education programs, and programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in industrial process optimization by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate complex, integrated production systems. Current methodologies for improving manufacturing workflows, quality control, and resource allocation often rely on compartmentalized analyses that fail to account for dynamic interdependencies between equipment performance, material flow variability, and human operational factors. This limitation leads to suboptimal resource use, increased waste, and reduced adaptability in rapidly evolving industrial environments. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework that integrates discrete-event simulation, finite element analysis, and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of large-scale datasets from sensor networks and historical production records while simultaneously executing high-fidelity simulations of equipment behavior under varying operational constraints. Key objectives include creating adaptive digital twins of manufacturing lines, optimizing real-time decision-making algorithms for process adjustments, and quantifying uncertainty propagation across interconnected systems. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models that reduce energy consumption by 15–20% in target industrial use cases, along with open-source tools for system resilience assessment. The computational demands of this work—particularly the need for distributed memory processing and GPU-accelerated deep learning training—require sustained access to HPC resources capable of handling terabyte-scale datasets and complex optimization workflows. By bridging gaps between theoretical process models and practical operational constraints, this research will provide actionable frameworks for small-to-medium enterprises in advanced manufacturing sectors, directly supporting workforce training initiatives in applied systems integration and data-driven process management. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and integrated into project-based curricula for engineering technology students.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the longitudinal efficacy of spiritual care interventions in mitigating psychological distress among patients with chronic illnesses. Despite growing recognition of spiritual care as a component of holistic healthcare, empirical models to quantify its impact on patient outcomes—particularly in dynamic, real-world clinical settings—remain underdeveloped. This research addresses this gap by integrating computational linguistics, psychometric analysis, and machine learning to evaluate unstructured data from chaplain-patient interactions (e.g., session transcripts, self-reported narratives) alongside clinical biomarkers of stress (e.g., cortisol levels, heart rate variability). The primary computational challenge lies in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive datasets to identify latent patterns linking pastoral counseling techniques to measurable health improvements. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines, we will extract semantic and emotional features from counseling dialogues, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will model temporal relationships between intervention timing, linguistic markers of coping, and physiological stress indicators. Parallelized Bayesian inference methods will be employed to account for heterogeneity in patient demographics, spiritual backgrounds, and disease trajectories. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework to optimize spiritual care delivery by identifying intervention characteristics most strongly associated with reduced anxiety, improved emotional resilience, and enhanced treatment adherence. This work will establish a novel computational paradigm for evaluating non-pharmacological psychosocial interventions, with implications for personalized care planning and interdisciplinary collaboration in clinical settings. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of patient-provider interactions, the project advances methodological innovation at the intersection of pastoral theology, healthcare psychology, and data science.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including but not limited to, ordained clergy and other counseling professionals to respond to the emotional and/or spiritual needs of patients and families in health care emergencies and other situations, and to consult with and counsel other health care professionals. Includes instruction in advanced interpersonal communication; individual and small group counseling; interdisciplinary teamwork; crisis management; extended care relationships; self-analysis; medical ethics; pastoral care art; spiritual dimensions of human growth and health; counseling psychology and therapy; and applications to grief, death, emotional collapse, injury, individual/family adjustment, and chronic illness situations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive security protocols in dynamic, large-scale urban environments, where traditional static security measures often fail to address evolving threats. The core challenge lies in integrating real-time behavioral data, environmental variables, and threat prediction models to enable responsive security systems capable of adjusting to unpredictable scenarios. Current approaches lack the granularity to model complex human-environment interactions at city-wide scales, particularly under conditions of partial observability or rapidly shifting risks. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and reinforcement learning (RL) approach, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate millions of agent decisions across multi-layered urban networks. The computational model will incorporate anonymized mobility patterns, infrastructure interdependencies, and stochastic threat generators to test resilience against cascading security failures. Key technical innovations include the development of a graph neural network architecture to predict emergent crowd behaviors and a parallelized optimization engine for evaluating countermeasure efficacy across simulated scenarios. By coupling these components through distributed computing workflows, the framework aims to identify latent vulnerabilities in existing security configurations while proposing dynamic resource allocation strategies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmark dataset of simulated threat-response scenarios and open-source tools for adaptive security planning. This work bridges computational social dynamics with security operations, offering a novel paradigm for proactive risk mitigation in complex human-centric systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution in simulations, enabling validation against real-world incident datasets from partner security agencies.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular interactions between traditional herbal compounds and neuroinflammatory pathways implicated in chronic pain disorders. Despite growing interest in plant-based therapies as adjuncts to conventional pain management, the mechanistic basis of many traditional remedies remains poorly characterized, limiting their integration into evidence-based care. Using an interdisciplinary approach blending ethnobotanical data, cheminformatics, and systems biology, we aim to map the polypharmacological effects of 50 prioritized plant-derived compounds on glial cell signaling networks. The computational workflow will involve three phases: (1) molecular docking simulations to predict binding affinities between phytochemicals and 27 validated protein targets in neuroinflammation, (2) machine learning-driven network pharmacology models to identify synergistic compound combinations, and (3) comparative molecular dynamics simulations of top candidate complexes under physiological membrane conditions. The scale of these analyses requires HPC capabilities to manage ~200,000 docking simulations, train predictive models on multi-omics datasets (including scRNA-seq from human microglia), and perform nanosecond-scale simulations across multiple binding states. Expected outcomes include the identification of 3-5 high-priority phytochemical complexes with predicted blood-brain barrier permeability and multimodal anti-inflammatory activity, accompanied by mechanistic hypotheses for preclinical validation. This work will establish a computational framework for evaluating traditional medicine bioactivity at unprecedented resolution while addressing critical gaps in understanding how complex herbal formulations may modulate neuroimmune crosstalk. Results will be disseminated through open-access databases and collaborations with clinical researchers exploring integrative approaches for refractory pain syndromes. By bridging computational biology and traditional knowledge systems, the project aims to advance rigorous, data-driven methodologies for studying alternative therapeutic paradigms.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medical Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medical support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale digitized archives of Japanese cultural artifacts, textual materials, and visual media to investigate evolving representations of identity and social belonging in Japan from the late Edo period to the present. The research addresses a critical gap in Japanese Studies: while historical and cultural datasets are increasingly digitized, existing methods lack the capacity to systematically trace nuanced patterns in language use, visual symbolism, and cross-media narratives across centuries. Computational approaches are essential to map how concepts such as regional identity, gender roles, and community boundaries have been constructed, contested, and renegotiated in public discourse. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze multilingual corpora spanning historical newspapers, literature, and governmental records, alongside computer vision algorithms to classify iconographic motifs in ukiyo-e prints, photography, and contemporary media. Transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to detect semantic shifts in culturally specific terminology, while graph neural networks will model the intertextual relationships between visual and textual narratives. By integrating these methods, the research aims to identify previously unrecognized correlations between socio-political events and representational trends in popular culture. Outcomes will include open-access datasets of annotated materials, a computational framework for interdisciplinary cultural analysis, and new insights into how marginalized groups—such as Ainu, Okinawan, and zainichi communities—have been depicted in mainstream Japanese media. This work will advance methodological innovation in area studies by demonstrating how HPC can bridge qualitative cultural scholarship and data-driven inquiry, while contributing to broader debates about heritage preservation and the ethics of representation in digitized archives. The requested resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte datasets, training of domain-specific machine learning models, and large-scale parallelism for comparative timeline analysis across regions and media types.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Japan, and related island groups and coastal neighbors.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize behavioral and environmental management strategies for domestic animal shelters, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in resource allocation and animal welfare outcomes. Animal shelters face complex operational challenges, including fluctuating intake rates, variable adoption demand, and the need to balance finite resources (e.g., space, staffing, veterinary care) with the health and behavioral needs of diverse animal populations. Traditional management approaches often rely on heuristic methods, which may fail to account for dynamic interactions between environmental factors, animal stress indicators, and operational constraints. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating ethological data, facility logistics, and machine learning to model shelter ecosystems. Behavioral metrics (e.g., activity levels, vocalization patterns, and social interactions) and environmental variables (e.g., enclosure layouts, noise levels, and staffing schedules) will be collected via IoT sensors and shelter databases. These data will feed into a multi-agent simulation platform, built using parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms, to model individual and population-level responses to management interventions. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization, simulating thousands of scenarios to identify strategies that minimize stress-related outcomes (e.g., illness, aggression) while maximizing adoption rates and operational efficiency. The project will also employ graph neural networks to predict network effects of resource reallocation, such as how shifting staff hours between intake processing and enrichment activities propagates through shelter operations. Outcomes will include an open-source decision-support tool for shelter administrators, validated against real-world data from partner organizations. By bridging computational modeling and animal services, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for evidence-based shelter management, offering novel insights into the application of HPC in non-traditional, socially impactful domains.
cip_title: Agricultural and Domestic Animal Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural and domestic animal services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social behavior, neurocognitive development, and digital environmental exposure in adolescents using a novel computational framework. The research problem centers on understanding how heterogeneous patterns of social media engagement influence emergent mental health outcomes through bidirectional interactions with neurobiological maturation—a question requiring integration of behavioral, psychological, and neuroimaging data at scales that challenge conventional analytical methods. We propose developing a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) coupled with machine learning pipelines to simulate longitudinal biobehavioral systems across 10,000+ synthetic adolescent agents. The ABM will incorporate neurodevelopmental trajectories derived from diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) datasets, real-world social network topologies, and temporally resolved digital interaction logs to capture multilevel feedback loops between prefrontal cortex maturation, peer influence dynamics, and platform-specific engagement behaviors. Computational challenges include optimizing parallelized parameter sweeps across neurocognitive growth variables, scaling graph neural networks to process time-varying social connectivity data, and implementing Bayesian inference for personalized risk stratification. The HPC resources will enable simulations at population-representative scales, reducing sampling bias inherent in single-cohort studies. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical neurodevelopmental windows where digital exposure disproportionately impacts emotional regulation pathways, (2) predictive biomarkers linking platform-specific interaction patterns to latent anxiety/depression risk, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for simulating digitally mediated biobehavioral systems. This work bridges gaps between computational social science, developmental neuroscience, and digital epidemiology, offering a paradigm to study emerging technology’s role in shaping adolescent mental health through an interdisciplinary lens. Results will inform targeted intervention strategies and ethical AI design principles for youth-facing platforms.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on the social sciences, psychology, and biomedical sciences to study complex problems of human individual and social growth and behavior.

abstract: Laboratory animal models are critical for advancing biomedical research, yet variability in experimental outcomes and translational efficacy remains a significant challenge. This project addresses the need to optimize preclinical research design by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multimodal datasets derived from laboratory animal studies. We will integrate genomic, proteomic, behavioral, and clinical data from murine and non-human primate models of neurodegenerative diseases, combining longitudinal health records, high-resolution imaging, and sensor-based activity monitoring. The computational approach employs machine learning algorithms to identify biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response while accounting for inter-individual variability in genetic background, environmental factors, and comorbid conditions. A key innovation involves developing predictive models that simulate interactions between host physiology, experimental interventions, and laboratory-specific environmental parameters to improve reproducibility. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets, Bayesian network analyses to map causal pathways in disease phenotypes, and validation of computational models against independent experimental cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for optimizing animal model selection and experimental design, (2) predictive algorithms to reduce sample size requirements while maintaining statistical power, and (3) open-source tools for standardizing data integration across veterinary research facilities. This work will directly enhance the translational validity of preclinical studies while addressing ethical imperatives to refine animal research practices. By bridging computational science and laboratory animal medicine, the project aims to establish new best practices for data-driven management of veterinary research laboratories and improve the reliability of biomedical discoveries.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied veterinary research and related techniques, equipment, data systems and research design. May included related research in the management of veterinary and other animal research laboratories and health care facilities.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic and phenotypic datasets in livestock research necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in precision breeding and disease resilience. This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for integrating multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics) to identify genetic markers associated with disease resistance in swine populations. Current methods struggle to process high-dimensional datasets efficiently, limiting the discovery of epistatic interactions and non-linear genetic effects. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning models, including graph neural networks (GNNs) and gradient-boosted trees, trained on whole-genome sequencing data from 5,000 individuals with linked health records. Parallelized genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be conducted using distributed computing frameworks to map loci influencing immune response variability. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model disease transmission dynamics within heterogeneous herds, incorporating stochastic environmental variables and host-pathogen interactions at scale. The computational workflow will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, with an expected data throughput of 200 TB. Outcomes will include (1) predictive models linking genetic architecture to disease susceptibility, (2) optimized breeding strategies targeting resilience traits, and (3) open-source tools for large-scale agricultural genomics. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to reduce reliance on antimicrobial interventions while improving swine health outcomes, directly supporting sustainable livestock production. The requested resources will enable processing times reduced from weeks to days, facilitating rapid iteration critical for addressing emerging zoonotic threats.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the animal sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and systemic factors influencing equity gaps in K-12 educational outcomes across diverse geographic and institutional contexts. Current policy evaluations often rely on aggregated data or simplified models, limiting their ability to disentangle the complex interactions between policy implementation, resource allocation, and student outcomes. This research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate multi-level policy impacts using fine-grained longitudinal data spanning student performance metrics, funding patterns, and policy compliance records from 12 states. The project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate how localized variations in policy adoption (e.g., Title I fund distribution, teacher credentialing requirements) interact with community-level socioeconomic factors at scale. Computational demands arise from iterative parameter optimization across 50+ policy scenarios, machine learning-driven pattern recognition in unstructured administrative records, and probabilistic forecasting of equity outcomes under alternative policy configurations. By integrating 15 terabytes of longitudinal student data, institutional records, and policy datasets, the models will quantify how specific allocation mechanisms either exacerbate or mitigate disparities in access to advanced coursework and extracurricular resources. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating education policy trade-offs, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing compliance monitoring systems, and (3) predictive metrics to identify districts at highest risk of unintended policy consequences. Results will advance methodological approaches to policy analysis by demonstrating how computational scalability enables more nuanced, dynamic assessments of education systems than traditional regression-based methods permit. This work directly supports the program’s mission to improve policy evaluation frameworks through innovative applications of computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to education and educational systems at the local, state, national, and international levels. Includes instruction in social and cultural issues in education, contemporary educational policies, history of education, economics of education, international and comparative education, education and social change, educational research and evaluation methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: Decompression illness (DCI) and hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) applications present complex physiological challenges, including gas bubble dynamics, tissue oxygenation variability, and patient-specific treatment optimization. Current clinical protocols rely on population-based thresholds, which may inadequately address individual risk factors or dynamic physiological responses. This project seeks to develop predictive, patient-specific models of DCI progression and HBOT efficacy using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale physiological processes. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) modeling inert gas bubble formation, growth, and dissolution across tissues under varying pressure profiles; (2) optimizing HBOT dosing schedules for heterogeneous conditions such as radiation-induced tissue damage and chronic wounds through tissue-level oxygen transport simulations; and (3) creating risk stratification frameworks for diving operations using machine learning analysis of diver biometrics, environmental data, and treatment outcomes. Computational methods will integrate finite element analysis for tissue-scale gas dynamics, computational fluid dynamics for microvascular bubble interactions, and reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine treatment parameters. These simulations will leverage existing clinical datasets from hyperbaric centers and diver monitoring systems, scaled through synthetic data generation to account for rare adverse events. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D tissue models, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic risk assessment, and real-time parameter optimization during model training. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for DCI severity classification, optimized HBOT protocols with simulated outcome probabilities, and operational guidelines for hyperbaric chambers based on dynamic risk modeling. By translating computational insights into clinical decision-support systems, this work aims to reduce neurological sequelae in diving accidents, improve healing rates in non-responsive wounds, and establish safety thresholds for occupational divers. The resource-intensive nature of these multi-physics simulations, requiring terabyte-scale memory handling and GPU-accelerated computations, necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat decompression illness and diving accident cases; to use hyperbaric oxygen therapy treatment for conditions such as carbon monoxide poisoning, gas gangrene, non-healing wounds, tissue damage from radiation and burns, and bone infections; to serve as consultant in all aspects of hyperbaric chamber operations; and to assess risks and apply appropriate standards to prevent disease and disability in divers and other persons working in altered atmospheric conditions.

abstract: Traumatic injuries and critical illnesses present complex, heterogeneous clinical trajectories influenced by dynamic interactions between physiological, genetic, and environmental factors. Current risk stratification tools and treatment protocols lack the granularity to address this complexity, resulting in suboptimal outcomes for high-risk patients. This project seeks to develop predictive multiscale models of trauma-induced organ dysfunction and sepsis using high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multimodal clinical data, including high-resolution electronic health records, proteomic biomarkers, and real-time vital sign streams. The computational approach will employ ensemble machine learning frameworks to identify early signatures of clinical deterioration, coupled with mechanistic agent-based models simulating immune-endothelial interactions in sepsis. These models will be trained and validated on a retrospective cohort of 15,000 trauma patients from three Level I trauma centers, with prospective validation in an active critical care registry. The HPC environment is essential for managing the scale and velocity of data (≥5 TB of time-series data), optimizing hyperparameters across distributed nodes, and executing parallelized simulations of cellular-scale inflammatory cascades. Expected outcomes include (1) validated prediction algorithms for trauma-related sepsis and multi-organ failure with improved accuracy (target AUC >0.92) over existing scores, (2) mechanistic insights into patient-specific immune dysregulation patterns, and (3) open-source computational workflows for real-time risk visualization in ICUs. By enabling granular phenotype discovery and in silico treatment testing, this work aims to advance personalized resuscitation strategies and reduce preventable deaths in trauma-critical care transitions. The proposed models will also establish a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into dynamic clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on Trauma and Critical Care

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the longitudinal efficacy of Clinical Pastoral Counseling (CPC) interventions in mitigating trauma-related psychological distress among chronically ill patients. While CPC integrates spiritual care with psychosocial support, evidence-based tools to quantify its impact on neuropsychological outcomes remain limited. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets from 2,000+ patients, including transcribed counseling sessions (NLP-processed), physiological biomarkers (heart rate variability, cortisol levels), and standardized mental health assessments collected over 24 months. A hybrid neural architecture will be trained to identify latent patterns linking counselor linguistic features (e.g., metaphor use, emotion-focused phrasing) with patient self-reported spiritual well-being and clinician-rated resilience metrics. Parallelized Bayesian networks will model temporal dynamics of therapeutic alliances, while agent-based simulations will test how variations in counseling protocols affect hypothetical crisis response scenarios. The computational pipeline requires HPC resources to manage GPU-accelerated transformer models for semantic analysis, Monte Carlo simulations for intervention outcome projections, and federated learning to preserve privacy across hospital datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model correlating specific CPC communication strategies with reduced post-traumatic stress symptoms, (2) dynamically adjustable intervention templates for personalized spiritual care, and (3) open-source tools to visualize counselor-patient interaction epigenetics. This work addresses a critical gap in empirically grounding spiritual care methodologies, offering a scalable framework to optimize CPC training and integration within precision medicine paradigms.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including but not limited to, ordained clergy and other counseling professionals to respond to the emotional and/or spiritual needs of patients and families in health care emergencies and other situations, and to consult with and counsel other health care professionals. Includes instruction in advanced interpersonal communication; individual and small group counseling; interdisciplinary teamwork; crisis management; extended care relationships; self-analysis; medical ethics; pastoral care art; spiritual dimensions of human growth and health; counseling psychology and therapy; and applications to grief, death, emotional collapse, injury, individual/family adjustment, and chronic illness situations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary study of historical textual transmission and cultural exchange through large-scale computational analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in digital humanities: the inability to efficiently process and analyze vast, multilingual corpora spanning multiple centuries, which are essential for tracing the evolution of ideas, textual reuse, and cross-cultural influence. Traditional methods, limited by scale and computational power, struggle to identify subtle patterns in syntax, semantic shifts, or intertextual connections across such datasets. The proposed work will develop and apply machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures and graph neural networks, to map textual relationships within a curated corpus of over 50,000 digitized manuscripts, pamphlets, and printed works from 1500–1900. These models will be trained to detect stylistic features, semantic anomalies, and citation networks, while accounting for OCR errors, orthographic variations, and multilingual contexts. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) pipelines with geospatial and temporal metadata to visualize knowledge dissemination pathways. HPC resources are essential for training large language models on heterogeneous historical data, parallelizing feature extraction across distributed systems, and optimizing memory-intensive tasks such as network graph generation. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for diachronic text analysis, novel metrics for quantifying textual influence, and case studies demonstrating how computational methods can revise existing narratives about the circulation of Enlightenment-era political texts. By enabling scalable analysis of understudied primary sources, this project aims to bridge methodological divides between computational linguistics and traditional hermeneutics, offering humanities scholars new frameworks for interrogating cultural change at unprecedented granularity.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in digital humanities and textual studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of botanical medicine with precision health approaches in naturopathic medicine remains underexplored due to the complexity of multi-compound botanical interactions and their systemic effects on human physiology. Current clinical frameworks lack predictive models to optimize individualized botanical protocols, particularly for chronic inflammatory conditions where polypharmacological effects and patient-specific variables (e.g., metabolomic profiles, gut microbiome diversity) critically influence outcomes. This project proposes to develop a computational platform integrating multi-omics data with phytochemical networks to predict patient-specific responses to botanical therapies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will construct a graph-based model representing interactions between 500+ bioactive phytochemicals (curated from pharmacognosy databases) and human molecular targets implicated in inflammation, immune modulation, and oxidative stress. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on clinical datasets from naturopathic practice, including longitudinal metabolomic profiles, microbiome sequencing data, and patient-reported outcomes. Parallel molecular dynamics simulations will characterize binding affinities of lesser-studied phytochemicals to inflammatory biomarkers (e.g., NLRP3 inflammasome components). The computational workflow will enable probabilistic modeling of protocol efficacy across diverse patient archetypes, accounting for genetic polymorphisms, microbiome-mediated biotransformation, and herb-drug interaction risks. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for personalized botanical protocol design, identification of novel synergistic phytochemical combinations, and quantitative safety-efficacy profiles for complex herbal formulations. This work addresses a critical gap in evidence-based naturopathic therapeutics by providing computational tools to reconcile traditional empirical knowledge with modern systems biology paradigms. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of phytochemical interactions, scaling multi-omics integration, and enabling real-time clinical decision support through containerized model deployment in naturopathic electronic health record systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of naturopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic approach combining medical knowledge with noninvasive natural, homeopathic, and non-Western therapies and emphasizing disease prevention, wellness, and self-healing. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, biostatistics, public and community health, laboratory and clinical diagnosis, pharmacognosy, botanical medicine, homeopathy, principles of Oriental medicine and Ayurveda, manipulative therapy, naturopathic therapeutics, therapeutic nutrition, case analysis and management, philosophy of naturopathy, patient counseling, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between individual cognitive biases, social network structures, and environmental stressors in shaping collective decision-making during public health crises. Traditional behavioral models often isolate psychological, social, or environmental factors, limiting their ability to predict emergent group behaviors in complex, real-world scenarios. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating cognitive science principles, epidemiological data, and geospatial information to simulate how misinformation spreads and influences health-related choices in diverse populations. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to execute large-scale agent-based simulations that parameterize agents with empirically derived cognitive profiles—including risk perception biases and memory distortions—while embedding them in multilayer social networks reflecting both online and offline interactions. Environmental stressors, such as localized resource scarcity or pollution exposure, are incorporated via geospatial datasets to modulate agent decision thresholds. Machine learning techniques will identify critical tipping points in misinformation propagation and test intervention strategies (e.g., targeted messaging, network hub prioritization) across synthetic populations mirroring census-derived demographics. By parallelizing thousands of scenario variations, HPC resources will enable robust sensitivity analyses to quantify how individual neurocognitive variability interacts with macro-scale social and environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models of health behavior emergence under crisis conditions, validated against longitudinal survey data from recent pandemic responses, and actionable insights for designing adaptive public health communication frameworks. This interdisciplinary approach bridges neurobehavioral science, computational sociology, and spatial epidemiology, advancing methodological integration across behavioral sciences while addressing urgent challenges in population health resilience.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on the social sciences, psychology, and biomedical sciences to study complex problems of human individual and social growth and behavior.

abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a critical role in modulating host immune responses, yet the mechanisms underlying microbial community resilience during inflammatory perturbations remain poorly understood. This project seeks to unravel how dynamic interactions between commensal bacteria, invasive pathogens, and host immune cells drive stability or dysbiosis in the gut ecosystem. We propose to develop a high-resolution, agent-based computational model to simulate spatially structured microbial communities under varying host inflammatory conditions. The model will integrate empirical data on bacterial growth kinetics, metabolic cross-feeding, and immune signaling (e.g., cytokine gradients, phagocyte activity) derived from in vitro and murine studies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the stochastic, multi-scale nature of these interactions, which involve millions of agents operating across micrometer-to-millimeter spatial domains and second-to-hour temporal scales. Parallelized simulations will explore how factors such as oxygen gradients, antimicrobial peptide diffusion, and T-cell recruitment influence competition between commensals (e.g., Bacteroides spp.) and enteric pathogens (e.g., Salmonella Typhimurium). Sensitivity analyses will identify critical parameters controlling community tipping points, while synthetic microbial consortia experiments will validate model predictions. This work will generate the first computational framework capable of predicting microbiome trajectories during localized inflammation, addressing a major gap in translating microbiome research into therapies for inflammatory bowel disease. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulation batches, large-scale parameter space exploration, and machine learning-assisted analysis of emergent community behaviors. Outcomes will provide mechanistic insights into host-microbe resilience strategies and inform the design of microbiota-targeted interventions to prevent pathogen invasion or chronic inflammation. By bridging microbial ecology and mucosal immunology through computational modeling, this project advances foundational knowledge with translational relevance for immune-mediated disorders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the microbiological sciences and immunology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and energy efficiency integration in full-service hotels using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between guest behavior, operational systems, and sustainability goals. While revenue management and environmental practices are well-studied in hospitality, existing models treat pricing algorithms and energy systems as separate domains. This creates suboptimal outcomes when hotels balance profit margins against emissions targets, particularly during demand fluctuations. The computational challenge lies in simulating real-time decision-making across interconnected systems—including IoT-enabled HVAC, occupancy sensors, and historical booking data—while accounting for stochastic variables such as weather patterns, event-driven demand spikes, and evolving guest sustainability preferences. The project will develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework to model these interactions at scale, requiring parallelized simulations of thousands of hypothetical hotel configurations under varying market and environmental conditions. HPC resources will enable the simultaneous training of competing optimization objectives (revenue maximization vs. carbon minimization) across heterogeneous datasets spanning five years of operational records from 12 urban hotels. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between short-term pricing strategies and long-term sustainability performance, validated against real-world energy consumption and booking data. This work bridges computational sustainability and hospitality operations, offering a novel methodology for aligning profit-driven systems with decarbonization mandates in the hotel industry. By addressing the temporal and spatial complexity of resource allocation in lodging environments, the project aims to establish scalable computational frameworks adaptable to emerging regulatory landscapes and climate-aware consumer behavior.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage and control; hotel facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; marketing and sales promotion; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotels and motel operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative decision-making in multiparty systems and its impact on economic policy coherence, using advanced computational methods. The core problem addressed is the lack of scalable frameworks to model how fragmented political institutions—particularly in proportional representation systems—generate economic policies with varying degrees of stability, equity, and efficiency. Existing studies often rely on simplified game-theoretic models or case studies, limiting their ability to account for complex interactions among ideologically diverse actors, institutional veto points, and dynamic public opinion. To address this gap, the project will develop an agent-based model (ABM) simulating legislative bargaining processes, integrating granular data on party platforms, voter preferences, and macroeconomic indicators from 25 parliamentary democracies (1990–2020). The ABM will incorporate neural network modules to approximate boundedly rational negotiation strategies, trained on historical coalition formation outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations testing 10^6+ policy negotiation scenarios under different electoral rules and economic shocks; (2) evolutionary algorithms optimizing parameter space exploration for coalition stability thresholds; and (3) real-time visualization of emergent policy cascades across multi-dimensional ideological and economic landscapes. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of policy instability drivers in multiparty democracies, predictive metrics for economic reform durability, and open-source tools for computational political economy. Results will advance scholarly understanding of institutional design trade-offs while providing policymakers with evidence-based insights into mitigating boom-bust cycles exacerbated by legislative fragmentation. The proposed HPC allocation enables computationally intensive analysis that standard political science methods cannot achieve, particularly in scaling from individual actor interactions to system-level policy outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction between politics and economics in the formation of public policy. Includes instruction in microeconomics; macroeconomics; political theory; American, comparative, and international political economy; and quantitative methods.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a large-scale computational framework to analyze stylistic evolution in English literary texts across distinct historical periods, with a focus on identifying patterns of linguistic innovation and intertextual influence. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on manual close reading, the sheer volume of extant texts—from Early Modern pamphlets to 20th-century novels—necessitates scalable computational methods to detect subtle, systemic shifts in language use and narrative structure. The research will employ natural language processing techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on period-specific corpora, to quantify syntactic complexity, semantic field distributions, and metaphor density across a curated dataset of 30,000 primary texts. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: parallel processing of heterogeneous archival formats (TEI XML, OCR-scanned texts), training domain-specific word embeddings using dynamic temporal contexts, and implementing graph neural networks to map citation networks and thematic diffusion. By correlating linguistic features with sociocultural metadata, the analysis will test hypotheses about how major events like the Industrial Revolution or suffrage movements influenced literary expression. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated texts, visualization tools for diachronic stylistic trends, and statistical models quantifying the relationship between lexical innovation and canon formation. This work will advance methodological debates in digital humanities by demonstrating how computational approaches can complement qualitative interpretation, while providing new empirical evidence for longstanding theoretical claims about literary periodization. The resource demands—particularly GPU-intensive model training and large-scale graph traversal—require dedicated HPC allocation to ensure feasible processing times for terabyte-scale textual data.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the English language, including its history, structure and related communications skills; and the literature and culture of English-speaking peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing inefficiencies in large-scale data processing workflows within microcomputer-based systems, which are increasingly limited by traditional single-node computing architectures. As data entry and processing tasks expand in volume and complexity—particularly in sectors such as healthcare, logistics, and financial record management—existing microcomputer applications struggle with scalability, latency, and energy consumption. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes the development of a distributed computing framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, enabling parallelized data entry validation, transformation, and analysis. The core computational approach involves adapting legacy data entry algorithms to a distributed model using MPI and OpenMP, while integrating machine learning classifiers to automate error detection in heterogeneous datasets. Resource-intensive simulations will benchmark the framework’s performance against conventional single-threaded systems under varying workloads (10⁴–10⁸ records), with an emphasis on latency reduction, accuracy, and energy efficiency. Additionally, the project will explore GPU-accelerated preprocessing techniques to handle unstructured data common in mixed-format data entry environments. Expected outcomes include a 40–60% improvement in processing throughput for terabyte-scale datasets, a modular toolkit for deploying microcomputer applications on HPC infrastructures, and energy consumption models to guide sustainable scaling. The results will directly benefit organizations reliant on high-volume data entry systems while providing a case study for integrating HPC resources into non-traditional, microcomputer-centric workflows. This work will also contribute open-source software packages to support curriculum development in data-driven microcomputer applications, bridging gaps between theoretical instruction and industry-scale computational challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data entry/microcomputer applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric patients exhibit unique pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles that differ significantly from adults, yet many drug therapies lack optimized dosing protocols tailored to these populations. Current approaches to pediatric drug development and dose individualization often rely on extrapolation from adult data or sparse pediatric trials, leading to suboptimal efficacy and safety outcomes. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing high-resolution computational models to predict drug disposition and response across pediatric age groups, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome the challenges of modeling complex physiological and developmental variability. The research will integrate physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, machine learning, and population pharmacokinetic analyses to simulate drug behavior in pediatric subpopulations.
