Key computational tasks include large-scale parameter estimation using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, virtual population generation accounting for ontogeny of metabolic enzymes and organ function, and ensemble modeling to quantify uncertainty in dose predictions. HPC resources are critical for executing millions of parallel simulations across heterogeneous virtual cohorts, processing multi-terabyte electronic health record datasets, and training neural networks to identify nonlinear relationships between patient characteristics and drug outcomes. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for 3-5 high-priority pediatric medications, dose optimization frameworks adaptable to rare genetic subgroups, and open-source tools for real-time dose individualization in clinical settings. This work will directly inform precision dosing guidelines, reduce adverse drug events in children, and establish a scalable computational infrastructure for future pediatric pharmacotherapy research. By bridging developmental pharmacology with advanced computing, the project aims to transform evidence generation for pediatric drug therapy where traditional clinical trials remain ethically or logistically challenging.
cip_definition: Research focused on pediatric pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the design and fabrication of custom wood components in cabinetmaking and millwork, addressing inefficiencies in traditional trial-and-error approaches. The research problem centers on the limitations of manual methods in predicting material behavior, structural integrity, and machining outcomes for complex geometries or non-traditional wood composites. To resolve this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning, and generative design algorithms. Computational models will simulate stress distribution, moisture-induced deformation, and toolpath efficiency across diverse wood species and machining parameters. Machine learning components will train on experimental datasets (e.g., wood grain orientation effects, adhesive performance under load) to predict optimal joinery configurations and material pairings. Generative design workflows will iteratively propose component geometries that minimize waste while meeting structural requirements. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these resource-intensive simulations across multidimensional parameter spaces, including variable humidity conditions, composite material properties, and CNC tool wear scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for warp prevention in panel components, a decision-support tool for machining parameter selection, and generative templates for waste-reduced cabinet assemblies. Results will be experimentally verified through physical prototypes instrumented with strain gauges and digital image correlation systems. This work aims to advance precision in sustainable woodcraft by replacing empirical methods with computationally guided fabrication protocols, potentially reducing material waste by 15-20% in custom millwork production. The developed models will be disseminated as open-access plugins for computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) software, democratizing access to advanced computational design strategies in vocational and small-scale industrial settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate and repair industrial woodworking machinery, and to use such machinery to design and fabricate wooden components and complete articles.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of blood coagulation disorders, a critical area in hematology technology. Current diagnostic methods for thrombotic and bleeding disorders often rely on static laboratory tests, which may fail to capture dynamic molecular interactions underlying pathological clotting. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models that integrate molecular dynamics simulations of clotting factor interactions with systems-level analyses of coagulation cascade regulation. These models will simulate blood clot formation under varying physiological and pathological conditions, incorporating patient-derived data on genetic mutations, platelet function, and plasma protein levels. The computational framework will utilize parallelized algorithms to handle the high-dimensional parameter space and stochasticity inherent to coagulation biology. Machine learning approaches will further refine predictive accuracy by identifying patterns in clinical datasets linked to thrombotic risk or therapeutic response. By utilizing HPC resources, this project will overcome the limitations of traditional in vitro experiments, enabling rapid, large-scale simulations of clotting mechanisms across diverse patient populations. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, predictive models for personalized anticoagulant therapy, and a deeper understanding of how genetic and environmental factors disrupt hemostatic balance. This work aligns with the clinical priorities of hematology technology by enhancing the precision of diagnostic workflows and informing the development of targeted therapies. The requested computing resources are essential for managing the project’s data-intensive workloads, which involve terabytes of simulation outputs and high-throughput clinical data integration. Successful execution will provide a scalable computational toolkit for translational research in hematology, bridging gaps between laboratory testing and patient-specific clinical decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists and health care professionals, to perform tests and analyses of blood samples. Includes instruction in clinical laboratory procedures; blood anatomy and physiology; cellular and molecular biology; blood pathology and disease indicators; quantitative, qualitative, and coagulation testing methodologies; equipment operation and maintenance; and record-keeping.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamics of cross-platform misinformation propagation in digital media ecosystems, a critical challenge for communication studies in an era of fragmented information landscapes. Current methods lack the capacity to analyze hyperconnected, real-time media flows across social networks, messaging apps, and emerging platforms, where multimodal content (text, video, memes) undergoes continuous remixing. We propose developing a computational framework requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process 2.3TB of timestamped user-generated content from 17 platform APIs, including encrypted channels and ephemeral media. The methodology combines transformer-based multilingual NLP for cross-cultural content analysis, dynamic hypergraph modeling to track mutation pathways of visual narratives, and attention-based neural networks to detect coordinated amplification patterns. HPC capabilities are essential for three core tasks: 1) parallel processing of encrypted data streams while maintaining ethical analysis protocols, 2) training multi-modal deep learning models on GPU clusters to identify deepfake-mediated disinformation, and 3) running agent-based simulations of information cascades under different moderation policy scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include a novel typology of platform-agnostic misinformation adaptation strategies, quantitative metrics for cultural resonance in visual arguments, and predictive models of narrative spillover across ideological clusters. The research will produce open-access tools for scalable media ecosystem analysis while addressing critical gaps in communication theory regarding hybrid (human+algorithmic) information gatekeeping. By enabling analysis at previously impractical temporal resolutions (sub-15-minute intervals) and cross-platform breadth, this work positions computational communication studies to meaningfully engage with the sociotechnical complexity of 21st-century media environments. The requested resources directly support computationally intensive tasks that exceed the capacity of existing departmental infrastructure by 3-4 orders of magnitude in both processing speed and dataset complexity.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication and media studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Celtic languages by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model linguistic evolution, dialectal variation, and morphosyntactic complexity. Despite their cultural and historical significance, Celtic languages remain underrepresented in digital humanities research, particularly in large-scale comparative studies. Current challenges include processing fragmented or non-standardized historical texts, analyzing phonetic shifts across dialects, and reconstructing proto-language features. This research will employ computational linguistics methods, including machine learning-driven morphological parsing, phylogenetic algorithms for language divergence modeling, and geospatial analysis of dialect distributions. The project will integrate digitized manuscripts, modern speech corpora, and sociolinguistic data to build a unified analytical framework. HPC resources are essential for training neural models on low-resource languages, simulating language contact scenarios, and processing high-resolution audio data for phonetic studies. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive dialect atlas of Breton, computational reconstructions of extinct Continental Celtic varieties, and open-access tools for automated analysis of Irish verb morphology. These results will advance theoretical understanding of language change in insular contexts, support revitalization initiatives through pedagogically oriented resources, and provide scalable methodologies for under-resourced languages globally. By bridging gaps between traditional philology and computational innovation, this work will establish new interdisciplinary benchmarks for Celtic studies while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in minority language research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by the Celtic peoples of the British Isles, Continental Europe, and Asia Minor, including, but not limited to, modern languages such as Irish, Scots Gaelic, Welsh, and Breton; and extinct or revived languages such as Cornish, Manx, Galatian, and others. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Child and adolescent psychiatric disorders, such as autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and pediatric depression, exhibit complex etiologies involving dynamic interactions between genetic, neurobiological, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic frameworks and treatment strategies often lack precision due to heterogeneity in symptom presentation and insufficient understanding of underlying mechanisms. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including longitudinal neuroimaging (fMRI, structural MRI), genomic sequencing, and electronic health records from pediatric cohorts. The primary research aim is to identify predictive biomarkers and subtype-specific pathways that correlate with clinical outcomes, enabling personalized intervention strategies. Computational challenges include processing terabytes of neuroimaging data, integrating sparse longitudinal clinical variables, and performing genome-wide association studies (GWAS) coupled with polygenic risk scoring. Machine learning approaches, such as federated ensemble models and graph neural networks, will be deployed to handle data heterogeneity while preserving patient privacy. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of imaging pipelines (e.g., FSL, FreeSurfer), large-scale permutation testing for genomic associations, and simulation of neurodevelopmental trajectories using dynamical systems models. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for integrative multi-omics analysis in pediatric psychiatry, validated predictive models for treatment response in early-onset depression, and actionable insights into the neurodevelopmental impact of rare genetic variants. These results will directly inform clinical trial design and advance mechanistic understanding of resilience and risk factors, addressing a critical need for data-driven frameworks in child mental health. The project’s computational demands—particularly its reliance on GPU-accelerated deep learning, distributed memory architectures for population-level simulations, and high-throughput genomic analysis—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve scalable, reproducible results within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of developmental, behavioral, emotional, and mental disorders of childhood and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize construction site management by integrating high-performance computing (HPC) with dynamic risk prediction and resource allocation models. Construction projects are inherently complex, involving interdependent variables such as labor productivity, equipment availability, material logistics, and environmental factors, which traditional static scheduling tools often fail to adapt to in real time. This research addresses the critical challenge of minimizing delays, rework, and safety incidents through predictive analytics and scenario-based simulations. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to create a hybrid digital twin of construction sites, capable of ingesting real-time data from IoT sensors, weather APIs, and workforce tracking systems. Machine learning models, trained on historical accident reports and project timelines, will identify risk patterns and predict bottlenecks or safety hazards. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across thousands of scenarios, enabling rapid evaluation of mitigation strategies, such as reallocating labor or adjusting equipment schedules under constraints like diversity training compliance or union regulations. The expected outcomes include an open-source tool that provides site managers with actionable recommendations for resource distribution, contingency planning, and accident prevention. By quantifying the impact of variables like crew diversity, communication protocols, and subcontractor coordination on project efficiency, this research aims to reduce average project overruns by 15–20% and lower incident rates through proactive risk management. The results will advance the integration of computational decision-support systems in construction education and practice, aligning with industry demands for data-driven, adaptive management strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise, manage, and inspect construction sites, buildings, and associated facilities. Includes instruction in site safety, personnel supervision, labor relations, diversity training, construction documentation, scheduling, resource and cost control, bid strategies, rework prevention, construction insurance and bonding, accident management and investigation, applicable law and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in heterogeneous computing architectures through the development of adaptive resource allocation algorithms optimized for emerging edge computing and AI-driven workloads. As heterogeneous systems integrating CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, and specialized accelerators become ubiquitous, traditional static allocation strategies fail to account for dynamic workload variability, leading to suboptimal energy efficiency and latency. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining real-time system telemetry with machine learning-driven optimization models to predict and allocate resources across hybrid hardware platforms. The research will employ distributed simulations of edge computing environments using parameterized workload generators and hardware performance models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to realistic node counts (1,000+ devices) and for training deep reinforcement learning models on the resulting multi-terabyte telemetry datasets. Parallel computing frameworks, including MPI and CUDA, will be used to simulate concurrent device interactions, while PyTorch and TensorFlow will enable iterative model training. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source algorithms for dynamic resource partitioning in heterogeneous systems, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing energy efficiency and throughput against static allocation baselines, and (3) a scalable simulation toolkit for edge computing environments. This work directly supports the Computer Engineering Technologies field by providing methodologies to optimize next-generation computing infrastructures for AI/ML, IoT, and real-time applications. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale validation of our approach, which would be computationally infeasible on local clusters due to memory constraints (>4 TB working datasets) and the need for simultaneous multi-node simulation. Results will be disseminated through academic publications and industry partnerships to advance both theoretical and applied research in adaptive computing systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and testing of complex mechanical systems, such as energy-efficient industrial actuators and modular manufacturing equipment, through high-fidelity simulations. Current design processes in mechanical engineering technology rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-consuming, costly, and limited in capturing multi-physics interactions under dynamic operating conditions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement advanced finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models that simulate thermal, structural, and fluid-structure interaction behaviors. These simulations will integrate empirical data from existing prototype testing to validate predictive accuracy. Key objectives include analyzing stress distributions in composite materials under cyclic loading, optimizing heat dissipation in high-torque electromechanical systems, and evaluating wear patterns in automated assembly line components. The computational workflow will utilize open-source solvers like OpenFOAM and Code_Aster, parallelized to exploit HPC architectures for scalability. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce simulation dimensionality and accelerate parameter optimization. Outcomes will include validated digital twin models for rapid virtual prototyping, reducing physical testing cycles by an estimated 40%, and actionable design guidelines to enhance the durability and energy efficiency of mechanical systems. This work directly supports applied research in industrial automation and sustainable manufacturing, aligning with regional industry needs for cost-effective, reliable mechanical solutions. The project will also provide training opportunities for undergraduate students in HPC-driven engineering workflows, bridging gaps between theoretical mechanics and practical computational tools. Resource allocation will enable the handling of large-scale meshes (>10 million elements) and multi-variable optimization tasks impractical on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the design and development phases of a wide variety of projects involving mechanical systems. Includes instruction in principles of mechanics, applications to specific engineering systems, design testing procedures, prototype and operational testing and inspection procedures, manufacturing system-testing procedures, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and performative elements of comedic storytelling through computational analysis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model large-scale datasets of comedic performances. While comedy’s impact is well-documented anecdotally, systematic analysis of its underlying mechanics—such as timing, linguistic patterns, and audience response dynamics—remains underexplored due to the complexity of multimodal data and the need for real-time processing. The research problem centers on identifying quantifiable metrics that correlate with comedic success, defined by audience engagement and laughter frequency, across diverse genres (e.g., stand-up, sketch, improvisation). To address this, we propose a mixed-methods approach combining natural language processing (NLP) for script and transcript analysis, computer vision techniques to evaluate performer-audience interactions from video datasets, and machine learning models to simulate and predict comedic timing. HPC resources are critical for training these models on terabytes of audiovisual recordings, historical comedy archives, and live performance data, as well as for running agent-based simulations of audience reactions under varying comedic stimuli. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for evaluating comedic content, tools to assist writers and performers in refining material, and new insights into how cultural and historical contexts shape humor reception. This work bridges computational methods with performing arts scholarship, offering a novel methodology for analyzing comedy’s ephemeral qualities at scale. By enabling the processing of heterogeneous, high-volume datasets, HPC infrastructure will directly support advancements in both academic research and practical comedy production, fostering innovation in an art form traditionally reliant on subjective interpretation.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical, cultural, and theoretical dimensions of comedy as an art form, and the writing, performance, and production of comedy. Includes instruction in comedic storytelling, comedy production, comedy writing, history of comedy, improvisation, and sketch writing.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing electrical power transmission systems under increasing demand and the integration of variable renewable energy sources. Existing infrastructure often struggles with dynamic load balancing, fault resilience, and efficiency maintenance, particularly in non-standard grid configurations common to emerging smart grid applications. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing advanced computational models that simulate complex transmission network behaviors under diverse operational scenarios. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale, multi-physics simulations integrating electromagnetic transient analysis, thermal dynamics, and machine learning-driven predictive maintenance algorithms. Key computational tasks include parallelized finite-element modeling of power line stress distributions, GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic fault forecasting, and real-time optimization of distributed energy resource allocation. The proposed methods will account for heterogeneous data inputs, including historical grid performance records, weather patterns, and real-time sensor feeds from prototype installations. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for identifying high-risk infrastructure components, adaptive control strategies for voltage regulation in mixed AC/DC systems, and quantifiable metrics for upgrading legacy installations. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in modeling large networks with sub-millisecond temporal resolution—a critical requirement for analyzing cascading failures and transient phenomena. The results will directly support the development of safer, more resilient power transmission standards while providing training materials for workforce education on next-generation grid technologies. This project bridges a gap in computational research specific to non-traditional electrical installation paradigms, offering scalable tools for utilities and policymakers navigating the transition to decarbonized energy systems.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Environmental health research faces a critical challenge in understanding how complex, interacting environmental exposures collectively impact human health outcomes. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to disentangle the effects of multiple simultaneous stressors—such as air pollutants, water contaminants, and socioeconomic factors—limiting our ability to assess cumulative risks accurately. This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multifactorial environmental exposures and their population-level health implications across spatial and temporal scales. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-modal datasets, including satellite-derived environmental measurements, EPA monitoring records, electronic health repositories, and census-derived demographic data. Agent-based modeling will simulate exposure pathways and health responses under various policy scenarios, while parallelized geospatial analytics will identify high-risk regions through vulnerability indices combining environmental, clinical, and social determinants. Computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated tensor operations for deep learning architectures and distributed memory systems for large-scale epidemiological simulations. The anticipated outcomes include: (1) predictive models quantifying dose-response relationships for exposure mixtures, (2) open-source tools for community-level risk stratification, and (3) evidence-based projections of intervention effectiveness across different environmental justice contexts. By enabling analysis of petabyte-scale datasets and complex systems interactions beyond single-workstation capabilities, the requested resources will advance understanding of environmental health disparities while providing actionable insights for targeted public health strategies. This work directly supports priority initiatives in climate resilience and equitable health protection outlined by federal environmental health agencies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of environmental sciences, public health, the biomedical sciences, and environmental toxicology to the study of environmental factors affecting human health, safety, and related ecological issues, and prepares individuals to function as professional environmental health specialists. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, toxicology, public policy analysis, public management, risk assessment, communications, environmental law, occupational health and safety emergency response, and applications such as air quality, food protection, radiation protection, solid and hazardous waste management, water quality, soil quality, noise abatement, housing quality, and environmental control of recreational areas.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of team coordination and decision-making in distributed work environments using agent-based computational modeling. As organizations increasingly adopt hybrid and remote work structures, understanding how digital communication tools, asynchronous workflows, and reward structures influence collective problem-solving has become critical. Traditional survey-based methods in industrial-organizational psychology struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions and emergent behaviors inherent in complex team systems. We propose developing a high-fidelity simulation environment leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-agent teams with heterogeneous cognitive profiles, communication patterns, and incentive structures. The computational framework will integrate reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate adaptive decision-making under varying organizational constraints, including resource allocation conflicts and time pressure scenarios. By parameterizing models with empirical data from longitudinal field studies of technology sector teams, we aim to identify optimal intervention points for enhancing team resilience and reducing coordination failures. The HPC infrastructure will enable simultaneous execution of thousands of simulation iterations with dynamically adjusted environmental variables, permitting robust sensitivity analyses across cultural, operational, and technological dimensions. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model of team performance degradation thresholds and actionable insights for designing adaptive performance management systems. This work bridges theoretical gaps in organizational behavior literature by quantifying the interaction effects between individual motivation systems and group-level emergent phenomena, while providing practical tools for workforce strategy optimization in rapidly evolving digital workplaces. The computational demands of modeling real-time multi-agent interactions at organizational scales necessitate dedicated HPC resources to achieve sufficient granularity and statistical power in our simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and group behavior in institutional settings, applications to related problems of organization and industry, and that may prepare individuals to apply such principles in industrial and organizational settings. Includes instruction in group behavior theory, organizational theory, reward/punishment structures, human-machine and human-computer interactions, motivation dynamics, human stress studies, environmental and organizational influences on behavior, alienation and satisfaction, and job testing and assessment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying complex trait variation in domesticated livestock, with a focus on cattle and poultry. A critical challenge in animal genetics is resolving how non-coding regulatory elements, structural genomic variation, and epigenetic modifications interact to influence traits such as disease resistance, feed efficiency, and reproductive performance. Traditional single-omics approaches often fail to capture these multilayered interactions, necessitating integrative analyses of whole-genome sequencing, chromatin accessibility data, and methylation profiles across diverse populations. The proposed research will develop computational workflows to identify conserved regulatory networks and lineage-specific epigenetic signatures associated with adaptive and production-related traits. Methods will include comparative genomics to detect evolutionary constraints in regulatory regions, graph-based genome assemblies to resolve structural variants in repetitive loci, and machine learning models to predict the functional impact of non-coding mutations. Large-scale genotype-environment interaction analyses will be conducted to quantify epigenetic plasticity in response to stressors like heat and pathogen exposure. HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets, running population-scale simulations, and optimizing deep learning architectures for regulatory element prediction. Expected outcomes include (1) a catalog of functionally validated regulatory variants linked to economically important traits, (2) predictive models of epigenetic modification under environmental perturbation, and (3) open-access tools for integrating chromatin conformation data with traditional breeding values. These results will directly inform precision breeding strategies and provide a framework for conserving adaptive genetic diversity in livestock populations. By bridging molecular genetics with applied animal science, this work advances fundamental understanding of complex trait architecture while addressing urgent agricultural sustainability challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of multicellular animal life forms from the experimental, comparative, and clinical (veterinary and medical) viewpoints. Includes instruction in molecular genetics, gene expression, gene regulation, genomics, epigenetic phenomena, DNA recombination and repair, genetic interactions at the microbial and higher levels, and molecular evolution.

abstract: Effective communication of agricultural research and practices is critical for bridging the gap between scientific advancements and their practical application by farmers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders. However, the dynamic nature of agricultural systems, combined with diverse audience needs and rapidly evolving digital platforms, poses challenges in tailoring communication strategies for optimal engagement and comprehension. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the efficacy of agricultural communication strategies at scale. Using computational methods, we will process large datasets—including agricultural research publications, social media content, multimedia campaigns, and audience analytics—to identify patterns in information dissemination and reception. Natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques will be applied to evaluate how technical agricultural content is framed, translated, and consumed across different demographics and media formats. Agent-based modeling will simulate information diffusion networks to assess how variables such as message timing, platform choice, and visual storytelling impact audience behavior and knowledge retention. Additionally, predictive analytics will forecast emerging topics in agricultural sciences (e.g., climate-resilient crops, precision livestock farming) to proactively design communication frameworks. The computational demands of processing multimodal data (text, video, geospatial) and running iterative simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include actionable insights for creating adaptive, audience-specific communication tools and a publicly accessible repository of optimized content templates. This work will enhance the capacity of agricultural journalists and communicators to deliver scientifically accurate, contextually relevant information, ultimately supporting informed decision-making in farming communities and strengthening public understanding of agricultural innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply journalistic, communication, and broadcasting principles to the development, production, and transmittal of agricultural information. Includes instruction in basic journalism, broadcasting, film/video, and communication techniques; the production of technically specialized information products for agricultural audiences; and the principles of agricultural sciences and business operations needed to develop and communicate agricultural subject matter in effective ways.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of geometric flows on Riemannian manifolds with singular metrics, a central topic in geometric analysis with implications for understanding the structure and evolution of complex geometric spaces. The research focuses on analyzing the long-time behavior of Ricci-DeTurck flows in settings where the initial metric admits controlled singularities or incomplete regions—a regime critical to conjectures in global analysis and manifold topology. While foundational work has established short-time existence results, the convergence properties and stability of such flows under perturbations remain unresolved, particularly in dimensions ≥4. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining adaptive finite element methods on simplicial complexes with spectral techniques to discretize and evolve the flow equations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multiscale curvature dynamics and manage the high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to these problems. Simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor operations for parallelized metric updates and employ scalable solvers for nonlinear parabolic PDE systems. Key challenges include maintaining numerical stability near singularities and preserving geometric invariants during discretization. The project will validate conjectures related to singularity formation in non-compact settings and test criteria for flow convergence proposed in recent theoretical work. Outcomes will provide quantitative insights into the regularity of geometric flows, inform analytic approaches to open problems in differential geometry, and yield open-source software tools for large-scale geometric PDE computation. Successful results may also clarify connections between flow-driven metrics and topological obstructions in manifold classification. This work requires sustained access to HPC clusters due to the O(10^5) core-hour demands of 3D/4D simulations and the need for iterative parameter sweeps to characterize flow dependence on initial data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties, measurements, and relationships pertaining to points, lines, angles, surfaces, and solids. Includes instruction in global analysis, differential geometry, Euclidian and Non-Euclidian geometry, set theory, manifolds, integral geometry, and applications to algebra and other topics.

abstract: Plants exhibit complex biomechanical behaviors critical for survival, such as tropic movements and structural adaptation, yet the molecular-to-organ scale dynamics governing these processes remain poorly understood. This project seeks to model the emergent mechanical intelligence of plant systems through high-resolution simulations of cellular actuator networks—specialized tissues that generate coordinated motion via hydraulic or osmotic triggers. The research focuses on the fern *Ceratopleris thalictroides*, which performs rapid stereotypic motion using bilayered motor cells, as a model system. We propose developing a multiscale computational framework integrating (1) finite element models of cell wall elasticity and fluid-structure interactions during turgor-driven actuation and (2) agent-based simulations of intercellular signaling that synchronize tissue-scale movement. The HPC component will optimize GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods for simulating cytoplasmic streaming dynamics across 3D cell networks, coupled with Monte Carlo sampling of ion channel gating probabilities under varying environmental conditions. Resource requests include 12,000 node-hours for parameter space exploration and validation against microfluidic experiments measuring real-time pressure gradients. Anticipated outcomes include the first predictive model of distributed biomechanical control in plants, revealing design principles for soft robotics and adaptive materials. This work bridges plant physiology with mechanical engineering paradigms, establishing a novel computational paradigm for studying non-neural biological control systems. By elucidating how decentralized cellular networks achieve precise macroscopic movement without centralized coordination, the project advances fundamental knowledge in plant biomechanics while providing open-source simulation tools for bio-inspired engineering applications.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in botany/plant biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance ethical decision-making frameworks in healthcare through large-scale computational modeling and analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in bioethics: the lack of empirically grounded, dynamic models to evaluate how ethical principles—such as autonomy, justice, and beneficence—interact with real-world variables like resource constraints, cultural diversity, and institutional policies. Current methodologies often rely on static case analyses or qualitative assessments, limiting their ability to predict outcomes in complex, evolving scenarios such as triage during public health emergencies, equitable organ allocation, or AI-driven clinical tools. To address this, the project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating interactions among patients, providers, and policymakers under varying ethical priorities and resource conditions. These models will integrate datasets from clinical trials, public health records, and sociological surveys to parameterize agents’ decision-making behaviors. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze historical ethical guidelines, case law, and institutional policies, identifying patterns and biases in ethical reasoning. Machine learning algorithms will further assess how demographic, socioeconomic, and cultural factors influence perceptions of ethical care. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing required for Monte Carlo simulations exploring thousands of scenario permutations—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify trade-offs in policy decisions, a repository of scenario-based ethical “stress tests” for healthcare systems, and evidence-based frameworks to guide resource allocation in crises. By bridging computational scalability with normative analysis, this work aims to enhance the rigor, equity, and adaptability of bioethics in practice, offering stakeholders actionable insights for policy design and clinical training.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing performance and security in distributed software systems, particularly for applications in cloud computing and real-time data processing environments. Modern software systems face challenges in balancing computational efficiency, scalability, and robustness against evolving security threats, especially when operating across heterogeneous architectures. To tackle these issues, this research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced algorithms for dynamic workload distribution, energy-aware task scheduling, and real-time anomaly detection in large-scale software deployments. Computational methods will include parallelized simulations of distributed systems under varying load conditions, machine learning-driven optimization of resource allocation strategies, and cryptographic protocol testing using Monte Carlo-based vulnerability assessments. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of multi-objective optimization models, large-scale dataset processing for training anomaly detection systems, and stress-testing of proposed encryption techniques against brute-force and side-channel attacks. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for adaptive resource management in distributed environments, empirical benchmarks for energy-efficient software design, and open-source tools to automate security vulnerability detection in cloud-native applications. By providing scalable computational workflows and reproducible testing environments, this work aims to advance best practices in software engineering for high-performance systems while addressing critical gaps in secure, sustainable software development. The requested resources—including GPU-accelerated nodes, high-memory computing clusters, and distributed storage—are essential for handling the project’s data-intensive simulations and ensuring timely validation of results across diverse hardware configurations. Findings will directly contribute to the broader field of computer software technology by enabling more resilient and efficient systems for sectors reliant on distributed computing, such as IoT networks, financial services, and intelligent transportation systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in developing, implementing, and evaluating computer software and program applications. Includes instruction in computer programming, programming languages, databases, user interfaces, networking and warehousing, encryption and security, software testing and evaluation, and customization.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of programmable biomolecular adhesives inspired by extremophile organisms, a novel niche intersecting synthetic biology, materials science, and environmental biotechnology. Current synthetic adhesives face limitations in biocompatibility, recyclability, and performance under extreme conditions, while natural bioadhesives (e.g., mussel foot proteins) lack the tunability required for industrial scalability. We propose a computational pipeline to design de novo adhesive peptides that emulate the hierarchical structure and pH-responsive behavior of archaeal surface proteins, which enable adhesion in hypersaline, high-temperature environments. Molecular dynamics simulations (GROMACS, AMBER) will model peptide folding, surface interaction dynamics, and stress response under parametrized extreme conditions (0–120°C, pH 1–13, salinity up to 5M NaCl). Machine learning (PyTorch, AlphaFold2) will iteratively optimize sequences for target substrate binding (metals, polymers) and environmental resilience. Multi-scale modeling will bridge quantum mechanical calculations of metal-coordination dynamics (VASP) with coarse-grained simulations of bulk adhesive behavior. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from engineered microbial expression systems (Shewanella oneidensis chassis) and industrial adhesion assays. Anticipated outcomes include a validated library of non-canonical adhesive peptides, open-source force fields for extreme-environment biomaterials, and a scalable framework for HPC-driven bioadhesive design. This work addresses critical gaps in sustainable manufacturing and extreme-condition biotechnology, with potential applications in medical device coatings, deep-sea robotics, and recyclable construction materials. Successful implementation requires HPC resources to manage ~2 PB of simulation data, parallelize Monte Carlo sampling across 10,000+ candidate sequences, and reduce optimization cycle times from months to days.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences, biochemistry, and genetics to the preparation of new and enhanced agricultural, environmental, clinical, and industrial products, including the commercial exploitation of microbes, plants, and animals. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, gene identification, phylogenetics and comparative genomics, bioinorganic chemistry, immunoassaying, DNA sequencing, xenotransplantation, genetic engineering, industrial microbiology, drug and biologic development, enzyme-based production processes, patent law, biotechnology management and marketing, applicable regulations, and biotechnology ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance mechanistic understanding of pollutant behavior and remediation in complex environmental systems. A critical challenge in environmental chemistry lies in predicting the fate of contaminants—such as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and heavy metals—across dynamic air-water-soil interfaces, where molecular-scale interactions govern transport, persistence, and reactivity. Experimental approaches alone struggle to resolve these processes due to temporal and spatial limitations, necessitating multiscale computational modeling. The proposed work integrates quantum mechanical calculations, classical molecular dynamics (MD), and machine learning to simulate contaminant interactions with natural organic matter, mineral surfaces, and reactive oxygen species. Density functional theory (DFT) will quantify degradation pathways and free energy barriers for redox-active pollutants, while MD simulations parameterized with experimental data will model sorption/desorption kinetics at environmental interfaces. A machine learning framework will predict contaminant speciation under variable pH, ionic strength, and organic carbon conditions. These computational workflows require HPC capabilities to manage large-scale system sizes (10,000+ atoms), long simulation timescales (µs-range), and high-throughput screening of remediation scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic insights into PFAS retention mechanisms in soil organic coatings, (2) kinetic models for photocatalytic degradation of chlorinated solvents, and (3) predictive tools linking contaminant properties to transport outcomes in heterogeneous matrices. By elucidating molecular drivers of pollutant fate, this work will inform the design of targeted remediation strategies and advance predictive frameworks for environmental risk assessment. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome current limitations in modeling complex, multi-phase systems at environmentally relevant scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of natural systems (air, water, and soil) through the use of chemical techniques and instrumentation, with an emphasis on the movement and fate of pollutants and chemical aspects of contaminant remediation. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; aquatic, soil, and atmospheric chemistry; environmental engineering; environmental toxicology; and analytical methods.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of silicate melt behavior under extreme pressure-temperature (P-T) conditions to resolve long-standing questions about magma differentiation and crust-mantle interaction. A critical barrier in geochemical modeling is the limited accuracy of existing thermodynamic frameworks for multi-component silicate systems, particularly in predicting phase equilibria, trace element partitioning, and isotopic fractionation at conditions relevant to subduction zones and planetary interiors. Current models rely on simplified approximations of melt structure and cation coordination, leading to uncertainties in interpreting geochemical proxies from igneous rocks. To address this, we propose a coupled computational approach integrating quantum mechanical simulations, machine learning (ML)-augmented thermodynamic modeling, and high-throughput phase equilibrium calculations. First, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations will quantify the energetics of silicate melt polymerization and metal isotope partitioning at varying P-T-X conditions. These data will train ML interatomic potentials to extend simulations to larger systems (1,000+ atoms) and longer timescales. Concurrently, a Monte Carlo-based phase equilibrium solver will be optimized to handle 10+ component systems, leveraging parallelization to map stability fields of key mineral assemblages. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental datasets from high-pressure piston-cylinder experiments. The resulting framework will enable predictive modeling of melt-rock reaction pathways, rare earth element mobility, and radiogenic isotope resetting during metamorphism. By elucidating the links between atomic-scale processes and geochemical signatures, this work will transform the interpretation of planetary differentiation records. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential for managing the ∼500,000 core-hour demand of AIMD simulations, ML training on petabyte-scale datasets, and global optimization routines for phase equilibria. Outcomes will be disseminated through open-source code releases and applications to unresolved problems in arc magma genesis and mantle metasomatism.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical properties and behavior of the silicates and other substances forming, and formed by geomorphological processes of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in chemical thermodynamics, equilibrium in silicate systems, atomic bonding, isotopic fractionation, geochemical modeling, specimen analysis, and studies of specific organic and inorganic substances.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the structural and semantic patterns of ritual oral traditions within Indigenous Australian Aboriginal spiritual practices, an understudied area in theological and ministerial studies that intersects anthropology, linguistics, and digital humanities. While extensive work exists on written religious texts, non-literate spiritual traditions—particularly those transmitted orally across generations—remain poorly documented and analyzed due to their ephemerality and cultural sensitivity. The project addresses this gap by employing computational methods to analyze a curated corpus of audio recordings (made in collaboration with Indigenous custodians under strict ethical protocols) to identify recurring linguistic, rhythmic, and narrative structures that encode theological concepts and communal memory. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing large audio datasets, applying machine learning models for phonetic segmentation and pattern recognition, and simulating the diffusion of oral narratives across hypothetical kinship networks using agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) tools adapted for Indigenous Australian languages, spectral analysis of vocal performances, and network theory to map relationships between ritual speech acts and cosmological frameworks. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital methodology for analyzing oral theological traditions without compromising their cultural integrity, new insights into how non-literate spiritual practices sustain coherence amid generational transmission, and publicly shareable computational models (sans culturally restricted data) to support comparative studies of minority religious traditions. By centering Indigenous knowledge systems, this work challenges Eurocentric biases in theological analytics while demonstrating how HPC can advance the study of ephemeral cultural heritage within interdisciplinary humanities research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in theological and ministerial studies not elsewhere classified, including preparation for religious vocations in faiths other than Christianity and Judaism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational methodologies to address evolving challenges in cyber forensics and counterterrorism investigations, particularly the rapid analysis of encrypted, fragmented, or obfuscated digital evidence generated by terrorist networks. Current forensic tools struggle with the scale and complexity of modern operational environments, where adversaries leverage distributed systems, ephemeral communication platforms, and AI-driven obfuscation techniques. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale parallel processing of forensic data, machine learning-driven pattern recognition, and simulations of adversarial cyber tactics. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) optimizing distributed decryption and data reconstruction workflows across multi-terabyte datasets using GPU-accelerated algorithms; (2) training neural networks to identify latent behavioral signatures in encrypted communications metadata; and (3) modeling counterterrorism scenarios through agent-based simulations of dark web networks and operational security protocols. The computational framework will integrate forensic toolkits with custom Python-based analytics pipelines, employing MPI for task parallelism and TensorFlow for deep learning models. Expected outcomes include novel forensic techniques for tracing cryptocurrency laundering patterns, automated detection of steganographic payloads in multimedia files, and predictive models of cyberterrorism infrastructure development. By reducing analysis timelines from weeks to hours for complex cases, this work aims to provide law enforcement and intelligence agencies with actionable insights while maintaining evidentiary integrity. The project will also contribute open-source modules for distributed forensic processing, advancing capabilities at the intersection of computational criminology and cybersecurity.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques used to identify, search, seize and analyze digital media and to conduct cyber investigations against criminal and terrorist activity. Includes instruction in computer boot processes and drives, jumper setting, file access and reconstruction, hacking, network systems, cryptography, programming, investigative techniques, forensic imagery, web-based investigation methods, cyberterrorism, and applicable laws and administrative procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of neurological disorders demands innovative approaches to map dynamic brain network interactions and their disruption in conditions such as traumatic brain injury (TBI) and epilepsy. Current neuroimaging analyses often rely on static connectivity models, failing to capture millisecond-scale network reconfigurations that may underlie symptom variability and treatment resistance. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating magnetoencephalography (MEG), intracranial EEG (iEEG), and machine learning to model spatiotemporal network dynamics at unprecedented temporal granularity. We will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte neurophysiological datasets from 200 patients with post-traumatic epilepsy and 150 controls, employing adaptive graph theory algorithms to track time-varying connectivity patterns. The computational pipeline will include GPU-accelerated signal processing, dynamic community detection optimized for irregular time series, and recurrent neural networks trained to predict network destabilization events preceding seizures. Validation will occur through closed-loop stimulation data from implantable neurodevices, correlating computational predictions with observed neural responses. This work addresses critical gaps in translating network neuroscience to clinical practice by establishing computational biomarkers of network resilience and vulnerability. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolbox for high-temporal-resolution connectomics, 2) classification models linking specific dynamic network motifs to seizure propagation pathways, and 3) proof-of-concept simulations for personalized neuromodulation strategies. The requested HPC resources are essential given the combinatorial complexity of analyzing 10^8+ neural edges across subsecond timescales, which exceeds the capacity of local institutional clusters. By bridging computational neuroscience and clinical neurophysiology, this project aims to advance precision medicine approaches for neurological disorders through enhanced mechanistic modeling of brain network dysfunction.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated clinical science program that prepares clinicians to conduct clinical and translational research in various areas. Note: programs that prepare clinicians to conduct research in specific scientific fields should report under the relevant CIP code series (e.g., Series 26 Biological and Biomedical Sciences).

abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of modern diagnostic medicine, yet persistent challenges in motion artifact reduction, scan time efficiency, and image reconstruction accuracy limit its utility in dynamic or sensitive clinical scenarios. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing advanced computational models for real-time motion correction and accelerated image acquisition. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to implement and optimize machine learning algorithms trained on simulated and clinical MRI datasets to predict and compensate for patient motion during scans. Additionally, the project will explore compressed sensing and parallel imaging techniques to reduce acquisition times while maintaining diagnostic quality. The computational workflow involves large-scale simulations of physiological motion patterns, iterative training of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for artifact detection and correction, and validation against high-resolution phantom and patient datasets. HPC resources are critical to manage the processing demands of 4D spatiotemporal data, enable rapid prototyping of reconstruction pipelines, and support GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks. Success in this work is expected to yield two key outcomes: (1) a deployable software toolkit for real-time motion correction, integrated with existing MRI scanner systems, and (2) optimized protocols for rapid MRI acquisition in clinical settings, particularly for pediatric, geriatric, and trauma patients where motion artifacts are most prevalent. By improving image quality and reducing scan durations, this research directly aligns with the program’s focus on enhancing diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes. The resulting computational frameworks will be shared as open-source resources to advance MRI innovation across the health professions community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals who are AART-certified radiological technicians to utilize MRI technology to obtain still and moving images of various vascular structures in the human body that aid the physician in the diagnosis or treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in MRI imaging, sectional anatomy and pathology, MRI technology, MRI techniques and procedures, MRI physics, and clinical training.

abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified challenges in managing real-time decision-making, scalability, and security across dynamic digital markets. Existing computational methods struggle to optimize complex, large-scale systems—such as personalized recommendation engines, supply chain networks, and fraud detection algorithms—while maintaining responsiveness and data integrity. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test computational models that address these limitations. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating multi-agent e-commerce ecosystems to evaluate adaptive pricing strategies under fluctuating demand, (2) training deep reinforcement learning models for real-time inventory optimization across distributed warehouses, and (3) deploying privacy-preserving federated learning frameworks to detect cross-platform transactional fraud without compromising sensitive user data. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized architectures to process terabyte-scale datasets, including customer interaction logs, supply chain telemetry, and synthetic transaction records generated via generative adversarial networks (GANs). The project integrates graph neural networks to model interdependencies in global supplier networks and employs GPU-accelerated hyperparameter tuning to enhance model accuracy. Outcomes will include open-source tools for scalable demand forecasting, resource allocation algorithms to reduce logistics-related emissions, and a benchmark dataset for evaluating e-commerce fraud detection systems. By enabling granular analysis of system-wide trade-offs between efficiency, cost, and security, this work will advance scalable solutions for sustainable digital commerce. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and latency constraints inherent in traditional cloud environments, ensuring the practical applicability of findings for businesses operating in data-intensive, latency-sensitive markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, supervise, and market electronic business operations, products, and services provided online via the Internet. Includes instruction in business administration, information technology, information resources management, web design, computer and Internet law and policy, computer privacy and security, e-trading, insurance, electronic marketing, investment capital planning, enterprise operations, personnel supervision, contracting, and product and service networking.

abstract: The increasing complexity of software ecosystems demands innovative approaches to optimize code maintenance and adaptability in heterogeneous computing environments. This project addresses the challenge of automating context-aware program refactoring for legacy systems operating across hybrid architectures (CPU/GPU/FPGA). Traditional static analysis tools struggle to account for dynamic runtime behaviors and hardware-specific performance characteristics, particularly when scaling to large codebases. We propose developing a machine learning-driven framework that integrates execution trace analysis, hardware telemetry, and semantic code pattern recognition to recommend optimized code transformations. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model interprocedural code dependencies with reinforcement learning agents trained on performance outcome simulations. High-performance computing resources are critical for two components: (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale execution traces from distributed instrumentation nodes, and (2) simultaneous training of multiple architecture-specific optimization models through hyperparameter-optimized ensemble learning. Our methodology employs containerized microservices to process diverse data streams, including low-level hardware performance counters and abstract syntax tree representations. The expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit capable of suggesting context-sensitive code modifications that preserve functional equivalence while improving energy efficiency by 15-30% across target architectures. This research bridges gaps between conventional program optimization techniques and emerging requirements for adaptive computing infrastructure, particularly in edge computing scenarios where hardware heterogeneity and resource constraints complicate traditional maintenance paradigms. Success metrics will evaluate both computational efficiency gains in the refactoring pipeline itself and downstream performance improvements in transformed applications. The results aim to establish new methodologies for sustainable software evolution in increasingly complex computing environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general writing and implementation of generic and customized programs to drive operating systems and that generally prepares individuals to apply the methods and procedures of software design and programming to software installation and maintenance. Includes instruction in software design, low- and high-level languages and program writing; program customization and linking; prototype testing; troubleshooting; and related aspects of operating systems and networks.

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation aims to restore oral function and aesthetics through advanced materials and devices, yet long-term clinical success remains limited by biomechanical failures, material degradation, and patient-specific anatomical variability. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to model the multiscale interactions between prosthetic devices, biological tissues, and dynamic oral environments, particularly over clinically relevant timescales. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate the biomechanical behavior of prosthodontic systems under diverse functional and biological conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with computational fluid dynamics to model stress distribution in dental implants, removable prostheses, and multi-unit fixed restorations. Patient-specific anatomical data derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and intraoral scans will inform geometric models, while machine learning algorithms will optimize material property assignments based on heterogeneous bone density and soft tissue characteristics. A parallelized multiscale modeling approach will bridge molecular-scale material interactions with macroscale mechanical performance, enabling predictive analysis of fatigue failure in zirconia-based restorations and polymer-acrylic denture bases. Stochastic modeling will further evaluate the probabilistic nature of occlusal loading patterns across demographic cohorts. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro mechanical testing data and longitudinal clinical outcomes from retrospective patient records. By elucidating failure mechanisms and optimizing device design parameters, this work aims to establish predictive guidelines for prosthodontic treatment planning, reduce postoperative complications, and accelerate the development of next-generation bioactive materials. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large-scale simulations, managing high-resolution anatomical datasets, and enabling rapid iteration of design prototypes, ultimately advancing personalized, evidence-based prosthodontic care.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the restoration and maintenance of teeth, oral function, and aesthetic form through the use of single or compound materials, structures, and artificial devices. Includes instruction in implant dentistry, surgical procedures, denture design and fabrication, fixed and removable prosthodontics, restorative techniques, occlusion therapy and devices, geriatric dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how variations in electoral systems influence the emergence and persistence of political polarization in multiparty democracies. While existing literature highlights correlations between electoral rules and polarization, the causal mechanisms driving these relationships remain poorly understood, particularly in dynamic, interactive environments. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based computational model simulating voter-party interactions under different electoral frameworks, including proportional representation and mixed-member systems. The model will incorporate adaptive party strategies aimed at vote maximization, voter preference shifts based on ideological proximity, and real-time feedback mechanisms between electoral outcomes and strategic behavior. Due to the high-dimensional parameter space and the necessity for Monte Carlo simulations to assess robustness across diverse initial conditions, the project requires high-performance computing resources. These resources will enable parallelized execution of thousands of simulation iterations, each modeling complex interactions among hundreds of agents over extended temporal horizons. Expected outcomes include identifying specific electoral configurations that mitigate polarization by incentivizing centrist policy positions, as well as characterizing threshold effects where minor rule changes precipitate significant shifts in party system fragmentation. The findings will contribute to theoretical debates on institutional design and provide actionable insights for policymakers considering electoral reforms. By leveraging computational social science methodologies, this research advances the study of political systems beyond static comparative analyses, offering a dynamic framework to evaluate the long-term consequences of institutional choices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Oral and maxillofacial diseases exhibit significant heterogeneity in clinical presentation, molecular drivers, and treatment responses, complicating accurate diagnosis and personalized management. Current approaches often rely on histopathological analysis or isolated molecular biomarkers, which lack the resolution to fully capture disease complexity. This project proposes an integrative computational framework to analyze multi-modal datasets—including whole-slide histopathology images, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical metadata—to identify predictive signatures of disease progression and therapeutic resistance in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of high-resolution imaging data, perform GPU-accelerated deep learning for feature extraction, and run large-scale simulations of molecular interaction networks. Computational pipelines will employ convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect micro-anatomic patterns in histopathology slides, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model cell-cell communication dynamics, and Bayesian hierarchical models to integrate multi-omics data with clinical outcomes. The project will leverage distributed computing frameworks to parallelize analysis across 500+ patient samples from international collaborator networks. Expected outcomes include: 1) validated computational biomarkers for early detection of high-risk OSCC subtypes, 2) mechanistic insights into medication-related ONJ pathogenesis through simulated bone remodeling pathways, and 3) open-source tools for multimodal data fusion in oral pathology. Results will address critical gaps in prognostic stratification and inform targeted therapeutic strategies. The scale of data processing—requiring >2 PB storage, >50,000 GPU hours, and multi-node memory allocation—necessitates dedicated HPC infrastructure beyond institutional cluster capabilities. This work establishes a paradigm for computational pathology in oral health research, with translational potential for clinical decision-support systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions, using clinical, radiographic, microscopic, biochemical, or other examinations.

abstract: This project seeks to address a critical gap in personalized financial planning by integrating behavioral dynamics with high-dimensional computational optimization under uncertainty. Traditional portfolio optimization models often rely on static assumptions of rational decision-making, neglecting the heterogeneous and time-varying behavioral biases observed in real-world clients, such as loss aversion, overconfidence, and framing effects. To bridge this divide, we propose a computational framework that combines agent-based modeling, stochastic optimization, and reinforcement learning to simulate and optimize client-specific financial strategies in dynamically evolving market and behavioral environments. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to operationalize three interconnected modules: (1) a scalable behavioral agent simulator capturing client-specific cognitive biases and life-event triggers, (2) a multi-stage stochastic optimization engine for adaptive goal-based planning, and (3) a deep reinforcement learning system trained to recommend interventions balancing quantitative outcomes with behavioral adherence. By processing terabytes of historical market data, demographic records, and psychometric survey inputs, the HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of synthetic client scenarios while maintaining real-time responsiveness for practical deployment. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for financial advisors to stress-test strategies against both market volatility and behavioral drift, alongside novel insights into the stability conditions of hybrid human-AI financial planning systems. This work aims to advance the emerging field of computational behavioral finance by providing empirically grounded, adaptive frameworks that reconcile mathematical optimization with psychological realism, ultimately enhancing the robustness and personalization of financial services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage the financial interests and growth of individuals and institutions. Includes instruction in portfolio management, investment management, estate planning, insurance, tax planning, strategic investing and planning, financial consulting services, and client relations.

abstract: Understanding the evolutionary relationships among species within rapidly radiating clades remains a central challenge in systematic biology, particularly when morphological and molecular data yield conflicting phylogenetic signals. This project seeks to resolve the evolutionary history of a hyper-diverse tropical plant clade (genus *Neotropicala*) that exhibits exceptional species richness, complex biogeographic patterns, and ambiguous trait evolution. Current phylogenetic hypotheses based on single-locus or limited morphological matrices are incongruent, hindering taxonomic stability and conservation prioritization. To address this, we propose a computationally intensive integration of genome-scale sequence data (targeted sequence capture of 1,500 loci), high-resolution 3D morphological trait modeling from herbarium specimens, and historical biogeographic reconstructions.
