A key computational bottleneck lies in reconciling heterogeneous gene trees with species trees under complex evolutionary scenarios (e.g., hybridization, incomplete lineage sorting) while simultaneously modeling correlated trait evolution across a phylogeny of ~800 extant species. We will employ Bayesian multi-species coalescent frameworks (e.g., StarBEAST2) and parallelized maximum likelihood approaches (IQ-TREE) to infer phylogenies from terabyte-scale sequence alignments, coupled with phylogenetic comparative methods (RevBayes) to assess trait evolution and biogeographic dispersal models. These analyses demand high-performance computing resources for Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling across thousands of gene trees, iterative model testing, and likelihood optimization under partitioned schemes. The project will leverage GPU acceleration for morphological landmark analyses and containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility. Expected outcomes include (1) a robust, dated phylogeny resolving deep-node conflicts, (2) taxonomic revisions informed by explicit evolutionary delimitation criteria, and (3) new insights into how abiotic factors and trait innovation drive tropical diversification. By addressing computational constraints in large-scale phylogenetic synthesis, this work will advance methodological frameworks for integrating heterogeneous biological data while directly informing conservation strategies for threatened Neotropical biodiversity hotspots.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive learning systems (ALS) to deliver personalized, real-time instructional interventions in large-scale educational environments. While ALS have shown promise in improving learning outcomes, their effectiveness is constrained by the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous data streams—including learner interactions, multimodal content engagement, and biometric indicators—in dynamic, real-world educational contexts. Current approaches struggle to balance model granularity with latency requirements, particularly when scaling to thousands of concurrent users. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for training and deploying machine learning models that analyze temporal patterns in learner behavior while maintaining responsiveness. The research will utilize distributed deep learning architectures to process multimodal educational datasets, including clickstream logs, video annotation patterns, and writing process analytics captured from 15,000+ learners across six institutional partners. Computational experiments will compare transformer-based models, temporal graph networks, and hybrid neuro-symbolic approaches for predicting learner confusion states and knowledge retention. GPU-accelerated simulations will model intervention timing effects across diverse pedagogical scenarios, while containerized microservices will enable A/B testing of adaptive strategies in live environments. Expected outcomes include optimized algorithms for low-latency personalization in web-based instruction, validated metrics for computational efficiency in educational AI systems, and open-source tools for scalable learning analytics. By establishing HPC-powered methods to reconcile model complexity with real-time constraints, this work aims to advance the design of next-generation educational software capable of supporting equitable, data-driven instruction at institutional scales. The results will provide empirically grounded frameworks for integrating high-dimensional learning data into adaptive curricula, contributing to evidence-based practices in educational technology research.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, computer applications, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: The study of virus-host interactions at the molecular level is critical to understanding viral pathogenesis and developing targeted therapeutic strategies. A key challenge in virology lies in modeling the dynamic interplay between viral proteins and host cell machinery, particularly during early infection stages. Traditional experimental approaches face limitations in resolving the structural and temporal complexity of these interactions. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate viral entry mechanisms and replication processes for RNA viruses, with a focus on influenza A and coronaviruses. Specifically, we aim to characterize the conformational dynamics of viral fusion proteins and their binding affinity to host receptors under varying physiological conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be performed using all-atom and coarse-grained models to capture time-dependent changes in protein structures and membrane interactions. These simulations will integrate cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography data to refine energy landscapes and predict critical binding intermediates. Additionally, we will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-omics datasets from infected cell lines, identifying host factors that correlate with viral replication efficiency. The computational workflow requires significant parallel processing capabilities due to the scale of simulation systems (>1 million atoms) and the need for repeated sampling across microsecond timescales. Access to HPC resources will enable the execution of ensemble simulations, free energy calculations, and large-scale parameter optimization, which are infeasible with local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into viral membrane fusion, identification of host dependency factors, and predictive models of viral evolution under selective pressure. This work will directly inform experimental virology efforts by prioritizing high-value targets for antibody neutralization studies and antiviral drug design. By bridging computational biophysics with virological research, the project advances foundational knowledge of viral pathogenesis while contributing to the development of resilience strategies against emerging viral threats.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of subcellular pieces of genetic material, called viruses, that inhabit living cells in parasitical relationships and their role in disease. Includes instruction in virus taxonomy and systematics, viral structures, viral genetics, prions, virus/host cell interaction, viral pathogenesis, and applications to specific topics such as cancer biology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the diffusion and transformation of cultural narratives across sub-Saharan Africa and its diasporas through large-scale textual and multimedia datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in African cultural studies: the lack of systematic, computationally driven methodologies to map how oral traditions, folktales, and vernacular art forms evolve as they intersect with modern digital platforms, migration patterns, and transnational identity formations. Current scholarship relies heavily on localized ethnographic case studies, limiting comparative insights into pan-African cultural dynamics. To address this, the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to digitized archives of oral histories, contemporary social media content, and visual art repositories. Custom transformer models will be trained to detect linguistic and thematic motifs across diverse African languages and dialects, while graph-based algorithms will model the networked circulation of narratives between geographic regions and diasporic communities. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including high-resolution imagery of material culture and multilingual text corpora, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage systems. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas visualizing cultural narrative flows from the precolonial era to the present, alongside computational frameworks for ethically grounded analysis of indigenous knowledge systems. By revealing understudied connections between historical memory and contemporary identity expression, this work aims to reshape scholarly approaches to cultural preservation and diaspora studies while providing open-source tools for African institutions engaged in digital heritage initiatives. The project’s scale and interdisciplinary demands—bridging African humanities, computational linguistics, and ethical AI—make HPC infrastructure indispensable to its execution.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara, and including the African diasporas overseas.

abstract: The study addresses the computational analysis of regional Slovak dialects, which exhibit significant lexical, phonetic, and syntactic variation that remains under-documented in contemporary linguistic research. Traditional methods, reliant on manual transcription and comparative analysis, struggle to process the vast corpus of audio recordings and historical texts needed to map dialect evolution and inter-regional influences comprehensively. This project seeks to deploy high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale natural language processing (NLP) of digitized archival materials, including 20th-century folk narratives, modern spoken-word corpora, and regional publications. Computational workflows will integrate phonetic alignment algorithms to compare audio recordings against standardized Slovak, transformer-based models for diachronic text analysis, and graph-based clustering to identify lexical diffusion patterns across geographic and temporal axes. The HPC infrastructure will accelerate the training of custom dialect identification models, reduce processing times for acoustic feature extraction, and facilitate the synthesis of multidimensional datasets (text, audio, metadata) through parallelized pipelines. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialect features, interactive visualizations of language change, and probabilistic models quantifying the influence of sociohistorical factors on linguistic divergence. By bridging computational linguistics with Slavic philology, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for minority language preservation while offering new insights into the dynamics of Slovak as a pluricentric language. The resource allocation will directly support the first systematic, data-driven study of Slovak dialectometry, with implications for educational resource development, cultural heritage digitization, and cross-disciplinary applications in sociolinguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Slovak language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation aims to optimize functional outcomes for children with disabilities, yet the development of personalized, evidence-based interventions remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of patient populations and the complexity of multi-modal data. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale clinical, biomechanical, and neuroimaging datasets. The primary research problem involves identifying predictive biomarkers of motor recovery in children with cerebral palsy (CP) and tailoring rehabilitation protocols based on individualized computational models. Current statistical methods lack the capacity to integrate high-dimensional data—including motion capture kinematics, electromyography, diffusion tensor imaging, and electronic health records (EHRs)—while accounting for nonlinear interactions and temporal dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining deep learning architectures with mechanistic biomechanical simulations. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will process neuroimaging data to map white matter integrity to motor function, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will model longitudinal EHRs and wearable sensor data to predict treatment responses. These data-driven models will be coupled with physics-based simulations of musculoskeletal dynamics to explore hypothetical rehabilitation scenarios in silico. The HPC environment is critical for training ensemble models across thousands of patient cases, running parallelized simulations, and performing hyperparameter optimization at scale. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool for stratifying CP patients into optimal therapy pathways, (2) quantitative biomarkers linking neuroplasticity to functional gains, and (3) open-source computational workflows for pediatric rehabilitation research. By enabling the synthesis of diverse data types at unprecedented resolution, this work will advance precision rehabilitation paradigms, reduce trial-and-error in clinical decision-making, and provide a template for computationally intensive analyses in pediatric populations. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for petabyte-scale datasets, and high-throughput processing of simulated rehabilitation trials.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Rehabilitation

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of hemodynamic and metabolic responses during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) procedures, a core component of perfusion technology. Despite standardized protocols, patient-specific variability in physiological responses to CPB—such as inflammatory cascades, hemodynamic instability, and end-organ perfusion imbalances—remains a critical challenge. Current clinical approaches rely on reactive adjustments during surgery, which may delay intervention and increase perioperative risks. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating patient-specific hemodynamic data, real-time sensor inputs, and multi-scale physiological models to predict dynamic responses to CPB. The project will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model blood flow through extracorporeal circuits and coupled organ-specific metabolic models to predict oxygen delivery, acid-base balance, and inflammatory mediator dynamics. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective clinical datasets to identify patterns linking preoperative patient characteristics (e.g., comorbidities, vascular compliance) to intraoperative instability. HPC resources are essential to resolve the high dimensionality of these models, enable parallelized parameter optimization, and process real-time data streams within clinically relevant timeframes. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool to guide perfusionists in preemptive parameter adjustments (e.g., pump flow rates, anticoagulation dosing) and a publicly accessible simulation library for extracorporeal circulation scenarios. By reducing trial-and-error decision-making, this work aims to improve patient outcomes, minimize postoperative complications, and establish computational modeling as a translational pillar in perfusion education. The resulting datasets and models will also support future research into personalized perfusion strategies and virtual training environments for perfusion students.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to operate extracorporeal circulation and autotransfusion equipment during medical procedures and surgeries where the support or temporary replacement of a patient's own respiratory or circulatory system is required. Includes instruction in equipment selection and operation, physician and medical team consultation, patient condition monitoring, procedural techniques, and principles of respiratory and circulatory physiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance clinical decision-making models for optimizing patient care coordination in the Clinical Nurse Leader (CNL) role. CNLs operate in complex healthcare environments where dynamic patient data, evidence-based guidelines, and interdisciplinary collaboration intersect. However, integrating real-time patient variables (e.g., vital signs, medication responses, comorbidities) with population-level epidemiological trends and clinical protocols remains computationally intensive, limiting the scalability of predictive tools for individualized care planning. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning framework that synthesizes heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, wearable device outputs, and public health databases—to model patient-specific risks and recommend interventions. HPC resources will enable the training of deep neural networks on multi-modal data streams, parallelized simulations of care pathways under varying constraints, and sensitivity analyses to quantify protocol efficacy across diverse patient subgroups. Key computational challenges include managing high-dimensional temporal data, resolving inconsistencies in clinical documentation formats, and ensuring model interpretability for frontline use. Outcomes will include an open-source predictive tool to prioritize interventions for acute and chronic conditions, validated against retrospective patient outcomes, and a framework for dynamically updating care plans based on real-time data. This work directly supports the CNL’s role in bridging research and practice by translating large-scale clinical data into actionable insights, with potential impacts on reducing hospital readmissions, adverse events, and costs. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project aims to advance precision nursing workflows while fostering interdisciplinary innovation in healthcare analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: The accelerating loss of biodiversity and ecosystem resilience due to habitat fragmentation and climate change necessitates predictive frameworks to guide conservation interventions. This project addresses critical gaps in understanding how multispecies assemblages across heterogeneous landscapes will respond to synergistic pressures from anthropogenic land-use change and shifting climatic regimes. We propose to develop an integrative, spatially explicit modeling platform to simulate population dynamics, species interactions, and habitat connectivity under multiple future scenarios. The computational approach combines agent-based models for focal species with dynamic vegetation models, parameterized using empirical data from long-term ecological monitoring networks across three threatened biomes (tropical montane forests, coastal wetlands, and temperate grasslands). High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve complex feedbacks between fine-scale habitat structure, metapopulation viability, and landscape-scale dispersal processes across decadal timescales. Key innovations include the incorporation of genomic data to estimate adaptive capacity thresholds and machine learning techniques to optimize habitat corridor designs under resource constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical habitat nodes and dispersal corridors for 27 IUCN Red List species, (2) predictive maps of ecosystem collapse thresholds under different climate pathways, and (3) a decision-support toolkit for prioritizing conservation investments across spatial scales. By integrating evolutionary resilience metrics with landscape permeability analyses, this work will advance conservation planning paradigms beyond static protected area models toward dynamic, climate-adaptive strategies. The resulting open-source simulation framework will enable resource managers to evaluate trade-offs between biodiversity preservation and human development pressures in rapidly changing environments.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences to the specific problems of biodiversity, species preservation, ecological sustainability, and habitat fragmentation in the face of advancing human social, economic, and industrial pressures. Includes instruction in ecology, environmental science, biological systems, extinction theory, human-animal and human-plant interaction, ecosystem science and management, wetland conservation, field biology, forest and wildlife biology, and natural history.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance understanding of feedback mechanisms between terrestrial hydrological systems and biogeochemical cycles under climate change, with a focus on quantifying how shifting precipitation regimes and land-use practices alter water-carbon-nutrient dynamics at regional scales. Current models often treat hydrological and biogeochemical processes in isolation, limiting their ability to predict cascading impacts on ecosystem resilience and carbon sequestration. This project will develop an integrated high-resolution modeling framework coupling a physically based hydrological model with a biogeochemical reaction network to simulate spatially explicit nutrient fluxes, soil carbon turnover, and vegetation responses. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve fine-scale heterogeneities in soil properties, topography, and land cover across a 100,000 km² study domain in a temperate mixed-forest biome. Satellite remote sensing data (Sentinel-2, Landsat) will be assimilated to constrain vegetation dynamics and soil moisture patterns, while machine learning techniques will optimize parameterization of subsurface biogeochemical reactions. Parallelized model workflows will employ MPI-based domain decomposition to handle >10⁸ grid cells, with iterative ensemble runs conducted to quantify uncertainty under multiple climate scenarios (CMIP6). Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold precipitation values that trigger nonlinear changes in soil carbon loss and nitrogen leaching, (2) quantification of land-management strategies that buffer ecosystems against hydroclimate extremes, and (3) open-source release of optimized model code for community use. The HPC resources requested are critical for achieving the required spatial-temporal resolution and ensemble size, as a single model year currently requires ~12,000 CPU-hours. By bridging gaps between hydrological and biogeochemical modeling paradigms, this work will provide actionable insights for policymakers addressing interconnected challenges of water security, agricultural sustainability, and climate mitigation in terrestrial Earth systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction of the Earth's oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial systems. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: The increasing complexity of health insurance claims, driven by rising claim volumes, evolving regulations, and sophisticated fraud schemes, necessitates advanced computational tools to enhance accuracy and efficiency in claims adjudication. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to automate the detection of anomalous claims patterns, optimize adjudication workflows, and evaluate compliance with regulatory standards. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources is critical due to the scale of claims data—millions of records spanning structured claims data, unstructured clinical notes, and policy documents—and the computational demands of training deep learning models on such heterogeneous datasets. The research will utilize a hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP) for text extraction from medical records, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model relationships between providers, patients, and procedures, and reinforcement learning to simulate adjudication decision-making under dynamic regulatory constraints. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing multi-terabyte datasets, training ensemble models for fraud prediction, and running large-scale simulations to assess system performance under varying policy scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable, interpretable framework for real-time claims analysis, validated against historical claims data from partner insurers, and a regulatory compliance dashboard to flag high-risk cases. This work aims to reduce administrative costs, improve detection of fraudulent or erroneous claims, and provide decision-support tools for claims examiners. The HPC infrastructure is essential to manage distributed training across GPU nodes, optimize hyperparameter tuning, and enable rapid iteration of models in response to emerging fraud tactics or regulatory changes. By integrating computational advances with domain-specific expertise in health insurance operations, this project bridges a critical gap in claims examination methodologies and supports the development of ethically aligned, transparent AI tools for the healthcare industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized investigatory, analytical, evaluative, and consultative functions related to health/medical insurance operations and their regulation. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes and procedures, health insurance law and regulations, health care industry law, record-keeping, analytic and investigatory techniques, evaluation methods, field operations methods, office procedures, related software applications, oral and written communications skills, interviewing techniques, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in detecting anomalous health insurance claims through the development of a machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC). Current manual and rule-based methods for claims evaluation struggle to scale with the growing volume and complexity of claims data, leading to delayed fraud detection, unnecessary administrative costs, and inconsistent adjudication outcomes. We propose a computational approach leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) to model dynamic relationships between providers, patients, and billing patterns across multi-modal datasets, including claims histories, electronic health records, and geospatial service utilization trends. The HPC environment is critical for training GNNs on terabyte-scale claims datasets spanning 50 million anonymized records, while maintaining compliance with data privacy constraints through distributed, in-memory processing. Key technical challenges include optimizing sparse matrix operations for heterogeneous GPU clusters and developing novel attention mechanisms to prioritize high-risk claim features across temporal windows. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time anomaly scoring of claims, validated against confirmed fraud cases from historical data. Success metrics include a 30% improvement in early fraud detection rates compared to existing systems and a 50% reduction in computational latency during batch processing. This research bridges gaps between health insurance informatics and advanced computational analytics, offering scalable tools to enhance claims examiners’ decision-making while contributing methodological innovations in graph-based machine learning for regulatory applications. Results will inform operational guidelines for integrating AI-assisted workflows into claims examination protocols, with potential applications in payer oversight and healthcare policy analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized investigatory, analytical, evaluative, and consultative functions related to health/medical insurance operations and their regulation. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes and procedures, health insurance law and regulations, health care industry law, record-keeping, analytic and investigatory techniques, evaluation methods, field operations methods, office procedures, related software applications, oral and written communications skills, interviewing techniques, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex infectious and non-communicable diseases in livestock populations poses significant challenges to global food security and animal welfare. Current approaches to understanding disease mechanisms and optimizing treatment strategies are limited by the computational demands of analyzing large-scale genomic, proteomic, and clinical datasets. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision veterinary medicine through the integration of multi-omics data and machine learning. The primary research problem centers on identifying genetic and molecular biomarkers associated with disease susceptibility and treatment response in cattle populations affected by bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), a leading cause of economic loss in the livestock industry. We propose a computational pipeline combining whole-genome sequencing data from 5,000 cattle, longitudinal health records, and pathogen metagenomic profiles to model host-pathogen interactions. Deep learning architectures will be trained to predict disease outcomes and optimize therapeutic protocols based on individual genetic profiles and microbial communities. The scale of data (estimated at 400 TB) and complexity of network analyses necessitate distributed computing for genome-wide association studies, metagenomic assembly, and neural network training. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of candidate genes influencing BRDC resistance, (2) predictive models for treatment efficacy across genetic subpopulations, and (3) open-source tools for genomic risk assessment in veterinary practice. This work will establish a framework for data-driven animal health management while addressing critical gaps in translational bioinformatics for livestock species. Successful implementation could reduce antibiotic overuse through targeted interventions, directly supporting sustainable agricultural practices and advancing veterinary care standards. The requested computing resources will enable processing timelines impractical on local clusters, particularly for comparative analyses across 20+ pathogen strains and genome-scale simulations of host immune responses.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary or animal health technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical and physiological factors contributing to sports-related injuries through advanced computational modeling. Athletic trainers currently rely on generalized protocols for injury prevention and rehabilitation, which often lack personalization due to the complexity of human movement dynamics and tissue response. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate injury mechanisms, optimize therapeutic interventions, and predict recovery outcomes. The research will integrate multi-modal data, including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and medical imaging, to construct patient-specific models of musculoskeletal stress during athletic activities. Finite element analysis and machine learning algorithms will be employed to model tissue-level damage (e.g., ligament tears, muscle strains) and evaluate the efficacy of rehabilitation exercises under varying biomechanical conditions. The computational pipeline will leverage parallel processing to handle large datasets and perform iterative simulations across diverse scenarios, such as sport-specific movements, equipment adjustments, and physiological stressors. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk movement patterns, data-driven guidelines for personalized rehabilitation, and open-source tools to assist athletic trainers in designing targeted interventions. By elucidating the relationships between biomechanical load, tissue adaptation, and recovery, this work aims to reduce injury recurrence rates and improve return-to-play decision-making. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling these analyses across heterogeneous datasets and ensuring robust validation through parameter sweeps and sensitivity testing. This project will advance evidence-based practices in athletic training, offering a transformative approach to injury management grounded in computational precision.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work in consultation with, and under the supervision of physicians to prevent and treat sports injuries and associated conditions. Includes instruction in the identification, evaluation, and treatment of athletic injuries and illnesses; first aid and emergency care; therapeutic exercise; anatomy and physiology; exercise physiology; kinesiology and biomechanics; nutrition; sports psychology; personal and community health; knowledge of various sports and their biomechanical and physiological demands; and applicable professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize multi-stage procurement decision-making under supply chain uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address scalability challenges in real-world contracting scenarios. Traditional procurement models struggle to integrate dynamic variables such as fluctuating supplier reliability, geopolitical risks, and real-time market pricing at enterprise scales, often relying on oversimplified assumptions. We propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach combining Monte Carlo methods, agent-based modeling, and stochastic integer programming to capture complex interdependencies between vendor selection, contract terms, and risk mitigation strategies. The computational workflow will process large-scale datasets—including historical vendor performance metrics, geopolitical event logs, and commodity price trajectories—to train gradient-boosted tree models predicting supply disruption probabilities. These predictions will inform parallelized contract scenario evaluations across thousands of simulated risk profiles using CUDA-accelerated optimization kernels. A key innovation involves embedding legal constraint satisfaction directly into the optimization loop through automated parsing of contract clause libraries using natural language processing techniques. Initial pilot studies on regional-scale problems show promising results but face memory bottlenecks when scaling to multinational procurement networks with >10^4 decision variables. Access to HPC resources will enable full deployment of our distributed genetic algorithm for Pareto-optimal contract portfolio generation, requiring simultaneous evaluation of 50,000+ candidate solutions per iteration. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for procurement risk analytics and empirically validated thresholds for centralized vs. decentralized contracting strategies in volatile markets. This work directly advances computational methods in acquisition management while providing actionable insights for organizations managing high-value, long-lead-time procurement systems.
cip_title: Purchasing, Procurement/ Acquisitions and Contracts Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and/or administer the processes by which a firm or organization contracts for goods and services to support its operations, as well as contracts it to sell to other firms or organizations. Includes instruction in contract law, negotiations, buying procedures, government contracting, cost and price analysis, vendor relations, contract administration, auditing and inspection, relations with other firm departments, and applications to special areas such as high-technology systems, international purchasing, and construction.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in healthcare administrative workflows, particularly in scheduling, communication, and resource coordination, which contribute to operational delays, increased costs, and reduced patient satisfaction. Medical administrative professionals are critical to managing these workflows, yet existing tools often lack the computational power to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., electronic health records, appointment logs, staff communications) required for optimizing decision-making. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that identify bottlenecks in healthcare operations. Using anonymized datasets from partner clinics, we will train machine learning algorithms to forecast patient no-show rates, predict resource utilization conflicts, and model the impact of alternative scheduling protocols. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze communication patterns between administrative staff and clinical teams, identifying inefficiencies in task delegation and urgency prioritization. Agent-based simulations will further test the scalability of proposed workflow adjustments under varying patient volumes and staffing conditions. The computational intensity of processing multi-modal data (structured records, unstructured text, temporal sequences) necessitates HPC infrastructure to enable parallelized model training and real-time simulations. Outcomes will include actionable insights for redesigning administrative protocols, reducing patient wait times, and improving alignment between staffing resources and demand. This work directly supports the training goals of medical administrative professionals by advancing data-driven tools for operational decision-making, while adhering to healthcare privacy regulations and ethical standards. Results will be disseminated through open-source workflow optimization frameworks tailored for non-technical users, ensuring accessibility for healthcare administrators and educators.
cip_title: Medical Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing physicians and nurses, health care facilities and services administrators, and other health care professionals. Includes instruction in business and medical communications, medical terminology, principles of health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The adverse effects of synthetic and naturally occurring chemical substances on animals present complex challenges in veterinary toxicology, particularly in understanding dose-response relationships, metabolic pathways, and mechanisms of organ-specific toxicity. Traditional experimental approaches to evaluate these outcomes are resource-intensive, limited in scalability, and often fail to capture interspecies variability or synergistic effects of chemical mixtures. This project proposes a computational toxicology framework to model chemical interactions, predict toxicokinetic profiles, and identify biomarkers of exposure across diverse animal species. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate physicochemical property databases, species-specific genomic and proteomic datasets, and clinical toxicology reports to develop machine learning models capable of simulating toxin absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) processes. Molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to study toxin-receptor binding affinities and conformational changes in target proteins associated with neurobehavioral and reproductive toxicities. A multi-scale modeling approach will bridge quantum mechanical calculations of reactive metabolite formation with population-level pharmacokinetic predictions. The computational pipeline will be validated against existing in vivo data from companion animals and livestock exposed to pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and environmental contaminants. Expected outcomes include predictive models to accelerate risk assessment of emerging chemical threats, optimize antidote development, and inform species-specific treatment protocols. By enabling large-scale analysis of chemical-biological interactions across taxonomic groups, this work addresses critical gaps in veterinary clinical toxicology while reducing reliance on animal testing. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational demands of parallelized simulations, deep learning architectures, and integration of heterogeneous biological datasets at clinically relevant scales.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical application of research on the nature and extent of adverse effects of synthetic and naturally occurring chemical substances on animals. May included related research in chemical mechanisms and the specialties of reproductive, developmental, genetic, forensic, inhalation and neurobehavioral toxicology.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate high-performance computing (HPC) into the interdisciplinary study of jewelry arts to address challenges in material optimization, design complexity, and sustainable innovation. Traditional jewelry design relies heavily on manual experimentation, which limits the exploration of intricate geometries, novel material combinations, and structural durability under real-world conditions. The research problem centers on overcoming these constraints by leveraging computational modeling to simulate material behaviors, predict mechanical performance, and generate design iterations that balance aesthetic intent with functional feasibility. The project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution in wearable pieces, machine learning (ML) algorithms to analyze historical design patterns and propose culturally resonant yet innovative forms, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to optimize casting and electroforming processes. Additionally, high-fidelity 3D rendering and virtual prototyping will be used to visualize complex textures, gemstone interactions, and light-reflective properties in diverse environments. These simulations require HPC resources due to the high-resolution meshing, multi-physics interactions, and large datasets involved. Proposed outcomes include a computational framework for predicting metal fatigue in micro-scale jewelry components, a generative AI tool for rapid design iteration, and data-driven guidelines for reducing material waste in lapidary processes. The integration of HPC aims to advance jewelry arts by enabling precision in craftsmanship, expanding creative possibilities for non-traditional materials, and fostering sustainable practices. This work bridges artisanal traditions with computational innovation, offering a model for interdisciplinary collaboration in visual arts and design. Results will be disseminated through open-access datasets, exhibitions featuring computationally co-designed pieces, and workshops to train emerging artists in hybrid digital-physical methodologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by fashioning jewelry from gems, other stones, and precious metals. Includes instruction in design concepts, electroforming, enameling, gemology, lapidary technique and art, metal and non-metal casting and molding, metal coloring, metalsmithing and finishing, personal style development, photo etching, and stone cutting and polishing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing industrial manufacturing processes through advanced simulation and machine learning, addressing the challenge of balancing efficiency, cost, and sustainability in complex production systems. Traditional trial-and-error approaches and simplified analytical models often fail to account for the dynamic interactions between material properties, equipment behavior, environmental factors, and workflow constraints. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute multi-scale, multi-physics simulations integrated with real-time sensor data and predictive analytics. The computational approach will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and thermal modeling of manufacturing components, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for process flow optimization, and agent-based modeling to simulate production line logistics. Machine learning algorithms will then analyze these datasets to identify bottlenecks, predict equipment degradation, and recommend parameter adjustments. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of these concurrent simulations, which require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets with millisecond-level temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin prototype capable of reducing material waste by 15–20% in additive manufacturing use cases, improving energy efficiency in CNC machining operations by 12–18%, and enabling adaptive control of hybrid production systems. The research will also yield generalized optimization workflows applicable to small-to-medium enterprises in the aerospace and automotive sectors. By providing open-source tools for HPC-driven process optimization, this work aims to advance the implementation of Industry 4.0 technologies while addressing workforce training needs through case studies on system integration and computational resource management. Successful implementation will be validated through partnerships with three regional manufacturers, using production logs and IoT sensor data from active facilities.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: Agricultural systems face mounting pressure to optimize post-harvest storage of perishable commodities under climate variability, yet current facility designs often lack adaptive, region-specific solutions to minimize spoilage. This project proposes a computational framework to model multi-scale interactions between environmental conditions, microbial dynamics, and engineered storage systems for perishable crops in tropical regions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop coupled simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow patterns, discrete element modeling (DEM) for crop pile mechanics, and agent-based modeling (ABM) for microbial colonization processes. These models will be parameterized using field data from partner cooperatives in Southeast Asia, focusing on rice and tuber storage systems. Machine learning techniques will be employed to identify critical thresholds in temperature, humidity, and ventilation rates that accelerate spoilage under varying climatic scenarios. A novel aspect involves inverse design optimization using genetic algorithms to propose low-energy storage configurations adaptable to fluctuating external conditions. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from hyperspectral imaging of crop quality degradation and IoT sensor arrays monitoring real storage environments. Expected outcomes include predictive digital twins of storage ecosystems, validated against physical prototypes, that reduce post-harvest mass loss by 15-30% compared to conventional designs. This work bridges gaps between agricultural process engineering, microbial ecology, and climate resilience planning, providing open-source simulation tools to aid smallholder farmers and storage operators in resource-limited settings. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the non-linear, multi-physics nature of these interactions at operational timescales, enabling parametric studies across thousands of climate-realized futures and design permutations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems, equipment and facilities for production, processing, storage, handling, distribution and use of food, feed, and fiber. Includes applications to aquaculture, forestry, human and natural resources.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the multifactorial mechanisms underlying endometriosis, a chronic condition affecting 10% of reproductive-aged women, with significant diagnostic delays and limited therapeutic options. Despite advances in genomic and hormonal profiling, the integration of high-dimensional datasets—including single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomics, and longitudinal clinical data—remains computationally prohibitive for identifying predictive biomarkers and disease subtypes. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-omics integration framework capable of analyzing terabytes of heterogeneous data from a cohort of 2,000 patients across five clinical sites. A hybrid machine learning pipeline will be implemented, combining graph neural networks to model cellular signaling pathways with Bayesian hierarchical models to account for population-level hormonal variability. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further explore the role of immune cell migration patterns in lesion microenvironment formation. These analyses require parallelized processing of sparse matrices and iterative parameter optimization, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory architectures. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets linked to prostaglandin signaling dysregulation, a validated risk stratification tool for surgical intervention timing, and a public omics database annotated with clinical phenotypes. By elucidating spatial and temporal drivers of endometriosis progression, this work aims to reduce diagnostic latency by 30% in validation cohorts and inform precision medicine trials. The requested HPC allocation is essential to overcome current bottlenecks in data harmonization and real-time model training, ensuring scalable, reproducible workflows for future studies in underrepresented gynecologic conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on Women's Health

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for optimizing context-aware multimedia delivery in heterogeneous web environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address dynamic resource allocation challenges inherent to adaptive user interfaces. Current web design paradigms struggle to balance real-time multimedia personalization—such as device-specific resolution scaling, bandwidth-aware asset selection, and accessibility-driven content adaptation—with the computational overhead required to maintain low-latency user experiences. Traditional edge-computing solutions lack the capacity to model complex, multi-objective optimization scenarios involving thousands of concurrent user contexts, including variable network conditions, device capabilities, and user preference profiles. The proposed research will implement a distributed simulation environment using GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning agents to iteratively train adaptive content delivery policies. By parallelizing agent-environment interactions across HPC nodes, we aim to model hyperparameter optimization for a novel decision engine that dynamically adjusts media encoding, asset prioritization, and fallback strategies while respecting WCAG 3.0 compliance constraints. Computational workflows will integrate browser engine emulation (via Headless Chromium clusters) with network condition synthetics, generating training datasets that reflect global connectivity disparities. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for stress-testing adaptive web interfaces under extreme concurrency scenarios, quantifiable metrics for trade-offs between computational resource expenditure and user experience consistency, and a generative model for predicting resource allocation thresholds in emerging immersive media formats like volumetric video. This work bridges gaps between information resource design, HPC-driven optimization, and inclusive web standards, offering methodologies to democratize high-quality multimedia access across diverse socioeconomic and technological contexts.
cip_title: Web Page, Digital/ Multimedia and Information Resources Design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply HTML, CSS, XML, JavaScript, graphics applications, and other authoring tools to the design, editing, and publishing (launching) of documents, images, graphics, sound, and multimedia products on the World Wide Web. Includes instruction in Internet theory, web page standards and policies, elements of web page design, user interfaces, vector tools, special effects, interactive and multimedia components, search engines, navigation, morphing, e-commerce tools, and emerging web technologies.

abstract: Epilepsy remains a significant neurological disorder, with approximately one-third of patients experiencing drug-resistant seizures. Surgical intervention can offer relief, yet outcomes depend critically on accurate localization of epileptogenic zones, which current diagnostic tools—including scalp EEG, MRI, and clinical semiology—often fail to resolve with sufficient precision. This project seeks to address this challenge by developing patient-specific computational models of seizure generation and propagation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multimodal neuroimaging, electrophysiological data, and biophysical neural network simulations. The core research problem centers on improving the spatial and temporal resolution of epileptogenic zone mapping to guide surgical planning and reduce post-operative recurrence. To achieve this, we will construct individualized brain models using structural MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and intracranial EEG (iEEG) data, incorporating neuron-glial interactions and network connectivity derived from empirical patient records. Large-scale simulations of seizure dynamics will be performed using parallelized implementations of coupled neural mass models and finite-element methods to account for tissue heterogeneity. Machine learning pipelines will analyze simulation outputs alongside clinical datasets to identify predictive biomarkers of seizure spread. The computational demands of these tasks—including the need for real-time parameter optimization, high-dimensional data processing, and ensemble modeling across heterogeneous cohorts—necessitate HPC resources for memory-intensive workloads and GPU-accelerated computation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for integrating multimodal data into dynamic seizure propagation models, (2) improved preoperative localization accuracy compared to current clinical standards, and (3) open-source tools for simulating patient-specific therapeutic interventions, such as virtual resections or neurostimulation protocols. By enabling precise mapping of epileptic networks, this work has the potential to directly enhance surgical outcomes, reduce invasive monitoring burdens, and provide a platform for in silico testing of novel antiepileptic therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of patients with epileptic seizures or with symptoms and signs whose differential diagnosis includes epileptic seizures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of cultural narratives within African-American and Black diaspora communities across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. The research addresses a critical gap in large-scale, comparative analyses of cultural production—such as oral histories, vernacular texts, and community archives—that reflect shared and divergent experiences of identity, resistance, and collective memory. Traditional methodologies struggle to process the volume and heterogeneity of these materials, which span three centuries and include digitized manuscripts, audio recordings, and visual media. By employing natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, this project will systematically analyze linguistic patterns, thematic shifts, and intertextual connections across regions and time periods. Key computational tasks include training custom transformer models to recognize dialectal variations in historical texts, clustering multimedia artifacts by semantic content, and mapping transnational influences in creative works. The scale of data—over 10TB of unstructured records from libraries, museums, and grassroots collections—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are only feasible via HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas visualizing cultural exchange networks and an open-source toolkit for ethically grounded computational analysis of diasporic materials. This work will provide scholars, educators, and community stakeholders with novel frameworks to interrogate how localized cultural practices have sustained transnational Black identities amid displacement and systemic marginalization. By centering computational rigor in cultural studies, the project aims to redefine interdisciplinary methodologies for studying the African diaspora while ensuring equitable access to digital resources for underrepresented narratives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: The increasing demand for competitive performance in motorsports requires innovative approaches to vehicle design and optimization, particularly in aerodynamics, powertrain efficiency, and structural durability. However, current computational workflows for simulating these systems are constrained by limited access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, restricting the fidelity and scale of models that can be practically analyzed. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging HPC to enable high-resolution simulations of complex, interacting systems in motorsports engineering. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) transient computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of aerodynamic interactions between vehicles in race conditions, (2) multi-physics simulations of hybrid powertrain thermal management under dynamic loads, and (3) topology optimization of lightweight chassis components using machine learning-augmented finite element analysis (FEA). These simulations will utilize open-source and commercial software (e.g., OpenFOAM, ANSYS, and Abaqus) adapted for parallel processing on GPU-accelerated clusters. Key challenges include managing large-scale datasets from real-world sensor inputs, resolving turbulent flow features at sub-millimeter scales, and optimizing coupled systems with conflicting performance objectives. The requested computing resources will allow parametric studies across race configurations, materials, and environmental conditions while maintaining computational feasibility. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting aerodynamic draft effects in pack racing, improved cooling system designs for electric vehicle components in endurance events, and generative algorithms for structurally efficient component geometries. This work will directly support student-led motorsports teams through access to advanced simulation capabilities while contributing methodological advances in multi-disciplinary design optimization. By bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical racing constraints, the project aims to establish a scalable computational framework for accelerating innovation in motorsports technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the evolutionary and functional dynamics of recombination rate variation across eukaryotic genomes, with a focus on identifying genetic and epigenetic factors that influence localized crossover frequency. Despite the central role of recombination in generating genetic diversity and ensuring proper chromosome segregation, the mechanisms underlying its striking variation within and between species remain poorly resolved. This project will employ population genetic simulations and comparative genomic analyses to model how sequence features, chromatin accessibility, and epigenetic modifications interact to shape recombination landscapes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for executing large-scale, stochastic simulations of evolving populations under varying selective pressures and recombination parameters. These simulations will integrate empirical data from model organisms to parameterize context-dependent recombination rates, enabling the exploration of evolutionary scenarios that cannot be tested experimentally. Key outcomes will include (1) a computational framework linking epigenetic states to recombination hotspot formation, (2) quantitative estimates of selection’s role in maintaining recombination rate variation, and (3) predictions about how chromatin architecture constrains crossover positioning over evolutionary timescales. The work will leverage parallelized algorithms to analyze genome-wide association datasets and simulate population-scale inheritance patterns across millions of generations. By clarifying how genetic and epigenetic systems jointly modulate recombination, this research will advance fundamental knowledge of genome evolution while providing insights into fertility-related disorders linked to aberrant crossover distributions. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at biologically relevant scales, overcoming current limitations in simulating complex interactions between nucleotide sequences, chromatin features, and population dynamics.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the organization, recombination, function, regulation, and transmission of heritable information in biological organisms at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in Mendelian genetics, mechanisms of gene regulation, chromosome structure and replication, epigenetic phenomena, DNA repair and recombination, sex determination, genetic interactions between genomes, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate dysregulated calcium (Ca²⁺) signaling dynamics in cancer cells, a critical yet poorly understood driver of tumor proliferation and metastasis. In solid tumors, aberrant Ca²⁺ flux disrupts intracellular communication, alters metabolic pathways, and promotes invasive behavior, but the systems-level integration of these processes remains elusive due to the spatial and temporal complexity of ion channel networks. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve the multiscale interactions between Ca²⁺-dependent signaling effectors, membrane transporters, and organelle-specific responses. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining stochastic modeling of ion channel clusters, deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems for cytosolic Ca²⁺ waves, and data-informed agent-based models (ABMs) of cellular decision-making under metabolic stress. The HPC environment will enable parallelized parameter sweeps across physiologically relevant ranges of channel densities, ATP gradients, and hypoxia profiles, integrated with single-cell RNA-seq datasets from patient-derived tumor models. Key deliverables include predictive maps of Ca²⁺ signaling thresholds that trigger epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in breast cancer cells and a publicly accessible simulation library for probing therapeutic perturbations. By quantifying how oncogenic mutations rewire Ca²⁺-dependent crosstalk between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial voltage-dependent anion channels (VDACs), this work will establish computational benchmarks for targeting metabolic vulnerabilities in therapy-resistant cancers. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations of 3D multicellular systems (>10⁵ cells) over biologically relevant timescales, addressing a critical gap in translating cell physiological insights into clinical oncology strategies. Outcomes will advance mechanistic understanding of microenvironment-driven cancer progression while providing scalable tools for simulating adaptive cell behaviors in heterogeneous tumors.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of physiological processes operating within and among cells, and intracellular communication and behavior, in the context of larger systems and whole organisms. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology, molecular physiology, cell cycle control, signal transduction, protein structure, membrane biochemistry and structure, ion channel physics, cell respiration and digestion, secretory functions, cell adhesion and communication, information encoding and decoding, and the relation of cell physiology to tissue, organ, and organismic functioning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing decentralized supply chain networks under dynamic risk constraints, leveraging quantum-inspired algorithms and agent-based modeling. Traditional supply chain optimization models often assume centralized decision-making or static risk profiles, limiting their applicability to modern, distributed ecosystems where geopolitical, environmental, and market risks evolve unpredictably. The research problem centers on addressing the computational complexity of modeling multi-agent negotiations, adaptive inventory routing, and real-time risk mitigation in large-scale networks—a challenge requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate stochastic scenarios and solve high-dimensional optimization problems. The computational approach integrates quantum annealing techniques with hybrid reinforcement learning to explore non-convex solution spaces efficiently, while agent-based simulations will emulate decentralized decision-making across 10,000+ nodes. HPC resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate risk propagation and validate resilience strategies under diverse perturbation regimes, including cascading disruptions and demand shocks. Expected outcomes include (1) a benchmark dataset of optimized network configurations for critical industries, (2) performance metrics comparing quantum-inspired solvers to classical optimization methods in dynamic settings, and (3) scalable protocols for balancing efficiency and robustness in cross-organizational supply chains. By advancing computational methods at the intersection of operations research and quantum computing, this work aims to establish new paradigms for resilient network design while providing open-source tools to bridge theoretical quantum advantage with practical supply chain applications. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated training of deep reinforcement learning agents, distributed memory computations for large-scale network simulations, and quantum circuit emulation to prototype hybrid algorithms.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the application of statistical modeling, data warehousing, data mining, programming, forecasting and operations research techniques to the analysis of problems of business organization and performance. Includes instruction in optimization theory and mathematical techniques, data mining, data warehousing, stochastic and dynamic modeling, operations analysis, and the design and testing of prototype systems and evaluation models.

abstract: Health education teachers require training that integrates evidence-based pedagogical strategies with the dynamic, context-sensitive demands of modern classrooms. However, existing teacher education programs often lack scalable tools to simulate diverse student populations, adaptive learning environments, and real-time decision-making scenarios. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to model health education classrooms, enabling the systematic study of instructional effectiveness across varied socio-cultural and cognitive contexts. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct agent-based simulations that replicate student-teacher interactions, peer dynamics, and the impact of health-related misinformation. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze how novice teachers adapt lesson delivery in response to simulated student feedback, with neural networks trained to predict optimal intervention strategies. Additionally, the project will generate synthetic datasets representing diverse demographic profiles to evaluate equity in pedagogical outcomes. Computational demands include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario variability testing, natural language processing of simulated dialogue, and large-scale parameter optimization for adaptive learning models. The outcomes will yield (1) a validated simulation platform for prototyping health education curricula, (2) actionable insights into competency gaps among pre-service teachers, and (3) open-source tools for personalized teacher training. By quantifying the relationship between instructional tactics and student engagement in controlled virtual environments, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in health teacher education while reducing reliance on resource-intensive in-person practicums. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the necessary scale, speed, and complexity for these simulations, which exceed the capabilities of local computing resources. This project bridges computational innovation and teacher preparation, directly supporting the development of educators equipped to address public health challenges in K–12 settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach health education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural dynamics of large-scale human behavioral networks in prehistoric settlement systems using advanced computational modeling. Anthropological research on ancient societies often faces challenges in reconstructing complex social interactions from fragmented archaeological data, particularly when analyzing regional settlement patterns over multi-century timescales. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to systematically evaluate how ecological constraints, resource distribution, and social exchange networks shaped community resilience and cultural transmission. Our research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate decision-making processes among Neolithic agricultural populations in understudied regions of Southwest Asia. The computational framework integrates paleoenvironmental datasets, archaeological site distributions, and ethnographic analogs to parameterize agent behaviors related to land use, mobility, and intergroup cooperation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for running ensemble simulations at population scales exceeding 10^4 autonomous agents across 500-year temporal sequences, with sensitivity analyses testing 27 ecological and social variables. Parallelized model iterations will quantify emergent properties of settlement clustering, trade network formation, and systemic responses to climate stressors. Expected outcomes include the identification of non-linear thresholds in carrying capacity dynamics and evidence for adaptive strategies that promoted long-term socio-ecological stability. Results will advance anthropological theories about collective action in pre-state societies while establishing a reusable computational workflow for analyzing sparse archaeological records through simulation-based hypothesis testing. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes will enable statistically robust exploration of parameter spaces that are computationally intractable on local workstations, directly supporting peer-reviewed publications and open-source model releases to the anthropological research community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Anthropology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and operational reliability of automated electromechanical systems, which are critical to modern manufacturing and industrial automation. A key challenge in electromechanical engineering technology lies in balancing real-time control performance with energy efficiency and mechanical durability, particularly in systems integrating servomechanical actuators, sensor networks, and programmable logic controllers (PLCs). Current analytical methods often oversimplify multiphysics interactions, leading to suboptimal prototypes that require costly iterative testing. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), dynamic system simulation, and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive maintenance algorithms. The computational workflow will model electromechanical coupling effects at unprecedented resolution, including thermal-structural deformation in servo motors, electromagnetic interference in control circuits, and wear patterns in mechanical linkages under variable loads. Parallelized simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers to analyze thousands of operational scenarios, while ML models trained on synthetic and experimental sensor data will predict failure modes and optimize maintenance schedules. This approach directly supports the program’s focus on prototype testing and systems analysis by enabling virtual validation of designs prior to physical fabrication. Anticipated outcomes include a validated library of multiphysics simulation templates for common electromechanical components, an open-source toolset for reliability-centered maintenance planning, and case studies demonstrating 30-50% reductions in prototype development cycles for industrial partners. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of coupled electromechanical simulations, which require teraflop-scale processing for parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses. By bridging the gap between theoretical models and practical implementation constraints, this work will advance both educational resources in engineering technology and industry adoption of data-driven electromechanical system design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Agricultural businesses face growing challenges in optimizing operational efficiency and resilience amid climate variability, market volatility, and supply chain disruptions. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to integrate high-resolution spatial, temporal, and economic datasets, limiting predictive accuracy for critical outcomes such as crop yield forecasting, resource allocation, and risk mitigation. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a scalable computational framework to model complex interactions between agronomic practices, environmental conditions, and market dynamics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating farm-level decision-making processes and supply chain networks across regional scales.
