These models will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including satellite-derived soil moisture indices, historical commodity pricing, and real-time logistics data, to evaluate adaptive strategies under scenarios of climatic stress and economic uncertainty. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify probabilistic outcomes for key performance indicators, such as profit margins and input-use efficiency, while machine learning pipelines will identify emergent patterns in system resilience. The computational workload necessitates large-scale memory and processing capabilities due to the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and iterative optimization requirements. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic risk assessment and a decision-support platform enabling stakeholders to test operational interventions in silico. By bridging gaps between agronomic data science and business analytics, this work aims to advance evidence-based management practices, enhance supply chain agility, and improve the long-term viability of agricultural enterprises in resource-constrained environments.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage agricultural businesses and agriculturally related operations within diversified corporations. Includes instruction in agriculture, agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, finance, marketing, planning, human resources management, and other managerial responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing personalized therapeutic recreation (TR) interventions targeting neurodevelopmental and chronic pain conditions. TR utilizes structured leisure activities to improve physical, cognitive, and psychosocial outcomes, yet current protocols rely on generalized guidelines with limited predictive power for individual response variability. The research problem centers on the lack of computational tools to analyze complex, multimodal datasets—including biometric wearables, patient-reported outcomes, and neurobehavioral assessments—that could dynamically tailor TR interventions. We propose a machine learning pipeline integrating temporal convolutional networks and graph neural networks to model nonlinear interactions between intervention parameters (activity type, duration, social context) and multidimensional health outcomes (motor function, emotional regulation, pain biomarkers). The computational approach will process high-dimensional datasets from a longitudinal cohort (n=450) undergoing TR protocols, incorporating federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy across collaborating clinical sites. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble models on heterogeneous data streams (sampled at 10-100Hz) and simulating intervention efficacy through agent-based modeling of virtual patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source platform for adaptive TR prescription, identification of latent biomarkers predictive of intervention success, and quantitative frameworks to personalize activity sequencing based on real-time physiological feedback. This work bridges health sciences and computational modeling to advance precision therapeutic recreation, offering novel methodologies for non-pharmacological intervention design while addressing scalability challenges in allied health research. Results will directly inform clinical guidelines for TR in underserved populations with complex comorbidities, enhancing accessibility to evidence-based, data-driven rehabilitation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, organize, and direct recreational activities designed to promote health and well-being for patients who are physically, mentally, or emotionally disabled. Includes instruction in the foundations of therapeutic recreation, leisure education and counseling, program planning, therapeutic recreational modalities, basic anatomy and physiology, psychology, medical terminology, human growth and development, patient observation and evaluation, special needs populations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Athletic injuries to the musculoskeletal system present complex biomechanical and physiological challenges, with prevention and rehabilitation strategies often limited by incomplete understanding of injury mechanisms across diverse populations. This project seeks to develop multiscale computational models integrating tissue-level biomechanics, athlete-specific motion patterns, and biological healing processes to predict injury risks and optimize rehabilitation protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process large datasets from wearable sensors, 3D motion capture, and medical imaging (MRI, ultrasound) of 500+ athletes, alongside mechanistic simulations of load distribution in bone, muscle, and connective tissues. Machine learning pipelines will analyze movement patterns associated with common injuries (e.g., ACL tears, rotator cuff strains), while finite element modeling will simulate tissue stress responses under dynamic sporting loads. A novel agent-based model will further explore cellular-level healing timelines post-injury, incorporating individual variability in inflammation markers and genetic profiles. The computational workflow demands parallel processing for real-time parameter optimization in athlete-specific models and probabilistic risk assessments across heterogeneous cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for injury susceptibility, validated against prospective clinical data from three collegiate sports programs, and personalized rehabilitation guidelines informed by simulated healing trajectories. This work directly addresses critical gaps in evidence-based injury prevention by quantifying interactions between biomechanical forces, biological recovery processes, and athlete-specific factors at unprecedented resolution. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for clinical researchers and partnerships with sports medicine providers to reduce reinjury rates and improve return-to-play decision-making.
cip_definition: Research on how to prevent and manage athletic injuries and to provide appropriate care for all structures of the musculoskeletal system directly affected by participation in sporting activity.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in construction project management and finishing quality through the development of advanced computational models that optimize resource allocation, material performance, and defect detection. Construction projects face persistent challenges, including delays from dynamic scheduling conflicts, suboptimal material curing conditions, and human error in manual inspections. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating machine learning (ML), finite element analysis (FEA), and real-time sensor data analytics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large datasets from IoT-enabled construction sites, including thermal, humidity, and stress data from embedded sensors, alongside imagery from drones and LiDAR systems. ML models will predict material curing times under variable environmental conditions, while FEA simulations will assess structural integrity of finishing materials under load scenarios. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize workforce and equipment scheduling under uncertainty. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing to handle 3D point clouds for automated defect detection, coupled with Monte Carlo simulations to quantify project risk. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for real-time decision support, reducing project overruns by 15–20% and minimizing material waste through precision curing protocols. The project will also generate open-access datasets of annotated construction defects and material performance metrics, advancing computational methodologies in a field traditionally reliant on empirical practices. By bridging gaps between construction management theory and data-driven automation, this work aims to establish scalable benchmarks for sustainable, high-quality building practices. The requested HPC resources will enable the iterative training of deep neural networks, large-scale parametric simulations, and the integration of heterogeneous data streams into a unified digital twin platform for construction lifecycle management.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) systems face complex challenges in optimizing prehospital care delivery, particularly during dynamic, high-acuity scenarios such as mass casualty incidents, disasters, or resource-constrained environments. Current approaches to EMS system design and medical oversight often rely on retrospective data analysis or simplified simulations, limiting their ability to model real-world operational complexity or predict emergent outcomes under stress. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate EMS operations at scale, integrating clinical, logistical, and environmental variables to inform evidence-based system improvements. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement agent-based modeling techniques to simulate multi-dimensional interactions between EMS providers, patients, transport networks, and healthcare facilities across urban and rural environments. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to historical EMS dispatch data, patient care records, and geospatial information systems (GIS) data to parameterize models and predict system performance under varying conditions. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of large-scale spatiotemporal datasets, real-time optimization of resource allocation during simulated crisis scenarios, and sensitivity analyses for wilderness EMS logistics. Expected outcomes include predictive models for EMS response time optimization under disaster conditions, quantitative frameworks for balancing clinical quality metrics with operational costs, and decision-support tools for medical directors evaluating protocol changes. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling rare but critical events, such as simultaneous multi-agency responses or cascading infrastructure failures during public health emergencies. By bridging clinical medicine with complex systems science, this work aims to advance EMS leadership capabilities in designing resilient care systems while maintaining rigorous standards for patient-centered outcomes. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation platforms to support quality improvement initiatives across emergency care networks.
cip_definition: Research focused on the leadership and medical oversight of pre- and out-of-hospital emergency care systems with advanced competencies in Emergency Medical System (EMS) system design, administration, and clinical care. Includes instruction in clinical aspects of EMS, medical oversight of EMS, mass casualty management, disaster planning and operations, wilderness EMS systems, and quality management and research.

abstract: Stratigraphic heterogeneity exerts a fundamental control on subsurface fluid flow, influencing energy resource distribution, aquifer dynamics, and carbon sequestration potential. However, existing models of sedimentary basin evolution often oversimplify the interplay of depositional processes, erosion, and post-depositional modification, limiting their predictive power. This project seeks to advance high-resolution 3D stratigraphic modeling by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate sediment transport, deposition, and diagenesis across scales relevant to basin analysis (10^2–10^5 years; 1 m–10 km spatial resolution). The research will employ a coupled modeling framework integrating process-based sediment transport algorithms (e.g., reduced-complexity cellular automata) with stochastic stratigraphic realizations conditioned by field-derived datasets from fluvial-deltaic systems. Key computational challenges include resolving multi-phase grain interactions during deposition, simulating differential compaction and cementation patterns, and quantifying uncertainty in paleoenvironmental reconstructions. The HPC workflow will utilize parallelized finite-volume solvers and machine learning emulators to accelerate ensemble runs exploring parameter space sensitivity. Anticipated outcomes include (1) novel metrics for quantifying stratigraphic connectivity and reservoir heterogeneity, (2) a publicly accessible database of synthetic stratigraphic architectures tied to depositional scenarios, and (3) improved inverse modeling workflows to reduce uncertainty in subsurface predictions. This work directly addresses critical gaps in sedimentological process representation, with applications to hydrocarbon exploration, CO₂ storage site characterization, and groundwater resource management. The requested computing resources will enable petascale simulations necessary to capture the non-linear feedbacks between sedimentation dynamics and preserved stratigraphic records, advancing predictive capabilities in basin analysis and subsurface resource evaluation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of sedimentary rocks and the processes that shaped the surface of the Earth and how those processes have interacted to control the Earth system.

abstract: The proposed research project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing public service delivery by leveraging advanced computational modeling to simulate the impacts of policy interventions on complex administrative systems. Public administrators increasingly face dynamic, interconnected challenges—such as budget constraints, shifting demographics, and evolving equity requirements—that demand data-driven decision-making. However, existing analytical tools often lack the capacity to model large-scale, multi-agent interactions or predict long-term systemic outcomes under uncertainty. This project will develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate public administration scenarios, integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and geospatial analytics. The computational approach will focus on two case studies: (1) simulating the effects of alternative funding allocation strategies on municipal healthcare access and (2) modeling workforce distribution patterns in state-level emergency management agencies during crisis events. By processing terabyte-scale datasets—including historical policy records, real-time service utilization metrics, and demographic microdata—the models will identify leverage points for improving operational efficiency while maintaining equity goals. The HPC environment is essential for running parallelized simulations across thousands of policy permutations, enabling probabilistic risk assessments and sensitivity analyses that account for nonlinear system behaviors. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario-based policy testing and peer-reviewed insights into computational public administration methodologies. This work will provide actionable guidance for resource prioritization in government agencies while advancing the adoption of HPC resources in non-traditional, social service-oriented research domains. The project team will collaborate with three state-level public administration partners to validate models against real-world policy implementation data, ensuring practical relevance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as managers in the executive arm of local, state, and federal government and that focuses on the systematic study of executive organization and management. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern irrigation systems by developing a high-resolution computational framework to optimize water delivery in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes. Current irrigation management practices often rely on static schedules or coarse sensor networks, leading to overwatering, soil salinization, and energy waste. While precision agriculture technologies show promise, their adoption is limited by computational constraints in handling spatial-temporal variability across large farms. We propose to create a scalable simulation platform integrating soil moisture dynamics, crop water demand models, and hydraulic network analysis to dynamically allocate water resources. The research will employ parallelized finite element methods to solve 3D Richards’ equations governing water transport in unsaturated soils, coupled with machine learning surrogates trained on multi-spectral satellite data and IoT sensor inputs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve sub-meter hydrological processes across entire irrigation districts while maintaining real-time decision-making capabilities. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool for pressure-regulated drip system optimization and adaptive scheduling algorithms that reduce water use by 15-30% compared to conventional practices. The computational framework will be validated using field data from partner farms in arid regions, with particular focus on cotton and citrus production systems. By enabling fine-grained control of irrigation infrastructure, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical water-saving strategies and practical implementation, directly supporting workforce training in irrigation technology through case studies integrated into the academic program curriculum. The proposed HPC allocations will accelerate parameter sensitivity analyses and uncertainty quantification critical for robust system design under climate variability.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in the field of agricultural technology and irrigation. Includes instruction in irrigation and drainage methodologies, pumping and delivery systems, system design and evaluation, and principles of installation and repair of irrigation systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of regional German dialect variation and its historical evolution. While German dialectology has long relied on manual transcription and qualitative methods, the increasing digitization of historical texts, speech corpora, and ethnographic records presents an opportunity to systematically analyze linguistic shifts across time and geography at unprecedented scale. The primary challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, unstructured data—including scanned manuscripts, audio recordings, and modern social media—to identify phonetic, syntactic, and lexical patterns that correlate with documented sociohistorical trends. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational pipeline integrating optical character recognition (OCR) correction for historical prints, dialect-specific speech-to-text alignment for audio archives, and transformer-based language models fine-tuned on regional corpora. These workflows require significant parallel processing capabilities due to the volume of data (over 10 TB of text and audio) and the iterative nature of training domain-specific neural models. HPC resources will enable large-scale comparative analyses, such as tracing the decline of Low German features in 19th-century urban centers or mapping the adoption of technolectal borrowings in contemporary Austrian scientific discourse. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access repository of computationally enhanced dialect corpora spanning 1800–2020; (2) quantifiable models of language contact phenomena informed by socioeconomic metadata; and (3) methodological frameworks for diachronic dialectometry applicable to other under-resourced languages. By bridging traditional philological research with NLP innovation, this project aims to transform how linguistic diversity is studied within German studies while providing actionable insights for language preservation initiatives.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the German language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the computational modeling of vernacular architectural morphologies and their adaptive responses to socio-cultural and environmental dynamics, a niche area bridging architectural theory, cultural analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC). While contemporary architectural research often prioritizes engineering-driven simulations, this study focuses on non-mechanistic, community-driven design processes documented in understudied vernacular traditions. The research problem centers on decoding how intangible cultural practices—such as ritual land-use patterns or collective memory—interact with material constraints to shape evolving architectural forms. Current analytical methods lack the capacity to process heterogeneous qualitative data (oral histories, ethnographic records, spatial layouts) alongside environmental variables at scale, necessitating novel computational frameworks. The project will develop agent-based models simulating decision-making processes in vernacular settlements, integrating graph neural networks to analyze relational patterns between cultural narratives and built structures. High-performance computing resources are critical for training models on multimodal datasets spanning centuries of architectural adaptation across six case study regions, as well as running iterative spatial simulations with probabilistic cultural-environmental parameters. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit to quantify cultural resilience in architectural systems, offering architects and policymakers evidence-based strategies for culturally grounded adaptive reuse. By situating HPC within a humanistic architectural context, this work challenges dominant technocentric paradigms while advancing methodological synergies between computational social science and design research. The resulting models will be disseminated as open-access resources to support global heritage conservation and participatory design practices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture and related programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of pharmacotherapeutic interventions demands advanced computational tools to optimize drug efficacy, safety, and personalization. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting individual patient responses to high-risk medications, particularly in populations with comorbidities or genetic polymorphisms affecting drug metabolism. Current pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models often fail to integrate multi-omics data, real-world evidence, and dynamic physiological variables at scale, limiting their clinical utility. To overcome this, we propose the development of a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate drug behavior across molecular, cellular, and organ-level systems. The framework will incorporate machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, genomic profiles, and high-resolution molecular dynamics simulations of drug-target interactions. Key computational challenges include parallelized optimization of differential equation systems for population PK/PD modeling, GPU-accelerated molecular docking studies for variant-specific enzyme kinetics, and federated learning approaches to preserve patient privacy during model training. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative refinement of models through feedback loops between in silico predictions and experimental validation via partner laboratories. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dose individualization of anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, and oncolytics, with validated reductions in adverse event risks in pilot clinical cohorts. By bridging mechanistic pharmacology and data-driven clinical decision support, this work aims to establish a scalable computational pipeline for precision pharmacotherapy, directly addressing the National Institutes of Health’s priorities for reducing trial-and-error prescribing. The requested resources will support GPU node allocations for deep learning tasks, high-memory nodes for genomic association studies, and secure data storage for sensitive patient datasets, enabling transformative advances in evidence-based medication optimization.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pharmacotherapy

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize administrative workflows in hospital patient care units, addressing inefficiencies in resource allocation, staff scheduling, and patient flow coordination. Health Unit Coordinators (HUCs) manage dynamic, high-stakes tasks such as transcribing orders, scheduling procedures, and monitoring personnel, yet existing tools often rely on static protocols that do not adapt to real-time demands. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-variable workflows, simulate operational scenarios, and identify bottlenecks using agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation. Patient admission patterns, staff availability, and equipment utilization data from electronic health records will inform these models. Machine learning algorithms will then predict high-risk periods for workflow delays and recommend adaptive scheduling interventions. The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing to automate the extraction of actionable tasks from unstructured clinical orders, reducing transcription errors. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, the project will evaluate thousands of operational permutations to derive optimal staffing and resource allocation strategies under diverse constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating unit-specific workflows, predictive dashboards for HUCs, and evidence-based guidelines for balancing administrative workloads. This work aims to reduce delays in care delivery, improve coordination accuracy, and provide training modules for HUC students using scenario-based simulations. The scalability of HPC-enabled models will support broader applications in healthcare operations research, directly aligning with the program’s goal of equipping professionals with data-driven decision-making skills in complex care environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern railway systems demands advanced computational tools to optimize operational efficiency, safety, and infrastructure resilience. This project seeks to address critical challenges in railroad transportation—such as real-time traffic management, predictive maintenance of track networks, and risk mitigation for hazardous material transport—through the development of high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation and machine learning frameworks. Current approaches often rely on static models or simplified heuristics, which fail to capture the dynamic interactions between trains, infrastructure, environmental conditions, and human operators at scale. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-faceted computational strategy. First, large-scale agent-based simulations will model rail traffic under variable scenarios (e.g., weather disruptions, track failures) using parallelized computing to resolve micro-level interactions across continental-scale networks. Second, graph neural networks will be trained on historical maintenance records and sensor data to predict localized track degradation, requiring GPU-accelerated processing of terabyte-scale datasets. Third, probabilistic risk analysis frameworks will evaluate hazardous material routing strategies under uncertainty, leveraging Monte Carlo methods to quantify low-probability, high-consequence events. These efforts depend on HPC resources to achieve the necessary computational throughput, particularly for time-sensitive operational decision support. Expected outcomes include validated models for reducing network-wide delays by 15–20%, identifying at-risk infrastructure components weeks in advance of failures, and optimizing safety protocols for hazardous shipments. The project will also generate open-source tools to help railway operators transition from legacy systems to data-driven management practices. By integrating domain-specific railway operational constraints with cutting-edge computational methods, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for scalable, adaptive railway system optimization, directly supporting the transportation industry’s goals of reliability, safety, and sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the safety and diagnostic accuracy of multi-modal medical imaging through advanced computational modeling and optimization. Current clinical imaging protocols for x-ray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and ultrasound systems rely on generalized parameters that may not account for patient-specific anatomical variability or optimize the trade-offs between image quality and radiation dose (for ionizing modalities). To address this, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate and optimize imaging parameters across these modalities. The research will focus on three aims: (1) creating patient-specific digital phantoms using generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on anonymized clinical CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets; (2) implementing Monte Carlo simulations for x-ray/gamma-ray transport and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) models for ultrasound and MRI field interactions; and (3) deploying deep reinforcement learning algorithms to identify optimal imaging protocols that minimize radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic utility. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallel processing to manage stochastic simulations across diverse anatomical models and imaging scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated protocol optimization pipelines capable of reducing patient dose by 20-40% in radiographic exams without compromising diagnostic value, along with open-source tools for simulating hybrid imaging systems. This work directly supports radiation safety advancements in diagnostic radiology and provides a foundation for personalized imaging approaches. The scale of data processing (>1 PB of simulated imaging studies) and complexity of coupled physical models necessitate access to HPC resources with GPU-accelerated nodes, high-memory capacity, and parallel file systems to achieve clinically relevant turnaround times for protocol validation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnostic applications of x-rays, gamma rays from sealed sources, ultrasonic radiation, and magnetic resonance; and in the use of equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nuclear reactor material degradation under extreme operational conditions through advanced computational modeling. Nuclear power plants rely on structural materials subjected to intense radiation, thermal stress, and corrosive environments, which lead to embrittlement, swelling, and reduced lifespan. Current experimental methods to study these phenomena are limited by cost, time, and the inability to probe atomic-scale mechanisms in real time. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven multiscale simulation framework integrating quantum mechanical calculations, molecular dynamics, and continuum-scale finite element analysis. The research will model radiation damage cascades in reactor-grade steels, zirconium alloys, and advanced accident-tolerant fuel cladding materials, capturing defect evolution and mechanical property changes across spatial and temporal scales. Large-scale parallelized simulations will quantify the synergistic effects of neutron irradiation, hydrogen embrittlement, and thermal cycling on microstructural stability. Machine learning interatomic potentials will be trained on ab initio datasets to balance accuracy and computational efficiency for defect migration energetics. The HPC workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated codes (e.g., LAMMPS, DAMASK) to simulate representative volume elements containing millions of atoms over nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive models for material failure thresholds, validated against experimental irradiation data from collaborating national laboratories. These results will directly inform safety margins, maintenance schedules, and the development of radiation-resistant alloys for next-generation reactors. By enabling atomic-to-macro property linkages, this work bridges a critical gap in nuclear materials science while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in accelerating the design cycle for nuclear energy systems. The requested computing resources will support over 500,000 node-hours of simulations, generating datasets to advance both academic understanding and industrial applications of nuclear technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of research scientists and operating engineers engaged in the running of nuclear reactors, and in nuclear materials processing and disposal. Includes instruction in basic nuclear physics and nuclear engineering, monitoring and safety procedures, radioactive materials handling and disposal, equipment maintenance and operation, and record keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision and sustainability in cabinetmaking and millwork through computational modeling of wood machining processes. The research addresses a critical gap in the field: the lack of high-fidelity simulations to predict tool wear, material deformation, and energy consumption during complex woodworking operations. Traditional trial-and-error approaches for optimizing feed rates, spindle speeds, and tool geometries remain costly and time-intensive, particularly for rare wood species or composite materials. We propose developing a multiscale simulation framework leveraging finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element methods (DEM) to model interactions between cutting tools and anisotropic wood substrates at microstructural levels. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the transient thermal-mechanical coupling inherent to high-speed milling and routing processes, which involve localized stresses exceeding 100 MPa and temperatures surpassing 200°C. The computational workflow will integrate material property databases for 15+ wood species, calibrated through experimental machining trials conducted with industry partners. Machine learning techniques will then map simulation outputs to operational parameters that minimize waste while maintaining dimensional tolerances specified in architectural millwork standards. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models that reduce material scrap by 18-25% in complex joinery operations and extend tool life through wear-adaptive machining strategies. By enabling first-principles optimization of fabrication workflows, this research will directly support sustainable manufacturing practices in woodworking industries while providing students with hands-on experience in computational design-to-production pipelines. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will lower barriers to digital innovation for small-scale cabinetmaking enterprises, aligning with broader workforce development goals in advanced manufacturing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate and repair industrial woodworking machinery, and to use such machinery to design and fabricate wooden components and complete articles.

abstract: In contemporary healthcare, optimizing medication systems is critical to enhancing patient safety and operational efficiency. However, the complexity of clinical workflows, variability in patient responses, and the sheer volume of pharmacological data pose significant challenges. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the dynamic interactions within medication systems, necessitating advanced computational approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale simulation models and machine learning algorithms that analyze electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time sensor inputs. The computational framework will integrate discrete-event simulation to model hospital-wide medication workflows, agent-based modeling to evaluate individual patient-clinician interactions, and deep neural networks to predict adverse drug reactions and optimal dosing regimens. By processing terabytes of heterogeneous data across parallelized environments, these models will identify systemic inefficiencies, predict risk scenarios, and generate personalized treatment recommendations. The HPC infrastructure is essential to accommodate the iterative nature of model training, the stochasticity inherent in simulation-based optimization, and the need for real-time analytics in critical care settings. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for reducing medication errors by 20–30%, decreasing hospital readmission rates through precision dosing, and informing policy updates on medication management protocols. This research will provide a scalable computational foundation for transforming medication systems into adaptive, patient-centered networks, ultimately advancing clinical outcomes and healthcare sustainability.
cip_definition: Research focused on Medication Systems and Operations

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for high-dimensional statistical inference under complex dependency structures, a core challenge in modern probability and mathematical statistics. Traditional approaches to Bayesian hierarchical modeling, stochastic process simulation, and resampling-based inference face prohibitive computational demands when applied to high-dimensional parameter spaces or dependent data regimes such as spatially indexed time series. We propose to address these limitations through three interconnected thrusts: (1) Designing adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms with dimension-independent convergence rates for Banach space-valued parameters, leveraging theoretical advances in Gaussian process priors and operator-valued kernels; (2) Developing distributed resampling frameworks for dependent particle systems that maintain statistical consistency while exploiting GPU-accelerated parallelization; (3) Implementing rigorous numerical studies of infinite-dimensional stochastic process approximations, including measure-valued martingales and interacting particle systems, to characterize finite-sample performance. The computational workload involves large-scale simulations of multivariate time series (n > 10⁶ observations), iterative optimization over parameter spaces with O(10⁴) dimensions, and comparative benchmarking of asymptotic versus finite-sample properties under non-standard dependence. High-performance computing resources are essential for managing memory-intensive linear algebra operations on structured covariance matrices, parallel tempering across MCMC chains, and validation against empirical datasets from spatial epidemiology. Expected outcomes include new theoretical guarantees for scalable nonparametric inference, open-source software implementing provably convergent algorithms, and methodological advances in quantifying uncertainty for high-dimensional decision processes. This work directly addresses foundational gaps in statistical computing while maintaining rigorous mathematical grounding in measure-theoretic probability and functional analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical theory underlying statistical methods and their use. Includes instruction in probability theory parametric and non-parametric inference, sequential analysis, multivariate analysis, Bayesian analysis, experimental design, time series analysis, resampling, robust statistics, limit theory, infinite particle systems, stochastic processes, martingales, Markov processes, and Banach spaces.

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) plays a critical role in preventing neurological injury during high-risk surgeries, yet current systems face challenges in processing complex, multimodal neural data in real time with sufficient accuracy. This project seeks to address the computational limitations of existing IONM workflows by developing a machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) to enhance the speed and precision of neural signal interpretation. The research focuses on integrating electrocorticography (ECoG), electromyography (EMG), and somatosensory evoked potential (SSEP) data streams into a unified predictive model capable of identifying early signs of neurological compromise during spinal and cranial procedures. Current methods rely on threshold-based alerts and manual interpretation, which introduce delays and variability, particularly in surgeries involving pediatric or anatomically atypical patients. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a hybrid computational architecture combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction from ECoG/SSEP waveforms and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model temporal dependencies in EMG signals. The framework will be trained on a curated dataset of over 10,000 anonymized surgical cases, including rare events such as ischemic cord compression and cranial nerve irritation, which are underrepresented in conventional datasets. HPC resources will enable parallelized hyperparameter optimization, real-time simulation of signal degradation scenarios, and validation against intraoperative video recordings to correlate model predictions with surgical maneuvers. Expected outcomes include a deployable inference pipeline capable of operating within the subsecond latency constraints of surgical environments, reducing false-positive alarm rates by an estimated 40-60% compared to existing systems. The project will also generate open-source tools for neuromonitoring signal preprocessing and synthetic data generation to support broader research in surgical neurodynamics. By bridging gaps in computational neurology and real-time clinical decision support, this work aims to establish a new standard for adaptive intraoperative risk mitigation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the development of advanced biomedical technologies through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of complex biological systems and medical device interactions. Current limitations in computational power restrict the resolution and scale of models used to optimize implantable devices, biosensors, and therapeutic delivery systems, often leading to oversimplified assumptions about dynamic biological environments. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging HPC resources to execute multi-scale simulations integrating molecular dynamics, finite element analysis, and fluid-structure interaction modeling. These methods will enable real-time analysis of biomechanical stress distributions in cardiovascular stents, protein-ligand binding kinetics for targeted drug delivery nanoparticles, and hemodynamic patterns in artificial organ prototypes. A key innovation involves coupling machine learning algorithms with physics-based models to predict long-term biocompatibility and failure modes of biomedical devices under physiological conditions. The computational workflows will utilize parallelized codebases optimized for GPU-accelerated nodes, enabling parameter sweeps across design variations and biological variability. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal material configurations for neural interface electrodes, validated predictive models of inflammatory responses to synthetic implants, and data-driven protocols for calibrating biosensor arrays. By bridging high-fidelity simulations with experimental validation, this work will accelerate the translation of robust biomedical technologies into clinical applications while reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping. The resulting open-source computational tools and datasets will provide the broader research community with frameworks to advance personalized medical device development and precision therapeutic systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of political disinformation spread across social media platforms and its interaction with traditional media ecosystems during election cycles. The rise of computationally sophisticated disinformation campaigns—which leverage AI-generated content, microtargeting, and cross-platform coordination—presents novel challenges for understanding how false narratives emerge, evolve, and influence public opinion. Existing studies often lack the scale and temporal resolution to model these phenomena holistically, particularly in multilingual and cross-media contexts. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods computational framework combining large-scale social media data ingestion (X/Twitter, Facebook, Telegram), broadcast media transcripts, and longitudinal polling data. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will classify disinformation narratives and track their mutation across platforms using transformer-based models fine-tuned for political discourse. Temporal network analysis will map coordination patterns among accounts and media outlets, while agent-based modeling will simulate information diffusion under varying platform moderation scenarios. The scale of analysis—spanning 10TB of multimodal data across six election contexts—necessitates high-performance computing resources for distributed data processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available benchmark dataset of annotated disinformation clusters, 2) computational models quantifying the cross-platform amplification of false narratives, and 3) evidence-based recommendations for real-time monitoring systems to be used by journalists and fact-checking organizations. By elucidating the interplay between algorithmic content distribution and human information processing, this work aims to advance theoretical frameworks in political communication while providing actionable tools to mitigate electoral interference. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impractical on standard infrastructure, particularly for transformer inference on multilingual text and dynamic network analysis at sub-hourly resolutions.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human and media communication in the political process and that prepares individuals to function as members of political and public affairs organizations, political campaign staffs, and related government and media entities. Includes instruction in media effects, political speaking and debating, political advertising and marketing, image management, political journalism, opinion polling, and aspects of print and broadcast media related to the production and distribution of media messages in political settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex decision-making challenges in dynamic business environments, with a focus on optimizing organizational resilience under uncertainty. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the interdependencies and nonlinear feedback inherent in large-scale business systems, particularly when modeling disruptions such as supply chain failures, market volatility, or regulatory shifts. The proposed study will develop and validate agent-based simulation models integrated with machine learning techniques to analyze multi-stakeholder decision pathways, resource allocation trade-offs, and adaptive strategy formulation. Computational workflows will process real-world datasets spanning operational metrics, market signals, and macroeconomic indicators, requiring parallel processing capabilities to manage stochastic simulations across thousands of scenario permutations. Key methodological components include Monte Carlo methods for risk propagation analysis, graph neural networks to model interorganizational dependencies, and evolutionary algorithms for adaptive strategy optimization. The HPC infrastructure is critical for maintaining computational feasibility given the project's scale: baseline models anticipate 50,000+ concurrent agent interactions per simulation epoch, with sensitivity analyses requiring 100+ parameter combinations across 12-month forecast horizons. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying resilience thresholds in enterprise operations, decision support tools for resource reallocation during crises, and benchmarks for operational flexibility across industries. Results will advance academic understanding of complexity-aware strategic management while providing practitioners with empirically validated models to balance efficiency and robustness in capital allocation. This work directly addresses gaps in computational business analytics by enabling high-dimensional scenario testing impractical on conventional systems, with particular relevance to post-pandemic recovery planning and climate-related operational risk mitigation.
cip_title: Business Administration, Management and Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance interdisciplinary research in Scandinavian cultural and gender studies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale textual and visual datasets spanning Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Iceland, and Greenland from the 19th century to the present. The core research problem centers on identifying and mapping underrepresented cultural narratives—particularly those related to gender, indigeneity, and regional identity—within digitized archives of Scandinavian folklore, literature, and visual art. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically trace subtle thematic patterns across these vast, multilingual corpora, which include over 500,000 pages of texts and 20,000 images. To address this, we propose a computational workflow combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of textual sources, computer vision techniques for iconographic classification in visual materials, and graph neural networks to model cultural transmission networks. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models on historical Scandinavian languages (e.g., Old Norse, Sami variants) and processing high-resolution archival images. Expected outcomes include 1) quantitative frameworks for tracking the evolution of gender representations in Nordic cultural production, 2) geotemporal visualizations of narrative diffusion across Scandinavia’s borderlands, and 3) open-access tools for analyzing low-resource North Germanic languages. By bridging computational methods with humanities-driven inquiry, this work aims to reveal previously obscured intersections between regional identity formation and marginalized voices in Scandinavian cultural history. The results will directly support ongoing collaborations with Nordic cultural institutions and Indigenous Sami researchers, while the computational pipelines developed will serve as a model for resource-constrained language analysis in area studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Scandinavia, defined as Northern Europe including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and related island groups (e.g., Greenland) and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay of family relational patterns and mental health outcomes in systemic therapy contexts. Despite growing evidence that family interactions significantly influence individual well-being, computational tools capable of capturing the non-linear, time-dependent complexities of relational behaviors remain underdeveloped. Traditional statistical methods often fail to account for the high-dimensional, interdependent variables inherent in family systems, such as communication styles, emotional reciprocity, and cultural or generational influences. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to simulate and predict how micro-level relational shifts—identified in therapy sessions—propagate through family networks to affect mental health trajectories. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with natural language processing (NLP) to analyze longitudinal therapy session transcripts, behavioral surveys, and biometric data (e.g., wearable device outputs). Machine learning algorithms will be trained on anonymized datasets from diverse family structures to identify critical inflection points in therapeutic progress, while graph neural networks will map relational dependencies. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing simulations of large family networks (n > 1,000 synthetic cohorts) and optimizing hyperparameters in real-time feedback loops. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for identifying families at risk of poor therapeutic outcomes due to entrenched relational patterns, (2) a generative AI tool to assist clinicians in tailoring interventions based on simulated system-wide responses, and (3) open-source code for replicating the framework in other systemic therapy contexts. By bridging computational science and relational health, this work aims to advance precision approaches in marriage and family therapy while establishing scalable methodologies for studying complex interpersonal systems in mental health care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of marriage and family therapy, involving the diagnosis of cognitive, affective, and behavioral domain disorders, both mental and emotional, within the context of marriage and family systems and the application of short- and long-term therapeutic strategies in family group contexts. Includes instruction in psychotherapy, family systems and studies, small group intervention and therapy, marital problems, depression, identification of psychopathologies and behavioral disorders, holistic health care, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Nuclear radiology faces critical challenges in optimizing diagnostic accuracy through quantitative analysis of radionuclide imaging and biodistribution data. Current clinical workflows rely on static, low-resolution imaging protocols and simplified pharmacokinetic models, which inadequately capture dynamic biological processes and spatial heterogeneity in disease states. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to integrate dynamic positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) data with patient-specific physiological models. The primary research problem centers on improving the spatiotemporal resolution of functional imaging while reducing radiation exposure, enabling earlier and more precise diagnosis of oncological and neurodegenerative diseases. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) parallelized reconstruction of time-resolved tomographic data using iterative algorithms optimized for GPU acceleration, (2) development of a multiscale biodistribution model incorporating vascular dynamics, tissue permeability, and receptor binding kinetics, and (3) machine learning-driven synthesis of imaging biomarkers with electronic health record data for predictive analytics. These methods require HPC resources due to the need for rapid processing of 4D imaging datasets (>1 TB/study), Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport through heterogeneous tissues, and training of deep neural networks on multi-institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for sub-millimeter resolution dynamic PET/SPECT reconstruction, open-source tools for personalized dosimetry calculations, and predictive models linking radionuclide uptake patterns to molecular biomarkers. This work will directly enhance clinical decision-making in radionuclide therapy planning while establishing computational infrastructure for future research in theranostic applications. The requested computing resources will enable processing times compatible with clinical workflows while maintaining rigorous reproducibility standards for translational research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: The emergence and spread of infectious diseases at the human-animal-environment interface present complex challenges to global health, requiring advanced predictive tools to inform preventive strategies. This project addresses critical gaps in understanding the dynamics of zoonotic pathogen transmission within livestock populations and their spillover risks to humans, with a focus on highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in poultry systems. Current epidemiological models often lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale data—including genomic, environmental, and husbandry factors—that drive transmission heterogeneity. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. This framework will synthesize individual animal movement data, viral genomic sequences, and spatially explicit environmental variables (e.g., land use, climate) to simulate transmission pathways under diverse agricultural practices. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify genomic signatures associated with host adaptation and antiviral resistance in influenza strains using whole-genome sequencing data from poultry and wild bird reservoirs. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing of 10,000+ simulated outbreak scenarios with varying intervention parameters (e.g., vaccination thresholds, culling radii) and Bayesian phylogenetic analyses of 50,000+ viral genomes. HPC resources will enable parameter optimization through Monte Carlo methods and real-time integration of surveillance data streams. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of HPAI outbreak risk, evidence-based recommendations for biosecurity protocols, and a publicly accessible genomic surveillance dashboard. This work will directly enhance veterinary public health capacity to preempt zoonotic threats while demonstrating scalable computational methods for One Health research. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of storage will support these computationally intensive tasks, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: Research focused on the investigation of and intervention in health and disease problems of animal and related human communities, comparative medicine, and animal public health. May included related research in biostatistics, epidemiology, environmental control, toxicology and the planning and administration of animal health programs and services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the cascading impacts of emerging technologies on strategic stability in multipolar security environments. As AI, autonomous systems, and dual-use biotechnology accelerate, their unpredictable integration into national security ecosystems creates novel risks that traditional policy frameworks struggle to anticipate. The core research problem centers on simulating how rapid technological diffusion interacts with adversarial decision-making cycles, alliance commitments, and escalatory dynamics. Using a mixed-methods approach, the computational framework integrates three components: (1) agent-based modeling of state and non-state actors’ adaptive responses to disruptive technologies, calibrated via historical case studies of technological shocks (e.g., nuclear proliferation, cyber warfare emergence); (2) natural language processing (NLP) of cross-national policy documents and technical literature to identify latent dependencies between technological capabilities and perceived strategic vulnerabilities; and (3) dynamic network analysis to map how asymmetric technological advantages reshape alliance structures and deterrence postures under crisis conditions. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale of concurrent simulations (10,000+ parameterized scenarios), processing multilingual unstructured data, and optimizing neural networks that predict tipping points in stability metrics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers to stress-test proposed technology governance frameworks, alongside peer-reviewed insights into mitigating arms-race dynamics in AI and biotechnology domains. By quantifying second-order effects of technological disruption on deterrence logics and conflict pathways, this work aims to establish a new evidence base for aligning national security strategies with the velocity of 21st-century innovation.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and application of intelligence, diplomacy, military power, and related tools of statecraft to national defense policy formulation and power projection. Includes instruction in history, political theory, public policy analysis, civil-military relations, military and defense studies, homeland security, leadership, threat scenarios, regional and local issues, alliance and coalition issues, defense budgeting and economics, intelligence, and strategy.

abstract: The diagnosis of complex pathologies in veterinary medicine relies heavily on the integration of histopathological, molecular, and clinical data. Current workflows for analyzing diseased animal tissues face challenges in scalability, reproducibility, and quantitative precision, particularly when handling large-scale datasets from digital histopathology, genomic sequencing, or multiplex imaging. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational pathology pipeline optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The research will focus on automating the detection and classification of histomorphometric features in veterinary cancers and inflammatory diseases using deep learning models trained on whole-slide imaging (WSI) datasets. A secondary aim involves integrating spatially resolved transcriptomic data with histopathology findings to identify microenvironmental biomarkers of disease progression. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated image analysis frameworks (e.g., MONAI, PyTorch) for WSI processing and graph neural networks to model tissue-omics interactions. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte slide repositories, hyperparameter optimization for complex neural architectures, and genome-scale variant analysis. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for standardized lesion quantification in common veterinary species, open-source tools for multimodal data integration, and predictive models linking tissue-level patterns to clinical outcomes. By enhancing analytical throughput and precision, this work will directly inform diagnostic protocol improvements, therapeutic target discovery, and comparative disease modeling across species. The requested computing infrastructure is critical to manage memory-intensive analyses that exceed the capacity of local workstations, ensuring statistically robust validation across diverse case cohorts. Results will advance computational pathology capabilities in veterinary medicine while contributing reusable frameworks for biomedical machine learning applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of diseased animal tissues and anatomic abnormalities. May included related research in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management and quality control.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of coupled hydro-mechanical processes in contaminated soil systems, with a focus on improving the stability and environmental performance of waste containment structures. The research addresses critical gaps in understanding how dynamic loading events, such as earthquakes or cyclic waste settlement, interact with geochemical degradation processes to compromise landfill liners and subsurface barriers. Current analytical models oversimplify the interplay between soil deformation, fluid flow, and contaminant transport, particularly under time-varying boundary conditions. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a parallelized finite element framework integrating three-dimensional elastoplastic soil behavior, transient multiphase flow, and reactive solute transport. High-resolution simulations will capture microstructural changes in engineered clay-geosynthetic composites during cyclic wet-dry and load-unload scenarios, informed by experimental datasets on material properties under extreme environmental conditions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter calibration and uncertainty quantification across heterogeneous soil profiles. The computational workflow will be validated against field monitoring data from instrumented landfill sites and scaled to assess regional-scale impacts of proposed waste containment designs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing barrier system resilience against climate-induced hydraulic gradients and seismic hazards, directly supporting sustainable infrastructure design. By enabling previously intractable simulations of long-term geoenvironmental system performance, this work will provide novel insights into failure mechanisms at the soil-contaminant interface, informing regulatory guidelines and risk mitigation strategies for contaminated land management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply geotechnical engineering methods, which deal with the analysis, design and construction of earth and earth supported structures, to the application of environmental problems, such as waste containment, waste disposal, construction of land fills, soil permeation, soil analysis, and soil improvement. Includes instruction in soil mechanics, soil dynamics, soil behavior, waste management and containment systems, geosynthetics, geochemistry, earth structures, geoenvironmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, and foundation engineering

abstract: The proposed research seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the documentation, analysis, and revitalization of the Hawaiian language (‘Ōlelo Hawai‘i) and its regional dialects, which face critical endangerment despite ongoing preservation efforts. While existing scholarship has produced foundational lexicographic and grammatical resources, significant gaps remain in understanding syntactic variation across historical and contemporary texts, dialectal divergence in understudied communities, and the application of computational tools to support pedagogical and community-driven language initiatives. This project addresses these challenges through two interconnected computational workflows. First, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to analyze a digitized corpus of 19th-century Hawaiian-language newspapers, mele (chants), and archival manuscripts, identifying patterns in morphology, loanword integration, and discourse structures. Second, we will develop a parallelized framework for dialect mapping using acoustic and phonetic data from native speaker recordings, integrating spectral analysis and machine learning classifiers to quantify phonological shifts across geographic regions. These workflows demand HPC capabilities due to the scale of textual data (over 20,000 digitized pages), the complexity of training custom NLP models for a low-resource language, and the computational intensity of real-time signal processing for audio datasets. Outcomes will include the first open-access repository of computationally annotated Hawaiian texts, a dialect classification tool for educational applications, and evidence-based recommendations for orthographic standardization of regional variants. By bridging computational linguistics with Indigenous language revitalization frameworks, this project aims to empower Hawaiian-speaking communities with scalable digital resources while contributing novel methodologies for the study of endangered languages globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hawaiian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that optimize decision-making processes in educational supervision and curriculum administration. A critical challenge in educational leadership is the dynamic allocation of instructional resources—such as staff, training, and curricular materials—across diverse learning environments. Traditional methods for modeling these complex systems are limited in scalability and fail to account for real-time variables, including fluctuating student needs, staff capacity, and interdisciplinary program requirements. To address this gap, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate interactions between administrators, educators, and students under varying resource constraints, using anonymized district-level datasets on staffing patterns, student performance, and budget allocations. Second, machine learning algorithms will identify optimal supervisory strategies by analyzing historical outcomes and iteratively refining predictive models. The HPC environment is essential for processing large-scale datasets (spanning 10+ years from 200+ institutions) and running parallel simulations to evaluate thousands of resource allocation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time decision support in curriculum supervision, validated through retrospective comparison with existing administrative data. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing inefficiencies in staff deployment and curricular resource distribution, directly addressing priorities in education leadership training programs. By open-sourcing the computational tools developed, the project aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven supervision in K-12 and higher education settings, advancing the integration of computational analytics into administrative practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise instructional and support personnel at the school building, facility or staff level. Includes instruction in the principles of staffing and organization, the supervision of learning activities, personnel relations, administrative duties related to departmental or unit management, and specific applications to various educational settings and curricula.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing hydraulic fracturing operations in heterogeneous shale formations through advanced computational modeling. Hydraulic fracturing efficiency is critical for maximizing hydrocarbon recovery while minimizing environmental risks, yet current predictive tools often fail to account for the complex interplay of geological heterogeneity, fluid dynamics, and geomechanical stress. The research problem centers on improving fracture network prediction accuracy in irregular shale layers, where variations in rock porosity, mineral composition, and natural fracture density lead to unpredictable fluid pathways and suboptimal resource extraction. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a multi-scale computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for geomechanical stress modeling, lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) for fluid flow simulation, and machine learning (ML) to identify fracture propagation patterns from historical field data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve 3D subsurface models at reservoir scale (1–5 km) with millimeter-resolution fracture details, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of cores. The workflow integrates real-time sensor data from downhole pressure gauges and microseismic arrays to calibrate models dynamically. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for fracture network geometry under varying lithological conditions, enabling engineers to design stage-by-stage fracking plans that enhance contact with hydrocarbon-rich zones while avoiding aquifer breaches. By quantifying stress-shadow effects and proppant transport efficiency in complex geology, this research will directly inform operational decisions to reduce water usage, mitigate induced seismicity risks, and improve well cluster spacing strategies. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will provide the petroleum technology community with a scalable platform for testing extraction scenarios, advancing both economic and environmental objectives in unconventional resource development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of oil and natural gas extraction and processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of petroleum extraction and related geology, petroleum field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, laboratory analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, environment and safety monitoring procedures for oil/gas fields and facilities, facility inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of dialectal variation in contemporary Portuguese through large-scale computational analysis, addressing critical gaps in understanding how regional and sociolinguistic factors shape language evolution. Despite the global presence of Portuguese, comprehensive models of its dialectal diversity—particularly across underserved regions like Africa and Asia—remain underdeveloped due to the scarcity of integrated, high-resolution linguistic data and the computational demands of processing multimodal corpora. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze a curated dataset of 10,000+ hours of spoken and written Portuguese from eight countries, integrating sociodemographic metadata to map correlations between linguistic features and variables such as urbanization, education, and migration. Computational methods will include phonetic alignment using hidden Markov models (HMMs) to trace vowel shifts, transformer-based NLP for syntactic variation detection, and graph-theoretical network analysis to model lexical borrowing patterns. These tasks require parallelized processing of audio transcripts, text corpora, and historical records, which exceed the capacity of standard workstations due to memory-intensive algorithms and terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access geotemporal dialect atlas, predictive models of language change, and a benchmark dataset for Lusophone computational linguistics. The project will directly support pedagogical tools for heritage language preservation and inform natural language processing systems serving multilingual Portuguese-speaking populations.
