By elucidating how non-European varieties influence global Portuguese, this work aims to reshape philological frameworks and foster equitable representation of underrepresented dialects in academic and technological contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Portuguese language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Metropolitan Portuguese; Luso-Brazilian Portuguese; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community health intervention planning by modeling the multilevel determinants of health disparities in urban populations. Despite extensive data on social, environmental, and clinical risk factors, integrating these heterogeneous datasets to simulate population-level outcomes of preventive interventions remains computationally prohibitive. Current models often oversimplify dynamic interactions between behavioral, socioeconomic, and environmental variables, limiting their utility for real-world policy decisions. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that synthesizes electronic health records, geospatial data, and community survey inputs to simulate health outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. The ABM will incorporate machine learning-derived predictors of health behaviors, calibrated using Bayesian inference, to capture non-linear relationships and feedback loops affecting chronic disease prevalence. Computational workflows will parallelize parameter sweeps across intervention types (e.g., mobile screening access, nutrition programs) and population segments, requiring scalable memory and GPU resources for stochastic simulations across 10^5 agent populations. A second aim employs natural language processing to analyze unstructured clinical notes and social media data, identifying barriers to healthcare access in underserved neighborhoods. This component utilizes transformer-based models fine-tuned on regional dialect and cultural context, trained across distributed nodes to handle terabyte-scale text corpora. Outcomes will quantify the cost-efficacy of combined clinical-community strategies for reducing cardiovascular and metabolic disease disparities. By enabling granular, dynamic modeling of community health systems, this work will provide actionable insights for optimizing resource allocation in local public health agencies while advancing computational methods for health equity research. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to managing memory-intensive simulations and machine learning workloads that exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to plan and manage health services in local community settings, including the coordination of related support services, government agencies, and private resources. Includes instruction in public health, community health services and delivery, health behavior and cultural factors, local government operations, human services, health communication and promotion, health services administration in local settings, environmental health, preventive and comparative medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, family and community health, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: The emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens and immune-evading viral strains presents a critical challenge in microbial pathogenesis and host defense. This project seeks to investigate molecular mechanisms underlying pathogen immune evasion and host-microbe interactions through large-scale computational modeling of microbial surface proteins and host receptor dynamics. A key focus is on structural and functional analysis of pathogen-derived virulence factors (e.g., bacterial secretion systems, viral fusion glycoproteins) and their interplay with innate immune components such as Toll-like receptors and complement system proteins. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of these complexes at biologically relevant timescales, employing all-atom and coarse-grained models to capture conformational changes during host-pathogen recognition. Parallelized docking algorithms will screen microbial peptide libraries against immune receptor variants to identify evolutionary adaptation patterns. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate population-level interactions between pathogens and immune cells in tissue microenvironments, incorporating single-cell RNA-seq data from infected host models. The computational workflow requires multi-node GPU acceleration for MD simulations, distributed memory clusters for ensemble docking analyses, and high-throughput processing of spatial interaction datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved structural motifs in immune-evading pathogens, predictive maps of host receptor binding hotspots exploitable for therapeutic intervention, and mechanistic insights into how microbial heterogeneity modulates infection outcomes. This work directly addresses gaps in understanding pathogen adaptability while informing the design of targeted antimicrobials and immune-focused therapies. By integrating computational biophysics with immunological frameworks, the project advances core priorities in microbiology and immunology research, with translational relevance for combating antimicrobial resistance and viral persistence.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microorganisms that cause disease and the host immune response to them. Includes instruction in microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, pathogenic bacteriology, disease mechanisms, immunology, immunogenetics, autoimmunity, and bioinformatics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the complex interplay of biopsychosocial factors influencing symptom trajectories in patients receiving hospice and palliative care. Current clinical tools inadequately capture the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between physical symptoms (e.g., pain, dyspnea), psychological distress, social determinants, and therapeutic interventions, limiting personalized care planning. We propose an integrative approach using high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets spanning electronic health records, wearable sensor data, patient-reported outcomes, and caregiver narratives from 15,000+ historical cases. Agent-based modeling will simulate individual patient trajectories under varying care protocols, while natural language processing will extract latent psychosocial patterns from unstructured clinical notes and advance care planning documents. Graph neural networks will map temporal dependencies between symptoms, treatments, and quality-of-life metrics, with particular attention to rare but clinically critical events like terminal restlessness or rapid functional decline. Computational experiments will evaluate the impact of alternative care schedules, complementary therapy integrations, and ethical decision-making thresholds on predicted outcomes. The resulting models aim to identify high-risk transition points and optimize intervention timing for heterogeneous patient subgroups, validated through retrospective survival analysis and prospective pilot data from three hospice networks. By enabling real-time simulation of care pathway outcomes at scale, this work addresses a critical gap in precision palliative medicine, offering a decision-support tool to balance symptom control, patient autonomy, and resource allocation in end-of-life care. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets, training deep learning architectures with attention mechanisms, and running parallelized sensitivity analyses across diverse demographic and diagnostic cohorts.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: The discovery and optimization of natural product-derived therapeutics are hindered by the structural complexity of bioactive compounds and the computational demands of analyzing their interactions with biological targets. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the identification and mechanistic characterization of natural products with pharmacological potential. A key challenge lies in efficiently modeling the dynamic behavior of structurally diverse compounds—such as alkaloids, terpenoids, and polyketides—within complex biosynthetic pathways and protein-binding environments. We propose an integrated computational workflow combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and machine learning (ML)-guided virtual screening to predict bioactivity, metabolic stability, and target engagement. MD simulations will map conformational landscapes of lead compounds interacting with therapeutic targets (e.g., kinase enzymes, GPCRs), while DFT will optimize reaction coordinates for enzymatic modifications of natural product scaffolds. Concurrently, a neural network trained on ethnobotanical databases and biophysical assay data will prioritize compounds for experimental validation. The scale of these analyses—requiring millions of CPU-core hours for ensemble simulations and quantum mechanical computations—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of three candidate compounds with enhanced binding affinity to inflammation and oncology-related targets, (2) predictive models linking structural motifs to pharmacokinetic properties, and (3) a publicly accessible database of annotated natural product conformers. This work bridges traditional pharmacognosy with computational innovation, accelerating the translation of bioactive natural products into preclinical candidates while reducing reliance on resource-intensive screening. By elucidating structure-activity relationships at unprecedented resolution, the project will advance methodological frameworks for natural product drug discovery within pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic pricing and inventory allocation in apparel and accessories retail through real-time, data-driven decision-making. The rapid evolution of consumer preferences, seasonal trends, and supply chain volatility in this sector creates complex interdependencies between marketing operations, inventory turnover, and profit margins. Traditional forecasting models struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams—including social media sentiment, live sales metrics, and supplier lead times—while maintaining computational efficiency at scale. We propose developing a hybrid machine learning framework combining transformer-based natural language processing for trend detection from unstructured data (e.g., influencer content, product reviews) with reinforcement learning agents trained to optimize pricing and distribution strategies across multi-echelon retail networks. The computational intensity arises from processing petabytes of real-time social media feeds, simulating thousands of parallel market scenarios, and continuously retraining models to adapt to microtrends. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: 1) Distributed training of multimodal architectures fusing image, text, and transactional data 2) Multi-agent reinforcement learning simulations modeling competitive retailer interactions 3) Hyperparameter optimization across spatial-temporal hierarchies (global vs. regional warehouses, hourly demand shifts). Expected outcomes include a deployable system capable of reducing excess inventory by ≥15% through adaptive markdown strategies while increasing gross margins via precision targeting of trend-responsive pricing. This interdisciplinary approach bridges marketing analytics, operations research, and computational social science, offering a novel paradigm for responsive retail operations in fast-fashion ecosystems. The computational infrastructure will enable experimentation with graph neural networks to model supply chain resilience and consumer behavior cascades at unprecedented granularity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of apparel and accessories. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, apparel technologies, distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: The diagnosis and management of neurological disorders in pediatric populations remain challenging due to the heterogeneity of genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors contributing to conditions such as epileptic encephalopathies, neonatal hypoxic-ischemic injury, and neurodevelopmental disorders. Current approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multimodal datasets at scale, hindering the identification of biomarkers and personalized therapeutic strategies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, neuroimaging, and clinical datasets from a cohort of 2,000 pediatric patients with undiagnosed or treatment-resistant neurological disorders. Using whole-genome sequencing data, longitudinal MRI/DTI imaging, and electronic health records, we will implement machine learning pipelines to identify pathogenic genetic variants, map structural and functional neural network abnormalities, and correlate these findings with clinical outcomes. Computational workflows will include variant prioritization via deep learning models trained on multi-omic databases, graph-based analyses of brain connectivity, and survival models to predict disease progression. The scale of data integration—spanning terabytes of imaging and genomic data—necessitates distributed computing frameworks for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel genotype-phenotype associations, predictive algorithms for early intervention in high-risk neonates, and a publicly accessible computational toolkit for pediatric neurology research. By elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment resistance and developmental trajectories, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches, reduce diagnostic odysseys, and improve functional outcomes for children with neurological disorders. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving these goals, enabling analyses that are infeasible with standard clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of neurologic disorders of the neonatal period, infancy, early childhood, and adolescence. Requires training in neurology with additional training in child neurology.

abstract: This project seeks to analyze the evolution of partisan polarization and legislative decision-making in Canadian federal politics through computational modeling of parliamentary speech, voting records, and electoral data. Despite extensive qualitative research on Canadian political institutions, quantitative gaps persist in understanding how intra-party cohesion, inter-regional representation, and ideological alignment shape legislative efficiency and policy outcomes. To address this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze structured and unstructured datasets spanning 40 years of parliamentary debates (1980–2020), voting logs from the House of Commons, and constituency-level election results. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on Canadian political text, will classify speech content by policy domain, sentiment, and rhetorical strategy. These outputs will be integrated with voting cohesion metrics and demographic data using network analysis and multilevel regression models to identify patterns in party discipline, cross-bench collaboration, and regional representation. The computational demands of processing over 1.5 million speech transcripts, coupled with the need for parallelized model training and large-scale graph computations, necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for mapping ideological shifts within Canadian parties, quantifying the impact of regional interests on federal policymaking, and evaluating how institutional designs—such as electoral systems and committee structures—mediate partisan conflict. Results will contribute to comparative legislative studies and provide evidence-based insights for debates on parliamentary reform, democratic accountability, and the role of regionalism in national governance. All models and processed datasets will be made publicly available to support future research in Canadian political science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of Canadian political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in British and North American political theory, political parties and interest groups, provincial and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for creating and analyzing large-scale generative visual artworks and immersive media environments. A central challenge in contemporary digital art and design lies in balancing aesthetic innovation with the technical constraints of real-time rendering, high-resolution output, and interactive audience engagement. Traditional workflows for generative art, 3D modeling, and interactive installations often rely on precomputed elements or simplified simulations, limiting their adaptability and complexity. This project addresses these limitations by developing dynamic, AI-driven systems that integrate real-time data processing, neural network training, and physics-based simulations to produce adaptive visual experiences. Computational methods include parallelized rendering pipelines for 4K/8K resolution outputs, distributed training of generative adversarial networks (GANs) on curated visual datasets, and agent-based modeling of audience interaction patterns within virtual environments. These workflows require substantial memory, GPU acceleration, and multi-node processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets and latency-sensitive feedback loops. The project’s outcomes aim to establish new methodologies for computationally intensive art creation, enabling artists to prototype interactive installations and generative works at unprecedented scales. Anticipated significance includes open-source tools for HPC-aided design, peer-reviewed publications on hybrid human-AI creative processes, and public exhibitions demonstrating the integration of computational scalability with artistic intent. By bridging gaps between visual arts practice and advanced computing, this work will expand the technical and conceptual boundaries of digital media, offering frameworks applicable to fields such as virtual production, architectural visualization, and cultural analytics. The requested resources are critical to overcoming current bottlenecks in rendering times, model training efficiency, and real-time interactivity, ensuring rigorous testing and reproducibility of results.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in visual and performing arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time decision-making in fashion show logistics and display design through advanced computational modeling, addressing the gap in data-driven frameworks for dynamic event coordination within the fashion modeling industry. Current practices rely heavily on experiential knowledge, leading to inefficiencies in managing variables such as model scheduling, spatial layouts, audience movement, and environmental factors (e.g., lighting, acoustics). The project proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation platform leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and reinforcement learning (RL) to predict and optimize resource allocation across these interdependent parameters. Using anonymized historical data from partner agencies—including model gait speeds, set change timelines, and audience engagement metrics—the ABM will simulate interactions between human agents (models, crew, attendees) and physical elements (runways, lighting rigs). RL algorithms will then iteratively refine scheduling and spatial configurations to minimize delays and maximize aesthetic impact. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to reflect the complexity of large-scale fashion events, enabling parallelized testing of thousands of scenario variations under stochastic conditions (e.g., equipment failures, last-minute lineup changes). Expected outcomes include a proprietary optimization toolkit capable of reducing event setup times by 15–20% while improving audience sightline coverage by 30%, metrics that directly translate to cost savings and enhanced brand value for stakeholders. Additionally, the project will produce a novel dataset correlating computational design choices with perceptual outcomes (e.g., audience attention patterns quantified via virtual eye-tracking), advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of operational logistics and sensory marketing. By formalizing tacit industry knowledge into transferable AI-driven models, this work establishes a foundation for computational resource management in niche creative industries that remain underserved by conventional business analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to present and display fashion, apparel, and accessories products in wholesale and retail settings, either on the person or via props and natural or artificial settings. Includes instruction in modeling skills, health and cosmetic principles, fashion show management, display design and production, and applicable aspects of advertising and fashion photography.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation within Russian media and literary texts from the late Soviet period to the present, focusing on understudied regional and non-state publications. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how decentralized cultural production—particularly in digital archives, independent journals, and grassroots media—has shaped conceptions of Russian identity amidst geopolitical and social transformations. Existing scholarship relies heavily on manual analysis of limited curated sources, which cannot capture the scale, diversity, or intertextual dynamics of these materials. To overcome this limitation, we propose a computational humanities approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Our team will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned for historical and regional Russian dialects, to analyze a corpus of over 500,000 digitized texts spanning 1985–2025. Semantic network analysis and dynamic topic modeling will be employed to trace narrative shifts, conceptual linkages, and the circulation of cultural symbols across time and regions. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for training custom embeddings, graph-based algorithms for mapping discourse communities, and storage for multi-modal data (text, images, metadata). Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously unrecognized narrative frameworks influencing post-Soviet identity construction, 2) quantitative evidence of regional cultural divergences and continuities, and 3) an open-access computational toolkit for Slavic digital humanities research. This work will provide the first systematic analysis of decentralized cultural production’s role in redefining Russian identity, offering methodological innovations for area studies while informing contemporary debates on cultural pluralism in the region. The scale and complexity of multilingual, historically layered materials necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve statistically robust and temporally granular insights.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Russian Federation and its Soviet, Czarist, and medieval predecessors and related borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational framework to optimize next-generation sustainable packaging materials with enhanced functional and environmental performance. Current packaging systems face critical trade-offs between mechanical durability, barrier properties, biodegradability, and carbon footprint, exacerbated by the complex interplay of material behaviors across molecular, structural, and supply chain scales. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to efficiently explore these multidimensional design spaces due to the combinatorial explosion of potential biomaterial formulations, processing conditions, and reuse scenarios. We propose an integrated computational strategy combining molecular dynamics simulations of biopolymer-nanocomposite interactions, finite element analysis of package structural performance under dynamic transport loads, and machine learning-driven life cycle assessment. High-performance computing resources are essential to execute these coupled simulations at scale, enabling parametric studies of cellulose-based hybrid materials, mycelium composites, and enzymatically recyclable polymers under diverse humidity, temperature, and mechanical stress regimes. The computational framework will incorporate stochastic modeling of distribution network vibrations and drop impacts to probabilistically predict real-world failure modes while optimizing for end-of-life scenarios through agent-based recycling process simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating molecular architectures with macroscale functionality, validated against experimental data from industry partners, and a decision-support tool for designing regionally tailored packaging systems that minimize waste without compromising product protection. This research will advance fundamental understanding of multi-functional material design principles specific to packaging applications while establishing computational workflows adaptable to emerging challenges in active/intelligent packaging development. The resource allocation will directly support urgent industry needs to transition from single-use plastics, potentially reducing packaging-related carbon emissions by enabling data-driven material substitutions at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific, technological, design, and business principles to the development of packages and packaging materials, including raw material production, conversion of raw materials into usable forms, design, distribution, and post-use recycling and reuse. Includes instruction in principles of packaging, materials sciences, distribution and transportation, engineering and technology, graphic design, packaging regulations, and business and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the modeling of plasma-driven instabilities in high-energy-density systems, a critical challenge in applied physics with implications for fusion energy, propulsion, and industrial plasma applications. While experimental studies of turbulent plasma behavior under extreme conditions remain constrained by diagnostic limitations and safety protocols, computational approaches offer a pathway to resolve multiscale dynamics. However, existing simulations struggle to concurrently capture kinetic effects, electromagnetic field evolution, and fluid-scale transport over experimentally relevant spatiotemporal domains. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining particle-in-cell (PIC) methods for non-equilibrium electron dynamics with continuum-based magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) for bulk ion transport. The project will implement adaptive mesh refinement to allocate computational resources dynamically, focusing resolution on regions of strong field gradients or particle acceleration. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to optimize parameter sampling across the high-dimensional phase space governing instability growth rates. The proposed work requires high-performance computing resources to manage the memory-intensive PIC-MHD coupling and the parallel processing demands of three-dimensional simulations spanning microseconds of physical time. Anticipated outcomes include validated instability thresholds for tokamak-relevant magnetic confinement configurations and predictive models of energy dissipation pathways in pulsed plasma thrusters. Results will directly inform the design of next-generation plasma containment systems, with open-source code releases enabling broader community access to multiscale simulation tools. This work bridges fundamental plasma physics with engineering applications, aligning with the applied physics program’s emphasis on interdisciplinary technical innovation. The requested computing allocation will support 18 months of large-scale simulations, with validation against collaborative experimental datasets from partner institutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics to a technical discipline or with the interface between physics and other disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model aerothermal-structural interactions in hypersonic vehicle components during atmospheric entry, a critical challenge in aerospace engineering. Current design practices rely on decoupled simulations that inadequately capture the interplay between turbulent hypersonic flows, extreme heating, and nonlinear structural deformation, leading to overconservative thermal protection systems (TPS) or unexpected failure risks. The research problem centers on resolving the multi-physics coupling across fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and material response at Mach 7+ conditions, where experimental data are scarce and existing empirical models lack generalizability. The proposed approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to execute fully coupled simulations using a partitioned finite volume-finite element methodology. This includes direct numerical simulation (DNS) of boundary layer transition in chemically reactive flows, conjugate heat transfer modeling for ablative TPS materials, and nonlinear thermoelasticity solvers for composite structures. The computational workflow will exploit adaptive mesh refinement to resolve localized phenomena such as shock-boundary layer interactions and material pyrolysis, while iterative coupling algorithms ensure stability across disparate timescales. The project will validate models against limited ground-test data from arc-jet facilities and flight measurements from prior missions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for TPS degradation under realistic flight conditions, optimized material layup designs to mitigate thermal buckling, and open-source computational modules for coupled aerothermal-structural analysis. By enabling high-resolution 3D simulations of full-scale vehicle segments, this work aims to reduce reliance on empirical safety margins in hypersonic systems, directly supporting the development of reusable space vehicles and next-generation planetary entry capsules. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the exascale computational demands of DNS-resolution coupled simulations, which require sustained petascale performance for O(10^6) core-hour allocations per design iteration.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their system. Combines instruction in mechanical and aerospace engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the nail care industry, specifically within the niche of advanced gel polish formulation and curing dynamics. Despite the growing demand for durable, hypoallergenic, and aesthetically versatile nail products, the chemical and physical processes underlying gel curing remain poorly characterized, leading to inconsistent results, allergic reactions, and inefficiencies in application. Current industry practices rely on trial-and-error experimentation, which is resource-intensive and fails to account for the complex interplay of photoinitiators, oligomers, and UV-LED curing parameters. This research proposes a computational approach to model photopolymerization kinetics and light penetration dynamics during gel curing. Molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to predict cross-linking behavior and stress distribution within cured gel layers under varying wavelengths (365–405 nm) and exposure durations. Finite element analysis will complement these simulations to optimize heat dissipation in UV-LED lamps, mitigating thermal damage to the nail plate. Additionally, machine learning models trained on spectral data from experimental curing trials will identify correlations between formulation components and clinical outcomes such as adhesion longevity and biocompatibility. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the high dimensionality of parameter space (e.g., monomer ratios, irradiance profiles) and the need for real-time visualization of polymerization pathways. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for formulating safer, faster-curing gels and evidence-based protocols for minimizing dermatological risks. By bridging cosmetic chemistry, materials science, and computational modeling, this project aims to establish a foundational knowledge base for next-generation nail care technologies, directly benefiting practitioners through enhanced product reliability and reduced occupational hazards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized, AI-driven clinical decision support tools tailored for pre-procedural risk assessment in rare genetic disorders—a niche intersecting genomics, computational modeling, and clinical practice. Current risk stratification models for surgical and interventional procedures lack granularity for patients with ultra-rare syndromes (affecting ≤1 in 50,000 individuals), often leading to suboptimal perioperative planning. We aim to address this gap by integrating multi-omics data, electronic health records, and biomechanical simulations to predict individualized complication risks. The computational workflow will involve three phases: 1) Training graph neural networks on federated genomic and phenotypic datasets from international rare disease registries to identify syndrome-specific risk signatures; 2) Developing finite element models of tissue biomechanics informed by patient-specific MRI-derived anatomical features; and 3) Implementing reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize intervention timing and technique based on evolving physiological parameters. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the heterogeneous data streams, running parallelized biomechanical simulations, and iterating deep learning architectures at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for rare disease procedural planning and validated risk prediction modules for five target syndromes currently lacking evidence-based guidelines. This work bridges a critical gap in precision perioperative medicine while establishing computational methods adaptable to other underserved clinical niches. By aligning with pre-professional physician assistant competencies in complex care coordination and evidence-based intervention, the project also contributes novel educational resources for translating computational predictions into collaborative clinical decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional physician assistant program.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of stylistic and thematic evolution in Anglophone literary texts from the 18th to the 21st century. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on close reading of select works, this study aims to systematically trace patterns across a corpus of over 50,000 novels, plays, and poems, digitized through partnerships with academic archives. The primary research problem centers on identifying macro-level shifts in linguistic innovation, genre boundaries, and sociocultural representation—patterns that remain opaque at smaller scales of analysis. Current methodologies lack the capacity to process such volumes of unstructured text while accounting for historical context, rhetorical nuance, and intertextuality. To address this, the project will implement a hybrid computational approach combining transformer-based language models (fine-tuned BERT and GPT-3.5 architectures) for semantic role labeling and sentiment analysis, alongside graph neural networks to map citation networks and thematic diffusion. HPC resources are critical for training these models on the multi-terabyte corpus, enabling parallelized processing of syntactic structures and latent narrative features across temporal and geographic axes. Expected outcomes include: (1) quantitative frameworks for tracking literary influence and stylistic convergence in post-Enlightenment literature, (2) interactive visualizations of genre evolution correlated with historical events, and (3) open-access datasets annotating rhetorical strategies in underrepresented authors. By bridging computational linguistics and literary theory, this work will establish reproducible pipelines for humanities-focused NLP while challenging canonical narratives of literary periodization. The scale of analysis, made feasible through HPC infrastructure, promises to redefine scholarly understanding of how collective cultural values manifest in—and are shaped by—large-scale linguistic trends.
cip_title: English Language and Literature/ Letters, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in English language and literature, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of horticultural science with public education requires innovative approaches to address the challenges of optimizing plant health, visitor engagement, and operational efficiency in dynamic urban environments. This project seeks to develop computational models to predict plant performance and visitor interactions in public horticultural spaces, such as botanical gardens and urban farms, under varying environmental and socioeconomic conditions. Current methods for managing these spaces rely on generalized protocols, which often fail to account for localized stressors like microclimate variability, soil heterogeneity, or fluctuating visitor foot traffic. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets, including high-resolution sensor data from IoT-enabled horticultural installations, genomic information from stress-tolerant plant varieties, and visitor behavioral metrics. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns in plant resilience and visitor engagement, while agent-based models will simulate the impact of layout designs and educational programming on operational outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate hyperspectral imaging data to assess plant physiological responses and reinforcement learning to optimize irrigation and nutrient delivery systems in real time. By parallelizing these analyses across HPC nodes, the project aims to generate predictive frameworks that balance horticultural viability, economic feasibility, and educational value. Expected outcomes include open-source decision-support tools for public horticulture practitioners, enabling data-driven design of spaces that enhance community learning while minimizing resource use. This work will advance the interdisciplinary nexus of plant science and public outreach, providing scalable solutions for urban horticulture institutions adapting to climate variability and evolving educational demands.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on combining traditional horticulture and public education and outreach. Includes instruction in botany, soil science, plant science, agricultural economics, leadership, and business.

abstract: This project addresses the challenge of preparing social studies teachers to effectively navigate complex, dynamic classroom environments shaped by diverse student perspectives and rapidly evolving sociopolitical contexts. Current teacher education models often lack scalable tools to simulate realistic, data-rich scenarios that develop pedagogical adaptability. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create large-scale simulations of classroom discourse and decision-making processes, informed by multimodal datasets of historical and contemporary social studies teaching practices. Agent-based modeling will be used to simulate student-teacher interactions across varied demographic and ideological conditions, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will analyze patterns in classroom dialogue transcripts, curricular materials, and student-generated content. These computational approaches will enable parametric studies of instructional strategies under thousands of simulated classroom configurations, identifying approaches that optimally balance content delivery, critical thinking development, and inclusive participation. The project will utilize existing datasets from classroom observations, teacher reflections, and student work samples, supplemented by synthetic data generation to model underrepresented scenarios. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access repository of simulated classroom interaction models specific to social studies pedagogy, (2) predictive analytics frameworks to guide instructional adaptations during lesson implementation, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for designing teacher education experiences that address emerging challenges in civic education. By enabling rapid iteration through complex educational scenarios that would require years to observe in physical classrooms, this HPC-supported approach aims to advance the preparation of socially conscious, computationally literate educators equipped to foster democratic discourse in K-12 settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general social studies programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Operational oceanography in military contexts requires the integration of high-resolution environmental data with dynamic modeling to support tactical decision-making in complex, contested maritime environments. Existing oceanographic models often lack the granularity and computational efficiency needed to predict localized phenomena—such as nearshore turbulence, acoustic propagation anomalies, or rapid thermocline shifts—that directly impact mission success. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a multi-scale, adaptive modeling framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The research will focus on three interconnected challenges: (1) real-time assimilation of heterogeneous data streams (satellite, autonomous sensors, and legacy hydrographic datasets) into predictive models, (2) coupling hydrodynamic and acoustic propagation models at tactically relevant spatiotemporal scales (meters to kilometers, minutes to hours), and (3) quantifying uncertainty in rapidly evolving littoral zones. Computational methods will leverage parallelized finite-element solvers for non-linear wave equations, machine learning techniques for parameterizing subgrid-scale processes, and ensemble-based data assimilation to improve forecast reliability. By deploying these models on HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce latency in operational predictions by 40–60% compared to current operational systems while maintaining sub-kilometer resolution. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for adaptive oceanographic forecasting, validated against field measurements from recent naval exercises in the Indo-Pacific region. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—requiring petascale processing capabilities and high-bandwidth memory—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. Successful implementation will provide military operators with enhanced situational awareness in dynamic coastal environments, directly informing mission planning related to mine countermeasures, antisubmarine warfare, and amphibious operations. This work bridges oceanographic science and defense priorities, advancing computational methods for time-sensitive, security-critical applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of physical oceanography as applied to the naval tactical and strategic environment and the support of military operations. Includes instruction in atmospheric thermodynamics and radiation propagation, air-ocean fluid dynamics, ocean waves, nearshore environments and processes, ocean acoustics, ocean analysis, tactical oceanography, prediction, and related quantitative and experimental methods.

abstract: The increasing demand for resilient coastal infrastructure and sustainable ocean energy systems necessitates advanced predictive models capable of capturing the complex interactions between marine structures and dynamic fluid environments. Traditional approaches in ocean engineering often rely on simplified hydrodynamic assumptions or scale-model testing, which struggle to account for multi-scale phenomena such as turbulent flow-structure interactions, sediment transport under extreme wave conditions, and the coupled effects of biofouling on structural fatigue. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate these interdependent processes at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Leveraging coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA), the framework will integrate machine learning techniques to optimize adaptive mesh refinement and reduce computational overhead while preserving accuracy. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve sub-meter-scale vorticity fields around submerged structures, model long-term morphological changes in seabed topography, and quantify uncertainty across stochastic wave climate scenarios. The research will employ open-source solvers, including OpenFOAM and FEniCS, parallelized for GPU-accelerated clusters to handle billion-element meshes and multi-physics coupling. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for optimizing offshore renewable energy arrays, assessing the lifespan of artificial reef systems, and informing climate-resilient coastal protection designs. By bridging gaps between fluid mechanics, materials science, and environmental dynamics, this work aims to establish new standards for computational ocean engineering, directly supporting the development of infrastructure that balances ecological sustainability with human-centric engineering demands. The resulting datasets and models will be made accessible to the broader research community to accelerate innovation in marine resource management and hazard mitigation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to monitor, control, manipulate and operate within coastal or ocean environments, such as underwater platforms, flood control systems, dikes, hydroelectric power systems, tide and current control and warning systems, and communications equipment; the planning and design of total systems for working and functioning in water or underwater environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as the action of water properties and behavior on physical systems and people, tidal forces, current movements, and wave motion.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing algorithmic decision-making in human resources (HR). As organizations increasingly deploy artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) tools for hiring, performance evaluation, and workforce management, disparities in compliance with anti-discrimination laws, data privacy regulations, and jurisdictional mandates have emerged as a critical challenge. Traditional legal analysis struggles to systematically evaluate the scale and interaction of these tools with heterogeneous legal requirements, particularly across multinational contexts. To address this gap, the project will develop a computational legal analytics framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and simulation modeling. Legal texts—including statutes, case law, administrative guidance, and enforcement actions from multiple jurisdictions—will be processed using transformer-based models to identify obligations, risks, and conflicts related to algorithmic HR systems. Agent-based simulations will then model organizational compliance behaviors under varying regulatory conditions, while graph neural networks will map cross-jurisdictional legal influences. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale legal corpora, iterative training of domain-specific ML models, and large-scale scenario testing—tasks requiring HPC infrastructure for distributed storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-throughput simulations. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of algorithmic HR compliance risks, predictive tools for assessing policy impacts on equitable workplace outcomes, and a public dataset linking legal provisions to technical system requirements. By bridging computational methods and HR law, this work aims to advance evidence-based regulatory design and provide organizations with scalable strategies for maintaining legal and ethical AI deployments in HR practices.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting human resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize investigative decision-making in law enforcement interviews by modeling complex human behavioral dynamics and scenario outcomes. Traditional interview techniques often rely on heuristic approaches, which may introduce biases or inefficiencies when evaluating suspect responses, witness reliability, or evidence consistency. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale, adaptive interview scenarios integrating psychological, linguistic, and contextual variables. Agent-based modeling will be employed to create synthetic populations of interviewees with diverse behavioral profiles, trained on anonymized case data and validated against ground-truth psychological studies. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will analyze semantic patterns, emotional valence, and response latency in simulated dialogues, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine interview strategies to maximize information accuracy and procedural fairness. The computational workflow will parallelize thousands of interview permutations across HPC nodes, testing hypotheses about question phrasing, rapport-building tactics, and deception detection under varying legal and cultural constraints. Outcomes will include a predictive tool to recommend context-specific interview protocols, a bias-mitigation scoring system for investigative workflows, and a dataset linking behavioral markers to case resolution metrics. By bridging computational modeling and investigative practice, this work aims to advance empirically grounded, ethically informed interviewing methodologies while maintaining compliance with evolving legal standards. The project’s scalability and focus on human-AI collaboration address a critical gap in modern law enforcement training and operational decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, procedures, techniques, legal concerns, and problems associated with a criminal investigation. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, courtroom evidence management and preparation, case presentation and court testimony, description and identification, state and federal criminal law and procedures, informant and suspect rights, officer liability, informant and witness management, victim awareness, tactical interviewing, psychology, criminal investigation methods and procedures, report writing and documentation, investigative techniques, and case management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of robotic systems in industrial applications demands advanced computational tools to optimize design, control, and operational efficiency. Current robotics technologies face challenges in real-time adaptive decision-making, multi-sensor data fusion, and dynamic environment interaction, particularly in unstructured settings such as flexible manufacturing or logistics automation. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity simulation frameworks and machine learning models to enhance robotic autonomy and performance. The research will focus on creating scalable algorithms for robotic path planning, collision avoidance, and task optimization under variable constraints. A key computational challenge lies in managing the high-dimensional state spaces inherent to multi-joint robotic systems and stochastic environments, which require iterative simulations and large-scale parameter sweeps. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to accelerate the training of reinforcement learning agents, parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for system reliability analysis, and validate hybrid control strategies that integrate vision-based sensing with actuator dynamics. The proposed workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated frameworks for neural network training and distributed computing for real-time simulation of multi-robot coordination scenarios. Expected outcomes include optimized control algorithms for energy-efficient robotic operations, probabilistic models for failure prediction in complex tasks, and open-source simulation tools tailored for industrial robotics applications. These results will directly benefit collaborative robotics research and provide actionable insights for deploying adaptable robotic systems in small-to-medium enterprises. By utilizing HPC resources, this project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical control strategies and practical implementation, advancing the scalability of robotics solutions in non-standardized industrial environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using robots. Includes instruction in the principles of robotics, design and operational testing, system maintenance and repair procedures, robot computer systems and control language, specific system types and applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: Sleep disorders, such as obstructive sleep apnea, insomnia, and circadian rhythm disruptions, are pervasive yet mechanistically poorly understood, in part due to the complex interplay of physiological, genetic, and environmental factors. Current clinical approaches often rely on simplified diagnostic criteria or subjective patient reports, limiting personalized treatment strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by integrating large-scale, multi-modal datasets—including high-density polysomnography, actigraphy, genomic sequencing, and electronic health records—to identify novel biomarkers and mechanistic pathways underlying sleep disorders. The computational challenges inherent in analyzing these high-dimensional, temporally resolved datasets necessitate advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Traditional methods lack the scalability to process terabytes of physiological signals or to model dynamic interactions across neural, respiratory, and genetic systems. We propose a hybrid machine learning and biophysical modeling approach. Deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models and 3D convolutional neural networks, will be trained on raw polysomnographic waveforms to classify sleep stages and detect pathological events with higher resolution than current clinical tools. Concurrently, mechanistic models of respiratory control circuits and sleep-wake regulatory networks will simulate how genetic variants or neural circuit dysregulation manifest as observable sleep disruptions. These models will be parameterized using population-scale genomic data and validated against clinical outcomes. By leveraging HPC clusters, we will parallelize training across thousands of GPU nodes, optimize hyperparameters via Bayesian methods, and run large-scale simulations of neural systems under varying physiological conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific genetic or neural signatures to sleep disorder subtypes, as well as open-source tools for automated, precision-focused sleep analysis. This work has the potential to redefine clinical frameworks for sleep disorder diagnosis, inform targeted therapies, and provide a computational blueprint for integrating multi-omics data into dynamic physiological models.
cip_definition: Research focused on Sleep Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and semantic evolution of ritual practices within understudied diasporic religious communities, focusing on 20th-century syncretic movements that blend Indigenous spiritual traditions with Abrahamic frameworks. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable methodologies to map how ritual narratives, gestures, and material artifacts transform across generations—a process critical to understanding cultural resilience but often obscured by fragmented oral histories and non-linear textual sources. Using a corpus of multilingual ritual transcripts, ethnographic field recordings, and community-produced visual media spanning 1945–2015, we will apply transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for low-resource languages and dialectal variations to identify latent thematic shifts. Concurrently, spatial network analysis will reconstruct the diffusion pathways of ritual elements using georeferenced historical data. The computational workflow integrates probabilistic topic modeling (via Latent Dirichlet Allocation) with temporal graph embeddings to trace how socio-political disruptions (e.g., forced migrations, interfaith tensions) correlate with innovations in liturgical syntax and symbolism. HPC resources are essential for processing over 15TB of multimodal data, training custom vision-language models for ritual gesture classification, and simulating counterfactual diffusion scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking ritual morphologies to specific historical stressors, (2) novel metrics for quantifying cultural hybridity in religious practices, and (3) computational frameworks adaptable to other marginalized spiritual traditions. This work bridges computational anthropology, digital hermeneutics, and diaspora studies while advancing methodological rigor in documenting non-institutionalized religious expressions at risk of erasure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in theological studies and religious vocations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize dynamic stability and transient response in hybrid power plants integrating intermittent renewable generation (e.g., solar, wind) with grid-forming inverters and synchronous generator-based assets. Modern power systems face critical challenges in maintaining frequency and voltage stability during rapid generation shifts or fault conditions, exacerbated by the nonlinear interactions between legacy infrastructure and inverter-based resources. Existing simulation tools struggle to resolve these multi-timescale dynamics at the system level while preserving device-level granularity, limiting predictive accuracy for contingency planning. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid modeling approach combining physics-based differential-algebraic equations for electromechanical dynamics with data-driven surrogate models of power electronics, trained on experimental device characterization data. The framework will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform massively parallel transient stability simulations across thousands of operational scenarios, including stochastic variations in renewable output and fault locations. Key computational challenges include adaptive time-stepping for stiff systems, distributed memory optimization for large-scale network topologies, and uncertainty quantification through Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of stability-critical operating envelopes for hybrid plants under grid code compliance constraints, (2) development of novel control coordination strategies between inverters and synchronous condensers, and (3) open-source tools for scenario-based resilience benchmarking. This work will directly inform industry standards for hybrid plant grid interconnection while advancing computational methodologies for power system stability analysis in high-renewable penetration contexts. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution and parametric sweep breadth within tractable simulation timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan electrical systems and modify existing electrical systems that generate and use large amounts of electricity required for distribution networks that are economical, safe, and functional. Includes instruction in alternative/renewable energy systems; calculus; circuit analysis; electrical power systems and industry practices; electrical system design; microprocessor architecture; motor control systems; power electronics operation, planning and protection; programmable logic controllers; and project management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze behavioral and therapeutic patterns in child-client play therapy sessions, with the goal of advancing evidence-based training and intervention strategies for Registered Play Therapists (RPTs). Play therapy relies on nuanced, real-time observations of play behaviors to assess emotional and developmental states, but manual coding of sessions is labor-intensive and prone to subjective bias. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale video datasets of therapy sessions, integrating computer vision, machine learning, and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The research problem centers on identifying quantifiable markers of therapeutic progress—such as play theme consistency, emotional expression dynamics, and therapist-client interaction patterns—that correlate with clinical outcomes. Video data will be annotated using established play therapy frameworks (e.g., the Play Therapy Dimensions Model) and processed via neural networks trained to detect non-verbal cues (e.g., facial expressions, object interactions) and verbal exchanges. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution video streams, feature extraction at scale, and iterative model training to account for developmental and cultural variability in child behavior. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated session analysis, predictive models linking specific play behaviors to therapeutic milestones, and a dataset anonymized for community use. This work holds significance for standardizing play therapy assessment, reducing therapist workload, and enhancing training through data-driven feedback. By quantifying previously subjective metrics, the project aims to strengthen the empirical foundation of play therapy while adhering to ethical guidelines for child data privacy. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with play therapy accreditation bodies to ensure translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber-physical attacks targeting industrial control systems (ICS) necessitates novel methods to audit and fortify embedded device security without disrupting operational continuity. Traditional vulnerability assessments in ICS environments rely on static protocol analyses or passive network monitoring, which fail to capture dynamic adversarial interactions in hybrid digital-physical workflows. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework to model attack-defense scenarios in ICS networks, explicitly integrating device firmware behavior, process-aware threat vectors, and real-time safety constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the framework will execute massively parallel simulations of compromised operational technology (OT) nodes under varying threat models, including stealthy code injection, sensor spoofing, and cascading process failures. Computational experiments will employ containerized device emulation, discrete-event process modeling, and evolutionary optimization algorithms to iteratively identify critical security gaps in simulated water treatment and energy distribution testbeds. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—requiring synchronized execution of thousands of virtualized Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), physics-based process models, and adaptive penetration testing agents—demands distributed memory architectures and GPU-accelerated compute nodes. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly available benchmark dataset of ICS attack trajectories, quantitative metrics for resilience auditing in safety-critical infrastructure, and prescriptive guidelines for deploying runtime attestation mechanisms in heterogeneous OT environments. By bridging cybersecurity auditing with industrial process modeling, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive risk assessment in cyber-physical systems, directly supporting the development of next-generation industrial security standards.
cip_title: Computer and Information Systems Security/ Auditing/ Information Assurance
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assess the security needs of computer and network systems, recommend safeguard solutions, and manage the implementation, auditing, and maintenance of security devices, systems, and procedures. Includes instruction in computer architecture, programming, and systems analysis; networking; telecommunications; cryptography; security system auditing and design; applicable law and regulations; risk assessment and policy analysis; contingency planning; user access issues; investigation techniques; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and simulate the dynamics of information operations in contemporary conflict environments, with a focus on psychological impact and strategic outcomes. Modern military engagements increasingly rely on information as a central domain of competition, yet existing models inadequately capture the real-time interplay between adversarial narratives, media ecosystems, and population sentiment in contested regions. The research addresses this gap by integrating heterogeneous datasets—including multilingual social media streams, state-sponsored media outputs, and simulated adversarial campaigns—into a unified analytical platform. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate multi-actor interactions (e.g., military communicators, civilian populations, adversarial networks) under varying information conditions. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to detect emerging narratives and sentiment shifts across culturally diverse contexts, while network analysis will map the diffusion pathways of disinformation campaigns. Machine learning classifiers will identify patterns in adversarial tactics, enabling predictive assessments of likely escalation vectors. The computational intensity of processing terabyte-scale multilingual text corpora, coupled with the need for parallelized simulation of thousands of scenario variants, necessitates dedicated HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for assessing the probable effectiveness of counter-narrative strategies, quantifying the psychological resilience of target populations, and optimizing media engagement timelines. This work will advance methodological approaches at the intersection of computational social science and defense studies, providing novel insights into the operationalization of information as both a weapon and a shield in hybrid warfare contexts. The resulting models and datasets will be made available to authorized defense analysts through secure research portals, informing both tactical planning and long-term doctrine development for information-centric military operations.
cip_title: Information/ Psychological Warfare and Military Media Relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the support of military and strategic operations and policy via the use of information as a tool of statecraft and warfighting. Includes instruction in information technology and systems, information security, command and control, satellite communications, global information dissemination, communications and media management, intelligence, psychological warfare, strategic planning, security policy and doctrine, and applications to specific operations, services, and scenarios.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Disability Studies by analyzing large-scale qualitative and multimodal datasets that capture the lived experiences and cultural representations of disabled communities. The research problem centers on the lack of computationally driven methodologies to systematically examine how disability is constructed, negotiated, and represented across diverse sociocultural contexts. Current scholarship relies heavily on small-scale qualitative analyses, limiting the capacity to identify patterns in disability narratives across time, geography, and media. To address this gap, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to process textual data from archival records, disability rights advocacy materials, literature, and social media, alongside image analysis of visual art and protest signage created by disabled artists and activists. Computational workflows will be designed to identify themes, rhetorical strategies, and representational shifts in disability discourse while preserving the nuance of embodied and intersectional perspectives. By integrating critical disability theory with computational methods, this work will map how stigmatizing language, metaphors of overcoming, and emancipatory frameworks manifest at scale. The HPC environment is essential for training custom transformer models on disability-specific corpora, conducting sentiment and network analyses across multilingual sources, and processing high-resolution visual datasets. Expected outcomes include novel computational tools tailored to Disability Studies, open-access datasets annotated with disability-centered metadata, and visualizations that trace the evolution of disability identity and resistance movements. These resources will provide scholars, educators, and activists with evidence-based insights to challenge ableist narratives and advance equity in cultural, educational, and healthcare systems. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in centering marginalized voices within interdisciplinary social science research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature, meaning, and consequences of what it is to be defined as disabled and explores the historical, cultural, economic, physiological, and socio-political dynamics of disability. Includes instruction in disability rights, legal issues, and public policy; literature, philosophy, and the arts; and/or research in the social sciences, education, and health sciences addressing social and experiential aspects of disability.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cognitive workload and decision-making accuracy in complex human-machine systems, with a focus on optimizing interface design to enhance performance and reduce operational errors. While existing models of cognitive load provide foundational insights, they often lack the granularity to account for real-world variability in task demands, individual differences, and dynamic system feedback. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate human-system interactions at scale. Agent-based models will be developed to represent heterogeneous user populations, incorporating psychophysiological data (e.g., eye-tracking, response latency) from empirical studies to parameterize agents’ cognitive processing and adaptive behaviors. Monte Carlo simulations will explore system performance under stochastic task conditions, while machine learning techniques will identify critical design thresholds associated with performance degradation or error escalation. The HPC environment is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent scenarios, iterative parameter optimization, and real-time analysis of high-dimensional interaction data. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for interface customization based on user cognitive profiles, evidence-based recommendations for error mitigation in safety-critical systems (e.g., aviation, medical technology), and methodological advancements in modeling human factors at ecological scales. By integrating computational rigor with human-centered design principles, this work aims to advance theoretical understanding of cognitive resilience in sociotechnical systems while delivering actionable tools for practitioners. The requested resources will directly support the generation of open-access simulation platforms and datasets to catalyze interdisciplinary collaboration in human factors research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to understand of interactions among humans and other elements of a system. Includes instruction in applying theory, principles, data and methods to design in order to optimize human well-being and overall system performance.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the computational and environmental constraints underlying decision-making processes in dynamic, uncertain environments. Traditional experimental paradigms in behavioral psychology often simplify real-world complexity to maintain methodological tractability, limiting ecological validity. To address this, we propose a series of agent-based models that simulate multi-stage decision tasks with interacting probabilistic rewards, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to systematically explore high-dimensional parameter spaces. The research will implement reinforcement learning architectures and Bayesian inference models to simulate adaptive behavior under varying uncertainty regimes, requiring stochastic simulations across millions of parameter combinations. Key computational challenges include parallelized likelihood estimation for hierarchical models, real-time optimization of reward schedules, and large-scale pattern detection in simulated choice histories. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration over experimental designs in silico before empirical validation, while machine learning pipelines will identify critical thresholds where decision strategies shift between model-based and model-free operations.
