Expected outcomes include (1) a computational taxonomy of adaptive decision-making under uncertainty, (2) optimized experimental protocols for studying complex behavioral dynamics, and (3) open-source tools for scalable cognitive modeling. By bridging theoretical learning frameworks with computationally intensive simulations, this work aims to advance predictive models of behavior while establishing methodological benchmarks for resource-intensive psychological research. The requested resources directly address the need for specialized computing capabilities in handling terabyte-scale simulation outputs and concurrent optimization tasks that exceed the capacity of standard laboratory computing environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of behavior under experimental conditions and the analysis of controlled behavioral responses. Includes instruction in learning theory, research design and experimental methods, psychological measurement, statistical design and methods, analysis of cognitive and behavioral variables, and the conduct of specialized and large-scale studies.

abstract: Plant nurseries face complex challenges in optimizing growth conditions while managing operational costs and environmental sustainability. Traditional approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for dynamic environmental variables or species-specific physiological responses. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to model plant growth dynamics under varying nursery conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will integrate multi-scale datasets, including real-time sensor data (light, humidity, soil nutrients), genomic information, and historical growth records, into a machine learning-driven predictive model. The framework will employ parallelized agent-based simulations to evaluate millions of scenario combinations, identifying optimal irrigation schedules, nutrient delivery systems, and climate control strategies tailored to different plant species and developmental stages. Additionally, we will implement reinforcement learning algorithms to adaptively refine management policies based on continuous data input. The expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that enables nursery operators to maximize crop yield and quality while minimizing resource waste. This research will advance precision agriculture in horticultural production by bridging gaps between plant physiology insights and scalable computational solutions, ultimately contributing to more sustainable and economically viable nursery operations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage outdoor plant farms, tree and shrub nurseries, and related facilities that develop domesticated plant products for propagation, harvesting, and transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science, farm and business management, nursery operations, equipment operation and maintenance, safety procedures, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the neurocomputational and biomechanical underpinnings of acquired communication disorders, such as aphasia and dysarthria, through advanced computational modeling. Current clinical assessments in speech-language pathology often rely on behavioral observations and static imaging, which lack the resolution to capture dynamic, multiscale interactions between neural processing, vocal tract physiology, and linguistic output. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation framework integrating neural network models of language processing, 3D biomechanical models of vocal articulation, and real-world speech datasets from diverse patient populations. The research will employ deep learning architectures to analyze patterns in high-dimensional speech acoustics and electroglottographic data, coupled with finite element modeling of swallowing mechanics and vocal fold dynamics. These components will be unified through multi-agent reinforcement learning systems to simulate adaptive communication strategies under varying deficit profiles. The computational intensity of training such hybrid models—particularly the parallel processing of multimodal data streams (audio, kinematic, fMRI)—necessitates high-performance computing resources for iterative optimization and large-scale parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific neural lesion patterns to articulatory compensations, validated against longitudinal clinical data. This work will directly inform personalized therapy planning by quantifying how individualized motor learning algorithms could be harnessed during rehabilitation. The resulting open-source tools will enable clinicians to simulate treatment outcomes based on patient-specific biomechanical constraints and residual neural circuitry, advancing precision medicine approaches in communication disorders. By bridging computational neuroscience with speech motor control theory, this project aims to establish new paradigms for both assessment technology and mechanism-driven intervention design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate the speaking, language interpretation, and related physiological and cognitive capabilities of children and/or adults and develop treatment and rehabilitative solutions in consultation with clinicians and educators. Includes instruction in the anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing, biomechanics of swallowing and vocal articulation, communications disorders, psychology of auditory function and cognitive communication, language assessment and diagnostic techniques, and rehabilitative and management therapies.

abstract: Military information systems increasingly operate in contested, data-dense environments where rapid decision-making and adaptive security are critical. Current systems struggle to balance real-time data processing, dynamic threat response, and energy efficiency while maintaining compliance with evolving military protocols. This project proposes the development of a novel computational framework for optimizing distributed military command-and-control networks under adversarial conditions, with a focus on latency-sensitive operations in bandwidth-constrained theaters. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will model multi-domain operations (cyber, electronic warfare, and kinetic) through a hybrid approach combining discrete-event simulation, graph-based threat propagation analysis, and reinforcement learning for adaptive resource allocation. Key challenges include simulating tera-scale network topologies with embedded adversarial agents, analyzing emergent vulnerabilities in decentralized communication protocols, and training context-aware algorithms to prioritize mission-critical data flows during partial system compromises. The computational workflow will integrate parallelized Monte Carlo methods for stress-testing network configurations against synthetic adversarial campaigns, while federated learning techniques will enable privacy-preserving collaboration across simulated coalition partner systems. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for (1) predictive load balancing under asymmetric cyber-physical threats, (2) protocol-agnostic anomaly detection in encrypted military traffic, and (3) energy-aware failover strategies for degraded infrastructure environments. By advancing computational methods tailored to military operational constraints, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for resilient information systems that maintain functionality despite sophisticated denial-of-service, spoofing, and infiltration attempts. The HPC component is essential for achieving militarily relevant scale, with preliminary estimates requiring 250,000 core-hours to model theater-level network dynamics across 10^6 node configurations and adversarial scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, design and application of computer and networking technology to the military environment. Includes instruction in planning; program development; graphical user interfaces; rapid prototyping; program construction; data types, operations; control flow; arrays; records; file I/O; database access; event-driven OOP structures; and enabling global-networked communications, including databases, systems analysis and design, decision support systems, and network security.

abstract: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources and distributed storage systems into modern power grids has introduced unprecedented challenges in maintaining dynamic stability and operational efficiency. Existing energy systems engineering frameworks struggle to model the multi-scale, nonlinear interactions between heterogeneous assets—such as solar-wind hybrids, flow batteries, and demand-responsive loads—under rapidly varying grid conditions. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based computational platform to simulate and optimize next-generation hybrid microgrids with embedded resilience mechanisms. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement parallelized multi-agent system simulations that integrate physics-based models of electrochemical storage degradation, weather-dependent renewable generation, and adaptive load management protocols. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, will be embedded within the simulation framework to enable real-time topology optimization and fault response strategies. The computational workflow will employ a hybrid MPI-OpenMP architecture to scale across thousands of concurrent agents, with stochastic optimization routines addressing uncertainties in generation forecasts and load profiles. Validation will utilize real-world data from islanded microgrid deployments in coastal regions, where salinity gradients and tidal patterns introduce unique energy storage synergies. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for resilience-aware microgrid design, quantitative guidelines for balancing distributed energy resource diversity against stability margins, and novel metrics for assessing grid vulnerability to correlated climate stressors. This work directly addresses the critical gap between renewable energy integration targets and operational reliability constraints, providing actionable insights for utilities and policymakers. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the required temporal and spatial resolution in simulating continent-scale propagation of grid disturbances while maintaining computational feasibility for sensitivity analyses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of energy generation, storage, conversion, and distribution systems. Includes instruction in conventional and alternative/renewable energy systems, electrical power systems, and electrical system design.

abstract: The sustainable scaling of microbial bioenergy systems is hindered by inefficiencies in bioprocessing and gaps in understanding how microbial consortia interact dynamically under industrial conditions. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the multi-scale complexity of these systems, which span genetic regulation, metabolic fluxes, and large-scale bioreactor hydrodynamics. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated computational framework that bridges genome-scale metabolic modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and life cycle assessment (LCA) for the optimization of lignocellulosic biofuel production. Using genome-resolved metagenomic data from pilot-scale anaerobic digesters, we will parameterize agent-based models to simulate microbial community responses to fluctuating feedstock compositions and reactor conditions. These models will be coupled with CFD simulations of industrial-scale bioreactors to predict how hydrodynamic stressors and nutrient gradients influence microbial metabolism and overall conversion efficiency. Machine learning techniques will then identify optimal operational parameters and microbial consortia configurations to maximize ethanol yield while minimizing energy inputs. The computational pipeline will further integrate techno-economic and environmental impact assessments to evaluate scalability and sustainability trade-offs. By simulating thousands of design permutations across spatial and temporal scales, this HPC-driven approach will bypass costly iterative experimentation, accelerating the translation of lab-scale findings to commercial applications. Expected outcomes include predictive models of microbial resilience in heterogeneous bioreactor environments, validated strategies for feedstock flexibility, and a publicly accessible database linking microbial traits to process performance metrics. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation biorefineries, advancing the economic viability and ecological sustainability of bioenergy systems within resource-constrained agricultural landscapes.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the environmental and economic impact of using plants and microbes for the production of bio-based fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel. Includes instruction in biochemical engineering, bioprocessing, bioseparations, conversion, feedstock, economics, environmental sustainability, hydrology, and natural resource management.

abstract: The interaction of light with biological systems drives critical processes such as vision, photosynthesis, and circadian rhythm regulation, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these light-induced reactions remain poorly resolved at ultrafast timescales. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the structural and electronic dynamics of photoreceptor proteins and photosynthetic complexes. Specifically, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to investigate photon absorption, energy transfer, and conformational changes in rhodopsin, cryptochromes, and photosystem I. These simulations will resolve femtosecond-to-microsecond dynamics of chromophore-protein interactions, including transient intermediate states inaccessible to experimental techniques. A key focus is elucidating how environmental factors, such as UV exposure or oxidative stress, alter photochemical pathways in retinal proteins, contributing to degenerative eye diseases. The computational workflow integrates spectral data to validate predicted absorption maxima and fluorescence lifetimes against experimental benchmarks. By mapping energy landscapes and electron transfer pathways, this study will identify conserved motifs that optimize light harvesting and signaling efficiency in biological systems. The outcomes will advance the development of targeted phototherapies for ocular disorders and bioengineered light-driven catalysts for sustainable energy applications. The scale of these simulations—involving multi-million-atom systems, long-timescale sampling, and iterative QM/MM optimizations—necessitates HPC resources for parallelized GPU-accelerated computations. Results will be disseminated as open-access trajectory datasets and machine learning-ready force field parameters, providing foundational tools for the photobiology community. This work bridges molecular-scale photophysics to organism-level photoresponses, offering transformative insights into light-driven life processes.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the effects of light energy on living organisms, the manufacture and processing of luminescence by organisms, and the uses of light in biological research. Includes instruction in bioluminescence, chronobiology, photomedicine, environmental photobiology, organic photochemistry, photomorphogenesis, photoreceptors and photosensitization, molecular mechanics of photosynthesis, phototechnology, vision, ultraviolet radiation, radiation physics, and spectral research methods.

abstract: Agricultural production operations face complex challenges in balancing resource efficiency, economic viability, and environmental sustainability under dynamic conditions such as fluctuating market demands, labor availability, and climate variability. Traditional decision-making frameworks often struggle to account for the high dimensionality of these interacting factors, particularly when scaling to regional or multi-enterprise levels. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled optimization platform to model and simulate agricultural production systems, with a focus on integrated crop-livestock operations. The computational framework will leverage agent-based modeling and mixed-integer linear programming to dynamically allocate machinery, labor, water, and financial resources across spatial and temporal scales. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to process real-time data streams from IoT sensors, equipment telemetry, and weather forecasts, enabling adaptive scenario analysis. Key objectives include optimizing planting-harvest schedules under weather uncertainty, minimizing input waste through precision application models, and evaluating capital investment strategies for equipment upgrades. The HPC infrastructure is essential for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of stochastic climate and market scenarios while maintaining sub-daily resolution over multi-year horizons. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for reducing operational costs by 15–20% in benchmark farming systems, a decision-support toolkit for agribusiness planners, and novel metrics for quantifying resilience in production workflows. By advancing computational capabilities in agricultural operations research, this work aims to bridge critical gaps between precision agriculture technologies and whole-farm economic optimization, ultimately strengthening the competitiveness of small-to-medium scale producers in global supply chains.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general planning, economics, and use of facilities, natural resources, equipment, labor, and capital to produce plant and animal products, and that may prepare individuals for work in farming, ranching, and agribusiness.

abstract: The increasing complexity of emergency medical services (EMS) demands innovative approaches to optimize prehospital care delivery. This project addresses a critical gap in emergency care attendant (ECA) operations: real-time, dynamic resource allocation during mass casualty incidents (MCIs) or surge events, where traditional dispatch protocols often fail due to unpredictable patient distributions and resource constraints. We propose developing a machine learning-driven simulation framework to model ambulance routing, ECA skill matching, and equipment utilization under high-stress scenarios. The research problem centers on minimizing time-to-treatment intervals while balancing crew fatigue, equipment availability, and evolving patient acuity levels—a multidimensional challenge requiring high-dimensional optimization. Computational methods will integrate discrete-event simulation with reinforcement learning agents trained on synthetic MCI datasets generated through probabilistic injury progression models. High-performance computing resources are essential for parallelizing thousands of scenario variations, processing real-time geospatial data streams, and training neural networks on emergent triage patterns. Expected outcomes include a predictive decision-support system that adapts to evolving incident landscapes, providing ECAs with optimized patient transport sequences and resource deployment strategies. The model’s significance lies in its potential to reduce preventable mortality through computational anticipation of bottleneck scenarios while maintaining operational feasibility for EMS systems. By focusing on the unique constraints of prehospital emergency care rather than hospital-based interventions, this work occupies an emerging niche at the intersection of operational informatics, emergency medicine, and computational logistics. Successful implementation could establish a new paradigm for data-driven EMS management, directly impacting the 240 million emergency calls annually handled by EMT personnel worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist licensed EMTs, under the supervision of a physician, to prepare and transport ill or injured patients, and to operate emergency vehicles and equipment such as life support units. Includes instruction in first aid and emergency medicine field techniques, patient stabilization and care, medical field communications, equipment operation and maintenance, emergency vehicle operation, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize forklift operation workflows and accident risk prediction in dynamic industrial environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While forklift operation training emphasizes safety protocols and manual skill development, current practices lack data-driven tools to model complex interactions between operators, equipment, and workspaces in real time. The research problem centers on mitigating workplace accidents caused by situational factors such as load instability, blind spots, and multi-agent coordination challenges in high-density storage facilities. Using agent-based modeling and physics-informed machine learning, we will simulate forklift kinematics, load dynamics, and human operator decision-making across diverse warehouse configurations. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to quantify risk probabilities under variable conditions (e.g., uneven terrain, lighting gradients, traffic patterns) while integrating real-world sensor data from IoT-enabled forklifts. Computational models will be validated against empirical accident datasets and biomechanical analyses of operator response times. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive risk heatmaps for facility layout optimization, (2) AI-driven training modules that adapt to operator skill levels, and (3) a digital twin framework for evaluating safety interventions without physical prototyping. By bridging gaps between vocational training paradigms and computational engineering, this work aims to reduce forklift-related injuries by 15-30% in modeled scenarios while informing ISO standards for adaptive safety systems. The project will also establish a novel HPC workflow template for industrial equipment training programs, demonstrating how high-fidelity simulations can augment hands-on technical education in the Technology and Technical Fields domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate forklifts in a variety of work environments. Includes instruction in accident prevention, forklift operation, materials handling, and worksite safety.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cultural perceptions of mental illness, social support networks, and barriers to accessing psychiatric care in cross-cultural contexts. Despite growing global mental health disparities, few studies integrate socio-cultural narratives with behavioral data to model how stigma, community dynamics, and institutional mistrust collectively shape health-seeking trajectories. Our research employs a mixed-methods computational framework to analyze ethnographic interviews, community surveys, and anonymized healthcare utilization records from a multi-year study of refugee populations in urban settings. We propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating decision-making processes related to mental health care access, incorporating culturally specific variables such as stigma thresholds, trust in traditional vs. biomedical systems, and kinship network influence. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for calibrating the ABM’s high-dimensional parameter space using Bayesian optimization techniques and for processing natural language data from interviews through transformer-based NLP models to extract thematic predictors. Parallelized simulations will explore how interventions targeting community education or healthcare provider training might alter emergent care-access patterns across diverse subpopulations. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for reducing structural inequities in mental health service use and generating a transferable methodology for bridging qualitative anthropological data with computational social science approaches. This work directly advances medical anthropology’s capacity to address complex health challenges through scalable, culturally grounded models while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in analyzing humanistic-health systems interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological, socio-cultural, psychological, and behavioral factors as they relate to health, illness, medical practices, and access to health care services. Includes instruction in ethno-medicine, urban health, international health, psychiatric and psychological anthropology, aging, and health and identity.

abstract: This project addresses the pressing need to optimize agroecosystem management by resolving critical knowledge gaps in the multi-scale interactions between crops, soils, microbial communities, and climate variables. Current empirical and modeling approaches struggle to capture the dynamic, nonlinear feedbacks governing nutrient cycling, pest resilience, and crop productivity under climate variability, limiting the design of scalable, context-specific sustainable practices. To overcome these barriers, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and high-resolution climate data assimilation. The ABM will simulate spatially explicit agroecosystem dynamics at the field-to-landscape scale, incorporating microbial metabolic processes, root-soil interactions, and pollinator behavior. ML algorithms will parameterize models using heterogeneous datasets, including multi-omics data from soil microbiomes, remote sensing imagery, and historical yield records. Climate resilience assessments will integrate regional CMIP6 projections to evaluate management strategies under diverse emission scenarios. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing of large-scale simulations and real-time ML training—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources to achieve biologically meaningful spatiotemporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include identifying crop rotation sequences that enhance soil carbon sequestration, optimizing cover crop mixtures for pest suppression and water retention, and quantifying trade-offs between yield stability and input reduction across agroclimatic zones. By bridging molecular-scale processes to landscape-level outcomes, this work will provide actionable insights for farmers and policymakers, advancing the dual goals of climate resilience and food security. The resulting open-source tools will empower stakeholders to simulate site-specific management scenarios, fostering adoption of practices that align ecological integrity with socioeconomic viability. This project thus directly supports the program’s mission to develop agricultural systems that are productive, resource-efficient, and socially equitable.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: This project addresses the growing computational demands of creating immersive, algorithmically generated art installations that integrate real-time interactivity with large-scale 3D visualizations. As digital artists increasingly employ machine learning, fluid dynamics simulations, and photogrammetric data processing in their practice, existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to maintain the low-latency responsiveness required for participatory works or the rendering fidelity needed for architectural-scale projections. The research focuses on developing optimized workflows for simulating organic material behaviors—such as ceramic fracture patterns and textile fluidity—through parallelized finite element analysis running on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. A custom pipeline will be created using MPI-based distributed rendering techniques to process terabyte-scale volumetric datasets captured from traditional sculptural forms, enabling their transformation into responsive digital counterparts. The computational methodology also incorporates generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on art historical corpora to synthesize hybrid aesthetic patterns, requiring multi-GPU nodes for rapid iteration. By allocating dedicated HPC resources, this project aims to overcome current bottlenecks in real-time ray tracing of intricate virtual environments and dynamic texture mapping for site-specific installations. Anticipated outcomes include a suite of containerized tools for artists working with computational geometry, validated benchmarks for GPU-accelerated creative workflows, and a publicly accessible repository of optimized simulation presets for common studio art materials. This work bridges critical gaps between emerging digital art practices and advanced computing infrastructure, empowering artists to explore complex systems and scale-dependent phenomena while establishing best practices for HPC utilization in visual arts research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally function as creative artists in the visual and plastic media. Includes instruction in the traditional fine arts media (drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, CAD/CAM) and/or modern media (ceramics, textiles, intermedia, photography, digital images), theory of art, color theory, composition and perspective, anatomy, the techniques and procedures for maintaining equipment and managing a studio, and art portfolio marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of computational design methodologies within interior architecture, focusing on optimizing human-centric spatial experiences in dynamic built environments. While traditional design processes rely on static models and manual iterations, the increasing complexity of variables—such as real-time occupant behavior data, adaptive environmental systems, and multi-objective sustainability goals—demands advanced computational frameworks. The research addresses the gap in tools capable of simulating hyper-detailed, temporally evolving interior spaces that balance aesthetic, functional, and ecological criteria. Using parametric modeling, agent-based simulations, and machine learning algorithms, the project will develop a scalable computational workflow to analyze and predict spatial performance under variable conditions. Key objectives include simulating occupant movement patterns in response to modular architectural elements, optimizing acoustic and thermal comfort through iterative material configurations, and validating energy-efficient lighting designs via photon-mapping techniques. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of large-scale datasets derived from LiDAR scans, IoT sensor networks, and user biometric feedback, facilitating real-time visualization of multi-dimensional design trade-offs. Expected outcomes include a novel simulation platform that bridges architectural design software with environmental analysis tools, reducing reliance on physical prototyping and accelerating evidence-based decision-making. By establishing a computational foundation for adaptive interior architecture, this research aims to redefine design practices in contexts such as co-working spaces, healthcare environments, and disaster-resilient shelters, where dynamic human-environment interactions are critical. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-source modules to support broader innovation in non-STEM design disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply architectural principles in the design of structural interiors for living, recreational, and business purposes and to function as professional interior architects. Includes instruction in architecture, structural systems design, heating and cooling systems, occupational and safety standards, interior design, specific end-use applications, and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale, interdisciplinary investigation of African-American and Black diaspora cultural production through computational textual and spatial analysis. The research addresses the challenge of synthesizing fragmented and understudied historical and literary archives—spanning the United States, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America—to trace transnational narratives of resistance, identity formation, and cultural exchange across three centuries. Traditional methodologies struggle to systematically analyze the scale and linguistic diversity of these materials, which include slave narratives, abolitionist writings, mid-20th-century political essays, and contemporary literature, alongside oral histories and ephemera from marginalized communities. By employing natural language processing (NLP) techniques—including transformer-based models for multilingual text classification, dynamic topic modeling, and sentiment analysis—this project will identify thematic continuities and disruptions within and across regions. Geospatial machine learning will map the diffusion of cultural motifs and migration patterns, while network analysis will reconstruct intellectual and artistic collaborations obscured by historical silences. Computational demands include processing terabytes of unstructured text, audio-to-text conversions of oral archives, and training custom models to recognize dialectical variations and period-specific vernacular. HPC resources are critical for managing parallelized workflows, reducing latency in iterative model training, and storing intermediate datasets. Anticipated outcomes include a public-facing digital repository with interactive visualizations of diasporic cultural flows, scholarly articles reinterpreting Black transnationalism through computational lenses, and open-source tools for humanities researchers working with underrepresented archives. This project bridges computational and humanistic inquiry, offering new methodologies to amplify marginalized voices while preserving the interpretive nuance central to African-American studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of sustainable, resilient construction materials and structural systems through high-fidelity computational modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in construction engineering: the inability to efficiently simulate multi-physical interactions (e.g., thermal, mechanical, and chemical processes) in novel materials like carbon-cured concrete and bio-based composites under real-world environmental stressors. Current models oversimplify time-dependent material degradation and fail to account for spatially variable site conditions, limiting their utility for infrastructure projects in climate-vulnerable regions. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), discrete element method (DEM), and machine learning (ML) surrogate models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of material behavior across atomic, meso-, and macro-structural scales, coupled with probabilistic climate impact scenarios. The workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for DEM-FEA hybrid simulations of crack propagation in heterogeneous materials and train graph neural networks on simulated datasets to predict long-term durability. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source computational toolkit for optimizing material compositions and structural designs under site-specific constraints, (2) probabilistic maps of infrastructure degradation risks for coastal urban areas, and (3) validated guidelines for bio-composite material use in high-humidity environments. By enabling precise modeling of material-environment interactions at unprecedented scales, this work will directly inform climate-adaptive construction standards and reduce trial-and-error prototyping costs for sustainable infrastructure projects. The requested HPC allocation will support 18 months of simulations encompassing 50+ material variants and 10,000+ coupled physical scenarios, requiring ~2.5 million core-hours for multi-physics modeling and ML training on terabyte-scale datasets.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and management principles to the planning, design, and building of facilities and structures. Includes instruction in civil engineering, structural principles, site analysis, computer-assisted design, geology, evaluation and testing, materials, contracting, project management, graphic communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Counseling and applied psychology face pressing challenges in understanding the dynamic, multilevel factors influencing therapeutic outcomes across diverse populations. This project seeks to address the gap in scalable, personalized intervention strategies by leveraging advanced computational modeling to analyze high-dimensional data from real-world counseling settings. The research problem centers on identifying nonlinear interactions between client characteristics (e.g., cultural background, coping styles), counselor techniques, and contextual variables (e.g., session frequency, community resources) that predict resilience-building outcomes in brief interventions. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets from school-based and community mental health programs (N ≈ 50,000 cases), we will implement machine learning architectures—including recurrent neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees—to model temporal patterns in therapeutic progress while accounting for hierarchical data structures. High-performance computing resources are critical for training these models on multimodal features (linguistic markers from session transcripts, demographic covariates, and ecological momentary assessment data) and conducting counterfactual simulations of intervention scenarios. The computational approach will extend current methods by implementing a novel hybrid framework combining interpretable AI techniques with multilevel survival analysis, enabling both prediction accuracy and clinical interpretability. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model identifying optimal intervention timing and component sequencing for distinct client profiles, and (2) open-source tools for simulating resource allocation tradeoffs in community mental health systems. This work will advance applied psychology research by enabling data-driven personalization of counseling strategies while maintaining ethical rigor through embedded fairness-aware algorithms. The requested computing resources will directly support 8,000+ GPU hours for model training and 200TB of secure data processing capacity, facilitating translational insights to improve equity in mental health service delivery.
cip_title: Clinical, Counseling and Applied Psychology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical, counseling and applied psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Wilderness medicine addresses critical challenges in delivering healthcare under environmental stressors with limited resources, such as extreme temperatures, altitude, or isolation. A significant gap exists in predicting patient deterioration or optimizing interventions in these dynamic settings, where environmental factors directly interact with physiological responses. This project proposes to develop computational models of human physiology under environmental stress to simulate clinical scenarios, predict outcomes, and inform evidence-based protocols for austere care. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the complexity of these models, which integrate real-world environmental data, multi-scale physiological systems, and stochastic resource constraints. The research will first aggregate and analyze existing clinical datasets from wilderness and disaster settings to identify key variables influencing outcomes. Agent-based modeling and finite element analysis will then simulate interactions between environmental parameters (e.g., hypothermia, hypoxia) and patient-specific factors (e.g., comorbidities, injuries). Machine learning approaches will optimize model accuracy by training on outcomes from field case reports and controlled experimental data. Finally, Monte Carlo methods will evaluate the robustness of proposed treatment strategies across variable resource availability and environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide triage, intervention timing, and resource allocation in austere environments, as well as generalized frameworks for adapting clinical guidelines to novel environmental insults. This work will directly support the development of scalable, context-specific protocols for wilderness medicine practitioners, from prehospital providers to disaster response teams. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process high-dimensional data and run computationally intensive simulations, the project aims to reduce preventable morbidity in resource-limited settings while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of clinical medicine and environmental systems modeling.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine with limited resources in austere environments or to provide healthcare anywhere in which environmental conditions have physiologic insult to a patient.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for efficient, high-quality live broadcasting in dynamic environments by developing adaptive, AI-driven workflows for real-time multimedia production. Traditional broadcasting systems face challenges in managing unpredictable variables such as network latency, fluctuating bandwidth, and heterogeneous viewer device capabilities, particularly during large-scale live events. To overcome these limitations, this research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and optimize multi-camera production pipelines, real-time compression algorithms, and adaptive streaming protocols. Computational methods will include parallelized neural networks for automated scene composition and object tracking, Monte Carlo simulations to model network congestion scenarios, and GPU-accelerated encoding/decoding trials across diverse resolution and bitrate combinations. The project will utilize existing broadcast datasets alongside synthetically generated content to train models under variable conditions. Key outcomes will include a framework for intelligent resource allocation in cloud-based production environments, improved error resilience for 4K/8K streaming, and data-driven recommendations for balancing computational overhead with quality-of-service targets. By enabling more robust and scalable broadcasting systems, this work aims to directly benefit educational media programs, local broadcasters adapting to IP-based infrastructure, and content creators operating in bandwidth-constrained regions. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of audiovisual training data, running real-time multi-stream simulations, and validating models against industry-standard quality metrics (e.g., PSNR, VMAF) at production-scale parameters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of radio and television programs, and related operations, under the supervision of broadcast and studio managers, directors, editors, and producers. Includes instruction in sound, lighting, and camera operation and maintenance; power and feed control; studio operations; production preparation; broadcast engineering; related computer applications; and specialized applications such as news, entertainment, live talk, sports, commercials, and taping.

abstract: In the commercial poultry industry, infectious diseases pose significant threats to animal welfare, economic stability, and food security. Current approaches to disease management often lack the capacity to model complex, large-scale interactions among pathogens, host populations, and environmental factors, leading to suboptimal intervention strategies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that enhance understanding of disease dynamics and inform targeted mitigation efforts. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) constructing agent-based models to simulate disease transmission within and between poultry flocks under varying management practices; (2) applying machine learning algorithms to integrate multi-omic data (genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic) with epidemiological surveillance data, enabling predictive analytics for outbreak risk; and (3) employing phylodynamic analyses to trace pathogen evolution and spread across geographic regions. By utilizing HPC capabilities, these models will process vast datasets encompassing genetic diversity of poultry populations, pathogen genomic sequences, and real-time environmental variables, which are computationally infeasible with traditional infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of genetic markers associated with disease resistance, predictive tools for preemptive biosecurity measures, and optimized vaccination protocols tailored to regional pathogen strains. The integration of computational epidemiology with poultry health research will provide a transformative framework for reducing antimicrobial use, minimizing production losses, and improving the sustainability of global poultry systems. This project underscores the critical role of HPC in advancing veterinary clinical research and fostering resilience in agri-food industries.
cip_definition: Research focused on the commercial poultry industry, providing services and technical support pertaining to prevention, diagnosis, and management of disease; epidemiology; genetics; and nutrition.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the complex interplay between oral microbiomes and systemic health conditions, such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Despite emerging evidence linking dysbiosis in oral microbial communities to systemic inflammation and chronic diseases, large-scale computational analyses required to unravel these relationships remain limited in dental research. The project will analyze multi-omic datasets—including metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metabolomic data—from longitudinal clinical cohorts of patients with periodontal disease and comorbid systemic conditions. Advanced bioinformatics pipelines will be implemented to characterize microbial diversity, functional pathways, and host-microbe interactions, while machine learning models will identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression. HPC resources are critical for handling the volume and complexity of these datasets, enabling parallel processing of sequencing data, high-dimensional statistical modeling, and iterative training of deep neural networks. Expected outcomes include the discovery of microbial signatures associated with elevated systemic disease risk, mechanistic insights into oral-systemic health connections, and the development of computational tools for early intervention strategies. By integrating computational biology with clinical dental research, this work aims to advance personalized diagnostic and therapeutic approaches, ultimately improving interdisciplinary care paradigms in dental and general health practice. The requested resources will also support the creation of open-access databases and analytical frameworks to benefit future studies in dental services and allied health fields.
cip_title: Dental Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dental services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing chemical reactor design for multi-phase catalytic processes, a cornerstone of industrial applications in pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals, and sustainable energy systems. Traditional empirical models often fail to predict complex interactions between fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and reaction kinetics at scale, leading to suboptimal reactor performance, energy inefficiencies, and elevated emissions. To overcome these limitations, this project will develop a high-fidelity computational framework integrating multi-scale simulations with machine learning (ML) to model and optimize reactor behavior under dynamic operating conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatially and temporally varying phenomena, such as turbulent flow patterns in packed-bed reactors or transient catalyst deactivation in fluidized systems, which require parallelized solving of coupled partial differential equations across millions of grid points. The computational approach will combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for surface reaction mechanisms, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for macro-scale transport processes, and graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on simulation data to predict optimal operating parameters. Key deliverables include an open-source software package for reactor optimization and a validated database of multi-phase reactor simulations spanning diverse industrial conditions. Expected outcomes include identifying novel reactor configurations that reduce energy consumption by 15–20% in benchmark catalytic cracking processes and providing actionable strategies to mitigate fouling in polymerization reactors. By leveraging HPC resources, this work will enable unprecedented resolution of micro-scale catalyst-fluid interactions while maintaining feasibility for plant-scale simulations, directly addressing scalability gaps in existing models. The results will advance sustainable process intensification and support the chemical industry’s transition to low-carbon operations, with broader implications for computational science in multi-physics system optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of chemical processing equipment in industries such as chemical manufacturing, petroleum refining, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and waste water treatment. Includes instruction in mathematics, chemistry, and physics; computer applications; chemical and refinery plant operations, processes, and equipment; safety, health, and environment; instrumentation; troubleshooting; and applications to specific industries.

abstract: Polarity Therapy, an integrative therapeutic system rooted in Human Energy Field (HEF) theory, posits that health outcomes are influenced by dynamic interactions between bioenergetic patterns and physiological processes. Despite its clinical use, the mechanistic basis of Polarity Therapy remains poorly characterized, limiting its integration into evidence-based healthcare frameworks. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational model to simulate HEF dynamics and quantify their relationship to observable biological states. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct a multiscale biophysical model integrating electromagnetic field simulations with physiological datasets (e.g., heart rate variability, cytokine profiles, EEG patterns) from a longitudinal clinical study of Polarity Therapy interventions. Computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis will be applied to simulate energy flow patterns theorized in Polarity bodywork, while machine learning algorithms will identify correlations between simulated HEF perturbations, therapeutic interventions (e.g., polarity yoga, energetic nutrition), and multi-omics data from patient biospecimens. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high dimensionality of spatiotemporal energy field data, running parallelized simulations of HEF-physiology coupling, and training predictive models on heterogeneous datasets (clinical, biophysical, and molecular). Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework mapping HEF modifications to measurable health biomarkers, (2) predictive models for optimizing polarity-based interventions in chronic stress-related conditions, and (3) open-source tools for quantifying energy field parameters in therapeutic settings. This work will provide the first computational evidence base for Polarity Therapy’s bioenergetic mechanisms, advancing its scientific credibility and enabling personalized energy medicine approaches. The project establishes a paradigm for interdisciplinary research bridging energy medicine, systems biology, and HPC-driven computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote health and well-being through application of the integrative therapeutic system based on the Human Energy Field theory developed by Randolph Stone. Includes instruction in polarity theory and principles, energy-based and orthodox anatomy and physiology, polarity processing, polarity bodywork, polarity yoga, energetic nutrition, energetic evaluation and assessment, client communication, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The management of complex cardiopulmonary diseases requires precise, patient-specific approaches to optimize therapeutic outcomes. Current clinical practices often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for individual variations in cardiopulmonary dynamics, leading to suboptimal treatment efficacy. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework that integrates multi-modal patient data—including high-resolution imaging, hemodynamic parameters, and gas exchange metrics—to simulate and predict personalized therapeutic responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct multi-scale models combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate blood flow and respiratory mechanics with machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data. These models aim to identify optimal ventilator settings, pharmacological interventions, and rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual pathophysiological profiles. The computational demands of processing 4D imaging datasets, real-time sensor inputs, and performing ensemble simulations necessitate distributed-memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated computations, which are only feasible with HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and congestive heart failure management, demonstrating ≥15% improvement in treatment response prediction accuracy compared to standard protocols. By establishing a bridge between computational biomechanics and clinical decision-making, this research will provide a foundation for data-driven precision medicine in cardiopulmonary care, potentially reducing ICU stays and healthcare costs through optimized interventions. The proposed HPC allocation will directly support the development of open-source tools for clinical researchers, fostering broader adoption of computational methods in allied health specialties.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to perform both cardiovascular and pulmonary diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Includes instruction in cardiopulmonary pharmacology; anatomy and physiology of the heart, peripheral vascular system, and lungs; pulmonary and cardiovascular disease and dysfunction; peripheral vascular Doppler procedures; invasive and non-invasive cardiology; pulmonary function tests; blood gas analysis; echocardiograph procedures; bronchoscopy; patient management; patient history taking and record-keeping; applications to clinical research; and emergency procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance geography education by developing data-driven computational models to analyze and predict the effectiveness of pedagogical strategies for teaching geospatial technologies (GSTs) in K-12 classrooms. Despite the growing importance of GSTs—such as geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and spatial analysis—in addressing societal challenges, many educators lack training in both GST implementation and evidence-based methods for teaching spatial reasoning. Existing research on GST pedagogy is limited by small sample sizes and a lack of granular spatial-temporal data on student engagement and skill acquisition. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating anonymized student performance datasets, geospatial classroom interaction logs, and teacher training records from 200+ U.S. school districts. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to 1) process multi-terabyte geospatial education datasets using parallelized data pipelines, 2) train machine learning models to identify patterns in spatial skill development across diverse demographic groups, and 3) simulate classroom-scale knowledge transfer dynamics through agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will combine spatial statistics, natural language processing of open-response assessments, and network analysis of concept mastery pathways. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for optimizing GST curriculum sequencing, evidence-based recommendations for differentiated spatial pedagogy, and predictive models of technology integration barriers in under-resourced schools. By leveraging HPC capabilities to analyze education datasets at unprecedented scale and resolution, this work will provide actionable insights for teacher preparation programs while advancing computational methods in geography education research. The results will directly inform the development of a national GST teaching competency framework and adaptive learning tools for pre-service geography educators.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Thai philology and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in large-scale linguistic and textual studies of pre-modern and modern Thai languages. The primary research problem centers on the lack of comprehensive, data-driven analyses of Thai linguistic evolution, dialectal variation, and literary patterns across historical periods, particularly due to the computational challenges posed by the complexity of Thai script, non-Latin orthography, and the scarcity of digitized corpora. To address this, the project will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to Thai morphology and syntax, enabling the automated parsing, annotation, and comparative analysis of a curated corpus spanning 15th-century Sukhothai inscriptions, 19th-century Rattanakosin literature, and contemporary regional dialects. Computational methods will include transformer-based models for semantic role labeling, graph-based algorithms for dialectometric mapping, and phylogenetic tools to model language change. The HPC infrastructure will facilitate training domain-specific language models on GPU clusters, processing multi-terabyte text datasets, and running Monte Carlo simulations to assess historical linguistic hypotheses. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative typology of Thai dialect boundaries, a diachronic dataset linking literary forms to sociocultural shifts, and open-access tools for Thai corpus linguistics. This work will significantly enhance scholarly capacity to analyze Thai language history at unprecedented scales while preserving endangered dialectal data. Results will directly inform curriculum development in Thai studies and provide methodological frameworks applicable to other non-Latin script languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Thai languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of data across scientific and industrial domains necessitate advanced computational strategies to enable efficient processing, transformation, and analysis. This project seeks to address critical bottlenecks in large-scale data processing workflows, particularly those involving heterogeneous datasets, real-time transformations, and high-dimensional feature extraction. Traditional single-node systems and conventional databases often fail to meet the performance demands of modern applications, such as genomic sequence alignment, sensor network analytics, or dynamic financial modeling, where latency, scalability, and iterative processing are paramount. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development and optimization of parallelized data processing pipelines leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The computational approach integrates distributed computing frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark, Dask) with GPU-accelerated libraries for tasks like dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, and graph-based data traversal. Custom algorithms will be implemented to optimize resource utilization during multi-stage workflows, including adaptive load balancing for irregular data distributions and in-memory caching strategies to minimize I/O overhead. The project will benchmark performance against industry-standard datasets and synthetic workloads simulating terabyte-scale inputs with non-uniform access patterns. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for HPC-optimized data transformation, validated through case studies in climate modeling and biomedical signal processing. By reducing processing latency by an estimated 40-60% compared to existing cloud-based solutions, this work aims to democratize access to high-efficiency data manipulation for resource-constrained research teams. Additionally, the project will generate best-practice guidelines for configuring HPC environments to support diverse data processing workloads, addressing gaps in current technical training frameworks. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and modular code repositories to foster collaboration across the data-intensive research community.
cip_title: Data Processing and Data Processing Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master and use computer software programs and applications for inputting, verifying, organizing, storing, retrieving, transforming (changing, updating, and deleting), and extracting information. Includes instruction in using various operating system configurations and in types of data entry such as word processing, spreadsheets, calculators, management programs, design programs, database programs, and research programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision health strategies for metabolic disorders through the integration of multi-omics data and dynamic computational modeling. The research addresses the challenge of predicting individualized metabolic responses to dietary interventions, a problem complicated by the interplay of genomic, proteomic, and gut microbiome variability. Current approaches often rely on population-level correlations, which fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between host physiology, microbial metabolism, and nutrient bioavailability. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining genome-scale metabolic modeling of human tissues and microbial communities with machine learning-driven analysis of longitudinal multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and proteomic). HPC resources will enable the parallelized simulation of thousands of personalized metabolic networks, each parameterized by individual-specific genomic variants, microbiome composition, and clinical biomarkers. These simulations will be coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify optimal dietary patterns that stabilize glucose metabolism and minimize inflammatory responses in silico. Validation will utilize existing cohort data from clinical studies on prediabetes and obesity, with iterative model refinement based on observed physiological outcomes. The expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational platform for predicting patient-specific nutritional interventions, (2) novel biomarkers linking microbial metabolic pathways to host insulin sensitivity, and (3) open-access tools for simulating diet-microbiome-host interactions. By elucidating mechanistic links between microbial ecology and metabolic health, this work aims to establish a foundation for computationally guided precision nutrition—a critical need in allied health practice, where dietitians and clinicians currently lack robust tools to personalize dietary recommendations at the systems biology level. The proposed HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of models integrating trillion-variable microbiome datasets with host metabolic simulations.
cip_title: Health Services/ Allied Health/ Health Sciences, General
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health services occupations that prepares individuals for either entry into specialized training programs or for a variety of concentrations in the allied health area. Includes instruction in the basic sciences, research and clinical procedures, and aspects of the subject matter related to various health occupations.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize next-generation telecommunications network infrastructure investments by integrating dynamic business, regulatory, and technological variables into a unified computational framework. Telecommunications operators face escalating complexity in allocating capital amid rapid 5G/6G deployments, edge computing expansion, IoT proliferation, and evolving cybersecurity regulations. Traditional cost-benefit analyses often fail to capture nonlinear interactions between technical performance metrics, jurisdictional policy constraints, and emerging cyber-risk landscapes, resulting in suboptimal resource allocation. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation environment that models multi-stakeholder decision pathways under uncertainty. The system will combine agent-based modeling of infrastructure deployment scenarios with machine learning-driven predictive analytics for cybersecurity threat evolution and regulatory change impacts. Large-scale optimization algorithms will evaluate trade-offs between network performance metrics (latency, bandwidth), capital expenditure patterns, and compliance risks across heterogeneous geographic markets. Computational experiments will leverage real-world datasets spanning network topology maps, historical cyberattack patterns, and international telecommunications policy frameworks. The HPC environment is critical for processing petabyte-scale network simulations while maintaining the temporal resolution required to model real-time adaptive strategies for infrastructure hardening and spectrum allocation. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit enabling telecom managers to quantify risk-adjusted returns for infrastructure investments under diverse technological adoption curves and regulatory regimes. This research advances telecommunications management practice by establishing quantitative links between technical network parameters, business sustainability metrics, and policy compliance frameworks—a novel integration currently absent in operational planning tools. Results will inform both corporate investment strategies and public-sector infrastructure policy formulation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business skills to design, implement, and manage the voice, video, and data networking systems of organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications concepts and technologies, network operations and management, wireless communications and mobile computing, cybersecurity, regulation and public policy, business practices and management, and written and oral communications.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in tourism ecosystems under climate volatility and shifting traveler preferences. The tourism industry faces unprecedented challenges due to increasing frequency of extreme weather events, evolving sustainability expectations, and demand volatility for destination services. Traditional linear models fail to capture the complex interdependencies between environmental factors, infrastructure capacity, and multi-agent decision-making by travelers, businesses, and regulators. We propose an adaptive simulation platform combining agent-based modeling, climate impact forecasting, and reinforcement learning to enable real-time optimization of tourism resource networks. High-performance computing resources will be critical for executing parallelized simulations that integrate heterogeneous data streams—including climate projections, social media sentiment analysis, transportation network topologies, and accommodation capacity metrics—across multiple temporal and spatial scales. The computational architecture will employ graph neural networks to model destination resilience thresholds and deep reinforcement learning agents to test adaptive pricing, routing, and capacity management strategies. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of forecasting critical pressure points in tourism value chains (e.g., transportation bottlenecks during climate disruptions) and recommending preemptive resource reallocations. This work advances tourism management research by introducing a novel computational paradigm that bridges operations research, climate science, and behavioral economics—enabling quantitative analysis of emergent phenomena in complex tourism systems. Successful implementation could reduce economic losses from climate-related disruptions by 15-30% in simulated scenarios while maintaining service quality benchmarks, providing actionable insights for destination management organizations and policymakers invested in sustainable tourism development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage travel-related enterprises and related convention and/or tour services. Includes instruction in travel agency management, tour arranging and planning, convention and event planning, travel industry operations and procedures, tourism marketing and promotion strategies, travel counseling, travel industry law, international and domestic operations, and travel and tourism policy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational limitations inherent in creating dynamic, large-scale generative art and design systems that integrate real-time data streams and high-resolution interactive media. Current tools for computational design and digital artistry struggle to synthesize complex, evolving visual forms at the scale required for immersive installations or data-driven public artworks, particularly when processing inputs from heterogeneous sources such as environmental sensors, social media feeds, or high-dimensional user interactions. To overcome these constraints, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable framework for real-time generative design. The computational approach combines GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines with machine learning models—including transformer-based architectures and diffusion models—to process multi-modal datasets and generate high-fidelity visual outputs. Parallelized workflows will enable simultaneous training of generative algorithms on curated artistic datasets while deploying inference engines for interactive applications, such as site-specific installations responsive to live environmental or participatory data. The project’s outcomes aim to advance computational design methodologies by establishing protocols for HPC-augmented creative practice, enabling artists to prototype complex systems beyond the reach of consumer-grade hardware. Anticipated contributions include open-source tools for distributed rendering of generative visual media, a case study analyzing the aesthetic implications of latency reduction in interactive art, and a publicly exhibited installation demonstrating real-time synthesis of ecological data into large-scale projection mapping. By bridging computational scalability with artistic innovation, this work will expand the technical and conceptual frontiers of applied digital arts while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between HPC research and creative practice.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in design and applied arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy efficiency and guest experience in smart hotel environments, addressing the hospitality industry’s urgent need to balance sustainability goals with service quality. While energy management systems in hospitality settings are increasingly data-driven, existing approaches lack the capacity to integrate real-time sensor data, weather forecasts, and dynamic occupancy patterns at scale. The research problem centers on designing adaptive algorithms that minimize energy consumption in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems without compromising guest comfort—a challenge requiring high-resolution simulations of thermal dynamics, occupant behavior, and operational constraints. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on multi-modal datasets (including IoT sensor streams, reservation logs, and environmental reports) and run parallelized simulations of energy use scenarios across diverse hotel layouts and climatic conditions. Methods include reinforcement learning to optimize HVAC control policies, agent-based modeling to predict guest movement patterns, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in demand forecasts. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that recommends real-time energy adjustments while maintaining predefined comfort thresholds, validated against historical data from partner hotels. This work aims to reduce hospitality sector carbon footprints by an estimated 15–20% in simulated environments, with broader implications for resource allocation in service industries where operational efficiency intersects with customer satisfaction. The computational intensity of modeling fine-grained spatial-temporal interactions necessitates HPC capabilities, particularly for GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale parameter optimization. By bridging hospitality management, building science, and computational sustainability, this project advances an emerging niche in data-driven service operations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in hospitality service management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Mammography positioning accuracy is critical for diagnostic efficacy but remains challenging due to anatomical variability and subjective technologist judgment. Suboptimal positioning contributes to reduced image quality, increased recall rates, and delayed cancer detection. This project proposes developing a high-fidelity computational framework to model tissue deformation and X-ray attenuation patterns during breast compression—a process poorly characterized by existing empirical guidelines. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will implement finite element models simulating biomechanical interactions between compression paddles and heterogeneous breast tissues across diverse morphologies (density, size, mobility). Monte Carlo methods will then simulate X-ray transport through modeled geometries to quantify the impact of positioning on lesion conspicuity. A convolutional neural network will be trained on synthetic images to predict optimal paddle angulation and compression force thresholds for maximizing tumor signal-to-noise ratios while minimizing patient discomfort. The workflow requires parallelized computation of >10,000 biomechanical simulations across parameter spaces (compression angles, forces, breast density distributions) and GPU-accelerated image synthesis. Successful validation against clinical mammograms (retrospective dataset: n=1,200 cases) will establish the first predictive system for personalized positioning recommendations.
