Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool to enhance technologist training through scenario-based simulations, objective quality metrics for compression adequacy, and evidence-based refinements to mammography protocols. This interdisciplinary integration of computational biomechanics, radiation physics, and imaging science addresses a critical gap in radiographer education and breast imaging optimization, with potential to reduce diagnostic ambiguities in early-stage cancer detection.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered radiographers to become registered mammographers. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, mammography instrumentation, mammography positioning, principles and procedures of mammography, and quality assurance.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the atomic-scale mechanisms governing ion transport and interfacial stability in next-generation solid-state electrolytes for energy storage applications. Solid-state batteries promise transformative improvements in energy density and safety compared to conventional liquid electrolyte systems. However, their practical deployment is hindered by poorly understood limitations, including sluggish ion mobility across heterogeneous interfaces and mechanical degradation during cycling. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve the dynamic, nanoscale processes underlying these phenomena. We propose a multiscale computational framework combining density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning-accelerated potential models to systematically evaluate ion diffusion kinetics, phase stability, and defect interactions in lithium- and sodium-based solid electrolytes. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations to realistic system sizes (>100,000 atoms) and timescales (microseconds), enabling direct comparison with operando characterization data. Key objectives include mapping cation transport pathways under mechanical strain, quantifying the role of grain boundary chemistry on interfacial resistance, and predicting thermodynamically stable electrode-electrolyte combinations. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-optimized codes (VASP, LAMMPS) and custom analysis pipelines to process terabytes of trajectory data, extracting descriptors for microstructure-property relationships. Expected outcomes include predictive models for electrolyte performance under operational stressors and design rules for interface engineering. By bridging atomic-scale insights with mesoscale microstructural evolution, this work aims to accelerate the development of durable, high-conductivity solid electrolytes, directly supporting national priorities in sustainable energy infrastructure. The requested resources will enable 15M core-hours for ensemble simulations across multiple material systems, with dedicated GPU nodes for training neural network potentials on quantum-mechanical datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical and scientific principles to the analysis and evaluation of the characteristics and behavior of solids, including internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, compound materials, and research on industrial applications of specific materials.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale digital communication data and optimize strategic messaging frameworks for organizational crisis response. As digital platforms generate vast, dynamic datasets during crises—ranging from social media discourse to real-time news cycles—traditional analytical tools struggle to process these inputs efficiently. This creates gaps in identifying emerging narratives, predicting misinformation spread, and tailoring rapid, audience-specific responses. The research addresses this problem by developing computational models to map communication networks, simulate message diffusion patterns, and evaluate the effectiveness of crisis communication strategies across diverse media ecosystems. Methods include natural language processing (NLP) to classify sentiment and thematic clusters in public discourse, machine learning algorithms to forecast misinformation trajectories, and agent-based modeling to test stakeholder engagement scenarios. These approaches require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train deep learning models on multimodal data (text, video metadata, platform analytics), and run parallelized simulations of communication cascades. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for real-time crisis communication monitoring, evidence-based guidelines for preemptive message design, and open-source tools to visualize stakeholder influence networks. By integrating computational social science methods with communication management theory, this project aims to advance strategic communication practices while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in non-STEM fields. The results will directly benefit organizations navigating complex information environments, from public health agencies to corporate entities, by enhancing their capacity to mitigate reputational risks and align crisis messaging with empirically observed audience behaviors.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the critical thinking, analysis, and practical skills essential to developing and implementing communication strategies that advance organizations goals and missions. Includes instruction in communication management, crisis communication, communications law, digital and traditional marketing strategies, media relations, social media strategies, strategic communication, traditional and emerging media, and writing for the media.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges in analyzing syntactic and semantic evolution across premodern and modern East Asian literary texts, with a focus on under-resourced dialects and classical languages. Traditional methods in philology and comparative linguistics are limited in scalability when applied to large, heterogeneous corpora spanning multiple centuries. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement natural language processing (NLP) pipelines and deep learning models. The research will process digitized texts in Classical Chinese, Middle Korean, and early modern Japanese variants, employing transformer-based architectures for unsupervised syntactic parsing and semantic role labeling. These models will be trained to identify diachronic shifts in grammatical structures and lexical usage, correlating them with sociohistorical contexts. The scale of the corpus—over 10 million tokens across diverse genres—necessitates parallelized processing and distributed training protocols achievable only through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the development of open-access computational tools tailored for historical East Asian languages, a multilingual dataset annotated with syntactic and semantic features, and new insights into language contact phenomena in premodern East Asia. By enabling large-scale, data-driven analysis, this project aims to bridge computational linguistics with area studies, fostering interdisciplinary collaborations and enhancing the visibility of East Asian linguistic heritage in digital humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: East Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in East Asian languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems, such as power grids, transportation networks, and communication systems, face escalating threats from adversarial cyber-physical attacks and cascading failures exacerbated by interdependencies. Current risk assessment models often oversimplify these interdependencies or lack the computational capacity to simulate large-scale, dynamic scenarios, limiting their utility in real-world mitigation planning. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model and analyze multi-sector infrastructure vulnerabilities under hybrid cyber-physical threat scenarios. The research will integrate agent-based modeling, network dynamics simulations, and machine learning techniques to capture the nonlinear interactions between physical infrastructure components, cyber control systems, and human operator responses. Computational workflows will simulate coordinated attacks on interdependent systems, incorporating stochastic threat vectors, adaptive adversary behaviors, and cascading failure pathways. The HPC environment will enable parallelized scenario testing across thousands of parameter combinations, including climate stressors, infrastructure age profiles, and regional interdependency configurations. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for quantifying systemic risks, identifying critical failure cascades, and evaluating the resilience of redundancy configurations. The project will also produce AI-driven threat detection modules capable of processing real-time operational data streams from supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems. By leveraging HPC resources to overcome scale limitations in existing methods, this work aims to advance evidence-based infrastructure protection strategies, providing policymakers and operators with actionable insights for hardening nationally significant assets. The resulting computational framework will be adaptable to emerging threat landscapes and support the development of standardized resilience metrics for cross-sector infrastructure governance.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial equipment and the critical need to minimize unplanned downtime in heavy machinery operations necessitate advanced predictive maintenance frameworks. Current methodologies often rely on simplified analytical models or limited sensor data, which struggle to account for the multi-physics interactions, material degradation patterns, and operational variability inherent to industrial environments. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate equipment degradation mechanisms and optimize maintenance schedules using high-performance computing (HPC). The research will integrate sensor-derived operational data with multiphysics simulations—including finite element analysis for structural stress, computational fluid dynamics for thermal and hydraulic systems, and tribological modeling for wear prediction—to create a holistic digital twin of heavy industrial equipment. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to identify failure precursors from heterogeneous datasets spanning vibration, thermal, and lubrication metrics. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, real-time Bayesian inference for probabilistic failure forecasting, and iterative optimization of maintenance protocols under diverse operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable predictive maintenance platform capable of reducing equipment downtime by 20–30%, extending component lifespans through optimized lubrication and load management, and providing actionable insights for resource allocation in maintenance workflows. This work will establish a novel paradigm for data-driven decision-making in industrial maintenance, directly contributing to operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability in sectors reliant on heavy machinery. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the required computational granularity and temporal resolution to resolve complex failure modes while maintaining practical scalability for industry adoption.
cip_title: Heavy/ Industrial Equipment Maintenance Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in heavy or industrial equipment maintenance technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of multiscale interactions between cloud microphysics and atmospheric turbulence, a critical gap in current models of convective storm dynamics. Despite improvements in numerical weather prediction, the coupling of turbulence-driven updraft processes with cloud droplet formation and precipitation remains poorly resolved, leading to uncertainties in extreme weather forecasts and climate projections. We propose high-resolution large eddy simulations (LES) using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model, enhanced with a Lagrangian particle-based microphysics scheme, to explicitly resolve turbulent eddies at sub-10-meter scales while tracking individual hydrometeor growth. The simulations will target supercell thunderstorm environments, where misrepresentation of turbulent entrainment frequently skews hail and precipitation forecasts. Computational demands necessitate sustained access to high-performance computing resources for ensembles of 10^4-core simulations, each requiring ~2 million CPU-hours to resolve 5-meter grid spacing over 100 km^3 domains with 10^8 Lagrangian particles. Memory-intensive workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated data reduction to manage 500 TB of 4D output per ensemble. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of turbulence-microphysics feedbacks influencing storm longevity, (2) improved parameterizations for entrainment-driven hydrometeor redistribution in mesoscale models, and (3) open-source release of optimized LES code adaptations. By bridging the scale gap between cloud-resolving and operational models, this work directly addresses priorities in atmospheric predictability research while providing foundational datasets for cross-scale model evaluation. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution of stochastic turbulence impacts on precipitation pathways, with applications ranging from short-term hazardous weather forecasting to climate-scale convective representation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the processes governing the interactions, movement, and behavior of atmospheric phenomena and related terrestrial and solar phenomena. Includes instruction in cloud and precipitation physics, solar radiation transfer, active and passive remote sensing, atmospheric electricity and acoustics, atmospheric wave phenomena, turbulence and boundary layers, solar wind, geomagnetic storms, coupling, natural plasma, and energization.

abstract: This project seeks to advance welding process optimization through high-fidelity computational modeling of thermal, mechanical, and metallurgical phenomena in fusion-based welding. The research problem centers on minimizing defects such as porosity, residual stress, and microstructural heterogeneity in steel and aluminum welds—issues that lead to structural failures in critical applications. Current experimental trial-and-error approaches are costly and time-intensive, while existing analytical models lack the resolution to predict localized phase transformations and stress evolution at the scale of individual weld passes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-physics simulation framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for melt pool behavior, finite element analysis (FEA) for thermal stress modeling, and phase-field methods for microstructure prediction. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale features across centimeter-scale weldments while capturing rapid thermal gradients (10^3–10^6 K/s) and solidification kinetics. Parallelized simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for coupled heat-mass transfer equations and machine learning surrogates to explore parameter spaces encompassing shielding gas compositions, filler material feed rates, and alternating current waveforms. Validation will employ synchrotron X-ray diffraction data from collaborating institutions quantifying real-time strain and phase distributions. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for a) predicting defect formation thresholds in novel alloy combinations and b) optimizing pulsed welding parameters to control grain morphology. The computational toolkit will be disseminated as open-source modules to support weld procedure specification development, reducing certification costs for aerospace and renewable energy applications. By enabling first-principles design of welding protocols, this work aims to decrease post-weld rework by 30–50% in additive manufacturing use cases while improving joint toughness in next-generation high-entropy alloy welds.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to join or cut metal surfaces. Includes instruction in arc welding, resistance welding, brazing and soldering, cutting, high-energy beam welding and cutting, solid state welding, ferrous and non-ferrous materials, oxidation-reduction reactions, welding metallurgy, welding processes and heat treating, structural design, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of somatic bodywork interventions, with the goal of optimizing therapeutic protocols and personalizing treatment strategies. While somatic therapies such as Rolfing, lymphatic drainage, and Hellerwork are empirically recognized for their benefits, their mechanisms of action at the tissue, circulatory, and nervous system levels remain poorly quantified. Current practice relies heavily on practitioner experience, with limited predictive tools to assess how specific techniques interact with individual anatomical variations or chronic physiological imbalances. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale simulation approach integrating high-resolution biomechanical modeling, fluid dynamics for circulatory and lymphatic systems, and neural network analyses of proprioceptive feedback. The computational pipeline will leverage clinical data from motion capture, pressure sensors, and pre/post-treatment physiological biomarkers (e.g., cortisol levels, inflammatory markers) to parameterize patient-specific models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, particularly for simulating 3D fascial deformation under varying manual techniques, coupled with transient fluid-structure interactions in lymphatic vessels. Machine learning components will be implemented to identify patterns in treatment efficacy across diverse demographic and health history profiles. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating manual intervention parameters (pressure, direction, duration) with quantifiable physiological responses, enabling evidence-based refinement of training protocols. The project will also generate open-access simulation tools to support practitioner education and interdisciplinary research connecting manual therapy with systems biology. By establishing a computational foundation for somatic bodywork, this work aims to bridge traditional hands-on practices with modern biophysical analytics, advancing both therapeutic precision and scientific validation in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of generative artificial intelligence (AI), computational design, and large-scale visual media analysis. Contemporary visual arts and design practices increasingly integrate AI-driven tools to create complex, data-rich works, yet computational limitations hinder the exploration of high-resolution outputs, real-time interactive systems, and ethically informed generative models. The primary research problem addresses the gap between artistic intent and technical scalability, particularly when working with multimodal datasets (e.g., 3D scans, hyperspectral imagery, or dynamic video feeds) that require intensive processing. Proposed computational methods include training diffusion models and transformer-based architectures on GPU clusters to synthesize high-fidelity visual content, optimizing memory usage for terabyte-scale datasets, and implementing distributed rendering pipelines for immersive installations. Additionally, the project will develop computational frameworks to audit bias in generative systems by analyzing latent spaces across diverse cultural datasets. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for artists to deploy ethically aligned AI models efficiently, novel methodologies for real-time collaboration in virtual production environments, and a publicly accessible repository of computationally generated visual assets validated through interdisciplinary exhibitions. The research will directly contribute to emerging discourses in AI-mediated creativity, offering scalable solutions for resource-intensive workflows in digital art and design. By integrating HPC capabilities, this work aims to democratize access to advanced computational tools within the visual arts community while establishing benchmarks for sustainable, equitable practices in generative media production.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in visual and performing arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize resource allocation and environmental management in commercial plant nurseries, addressing challenges posed by dynamic climate conditions and operational scalability. Current nursery practices often rely on generalized protocols for irrigation, fertilization, and climate control, leading to inefficiencies in water use, energy consumption, and plant health during propagation. To resolve this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating real-time sensor data, plant physiological models, and machine learning to predict species-specific growth responses under variable nursery conditions. Multi-agent simulations will model individual plant interactions with microenvironments, while parallelized optimization algorithms will iteratively refine irrigation schedules, substrate compositions, and thermal regimes across production zones. The computational pipeline will process hyperspectral imaging data to detect stress biomarkers and correlate these with growth outcomes using convolutional neural networks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters, the system will simulate thousands of operational scenarios to identify cost-effective strategies balancing productivity, resource use, and labor constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for customizing cultivation protocols across diverse species, reducing water and nutrient waste by an estimated 20–35%, and improving seedling survival rates during transplantation. This work will provide nursery operators with scalable decision-support systems adaptable to shifting market demands and climate variability, directly enhancing the economic and environmental sustainability of nursery operations. The resulting datasets and models will be disseminated through an open-access portal to support industry adoption and further research in precision horticulture.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage outdoor plant farms, tree and shrub nurseries, and related facilities that develop domesticated plant products for propagation, harvesting, and transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science, farm and business management, nursery operations, equipment operation and maintenance, safety procedures, and personnel supervision.

abstract: The increasing complexity of medical billing systems and insurance claim adjudication processes has created significant challenges in optimizing revenue cycle management for healthcare providers. This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence-driven framework to analyze patterns in claim denials, identify systemic inefficiencies, and predict reimbursement outcomes across heterogeneous insurance networks. Leveraging natural language processing (NLP) techniques and graph-based machine learning models, we will process structured billing data alongside unstructured clinical documentation and insurer policy documents to uncover hidden relationships between coding practices, payer-specific rules, and denial probabilities. High-performance computing resources are required to train deep learning architectures on multi-modal datasets spanning millions of de-identified claims, electronic health records, and evolving regulatory guidelines from public and private insurers. The computational workflow will involve parallel processing of insurance transaction logs, semantic analysis of denial reason codes, and dynamic simulation of claim resubmission strategies under different coverage scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics platform capable of recommending optimized billing pathways, flagging high-risk claims for pre-emptive review, and simulating the financial impact of emerging insurance policies. This research addresses a critical gap in health systems operations by applying advanced computational methods to medical revenue integrity challenges, with potential to reduce administrative costs by 15-20% in pilot healthcare networks while improving compliance with evolving value-based care reimbursement models. The work bridges health informatics, computational linguistics, and actuarial science to create novel decision-support tools for medical billing specialists operating in increasingly complex payment ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and manage the medical and health insurance operations in a medical office, health care facility, health maintenance organization, or insurance provider. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes; health insurance law, policy, and regulations; insurance records and paperwork administration; insurance office administration; health/medical insurance software applications; personnel supervision; business mathematics; billing and collection procedures; medical terminology; and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the multi-dimensional impacts of public policy interventions, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation in contexts involving competing social priorities. Traditional policy evaluation methods often struggle to account for dynamic interactions between stakeholders, cascading systemic effects, and rapidly evolving constraints—particularly in crises such as climate-driven displacement or public health emergencies. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to build a modular simulation platform that integrates agent-based modeling, geospatial data, and machine learning to evaluate policy trade-offs under uncertainty. The platform will model how heterogeneous populations (e.g., communities, local governments, NGOs) adapt to policy incentives, incorporating real-world datasets on infrastructure, demographic shifts, and environmental stressors. A core innovation involves coupling microsimulation of decision-making processes with macro-scale cost-benefit analyses, enabling policymakers to visualize second-order effects of interventions. Computational demands arise from the need to run thousands of parameterized scenarios, train predictive models on high-resolution spatial-temporal data, and optimize resource distribution across multi-objective constraints (e.g., equity, fiscal sustainability, crisis response). HPC resources will accelerate scenario testing by parallelizing simulations and enabling sensitivity analyses across diverse policy assumptions. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool for rapid policy prototyping, validated against case studies in climate adaptation planning, and a comparative analysis of allocation strategies for disaster relief funding. This work aims to advance evidence-based policymaking by providing a scalable, data-driven method to anticipate unintended consequences and prioritize interventions in complex, resource-constrained environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues and decision processes. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, microeconomic analysis of policy issues, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing large-scale, dynamic supply chain networks under uncertainty, with applications to business operations in manufacturing and logistics. Modern supply chains face escalating complexity due to globalization, demand variability, and disruptive events such as geopolitical shifts or pandemics. Existing optimization models often struggle to balance real-time adaptability with computational tractability, particularly when human decision-making processes interact with automated systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating two-stage stochastic programming, agent-based simulation, and reinforcement learning. The stochastic programming component will model uncertainty in demand and supplier reliability, while agent-based simulations will capture human-in-the-loop decision patterns across procurement, production, and distribution nodes. Reinforcement learning agents will then be trained to recommend resource allocation strategies that align operational costs with organizational risk tolerances. The computational intensity of this approach necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources: Monte Carlo simulations for risk scenario generation, parallelized mixed-integer programming solvers for stochastic subproblems, and distributed training of neural networks for policy optimization will require significant GPU and CPU cluster capabilities. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly available benchmark dataset of annotated supply chain decision scenarios, (2) performance-optimized algorithms for real-time resource allocation in interruptible production environments, and (3) quantitative insights into the value of human-AI collaboration patterns under different disruption regimes. Results will be validated through case studies with industry partners in automotive component manufacturing and cold chain logistics. By advancing both methodological capabilities and applied decision tools, this work aims to establish new best practices for computationally-assisted operations management while contributing fundamental knowledge about human-system interaction in complex industrial networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems. These programs have a focus on business operations or applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on computational models of second language acquisition (SLA) in English as a Second Language (ESL) learners. Current pedagogical approaches often rely on static frameworks for assessing proficiency or designing curricula, which inadequately account for the dynamic interplay of linguistic, cognitive, and sociocultural factors influencing SLA. To address this gap, we propose developing machine learning models trained on multimodal datasets—including written texts, speech recordings, and eye-tracking data from ESL learners—to identify patterns in language processing, error emergence, and fluency development. The computational workload involves natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for syntactic and semantic analysis, neural networks for predicting proficiency trajectories, and agent-based simulations of classroom interactions under varied instructional strategies. These tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model training, necessitating HPC infrastructure for efficient execution. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for mapping individual learner profiles to optimal pedagogical interventions, (2) automated tools for real-time error detection and adaptive feedback in digital learning environments, and (3) empirically validated insights into how cross-linguistic transfer mechanisms vary across typologically diverse first languages. By integrating computational linguistics with SLA theory, this research aims to enhance the precision of proficiency assessments and inform scalable, personalized ESL instruction. The requested resources will enable large-scale hypothesis testing across heterogeneous learner populations, advancing both theoretical understanding of language acquisition and practical applications in postsecondary ESL programs.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: Educational leadership and administration face growing complexity in optimizing institutional resource allocation amid evolving policy landscapes, demographic shifts, and fiscal constraints. Current decision-making frameworks often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between stakeholders, operational variables, and long-term outcomes. This project proposes the development of a scalable computational model to simulate district- and institution-level administrative scenarios, enabling data-driven strategies for equitable resource distribution, staff deployment, and program sustainability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate multi-year datasets on student enrollment, staffing patterns, budget allocations, and policy compliance metrics from K-12 and higher education systems. These ABMs will simulate how funding mechanisms, leadership interventions, and external pressures propagate through educational ecosystems, with particular focus on underserved regions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical data to identify critical leverage points for improving administrative efficiency while maintaining educational equity. The computational intensity of modeling thousands of interacting agents across heterogeneous institutional contexts necessitates parallelized simulations and large-scale parameter sweeps achievable only through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating policy impacts on operational workflows, predictive metrics for anticipating resource gaps under demographic change, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive leadership strategies. This work directly addresses the urgent need for sophisticated analytical capacity in educational administration, providing administrators with actionable insights to balance fiscal responsibility, regulatory requirements, and student success imperatives. By bridging computational social science methods with leadership theory, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive, systems-aware decision-making in education governance.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in education administration and supervision, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pharmacological research faces significant challenges in predicting the therapeutic and toxicological outcomes of drug interactions within complex biological systems. Traditional experimental approaches are limited by the vast combinatorial space of drug combinations, genetic variability in metabolic enzymes, and dynamic patient-specific factors. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to model drug-receptor binding affinities, metabolic pathways, and population-level pharmacokinetic variability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the structural determinants of drug binding to target receptors and off-target proteins implicated in adverse effects. Concurrently, physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models will be parameterized using population pharmacokinetic data to simulate drug disposition across diverse demographic and genetic subpopulations. Machine learning algorithms will integrate simulation outputs with clinical datasets to predict context-dependent drug-drug interactions and dose-response relationships. The computational demands of these tasks—including parallelized simulation workflows, optimization of multi-scale models, and analysis of high-dimensional datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for drug toxicity, predictive models for personalized dosing regimens, and mechanistic insights into polymorphic enzyme contributions to interindividual variability. This research will advance computational pharmacology by establishing scalable methods to prioritize safe drug combinations and optimize therapeutic efficacy, directly addressing unmet needs in precision medicine and pharmacovigilance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drug interactions on biological systems and organisms and the sources, chemical properties, biological effects, and therapeutic uses of drugs. Includes instruction in pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, drug therapeutics, drug action, bodily responses to drug events, biochemical proliferation and differentiation, apoptosis, cell biology, medicinal chemistry, and studies of specific drugs and drug interactions.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine through the integration of multi-omics data and clinical informatics. A critical challenge in modern medicine lies in understanding the complex molecular and environmental interactions underlying heterogeneous diseases such as cancer, autoimmune disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to capture the dynamic, high-dimensional relationships between genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and electronic health record (EHR) datasets, limiting the development of personalized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. This project will employ scalable machine learning frameworks and network-based computational models to identify disease subtypes, predict treatment responses, and uncover novel biomarkers. Key computational methods include federated learning for privacy-preserving analysis of distributed EHR data, graph neural networks to model biological pathway interactions, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize protein-ligand binding affinities for drug repurposing. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization for deep learning architectures, and ensemble modeling to improve predictive robustness. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for integrative multi-omics analysis, validated predictive models for chemotherapy response in breast cancer cohorts, and the identification of candidate therapeutic targets for Alzheimer’s disease. By bridging computational innovation with clinical translation, this work aims to enhance the granularity of patient stratification, reduce trial-and-error treatment approaches, and accelerate the discovery of precision therapies. The requested computing resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of these analyses, which involve millions of variables and require real-time collaboration across geographically dispersed research teams. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, clinical partnerships, and a public repository to foster reproducibility in computational medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illnesses, injuries, and other disorders of the human body. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, clinical medicine, examination and diagnosis, patient communications, medical ethics and law, professional standards, and rotations in specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, orthopedics, neurology, ophthalmology, radiology, clinical pathology, anesthesiology, family medicine, and psychiatry.

abstract: Livestock production systems face mounting challenges in balancing efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare under evolving environmental and regulatory constraints. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize feeding regimens, disease resistance, and housing design are limited by the biological complexity of livestock systems, which involve nonlinear interactions between genetic, physiological, and environmental factors. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating mechanistic models of animal metabolism, machine learning-driven genomic selection tools, and facility operation simulations to address these multidimensional challenges. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for parameterizing models using multi-omics datasets (transcriptomics, metabolomics) from cattle and poultry cohorts, conducting genome-wide association studies at scale, and simulating thermal regulation dynamics in livestock housing under varying climate scenarios. The computational workflow will couple agent-based modeling of nutrient partitioning in individual animals with system-scale optimization of feed formulations and ventilation strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking genetic markers to methane emission traits, decision support tools for precision feeding systems, and validated digital twins of production facilities that minimize energy use while maintaining animal health benchmarks. By enabling simultaneous analysis of genomic, metabolic, and operational datasets that exceed 500 TB in aggregate, the requested HPC allocation will support transformative advances in reducing the environmental footprint of livestock operations while improving productivity. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and collaborations with extension services to ensure practical translation to dairy, beef, and poultry production systems. This work directly aligns with national priorities for climate-smart agriculture and fills critical gaps in computational infrastructure for next-generation animal husbandry research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, breed, care for, process, and market livestock and small farm animals. Includes instruction in basic animal science, animal nutrition, and animal health as applied to various species and breeds; design and operation of housing, feeding, and processing facilities; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize the resilience of urban transportation systems under compound climate stressors, with a focus on flood and heatwave scenarios. Urban infrastructure faces escalating risks from climate-driven extremes, yet existing models often lack the integration of dynamic environmental variables, multimodal transport interactions, and real-time asset degradation processes. The research will employ coupled hydrodynamic and traffic simulation models, leveraging GPU-accelerated finite volume methods for flood propagation and agent-based modeling for evacuation routing. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on historical failure data to predict bridge and pavement performance under thermally induced material fatigue. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve meter-scale hydrologic processes across metropolitan regions while simultaneously simulating traffic flows at 15-minute intervals over decadal horizons. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies cascading failures in transportation networks, identifies priority retrofits for critical corridors, and evaluates nature-based adaptation strategies. The computational platform will be validated using lidar-derived terrain data and sensor networks from three flood-prone U.S. cities. By enabling probabilistic risk assessment at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions, this work will advance equitable climate adaptation planning methodologies while reducing computational costs for municipal engineers. The resulting open-source codebase will support replication studies across diverse urban morphologies, directly contributing to NSF’s critical infrastructure resilience objectives. Resource allocations will specifically enable ensemble runs exploring 10^4 climate-realized scenarios, a computational load exceeding local cluster capabilities by two orders of magnitude.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in civil engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of policy implementation and organizational decision-making in educational systems. Educational institutions face persistent challenges in aligning leadership strategies with policy mandates, particularly as they navigate complex, multi-level systems involving districts, schools, and community stakeholders. Current approaches to analyzing these interactions rely on limited-scale qualitative case studies or simplified quantitative models, which fail to capture the emergent, nonlinear behaviors inherent in large-scale organizational networks. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate decision-making processes among administrators, educators, and policymakers under varying resource constraints and policy scenarios. These models will integrate institutional data (e.g., budget allocations, staffing patterns, policy compliance records) with network analysis to quantify how information flows, power structures, and stakeholder priorities influence systemic outcomes. HPC resources are critical to iteratively test hypotheses across thousands of simulated scenarios, manage large-scale graph-based datasets, and apply machine learning techniques to identify latent patterns in organizational behavior. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for predicting bottlenecks in policy adoption, optimizing leadership interventions, and evaluating the equity implications of resource distribution strategies. This work will advance the application of computational social science in educational leadership by providing empirically grounded tools to support data-driven governance. Results will be validated against longitudinal case studies from three urban school districts, with dissemination targeting both academic audiences and practitioner communities in education administration. The project aligns with the program’s focus on organizational development and policy innovation, offering novel methodologies to bridge theoretical and applied challenges in education leadership.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Organizational Leadership and Policy Development with an emphasis on education. Includes instruction on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, education administration and supervision, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: The development of efficient hydrocarbon recovery strategies in complex reservoirs requires high-fidelity simulations to address subsurface heterogeneities, multiphase flow dynamics, and coupled thermal-hydro-mechanical processes. Conventional reservoir modeling approaches often rely on coarse grid resolutions or simplified physics due to computational limitations, leading to inaccuracies in predicting fluid behavior and optimizing extraction processes. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance reservoir simulation capabilities through large-scale, three-dimensional modeling of fractured unconventional reservoirs with dynamic fracture propagation and multiphase flow interactions. The research will employ parallelized finite element methods coupled with discrete fracture network models to resolve fine-scale features, including stress-dependent fracture apertures, proppant transport, and non-Darcy flow effects. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to calibrate model parameters using historical production data and microseismic monitoring results, enabling adaptive grid refinement in critical regions. The computational workflow will leverage distributed-memory architectures to simulate reservoir domains exceeding 10^8 grid cells, capturing high-resolution interactions between hydraulic fractures, natural fracture networks, and matrix permeability. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize fracture spacing, fluid injection schedules, and well placement under geomechanical constraints, directly addressing challenges in enhancing recovery rates in low-permeability shale and tight oil reservoirs. The results will provide novel insights into the role of fracture connectivity and stress shadowing on long-term production performance, with applications to sustainable reservoir management and reduced environmental footprint. By utilizing HPC resources, this work aims to bridge the gap between laboratory-scale experimental data and field-scale operational decision-making, offering a computational framework to maximize hydrocarbon recovery while minimizing water usage and greenhouse gas emissions associated with hydraulic fracturing operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for locating, extracting, processing and refining crude petroleum and natural gas, including prospecting instruments and equipment, mining and drilling systems, processing and refining systems and facilities, storage facilities, transportation systems, and related environmental and safety systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize landscape management practices through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of plant-environment interactions. Landscaping systems face challenges in balancing aesthetic goals, plant health, and resource efficiency, particularly under variable environmental conditions. Current irrigation, fertilization, and pest control strategies often rely on generalized protocols, leading to overuse of water, chemicals, and labor. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling approach integrating plant physiology, soil hydrology, and microclimate dynamics at fine spatial-temporal resolutions. The model will simulate growth patterns of ornamental species, turfgrass, and groundcovers under diverse irrigation schedules, nutrient regimes, and maintenance practices, incorporating real-world sensor data on soil moisture, temperature, and light exposure. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify nonlinear relationships between maintenance inputs and landscape outcomes, enabling predictive optimization. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the parallel processing requirements of multi-agent simulations across heterogeneous virtual landscapes (10m²–1km² scales) and long-term climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends resource-efficient strategies tailored to site-specific conditions, reducing water use by 15–25% and chemical inputs by 10–20% while maintaining plant vitality. This work bridges gaps between empirical horticulture and computational sustainability, offering scalable solutions for urban planners, commercial groundskeepers, and agricultural extension services. By coupling process-based models with data-driven optimization, the project advances precision landscaping as a subdomain of computational agriculture, with potential applications in adaptive green infrastructure design under climate change.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of stylistic and thematic patterns in British and Commonwealth literary texts from the 18th century to the present. While traditional literary scholarship relies on close reading, emerging computational methods enable systematic comparisons across vast corpora, revealing latent connections and historical shifts undetectable through manual analysis. The research problem centers on identifying and contextualizing underrepresented narrative strategies—particularly those tied to evolving conceptions of empire, identity, and place—within anglophone literary traditions. By analyzing linguistic features, metaphor frequency, and syntactic structures across ~50,000 digitized texts from the Chadwyck-Healey and EarlyPrint databases, this study aims to trace how colonial and postcolonial authors negotiated cultural hybridity and power dynamics through form. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for entity recognition and sentiment analysis, machine learning classifiers to detect genre-blending in postcolonial works, and network analysis to map intertextual influences. HPC resources are critical due to the scale of textual data, the complexity of training custom transformer models on historical English variants, and the need for parallel processing to iteratively refine stylistic metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-access dataset of annotated literary features, a quantitative framework for periodizing stylistic innovation in Commonwealth literature, and scholarly articles re-evaluating canon formation through computational lenses. By integrating computational rigor with literary theory, this project aims to expand methodological diversity in English studies while foregrounding marginalized voices in the British imperial archive.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literatures and literary developments of the English-speaking peoples of the British Isles and the British Commonwealth, from the origins of the English language to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, country and regional specializations, literary criticism, and the study of folkloric traditions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neurophenomenological correlates of contemplative practices across diverse populations, integrating multimodal neuroimaging, behavioral data, and first-person experiential reports. Contemplative traditions emphasize training attention and self-regulation through practices like meditation, yet the dynamic interplay between large-scale brain network reorganization, behavioral outcomes, and subjective experience remains poorly quantified. Current limitations stem from fragmented analytical approaches that struggle to model nonlinear interactions across spatiotemporal scales or reconcile objective neurobiological metrics with qualitative phenomenological data. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework for analyzing longitudinal datasets (fMRI, EEG, pupillometry, and self-report) from 300+ participants engaged in structured mindfulness-based interventions. The HPC environment will enable three core innovations: (1) implementation of multilevel Bayesian models to map individual trajectories of neurocognitive change while accounting for baseline traits and practice adherence; (2) simulation of whole-brain dynamic functional connectivity patterns using empirically derived neural mass models, parameterized by participant-specific neuroimaging data; and (3) natural language processing (NLP) of free-response experiential journals through transformer-based architectures to identify latent semantic clusters that predict neurobehavioral outcomes. Computational challenges include managing high-dimensional data integration (10+ TB across modalities), optimizing parallelized parameter estimation for hierarchical models, and training hybrid neural-symbolic NLP pipelines. Expected outcomes include a publicly shared toolbox for contemplative neuroscience analytics, predictive models linking specific practice components to neuroplasticity markers, and novel metrics quantifying mind-body interaction dynamics. This work bridges contemplative science with computational neuroscience, offering methodological advances for studying subjective experience while informing personalized mental health interventions. By elucidating how introspective training sculpts brain-body communication, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of consciousness studies, clinical psychology, and systems biology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophical, psychological, and scientific bases of human contemplative experience. Includes instruction in cognitive science, meditation, mindfulness, neuroscience, philosophy, psychology, and religion.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model the dynamics of intergroup conflict escalation and resolution in fragile sociopolitical environments, integrating computational social science, behavioral psychology, and network theory. While traditional peace studies rely on qualitative case analyses or simplified quantitative models, this research addresses the critical gap in simulating complex, adaptive systems where nonlinear interactions between cultural narratives, economic disparities, and communication patterns drive conflict. The core computational challenge lies in scaling agent-based models (ABMs) to incorporate millions of heterogeneous agents—representing individuals, institutions, and external actors—operating across temporal, spatial, and sociocultural dimensions. These agents will be programmed with empirically derived behavioral rules informed by field data from post-conflict regions, including decision-making biases, trust thresholds, and coalition-formation heuristics. The HPC framework will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore probabilistic pathways of conflict diffusion under varying policy interventions, such as resource redistribution or mediated dialogue protocols. Key innovations include coupling graph neural networks with ABMs to capture evolving alliance structures and deploying natural language processing to analyze sentiment shifts in simulated discourse. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for predicting tipping points in communal tensions and optimizing conflict mitigation strategies. By quantifying the systemic effects of socioeconomic variables and intervention timing, this work aims to provide actionable insights for peacebuilding organizations while advancing computational methods for interdisciplinary conflict science. The scale of required simulations—necessitating terabyte-scale memory management and GPU-accelerated parameter sweeps—makes HPC resources indispensable for achieving statistically robust, generalizable results.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of international and inter-group conflicts. Includes instruction in peace research methods and related social scientific and psychological knowledge bases.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the morphosyntactic evolution of understudied Germanic language varieties using computational modeling, with a focus on historical dialectal divergence in Low German and Frisian texts from the 15th to 19th centuries. Despite their significance to understanding North Sea Germanic linguistic networks, these varieties lack comprehensive diachronic analyses due to fragmented textual records and the labor-intensive nature of traditional philological methods. The research problem centers on reconstructing probabilistic pathways of grammatical change—particularly in case system erosion and clause structure variation—while accounting for cross-dialectal contact and sociolinguistic factors. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and agent-based modeling within a high-performance computing (HPC) framework. Custom transformer-based models will be trained on a newly compiled corpus of digitized manuscripts (∼5 TB of text and metadata) to automate syntactic annotation and identify latent patterns of change. Parallelized agent simulations will then model the diffusion of morphosyntactic features across virtual speaker populations, incorporating historical demographic data and geographic constraints. This dual methodology requires significant GPU-accelerated computing resources for 1) training domain-specific language models on non-standardized historical orthographies, 2) running large-scale evolutionary simulations with adaptive parameter spaces, and 3) performing Bayesian phylogenetic analyses of reconstructed change trajectories. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative typology of grammatical innovation in post-Hanseatic Low German, a computational framework for contact-induced change modeling applicable to minority Germanic languages, and an open-access toolset for historical syntactic annotation. The project will advance methodologies in computational historical linguistics while addressing critical gaps in the diachronic study of West Germanic microvariation, with implications for language preservation initiatives and theoretical models of syntactic change.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Germanic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Germanic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pharmacy research faces increasing demands to optimize drug delivery systems and predict complex molecular interactions, particularly in developing nanoparticle-based formulations. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and time-consuming, often struggling to capture the dynamic behavior of drug-carrier systems at atomic resolution. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational models of drug-nanoparticle interactions, focusing on pharmacokinetic profiles and stability under physiological conditions. The research will employ all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to analyze binding affinities, diffusion rates, and degradation pathways of candidate drug molecules within polymeric nanoparticle matrices. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict formulation efficacy and toxicity, using datasets derived from experimental literature and public pharmacology databases. Key challenges include scaling simulations to biologically relevant timescales (microseconds to milliseconds) and managing the high-dimensional parameter space of multicomponent drug delivery systems. HPC resources are critical to parallelize these computations, enabling iterative refinement of forcefield parameters and ensemble-based sampling. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal polymer-drug pairings for enhanced bioavailability in preclinical models, with a focus on antibiotics and cancer therapeutics. This work will provide a framework for rational design of nanoparticle formulations, reducing trial-and-error experimentation in early-stage drug development. Additionally, the project will support training opportunities for pre-pharmacy students in computational pharmaceutics, bridging gaps between traditional pharmacy curricula and modern data-driven research methods. By integrating HPC-based modeling with experimental validation, this research aims to accelerate the translation of theoretical drug delivery concepts into practical applications, directly aligning with the program’s mission to prepare students for advanced pharmacy education and innovation in pharmaceutical sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: Diabetes mellitus remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, driven by complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors. Current therapeutic strategies often fail to achieve sustained glycemic control or prevent complications, underscoring the need for deeper mechanistic insights. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics datasets, including genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, with clinical data from longitudinal cohorts of patients with type 2 diabetes. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms to identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response, coupled with network medicine frameworks to map dysregulated pathways. Molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between candidate therapeutic compounds and putative targets identified through these analyses. The scale of data—encompassing >10,000 patient records and terabyte-level omics datasets—necessitates HPC infrastructure for efficient parallel processing, large-scale optimization of predictive models, and high-fidelity simulations. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel subtype-specific therapeutic targets, validated predictive models for complications such as diabetic nephropathy, and optimized drug candidates for experimental validation. By elucidating context-specific disease mechanisms, this research aims to advance precision medicine approaches in diabetes care, directly addressing the critical gap between molecular discovery and clinical translation. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated computations, high-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies, and secure storage for sensitive health data, ensuring robust execution of this computationally intensive initiative.
cip_definition: Research focused on Diabetes

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for collision damage assessment and repair optimization in automotive bodies. Current methodologies in collision repair rely heavily on empirical techniques and manual inspection, which can lead to inefficiencies in diagnosing structural weaknesses, estimating repair costs, and selecting materials. To address these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and multi-physics simulations to model collision dynamics, material deformation, and adhesive bonding behavior under diverse impact scenarios. High-fidelity simulations will replicate real-world collisions, analyzing stress distribution in vehicle frames, composite material failure thresholds, and the performance of adhesives and coatings under thermal and mechanical loads. ML algorithms will be trained on simulated and empirical datasets to predict optimal repair strategies, including material selection, heat treatment parameters, and refinishing techniques. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across thousands of collision scenarios while accounting for variables such as impact angle, velocity, and material heterogeneity. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of collision simulation results, predictive tools for rapid damage assessment, and data-driven guidelines for improving repair durability and safety. By integrating computational modeling into collision repair education, this project also aims to enhance technician training programs with virtual labs and scenario-based learning modules. The results will directly contribute to reducing material waste, lowering repair costs, and advancing the adoption of lightweight materials in automotive design, aligning with industry demands for sustainability and precision in collision repair technologies.
cip_title: Autobody/ Collision and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, reconstruct and finish automobile bodies, fenders, and external features. Includes instruction in structure analysis, damage repair, non-structural analysis, mechanical and electrical components, plastics and adhesives, painting and refinishing techniques, and damage analysis and estimating.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance innovation in the Baking and Pastry Arts by addressing the lack of predictive, data-driven frameworks for optimizing complex baking processes. Traditional methods for recipe development, texture engineering, and quality control rely heavily on iterative experimentation, which is resource-intensive and limited in its ability to account for dynamic variables such as ingredient heterogeneity, environmental conditions, and microbial activity during fermentation. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) developing multi-scale computational models to simulate molecular interactions in dough and pastry matrices under varying thermal and hygroscopic conditions, and (2) training machine learning algorithms to predict optimal ingredient ratios, baking parameters, and shelf-life outcomes. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model heat and mass transfer in industrial ovens, while molecular dynamics simulations will analyze starch-protein-water interactions critical to texture formation. A curated dataset of ingredient properties, processing variables, and sensory outcomes from professional bakeries will inform neural networks designed to generate novel recipe adaptations for dietary restrictions (e.g., gluten-free or low-sugar products). By integrating these approaches, the project aims to establish a computational pipeline that reduces trial-and-error waste, enhances product consistency, and accelerates the design of sustainable, market-responsive baked goods. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling large-scale simulations of stochastic biochemical processes and high-dimensional optimization tasks. Expected outcomes include open-access models for the culinary industry, a digital repository of ingredient behavior profiles, and new interdisciplinary methodologies bridging gastronomy, computational chemistry, and data science. This work positions computational baking as a novel niche within vocational STEM, offering tools to address global challenges in food waste, nutrition, and scalable artisanal production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares  individuals to serve as professional bakers and pastry specialists in restaurants or other commercial baking establishments.  Includes instruction in bread and pastry making, bread and pastry handling and storage, cake and pastry decorating, baking industry operations, product packaging and marketing operations, and counter display and service.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the photochemical degradation pathways of microplastics in freshwater and marine systems, integrating environmental chemistry, photophysics, and computational modeling to address a critical gap in understanding the persistence and ecological impact of microplastic pollution. While microplastics’ physical distribution is well studied, their molecular-scale interactions with solar radiation and dissolved organic matter remain poorly characterized, limiting predictive models of long-term environmental behavior. We propose a multiscale computational framework combining quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to map degradation kinetics under variable environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale QM/MD simulations of common polymer structures (e.g., polyethylene, polypropylene) interacting with UV-visible light spectra and organic ligands, capturing bond-breaking dynamics and the formation of reactive oxygen species. Concurrently, ML models trained on simulation outputs and experimental validation datasets will predict site-specific degradation rates across salinity, pH, and light exposure gradients. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated ab initio codes (CP2K, Gaussian) and custom neural network architectures optimized for chemical reaction prediction. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between materials science, environmental photochemistry, and computational physics, providing atomistic insights into microplastic aging processes that govern bioavailability and toxicity. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of degradation pathways, predictive tools for assessing microplastic lifetimes in aquatic ecosystems, and foundational knowledge to inform bioremediation strategies. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for parallelized QM simulations across thousands of polymer-ligand configurations—necessitate allocation of HPC resources to achieve the required spatial and temporal resolution. Results will advance both fundamental understanding of polymer-environment interactions and applied efforts to mitigate global microplastic pollution.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on one or more of the physical and biological sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and simulating the dynamics of decentralized information ecosystems, with a focus on emergent behaviors in distributed, privacy-preserving media platforms. The research addresses the challenge of modeling how user-generated content evolves in environments where data sovereignty and algorithmic transparency are prioritized—a growing niche as regulatory and ethical concerns reshape digital interactions. Traditional social media models, which rely on centralized control and opaque recommendation systems, are ill-suited to these emerging paradigms, necessitating novel approaches to understand stability, misinformation spread, and community formation in decentralized networks. The project will employ agent-based modeling combined with graph neural networks to simulate user interactions at scale, incorporating differential privacy mechanisms and federated learning constraints. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: (1) large-scale parallel simulations of network topologies with >10^6 nodes, (2) training attention-based models on synthetically generated interaction graphs that preserve privacy guarantees, and (3) real-time visualization of ecosystem evolution through dimensionality reduction techniques. Expected outcomes include a publicly available software toolkit for simulating decentralized information flows, quantitative metrics for assessing systemic resilience to coordinated manipulation campaigns, and evidence-based design principles for next-generation media architectures. This work bridges gaps between distributed systems theory, computational social science, and privacy-aware machine learning, offering foundational insights for developers, policymakers, and researchers working on ethical information systems beyond conventional centralized platforms. The computational demands of simultaneously maintaining privacy constraints, modeling emergent phenomena, and handling sparse, heterogeneous data streams make access to GPU-accelerated clusters and high-memory nodes essential for achieving statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
cip_title: Computer Software and Media Applications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer software and media applications, not elsewhere classified
