We propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze terabyte-scale genomic datasets from 20 *Vitis vinifera* cultivars and associated rootstock hybrids, alongside metagenomic data from fermentation trials. ML models will identify genotype-phenotype associations for traits such as drought tolerance and resistance to powdery mildew (*Erysiphe necator*), while ABMs will simulate microbial population dynamics under temperature and pH gradients reflective of projected climate scenarios. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing genome-wide association studies (GWAS), training deep neural networks on hyperspectral imagery of grapevine phenotypes, and running stochastic simulations of microbial interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for breeding resilient grape varieties, optimized fermentation protocols to maintain wine quality under abiotic stress, and open-source tools for the viticulture community to simulate climate impacts on vineyard management. This work will advance precision viticulture by reducing reliance on chemical interventions, lowering production risks, and enhancing the scientific basis for sustainable winegrowing practices in evolving agroclimatic zones.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific and agribusiness principles to the production of grapes, the making of wine, and the wine business. Includes instruction in grapes and wines of the world; grape production; winemaking technology; plant biology; chemistry; food science, safety, and packaging; soil science; pest management; and marketing and business management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation diffusion across digital media platforms through advanced computational modeling, addressing critical gaps in understanding how cultural, social, and technological variables influence communication patterns. While prior research has explored misinformation spread in homogeneous groups, few studies account for the interplay of intercultural communication norms, algorithmic amplification, and multimodal content (e.g., text, images, video) in shaping large-scale dissemination. Our work integrates communication theory with computational social science methods to analyze multi-platform datasets (Twitter, TikTok, and Reddit) encompassing 50 million posts, with metadata on user demographics, network structures, and engagement metrics. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a three-phase approach: (1) automated content analysis via transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for cross-cultural linguistic nuances and multimodal disinformation detection; (2) temporal network analysis using dynamic graph neural networks to map community-specific diffusion pathways; and (3) agent-based simulations modeling intercultural communication behaviors under varying platform moderation scenarios. Computational demands include processing terabyte-scale datasets, training multimodal deep learning architectures, and running parallelized simulations across 10,000+ parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting misinformation propagation across cultural boundaries, validated through case studies on climate change and public health narratives. Results will advance communication theories of intercultural influence while providing actionable insights for platform designers and policymakers. The project’s scale necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory simulations beyond typical departmental computing infrastructure. By bridging communication studies with computational methodologies, this work aims to establish novel paradigms for studying digital discourse at unprecedented granularity and cultural specificity.
cip_definition: An program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, research and research methods, and theories of communication, and that spans specialties within the field of communications. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models for optimizing speech and language intervention strategies for K–12 students with communication disorders. Current methods for designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual, qualitative assessments, which can limit scalability and personalization. To address this, we propose a machine learning framework to analyze multimodal datasets—including speech audio recordings, longitudinal academic performance metrics, and clinician-reported progress notes—to identify patterns in language acquisition barriers and predict intervention outcomes. The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for parsing speech samples, graph neural networks to model relationships between linguistic features and educational milestones, and reinforcement learning to simulate personalized intervention scenarios. A key innovation involves training domain-specific language models on curated datasets of impaired speech phonology and syntax, which require significant parallel processing capabilities due to the heterogeneous, high-dimensional nature of the data. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization for these models and probabilistic simulations of language development trajectories under varying intervention conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to recommend IEP adjustments based on real-time student progress data, (2) quantifiable thresholds for phonological and syntactic features that correlate with improved academic outcomes, and (3) open-source codebases for simulating language intervention strategies. This work directly supports the program’s mission by bridging computational advances with special education praxis, equipping educators with evidence-based, data-driven tools to address speech and language impairments. The requested resources are critical for handling the project’s computational load, as preliminary tests on smaller clusters exceeded local capacity when processing >10,000 hours of speech data or simulating >1,000 agent-based student interaction models concurrently.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Speech or Language Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study and design of educational services for children or adults with speech and language impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with speech and language impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with speech disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to assess the impacts of climate change on coupled human-natural systems in critical watershed regions, with a focus on quantifying trade-offs between ecosystem services and resource use. The research addresses a gap in current environmental studies: high-resolution, dynamic models that simultaneously capture ecological processes, hydrological cycles, and anthropogenic decision-making under climate uncertainty. Using the Colorado River Basin as a case study, we propose to combine agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-enhanced hydrological simulations to project water availability, biodiversity responses, and land-use patterns through 2100 under multiple climate scenarios. The computational approach requires coupling a 3D hydro-ecological model (via modified Soil & Water Assessment Tool code) with socio-economic ABM agents representing agricultural, municipal, and conservation stakeholders. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the stochastic ensemble simulations across 0.5-km² grid resolution, process multi-terabyte datasets from CMIP6 climate models and Landsat time series, and perform variance-based sensitivity analysis on >50 coupled model parameters. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of tipping points in groundwater-dependent ecosystems under projected drought intensification, 2) spatial optimization maps for conservation interventions balancing riparian health and agricultural needs, and 3) open-source tools for participatory scenario testing with regional policymakers. The HPC implementation will leverage GPU acceleration for neural network emulators of evapotranspiration processes and parallelize Monte Carlo iterations across climate uncertainty dimensions. By advancing the integration of ecological dynamics with human behavioral modeling at watershed scales, this work aims to provide actionable frameworks for climate-resilient natural resource management while demonstrating novel computational methods for transdisciplinary environmental research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on environment-related issues using scientific, social scientific, or humanistic approaches or a combination. Includes instruction in the basic principles of ecology and environmental science and related subjects such as policy, politics, law, economics, social aspects, planning, pollution control, natural resources, and the interactions of human beings and nature.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in evidence-based integrative medicine research, specifically the challenge of modeling complex, multi-modal interactions between patient-specific factors, therapeutic interventions, and health outcomes. Integrative medicine emphasizes personalized, whole-person care that combines conventional and complementary therapies, but the combinatorial complexity of these interventions—coupled with heterogeneous biological, psychosocial, and lifestyle variables—exceeds the analytical capacity of traditional statistical methods. To overcome this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML), network medicine analytics, and dynamical systems modeling. The research will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs), multi-omics data, and patient-reported outcomes from a longitudinal cohort of 15,000 individuals with chronic conditions. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these multimodal datasets, training of ensemble ML models to predict treatment response, and simulation of intervention cascades across biological networks. Key computational challenges include managing high-dimensional data sparsity, resolving temporal dependencies in longitudinal care pathways, and quantifying uncertainty in heterogeneous treatment effects. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of optimized, patient-specific therapy combinations, (2) predictive biomarkers for integrative intervention success, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic treatment regime modeling. By elucidating how multi-component interventions interact with individual patient profiles, this work will provide a quantitative evidence base to guide clinical decision-making in integrative medicine, ultimately advancing its goal of delivering personalized, effective whole-person care. The scale of data integration and computational intensity required necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine in a way that reaffirms the importance of the relationship between practitioner and patient; focuses on the whole person; is informed by evidence; and makes use of all appropriate therapeutic approaches, healthcare professionals, and disciplines to achieve optimal health and healing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize safety and operational efficiency in forklift operations through high-fidelity simulation and predictive modeling. Despite extensive training protocols, forklift-related accidents remain a critical concern in industrial settings, often due to dynamic variables such as load instability, operator decision-making under stress, and environmental unpredictability. Current training tools lack the capacity to model these complex, real-time interactions at scale. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-agent warehouse environments, integrating physics-based forklift dynamics, human operator behavior models, and stochastic risk factors. The computational approach will utilize discrete event simulation (DES) to replicate workflow patterns and Monte Carlo methods to assess accident probabilities under diverse scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and real-world sensor data to predict high-risk conditions and recommend corrective actions. The simulations will incorporate variables such as load weight distribution, operator fatigue metrics, and spatial constraints derived from LiDAR-scanned warehouse layouts. By parallelizing these simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to generate statistically robust insights into accident causation and evaluate the efficacy of proposed safety interventions. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for proactive risk assessment, data-driven revisions to operator training curricula, and optimized load-handling guidelines tailored to heterogeneous environments. This work will advance the integration of computational modeling into industrial safety research, with potential applications in certification standard development and regulatory policy. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational throughput for parameter space exploration and real-time feedback system prototyping, which are infeasible on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate forklifts in a variety of work environments. Includes instruction in accident prevention, forklift operation, materials handling, and worksite safety.

abstract: The safe and effective use of explosives in construction and demolition relies on precise control of blast dynamics, yet current methods for optimizing blast parameters remain constrained by empirical models and trial-and-error approaches. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate rock fracturing, stress wave propagation, and fragment distribution during controlled blasting, enabling data-driven design of blast patterns. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of existing analytical models, which struggle to account for heterogeneous geological conditions, complex charge geometries, and dynamic material responses at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to resolve multiphysics interactions across spatial scales (millimeters to meters) and temporal scales (microseconds to seconds) using coupled finite element and discrete element methods. Simulations will integrate geomechanical property datasets, 3D subsurface geometries, and stochastic variations in rock mass integrity to model fracture network development under explosive loading. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs by training surrogate models on HPC-generated data, enabling rapid parameter sweeps for charge placement, timing, and energy distribution. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for blast-induced ground vibration, flyrock trajectory, and fragmentation size distribution, with direct applications in quarry operations, tunneling, and urban demolition. By linking computational results to field data from instrumented blasts, this work will establish a foundation for adaptive blast design protocols that improve safety margins, reduce environmental impact, and lower material waste. The requested HPC allocation will support large-scale parallel simulations (10,000+ cores) to achieve the spatial resolution required for mesoscale fracture modeling while maintaining domain sizes representative of industrial-scale blasts. This project bridges critical gaps in blasting science by providing a physics-based alternative to legacy heuristic methods, with potential impacts on workforce training programs and regulatory frameworks for explosive use in sensitive environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in using a variety of explosive materials to aid in the construction process. Includes instruction in safety procedures for storing, handling, placement, charge power determination, drilling, pounding, building demolition, preparing rocky surfaces for building foundations and demolition of explosives.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive, resource-efficient frameworks for next-generation edge computing systems, which face critical challenges in balancing computational demands with energy constraints and latency requirements. As edge devices proliferate in applications such as autonomous systems and distributed sensor networks, traditional resource allocation strategies struggle to dynamically optimize heterogeneous workloads under variable operating conditions. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining real-time reinforcement learning (RL) models with discrete-event simulations to predict and manage resource allocation across edge-node hierarchies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train these RL agents on large-scale synthetic datasets emulating edge network topologies, as well as to parallelize simulations evaluating energy-latency tradeoffs under diverse scenarios. The project will implement containerized workflows to orchestrate distributed training across GPU nodes and validate models using trace-driven emulation of IoT traffic patterns. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for dynamic task offloading and energy-aware scheduling, reducing simulated edge network latency by 20–40% compared to static allocation baselines. These results will provide a foundation for deploying adaptive edge systems in environments with intermittent connectivity or strict power budgets, directly supporting research in resilient cyber-physical infrastructures. By open-sourcing the simulation framework and benchmarking datasets, this work will also enable broader community efforts to optimize computational resources in emerging edge and fog computing paradigms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize resource allocation strategies in large, multi-school educational systems, addressing the complex challenges faced by district-level administrators. School districts must balance competing priorities—such as equitable funding distribution, staffing needs, facility maintenance, and compliance with policy mandates—while contending with dynamic variables like fluctuating enrollment, budget constraints, and shifting demographic patterns. Traditional decision-making approaches often rely on static spreadsheets or historical precedents, which fail to account for systemic interdependencies or simulate long-term outcomes of policy choices. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach coupled with machine learning (ML) techniques to create dynamic simulations of district-wide resource allocation scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support the iterative training of ML models on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., student performance metrics, staffing ratios, facility utilization rates, and regional socioeconomic indicators) and to run large-scale simulations that capture the behavior of thousands of interacting agents (schools, administrators, students, and community stakeholders) across multi-year time horizons. The computational workflow will integrate geospatial analysis to evaluate equity impacts of funding decisions and discrete-event simulations to stress-test contingency plans for enrollment shifts or budget cuts. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between competing allocation strategies, predicts downstream effects of policy interventions, and identifies cost-efficient pathways to achieve district performance goals. This work will provide superintendents and system administrators with evidence-based frameworks to navigate complex resource allocation challenges while advancing computational social science methodologies in educational leadership. The project’s scale—modeling entire districts with 50+ schools and 30,000+ students—requires HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory data handling, and rapid scenario testing to deliver actionable insights within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leading and managing multi-school educational systems and school districts and prepares individuals to serve as systems administrators and district superintendents. Includes instruction in educational administration; education of students at various levels; system planning and budgeting; educational policy; educational law and regulations; public relations; professional standards and ethics; and applications to specific issues, cultural context, and geographic locales.

abstract: Climate change poses a significant threat to global crop productivity by intensifying abiotic stressors such as drought, heat, and salinity. While advances in plant genomics have identified candidate genes associated with stress tolerance, translating these findings into resilient crop varieties remains limited by the complexity of genotype-environment interactions and the computational challenges of modeling polygenic traits at scale. This project seeks to address these bottlenecks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of plant stress responses integrating multi-omics data, environmental variables, and physiological traits. We propose a two-phase computational approach: (1) large-scale genomic prediction using machine learning algorithms trained on existing transcriptomic, epigenomic, and phenomic datasets from Arabidopsis thaliana and key crops (soybean, maize); and (2) dynamic systems modeling to simulate how genetic variants influence metabolic pathways under stress scenarios. The first phase will employ neural architecture search to optimize predictive models for yield stability, while the second will utilize constraint-based metabolic modeling (CBM) frameworks like COBRApy, scaled through parallelized flux balance analysis. By coupling these methods, we aim to identify conserved genetic modules that enhance stress resilience across species and generate testable hypotheses for CRISPR-based editing targets. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing datasets exceeding 500 TB, running computationally intensive simulations (>10,000 core-hours per model iteration), and enabling rapid parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of predicted stress-responsive gene networks, validated through subsequent wet-lab experiments, and computational workflows that accelerate the design of climate-resilient crops. This work directly addresses urgent agricultural needs while advancing computational methodologies for plant systems biology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plant sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a predictive optimization framework for dynamic resource allocation in next-generation telecommunications networks, with a focus on balancing cost-efficiency, service quality, and cybersecurity resilience in business environments. The core challenge lies in managing heterogeneous network resources—including edge computing nodes, 5G/6G spectrum bands, and cloud-based infrastructure—under fluctuating demand patterns exacerbated by IoT proliferation and real-time enterprise applications. Current static allocation models fail to account for the nonlinear relationships between latency-sensitive workloads, energy consumption tradeoffs, and evolving cyberthreat landscapes, creating operational inefficiencies for telecom-dependent businesses. To address this, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach enhanced by graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex interdependencies across network layers while incorporating business constraints such as service-level agreements (SLAs) and regulatory compliance requirements. The computational methodology will leverage high-performance computing resources to: 1) simulate large-scale network environments using parallelized discrete-event modeling, 2) train deep reinforcement learning agents on adversarial scenarios combining traffic spikes and security breach attempts, and 3) optimize multi-objective reward functions through evolutionary algorithms. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of prescriptive resource allocation under uncertainty, validated through benchmarking against industry-standard network management platforms. The research will produce novel metrics for quantifying the business value of adaptive network resource allocation, particularly in verticals like smart manufacturing and distributed fintech services. By integrating computational intelligence with telecommunications management principles, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for strategic infrastructure investment decisions in connectivity-driven business models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business skills to design, implement, and manage the voice, video, and data networking systems of organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications concepts and technologies, network operations and management, wireless communications and mobile computing, cybersecurity, regulation and public policy, business practices and management, and written and oral communications.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing soil management practices to enhance agricultural productivity under increasing environmental variability. Soil degradation, nutrient depletion, and shifting hydrological patterns threaten crop yields globally, yet current models struggle to predict soil-plant interactions at scales relevant to farm-level decision-making. We propose a computational framework integrating high-resolution soil process modeling with machine learning to simulate dynamic soil behavior across heterogeneous landscapes. The research will employ mechanistic models of soil-water-plant systems, parameterized using regional soil chemistry, physics, and microbial activity data, to predict nutrient cycling, moisture retention, and root growth at sub-field resolution. These models will be coupled with convolutional neural networks trained on multi-spectral satellite imagery and sensor-derived soil health indicators to upscale localized predictions across broader agroecological zones. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the iterative parameter optimization required for spatially explicit simulations, the large-scale integration of 3D soil hydrology models (HYDRUS-3D) with crop growth modules (DSSAT), and the processing of terabyte-scale remote sensing datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for identifying soil management strategies that maximize nitrogen use efficiency while minimizing irrigation demands under climate uncertainty. By enabling micro-scale analysis of soil carbon sequestration potential and aggregate stability dynamics, this work will directly inform precision agriculture practices for staple crops in erosion-prone regions. The requested allocation of GPU nodes and parallel processing capacity will support 10⁶ core-hours of ensemble simulations across soil type × climate scenario matrices, advancing fundamental understanding of how soil biological communities mediate drought resilience in agroecosystems. Results will be disseminated through open-access soil health decision support systems, providing stakeholders with science-based strategies for sustainable intensification of food production systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that generally focuses on the scientific classification of soils, soil properties, and their relationship to agricultural crops. Includes instruction in soil chemistry, soil physics, soil biology, soil fertility, morphogenesis, mineralogy, hydrology, agronomy, and soil conservation and management.

abstract: The increasing adoption of digital workflows in dentistry has transformed diagnostic and restorative processes, yet critical gaps persist in optimizing patient-specific biomechanical outcomes for CAD/CAM-generated dental restorations. Current approaches rely on generalized material properties and static occlusal models, which inadequately capture the dynamic, heterogeneous forces exerted during mastication. This limitation often results in suboptimal restoration design, leading to premature failure, biomechanical mismatch, or unnecessary removal of healthy tooth structure. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating high-resolution intraoral scan data, real-time masticatory force simulations, and machine learning-driven material optimization to enable predictive, patient-tailored restorative workflows. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multi-scale finite element analysis (FEA) of proposed restoration designs under physiologically accurate loading conditions, incorporating individual variations in bite force, temporal mandibular joint kinematics, and enamel/dentin microstructure derived from micro-CT datasets. Concurrently, a generative adversarial network (GAN) will be trained on a curated dataset of 15,000+ clinical cases to predict stress distribution patterns and recommend geometry modifications that minimize peak tensile stresses while preserving occlusal function. Validation will involve comparative analysis of computationally optimized designs against conventional CAD/CAM outputs in simulated and physical fatigue testing environments. This project requires HPC capabilities to manage the computational complexity of concurrent multi-physics simulations (10^6+ elements per model), real-time data assimilation from heterogeneous sources (3D scans, force sensors, and material databases), and iterative deep learning optimization cycles. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for restoration failure risk reduction, an open-source toolkit for biomechanically informed CAD/CAM workflows, and quantitative guidelines for material selection based on patient-specific functional demands. By bridging computational biomechanics with clinical dentistry, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision digital restorations while providing a scalable framework for future innovation in adaptive dental prosthetics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of digital and CAD/CAM technology in dental treatment. Includes instruction in digital diagnostic and treatment planning techniques, CAD/CAM restoration, and patient management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to optimize hazardous materials (hazmat) incident response and risk mitigation using advanced modeling, real-time data assimilation, and high-performance computing (HPC). Current hazmat management systems face challenges in dynamically processing multi-source environmental data, predicting contamination spread patterns, and coordinating emergency response under uncertainty. Our research will address these gaps through three computational pillars: (1) physics-informed neural networks trained on historical incident data to predict contaminant dispersion across heterogeneous terrains, (2) agent-based modeling of human movement and emergency responder coordination during crises, and (3) multi-objective optimization algorithms balancing economic, environmental, and public health priorities in containment strategies. The proposed HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations of atmospheric and hydrological transport models at meter-scale resolution, coupled with real-time sensor data streams from IoT networks. Machine learning workflows will be accelerated using GPU clusters to process geospatial datasets spanning chemical properties, infrastructure layouts, and demographic variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system capable of simulating 10,000+ scenario variations per hour during live incidents, significantly improving prediction accuracy for plume trajectories (targeting <15% error reduction from current benchmarks) and resource allocation efficiency. The computational infrastructure developed through this project will provide critical capabilities for training next-generation hazmat professionals in complex system analysis while advancing predictive modeling techniques applicable to emerging environmental health threats. By integrating technical workflows with human factors modeling, this work bridges critical gaps between information systems theory and field-ready hazardous materials management solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing, monitoring, and enforcing hazardous materials management and removal. Includes instruction in environmental science, environmental health, human behavior, economics, management science, information systems and applications, and communication skills.

abstract: Pediatric cardiovascular diseases present unique challenges due to the heterogeneity of congenital and acquired conditions, dynamic developmental physiology, and limited datasets for modeling. This project seeks to develop patient-specific computational models of cardiopulmonary hemodynamics in children with complex congenital heart defects (CHDs), such as single-ventricle physiology and tetralogy of Fallot, to optimize surgical planning and predict long-term outcomes. A critical barrier is the integration of multi-scale, multi-modal clinical data—including 4D flow MRI, echocardiography, and catheterization-derived pressures—into predictive frameworks that account for growth-related changes and postoperative remodeling. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations coupling finite element analysis of myocardial mechanics with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of blood flow. These simulations will be informed by machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data to parameterize boundary conditions and validate against longitudinal outcomes. The computational pipeline will also incorporate uncertainty quantification to assess model robustness across anatomic and physiologic variability. By scaling these analyses across a cohort of 200+ patients via parallelized workflows, we aim to identify hemodynamic risk factors for adverse events (e.g., ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias) and simulate virtual surgical interventions to guide personalized approaches. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the computational burden of 3D transient simulations, which require ~10^6 core-hours annually for meshing, solver iterations, and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for clinical decision support, open-source tools for pediatric cardiovascular modeling, and foundational data for future studies on developmental cardiology. This work bridges gaps between clinical observation and mechanistic understanding, with potential to reduce invasive testing and improve quality of life for children with CHDs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases and disorders of the cardiovascular and cardiopulmonary systems of infants, children, and adolescents. May include related research in public health and community medicine issues.

abstract: Transportation infrastructure systems face escalating demands due to urbanization, climate change, and evolving mobility needs, requiring advanced tools to optimize investments while addressing equity and sustainability. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-modal transportation network optimization framework integrating spatial, economic, and environmental constraints. The research problem centers on modeling large-scale urban networks under scenarios of population growth, decarbonization policies, and extreme weather events, with a focus on identifying trade-offs between system efficiency, accessibility, and resilience. Computational methods will combine agent-based transportation simulations, geospatial analytics via GPU-accelerated GIS processing, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to evaluate infrastructure interventions across 10+ metropolitan regions. Machine learning models will predict travel demand shifts under policy scenarios, while graph-based network analysis will assess cascading failure risks in critical infrastructure. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of stochastic climate and socioeconomic futures, reducing runtime from months to days. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable open-source toolkit for infrastructure vulnerability assessment, (2) evidence-based recommendations for prioritizing transit-oriented development corridors, and (3) quantitative metrics linking infrastructure design to regional emissions targets. By enabling high-resolution analysis of interconnected transportation, energy, and land-use systems, this work will advance equitable adaptation planning while addressing computational bottlenecks in existing regional-scale models. Results will directly inform state and municipal infrastructure investment plans, particularly in underserved communities disproportionately affected by transport-related pollution and service gaps.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the economic, social, spatial, and environmental aspects of transportation and infrastructure planning. Includes instruction in economics, environmental analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, risk analysis, transportation economics, transportation evaluation, transportation planning, transportation policy, and urban transportation planning.

abstract: Gene therapy holds transformative potential for treating genetic disorders, yet critical challenges persist in optimizing delivery vectors, minimizing off-target effects, and predicting immune responses to engineered constructs. This project seeks to address these barriers by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational models of viral and nonviral gene delivery systems, CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing fidelity, and host immune interactions. Current limitations in experimental throughput and resolution necessitate atomistic and systems-level simulations to elucidate molecular mechanisms that dictate therapeutic efficacy and safety. We propose multiscale molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the structural stability of adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids under physiological conditions, alongside free energy calculations to map DNA-protein binding affinities in CRISPR-guided editing. Concurrently, machine learning models trained on bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets will predict immune activation risks associated with vector serotypes and transgene products. These computational workflows will integrate genomic, proteomic, and biophysical data to generate predictive frameworks for vector design and editing specificity. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of simulations involving million-atom systems, iterative training of deep neural networks on multi-terabyte genomic datasets, and Bayesian optimization of therapeutic parameters. Expected outcomes include optimized AAV capsid variants with enhanced tissue tropism, CRISPR guide RNA designs with minimized off-target propensity, and actionable biomarkers for immune-related adverse events. By bridging computational discovery with preclinical validation, this work aims to accelerate the development of safer, more precise genetic therapies while reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error experimentation. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated through open-source platforms to support broader innovation in gene therapy research and clinical translation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies. Includes instruction in medical genetics, genome analysis, pharmacology of gene transfer, viral vectors, nonviral therapeutic techniques, genetic screening, targeted gene delivery, vector production, safety and quality assurance, clinical trials management, and bioethics.

abstract: Commercial fishing operations face increasing challenges in balancing economic efficiency, regulatory compliance, and environmental sustainability. Traditional methods for optimizing catch yields, minimizing bycatch, and adhering to dynamic regulatory frameworks often rely on static models or anecdotal experience, which fail to account for real-time environmental variability and complex ecosystem interactions. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution, machine learning-driven simulation platform to model commercial fishing activities in response to multi-scale environmental, biological, and regulatory inputs. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate heterogeneous datasets, including satellite-derived oceanographic data (e.g., sea surface temperature, chlorophyll concentrations), historical catch records, species distribution models, and vessel tracking data. Computational workflows will employ ensemble modeling techniques to simulate gear performance, fish behavior, and fleet dynamics under varying scenarios, such as shifting stock distributions, climate-driven habitat changes, and evolving fishing quotas. A key innovation involves coupling agent-based models of fishing decision-making with hydrodynamic simulations to predict interactions between gear types (e.g., trawls, longlines) and marine environments at meter-scale resolutions. The project will also quantify the computational efficiency gains of GPU-accelerated frameworks for processing real-time data streams from onboard sensors. Outcomes will include open-source tools for adaptive fisheries management, predictive maps of bycatch risk, and evidence-based recommendations for gear modifications to reduce environmental impact. By enabling granular, dynamic resource allocation strategies, this work aims to advance the technological capacity of commercial fishing operations to meet sustainability goals while maintaining economic viability. The scale of spatiotemporal analysis and the integration of high-dimensional ecological data necessitate dedicated HPC resources to achieve the required computational throughput and storage capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as commercial fishermen, fishing operations supervisors or in related fishing industry operations. Includes instruction in fishing vessel operation; fishing equipment operation and maintenance; equipment repair; catch identification, sorting, and storage; safety procedures; record keeping; and applicable legal regulations.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment planning requires precise prediction of craniofacial growth patterns, biomechanical responses to orthodontic forces, and long-term stability of dental alignment. Current clinical methods rely heavily on generalized population data and static imaging, which inadequately account for patient-specific biomechanical variability, dynamic tissue adaptation, or complex interactions between orthodontic appliances and craniofacial structures. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution, patient-specific computational framework to simulate craniofacial growth, orthodontic tooth movement, and bone remodeling under varying treatment conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multiscale finite element models integrating cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) data, intraoral scan-derived occlusal forces, and mechanobiological bone response algorithms. Simulations will account for anisotropic bone properties, periodontal ligament viscoelasticity, and appliance-specific force systems, enabling dynamic 3D visualization of tissue displacement and stress distributions over treatment timelines. Machine learning models trained on longitudinal clinical outcome data will augment simulations to predict individual treatment durations and relapse risks. The computational pipeline will be validated against retrospective patient records and in vitro force measurement studies. Successful implementation of this framework will provide clinicians with a decision-support tool to optimize appliance selection, force application protocols, and retention strategies, reducing treatment times and improving post-treatment stability. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated biomechanical responses for common malocclusions, fostering collaboration in computational orthodontics. By addressing the critical gap in personalized, dynamic treatment planning, this work advances the translation of biomechanical research into clinical orthodontic practice, with potential applications in complex cases such as cleft palate rehabilitation and surgical orthodontics. The scale of data integration, parallelized simulation of heterogeneous tissues, and iterative model training necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically feasible processing times and resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the guidance of growing dental structures and the correction of misalignments, disproportionate growth, and traumas caused by genetics, disease, injuries, and dysfunctional behaviors. Includes instruction in craniofacial growth and development, malocclusion, design and fabrication of orthodontic appliances, craniofacial alignment, physiological function and analysis, cephalometrics, model analysis, space analysis, surgical orthodontics, cleft lip and palate, and treatment planning and management.

abstract: The development of stable and efficacious pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations is hindered by the complex interplay of physicochemical properties, excipient compatibility, and environmental factors. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize formulations are resource-intensive, requiring iterative trial-and-error processes that delay product development and increase costs. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive multiscale models for formulation design and stability assessment. The research will focus on two key areas: (1) simulating molecular interactions in semi-solid formulations (e.g., creams, gels) to predict rheological behavior and phase stability under varying storage conditions, and (2) modeling polymorphic transitions in active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) to anticipate crystallization risks in liquid dosage forms. Computational methods will integrate molecular dynamics simulations (using GROMACS and LAMMPS) to resolve nanoscale interactions, finite element analysis (via COMSOL Multiphysics) for macroscale property prediction, and machine learning algorithms (TensorFlow-based neural networks) trained on experimental datasets to correlate simulation outputs with real-world stability outcomes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high-throughput demands of parameter space exploration, particularly for systems involving multicomponent surfactants, lipids, or polymeric matrices. Expected outcomes include a computational framework capable of identifying optimal excipient combinations, predicting shelf-life under thermal and humidity stress, and guiding reformulation strategies for failed stability batches. By reducing experimental redundancies and enabling in silico preformulation screening, this work aims to accelerate development timelines for topical drug products and cosmetic emulsions while enhancing quality control protocols. The resulting models will be validated against industrial case studies, with implications for improving regulatory submissions through data-driven stability justification.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate patterns in student writing development across diverse educational contexts, with the goal of informing adaptive pedagogical strategies for English language arts (ELA) instruction. A critical challenge in teacher education lies in equipping educators with data-driven insights into the heterogeneous trajectories of writing skill acquisition, particularly as students grapple with complex tasks such as argumentative composition, narrative structuring, and syntactic complexity. While existing qualitative studies offer valuable pedagogical frameworks, the computational analysis of large-scale, longitudinal writing corpora remains underexplored due to processing limitations. This research will utilize natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and syntactic dependency parsing, to analyze a corpus of 50,000+ anonymized student essays spanning grades 6–12 from urban, suburban, and rural school districts. The computational workflow will involve 1) training domain-specific language models to assess rhetorical moves and grammatical patterns, 2) clustering temporal development pathways using graph-based neural networks, and 3) simulating the impact of instructional interventions through agent-based modeling. HPC resources are essential for managing the distributed training of deep learning architectures, processing high-dimensional textual features, and running iterative simulations of classroom learning dynamics. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of critical transition points in writing proficiency, evidence-based typologies of common compositional challenges, and open-source tools to help teacher candidates analyze writing artifacts during practicum experiences. By bridging computational linguistics with ELA pedagogy, this work aims to enhance how teacher education programs prepare educators to diagnose and respond to the multidimensional nature of writing development, ultimately supporting equitable literacy instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach English grammar, composition and literature programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a critical role in gastrointestinal diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), colorectal cancer, and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). However, elucidating the complex, dynamic interactions between microbial communities, host genetics, and environmental factors remains a major computational challenge. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale models integrating longitudinal metagenomic, metabolomic, and clinical data from a 1,200-patient cohort to identify predictive biomarkers and mechanistic drivers of disease progression. Current approaches lack the resolution to capture nonlinear microbial network dynamics or host-microbe metabolic cross-talk at scale. We propose a hybrid computational framework combining Bayesian hierarchical modeling, deep learning for time-series forecasting, and agent-based simulations of microbial ecosystems. This framework will be applied to three aims: (1) model spatial and temporal heterogeneity in gut microbiome composition associated with IBD flare events, (2) quantify strain-level metabolic interactions influencing chemotherapy response in colorectal cancer, and (3) predict personalized dietary interventions for IBS using genome-scale metabolic reconstructions of patient-specific microbiomes. The scale of metagenomic assembly (≥50 TB raw sequencing data), the combinatorial complexity of microbial community simulations (>10^6 agent-agent interactions per model), and the need for iterative hyperparameter optimization in deep neural networks necessitate dedicated HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the first computational platform capable of resolving strain-level microbiome dynamics across disease states, validated predictive biomarkers for therapeutic response in two clinical trials, and open-source tools for microbiome systems medicine. By enabling real-time analysis of complex host-microbiome datasets, this work will advance precision gastroenterology and provide a template for computational biomarker discovery in mucosal immunology. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for metagenomic assembly, and high-throughput job scheduling for ensemble simulations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of criminal behavior patterns using large-scale, multi-modal datasets to model how urban infrastructure, digital communication networks, and environmental factors interact to influence crime emergence and diffusion. The research addresses a critical gap in computational criminology by developing a framework that integrates real-time social media activity, anonymized mobility traces, and historical crime records to simulate complex adaptive systems underlying criminal networks. The core computational challenge involves analyzing terabyte-scale datasets spanning heterogeneous sources (geospatial records, text corpora, sensor data) while maintaining ethical constraints on sensitive behavioral information. High-performance computing resources will enable the implementation of distributed graph neural networks to model criminal network evolution, coupled with agent-based simulations of offender decision-making processes under varying environmental conditions. Parallelized natural language processing pipelines will extract latent behavioral signals from unstructured text data (e.g., forum posts, localized news reports), while differential privacy techniques will safeguard individual identities in mobility datasets. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for crime pattern simulation, predictive models of crime displacement following targeted interventions, and evidence-based recommendations for dynamic resource allocation in law enforcement. By advancing computational methods to analyze criminal behavior as an emergent property of socio-technical systems, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven crime prevention strategies that account for the complex interdependencies between digital ecosystems and physical urban environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of crime as a sociopathological phenomenon, the behavior of criminals, and the social institutions evolved to respond to crime. Includes instruction in the theory of crime, psychological and social bases of criminal behavior, social value systems and the theory of punishment, criminal law and criminal justice systems, penology, rehabilitation and recidivism, studies of specific types of crime, social attitudes and policy, and applications to specific issues in law enforcement administration and policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-resourced Celtic languages, with a focus on morphosyntactic variation and historical language change. Despite their cultural significance, languages like Irish, Welsh, Breton, and revitalized varieties such as Cornish lack large-scale annotated corpora and computational tools necessary for advanced linguistic research. Current studies rely on fragmented datasets, limiting the ability to model dialectal diversity, trace syntactic evolution, or quantify the influence of language contact—particularly between Celtic languages and English or French. This project proposes the development of a unified computational framework to analyze structural features across modern and historical Celtic languages, integrating digitized manuscripts, modern speech corpora, and comparative linguistic data. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for low-resource language parsing, implementing phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct proto-Celtic syntactic features, and simulating dialect convergence using agent-based models. HPC resources are essential for processing heterogeneous data (e.g., OCR-corrected medieval texts, sociolinguistic interviews) at scale, running parallelized simulations of language change, and optimizing neural architectures for morphologically complex languages. Expected outcomes include the first open-access repository of computationally annotated Celtic language corpora, a diachronic atlas of syntactic shifts in Insular Celtic, and evidence-based frameworks for evaluating revitalization strategies. By bridging computational linguistics and Celtic philology, this work will enable quantitative insights into language preservation, contact dynamics, and the operationalization of historical linguistics theories. The tools and datasets produced will support interdisciplinary research in language technology, education, and heritage preservation, addressing a longstanding infrastructural inequity in minority language studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by the Celtic peoples of the British Isles, Continental Europe, and Asia Minor, including, but not limited to, modern languages such as Irish, Scots Gaelic, Welsh, and Breton; and extinct or revived languages such as Cornish, Manx, Galatian, and others. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design of next-generation high-temperature alloys for energy and industrial applications, where materials are subjected to extreme thermomechanical stresses and corrosive environments. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize alloy composition and processing parameters are time-intensive and costly, particularly when evaluating microstructural evolution under dynamic operational conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the interplay between atomic-scale defect dynamics, mesoscale grain-boundary interactions, and macroscale mechanical performance. The research will integrate quantum-mechanical calculations (density functional theory) to predict phase stability and solute segregation tendencies, molecular dynamics simulations to analyze dislocation propagation and creep mechanisms, and finite element models to simulate stress distribution and fracture initiation in polycrystalline systems. Machine learning algorithms will further accelerate the exploration of alloy design spaces by correlating processing variables (e.g., heat treatment, forging rates) with microstructural features and performance metrics. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of these simulations, which involve millions of atoms and complex boundary conditions, while facilitating data-driven optimization of additive manufacturing parameters to minimize residual stresses and defect formation. Expected outcomes include predictive models for alloy behavior under cyclic loading, validated against synchrotron X-ray diffraction data, and a computational toolkit to guide the development of cobalt-nickel superalloys with enhanced fatigue resistance and oxidation stability. This work will directly support advancements in metallurgical engineering by reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error methods, enabling faster translation of novel materials to applications in power generation systems and heavy machinery. The resulting open-source simulation workflows will also serve as a resource for the broader materials community, fostering collaboration in computational alloy design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and metallurgical principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of metal components of structural, load-bearing, power, transmission, and moving systems; and the analysis of engineering problems such as stress, creep, failure, alloy behavior, environmental fluctuations, stability, electromagnetic and thermodynamic characteristics, optimal manufacturing processes, and related design considerations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern railway systems, compounded by dynamic operational variables such as fluctuating demand, real-time disruptions, and stringent safety regulations, necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize network efficiency and reliability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate large-scale railway operations, integrating real-time data streams, signal system dynamics, and hazardous material transport protocols. Current methodologies often rely on static models that fail to capture the interdependencies between scheduling, infrastructure constraints, and emergent risks, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and increased vulnerability to delays. The proposed research will employ parallelized agent-based simulations to model train movements, crew assignments, and switching operations across interconnected railyards, while machine learning algorithms will predict congestion patterns and optimize schedules under stochastic disturbances. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing clusters, the framework will perform Monte Carlo analyses to assess the probabilistic impact of extreme weather events, equipment failures, and cargo-specific hazards on network resilience. The anticipated outcomes include actionable insights into capacity expansion strategies, adaptive scheduling protocols, and risk mitigation measures tailored to heterogeneous railway environments. This work aims to establish a scalable computational platform that enhances decision-making for railway operators, reduces operational costs through predictive maintenance models, and improves compliance with safety standards outlined in the General Code of Operation rules. The integration of HPC resources is critical to achieving the requisite computational granularity and temporal resolution, enabling stakeholders to transition from reactive to proactive management paradigms in an increasingly interconnected transportation landscape.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance survey research methodology by addressing the computational challenges of modeling complex, multidimensional measurement error in large-scale, multimodal survey data. Traditional approaches to measurement error correction—critical for ensuring validity in social science research—often rely on simplified assumptions that fail to account for dynamic interactions between respondent behavior, questionnaire design, and contextual factors across diverse populations. The increasing use of hybrid data collection methods (e.g., web, mobile, and biometric sensors) compounds these challenges, generating high-dimensional datasets with heterogeneous error structures. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating multilevel structural equation modeling (SEM) with machine learning techniques to dynamically model error sources across survey modes and demographic subgroups. The research will develop and validate a scalable algorithm for simultaneous error adjustment and latent trait estimation, leveraging Bayesian hierarchical models and graph neural networks to capture nonlinear dependencies in response patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on synthetic and real-world survey datasets (n ≈ 500,000 respondents), enabling parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess robustness under varying error scenarios and large-scale optimization of adaptive questionnaire designs. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for error-aware survey analysis, empirically grounded guidelines for minimizing mode-specific measurement biases, and novel metrics for evaluating cross-cultural equivalence in multinational surveys. By addressing computational bottlenecks in modeling intricate error dynamics, this work aims to enhance the reliability of survey-derived insights for emerging interdisciplinary applications, such as public health behavior tracking and decentralized community needs assessments, where traditional disciplinary boundaries are increasingly inadequate to address methodological complexity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on survey research design to gather data about behaviors, demographics, opinions, and data analysis to answer complex questions. Includes instruction in the analysis of survey data, cross-cultural and multi-population survey methodology, data collection methods, modes of survey analysis, quantitative analysis, questionnaire design, research design, sampling, survey error, and structural equation modeling.

abstract: Occupational exposure to hazardous substances remains a critical public health challenge, with complex interactions between workplace environments, worker behaviors, and chemical toxicodynamics influencing health risks. Current risk assessment models often lack granularity to account for real-time variations in exposure levels, dynamic worksite conditions, and multi-agent interactions. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to simulate exposure risks in industrial settings, integrating fluid dynamics, machine learning, and agent-based modeling. The research problem centers on overcoming limitations in traditional static risk models by capturing spatiotemporal variability in airborne contaminant dispersion, worker movement patterns, and equipment use. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations of multiphase pollutant transport across diverse industrial geometries, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms that optimize sensor placement for exposure monitoring. Agent-based models will simulate worker interactions with machinery and protective equipment under evolving scenarios, while toxicokinetic models predict dose-response relationships at the individual level. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for identifying high-risk exposure zones, optimizing ventilation designs, and informing adaptive safety protocols. The computational approach will leverage parallelized simulations across GPU clusters to manage the high dimensionality of 4D environmental data and stochastic behavioral inputs. By enabling real-time risk visualization and scenario testing, this work aims to advance evidence-based interventions in occupational health, reduce chronic disease burdens among workers, and provide a scalable platform for regulatory compliance assessments. The requested HPC resources will directly support iterative model training, sensitivity analyses of 10,000+ parameter combinations, and validation against experimental data from partner manufacturing facilities. This project bridges gaps between industrial hygiene practice and computational innovation, with implications for mitigating emerging risks in advanced manufacturing and green energy sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to monitor and evaluate health and related safety standards in industrial, commercial, and government workplaces and facilities. Includes instruction in occupational health and safety standards and regulations; health-related aspects of various occupations and work environments; health hazard testing and evaluation; test equipment operation and maintenance; industrial toxicology; worker health and safety education; and the analysis and testing of job-related equipment, behavior practices, and protective devices and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of somatic bodywork therapies, with the goal of optimizing therapeutic protocols for diverse populations. Despite growing clinical evidence supporting the efficacy of manual therapies such as Structural Integration and lymphatic drainage, the field lacks quantitative models to predict how specific techniques influence tissue dynamics, autonomic nervous system responses, and long-term functional outcomes. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating heterogeneous data types—including biomechanical imaging, wearable sensor outputs, and patient-reported outcomes—into predictive simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multimodal datasets spanning 3D motion capture, MRI-derived tissue strain analyses, and real-time physiological monitoring (heart rate variability, galvanic skin response) from clinical studies. Computational methods will include finite element modeling of fascial and musculoskeletal networks under varying manual pressure vectors, machine learning-driven pattern recognition in autonomic response datasets, and agent-based simulations of cumulative therapeutic effects over multi-session interventions. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models correlating manual technique parameters (e.g., force vector, duration, rhythm) with immediate biophysical responses and longitudinal health outcomes, (2) an open-source toolkit for practitioners to simulate intervention impacts based on individual client biomarkers, and (3) quantitative evidence to inform standardized competency frameworks in somatic education. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to process high-resolution temporal-spatial data across scales—from cellular mechanotransduction effects to whole-body movement patterns—requiring parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets. By establishing predictive relationships between manual interventions and systemic health outcomes, this work aims to advance evidence-based practice in somatic therapies while providing a computational foundation for personalized treatment planning in rehabilitative and wellness contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: Interindividual variability in drug response remains a critical challenge in clinical pharmacy, particularly for drugs with narrow therapeutic indices such as anticoagulants, chemotherapeutics, and immunosuppressants. Current dose optimization strategies often rely on population averages or iterative clinical adjustments, which can delay therapeutic efficacy, increase toxicity risks, and elevate healthcare costs. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to predict patient-specific drug dosing using integrative pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, genomic data, and machine learning. The research will focus on creating multi-scale models that incorporate patient-specific factors, including genetic polymorphisms in drug-metabolizing enzymes, transporter proteins, and clinical biomarkers, to simulate drug exposure and response dynamics. High-resolution PK/PD simulations will be performed using parallelized computational workflows to account for population-level variability and optimize dosing regimens under diverse physiological scenarios. Key computational methods include Bayesian hierarchical modeling for parameter estimation, neural networks for identifying nonlinear relationships between genetic variants and drug clearance, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in dose predictions. The project will leverage existing clinical datasets from institutional electronic health records and biobanks, augmented by synthetic data generation to address sparsity in underrepresented populations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for warfarin, tacrolimus, and carboplatin dosing, deployable via a clinician-facing decision support tool. This work aims to advance precision pharmacotherapy by reducing trial-and-error dosing, minimizing adverse drug events, and improving therapeutic outcomes in oncology, transplant, and anticoagulation management. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the computational complexity of genome-integrated models, large-scale parameter sweeps, and real-time optimization tasks, which are infeasible with standard clinical workstations. Successful implementation will provide a scalable template for integrating computational pharmacology into routine clinical pharmacy practice.
cip_title: Clinical, Hospital, and Managed Care Pharmacy
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to deliver specialized pharmacy services and produce pharmaceutical products in clinical settings in conjunction with other health care professionals. Includes instruction in biostatistics; clinical pharmacokinetics; biopharmaceutics; neuropharmacology; pharmacodynamics; drug metabolism; clinical sampling and research design; drug delivery systems; chemotherapy; pharmacotherapy; clinical pharmacy management; medical and research ethics; and applications to nuclear, nutrition support, oncology, psychiatric, and therapeutic pharmacy.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing modular construction supply chains, which are critical for meeting rising demands for affordable housing and sustainable infrastructure. Current methodologies struggle to dynamically adapt to volatile material costs, labor shortages, and logistical disruptions, leading to project delays and cost overruns. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision support system to model and simulate multi-echelon modular supply chains under uncertainty. The research will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with discrete-event simulation (DES) to capture complex interactions among suppliers, manufacturers, transporters, and construction sites across geographies. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks (GNNs) and reinforcement learning (RL), will be deployed to predict bottlenecks and optimize real-time resource allocation. The computational framework will require parallel processing of large-scale spatiotemporal datasets—including IoT sensor feeds, supplier transaction records, and weather patterns—to generate probabilistic scenarios for risk mitigation. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing, the team aims to reduce simulation runtime for 12-month project horizons from weeks to hours, enabling rapid iteration of "what-if" analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of recommending resilient procurement strategies, inventory buffers, and transportation routing adjustments. This work bridges gaps in construction informatics and operations research, offering a scalable solution to enhance the economic and environmental efficiency of modular building techniques. The computational infrastructure will also support future extensions into circular economy models for material reuse, advancing the industry’s transition toward net-zero construction practices.
cip_definition: Any program in construction management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address operational and sociocultural challenges in funeral service management, a specialized niche within non-science and engineering disciplines. The funeral service industry faces increasing complexity due to fluctuating demand patterns, evolving cultural expectations around memorialization, and the need for data-driven decision-making in resource allocation. Traditional manual or low-throughput analytical methods are insufficient for modeling dynamic variables such as seasonal mortality trends, staff scheduling under crisis conditions (e.g., pandemics), or optimizing sustainable practices in funeral home operations. This project will develop computational models to simulate service workflows, predict resource requirements, and analyze the socioeconomic factors influencing consumer preferences across diverse demographics. Methods will include agent-based modeling to recreate funeral home operational ecosystems, natural language processing of historical service records to identify cultural trends, and machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized industry data to forecast regional service demands.
