By parallelizing these analyses across HPC architectures, the project aims to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing large, heterogeneous datasets spanning mortuary science, psychology of grief, and business logistics. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for funeral home capacity planning, evidence-based recommendations for balancing operational efficiency with compassionate care standards, and novel frameworks for evaluating the environmental impact of burial practices. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scalability in modeling this socially vital but understudied sector, ultimately supporting funeral directors in maintaining service quality during demographic shifts and public health emergencies. This work establishes a foundation for computational social science applications in thanatology while adhering to ethical guidelines for sensitive data in deathcare contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional licensure as funeral directors and as managers of funeral homes, cemeteries, and related services.  Includes instruction in the sociology of death and dying, psychology of grief and grief counseling, history of funeral service, funeral direction, business law, funeral service law, funeral home management, accounting and related computer operations, and funeral services marketing and merchandising.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of interactions between atmospheric chemistry and climate dynamics, with a focus on improving the representation of aerosols and trace gases in regional and global climate models. Despite their critical role in radiative forcing and cloud formation, uncertainties persist in modeling the lifecycle, spatial distribution, and reactivity of short-lived climate forcers such as secondary organic aerosols (SOAs) and reactive nitrogen compounds. These gaps limit the predictive accuracy of climate projections, particularly under evolving emission scenarios. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled study integrating observational datasets with the Community Earth System Model (CESM) and a custom-modified version of the GEOS-Chem atmospheric chemistry model. The computational workflow will resolve fine-scale processes, including aerosol microphysics, heterogeneous chemistry, and bidirectional aerosol-cloud interactions, at unprecedented horizontal resolutions (3–10 km regionally, 25 km globally) over decadal timescales. Key innovations include the assimilation of satellite-derived aerosol optical depth and airborne in situ trace gas measurements to constrain model parameters, as well as machine learning techniques to optimize computationally expensive chemical mechanisms. The project requires access to HPC resources capable of supporting large ensemble simulations, petabyte-scale data storage, and parallelized post-processing workflows. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of feedbacks between anthropogenic emissions, aerosol chemistry, and regional climate variability in critical zones such as the Arctic and tropical marine boundary layers; (2) improved parameterizations of aerosol aging and wet deposition processes for next-generation Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) models; and (3) publicly accessible datasets linking emission pathways to aerosol radiative forcing uncertainties. By elucidating chemistry-climate couplings at process-resolving scales, this work will directly inform mitigation strategies and advance predictive capabilities for climate extremes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of atmospheric constituents, reactions, measurement techniques, and processes in predictive, current, and historical contexts. Includes instruction in climate modeling, gases and aerosols, trace gases, aqueous phase chemistry, sinks, transport mechanisms, computer measurement, climate variability, paleoclimatology, climate diagnosis, numerical modeling and data analysis, ionization, recombination, photoemission, and plasma chemistry.

abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) represent complex, multifactorial conditions with heterogeneous progression patterns and treatment responses. Current clinical models struggle to integrate genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and radiomic data at scale, limiting personalized risk stratification and therapeutic targeting. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled, multi-scale computational framework to model liver disease progression by synthesizing multi-omics datasets, longitudinal clinical records, and dynamic imaging features. Leveraging machine learning (ML) and mechanistic modeling, we will train ensemble algorithms on a retrospective cohort of 12,000 patients with histologically confirmed liver disease to identify cross-modal biomarkers predictive of fibrosis progression, HCC development, and drug-induced liver injury. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate hepatocyte-stellate cell-immune interactions under varying genetic and metabolic perturbations, parameterized by single-cell RNA sequencing data from human liver biopsies. These simulations, requiring parallelized computation across thousands of cores, will generate testable hypotheses about microenvironmental drivers of disease transitions. Validation will occur through prospective comparison with real-world outcomes from three ongoing clinical trials (NCT04880212, NCT05281471). The computational pipeline will utilize containerized workflows on GPU-accelerated nodes to process >50 TB of imaging and sequencing data, with differential privacy protocols ensuring patient confidentiality. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated predictive model for 5-year HCC risk in MASLD, (2) mechanistic insights into metabolic-inflammatory crosstalk in early hepatocarcinogenesis, and (3) open-source tools for liver-specific digital twin development. This resource will enable precision surveillance strategies and accelerate therapeutic discovery for understudied patient subpopulations, directly addressing NIH Liver Disease Research Priorities 2023.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hepatology

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision systems maintenance and repair by developing advanced computational models to predict and mitigate failures in high-tolerance mechanical and electromechanical systems. Precision systems, such as those used in aerospace, advanced manufacturing, and medical devices, require maintenance protocols that account for micro-scale wear, environmental stressors, and real-time operational data. Traditional diagnostic methods often lack the resolution to model complex interactions between components or optimize repair strategies under dynamic conditions. To overcome these limitations, this research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-physics simulations coupled with machine learning (ML) frameworks. The computational approach will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and lubrication effects, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map system degradation patterns across interconnected components. Large-scale datasets from sensor arrays and historical maintenance records will be processed to train predictive models for anomaly detection and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. The HPC environment is essential to parallelize simulations across diverse operational scenarios, reduce computational latency in real-time digital twin applications, and scale ML training to address high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for adaptive maintenance scheduling, validated against experimental data from CNC machining and robotic assembly testbeds. This work aims to advance predictive maintenance frameworks that minimize unplanned downtime, extend equipment lifespan, and reduce resource waste in precision systems. By making the models open-source, the project will contribute to standardized benchmarks for maintenance AI in technology and technical education programs, fostering workforce training in next-generation repair methodologies. The requested computing resources will enable the iterative refinement of models, ensuring robustness across heterogeneous systems while maintaining the interpretability required for technician decision support.
cip_title: Precision Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision systems maintenance and repair, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of embedded systems in modern computing applications demands robust methodologies to optimize hardware-software co-design under stringent power, latency, and reliability constraints. This project seeks to address challenges in developing adaptive embedded architectures for edge computing devices, where traditional simulation tools fail to scale efficiently for heterogeneous system-on-chip (SoC) designs. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize and accelerate the simulation, validation, and optimization of configurable computing platforms. The research will focus on three computational phases: (1) emulating multi-core SoC architectures with reconfigurable peripheral interfaces using cycle-accurate models, (2) implementing machine learning-driven design space exploration to identify optimal task partitioning strategies, and (3) stress-testing fault tolerance mechanisms through Monte Carlo simulations of component failure scenarios. By distributing these compute-intensive tasks across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce simulation time for complex configurations from weeks to days while maintaining high modeling fidelity. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for scalable embedded system prototyping and quantitative guidelines for balancing computational parallelism with inter-process communication overhead in reconfigurable architectures. The results will directly support the development of energy-efficient edge computing solutions for industrial IoT applications while providing Computer Engineering Technology students with hands-on experience in HPC-accelerated hardware design workflows. This work bridges critical gaps between theoretical embedded systems concepts and practical large-scale computational evaluation, addressing a key need in engineering technology education and industry-ready tool development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized dietary interventions for patients with chronic metabolic conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the complexity of individual nutritional needs. Current approaches to diet planning often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for the dynamic interplay of genetic, metabolic, microbiome, and lifestyle factors influencing nutrient absorption and health outcomes. The research problem centers on creating scalable models that integrate heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, microbiome sequencing data, and real-time dietary logs—to predict patient-specific responses to dietary changes. The computational approach combines machine learning algorithms with mechanistic models of nutrient metabolism to simulate how varying macronutrient ratios, micronutrient profiles, and meal timing affect biomarkers such as blood glucose, lipid levels, and inflammatory markers. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing parameter optimization across thousands of simulated patient profiles, training deep learning architectures on high-dimensional datasets, and conducting sensitivity analyses to identify critical intervention variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating adaptive dietary recommendations, validated against clinical data from partnering community health centers. This work will directly enhance the precision of dietetic technician practice by providing evidence-based, data-driven decision support tools. Additionally, the project will integrate case studies derived from model outputs into the Dietetic Technician curriculum, exposing students to computational nutrition methodologies. By bridging gaps between clinical practice and quantitative systems biology, this research aims to improve dietary intervention efficacy while advancing pedagogical innovation in dietetics education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of registered dietitians and nutritionists, to implement nutritional and dietetic plans and provide direct client and patient services. Includes instruction in human nutrition, client interviewing and record keeping, dietary planning, food preparation and safety, food worker supervision, food service establishment monitoring and inspection, and applicable procedures and regulations.

abstract: Forest ecosystems face increasing threats from climate change, invasive species, and anthropogenic disturbances, necessitating advanced predictive tools to optimize management strategies. Current approaches often rely on static models with limited capacity to integrate high-resolution spatial data, dynamic ecological processes, and stochastic disturbances at landscape scales. This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate forest growth, disturbance regimes, and management interventions under climate uncertainty. The research will integrate multi-source data, including LiDAR-derived canopy structure, hyperspectral imagery, soil moisture sensors, and decades of forest inventory plots, into a machine learning-enhanced agent-based model. Key computational challenges include parameterizing species-specific responses to microclimate variability, resolving fire spread and pest dispersal dynamics at fine spatial resolutions (<10 m), and optimizing harvest scheduling under ecological and economic constraints. The HPC environment will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in long-term carbon sequestration potential and biodiversity outcomes across alternative management scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for evaluating trade-offs between timber yield, habitat connectivity, and wildfire risk mitigation. By harnessing GPU-accelerated computing for near-real-time scenario testing, this work will provide land managers with actionable insights to balance production forestry with ecosystem resilience. The computational workflows developed will also advance methodological integration of remote sensing big data with process-based ecological models, offering transferable value for sustainable resource management in dynamic landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of forestry and natural resources management to the administration of forest lands and related resources. Includes instruction in silviculture, forest mensuration, forest protection, inventorying, biometrics, geographic information systems, remote sensing, photogrammetry, forest policy and economics, forest land use planning, fire protection and management, and related administrative skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address ethical challenges in the deployment of machine learning (ML) systems for triage decision support in critical care, a domain where algorithmic transparency, bias mitigation, and value alignment intersect with time-sensitive clinical imperatives. While ML-driven triage tools show promise in optimizing resource allocation during crises, their ethical integration requires granular analysis of how implicit biases in training data propagate to triage recommendations and how conflicting moral frameworks (e.g., utilitarianism vs. equity-based prioritization) are computationally operationalized. We propose a computational bioethics approach combining normative analysis with large-scale simulation to evaluate the moral trade-offs embedded in such systems. High-performance computing resources will enable the creation of synthetic patient cohorts (n > 10^6) reflecting diverse demographic, comorbidity, and acuity profiles, coupled with multi-agent reinforcement learning models that simulate triage decisions under competing ethical paradigms. Parallelized simulations will quantify disparities in care access across subpopulations under varying reward functions (e.g., maximizing lives saved vs. prioritizing worst-off patients) while Bayesian inverse optimization techniques will infer latent value hierarchies from existing triage protocols. Sensitivity analyses will map how perturbations in training data distributions affect fairness metrics and clinician trust. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for auditing ethical dimensions of clinical ML systems, evidence-based guidelines for embedding procedural fairness into triage algorithms, and probabilistic models linking algorithmic design choices to moral hazard risks. By bridging formal ethics with computational social choice theory, this work aims to establish scalable methods for value-sensitive design in high-stakes healthcare AI, directly informing policy debates on algorithmic accountability in acute care settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: The relentless scaling of integrated circuit (IC) technologies toward nanometer nodes has introduced unprecedented challenges in balancing performance, power efficiency, and reliability. Traditional design methodologies struggle to account for multi-physical interactions—such as thermal gradients, process variability, and electromagnetic interference—that degrade circuit behavior in advanced semiconductor devices. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity simulation framework for next-generation IC design, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on optimizing analog and mixed-signal circuits for ultra-low-power applications, targeting emerging technologies like 3D-stacked ICs and non-von Neumann architectures. Computational workflows will integrate finite-element modeling for thermal and stress analysis, Monte Carlo simulations for statistical variation analysis, and machine learning-driven optimization to explore design spaces efficiently. These methods require parallelized execution across thousands of cores due to the exponential growth in parameter combinations and the need for nanosecond-scale transient simulations with sub-atomic spatial resolution. By leveraging HPC resources, the project aims to reduce simulation times from weeks to days while maintaining the accuracy required for sub-7nm process nodes. Anticipated outcomes include novel design rules to mitigate thermal crosstalk in 3D ICs, robust circuit topologies resilient to manufacturing variations, and open-source models for predicting electromigration failures in high-current interconnects. The results will advance the semiconductor industry’s ability to co-optimize power, performance, and area (PPA) in energy-constrained edge computing and IoT devices. Additionally, the project will generate curated datasets to accelerate machine learning applications in automated IC design, bridging a critical gap in open-access resources for academic and industrial research. This work will directly support the training of graduate students in computational IC design methodologies, fostering expertise at the intersection of microelectronics and HPC-driven engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to design circuits in microelectronics. Includes instruction in circuit design, circuit layout, circuit analysis, computer-aided drafting, and semi-conductor technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to address the growing challenges of decrypting and analyzing encrypted communications used by terrorist organizations, which increasingly leverage sophisticated cryptographic methods and obfuscation techniques to evade detection. Current forensic tools struggle to process large-scale digital evidence efficiently, particularly when dealing with fragmented data, multi-layered encryption, and covert channels embedded in network traffic. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized brute-force decryption, machine learning-driven pattern recognition, and large-scale network traffic simulation. The project will focus on three computational objectives: (1) optimizing distributed algorithms to accelerate password cracking and cryptographic key recovery for common encryption protocols identified in counterterrorism cases; (2) training deep learning models on HPC clusters to detect anomalies in partially reconstructed data sets, including metadata patterns indicative of covert messaging; and (3) simulating terrorist cyber-attack scenarios using virtualized network environments to identify vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure systems. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing and scalable memory architectures, this approach will significantly reduce the time required to process terabyte-scale forensic images and network packet captures. Anticipated outcomes include a novel framework for prioritizing forensic artifacts in large datasets, improved decryption success rates for law enforcement agencies, and actionable intelligence about emerging cyberterrorism tactics. The computational workflows developed will be validated against real-world case data from partner agencies, with results contributing to open-source forensic toolkits. This research directly supports national security priorities by enhancing the technical capabilities of investigators to disrupt terrorist activities in compliance with legal and procedural standards.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques used to identify, search, seize and analyze digital media and to conduct cyber investigations against criminal and terrorist activity. Includes instruction in computer boot processes and drives, jumper setting, file access and reconstruction, hacking, network systems, cryptography, programming, investigative techniques, forensic imagery, web-based investigation methods, cyberterrorism, and applicable laws and administrative procedures.

abstract: Radiation therapy treatment planning requires precise optimization of dose delivery to maximize tumor control while minimizing toxicity to surrounding healthy tissues. Current clinical practices rely on static anatomical models and simplified dose calculation algorithms, which may not adequately account for dynamic physiological changes during treatment, such as tumor shrinkage or organ motion. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and predict anatomical variations in real time, enabling adaptive radiotherapy workflows. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks that limit the integration of complex, patient-specific biomechanical models and Monte Carlo dose calculations into clinical decision-making. We propose a hybrid approach combining finite element modeling (FEM) to simulate soft tissue deformations with GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations (using TOPAS-nBio) to dynamically update dose distributions based on predicted anatomical changes. Machine learning techniques will be employed to reduce computational costs by training surrogate models on HPC-generated datasets, capturing relationships between imaging biomarkers, biomechanical parameters, and dose deposition patterns. The project will utilize anonymized patient CT/MRI datasets and treatment logs from collaborating clinics to validate model accuracy against clinical outcomes. By deploying these tools on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve submillimeter spatial resolution in deformation modeling and reduce Monte Carlo statistical uncertainties below 1% within clinically feasible timeframes (<10 minutes per fraction). Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for real-time adaptive planning, quantitative insights into dose accumulation uncertainties in moving targets, and open-source tools to bridge computational research with clinical implementation. This work has the potential to advance personalized radiotherapy by improving target accuracy in organs prone to motion, such as lung and liver tumors, ultimately reducing treatment-related complications and enhancing the therapeutic ratio. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the parallelized simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and data storage demands inherent to this multimodal approach.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and psychosocial impacts of structured arts interventions on chronic pain management using high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic interactions between artistic engagement, neural activity, and subjective health outcomes. Chronic pain affects over 20% of adults globally, yet existing pharmacological treatments often prove inadequate or carry significant risks. Emerging evidence suggests arts-based modalities—such as music improvisation and guided visual art creation—may modulate pain perception through multisensory integration and emotional regulation, but the mechanistic pathways remain poorly characterized. The research will employ a dual computational approach: 1) Large-scale neural network simulations using biologically constrained models of sensory and limbic systems, trained on functional MRI datasets from arts intervention trials, to identify key connectivity patterns associated with pain attenuation; and 2) Machine learning analysis of multimodal biometric data (electrodermal activity, heart rate variability, facial expression coding) collected during real-time arts engagement sessions with participants diagnosed with fibromyalgia and neuropathic pain. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (10TB+ neuroimaging/time-series data), running parallelized simulations of whole-brain dynamics at millisecond resolution, and optimizing hybrid neural networks that integrate neurobiological constraints with behavioral outcome predictions. Expected outcomes include a computational framework quantifying dose-response relationships between specific artistic stimuli (e.g., rhythm complexity in music, color palettes in visual art) and neurophysiological signatures of pain modulation, enabling personalized arts therapy design. The project will also generate open-source tools for analyzing arts-health intervention efficacy through computational psychiatry lenses, advancing interdisciplinary methodology at the intersection of performance arts, cognitive neuroscience, and clinical pain management. Results could inform scalable non-pharmacologic treatment protocols while establishing quantitative benchmarks for arts-based modalities in integrative medicine.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of programs that use the visual and performing arts in support of health and wellness among diverse individuals and communities. Includes instruction in dance, literary arts, music, theatre, healthcare systems, program administration, and public health.

abstract: The development of advanced drug delivery systems requires precise optimization of formulation parameters to ensure therapeutic efficacy, stability, and controlled release. A critical challenge in pharmaceutics lies in predicting how nanoscale interactions between drug molecules, excipients, and biological interfaces influence macroscopic drug behavior. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and often fail to capture the dynamic complexity of these multicomponent systems. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate drug-polymer interactions in nanoparticle-based delivery systems, with a focus on optimizing encapsulation efficiency and release kinetics. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization, we will investigate the self-assembly of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles loaded with hydrophobic anticancer agents. The computational workflow will integrate all-atom and coarse-grained MD simulations to characterize drug-polymer binding affinities, solvation dynamics, and degradation-mediated release profiles under physiological conditions. Concurrently, neural network models will be trained on simulation-derived datasets to predict optimal drug-polymer ratios, nanoparticle sizes, and surface modifications for targeted tissue penetration. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of simulations across diverse thermodynamic and compositional parameter spaces, which is infeasible with local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for rational design of PLGA-based formulations, validated against in vitro dissolution and cytotoxicity assays. This work will advance computational pharmaceutics by bridging nanoscale mechanistic insights with clinically relevant performance metrics, potentially accelerating the development of personalized oncology therapeutics. The computational pipelines developed will also be adaptable to other drug delivery platforms, offering a template for resource-efficient formulation screening in academic and industrial research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the formulation of medicinal substances into product vehicles capable of being stored, transported, and then introduced into the patient and behaving in ways optimal to therapeutic interaction. Includes instruction in statistics, biopharmaceutics, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, physical pharmacy, pharmacological analysis, drug design and development, pharmacological biotechnology, chemical separations, spectroscopy, drug-host interactions, immunology, quantitative drug measurement, enzymatic transformations, and metabolic excretion.

abstract: The increasing complexity of managing chronic diseases in primary care requires advanced analytical tools to optimize clinical decision-making. Family Medicine research faces unique challenges due to heterogeneous patient populations, multimorbidity, and the need for personalized, context-sensitive interventions. This project aims to develop predictive models for chronic disease trajectories and treatment outcomes using high-dimensional electronic health record (EHR) data from diverse primary care settings. A critical barrier is the computational demand of integrating structured EHR data, unstructured clinical notes, and social determinants of health while preserving temporal relationships across longitudinal patient records. We propose a multi-stage computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges. First, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process unstructured clinical text at scale, extracting latent features related to symptom evolution and treatment adherence. Second, graph neural networks will model patient-provider interaction patterns and comorbidity networks across 300,000+ patient records. Finally, transformer-based architectures will predict 5-year risks of diabetes complications, cardiovascular events, and polypharmacy-related hospitalizations, adjusting for regional practice variation. HPC resources are essential for training these models on multi-terabyte datasets, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized Bayesian search, and conducting sensitivity analyses through large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated risk stratification tools deployable in real-world primary care workflows, (2) insights into modifiable social factors influencing chronic disease outcomes, and (3) open-source computational frameworks for temporal modeling of primary care data. This work will directly inform the development of adaptive clinical decision support systems, potentially reducing preventable hospitalizations by 15-20% in participating health networks while advancing methodological standards for computational research in Family Medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on Family Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in industrial measurement and control systems, where traditional calibration and instrumentation design methods struggle to adapt to dynamic operational environments with high sensor density. Current approaches often rely on static models that fail to optimize real-time performance or predict system degradation under variable loads, leading to costly downtime and calibration drift. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of adaptive, data-driven control algorithms using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational workflow will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating strain and thermal effects on sensor arrays with machine learning models trained on multi-physics datasets to predict calibration drift patterns. Agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate distributed sensor networks under stochastic industrial conditions, enabling the identification of failure thresholds and optimal maintenance schedules. The HPC environment will facilitate parallelized simulations of large-scale instrumentation systems (10,000+ nodes) and iterative training of neural networks on time-series data from industrial partners. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predictive maintenance of instrumentation clusters, reduced calibration errors by 30–50% in simulated high-vibration environments, and optimized resource allocation protocols for industrial control systems. This work will directly support the development of next-generation instrumentation standards for smart manufacturing and energy infrastructure, bridging gaps between theoretical control models and real-world operational constraints. By leveraging distributed computing architectures, the project will also advance methodologies for deploying lightweight, adaptive algorithms on edge devices in resource-constrained industrial settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing control and measurement systems and procedures. Includes instruction in instrumentation design and maintenance, calibration, design and production testing and scheduling, automated equipment functions, applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision engineering in gunsmithing through computational modeling and simulation of firearm dynamics, material behavior, and manufacturing processes. Traditional gunsmithing relies heavily on iterative physical prototyping and manual testing, which limits the efficiency of optimizing complex parameters such as heat dissipation, mechanical stress distribution, and ballistic performance. The research problem centers on addressing these limitations by developing predictive models to simulate the interplay of thermal, structural, and fluid dynamic forces in firearm components under operational conditions. A key focus is analyzing barrel erosion, chamber pressure dynamics, and receiver fatigue—critical factors influencing firearm safety, longevity, and performance. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for stress and thermal modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for internal ballistics and gas flow, and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms to iteratively refine component geometries and material selections. These simulations will integrate multi-physics datasets, requiring parallel processing capabilities to resolve high-resolution meshes and transient phenomena at microsecond timescales. Validation will cross-reference simulation outputs with experimental data from strain gauges, high-speed thermography, and ballistic chronographs. The anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for identifying failure thresholds in custom firearm designs, optimizing alloy compositions for additive manufacturing, and reducing prototyping cycles. By establishing a computational framework tailored to gunsmithing challenges, this work aims to bridge empirical craftsmanship with data-driven innovation, enhancing educational training modules and supporting small-scale manufacturers in adopting advanced simulation techniques. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary scale and fidelity for these simulations, which are computationally prohibitive on local workstations. This project will contribute foundational insights into the computational mechanics of firearms, fostering safer, more efficient design paradigms in a traditionally artisanal field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and modify firearms according to blueprints or customer specifications, using specialized hand tools and machines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing resilient supply chain networks in high-uncertainty environments, integrating stochastic operational dynamics with multi-objective decision-making under disruptive scenarios. Traditional supply chain models often fail to account for real-time disruptions such as geopolitical shifts, resource shortages, or sudden demand fluctuations, leading to systemic vulnerabilities. The research addresses this gap by combining large-scale discrete-event simulation, machine learning (ML)-driven risk prediction, and distributed optimization algorithms to model adaptive reconfiguration of production-distribution systems. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to manage the combinatorial complexity of multi-echelon networks, where millions of potential scenarios—spanning supplier failures, transportation delays, and demand spikes—are evaluated concurrently. Custom ML models will predict disruption probabilities from heterogeneous data streams (e.g., logistics APIs, economic indices), while mixed-integer programming and graph-based resilience metrics will guide re-routing and inventory buffering strategies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for parallelizing scenario analyses, training deep reinforcement learning agents for dynamic resource allocation, and solving high-dimensional optimization problems with latency constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario-aware supply chain resilience, validated against real-world data from automotive and pharmaceutical manufacturing partners. This work will advance industrial management practices by enabling computationally tractable, real-time decision support systems that balance cost, sustainability, and robustness in volatile markets. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed memory processing for large-scale optimizations, and high-throughput data pipelines to handle global supply chain datasets. Success in this project will provide a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into operational risk management frameworks, fostering more agile and fault-tolerant industrial ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of engineering principles to the planning and operational management of industrial and manufacturing operations, and prepares individuals to plan and manage such operations. Includes instruction in accounting, engineering economy, financial management, industrial and human resources management, industrial psychology, management information systems, mathematical modeling and optimization, quality control, operations research, safety and health issues, and environmental program management.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the drivers of infectious disease transmission dynamics in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where complex interactions between environmental, socioeconomic, and behavioral factors challenge conventional public health interventions. The research aims to develop an agent-based modeling framework to simulate disease spread across heterogeneous populations, integrating spatially explicit data on mobility patterns, healthcare access, and social determinants of health. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and execute large-scale simulations that capture multilevel interactions across urban-rural gradients, informal settlements, and transient populations. The computational approach will leverage georeferenced demographic data, climate variables, and anonymized mobile health records to construct synthetic populations with granular behavioral and contact networks. Machine learning methods will then optimize model calibration against historical outbreak data while quantifying uncertainty in intervention scenarios. By running parallelized simulations across diverse LMIC contexts, this work will identify high-impact leverage points for targeted vaccination campaigns, resource-limited quarantine strategies, and context-specific health communication programs. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into how localized transmission hotspots emerge and persist, as well as predictive tools to evaluate the equity implications of competing intervention policies under constrained budgets. The project will generate open-access computational models to support evidence-based decision-making by health ministries and NGOs, while advancing methodological innovation in simulating coupled social-epidemiological systems. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, perform iterative parameter sweeps, and reduce computational bottlenecks in real-time scenario testing—tasks infeasible on standard institutional infrastructure. This work directly aligns with global health priorities by bridging computational science and international health policy to reduce disparities in outbreak preparedness and response.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: The decline of honeybee populations due to pathogens, pesticides, and environmental stressors poses critical risks to agricultural pollination and global food security. While field studies and controlled experiments have advanced our understanding of colony health, the complex interactions between biological, chemical, and climatic factors remain poorly quantified. This project proposes a computational approach to model colony resilience and collapse dynamics at unprecedented scales, integrating multi-agent systems, machine learning, and genomic analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate the behavior of thousands of individual bees across spatiotemporal gradients, capturing hive-level responses to stressors such as Varroa mite infestations, neonicotinoid exposure, and temperature fluctuations. Agent-based models will parameterize individual bee physiology, task allocation, and social interactions, while neural networks trained on existing apiary datasets (e.g., hive weight, brood patterns, pesticide residues) will predict colony trajectories under varying management practices. Concurrently, genomic workflows will analyze RNA-seq data from stress-exposed bees to identify biomarkers of resilience, leveraging parallelized pipelines for differential gene expression and pathway enrichment. By coupling these computational layers, the project aims to identify synergistic stressors, optimize beekeeping interventions, and propose genetic targets for breeding programs. The expected outcomes include predictive tools for colony failure risk, data-driven guidelines for seasonal hive management, and open-source software to link simulated results with field observations. This work directly supports the agricultural sciences by advancing sustainable apiculture practices, enhancing pollination-dependent crop yields, and mitigating economic losses from colony collapse. Successful implementation requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks, high-memory processors for population-scale genomic analyses, and scalable storage for petabyte-level simulation outputs.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on improving the beekeeping industry, promoting pollination of fruits and vegetables, and bee colony expansion and maintenance. Includes instruction in apiary behavior, apiary equipment and supplies, beekeeping, bee pests and parasites, handling bees, hive set up and care, queen rearing, and seasonal management practices.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of optimizing real-time communication strategies during organizational crises, where rapid shifts in public sentiment and information diffusion across digital platforms demand computationally intensive analysis. While existing studies in public relations and advertising emphasize the importance of timely messaging, current approaches often lack the capacity to process large-scale, dynamic social media datasets or simulate complex stakeholder interactions at the speed required for actionable insights. To bridge this gap, the project employs natural language processing (NLP) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze crisis-related discourse patterns and predict the efficacy of response strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based NLP models on terabytes of multilingual social media data, identifying sentiment trajectories, and mapping emergent misinformation networks. Concurrently, ABM simulations will model how demographic variables, platform algorithms, and message framing influence information spread across synthetic populations exceeding 10 million agents. These parallel workflows require distributed computing architectures to manage memory-intensive tasks and reduce processing times from weeks to hours. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating crisis communication tactics, validated against historical case studies (e.g., product recalls, reputational crises). The project will produce open-access tools for sentiment-aware message optimization, directly benefiting communication practitioners while advancing computational methods in applied communication research. By quantifying the impact of real-time adaptive messaging, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for data-driven decision-making in public relations and organizational communication.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in organizational communication, public relations, and advertising, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how institutional structures and partisan dynamics shape the resilience of economic policies to political shocks, with a focus on democratic systems experiencing rising polarization. The research problem centers on disentangling the feedback loops between policy stability, electoral competition, and economic outcomes—a complex adaptive system that defies analysis through conventional statistical methods due to nonlinear interactions, path dependencies, and high-dimensional parameter spaces. We propose a computational political economy framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-enhanced institutional analysis. The ABM component will simulate strategic interactions between elected officials, bureaucratic actors, and organized interest groups under varying constitutional constraints, while recurrent neural networks trained on historical policy datasets (1945–2020) will identify latent patterns in policy durability across institutional designs. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across 50+ institutional configurations, (2) processing multimodal data (legislative texts, voting records, economic indicators) through transformer-based NLP pipelines, and (3) optimizing counterfactual policy scenarios via genetic algorithms. The computational architecture will leverage graph databases to map principal-agent relationships and Bayesian hierarchical models to account for cross-national heterogeneity. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of institutional safeguards against policy volatility, quantitative estimates of partisan capture thresholds under different electoral systems, and open-source simulation tools for assessing constitutional reform proposals. By enabling large-scale exploration of emergent phenomena in political-economic systems, this research aims to advance predictive theories of policy sustainability while providing methodological innovations for computational social science. The requested resources will support parameter space exploration exceeding 100,000 core-hours, including GPU-accelerated training of policy classification models on terabyte-scale historical archives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction between politics and economics in the formation of public policy. Includes instruction in microeconomics; macroeconomics; political theory; American, comparative, and international political economy; and quantitative methods.

abstract: This research project addresses the critical challenge of optimizing medication distribution systems in large-scale healthcare networks to reduce preventable errors and improve operational efficiency. Despite advancements in clinical practices, systemic inefficiencies—such as delays in medication delivery, miscommunication between care teams, and suboptimal resource allocation during high-demand periods—persist, contributing to adverse patient outcomes and increased costs. To tackle this, we propose developing a computational framework that integrates high-fidelity simulation, machine learning, and real-time data analytics to model medication workflows, predict bottlenecks, and test intervention strategies. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacy dispensing logs, and hospital operational databases, which encompass millions of patient interactions and complex temporal dependencies. Agent-based modeling will simulate dynamic interactions between healthcare providers, patients, and infrastructure, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize decision-making under uncertainty. Computational demands include parallel processing for Monte Carlo simulations, training deep neural networks on high-dimensional time-series data, and running sensitivity analyses across diverse clinical scenarios. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into system redesigns that minimize medication errors, reduce wait times, and enhance resource utilization. The models will also generate generalizable protocols for crisis response, such as surge capacity planning during public health emergencies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical operations research and real-world clinical implementation, ultimately advancing the safety, equity, and sustainability of medication systems. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for healthcare simulation, enabling broader adoption and iterative improvement by the research community.
cip_definition: Research focused on Medication Systems and Operations

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized rehabilitation strategies for patients with motor impairments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in data processing and model complexity. Rehabilitation programs often rely on generalized protocols that fail to account for individual variability in recovery trajectories, physiological responses, and functional goals. While advances in wearable sensors and motion capture systems have generated rich multimodal datasets—including kinematic, electromyographic, and patient-reported outcomes—existing tools lack the capacity to integrate these heterogeneous data streams efficiently or model their dynamic interactions at scale. The proposed research will address this gap by constructing predictive computational models to simulate patient-specific recovery pathways and recommend adaptive therapeutic interventions. Using HPC clusters, we will train machine learning algorithms on aggregated clinical datasets to identify patterns in functional improvement, classify patient subgroups, and forecast responses to specific exercises or assistive devices. Agent-based modeling will further simulate neuromuscular adaptation processes under varying therapy regimens, enabling in silico testing of intervention efficacy. These computational workflows demand parallelized processing for large-scale parameter optimization, real-time biomechanical simulations, and high-dimensional data integration. Outcomes will include an open-source software toolkit to assist rehabilitation aides in designing tailored therapy plans, dynamically adjusting interventions based on patient progress, and communicating data-driven insights to supervising clinicians. By enhancing the precision of rehabilitation support services, this project aims to reduce trial-and-error in therapy design, accelerate functional recovery timelines, and improve resource allocation in clinical settings. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational throughput for these analyses, which involve terabytes of motion capture data, millions of model iterations, and computationally intensive statistical inference tasks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other therapeutic professionals, and to perform routine functions in support of rehabilitation. Includes instruction in roles and responsibilities of rehabilitation providers, basic function of the human body, disabling conditions, therapeutic skills, client management, and communication skills.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-speed, low-latency telecommunications systems necessitates advanced computational methods to optimize network performance, particularly in emerging 5G/6G and IoT architectures. A critical challenge lies in efficiently allocating network resources—such as bandwidth, spectrum, and processing power—across heterogeneous, dynamically changing environments. Traditional simulation tools and analytical models struggle to scale with the complexity of modern telecommunication systems, which involve massive datasets, real-time adaptive protocols, and multi-objective optimization constraints. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate novel algorithms for dynamic resource allocation. The research will focus on three computational tasks: (1) simulating large-scale network topologies with variable traffic loads using parallelized discrete-event simulations (e.g., NS-3 with MPI), (2) training machine learning models to predict congestion patterns and optimize routing protocols under stochastic conditions, and (3) implementing digital signal processing workflows for real-time interference mitigation in dense millimeter-wave deployments. The proposed methods integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) for topology-aware resource mapping and federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy in distributed network nodes. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work aims to reduce simulation wall times by 60–80% compared to conventional cluster setups while handling datasets exceeding 10 TB. Expected outcomes include open-source optimization frameworks for telecommunications operators, validated models for spectrum-sharing efficiency in urban environments, and benchmarks for energy-aware network slicing. These contributions will directly support the development of scalable, AI-driven telecommunication systems, with potential applications in smart cities and emergency response networks. The project will also train graduate students in HPC-driven telecommunications research, bridging gaps between theoretical network models and practical implementation challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to help design and implement telecommunications systems. Includes instruction in communications protocol, data networking, digital compression algorithms, digital signal processing, Internet access, object-oriented and relational databases, and programming languages.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of electrical and electronic system design by developing advanced computational workflows optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. Modern electrical drafting and CAD/CADD applications face challenges in simulating large-scale circuits, optimizing component layouts for energy efficiency, and validating designs against multi-domain constraints (e.g., thermal, electromagnetic). Current software tools often lack the scalability to handle intricate industrial systems, leading to time-consuming iterative processes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating parallelized electromagnetic field solvers, machine learning-assisted routing algorithms, and distributed multi-physics simulation frameworks. The HPC resources will enable rapid evaluation of thousands of design permutations for power distribution networks and embedded systems, with automated constraint checking against industry standards (e.g., IPC, IEEE). Key innovations include GPU-accelerated parasitic extraction for high-frequency circuits and topology optimization algorithms adapted for manufacturability in printed circuit board (PCB) design. Expected outcomes include a prototype computational pipeline capable of reducing design iteration cycles by 40-60% for complex systems, validated through case studies involving smart grid components and industrial automation controllers. The project will additionally produce benchmark datasets for AI-driven layout optimization, bridging gaps between traditional drafting practices and emerging computational design paradigms. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish new best practices for resource-efficient electrical CAD workflows while enhancing educational materials for next-generation drafting technicians. Success metrics will focus on computational efficiency gains, design error reduction rates, and scalability demonstrations for systems exceeding 10,000 components.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Drafting and Electrical/ Electronics CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working schematics and representations in support of electrical/electronic engineers, computer engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic electronics, electrical systems and computer layouts; electrode-mechanical drafting; manufacturing circuitry; computer-aided drafting (CAD); and electrical systems specification interpretation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of individualized education programs (IEPs) for students with multiple disabilities, addressing the challenge of personalizing instruction amid complex, overlapping needs. Current IEP development relies on manual analysis of heterogeneous data—including behavioral, sensory, and cognitive assessments—which limits the ability to model interactions between disabilities and predict the efficacy of interventions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on multimodal datasets spanning historical IEPs, student performance metrics, and teacher-reported outcomes. These models will identify patterns in effective interventions for specific disability profiles and simulate the dynamic impacts of pedagogical strategies across diverse scenarios. Agent-based modeling will further explore how environmental and instructional variables interact with individual needs. The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing to analyze unstructured data from progress reports and adaptive learning tools, enabling real-time refinement of recommendations. By scaling these analyses across thousands of simulated student profiles, HPC resources will enable the generation of evidence-based, adaptive IEP templates tailored to evolving student requirements. Outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators to forecast intervention outcomes, prioritize learning objectives, and adjust teaching strategies dynamically. This work aims to reduce the time and subjectivity inherent in manual IEP design while improving accessibility and personalization. The project bridges computational analytics and special education practice, offering a novel approach to teacher training by embedding simulation-driven case studies into professional development programs. Expected significance lies in advancing data-driven decision-making for complex disability education, with potential applications in assistive technology development and policy-informed resource allocation.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern residential and commercial appliances, coupled with rising consumer expectations for energy efficiency and durability, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize repair protocols and diagnostic accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for appliance failure modes and simulate the thermodynamic, mechanical, and electrical performance of appliances under varied operational conditions. A key challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous data—including sensor outputs, material degradation patterns, and historical repair records—into unified computational frameworks capable of identifying early-stage malfunctions and recommending targeted interventions. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model stress distribution in components such as compressor valves and drum bearings, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate heat transfer in refrigeration systems, and machine learning algorithms trained on failure datasets to predict component lifespans. These simulations require parallel processing capabilities to handle high-resolution meshes and iterative optimization tasks, which exceed the capacity of standard workstations. Expected outcomes include open-source diagnostic algorithms for common appliance faults, validated thermal management strategies to enhance energy efficiency, and a digital twin framework for virtual testing of repair techniques. By bridging computational engineering with applied technician training, this work aims to reduce repair times, extend appliance service life, and inform curriculum updates in appliance technology programs. The resulting tools will empower technicians to address emerging challenges posed by smart appliances and sustainability standards, ultimately lowering operational costs for consumers and service providers.
cip_title: Appliance Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, install, and service major gas, electric, and microwave consumer appliances such as stoves, refrigerators, dryers, water heaters, washers, dishwashers, and commercial units such as ice makers and coffee makers.

abstract: Pediatric respiratory diseases, including asthma, cystic fibrosis, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia, represent a significant burden on child health, with disease mechanisms often linked to developmental, genetic, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies are limited by an incomplete understanding of how lung growth dynamics interact with disease pathways. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models of pediatric lung development and disease progression, integrating multi-omic, imaging, and clinical data. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets from longitudinal cohorts of patients with respiratory conditions, including high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) scans, single-cell RNA sequencing, and real-time pulmonary function metrics. Computational workflows will employ machine learning frameworks to identify developmental trajectories associated with disease susceptibility and create predictive models of treatment response. Additionally, fluid dynamics simulations will model airflow patterns in anatomically accurate, age-specific airway reconstructions derived from clinical imaging. These simulations will quantify the impact of structural anomalies (e.g., airway malacia) on respiratory mechanics and gas exchange. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational complexity of 3D airway meshing, parallelized simulation runs, and genome-scale association analyses. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers for early disease detection, patient-specific models to optimize ventilator support strategies in critical care, and mechanistic insights into how genetic variants alter cellular behavior in developing lung tissue. By bridging developmental biology and clinical data science, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches for pediatric respiratory diseases, ultimately reducing morbidity and healthcare disparities in this vulnerable population.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention and treatment of all respiratory diseases affecting infants, children, and young adults, based on knowledge of the growth and development of the lung, assessment of respiratory function in infants and children, and experience in a variety of invasive and noninvasive diagnostic techniques.

abstract: The cultivation of ornamental plants is critical for enhancing urban landscapes, supporting ecosystem services, and driving economic value in horticultural industries. However, optimizing ornamental cultivars for aesthetic traits, climate resilience, and pest resistance remains a complex challenge due to the polygenic nature of these characteristics and their interactions with dynamic environmental conditions. Traditional breeding approaches are often slow and resource-intensive, limiting the pace of innovation. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive genomic and phenomic models that accelerate the design of next-generation ornamental plants. Using genomic datasets from diverse ornamental species (e.g., *Rosa*, *Hydrangea*, and ornamental grasses), we will implement genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and machine learning frameworks to identify genetic markers linked to desirable traits such as drought tolerance, bloom longevity, and foliage coloration. Concurrently, 3D plant architecture modeling will simulate growth patterns under varying climatic scenarios to predict phenotypic outcomes. These computational workflows require large-scale parallel processing for genotype-phenotype association analyses, climate resilience simulations, and high-resolution image processing of plant morphologies. The integration of multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, and phenomics) will demand substantial memory and storage capacity, while iterative machine learning training will benefit from GPU-accelerated nodes. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes for targeted breeding, predictive models for trait selection under environmental stress, and optimized growth protocols for commercial nurseries. By reducing trial-and-error in breeding programs, this research will enhance the efficiency of developing ornamentals that meet aesthetic and functional demands in changing climates. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of these analyses, enabling rapid advancements in ornamental horticulture that align with sustainability goals and market needs.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on domesticated plants and plant materials used for decorative and recreational applications and prepares individuals to breed, grow, and utilize ornamental plant varieties for commercial and aesthetic purposes. Includes instruction in applicable plant science subjects, the environmental design and artistic aspects of horticultural product usage, and the management of horticultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive maintenance frameworks for industrial machinery by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex mechanical degradation processes. Traditional maintenance strategies often rely on reactive or schedule-based protocols, which can lead to unplanned downtime, inefficient resource use, and accelerated equipment wear. To address this, the research will develop computational models that integrate multi-physics simulations—including thermal, vibrational, and stress analysis—with machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on real-world sensor data. These models will simulate failure modes in critical components such as bearings, gears, and hydraulic systems under diverse operational conditions. The HPC environment is essential to process high-resolution, time-dependent datasets from industrial IoT sensors and to run parallelized simulations that capture interactions between material fatigue, lubrication dynamics, and environmental factors. A key innovation involves coupling finite element analysis (FEA) with ML-driven anomaly detection to predict failure thresholds with higher accuracy than current statistical methods. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from controlled wear tests and field deployments in manufacturing and transportation sectors. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for optimizing maintenance schedules, reducing downtime by an estimated 15–30%, and extending machinery lifespan. By bridging computational mechanics with data-driven decision-making, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for predictive maintenance, directly supporting workforce training in next-generation repair technologies and fostering resource-efficient practices across technology and technical fields.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of tools, equipment, and machines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic facility management strategies by integrating real-time environmental data, organizational behavior metrics, and predictive spatial analytics. Traditional facility planning approaches often rely on static models that inadequately address the fluctuating demands of modern workplaces, such as hybrid work schedules, evolving safety protocols, and event-driven space reconfigurations. The research problem centers on bridging this gap through high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between physical infrastructure, human behavior, and operational constraints. The computational approach will leverage agent-based modeling to simulate occupant movement and space utilization patterns under varying scenarios, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on IoT-derived datasets (e.g., occupancy sensors, HVAC performance metrics, and ergonomic feedback). Additionally, multi-objective optimization techniques will be applied to balance competing priorities such as energy efficiency, accessibility compliance, and user satisfaction. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-resolution spatial-temporal data across large-scale virtual facilities while iterating thousands of design permutations. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of recommending adaptive floor plans, resource allocations, and risk mitigation strategies in response to real-time operational data. This work aims to advance facility management practices by introducing a methodology that dynamically aligns physical environments with organizational needs, ultimately reducing operational costs by 15–20% in pilot case studies while improving compliance with emerging workplace safety standards. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-source modules to support facility managers in addressing similar challenges across diverse institutional contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract: Blood transfusion efficacy and safety are critically dependent on the integrity of stored blood components, yet the biochemical and cellular mechanisms driving storage-related degradation remain poorly understood. This project seeks to develop predictive computational models to optimize blood component storage protocols, minimize storage lesions in red blood cells (RBCs) and platelets, and extend functional shelf life. A key challenge is the multivariate nature of degradation, which involves dynamic interactions between biochemical pathways, donor-specific biological variability, and storage conditions (e.g., temperature, additive solutions). Existing experimental approaches are resource-intensive and lack the resolution to disentangle these factors systematically. To address this, we propose a multiscale modeling framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations of membrane protein stability, kinetic models of metabolic flux in stored RBCs, and machine learning (ML) to predict component quality from donor metadata and storage parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize models using large-scale proteomic and metabolomic datasets (>10 TB) from longitudinal blood storage studies, simulate rare events in membrane degradation, and train ML algorithms on heterogeneous clinical data. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated simulations for protein folding dynamics and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in metabolic network predictions. Expected outcomes include validated models identifying critical thresholds for pH, oxidative stress, and nutrient depletion in RBCs, as well as a decision-support tool for blood banks to tailor storage protocols to donor-specific risk profiles. This work will directly inform revised guidelines for blood component storage, reduce wastage of expired units, and improve transfusion outcomes for recipients. By aligning computational discovery with clinical blood banking workflows, the project advances translational goals of ensuring blood supply resilience and precision in transfusion medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for the maintenance of an adequate blood supply, blood donor and patient-recipient safety, and appropriate blood utilization. Includes directing the preparation and safe use of specially prepared blood components, including red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma constituents, and marrow or stem cells for transplantation.
