abstract: The increasing demand for precision and sustainability in woodworking manufacturing necessitates advanced computational tools to address the anisotropic and heterogeneous nature of wood. Traditional empirical methods for optimizing toolpaths, predicting material behavior, and minimizing waste struggle to account for the complex interactions between wood grain variability, moisture dynamics, and mechanical stresses during machining. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model these multiphysics processes, enabling predictive insights into woodworking outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) simulations to resolve microscale grain structures and macroscale tool-workpiece interactions. Machine learning models, trained on simulated and experimental datasets, will identify optimal machining parameters (e.g., feed rate, spindle speed) to reduce defects like tear-out and chipping while maximizing material efficiency. The HPC environment will facilitate large-scale parametric studies across diverse wood species, moisture conditions, and tool geometries, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. Additionally, we will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model heat generation and dissipation during high-speed cutting, addressing thermal degradation risks. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools tailored for woodworking applications, validated through collaboration with industrial partners, and a public dataset linking material properties to machining performance. This work aims to advance sustainable manufacturing by reducing material waste by an estimated 15–20% in CNC-based production and providing a foundation for digital twins in artisanal and industrial woodworking. The requested resources will directly support the parallelization of multiscale simulations and the training of deep neural networks on 3D voxelized grain models, which require teraflop-scale computational capacity and GPU-accelerated workflows.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in woodworking, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive modeling capabilities for integrated water resource management under climate uncertainty, with a focus on optimizing flood resilience and drought adaptation strategies in mixed-use watersheds. Current challenges include the computational limitations of resolving fine-scale hydrological processes across large spatial domains while incorporating dynamic climate projections, land-use changes, and competing water demands. To address this, we propose developing a coupled modeling framework that integrates a high-resolution hydrodynamic model (GPU-accelerated HEC-RAS 2D) with a machine learning-enhanced water allocation optimizer. The computational workflow will process multi-decadal ensemble climate data (CMIP6), LiDAR-derived terrain inputs, and real-time sensor networks to simulate flood inundation patterns, groundwater recharge dynamics, and water distribution trade-offs under multiple scenarios. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parallel execution of >10,000 scenario combinations at 1-3 meter spatial resolution across watersheds exceeding 5,000 km², reducing simulation wall times from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include (1) probabilistic flood risk maps quantifying infrastructure vulnerability under extreme precipitation shifts, (2) optimized water allocation policies balancing agricultural, municipal, and ecological needs during drought sequences, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive reservoir operation incorporating ensemble streamflow forecasts. By advancing the spatial-temporal resolution of coupled surface-groundwater modeling at basin scales, this work will provide critical decision support for infrastructure hardening, environmental flow maintenance, and climate adaptation planning. The computational methods developed will be validated against historical flood events and drought responses in three test basins with contrasting hydrological regimes, establishing transferable workflows for water resource agencies managing climate-compounded risks.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for collecting, storing, moving, conserving and controlling surface- and groundwater, including water quality control, water cycle management, management of human and industrial water requirements, water delivery, and flood control.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing vocal performance and pedagogical strategies in opera and classical singing through advanced computational modeling of vocal physiology and acoustic dynamics. Despite extensive training, singers often face variability in technical efficacy, endurance, and injury risk due to the complex interplay of biomechanical, aerodynamic, and resonant factors inherent in vocal production. Current pedagogical methods rely heavily on subjective assessment, lacking granular, data-driven insights into real-time physiological processes during performance. This research proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate vocal fold dynamics, respiratory support mechanisms, and acoustic output under diverse performance conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement multiphysics simulations integrating finite element analysis of vocal fold tissue mechanics, computational fluid dynamics of glottal airflow, and wave propagation models for vocal tract resonance. These simulations will be validated against empirical data from laryngoscopic imaging, electropalatography, and 3D audio recordings of professional operatic performances. Machine learning techniques will further identify patterns linking physiological parameters to acoustic outcomes and perceptual qualities of vocal excellence. The project aims to establish a predictive framework for evaluating technique efficiency, fatigue thresholds, and injury risks across vocal registers, dynamic ranges, and repertoire demands. Outcomes will include open-access tools for real-time biofeedback during vocal training, personalized exercise regimens to enhance endurance, and evidence-based guidelines for repertoire selection tailored to individual physiological profiles. By bridging computational science and performing arts pedagogy, this work will advance sustainable vocal practices, reduce career-limiting injuries among performers, and elevate artistic outcomes in operatic training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the human voice and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers in concert, choir, opera, or other forms of singing. Includes instruction in voice pedagogy, diction, vocal physiology and exercise, expressive movement, repertoire, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic resource allocation and communication efficiency in high-traffic receptionist environments through advanced computational modeling. The problem centers on the escalating complexity of frontline public relations tasks in modern service-oriented businesses, where receptionists must balance real-time caller demands, visitor management, equipment operations, and schedule coordination under unpredictable workloads. Traditional training protocols and static scheduling systems fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these variables, leading to bottlenecks, service delays, and reputational risks. We propose developing an adaptive simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-agent interactions across three dimensions: 1) stochastic call arrival patterns and queue management, 2) visitor flow optimization under spatial constraints, and 3) cognitive load balancing for human operators interfacing with automated systems. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation, graph neural networks for predicting service cascade failures, and reinforcement learning agents trained on synthetic datasets representing diverse organizational layouts and communication infrastructures. By parallelizing millions of scenario iterations across GPU clusters, we aim to identify robust decision policies that minimize response latency while preserving human operator effectiveness. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for (a) quantifying environment-specific capacity thresholds, (b) generating adaptive training modules based on stress-test simulations, and (c) recommending hybrid human-AI task allocation strategies. This work bridges operational research, human factors engineering, and service systems design, offering novel methodologies to enhance frontline business interfaces in healthcare, hospitality, and enterprise services—sectors where receptionist performance directly impacts organizational efficiency but remains understudied in computational contexts. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving sufficient parameter space exploration and real-time simulation fidelity across heterogeneous service environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform frontline public relations duties for a business, organization, or answering service. Includes instruction in telephone answering techniques, responding to information requests, keeping caller and/or visitor records, placing business calls, operating telephone switchboards and/or other communications equipment, relaying incoming and interoffice calls, schedule maintenance, and public relations skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational models for optimizing movement therapy and education protocols. Movement-based interventions rely on nuanced, individualized approaches to enhance somatic awareness and psychophysical function. However, current methods for analyzing movement patterns, neuromuscular coordination, and therapeutic outcomes remain limited by the scalability of manual observation and the computational demands of processing high-dimensional biomechanical data. This research aims to address these gaps by creating predictive models that integrate multimodal data—including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and patient-reported outcomes—to identify optimal movement strategies for diverse populations. A key challenge is the real-time processing and analysis of large datasets to enable dynamic feedback during therapy sessions, which requires significant computational power. The proposed computational approach involves three phases: (1) developing machine learning algorithms to classify movement patterns and predict therapeutic responsiveness using historical clinical data; (2) simulating neuromuscular dynamics under varying therapeutic constraints to model ideal movement adaptations; and (3) implementing a real-time biofeedback system powered by GPU-accelerated neural networks to guide personalized interventions. By utilizing HPC clusters, these workflows will efficiently manage terabytes of kinematic and physiological data while running parallel simulations to test hypotheses about movement efficiency and injury prevention. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting patient-specific therapeutic gains, a framework for automating movement quality assessment, and open-source tools to bridge computational analysis with clinical practice. This work will enhance the precision of movement therapies, reduce trial-and-error in protocol design, and establish scalable computational methods for a field traditionally reliant on qualitative observation. The results will directly inform curriculum development in movement education, emphasizing data-driven strategies to improve training outcomes for future practitioners.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use functional and expressive integration strategies to help promote somatic awareness and optimal psychophysical functioning. Includes instruction in skilled touch techniques, kinesthetic awareness processes, movement observation, patterning, client assessment and guidance, verbal and nonverbal communication, practice management, professional standards and ethics, and specific therapeutic and educational modalities

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in welding process optimization and defect mitigation through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations in traditional experimental and analytical methods. Welding processes involve complex multi-physics interactions, including transient heat transfer, molten metal fluid dynamics, phase transformations, and residual stress development, which collectively influence joint integrity, mechanical performance, and susceptibility to defects such as porosity or cracking. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture these interrelated phenomena at relevant spatial and temporal scales, while simplified analytical models lack predictive accuracy for emerging materials and advanced welding techniques. To bridge this gap, this research will implement high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model arc welding processes across multiple scales. These simulations will integrate thermodynamic material properties, non-linear constitutive relationships, and machine learning-derived phase transformation kinetics to predict thermal histories, microstructural evolution, and stress distributions in carbon steel and aluminum alloy welds. Additionally, a parallelized Monte Carlo framework will assess process robustness by quantifying sensitivity to parameter variations inherent in real-world manufacturing environments. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high mesh resolution required for accurate fusion zone prediction, coupled with the need for parametric studies spanning hundreds of process configurations. Expected outcomes include validated models for optimizing heat input, travel speed, and post-weld heat treatment parameters, with direct applications to robotic welding automation and additive manufacturing. The results will advance fundamental understanding of weld pool solidification mechanics and provide a computational framework for virtual qualification of welding procedures, reducing reliance on physical trial-and-error testing. By enabling predictive defect analysis and microstructure control, this work supports the development of next-generation welding codes and inspection protocols for critical infrastructure applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the design and engineering of welding and joining systems and the implementation of welding processes. Includes instruction in materials science; computer-aided design; welding design; welding processes; welding metallurgy; automation and robotics; and codes, inspections, testing, and quality assurance.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in culturally responsive educational tools for Indigenous K-12 students by developing computational models to analyze and enhance the integration of Tribal knowledge systems into STEM curricula. Despite growing recognition of the pedagogical value of Indigenous epistemologies, educators in Tribal schools often lack scalable, evidence-based frameworks to adapt existing materials while maintaining cultural and linguistic fidelity. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process multimodal educational datasets—including digitized oral histories, language corpuses, and student interaction metrics—from three partner Tribal school districts. Machine learning techniques will identify patterns in how culturally grounded content influences engagement and conceptual understanding, while agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of different curricular scaffolding strategies in diverse classroom contexts. Key computational challenges include natural language processing of low-resource Indigenous languages with polysynthetic structures and geospatial analysis of place-based learning activities tied to specific ecosystems. Outcomes will include an open-access toolkit for generating adaptive lesson plans that align with both state academic standards and locally defined cultural priorities, as well as a repository of anonymized interaction data to support future research in Indigenous pedagogies. By leveraging parallelized workflows to handle heterogeneous data types and iterative model training, this work aims to empower Tribal educators with computationally informed strategies that honor students’ cultural identities while improving measurable learning outcomes in STEM fields. The requested resources will enable large-scale validation of these approaches across distinct linguistic and regional contexts, ensuring broader applicability to Indigenous education initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of instructional and advising services for American Indian, Alaska Native, and Hawaiian Native students at various learning levels and that prepares individuals to perform teaching and administrative functions in Tribal/First Nation schools. Includes instruction in the cultural traditions and social patterns, history and politics, learning styles and issues, curriculum design, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling techniques and social issues, rural education services, distance education, adult education techniques, school administration, applicable laws and regulations, and research issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation for private security and loss prevention operations, addressing the challenge of balancing proactive risk mitigation with cost efficiency in complex, real-world environments. Traditional security resource planning relies heavily on static schedules and human intuition, which often fail to adapt to evolving threats, spatial vulnerabilities, and fluctuating client needs. Our research proposes an innovative approach integrating geospatial risk modeling, behavioral pattern analysis, and reinforcement learning to create adaptive patrol routing and personnel deployment strategies. Using anonymized historical incident data, sensor network inputs, and environmental variables, we will train machine learning models to predict high-probability risk zones across temporal and spatial dimensions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets of movement patterns and security logs, running parallelized simulations of patrol efficacy under thousands of scenario permutations, and optimizing neural networks for real-time decision support. The computational workflow will employ graph-based algorithms to model facility layouts as threat propagation networks, coupled with Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in emergent risks such as coordinated diversion tactics. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that reduces false alarm responses by ≥30% while maintaining sub-5-minute critical incident response times, validated through computational experiments mirroring ISO 31000 risk management standards. This interdisciplinary work bridges operational security protocols with computational logistics, advancing predictive analytics capabilities for an industry that currently lacks AI-driven optimization frameworks tailored to its unique constraints. The resulting models will be shared as open-source modules to foster innovation in physical security resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine inspection, patrol and crime prevention services for private clients. Includes instruction in the provision of personal protection as well as property security.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and control of decentralized, multi-agent quantum-thermal systems (QTS) in hybrid energy networks—an emerging niche at the intersection of quantum engineering, thermodynamics, and distributed systems. Current approaches to managing thermal and quantum energy flows in microgrids remain siloed, relying on classical optimization methods ill-suited for real-time coordination of quantum-enhanced devices (e.g., coherent heat pumps, superconducting sensors) with conventional infrastructure. The research problem centers on overcoming scalability bottlenecks in modeling dynamic interactions between quantum and classical subsystems, which exhibit nonlinear, high-dimensional behavior under fluctuating loads. The computational approach integrates tensor network simulations of quantum thermal states with graph-based reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize energy distribution across hybrid networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for training graph-RL agents on large-scale parametric sweeps of QTS configurations (10^4–10^5 nodes) and for executing parallelized density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations to capture entanglement-driven thermal transport. Expected outcomes include an open-source library for adaptive QTS control, validated against experimental data from collaborating labs, and generalized protocols for minimizing entropy generation in heterogeneous energy systems. This work aims to establish foundational principles for engineering quantum-aware thermal networks, with potential applications in precision manufacturing, quantum data center cooling, and grid resilience. The project bridges gaps between quantum thermodynamics and distributed control theory, advancing a new paradigm for sustainable energy infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to solve a wide variety of practical problems in industry, social organization, public works, and commerce. Includes instruction in undifferentiated and individualized programs in engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive educational tools and intervention strategies for students with multiple disabilities. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) often rely on manual analysis of behavioral, sensory, and academic data, which limits the scalability and personalization of interventions for learners with complex, co-occurring needs. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing multimodal datasets—such as eye-tracking, gesture recognition, and communication device logs—to model student engagement and predict optimal instructional pathways. The project will employ machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, to analyze heterogeneous data streams from classroom observations and assistive technology use. These models will be trained to identify patterns in student responsiveness to specific interventions, accounting for variables like sensory processing profiles, motor limitations, and communication modalities. By parallelizing large-scale simulations of hypothetical IEP scenarios on HPC clusters, the team will iteratively refine adaptive learning algorithms that dynamically adjust content delivery, pacing, and sensory supports. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational framework for generating evidence-based IEP recommendations, validated through collaboration with special education teachers. This framework aims to reduce trial-and-error in intervention design while maintaining alignment with legal and pedagogical requirements for students with multiple disabilities. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the project’s data volume (estimated at 50+ TB of annotated video and sensor data) and enabling real-time analysis during classroom pilot studies. Successful implementation could transform how educators individualize instruction for this population, bridging gaps between assistive technology innovation and practical teaching workflows.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methodologies in architectural design, specifically targeting the emergent niche of generative systems for culturally adaptive urban spaces. Traditional architectural workflows often prioritize efficiency or aesthetics but lack robust frameworks for integrating dynamic socio-cultural data—such as community interaction patterns, historical narratives, or localized spatial practices—into generative design processes. This gap limits the ability of architects to create environments that respond meaningfully to evolving cultural contexts. To address this, the project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining parametric modeling, agent-based simulations, and machine learning (ML) to generate architectural prototypes that dynamically adapt to socio-cultural inputs. The research problem centers on developing scalable algorithms capable of processing heterogeneous datasets (e.g., ethnographic surveys, mobility traces, and heritage records) and translating them into spatial configurations that balance structural feasibility with cultural resonance. Computational workflows will involve training ML models on curated datasets of culturally significant architectural case studies, followed by iterative simulations using HPC to optimize multi-objective design criteria (e.g., spatial connectivity, material efficiency, and symbolic meaning). Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework for culturally adaptive design, validated through case studies in post-industrial urban redevelopment contexts. The project’s significance lies in bridging architectural theory with computational innovation, offering tools to address pressing challenges in equitable urban regeneration. By utilizing HPC to manage complex, non-linear relationships between cultural data and spatial design, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for interdisciplinary architectural research, with implications for policy, heritage preservation, and community-driven design practices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture and related programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Mental health interventions often exhibit variable efficacy across individuals, a challenge exacerbated by the complex interplay of neurobiological, genetic, and psychosocial factors. Current approaches to personalizing treatments remain limited by fragmented data integration and insufficient computational power to model dynamic, multiscale interactions. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to analyze multimodal datasets—including functional neuroimaging, polygenic risk scores, real-time behavioral sensing, and electronic health records—to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response in major depressive disorder (MDD). The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in modeling non-linear relationships across heterogeneous data types while preserving temporal and contextual granularity. Leveraging GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines, we will implement graph neural networks to map neurocognitive networks, coupled with transformer-based architectures for longitudinal outcome prediction. Federated learning protocols will enable privacy-preserving analysis across decentralized clinical datasets. The computational workflow will optimize resource allocation through adaptive scaling of memory-intensive tasks (e.g., whole-brain connectome analysis) and parallelized Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) a validated predictive model of MDD treatment response with >30% improvement over current clinical benchmarks, 2) identification of latent neuro-behavioral subtypes associated with differential outcomes, and 3) an open-source computational framework for real-time adaptive intervention design. This work bridges gaps between computational psychiatry, neuroinformatics, and clinical decision science, offering a paradigm shift in precision mental health through HPC-driven analytics. The requested resources will directly support the training of large-scale foundation models on integrated biological-behavioral data, a capability currently absent in community mental health research infrastructure.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in producing high-resolution, dynamic illustrations that integrate real-time interactivity and complex visual effects, which are increasingly demanded in fields such as digital publishing, augmented reality (AR), and interactive media. Current workflows for illustrators are constrained by the limitations of consumer-grade hardware, particularly when rendering intricate 3D models, simulating physical materials (e.g., fabric, lighting), or applying machine learning (ML) techniques to automate stylistic adaptations across multi-platform deliverables. The research problem centers on scaling artistic workflows to accommodate large datasets—such as 3D-scanned environments or generative asset libraries—while maintaining the precision and aesthetic nuance required in professional illustration. To overcome these barriers, the project proposes a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources for distributed rendering, parallelized simulation of material behaviors, and training ML models for style transfer and asset generation. Custom pipelines will be developed to optimize tasks like batch-processing thousands of high-fidelity frames for animated illustrations or dynamically adjusting vector-based designs for cross-media formatting. The use of GPU-accelerated nodes will enable real-time collaboration tools for artists working on shared virtual canvases, reducing latency in iterative design processes. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools tailored for illustrators, benchmarks for HPC-driven artistic workflows, and case studies demonstrating scalable solutions for client-driven projects, such as interactive children’s books or AR-enhanced fashion catalogs. By bridging the gap between computational scalability and artistic practice, this work aims to expand the technical possibilities for illustrators, reduce production bottlenecks, and establish new standards for computationally intensive creative workflows in the visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: Aromatherapy’s therapeutic potential is increasingly recognized, yet its mechanistic underpinnings remain poorly understood due to the complexity of essential oil compositions and their interactions with human physiology. This project seeks to address this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model the molecular dynamics of bioactive compounds in essential oils and their effects on neurological and immunological pathways. The research problem centers on the lack of systematic, quantitative frameworks to predict how specific oil blends interact with cellular targets, limiting clinical validation and optimization of aromatherapeutic protocols. Using a computational approach, we will simulate interactions between key terpenes, sesquiterpenes, and phenolic compounds found in essential oils (e.g., lavender, eucalyptus, frankincense) and human ion channels, G-protein-coupled receptors, and cytokine networks. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations will be performed to characterize binding affinities, conformational changes, and thermodynamic properties of these interactions. HPC resources are critical due to the need for large-scale parallel processing to handle combinatorial complexity (e.g., multi-component oil mixtures) and long-timescale MD simulations (µs-ms range) to capture rare binding events. Expected outcomes include identifying synergistic compound combinations that modulate pain perception, inflammation, or stress responses, validated against in vitro assays. Additionally, machine learning models trained on simulation data will predict optimal oil blends for specific physiological outcomes. This work will establish a foundational computational platform for aromatherapy research, enabling data-driven design of therapeutic protocols, reducing reliance on trial-and-error practices, and informing future clinical studies. The project bridges computational chemistry, systems biology, and clinical aromatherapy, offering a novel paradigm to advance evidence-based practice in this emerging health science niche.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic care through the preparation and application of extracted essential oils from plants, including flowers (botanicals), roots, berries, and bark. Includes instruction in aromatherapy history and theory, basic physiology of absorption, aromachemistry, organic chemistry, botanical taxonomy, carrier oils, essential oils, extraction methods, blending techniques, application methods, safety, client consultation and treatment planning, business management, professional standards and ethics, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of syntactic and morphological patterns in historical and contemporary Czech literary texts. Despite the growing availability of digitized Czech corpora, large-scale investigations into linguistic evolution and stylistic variation remain constrained by the computational demands of processing complex, morphologically rich structures across centuries of texts. The research will focus on two interrelated problems: (1) quantifying syntactic shifts in Czech prose from the National Revival period (late 18th–19th centuries) to post-1989 literature, and (2) modeling dialectal influences on morphological choices in regional narratives. Computational workflows will integrate rule-based morphological analyzers with transformer-based language models (e.g., Czech BERT variants) to disambiguate lexical and grammatical features at scale. Parallelized pipelines will process approximately 10TB of text data, employing distributed computing for frequency analysis, dependency parsing, and temporal clustering. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive diachronic profile of Czech syntactic complexity, a geolocated dataset linking morphological trends to regional dialects, and open-source tools optimized for Czech literary analysis. These resources will directly support philological research on language standardization processes while providing methodological frameworks applicable to under-resourced Slavic languages. The project addresses critical gaps in Czech linguistic scholarship by enabling data-driven inquiry into literature’s role in shaping national identity, with broader implications for computational humanities methodologies in morphologically complex languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Czech language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the automated curation and semantic enrichment of large-scale, heterogeneous digital collections within library and information science. As cultural heritage institutions increasingly digitize materials, traditional metadata generation methods—often manual and labor-intensive—struggle to scale, resulting in incomplete or inconsistent descriptions that hinder discoverability and long-term preservation. The research problem centers on developing computational workflows to automate metadata extraction, entity linking, and contextual analysis across multimodal datasets (text, images, audiovisual content) while adhering to ethical frameworks for culturally sensitive materials. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models, including transformer-based architectures fine-tuned for historical and domain-specific language, alongside computer vision techniques for object recognition and spatial analysis in digitized artifacts. Computational workflows will integrate probabilistic graph databases to model uncertain or conflicting metadata relationships and enable dynamic knowledge representation. HPC resources are critical for training domain-adapted machine learning models on terabyte-scale corpora, optimizing parallel processing of non-uniform digital objects, and simulating user interaction patterns to refine retrieval algorithms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for libraries to automate metadata enhancement, a benchmarking framework for evaluating algorithmic bias in cultural heritage datasets, and novel strategies for preserving contextual integrity in aggregated digital collections. By bridging gaps between computational scalability and curatorial best practices, this work aims to advance sustainable infrastructure for next-generation digital archives while contributing methodological innovations at the intersection of information science, ethical AI, and computational humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the knowledge and skills required to develop, organize, store, retrieve, administer, and facilitate the use of local, remote, and networked collections of information in print, audiovisual, and electronic formats and that prepares individuals for professional service as librarians and information consultants.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between cultural practices and social resilience in small-scale societies, with a focus on how ritual behaviors adapt to environmental and demographic stressors. Anthropological research on cultural transmission often relies on qualitative ethnography or limited quantitative models, but the complexity of multi-generational cultural systems—particularly when integrating ecological, demographic, and symbolic variables—exceeds the capacity of conventional computational tools. We propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate cultural evolution across hypothetical and historically informed scenarios, incorporating high-resolution ethnographic data on kinship networks, ritual participation, and resource-sharing practices. The models will parameterize variables such as environmental shocks, migration rates, and intergroup conflict to test hypotheses about cultural persistence and transformation. A second component employs natural language processing (NLP) to analyze comparative ethnographic texts from the Human Relations Area Files (HRAF), training transformer-based models to detect patterns in ritual descriptions that correlate with societal-scale adaptive outcomes. HPC resources are critical for scaling ABM simulations to realistic population sizes (10^4–10^5 agents) over multi-century timeframes, conducting parameter sweeps across diverse cultural configurations, and processing terabytes of unstructured textual data with deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying computational signatures of cultural resilience, (2) generating testable frameworks for linking micro-scale ritual behaviors to macro-scale social durability, and (3) advancing methodological integration between ethnographic fieldwork and computational anthropology. Results will contribute to theoretical debates about cultural adaptation while providing open-source tools for simulating culturally-grounded decision-making processes, with implications for understanding societal responses to contemporary crises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of culture and the relationship of culture to other aspects of social life. Includes instruction in cultural anthropology, anthropological theory, ethnography, linguistics, and quantitative and qualitative research methods.

abstract: The utilization of wood and wood-derived materials in industrial applications requires precise understanding of their structural, chemical, and mechanical properties to optimize processing efficiency and product performance. However, traditional experimental methods for analyzing complex lignocellulosic interactions in wood and pulp systems are often time-intensive, cost-prohibitive, and limited in resolving multi-scale phenomena. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced computational models that bridge molecular-scale interactions to macro-scale material behavior in wood products and pulp-paper systems. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) simulating the dynamic degradation of lignin and hemicellulose during thermo-mechanical pulping using molecular dynamics (MD) and coarse-grained modeling to identify energy-efficient processing pathways, and (2) employing finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning to predict the anisotropic mechanical behavior of engineered wood composites under varying environmental conditions. These computational workflows will integrate experimental data from spectroscopy and mechanical testing to validate multi-physics models. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale simulations involving millions of particles in MD systems, iterative optimization of composite designs, and real-time analysis of heterogeneous datasets. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel pulping catalysts to reduce chemical consumption, predictive models for composite durability in humid environments, and open-source simulation tools for the wood products community. By elucidating fundamental structure-property relationships in lignocellulosic materials, this work aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices, reduce energy inputs in pulp processing, and accelerate the development of high-performance, climate-resilient wood products aligned with circular economy principles.
cip_title: Wood Science and Wood Products/ Pulp and Paper Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the analysis of the properties and behavior of wood and wood products and the development of processes for converting wood into paper and other products. Includes instruction in wood classification and testing, product development, manufacturing and processing technologies, and the design and development of related equipment and systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical gaps in health professions education by developing an adaptive, AI-driven simulation platform to train clinicians in navigating complex ethical dilemmas arising from emerging technologies in patient care. Current pedagogical approaches often rely on static case studies, which lack the dynamic, context-sensitive decision-making required for real-world scenarios involving AI diagnostics, robotic surgery, or genomic data stewardship. The proposed computational framework will integrate natural language processing, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and immersive virtual environments to simulate ethically charged clinical interactions that evolve in response to trainee decisions. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on curated corpora of historical ethical cases, real-time rendering of branching narrative trajectories, and parallel processing of simulated patient outcomes across diverse demographic profiles. The platform will employ graph neural networks to model cascading consequences of clinical choices and Bayesian inference engines to quantify uncertainty in moral reasoning patterns. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated computational model of ethical decision-making under technological mediation, 2) quantitative metrics for assessing trainee competency in techno-ethical reasoning, and 3) open-source tools for generating culturally responsive training scenarios. This work bridges health humanities with computational social science, offering novel methods to prepare clinicians for challenges at the intersection of biomedical innovation, patient autonomy, and algorithmic bias. The requested resources will enable large-scale validation trials comparing simulation-trained cohorts with traditional learners through multimodal data integration, including eye-tracking patterns, dialogue analysis, and physiological stress markers during simulated consultations. By establishing computational infrastructure for ethics education research, this project aims to transform how health professionals develop moral agency in technology-saturated clinical environments.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in evidence-based decision-making for human services programs by developing computational models to simulate the dynamics of social service delivery and its impact on vulnerable populations. Despite the growing complexity of social challenges—such as housing insecurity, mental health crises, and systemic inequities—agencies often rely on fragmented data and static analyses, limiting their ability to predict outcomes or optimize interventions. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct large-scale, multi-agent simulation models that integrate demographic, socioeconomic, and service utilization data from public agencies, nonprofits, and community surveys. These models will capture interactions between individuals, service providers, and policy environments at a granular level, enabling dynamic scenario testing under varying resource allocation strategies. Computational methods will include machine learning for pattern recognition in service access disparities, network analysis to map interagency collaboration efficiencies, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risks associated with policy alternatives. The scale of data integration (spanning millions of anonymized client records and longitudinal outcomes) necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing and real-time sensitivity analyses. Anticipated outcomes include a framework to identify service delivery bottlenecks, predict the cascading effects of funding changes, and recommend equity-centered resource distribution plans. By translating computational insights into actionable policy tools, this work aims to strengthen the capacity of human services organizations to address systemic inequities, reduce operational inefficiencies, and improve program outcomes for marginalized communities. The project will also produce open-source tools tailored for non-technical stakeholders, bridging the gap between computational social science and applied public administration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and provision of human and social services to individuals and communities and prepares individuals to work in public and private human services agencies and organizations. Includes instruction in the social sciences, psychology, principles of social service, human services policy, planning and evaluation, social services law and administration, and applications to particular issues, services, localities, and populations.

abstract: Hospice and palliative care patients often experience complex, dynamic symptom burdens and heterogeneous trajectories of functional decline, yet existing prognostic tools lack precision for individualized care planning. This project seeks to develop computational models that integrate multimodal clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), patient-reported outcomes, and wearable sensor metrics—to predict symptom exacerbation, functional decline, and survival in patients with advanced serious illnesses. A key challenge lies in analyzing high-dimensional, temporally irregular datasets while accounting for interactions between biological, psychological, and social determinants of outcomes. To address this, we propose a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble models combining recurrent neural networks, transformer architectures for clinical note analysis, and Bayesian survival models. Computational workflows will process structured EHR data (medications, lab values, diagnoses) alongside unstructured clinician notes (processed via natural language processing) and continuous wearable data (activity levels, vital signs). The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory CPU nodes for large-scale survival analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for 30- and 90-day trajectories of pain, dyspnea, and functional status, (2) identification of modifiable risk factors for acute care utilization in hospice populations, and (3) open-source tools for temporal fusion of palliative care datasets. By enabling real-time analysis of longitudinal data from 15,000+ patients across three health systems, this HPC-supported approach aims to advance personalized goal-concordant care while addressing computational bottlenecks in palliative care research. The resource allocation will directly support model training at scale, sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups, and simulation studies to evaluate clinical implementation scenarios.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hospice and Palliative Medicine

abstract: Commercial fishing operations face critical challenges in balancing economic productivity with ecological sustainability, while ensuring crew safety and regulatory compliance. Traditional methods for optimizing fishing routes, predicting fish stocks, and assessing equipment durability under dynamic marine conditions are often inadequate due to the complex interplay of environmental, biological, and operational variables. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models that simulate marine ecosystems, vessel dynamics, and gear performance at unprecedented resolutions. We will integrate multi-source data streams, including satellite-derived oceanographic data, historical catch records, and real-time sensor inputs from fishing vessels, to create predictive frameworks using machine learning algorithms. Hydrodynamic models will simulate vessel behavior and gear stress under varying sea states, enabling the identification of optimal fishing zones and equipment configurations that minimize environmental impact and mechanical failure risks. Additionally, agent-based models will explore the long-term effects of different harvesting strategies on fish population resilience, supporting adaptive management aligned with regulatory frameworks. The computational demands of these multi-scale, spatially explicit models necessitate HPC resources for parallel processing, large-scale parameter optimization, and stochastic uncertainty analyses. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for reducing bycatch, enhancing fuel efficiency, and prolonging equipment lifespans, thereby improving the economic viability and sustainability of commercial fisheries. By translating these results into open-access decision-support tools and training modules, this research will directly benefit industry stakeholders, policymakers, and vocational training programs focused on modernizing fishing practices in line with 21st-century technological and environmental standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as commercial fishermen, fishing operations supervisors or in related fishing industry operations. Includes instruction in fishing vessel operation; fishing equipment operation and maintenance; equipment repair; catch identification, sorting, and storage; safety procedures; record keeping; and applicable legal regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational modeling of sign language linguistics by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and sociolinguistic complexity of American Sign Language (ASL) and other global sign languages. Despite advances in natural language processing (NLP) for spoken and written languages, computational tools for sign languages remain underdeveloped due to the unique visual-spatial modality of signing, which integrates handshape, movement, facial expressions, and 3D articulatory dynamics. Current methods struggle to scale with the high-dimensional data inherent in sign language corpora, limiting progress in phonological, syntactic, and sociolinguistic research. This project proposes a multi-modal computational framework to model sign language phonology and syntax using parallelized processing of 3D motion-capture datasets, video annotations, and linguistic metadata from ASL, Auslan, LSF, and Shuwa jiten corpora. Deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models adapted for sequential visual data) will be trained to identify cross-linguistic patterns in morphological productivity and syntactic non-manual markers, while graph-based algorithms will map sociolinguistic variation across deaf communities. HPC resources are essential to handle the terabyte-scale datasets, optimize neural networks for real-time annotation, and run simulations of diachronic language change. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated sign language analysis, a comparative database of sign language structures, and novel theoretical insights into the universality of linguistic features across modalities. By bridging computational and theoretical sign language linguistics, this work aims to advance equitable language technologies for deaf users, inform policy on sign language preservation, and reshape foundational models of human language to encompass visual-spatial grammar systems.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Linguistics of ASL and Other Sign Languages
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and scholarly study of the development, structure, and use of American Sign Language (ASL) and other visual signed languages, both as vehicles for communication within the deaf community and in relation to spoken and written languages. Includes instruction in cognitive linguistics; ASL and sign language phonology, syntax, and morphology; sociolinguistics of the deaf community; comparative linguistics; and studies of specific sign languages, including, but not limited to, ASL, Auslan (Australian Sign Language), LSF (French Sign Language), Shuwa jiten (Japanese Sign Language), HamNoSys (German Sign Language), and Gestuno.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern platemaking and digital imaging workflows, which face growing demands for precision, speed, and sustainability in the communication and journalism sectors. Traditional plate production methods and direct-to-press workflows often struggle with material waste, inconsistent quality in high-resolution outputs, and computational bottlenecks when processing complex graphic datasets. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to optimize image rendering, plate surface simulation, and color calibration processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support large-scale image analysis, including the training of machine learning models to predict plate degradation patterns under varying press conditions, as well as GPU-accelerated simulations of ink dispersion dynamics on novel substrate materials. The project will integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as 3D surface scans, spectral color profiles, and press performance metrics—into a unified optimization pipeline, leveraging parallelized algorithms to reduce computational overhead in preprocessing workflows. Expected outcomes include a reduction in material waste by 20–30% through predictive modeling of plate longevity, improved color fidelity in high-speed printing environments, and a 40–50% acceleration in digital prepress workflows for complex graphic designs. By bridging gaps between traditional platemaking techniques and data-driven computational methods, this work will enhance the sustainability and technical capacity of imaging workflows critical to publishing, packaging, and digital media production. The requested HPC resources will enable iterative testing of hybrid (physical-digital) workflow models at scales unachievable with local computing infrastructure, directly benefiting academic training programs in platemaking and industry partners seeking to adopt next-generation imaging systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare film, digital data, and surfaces to reproduce printed or graphic images. Includes instruction in platemaking, stripping, camerawork, imposition, digital imaging, computer direct-to-plate and direct-to-press, and related processes.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven diagnostic support tool to enhance the precision of anterior eye segment analysis in optometric practice, with a focus on addressing subtle corneal irregularities that are frequently underdetected in routine screenings. Optometric technicians and assistants routinely capture high-resolution imaging data, including corneal topography and optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans, but current clinical workflows lack automated systems to identify early-stage keratoconus, post-surgical ectasia, or subclinical dry eye-related corneal distortion. The research problem centers on bridging this diagnostic gap by leveraging computational power to analyze multimodal ophthalmic datasets with greater sensitivity than manual interpretation allows. We will train convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on a curated dataset of 50,000 anonymized corneal images, integrating topography, tomography, and tear film stability metrics to detect microstructural anomalies. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing 3D OCT volumes (averaging 1.2 GB per scan) and optimizing feature extraction across heterogeneous data types through parallelized processing. The computational workflow will employ PyTorch for model development, with Bayesian optimization to refine architecture hyperparameters, while maintaining interpretability through gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) visualizations. Expected outcomes include a validated prediction framework capable of flagging suspicious cases with 92% sensitivity (target) at specificity ≥85%, benchmarked against gold-standard Scheimpflug imaging. This tool would empower optometric technicians to prioritize high-risk patients for comprehensive evaluation, potentially reducing progression to vision-impairing stages of corneal disease. The project advances health sciences by creating a novel interface between ophthalmic imaging, computational biomechanics, and clinical decision support systems specifically tailored to optometric paraprofessional workflows. Successful implementation could establish new standards for preventive eye care through enhanced human-AI collaboration in primary vision health settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist optometrists in providing patient care, administering examinations and treatments, and performing office administrative functions. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology of the eye, visual testing, patient communication, patient preparation, medications and administration, dispensing and fitting of eyeglasses and contact lenses, record-keeping, and office management skills.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in predicting molecular interactions, optimizing pharmacokinetics, and mitigating off-target effects. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational framework to accelerate the design of small-molecule inhibitors targeting enzyme mutations associated with antibiotic resistance in bacterial pathogens. A critical barrier lies in simulating the dynamic conformational changes of mutant enzymes and their binding landscapes with sufficient accuracy and throughput. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, and machine learning (ML)-guided virtual screening. The MD simulations will model mutant β-lactamase enzymes over microsecond timescales to identify cryptic binding pockets and allosteric networks. Concurrently, FEP will quantify relative binding affinities of lead compounds across 20 clinically relevant enzyme variants. A neural network trained on simulation data and experimental inhibition profiles will predict resistance-liability scores for candidate molecules. This integrated approach requires substantial computational power: an estimated 250,000 core-hours for MD sampling, 50,000 GPU-hours for FEP, and distributed training of deep learning models on multi-node clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) a ranked list of inhibitor candidates with resistance-evasion potential, (2) mechanistic insights into mutation-driven binding plasticity, and (3) open-source tools for mutation-adaptive drug design. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the need for parallelized sampling of large protein systems and iterative ML optimization—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Success in this work will directly inform experimental synthesis and testing pipelines, reducing the empirical burden of combating antibiotic resistance. By bridging conformational dynamics, binding thermodynamics, and predictive analytics, this project aims to advance computational methodologies in pharmaceutical sciences while addressing a pressing public health challenge.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the basic sciences that underlie drugs and drug therapy and that prepares individuals for further study and/or careers in pharmaceutical science and research, pharmaceutical administration and sales, biotechnology, drug manufacturing, regulatory affairs, and related fields. Includes instruction in mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, statistics, pharmaceutics, pharmacology and toxicology, dosage formulation, manufacturing, quality assurance, and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic research on understudied Southeast Asian languages, focusing on syntactic diversity, language contact phenomena, and the development of scalable natural language processing (NLP) tools for low-resource languages in the region. While Southeast Asia hosts exceptional linguistic diversity—including Thai, Burmese, Javanese, and Tagalog—many languages lack robust digital corpora or computational models, hindering comparative analysis and preservation efforts. Current NLP frameworks, optimized for Indo-European languages, perform poorly on Southeast Asian languages due to structural differences in morphology, syntax, and phonology. This project addresses these gaps through two interconnected computational workflows. First, we will employ transformer-based models and distributed training techniques to process and annotate multilingual text corpora from archival sources, field recordings, and digitized literature, prioritizing tonal languages (e.g., Thai) and agglutinative languages (e.g., Malay dialects). Second, we will develop phylogenetic models to trace contact-induced grammatical changes across Austroasiatic and Malayo-Polynesian languages, using probabilistic programming to infer historical relationships from syntactic and lexical features. HPC resources are critical for training large language models on heterogeneous data (including non-Roman scripts), running parallel simulations of language evolution, and optimizing memory-intensive alignment algorithms for comparative linguistics. Expected outcomes include open-access annotated corpora, transfer learning frameworks for cross-linguistic NLP applications, and novel insights into language diversification in maritime Southeast Asia. By integrating computational methods with linguistic theory, this work will support endangered language revitalization and expand the methodological toolkit for regional studies, directly benefiting researchers in Southeast Asian linguistics and digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the modern languages spoken in mainland Southeast Asia and the Indonesian and Philippines Archipelagoes, including, but not limited to, members of the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing evidence-based clinical decision-making in acute care settings through advanced computational modeling of patient outcomes. Current nursing practice relies on static clinical guidelines, which often fail to account for dynamic, multifactorial interactions between patient comorbidities, treatment protocols, and staffing variables. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model patient trajectories under varying care scenarios, integrating electronic health record (EHR) data from 350,000+ hospital encounters, nurse staffing patterns, and real-time vital sign streams. Machine learning architectures, including transformer-based temporal models and graph neural networks, will be implemented to capture longitudinal relationships between nursing interventions and outcomes such as pressure injury development, sepsis progression, and 30-day readmissions. The computational workflow requires distributed training of ensemble models across GPU nodes to handle high-dimensional temporal data while maintaining interpretability through attention mechanisms. Sensitivity analyses will quantify how nurse-to-patient ratios and intervention timing modulate risk profiles. By leveraging parallelized parameter optimization, the project aims to generate actionable thresholds for early clinical escalation and personalized care pathways. Anticipated outcomes include open-source predictive tools for bedside nursing prioritization and a novel framework for evaluating care delivery trade-offs in resource-constrained environments. This work directly advances nursing science’s capacity to operationalize big data in clinical practice while informing health system policies that balance patient safety with workforce sustainability. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing petabytes of streaming clinical data and achieving the sub-hourly model refresh rates required for real-time decision support.
cip_title: Registered Nursing, Nursing Administration, Nursing Research and Clinical Nursing, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in registered nursing, nursing administration, nursing research, and clinical nursing, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare data and the demand for precision in medication management necessitate advanced computational approaches to optimize therapeutic outcomes. Pharmacy informatics research faces significant challenges in integrating multi-modal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, pharmacogenomic data, and real-world evidence—to predict drug efficacy, adverse events, and patient-specific dosing. Traditional analytical tools are insufficient for handling the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of these data, limiting the ability to derive actionable insights for clinical decision-making. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for drug response variability and adverse drug interaction risks. The computational approach will employ machine learning frameworks, such as graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to analyze structured and unstructured EHR data alongside genomic variants. Molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted at scale to model protein-drug interactions and identify mechanistic drivers of toxicity. Additionally, federated learning techniques will enable privacy-preserving analysis across decentralized datasets. The HPC infrastructure will facilitate parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times for deep learning architectures, and support high-throughput virtual screening of drug combinations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for drug safety, personalized dosing algorithms for high-risk populations, and a scalable platform for real-time pharmacovigilance. This research will advance precision pharmacy practice by enabling data-driven clinical decisions, reducing medication-related harm, and informing guidelines for complex drug regimens. The computational workflows and models generated will be disseminated as open-source tools to support broader translational research in healthcare.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pharmacy Informatics

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social behavior, neurobiological signaling, and environmental stressors in shaping decision-making under uncertainty, with a focus on populations exposed to chronic socioeconomic adversity. Combining behavioral experiments, functional neuroimaging meta-analysis, and agent-based modeling, the research aims to resolve how adaptive decision strategies emerge from multiscale interactions between individual neurocognitive processes and group-level social learning. A core challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets—including fMRI-derived neural activation patterns, real-world behavioral surveys, and simulated socio-environmental conditions—into a unified computational framework. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address this complexity, enabling large-scale parameter space exploration for neural-behavioral network models and parallelized simulation of population-level decision dynamics across diverse virtual environments. The computational pipeline will leverage machine learning to identify latent biomarkers of resilience in neuroimaging data, then embed these features within hybrid models that couple individual biophysical simulations with mesoscale social network interactions. Validation will occur through iterative alignment with empirical behavioral data collected from urban and rural cohorts experiencing economic instability. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel multiscale model of stress-decision interactions applicable to public health interventions, 2) optimized algorithms for detecting neurobehavioral tipping points in heterogeneous populations, and 3) open-source tools for simulating policy impacts on community-level adaptive capacity. By bridging neurobiology, behavioral economics, and computational social science, this work advances predictive frameworks for human adaptation in rapidly changing environments while demonstrating how HPC-enabled integration of biological and social data can address pressing challenges in behavioral science.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on the social sciences, psychology, and biomedical sciences to study complex problems of human individual and social growth and behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in advancing Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) technology through the development of high-resolution, real-time vascular imaging protocols. Current MRI processing pipelines struggle to efficiently manage the computational demands of reconstructing dynamic, high-fidelity images of vascular structures, particularly in applications requiring rapid acquisition or motion correction. These limitations hinder diagnostic accuracy in time-sensitive clinical scenarios, such as assessing stroke risk or vascular anomalies. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable scalable, GPU-accelerated reconstruction algorithms and machine learning (ML)-enhanced hemodynamic modeling. Our computational approach will focus on two parallel workflows: (1) optimizing parallelized iterative reconstruction techniques for 4D flow MRI datasets using distributed memory architectures, reducing processing times from hours to minutes, and (2) training physics-informed neural networks to predict microvascular dynamics from sparse MRI acquisitions. The HPC environment will facilitate large-scale parameter sweeps to refine pulse sequence optimization while maintaining compatibility with clinical MRI hardware constraints. Anticipated outcomes include a validated pipeline for submillimeter-resolution vascular imaging with 40% faster processing speeds compared to existing methods, as well as open-source tools for simulating blood flow patterns in pathological vasculature. Successful implementation will directly enhance clinical capabilities for early detection of cerebrovascular and cardiovascular pathologies while establishing a computational framework adaptable to emerging MRI techniques. By integrating HPC-driven innovation with MRI physics expertise, this work aims to bridge critical gaps between theoretical imaging advances and practical clinical translation, ultimately improving patient outcomes in vascular disease management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals who are AART-certified radiological technicians to utilize MRI technology to obtain still and moving images of various vascular structures in the human body that aid the physician in the diagnosis or treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in MRI imaging, sectional anatomy and pathology, MRI technology, MRI techniques and procedures, MRI physics, and clinical training.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model the neurocognitive and behavioral effects of drama therapy interventions, with a focus on optimizing therapeutic protocols for individuals with trauma-related dissociation. Drama therapy employs embodied, narrative-based techniques to address fragmented self-perception and emotional dysregulation, but the neural and cognitive mechanisms underlying its efficacy remain poorly understood. The research problem centers on identifying how specific drama therapy methods (e.g., role reversal, sociodramatic metaphor) dynamically engage distributed brain networks involved in autobiographical memory, emotional processing, and self-referential thought. To address this, we will integrate multimodal data from wearable biosensors (EEG, electrodermal activity), motion capture systems, and therapist-client interaction logs collected during structured drama therapy sessions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to implement a multilayer network analysis pipeline that combines dynamic functional connectivity modeling with natural language processing of session transcripts and kinematic feature extraction. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) creating personalized brain-body interaction graphs using time-locked neural and physiological data, (2) training transformer-based models to detect linguistic markers of therapeutic breakthroughs in session narratives, and (3) developing agent-based simulations of therapist-client co-regulation dynamics. Expected outcomes include a predictive model correlating specific dramatic intervention sequences with normalized connectivity patterns in the default mode and salience networks, validated against longitudinal clinical outcomes. This work will establish the first quantitative framework for optimizing drama therapy protocols in trauma care while preserving the art-based integrity of interventions. The computational tools developed will enable real-time adaptive therapy design and provide foundational insights into how performative embodiment influences neurocognitive integration—advancing both therapeutic practice and interdisciplinary understanding of arts-based healing mechanisms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in association with a rehabilitation team or in private practice, to use dramatic play, theater, role play, psychodrama, and dramatic ritual in therapeutic relationships to address the physical, psychological, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of clients. Includes instruction in drama theory and performance, human growth and development, biomedical sciences, abnormal psychology, disabling conditions, patient assessment and diagnosis, treatment plan development and implementation, clinical evaluation, record-keeping, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of regulatory submissions for novel biomedical products necessitates advanced computational tools to ensure compliance, safety, and efficacy. Current approaches to analyzing multi-dimensional datasets—spanning clinical trials, real-world evidence, manufacturing quality metrics, and post-market surveillance—are hindered by scalability limitations and inefficiencies in processing heterogeneous data.
