This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through the development of machine learning (ML) models, large-scale simulations, and automated natural language processing (NLP) workflows. ML algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on integrated datasets to predict adverse events, optimize clinical trial enrollment criteria, and identify risk factors in manufacturing deviations. Parallelized simulations will model drug product stability under diverse environmental conditions to assess compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP). NLP pipelines will automate the extraction of critical data from regulatory documents, such as FDA submissions and adverse event reports, enabling real-time synthesis of evidence for regulatory decision-making. The computational intensity of training complex models on terabyte-scale datasets, coupled with the need for rapid iteration of simulations across parameter spaces, requires HPC infrastructure for efficient execution. Anticipated outcomes include scalable tools for automating regulatory workflows, reducing submission review times, and enhancing predictive accuracy in safety assessments. These advancements will directly support regulatory scientists in navigating evolving FDA frameworks while maintaining rigorous standards for product quality. The resulting open-source software and validated models will be disseminated to the regulatory science community, fostering collaboration and innovation in public health policy and industry practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the regulatory process for companies innovating and developing cutting edge products in science, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Includes instruction in regulatory affairs, clinical documentation, human and animal subject protection, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, data management and analysis, good manufacturing practices, and quality management.

abstract: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of enzymatic allostery remains a critical challenge in biochemistry, with implications for designing therapeutics and engineered biocatalysts. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve the dynamic, multi-scale conformational changes that underlie allosteric regulation. This project seeks to integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and free energy calculations to map the thermodynamic landscapes of allosteric transitions in a model enzyme system: aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase). ATCase’s complex hexameric architecture and cooperative substrate binding make it an ideal system for probing how localized perturbations propagate across protein domains to modulate activity. We propose to perform multi-microsecond, all-atom MD simulations of ATCase under varying ligand-binding states and mutant backgrounds, combined with Markov state models to identify metastable conformations and transition pathways. Enhanced sampling techniques, including replica exchange and metadynamics, will be employed to overcome timescale limitations and quantify free energy barriers. These simulations will be validated against existing crystallographic and mutagenesis data, with newly generated experimental kinetic measurements from collaborators. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing resources due to the system size (~300,000 atoms), need for extensive sampling across multiple replicates, and iterative analysis of terabyte-scale trajectory data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific residue interactions to allosteric efficiency, which could inform the rational design of allosteric inhibitors or engineered enzymes with tailored regulatory properties. By elucidating fundamental principles of protein dynamics, this work will advance methodologies for studying complex biomolecular systems and bridge gaps between structural data and functional mechanisms in molecular biology.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_title: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Molecular Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biochemistry, biophysics and molecular biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance clinical decision-making and intervention strategies in medical social work through the development of predictive computational models. A critical challenge in clinical social work is the timely identification of patients at high risk for adverse outcomes—such as hospital readmission, mental health crises, or disengagement from care—amidst complex, multidimensional data spanning electronic health records (EHRs), social determinants of health, and patient-reported outcomes. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to integrate these heterogeneous datasets or capture nonlinear interactions between variables, limiting their utility for personalized care planning. To address this, we propose a machine learning (ML) framework that combines natural language processing (NLP) of clinical notes with structured data analysis to predict patient risks and optimize intervention pathways. The NLP component will process unstructured clinician and social worker notes to extract psychosocial stressors, therapeutic progress, and barriers to care, while deep learning models will analyze temporal patterns in EHRs and community resource utilization. HPC resources are essential given the scale of data (spanning 10+ years of patient records across five regional hospitals) and the computational demands of training transformer-based architectures and ensemble models. The project will validate these tools through retrospective analysis and pilot real-time risk prediction in collaboration with hospital social workers. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools to prioritize high-risk patients, dynamically adjust care plans, and allocate community resources efficiently. By integrating computational advances with clinical social work practice, this research aims to reduce health disparities, improve patient outcomes, and establish scalable methodologies for data-driven intervention design in healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the specialized professional practice of social work, in collaboration with other health care professionals, in hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in social work, psychiatric case work, clinical interviewing techniques, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient testing and evaluation, patient and family counseling, social rehabilitation, patient care planning, record-keeping, and support services liaison.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment outcomes are influenced by complex biomechanical interactions between appliances and craniofacial structures, yet current clinical protocols rely on generalized force systems that inadequately account for individual variations in bone density, periodontal ligament properties, and dental morphology. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient-specific biomechanical responses to orthodontic forces, aiming to optimize treatment planning for malocclusion correction while minimizing adverse effects such as root resorption. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models derived from anonymized cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans of pre-treatment orthodontic patients, integrating heterogeneous tissue properties and dynamic force profiles from common appliances (e.g., brackets, aligners). Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated datasets to predict strain distributions in the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone remodeling patterns under varying load conditions. The computational pipeline will validate predictions against longitudinal clinical data from retrospective cases, assessing accuracy in forecasting tooth displacement rates and biological tissue responses. Successful implementation requires parallelized solvers for large-scale meshes (>50 million elements) and GPU-accelerated training of 3D convolutional neural networks. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to guide force system customization based on patient anatomy and biomechanical risk factors, potentially reducing treatment duration by 15-20% in simulated cohorts. This interdisciplinary approach bridges dental biomechanics, materials science, and computational modeling, advancing precision orthodontics while providing a scalable platform for future studies on temporomandibular joint dynamics and craniofacial growth adaptations. The project will additionally serve as an educational resource for pre-dentistry students, demonstrating computational applications in modern treatment planning through curated workshops on the developed tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in dentistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-sensor data fusion framework to enhance the precision and efficiency of geospatial mapping in complex urban and natural environments. Traditional surveying methods face challenges in integrating heterogeneous datasets—such as LiDAR, UAV photogrammetry, and GNSS observations—into cohesive 3D models, particularly in areas with dynamic terrain or dense infrastructure. To address this, we propose a computational workflow leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to automate the alignment, error correction, and synthesis of large-scale geospatial data. The core innovation lies in parallelized processing of point cloud and imagery datasets using GPU-accelerated feature matching algorithms and stochastic error modeling. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained to classify terrain features and predict systematic biases in sensor outputs under varying environmental conditions. The HPC environment is critical for handling datasets exceeding 100 TB, enabling rapid iteration of Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in fused geospatial products. Expected outcomes include an open-source software toolkit for real-time data integration, validated against ground-truth measurements from case studies in flood-prone coastal regions and urban transportation corridors. This work will advance surveying engineering by providing a scalable solution for high-accuracy topographic modeling, with direct applications in infrastructure resilience planning, autonomous vehicle navigation systems, and climate change adaptation strategies. The requested computing resources will support the development of these computational workflows, reducing processing times from weeks to days while maintaining sub-centimeter accuracy across multi-kilometer survey areas.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the determination of the location, elevations, and alignment of natural and manmade topographic features. Includes instruction in property line location, surveying, surface measurement, aerial and terrestrial photogrammetry, remote sensing, satellite imagery, global positioning systems, computer applications, and photographic data processing.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to optimize personalized vocational rehabilitation (VR) plans for individuals with disabilities by integrating multimodal biopsychosocial data. Current VR counseling relies on heuristic decision-making, which struggles to account for dynamic interactions between physiological, cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors that influence vocational outcomes. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive, data-driven tools to model these complex relationships and tailor interventions in real time. We will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to process heterogeneous datasets, including wearable sensor streams (tracking stress, mobility, and sleep), neurocognitive assessments, client-reported psychosocial metrics, and labor market analytics. A hybrid machine learning architecture will be implemented, combining graph neural networks to map interdependencies among variables, reinforcement learning to simulate intervention pathways, and Bayesian optimization to recommend adaptive VR strategies. Computational challenges include handling temporal-spatial data at scale (10,000+ client trajectories), managing missing data across modalities, and ensuring interpretability for clinical translation. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and CPU clusters for parallelized scenario testing across diverse demographic cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive platform identifying critical windows for VR interventions, (2) quantitative evidence linking specific biobehavioral markers to vocational readiness thresholds, and (3) generative models simulating long-term socioeconomic impacts of personalized VR strategies. By bridging computational science and rehabilitation counseling, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision vocational rehabilitation, reducing trial-and-error in service delivery while addressing systemic disparities in employment outcomes for marginalized populations with disabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel and assist disabled individuals and recovering patients in order to achieve their greatest physical, mental, social, educational, and vocational potential. Includes instruction in patient evaluation and testing, rehabilitation program planning, patient support services and referral, job analysis, adjustment psychology, rehabilitation services provision, patient counseling and education, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Periodontal diseases are multifactorial conditions influenced by complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and biomechanical factors. Despite advances in clinical research, gaps persist in understanding the dynamic mechanisms driving disease progression, treatment response variability, and long-term dental implant success. This project proposes a computational approach to model these interactions at scale, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations in data volume, model complexity, and real-time simulation feasibility. The research will integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) from longitudinal clinical cohorts with biomechanical simulations of implant-tissue interfaces. Machine learning pipelines will identify microbial and molecular signatures predictive of disease severity or implant failure, while finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate stress distribution in peri-implant bone under varying physiological loads. Agent-based modeling will explore host-microbe dynamics during periodontal inflammation and resolution, incorporating spatial and temporal heterogeneity derived from clinical imaging and biomarker data. These computational workflows require parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization, stochastic simulations, and high-resolution 3D modeling. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized treatment planning, mechanistic insights into microbial-immune crosstalk, and biomechanical guidelines for implant design optimization. By bridging clinical data with computational biology and engineering, this work aims to advance precision periodontology, reduce trial-and-error in therapeutic interventions, and establish scalable frameworks for simulating oral tissue responses. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational burden of multi-modal data integration, enabling iterative model refinement, and delivering translatable results within clinically relevant timelines. This project will provide open-access tools for the dental research community, fostering collaboration in computational periodontology and accelerating innovation in gum disease management and implant dentistry.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, and in the placement and maintenance of dental implants.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of chaplaincy in mediating ethical and existential decision-making within high-stakes, multi-faith environments, using computational modeling to analyze patterns of crisis response and spiritual care. While chaplaincy studies traditionally rely on qualitative methods, this research addresses the gap in scalable, data-driven frameworks for understanding how chaplains navigate complex ethical dilemmas, cultural diversity, and emotional labor in contexts such as disaster zones, correctional facilities, and interdisciplinary healthcare teams. The research problem centers on identifying adaptive strategies and decision-making heuristics that optimize compassionate care across heterogeneous populations under resource constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), the project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate chaplain-client interactions across diverse cultural, religious, and crisis scenarios, incorporating variables such as trauma severity, belief systems, and institutional policies. Natural language processing (NLP) will be applied to anonymized pastoral care records and interview transcripts to detect latent patterns in communication efficacy and ethical reasoning. Machine learning classifiers will further analyze longitudinal outcomes related to patient or inmate well-being, workforce retention among chaplains, and interprofessional collaboration. By integrating these computational methods, the project aims to generate predictive models of effective chaplaincy practices and propose evidence-based training protocols for crisis resilience. Outcomes will include an open-access dataset of simulated scenarios, a toolkit for optimizing spiritual care resource allocation, and a methodological framework for applying HPC to humanities-driven care ethics. This work will advance chaplaincy studies as a computational humanities discipline while offering practical insights for institutions seeking to enhance the scalability and cultural responsiveness of spiritual care services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide caregiver, pastoral, and spiritual support in an institutional, hospice, military, or sports setting. Includes instruction in global, healthcare, prison, and sports chaplaincy; addiction, crisis, disaster, family, marriage, grief, and loss counseling; ethics; leadership; multi-cultural, multi-faith contexts; and worship.

abstract: Workplace exposure to hazardous substances and environmental conditions poses significant risks to worker health, yet current methods for assessing these risks often lack the resolution and predictive power needed for proactive intervention. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model complex occupational exposure scenarios and optimize safety protocols in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate large-scale sensor datasets, industrial hygiene metrics, and biomonitoring data with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and machine learning (ML) models. The CFD simulations will resolve spatially and temporally varying contaminant dispersion patterns in diverse workplaces, such as manufacturing facilities and construction sites, while ML algorithms will identify exposure risk factors from heterogeneous data streams, including ventilation parameters, equipment usage logs, and toxicological profiles. A key innovation involves coupling these models to predict acute and chronic health risks under dynamic operational conditions, enabling scenario testing for safety measure efficacy. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across multiple nodes, given the high dimensionality of 3D workspace geometries and the need for real-time feedback in hazard prediction. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for granular exposure assessment, validated against field data from partner industries, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive safety interventions. By enhancing the precision of hazard evaluations and enabling predictive risk management, this research will directly support the development of more resilient occupational health policies and reduce the incidence of work-related illnesses. The scale of data integration and model complexity requires the advanced processing capabilities of HPC infrastructure, which is critical to achieving the project’s translational goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to monitor and evaluate health and related safety standards in industrial, commercial, and government workplaces and facilities. Includes instruction in occupational health and safety standards and regulations; health-related aspects of various occupations and work environments; health hazard testing and evaluation; test equipment operation and maintenance; industrial toxicology; worker health and safety education; and the analysis and testing of job-related equipment, behavior practices, and protective devices and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in sustainable supply chain optimization for multi-location restaurant franchises, a critical yet understudied challenge at the intersection of food services management, environmental economics, and logistics. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational frameworks to model dynamic trade-offs between cost efficiency, carbon footprint reduction, and operational resilience across geographically dispersed food service networks. Current industry practices rely on static, location-specific models that fail to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating regional ingredient availability, energy grid variability in refrigeration logistics, and consumer demand patterns influenced by climate events. The proposed computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to create a multi-objective optimization platform capable of processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning procurement records, transportation networks, and regional sustainability metrics. By parallelizing genetic algorithms across HPC clusters, the system will identify Pareto-optimal solutions for inventory distribution, cold chain routing, and waste reduction strategies under thousands of simultaneous constraint scenarios. The project will validate models against historical data from a participating national quick-service restaurant chain, incorporating real-time IoT sensor data from their distribution network. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support tool that quantifies the financial and environmental impacts of alternative supply chain configurations, enabling data-driven transitions to circular economy practices in food services. This work will advance computational methodologies for ethical resource allocation in hospitality while establishing benchmark metrics for Scope 3 emissions accounting specific to franchise restaurant operations. The resulting open-source framework aims to set new industry standards for balancing profitability with planetary boundaries in mass-scale food provisioning systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market restaurants, food services in hospitality establishments, food service chains and franchise networks, and restaurant supply operations. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, food services management, wholesale logistics and distribution, franchise operations, business networking, personnel management, culinary arts, business planning and capitalization, food industry operations, marketing and retailing, business law and regulations, finance, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for evaluating the economic efficiency and environmental trade-offs of climate adaptation policies under deep uncertainty. As climate change accelerates, policymakers face challenges in designing robust strategies that balance mitigation costs, ecosystem preservation, and socioeconomic outcomes. Existing approaches often rely on deterministic models that inadequately capture complex feedbacks between human systems and biophysical processes. Our research addresses this gap by creating a high-resolution, stochastic optimization model that integrates climate projections, land-use patterns, and heterogeneous agent behavior across multiple temporal and spatial scales. The computational methodology combines dynamic programming with Monte Carlo simulations to assess policy performance across 10,000+ climate-economic scenarios, incorporating non-linear threshold effects in natural systems and adaptive learning in economic decision-making. The model requires processing multi-terabyte datasets from climate models (CMIP6), global agricultural production records, and regional economic indicators, necessitating parallelized computation across GPU-accelerated nodes. Key innovations include a novel algorithm for solving high-dimensional dynamic optimization problems with discontinuous payoff surfaces and a machine learning component to reduce dimensionality in agent-based simulations. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of Pareto-efficient policy bundles that minimize economic disruption while achieving biodiversity conservation targets, (2) quantification of value-at-risk metrics for critical ecosystem services under alternative warming trajectories, and (3) open-source tools for stochastic cost-benefit analysis in coupled human-environment systems. By leveraging high-performance computing resources, this work will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling cross-scale interactions between economic activities and ecological constraints, directly informing the design of climate-resilient natural resource management strategies. Results will advance methodological capabilities in environmental economics while providing actionable insights for multilateral institutions and national agencies addressing interlinked climate and biodiversity crises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic concepts and methods to the analysis of issues such as air and water pollution, land use planning, waste disposal, invasive species and pest control, conservation policies, and related environmental problems. Includes instruction in cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, evaluation and assessment of alternative resource management strategies, policy evaluation and monitoring, and descriptive and analytic tools for studying how environmental developments affect the economic system.

abstract: Nursing practice increasingly relies on data-driven decision-making to optimize patient outcomes, yet scalable computational tools tailored to clinical nursing workflows remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting patient deterioration in acute care settings by developing machine learning models that integrate real-time physiological data, electronic health records (EHRs), and nurse-generated assessments. Existing predictive tools often exclude contextual nursing observations—such as subtle behavioral changes or caregiver-reported symptoms—which limits their clinical utility. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets spanning 50,000+ de-identified patient encounters from three hospital systems, including time-series vital signs, medication administration records, and structured nursing notes. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing to extract latent patterns from free-text nursing documentation, coupled with ensemble learning architectures to model temporal interactions between observed parameters and adverse outcomes (e.g., sepsis, falls). By parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across GPU nodes, we aim to reduce model training times by 85% compared to local compute capabilities, enabling rapid iteration of context-aware algorithms. Validated models will be deployed as prototype dashboards to simulate real-time risk stratification, providing nurses with prioritized clinical alerts during electronic handoffs. This work is expected to advance precision nursing by demonstrating how large-scale computational analysis can bridge gaps between bedside assessments and predictive analytics. Outcomes will include open-source code repositories for EHR feature extraction, benchmarks comparing model performance with/without nursing data inputs, and a framework for integrating HPC-derived insights into shift-level clinical workflows. The project directly aligns with national priorities to reduce preventable hospital complications through nurse-led innovation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: The oral cavity represents a complex ecosystem where microbial communities interact dynamically with host tissues, influencing health and disease states. Emerging evidence suggests that dysbiotic shifts in the oral microbiome are linked to oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), yet the mechanistic pathways and predictive biomarkers remain poorly characterized. This project seeks to integrate high-resolution metagenomic sequencing, host transcriptomic data, and spatially resolved proteomic imaging to model microbiome-host interactions in OSCC progression. A critical barrier to advancing this research is the computational demand of analyzing multi-omic datasets at scale, particularly when resolving spatial and temporal heterogeneity across tumor microenvironments. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid computational pipeline combining neural network architectures for feature extraction, Bayesian probabilistic modeling to infer causal microbial-host networks, and agent-based simulations to predict dysbiosis-driven carcinogenic pathways. The pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets from 150 OSCC patient samples, including matched tumor, adjacent normal, and distant mucosal tissues. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive spatial transcriptomic alignments and optimizing parallelized simulations of microbial community dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved microbial taxa and metabolic pathways associated with malignant transformation, (2) predictive models linking spatial microbiome patterns to immune evasion mechanisms, and (3) open-source tools for integrative analysis of multi-omic oral cancer datasets. This work will establish a computational framework to decode microbiome contributions to OSCC, offering novel targets for early detection and microbiome-modulating therapies. By addressing the unique computational demands of spatially resolved multi-omics in oral oncology, this project fills a critical niche at the intersection of microbial ecology, cancer systems biology, and clinical dentistry.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating computational methodologies into the creation and analysis of complex textile structures, which traditional manual and analog techniques struggle to model at scale. The research focuses on developing predictive models for nonlinear material behaviors in woven and non-woven fibrous systems, particularly under dynamic environmental conditions or mechanical stresses. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ multi-scale simulations to analyze interactions between fiber composition, structural geometry, and external stimuli such as humidity, temperature, and tension. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model dye dispersion in heterogeneous textiles, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict deformation patterns in 3D knitted architectures. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on empirical data from traditional weaving and experimental textile samples to generate generative design proposals that optimize aesthetic and functional parameters. These computational approaches aim to bridge gaps between material experimentation and digital prototyping, enabling rapid iteration of textile art concepts that require precise control over thousands of variables. The expected outcomes include a framework for simulating hybrid textile systems that combine organic and synthetic fibers, as well as predictive tools for pigment migration in multi-layered fabric constructions. This research will advance the field of fiber arts by providing artists with evidence-based computational strategies to expand the scope of tactile and visual expression, while contributing new interdisciplinary methods at the intersection of material science and digital design. Results will be validated through physical prototypes created using computer-numerical-control (CNC) loom systems and robotic fiber placement, ensuring alignment between simulated predictions and material realities. The project’s computational workflows will be disseminated as open-source tools to foster innovation in sustainable textile practices and adaptive material design.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by constructing art works from woven or non-woven fabrics and fibrous materials. Includes instruction in weaving techniques and loom operation; non-woven techniques such as knitting, coiling, netting, and crocheting; quilting; dyeing and pigmentation; printing and other finishing techniques; pattern design; tapestry; and personal style development.

abstract: Veterinary medicine faces growing challenges in addressing complex, multifactorial diseases that impact animal health and intersect with public health through zoonotic transmission. A critical bottleneck lies in analyzing vast, heterogeneous datasets—ranging from genomic sequences to population-level epidemiological data—to uncover patterns of disease spread, host-pathogen interactions, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) evolution. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analyses aimed at advancing predictive modeling of infectious disease dynamics in animal populations. The research will integrate whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from veterinary pathogens with clinical metadata, environmental variables, and livestock movement records to identify drivers of AMR emergence and transmission across species. Agent-based models will simulate disease spread under varying intervention scenarios, while molecular dynamics simulations will probe structural mechanisms of drug resistance in priority pathogens such as *Salmonella enterica* and *Staphylococcus pseudintermedius*. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to predict outbreak risks and optimize treatment protocols based on regional pathogen surveillance data. By leveraging parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated computing, these analyses will overcome limitations of conventional computing infrastructures, which lack the capacity to process terabyte-scale datasets or execute complex simulations at necessary resolutions. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into AMR transmission networks, validated strategies for outbreak mitigation in livestock systems, and open-access tools for real-time genomic surveillance. This work will directly inform veterinary clinical decision-making, antimicrobial stewardship policies, and One Health initiatives aimed at reducing zoonotic threats. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieving the scale, speed, and integration required for transformative advances in veterinary computational epidemiology and precision medicine.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of veterinary medicine, involving the diagnosis, treatment, and health care management of animals and animal populations and the prevention and management of zoonosis. Includes instruction in the veterinary basic sciences, infectious and noninfectious disease, diagnostic procedures, veterinary clinical medicine, obstetrics, radiology, anesthesiology, surgery, toxicology, animal health and preventive medicine, clinical nutrition, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize hyper-personalized merchandising strategies in fragmented digital marketplaces, leveraging high-dimensional behavioral data and real-time consumer interaction patterns. Traditional marketing models struggle to adapt to the rapid proliferation of niche platforms and micro-communities, where consumer preferences evolve dynamically across decentralized ecosystems. The research problem centers on identifying latent decision drivers in these environments, where conventional segmentation fails due to sparse, heterogeneous data and nonlinear preference cascades. Using anonymized multi-platform transaction logs, biometric response datasets (e.g., eye-tracking, dwell times), and generative adversarial networks (GANs), we will simulate marketplace environments to test adaptive merchandising interventions. High-performance computing resources are critical for training transformer-based architectures on terabyte-scale interaction graphs, which encode temporal, spatial, and social influence dimensions simultaneously. The computational pipeline includes 1) graph neural networks to model cross-platform consumer journeys, 2) reinforcement learning agents to simulate merchandising policy impacts under constrained inventory scenarios, and 3) counterfactual analysis using differential privacy-preserving synthetic data generation. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of prescribing platform-specific merchandising configurations that balance short-term conversion goals with long-term brand equity metrics. This work addresses the operational challenge of resource allocation in contextually fluid digital markets while advancing methodological integration of neuromarketing principles with large-language model interpretability techniques. The resulting models will be validated against A/B test results from three industry partners specializing in augmented reality commerce, providing empirical evidence for computational efficiency gains in real-time personalization workflows.
cip_title: Specialized Merchandising, Sales, and Marketing Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sales, marketing, and distribution operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive analytics framework to optimize credentialing and privileging workflows in healthcare institutions, addressing inefficiencies in Medical Staff Services (MSS) operations. Traditional credentialing processes are labor-intensive, prone to delays, and vulnerable to human error, creating bottlenecks that impact healthcare workforce readiness and institutional compliance. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to automate the extraction, validation, and risk assessment of practitioner credentials from heterogeneous data sources (e.g., licensure records, malpractice claims, peer references). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training large-scale language models on sensitive, unstructured text data (CVs, accreditation documents, legal transcripts) and constructing dynamic knowledge graphs mapping practitioner competencies, institutional requirements, and regulatory constraints. The pipeline will include federated learning to preserve data privacy across collaborating healthcare systems while enabling model refinement. Anticipated outcomes include a real-time decision support tool that reduces credentialing cycle times by ≥40%, identifies high-risk privileging scenarios with >90% precision, and dynamically aligns staffing resources with evolving care standards. By leveraging HPC to process multi-modal datasets at scale, this work bridges gaps between healthcare administration, regulatory informatics, and computational ethics—advancing a novel, technology-driven paradigm for MSS operations. The resulting open-source framework will be validated against retrospective data from three academic medical centers, with benchmarks shared publicly to inform standards for AI-augmented healthcare workforce management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform credentialing, privileging, personnel management, and accreditation compliance services for hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in medical staff organization and management, medical terminology, credentialing and re-credentialing, health care accreditation and regulatory standards, health care law, meeting and negotiation management, and office information systems management.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize precision irrigation and plant health management in urban landscaping systems using computational modeling and machine learning. Current irrigation practices often rely on generalized schedules, leading to water waste, nutrient runoff, and suboptimal plant growth due to variable soil conditions, microclimates, and species-specific requirements. To address this, we propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework integrating real-time sensor data, plant physiology models, and soil-water dynamics. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate root-water uptake patterns across heterogeneous landscapes, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine irrigation strategies under dynamic environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets from IoT soil moisture sensors, weather stations, and drone-based multispectral imagery, as well as to run parallelized simulations testing thousands of scenario permutations. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for identifying water-efficient irrigation schedules tailored to mixed-species plantings, soil types, and localized microclimate factors. The computational framework will also enable proactive disease risk assessments by correlating canopy temperature anomalies and soil hydration patterns with historical pathogen spread data. This work will advance sustainable landscaping practices by reducing water consumption by an estimated 20-35% in testbed urban gardens while maintaining horticultural quality benchmarks. The models and workflows developed will be shared as open-source resources to support groundskeeping education programs, providing students with hands-on training in data-driven landscape management. By bridging computational agriculture with practical horticultural operations, this project aims to establish scalable protocols for resource-efficient urban green space maintenance.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: Understanding the drivers and implications of population change requires analyzing complex, high-dimensional demographic data, often spanning large geographic and temporal scales. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model nonlinear interactions between factors such as migration, fertility, mortality, and environmental stressors, particularly when integrating heterogeneous data sources like census records, health surveys, and geospatial layers. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing scalable computational models to simulate population dynamics under varying socioeconomic and environmental scenarios. Using agent-based modeling and Bayesian hierarchical frameworks, we will quantify how multilevel factors—from individual decision-making to regional policy shifts—interact to shape demographic outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to fit models to longitudinal demographic data from 15 countries, process high-resolution geospatial inputs, and run computationally intensive sensitivity analyses. Key computational challenges include parallelizing microsimulation workflows, optimizing memory usage for large agent populations, and implementing spatial interpolation algorithms across distributed nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models identifying critical leverage points in demographic systems, particularly in aging populations and climate-related migration contexts; (2) open-source tools for demographic simulation optimized for HPC architectures; and (3) policy-relevant projections of population resilience under alternative development pathways. By enabling analysis at unprecedented spatial granularity and temporal depth, this work will advance methodological integration in population studies while providing actionable insights for sustainable development planning. The requested computing resources are essential for managing the scale of stochastic simulations required to robustly characterize uncertainty in demographic forecasts.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in demography, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time collaborative document formatting in multilingual environments, addressing inefficiencies in current word processing systems when handling concurrent edits across diverse linguistic and typographic conventions. While modern tools excel in basic text manipulation, they struggle with dynamic alignment of bidirectional text (e.g., Arabic-English mixtures), context-aware table restructuring during multi-author workflows, and predictive layout adjustments for non-Latin scripts—all of which create bottlenecks in cross-cultural academic and technical documentation. The research employs hybrid neural-symbolic models to analyze formatting intent from user interaction sequences, combining graph-based representations of document structure with transformer architectures trained on multimodal workflow patterns (keystrokes, cursor movements, formatting selections). High-performance computing resources are critical for three phases: 1) simulating 10,000+ concurrent editing sessions across 15+ script systems to train robustness, 2) parallel optimization of layout recalculation algorithms through GPU-accelerated constraint solving, and 3) real-time validation of adaptive formatting suggestions via large-language-model-based semantic coherence checks. Expected outcomes include an open-source API for context-sensitive formatting prediction, reducing manual adjustments by 40-60% in mixed-script environments, and quantitative metrics for measuring typographic workflow efficiency. This work bridges gaps between human-computer interaction, computational linguistics, and distributed systems engineering, offering novel methods to automate document structure optimization while preserving authorial intent—a growing need in global research collaborations and multilingual publishing ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: The development of advanced neural interfaces for next-generation prosthetics requires overcoming significant challenges in optimizing bio-electrical compatibility and long-term functional integration with human tissue. Current experimental approaches to design neural interfaces are constrained by the slow, costly iterative processes of physical prototyping and in vivo testing. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate interactions between engineered neural interfaces and biological systems. These models will integrate molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate material-tissue interfaces, finite element analyses to predict strain and electrical signal propagation across cellular networks, and machine learning algorithms to iteratively optimize device geometries and material compositions. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to rapidly explore design parameters—such as electrode topography, polymer flexibility, and charge injection thresholds—that influence neural stimulation efficacy and chronic immune response. The computational framework will also incorporate patient-specific anatomical and electrophysiological data to enable personalized device predictions. Successful implementation will yield validated models capable of reducing experimental trial cycles by 50% and identifying candidate designs with >90% predicted biocompatibility, directly addressing the translational gap between prototype development and clinical deployment. This work aligns with the Biomedical Technology program’s focus on engineering biological systems by providing a scalable computational toolset to innovate medical device testing, enhance system safety through virtual failure mode analysis, and streamline procurement processes via data-driven design specifications. Outcomes will advance the engineering of adaptive neural prosthetics for patients with limb loss or neurological disorders while establishing a template for HPC-driven optimization of biohybrid technologies.
detailed_field: Biological/ biosystems engineering and biomedical technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous biological datasets to uncover dynamic patterns in protein interaction networks and their role in cellular signaling processes. Current methods for network analysis struggle with scalability and precision when handling high-dimensional data from diverse sources, such as proteomics, phosphoproteomics, and structural interactome databases. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-optimized pipeline integrating graph neural networks (GNNs) and parallelized Monte Carlo simulations. The pipeline will model time-resolved protein interaction dynamics, predict context-specific signaling pathways, and quantify uncertainty in network inferences. By leveraging distributed computing frameworks (e.g., Dask and MPI) and GPU-accelerated GNN training, the approach will efficiently process datasets spanning millions of interactions across multiple experimental conditions. Key outcomes include (1) novel algorithms for scalable network topology optimization, (2) probabilistic models of signaling crosstalk, and (3) an open-source software package for community use. The computational demands—including memory-intensive graph operations, thousands of parallel simulation trials, and hyperparameter optimization—necessitate dedicated HPC resources. Successful implementation will enable unprecedented resolution of signaling network plasticity, with applications to therapeutic target identification and precision medicine. This work directly advances bioinformatics methodologies by bridging gaps between network theory, statistical learning, and systems biology, while providing infrastructure for future large-scale omics integration studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer-based technologies and services to biological, biomedical, and biotechnology research. Includes instruction in algorithms, network architecture, principles of software design, human interface design, usability studies, search strategies, database management and data mining, digital image processing, computer graphics and animation, CAD, computer programming, and applications to experimental design and analysis and to specific quantitative, modeling, and analytical studies in the various biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for legacy and modern business machines using high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in manual diagnostic processes. Current repair protocols rely heavily on technician expertise and static troubleshooting guidelines, which struggle to adapt to the increasing complexity of integrated electromechanical systems in devices such as multifunction printers, automated mailing systems, and data processing equipment. The research will employ computational modeling to simulate failure modes in business machines, integrating principles of mechanics, circuit analysis, and materials science. Finite element analysis (FEA) will be applied to model mechanical wear in components like printer rollers and gear assemblies, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will assess thermal stress in electronic control boards. Machine learning models—including graph neural networks to represent system interdependencies and time-series forecasting for component degradation—will be trained on synthetic failure datasets generated through these simulations, supplemented by real-world repair logs. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale parametric studies of machine configurations and accelerating the training of ensemble models that correlate multi-physics simulation data with observed failure patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic recommendation system that prioritizes likely fault sources based on symptom input, reducing equipment downtime by 30–50% in preliminary testing scenarios. Additionally, the project will produce a digital twin framework to simulate repair interventions before physical implementation, lowering costs associated with trial-and-error component replacement. By bridging traditional repair methodologies with computational engineering, this work aims to establish new standards for data-driven decision-making in business machine maintenance, with potential applications in vocational training programs and sustainability initiatives targeting extended device lifespans.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain and repair a variety of office machines, such as typewriters, word processing and dictation machines, calculators, data processing equipment, duplicating machines, and mailing machines. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment, and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of business machines.

abstract: This proposal seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on simulating and mitigating complex security threats to critical infrastructure. Modern security challenges—such as coordinated cyber-physical attacks, cascading failures in interconnected systems, and dynamic threat landscapes—demand computational models capable of analyzing large-scale, multi-domain data and predicting emergent risks. However, existing tools often lack the resolution or scalability to model interdependent infrastructure systems (e.g., power grids, transportation networks) under realistic threat scenarios. This project will develop a multi-layered simulation framework integrating agent-based modeling, network theory, and machine learning to assess vulnerabilities and optimize response strategies. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of attack vectors (e.g., malware propagation, physical sabotage) across heterogeneous infrastructure models, leveraging real-world datasets to calibrate system interdependencies. Additionally, graph neural networks will be trained on HPC clusters to identify high-risk nodes and predict cascading failures in near-real time. The computational workflow will employ MPI for distributed simulations and GPU acceleration for deep learning inference. Outcomes will include a validated toolkit for infrastructure resilience planning, actionable risk assessments for policymakers, and novel algorithms for adaptive threat detection. By quantifying the impact of hybrid threats and enabling rapid scenario testing, this work aims to bridge gaps in security science, offering scalable methods to enhance national preparedness. The requested resources will directly support 10,000+ core-hour simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the development of open-source software for the security research community.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: Veterinary administrative services face growing challenges in optimizing operational efficiency, resource allocation, and client care coordination as clinics and animal care facilities manage increasing caseloads and complex workflows. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive models and simulation frameworks tailored to veterinary administrative decision-making. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational tools to analyze heterogeneous data streams—such as appointment scheduling patterns, inventory turnover rates, staff productivity metrics, and client communication logs—that collectively impact clinic performance. By integrating anonymized operational datasets from multiple veterinary facilities with machine learning algorithms, the project aims to identify bottlenecks in service delivery, forecast resource demand under varying conditions, and simulate the outcomes of workflow interventions. Computational methods will include time-series forecasting, agent-based modeling of clinic operations, and natural language processing to analyze unstructured client interaction data. The HPC environment is critical for handling large-scale datasets and parallelizing simulations across diverse clinic profiles. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for veterinary administrators to model operational scenarios, optimize staffing and inventory decisions, and evaluate ethical trade-offs in resource allocation. This work bridges a gap in non-science computational research by applying advanced analytics to veterinary management—a specialized niche where administrative complexity intersects with animal welfare priorities. The results could establish scalable frameworks for data-driven decision-making in veterinary practice management while maintaining compliance with professional ethics and client privacy standards.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to provide administrative support services in a veterinary office or animal care facility. Includes instruction in business office operations, customer service, principles of veterinary health care operations, record-keeping, veterinary terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Aerospace systems operating in hypersonic regimes face extreme aerothermal loads that challenge conventional design methodologies, particularly in predicting coupled fluid-thermal-structural behavior. Current simulations often rely on simplified models or decoupled analyses, limiting their ability to resolve the multiscale, multiphysics interactions inherent in high-speed flows. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity computational framework for coupled aerothermal-structural analysis, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will leverage large-eddy simulation (LES) for turbulence modeling, coupled with finite element methods (FEM) for transient thermal-structural response, to simulate hypersonic flow over deformable vehicle surfaces. These simulations will resolve boundary layer transitions, shock-wave interactions, and material ablation phenomena at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational approach requires distributed-memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated solvers to manage the high dimensionality of the problem, with meshes exceeding 100 million cells and iterative solver stability across tightly coupled physics domains. Validation will utilize experimental data from wind tunnel tests and prior flight campaigns. The outcomes aim to advance predictive capabilities for thermal protection system (TPS) design, reduce reliance on costly physical testing, and inform material selection for next-generation reusable hypersonic vehicles. By quantifying the interplay between aerodynamic heating, structural deformation, and material degradation, this work will directly support the development of safer, more efficient aerospace systems capable of sustained operation in extreme environments. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieve the necessary scale and fidelity, as local computing infrastructure cannot support the memory and processing demands of these multidisciplinary simulations.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. Includes instruction in aircraft/spacecraft systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Industrial electronics systems are critical to modern manufacturing, yet their increasing complexity poses challenges in reliability, efficiency, and predictive maintenance. Traditional analytical methods and small-scale simulations often fail to capture the dynamic interactions within multiphysics environments, such as thermal, electrical, and mechanical stresses in high-power motor drives or automated control systems. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced computational models that address these limitations. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) creating machine learning (ML) frameworks for real-time anomaly detection in industrial sensor networks, and (2) simulating the long-term performance of power electronics under variable operational conditions using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The ML component will leverage distributed computing to process terabytes of historical and real-time sensor data, training deep neural networks to predict equipment failures in systems such as variable frequency drives and programmable logic controllers. Concurrently, multiphysics simulations will model thermal dissipation, electromagnetic interference, and material degradation in industrial-grade converters and inverters, requiring parallelized solvers to handle meshes with over 10^6 elements. These simulations will inform design optimizations to extend component lifespans and reduce energy losses. By integrating data-driven and physics-based approaches, the project aims to establish a predictive maintenance pipeline capable of reducing unplanned downtime in manufacturing by an estimated 15–20%. The computational workflows developed will also serve as pedagogical tools for training technicians in simulation-driven diagnostics. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the scale of data and complexity of models, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations. Outcomes will advance industrial electronics by bridging gaps between theoretical models, operational data, and field-level decision-making, directly supporting the program’s mission to prepare technicians for emerging smart manufacturing challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair electrical/electronic equipment used in industry and manufacturing. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: Maritime law enforcement agencies face significant challenges in dynamically responding to illicit activities across vast and complex maritime domains, where factors such as evolving criminal tactics, environmental variability, and jurisdictional ambiguities complicate operational planning. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing maritime interdiction strategies through high-fidelity simulations of vessel behavior, threat pattern analysis, and resource allocation under uncertainty. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including historical interdiction records, Automatic Identification System (AIS) trajectories, meteorological data, and geopolitical risk indicators—to model interactions between law enforcement assets and illicit actors. Agent-based modeling will simulate adaptive decision-making processes of both patrol units and offenders, incorporating stochastic elements such as weather disruptions, intelligence reliability, and jurisdictional constraints. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent spatial-temporal patterns in smuggling routes and predict emerging hotspots. The computational workflow will further evaluate the efficacy of multi-agency coordination protocols and sensor network deployments under varying operational scenarios. By enabling large-scale parallelized simulations, HPC infrastructure is critical to resolving the high dimensionality of the problem, which encompasses thousands of vessels, multi-sensor data streams, and probabilistic legal frameworks. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating risk-optimized patrol schedules, resource deployment recommendations, and contingency protocols for cross-jurisdictional incidents. This work aims to advance maritime operational analytics by bridging gaps between legal frameworks, tactical planning, and computational modeling, offering a scalable approach to enhancing maritime domain awareness while respecting the legal and procedural constraints unique to law enforcement contexts.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement and security principles and procedures to the marine environment. Includes instruction in criminal and nautical law, nautical terminology, seamanship and vessel operation, vessel maintenance, navigation and navigation systems, meteorology, vessel and passenger safety, radar and remote sensing systems, communications systems, vessel pursuit and stop, boarding and arrest techniques, investigative and evidence techniques, weaponry and applications to specific situations such as piracy, drug trafficking and smuggling.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale mental health datasets and optimize predictive models for personalized treatment planning in psychiatric care. Mental health disorders exhibit complex, heterogeneous trajectories influenced by biological, psychological, and social factors, complicating the development of standardized interventions. Current clinical tools often lack the computational power to integrate multimodal data—such as electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, patient-reported outcomes, and real-time behavioral metrics—into actionable frameworks. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline combining machine learning (ML) and network analysis to identify dynamic biomarkers of treatment response and predict patient-specific risks of adverse outcomes. The project will utilize federated learning techniques to train models on distributed datasets while preserving patient confidentiality, a critical consideration in mental health research. Key computational challenges include handling high-dimensional data, managing temporal variability in symptom presentation, and simulating treatment scenarios across diverse demographic subgroups. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of neuroimaging data, large-scale parameter optimization for deep learning architectures, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in treatment effect estimates. Expected outcomes include (1) validated ML models to guide medication selection and dosage adjustments for patients with treatment-resistant depression, (2) an open-source toolkit for risk stratification using EHR-derived social determinants of health, and (3) synthetic data generation frameworks to address sparse data limitations in rare psychiatric conditions. By enhancing the precision of clinical decision-support tools, this work directly aligns with the training objectives of psychiatric/mental health technicians, offering scalable methods to inform bedside care, crisis intervention protocols, and longitudinal patient management. The computational infrastructure developed through this project will be disseminated via partnerships with regional mental health clinics, creating a template for data-driven resource allocation in under-resourced care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses, and other mental health care professionals, to provide direct patient care services, assist in developing and implementing treatment plans, administer medications, and perform related administrative functions. Includes instruction in mental health theory, applied psychopathology, patient communication and management, crisis intervention, psychotropic medication, mental health treatment procedures, substance abuse, record-keeping, clinical administrative skills, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the challenge of optimizing energy-efficient thermal management systems in advanced manufacturing processes, a critical bottleneck in industrial applications of mechanical engineering-related technologies. Current analytical models fail to capture the complex multiphysics interactions between phase-change materials, transient heat loads, and nonlinear fluid-structure phenomena in high-precision machining environments. This project will develop a scalable computational framework combining lattice Boltzmann methods for multiphase flow simulation with finite element analysis of thermoelastic deformation. The framework will be implemented on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to enable coupled 3D simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (sub-10µm scale) and temporal durations (full operational cycles). Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement for dynamic interface tracking and hybrid OpenMP-MPI parallelization to efficiently distribute memory-intensive calculations across nodes. Initial validation against experimental infrared thermography data from CNC machining centers demonstrates the method's potential to predict thermal warping with <5% error relative to physical measurements. Successful implementation will enable virtual prototyping of next-generation cooling systems with predictive maintenance capabilities, directly addressing industry needs for reduced energy consumption and improved machining accuracy. The requested computing resources will support parametric studies across 200+ design configurations, generating a public dataset of simulated thermal profiles to benefit the broader manufacturing research community. Outcomes will advance computational methodologies in mechanical systems analysis while providing practical tools for sustainable manufacturing optimization, with estimated energy savings potential of 15-20% in target industrial use cases.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid quantum-classical communication networks necessitates advanced computational tools to model, optimize, and secure these systems under dynamic operational constraints. Existing network management frameworks struggle to address the unique challenges posed by integrating quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols and entanglement-based routing with classical telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in scenarios involving intermittent quantum coherence and heterogeneous device interoperability. This project seeks to develop a scalable simulation environment to analyze hybrid network performance, optimize resource allocation across quantum and classical layers, and evaluate resilience against targeted cyber-physical attacks. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a multi-layered network model incorporating stochastic quantum channel behavior, decoherence effects, and adaptive classical-quantum protocol translation. The computational framework will combine discrete-event simulation for network traffic dynamics with tensor network methods to simulate quantum state evolution across distributed nodes. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize real-time routing decisions and failure recovery pathways under varying security postures. Expected outcomes include novel metrics for hybrid network efficiency, validated strategies for bandwidth partitioning between quantum and classical data streams, and vulnerability profiles for emerging QKD-enhanced architectures. This work will provide the first open-source toolkit for simulating large-scale quantum-classical networks, addressing a critical gap in next-generation cybersecurity and infrastructure planning. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10^4+ node configurations, Monte Carlo simulations for attack surface analysis, and benchmarking against conventional networks in realistic traffic scenarios. Results will directly inform standardization efforts for quantum-resistant telecommunications frameworks while advancing computational methods at the intersection of quantum information science and network systems engineering.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of linked systems of computers, peripherals, and associated software to maximize efficiency and productivity, and that prepares individuals to function as network specialists and managers at various levels. Includes instruction in operating systems and applications; systems design and analysis; networking theory and solutions; types of networks; network management and control; network and flow optimization; security; configuring; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of efficiently synthesizing and disseminating complex agricultural data to diverse stakeholders through advanced computational methods. Agricultural communication faces a critical bottleneck: the rapid generation of multidimensional datasets—including crop yield predictions, climate resilience analytics, livestock health monitoring, and consumer trend analyses—exceeds the processing capacity of conventional tools. This limits the ability to translate technical agricultural research into actionable, timely, and audience-specific communication outputs. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable framework for real-time data integration, analysis, and visualization tailored for agricultural journalism applications. Our computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) to automate the distillation of peer-reviewed research into accessible summaries, machine learning models to identify emerging agricultural trends from heterogeneous datasets (satellite imagery, sensor networks, social media), and agent-based simulations to optimize information delivery strategies across regional communication networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale agricultural datasets, training of deep learning models on geospatial and temporal data, and stochastic modeling of information diffusion patterns in rural communities. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for generating dynamic, data-driven communication materials (interactive maps, predictive dashboards, multimedia storyboards) that adapt to localized agricultural contexts. This work will enhance the capacity of agricultural journalists to communicate scientific insights with greater accuracy, speed, and relevance, particularly in crisis scenarios such as pest outbreaks or market disruptions. By integrating computational rigor with communication theory, the project aims to establish new best practices for translating agricultural science into public knowledge, ultimately supporting evidence-based decision-making among farmers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply journalistic, communication, and broadcasting principles to the development, production, and transmittal of agricultural information.
