Includes instruction in basic journalism, broadcasting, film/video, and communication techniques; the production of technically specialized information products for agricultural audiences; and the principles of agricultural sciences and business operations needed to develop and communicate agricultural subject matter in effective ways.

abstract: Modern avionics systems integrate complex sensor arrays, adaptive control algorithms, and networked communication protocols, creating maintenance challenges that outpace traditional diagnostic methods. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to predict cascading subsystem failures in next-generation aircraft electronics, a problem exacerbated by interdependent components and nonlinear degradation patterns. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train graph neural networks (GNNs) on multi-modal datasets spanning historical maintenance logs, real-time telemetry from flight data recorders, and physics-based simulations of component wear. Computational workflows will integrate time-series analysis of sensor streams with 3D finite element models of thermal and vibrational stress distributions across avionics hardware. A key innovation involves coupling these models with federated learning architectures to preserve data privacy while aggregating insights from distributed maintenance partners. The project will validate predictions against empirical failure data from three aircraft fleets, using HPC-enabled Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in fault propagation timelines. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic toolkit capable of identifying high-risk failure pathways with 72-hour advance warning at 90% precision, reducing unplanned maintenance downtime by an estimated 33%. By establishing computational methods to disentangle coupled failure modes in modern avionics architectures, this work will directly enhance technician training protocols while informing FAA-certified predictive maintenance standards. Resource requirements focus on GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory instances for multi-physics simulations, enabling a critical shift from reactive to proactive maintenance paradigms in aviation electronics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft operating, control, and electronic systems. Includes instruction in flight instrumentation, aircraft communications and homing systems, radar and other sensory systems, navigation aids, and specialized systems for various types of civilian and military aircraft.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions aim to optimize patient independence by addressing complex interactions between individuals, tasks, and environments. However, current methods for personalizing interventions lack robust predictive tools to model how dynamic environmental factors—such as noise, lighting, or spatial layout—interact with patient-specific motor and cognitive capacities to influence functional performance. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate these interactions and predict optimal environmental modifications for individuals with neurological conditions, such as traumatic brain injury or stroke. Using agent-based modeling and finite element analysis, we will create patient-specific avatars that replicate biomechanical and cognitive profiles derived from clinical assessments, wearable sensor data, and neuroimaging. These avatars will interact with virtual environments parameterized using real-world spatial and sensory data collected via 3D LiDAR scanning and IoT sensors. Computational experiments will evaluate how variations in environmental stimuli affect task performance metrics (e.g., time to complete activities of daily living, error rates). Machine learning models will then identify intervention strategies that maximize functional outcomes. The scale of data integration (high-resolution imaging, real-time sensor streams) and the combinatorial complexity of environmental variables necessitate HPC resources for parallelized simulations and optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform to guide clinicians in designing context-aware interventions, reducing the trial-and-error approach currently prevalent in OT practice. This work bridges computational neuroscience, ergonomics, and rehabilitation science, offering a novel methodology to advance precision occupational therapy. By leveraging HPC, the project addresses a critical gap in translating heterogeneous clinical and environmental data into actionable, personalized therapeutic strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist patients limited by physical, cognitive, psychosocial, mental, developmental, and learning disabilities, as well as adverse environmental conditions, to maximize their independence and maintain optimum health through a planned mix of acquired skills, performance motivation, environmental adaptations, assistive technologies, and physical agents. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, psychology, sociology, patient assessment and evaluation, standardized and non-standardized tests and measurements, assistive and rehabilitative technologies, ergonomics, environmental health, special education, vocational counseling, health education and promotion, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the interplay between ecological dynamics and evolutionary adaptation in spatially structured populations under climate-driven environmental shifts. A critical challenge in ecology and evolutionary biology lies in disentangling how species interactions, dispersal limitations, and trait plasticity jointly shape adaptive trajectories in heterogeneous landscapes. Current models often simplify spatial complexity or neglect eco-evolutionary feedbacks, limiting their predictive power for biodiversity conservation. To address this, we propose a spatially explicit, individual-based modeling framework integrating genomic variation, species interaction networks, and dynamic environmental gradients. The model will simulate multi-trophic communities across realistic landscapes, parameterized with empirical data on plant-pollinator networks and genomic clines from ongoing field studies in montane ecosystems. HPC resources are essential to resolve fine-grained spatial heterogeneity, track allele frequencies across millions of individuals, and run replicate simulations under diverse climate scenarios. Key computational challenges include parallelizing fitness calculations across interacting species, optimizing memory usage for large genomic datasets, and implementing adaptive time-stepping algorithms to capture timescales spanning ecological and evolutionary processes. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how landscape connectivity mediates trade-offs between local adaptation and range shifts, predictions of extinction risk for species with contrasting dispersal strategies, and identification of conservation corridors that maintain coevolutionary potential. Results will directly inform management strategies for biodiversity hotspots facing rapid environmental change, while advancing theoretical frameworks at the interface of community ecology and evolutionary genetics. This work underscores the necessity of HPC capabilities to bridge traditionally separate scales of biological organization in predictive conservation science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions across levels of biological organization--genes and genomes, organisms, species, and ecosystems--and how these change over time, including the origins and history of species, the processes by which biodiversity has evolved, and the ecological context in which this evolution takes place. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the acoustical and performative dynamics of stringed instruments through advanced computational modeling and analysis. While traditional pedagogical and analytical methods in string performance emphasize subjective, experiential learning, they lack granular tools to quantify the relationship between instrumental technique, physical gesture, and resulting sound. This gap limits the ability to systematically decode complex performance practices or innovate instrument design. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) of string vibration, machine learning (ML)-based audio feature extraction, and motion capture data analysis from live performances. HPC resources are critical for simulating high-resolution, time-domain models of string behavior under diverse bowing/plucking conditions, which demand parallelized solvers to handle nonlinear interactions between strings, resonating bodies, and environmental factors. Concurrently, ML pipelines will process terabytes of multimodal performance data—audio, gesture kinematics, and physiological signals—to identify patterns linking technical execution to timbral outcomes. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated performance corpora, predictive models of tone production efficiency, and interactive visualization tools for educators to demonstrate biomechanical principles in real time. By bridging computational acoustics and performance pedagogy, this work aims to establish empirically grounded frameworks for skill acquisition, instrument design optimization, and the preservation of endangered performance traditions. The project directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance mastery of stringed instruments through interdisciplinary innovation, offering performers and luthiers data-driven insights into the physical and artistic dimensions of their craft.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individual to master a stringed instrument and performing arts as solo, ensemble and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing resource-constrained edge computing systems for real-time, distributed applications in smart infrastructure and industrial IoT. As edge devices proliferate in scale and heterogeneity, traditional simulation tools fail to accurately model the dynamic interactions between hardware architectures, energy budgets, and latency-critical workloads at operational scales. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate multi-agent edge networks with 10,000+ nodes, incorporating hardware-in-the-loop validation for embedded processors and reconfigurable computing platforms. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation with parallelized digital twins of field-programmable gate array (FPGA) clusters and microcontrollers, leveraging GPU-accelerated task scheduling algorithms to model energy-time tradeoffs under varying network topologies. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to predict optimal resource allocation strategies for mixed-criticality workloads. The project requires access to HPC resources for large-scale parameter sweeps across device configurations, communication protocols, and failure scenarios, which are computationally intractable on local clusters. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for edge computing design, quantitative benchmarks for energy-efficient task partitioning in heterogeneous environments, and novel scheduling heuristics adaptable to hardware runtime constraints. This work will directly benefit practitioners developing next-generation industrial control systems and smart city infrastructure by providing validated models to balance computational performance with power and latency requirements. Results will be disseminated through engineering technology conferences and industry partnerships, bridging gaps between theoretical resource allocation models and deployable embedded system implementations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian hierarchical models to analyze high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets common in public health and environmental science applications. Traditional statistical methods struggle with the computational demands of modern datasets, which often include spatial-temporal dependencies, missing data, and complex interaction effects. Our research focuses on creating efficient Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling algorithms optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures, enabling inference on models with millions of parameters. The computational approach combines adaptive Metropolis-Hastings methods with parallel tempering techniques, implemented through a hybrid MPI-OpenMP framework to maximize node-level efficiency on cluster architectures. We propose novel preconditioning strategies for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) samplers to reduce autocorrelation in chains while maintaining computational tractability. The project will validate methods through case studies in two domains: (1) multi-scale modeling of climate-health interactions using merged satellite imagery and electronic health records, and (2) Bayesian network analysis of genomic-epidemiological data with latent confounding variables. Resource requests include GPU-accelerated nodes for gradient calculations in HMC and large-memory nodes for covariance matrix operations in Gaussian process components. Expected outcomes include open-source R/Python packages implementing the optimized algorithms, quantitative benchmarks comparing convergence rates across HPC configurations, and substantive findings about environmental drivers of health disparities. This work addresses critical gaps in statistical computing for massive observational datasets while advancing methodological foundations for uncertainty quantification in decision-making pipelines. Successful implementation would enable applied researchers to fit previously intractable models without sacrificing Bayesian rigor, particularly benefiting interdisciplinary teams working on urgent societal challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Armenian linguistic diversity and historical language evolution. Despite its rich literary tradition and dialectal complexity, Armenian remains underrepresented in digital philology and computational linguistics, with limited scalable tools for analyzing its phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variations across time and geography. The research problem centers on the lack of integrated, large-scale datasets and models capable of capturing the dynamic interplay between Classical Armenian (Grabar), modern standardized forms (Eastern/Western Armenian), and regional dialects, which are increasingly endangered. To address this, the project will employ computational methods including natural language processing (NLP), machine learning-based dialect classification, and phylogenetic modeling of language change. HPC resources will enable the processing of digitized historical manuscripts, contemporary texts, and oral corpora—spanning over 1,500 years—to construct a unified linguistic corpus. Parallelized algorithms will map phonetic shifts and grammatical innovations across dialects, while transformer-based models will be trained to identify diachronic and synchronic patterns in lexical semantics. Additionally, agent-based simulations will test hypotheses about language contact effects, particularly between Armenian and neighboring languages. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts, predictive models of dialectal divergence, and tools for automated transliteration of non-standard orthographies. These resources will significantly advance Armenian language scholarship by enabling quantitative, data-driven approaches to philological inquiry, supporting preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and fostering applications in language education, translation technologies, and cross-disciplinary humanities research. The project’s computational demands—including large-scale data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and multi-node phylogenetic analyses—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve scalability, reproducibility, and open access to results.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by Armenians. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The development of therapeutic agents with high efficacy and specificity remains challenging due to the complexity of drug-target interactions, particularly in systems prone to resistance or off-target effects. Current limitations in experimental screening and structural analysis often delay the identification of viable candidates, especially for emerging targets in oncology and infectious diseases. This project proposes a computational strategy integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML), and virtual screening to accelerate the discovery of novel compounds targeting kinase inhibitors and antimicrobial proteins. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform large-scale, atomistic MD simulations (using AMBER and GROMACS) that capture conformational dynamics of target proteins over microsecond timescales, enabling the identification of cryptic binding pockets and allosteric sites. Parallelized virtual screening of >500,000 compounds from the ZINC15 library will be conducted via ensemble docking (AutoDock-GPU) across multiple protein conformations to account for structural flexibility. ML models (PyTorch, DeepChem) will predict binding affinities and pharmacokinetic properties using features derived from simulation trajectories and ligand descriptors. The HPC environment will support training these models on terabytes of structural data while enabling hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include the identification of lead compounds with improved selectivity for mutant kinases and bacterial efflux pump inhibitors, as well as mechanistic insights into resistance pathways. This work will establish a scalable framework for rational drug design, reducing reliance on low-throughput experimental screens. The resource allocation will also facilitate the development of open-source tools for predictive toxicology and support cross-disciplinary training in computational medicinal chemistry, bridging gaps between molecular modeling and translational pharmacology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemistry to the study of biologically and clinically active substances, biological and pharmacological interactions, and the development of associated research methods, techniques, and clinical trial procedures. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular graphics, rational drug design, toxicology, molecular biology, pharmacology, enzyme mechanisms, receptor theory, neurochemistry, drug metabolism, drug synthesis, biological mechanisms of drug action, research tools and techniques, and laboratory safety.

abstract: Social service systems face critical challenges in equitably and efficiently allocating resources to vulnerable populations, particularly during crises such as natural disasters or pandemics. Current decision-making frameworks often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between community needs, resource availability, and systemic inequities. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate and optimize resource allocation strategies for social service delivery under crisis conditions. The research will leverage agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with machine learning (ML) techniques to represent heterogeneous populations, service providers, and environmental stressors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations that account for multi-level variables—including demographic disparities, real-time resource constraints, and policy interventions—across synthetic populations mirroring real-world complexity. Computational experiments will evaluate scenarios such as emergency housing distribution, mental health service access, and disaster relief logistics, using empirical data from public health agencies and community partners. Expected outcomes include the identification of resilience-building allocation policies, metrics for quantifying equity-efficiency tradeoffs, and open-source tools for adaptive decision support. By advancing computational social work methodologies, this project aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers and practitioners while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional domains. The resulting framework will be generalizable to diverse service contexts, offering a foundation for data-driven advocacy and systemic change in public administration.
cip_definition: Any program providing instruction in social work and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in motorcycle engine performance optimization and predictive maintenance through advanced computational modeling. Modern motorcycles integrate complex mechanical, electrical, and fuel systems, where small inefficiencies in components such as carburetors, ignition timing, or cooling systems can lead to significant performance degradation or failure. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to diagnostics and tuning are time-intensive and often fail to account for dynamic interactions between subsystems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of high-fidelity simulations leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multiphysics interactions within motorcycle engines and drivetrains. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to analyze fuel-air mixture dynamics in carburetion systems under varying operational conditions, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess thermal stress distributions in engine components. Machine learning models trained on synthetic and experimental datasets will predict wear patterns in moving parts and optimize maintenance schedules. The scale of these simulations—particularly the resolution required for micron-level fuel droplet behavior in carburetors and real-time thermal profiling—necessitates parallelized computing architectures. By integrating these computational tools, the project aims to generate actionable insights for (1) optimizing fuel efficiency and emissions in legacy and modern engines, (2) developing predictive maintenance algorithms to reduce mechanical failures, and (3) informing the design of next-generation lubrication and cooling systems. Outcomes will be validated against dynamometer tests and field data from industry partners. Successful implementation will provide a template for data-driven motorcycle maintenance protocols, reduce environmental impact through emission minimization, and enhance the technical toolkit available to motorcycle repair technicians. This work directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance repair technologies through innovative technical methodologies.
cip_title: Motorcycle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain motorcycles and other similar powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication and cooling systems, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuel systems and adjustments of moving parts.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying human-animal interactions during animal-assisted therapy (AAT) sessions, with a focus on optimizing intervention protocols for individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Despite growing clinical adoption of AAT, the dynamic interplay between patient stress biomarkers, therapy animal behavior, and environmental variables remains poorly quantified, limiting evidence-based standardization. The research employs high-resolution multimodal data integration, combining wearable biometric sensors (measuring heart rate variability, electrodermal activity), synchronized video recordings of human-animal dyads, and environmental context logging. A computational pipeline will be developed to process these heterogeneous datasets at scale, utilizing machine learning models to identify temporal patterns linking animal behavioral cues (e.g., proximity, gaze direction, tactile interactions) to autonomic nervous system responses in participants. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: 1) Parallel processing of high-frequency biometric time series (≥1kHz sampling rates) across extended observation periods, 2) Training deep learning architectures on video data to automatically classify nuanced interspecies interaction patterns, and 3) Running agent-based simulations modeling different therapy session parameters. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for personalizing AAT session structures based on real-time physiological feedback and the identification of neuroregulatory pathways activated during effective human-animal interactions. This work bridges gaps between comparative neuroscience, computational ethology, and clinical rehabilitation sciences, providing quantitative foundations for optimizing AAT protocols while establishing novel metrics for assessing interspecies therapeutic efficacy. The computational tools developed will enable future investigations into cross-species social cognition mechanisms across diverse clinical populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares health and human service professionals to integrate the use of animals into their treatment practices in order to facilitate change in people with mental and physical disabilities. Includes instruction in psychology, psychology of disabilities, animal behavior, animal training, the human-animal bond, integration of animals into therapeutic settings, and ethical and cultural issues.

abstract: The increasing complexity of urban transportation networks, coupled with growing demands for efficiency and sustainability, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize infrastructure planning and traffic management. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework for evaluating multimodal transportation systems under dynamic conditions, integrating traffic flow modeling, infrastructure resilience assessment, and emissions forecasting. Current approaches often rely on simplified network representations or static demand profiles, limiting their ability to capture emergent congestion patterns, cascading failure risks, and environmental impacts in heterogeneous transportation corridors. To address these limitations, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture coupled with parallelized finite element analysis, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources for large-scale parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification. The computational workflow will process terabyte-scale datasets from connected vehicle sensors, traffic cameras, and infrastructure health monitors, employing GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to model interactions between autonomous vehicles, public transit, and active transportation modes. Key challenges include real-time calibration of mesoscopic traffic models, energy-efficient routing under stochastic demand scenarios, and lifecycle assessment of pavement materials under climate variability. The proposed HPC implementation will enable ensemble simulations across 10^4 scenario permutations at metropolitan-scale resolution, reducing wall-clock time from weeks to hours compared to conventional cluster computing. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for prioritizing infrastructure investments, dynamic congestion pricing policies, and decarbonization strategies aligned with regional climate goals. This work will provide transportation agencies with decision-support frameworks that balance mobility, equity, and environmental objectives while addressing computational bottlenecks in large-scale transportation system analysis. Resource allocation requests focus on distributed memory architectures with high-core-count nodes and GPU partitions to support mixed-precision calculations across spatial-temporal scales.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems for the physical movement of people, materials and information, including general network design and planning, facilities planning, site evaluation, transportation management systems, needs projections and analysis, and analysis of costs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale comparative analysis of syntactic and phonetic shifts across regional Romance language varieties, with a focus on understudied dialects of Occitan, Sardinian, and Rhaeto-Romance. While historical linguistics has long relied on manual corpus analysis, the increasing digitization of regional texts, oral histories, and phonetic datasets now enables computational approaches to modeling language evolution. However, processing these heterogeneous datasets—spanning centuries of textual records, audio fragments, and modern speech samples—requires significant computational power for parallelized text parsing, acoustic feature extraction, and machine learning-driven pattern detection. Our methodology integrates NLP tools adapted for non-standard orthographies with neural models trained to identify diachronic and synchronic variations in morphosyntactic structures. Phonetic data will undergo spectral analysis via GPU-accelerated pipelines to map vowel shifts and consonantal innovations across geographic clusters. The project’s computational demands center on managing multi-terabyte datasets, running iterative simulations of language change hypotheses, and training transformer-based models on dialect-specific corpora. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database linking syntactic innovations to sociocultural factors, (2) probabilistic models of language contact effects in Romance microvarieties, and (3) open-source tools for low-resource dialect analysis. By bridging computational linguistics with philological expertise, this work aims to reshape understanding of Romance language diversification while developing scalable methods applicable to other under-resourced linguistic systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling memory-intensive comparative analyses and ensuring reproducibility across iterative model training phases.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Romance languages of Western, Central, and Southern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and deployment of sensor networks for monitoring industrial emissions in complex urban environments. Current methods for pollution tracking often rely on sparse, static sensor arrays, which struggle to capture dynamic pollutant dispersion patterns influenced by variable meteorological conditions, heterogeneous building layouts, and multi-source emissions. To address this gap, we propose coupling high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with machine learning-driven sensor placement algorithms. The CFD models will simulate airborne contaminant transport at neighborhood scales using open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM), incorporating real-world building geometry data and time-varying emission sources. Concurrently, reinforcement learning models will iteratively optimize sensor locations to maximize detection sensitivity while minimizing deployment costs. The integration of these components demands high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the need for parallelized simulations across hundreds of parameterized scenarios, large-scale spatial-temporal data processing, and training of deep neural networks on 3D flow fields. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive sensor network design, validated against field data from collaborating industrial partners. This work directly supports environmental engineering technologists in implementing cost-effective, data-driven air quality monitoring systems, with potential applications in regulatory compliance, public health risk mitigation, and emissions source identification. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sensitivity studies, model calibration at unprecedented spatial resolutions (sub-1m grid scales), and benchmarking against legacy monitoring approaches. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops targeting environmental technology practitioners, ensuring translational impact beyond academic circles.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using indoor and outdoor environmental pollution control systems. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The emergence and spread of infectious diseases in livestock populations present critical challenges to animal health, agricultural productivity, and food security. Current limitations in predicting pathogen evolution, host-pathogen interactions, and disease transmission dynamics hinder proactive interventions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating genomic, epidemiological, and environmental data. We propose a hybrid approach combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate disease spread across heterogeneous livestock populations and landscapes. Genomic datasets from pathogens and host species will be analyzed using phylogenetic tools and deep learning architectures to identify evolutionary patterns and genetic markers associated with virulence or resistance. Concurrently, ABM frameworks will incorporate animal movement data, climate variables, and husbandry practices to model transmission risks at regional scales. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing of large genomic datasets (>100 TB) and iterative simulations across parameter spaces, exceeding the capacity of local computing infrastructure. Access to HPC resources will enable the deployment of containerized workflows for scalable genomic analysis and GPU-accelerated training of ML models. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize surveillance efforts, optimize vaccine targets, and assess mitigation strategies under varying scenarios. This work will directly inform livestock management policies and biosecurity protocols, reducing economic losses and zoonotic risks. By bridging veterinary science and computational innovation, the project aims to establish a framework for real-time, data-driven decision-making in animal health crises, with potential applications in global agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary or animal health technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in patent law research, specifically focusing on the analysis of patent litigation trends and the evolution of legal doctrines in response to emerging technologies. While patent law is a specialized legal domain, its increasing intersection with fast-paced technological innovation—such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and quantum computing—creates complex, data-driven research questions that traditional legal methodologies struggle to address efficiently. The primary research problem lies in systematically evaluating how judicial decisions and patent examination practices adapt to novel technical domains, a task requiring large-scale text analysis, pattern recognition, and predictive modeling across heterogeneous datasets. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques to parse legal texts (court opinions, patent filings, and administrative rulings) with machine learning algorithms to identify doctrinal shifts, semantic trends, and correlations between technical patent claims and litigation outcomes. Graph-based analytics will map citation networks and precedent influence within case law, while clustering methods will categorize patent disputes by technical complexity and jurisdictional variance. These workflows demand significant memory allocation and parallel processing capabilities due to the volume of unstructured data (millions of patent documents and legal opinions) and the iterative nature of training domain-specific language models. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational framework for real-time monitoring of patent law evolution, predictive tools to assess litigation risks for emerging technologies, and quantitative insights into how legal frameworks lag behind or adapt to technological disruption. The project bridges computational science and legal scholarship, offering a template for data-driven policy analysis in specialized professional disciplines. By enabling scalable analysis of legal systems, this work aims to inform reforms in patent adjudication, enhance transparency in patent quality assessment, and provide stakeholders with actionable tools to navigate rapidly changing innovation ecosystems.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting patents.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance evidence-based intervention strategies for students exhibiting behavioral challenges by leveraging large-scale, multidimensional datasets through advanced computational modeling. School psychologists often face complex decisions when designing interventions, as student outcomes are influenced by dynamic interactions between individual, classroom, and systemic factors. Traditional statistical methods struggle to capture these nonlinear relationships or optimize personalized recommendations across diverse student populations. To address this gap, we propose developing machine learning (ML) models to analyze longitudinal datasets encompassing academic performance, behavioral assessments, socioemotional surveys, and intervention histories from 50,000+ K–12 students. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training neural networks and ensemble models capable of identifying latent patterns in high-dimensional data, including text-based counseling notes and temporal sequences of behavioral incidents. Computational workflows will integrate feature engineering, cross-validation, and sensitivity analyses to evaluate model robustness, with a focus on equitable outcomes across demographic subgroups. Additionally, agent-based simulations will test hypothetical intervention scenarios under varying classroom conditions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize interventions for at-risk students, personalized strategy recommendations, and actionable insights into systemic barriers affecting implementation fidelity. By quantifying the interplay of factors shaping intervention efficacy, this work aims to advance data-driven practices in school psychology, reduce trial-and-error decision-making, and improve scalability of support services. The project aligns with the program’s emphasis on ethical, culturally responsive applications of psychological principles, ensuring models are interpretable for practitioners and compliant with student privacy regulations. HPC resources will enable the iterative refinement required to balance computational complexity with practical utility in school settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing large-scale construction project planning and execution under dynamic uncertainties, including variable material behaviors, environmental conditions, and logistical constraints. Traditional computational methods often fail to integrate multi-physics simulations with real-time decision-making, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation, cost overruns, and safety risks. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable high-fidelity, multi-scale modeling of construction processes. The approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessment, discrete-event simulation for logistics optimization, and machine learning algorithms to predict material performance under diverse environmental conditions. By parallelizing these computationally intensive workflows, HPC resources will facilitate rapid iteration of design alternatives, sensitivity analyses of site-specific geotechnical data, and stochastic risk modeling for schedule delays. The project will also develop a digital twin platform to visualize and simulate interactions between construction phases, supply chains, and external factors such as weather patterns. Expected outcomes include scalable algorithms for real-time adaptive project management, validated against case studies of bridge and high-rise construction projects. This research will advance computational capabilities in construction engineering by providing open-source tools for integrating HPC into civil infrastructure planning, ultimately reducing project timelines and enhancing resilience. The results will directly inform industry standards for data-driven decision-making, contributing to sustainable infrastructure development and cost-effective resource utilization in urban environments.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and management principles to the planning, design, and building of facilities and structures. Includes instruction in civil engineering, structural principles, site analysis, computer-assisted design, geology, evaluation and testing, materials, contracting, project management, graphic communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Maternal and neonatal health outcomes are influenced by complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors, yet current clinical tools often fail to adequately predict or mitigate risks such as preterm birth, preeclampsia, or neonatal sepsis. This project seeks to develop computational models to identify multifactorial risk signatures and optimize personalized care pathways for pregnant individuals and newborns. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), multi-omics datasets, and longitudinal environmental exposure data from diverse maternal-child cohorts. Machine learning approaches, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be applied to integrate heterogeneous data types and uncover predictive biomarkers for adverse outcomes. Concurrently, multiscale physiological modeling will simulate maternal-fetal systems to explore mechanisms underlying placental dysfunction and neonatal metabolic instability. These computational workflows demand significant memory and parallel processing capabilities due to the volume of EHRs (over 500,000 patient records), high-resolution genomic data, and iterative model training requirements. The project will also employ agent-based modeling to assess the impact of dynamic variables, such as gestational nutrition or pharmacological interventions, on maternal-newborn health trajectories. Outcomes will include validated risk stratification tools for clinical use, open-access predictive models to guide neonatal resuscitation protocols, and mechanistic insights into pathways linking maternal stressors to neonatal outcomes. By enabling real-time analysis of complex datasets and high-fidelity simulations, HPC resources will directly support the translation of computational findings into scalable interventions, reducing disparities in maternal and neonatal morbidity. This work aligns with national priorities to enhance perinatal care through precision health approaches, offering novel strategies to optimize resource allocation in under-resourced clinical settings.
cip_title: Maternal/ Child Health and Neonatal Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide prenatal care to pregnant women and to mothers and their newborn infants. Includes instruction in perinatal and newborn health assessment, stabilization, and care; pathophysiology of pregnancy, fetuses, and the newborn; clinical management of high-risk pregnancies and newborns; perinatal and neonatal technology and clinical procedures; and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to optimize energy-efficient environmental control systems for urban buildings, addressing the critical challenge of reducing carbon emissions while maintaining occupant comfort. Current heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems often operate suboptimally due to dynamic environmental variables, leading to excessive energy use. To overcome this, we propose a multi-physics modeling approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML), and real-time sensor data assimilation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex interactions between airflow, thermal transfer, and particulate dispersion at high spatial-temporal resolutions across diverse building geometries. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized CFD simulations to generate training datasets for ML models, which will then predict optimal HVAC control parameters under varying occupancy, weather, and pollution conditions. Validation will utilize historical building performance data from municipal partners. The expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of reducing HVAC energy consumption by 20–30% in simulated urban buildings, with direct applications to retrofitting existing infrastructure. This research will also quantify trade-offs between energy savings and indoor air quality, providing actionable insights for policymakers. By deploying HPC resources, the project aims to overcome current limitations in simulation fidelity and computational speed, enabling city-scale analyses that are infeasible on conventional systems. The results will advance sustainable building technologies and support climate resilience goals, aligning with global efforts to decarbonize urban environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental control technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamics of social networks and behavioral patterns within correctional facilities, with the goal of identifying systemic factors that influence conflict escalation and rehabilitation outcomes. Despite the critical role of correctional environments in public safety and social reintegration, predictive tools to analyze large-scale, longitudinal interactions among incarcerated individuals, staff, and institutional policies remain underdeveloped. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex, adaptive systems within carceral settings, integrating anonymized administrative data (e.g., incident reports, program participation records) with agent-based modeling (ABM) to represent heterogeneous populations. Computational workflows will parameterize individual behaviors, group affiliations, and environmental stressors, enabling the testing of hypothetical interventions—such as modified housing assignments or educational programming—under controlled virtual scenarios. A hybrid approach combining graph theory, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning will be employed to detect latent patterns in historical data and validate model accuracy against real-world outcomes. The scale of analysis (spanning thousands of agents over multi-year timelines) necessitates distributed computing architectures to manage memory-intensive simulations and probabilistic sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for correctional administrators to evaluate policy impacts on facility safety and recidivism reduction, as well as novel metrics for quantifying the cascading effects of institutional decision-making. By bridging computational social science with correctional practice, this work addresses a critical gap in evidence-based carceral management while adhering to ethical guidelines for data anonymization and bias mitigation. The proposed HPC resources are essential to achieving the granularity, iteration speed, and statistical power required for actionable insights in this high-stakes domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study the theories and principles, of correctional science and to function as professional corrections officers and other workers in public and/or private incarceration facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-species signaling networks in rapidly changing coastal ecosystems, integrating ecological, geochemical, and acoustic data streams to model anthropogenic impacts on interspecies communication. Coastal zones face unprecedented pressures from urbanization, climate change, and industrial activity, yet the computational synthesis of multi-modal biological and environmental data remains underdeveloped. Our research addresses this gap by developing a novel framework to analyze how noise pollution, chemical contaminants, and habitat fragmentation disrupt vibrational and chemical signaling among invertebrates, fish, and marine mammals—processes critical to mating, predation avoidance, and collective behavior. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will process petabyte-scale datasets from hydrophone arrays, mass spectrometry, and satellite imagery using hybrid convolutional neural networks and graph-based dynamical systems models. The computational workflow will synchronize heterogeneous temporal resolutions (millisecond acoustic events to decadal chemical concentration trends) and spatially explicit interactions across three study regions with varying anthropogenic footprints. Key innovations include adaptive attention mechanisms for cross-domain feature fusion and agent-based simulations of signaling cascades under future climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first unified atlas of coastal biosignaling networks, predictive models of threshold effects on communication resilience, and open-source tools for real-time monitoring of ecosystem-scale stress indicators. By bridging marine biology, complexity science, and environmental informatics, this work will establish computational standards for assessing multispecies vulnerability while informing policy frameworks for acoustic and chemical pollution mitigation. The scale of data integration and need for ensemble simulation across parameter spaces necessitates HPC resources to achieve sufficient temporal granularity and spatial coverage for robust ecological inference.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the scalability and responsiveness of adaptive troubleshooting systems designed for heterogeneous user populations in enterprise environments. Current help desk tools often rely on static decision trees or generalized user models, which struggle to account for the variability in user technical literacy, neurodiversity, or situational stressors, leading to inefficient resource use and prolonged issue resolution. To address this gap, we propose developing a dynamic, machine learning-driven framework that personalizes troubleshooting workflows in real time by integrating multimodal user interaction data (e.g., speech patterns, clickstream dynamics, and biometric feedback from wearable devices) with system diagnostics. The core computational challenge lies in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive data streams while maintaining low-latency responses—a task requiring distributed GPU-accelerated architectures. Using high-performance computing resources, we will train ensemble models combining transformer-based natural language processing for ticket analysis, temporal convolutional networks for interaction sequence modeling, and federated learning to preserve user privacy across organizational silos. Simulations will replicate diverse user cohorts and infrastructure scenarios to stress-test the system’s adaptability. Expected outcomes include an open-source middleware prototype that reduces mean ticket resolution time by ≥30% in pilot deployments and a corpus of annotated multimodal troubleshooting datasets. This work bridges human-computer interaction, operational analytics, and edge computing, directly advancing the capabilities of computer support specialists to deliver equitable, context-aware assistance in complex socio-technical ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical assistance, support, and advice to computer users to help troubleshoot software and hardware problems. Includes instruction in computer concepts, information systems, networking, operating systems, computer hardware, the Internet, software applications, help desk concepts and problem solving, and principles of customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address inverse problems arising in medical imaging, specifically focusing on reconstructing high-resolution images from sparse or noisy data. Such problems are governed by ill-posed integral equations, where traditional reconstruction techniques struggle with stability, accuracy, and computational efficiency. The research aims to bridge this gap by formulating novel iterative regularization frameworks that integrate spatially adaptive priors and stochastic optimization. A key challenge lies in solving large-scale, nonlinear optimization problems with millions of variables, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach combines parallelized Krylov subspace methods for linear systems with GPU-accelerated proximal gradient algorithms, leveraging distributed memory architectures to manage memory-intensive operations. Adaptive mesh refinement will be implemented to dynamically resolve regions of high geometric complexity or data sensitivity. The project will validate these methods using simulated and experimental datasets from X-ray computed tomography (CT) and diffuse optical tomography (DOT), benchmarking against clinical reconstruction standards. Successful implementation is expected to yield algorithms that reduce reconstruction errors by 20-30% compared to conventional methods while maintaining feasible runtime for clinical workflows. The outcomes will provide open-source software tools for the medical imaging community, with potential applications in real-time diagnostic imaging and personalized treatment planning. Access to HPC resources is critical to handle the O(10^7)-dimensional parameter spaces, perform hyperparameter tuning via large-scale Bayesian optimization, and enable reproducibility across diverse imaging modalities. This work advances applied mathematics by unifying theoretical analysis of inverse problems with cutting-edge computational techniques, directly addressing scalability barriers in modern medical imaging technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in applied mathematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize hazardous waste treatment processes and predict long-term environmental risks associated with contaminant transport in heterogeneous subsurface environments. Current methods for managing mixed hazardous wastes—particularly those involving reactive chemical or biological agents—often rely on empirical trial-and-error approaches, leading to inefficiencies in treatment efficacy, energy use, and cost. Additionally, existing predictive tools for contaminant migration lack the resolution to account for microscale interactions between waste constituents and geochemical matrices. To address these gaps, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating quantum mechanical calculations, reactive transport simulations, and machine learning-driven optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable density functional theory (DFT) simulations to characterize degradation pathways of priority pollutants, coupled with pore-scale lattice Boltzmann models to resolve fluid-contaminant interactions in engineered barrier systems. These outputs will inform macroscale finite element models simulating contaminant dispersion under varying hydrological regimes. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize waste treatment parameters to minimize resource consumption while meeting regulatory thresholds. The computational intensity of coupling these methods necessitates parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows and large-memory nodes for handling complex 3D geospatial datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide the design of safer waste stabilization protocols, risk assessment matrices for legacy disposal sites, and open-source modules for adaptive treatment process control. By enhancing the precision of hazardous material lifecycle management, this work aims to reduce environmental remediation costs, improve regulatory decision-making, and mitigate long-term public health hazards. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial-temporal resolution required for actionable insights in this high-stakes domain.
cip_title: Hazardous Materials Management and Waste Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in identifying and disposing of hazardous materials. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, biohazard identification, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, hazardous waste disposal procedures and systems, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of the inner ear’s biomechanical and neurophysiological systems, with the goal of improving treatment strategies for hearing loss and vestibular disorders. Current clinical interventions for conditions such as Meniere’s disease, otosclerosis, and noise-induced hearing loss are limited by incomplete understanding of how pathological changes in the temporal bone affect mechano-electrical signal transduction in the cochlea and vestibular organs. To address this, we propose developing multiscale finite element models (FEMs) that integrate micro-computed tomography (µCT) data of human temporal bones with biophysical simulations of hair cell activation, neural encoding, and fluid-structure interactions in the inner ear. These models will require iterative solvers and parallelized workflows to resolve micron-scale geometries and nonlinear, time-dependent dynamics across multiple physical domains (acoustic, mechanical, electrochemical). HPC resources are essential to manage the computational load, as preliminary single-node simulations of simplified cochlear segments already exceed 72 hours runtime. We will parameterize models using patient-specific µCT and audiometric datasets from a retrospective cohort (n=150) to simulate disease progression and predict outcomes for surgical interventions (e.g., stapedectomy, cochlear implantation). Machine learning pipelines will then analyze simulation outputs to identify biomarkers of treatment efficacy. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models of post-intervention hearing and balance recovery, (2) optimization frameworks for personalized device tuning, and (3) open-source simulation tools to accelerate translational research in neurotology. By bridging spatial scales and physical processes that are experimentally intractable, this computational approach has the potential to redefine preoperative planning paradigms and reduce trial-and-error in clinical management of temporal bone disorders.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat diseases of the ear and temporal bone, including disorders of hearing and balance.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of microbial dysbiosis and host-microbe metabolic cross-talk in the progression of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) to squamous cell carcinoma. Despite advances in understanding genetic drivers of oral carcinogenesis, the contribution of localized microbial communities and their interaction with host immune and epithelial cells remains poorly characterized. This project employs a computational systems biology approach to model dynamic interactions between oral microbiome composition, host tissue microenvironment remodeling, and metabolic pathway alterations across stages of malignancy. High-performance computing resources are required to analyze multi-omics datasets from longitudinal clinical samples (shotgun metagenomics, host transcriptomics, and spatially resolved metabolomics) and simulate emergent behaviors in agent-based models (ABMs) of microbial community-host tissue interfaces. Custom pipelines will integrate taxonomic and functional microbiome data with host cell signaling networks, while ABMs parameterized by clinical and experimental data will simulate how microbial metabolite exchange influences epithelial stem cell differentiation patterns and immune evasion mechanisms. The research aims to identify conserved microbial signatures predictive of malignant transformation and characterize critical nodes in host-microbe metabolic networks that could serve as therapeutic targets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated microbial genomes from oral dysplastic lesions, predictive models of microbial community dynamics during carcinogenesis, and computational frameworks for assessing microenvironment-specific intervention strategies. This work addresses a critical gap in oral cancer prevention by bridging microbial ecology with tissue-scale systems biology, enabling precision approaches to intercept malignant progression in understudied OPMD subtypes.
cip_title: Oral Biology and Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the growth, development, diseases, healing properties, and neurological components of the oral cavity, related tissues and organs, and associated craniofacial areas. Includes instruction in oral microbiology microanatomy, craniofacial pain, humoral aspects of disease, etiology and histology of caries, plaque ecology, wound healing, oral disease epidemiology, oral manifestations of systemic disease, lesions, normal and pathologic physiology, and related molecular and physical studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary study of textual transmission and variation across premodern and early modern manuscript cultures. The research problem centers on the challenges of modeling complex textual relationships within large, multilingual corpora, where manual analysis of variant readings, scribal interventions, and material annotations remains prohibitively time-intensive. By integrating computational methods with traditional philological and codicological frameworks, this work aims to reconstruct dynamic pathways of textual dissemination and adaptation across diverse cultural contexts. The proposed computational approach employs machine learning algorithms to detect patterns in textual variants, supplemented by graph-based network analysis to map genealogical relationships (stemmatology) and paleographic features. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution manuscript images (digitized codices, marginalia, and palimpsests) using convolutional neural networks trained to identify scribal hands and material degradation. Additionally, probabilistic models will simulate textual evolution under varying historical and sociocultural constraints, testing hypotheses about lost archetypes and regional transmission hubs. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for automated collation and annotation of digitized texts, a scalable database of cross-referenced textual variants, and visualizations of manuscript networks that integrate linguistic, material, and historical metadata. These resources will enhance collaborative scholarship in textual criticism and book history while addressing methodological gaps in analyzing non-linear, multigenerational textual adaptation. The project’s significance lies in its capacity to bridge computational scalability with humanistic interpretative rigor, offering new pathways to study how texts mutate across media, languages, and epistemic shifts. By situating HPC-driven analysis within interdisciplinary textual studies, this research will provide replicable frameworks for modeling cultural transmission at scale, with implications for archival practices, digital editions, and the preservation of textual heritage.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interconnected histories of digital or print texts and manuscripts for cultural and literary study. Includes instruction in archiving texts, bibliography, book and literary history, cultural studies, codicology, paleography, stemmatology, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the morphological and syntactic evolution of North Germanic languages, with a focus on quantifying divergence patterns among modern Scandinavian languages and their historical antecedents. Despite rich philological scholarship on Old Norse and its descendants, the dynamics of language change—particularly the interplay of sociocultural factors and structural innovations—remain under-modeled in computational terms. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze a diachronic corpus spanning Old Norse manuscripts (8th–14th centuries), early modern texts (1500–1800), and contemporary digital sources. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based language models to detect syntactic shifts, implementing phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct proto-features, and simulating contact-induced changes across regional dialects. The corpus, comprising digitized sagas, legal texts, and modern speech transcripts (≈10 TB), necessitates parallelized processing for tokenization, morphological tagging, and dependency parsing. Expected outcomes include (1) a probabilistic model of morphological regularization in Norwegian and Swedish, (2) a comparative analysis of vowel harmony loss in Icelandic versus retention in Faroese, and (3) an open-access toolkit for diachronic morphosyntactic annotation. By integrating computational linguistics with philological expertise, this work will advance understanding of language divergence in Scandinavia while establishing scalable methods for resource-lean historical languages. The requested HPC allocation will enable GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and storage of intermediate linguistic representations, which are infeasible on local clusters. Results will directly support three peer-reviewed publications and a pedagogical platform for Nordic linguistic heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages, literatures, and linguistics of the peoples of Scandinavia and associated Northern European island groups. Programs may involve multiple languages and language families, not be specific as to the name of the language(s) studied, or be otherwise undifferentiated.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamics of collective decision-making in decentralized, ephemeral online communities—specifically, how transient digital groups negotiate consensus without formal hierarchies or enduring structures. While traditional social sciences have explored group behavior in stable organizations, the rise of platform-based, short-lived collectives (e.g., crowdsourced crisis response teams, pop-up activism networks) presents novel challenges. The research problem centers on identifying scalable computational patterns that predict successful consensus outcomes in these fluid environments, where participation is asynchronous, geographically dispersed, and culturally heterogeneous. The project leverages high-performance computing to analyze multi-modal datasets from three platforms (Discourse, Mastodon, and custom web-forums) encompassing 2.3 million text interactions, user metadata, and temporal activity logs. Natural language processing pipelines will extract semantic features, sentiment trajectories, and argumentation structures, while graph neural networks model interaction networks evolving over sub-hourly timescales. Agent-based simulations will test hypotheses about optimal communication architectures under resource constraints, simulating 10,000+ synthetic communities with varying rulesets for proposal ratification. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of decision-making failure modes in transient groups, (2) an open-source framework for real-time consensus health monitoring, and (3) evidence-based design principles for platforms hosting high-stakes decentralized deliberations. By bridging computational social science with distributed systems theory, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding how trust and coordination scale in digitally native social formations, with implications for disaster response coordination, decentralized governance protocols, and ethical AI-mediated dialogue systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in social sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision nutrition research by modeling complex interactions between dietary patterns, metabolic pathways, and population health outcomes. Current clinical nutrition strategies often rely on generalized guidelines, which inadequately address individual variability in nutrient metabolism, genetic predispositions, and gut microbiome composition. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (genomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic) with dynamic dietary intake records to predict personalized nutrient requirements and metabolic responses. The research problem centers on the computational limitations of existing tools, which struggle to process high-dimensional datasets and simulate non-linear biological interactions at scale. Our approach employs machine learning models, including ensemble methods and graph neural networks, to identify biomarkers of nutrient utilization efficiency, coupled with agent-based simulations to explore how individualized dietary recommendations could mitigate chronic disease risks in diverse populations. Additionally, we will simulate metabolic flux using constraint-based models to predict tissue-specific nutrient partitioning under varying dietary conditions. HPC resources are critical for training large-scale models on linked datasets from public biobanks (e.g., NHANES, UK Biobank) and local clinical cohorts, as well as for running parallelized simulations of metabolic networks and population-scale interventions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dietitians to generate data-driven nutrition plans, a predictive atlas of metabolic responses to dietary components, and evidence-based frameworks for tailoring public health nutrition policies to genetic and microbiome diversity. By elucidating the systems-level effects of diet on health, this work aims to bridge gaps between clinical nutrition practice, biomedical research, and computational science, ultimately supporting more effective, individualized dietary interventions for chronic disease prevention and management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to integrate and apply the principles of the food and nutrition sciences, human behavior, and the biomedical sciences to design and manage effective nutrition programs in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in human nutrition; nutrient metabolism; the role of foods and nutrition in health promotion and disease prevention; planning and directing food service activities; diet and nutrition analysis and planning; supervision of food storage and preparation; client education; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for analyzing and simulating the interplay between human spatial perception and environmental sustainability in pre-architectural design. Traditional architectural pedagogy and practice often rely on static models or simplified simulations, which inadequately capture dynamic human-environment interactions across diverse scales and contexts. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating a parametric, data-driven toolset capable of modeling real-time behavioral responses to spatial configurations while integrating ecological performance metrics (e.g., energy use, material efficiency, thermal comfort). The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate occupant movement and decision-making with finite element analysis (FEA) for evaluating structural and environmental performance. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on datasets spanning historical architectural case studies, biometric feedback from virtual reality (VR) environments, and climate-specific sustainability benchmarks to predict optimal design trade-offs. By deploying these methods on HPC clusters, the project will enable parallel processing of high-resolution spatial datasets and iterative optimization of design parameters—tasks infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a modular software prototype for pre-architecture education, allowing students to visualize and quantify the human and ecological implications of design choices in immersive 3D environments. The project’s significance lies in its interdisciplinary synthesis of architectural theory, environmental science, and computational neuroscience, offering a novel methodology to advance evidence-based, human-centric design principles. Results will contribute to redefining pedagogical tools in pre-architecture curricula while providing a scalable model for integrating performance-based analytics into early-stage architectural ideation.
cip_definition: A program of study that is a precursor to an advanced degree in architecture. Includes instruction in architectural design, architectural graphics, architectural history, architectural technology, architectural theory and criticism, building technology, calculus, design studio, human factors, environmental architecture, geometry and trigonometry, physics, and technical drawing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize heavy equipment operations in earthmoving processes, with the goal of reducing fuel consumption, operational costs, and environmental impact while improving efficiency. Current practices in construction and earthmoving rely heavily on operator experience and generalized guidelines, leading to suboptimal machine utilization, uneven wear, and excessive energy use. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex interactions between heavy equipment, materials, and terrain under dynamic worksite conditions. The research will employ discrete element method (DEM) simulations to model soil and aggregate behavior during excavation, grading, and loading cycles, coupled with multi-body dynamics to simulate equipment kinematics and hydraulic systems. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to analyze simulation outputs and identify optimal operational parameters—such as blade angles, bucket trajectories, and engine torque—for diverse scenarios. The computational workflow will also incorporate real-world sensor data from equipment telemetry systems to validate and refine models. By scaling these simulations across HPC clusters, we aim to generate predictive models that account for variable soil types, moisture levels, and equipment configurations.
