Expected outcomes include actionable guidelines for energy-efficient operation, predictive maintenance schedules based on simulated stress distributions, and a decision-support tool for training operators in virtual environments. This work will advance sustainable practices in construction by bridging empirical knowledge with data-driven insights, potentially reducing fuel use by 15–20% in modeled scenarios. The project will also contribute to academic objectives by integrating HPC-based research into the heavy equipment curriculum, preparing students to engage with digital transformation in the industry.
cip_title: Construction/ Heavy Equipment/ Earthmoving Equipment Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate and maintain a variety of heavy equipment, such as a crawler tractors, motor graders and scrapers, shovels, rigging devices, hoists, and jacks. Includes instruction in digging, ditching, sloping, stripping, grading, and backfilling, clearing and excavating.

abstract: Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of cancer treatment, yet optimizing its efficacy while minimizing toxicity to healthy tissues requires precise, patient-specific modeling of radiation interactions with biological systems. Current treatment planning systems rely on simplified approximations of radiation transport and radiobiological effects, which may compromise accuracy in complex clinical scenarios, such as heterogeneous tumor geometries or adaptive therapies. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models that integrate Monte Carlo-based radiation transport simulations with dynamic radiobiological response algorithms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale, multi-physics simulations that capture the stochastic nature of radiation interactions at the sub-millimeter scale, coupled with spatially resolved biological damage assessments. Key computational challenges include managing terabyte-scale output from particle-tracking simulations, parallelizing radiobiological dose-effect calculations across thousands of CPU cores, and training machine learning surrogates to accelerate parameter optimization for clinical deployment. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time adaptive planning workflows, enabling the analysis of on-board imaging data during treatment sessions. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting tumor control probabilities and normal tissue complication risks with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, which will be tested against retrospective clinical datasets from head-and-neck and lung cancer cohorts. By eliminating reliance on generic dose-prediction algorithms, this work aims to establish a framework for personalized, biologically guided radiation therapy, potentially reducing treatment-related morbidity and improving local control rates. The computational pipelines developed will be disseminated as open-source tools to advance reproducible research in radiation oncology, with direct translational implications for clinical trial design and precision medicine initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of ionizing radiation to treat patients with cancer and other diseases. Includes instruction in treatment planning, instrument design and operation, radiation physics and radiobiology. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: The dynamics of crustal deformation and tectonic plate interactions remain poorly understood due to the complex, multi-scale nature of geophysical processes governing lithospheric behavior. This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of strain localization and fault network evolution in active tectonic regions using high-performance computing (HPC). Current limitations in spatial resolution and temporal scalability hinder the integration of critical variables such as heterogeneous rock rheology, thermal gradients, and fluid-rock interactions at seismogenic depths. To address this, we propose developing a 3D finite element model that couples thermo-mechanical stress evolution with poroelastic fluid transport, calibrated against field observations from the Himalayan orogeny and Basin and Range Province. The computational framework will leverage parallelized solvers to simulate deformation across scales—from grain-boundary processes (micrometers) to regional fault systems (kilometers)—over geologic timescales (1–10 Myr). HPC resources are essential to manage the ~10^8-element mesh required for resolving strain partitioning in multi-phase lithologies and to perform ensemble runs testing sensitivity to initial conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of feedbacks between fluid migration, metamorphic reactions, and shear zone nucleation, (2) probabilistic maps of stress accumulation rates in seismically active regions, and (3) open-source release of optimized viscoelastic solver modules for the geodynamics community. By bridging microstructural constraints with plate-scale dynamics, this work will provide a mechanistic basis for interpreting geodetic signals and seismic hazard assessments while advancing computational capabilities in geomechanical modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and the behavior of the solids, liquids and gases comprising it. Includes instruction in historical geology, geomorphology, and sedimentology, the chemistry of rocks and soils, stratigraphy, mineralogy, petrology, geostatistics, volcanology, glaciology, geophysical principles, and applications to research and industrial problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and predict emergent consumer behavior in decentralized digital marketplaces, with a focus on blockchain-based platforms and tokenized economies. Traditional marketing frameworks struggle to address the dynamic, non-linear interactions between users, algorithms, and cryptographic incentives in these environments, where purchasing decisions are influenced by real-time token valuations, community governance mechanisms, and automated smart contracts. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to simulate multi-agent systems representing diverse stakeholder behaviors—including retail investors, liquidity providers, and autonomous trading bots—under varying market conditions. Agent-based modeling will be combined with reinforcement learning to capture adaptive strategies in decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), while graph neural networks will analyze transactional network topology for latent patterns in asset flows. The computational approach requires parallelized simulations of 10^5+ agents interacting across synthetic markets, with Monte Carlo methods applied to stress-test incentive structures and tokenomic policies. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for community-driven price discovery, identification of critical thresholds in liquidity pool dynamics, and actionable insights for designing marketing strategies that align decentralized governance with user acquisition goals. By quantifying how cryptographic primitives reshape traditional concepts of brand loyalty and customer lifetime value, this work aims to establish a novel interdisciplinary nexus between computational marketing, mechanism design, and cryptoeconomic theory. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of interacting economic agents and real-time blockchain data streams, enabling validation against live market datasets from Ethereum-based platforms. Results will contribute methodological tools for marketers operating in Web3 ecosystems while advancing academic understanding of emergent collective behavior in algorithmically mediated markets.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to undertake and manage the process of developing consumer audiences and moving products from producers to consumers. Includes instruction in buyer behavior and dynamics, principle of marketing research, demand analysis, cost-volume and profit relationships, pricing theory, marketing campaign and strategic planning, market segments, advertising methods, sales operations and management, consumer relations, retailing, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the synergistic effects of multi-modal holistic interventions on chronic stress resilience, integrating physiological, behavioral, and environmental data. Chronic stress is a complex health challenge influenced by interconnected factors that conventional reductionist approaches often fail to address comprehensively. While holistic practices such as mindfulness, personalized nutrition, and biofeedback show promise, their combined efficacy and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the lack of tools capable of analyzing dynamic, multi-scale interactions. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate how these interventions interact with individual biopsychosocial profiles. Using a hybrid approach, we will combine agent-based modeling to simulate systemic stress responses with machine learning analysis of multi-omics data (e.g., microbiome, metabolome), wearable-derived physiological metrics (heart rate variability, sleep patterns), and self-reported lifestyle factors. Dynamical systems models will map temporal interactions between interventions, such as the compounding effects of mindfulness practice and adaptogenic herb supplementation on hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis regulation. The computational pipeline will be validated against longitudinal data from a pilot cohort undergoing personalized holistic stress management protocols. By quantifying non-linear relationships and emergent outcomes, this work aims to identify optimal intervention sequences and predict individual-specific responses. The project will generate open-source tools for simulating holistic health strategies, advancing evidence-based integration of complementary therapies. Outcomes will provide a foundation for precision holistic medicine, enabling clinicians to tailor multi-modal wellness plans while reducing trial-and-error inefficiencies. This research addresses a critical gap in health sciences by uniting systems biology, computational modeling, and integrative health paradigms, ultimately fostering scalable strategies to enhance resilience in diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the holistic interconnectedness of physical, psychological, social, spiritual, and environmental well-being and that integrates aspects of alternative, complementary, and conventional medicine to alleviate illness and promote, maintain, and optimize wellness. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, alternative diagnostic and healing methods, aromatherapy, biofeedback, energy medicine, environmental psychology, ethics, health coaching, herbal medicine, mind-body medicine, mindfulness, nutrition, somatic bodywork, and stress management.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the spatial dynamics of human decision-making during natural disaster evacuations, integrating behavioral geography with advanced geospatial analytics to address gaps in evacuation modeling. Current models often oversimplify human behavior, leading to inefficient emergency plans. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this study will process and analyze large-scale, high-resolution mobility datasets—including GPS traces, social media geotags, and transportation network data—from historical disaster events to identify patterns in evacuation timing, route selection, and crowding. Computational methods will include spatial network analysis to model mobility constraints, machine learning to classify behavioral clusters, and agent-based simulations to test how real-world behavioral heterogeneity influences evacuation outcomes under varying infrastructural and environmental conditions. The HPC environment is critical for handling the scale and complexity of these datasets, enabling parallel processing of terabytes of geospatial data and iterative simulation runs across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a novel, open-source framework for behavior-sensitive evacuation modeling, which will improve predictions of bottleneck formation and resource demand surges. Results will be synthesized into interactive cartographic tools for local governments, offering dynamic visualizations of risk hotspots and alternative evacuation scenarios. This work bridges computational social science and disaster resilience planning, advancing geographic information science by embedding empirically grounded human behavior into spatial decision-support systems. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—spanning behavioral geography, urban informatics, and HPC-driven geospatial analytics—will provide a replicable methodology for studying human-environment interactions in high-stakes scenarios, with direct applications to public safety policy and community-led disaster preparedness initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of map-making and the application of mathematical, computer, and other techniques to the analysis of large amounts of geographic data and the science of mapping geographic information. Includes instruction in cartographic theory and map projections, computer-assisted cartography, geographic information systems, map design and layout, photogrammetry, air photo interpretation, remote sensing, spatial analysis, geodesy, cartographic editing, and applications to specific industrial, commercial, research, and governmental mapping problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of understudied Southeast Asian languages, focusing on the Thai, Malayo-Polynesian, and Tibeto-Burman language families. While advancements in natural language processing (NLP) have revolutionized linguistic research, many Southeast Asian languages remain underrepresented in digital corpora and computational models due to their typological complexity, dialectal diversity, and limited standardized resources. This research aims to develop scalable, language-specific tools to analyze syntactic structures, phonological patterns, and dialectal variations across these languages, with an emphasis on low-resource and endangered varieties. The computational workload involves training machine learning models on newly assembled multilingual datasets, including annotated texts, audio recordings, and historical documents, to perform tasks such as automated morphological segmentation, dialect classification, and cross-linguistic semantic mapping. HPC resources are essential to process large volumes of unstructured data, optimize transformer-based models for agglutinative and tonal languages, and run simulations of language evolution under varying sociolinguistic scenarios. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access computational lexicons, enhanced phylogenetic models of language relationships within the region, and geospatial visualizations of dialect continua. These resources will support both theoretical advancements in understanding language contact phenomena and practical applications in language preservation, particularly for communities experiencing rapid linguistic shift. By integrating computational methods with traditional philological approaches, this project bridges a methodological divide in the humanities, offering a replicable framework for the study of non-dominant languages in a high-performance computing environment.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the modern languages spoken in mainland Southeast Asia and the Indonesian and Philippines Archipelagoes, including, but not limited to, members of the Thai, Tibeto-Burman, and Malayo-Polynesian language families.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of dynamic visual communication design in digital environments, where traditional computational tools struggle to efficiently process high-resolution multimedia content, simulate real-time user interactions, and generate adaptive design outputs at scale. The research focuses on developing a computational framework to automate and optimize the creation of personalized visual media, leveraging machine learning (ML) and large-scale data analysis. Key challenges include processing terabytes of image, video, and user-behavior datasets; training generative models for context-aware design variations; and simulating immersive, interactive environments for user testing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to overcome latency and scalability limitations in rendering 3D visualizations, running parallelized ML workflows, and conducting iterative A/B testing across diverse user scenarios. The proposed methodology integrates GPU-accelerated neural networks for style transfer and layout generation, distributed computing for real-time collaboration in multi-user design platforms, and agent-based modeling to predict audience engagement metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scalable visual content generation, validated through case studies in augmented reality (AR) advertising and adaptive web interfaces. This work aims to advance design practices by enabling data-driven, responsive visual communication strategies while reducing production timelines. The resource request supports benchmarking against industry standards, ensuring reproducibility of complex simulations, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between visual designers and computational researchers. By bridging gaps in processing power and algorithmic efficiency, this project will empower creators to address emerging demands for hyper-personalized, interactive media in consumer and enterprise contexts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that focuses on the general principles and techniques for effectively communicating ideas and information, and packaging products, in digital and other formats to business and consumer audiences, and that may prepare individuals in any of the applied art media.

abstract: The rapid urbanization of coastal regions has intensified the need for advanced environmental control systems capable of mitigating flood risks while maintaining water quality. Current hydrodynamic models lack the resolution to simulate complex interactions between stormwater infrastructure, tidal fluctuations, and pollutant transport in high-density urban areas, limiting the efficacy of adaptive management strategies. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale simulation framework to optimize hybrid green-gray infrastructure systems in coastal cities. The computational approach integrates GPU-accelerated shallow water equations solvers with agent-based models of sediment and contaminant transport, resolving spatial scales from individual bioswales (<1m) to watershed-level hydrology (>10km). Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to enable real-time uncertainty quantification under stochastic rainfall and sea-level rise scenarios. By leveraging parallelized parameter optimization, the framework will identify infrastructure configurations that minimize flood duration, nutrient runoff, and capital costs across 50-year climate projections. The required simulations involve ~10^8 grid cells and 10^5 agent interactions per timestep, necessitating access to petascale computing resources for ensemble runs. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive urban water management and generalized design guidelines for climate-resilient cities. This work will directly inform municipal policy in three pilot regions, potentially reducing combined sewer overflows by 15-25% in vulnerable communities. The computational methodologies developed will establish new benchmarks for integrating ecological and engineered systems in environmental control simulations, with applications extending to coastal restoration and distributed water treatment networks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental control technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational workflows in civil drafting and computer-aided design (CAD/CADD) for infrastructure planning and geological modeling. A critical challenge in civil engineering CAD workflows is the limited capacity of standard computing systems to efficiently process large-scale geospatial datasets, simulate complex structural or hydrological systems, and optimize designs under dynamic environmental constraints. Current tools often rely on simplified models to reduce computational load, sacrificing accuracy and failing to account for multi-variable interactions such as soil-structure dynamics, fluid flow in drainage systems, or seismic stress distribution. This research proposes a computational framework integrating CAD software with HPC-enabled finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-based design optimization. The project will develop parallelized algorithms to process high-resolution LiDAR surveys, automate 3D mesh generation for geological formations, and simulate infrastructure performance under stochastic loading scenarios. Key workflows include GPU-accelerated rendering of large-scale civil layouts, distributed computing for real-time parametric design adjustments, and AI-driven topology optimization for cost-effective material usage. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for HPC-augmented CAD workflows that reduce simulation times by 40–60% while maintaining millimeter-scale precision in critical structural components. The research will also generate benchmark datasets for pipe network resilience under flood conditions and slope stability analysis in heterogeneous soils. By enabling higher-fidelity simulations within practical timeframes, this work aims to improve decision-making in sustainable infrastructure design, reduce over-engineering in civil projects, and enhance CAD/CADD pedagogy through case studies demonstrating HPC integration. The requested resources will directly support graduate student training in computational civil engineering techniques, bridging gaps between traditional drafting practices and emerging HPC applications in the engineering technology sector.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: The safe and efficient management of hazardous materials requires advanced predictive tools to address complex interactions between contaminants, environmental systems, and engineered remediation strategies. Current risk assessment models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic multi-phase transport, heterogeneous subsurface conditions, and site-specific biogeochemical processes, leading to uncertainties in waste disposal protocols. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate contaminant fate and transport in hazardous waste scenarios, with a focus on optimizing containment and treatment systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to integrate multi-scale numerical models coupling fluid dynamics, reactive transport, and microbial degradation processes. The computational approach will employ finite element and lattice Boltzmann methods to resolve pore-scale interactions in engineered barriers, while machine learning techniques will parameterize regional-scale models using historical contamination datasets. Key objectives include validating simulations against experimental column studies of heavy metal leaching and organic compound biodegradation, then scaling these results to predict long-term performance of landfill liners and in situ bioremediation systems. The HPC environment is critical for managing large parameter spaces, iterative optimization of remediation designs, and probabilistic risk analyses under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible modeling toolkit for predicting contaminant breakthrough times, quantifying uncertainty in waste containment systems, and identifying cost-effective strategies for legacy site cleanup. By enabling higher-resolution simulations of coupled physical, chemical, and biological processes, this work aims to reduce environmental liabilities and advance evidence-based policies for hazardous waste management. The requested computing resources will directly support 3D transient simulations requiring parallelized solvers, GPU-accelerated machine learning workflows, and petascale data storage for sensitivity analyses across thousands of scenario permutations.
cip_title: Hazardous Materials Management and Waste Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in identifying and disposing of hazardous materials. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, biohazard identification, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, hazardous waste disposal procedures and systems, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Infertility and reproductive endocrine disorders, such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometriosis, affect millions globally, yet their multifactorial etiologies—spanning genetic, hormonal, metabolic, and environmental interactions—remain poorly characterized. Current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches are often empiric, with suboptimal success rates, due to limited tools for modeling the complexity of these systems. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative computational models that decode the dynamic interplay of biological factors driving reproductive endocrine dysfunction and infertility. The research will focus on multi-omics data integration (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets from clinical cohorts) to identify predictive biomarkers and mechanistic pathways. Machine learning frameworks, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be employed to model non-linear interactions and temporal patterns in high-dimensional datasets. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular and molecular interactions within ovarian and endometrial microenvironments to test hypotheses about folliculogenesis, implantation failure, and hormonal dysregulation. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further analyze uterine hemodynamic changes associated with infertility. These approaches demand HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-scale parameter optimization, and handling datasets exceeding 100 TB. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, stratification of patient subgroups for personalized interventions, and predictive models to optimize assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes. By elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment resistance and disease heterogeneity, this work aims to advance precision medicine in reproductive endocrinology. The requested resources will enable rapid iteration of models, validation against clinical datasets, and scalable analysis of emerging multi-institutional data, directly addressing a critical need for computational power in this data-rich but hypothesis-sparse field.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage complex problems relating to reproductive endocrinology and infertility.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the impacts of land-use policy and climate change on biodiversity in coupled human-natural systems. The research addresses a critical gap in environmental management: current policy frameworks often fail to account for dynamic feedbacks between ecological processes, socioeconomic decision-making, and shifting climate conditions. We propose an integrative computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM), spatially explicit ecosystem simulations, and machine learning-driven climate projection analysis. The ABM component will simulate landowner decision-making under varying policy scenarios, incorporating economic incentives, regulatory constraints, and climate risk perceptions. These outputs will feed into ecological models that predict habitat connectivity, species migration patterns, and ecosystem service provision at 1km resolution across multi-decadal timescales. Computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale remote sensing datasets, calibrating models with heterogeneous ecological survey data, and running Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in policy outcomes. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive spatial computations, parallelizing parameter optimization across thousands of cores, and achieving the temporal resolution required for actionable policy insights. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating trade-offs between conservation targets, economic development goals, and climate adaptation strategies. Results will directly inform state-level natural resource agencies in redesigning habitat conservation plans under projected 2050 climate scenarios. By quantifying how policy interventions scale across ecological and institutional boundaries, this work advances computational methods for sustainability science while addressing pressing needs in adaptive resource governance.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Management and Policy, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, manage, and evaluate programs to protect and regulate natural habitats and renewable natural resources. Includes instruction in the principles of wildlife and conservation biology, environmental science, animal population surveying, natural resource economics, management techniques for various habitats, applicable law and policy, administrative and communications skills, and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the co-evolution of scientific methodologies and industrial technologies in 19th-century Europe through computational analysis of historical texts, patent records, and socio-economic datasets. The research problem centers on identifying how epistemic shifts in scientific practice—such as the rise of experimental standardization—interacted with technological innovation cycles, and how these dynamics were shaped by broader cultural and economic forces. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to systematically analyze the scale and complexity of these interactions across dispersed archives, necessitating a computational approach. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will apply natural language processing (NLP) to a curated corpus of 250,000 pages of scientific journals, technical manuals, and industrial correspondence from 1800–1900, supplemented by structured data from patent registries and trade ledgers. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect semantic shifts in terminology related to measurement, precision, and material processes, while graph network analyses will map temporal and geographic patterns of knowledge exchange between academic institutions and industries. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling to simulate how resource allocation in emerging engineering disciplines (e.g., thermodynamics, metallurgy) influenced regional technological adoption rates. Computational demands include large-scale parallelized text embedding, dynamic network visualization of citation clusters, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing counterfactual developmental scenarios. Expected outcomes include: (1) a quantitative framework for evaluating the material constraints on scientific theory formation, (2) identification of previously overlooked institutional actors in cross-disciplinary innovation, and (3) open-access tools for computational historiography. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with philosophical models of epistemic change, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying technoscientific evolution while critically examining assumptions about linear progress in standard narratives of the Industrial Revolution.
detailed_field: History/ philosophy of science, technology, and society
cip_title: History and Philosophy of Science and Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution of scientific theories, science applications and technologies, and the scientific, medical, and technological disciplines, as well as the philosophy of science and its historical socio-economic context. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of philosophical inquiry; historiography of science; history of science, medicine, and technology; and research methods in the history of the scientific and engineering disciplines, including mathematics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate quantum many-body dynamics in strongly correlated fermionic systems using advanced computational methods. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding non-equilibrium behavior and thermalization processes in systems with high entanglement, which are inaccessible to analytical solutions or classical simulation techniques. The central challenge lies in simulating large-scale quantum systems with sufficient accuracy to resolve emergent phenomena, such as many-body localization and quantum phase transitions, which govern the interplay between disorder, interactions, and quantum coherence. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining tensor network algorithms—specifically matrix product states (MPS) and projected entangled pair states (PEPS)—with stochastic variational Monte Carlo methods. These techniques will be optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures to handle the exponential scaling of Hilbert space dimensions, enabling simulations of 2D lattices with up to 100 sites and long-time evolution under realistic interaction parameters. The computational workload will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for tensor contractions and parallel CPU clusters for stochastic sampling, with adaptive memory management to reduce overhead. Expected outcomes include the identification of universal signatures of thermalization in disordered fermionic systems, quantitative predictions of critical exponents near quantum phase transitions, and validation of proposed effective field theories. These results will provide foundational insights into the robustness of quantum coherence in engineered systems, with implications for quantum information science and the design of next-generation quantum simulators. The project’s success hinges on access to HPC resources capable of sustaining petascale operations, including multi-node GPU allocations and high-memory nodes for storing large tensors. By bridging theoretical predictions with numerical benchmarks, this work will advance the understanding of quantum matter and establish scalable computational protocols for future studies of complex quantum systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the theories that explain the fundamental structure of our world and the universe and which draws from physics and astronomy. Includes instruction in astronomy, calculus, cosmology, differential equations, electricity, magnetism, data analysis, physics, quantum mechanics, space science, spectroscopy, and thermal physics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized learning pathways for pre-service teachers in STEM disciplines, addressing the challenge of efficiently preparing educators to adapt pedagogy to diverse classroom needs. Current teacher training programs often rely on static curricula and limited case studies, which inadequately prepare educators for the dynamic, variable demands of real-world classrooms. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate classroom environments, analyze historical teaching performance data, and generate adaptive training modules. The research problem centers on identifying scalable methods to enhance pedagogical flexibility while maintaining alignment with evidence-based teaching standards. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling to simulate student-teacher interactions across diverse demographic and cognitive profiles, coupled with natural language processing (NLP) to evaluate trainee responses to simulated classroom scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will iteratively refine module recommendations based on performance metrics from these simulations. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing to parallelize thousands of classroom interaction scenarios and train deep learning models on multimodal data (text, audio, and behavioral logs). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating context-aware teaching simulations and quantitative evidence linking specific training patterns to competency development. By enabling large-scale analysis of pedagogical strategies across synthetic classroom populations, this work aims to transform how teacher education programs individualize professional development. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of real-time scenario generation and multivariate analysis across millions of simulated interactions, which would be infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. Results will directly inform the design of next-generation teacher preparation programs, with particular relevance to underserved regions where access to diverse classroom training opportunities is limited.
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Subject Areas, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education, specific academic and vocational programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in resource allocation for heterogeneous computing systems, which integrate diverse hardware components such as CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs to optimize performance for specialized workloads. Modern applications in artificial intelligence, real-time data processing, and scientific simulations increasingly rely on these systems, yet dynamically balancing computational tasks across hybrid architectures remains a significant challenge. Current static allocation strategies often lead to underutilization, energy waste, and latency bottlenecks, particularly as workloads scale in complexity. To tackle this, we propose developing adaptive resource management algorithms that leverage machine learning and parallel computing frameworks to predict and distribute tasks in real time. The computational approach involves simulating heterogeneous environments using high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to model hardware interactions under varying workloads. These simulations will train neural networks to recognize patterns in resource demand, enabling proactive allocation adjustments. Additionally, we will implement and benchmark a prototype scheduler within an open-source distributed computing platform, integrating feedback mechanisms to refine decision-making processes. The project requires HPC resources to handle large-scale simulations, which involve millions of parallel tasks and multi-node GPU/FPGA configurations. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for dynamic resource optimization, validated through metrics such as throughput improvement, energy efficiency gains, and latency reduction. This work will provide actionable insights for system administrators and developers managing hybrid infrastructures, while contributing open-source tools to the broader research community. By enhancing the adaptability of heterogeneous systems, the project aims to support emerging applications in autonomous systems, edge computing, and high-performance data analytics, aligning with the program’s focus on practical, technology-driven solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: Healthcare facilities face increasing pressure to optimize operational efficiency while maintaining high-quality patient care, particularly amid fluctuating demand, resource constraints, and evolving regulatory requirements. Traditional management approaches often rely on static models that fail to account for dynamic variables, such as patient inflow variability, staff scheduling complexities, and real-time resource allocation trade-offs. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a scalable, data-driven simulation framework to model hospital operations and evaluate optimization strategies under diverse scenarios. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute agent-based simulations that integrate multi-source data, including electronic health records (EHR), staffing patterns, equipment utilization rates, and facility layouts. Computational models will simulate patient flow, staff interactions, and resource allocation processes to identify bottlenecks, predict downstream impacts of operational decisions, and test interventions such as dynamic bed management, predictive staffing adjustments, and energy-efficient facility operations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical and synthetic datasets to refine predictive accuracy and generate adaptive decision-support tools for administrators. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to run thousands of parallel simulations with high-dimensional parameter spaces, requiring significant memory and processing power. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into cost-quality trade-offs, validated strategies for reducing patient wait times, and a publicly accessible toolkit for scenario planning in healthcare management. By enabling granular, real-time modeling of complex systems, this work aims to advance evidence-based administration practices, supporting facilities in achieving operational resilience, financial sustainability, and improved patient outcomes. The proposed HPC resources are critical to achieving the scale, speed, and precision required for these computationally intensive analyses.
cip_title: Hospital and Health Care Facilities Administration/ Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and other health care facilities. Includes instruction in facilities planning, building and operations management, business management, financial management and insurance, fund-raising and marketing, public relations, human resources management and labor relations, health care facilities operations, principles of health care delivery, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in understanding the interplay between instrumental acoustics, performer biomechanics, and real-time artistic decision-making in woodwind performance. While traditional analyses of woodwind playing often isolate variables such as airflow dynamics, finger kinematics, or acoustic resonance, the complex, nonlinear interactions between these factors during live performance remain poorly quantified. This gap limits the development of evidence-based pedagogical tools and inhibits innovations in instrument design tailored to diverse physiological and artistic needs. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating fluid-structure interaction simulations, biomechanical modeling, and machine learning-driven analysis of performance data. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate time-dependent airflow through instrument bores and reed systems under dynamically varying embouchure parameters, while finite element analysis (FEA) will capture structural vibrations in instrument bodies and player-instrument contact mechanics. Concurrently, motion capture datasets from professional performers will inform agent-based models of ergonomic finger movement optimization. These multiscale models will be coupled via HPC-enabled parallelization to analyze feedback loops between physiological inputs and acoustic outputs at sub-millisecond resolution. Machine learning classifiers will then identify patterns in simulated and empirical performance data to correlate technical execution with perceptual markers of artistic quality. The resulting computational platform will enable unprecedented investigations into how microvariations in breath control, articulation, and fingering technique propagate through the performer-instrument system to shape timbral expression. Outcomes will include open-access datasets mapping biomechanical strategies to acoustic outcomes, predictive models for personalized pedagogical feedback, and a foundation for computationally guided instrument design innovations. By integrating HPC-driven simulations with performance research, this work aims to advance both the scientific understanding of woodwind artistry and the development of computational tools for nurturing technical excellence in music education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a woodwind instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the acoustic and biomechanical interactions inherent in brass instrument performance through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in understanding how player technique shapes sound production. Brass performance involves nonlinear systems—such as lip vibration, airflow dynamics, and instrument resonance—that are challenging to model in real time due to their complexity and interdependence. Traditional experimental methods provide limited resolution for analyzing these systems, while existing computational approaches often oversimplify physical interactions or lack the scalability to explore diverse performance scenarios. This project proposes a hybrid methodology combining finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating mechanical wave propagation in brass instruments, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airflow and pressure variations in the oral cavity and instrument bore, and machine learning (ML) techniques to correlate simulated data with empirical performance recordings. HPC resources are critical for executing large-scale parallel simulations that capture high-resolution temporal and spatial data across variables such as embouchure adjustments, valve/piston kinematics, and dynamic tuning. Expected outcomes include the development of a modular, open-source framework for simulating brass performance mechanics, validated against motion-capture and acoustic datasets from professional performers. This work will advance pedagogical tools by quantifying relationships between technique and timbre, enabling personalized feedback systems for musicians. Additionally, the models will inform the design of adaptive digital accompanists capable of real-time harmonic and dynamic responsiveness, broadening access to ensemble practice environments. By bridging computational acoustics and performing arts pedagogy, this project aims to establish a foundational resource for interdisciplinary research in instrumental music education and performance innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a brass instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: The formation and evolution of galactic structures in the early universe remain poorly understood due to the complex interplay between baryonic matter, dark matter, and feedback processes from star formation and active galactic nuclei (AGN). Current simulations often lack the resolution and physical fidelity required to model these multi-scale interactions accurately, particularly in diverse galactic environments. This project proposes a suite of high-resolution cosmological hydrodynamical simulations to investigate the role of AGN feedback in regulating star formation and shaping galaxy morphologies during critical epochs (z ≈ 1–5). Leveraging the adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) capabilities of the Enzo code, we will simulate galactic volumes at sub-100 pc resolution, explicitly modeling radiative transfer, molecular cloud formation, and black hole accretion dynamics. The computational approach integrates novel subgrid prescriptions for stellar feedback efficiency calibrated against recent JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies. By systematically varying initial conditions and feedback parameters across 50 simulation runs, we aim to identify dominant mechanisms driving observed scaling relations between black hole mass, stellar velocity dispersion, and star formation quenching. The simulations will utilize 750,000 CPU-hours on a high-performance computing cluster to manage the memory-intensive AMR hierarchies and parallel radiative transfer calculations. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative constraints on AGN feedback energetics required to reproduce observed galaxy mass functions, (2) predictive maps of interstellar medium conditions in progenitors of modern elliptical galaxies, and (3) open-source data products for comparing simulated spectral energy distributions with upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Telescope surveys. This work will advance theoretical frameworks for galaxy evolution while providing essential benchmarks for interpreting multi-wavelength observations of cosmic dawn systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in astronomy and astrophysics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing individualized reading intervention strategies for K–12 students with dyslexia and related literacy difficulties. While evidence-based instructional frameworks exist, the dynamic interplay of cognitive, linguistic, and socioemotional factors in reading acquisition remains poorly quantified, limiting the personalization of interventions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational model that simulates reading development trajectories under varying instructional conditions. The model will integrate behavioral datasets—including longitudinal literacy assessments, eye-tracking metrics, and student demographic profiles—with neurocognitive principles derived from existing literature on phonological processing, orthographic mapping, and working memory. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal data from over 10,000 anonymized student records, train machine learning classifiers to identify early risk markers, and run agent-based simulations of classroom-scale intervention scenarios. Key computational tasks include natural language processing of student-written responses, Bayesian network modeling of skill mastery sequences, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses to evaluate instructional variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for mapping learner profiles to optimal intervention types and dosages, (2) an open-access toolkit for generating synthetic student performance data to support teacher training, and (3) empirical guidelines for sequencing multisensory instructional components in digital learning platforms. By leveraging large-scale parallel processing to analyze heterogeneous educational data, this work will provide novel insights into the nonlinear dynamics of reading development while advancing computational applications in teacher preparation. Results will directly inform the design of adaptive professional development modules for reading specialists, ultimately aiming to reduce disparities in literacy outcomes for neurodiverse learners.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose reading difficulties and to teach reading programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Urban forests are critical for mitigating climate impacts and enhancing urban livability, yet their sustainability is threatened by complex interactions between environmental stressors, pest dynamics, and anthropogenic factors. Current models for urban tree mortality and health often lack the resolution to account for spatially heterogeneous microclimates, species-specific stress responses, and real-time biotic threats, limiting predictive accuracy and management efficacy. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate urban forest dynamics under diverse scenarios of climate change, pest infestation, and urbanization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale datasets—including remote sensing imagery, IoT sensor networks, pest population genomics, and socio-environmental databases—into a coupled agent-based and machine learning model. The agent-based component will simulate individual tree responses to localized stressors (e.g., heat islands, soil compaction, air pollution), while machine learning modules will predict emergent patterns of canopy loss, species vulnerability, and pest spread across urban gradients. Computational demands include large-scale parameter optimization, real-time data assimilation, and ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into species selection, targeted intervention zones, and climate-resilient planting strategies. By scaling from individual trees to city-wide systems, this work will provide municipalities with adaptive management tools to optimize urban forest ecosystem services, such as carbon sequestration and heat mitigation. The project directly aligns with urban forestry policies emphasizing data-driven stewardship and underscores the necessity of HPC for resolving the spatiotemporal complexity inherent in urban ecological systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of forestry and related sciences to the development, care, and maintenance of individual trees and forested areas within or close to areas of dense human habitation. Includes instruction in urban environments; effects of pollution on tree species; environmental design and landscaping; urban pest infestation; urban forest management; and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Swedish dialectology and historical linguistics. The research problem centers on analyzing linguistic variation and evolution across Swedish dialects and pre-modern texts, which remain understudied due to the scale and complexity of the data. Traditional manual methods struggle to process the vast corpus of digitized texts, audio recordings, and metadata now available, limiting insights into patterns of language change, dialect boundaries, and sociolinguistic influences. To address this, we propose developing a computational pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques tailored to Swedish linguistic features. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on historical and contemporary Swedish texts to automate syntactic and semantic analysis, applying phonetic alignment algorithms to dialect recordings, and employing spatial-temporal modeling to map language change across regions and centuries. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling large datasets (20+ TB of text and audio), parallelizing computationally intensive tasks like neural network training and phylogenetic clustering, and storing intermediate outputs. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of previously unrecognized dialectal transition zones, (2) quantitative models linking linguistic shifts to historical migration patterns, and (3) open-access tools for automated analysis of Swedish historical texts. These results will directly benefit philological research, inform preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and enable new interdisciplinary connections—such as applying linguistic divergence metrics to improve dating of undocumented texts. By integrating computational rigor with domain-specific expertise, this project aims to establish a framework for data-driven humanities research while addressing core questions in Swedish language studies that were previously intractable at scale.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Swedish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and linguistic identities in Ukraine’s border regions, with a focus on the interplay between historical narratives, media representation, and community-driven discourses. The research addresses a critical gap in Ukraine Studies: the lack of large-scale, longitudinal analyses of cultural self-determination in multiethnic border zones, particularly in contexts of geopolitical conflict and shifting territorial affiliations. By integrating digitized archival materials, regional press corpora (1945–present), and contemporary social media data, the project aims to map patterns of cultural hybridity, language use, and collective memory across time and space. Computational methods will include multilingual natural language processing (NLP) tailored to Ukrainian, Crimean Tatar, and minority languages; network analysis to trace thematic linkages in media narratives; and geospatial modeling to visualize cultural diffusion. These methods require HPC capabilities due to the scale of unstructured text data (estimated at 15 TB), the complexity of training transformer models on low-resource languages, and the iterative processing needed for temporal network reconstructions. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible digital atlas of cultural identity markers in Ukraine’s borderlands, (2) algorithms for detecting linguistic interference and code-switching in multiethnic media, and (3) quantitative frameworks to assess the impact of state-level cultural policies on regional identity formation. The project will advance methodological innovation in area studies by demonstrating how computational approaches can disentangle overlapping cultural narratives while respecting contextual specificities. Results will inform cultural preservation initiatives and provide empirical grounding for debates on minority rights in post-conflict societies. By prioritizing computational reproducibility, the workflows developed will serve as a template for interdisciplinary studies of identity in other contested regions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: The development of stable and efficacious pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations is a resource-intensive process, often hindered by the empirical nature of traditional trial-and-error experimentation. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling approaches for predicting the physicochemical behavior of complex drug delivery systems and cosmetic emulsions. The research will focus on overcoming challenges in preformulation evaluation, stability testing, and product reformulation by integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) models, and finite element analysis (FEA) of multi-phase systems. Key objectives include simulating API-excipient interactions under varied thermodynamic conditions, optimizing emulsion droplet size distributions through computational fluid dynamics, and predicting degradation pathways for small molecules in topical formulations. The computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated MD packages (e.g., GROMACS) for nanoscale system characterization and distributed ML frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow) to analyze structure-stability correlations across large formulation datasets. By enabling rapid in silico screening of prototype formulations, this approach aims to reduce experimental iterations in physical stability testing by an estimated 40-60%, while providing mechanistic insights into failure modes observed during accelerated aging studies. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-throughput simulations required to model complex semi-solid matrices and for training neural networks on historical formulation data spanning multiple product categories. Outcomes will directly inform industrial formulation strategies, enhance predictive capabilities in pharmaceutical development, and establish computational workflows that align with quality-by-design (QbD) principles for regulatory submissions. This work bridges critical gaps between computational pharmaceutics and real-world formulation challenges, offering transformative potential for both industrial pharmacy operations and cosmetic science innovation.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: Geological systems are characterized by complex, nonlinear interactions between subsurface materials, hydrological processes, and mechanical stresses, presenting significant challenges for predictive modeling in geotechnical and geoenvironmental applications. This project seeks to advance the simulation of multiphysics phenomena—such as fracture propagation in rock masses, sediment transport under dynamic fluid flows, and stress redistribution during tectonic events—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome computational limitations inherent in conventional methods. Current approaches often rely on simplified geometries or decoupled analyses, which inadequately capture the interdependencies driving real-world geological behavior. To address this, we propose a parallelized computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) for solid mechanics, lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) for fluid dynamics, and discrete fracture network (DFN) simulations to represent heterogeneous geological media. The HPC resources will enable high-resolution 3D simulations of coupled processes at scales relevant to field applications, such as landslide initiation, reservoir stability, and contaminant transport in fractured aquifers. Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement to focus computational effort on critical regions (e.g., evolving fracture tips) and machine learning-driven parameter optimization using field data from LiDAR, seismic surveys, and borehole logs. The outcomes will yield validated models for predicting infrastructure resilience to geological hazards and optimizing subsurface resource extraction strategies. By quantifying uncertainties in spatially variable geological properties, this work will directly inform risk assessment frameworks and sustainable engineering design practices. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required computational throughput for ensemble simulations and to scale validated models from laboratory to regional dimensions, providing actionable insights for stakeholders in civil engineering, environmental management, and geohazard mitigation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and geological principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, including the geological evaluation of construction sites, the analysis of geological forces acting on structures and systems, the analysis of potential natural resource recovery sites, and applied research on geological phenomena.

abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic pressures are increasingly altering the resilience of natural ecosystems, yet predicting the cascading impacts on biodiversity and critical ecosystem services remains a complex challenge. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a spatially explicit, multi-scale computational model to simulate interactions between climate variability, land-use change, and species distribution shifts in temperate forest ecosystems. The research will integrate high-resolution remote sensing data (LiDAR, hyperspectral imagery), long-term ecological field datasets, and climate projections to parameterize dynamic vegetation models under alternative management scenarios. A key innovation is the coupling of species-specific habitat suitability indices with hydrologic connectivity algorithms to predict population fragmentation risks for threatened wildlife, including amphibians and migratory birds. Given the scale and resolution of input datasets (1TB+), the need for iterative ensemble runs to quantify uncertainty, and the computational demands of agent-based dispersal simulations, high-performance computing resources are essential. The project will employ parallelized workflows using Python-based ecological libraries and MPI-enabled Fortran code to optimize runtime across 10,000+ core-hour allocations. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identification of climate refugia and corridors for priority species, (2) quantification of tipping points in ecosystem service provision under combined stressors, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive conservation planning. Results will directly inform state and federal land management strategies while advancing methodological frameworks for scaling ecological forecasts. By resolving fine-grained ecological processes within regional climate systems, this work aims to transform static conservation paradigms into dynamic, data-driven approaches for preserving biodiversity in rapidly changing environments.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the studies and activities relating to the natural environment and its conservation, use, and improvement. Includes instruction in subjects such as climate, air, soil, water, land, fish and wildlife, and plant resources; in the basic principles of environmental science and natural resources management; and the recreational and economic uses of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of natural hazards due to climate change necessitates advanced computational tools to evaluate the resilience of civil infrastructure. Current structural engineering practices often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture coupled multihazard interactions, such as simultaneous seismic and hydrodynamic loading on coastal bridges or wind and flood impacts on high-rise buildings. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework integrating multiscale finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate complex structural responses under multifactorial hazard scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform large-scale parallel simulations to resolve critical phenomena, including nonlinear material behavior, fluid-structure interaction, and progressive collapse mechanisms. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to optimize retrofitting strategies and identify vulnerability thresholds in existing structures. The computational demands of these simulations—requiring millions of core-hours for parametric studies across diverse environmental conditions—exceed the capacity of local computing clusters. The proposed HPC allocation will enable the generation of predictive models validated against experimental data from shake-table tests and field monitoring systems. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of hazard-resilient design guidelines, probabilistic risk assessment tools for infrastructure stakeholders, and validated retrofit solutions for aging bridges and offshore platforms. This research will directly inform updates to national building codes and enhance the climate adaptation strategies critical for urban resilience in coastal and seismically active regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and systems used in building load-bearing structures for various purposes and in different environments, including buildings, roads, rail lines, bridges, dams, conduits, offshore platforms and work stations, and other structural shells; and the analysis of structural problems such as, failure, fabrication, safety, and natural hazards.

abstract: Sterile processing technology (SPT) is a critical yet understudied component of healthcare infrastructure, directly impacting surgical safety and infection prevention. Current sterilization protocols for complex surgical instruments—particularly those with narrow lumens, hinges, or textured surfaces—rely on empirically derived parameters that may inadequately address microbial persistence or material degradation. This project seeks to computationally model and optimize sterilization workflows using high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve two interconnected challenges: (1) predicting fluid dynamics and microbicidal agent diffusion within intricate instrument geometries, and (2) evaluating long-term material fatigue caused by repeated sterilization cycles. A multi-scale computational framework will integrate 3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of vaporized hydrogen peroxide and steam penetration with finite element analysis (FEA) of thermal and chemical stress on instrument substrates. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs and experimental validation data to identify parameter combinations that maximize microbial inactivation while minimizing equipment wear. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-resolution instrument scans, simulating multiphase flows in porous geometries, and iterating through combinatorial sterilization variables (e.g., temperature, cycle duration, agent concentration). Expected outcomes include predictive models for sterilization efficacy across instrument classes, evidence-based thresholds for equipment retirement, and a decision-support tool for dynamically adjusting protocols based on instrument design trends. This work bridges gaps between clinical microbiology, materials science, and operational logistics, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to predictive sterile processing. By addressing computational bottlenecks in modeling real-world instrument heterogeneity, the project aims to reduce healthcare-associated infections, extend surgical instrument lifespans, and establish scalable computational methodologies for emerging sterilization technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean, sterilize, and assemble surgical instruments, equipment, and supplies for use in operating rooms and other medical and surgical facilities. Includes instruction in sterilization; infection control; decontamination; and surgical instrumentation processing, distribution, and record-keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Polish philology and dialectology, addressing gaps in large-scale analysis of linguistic variation and historical language change. The core research problem centers on the limited application of computational methods to study regional Polish dialects and their evolution, particularly in relation to sociocultural influences and literary production. While existing scholarship has cataloged dialectal features manually, the scale and complexity of audio recordings, historical texts, and modern speech corpora require advanced processing to uncover patterns across time and geography. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze digitized texts spanning the 16th to 21st centuries, including regional literature, archival manuscripts, and transcribed oral histories. Parallelized acoustic analysis workflows will process dialect recordings to map phonetic shifts, while transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned for Polish) will quantify stylistic and lexical changes in literary works against sociopolitical contexts. Computational demands include training multilingual models for cross-dialect comparison, running phylogenetic algorithms to model language divergence, and storing/querying multi-terabyte linguistic datasets. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Polish dialect boundaries, an annotated corpus of diachronic linguistic features linked to literary movements, and open-access tools for automated dialect classification. These resources will directly support endangered language preservation efforts and inform curriculum development for advanced Polish studies. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological frameworks, this work aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing Slavic languages at scale while providing infrastructure for future interdisciplinary collaborations in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize spinal adjustment protocols in chiropractic care by integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling with clinical outcome data. Despite the widespread use of manual and instrument-assisted spinal adjustments, current protocols rely heavily on empirical approaches, with limited understanding of how tissue-level biomechanical responses—particularly in vertebral joints, ligaments, and intervertebral discs—vary across patient demographics or pre-existing spinal conditions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale biomechanical interactions during spinal adjustments using finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning. Patient-specific spinal geometries will be reconstructed from de-identified radiographic datasets (X-ray and MRI) sourced from clinical partners, with material properties calibrated using anonymized biomechanical testing data. FEA simulations will model force propagation under varying adjustment parameters (angle, velocity, magnitude), while a neural network trained on retrospective clinical outcomes (pain reduction, mobility improvement) will correlate simulated stress-strain distributions with therapeutic efficacy. The HPC environment is critical for handling the computational intensity of 3D model generation (~10^6 elements per simulation), iterative parameter optimization, and large-scale data integration across heterogeneous datasets (imaging, biomechanical, clinical). Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide adjustment protocols for specific spinal pathologies (e.g., disc degeneration, hypermobility) and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for chiropractic educators. This work bridges clinical chiropractic practice with computational biomechanics, offering a foundation for data-driven personalization of spinal care while maintaining alignment with the hands-on technical skills emphasized in chiropractic assistant training programs. Resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, automated meshing workflows, and secure storage for sensitive clinical datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a chiropractor, to provide patient management, examination, and treatment services. Includes instruction in the principles and procedures of chiropractic, radiographic X-Ray procedures and techniques, X-Ray film analysis and media studies, orthopedic and neurological testing, clinical laboratory procedures, patient management and education, office administrative skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Urban horticulture faces unique challenges due to heterogeneous microclimates, soil contamination risks, and spatial constraints in densely populated areas. These factors complicate efforts to optimize crop yields, resource efficiency, and ecological sustainability. To address these challenges, this project proposes a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate plant-soil-environment interactions across diverse urban landscapes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model fine-scale spatial heterogeneity, including variations in light exposure, pollutant dispersion, and irrigation patterns, while incorporating multi-year climate projections and real-time sensor data from urban farms. The ABM will simulate crop growth dynamics under resource-limited conditions, while ML algorithms will identify predictive relationships between environmental variables, soil amendments, and crop performance.
