Current clinical models for dosing and monitoring rely on population averages and static protocols, which fail to account for dynamic physiological variability, genetic factors, and complex drug interactions. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate personalized anesthesia outcomes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Leveraging pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, machine learning, and patient-specific data from electronic health records (EHRs), the study aims to predict individualized responses to anesthetic regimens under diverse clinical scenarios. The computational workflow will integrate multi-scale models of drug metabolism, hemodynamic changes, and neural signaling to simulate real-time interactions between anesthetic agents, adjunctive drugs, and patient physiology. Monte Carlo methods will be employed to quantify uncertainty in dosage thresholds and adverse event probabilities across heterogeneous patient populations. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize simulations for large synthetic cohorts, and train predictive algorithms on multimodal clinical data. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for dynamically adjusting anesthesia delivery based on patient risk profiles, potentially reducing intraoperative instability and postoperative complications. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated anesthesia scenarios to advance research in precision nursing practices. By bridging computational science and clinical anesthesia, this work aligns with the program’s emphasis on evidence-based, patient-centered care and addresses a critical gap in perioperative risk mitigation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in movement biomechanics and rehabilitation optimization, critical areas for pre-physical therapy education and clinical practice. Current physical therapy (PT) interventions often rely on generalized protocols for injury recovery, which may not account for individual variability in biomechanics, neuromuscular control, or tissue healing. To address this gap, we propose developing patient-specific computational models to simulate musculoskeletal dynamics during rehabilitation exercises and predict personalized recovery trajectories. The research problem centers on the computational complexity of modeling high-resolution, multi-scale interactions between muscle activation, joint kinematics, and tissue adaptation—a task requiring intensive parallel processing. Our approach integrates motion capture data from human subjects, finite element modeling of soft tissue mechanics, and machine learning algorithms to optimize rehabilitation parameters. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to assess how variations in exercise intensity, frequency, and form influence biomechanical outcomes across diverse patient populations. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation framework for designing adaptive PT protocols and a predictive tool to identify injury recurrence risks. This work directly supports pre-PT education by providing students with hands-on experience in computational biomechanics, bridging gaps between traditional clinical training and data-driven rehabilitation strategies. The project will also generate datasets for coursework on movement analysis and evidence-based practice. By reducing the computational barriers to personalized PT research, this initiative aims to accelerate translational outcomes in musculoskeletal health while preparing future physical therapists to engage with emerging technologies in healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in physical therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenges of processing and analyzing large-scale visual media datasets in photojournalism, where the volume, velocity, and ethical complexity of digital imagery demand advanced computational tools. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to authenticate, contextualize, and ethically evaluate photographic and video content in real-time news environments, particularly as AI-generated media and misinformation proliferate. Current workflows lack the computational capacity to rapidly analyze high-resolution visual data across temporal, geospatial, and semantic dimensions while maintaining journalistic integrity. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable three key innovations: (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale historical photo archives to identify narrative patterns and ethical concerns in visual reporting trends, (2) real-time multimodal analysis combining computer vision, natural language processing, and blockchain-based provenance verification for breaking news scenarios, and (3) ethical AI training pipelines that maintain human editorial oversight while automating sensitive content detection. The methodology integrates adapted neural networks for image forensics, distributed database architectures for metadata correlation, and GPU-accelerated rendering for recreating contested photographic scenarios through 3D scene reconstruction. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for news organizations to audit visual content authenticity, computational guidelines for ethical AI integration in photojournalism workflows, and new visualizations of bias patterns in crisis reporting imagery. By allocating HPC resources for distributed storage, GPU clusters, and high-memory nodes, this work will advance computational journalism research while preserving the human-centered values of photojournalism practice. The project directly supports the program's mission to combine technical photographic expertise with rigorous journalistic standards in the digital age.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of still and motion photography in journalism and prepares individuals to function as news photographers and photographic editors. Includes instruction in photography, journalism, studio procedures and techniques, camera and equipment operation and technique, news editing, print and film editing, news scene composition, subject surveillance, media law and policy, news team field operations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable energy solutions has driven interest in harnessing tidal and wave energy in coastal regions. However, the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between turbulent ocean flows and energy-conversion systems present significant engineering challenges. Current predictive models lack the resolution to capture critical fluid-structure interactions and sediment transport phenomena, limiting the efficiency and environmental compatibility of deployed systems. This project seeks to address these gaps through large-scale, high-fidelity computational modeling of coupled hydrodynamic-structural-sediment systems in nearshore environments. Using a parallelized finite volume approach with adaptive mesh refinement, we will simulate three-dimensional wave-current interactions with deformable turbine arrays and mobile seabeds at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions. The simulations will integrate multiphysics solvers for fluid dynamics, structural response, and granular transport, validated against experimental wave tank data. Machine learning techniques will then optimize turbine placement and control strategies under varying tidal conditions. By leveraging high-performance computing resources, this research aims to (1) quantify the impact of seabed morphodynamics on array performance, (2) develop predictive tools for long-term system reliability, and (3) establish design principles that balance energy output with coastal preservation. The outcomes will advance the engineering of resilient marine renewable energy infrastructure while informing sustainable management of sediment-sensitive ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to monitor, control, manipulate and operate within coastal or ocean environments, such as underwater platforms, flood control systems, dikes, hydroelectric power systems, tide and current control and warning systems, and communications equipment; the planning and design of total systems for working and functioning in water or underwater environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as the action of water properties and behavior on physical systems and people, tidal forces, current movements, and wave motion.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing patient care delivery and clinical decision-making in complex healthcare environments through advanced computational modeling of nursing-sensitive outcomes. Despite the growing availability of electronic health record (EHR) data, traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to integrate multi-modal datasets—including longitudinal patient histories, real-time physiological streams, and institutional staffing variables—to predict risks such as preventable readmissions, sepsis onset, or staffing-related care delays. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning models capable of processing terabyte-scale clinical data from six regional hospital systems. The computational approach will employ federated learning frameworks to preserve data privacy while aggregating insights across institutions, combined with time-series analysis using recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to identify early warning patterns in patient trajectories. Parallelized hyperparameter optimization will enable rapid iteration of predictive models targeting adverse event reduction. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model the impact of dynamic nurse staffing strategies on care quality metrics under varying patient acuity conditions. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel, actionable predictors of nursing-sensitive outcomes and the generation of evidence-based staffing recommendations validated through in silico experiments. By elucidating hidden relationships between care processes and patient outcomes at scale, this research will provide nurse administrators and clinicians with tools to proactively mitigate risks, allocate resources efficiently, and personalize care pathways. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the computational demands of training deep learning models on distributed EHR data, running millions of parallel simulations, and maintaining compliance with healthcare data security standards through encrypted in-memory processing.
cip_title: Registered Nursing, Nursing Administration, Nursing Research and Clinical Nursing, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in registered nursing, nursing administration, nursing research, and clinical nursing, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of preserving and providing equitable access to culturally significant digital artifacts within large-scale, heterogeneous collections, a critical concern for libraries and archives in the digital age. Current methods for managing digital preservation workflows—particularly for non-textual materials such as born-digital art, interactive media, and complex multimedia datasets—struggle to scale efficiently due to limitations in processing power and algorithmic adaptability. The research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and refine computational models that automate the analysis, categorization, and risk assessment of at-risk digital objects. Using a hybrid approach combining machine learning (e.g., transformer-based models for contextual metadata generation) and graph-based network analysis, the project will map dependencies between file formats, software dependencies, and degradation patterns to predict preservation priorities. Additionally, the team will simulate decentralized storage strategies to optimize redundancy and access latency across geographically distributed archival networks. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including emulated legacy software environments and temporal metadata graphs, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure. Outcomes will include open-source tools for dynamic preservation prioritization, a framework for evaluating computational resource trade-offs in digital stewardship, and novel benchmarks for assessing fidelity loss in complex digital objects. By integrating HPC capabilities into library workflows, this research aims to bridge gaps between traditional curation practices and emerging computational demands, ensuring the longevity of digital cultural heritage while addressing equity in access for marginalized or under-resourced collections. The project’s interdisciplinary approach advances Library and Information Science by establishing scalable, computation-driven methodologies for stewardship challenges that existing analog paradigms cannot resolve.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the knowledge and skills required to develop, organize, store, retrieve, administer, and facilitate the use of local, remote, and networked collections of information in print, audiovisual, and electronic formats and that prepares individuals for professional service as librarians and information consultants.

abstract: The increasing complexity of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads necessitates advanced hardware accelerators capable of delivering high throughput with energy efficiency. However, existing architectures often struggle to adapt to dynamic computational graphs and real-time constraints, leading to suboptimal performance in applications such as autonomous systems and edge computing. This project seeks to address these challenges through the development of a simulation framework for designing next-generation AI accelerators optimized for adaptive workloads. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will conduct large-scale cycle-accurate simulations to model heterogeneous computing architectures integrating specialized processing units and reconfigurable interconnects. Machine learning techniques will be employed to automate design space exploration, targeting optimal configurations for latency, power consumption, and area utilization. The computational workload involves parallel execution of neural architecture search algorithms coupled with hardware parameter optimization, requiring significant memory bandwidth and multi-node coordination. Additionally, we will validate our models against FPGA-based prototypes using hardware description language (HDL) co-simulation. Expected outcomes include novel accelerator designs demonstrating ≥40% improvement in energy-delay product compared to current GPUs and TPUs, along with open-source tools for hardware-software co-design. This research will provide critical insights into the trade-offs between computational flexibility and efficiency, advancing the development of scalable computing systems for emerging AI applications. The requested resources will enable rapid iteration across billions of design permutations while maintaining fidelity to physical constraints—a capability unattainable with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer hardware and software systems and related equipment and facilities; and the analysis of specific problems of computer applications to various tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation diffusion and its impact on electoral behavior using advanced computational methods, with a focus on large-scale social media and news media datasets. The research problem centers on identifying how algorithmic curation, partisan media ecosystems, and networked communication patterns interact to amplify politically consequential misinformation during election cycles. Traditional approaches to political communication analysis struggle to process the velocity, volume, and heterogeneity of modern digital trace data, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The proposed work will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to classify multimodal content (text, images, video metadata) across platforms, coupled with temporal network analysis to model information cascades. Agent-based modeling will simulate voter exposure trajectories under different media consumption scenarios, requiring iterative parameter sweeps across millions of agent profiles. Computational demands include training transformer-based models for detecting nuanced persuasive strategies in political advertisements, processing multi-terabyte streaming datasets from API feeds, and running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of opinion formation dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for mapping cross-platform misinformation flows in real time, (2) empirical evidence quantifying the relationship between platform-specific message propagation patterns and shifts in voter sentiment, and (3) open-source tools for computational analysis of political discourse at scale. These results will directly inform policy debates about platform accountability and electoral integrity while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of communication studies and computational social science. The requested HPC resources are essential given the need for GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for temporal network graphs, and capacity to handle concurrent analysis of heterogeneous data streams across extended temporal windows encompassing multiple election cycles.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human and media communication in the political process and that prepares individuals to function as members of political and public affairs organizations, political campaign staffs, and related government and media entities. Includes instruction in media effects, political speaking and debating, political advertising and marketing, image management, political journalism, opinion polling, and aspects of print and broadcast media related to the production and distribution of media messages in political settings.

abstract: The transition from elementary to secondary education presents unique challenges for middle school students, who often experience declines in academic engagement and performance. To address this, educators require evidence-based strategies tailored to diverse learning needs, yet the development of such approaches remains limited by the complexity of analyzing multifaceted educational data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the efficacy of differentiated instructional practices in middle school classrooms. By integrating anonymized student performance data, behavioral surveys, and demographic records from 25 school districts, we will employ machine learning algorithms to identify patterns linking specific teaching methods—such as project-based learning or flipped classrooms—to measurable improvements in student outcomes. Agent-based simulations will further test how these strategies perform under varying classroom conditions, including differences in class size, socioeconomic factors, and resource availability. The computational demands of processing terabytes of longitudinal data, training predictive models, and running thousands of parallelized simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a framework for optimizing lesson plans based on real-time student needs and a scalable digital tool to help teacher candidates during practicum training. This tool will simulate classroom scenarios, enabling pre-service teachers to experiment with instructional choices and receive AI-generated feedback. By bridging gaps between educational theory and data-driven practice, the project aims to empower middle school educators with adaptable, empirically validated teaching strategies, ultimately fostering improved student engagement and academic resilience during this critical developmental period.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Junior High/ Intermediate/ Middle School Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the middle, intermediate or junior high grades, which may include grades four through nine by regulation.

abstract: Environmental education faces critical challenges in preparing K-12 educators to teach complex, interconnected ecological systems, such as climate change or biodiversity loss, in ways that foster student engagement and systems thinking. Current teacher training programs often lack tools to model dynamic environmental processes or simulate the impacts of human decisions on ecosystems, limiting educators’ ability to contextualize abstract concepts for learners. This project proposes the development of an interactive computational platform to address this gap, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create scalable, agent-based models of environmental systems tailored for classroom use. The research will focus on two objectives: (1) simulating multi-scale ecological interactions (e.g., predator-prey dynamics, carbon cycling, urban heat island effects) with variable parameters educators can adjust to explore "what-if" scenarios, and (2) analyzing how real-time visualization of these models impacts pre-service teachers’ pedagogical strategies during lesson design. Computational workflows will integrate NetLogo for model prototyping, Python-based data analysis of teacher-generated simulation outputs, and machine learning to identify patterns in educators’ model customization choices. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across diverse ecological contexts and educational use cases, enabling rapid iteration of models under differing biophysical and socio-economic constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of computationally optimized environmental education modules, paired with evidence-based guidelines for integrating systems modeling into teacher training programs. By bridging computational science and environmental pedagogy, this work aims to enhance K-12 students’ capacity to reason about sustainability challenges while demonstrating how HPC can advance resource-efficient innovation in teacher education. The project will also contribute benchmark datasets on computational tool adoption in classroom contexts, informing future interdisciplinary collaborations between environmental and educational sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach environmental education at various educational levels as a K-12 classroom educator. Includes instruction in foundations of environmental education, instructional methods, and related content knowledge.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in disease registry data management by developing scalable computational frameworks to integrate, analyze, and interpret heterogeneous multi-modal health datasets. Disease registries face growing challenges in harmonizing high-dimensional data—including genomic, clinical, environmental, and patient-reported outcomes—while maintaining compliance with evolving privacy standards. Traditional tools struggle with the volume, velocity, and complexity of modern registry data, particularly when linking dynamic real-world evidence (RWE) with longitudinal outcomes. Our research focuses on creating an adaptive high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to automate data curation, enable federated analytics across decentralized registries, and model disease progression pathways in underrepresented populations. Leveraging graph-based architectures and machine learning, we will optimize entity resolution across fragmented records, detect latent patterns in rare disease cohorts, and simulate intervention impacts using synthetic data derivatives. The computational workflow will deploy containerized modules for privacy-preserving federated learning, probabilistic record linkage, and time-to-event analyses scaled across distributed GPU clusters. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for interoperable registry analytics, validated on autoimmune disorder and pediatric cancer registries, which collectively encompass >2 million patients with sparse multi-omics data. This work will advance precision medicine by enabling real-time risk stratification, reducing biases in underrepresented subgroups, and establishing computational standards for emergent registry types (e.g., long COVID, environmental exposure). The requested HPC resources are essential for training deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, running parallelized simulations of disease trajectories, and testing federated architectures under realistic network constraints. By bridging computational scalability with clinical epidemiology, this project aims to transform disease registries into dynamic platforms for hypothesis generation and equitable intervention planning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to find, interpret, and record demographic and medical information on individuals for healthcare agencies and disease registries. Includes instruction in anatomy, data management, disease registry organization and operations, epidemiology, ethics, fundamentals of disease coding and staging, medical terminology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, physiology, quality management, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of intergenerational communication patterns within family systems and their impact on adolescent emotional regulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, longitudinal interactions. While prior work has examined family communication in broad terms, this study focuses on the role of digital mediation—such as asynchronous messaging and social media—in shaping developmental outcomes, a niche intersecting developmental psychology, communication studies, and computational social science. The research problem centers on disentangling how technology-augmented communication influences emotional co-regulation between caregivers and adolescents, particularly in families with geographically dispersed members. Using a mixed-methods approach, we will integrate qualitative coding of interview data with computational modeling of interaction patterns derived from anonymized smartphone metadata (e.g., response latency, emoji use, and media-sharing frequency). Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate family communication networks under varying constraints, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will predict emotional valence trajectories from text-based interactions. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale temporal datasets (spanning 12-18 months per family) and running parallelized simulations to explore counterfactual scenarios (e.g., altered communication frequency or modality). Expected outcomes include (1) identifying nonlinear thresholds at which digital mediation disrupts or enhances emotional attunement and (2) generating evidence-based guidelines for technology use in maintaining intergenerational bonds across developmental stages. By bridging developmental theory with computational techniques, this work aims to advance understanding of digitally embedded family systems while providing a methodological framework for analyzing high-dimensional behavioral data in developmental contexts. Findings will inform interventions targeting technology literacy in caregiver-adolescent relationships, with implications for family counseling programs and digital wellness initiatives.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework to optimize real-time analysis of dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) datasets in oncologic imaging, with the goal of enhancing the diagnostic support role of Radiologist Assistants (RAs). The increasing complexity of multiparametric imaging protocols generates vast, temporally resolved datasets that challenge traditional manual or semi-automated analysis methods. RAs, tasked with preliminary image evaluation and patient management, require tools to rapidly identify physiologically relevant biomarkers—such as perfusion kinetics or spatial heterogeneity—without compromising diagnostic accuracy. We propose a computational pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to train deep learning models on dynamically acquired DCE-MRI sequences, integrating 4D spatiotemporal convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with biomechanical models of contrast diffusion. The project will utilize federated learning across anonymized datasets from collaborating institutions to ensure robustness while adhering to patient privacy standards. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive 4D data (∼1 TB per patient scan), reducing latency in model inference for clinical workflows, and disentangling overlapping contrast kinetics in heterogeneous tumors. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for RA-specific decision support, validated against radiologist annotations, that prioritizes explainable AI outputs to align with RA scope-of-practice guidelines. Successful implementation could reduce time-to-preliminary-report by 30–50% in initial pilot studies, while quantifying previously undersampled tumor heterogeneity metrics. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational imaging, oncology, and radiology practice, directly supporting RAs in scaling their role within precision medicine paradigms without encroaching on diagnostic radiology responsibilities. HPC resources are critical for model training, large-scale data harmonization, and simulating contrast dynamics across diverse patient anatomies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to perform patient assessment, patient management, selected imaging procedures and to make initial observations of diagnostic images. Includes instruction in radiologic procedures and techniques, cross sectional anatomy, pharmacology, pathophysiology, patient assessment, patient care and management, and radiation biology.

abstract: Respiratory care therapies, such as aerosolized drug delivery and mechanical ventilation, rely on empirically derived protocols that often fail to account for patient-specific cardiopulmonary biomechanics, leading to suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model and optimize respiratory therapies using patient-specific anatomical and physiological data. The primary research problem centers on the dynamic interplay between airway geometry, airflow patterns, and aerosol deposition in heterogeneous lung pathologies, such as cystic fibrosis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Current clinical approaches lack granular, real-time adaptability to individual biomechanical profiles, resulting in inconsistent drug delivery efficiency and prolonged ventilator dependence in critical cases. To overcome this, the proposed work will integrate high-resolution computed tomography (CT) imaging data with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to construct patient-specific airway models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for running large-scale, transient CFD simulations that capture turbulent and laminar flow regimes across bifurcating airways, as well as particle tracking for aerosol dispersion. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to predict optimal drug delivery parameters (e.g., particle size, inhalation flow rate) and ventilator settings tailored to individual pathophysiological states. The expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform that enables respiratory therapists to customize treatment plans with unprecedented precision, potentially reducing treatment failures and hospital readmissions. By bridging biomechanical modeling, clinical respiratory care, and computational analytics, this project advances an emerging niche in precision therapeutics, offering a paradigm shift from population-based protocols to patient-specific optimization. The requested HPC resources will directly support the computationally intensive simulations required to achieve these objectives, fostering innovation at the intersection of health sciences and engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the accuracy and scalability of 3D bloodstain pattern analysis (BPA) in forensic investigations, a critical yet resource-intensive process for reconstructing violent crime scenes. Traditional BPA relies on manual measurements and simplified 2D geometric models, which often fail to account for complex fluid dynamics, environmental variables, or overlapping spatter events, leading to ambiguities in event reconstruction. To address these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity simulation approach using lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) coupled with machine learning to model blood dispersion under diverse conditions (e.g., impact velocity, surface textures, atmospheric effects). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multiscale, multiphase physics of blood droplets at forensic-relevant spatial resolutions while iterating across thousands of parameter combinations. Additionally, neural networks will be trained on simulation outputs to rapidly classify real-world spatter patterns and infer causative dynamics from crime scene data. The integration of LBM-based simulations with AI-driven analysis will enable probabilistic reconstructions of bloodshed events, quantifying uncertainties inherent to degraded or conflicting evidence. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for forensic examiners, validated against controlled experimental datasets, to improve the reliability of BPA in legal contexts. By bridging computational fluid dynamics, statistical inference, and forensic methodology, this work aims to establish a new standard for evidence-based bloodstain analysis, reducing subjective interpretations and enhancing the scientific rigor of courtroom testimony.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the physical, biomedical, and social sciences to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence, human testimony and criminal suspects. Includes instruction in forensic medicine, forensic dentistry, anthropology, psychology, entomology, pathology, forensic laboratory technology and autopsy procedures, DNA and blood pattern analysis, crime scene analysis, crime scene photography, fingerprint technology, document analysis, witness and suspect examination procedures, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The application of advanced computational methods in forensic pathology has the potential to transform the precision and scope of postmortem investigations, yet remains underexplored. This project seeks to address critical gaps in the integration and analysis of complex, multi-modal datasets generated during medical autopsies, including high-resolution imaging, toxicology, genetic data, and crime scene reconstructions. Traditional approaches often struggle with the volume and heterogeneity of these data, limiting the ability to identify subtle pathological patterns or contextualize findings within legal frameworks. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational pathology platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for cause-of-death determination, injury mechanism analysis, and population-level mortality trends. Key computational methods include deep learning architectures (e.g., 3D convolutional neural networks) for processing whole-body CT scans and histopathology slides, finite element simulations to model traumatic injury dynamics, and natural language processing algorithms to extract actionable insights from autopsy reports and legal documents. These workflows will be integrated into a unified framework, enabling probabilistic linkages between biological findings, circumstantial evidence, and forensic standards. The HPC environment is essential for training large-scale models on anonymized datasets spanning 20,000+ historical cases, running iterative biomechanical simulations, and performing genome-wide association studies to identify mortality-linked biomarkers. Expected outcomes include validated tools for (1) automated detection of occult pathologies in decomposed remains, (2) quantitative assessment of injury causation probabilities for courtroom testimony, and (3) geospatial mortality dashboards to guide public health interventions. By bridging computational innovation with forensic practice, this research aims to enhance the objectivity of postmortem diagnoses, reduce diagnostic discrepancies in contentious cases, and strengthen the scientific foundation of death investigation systems. The proposed platform will be disseminated as an open-source toolkit for medical examiners, fostering equitable access to advanced computational resources in forensic pathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the performance of medical autopsies, the analysis of human remains and crime scenes, and the legal follow-up and responsibilities of public pathologists.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing building systems for energy efficiency, structural resilience, and environmental adaptability in urban environments. Current design workflows in architectural engineering often rely on fragmented simulations that inadequately capture the interdependencies between structural, mechanical, and environmental systems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of an integrated high-performance computing (HPC) framework to model multi-physics interactions within building systems at unprecedented resolution. The computational approach combines finite element analysis for structural dynamics, computational fluid dynamics for airflow and thermal distribution, and machine learning algorithms to automate design parameter optimization. By leveraging parallel processing capabilities, the framework will simulate real-world stressors—such as extreme weather events, dynamic occupancy patterns, and material degradation—across multi-year operational cycles. Validation will occur through scaled physical prototypes instrumented with IoT sensors, creating a feedback loop to refine digital twins. The HPC resources will enable parametric exploration of 1,000+ design variants per simulation cycle, focusing on passive cooling strategies, hybrid material assemblies, and responsive façade systems. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for lifecycle energy use, generative design templates for climate-specific building envelopes, and a publicly accessible dataset of optimized system configurations. This work directly supports the development of next-generation architectural design tools that balance sustainability mandates with cost-effective construction practices. By enabling rapid, holistic analysis of building performance, the project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in design workflows and advance data-driven decision-making for urban planners and architectural firms. Results will contribute to evidence-based revisions of building codes and inform scalable solutions for retrofitting aging infrastructure in high-density regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the efficacy of pastoral counseling interventions in acute and chronic healthcare settings, with a focus on identifying linguistic and behavioral patterns that correlate with improved patient emotional and spiritual outcomes. Despite growing recognition of the role of pastoral care in holistic healthcare, there remains a critical gap in understanding how specific counseling strategies—such as crisis communication, ethical deliberation, or spiritual reframing—impact patient resilience, treatment adherence, and psychological well-being. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods study combining qualitative data from transcribed counseling sessions, patient surveys, and clinical outcomes with advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale textual datasets (≥10,000 hours of session transcripts) and train context-sensitive models capable of detecting subtle semantic shifts, emotional valence, and thematic coherence in counselor-patient interactions. Custom transformer-based architectures will be optimized to recognize domain-specific features, such as spiritual metaphor usage, ethical conflict resolution, and interdisciplinary communication patterns. Concurrently, graph neural networks will model longitudinal patient outcomes to identify intervention pathways linked to improved coping strategies. The computational pipeline will integrate privacy-preserving federated learning to comply with healthcare data regulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated toolkit for assessing pastoral counseling effectiveness, (2) evidence-based guidelines for tailoring interventions to diverse medical crises, and (3) open-source models to support training programs in clinical pastoral education. By bridging computational social science and healthcare chaplaincy, this work aims to establish reproducible metrics for spiritual care quality while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for studying complex human interactions in medical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including but not limited to, ordained clergy and other counseling professionals to respond to the emotional and/or spiritual needs of patients and families in health care emergencies and other situations, and to consult with and counsel other health care professionals. Includes instruction in advanced interpersonal communication; individual and small group counseling; interdisciplinary teamwork; crisis management; extended care relationships; self-analysis; medical ethics; pastoral care art; spiritual dimensions of human growth and health; counseling psychology and therapy; and applications to grief, death, emotional collapse, injury, individual/family adjustment, and chronic illness situations.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with complex conditions such as acute myocardial infarction and malignant arrhythmias posing significant challenges in clinical management. Current approaches to risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making are often limited by their reliance on population-level data and static diagnostic parameters, which fail to capture the dynamic, patient-specific interplay of structural, electrophysiological, and hemodynamic factors driving disease progression. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multiscale, patient-specific modeling of cardiac pathophysiology. Leveraging clinical imaging, electrophysiological recordings, and genomic data, we will construct integrated computational models to simulate myocardial electromechanics, coronary blood flow, and arrhythmogenic substrate formation at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational pipeline will employ finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, and machine learning algorithms to quantify interactions between ischemic injury, ventricular remodeling, and arrhythmia vulnerability. By validating model predictions against prospectively collected clinical outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndromes and inherited arrhythmia disorders, we aim to identify novel biomarkers of sudden cardiac death risk and optimize personalized treatment strategies, including catheter ablation targets and ventricular assist device placement. The scale of these simulations—requiring millions of core-hours for parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous cohorts—necessitates access to HPC resources. Successful implementation will advance precision cardiology by enabling real-time, patient-tailored simulations of disease mechanisms, directly informing clinical trials and practice guidelines. This work has the potential to transform the management of complex cardiovascular conditions by bridging critical gaps between cellular pathophysiology, organ-level dysfunction, and therapeutic intervention.
cip_definition: Research on how to specialize in diseases of the heart and blood vessels and to manage complex cardiac conditions such as heart attacks and life-threatening, abnormal heartbeat rhythms.

abstract: The integration of multi-omics data and advanced computational modeling in chemical pathology has the potential to revolutionize diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic decision-making. However, current workflows face challenges in processing high-dimensional datasets (e.g., metabolomic, proteomic, and lipidomic profiles) and linking them to clinical outcomes due to limitations in computational power and algorithmic scalability. This project seeks to address these bottlenecks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for disease stratification and laboratory test optimization. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to identify novel biomarkers for metabolic disorders, such as diabetes and inborn errors of metabolism, by analyzing multi-scale chemical pathology data from retrospective cohorts, and (2) simulating dynamic biochemical pathway perturbations using systems biology models to predict patient-specific responses to therapeutic interventions. Computational workflows will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures (e.g., graph neural networks for metabolite interaction mapping) and parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification in diagnostic thresholds. By unifying heterogeneous datasets—including mass spectrometry outputs, electronic health records, and real-time sensor data from laboratory instrumentation—this approach aims to reduce diagnostic latency and improve the precision of chemical test interpretation. The outcomes will directly inform clinical protocols for laboratory test prioritization and resource allocation in pathology departments, while the open-source tools developed will enable reproducible analysis pipelines for the broader community. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in bridging gaps between high-throughput analytical chemistry and actionable clinical insights, ultimately advancing personalized medicine in chemical pathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use and interpretation of chemical analyses, chemical diagnoses and management, and the supervision of chemical pathology laboratories. May included related research in basic and applied analytical chemical pathology; instrumentation data processing and chemical laboratory management.

abstract: The integration of multimodal clinical data for real-time prediction of patient deterioration in intensive care units (ICUs) remains a significant challenge in clinical informatics. Current predictive models often fail to synthesize high-frequency streaming data from electronic health records (EHRs), wearable sensors, and medical imaging, leading to delayed interventions. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a scalable deep learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The research will focus on aggregating heterogeneous data streams, including time-series vital signs, radiology images, and unstructured clinical notes, to predict critical events such as sepsis or cardiac arrest. Computational methods will involve hybrid architectures combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image analysis, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with attention mechanisms for temporal data, and transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for clinical text interpretation. Federated learning techniques will be implemented to train models across multiple institutions while preserving data privacy. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of petabytes of data, hyperparameter optimization at scale, and real-time inference simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for multimodal clinical data integration, validated predictive models with sub-hourly deterioration alerts, and benchmarks for federated learning efficiency in healthcare settings. This work aims to provide clinicians with actionable, timely insights to improve ICU outcomes while establishing computational best practices for privacy-preserving machine learning in clinical informatics. The requested resources are critical for managing the computational intensity of training deep learning models on multimodal datasets and ensuring the translational relevance of these tools in dynamic healthcare environments.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Informatics

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced computational framework for analyzing the acculturation challenges faced by foreign-trained lawyers adapting to U.S. legal systems. While existing programs for foreign lawyers emphasize doctrinal instruction, scant attention has been paid to the implicit cognitive and linguistic shifts required to navigate common law reasoning, statutory interpretation, and culturally embedded legal norms. The project addresses this gap by employing natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to model the semantic and structural disparities between legal argumentation patterns in foreign jurisdictions (e.g., civil law systems) and U.S. case law. A corpus comprising judicial opinions, legal briefs, and law school examination responses will be processed using transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants) to identify latent syntactic and rhetorical divergences. Computational experiments will simulate how foreign lawyers reinterpret U.S. legal texts through the lens of their native juridical frameworks, with iterative training cycles to map points of conceptual friction. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across multilingual datasets and optimizing model architectures to handle the high dimensionality of legal discourse. Expected outcomes include (1) a diagnostic tool to predict areas of systemic misinterpretation in transnational legal education, (2) dynamically generated adaptive learning modules tailored to individual cognitive profiles, and (3) quantitative metrics for assessing jurisprudential acculturation. By bridging computational linguistics and comparative legal pedagogy, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for cross-border legal training while advancing methodologies for analyzing expert domain acculturation in computationally underserved humanities-adjacent fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares lawyers educated outside the United States to understand U. S. or Canadian law and jurisprudence.

abstract: Clinical Nurse Specialists (CNSs) are pivotal in optimizing patient outcomes through advanced clinical decision-making, yet variability in patient responses to complex interventions remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to address the gap in predictive tools for personalizing care strategies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-dimensional clinical data. The research problem centers on the integration of heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacotherapeutic histories, patient-reported outcomes, and biomarker data—to model individualized treatment responses in acute and chronic care populations. Current analytical methods lack the computational capacity to process these data at scale, limiting real-time clinical applicability. The proposed computational approach combines machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient trajectories under varying interventions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large-scale EHR datasets (n > 100,000 patients) to train ML models predicting adverse drug events, readmission risks, and recovery pathways. Concurrently, ABM will simulate the impact of CNS-led interventions, such as tailored pharmacotherapeutic adjustments or patient education protocols, on population health outcomes. Validation will involve retrospective cohort analysis and prospective pilot data. Expected outcomes include the development of a scalable predictive framework to guide CNSs in personalizing interventions, reducing trial-and-error approaches, and minimizing healthcare costs. The project will also generate open-access tools for clinical simulation, fostering evidence-based policy updates in nurse-led care. By aligning computational advances with CNS expertise, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven precision nursing, directly enhancing patient safety, treatment efficacy, and health equity in diverse care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver direct patient and client care in clinical settings. Includes instruction in clinical pharmacotherapeutics, advanced clinical practice, holistic nursing, nursing practice and health care policy, administration and consultation services, health assessment, patient stabilization and care, and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the doctrinal evolution of early Christian Trinitarian theology across multilingual textual corpora spanning the 2nd to 5th centuries CE. While traditional theological scholarship has relied on close reading of select texts, the sheer volume of extant writings—including patristic treatises, conciliar documents, liturgical texts, and apologetic works in Greek, Latin, Syriac, and Coptic—presents a challenge for comprehensive analysis. This research addresses this gap by applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to trace conceptual developments, semantic shifts in key theological terms (e.g., *homoousios*, *hypostasis*), and intertextual networks of influence. The computational pipeline will integrate optical character recognition (OCR) for digitized manuscripts, transformer-based multilingual embeddings for semantic analysis, and graph neural networks to model doctrinal transmission across geographical and temporal axes. By processing approximately 15,000 pages of primary texts and 10,000 pages of secondary scholarship, the project aims to identify previously unrecognized patterns in theological argumentation, quantify the impact of socio-political factors on doctrinal formulations, and reconstruct fragmentary textual traditions through probabilistic modeling. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated theological texts, visualization tools for doctrinal development timelines, and statistical models correlating linguistic features with doctrinal controversies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational linguistics and historical theology, offering a novel framework for studying doctrinal formation at scale while preserving the nuance of theological reasoning. The results will provide new insights into how core Christian doctrines emerged through complex interactions between textual interpretation, philosophical adaptation, and ecclesiastical negotiation, with methodological implications for digital humanities in theological studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the beliefs and doctrine of a particular religious faith from the intramural point of view of that faith. Includes instruction in systematic theology, historical theology, moral theology, doctrinal studies, dogmatics, apologetics, and applications to specific questions of ecclesiastical polity and religious life.

abstract: This project seeks to address gaps in equitable community health intervention planning by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model population-level health risks and optimize nurse-led resource allocation. Community nursing practice faces challenges in efficiently targeting preventive care and chronic disease management across diverse, dynamic populations, particularly in under-resourced regions. Current manual or small-scale analytical methods struggle to integrate multi-source data—such as electronic health records, socioeconomic indicators, and environmental factors—at the granularity required for precision public health. To overcome this, we propose developing a computational framework using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate community health outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. The ABM will represent individual and household health behaviors, social networks, and access to nursing services, calibrated using de-identified patient data from regional health systems. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify high-risk population clusters by analyzing spatial-temporal patterns in disease incidence, health service utilization, and community-reported needs. HPC resources are critical to process large-scale datasets (spanning 500,000+ individuals across five counties) and perform iterative simulations testing hypothetical nurse-led outreach strategies, staffing configurations, and resource distribution plans. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for hypertension and diabetes management prioritization, geospatial maps of intervention hotspots, and decision-support tools to guide community health nurses in allocating mobile clinic hours, educational campaigns, and home-visit programs. By quantifying the projected impact of resource allocation choices on health disparities, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in community nursing, ultimately improving cost-efficiency and health equity in underserved areas. The computational tools developed will be scalable to other regions and adaptable to emerging public health threats.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to promote health and provide preventive and curative nursing services for groups or communities under the supervision of a public health agency. Includes instruction in community and rural health, family therapy and intervention, disease prevention, health education, and community health assessment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize marine vessel repair and maintenance processes, with a focus on improving the durability, safety, and efficiency of ship components in corrosive and high-stress marine environments. A critical challenge in marine maintenance is predicting the degradation of materials such as steel, fiberglass, and composite hulls under dynamic operational conditions, as well as optimizing repair workflows for complex systems like propulsion shafts and steering mechanisms. Traditional trial-and-error approaches are time-intensive and costly, necessitating data-driven solutions. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale mechanical, chemical, and hydrodynamic interactions affecting vessel integrity. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model stress distribution in hulls and propulsion systems under varying loads, while machine learning algorithms trained on historical failure data will identify corrosion patterns and predict component lifespans. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate repair workflows in virtual drydock environments to optimize technician task allocation and resource use. By integrating these computational approaches, the project aims to generate predictive maintenance frameworks tailored to specific vessel types and operational profiles. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for material failure prediction, adaptive repair protocols to extend component service life, and decision-support tools for prioritizing maintenance interventions. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in marine repair technician training programs, bridging gaps between empirical practices and computational methodologies. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling large-scale simulations of heterogeneous materials and complex fluid-structure interactions, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. This work aligns with broader industry goals to reduce downtime, lower repair costs, and enhance safety in global maritime operations.
cip_title: Marine Maintenance/ Fitter and Ship Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair outboard and inboard engines; test, maintain, and repair steering devices and electrical systems; repair metal, wood, and fiberglass hulls and vessel components; fabricate and maintain sails; and repair and balance propellers and drive shafts.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale digital humanities study analyzing the evolution of cultural narratives across multilingual historical texts and visual media from the 16th to 19th centuries. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional sociopolitical events influenced transcontinental artistic and literary movements during this period, a task complicated by the fragmented nature of digitized archives, linguistic diversity, and the computational complexity of multimodal analysis. The team will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical languages (including Latin, Early Modern French, and Ottoman Turkish) and computer vision models to detect iconographic patterns in digitized artworks. Key computational methods include transformer-based embeddings fine-tuned on period-specific corpora, graph neural networks to map discourse networks across texts, and geospatial-temporal visualization of metadata. These workflows require parallelized processing of over 50TB of heterogeneous data—including scanned manuscripts, museum collections, and multilingual print materials—which exceeds the capacity of local institutional infrastructure. The requested HPC resources will enable distributed training of custom NLP models, large-scale alignment of text and image embeddings, and iterative network analysis across temporal slices. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access interactive platform visualizing narrative diffusion pathways, a publicly shared multilingual model suite for historical language analysis, and new quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural influence in premodern sources. By integrating computational scalability with humanistic interpretative rigor, this project aims to establish reproducible methods for cross-domain humanities research while providing resources to support broader scholarly and public engagement with understudied transnational cultural histories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of new technologies, advanced computing, and public engagement to investigate and analyze questions in the humanities. Includes instruction in anthropology, art, data mining and machine learning, design, digital archives, geospatial technologies, history, human-computer interface design, literature, markup languages, social media technologies, and software development.

abstract: Home Economics Teacher Education programs face increasing demands to integrate computational tools into pedagogical training, particularly for addressing complex, data-driven challenges in nutrition, textiles, and sustainable resource management. However, existing curricula often lack the infrastructure to model large-scale simulations or analyze multidimensional datasets, limiting educators’ capacity to prepare students for real-world problem-solving. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and implement advanced computational models tailored to Home Economics education. The research will focus on two primary areas: (1) machine learning-driven analysis of nutritional patterns and dietary interventions across diverse populations, and (2) agent-based modeling of household resource allocation strategies under varying socioeconomic and environmental constraints. These methods require parallel processing capabilities to handle datasets spanning demographic, geographic, and temporal dimensions while maintaining fidelity to real-world scenarios. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of predictive models, sensitivity analyses of sustainable practices, and visualization of complex relationships between consumer choices and systemic outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include scalable frameworks for integrating computational literacy into Home Economics pedagogy, evidence-based modules on data-informed decision-making, and open-access datasets for educator training. By equipping future teachers with tools to demonstrate interdisciplinary connections between Home Economics and STEM disciplines, this work aims to elevate the field’s relevance in addressing 21st-century challenges related to health equity, climate resilience, and responsible consumption. The project will directly enhance teacher preparedness to foster critical thinking and technical proficiency in students, bridging gaps between traditional Home Economics content and emerging computational methodologies.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Home Economics Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational home economics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in legal administrative workflows through the development of a predictive framework for optimizing document management and task prioritization in high-volume legal environments. While legal administrative professionals routinely handle complex document systems, case scheduling, and compliance tracking, current software tools lack adaptive intelligence to anticipate workflow bottlenecks or dynamically allocate resources based on case urgency, document complexity, or jurisdictional requirements. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze anonymized datasets comprising historical case timelines, document metadata, and resource allocation patterns from mid-sized law firms. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to classify legal document types and extract contextual features, while graph-based computational models will map interconnections between case components, deadlines, and staff roles. A reinforcement learning system will then simulate workflow optimization scenarios across thousands of parallelized iterations to identify robust decision-making patterns. The computational intensity of training multi-modal models on sensitive, heterogeneous legal data necessitates HPC infrastructure to ensure both scalability and data security through partitioned processing. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for intelligent task routing and a benchmark dataset for legal workflow analysis, both designed to integrate with existing case management systems without requiring proprietary software dependencies. By applying advanced computational methods to a domain traditionally underserved by technical innovation, this work aims to establish quantitative metrics for legal administrative efficiency while maintaining strict adherence to ethical standards governing confidential data. The results will provide actionable insights for legal education programs seeking to modernize curricula around emerging technologies in legal operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as legal office managers, special assistants, and legal secretaries. Includes instruction in office management, secretarial science, principles of U.S. or Canadian law, legal terminology and documentation, legal research, legal software applications, law office procedures, record-keeping, billing, applicable policies and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of adaptive human-computer interaction systems in niche domains, such as assistive technologies for neurodiverse populations, demands computational frameworks that integrate real-time behavioral data with dynamic interface adjustments. Traditional programming paradigms struggle to address the non-linear, context-sensitive feedback loops required for personalized user experiences in these applications. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computational model for real-time analysis of multimodal interaction data—including eye-tracking, gesture inputs, and biometric signals—to enable instantaneous interface adaptations. The research employs a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for modeling user behavior patterns and low-latency reinforcement learning agents for decision-making under strict temporal constraints. High-performance computing resources are critical for two phases: 1) parallelized training of context-aware GNNs on heterogeneous datasets spanning sensory inputs and user response histories, and 2) large-scale simulations of interface adaptation scenarios across diverse neurocognitive profiles. The computational workflow leverages containerized microservices to manage GPU-accelerated model inference and CPU-bound scenario simulations concurrently. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for developing adaptive interfaces with sub-200ms response times and a benchmark dataset capturing interaction patterns across neurodiversity spectra. This work bridges gaps between human-centered computing, real-time systems programming, and cognitive accessibility—a domain underserved by conventional human-computer interaction research. The requested resources will enable validation of the model’s scalability to population-level diversity while maintaining strict quality-of-service requirements, directly addressing computational bottlenecks in personalized assistive technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer programming, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize animal grooming practices through biomechanical and behavioral modeling, addressing gaps in standardized, evidence-based methodologies for diverse species and coat types. Despite the growing demand for specialized pet grooming services, current techniques often rely on anecdotal expertise, leading to variability in outcomes, potential animal stress, and suboptimal coat health. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to simulate interactions between grooming tools (e.g., clippers, brushes) and biological systems (skin, fur, muscle) across species, integrating data from 3D coat texture scans, physiological stress markers, and behavioral response datasets. Computational models will employ finite element analysis to map tool pressure distribution, machine learning to predict coat matting dynamics, and agent-based modeling to assess animal discomfort thresholds during grooming procedures. The workflow will parallelize simulations across grooming variables (tool type, speed, angle) and biological parameters (coat density, skin sensitivity, species-specific anatomy). Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends grooming protocols tailored to individual animals, minimizing stress while maximizing coat health. This research bridges computational biomechanics and animal care, establishing quantitative metrics for grooming efficacy and safety. By formalizing data-driven guidelines, the project aims to advance professional training standards, reduce industry reliance on trial-and-error practices, and improve welfare outcomes for companion animals. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling high-resolution biological datasets and scaling simulations across the combinatorial space of grooming scenarios, which cannot feasibly be tested in vivo due to ethical and logistical constraints. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and collaborations with grooming certification bodies, fostering innovation in this understudied yet socially impactful domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation outcomes are influenced by complex interactions between genetic, immunologic, metabolic, and clinical factors, yet current risk stratification and therapeutic strategies lack precision for pediatric populations. This project aims to address this gap by developing a predictive computational framework to optimize post-transplant management and improve long-term graft survival in children. A critical challenge lies in integrating multi-dimensional datasets—including longitudinal clinical data, donor-recipient genomic compatibility, immune cell profiling, and metabolomic signatures—into actionable models that account for the dynamic biological and developmental changes unique to pediatric patients. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze heterogeneous datasets from a multicenter cohort of 1,200 pediatric liver transplant recipients. Machine learning models, including ensemble algorithms and deep neural networks, will be trained to predict graft rejection, metabolic complications, and immunosuppression response. Computational simulations will explore virtual patient cohorts to evaluate how age-specific pharmacokinetic parameters and immune maturation trajectories influence outcomes. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-throughput sequencing data, running parallelized model training across hyperparameter configurations, and conducting large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive tools for early identification of high-risk patients, (2) mechanistic insights into age-dependent immune tolerance pathways, and (3) open-source computational workflows for pediatric-specific transplant analytics. By enabling real-time integration of complex biomarkers with clinical variables, this work will directly inform personalized immunosuppression regimens and surveillance protocols, reducing morbidity associated with prolonged steroid use and late rejection episodes. The resource-intensive nature of multi-omic integration and longitudinal modeling necessitates the scalability and computational throughput uniquely provided by HPC systems, which will accelerate translation of findings into clinical trials and practice guidelines for this vulnerable population.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize sustainable building design by integrating energy efficiency modeling, structural performance analysis, and material lifecycle assessment. Current architectural engineering workflows often treat these domains in isolation, leading to suboptimal solutions that fail to balance environmental impact, construction costs, and long-term resilience. Our research addresses this gap by creating a multi-objective optimization platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate interdependent building systems at scale. The computational approach combines parametric building information modeling (BIM) with finite element analysis for structural integrity testing, coupled with machine learning-driven energy simulations using weather datasets spanning diverse climatic zones. Parallelized algorithms will evaluate thousands of design permutations, incorporating dynamic variables such as passive solar strategies, hybrid material systems, and mechanical equipment efficiency. HPC resources are critical for managing the computational intensity of fluid dynamics simulations for natural ventilation analysis and Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic lifecycle assessment. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that identifies Pareto-optimal solutions for low-carbon building designs while meeting safety and operational requirements.
