The research will produce open-access datasets correlating design parameters with embodied carbon metrics and energy use intensity, addressing a critical need in architectural practice for data-driven sustainability frameworks. By enabling rapid iteration of complex, systems-integrated designs, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for net-zero buildings while establishing scalable computational methods for interdisciplinary building performance analysis. Results will directly inform curriculum updates in architectural engineering technology programs, bridging gaps between design visualization tools and engineering analysis workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Orthopedic interventions such as casting, splinting, and bracing rely on precise biomechanical optimization to ensure patient recovery while minimizing complications like pressure injuries or joint stiffness. Current protocols, however, often employ generalized guidelines that do not fully account for individual anatomical variability, tissue biomechanics, or dynamic healing processes. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model patient-specific orthopedic interventions, enabling data-driven customization of treatment plans. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate tissue-device interactions under varying physiological loads, healing timelines, and material properties. Multiscale finite element analysis (FEA) will be applied to anatomically accurate 3D models derived from patient CT/MRI scans, incorporating heterogeneous material properties of bone, soft tissue, and immobilization devices. Machine learning techniques will further be employed to analyze historical clinical outcomes and optimize device design parameters, including rigidity, padding distribution, and load transfer mechanisms. Validation will involve retrospective comparison with clinical data on recovery rates and complication frequencies. The computational demands of this project—particularly the need for parallelized simulations across thousands of patient-specific scenarios and high-dimensional optimization of design variables—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include open-source predictive models for orthopedic device performance, evidence-based guidelines for personalized immobilization strategies, and a computational pipeline adaptable to emerging materials like 3D-printed splints. This work aims to reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, improve functional recovery times, and establish a foundation for AI-assisted orthopedic decision-making in resource-constrained settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to cast, splint, and brace orthopedic injuries. Includes instruction in patient assessment; casting, splinting, and orthopedic appliances; radiographic interpretation; traction; and wound care.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time decision-making in frontline receptionist operations through advanced computational modeling, addressing the dynamic interplay of call volume, visitor traffic, and scheduling conflicts in high-pressure service environments. Traditional methods for managing these tasks rely on static protocols or human intuition, often leading to inefficiencies during peak demand or unexpected disruptions. The project proposes a novel integration of agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate and predict optimal resource allocation strategies, such as staff deployment, communication channel prioritization, and interruption handling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-modal data streams—including historical call logs, real-time sensor inputs from visitor tracking systems, and calendar metadata—while running parallelized simulations of thousands of scenario variations. The ABM framework will emulate interactions between visitors, staff, and digital systems, with reinforcement learning algorithms dynamically adjusting policies based on simulated outcomes. Key challenges include minimizing latency in scenario evaluation and scaling models to accommodate heterogeneous environments, from corporate offices to healthcare facilities. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit capable of reducing average wait times by 15-30%, improving schedule adherence, and quantifying the trade-offs between automated routing and human-centric service delivery. The computational outputs will be validated against empirical data from partner organizations, with sensitivity analyses to ensure robustness across diverse operational contexts. By bridging service operations research with computational social science, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for resource optimization in customer-facing roles, offering scalable solutions for industries where first impressions directly impact organizational success. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable the iterative refinement of models that would otherwise be computationally intractable, accelerating insights into emergent service dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform frontline public relations duties for a business, organization, or answering service. Includes instruction in telephone answering techniques, responding to information requests, keeping caller and/or visitor records, placing business calls, operating telephone switchboards and/or other communications equipment, relaying incoming and interoffice calls, schedule maintenance, and public relations skills.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting cerebral aneurysm rupture risk—a life-threatening cerebrovascular event—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific hemodynamic models. Current clinical assessments rely on static anatomical metrics, which poorly capture the dynamic, flow-driven biomechanical factors driving aneurysm progression and rupture. This project aims to bridge this gap by integrating time-resolved medical imaging data with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to quantify hemodynamic stressors, such as wall shear stress and flow instability, at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational pipeline will process 4D flow MRI and angiographic data to reconstruct patient-specific vascular geometries, simulate blood flow using finite volume methods optimized for HPC architectures, and analyze emergent flow patterns through machine learning-driven feature extraction. The scale of these simulations—requiring meshes exceeding 50 million elements and transient analyses over thousands of cardiac cycles—necessitates access to parallelized computing resources for efficient solver performance and large-scale data storage. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel, dynamic biomarkers for rupture risk and an open-source computational framework to enable clinically actionable risk stratification. By advancing the resolution and personalization of hemodynamic modeling, this work has the potential to transform the management of cerebral aneurysms, reducing unnecessary invasive interventions while prioritizing high-risk cases. The project also establishes a methodological foundation for extending real-time CFD applications to other vascular pathologies, aligning with broader efforts to integrate computational engineering innovations into precision healthcare.
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize dynamic decision-making processes in casino operations, focusing on the integration of real-time data analytics and probabilistic modeling to enhance gaming floor efficiency and security. The research addresses a critical gap in operational strategies for casinos, where traditional heuristic methods often fail to adapt to complex, variable environments such as fluctuating patron behavior, game demand patterns, and security threat detection. By developing computational models that simulate high-dimensional scenarios—including player traffic, dealer performance, and surveillance system responsiveness—the project aims to create adaptive frameworks for resource allocation, staff scheduling, and anomaly detection. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and deep learning architectures to process large-scale datasets from casino management systems, surveillance feeds, and historical gaming records. Key challenges include scaling neural networks for real-time video analysis of surveillance streams to identify irregular behaviors and optimizing parallelized simulations to predict optimal table game configurations under varying demand. The expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for probabilistic risk assessment in gaming operations, a predictive model for minimizing service bottlenecks, and a novel anomaly detection algorithm tailored to casino environments. These outputs will provide actionable insights for reducing operational costs, improving regulatory compliance, and mitigating fraud risks. The project’s interdisciplinary nature bridges computational social science, operations research, and ethical AI applications, offering a template for data-driven decision-making in hospitality industries while adhering to jurisdictional gaming laws. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC-enabled analytics can address niche, high-stakes challenges in non-traditional STEM domains, fostering innovation in service industries with complex human-technological interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on casino operations and services. Includes instruction in casino operations, casino security and surveillance, casino dealing, principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation remains a critical intervention for children with end-stage liver disease, yet significant challenges persist in predicting post-transplant outcomes and optimizing immunosuppressive regimens. Current clinical decision-making relies on static biomarkers and limited phenotypic data, which inadequately capture the complex interplay of immunological, metabolic, and genomic factors influencing graft survival. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing predictive computational models that integrate multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with longitudinal clinical records from pediatric transplant recipients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ machine learning frameworks to analyze high-dimensional datasets from a multicenter cohort of 1,200 patients, including rare post-transplant complications such as biliary strictures and antibody-mediated rejection. Computational workflows will include ensemble learning for risk stratification, neural networks to identify nonlinear interactions between immunosuppression levels and immune cell profiles, and agent-based simulations of immune response dynamics. The scale of data—spanning >50,000 genomic variants, longitudinal cytokine measurements, and electronic health record parameters—necessitates distributed computing for feature selection, model training, and validation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated algorithm to predict graft rejection risk within the first post-transplant year, (2) optimization protocols for personalized immunosuppression dosing based on real-time immune monitoring, and (3) identification of novel biomarkers for early detection of fibrotic graft injury. By enabling rapid analysis of heterogeneous data streams, HPC resources will accelerate translational insights into pediatric-specific immunological tolerance mechanisms, directly addressing the urgent need for evidence-based strategies to improve long-term outcomes in this vulnerable population. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for pediatric transplant centers and integrated into clinical trial designs for targeted immunosuppressive therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex, dynamic interactions between household decision-making, resource allocation, and socio-economic stressors in diverse family structures. While traditional Work and Family Studies research relies on survey data and qualitative methods, this project addresses a critical gap: the inability to simulate large-scale, longitudinal scenarios that account for real-world variables such as fluctuating income, childcare logistics, and health-related disruptions. By integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning techniques, we aim to create a computational framework that simulates how families adapt to policy changes, economic shocks, and evolving cultural norms. The model will ingest heterogeneous datasets, including anonymized census data, time-use diaries, and regional economic indicators, to parameterize agents representing individuals, households, and community resources. Computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for thousands of interacting agents, managing stochastic elements in decision trees, and validating model outputs against longitudinal cohort studies. Expected outcomes include the identification of non-linear relationships between policy interventions (e.g., remote work mandates, childcare subsidies) and family well-being metrics, such as caregiver stress levels or intergenerational resource transfers. The HPC infrastructure is essential for running iterative simulations across multiple demographic profiles and crisis scenarios, enabling sensitivity analyses that traditional methods cannot feasibly support. Results will inform targeted interventions for vulnerable populations while advancing methodological innovation in family science through scalable computational tools. This work bridges empirical social science with data-intensive modeling techniques, offering a template for studying complex human systems in non-STEM disciplines.
cip_definition: An introductory program that focuses on family and consumer science concepts and principles at the basic and vocational levels, and the various potential career paths open to interested students. Includes instruction in career, community, and family connections; family and family/consumer resources; human development; interpersonal relationships; nutrition and wellness; parenting; and career possibilities in various related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the integration of computational modeling in psychology teacher education by investigating how adaptive instructional strategies can be optimized for diverse student populations in secondary psychology courses. A persistent challenge in teacher preparation is the lack of empirically validated frameworks to guide psychology educators in tailoring instruction to heterogeneous learner needs, particularly when addressing complex cognitive and affective learning outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity agent-based model (ABM) simulating student-teacher interactions in virtual classroom environments. The ABM will incorporate individual differences in prior knowledge, cognitive load thresholds, and motivation, calibrated using longitudinal datasets from high school psychology classrooms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the model's scale, which requires parallelized execution of 10,000+ parameterized simulations to identify optimal teaching strategies under varying conditions. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to detect patterns in effective instructional sequencing and feedback timing. The computational workflow includes sensitivity analyses to evaluate how specific teaching interventions propagate through social learning networks within classrooms. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive model linking teaching strategies to measurable learning gains in psychological reasoning skills, and 2) actionable guidelines for scaffolding metacognitive development in adolescent learners. By bridging computational pedagogy with discipline-specific teacher training, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for psychology instruction while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-enabled simulation in teacher education research. Resulting datasets and model architectures will be made available to the educational community through open repositories to support further innovation in subject-specific pedagogical training.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the usability and effectiveness of multimodal technical communication materials, with a focus on optimizing complex documentation systems for diverse audiences. As technical communication increasingly relies on interactive digital platforms, traditional text-centric evaluation methods fail to account for dynamic user interactions, multivariate content delivery, and accessibility requirements across devices. The research problem centers on creating scalable models to simulate user engagement patterns, predict comprehension barriers, and test adaptive content strategies in high-dimensional scenarios. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement agent-based simulations of user interactions with technical documentation systems, incorporating natural language processing to analyze semantic coherence across multimedia components and machine learning models to identify patterns in large-scale usability datasets. Computational experiments will evaluate how variables such as information architecture, visual hierarchy, and adaptive content delivery impact user task success rates across different demographic and expertise groups. The project will also employ GPU-accelerated rendering to model real-time document accessibility adjustments for users with disabilities. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing technical communication products during the design phase, reducing iterative testing costs, and improving inclusivity metrics. By enabling large-scale simulation of user experiences that would be impractical to test empirically, this research aims to advance evidence-based practices in technical communication while developing computational methods transferable to emerging domains like augmented reality documentation systems. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the parallel processing demands of multivariate simulations and training deep learning models on interaction log datasets exceeding 10^6 events.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the communication of technical and scientific knowledge to a variety of audiences through print, video, and digital media; and that prepares individuals to function as technical writers and editors, documentation developers, web designers, and usability specialists. Includes instruction in scientific and technical writing and editing, graphic and information design, web design, audience analysis, document usability and field testing, publications management, and applications to specific technical fields.

abstract: The increasing complexity of edge computing ecosystems, characterized by heterogeneous devices, fluctuating workloads, and stringent latency requirements, presents significant challenges in resource allocation and system resilience. Traditional centralized network management paradigms struggle to adapt to the dynamic, distributed nature of edge environments, leading to suboptimal performance, resource contention, and elevated operational costs. This project proposes the development of a decentralized, AI-driven orchestration framework designed to autonomously manage computational and networking resources across edge-to-cloud continuum infrastructures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will simulate large-scale edge networks with varying topologies, traffic patterns, and device capabilities to train and validate multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) models. These models will optimize task offloading, energy consumption, and latency while adhering to constraints such as bandwidth variability and hardware heterogeneity. The computational approach integrates real-time network telemetry with predictive analytics to enable proactive resource reallocation during demand spikes or node failures. Key innovations include a federated learning component to preserve data locality and a lightweight blockchain-inspired mechanism for auditing resource usage across administrative domains. The project will benchmark performance against existing orchestration systems in simulated scenarios mirroring smart city sensor networks and industrial IoT deployments. Successful implementation is expected to yield a scalable framework that reduces service latency by 30–50%, improves resource utilization efficiency by 20–40%, and enhances fault tolerance in distributed edge environments. Outcomes will provide network administrators with novel tools for managing next-generation infrastructures while advancing methodologies for autonomous system coordination in emergent computing paradigms. This work bridges gaps between network operations research, distributed systems optimization, and edge computing, offering practical solutions for evolving LAN/WAN management challenges in resource-constrained, geographically dispersed environments.
cip_title: System, Networking, and LAN/ WAN Management/ Manager
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to oversee and regulate the computer system and performance requirements of an entire organization or network of satellite users. Includes instruction in performance balancing; redundancy; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) network management; system migration and upgrading; outage control; problem diagnosis and troubleshooting; and system maintenance, budgeting, and management.

abstract: Chronic lung diseases, such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), involve complex, multiscale pathophysiological processes that remain incompletely understood. Current therapeutic strategies are limited by heterogeneous patient responses and an incomplete grasp of disease-driving mechanisms across molecular, cellular, and organ-level systems. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multiscale computational models integrating genomic, proteomic, biomechanical, and clinical data. We will employ agent-based modeling to simulate cellular interactions in fibrotic lung microenvironments, coupled with computational fluid dynamics to analyze airflow obstruction patterns in COPD. Machine learning pipelines will be applied to multi-omics datasets from longitudinal patient cohorts to identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response. These models will be iteratively refined using clinical imaging data and validated against in vitro organoid systems. The computational demands of these tasks—including large-scale parameter optimization, high-resolution 3D simulations of lung tissue mechanics, and parallel processing of heterogeneous datasets—necessitate access to HPC resources. Expected outcomes include predictive models of disease subphenotypes, optimized therapeutic targeting strategies for antifibrotic therapies, and mechanistic insights into microenvironmental drivers of pulmonary vascular remodeling. This work will directly inform the design of two upcoming clinical trials investigating personalized dosing regimens for IPF and biomarker-guided therapies in severe COPD. By bridging molecular mechanisms with clinical manifestations through computational integration, this project aims to advance precision medicine paradigms for pulmonary diseases while establishing scalable frameworks for simulating multiscale pathophysiology in other complex respiratory disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on pulmonary physiology and the treatment of lung diseases, pulmonary malignancies, related vascular diseases, respiratory disorders, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, and pulmonary pathology.

abstract: Prostate cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, with significant variability in treatment response and disease progression. Current risk stratification tools lack precision in integrating multi-omics data, imaging biomarkers, and longitudinal clinical outcomes, limiting personalized therapeutic strategies. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model tumor heterogeneity, predict treatment resistance, and identify molecular drivers of aggressive disease using high-dimensional datasets. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze whole-genome sequencing, bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, radiomic features from multiparametric MRI, and electronic health record data from a retrospective cohort of 1,200 patients with localized or metastatic prostate cancer. Machine learning pipelines will be implemented to integrate these multimodal datasets, including unsupervised clustering for subtype discovery, graph neural networks to model tumor-immune microenvironment interactions, and survival analysis with time-varying covariates. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further characterize urinary flow dynamics in patients with post-treatment urethral strictures, a common surgical complication. The scale of data (estimated at 400 TB) and complexity of models necessitate parallelized processing, GPU-accelerated training, and large-memory nodes for in-memory data integration. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for biochemical recurrence and metastatic progression, validated against an external cohort; (2) mechanistic insights into clonal evolution under treatment pressure; and (3) optimized surgical planning parameters to reduce stricture risk. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs for targeted therapies and advance precision urologic oncology. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source packages to enable reproducibility. By bridging large-scale data science with clinical urology, this project aims to translate computational findings into actionable biomarkers and decision-support systems for improved patient care.
cip_definition: Research focused on Urology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework for optimizing radiographic analysis and procedural efficiency in dental assisting. Dental radiographs are critical for diagnosing pathologies, yet manual interpretation by practitioners is time-intensive and subject to variability, particularly in fast-paced clinical environments where dental assistants play a key role in image acquisition and preliminary assessments. The research problem centers on improving diagnostic accuracy and workflow efficiency by automating the detection of common dental anomalies (e.g., caries, periapical lesions) and optimizing real-time image processing for chairside applications. A multimodal convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on a curated dataset of intraoral and panoramic radiographs, annotated with clinical findings from dental records, to identify subtle pathological features. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will further model instrument sterilization workflows to minimize procedural delays and microbial risk. The HPC environment is essential for handling large-scale image datasets (≥50,000 high-resolution radiographs), parallelizing CNN training across multiple GPU nodes, and running iterative CFD optimizations under diverse clinical scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source AI tool integrated with dental imaging software to provide real-time diagnostic suggestions, reducing interpretation time by ≥40% in pilot testing, and a validated sterilization protocol that decreases equipment downtime by 25%. By enhancing the precision and scope of dental assistants' roles in diagnostic support and clinical operations, this research bridges a gap in chairside technology adoption, offering scalable solutions to improve patient outcomes and resource allocation in oral healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide patient care, take dental radiographs (x-ray photographs), prepare patients and equipment for dental procedures, and discharge office administrative functions under the supervision of dentists and dental hygienists. Includes instruction in medical record-keeping, general office duties, reception and patient intake, scheduling, equipment maintenance and sterilization, basic radiography, pre- and post-operative patient care and instruction, chairside assisting, taking tooth and mouth impressions, and supervised practice.

abstract: Chronic pain management remains a significant clinical challenge due to the heterogeneity of pain mechanisms, variability in treatment responses, and the limitations of existing diagnostic tools. Current approaches to pain assessment and therapeutic decision-making rely heavily on subjective patient reports and trial-and-error pharmacologic strategies, which often delay effective care and increase risks of adverse outcomes. This project seeks to address these gaps by integrating multimodal clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomics, and wearable sensor metrics—to develop predictive models of pain progression and treatment responsiveness. The primary research objective is to identify patient-specific biomarkers and computational signatures that enable precision pain medicine. To achieve this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale datasets, which include multi-omic profiles (e.g., transcriptomic, epigenomic) from patients with chronic low back pain, chemotherapy-induced neuropathy, and post-surgical pain. Machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to uncover latent patterns linking molecular pathways, brain connectivity metrics, and clinical outcomes. Additionally, mechanistic modeling of nociceptive signaling pathways will be conducted using differential equation-based simulations to explore how genetic variants and pharmacologic interventions modulate pain perception. The computational workflow demands parallelized processing of neuroimaging data (>10 TB), real-time analysis of biosensor streams, and iterative model optimization, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for opioid efficacy, non-addictive analgesic combinations, and neural circuit targets for neuromodulation therapies. By translating these insights into clinical decision support tools, this research aims to reduce the burden of chronic pain through data-driven, individualized treatment strategies. The proposed HPC resources are critical to handling the computational complexity and scale of this integrative approach, which bridges clinical medicine and systems biology to advance pain research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of the entire range of painful disorders, either as a primary physician or consultant, for patients experiencing problems with acute, chronic, and/or cancer pain in both hospital and ambulatory settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design, installation, and performance evaluation of glazing systems using high-performance computing (HPC). Glaziers face challenges in balancing structural integrity, energy efficiency, and material costs, particularly as building codes evolve and environmental demands increase. Traditional empirical methods for material selection, load analysis, and thermal performance estimation are limited in scalability and precision, especially for complex geometries or extreme environmental conditions. To address this, we propose a multi-physics simulation approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model the mechanical, thermal, and optical behaviors of glazing materials under dynamic stresses. HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of glass and polymer composites under simulated wind, seismic, and thermal loads, while ML algorithms will identify patterns in historical failure data to predict optimal material configurations. Additionally, we will develop a generative design tool to automate the layout of fenestration systems, minimizing waste during cutting and installation. The computational pipeline will incorporate real-world variables such as site-specific climate data, architectural constraints, and safety standards. Outcomes will include open-access simulation templates for stress distribution visualization, a database of material performance metrics, and predictive models for energy efficiency and durability. This work will provide glaziers with data-driven decision-support tools, reducing trial-and-error in installations and advancing compliance with sustainability benchmarks. By coupling HPC with domain-specific technical knowledge, the project aims to bridge gaps between traditional craftsmanship and computational innovation in the glazing trade.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair fixtures, sheets, windows, and skylights made of glass, plexiglass, and other transparent materials. Includes instruction in site measurement, job analysis and estimation, material cutting and trimming, window and door installation, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of environmental and social dynamics in shaping early agricultural decision-making among Neolithic communities in Southwest Asia using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While archaeological studies have traditionally relied on regional site-specific data, a critical gap persists in modeling how micro-scale environmental variables (e.g., localized rainfall, soil depletion) interacted with social factors (e.g., resource-sharing norms, intergroup conflict) to drive the adoption or abandonment of crop cultivation strategies. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrating paleoclimate reconstructions, ethnographic data, and archaeobotanical records to simulate decision-making processes across heterogeneous landscapes. The computational model will parameterize individual and household agents with adaptive behavioral rules, enabling them to respond dynamically to stochastic environmental events, resource scarcity, and social networks. HPC resources are essential to execute ensemble simulations at scale, testing thousands of permutations of climate scenarios and social parameters to identify tipping points in agricultural resilience. Additionally, machine learning workflows will analyze simulation outputs alongside archaeological data to detect emergent patterns in crop selection and land-use practices. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework for analyzing human-environment耦合 systems in prehistory, with implications for understanding the long-term sustainability of agricultural transitions. Results will be validated against regional datasets from key Neolithic sites, offering empirically grounded insights into how early farming communities navigated environmental uncertainty—a research priority with parallels to modern climate adaptation challenges. This project underscores the potential of computational archaeology to advance social science inquiries beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries, leveraging HPC to bridge micro-scale human behavior and macro-scale cultural change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in water resource sustainability under climate change by developing a high-resolution, integrated hydrologic modeling framework to predict water availability and flood risks in complex watershed systems. Rapidly shifting precipitation patterns, intensified droughts, and extreme flood events are straining existing water management infrastructure, necessitating advanced computational tools to optimize reservoir operations, groundwater recharge strategies, and urban drainage systems. Current models often decouple surface water and groundwater dynamics or oversimplify land-atmosphere interactions, limiting their predictive accuracy at regional scales. We propose a coupled modeling approach using ParFlow-CLM to simulate 3D surface-subsurface hydrologic processes while incorporating machine learning techniques to assimilate real-time sensor data and remote sensing inputs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine spatial-temporal scales (10m grid resolution, hourly timesteps) across multi-decadal simulations, enabling the quantification of uncertainty in climate projections and infrastructure performance. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized parameter calibration, ensemble climate scenarios from CMIP6, and GPU-accelerated hydrodynamic flood routing. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of evaluating adaptive management strategies for water allocation, green infrastructure placement, and flood mitigation under diverse climate futures. This work directly supports state agencies in prioritizing reservoir upgrades and groundwater policy reforms while advancing computational hydrology methods through open-source model integration. By quantifying trade-offs between agricultural water use, urban resilience, and ecological flows at unprecedented resolution, the project will provide actionable insights for balancing competing water demands in rapidly changing environments.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for collecting, storing, moving, conserving and controlling surface- and groundwater, including water quality control, water cycle management, management of human and industrial water requirements, water delivery, and flood control.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Dutch and Flemish dialectal variation across historical and contemporary texts. While Dutch philology has a rich tradition of manual dialect mapping, the scale and complexity of digitized corpora—spanning medieval manuscripts, early modern print sources, and modern social media data—exceed the capacity of traditional methods. The research problem centers on identifying and modeling nuanced linguistic shifts, particularly in understudied regional dialects and Dutch-based creoles, which are often marginalized in broader language studies due to fragmented data and computational limitations. The project will develop and apply machine learning models to analyze phonetic, syntactic, and lexical patterns across diverse textual sources. Computational workflows will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for tokenizing non-standardized orthographies, training transformer-based models for dialect classification, and employing geospatial algorithms to visualize linguistic change over time. A key innovation involves adapting existing NLP frameworks to accommodate historical Dutch spellings and creole structures, which lack standardized training data. By integrating heterogeneous datasets—including the Digitale Bibliotheek voor de Nederlandse Letteren (DBNL), crowdsourced oral histories, and colonial-era texts—the project aims to reconstruct dialect continua and quantify the influence of sociohistorical factors on language evolution. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialect features, predictive models for language change, and methodological frameworks for computational philology in low-resource language contexts. These results will advance scholarly understanding of Dutch linguistic diversity, support preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and demonstrate scalable approaches for HPC-driven humanities research. The computational demands of training large language models on multilingual texts, processing high-resolution scanned manuscripts via optical character recognition (OCR), and running iterative simulations of language contact scenarios necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to ensure feasibility within project timelines.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Dutch language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; Dutch Creoles; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze patterns in historical thinking development among pre-service history teachers using large-scale interaction data from digital primary source archives. The research problem centers on the lack of granular, evidence-based models for how emerging educators build skills in source evaluation, contextualization, and argumentation—competencies critical for effective history instruction. While digital archives have become common pedagogical tools, existing studies rarely leverage the rich behavioral data they generate to understand learning processes at scale. This project will employ high-performance computing resources to process multimodal interaction logs (text analysis selections, annotation behaviors, temporal navigation patterns) from 50,000+ user sessions across multiple digital archive platforms. Natural language processing pipelines will be developed to classify inquiry strategies in written reflections, while recurrent neural networks will model temporal sequences of document access and annotation. Comparative analysis across demographic cohorts and institutional contexts will identify factors influencing skill development trajectories. The computational demands stem from the need to process terabyte-scale text corpora, train sequence models on longitudinal interaction data, and run parallelized simulations of instructional scaffolding strategies. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based typologies of historical thinking development stages, (2) predictive models linking specific digital archive interaction patterns to critical thinking gains, and (3) an open-source toolkit for adaptive scaffolding of primary source analysis tasks. By computationally modeling novice-expert transitions in historical reasoning, this work aims to transform how teacher education programs design and assess practice with digital evidence—ultimately improving secondary students' ability to engage critically with historical sources. The requested resources are essential for handling the dataset's scale and complexity while maintaining reproducibility across multiple experimental conditions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach history programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a multidisciplinary investigation into the transnational circulation of literary and cultural texts across marginalized communities in the 20th century. Traditional methods in cultural studies and comparative literature struggle to systematically analyze the vast, multilingual corpora required to trace patterns of adaptation, translation, and ideological reinterpretation at scale. The research problem centers on identifying how socio-political narratives—particularly those addressing decolonization and diaspora—were transformed as they moved between regions in Africa, South Asia, and the Caribbean. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, including multilingual topic modeling, semantic network mapping, and transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) techniques. These methods will process digitized archives of novels, political pamphlets, periodicals, and oral histories (≈50TB of unstructured text), requiring distributed storage and GPU-accelerated workflows for parallelized model training. Custom pipelines will align conceptual keywords across languages (e.g., Swahili, Bengali, English) using embeddings, while graph algorithms will map intertextual connections between authors and movements. The computational approach necessitates HPC capabilities to handle memory-intensive tasks like training domain-specific language models and visualizing high-dimensional cultural discourse networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable framework for cross-linguistic literary analysis, (2) datasets documenting narrative diffusion pathways, and (3) interactive visualizations revealing how localized struggles were reinterpreted transnationally. By integrating computational rigor with close-reading methodologies, this work aims to redefine understandings of cultural exchange in postcolonial contexts while demonstrating how HPC resources can catalyze humanities research traditionally constrained by manual analytical scales. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools and a monograph analyzing computational findings through critical theory lenses.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of cultural studies and comparative literature or a specialization which draws from cultural studies and comparative literature. Includes instruction in anthropology, comparative linguistics, cultural studies, history, literary criticism, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, sociology, and textual studies.

abstract: Livestock productivity and resilience are critical to global food security, yet optimizing these traits remains constrained by the complexity of genotype-environment interactions and the computational limits of traditional analytical methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance genomic selection and precision husbandry in cattle, with a focus on improving disease resistance and feed efficiency. Current models for predicting genetic merit or environmental adaptability rely on simplified statistical frameworks that inadequately capture nonlinear relationships or high-dimensional genomic, metabolic, and environmental data. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS), deep learning architectures, and agent-based simulations to model cattle populations under diverse management scenarios. The first phase will process whole-genome sequencing data from 10,000 cattle across multiple breeds to identify pleiotropic loci associated with immune response and nutrient utilization. Parallelized Bayesian networks and recurrent neural networks will then be trained on longitudinal productivity records, microbiome data, and climate variables to predict phenotypic outcomes. Finally, agent-based simulations will test optimized breeding and feeding strategies in silico under projected climate scenarios. This workflow demands substantial HPC resources due to the scale of genomic datasets (~500 TB), the computational intensity of training ensemble models on heterogeneous data types, and the need for high-throughput simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for precision livestock management, novel biomarkers for selective breeding, and scalable frameworks for simulating genetic gains in complex production environments. By bridging computational genomics and agricultural practice, this work will directly inform strategies to enhance sustainable animal protein production while reducing resource inputs and greenhouse gas emissions per unit output.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding and husbandry of agricultural animals, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural animal products. Includes instruction in the animal sciences, animal husbandry and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: Soil aggregation and pore structure dynamics are critical determinants of soil hydraulic properties, nutrient cycling, and carbon sequestration, yet their microscale interactions remain poorly quantified due to the complexity of organic-mineral interfaces and heterogeneous physicochemical processes. This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to simulate soil aggregation mechanisms and their impacts on water retention and solute transport in agricultural soils. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of organic matter adsorption onto mineral surfaces with pore-scale lattice Boltzmann (LB) modeling of fluid flow and reactive transport in 3D soil aggregates. The MD component will parameterize free energy landscapes for binding processes involving polysaccharides, humic acids, and clay minerals under varying moisture and ionic conditions. These parameters will inform LB simulations of aggregate stability and pore network evolution under dynamic wetting-drying cycles, validated against synchrotron-based X-ray microtomography data. A Bayesian calibration approach using Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling will reconcile model predictions with experimental measurements of soil water characteristic curves and hydraulic conductivity. The computational scale required—billions of grid points for LB simulations across representative elementary volumes and nanosecond-scale MD trajectories—necessitates parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows. Outcomes will yield predictive models linking molecular-scale interactions to macroscale soil hydraulic behavior, advancing precision management of soil structure for optimized water use efficiency and carbon stabilization. This work directly addresses gaps in process-based understanding of soil physical-chemical coupling, with applications to sustainable crop production and climate-resilient agricultural systems. By elucidating how organic amendments and tillage practices influence aggregation dynamics, the results will inform strategies to mitigate soil degradation while enhancing computational methodologies for soil systems science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and physical principles to research and analysis concerning the nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instruction in soil and fluid mechanics, mineralogy, sedimentology, thermodynamics, geomorphology, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize office management processes in dynamic organizational environments, with a focus on improving resource allocation, workforce scheduling, and operational efficiency. While traditional office management strategies rely on static protocols, modern workplaces face challenges from fluctuating workloads, hybrid staffing models, and evolving space utilization needs. Current manual or rule-based approaches often fail to adapt to real-time constraints, leading to productivity losses and increased operational costs. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) system coupled with machine learning (ML) to simulate office ecosystems and identify adaptive management strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of modeling multi-agent interactions across variables such as task priorities, employee skill sets, equipment availability, and physical workspace configurations. The computational workflow will integrate discrete-event simulations to model workflow bottlenecks, reinforcement learning to optimize scheduling decisions, and network analysis to evaluate communication efficiency in office layouts. Large-scale parameter sweeps will test scenarios ranging from routine operations to crisis response protocols. Expected outcomes include predictive models for proactive resource allocation, data-driven recommendations for space management, and decision-support tools for supervisors balancing productivity with employee well-being. By quantifying trade-offs in office management strategies under diverse conditions, this research aims to advance evidence-based practices in business administration. The resulting open-source tools will empower organizations to reduce operational inefficiencies while maintaining scalability—a critical need as workplaces increasingly adopt flexible and distributed work models. This work aligns with national priorities to enhance organizational resilience through computational social science applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and manage the operations and personnel of business offices and management-level divisions. Includes instruction in employee supervision, management, and labor relations; budgeting; scheduling and coordination; office systems operation and maintenance; office records management, organization, and security; office facilities design and space management; preparation and evaluation of business management data; and public relations.

abstract: Dental assistants experience a high prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) due to prolonged static postures, repetitive motions, and suboptimal ergonomic practices inherent to clinical workflows. Current ergonomic guidelines for dental settings remain generalized, lacking task-specific, data-driven recommendations tailored to the unique biomechanical demands of chairside assisting, instrument handling, and radiographic procedures. This project proposes a computational biomechanics approach to model musculoskeletal stress patterns during common dental assisting tasks and identify interventions to mitigate injury risks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations integrating motion capture data from clinical scenarios, anatomically precise musculoskeletal models, and finite element analysis of joint and soft tissue loading. Machine learning algorithms will process kinematic datasets to classify high-risk movement patterns and predict the efficacy of ergonomic adjustments, such as equipment repositioning, postural modifications, or workflow redesign. By simulating thousands of task iterations under varying ergonomic conditions, the project aims to generate granular, evidence-based guidelines for workstation configuration, tool placement, and movement protocols specific to dental assisting. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models linking task duration, posture, and equipment design to cumulative injury risk, as well as a framework for real-time ergonomic feedback systems in training environments. This research addresses a critical gap in occupational health for dental professionals, combining computational biomechanics, machine learning, and clinical ergonomics to advance injury prevention strategies in a high-risk, understudied population. The findings will directly inform dental education curricula, workplace safety standards, and the design of ergonomic dental equipment, ultimately reducing MSD incidence and improving workforce sustainability in oral healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide patient care, take dental radiographs (x-ray photographs), prepare patients and equipment for dental procedures, and discharge office administrative functions under the supervision of dentists and dental hygienists. Includes instruction in medical record-keeping, general office duties, reception and patient intake, scheduling, equipment maintenance and sterilization, basic radiography, pre- and post-operative patient care and instruction, chairside assisting, taking tooth and mouth impressions, and supervised practice.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly threatened by climate change, invasive species, and anthropogenic disturbances, necessitating advanced predictive models to inform adaptive management strategies. Current approaches often lack the spatial resolution and temporal scope to capture complex interactions between biotic and abiotic factors at landscape scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework to simulate forest dynamics under multiple climate and disturbance scenarios, with a focus on boreal and temperate systems in North America. The model will integrate multi-source data, including remote sensing imagery, LiDAR-derived canopy structure, soil moisture networks, and species-specific trait databases, to predict shifts in species composition, carbon sequestration potential, and disturbance regimes over decadal timescales. Computational challenges include parameterizing millions of individual tree agents, resolving fine-scale microclimate feedbacks, and conducting ensemble simulations across uncertainty ranges for precipitation and temperature projections. These tasks require high-performance computing resources to manage memory-intensive spatial datasets (>100 TB), parallelize Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of cores, and optimize machine learning workflows for pattern detection in output data. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold responses in forest resilience to compound stressors, (2) spatially explicit maps of vulnerability hotspots for targeted conservation, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive silviculture planning. The results will directly support federal land management agencies in prioritizing intervention areas and contribute to international assessments of nature-based climate solutions. By advancing mechanistic understanding of forest-climate feedbacks, this work addresses critical knowledge gaps in ecosystem service maintenance under global change scenarios while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-enabled ecological forecasting.
cip_definition: Any program in forestry, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of next-generation composite materials for applications in aerospace, automotive, and renewable energy systems. Composite materials face critical challenges in optimizing their mechanical properties, durability, and manufacturability due to the complex interplay of fiber-matrix interactions, curing processes, and environmental factors. Traditional experimental approaches to design and test these materials are resource-intensive, time-consuming, and limited in their ability to predict multiscale behaviors. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to model composite performance across micro-, meso-, and macro-structural scales. FEA will simulate stress distribution and failure modes in component geometries under operational loads, while MD simulations will resolve atomic-scale interactions between polymer matrices and reinforcing fibers. ML algorithms, trained on these datasets, will identify optimal material configurations and processing parameters, such as resin viscosity gradients and fiber orientation patterns, to enhance mechanical strength and reduce defect formation. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of simulations, reducing computational bottlenecks in solving nonlinear, multiphysics problems. Expected outcomes include predictive models for composite fatigue life, damage tolerance, and thermal stability, validated against experimental data from partner industries. These tools will accelerate the design of lightweight, high-performance composites for wind turbine blades and medical prostheses, reducing reliance on physical prototyping. The project will also generate open-access datasets and workflows to support workforce training in computational materials science, aligning with the program’s mission to integrate advanced technical skills with industry needs. By bridging simulation-driven innovation with practical applications, this research aims to position composite materials technology at the forefront of sustainable engineering solutions.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and use of composite materials in aircraft technology, automotive technology, boats, medical prostheses, and wind turbines. Includes instruction in computer-aided design and drafting, composite materials and processes, composite maintenance, composite manufacturing, composite repair, material science, and mold manufacturing and production.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of high-power ultrafast laser systems, which are limited by nonlinear optical effects and thermal distortions that degrade beam quality and operational efficiency. Current analytical models fail to capture the coupled dynamics of electromagnetic wave propagation, thermal diffusion, and nonlinear material interactions at the spatiotemporal scales required for next-generation applications. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for optical field evolution with finite element analysis (FEA) for multiphysics thermal-structural coupling. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve micron-scale beam profiles over millisecond timescales while incorporating quantum-mechanical models of photon-electron interactions in gain media. Key objectives include optimizing resonator geometries for dispersion compensation, predicting failure thresholds in optical coatings under extreme photon densities, and designing adaptive cooling systems for high-repetition-rate lasers. The simulations will utilize GPU-accelerated parallel computing to manage the 4D parameter space (wavelength, power, pulse duration, repetition rate) governing these phenomena. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for nonlinear beam degradation and thermal lensing effects, enabling the development of compact, high-efficiency laser systems with applications in precision manufacturing and photonic device testing. By providing open-source simulation tools tailored for optical engineering, this work will advance the broader community’s capacity to design directed energy systems and nonlinear optical components without relying on costly empirical prototyping. The requested HPC allocation is essential to achieve the necessary spatial resolution (<1 µm) and temporal fidelity (<1 ps sampling) across coupled physics domains, which exceed the capabilities of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of optical systems, lasers and related electronic devices. Includes instruction in wave theory and mechanics, electromagnetic applications, linear and non-linear optics, photon detecting, laser beam properties, directed energy, harmonic generation, optical systems, shielding and the design and implementation of related systems and equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of industrial automation systems, which integrate programmable logic controllers (PLCs), sensor-actuator networks, and multi-domain control systems (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic). As these systems scale to meet demands for precision and adaptability in applications such as robotic assembly and process manufacturing, traditional simulation and optimization methods become computationally prohibitive. Challenges include modeling dynamic interactions across heterogeneous components, optimizing real-time control under uncertainty, and validating system resilience at scale. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation framework capable of virtualizing large-scale automation environments. Computational workflows will combine finite element analysis for electromechanical components, discrete-event simulations for control logic, and data-driven digital twins to emulate sensor feedback loops. Parallelized optimization algorithms will iteratively refine control parameters for energy efficiency and fault tolerance, while machine learning models—trained on HPC-generated datasets—will predict system degradation and recommend maintenance protocols. The project also includes benchmarking real-time control strategies for robotic coordination in high-throughput scenarios, requiring low-latency processing of terabyte-scale sensor datasets. Expected outcomes include validated models for rapid prototyping of automation systems, reduced physical testing costs, and adaptive control templates deployable to industrial PLCs. By enabling high-fidelity, large-scale simulations, this work aims to advance the design of resilient automation architectures, directly supporting smart manufacturing and Industry 4.0 initiatives. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the memory-intensive workloads and parallel computations inherent to these multi-objective, multi-domain analyses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, installing, calibrating, modifying and maintaining automated systems. Includes instruction in computer systems; electronics and instrumentation; programmable logic controllers (PLCs); electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control systems; actuator and sensor systems; process control; robotics; applications to specific industrial tasks; and report preparation.

abstract: Earth science educators face significant challenges in teaching complex, interconnected systems such as climate dynamics, geophysical processes, and planetary evolution, particularly when constrained by limited access to advanced computational tools. This project seeks to address this gap by developing and deploying high-fidelity, interactive earth system simulations tailored for classroom use. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to generate multi-scale models of geological and climatic phenomena, including real-time visualization of tectonic plate interactions, probabilistic wildfire spread under varying climate scenarios, and ocean-atmosphere feedback loops. These simulations will be integrated into modular teaching frameworks designed for pre-service and in-service earth science teachers, aligning with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) and inquiry-based pedagogy. Computational workflows will employ parallelized numerical solvers for partial differential equations governing fluid dynamics and heat transfer, coupled with machine learning emulators to reduce latency for classroom applications. The project will also analyze the scalability of adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques to balance resolution needs with computational costs. Expected outcomes include open-access simulation toolkits, lesson plans co-developed with educators, and quantitative assessments of how HPC-enabled visualization improves pedagogical efficacy. By bridging cutting-edge computational earth science with teacher training, this work aims to enhance STEM education quality, equipping educators to contextualize abstract concepts through data-driven, immersive learning experiences. The requested HPC allocation will directly support model development, parameter space exploration, and the creation of reproducible workflows for academic institutions lacking dedicated infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach earth science programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to optimize real-time resource allocation during multi-hazard disaster responses, addressing critical gaps in adaptive decision-making under dynamic crisis conditions. Disasters such as compound hurricanes, wildfires, and terrorist attacks create rapidly evolving environments where traditional resource distribution models—often reliant on static risk assessments and linear planning—fail to account for cascading infrastructure failures, shifting population needs, and competing jurisdictional priorities. The research problem centers on creating a computational system that integrates live data streams (e.g., sensor networks, social media, satellite imagery) with probabilistic hazard propagation models to generate actionable resource allocation strategies through the incident command system (ICS) structure. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate civilian and responder behaviors, Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in hazard trajectories, and graph neural networks to optimize supply chain routing amid disrupted transportation networks. By leveraging parallelized computations on HPC clusters, the models will dynamically update evacuation plans, medical resource deployment, and interagency coordination protocols at scale, incorporating real-time feedback from simulated ICS decision cycles. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for emergency managers that reduces resource deployment latency by 30–50% in benchmark scenarios compared to current ICS protocols, as validated through historical case studies (e.g., Hurricane Katrina, Camp Fire). The project will further quantify how HPC-enabled adaptive resource balancing improves survival rates in densely populated regions and enhances equity in disaster aid distribution. Results will directly inform training protocols for ICS personnel and provide a scalable architecture for integrating machine learning into crisis management infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of the incident command system model to formulating and implementing effective response to natural and man-made disasters. Includes instruction in contingency planning, hazard and risk assessment, joint operations, law and ethics, emergency response and recovery, event mitigation, emergency rescue and medical operations, incident command, terrorism and national security issues, law enforcement, relief administration, volunteer and citizen coordination, public relations and applications to specific types of incidents.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the multi-level determinants of health behavior and evaluate intervention strategies aimed at reducing chronic disease disparities in underserved populations. Despite advances in behavioral health research, computational limitations persist in modeling complex, dynamic interactions between biological, psychological, and socio-environmental factors that influence health outcomes. Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture non-linear relationships, temporal dependencies, and heterogeneous effects across populations. To address this, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) and machine learning (ML) pipelines to simulate population-level health behaviors and predict intervention efficacy under varying socio-cultural conditions. The ABMs will integrate empirical data from longitudinal cohort studies, electronic health records, and geospatial databases to represent individual decision-making processes, social networks, and environmental exposures. Concurrently, ML algorithms will be trained on multimodal datasets to identify biomarkers, behavioral signatures, and structural barriers associated with health inequities. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to realistic population sizes (>100,000 agents), optimizing hyperparameters in ML architectures, and conducting sensitivity analyses across diverse virtual scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework to test hypotheses about mechanisms driving health behavior change, (2) predictive tools to prioritize interventions for specific subpopulations, and (3) open-source software for simulating policy impacts on health equity. This work will directly inform the design of adaptive behavioral interventions and provide a replicable approach for translating complex systems science into public health practice. By enabling large-scale, data-driven modeling, the requested resources will advance understanding of how individual choices and structural factors jointly shape population health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biological, behavioral, and socio-cultural determinants of health and health behavior, and the interventions and policies aimed at improving community and population health. Includes instruction in behavioral sciences, public health practice and policy, human services, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a computational framework to enhance the design and evaluation of competency-based training modules in Trade and Industrial Teacher Education (TITE). A critical challenge in vocational education is ensuring that instructional strategies align with the dynamic technical and pedagogical demands of modern industrial environments. While existing curricula emphasize hands-on skill development, there is a lack of scalable tools to simulate complex trade scenarios, model learner progression, and optimize teaching methods for diverse student cohorts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build adaptive simulation environments and predictive analytics models. The research will focus on three interconnected computational tasks: (1) developing physics-based simulations of industrial tasks (e.g., mechatronic systems troubleshooting, precision machining) using finite element analysis and discrete event modeling; (2) training machine learning classifiers to identify patterns in learner performance data from virtual labs; and (3) implementing multi-agent reinforcement learning systems to model classroom interactions and pedagogical decision-making. These methods require parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale datasets of student interactions, high-fidelity equipment simulations, and stochastic modeling of educational outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of training scenarios across variables such as class size, skill heterogeneity, and resource availability. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for generating evidence-based teaching recommendations, predictive models of skill acquisition timelines, and optimized virtual training environments that mirror real-world trade workplaces. By computationally bridging the gap between industrial practice and teacher preparation, this work aims to elevate the precision and scalability of vocational educator training while maintaining strict alignment with industry standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational trades and industries programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize decision-making processes in military Information Operations (IO) under conditions of uncertainty, adversarial adaptation, and multi-domain complexity. Current IO planning tools lack the capacity to simulate large-scale, dynamic interactions between friendly, neutral, and adversarial information networks, particularly when accounting for emergent technologies like generative AI-driven disinformation campaigns or decentralized communication protocols. The research problem centers on creating a high-fidelity simulation environment that integrates heterogeneous data streams—social media activity, network traffic patterns, and psychological operations (PSYOP) metrics—to predict second- and third-order effects of IO strategies. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning to represent adversarial adaptation loops and cascading impacts across cyber, cognitive, and physical domains. High-performance computing resources are required to execute parallelized simulations of network-of-networks interactions at operational scales, including real-time stress-testing of contingency plans against probabilistic threat scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that quantifies risk trade-offs in IO resource allocation, identifies critical vulnerabilities in adversarial information ecosystems, and recommends adaptive strategies to preserve coalition narrative coherence during contested operations. This work addresses a critical gap in joint force capabilities by advancing computational methods tailored to the unique temporal, ethical, and escalatory constraints of military information environments, ultimately enhancing the scalability and agility of IO planning processes. The resulting models will be validated against historical case studies and synthetic scenarios co-developed with operational partners, ensuring relevance to both tactical execution and strategic policy frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the strategic and operational use of information relative to the support of military and strategic policy and objectives.
