Includes instruction in information technology, decision theory and applications, military operations, command and control technology, network operations, network systems integration, computer network defense, space communications technology, and applications to specific military operational tasks.

abstract: Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, yet the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects on neuromusculoskeletal (NMS) conditions remain incompletely characterized. Current clinical studies often lack the resolution to model complex tissue interactions or analyze large-scale multimodal datasets, limiting the ability to optimize treatment protocols. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling and data-driven analyses of OMT’s impact on NMS systems. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) developing multiscale biomechanical models to simulate OMT-induced tissue strain, fluid dynamics, and neural signaling across spinal, cranial, and peripheral NMS structures, and (2) applying machine learning (ML) to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response from integrated datasets, including motion capture, electronic health records (EHRs), and high-resolution imaging (MRI/fMRI). Computational models will integrate finite element analysis, agent-based modeling, and dynamical systems approaches to capture hierarchical interactions from cellular to organismal scales. ML pipelines will employ federated learning frameworks to process decentralized clinical data while preserving patient privacy. The HPC environment is critical for managing iterative simulations of heterogeneous tissue properties, real-time optimization of ML hyperparameters, and processing terabyte-scale imaging cohorts. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into OMT’s effects on proprioceptive feedback loops, inflammatory modulation, and biomechanical load distribution, as well as clinically actionable models to personalize treatment targeting and dosing. By bridging computational science and osteopathic clinical practice, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for evidence-based OMT innovation, with broader implications for reducing reliance on pharmacologic interventions in chronic NMS care. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory CPUs for large-scale finite element simulations.
cip_definition: Research focused on osteopathic neuromusculoskeletal diagnosis and Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT).

abstract: The integration of multi-modal clinical and anatomic data presents a critical challenge in advancing diagnostic precision for complex diseases. Current approaches in anatomic and clinical pathology often rely on fragmented analyses of histopathology images, genomic profiles, and laboratory biomarkers, limiting the ability to uncover systemic pathophysiological relationships. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a scalable computational framework to unify heterogeneous datasets, including whole-slide imaging (WSI), next-generation sequencing (NGS), and clinical laboratory metrics, for enhanced disease classification and prognostic modeling. The primary research problem lies in efficiently processing and correlating high-dimensional data—such as terabyte-scale WSIs and genome-wide variant calls—while accounting for spatial, molecular, and temporal heterogeneity within patient cohorts. To achieve this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline leveraging distributed deep learning for WSI analysis, parallelized bioinformatics workflows for NGS data, and graph-based algorithms to model cross-modal interactions. Computational methods will include training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on GPU clusters to detect subtle anatomic abnormalities in WSIs, deploying Apache Spark for cohort-scale genomic variant aggregation, and employing graph neural networks (GNNs) to map tissue-level morphologic features to molecular alterations. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of ensemble models integrating pathology, genomics, and laboratory data, with validation across retrospective cases from institutional biorepositories. Expected outcomes include (1) a reproducible framework for multi-modal data fusion in diagnostic pathology, (2) predictive models linking anatomic phenotypes to molecular subtypes in solid tumors and inflammatory disorders, and (3) open-source tools to optimize laboratory workflow integration. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy, inform targeted testing protocols, and establish computational best practices for pathology departments transitioning to digital workflows. By addressing critical bottlenecks in data scale and complexity, the project aligns with national priorities for precision medicine and AI-ready clinical laboratories.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease and anatomic abnormalities. Includes instruction in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management, and quality control.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the morphosyntactic complexity of understudied Slavic languages, with a focus on dialectal variations in Eastern European minority language communities. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational models for analyzing non-standardized Slavic dialects, which exhibit high morphological richness and syntactic ambiguity. Traditional methods struggle to process these features efficiently, particularly when handling large corpora of spoken and historical texts. The project will employ transformer-based neural architectures and probabilistic graphical models to automate the parsing and annotation of dialectal data, integrating diachronic (historical) and synchronic (contemporary) linguistic patterns. Key tasks include training language-specific models on curated datasets of Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Serbian dialects, optimizing for low-resource scenarios, and simulating language contact effects through agent-based modeling. HPC resources are critical for managing the iterative training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale text corpora, parallelizing hyperparameter searches, and running large-scale simulations of language evolution. Expected outcomes include open-source NLP tools tailored to Slavic dialectology, a comparative analysis of morphological convergence in border regions, and a framework for predicting language shift dynamics in minority communities. These results will directly contribute to preservation efforts for endangered Slavic varieties while offering methodological innovations for computational linguistics. The project bridges gaps between traditional philological research and data-driven approaches, demonstrating how HPC can address longstanding challenges in Slavic linguistic typology and support interdisciplinary humanities scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Slavic languages of Central and Eastern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize adaptive resource management frameworks for heterogeneous edge computing ecosystems, where dynamic workloads and fluctuating infrastructure capabilities challenge traditional system design paradigms. Current edge environments—comprising distributed devices with varying computational power, energy constraints, and intermittent connectivity—struggle to balance latency-sensitive tasks with resource efficiency under real-world conditions. The research problem centers on developing a scalable, self-optimizing orchestration layer that dynamically allocates computational tasks across edge nodes while integrating predictive analytics to preempt bottlenecks. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will simulate large-scale edge networks with thousands of nodes, modeling diverse hardware configurations, stochastic workload patterns, and variable network topologies. Computational methods will combine hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to train decision-making agents under constrained scenarios, iteratively testing policies for task offloading, energy-aware scheduling, and fault tolerance. Key innovations include a modular architecture for interoperability with legacy systems and a novel cost function that weights computational urgency against device longevity. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for real-time edge resource allocation, benchmarked against existing static and heuristic-based approaches, with quantifiable improvements in system uptime (targeting ≥20% gains) and energy efficiency (≥15% reduction in peak consumption). The work will produce open-source tools for simulating edge environments, enabling reproducibility in emerging domains like decentralized IoT for smart infrastructure or disaster response systems. By addressing the gap between theoretical edge computing models and operational realities, this research aims to establish actionable best practices for deploying resilient, adaptive systems in resource-constrained settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply programming and systems analysis principles to the selection, implementation, and troubleshooting of customized computer and software installations across the life cycle. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software; compilation, composition, execution, and operating systems; low- and high-level languages and language programming; programming and debugging techniques; installation and maintenance testing and documentation; process and data flow analysis; user needs analysis and documentation; cost-benefit analysis; and specification design.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of casino table game dealing techniques through computational modeling of real-time decision-making and biomechanical efficiency. The research problem centers on the lack of empirical frameworks for training dealers in high-pressure, dynamic gaming environments, where split-second accuracy, ergonomic precision, and adaptive crowd management directly influence operational outcomes. Current pedagogical approaches rely on experiential repetition without robust quantitative analysis of performance variables. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models simulating multi-player table interactions across Blackjack, Craps, and Roulette, incorporating stochastic event chains (e.g., irregular bet placements, rule disputes, and dealer error recovery). High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of 10,000+ gameplay scenarios, capturing probabilistic distributions of dealer response latencies, motion trajectories, and cognitive load under varying casino floor conditions. Custom physics engines will model biomechanical efficiency in chip handling, card distribution, and wheel operation, integrating motion capture data from professional dealers. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework identifying critical thresholds for dealer error rates relative to game complexity and player density, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive training modules targeting situational stress resilience, and (3) generative algorithms proposing optimized table layouts to minimize repetitive motion injuries. By bridging computational ergonomics, behavioral modeling, and gaming operations, this work aims to establish a novel research niche at the intersection of hospitality technology and human performance analytics, offering translational benefits for both vocational education standards and casino operational integrity protocols.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and knowledge to become table games dealers in casinos or other recreational settings. Includes instruction in dealing techniques for Baccarat, Blackjack, Carnival Games, Craps, Poker, and Roulette.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex, multilevel social systems and evaluate community-based intervention strategies in the context of mental health disparities. Community psychology emphasizes understanding how systemic factors—such as neighborhood environments, social networks, and institutional policies—interact with individual behaviors to perpetuate inequities. However, simulating these dynamic, interdependent relationships at scale remains computationally prohibitive using conventional methods. The proposed research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis to simulate how variations in resource allocation (e.g., access to community centers, outreach programs) and social norms influence collective mental health outcomes across diverse populations. Agent rules will integrate empirical data from public health databases, community surveys, and regional policy records to parameterize individual decision-making, social influence dynamics, and structural barriers. Computational demands arise from simulating thousands of agents with heterogeneous attributes, nested within multilayer networks (e.g., familial, peer, institutional ties), over extended temporal horizons to capture feedback loops and delayed intervention effects. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to test hypotheses under varying policy scenarios, including resource distribution models and crisis response protocols. Expected outcomes include identifying critical leverage points for reducing mental health disparities, such as optimal timing for preventive interventions or configurations of community partnerships that amplify program efficacy. Results will be disseminated to local stakeholders via interactive data visualizations to support evidence-based policymaking. This work advances community psychology’s commitment to social justice by providing a scalable computational framework to evaluate equitable intervention strategies, bridging the gap between individual well-being and systemic change. The project’s computational tools will be made open-source to facilitate replication in underserved global contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply psychological principles to the analysis of social problems, and the implementation of intervention strategies for addressing these problems. Includes instruction in social ecology, primary and secondary prevention of social pathologies, social intervention strategies and tactics, large group counseling, social services systems behavior, creating settings, cultural stress, and the dynamics of social change.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing grant allocation strategies in mission-driven organizations, focusing on the understudied intersection of computational social science, behavioral economics, and philanthropic decision-making. The core problem addressed is the inefficiency in matching limited grant resources to high-impact proposals, exacerbated by the growing complexity of interdisciplinary projects and the subjective nature of traditional review processes. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with natural language processing (NLP) to simulate funding ecosystems, analyze historical grant outcomes, and identify latent patterns in successful proposal characteristics. The ABM component will model interactions between funders, applicants, and external stakeholders across diverse scenarios, incorporating behavioral parameters derived from experimental economics literature. Concurrently, transformer-based NLP models will process unstructured text from 500,000+ historical grant applications and outcomes to detect linguistic markers correlated with funding success and social impact. HPC resources are critical for training large language models on this heterogeneous dataset while maintaining proposal confidentiality through distributed federated learning architectures. The research will also develop novel metrics for quantifying the "adaptability potential" of proposed projects in uncertain environments using Monte Carlo simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support system that improves grantmakers' ability to identify proposals with high systemic impact while reducing implicit bias in evaluation processes. This work bridges computational methods with philanthropic practice, offering quantitative tools to enhance the societal return on grant investments. The computational infrastructure will enable real-time scenario testing at scale, providing actionable insights for both funders and applicants in increasingly competitive funding landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and write grant proposals to support an organization or cause. Includes instruction in identifying grant opportunities, developing an effective proposal, budget justifications, and developing a working relationship with the funder.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Deaf Studies through large-scale computational analysis of American Sign Language (ASL) datasets. The research problem centers on understanding the dynamic evolution of ASL linguistic structures and regional variations, which are underexplored due to the scarcity of tools capable of processing multimodal visual-language data at scale. Current methodologies for analyzing ASL rely on manual annotation or small-sample studies, limiting insights into sociolinguistic patterns, historical shifts, and cross-community dialect formation. This project proposes a computational approach using machine learning and computer vision models to analyze video corpora of ASL interactions, historical recordings, and educational materials. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabytes of video data, training 3D convolutional neural networks to extract phonological, morphological, and syntactic features from sign sequences. Spatial-temporal graph modeling will map variations in sign production across demographics, while natural language processing techniques adapted for gloss annotations will trace lexical changes over time. The computational pipeline will integrate ethical frameworks for culturally responsive data stewardship, developed in collaboration with Deaf community advisors. Expected outcomes include the first large-scale typological analysis of ASL dialects, quantitative models of language contact effects between ASL and English, and open-source tools for automated ASL annotation. These results will directly inform pedagogical strategies for ASL instruction, support preservation initiatives for endangered regional signs, and provide empirical foundations for policy advocacy related to linguistic equity. By bridging computational linguistics with Deaf cultural studies, this project aims to transform methodological paradigms in a field traditionally reliant on qualitative approaches, while ensuring HPC advancements align with the priorities of Deaf stakeholders.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the sociological, historical and linguistic aspects of the deaf and hearing impaired, and that prepares individuals to work with the deaf and hearing impaired. Includes instruction in American Sign Language, deaf studies, American deaf culture, structure of American Sign Language, history of the American deaf community, and civil rights of deaf people.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-precision, energy-efficient machining of advanced materials such as high-entropy alloys and carbon-fiber composites has exposed limitations in traditional trial-and-error process optimization. Current methods for predicting tool wear, thermal deformation, and material behavior under dynamic machining conditions lack the resolution and multi-physics integration required to address modern manufacturing challenges. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for simulating machining processes at unprecedented temporal and spatial scales. The research will employ multi-scale finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model chip formation, heat generation, and tool-workpiece interactions during high-speed machining operations. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict tool life and optimize cutting parameters by training on simulation outputs and experimental datasets. A key innovation involves implementing distributed computing architectures to handle the concurrent analysis of thermal, mechanical, and tribological phenomena across varying time scales—from nanosecond-level tool vibrations to hour-long production cycles. The HPC infrastructure will enable parametric studies of novel cooling strategies, including cryogenic and minimum quantity lubrication systems, through three-dimensional flow and phase-change modeling. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for surface integrity in hard-to-machine materials, optimized toolpath strategies to reduce energy consumption by 15–20%, and digital twins for real-time process monitoring. By transitioning from physical prototyping to virtual process development, this research aims to significantly reduce material waste and machine downtime in precision manufacturing. The computational tools developed will be integrated into advanced machining curricula, providing students with hands-on experience in physics-based simulation and data-driven manufacturing optimization. This project bridges critical gaps in digital manufacturing capabilities while fostering workforce development in emerging computational machining technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, manufacture, assemble, test, and repair parts, mechanisms, machines, and structures in which materials are cast, formed, shaped, molded, heat treated, cut, twisted, pressed, fused, stamped or worked.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of optimizing buyer-supplier negotiation strategies in Merchandising and Buying Operations by leveraging computational models to simulate dynamic, multi-variable scenarios. Traditional negotiation frameworks often rely on static pricing models and historical data, failing to account for real-time shifts in consumer demand, supply chain disruptions, and supplier capacity constraints. To bridge this gap, the study proposes an agent-based simulation platform that integrates machine learning, game theory, and real-time market analytics to model adaptive negotiation processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train reinforcement learning agents on large datasets spanning historical procurement transactions, supplier reliability metrics, and consumer sentiment signals from social media and e-commerce platforms. These agents will simulate iterative buyer-supplier interactions under diverse conditions, optimizing for cost, lead times, and risk mitigation. Concurrently, Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in supplier performance and demand volatility, enabling probabilistic scenario planning. The computational framework will also incorporate ethical sourcing parameters to evaluate trade-offs between cost efficiency and sustainability goals. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that dynamically recommends negotiation tactics based on real-time data streams, enhancing agility in procurement workflows. By quantifying previously intangible factors—such as supplier trust and geopolitical risks—the project aims to advance data-driven negotiation paradigms tailored to modern retail ecosystems. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science and operational research, offering novel methodologies for emerging niches in business analytics. The results will provide scalable strategies for buyers navigating complex global supply chains, directly contributing to improved profitability and resilience in merchandising operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional buyers of resale products and product lines for stores, chains, and other retail enterprises. Includes instruction in product evaluation, merchandising, applicable aspects of brand and consumer research, principles of purchasing, and negotiation skills.

abstract: Environmental education faces a critical challenge in equipping K-12 students with the ability to analyze complex, interconnected ecological systems. Traditional pedagogical tools often oversimplify dynamic environmental processes, limiting students’ capacity to engage with real-world scenarios such as climate change impacts, biodiversity loss, or watershed management. This project seeks to address this gap by developing high-fidelity, interactive computational models that simulate multi-scale environmental systems, enabling educators to present spatially explicit, data-driven scenarios in classroom settings. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models and spatially resolved simulations integrating real-time environmental data from satellite imagery, sensor networks, and public databases. These models will be designed to run probabilistic scenario analyses, allowing students to manipulate variables (e.g., land use policies, carbon emissions) and observe cascading effects on ecosystems. Computational workflows will utilize parallelized processing to handle large datasets and complex parameter spaces, while machine learning techniques will optimize model accuracy and reduce runtime for classroom applications. The expected outcomes include an open-access platform hosting these simulations, coupled with curricular modules aligned with Next Generation Science Standards. By providing scalable, evidence-based tools that bridge computational science and pedagogy, this research aims to enhance spatial reasoning and systems thinking skills among K-12 learners. The project will also establish a framework for integrating HPC-driven modeling into teacher training programs, fostering a new generation of educators adept at using advanced computational resources to teach environmental literacy. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC can transform STEM education by making complex systems accessible and actionable for diverse student populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach environmental education at various educational levels as a K-12 classroom educator. Includes instruction in foundations of environmental education, instructional methods, and related content knowledge.

abstract: Healthcare systems face increasing demands for efficient resource allocation amid rising operational costs and variability in patient care needs. Current administrative decision-making tools often lack the computational power to integrate real-time data streams, predictive analytics, and multi-objective optimization required for dynamic resource management. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a scalable computational framework to model and simulate hospital resource allocation strategies under diverse scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models and machine learning algorithms to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), staffing patterns, equipment utilization logs, and financial metrics. These models will simulate patient flow, staff scheduling, and supply chain logistics under constraints such as seasonal demand fluctuations, public health emergencies, and budget limitations. A key innovation involves coupling discrete-event simulation with reinforcement learning to identify adaptive policies that minimize costs while maintaining care quality. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing of large-scale datasets (10+ TB) and iterative optimization across thousands of simulated scenarios, which exceeds the capacity of local institutional servers. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for hospital administrators to test allocation strategies in silico, reducing trial-and-error implementation risks. This work will advance computational methods in healthcare operations research while directly addressing the National Academy of Medicine’s call for data-driven administrative solutions. Successful validation against retrospective data from three partner hospitals will demonstrate translational potential, with projected 12-18% efficiency gains in pilot use cases. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sensitivity analyses, model validation at scale, and benchmarking against existing allocation heuristics, forming the basis for peer-reviewed publications and a grant proposal to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ).
cip_title: Health and Medical Administrative Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of disaster response logistics demands real-time integration of heterogeneous data streams—including social media, satellite imagery, and IoT sensor networks—to optimize resource deployment and situational awareness. Existing decision-support systems lack the computational scalability to process multi-modal data under latency constraints, leading to suboptimal coordination during critical events. This project proposes the development of a dynamic, graph-based resource allocation framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to model evolving disaster scenarios, prioritize interventions, and simulate cascading impacts across infrastructure networks. The computational approach combines time-series graph neural networks (GNNs) for spatiotemporal pattern recognition with multi-agent reinforcement learning to adaptively allocate personnel, equipment, and communication bandwidth. Key challenges include handling petascale geospatial-temporal datasets, maintaining sub-minute inference times for real-time decision loops, and ensuring robustness against data source failures. The research will utilize parallelized graph processing on GPU clusters to accelerate GNN training and inference, while distributed agent-based simulations will model resource interactions across urban-rural divides. Expected outcomes include an open-source middleware layer for interoperable disaster data fusion and a set of validated performance benchmarks for emergency response HPC workflows. This work bridges gaps between operational research, distributed systems, and crisis informatics, offering a template for computational resilience in public-sector resource management. Successful implementation could reduce emergency response latency by 40-60% in simulated scenarios, directly supporting climate adaptation planning and regional infrastructure hardening initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of technological information systems, including computing systems, as solutions to business and research data and communications support needs. Includes instruction in the principles of computer hardware and software components, algorithms, databases, telecommunications, user tactics, application testing, and human interface design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to analyze temporally dynamic human behavioral data derived from mixed-method studies, integrating qualitative narrative inputs with high-frequency sensor data. The research addresses a critical gap in social science methodology: the lack of tools to model complex, time-dependent interactions between self-reported experiences and physiological or environmental signals (e.g., wearables, geolocation tags). Traditional longitudinal analysis methods struggle with the heterogeneous temporal resolutions and latent dependencies inherent in such datasets, particularly at scales exceeding 10,000 participants. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid approach combining Bayesian hierarchical models with transformer-based architectures, optimized for parallel processing on GPU clusters. The computational workflow will first preprocess and synchronize multimodal data streams using Apache Spark, then train temporal attention networks to identify phase-dependent predictors of behavioral outcomes. A second layer will apply Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to quantify uncertainty in cross-level interactions (individual vs. contextual factors). The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage memory-intensive operations during model training (estimated 250 TB of temporal graph data) and to run distributed simulations validating robustness across synthetic missing-data scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for temporal mixed-methods analysis and novel insights into the nonlinear dynamics of decision-making under sensory-cognitive feedback. This work will advance methodological capacity to study emerging interdisciplinary questions in digital behavioral phenotyping, with applications ranging from personalized intervention design to ethical AI development. By bridging computational scalability with methodological rigor, the project aims to establish new standards for reproducibility in high-dimensional social science research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of research studies, measurement of variables, data analysis, and formulation of models. Includes instruction in experimental, quasi-experimental, and case study methods; historical research; participant observation; questionnaire design; sampling theory; and statistical methods.

abstract: Grapevine cultivation and wine production face mounting challenges due to shifting climatic conditions, which alter phenological cycles, stress responses, and microbial ecosystems critical to fermentation. This project seeks to develop a predictive framework integrating multi-omics data, climate modeling, and microbial community dynamics to optimize viticultural practices and fermentation outcomes under climate variability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale genomic datasets from grape cultivars, simulate region-specific microclimate impacts on berry biochemistry, and model stochastic interactions within fermentative microbial consortia. We will employ machine learning algorithms to correlate hyperspectral imaging data of vineyards with transcriptomic and metabolomic profiles, identifying stress-resilient traits. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate yeast and bacterial population dynamics under varying temperature and nutrient conditions, incorporating real-world metabolomics data from experimental fermentations. These computationally intensive workflows require parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of sensor data, high-resolution climate projections, and combinatorial simulations of microbial interactions. Expected outcomes include (1) a decision-support tool for cultivar selection and canopy management tailored to evolving growing regions, (2) predictive metrics for balancing sugar-acid ratios in grapes under heat stress, and (3) optimized fermentation protocols leveraging climate-adapted microbial communities. The project will provide the viticulture and enology community with open-access computational models to mitigate climate-driven risks to grape quality and fermentation efficiency, directly supporting sustainable wine production in shifting agroecological contexts. By bridging plant biochemistry, microbial ecology, and precision agriculture through advanced computation, this work advances adaptive strategies for a critical agricultural sector facing unprecedented environmental transitions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific and agribusiness principles to the production of grapes, the making of wine, and the wine business. Includes instruction in grapes and wines of the world; grape production; winemaking technology; plant biology; chemistry; food science, safety, and packaging; soil science; pest management; and marketing and business management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for Lao language studies, particularly in analyzing its historical texts, dialectal diversity, and under-resourced digital infrastructure. Despite Lao’s cultural significance and its status as a Tai-Kadai language with rich oral and written traditions, existing linguistic tools and corpora remain limited, hindering large-scale philological and sociolinguistic research. The primary research problem involves overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing Lao’s complex orthography, dialect variations, and fragmented historical records—challenges that conventional methods cannot resolve efficiently. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to Lao’s linguistic features. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for automated text normalization and morphosyntactic annotation of classical Lao manuscripts, many of which exist in non-standardized or digitized forms. Concurrently, dialectometric analyses will map regional phonological and lexical variations using parallelized acoustic and text-based datasets. HPC resources will enable the rapid processing of terabyte-scale corpora, including OCR-digitized palm-leaf manuscripts and modern literary texts, while machine learning classifiers will identify diachronic shifts in syntactic patterns across literary epochs. Expected outcomes include the first open-access digital repository of annotated Lao texts, computational tools for dialect classification, and NLP models adaptable to educational or commercial applications, such as Lao-language text-to-speech systems. These resources will empower scholars to investigate historical language contact, literary evolution, and sociolinguistic dynamics with unprecedented precision. By integrating computational linguistics with Lao philology, this project aims to preserve vulnerable textual heritage, advance methodological innovation for low-resource languages, and foster interdisciplinary collaborations across Southeast Asian studies. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage memory-intensive workflows and ensure the reproducibility of large-scale analyses, directly supporting the program’s mission to expand Lao language research into technology-driven academic domains.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Lao language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of 3-D modeling and additive manufacturing demands computational resources capable of handling large-scale simulations, high-resolution data processing, and iterative design optimization. Current limitations in local computing infrastructure hinder the ability to efficiently execute multi-physics simulations, generative design algorithms, and real-time analysis of 3-D scanned datasets, particularly for applications in advanced manufacturing and precision construction. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges by enabling rapid, large-scale simulations and data-driven optimization workflows critical for next-generation 3-D modeling and design. The research focuses on two primary objectives: (1) developing parallelized computational workflows to simulate thermo-mechanical behavior in metal 3-D printing processes, reducing defects through predictive modeling, and (2) optimizing topology optimization algorithms for lightweight, high-strength structural components using generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on terabyte-scale CAD datasets. Computational methods will leverage distributed computing frameworks to manage finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and lattice structure generation, while integrating real-time feedback from 3-D scanning systems to refine model accuracy. Expected outcomes include novel computational pipelines that reduce iterative design cycles by 40–60%, validated protocols for defect-free additive manufacturing, and open-source tools for scalable 3-D model parameterization. These advancements will directly benefit industries reliant on precision 3-D fabrication, such as aerospace and biomedical device manufacturing, while providing students in the 3-D Modeling and Design Technology program with hands-on experience in HPC-driven design methodologies. The project underscores the critical role of scalable computing in bridging theoretical design principles with industrial applications, fostering innovation in both academic research and commercial production ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: The integration of personalized nutrition into clinical and community settings remains a critical challenge due to the complex interplay of dietary requirements, health conditions, and patient preferences. Current methods for meal planning in dietetics rely heavily on manual processes, which are time-intensive and may not fully optimize nutritional adequacy, cost-effectiveness, or adherence to dietary guidelines. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to automate and optimize meal planning for individuals with specific dietary needs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the combinatorial complexity of multi-objective constraints. The research will focus on creating machine learning models trained on diverse datasets, including electronic health records, dietary intake logs, and nutrient databases, to predict patient-specific nutritional gaps and preferences. Concurrently, optimization algorithms will be designed to balance medical requirements (e.g., diabetes management, renal diets), allergen avoidance, cultural preferences, and budget limitations. HPC resources are essential to enable large-scale parallelization of these tasks, particularly for solving high-dimensional optimization problems in near real-time and simulating long-term dietary outcomes across heterogeneous patient populations. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool that assists dietitians in generating tailored meal plans with quantified trade-offs between objectives, reducing planning time while improving adherence to clinical guidelines. The project will also validate the framework through retrospective analysis of historical patient data and prospective pilot studies in partnership with clinical dietitians. By enhancing the scalability and precision of dietary interventions, this work aims to improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and establish a model for data-driven decision support in nutrition care. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a foundational resource for future research in precision nutrition and dietetics education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of terrestrial ecosystem resilience to climate-driven disturbances by integrating high-resolution hydrological modeling, biogeochemical cycling, and satellite remote sensing data. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting how dynamic interactions between soil moisture regimes, vegetation productivity, and carbon-nutrient fluxes influence landscape-scale recovery from droughts and extreme precipitation events. Current models often treat these processes in isolation or at coarse spatial resolutions, limiting their utility for regional adaptation planning. We propose developing a novel computational framework that couples a parallelized hydrological model (HYDRUS-3D) with a biogeochemical reaction network solver (CLM-CN) at unprecedented 100-meter resolution across five major U.S. ecoregions. The integration of daily MODIS and Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, SMAP soil moisture products, and PRISM climate data will enable data assimilation at scales relevant to ecosystem management decisions. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve fine-scale heterogeneity in soil texture, topography, and land cover while simulating decadal timeseries under multiple climate scenarios (CMIP6). Each ensemble member will require 48 hours on 256 cores to complete the coupled surface-subsurface hydrology calculations, followed by iterative biogeochemical simulations using GPU-accelerated matrix solvers. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold behaviors in soil carbon storage following hydroclimatic extremes, (2) quantification of landscape connectivity impacts on nutrient transport, and (3) open-source tools for optimizing groundwater recharge interventions in agricultural watersheds. The 10TB of generated outputs will be synthesized into a public knowledge portal supporting USDA and USGS land stewardship initiatives. By elucidating cross-scale feedbacks between physical and biogeochemical processes, this work will provide actionable insights for maintaining critical zone services under increasing climate variability.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction of the Earth's oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial systems. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the performance and sustainability of coating materials and application techniques used in the painting and wall covering trades. Traditional approaches to evaluating paint adhesion, durability, and environmental resilience rely heavily on physical experimentation, which is time-consuming, resource-intensive, and limited in scope. The research problem centers on overcoming these constraints by creating predictive models that simulate the interactions between coatings, substrates, and environmental factors under diverse conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will conduct multiscale computational analyses integrating molecular dynamics simulations to study adhesion mechanisms at material interfaces, fluid dynamics models to assess spray application efficiency, and machine learning frameworks to correlate compositional variables (e.g., pigment concentration, binder properties) with performance outcomes. These models will account for variables such as humidity, temperature, surface roughness, and substrate porosity, which are critical to real-world performance but challenging to systematically test experimentally. The computational workflow will be validated against empirical data from industry partners, ensuring relevance to practical scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset to accelerate the design of eco-friendly coatings with enhanced durability, reduced VOC emissions, and optimized application parameters. By reducing trial-and-error experimentation, this work aims to lower material waste and energy consumption in both manufacturing and on-site application processes. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets and case studies to integrate computational literacy into vocational training programs, bridging gaps between traditional trade practices and emerging digital tools. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the high computational demands of parallelized simulations and large-scale parameter space exploration, enabling insights that could transform standards in surface coating technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to finish exterior and interior structural surfaces by applying protective or decorative coating materials, such as paint, lacquer, and wallpaper. Includes instruction in surface preparation; selecting, preparing, and applying paints and other coatings; hanging wallpaper; equipment operation and maintenance; finish selection; safety and clean-up; environmental effects on finishes; adhesion properties; and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to predict the cumulative impacts of climate change, nutrient pollution, and coastal development on critical aquatic ecosystems, including estuarine wetlands and coral reef habitats. Current management strategies often rely on siloed hydrological or ecological models that inadequately capture cross-system feedbacks, such as how altered sediment transport from watershed urbanization compounds thermal stress on marine biota. To address this gap, we propose coupling a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model (Delft3D Flexible Mesh) with biogeochemical (FABM) and ecological (Ecopath with Ecosim) modules to simulate multi-stressor interactions across freshwater-marine continua. The computational intensity of this approach necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve fine-scale processes (e.g., sub-kilometer tidal dynamics, daily nutrient fluxes) across decadal timescales while incorporating ensemble climate projections (CMIP6) and land-use scenarios. Key challenges include parallelizing particle-tracking algorithms for contaminant dispersion and optimizing memory usage for high-resolution habitat suitability analyses. Expected outcomes include quantitative vulnerability assessments for 12 case study regions, identifying leverage points where targeted management interventions could disproportionately enhance ecosystem resilience. The resulting open-source framework will enable resource managers to evaluate tradeoffs between flood control infrastructure, wastewater treatment upgrades, and habitat restoration investments under uncertain climatic futures. By advancing coupled terrestrial-aquatic system modeling at management-relevant scales, this work directly supports the program’s mission to integrate ecological and economic perspectives in water resource decision-making. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning-based parameterization and 500 TB of scalable storage for global sensitivity analyses across 10^4+ model iterations.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Water, Wetlands, and Marine Resources Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of marine/aquatic biology, oceanography, natural resource economics, and natural resources management to the development, conservation, and management of freshwater and saltwater environments. Includes instruction in subjects such as wetlands, riverine, lacustrine, coastal, and oceanic water resources; water conservation and use; flood control; pollution control; water supply logistics; wastewater management; aquatic and marine ecology; aquatic and marine life conservation; and the economic and recreational uses of water resources.

abstract: The increasing complexity of digital and physical evidence in criminal investigations has exposed critical gaps in the computational tools available for forensic reconstruction and analysis. Current methodologies often rely on fragmented software solutions that struggle to integrate heterogeneous data types—such as 3D crime scene scans, biometric data, and trace evidence patterns—into unified, actionable models. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to enable scalable, dynamic crime scene reconstruction and probabilistic evidence linkage. Leveraging parallelized algorithms and machine learning architectures, the system will process multi-modal datasets (e.g., LiDAR scans, DNA methylation timelines, and toolmark morphometrics) to simulate crime scenarios under variable spatiotemporal parameters. A key innovation lies in the integration of Bayesian inference networks to quantify evidentiary uncertainty and generate probabilistic timelines of criminal events, addressing the limitations of deterministic reconstruction approaches. The computational workflow will optimize GPU-accelerated pattern recognition for trace evidence classification and employ graph-based models to map associative networks between disparate evidentiary elements. By containerizing these processes within an adaptive HPC environment, the framework will support real-time collaborative analysis by geographically distributed forensic teams. Anticipated outcomes include a 40–60% reduction in processing time for complex evidence synthesis compared to existing tools, alongside the creation of reproducible, court-admissible visualization protocols. This resource will directly enhance the reliability of forensic conclusions in cases involving high-volume digital evidence or ambiguous physical traces, such as cold case re-examinations or multi-jurisdictional organized crime investigations. The project’s open-source computational modules will be validated through case studies with law enforcement partners, establishing a foundation for standardized, scalable forensic analytics in an era of increasingly data-driven criminal justice systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of clinical and criminal laboratory science, investigative techniques, and criminology to the reconstruction of crimes and the analysis of physical evidence. Includes instruction in laboratory science, laboratory procedures, criminology and police science, evidentiary testing and analysis, computer applications, record-keeping, reconstruction techniques, evidence handling and storage, and applications to specific types of evidence and crimes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize vehicle emissions inspection protocols and enhance diagnostic accuracy for complex emission control systems. Despite advancements in onboard diagnostics (OBD) and emissions testing, discrepancies persist between laboratory-based certification tests and real-world vehicle performance, particularly under heterogeneous operating conditions. These gaps hinder compliance with environmental regulations and limit the effectiveness of technician training programs. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics emission processes across diverse vehicle architectures, fuel types, and environmental scenarios. The computational approach integrates large-eddy simulation (LES) for exhaust flow dynamics, chemical kinetics models for catalytic converter efficiency, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to correlate sensor data with emission anomalies. Training datasets will include real-world OBD-II logs, remote sensing data, and parametric engine performance models. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of scenarios spanning temperature, altitude, and driving cycles while accounting for component degradation over time. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model to identify high-emission risk factors in aging vehicles, (2) a virtual testing platform for evaluating inspection station workflows under simulated load, and (3) ML-driven diagnostic tools to assist technicians in differentiating sensor failures from actual emission control system faults. By quantifying the sensitivity of emissions to maintenance variables and inspection parameters, this research will directly inform updates to technician certification standards and regulatory policy. The computational toolkit developed will be disseminated as open-source educational modules, bridging advanced simulation methods with hands-on technician training in emissions system maintenance.
cip_title: Vehicle Emissions Inspection and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to test, repair, service, and maintain vehicle emission systems in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Romanian linguistic and dialectal variation, with a focus on uncovering patterns in historical and contemporary text corpora. Despite Romania’s rich linguistic diversity, comprehensive studies of regional dialects and diachronic language evolution remain limited due to the manual labor required to process large, unstructured datasets. This research addresses this gap by developing scalable computational methods to analyze phonetic, lexical, and syntactic features across digitized texts, including historical manuscripts, modern literature, and transcribed oral narratives. Key objectives include mapping dialect boundaries using geospatial clustering algorithms, identifying linguistic shifts between pre-modern and contemporary Romanian, and training neural models to classify understudied regional speech varieties. The computational workflow integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques—such as tokenization, morphological tagging, and semantic role labeling—tailored to Romanian’s grammatical complexity, including its case system and verb morphology. HPC resources are critical for managing the project’s scale: processing terabytes of text data, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks (e.g., training transformer-based models on dialectal corpora), and running iterative simulations to validate hypotheses about language contact and change. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas of Romanian dialects, a diachronic corpus annotated for linguistic features, and publicly available NLP tools optimized for regional language variants. These resources will empower philological research, support language preservation efforts, and enhance technologies like automated translation systems for Romanian. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional philology, this project aims to redefine methodological standards in Romanian studies while contributing to broader discussions about language diversity in the digital humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Romanian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance clinical decision-making training for pre-nursing students through the development of high-fidelity, AI-driven patient simulation models. Current simulation tools used in nursing education often rely on static scenarios or simplified probabilistic algorithms, limiting their ability to replicate the dynamic complexity of real clinical environments. To address this gap, we propose creating adaptive virtual patient models that incorporate real-world electronic health record (EHR) data, physiological variability, and contextual social determinants of health. The research problem centers on optimizing these models to provide personalized, responsive training scenarios that improve diagnostic reasoning and intervention prioritization skills. Our computational approach leverages deep reinforcement learning architectures to simulate patient responses to nursing interventions, trained on de-identified EHR datasets encompassing 250,000+ patient encounters from diverse care settings. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multi-modal clinical data (including time-series vital signs, medication histories, and narrative notes) while maintaining the low-latency interaction required for immersive simulations. We will employ distributed training across GPU nodes to optimize recurrent neural networks capturing temporal disease progression patterns, with parallelized Monte Carlo tree search enabling real-time scenario branching. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation framework that adapts to learner performance levels, dynamically adjusting case complexity and clinical ambiguity. The resulting open-source platform will provide nursing programs with cost-effective, scalable training tools that better prepare students for clinical rotations. By integrating HPC-powered predictive modeling with nursing education pedagogy, this work aims to reduce skill gaps in early-career nurses, potentially improving patient safety outcomes in high-acuity settings. Resource allocation will support both model development and large-scale validation studies comparing simulation effectiveness against traditional methods.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in Nursing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized culinary experiences through the integration of sensory science, consumer behavior analytics, and molecular gastronomy. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to predict how individualized dietary preferences, cultural contexts, and physiological responses interact to shape culinary satisfaction. Current approaches rely heavily on generalized surveys or small-scale experiments, which fail to capture the dynamic, multidimensional variables influencing taste perception, texture preferences, and emotional engagement with food. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex networks of consumer-food interactions using agent-based modeling, machine learning, and multiscale sensory datasets. Computational models will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including biochemical properties of ingredients, real-time biometric feedback (e.g., salivary response, neuroimaging correlates of flavor perception), and sociodemographic variables—to generate predictive profiles of personalized culinary outcomes. The project will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures to analyze high-resolution spectral data from food matrices, coupled with natural language processing of consumer reviews and cultural narratives. Validation will involve iterative comparisons between simulated outcomes and empirical data from controlled culinary trials. Anticipated outcomes include a novel decision-support tool for chefs and food service providers to design hyper-personalized menus, reducing waste and enhancing consumer engagement. This work will establish a foundation for computational gastronomy as an interdisciplinary field, bridging gaps between data science, cultural studies, and culinary arts. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s large-scale datasets, real-time simulations of multi-agent interactions, and computationally intensive optimization algorithms, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure. By advancing predictive analytics in culinary personalization, this research aims to transform hospitality services while contributing methodological innovations to non-STEM domains.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy efficiency in industrial-scale heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, which are critical yet energy-intensive components of environmental control infrastructure. Current HVAC optimization strategies rely on generalized models that fail to account for dynamic interactions between equipment performance, facility layouts, and fluctuating environmental conditions. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML), and real-time sensor data assimilation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex spatiotemporal interactions within large industrial environments, including airflow patterns, heat exchange dynamics, and particulate dispersion. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized CFD solvers to simulate multi-zone thermal behavior at scale, coupled with ML algorithms trained on operational data to predict system responses under variable load scenarios. A digital twin platform will be developed to test control strategies for minimizing energy consumption while maintaining regulatory compliance and occupant safety. Expected outcomes include a validated optimization toolkit capable of reducing HVAC energy use by 15–25% in target industrial facilities, with broader applications in retrofit planning for aging infrastructure. The project will also generate open-access datasets on HVAC performance under diverse operating conditions, addressing a critical gap in environmental control technology research. By enabling precision adjustments to climate management systems, this work directly supports decarbonization goals while advancing computational methods for sustainable infrastructure optimization. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and ML training workflows that exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental control technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize radiation therapy protocols and assess environmental radiation exposure risks, with the goal of improving public health outcomes. Current models for predicting radiation dose distributions in heterogeneous tissues and evaluating population-level health risks from environmental radioactivity lack the resolution and scalability needed to account for individual anatomical variability, dynamic environmental factors, and long-term epidemiological trends. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations, machine learning-driven predictive analytics, and geospatial-temporal modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute GPU-accelerated particle transport simulations (using Geant4 and TOPAS) for personalized radiotherapy planning, which require ~10^8 particle histories per patient to achieve sub-millimeter precision. Concurrently, we will train graph neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets linking environmental radiation monitoring data, electronic health records, and genomic databases to identify susceptibility patterns across diverse populations. The computational workflow will be deployed on a hybrid CPU-GPU architecture, with an estimated need for 250,000 node-hours to process regional-scale environmental models spanning decade-long exposure timelines. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for radiotherapy toxicity risk (reducing late complications by ≥15% in benchmark scenarios) and a public dashboard for real-time radiation hazard assessment in urban environments. This work will directly inform clinical guidelines on radiation safety margins and public health policies for radiation risk communication, particularly in regions with elevated natural background radiation. By bridging clinical medical physics and population health, the project demonstrates how HPC-enabled integration of mechanistic and data-driven approaches can transform radiation risk mitigation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics, nuclear science, and engineering physics to diagnostic, treatment, and therapeutic processes and public health protection. Includes instruction in radiation biophysics, biophysics, health effects of natural and artificially induced radiation, hazard evaluation, environmental radioactivity, nuclear physics, engineering physics, radiobiology, medical radiology, calibration and dosage theory, computer applications and medical informatics, and specific research problems.

abstract: Dental hygiene practice faces emerging challenges in understanding the complex interactions between oral microbiomes, preventive treatments, and patient-specific risk factors. Current clinical protocols often rely on generalized approaches, which may not account for the heterogeneity of microbial communities or the dynamic responses of biofilms to interventions. This project proposes a computational study to model oral microbiome dynamics and evaluate the efficacy of personalized preventive strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will analyze metagenomic sequencing data from diverse patient cohorts to identify microbial signatures associated with caries and periodontal disease, employing machine learning algorithms to predict disease progression risks. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate biofilm development under varying hygienic conditions, including the application of antimicrobial agents and mechanical cleaning protocols. These simulations will integrate real-world data on enamel demineralization, pH fluctuations, and salivary biomarkers to enhance biological fidelity. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale genomic datasets, training predictive models, and running high-resolution biofilm simulations necessitate parallelized workflows and large-scale memory allocation, which are only feasible with HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into microbiome-driven disease mechanisms, optimized intervention timelines, and a framework for tailoring patient education based on computational risk assessments. By bridging gaps between microbial ecology and clinical practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based dental hygiene, reduce preventable oral diseases, and empower practitioners with data-driven decision-support tools. The findings will also inform curriculum updates, ensuring future hygienists are adept in interpreting computational analytics as part of comprehensive care. This project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in addressing public health challenges within oral healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean teeth and apply preventive materials, provide oral health education and treatment counseling to patients, identify oral pathologies and injuries, and manage dental hygiene practices. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, microbiology, and pathology; dental hygiene theory and techniques; cleaning equipment operation and maintenance; dental materials; radiology; patient education and counseling; office management; supervised clinical training; and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing grant-seeking strategies in mission-driven organizations, with a focus on computational grantsmanship—an emerging interdisciplinary niche integrating business analytics, behavioral economics, and natural language processing. The research addresses the critical challenge of resource allocation in competitive funding environments, where organizations often lack data-driven methods to prioritize grant opportunities, align proposals with funder priorities, and predict success probabilities. Current approaches rely on manual processes and heuristic decision-making, resulting in inefficiencies and suboptimal outcomes. The project will employ machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets, including historical grant awards, funder mission statements, proposal text corpora, and economic indicators. Computational experiments will utilize agent-based simulations to model funder-organization interactions under varying resource allocation scenarios, while transformer-based architectures will analyze semantic patterns in successful proposals. Key technical challenges include scaling graph neural networks to map evolving funder networks and processing multi-modal data streams in real time. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for probabilistic grant opportunity scoring, dynamic budget allocation optimization algorithms, and a generative AI assistant for proposal tailoring. These deliverables aim to reduce the cost-per-award ratio by an estimated 30-40% for nonprofit and social enterprise users while advancing computational methods for ethical AI in resource-constrained business contexts. The research will contribute novel insights into the behavioral dynamics of philanthropic markets and establish benchmarks for data-driven grantsmanship, with implications for emerging fields such as altruism analytics and impact finance. HPC resources are essential for training large language models on proprietary grant databases, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of funding ecosystems, and maintaining secure, auditable workflows for sensitive organizational data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and write grant proposals to support an organization or cause. Includes instruction in identifying grant opportunities, developing an effective proposal, budget justifications, and developing a working relationship with the funder.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational design methodologies in industrial and product design, with a focus on optimizing form, function, and sustainability in consumer products. Current design workflows struggle to balance aesthetic innovation, structural integrity, and material efficiency, particularly when iterating complex 3D models or simulating user interactions at scale. Traditional software tools are limited in handling high-resolution generative design algorithms, multi-physics simulations, or large datasets of user feedback, creating bottlenecks in prototyping and validation. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating parametric modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven ergonomic evaluation. The project will deploy GPU-accelerated generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize and refine product geometries based on aesthetic and functional constraints, while parallelized FEA simulations will assess structural performance under real-world stress conditions. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate user interactions across diverse demographic datasets to iteratively optimize ergonomic design parameters. By utilizing HPC clusters, these computationally intensive processes—which would otherwise require weeks of serial processing—can be compressed into days, enabling rapid design exploration and validation cycles. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for data-driven product design, novel algorithms for multi-objective optimization of aesthetic and functional criteria, and open-source tools to democratize HPC access for design researchers. This work will directly support the development of next-generation wearable technologies, modular furniture systems, and eco-friendly packaging solutions, while contributing foundational insights into computational creativity within applied visual arts. The results aim to bridge gaps between artistic intuition and engineering rigor, fostering sustainable design practices through reduced material waste and enhanced product longevity.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via the creation of effective forms, shapes, and packaging for manufactured products. Includes instruction in designing in a wide variety of plastic and digital media, prototype construction, design development and refinement, principles of cost saving, and product structure and performance criteria relevant to aesthetic design parameters.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance French language pedagogy by developing computational tools to analyze and model second-language acquisition patterns in classroom settings. A critical challenge in teacher education is the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to diagnose common learner errors in real time, particularly in phonetics, syntax, and discourse. While traditional pedagogical approaches rely on manual assessment, the increasing diversity of learner backgrounds and classroom sizes necessitates automated, high-fidelity solutions. This research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models on multimodal datasets of learner interactions, including spoken French recordings, written compositions, and instructor feedback logs. The computational pipeline will integrate speech recognition, grammatical error detection, and semantic analysis models, optimized for parallel processing to handle large volumes of heterogeneous educational data. Key objectives include (1) identifying latent error patterns across proficiency levels using clustering algorithms, (2) simulating error propagation in classroom dialogues via agent-based modeling, and (3) generating adaptive feedback templates for teacher trainees. By processing over 10,000 hours of annotated classroom data from francophone immersion programs, the models will capture dialectal variations and context-specific pedagogical challenges. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for French teacher educators, enabling trainee instructors to visualize learner progressions and refine intervention strategies. The scalability of this approach—enabled by HPC—will address critical gaps in personalized language instruction while maintaining pedagogical rigor. Results will directly inform curriculum design in francophone teacher certification programs, with potential applications to other less commonly taught languages.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach French language programs at various educational levels.
