abstract: Athletic injuries present complex challenges in sports medicine, requiring precise understanding of biomechanical stress patterns, tissue-level damage mechanisms, and longitudinal recovery dynamics. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict individualized injury risks or optimize rehabilitation protocols that account for both physiological and psychological recovery factors. This project proposes a computational framework integrating multi-modal athlete data—including motion capture kinematics, musculoskeletal imaging, and psychometric evaluations—to model injury causality and recovery pathways. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets from wearable sensors and 3D biomechanical simulations, which capture dynamic joint loading during sport-specific movements. Finite element modeling will quantify tissue stress distributions in anatomically accurate musculoskeletal structures, while machine learning algorithms will identify risk biomarkers from heterogeneous datasets spanning biomechanical, radiological, and psychological domains. A novel computational pipeline will couple agent-based simulations of rehabilitation adherence behaviors with finite element-derived tissue healing timelines, enabling personalized recovery forecasting. The HPC environment will accelerate Monte Carlo sampling for probabilistic injury risk assessment and enable parallel processing of patient-specific rehabilitation scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for anterior cruciate ligament and rotator cuff injuries in collegiate athletes, (2) AI-driven decision support tools for customizing rehabilitation plans, and (3) open-source computational workflows for correlating psychological recovery milestones with biomechanical readiness metrics. This resource-intensive approach addresses critical gaps in sports medicine by bridging tissue-scale biomechanics with clinical recovery outcomes, ultimately aiming to reduce reinjury rates and improve return-to-play decision-making through computationally derived insights.
cip_definition: Research focused on the pathology and biomechanics of athletic injuries and the effects of injury on the athlete, including both physical and psychological manifestations. Includes instruction in acute and chronic patient supervision, therapy and rehabilitation, and diagnostic procedures.

abstract: The proposed research addresses critical challenges in understanding turbulent transport mechanisms within magnetically confined high-temperature plasmas, a key obstacle to achieving sustainable nuclear fusion. While prior studies have characterized macroscopic plasma behavior, the multi-scale interplay between kinetic-scale instabilities, electromagnetic fluctuations, and global magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) modes remains poorly quantified. This project aims to bridge this gap by developing a coupled computational framework integrating particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations for kinetic effects with global MHD solvers, enabling first-principles analysis of cross-scale interactions in toroidal geometries representative of fusion devices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the vast separation of spatial and temporal scales: kinetic simulations will track electron-scale dynamics (μm/ps) alongside MHD phenomena (cm/ms), requiring massively parallel execution with adaptive mesh refinement. The computational approach leverages a modified version of the Gkeyll codebase, optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures, to simulate turbulent cascades and non-linear mode coupling in 3D configurations. Anticipated outcomes include (1) quantitative predictions of anomalous heat loss driven by microturbulence under varying magnetic shear profiles, (2) identification of instability thresholds for macroscopic tearing modes exacerbated by kinetic effects, and (3) validation against experimental Langmuir probe and soft X-ray diagnostics from the DIII-D tokamak. By elucidating how kinetic processes modify transport barriers and MHD stability boundaries, this work will directly inform operational scenarios for ITER and next-generation spherical tokamaks. Successful execution requires sustained access to HPC systems capable of hosting multi-petaflop simulations with >10^8 core-hours annually, as single discharges demand weeks of runtime on >10,000 cores to achieve converged statistics. The resulting dataset, comprising over 500 TB of spatiotemporal plasma profiles, will be made available to the fusion community via the OMFIT integrated modeling platform.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of properties and behavior of matter at high temperatures, such that molecular and atomic structures are in a disassociated ionic or electronic state. Includes instruction in magnetohydrodynamics, free electron phenomena, fusion theory, electromagnetic fields and dynamics, plasma and non-linear wave theory, instability theory, plasma shock phenomena, quantitative modeling, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize decision-making processes within distributed military command, control, and intelligence operations. Modern military environments involve dynamic, data-intensive scenarios where human operators must integrate fragmented information streams—including sensor data, communications, and intelligence reports—under time constraints and adversarial conditions. Traditional analytical methods struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between human cognitive load, organizational hierarchies, and real-time information flows. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-echelon decision networks and evaluate adaptive strategies for resource allocation under uncertainty. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to capture the interplay between individual decision-makers, institutional protocols, and emerging threats. Custom ABM modules will represent command structures, while RL algorithms will train agents to prioritize tasks, allocate sensors or analysts, and mitigate bottlenecks. Large-scale parallelism will enable the exploration of millions of scenario variations, including adversarial perturbations and resource constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation environment for stress-testing command architectures, quantitative metrics for organizational resilience, and prescriptive guidelines for balancing human judgment with automated support. This work directly supports the development of next-generation command systems capable of maintaining operational tempo in contested environments. By quantifying trade-offs between centralized control and decentralized adaptation, the project aims to inform doctrine and training protocols while advancing computational social science methodologies tailored to military contexts. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the necessary scale and fidelity for these simulations, which involve heterogeneous agents, high-dimensional parameter spaces, and real-time data assimilation requirements.
cip_title: Intelligence, Command Control and Information Operations, Other (MILITARY)
cip_definition: Any instructional program in intelligence, command control and information operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental assisting practice faces critical challenges in optimizing clinical workflows, improving diagnostic support tools, and advancing educational simulations. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale clinical datasets and simulating complex biomechanical processes hinder progress in these areas. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address three interconnected aims: (1) developing machine learning models to automate anomaly detection in dental radiographs, (2) simulating sterilization efficacy under varying instrument configurations and microbial loads, and (3) creating virtual reality training environments with real-time biomechanical feedback. The computational workflow will integrate convolutional neural networks for radiographic image analysis, computational fluid dynamics simulations for sterilization chamber optimization, and finite element modeling for tooth-material interaction studies. A novel multimodal dataset will be curated from partner clinics, encompassing 50,000 anonymized radiographs, instrument sterilization logs, and 3D intraoral scans. Resource-intensive tasks include training vision transformers on radiographic datasets requiring GPU-accelerated nodes and running parallelized fluid dynamics simulations across multiple CPU cores. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic support tool for early caries detection (achieving >90% sensitivity in preliminary benchmarks), validated sterilization protocols reducing process time by 15-20%, and adaptive training modules demonstrating improved student competency scores. By establishing computational frameworks tailored to dental assisting challenges, this research aims to elevate clinical standards, enhance educational outcomes, and provide evidence-based protocols for infection control—directly addressing critical needs in dental workforce development. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of clinically significant dataset sizes while maintaining temporal resolution required for practical implementation timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide patient care, take dental radiographs (x-ray photographs), prepare patients and equipment for dental procedures, and discharge office administrative functions under the supervision of dentists and dental hygienists. Includes instruction in medical record-keeping, general office duties, reception and patient intake, scheduling, equipment maintenance and sterilization, basic radiography, pre- and post-operative patient care and instruction, chairside assisting, taking tooth and mouth impressions, and supervised practice.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and physicochemical interactions of hair fibers during styling processes, with the goal of optimizing tool design, product formulation, and technique efficacy in professional cosmetology. While hair styling is an established practice, current approaches rely heavily on empirical trial-and-error due to the complex interplay of variables such as hair porosity, chemical treatment history, thermal tool dynamics, and product absorption rates. This research addresses the critical gap in predictive modeling capabilities for these nonlinear, multiscale interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the creation of molecular dynamics simulations to analyze cuticle-level responses to thermal stress and chemical treatments, coupled with continuum-scale finite element models of hair bundle deformation during braiding, cutting, and setting. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and experimental datasets to predict style longevity under varying humidity conditions and product combinations. The computational pipeline will integrate 3D-scanned hair morphology data with real-world environmental parameters to generate personalized styling recommendations. Expected outcomes include: (1) quantitative guidelines for minimizing heat damage during tool use through optimized temperature-time profiles, (2) predictive metrics for color retention in chemically treated hair, and (3) physics-informed neural networks for virtual style prototyping. By establishing the first HPC-enabled platform for computational cosmetology, this work aims to reduce material waste in product development cycles, improve educational tools for stylist training programs, and enable data-driven personalization of hair care regimens. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations of molecular interactions in keratin-protein systems and large-scale optimization of styling process parameters through parallelized parameter sweeps.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shampoo, cut, style, set, and dress the scalp hair of women and/or men, braid hair, apply hair cosmetics and wigs, and prepare for licensure as professional cosmetologists, hairdressers, and barbers at various levels.  Includes instruction in hair design theory and concepts, hair cleaning and shampooing, hair coloring, chemical applications and permanent reconstructions, hair anatomy and physiology, scalp diseases and treatments, wig and hairpiece fitting, hair braiding, customer service, shop management, equipment operation, health and safety, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize resource use while maintaining economic viability. Current decision-making tools often struggle to integrate real-time data from diverse sources such as soil sensors, weather forecasts, satellite imagery, and machinery telemetry, leading to inefficient allocation of water, fertilizers, and labor. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a scalable computational framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to synthesize multi-modal agricultural data and generate actionable insights. The research will employ machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, to model crop growth dynamics and predict yield outcomes under varying management scenarios. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model farm operations to evaluate the economic and logistical impacts of different resource allocation strategies. By coupling these approaches within an HPC environment, the project aims to enable real-time optimization of agricultural inputs, reducing waste and improving profitability. The computational workflow will utilize parallel processing to handle high-dimensional datasets and stochastic optimization algorithms to account for uncertainties in weather and market conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for precision agriculture, validated through case studies on midwestern U.S. grain farms, which demonstrate measurable improvements in resource efficiency and cost savings. This work will provide a foundation for adaptive, data-driven decision-making in agribusiness, enhancing the resilience of agricultural operations in the face of climate variability and evolving market demands.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general planning, economics, and use of facilities, natural resources, equipment, labor, and capital to produce plant and animal products, and that may prepare individuals for work in farming, ranching, and agribusiness.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery necessitates advanced computational tools to predict pharmacological and toxicological outcomes with higher accuracy. Traditional experimental approaches for evaluating drug efficacy, safety, and metabolism remain resource-intensive and limited in their ability to model polypharmacology or multi-organ toxicity. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale computational models of drug action and toxicity. The research will focus on simulating drug-receptor binding dynamics across diverse tissue environments, integrating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) parameters to predict organ-specific responses. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be employed to study time-dependent interactions between drugs and off-target proteins implicated in adverse reactions, while machine learning models trained on curated pharmacological and toxicological datasets will identify patterns in drug-induced cellular stress pathways. Key objectives include optimizing algorithms for parallel processing to handle large-scale simulations of drug diffusion across biological membranes and parameterizing population variability in drug metabolism using stochastic modeling. The computational framework will be validated against experimental data from in vitro toxicity assays and clinical pharmacokinetic studies. Successful implementation of this project is expected to yield predictive tools for identifying high-risk drug candidates early in development, reducing reliance on late-stage animal testing. Additionally, the models will provide mechanistic insights into idiosyncratic drug reactions and enable the rational design of safer therapeutic regimens. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance translational pharmacology through scalable, systems-level analyses of drug behavior, directly addressing the critical need for computational innovation in toxicology and therapeutic optimization.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drug interactions on biological systems and organisms and the sources, chemical properties, biological effects, and therapeutic uses of drugs. Includes instruction in pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, drug therapeutics, drug action, bodily responses to drug events, biochemical proliferation and differentiation, apoptosis, cell biology, medicinal chemistry, and studies of specific drugs and drug interactions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal dynamics of African-American community formation and migration across North America and the Caribbean from the late 18th to early 20th centuries. Traditional historiography has struggled to synthesize fragmented archival records—such as census data, Freedmen’s Bureau documents, and plantation ledgers—into cohesive narratives of population movement, economic adaptation, and resistance strategies. This research addresses this gap by applying computational methods to reconstruct migratory pathways, settlement patterns, and socio-economic networks at scale. Using geospatial machine learning models, natural language processing (NLP) for handwritten text recognition, and network analysis algorithms, the project will process digitized and born-digital datasets totaling approximately 15 TB, including maps, government records, and personal correspondence. Key objectives include identifying clusters of Black-led institutions (e.g., churches, mutual aid societies) and correlating their locations with historical events such as the Great Migration and post-emancipation land redistribution. HPC resources are critical for training custom NLP models to extract entity relationships from heterogeneous sources and for running agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about decision-making under systemic constraints. Anticipated outcomes include open-access interactive visualizations of migration corridors, a public database of reconstructed kinship networks, and peer-reviewed findings on how environmental factors and policy shifts influenced community resilience. By integrating computational rigor with archival scholarship, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in African-American history while centering marginalized voices in historical narratives. The scalability of the framework will also provide a template for future studies on transnational diasporic connections.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the design and analysis of civil infrastructure systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Civil engineering drafting and design increasingly rely on complex simulations to model structural integrity, environmental interactions, and material behavior under dynamic loads. However, current software tools for computer-aided drafting and design (CADD) often operate with simplified assumptions due to computational limitations, leading to conservative designs or overlooked failure modes in extreme scenarios. This research addresses these gaps by integrating high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) algorithms into CADD workflows to improve predictive accuracy and enable data-driven optimization. The project will focus on two key applications: (1) simulating the resilience of transportation infrastructure (e.g., bridges, tunnels) under combined seismic and hydrological stresses, and (2) automating the generative design of stormwater management systems using topology optimization and real-time environmental datasets. HPC resources will be critical for scaling parametric studies, training ML models on heterogeneous geospatial data, and resolving multi-physics interactions at millimeter-scale resolutions across large domains. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed memory parallelism to reduce simulation times from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include open-source CADD plugin modules for Ansys and AutoCAD Civil 3D, validated against physical scale models and field data, which will enable engineers to iteratively refine designs with reduced material waste and improved safety margins. By bridging the gap between traditional drafting practices and cutting-edge computational engineering, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for precision in civil infrastructure planning, particularly in climate-vulnerable regions. The project will also provide training materials to integrate HPC-driven design methodologies into civil engineering CADD curricula, fostering workforce readiness for next-generation infrastructure challenges.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of next-generation air traffic management systems through high-fidelity computational modeling of airspace operations under evolving environmental and operational constraints. Current air traffic simulations struggle to integrate real-time variables such as extreme weather disruptions, dynamic rerouting for reduced emissions, and the integration of uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) into shared airspace. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate air traffic flows, aircraft performance, and atmospheric interactions at unprecedented resolution. The model will combine computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of localized wake turbulence and weather impacts with agent-based modeling of system-wide traffic patterns, optimized via machine learning algorithms to balance efficiency, safety, and sustainability metrics. Key challenges include parallelization of heterogeneous physics models, real-time data assimilation from weather satellites and ADS-B trackers, and validation against historical air traffic control datasets. The HPC resources will enable simultaneous execution of 10,000+ agent-based aircraft trajectories with minute-scale meteorological updates across a continental-scale domain, requiring distributed memory architectures and GPU-accelerated CFD solvers. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for air traffic congestion under climate change scenarios, optimized routing algorithms to reduce sector-wide aviation emissions by an estimated 8-12%, and safety criteria for UAV integration in high-density corridors. Results will directly inform FAA modernization initiatives and open-source aviation simulation tools, providing a critical computational testbed for decarbonizing air transportation systems while maintaining capacity growth. This work underscores the necessity of HPC resources in bridging the gap between aircraft-level physics and system-level airspace optimization in an era of rapidly evolving aviation technologies.
cip_title: Aeronautics/ Aviation/ Aerospace Science and Technology, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of aviation and the aviation industry, including in-flight and ground support operations. Includes instruction in the technical, business, and general aspects of air transportation systems.

abstract: Current approaches to complex maxillofacial reconstruction often rely on static anatomical models, which fail to account for dynamic biomechanical forces during postoperative functional loading. This limitation contributes to suboptimal outcomes, including implant failure, delayed healing, and compromised occlusal function. To address this gap, we propose the development of a high-fidelity computational framework integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling with machine learning-driven optimization to predict and enhance surgical outcomes. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute finite element analysis (FEA) simulations derived from preoperative computed tomography (CT) scans, incorporating anisotropic bone properties, soft tissue viscoelasticity, and mastication force variability. Concurrently, a deep learning model trained on retrospective surgical outcomes data will iteratively refine implant positioning and fixation strategies. The computational workflow will dynamically couple biomechanical simulations with neural network-based optimization, requiring parallel processing capabilities to manage iterative analyses across >10,000 degrees of freedom. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for strain distribution patterns in reconstructed mandibles, an open-source surgical planning toolkit optimized for HPC architectures, and clinical guidelines for force-adaptive reconstruction protocols. This research will establish a novel paradigm for biomechanically intelligent oral surgery, potentially reducing revision rates by 30-40% in complex trauma and oncology cases while advancing computational methods for personalized surgical interventions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the diagnosis and intrusive and adjunctive treatment of diseases, injuries, and defects of the oral and maxillofacial regions, including functional and aesthetic aspects. Includes instruction in pharmacology, analgesia, anesthesia, anxiety control, surgical procedures and techniques, surgical instrumentation, exodontia, oral diseases and malfunctions, soft and hard tissue pathology, dentoalveolar surgery, infection management, and prosthetic implantation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize real-time monitoring and mitigation of airborne pollutants in urban environments, where complex interactions between emission sources, meteorological factors, and built infrastructure challenge existing pollution control systems. Current sensor networks often lack the spatial resolution and predictive capacity to inform timely interventions, while static maintenance schedules for monitoring equipment risk operational inefficiencies. To address these gaps, we propose integrating high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with machine learning (ML) models to predict pollutant dispersion patterns and dynamically optimize sensor placement, calibration, and maintenance protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve large-scale 3D urban airflow simulations at meter-scale resolution, capturing turbulence and pollutant transport mechanisms across diverse weather scenarios. Parallelized CFD outputs will train ML algorithms to correlate real-time sensor data with predicted emission hotspots, enabling adaptive network reconfiguration. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess failure risks across sensor nodes under varying environmental conditions, informing predictive maintenance schedules to minimize downtime. The computational pipeline will be validated against field data from pilot sites, including particulate matter and NO2 measurements. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolset for municipalities to enhance monitoring accuracy, reduce operational costs, and prioritize mitigation efforts in high-impact zones. By bridging high-fidelity environmental modeling with infrastructure management strategies, this work aims to advance resilient pollution control systems that proactively address public health risks while maintaining compliance with evolving air quality standards. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the iterative simulation workloads, ML training processes, and uncertainty quantification analyses central to this effort.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using indoor and outdoor environmental pollution control systems. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation models for boutique hotel networks using high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of real-time demand forecasting in hyper-seasonal tourism markets. Traditional revenue management systems struggle to integrate real-time data streams—such as social media sentiment, localized event triggers, and climate anomalies—with operational constraints like staff scheduling and energy consumption patterns. The computational complexity of modeling these multidimensional variables at scale requires advanced parallel processing capabilities. We propose developing an adaptive machine learning framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of tourist decision-making behaviors with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate pricing strategies across heterogeneous market conditions. The HPC infrastructure will enable simultaneous processing of terabyte-scale datasets from property management systems, IoT sensors, and third-party booking platforms, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in demand projections. Key innovations include spatial-temporal graph neural networks to capture cross-property demand spillover effects and a federated learning architecture to preserve data privacy across independent hotel operators. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of reducing revenue leakage by 12-18% in pilot implementations, with particular significance for small-to-midsize hospitality businesses competing in algorithmically dominated markets. The computational workflows will be containerized for cloud deployment, creating a scalable template for ethical AI adoption in tourism micro-enterprises. This interdisciplinary approach bridges operations research, behavioral economics, and computational social science, advancing resource optimization paradigms beyond conventional yield management frameworks.
cip_title: Tourism and Travel Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide direct retail services to hotel and motel clients and customers in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in the principles of hotel/motel operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, and basic office management.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical operational and decision-making challenges in correctional facility management through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Correctional systems face complex, dynamic problems, including overcrowding, resource allocation inefficiencies, and risk prediction for inmate behavior, yet traditional analytical tools often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between institutional policies, environmental factors, and human dynamics. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution agent-based simulation framework to model facility operations, inmate population dynamics, and staff-inmate interactions. The framework will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including historical incident reports, staffing patterns, and facility infrastructure metrics—to simulate scenarios such as contagion spread during health crises, resource strain during intake surges, and the cascading effects of policy changes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps, optimize hyperparameters for machine learning components embedded in agent decision trees, and validate models against real-world operational data. Computational outcomes will be paired with interpretability algorithms to identify leverage points for improving safety, reducing costs, and mitigating systemic risks. Expected deliverables include an open-source simulation toolkit tailored for corrections administrators, predictive models for incident hot-spot mapping, and evidence-based recommendations for adaptive staffing protocols. By bridging computational social science, operations research, and correctional theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven corrections management while adhering to ethical guidelines for algorithmic transparency and bias mitigation. The project’s computational demands—particularly its need for parallelized simulations across thousands of agents and multi-year temporal horizons—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve practical scalability and real-world relevance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study the theories and principles, of correctional science and to function as professional corrections officers and other workers in public and/or private incarceration facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the computational modeling of dynamic learning ecosystems in hybrid educational environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex interactions between digital platforms, student behavioral data, and institutional resource allocation. Traditional educational research often focuses on isolated variables (e.g., curriculum efficacy or engagement metrics), but emerging hybrid models—blending in-person, online, and AI-mediated interactions—require systems-level approaches to understand emergent patterns and inefficiencies. The research problem centers on mapping how heterogeneous data streams (e.g., LMS usage patterns, real-time collaboration metrics, and biometric feedback from wearable devices) coalesce into transient "learning ecologies" that influence outcomes. Current tools lack the capacity to process multimodal, high-frequency datasets while simulating macro-scale educational dynamics. The proposed computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, network analysis, and machine learning to create a scalable simulation framework. Agent-based models will represent students, instructors, and digital tools as interacting entities, with parameters derived from anonymized datasets spanning 15 institutional partners. Network analyses will identify critical junctures where resource bottlenecks (e.g., uneven access to AI tutors or asynchronous content delays) disproportionately affect marginalized subgroups. Deep learning architectures will be trained on temporal sequences of interaction logs to predict systemic stress points under varying resource distribution policies. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing simulations across diverse demographic and infrastructural scenarios, enabling real-time sensitivity analyses for interventions. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating equity-focused resource allocation in hybrid education, (2) evidence-based thresholds for scaling digital supports in under-resourced contexts, and (3) dynamic visualizations of how micro-level interactions propagate to institutional outcomes. By bridging computational social science and educational theory, this work aims to advance decision-making frameworks for adaptive, ethically grounded resource distribution in increasingly complex learning environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory, practice, organization of, and public policies in education. Includes instruction in learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources into modern power grids has introduced unprecedented challenges in maintaining dynamic stability, particularly during transient events such as fault-induced delayed voltage recovery (FIDVR) or rapid frequency deviations. Traditional grid models, which rely on static assumptions and decoupled analyses of electromechanical and electromagnetic phenomena, are insufficient to capture the complex, multi-timescale interactions between inverter-based resources, legacy synchronous generators, and emerging grid-forming technologies. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL)-validated computational framework to simulate power system dynamics at unprecedented resolution, integrating device-level semiconductor switching behaviors with grid-scale transient stability models. The research will employ parallelized differential-algebraic equation solvers optimized for heterogeneous computing architectures to concurrently resolve nanosecond-scale power electronics transitions and second-scale machine dynamics. Machine learning techniques will be applied to surrogate modeling of component-level behaviors, enabling real-time predictive stability assessment without sacrificing physical interpretability. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing resources for three primary tasks: (1) massively parallel time-domain simulations of 10,000+ bus systems with mixed AC/DC topologies, (2) training physics-informed neural networks on petascale datasets generated by parametric sweeps of renewable penetration scenarios, and (3) deployment of digital twins for contingency analysis through cloud-HPC hybrid architectures. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible library of validated component models, adaptive protection coordination algorithms for hybrid grids, and stability margin quantification metrics that account for multi-energy coupling effects. This work aims to provide grid operators with computationally tractable tools for maintaining reliability in systems with >80% renewable generation, directly supporting decarbonization targets while addressing a critical gap in current power plant engineering capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan electrical systems and modify existing electrical systems that generate and use large amounts of electricity required for distribution networks that are economical, safe, and functional. Includes instruction in alternative/renewable energy systems; calculus; circuit analysis; electrical power systems and industry practices; electrical system design; microprocessor architecture; motor control systems; power electronics operation, planning and protection; programmable logic controllers; and project management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variation across French dialects and creoles, with a focus on under-resourced varieties such as Caribbean Creoles and Acadian French. The research problem centers on the challenges of modeling linguistic evolution and contact phenomena in these varieties, which involve complex, multidimensional data spanning historical texts, contemporary speech corpora, and sociolinguistic metadata. Traditional comparative methods struggle to systematically analyze such datasets due to their scale, heterogeneity, and the non-linear interactions between linguistic features over time. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and regional French variants, machine learning classifiers to detect patterns of language contact, and acoustic-phonetic modeling to quantify shifts in pronunciation. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on distributed textual corpora (15th–21st centuries), parallelizing comparative analyses across 20+ dialects/creoles, and running agent-based simulations of language change scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) the first unified digital atlas mapping phonetic convergence between Metropolitan French and its creoles, (2) probabilistic models identifying syntactic innovations driven by language contact in North American French varieties, and (3) open-access tools for automated parsing of non-standard French orthographies. By enabling the synthesis of fragmented regional datasets, this work will advance theoretical understanding of dialect formation in Francophone contexts while supporting preservation initiatives for endangered varieties. The computational frameworks developed will also provide a template for similar studies in other under-documented language families.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the French language and related dialects and creoles. Includes instruction in philology; Metropolitan French; Canadian French; African and Caribbean Creoles; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the early detection and management of complex ophthalmic conditions, including glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration. Current diagnostic workflows in optometric and ophthalmic support services face challenges in integrating heterogeneous data sources—such as high-resolution retinal imaging, optical coherence tomography (OCT), and patient-specific biomarkers—into unified predictive models. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning algorithms capable of synthesizing large-scale clinical datasets. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale ophthalmic imaging datasets to extract spatially resolved features, (2) development of graph neural networks to model disease progression pathways using longitudinal patient data, and (3) uncertainty quantification to assess model robustness across diverse demographic populations. The computational pipeline will utilize GPU-accelerated containers for scalable inference, coupled with distributed data storage solutions to manage multi-institutional collaborations. Successful implementation is expected to yield validated predictive tools that identify subclinical disease signatures up to 12 months earlier than current clinical standards, with particular emphasis on optimizing resource-constrained screening environments. By enabling rapid reanalysis of imaging archives through on-demand HPC scaling, this work aims to establish new protocols for personalized risk stratification in optometric practice. Outcomes will be disseminated as open-source modules compatible with common electronic health record systems, directly supporting allied health professionals in clinical decision-making. The requested computing resources are critical for maintaining model fidelity across the projected 250,000+ patient datasets while adhering to HIPAA-compliant federated learning frameworks. This project bridges computational innovation with ophthalmic support services, offering transformative potential for preventive eye care delivery.
cip_title: Ophthalmic and Optometric Support Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ophthalmic and optometric support services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational philological research on the evolution of Hebrew across its historical stages and regional dialects. A central challenge in Hebrew linguistics lies in systematically analyzing diachronic linguistic shifts and synchronic dialect variations, particularly given the morphological complexity of Hebrew and the fragmented nature of textual corpora spanning ancient to modern periods. Traditional manual methods struggle to process large, heterogeneous datasets, including digitized Biblical manuscripts, Rabbinic commentaries, and Modern Hebrew speech corpora. The proposed research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to model phonetic, morphological, and syntactic changes across three key phases: Biblical Hebrew (including transitional Post-Exilic forms), Rabbinic Medieval Hebrew, and contemporary Israeli Hebrew. Computational workflows will be developed to train transformer-based models on annotated corpora, with custom tokenization strategies addressing non-standardized orthographies in historical texts. Parallelized morphological parsers will analyze inflectional patterns across dialects, while syntactic dependency treebanks will be computationally aligned to trace grammatical innovations. HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale multilingual datasets, optimizing neural architectures through hyperparameter tuning, and running comparative analyses across temporal-spatial axes. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable computational framework for diachronic Hebrew analysis, 2) quantitative models of lexical and grammatical change trajectories, and 3) open-access tools for automated variant detection in understudied regional dialects. This work will provide novel insights into language contact phenomena, the impact of technological modernization on Hebrew’s semantic expansion, and methodological innovations for computational Semitic linguistics. By bridging traditional philology with advanced NLP, the project aims to establish new infrastructure for data-driven humanities research while addressing critical gaps in understanding Hebrew’s dynamic adaptation across millennia.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hebrew language. Includes instruction in philology; Biblical Hebrew (including Pre- and Post-Exilic scripts); Modern Hebrew; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Agricultural extension services face increasing demands to provide timely, data-driven recommendations to farmers amidst complex challenges such as evolving pest dynamics, climate variability, and market shifts. Current decision-support tools often lack the computational capacity to integrate real-time agricultural datasets—including soil health metrics, pest surveillance data, satellite imagery, and farm management records—at scales necessary for hyper-localized guidance. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a machine learning framework for predictive modeling of region-specific crop management strategies. The research will focus on optimizing pest control and yield prediction by training ensemble models on multi-modal datasets spanning 10+ years of agronomic records from cooperating farms, weather station networks, and drone-captured field imagery. Computational workflows will include GPU-accelerated neural networks for image-based pest identification, agent-based simulations of pest population dynamics under climate scenarios, and Bayesian optimization to tailor irrigation and fertilizer schedules. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce model training times from weeks to days, enabling iterative testing of management strategies against stochastic variables. Outcomes will include open-source tools for extension agents to generate dynamic recommendations via user-friendly dashboards, validated through on-farm trials in collaboration with regional producer networks. This work addresses critical gaps in scalable, adaptive precision agriculture tools, with potential to enhance the responsiveness of extension services to localized agricultural challenges while reducing economic and environmental risks for stakeholders. The computational infrastructure will also support future integration of real-time sensor data streams, fostering long-term innovation in agricultural education and decision-support systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide referral, consulting, technical assistance, and educational services to gardeners, farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and other organizations. Includes instruction in basic agricultural sciences, agricultural business operations, pest control, adult education methods, public relations, applicable state laws and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: Sustainable forest management requires balancing timber production with ecosystem preservation, yet current decision-making tools lack the resolution to optimize this balance under climate change pressures. This project proposes developing a computational framework to model forest growth, harvest impacts, and regeneration dynamics across spatial scales from individual stands to regional landscapes. The research will integrate multi-temporal LiDAR data, soil moisture sensors, and historical growth records to parameterize species-specific growth models using machine learning techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations of alternative management scenarios, including variable-density thinning, harvest rotation schedules, and climate adaptation strategies. Agent-based modeling will simulate microsite conditions affecting tree mortality and regeneration success, while graph neural networks will predict downstream impacts on wood fiber quality and processing yields. The computational workflow will quantify tradeoffs between carbon sequestration potential, biodiversity metrics, and economic returns under different management regimes. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system that enables forest managers to visualize 3D stand projections, optimize equipment deployment patterns, and assess climate resilience thresholds. By processing petabytes of remote sensing data and running millions of parameter combinations, the HPC implementation will overcome current limitations in spatial granularity and temporal forecasting common in conventional forestry models. This work directly advances precision forestry capabilities while addressing core challenges in the Forest Resources Production and Management curriculum, particularly regarding sustainable yield optimization and adaptive management. Results will inform regional forest action plans and provide training datasets for industrial harvesting automation systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of forestry principles to the production, harvesting, and processing of forest resources and that prepares individuals to perform associated technical and managerial functions. Includes instruction in forest production and utilization, industrial forestry, agroforestry, transplantation, timber harvesting, selection and identification of trees, processing technologies and systems, equipment operations and maintenance, and related management skills.

abstract: Soil systems are dynamic interfaces where complex chemical and microbiological interactions govern nutrient cycling, organic matter decomposition, and carbon sequestration. Current models often treat soil chemistry and microbial community dynamics in isolation, limiting predictive accuracy for soil health under changing agricultural practices and climate conditions. This project seeks to address this gap by developing an integrated, multiscale computational framework to simulate coupled biogeochemical and microbial processes in soil ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of soil environments, parameterize reaction networks involving organic-inorganic colloids and microbial metabolisms, and quantify feedbacks between soil microbiota and plant-root exudates. We propose a hybrid modeling approach combining molecular dynamics simulations of mineral-organic interactions, agent-based microbial community models, and reactive transport algorithms to capture processes from nanometer to field scales. Machine learning will augment these simulations by assimilating experimental data from soil metagenomics, spectroscopy, and gas flux measurements. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers and GPU acceleration to manage the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and stochastic microbial behaviors. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking soil microbiome composition to carbon stabilization efficiency, nitrogen leaching rates, and phosphorus bioavailability under varying management practices. These tools will advance precision soil management strategies to optimize crop productivity while minimizing fertilizer inputs and greenhouse gas emissions. The resulting open-source software will provide a scalable platform for interdisciplinary soil research, bridging molecular-scale mechanisms to ecosystem-scale outcomes. By elucidating synergies between soil chemistry and microbiology, this work aims to inform sustainable agricultural systems resilient to environmental stressors.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and microbiological theories and methods (in combination) to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instructional combination of microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: The increasing demand for advanced materials with tailored mechanical and thermal properties necessitates a fundamental understanding of defect dynamics and microstructure evolution under extreme conditions. This project seeks to develop predictive multiscale models to unravel the interplay between dislocations, grain boundaries, and phase transformations in next-generation high-entropy alloys (HEAs) subjected to high-strain-rate deformation and elevated temperatures. Current experimental techniques face limitations in resolving atomic-scale mechanisms during dynamic loading, while existing computational approaches lack the fidelity to bridge quantum-accurate energetics with mesoscale microstructural responses. To address this, we propose an integrated workflow combining large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations parameterized by density functional theory (DFT) calculations and phase-field crystal (PFC) modeling. The MD component will employ machine learning-accelerated interatomic potentials to simulate defect nucleation and propagation across >10^8-atom systems, while DFT workflows will quantify stacking fault energies and interfacial bonding characteristics critical for HEA design. The PFC models will extend these insights to mesoscale microstructural evolution under thermomechanical stress. This research requires high-performance computing resources to manage the extreme concurrency of billion-atom MD trajectories, iterative DFT relaxations across thousands of alloy configurations, and GPU-accelerated phase-field solvers. Expected outcomes include validated structure-property relationships for HEAs, predictive frameworks for dislocation-mediated plasticity in multiphase systems, and open-source tools for microstructure-sensitive materials design. The results will directly inform alloy processing strategies for applications in extreme environments, including advanced manufacturing tools and high-efficiency energy systems. By integrating quantum-to-continuum modeling paradigms on HPC infrastructure, this work aims to establish a computational foundation for accelerating the discovery of deformation-resistant materials beyond empirical trial-and-error approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical, engineering and scientific principles such as internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, and compound materials, to the analysis, design, evaluation, industrial applications, and production of materials a in a wide variety of settings.

abstract: The early detection of cellular abnormalities through cytopathological analysis is critical for diagnosing malignancies and precancerous conditions, yet manual screening remains labor-intensive and subject to diagnostic variability. This project proposes the development of a scalable, deep learning-driven computational framework to automate the identification of subtle cytomorphological features associated with early-stage neoplasms in liquid-based cytology specimens. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to process and analyze high-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs) of cervical, urinary, and serous effusion samples, which present heterogeneous cellularity and complex staining artifacts that challenge conventional algorithms. The computational workflow will integrate patch-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for nucleus segmentation and feature extraction, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial relationships among cell clusters, and transformer architectures to capture long-range dependencies in large WSIs. A novel self-supervised pretraining strategy will be implemented using unlabeled historical datasets (50,000+ slides) to improve model generalizability across specimen types and staining protocols. Validation will involve benchmarking against a curated dataset of 5,000 expert-annotated slides with ground-truth histopathological correlations. The HPC environment is essential for training memory-intensive models on multi-terabyte imaging data while maintaining slide-level context through distributed parallel processing. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for quantitative cytomorphometric profiling, capable of flagging rare aberrant cells with 95% sensitivity at clinically relevant specificity thresholds. By establishing computational correlates of diagnostic uncertainty, this tool could refine triage protocols for pathologist review, reduce inter-observer variability, and enable longitudinal analysis of cellular evolution in high-risk patients. The project bridges computational pathology with clinical cytotechnology practice, advancing precision diagnostics through scalable AI/ML infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with pathologists to detect changes in body cells that may indicate, and permit diagnosis of, the early development of cancers and other diseases. Includes instruction in biochemistry, microbiology, applied mathematics, microscopy, slide preparation, identification of cellular structures and abnormalities, and laboratory procedures and safety.

abstract: The integration of multi-omics data and predictive computational modeling has emerged as a critical tool for advancing precision medicine, yet the analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous clinical datasets remains a bottleneck due to computational limitations. This project seeks to address this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning models capable of predicting patient-specific therapeutic responses in oncology. The research focuses on glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), a highly aggressive brain cancer with significant interpatient variability in treatment outcomes. Current approaches often rely on static genomic profiling, which fails to account for dynamic tumor microenvironment interactions or longitudinal treatment effects. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and real-world clinical data to model tumor evolution and drug sensitivity. Deep neural networks and ensemble methods will be trained on multi-institutional datasets to predict resistance mechanisms and optimize combination therapies. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabytes of genomic data, running parallelized parameter optimization for neural architectures, and performing in silico simulations of treatment scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for merging heterogeneous clinical and omics data, (2) validated predictive models of GBM progression under therapy, and (3) open-source computational tools for adaptive treatment personalization. By enabling rapid iteration of complex models across large cohorts, this work will directly inform prospective clinical trials investigating adaptive immunotherapy regimens. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated training, high-memory nodes for single-cell data analysis, and secure storage for sensitive patient data. This project bridges computational innovation and clinical translation, advancing capabilities in precision oncology while establishing a framework extendable to other complex malignancies.
cip_title: Medical Clinical Sciences/ Graduate Medical Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in medical clinical sciences or graduate medical studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive optimization framework for sustainable capacity management in integrated resort ecosystems. The research addresses the critical challenge of balancing operational efficiency, guest satisfaction, and environmental sustainability in large-scale resort operations—a complex systems problem involving dynamic interactions between hospitality services, recreational infrastructure, and natural resource constraints. Current analytical approaches in resort management lack the computational power to model real-time, multi-objective decision-making across the full spectrum of resort operations, from energy-intensive amenities (e.g., climate-controlled facilities, water parks) to perishable service inventories (e.g., spa bookings, guided tours). The proposed computational methodology combines agent-based modeling of guest behavior patterns with parallelized multi-objective optimization algorithms to simulate operational scenarios at resort-scale resolution. By integrating heterogeneous data streams—including IoT sensor networks, weather forecasts, and real-time booking systems—the framework will optimize staffing schedules, energy allocation, and facility utilization under variable demand conditions. Key technical challenges involve developing hybrid machine learning architectures to predict guest flow patterns and implementing GPU-accelerated constraint solvers for rapid scenario evaluation. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of reducing operational carbon footprints by 15-20% while maintaining service quality benchmarks, as well as novel metrics for quantifying sustainability-performance tradeoffs in resort operations. The computational intensity of simulating millions of daily guest interactions across diverse facility types necessitates HPC resources, particularly for memory-intensive Monte Carlo simulations of peak-season scenarios and evolutionary algorithm training across multi-node clusters. This research fills a critical gap in applied computational sustainability for the hospitality sector, offering both methodological advances in complex system optimization and practical tools for resort operators navigating climate-conscious operational challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market comprehensive vacation facilities and services and related products. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, hotel/motel management, restaurant and food services management, facilities planning, leisure studies, recreation administration, marketing, recreation equipment and grounds operations and maintenance, business finance, insurance and taxation, event management and guest services, personnel management, travel and logistics management, safety and health services, professional standards and ethics, and applications to specific vacation types and locations.

abstract: The emergence of horizontal gene transfer (HGT) as a dominant driver of microbial adaptation and eukaryotic genome evolution presents unresolved questions about its regulatory dynamics in multispecies communities. While HGT is well-characterized in isolated systems, the interplay between genetic exchange, epigenetic regulation, and host-symbiont interactions in complex microbiomes remains poorly understood. This project seeks to model HGT networks across diverse microbial and eukaryotic systems using genome-scale metabolic reconstructions and agent-based simulations. Our computational framework will integrate pan-genomic datasets from archaea, bacteria, and protists to parameterize context-dependent transfer probabilities, incorporating epigenetic modifiers and host defense mechanisms as dynamic constraints. High-performance computing resources are essential to simulate population-scale genomic interactions across 10^4-10^6 microbial cells with variable plasmid/viral loads, while tracking emergent patterns of gene flux. The proposed work will leverage existing genomic libraries from marine biofilm and rhizosphere communities to validate models against observed transfer rates. Key deliverables include (1) a probabilistic atlas of HGT hotspots across phylogenetic boundaries, (2) mechanistic insights into how eukaryotic nuclear pore complexes filter incoming prokaryotic DNA, and (3) predictive models of how nutrient stress modulates epigenetic suppression of mobile elements. These outcomes will advance fundamental understanding of cross-kingdom genetic integration while addressing practical challenges in managing antibiotic resistance dissemination. By mapping the rules governing genetic material exchange at microbial-eukaryotic interfaces, this work directly aligns with the program’s focus on parasitic/symbiotic interactions and comparative genomics. The requested GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory allocations will enable iterative simulations at biologically relevant scales, overcoming current limitations in modeling real-world genetic networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of viruses, infectious agents, organelles, nuclear genomes, eubacteria, archaebacteria, and eukaryotic organisms. Includes instruction in molecular genetics and evolution, parasitic and symbiotic interaction at the genetic level, epigenetic phenomena, microbial interactions, and genomics.

abstract: Critical care nursing faces significant challenges in predicting patient deterioration and optimizing interventions due to the complexity of integrating real-time physiological data, clinical histories, and heterogeneous care protocols. Current predictive models in intensive care settings often lack the computational power to process multimodal data streams—including high-frequency vital sign recordings, imaging, laboratory results, and clinician notes—at the scale and speed required for timely decision-making. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework to analyze these multidimensional datasets, with the goal of identifying early warning signals of clinical decline and recommending personalized interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models, such as transformer-based architectures and temporal convolutional networks, on retrospective electronic health records from adult, neonatal, and pediatric critical care units. Key computational challenges include managing irregularly sampled time-series data, addressing class imbalance in rare adverse events, and ensuring model interpretability for clinical adoption. By parallelizing hyperparameter optimization and enabling large-batch training across GPU nodes, HPC infrastructure will accelerate model development and validation. Expected outcomes include a deployable predictive tool for real-time risk stratification, validated against clinician judgments, and a publicly accessible benchmark dataset for critical care analytics. This work aims to reduce unplanned transitions to life support, improve resource allocation in ICUs, and establish scalable computational methods for future research in critical care nursing. The integration of HPC-driven analytics with clinical expertise has the potential to advance evidence-based practice, reduce cognitive burden on care teams, and ultimately improve survival rates in high-acuity populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide specialized care to patients with life-threatening problems, including those in intensive care facilities and on life support. Includes instruction in adult, neonatal, and pediatric critical care; technical skills; patient monitoring and assessment; normal and abnormal readings; and troubleshooting.

abstract: The study of strongly correlated electron systems in condensed matter physics presents a fundamental challenge due to the complex interplay of quantum fluctuations, spin-orbit coupling, and electron-electron interactions. These systems exhibit emergent phenomena such as unconventional superconductivity, quantum spin liquids, and non-Fermi liquid behavior, which defy conventional theoretical frameworks. Current computational limitations restrict the exploration of realistic three-dimensional models with multi-orbital interactions, hindering progress in understanding materials like high-Tc cuprates, heavy fermion compounds, and twisted bilayer graphene. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale numerical simulations of correlated electron systems using advanced quantum many-body techniques. The computational approach combines dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) with tensor network methods to resolve finite-size effects and access low-temperature regimes. Exact diagonalization and quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations will be employed to study phase diagrams under varying doping, strain, and magnetic field conditions, with explicit treatment of spin-orbit coupling and orbital hybridization. The simulations will utilize open-source software packages, including TRIQS and ALPS, optimized for parallel architectures. Key objectives include identifying universal signatures of quantum criticality in spectral functions, quantifying the role of orbital selectivity in nematic transitions, and mapping the stability of superconducting phases against disorder. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations at unprecedented system sizes (up to 10^4 lattice sites) and energy resolution (sub-meV scales), directly addressing discrepancies between experimental observations and existing theoretical predictions. Outcomes will provide mechanistic insights into the design of robust quantum materials and inform experimental efforts to synthesize next-generation superconductors and topological states. By bridging the gap between model Hamiltonians and real material systems, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities in condensed matter physics while fostering open data sharing through a curated repository of simulation results.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of macroscopic physical phenomena and properties that arise from basic microscopic interactions. Includes instruction in low-temperature and solid-state physics, x-ray physics, liquids and soft materials, including the study of semiconductors, metals, superliquids, magnets, superconductors, glasses, gels, polymers, colloids, neural networks, and macromolecules.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing cross-border digital financial transactions, with a focus on systemic risks posed by algorithmic tax optimization strategies employed by multinational enterprises (MNEs). The research addresses a critical gap in international tax law: the lack of computational tools to model the dynamic interplay between rapidly advancing financial technologies, opaque tax arbitrage mechanisms, and heterogeneous national regulatory regimes. Traditional legal analysis struggles to quantify the cascading effects of automated profit-shifting algorithms or predict emergent vulnerabilities in global tax governance systems. To bridge this gap, the project will develop agent-based models simulating MNE decision-making under competing jurisdictional rules, paired with natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze regulatory texts from 150+ national tax authorities and international agreements. The computational framework will integrate game-theoretic representations of corporate strategic behavior, temporal network analysis of treaty shopping patterns, and probabilistic assessments of audit outcomes under machine learning-enhanced compliance monitoring systems. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for identifying high-risk tax avoidance pathways in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems, stress-test scenarios for proposed global minimum tax architectures, and a novel taxonomy of regulatory conflicts arising from AI-driven transfer pricing models. By combining legal domain expertise with large-scale computational simulations, this work aims to produce actionable insights for policymakers addressing tax base erosion while maintaining innovation incentives in digital commerce. The HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets of corporate financial disclosures, legal rulings, and transactional blockchain records, as well as for running complex multi-jurisdictional simulations requiring parallelized optimization algorithms and real-time sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations.
cip_title: International Business, Trade, and Tax Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing transnational business and commercial practices, including the specialized tax law related to international financial transactions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research on the historical phonology and morphological evolution of Sanskrit and Prakrit languages. The research problem centers on tracing systematic sound changes and morphological shifts across Vedic Sanskrit, Classical Sanskrit, and early Prakrits—a process critical to understanding the diversification of Indo-Aryan languages and their relationship to broader Indo-European developments. Traditional comparative methods, limited by manual analysis of fragmented textual corpora, struggle to address the combinatorial complexity of phonetic environments and intersecting linguistic variables. To overcome these constraints, we propose a computational workflow integrating rule-based phonological modeling, probabilistic alignment algorithms, and phylogenetic inference. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of digitized corpora (ca. 10 million lexical tokens across 150+ texts) through customized pipelines that automate grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, apply ordered sound change rules under varying dialectal parameters, and generate probabilistic trees of linguistic divergence. Validation will employ attested historical changes documented in śikṣā (phonetic) treatises and Pāṇinian grammatical literature. Expected outcomes include 1) a probabilistic model of Prakritization processes accounting for geographic and register-based variation, 2) quantitative revisions to existing periodizations of Sanskrit-Prakrit differentiation, and 3) an open-source toolkit for simulating sound change cascades in Indo-Aryan philology. By bridging computational methods with traditional philological scholarship, this work aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing linguistic evolution in under-resourced ancient languages while providing empirical insights into the prehistoric dialect geography of South Asia.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Sanskrit and Classical Indian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Sanskrit and related ancient and classical Indo-Aryan languages. Includes instruction in Vedic and Classical Sanskrit, Pali and other Prakrits, and the historical development of Indo-Aryan languages and their relation to Indo-European languages such as Greek, Latin and the Baltic languages.

abstract: The safe and efficient delivery of medications in clinical settings remains a critical challenge, with systemic inefficiencies, medication errors, and operational bottlenecks contributing to patient harm and increased healthcare costs. This project seeks to optimize medication systems through computational modeling of large-scale clinical workflows, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex operational dynamics and simulate interventions. The research focuses on integrating electronic health record (EHR) data, pharmacy dispensing logs, and real-time sensor data from automated dispensing cabinets to build multi-agent simulation models that replicate medication distribution processes across hospital networks. A key computational challenge involves scaling these models to represent diverse clinical scenarios—spanning emergency departments, inpatient units, and outpatient pharmacies—while accounting for stochastic variables such as patient arrival patterns, staff workflows, and machine downtime. HPC resources are essential to run thousands of parallelized simulations using Monte Carlo methods, enabling the identification of high-risk failure points and the evaluation of targeted interventions (e.g., dynamic staffing algorithms, predictive inventory systems). Machine learning pipelines will further analyze historical error reports to prioritize computational experiments. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source optimization frameworks for medication operations, validated against retrospective EHR data from three partner health systems.
