By quantifying trade-offs between safety, cost, and throughput, this work aims to provide actionable guidelines for redesigning medication systems, with projected reductions in error rates (15–20%) and waste (10–15%) in pilot settings. The scale of data processing (>50 TB of structured and temporal healthcare data) and the need for real-time simulation of network-wide cascading effects necessitate access to clustered computing environments with GPU acceleration and large-memory nodes. This project bridges computational engineering and clinical operations, offering a replicable methodology for advancing evidence-based improvements in medication management.
cip_definition: Research focused on Medication Systems and Operations

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of the interplay between dark matter, baryonic physics, and relativistic effects in the formation and evolution of galaxy clusters, the largest gravitationally bound structures in the universe. Despite their importance as cosmological probes, current simulations struggle to resolve the multiscale physics governing intracluster plasma, star formation feedback, and relativistic turbulence in cluster cores. This work will employ high-resolution cosmological simulations combining N-body, magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), and non-equilibrium radiation transfer to model the self-consistent co-evolution of dark matter halos and baryonic components across 12 orders of magnitude in mass. The simulations will utilize a novel adaptive mesh refinement code optimized for GPU-accelerated exascale architectures, incorporating relativistic corrections to plasma kinetics and radiation fields in curved spacetime. Key challenges include tracking the thermal history of the intracluster medium under feedback from active galactic nuclei, modeling the impact of primordial magnetic fields on large-scale structure, and calibrating synthetic observables against multiwavelength data from Chandra, Euclid, and CMB-S4. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable unprecedented spatial resolution (<100 pc in cluster cores) while maintaining cosmological volume (1 Gpc³), requiring 2.5 million core-hours and 200 TB of memory-optimized storage. Expected outcomes include (1) improved constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections from small-scale structure comparisons, (2) predictions for X-ray polarization signatures of turbulent dynamos in merging clusters, and (3) open-source release of synthetic sky catalogs to support observational campaigns. By bridging numerical relativity, plasma astrophysics, and observational cosmology, this work will critically inform next-generation surveys probing cosmic acceleration and large-scale structure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical, observational, and numerical study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena of the universe on a large scale. Includes instruction in clusters of galaxies, the cosmic microwave background, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to advance early intervention strategies for neurodevelopmental vulnerability in infants and toddlers by modeling complex interactions between genetic, neurobiological, and environmental factors. Current mental health services for young children lack predictive tools to identify subtle, pre-symptomatic risks for social-emotional dysregulation, particularly in cases where developmental trajectories diverge from population norms without clear clinical markers. The research problem centers on integrating high-dimensional datasets—including functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings of cortical activation, polygenic risk scores, and longitudinal caregiver-child interaction videos—to build dynamic models of neural-behavioral adaptation. A core computational challenge involves analyzing time-varying, multimodal data streams at scale while accounting for heterogeneities in developmental pacing and environmental inputs. The proposed approach combines graph neural networks to model brain-behavior connectivity patterns with transformer-based architectures for temporal sequence prediction, trained on a novel corpus of infant neurodevelopmental data. High-performance computing resources are essential to process raw fNIRS signals (sampled at 10Hz across 128 channels), genomic variant matrices (>500,000 SNPs), and frame-level video features (30fps) within unified embedding spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for identifying latent risk signatures up to 18 months before behavioral symptoms emerge, (2) validated computational markers of caregiver responsiveness that mediate neurodevelopmental outcomes, and (3) open-source tools for simulating intervention impacts via counterfactual reinforcement learning. By enabling real-time analysis of developmental cascades across biological and behavioral timescales, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for personalized prevention strategies in infant mental health. The requested resources will support distributed training of multi-modal architectures across GPU nodes, large-scale hyperparameter optimization for time-series models, and secure processing of protected health data through containerized workflows.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide mental health services to infants, toddlers, and preschoolers and their families. Includes instruction in developmental psychology, cognitive and biological development, social and emotional development, research methods, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize pedagogical strategies for cosmetology and barbering education, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in instructor training efficacy. Traditional cosmetology pedagogy relies heavily on experiential learning, yet there is limited quantitative understanding of how instructional techniques—such as curriculum sequencing, adaptive feedback systems, or multimodal teaching aids—affect skill acquisition across diverse student cohorts. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven tools to simulate classroom dynamics, predict learning outcomes, and personalize instructor training programs at scale. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate virtual classrooms, incorporating variables such as student learning styles, skill progression rates, and instructional intervention timing. High-fidelity simulations will integrate real-world datasets from cosmetology schools, including performance metrics, demographic factors, and psychomotor skill assessments. Machine learning algorithms will then analyze simulation outputs to identify optimal teaching strategies under varying constraints, such as class size or hybrid learning environments. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the complexity of modeling thousands of concurrent agent interactions and the iterative optimization required for personalized training protocols. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for instructor effectiveness, an open-access toolkit for curriculum design, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive teaching in tactile skill domains. By bridging computational analytics with cosmetology education, this work aims to elevate instructional standards, reduce attrition rates, and enhance licensure preparedness in a field critical to vocational workforce development. The interdisciplinary approach—merging education theory, behavioral modeling, and high-performance computing—establishes a novel paradigm for technical pedagogy research beyond traditional STEM domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares cosmetologists, barbers, stylists, nail technicians, and other grooming specialists to teach their specializations in licensed and accredited schools of cosmetology and barbering, and to prepare for licensure as instructors.  Includes instruction in cosmetology arts and sciences teaching principles; student learning styles; professional curricula development; instructional planning; instructional methods and aids; student counseling and career assistance; test development; and classroom/clinic management.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance and novel viral pathogens in animal populations presents significant challenges to veterinary medicine and public health. Traditional laboratory techniques often lack the resolution to unravel complex host-microbe interactions at scale, necessitating advanced computational approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underpinning pathogen virulence, transmission dynamics, and host immune evasion in agriculturally and companionally relevant species. Using multi-omics integration, we will analyze genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from clinically significant bacterial and viral pathogens, including avian influenza strains and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural variations in key virulence factors under selective pressure from antimicrobial agents. Epidemiological modeling powered by agent-based frameworks will simulate outbreak scenarios across diverse animal populations. The computational pipeline will employ machine learning algorithms to identify conserved antigenic epitopes for vaccine development and predict resistance gene transfer probabilities. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, improved risk assessment models for zoonotic spillover events, and optimized vaccination protocols tailored to specific livestock production systems. By integrating large-scale data analytics with mechanistic modeling, this research aims to advance translational veterinary medicine while informing One Health initiatives at the animal-human-environment interface. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of sequencing data, executing computationally intensive simulations, and training predictive models—tasks infeasible with standard laboratory infrastructure. This work will directly contribute to mitigating antimicrobial resistance, enhancing animal welfare, and reducing economic losses in agricultural systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: The increasing demand for patient-specific dental implants and regenerative oral therapies necessitates the development of advanced biomaterials capable of integrating dynamically with heterogeneous bone structures. Current approaches to designing such materials often rely on simplified mechanical and biological assumptions, leading to suboptimal performance in complex clinical scenarios. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing 3D-printed bioactive scaffolds for mandibular bone regeneration by simulating multiscale interactions between material microarchitecture, mechanical stress distributions, and osteogenic cell behavior. A critical gap exists in predicting how scaffold designs influence long-term tissue remodeling under physiological loading conditions unique to the oral cavity, particularly in patients with comorbidities such as osteoporosis or diabetes. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), agent-based modeling (ABM), and machine learning (ML) to iteratively refine scaffold geometries and material compositions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of bone-scaffold interfacial mechanics at micron resolution, coupled with stochastic models of cellular differentiation and extracellular matrix deposition across clinically relevant timescales. Parametric studies will evaluate over 10,000 design permutations, incorporating patient-specific variability in bone density, occlusal forces, and biochemical microenvironments. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify nonlinear relationships between scaffold properties and osteointegration outcomes, accelerating the discovery of adaptive designs. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for scaffold performance and a dataset linking computational parameters to in vitro cell culture results. This work will advance personalized dental rehabilitation strategies while establishing a transferable computational pipeline for biomaterial optimization in craniofacial applications. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the high computational burden of multiscale simulations, which require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and GPU-accelerated ML training. By bridging computational mechanics, materials science, and developmental biology, this project aims to redefine standards for precision in oral regenerative engineering.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing next-generation superconducting energy storage systems through high-fidelity simulations and machine learning-driven design. Modern superconducting networks face critical challenges in balancing energy density, thermal stability, and electromagnetic interference mitigation, particularly when scaling to grid-level applications. Existing simulation tools struggle to model the multi-physics interactions between quantum material behaviors, transient electromagnetic fields, and cryogenic thermal dynamics at relevant spatial and temporal scales. Our interdisciplinary approach combines finite-element analysis of electromagnetic wave propagation in type-II superconductors with graph neural networks trained on mesoscale material defect distributions. The proposed computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods for modeling flux pinning dynamics and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for optimizing coil geometries in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems. By employing distributed-memory parallelization across multi-node clusters, we aim to simulate full-scale superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) units with sub-micron spatial resolution—a 100x improvement over current state-of-the-art models. Expected outcomes include predictive digital twins for superconducting component degradation and open-source machine learning models for topology optimization under electromagnetic constraints. This work will directly address the computational bottlenecks preventing widespread adoption of superconducting energy storage, while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of computational electromagnetics, materials informatics, and high-performance computing. The developed framework will enable the design of more efficient fault-tolerant power networks and provide foundational tools for simulating emerging quantum-electronic hybrid systems. Resource allocation will support critical benchmarks in parallel scaling efficiency and memory optimization required for transitioning from laboratory-scale prototypes to utility-scale deployment models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components computer theory, computing problems and solutions, including electrical power generation systems; the design of computer systems and user interfaces; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification. c and the design of computer systems and user interfaces

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting treatment outcomes for patients with complex mental health conditions, including schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and co-occurring substance use disorders. Despite advances in psychiatric care, treatment selection remains largely trial-and-error due to the heterogeneity of patient responses and the multifactorial nature of mental illnesses, which involve genetic, neurobiological, and socio-environmental variables. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive modeling framework that integrates multi-modal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomic data, and patient-reported outcomes—to identify personalized intervention strategies. The computational approach will leverage machine learning algorithms, such as ensemble models and graph neural networks, to analyze longitudinal datasets from 15,000 patients across five regional mental health systems. These models will map interactions between biomarkers, psychosocial risk factors, and treatment histories to predict trajectories of symptom remission, relapse, and functional recovery. A key innovation involves simulating crisis intervention scenarios using agent-based modeling to optimize care delivery protocols under resource constraints. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of neuroimaging data, running parallelized model training across thousands of parameters, and conducting real-time sensitivity analyses for clinical decision support tools. Expected outcomes include the identification of reproducible digital phenotypes associated with optimal responses to specific pharmacological and behavioral therapies, as well as risk stratification algorithms for early intervention in high-risk populations. By translating these computational insights into actionable clinical guidelines, this work aims to empower psychiatric-mental health nurses with evidence-based tools to reduce hospitalization rates, improve medication adherence, and tailor psychoeducation strategies. The resource allocation will directly support advancements in precision nursing care for underserved populations with dual diagnoses and severe mental illness.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to promote mental health and provide nursing care to patients with mental, emotional or behavioral disorders, in mental institutions or other settings. Includes instruction in psychopathology, behavioral health, counseling and intervention strategies, psychoeducation, mental health assessment and dual diagnosis, stabilization and management of psychotic illness, psychiatric care and rehabilitation, substance abuse, and crisis intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of homiletic rhetoric within Christian liturgical traditions, focusing on understudied denominational shifts and their socio-cultural impacts. While homiletics—the art of preaching—is central to divinity and ministry, its historical development remains fragmented in scholarly discourse, particularly for smaller denominations and non-Western contexts. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in rhetorical strategies, thematic emphasis, and linguistic adaptation across 10,000+ digitized sermons (1600–present) from diverse Christian traditions, including Anabaptist, Pentecostal, and Global South communities often excluded from broader theological analyses. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) to detect semantic shifts, sentiment analysis to map doctrinal prioritization, and network modeling to trace the diffusion of homiletic frameworks across regions and denominations. The scale of textual data (multilingual, spanning four centuries) necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing of unstructured texts, training transformer-based models for context-aware theological classification, and simulating rhetorical influence networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible corpus tagged for rhetorical devices, theological themes, and cultural contextualization, alongside a framework for quantifying homiletic adaptation in response to societal changes (e.g., industrialization, decolonization). This work bridges computational humanities and practical divinity by providing data-driven insights into how preaching traditions have mediated theological authority and communal identity, with applications in ministerial training and interdenominational dialogue. The project’s computational demands—particularly in handling low-resource languages and diachronic textual variance—require GPU-accelerated workloads and large-memory nodes to manage model training and corpus alignment, resources not feasible without HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as ministers or priests in any of the Christian religious traditions. Includes instruction in the theology and polity of a particular church, church law, liturgy and ritual, principles of pastoral ministry, homiletics, evangelism, church/parish organization and management, Christian ethics, church history, and related studies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying music therapy interventions for individuals with acquired communication disorders, such as aphasia and apraxia of speech, using advanced computational modeling. While music therapy has shown empirical promise in enhancing speech rehabilitation, the field lacks robust quantitative frameworks to characterize how specific auditory-motor entrainment protocols modulate neural plasticity or optimize therapeutic outcomes. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating high-resolution neuroimaging data, acoustic feature extraction, and patient-specific biophysical models to decode the dynamic interplay between rhythmic auditory stimuli, cortical reorganization, and functional recovery. The computational approach employs machine learning pipelines to analyze multimodal datasets (fMRI, EEG, and kinematic speech recordings) from 120 participants undergoing rhythm-based therapy, identifying patterns in neural oscillation coupling, sensorimotor synchronization, and speech production metrics. Concurrently, biologically constrained neural network models will simulate intervention effects on damaged language networks, incorporating individual lesion profiles and neurotransmitter dynamics. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabytes of temporally dense neuroimaging data, training deep learning architectures on heterogeneous feature sets, and running large-scale parameter sweeps in personalized neural simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking therapeutic music parameters (tempo, spectral complexity, pulse clarity) to neurobehavioral response profiles, enabling data-driven personalization of intervention protocols. The project aims to establish foundational computational tools for optimizing music therapy efficacy while advancing mechanistic understanding of auditory-motor integration in neurorehabilitation. By leveraging HPC capabilities to address the multidimensionality of music-based interventions, this work will foster translational innovation at the intersection of clinical neuroscience, computational psychiatry, and therapeutic arts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in association with a rehabilitation team or in private practice, to use music in therapeutic relationships to address the physical, psychological, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of clients. Includes instruction in music theory and performance, human growth and development, biomedical sciences, abnormal psychology, disabling conditions, patient assessment and diagnosis, treatment plan development and implementation, clinical evaluation, record-keeping, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing personalized learning interventions for students with diverse social-emotional and academic needs. A critical challenge in educational psychology lies in identifying which intervention strategies—such as targeted counseling, behavioral support, or adaptive learning tools—most effectively improve outcomes for specific student subgroups, particularly within large, heterogeneous school populations. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model the dynamic, multi-level interactions between student characteristics (e.g., cognitive profiles, socioemotional states), intervention types, and longitudinal academic progress. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models trained on longitudinal datasets encompassing academic performance metrics, behavioral records, and psychosocial assessments from K-12 schools. These models will integrate hierarchical Bayesian inference and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate intervention efficacy across diverse virtual student profiles while accounting for contextual factors like classroom climate and resource availability. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of anonymized student data, perform hyperparameter optimization for high-dimensional models, and run computationally intensive Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in intervention outcomes. The project will produce open-source tools for educators to predict intervention success probabilities in real-world settings, alongside frameworks for ethically aligning AI-driven recommendations with counseling best practices. Expected outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for deploying multi-tiered support systems (MTSS) that balance scalability with individualized student needs, ultimately reducing achievement gaps and fostering equitable learning environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic production scheduling in multi-stage manufacturing systems under uncertainty, a critical challenge in operations management. Traditional scheduling models often fail to account for real-time disruptions such as machine breakdowns, demand variability, and supply chain delays, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and reduced operational efficiency. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach integrating discrete-event simulation, reinforcement learning (RL), and stochastic integer programming. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train RL agents on large-scale synthetic production environments, simulate millions of perturbation scenarios, and solve stochastic optimization models with high-dimensional decision variables. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate resilience metrics and multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to balance throughput, cost, and service-level targets. By modeling interdependencies between production stages, maintenance schedules, and inventory policies, the framework aims to generate adaptive scheduling policies that minimize downtime and waste while maximizing equipment utilization. Expected outcomes include scalable decision-support tools for plant managers, validated through collaboration with an automotive parts manufacturer, and generalized insights into bottleneck mitigation under uncertainty. The project will contribute novel methodologies to the operations management field by advancing the integration of AI and optimization techniques for complex production systems. Access to HPC resources will enable the exploration of high-fidelity models that capture real-world complexity, which is computationally intractable on local clusters. Results will inform best practices for resilient manufacturing operations and provide open-source simulation templates for industry and academic use.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and direct the physical and/or technical functions of a firm or organization, particularly those relating to development, production, and manufacturing. Includes instruction in principles of general management, manufacturing and production systems, plant management, equipment maintenance management, production control, industrial labor relations and skilled trades supervision, strategic manufacturing policy, systems analysis, productivity analysis and cost control, and materials planning.

abstract: The increasing reliance on digital infrastructure in clinical environments has exposed critical vulnerabilities in the operational continuity of medical offices, particularly in managing hardware-software integration for diagnostic and administrative systems. Frequent system failures, often due to unanticipated incompatibilities between legacy medical devices and modern software updates, disrupt patient care workflows and introduce risks to data integrity. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing an adaptive compatibility framework (ACF) powered by machine learning to predict and mitigate interoperability failures in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze heterogeneous datasets spanning device performance logs, software version histories, and error reports from diverse clinical settings. Computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex dependencies between hardware components and software dependencies, while reinforcement learning agents will simulate update scenarios to identify failure-prone configurations. The ACF will be validated against a multi-institutional corpus of de-identified medical office system data, with performance benchmarks comparing failure prediction accuracy and mitigation success rates against existing rule-based compatibility tools. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for proactive system maintenance, reducing unplanned downtime by an estimated 40–60% in test environments. By focusing on the intersection of clinical operations and computational systems engineering, this research bridges a gap in health sciences informatics, offering a specialized solution to infrastructure resilience that enhances both patient care delivery and operational efficiency. The project’s HPC requirements—including GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale simulation of device networks—are essential to address the temporal and structural complexity of real-world medical office ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: Infectious diseases caused by microbial agents remain a critical global health challenge, exacerbated by emerging pathogens and antimicrobial resistance. Current clinical workflows for isolating and identifying microbial species from complex samples—such as blood, sputum, or tissue—rely heavily on culture-based methods, which are time-intensive and fail to detect unculturable or fastidious organisms. While metagenomic sequencing offers a culture-independent alternative, analyzing these datasets requires substantial computational resources to disentangle host-microbe interactions, resolve low-abundance pathogens, and detect genetic markers of virulence or resistance. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced computational workflows for rapid, precise microbial identification and characterization directly from clinical samples. Using GPU-accelerated pipelines, we will process raw sequencing data to perform de novo genome assembly, taxonomic classification, and functional annotation of microbial communities. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-omic datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic) to predict antimicrobial resistance phenotypes and infer pathogenicity mechanisms. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model microbial community dynamics under varying host immune conditions and antibiotic exposures. These computational approaches will be validated against gold-standard clinical microbiology results from a retrospective cohort of 500 patients with sepsis of unknown etiology. The integration of HPC resources will enable the analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce turnaround times for pathogen identification from days to hours, and uncover novel associations between microbial genotypes and clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include open-source bioinformatics tools optimized for clinical metagenomics, a curated database of pathogen-specific biomarkers, and actionable insights into underdiagnosed microbial contributors to infectious disease. This work will directly inform precision antimicrobial therapy and outbreak surveillance, addressing a critical gap in translational medical microbiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the isolation and identification of microbial agents that cause infectious disease, including viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation medicine faces significant challenges in addressing the heterogeneous nature of congenital and childhood-onset physical impairments, which often involve complex interactions between medical, functional, and psychosocial factors. Current clinical tools for predicting long-term outcomes or optimizing personalized rehabilitation strategies lack the capacity to integrate multimodal data at scale, limiting their ability to inform precision interventions. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model patient trajectories and treatment responses using multidimensional datasets. The research will integrate clinical assessments, wearable sensor data, neuroimaging, and patient-reported outcomes from a longitudinal cohort of 1,200 children with cerebral palsy, spina bifida, and acquired brain injuries. Computational methods will include mechanistic modeling of neuromotor development, machine learning for phenotype clustering, and finite element simulations of musculoskeletal adaptations during growth. Key challenges requiring HPC resources include processing high-frequency sensor data (50TB raw input), running ensemble models to quantify uncertainty in personalized predictions, and optimizing neural networks for real-time adaptation to patient-specific biomechanical parameters. The computational pipeline will be validated through iterative comparison with clinical outcomes over a 24-month observation window. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for simulating rehabilitation scenarios, predictive biomarkers of treatment-resistant motor impairment, and evidence-based criteria for allocating therapeutic resources across developmental stages. By enabling dynamic, data-driven models of impairment progression, this work aims to transform clinical decision-making in pediatric rehabilitation, reducing trial-and-error approaches while addressing functional, social, and vocational dimensions of disability. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the computational intensity of whole-body biomechanical simulations at scale and advancing interdisciplinary rehabilitation research paradigms.
cip_definition: Research on how to use an interdisciplinary approach to prevent, diagnose, treat, and manage congenital and childhood-onset physical impairments in children and young adults, including related medical, physical, functional, psychosocial, and vocational limitations or conditions.

abstract: The motorsports industry faces increasing demands for vehicle performance optimization under complex aerodynamic, thermal, and mechanical constraints. Current design workflows rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and simplified simulations, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in capturing multi-physics interactions critical to racing performance. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model and optimize motorsports systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these limitations. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) aerodynamic analysis of vehicle-body and component designs under dynamic track conditions using unsteady computational fluid dynamics (CFD), (2) coupled thermal-structural simulations of powertrain systems to evaluate performance limits and failure modes, and (3) data-driven optimization of vehicle dynamics through machine learning models trained on sensor data and simulation outputs. The computational approach will employ parallelized solvers, adaptive meshing techniques, and GPU-accelerated workflows to manage the scale and resolution required for transient, multi-phase simulations. Integration of CAD parameterization tools will enable automated design exploration. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to reduce simulation turnaround times from weeks to days while resolving finer spatial and temporal scales than current institutional computing infrastructure allows. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting drag reduction strategies, engine cooling efficiency improvements, and tire-road interaction dynamics under extreme racing conditions. This work will directly enhance student and faculty capabilities in motorsports engineering at the intersection of computational methods and applied design, while generating open-access case studies for curriculum integration. The results will also provide actionable insights for industry partners seeking to adopt simulation-driven design practices, ultimately contributing to safer, more competitive motorsports technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: Gynecologic malignancies, including ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers, exhibit significant molecular heterogeneity, complicating treatment optimization and contributing to high rates of recurrence and therapy resistance. Current clinical stratification methods often fail to account for this variability, leading to suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets and develop predictive models of tumor behavior and treatment response. The research will integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic data from patient-derived samples, including bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and longitudinal clinical data, to identify molecular subtypes and dynamic biomarkers associated with therapeutic resistance. Computational workflows will employ machine learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) to classify tumor subtypes and predict drug sensitivity, while mechanistic models will simulate tumor evolution under selective pressures of chemotherapy and targeted therapies. Agent-based modeling and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations will further explore tumor-immune interactions and drug penetration in heterogeneous microenvironments. The scale of data (≥100 TB) and complexity of iterative model training necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallel processing, large-scale matrix operations, and high-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for personalized therapy selection, novel biomarkers for early detection of resistance, and mechanistic insights into microenvironment-driven recurrence. These findings will directly inform clinical trial designs and real-time decision support tools for gynecologic oncology care, aiming to improve progression-free survival and reduce unnecessary treatment toxicity. The project bridges computational biology and clinical practice, underscoring the critical role of HPC in advancing precision oncology for complex gynecologic cancers.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for consultation and comprehensive management of patients with gynecologic cancer, including those diagnostic and therapeutic procedures necessary for the total care of the patient with gynecologic cancer and resulting complications.

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation requires precise integration of biomechanical principles, material science, and patient-specific anatomies to optimize functional and aesthetic outcomes. However, current methods for designing and evaluating dental prostheses, implants, and occlusal devices rely heavily on static clinical metrics and trial-and-error adjustments, limiting their ability to predict long-term performance under dynamic physiological loads. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to simulate multiscale biomechanical interactions within the masticatory system, including bone-implant interfaces, stress distribution in prostheses, and soft tissue responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model these complex systems at clinically relevant resolutions, incorporating patient-derived 3D imaging data, heterogeneous material properties, and time-dependent loading conditions representative of mastication, parafunction, and speech. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to assess stress concentrations, fatigue resistance of restorative materials, and fluid flow patterns around implant surfaces. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze large datasets from clinical cohorts to identify predictors of prosthetic failure or complications. The proposed simulations will enable virtual prototyping of patient-specific prosthodontic solutions, reducing iterative physical adjustments and chairside time. Expected outcomes include validated computational models for predicting biomechanical risks in implant-supported prostheses, guidelines for material selection in geriatric and high-load cases, and open-source tools for optimizing occlusal device design in temporomandibular joint dysfunction. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance evidence-based prosthodontics, improve clinical decision-making, and enhance the longevity and patient satisfaction of restorative treatments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the restoration and maintenance of teeth, oral function, and aesthetic form through the use of single or compound materials, structures, and artificial devices. Includes instruction in implant dentistry, surgical procedures, denture design and fabrication, fixed and removable prosthodontics, restorative techniques, occlusion therapy and devices, geriatric dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance three-dimensional structural analyses of cellular and tissue dynamics in musculoskeletal systems, with a focus on age-related degenerative changes. A central challenge in anatomical research is resolving how spatial organization and mechanical interactions at cellular and subcellular scales influence tissue-scale function and pathology. Traditional imaging and biomechanical models often lack the resolution or computational capacity to integrate multiscale data, limiting insights into mechanisms driving conditions such as sarcopenia or osteoarthritis. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework combining large-scale electron microscopy datasets, agent-based modeling, and finite element simulations. High-resolution volumetric imaging of muscle and joint tissues from murine models will generate terabytes of structural data, capturing cellular architectures, extracellular matrix organization, and organelle distributions. These datasets will inform agent-based models simulating cellular responses to mechanical stress, while finite element analyses will predict tissue-level strain patterns under physiological loads. HPC resources are critical for managing data storage, parallel processing of multiscale simulations, and machine learning-driven segmentation of complex tissue features. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking subcellular alterations (e.g., mitochondrial displacement, cytoskeletal rearrangements) to tissue mechanical failure in aging, (2) identification of structural biomarkers preceding macroscopic degeneration, and (3) open-source tools for automated analysis of anatomical ultrastructure. By enabling integration of cellular-scale dynamics with organ-level biomechanics, this work will provide foundational insights into anatomical adaptations during aging while establishing computational workflows for hypothesis-driven exploration of tissue pathophysiology. The requested resources will directly support time-sensitive simulations requiring >10,000 core-hours and GPU-accelerated deep learning pipelines for image processing, advancing anatomical discovery through scalable, data-intensive computational approaches.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of organ systems, tissue structures, and whole bodies together with their cellular and structural components and dynamics. Includes instruction in cell biology and histology, structural biology, molecular mechanics, regional and gross anatomy, embryology, neuroanatomy, endocrinology and secretory dynamics, and applications to such topics as aging and disease conditions.

abstract: The development of investigational drugs requires rigorous evaluation of efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) profiles to advance candidates into clinical trials. A critical challenge lies in predicting patient-specific responses to novel therapeutics, particularly in heterogeneous populations with complex comorbidities or genetic variations. Traditional trial-and-error approaches remain resource-intensive and prone to high attrition rates, underscoring the need for advanced computational models to optimize drug selection and trial design. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale, patient-derived models that integrate genomic, proteomic, and clinical data to simulate drug behavior across virtual cohorts. The computational framework will employ molecular dynamics simulations to characterize drug-target binding affinities, machine learning algorithms to predict off-target effects and toxicity risks, and population PK/PD modeling to quantify inter-individual variability in drug exposure and response. Large-scale genomic datasets from public repositories (e.g., UK Biobank, TCGA) and proprietary clinical trial data will be processed to identify biomarkers of therapeutic response and adverse events. Parallelized workflows will enable the simultaneous evaluation of thousands of drug-candidate combinations under diverse physiological scenarios, while Bayesian optimization techniques will prioritize compounds with the highest likelihood of clinical success. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for dose optimization, patient stratification strategies, and mechanistic insights into drug resistance pathways. By reducing reliance on costly late-stage trial failures, this work aims to accelerate the translation of investigational drugs into clinically viable therapies. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational demands of iterative model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the integration of high-dimensional omics data. Successful implementation will provide a scalable platform for precision medicine applications, directly supporting the development of safer, more effective therapeutics for complex diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on Investigational Drugs and Research

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a cross-cultural study of long-term social network dynamics and cultural transmission processes in premodern human societies. Anthropological theories posit that social structures and resource-sharing practices co-evolve with cultural norms, but modeling these interactions at scale remains computationally prohibitive due to the nonlinear relationships between variables such as kinship systems, ecological constraints, and symbolic communication patterns. The proposed work will develop and implement agent-based models (ABMs) simulating population-level interactions across parameter spaces informed by ethnographic and archaeological datasets from 30+ globally distributed case studies. Computational demands arise from the need to run thousands of parallelized simulations incorporating multi-layered networks (kinship, trade, ritual), environmental stochasticity, and heterogeneous agent decision-making algorithms derived from anthropological frameworks. A second component applies phylogenetic comparative methods to linguistic and material culture datasets spanning 15 language families, requiring Bayesian inference of cultural trait evolution under varying selective pressures. This dual approach—combining fine-grained simulation with macro-scale comparative analysis—addresses critical gaps in understanding how feedback loops between individual agency and structural constraints shape cultural resilience. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of petascale simulation outputs and complex likelihood calculations impractical on local clusters. Expected outcomes include 1) validated computational frameworks for integrating qualitative ethnographic data with quantitative cultural evolutionary models, 2) open-source tools for anthropological simulation design, and 3) empirical insights into the role of network redundancy in mitigating cultural information loss during demographic crises. These results will provide methodological foundations for computational anthropology while offering actionable perspectives on human adaptive strategies relevant to contemporary challenges in cultural heritage preservation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human beings, their antecedents and related primates, and their cultural behavior and institutions, in comparative perspective. Includes instruction in biological/physical anthropology, primatology, human paleontology and prehistoric archeology, hominid evolution, anthropological linguistics, ethnography, ethnology, ethnohistory, socio-cultural anthropology, psychological anthropology, research methods, and applications to areas such as medicine, forensic pathology, museum studies, and international affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in multi-agent business ecosystems under uncertainty, integrating stochastic modeling, behavioral economics, and distributed machine learning. Contemporary enterprises operate in environments characterized by rapidly shifting consumer preferences, competitive actions, and supply chain disruptions, yet existing analytical tools often fail to capture the emergent complexity arising from interdependent stakeholder interactions. The research will create agent-based simulation architectures that model strategic decision pathways across three scales: individual consumer micro-behaviors, organizational resource allocation patterns, and macroeconomic shock propagation. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore decision trees across 10^6+ possible state configurations, coupled with evolutionary algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal strategies balancing risk and innovation. A novel feature involves embedding transformer-based neural networks within simulation agents to enable adaptive learning from real-time streaming data on market sentiment and competitor actions. Computational challenges include managing asynchronous updates across heterogeneous agents, optimizing memory allocation for high-dimensional state representations, and ensuring numerical stability in gradient-based strategy updates. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario stress-testing in strategic planning, validated through case studies in cross-industry partnerships facing climate transition risks. The resource request targets GPU-accelerated nodes for deep reinforcement learning components and high-memory nodes for large-scale sensitivity analyses. By bridging discrete optimization, behavioral simulation, and enterprise-scale analytics, this work aims to advance decision theory while providing practical frameworks for resilient business adaptation in volatile markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to solve business challenges. Includes instruction in machine learning, optimization methods, computer algorithms, probability and stochastic models, information economics, logistics, strategy, consumer behavior, marketing, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for small businesses operating in hyper-volatile markets, such as those influenced by rapid technological disruption or climate-driven supply chain instability. While traditional business research often assumes stable operating environments, this work addresses the critical gap in adaptive decision-making tools for enterprises facing nonlinear, unpredictable risks. The core research problem involves modeling interdependencies between financial liquidity, human capital flexibility, and infrastructure resilience under cascading disruption scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based computational models that simulate thousands of small business archetypes across diverse sectoral and geographic contexts. These models will integrate real-world datasets including transaction records, supply chain interruption logs, and workforce mobility patterns. A machine learning-driven network analysis layer will identify critical leverage points where targeted resource investments yield disproportionate stability benefits. Computational experiments will test dynamic allocation strategies that balance short-term survival tactics with long-term adaptation capacity, accounting for multi-stakeholder priorities and ethical constraints in resource distribution. The project’s HPC requirements stem from the need to process terabyte-scale datasets from public business registries and private sector partnerships while running parallelized scenario simulations with <10ms latency for real-time decision support applications. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for resilience-aware resource allocation, validated through retrospective analysis of business survival rates during COVID-19 supply chain shocks. This work bridges computational social science with entrepreneurial practice, offering novel methodologies for small business sustainability in an era of compounding crises.
cip_title: Entrepreneurial and Small Business Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in enterprise management and entrepreneurship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decentralized supply chain networks using blockchain-enabled multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Traditional supply chain models often struggle with dynamic resource allocation, information asymmetry, and trust deficits in multi-stakeholder environments, particularly in emerging decentralized business ecosystems. The proposed work addresses this gap by integrating cryptographic verification, smart contracts, and adaptive learning algorithms to model complex interactions among autonomous agents in supply networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale networks with thousands of concurrent agents, each making real-time decisions under constraints such as fluctuating demand, sustainability targets, and geopolitical risks. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to represent supply network topologies with MARL algorithms trained on GPU clusters to optimize inventory routing, carbon-aware procurement, and conflict resolution mechanisms. Validation will occur through synthetic data generation mirroring cross-border e-commerce logistics and physical simulations of perishable goods distribution. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying resilience in decentralized supply chains and open-source tools for dynamic resource reallocation under disruption scenarios. This work contributes to quantitative management science by advancing computational methods for trust-centric coordination in business networks, with potential applications in circular economy transitions and crisis-responsive value chains. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable parameter space exploration at scales infeasible with commercial cloud resources, particularly for privacy-preserving federated learning architectures that require distributed computation across simulated organizational boundaries.
cip_title: Management Sciences and Quantitative Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business quantitative methods and management science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of integrating multi-omics data into genetic counseling practice to improve the interpretation of complex genomic findings. While advances in sequencing technologies have expanded access to genomic testing, clinical workflows struggle to efficiently synthesize heterogeneous data types—including genomics, epigenomics, and transcriptomics—into actionable insights for patients. Current variant classification pipelines rely on static databases and manual curation, creating bottlenecks that delay diagnoses and limit the personalization of risk communication. To overcome this, we propose developing a dynamic, machine learning-driven framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. This framework will integrate population-scale genomic datasets, functional genomic annotations, and patient-specific clinical data to predict variant pathogenicity and phenotypic outcomes with higher resolution. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized algorithms to process multi-terabyte datasets, train deep learning models on graph-based representations of gene regulatory networks, and simulate genotype-phenotype associations under diverse demographic and environmental conditions. A key innovation involves embedding probabilistic counseling scenarios into the model architecture, enabling real-time adjustment of risk estimates based on evolving evidence. The HPC infrastructure will also support the development of interactive visualization tools to help genetic counselors communicate multidimensional risk profiles to patients. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for rapid variant reclassification, personalized risk assessment templates, and a novel dataset linking computational predictions to longitudinal patient outcomes. By bridging computational genomics and clinical communication strategies, this work aims to reduce diagnostic uncertainty, enhance patient autonomy in decision-making, and establish best practices for deploying AI-driven tools in genetic counseling. The resource request directly supports advancements in precision medicine while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for transparency and equity in genomic data interpretation.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel patients and families concerning inherited genetic disorders and diseases; assess risk factors and planning options associated with potential and actual inherited conditions; and serve as patient advocates and provide referral services in relation to private and public support services. Includes instruction in clinical/medical genetics, methods of genetic testing, interviewing and counseling skills, genetic and support services delivery, principles of public health, medical ethics, law and regulations, patient advocacy, and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance structural integrity assessment and risk prediction in aging buildings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in current construction inspection practices. While existing inspection protocols rely heavily on manual evaluations and static code compliance, they often fail to account for dynamic environmental stressors (e.g., seismic activity, material fatigue, climate-induced degradation) that evolve over a structure’s lifecycle. To address this, we propose a multi-physics modeling approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and real-world sensor data to simulate structural behavior under diverse stress scenarios. The computational workflow will model interactions between building materials, mechanical loads, and environmental factors at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, using HPC resources to parallelize simulations across thousands of parametric variations. Key objectives include (1) training ML models on historical failure data to predict high-risk zones in building systems, (2) automating code-compliance checks via generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on regional building codes and inspection reports, and (3) developing a probabilistic risk assessment tool to prioritize inspection workflows. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale FEA simulations of multi-story structures. Outcomes will directly benefit the construction inspection field by enabling data-driven, predictive maintenance strategies, reducing human error in code interpretation, and improving resilience planning for climate-vulnerable regions. By quantifying uncertainty in material degradation patterns and load-bearing capacities, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for computationally assisted inspection protocols, ultimately enhancing public safety while reducing long-term infrastructure costs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply industrial, labor, and governmental standards and laws to the oversight of construction projects and the maintenance of completed buildings and other structures. Includes instruction in construction processes and techniques, materials analysis, occupational safety and health, industry standards, building codes and specifications, blueprint interpretation, testing equipment and procedures, communication skills, accident investigation, and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the diachronic and synchronic dynamics of Romance language evolution, with a focus on identifying patterns of syntactic and morphological change across geographically dispersed dialects. The study addresses a critical gap in computational Romance linguistics: modeling how contact phenomena (e.g., bilingualism, language shift) and sociolinguistic variables drive structural divergence in languages such as Occitan, Sardinian, and Galician, which exist in dynamic contact with dominant state languages. Current methodologies lack the computational power to process large-scale, multi-modal corpora—including historical texts, sociolinguistic interviews, and dialectal audio recordings—while accounting for the nonlinear interactions between linguistic variables. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with transformer-based natural language processing (NLP). The ABM framework will simulate language contact scenarios over centuries, parameterized by demographic data and attested sound laws, while fine-tuned NLP models (e.g., BERT variants trained on historical Romance texts) will analyze morphosyntactic variation across 15th–21st century corpora. HPC resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized ABM simulations across thousands of parameter combinations to model probabilistic language change; (2) training domain-specific language models on terabyte-scale textual and phonetic datasets; and (3) real-time alignment of simulation outputs with empirical data using GPU-accelerated phylogenetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include the first probabilistic maps of syntactic convergence risks for endangered Romance varieties, a publicly accessible database of annotated dialectal features, and methodological frameworks for scalable diachronic linguistic analysis. This work will directly inform language revitalization efforts and enhance computational tools for minority language education, while advancing interdisciplinary connections between Romance linguistics and computational social science.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Romance languages of Western, Central, and Southern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in chemistry teacher preparation by developing a computational framework to model and predict how pre-service teachers conceptualize molecular-level interactions—a foundational yet commonly misunderstood topic in chemistry education. Current training programs often rely on static visualizations and textbook descriptions, which fail to capture the dynamic, probabilistic nature of molecular behavior. This disconnect contributes to persistent pedagogical challenges, as educators struggle to translate abstract concepts into effective, evidence-based instruction. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate interactive molecular dynamics scenarios tailored to teacher education contexts. Using molecular dynamics software (e.g., GROMACS, NAMD), we will generate large-scale simulations of chemical systems (e.g., aqueous solutions, reaction equilibria) under varied conditions, coupled with machine learning analysis to identify patterns in how users interpret real-time simulation data. These simulations will be integrated into adaptive training modules where pre-service teachers manipulate variables, observe outcomes, and confront misconceptions through guided computational experimentation. The HPC environment is essential for handling the parallel processing demands of simulating thousands of molecular trajectories across parameter spaces, as well as for training neural networks to classify learner reasoning pathways from interaction logs. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of annotated simulation datasets optimized for chemistry education contexts, (2) quantitative frameworks linking specific simulation features to improvements in pedagogical content knowledge, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for incorporating dynamic computational models into teacher training curricula. By grounding chemistry education strategies in atomistically detailed, interactive computational experiences, this work aims to transform how future educators visualize and teach fundamental chemical concepts, ultimately improving secondary and undergraduate students’ understanding of molecular science. The requested resources will directly support simulation runtime, data storage, and machine learning workflows critical to achieving these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach chemistry programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for sustainable apparel design, focusing on optimizing textile reuse and waste reduction through predictive modeling. The global fashion industry faces escalating environmental challenges, with textile waste accounting for 9% of annual microplastic pollution and over 92 million tons of landfill contributions. Current approaches to circular design remain constrained by manual processes and limited scalability in analyzing complex material interactions. Our research addresses this gap by developing a novel computational framework that integrates lifecycle assessment data, textile degradation models, and consumer behavior patterns to simulate multi-stage reuse pathways for post-consumer garments. The project employs finite element analysis to model mechanical wear across diverse fabric types, combined with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to predict aesthetic degradation under varying environmental conditions. Agent-based modeling will simulate market dynamics of textile recovery systems at urban scales, requiring parallel processing of 10^6+ agent interactions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for designers to quantify the environmental impact of design choices during prototyping phases, potentially reducing sample production waste by 30-50% in partner manufacturing trials. The computational intensity of coupling physical simulations with socioeconomic datasets necessitates HPC capabilities for both training deep learning models on terabyte-scale material databases and running Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses across design parameters. By bridging computational materials science with sustainable design praxis, this work establishes a foundation for data-driven circular economy strategies in apparel production while advancing methodological synergies between HPC applications and creative industries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in apparel and textiles, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Law enforcement intelligence analysis increasingly relies on synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—including surveillance records, financial transactions, digital communications, geospatial information, and open-source data—to identify threats and criminal networks. However, the volume, velocity, and complexity of these datasets challenge traditional analytical methods, which struggle to integrate multi-modal information at scale and deliver timely, actionable insights. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing computational workflows that leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to automate and enhance intelligence analysis processes. The research focuses on three core objectives: (1) optimizing large-scale link analysis to map relationships within fragmented criminal networks using graph-based machine learning models; (2) advancing geospatial pattern detection by parallelizing spatial-temporal clustering algorithms across distributed computing architectures; and (3) designing ensemble classifiers to improve the accuracy of real-time threat prediction by fusing structured operational data with unstructured text and multimedia inputs. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated graph neural networks, distributed in-memory processing of geospatial data via Apache Sedona, and hybrid CPU-GPU pipelines for multimodal deep learning. These workflows will be tested against real-world case data from law enforcement partners, anonymized and compliant with privacy regulations. The expected outcomes include scalable tools for automating network inference, detecting emergent spatial threats (e.g., trafficking routes), and reducing false positives in risk assessments. By enabling rapid analysis of petabyte-scale datasets, this project aims to strengthen evidence-based decision-making in operational planning and resource allocation for law enforcement agencies. The resulting frameworks and models will be disseminated as open-source resources to support intelligence training programs and advance research in computational criminology.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the preparation of law enforcement personnel to perform intelligence and surveillance operations and to analyze and use data collected via such operations. Includes instruction in the intelligence cycle, information sources, data retrieval, digital investigation, financial investigations, document analysis, external sources, geographic information systems, link analysis, operation planning and security, case management, applicable law and regulations, and case preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to enhance the precision and efficiency of large-scale geospatial data processing in terrestrial surveying applications. Modern surveying technologies, including high-resolution LiDAR, photogrammetry, and GNSS networks, generate vast datasets that require intensive processing to extract accurate topographic and cadastral information. However, traditional computational methods struggle with the scale and complexity of these datasets, leading to bottlenecks in data integration, error correction, and 3D modeling—particularly in urban or geologically dynamic environments. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize key workflows, such as point cloud classification, least-squares adjustment of survey networks, and automated feature extraction using machine learning. The computational approach will involve optimizing existing geodetic algorithms for distributed-memory architectures, implementing GPU-accelerated solvers for iterative adjustments, and training convolutional neural networks to identify boundary features in multispectral imagery. By scaling these processes across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce processing times for regional-scale surveys by an order of magnitude while maintaining sub-centimeter accuracy. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for parallelized survey data processing, validated against ground-truth measurements from traditional total stations and RTK-GNSS field surveys. These tools will enable rapid updates to cadastral databases, support infrastructure resilience planning in tectonically active regions, and improve the detection of subtle terrain changes in landslide-prone areas. The requested resources will directly advance the integration of HPC into geomatics education and practice, fostering new methodologies for handling the exponentially growing data volumes in modern surveying.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the delineation, determination, planning and positioning of land tracts, land and water boundaries, land contours and features; and the preparation of related maps, charts and reports. Includes instruction in applied geodesy, computer graphics, photointerpretation, plane and geodetic surveying, mensuration, traversing, survey equipment operation and maintenance, instrument calibration, and basic cartography.

abstract: This project seeks to address challenges in optimizing industrial-scale chemical processes through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial chemical production often involves complex multiphase reactions, heat and mass transfer phenomena, and fluid dynamics that are difficult to predict using conventional experimental methods or simplified simulations. Current limitations in modeling these systems at scale result in suboptimal reactor designs, energy inefficiencies, and safety risks during scale-up from laboratory to production environments. To overcome these barriers, this research will develop high-fidelity simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), reactive transport modeling, and machine learning-driven optimization. The project will focus on catalytic reactor systems for sustainable chemical manufacturing, incorporating heterogeneous catalysis and non-Newtonian fluid behavior. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of multiscale phenomena—from molecular-scale surface reactions to meter-scale reactor hydrodynamics—using open-source tools such as OpenFOAM and LAMMPS, coupled with custom code for reaction network analysis. Validation will utilize experimental datasets from collaborative industry partners, including temperature profiles and reaction yields. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing reactor geometry, operating conditions, and catalyst configurations to maximize product selectivity while minimizing energy consumption and waste generation. The computational framework will also assess process safety by simulating failure scenarios, such as thermal runaway or flow instabilities. By bridging the gap between laboratory research and industrial implementation, this work aims to advance sustainable chemical manufacturing practices, reduce environmental impacts, and provide a template for HPC-driven process intensification in the chemical engineering technology sector. Results will be disseminated through open-access datasets and workshops to support workforce training in computational process engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: The rapid growth of global air traffic and evolving technological demands in aviation necessitate advanced computational tools to address complex challenges in aircraft design, operational efficiency, and safety. Current simulations for aerodynamics, structural integrity, and air traffic management often lack the resolution or scale to capture multi-physics interactions under real-world conditions, limiting their predictive accuracy and applicability.
