This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy high-fidelity computational models that integrate fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, and machine learning (ML) to optimize next-generation aviation systems. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) large-eddy simulations of turbulent flows around novel aircraft configurations to improve aerodynamic efficiency, (2) finite element analysis of composite material fatigue under combined thermal and mechanical stresses, and (3) reinforcement learning-driven optimization of air traffic control algorithms in congested airspace. These tasks require parallelized computations across thousands of cores to manage the extreme scale of datasets and iterative ML training processes. By coupling GPU-accelerated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with distributed deep learning frameworks, the project aims to reduce simulation wall times by 40–60% compared to existing methods. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for low-drag wing designs, predictive maintenance protocols for aging aircraft, and dynamic airspace management strategies that reduce fuel consumption and emissions. The results will directly inform industry standards and regulatory policies while providing open-source computational workflows to bridge gaps between academic research and aviation engineering practices. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in advancing sustainable aviation technologies amid escalating climate and operational constraints.
cip_title: Aeronautics/ Aviation/ Aerospace Science and Technology, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of aviation and the aviation industry, including in-flight and ground support operations. Includes instruction in the technical, business, and general aspects of air transportation systems.

abstract: Orthopedic interventions, such as casting, splinting, and bracing, require precise customization to optimize patient outcomes while minimizing complications like pressure injuries or delayed healing. Current clinical practices rely heavily on manual techniques and generalized protocols, which may not account for biomechanical variability across patients or dynamic changes in tissue response during recovery. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient-specific biomechanics and simulate the mechanical interactions between orthopedic devices and anatomical structures under varying physiological conditions. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that integrate heterogeneous data—including imaging, material properties, and load dynamics—to guide device design and application protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large datasets from clinical imaging (e.g., CT, MRI) and wearable sensors, perform finite element analysis (FEA) of device-tissue interactions at scale, and train machine learning algorithms to identify optimal device configurations. Computational workflows will incorporate multiphysics simulations to evaluate stress distribution, tissue deformation, and microvascular perfusion in virtual patient cohorts representing diverse anatomies and injury patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models predicting device efficacy and risk profiles for specific clinical scenarios, (2) open-source tools for clinicians to simulate interventions preoperatively, and (3) data-driven guidelines for personalized device selection and adjustment timelines. By linking computational insights to clinical workflows, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error practices, improve recovery rates, and lower healthcare costs associated with prolonged immobilization or device-related complications. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable iterative model refinement, sensitivity analyses across thousands of virtual cases, and real-time visualization of biomechanical parameters—tasks infeasible with standard computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to cast, splint, and brace orthopedic injuries. Includes instruction in patient assessment; casting, splinting, and orthopedic appliances; radiographic interpretation; traction; and wound care.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges in systematically analyzing the syntactic and lexical evolution of Dutch dialects and Creole varieties, which remain understudied due to the scale and heterogeneity of textual sources. Traditional philological methods struggle to manage the vast corpora spanning medieval manuscripts, early modern print sources, and contemporary digital texts, alongside Dutch Creoles with divergent grammatical structures. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational linguistics approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will compile and preprocess a multi-register corpus of over 10 million tokens, integrating historical Dutch texts, modern dialectal data, and Creole documents. Using NLP pipelines optimized for parallel processing, we will perform large-scale tokenization, morphological analysis, and dependency parsing to track syntactic shifts across time and space. Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures, will be trained to identify latent patterns in lexical variation and contact-induced changes in Creole morphology. HPC infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as training deep neural networks on heterogeneous text data and running comparative phylogenetic algorithms to model dialectal relationships. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus, novel findings on the divergence and convergence of Dutch varieties, and methodological advances in applying computational methods to low-resource historical languages. This research will enhance understanding of Dutch linguistic heritage, support preservation efforts for endangered Creoles, and provide a scalable framework for similar studies in other language families.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Dutch language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; Dutch Creoles; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of Italian cultural identity through large-scale textual and visual analysis. The research focuses on tracing how regional dialects, literary movements, and visual media (e.g., film, posters, and archival photography) have shaped collective narratives of belonging and dissent across Italy from the post-Unification period (post-1861) to the late 20th century. A central challenge lies in processing and analyzing unstructured, multilingual datasets—including digitized newspapers, manuscripts, and audiovisual materials—that exceed the capacity of standard computational tools due to their volume (estimated at 15+ TB) and linguistic complexity. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical Italian and regional languages (e.g., Neapolitan, Sicilian), combined with computer vision models to detect stylistic patterns in visual media. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for semantic analysis of ideological shifts in literature, clustering dialectal variations across time and geography, and mapping visual motifs tied to socio-political movements. These workflows require parallelized GPU computing for model training, distributed storage for cross-referencing heterogeneous datasets, and high-memory nodes for network analysis of cultural influence patterns. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated materials, visualizations of cultural transmission pathways, and methodological frameworks for computationally analyzing underrepresented Italian dialects. The findings aim to deepen scholarly understanding of how localized cultural production influenced national identity formation, while demonstrating scalable approaches for interdisciplinary humanities research. By integrating HPC capabilities with archival research, this project addresses critical gaps in Italian Studies’ engagement with computational methods and fosters new avenues for studying cultural change at scale.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of modern Italy and its predecessors on the Italian Peninsula, including the overseas migrations of Italian peoples.

abstract: The integration of advanced materials in high-performance engineering systems requires precise control over manufacturing processes to ensure reliability. However, current approaches in additive manufacturing (AM) often lead to microstructural defects and inconsistent mechanical properties, particularly in multi-material components. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework to optimize AM process parameters, thereby enhancing the quality and performance of manufactured parts. The research will employ high-fidelity multi-physics simulations combining finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model thermal gradients, phase transformations, and residual stresses during the AM process. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to identify correlations between input parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed, material composition) and output metrics such as porosity, dimensional accuracy, and tensile strength. These models require the processing of large datasets generated from high-resolution simulations, necessitating access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized computation and efficient data management. The anticipated outcomes include predictive models that reduce experimental trial-and-error, enabling the fabrication of components with tailored microstructures and optimized mechanical properties. Success in this work will advance the adoption of AM in critical industries such as aerospace and biomedical devices, where material performance and manufacturing precision are paramount. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the scalability of simulations, allowing for parameter space exploration at unprecedented resolution and accelerating the translation of computational insights into practical manufacturing guidelines.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering technologies and engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing STEM instructional strategies for diverse PreK-12 classrooms through computational modeling of teaching practices and student learning dynamics. Current approaches to evaluating pedagogical interventions often rely on small-scale trials or qualitative assessments, limiting generalizability and hindering the development of adaptive, evidence-based methods tailored to heterogeneous student needs. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate classroom interactions under varying instructional scenarios. Agent-based models will be developed to represent student cohorts with differences in prior knowledge, cognitive processing styles, and engagement levels, while reinforcement learning algorithms will train virtual instructors to dynamically adjust problem-based learning activities, technology integrations, and scaffolding techniques. The computational framework will integrate empirical datasets from STEM education research—including student assessment metrics, eye-tracking data, and teacher feedback—to parameterize agents and validate models. By scaling simulations across thousands of virtual classrooms on HPC infrastructure, we aim to identify optimal strategy combinations for specific learning contexts and demographic profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model linking instructional variables to learning gains in STEM domains, (2) actionable guidelines for personalizing lesson plans while maintaining curricular coherence, and (3) an open-access toolkit enabling educators to test hypothetical interventions in simulated environments. This work directly supports teacher education by providing data-driven insights into adaptive pedagogy, reducing trial-and-error implementation barriers, and fostering computational thinking among STEM educators. The requested resources are critical for handling complex model architectures, parallelized simulation runs, and large-scale sensitivity analyses that would be infeasible on standard computing systems.
cip_title: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Educational Methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to connect education practices with scientific, engineering, and mathematical principles for PreK-12 students. Includes instruction in critical thinking, curriculum and instruction, history of STEM education, integrating STEM across curricula, learning sciences and technology, STEM education methods, and teacher leadership in STEM education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing the evolution of architectural design principles in response to socio-environmental stressors across pre-industrial urban centers. While traditional architectural historiography relies on qualitative analysis of physical artifacts and archival records, this research addresses the gap in scalable, data-driven methodologies for modeling how non-elite structures—often underrepresented in canonical archives—adapted to environmental pressures such as resource scarcity, climatic shifts, and demographic changes. By integrating digitized archaeological datasets, geospatial records, and probabilistic reconstructions of lost or degraded structures, the project employs agent-based modeling (ABM) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to simulate design decision-making processes within constrained historical contexts. Computational workflows will process heterogeneous data spanning 12th–18th century Eurasian trade hubs, including fragmentary blueprints, material provenance records, and climate proxy data, to identify latent patterns in vernacular architectural resilience. The HPC environment is critical for handling the iterative training of GANs on sparse, high-dimensional input data and for running large-scale ABM simulations that test hypotheses about resource allocation trade-offs in historic urban planning. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of simulated architectural ensembles, a methodological framework for quantifying design resilience in historical contexts, and visualizations that challenge Eurocentric narratives of architectural innovation by foregrounding adaptive strategies in marginalized communities. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, heritage informatics, and architectural theory, offering new tools for preserving intangible design knowledge and informing contemporary sustainable architecture through historical analogues.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the aesthetic, technical, and social development of the built environment and the architectural profession from earliest times to the present. Includes instruction in the principles of architecture and related fields; art history; historiography of architecture; architectural theory and criticism; related aspects of the history of technology and social and economic history; and various period, cultural, and stylistic specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the detection and interpretation of complex structural genomic variations underlying hematologic malignancies and congenital disorders. Current cytogenetic methods, including karyotyping and fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), face limitations in resolving cryptic rearrangements or low-frequency mosaicism, while emerging sequencing-based approaches struggle with accurate phasing and integration of cytogenetic data. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multimodal framework that synergizes whole-genome sequencing (WGS), high-resolution imaging, and deep learning to improve the characterization of clinically significant genomic aberrations. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing WGS reads, FISH image stacks, and spectral karyotyping data, employing graph-based genome assembly algorithms optimized for GPU-accelerated environments to resolve complex structural variants. Concurrently, a 3D convolutional neural network architecture will analyze multidimensional FISH image arrays to detect spatial patterns indicative of cryptic translocations. Resource-intensive tasks, including population-scale haplotype phasing and batch processing of high-throughput imaging data, will leverage parallelized workflows across HPC nodes. Validation will utilize retrospective cohorts from pediatric leukemia and rare chromosomal disorder cases with unresolved cytogenetic diagnoses. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source platform for integrated cytogenomic analysis, improved detection thresholds for mosaic structural variants (<5% allele frequency), and benchmarked protocols for correlating computational predictions with clinical phenotypes. This work will advance precision diagnostics by bridging molecular cytogenetics with scalable computational infrastructure, directly impacting patient stratification for targeted therapies and transplantation protocols.
cip_title: Cytogenetics/ Genetics/ Clinical Genetics Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform analyses of the human genome and chromosomes for the research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes instruction in chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized rehabilitation protocols for individuals with neuromuscular impairments by integrating high-resolution biomechanical simulations, neural network-driven motor learning models, and real-time physiological data streams. Current clinical practices in movement rehabilitation often rely on generalized therapeutic strategies that fail to account for the complex interplay between individual neurophysiology, biomechanical constraints, and adaptive motor patterns. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multiscale simulations that couple musculoskeletal modeling with dynamic neural control systems. The computational pipeline will process motion capture data, electromyography signals, and patient-specific medical imaging to generate individualized digital twins, enabling predictive analysis of rehabilitation outcomes under varying therapeutic conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed to identify latent patterns in longitudinal recovery trajectories across heterogeneous patient cohorts, while finite element modeling will quantify tissue-level stress distributions during therapeutic exercises. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of parallelized simulations, real-time optimization of treatment parameters, and large-scale sensitivity analyses across multidimensional input spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for clinicians to prescribe targeted interventions that minimize rehabilitation duration and mitigate secondary injury risks. This work bridges computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation science, establishing a foundation for data-driven precision therapeutics in movement disorders. By addressing the scalability challenges inherent in personalized neuromotor rehabilitation, the project aims to advance both methodological paradigms in therapeutic design and clinical outcomes for patients with acquired or degenerative neuromuscular conditions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rehabilitation and therapeutic professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic network mechanisms underlying cognitive deficits in neuropsychiatric disorders, with a focus on aberrant synaptic plasticity and large-scale neural circuit dysregulation. Despite advances in identifying genetic and molecular risk factors for conditions such as schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders, bridging the gap between cellular-level disruptions and system-level cognitive dysfunction remains a critical challenge. We propose to develop a multi-scale computational model integrating biophysically detailed cortical microcircuits with macroscale whole-brain dynamics derived from human neuroimaging data. The model will simulate how localized synaptic pathology—specifically NMDA receptor hypofunction and GABAergic interneuron dysregulation—propagates to disrupt oscillatory coherence, functional connectivity, and information coding across prefrontal-hippocampal-thalamic networks. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of parameter space exploration across molecular, cellular, and network levels, requiring parallelized simulations of 10⁵-10⁶ spiking neurons with realistic synaptic plasticity rules. Machine learning pipelines will analyze simulated local field potentials and fMRI-derived functional connectivity patterns against empirical data from human patients and animal models. Expected outcomes include identification of critical control points in hierarchical neural systems where targeted interventions could restore cognitive processing, as well as predictive biomarkers of circuit-level vulnerability to synaptic dysfunction. This work will establish a computational framework for testing multiscale hypotheses about neuropsychiatric disease mechanisms while providing open-source tools for simulating brain network dynamics at unprecedented resolution. The requested resources will enable parameter optimization across biologically plausible ranges, statistical validation against multi-modal datasets, and systematic exploration of therapeutic intervention strategies in silico.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary scientific study of the molecular, structural, physiologic, cognitive, and behavioral aspects of the brain and nervous system. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, molecular and biochemical bases of information processing, behavioral neuroscience, biology of neuropsychiatric disorders, and applications to the clinical sciences and biomedical engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance pharmacoeconomic and policy analyses evaluating the cost-effectiveness, accessibility, and regulatory impacts of novel therapies in the U.S. healthcare system. A critical challenge in pharmacy administration is modeling complex interactions between drug pricing, insurance reimbursement policies, patient outcomes, and health system budgets, particularly as high-cost biologics, gene therapies, and specialty medications enter markets. Existing decision-analytic models often oversimplify dynamic factors such as regional formulary variability, adherence patterns, and long-term population health outcomes. To address this, we propose developing a scalable microsimulation framework integrating real-world data from Medicare Part D claims, FDA approval timelines, and manufacturer pricing databases. Agent-based modeling will capture stakeholder behaviors (e.g., prescribers, payers, patients) under varying policy scenarios, while parallelized discrete-event simulations will project 10-year budget impacts across health systems. Machine learning methods (e.g., ensemble models, natural language processing) will be applied to unstructured regulatory documents and prior authorization records to identify predictors of coverage restrictions. Computational demands are substantial: parameter sweeps across 50+ policy variables, bootstrap analyses for uncertainty quantification, and processing of multi-terabyte claims datasets require distributed-memory clusters and GPU-accelerated workloads. Anticipated outcomes include (1) granular cost-benefit estimates for emerging drug pricing models (e.g., outcome-based contracts), (2) policy simulations quantifying the population health effects of Medicaid drug rebate reforms, and (3) open-source tools for rapid analysis of state/federal regulatory proposals. Results will inform pharmacy benefit managers, health systems, and policymakers in balancing medication access with financial sustainability, directly aligning with the program’s focus on evidence-based pharmacy services management and regulatory risk assessment. HPC resources are essential to achieve the spatial-temporal resolution and computational throughput required for actionable, stakeholder-specific insights.
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize additive manufacturing (AM) processes for advanced metallic alloys, addressing critical challenges in defect formation and microstructure control. Current AM techniques suffer from inconsistent mechanical properties due to rapid, non-uniform thermal gradients and residual stresses, which are difficult to predict using conventional modeling tools. To overcome these limitations, the proposed research will employ multi-physics simulations integrating thermal, fluid dynamics, and solid mechanics models to capture the complex interactions during laser-powder bed fusion. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale melt pool dynamics, track phase transformations, and predict stress evolution across macroscale part geometries. A hybrid approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-based surrogate models will be implemented to reduce computational costs while maintaining accuracy. The simulations will be validated against synchrotron X-ray imaging and electron backscatter diffraction data from collaborative experimental trials. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for optimizing laser parameters, scan strategies, and support structures to minimize defects such as porosity and cracking. This work will advance the fundamental understanding of process-structure-property relationships in AM, enabling the reliable production of high-performance components for aerospace and energy applications. The requested HPC allocation will support large-scale parametric studies (>10,000 core-hours) requiring parallelized solvers and distributed memory architectures to handle datasets exceeding 50 TB. By bridging simulation scales and accelerating process development, this project aims to reduce trial-and-error costs by 30-40% and establish open-source benchmarks for the AM research community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of African-American/Black literary texts and oral traditions across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. While the cultural and aesthetic complexity of this literature—spanning novels, poetry, folklore, sermons, and musical forms like spirituals and hip-hop—has been richly documented, systematic computational studies of its linguistic patterns, thematic evolution, and intertextual networks remain limited. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to synthesize the vast, multilingual, and multimedia corpora that reflect the diaspora’s literary and folkloric diversity. This project addresses this gap by developing scalable text and audio analysis pipelines to map stylistic, rhetorical, and thematic connections across genres, periods, and regions. Computational methods include natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned on African-American vernacular English (AAVE) and Creole-language texts, network analysis to trace the circulation of motifs (e.g., trickster figures, ancestral memory), and machine learning classifiers to identify rhetorical strategies tied to resistance and cultural preservation. Audio recordings of oral narratives and performances will be processed using speech-to-text algorithms and spectral analysis to correlate linguistic features with rhythmic or tonal patterns. HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, training custom transformer-based models, and running parallelized analyses across hybrid text/audio workflows. Expected outcomes include a public digital archive of annotated texts and oral histories, visualizations of transnational literary networks, and new methodologies for computational humanities research centered on African diasporic contexts. By integrating computational rigor with cultural specificity, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of how Black literary traditions innovate, adapt, and sustain collective memory amid shifting sociopolitical landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and operation of hybrid energy systems integrating renewable generation, storage, and grid infrastructure. Current approaches struggle to balance efficiency, cost, and reliability due to the complex interdependencies between system components, fluctuating demand patterns, and uncertainties in renewable output. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled methodology combining multi-physics simulations with machine learning-driven optimization. Large-scale transient models will capture electromechanical, thermal, and chemical interactions across wind turbines, photovoltaic arrays, battery banks, and power electronics. These simulations will be coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms trained on historical weather and load data to identify control policies that minimize energy loss while maintaining stability under diverse operating conditions. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers for differential-algebraic equations and distributed neural network training across GPU clusters to manage the combinatorial complexity of multi-objective optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for scenario-based energy system analysis, quantitative benchmarks comparing hybrid configurations under regional climate constraints, and adaptive control strategies demonstrating ≥15% efficiency gains over rule-based methods in preliminary case studies. By enabling high-resolution modeling of integrated energy networks at scale, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making for sustainable infrastructure deployment while providing a template for HPC applications in energy technology education. The requested computing resources will support parametric sweeps across 10,000+ system permutations, long-horizon transient analyses, and comparative validation against experimental microgrid data from partner institutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing energy-efficient systems or monitoring energy use. Includes instruction in principles of energy conservation, instrumentation calibration, monitoring systems and test procedures, energy loss inspection procedures, energy conservation techniques, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the creation of immersive, interactive digital art by addressing the computational limitations inherent in real-time rendering, large-scale 3D environment simulation, and AI-driven generative design. Current workflows in digital arts—particularly in domains such as virtual reality (VR), procedural animation, and dynamic multimedia installations—often encounter bottlenecks when processing high-resolution assets, physics-based simulations, or neural network models for creative applications. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable complex, multi-layered workflows that integrate real-time ray tracing, photorealistic fluid and particle simulations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on large artistic datasets. The research will focus on three interconnected strands: (1) optimizing GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for 360-degree, 4K-resolution immersive environments; (2) simulating dynamic interactions between virtual materials, lighting, and soundscapes in interactive installations; and (3) developing hybrid human-AI co-creation tools that utilize distributed computing for rapid iteration of generative design outputs. By utilizing parallel processing and high-memory nodes, the project aims to reduce latency in real-time applications by 40–60% compared to conventional workstations, while scaling generative model training efficiency for datasets exceeding 10TB of multimodal artistic content. Outcomes will include open-source frameworks for computationally intensive digital arts workflows, validated through case studies in collaborative VR storytelling and AI-augmented motion graphics. This work will expand the technical and creative possibilities for digital artists, offering new methodologies for integrating cutting-edge computational tools into artistic practice while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between arts and computational sciences. The resource allocation will directly support faculty and student researchers in developing scalable, reproducible workflows with potential applications in gaming, virtual production, and public interactive art installations.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the use of computerized digital images as the primary medium of expression in the visual and performing arts, and that may prepare individuals for a wide variety of careers using new media, including graphic design, digital animation, motion graphics, 3D visualization, game and interactive media design, music and sound design, video production, web design, photography, and other fields.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the documentation, analysis, and revitalization of endangered Indigenous languages across the Americas. Many Native American languages exhibit complex morphological structures, intricate verb systems, and unique phonological patterns that challenge conventional linguistic analysis tools. The research problem centers on scaling computational methods to process large, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized oral histories, legacy texts, and modern speech recordings—across diverse language families such as Uto-Aztecan, Mayan, and Algonquian. Current software tools for morphological parsing, acoustic analysis, and corpus linguistics are not optimized for these languages’ typological features, nor do they efficiently handle the volume of multimodal data required for robust analysis. The project will employ parallelized workflows on HPC clusters to train neural models for automated morphological segmentation and syntactic annotation, conduct phylogenetic analyses of language diversification using Bayesian inference frameworks, and simulate sound change trajectories across dialect networks. These computational tasks demand significant memory allocation and multi-node processing due to the iterative nature of probabilistic modeling and the need to cross-reference thousands of lexical items across related languages. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access computational lexicons, enhanced speech recognition models for under-resourced languages, and phylogenetic trees that clarify historical relationships among language varieties. By integrating computational linguistics with community-driven documentation efforts, this work will provide scalable infrastructure for both academic research and Indigenous language revitalization programs, addressing critical gaps in linguistic theory while supporting cultural preservation imperatives. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity inherent in analyzing polysynthetic languages and to ensure equitable access to advanced computational methods for Indigenous language scholars.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: American Indian/ Native American Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the Western Hemisphere, with an emphasis on American Indian languages, but including other Native American languages. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; Inuit and Aleut languages; North American language families, including, but not limited to, Algonkian, Athabascan, Siouan, Muskogean, Iroquoian, Kumeyaay, Yuman, Mayan, Zapotecan, and Uto-Aztecan; South American language families, including, but not limited to, Andean-Equatorial, Ge-Pano-Carib, and Macro-Chibchan; and other minor languages.

abstract: The integrity and functionality of red blood cells (RBCs) during storage are critical for successful transfusions, yet current storage protocols rely on empirical data with limited understanding of biochemical degradation mechanisms. Prolonged storage leads to progressive RBC membrane damage, metabolic dysfunction, and reduced post-transfusion viability, contributing to adverse patient outcomes and significant resource waste in blood banks. This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to model RBC degradation under varied storage conditions, enabling data-driven optimization of preservation strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform multiscale simulations integrating molecular dynamics to study membrane protein interactions and agent-based models to track metabolic pathway alterations over time. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulation outputs alongside experimental hematology data—including morphology metrics, oxidative stress markers, and adenosine triphosphate levels—to identify key predictors of RBC viability. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro studies measuring hemolysis rates and microfluidic-based deformability assays. By elucidating the temporal dynamics of storage-induced damage, this work aims to establish predictive guidelines for storage solution composition, temperature thresholds, and maximum shelf life. The resulting models will provide a foundation for designing next-generation preservatives and personalized storage protocols tailored to donor-specific RBC characteristics. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational biology, hematology, and clinical transfusion medicine, addressing an unmet need in blood bank technology through advanced resource-efficient computational methodologies. Anticipated outcomes include reduced RBC discard rates, improved transfusion efficacy, and enhanced safety profiles for recipients, with broader implications for managing rare blood types and cellular therapy products.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists and health care professionals, to perform tests and analyses of blood samples. Includes instruction in clinical laboratory procedures; blood anatomy and physiology; cellular and molecular biology; blood pathology and disease indicators; quantitative, qualitative, and coagulation testing methodologies; equipment operation and maintenance; and record-keeping.

abstract: The increasing complexity of delivering equitable special education services, compounded by evolving legal mandates and heterogeneous student needs, necessitates data-driven strategies to optimize resource allocation and program administration. Current approaches to managing individualized education programs (IEPs), staffing, and budgetary decisions often rely on fragmented datasets and heuristic methods, limiting scalability and adaptability across diverse districts. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate resource allocation scenarios in special education administration, enabling evidence-based decision-making under constraints. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets from K-12 districts (including IEP records, staffing patterns, budget allocations, and student outcome metrics), we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between administrators, educators, students, and resources. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to run large-scale parameter sweeps analyzing how variables such as disability type prevalence, staff-to-student ratios, and funding fluctuations impact service delivery efficacy. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive patterns in historical data, while optimization algorithms will propose resource distribution strategies that balance compliance, cost-effectiveness, and student outcomes. The computational pipeline will integrate geospatial analysis to account for regional disparities in resource availability. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating policy impacts, actionable metrics for benchmarking district performance, and adaptive models to project resource needs under demographic or regulatory changes. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process multi-terabyte datasets and computationally intensive simulations, this work aims to advance administrative practices in special education, ultimately supporting more equitable and efficient systems for over 7 million students with disabilities in U.S. public schools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage programs for exceptional students and their parents. Includes instruction in special education theory and practice, special education program development, evaluation and assessment in special education, state and federal law and regulations, managing individual education plans, problems of low- and high- disability students, mainstreaming, special education curricula, staff management, parent education, communications and community relations, budgeting, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the resilience of urban infrastructure systems under climate change and population growth stressors, with a focus on integrated water, transportation, and structural networks. Current models often analyze these systems in isolation or rely on simplified assumptions, limiting their capacity to capture cascading failures during extreme events such as floods or heatwaves. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a coupled simulation approach combining agent-based traffic modeling, finite element structural analysis, and hydrodynamic flood prediction to evaluate interdependencies across systems. The computational workflow will integrate real-time sensor data from municipal networks with probabilistic climate projections to simulate multi-hazard scenarios at city-scale resolution. Key challenges include managing the high dimensionality of spatiotemporal datasets, resolving nonlinear interactions between physical and human systems, and scaling iterative optimization algorithms for Pareto-efficient resource allocation. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of scenario permutations using adaptive mesh refinement for flood modeling and GPU-accelerated machine learning to identify critical failure thresholds. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source platform for coupled infrastructure resilience assessment, (2) probabilistic risk maps identifying vulnerable nodes in transportation corridors and water distribution networks, and (3) decision support tools for prioritizing climate adaptation investments. This work directly addresses the growing need for computational methods that bridge civil engineering domains while accounting for environmental variability, with potential applications in urban planning, emergency management, and infrastructure policy. The scalability of the framework will be demonstrated through case studies on mid-sized coastal cities experiencing compound flooding and sea-level rise pressures.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures. Combines instruction in civil and environmental engineering.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of environmental contaminants and emerging xenobiotics poses significant risks to animal health, food safety, and ecosystem resilience. Veterinary toxicology and pharmacology face critical challenges in predicting toxicokinetic outcomes across species, elucidating molecular mechanisms of toxin action, and designing targeted antidotes. Traditional experimental approaches are limited by interspecies variability, ethical constraints, and the combinatorial complexity of toxin interactions with biological systems. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models that integrate pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) principles, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to address these gaps. We propose to simulate xenobiotic metabolism pathways across diverse animal species, including livestock and wildlife, using all-atom MD to map toxin-receptor binding affinities and predict neuropharmacological effects. Concurrently, ensemble ML models will be trained on heterogeneous datasets—including toxicogenomic profiles, pesticide residue analytics, and historical poisoning cases—to identify biomarkers of drug resistance and prioritize antidote candidates. HPC resources will enable large-scale virtual screening of chemical libraries against toxin targets, such as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, while accounting for genetic polymorphisms in detoxification enzymes. The computational framework will also model environmental toxin dispersion dynamics to assess species-specific exposure risks. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for interspecies extrapolation of toxicity thresholds, optimized dosing regimens for veterinary antidotes, and mechanistic insights into neurotoxicant action. These advances will directly inform regulatory policies for agrochemicals, improve therapeutic strategies for poisoned animals, and reduce reliance on in vivo testing. By bridging computational toxicology and veterinary pharmacology, this work aims to enhance the resilience of animal populations to evolving chemical threats while supporting sustainable agricultural practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of specific environmental and food hazards affecting domestic and wild animals and the development and action of chemical antidotes and treatments. Includes instruction in small and large animal toxicology and pharmacology, neurotoxicology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, neuropharmacology, xenobiotics, drug resistance, pesticides, toxicological pathology, genetic and molecular toxicology, environmental toxicology, drug and toxicant analysis and evaluation, and environmental radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing adaptive, evidence-based curricula that respond to heterogeneous learner needs in K-12 STEM education. Despite advances in learning sciences, curriculum development often relies on static, one-size-fits-all frameworks that inadequately account for variability in student backgrounds, cognitive processes, and real-time engagement patterns. The research aims to develop a computational model for dynamically optimizing curriculum sequences and instructional materials using multimodal learner data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process large-scale datasets comprising student interaction logs, formative assessments, and eye-tracking metrics from digital learning platforms. Machine learning techniques, including transformer-based architectures and reinforcement learning, will be employed to simulate learning trajectories across diverse student profiles and identify curriculum configurations that maximize conceptual understanding. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze semantic relationships within instructional content to evaluate coherence and prerequisite dependencies. The computational workflow involves iterative simulation of curriculum variants, validation against empirical learning outcomes, and sensitivity analyses to quantify how minor adjustments in content sequencing affect longitudinal performance. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for curriculum personalization, empirically grounded design principles for modular instructional materials, and open-source tools for curriculum analytics. By enabling real-time adaptation of educational content at scale, this work advances theoretical understanding of curriculum-design principles while providing practical resources for educators to implement data-driven instructional strategies. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s computational intensity, particularly the parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and the training of deep learning models with numerous hyperparameter configurations. Results will contribute to reducing disparities in STEM achievement through more equitable, responsive curriculum design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the curriculum and related instructional processes and tools, and that may prepare individuals to serve as professional curriculum specialists. Includes instruction in curriculum theory, curriculum design and planning, instructional material design and evaluation, curriculum evaluation, and applications to specific subject matter, programs or educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of cardiopulmonary interactions in patients with complex cardiovascular and respiratory comorbidities. Despite the interdependence of cardiac and pulmonary systems in conditions such as pulmonary hypertension, heart failure, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), current diagnostic and therapeutic protocols often address these systems in isolation. This gap limits the ability to predict disease progression or optimize interventions for patients with overlapping pathologies. To address this, we propose developing multiscale computational models that integrate hemodynamic, respiratory, and gas-exchange dynamics using patient-specific clinical data, including echocardiograph readings, pulmonary function tests, and arterial blood gas analyses. The models will employ finite element methods to simulate blood flow through cardiac chambers and pulmonary vasculature, coupled with agent-based modeling of alveolar oxygen-carbon dioxide exchange. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify patterns in retrospective patient datasets, enabling the calibration of model parameters to individual physiological variability. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the real-time coupling of 3D fluid dynamics with systemic physiological responses—necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of simulating disease trajectories under varying therapeutic scenarios (e.g., ventilator adjustments, vasodilator therapies) and the identification of novel biomarkers for early detection of cardiopulmonary decompensation. Successful validation against clinical outcomes will provide a framework for personalized treatment planning and inform the development of next-generation decision-support tools for cardiopulmonary technologists. By elucidating system-level interactions, this research aims to bridge the current divide between cardiovascular and pulmonary care paradigms, ultimately improving outcomes for patients with multisystem dysfunction. The requested computing resources will enable the iterative refinement of models and ensure scalability for future integration into clinical research protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to perform both cardiovascular and pulmonary diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Includes instruction in cardiopulmonary pharmacology; anatomy and physiology of the heart, peripheral vascular system, and lungs; pulmonary and cardiovascular disease and dysfunction; peripheral vascular Doppler procedures; invasive and non-invasive cardiology; pulmonary function tests; blood gas analysis; echocardiograph procedures; bronchoscopy; patient management; patient history taking and record-keeping; applications to clinical research; and emergency procedures.

abstract: Play therapy is a critical intervention for addressing childhood psychological disorders, yet the field lacks robust computational tools to analyze complex, multimodal interactions within therapeutic sessions. Current methods for assessing play therapy efficacy rely heavily on qualitative observation and manual coding, which are time-intensive, subject to human bias, and unable to capture dynamic, non-verbal cues such as micro-expressions, play patterns, or physiological responses in real time. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to quantitatively evaluate therapist-child interactions, model therapeutic outcomes, and identify predictors of successful interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets comprising video recordings, wearable sensor data (e.g., heart rate, motion tracking), and longitudinal clinical outcomes from diverse pediatric populations. Machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for visual pattern recognition and transformer-based architectures for temporal sequence analysis, will be trained to classify therapeutic techniques, correlate behavioral markers with symptom reduction, and simulate intervention scenarios. Additionally, generative AI methods will be explored to create synthetic datasets for training and validating models while adhering to ethical guidelines for patient data privacy. The computational demands of processing high-resolution video streams, synchronizing multimodal data, and iteratively refining deep learning architectures necessitate scalable HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for play therapy analytics, predictive models to personalize interventions, and novel insights into the neurobehavioral mechanisms underlying play therapy’s effectiveness. This work will directly support the training of Registered Play Therapists by providing evidence-based tools to refine clinical practice, enhance supervisory feedback, and advance standardized metrics for accreditation. By integrating computational innovation with developmental psychology, the project aims to bridge a critical gap in child mental health research and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: The rapid development of quantum computing necessitates efficient classical simulation tools to validate quantum algorithms and benchmark emerging hardware. However, simulating large-scale quantum systems remains computationally prohibitive due to the exponential scaling of state vector representations, with existing methods struggling beyond 40 qubits. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by developing optimized simulation frameworks leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose a hybrid approach integrating tensor network decomposition techniques with machine learning-driven optimization of contraction paths, significantly reducing memory and computational overhead. The computational workload will be parallelized across distributed GPU nodes, exploiting sparsity in quantum circuits through dynamic task scheduling and adaptive load balancing. Additionally, we will implement domain-specific compiler optimizations to accelerate tensor operations within heterogeneous computing architectures. The expected outcomes include the ability to simulate quantum circuits exceeding 50 qubits with higher fidelity than current state-of-the-art tools, enabling the exploration of error mitigation strategies and the co-design of quantum-classical algorithms. This research will produce open-source software modules compatible with existing quantum development kits, fostering collaboration across academia and industry. By addressing critical bottlenecks in quantum simulation, this work aims to accelerate progress toward practical quantum advantage in areas such as cryptography, optimization, and materials modeling, while providing foundational insights into the resource requirements of scalable quantum computing systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for executing large-scale simulations, training neural network models on circuit datasets, and validating performance across diverse hardware configurations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical threat to global public health, necessitating advanced computational approaches to unravel the molecular mechanisms driving resistance and accelerate therapeutic discovery. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model bacterial genomic evolution under selective drug pressure, predict resistance-conferring mutations, and identify potential targets for next-generation antibiotics. The research focuses on multidrug-resistant pathogens prioritized by the WHO, including *Acinetobacter baumannii* and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae. Current limitations in experimental throughput and the sheer scale of genomic-phenotypic datasets hinder progress; HPC-enabled workflows are essential to address these gaps. Computational methods will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of bacterial enzymes (e.g., beta-lactamases, efflux pumps) with machine learning models trained on multi-omic datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic profiles from clinical isolates). These simulations will map free-energy landscapes of drug-target interactions under mutation scenarios, while neural networks will predict resistance phenotypes from sequence data. Parallelized phylogenetic analyses will reconstruct evolutionary trajectories of resistance genes across bacterial populations. The project requires significant GPU and CPU resources for large-scale simulations, distributed training of deep learning models, and comparative genomics workflows. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of high-risk mutation pathways associated with emergent resistance, (2) predictive frameworks for resistance gene dissemination, and (3) prioritized drug candidates with reduced susceptibility to resistance mechanisms. By bridging structural biology, population genomics, and AI-driven predictive modeling, this work will provide actionable insights for stewardship programs and drug development pipelines, directly addressing the urgent need for computational innovation in AMR mitigation.
cip_definition: Any program in medicine, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex dynamics of legislative decision-making in polarized political environments, focusing on how partisan alignment and interest group lobbying interact to shape policy outcomes. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions and large-scale data inherent in modern legislative processes. To address this gap, the research employs a dual computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques. The ABM framework simulates legislators as autonomous agents with varying ideological preferences, party affiliations, and responsiveness to interest group pressures, enabling the exploration of emergent outcomes under different institutional rules and coalition structures. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze historical legislative datasets spanning multiple parliamentary systems to identify patterns in bill passage rates, amendment adoption, and coalition formation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for executing thousands of parallelized ABM simulations with heterogeneous parameter configurations and processing terabyte-scale legislative text corpora through deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model quantifying the relative impact of ideological polarization versus external lobbying on legislative efficiency, (2) predictive tools for assessing the viability of proposed legislation under varying political conditions, and (3) comparative insights into institutional designs that mitigate policy stagnation. By integrating computational social science methodologies with substantive political theory, this research aims to advance empirical understanding of democratic governance while providing scalable analytical frameworks for political scientists studying legislative behavior across different governmental systems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the systematic study of political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in political philosophy, political theory, comparative government and politics, political parties and interest groups, public opinion, political research methods, studies of the government and politics of specific countries, and studies of specific political institutions and processes.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the long-term socio-political impacts of colonial-era administrative systems on contemporary governance structures in postcolonial states. Combining archival historiography with computational political science, the study integrates unstructured historical records (e.g., colonial correspondence, policy drafts, and regional reports) and structured modern governance datasets (e.g., legislative voting patterns, public expenditure records, and electoral outcomes) across 12 former British and French colonies. The central research problem lies in disentangling path-dependent institutional behaviors from emergent political adaptations, particularly how colonial bureaucratic frameworks persist or dissolve in modern administrative systems. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of multi-century, cross-regional datasets, necessitating advanced computational approaches. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract relational data from digitized colonial documents, coupled with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate institutional evolution under varying historical constraints. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of multilingual archival texts (∼8TB) and iterative ABM runs testing 50+ governance variables across 10,000+ simulated policy cycles. Expected outcomes include a computational historiography framework for identifying institutional "echoes" in modern political systems, predictive models of decolonial policy diffusion, and open-access tools for interdisciplinary temporal analysis. Results will advance comparative historical analysis methodologies while informing contemporary policy design in transitional democracies. The project’s computational demands—particularly GPU-accelerated NLP training and high-memory ABM ensembles—exceed local institutional capacities, requiring dedicated HPC allocations to achieve statistically robust, temporally granular insights at this unprecedented geographic and temporal scope.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and political science or a specialization which draws from history and political science. Includes instruction in comparative government and politics, historiography, historical research methods, political science, political theory, records administration, and systematic study of political institutions and behavior.

abstract: Veterinary internal medicine faces significant challenges in diagnosing and managing complex, multifactorial diseases in animals, such as chronic kidney disease, endocrine disorders, and immune-mediated conditions. These conditions often involve intricate interactions between genetic, environmental, and clinical factors that are poorly characterized using conventional analytical methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of disease progression and treatment response by integrating multi-modal datasets, including genomic sequences, longitudinal clinical records, proteomic profiles, and behavioral data from companion animals. A primary focus is on analyzing high-dimensional datasets from feline and canine patients with diabetes mellitus, a condition with heterogeneous presentation and suboptimal management outcomes. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms, such as gradient-boosted ensembles and graph neural networks, to identify biomarkers, stratify disease subtypes, and simulate treatment scenarios. Agent-based modeling will be implemented to study population-level impacts of diagnostic referral patterns and aging-related comorbidities. The scale of data integration—encompassing over 10,000 patient records and terabyte-scale omics data—necessitates distributed computing architectures for parallelized feature engineering and hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for clinical decision support, open-source diagnostic algorithms tailored to veterinary workflows, and novel insights into conserved pathophysiological mechanisms across species. By enabling rapid analysis of complex clinical datasets, this research aims to advance evidence-based veterinary care, reduce diagnostic delays, and establish computational frameworks adaptable to other non-surgical conditions in aging animal populations. The proposed HPC resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in processing capacity and model complexity, directly addressing unmet needs in veterinary translational research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of general medical services to animals with a wide range of non-surgical clinical problems. May included related research in behavioral aspects of diseases, animal diagnosis, animal aging, and referral procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in clinical esthetics through the development of a predictive modeling framework for personalized skin treatment protocols. While esthetic practice traditionally relies on manual assessment and generalized treatment plans, emerging demands for hyper-personalized care—particularly in post-operative or dermatologically complex cases—require data-driven approaches to optimize outcomes. The primary challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets (e.g., high-resolution skin imaging, longitudinal treatment responses, biometric sensor data, and patient-reported outcomes) to model individualized skin healing trajectories and treatment efficacy. The computational approach will employ machine learning architectures, including graph neural networks to capture spatial relationships in layered skin structures and transformer-based models for temporal pattern recognition in treatment response data. High-fidelity simulations of biochemical interactions between topical agents and diverse skin phenotypes will be implemented using molecular dynamics toolkits adapted for cosmetic formulations. By analyzing multi-modal data from 10,000+ anonymized clinical cases (spanning Fitzpatrick skin types I-VI and common comorbidities), the project aims to generate predictive algorithms that recommend optimal treatment sequences, minimize adverse reactions, and forecast recovery timelines. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for licensed estheticians to simulate treatment impacts prior to application, reducing trial-and-error practices in sensitive cases. The work bridges clinical esthetics with computational biology, establishing a novel framework for evidence-based practice in an understudied domain. Access to HPC resources is critical given the need for parallel processing of 3D skin model simulations and real-time optimization of treatment parameters across large datasets. This research directly addresses gaps in standardized protocols for medical esthetics, with potential applications in telehealth platforms and postoperative care coordination.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and body with advanced chemical and cosmetic preparations and esthetic medical treatments, and to function as licensed master or medical estheticians in dermatologists' and plastic surgeons' offices as well as in salons and spas. Includes instruction in advanced anatomy and physiology, skin properties and disorders, sanitation and infection control, advanced facial treatments, spa body treatments, advanced extractions, corrective makeup, chemical peels, microdermabrasion, lymphatic drainage and advanced massage techniques, pre- and post-operative esthetic skin care, client/patient evaluation and care, applicable laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Tribal/Indigenous Law, specifically addressing the challenge of analyzing complex, large-scale legal and cultural datasets critical to understanding the interplay between tribal sovereignty, historical treaties, and contemporary legal frameworks. Tribal legal systems and Indigenous rights discourse generate multifaceted data, including digitized historical records, oral histories, treaty texts, court decisions, and ethnographic materials, which are often fragmented across repositories or embedded in non-standardized formats. Traditional legal research methods struggle to synthesize these datasets at scale, limiting insights into systemic patterns of rights violations, policy impacts, or cultural preservation needs. The proposed research will employ computational text analysis, network modeling, and machine learning techniques to (1) identify correlations between historical treaty language and modern judicial interpretations, (2) map the evolution of tribal governance structures in response to federal policies, and (3) simulate the potential impacts of proposed legislation on Indigenous resource rights. Custom NLP pipelines will process multilingual and non-textual sources (e.g., oral tradition transcripts), while graph-based algorithms will model relationships between legal entities across temporal and jurisdictional boundaries. HPC resources are essential to handle the volume and heterogeneity of data, enable parallel processing of linguistically diverse materials, and support iterative scenario testing. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for tribal legal practitioners, policy simulations to inform advocacy strategies, and novel methodologies for centering Indigenous epistemologies in sociolegal data analysis. This work bridges computational social science and critical legal studies, offering a model for ethically engaged, community-responsive research that amplifies Indigenous self-determination in legal discourse.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting federal Indian law, tribal law and policy, and Indigenous peoples' human rights.

abstract: Understanding population dynamics in the context of rapid environmental and societal change requires advanced computational tools to model complex interactions between individual behaviors and macro-level demographic trends. This project seeks to investigate how environmental stressors, such as extreme weather events and resource scarcity, interact with social networks and policy interventions to shape migration patterns and population redistribution. Traditional demographic models often struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback loops and heterogeneous decision-making processes that drive these phenomena. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) that simulates individual and household-level migration decisions under varying environmental and policy scenarios. The ABM will integrate spatially explicit environmental data, longitudinal demographic surveys, and policy records to parameterize agents’ adaptive behaviors. Given the scale of simulation—encompassing millions of agents over multi-decadal timeframes—high-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for parallelizing computational workloads, optimizing parameter space exploration, and enabling real-time visualization of emergent population patterns. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into how targeted policy measures could mitigate displacement risks in climate-vulnerable regions, as well as methodological advances in coupling demographic theory with computational social science frameworks. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance the granularity and predictive accuracy of demographic models, providing a replicable toolkit for studying complex socio-environmental systems. The results will contribute to interdisciplinary dialogues on sustainable development while addressing a critical gap in demography’s capacity to inform adaptive governance in an era of global change.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in demography, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize additive manufacturing processes for complex, multi-material structures, addressing critical gaps in process reliability and material efficiency. Current approaches struggle to predict thermo-mechanical distortions and interfacial defects in heterogeneous material systems due to the interplay of rapid phase changes, residual stresses, and anisotropic thermal gradients. To overcome these limitations, the research will implement a coupled finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) model, integrated with machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale melt pool dynamics and layer-wise stress accumulation across macro-scale geometries, which require parallelized simulations across millions of elements. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for thermal-fluid interactions and distributed memory architectures for stochastic defect propagation analysis. Key outcomes include predictive models for defect formation under varying process parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed) and a generative design tool to recommend material-specific printing strategies. Successful validation against experimental tomography and strain gauge data will establish a benchmark for virtual process certification. By reducing trial-and-error iterations in industrial settings, this work aims to lower energy consumption by 15–20% in metal additive manufacturing and enable reliable production of load-bearing components with embedded sensors. The proposed framework will be disseminated as open-source modules to support workforce training in advanced manufacturing technologies, aligning with national priorities for sustainable industrial innovation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the analysis of spinal biomechanics and radiographic imaging data in chiropractic care, with the goal of improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning for neuromusculoskeletal disorders. Chiropractic technicians routinely assist in evaluating complex datasets, including dynamic spinal motion, X-ray films, and patient-specific clinical metrics. However, current manual and semi-automated methods for interpreting these data are time-intensive and prone to variability, particularly in identifying subtle biomechanical imbalances or early degenerative changes. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on aggregated de-identified patient datasets, including high-resolution radiographic images, kinematic recordings, and electronic health records. These models will be optimized to detect patterns associated with spinal misalignment, disc degeneration, and soft tissue dysfunction, while finite element simulations will model spinal load distributions under varying therapeutic interventions.
