The computational workflow will integrate Python-based image processing libraries (e.g., OpenCV), TensorFlow for deep learning tasks, and ANSYS for biomechanical simulations, requiring parallelized processing to manage large-scale datasets (10,000+ images) and complex multiphysics models. Successful implementation will yield two key outcomes: (1) an open-source toolset for automated radiographic anomaly detection and biomechanical risk stratification, validated against clinician assessments, and (2) a simulation platform to predict patient-specific responses to chiropractic adjustments, reducing trial-and-error in treatment protocols. By providing chiropractic technicians with advanced computational decision-support tools, this work aims to streamline clinical workflows, enhance educational training through data-driven case studies, and contribute to evidence-based practices in spinal health management. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational scale and speed for model training and simulation, which cannot be feasibly executed on local workstations given memory and processing constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a chiropractor, to provide patient management, examination, and treatment services. Includes instruction in the principles and procedures of chiropractic, radiographic X-Ray procedures and techniques, X-Ray film analysis and media studies, orthopedic and neurological testing, clinical laboratory procedures, patient management and education, office administrative skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of symbiotic microbial communities in mediating heat tolerance in agriculturally significant entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs). EPNs are critical biocontrol agents for insect pests, but their efficacy declines under rising soil temperatures linked to climate change. While prior studies focus on nematode physiology, the contribution of their native microbiota to thermal resilience remains uncharacterized. This project integrates metagenomic sequencing, metabolic network modeling, and agent-based simulations to elucidate how symbiotic bacteria influence EPN survival and insect host infection dynamics under thermal stress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process terabase-scale metagenomic datasets from heat-exposed nematode populations, reconstruct strain-specific metabolic models for 200+ bacterial symbionts, and simulate host-microbe interactions across spatial temperature gradients. Custom computational pipelines will identify thermal response genes in symbiont genomes, predict metabolite exchange networks sustaining nematode energetics, and model population-scale shifts in EPN foraging behavior under simulated warming scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting climate-driven disruptions in nematode biocontrol efficacy, identification of candidate thermal-protective symbionts for agricultural inoculation, and foundational insights into the evolution of metazoan-microbe thermo-adaptation. By bridging microbial ecology, thermodynamics, and population dynamics, this work establishes a new computational paradigm for studying symbiosis in invertebrate systems while addressing urgent needs in sustainable pest management. The requested resources will enable previously intractable analyses of multi-species metabolic coupling and large-scale parameter space exploration essential for translating microbial community dynamics into predictive conservation tools.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) and insect species/populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern hybrid cloud ecosystems has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource management frameworks, particularly for organizations operating across distributed, multi-vendor IT infrastructures. This project addresses the challenge of real-time resource optimization in heterogeneous computing environments where traditional static allocation strategies fail to account for dynamic workload patterns, energy efficiency constraints, and evolving security requirements. We propose developing a novel decision architecture that integrates graph-based workload modeling with reinforcement learning to enable context-aware resource distribution. The computational approach will leverage temporal graph neural networks to model infrastructure interdependencies while training multi-objective reinforcement learning agents on HPC clusters to simultaneously optimize for latency, energy consumption, and fault tolerance. Key innovations include a differentiable simulation environment for hybrid cloud systems and a federated learning component that preserves organizational data sovereignty during model training. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process real-world workload traces spanning 10,000+ node infrastructures, requiring parallelized training of multiple reinforcement learning agents across GPU nodes and large-scale graph processing capabilities for dependency analysis. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive resource orchestration that demonstrates 30-50% improvements in resource utilization efficiency compared to current industry standards, along with new metrics for quantifying resilience-energy tradeoffs in distributed systems. This work bridges computational systems engineering with operational IT management, advancing capabilities for next-generation sustainable computing infrastructure while establishing formal methods for intelligent service administration in complex, evolving technological ecosystems.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical and energetic mechanisms underlying Polarity Therapy, an integrative health approach centered on the Human Energy Field (HEF) theory, using advanced computational modeling. Despite its clinical application in energy-based healing, the quantitative dynamics of HEF interactions with physiological systems remain poorly characterized, limiting evidence-based validation and protocol optimization. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models integrating principles of polarity theory with empirical biomechanical, bioelectrical, and biochemical datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable finite element simulations of energy flow patterns across anatomical regions, molecular dynamics analyses of hypothesized biofield-cellular interactions, and machine learning-driven correlations between therapeutic interventions (e.g., polarity bodywork, yoga postures) and physiological outcomes (e.g., autonomic nervous system responses, cytokine profiles). The computational framework will incorporate clinical data from electromyography, heart rate variability monitoring, and patient-reported outcomes to parameterize energy field dynamics. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of therapist-client energy exchanges during polarity processing sessions, simulating charge distribution and resonance effects theorized in HEF theory. The project will also employ neural networks to identify predictive signatures linking specific energetic interventions to therapeutic outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. Expected outcomes include validated models of energy field modulation mechanisms, optimized treatment parameters for common health conditions, and open-source tools for simulating polarity-based interventions. By elucidating quantifiable connections between energy medicine principles and measurable biological effects, this work aims to advance Polarity Therapy’s scientific foundation, enhance clinical training protocols, and inform personalized treatment strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling complex simulations of nonlinear energy systems, large-scale data integration, and iterative model refinement, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote health and well-being through application of the integrative therapeutic system based on the Human Energy Field theory developed by Randolph Stone. Includes instruction in polarity theory and principles, energy-based and orthodox anatomy and physiology, polarity processing, polarity bodywork, polarity yoga, energetic nutrition, energetic evaluation and assessment, client communication, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Emerging zoonotic diseases at the human-wildlife interface present complex challenges shaped by ecological dynamics, host-pathogen evolution, and anthropogenic environmental change. This project seeks to quantify how landscape fragmentation and wildlife community composition interact to drive cross-species transmission risk for priority pathogens in tropical biodiversity hotspots. We propose developing an integrative computational framework combining high-resolution spatial datasets of land-use change, wildlife movement ecology, and longitudinal pathogen surveillance data from bat reservoirs in Southeast Asia. Agent-based models will simulate host foraging behavior under varying habitat connectivity scenarios, while Bayesian phylodynamic models will reconstruct viral evolutionary trajectories from genomic data. A novel spatial metapopulation component will incorporate host immune landscape heterogeneity derived from eco-immunological field sampling. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage iterative parameterization of stochastic transmission models across 10⁶ simulated landscapes, parallelized phylogenetic inference for 15,000+ viral sequences, and real-time integration of satellite-derived forest cover data at 30m resolution. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical habitat thresholds amplifying spillover risk through host crowding and immune depletion, (2) predictive maps of evolutionarily vulnerable viral lineages based on host shifting potential, and (3) open-source tools for coupling ecological metacommunity dynamics with pathogen genomic surveillance. This work addresses a fundamental gap in spatial epidemiology by unifying ecological scaling principles with evolutionary predictors of cross-species transmission, directly informing planetary health strategies at the nexus of conservation and pandemic prevention. The requested GPU nodes and distributed memory architecture will enable processing of petabyte-scale remote sensing inputs while maintaining phylogenetic likelihood calculations for complex evolutionary models.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of epidemiology and biostatistics or a specialization which draws from epidemiology and biostatistics. Includes instruction in biostatistics, disease and injury determinants, epidemiology, health services research, pathology, spatial analysis, and statistics.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational modeling into earth science education remains underdeveloped, limiting educators’ ability to teach complex, dynamic Earth systems effectively. This project seeks to address this gap by developing high-resolution, interactive simulations of geological, atmospheric, and hydrological processes tailored for pedagogical use. A critical barrier lies in the computational demands of rendering spatially and temporally detailed models that balance scientific accuracy with accessibility for pre-service and in-service teachers. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to generate ensemble climate simulations, 3D geophysical visualizations, and real-time data assimilation workflows. These outputs will be processed into modular, classroom-ready tools via a cloud-based interface, enabling educators to explore scenarios such as regional climate change impacts, tectonic plate dynamics, or watershed management. The computational workflow will utilize existing Earth system models (e.g., CESM, WRF) and custom Python-based analysis pipelines to downscale global datasets to local contexts, a process requiring parallelized processing of terabyte-scale climate outputs. Machine learning methods will further optimize model reduction for educational use cases. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of adaptable teaching modules, paired with professional development frameworks to train educators in utilizing computational tools. This work will directly enhance the pedagogical capacity of Earth science teachers by bridging cutting-edge research with classroom practice, fostering data literacy and systems thinking in K-12 and undergraduate students. The requested HPC allocation is essential to achieve the necessary scale and resolution for robust, region-specific simulations while maintaining usability for non-specialist educators. By democratizing access to high-fidelity modeling resources, this project aims to transform how Earth systems science is taught, aligning instructional strategies with the computational realities of modern geoscience research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach earth science programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how adaptive instructional strategies in digital learning environments influence cognitive engagement and learning outcomes across diverse student populations. A critical challenge in learning sciences is disentangling the interplay between individualized learning pathways, socio-cultural contexts, and real-time cognitive states—a task requiring analysis of multimodal data streams (e.g., interaction logs, eye-tracking, physiological sensors, and discourse analytics) at scales that exceed conventional computational capabilities. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to process and model these large, heterogeneous datasets, enabling the identification of dynamic patterns in learning behaviors and instructional efficacy. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures to classify engagement states from temporal sensor data, natural language processing to analyze collaborative discourse, and agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about scaffolded instruction in varied socio-cultural contexts. Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify how individual differences (e.g., prior knowledge, language background) mediate responses to adaptive feedback. By parallelizing these analyses across GPU clusters, the project will achieve the throughput necessary to generalize findings across 10,000+ learners from globally diverse demographics. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing real-time instructional adjustments in digital platforms, validated metrics of context-sensitive cognitive engagement, and open-source tools for multimodal learning analytics. This work will advance theoretical models of situated learning while addressing equity gaps in adaptive education systems. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the project’s petabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local infrastructure.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the multiple aspects of learning in different environments, including specific aspects of the content to be mastered, cognitive aspects of the student, the instructional environment and materials, the preparation and activities of the instructor, socio-cultural and linguistic components, and assessment outcomes. Includes instruction in the social, organizational, and cultural dynamics of learning; learning and cognition; learning strategies; educational psychology; educational testing and measurement; instructional design and technology; and statistical design of educational research.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal analytics, an emerging interdisciplinary domain intersecting legal research, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning (ML). The research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing vast, unstructured legal corpora—including judicial opinions, legislative texts, and contractual agreements—to identify latent patterns, biases, and decision-making frameworks that are inaccessible through traditional legal methodologies. Current tools for legal text analysis remain limited in scalability and nuance, particularly when handling cross-jurisdictional datasets or temporally evolving legal principles. The project proposes a computational pipeline integrating transformer-based NLP models, graph neural networks (GNNs), and temporal analysis frameworks to process multi-terabyte legal datasets spanning federal and state court records, international treaties, and regulatory filings. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of domain-specific language models fine-tuned on legal lexicons, coupled with network analyses of case citation graphs to map precedent influence and doctrinal shifts. A key innovation involves simulating hypothetical legal scenarios via generative AI to assess the robustness of inferred judicial decision patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for legal practitioners and scholars to query large-scale legal data with granular contextual awareness, as well as empirical insights into systemic inequities in case outcomes. By bridging computational scalability with jurisprudential rigor, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for data-driven legal research while adhering to ethical frameworks for AI in professional legal contexts. The requested resources are critical to handling the memory-intensive processing of heterogeneous legal texts and achieving statistically significant results across diverse jurisdictional contexts.
cip_title: Legal Research and Advanced Professional Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in legal research and advanced professional studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Cytopathological diagnostics face growing challenges due to the complexity and scale of cellular imaging data, compounded by the need to integrate molecular and clinical information for accurate disease characterization. Current analytical workflows struggle with processing high-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs) and correlating morphological features with molecular profiles, limiting diagnostic throughput and precision. This project proposes the development of a computational platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable scalable, AI-driven analysis of cytopathological data. We will train deep learning models, including vision transformers and graph neural networks, to detect malignant and precancerous cellular anomalies across diverse specimen types (e.g., cervical, thyroid, and pleural fluids). The models will be optimized to process multi-gigapixel WSIs while incorporating spatially resolved molecular data from concurrent immunostaining and RNA sequencing. HPC resources will accelerate model training through distributed parallelism, enable terabyte-scale image storage, and facilitate batch processing of retrospective datasets (>50,000 annotated cases). Computational outcomes will include automated quality control modules for specimen adequacy assessment, quantitative feature extraction pipelines for nuclear pleomorphism scoring, and predictive models linking cytomorphological patterns to mutational signatures. Validation will involve benchmarking against gold-standard pathologist interpretations and prospective clinical testing. Successfully implemented, this resource will reduce diagnostic variability, uncover novel biomarkers for early cancer detection, and provide an open computational framework for the cytopathology community. The project directly addresses NIH priorities in precision diagnostics by creating infrastructure to unify cellular imaging analysis with molecular medicine, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and enabling data-driven management of neoplastic and infectious diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals to study, prevent, and manage human diseases manifested in cells. Includes instruction in laboratory procedures, laboratory management, quality assurance, screening, specimen collection, cytopreparation, cytometric and image analysis, and related immunological and molecular techniques.

abstract: Marine propulsion systems face increasing demands to optimize efficiency, reliability, and environmental compliance amid evolving operational conditions and regulatory standards. Current simulation tools for marine diesel engines, hybrid power systems, and thermal management components (e.g., refrigeration, steam cycles) often rely on simplified assumptions that inadequately capture transient behaviors, multi-phase interactions, or system-level interdependencies. This project seeks advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-fidelity computational models of integrated marine propulsion systems. The research will employ multi-physics simulations combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion and exhaust flow analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural-thermal stresses in engine components, and system dynamics modeling to assess interactions between mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic subsystems. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate parametric optimization of engine performance under variable loads and fuel types. Simulations will be calibrated against experimental data from laboratory-scale marine diesel engines and existing shipboard sensor datasets. The outcomes will address critical gaps in predicting wear patterns in turbochargers, optimizing waste heat recovery systems, and mitigating cavitation in fuel injection systems. By enabling granular analysis of transient operational states—such as cold starts, rapid load changes, or hybrid power switching—this work aims to advance predictive maintenance frameworks and inform the design of next-generation, low-emission marine engines. The requested HPC resources will support large-scale parallel computations, reducing simulation timescales from weeks to days while maintaining the resolution required for component-level insights. Results will directly benefit maritime industries striving to meet International Maritime Organization emissions targets and enhance the operational lifespan of propulsion systems. Additionally, the project will provide training opportunities for marine engineering students in applying HPC methodologies to real-world maritime energy challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in shipboard mechanical and electrical engineering and the maintenance and operation of marine engines, including gas, diesel, and steam engines. Includes instruction in automation, diesel-powered systems, electrical circuits and systems, engine performance, hydraulics, manufacturing, motor-powered systems, refrigeration and air-conditioning, steam-powered systems, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the theoretical foundations of high-dimensional Bayesian inference by addressing computational bottlenecks in sampling from complex posterior distributions. Current Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods struggle with scalability in models involving stochastic processes with infinite-dimensional parameter spaces, such as those arising in nonparametric Bayesian analysis of time series or spatial data. The research will develop novel hybrid algorithms combining adaptive Metropolis-Hastings schemes, parallel tempering, and gradient-based Hamiltonian dynamics, specifically targeting Banach space-valued parameters common in functional data settings. Key challenges include establishing geometric ergodicity for infinite-particle system samplers, optimizing communication patterns in distributed memory environments, and quantifying approximation errors when truncating infinite-dimensional proposals. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing resources to (1) implement large-scale simulations comparing mixing times across parameter dimensions, (2) validate theoretical convergence rates under various covariance structures of Gaussian process priors, and (3) benchmark against resampling-based alternatives in robust inference tasks. Expected outcomes include a unified framework for analyzing discretization-invariant MCMC methods, open-source software optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters, and practical guidelines for tuning samplers in high-throughput experimental design contexts. This work will directly impact statistical applications requiring uncertainty quantification in complex systems, such as stochastic volatility models in financial mathematics and infinite-dimensional inverse problems in geophysical tomography. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the O(10⁶)-dimensional optimization subproblems and O(10⁴)-chain parallel tempering configurations required to probe the thermodynamic limits of these samplers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical theory underlying statistical methods and their use. Includes instruction in probability theory parametric and non-parametric inference, sequential analysis, multivariate analysis, Bayesian analysis, experimental design, time series analysis, resampling, robust statistics, limit theory, infinite particle systems, stochastic processes, martingales, Markov processes, and Banach spaces.

abstract: Maritime law enforcement operations face unique challenges due to the dynamic interplay of environmental, logistical, and jurisdictional variables in marine environments. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize tactical decision-making for maritime interdiction operations, with a focus on countering illicit activities such as smuggling and illegal fishing. Current strategies often rely on static protocols that inadequately account for real-time variables such as vessel behavior patterns, hydrodynamic conditions, and jurisdictional boundaries, leading to inefficiencies in resource deployment. To address this gap, the proposed research will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including automatic identification system (AIS) feeds, historical interdiction records, oceanographic models, and jurisdictional geofencing data—into a machine learning-driven simulation platform. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale spatiotemporal data streams, train predictive models for vessel intent classification, and simulate interdiction scenarios under varying environmental and operational constraints. Agent-based modeling will be employed to test adaptive patrol strategies, while hydrodynamic simulations will assess pursuit risks in diverse sea states. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating real-time risk assessments and route recommendations for maritime law enforcement agencies, reducing response times and operational costs. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to parallelize complex simulations across multiple nodes, manage high-velocity data ingestion, and optimize deep learning architectures for irregular maritime datasets. By bridging gaps between nautical operations, computational modeling, and law enforcement logistics, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for enhancing maritime security in an era of increasingly sophisticated maritime threats.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement and security principles and procedures to the marine environment. Includes instruction in criminal and nautical law, nautical terminology, seamanship and vessel operation, vessel maintenance, navigation and navigation systems, meteorology, vessel and passenger safety, radar and remote sensing systems, communications systems, vessel pursuit and stop, boarding and arrest techniques, investigative and evidence techniques, weaponry and applications to specific situations such as piracy, drug trafficking and smuggling.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and visualize the long-term social and ecological impacts of community-engaged art interventions in urban environments. While participatory art practices have demonstrated potential to foster civic dialogue and environmental stewardship, evaluating their sustained effects remains methodologically challenging due to the dynamic, multi-scalar interactions between artworks, communities, and ecosystems. Current qualitative assessment tools struggle to model these complex relationships over time or account for indirect outcomes like policy changes or shifts in public perception. To address this gap, we propose an interdisciplinary approach combining geospatial data, social media analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate how art interventions influence collective behaviors and environmental metrics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing large datasets from municipal records (e.g., waste management, green space usage) and real-time social media feeds, as well as running iterative simulations of community response patterns. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify correlations between specific artistic strategies (e.g., participatory murals, recycled material sculptures) and measurable changes in community engagement or ecological indicators. A parallel computational pipeline will generate interactive 3D visualizations of projected outcomes under different intervention scenarios, enabling artists and policymakers to iteratively refine project designs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for impact forecasting in socially engaged art, validated through case studies in three post-industrial cities. By computationally modeling the cascading effects of artistic practices, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based approaches to art-driven community development while advancing methods for analyzing cultural ecosystems as complex adaptive systems. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets and concurrent simulation of 10,000+ agent interactions over decadal time horizons.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on using the arts to promote activism, civic dialog, community development, ecological and environmental awareness, or social justice. Includes instruction in community organizing, cultural criticism, social practice, studio art, and visual and performing arts.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing behavioral welfare assessments for livestock in intensive agricultural systems through advanced computational modeling. Current methods for evaluating stress and social dynamics in herds rely on manual observation or simplistic statistical models, which fail to capture complex, non-linear interactions between environmental variables, genetic predispositions, and group behavior. We propose developing a high-fidelity agent-based model (ABM) to simulate the emergent behaviors of cattle populations under varying management conditions, including feedlot densities, climate stressors, and handling protocols. The ABM will integrate real-world biometric datasets (e.g., cortisol levels, activity trackers, vocalization patterns) with environmental sensor data to parameterize individual and group decision-making processes. High-performance computing resources are critical for scaling these simulations to herd-level granularity while incorporating machine learning submodules that dynamically adapt agent interactions based on reinforcement learning. Expected outcomes include identifying threshold conditions for stress propagation within herds, validating interventions to mitigate maladaptive behaviors, and generating predictive tools for producers to balance welfare metrics with operational constraints. By bridging computational ethology with precision livestock farming, this work aims to establish a framework for data-driven welfare optimization that transcends traditional trial-and-error approaches. The resulting models will be disseminated as open-source tools to support evidence-based policy in animal husbandry, with potential applications in certification systems and regulatory compliance.
cip_title: Agricultural and Domestic Animal Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural and domestic animal services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the longitudinal efficacy of Waldorf/Steiner pedagogical practices in fostering holistic student development. While Steiner’s methods emphasize experiential, arts-integrated, and developmentally attuned learning, systematic evaluation of their long-term impacts remains challenging due to the qualitative, multidimensional nature of outcomes and the lack of scalable tools to model complex educational interactions. Current assessment paradigms, often reliant on standardized metrics, fail to capture the dynamic interplay of cognitive, creative, and social-emotional growth central to Steiner’s philosophy. This research addresses this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process and synthesize heterogeneous datasets—including student portfolios, teacher narratives, and observational records—collected over a 15-year period from Waldorf schools globally. Machine learning models, including transformer-based natural language processing and multimodal neural networks, will be trained to identify patterns in qualitative data (e.g., thematic shifts in reflective writing, artistic progression) and correlate these with quantitative developmental milestones. Agent-based simulations will further model classroom dynamics under varying implementations of Steiner principles to isolate critical factors influencing student engagement and resilience. The computational workflow demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale unstructured data and iterative simulation runs, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Outcomes will include an open-source analytics toolkit for Steiner educators, enabling evidence-based refinement of curricular timing and instructional strategies. By quantitatively validating the systemic impacts of holistic pedagogy, this work aims to strengthen teacher training programs through data-driven insights, ensuring fidelity to Steiner’s principles while adapting to diverse contemporary educational contexts. The project also advances computational social science methodologies by pioneering techniques to operationalize complex, humanistic educational paradigms at scale.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Rudolf Steiner and his followers.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced robotic control systems for collaborative industrial robots (cobots) operating in unstructured environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational challenges of real-time adaptive planning and multi-sensor fusion. Traditional cobot systems rely on predefined trajectories and limited environmental feedback, resulting in inefficiencies when handling variable tasks such as flexible assembly or dynamic object manipulation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and distributed optimization algorithms to enable continuous trajectory adaptation, collision prediction, and force-torque coordination. The core research problem involves balancing low-latency responsiveness with the high computational demands of simulating complex contact dynamics, processing multimodal sensor data (vision, LiDAR, tactile), and training adaptive control models. Our approach will implement parallelized simulations using ROS/Gazebo environments scaled across HPC nodes, with Kubernetes-managed workflows orchestrating digital twin updates, reinforcement learning-based policy training, and Monte Carlo robustness testing. Key computational challenges include GPU-accelerated solving of inverse kinematics for redundant manipulators under dynamic constraints and memory-efficient storage of high-dimensional sensor histories for online learning. Expected outcomes include open-source control modules for ROS 2, validated through virtual commissioning benchmarks targeting 30% faster cycle times in pick-and-place variability tests compared to conventional PID-based systems. The requested HPC resources will directly support large-scale hyperparameter optimization for neural controllers and statistical validation of safety-critical failure modes under 10,000+ simulated environmental permutations. This work aims to establish scalable computational methodologies for next-generation industrial robotics, reducing deployment barriers for small-batch manufacturing applications while maintaining real-time performance standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using robots. Includes instruction in the principles of robotics, design and operational testing, system maintenance and repair procedures, robot computer systems and control language, specific system types and applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of interpreting complex, multi-modal clinical laboratory data to improve diagnostic accuracy for heterogeneous autoimmune disorders, which often present with overlapping biomarkers and nonspecific symptomatology. Current diagnostic workflows rely on sequential, single-analyte testing, leading to delayed or ambiguous diagnoses. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing an integrated computational framework that combines high-throughput proteomic profiles, flow cytometry data, and autoantibody arrays from patient sera with clinical metadata. The research will employ machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, to identify latent patterns across disparate data types while accounting for technical variability inherent in clinical laboratory instrumentation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on multi-terabyte datasets, optimizing hyperparameters via large-scale grid searches, and performing permutation-based significance testing. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive algorithm for distinguishing clinically similar autoimmune conditions (e.g., Sjögren’s syndrome vs. lupus nephritis) and an open-source toolkit for adaptive data harmonization across different laboratory platforms. The computational pipeline will be designed for eventual deployment in clinical laboratory information systems, enabling real-time decision support. This work bridges gaps between experimental laboratory medicine, computational immunology, and diagnostic informatics, with potential to reduce diagnostic odysseys for patients while establishing new paradigms for data-driven test interpretation in routine clinical practice.
cip_title: Clinical/ Medical Laboratory Science and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical/medical laboratory science and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to identify factors influencing student retention and academic success across diverse institutional contexts in higher education. Despite the proliferation of student data—including academic records, demographic information, engagement metrics, and unstructured text from advising notes—many institutions lack the computational capacity to integrate and analyze these datasets at scale. Traditional statistical tools often struggle with the volume, heterogeneity, and temporal nature of these data, limiting actionable insights. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through advanced machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The primary computational workload involves training ensemble models (e.g., gradient-boosted trees, transformer-based architectures) on multi-year, multi-institutional datasets spanning over 10 million student records. NLP pipelines will process text data to extract themes from academic advising interactions, while federated learning approaches will preserve institutional data privacy during cross-institutional model training. Resource-intensive tasks include hyperparameter optimization for imbalanced class distributions, parallelized feature engineering across decades of longitudinal data, and real-time simulation of intervention impacts via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for identifying early warning indicators of attrition, (2) probabilistic models quantifying how institutional policies moderate equity gaps, and (3) open-source tools enabling resource-constrained colleges to deploy these analyses. By integrating HPC capabilities with institutional research practice, this work aims to advance methodological paradigms in education research, shifting from retrospective descriptive analytics to proactive, computationally intensive predictive and prescriptive modeling. Results will directly inform equity-focused retention strategies while establishing benchmarks for ethical AI applications in educational settings. The requested computing resources are essential for handling memory-intensive workflows, reducing model training times from weeks to days, and enabling complex sensitivity analyses across hypothetical institutional scenarios.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares an individual to be an institutional researcher at a postsecondary educational institution. Includes instruction in data analysis, data-driven decision-making, data mining, higher education administration and organization, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: Franchising, a critical growth strategy in global business ecosystems, faces systemic challenges in optimizing network expansion due to the dynamic interplay of market heterogeneity, regulatory constraints, and operational interdependencies. Traditional analytical models fail to capture the spatiotemporal complexity of multi-unit franchising decisions, particularly when balancing local adaptability with brand consistency. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate and optimize franchise network growth under real-world constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability limitations in existing decision-support tools. The research will develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) system integrating geospatial analytics, reinforcement learning, and multi-objective optimization to evaluate franchise performance drivers across diverse demographic and economic contexts. By parameterizing legal requirements, setup costs, and market saturation thresholds, the model will simulate thousands of franchise configurations while dynamically adjusting for competitive landscapes and consumer behavior patterns. Computational experiments will utilize historical franchise performance data and synthetic datasets to stress-test expansion strategies under varying capital allocation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics platform capable of identifying optimal franchise density thresholds, quantifying cannibalization risks in overlapping territories, and forecasting ROI timelines under different financing structures. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional optimization problems involving 10^6+ parameter combinations, a computational scale intractable with conventional methods. By bridging operations research, computational economics, and spatial analytics, this work aims to advance evidence-based franchising strategies while establishing methodological foundations for complex franchise system analysis. Resulting open-source tools and simulation libraries will empower franchisors to mitigate expansion risks and enhance network resilience, with direct applications to emerging markets where data scarcity exacerbates traditional planning challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and operate franchises. Includes instruction in legal requirements, set-up costs and capitalization requirements, financing, and applications to specific franchise opportunities.

abstract: Rural populations face significant health disparities, including limited access to specialized care, higher rates of chronic diseases, and poorer health outcomes compared to urban counterparts. These challenges are compounded by sparse data infrastructure and geographic barriers, which hinder the development of targeted clinical interventions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal health data from rural communities, aiming to identify patterns in disease prevalence, treatment efficacy, and healthcare utilization. The research will integrate electronic health records (EHRs), geospatial data, environmental exposures, and genomic information from rural patients across five states, focusing on cardiometabolic diseases and mental health comorbidities—conditions disproportionately affecting these regions. Computational workflows will employ machine learning models to predict disease trajectories, optimize risk stratification, and evaluate the impact of telehealth interventions. Spatial-temporal modeling will map disparities in care access and environmental risk factors, while federated learning techniques will preserve data privacy across decentralized clinical sites. The scale and complexity of these datasets—encompassing over 10 million patient-years of records and high-resolution geospatial layers—necessitate HPC resources for parallel processing, large-scale simulations, and efficient storage. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into modifiable risk factors, validated predictive tools for early clinical intervention, and policy recommendations for equitable resource allocation. By bridging computational innovation with rural health challenges, this work aims to reduce care gaps, inform precision medicine approaches tailored to rural settings, and establish a scalable framework for data-driven rural health research. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models, replication of analyses across diverse subpopulations, and open sharing of computational tools with rural healthcare networks.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rural Health

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets central to understanding the development of Canadian social and political institutions in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The core research problem involves identifying and mapping patterns of institutional influence, migration, and policy diffusion across Canada’s provinces during a period of rapid industrialization and urbanization. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to systematically process the volume and complexity of digitized primary sources—including census records, parliamentary debates, regional newspapers, and municipal archives—that are critical to tracing these phenomena at a national scale. To address this, the project employs computational text mining, network analysis, and geospatial modeling. Custom Python-based pipelines will preprocess and tokenize multilingual texts (English and French), while transformer models fine-tuned on historical Canadian corpora will extract named entities and thematic clusters. Network graphs will visualize relationships between policymakers, civic organizations, and demographic shifts, with parallelized algorithms running on HPC clusters to manage scalability. Spatial-temporal models, built using R and PostgreSQL, will integrate georeferenced data to track regional disparities in infrastructure development. The computational workflow demands significant memory and processing power due to the terabyte-scale datasets and iterative machine learning tasks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive database of institutional networks, peer-reviewed publications on methodological synergies between computational social science and history, and new insights into how regional identities shaped federalism in Canada. By combining HPC capabilities with archival research, this project aims to advance digital historiography, offering replicable frameworks for analyzing complex societal change in resource-constrained historical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the society, culture, and institutions of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in Canadian historiography, sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-disciplinary data integration in addressing complex societal challenges at the intersection of cultural, economic, and environmental systems. The research problem centers on the limitations of existing analytical frameworks to model nonlinear interactions between heterogeneous datasets—such as regional folklore archives, localized economic activity metrics, and geospatial climate vulnerability indices—which are critical for understanding community resilience in underrepresented regions. Current approaches struggle to reconcile disparate data structures, temporal scales, and qualitative-quantitative divides, particularly when analyzing patterns across decades or centuries. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a novel computational architecture leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) and transformer-based multimodal fusion techniques optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The workflow will involve parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets through containerized pipelines on GPU clusters, enabling simultaneous training of multiple model variants for comparative analysis. Key innovations include adaptive attention mechanisms for cross-domain feature alignment and synthetic data generation to address archival gaps in historical records. The project will validate its framework through case studies examining 20th-century livelihood transitions in culturally distinct floodplain communities, correlating oral history transcripts with agricultural production records and hydrological data. Successful implementation will produce three principal outcomes: (1) an open-source toolkit for temporal-spatial data integration across humanities and environmental sciences, (2) new quantitative evidence about threshold effects in community adaptation strategies, and (3) benchmarks for HPC resource allocation in mixed-methods interdisciplinary research. By enabling scalable analysis of traditionally incompatible datasets, this work aims to establish computational best practices for transdisciplinary studies while informing equitable climate adaptation policies. The requested computing resources are essential for managing memory-intensive model parallelism and hyperparameter optimization across cultural-environmental data dimensions that cannot be feasibly processed on standard academic infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing programming skill acquisition through adaptive, data-driven pedagogical frameworks, an emerging niche intersecting computational education and cognitive ergonomics. Traditional programming instruction often employs static curricula, which fail to account for heterogeneous learner backgrounds, cognitive styles, and knowledge retention patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computational infrastructure to model and simulate individualized learning trajectories. The core methodology involves deploying ensemble machine learning algorithms on multimodal educational datasets—including code submission histories, error-resolution patterns, and temporal engagement metrics—to identify latent correlations between instructional strategies and competency development. These models will drive dynamic content generation systems that adjust problem difficulty, conceptual focus, and feedback mechanisms in real time. The computational demands arise from processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning decades of anonymized student records, coupled with parallelized reinforcement learning architectures that require iterative optimization across thousands of simulated learner personas. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for personalized programming education, validated through longitudinal A/B testing against conventional teaching paradigms. Success metrics will quantify reductions in skill attainment disparities across demographic groups and improvements in complex problem-solving transfer rates. By establishing scalable, evidence-based approaches to programming pedagogy, this work aims to redefine how computational resources can democratize access to technical education while advancing interdisciplinary research at the nexus of educational psychology and adaptive systems design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer programming, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and social dynamics of Holocaust-era population movements, integrating fragmented archival datasets to reconstruct obscured patterns of displacement, survival, and community dissolution. Despite extensive scholarship, critical gaps persist in understanding how micro-scale interactions—such as informal networks among displaced persons or localized resistance efforts—shaped survival outcomes. Existing datasets, including deportation records, survivor testimonies, and geospatial metadata, remain siloed across disciplines and formats, limiting holistic analysis. The research addresses this by developing computational workflows to harmonize multilingual textual records, tabular data, and georeferenced sources, enabling network analysis, agent-based modeling, and machine learning-driven pattern recognition at scale. Key computational challenges include NLP processing of handwritten documents in multiple languages (e.g., Yiddish, Polish, German), probabilistic record linkage across incomplete datasets, and simulating population behavior under constrained resource conditions. By modeling interactions between individuals, groups, and institutional actors, the project aims to identify previously unrecognized factors influencing survival rates, such as the role of small-scale mutual aid networks or variations in deportation logistics. Outcomes will include open-source tools for historical data integration, visualizations of multi-layered displacement patterns, and empirically grounded models of resilience under genocide conditions. This work bridges historiographic methods with computational social science, offering novel insights into the Holocaust’s human geography while establishing scalable frameworks for interdisciplinary genocide studies. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive tasks, including large-language model fine-tuning for document analysis and parallelized simulations of population scenarios across diverse archival contexts. Ethical considerations, including data anonymization and sensitivity to survivor narratives, are embedded in the computational design. The project’s findings will advance scholarly understanding of collective trauma dynamics and inform contemporary atrocity prevention strategies by quantifying the impact of grassroots agency amid systemic violence.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on genocide in human history with particular reference to Twentieth Century genocides such as that of the Ottoman Armenians during World War I and the Nazi Holocaust during World War II. Programs also focus on topics such as survivor studies and counseling, war crimes research and prevention, reconciliation and compensation, ethical and spiritual issues, holocaust art and literature, and legacy and effect in relation to subsequent generations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a multimodal analysis of cultural resilience and linguistic diversity in Appalachia, with a focus on understudied oral histories, folk narratives, and vernacular music traditions. Appalachia’s cultural heritage is richly documented in community archives, but fragmented digitization efforts and the scale of unstructured data—including audio recordings, transcribed interviews, and textual folklore collections—hinder systematic analysis. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural continuity and adaptation across generations, particularly in marginalized communities, through large-scale computational methods that traditional humanities approaches cannot feasibly execute. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze dialectal variations and thematic shifts in oral histories, machine learning models to classify musical motifs in ethnomusicological datasets, and network analysis to map the diffusion of narrative themes across geographic and temporal axes. These methods require HPC capabilities to process terabytes of audio files, manage parallelized text corpus analyses, and train deep learning models on multimodal datasets. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated cultural materials, visualizations of linguistic and musical networks, and scholarly articles examining how Appalachian communities negotiate identity amid socioeconomic change. By integrating computational rigor with humanities-driven inquiry, this work aims to redefine methodologies in regional cultural studies while supporting Appalachian stakeholders in preserving intangible heritage. The requested resources are critical to handling data at scale, ensuring reproducibility, and enabling interdisciplinary collaboration between regional scholars, technologists, and community archivists.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, sociology, culture, and economics of the Appalachian region of the United States. Includes instruction in contemporary issues in Appalachia, political economy of Appalachia, community-based research, ethnomusicology, and oral and written languages of Appalachia.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a quantum machine learning (QML) framework to optimize real-time business decision-making in high-velocity data environments, addressing the computational limitations of classical models in processing unstructured, multimodal data streams. While quantum computing has shown promise in theoretical optimization, its practical application to dynamic business analytics—particularly for time-sensitive scenarios like algorithmic trading, supply chain risk mitigation, or customer sentiment tracking—remains underexplored. The research will focus on hybrid quantum-classical neural architectures capable of operating on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, simulating quantum circuit performance via high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to overcome current hardware constraints. Key computational challenges include optimizing variational quantum algorithms for heterogeneous data inputs (e.g., IoT sensor feeds, financial tickers, social media text) and reducing latency in hybrid model inference. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated quantum simulators and distributed tensor networks to benchmark scalability against classical deep learning baselines across terabyte-scale datasets from partner financial institutions and e-commerce platforms. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel QML architecture demonstrating ≥40% faster convergence on real-time forecasting tasks compared to classical counterparts, (2) an open-source framework for simulating quantum-enhanced business analytics pipelines, and (3) empirical evidence quantifying the trade-offs between quantum circuit depth and predictive accuracy in enterprise decision contexts. By establishing performance benchmarks for NISQ-era algorithms in business operations, this work aims to bridge the gap between quantum computing research and practical business intelligence applications, while informing infrastructure investment strategies for post-quantum data ecosystems. The requested HPC resources are critical for maintaining parity with commercial quantum cloud services and enabling reproducible, large-scale experiments across simulated quantum processing units (QPUs).
cip_title: Management Information Systems and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any program in business information and data processing services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Vascular diseases of the nervous system, including ischemic stroke and intracranial hemorrhage, represent leading causes of global morbidity and mortality. Current clinical management strategies remain limited by incomplete understanding of disease heterogeneity, dynamic pathophysiological processes, and variable treatment responses. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of cerebrovascular disease progression and optimize individualized therapeutic interventions. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) developing multiscale computational models integrating hemodynamic, thromboembolic, and tissue injury dynamics to simulate stroke pathophysiology across spatial and temporal scales, and (2) creating machine learning frameworks to analyze high-dimensional clinical datasets, including neuroimaging, biomarker profiles, and electronic health records. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model cerebral blood flow alterations in patient-specific vascular geometries derived from angiographic data, while finite element analyses will predict tissue-level responses to ischemia-reperfusion injury. Parallelized deep learning architectures will process multimodal datasets to identify prognostic signatures and predict treatment outcomes. These approaches require HPC capabilities due to the scale of 4D neuroimaging analyses (>10 TB/cohort), real-time coupling of differential equation systems in multiscale models, and hyperparameter optimization across neural networks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for hemorrhagic transformation risk post-thrombolysis, optimized clot retrieval strategies for large-vessel occlusion, and dynamic biomarkers of penumbral tissue viability. By enabling complex simulations of neurovascular pathophysiology that are infeasible on standard computing infrastructure, this research will directly inform clinical trial design and bedside decision-making. The resulting computational tools aim to reduce disability-adjusted life years through precision neurology approaches, addressing a critical need in cerebrovascular care. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated workflows, large-scale data storage for longitudinal cohort analyses, and high-throughput processing of real-world clinical data streams.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation, prevention, treatment, and recovery from vascular diseases of the nervous system resulting from a large number of causes, such as ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, spinal cord ischemia, and spinal cord hemorrhage.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of transnational missionary networks between 1850 and 1950 through computational analysis of multilingual archival materials, including correspondence, field reports, and ethnographic records. Missionary activities during this period involved complex interactions between religious, medical, and colonial institutions, yet the scale and heterogeneity of these records have hindered systematic analysis of their global networks, knowledge exchanges, and unintended societal impacts. The research addresses this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to process and analyze over 500,000 digitized pages from missionary archives, spanning 15 languages and six continents. Computational methods will integrate transformer-based language models fine-tuned for historical texts, multilingual named entity recognition to map institutional and interpersonal connections, and network analysis to trace the evolution of resource flows and ideological diffusion. A key innovation involves simulating counterfactual scenarios of missionary mobility and resource allocation using agent-based modeling, informed by historical climate, disease, and geopolitical datasets. By leveraging GPU-accelerated NLP and distributed computing for large-scale network inference, this approach will reconstruct how missionary strategies adapted to local crises, colonial policies, and interdenominational competition. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking missionary activities to longitudinal demographic and cultural change indicators, as well as methodological frameworks for analyzing contested historical networks in low-resource languages. The project aims to provide new insights into the role of missionary institutions as early transnational actors while critically examining the computational challenges of studying marginalized voices and asymmetrical power dynamics in archival corpora. Results will inform interdisciplinary scholarship on religion, globalization, and cross-cultural encounter, with implications for heritage digitization and ethical archival practices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of religious outreach, social service and proselytization, and that prepares individuals for mission vocations. Includes instruction in theology, evangelism, preaching, medical and social mission work, missionary education, missionary aviation, emergency services, legal and political aspects of working in other countries, and preparation for ordination as missionaries.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of understudied Iranian languages, with a focus on historical linguistic evolution and dialectal variation. While Persian and related languages have rich textual traditions spanning millennia, computational approaches to their study remain limited due to sparse digitized corpora, morphological complexity, and a lack of language-specific NLP tools. This research addresses these challenges by developing scalable methods to analyze phonological, syntactic, and lexical patterns across diachronic and synchronic language stages. Key objectives include constructing annotated corpora for Middle Persian (Pahlavi) and early New Persian texts, training transformer-based models for automated morphological parsing, and implementing dialectometric analyses of modern Iranian languages such as Kurdish and Balochi. Computational workflows will integrate unsupervised clustering algorithms to detect linguistic shifts in historical texts and graph-based models to map contact-induced changes across regional varieties. HPC resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets of digitized manuscripts, optimizing neural architectures for low-resource languages, and running parallelized comparative analyses across linguistic features. Anticipated outcomes include open-access computational tools for Iranian language processing, quantitative models of language change trajectories, and enhanced documentation of endangered varieties. By bridging computational linguistics with Iranian philology, this work aims to deepen understanding of language development in contact zones while establishing replicable methods for analyzing morphologically complex languages with non-Latin scripts. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale text alignment, and storage of heterogeneous linguistic data, enabling interdisciplinary research at the intersection of humanities computing and historical linguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages used in ancient, medieval, and modern Iran and its border regions, including modern Persian, Avestan/Old Persian, and related modern and extinct languages. Includes instruction in applications of modern Persian and other languages in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The integration of alternative and complementary medical systems into evidence-based healthcare requires a robust understanding of the molecular and systems-level mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects. Many therapies in this domain, such as herbal formulations or biofield interventions, involve complex, multi-component interactions that challenge traditional reductionist research methodologies. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the polypharmacological networks and biophysical dynamics of complementary therapies. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) simulating the interactions of multi-herbal formulations with human proteomes to identify synergistic mechanisms, and (2) analyzing large-scale clinical datasets to uncover patterns linking self-reported outcomes with biomarkers in patients using complementary therapies. Computational methods will include molecular dynamics simulations of phytochemical-protein interactions, machine learning-driven network pharmacology models, and Bayesian inference frameworks for heterogeneous data integration. These approaches require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including genomic repositories, phytochemical libraries, and electronic health records. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for molecular simulations and distributed memory clusters for population-level analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of key molecular targets for common herbal therapies, predictive models of therapy-responder subgroups, and an open-access computational platform for validating traditional pharmacopeia claims. By elucidating mechanistic pathways and optimizing personalized therapy selection, this work aims to bridge the evidence gap between alternative medical systems and conventional healthcare paradigms. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-target therapies and achieving statistically robust conclusions from real-world datasets with high dimensionality. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, a public database of therapy-pathway associations, and clinical decision-support tools for integrative medicine practitioners.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing sustainable product design processes through high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial and product design faces growing challenges in balancing aesthetic innovation, material efficiency, and environmental impact, particularly when prototyping complex forms or novel materials. Traditional iterative design methods, which rely on physical prototypes and manual adjustments, are resource-intensive and limit exploration of high-dimensional design variables. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) for form exploration, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and thermal performance prediction, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to reconcile competing design criteria (e.g., ergonomics, manufacturability, carbon footprint). The computational workload requires parallel processing of large-scale parametric studies, including real-time rendering of 3D models in virtual environments and physics-based simulations of biodegradable material behaviors under stress. HPC resources will enable simultaneous evaluation of thousands of design variants across distributed GPU nodes, reducing iteration cycles from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include a validated workflow for generating structurally sound, visually compelling product designs with minimized material waste, alongside an open-access dataset correlating computational predictions with physical prototype testing. This research directly supports the program’s focus on cost-effective, sustainable design by establishing quantitative links between digital modeling choices and real-world performance. The project will also advance computational methods for aesthetic evaluation through machine learning, bridging gaps between subjective visual criteria and engineering constraints in applied visual arts. Results will be disseminated through design software plugins and workshops to empower practitioners in adopting HPC-driven methodologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via the creation of effective forms, shapes, and packaging for manufactured products. Includes instruction in designing in a wide variety of plastic and digital media, prototype construction, design development and refinement, principles of cost saving, and product structure and performance criteria relevant to aesthetic design parameters.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-spatial dynamics of communal housing environments through computational modeling to address gaps in understanding how architectural layouts influence social cohesion and conflict. While housing design is recognized as a mediator of human interaction, existing studies lack granular, scalable tools to simulate emergent behaviors in diverse populations over time. The research proposes an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate how residents with varying cultural, economic, and behavioral profiles adapt to shared spaces under constraints such as limited privacy or resource access. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parameterize thousands of virtual agents with real-world demographic data, model multiyear interactions across high-resolution spatial grids, and analyze nonlinear outcomes through machine learning classifiers. The ABM will integrate datasets from urban ethnography, behavioral psychology, and architectural schematics to simulate scenarios ranging from high-density urban co-living complexes to transitional housing for displaced populations. Computational experiments will test how design interventions—such as modular partitions, decentralized amenities, or circulation patterns—affect metrics of well-being, conflict frequency, and collective problem-solving. Outcomes will yield a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers and designers to proactively evaluate housing prototypes for social resilience. By bridging computational social science with human-environment theories, this work advances an understudied interdisciplinary niche in housing studies, offering empirically grounded strategies to mitigate systemic inequities in communal living contexts. The project’s scale—requiring parallelized simulations across 10,000+ core-hours—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve the resolution and statistical power needed for generalizable insights.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in housing and human environments, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the efficacy of arts-based health interventions (ABHIs) in improving physiological, psychological, and social outcomes across diverse populations. While arts modalities—such as music therapy, dance movement therapy, and participatory visual arts—are increasingly integrated into healthcare, the mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly quantified. Current evaluation methods often rely on small-scale qualitative data or siloed quantitative metrics, limiting the ability to model complex, multimodal interactions between artistic engagement, neurobiological responses, and long-term health outcomes. This research will address this gap by developing computational models to synthesize heterogeneous datasets, including biometric data (e.g., EEG, cortisol levels), behavioral observations, self-reported surveys, and longitudinal health records from ABHI participants. Machine learning pipelines will be designed to identify latent patterns linking specific artistic practices (e.g., rhythm-based music, narrative-focused theater) to biomarkers of stress reduction, immune function, and emotional regulation. Agent-based modeling will simulate how community-level arts programs propagate health benefits through social networks, particularly in underserved populations. HPC resources are critical for processing high-frequency biometric streams, training multimodal deep learning architectures, and running large-scale simulations that account for demographic variability. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks to optimize art modality selection for targeted health conditions, (2) evidence-based thresholds for intervention dosage and duration, and (3) open-source tools to support real-time adaptation of arts programs in clinical and community settings. By quantifying the dynamic interplay between artistic engagement and health, this work aims to advance equitable resource allocation for arts-in-health initiatives while establishing computational methodologies for transdisciplinary health humanities research.
