cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of programs that use the visual and performing arts in support of health and wellness among diverse individuals and communities. Includes instruction in dance, literary arts, music, theatre, healthcare systems, program administration, and public health.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize clinical decision-making and care coordination for complex patient populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in real-time, evidence-based practice. Clinical Nurse Leaders (CNLs) face challenges in synthesizing heterogeneous data—including electronic health records, real-time physiological monitoring, and longitudinal patient histories—to guide interventions for high-acuity patients. Current methods often rely on static protocols or fragmented analyses, which may fail to capture dynamic interactions between comorbidities, treatment responses, and care team workflows. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation and predictive modeling approach. Agent-based models will simulate patient trajectories and care team interactions under varying clinical scenarios, parameterized by data from a retrospective cohort of 15,000+ patients with chronic cardiopulmonary conditions. Machine learning models, trained on this dataset, will predict risks of decompensation and resource bottlenecks. These components will be integrated into an HPC-optimized decision support tool, enabling CNLs to test intervention strategies in silico before implementation. The computational workflow requires parallel processing for large-scale parameter sweeps and real-time Bayesian updating of patient-specific predictions. Anticipated outcomes include validated models of care coordination efficiency, personalized risk stratification algorithms, and a prototype interface for scenario planning. This work will advance nursing science by establishing a methodological bridge between granular clinical data and systems-level care optimization, directly supporting the CNL role in improving patient outcomes while reducing preventable complications. By quantifying the impact of nurse-led interventions on care quality metrics, the project aims to generate scalable insights for evidence-based practice in acute and transitional care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive maintenance frameworks for hybrid and electric vehicle (HEV/EV) systems, addressing the growing complexity of modern automotive technologies. Current diagnostic tools struggle to integrate real-time sensor data with historical failure patterns, particularly for emerging powertrain architectures, leading to inefficient repair workflows and extended downtime. To bridge this gap, the project proposes developing a machine learning (ML)-driven simulation platform capable of modeling multi-physics interactions within HEV/EV systems—including thermal dynamics, battery degradation, and power electronics behavior—under diverse operational conditions. The computational approach will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for component stress modeling with graph neural networks (GNNs) to map interdependencies across subsystems. Large-scale datasets from onboard diagnostics, telematic systems, and manufacturer failure databases will be processed using distributed computing frameworks to train anomaly detection models. Key challenges include optimizing parallelization for heterogeneous data streams and reducing latency in physics-informed neural network training. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin framework that predicts component failures with >90% accuracy 500–1,000 operational hours in advance, validated against empirical data from partner automotive workshops. The project will also generate open-access benchmark datasets for rare failure modes in HEV/EV systems, addressing a critical gap in technician training resources. By enabling proactive maintenance strategies, this work aims to reduce repair costs by an estimated 15–20% for fleet operators while providing a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into vocational technical education. Results will be disseminated through industry collaborations and adapted into advanced diagnostic modules for vehicle repair curricula.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Ambulatory care settings face growing challenges in managing patient populations with complex chronic conditions, where timely intervention and personalized care pathways are critical to reducing hospitalizations and improving outcomes. However, predicting individual patient risks and optimizing care plans in real-world ambulatory environments remains computationally intensive, requiring integration of heterogeneous data streams (e.g., electronic health records, wearable devices, socio-demographic factors) and high-dimensional modeling. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework to analyze multimodal ambulatory care data, aiming to identify dynamic risk trajectories and recommend adaptive care interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and harmonize large-scale datasets from 50,000+ patients across partnered health systems, train ensemble models combining gradient-boosted decision trees and temporal convolutional networks, and simulate intervention impacts via agent-based modeling. Key computational challenges include managing irregularly sampled time-series data, addressing missingness and bias in real-world clinical records, and ensuring model interpretability for clinical translation. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across thousands of model configurations, conducting sensitivity analyses on simulated care pathways, and deploying federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across institutions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for 30-day preventable hospitalization risk, optimized intervention timing thresholds for common chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, heart failure), and an open-source computational toolkit for ambulatory care analytics. By enabling rapid iteration of complex models at scale, this work aims to advance precision ambulatory care strategies while establishing a template for computationally driven research in resource-constrained outpatient settings. Results will be disseminated through clinical informatics conferences and partnerships with ambulatory care networks to pilot implementation.
cip_definition: Research focused on Ambulatory Care

abstract: The proposed research addresses the critical challenge of optimizing nanoscale photonic metamaterials for ultra-efficient light-matter interaction in quantum sensing applications. While advances in nanofabrication have enabled precise control over subwavelength structures, the design of dynamically tunable metamaterials—capable of real-time spectral adaptation—remains hindered by the computational complexity of modeling nonlinear optical responses across multiphysics domains. Traditional finite-element methods struggle to resolve the coupled electromagnetic, thermal, and quantum mechanical effects in such systems at experimentally relevant scales (1–100 nm). This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multiscale simulation framework integrating time-domain Maxwell solvers, ab initio quantum transport calculations, and machine learning-driven optimization. The computational approach will combine GPU-accelerated finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for electromagnetic behavior, density functional theory (DFT) workflows for nonlinear material properties, and neural network surrogates to bridge timescales between photon dynamics and electron-phonon interactions. Key objectives include parameterizing disorder effects in self-assembled plasmonic arrays, predicting thermo-optic tuning limits in hybrid metal-dielectric nanostructures, and identifying optimal geometries for entanglement-enhanced photon emission. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source codebase for nanophotonic metamaterial design and a dataset of engineered structures with predicted quantum sensing figures of merit (e.g., Purcell factor >1,000, decoherence rates <10 GHz). This work directly supports experimental efforts in quantum metrology by reducing iterative fabrication cycles and provides foundational insights into nonequilibrium nanoscale energy transfer mechanisms. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations spanning 10^6–10^8 grid points over picosecond-scale durations, exceeding the memory and parallelization capabilities of local cluster infrastructure. Successful implementation will advance the integration of nanophotonics with quantum technologies while establishing computational protocols adaptable to other emerging nanoscale systems requiring multiphysics optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical, scientific, and engineering principles and technical skills to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) and to design, fabricate, and integrate nanoscale structures, devices, and systems. Includes instruction in materials science, thermodynamics, nanomaterials, nanoelectronics, and nano/micro device fabrication and testing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interplay between historical sociopolitical shifts and linguistic evolution across multilingual literary corpora from the 15th to 19th centuries in Europe and colonial Latin America. The research addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary humanities scholarship: the lack of scalable methods to systematically trace how macrohistorical events (e.g., imperial expansions, revolutions, print culture diffusion) influenced semantic changes, lexical borrowing, and narrative structures in vernacular texts. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to process the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources, including manuscripts, early printed books, and periodicals in Spanish, Nahuatl, English, French, and Indigenous languages. To overcome this, we propose a computational pipeline combining transformer-based multilingual language models fine-tuned on historical texts, dynamic topic modeling, and network analysis of semantic shifts across temporal and geographic axes. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific embeddings on our curated corpus of 250,000+ digitized pages, enabling GPU-accelerated parallel processing of low-resource historical language variants. Expected outcomes include 1) a diachronic atlas of concept migration correlated with archival event data, 2) quantitative models of cross-linguistic influence in colonial administrative and literary documents, and 3) open-access tools for temporal sentiment analysis adapted to premodern orthographies. By integrating computational linguistics with historiographical frameworks, this work will provide novel insights into how language acted as both a vehicle and artifact of cultural negotiation during periods of upheaval, while establishing replicable methods for resource-efficient analysis of non-standardized historical languages. The project directly supports the program’s mission to advance multidisciplinary scholarship through methodological innovation at the intersection of philology, digital humanities, and historical theory.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; linguistics; literature, philology; and studies of specific periods, issues and cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision metal working by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize advanced manufacturing processes. Precision metal fabrication techniques, such as laser cutting, micro-machining, and additive manufacturing, require tight control over thermal, mechanical, and metallurgical variables to minimize defects and ensure dimensional accuracy. However, existing empirical methods struggle to predict complex phenomena like residual stress formation, microstructural evolution, and tool wear under dynamic conditions, leading to costly trial-and-error approaches. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning (ML), and large-scale data analytics. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate thermo-mechanical interactions during metal processing at micron-scale resolutions, while ML algorithms will identify optimal parameter sets (e.g., laser power, feed rates, cooling strategies) to mitigate defects. The HPC environment is essential for resolving spatially heterogeneous material behaviors and coupling multiphase phenomena—tasks infeasible with conventional computing due to their high memory and processing demands. Expected outcomes include predictive models for defect-free fabrication, validated against experimental data from partner manufacturing facilities, and an open-access dataset of simulated process-performance correlations. This work will advance the scalability of precision metalworking technologies for high-value aerospace and medical components, reduce material waste, and provide training resources to bridge HPC literacy gaps in technical education. By integrating computational rigor with industrial practice, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for smart manufacturing in technology-driven metalworking fields.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision metal work, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Veterinary radiology faces significant challenges in optimizing diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes due to the anatomical diversity of animal species and the complexity of pathologies visible in radiologic imaging. Current methods for analyzing imaging data, such as manual segmentation or traditional computational pipelines, are time-intensive, prone to variability, and ill-suited for high-throughput or real-time applications. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing advanced machine learning models and simulation frameworks to automate and enhance the analysis of veterinary radiologic data. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating species-adaptive algorithms for detecting and characterizing tumors, fractures, and degenerative diseases across diverse animal anatomies using multimodal imaging data (MRI, CT, radiography), and (2) modeling radiation therapy dosimetry to improve precision in treatment planning for malignancies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train deep neural networks on large, heterogeneous datasets spanning multiple species, perform Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport in complex anatomical geometries, and optimize hyperparameters for clinical deployability. Computational workflows will integrate open-source tools (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, Geant4) with custom code for data augmentation, domain adaptation, and uncertainty quantification. Expected outcomes include validated pipelines for automated lesion detection with quantified sensitivity/specificity improvements over manual methods, optimized radiation dosing protocols to minimize collateral tissue damage, and open-access benchmarks for veterinary imaging AI. By enabling rapid, reproducible analysis of radiologic data, this work aims to directly improve diagnostic turnaround times, reduce inter-observer variability, and support evidence-based therapeutic decisions in veterinary care. The developed frameworks may also inform translational applications in human medical imaging, particularly for rare diseases or pediatric cases where anatomical variability poses similar challenges.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radiologic imaging and therapies to diagnose and treat animal diseases and health problems. May included related research in the use and handling of equipment for radionuclides detection and application.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving pedagogical and cultural frameworks within pre-ministerial education, focusing on the integration of digital hermeneutics and ethical decision-making simulations. While pre-theological training traditionally emphasizes scriptural exegesis and pastoral care, modern ministerial contexts increasingly require fluency in navigating complex, technology-mediated social dynamics. The project addresses a critical gap: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to model how aspirants internalize ethical reasoning and intercultural competencies in digitally saturated environments. Using anonymized datasets from 15 interdenominational seminaries—including longitudinal performance metrics, reflective writing samples, and simulated pastoral scenario responses—we will apply natural language processing (NLP) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to map cognitive-emotional patterns in ethical deliberation. Custom transformer models will identify latent biases and thematic shifts in trainees’ written reflections, while ABM simulations will test how varying curricular interventions affect decision-making outcomes in hypothetical community conflict scenarios. Computational demands include training multi-modal neural networks on unstructured text and video data (~50 TB), parallelized scenario simulations across diverse demographic parameters, and real-time visualization of emergent behavioral clusters. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing pastoral training modules, predictive analytics to identify at-risk cohorts, and open-source tools for dynamically adapting curricula to regional sociotechnical challenges. By bridging computational social science and theological pedagogy, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for enhancing the resilience of ministerial training programs amid rapid cultural digitization, thereby contributing to interdisciplinary humanities research at the intersection of education, ethics, and technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to enter a seminary or other program leading to religious ordination, or a related religious vocation.

abstract: Clinical pharmacogenomics aims to optimize drug therapies by integrating genomic variability with patient-specific factors, yet challenges persist in predicting multifactorial drug response due to the polygenic nature of traits, population diversity, and environmental interactions. Current models often lack scalability to handle high-dimensional genomic data alongside clinical variables, limiting their utility in real-world settings. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze large-scale pharmacogenomic datasets, including whole-genome sequences, electronic health records (EHRs), and longitudinal drug outcome data, to identify genetic and non-genetic predictors of drug efficacy and toxicity. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to model complex gene-drug-environment interactions. These models will be trained on multi-ethnic cohorts to address population biases and improve generalizability. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted to explore functional mechanisms of prioritized genetic variants affecting drug metabolism pathways (e.g., CYP450 isoforms). The computational pipeline will integrate genome-wide association studies (GWAS), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling, and real-world evidence from EHRs to enable patient stratification. HPC resources are critical for managing the terabytes of genomic data, parallelizing computationally intensive simulations, and optimizing hyperparameters for deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dose optimization, risk stratification tools for adverse drug reactions, and novel biomarkers for targeted therapies. These results will be validated through collaboration with clinical partners using retrospective EHR data and prospective pilot studies. By enhancing the precision of pharmacogenomic guidance, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error prescribing, mitigate adverse events, and advance equitable implementation of personalized medicine across diverse populations. The scalability of the framework will also provide a template for future studies integrating multi-omics data into clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Pharmacogenomics

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural and computational mechanisms underlying real-time language comprehension under cognitive load, with a focus on resolving syntactic and semantic ambiguities. A core challenge in psycholinguistics is understanding how limited cognitive resources shape incremental language processing, particularly when contextual cues conflict with probabilistic linguistic expectations. While behavioral studies offer insights into processing bottlenecks, they lack the resolution to disentangle competing neurocognitive models of resource allocation. To address this gap, we propose developing a neurocomputational framework integrating predictive coding architectures with biologically constrained working memory systems. This approach requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale neural network simulations that mirror the temporal dynamics and parallel processing observed in human cognition. Key computational tasks include training recurrent neural networks on corpus-derived linguistic patterns, systematically varying memory capacity constraints, and analyzing emergent activation patterns during ambiguous phrase parsing. The models will be validated against multimodal empirical data (eye-tracking, EEG) from ongoing experiments on garden-path sentence processing. HPC resources are essential for optimizing network architectures through hyperparameter searches across thousands of iterations, simulating neural population dynamics at millisecond resolution, and performing Bayesian model comparison across competing theoretical accounts. Expected outcomes include a mechanistic understanding of how memory limitations interact with predictive processing during language comprehension, with implications for computational models of cognitive architecture. The project will produce open-access simulation tools for modeling resource-constrained language processing, along with benchmarks for evaluating neurocognitive theories of attention and memory in complex linguistic tasks. Results will advance theoretical debates about the scalability of predictive processing models while informing experimental paradigms in psycholinguistics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the mechanisms and processes of learning and thinking, and associated information encoding, decoding, processing and transmitting systems. Includes instruction in theories of cognition and intelligence; studies of cognitive processes such as memory, sensation, perception, pattern recognition, problem solving, and conceptual thinking; cybernetics; psycholinguistics; and the study of biological and social communications mechanisms and processes.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber threats in military operations necessitates advanced computational tools to model, predict, and counter adversarial tactics in real time. This project seeks to develop a dynamic, AI-driven simulation framework for analyzing multi-vector cyber-physical attacks on military networks, with a focus on adversarial behavior patterns that exploit vulnerabilities across integrated command, control, and communications (C3) systems. Current threat assessment models lack the granularity to evaluate cascading failures in hybrid environments where cyber operations intersect with electronic warfare (EW) capabilities, such as jamming, spoofing, and electromagnetic spectrum manipulation. To address this gap, the research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale, adaptive attack scenarios incorporating machine learning (ML)-based adversarial agents, probabilistic failure propagation models, and real-time defensive response algorithms. Computational methods will include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess system resilience under stochastic threat conditions, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map interdependencies between cyber and electronic warfare nodes, and evolutionary optimization techniques to iteratively harden defense postures. The framework will integrate classified threat intelligence datasets with synthetic data generation to balance operational security requirements with model fidelity. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for identifying critical vulnerabilities in next-generation C3 architectures, metrics for quantifying mission degradation under coordinated cyber-EW attacks, and actionable recommendations for adaptive resource allocation in contested environments. By enabling multi-domain threat modeling at unprecedented scale and speed, this work aims to directly inform doctrine development and capability investments for modern electronic warfare and cyber operations. The proposed HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of simulating nation-state-level adversarial tactics while maintaining the low-latency processing required for operational relevance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance the integration of biophysical motor control models with artificial intelligence (AI) to simulate human-like adaptive movement in dynamic environments. While AI has made strides in pattern recognition and decision-making, current systems lack the nuanced, energy-efficient motor adaptability observed in humans, particularly under variable physical constraints (e.g., carrying loads, terrain shifts). This gap limits the deployment of AI in robotics, prosthetics, and human-in-the-loop systems requiring real-time biomechanical coordination. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining spiking neural networks (SNNs) with musculoskeletal simulations to model how sensorimotor feedback and cortical plasticity enable adaptive locomotion. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical to simulate multi-scale interactions: microscale neural dynamics (via SNNs), macroscale muscle-tendon mechanics, and environmental physics. The project will parameterize models using motion capture and electromyography data from human subjects performing tasks with perturbed kinetics. Parallelized optimization algorithms will iteratively refine neural controller architectures and biomechanical parameters to minimize metabolic cost while maximizing stability. Expected outcomes include a novel AI architecture capable of generalizing motor strategies across unseen physical scenarios, insights into neural redundancy principles for fault-tolerant control, and open-source tools for embodied AI development. This work bridges computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and machine learning, offering foundational advances for adaptive robotics and personalized rehabilitation technologies. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, real-time physics simulations, and comparative analyses of energy-optimal versus error-minimizing control policies—tasks infeasible on local clusters due to memory-intensive multibody dynamics and spike-based neural computations. Successful implementation will establish a benchmark for biologically grounded motor AI, with applications in assistive devices and human-robot collaboration systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the symbolic inference, representation, and simulation by computers and software of human learning and reasoning processes and capabilities, and the computer modeling of human motor control and motion. Includes instruction in computing theory, cybernetics, human factors, natural language processing, and applicable aspects of engineering, technology, and specific end-use applications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address challenges in analyzing high-dimensional, heterogeneous biomedical data, with a focus on longitudinal studies and spatial disease modeling. A critical bottleneck in biostatistical research is the computational inefficiency of existing tools when handling complex data structures, such as temporally correlated measurements, missing data patterns, or spatially varying disease risk factors. We propose to design and implement Bayesian hierarchical models with adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. These models will integrate multi-source clinical and public health datasets to estimate time-varying treatment effects in chronic disease cohorts while accounting for missingness mechanisms. A parallelized spatial analysis pipeline will also be developed to model disease spread using Gaussian process regression, enabling real-time risk mapping at granular geographic scales. The computational workflows will leverage distributed memory architectures through MPI-based parallelization and GPU acceleration for likelihood evaluations in large parameter spaces. Resource requests include allocations for benchmarking scalability across node configurations, storing intermediate outputs from 10,000+ simulated trial datasets, and running production analyses on cohorts exceeding 500,000 subjects with multi-omics covariates. Anticipated outcomes include open-source R/Python packages for efficient Bayesian inference on HPC clusters, validated through applications to NIH-funded studies on cardiovascular disease progression and mosquito-borne illness surveillance. This work will provide methodological advances in handling computationally intensive biostatistical problems while demonstrating how HPC resources can enable precise, real-time health risk assessments that traditional single-node systems cannot feasibly deliver. The tools developed will directly enhance reproducibility in clinical research and inform public health interventions through spatially resolved risk predictions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of descriptive and inferential statistics to biomedical research and clinical, public health, and industrial issues related to human populations. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, modeling, clinical trials methodology, disease and survival analysis, longitudinal analysis, missing data analysis, spatial analysis, computer tomography, biostatistics consulting, and applications to such topics as genetics, oncology, pharmacokinetics, physiology, neurobiology, and biophysics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the rational design of functional polymers by addressing critical gaps in understanding the molecular-scale mechanisms governing polymerization kinetics, macromolecular interactions, and structure-property relationships. Experimental approaches often struggle to resolve dynamic processes such as crosslinking in thermosetting resins or transient intermediates in catalytic polymerization, limiting the efficient development of polymers with tailored functionalities. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) methods. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model systems of industrially relevant complexity, including copolymerization networks and solvent-polymer interfacial phenomena. QM simulations will elucidate electronic interactions during initiation and propagation steps in radical polymerization, while coarse-grained MD will capture mesoscale chain dynamics under varying thermodynamic conditions. The kMC approach will integrate these insights to predict polymerization rates and molecular weight distributions. Key outcomes include identifying kinetic bottlenecks in sustainable polymer synthesis, optimizing reaction conditions for high-performance elastomers, and elucidating degradation pathways of unstable polyelectrolytes in solution. By mapping how monomer chemistry and process parameters influence macromolecular architecture, this work will directly inform the design of polymers for energy-efficient coatings and biodegradable packaging materials. The requested computing resources will enable simulations spanning nanoseconds to microseconds for systems exceeding 500,000 atoms, which is intractable with existing campus infrastructure. Successful execution will provide a predictive toolkit to reduce trial-and-error experimentation in polymer development, aligning with industrial priorities for rapid material innovation. All data and validated force fields will be shared publicly to accelerate broader research in polymer chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in business and economic journalism, addressing the growing complexity of analyzing large-scale financial and economic datasets for real-time, data-driven storytelling. Business journalists increasingly face challenges in processing vast volumes of unstructured data—such as earnings call transcripts, regulatory filings, social media sentiment, and global market indicators—while maintaining accuracy, context, and narrative coherence. Traditional tools for data analysis are insufficient for handling the scale, velocity, and heterogeneity of modern economic information, particularly when investigating cross-border financial trends, corporate misconduct, or systemic market risks. The proposed research will develop computational workflows integrating natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML), and network analysis to automate the extraction of actionable insights from multimodal sources. Key objectives include training domain-specific language models to identify nuanced financial jargon and rhetorical patterns in corporate communications, constructing dynamic economic indicator dashboards using real-time data streams, and simulating market behavior under hypothetical policy scenarios. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing ML models for low-latency inference, and running agent-based simulations of economic systems. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated fact-checking of financial claims, interactive visual storytelling platforms, and frameworks for ethical AI-augmented journalism. This work will enhance the capacity of journalists to uncover underreported economic stories, improve public understanding of financial systems, and mitigate misinformation in business reporting. By bridging computational methods with journalistic practice, the project aims to establish scalable, reproducible standards for data-intensive investigative journalism in the digital economy.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares students to gather, analyze, and synthesize verbal and visual information to communicate stories related to business and economics across multiple media platforms. Includes instruction in accounting, business, business and economic reporting, business law, economics, finance, financial accounting and reporting, ethics, journalistic research methods and resources, and journalism skills and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in multivalent atomic systems subjected to intense electromagnetic fields, a problem central to atomic and molecular physics. Current experimental techniques, such as attosecond laser spectroscopy, reveal ultrafast electron correlations and ionization processes that challenge theoretical models. Traditional single-active-electron approximations fail to capture collective multielectron effects, necessitating high-fidelity ab initio simulations. The research will employ time-dependent configuration interaction (TD-CI) and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) to model correlated electron dynamics in atoms like argon and xenon under strong-field conditions. These methods require solving high-dimensional Schrödinger equations with adaptive basis sets, a task infeasible without high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to exponential scaling with electron count. The project will leverage parallelized algorithms on GPU-accelerated architectures to optimize wavefunction propagation and reduce memory bottlenecks. Key objectives include quantifying the role of electron-electron interactions in high-harmonic generation and predicting ionization pathways in multivalent species. Outcomes will provide foundational insights into ultrafast quantum processes, aiding the design of next-generation photonic devices and attosecond metrology tools. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across field intensities and frequencies, generating datasets to validate against cutting-edge experiments. By bridging gaps between theory and observation, this work aims to establish predictive frameworks for controlling quantum states in extreme environments, with implications for quantum information science and precision measurement technologies. The computational workflows developed will also be disseminated as open-source tools, enhancing capabilities for the broader atomic physics community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for individuals with neuromotor impairments by integrating high-resolution biomechanical modeling, wearable sensor data, and machine learning to optimize assistive device design. Current approaches to prescribing mobility aids (e.g., exoskeletons, smart orthoses) often rely on population-level data, leading to suboptimal outcomes due to individual variations in neuromuscular control, tissue mechanics, and compensatory movement patterns. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework that combines patient-specific musculoskeletal simulations with dynamic analyses of real-world movement variability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal data streams—including motion capture, electromyography, and inertial measurement unit (IMU) signals—at scale while training neural networks to predict optimal device parameters under diverse functional scenarios (e.g., stair ascent, uneven terrain). The computational pipeline will leverage finite element modeling to simulate tissue-device interactions and reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine assistive torque profiles in silico. Expected outcomes include validated models linking biomechanical adaptability to clinical measures of mobility, an open-source toolkit for adaptive device tuning, and predictive metrics for long-term neuromuscular adaptation. By enabling rapid prototyping of personalized rehabilitation technologies, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in clinical device fitting, improve functional independence, and inform broader rehabilitation engineering standards. The scale of data assimilation (terabytes of kinematic, kinetic, and physiological inputs per subject) and the need for real-time simulation of multi-joint dynamics necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized optimization and large-scale parameter sensitivity analyses. This interdisciplinary approach bridges rehabilitation science, computational biomechanics, and AI-driven design, offering a novel pathway to precision rehabilitation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human function, disability, and rehabilitation from the perspectives of the health sciences, social sciences, psychology, engineering, and related fields. Includes instruction in psychological, social, and cultural aspects of disability and rehabilitation; sensory and motor function and dysfunction; biomechanics and kinesiology; assistive technology; rehabilitation instrumentation and methodology; statistics; and health and rehabilitation policy.

abstract: This study aims to address the critical challenge of modeling complex family system dynamics and their relationship to therapeutic outcomes in Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT). While systemic interventions are central to MFT, current research lacks computational tools to simulate the nonlinear, interdependent interactions among family members over time, limiting predictive insights into treatment efficacy. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational model of family communication networks and emotional regulation patterns using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML). The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets, including de-identified therapy session transcripts (NLP-analyzed for emotional valence and interaction patterns), physiological synchrony data from wearable devices, and longitudinal clinical outcome measures. Computational workflows will simulate thousands of family interaction scenarios under varying therapeutic strategies, identifying critical thresholds and feedback loops that predict successful outcomes. The scale of data integration (terabytes of audio, text, and biometric streams) and the need for real-time parameter optimization in ABM simulations necessitate parallelized GPU computing and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for optimizing intervention timing and modality based on family system characteristics, (2) open-access tools for visualizing interaction dynamics in therapy training contexts, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for personalizing systemic interventions. By elucidating how micro-level interactions propagate through family systems, this work will advance both MFT theory and clinical decision-making, offering a novel computational lens to study relational health. The proposed models will be validated against a longitudinal dataset of 300+ families undergoing therapy, ensuring clinical relevance while maintaining strict ethical safeguards for sensitive health data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of marriage and family therapy, involving the diagnosis of cognitive, affective, and behavioral domain disorders, both mental and emotional, within the context of marriage and family systems and the application of short- and long-term therapeutic strategies in family group contexts. Includes instruction in psychotherapy, family systems and studies, small group intervention and therapy, marital problems, depression, identification of psychopathologies and behavioral disorders, holistic health care, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize hydrocarbon recovery from unconventional reservoirs with complex subsurface heterogeneity, a critical challenge in petroleum engineering. Current reservoir simulation tools struggle to capture fine-scale geological features and coupled multiphase flow-geomechanical processes, leading to uncertainties in production forecasts and suboptimal recovery strategies. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating reservoir characterization data, finite element-based geomechanics, and parallelized compositional flow simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve millimeter-to-kilometer scale heterogeneities through adaptive mesh refinement and to perform ensemble simulations quantifying uncertainty in reservoir performance. Machine learning workflows will be implemented to accelerate history matching and optimize well placement and hydraulic fracturing designs under economic and environmental constraints. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed-memory parallelism to handle models exceeding 10^9 grid cells, reducing simulation times from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for predicting fracture propagation in stress-sensitive formations, improved quantification of hydrocarbon-in-place uncertainties, and data-driven strategies to enhance recovery rates while minimizing water usage and carbon intensity. By enabling high-resolution simulations of coupled processes at field scales, this work will provide operators with tools to reduce development risks in complex reservoirs, extend the productive life of mature assets, and support sustainable extraction practices. The requested HPC resources will directly advance these objectives by facilitating the execution of large parameter studies, sensitivity analyses, and machine learning training tasks that are infeasible on local computing clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for locating, extracting, processing and refining crude petroleum and natural gas, including prospecting instruments and equipment, mining and drilling systems, processing and refining systems and facilities, storage facilities, transportation systems, and related environmental and safety systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced simulation and optimization framework for industrial automation systems, addressing the challenge of deploying adaptive control strategies in dynamic production environments. Current automation systems often struggle to balance real-time responsiveness with energy efficiency and precision when operating under variable loads, uncertain sensor inputs, or rapidly changing process requirements. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this work will model multi-domain automation architectures integrating programmable logic controllers (PLCs), hydraulic-pneumatic actuators, and vision-based robotic systems. Computational methods will combine discrete-event simulation of control logic with parallelized fluid dynamics modeling of pneumatic networks and reinforcement learning algorithms for adaptive parameter tuning. Large-scale parameter sweeps will optimize system configurations across conflicting metrics including cycle time, positional accuracy, and energy consumption. The simulations will incorporate digital twins of industrial robotic workcells and material handling systems, validated against physical testbeds with embedded IoT sensor data. Expected outcomes include novel control architectures capable of self-optimization under stochastic operating conditions, predictive maintenance models for electromechanical actuators, and generalized design guidelines for fault-tolerant automation networks. By enabling computationally intensive co-simulation of mechanical, electrical, and control subsystems at production-relevant scales, this research will advance the deployment of resilient automation in small-to-medium manufacturing enterprises. The requested HPC resources will specifically accelerate evolutionary optimization workflows and deep reinforcement learning trials that exceed the capacity of local laboratory computing infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation templates and industry partnerships focused on upgradable automation systems aligned with Industry 4.0 standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, installing, calibrating, modifying and maintaining automated systems. Includes instruction in computer systems; electronics and instrumentation; programmable logic controllers (PLCs); electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control systems; actuator and sensor systems; process control; robotics; applications to specific industrial tasks; and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of household financial resilience under evolving macroeconomic and climate-related stressors. The study focuses on integrating behavioral economics, predictive analytics, and granular demographic data to simulate decision-making patterns in diverse household archetypes, particularly those underrepresented in traditional economic models. Current tools for assessing financial vulnerability rely on static, aggregate-level datasets, limiting their capacity to capture nonlinear interactions between income volatility, adaptive consumption behaviors, and region-specific environmental risks. To address this gap, the project will develop an agent-based modeling framework that simulates multi-scale feedback loops—from individual spending adjustments to systemic shocks in critical infrastructure networks. Computational workflows will combine structured financial microdata with unstructured behavioral indicators (e.g., sentiment analysis from community financial counseling transcripts) using graph neural networks to map latent risk pathways. HPC resources are essential for iteratively training these models across parameter spaces encompassing 10,000+ synthetic households, each with dynamically updating economic profiles and adaptive strategies. Expected outcomes include identifying early warning signals for financial fragility in subpopulations facing intersecting economic and climate pressures, as well as validating scenario-based policy interventions. The computational architecture produced will serve as a replicable toolkit for analyzing hyper-localized consumer economics challenges, bridging gaps between traditional econometric approaches and complex systems science. By quantifying how micro-level financial decisions propagate through socio-economic networks, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for enhancing household resilience while establishing methodological benchmarks for resource-intensive simulations in non-traditional consumer economics research.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Economics and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer economics and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling in hair design, focusing on the biomechanical and chemical dynamics of hair treatments. Traditional cosmetology research relies heavily on empirical trial-and-error methods, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to predict outcomes across diverse hair types or environmental conditions. Our work addresses this gap by developing physics-based simulations of hair fiber interactions during styling processes, such as heat tool application, chemical straightening, and coloring. Using molecular dynamics (MD) frameworks, we will model the structural response of keratin proteins under thermal and chemical stress, while finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate macro-scale hair behavior during cutting, braiding, and styling. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to predict outcomes like curl retention, color fade, and damage thresholds. The computational pipeline will integrate multi-scale data, from atomic-level disulfide bond reorganization to strand-level elasticity, enabling personalized styling recommendations based on hair porosity, density, and environmental factors like humidity. HPC resources are critical due to the need for parallelized simulations across thousands of hair strands, real-time rendering of complex geometries, and optimization of stochastic chemical diffusion processes. Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for cosmetology educators, a predictive database linking treatment parameters to hair health metrics, and a framework for virtual testing of novel styling products. This interdisciplinary approach bridges cosmetology, materials science, and computational engineering, offering a paradigm shift in beauty industry R&D by reducing reliance on physical prototyping and enabling data-driven, sustainable innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shampoo, cut, style, set, and dress the scalp hair of women and/or men, braid hair, apply hair cosmetics and wigs, and prepare for licensure as professional cosmetologists, hairdressers, and barbers at various levels.  Includes instruction in hair design theory and concepts, hair cleaning and shampooing, hair coloring, chemical applications and permanent reconstructions, hair anatomy and physiology, scalp diseases and treatments, wig and hairpiece fitting, hair braiding, customer service, shop management, equipment operation, health and safety, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the computational design of high-performance polymer systems with tailored thermal, mechanical, and chemical properties for industrial applications. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize polymer formulations and processing conditions are time- and resource-intensive, particularly when targeting multifunctional materials for extreme environments (e.g., high-temperature stability or chemical resistance). To overcome these limitations, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating atomistic molecular dynamics (MD), coarse-grained polymer models, and machine learning (ML) to predict structure-property relationships in complex polymer networks. The research will focus on simulating polymerization kinetics, crosslinking dynamics, and stress-strain behavior under operational conditions for novel thermosetting resins and elastomers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational demands of large-scale MD simulations (10^5-10^6 atoms) over nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales, coupled with iterative ML training using neural network architectures to map monomer chemistries to bulk material performance. Key deliverables include predictive models for glass transition temperature modulation in epoxy composites and fatigue resistance in 3D-printed photopolymers. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated simulations (LAMMPS, GROMACS) and custom Python-based analysis pipelines. Outcomes will directly inform experimental synthesis protocols for industry partners in automotive and renewable energy sectors, potentially reducing development cycles for polymer-based components by 30-50%. This work advances fundamental understanding of nonequilibrium polymer behavior while establishing scalable computational tools for next-generation materials discovery in chemical engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of synthesized macromolecular compounds and their application to specific engineering uses, including the development of industrial materials with tailored properties, the design of lightweight structural components, the use of liquid or solid polymers, and the analysis and control of polymerization processes.

abstract: The evolving landscape of homeland security threats necessitates advanced computational tools to model complex, multi-domain risks and optimize response strategies. This project addresses the critical challenge of simulating large-scale urban emergencies, where interdependent factors—including population dynamics, infrastructure vulnerabilities, and environmental conditions—create cascading effects that exceed the capabilities of conventional modeling approaches. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to analyze threat scenarios such as coordinated cyber-physical attacks, bioterrorism events, and critical infrastructure failures. The computational methodology integrates agent-based modeling to simulate crowd behavior, graph theory to assess networked infrastructure resilience, and machine learning to predict threat escalation patterns under uncertainty. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify probabilistic risks across thousands of scenario variants, while real-time data assimilation techniques will enable dynamic response optimization. The research will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for computationally intensive tasks such as fluid dynamics modeling of airborne hazard dispersion and neural network training for anomaly detection in large-scale sensor networks. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of generating prioritized mitigation strategies, optimizing resource allocation during multi-agency responses, and identifying choke points in urban emergency preparedness networks. By leveraging petascale computing resources to process terabytes of geospatial, demographic, and sensor-derived data, this work will advance the fundamental understanding of systemic vulnerabilities in heterogeneous urban environments. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated to public safety agencies, providing actionable insights to enhance national preparedness policies. This project directly aligns with homeland security priorities by bridging the gap between theoretical risk models and operational requirements for rapid, evidence-based crisis response.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and gendered dimensions of identity formation within Canadian immigrant and Indigenous communities, as reflected in multilingual textual archives and digital media. The research problem centers on the fragmented accessibility and analytical limitations of large-scale, heterogeneous cultural datasets—including digitized colonial-era documents, post-1960s immigrant community publications, and contemporary Indigenous digital storytelling platforms—which currently hinder systematic exploration of how intersecting identities have been negotiated across time and space in Canada. Using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques optimized for historical and multilingual texts, the project will analyze semantic shifts in self-representation, gendered discourse patterns, and cross-cultural narrative influences. Computational workflows will be tailored to handle low-resource languages (e.g., pre-standardization Indigenous orthographies, non-dominant immigrant languages) and ethically sensitive materials through collaborative model training with community partners. HPC capabilities are critical for processing terabyte-scale corpora, running parallelized sentiment/theme detection across temporal slices, and training transformer-based models for cross-linguistic comparison. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access repository of annotated datasets tracing identity-related discourse in underrepresented Canadian communities; (2) computational models identifying patterns of cultural hybridity and resistance in gendered narratives; and (3) visualization tools mapping the evolution of identity constructs across colonial, federal, and contemporary periods. By bridging computational methods with critical Canadian Studies frameworks, this research aims to redefine scholarly understanding of cultural memory and identity negotiation while establishing scalable protocols for ethically engaged digital humanities in pluralistic societies. The project directly addresses gaps in area-specific cultural analytics, offering methodological innovations for studying intersectional identities without relying on disciplinary approaches excluded by the program guidelines.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Canada and its Pre-Columbian, colonial, and pre-federation predecessors, including immigrant flows and related borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize energy efficiency and thermal performance in next-generation heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC&R) systems under dynamic environmental conditions. HVAC&R systems account for a significant proportion of global energy consumption, yet existing designs struggle to adapt efficiently to variable loads, extreme climates, and heterogeneous building environments. Current simulation tools often rely on steady-state assumptions or simplified transient analyses, limiting their ability to predict complex multi-physics interactions in real-world scenarios. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), transient energy modeling, and machine learning-driven optimization. Large-scale 3D CFD simulations will resolve turbulent airflow patterns, heat transfer dynamics, and refrigerant phase changes at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolutions using open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM) modified for HVAC-specific physics. Concurrently, system-level models will couple these results with building energy simulations (EnergyPlus) and component performance data through co-simulation protocols. A neural architecture search approach will then identify optimal control strategies and hardware configurations across diverse operating conditions. The computational workload demands parallelized execution across hundreds of CPU cores for parametric studies spanning design variables, climate zones, and load profiles, with GPU acceleration applied to machine learning workflows. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for adaptive HVAC&R operation, quantitative guidelines for fault detection under partial-load conditions, and novel design templates reducing energy use by 15-30% compared to conventional systems. This research will provide open-access datasets and modular code to support industry adoption, directly contributing to decarbonization goals in building infrastructure while advancing computational methodologies for thermal systems engineering.
cip_title: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, and heating systems. Includes instruction in principles of heating and cooling technology, design and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, installation and operation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of generative adversarial networks (GANs) in simulating and analyzing emergent patterns within decentralized information ecosystems, with a focus on ethical implications in understudied digital communities. The research addresses the challenge of modeling decentralized, user-driven platforms—such as niche collaborative storytelling forums or ephemeral media-sharing networks—where traditional computational frameworks struggle to capture nonlinear interactions between human creativity, algorithmic recommendation systems, and cultural evolution. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will develop a multi-agent simulation environment that integrates transformer-based language models with graph neural networks to map how micro-level user decisions propagate through these systems. The computational architecture will process terabyte-scale datasets of anonymized user interactions, synthetic text generation, and temporal network dynamics, requiring distributed training across GPU nodes and memory-intensive graph traversal algorithms. Key innovations include adaptive reward mechanisms for GAN discriminators that account for culturally specific norms and a novel metric for quantifying information "vulnerability" in non-hierarchical networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for ethical simulation of decentralized digital communities, empirical insights into resilience factors for minority cultural expressions in algorithmically mediated spaces, and methodological advances in scaling heterogeneous machine learning pipelines across hybrid CPU/GPU architectures. This work bridges computational social science, human-centered AI, and information ethics while operating outside conventional computer science paradigms, directly supporting the development of culturally aware media analysis frameworks.
cip_title: Computer Software and Media Applications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer software and media applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The optimization of animal diets to enhance health, productivity, and sustainability requires a mechanistic understanding of nutrient metabolism and its interactions with host physiology and the gut microbiome. Current challenges in animal nutrition research stem from the complexity of these biological systems, which involve dynamic, non-linear relationships between dietary components, microbial communities, and host metabolic pathways. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to disentangle these interactions at scale, limiting the ability to predict outcomes of novel feed formulations or additives. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing computational models that integrate multi-omics data, host-microbiome dynamics, and nutrient metabolism to enable precision diet design. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will construct genome-scale metabolic models of key gut microbial species and couple these with host tissue-specific metabolic networks to simulate system-wide responses to dietary changes. Machine learning approaches will be applied to high-throughput metagenomic and metabolomic datasets from poultry and swine feeding trials to identify predictive biomarkers of nutrient utilization efficiency. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will characterize the binding interactions between dietary additives (e.g., enzymes, prebiotics) and target substrates or microbial receptors. The computational workflow will require large-scale parallelization for parameter optimization in metabolic models, training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous biological data, and ensemble simulations of molecular interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing feed efficiency, mitigating enteric methane emissions in ruminants, and tailoring diets to animal life stages or health conditions. By enabling in silico testing of thousands of dietary scenarios, this resource-intensive approach will accelerate the development of targeted nutritional strategies that improve animal productivity while reducing environmental impacts. The resulting models and tools will be disseminated to the animal science community to advance research in precision livestock feeding systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the challenge of optimizing high-power laser systems for precision material processing applications, where thermal effects and nonlinear optical phenomena limit efficiency and accuracy. Current experimental approaches to mitigate these issues are time-intensive and costly, while existing computational models lack the resolution to capture multi-scale interactions between laser parameters, material response, and thermal diffusion. This project seeks to develop a parallelized computational framework combining finite-element analysis for thermal modeling with time-domain beam propagation methods to simulate laser-matter interactions across spatial scales from nanometers to millimeters. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to implement GPU-accelerated solvers for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation governing ultrafast laser propagation, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify optimal pulse sequences and beam profiles. Key deliverables include an open-source simulation toolkit for laser system design and validated protocols for minimizing thermal damage in glass micromachining processes. Expected outcomes will advance optical manufacturing techniques by enabling predictive modeling of complex laser-material interactions, reducing trial-and-error prototyping cycles by an estimated 60%. The computational infrastructure developed will directly support curriculum modernization in laser applications coursework, providing students with hands-on experience in photonics simulation while addressing industry needs for energy-efficient laser processing systems. This work bridges critical gaps between theoretical optical principles and practical engineering implementation, with potential applications in photonic device fabrication and advanced optical metrology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using lasers and other optical for commercial or research purposes. Includes instruction in laser and optical principles, testing and maintenance procedures, safety precautions, specific applications to various tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of disease pathogenesis in animals demands advanced computational tools to unravel multifactorial interactions between pathogens, host genetics, and environmental factors. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale genomic, proteomic, and epidemiological datasets hinder progress in diagnosing and managing emerging infectious diseases, metabolic disorders, and toxicological syndromes in veterinary populations. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support the development of integrated computational models that bridge molecular-scale pathogen-host dynamics with population-level disease transmission patterns. Leveraging machine learning algorithms and agent-based modeling frameworks, we will analyze multi-omics datasets from livestock and wildlife species affected by viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens, including spatially resolved environmental exposure data. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to enable genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for inherited metabolic diseases in companion animals, molecular dynamics simulations of pathogen-receptor interactions, and real-time phylogenetic tracing of outbreak strains. The HPC environment will also facilitate the creation of a federated learning platform for collaborative analysis of sensitive veterinary diagnostic data across institutions while maintaining privacy constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive models for antimicrobial resistance emergence in zoonotic pathogens, identification of genetic markers for early disease detection, and optimized therapeutic strategies for toxicant exposure scenarios. These computational advances will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy, inform targeted vaccination protocols, and improve outbreak response capabilities in veterinary medicine. By integrating cutting-edge computational approaches with pathological expertise, this work aims to establish a transformative framework for understanding complex disease mechanisms in animal populations, with translational implications for One Health initiatives.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the development and process of disease in domestic and wild animals and applications to diagnosis, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in pathogenesis, immunoparasitology, viral therapy, inherited metabolic diseases, environmental toxicology, anatomical and clinical pathology, necropsy and biopsy techniques, clinical laboratory analysis, pathological interpretation, and disease diagnosis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to assess landslide susceptibility in tectonically active regions, with a focus on improving infrastructure resilience and site evaluation practices. Current methods for landslide prediction often rely on simplified geotechnical parameters or static geological maps, which inadequately capture dynamic interactions between hydrological processes, seismic activity, and heterogeneous subsurface materials. To address this, we propose a high-resolution, multiphysics framework integrating 3D finite element modeling of slope stability, machine learning-driven soil property estimation, and probabilistic seismic triggering scenarios. The computational workflow will process terabytes of geospatial data, including LiDAR-derived topography, InSAR deformation records, and regional borehole logs, to parameterize models at meter-scale resolution across 100+ km² study areas. High-performance computing resources are essential to execute Monte Carlo simulations quantifying uncertainty in failure thresholds under climate-driven precipitation extremes and earthquake recurrence intervals. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible risk assessment toolkit for engineers and a novel database correlating lithological heterogeneity with slope failure mechanisms. By enabling real-time updates of hazard maps during extreme weather events, this work directly supports the design of adaptive transportation infrastructure and improves construction site selection protocols in geologically complex terrains. The scalability of the framework will be validated across case studies in the Pacific Northwest and Himalayan regions, with potential applications to natural resource corridor planning and post-disaster recovery strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and geological principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, including the geological evaluation of construction sites, the analysis of geological forces acting on structures and systems, the analysis of potential natural resource recovery sites, and applied research on geological phenomena.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of doctrinal formulations in pre-modern Christian theological texts, with a focus on identifying patterns of conceptual adaptation across linguistic, cultural, and geopolitical contexts. While theological studies have traditionally relied on close textual analysis, the scale and complexity of doctrinal corpora—spanning Greek, Latin, Syriac, and Coptic sources from the 4th to 15th centuries—require computational methods to systematically trace theological innovations, semantic shifts, and intertextual dependencies. The research problem centers on how doctrinal statements negotiated continuity and change amid competing theological schools, ecumenical councils, and socio-political transformations, a process poorly understood at macrohistorical scales. Using a hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis, the project will process digitized critical editions of conciliar acts, patristic writings, and scholastic summas to construct a multilayer graph model mapping (1) terminological diffusion across genres and languages, (2) citation networks linking authoritative sources to later interpretations, and (3) temporal correlations between doctrinal developments and external historical events. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect theological argument structures and conceptual reconfigurations in low-resource ancient languages, while HPC-enabled simulations will test hypotheses about doctrinal stabilization mechanisms. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing eight centuries of theological discourse, computational tools for diachronic semantic analysis of doctrinal texts, and quantitative frameworks for assessing the relative impacts of intramural theological debate versus external factors on doctrinal change. By bridging computational humanities and historical theology, this project aims to establish new methodologies for studying religious thought as a complex adaptive system while providing resources for interdisciplinary scholarship on tradition formation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the beliefs and doctrine of a particular religious faith from the intramural point of view of that faith.
