By bridging consumer economic theory with computational social science methods, this work aims to establish normative frameworks for evaluating digital consumption environments that currently operate outside conventional policy paradigms. The requested resources will enable iteration cycles necessary to account for DeFi’s rapid protocol evolution and validate models against real-world transaction networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of micro- and macro-economic theory to consumer behavior and individual and family consumption of goods and services. Includes instruction in modeling, economic forecasting, indexing, price theory, and analysis of individual commodities and services and/or groups of related commodities and services.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biological systems demands advanced computational tools to integrate heterogeneous, multi-scale data and predict emergent behaviors. Current approaches in systems biology struggle to reconcile dynamic molecular interactions with population-level phenotypic outcomes, particularly when analyzing high-dimensional datasets from single-cell omics, live imaging, and spatially resolved transcriptomics. This project seeks to develop a scalable, open-source computational framework to model cross-scale biological processes by coupling mechanistic simulations with machine learning-driven parameter optimization. The research will focus on creating modular, parallelized algorithms to simulate intracellular signaling networks, cell-cell communication, and tissue-scale dynamics within a unified architecture. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for three components: (1) deploying ensemble simulations to explore parameter spaces of stochastic differential equation models, (2) training graph neural networks on spatial omics data to infer interaction rules, and (3) optimizing hybrid models through differentiable programming techniques. The proposed framework will implement adaptive load balancing and GPU-accelerated tensor operations to efficiently utilize distributed memory systems. Expected outcomes include novel statistical metrics for quantifying model-data concordance in multi-omics studies, validated through applications to publicly available datasets on developmental patterning and immune cell coordination. By enabling integration of disparate data types while maintaining biophysical interpretability, this work will address critical gaps in predictive systems biology. The resulting tools will be disseminated as containerized workflows to enhance reproducibility, with performance benchmarks guiding best practices for HPC utilization in computational biology. This project directly advances methodological innovation in biological simulation and data integration, with broader implications for designing targeted interventions in complex diseases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computational theoretical approaches to understanding biological systems, including computational models of biological processes, computational management of large-scale projects, database development and data-algorithm development, and high-performance computing, as well as statistical and mathematical analyses.

abstract: The increasing demand for air transportation, coupled with stringent environmental regulations, necessitates advancements in aerodynamic efficiency and operational optimization of next-generation aircraft. Current challenges in computational aerodynamics, such as accurately modeling turbulent flows at high Reynolds numbers and optimizing complex geometries under multidisciplinary constraints, require high-fidelity simulations that surpass the capabilities of conventional computing resources. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable large-scale, multiphysics simulations of aircraft aerodynamics and propulsion systems. The research will employ advanced computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods, including detached eddy simulation (DES) and lattice Boltzmann models, to resolve fine-scale turbulence and aeroacoustic phenomena in wing design and engine integration. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate optimization workflows for airframe-propulsion coupling, reducing computational costs while maintaining accuracy. The proposed HPC resources will facilitate parametric studies across diverse flight regimes (subsonic to transonic) and operational scenarios, including ground effect dynamics during takeoff and landing. Expected outcomes include the development of optimized aircraft configurations with reduced drag and noise profiles, validated against experimental wind tunnel data. These results will directly contribute to lowering fuel consumption and emissions in commercial aviation, aligning with global sustainability targets. The computational frameworks developed will also be disseminated as open-source tools to support broader academic and industry research in aerospace systems. By addressing scalability bottlenecks in high-resolution simulations, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities in aeronautical science and inform future certification standards for environmentally adaptive aircraft designs.
cip_title: Aeronautics/ Aviation/ Aerospace Science and Technology, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of aviation and the aviation industry, including in-flight and ground support operations. Includes instruction in the technical, business, and general aspects of air transportation systems.

abstract: Cybersecurity defense strategies require dynamic, evidence-based policy frameworks capable of adapting to rapidly evolving adversarial tactics and systemic vulnerabilities. Traditional policy evaluation methods often lack the granularity to model complex, large-scale interactions between cyber adversaries, defenders, and infrastructure, particularly under scenarios involving cascading failures or multi-actor coordination. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational model to simulate cyber conflict dynamics and evaluate the resilience of policy interventions in real-world, heterogeneous network environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-driven threat behavior prediction to analyze how strategic policy decisions—such as incident reporting mandates, public-private threat intelligence sharing protocols, and cross-border regulatory harmonization—impact systemic risk reduction and attack surface management. The computational framework will ingest real-world datasets, including historical cyber incident reports, geopolitical event timelines, and critical infrastructure metadata, to generate probabilistic scenarios for stress-testing policy efficacy under varying adversarial capabilities and societal dependencies. Key outcomes will include a policy optimization toolkit for identifying context-specific resilience thresholds, a taxonomy of high-impact cyber deterrence failure modes linked to regulatory gaps, and predictive metrics for quantifying the societal cost-benefit tradeoffs of emerging defense paradigms. By bridging computational scalability with policy analytics, this work aims to advance the operationalization of adaptive governance frameworks in cybersecurity, offering stakeholders actionable insights into long-term strategic planning and resource allocation for cyber defense ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing ensemble synchronization and expressive coherence in complex musical performances through advanced computational modeling. Conductors must process multifaceted auditory and gestural information in real time to guide ensembles, yet the dynamic interplay between conductor intent, performer interpretation, and acoustic outcomes remains poorly quantified. Traditional pedagogical and analytical methods lack the capacity to model these interactions at scale, particularly for large ensembles performing intricate works. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for simulating and analyzing conductor-ensemble dynamics. Motion-capture data from professional conductors will be integrated with multi-track audio recordings of ensemble performances, capturing temporal, spatial, and spectral relationships. Machine learning models, trained on this multimodal dataset, will identify patterns linking conducting gestures to ensemble responsiveness across diverse repertoire and ensemble configurations. Concurrently, physics-based acoustic simulations will model sound propagation in virtual performance spaces, enabling the study of how conductor decisions influence collective intonation and balance. The scale of data processing—terabytes of high-resolution motion and audio data—and the parallelized nature of acoustic simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime. Expected outcomes include predictive models of gesture efficacy, tools for automated score-based rehearsal planning, and a virtual rehearsal environment to test conducting strategies under variable acoustic and ensemble conditions. This work will provide novel insights into performance pedagogy, offering empirically grounded frameworks for conductors to refine their technical and interpretive approaches. By quantifying elements of artistic leadership traditionally governed by intuition, the project aims to advance the scholarly understanding of conducting while developing scalable computational tools for the performing arts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the art of leading bands, choirs, orchestras and other ensembles in performance, and related music leadership. Includes instruction in score analysis and arranging, rehearsal and performance leadership, music coaching, arrangement and performance planning, ensemble operations management, and applications to specific school or professional ensembles.

abstract: The development of advanced metallic alloys with tailored microstructures for high-temperature, load-bearing applications remains a critical challenge in metallurgical engineering. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize alloy composition and thermomechanical processing parameters are time-intensive and limited in resolving the complex interplay between atomic-scale phenomena and macroscopic properties. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to establish a multiscale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD), phase-field modeling, and finite element analysis (FEA). The research will focus on elucidating the mechanisms of creep deformation and fatigue crack propagation in nickel-based superalloys and refractory high-entropy alloys under extreme thermal and mechanical conditions. Atomistic simulations will quantify dislocation mobility and grain boundary segregation effects, while mesoscale phase-field models will predict microstructural evolution during heat treatment and service. Macroscale FEA will correlate these results with component-level stress distributions and failure thresholds. The computational workflow will be validated against synchrotron X-ray diffraction and electron backscatter diffraction data from collaborating experimental groups. By systematically linking processing-structure-property relationships across scales, this work aims to identify alloy compositions and processing routes that enhance resistance to cyclic oxidation and stress-driven degradation. The requested HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across compositionally complex systems and statistically significant sampling of microstructural configurations, which are infeasible with local computing infrastructure. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools for microstructure-sensitive alloy design and a database of computationally optimized heat treatment protocols. This research directly addresses the metallurgical engineering community’s need for predictive tools to accelerate the development of next-generation alloys for energy generation systems and heavy industrial machinery, where performance limits are increasingly constrained by current materials capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and metallurgical principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of metal components of structural, load-bearing, power, transmission, and moving systems; and the analysis of engineering problems such as stress, creep, failure, alloy behavior, environmental fluctuations, stability, electromagnetic and thermodynamic characteristics, optimal manufacturing processes, and related design considerations.

abstract: The development of stable, efficacious, and scalable pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations requires precise control over molecular interactions and material behaviors under diverse conditions. Current experimental approaches to optimize formulation parameters (e.g., excipient compatibility, rheological properties, and long-term stability) are resource-intensive and time-consuming, particularly when scaling laboratory prototypes to industrial production. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex formulation systems at multiple scales, enabling predictive insights into product performance and manufacturability. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) developing multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to predict excipient-drug interactions and phase behavior in novel topical drug delivery systems, and (2) employing finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning (ML) to model the impact of industrial processing conditions (e.g., shear forces, temperature gradients) on product microstructure and stability. Computational workflows will integrate quantum mechanical calculations for specific interaction energies, coarse-grained MD for mesoscale aggregation phenomena, and continuum-scale FEA for equipment-scale process simulations. These models will be validated against experimental data from collaborative laboratory studies, including accelerated stability testing and rheological characterization. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to formulation optimization, particularly for systems containing multiple active ingredients, surfactants, and polymers. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to reduce trial-and-error experimentation in preformulation stages, identify stability risks under real-world storage conditions, and optimize manufacturing parameters for continuous production processes. By bridging molecular-level understanding with industrial-scale operational constraints, this work aims to advance computational pharmaceutics as a decision-support tool for faster, more sustainable product development while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards for quality-by-design (QbD) principles.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: Neurodevelopmental disabilities (NDDs) in children, including autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, and sensory impairment-related delays, present complex challenges due to heterogeneous etiology, multifactorial interactions, and variability in treatment response. Current clinical approaches often lack precision, partly due to insufficient understanding of the interplay between genetic, neural, and environmental factors shaping neurodevelopmental trajectories. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of neurodevelopmental outcomes and optimize personalized intervention strategies. The research integrates multimodal datasets—including longitudinal neuroimaging (fMRI, DTI), electrophysiology (EEG), genomic data, and clinical phenotyping from a cohort of 1,200 children with NDDs—to identify biomarkers of treatment response and developmental progression. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble methods) to model dynamic brain network reorganization during skill acquisition, simulating how targeted therapies alter neural plasticity. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of sensorimotor and cognitive skill development, calibrated to patient-specific parameters derived from real-world wearable sensor data. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional neuroimaging datasets (>10 TB), parallelizing computationally intensive simulations of neural circuit maturation, and enabling real-time optimization of adaptive therapeutic protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for stratifying children into subgroups based on computationally derived neurobehavioral profiles, (2) predictive models linking early biomarkers to long-term functional outcomes, and (3) open-source tools for simulating intervention effects across developmental timelines. This work addresses a critical gap in translating neurocomputational insights into clinical practice, with potential to reduce diagnostic delays and improve targeted resource allocation in early intervention programs. By elucidating mechanisms of neuroplasticity in diverse NDD populations, the project aims to advance evidence-based, individualized therapeutic approaches for children with complex developmental needs.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat children having developmental delays or learning disorders, including those associated with visual and hearing impairment, developmental delays, cerebral palsy, spina bifida, autism, and other chronic neurologic conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of pest population dynamics and optimize integrated pest management (IPM) strategies in agroecosystems. Current models struggle to integrate multi-scale data—spanning genomic, ecological, and environmental variables—that drive pest behavior, pesticide resistance evolution, and crop-pest interactions. This limitation hinders the design of targeted, sustainable interventions. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and spatially explicit simulations. The ABM will simulate pest movement, reproduction, and adaptation under varying climatic conditions and management practices, while ML algorithms trained on field and omics datasets (e.g., pest genomic variants, crop phenomics) will predict resistance emergence and host-plant susceptibility. Large-scale parameter sweeps will evaluate the efficacy of IPM tactics, including biopesticide rotation, habitat manipulation, and precision chemical applications. HPC resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of these simulations, which involve millions of agents, high-resolution geospatial data, and stochastic climate projections. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of regional pest outbreak thresholds linked to environmental drivers, (2) genomic markers associated with rapid resistance development, and (3) decision-support tools for dynamically optimizing pesticide deployment and biocontrol agent introductions. By enabling real-time adaptation of IPM strategies to shifting pest pressures and climate variability, this work aims to reduce crop losses by 15–30% in test systems while minimizing non-target chemical impacts. The resulting open-source computational tools will empower agricultural stakeholders to implement data-driven, ecologically resilient pest management protocols.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Plant Protection and Integrated Pest Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific principles to the control of animal, insect and weed infestation of domesticated plant populations and other settings, including agricultural crops; the prevention/reduction of attendant economic loss; and the control of environmental pollution and degradation related to pest infestation and pest control measures. Includes instruction in entomology, applicable animal sciences, plant pathology and physiology, weed science, crop science, and environmental toxicology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of early and accurate diagnosis of rare retinal disorders, which often present with subtle, heterogeneous features in multimodal ophthalmic imaging. Current clinical workflows rely on manual interpretation of optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus photography, and fluorescein angiography by ophthalmic technicians and ophthalmologists—a process prone to variability and delayed detection. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, high-resolution retinal imaging datasets. The research will focus on integrating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models to identify pathognomonic patterns across imaging modalities, including subclinical biomarkers in OCT angiography and spatial-temporal features in dynamic contrast imaging. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets from multi-institutional collaborations, ensuring robust generalization across demographics and imaging devices. Key innovations include the development of anomaly detection algorithms tailored to low-prevalence diseases and synthetic data augmentation pipelines to address class imbalance. Expected outcomes include a deployable tool that prioritizes cases with high-risk features, provides interpretable saliency maps for technician review, and reduces diagnostic latency. By enhancing the precision of preliminary assessments made by ophthalmic technicians, this resource could significantly improve triage efficiency in clinical workflows, enabling timely specialist intervention. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in scaling AI solutions for niche ophthalmic applications, directly supporting the technical and diagnostic responsibilities outlined in ophthalmic technologist training paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist ophthalmologists and optometrists in examining and treating patients with vision problems, vision disorders, and eye diseases. Includes instruction in taking patient histories, administering directed treatments and topical medications, diagnostic test procedures and equipment operation, anatomical and functional ocular measurements, patient care and instruction, ophthalmic and surgical equipment maintenance, safety and sterilization procedures, and office administrative procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern agricultural machinery, particularly in hydraulic, electrical, and combustion systems, demands advanced computational tools to optimize performance and reduce operational failures. Current maintenance protocols for equipment such as crop-spraying systems, tractors, and automated harvesters rely on reactive or schedule-based approaches, which often lead to inefficient resource use, unexpected downtime, and environmental risks from leaks or over-application of inputs. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing predictive maintenance frameworks through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations and machine learning. We propose to model multi-physics interactions within hydraulic and combustion systems under diverse operational conditions, integrating sensor data from field equipment to train neural networks for anomaly detection. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will analyze fluid behavior in irrigation pumps and sprayer nozzles, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess mechanical stress in tillage and harvesting components. These simulations will be coupled with real-world telemetry data to identify failure precursors, such as pressure fluctuations or thermal imbalances, and predict component degradation timelines. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large datasets from IoT-enabled machinery and accelerate iterative design optimization for critical subsystems. Expected outcomes include validated predictive maintenance algorithms deployable on edge computing platforms, reduced machinery downtime by 20–30%, and design recommendations for next-generation agricultural equipment with improved energy efficiency. By advancing computational methodologies tailored to agricultural mechanization, this research will directly support the sustainability of farm operations, lower maintenance costs, and minimize environmental impacts from equipment inefficiencies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural Mechanics and Equipment/ Machine Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to maintain and repair specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment and vehicles. Includes instruction in the principles of diesel, combustion, electrical, steam, hydraulic, and mechanical systems and their application to the maintenance of terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos; irrigation and pumping equipment; dairy, feeding, and shearing operations; and processing systems.

abstract: The development of novel pharmaceutical agents requires overcoming significant challenges in optimizing drug efficacy, safety, and manufacturability. Traditional experimental approaches to drug design, process optimization, and quality control are often resource-intensive, time-consuming, and limited in their ability to model complex biological and industrial systems at scale. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate computational workflows in small-molecule and biologic drug development. The research will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study drug-target binding kinetics and stability, machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-omics datasets to predict drug-protein interactions, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling to optimize dosing regimens. Additionally, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be applied to improve bioreactor design for plasmid DNA and protein expression systems, with parallelized Monte Carlo methods used to assess manufacturing process robustness under variable conditions. These approaches require substantial computational power due to the need for long-timescale MD simulations (microsecond to millisecond ranges), large-scale parameter space exploration in PK/PD models, and high-resolution 3D simulations of industrial-scale bioprocessing equipment. Expected outcomes include the identification of lead compounds with improved binding specificity, optimized bioproduction protocols to enhance yield and purity, and predictive models for quality assurance that reduce batch failure rates. The integration of HPC-enabled computational methods aims to shorten development timelines by 30-50% for select case study compounds while improving compliance with regulatory standards for process validation. By bridging computational pharmacology with industrial-scale optimization, this work will provide a framework for data-driven decision-making in pharmaceutical R&D, ultimately supporting more efficient translation of therapeutic candidates into manufacturable products. Resource allocation will directly enable critical benchmarks in simulating complex drug delivery systems, host-cell protein interactions, and large-N analyses of formulation stability under diverse environmental conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific application of pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and industrial management to the development, production, marketing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Includes instruction in industrial microbiology, plasmids, expression vectors, protein chemistry, assay and evaluation, drug synthesis and purification, quality control, industrial management, production security, patent procedures, intellectual property regulations and issues, patent enforcement and defense, and research design and testing.

abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying collective decision-making in social animal groups remains a critical challenge in behavioral neuroscience. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to disentangle the dynamic interplay between individual cognitive processes, sensorimotor integration, and emergent group-level behaviors. This project proposes to develop an integrative computational framework combining large-scale neural network simulations with agent-based modeling to investigate how decentralized neural computations scale to produce adaptive collective behaviors in schooling fish. The research employs three computational pillars: 1) Biologically constrained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained on experimental motion tracking data from individual fish, 2) Multi-scale simulations of visual processing and hydrodynamic sensing in realistic aquatic environments, and 3) Evolutionary algorithms optimizing neural architectures for group coordination under ecological constraints. High-performance computing resources are essential for simulating thousands of interacting agents with biologically plausible neural models while maintaining millisecond temporal resolution across hours of behavioral sequences. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how evolutionary pressures shape neural circuit organization for collective intelligence, predictive models of group response thresholds to environmental perturbations, and a computational toolkit for analyzing emergent information flow in animal collectives. The results will advance fundamental understanding of distributed cognition in biological systems while informing the design of bio-inspired swarm robotics. By bridging neuroethology with complex systems science, this work establishes new computational paradigms for studying collective behavior across biological scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the psychological and neurological bases of animal sensation, perception, cognition, behavior, and behavioral interactions within and outside the species. Includes instruction in ethology, behavioral neuroscience, neurobiology, behavioral evolution, cognition and sensory perception, motivators, learning and instinct, hormonal controls, reproductive and developmental biology, community ecology, functional behavior, and applications to specific behaviors and patterns as well as to specific phyla and species.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive pedagogical models for social science teacher education. A critical challenge in preparing educators is the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze how novice teachers integrate interdisciplinary social science content (e.g., economics, civics, geography) with evidence-based instructional strategies. Current approaches rely on small-scale qualitative assessments or simplified quantitative metrics, limiting the ability to model complex interactions between teacher knowledge, classroom discourse, and student outcomes. To address this gap, the project will employ computational text analysis, network modeling, and agent-based simulations to analyze large multimodal datasets from teacher training programs, including video recordings of practice lessons, written reflection journals, and student assessment records. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to quantify discourse patterns and content alignment in simulated classroom interactions, while graph-based methods will map conceptual understanding growth across diverse social science domains. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training transformer-based NLP models on domain-specific educational corpora, and running parallelized simulations to test how variations in pedagogical training scenarios propagate through educational systems. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for modeling social science teaching efficacy, validated against longitudinal outcomes from partner K-12 districts. The results will directly inform the design of targeted professional development modules and provide empirical guidance for balancing interdisciplinary content coverage with pedagogical skill development in teacher education curricula. By integrating computational social science methods with education research, this work aims to establish scalable infrastructure for improving equity in social science instruction across diverse classroom contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific social science subjects and programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize texture-modified meal planning for patients with dysphagia, a swallowing disorder affecting over 500 million individuals globally. Current dietitian-led approaches rely on manual adjustments to food consistency using standardized scales (e.g., IDDSI), but these methods often fail to account for dynamic interactions between nutritional content, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability during preparation. We propose an HPC-driven approach to model multi-parameter relationships between ingredient composition, processing techniques (e.g., mechanical softening, thickening agents), and post-preparation food behavior. A hybrid pipeline will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of hydrocolloid interactions, finite element analysis of mechanical stress distribution in heterogeneous food matrices, and machine learning models trained on clinical outcomes data from 15,000+ patient records. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated parallel processing to iteratively optimize meal plans against conflicting constraints: maximizing nutrient retention, ensuring safe swallowing rheology, maintaining palatability, and minimizing preparation time. Validation will involve 3D-printed food analogs with embedded sensors to quantify real-world deformation forces against simulated predictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that reduces dietitians’ trial-and-error workload by 40–60% while improving patient adherence through personalized texture-nutrient profiles. This work bridges gaps between food rheology, clinical nutrition, and computational modeling, addressing a critical need in under-resourced healthcare settings where dysphagia management is frequently deprioritized. The resulting framework will establish scalable methodologies for adaptive meal optimization applicable to other chronic conditions requiring specialized diets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between multigenerational family communication patterns and adolescent identity development in emergent digital socialization spaces. While prior work in Human Development and Family Studies has examined offline family interactions, the proliferation of hybrid communication ecosystems—integrating messaging platforms, social media, and AI-mediated tools—creates novel developmental contexts that remain poorly understood. The research addresses this gap by analyzing longitudinal, multimodal interaction data (text, audio, video) from 150 families to model how digitally mediated communication influences identity negotiation processes during adolescence. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets through three integrated computational approaches: 1) transformer-based NLP pipelines to detect semantic and pragmatic features in cross-generational dialogues, 2) temporal network analysis of interaction patterns across platforms, and 3) agent-based modeling simulating identity development trajectories under varying communication constraints. The computational framework will incorporate psychological theories of self-concept formation while advancing methodological integration of developmental science with computational social science. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of digital communication ecotypes in family systems, predictive models of technology-mediated identity development pathways, and open-source tools for analyzing multimodal family interactions at scale. This work provides critical insights into how evolving digital environments reshape fundamental developmental processes, with implications for designing family-centered interventions that support healthy identity formation in technologically saturated societies. The requested resources will enable processing of temporally dense, high-dimensional data that exceeds conventional computing capabilities, particularly for training domain-specific language models and running large-scale simulations of longitudinal developmental processes.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of interactive narrative systems in modern video games demands computational approaches capable of dynamically adapting storylines while maintaining coherence, emotional resonance, and player agency. Traditional procedural content generation methods often prioritize efficiency over narrative depth, resulting in formulaic or disjointed storytelling experiences. This project proposes the development of a hybrid AI-driven narrative framework that integrates large language models (LLMs), affective computing, and real-time player behavior analysis to generate contextually rich, emotionally adaptive story arcs. The research addresses the computational challenge of balancing low-latency narrative adjustments during gameplay with the high-dimensional optimization required for multi-character plot consistency across extended play sessions. A multi-stage architecture will be implemented, combining transformer-based dialogue systems, graph neural networks for plot state tracking, and reinforcement learning agents trained to maximize narrative novelty while preserving causal logic. High-performance computing resources are essential for training ensemble models on heterogeneous datasets encompassing literary structures, player interaction logs, and psycholinguistic annotations. GPU-accelerated simulations will test dynamic narrative branching under variable player decision densities, while distributed computing will enable large-scale A/B testing of emotional valence predictions across diverse demographic profiles. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for emotion-aware narrative generation, quantitative metrics for evaluating interactive story coherence, and novel techniques for real-time constraint satisfaction in branching narrative systems. This work bridges gaps between computational creativity, affective human-computer interaction, and game design, offering foundational methods for next-generation storytelling in games and immersive media.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying voltage-gated ion channel function, a critical yet poorly understood process in cellular electrophysiology. Despite advances in structural biology, the dynamic coupling between voltage-sensing domains and pore gating remains unresolved due to limitations in experimentally capturing transient conformational states. We propose a computational approach integrating atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with enhanced sampling techniques to model the complete activation pathway of a prototypical potassium channel (Kv1.2) under physiological membrane potentials. All-atom MD simulations will employ the CHARMM36 force field in GROMACS, simulating systems exceeding 150,000 atoms over microsecond timescales to capture slow gating transitions. Metadynamics and umbrella sampling will be applied to calculate free energy landscapes associated with voltage sensor movement and pore opening. These simulations require substantial high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the need for replica exchanges across multiple electric field conditions, explicit solvent models, and statistical convergence across >10 independent trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of intermediate states linking voltage sensor activation to pore dilation, (2) quantification of energy barriers governing gating kinetics, and (3) validation of a novel helical-screw mechanistic model through direct comparison with patch-clamp electrophysiology data. The results will advance fundamental understanding of bioelectrical signaling while providing a computational framework to study pathogenic mutations in channelopathies. Successful completion demands dedicated access to GPU-accelerated nodes for rapid sampling and >500,000 core-hours annually to achieve sufficient temporal and statistical resolution. This work directly aligns with biophysical priorities in membrane biology and protein dynamics, bridging gaps between static structures and functional measurements through physics-based modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Italian dialectal variation and its historical-literary intersections. Despite Italy’s rich linguistic diversity, systematic studies of regional dialects remain fragmented due to the scale and complexity of data, which spans centuries of textual production, oral recordings, and sociolinguistic metadata. Traditional manual methods struggle to model nuanced phonetic, syntactic, and lexical patterns across time and geography, limiting insights into language evolution and its cultural implications. Our research aims to bridge this gap by developing scalable computational workflows to analyze digitized corpora of regional texts, speech samples, and historical documents. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for low-resource dialects, we will train transformer-based models to detect phonetic shifts, morphosyntactic features, and lexical borrowing across regions. Parallelized geospatial analysis will map dialect boundaries and their correlation with literary production trends extracted from metadata-rich archives (e.g., 19th-century regional novels, Renaissance merchant correspondence). HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, run distributed training for dialect-specific language models, and perform Monte Carlo simulations testing hypotheses about contact-induced language change. Expected outcomes include an open-access dialect atlas visualizing linguistic variation, computational tools for automated philological annotation, and quantitative models linking dialectal features to literary innovation. This work will provide scholars with novel methodologies to trace language dynamics at unprecedented resolution, inform preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and deepen understanding of Italy’s linguistic identity. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, the project exemplifies the transformative potential of HPC in advancing research on under-resourced languages and their cultural heritage.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Italian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in modeling nonlinear optical processes driven by ultrafast laser pulses in complex media, a problem requiring high-resolution simulations of light-matter interactions across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Current analytical models struggle to predict nonlinear responses in disordered or dynamically evolving systems, such as turbulent plasmas or optofluidic environments, where inhomogeneities and transient phenomena dominate. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled computational framework integrating time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for electron dynamics with finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for electromagnetic wave propagation. By resolving sub-cycle optical field variations alongside quantum-scale electron correlations, this approach aims to uncover mechanisms governing high-harmonic generation, soliton formation, and chaotic light propagation in non-stationary systems. Key computational challenges include managing petabyte-scale datasets from 4D spatiotemporal simulations, optimizing parallelized algorithms for GPU-accelerated architectures, and validating models against experimental ultrafast spectroscopy data. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration for laser pulse durations (attosecond to picosecond), intensities (10¹²–10¹⁸ W/cm²), and material configurations beyond current laboratory capabilities. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for tailoring extreme nonlinear optical effects in emerging photonic technologies, with applications to compact laser-driven particle accelerators and terahertz waveguides. This work will advance fundamental understanding of non-perturbative light-matter coupling while providing open-source simulation tools for the optics community, bridging critical gaps between quantum optical theory and engineered systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of light energy, including its structure, properties and behavior under different conditions. Includes instruction in wave theory, wave mechanics, electromagnetic theory, physical optics, geometric optics, quantum theory of light, photon detecting, laser theory, wall and beam properties, chaotic light, non-linear optics, harmonic generation, optical systems theory, and applications to engineering problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and control of industrial-scale electromechanical systems, with a focus on improving energy efficiency and operational reliability in automated manufacturing environments. A key challenge in these systems lies in the dynamic coupling of mechanical, electrical, and control subsystems, which introduces nonlinear behaviors and transient instabilities that are difficult to predict using conventional simulation tools. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale multi-physics simulations that integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for electromechanical component stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management, and real-time digital twin simulations for control algorithm validation. Parallelized solvers will be employed to resolve time-domain interactions between servo motor dynamics, power electronics, and programmable logic controller (PLC) networks under varying load conditions. Machine learning techniques will further enhance optimization workflows by training surrogate models on HPC-generated datasets to identify failure-prone operating regimes and recommend design modifications. The anticipated outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for reducing prototyping costs in electromechanical system development, predictive maintenance strategies for industrial robotics, and improved control logic templates for adaptive manufacturing processes. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing of complex electromechanical interactions, this research will directly support workforce training initiatives in smart manufacturing while advancing scalable solutions for sustainable industrial automation. The requested computing resources are critical to managing the memory-intensive demands of coupled simulations and achieving statistically significant results across diverse operational scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation for multi-threat homeland security scenarios, addressing the challenge of dynamically prioritizing limited personnel, equipment, and funding across competing risks such as cyberattacks, bioterrorism, and critical infrastructure failures. Current risk assessment models often operate in silos, lacking the capacity to simulate cascading threats or interdependencies between physical and digital systems. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform that integrates agent-based modeling, geospatial analytics, and machine learning to simulate threat propagation, resource deployment, and socio-technical system resilience at scale. The computational approach will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate millions of threat permutations, incorporating real-time data streams from federal and municipal databases, IoT sensors, and social media. Custom graph neural networks will model infrastructure interdependencies, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize response strategies under constrained budgets. The project requires access to HPC resources for large-scale distributed memory processing to handle high-resolution spatial datasets (e.g., urban infrastructure networks) and computationally intensive ensemble simulations. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of quantifying trade-offs in preparedness investments, predicting failure cascades across energy grids and transportation systems, and recommending adaptive allocation policies for federal and state agencies. This work directly supports the Department of Homeland Security's risk-informed resource management objectives, with potential applications to FEMA disaster planning and CBP border security operations. By enabling granular, evidence-based scenario analysis, the framework aims to reduce vulnerability gaps identified in the 2024 National Risk Assessment while maintaining compliance with privacy-preserving data governance protocols. Results will be validated against historical incident response metrics and peer-reviewed through collaboration with the DHS Science and Technology Directorate.
cip_definition: A program focusing on security policy, planning and operations dedicated to the protection of U.S. territory, assets, infrastructure, institutions and citizens from external threats. Includes instruction in national security policy, government relations, intelligence, law enforcement, security technology, communications and information technology, homeland security planning and operations, disaster planning and applications to specific threat scenarios.

abstract: Non-profit and public organizations face complex operational challenges due to constrained resources, dynamic stakeholder demands, and the need to balance mission-driven priorities with financial sustainability. This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize decision-making processes in these organizations, with a focus on resource allocation, program impact forecasting, and risk assessment under uncertainty. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-dimensional datasets—including financial records, service delivery metrics, and demographic data—and simulate organizational scenarios at scale. Agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate stakeholder interactions and resource flows, while machine learning techniques will identify patterns in historical data to predict outcomes of strategic choices. A key innovation involves integrating game-theoretic frameworks to model collaborative decision-making among non-profit networks and public-private partnerships. The computational demands arise from processing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (spanning years of operational data from 500+ organizations) and running millions of simulation iterations to account for probabilistic variables in funding cycles, policy changes, and community needs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for non-profit managers that enables real-time scenario analysis, optimized budget allocation strategies, and evidence-based policy recommendations. This work will advance computational social science methodologies while addressing critical gaps in organizational management theory, particularly in understanding how mission-driven entities can maintain operational resilience. By enabling data-intensive modeling of complex non-profit ecosystems, the project aims to enhance the capacity of public service organizations to maximize social impact per dollar spent, ultimately supporting more equitable and sustainable community outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the business affairs of non-profit corporations, including foundations, educational institutions, associations, and other such organizations, and public agencies and governmental operations. Includes instruction in business management, principles of public administration, principles of accounting and financial management, human resources management, taxation of non-profit organizations, and business law as applied to non-profit organizations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize cross-cultural consumer response patterns in global digital marketing campaigns. The core problem lies in the inability of traditional analytical tools to process the high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets generated by multinational marketing efforts, which include multilingual social media interactions, real-time transactional data, and geographically fragmented consumer behavior signals. Current methods struggle to integrate cultural variables—such as localized values, linguistic nuance, and regulatory constraints—with dynamic market feedback at scale, leading to suboptimal campaign adjustments and resource misallocation. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining transformer-based multilingual sentiment analysis, agent-based modeling of cross-cultural decision-making, and hypergraph representations of transnational consumer networks. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets from 25 target markets, training deep learning models to identify latent cultural drivers of purchasing behavior while simulating the cascading effects of marketing interventions across interdependent regions. Key challenges include minimizing latency in real-time A/B testing across time zones and resolving conflicting optimization objectives (e.g., brand consistency versus local customization) through multi-agent reinforcement learning. Expected outcomes include a predictive dashboard for quantifying cultural risk exposure in marketing content, an adaptive resource allocation engine that dynamically redistributes campaign budgets based on simulated cultural friction coefficients, and novel metrics for measuring the transnational virality potential of marketing assets. By enabling granular analysis of how cultural variables modulate marketing ROI at global scale, this work aims to establish computational cross-cultural analytics as a distinct capability within international marketing science, with direct applications in emerging markets where traditional cultural taxonomies fail to capture rapid socio-digital evolution.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing activities in enterprises primarily engaged in exporting or importing goods and services in world markets. Includes instruction in international trade controls, foreign trade operations, locating markets, negotiation practices, monetary issues, and international public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize quality control and safety assurance in complex industrial processes, where traditional statistical methods struggle with high-dimensional, heterogeneous data streams. The research addresses the challenge of integrating real-time sensor data, historical defect records, and environmental variables to predict anomalies and safety risks in dynamic production environments. Current approaches often rely on simplified models or manual inspections, which lack the resolution to detect emerging defects in systems with nonlinear interactions, such as multi-stage manufacturing or automated assembly lines. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid machine learning and simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. A graph neural network architecture will model interdependencies between process variables, trained on terabyte-scale operational datasets to identify precursor signatures of quality deviations. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will test safety-critical failure scenarios under diverse operating conditions, enabling probabilistic risk assessments. The computational workflow requires parallelized training across GPU nodes for model optimization and distributed memory systems for large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of rare events. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive quality prediction and a decision-support tool to prioritize safety interventions based on risk severity. This work will advance the integration of AI-driven analytics with safety engineering principles, providing industries with scalable methods to reduce defect rates and preempt hazards in compliance with evolving regulatory standards. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the project’s data volume, complex model architectures, and need for rapid iteration across simulation parameters—capabilities beyond the scope of local computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Quality Control and Safety Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in quality control and safety technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the design, optimization, and maintenance of modern communications systems, including 5G networks, IoT infrastructure, and hybrid broadband-cellular architectures. As these systems grow in complexity, traditional empirical methods for installation and repair struggle to account for dynamic environmental variables, interference patterns, and multi-scale performance trade-offs. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate real-world deployment scenarios, enabling technicians to proactively identify failure points, optimize signal integrity, and reduce service disruptions. Computational methods will include finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations to model electromagnetic wave propagation in diverse physical environments, machine learning algorithms trained on synthetic and field-collected datasets to predict equipment degradation, and graph-based optimization techniques for routing and bandwidth allocation in heterogeneous networks. These simulations require parallelized processing to handle large-scale parameter spaces, such as terrain data, material properties, and interference sources, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for simulating installation configurations under stress-test conditions, validated against experimental data from partner telecommunications providers. The project aims to advance technician training by integrating computational diagnostics into curricula, bridging theoretical electronics principles with practical repair workflows. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping of communication systems, this work will reduce operational costs, extend hardware lifespans, and improve service reliability in underserved urban and rural areas. HPC resources are essential to achieving the necessary scale, speed, and accuracy for these simulations, directly supporting the program’s mission to innovate technical education and modernize infrastructure maintenance practices.
cip_title: Communications Systems Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair one- and two- way communications equipment and systems, including television cable systems and mobile or stationary communication devices. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of communications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between linguistic narratives in international trade agreements and their measurable economic outcomes, focusing on understudied languages in emerging markets. While economic analyses of trade agreements often overlook the role of linguistic nuance and translation practices, this research posits that variations in treaty language—particularly in multilingual contexts—correlate with discrepancies in implementation efficacy, dispute resolution patterns, and long-term trade balances. Using a novel integration of computational linguistics and econometric modeling, we will analyze a curated corpus of 20,000+ treaty documents across six languages (Arabic, Mandarin, Swahili, Portuguese, Russian, and Bengali), focusing on semantic ambiguities, culturally specific terminology, and translation shifts. High-performance computing resources will enable three core tasks: 1) training multilingual transformer models to detect non-literal translations of economic clauses, 2) running agent-based simulations of treaty negotiation dynamics under varying linguistic constraints, and 3) applying causal inference models to quantify how specific linguistic features predict post-agreement investment flows. The computational pipeline combines natural language processing tools (fine-tuned BERT variants) with Bayesian hierarchical economic models, requiring parallel GPU-CPU architectures for large-scale hyperparameter optimization and Monte Carlo simulations. Expected outcomes include a framework to identify linguistically high-risk clauses in real-time treaty drafting and evidence-based guidelines for equitable translation protocols in multilateral negotiations. By bridging lexical analysis with developmental economics, this work aims to establish language as a measurable variable in trade policy optimization while advancing computational methods for cross-disciplinary humanities–social science research.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in comparative economic systems, econometrics, economic theory, money and banking systems, international economics, international trade, linguistics, philology, and translation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the interplay between urban microclimate dynamics and human behavioral patterns, integrating environmental sensor data, social media activity, and high-resolution satellite imagery. Rapid urbanization has created complex feedback loops between localized weather phenomena (e.g., urban heat islands, particulate dispersion) and population-scale mobility or activity, yet existing models lack the granularity to resolve these interactions at city-block resolution over multi-temporal scales. The research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that couples fluid dynamics simulations with machine learning-driven behavioral prediction. Atmospheric modeling using finite volume methods will generate 3D microclimate profiles, while transformer-based neural networks trained on geotagged social media data and pedestrian mobility traces will predict human activity shifts in response to environmental conditions. These components will be iteratively linked to simulate bidirectional influences, requiring massive parallelization for parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous data streams. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and distributed memory systems for large-scale climate simulations, with middleware enabling real-time data assimilation from municipal IoT networks. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for urban resilience planning, capable of forecasting localized climate-behavior interactions under scenarios such as heatwaves or pollution events. Results will provide actionable insights for city planners and public health officials, bridging gaps between environmental science, computational social science, and urban design. This work establishes a novel methodology for studying emergent human-environment systems, advancing data science applications in spatially embedded socio-ecological research while avoiding disciplinary silos that limit existing approaches.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Securing critical infrastructure and urban environments against evolving threats requires advanced predictive models capable of simulating complex, multi-hazard scenarios. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time risk assessment and mitigation planning, integrating physical security, cyber-physical system vulnerabilities, and fire dynamics. Current approaches often treat these domains in isolation, leading to fragmented resilience strategies. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model interdependencies between human behavior, structural integrity, fire propagation, and cyberattacks under crisis conditions. The computational workflow combines agent-based modeling for crowd dynamics, finite element analysis for structural response, computational fluid dynamics for fire and smoke spread, and network theory for cyber-physical system interdependencies. These modules will be coupled using a message-passing interface (MPI) architecture to enable parallelized, time-dependent simulations of hybrid threat scenarios. The project will validate models against experimental data from fire tests and security breach experiments, requiring iterative parameter optimization via machine learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for evaluating compound threats to transportation hubs and energy grid substations, with specific deliverables including predictive metrics for emergency egress under combined fire and active threat conditions. The HPC resources are critical for achieving sufficient spatial-temporal resolution across interacting physical domains while maintaining computational feasibility for scenario exploration. Results will advance integrated security science by providing decision-support tools that account for cascading failures across infrastructure systems, directly supporting homeland security priorities in critical infrastructure protection. This work will also establish performance benchmarks for next-generation emergency response planning systems requiring tera-scale computational resources.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the critical challenge of predicting and preventing early childhood caries (ECC) progression in pediatric populations through advanced computational modeling of oral microbiome dynamics and enamel demineralization processes. Despite established clinical protocols, ECC remains the most common chronic disease in children globally, with complex, multifactorial etiology involving microbial ecology, host immunology, and behavioral factors. Current diagnostic tools lack predictive precision for individual risk trajectories, particularly in patients with developmental disabilities who exhibit unique oral microbiome profiles. This project will develop a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling of biofilm formation, finite element analysis of enamel stress distribution, and machine learning analysis of longitudinal clinical-metagenomic datasets from a diverse pediatric cohort (n=1,200). High-performance computing resources are essential to simulate 3D tooth surface interactions across micron-scale spatial resolutions while concurrently processing terabyte-scale genomic data from saliva samples. The computational pipeline will parameterize microbial community networks (including *Streptococcus mutans*, *Candida albicans*, and aciduric symbioses) against pH cycling patterns and dietary variables, then validate predictions through parallel in vitro microfluidic tooth models. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a predictive risk stratification algorithm for ECC progression incorporating real-time sensor data from smart dental devices, 2) identification of keystone microbial taxa influencing caries acceleration in neurodiverse patients, and 3) optimized remineralization protocols personalized to salivary biochemistry. By bridging gaps between computational microbiology, materials science, and clinical pedodontics, this work will establish a novel paradigm for precision prevention in pediatric oral health, with particular significance for patients requiring special care dentistry. The resource-intensive simulations (requiring >200,000 core-hours) and integrative data analytics exceed current institutional computing capacities, necessitating access to large-scale GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to optimize welding processes for high-strength, dissimilar material joints, addressing critical challenges in defect formation and mechanical performance. Welding of advanced alloys and hybrid material systems (e.g., steel-aluminum combinations) is increasingly demanded in energy, transportation, and manufacturing sectors, yet process parameter selection remains largely trial-based. Traditional experimental methods are cost-prohibitive and fail to capture the multiphysics interactions governing microstructure evolution and residual stress development. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity modeling approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for thermomechanical process simulation, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for melt pool dynamics, and machine learning (ML) for parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale thermal gradients, solidification kinetics, and phase transformations across macro-scale weldments while accounting for variable joint geometries and material compositions. Parallelized simulations will generate datasets correlating input parameters (e.g., heat input, travel speed, shielding gas composition) with outputs such as porosity distribution, hardness profiles, and fatigue life indicators. A neural network trained on these data will identify Pareto-optimal process windows that simultaneously minimize defects and maximize mechanical properties. Expected outcomes include a validated open-access computational toolkit for welding engineers, reducing iterative prototyping by 40-60% in industrial applications. The work will advance fundamental understanding of process-structure-property relationships in multi-material welding systems, directly supporting curriculum development in robotic welding automation and nondestructive testing within our Welding Engineering Technology program. By enabling rapid virtual process design, this project addresses workforce needs for computationally skilled welding professionals while promoting energy-efficient manufacturing practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the design and engineering of welding and joining systems and the implementation of welding processes. Includes instruction in materials science; computer-aided design; welding design; welding processes; welding metallurgy; automation and robotics; and codes, inspections, testing, and quality assurance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of the Punjabi language and its literary traditions. Despite Punjabi’s status as a major global language with rich dialectal diversity and a centuries-old literary corpus, computational tools for its study remain underdeveloped compared to those for Indo-European peers. The project aims to resolve two interconnected challenges: (1) the lack of large-scale, annotated digital corpora capturing Punjabi’s morphological complexity and dialectal variations, and (2) the absence of robust natural language processing (NLP) models tailored to Punjabi’s unique syntactic and phonetic features. To achieve this, we propose building a multimodal corpus spanning classical texts, modern literature, and spoken dialects, annotated for grammatical, semantic, and sociolinguistic features. Computational workflows will employ transformer-based architectures for dialect classification, neural machine translation for historical text modernization, and phonetic modeling to map sound changes across regional variants. HPC resources are essential for training these models, given the need for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization of deep learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include open-access datasets, dialect-specific NLP pipelines, and interactive visualizations of linguistic shifts across time and geography. These resources will empower scholars to analyze literary evolution, trace sociocultural influences, and preserve endangered dialects. Additionally, the project will advance methodological frameworks for low-resource language computation, with applications in education, language technology development, and cross-disciplinary digital humanities research. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to establish Punjabi studies as a forward-looking field while safeguarding the language’s heritage in an increasingly digitized world.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Punjabi language (Punjabi) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized rehabilitation protocols for individuals with mobility impairments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale biomechanical and clinical datasets. Current rehabilitation practices often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for the complex interplay of biomechanical factors, patient-specific conditions, and therapeutic intervention efficacy. To address this gap, we propose integrating motion capture data, electromyography (EMG) signals, and patient health records into predictive models that simulate rehabilitation outcomes under varying therapeutic parameters. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) preprocessing and harmonizing multimodal datasets using parallelized data pipelines to handle heterogeneous formats and missing data; (2) training machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to predict functional recovery trajectories based on patient characteristics and intervention types; and (3) simulating biomechanical stress patterns via finite element analysis to evaluate the safety and efficacy of proposed interventions for diverse patient anatomies.
