These tasks require HPC resources due to the scale of data (10,000+ patient records, 3D motion datasets), the computational intensity of biomechanical simulations, and the iterative nature of model tuning. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool to assist rehabilitation aides and therapists in designing targeted interventions, reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular code for simulating common rehabilitation scenarios, fostering collaboration across health professions. By bridging computational modeling and clinical rehabilitation, this work aims to advance evidence-based, patient-centered care while providing training opportunities for rehabilitation students in data-driven therapeutic practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other therapeutic professionals, and to perform routine functions in support of rehabilitation. Includes instruction in roles and responsibilities of rehabilitation providers, basic function of the human body, disabling conditions, therapeutic skills, client management, and communication skills.

abstract: Rehabilitation science faces a critical challenge in integrating multi-modal, high-dimensional data to advance personalized therapeutic interventions. Current approaches to analyzing biomechanical, neurophysiological, and patient-reported outcomes often rely on simplified models or fragmented datasets, limiting their capacity to capture the complex interactions between biological, behavioral, and environmental factors that influence recovery. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a unified computational framework for modeling rehabilitation processes. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating patient-specific musculoskeletal simulations to predict functional outcomes of motor rehabilitation strategies in individuals with spinal cord injuries, and (2) employing machine learning to identify patterns in multi-omics, wearable sensor, and clinical assessment data that correlate with optimal assistive technology configurations. Computational workflows will combine finite element modeling of neuromuscular systems with deep learning architectures trained on heterogeneous datasets from existing clinical trials and real-world mobility monitoring. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large-scale simulations, optimization of hyperparameters in neural networks, and integration of real-time sensor data streams. Anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms to guide therapy personalization, quantitative biomarkers for monitoring neuroplasticity, and open-source tools for simulating assistive device interactions with human biomechanics. By bridging gaps between computational modeling and clinical rehabilitation practice, this work has the potential to transform evidence-based care paradigms, reduce trial-and-error in therapeutic decision-making, and inform the development of next-generation rehabilitation technologies. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome current bottlenecks in processing speed and data complexity, facilitating breakthroughs that could improve functional independence for millions living with disabilities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human function, disability, and rehabilitation from the perspectives of the health sciences, social sciences, psychology, engineering, and related fields. Includes instruction in psychological, social, and cultural aspects of disability and rehabilitation; sensory and motor function and dysfunction; biomechanics and kinesiology; assistive technology; rehabilitation instrumentation and methodology; statistics; and health and rehabilitation policy.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic pricing strategies in omnichannel retail environments, where traditional heuristic models fail to adapt to real-time fluctuations in consumer demand, supply chain disruptions, and competitive pricing signals. Current approaches often rely on simplified assumptions about buyer behavior or static market segmentation, leading to suboptimal profit margins and inventory mismatches across sales channels. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework capable of simulating heterogeneous consumer decision-making processes while simultaneously optimizing pricing, promotion, and inventory allocation decisions across digital and physical distribution networks. The computational complexity arises from modeling high-dimensional, interdependent variables—including geospatial demand patterns, social media sentiment trends, and supplier lead time variability—at a granular temporal resolution. High-performance computing resources are critical for training deep neural networks on historical transaction datasets (spanning 10M+ SKU-channel combinations) and conducting parallelized simulations of alternative pricing policies under stochastic market conditions. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision support tool that identifies context-specific trade-offs between revenue maximization and customer retention metrics, validated through retrospective analysis of seasonal sales cycles. The project bridges computational economics and operations research, offering novel insights into the resilience of adaptive pricing systems during demand shocks. Results will be disseminated through open-source algorithmic libraries designed for mid-market retailers lacking in-house AI infrastructure, potentially reducing computational costs for real-time pricing deployments by 40-60% compared to commercial cloud-based solutions.
cip_title: Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Operations, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general process and techniques of direct wholesale and retail buying and selling operations and introduces individuals to related careers. Includes instruction in the principles of entrepreneurial economics, basic sales skills, the distribution channels for goods and services, and supervised practical application experiences.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug development and the growing demand for personalized pharmacotherapy necessitate advanced computational tools to model drug interactions, optimize formulations, and predict patient-specific responses. Traditional experimental approaches in pre-pharmacy research are often limited by cost, time, and scalability, particularly when analyzing large datasets or simulating molecular dynamics at biologically relevant scales. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and kinetic behavior of small-molecule drugs interacting with target proteins and lipid-based drug delivery systems. The primary focus will be on elucidating mechanisms of drug-receptor binding, stability of drug-carrier complexes, and variability in drug metabolism linked to genetic polymorphisms. Computational methods will include molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using AMBER and GROMACS to model atomic-level interactions over microsecond timescales, machine learning (ML)-driven quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models to predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) profiles, and high-throughput virtual screening of compound libraries against protein targets implicated in chronic diseases. These workflows require parallelized computing architectures to manage terabytes of trajectory data, iterative ML training on heterogeneous biological datasets, and ensemble docking simulations across thousands of ligand conformations. Expected outcomes include identifying novel drug candidates with enhanced specificity for understudied targets, optimizing nano-carrier formulations for improved bioavailability, and developing predictive models for genotype-dependent drug responses. The results will advance foundational knowledge in pharmaceutical sciences while providing pre-pharmacy students with hands-on experience in computational research methodologies, bridging gaps between theoretical coursework and emerging data-driven practices in modern pharmacy. By integrating HPC-based approaches into pre-pharmacy training, this project aims to cultivate a workforce adept at addressing complex healthcare challenges through interdisciplinary innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of phase transitions and microstructural evolution in advanced ceramic composites under extreme thermal and mechanical loads, with applications in high-temperature industrial systems and wear-resistant components. A critical challenge in ceramic engineering lies in predicting crack propagation and stress distribution in multiphase systems during sintering and operational use, where experimental characterization is limited by material opacity and rapid failure mechanisms. We propose a multiscale computational framework combining density functional theory (DFT) calculations of interfacial bonding energetics with finite element analysis (FEA) of bulk thermo-mechanical properties. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of grain boundary dynamics in alumina-zirconia composites, coupled with phase-field modeling of microcrack nucleation under cyclic thermal stress. The simulations will integrate experimental XRD and SEM data from collaborative laboratory work to validate interfacial adhesion parameters and fracture toughness predictions. Expected outcomes include a predictive model for optimizing sintering protocols to minimize residual porosity while maximizing fracture resistance in gradient-structured ceramics. This work directly addresses the materials-by-design gap in ceramic engineering by establishing computational workflows to accelerate the development of next-generation ceramic superconductors and ultra-high-temperature structural components. The requested GPU-accelerated computing resources are essential for handling the 10^6-atom systems and mesoscale microstructure domains required to capture realistic material behavior, significantly reducing development cycles for industrial ceramics through virtual prototyping. Results will be disseminated through open-source code repositories and partnerships with national laboratories working on ceramic matrix composites for energy applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of inorganic non-metallic materials, such as porcelains, cements, industrial ceramics, ceramic superconductors, abrasive, and related materials and systems.

abstract: Orthopedic immobilization devices, such as casts and splints, are critical for fracture recovery but face persistent challenges in balancing structural stability with patient comfort and tissue health. Traditional design protocols rely on generalized anatomical templates and static material properties, which fail to account for dynamic physiological changes during healing, including edema resolution, muscle atrophy, and metabolic variations. This project proposes a computational framework to optimize personalized orthopedic immobilization strategies by integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling, real-time sensor data assimilation, and adaptive material response simulations. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that dynamically adjust device configurations to maintain optimal interfacial pressure, thermal regulation, and load distribution throughout the healing process. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable finite element analysis of multi-layered composite materials under complex physiological conditions, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets (clinical imaging, wearable sensor outputs, and histocompatibility metrics). Computational workflows will simulate time-dependent interactions between device mechanics and biological systems at cellular, tissue, and structural scales, incorporating stochastic variations in patient mobility and inflammatory responses. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for virtual prototyping of adaptive orthopedic devices and evidence-based guidelines for material selection in comorbid populations (e.g., diabetic patients with impaired wound healing). By establishing quantitative relationships between device microarchitecture and clinical outcomes, this work aims to reduce complications such as pressure ulcers and joint stiffness while advancing computational orthotics as a distinct interdisciplinary domain within health sciences. The requested HPC allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated multiphysics simulations and large-scale parameter optimization requiring parallel processing of 10^4+ biomechanical scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to cast, splint, and brace orthopedic injuries. Includes instruction in patient assessment; casting, splinting, and orthopedic appliances; radiographic interpretation; traction; and wound care.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex ocular conditions, such as keratoconus and post-surgical corneal ectasia, necessitates advanced computational models to optimize treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes. Current clinical tools for simulating corneal biomechanics and optical performance rely on simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to predict individualized responses to interventions like specialty contact lenses or corneal cross-linking. This project proposes the development of high-resolution, patient-specific finite element models (FEMs) of the human cornea integrated with optical ray-tracing simulations. These models will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal clinical data—including corneal topography, optical coherence tomography, and intraocular pressure measurements—into 3D meshes with sub-micron spatial resolution. Computational workflows will simulate mechanical stress distributions under various loading conditions (e.g., contact lens wear) while simultaneously evaluating visual acuity impacts through dynamic light propagation algorithms. Machine learning techniques will be employed to accelerate parameter optimization and identify biomechanical risk factors for disease progression. The HPC environment is critical for handling the ∼10^6 degree-of-freedom FEMs, parallelized Monte Carlo ray-tracing routines, and large-scale parameter space exploration required for clinical relevance. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform for optometrists to virtually test intervention strategies, reducing trial-and-error fitting processes for complex cases. The resource will also enable novel insights into structure-function relationships in corneal pathologies, with potential applications in personalized myopia control and surgical planning. By bridging computational engineering with clinical optometry, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift in evidence-based, data-driven ocular therapeutics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of optometry and that focuses on the principles and techniques for examining, diagnosing and treating conditions of the visual system. Includes instruction in prescribing glasses and contact lenses, other optical aids, corrective therapies, patient counseling, physician referral, practice management, and ethics and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the emerging field of computational gastronomy, specifically targeting the optimization of plant-based and alternative protein food products. The culinary science challenge lies in replicating the texture, flavor, and structural integrity of traditional animal-derived foods using sustainable ingredients—a complex task requiring the integration of molecular-level food science, rheological modeling, and data-driven culinary design. Current industry approaches rely heavily on iterative physical experiments, which are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in their ability to predict multi-scale interactions between novel ingredients. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of protein-polysaccharide interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for texture prediction under mechanical stress, and machine learning (ML) models trained on sensory evaluation datasets from chef-led panels. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parallelization of MD simulations to map binding affinities between plant proteins and functional additives, while FEA workflows will model viscoelastic behaviors across varying processing conditions (e.g., extrusion temperatures, shear rates). Concurrently, ML algorithms will correlate computational outputs with human sensory perceptions of "mouthfeel" and "bite," creating predictive tools for designing formulations that balance physicochemical stability with culinary acceptability. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for rapid prototyping of alternative protein matrices, significantly reducing development cycles for sustainable food products. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between food chemistry, soft matter physics, and culinary arts, establishing a novel computational paradigm for the culinology field. The research aligns with global sustainability goals while addressing industry demands for scalable methods to engineer plant-based foods that meet both technical and sensory benchmarks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the blending of food science and the culinary arts and that prepares individuals to work as research chefs and related research and development positions in the food industry. Includes instruction in culinary arts, food chemistry, food safety and quality, food processing, nutrition, and business management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling of infectious disease transmission dynamics in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), with a focus on malaria and arboviral diseases. Despite progress in disease control, heterogeneous environmental, sociodemographic, and behavioral factors complicate intervention planning in resource-limited settings. Current models often oversimplify spatial-temporal interactions between climate variability, vector ecology, and human mobility, limiting their utility for real-world policy decisions. To address this, we propose an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), Bayesian inference, and machine learning to simulate disease spread at high resolution across diverse LMIC contexts. The ABM will incorporate geospatial data (e.g., satellite-derived land use, precipitation), anonymized mobile phone mobility traces, and longitudinal health surveillance data to capture multiscale transmission drivers. Bayesian methods will quantify uncertainty in parameter estimation, while recurrent neural networks will forecast outbreak trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. The scale of analysis—spanning 10-50 million agent interactions across multi-year simulations—necessitates parallelized computing for parameter calibration, sensitivity analyses, and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include identification of high-risk transmission corridors, optimization of targeted vector control strategies, and open-source tools for evaluating the cost-effectiveness of interventions under climate change. By elucidating context-specific pathways of disease spread, this work will directly inform national health agencies and global partners in prioritizing limited resources. The requested HPC allocation will enable computationally intensive analyses that are infeasible with standard infrastructure, thereby advancing methodological innovation in computational epidemiology and strengthening evidence-based decision-making for infectious disease mitigation in LMICs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized learning pathways in adaptive educational technologies, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the scalability and real-time responsiveness challenges inherent in dynamic, multimodal learning environments. While adaptive learning systems increasingly integrate artificial intelligence (AI) to tailor content delivery, existing approaches often rely on simplified models of learner behavior, neglecting the interplay between cognitive load, affective states, and environmental factors. This research addresses the critical gap in modeling these complex, interdependent variables at scale, particularly for learners with neurodiverse profiles or in resource-constrained settings. The project will utilize heterogeneous datasets, including eye-tracking metrics, physiological signals (e.g., heart rate variability), and interaction logs from digital learning platforms, to train multimodal deep learning architectures. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of temporal data streams, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and simulations of population-level learning outcomes under varying intervention strategies. Key computational challenges include real-time fusion of sparse, noisy multimodal data and the development of reinforcement learning agents capable of operating within ethical constraints for educational decision-making. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive system design, validated against randomized controlled trials in K-12 mathematics classrooms, and a novel benchmarking dataset for evaluating computational models of situated learning. By advancing the computational fidelity of learner-state representations, this work aims to establish new standards for ethically grounded, evidence-driven adaptive technologies while providing scalable methods for resource-efficient personalization—a critical need as education systems worldwide confront growing demands for inclusivity and accessibility.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate scalable computational models of protein interaction networks underlying complex diseases. Current approaches to understanding these networks are limited by the computational intensity of simulating dynamic protein behaviors across large datasets and the inability to integrate multi-omic data efficiently. The proposed research addresses these gaps by combining graph-theoretic algorithms, parallelized molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning to predict interaction patterns and identify critical regulatory nodes. Key computational challenges include managing terabytes of proteomic and transcriptomic data from public repositories (e.g., AlphaFold DB, TCGA), optimizing memory usage for network inference, and scaling ensemble simulations to capture stochastic variability. The HPC infrastructure will enable (1) rapid parameter sweeps for refining coarse-grained protein models, (2) distributed training of graph neural networks on heterogeneous biological data, and (3) real-time analysis of simulation trajectories to detect rare conformational states. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of predicted disease-associated interaction hubs, validated against experimental datasets from collaborators, and open-source tools for probabilistic network alignment. This work will advance computational methodologies for systems-level biology by providing frameworks to prioritize therapeutic targets in understudied diseases, such as fibrotic disorders, where traditional molecular biology approaches have struggled to disentangle multifactorial mechanisms. The requested resources will directly support 12 months of intensive computations, with scalability analyses ensuring broader utility for the computational biology community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computational theoretical approaches to understanding biological systems, including computational models of biological processes, computational management of large-scale projects, database development and data-algorithm development, and high-performance computing, as well as statistical and mathematical analyses.

abstract: Global agricultural systems face increasing pressure to adapt to climate variability, population growth, and shifting socio-economic demands. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize crop selection and management strategies across diverse agroecological zones, with a focus on enhancing food security in low-resource regions. The research integrates high-resolution climate projections, soil health data, and genomic information from staple crops (e.g., maize, sorghum) to simulate yield outcomes under multiple scenarios of environmental stress and intervention. A central computational challenge involves processing petabyte-scale datasets spanning 40 years of global agricultural records, satellite-derived vegetation indices, and continent-scale soil microbiome profiles. We propose using ensemble machine learning models coupled with agent-based simulations to capture interactions between biophysical constraints, farmer decision-making, and market dynamics. High-performance computing resources are essential to run spatially explicit simulations at 1 km² resolution across 15 target countries, enabling comparative analysis of irrigation practices, drought-tolerant crop varieties, and nutrient management policies. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated training of neural networks for phenotype prediction and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in climate-agriculture feedback loops. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access decision support tool for regional policymakers to prioritize climate-resilient agricultural investments, (2) identification of genomic markers associated with yield stability in marginal environments, and (3) quantitative assessments of how emerging technologies like precision agriculture could reduce yield gaps in smallholder systems. By bridging gaps between crop science, climate modeling, and socio-economic analysis, this work aims to establish a scalable computational platform for evaluating sustainable intensification strategies across heterogenous agricultural landscapes.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of agricultural management and scientific principles to the problems of global food production and distribution, and to the study of the agricultural systems of other countries. Includes instruction in agricultural economics; comparative agricultural systems; international agribusiness and law; third-world development studies and economic development; and global applications of climate, soil, water resources, ecological and environmental studies, and animal and plant sciences.

abstract: Healthcare systems face mounting pressure to improve outcomes, reduce costs, and adapt to rapidly evolving technologies, yet innovation is often hindered by the complexity of integrating multi-scale data and modeling dynamic organizational interactions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating healthcare delivery networks and optimizing intervention strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, real-time models that synthesize electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, resource utilization metrics, and socio-behavioral factors to guide evidence-based decision-making. Current approaches struggle to address the non-linear relationships and feedback loops inherent in healthcare systems, particularly when analyzing large, heterogeneous datasets. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and network analysis. Agent-based simulations will represent patient populations, care teams, and medical devices, while deep learning architectures will process temporal EHR data to predict care pathway outcomes. Graph-based network models will map resource dependencies and workflow bottlenecks across departments. These components will be integrated into a unified HPC-powered platform to evaluate hypothetical scenarios, such as the impact of novel medical device integration or staffing policy changes. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, distributed training of neural networks, and real-time simulation of millions of agent interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying high-risk patient cohorts, optimized resource allocation templates for emergency departments, and a validated framework for assessing the systemic impacts of healthcare innovations. This work will provide healthcare leaders with actionable tools to simulate organizational changes before implementation, potentially reducing trial-and-error costs while accelerating the adoption of effective interventions. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sensitivity analyses at unprecedented scales, ensuring robust, generalizable solutions for diverse healthcare settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to innovate solutions and lead change within a healthcare organization. Includes instruction in innovation management, medical device development, evidence-based practice, systems thinking, information technology, healthcare policy and finance, organizational change, and leadership.

abstract: The genetic basis of many rare developmental disorders remains unexplained, particularly for cases linked to non-coding genomic regions. Traditional sequencing approaches often focus on exonic variants, leaving regulatory and structural elements underexplored. This project seeks to identify pathogenic non-coding variants associated with congenital neurogenetic disorders using whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 5,000 trios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform genome-wide association analyses integrating chromatin conformation data, epigenetic annotations, and machine learning-based variant prioritization. Computational challenges include processing >1 petabyte of raw sequencing data, running complex haplotype phasing algorithms, and training deep neural networks to predict variant pathogenicity across 3D genomic contexts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel execution of these tasks, reducing analysis time from months to weeks. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel regulatory variants impacting neurodevelopmental genes, characterization of their mechanistic roles in gene dysregulation, and validation through CRISPR screening in cellular models. This work will advance understanding of non-coding contributions to genetic diseases, directly informing clinical diagnostic pipelines and therapeutic target development. By resolving previously undiagnosed cases, the project aligns with precision medicine initiatives while demonstrating scalable computational frameworks for analyzing non-coding variation at population scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of human genetics from the standpoint of medical applications such as clinical diagnosis, genetic engineering and therapy, transplantation, and the study of genetic diseases and disabilities and their defense. Includes instruction in human molecular genetics; genetic factors causing disease; changes in gene expression during development, differentiation, and pathogenesis; recombinant DNA; gene therapy; clinical genetics; genetic epidemiology; immunogenetics; cytogenetics; and genetics of specific disorders and diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model dynamic household financial decision-making under economic uncertainty, with a focus on identifying patterns of resilience and vulnerability across diverse demographic groups. The research addresses a critical gap in family and consumer economics: traditional static models inadequately capture the interdependencies between real-time market fluctuations, behavioral biases, and heterogeneous household priorities (e.g., intergenerational caregiving, education savings, or debt management). By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to implement a large-scale agent-based model that simulates decision pathways across 100,000+ synthetic households parameterized using merged microdata from financial surveys, census records, and behavioral experiments. The model will integrate machine learning classifiers to predict tipping points at which households transition between stable and unstable financial states when exposed to simulated economic shocks, such as inflationary periods or abrupt policy changes. Computational challenges include optimizing parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing and training neural networks on imbalanced temporal datasets representing rare but consequential financial events (e.g., medical bankruptcies). Outcomes will yield a publicly accessible toolkit for policymakers to evaluate how localized economic interventions might differentially affect households based on asset portfolios, cultural norms around resource sharing, and access to financial literacy resources. This work bridges computational social science with consumer economics, offering novel methodologies to analyze complex, adaptive decision-making processes that defy reduction to conventional economic assumptions.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Economics and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer economics and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of personalized biomechanical models with adaptive biosystem dynamics remains a critical challenge in developing advanced prosthetics and implantable medical devices. Current approaches often rely on static anatomical datasets or generalized material properties, leading to suboptimal device fit, accelerated wear, and limited long-term biocompatibility. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multiscale, patient-specific simulations that dynamically couple musculoskeletal mechanics, tissue remodeling, and device-tissue interfacial behaviors. The research will utilize clinical imaging data, biomechanical sensor inputs, and longitudinal biological response datasets to parameterize finite element models of lower-limb prosthetic interfaces and cardiac implant surfaces. These models will integrate computational fluid dynamics for nutrient transport in peri-device tissues, agent-based simulations of inflammatory cell recruitment, and machine learning-driven optimization of device geometry and material stiffness gradients. By deploying these computationally intensive workflows on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve near-real-time predictive modeling of device performance across diverse patient populations while accounting for temporal changes in tissue physiology. The expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for optimizing patient-device biomechanical compatibility, (2) open-source simulation tools for prosthetic design iteration, and (3) quantitative biomarkers linking computational parameters to clinical outcomes such as osseointegration rates and chronic inflammation risk. This work directly aligns with national priorities in precision bioengineering by establishing a computational pipeline to accelerate the translation of adaptive biomedical devices from bench to bedside, ultimately reducing revision surgeries and improving quality of life for patients with limb loss or organ failure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: The development of efficient quantum-enhanced nanoscale energy systems presents a critical challenge at the intersection of applied physics and engineering, where traditional thermodynamic frameworks fail to capture the interplay of quantum coherence, nonequilibrium dynamics, and nanoscale heat transport. This project addresses the computational bottleneck in modeling energy transduction processes within hybrid quantum-classical systems, particularly focusing on optically active nanostructures coupled to superconducting resonators. Current analytical methods cannot resolve the timescales required to optimize energy transfer efficiency while accounting for quantum fluctuations and decoherence effects across multiple physical domains. The proposed research employs large-scale numerical simulations combining time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for electron-photon interactions, stochastic Lindblad master equations for open quantum system dynamics, and finite-element modeling of thermal gradients in superconducting substrates. These coupled simulations will be implemented on high-performance computing clusters using a hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization scheme to handle the exponential scaling of quantum state spaces with system size. Key objectives include identifying geometric and material parameters that maximize coherent energy transfer under cryogenic conditions and developing machine learning surrogates to accelerate device optimization. The computational demands arise from the need to simulate 10^4–10^5 interacting quantum states across picosecond-to-nanosecond trajectories while maintaining nanoscale spatial resolution. Successful implementation will yield validated design principles for quantum-enhanced energy harvesting systems, with potential applications in photonic computing and ultra-low-power sensor networks. This work establishes a computational framework to bridge quantum thermodynamics with practical nanodevice engineering, addressing a critical gap in the scalable implementation of quantum-coherent energy technologies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the use of physics principles in the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems and other scientific applications. Includes instruction in high- and low-temperature phenomena, computational physics, superconductivity, applied thermodynamics, molecular and particle physics applications, and space science research.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution and sociocultural impact of medieval ecclesiastical legal texts through computational textual and network analysis. While canon law studies traditionally rely on close reading and qualitative methods, the scale and complexity of surviving manuscripts—spanning centuries, jurisdictions, and languages—present challenges for identifying macro-level patterns in legal development, cross-jurisdictional influences, and the relationship between doctrinal shifts and historical events. The research addresses this gap by applying natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based network modeling to a curated corpus of digitized canon law texts (e.g., Decretum Gratiani, papal decretals) and parallel secular legal documents from 1100–1500 CE. Computational methods will detect semantic shifts in key juridical concepts, map citation networks between legal authorities, and correlate doctrinal changes with geopolitical developments using spatiotemporal metadata. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual Latin and vernacular texts, training custom transformer models for ancient legal language, and simulating the diffusion of legal norms across diocesan boundaries. Expected outcomes include a quantitative framework for periodizing canon law’s doctrinal development, identification of understudied textual influences on early modern legal systems, and an open-access digital archive of annotated texts with interactive visualization tools. By integrating computational humanities approaches with canonical jurisprudence, this project aims to redefine scholarly understanding of how religious law shaped premodern societal structures while establishing scalable methodologies for analyzing legal corpora across disciplines.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, theology, and philosophy of religious, church, and ecclesiastical law and that prepares individuals to serve as professional canonists.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern IoT-driven disaster response networks demands resilient, low-latency communication frameworks capable of operating in dynamically degraded environments. Traditional network resource allocation strategies, optimized for stable conditions, struggle to adapt to the abrupt topology changes, intermittent connectivity, and heterogeneous data flows characteristic of emergency scenarios. This project proposes the development of a bio-inspired, adaptive resource orchestration system for edge computing nodes in disaster-area networks, leveraging decentralized decision-making algorithms modeled after collective insect swarm behaviors. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale disaster environments with up to 50,000 nodes, incorporating real-world datasets on terrain, weather, and infrastructure damage patterns. Agent-based modeling will test emergent coordination between edge devices under bandwidth constraints, while Monte Carlo methods will evaluate fault tolerance across stochastic failure regimes. Key innovations include a pheromone-inspired metadata propagation system for rapid state synchronization and a dynamic priority queuing mechanism that weights data criticality against energy budgets. Computational outcomes will inform the design of lightweight middleware for field deployment in humanitarian aid networks, with performance benchmarks targeting 40% improvements in packet delivery ratios during connectivity blackouts compared to existing delay-tolerant networking protocols. By bridging swarm intelligence principles with telecommunications infrastructure, this work aims to establish new paradigms for self-organizing emergency networks while advancing computational methodologies for modeling decentralized systems at scale. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration across variable disaster typologies, providing foundational insights into resilience-computability tradeoffs in ad hoc edge environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of linked systems of computers, peripherals, and associated software to maximize efficiency and productivity, and that prepares individuals to function as network specialists and managers at various levels. Includes instruction in operating systems and applications; systems design and analysis; networking theory and solutions; types of networks; network management and control; network and flow optimization; security; configuring; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework for optimizing industrial production systems under dynamic constraints, with a focus on enhancing operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and environmental sustainability. Industrial management faces persistent challenges in balancing competing objectives such as minimizing energy consumption, reducing waste, maintaining product quality, and meeting fluctuating demand. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these factors, particularly in large-scale, multi-stage production environments. To address this gap, the research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining discrete-event simulation, multi-objective optimization, and machine learning. The computational model will simulate complex manufacturing workflows, incorporating real-world variables such as equipment failure rates, workforce scheduling, and supply chain disruptions. Parallelized genetic algorithms and deep reinforcement learning techniques will be employed to identify Pareto-optimal solutions for resource allocation, while stochastic optimization methods will address uncertainties in demand and material availability. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these computations to realistic industrial scenarios, enabling the analysis of millions of potential operational configurations across distributed manufacturing nodes. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive production schedules, predictive maintenance plans, and sustainability-oriented resource utilization strategies. This work will contribute novel methodologies to industrial operations research, with potential applications in automotive, aerospace, and consumer goods manufacturing sectors. By quantifying trade-offs between economic and environmental performance metrics, the project aims to advance the integration of circular economy principles into industrial management practices. The requested computing resources will support large-scale dataset processing, computationally intensive Monte Carlo simulations, and the training of neural networks for real-time anomaly detection in production systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of engineering principles to the planning and operational management of industrial and manufacturing operations, and prepares individuals to plan and manage such operations. Includes instruction in accounting, engineering economy, financial management, industrial and human resources management, industrial psychology, management information systems, mathematical modeling and optimization, quality control, operations research, safety and health issues, and environmental program management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution and diffusion of esoteric religious narratives across premodern Afro-Eurasian societies through computational textual and network analysis. While historical scholarship has identified syncretic patterns in mystical traditions—such as the blending of Neoplatonic, Gnostic, and Sufi thought—systematic analysis of these phenomena remains constrained by the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources. Our interdisciplinary team proposes to develop machine learning pipelines to analyze a multilingual corpus of digitized religious texts (Arabic, Greek, Syriac, and Persian) spanning 200 BCE to 1200 CE, complemented by non-textual data on trade routes and pilgrimage sites. Using transformer-based models fine-tuned for ancient languages, we will automate the detection of conceptual parallels, metaphorical structures, and terminological borrowings across traditions. Graph neural networks will then model the probable pathways of ideological transmission through reconstructed cultural contact networks. High-performance computing resources are essential for training cross-lingual embeddings on our 15TB corpus, running large-scale semantic similarity analyses, and simulating transmission dynamics across spatial-temporal networks with >10^6 nodes. Expected outcomes include 1) a quantitative framework for evaluating hypotheses about religious syncretism, 2) interactive visualizations of doctrinal diffusion patterns, and 3) an open-source toolkit for computational religious studies. This work challenges Eurocentric periodizations of religious history by computationally tracing multidirectional exchanges between Mediterranean, Mesopotamian, and South Asian traditions. The resource request supports both model training and the development of a web platform to make analytical tools accessible to humanities researchers without prior computational training.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religion/religious studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop and estimate high-dimensional econometric models to analyze the dynamic interdependencies between macroeconomic variables, financial markets, and policy shocks in a global context. Traditional econometric methods face computational limitations when scaling to systems with hundreds of interdependent time series, particularly when incorporating latent factors, structural breaks, and nonlinearities inherent to modern economic systems. The research problem centers on overcoming these barriers through advanced computational strategies, enabling robust analysis of complex economic networks and their stability under various shock scenarios. The project will employ Bayesian vector autoregressive (BVAR) frameworks with hierarchical priors, combined with stochastic volatility models and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling techniques adapted for distributed computing architectures. These methods require iterative estimation of high-dimensional parameter spaces and repeated simulation of counterfactual scenarios, necessitating parallelized computation and large-scale memory management. The requested high-performance computing resources will support 1) the calibration of models using historical datasets spanning national accounts, asset prices, and central bank policies across 50+ economies; 2) real-time nowcasting experiments integrating unstructured data sources; and 3) stress-testing exercises evaluating systemic risk propagation. Expected outcomes include new computational workflows for economic forecasting under parameter uncertainty, open-source tools for massive-scale econometric estimation, and empirically grounded insights into the resilience characteristics of interconnected economic systems. By enabling analysis at previously impractical scales, this work aims to advance quantitative economics through methodological innovation while providing policymakers with enhanced frameworks for evaluating macroeconomic stability. The resource-intensive nature of these computations—particularly the need for multi-node GPU acceleration and petabyte-scale data handling—makes high-performance computing infrastructure essential to achieving these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of mathematical and statistical analysis of economic phenomena and problems. Includes instruction in economic statistics, optimization theory, cost/benefit analysis, price theory, economic modeling, and economic forecasting and evaluation.

abstract: Clinical pathology laboratories generate vast multidimensional datasets through advanced diagnostic modalities, yet integrating these data to improve disease classification and predictive modeling remains computationally challenging. This project proposes developing a machine learning framework to harmonize clinical chemistry, genomic, proteomic, and digital pathology data for enhanced diagnosis of complex autoimmune disorders and hematologic malignancies. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabyte-scale datasets from mass spectrometry, next-generation sequencing, and whole-slide imaging systems. Computational workflows will employ federated learning architectures to maintain data privacy across collaborating institutions while training neural networks on distributed GPU clusters. Key methods include variational autoencoders for dimensionality reduction of heterogeneous biomarkers, graph-based models to map molecular interactions in immune dysregulation, and explainable AI techniques to validate clinically actionable patterns. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these analyses across 10,000+ patient cases and enabling real-time inference compatible with diagnostic laboratory workflows. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated multimodal classifier for early detection of treatment-resistant autoimmune profiles, (2) dynamic risk stratification models for myelodysplastic syndromes integrating cytogenetic and flow cytometry data, and (3) an open-source pipeline for clinical laboratories to implement adaptive machine learning in test interpretation. This work addresses critical gaps in precision diagnostics by enabling robust integration of cross-disciplinary laboratory data while establishing computational infrastructure for rapid validation of emerging biomarkers. Successful implementation could reduce diagnostic delays by 30-40% in target conditions and provide a template for AI-driven analytics in clinical pathology practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease. Includes instruction in performing clinical chemistry, cytogenetics, immunology, laboratory management, microbiology, molecular biology, quality control, serology, toxicology, and virology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, spatially correlated data with complex dependence structures, a common challenge in environmental monitoring, epidemiological studies, and climate science. Traditional statistical models for spatial and spatiotemporal data struggle with computational feasibility when applied to massive datasets, particularly when incorporating non-Gaussian response variables or accounting for measurement error. To address this, we propose a novel Bayesian hierarchical framework that combines low-rank approximations, sparse matrix techniques, and adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms optimized for distributed-memory high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The computational core of this work involves implementing parallelized gradient-based sampling methods for latent Gaussian processes, coupled with dynamic load-balancing strategies to manage irregular computational workloads arising from spatially heterogeneous observation densities. A key innovation is the integration of dimension-adaptive stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) discretizations, which automatically refine spatial resolution in regions of high predictive uncertainty. The project will validate methods using synthetic data and apply them to a national-scale analysis of air pollution health effects, leveraging multi-terabyte exposure and health outcome datasets with fine spatial-temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for large-scale spatial statistics, theoretical advances in scalable uncertainty quantification, and policy-relevant insights into environmental health risks. The requested HPC resources are critical for testing algorithmic scalability, conducting simulation studies to assess frequentist properties of Bayesian estimators, and processing real-world datasets that exceed the memory and compute capabilities of standard workstations. By bridging modern statistical theory with HPC-driven implementation, this work aims to expand the frontiers of data-intensive spatial statistics while maintaining rigorous probabilistic foundations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mathematics and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric urology faces significant challenges in managing congenital and acquired genitourinary tract anomalies, where anatomical variability and dynamic growth complicate treatment optimization. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, often lacking patient-specific predictive tools to anticipate surgical outcomes or long-term functional risks. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework integrating patient-specific anatomical modeling, biomechanical simulations, and machine learning to predict postoperative outcomes in complex pediatric urologic conditions, such as bladder exstrophy and obstructive uropathies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the multi-scale, multi-modal datasets involved, including high-resolution imaging, urodynamic studies, and longitudinal clinical records. Anatomical models derived from MRI/CT scans will undergo finite element analysis to simulate tissue mechanics and urinary flow dynamics under surgical correction scenarios. Concurrently, machine learning models will analyze clinical datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of complications, such as renal dysfunction or incontinence. The integration of these approaches requires large-scale parallel processing for iterative simulation refinements and training of predictive algorithms on heterogeneous data. By leveraging HPC, this project aims to establish a platform for virtual surgical planning and risk stratification, enabling personalized intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for postoperative bladder compliance, urinary flow rates, and renal functional preservation, which will be tested against retrospective clinical data and prospectively validated in a pilot cohort. This work has the potential to transform clinical practice by reducing revision surgeries, optimizing resource allocation, and improving quality of life for pediatric patients. The computational pipelines developed will also be shared as open-source tools to advance collaborative research in pediatric urology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals in the study, prevention, and management of congenital, childhood-acquired, and overlapping adolescent anomalies of the genitourinary tract, including problems, diseases, tumors, and traumas.

abstract: Livestock breeding programs face increasing complexity in integrating multi-omics data to optimize genetic selection while balancing productivity, health, and sustainability goals. Current genomic prediction models struggle to efficiently process large-scale datasets encompassing genotypes, phenotypes, metabolomics, and environmental variables, particularly for traits with non-additive genetic architectures. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy advanced machine learning frameworks for predictive modeling of complex traits in cattle. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture gene interaction networks and transformer-based architectures to model temporal patterns in longitudinal production data. The workflow will integrate existing genomic databases from 50,000 Holstein cattle with new hyperspectral imaging data quantifying meat and milk quality traits. Computational experiments will benchmark model performance against traditional genomic selection methods, with validation through CRISPR-edited cell lines. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training across thousands of genomic loci, reducing runtime for genome-wide association analyses from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include optimized neural architecture configurations for polygenic trait prediction and open-source tools for efficient parameter tuning in agricultural genomics. Successful implementation will advance precision breeding strategies to enhance disease resistance and nutrient utilization efficiency in livestock, directly supporting sustainable animal protein production. By establishing scalable pipelines for multi-omics data integration, this work will provide a template for computational genomics applications across agricultural sciences, bridging the gap between high-throughput biological data and practical breeding decisions. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for genome assembly tasks, and secure storage for sensitive agricultural data.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding and husbandry of agricultural animals, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural animal products. Includes instruction in the animal sciences, animal husbandry and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of microbial biofilm communities in extreme engineered environments, integrating principles from microbiology, materials science, and fluid dynamics to address a critical gap in predictive modeling of biofilm resilience. Biofilms in industrial systems (e.g., water treatment membranes, geothermal energy pipelines) exhibit complex interactions with abiotic surfaces and fluctuating physicochemical conditions, yet current models fail to capture their adaptive behaviors at multiple scales. The research problem centers on understanding how microscale biofilm-material interactions propagate to macroscale system fouling and failure, particularly under thermal and chemical stressors. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of extracellular polymeric substance (EPS)-surface adhesion, lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) fluid-structure interactions, and agent-based modeling (ABM) of microbial metabolic cooperation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve time- and space-dependent processes across 12 orders of magnitude, from nanometer-scale polymer conformations to meter-scale flow dynamics. GPU-accelerated MD will parameterize EPS binding energies on titanium dioxide and graphene-based surfaces, while hybrid OpenMP-MPI parallelization will enable 3D LBM-ABM coupling for systems spanning 10^6 microbial agents. Expected outcomes include the first predictive model linking surface chemistry modifications to biofilm lifecycle regulation under extreme pH (2–12) and temperature (5–95°C) gradients. This will advance fundamental knowledge of interfacial bio-processes while directly informing the design of antifouling materials for renewable energy infrastructure. The computational toolkit developed will be adaptable to other interfacial biological systems, from marine bio-corrosion to biomedical implant infections, establishing a new paradigm for interdisciplinary biofilm research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Oral and maxillofacial pathologies, such as oral squamous cell carcinoma and osteonecrosis, present diagnostic and prognostic challenges due to their heterogeneous molecular and morphological features. Current clinical workflows often rely on subjective interpretations of histopathological or radiographic data, which may lack precision in predicting disease behavior or therapeutic response. This project proposes to address these limitations by integrating multi-modal datasets—including high-resolution 3D radiographic imaging, whole-slide histopathology scans, genomic profiles, and longitudinal clinical records—into a unified computational framework. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models capable of identifying subtle patterns across these diverse data types. Key computational steps include preprocessing terabyte-scale imaging data via GPU-accelerated pipelines, training deep convolutional neural networks for feature extraction, and implementing federated learning approaches to preserve patient privacy while pooling multi-institutional data. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate protein interactions underlying drug resistance in oral cancers. The project’s computational demands necessitate scalable storage, parallel processing, and advanced GPU nodes to manage iterative model training and large-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for early malignancy detection, risk stratification tools for osteonecrosis in patients undergoing antiresorptive therapy, and mechanistic insights into tumor microenvironment dynamics. By enabling data integration at unprecedented scale, this work aims to advance precision diagnostics and inform targeted therapeutic strategies, directly addressing unmet clinical needs in oral and maxillofacial disease management. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in processing speed and model complexity, ensuring robust validation of findings across diverse patient cohorts.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions, using clinical, radiographic, microscopic, biochemical, or other examinations.

abstract: The repair and restoration of footwear and leather goods remain deeply rooted in artisanal practices, with limited integration of computational tools to systematically analyze material behavior, structural integrity, and repair efficacy. This project addresses the critical need to modernize these practices by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model the complex interactions between leather substrates, adhesives, and environmental stressors. Specifically, we aim to investigate the biomechanical and chemical processes underlying common failure modes in repaired footwear—such as sole detachment, seam splitting, and leather cracking—as well as the performance of dyes and finishes under varying humidity and temperature conditions. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution in repaired regions, molecular dynamics (MD) to study adhesive bonding at the nanoscale, and machine learning (ML) to predict optimal repair protocols based on material properties and usage patterns. A key focus will be orthopedic footwear, where personalized biomechanical load profiles will inform simulations of custom repairs to enhance durability and comfort. Additionally, we will develop predictive models for leather aging and degradation to guide conservation strategies for heritage items. The outcomes of this research will yield a computational framework for optimizing repair techniques, reducing material waste, and extending the lifespan of leather goods. By generating open-access datasets and simulation tools tailored to artisan workflows, this project bridges traditional craftsmanship with computational innovation, fostering sustainability in a historically resource-intensive field. The scale and resolution of these simulations—particularly MD trajectories and ML training on heterogeneous material datasets—necessitate HPC resources beyond local infrastructure, ensuring robust, generalizable results with practical applications for industry and cultural preservation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair all types of footwear, including replacement and mending of worn parts, repairing orthopedic footwear, refinishing and dyeing leather, and repairing other leather goods such as handbags, belts, and luggage.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding how dynamic population changes intersect with public health infrastructure needs, with a focus on aging populations in urban and rural regions. Leveraging large-scale demographic simulations, the research will model the spatial and temporal evolution of age-specific health service demands under varying migration, fertility, and mortality scenarios. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling with high-resolution geographic data to simulate individual-level demographic behaviors and their aggregate impacts on healthcare systems. Key challenges include processing multi-source datasets (e.g., census microdata, electronic health records, and satellite-derived land-use maps) and calibrating models to account for regional disparities in access and resource allocation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the iterative simulation of millions of agents across decadal timeframes, parallelize spatial analytics using GPU-accelerated geographic information systems (GIS) workflows, and apply machine learning techniques to identify emergent patterns in service gaps. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of healthcare demand hotspots, policy-ready metrics for infrastructure investment prioritization, and an open-source computational framework for scalable demographic modeling. This work will directly support state and local health departments in optimizing resource distribution while advancing methodological innovation in applied demography. By quantifying the cascading effects of demographic shifts on public systems, the project bridges technical population science and actionable decision-making tools for government and nonprofit stakeholders.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the practical application of demographic methods and materials for decision-making in business, education, health, and government. Includes instruction in statistics, research methods, geographic information systems, and demographic methods and techniques.

abstract: Modern applied statistics faces challenges in analyzing high-dimensional and heterogeneous datasets, particularly in domains such as public health and environmental science, where traditional computational methods are inadequate for complex Bayesian models and non-parametric techniques. This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methodologies to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on two primary areas: (1) implementing parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms for Bayesian hierarchical models that integrate multi-source data with spatial and temporal dependencies, and (2) optimizing resampling-based inference for high-dimensional non-parametric regression, enabling uncertainty quantification in large-scale settings. The computational approach will utilize distributed memory architectures to manage memory-intensive tasks and employ GPU acceleration for likelihood evaluations in stochastic simulations. By overcoming current bottlenecks in computation time and memory constraints, this work aims to produce statistically robust tools for applications such as disease risk mapping and climate impact assessment. The expected outcomes include open-source software packages tailored for HPC environments, methodological advances in efficient Monte Carlo sampling, and case studies demonstrating improved inference in real-world datasets with millions of observations. This project will enhance the capacity of applied researchers to tackle computationally prohibitive problems while advancing statistical theory at the intersection of scalability and uncertainty quantification.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing epigenetic editing for tissue-specific gene therapy using high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic chromatin interactions. While CRISPR-based gene editing has advanced therapeutic targeting, epigenetic modifiers—such as CRISPR-dCas9 systems—require precise spatiotemporal control to avoid off-target effects and ensure stable transcriptional modulation. Current experimental approaches struggle to predict how epigenetic editors interact with the 3D genome architecture of specific cell types, particularly in dynamic disease contexts like fibrosis or neurodegenerative disorders. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omic data (ATAC-seq, Hi-C, and single-cell RNA-seq) with molecular dynamics simulations to predict optimal epigenetic editing windows and delivery strategies. The HPC component will involve two phases: (1) large-scale parallelized modeling of chromatin conformational changes under editing perturbations using coarse-grained molecular dynamics, and (2) machine learning-driven optimization of guide RNA designs for cell-type specificity by training on epigenomic landscapes from diverse human tissues. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to process terabyte-scale chromatin interaction datasets, while the ML models will employ federated learning techniques to maintain data privacy across collaborating clinical partners. Expected outcomes include a predictive atlas of editable epigenetic loci for 12 high-priority therapeutic targets, validated in vitro using patient-derived iPSC models. This work will establish a pipeline for rational design of epigenetic therapies, reducing experimental trial-and-error cycles and accelerating translational workflows. By prioritizing computational exploration of off-target risks and tissue-specific efficacy, the project addresses a critical bottleneck in scalable, ethical gene therapy development. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated via a cloud-based platform to support reproducibility and community-driven refinement of epigenetic editing strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies. Includes instruction in medical genetics, genome analysis, pharmacology of gene transfer, viral vectors, nonviral therapeutic techniques, genetic screening, targeted gene delivery, vector production, safety and quality assurance, clinical trials management, and bioethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into the analysis of multimodal electrophysiological data to improve the diagnosis and stratification of neurological disorders. Clinical neurophysiology relies heavily on interpreting complex signals from EEG, EMG, and NCS, yet current methodologies often struggle with the volume, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of modern datasets. Conventional analytical pipelines lack the scalability to process long-term monitoring data efficiently or to integrate multimodal signals in real time, limiting their utility in personalized clinical decision-making. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging parallelized signal processing, machine learning (ML), and network neuroscience algorithms. The core objectives include (1) developing GPU-accelerated pipelines for preprocessing large-scale EEG/EMG datasets, including artifact removal and feature extraction; (2) training deep neural networks to classify patterns associated with epilepsy, neuromuscular junction disorders, and autonomic dysfunction using multi-site patient data; and (3) constructing dynamic functional connectivity models from high-density EEG to map disease-specific network disruptions. HPC resources are critical for managing terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters in ML models, and running computationally intensive simulations of neural network dynamics. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for automated anomaly detection in EEG/EMG, predictive biomarkers for early disease differentiation, and open-source tools for real-time multimodal signal integration. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in clinical neurophysiology, reduce interpretation variability, and provide a scalable infrastructure for future translational studies. By coupling electrophysiological data with advanced computational methods, the project aims to establish a paradigm shift toward data-driven, precision-based management of neurological disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous system disorders using a combination of clinical evaluation and electrophysiologic testing such as electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and nerve conduction studies (NCS).

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of large-scale, data-driven art installations that integrate environmental sensor data with community narratives to address ecological crises. The core problem lies in the limited capacity of traditional artistic methods to process and visualize complex, real-time environmental datasets (e.g., air quality, deforestation rates, urban heat islands) in ways that engage diverse publics and catalyze dialogue on climate justice. To bridge this gap, the project employs computational modeling, machine learning, and immersive 3D rendering techniques to synthesize geospatial data, participatory community input, and generative visual art. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale environmental datasets from satellite imagery and IoT sensors, training generative adversarial networks (GANs) to create dynamic visualizations reflecting localized ecological impacts, and simulating interactive installations in virtual environments for public feedback cycles. The computational pipeline will prioritize ethical frameworks for data sovereignty, ensuring community contributors retain agency over how their stories and landscapes are represented. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for artists working at the intersection of environmental justice and computational media, as well as a publicly accessible digital archive of the generated artworks. These resources aim to democratize the use of HPC in socially engaged art practice, fostering interdisciplinary collaborations between artists, environmental scientists, and advocacy groups.
