By translating abstract ecological data into emotionally resonant visual narratives, the project seeks to amplify marginalized voices in climate discourse and inspire collective action, while expanding methodologies for computational art that prioritize both technical rigor and community co-creation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on using the arts to promote activism, civic dialog, community development, ecological and environmental awareness, or social justice. Includes instruction in community organizing, cultural criticism, social practice, studio art, and visual and performing arts.

abstract: The commercial poultry industry faces significant challenges from infectious diseases, which threaten animal welfare, economic stability, and food security. Current approaches to disease management often rely on reactive measures, limited by gaps in understanding pathogen transmission dynamics, host-pathogen interactions, and genetic or nutritional factors influencing disease susceptibility. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and analyze large-scale datasets spanning genomics, epidemiology, and production metrics. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) constructing agent-based models to simulate disease spread within poultry flocks under varying management practices, and (2) applying machine learning to identify genetic markers associated with disease resistance and nutritional interventions that optimize immune function. These computational approaches require processing multi-terabyte datasets, including whole-genome sequences of common poultry pathogens (e.g., avian influenza, Newcastle disease), longitudinal health records from commercial farms, and high-resolution environmental sensor data. HPC resources will enable the parallelization of phylogenetic analyses to track pathogen evolution, the training of neural networks on heterogeneous data streams for early outbreak prediction, and the execution of complex simulations evaluating biosecurity protocols. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for preemptive disease mitigation, genetic selection criteria to enhance flock resilience, and data-driven nutritional guidelines. By integrating computational modeling with clinical veterinary insights, this work aims to transform poultry health management from crisis-driven responses to proactive, precision-based strategies. The requested computing resources will directly support the scalability and reproducibility of these analyses, ensuring findings are translatable to diverse production systems. This project aligns with broader goals of sustaining global protein supplies while reducing antimicrobial use in livestock, with methodological advances applicable to computational research in veterinary and agricultural sciences.
cip_definition: Research focused on the commercial poultry industry, providing services and technical support pertaining to prevention, diagnosis, and management of disease; epidemiology; genetics; and nutrition.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenges of optimizing next-generation wireless communication systems, particularly in densely populated urban environments where network congestion, interference, and latency critically impact performance. As 5G/6G networks expand to support IoT devices, autonomous systems, and high-bandwidth applications, existing resource allocation frameworks struggle to dynamically balance spectral efficiency, energy consumption, and quality-of-service demands. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of a machine learning-driven computational model for real-time network optimization, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale, heterogeneous telecommunications environments. The research will integrate multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithms with high-fidelity channel modeling to predict interference patterns, allocate radio resources, and adaptively route traffic across software-defined networks. Computational workloads will involve parallelized simulations of urban-scale network topologies with millions of nodes, emulating diverse traffic scenarios and mobility patterns. Additionally, the project will implement digital signal processing pipelines to optimize error-correcting codes and compression algorithms under varying channel conditions, requiring GPU-accelerated computations for training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of network telemetry. Expected outcomes include novel protocols for dynamic spectrum sharing, reduced latency in edge computing architectures, and quantifiable improvements in network capacity. These advancements will directly inform the design of scalable telecommunications infrastructure, with open-source tools and datasets contributing to industry standards. The HPC resources are essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of optimization variables, enabling parameter sweeps across physical-layer configurations and network-layer policies that are computationally intractable on conventional systems. By bridging algorithmic innovation with practical deployment constraints, this work aims to advance the robustness and adaptability of modern telecommunication systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to help design and implement telecommunications systems. Includes instruction in communications protocol, data networking, digital compression algorithms, digital signal processing, Internet access, object-oriented and relational databases, and programming languages.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the emerging challenge of quantifying and mitigating workplace cognitive fatigue in distributed, hybrid work environments—a critical yet understudied aspect of modern human capital sustainability. Traditional HR metrics and surveys lack the temporal resolution and predictive capacity to capture dynamic cognitive load fluctuations, which are exacerbated by asynchronous communication tools, prolonged virtual collaboration, and algorithmically managed task allocation systems. We propose developing a computational framework that integrates multimodal data streams—including communication patterns, task-switching frequency, biometric sensor inputs, and environmental variables—to model workforce cognitive fatigue at scale. The methodology combines graph neural networks to map interdependencies in collaborative workflows with reinforcement learning agents simulating adaptive workload redistribution strategies. By processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning 12 multinational organizations, the HPC infrastructure will enable real-time simulation of over 10^5 possible intervention scenarios per decision cycle, accounting for individual neurodiversity profiles and team composition variables. Expected outcomes include a predictive taxonomy of cognitive fatigue cascades in distributed teams and an open-source toolkit for optimizing task allocation policies. This work bridges computational neuroscience, distributed systems theory, and HR analytics, offering novel insights into preserving workforce mental capital while maintaining operational efficiency. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, high-dimensional parameter space exploration, and privacy-preserving federated learning across anonymized employee data partitions. Results will advance evidence-based strategies for cognitive resource management in increasingly digital-first workplaces, with implications for productivity metrics, attrition risk modeling, and ethical AI deployment in HR decision systems.
cip_title: Human Resources Management and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in human resources management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Child abuse and neglect present complex diagnostic and management challenges due to the multifactorial nature of cases, which often involve heterogeneous data from medical histories, imaging, social determinants, legal records, and multidisciplinary team inputs. Current approaches to synthesizing these data remain fragmented, leading to inconsistencies in abuse identification, risk stratification, and prevention strategies. This project proposes the development of an integrated computational framework to improve the accuracy of abuse diagnosis, optimize case management workflows, and predict long-term outcomes for affected children. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will aggregate and analyze multimodal datasets—including electronic health records, radiological imaging, forensic reports, and socioeconomic variables—from a retrospective cohort of 15,000+ cases across pediatric care networks. Machine learning models, such as graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures, will be trained to detect subtle patterns indicative of abuse, differentiate abusive injuries from accidental trauma, and quantify cumulative risk factors. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model interactions between healthcare providers, social services, and legal systems to identify bottlenecks in multidisciplinary collaboration. Computational demands include large-scale data integration (≥100 TB), parallelized model training across thousands of parameters, and real-time inference for clinical decision support. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive analytics platform to reduce diagnostic errors and false-positive referrals, (2) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing team-based case reviews, and (3) risk-prediction tools to prioritize prevention programs for high-burden communities. By enabling rapid analysis of complex, interdependent variables, HPC resources are critical to advancing translational research in child abuse pediatrics, with direct implications for clinical practice, legal proceedings, and population-level harm reduction.
cip_definition: Research on how to accurately diagnose abuse, consult with community agencies on child safety, provide expertise in courts of law, treat consequences of abuse and neglect, direct child abuse and neglect prevention programs and participate on multidisciplinary investigative teams, and manage child abuse cases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing industrial systems under dynamic constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address scalability challenges in modeling complex production environments. Industrial processes increasingly face demands for efficiency, adaptability, and sustainability, yet existing optimization tools struggle to integrate real-time human factors, equipment variability, and logistical uncertainties at scale. The proposed research will focus on hybrid simulation-optimization methods, combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of workforce interactions with discrete-event simulations (DES) of production lines. These models will be coupled with metaheuristic algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal solutions for multi-objective problems, such as balancing throughput, energy use, and ergonomic safety. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing simulations across thousands of scenarios, enabling sensitivity analyses of stochastic parameters (e.g., machine downtime, supply chain delays) and reducing computation time from weeks to days. The project will validate results using case studies from automotive manufacturing and semiconductor fabrication, provided by industry partners. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for industrial technologists to simulate resource allocation strategies under uncertainty, alongside predictive metrics for operational resilience. This work will advance the integration of human factors into large-scale optimization—a gap in current industrial engineering practices—while demonstrating how HPC can democratize access to high-fidelity process modeling for small- and medium-sized enterprises. By bridging computational scalability with practical usability, the project aims to contribute novel methodologies to industrial technology research and foster data-driven decision-making in resource-constrained environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of industrial engineers and managers. Includes instruction in optimization theory, human factors, organizational behavior, industrial processes, industrial planning procedures, computer applications, and report and presentation preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent properties of multi-species biological communities through large-scale simulations of interspecies interactions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex systems that cannot feasibly be studied in controlled laboratory settings. A central challenge in general biology lies in understanding how collective behaviors, stability, and resilience arise from the dynamic interplay of diverse organisms in shared environments. Traditional experimental approaches are limited by scalability and the inability to simultaneously track multiple variables across temporal and spatial scales. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with dynamical systems theory to simulate community-level interactions. The ABM component will represent individual organisms with species-specific behavioral and metabolic rules, while system-level differential equations will capture nutrient cycling, energy flow, and environmental stressors. HPC resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations across parameter spaces encompassing thousands of species combinations, varying resource gradients, and perturbation scenarios. By analyzing phase transitions and stability thresholds in these simulations, we aim to identify universal principles governing biodiversity maintenance and collapse. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking micro-scale interactions to macro-scale ecological patterns, validated against existing empirical datasets from simplified experimental ecosystems. This work will provide foundational insights into the rules underlying biological complexity, with potential applications in conservation strategy design and ecosystem management. The requested computing allocation will enable parameter sensitivity analyses, long-term stability assessments, and high-resolution visualization of multidimensional data, all essential for advancing systems-level understanding in general biological sciences.
cip_definition: A general program of biology at the introductory, basic level or a program in biology or the biological sciences that is undifferentiated as to title or content. Includes instruction in general biology and programs covering a variety of biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of detecting and mitigating visual misinformation in digital communication ecosystems, such as manipulated images, deepfake videos, and AI-generated multimedia content, which threaten public trust and information integrity. Current manual and automated tools are insufficient for analyzing the scale, diversity, and sophistication of modern visual media, particularly in real-time scenarios critical to journalism and public communication. To bridge this gap, the research will employ advanced deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial network (GAN) detectors, to identify tampered content across heterogeneous multimedia datasets. These models require training on massive, labeled datasets of authentic and altered media, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage parallel processing, hyperparameter optimization, and rapid inference tasks. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of high-resolution images and video frames, leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and validation. Outcomes will include an open-source detection framework optimized for integration into journalistic workflows, enabling faster verification of user-generated content during breaking news events. The project also aims to map trends in visual misinformation tactics, providing actionable insights for media literacy initiatives and policy discussions. By combining communication theory with scalable computational methods, this work will enhance the capacity of journalists, fact-checkers, and platforms to maintain informational authenticity in increasingly visual digital landscapes. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary model accuracy and speed, which exceed the capabilities of standard cloud-based or local computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Communications Technologies and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications technologies and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in correctional facility operations through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Correctional systems face challenges in balancing security, resource allocation, and rehabilitative outcomes, yet operational decision-making often relies on legacy frameworks ill-suited for dynamic, large-scale environments. The research problem centers on developing an agent-based simulation platform to model inmate movement, staff-inmate interactions, and facility-wide resource flows under varying policy scenarios. By integrating anonymized historical data on facility incidents, staffing patterns, and program participation, the model will simulate emergent behaviors and stress-test operational protocols (e.g., lockdown procedures, educational program scheduling) to identify failure points and optimization opportunities. Computational methods will combine discrete-event simulation with machine learning techniques to iteratively refine predictive accuracy, requiring parallel processing capabilities to manage stochastic simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of identifying trade-offs between security expenditures, rehabilitative programming access, and operational overhead. The project’s significance lies in its novel application of HPC to corrections management—a domain traditionally underserved by computational social science—while adhering to ethical constraints through synthetic data safeguards. Results will provide actionable insights for facility administrators and contribute methodological frameworks for complex system analysis in criminal justice contexts. This work bridges gaps between computational social science and applied corrections research, offering a template for evidence-based operational design without direct overlap with excluded disciplines such as public administration or social services. The requested resources will enable simulations at unprecedented granularity, capturing multi-scale interactions across 10,000+ agent populations in real-world facility geometries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in corrections and criminal justice, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the biomechanical and physiological factors influencing lactation success, with the goal of optimizing clinical strategies for breastfeeding support. Despite established benefits of breastfeeding, many individuals face challenges due to anatomical, hormonal, or environmental factors that remain poorly characterized at a systems level. Current clinical protocols rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for individual variability in lactation physiology. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling framework integrating multi-omics data, biomechanical simulations of milk ejection dynamics, and machine learning (ML) to identify personalized predictors of lactation outcomes. Large-scale genomic datasets (e.g., hormone receptor polymorphisms) will be analyzed alongside clinical variables (infant latch patterns, maternal metabolic markers) and dynamic 3D simulations of mammary tissue stress during milk expression. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution ultrasound imaging data, training ML models on heterogeneous datasets (n > 10,000 clinical cases), and running finite element models of breast tissue mechanics under varying physiological conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to flag high-risk patients for early intervention, (2) biomechanical thresholds for optimal pump suction patterns, and (3) a public computational toolkit for simulating lactation scenarios. This work will directly inform evidence-based updates to lactation consultant training programs and clinical decision-support tools, bridging a critical gap between population-level guidelines and individualized care. By elucidating the interplay of biological, mechanical, and behavioral factors in lactation success, the project aims to reduce disparities in breastfeeding access and outcomes, particularly among populations with limited clinical support resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide lactation management services and breastfeeding support to women, and to work as a Lactation Consultant in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology of lactation, nutrition, breastfeeding techniques and technologies, common concerns and solutions, management of special situations, breastfeeding instruction, professional and legal concerns, and advocacy.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing material efficiency, structural performance, and project timelines while balancing sustainability goals. Current manual and semi-automated approaches to construction planning and material selection lack the precision required to minimize waste and energy use in complex projects. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework for simulating and optimizing construction workflows, material choices, and structural systems using high-performance computing (HPC). The research will focus on three interconnected components: (1) multi-physics simulations of novel composite materials under dynamic environmental loads, (2) machine learning-driven optimization of construction sequencing for large-scale projects, and (3) parametric modeling of energy-efficient building envelopes. These components will leverage parallelized finite element analysis, evolutionary algorithms, and deep reinforcement learning models to process heterogeneous datasets spanning material properties, climate patterns, and equipment performance metrics. The computational demands of processing high-resolution 3D construction site scans (up to 1 TB per project) and running millions of parametric design iterations necessitate access to HPC resources with GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include predictive models for material degradation in extreme weather conditions, automated workflow generators that reduce idle equipment time by 15-25%, and adaptive design templates that lower embodied carbon in structural systems by 20% compared to conventional methods. By establishing an open-source computational toolkit for construction optimization, this research will provide trade professionals with data-driven decision support tools while advancing academic understanding of scalable digital twins in construction management. The project directly addresses workforce training needs by integrating HPC-derived insights into vocational training modules for next-generation construction specialists.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in construction trades, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric infectious diseases present unique challenges due to the dynamic interplay between developing immune systems, pathogen variability, and heterogeneous treatment responses. Current clinical models often fail to account for the multifactorial nature of severe or atypical infections in children, leading to suboptimal therapeutic strategies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-dimensional datasets, including host genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles, alongside pathogen genomic data and longitudinal clinical records. Using machine learning approaches, we will develop predictive models to identify risk factors for severe disease progression, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and individualized treatment responses. Computational workflows will involve large-scale data harmonization, feature selection, and ensemble modeling to handle sparse, high-dimensional data inherent in pediatric cohorts. HPC resources are critical for training deep neural networks on whole-genome sequencing data and conducting real-time simulations of host-pathogen interactions across diverse pediatric populations. The expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers for early diagnosis, stratification of patients based on predicted therapeutic efficacy, and the generation of actionable insights for managing complex cases. By enabling rapid analysis of complex biological and clinical data, this research aims to advance precision medicine in pediatric infectious diseases, ultimately reducing morbidity and mortality in vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases in children; and to effect a better outcome for pediatric infections with complicated courses, underlying diseases that predispose to unusual or severe infections, unclear diagnoses, uncommon diseases, and complex or investigational treatments.

abstract: The emerging field of homeopathic medicine faces a critical challenge in validating the bioactivity of highly diluted remedies and understanding their interaction with biological systems at a molecular level. While clinical observations and traditional methodologies provide anecdotal evidence, there remains a lack of rigorous, large-scale computational analysis to model the physicochemical behavior of homeopathic preparations or correlate patient constitutional types with remedy efficacy. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of ultra-diluted solutions and machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of clinical case data. The MD simulations will model solvent nanostructure dynamics and solute-solvent interactions across a range of homeopathic potencies (e.g., 6C to 30C dilutions), incorporating quantum mechanical calculations for key molecular clusters. Concurrently, anonymized patient datasets spanning symptom profiles, constitutional types, and treatment outcomes will be analyzed using deep learning architectures to identify predictive patterns in remedy selection and response. The computational workflow requires significant parallel processing capabilities due to the need for extended simulation timescales (µs-ms range) across multiple dilution scenarios and the analysis of high-dimensional clinical data. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based models of potential nanoscale bioactive structures in homeopathic remedies, (2) mechanistic insights into remedy-target interactions informed by solvent dynamics, and (3) ML-derived correlations between patient constitutional factors and therapeutic success rates. This dual computational approach bridges traditional homeopathic principles with modern biophysical and data science methods, offering a foundation for standardized research protocols in the field. Results will directly inform clinical training programs, materia medica refinements, and interdisciplinary dialogues regarding homeopathy’s role in integrative healthcare. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in processing power that restrict simulation fidelity and dataset scope.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of homeopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic system using naturally occurring substances in highly diluted forms to mimic symptoms of illness and trigger autoimmune responses, based on the law of similars and other principles derived from the work of Samuel Hahnemann and others. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, toxicology, philosophy and theory of homeopathy, casetaking and case analysis, repertory, material medica, constitutional typing, proving, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of stylistic and thematic evolution in anglophone literary traditions. While close reading remains foundational to literary studies, the scale of digitized texts—spanning centuries, genres, and regions—exceeds manual analytical capacities. Current gaps persist in systematically mapping macro-level patterns, such as shifts in narrative voice, semantic networks, or metaphor usage across periods, which are critical to understanding cultural and linguistic change. This research addresses these challenges by developing computational workflows to analyze curated corpora of English-language literature, including novels, poetry, and drama from the early modern period to the 21st century. Methodologically, the project employs natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic role labeling, dynamic topic modeling, and sentiment analysis, alongside custom algorithms to trace rhetorical devices and syntactic structures. These tools will process terabytes of text data from sources such as EEBO, ECCO, and Project Gutenberg, requiring parallelized computing for feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, and temporal network analysis. HPC resources are essential to train domain-specific language models, optimize hyperparameters for historical texts, and manage memory-intensive tasks like cross-corpus comparisons. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identifying previously underexamined stylistic continuities and ruptures in literary history, (2) generating visualizable datasets mapping the diffusion of linguistic innovations, and (3) publishing open-access tools for computational literary analysis. By bridging qualitative scholarship with scalable computational methods, this work aims to enrich debates about canon formation, intercultural exchange in anglophone literatures, and the relationship between linguistic form and cultural meaning. The requested allocation will directly support these objectives, enabling analyses that are infeasible on local infrastructure due to processing bottlenecks and data volumes.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the English language, including its history, structure and related communications skills; and the literature and culture of English-speaking peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in the design and optimization of complex electrical and electronic systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance computer-aided drafting (CAD) workflows. Current industry-standard CAD tools face limitations in simulating large-scale circuit layouts, analyzing electromagnetic interference (EMI) in multi-layer printed circuit boards (PCBs), and automating the iterative refinement of power distribution networks. These challenges stem from the computational intensity of modeling high-frequency signal integrity, thermal dynamics, and component-level interactions in modern, densely packed systems. To overcome these barriers, this research will develop parallelized computational methods for real-time multi-physics simulations, integrating finite-element analysis (FEA) and machine learning-driven topology optimization. The HPC environment will enable distributed processing of parametric sweeps to identify optimal component placement, routing configurations, and material selections under constraints such as energy efficiency, manufacturability, and regulatory compliance. A key innovation involves adapting GPU-accelerated algorithms to automate error detection in schematic-to-layout translation, reducing manual verification steps. The project will validate these methods using industrial-grade CAD datasets representing mixed-signal embedded systems and IoT device architectures. Successful implementation is expected to reduce design iteration cycles by 40–60% while improving simulation accuracy for high-speed digital and analog circuits. Outcomes will directly benefit educational programs in electrical/electronics drafting by providing scalable, open-source computational tools that bridge theoretical coursework and industry practices. The resource allocation will also support curriculum development in HPC-augmented CAD workflows, preparing students to address emerging challenges in smart grid infrastructure, wearable electronics, and automated manufacturing systems. By democratizing access to advanced computational resources, this initiative aims to elevate the precision and scalability of electrical drafting methodologies within engineering technology domains.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Drafting and Electrical/ Electronics CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working schematics and representations in support of electrical/electronic engineers, computer engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic electronics, electrical systems and computer layouts; electrode-mechanical drafting; manufacturing circuitry; computer-aided drafting (CAD); and electrical systems specification interpretation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of novel materials for high-efficiency energy conversion systems by leveraging large-scale computational modeling and simulation. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding the dynamic behavior of non-equilibrium quantum materials under extreme thermal and electromagnetic conditions, which are central to next-generation thermoelectric and optoelectronic devices. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve transient atomic-scale interactions in these systems, while existing computational models lack the fidelity to capture multi-physics coupling at relevant scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-modal computational framework integrating ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT), and machine learning-accelerated Monte Carlo sampling. These methods will be deployed on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to simulate mesoscale material domains (10^4–10^6 atoms) over nanosecond timescales, explicitly coupling electronic, vibrational, and spin degrees of freedom. The computational workflow will utilize hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization across GPU-accelerated nodes to manage the combinatorial complexity of the parameter space, with post-processing pipelines for feature extraction and phase-space analysis. Expected outcomes include the identification of metastable material states with enhanced energy conversion coefficients and predictive design rules for defect engineering in chalcogenide-based systems. The generated datasets will be made available through an open-access repository, providing a foundation for experimental validation and industrial collaboration. This work directly supports national priorities in sustainable energy technologies while establishing new computational benchmarks for multi-scale materials discovery. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC system with high-memory nodes and GPU support is essential to achieve the target resolution and throughput for these computationally intensive simulations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical science technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Nuclear radiology relies on precise imaging and quantification of radionuclide biodistribution to diagnose diseases such as cancer, neurological disorders, and cardiovascular conditions. However, current methods for reconstructing tomographic images and modeling radiotracer kinetics face limitations in accuracy and resolution, particularly in heterogeneous tissues or dynamic physiological conditions. These challenges stem from computational constraints in handling complex photon transport physics, noise reduction, and the integration of multi-modal patient data. This project proposes to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational frameworks for optimizing nuclear imaging protocols and predictive biodistribution models. The research will focus on two aims: (1) creating patient-specific Monte Carlo simulations of photon interactions in hybrid SPECT/CT and PET/MRI systems to improve image reconstruction accuracy, and (2) training deep learning models to predict radiotracer kinetics using spatially resolved, time-dependent datasets from clinical studies. The simulations will account for tissue heterogeneity, scatter effects, and motion artifacts, while the machine learning component will integrate imaging data with genomic and metabolic profiles to identify biomarkers of abnormal tracer uptake. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization, parallel processing of high-resolution voxelized phantoms, and iterative training of neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for reducing radiation dose without compromising diagnostic quality, predictive models linking biodistribution patterns to molecular subtypes of disease, and open-source tools for reproducible analysis of nuclear radiology data. This work has direct translational implications for personalizing diagnostic workflows, enhancing early detection of treatment-resistant malignancies, and improving the safety of longitudinal imaging in vulnerable populations. By bridging computational innovation with clinical nuclear radiology, the project aims to establish a scalable framework for advancing precision medicine in radionuclide-based diagnostics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: This project investigates the spatial and temporal dynamics of informal settlement adaptation to climate stressors in rapidly urbanizing coastal regions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model coupled human-environment interactions at unprecedented granularity. Informal settlements, home to over 1 billion people globally, face disproportionate climate risks due to precarious locations and infrastructural marginalization, yet their adaptive capacities remain poorly quantified. Current models insufficiently capture the nonlinear feedbacks between localized environmental changes (e.g., tidal flooding, erosion), community-led adaptation practices, and municipal governance frameworks. Our research integrates fine-scale geospatial data (3D UAV-derived settlement maps, daily tidal inundation records), ethnographic surveys of material improvisation strategies, and multi-agent simulations of household decision-making under resource constraints. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution time-series satellite imagery (1m/pixel) to track micro-scale land cover changes across 15 coastal settlements over a 20-year period, coupled with agent-based models simulating 100,000+ individual actors responding to stochastic climate events. Machine learning pipelines will identify patterns in self-organized infrastructure development, while GPU-accelerated hydrodynamic models predict flood exposure under varying adaptation scenarios. Outcomes will yield a novel framework for quantifying resilience in informal urban contexts, challenging top-down vulnerability assessments by centering community-driven spatial practices. The computational toolkit developed will be open-sourced to support equitable climate planning, directly informing municipal policies in our case study regions (Southeast Asia, East Africa). By bridging cultural geography, urban climatology, and complex systems science, this work advances methodological innovation in studying human-environmental interdependencies while addressing critical gaps in climate justice scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human cultures and their adaptation to physical environments. Includes instruction in archaeology, biogeography, climatology, cultural anthropology, cultural geography, economic development, environmental geography, geomorphology, global environmental change, historical geography, mapping sciences, physical anthropology, political ecology, Quaternary studies, and urban geography.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop patient-specific biomechanical models that optimize assistive device design and rehabilitation protocols for individuals with movement disorders, such as cerebral palsy or post-stroke hemiparesis. Current approaches to physical therapy interventions often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for the complex interplay of neuromuscular variability, tissue mechanics, and functional goals unique to each patient. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating individualized anatomical data, dynamic movement patterns, and predictive simulations to tailor assistive strategies. The computational approach combines finite element modeling (FEM) of musculoskeletal structures with machine learning algorithms trained on motion capture datasets, electromyography (EMG) signals, and clinical outcome metrics. High-resolution MRI/CT scans will inform patient-specific anatomical geometries, while iterative simulations will model the biomechanical effects of orthotic devices, exoskeletons, and therapeutic exercises under varying physiological loads. A parallelized computational pipeline will be implemented to handle the multi-scale nature of the problem, spanning cellular-level muscle activation dynamics to whole-body movement kinematics. Machine learning components will identify predictive biomarkers of treatment responsiveness, enabling adaptive optimization of rehabilitation plans. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the computational intensity of 3D musculoskeletal simulations, real-time parameter optimization, and large-scale data integration across heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework for generating personalized therapeutic recommendations, validated against clinical mobility assessments. This work aims to advance precision rehabilitation by translating biomechanical insights into actionable clinical tools, reducing trial-and-error in device fitting and exercise prescription. By enhancing the efficacy of physical therapy interventions, the project aligns with the evolving role of physical therapist assistants in implementing data-driven care strategies while addressing a critical niche in computational rehabilitation science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physical therapist, to implement physical therapy treatment care plans, train patients, conduct treatment interventions, use equipment, and observe and record patient progress. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, behavioral sciences, biomechanics, clinical documentation, clinical pathology, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and operational decision-making in hospital and health care facilities, addressing the critical challenge of balancing cost-efficiency with high-quality patient care. Current management strategies often rely on static models that inadequately capture the dynamic, multi-variable nature of healthcare operations, including fluctuating patient demand, staffing constraints, equipment availability, and regulatory requirements. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale simulations and machine learning models that integrate real-time and historical data from electronic health records, facility sensors, and staffing logs. Agent-based modeling will simulate patient flow through emergency departments, surgical units, and inpatient wards under diverse scenarios, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize bed allocation, staff scheduling, and equipment procurement. Predictive analytics will forecast patient admission rates and readmission risks to inform proactive resource deployment. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing required for Monte Carlo simulations of facility-wide operations and the training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated decision-support tools that enable administrators to dynamically adjust resource distribution, reduce operational bottlenecks, and minimize costs without compromising care standards. By quantifying trade-offs between financial constraints and clinical outcomes, this research will contribute novel methodologies to the field of healthcare facilities management, with potential applications in disaster response planning, capacity expansion strategies, and policy evaluation. The resulting open-source framework will be tested across three partner hospitals, with scalability to diverse facility types.
cip_title: Hospital and Health Care Facilities Administration/ Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and other health care facilities. Includes instruction in facilities planning, building and operations management, business management, financial management and insurance, fund-raising and marketing, public relations, human resources management and labor relations, health care facilities operations, principles of health care delivery, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for optimizing large-scale, stochastic industrial systems, with applications to supply chain resilience and production scheduling under uncertainty. Industrial systems increasingly face disruptions from geopolitical, environmental, and market volatility, necessitating real-time adaptive decision-making. However, existing optimization frameworks struggle with combinatorial complexity when modeling multi-echelon networks or high-dimensional uncertainty spaces, limiting their practical utility. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture integrating distributed stochastic optimization, parallelized Monte Carlo simulation, and graph-based machine learning. The methodology leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to decompose problems across temporal and spatial dimensions while maintaining coordination through asynchronous consensus algorithms. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated scenario generation for non-stationary disruption risks and memory-efficient graph neural networks to predict cascading failures in interconnected production networks. Computational experiments will evaluate system performance under synthetic and real-world datasets spanning semiconductor manufacturing logistics and hospital resource allocation networks. The project requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale optimization models, parallelize millions of scenario evaluations, and train deep reinforcement learning agents on GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source algorithmic frameworks for stochastic industrial system optimization, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational scalability against commercial solvers, and (3) case studies demonstrating 15-30% improvements in recovery time and resource utilization under disruption scenarios. By enabling rapid analysis of complex trade-offs between efficiency, cost, and risk, this work will provide foundational tools for next-generation resilient systems engineering. Results will be disseminated through the INFORMS Journal on Computing and collaborations with industry partners in advanced manufacturing and healthcare operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize automated analysis of complex tissue microarchitecture in histologic samples, addressing critical inefficiencies in current manual and semi-automated methods. Histologic technicians routinely process tissue sections for diagnostic and research purposes, yet quantitative assessment of structural features—such as extracellular matrix organization, cellular spatial distributions, and microvascular patterns—remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. Our research focuses on creating deep learning models capable of parsing high-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs) to map 3D tissue architecture from serial sections, a task requiring immense computational resources due to gigapixel-scale datasets and the need for volumetric reconstructions. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will train 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on annotated WSIs spanning diverse tissue types and staining protocols (e.g., H&E, Masson’s trichrome), integrating spatial transcriptomics data where available to ground structural patterns in molecular context. A parallel computational pipeline will simulate tissue deformation during processing—factoring in fixation, embedding, and sectioning variables—to improve alignment algorithms for 3D reconstructions. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and CPU clusters for large-scale batch processing of archival slides. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for volumetric histologic analysis, validated against gold-standard manual annotations, and a novel simulation engine to guide optimal tissue preparation protocols. This work directly enhances the precision and scope of histotechnicians' diagnostic capabilities while enabling researchers to interrogate tissue structure-function relationships at unprecedented scales. By bridging computational science and histotechnology, the project establishes a foundation for AI-driven innovation in tissue-based diagnostics, with applications in fibrosis research, tumor microenvironment studies, and regenerative medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize hydraulic fracturing operations in unconventional shale reservoirs, addressing critical challenges in predicting fracture network propagation and fluid-rock interactions under complex subsurface conditions. Current models often oversimplify heterogeneities in rock mechanics, fluid transport, and stress anisotropy, leading to suboptimal well completions and hydrocarbon recovery rates. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework integrating discrete fracture network (DFN) modeling, coupled hydro-mechanical simulations, and machine learning-based parameter calibration. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve centimeter-scale fracture dynamics across kilometer-scale reservoir domains while capturing transient fluid flow, proppant transport, and stress shadow effects. Parallelized finite element methods and graph neural networks will be employed to accelerate multiphysics simulations and uncertainty quantification across thousands of stochastic realizations. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-optimized solvers for near-real-time inversion of microseismic and distributed fiber-optic sensing data during operational planning phases. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source simulation platform capable of predicting fracture geometry with <15% error relative to field measurements, enabling operators to maximize stimulated reservoir volume while minimizing water usage and environmental footprint. Results will directly inform completion strategies for five active Permian Basin assets, with potential to improve 30-year recovery factors by 3-5% in liquid-rich plays. This work will advance fundamental understanding of fracture containment mechanisms in layered formations and establish best practices for HPC-enabled fracture optimization in petroleum engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for locating, extracting, processing and refining crude petroleum and natural gas, including prospecting instruments and equipment, mining and drilling systems, processing and refining systems and facilities, storage facilities, transportation systems, and related environmental and safety systems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of self-organizing, multiscale material systems inspired by biological and ecological networks, integrating computational modeling, nonlinear dynamics, and stochastic optimization. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting emergent behaviors in hybrid bio-engineered materials, where traditional continuum models fail to capture discrete, agent-based interactions at the micro-to-meso scale. We propose a novel computational framework combining agent-based stochastic simulations with graph neural networks (GNNs) to model dynamic resource allocation in synthetic biofilm analogs—a system exhibiting properties relevant to environmental remediation, programmable biopolymers, and adaptive manufacturing scaffolds. The core challenge lies in simulating 10^6–10^7 discrete cellular agents interacting with heterogeneous chemical gradients and mechanical stresses across temporal scales spanning milliseconds to days. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for parallelized execution of hybrid models: molecular dynamics (LAMMPS) will resolve nanoscale polymer interactions, while custom CUDA-accelerated agent-based modules (developed using Julia/JuGPU) will simulate population dynamics. Machine learning components will train surrogate models in situ to accelerate parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include 1) predictive models of stress-induced pattern formation in metabolically active materials, 2) optimization protocols for resource distribution in 3D-printed biotic-abiotic interfaces, and 3) open-source tools for coupled physical-biological simulation at unprecedented scales. This work bridges synthetic biology, materials science, and distributed computing, offering foundational insights into engineering living material systems with applications in sustainable manufacturing and ecosystem engineering. The requested allocation of 200,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated architectures will enable parameter sweeps across critical regimes (nutrient diffusion coefficients, shear moduli, population densities) currently inaccessible to conventional computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to science, mathematics, and engineering practice. Includes instruction in applied mathematics and statistics, data science, numerical analysis and scientific computing, computational mechanics and physics, parallel computing and computer architecture, and mathematical modeling.

abstract: This project seeks to address the scalability and accuracy challenges inherent in automating real-time accounting processes for multinational enterprises, where traditional software systems struggle with high-volume, heterogeneous transaction data across diverse regulatory environments. The rapid digitization of global financial systems, coupled with increasing transaction velocities and compliance demands, necessitates computational frameworks capable of dynamically reconciling ledgers, detecting anomalies, and enforcing jurisdiction-specific rules at scale. We propose developing a hybrid architecture combining graph-based transaction modeling, federated learning for localized compliance pattern recognition, and parallelized blockchain-inspired consensus mechanisms to enable secure, auditable record-keeping across distributed entities. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate enterprise-scale transaction environments (10^8+ daily events) with varying tax regimes and reporting standards, training machine learning models on synthetically generated financial data while maintaining data isolation constraints. Computational experiments will focus on optimizing distributed ledger sharding techniques for real-time balance sheet synchronization and stress-testing anomaly detection algorithms under peak load scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive accounting system design, quantitative benchmarks for transaction throughput versus auditability tradeoffs in multi-jurisdictional contexts, and novel metrics for measuring algorithmic fairness in automated compliance decisions. By advancing the computational infrastructure underlying next-generation accounting technologies, this work aims to reduce latency in financial reporting cycles by 40-60% for large organizations while maintaining sub-0.1% error rates in automated regulatory adherence—a critical capability as real-time fiscal transparency becomes central to global business operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical administrative support to professional accountants and other financial management personnel. Includes instruction in posting transactions to accounts, record-keeping systems, accounting software operation, and general accounting principles and practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study focused on analyzing the evolution of cultural narratives across time and space through large-scale, multimodal datasets. The research problem centers on the limitations of current computational methods in processing and interpreting heterogeneous humanities data—including digitized historical texts, artworks, geospatial records, and social media archives—at scales necessary to identify nuanced patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance. Traditional approaches struggle with the volume, complexity, and temporal-spatial interdependencies of these datasets, which span centuries and multiple linguistic, visual, and geographic domains. The proposed computational approach integrates machine learning (e.g., transformer models for multilingual text analysis, graph neural networks for mapping cultural networks), geospatial clustering algorithms, and computer vision techniques to trace thematic continuities and ruptures in cultural production. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific models on terabytes of unstructured data, conducting hyperparameter optimization for multimodal fusion, and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about narrative diffusion. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for cross-modal humanities analytics, (2) interactive visualizations of narrative trajectories for public engagement, and (3) open-access tools for annotating and querying digitized archives using semantic and geotemporal criteria. By enabling computationally intensive analysis of understudied connections between historical and contemporary cultural practices, this project aims to demonstrate how advanced computing can reshape humanities scholarship, offering new methodologies for interdisciplinary research while supporting the preservation and accessibility of cultural heritage. The requested allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for graph-based network analysis, and high-throughput storage for managing distributed archival collections.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of new technologies, advanced computing, and public engagement to investigate and analyze questions in the humanities. Includes instruction in anthropology, art, data mining and machine learning, design, digital archives, geospatial technologies, history, human-computer interface design, literature, markup languages, social media technologies, and software development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the reliability and efficiency of investigative interviewing in law enforcement by addressing systemic challenges in detecting deception, minimizing cognitive biases, and optimizing interview protocols. Traditional methods rely heavily on subjective human judgment, which can be influenced by implicit biases, environmental stressors, and variable adherence to legally compliant practices. To address this, the research will integrate behavioral psychology, linguistic analysis, and decision-making theory into a machine learning model trained on multimodal datasets, including anonymized interview transcripts, audio-visual recordings, and physiological data (e.g., vocal stress patterns, micro-expressions). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process and analyze these large, heterogeneous datasets, which span terabytes of unstructured text, video, and sensor data. Computational workflows will employ deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based NLP models, convolutional neural networks for visual data) to identify patterns associated with truthful versus deceptive statements, contextual stressors, and interviewer tactics that correlate with successful outcomes. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate diverse interview scenarios to evaluate the robustness of proposed protocols under varying conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for agencies to assess interview quality in real time, a bias-detection algorithm to flag potential procedural deviations, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive questioning strategies. By bridging gaps between theoretical research and operational practice, this work aims to reduce wrongful convictions, improve investigative transparency, and foster public trust in law enforcement processes. The scalability of the models, enabled by HPC, ensures applicability across jurisdictions with differing legal frameworks and demographic contexts.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, procedures, techniques, legal concerns, and problems associated with a criminal investigation. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, courtroom evidence management and preparation, case presentation and court testimony, description and identification, state and federal criminal law and procedures, informant and suspect rights, officer liability, informant and witness management, victim awareness, tactical interviewing, psychology, criminal investigation methods and procedures, report writing and documentation, investigative techniques, and case management.

abstract: Radiation therapy efficacy is critically dependent on the precise delivery of tumoricidal doses while sparing adjacent healthy tissues, a challenge exacerbated by dynamic anatomical changes (e.g., organ motion, tumor shrinkage) during treatment. Current adaptive radiotherapy workflows, which adjust plans using periodic imaging, are limited by computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution, real-time imaging data and rapidly recalculating optimized dose distributions. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework for real-time adaptive radiation therapy (RT-ART) in Medical Radiologic Technology. The research problem centers on integrating continuous MRI-guided imaging with instantaneous dose recalculation, enabling submillimeter accuracy in targeting moving tumors. The computational approach combines GPU-accelerated deformable image registration algorithms, Monte Carlo dose simulation, and machine learning models trained to predict short-term anatomical shifts from time-resolved 4D-MRI data. These models will be iteratively refined using retrospective clinical datasets from thoracic and abdominal radiotherapy patients, with HPC resources enabling parallel processing of multi-terabyte imaging repositories. Key technical challenges include reducing latency in dose optimization loops to under 10 seconds and validating computational predictions against physical phantom measurements. Expected outcomes include a scalable RT-ART pipeline capable of dynamically adjusting beam parameters during treatment delivery, potentially reducing planning target volume margins by 30–50% and lowering radiation-induced toxicity risks. The project’s significance lies in bridging a critical gap between emerging imaging technologies and their clinical translation, offering a foundation for personalized, motion-robust radiotherapy. Successful implementation will require access to HPC clusters with high-memory nodes, multi-GPU configurations, and fast interconnects to handle concurrent image analysis, dose computation, and uncertainty modeling tasks.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Public health nursing interventions require precise, data-driven strategies to address complex community health challenges, yet computational limitations often hinder the scalability of advanced predictive models and simulations. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate the spread of chronic diseases and evaluate targeted nursing interventions in diverse community settings. The research focuses on identifying how socioeconomic, environmental, and behavioral factors interact to influence health outcomes, particularly in underserved rural and urban populations. Using anonymized electronic health records, census data, and geospatial datasets, we will parameterize ABMs to reflect dynamic community networks, disease transmission pathways, and intervention scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to refine model accuracy by analyzing temporal patterns in health disparities and intervention efficacy. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing capabilities to run thousands of simulations across parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and uncertainty quantification—tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into cost-effective intervention strategies, such as optimized timing and placement of community health screenings or tailored health education programs. This work will directly inform public health nursing practices by quantifying the potential impact of preventive measures on reducing hospitalizations for conditions like diabetes and hypertension. Additionally, the models will serve as a scalable framework for future research on infectious disease outbreaks or disaster response planning. By bridging computational science and community health, this project aims to advance evidence-based nursing practices, reduce health inequities, and empower policymakers with tools to prioritize resource allocation in vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to promote health and provide preventive and curative nursing services for groups or communities under the supervision of a public health agency. Includes instruction in community and rural health, family therapy and intervention, disease prevention, health education, and community health assessment.

abstract: Agricultural teacher education faces challenges in effectively integrating emerging agricultural technologies and data-driven practices into vocational curricula. Traditional pedagogical approaches often lack the computational tools to model complex agricultural systems or analyze large-scale educational datasets, limiting the ability to prepare educators for rapidly evolving agri-technological environments. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and evaluate dynamic, simulation-based training modules for agricultural educators. The research problem centers on quantifying how immersive computational modeling of agricultural systems—such as precision agriculture workflows, sustainable resource management scenarios, or climate adaptation strategies—impacts pedagogical effectiveness and student outcomes in teacher preparation programs. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling of classroom knowledge transfer processes, machine learning analysis of longitudinal educator competency data, and large-scale simulations of agricultural education ecosystems under varying technological adoption rates. By parallelizing these analyses across HPC nodes, the project will achieve the processing scale required to model multi-year educational outcomes across diverse agricultural contexts while maintaining granular detail at the individual learner level. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access repository of computationally intensive teaching modules aligned with agricultural education standards, 2) predictive models identifying critical technological competencies for vocational agriculture instructors, and 3) evidence-based frameworks for optimizing the integration of agricultural big data applications into teacher training curricula. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—particularly the need to simultaneously process high-resolution environmental datasets, educational metrics, and socioeconomic variables—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. This work will directly enhance the capacity of agricultural teacher education programs to produce instructors skilled in both foundational pedagogical practices and cutting-edge agricultural technologies, ultimately strengthening workforce development in food and natural resource systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational agricultural programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modern electrical infrastructure resilience and efficiency through advanced computational modeling of power line systems. As aging grids face increasing demands from renewable energy integration, extreme weather events, and evolving communication technologies, lineworkers require predictive tools to optimize maintenance and minimize service disruptions. Current approaches to assessing mechanical stress, thermal load distribution, and failure risks in overhead and underground systems rely heavily on static models that inadequately capture dynamic environmental interactions. This research will develop high-fidelity simulations of multi-physics phenomena affecting power lines, including wind-induced conductor galloping, ice accumulation dynamics, and soil-cable thermal coupling in buried installations. Using finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics implemented on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, we will model regional-scale grid segments with granular material properties and real-world environmental inputs. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical fault data and sensor-derived operational parameters to establish predictive maintenance frameworks. The computational workflow will integrate LiDAR-scanned terrain models, weather station feeds, and material degradation databases to simulate decade-long wear patterns under climate change scenarios. By leveraging parallelized solvers and GPU acceleration, these simulations will achieve unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution while maintaining computational feasibility. Expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for line failure hotspots, optimized crew deployment strategies, and evidence-based recommendations for code updates regarding vegetation clearance distances and underground cable depth requirements. The project will produce open-source simulation templates adaptable to regional grid architectures, directly enhancing lineworker training programs through virtual reality-based scenario modules. Successful implementation will reduce grid vulnerability to extreme weather by 15-20% in pilot regions while providing utility companies with decision-support tools to prioritize infrastructure upgrades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain and repair local, long-distance, and rural electric power cables and communication lines; erect and construct pole and tower lines; and install underground lines and cables. Includes instruction in cable installation and repair, fibre-optic technology, trenching, mobile equipment and crane operation, high-voltage installations, maintenance and inspection, safety, remote communications, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the dynamic mechanisms of membrane protein interactions involved in ion transport and signal transduction, a critical yet poorly understood aspect of cellular biophysics. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve the nanosecond-scale conformational changes and energy landscapes governing these processes. To address this, we propose a computational biophysics approach combining all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with enhanced sampling techniques to model the structural dynamics of key ion channels and G-protein-coupled receptors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large membrane-protein systems (≥500,000 atoms) over biologically relevant timescales (microseconds), leveraging explicit solvent models and force fields optimized for lipid bilayers. We will employ adaptive sampling algorithms to map free energy barriers associated with gating transitions and ligand binding, supplemented by hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to probe electronic interactions in catalytic sites. Expected outcomes include atomistic models of metastable states in transport cycles, predictions of allosteric regulation sites, and quantitative estimates of thermodynamic driving forces. These results will advance fundamental understanding of bioenergetics in transmembrane signaling, with broader implications for designing targeted therapies against channelopathies and neurodegenerative diseases. The computational workflows developed will be disseminated as open-source tools for simulating supramolecular assemblies, bridging gaps between molecular-scale biophysical theory and cellular-scale functional modeling. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on physics-driven mechanistic studies of biological complexity, excluding purely genomic or cell-biological approaches. Resource allocation will enable the scaling of simulations across multiple GPU nodes, with data management plans ensuring reproducibility and interoperability with experimental biophysics datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze spatial-temporal patterns of Holocaust survivor displacement and migration through the integration of fragmented archival records, testimonies, and demographic datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in Holocaust studies: the lack of systematic, large-scale computational frameworks to reconstruct and model survivor trajectories across shifting geopolitical boundaries, clandestine escape routes, and displacement camps. Traditional historical methods struggle to synthesize heterogeneous, multilingual sources—including deportation lists, Red Cross registries, oral histories, and postwar resettlement documents—into cohesive narratives. By developing a scalable computational pipeline, this project will apply natural language processing (NLP) to extract and disambiguate location names, dates, and transport routes from unstructured texts, geospatial algorithms to map trajectories onto historical boundaries, and network analysis to identify hubs of survival and resistance. Agent-based modeling will simulate population movements under varying constraints (e.g., border closures, forced labor allocations) to test hypotheses about survival strategies and systemic vulnerabilities. The computational demands—processing terabytes of digitized records, training multilingual NLP models on historical vernacular, and running iterative simulations—require HPC infrastructure for parallelized data ingestion, distributed geocoding, and GPU-accelerated machine learning.
