cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in comparative economic systems, econometrics, economic theory, money and banking systems, international economics, international trade, linguistics, philology, and translation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a machine learning-driven framework to optimize real-time credentialing and privileging workflows for medical staff, addressing inefficiencies in reconciling multi-source healthcare provider data with dynamic regulatory requirements. Current credentialing processes in healthcare facilities rely on manual verification of provider qualifications, licensure, and compliance histories—a time-intensive task prone to delays and human error, particularly as accreditation standards evolve. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models on unstructured regulatory documents (e.g., CMS guidelines, state medical board rulings) and provider credential datasets. The computational pipeline will integrate federated learning techniques to process sensitive credentialing data from participating hospitals while maintaining privacy, followed by fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) to automate cross-validation of provider applications against current standards. A secondary aim involves simulating credentialing decision pathways via graph neural networks to identify bottlenecks and predict privileging outcomes under varying regulatory scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams—including text, temporal licensure records, and audit trails—at a scale necessary for robust model training. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive credentialing workflow optimization, validated against retrospective data from three academic medical centers. This research addresses a critical gap in healthcare operations technology by creating computational tools that enhance the responsiveness of medical staff services to regulatory changes while reducing administrative latency. Successful implementation could decrease average credentialing processing times by 30-50%, mitigate compliance risks, and establish a replicable framework for AI-assisted healthcare workforce management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform credentialing, privileging, personnel management, and accreditation compliance services for hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in medical staff organization and management, medical terminology, credentialing and re-credentialing, health care accreditation and regulatory standards, health care law, meeting and negotiation management, and office information systems management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the biomechanical interactions between barbering tools and human tissue, with the goal of reducing occupational injuries and improving ergonomic tool design. Barbers experience disproportionately high rates of musculoskeletal disorders due to repetitive motions, static postures, and suboptimal tool ergonomics, yet current solutions remain anecdotal rather than data-driven. The project will develop computational simulations of hand-tool-tissue dynamics during common barbering tasks (e.g., precision scissor work, razor shaving) using finite element analysis and multibody dynamics frameworks. High-resolution 3D models of tools, hands, and facial/neck anatomy will be constructed from MRI and motion-capture data, incorporating material properties of skin, muscle, and hair. HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across tool geometries, grip angles, and force profiles to quantify tissue stress distributions and joint loading patterns under varying conditions. Machine learning techniques will then identify optimal tool modifications and handling techniques to minimize biomechanical strain. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking tool design to injury risk, (2) prototype specifications for ergonomic tools tailored to diverse hand morphologies, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for technique adjustments. By bridging barbering practice with computational biomechanics, this work addresses a critical gap in vocational health research while demonstrating how HPC can advance safety and innovation in non-traditional technical fields. The resulting frameworks may also inform tool design paradigms for other manual professions lacking quantitative ergonomic standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shave and trim facial/neck hair and beards, cut and dress hair, fit hairpieces, give facial and scalp massages, apply cosmetic treatments, and to prepare for licensure as professional barbers at various levels.  Includes instruction in facial shaving; beard and mustache shaping and trimming; shampooing; hair cutting; hair styles and styling art; facial treatments and massage; chemical applications; hair and scalp anatomy and physiology; hairpiece and toupee fitting; equipment operation; health and safety; customer service; and shop business practices.

abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing processes, such as deposition, etching, and lithography, involve complex multi-physics interactions that are challenging to optimize experimentally due to high costs, material waste, and time constraints. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to simulate these processes at the atomic and mesoscopic scales, enabling rapid identification of defect mechanisms and process optimization. The research problem centers on the need to reduce yield-limiting defects—such as line-edge roughness in lithography or non-uniform thin-film deposition—while improving energy efficiency and equipment longevity in fabrication environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for atomic-scale material interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for thermo-mechanical stress modeling, and machine learning (ML) to predict defect formation under varying process parameters. These models will integrate experimental data from in-situ sensors monitoring plasma conditions, temperature gradients, and gas flow dynamics during etching and deposition. The HPC environment is critical to handle the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations, which require parallelized execution across thousands of cores, large memory nodes for 3D nanostructure modeling, and GPU acceleration for ML training on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing process parameters (e.g., pressure, RF power, precursor flow rates), reducing defect rates by an estimated 15–20%, and identifying failure precursors in equipment components such as electrostatic chucks or plasma sources. The results will directly inform adaptive process control strategies and maintenance protocols, advancing sustainable manufacturing practices. This work aligns with industry priorities to enhance production yields and transition to next-generation nodes (sub-3nm) while reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error methodologies. The requested computing resources will enable the creation of open-access simulation tools for academic and industrial training programs, fostering workforce development in semiconductor manufacturing technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to operate and monitor equipment for the fabrication of semiconductors or microchips from silicon wafers, and to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair the specialized equipment used in this process. Includes instruction in AC and DC circuits, digital fundamentals, solid state devices, manufacturing processes, vacuum principles and technology, industrial electronics, quality assurance, and semiconductor manufacturing technology.

abstract: This research seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the behavioral and systemic impacts of decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) on accounting practices, with a focus on real-time auditing and compliance challenges. DAOs—blockchain-based entities governed by smart contracts and distributed decision-making—are disrupting traditional organizational structures, yet their rapid growth has outpaced regulatory and accounting frameworks. Current methods struggle to model the dynamic, trustless interactions within DAOs or assess risks related to automated financial flows, tokenized incentives, and cross-jurisdictional governance. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model DAO ecosystems at scale. The computational approach will integrate agent-based modeling, network analysis, and stochastic optimization to simulate interactions among DAO participants, smart contracts, and external auditors under varying regulatory scenarios. Synthetic transaction datasets representing tokenized voting, treasury management, and profit-sharing mechanisms will be generated to stress-test auditing algorithms. Key challenges include scaling graph-based analyses of on-chain transaction networks, optimizing real-time anomaly detection in permissionless environments, and quantifying emergent systemic risks. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for parallelized contract emulation and federated learning techniques to preserve privacy while training fraud detection models. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of DAO-specific accounting risks, (2) benchmarks for auditing latency and accuracy in decentralized contexts, and (3) open-source tools for simulating compliance scenarios. This work aims to provide foundational insights for accounting standards bodies and regulatory agencies navigating Web3 ecosystems while advancing computational methods for analyzing emergent organizational forms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the profession of accounting and to perform related business functions. Includes instruction in accounting principles and theory, financial accounting, managerial accounting, cost accounting, budget control, tax accounting, legal aspects of accounting, auditing, reporting procedures, statement analysis, planning and consulting, business information systems, accounting research methods, professional standards and ethics, and applications to specific for-profit, public, and non-profit organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing the design and safety evaluation of civil infrastructure systems, with a focus on cost-effective and resilient public works projects. Current methodologies for assessing structural integrity and material performance in civil engineering technologies rely heavily on physical testing and simplified computational simulations, which are time-intensive, resource-limited, and often fail to capture complex real-world interactions. To address these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating multi-scale finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML)-driven material behavior prediction, and probabilistic risk assessment. The HPC environment will enable high-resolution modeling of structural components—such as bridge joints, retaining walls, and foundation systems—under dynamic loads (e.g., seismic activity, vehicular traffic) and environmental stressors (e.g., corrosion, thermal cycling). Large-scale parametric studies will be conducted to evaluate the sensitivity of designs to material variability, construction tolerances, and long-term degradation. Machine learning algorithms, trained on synthetic and experimental datasets, will accelerate the identification of critical failure modes and optimal reinforcement strategies. Outcomes will include validated computational workflows for rapid prototyping of infrastructure designs, enhanced guidelines for field testing protocols, and open-access datasets correlating simulation results with laboratory measurements. By reducing reliance on physical prototypes and enabling data-driven decision-making, this work aims to improve the efficiency of civil engineering project planning while maintaining rigorous safety standards. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of 3D multiphysics simulations, iterative ML model training, and uncertainty quantification across millions of design permutations, which exceed the capabilities of local institutional hardware.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of civil engineers engaged in designing and executing public works projects such as highways, dams, bridges, tunnels and other facilities. Includes instruction in site analysis, structural testing procedures, field and laboratory testing procedures, plan and specification preparation, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Agricultural productivity faces increasing challenges from climate variability, necessitating rapid development of resilient crop varieties. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance genomic prediction models and multi-scale simulations of plant-environment interactions. By integrating large-scale genomic datasets with high-resolution environmental data, we aim to identify genetic markers associated with drought tolerance and heat resistance in staple crops such as wheat and maize. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze genotype-phenotype relationships and predict crop performance under diverse climatic scenarios. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate field-scale crop growth dynamics, incorporating soil heterogeneity, irrigation patterns, and pest pressures. These simulations will generate actionable insights for optimizing breeding strategies and cultivation practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of sequencing data, running complex parallelized simulations, and reducing computational bottlenecks in iterative model training. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes for targeted breeding, validated predictive models for yield optimization, and open-source tools for scalable agricultural analytics. This research will directly contribute to enhancing crop resilience, supporting global food security efforts, and providing a computational framework adaptable to other agronomically significant species. By bridging genomic insights with agronomic applications, the project aligns with the broader goals of advancing plant sciences through data-driven innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding, cultivation, and production of agricultural plants, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural plant products. Includes instruction in the plant sciences, crop cultivation and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation within Chinese diaspora communities through large-scale textual and visual datasets. The study addresses a critical gap in contemporary Chinese Studies by examining how diasporic groups negotiate cultural heritage across generations, particularly through vernacular media, community archives, and digital platforms, which remain underexplored due to the technical challenges of processing multilingual, multimedia materials at scale. The project will utilize computational text analysis, image recognition, and network analysis to process over 10,000 digitized items—including personal correspondence, oral history transcripts, community newsletters, and grassroots art—from 20th-century Chinese migrant communities in Southeast Asia and North America. Custom transformer-based models will be fine-tuned for historical vernacular Chinese and regional dialects to perform sentiment analysis, thematic clustering, and intertextual linkage detection, while computer vision pipelines will classify visual motifs in self-published artworks and photographs. These computational workflows will be integrated with spatial and temporal metadata to map shifting expressions of identity against geopolitical events and transnational policy changes. The scale of data, need for parallel processing of heterogeneous formats, and iterative training of multimodal machine learning models necessitate HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. Anticipated outcomes include the first longitudinal framework for quantifying cultural retention and hybridization in diaspora studies, a public corpus of annotated materials for interdisciplinary reuse, and methodological advances in applying HPC to non-Western, non-canonical cultural datasets. By revealing patterns in grassroots identity negotiation often obscured in state-centric or institutional narratives, this work aims to refocus scholarly discourse on agency and adaptation within transnational Chinese communities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of present-day China and its historical predecessors, related borderlands and island groups, and the overseas Chinese diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Islamic theological and legal concepts across time, regions, and interpretive traditions. The research addresses a critical challenge in Islamic Studies: systematically tracing how foundational texts—such as the Qur’an, Hadith, and classical juridical commentaries—have been interpreted, contested, and adapted by scholars in diverse cultural contexts. Traditional methods struggle to process the vast corpus of multilingual manuscripts, marginalia, and secondary literature, which span over 1,400 years and encompass Arabic, Persian, Ottoman Turkish, and other languages. The project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning to map semantic shifts in key doctrinal terms, identify patterns in scholarly citation networks, and model the diffusion of legal rulings (fatāwā) across geographic and sectarian boundaries. Customized NLP pipelines will be developed to handle classical Arabic morphology and transliterated texts, while graph-based algorithms will reconstruct intellectual lineages among scholars. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, the team will process terabytes of digitized manuscripts from repositories such as al-Maktaba al-Shamela and OpenITI, enabling large-scale comparative analysis previously unfeasible with manual methods. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking doctrinal developments to sociohistorical contexts, quantitative models of interpretive authority in Sunni and Shia traditions, and new frameworks for understanding Islam’s intellectual pluralism. This work will advance methodological innovation in the digital humanities, provide resources for cross-disciplinary religious studies, and inform contemporary discourses on Islamic legal reasoning and theological continuity. The computational demands of training multilingual transformer models, conducting graph simulations at scale, and managing heterogeneous textual data necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to ensure timely execution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Islam as preached by the Prophet Muhammad in 6th century Arabia and subsequently interpreted and elaborated by Islamic scholars and others; together with the cultural and social milieu related to the faith in various periods, localities, and branches. Includes instruction in Islamic scripture and related written authorities and commentaries

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of legislative gridlock and coalition formation in the contemporary U.S. Congress. A central challenge in American politics lies in understanding how polarization, procedural rules, and shifting party alignments interact to shape legislative outcomes. While existing studies rely on simplified models or aggregate data, this research proposes a computational framework to simulate legislative decision-making at scale, integrating formal game-theoretic models with empirically grounded agent-based simulations. The project will model individual legislators as adaptive agents with preferences derived from historical voting records, constituency demographics, and campaign finance data. Interactions between agents, committees, and party leadership will be simulated under varying procedural conditions (e.g., filibuster rules, discharge petitions) to assess how institutional designs mediate partisan conflict. A key innovation involves using natural language processing (NLP) to dynamically update agent preferences based on real-time analysis of congressional speech, press releases, and social media. The computational intensity of running thousands of stochastic simulations across multi-dimensional parameter spaces—combined with large-scale NLP tasks—necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing and data management. Expected outcomes include identifying institutional leverage points that reduce gridlock, quantifying the conditional effects of procedural reforms, and generating predictive insights about coalition stability in future Congresses. Results will contribute to political science scholarship on institutional design while providing empirically grounded perspectives on debates about congressional reform. By bridging theoretical models with behavioral data, this project aims to advance computational social science methodologies within the study of American government.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of United States political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in American political theory, political parties and interest groups, state and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, necessitating advancements in electrocardiograph (ECG) diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. Current clinical workflows for ECG interpretation face challenges in scalability, particularly when analyzing high-volume datasets or subtle arrhythmic patterns that may evade manual detection. This project proposes the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced ECG analysis platform to automate and refine cardiac rhythm classification, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome computational barriers. The research problem centers on optimizing machine learning (ML) models for real-time, high-fidelity ECG signal processing while addressing noise variability, patient-specific physiological differences, and rare arrhythmia detection. The computational approach integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures trained on multi-institutional ECG datasets, including 12-lead recordings and ambulatory monitor outputs. HPC resources will enable large-scale hyperparameter tuning, distributed training across GPU nodes, and validation against a repository of over 500,000 anonymized patient traces. Parallel processing frameworks will be employed to simulate real-world clinical scenarios, including artifact suppression and adaptive model calibration for diverse patient demographics. Expected outcomes include a deployable ML pipeline capable of identifying 30+ cardiac rhythm categories with ≥98% specificity, reducing false-positive alerts by 40% compared to existing commercial algorithms. The project will further generate open-source tools for ECG signal preprocessing and synthetic data augmentation, addressing privacy-preserving model training challenges. By enhancing diagnostic precision and operational throughput, this work directly aligns with the Electrocardiograph Technology program’s emphasis on improving patient care through technological innovation. The computational infrastructure requested will also support educational initiatives, enabling students to engage with cutting-edge AI applications in cardiovascular diagnostics while maintaining compliance with healthcare data governance standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) are leading causes of liver-related mortality, yet their molecular underpinnings remain incompletely characterized. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the dynamic interactions between genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental factors driving disease progression. We propose a computational framework integrating bulk and single-cell multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility) from human liver biopsies and murine models to identify conserved regulatory networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing >10 TB of sequencing data, performing parallelized alignment, variant calling, and chromatin peak detection across 800+ samples. Machine learning models will be trained to classify disease states using chromatin conformation (Hi-C) data and predict transcription factor binding sites governing fibro-inflammatory pathways. Agent-based modeling will simulate hepatocyte-stellate cell crosstalk under varying metabolic stress conditions, requiring GPU-accelerated simulations of 100,000+ interacting cellular agents. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive atlas of non-coding regulatory elements linked to HCC/MASH progression, (2) mechanistic insights into lipid metabolism-associated epigenetic reprogramming, and (3) candidate combination therapy targets validated through in silico perturbation of prioritized networks. This resource will enable unprecedented resolution of spatial transcriptomic patterns in cirrhotic nodules and facilitate the development of combinatorial therapeutic strategies. The computational infrastructure will be shared via a cloud-based portal for the hepatology community, directly addressing the NIH’s mandate for scalable analytical frameworks in precision hepatology. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to accelerate biomarker discovery and inform clinical trial designs for at-risk populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hepatology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing water distribution and waste removal systems in residential and commercial plumbing networks. Current methodologies for designing and maintaining piping systems rely heavily on static codes and generalized empirical data, which often fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, pipe corrosion rates, or transient pressure waves in complex networks. The research problem centers on integrating real-time sensor data, fluid dynamics simulations, and machine learning to create adaptive models that improve system resilience, reduce water waste, and preemptively identify failure points. Computational workflows will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating stress distributions in pipe materials under varying thermal and mechanical loads, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model water flow efficiency and sediment accumulation, and graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on historical failure datasets to predict vulnerabilities in networked systems. These multi-scale simulations require HPC resources to process large spatial-temporal datasets, resolve fine-grained interactions in 3D pipe geometries, and iteratively optimize system designs under thousands of operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for plumbers and engineers to simulate system upgrades, validate code compliance computationally, and prioritize maintenance interventions. By bridging computational engineering with applied plumbing practices, this work aims to reduce infrastructure costs, extend system lifespans, and mitigate public health risks from leaks or contamination. The project will also generate training modules to integrate computational literacy into plumbing technology curricula, fostering a workforce capable of deploying data-driven solutions in the trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice as licensed plumbers by applying technical knowledge and skills to lay out, assemble, install, and maintain piping fixtures and systems for steam, natural gas, oil, hot water, heating, cooling, drainage, lubricating, sprinkling, and industrial processing systems in home and business environments. Includes instruction in source determination, water distribution, waster removal, pressure adjustment, basic physics, technical mathematics, blueprint reading, pipe installation, pumps, welding and soldering, plumbing inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the impact of adaptive music pedagogy strategies on student engagement and skill acquisition in K–12 classrooms. Despite advances in music education research, there remains a critical gap in understanding how real-time adjustments to teaching methods—such as modifying lesson pacing, repertoire complexity, or feedback delivery—affect learning outcomes across diverse student populations. Traditional observational studies struggle to model the dynamic, multivariate interactions between instructional choices and student responses. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that integrates machine learning, acoustic signal processing, and agent-based modeling. The system will ingest multimodal datasets from classroom recordings (audio, video, and student performance metrics) to train generative models of teacher-student interactions. These models will simulate virtual classrooms with varying demographic, socioeconomic, and cognitive profiles, enabling large-scale parameter sweeps to test pedagogical strategies under controlled yet realistic conditions. Computational demands include parallelized processing of terabyte-scale audio-visual datasets for feature extraction, GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for predicting engagement patterns, and ensemble simulations of 10,000+ student agents with individualized learning trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model linking specific teaching interventions to quantifiable skill development metrics, (2) an open-source toolkit for optimizing lesson plans based on student cohort characteristics, and (3) novel insights into the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying music skill transfer. By leveraging HPC resources, this work will provide empirically grounded frameworks to enhance music teacher training programs, directly addressing the program’s mission to improve instructional quality in music education. The scalability of our approach will additionally permit future expansion to study longitudinal teaching effectiveness across multi-year curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach music and music appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the interplay between individualized metabolic heterogeneity and dietary response variability, with a focus on optimizing clinical nutrition strategies for chronic disease management. Current dietary recommendations often adopt generalized approaches, which fail to account for inter-individual differences in metabolic pathways, gut microbiome composition, and epigenetic regulation. This gap limits the efficacy of nutrition interventions for conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disorders. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (metabolomic, metagenomic, and epigenomic profiles) with dynamic systems modeling to predict patient-specific responses to macronutrient manipulation. The project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate metabolic flux variations across virtual patient cohorts, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal clinical datasets to identify biomarkers of dietary responsiveness. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses to account for the combinatorial complexity of nutrient interactions, high-dimensional data integration, and stochastic variability in physiological systems. Expected outcomes include the development of a predictive tool to guide personalized dietary prescriptions and the identification of novel metabolic targets for precision nutrition therapies. This work bridges computational biology, systems nutrition, and clinical dietetics, offering a transformative approach to evidence-based nutrition care that aligns with emerging paradigms in precision medicine. The computational pipelines and models generated will be made publicly available to support future research in niche areas of clinical nutrition science.
cip_title: Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dietetics and clinical nutrition services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for high-efficiency, low-emission engines in automotive and commercial vehicles necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize engine design, machining processes, and material performance. Current methods for engine reconstruction and component machining rely heavily on empirical testing and iterative physical prototyping, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to predict complex interactions between thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamic factors. This project proposes a computational research initiative to model and simulate critical engine machining and assembly processes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) developing multi-physics simulations of engine component behavior under operational stresses, including thermal expansion, fatigue, and wear patterns; (2) optimizing machining parameters for crankshafts, cylinder blocks, and pistons through finite element analysis (FEA) of material removal processes; and (3) employing machine learning algorithms to predict the outcomes of crack repair and surface finishing techniques across diverse engine configurations. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project will enable high-resolution modeling of microstructural changes during machining, transient thermal gradients in diesel versus gasoline systems, and fluid-structure interactions in lubrication pathways. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for component longevity, data-driven guidelines for machining tolerances, and a digital twin framework for virtual engine assembly validation. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in the Engine Machinist program while providing industry partners with scalable computational tools to reduce prototyping costs and accelerate sustainable engine development. The requested computing resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the storage of terabyte-scale datasets encompassing material properties, toolpath geometries, and operational scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the building and reconstruction of automotive and commercial vehicle engines. Includes instruction in cylinder head and block, crack repair, crankshaft inspection and repair, connecting rods and pistons, balancing, block preparation, disassembly and repair, engine assembly, gas and diesel technology, and inspection and machining.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing domain-specific programming workflows in high-dimensional parameter spaces, targeting applications in experimental design automation for materials science. The research addresses the challenge of efficiently navigating complex, non-linear design landscapes where traditional combinatorial optimization methods become computationally intractable due to the exponential growth of possible configurations. We propose a hybrid approach combining constrained neural architecture search with multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization, specifically adapted for heterogeneous computing architectures. The computational methodology will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor operations for rapid candidate evaluation and implement asynchronous parallelism to manage disparate simulation timescales inherent in multi-physics models. Key innovations include adaptive batching strategies for mixed-precision calculations and runtime compilation techniques to minimize memory overhead in large-scale parameter sweeps. The project requires high-performance computing resources to support three primary components: 1) distributed training of surrogate models across multiple nodes, 2) concurrent execution of physics-based simulations at varying resolution levels, and 3) validation through comparative analysis against existing experimental datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated experimental protocol generation, demonstrated on perovskite solar cell design optimization as a benchmark case. This work aims to establish new best practices for resource-aware computational design in applied scientific programming, potentially reducing typical exploration timescales from months to days while maintaining physical interpretability constraints. Successful implementation would provide a template for translating complex material property relationships into executable experimental pipelines across multiple domains of applied computational science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of general computer programming to the solution of specific operational problems and customization requirements presented by individual software users and organizational users. Includes training in specific types of software and its installation and maintenance.

abstract: Wildland fires present complex, dynamic challenges requiring advanced predictive models and forensic analysis to enhance mitigation, response, and investigation efforts. Current fire behavior models often lack sufficient resolution to account for multiscale interactions between fire dynamics, atmospheric conditions, heterogeneous fuels, and terrain—a gap that limits real-time decision-making and post-event forensic accuracy. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to advance wildfire simulation and investigation capabilities. The research will integrate coupled fire-atmosphere modeling using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with machine learning (ML) techniques to resolve fine-scale fire spread processes, ember transport, and suppression impacts under varying meteorological and fuel conditions. High-resolution satellite imagery, LiDAR-derived terrain data, and historical fire records will parameterize simulations, while ensemble methods will quantify prediction uncertainties. For forensic applications, the project will employ graph-based algorithms and ML-driven pattern recognition to analyze ignition sources, burn patterns, and arson-related spatial data. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of 3D wildfire simulations, which require parallelized solvers for reacting flow equations, and the processing demands of large geospatial datasets. Expected outcomes include improved fire spread prediction accuracy for operational use during active incidents, optimized fuel management strategies, and enhanced forensic tools for arson detection. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to directly support firefighter safety, resource allocation, and post-fire investigations, contributing to the broader goals of wildfire resilience and homeland security.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science, firefighting and investigation to the prevention, control and mitigation of wildland fires and the analysis of causes. Includes instruction in fire science and behavior, wildland environments, meteorology, wildland fire hydraulics and dynamics, water and chemical supply systems, wildland firefighting operations, airborne firefighting, firebreak engineering, communications systems, wildland arson, forensic procedures, wildland fire prevention, investigation techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling and optimizing microbial consortia in engineered biosystems, a critical barrier to advancing scalable bioenergy production and precision bioremediation. Microbial communities exhibit intricate metabolic interactions that dictate system efficiency, but their dynamic behavior under variable environmental conditions remains poorly understood. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in resolving real-time, multi-scale interactions, while existing computational models often oversimplify community dynamics or lack the resolution to predict emergent properties. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), genome-scale metabolic networks, and machine learning (ML). The ABM component will simulate spatial and temporal interactions among microbial species at the individual cell level, incorporating stochastic gene expression and metabolite exchange. Genome-scale flux balance analysis will be dynamically coupled to ABM agents to model metabolic trade-offs under nutrient gradients. Concurrently, ML algorithms will iteratively refine model parameters using experimental datasets from bioreactor metagenomics, transcriptomics, and extracellular metabolite profiling. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of microbial networks, parallelize stochastic simulations across thousands of cores, and train high-dimensional ML models. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform for designing synthetic microbial consortia with tunable stability and metabolic output, directly applicable to optimizing anaerobic digestion systems and pollutant-degrading biofilms. This work will advance fundamental understanding of emergent behaviors in engineered biological systems while providing a computational toolkit for accelerating the design-build-test cycle in biosystems engineering. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project bridges critical gaps between microbial ecology theory and scalable biotechnological applications.
detailed_field: Biological/ biosystems engineering and biomedical technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and management of biological systems; and includes applications to biology, biochemistry, ecology, and microbiology. Includes instruction in organic chemistry; microbiology; biochemistry; chemical, biological, biochemical, and process engineering; thermodynamics; process control; kinetics and reactor design; electric circuits; biosystem modeling; and bioelectronics and instrumentation.

abstract: Regulatory science faces increasing challenges in evaluating the safety and efficacy of novel biomedical products, particularly as innovations in gene therapies, personalized medicine, and AI-driven medical devices introduce unprecedented complexity. Traditional regulatory workflows struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including multi-omics, real-world evidence, and manufacturing quality metrics—while ensuring compliance with evolving FDA frameworks. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize regulatory decision-making by simulating product lifecycle outcomes under diverse scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train machine learning algorithms on historical regulatory submissions, clinical trial data, and post-market surveillance records to identify predictors of approval timelines and compliance risks. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between sponsors, regulators, and healthcare systems, incorporating stochastic variations in review processes and market dynamics. Computational pipelines will integrate natural language processing of regulatory documents with quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models for biologics characterization. The scale of data—terabytes of structured regulatory filings, omics datasets, and real-world evidence—necessitates parallelized computing for timely analysis. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool to forecast regulatory pathways, quantify risk-benefit tradeoffs, and recommend evidence-generation strategies for emerging product categories. This work will advance regulatory science by enabling data-driven approaches to balance innovation acceleration with patient safety. Successful implementation could reduce development costs for sponsors while strengthening quality management systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations and training deep learning models on sensitive, de-identified regulatory datasets in secure environments compliant with 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the regulatory process for companies innovating and developing cutting edge products in science, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Includes instruction in regulatory affairs, clinical documentation, human and animal subject protection, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, data management and analysis, good manufacturing practices, and quality management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize the sensory, operational, and economic dynamics of cocktail creation and bar management—an underexplored domain at the intersection of hospitality, human sensory perception, and supply chain logistics. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven methodologies in mixology, where ingredient selection, flavor balancing, and inventory decisions remain largely heuristic, leading to inefficiencies in cost control, waste reduction, and customer satisfaction. Current approaches in beverage service management rely on static recipes and manual demand forecasting, which fail to adapt to dynamic variables such as seasonal ingredient availability, shifting consumer preferences, or real-time sales patterns. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-parameter systems underlying bar operations. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling to predict flavor perception across diverse demographic groups, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic inventory optimization, and graph neural networks to map ingredient synergies from historical sales and sensory review datasets. The models will integrate physicochemical properties of beverages (e.g., viscosity, volatile compound diffusion) with behavioral and operational data, requiring parallelized processing of heterogeneous datasets spanning chemistry, sensory science, and transactional records. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for dynamic recipe optimization, waste prediction algorithms to minimize perishable stock loss, and a generative AI module for novel cocktail development constrained by regional ingredient availability. By establishing a computational foundation for data-driven mixology, this work aims to redefine resource efficiency in hospitality contexts while preserving the craft’s artistic integrity. The project’s computational demands—particularly in training multi-modal models and simulating stochastic operational scenarios—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve scalability and real-world applicability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally prepare mixed alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and related products and manage bars, lounges, and beverage service operations in the hospitality industry.  Includes instruction in mixology, oenology, accounting and cash management, inventory and cellar management, bar and lounge management, applicable laws and regulations, customer service, and labor/employment regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing dynamic pricing strategies in multi-agent, real-time market environments characterized by incomplete information and stochastic demand. Traditional pricing models often rely on static equilibria or simplified game-theoretic assumptions, limiting their applicability in volatile markets where decentralized actors—such as gig economy platforms, automated traders, and IoT-enabled supply chains—compete with asymmetric data. The core challenge lies in modeling adaptive agent behaviors while integrating high-frequency external data streams (e.g., sentiment analysis, logistics disruptions) to simulate emergent market dynamics. To address this, we propose a hybrid methodology combining agent-based modeling, distributed stochastic optimization, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to iteratively refine pricing policies under uncertainty. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling two parallel computational tasks: (1) massive Monte Carlo simulations of agent interactions across synthetic and historical market regimes, and (2) training multi-agent DRL architectures using partitioned environments to avoid reward function collisions. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated libraries for matrix-free optimization and graph neural networks to capture cross-agent dependencies. Expected outcomes include a benchmark dataset of simulated market trajectories under varying coordination mechanisms and an open-source toolkit for testing pricing resilience to systemic shocks. By quantifying how computational resource allocation impacts convergence in decentralized learning systems, this work aims to advance decision-making paradigms in emergent business contexts where traditional operations research models fail to account for adaptive, data-driven competitors. Successful implementation could inform regulatory frameworks for algorithmic collusion avoidance while providing enterprises with adaptive tools for high-velocity markets. The requested HPC infrastructure—particularly multi-node clusters with low-latency interconnects and specialized accelerators—is essential given the project’s O(n³) complexity scaling with agent populations and real-time inference requirements.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the application of statistical modeling, data warehousing, data mining, programming, forecasting and operations research techniques to the analysis of problems of business organization and performance. Includes instruction in optimization theory and mathematical techniques, data mining, data warehousing, stochastic and dynamic modeling, operations analysis, and the design and testing of prototype systems and evaluation models.

abstract: Clinical social work interventions in healthcare settings require tailored strategies to address the complex psychosocial needs of patients, yet current methods for predicting intervention outcomes or optimizing care plans remain limited by fragmented data and insufficient computational tools. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate predictive models that integrate multidimensional patient data—including electronic health records, psychosocial assessments, and social determinants of health—to improve intervention personalization and effectiveness. The research problem centers on the challenge of synthesizing heterogeneous, high-volume datasets to identify patterns in patient responses to clinical social work interventions, particularly for populations with co-occurring medical, mental health, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities. Using machine learning techniques such as ensemble classifiers and neural networks, the computational approach will analyze retrospective patient data to model relationships between intervention types, contextual factors, and health outcomes. Agent-based simulations will further test hypothetical intervention scenarios in dynamic, systems-level environments. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing large-scale datasets (>100,000 patient records), training computationally intensive models, and running iterative simulations with varying parameters. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-impact intervention components, risk stratification tools for clinical decision support, and a framework for simulating the long-term effects of psychosocial interventions on hospital readmission rates and patient well-being. This work will advance evidence-based practices in medical social work by enabling data-driven, real-time adjustments to care plans and fostering collaboration between social workers and multidisciplinary healthcare teams. The resulting models and tools will be disseminated as open-source resources to support scalability and reproducibility in similar clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the specialized professional practice of social work, in collaboration with other health care professionals, in hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in social work, psychiatric case work, clinical interviewing techniques, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient testing and evaluation, patient and family counseling, social rehabilitation, patient care planning, record-keeping, and support services liaison.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in warehouse operations and maintenance through advanced computational modeling and optimization, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance decision-making in inventory management, equipment maintenance, and workflow design. Traditional methods for optimizing warehousing systems often rely on static models or simplified heuristics, which fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, equipment degradation, or real-time supply chain disruptions. The research problem centers on developing adaptive, data-driven frameworks capable of simulating large-scale warehouse environments and predicting operational bottlenecks with high fidelity. Using agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation, this project will replicate complex interactions between personnel, automated systems, and inventory flows under diverse scenarios. Parallelized optimization algorithms, including genetic algorithms and deep reinforcement learning, will be employed to iteratively refine maintenance schedules, inventory placement strategies, and equipment utilization protocols. High-performance computing is critical to process multi-terabyte datasets from IoT sensors, historical maintenance logs, and enterprise resource planning systems, enabling real-time anomaly detection in equipment performance and predictive failure analysis. The computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks to model dependencies between warehouse subsystems and stochastic optimization techniques to account for uncertainty in supply chain variables. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for warehouse operations, predictive maintenance algorithms with quantified error margins, and evidence-based resource allocation guidelines to minimize downtime. By enabling hyperparametric tuning of simulation models and reducing computational latency in optimization loops, HPC resources will directly contribute to operational cost reductions of 15–25% in simulated test cases. The resulting tools aim to set new benchmarks for resilience in warehousing systems while providing open-source computational frameworks for workforce training in maintenance technology programs.
cip_title: Parts and Warehousing Operations and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain inventory control, care for inventory, and make minor repairs to warehouse equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel framework for adaptive human-computer symbiosis in microtask-driven data workflows, addressing inefficiencies in traditional data entry systems that rely on rigid, error-prone manual input. Current approaches in microcomputer applications often fail to dynamically integrate user behavior patterns, environmental context, or real-time quality metrics, leading to high cognitive load and error rates in specialized domains such as clinical data curation or multilingual archival digitization. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble models that combine eye-tracking analytics, keystroke dynamics, and contextual semantic validation. These models will power an adaptive interface capable of predicting user intent, pre-filling context-aware templates, and flagging inconsistencies during data entry sessions. Computational workflows will leverage distributed GPU-accelerated architectures to process multimodal interaction data at millisecond latency, while federated learning techniques will preserve privacy when aggregating patterns across institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in task completion time and a 60% decrease in post-processing correction needs across pilot deployments in healthcare transcription and cultural heritage digitization. The project will yield open-source libraries for real-time microtask optimization, advancing the understudied intersection of cognitive ergonomics and edge computing in microcomputer applications. By establishing scalable methods for human-in-the-loop adaptation, this work aims to redefine data entry systems as collaborative processes rather than static transactional interfaces, with implications for workforce training, accessibility design, and low-resource language preservation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data entry/microcomputer applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize pedagogical strategies for cosmetology and barbering education, addressing the lack of data-driven tools tailored to vocational instructor training. Current methods for designing curricula and assessing student competency in cosmetology programs rely heavily on anecdotal experience and static lesson plans, which may not account for diverse learning trajectories or emerging trends in beauty techniques. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets—including student performance metrics, practical skill demonstration videos, and demographic profiles—and simulate adaptive learning environments. Machine learning models will identify patterns in skill acquisition rates, predict competency gaps, and evaluate the efficacy of instructional aids (e.g., augmented reality tutorials, haptic feedback tools). Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model virtual classroom dynamics to test how variations in teaching methods, class sizes, and pacing affect outcomes. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for large-scale data aggregation (spanning decades of licensure records) and real-time rendering of 3D simulations for tactile skill training. Expected outcomes include a generative AI toolkit to assist instructors in creating personalized lesson plans, a predictive dashboard for early identification of at-risk students, and evidence-based guidelines for integrating emerging technologies (e.g., VR hairstyling modules) into accreditation standards. By quantifying the relationship between instructional variables and student success, this work aims to elevate pedagogical precision in cosmetology education while establishing a scalable computational model for other vocational disciplines. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—synthesizing education theory, human-computer interaction, and cosmetology practice—exemplifies innovation in a non-traditional computing domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares cosmetologists, barbers, stylists, nail technicians, and other grooming specialists to teach their specializations in licensed and accredited schools of cosmetology and barbering, and to prepare for licensure as instructors.  Includes instruction in cosmetology arts and sciences teaching principles; student learning styles; professional curricula development; instructional planning; instructional methods and aids; student counseling and career assistance; test development; and classroom/clinic management.

abstract: Surgical nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to optimize patient outcomes in high-stakes environments. However, current approaches to predicting postoperative complications (e.g., surgical site infections, anesthesia-related adverse events) often rely on static risk scores that fail to integrate real-time intraoperative data streams or account for complex interactions between patient physiology, surgical workflows, and nurse interventions. This project proposes developing a dynamic predictive modeling framework to address these gaps using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will analyze multi-modal perioperative datasets, including electronic health records, intraoperative vital sign streams, surgical instrument logs, and nurse documentation from 15,000+ procedures across three academic medical centers. Machine learning models (ensemble methods, temporal convolutional networks) will be trained to identify early warning signatures for complications and simulate the impact of nursing interventions on risk trajectories. Computational challenges include managing high-frequency time-series data, addressing class imbalance in rare outcomes, and ensuring model interpretability for clinical teams. The HPC environment is critical for parallel hyperparameter optimization, large-scale cross-validation, and real-time simulation of surgical scenarios to stress-test decision protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive tools to guide nurse-led interventions during critical surgical phases, (2) optimized workflow recommendations for instrument preparation and sterile field management, and (3) open-source code for adaptive clinical decision support. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process complex surgical datasets, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in perioperative nursing while maintaining rigorous computational reproducibility standards. Results will inform both clinical practice and nursing education modules on data-enhanced surgical care.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of digital engagement and spiritual formation among adolescents in contemporary youth ministry contexts. As digital platforms increasingly mediate religious practices, ministry leaders face challenges in understanding how online interactions—such as virtual worship, social media discourse, and AI-driven pastoral tools—shape youth identity, community belonging, and ethical decision-making. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the scale and nonlinearity of these interactions, necessitating computational approaches. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze multi-modal datasets, including anonymized text from youth-led prayer forums, video transcripts of virtual small-group sessions, and longitudinal survey responses measuring spiritual resilience. Agent-based modeling will simulate how algorithmic content delivery on platforms like TikTok and Discord influences the spread of theological ideas within adolescent networks. Additionally, graph neural networks will map evolving peer influence patterns across hybrid (online/in-person) ministry ecosystems. By integrating computational social science with practical theology, this project aims to identify scalable strategies for mitigating digital polarization while fostering inclusive spiritual growth. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time analysis of youth engagement metrics, predictive models to optimize ministry resource allocation, and ethical guidelines for AI-augmented pastoral care. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training deep learning architectures on sensitive conversational datasets, and running large-scale simulations of emergent community behaviors. This interdisciplinary work bridges gaps between humanities research, adolescent psychology, and computational innovation, offering novel methodologies for faith-based organizations navigating rapidly evolving digital landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to children, adolescents, and young adults. Includes instruction in child and adolescent psychology, human growth and development, family studies, communication skills, religious education, youth counseling, small group leadership, planning and organizing youth activities, volunteer supervision, and youth evangelism and worship.

abstract: Oral diseases, including periodontitis and oral cancer, are driven by complex interactions between genetic, microbial, and environmental factors. Despite advances in clinical dentistry, the mechanistic underpinnings of these interactions remain poorly understood, limiting the development of targeted diagnostics and therapies. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multifactorial disease dynamics and predict patient-specific outcomes. We propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data—including host genomics, salivary proteomics, and oral microbiome metagenomics—with clinical variables to identify biomarkers and mechanistic pathways. Machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained on heterogeneous datasets to stratify disease subtypes and forecast treatment responses. Agent-based modeling will simulate microbial community behaviors under varying host immune conditions, while finite element analysis will assess biomechanical stress impacts on oral tissues in degenerative diseases. These computationally intensive workflows require parallel processing, large-scale data storage, and GPU acceleration to manage terabytes of sequencing data, optimize hyperparameters across thousands of iterations, and run stochastic simulations at biologically relevant scales. Expected outcomes include predictive models for early disease detection, personalized intervention strategies, and mechanistic insights into oral microbiome-host crosstalk. By elucidating context-specific disease drivers, this research aims to advance precision dentistry and inform clinical guidelines for high-risk populations. The developed computational pipelines will also serve as a replicable foundation for future studies integrating complex biological data in dental research. Access to HPC resources is critical to overcome current limitations in processing capacity and enable transformative insights into oral disease pathogenesis.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the stability and efficiency of next-generation electrical power systems, with a focus on integrating renewable energy sources and advanced power electronics. The increasing complexity of modern grids—driven by variable renewable generation, distributed energy resources, and high-power semiconductor devices—demands high-fidelity modeling of dynamic interactions that traditional simulation tools cannot resolve in practical timeframes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics, multi-timescale simulation framework combining electromagnetic transients analysis, power flow optimization, and machine learning-driven stability prediction. The computational approach will employ parallelized finite element methods for modeling high-frequency switching dynamics in wide-bandgap semiconductor devices, coupled with distributed optimization algorithms to solve non-convex optimal power flow problems across large-scale networks. Machine learning models will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to predict transient stability margins under stochastic operating conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models for real-time stability assessment of hybrid AC/DC grids, (2) open-source tools for co-simulation of power electronic converters and transmission networks, and (3) scalable optimization strategies for grid resilience against renewable intermittency. This work will directly support the design of adaptive protection systems and inform standards for grid-forming inverter technologies, addressing a key bottleneck in global renewable energy integration. The requested computing resources are essential for handling tera-scale parameter spaces in device-circuit-network co-design, enabling millisecond-resolution simulations over hour-long horizons, and accelerating neural network training on heterogeneous grid topologies. Results will advance foundational knowledge in power systems computation while providing practical frameworks for utilities and manufacturers transitioning to low-inertia, high-renewable power systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components, including electrical power generation systems; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification.

abstract: The persistence of health disparities in chronic disease outcomes remains a critical challenge in public health, driven by complex interactions between social determinants, environmental exposures, and clinical care access. Traditional analytical approaches often struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets spanning these domains, limiting the ability to identify modifiable risk factors and prioritize interventions. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable analytical framework integrating electronic health records, geospatial data, and socioeconomic indicators from urban populations. Computational methods will include machine learning models to identify predictive signatures of disease risk and agent-based simulations to evaluate the population-level impact of hypothetical policy interventions. The analysis will focus on cardiometabolic diseases in underserved communities, utilizing multi-source data harmonization techniques and GPU-accelerated algorithms to handle datasets exceeding 10 million patient-years. Expected outcomes include the identification of neighborhood-level factors contributing to disparities, predictive models for targeted screening programs, and simulation-based evidence for cost-effective intervention strategies. By enabling the synthesis of heterogeneous data at unprecedented scales, this research aims to advance precision public health approaches and provide actionable insights for reducing health inequities. The requested computing resources are essential for processing large-scale datasets within feasible timeframes and conducting computationally intensive simulations that inform real-world policy decisions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public health, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Critical care nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to manage patients with life-threatening conditions, yet current methods for analyzing complex, high-dimensional clinical data remain limited. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that optimize real-time clinical decision support in critical care settings. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records (EHRs), continuous vital sign monitoring, and laboratory results—to identify early warning signals of clinical deterioration, predict patient-specific responses to interventions, and model the efficacy of treatment protocols under varying physiological conditions. Current computational tools struggle to process these datasets at scale, particularly when analyzing time-sensitive, multimodal data in dynamic ICU environments. To address this, the project will employ machine learning (ML) algorithms, such as ensemble models and deep neural networks, to identify patterns in retrospective EHR data from adult, neonatal, and pediatric ICUs. Parallel computing will enable large-scale parameter optimization for these models, while agent-based simulations will test hypothetical clinical scenarios, such as sepsis progression or ventilator weaning protocols. The HPC infrastructure will also support real-time data processing pipelines to validate models against prospective ICU data. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for early detection of complications (e.g., acute respiratory failure, septic shock) and evidence-based recommendations for personalized intervention thresholds. By enhancing the precision and speed of clinical assessments, this work aims to reduce preventable mortality, shorten ICU stays, and improve resource allocation in critical care units. The computational frameworks developed will be scalable to diverse healthcare systems, offering a template for data-driven innovation in nursing practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide specialized care to patients with life-threatening problems, including those in intensive care facilities and on life support. Includes instruction in adult, neonatal, and pediatric critical care; technical skills; patient monitoring and assessment; normal and abnormal readings; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the adaptive strategies of multidenominational religious institutions in navigating evolving legal and administrative landscapes, particularly in contexts where secular regulations intersect with doctrinal principles. The research problem centers on understanding how such institutions reconcile compliance with legal frameworks—such as data privacy laws, labor regulations, and nonprofit governance standards—while maintaining theological integrity and operational coherence. Existing scholarship often addresses doctrinal or historical dimensions of religious institutions but lacks systematic analysis of their administrative decision-making under legal constraints. To address this gap, the project employs a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing large corpora of legal documents, institutional policies, and archival records, enabling semantic analysis of regulatory texts and comparative mapping of policy adaptations across denominations. ABM simulations will model decision-making dynamics within administrative bodies, incorporating variables such as doctrinal rigidity, stakeholder influence, and legal risk tolerance. The integration of these methods aims to identify patterns in institutional adaptability and predict responses to emerging regulatory challenges. Expected outcomes include a framework for assessing policy alignment between religious and legal norms, predictive tools for institutional compliance planning, and a publicly accessible dataset of annotated legal-religious policy interactions. This research holds significance for both academic and practical domains, offering interdisciplinary insights into governance at the intersection of law and religion while providing actionable guidance for religious institutions operating in pluralistic legal environments.
cip_title: Religious Institution Administration and Law, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious institution administration and law, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Veterinary administrative services face growing challenges in managing complex operational workflows, data interoperability, and resource allocation across increasingly digitized clinical environments. This project seeks to address inefficiencies in veterinary administrative decision-making by developing predictive computational models to optimize resource distribution, staff scheduling, and inventory management in multi-service veterinary hospitals. The research problem centers on the lack of tailored analytical tools capable of processing heterogeneous administrative data streams—including electronic medical records, supply chain metrics, client communication logs, and financial transactions—while accounting for the unique constraints of animal healthcare ecosystems.
