Using high-performance computing resources, we propose to implement a hybrid architecture combining agent-based modeling, natural language processing of clinical notes, and time-series forecasting through recurrent neural networks. This computational approach will enable simulation of clinic operations under variable demand scenarios, automated extraction of diagnostic-procedure correlations from unstructured medical narratives, and predictive modeling of medical supply utilization patterns. The models will be trained on a deidentified dataset spanning 5 years of operations from 18 partner veterinary hospitals, comprising over 2.3 million patient encounters and associated administrative records. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time adaptive resource allocation that accounts for seasonal disease patterns, emergency caseload fluctuations, and specialized equipment utilization rates. The computational tools developed through this research aim to reduce operational costs by 12-18% in pilot implementations while maintaining compliance with veterinary medical ethics standards and data privacy regulations. By bridging gaps between veterinary practice management and advanced computational analytics, this project will establish new methodologies for data-driven administration in animal healthcare—a critical yet understudied domain requiring specialized infrastructure beyond conventional business informatics approaches.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative speech and partisan polarization in the Canadian Parliament using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on understanding how political rhetoric has evolved in response to shifting policy priorities, regional disparities, and federal-provincial tensions over the past three decades. While qualitative studies have explored these themes, existing scholarship lacks systematic analysis of large-scale parliamentary debate records to identify patterns in ideological positioning, coalition-building, and issue framing. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and time-series modeling applied to the complete corpus of House of Commons debates (1990–2023). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing over 10 million speech entries, training transformer-based language models to detect policy-specific sentiment and thematic clusters, and simulating interaction networks across party lines. The computational workflow will involve distributed text preprocessing (Apache Spark), GPU-accelerated model fine-tuning (BERT variants), and dynamic community detection algorithms to map changing alliances on key issues like climate policy, Indigenous reconciliation, and fiscal federalism. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database linking rhetorical strategies to legislative outcomes, 2) quantitative evidence of polarization thresholds that impede cross-partisan collaboration, and 3) machine learning tools adaptable for studying regional representation in committee systems. By revealing how computational social science methods can enhance institutional analysis, this project aims to provide actionable insights for improving parliamentary accountability and intergovernmental dialogue in Canada’s multi-level governance framework.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of Canadian political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in British and North American political theory, political parties and interest groups, provincial and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: The apparel and accessories industry faces mounting pressure to reconcile rapid trend cycles with sustainable practices, requiring agile operational strategies that minimize waste while maximizing customer engagement. Traditional demand forecasting and inventory management approaches struggle to account for real-time consumer sentiment, environmental impact metrics, and dynamic supply chain disruptions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating social media analytics, IoT-enabled customer interaction data, and multi-objective optimization to balance sustainability targets with commercial viability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid machine learning architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing (to extract latent sustainability preferences from user-generated content) and graph neural networks (to model interdependencies among suppliers, materials, and distribution channels). Concurrently, agent-based simulations will test inventory allocation strategies under varying carbon pricing scenarios and geopolitical constraints. The computational intensity of training these models on terabytes of unstructured text, image, and transactional data—while maintaining low-latency responses for real-time scenario planning—necessitates distributed computing capabilities. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between production lead times, textile waste reduction, and personalized marketing efficacy, validated against historical data from three multinational apparel retailers. By enabling simultaneous optimization of environmental impact and customer retention metrics, this research aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven operational sustainability in fashion marketing ecosystems, addressing a critical gap in applied computational business research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of apparel and accessories. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, apparel technologies, distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression and its associated complications present a significant clinical challenge, with molecular mechanisms underlying heterogeneous patient outcomes remaining poorly characterized. This project seeks to integrate multi-omics data—including genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—with clinical variables to identify predictive biomarkers and mechanistic drivers of CKD progression. A key limitation in prior studies is the inability to computationally model dynamic interactions across large-scale, high-dimensional datasets while accounting for patient-specific variables such as comorbidities and pharmacotherapy. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform integrative analyses of longitudinal datasets from 5,000 participants in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) study and multi-omics profiles from 1,200 renal biopsy specimens. The computational pipeline will employ graph neural networks to model molecular interaction networks, coupled with Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify uncertainty in cross-modal data integration. Molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted to characterize structural-functional relationships in kidney-specific protein variants identified through whole-exome sequencing. The scale of data (≥300 TB) and complexity of simulations (requiring >10,000 CPU-core hours weekly) necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallelized processing, real-time model optimization, and large-scale parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model stratifying CKD progression risk with ≥85% cross-validated accuracy, (2) identification of novel therapeutic targets within glomerular signaling pathways, and (3) open-source computational tools for nephrology biomarker discovery. By elucidating mechanisms of renal function decline, this work will directly inform clinical trial design for targeted therapies and advance precision medicine approaches in nephrology. The requested computing resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in data integration capacity and enabling real-time analytics for translational hypothesis testing.
cip_definition: Research focused on Nephrology

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in scalable, data-driven methodologies for evaluating ethical decision-making competencies in health professions education. Traditional approaches to assessing ethics training often rely on qualitative, small-scale analyses, which lack the capacity to model complex, real-world scenarios or generalize across diverse populations. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of a high-fidelity computational framework that integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate ethical dilemmas and evaluate learner responses in dynamic, multi-stakeholder healthcare environments. The ABM component will simulate interactions between virtual patients, clinicians, and learners under varying clinical, cultural, and resource-constrained conditions, generating synthetic datasets of ethical decision-making pathways. Concurrently, NLP algorithms will analyze longitudinal textual data from ethics case journals, simulation debriefs, and interdisciplinary team communications to identify patterns in moral reasoning and communication efficacy. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support large-scale parallel simulations, real-time rendering of complex clinical scenarios, and training of transformer-based language models on multimodal educational data. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model of ethical competency development, actionable insights into curriculum design, and an open-access toolkit for simulating culturally responsive ethics training scenarios. By enabling the systematic study of emergent ethical behaviors across heterogeneous populations, this work aims to advance equity-focused pedagogical strategies while establishing computational humanities as a transformative paradigm in health professions education.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project investigates the dynamics of trust formation and erosion in decentralized digital communities, an emerging social science niche intersecting computational social psychology, digital ethnography, and complex systems analysis. While traditional studies of social trust focus on physical communities or institutional frameworks, the proliferation of algorithmically mediated platforms—including blockchain-based governance systems, decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), and peer-to-peer knowledge networks—has created novel social architectures that challenge existing theoretical models. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how trust emerges, scales, and destabilizes in these contextually fluid, pseudonymous environments where conventional social cues are absent. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will analyze multi-modal behavioral traces from three active DAO ecosystems (totaling ~2.3TB of text, transaction, and voting data) through a novel computational framework combining three methods: 1) transformer-based NLP to map semantic networks in community discourse, 2) temporal graph neural networks to model evolving interaction patterns, and 3) agent-based simulations testing hypotheses about trust cascades under different incentive structures. The computational pipeline requires parallel processing of heterogeneous temporal graphs with >10^8 edges and training of domain-adapted large language models to detect subtle trust signals in multilingual technical discussions. Expected outcomes include a validated taxonomy of digital trust mechanisms, predictive models of community fragility thresholds, and an open-source toolkit for auditing decentralized governance systems. This work advances fundamental knowledge about human collaboration in post-institutional contexts while providing practical frameworks for designing more resilient socio-technical systems. Results will be disseminated through computational social science venues and Web3 development communities, bridging academic and practitioner perspectives on next-generation social organization.
cip_definition: A program that combines sociology and anthropology to study how society is organized, the origins and development of social institutions, social change, social organizations, race, class, gender and culture.

abstract: This project seeks to develop adaptive, data-driven instructional models for adult learners in non-traditional educational settings using machine learning and large-scale simulations. Adult learners face unique challenges, including heterogeneous educational backgrounds, time constraints, and varied skill retention patterns, which existing pedagogical frameworks often inadequately address. To address this, we propose analyzing multi-modal educational datasets—including longitudinal learning outcomes, engagement metrics from digital platforms, and demographic profiles—to identify patterns in skill acquisition and knowledge decay. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing these complex datasets (spanning 10,000+ learners across five institutional partners) and training neural networks to simulate personalized learning trajectories. Computational workflows will include clustering algorithms to categorize learner archetypes, natural language processing to analyze open-response feedback, and agent-based modeling to test intervention strategies in synthetic classroom environments. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of adult learner success under different instructional conditions, (2) optimized curriculum sequencing algorithms adaptable to workforce development contexts, and (3) open-source tools for simulating the impact of resource allocation decisions in continuing education programs. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will enable real-time analysis of dynamic interactions between instructional methods, learner characteristics, and institutional constraints—a computational challenge infeasible with standard infrastructure. Results will directly inform the design of modular teacher training materials focused on data-enhanced pedagogy for adult educators, addressing a critical gap in teacher education research. The project aligns with national priorities upskilling adult populations while demonstrating how computational methods can advance evidence-based practices in non-traditional teaching contexts.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_title: Adult and Continuing Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach adult students in various settings, including basic and remedial education programs, continuing education programs, and programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance numerical investigations of large-scale cosmic structure formation, with a focus on resolving tensions between theoretical predictions and observational data from galaxy surveys and the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Current cosmological models struggle to reconcile small-scale structure discrepancies, such as the observed diversity in galactic rotation curves and the overprediction of satellite galaxies in cold dark matter (CDM) simulations. To address this, we propose a suite of high-resolution, cosmological-scale simulations incorporating non-equilibrium radiation transfer, relativistic corrections, and multi-scale baryonic feedback processes. These simulations will utilize adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques within the ENZO and RAMSES frameworks to model galaxy cluster assembly and intracluster medium dynamics at unprecedented resolution, while self-consistently tracking radiation fields from active galactic nuclei and star-forming regions. A novel aspect involves coupling Monte Carlo radiative transfer algorithms with relativistic N-body solvers to account for light-cone effects in synthetic CMB maps derived from simulated large-scale structure. The computational demands are substantial, requiring petascale parallelism to handle ~10^10 particle ensembles and multi-physics couplings across 15 orders of magnitude in spatial scale. Anticipated outcomes include refined constraints on dark matter particle properties, improved templates for CMB foreground subtraction in next-generation surveys, and quantitative predictions for galaxy cluster morphology as testable targets for JWST and Euclid. By resolving the interplay between baryonic physics and dark matter halo evolution, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in our understanding of cosmic structure formation while providing open-source simulation datasets to support cross-disciplinary analysis in the cosmology community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical, observational, and numerical study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena of the universe on a large scale. Includes instruction in clusters of galaxies, the cosmic microwave background, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate advanced computational models to enhance the pedagogical strategies used in chemistry teacher education, addressing the challenge of effectively teaching dynamic chemical processes and molecular-level interactions. Traditional teaching methods often struggle to convey the complexity of real-time chemical phenomena, such as reaction mechanisms, equilibrium dynamics, or spectroscopic behavior, which are critical for student conceptual understanding. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and visualize these processes at unprecedented scales and resolutions. The research will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, quantum mechanical calculations (via density functional theory), and machine learning (ML)-driven analysis to generate interactive, adaptable teaching modules. These modules will model chemical systems under diverse conditions, enabling educators to demonstrate how variables like temperature, concentration, or catalyst design influence outcomes. Additionally, ML algorithms will process anonymized student interaction data from virtual labs to identify common misconceptions and optimize feedback mechanisms. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the computational load of parallelized MD trajectories, ab initio calculations across large molecular datasets, and training predictive ML models on heterogeneous educational data. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of validated, curriculum-aligned simulations; (2) quantitative frameworks linking simulation fidelity to learning gains in pre-service teacher assessments; and (3) AI-driven tools that help educators customize content based on learner needs. By integrating computational chemistry directly into teacher training, this work aims to establish scalable, evidence-based practices that empower chemistry educators to foster deeper conceptual mastery and engagement in their classrooms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach chemistry programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of individualized biomechanical optimization in athletic performance, an emerging interdisciplinary niche integrating sports science, computational modeling, and machine learning. Current approaches to injury prevention and performance enhancement in sports often rely on generalized population-level data, neglecting the nuanced biomechanical variability among athletes. This gap limits the development of personalized training regimens and rehabilitation protocols. To address this, the research will employ large-scale simulations of human movement dynamics using musculoskeletal modeling and finite element analysis, informed by high-resolution motion capture, physiological, and genetic datasets. The computational workflow will involve iterative optimization algorithms to map stress distributions across joints and soft tissues under varying load conditions, alongside deep learning models trained to predict injury risks and performance outcomes based on athlete-specific biomechanical profiles. By parallelizing these processes across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks inherent in real-time, multi-body simulations and enable rapid scenario testing. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for generating personalized biomechanical insights, which could inform adaptive training programs tailored to an athlete’s unique physiological constraints and competitive goals. This work bridges gaps between traditional sports science and advanced computational methodologies, offering novel tools for coaches, clinicians, and sports technologists. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s data-intensive demands, including the processing of terabyte-scale biomechanical datasets and the deployment of computationally expensive multi-physics simulations. Results will contribute to a growing body of research prioritizing precision in sports medicine and performance analytics, with potential applications in rehabilitation robotics, wearable technology design, and injury mitigation strategies for elite and recreational athletes alike.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sports, kinesiology, and physical education/fitness, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research aims to investigate the combinatorial structure of integer partitions and their associated rank statistics, a central problem in additive number theory. Despite significant advances in understanding partition congruences and asymptotic behavior, the distribution of partition ranks—introduced by Freeman Dyson to explain Ramanujan’s congruences—remains poorly characterized for large integers. Current conjectures posit deep connections between rank distributions, modular forms, and mock theta functions, but empirical validation has been limited by computational intractability. This project seeks to address these gaps by deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to systematically generate and analyze partition rank data at unprecedented scales. Using optimized parallel algorithms, we will compute the ranks of partitions for integers up to \(n \approx 10^6\), extending existing tabulations by orders of magnitude. These computations will leverage distributed-memory architectures to manage the exponential growth of partition counts, employing dynamic programming and combinatorial generation techniques optimized for GPU acceleration. The resulting datasets will be analyzed to test conjectures regarding rank equidistribution, sign balance phenomena, and connections to Maass forms. Additionally, the project will explore the existence of "hidden" congruences in rank statistics modulo small primes, which could refine the celebrated Andrews-Dyson-Hickerson framework. The outcomes are expected to provide rigorous empirical foundations for theoretical developments in partition theory, potentially uncovering new links between combinatorial and analytic number theory. By resolving long-standing questions about rank behavior, this work will enhance the toolkit for studying modular symmetries in additive functions and inform future conjectures in the field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of integers, integer-valued functions, including combinatorics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular dynamics of highly diluted homeopathic formulations using high-performance computing (HPC) to model solute-solvent interactions at ultrahigh dilutions (beyond Avogadro’s limit). Despite clinical usage, homeopathic remedies lack a robust physicochemical explanation for purported bioactivity, particularly in regimes where active solute molecules are absent. The research problem centers on characterizing nanoscale solvent structures or long-range ordering in aqueous solutions that may arise during succussion (serial dilution with agitation)—a process hypothesized to impart therapeutic information via persistent hydrogen-bond networks or epitaxial water clusters. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will model succussed solutions of exemplar substances (e.g., Arnica montana, silica) across dilution levels (6X to 30X), analyzing solvent conformational stability, interfacial phenomena, and emergent supramolecular patterns under varying agitation parameters. Quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods will assess electronic polarization effects. Parallelized simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to achieve millisecond-scale sampling for statistically robust trajectory analysis. Machine learning pipelines will classify agitation-induced structural signatures correlated with in vitro bioassay data from collaborating labs. Outcomes aim to identify reproducible solvent-level phenomena that differentiate homeopathic preparations from controls, providing a testable framework for the "memory of water" hypothesis. By bridging nanoscale modeling with empirical validation, this work could redefine the biophysical plausibility of homeopathic mechanisms while advancing computational methodologies for ultra-dilute systems. Results will inform optimized remedy production protocols and contribute foundational data to interdisciplinary debates on water structure-function relationships in therapeutic contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of homeopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic system using naturally occurring substances in highly diluted forms to mimic symptoms of illness and trigger autoimmune responses, based on the law of similars and other principles derived from the work of Samuel Hahnemann and others. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, toxicology, philosophy and theory of homeopathy, casetaking and case analysis, repertory, material medica, constitutional typing, proving, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address critical gaps in optimizing diagnostic workflows and therapeutic protocols for complex, multifactorial health conditions through advanced computational modeling. Allied health professionals frequently encounter challenges in integrating heterogeneous patient data—such as imaging, electronic health records (EHRs), and biomarker profiles—into timely, personalized interventions. Current manual and semi-automated approaches struggle to scale with growing data complexity, leading to delays and suboptimal outcomes. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that synthesize multimodal data into actionable clinical insights. The computational approach centers on three pillars: (1) training deep learning architectures on anonymized medical imaging datasets (e.g., MRI, CT scans) to detect subtle pathological patterns; (2) deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract structured information from unstructured EHR narratives; and (3) implementing agent-based simulations to model patient-specific responses to therapeutic interventions under varying physiological conditions. These components will be integrated into a unified framework validated against retrospective clinical data from partnering allied health facilities. The HPC environment is essential for handling large-scale datasets (>100 TB), parallelizing computationally intensive tasks (e.g., 3D image segmentation), and iteratively refining models through hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated computational toolkit to assist allied health practitioners in rapidly identifying high-risk patients, predicting intervention efficacy, and minimizing adverse events. The project will also generate open-source algorithms tailored to understudied conditions within allied health domains, such as chronic musculoskeletal disorders and neurorehabilitation pathways. By bridging data science and clinical practice, this work has the potential to significantly reduce diagnostic latency, improve resource allocation in therapy programs, and establish scalable methodologies for evidence-based decision support in diverse care settings.
cip_title: Allied Health Diagnostic, Intervention, and Treatment Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health diagnostic, intervention, and treatment professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural change and adaptation in globally interconnected societies through advanced computational modeling and analysis. Traditional ethnographic methods, while rich in qualitative depth, struggle to capture the scale, complexity, and real-time evolution of cultural systems in contexts shaped by digital communication, migration, and transnational exchange. The research problem centers on identifying patterns and mechanisms of cultural transmission, transformation, and resilience across heterogeneous populations, with a focus on how localized practices interact with globalizing forces. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop agent-based models simulating cultural exchange networks and to analyze large-scale, mixed-method datasets. The computational approach integrates three components: (1) network analysis of cross-cultural interaction patterns using anonymized social media and communication data, (2) natural language processing (NLP) of ethnographic interview transcripts and historical records to trace semantic shifts in cultural narratives, and (3) probabilistic modeling of cultural trait diffusion across simulated environments with variable constraints. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage high-dimensional data, execute parallelized simulations, and train machine learning models for pattern recognition in unstructured text. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for quantifying cultural hybridity and predictive models of cultural adaptation under scenarios of environmental or social disruption. The project will produce open-source tools for anthropologists to analyze cultural datasets at unprecedented scales while maintaining interpretive rigor. By bridging computational social science and anthropological theory, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in the discipline and generate insights relevant to challenges such as intercultural conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural diversity in rapidly changing societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of culture and the relationship of culture to other aspects of social life. Includes instruction in cultural anthropology, anthropological theory, ethnography, linguistics, and quantitative and qualitative research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive decision-support systems for high-stakes military operational environments through the integration of computational cognitive modeling and real-time data synthesis. Military decision-making increasingly occurs in complex, dynamic scenarios involving hybrid human-AI teams, yet existing frameworks struggle to account for the interplay between cognitive biases, environmental stressors, and machine-generated recommendations. The research problem centers on simulating and optimizing these interactions to enhance mission outcomes while mitigating risks associated with information overload and trust calibration. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-layered agent-based modeling approach that combines validated behavioral datasets with synthetic scenario generation. Computational methods will include (1) large-scale parallelized simulations of decision trajectories under variable stress conditions, (2) evolutionary algorithms to identify optimal human-AI task allocation patterns, and (3) neural network architectures for predicting critical inflection points in team performance degradation. The simulation environment will incorporate physiologically grounded models of fatigue, situational awareness, and decision latency, validated against experimental data from field exercises. Expected outcomes include a novel metric framework for assessing human-AI complementarity in time-constrained operations and actionable insights for designing next-generation tactical decision aids. By enabling the simultaneous processing of heterogeneous data streams—including biometric, environmental, and system telemetry—the requested HPC infrastructure will support unprecedented granularity in modeling human-machine team dynamics. This work addresses a critical gap in applied military sciences, where traditional human factors research has not kept pace with the computational demands of modern asymmetric threat environments. The resulting methodologies will inform both system design principles and operational doctrine for human-AI collaboration in defense applications.
cip_title: Military Technologies and Applied Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military technologies and applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and validation of computational models for optimizing personalized counseling interventions in diverse populations. Counseling psychology faces a critical challenge in tailoring therapeutic strategies to individual clients’ dynamic needs, particularly when addressing complex, overlapping distress symptoms (e.g., anxiety, relational conflicts, identity-related stressors) that vary across cultural and socioeconomic contexts. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between client characteristics, intervention techniques, and longitudinal outcomes. To address this, we propose building machine learning (ML) frameworks trained on multimodal datasets, including anonymized clinical session transcripts, client self-report metrics, and demographic data from supervised counseling practice archives. These models will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to analyze therapeutic dialogue patterns, graph neural networks to map symptom interdependencies, and reinforcement learning to simulate intervention adaptation over time. The scale of data (projected at 50,000+ session records) and complexity of modeling temporal, textual, and relational variables necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized training and large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to identify client subgroups most likely to benefit from specific counseling modalities, (2) a computational framework for simulating the longitudinal impacts of culturally adapted interventions, and (3) open-source algorithms to help practitioners refine case conceptualizations. By bridging counseling psychology’s human-centered ethos with computational rigor, this work aims to enhance equitable access to effective mental health support while maintaining ethical alignment with client autonomy and therapeutic relationship principles. The requested resources will enable iterative model development, including sensitivity analyses to mitigate algorithmic bias and ensure interpretability for clinical utility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of psychological counseling, involving the rendering of therapeutic services to individuals and groups experiencing psychological problems and exhibiting distress symptoms. Includes instruction in counseling theory, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient/counselor relationships, testing and assessment methods and procedures, group therapy, marital and family therapy, child and adolescent therapy, supervised counseling practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the supporting structures of teeth, is driven by complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and genetic and environmental factors. While advances in high-throughput sequencing and multi-omics technologies have generated vast datasets linking dysbiotic microbiomes and host pathways to disease progression, integrating these heterogeneous data to identify predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate host-microbial dynamics in periodontitis. Using longitudinal metagenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from clinical cohorts, we will apply machine learning frameworks to identify microbial consortia and inflammatory mediators associated with disease severity and treatment outcomes. Agent-based modeling will simulate spatial interactions between microbial biofilms, host immune cells, and tissue remodeling processes in the periodontium, incorporating patient-specific omics data to predict responses to mechanical or pharmacological interventions. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will explore how bacterial virulence factors interact with host cell receptors to modulate inflammation. These computational approaches require HPC resources to manage large-scale data integration, optimize predictive algorithms, and perform parallelized simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) a systems biology framework linking microbiome-host networks to clinical phenotypes, (2) predictive models for personalized treatment stratification, and (3) novel insights into mechanistic drivers of tissue destruction. By bridging computational biology and clinical periodontology, this work aims to advance precision therapies and improve long-term outcomes for patients with periodontitis. The scalability of these models will also establish a foundation for studying other oral-systemic inflammatory conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of efficiently processing and enhancing accessibility for large-scale, heterogeneous archival collections through the development of machine learning (ML) models optimized for automated metadata generation and contextual classification. As libraries and archives increasingly digitize physical holdings, the volume of unstructured or minimally described digital assets—including scanned documents, photographs, audiovisual materials, and born-digital records—has outpaced the capacity of traditional cataloging workflows. Manual processing of these materials is time-intensive, creating bottlenecks that delay public and scholarly access. To mitigate this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy ML models capable of analyzing multimodal data (text, images, audio) to infer descriptive metadata, detect contextual relationships, and recommend preservation actions. Computational methods will include transformer-based natural language processing for text extraction and entity recognition, convolutional neural networks for visual pattern detection in non-textual materials, and graph-based algorithms to map inter-resource connections. The scale and diversity of archival datasets—spanning centuries, languages, and formats—require distributed training across GPU nodes to manage memory-intensive tasks and ensure model generalizability. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit integrating these models into existing archival management systems, enabling semi-automated metadata augmentation, anomaly detection for preservation risks, and improved search granularity. By reducing manual labor in cataloging, this work aims to accelerate the availability of underrepresented or at-risk collections, support equitable access to cultural heritage, and establish scalable frameworks for emerging challenges in digital stewardship. The project bridges archival science, information management, and computational linguistics, advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for memory institutions in the digital age.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist professional librarians and archivists. Includes instruction in principles, systems, processes, and procedures of library and archive operation; library resources and services; processes of acquisition, cataloging, storage, and display systems; discovery and retrieval of requested materials; and management of books, periodicals, and other documents and records.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized learning pathways for middle school students in special education programs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational data. Students with disabilities often exhibit heterogeneous learning profiles, yet educators face challenges in efficiently integrating diverse data sources—such as academic performance, behavioral logs, individualized education program (IEP) goals, and real-time classroom interactions—to inform instructional decisions. Current tools lack the scalability to process these complex datasets or simulate longitudinal outcomes of pedagogical strategies. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline that processes structured and unstructured data (e.g., written teacher feedback, sensor-based engagement metrics) using natural language processing and time-series analysis. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of ensemble models to predict student progress across learning domains (e.g., literacy, numeracy) under varying intervention scenarios. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom-scale interactions, testing how resource allocation (e.g., assistive technology deployment, paraeducator support timing) affects both individualized and group outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate anonymized datasets from 15 middle school special education programs, comprising over 5,000 student-hours of observational and assessment data. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable tool for generating dynamic IEP recommendations based on predictive analytics, (2) quantified thresholds for intervention efficacy across disability categories, and (3) optimized scheduling strategies for special education classrooms derived from simulation results. This work will provide evidence-based frameworks to help teachers prioritize instructional targets, reduce trial-and-error in intervention design, and allocate limited classroom resources more effectively. By coupling educational theory with computational modeling, the project aims to advance data-driven practices in special education teacher preparation and middle school classroom implementation.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Junior High/ Middle School Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in junior high/middle school. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for middle school special education; and principles of middle school instruction in specific subjects.

abstract: Directed energy systems (DES) represent a critical frontier in modern defense technologies, yet their operational efficacy is constrained by the complex interplay of atmospheric turbulence, thermal blooming, and dynamic target tracking in real-world scenarios. This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling high-energy laser (HEL) propagation and adaptive control under realistic battlefield conditions, focusing on optimizing beam stability and target engagement in heterogeneous environments. Current simulations rely on simplified assumptions that inadequately capture multi-physics interactions, limiting predictive accuracy for mission-critical decision-making. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate three-dimensional adaptive optics modeling, nonlinear atmospheric thermodynamics, and machine learning-driven beam control algorithms. The research will employ parallelized finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods to resolve laser-matter interactions at microscales, coupled with large-eddy simulations (LES) for turbulence effects across varying altitudes and weather conditions. Reinforcement learning models will be trained on HPC clusters to optimize beam steering and power modulation in response to real-time sensor inputs, emulating adaptive threat scenarios. Key outcomes include validated predictive models for HEL performance degradation in turbulent media, a scalable toolkit for rapid scenario testing, and actionable insights into system design trade-offs for deployable directed energy platforms. By enabling unprecedented resolution of spatiotemporal complexities in DES operations, this work aims to advance the reliability and strategic utility of directed energy technologies, directly supporting next-generation defense capabilities while minimizing costly physical prototyping. Computational resources will be critical for managing the exascale data generated by coupled multi-physics simulations and the iterative training of AI-driven control systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational archaeology research focused on modeling the socioecological dynamics of ancient urban systems in understudied regions of the Americas. The research problem centers on understanding how pre-Columbian settlements adapted to environmental stressors, such as shifting hydrological patterns and resource scarcity, through the integration of large-scale spatial, climatic, and material culture datasets. Existing studies in the region rely on localized excavations or qualitative assessments, leaving systemic interactions between settlement networks, land-use practices, and environmental feedback loops poorly quantified. To address this gap, the project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating decision-making processes in ancient agricultural and resource distribution systems, calibrated against archaeological evidence from lidar surveys, radiocarbon dating, and ceramic provenance analyses. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to regional levels, incorporating high-resolution paleoclimate reconstructions (1km² grids), and iteratively testing hypotheses about resilience strategies across 500–1500 CE timescales. Parallelized workflows will process multi-terabyte datasets, while machine learning algorithms (e.g., random forests, convolutional neural networks) will classify settlement patterns from remotely sensed imagery and identify correlations between artifact distributions and ecological variables. Expected outcomes include (1) the first open-source computational framework for simulating preindustrial urban resilience in tropical environments, (2) high-resolution maps of archaeological sensitivity to guide conservation efforts, and (3) quantitative insights into how past societies balanced population density and resource carrying capacity—a topic with implications for modern sustainability science. The project will generate publicly accessible digital repositories of simulation code, trained models, and integrated archaeological-environmental datasets, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in computational heritage studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of extinct societies, and the past of living societies, via the excavation, analysis and interpretation of their artifactual, human, and associated remains. Includes instruction in archeological theory, field methods, dating methods, conservation and museum studies, cultural and physical evolution, and the study of specific selected past cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize risk assessment and accident prevention strategies in industrial environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial safety management faces challenges in modeling complex, dynamic interactions between human operators, equipment, and environmental factors, which contribute to latent risks and system failures. Traditional risk analysis methods often rely on static models or simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to predict cascading failures or emergent hazards in real-world settings. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning to analyze industrial processes under varying operational conditions. The project will simulate scenarios such as hazardous material dispersion, equipment malfunction cascades, and human-error pathways in high-fidelity virtual environments. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations, process large datasets from IoT sensors and incident reports, and train predictive models that account for ergonomic, behavioral, and systemic variables. Expected outcomes include a modular risk prediction toolkit capable of identifying critical safety thresholds, optimizing evacuation protocols, and recommending adaptive safety interventions. This work will advance industrial safety technology by enabling proactive, data-driven decision-making, reducing reliance on reactive measures. The computational framework will be validated using case studies from chemical manufacturing and energy production facilities, with results disseminated as open-source tools for safety professionals. By quantifying previously intractable risk interactions, this research aims to reduce workplace accidents, lower compliance costs, and inform updates to industrial safety standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing and enforcing industrial safety standards to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in industrial processes, industrial hygiene, injury prevention, toxicology, ergonomics, risk analysis, system and process safety, safety performance measurement, human factors, human behavior, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational text analysis in Talmudic Studies, a field traditionally reliant on manual, labor-intensive methods. The research problem centers on the challenges of analyzing the Talmud’s vast, interconnected corpus—comprising legal debates, narrative exegesis, and later commentaries—which spans centuries and integrates diverse disciplines such as jurisprudence, ethics, and philosophy. Traditional approaches struggle to systematically trace the evolution of legal concepts, identify cross-textual thematic patterns, or model the influence of sociohistorical contexts on interpretive traditions. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for rabbinic Hebrew and Aramaic, machine learning models to detect semantic and structural relationships within multilayered commentaries, and network analysis to map the diffusion of legal and philosophical ideas across time and geographic regions. HPC resources are critical for training custom transformer-based models on digitized Talmudic texts, given the computational demands of processing morphologically rich Semitic languages and managing sparse, fragmentary historical data. Additionally, large-scale simulations will model hypothetical textual genealogies to test scholarly hypotheses about lost manuscript traditions. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for computational Talmudic analysis, new insights into the transmission of Jewish legal thought, and a publicly accessible database linking textual variants to historical contexts. This work bridges computational humanities with religious studies, offering a replicable framework for analyzing complex textual traditions while enhancing pedagogical resources for training students in both Talmudic scholarship and digital humanities methodologies. By integrating HPC-driven approaches, the project aims to redefine the scale and precision of research in Talmudic Studies, with implications for interdisciplinary studies of legal and philosophical corpora across cultures.
cip_definition: A program focused on intense study of the Talmud that fosters values, critical thinking, and scholarship skills; prepares students for entry into a broad spectrum of graduate and professional schools; and prepares students for entry into a variety of careers including the Rabbinate. Includes instruction in Jewish law, Jewish jurisprudence, ethics, philosophy, and related disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic coordination of circadian-regulated metabolic processes in plant root systems under fluctuating nutrient availability, a specialized niche integrating plant molecular biology, chronobiology, and systems-level computational modeling. While plant circadian systems are well studied in aerial tissues, the spatiotemporal regulation of root metabolic networks—particularly their synchronization with diurnal environmental changes and shoot-derived signaling—remains poorly understood. We propose to develop a multiscale computational framework combining agent-based modeling of root tip cell clusters with whole-organ metabolic flux analyses to decipher how circadian oscillators optimize nutrient uptake efficiency while balancing trade-offs between growth and stress adaptation. High-performance computing resources will enable the integration of single-cell RNA-seq datasets from Brassica rapa roots (generated through companion wet-lab experiments) with mechanistic models of transporter protein dynamics, phytohormone signaling gradients, and carbon allocation patterns. Key challenges include parameterizing stochastic variations in oscillator gene expression across root cell types and scaling these to predict emergent tissue-level behaviors under nutrient stress scenarios. The computational pipeline will leverage parallelized simulations to test hypotheses about phase entrainment mechanisms between shoot and root circadian systems, as well as machine learning approaches to identify critical nodes for metabolic resilience. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible model database for root chronometabolism, novel predictions about circadian control of root exudate composition, and foundational insights into engineering crop species with improved nutrient use efficiency through temporal optimization strategies. This work bridges molecular-scale regulatory mechanisms with organism-level adaptive responses, requiring computational resources capable of handling complex hybrid models that exceed current laboratory infrastructure capacities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of molecular biology, biochemistry, and biophysics to the study of biomolecular structures, functions, and processes specific to plants and plant substances. Includes instruction in the biochemistry of plant cells, nuclear-cytoplasmic interactions, molecular cytostructures, photosynthesis, plant molecular genetics, and the molecular biology of plant diseases.

abstract: Despite advancements in transfusion safety, a critical challenge persists in identifying low-frequency or novel antigen-antibody incompatibilities that evade conventional serological testing, contributing to delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions and alloimmunization. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex immunohematological interactions and predict high-risk donor-recipient pairings. Current methods rely on labor-intensive in vitro assays and curated antigen databases, which lack the resolution to detect rare epitopes or anticipate emergent antibody specificities. We propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of red blood cell membrane proteins with machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on multi-omic donor data, including genomic variants, glycoprotein expression profiles, and historical transfusion outcomes. The MD component will simulate antigen-antibody binding affinities across 3D structural ensembles of HLA and non-HLA antigens, while ML models will analyze patterns in alloimmunization risk from a de-identified dataset spanning 500,000 transfusion events. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of these simulations and iterative training of deep neural networks to identify predictive biomarkers. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for antigenic mismatch risk, validated against retrospective clinical data, and an open-access database of simulated antigen-antibody interaction kinetics. This work will directly inform precision transfusion protocols, particularly for patients with sickle cell disease, thalassemia, or rare blood types, who face disproportionate risks from undetected incompatibilities. By bridging computational biology and transfusion medicine, the project advances the operational capacity of blood banks to mitigate adverse reactions while optimizing donor inventory management—a critical need as demand for rare blood components grows globally.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational circulation of cultural narratives across the British Commonwealth, focusing on underrepresented voices in postcolonial literary and media archives. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of shared cultural identity and resistance in digitized texts, oral histories, and visual media from Commonwealth nations, particularly those marginalized by dominant historical frameworks. Existing studies have relied on manual close readings or limited computational sampling, leaving large-scale comparative analyses of linguistic, thematic, and representational trends unexamined. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for multilingual text classification, and computer vision algorithms to detect visual motifs in film and art archives. Computational workflows will integrate customized topic modeling to track evolving narratives of decolonization and hybrid cultural identity across temporal and geographic contexts. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data—including creolized language texts, digitized colonial records, and community-produced media—while maintaining sensitivity to dialectal variations and context-specific semantic meanings. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for cross-cultural narrative analysis, a publicly accessible dataset of annotated materials, and new insights into how marginalized communities negotiated cultural autonomy within Commonwealth networks. This work will advance methodological innovation in computational cultural studies while informing contemporary debates about heritage preservation and identity in postcolonial societies. The requested allocation will support GPU-intensive model training, parallel processing of multilingual corpora, and large-scale network analysis to map narrative diffusion pathways, enabling a previously unfeasible synthesis of regional specificity and Commonwealth-wide cultural dynamics.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries comprising components of the historical British Empire and modern British Commonwealth, including migration patterns, shared sociocultural and political features and problems, and contemporary relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize collision repair processes for modern automotive materials, including advanced high-strength steels, multi-material composites, and electric vehicle (EV)-specific components. As vehicle designs evolve, traditional repair methodologies struggle to address the complex structural behaviors and material interactions of these new systems, risking suboptimal repairs that compromise safety and longevity. The research problem centers on creating predictive tools to guide damage assessment, repair strategy selection, and material performance validation under diverse mechanical and environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) simulations of collision dynamics, multi-physics modeling of repair processes (e.g., welding thermal effects, adhesive curing kinetics), and machine learning-driven optimization of repair parameters. Computational models will integrate material property databases, damage propagation algorithms, and EV battery enclosure integrity assessments. Expected outcomes include a framework for simulating repair outcomes across material combinations, predictive guidelines for minimizing heat-affected zones during structural repairs, and quantitative metrics for evaluating post-repair crashworthiness. These results will be validated against physical crash test data and industry-standard repair protocols. The project aims to bridge gaps between collision repair education and emerging automotive technologies, providing technicians with data-driven decision support tools while advancing computational methods for applied technical fields. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work addresses critical industry needs for adaptive repair strategies in an era of rapidly evolving vehicle architectures.
cip_title: Autobody/ Collision and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, reconstruct and finish automobile bodies, fenders, and external features. Includes instruction in structure analysis, damage repair, non-structural analysis, mechanical and electrical components, plastics and adhesives, painting and refinishing techniques, and damage analysis and estimating.

abstract: The diagnosis and treatment of pediatric gastrointestinal (GI) disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), functional abdominal pain disorders, and cholestatic liver diseases, remain challenging due to the heterogeneity of disease presentation, complex host-microbiome interactions, and variable treatment responses. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized protocols that inadequately address individual patient factors, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by integrating multi-omic data (genomic, metagenomic, proteomic) with clinical records and endoscopic imaging to develop predictive models of disease progression and therapeutic efficacy in pediatric populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale datasets from a prospective cohort of 1,200 patients (ages 0–18) with diverse GI pathologies, including longitudinal microbiome sequencing (16S rRNA and shotgun metagenomics), host whole-exome sequencing, and time-series proteomic profiles. Machine learning pipelines will be implemented to identify biomarkers of treatment response, while agent-based modeling will simulate host-microbiome dynamics under varying therapeutic interventions. Computational demands include processing >500 TB of raw sequencing data, training deep learning models on endoscopic video feeds for automated lesion detection, and running parallelized simulations of microbial community interactions. The project requires GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training, high-memory nodes for genome assembly, and scalable storage for multi-institutional data sharing. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for personalized treatment selection in pediatric IBD, (2) mechanistic insights into microbiome-driven disease modifiers in cholestasis, and (3) an open-access computational platform for pediatric GI biomarker discovery. This work will directly inform clinical trial design and advance precision medicine approaches for children with complex digestive diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the digestive systems of infants, children, and adolescents; includes treatment of conditions such as abdominal pain, ulcers, diarrhea, cancer, and jaundice, and performance of complex diagnostic and therapeutic procedures using lighted scopes to see internal organs.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, with ventricular arrhythmias in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) posing significant risk of sudden cardiac death. Current clinical tools inadequately predict arrhythmic events due to limited understanding of how scar microstructure, electrophysiological heterogeneity, and mechanical stress interact dynamically. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a multi-scale computational framework to quantify arrhythmia susceptibility in ICM patients, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage complex simulations and large-scale data integration. We propose to construct patient-specific cardiac models using clinical imaging (cardiac MRI), electrophysiological mapping, and biomechanical data from 500 ICM patients. These models will incorporate finite element simulations of electrical propagation at cellular-to-tissue scales, accounting for scar border zone anisotropy and dynamic coupling with regional contractility. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated electrical behavior alongside longitudinal clinical outcomes to identify high-risk substrate features. HPC capabilities are essential for executing parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, processing high-resolution imaging data (≤400µm), and training predictive neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated risk stratification tool that improves sudden cardiac death prediction accuracy by ≥25% compared to current ejection fraction-based criteria. The project will also generate novel insights into mechano-electric feedback mechanisms in scar-related arrhythmogenesis, potentially informing targeted ablation strategies. By leveraging HPC to bridge clinical data with biophysical modeling, this work aims to advance precision cardiology paradigms, optimize implantable defibrillator allocation, and reduce arrhythmia-related mortality in high-risk populations. All models and computational pipelines will be shared openly to accelerate translational research in cardiac electrophysiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Cardiology

abstract: This project seeks to address persistent disparities in learning outcomes for culturally and linguistically diverse (CLD) students by developing computational models to optimize adaptive learning technologies for multicultural classrooms. Current adaptive systems often fail to account for the intersection of cultural identity, multilingualism, and learning preferences, resulting in tools that inadvertently reinforce inequities. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets—including student interaction logs, language proficiency assessments, and sociocultural surveys—from 15,000+ learners across diverse K-12 districts. Machine learning models (transformers, graph neural networks) will be trained to identify patterns in how cultural context influences engagement with digital curricula, while agent-based modeling will simulate classroom dynamics under varying instructional strategies. Key computational challenges include processing natural language data in 8+ languages, disentangling confounding variables in multicultural learning trajectories, and scaling simulations to represent regional demographic variations. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized hyperparameter tuning for bias-aware algorithms and real-time sensitivity analyses of cultural variables in our simulations. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source framework for evaluating cultural responsiveness in educational AI systems, (2) evidence-based design principles for multilingual adaptive content delivery, and (3) predictive models that help educators preempt equity gaps by aligning instructional technology with community-specific needs. By elucidating how computational systems can better honor cultural diversity in learning sciences, this work directly supports teacher education programs in preparing educators to implement technologically inclusive pedagogies. The requested resources are critical given the iterative nature of model development and the need for large-scale validation across synthetic and real-world datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, and implementation of instructional and advising services for culturally diverse learning populations. Includes instruction in cultural diversity, at-risk populations, multilingual and ESL education, program and curriculum design, instructional technology, information resources, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling and communicating with multicultural populations, law and regulations, and applications to specific cultural groups, educational services, and research issues.

abstract: Animal-assisted therapy (AAT) has demonstrated promise in improving outcomes for individuals with mental and physical disabilities, yet variability in therapeutic efficacy remains poorly understood. This variability is hypothesized to stem from complex, dynamic interactions between animal behavior, client characteristics, environmental factors, and intervention protocols. Current statistical methods lack the capacity to model these multidimensional, nonlinear relationships at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of AAT outcomes using heterogeneous datasets. We will integrate longitudinal behavioral data (e.g., animal stress indicators, client engagement metrics), biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels), and therapy session metadata (e.g., duration, setting, clinician annotations) from 15 partnered AAT clinics. Machine learning pipelines will be deployed to identify critical predictors of therapeutic success, including animal-client dyad compatibility and intervention timing. Agent-based modeling will simulate hypothetical scenarios to optimize therapy protocols while accounting for ethical constraints and animal welfare. Computational demands are substantial, requiring parallelized processing of high-frequency biometric streams (≥1TB/week), training of deep reinforcement learning models on dyadic interaction patterns, and large-scale sensitivity analyses. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated framework for personalizing AAT protocols based on client-animal profiles, (2) predictive biomarkers of intervention success, and (3) open-source tools for simulating therapy scenarios to minimize animal stress. By elucidating the mechanisms underlying effective human-animal therapeutic interactions, this work will advance evidence-based standards for AAT while ensuring ethical integration of computational methods into clinical practice. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage data complexity, enable real-time analytics for adaptive interventions, and foster collaboration across clinical and computational domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares health and human service professionals to integrate the use of animals into their treatment practices in order to facilitate change in people with mental and physical disabilities. Includes instruction in psychology, psychology of disabilities, animal behavior, animal training, the human-animal bond, integration of animals into therapeutic settings, and ethical and cultural issues.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of architectural design simulations, which increasingly require high-fidelity modeling of structural integrity, energy efficiency, and environmental interactions. Current architectural drafting and CAD workflows struggle to efficiently process large-scale simulations, particularly when integrating real-time data from building information modeling (BIM) systems or evaluating multi-physics phenomena such as thermal load distribution and material stress under dynamic conditions. The limitations of conventional computing resources hinder the ability to iteratively optimize designs for sustainability, safety, and compliance with evolving building codes. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized simulation workflows tailored to architectural applications. The computational approach will focus on developing scalable algorithms for parametric design optimization, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural validation, and deploying machine learning models to predict energy performance across diverse climate scenarios. Custom CADD scripts will interface with HPC clusters to automate resource-intensive tasks such as generative design iterations and multi-criteria decision analysis. A key innovation involves coupling BIM data with real-time sensor simulations to model building behavior under extreme environmental stresses. The project will validate results against physical prototypes and existing case studies to ensure computational accuracy. Expected outcomes include a framework for rapid, high-resolution architectural simulations that reduce design iteration times by 40–60% while improving predictive accuracy for energy use and structural resilience. This work will directly contribute to advancing sustainable design practices and provide open-source computational tools for educators, enabling students to engage with cutting-edge HPC-driven workflows in architectural drafting. The resource allocation will support both ongoing validation of a generative design algorithm for net-zero buildings and proposed work on AI-assisted material optimization, fostering innovation at the intersection of computational design and construction technology.
cip_title: Architectural Drafting and Architectural CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations for architectural and related construction projects. Includes instruction in basic construction and structural design, architectural rendering, architectural-aided drafting (CAD), layout and designs, architectural blueprint interpretation, building materials, and basic structural wiring diagramming.

abstract: This project seeks to address computational bottlenecks in large-scale geospatial data processing for surveying engineering applications, with a focus on improving the accuracy and efficiency of real-time terrain modeling and infrastructure alignment analysis. Modern surveying workflows integrate high-resolution LiDAR, multispectral satellite imagery, and dense GPS networks, generating datasets that strain conventional computing systems. The proposed research will develop parallelized algorithms for error-correction in multi-sensor fusion, automated feature extraction from aerial photogrammetry, and predictive modeling of ground deformation using distributed computing frameworks. A hybrid CPU-GPU architecture will be employed to accelerate computationally intensive tasks such as point cloud registration, least-squares adjustment of geodetic networks, and Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in dynamic environments. The HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from regional transportation corridor surveys, facilitating rapid alignment optimization while accounting for geological constraints and climate-induced shifts. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for near-real-time geospatial analytics, validated through case studies on urban rail expansion and floodplain mapping projects. The computational tools developed will advance precision in land-use planning, reduce iterative design cycles for civil infrastructure, and provide open-source modules for adaptive resource allocation in remote sensing workflows. By addressing the gap between data acquisition rates and processing capabilities, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for computational surveying methodologies in civil and environmental engineering contexts.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
