cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the determination of the location, elevations, and alignment of natural and manmade topographic features. Includes instruction in property line location, surveying, surface measurement, aerial and terrestrial photogrammetry, remote sensing, satellite imagery, global positioning systems, computer applications, and photographic data processing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing personalized rehabilitation strategies in patients with neuromuscular impairments, integrating biomechanical modeling, wearable sensor data, and machine learning. Current physical therapy protocols often rely on generalized treatment plans, which may fail to account for individual variations in movement patterns, tissue adaptation, and neural recovery. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven approach that combines dynamic motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data from patients undergoing post-stroke rehabilitation. These multimodal datasets will inform patient-specific musculoskeletal simulations using OpenSim, calibrated to individual neuromuscular parameters. The computational pipeline will employ finite element modeling to predict tissue stress distributions during therapeutic exercises and Bayesian optimization algorithms to iteratively refine intervention parameters (e.g., resistance levels, joint angle targets) based on real-time feedback. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations across diverse patient cohorts and processing high-dimensional datasets (>10 TB anticipated). Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for mapping patient-specific biomechanical constraints to optimal rehabilitation protocols, reducing trial-and-error adjustments in clinical practice. The project will also yield an open-source toolkit for physical therapy assistants to visualize simulated treatment outcomes, enhancing clinical decision-making. By bridging computational biomechanics and rehabilitation science, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision physical therapy, with potential applications in telerehabilitation and adaptive assistive device design. Successful implementation could decrease recovery times by an estimated 15-20% in targeted populations while mitigating risks of secondary injury through personalized load optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physical therapist, to implement physical therapy treatment care plans, train patients, conduct treatment interventions, use equipment, and observe and record patient progress. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, behavioral sciences, biomechanics, clinical documentation, clinical pathology, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the thematic and stylistic evolution of Canadian literature across historical periods, regional traditions, and oral storytelling practices. While existing scholarship has mapped key movements in Canadian literary history, the integration of large-scale computational methods remains underutilized, limiting the capacity to trace subtle patterns in language use, intertextual influences, and sociocultural shifts within a corpus spanning centuries. The research will compile a digitized collection of primary texts, including novels, poetry, folklore transcriptions, and Indigenous oral narratives (in collaboration with cultural stakeholders), to investigate how regional identities, multilingual encounters, and colonial legacies have shaped literary production. Computational approaches will include natural language processing (NLP) for semantic topic modeling, sentiment analysis to track evolving representations of national identity, and network analysis to visualize connections between authors, genres, and folkloric motifs. Stylometric algorithms will identify shifts in narrative structure and diction, particularly in works bridging oral and written traditions. Given the scale and heterogeneity of the corpus—encompassing over 5,000 texts in English, French, and Indigenous languages (with ethical protocols for culturally sensitive materials)—HPC resources are critical for parallel processing, managing memory-intensive tasks, and training machine learning models to classify underrepresented themes. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of annotated Canadian literary works, visualizations of transnational influence networks, and new frameworks for analyzing the interplay between formal literature and grassroots storytelling. By bridging computational humanities methodologies with decolonial literary theory, this project aims to redefine canonical narratives of Canadian literature while preserving the complexity of its regional and oral traditions. The findings will inform pedagogical tools, heritage preservation initiatives, and interdisciplinary collaborations exploring technology’s role in cultural scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is a critical intervention for conditions such as decompression sickness, chronic wounds, and radiation injury, yet the physiological and biophysical mechanisms underlying its efficacy and risks remain incompletely characterized. Current clinical protocols rely on generalized pressure and oxygenation parameters, which may not account for individual patient variability in tissue perfusion, gas diffusion kinetics, or susceptibility to oxygen toxicity. This project seeks to develop patient-specific computational models to optimize HBOT protocols, minimize adverse events, and predict therapeutic outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale physiological responses to hyperbaric exposures, integrating fluid dynamics, gas transport, and cellular metabolic processes. A key focus is modeling the dynamics of inert gas bubble dissolution in tissues during decompression, incorporating real-world variables such as body composition and comorbid conditions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) frameworks will simulate gas diffusion across capillary-tissue interfaces under varying hyperbaric pressures, while finite element models will predict tissue oxygenation gradients and oxidative stress thresholds. Machine learning approaches will be applied to anonymized patient datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment response. The HPC environment is essential for resolving these computationally intensive, multi-physics simulations at clinically relevant spatial and temporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for HBOT efficacy, risk stratification tools for oxygen toxicity, and open-source simulation frameworks to guide protocol personalization. By bridging gaps in mechanistic understanding, this work aims to advance evidence-based hyperbaric medicine, reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, and improve safety for patients with complex comorbidities. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as a template for future studies investigating pressure-mediated therapies across health professions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to operate hyperbaric (recompression) chambers for the treatment of disease. Includes instruction in patient assessment and management, hyperbaric safety, physics of hyperbaric and hypobaric exposures, physiology, hyperbaric chamber operation, and air decompression procedures.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance, sustainable polymers in industrial applications necessitates advanced computational tools to overcome the limitations of traditional trial-and-error material development. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize the synthesis, processing, and performance of novel polymer systems, with a focus on biodegradability and recyclability. The primary challenge lies in predicting macromolecular behavior under dynamic manufacturing conditions, including polymerization kinetics, thermal stability, and stress-response properties, which are experimentally time-intensive and cost-prohibitive to characterize. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms. MD simulations will model molecular interactions during polymerization and degradation, while FEA will assess mechanical performance under industrial processing parameters. ML models trained on experimental and simulated datasets will identify correlations between polymer architectures, processing variables, and end-use properties, enabling inverse design of materials with tailored characteristics. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of these tasks, particularly for simulating large-scale polymer networks (>100,000 atoms) and iterative optimization workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for designing biodegradable polymers with equivalent or superior mechanical properties to conventional plastics, as well as energy-efficient processing protocols to reduce manufacturing carbon footprints. This work will directly support ongoing industry partnerships aimed at commercializing circular-economy-compliant materials, while providing a computational resource framework for future research in polymer engineering education and applied R&D. The requested allocation will enable simulations at experimentally relevant timescales and system sizes, which are unfeasible with current institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using industrial polymers. Includes instruction in the principles of macromolecular chemistry, polymerization and plastic manufacturing processes and equipment, design and operational testing procedures, equipment maintenance and repair procedures, safety procedures, applications to specific products, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance earth science education by integrating high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex earth systems and improve pedagogical strategies for K-12 educators. Earth science concepts such as climate dynamics, geological processes, and ecosystem interactions involve multivariate, data-rich systems that are challenging to teach effectively using traditional methods. Current educational tools often oversimplify these phenomena, limiting students’ ability to engage with authentic scientific workflows. To address this gap, we propose developing scalable, interactive simulations of earth systems using HPC resources, enabling pre-service and in-service teachers to explore real-world datasets and dynamic models in classroom settings. The project will leverage existing geospatial and climate datasets (e.g., satellite observations, CMIP6 models) to build modular computational workflows. These workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to generate high-resolution visualizations and scenario-based simulations, such as regional climate impacts or tectonic plate interactions. Machine learning methods will be applied to streamline data preprocessing and parameterization, reducing latency for real-time educational applications. The outcomes will include a suite of open-access computational tools tailored for teacher training programs, designed to align with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). By bridging computational earth science with teacher education, this work aims to empower educators to foster data literacy and systems thinking in students. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling large datasets and iterative model runs, which are infeasible on standard infrastructure. Anticipated impacts include improved teacher confidence in using computational tools, increased student engagement with earth science content, and a broader integration of research-grade methods into STEM curricula. This project underscores the role of advanced computing in democratizing access to cutting-edge science within teacher preparation programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach earth science programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing patient-specific clinical decision-making in complex nursing care environments through advanced computational modeling. Nursing research increasingly relies on large, heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biometric monitoring, and patient-reported outcomes—to inform interventions. However, traditional analytical tools are insufficient for integrating these multidimensional data streams at scale, limiting the ability to predict patient deterioration, personalize care plans, or model staffing needs in dynamic clinical settings. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for predictive analytics in nursing science. The project will employ machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and recurrent neural networks, to analyze longitudinal patient data and simulate care delivery scenarios. Key computational tasks include parallel processing of EHR-derived time-series data, clustering of patient subpopulations based on risk trajectories, and agent-based modeling of nurse-patient interactions under varying staffing ratios. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models incorporating genomic, psychosocial, and clinical variables while maintaining compliance with health data security standards. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for sepsis onset in medical-surgical units, optimized shift scheduling algorithms balancing nurse workload with patient acuity, and personalized discharge readiness scores integrating biometric and social determinants of health. By leveraging scalable computational resources, this work aims to establish new methodologies for data-driven nursing research, directly informing clinical workflows and policy decisions. The proposed models will be tested against retrospective datasets from three academic medical centers before prospective validation, with potential to reduce preventable adverse events by 15-20% in pilot units. This project bridges a critical gap in nursing science by enabling complex, real-world data integration that traditional statistical approaches cannot support, ultimately advancing precision nursing care and operational efficiency.
cip_title: Registered Nursing, Nursing Administration, Nursing Research and Clinical Nursing, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in registered nursing, nursing administration, nursing research, and clinical nursing, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Chronic cardiometabolic diseases exhibit complex pathophysiology influenced by dynamic interactions between genomic, proteomic, and environmental factors. Current clinical risk stratification tools lack granularity to predict acute decompensation events (e.g., heart failure exacerbations, hyperglycemic crises) in real time, particularly in patients with multimorbidity. This project proposes to develop a multimodal computational framework integrating wearable sensor data, multi-omics profiles, and electronic health records (EHR) to identify personalized risk signatures for acute events. The central challenge lies in processing high-frequency biosensor streams (ECG, accelerometry, continuous glucose) alongside sparse genomic and clinical data while accounting for temporal dependencies and patient-specific confounders. We will employ transformer-based architectures adapted for irregularly sampled time series and graph neural networks to model cross-modal biological interactions. Federated learning techniques will be implemented to train models across three institutional EHR datasets without raw data transfer, preserving privacy. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for (1) preprocessing 50+ TB of raw sensor data via parallelized signal decomposition pipelines, (2) optimizing hybrid neural networks through hyperparameter searches across GPU clusters, and (3) simulating whole-body digital twins to test intervention scenarios via agent-based modeling. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for multimodal clinical forecasting validated against prospective data from 200 patients, novel biomarkers linking autonomic nervous system dynamics to mitochondrial gene expression patterns, and a proof-of-concept federated learning framework deployable across hospital systems. This work bridges translational gaps by creating computational infrastructure to convert heterogeneous data streams into actionable clinical predictions, directly supporting precision medicine initiatives in cardiometabolic care. Successful implementation will provide a template for real-time risk mitigation strategies in complex chronic diseases beyond current EHR-based predictive models.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares clinicians to direct a broad range of scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge into clinical practice, and bridge clinical science with laboratory investigations. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, and scientific writing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to evaluate the economic and ecological trade-offs of conservation policies under climate change uncertainty. A critical challenge in environmental economics lies in modeling the dynamic feedback between resource management decisions, ecosystem responses, and shifting market conditions at high spatial and temporal resolutions. Existing approaches often rely on simplified assumptions due to computational limitations, reducing their capacity to inform regionally tailored policies. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled system combining agent-based modeling, dynamic stochastic optimization, and machine learning to simulate land-use decisions, biodiversity outcomes, and economic welfare across heterogeneous landscapes. The framework will integrate satellite-derived land-cover data, species distribution models, and econometric estimates of production functions to parameterize decision-making agents (e.g., farmers, conservation agencies) operating under climatic and regulatory constraints. Key computational challenges include solving high-dimensional dynamic programming problems for adaptive management strategies, running Monte Carlo simulations across ensemble climate projections, and processing multi-terabyte geospatial datasets. Access to HPC resources will enable parallelization of optimization routines using MPI-based solvers, GPU-accelerated neural networks for parameter estimation, and distributed storage systems for real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) spatially explicit maps of cost-effective conservation investments under varying carbon pricing scenarios, (2) probabilistic assessments of policy resilience to extreme weather events, and (3) open-source tools for coupled ecological-economic decision support. Results will directly inform state-level habitat conservation plans and international biodiversity offset markets, while advancing methodological integration of ecological dynamics into economic models. The computational infrastructure developed will provide a scalable platform for testing emergent market-based conservation instruments, such as tradable resilience credits, across diverse socioecological contexts.
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Economics (NATURAL RESOURCES/ CONSERVATION SCIENCES)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic concepts and methods to the analysis of issues such as air and water pollution, land use planning, waste disposal, invasive species and pest control, conservation policies, and related environmental problems. Includes instruction in cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, evaluation and assessment of alternative resource management strategies, policy evaluation and monitoring, and descriptive and analytic tools for studying how environmental developments affect the economic system.

abstract: Emerging challenges in understanding complex disease mechanisms and therapeutic interventions necessitate advanced computational approaches in pre-medical research. This project seeks to investigate the structural dynamics of protein-ligand interactions associated with drug-resistant mutations in oncology-related kinases, a critical barrier in cancer treatment efficacy. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we aim to characterize atomic-level conformational changes in mutant kinase domains that diminish drug binding affinity while retaining pathological signaling activity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to perform all-atom, explicit-solvent MD simulations across multiple mutant systems (e.g., EGFR, ALK, BRAF) over microsecond timescales, coupled with Markov state modeling to identify metastable conformational states. Parallelized free energy calculations using alchemical perturbation methods will quantify relative binding affinities for clinically approved tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Complementary machine learning approaches will be employed to classify mutation-induced allosteric networks from simulation trajectories. This integrated computational framework will enable systematic comparison of wild-type versus mutant kinase dynamics, identifying conserved structural motifs that could inform the design of resistance-evading therapeutics. The project’s outcomes are expected to 1) establish predictive models linking specific mutation profiles to drug resistance mechanisms, 2) generate shareable datasets of kinase conformational landscapes, and 3) provide computational workflows adaptable to other pathogenic mutation studies. By elucidating fundamental biophysical principles underlying treatment resistance, this work directly supports the translational goals of pre-medical education while demonstrating how computational biology can bridge basic science and clinical problem-solving. The requested HPC allocation will empower scalable, reproducible analyses essential for handling complex biological systems, fostering technical skills in computational biomedicine critical for future physician-researchers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in medicine, osteopathic medicine, or podiatric medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic resource allocation in tertiary care hospitals using high-performance computing (HPC) to model real-time operational workflows and predict systemic bottlenecks. Current hospital administration strategies rely on static scheduling and retrospective data, limiting responsiveness to emergent patient influxes, equipment failures, or staff shortages. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to simulate multi-departmental interactions under variable conditions. The model will ingest real-time data streams—including patient triage levels, staff availability, equipment utilization rates, and facility throughput metrics—to generate adaptive resource allocation strategies. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations across parallelized scenarios, enabling rapid evaluation of contingency plans for rare but high-impact events such as mass casualty incidents or supply chain disruptions. Machine learning components will be trained on synthetic datasets generated through these simulations, augmented with historical operational data from partner hospitals. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for administrators to proactively balance competing priorities (e.g., surgical suite utilization vs. emergency department overcrowding) while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory constraints. The project will deliver open-source optimization algorithms tailored for healthcare management, validated against real-world metrics such as patient wait-time reduction and critical resource idle-time minimization. By bridging computational systems engineering and healthcare operations, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resilience in hospital administration.
cip_title: Hospital and Health Care Facilities Administration/ Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and other health care facilities. Includes instruction in facilities planning, building and operations management, business management, financial management and insurance, fund-raising and marketing, public relations, human resources management and labor relations, health care facilities operations, principles of health care delivery, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives across Western Europe from the medieval period to the early modern era, with a focus on underrepresented regional identities. Traditional scholarship in Western European Studies has often relied on manual analysis of localized textual and visual sources, limiting the scale at which transregional cultural dynamics can be examined. To address this gap, the research will employ computational text and image analysis methods on a curated corpus of digitized manuscripts, regional chronicles, and artistic works from Britain, Iberia, and the Western Mediterranean. The primary research problem centers on identifying and mapping patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance that shaped collective identities in borderland regions, particularly where Christian, Islamic, and Jewish traditions intersected. A hybrid computational approach will be implemented, combining transformer-based natural language processing models for multilingual text analysis (Latin, Old French, Medieval Arabic, and regional vernaculars) with graph neural networks to model cultural transmission networks across time and space. Image recognition algorithms will supplement textual analysis by detecting stylistic motifs in illuminated manuscripts and architectural illustrations. The scale of data—over 15TB of digitized primary sources from seven archival partners—necessitates distributed computing for parallelized feature extraction and dimensionality reduction. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas of cultural influence trajectories and a methodological framework for computationally assisted humanities research that bridges regional specificity with macro-scale analysis. This work will provide new insights into how decentralized cultural production in premodern Western Europe contributed to pluralistic identities, challenging homogenized narratives of regional heritage. By integrating HPC capabilities with humanistic inquiry, the project aims to establish scalable protocols for analyzing fragmented historical sources while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue in area studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of historical Western Europe, defined as including Britain, Ireland, France, the Low Countries, the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Western Mediterranean, and related island groups and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and optimizing sustainable architectural designs through advanced generative algorithms and physics-based modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in pre-professional architectural education: the limited integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into early-stage design processes, which traditionally rely on manual iteration and simplified environmental analyses. By leveraging HPC resources, we aim to create a scalable platform that dynamically evaluates architectural prototypes against multi-objective criteria—including energy efficiency, structural resilience, material circularity, and human spatial perception—in real time. The computational approach combines parametric design tools with finite element analysis (FEA) for stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for microclimate simulation, and machine learning models trained on historical architectural performance data. This integration enables the system to propose design adaptations that balance aesthetic intent with quantifiable sustainability metrics. A novel aspect involves developing neural networks to predict human perceptual responses to spatial geometries using eye-tracking and biometric datasets from prior architectural psychology studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational workflow that bridges conceptual design with performance analytics, providing architecture students with evidence-based feedback during the ideation phase. The project will also generate benchmark datasets correlating geometric features, environmental factors, and human factors in architectural systems. By deploying these resource-intensive simulations through parallelized computing, we overcome traditional bottlenecks in processing complex, interdependent variables at architectural scales. This work advances computational design pedagogy while establishing methodological foundations for data-driven, sustainable architecture—an emerging interdisciplinary niche combining design theory, environmental science, and human-computer interaction.
cip_definition: A program of study that is a precursor to an advanced degree in architecture. Includes instruction in architectural design, architectural graphics, architectural history, architectural technology, architectural theory and criticism, building technology, calculus, design studio, human factors, environmental architecture, geometry and trigonometry, physics, and technical drawing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance strategies for complex building systems, including HVAC, electrical networks, and plumbing infrastructure. Current maintenance practices often rely on reactive or schedule-based approaches, which can lead to inefficiencies, unexpected failures, and increased operational costs. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the degradation patterns of building components under diverse environmental and operational conditions. The research will integrate multi-physics simulations—such as computational fluid dynamics for HVAC efficiency analysis and finite element modeling for structural wear prediction—with machine learning algorithms trained on historical maintenance data and real-time sensor inputs. These simulations will account for variables like seasonal temperature fluctuations, humidity, occupancy patterns, and material fatigue. By scaling these models across entire building portfolios using HPC clusters, we aim to identify failure thresholds, optimize intervention schedules, and simulate the long-term impacts of maintenance decisions on energy consumption and system longevity. The computational workload requires parallel processing capabilities to handle high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets from IoT-enabled buildings and to iteratively refine predictive algorithms. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that prioritizes maintenance tasks based on risk and cost-benefit analyses, reducing downtime by an estimated 15–30% in simulated test cases. This work will advance data-driven approaches in building maintenance, directly contributing to sustainable infrastructure management and resilience planning for aging commercial and industrial properties. The proposed models will be validated against empirical data from partner facilities, with open-source code and performance benchmarks shared to support broader adoption in the technical education and facility management sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: Clinical Nurse Specialists (CNSs) face complex challenges in optimizing patient-specific care plans, particularly when managing comorbidities requiring tailored pharmacotherapeutic and holistic interventions. Current clinical decision-making frameworks often lack the computational power to integrate multidimensional data—such as electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biometric sensor outputs, pharmacogenomic profiles, and patient-reported outcomes—into dynamic predictive models. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive analytics platform to support CNSs in personalizing care strategies for high-risk populations. The research will leverage machine learning (ML) algorithms, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, to analyze heterogeneous datasets from 50,000+ de-identified patient cases. Key computational tasks include pharmacodynamic interaction modeling, adverse event risk stratification, and longitudinal outcome prediction across diverse demographic cohorts. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data and iterative training of ML models to account for evolving clinical variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for identifying optimal intervention timelines in chronic disease management, (2) risk quantification tools for adverse drug reactions in polypharmacy scenarios, and (3) open-source clinical dashboards integrating model outputs with EHR systems. By enhancing the precision of CNS-led care coordination, this work aims to reduce preventable hospital readmissions and improve quality-of-life metrics in patients with complex chronic conditions. The scalability of the HPC infrastructure will also support future research on adaptive care protocols in underrepresented populations, aligning with national priorities for equitable, data-driven nursing practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver direct patient and client care in clinical settings. Includes instruction in clinical pharmacotherapeutics, advanced clinical practice, holistic nursing, nursing practice and health care policy, administration and consultation services, health assessment, patient stabilization and care, and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between skeletal morphology and environmental stressors in hominin evolution using advanced computational modeling. A persistent challenge in physical anthropology lies in quantifying how biomechanical demands—such as locomotion patterns, tool use, or dietary shifts—shaped skeletal adaptations in fossil hominins. Current analyses rely heavily on static morphological comparisons, limiting our ability to model dynamic responses to evolutionary pressures. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating micro-CT data from fossil specimens, finite element analysis (FEA), and agent-based evolutionary simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-resolution 3D skeletal models (5–10 µm/voxel), run iterative FEA under simulated biomechanical loads, and model long-term adaptive trajectories across parameterized landscapes. The workflow will first reconstruct strain distributions in hominin fossil elements (e.g., femoral necks, mandibular rami) during hypothesized behaviors, then use these mechanical profiles to inform evolutionary algorithms that simulate morphological change over generational timescales. This approach will be validated against known evolutionary sequences in the hominin fossil record before being applied to contested adaptations, such as the emergence of bipedal femoral morphology in early Australopithecus. Expected outcomes include a validated computational pipeline for testing evolutionary hypotheses, quantitative benchmarks for skeletal adaptation thresholds, and novel insights into how developmental plasticity interacted with natural selection during key transitions. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale micro-CT datasets, parallelized FEA computations across 10,000+ core-hours, and evolutionary simulations tracking 50+ morphological variables over 100,000 generations. By bridging empirical paleoanthropology with computational biomechanics, this work aims to establish new methods for testing evolutionary hypotheses that are inaccessible to traditional comparative techniques.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and anthropology to the study of the adaptations, variability, and the evolution of human beings and their living and fossil relatives. Includes instructions in anthropology, human and mammalian anatomy, cell biology, paleontology, human culture and behavior, neuroscience, forensic anthropology, anatomical reconstruction, comparative anatomy, and laboratory science and methods.

abstract: The development of programmable nanoscale interfaces capable of dynamically modulating energy and information transfer remains a critical challenge, hindered by the limited understanding of nonlinear interactions between engineered nanostructures and their environments. This project addresses the computational bottleneck in modeling such systems by integrating quantum-mechanical, mesoscopic, and continuum approaches to predict emergent behaviors in metastable nanomaterial assemblies. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose to simulate hybrid systems comprising precisely arranged 2D nanomaterials (e.g., transition metal dichalcogenides) functionalized with molecular qubits, focusing on their non-equilibrium responses to optical and electromagnetic stimuli. Multiscale simulations will combine time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for electronic structure analysis, machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics for conformational sampling, and finite-element modeling of photonic coupling effects. The research specifically targets the optimization of coherent energy transfer pathways in these systems, which experimental methods struggle to characterize due to spatial and temporal resolution limits. Successful implementation will establish design principles for nanoscale interfacial systems exhibiting tunable optoelectronic properties and selective resonance behaviors, with potential applications in beyond-von-Neumann computing architectures and adaptive photonic networks. By resolving the interplay between quantum confinement effects and macroscopic device performance metrics, this work aims to create a predictive computational framework that bridges traditional gaps between nanomaterial synthesis and functional system integration. The requested resources will enable simulations spanning 10^4–10^6 atoms over nanosecond timescales, providing statistically significant data on rare-event dynamics and defect-mediated interactions. Outcomes will advance the engineering of spatially and temporally programmable matter while establishing methodologies for computationally driven nanoscale system design outside conventional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: Pediatric emergency care requires rapid, evidence-based decisions under high-stakes conditions, yet clinical guidance often relies on data from adult populations or small pediatric cohorts. Children exhibit unique physiological responses to critical illness, and the ethical complexity of conducting interventional studies in this vulnerable population limits the availability of high-quality real-world data. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to model pediatric emergency scenarios, predict outcomes, and optimize treatment strategies using high-performance computing (HPC). The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs) from 15 tertiary pediatric emergency departments, high-frequency vital sign streams, and genomic biomarkers of shock and sepsis. A machine learning pipeline will be implemented to identify dynamic risk patterns for decompensation in critically ill children, leveraging recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer architectures to process temporal data. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate physiological responses to interventions (e.g., fluid resuscitation, vasopressor titration) across developmental stages, incorporating pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic variability from neonatal to adolescent populations. Finite element analysis will model trauma-related injuries in pediatric anatomies derived from de-identified CT/MRI repositories. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, necessitating HPC resources for GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter space exploration, and real-time ensemble forecasting. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for early recognition of clinical deterioration, validated against multicenter prospective data; (2) age-stratified intervention thresholds for hemorrhagic shock and respiratory failure; and (3) open-source computational models of pediatric physiological systems. By creating the first HPC-enabled platform specifically designed for pediatric emergency simulations, this work aims to transform time-sensitive clinical decision-making while establishing scalable infrastructure for pediatric translational research.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage emergencies in infants and children.

abstract: Agronomic systems face mounting pressure to sustainably intensify production under climate variability while minimizing environmental impacts. Current process-based crop models struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning genomic, phenotypic, and edaphic factors at scale, limiting predictive capacity for nutrient use efficiency and genotype-environment interactions. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-omics simulation framework that couples machine learning with mechanistic crop modeling. We will parameterize a suite of modular models using terabyte-scale datasets from field trials (soil biogeochemistry, root architecture phenotyping, and yield metrics) and plant genomic repositories (transcriptomic and metabolomic profiles of nutrient-stress responses in Zea mays). Parallelized ensemble modeling will evaluate >10^6 parameter combinations across soil type × climate scenario × genotype permutations to identify optimal nitrogen management strategies under projected mid-century drought regimes. Graph neural networks will analyze spatial-temporal patterns in rhizosphere microbiome data to predict phosphorus mobilization potentials. The computational workflow will leverage containerized pipelines on GPU-accelerated nodes for training deep learning architectures, while distributed memory clusters will handle large-scale sensitivity analyses of soil-crop-atmosphere models. Expected outcomes include (1) genotype-specific nutrient response curves quantifying tradeoffs between yield stability and fertilizer inputs, (2) predictive biomarkers for root morphology traits affecting drought resilience, and (3) open-source tools for coupling process-based models with experimental omics data. By resolving critical gaps in scaling molecular insights to field-level management, this work will provide actionable strategies for breeding programs and precision nutrient recommendations, directly supporting climate-smart agronomy goals. The HPC infrastructure is essential for achieving the required throughput in simulating complex biological systems across multiple spatial scales and environmental contexts.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the chemical, physical, and biological relationships of crops and the soils nurturing them. Includes instruction in the growth and behavior of agricultural crops, the development of new plant varieties, and the scientific management of soils and nutrients for maximum plant nutrition, health, and productivity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in analyzing and modeling complex dance movement patterns, with a focus on advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in dance research. While dance is inherently embodied and ephemeral, emerging technologies now enable the capture and quantification of movement at unprecedented resolution. However, processing large-scale motion capture datasets—often comprising terabytes of multimodal data from wearable sensors, inertial measurement units, and optical systems—requires scalable computational infrastructure. The research problem centers on decoding the relationship between biomechanical efficiency and aesthetic intent in improvised contemporary dance, a domain lacking systematic computational frameworks. Current methods for segmenting and classifying movement sequences rely on simplified kinematic models, failing to capture the high-dimensional interplay of physiological, cultural, and creative factors that define dance practice. To address this, we propose a parallelized computational pipeline integrating musculoskeletal simulations, deep learning-based gesture recognition, and network analysis of improvisational logic. HPC resources will enable 1) biomechanical optimization of movement sequences using OpenSim-based simulations at scale, 2) training of transformer models on annotated video datasets to identify choreographic motifs across diverse cultural dance forms, and 3) real-time rendering of ensemble interactions in virtual environments for compositional experimentation. Expected outcomes include a publicly available movement analysis toolkit for dance scholars, quantitative frameworks for assessing injury risk in choreography, and novel metrics linking kinematic complexity to perceived artistic expression. By bridging computational science and dance theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for preserving intangible cultural heritage, enhancing dance pedagogy, and fostering collaborative creativity at the intersection of art and technology.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research project addresses the critical need for advanced computational tools in the analysis of Hungarian literary texts and their linguistic evolution, particularly in tracing morphological and syntactic shifts across historical periods. While Hungarian philology has a rich tradition of manual textual analysis, the increasing availability of digitized archives—including 19th-century manuscripts, early print materials, and contemporary literature—demands scalable methods to identify patterns in lexical usage, grammatical structures, and stylistic innovations. Current challenges include processing large corpora with diacritic-rich orthography, managing archaic vocabulary, and modeling dialectal variations in pre-standardization texts. This project will deploy high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-stage computational pipeline: first, training transformer-based models on domain-specific Hungarian texts to improve tokenization and morphological disambiguation; second, applying graph-based algorithms to map semantic networks in literary works; and third, conducting comparative analyses of syntactic complexity across genres using parallelized dependency parsing. The workflow will integrate existing NLP tools adapted for Hungarian’s agglutinative structure with custom scripts for frequency distribution analysis and stylometric profiling. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of 10,000+ historical and modern Hungarian texts, quantitative frameworks for assessing linguistic change, and visualizations of intertextual relationships in canonical works. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across centuries of Magyar literature, this research will advance scholarly understanding of language standardization processes, authorial influence networks, and the interplay between linguistic innovation and cultural identity. The computational resources requested are essential to handle memory-intensive tasks such as training specialized language models and processing multi-gigabyte text collections, which exceed the capacity of standard academic computing infrastructure. This project bridges computational linguistics with traditional literary studies, offering a replicable methodology for Uralic language research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hungarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and linguistic mechanisms underlying variability in second language (L2) developmental trajectories using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral data analysis. Despite advances in second language acquisition (SLA) research, significant gaps persist in understanding how individual differences in cognitive control, linguistic exposure, and instructional interventions interact to shape learning outcomes. Traditional methods, constrained by small datasets and limited computational capacity, struggle to capture the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between these factors. To address this, we propose a multidisciplinary approach integrating psycholinguistic theory, longitudinal learner corpora, and high-performance computing (HPC) to model L2 acquisition processes. The research will develop and train neural network models to simulate language learning under varying conditions of input quality, cognitive load, and pedagogical strategies. Parallelized processing will enable the analysis of multi-terabyte datasets comprising longitudinal speech, writing, and eye-tracking data from diverse L2 learners. Key computational tasks include natural language processing (NLP) for feature extraction from learner corpora, Bayesian hierarchical modeling to quantify individual differences, and reinforcement learning frameworks to optimize simulated instructional scenarios. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale and complexity of these analyses, particularly for training transformer-based models on unstructured linguistic data and running millions of parameter permutations in cognitive simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for predicting L2 proficiency trajectories based on learner profiles, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive language teaching methodologies, and (3) open-access tools for analyzing learner interactions in real-world educational contexts. By elucidating the computational principles of language acquisition, this work aims to advance SLA theory while providing practical insights for personalized language instruction. The project underscores the growing role of HPC in addressing non-uniform, high-dimensional research problems in the humanities and interdisciplinary social sciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, and maintenance of second languages. Includes instruction in language pedagogy, use, analysis and processes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing resource allocation in large-scale, stochastic operational systems, with applications in healthcare logistics and manufacturing supply chains. A core challenge in these domains is balancing competing objectives—such as cost minimization, service-level adherence, and resilience to disruptions—under uncertainty in demand, processing times, and resource availability. Existing methods often rely on simplifying assumptions that limit real-world applicability or fail to scale to industry-relevant problem sizes. To address this gap, we propose an integrated approach combining two-stage stochastic programming, simulation-based digital twin modeling, and parallelized reinforcement learning. The stochastic programming component will formalize multi-objective trade-offs using mixed-integer optimization models with scenario trees capturing demand and supply uncertainties. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the generation and evaluation of thousands of scenarios through distributed Monte Carlo simulations, implemented via MPI-based task parallelism. A digital twin of the operational environment will be developed using discrete-event simulation techniques to validate optimization results under dynamic conditions. For real-time adaptive decision-making, we will train deep reinforcement learning agents on HPC clusters using GPU-accelerated neural networks to approximate optimal policies for dynamic resource reallocation. The computational workflow will leverage containerized environments for reproducibility and hybrid OpenMP-MPI parallelization to efficiently manage memory-intensive scenario analyses. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source algorithmic implementations for stochastic resource allocation, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing solution quality and computational efficiency across problem scales, and (3) case studies demonstrating 10-20% cost reductions in hospital bed allocation and production line workforce scheduling under uncertainty. This work will advance operations research methodology by bridging gaps between traditional optimization and modern machine learning techniques while providing decision-support tools for practitioners in critical infrastructure sectors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research at the intersection of history, linguistics, and literary studies. The central research problem addresses the dynamic interplay between sociopolitical transformations and linguistic evolution in premodern European literary traditions, particularly in multilingual regions such as the Iberian Peninsula and the Balkans. Traditional methods of textual analysis struggle to systematically analyze the vast, heterogeneous corpora of manuscripts, legal documents, and literary works produced between the 12th and 17th centuries, which are critical to understanding how historical events—such as territorial conflicts, religious shifts, and trade networks—shaped vernacular languages and literary expression. To address this gap, the project proposes a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and geospatial modeling. NLP pipelines will be developed to process digitized texts in Latin, medieval Romance languages, and Slavic languages, identifying semantic shifts, lexical borrowing, and stylistic adaptations across genres and periods. Graph-based network models will map the diffusion of literary motifs and linguistic features against historical trade routes and political boundaries, while geospatial tools will visualize regional patterns of cultural exchange. HPC resources are essential to train transformer-based language models on fragmented, noisy historical texts, perform large-scale parallelized analysis of metadata-rich corpora, and simulate diffusion processes across centuries. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts, interactive visualizations of language-culture interactions, and a methodological framework for computational historico-literary studies. This work will provide novel insights into the coevolution of language and power structures in multicultural societies, while establishing scalable computational workflows for humanities scholarship. The results will be disseminated through open-access publications, a project-specific portal, and collaborations with digital humanities networks.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from history and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; linguistics; literature, philology; and studies of specific periods, issues and cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of non-perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD) in extreme conditions, focusing on the emergent properties of quark-gluon systems and their role in the confinement problem. A central challenge in elementary particle physics lies in resolving the dynamics of strongly interacting matter, where traditional perturbative methods fail. Current experimental efforts, such as heavy-ion collision studies and high-energy scattering experiments, generate data requiring precise theoretical benchmarks, yet computational limitations hinder first-principles predictions for systems with complex vacuum structures. To address this, we propose large-scale lattice QCD simulations using Monte Carlo methods to compute key observables, including hadronic spectral functions, equation-of-state parameters, and correlation functions in finite-temperature and high-density regimes. The simulations will employ improved staggered fermion discretizations on 4D Euclidean lattices with volumes up to \(64^3 \times 128\), requiring iterative solver algorithms and multi-grid techniques to mitigate critical slowing down. Our workflow integrates the Chroma software suite with custom GPU-optimized kernels to maximize efficiency on high-performance computing architectures. The requested resources will enable ensemble generation at near-physical pion masses and fine lattice spacings, reducing systematic uncertainties. Expected outcomes include refined predictions for quark-gluon plasma phase boundaries, insights into the hadronization process, and constraints on the QCD phase diagram relevant to next-generation collider experiments. Additionally, the project will produce open-source code optimizations for lattice QCD applications, benefiting the broader particle physics community. By bridging gaps between theoretical predictions and experimental observables, this work aims to elucidate fundamental aspects of confinement and chiral symmetry breaking, with implications for beyond-Standard Model scenarios involving strongly coupled sectors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the basic constituents of sub-atomic matter and energy, and the forces governing fundamental processes. Includes instruction in quantum theory, field theory, single-particle systems, perturbation and scattering theory, matter-radiation interaction, symmetry, quarks, capture, Schroedinger mechanics, methods for detecting particle emission and absorption, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: Periodontal disease, a leading cause of tooth loss and systemic health complications, involves complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and environmental factors. Current clinical and laboratory methods struggle to resolve the dynamic, multiscale processes driving disease progression, limiting the development of targeted therapies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model microbial-host interactions, predict disease trajectories, and optimize treatment strategies. We propose an integrative computational framework combining multi-omics data analysis, agent-based modeling, and machine learning to investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of periodontal pathogenesis. Metagenomic sequencing data from subgingival plaque samples (n=1,200) will be analyzed to map microbial community shifts during disease transitions. Concurrently, single-cell RNA sequencing of gingival tissue will characterize host immune cell heterogeneity and inflammatory pathways. These datasets will inform a multiscale agent-based model simulating biofilm formation, immune cell recruitment, and bone resorption dynamics under varying clinical conditions. Machine learning algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response using longitudinal clinical data paired with microbial and molecular profiles. The computational workflow requires HPC resources to manage large-scale data integration, parallelize simulations across parameter spaces, and train deep learning models on high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone pathogens and host pathways driving irreversible tissue damage, (2) predictive models for personalized treatment planning, and (3) in silico testing of novel therapeutic interventions targeting biofilm-immune crosstalk. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of periodontitis while providing a scalable computational platform for translational research in oral immunobiology. By elucidating disease mechanisms at unprecedented resolution, the project aligns with clinical priorities in periodontology to reduce therapeutic variability and improve long-term patient outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of patient intake and clinical workflows in ambulatory care settings demands innovative tools to optimize efficiency and accuracy. Medical assistants (MAs) play a critical role in bridging administrative and clinical tasks, yet current practices rely heavily on manual data entry, static protocols, and subjective triage decisions. This project proposes the development of an AI-driven clinical decision support system (CDSS) tailored to MAs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate real-time multi-modal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), wearable sensor outputs, and voice-recorded patient narratives—into actionable insights. The research problem centers on mitigating workflow bottlenecks and diagnostic inaccuracies during preliminary patient assessments, which can delay care and strain clinical resources. Using a combination of natural language processing (NLP) for symptom documentation, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for analyzing dermatological images (e.g., rashes, wounds), and time-series modeling of vital signs, the system will generate probabilistic risk assessments to prioritize urgent cases and suggest context-specific clinical protocols. Computational challenges include training models on heterogeneous datasets with inherent noise (e.g., fragmented EHR entries, variable sensor accuracy) and ensuring low-latency inference to support real-time workflows. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization for model training, synthetic data generation to address privacy-preserving data scarcity, and validation through simulated clinical scenarios. Expected outcomes include a deployable CDSS prototype validated against retrospective clinical data, with performance benchmarks targeting a 20-30% reduction in triage errors and 15% improvement in patient throughput during pilot testing. This interdisciplinary work sits at the intersection of clinical operations, edge computing, and adaptive AI, offering a novel framework to enhance the scope and precision of medical assistants’ roles while maintaining alignment with physician oversight and ethical guidelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical office administrative services and perform clinical duties including patient intake and care, routine diagnostic and recording procedures, pre-examination and examination assistance, and the administration of medications and first aid. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology; medical terminology; medical law and ethics; patient psychology and communications; medical office procedures; and clinical diagnostic, examination, testing, and treatment procedures.

abstract: Athletic injuries pose significant challenges to musculoskeletal health, often resulting in prolonged recovery, chronic disability, or premature career termination for athletes. Current injury prevention and management strategies are limited by insufficient understanding of the dynamic, multifactorial interactions between biomechanical forces, tissue adaptation, and rehabilitation protocols. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing computational models to predict injury risks, optimize rehabilitation pathways, and personalize return-to-play decisions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate large-scale datasets, including biomechanical motion capture, wearable sensor outputs, medical imaging, and longitudinal electronic health records. Multiscale finite element modeling will simulate stress distribution across musculoskeletal tissues during sport-specific movements, while machine learning algorithms will identify patterns associated with injury susceptibility and recovery outcomes. A key innovation involves coupling patient-specific anatomical data with real-time biomechanical metrics to create adaptive, predictive frameworks for injury prevention. Computational demands include parallel processing for finite element simulations of complex joint systems (e.g., knee, shoulder), GPU-accelerated deep learning for multimodal data fusion, and high-memory nodes for population-level statistical analyses. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated predictive models for common sports injuries (e.g., ACL tears, rotator cuff pathology), (2) data-driven guidelines for load management and rehabilitation dosing, and (3) open-source tools for clinical decision support. By elucidating the computational relationships between mechanical stressors, tissue responses, and recovery trajectories, this work aims to transform evidence-based practice in orthopedic sports medicine, reducing injury recurrence rates and improving long-term musculoskeletal health outcomes across diverse athlete populations.
cip_definition: Research on how to prevent and manage athletic injuries and to provide appropriate care for all structures of the musculoskeletal system directly affected by participation in sporting activity.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the efficacy of personalized, technology-assisted learning interventions for adolescents with diverse socioemotional and cognitive profiles, using computational modeling to optimize resource allocation in educational settings. Despite evidence supporting tailored interventions, scalable methods to dynamically match learners with contextually appropriate strategies—particularly in real-world classrooms—remain underdeveloped. The research integrates longitudinal data from 15 middle schools, including student performance metrics, behavioral engagement logs, and psychosocial surveys, to model how individual differences in self-regulation, motivation, and executive functioning mediate intervention outcomes. A high-performance computing (HPC) environment is required to implement parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms that simulate multi-agent classroom interactions under varying intervention conditions. These simulations will iteratively test hypotheses about optimal feedback timing, peer group composition, and adaptive task difficulty adjustments while accounting for instructor workload constraints. Additionally, natural language processing pipelines will analyze qualitative data from student-instructor interactions to refine model parameters. The computational demands stem from processing high-dimensional temporal data (≈50TB) across heterogeneous student subgroups and running millions of counterfactual simulation scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for predicting intervention success probabilities based on learner profiles, (2) evidence-based guidelines for balancing personalization with practical implementation limits in schools, and (3) open-source tools enabling educators to simulate intervention impacts using localized data. By elucidating how computational resources can mirror the complexity of human learning processes, this work aims to advance equitable resource distribution in educational psychology while maintaining methodological rigor appropriate for counseling-oriented applications. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the recursive optimization loops and large-scale pattern recognition inherent in modeling developmental trajectories across diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: The rapid integration of urban ecosystems and human-modified landscapes has created complex challenges for biodiversity conservation, requiring novel approaches that bridge ecological modeling, spatial data science, and urban planning. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to predict how heterogeneous urban environments influence species persistence and ecosystem resilience at regional scales. Current models often oversimplify the interplay between fine-grained habitat fragmentation, microclimate variability, and species behavior, limiting their utility for adaptive urban design. To address this gap, we propose coupling high-resolution geospatial datasets—including LiDAR-derived 3D urban structures, IoT sensor networks, and citizen science biodiversity observations—with agent-based simulations and machine learning to model multi-species responses to dynamic urban conditions. The computational workflow will integrate graph neural networks to analyze habitat connectivity, physics-informed neural operators to simulate microclimate cascades, and reinforcement learning to optimize conservation interventions. This requires high-performance computing resources to manage petabyte-scale environmental datasets, parallelize spatially explicit simulations across thousands of urban grid cells, and train generative models for scenario exploration. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform enabling municipalities to evaluate the ecological impact of infrastructure projects in near-real time, with pilot applications focused on pollinator corridor design and heat island mitigation. By fusing ecological theory with scalable data science methods, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for urban biodiversity analytics, directly informing policy frameworks that balance development needs with ecosystem health. The computational infrastructure developed will be adaptable to other interdisciplinary challenges requiring the synthesis of hyper-local environmental data with complex system dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis of large scale data sources from the interdisciplinary perspectives of applied statistics, computer science, data storage, data representation, data modeling, mathematics, and statistics. Includes instruction in computer algorithms, computer programming, data management, data mining, information policy, information retrieval, mathematical modeling, quantitative analysis, statistics, trend spotting, and visual analytics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interplay between multinational corporate structures, international tax law compliance, and regulatory enforcement mechanisms. The research problem centers on the lack of granular, dynamic simulations capable of analyzing how evolving tax avoidance strategies—particularly those involving digital services, intangible assets, and cross-jurisdictional profit shifting—respond to heterogeneous legal frameworks. Current policy evaluations rely on static datasets and simplified economic assumptions, failing to capture the adaptive behaviors of corporate entities operating across 190+ distinct tax regimes with conflicting incentives. The project will develop an agent-based computational model integrating three core components: (1) a multi-jurisdictional legal engine parsing tax treaty networks, transfer pricing rules, and anti-avoidance provisions; (2) a behavioral module simulating corporate decision-making under bounded rationality; and (3) a network analysis layer mapping spillover effects between national tax bases. By parameterizing over 15,000 real-world bilateral tax treaties and 50 years of OECD guidance, the model will simulate strategic interactions between firms and regulators at unprecedented scale, requiring parallelized computation for Monte Carlo experiments testing 100+ policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for predicting unintended consequences of tax reforms, quantitative metrics for measuring regulatory arbitrage risks in emerging digital economy sectors, and evidence-based recommendations for harmonizing disparate anti-avoidance regimes. The computational approach bridges legal text analysis, game-theoretic modeling, and large-scale economic simulation—advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational law and international tax policy while remaining firmly grounded in doctrinal legal research imperatives.
cip_title: International Business, Trade, and Tax Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing transnational business and commercial practices, including the specialized tax law related to international financial transactions.

abstract: Forest ecosystems play a critical role in global carbon cycling and biodiversity conservation, yet their resilience to climate change remains poorly quantified at regional scales. This project addresses the urgent need to model complex interactions between forest dynamics, climate variability, and anthropogenic disturbances to inform adaptive management strategies. Current limitations stem from the high dimensionality of ecological datasets—including multi-decadal remote sensing data, species distribution records, and eddy covariance flux measurements—and the computational intensity of integrating these with process-based forest growth models. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize and execute an ensemble of spatially explicit simulations across heterogeneous landscapes in the Pacific Northwest, USA. These simulations will couple a modified version of the Ecosystem Demography model (ED-2) with machine learning algorithms to assimilate LiDAR-derived canopy structure data and climate projections from CMIP6. Key computational challenges include scaling Bayesian calibration workflows across millions of grid cells, optimizing memory-intensive raster operations, and running Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses under alternative disturbance regimes. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of 10-meter resolution simulations over 50-year horizons, substantially improving upon current coarse-grained approaches. Expected outcomes include (1) probabilistic maps of carbon sequestration potential under varying emission scenarios, (2) identification of threshold responses in forest mortality linked to drought-fire feedbacks, and (3) open-source tools for real-time updating of forest vulnerability indices. By quantifying landscape-scale tradeoffs between carbon storage capacity and biodiversity hotspots, this work will directly support state agencies in prioritizing conservation investments. The computational framework developed here will be extensible to other temperate forests facing climate-driven regime shifts, advancing predictive ecology while addressing critical resource management needs.
cip_definition: Any program in forestry, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Infectious disease transmission dynamics in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are shaped by complex interactions between biological, social, and environmental factors. Current approaches to optimizing intervention strategies often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture spatial heterogeneity, population mobility, and evolving pathogen behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing an integrated computational framework to simulate disease spread and evaluate targeted public health interventions under resource-constrained conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based models (ABMs) coupled with machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-source data spanning demographic, epidemiological, and socioeconomic variables from three LMIC regions with high burdens of malaria, tuberculosis, and vaccine-preventable diseases.
