The computational workflow will simulate transmission scenarios across diverse urban-rural geographies while incorporating real-world constraints such as vaccine supply chains, healthcare workforce availability, and seasonal migration patterns. Bayesian inference methods will be applied to calibrate models using historical outbreak data, followed by scenario testing to compare the cost-effectiveness of alternative intervention packages. The computational demands of simultaneously modeling millions of agents across parameter spaces reflecting regional variability necessitate parallelized computing and large-scale data integration capabilities. Expected outcomes include identifying context-specific thresholds for herd immunity, optimizing clinic placement strategies, and predicting resource allocation trade-offs under climate change projections. Results will be disseminated through an open-access decision support toolkit designed for health ministries, enabling evidence-based prioritization of limited resources. This work advances methodological innovation in computational public health while directly addressing Sustainable Development Goal targets for equitable health access. Successful implementation requires sustained HPC access to manage memory-intensive simulations and iterative model refinement cycles over an 18-month period.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: Non-profit and public organizations face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation under dynamic constraints, including fluctuating funding, shifting community needs, and regulatory uncertainties. Existing decision-making frameworks often rely on simplified models that fail to capture the interdependencies between operational variables or scale effectively for large, multi-site organizations. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate and optimize resource allocation strategies for non-profit organizations operating in uncertain environments. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques, integrating heterogeneous datasets such as historical donation patterns, program outcomes, demographic trends, and real-time operational data from partner organizations. Computational experiments will simulate scenarios including crisis response, long-term budget planning, and cross-departmental coordination under varying constraints. By parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, the HPC environment will enable sensitivity analyses to identify critical leverage points in organizational decision-making. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario testing, evidence-based recommendations for adaptive resource allocation policies, and generalizable insights into the resilience of non-profit operational models. The project will advance computational social science methodologies in public management while providing practical tools to improve organizational efficiency and social impact. Results will be validated through partnerships with three regional non-profits, ensuring translational relevance. This work addresses a critical gap in data-driven management strategies for mission-driven organizations, with potential applications in disaster response coordination, educational program scaling, and community health resource distribution.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the business affairs of non-profit corporations, including foundations, educational institutions, associations, and other such organizations, and public agencies and governmental operations. Includes instruction in business management, principles of public administration, principles of accounting and financial management, human resources management, taxation of non-profit organizations, and business law as applied to non-profit organizations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of efficiently managing and securing large-scale medical data systems in clinical environments, which are increasingly strained by high-volume electronic health records (EHRs), diagnostic imaging, and real-time telemedicine applications. Medical offices face critical bottlenecks in processing speed, data interoperability, and compliance with evolving regulatory standards (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR), compounded by the need to integrate legacy systems with modern cloud-based platforms. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a scalable, AI-driven framework for optimizing medical software performance and cybersecurity. Computational workflows will include parallelized simulations of multi-site EHR networks to model data traffic patterns, machine learning algorithms to detect vulnerabilities in proprietary medical software, and GPU-accelerated testing of encryption protocols for patient data transmission. Additionally, we will benchmark the interoperability of open-source and commercial health informatics tools under simulated high-load scenarios, assessing latency and error rates. The project will utilize containerized environments to replicate diverse clinical IT infrastructures, enabling rapid iteration of system configurations. Outcomes will include predictive models for hardware resource allocation in medical offices, a validated toolkit for auditing compliance-ready software deployments, and open-access benchmarks for telemedicine platform scalability. By addressing computational bottlenecks in medical office IT systems, this work aims to reduce operational downtime, enhance data security, and support the cost-effective adoption of emerging technologies in healthcare settings. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of synthetic and anonymized clinical datasets, train deep learning models for anomaly detection, and execute large-scale network simulations that mirror real-world medical office environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance decision-support frameworks for adaptive logistics planning in contested multi-domain environments, a critical challenge in modern military operations. Traditional logistical models, optimized for static or predictable scenarios, struggle to account for the dynamic interdependencies and adversarial disruptions inherent in hybrid warfare contexts, such as cyber-physical attacks on supply networks or rapid resource reallocation demands. To address this gap, the project will develop a computational architecture integrating agent-based modeling, real-time risk assessment algorithms, and scenario trees to simulate cascading disruptions across land, maritime, and digital domains. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulation of thousands of contingency pathways, incorporating stochastic variables like weather patterns, adversarial behavior models, and infrastructure fragility. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical operational data and synthetic scenarios to identify resilient resource allocation patterns and failure thresholds. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for generating contingency playbooks that balance pre-positioning efficiency with adaptive redistribution capacity, validated against case studies from joint exercises. By quantifying trade-offs between redundancy, response latency, and vulnerability to emerging threats, this work aims to provide actionable insights for improving strategic readiness while maintaining computational tractability in resource-constrained environments. The project’s interdisciplinary approach bridges military logistics theory, computational game theory, and data-driven optimization, addressing a niche critical to next-generation defense planning but underrepresented in conventional science and engineering research paradigms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to enhance the precision and efficiency of large-scale geospatial data processing in modern surveying applications. Traditional methods for analyzing high-resolution topographic data, such as LiDAR point clouds and photogrammetric surveys, struggle with computational bottlenecks when handling datasets spanning hundreds of square kilometers. These limitations impede rapid error correction, integration of multi-source geospatial data, and real-time adjustments critical for applications like infrastructure planning or environmental monitoring. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize key workflows, including least-squares adjustment of geodetic networks, automated feature extraction via machine learning models, and error propagation modeling across heterogeneous datasets. Custom algorithms will be implemented using MPI and OpenMP to distribute tasks across nodes, optimizing memory usage for sparse matrix operations common in adjustment calculations. Deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based networks) will be trained on GPU clusters to improve recognition of boundary features in noisy or incomplete survey data. The computational pipeline will integrate existing geospatial libraries (GDAL, PDAL) with PyTorch-based models for end-to-end processing. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in processing time for terabyte-scale surveys compared to current industry standards, along with improved sub-centimeter accuracy in deformation analysis for landslide risk assessment use cases. The resulting open-source tools will enable surveying professionals to handle emerging challenges posed by climate-driven landscape changes and high-frequency monitoring requirements. By coupling HPC-optimized workflows with domain-specific validation metrics, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical geodesy and practical, large-area surveying operations while establishing benchmarks for computational efficiency in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the delineation, determination, planning and positioning of land tracts, land and water boundaries, land contours and features; and the preparation of related maps, charts and reports. Includes instruction in applied geodesy, computer graphics, photointerpretation, plane and geodetic surveying, mensuration, traversing, survey equipment operation and maintenance, instrument calibration, and basic cartography.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale literary corpora, advancing methodological innovations in computational literary studies. While traditional close reading remains foundational to literary analysis, the scale and complexity of available digitized texts—spanning centuries, genres, and cultural contexts—present challenges for manual examination. This research addresses the need for scalable, systematic approaches to identify macro-level patterns in literary production, such as shifts in narrative structure, thematic recurrence, or stylistic evolution across time. The primary computational focus involves developing and refining natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to process and analyze heterogeneous literary datasets, including novels, poetry, and drama from the 18th century to the present. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for context-aware semantic analysis, implementing graph-based algorithms to map intertextual networks, and applying unsupervised clustering techniques to detect latent stylistic or thematic groupings. A pilot study on 19th-century British novels demonstrated preliminary success in tracing the diffusion of Gothic tropes, but scaling this to multi-genre, transnational corpora requires HPC capabilities for distributed storage, parallel processing, and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a reusable computational framework for diachronic literary analysis, (2) empirical insights into genre hybridity and canon formation, and (3) public datasets annotated with computational metadata to support reproducibility. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to bridge methodological divides in literary scholarship, offering new tools to interrogate the relationships between form, content, and cultural change at scale. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale text collections, reduce runtime for iterative model training, and facilitate high-dimensional visualization of literary networks—tasks infeasible on standard institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on literature from one or more genres, cultures or traditions. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and studies of various types of literary text.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven computational framework to optimize dynamic risk assessment in high-hazard industrial processes, addressing critical gaps in traditional static or heuristic-based process safety methodologies. Current risk assessment models often fail to account for real-time operational variability, interdependencies between failure modes, and cascading effects in complex systems, leading to reactive rather than proactive safety interventions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose implementing multi-scale simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning to model accident propagation pathways under diverse operational scenarios. The computational approach will couple finite element analysis for equipment-level failure modeling with system-level Bayesian network simulations to quantify probabilistic risk chains, while reinforcement learning algorithms will identify optimal mitigation strategies under uncertainty. Key challenges include managing the combinatorial complexity of interacting process variables across temporal scales and the computational intensity of iteratively training predictive models on large-scale incident datasets. The requested HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10^5+ scenario permutations, real-time sensitivity analyses for non-linear process interactions, and accelerated convergence of optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for proactive risk visualization, predictive thresholds for early hazard detection, and adaptive safety decision-support tools benchmarked against industrial case studies. This work aims to advance process safety paradigms from compliance-driven frameworks to intelligent, resilience-oriented systems, with direct applications in chemical manufacturing, energy infrastructure, and hazardous material handling. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source modules to support academic and industrial collaborations in safety-critical domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing methods to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in design for injury prevention, engineering for process safety, environmental psychology, function-based risk analysis, fundamentals of industrial engineering, operations research, probability and statistics, risk assessment and reduction, and safety engineering.

abstract: This research seeks to address inefficiencies in law enforcement resource allocation through the development of a dynamic, data-driven simulation framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC). Traditional resource distribution models in policing often rely on static crime statistics and historical patterns, failing to adapt to real-time shifts in criminal behavior, community needs, or operational constraints. The project will construct an agent-based model simulating urban crime dynamics, officer patrol routes, and emergency response protocols under variable conditions such as seasonal crime trends, special events, and budget fluctuations. By integrating machine learning algorithms with geospatial crime data, demographic indicators, and anonymized body-worn camera metadata, the model will generate probabilistic risk maps and test adaptive resource allocation strategies. Computational demands include large-scale parallelism for Monte Carlo simulations of scenario permutations, natural language processing of incident reports to identify emerging patterns, and real-time optimization of patrol deployments using graph-based routing algorithms. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between response times, officer workload equity, and community trust metrics. The framework will be validated against historical dispatch records from three mid-sized U.S. cities, with sensitivity analyses to evaluate robustness across diverse jurisdictional contexts. This work bridges computational criminology and operations research, offering a novel methodological approach to public safety administration while addressing ethical AI considerations through transparency protocols for algorithmic recommendations. Successful implementation could inform policy frameworks for adaptive policing strategies that balance efficiency with procedural justice imperatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply theories and practices of organization management and criminal justice to the administration of public law enforcement agencies and operations. Includes instruction in law enforcement history and theory, operational command leadership, administration of public police organizations, labor relations, incident response strategies, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to enhance the diagnostic accuracy and predictive modeling of pathologies in the oral and maxillofacial region using high-resolution 3D imaging. Current clinical workflows for interpreting cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), MRI, and multispectral imaging data face challenges in detecting early-stage diseases—such as osteonecrosis, temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders, and occult fractures—due to subtle anatomical variations, artifacts, and the complexity of overlapping structures. To address this, we propose a multi-stage deep learning framework to automate segmentation, artifact reduction, and predictive analysis of volumetric imaging datasets. The computational pipeline will integrate convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for voxel-wise classification of bone and soft tissue pathologies, generative adversarial networks (GANs) for artifact correction, and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model disease progression trajectories. Training and validating these models require processing terabytes of annotated clinical scans from multi-institutional cohorts, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized GPU-accelerated training, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale inference. The project will leverage containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility and federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for automated lesion detection, risk stratification of pathological changes, and quantitative biomarkers for treatment response monitoring. These outcomes aim to reduce diagnostic variability, enable earlier intervention, and improve personalized surgical planning in oral and maxillofacial radiology. The requested HPC allocation is critical to overcoming memory and runtime constraints associated with 3D medical image analysis, ensuring clinically feasible turnaround times for translating computational insights into patient care.
cip_definition: Research focused on producing and interpreting images of the jaws, teeth, bone, and other structures of the head and neck region; and to diagnose and manage diseases, disorders, and conditions that affect this area of the body.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of preparing mathematics educators to effectively support diverse learners in understanding complex mathematical concepts. Current teacher education programs often lack tools to model and analyze the dynamic, non-linear processes by which students develop conceptual mastery, particularly in algebra and geometry. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate student learning trajectories and evaluate pedagogical strategies at scale. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to represent heterogeneous student populations, incorporating cognitive, affective, and socio-cultural factors that influence mathematics learning. These models will be informed by empirical datasets from classroom observations, standardized assessments, and pre-service teacher interventions. Machine learning techniques, including clustering algorithms and recurrent neural networks, will identify patterns in mathematical misconception formation and persistence across simulated learning environments. The computational framework will enable systematic testing of instructional approaches under varied classroom conditions, providing quantitative metrics on strategy effectiveness. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to analyze over 10,000 distinct teaching scenarios, significantly exceeding the scope of traditional experimental designs. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based frameworks for personalizing mathematics instruction, (2) predictive models of student conceptual development to inform teacher decision-making, and (3) interactive training modules that help pre-service teachers anticipate and respond to common learning barriers. This work will advance mathematics teacher education by creating scalable tools to study pedagogical practices, ultimately supporting the preparation of educators who can better address equity gaps in STEM achievement. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces and iterative refinement processes required to generate actionable insights for teacher development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach mathematics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in cross-jurisdictional emergency response coordination during large-scale disasters, a challenge within homeland security and protective services that remains understudied in computational research. Current approaches to resource allocation among law enforcement, firefighting, and emergency management agencies often rely on static protocols ill-suited for dynamic, multi-threat scenarios such as compound disasters (e.g., wildfires coinciding with cyber-physical infrastructure failures). The research proposes developing an adaptive decision-support framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interdependencies between personnel deployment, equipment logistics, and real-time threat evolution. Computational methods will integrate agent-based modeling to simulate responder behavior under stress, graph neural networks to map critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, and ensemble forecasting to predict cascading risks. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the team will conduct parameter sweeps across thousands of synthetic disaster scenarios varying in scale, hazard combinations, and inter-agency communication constraints. Key outcomes include probabilistic resource allocation templates optimized for rare but high-consequence events and a sensitivity analysis toolkit to identify systemic bottlenecks in existing response networks. The computational outputs will inform policy recommendations for interoperable resource-sharing agreements and training protocols for multi-agency command structures. This work fills a gap in applied computational research for emergency management, offering scalable methods to enhance resilience in public safety systems where traditional operations research approaches fail to account for emergent cross-domain threats. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling human-infrastructure interactions during crisis conditions, directly supporting the development of next-generation emergency response frameworks.
cip_title: Homeland Security, Law Enforcement, Firefighting and Related Protective Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, law enforcement, firefighting, and related protective services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable horticultural practices necessitates a deeper understanding of plant-environment interactions under variable climatic conditions. Current challenges in optimizing plant growth, yield, and resilience stem from the complex interplay of genetic, physiological, and environmental factors, which are difficult to model using traditional experimental approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale computational models that simulate plant responses to abiotic stressors, such as drought, temperature fluctuations, and soil nutrient variability, across diverse horticultural species. By integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and phenomic datasets with environmental parameters, these models will predict adaptive traits and growth patterns under projected climate scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify key genetic markers and metabolic pathways associated with stress tolerance, while agent-based modeling will simulate crop performance in dynamic agricultural systems. The computational framework will be calibrated using experimental data from controlled greenhouse trials and field observations. Access to HPC resources is critical to manage the high dimensionality of omics data, perform parallelized simulations, and optimize predictive accuracy through iterative model refinement. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate plant varieties with enhanced resilience, data-driven recommendations for precision irrigation and nutrient management, and open-source tools for real-time decision support in horticultural operations. This research will directly address gaps in scalable, climate-adaptive horticulture, providing actionable insights for growers, breeders, and policymakers to improve crop productivity and resource efficiency in a warming world.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general production and processing of domesticated plants, shrubs, flowers, foliage, trees, groundcovers, and related plant materials; the management of technical and business operations connected with horticultural services; and the basic scientific principles needed to understand plants and their management and care.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale comparative analyses of syntactic, semantic, and stylistic patterns across understudied modern languages and their literary traditions. While computational methods have transformed linguistic and literary research, their application remains disproportionately focused on widely spoken languages, leaving regional and minority languages underrepresented in digital scholarship. This gap limits our understanding of global linguistic diversity and its cultural intersections. To address this, our research will employ parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze multilingual corpora spanning 15+ languages, including Indigenous and diasporic varieties, with a focus on morphosyntactic variation, dialectal evolution, and cross-cultural narrative structures. The computational workflow integrates transformer-based models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, geospatial-temporal mapping of dialect features, and graph-based network analysis to trace literary influence across linguistic boundaries. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models, processing terabytes of digitized texts and speech data, and simulating language-contact scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: (1) novel frameworks for quantifying stylistic and structural convergence in multilingual literature, (2) open-access tools for automated analysis of under-resourced languages, and (3) high-resolution visualizations of dialect boundaries correlated with sociocultural factors. By enabling computationally intensive, cross-linguistic comparisons at unprecedented scale, this project will provide foundational insights into language preservation, the diffusion of literary forms, and the role of technology in sustaining linguistic diversity. Results will be disseminated through an interactive platform for collaborative humanities research, fostering interdisciplinary partnerships between computational linguists, literary scholars, and language communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more modern foreign languages that is not specific as to the name of the language(s) studied; that is otherwise undifferentiated; or that introduces students to language studies at the basic/elementary level.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of hybrid human-AI decision-making teams in organizational settings, leveraging computational modeling to understand how cognitive diversity and algorithmic transparency influence collective outcomes. Traditional organizational behavior research has struggled to capture the real-time, nonlinear interactions between human agents and adaptive AI systems, particularly in high-stakes environments such as financial forecasting or supply chain optimization. To address this gap, we propose developing a large-scale agent-based model (ABM) simulating mixed teams across diverse decision architectures. The model will incorporate empirically validated behavioral parameters from organizational psychology, reinforcement learning algorithms for AI agents, and dynamic network structures reflecting modern distributed workplaces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: 1) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore parameter spaces across 10^6+ team configurations, 2) real-time evolutionary optimization of AI policies through differentiable simulation techniques, and 3) natural language processing of synthetic team communication logs using transformer-based architectures. Expected outcomes include a computational framework predicting optimal human-AI composition thresholds under varying task complexities, quantitative metrics for "explainability overhead" in hybrid teams, and evidence-based protocols for organizational adoption of collaborative AI systems. The results will advance theoretical understanding of human-machine complementarity while providing practical tools for managing the transition to AI-augmented workforce structures. By bridging computational social science with organizational behavior, this work addresses a critical gap in preparing businesses for asymmetric technological change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior and motivations of individuals functioning in organized groups, and its application to business and industrial settings. Includes instruction in organization theory, industrial and organizational psychology, social psychology, sociology of organizations, reinforcement and incentive theory, employee relations strategies, organizational power and influence, organization stratification and hierarchy, leadership styles, and applications of operations research and other methodologies to organizational analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing sustainable fabric selection and garment design in the context of personalized fashion consulting. The research addresses a critical gap in the fashion industry: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to balance aesthetic preferences, material sustainability, and cost efficiency during client consultations. Current practices rely heavily on heuristic expertise, leading to inconsistencies in recommendations and suboptimal environmental outcomes. By integrating computational modeling with textile science and consumer behavior data, this work aims to create a decision-support system that dynamically simulates fabric performance, environmental impact, and style outcomes across diverse scenarios. The computational approach combines machine learning models trained on historical client interaction data, finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating fabric drape and durability under varied conditions, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to reconcile competing design priorities. Key challenges include processing high-dimensional datasets encompassing textile properties (e.g., tensile strength, dye absorption) and client-specific parameters (body measurements, style preferences), necessitating parallelized computation for real-time analysis. Expected outcomes include a novel metric for quantifying "sustainability-adjusted aesthetic value" and an open-access API enabling consultants to generate optimized fabric-design pairings during client sessions. The project’s interdisciplinary significance lies in bridging gaps between computational sustainability, materials informatics, and consumer-facing fashion services, while its technical contribution centers on adapting HPC workflows to domains traditionally dominated by qualitative methodologies. Successful implementation could reduce textile waste by an estimated 15-20% per consultation cycle while maintaining client satisfaction, establishing a template for computational resource integration in non-STEM professional services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in apparel and fashion selection, style coordination, customer sales and consulting, fabric selection, clothing specifications, and contract buying activities. Includes instruction in supplying regular clothing needs or acting as a consultant for special events such as weddings.

abstract: Urban heat islands (UHIs) disproportionately impact marginalized communities, but integrating multi-scale environmental and social data to design equitable mitigation strategies remains computationally challenging. This project employs high-performance computing to analyze synergies between microclimate dynamics, urban morphology, and socioeconomic vulnerability across five major U.S. cities. We will develop a novel modeling framework coupling 3D urban canopy models at 1m resolution with machine learning-driven socioeconomic risk assessment, utilizing multi-source satellite imagery (Landsat-9, Sentinel-2), LiDAR-derived building morphology, and census tract-level demographic data. Computational workflows will parallelize microclimate simulations across 50,000 urban grid cells while maintaining integration with city-scale energy balance calculations. The HPC environment enables temporal upscaling of episodic heat events through wavelet analysis of decade-long ERA5-Land climate reanalysis data. Expected outcomes include identification of high-priority zones for green infrastructure deployment, quantified projections of heat stress reduction under alternative urban planning scenarios, and open-source tools for coupled socio-environmental modeling. This interdisciplinary approach advances spatial justice in climate adaptation by resolving the scale mismatch between physical processes and human vulnerability patterns, directly informing municipal sustainability policies and federal heat resilience initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on interactions between people and the natural and built environments. Includes instruction in climate science, sustainability, environmental science and policy, research methods, geographic information systems (GIS), human geography, physical geography, remote sensing, and public policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of sustainable, high-performance wood-based materials and optimize pulping processes through multiscale computational modeling. A critical challenge in wood science lies in understanding the molecular-scale interactions governing lignin removal during chemical pulping, which remains energy-intensive and environmentally impactful. Additionally, predicting the mechanical behavior of engineered wood products under dynamic environmental conditions requires resolving complex, hierarchical structures across scales—a task infeasible with traditional experimental methods alone. To address these gaps, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model lignin-polysaccharide networks in softwood and hardwood species under varying thermochemical pulping conditions, identifying reaction pathways to improve delignification efficiency. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning will predict moisture-induced stress distributions in cross-laminated timber (CLT), integrating anisotropic material properties and hygrothermal effects. These computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from lab-scale pulping trials and mechanical testing. The HPC environment is essential for handling the >10^6-atom systems in MD, iterative parameter optimization in FEA, and large datasets linking microstructural features to macroscale performance. Anticipated outcomes include actionable strategies for reducing energy consumption in pulp production by 15–20% and frameworks for designing moisture-resistant CLT panels with extended service life. By bridging molecular insights to industrial-scale processes, this work aligns with natural resource conservation goals, offering pathways to decarbonize wood product manufacturing while enhancing material circularity. The generated models and datasets will be shared openly to accelerate innovation in sustainable forest product technologies.
cip_title: Wood Science and Wood Products/ Pulp and Paper Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the analysis of the properties and behavior of wood and wood products and the development of processes for converting wood into paper and other products. Includes instruction in wood classification and testing, product development, manufacturing and processing technologies, and the design and development of related equipment and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the detection and classification capabilities of undersea acoustic signals in contested environments through the development of high-fidelity computational models optimized for antisubmarine warfare (ASW) applications. Traditional signal processing methods struggle to distinguish low-signature submarines from complex background noise in shallow-water littoral zones, which are characterized by dynamic bathymetry, temperature gradients, and anthropogenic interference. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining physics-based acoustic propagation modeling with machine learning techniques to enhance target discrimination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of underwater soundscapes under varying operational conditions, including multi-static sonar configurations and clutter scenarios induced by marine life or civilian vessel traffic. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods will model broadband signal interactions with seabed structures, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on synthetic aperture sonar data will be deployed for real-time feature extraction. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated wave equation solvers with distributed training of deep learning architectures, requiring access to parallelized processing and high-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive sonar signal processing and quantitative metrics quantifying detection probability improvements in cluttered environments compared to legacy systems. By bridging physics-based simulation and data-driven analytics, this research aims to deliver actionable insights for next-generation ASW decision support systems while establishing scalable computational methodologies for undersea acoustic challenges at the intersection of defense technology and environmental complexity. The requested resources will directly support parametric studies across 10+ operational variables, reducing reliance on costly at-sea testing while accelerating algorithmic readiness for deployment on naval platforms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of acoustics and signals processing to undersea and antisubmarine warfare. Includes instruction in acoustics; electrical engineering; the generation, propagation and reception of underwater sound waves; military applications of underwater sound; and acoustic signal processing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in analyzing and synthesizing large-scale, high-resolution visual media datasets for applications in experimental film and computational photography. The research focuses on developing novel algorithms for real-time processing of multi-modal visual data—including 4K/8K video streams, 360-degree immersive footage, and gigapixel-scale photographic archives—to enable dynamic, AI-driven artistic workflows. A core problem lies in the inefficiency of conventional tools when handling non-linear narrative structures in interactive films or optimizing hyper-detailed image composites under time constraints, particularly when integrating machine learning models for style transfer or semantic segmentation. The proposed computational approach combines distributed rendering frameworks, GPU-accelerated neural networks, and adaptive compression techniques to process terabytes of visual data while preserving artistic intent. Key methods include parallelized training of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for photorealistic texture synthesis and deploying containerized pipelines for frame-accurate editing across heterogeneous media formats. Outcomes will advance computational aesthetics by producing open-source tools for scalable media manipulation, validated through case studies in collaborative virtual production and AI-augmented documentary filmmaking. By enabling artists to iteratively refine complex visual sequences without hardware limitations, this work aims to bridge gaps between data-driven creativity and technical feasibility, fostering new methodologies in digital visual storytelling. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as simulating real-world lighting dynamics in virtual sets or batch-processing decades of archival footage for generative heritage projects, which exceed the capacity of local workstations. Results will contribute to interdisciplinary dialogues at the intersection of media theory, computational art, and design innovation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_title: Film/ Video and Photographic Arts, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in film/video and photographic arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in designing scalable professional development programs for educational institutions by leveraging computational modeling to optimize resource allocation and program outcomes. Traditional approaches to professional development often rely on static frameworks that inadequately account for dynamic variables such as evolving institutional priorities, heterogeneous staff competencies, and fluctuating resource availability. To resolve this, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate organizational learning processes under diverse leadership strategies and resource constraints. These models will integrate longitudinal workforce data, including skill inventories, training participation records, and performance metrics from partner K-12 districts and higher education institutions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across multi-dimensional scenarios, enabling the identification of optimal intervention sequences and resource distribution patterns. Machine learning techniques will further refine model accuracy by correlating simulated outcomes with historical program success metrics. The computational workflow will employ parallelized simulations via MPI to test hypotheses about how leadership decisions—such as prioritizing technical training versus collaborative capacity building—affect long-term organizational adaptability. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between professional development investments and institutional performance indicators, such as staff retention and goal alignment. This work will advance leadership practices in educational administration by providing evidence-based strategies for aligning human resource development with organizational objectives. The resulting open-source framework will enable resource-constrained institutions to simulate tailored solutions, thereby enhancing equity in access to effective professional learning systems. By bridging computational social science with education leadership, the project contributes methodological innovations for studying complex organizational dynamics in human resource development.
cip_title: Education and Human Resource Studies/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the efficacy of digital pastoral care networks in addressing community-level spiritual and emotional needs, a critical but understudied dimension of lay ministry. While lay ministers increasingly operate in hybrid (in-person and virtual) environments, there is limited empirical understanding of how digital interactions influence pastoral outcomes, such as trust-building, crisis response, or long-term spiritual engagement. The research problem centers on mapping and modeling complex communication patterns across digital ministry platforms (e.g., video counseling logs, moderated forum discussions, and asynchronous prayer request systems) to identify scalable strategies for equitable, culturally responsive care. Using a mixed-methods computational approach, we will process multimodal datasets—including text, audio, and metadata from anonymized ministry interactions—through natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for theological discourse analysis. Advanced network modeling will map relational dynamics between lay ministers and communities, while sentiment analysis frameworks, trained on domain-specific lexicons (e.g., spiritual distress terminology), will quantify emotional and spiritual resonance in digital exchanges. HPC resources are essential due to the scale of data (projected 50,000+ interaction logs) and the need for real-time simulations testing intervention strategies across diverse demographic scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for assessing digital pastoral efficacy, (2) generative AI tools to simulate high-stakes ministry scenarios for training purposes, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing hybrid ministry workflows. By integrating computational social science with practical theology, this work aims to establish new methodologies for evaluating humanistic outcomes in religious care contexts, directly supporting the professional development of lay ministers serving underserved populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained individuals to serve as lay pastors, religious educators, youth leaders, and other professional positions open to the laity in local churches and other settings. Includes instruction in bible studies, theology, spirituality, pastoral counseling, foundations of ministry, effective communication, and church leadership.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computer hardware systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in energy efficiency, thermal management, and performance optimization at nanoscale geometries. This project aims to develop a scalable framework for simulating and optimizing next-generation integrated circuit architectures, focusing on mitigating electromigration, thermal hotspots, and signal integrity degradation in sub-7nm semiconductor devices. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-physics simulation approach combining finite-element analysis for electrothermal modeling, Monte Carlo methods for defect propagation analysis, and machine learning-driven optimization for physical layout refinement. The computational workflow will integrate open-source electronic design automation tools with custom CUDA-accelerated solvers to model transistor-level interactions across heterogeneous 3D chiplet architectures. By parallelizing time-domain circuit simulations across thousands of cores, we aim to achieve microsecond-scale operational analysis of full-chip designs while maintaining atomic-level fidelity in critical regions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for reliability-aware chip design, automated thermal management strategies for vertically stacked memory-processor configurations, and benchmark datasets for emerging beyond-CMOS technologies. This research will directly address the computational bottlenecks in hardware verification workflows, potentially reducing design iteration cycles by 40-60% compared to current industry-standard tools. The developed methods will be disseminated as modular components in the open-source SiliconCompass framework, enabling broader adoption in academic and industrial hardware engineering communities. Successful implementation of this project will advance the state of the art in computer hardware co-design methodologies while providing critical insights for sustainable scaling of computing performance within fundamental physical limits.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and evaluation of computer hardware and related peripheral equipment. Includes instruction in computer circuit and chip design, circuitry, computer systems design, computer equipment design, computer layout planning, testing procedures, and related computer theory and software topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Mongolian linguistic diversity and historical textuality by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current research in Mongolian philology and dialectology is constrained by the limited scalability of traditional methods when handling extensive corpora of both classical and contemporary texts, as well as oral literature recordings. The proposed research aims to systematically analyze morphological, syntactic, and lexical patterns across Mongolian dialects and historical periods using advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques and machine learning models. Key computational tasks include the development of parallelized pipelines for automated morphological segmentation, dialect classification via neural networks, and phonetic alignment algorithms for oral narrative preservation. By processing terabytes of textual and audio data across distributed nodes, HPC infrastructure will enable the identification of previously undocumented dialectal continua, the reconstruction of proto-forms, and the quantification of language contact effects. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of open-access annotated corpora, predictive models of linguistic change, and interactive visualization tools for scholarly use. These resources will significantly advance the field’s capacity to document endangered linguistic varieties, inform language revitalization initiatives, and enhance cross-disciplinary applications in areas such as multilingual NLP system development. The project’s computational demands—particularly in training transformer-based architectures on low-resource language data and conducting large-scale comparative analyses—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve rigorous, reproducible results within feasible timeframes.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Mongolian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; oral and written literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic spatial organization of cellular components and its impact on cell function in health and disease. A critical gap in cell biology lies in understanding how subcellular structures—such as organelles, cytoskeletal networks, and membrane systems—coordinate in three-dimensional space to regulate processes like intracellular transport, mechanical signaling, and structural adaptation. Traditional imaging and experimental approaches lack the resolution to model these interactions at the scale and complexity required to uncover system-level principles. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale 3D simulations of cellular environments with experimental data from advanced microscopy. Agent-based models will simulate the behavior of organelles and cytoskeletal elements under varying mechanical and biochemical conditions, while stochastic algorithms will map the probabilistic interactions driving localized molecular sorting and compartmentalization. These simulations will be parameterized using volumetric imaging datasets of mammalian cells, enabling iterative validation against empirical observations. The HPC environment is essential to handle the computational demands of modeling millions of interacting components in real time, as well as to perform parameter space explorations across diverse cell types and states. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how spatial misorganization of cellular architecture contributes to pathologies such as muscular dystrophy and age-related tissue degeneration. The resulting models will provide a predictive platform for testing hypotheses about structural adaptations during cell differentiation or stress responses. By bridging spatial cell biology with computational dynamics, this work will advance foundational knowledge of cellular anatomy and establish a scalable resource for the broader cell biology community to explore structural-function relationships in silico.
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cells, cellular systems, and the molecular basis of cell structure and function. Includes instruction in cell biology, cell chemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, and structural biology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the design and simulation of complex mechanical systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Mechanical drafting and CAD/CADD workflows increasingly require high-fidelity simulations to validate designs for manufacturability, structural integrity, and operational efficiency. However, traditional CAD tools struggle with the computational demands of multi-physics simulations (e.g., thermal-stress coupling, fluid-structure interactions) and large-scale parametric studies, particularly when applied to intricate assemblies or high-resolution geometries. This bottleneck limits the ability to explore design spaces efficiently and delays iterative improvements. To address this, the proposed research will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers tailored for mechanical drafting applications. These solvers will leverage GPU acceleration and distributed-memory architectures to handle meshes with >10^6 elements, enabling rapid evaluation of geometric variations under realistic operating conditions. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to predict stress concentrations, deformation thresholds, and manufacturing tolerances, integrating these predictions directly into CAD/CADD software via API-based frameworks. The outcomes will include optimized algorithms for automated geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) compliance, reduced computational overhead for multi-objective design optimization, and open-source templates for scalable simulation workflows. By bridging the gap between high-resolution simulation and practical drafting workflows, this work aims to enhance the precision of mechanical design processes, reduce prototyping costs, and support the adoption of additive manufacturing and other advanced production techniques. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary scale and speed for these computationally intensive tasks, which cannot be feasibly executed on local workstations.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in hospital-acquired infection (HAI) control through advanced computational modeling of resource allocation strategies. HAIs remain a critical challenge in healthcare systems, contributing to patient morbidity, prolonged hospital stays, and increased costs. Current approaches to mitigating HAIs often rely on static protocols that fail to adapt to dynamic hospital environments, variable patient flows, and resource constraints. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework to model pathogen transmission pathways and evaluate the impact of administrative decisions—such as staffing schedules, cleaning resource distribution, and equipment allocation—on infection rates. The computational model will integrate real-world data from electronic health records, environmental sensors, and staff movement patterns to simulate scenarios across diverse hospital units. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the scale of these simulations, which involve millions of agent interactions, stochastic event modeling, and parameter sweeps to identify optimal resource configurations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to refine predictive accuracy and generate actionable administrative guidelines. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool capable of recommending context-specific resource allocation strategies to minimize HAIs while balancing operational costs. This work will provide healthcare administrators with evidence-based strategies to enhance patient safety and operational efficiency, demonstrating the transformative potential of computational methods in health services management. The project’s findings will be disseminated through open-access simulation tools and partnerships with regional hospital networks to facilitate implementation.
cip_title: Health and Medical Administrative Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of pathology data, including high-resolution digital histopathology images, multi-omics datasets, and clinical records, present significant challenges for traditional analytical workflows. Current methods for pathological analysis often lack the computational scalability required to integrate and interpret these heterogeneous data types efficiently, limiting opportunities for precision diagnostics and biomarker discovery. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational workflows tailored for pathology applications. The primary research objective is to create a scalable, machine learning-driven platform for automated tissue annotation, multi-omics data integration, and predictive modeling of disease outcomes. The computational approach will utilize GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) to process whole-slide imaging data, identifying morphological patterns associated with specific pathologies. Concurrently, distributed computing architectures will enable the integration of genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets with clinical variables, employing graph neural networks to model complex biological interactions. A key innovation involves developing explainable AI models to maintain clinical interpretability while handling petabyte-scale data. The HPC infrastructure will support large-scale validation of these models across diverse patient cohorts, ensuring robustness across demographic and disease subtypes. Expected outcomes include: (1) optimized algorithms for rapid, automated analysis of pathological specimens, reducing diagnostic turnaround times; (2) novel computational biomarkers predictive of treatment response in oncopathology; and (3) open-source tools enabling pathologist assistants to implement these workflows in clinical and research settings. By bridging computational scalability gaps in pathology, this project aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, facilitate data-driven decision-making, and create new training resources for pathology trainees in computational analysis techniques. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive analyses, parallel processing of multi-modal data, and maintaining reproducible workflows across collaborative research networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model fire dynamics and arson-related scenarios, addressing critical gaps in predictive fire behavior analysis for forensic investigations. Current fire investigation methods often rely on simplified empirical models or physical reconstructions, which may inadequately capture complex interactions between fire spread, structural materials, ventilation effects, and human factors in realistic environments. The proposed work will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement advanced computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations using Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS) and custom multiphysics solvers. These simulations will integrate heterogeneous data inputs, including geospatial layouts, material pyrolysis properties, and weather conditions, to reconstruct fire scenarios with high spatial-temporal resolution. Machine learning techniques will be applied to automate pattern recognition in fire progression datasets and identify signatures of intentional versus accidental ignition. A key innovation involves coupling probabilistic risk assessment models with CFD outputs to quantify uncertainty in arson determination. The computational framework will be validated against experimental fire test data and historical case studies from the National Fire Incident Reporting System. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to assist investigators in determining fire origins, accelerant use likelihood, and failure points in fire prevention systems. By enabling rapid, scalable scenario testing, this work aims to advance evidence-based fire investigation protocols and inform targeted fire prevention strategies for urban and wildland-urban interface environments. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of 3D fire-atmosphere coupling simulations, parametric studies across thousands of ignition scenarios, and large-scale data assimilation from forensic case repositories. Results will be disseminated through an open-source analysis toolkit tailored for fire investigation agencies and homeland security stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and principles of fire combustion and behavior applied to the analysis of fires and their causes. Includes instruction in fire behavior and combustion, fire dynamics, hazardous materials chemistry, incendiary fire analysis, fire-related human behavior, forensic procedures, investigative techniques, case management and case preparation.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the morphosyntactic and stylistic evolution of modern Filipino/Tagalog across literary, media, and technical texts. While Tagalog’s agglutinative structure and code-switching practices present unique analytical challenges, existing digital tools remain insufficient for large-scale linguistic analysis, limiting scholarly engagement with contemporary language trends. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will process a multimodal corpus spanning 1987–2023, including novels, social media, parliamentary records, and STEM publications. Computational workflows will integrate rule-based morphological parsers with transformer-based language models (e.g., BERT variants) fine-tuned for Tagalog to automate semantic role labeling, dialect identification, and code-switch detection. Parallelized processing will enable comparative analysis of register-specific grammatical innovations, particularly in technology-related lexicon, while graph-based algorithms will map semantic shifts in postcolonial literature. The HPC environment is essential for training neural models on distributed GPU clusters, conducting real-time alignment of orthographic variants across 12 regional dialects, and applying transformer architectures to over 15 million tokens. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for Tagalog computational philology, an annotated diachronic corpus with longitudinal metadata, and quantitative models correlating syntactic complexity with genre evolution. This work will advance comparative Austronesian linguistics by systematizing methods for analyzing under-resourced languages with complex morphology, while directly supporting Philippine language policy through evidence-based insights into standardization debates. By bridging digital humanities and computational linguistics, the project establishes infrastructure for interdisciplinary studies of Tagalog’s dynamic role in national and technological discourse.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the modern Filipino/Tagalog language as used in the Philippines. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Maritime Studies, focusing on the dynamic interactions between maritime environmental change, historical trade patterns, and contemporary policy challenges. The research problem centers on the lack of integrated models that bridge oceanographic data, historical maritime activity, and geopolitical decision-making, particularly in contested regions such as the South China Sea and Arctic shipping routes. Existing studies often silo climatic, historical, or policy analyses, limiting holistic insights into how shifting ocean conditions influence both ecological systems and human systems like resource management, security protocols, and international law. To address this gap, the project will employ computational simulations combining hydrodynamic modeling, agent-based simulations of maritime traffic, and natural language processing (NLP) of historical maritime legal texts. Hydrodynamic models will process multi-decadal satellite and buoy data to map salinity, temperature, and current shifts, while agent-based models will simulate vessel routing decisions under evolving environmental and regulatory constraints. Concurrently, NLP algorithms will analyze 19th- and 20th-century maritime legal documents to identify precedents relevant to modern jurisdictional disputes exacerbated by climate-driven territorial changes. These parallel workflows require HPC capabilities to manage large geospatial datasets, run ensemble climate scenarios at high resolution, and process multilingual archival texts. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks linking oceanographic change to policy vulnerabilities, visualizations of historical trade corridor adaptations, and a public database of annotated legal-historical correlations. By integrating computational oceanography with humanities-driven policy analysis, this work aims to provide actionable insights for stakeholders addressing sea-level rise, navigational safety, and transboundary resource conflicts. The requested resources will enable scaling from regional case studies to global maritime system analysis, advancing multidisciplinary methodologies in a field traditionally constrained by disconnected analytical tools.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, science, policy issues, and literature of the ocean. Includes instruction in maritime history, maritime law, maritime literature, oceanography, maritime security, and maritime politics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized neuromuscular rehabilitation protocols through multiscale biomechanical and neurophysiological modeling. Despite progress in exercise science, optimizing post-injury recovery—particularly for complex musculoskeletal injuries like anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears—remains limited by insufficient integration of individual variability in neuromuscular control, tissue healing dynamics, and sensorimotor adaptation. Current clinical models rely on population-level data, neglecting patient-specific biomechanical loading patterns and neural drive interactions that influence recovery outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining finite element modeling of joint and soft tissue mechanics with dynamic simulations of motor neuron activation patterns derived from electromyography (EMG) and functional neuroimaging data. The HPC environment will enable the parallelization of multibody dynamics simulations to predict joint stresses under varying rehabilitation exercises, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on high-resolution diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) datasets to map corticospinal tract plasticity during recovery. This integration requires processing terabytes of motion capture, EMG, and neuroimaging data alongside stochastic modeling of motor unit recruitment thresholds. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of rehabilitation efficacy, optimization of patient-specific exercise regimens to minimize re-injury risk, and the creation of open-source simulation tools for clinical movement analysis. The computational demands of this project—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated neural network training and real-time finite element analysis—exceed the capacity of local resources. By bridging biomechanics, neurophysiology, and data science, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for precision rehabilitation, directly addressing the National Academy of Medicine’s priority of translating mechanistic movement science into actionable clinical tools.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and enhance pedagogical strategies in drama and dance education through motion capture and machine learning techniques. A critical challenge in teacher training for performing arts is the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to evaluate the effectiveness of instructional methods, particularly in kinesthetic and collaborative learning environments. Traditional assessments often rely on subjective observation, limiting opportunities for personalized feedback or longitudinal analysis of teaching efficacy. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets of classroom interactions, student performances, and instructor demonstrations. Motion capture data from dance rehearsals and drama exercises will be collected, annotated, and analyzed using deep learning models to quantify movement dynamics, spatial relationships, and verbal-nonverbal communication patterns. These models will be trained to identify correlations between teaching techniques and student engagement or skill acquisition, as measured through multimodal metrics. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothetical classroom scenarios to test the scalability of pedagogical interventions across diverse learner populations. The computational demands of processing high-dimensional motion data, training complex neural networks, and running iterative simulations necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for efficient parallelization and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for visualizing teaching effectiveness, generating automated feedback for educators, and informing evidence-based curriculum design. This work aims to advance drama and dance pedagogy by bridging qualitative educational practices with quantitative computational analysis, ultimately fostering more adaptive, inclusive approaches to performing arts instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Chronic wounds represent a significant clinical challenge, with persistent inflammation, impaired tissue repair, and microbial resistance contributing to prolonged patient suffering and healthcare costs. Current treatment strategies often lack personalization due to limited understanding of how patient-specific factors—including genetic variability, immune responses, and microbiome dynamics—interact with wound microenvironmental conditions. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating high-performance computing (HPC) to model wound healing processes across molecular, cellular, and tissue levels. Leveraging patient-derived genomic, proteomic, and clinical data, we will construct agent-based models simulating immune cell behavior, finite element analyses of biomechanical stress distributions, and machine learning algorithms to predict treatment outcomes. The computational pipeline will incorporate dynamic feedback between microbial colonization patterns, oxygen gradients, and cellular metabolic states, enabling real-time simulation of wound progression under various therapeutic interventions. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, perform parallelized simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts, and optimize adaptive treatment protocols via reinforcement learning. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of healing trajectories, the design of personalized wound care regimens targeting patient-specific dysregulations, and the generation of mechanistic insights into stalled healing phases. Validated against retrospective clinical datasets from 2,000+ chronic wound cases, this framework aims to reduce trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. Successful implementation could decrease time-to-healing by 20-30% in simulated cohorts, with potential translation to decision-support tools for clinicians. The resource allocation will directly support the scaling of models to incorporate real-world data streams from wearable wound sensors, advancing precision medicine in a field where computational approaches remain underexplored despite high clinical urgency.
cip_definition: Research focused on Wound Care

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges in analyzing linguistic evolution from Ottoman Turkish to Modern Turkish by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources.
