The primary research problem lies in the scarcity of digitized Ottoman texts and the computational complexity of processing their Arabic-derived script, which has hindered large-scale comparative studies. Current methodologies struggle with the morphological complexity and orthographic variations in historical manuscripts, limiting insights into syntactic and lexical changes over six centuries. To overcome these barriers, this project will employ optical character recognition (OCR) models tailored for Ottoman script, trained on a newly assembled corpus of digitized manuscripts (16th–19th centuries) alongside modern Turkish texts. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of approximately 50,000 pages, extraction of linguistic features, and training of transformer-based models to map diachronic shifts in grammar and vocabulary. The computational pipeline will integrate NLP tools for morphological disambiguation, dependency parsing, and semantic role labeling, adapted for historical Turkish variants. By aligning these annotations across temporal strata, the analysis will quantify the influence of language reform policies and contact phenomena with Persian and Arabic. Expected outcomes include the first open-access corpus of aligned Ottoman-Modern Turkish texts with syntactic annotations, a benchmark dataset for historical NLP, and publications detailing the sociolinguistic drivers of morphological simplification. The resource will empower philological research and inform computational tools for Turkic languages, bridging gaps between traditional scholarship and digital humanities. This project requires sustained access to GPU nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for corpus alignment tasks, which are infeasible on local infrastructure. The requested allocation will directly advance the computational rigor of Turkish linguistic studies while preserving endangered textual heritage through digitization.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Turkish language in either or both of its pre-modern and modern variants. Includes instruction in philology; Ottoman Turkish; Modern Turkish; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The ocean’s role in global biogeochemical cycles and climate regulation is mediated by complex interactions between physical transport processes and chemical transformations. However, resolving the multiscale dynamics of these interactions—from turbulent mixing to basin-scale circulation—remains a critical challenge, limiting predictive understanding of marine carbon storage, hypoxia, and acidification under climate change. This project seeks to advance high-resolution modeling of coupled physical-chemical processes in the Eastern Tropical Pacific, a region of intense oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) and disproportionate significance to marine biogeochemistry. Current models struggle to capture fine-scale features such as eddy-driven vertical transport and submesoscale frontal dynamics, which modulate nutrient supply, organic matter remineralization, and greenhouse gas fluxes. To address this, we propose a novel integration of a regional ocean model (ROMS) with a biogeochemical module (BGC-ROMS) optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Simulations will employ nested grids (1-3 km resolution) to resolve mesoscale and submesoscale processes, coupled with Lagrangian particle tracking to quantify advective-diffusive controls on chemical gradients. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized biogeochemical solvers and GPU-accelerated turbulence closure schemes to manage the high dimensionality of tracer interactions and boundary layer physics. Data assimilation techniques will integrate in situ sensor arrays and satellite-derived products to constrain model parameters. By elucidating how subgrid-scale processes amplify or dampen large-scale feedbacks in OMZ expansion and carbon cycling, this work will directly inform IPCC-class Earth system models. The requested HPC resources will enable decade-scale simulations at unprecedented resolution, generating datasets to disentangle mechanistic drivers of chemical variability. Outcomes will advance fundamental knowledge of ocean-atmosphere exchange processes while providing actionable insights for climate mitigation and marine resource management strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical components, mechanisms, structure, and movement of ocean waters and their interaction with terrestrial and atmospheric phenomena. Includes instruction in material inputs and outputs, chemical and biochemical transformations in marine systems, equilibria studies, inorganic and organic ocean chemistry, oceanographic processes, sediment transport, zone processes, circulation, mixing, tidal movements, wave properties, and seawater properties.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nursing care delivery and workforce optimization by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulation frameworks tailored to practical nursing contexts. Despite advancements in healthcare technology, nursing professionals—particularly in vocational and assistant roles—face persistent barriers in managing complex patient loads, preventing adverse events, and adapting to dynamic clinical environments. Current approaches to workforce planning and patient risk stratification often rely on static guidelines, which fail to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff skill mix, and resource availability. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze multi-source clinical datasets, including electronic health records, staffing logs, and patient outcome metrics. HPC resources will enable large-scale training of ML algorithms to identify patterns predictive of patient deterioration or readmission risks, while ABM simulations will model nurse-patient interactions under varying staffing ratios and workflow conditions. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of structured and unstructured data, requiring parallelized workflows for feature extraction, model validation, and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to prioritize at-risk patients for early intervention, (2) evidence-based staffing recommendations to balance clinical efficiency with nurse workload sustainability, and (3) open-source simulation platforms for nursing education programs to train students in resource-constrained decision-making. By quantifying relationships between nursing interventions and patient outcomes at unprecedented granularity, this research aims to inform policy reforms, optimize care delivery models, and reduce preventable complications in diverse healthcare settings. The scalability of these computational tools will support translational applications across nursing education and practice, ultimately enhancing both workforce preparedness and patient safety.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a real-time, adaptive traffic control framework for construction and maintenance zones using high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize safety and efficiency. Current static traffic management strategies often fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating traffic volumes, driver behavior, weather conditions, and emergency scenarios, leading to increased risks for workers and road users. To address this, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and real-time sensor data analysis. The ABM component will simulate interactions between drivers, pedestrians, construction crews, and traffic control devices (e.g., pavement markers, signage, flagger signals) under diverse scenarios, including freeway closures, utility work, and nighttime operations. ML algorithms will be trained on historical traffic patterns and real-time inputs from IoT sensors to predict congestion hotspots and recommend optimal flagger placement, signal timing, and lane closure configurations. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational intensity of large-scale parallel simulations, stochastic modeling of rare events (e.g., sudden traffic surges or accidents), and rapid retraining of ML models as conditions evolve. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for traffic control planners that reduces average delay times by 15–25% while maintaining compliance with safety protocols. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated traffic scenarios, including rare emergency cases, to advance research in adaptive infrastructure management. By enabling precise, scenario-specific resource allocation, this work aims to establish a new standard for proactive traffic control in temporary work zones, directly enhancing workforce and public safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to control the movement of traffic through construction and maintenance zones and to protect the safety of work crews, drivers, and pedestrians. Includes instruction in flagging duties and responsibilities, the traffic control zone, flagging signals, pavement markers, freeway flagging, utility flagging, emergency response flagging, and night traffic control.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing medication administration protocols through advanced computational modeling, with a focus on improving patient safety and efficacy in medication aide practice. Medication aides routinely manage complex patient-specific variables—such as comorbidities, polypharmacy interactions, and physiological responses—that influence medication outcomes. Current decision-support tools lack granular, real-time predictive capabilities for these dynamic scenarios. We propose developing machine learning models to predict individualized medication response patterns and adverse event risks using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Our approach integrates heterogeneous datasets, including de-identified electronic health records (demographics, vital signs, medication histories), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic parameters, and simulated physiological response data. Computational workflows will employ ensemble neural networks to model drug-drug and drug-body interactions, coupled with agent-based simulations of metabolic pathways under varying patient conditions. HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets, training high-parameter models with cross-validation, and running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in dose-response predictions. Expected outcomes include: 1) A predictive framework for identifying high-risk medication regimens in elderly patients with multiple chronic conditions, 2) Optimized titration schedules for common cardiovascular medications based on real-time vital sign trends, and 3) Open-source simulation tools to help medication aides visualize potential adverse reaction cascades. The computational infrastructure will enable rapid scenario testing equivalent to decades of clinical observation, directly informing safer medication administration protocols. This work bridges computational health sciences with frontline clinical practice, providing evidence-based decision support to reduce medication errors and improve care quality in settings where medication aides operate.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed medications; observe and report patient reactions and side effects; and perform related emergency and recording duties under the supervision of nurses and/or physicians. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, common medications and their effects, taking vital signs, oxygen administration, medication administration and application, record-keeping, and patient observation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern munitions systems, coupled with aging stockpiles and evolving operational requirements, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize performance, safety, and lifecycle management. Current methodologies for assessing structural integrity, corrosion dynamics, and energetic material stability in ordnance rely heavily on physical testing and empirical models, which are costly, time-intensive, and limited in predictive accuracy. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate multi-physics interactions in munitions systems under diverse environmental and operational conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate materials science models (e.g., stress-corrosion cracking, polymer aging), fluid-structure interaction simulations, and probabilistic risk assessment algorithms to predict degradation pathways and failure modes in conventional and composite munitions. Key computational challenges include resolving micron-scale material defects across macro-scale geometries, modeling shockwave propagation in heterogeneous environments, and quantifying uncertainty in multi-variable systems. The project will employ finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning-driven surrogate models to reduce computational expense while maintaining fidelity. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for identifying high-risk components in legacy stockpiles, optimizing inspection intervals, and informing next-generation munitions design. By enabling virtual testing of hazardous scenarios—such as sympathetic detonation risks in clustered storage or thermal runaway in damaged guidance systems—the work addresses critical safety gaps while reducing reliance on live-fire experiments. The resulting computational workflows will establish a foundation for data-driven lifecycle management protocols applicable to military and dual-use ordnance systems, with potential translational value for regulatory agencies and allied partners.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of ground or sea-based weapons systems, ordinance and munitions. Includes instruction in basic sciences, electronics, systems technology, fluid power, computer science, conventional weapons systems, nuclear weapons systems, munitions systems, storage and safety, equipment operation, guidance and control systems, hazardous materials, corrosion control, nondestructive testing and quality control, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized care strategies for family practice nurses managing complex, multi-dimensional patient data. Family nursing requires synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, genetic predispositions, socio-environmental factors, and longitudinal health trends—to tailor interventions for individuals and family units. However, existing analytical tools struggle to efficiently process these data at scale, limiting real-time clinical decision-making and holistic care planning. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models capable of predicting patient-specific health trajectories and simulating the outcomes of targeted interventions. The computational approach will integrate deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for unstructured clinical notes) with agent-based simulations to model family health dynamics and disease propagation. Parallelized workflows will enable rapid analysis of large-scale datasets, while probabilistic modeling will quantify uncertainty in risk stratification for conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and geriatric syndromes. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for risk prediction, intervention optimization, and resource allocation tailored to family practice contexts. By elucidating patterns in family-level health determinants, this work aims to enhance evidence-based care delivery, reduce preventable hospitalizations, and support nurses in designing proactive, patient-centered care plans. The project will also advance methodological innovation in nursing science by establishing scalable computational workflows for integrating multi-omic and socio-behavioral data into clinical practice. Successful implementation will demonstrate the transformative potential of HPC in bridging gaps between precision health paradigms and frontline family nursing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: The increasing demand for safe, nutritious, and shelf-stable food products necessitates the development of advanced non-thermal processing technologies, such as high-pressure processing (HPP), to balance microbial safety with nutrient retention. Current optimization of HPP parameters relies heavily on empirical trials, which are time-intensive and fail to capture the complex multi-scale interactions between microbial inactivation kinetics, food matrix effects, and nutrient degradation. This project seeks to address these limitations through a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model HPP efficacy and nutrient preservation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate the effects of high-pressure conditions (100–600 MPa) on microbial cell membrane integrity (via MD) and heterogeneous food matrices (via CFD), while ML algorithms will identify optimal pressure-time profiles that maximize pathogen reduction (e.g., *Listeria*, *E. coli*) and minimize vitamin C or polyphenol loss. The computational workflow will involve parallelized simulations across pressure gradients, food compositions, and bacterial strains, validated against experimental datasets from collaborating food microbiology labs. Expected outcomes include predictive models to accelerate the design of HPP protocols tailored to specific food products (e.g., juices, ready-to-eat meats), reducing energy consumption by 15–20% compared to conventional trial-based optimization. By elucidating the mechanochemical interactions between pressure, microbial physiology, and nutrient stability, this research will advance the scalability of non-thermal technologies, supporting the food industry’s transition toward sustainable, minimally processed products. The HPC-enabled framework will also be adaptable to other emerging processing methods, fostering innovation in food safety and quality engineering within agricultural sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: Dental materials must meet stringent biomechanical, biochemical, and biocompatibility requirements to ensure long-term functionality and safety in the dynamic oral environment. However, optimizing these materials—such as resin composites, ceramics, and bioactive coatings—remains challenging due to the complex interplay between their physicochemical properties, mechanical performance under cyclic loads, and interactions with oral tissues and microbial biofilms. This project seeks to address these challenges by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model and predict the behavior of next-generation dental materials at multiple scales. Specifically, the research will focus on (1) simulating the molecular dynamics of polymer-ceramic interfacial bonding in resin composites to reduce failure rates in restorative procedures, (2) analyzing stress distribution and fatigue behavior in zirconia-based prostheses using finite element modeling under occlusal loading conditions, and (3) predicting the degradation kinetics and ion release profiles of bioactive glass coatings designed to inhibit secondary caries. Atomistic simulations will elucidate interfacial adhesion mechanisms between filler particles and resin matrices, while mesoscale models will correlate microstructural heterogeneity with crack propagation resistance. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms trained on existing experimental datasets will accelerate the discovery of material compositions with optimal mechanical and antimicrobial properties. The computational workflows will integrate multi-physics simulations to account for thermal, chemical, and mechanical stressors encountered in vivo. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to overcome the limitations of traditional trial-and-error approaches, enabling rapid virtual screening of material designs. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for material longevity, data-driven design guidelines for improved prostheses, and foundational insights into material-tissue interactions that could reduce postoperative complications. The results will advance the development of durable, bioactive dental materials while establishing a computational framework translatable to other biomedical material challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and dynamic performance of personalized lower-limb prosthetic sockets using biomechanical simulations and machine learning. Current socket fabrication relies heavily on manual adjustments informed by static anatomical measurements, which often fail to account for real-time tissue deformation, pressure variability during gait, or long-term changes in residual limb morphology. These limitations contribute to discomfort, skin breakdown, and reduced mobility for users. To address this, we propose integrating high-resolution finite element analysis (FEA) with sensor-derived gait data and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to model socket-residuum interactions under dynamic loading conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable multi-scale simulations of soft tissue mechanics, interface pressures, and thermal profiles across diverse activity scenarios (e.g., walking, stair ascent). Concurrently, a GAN architecture trained on clinical imaging, pressure mapping, and patient-reported outcomes will generate candidate socket geometries that balance structural efficiency with physiological compatibility. Validation will involve comparing simulated pressure distributions against in-socket sensor data from 50 participants with transtibial amputations. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine designs based on feedback loops between simulation outputs and patient-specific biomechanical constraints. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for identifying high-risk pressure zones, a generative design protocol to reduce iterative casting sessions, and quantitative metrics linking socket morphology to functional outcomes. This work bridges clinical orthotics, materials engineering, and computational biomechanics, offering a paradigm shift toward data-driven, adaptive prosthetic solutions. The requested HPC allocation is critical for managing the computational intensity of coupled FEA-machine learning workflows, which require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and real-time parameter optimization across heterogeneous hardware architectures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the challenge of optimizing personalized rehabilitation protocols for individuals with neuromuscular disorders by integrating high-resolution biomechanical simulations with patient-specific neurophysiological data. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for the complex interplay between neural adaptation, muscle fatigue dynamics, and joint loading patterns in heterogeneous patient populations. This project will develop a computational framework to model neuromuscular response to rehabilitation stimuli at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations in processing multi-modal datasets, including electromyography, motion capture, and diffusion tensor imaging. A hybrid approach combining finite element modeling of musculoskeletal dynamics with machine learning algorithms will be implemented to predict optimal intervention parameters across diverse biomechanical and neuroanatomical profiles. The computational pipeline will require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and real-time optimization of multiphysics models, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for simulating rehabilitation outcomes under varying physiological constraints and a quantitative framework for clinical decision-making that reduces trial-and-error in therapy design. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation science, offering a paradigm shift toward precision neurorehabilitation while advancing methodological synergies in health-focused high-performance computing.
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to predict the impacts of climate variability and land-use change on watershed-scale hydrological systems, with a focus on informing sustainable natural resource management. Current models often lack the spatial resolution and interdisciplinary coupling required to capture dynamic interactions between climatological drivers, surface water dynamics, and anthropogenic stressors. We propose to address this gap by implementing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled system that combines regional climate modeling, machine learning–enhanced hydrological simulations, and geospatial analysis of human activity patterns. The computational workflow will utilize the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model dynamically coupled with the Soil & Water Assessment Tool (SWAT), downscaled to 1-km resolution across three ecologically sensitive watersheds in North America. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on multi-decadal satellite-derived hydrometeorological data and ground sensor networks to improve parameterization of evapotranspiration and groundwater recharge processes. Large ensemble simulations will assess scenarios of projected climate extremes and conservation policy interventions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale environmental datasets, executing parallelized model runs, and quantifying uncertainty through Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold conditions for water scarcity in vulnerable ecosystems, (2) predictive metrics for evaluating land-use policies on flood/drought resilience, and (3) open-access tools for optimizing conservation efforts under climate uncertainty. By advancing the spatial and temporal fidelity of coupled human-environment system modeling, this work will directly support evidence-based decision-making for watershed protection, biodiversity conservation, and climate adaptation strategies mandated under regional sustainability initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of the physical environment and the solution of environmental problems, including subjects such as abating or controlling environmental pollution and degradation; the interaction between human society and the natural environment; and natural resources management. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, geosciences, climatology, statistics, and mathematical modeling.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators teaching students with hearing impairments, including deafness. A critical challenge in this field is the high variability in students’ auditory processing abilities, communication modalities (e.g., sign language, speechreading, cochlear implants), and language acquisition trajectories, which complicates the design of individualized instructional strategies. Traditional approaches rely on static lesson plans or generalized assessments, often failing to account for real-time student engagement or dynamic learning needs. To address this, the research will employ machine learning (ML) models trained on multimodal classroom datasets—including visual sign language recognition, speech-to-text accuracy metrics, and eye-tracking patterns—to predict optimal instructional adjustments. Computational simulations will model how different teaching interventions (e.g., visual scaffolding techniques, pacing adjustments) interact with student-specific sensory and cognitive profiles. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution video data of sign language interactions, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and optimizing ML architectures for real-time feedback. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating personalized lesson recommendations and a simulation platform to train educators in adapting instruction for diverse auditory and language profiles. By quantifying the impact of specific teaching strategies on learning outcomes, this work aims to bridge gaps in evidence-based practices for deaf and hard-of-hearing education, directly supporting teacher preparation programs in aligning pedagogical training with the heterogeneous needs of this student population.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Hearing Impairments Including Deafness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with hearing impairments including deafness which adversely affect their educational performance, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with hearing impairments, including deafness, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising hearing-impaired students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Tourism promotion faces evolving challenges in adapting to dynamic, real-time shifts in traveler behavior, environmental disruptions, and socio-economic volatility. Traditional campaign strategies often rely on static datasets and lagging indicators, limiting responsiveness to emergent trends. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework for simulating and optimizing adaptive tourism promotion strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including social media sentiment, climate event alerts, and localized economic metrics—into a real-time decision support system. Agent-based modeling will simulate tourist decision-making under variable promotional stimuli, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze unstructured data from travel forums and review platforms to quantify perception trends. Concurrently, graph neural networks will model destination competitiveness across interdependent regional tourism ecosystems. These computationally intensive methods require parallelized processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets and complex network interactions. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for identifying optimal promotion windows, prioritizing resilient destinations during crises, and dynamically allocating marketing budgets across digital channels. The project’s significance lies in advancing data-driven, agile tourism operations that balance economic objectives with sustainability considerations. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the proposed framework aims to reduce resource waste in underperforming campaigns, enhance stakeholder coordination during disruptions, and improve ROI estimation for public-private tourism partnerships. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, marketing analytics, and destination management, offering a novel methodology for scalable, real-time promotion systems in an increasingly volatile global tourism landscape.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of tourism in public and private sector settings. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) present complex challenges due to the interplay of neurobiological, behavioral, and environmental factors. Current treatment paradigms in addiction counseling often rely on static protocols, which inadequately address the dynamic, individualized nature of recovery and relapse. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a computational framework to model the neurobehavioral trajectories of individuals undergoing substance abuse counseling, with a focus on predicting relapse risk and optimizing personalized intervention strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to integrate multimodal data—including functional neuroimaging (fMRI), real-time behavioral monitoring via mobile sensors, and longitudinal clinical assessments—to construct dynamic, patient-specific models of craving, decision-making, and therapeutic response. The computational approach combines mechanistic neural network simulations with machine learning algorithms to identify biomarkers of relapse vulnerability and simulate the efficacy of hypothetical counseling interventions in silico. Key challenges include processing high-dimensional neuroimaging datasets, resolving temporal dependencies in behavioral data streams, and scaling personalized models across heterogeneous cohorts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized parameter optimization for biophysical neural models, large-scale Bayesian inference for probabilistic behavioral forecasting, and ensemble learning techniques to improve predictive generalizability. Expected outcomes include a novel computational toolkit for addiction counselors to visualize patient-specific risk profiles, test intervention scenarios, and refine treatment plans dynamically. This work will advance the integration of computational neuroscience into clinical counseling practice, offering a data-driven framework to enhance the precision and adaptability of SUD interventions. By elucidating the neurocomputational mechanisms underlying therapeutic change, the project aims to establish a foundation for next-generation, technology-augmented addiction care paradigms.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to help prevent substance abuse, counsel individuals and families with drug and alcohol problems, and perform intervention and therapeutic services for persons suffering from addiction. Includes instruction in individual and group counseling skills, psychology of addiction, sociology, crisis intervention, substance abuse identification methodologies, substance abuse treatment modalities, substance abuse prevention and treatment resources, pharmacology and behavioral aspects of abused substances, treatment evaluation, patient observation and education, group dynamics, professional standards and ethics, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing the design and operational efficiency of urban parks and recreational facilities. The research addresses a critical gap in evidence-based decision-making for park management, where traditional planning methods often rely on static demographic data or qualitative assessments, leading to underutilized spaces or mismatches between user needs and facility offerings. The computational challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets—including real-time visitor behavior patterns, environmental sensor data (e.g., air quality, microclimate variability), and dynamic urban infrastructure metrics—into a unified simulation environment. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to simulate visitor interactions with park features under varying scenarios, such as seasonal changes, event scheduling, or capacity constraints. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in usage patterns, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will identify latent relationships between spatial layouts and visitor satisfaction metrics derived from social media sentiment analysis. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across diverse virtual park configurations, enabling parameter sweeps across thousands of design permutations. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool that predicts optimal facility placements, maintenance schedules, and adaptive programming strategies to maximize equitable access and ecological resilience. By bridging computational social science, urban informatics, and landscape architecture, this work establishes a novel methodological pipeline for data-driven recreation management, with potential applications to smart city initiatives and climate-adaptive public space design. The resulting open-source framework will empower municipal planners to balance competing priorities—such as biodiversity preservation, accessibility compliance, and recreational demand—using empirically validated optimization strategies.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Facilities Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage park facilities and other indoor and outdoor recreation and leisure facilities. Includes instruction in supervising support personnel, health and safety standards, public relations, and basic business and marketing principles.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to optimize hazardous materials (hazmat) risk assessment and emergency response planning through advanced data analytics and high-fidelity modeling. Current hazmat management systems face critical limitations in processing real-time environmental data, predicting contamination spread across heterogeneous terrains, and simulating human behavior during emergencies. These gaps hinder rapid decision-making in incidents involving chemical spills, radioactive leaks, or biological hazards. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex interactions between material properties, environmental conditions, and infrastructure vulnerabilities. The computational approach combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for atmospheric dispersion modeling, machine learning algorithms trained on historical incident datasets, and agent-based simulations of evacuation dynamics. Key innovations include the integration of high-resolution geospatial data (1m² resolution) with real-time sensor networks, and the development of adaptive risk prediction models that account for evolving weather patterns and urban morphology. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 10⁶+ parameter combinations for sensitivity analyses, reducing simulation times from weeks to hours compared to conventional methods. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible risk prediction toolkit for emergency planners, validated against EPA contamination datasets, and novel metrics for prioritizing hazmat storage locations in urban-industrial interfaces. This work directly supports the program’s mission by advancing information systems that bridge technical hazmat management with human-centered communication strategies, ultimately enhancing community resilience. The requested computing allocation (200,000 CPU-hours, 50 TB storage) will facilitate scaling to regional-level simulations while maintaining the granularity required for actionable insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing, monitoring, and enforcing hazardous materials management and removal. Includes instruction in environmental science, environmental health, human behavior, economics, management science, information systems and applications, and communication skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of workforce ecosystems in hybrid work environments, focusing on the interplay between algorithmic management systems, employee well-being, and organizational resilience. As organizations increasingly adopt AI-driven tools for task allocation, performance monitoring, and team composition optimization, critical gaps persist in understanding how these computational systems interact with human behavioral patterns and socio-technical factors. The study will develop agent-based models simulating multi-level organizational structures, incorporating real-world data on employee communication patterns, productivity metrics, and physiological stress indicators from wearable devices. Computational experiments will employ evolutionary algorithms to explore emergent phenomena in human-AI collaboration networks, particularly examining how different resource allocation strategies affect system stability during operational disruptions. A parallel stream of research will apply natural language processing to longitudinal employee feedback data, utilizing transformer-based architectures to detect subtle shifts in organizational culture and predict attrition risks. The computational intensity of modeling thousands of heterogeneous agents across extended temporal scales, combined with the need for real-time analysis of unstructured text data streams, necessitates access to HPC resources for parallel processing and large-scale parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include a framework for evaluating the ethical-efficiency tradeoffs in AI-enhanced workforce management systems, predictive models for maintaining organizational coherence in distributed work arrangements, and evidence-based guidelines for human-centered algorithm design in HR technologies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science with organizational psychology, offering novel insights into sustaining productive human-machine partnerships while addressing contemporary challenges in employee experience management.
cip_title: Human Resources Management/ Personnel Administration, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to manage the development of human capital in organizations, and to provide related services to individuals and groups. Includes instruction in personnel and organization policy, human resource dynamics and flows, labor relations, sex roles, civil rights, human resources law and regulations, motivation and compensation systems, work systems, career management, employee testing and assessment, recruitment and selection, managing employee and job training programs, and the management of human resources programs and operations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of vendor-specific software ecosystems demands robust, scalable methods to automate certification processes for installation and maintenance engineers. Current approaches rely on static checklists and manual validation, which struggle to adapt to dynamic dependencies, heterogeneous environments, and evolving vendor requirements. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate, validate, and optimize certification workflows for vendor-supported software products using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on developing adaptive certification pipelines that account for real-world system variability, including hardware configurations, network topologies, and cross-product interactions. The computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation, dependency graph analysis, and machine learning to model installation scenarios across thousands of virtualized environments in parallel. Containerized testing environments will be orchestrated at scale to evaluate certification criteria under diverse conditions, while reinforcement learning agents will iteratively optimize maintenance protocols. Key challenges include minimizing false positives in automated compliance checks and ensuring deterministic reproducibility across hybrid cloud architectures. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration over combinatorial parameter spaces, including multi-vendor interoperability edge cases that exceed the capabilities of conventional testing platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating vendor-agnostic certification profiles, predictive models for installation failure risk assessment, and quantitative benchmarks for certification process efficiency. This work bridges gaps between software engineering practice and computational validation methodologies, offering a paradigm shift in how vendor qualifications are designed and assessed. The results will directly benefit professional certification bodies, software vendors seeking to streamline partner onboarding, and organizations requiring auditable compliance with technical support standards. By addressing certification as a computational reproducibility challenge, this project establishes foundational methods for trustable automation in product-specific engineering credentials.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to fulfill the requirements set by vendors for professional qualification as certified installation, customization, and maintenance engineers for specific software products and/or processes. Includes training in specific vendor-supported software products and their installation and maintenance.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a large-scale computational analysis of thematic and stylistic patterns in Anglophone literary texts across multiple genres and historical periods. Traditional literary scholarship often relies on manual close reading, which limits the scale and scope of analysis, particularly when examining broad trends across centuries or diverse genres. To address this, we aim to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze a curated corpus of over 50,000 English-language novels, plays, essays, and poems from the 18th century to the present. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic role labeling and dynamic topic modeling, to trace the evolution of narrative structures, rhetorical strategies, and intertextual relationships. Computational challenges include managing memory-intensive operations for parsing syntactic dependencies in lengthy texts and training custom classifiers to identify genre-specific stylistic features (e.g., metaphorical density in poetry versus prose). The pipeline will integrate dimension reduction algorithms and network analysis tools to visualize shifts in literary conventions and influence. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database mapping correlations between sociohistorical contexts and formal literary innovations, 2) quantitative evidence supporting or complicating existing periodization frameworks in literary studies, and 3) methodological frameworks for scalable computational criticism. By enabling systematic analysis of cross-genre textual features at unprecedented scale, this work aims to advance digital humanities scholarship while preserving disciplinary engagement with interpretive nuance. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the heterogeneous data types, parallel processing demands, and iterative model training required to balance computational rigor with literary theoretical sophistication.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on literature from one or more genres, cultures or traditions. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and studies of various types of literary text.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare facility operations necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize patient care unit workflows, particularly in dynamic, high-acuity environments. This project addresses the challenge of real-time resource allocation and staff scheduling in hospital wards, where traditional heuristic methods fail to account for multivariate, interdependent factors such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff skill overlap, equipment availability, and regulatory constraints. We propose developing an adaptive decision-support system leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate operational scenarios and predict bottlenecks through hybrid modeling techniques. The computational framework integrates discrete-event simulation for patient flow dynamics with graph neural networks to model staff-patient-task interactions, incorporating real-time data streams from electronic health records, IoT sensors, and personnel tracking systems. By parallelizing millions of potential scheduling permutations across HPC nodes, the system will identify optimal resource distribution strategies under constraints that include fatigue metrics, certification requirements, and infection control protocols. Validation will utilize anonymized historical data from three tertiary care centers, encompassing 2.5 million patient-hours and staff movement patterns. Expected outcomes include a 15-30% reduction in preventable care delays and a 20% improvement in staff utilization efficiency metrics compared to current management systems. This research fills a critical gap in health operational sciences by providing unit managers with evidence-based, predictive tools to balance clinical demands with workforce sustainability—an urgent need given rising healthcare costs and staff retention challenges. The computational infrastructure will enable scaling to multi-unit hospital networks while maintaining sub-minute decision latency, creating a novel paradigm for responsive healthcare management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nursing or medical service administrators, to supervise and coordinate the operations of one or more patient care units in hospitals or other health care facilities. Includes instruction in planning and initiating administrative procedures, personnel supervision, interpersonal skills, general and/or specialized health care operations and procedures, and consultation with other medical, nursing, and administrative team members.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on cultural transmission and identity formation among Baltic Sea communities, with a focus on understudied linguistic and folkloric materials from minority populations in the region. The research addresses a critical gap in Baltic Studies: the lack of systematic, large-scale analysis of historical and contemporary cultural artifacts that reflect evolving group identities amid shifting geopolitical and social pressures. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the vast, multilingual corpora of digitized texts, oral histories, and visual media held in regional archives, limiting insights into patterns of cultural survival and assimilation. To address this, we propose computational methods including multilingual natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis to analyze over 10,000 digitized documents (19th–21st centuries) across Estonian, Latgalian, Lithuanian, and Sami languages. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to identify thematic motifs, semantic shifts, and cross-cultural references, while temporal network models will map the diffusion of narratives across communities. A second phase employs computer vision to analyze visual patterns in folk art and ritual objects from Baltic ethnographic collections, correlating stylistic features with linguistic and geographic data. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training domain-specific language models, and running iterative simulations of cultural exchange networks. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated materials, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural resilience, and visualizations of intergroup influence patterns. This work will provide novel methodologies for interdisciplinary Baltic cultural studies, inform heritage preservation initiatives, and offer scalable tools for analyzing minority identities in other global contexts. By bridging computational and humanistic approaches, the project aims to redefine how cultural survival is studied in complex, multiethnic regions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the coastlands of the Baltic Sea, including Baltic, Germanic, Scandinavian, and Slavic populations, related borderlands and island groups, and problems of cultural survival and assimilation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the theoretical and practical understanding of computational complexity in automated verification, with a focus on developing scalable algorithms for model checking temporal logic formulas. The core challenge lies in the exponential growth of state spaces for concurrent and distributed systems, which limits the applicability of existing verification tools to real-world systems. Traditional sequential algorithms for evaluating linear temporal logic (LTL) and computation tree logic (CTL) properties struggle with systems exceeding 10^6 states, necessitating new approaches that leverage parallel architectures. We propose a hybrid methodology combining symbolic model checking with distributed graph traversal techniques, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) developing a partitioned representation of transition systems using binary decision diagrams (BDDs) to minimize inter-node communication, (2) implementing asynchronous counterexample search algorithms across GPU and CPU clusters, and (3) creating adaptive heuristics that dynamically allocate resources based on formula structure and state space topology. The project will utilize MPI for distributed memory management and CUDA for GPU acceleration, with rigorous complexity analysis to quantify speedup factors under different scaling regimes. Expected outcomes include open-source implementations of the proposed algorithms, theoretical bounds on parallel verification complexity classes, and practical benchmarks demonstrating verification of systems with 10^8+ states. This work will directly contribute to foundational knowledge in computational logic while addressing critical bottlenecks in formal methods for safety-critical systems. Successful completion could enable new applications in automated reasoning for large-scale distributed protocols, biological system modeling, and AI safety verification, bridging theoretical computer science with practical engineering challenges. Resource requests emphasize GPU node allocation and large-memory systems for BDD manipulation, with an estimated need for 500,000 core-hours across the project timeline.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical techniques underlying computing, including the theory of computation, and logic in computer science and artificial intelligence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate the spread of chronic diseases in urban communities and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of preventive health interventions. Chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension disproportionately affect underserved populations, yet resource allocation for community-level prevention remains suboptimal due to gaps in predicting dynamic interactions between social determinants, health behaviors, and local policy constraints. The research will integrate multi-source data—including electronic health records, geospatial environmental exposures, and community survey responses—to parameterize a high-resolution simulation of disease transmission and intervention outcomes. Computational demands are substantial, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run thousands of parallelized simulations that account for heterogeneous population attributes, stochastic behavioral patterns, and time-dependent policy scenarios. Models will leverage machine learning techniques to calibrate parameters from real-world datasets and quantify uncertainties in intervention efficacy. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool to identify priority neighborhoods and intervention types (e.g., mobile screening clinics, subsidized nutrition programs) that maximize reductions in disease incidence per allocated dollar. This work directly addresses the program’s focus on community health planning by bridging epidemiological theory with practical resource allocation challenges. The computational framework will be designed for adaptability to other urban settings, with open-source code and documentation to empower local health departments. By simulating the long-term impacts of preventive strategies under budget constraints, this project aims to advance evidence-based approaches for reducing health disparities while optimizing finite public health resources. Successful implementation will depend on HPC capabilities to manage complex, memory-intensive simulations and enable rapid scenario testing for stakeholder engagement.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to plan and manage health services in local community settings, including the coordination of related support services, government agencies, and private resources. Includes instruction in public health, community health services and delivery, health behavior and cultural factors, local government operations, human services, health communication and promotion, health services administration in local settings, environmental health, preventive and comparative medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, family and community health, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Geothermal energy systems offer a sustainable pathway to meet growing energy demands, yet their deployment is hindered by challenges in predicting subsurface thermal behavior and optimizing energy extraction. Current models struggle to account for heterogeneous geological formations, dynamic fluid-rock interactions, and long-term reservoir performance, leading to uncertainties in system efficiency and economic viability. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced simulations of geothermal reservoirs, enabling precise characterization of subsurface processes and informed engineering decisions. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating multi-physics models that integrate heat transfer, fluid flow, and geomechanical deformation across varying spatial and temporal scales; (2) employing machine learning algorithms to calibrate models using field data from existing geothermal sites; and (3) optimizing well placement and operational parameters to maximize energy output while minimizing environmental impacts. Computational methods will include finite element analysis for coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical simulations, parallelized Monte Carlo techniques for uncertainty quantification, and neural networks for pattern recognition in heterogeneous rock strata. The HPC resources will enable computationally intensive tasks such as 3D reservoir modeling at meter-scale resolution and ensemble runs to assess scenario-based risks. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting reservoir longevity, a publicly accessible database of synthetic geothermal reservoir datasets, and guidelines for adaptive management of geothermal systems. By advancing predictive capabilities, this work will directly support the design of next-generation geothermal technologies, reduce exploration costs, and accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy infrastructure. The computational tools developed will be shared with the geothermal research community, fostering collaboration and innovation in renewable energy engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Emergency medicine research faces critical challenges in integrating heterogeneous clinical data to improve time-sensitive decision-making. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework for acute care outcomes by leveraging high-dimensional electronic health records (EHRs), real-time physiological waveforms, and multimodal imaging data from trauma and sepsis patients. Current models lack the computational capacity to process temporal-spatial relationships in waveform data while simultaneously analyzing structured EHR variables, limiting their clinical utility in emergency departments (EDs). We propose a hybrid machine learning architecture combining transformer-based temporal modeling for physiological signals (e.g., ECG, arterial line waveforms) with graph neural networks to represent complex interactions between clinical variables. The computational workflow requires distributed training of deep learning models across multi-GPU nodes, integration of 10+ terabytes of anonymized patient data from six regional EDs, and real-time simulation of clinical decision pathways through Monte Carlo methods. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) parallel processing of raw waveform data at scale using GPU-accelerated signal decomposition, (2) federated learning across institutional datasets while maintaining privacy constraints, and (3) validation through agent-based modeling of ED workflows under different prediction scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated risk stratification system for septic shock progression within 24 hours of ED admission and a resource allocation model optimizing critical care transitions. This work will establish computational infrastructure for future emergency medicine studies requiring rapid analysis of complex clinical data streams, with immediate applications for improving mortality prediction in undifferentiated critically ill patients. The developed models and pipelines will be disseminated through an open-source platform adaptable to diverse emergency care settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Emergency Medicine

abstract: The prehospital management of medical emergencies requires rapid, data-driven decisions to optimize patient outcomes amidst dynamic and resource-constrained environments. Current protocols for emergency medical services (EMS) resource allocation and crisis scene management often rely on static guidelines that may not adapt effectively to real-time variables such as fluctuating patient volumes, geographic constraints, and equipment availability. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate and optimize EMT response strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Leveraging historical EMS data, including dispatch records, patient vitals, and response timelines, we will construct agent-based models to replicate multi-incident scenarios and evaluate the efficacy of different resource allocation algorithms. Machine learning techniques, such as reinforcement learning, will be employed to train adaptive triage systems that prioritize interventions based on evolving patient conditions and logistical factors. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess the probabilistic outcomes of various deployment strategies under uncertainty. The computational demands of processing large-scale spatiotemporal datasets, running parallel simulations, and iteratively refining predictive models necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated decision-support tools for EMS coordination centers, dynamically adjustable triage protocols, and evidence-based recommendations for ambulance deployment patterns. By integrating real-world EMT workflows with advanced computational analytics, this research aims to reduce critical intervention times, improve survival rates in mass casualty events, and establish a scalable framework for prehospital emergency optimization. The findings will directly inform training curricula and operational guidelines for paramedic teams, enhancing both individual patient care and system-wide resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the remote supervision of physicians, to recognize, assess, and manage medical emergencies in prehospital settings and to supervise Ambulance personnel. Includes instruction in basic, intermediate, and advanced EMT procedures; emergency surgical procedures; medical triage; rescue operations; crisis scene management and personnel supervision; equipment operation and maintenance; patient stabilization, monitoring, and care; drug administration; identification and preliminary diagnosis of diseases and injuries; communication and computer operations; basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the relationship between digital writing environments and compositional practices using computational text analysis and visualization methods. While existing scholarship in rhetoric and composition has qualitatively examined how digital platforms shape writing processes, the scale of available digital writing artifacts—including multimodal drafts, revision histories, and peer feedback exchanges in online learning management systems—exceeds the analytical capacity of manual humanistic methods. Our interdisciplinary team proposes to apply natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to a corpus of 250,000 anonymized student writing artifacts (totaling ~75 million tokens) drawn from 15 years of first-year composition courses. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a three-phase analysis: (1) cluster analysis of syntactic patterns and rhetorical moves across genres and assignment types, (2) network analysis of citation practices and intertextual connections in argumentative essays, and (3) longitudinal modeling of stylistic changes in student writing correlated with platform migration (from traditional word processors to collaborative web-based editors). The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated transformers for latent semantic analysis and distributed computing frameworks for processing heterogeneous file formats (text, HTML, Markdown). Expected outcomes include new models for understanding how digital writing infrastructures influence rhetorical development, visualizations of large-scale compositional trends, and open-source tools for corpus-based writing studies. This research directly addresses gaps in empirical approaches to digital writing pedagogy while demonstrating how computational humanities methods can advance core questions in rhetoric and composition studies. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impractical on standard academic computing infrastructure, particularly for training custom NLP models on mixed-genre composition corpora.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the humanistic and scientific study of rhetoric, composition, literacy, and language/linguistic theories and their practical and pedagogical applications. Includes instruction in historical and contemporary rhetoric/composition theories; composition and criticism of written, visual, and mixed-media texts; analysis of literacy practices in cultural and cross-cultural contexts; and writing program administration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model biomechanical and hemodynamic factors influencing perinatal outcomes in low-risk pregnancies managed by direct-entry midwives. Despite the growing demand for community-based midwifery care, predictive tools to anticipate complications such as prolonged labor or postpartum hemorrhage remain underdeveloped, particularly for non-hospital settings. Current clinical guidelines rely on population-level data, which may not account for individual anatomical variability or dynamic physiological interactions during labor. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of pelvic floor mechanics with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of uteroplacental blood flow. The research will utilize anonymized patient-specific data from midwifery practices—including 3D ultrasound reconstructions, wearable sensor-derived uterine activity patterns, and hemodynamic biomarkers—to create multi-scale models of maternal-fetal physiology. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations testing how variations in pelvic morphology, cervical stiffness, and vascular resistance correlate with labor progression and neonatal outcomes. Machine learning techniques will then identify predictive signatures from these simulations, validated against a longitudinal dataset of 1,200 midwife-attended births. The resulting models aim to provide real-time decision support tools for midwives, enhancing their capacity to recognize early warning signs of dystocia or perfusion-related complications while maintaining low-intervention care principles. By bridging biomechanical modeling with clinical midwifery practice, this work advances personalized maternal care in out-of-hospital settings and establishes a computational foundation for studying physiological birth dynamics—a critical yet under-researched area in health sciences. The project’s outcomes will directly inform the development of open-source predictive analytics tools tailored to direct-entry midwifery education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide pre-natal, natural birth, and immediate postpartum care to pregnant women in jurisdictions licensing direct (non-nursing) training for midwives. Includes instruction in basic obstetrics, women's health, fetal development, childbirth education, maternal nutrition and health, labor support, natural childbirth, postpartum support, prebirth counseling and risk screening, management of obstetric emergencies, patient referral, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing real-time data integration in distributed environmental monitoring systems, addressing the critical challenge of harmonizing heterogeneous, high-velocity data streams from IoT sensors, satellite imagery, and legacy databases. Current data warehousing approaches struggle to balance low-latency ingestion, semantic consistency, and energy efficiency when processing spatially dispersed multimodal data with varying governance constraints. The research will implement a hybrid architecture combining adaptive schema-on-write strategies with graph-based metadata propagation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale deployment scenarios. Computational experiments will model dynamic workflows across federated Kubernetes clusters, testing distributed in-memory caching mechanisms and machine learning-driven schema alignment algorithms under variable network conditions. Key innovations include a topology-aware partitioning system that minimizes cross-node data movement and a probabilistic conflict resolution model trained on synthetic environmental metadata hierarchies. Expected outcomes include quantifiable benchmarks for latency reduction in edge-to-warehouse pipelines, validated through comparative analysis against existing industrial standards. The resulting framework will advance capabilities in ecological forecasting and disaster response systems while establishing design patterns for ethical data provenance tracking in cross-jurisdictional environmental datasets. Successful implementation requires access to HPC infrastructure supporting parallelized container orchestration, GPU-accelerated graph processing, and petascale storage for simulating multi-year temporal datasets across 10^4 node configurations. This work bridges gaps between spatial database theory, edge computing, and sustainability informatics, offering methodological advances for next-generation environmental data infrastructures.
cip_title: Data Modeling/ Warehousing and Database Administration
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and manage the construction of databases and related software programs and applications, including the linking of individual data sets to create complex searchable databases (warehousing) and the use of analytical search tools (mining). Includes instruction in database theory, logic, and semantics; operational and warehouse modeling; dimensionality; attributes and hierarchies; data definition; technical architecture; access and security design; integration; formatting and extraction; data delivery; index design; implementation problems; planning and budgeting; and client and networking issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Mormon Studies by analyzing complex patterns in Latter-day Saint theological discourse and community dynamics. The research problem centers on the need to systematically examine large-scale, unstructured textual and cultural datasets—including digitized sermons, doctrinal commentaries, and archival records—to identify shifts in theological emphasis, socioreligious adaptation, and the interplay between doctrinal authority and lived practice across time. Traditional qualitative methods face limitations in processing these datasets due to their volume, temporal scope, and multivariate nature. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning to perform semantic clustering, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling on corpora spanning 19th-century foundational texts to contemporary digital media. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate decision-making processes in historical and modern Mormon communities, testing hypotheses about cultural transmission and resilience under external pressures. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on domain-specific language, optimizing hyperparameters for historical text analysis, and running large-scale simulations with dynamic socioreligious variables. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal development trajectories, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural adaptation strategies, and open-access tools tailored to religious studies scholarship. This work will contribute to broader debates in the philosophy of religion regarding innovation within tradition and offer methodological advancements in applying computational methods to theological analysis. By bridging digital humanities and religious studies, the project aims to establish scalable, reproducible approaches for studying religious systems as dynamic, data-rich phenomena.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on beliefs, practices, culture, and history of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormon). Includes instruction in Mormon culture, history, literature, philosophy, sociology, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between economic policy narratives and their cross-linguistic reception, combining computational text analysis, econometric modeling, and comparative literary studies to address gaps in understanding how multilingual discourse shapes economic behavior. Focusing on post-2008 central bank communications and parliamentary debates across English, German, and Japanese contexts, the research analyzes how culturally embedded linguistic constructs—such as metaphor, narrative framing, and semantic ambiguity—influence public and market responses to fiscal austerity measures. The core computational challenge involves training multilingual transformer models to detect latent rhetorical patterns in economic texts while accounting for region-specific literary traditions that inform economic terminology.
