High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabytes of multilingual parliamentary records, central bank publications, and media responses, enabling simultaneous fine-tuning of language models and Bayesian structural time series analyses linking discourse features to macroeconomic indicators like bond yield volatility and household spending. By integrating natural language processing with dynamic stochastic general equilibrium models, the project aims to quantify the "narrative elasticity" of policy messaging—the degree to which linguistic choices amplify or dampen real economic effects across cultural contexts. Anticipated outcomes include a novel framework for cross-linguistic policy impact forecasting and an open-access corpus of aligned economic texts with multilingual sentiment and narrative annotations. This work bridges computational linguistics, comparative literature, and behavioral economics, offering policymakers tools to design culturally resonant economic communications while advancing methodologies for interdisciplinary text-as-data research. The requested GPU cluster resources will support parallelized model training across languages and large-scale counterfactual simulations of alternative narrative strategies.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions or a specialization which draws from economics and the language and literature of one or more countries or regions. Includes instruction in comparative economic systems, econometrics, economic theory, money and banking systems, international economics, international trade, linguistics, philology, and translation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genetic architecture of drought-resistance traits in wild and cultivated tomato species (Solanum sect. Lycopersicon). While advances in plant genomics have identified candidate genes linked to abiotic stress responses, the regulatory networks and epistatic interactions underlying phenotypic variation in drought resilience remain poorly resolved. Traditional genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in these outcrossing species are constrained by population structure and polygenic inheritance, necessitating advanced computational methods to disentangle causal loci from background genetic noise. We propose a two-pronged approach: (1) population genomic analysis of resequencing data from 500 accessions to identify selection signatures and structural variants associated with arid habitat adaptation, and (2) machine learning-driven genomic prediction models integrating epigenomic datasets (ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq) to map regulatory elements modulating drought-responsive gene expression. The computational workflow will employ graph-based pangenome alignments using PanTools, mixed linear models for GWAS (GEMMA), and neural networks trained on multi-omics layers to predict genotype-environment associations. These analyses require large-memory nodes (>1 TB RAM) for graph genome construction and GPU acceleration for deep learning model optimization. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved noncoding sequences regulating root architecture plasticity, characterization of heterochromatin remodeling patterns under water stress, and predictive models linking transposable element insertions to stomatal regulation phenotypes. By resolving the interplay between structural variation, chromatin accessibility, and drought adaptation, this work will provide actionable targets for marker-assisted breeding while advancing fundamental knowledge about evolutionary constraints on plant stress response pathways. The proposed computational framework will be shared as modular pipelines to support comparative studies in other crops facing climate-related selection pressures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of multicellular plants and fungi as related to botanical research as well as to applications in comparative genetics, ecology and evolutionary studies, clinical studies, and industrial research. Includes instruction in molecular genetics, gene expression, gene regulation, genomics, epigenetic phenomena, DNA recombination and repair, genetic interactions at the microbial and higher levels, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the performance and reliability of distributed renewable energy systems through advanced computational modeling. As the deployment of solar, wind, and hybrid energy installations accelerates, technicians and engineers face growing complexity in diagnosing system inefficiencies, predicting component failures, and ensuring seamless integration with existing infrastructure. Current analytical tools often lack the resolution to model dynamic interactions between mechanical, electrical, and environmental variables at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will employ multiphysics modeling techniques to analyze stress distributions in photovoltaic arrays under variable weather conditions, machine learning algorithms to predict inverter failure risks from heterogeneous sensor data, and agent-based simulations to optimize maintenance workflows for large-scale wind farms. Key datasets will include real-world telemetry from regional microgrids, material degradation studies, and synthetic scenarios generated via digital twin architectures. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, this work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in simulating multi-year operational timelines and complex fault propagation patterns. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maintenance protocols that decrease system downtime by 15–20%, actionable guidelines for resilient energy system design, and open-source diagnostic tools tailored for technician training programs. The computational resources will enable unprecedented scalability in testing installation configurations and failure scenarios, directly supporting workforce readiness for next-generation energy infrastructure demands.
cip_title: Energy Systems Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: Athletic injuries present complex biomechanical and physiological challenges, with recovery outcomes influenced by multifaceted interactions between tissue-level damage, rehabilitation protocols, and psychological factors. Current clinical models often oversimplify these dynamics, limiting their ability to predict injury risks or personalize interventions. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to simulate injury mechanisms, rehabilitation efficacy, and psychophysiological recovery trajectories using high-performance computing (HPC). The research integrates three methodological components: (1) multi-scale finite element modeling of musculoskeletal tissues under dynamic athletic loads to quantify stress distributions and failure thresholds, (2) agent-based simulations of cellular responses to therapeutic interventions, and (3) machine learning analysis of multimodal datasets combining biomechanical metrics, imaging data, and psychological assessments from collegiate athletes. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution anatomical models derived from clinical MRI/CT scans, real-time coupling of tissue mechanics with inflammatory cascades, and probabilistic forecasting of recovery timelines. Anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms to identify athletes at high risk of reinjury, optimized rehabilitation protocols tailored to individual biomechanical profiles, and evidence-based insights into the bidirectional relationship between physical recovery and psychological resilience. By bridging computational biomechanics with clinical sports medicine, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven injury management, directly informing therapeutic strategies that address both physiological healing and mental health. The scale of simulations—involving 10^6–10^7 degrees of freedom per model and terabyte-scale datasets—necessitates dedicated HPC resources to achieve clinically relevant throughput and resolution, advancing translational outcomes for athlete care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the pathology and biomechanics of athletic injuries and the effects of injury on the athlete, including both physical and psychological manifestations. Includes instruction in acute and chronic patient supervision, therapy and rehabilitation, and diagnostic procedures.

abstract: Adolescent healthcare presents unique challenges due to the dynamic interplay of biological maturation, psychosocial development, and environmental influences. Current clinical models often struggle to predict health outcomes in this population, particularly for conditions like eating disorders, substance use, and mental health crises, where multifactorial causality complicates intervention strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to integrate multi-modal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomic profiles, and social determinant surveys—to identify predictive biomarkers and social-environmental risk factors for adolescent health trajectories. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage and analyze large-scale, high-dimensional datasets, which are computationally prohibitive to process on standard systems. Machine learning models, including ensemble methods and graph neural networks, will be trained to detect latent patterns across heterogeneous data types, while mechanistic simulations will test hypotheses about intervention efficacy under varying biological and social conditions. A key innovation involves coupling natural language processing (NLP) of clinical notes with agent-based modeling to simulate how provider-patient communication dynamics influence treatment adherence. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for adolescent-specific health risks, (2) personalized intervention strategies optimized through in silico trials, and (3) open-source tools for scalable analysis of adolescent health data. By elucidating interactions between biological, behavioral, and social variables, this work aims to advance clinical decision-making and reduce disparities in adolescent care. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s computational demands, including parallel processing of neuroimaging data (~500 TB), genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across 10,000+ samples, and real-time optimization of simulation parameters. Results will inform the development of adaptive clinical guidelines and establish a replicable framework for translational research in adolescent medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the unique physical, psychological, and social characteristics of adolescents and their healthcare problems and needs.

abstract: The increasing threat of zoonotic disease emergence at the human-animal-environment interface necessitates advanced predictive tools to inform preventive strategies. Current limitations in simulating complex transmission dynamics across species and landscapes hinder proactive intervention in veterinary and public health systems. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution, multi-host epidemiological model to quantify spillover risks and evaluate targeted control measures for priority pathogens, including avian influenza viruses and Lyme disease-causing Borrelia species. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement spatially explicit agent-based models incorporating host movement ecology, pathogen genomics, climate variables, and anthropogenic land-use patterns at scales spanning individual farms to regional ecosystems. Model parameterization will utilize 15TB of existing veterinary surveillance data, wildlife tracking datasets, and remotely sensed environmental layers. Computational challenges include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, machine learning-driven parameter optimization, and real-time integration of heterogeneous data streams during outbreak scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for managing stochastic model ensembles across >10,000 CPU cores while maintaining the spatial granularity (<1km² resolution) required to identify localized risk hotspots. Expected outcomes include 1) predictive risk maps identifying high-probability spillover zones under climate change scenarios, 2) comparative effectiveness metrics for vaccination versus habitat modification interventions, and 3) open-source computational workflows adaptable to emerging pathogens. This work directly addresses the National Animal Health System’s mandate for evidence-based preventive medicine while advancing One Health integration through quantitative frameworks that bridge veterinary and human epidemiological modeling paradigms. Resource allocation will support sustained 6-month computational campaigns requiring 2.5M node-hours, including GPU-accelerated deep learning components for pattern recognition in complex transmission networks.
cip_definition: Research focused on the investigation of and intervention in health and disease problems of animal and related human communities, comparative medicine, and animal public health. May included related research in biostatistics, epidemiology, environmental control, toxicology and the planning and administration of animal health programs and services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of targeted neuropharmacological therapies by modeling drug interactions with dynamic neural receptor systems. A critical challenge in neuropharmacology is predicting how small-molecule drugs modulate the activity of structurally flexible receptors in the central nervous system (CNS), such as G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and ion channels. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve transient conformational states of these receptors or quantify the atomic-level effects of chemical modifications on drug efficacy and selectivity. To address this, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations paired with free-energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to map the binding landscapes of lead compounds against disease-relevant neural targets. Computational workflows will prioritize receptors implicated in addiction and neurodegenerative disorders, including dopamine D3 and NMDA receptors. HPC resources will enable microsecond-scale simulations of receptor-drug complexes under varying allosteric and orthosteric conditions, capturing rare but pharmacologically critical states. Parallelized virtual screening of compound libraries will further identify novel scaffolds with optimized blood-brain barrier permeability and reduced off-target toxicity. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into how receptor plasticity influences drug response, (2) predictive models linking chemical substructures to neuropharmacokinetic profiles, and (3) prioritized candidates for experimental validation. This work directly supports the development of precision therapies for opioid use disorder and Alzheimer’s disease while reducing reliance on low-throughput trial-and-error approaches. The scale of this project—requiring >1 million core-hours for ensemble simulations and terabyte-scale data analysis—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve statistically robust sampling of complex neuropharmacological systems. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools for structure-guided CNS drug design, benefiting interdisciplinary efforts to improve neurotherapeutic safety and efficacy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drugs that modify the function of the brain and central nervous system, the effects of such drugs on health, disease, perception, motor action, and behavior; and the development of countermeasures and treatment therapies. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, behavioral neuroscience, neurobiochemistry, neuropathology, the mechanisms of brain function, medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics, and studies of specific drugs and drug therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive computational framework to optimize personalized care protocols for Health Aides supporting patients with complex, multimorbid conditions in non-clinical settings. Health Aides often operate in environments with limited real-time access to clinical expertise, managing dynamic interactions between patient physiology, environmental factors, and care tasks. Current decision-support tools lack the capacity to integrate heterogeneous data streams (wearable sensors, environmental monitors, and patient-reported outcomes) while accounting for individual patient trajectories. We propose a machine learning approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model bidirectional relationships between care interventions and patient states across temporal scales. Multimodal data from a longitudinal cohort of 450 patients receiving Health Aide services will train hybrid neural networks combining temporal convolution layers for physiological time-series analysis with graph attention networks modeling intervention cascades. The computational workflow will include real-time simulation of intervention impacts using differentiable digital twin architectures, optimized for GPU-accelerated parameter space exploration. Key challenges include developing lightweight yet interpretable models deployable on edge devices, and quantifying uncertainty propagation in care recommendation systems. Expected outcomes include: 1) A validated predictive framework for adverse event mitigation (e.g., falls, medication timing errors) through anticipatory care adjustments 2) Automated generation of context-aware care checklists optimized for individual risk profiles 3) Open-source tools for simulating Health Aide workflow impacts on patient outcomes. By enabling precision health strategies at the paraprofessional care level, this research addresses critical gaps in scalable, equitable chronic disease management outside institutional settings. The HPC resources are essential for training multi-modal architectures, conducting virtual cohort studies through agent-based modeling, and maintaining rigorous privacy-preserving federated learning protocols across distributed care networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and assistance to patients under the direct supervision of other health care professionals, and/or to perform routine maintenance and general assistance in health care facilities and laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize nurse educator training and improve clinical instruction outcomes through data-driven modeling of educational interventions. Nursing education faces challenges in designing curricula that balance theoretical knowledge, clinical skill acquisition, and adaptive teaching strategies across diverse learner needs. Current approaches often rely on static competency assessments and small-scale evaluations, limiting scalability and personalization. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal educational data—including student performance metrics, clinical simulation logs, electronic health record interactions during training, and longitudinal competency evaluations—from six nursing programs. Machine learning models (recurrent neural networks and graph-based architectures) will identify patterns in skill development trajectories, while agent-based simulations will model the impact of variable clinical training scenarios on learner outcomes. These computational approaches require parallel processing to handle high-dimensional datasets (>10 TB) encompassing 15,000+ simulated patient encounters and 5 years of educational records. The project will also employ natural language processing to evaluate reflective writing assignments from trainees, correlating linguistic features with clinical reasoning development. Expected outcomes include predictive models for individualized learning pathway optimization, evidence-based guidelines for clinical instructor training, and open-source tools for simulating competency-based curricula. By enabling large-scale analysis of educational interactions and their downstream effects on patient care quality, this work aims to advance nursing pedagogy, reduce skill gaps in clinical settings, and establish computational methods as critical tools for health professions education research. The requested HPC resources are essential for training complex models, running ensemble simulations, and maintaining data security compliance for protected health information embedded in training materials.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to teach in academic and clinical settings, including staff development. Includes instruction in advanced nursing practice, nursing role development, curriculum and instruction, program and course design, clinical instruction, and evaluation of learning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize metal fabrication processes by simulating thermal-mechanical interactions during welding and cutting operations, with the goal of minimizing structural defects and improving material efficiency. Metal fabricators face persistent challenges in controlling heat-affected zones (HAZs), residual stresses, and dimensional inaccuracies in high-precision components, particularly when working with advanced alloys or complex geometries. Traditional trial-and-error methods to mitigate these issues are time-intensive and resource-heavy, limiting scalability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model multi-physics interactions during fabrication. High-resolution simulations will capture transient thermal gradients, phase transformations, and stress distributions in ferrous and non-ferrous metals under varying toolpaths, shielding gas flows, and energy inputs. A parametric ML model will then identify optimal process parameters to reduce warping and microcracking while maintaining production speed. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of 3D meshing requirements (10⁶–10⁷ elements), coupled multi-physics solvers, and iterative optimization loops across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit tailored for vocational training programs, predictive guidelines for minimizing post-fabrication machining, and a database linking material properties to process settings. By integrating computational modeling into metal fabrication workflows, this project aims to bridge gaps between theoretical metallurgy and shop-floor practices, reducing material waste by an estimated 15–20% in test cases while enhancing the precision of fabricated components. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops at partner fabrication institutes and integrated into the program’s blueprint interpretation curriculum, fostering data-driven decision-making in industrial trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to further process ferrous and/or non-ferrous metal plates or shapes, and to manufacture and/or install products as interpreted through technical drawings. Includes instruction in trade tools, shop equipment, reading and interpreting blueprints, material handling, welding, thermal cutting, metallurgy, template pattern development, plate and structural fabrication, destructive and non-destructive testing, inspection, shipment preparation and fabrication installation.

abstract: Fire investigation faces challenges in accurately determining the origin and cause of fires due to complex interactions between environmental variables, material properties, and human factors. Traditional methods often rely on physical evidence and expert interpretation, which can be subjective and limited in scenarios with incomplete data. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework that integrates high-fidelity fire dynamics simulations with probabilistic models of human behavior and material degradation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will conduct large-scale simulations using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model fire spread under diverse conditions, incorporating stochastic elements to represent uncertainties in witness accounts, material heterogeneity, and environmental fluctuations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze simulation outputs, identifying key patterns associated with ignition sources and propagation pathways. The resulting models aim to provide investigators with probabilistic maps of fire origin, enhancing the objectivity and reliability of forensic conclusions. Validation against historical case data will ensure model robustness, while the development of an interactive visualization platform will facilitate practical application by non-computational experts. The project's outcomes are anticipated to directly support legal proceedings by providing quantifiable evidence, reduce investigative timelines, and inform fire prevention policies through data-driven insights. Additionally, the project will generate an open-access dataset of simulated fire scenarios, serving as a benchmark for future research and training. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational intensity of multi-parameter simulations and enabling rapid iteration across hypothetical scenarios, ultimately contributing to more accurate arson detection and prevention strategies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and principles of fire combustion and behavior applied to the analysis of fires and their causes. Includes instruction in fire behavior and combustion, fire dynamics, hazardous materials chemistry, incendiary fire analysis, fire-related human behavior, forensic procedures, investigative techniques, case management and case preparation.

abstract: The development of nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems presents a critical challenge in optimizing therapeutic efficacy while minimizing off-target effects. Current experimental approaches to design such systems are constrained by the vast combinatorial space of nanoparticle compositions, surface modifications, and drug-polymer interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations through multiscale computational modeling to predict nanoparticle assembly, drug loading efficiency, and release kinetics under physiologically relevant conditions. We propose to employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using explicit solvent models to characterize polymer-drug interactions at atomic resolution, coupled with coarse-grained simulations to study nanoparticle self-assembly over microsecond timescales. Machine learning (ML) models will be trained on simulation-derived datasets to identify key physicochemical parameters governing stability and controlled release. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational burden of these simulations, which involve systems exceeding 500,000 atoms and require iterative sampling of thermodynamic ensembles. Additionally, ML workflows will integrate existing experimental data from our lab’s prior work on poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles with new simulation data to enhance predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for screening nanoparticle formulations, (2) quantitative relationships between polymer architecture and drug release profiles, and (3) identification of novel surface functionalization strategies to improve tumor-targeting specificity. This work will directly advance rational design in pharmaceutics by reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, accelerating the development of precision nanomedicines for oncology applications. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at a scale unachievable with local cluster infrastructure, particularly for free energy calculations and long-timescale conformational sampling. By bridging molecular-level insights with macroscale drug delivery performance, this project aims to establish a paradigm for computationally driven formulation optimization in pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the formulation of medicinal substances into product vehicles capable of being stored, transported, and then introduced into the patient and behaving in ways optimal to therapeutic interaction. Includes instruction in statistics, biopharmaceutics, drug metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, physical pharmacy, pharmacological analysis, drug design and development, pharmacological biotechnology, chemical separations, spectroscopy, drug-host interactions, immunology, quantitative drug measurement, enzymatic transformations, and metabolic excretion.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for advanced computational tools in processing and analyzing high-resolution audiovisual data, particularly within emerging media formats such as immersive 360-degree video, real-time interactive installations, and AI-driven content synthesis. Current workflows in audiovisual communication research face significant bottlenecks when handling large-scale datasets, including multi-channel audio, 4K/8K video streams, and dynamic 3D visualizations, which strain conventional computing systems. The research problem centers on optimizing latency, scalability, and fidelity in audiovisual processing pipelines to support real-time applications in remote collaboration, augmented reality journalism, and adaptive streaming technologies. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized media encoding/decoding, GPU-accelerated machine learning inference, and distributed rendering of complex audiovisual environments. Key methods include deploying containerized workflows for reproducibility, training transformer-based models for cross-modal analysis (e.g., synchronizing lip movements with audio in multilingual broadcasts), and simulating network conditions to test adaptive bitrate algorithms under varying bandwidth constraints. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale A/B testing of perceptual codecs and real-time processing of multi-camera feeds for volumetric video reconstruction. Expected outcomes include open-source toolkits for efficient audiovisual data management, benchmarks for latency-sensitive applications in journalism and telepresence, and novel metrics for evaluating perceptual quality in computationally intensive scenarios. By addressing these challenges, the project aims to advance accessibility standards for live captioning, reduce energy costs in media production pipelines, and provide scalable solutions for academic institutions exploring next-generation communication technologies. Results will directly inform curriculum development in audiovisual engineering while supporting collaborative research with media industry partners.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in audiovisual communications technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework for optimizing multi-body orbital trajectories of spacecraft in cislunar and deep space environments, a critical challenge in modern astronautical engineering. Current methods for trajectory design in dynamically complex gravitational regimes—such as those involving Earth-Moon Lagrange points or low-energy transfers—rely on simplified analytical models or heuristic approximations, which limit mission efficiency and scalability. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining direct collocation optimization, machine learning-aided gravity-assist sequencing, and parallelized n-body numerical integration. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to solve large-scale nonlinear programming problems characterizing fuel-optimal trajectories while accounting for time-varying perturbations from multiple celestial bodies. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive ephemeris data for long-duration simulations, implementing adaptive mesh refinement for trajectory discretization, and training neural networks on high-dimensional orbital datasets. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated mission design, validated against NASA’s Artemis program reference trajectories, with demonstrated improvements in propellant savings (15-30%) for crewed lunar gateway resupply scenarios. The work will directly advance capabilities in autonomous spacecraft navigation and enable computationally tractable solutions for multi-revolution transfers in chaotic dynamical systems. By integrating astrodynamics principles with scalable HPC architectures, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for precision in interplanetary trajectory optimization, with applications to next-generation space exploration initiatives and commercial satellite constellation deployments.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and operational evaluation of aircraft and space vehicles. Includes instruction in control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize real-time decision-making in the promotion of perishable and seasonal special products, such as artisanal foods and event-specific floral arrangements. The challenge lies in balancing dynamic consumer demand, supply chain constraints, and marketing efficacy for products with short lifecycle windows, where traditional campaign models struggle to adapt to rapidly shifting market conditions. Current approaches often rely on static historical data or heuristic strategies, leading to suboptimal resource allocation, wasted inventory, and missed revenue opportunities. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate consumer behavior, supply responses, and promotional channel interactions at scale. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of millions of agent interactions across diverse demographic and geospatial scenarios while processing real-time data streams from social media sentiment analysis, IoT-enabled inventory trackers, and point-of-sale systems. Key computational challenges include optimizing hyperparameters for RL-driven campaign adjustments under stochastic demand conditions and reducing latency in multi-objective optimization models that simultaneously prioritize profit margins, waste reduction, and brand engagement metrics. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of recommending adaptive promotional strategies at 12-24 hour intervals during critical sales periods, validated against historical performance data from partner firms in the specialty foods and floral industries. The project will contribute novel methodologies for time-sensitive marketing operations, demonstrating how computational intensity can replace traditional guesswork in niche product sectors. Results will be disseminated through open-source algorithm libraries and case studies quantifying reductions in product spoilage (target: 15-20%) and improvements in campaign ROI (target: 25-30%) relative to industry baselines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of special products, including floristry, food, and home and office products. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: Greenhouse operations require precise control of environmental variables to optimize plant growth, resource efficiency, and operational scalability. Current optimization strategies often rely on generalized guidelines or isolated sensor data, which fail to account for dynamic interactions between climate parameters, plant physiology, and facility-specific constraints. This project proposes a computational framework to model and simulate multi-variable greenhouse ecosystems at high resolution, enabling data-driven decision-making for energy, water, and nutrient allocation. The core challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets—including real-time sensor feeds, plant genomic traits, and 3D structural models of greenhouse layouts—into predictive models that balance biological, economic, and sustainability objectives. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process these large datasets and execute parallelized simulations of microclimate dynamics, crop yield projections, and resource-use scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and synthetic data to identify nonlinear relationships between environmental inputs (e.g., light spectra, CO₂ levels) and growth outcomes across plant species. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will further analyze airflow, humidity gradients, and thermal distribution within greenhouse architectures to inform infrastructure redesigns. The anticipated outcomes include optimized climate control protocols tailored to specific crops and facilities, predictive tools for stress response mitigation, and scalable models for automated resource allocation in semi-closed agricultural systems. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance precision greenhouse management, reduce operational waste, and establish a template for adaptive control systems in controlled-environment agriculture. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and partnerships with commercial greenhouse operators to accelerate adoption of computationally informed practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce, store, and deliver plant species in controlled indoor environments for wholesale, commercial, research, or other purposes. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science; climate, irrigation, and nutrition control equipment operation and maintenance; facilities management; inventory control; safety procedures; and personnel supervision.

abstract: Cancer progression and therapeutic resistance are driven by dynamic interactions between tumor cells and their microenvironment, yet the mechanisms underlying these processes remain poorly understood. This project seeks to characterize how spatial and temporal variations in tumor microenvironmental factors—including hypoxia, nutrient gradients, and stromal cell signaling—regulate metastatic behavior and therapy evasion in epithelial carcinomas. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model tumor cell decision-making processes at single-cell resolution across clinically relevant timescales. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate cancer cell phenotypic plasticity, incorporating experimental data on hormonal/growth factor signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, and treatment-induced selective pressures. The computational pipeline integrates multi-omics datasets (tissue-scale transcriptomics, proteomics) from human tumor biopsies to parameterize microenvironmental conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of tumor subpopulations (10⁶–10⁷ agents) under variable oxygenation, stromal crosstalk, and targeted therapy scenarios. Machine learning approaches will identify critical microenvironmental thresholds that trigger metastatic transitions or confer resistance to anti-angiogenic therapies. Validation will leverage longitudinal imaging data from murine xenograft models and clinical metastases. This work addresses a critical gap in predicting tumor adaptability by bridging tissue-scale physiology with subcellular decision-making processes. The computational framework will generate testable hypotheses about microenvironmental drivers of treatment failure while providing a platform to optimize combination therapies targeting both cancer cells and their ecological niches. Successful completion will advance precision oncology by elucidating how contextual signals shape cancer cell fate decisions, directly informing strategies to disrupt metastatic competence and improve therapeutic targeting in heterogeneous tumors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of carcinogens; the onset of malignancy in cells, tissues, blood, and organs; the genetics of cancer; the anatomy and physiology of cancer cells; and the study of cancer behaviors and treatments. Includes instruction in gene expression; oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes; viral genes and cancer proliferation; regulation of signal transduction; cancer proteins; hormonal and growth factors in cancer cells; tumor promotion, progression, and metastasis; carcinogen receptors and metabolism; carcinogen ecology; immunological targeting; and studies of genetic, chemical, radiologic and other treatment therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical and energetic mechanisms underlying Reiki healing practices using high-performance computing (HPC) to model interactions between human biofields and therapeutic interventions. Despite widespread use in holistic health, the physiological and energetic correlates of Reiki remain poorly characterized, limiting integration into evidence-based healthcare frameworks. Current challenges include mapping the dynamics of biofield modulation during Reiki techniques (e.g., aura clearing, symbol-based healing) and quantifying how energy transfer influences cellular or systemic outcomes. To address this, we propose multiscale computational simulations integrating electromagnetic field models, quantum bioinformatics, and machine learning. HPC resources will enable (1) agent-based modeling of energy transfer between practitioner and recipient during hands-on and distance healing, (2) finite element analysis of electromagnetic propagation through anatomical models under varying Reiki symbols and attunement protocols, and (3) probabilistic analysis of longitudinal clinical data from Reiki sessions to identify biomarkers of therapeutic efficacy. Simulations will incorporate empirical data from bioelectrography, heart rate variability measurements, and biochemical assays to validate model parameters. The computational framework will be iteratively refined using Bayesian optimization to reconcile theoretical energy medicine principles with observed biological responses. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of biofield interactions during Reiki therapies, quantitative metrics for optimizing practitioner training protocols, and evidence-based criteria for personalizing healing techniques. By elucidating mechanisms through which Reiki promotes homeostatic balance, this work aims to bridge energy medicine paradigms with mainstream biophysical research, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. The proposed HPC resources are critical for handling complex tensor calculations, large-scale parameter space exploration, and real-time visualization of energy field dynamics, which exceed the capacity of local workstations. Results will inform curriculum development for Reiki training programs and provide a foundation for clinical trials investigating Reiki’s role in integrative medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical, emotional, and spiritual balance and healing through the manipulation of the body's energy field to increase healing energy. Includes instruction in the history and philosophy of Usui Reiki, attunement, empowerment, self-treatment, direct and distance healing techniques, healing symbols, aura clearing, Reiki meditation, practice management, and related Reiki systems such as Lightarian, Urevia, and Magnified Healing.

abstract: This project seeks to advance computational workflows in drafting and design engineering technologies by developing scalable tools for automated design optimization and simulation-driven prototyping. Current drafting methodologies often rely on iterative manual adjustments to meet multi-objective constraints (e.g., structural integrity, material efficiency, manufacturability), a process that becomes computationally prohibitive for complex assemblies or non-standard geometries. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach integrating parametric modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML)-based surrogate models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for parallelizing large-scale design space explorations, where thousands of parametric variations are evaluated against mechanical, thermal, and cost-based criteria. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for FEA simulations and distributed training of ML models to predict performance outcomes from geometric and material inputs. A key innovation involves coupling generative adversarial networks (GANs) with topology optimization algorithms to propose novel component geometries that satisfy predefined constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for automated drafting workflows, validated through case studies in modular construction systems and precision tooling design. This work will directly impact industries reliant on rapid prototyping by reducing computational bottlenecks in design validation, enabling the exploration of non-intuitive solutions that balance performance and production feasibility. The requested HPC allocation will support large memory nodes for handling high-resolution meshes and multi-GPU configurations to accelerate both simulation and ML training phases. Results will be disseminated through engineering technology conferences and workshops targeting workforce development in advanced drafting applications.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in drafting/design engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of variability and inefficiency in histologic tissue processing through the development of a computational framework for protocol optimization. Current methods for tissue fixation, dehydration, embedding, and sectioning rely on empirical adjustments, leading to inconsistent sample quality, prolonged processing times, and suboptimal diagnostic outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating multi-scale computational modeling, machine learning (ML), and high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and predict the effects of processing variables on tissue integrity. The research will focus on two primary computational objectives: (1) simulating chemical diffusion dynamics during fixation and dehydration using fluid dynamics models, and (2) analyzing mechanical stress distributions during paraffin embedding and microtome sectioning via finite element analysis. These simulations will generate datasets correlating processing parameters (e.g., reagent concentrations, temperature, time, blade geometry) with tissue quality metrics (e.g., structural preservation, section uniformity). HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of thousands of parameter combinations, while ML algorithms will identify optimal protocols under constraints such as time, cost, and tissue type. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from murine and human tissue samples processed under controlled conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for protocol optimization, open-source simulation tools tailored for histotechnicians, and a framework for real-time adaptive adjustments in clinical workflows. By bridging computational science and histologic technique, this project aims to standardize tissue processing, reduce manual trial-and-error, and enhance diagnostic reliability in anatomic pathology. The scalability of the approach also opens avenues for addressing rare tissue types or novel processing methods, advancing precision in both research and clinical histology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets, with a focus on addressing computational bottlenecks in Bayesian hierarchical modeling and uncertainty quantification. Modern applications, such as genomic association studies and spatiotemporal environmental monitoring, increasingly involve complex data structures that challenge traditional estimation techniques. Existing algorithms for hierarchical models—particularly those relying on Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling—struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces due to poor mixing, memory constraints, and prohibitive runtime when applied to datasets with millions of observations. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining variational inference with parallelized, preconditioned MCMC samplers. This approach will leverage distributed computing architectures to partition parameter updates across nodes while maintaining theoretical guarantees on convergence. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated gradient calculations for variational objectives and a dynamic load-balancing system to mitigate bottlenecks in sparse data settings. The computational workflow will be implemented using Julia’s MPI.jl and CUDA.jl ecosystems, optimized for memory efficiency and scalability on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. We will validate the method through simulations and case studies in two domains: (1) multi-omics integration for cancer subtype classification, and (2) probabilistic nowcasting of extreme weather events using satellite-derived climate networks. Success will be measured by achieving a 50-100x speedup over state-of-the-art MCMC implementations for models with >10⁵ parameters, while maintaining inferential accuracy. The resulting software tools will be disseminated as open-source packages, accompanied by reproducibility benchmarks and user documentation. By enabling faster and more precise uncertainty quantification in large-scale statistical models, this work will advance methodological research in Bayesian statistics and directly support interdisciplinary collaborations requiring robust analysis of complex modern datasets.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to address challenges in automated auditing and anomaly detection within large-scale financial datasets, leveraging advances in machine learning (ML) and distributed computing. Modern accounting systems generate vast, heterogeneous data streams, but existing tools for real-time fraud detection and compliance monitoring struggle with scalability, interpretability, and adaptability to evolving financial instruments. By combining techniques from accounting analytics, natural language processing (NLP), and graph-based anomaly detection, this research aims to bridge gaps in processing efficiency and analytical precision. The core computational challenge involves training multimodal deep learning models on structured transactional data, unstructured audit narratives, and temporal ledger networks while maintaining traceability for regulatory compliance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle iterative model training on encrypted financial datasets (spanning terabytes of transaction records), optimize hyperparameters for federated learning architectures, and simulate adversarial attack scenarios to test system robustness. Key methodologies include GPU-accelerated graph neural networks for tracing transaction interdependencies, transformer-based NLP pipelines for auditing document analysis, and differentially private optimization to ensure data confidentiality. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for scalable audit analytics, (2) novel benchmarks for evaluating anomaly detection models in accounting contexts, and (3) performance-optimized workflows compatible with industry-standard accounting platforms. By enabling real-time analysis of cross-institutional financial data with rigorous privacy safeguards, this work will advance interdisciplinary research at the intersection of accounting ethics and computational trust systems. The requested HPC allocation will directly support large-scale experiments, including parallelized processing of synthetic financial graphs (10^8+ nodes) and comparative studies of cryptographic verification methods for audit trails. Results will inform both academic discourse on accountable AI in finance and practical frameworks for auditors adapting to blockchain-integrated economies.
cip_definition: A program that combines accounting with computer science and/or computer studies.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across European diasporic communities, with a focus on underrepresented voices in 20th-century colonial and post-colonial contexts. Current scholarship lacks systematic methods for tracing non-dominant cultural expressions across fragmented multilingual sources, including periodicals, personal correspondence, and grassroots artistic works. The research will employ transformer-based language models adapted for historical texts in French, Dutch, and indigenous European languages, combined with network analysis to map transnational cultural exchanges obscured by traditional archival methods. High-performance computing resources are required to process approximately 15TB of digitized materials from dispersed colonial archives, train multilingual embedding spaces that account for semantic shifts across temporal and geographic contexts, and simulate cultural transmission pathways through agent-based modeling. The computational pipeline will integrate computer vision techniques to analyze visual materials alongside textual data, addressing the challenge of multimodal cultural analysis at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated intercultural dialogues, quantitative metrics for measuring hybrid cultural influences, and visual analytics tools to support comparative studies of identity negotiation. This work aims to provide new methodological pathways for studying European civilization as a dynamic, contested process rather than a fixed geographic or political entity, with particular significance for understanding how marginalized groups reshaped cultural narratives through transnational networks. The resource-intensive nature of processing heterogeneous, low-quality historical documents at continental scale necessitates parallelized GPU computing and distributed storage solutions beyond typical institutional capacities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the European Continent, including the study of European migration patterns and colonial empires.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate fire dynamics and evacuation behaviors in complex, mixed-use urban environments, with a focus on understudied scenarios involving historical structures and adaptive reuse buildings. Current fire models often prioritize modern, code-compliant buildings, leaving gaps in predicting fire spread, smoke movement, and occupant egress in architecturally irregular or heritage spaces where traditional safety systems may be constrained. The research problem centers on the lack of tailored computational tools to address the unique fire risks in these environments, which are critical to urban resilience and cultural preservation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations—using open-source tools like Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS)—with agent-based models (ABMs) to capture bidirectional interactions between fire progression and human decision-making under stress. The computational approach will incorporate multi-scale modeling, combining 3D structural scans of case study buildings with probabilistic risk assessments of ignition sources and occupant density patterns. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize evacuation pathfinding algorithms in geometrically complex spaces. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for smoke infiltration rates in non-compartmentalized structures, dynamic risk maps for heritage sites, and evidence-based recommendations for retrofitting passive fire protection systems without compromising historical integrity. By addressing the intersection of fire safety engineering, heritage conservation, and behavioral psychology, this work will provide actionable insights for policymakers and preservationists, enhancing community safety while balancing regulatory and cultural priorities. The HPC resources are essential to manage the high-resolution simulations and parametric analyses required for scenario testing across diverse architectural typologies and occupancy conditions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize precision irrigation and nutrient delivery systems in controlled-environment horticulture, a critical challenge in modern agricultural operations. Current approaches to managing water and fertilizer use in greenhouse and vertical farming systems rely on generalized models that inadequately account for real-time interactions between plant genotypes, substrate properties, and microclimate variability. This limitation results in resource inefficiencies, increased operational costs, and environmental strain. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating hyperspectral plant phenotyping data, soil moisture dynamics simulations, and machine learning (ML) models. The project will utilize 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to process temporal-spectral image stacks capturing plant stress responses, coupled with finite element analysis to model water movement in heterogeneous growth media. These components will feed into a reinforcement learning system trained to recommend adaptive irrigation schedules that minimize water and nutrient waste while maximizing biomass production. The scale of data integration—terabyte-level sensor inputs from IoT-enabled greenhouse networks—and the need for parallelized execution of coupled physical-biological models necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for horticultural operators, validated against experimental trials in tomato and leafy green production systems. By enabling sub-hourly adjustments to resource delivery based on predictive plant-substrate feedback, this work aims to advance sustainable practices in commercial horticulture, reducing water use by an estimated 15–25% and fertilizer runoff by 10–20% in controlled environments. The computational framework will also provide a template for optimizing other dynamic horticultural processes, from pest management to harvest timing.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general production and processing of domesticated plants, shrubs, flowers, foliage, trees, groundcovers, and related plant materials; the management of technical and business operations connected with horticultural services; and the basic scientific principles needed to understand plants and their management and care.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance fire risk assessment and evacuation modeling in complex built environments. Current fire safety evaluations often rely on simplified assumptions about fire dynamics, human behavior, and structural responses, limiting their accuracy in predicting real-world scenarios. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for fire and smoke propagation, agent-based models (ABMs) for occupant evacuation, and finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity under thermal stress. The research will focus on simulating high-rise buildings and industrial facilities, where spatial complexity and occupancy density amplify risks. Key challenges include resolving turbulent combustion processes at varying scales, modeling adaptive human decision-making during emergencies, and assessing feedback between fire spread and structural deformation. HPC resources are critical to support parallelized simulations with high spatial-temporal resolution, particularly for large-domain CFD cases and Monte Carlo analyses evaluating probabilistic evacuation outcomes under diverse fire scenarios. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to historical fire incident data to refine behavioral parameters in ABMs. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for identifying critical failure points in evacuation routes, optimizing smoke control system designs, and quantifying the impact of material flammability on structural collapse timelines. These results will directly inform fire code revisions, emergency response training protocols, and cost-benefit analyses for retrofitting aging infrastructure. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing of safety interventions, this work aims to reduce uncertainties in fire risk management while minimizing reliance on physical prototypes. The requested computational allocation will empower novel insights into coupled fire-human-structure interactions, advancing both theoretical fire science and practical fire prevention strategies for urban resilience.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science and technology to problems of reducing fire risk, limiting loss, supervising substance removal, conducting safety inspections and investigations, and advising on matters of safety procedures and fire prevention policy. Includes instruction in fire behavior, fire simulation, structural risk assessment, materials analysis, detection and suppression systems, smoke management, supply and evacuation, public education, legal aspects of fire prevention, and related research and communications methods.

abstract: Ocular diseases in animals present complex challenges due to species-specific anatomical variations, multifactorial etiologies, and limited understanding of disease progression mechanisms. This project seeks to advance veterinary ophthalmology by developing computational models to simulate ocular biomechanics, disease pathways, and surgical interventions, with a focus on glaucoma and corneal disorders in companion animals. The research problem centers on the lack of high-fidelity, dynamic models to predict intraocular pressure (IOP) fluctuations, corneal wound healing responses, and outcomes of surgical techniques such as laser cyclophotocoagulation. Traditional experimental approaches are constrained by ethical limitations, interspecies variability, and the inability to capture real-time, multidimensional interactions within ocular tissues. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model biomechanical stress distributions in feline and canine globes under varying IOP conditions, while agent-based modeling will simulate cellular responses to corneal injury and repair. Machine learning algorithms, trained on multimodal datasets (optical coherence tomography, tonometry, histopathology), will identify predictive biomarkers for early-stage glaucoma. Molecular dynamics simulations will investigate the efficacy of novel topical therapeutics targeting corneal neovascularization. These computationally intensive workflows require parallelized processing of high-resolution 3D meshes, large-scale parameter optimization, and real-time visualization of surgical scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for IOP dysregulation, optimized surgical planning protocols, and candidate compounds for inhibiting pathological angiogenesis. The project will provide foundational tools for personalized treatment strategies in veterinary ophthalmology, reduce reliance on invasive experimental models, and establish scalable computational methodologies applicable to rare or genetically complex ocular conditions across species. Successful implementation hinges on access to HPC infrastructure capable of supporting GPU-accelerated simulations, petabyte-scale data storage, and multi-node processing for iterative model validation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders in animals, and related ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in animal eye surgery.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational tools for analyzing and modeling narrative structures in playwriting and screenwriting, addressing the challenge of quantifying creative choices in script development. While traditional script analysis relies on subjective interpretation, this research integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to systematically evaluate narrative coherence, emotional arc dynamics, and audience engagement potential in theatrical and cinematic texts. The core computational problem involves processing large corpora of scripts—both historical and contemporary—to identify patterns in dialogue pacing, character interaction networks, and thematic evolution. By training ML models on annotated datasets of award-winning plays and films, the project aims to generate predictive frameworks that correlate structural elements with documented audience or critical reception. A key technical hurdle is the real-time simulation of script permutations, requiring GPU-accelerated parallel processing to iteratively test variations in scene order, dialogue density, or character decisions within virtual staging environments. Proposed workflows include sentiment analysis pipelines for emotional valence mapping, graph-based algorithms to model character relationship dynamics, and Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic audience responses under different narrative conditions. Outcomes will include an open-access toolkit for writers and educators to visualize structural metrics in scripts, alongside a repository of computational models linking creative techniques to performance outcomes. This work bridges artistic practice and data-driven analysis, offering novel methodologies for script optimization while preserving creative intent. By advancing computational narratology within performing arts, the project aims to expand interdisciplinary dialogue between HPC applications and humanistic inquiry, fostering innovation in both storytelling craft and digital humanities research.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for communicating dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the composition of creative written works for the theatre, film, and/or television. Includes instruction in creative writing craft, scene writing, script development, stage and/or camera instructions, line and moment analysis, script reading, script editing, and the creation of full productions.

abstract: Forensic pathology faces growing challenges in synthesizing complex, multi-modal datasets to resolve ambiguous causes of death and support legal accountability. Current workflows for integrating histopathology, toxicology, genetic analyses, and crime scene reconstructions rely on manual correlation, which is time-intensive, prone to human error, and ill-suited for large-scale data. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to automate and enhance the analysis of forensic evidence through high-performance computing (HPC). The primary research problem involves creating predictive models that reconcile heterogeneous data—such as 3D postmortem imaging, mass spectrometry outputs, and genomic sequences—to identify subtle patterns indicative of trauma, poisoning, or natural disease. A hybrid machine learning approach will be employed, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image-based feature extraction (e.g., tissue injury quantification in autopsy photographs) with graph-based algorithms to map temporal and spatial relationships in crime scene data. Natural language processing (NLP) tools will parse autopsy reports and legal documents to extract contextual variables for model training. These components will be integrated into an HPC-optimized pipeline using parallelized workflows (MPI and CUDA) to manage terabyte-scale datasets. The project will validate the framework using retrospective cases with known ground truths, assessing accuracy gains over conventional methods. Anticipated outcomes include a reproducible, open-source platform for forensic data fusion, capable of identifying latent biomarkers (e.g., gene-environment interactions in drug-related deaths) and generating probabilistic reports to clarify pathologists’ legal testimony. By enabling rapid, evidence-based reconciliation of conflicting findings, this work aims to reduce diagnostic uncertainties in high-stakes forensic investigations and strengthen the scientific rigor of death certification processes in public health systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on the performance of medical autopsies, the analysis of human remains and crime scenes, and the legal follow-up and responsibilities of public pathologists.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical grids, driven by the integration of renewable energy sources, distributed generation, and smart grid technologies, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize power transmission infrastructure. This project seeks to address critical challenges in dynamic load balancing, fault prediction, and grid resilience by developing a high-fidelity simulation framework for power transmission networks. Current analytical models often lack the resolution to account for real-time variability in energy demand, intermittent renewable generation, and cascading failure risks in interconnected systems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a hybrid computational approach combining machine learning (ML)-based predictive analytics with physics-informed numerical simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallelization of power flow analyses, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic fault scenarios, and training of deep neural networks on historical grid performance data. The computational workflow will integrate grid topology datasets, real-time sensor inputs, and weather-dependent generation profiles to model transmission line stresses, voltage stability, and failure propagation under diverse operating conditions. Key outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for utilities to simulate grid behavior at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, identify high-risk infrastructure segments, and test mitigation strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in traditional power system analysis, enabling rapid scenario evaluation for grids with 10,000+ nodes. The results will provide actionable insights for upgrading aging transmission infrastructure, improving renewable integration capacity, and minimizing outage risks. This work aligns with national priorities for modernizing energy systems while advancing computational methodologies applicable to emerging smart grid technologies. All developed models and simulation datasets will be made publicly available to support industry and academic collaboration.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and microstructural interactions between dental implant materials and alveolar bone under dynamic physiological loading. Despite advancements in implantology, unpredictable failures due to stress shielding, micromotion, and osseointegration inefficiencies persist, often linked to mismatches in material properties and bone remodeling responses. Current experimental models struggle to capture the multiscale complexity of bone-implant interfaces, particularly under heterogeneous mechanical and biological conditions. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) at the macro-scale with agent-based modeling (ABM) of osteocyte-osteoblast signaling networks at the micro-scale. High-resolution µCT scans of patient-derived mandibular bone architectures will inform geometrically accurate FEA models, while molecular dynamics simulations will parameterize ABM rules for mechanotransduction and bone adaptation. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across diverse clinical scenarios, including variations in bone density, occlusal forces, and implant surface topographies. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize hyperparameters and identify critical failure thresholds. Expected outcomes include predictive models of long-term implant stability, validated against longitudinal clinical imaging data, and actionable design principles for next-generation bioactive coatings. This work bridges materials science, computational biomechanics, and clinical dentistry, offering a paradigm shift from trial-and-error material development to simulation-driven innovation. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will empower precision treatment planning and accelerate regulatory evaluation of novel dental biomaterials, ultimately reducing implant failure rates and improving patient-specific therapeutic outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of dentistry/dental medicine, encompassing the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and adjacent structures and their impact on the human body and health. Includes instruction in the basic biomedical sciences, occlusion, dental health and prevention, oral pathology, cariology, operative dentistry, oral radiology, principles of the various dental specialties, pain management, oral medicine, clinic and health care management, patient counseling, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and reliability of electrical power transmission systems under dynamic load conditions, with a focus on integrating renewable energy sources into existing grid infrastructures. The increasing complexity of modern electrical grids, compounded by variable renewable inputs and fluctuating demand, poses significant challenges for safe and efficient installation practices. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for real-time variability, leading to suboptimal designs, increased risk of equipment failure, and non-compliance with evolving safety standards. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale, multi-physics models of power transmission networks. These simulations will incorporate real-world data on load patterns, environmental factors, and material properties to evaluate stress distribution, thermal behavior, and electromagnetic interference across transmission lines and connected components. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to predict failure modes and identify optimal wiring configurations, grounding strategies, and insulation materials under diverse operational scenarios. The computational pipeline will also integrate code-compliant safety thresholds to automate compliance checks during the design phase. By enabling rapid iteration of system designs and proactive risk assessment, this work aims to reduce installation costs, minimize downtime, and enhance grid resilience. Outcomes will include open-source tools for simulating region-specific transmission networks and evidence-based guidelines for installers to adapt to emerging technologies such as distributed solar arrays and battery storage systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space and real-time data processing demands, which exceed the capabilities of local computational clusters. This research directly supports the program’s mission to advance technical training in electrical installation by bridging theoretical knowledge with data-driven, scalable solutions for next-generation power infrastructure.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installation/ Installer, General
