The research will focus on integrating heterogeneous datasets (e.g., geolocation logs, encrypted communications, and image metadata) to model timelines, interactions, and behavioral patterns relevant to criminal acts. Computational methods will include machine learning algorithms for anomaly detection in large-scale communication networks, graph-based analyses to map relationships between entities, and probabilistic simulations to test competing hypotheses about crime sequences. A key innovation involves coupling these techniques with forensic principles to ensure legally defensible results, including uncertainty quantification for probabilistic conclusions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, real-time visualization of reconstructed timelines, and iterative refinement of models through GPU-accelerated simulations. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit validated against historical case data, with demonstrated improvements in processing speed (targeting 10–50x reductions in analysis time for complex cases) and accuracy compared to manual methods. This work will directly support forensic investigators in resolving evidence backlogs, improving reconstruction reliability, and mitigating risks of misinterpretation. By advancing computational criminology methodologies, the project also aims to establish best practices for integrating HPC into criminalistics workflows, with broader implications for homeland security applications such as threat detection and preventive policing. Resource allocation will prioritize developing containerized workflows for portability, ensuring accessibility to law enforcement agencies with varying IT infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of clinical and criminal laboratory science, investigative techniques, and criminology to the reconstruction of crimes and the analysis of physical evidence. Includes instruction in laboratory science, laboratory procedures, criminology and police science, evidentiary testing and analysis, computer applications, record-keeping, reconstruction techniques, evidence handling and storage, and applications to specific types of evidence and crimes.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with complex mechanisms underlying conditions such as heart failure, arrhythmias, and ischemic heart disease. A critical barrier to advancing personalized cardiology is the integration of multi-modal clinical data—including imaging, electrophysiology, and genomics—into predictive models that account for patient-specific variability. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational frameworks capable of simulating cardiac pathophysiology at unprecedented resolution. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating multi-scale models of cardiac electromechanics that incorporate patient-derived data from MRI, CT, and intracardiac mapping to simulate arrhythmia propagation and hemodynamic outcomes, and (2) employing machine learning to identify genomic and proteomic biomarkers associated with adverse cardiac remodeling, using whole-genome sequencing and proteomic datasets from longitudinal cohort studies. The computational workflows will utilize finite element modeling, computational fluid dynamics, and deep learning algorithms, necessitating parallelized processing and large-scale memory allocation. By simulating interventions such as catheter ablation or pharmacological therapies in silico, the models aim to predict optimal treatment strategies for individual patients. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for sudden cardiac death risk stratification, the development of open-source simulation tools for clinical researchers, and validation of patient-specific treatment planning protocols through retrospective clinical data analysis. This work addresses a pressing need for computationally intensive approaches in cardiology, where traditional methods fail to capture the interplay between molecular, cellular, and organ-level dynamics. Successful implementation will advance precision cardiology by bridging gaps between computational research and clinical translation, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes for patients with complex cardiovascular conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on Cardiology

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in real-time spatial audio processing and acoustic environment simulation, which are constrained by the computational intensity of high-fidelity audio modeling. Current methods for simulating dynamic acoustic spaces or rendering immersive audio experiences—such as virtual reality (VR) environments or live sound reinforcement systems—rely on simplified approximations that sacrifice perceptual realism for computational feasibility. This research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model wave-based acoustic propagation, real-time auralization, and nonlinear signal processing chains with unprecedented precision. Leveraging parallelized finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms and GPU-accelerated digital signal processing pipelines, the project will simulate room acoustics at audible frequency resolutions (20 Hz–20 kHz) and integrate machine learning models to optimize perceptual audio quality in hybrid physical-virtual environments. The computational workload necessitates large-scale memory allocation and distributed processing to handle multi-channel, high-sample-rate audio data alongside 3D spatial simulations. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for wave-based acoustic simulation, a dataset of perceptually validated hybrid acoustics profiles, and optimized algorithms for low-latency spatial audio rendering. These resources will directly benefit audio engineering education and industry applications by enabling accurate auralizations of concert halls, studio environments, and augmented reality (AR) soundscapes. The project bridges gaps between computational acoustics and practical audio production, advancing the engineering of adaptive audio systems that respond dynamically to listener position, environmental variables, and source material characteristics. By deploying HPC resources, this work overcomes traditional bottlenecks in audio engineering research, fostering innovation in immersive media technologies and acoustics education.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the mixing, recording, and production of music. Includes instruction in acoustics, audio mixing, audio production, audio recording, computer composition of music, music theory, digital devices, and sound technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on Baltic cultural heritage preservation through the analysis of multilingual historical texts and ethnographic records. The Baltic region, characterized by dynamic linguistic and cultural exchanges over centuries, presents a complex mosaic of interactions among Baltic, Germanic, Scandinavian, and Slavic communities. However, the fragmented nature of surviving archival materials—spanning manuscripts, printed works, and oral histories—poses significant challenges for systematic analysis. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to scale across these vast, multilingual corpora, limiting insights into patterns of cultural transmission, adaptation, and resistance. This project addresses this gap by developing computational workflows to map and analyze cultural narratives, semantic shifts, and intertextual connections across time and linguistic boundaries. Using natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for low-resource Baltic languages (e.g., Latvian, Lithuanian, Estonian) and historical Germanic dialects, we will perform large-scale text mining, entity recognition, and semantic network analysis on digitized collections from 16th–20th centuries. HPC resources are essential to train transformer-based models on heterogeneous, noisy textual data and to simulate cultural diffusion patterns via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of understudied narrative motifs reflecting cross-cultural exchanges, (2) quantitative frameworks for tracking cultural resilience in minority communities, and (3) open-access tools tailored for Baltic linguistic and historical research. By integrating computational rigor with area studies expertise, this work will enable novel interpretations of cultural survival strategies while establishing scalable methodologies for regional humanities scholarship. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, parallelized corpus processing, and storage for intermediate datasets, which are infeasible on local infrastructure due to data volume and computational complexity.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the coastlands of the Baltic Sea, including Baltic, Germanic, Scandinavian, and Slavic populations, related borderlands and island groups, and problems of cultural survival and assimilation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cyber-physical systems (CPS) in critical infrastructure has exposed gaps in existing security auditing frameworks, particularly in scenarios requiring real-time anomaly detection across heterogeneous, distributed components. Traditional audit mechanisms, often reliant on centralized log analysis and static rule sets, struggle to scale with the dynamic interdependencies and high-throughput data streams inherent to modern CPS. This project seeks to address this challenge by developing a decentralized, machine learning (ML)-driven auditing framework that integrates cryptographic verification with adaptive anomaly detection. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will simulate large-scale CPS environments—including smart grids and industrial control systems—to model attack vectors such as stealthy sensor spoofing and coordinated command injection. Computational methods will focus on parallelized training of ensemble ML models optimized for temporal and spatial anomaly patterns, coupled with lightweight, post-quantum cryptographic primitives for secure audit trail generation. The HPC environment will enable stress-testing of the framework under scenarios emulating terabyte-scale log volumes and sub-millisecond latency constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated protocol for tamper-evident, real-time auditing in CPS, open-source tools for adaptive threshold tuning in anomaly detection, and benchmarks quantifying the trade-offs between cryptographic overhead and detection accuracy. By bridging cryptographic accountability with ML-driven adaptability, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for auditing in environments where traditional computer security approaches are insufficient due to scale, real-time demands, or physical system dependencies. The resulting methodologies will directly inform standards for resilient infrastructure auditing, with applications in energy, transportation, and manufacturing sectors.
cip_title: Computer and Information Systems Security/ Auditing/ Information Assurance
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assess the security needs of computer and network systems, recommend safeguard solutions, and manage the implementation, auditing, and maintenance of security devices, systems, and procedures. Includes instruction in computer architecture, programming, and systems analysis; networking; telecommunications; cryptography; security system auditing and design; applicable law and regulations; risk assessment and policy analysis; contingency planning; user access issues; investigation techniques; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the structure and dynamics of neutron-rich nuclei through advanced computational modeling. The research problem centers on the limitations of current theoretical frameworks in predicting the properties of nuclei under extreme isospin conditions, such as those found in neutron star crusts or heavy-ion collision environments. Existing models struggle to reconcile discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental observations of nuclear binding energies, decay modes, and collective excitation spectra for nuclei far from stability. To overcome these challenges, we propose large-scale ab initio simulations using realistic nucleon-nucleon interactions with three-body forces, implemented through the configuration space Monte Carlo method and symmetry-adapted no-core shell model techniques. These computationally intensive approaches require high-performance computing resources to handle the combinatorial complexity of many-body wavefunctions and the numerical precision demanded by quantum chromodynamics-informed potential models. The requested allocations will enable simulations of nuclei with mass numbers up to A=60 at unprecedented resolution, incorporating full treatment of continuum effects and time-dependent perturbation theory for decay processes. Expected outcomes include refined predictions for nuclear masses and beta-decay rates critical to r-process nucleosynthesis models, improved constraints on the symmetry energy term in nuclear equations of state, and validation of next-generation effective field theory parameters. The computational results will directly support planned experiments at rare isotope facilities while advancing fundamental knowledge of strong interaction physics. By leveraging petascale architectures for iterative diagonalization of large Hamiltonian matrices and Bayesian uncertainty quantification, this work will establish new benchmarks for precision nuclear theory and enable predictive modeling of exotic nuclear systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of atomic nuclei. Includes instruction in nuclear reaction theory, quantum mechanics, energy conservation, nuclear fission and fusion, strong and weak forces, nuclear modeling, nuclear decay, nucleon scattering, pairing, photon and electron reactions, the physics of nuclear effects, statistical methods, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize radiation therapy treatment planning while minimizing secondary cancer risks associated with ionizing radiation exposure—a critical public health concern. Current models for predicting long-term radiation effects often rely on population-averaged data, neglecting patient-specific anatomical variability, genetic susceptibility, and dosimetric uncertainties. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport with machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of radiobiological outcomes. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate radiation dose deposition at sub-millimeter resolution across diverse patient anatomies derived from clinical CT/MRI datasets. Parallelized simulations will quantify dose uncertainties in heterogeneous tissues, while ML models trained on longitudinal patient outcome data will predict secondary cancer risks based on individualized dosimetric, genomic, and environmental factors. A key innovation is the integration of probabilistic risk assessment algorithms to evaluate population-level impacts of treatment protocols, informing public health strategies for radiation safety. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental radiobiology data and clinical cohorts. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for personalized risk-adapted radiotherapy planning, reducing morbidity in cancer survivors. By bridging medical physics and public health, this work aims to establish scalable computational methods for evaluating radiation-related hazards across diverse populations, directly supporting the development of evidence-based guidelines for therapeutic radiation use. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the ∼500 TB of simulation data and computationally intensive ML training phases, enabling rapid iteration of models that would otherwise be infeasible on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics, nuclear science, and engineering physics to diagnostic, treatment, and therapeutic processes and public health protection. Includes instruction in radiation biophysics, biophysics, health effects of natural and artificially induced radiation, hazard evaluation, environmental radioactivity, nuclear physics, engineering physics, radiobiology, medical radiology, calibration and dosage theory, computer applications and medical informatics, and specific research problems.

abstract: Horticulture therapy (HT) leverages plant-based interventions to improve physical, cognitive, and psychological health outcomes, yet the mechanisms underlying these therapeutic effects remain poorly quantified. Current research faces a critical gap in modeling the multivariate interactions between plant biological traits, environmental conditions, and patient-specific physiological or behavioral responses. This project proposes to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate and predict HT outcomes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on the need to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including plant genomics, environmental sensor data, and longitudinal patient health metrics—into predictive models that account for dynamic, non-linear relationships. Computational methods will involve multi-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate plant-patient-environment interactions, machine learning (ML) pipelines for pattern recognition in high-dimensional health datasets, and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify plant traits correlated with therapeutic efficacy. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of large-scale genomic datasets, real-time ABM simulations across diverse virtual environments, and training ML models on anonymized patient data (e.g., biometrics, psychological assessments). Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models to optimize plant selection and therapeutic garden designs for specific patient populations, (2) identification of genetic markers in plants associated with stress reduction or cognitive improvement, and (3) open-source tools for personalized HT intervention planning. This work will advance evidence-based practices in horticulture therapy while contributing novel computational methodologies to the broader field of therapeutic intervention design. By bridging plant science, psychology, and data science, the project aligns with national priorities to integrate nature-based solutions into healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on plant science and horticulture techniques to achieve measurable physical and mental health outcomes for individuals with physical or mental challenges. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, adult development and aging, botany, facilities design, horticultural therapy, plant pathology, people-plant relationships, and psychology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to optimize the design and operational performance of energy-efficient building systems under dynamic environmental and structural loads. Current approaches to evaluating building performance often rely on compartmentalized simulations (e.g., isolated thermal, structural, or airflow analyses) that fail to capture critical interdependencies between systems, leading to suboptimal resource use and increased lifecycle costs. The proposed research addresses this gap by integrating multiphysics computational models—including computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and transient energy modeling—to holistically assess building behavior. Key challenges include resolving the scale disparities between micro-scale material responses and macro-scale environmental interactions, as well as managing the computational expense of long-duration, high-resolution simulations. The project will leverage parallelized solvers and adaptive mesh refinement techniques on HPC clusters to simulate coupled heat transfer, structural stress, and airflow patterns in buildings with complex geometries and hybrid material systems. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on simulation outputs to accelerate parametric studies of design variables such as insulation placement, HVAC configuration, and phase-change material integration. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for optimizing energy use and occupant comfort while maintaining structural resilience under extreme weather scenarios. This work will provide architects and engineers with actionable insights into balancing competing performance metrics during the design phase, directly supporting the development of sustainable, climate-adaptive buildings. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses and uncertainty quantification studies that are infeasible with local workstations, reducing time-to-solution by orders of magnitude. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and case studies on retrofitting existing structures, with potential impacts on reducing operational carbon footprints in the built environment.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials, systems, and methods used to construct and equip buildings intended for human habitation or other purposes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for large school districts, addressing systemic inefficiencies in budgeting, staffing, and facility management that disproportionately affect underserved communities. While educational leaders recognize the need for equity-centered decision-making, existing tools lack the capacity to model complex, district-wide trade-offs between competing priorities—such as teacher retention initiatives, infrastructure upgrades, and academic support programs—under dynamic demographic and fiscal constraints. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a multi-agent simulation platform that integrates real-world datasets from a partner urban school district (enrollment: 85,000+ students), including historical budget records, student performance metrics, staff mobility patterns, and facility utilization reports. Agent-based modeling will simulate how different allocation policies propagate through interconnected administrative, instructional, and operational systems over 10-year horizons. Computational experiments will evaluate scenarios balancing state accountability mandates, community input from town hall records (processed via NLP), and emergency budget contingencies. The models will employ Monte Carlo methods to account for demographic shifts and economic volatility, requiring parallelized parameter sweeps across thousands of permutations. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies equity impacts of budget choices, identifies non-linear relationships between resource inputs and student success metrics, and forecasts second-order effects of austerity measures or funding windfalls. This work directly advances the program’s focus on evidence-based system leadership by providing superintendents with scalable, data-driven methods to navigate complex trade-offs while maintaining compliance with evolving policy landscapes. The computational intensity of modeling entire districts at granular levels necessitates HPC capabilities, particularly for memory-intensive demographic microsimulations and rapid sensitivity analyses during public budget hearings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leading and managing multi-school educational systems and school districts and prepares individuals to serve as systems administrators and district superintendents. Includes instruction in educational administration; education of students at various levels; system planning and budgeting; educational policy; educational law and regulations; public relations; professional standards and ethics; and applications to specific issues, cultural context, and geographic locales.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance evidence-based public policy design by developing a computational framework to simulate the multi-scale impacts of policy interventions in complex social systems. Public policy analysis faces a persistent challenge in anticipating unintended consequences and emergent behaviors arising from policy decisions, particularly in domains with interconnected stakeholders, nonlinear feedback loops, and heterogeneous population dynamics. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with machine learning techniques to simulate policy scenarios across education access reforms and crisis response planning. The computational model will incorporate granular demographic data, institutional decision rules, and adaptive behavioral responses at individual and organizational levels. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the scale of simulations required, including parallel execution of 10,000+ stochastic realizations per policy scenario, sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations, and real-time calibration against historical policy outcome datasets. The project will employ Message Passing Interface (MPI)-optimized code to distribute computational workloads across nodes, coupled with GPU-accelerated deep learning modules for pattern detection in simulation outputs. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative assessments of policy trade-offs under different implementation constraints, (2) identification of leverage points for maximizing intervention effectiveness while minimizing systemic risks, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic policy impact forecasting. By enabling computationally intensive exploration of counterfactual scenarios, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive policy evaluation that accounts for complex social interdependencies often overlooked in conventional analytical approaches. The requested resources will directly support time-sensitive simulations tied to ongoing state-level policy reviews in education infrastructure investment and emergency preparedness planning.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public policy analysis, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze consumer behavior patterns and product safety risks in digital marketplaces, with a focus on identifying systemic vulnerabilities in underregulated e-commerce ecosystems. The proliferation of decentralized platforms and AI-driven product recommendations has created complex, dynamic environments where traditional consumer protection mechanisms struggle to scale. We propose combining natural language processing of user reviews, complaint databases, and regulatory reports with agent-based modeling of consumer-supplier interactions to map emergent risks. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning multilingual consumer narratives, product certification records, and supply chain networks while maintaining temporal resolution adequate for tracking fast-evolving marketplace dynamics. Our computational approach integrates transformer-based models fine-tuned on consumer protection lexicons with graph neural networks to detect hidden correlations between product categories, seller behaviors, and reported harms. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will stress-test intervention strategies under different regulatory scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a risk prediction dashboard for advocacy organizations to prioritize investigation targets, 2) evidence-based policy recommendations for algorithmic accountability in recommendation systems, and 3) novel metrics for quantifying ecological impacts of consumption patterns at product lifecycle resolution. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational social science with consumer law informatics, creating new tools to address asymmetries in digital markets while advancing foundational research in ethical consumption analytics. The scale of required data integration and real-time simulation of 100M+ agent interactions necessitates cluster computing capabilities with GPU acceleration for deep learning workflows and distributed memory architectures for large-scale network analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on providing end-use advice and representational services to individuals and groups within a variety of settings, and the analytical and research techniques needed to protect consumers from unsafe, unreliable, and/or unhealthy products and services. Includes instruction in consumer advocacy, family management systems, ecological impacts of consumption practices, and analyzing and testing product quality and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of self-representation and community discourse within Asian-American populations through computational analysis of historical newspapers and community publications. Existing scholarship has often relied on qualitative methods, limiting the scale at which patterns of cultural identity formation and community concerns can be analyzed across diverse subgroups and temporal periods. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze a large corpus of digitized Asian-American newspapers, organizational bulletins, and oral history transcripts spanning the 20th century. Computational methods will include optical character recognition (OCR) correction for archival materials, natural language processing (NLP) techniques for topic modeling and sentiment analysis, and temporal network analysis to map shifts in thematic emphasis and intercommunity dialogue. The scale of data—over 500,000 pages of multilingual texts—requires distributed computing capabilities for efficient text preprocessing, feature extraction, and machine learning model training. Expected outcomes include identifying key phases of collective identity negotiation, documenting responses to systemic challenges such as exclusionary policies, and revealing understudied intersections between regional subgroups. This research will provide the first large-scale computational framework for analyzing Asian-American archival texts, offering quantitative insights to complement traditional humanities scholarship. Results will be disseminated through interactive visualizations, open-access datasets, and partnerships with cultural heritage institutions, enhancing public understanding of Asian-American contributions to U.S. societal development. The project demonstrates how HPC-enabled digital humanities methodologies can transform the study of ethnic narratives while preserving linguistic and cultural specificity.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of Asian population groups who have immigrated to the United States and Canada, or sought refugee asylum, from the colonial period to the present, and including Chinese-Americans, Japanese-Americans, Korean-Americans, Vietnamese-Americans, Cambodian-Americans, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized biomechanical models for optimizing non-invasive neuromodulation therapies in patients with vocal fold paralysis (VFP). VFP, a debilitating condition affecting speech and swallowing, is traditionally managed through surgical interventions or voice therapy, yet outcomes remain inconsistent due to interpatient variability in laryngeal anatomy and neural recovery patterns. Current approaches lack the capacity to dynamically simulate patient-specific neuromuscular responses to emerging non-invasive techniques, such as transcutaneous electrical stimulation (TES). To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating high-resolution laryngeal imaging data, finite element modeling of electrical field distributions, and biophysically grounded neural activation algorithms. The research will utilize HPC clusters to process multimodal datasets (CT/MRI, electromyography) from a retrospective cohort of 50 VFP patients, constructing 3D finite element models of individualized laryngeal geometries. Machine learning pipelines will then iteratively optimize stimulation parameters (electrode placement, current amplitude, frequency) to predict neuromuscular recruitment patterns while minimizing off-target effects. Validation will involve cross-referencing computational predictions with clinical outcomes from a prospective pilot study (n=15). By enabling real-time, patient-specific simulations of TES interventions, this work aims to establish a paradigm for precision neuromodulation in otolaryngology, reducing reliance on trial-and-error therapeutic strategies. The anticipated outcomes include open-source computational tools for laryngeal biomechanics modeling and a foundation for integrating HPC-driven predictive analytics into clinical decision-making workflows. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between computational biomechanics, neural engineering, and rehabilitative medicine, offering a template for advancing personalized therapies in understudied neuromuscular disorders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical professional preparation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Contemporary intermedia practices increasingly demand the integration of real-time computational processes to synthesize interactive visual environments, dynamic generative systems, and multisensory data streams. However, the creation of large-scale, responsive multimedia installations faces significant technical barriers due to the latency, complexity, and volume of data involved in rendering high-resolution visuals, processing sensor inputs, and synchronizing heterogeneous media components. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test novel computational frameworks for immersive, real-time intermedia artworks. The research focuses on optimizing parallelized rendering pipelines for generative 3D environments, training machine learning models for adaptive audiovisual systems, and simulating particle-based visual phenomena at scale. Computational methods include GPU-accelerated physics simulations using Unity’s HDRP and custom shader networks, distributed training of diffusion models for texture synthesis, and latency-critical orchestration of IoT sensor data through Kubernetes-managed microservices. A core outcome will be an open-source toolkit for artists to deploy computationally intensive workflows across HPC clusters, enabling the creation of installations that dynamically respond to environmental or participant input with sub-50ms latency. Expected significance includes advancing methodologies for scalable real-time media synthesis, establishing performance benchmarks for edge computing in interactive art contexts, and demonstrating how HPC can expand the expressive potential of data-driven multimedia practices. The project will culminate in two public installations—exploring biofeedback-driven generative ecosystems and multi-user augmented reality narratives—that serve as case studies for computational resource allocation models in arts research. By bridging gaps between artistic intent and technical feasibility, this work aims to redefine the role of advanced computing infrastructure in fostering interdisciplinary innovation at the intersection of visual art, design, and emergent media technologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions in either two or three dimensions, through simultaneous use of a variety of materials and media.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of liturgical practices across Christian traditions through computational analysis of historical manuscripts, ritual texts, and multimedia records (e.g., chants, iconography). While liturgical studies is a core component of divinity training, existing scholarship remains largely qualitative and fragmented by denominational boundaries. The research problem centers on identifying macro-scale patterns in liturgical adaptation, synthesis, and cultural exchange that are undetectable through manual close reading alone. By applying natural language processing (NLP) to digitized manuscripts (4th–16th centuries) and network analysis to ritual elements (prayers, sacramental sequences, hymnody), we aim to model how theological, political, and social factors influenced liturgical development. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multilingual texts (Latin, Greek, Syriac, Old Church Slavonic) with transformer-based models, analyze temporal-spatial diffusion patterns across 50+ traditions, and simulate hypothetical pathways of influence using agent-based modeling. The project integrates divinity studies with computational humanities by developing novel metrics for "liturgical kinship" and training domain-specific embeddings to capture theological semantics. Expected outcomes include: (1) a public database linking liturgical elements to historical contexts, (2) visualization tools for comparative ritual analysis, and (3) evidence-based frameworks to inform ecumenical dialogue on shared liturgical heritage. This work pioneers computational methods in a field traditionally reliant on hermeneutic approaches, offering new capacity to trace the dynamic interplay between prescribed ritual forms and grassroots religious practice. By leveraging HPC to analyze previously intractable datasets, the project advances interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of computational linguistics, cultural analytics, and theological studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as ministers or priests in any of the Christian religious traditions. Includes instruction in the theology and polity of a particular church, church law, liturgy and ritual, principles of pastoral ministry, homiletics, evangelism, church/parish organization and management, Christian ethics, church history, and related studies.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of directed energy systems (DES) for military applications by addressing critical computational bottlenecks in modeling high-energy laser (HEL) propagation and adaptive control under dynamic battlefield conditions. Current simulations struggle to integrate real-time atmospheric turbulence, aerosol scattering, and thermal blooming effects with the precision required for tactical scenarios, limiting predictive accuracy for beam targeting and energy delivery. To overcome these challenges, the research will deploy high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics framework coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD), nonlinear optics, and machine learning (ML)-driven adaptive optics algorithms. The framework will simulate HEL interactions with heterogeneous environments at scales spanning microns to kilometers, incorporating stochastic weather models and adversarial countermeasure scenarios. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated wavefront propagation solvers optimized for turbulent media and a reinforcement learning module to predict optimal beam control strategies under rapidly changing conditions. By leveraging parallelized Monte Carlo methods, the project will quantify uncertainty in beam degradation across operational theaters, enabling robust system design. Expected outcomes include validated models for HEL performance prediction in contested environments, open-source tools for adaptive optics optimization, and scalability benchmarks to inform future DES hardware-software co-design. This work directly addresses the U.S. Department of Defense’s priority to enhance directed energy weapon reliability and lethality while minimizing collateral effects. The computational infrastructure requested will enable unprecedented resolution in simulating multi-domain photon-matter interactions, bridging a critical gap between theoretical laser physics and deployable military systems. Results will be disseminated through secure government partnerships and declassified technical reports to accelerate field-ready DES innovations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in classical philology and digital humanities, focusing on the analysis of textual transmission and linguistic evolution in understudied ancient Greek and Latin corpora. A central challenge in classics is reconstructing fragmented or corrupted texts and tracing their dissemination across centuries, which requires comparing vast manuscript networks and identifying subtle linguistic patterns. Traditional manual methods are insufficient for processing large-scale datasets or modeling complex relationships between textual variants. The proposed research will develop computational pipelines integrating natural language processing (NLP) techniques, phylogenetic algorithms, and machine learning models to analyze syntactic structures, stylistic features, and scribal errors across multilingual manuscripts. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on non-standardized orthographies, running parallelized comparisons of textual variants, and simulating probabilistic reconstructions of lost archetypes. The project will apply these methods to two case studies: (1) quantifying dialectal shifts in post-classical Greek technical writings, and (2) mapping the circulation of marginal annotations in Carolingian-era Latin codices. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for automated paleographic analysis, a database of annotated textual variants, and statistically grounded hypotheses about transmission pathways. By bridging computational linguistics and classical scholarship, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for analyzing historical languages while addressing longstanding debates about textual authenticity and scribal practices. The requested computing resources will enable processing terabytes of digitized manuscripts and running computationally intensive alignment algorithms, tasks impractical on standard infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary publications and integrated into digital humanities curricula, fostering new collaborations between classics and data science.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in funeral service and mortuary science, focusing on the development of predictive models for environmentally sustainable mortuary practices. Current approaches to body preservation, cemetery land use, and decomposition dynamics rely on empirical, localized data, limiting their scalability and adaptability to diverse ecological and regulatory contexts. The research problem centers on the lack of integrated computational frameworks that account for variables such as soil composition, climate variability, and chemical interactions in embalming fluids, which collectively impact ecological systems and public health. By employing agent-based modeling and fluid dynamics simulations, this project will analyze the spatial and temporal distribution of embalming byproducts in soil and groundwater systems, as well as simulate decomposition rates under varying environmental conditions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical and experimental datasets to identify patterns in biodegradation and optimize land use planning for cemeteries in urbanizing regions. The computational workflow will require parallel processing to manage large-scale geospatial datasets and stochastic simulations of chemical dispersion. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide policy on eco-friendly embalming alternatives, reduce groundwater contamination risks, and improve cemetery sustainability metrics. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets and modular codebases to support interdisciplinary collaboration between mortuary scientists, environmental planners, and computational researchers. By integrating domain-specific knowledge with advanced computational methods, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven decision-making in funeral service practices, addressing a critical gap in non-traditional STEM fields while promoting ecological stewardship in end-of-life care.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in funeral service and mortuary science not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and optimization of personalized therapeutic recreation (TR) interventions for individuals with complex physical, cognitive, or psychosocial disabilities. Current TR practice relies on manual assessment and generalized activity plans, which may not fully account for dynamic patient needs, environmental variables, or the heterogeneous effects of recreational modalities. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating patient biometric data, activity performance metrics, and psychosocial feedback to model individualized outcomes. The research problem centers on identifying scalable methods to predict optimal therapeutic activities in real time while accounting for multidimensional constraints, including motor function limitations, sensory processing differences, and social interaction dynamics. Using anonymized datasets from wearable sensors, electronic health records, and patient-reported outcomes, we will train machine learning models to correlate activity parameters (e.g., duration, intensity, social context) with physiological and psychological markers of therapeutic benefit. Agent-based simulations will model group therapy dynamics to evaluate how interpersonal interactions influence outcomes in populations with neurodevelopmental or psychiatric conditions. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze qualitative patient journals to identify subjective factors affecting engagement. The computational workload requires HPC resources due to the scale of multimodal data (10,000+ patient-hours), the complexity of reinforcement learning architectures, and the need for parallelized simulations across diverse virtual cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive models for activity efficacy, open-source tools for adaptive TR program design, and evidence-based guidelines for personalizing leisure education strategies. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making, reduce trial-and-error in intervention planning, and establish a computational foundation for data-driven TR research. By optimizing resource allocation in therapy settings, the project aims to improve health equity for populations with limited access to specialized care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, organize, and direct recreational activities designed to promote health and well-being for patients who are physically, mentally, or emotionally disabled. Includes instruction in the foundations of therapeutic recreation, leisure education and counseling, program planning, therapeutic recreational modalities, basic anatomy and physiology, psychology, medical terminology, human growth and development, patient observation and evaluation, special needs populations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of African-American/Black literary traditions across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. A central challenge in studying these diasporic literatures lies in mapping large-scale patterns of thematic evolution, intertextuality, and stylistic innovation across diverse genres, historical periods, and regional contexts. Traditional close-reading methods, while foundational, struggle to systematically trace connections within expansive corpora that include novels, poetry, essays, oral narratives, and digitized archival materials. This project addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis, machine learning, and network modeling to analyze relationships between canonical works, marginalized texts, and folkloric traditions. Key objectives include identifying latent thematic clusters across 19th- and 20th-century texts, modeling the diffusion of vernacular linguistic features, and visualizing transnational influences in postcolonial Caribbean literature. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing heterogeneous text corpora (including OCR-corrected historical documents), training transformer-based models for semantic similarity detection, and applying community detection algorithms to authorship networks. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of text data, fine-tuning large language models on domain-specific literature, and running iterative simulations to validate network hypotheses. Anticipated outcomes include a public-facing digital archive of annotated texts, interactive visualizations of literary influence networks, and open-source tools tailored for Black literary studies. By bridging computational methods with critical race theory and diaspora studies frameworks, this research aims to surface overlooked textual connections, challenge Eurocentric periodization models, and provide quantitative foundations for new pedagogical approaches. The project will deepen scholarly understanding of how African-American/Black literary aesthetics have dynamically responded to intersecting histories of migration, resistance, and cultural hybridity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the design, installation, and fault diagnosis of solar energy systems through advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. A critical challenge in solar technology is the variability of system performance due to site-specific environmental factors (e.g., irradiance patterns, shading, thermal stress) and component degradation, which complicates both installation planning and long-term maintenance. Current industry tools rely on simplified models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between system components and environmental variables, leading to suboptimal energy yields and delayed fault detection. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining physics-based simulations of photovoltaic (PV) arrays, power electronics, and thermal dynamics with machine learning models trained on synthetic and field-collected performance data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to simulate diverse installation scenarios (e.g., rooftop vs. utility-scale systems, varying panel orientations) under realistic weather conditions derived from historical and projected climate datasets. Concurrently, neural networks will be trained to predict component failures and efficiency losses using time-series data from simulated and real-world systems. The integration of these methods aims to produce adaptive decision-support tools for technicians, including a recommendation system for site-specific hardware configurations and an anomaly detection pipeline for proactive maintenance. Expected outcomes include validated models that reduce installation design time by 30-50% while improving annual energy output by 10-15% in simulated deployments, as well as a fault classification system with >90% accuracy in identifying common failure modes (e.g., microcracks, inverter malfunctions). By leveraging HPC to bridge high-resolution simulation and real-world operational data, this work will advance both the technical training curriculum for solar technicians and the scalability of solar energy systems in heterogeneous environments.
cip_title: Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair solar energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational comparative law study analyzing the evolution and interaction of legal principles across civil law, common law, and religious law systems. Traditional comparative legal scholarship relies on manual text analysis and case law comparisons, which struggle to systematically evaluate patterns across vast, multilingual corpora of statutes, judicial opinions, and scholarly commentaries spanning multiple jurisdictions. The proposed project addresses this gap by developing a scalable framework to model legal system dynamics using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. Key objectives include training transformer-based models on curated datasets of primary legal texts (e.g., codified laws, landmark court decisions) and secondary literature from 15 jurisdictions, then applying graph-based network analysis to trace doctrinal influences and divergences over time. Computational challenges include handling low-resource languages, disentangling context-dependent legal semantics, and resolving jurisdictional citation networks. The HPC environment is critical for parallel processing of terabyte-scale text datasets, fine-tuning multilingual legal embeddings, and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about cross-system legal convergence. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access repository of annotated legal corpora spanning multiple traditions, (2) quantitative metrics for measuring doctrinal alignment between systems, and (3) visualization tools mapping temporal shifts in jurisprudential reasoning. By integrating computational social science methods with legal theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven comparative law research while providing actionable insights for transnational policymaking and judicial training programs. The project’s computational demands—particularly in distributed training of domain-specific language models and large-scale network inference—necessitate allocation of GPU nodes and high-memory infrastructure to achieve proposed benchmarks.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of legal systems and philosophies in comparative perspective.

abstract: Maternal and neonatal health outcomes are influenced by complex, multifactorial interactions between biological, clinical, and environmental variables. Current risk prediction models for adverse events such as preterm birth, neonatal sepsis, or postpartum hemorrhage lack precision due to limitations in integrating high-dimensional data streams, including electronic health records, longitudinal biomarker profiles, and population-level health determinants. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for dynamic risk stratification and personalized intervention planning in perinatal and neonatal care. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze linked datasets encompassing 50,000+ maternal-neonatal dyads, including time-series vital sign data, multi-omics profiles, and geospatial health equity indicators. Machine learning architectures—including transformer-based models for temporal pattern recognition and graph neural networks for modeling care pathway dependencies—will be trained to identify critical transition points in pregnancy and neonatal trajectories. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further model uteroplacental blood flow abnormalities associated with intrauterine growth restriction. The scale of these multimodal datasets and the need for real-time parameter optimization in clinical decision support tools necessitate parallelized computing capabilities exceeding local cluster capacities. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for early detection of perinatal complications, optimized protocols for resource allocation in neonatal intensive care units, and open-source computational tools tailored for maternal-child health research. By enabling large-scale integration of heterogeneous data types while preserving temporal and spatial resolution, this HPC-supported approach aims to advance precision nursing interventions and reduce disparities in adverse maternal-neonatal outcomes.
cip_title: Maternal/ Child Health and Neonatal Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide prenatal care to pregnant women and to mothers and their newborn infants. Includes instruction in perinatal and newborn health assessment, stabilization, and care; pathophysiology of pregnancy, fetuses, and the newborn; clinical management of high-risk pregnancies and newborns; perinatal and neonatal technology and clinical procedures; and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address a critical gap in historical research: the systematic analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous historical datasets to uncover long-term patterns of social, economic, and cultural change in understudied regions. Focusing on 18th- and 19th-century maritime trade networks in Southeast Asia, the research integrates fragmented archival records—including ship logs, port ledgers, and colonial correspondence—into a unified geospatial and relational database. The computational challenges involve processing unstructured multilingual text (Dutch, Spanish, Malay, Chinese), reconciling inconsistent temporal and spatial references, and modeling dynamic networks across a 150-year period. To achieve this, the project employs natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical orthography, probabilistic record linkage algorithms to resolve entity ambiguities, and agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about trade route resilience during geopolitical shifts. HPC resources are essential for scaling these methods across ~500,000 digitized pages and ~1.2 million tabular entries, enabling parallelized text extraction, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in network reconstructions, and high-resolution spatiotemporal visualization. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative reconstruction of intra-Asian maritime commodity flows preceding European colonial dominance, challenging Eurocentric narratives of globalization. The computational workflows will be published as open-source tools to support similar data-driven historical inquiries, while the curated datasets will be made accessible through an interactive platform for public scholarship. By demonstrating how HPC can transform archival-scale evidence into actionable historical models, this project aims to establish a methodological benchmark for computational history, bridging qualitative scholarship and data science in the humanities.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in history, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for solving inverse problems in wave propagation through heterogeneous media, with applications to non-destructive material characterization and subsurface imaging. A key challenge lies in reconstructing spatially varying material properties—such as elasticity or density—from sparse, noisy boundary measurements, which involves solving high-dimensional, non-convex optimization problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Traditional approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs and ill-posedness when applied to large-scale, three-dimensional geometries. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating asymptotic waveform reconstruction with adjoint-based optimization. The forward wave model will leverage a parallelized discontinuous Galerkin solver, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures, to simulate acoustic-elastic interactions in complex media. For the inverse problem, we will derive reduced-order models using asymptotic expansions in high-frequency regimes, enabling efficient gradient computations via adjoint-state methods. The optimization loop will employ matrix-free iterative solvers and stochastic approximation techniques to mitigate sensitivity to local minima. The computational demands of resolving fine-scale wave dynamics across multiple frequencies, combined with the need for ensemble-based uncertainty quantification, necessitate access to HPC resources. Specifically, we request allocations for large-memory nodes to handle dense meshes in forward simulations and multi-node GPU clusters to accelerate matrix-vector operations in the optimization kernel. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for large-scale inverse wave problems and validated demonstrations on experimental datasets from seismic imaging and composite material testing. This work aims to advance computational methodologies in PDE-constrained optimization while providing tools for applications in geophysical prospecting and industrial non-destructive evaluation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as engineering and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in natural phenomena modeling continuum mechanics, reaction-diffusion, wave propagation, dynamic systems, numerical analysis, controlled theory, asymptotic methods, variation, optimization theory, inverse problems, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of regulatory frameworks governing sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient food systems, an emerging niche in Agriculture Law requiring advanced computational analysis. As global agricultural policies intersect with environmental, trade, and social equity mandates, stakeholders face challenges in systematically evaluating compliance risks, policy coherence, and systemic impacts across jurisdictions. This research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets spanning legal texts (treaties, statutes, case law), agricultural geospatial data, and climate projection models. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to extract obligations and permissions from 150,000+ agricultural law documents across 50 jurisdictions, while graph neural networks will map normative conflicts and synergies in multi-layered regulatory regimes. Agent-based modeling will simulate how proposed carbon credit policies might influence land-use decisions under varying climate scenarios, integrating legal constraints with agronomic and economic variables. The computational workflow requires parallelized text processing, large-scale graph traversals, and Monte Carlo simulations across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access legal analytics platform identifying compliance pathways for climate-smart agriculture and a policy impact framework quantifying trade-offs between regulatory stringency, farm viability, and emissions targets. By bridging legal semantics with systems modeling, this project advances methodological innovation in computational legal studies while providing actionable tools for policymakers, agricultural cooperatives, and environmental organizations navigating rapidly evolving governance landscapes. The research directly responds to urgent calls for data-driven approaches to food system resilience in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report and the UN Food Systems Summit 2021 action tracks.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in food and agriculture.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing parametric insurance structures in the context of climate-driven supply chain disruptions, an emerging interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of actuarial science, climate modeling, and operations research. Traditional insurance models struggle to address the non-linear, systemic risks posed by compounding climate events (e.g., concurrent floods and wildfires) that disrupt multi-tier supplier networks. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a novel hybrid simulation approach combining agent-based modeling of supply chain dynamics with probabilistic climate event cascades derived from CMIP6 ensemble data. Key computational challenges include real-time recalibration of trigger thresholds across 10,000+ simulated scenarios, Monte Carlo-based estimation of correlated losses in multi-region supplier networks, and gradient-free optimization of policy terms under non-convex constraints. The framework will integrate machine learning surrogates to accelerate convergence in high-dimensional parameter spaces while maintaining actuarial interpretability. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable method for pricing climate-contingent coverage layers that account for spatial and temporal risk dependencies, (2) sensitivity analyses quantifying the financial impact of alternative climate forcing scenarios on policy performance, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic exposure management in parametric insurance contracts. By enabling millimeter-scale resolution of regional climate impacts on specific supplier nodes while maintaining enterprise-wide risk aggregation capabilities, this HPC-supported approach aims to bridge critical gaps in climate adaptation financing for small-to-medium enterprises within global value chains. The computational workflows developed will provide a template for integrating Earth system models with actuarial applications at previously infeasible spatiotemporal scales.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage risk in organizational settings and provide insurance and risk-aversion services to businesses, individuals, and other organizations. Includes instruction in casualty insurance and general liability, property insurance, employee benefits, social and health insurance, loss adjustment, underwriting, risk theory, and pension planning.

abstract: Ensuring microbial safety while preserving nutritional and sensory quality in processed foods remains a critical challenge in food technology. Traditional thermal processing methods often rely on empirical models that inadequately balance energy efficiency, nutrient retention, and pathogen inactivation, particularly in heterogeneous food matrices. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to optimize thermal processing and packaging design for plant-based food products. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with kinetic models of microbial inactivation, nutrient degradation, and heat transfer to predict system behavior under varying processing conditions. A parallelized finite element approach will model heat distribution in complex food geometries, while machine learning algorithms will analyze large datasets to identify energy-efficient processing parameters that maximize safety and quality. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will assess gas diffusion properties of novel biodegradable packaging materials to extend shelf life. The computational intensity of these multi-physics models—requiring millions of processor hours for parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and 3D visualization—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for optimizing industrial-scale retort systems, data-driven packaging material design guidelines, and reduced energy consumption in food processing. This work will advance precision engineering in food manufacturing, directly supporting the development of sustainable, nutrient-dense food products while addressing global food safety challenges. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and collaborations with food processors to bridge academic research and industry innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient, reliable, and environmentally sustainable electricity generation necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize power plant operations. Current challenges include mitigating inefficiencies in turbine performance, managing dynamic load fluctuations, reducing emissions under variable operating conditions, and integrating renewable energy sources into conventional power generation systems. Traditional experimental and analytical approaches are limited in addressing these multi-scale, multi-physics problems, particularly when balancing real-time operational constraints with long-term reliability. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate power plant subsystems—including combustion dynamics, steam turbine thermodynamics, heat exchanger networks, and emissions control systems—using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) will be employed to study fluid-structure interactions in turbine blades, transient heat transfer in boilers, and pollutant dispersion in flue gas systems. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to calibrate models against real-time sensor data and predict equipment degradation. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parametric studies of combined-cycle plant configurations, sensitivity analyses of water chemistry impacts on corrosion rates, and probabilistic risk assessments for grid stability during renewable energy intermittency. Expected outcomes include validated operational protocols to reduce fuel consumption by 8–12%, predictive maintenance frameworks to extend turbine lifespan, and optimized control strategies for hybrid power systems incorporating solar thermal or hydrogen co-firing. These advancements will directly support workforce training in power plant instrumentation and industrial controls while providing actionable insights for utilities transitioning to low-carbon generation. The requested computing resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations of full-scale plant systems, which exceed the capacity of local clusters, ensuring alignment with national priorities for energy resilience and emissions reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) remain a critical challenge in modern operating rooms (ORs), with contamination risks persisting despite adherence to standardized aseptic protocols. This project proposes a computational study to model and optimize dynamic OR workflows, focusing on the interplay between surgical technologist movements, equipment handling, and airborne particle dispersion. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based simulations that integrate real-time sensor data from robotic surgical systems, environmental monitoring devices, and personnel tracking tools. The computational framework will employ discrete event simulation to map procedural workflows, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airborne pathogen spread under varying OR ventilation configurations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify high-risk temporal and spatial patterns in contamination pathways during complex multi-instrument procedures. Validation will utilize anonymized datasets from 12 academic medical centers, encompassing 23,000+ surgical cases with corresponding infection outcome records. Expected outcomes include predictive models for contamination risk stratification, evidence-based recommendations for instrument tray placement optimization, and dynamic workflow adjustments to minimize breaks in sterility. This research addresses a critical gap in surgical technology by quantifying previously intangible risks in aseptic practice, with potential to reduce SSI rates by an estimated 15-20% in robot-assisted procedures. The computational approach directly supports surgical technologists’ decision-making in real-time equipment management while advancing OR safety analytics through large-scale spatiotemporal pattern recognition. Successful implementation will establish a novel paradigm for data-driven sterility protocol design in next-generation hybrid OR environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and surgical nurses, to maintain, monitor, and enforce the sterile field and adherence to aseptic technique by preoperative, surgical team, and postoperative personnel. Includes instruction in instrument and equipment sterilization and handling, surgical supplies management, wound exposure and closure, surgical computer and robot operation and monitoring, maintenance of hemostasis, and patient and team scrubbing.

abstract: Nurse staffing optimization is a critical challenge in healthcare delivery, directly impacting patient outcomes, operational costs, and workforce sustainability. Current approaches to staffing allocation often rely on static nurse-to-patient ratios or retrospective analyses, which fail to account for dynamic patient acuity, nurse skill mix variability, and real-time operational constraints. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model and simulate staffing decisions in acute care settings, integrating multi-source electronic health record (EHR) data, nurse competency profiles, and institutional policy parameters. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling to simulate patient-nurse interactions across diverse clinical scenarios, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify adaptive staffing policies. The computational workload involves iterative optimization across millions of potential staffing configurations while maintaining compliance with Joint Commission standards and labor agreements. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models quantifying relationships between staffing flexibility and patient safety indicators, (2) decision support tools for real-time staffing adjustments during surge capacity events, and (3) policy simulations evaluating cost-benefit tradeoffs of competency-based staffing models. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale EHR datasets and conduct parallel scenario testing, this work addresses a critical gap in nursing administration research: the lack of computationally intensive, systems-level analyses tailored to nurse management contexts. Results will directly inform healthcare organizations’ strategic planning for nursing resource allocation while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of nursing science and computational decision analytics. This project requires dedicated GPU nodes for deep learning components and large-memory nodes for hospital-scale simulations, resources not available through conventional computing infrastructure in health sciences research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to manage nursing personnel and services in hospitals and other health care delivery agencies. Includes instruction in principles of health care administration, resource and financial management, health care law and policy, medical personnel management, and managed care operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and dynamic mechanisms underpinning viral-host cell interactions in RNA viruses, with a focus on paramyxoviruses. A critical gap in virology lies in understanding how viral surface proteins mediate host cell entry while evading immune detection, particularly in mutable regions that drive antigenic drift. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve the nanosecond-scale conformational changes and glycan-shield dynamics central to these processes. To address this, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the fusion glycoproteins of human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) and their interactions with host receptors and neutralizing antibodies.
