cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching French to students who are not proficient in French or who do not speak, read, or write French, and prepares individuals to serve as teachers and administrators.

abstract: The integration of heterogeneous, high-dimensional health data into actionable insights remains a critical challenge in health information management, particularly as electronic health records (EHRs) expand to include multi-omics, imaging, and real-time sensor data. Current systems struggle to harmonize these disparate data types while preserving patient privacy and enabling scalable analysis. This project proposes the development of a privacy-preserving, machine learning-driven framework to synthesize and analyze multimodal health data, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome computational bottlenecks. The research will focus on creating a federated analytics pipeline that operates across decentralized EHR datasets without raw data exchange, utilizing secure multi-party computation (sMPC) and differential privacy. Key computational tasks include training deep learning models for synthetic data generation that mirror statistical properties of sensitive patient records, optimizing graph-based algorithms to map patient trajectory correlations across modalities, and simulating large-scale data fusion scenarios to stress-test interoperability standards. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization for privacy-utility trade-offs, and validation of synthetic data fidelity through downstream predictive modeling tasks (e.g., early sepsis detection, readmission risk stratification). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for health systems to safely share synthetic derivatives of protected health information (PHI), novel metrics for quantifying re-identification risks in multimodal health data, and benchmark performance data for distributed learning architectures in HIPAA-compliant environments. This work directly addresses the growing need for advanced computing infrastructure in health information administration, where traditional methods fail to keep pace with the volume and complexity of modern medical data. By enabling secure, large-scale collaboration across institutions, the project aims to accelerate translational research while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for data stewardship—a crucial advancement for precision medicine initiatives reliant on diverse, representative health datasets.
cip_title: Health Information/ Medical Records Administration/ Administrator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage systems, processes, and facilities used to collect, store, secure, retrieve, analyze, and transmit medical records and other health information used by clinical professionals and health care organizations. Includes instruction in the principles and basic content of the biomedical and clinical sciences, information technology and applications, data and database management, clinical research methodologies, health information resources and systems, office management, legal requirements, and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized learning pathways in asynchronous online education environments, addressing the challenge of scaling adaptive instruction for diverse learners. While online teaching platforms generate vast datasets—including learner engagement metrics, assessment performance, and interaction patterns—existing analytical tools often fail to leverage this information dynamically to support instructor decision-making. The research problem centers on bridging this gap through predictive modeling of learner outcomes and real-time recommendation systems for instructional adjustments. The computational approach integrates machine learning techniques with principles from learning science, employing neural networks to analyze multimodal data (e.g., discussion forum text, video engagement logs, and formative assessment results) from learning management systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process these large-scale, heterogeneous datasets and train ensemble models that account for temporal patterns in learner behavior. Proposed methods include natural language processing (NLP) for qualitative feedback analysis, computer vision techniques to interpret video-based interaction cues, and agent-based simulations to test hypothetical pedagogical interventions in synthetic classroom environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for online educators to predict at-risk learners, recommend content modifications, and automate routine feedback tasks. By enabling data-driven personalization without compromising scalability, this work aims to reduce instructor cognitive load while improving equity in learning outcomes. The project’s use of HPC resources directly supports the development of ethically aligned AI systems that respect privacy constraints and pedagogical best practices, advancing the integration of computational tools into teacher education for online contexts.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various academic levels through online instructional technologies. Includes instruction in andragogy, pedagogy, assessment, instructional design and technology, and learning science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive decision-support framework for hazardous materials (hazmat) logistics and incident response using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current hazmat management systems face critical limitations in integrating real-time environmental, sensor, and operational data to predict risks or optimize mitigation strategies under dynamic conditions. We propose a computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM), geospatial analytics, and machine learning to simulate hazmat transport networks, contamination pathways, and emergency response scenarios. The ABM component will model interactions between human operators, infrastructure systems, and environmental variables, while deep learning architectures will process multi-modal data streams (e.g., weather patterns, traffic flows, chemical degradation rates) to predict spill dispersion dynamics. Geospatial-temporal analyses will map risk hotspots using historical incident databases and regulatory compliance records. The computational intensity of concurrently running thousands of scenario variations—each requiring 3D fluid dynamics simulations for airborne/waterborne contaminant spread—necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing. Expected outcomes include: (1) a probabilistic risk assessment tool that updates hazard predictions in near-real time, (2) optimized routing algorithms that balance economic efficiency with community safety thresholds, and (3) synthetic training datasets for AI-driven emergency response planning. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing clusters, this work will advance hazmat information systems beyond current static risk models, enabling proactive adaptation to climate variability, urban development pressures, and emerging chemical threats. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will directly support regional emergency management agencies and hazmat transportation operators in achieving compliance with evolving EPA and OSHA regulations while reducing computational latency in crisis decision-making by 40-60% compared to existing systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing, monitoring, and enforcing hazardous materials management and removal. Includes instruction in environmental science, environmental health, human behavior, economics, management science, information systems and applications, and communication skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in advancing jewelry design innovation and material optimization. Traditional jewelry arts rely on labor-intensive experimentation to balance aesthetic intent with material constraints, such as metal fatigue, gemstone structural integrity, and thermal behavior during casting or enameling. However, the complex interplay of physical forces, microstructural evolution, and geometric variables in these processes limits the scalability of empirical methods. This project proposes a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics simulations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to model material responses, predict fabrication outcomes, and explore design spaces. HPC resources will enable multi-physics simulations of metalforming techniques (e.g., electroforming current distribution, stress gradients in lapidary work) at micron-scale resolutions, coupled with machine learning-driven optimization of stone-cutting angles for light refraction efficiency. A parallel focus involves training GANs on historical and contemporary jewelry corpora to generate culturally informed, structurally feasible design variants while minimizing material waste. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating process parameters (e.g., alloy composition, annealing schedules) with mechanical and aesthetic properties, reducing trial-and-error cycles in studio practice. The integration of computational materials science with generative design aims to establish a new paradigm for sustainable jewelry production, preserving craft traditions while expanding creative possibilities through digital innovation. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for jewelry educators and workshops demonstrating computational workflows, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between artisanal practices and computational research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by fashioning jewelry from gems, other stones, and precious metals. Includes instruction in design concepts, electroforming, enameling, gemology, lapidary technique and art, metal and non-metal casting and molding, metal coloring, metalsmithing and finishing, personal style development, photo etching, and stone cutting and polishing.

abstract: Current methods for fitting contact lenses often rely on empirical adjustments and static anatomical measurements, which may not account for dynamic physiological interactions between the lens, corneal surface, and tear film. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model these interactions at the micron scale, enabling personalized lens parameter optimization. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement multi-physics simulations combining finite element analysis of lens deformation, computational fluid dynamics of tear film stability, and biomechanical corneal response under varying environmental conditions. Patient-specific data from corneal topography, blink patterns, and meibomian gland function will inform boundary conditions. Machine learning algorithms will then identify optimal lens curvature, material elasticity, and edge design parameters that minimize interfacial stress while maintaining optical performance. The proposed simulations require parallel processing capabilities to handle 3D meshes with >10^7 elements and iterative solvers for coupled differential equations across temporal scales. Successful validation against clinical outcomes from 200 retrospective cases will establish model accuracy. This approach aims to reduce fitting time by 40% and improve wearer comfort metrics by 30% compared to standard protocols. By integrating optometric practice with computational engineering, this project advances precision eye care tools while providing a scalable platform for investigating ocular surface disorders. The resource allocation will support critical developments at the intersection of clinical optometry and high-fidelity biomechanical modeling, fostering innovation in a specialized health sciences niche.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist optometrists in providing patient care, administering examinations and treatments, and performing office administrative functions. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology of the eye, visual testing, patient communication, patient preparation, medications and administration, dispensing and fitting of eyeglasses and contact lenses, record-keeping, and office management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of creating immersive, interactive graphic design environments that integrate real-time user input, dynamic visual elements, and machine learning-driven generative processes. While contemporary graphic design increasingly relies on high-fidelity simulations, 3D modeling, and AI-augmented creativity, existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to handle the latency, rendering complexity, and data throughput required for experimental, large-scale digital installations. The research will develop a framework for optimizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) and physics-based rendering pipelines using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Key computational challenges include parallelizing neural style transfer algorithms across GPU nodes to enable multi-resolution texture synthesis, simulating light-material interactions in complex 3D scenes, and maintaining sub-50ms response times for user-driven parametric design systems. The project will utilize distributed computing architectures to train AI models on heterogeneous datasets of design patterns, material properties, and gestural input data, while implementing containerized workflows to manage version-controlled design iterations. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for real-time collaborative design prototyping, quantitative benchmarks for computational-aesthetic quality evaluation, and novel methods for balancing artistic intent with algorithmic stochasticity in HPC environments. By establishing performance-optimized pipelines for computationally intensive design tasks, this work aims to expand the creative possibilities of data-driven visual storytelling while providing empirical insights into resource allocation strategies for hybrid human-AI design systems. The results will directly inform curriculum development in computational design literacy and offer open-source reference implementations for the visual arts community.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic and computer techniques to the interpretation of technical and commercial concepts. Includes instruction in computer-assisted art and design, printmaking, concepts sketching, technical drawing, color theory, imaging, studio technique, still and life modeling, multimedia applications, communication skills and commercial art business operations.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of hearing loss and the limitations of current assistive technologies in complex auditory environments necessitate advanced computational approaches to improve auditory rehabilitation. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, biophysically grounded model of the human auditory pathway to optimize next-generation hearing aid algorithms. Traditional hearing devices struggle to dynamically separate speech from background noise in real-world settings, largely due to insufficient integration of individual neurophysiological variability in auditory processing. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will simulate multiscale neural networks that replicate cochlear mechanics, brainstem signal integration, and cortical processing of acoustic features. The model will incorporate patient-specific data from electrocochleography, fMRI, and psychophysical tests to account for neuroanatomical and functional diversity. Computational workflows will involve finite element modeling of cochlear dynamics, coupled with spiking neural networks trained on large-scale neurophysiological datasets. HPC resources will enable parameter optimization across thousands of parallel simulations, reducing the time required to identify personalized amplification and noise-reduction strategies from months to days. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for predicting patient-specific hearing aid performance and a novel algorithm library that adapts to dynamic acoustic environments in real time. This interdisciplinary approach bridges systems neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and machine learning, offering a paradigm shift in auditory rehabilitation. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source software to accelerate translational research, with potential applications in cochlear implant optimization and diagnostic biomarker discovery for auditory processing disorders. By addressing the computational bottleneck in personalized audiology, this project aims to improve quality of life for millions with hearing impairment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose and treat hearing loss and other disorders involving the ear, advise patients on means to use their remaining hearing, and select and fit hearing aids and other devices. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of hearing, hearing measurement, auditory pathology, middle and inner ear analysis, rehabilitation therapies and assistive technologies, and pediatric and other special applications.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding how climate-driven shifts in hydrological regimes impact the resilience of riparian ecosystems, with implications for biodiversity conservation and water resource management. Current models often oversimplify interactions between hydrological dynamics, vegetation response, and anthropogenic stressors, limiting their utility for predicting ecosystem thresholds under future climate scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated computational framework combining high-resolution hydrologic modeling, species distribution forecasting, and agent-based simulations of human-environment interactions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute spatially explicit simulations at a basin scale (10,000+ km²) using a modified Soil & Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) calibrated with LiDAR-derived topography and 20-year satellite hydrology datasets. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze vegetation community responses to fluctuating water availability, informed by field-collected phenology and soil moisture data. A novel agent-based module will simulate stakeholder decision-making processes related to water extraction and land use, incorporating socioeconomic datasets. By iteratively coupling these components, the model will identify feedback loops and tipping points undetectable through conventional approaches. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of ecosystem vulnerability under IPCC climate projections, validated through collaboration with regional conservation agencies. The computational framework will be designed for scalability, enabling adaptation to other semi-arid regions facing water scarcity. This work directly supports evidence-based policymaking for sustainable water allocation and riparian habitat preservation, while advancing methodologies for complex socio-environmental system modeling. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the project’s terabyte-scale geospatial datasets, parallelize computationally intensive climate scenario ensembles, and reduce runtime for iterative model calibration from months to days.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on environment-related issues using scientific, social scientific, or humanistic approaches or a combination. Includes instruction in the basic principles of ecology and environmental science and related subjects such as policy, politics, law, economics, social aspects, planning, pollution control, natural resources, and the interactions of human beings and nature.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Vietnamese linguistic and literary heritage. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools for analyzing Vietnamese dialects, historical texts, and sociolinguistic patterns, which are essential for preserving linguistic diversity and understanding cultural evolution. Existing methodologies in Vietnamese studies remain constrained by manual analysis, limiting the scope of textual corpora and dialect datasets that can be processed. This project proposes a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and large-scale text mining to analyze digitized Vietnamese texts, including classical literature, regional dialects, and modern vernacular sources. Key objectives include the development of dialect classification models, automated annotation of syntactic and semantic features in pre-modern texts, and the identification of sociolinguistic shifts across historical periods. The computational approach will involve training transformer-based models on curated corpora spanning 15th–21st century Vietnamese texts, utilizing parallel processing to handle non-Latin script encoding challenges and phonological variations. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including audio recordings of endangered dialects and optically scanned manuscripts, which require intensive preprocessing for noise reduction and character recognition. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for dialect mapping, a searchable multilingual lexicon linking classical and contemporary Vietnamese, and quantitative insights into literary genre evolution. These resources will support interdisciplinary research in Southeast Asian cultural studies, language preservation initiatives, and pedagogical applications for advanced Vietnamese language education. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish a foundation for large-scale, collaborative research on Vietnamese language and literature, addressing both academic and community-driven needs for accessible, data-rich linguistic resources.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Vietnamese language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in complex, multi-stakeholder projects, addressing a critical gap in project management methodologies. Traditional resource allocation models often fail to account for real-time uncertainties, interdependent task networks, and competing stakeholder priorities, leading to cost overruns and delays. We propose an integrative approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to analyze how resource allocation strategies impact project outcomes under varying constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale simulations of project scenarios, including parametric variations in team composition, budget reallocations, and risk event cascades. Using historical project data from construction and IT sectors, neural networks will be trained to predict resource bottlenecks, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize allocation policies. The computational workflow will incorporate domain-specific parameters such as earned value management metrics, stakeholder influence networks, and risk exposure thresholds. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between resource allocation strategies and project success criteria (e.g., time, cost, quality). This work will advance project management practice by enabling data-driven, adaptive resource planning in environments with high uncertainty. The resulting models and open-source simulation toolkit will provide empirical insights into how granular resource decisions propagate through project lifecycles, benefiting both industry practitioners and academic research in adaptive project governance. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this study aims to overcome computational limitations that have previously restricted the scale and granularity of resource allocation analyses in business contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply quantitative and qualitative knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage projects in a wide range of fields and occupations. Includes instruction in project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the genetic basis of complex trait variation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic datasets. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci linked to polygenic traits, the role of non-coding regulatory elements and epistatic interactions in modulating phenotypic outcomes remains poorly characterized, particularly in understudied populations. The research will integrate whole-genome sequencing data from diverse cohorts with functional genomic annotations to identify regulatory variants influencing traits such as developmental timing and metabolic efficiency. Computational workflows will employ probabilistic graphical models to infer causal variants and machine learning frameworks to predict epistatic networks, requiring iterative parameter optimization across terabytes of data. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing population genetic simulations that model allele frequency dynamics under varying selective pressures, as well as for conducting permutation testing to establish statistical thresholds for interaction effects. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel regulatory loci contributing to trait heritability, refined models of gene-gene interaction architectures, and publicly accessible databases annotating population-specific regulatory variants. These results will advance foundational knowledge in complex trait genetics while providing methodological frameworks for analyzing high-dimensional genomic data. The computational pipelines developed will be disseminated to facilitate similar studies in non-model organisms, enhancing collaborative efforts to decipher genotype-to-phenotype relationships across species. By prioritizing scalability and reproducibility, this work aims to bridge technical limitations in current genetic analyses and foster equitable resource utilization across research communities.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in genetics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Healthcare-associated adverse events remain a significant challenge, contributing to patient harm, increased costs, and systemic inefficiencies. While existing quality improvement frameworks emphasize retrospective analysis, there is an urgent need for predictive, scalable computational tools to proactively identify risks and optimize care delivery protocols. This project seeks to develop a machine learning platform that integrates heterogeneous clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), incident reports, and sensor-derived human factors data—to model latent risks in care processes and predict adverse events in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train multimodal deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for clinical text, graph neural networks for care pathway analysis) on multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10 years of inpatient records from six academic medical centers. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further model patient flow bottlenecks contributing to medication errors and nosocomial infections. Key challenges include managing temporal dependencies in longitudinal EHR data, resolving semantic inconsistencies in unstructured clinical narratives, and scaling agent-based simulations to hospital-scale operational models. The HPC environment will enable parallel hyperparameter optimization across 50+ model configurations, GPU-accelerated inference for real-time risk scoring, and large-scale sensitivity analyses to evaluate intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for sepsis, falls, and postoperative complications with ≥85% precision-recall AUC, (2) actionable insights into modifiable workflow factors contributing to diagnostic delays, and (3) open-source tools for simulating safety interventions prior to clinical implementation. By bridging systems engineering principles with computational epidemiology, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven proactive risk mitigation, directly advancing the program’s mission to reduce preventable harm through transformative analytical approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of transformative mechanisms and evidence-based protocols to reduce preventable patient harm and improve clinical outcomes. Includes instruction in healthcare quality, patient safety, research methods, program evaluation, epidemiology, legal and regulatory compliance, systems thinking, human factors engineering, and risk management.

abstract: The integration of personalized immunotherapy into clinical oncology remains hindered by the dynamic complexity of immune-tumor interactions and interpatient variability. Current computational models lack the resolution to simulate these interactions at scale, limiting their utility in predicting patient-specific therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework to simulate immune cell behavior within the tumor microenvironment, informed by multi-omics data from individual patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale simulations capturing spatial and temporal dynamics of immune cell infiltration, tumor antigen presentation, and cytokine signaling networks. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to analyze simulation outputs, identify predictive biomarkers of response, and optimize combinatorial therapeutic strategies. Key computational challenges include managing the stochasticity of cell-cell interactions, scaling models to accommodate single-cell omics data, and ensuring real-time adaptability for clinical integration. By correlating simulated outcomes with longitudinal clinical data from patients undergoing immunotherapy, the project aims to validate model accuracy and refine predictive capabilities. Successful implementation of this framework could transform therapeutic decision-making by enabling clinicians to test virtual treatment scenarios, prioritize high-efficacy regimens, and minimize off-target effects. The requested HPC resources are critical to handle the computational load of parallelized simulations, which involve millions of interacting agents and parameter combinations. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for immuno-oncology research and clinically actionable insights into patient-specific resistance mechanisms. This interdisciplinary approach bridges systems biology, clinical oncology, and computational science, advancing precision medicine while operating squarely within the domain of medical therapeutic innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illnesses, injuries, and other disorders of the human body. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, clinical medicine, examination and diagnosis, patient communications, medical ethics and law, professional standards, and rotations in specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, orthopedics, neurology, ophthalmology, radiology, clinical pathology, anesthesiology, family medicine, and psychiatry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dialectal variation and historical linguistic shifts in Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian (BSH) languages using advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The research addresses a critical gap in BSH studies: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to systematically map dialect continua, track lexical and morphosyntactic changes across time, and quantify mutual intelligibility between regional varieties. Current methodologies rely heavily on manual analysis of limited text samples, which restricts the scope and reproducibility of findings. To overcome these limitations, we propose training transformer-based language models on a curated corpus of over 10 million words spanning contemporary and historical texts (19th–21st centuries), including novels, newspapers, oral histories, and social media. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing this heterogeneous dataset, which requires distributed training across multiple GPU nodes to handle memory-intensive tasks such as contextual embedding generation and diachronic semantic shift detection. Computational experiments will include dialect classification using attention mechanisms, phonetic alignment of regional speech variants, and graph-based network analysis to model lexical borrowing patterns. The project will also develop open-source tools for low-resource Slavic language processing, including a BSH-specific tokenizer and a web interface for visualizing dialect boundaries. Expected outcomes include new insights into the dynamic interplay between standard languages and regional varieties in post-Yugoslav contexts, with applications in language preservation, educational resource development, and cross-cultural NLP systems. By leveraging parallel computing architectures to manage the computational complexity of multilingual and multidialectal modeling, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for computational humanities research in understudied language communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian Languages and Literatures
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bosnian, Serbian and/or Croatian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational pathology platform to enhance the analysis of high-resolution histopathological imaging data, addressing the growing demand for precision in diagnostic workflows. The increasing use of digital whole-slide imaging (WSI) in pathology generates terabytes of complex data per case, creating bottlenecks in manual annotation, quantitative analysis, and integration with clinical metadata. Current methods for tissue segmentation, anomaly detection, and predictive modeling lack scalability, limiting their utility in time-sensitive diagnostic environments and large-scale research studies. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models capable of automating WSI analysis while maintaining diagnostic rigor. Our approach combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for multi-scale feature extraction with graph-based algorithms to model spatial relationships between tissue structures. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of thousands of WSIs, iterative optimization of 3D reconstruction pipelines for autopsy specimens, and validation of models against curated datasets spanning diverse pathological conditions. Key deliverables include an open-source framework for GPU-accelerated tissue segmentation, predictive models correlating histological patterns with clinical outcomes, and computational tools to standardize autopsy report generation. The successful implementation of this platform will reduce inter-observer variability in specimen analysis, accelerate turnaround times for complex cases, and enable population-scale studies of histopathological biomarkers. By integrating these tools into pathology workflows, we aim to enhance diagnostic accuracy for malignancies, inflammatory disorders, and forensic investigations while providing Pathologist Assistant trainees with advanced computational skills. This work will establish a scalable infrastructure for digital pathology research, directly supporting precision medicine initiatives and fostering collaborations between computational scientists and clinical diagnosticians.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Somatic psychology emphasizes the integration of bodily awareness and movement practices to address psychological well-being, yet the mechanisms underlying these interventions remain poorly understood at a systemic level. This project seeks to model the dynamic interactions between somatic practices, autonomic nervous system responses, and psychological states using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current research in this domain relies on small-scale datasets and simplified analytical frameworks, limiting insights into the nonlinear, time-dependent relationships between embodied practices (e.g., authentic movement, yoga) and outcomes such as emotional regulation or trauma recovery. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating multimodal data—including motion capture, electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and qualitative self-reports—from 300 participants engaged in structured somatic interventions. The project will employ dynamical systems modeling and machine learning techniques to analyze high-dimensional temporal datasets, capturing how specific movement sequences correlate with shifts in physiological arousal and cognitive-emotional states. HPC resources are critical for processing real-time biosignal data, running parallelized simulations of body-mind interaction networks, and training deep learning models to identify latent patterns across heterogeneous datatypes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework linking discrete somatic techniques to psychophysiological outcomes, (2) validated biomarkers for optimizing individualized therapeutic protocols, and (3) open-source tools for analyzing embodied interventions in counseling contexts. By elucidating the computational architecture of somatic integration, this work will advance evidence-based practices in applied psychology, offering scalable methods to evaluate and refine body-centered therapeutic approaches. The requested resources will enable the first large-scale, systems-level investigation of somatic psychology’s core premises, directly supporting the development of precision interventions for stress, anxiety, and interpersonal dysfunction.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on a holistic approach to solving interpersonal issues and psychological problems. Includes instruction in authentic movement, body-mind balance and integration, contact improvisation, dance, Pilates, Tai Chi, relaxation techniques, and Yoga.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the scientific understanding of complex, multi-component interventions in alternative and complementary medicine (ACM), such as herbal formulations, acupuncture, and mind-body therapies. A central challenge in ACM research lies in deciphering the synergistic mechanisms of therapies that involve numerous bioactive compounds, non-linear physiological responses, or dynamic interactions between biological systems. Traditional experimental methods often struggle to capture these multidimensional relationships, limiting mechanistic insights and evidence-based optimization. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular docking, machine learning, and dynamical systems modeling to analyze how ACM modalities interact with human physiology at scale. HPC resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to predict interactions between herbal compounds and protein targets, Bayesian network inference to map acupuncture’s systemic effects on neuro-immunological pathways, and ensemble machine learning models to identify patterns in clinical outcome data from heterogeneous ACM trials. Additionally, agent-based models will simulate the long-term impacts of mind-body therapies on stress-response networks. These methods require parallelized processing of multi-omics datasets, high-throughput virtual screening of phytochemical libraries, and iterative parameter optimization for non-linear systems—tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models of ACM treatment efficacy, safety profiles of herbal synergies, and mechanistic hypotheses for experimental validation. By bridging computational science and ACM, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for evaluating holistic therapies, informing personalized treatment strategies, and fostering integration of evidence-based ACM into broader healthcare paradigms. The requested resources will directly support 3–5 pilot studies, with results disseminated through open-access tools and interdisciplinary collaborations.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize aerosolized drug delivery in mechanically ventilated patients through advanced computational modeling of airway fluid dynamics, addressing a critical gap in personalized respiratory care. Current clinical protocols for aerosol therapy rely on generalized guidelines, which inadequately account for patient-specific anatomical variations, disease states, or ventilator settings. This limitation contributes to suboptimal drug deposition in 30-40% of cases, reducing therapeutic efficacy and prolonging ventilator dependence. We propose to develop high-fidelity simulations of bronchial airflow patterns and particle transport using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with machine learning-driven parameter optimization. High-performance computing resources will enable the creation of 3D patient airway models derived from thoracic CT scans, incorporating transient flow conditions, turbulent-particle interactions, and heterogeneous mucus layer dynamics. Simulations will evaluate aerosol delivery efficiency across diverse clinical scenarios, including obstructive lung diseases, pediatric anatomy, and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation. Validation will occur through parallel in vitro experiments using 3D-printed airway replicas and laser particle imaging velocimetry. The resulting predictive models will inform the development of adaptive nebulization algorithms that dynamically adjust particle size, flow rates, and dosing intervals based on real-time ventilator data. Anticipated outcomes include a 20-35% improvement in simulated alveolar deposition rates and clinically actionable thresholds for device settings across patient subgroups. By establishing a computational framework to personalize respiratory interventions, this work aims to reduce treatment failures in critical care while providing respiratory therapists with evidence-based decision support tools. The open-source simulation platform will additionally serve as an educational resource for training technicians in advanced ventilator management strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer general respiratory care procedures under the supervision of respiratory therapists in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in patient data collection and monitoring, airway management, installation of nebulizers and other respiratory assistance devices, application and monitoring of breathing gases, equipment operation and maintenance, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable regulations.

abstract: Dental implant success depends on the complex interplay of biomechanical, biological, and patient-specific factors, yet existing predictive models for long-term outcomes remain limited by oversimplified assumptions and static analyses. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to simulate bone remodeling, implant loading dynamics, and soft tissue integration under diverse clinical scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with agent-based modeling to capture time-dependent bone adaptation at the micro-architectural level, while integrating machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data (n=1,200+ cases) to account for patient-specific risk factors. The computational pipeline will process 3D CBCT scans, intraoral scans, and occlusal force data to generate patient-specific simulations of stress distribution and biological response over multi-year timelines. Validated against longitudinal clinical outcomes from a 5-year cohort study, these models aim to identify critical thresholds for bone resorption, optimal implant positioning strategies, and prosthetic design parameters that minimize mechanical failure risks. The HPC environment is essential for managing the iterative simulations required to model stochastic cellular processes in bone remodeling, resolve micron-scale strain gradients, and perform sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous anatomical datasets. Expected outcomes include clinically validated predictive tools to guide implant placement planning, personalized abutment design optimization, and data-driven criteria for early intervention in at-risk cases. By establishing an open-source computational platform for implantology research, this work will enable broader investigation of biomechanical interactions in dental rehabilitation while advancing precision medicine approaches in oral healthcare.
cip_definition: Research focused on the surgical and restorative aspects of implant dentistry.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the existence, stability, and regularity of solutions to high-dimensional nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in mathematical physics, particularly those governing wave propagation and dissipative dynamical systems. The equations under study—including nonlocal variants of Schrödinger-type equations and degenerate parabolic systems—exhibit complex interactions between dispersion, dissipation, and nonlinearity that challenge classical analytical methods. Key obstacles include establishing well-posedness in critical function spaces, characterizing long-time behavior, and quantifying stability under perturbations. To address these challenges, the project will employ a combination of modern functional-analytic techniques and advanced computational methods. Spectral decomposition approaches will be paired with adaptive wavelet-based discretizations to approximate solutions in high-dimensional settings, while Lyapunov functionals and harmonic analysis tools will guide stability analyses. The computational component requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to handle large-scale matrix operations for spectral methods, parallelized simulations of dynamic systems across parameter spaces, and memory-intensive wavelet transforms in dimensions ≥4. Expected outcomes include new criteria for global solvability in Sobolev–Bochner spaces, quantitative estimates for attractor dimensions in infinite-dimensional dynamical systems, and scalable algorithms for high-dimensional PDE analysis. These results aim to advance the rigorous treatment of multiscale phenomena in mathematical physics while developing computational frameworks that bridge abstract analysis with numerical verification. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter-space exploration at scales inaccessible to desktop computing, particularly for validating conjectured blow-up regimes and quantifying phase transitions in solution regularity. By synthesizing theoretical and computational approaches, this work will contribute foundational insights into the interplay between nonlinearity and dimensionality in PDE theory.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and behavior of equations, multivariate solutions, functions, and dynamic systems. Includes instruction in differential equations, variation, approximations, complex variables, integrals, harmonic analysis and wavelet theory, dynamic systems, and applications to mathematical physics.

abstract: The horticultural industry faces mounting challenges from climate unpredictability, which disrupts growth cycles, increases pest pressures, and threatens yield stability in high-value crops. Current breeding and management strategies lack the predictive capacity to rapidly adapt to these dynamic stressors, particularly for perennial species with long breeding timelines. This project proposes a computational framework to model genotype-by-environment interactions (G×E) in horticultural crops, integrating genomic, phenotypic, and high-resolution environmental data to accelerate the development of climate-resilient cultivars. We will focus on citrus, berry crops, and ornamental species critical to regional economies. Using machine learning architectures optimized for high-performance computing (HPC), we will analyze terabyte-scale datasets encompassing multi-omics profiles, historical yield records, and microclimate sensor networks from experimental orchards. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be coupled with agent-based models simulating pest population dynamics under future climate projections. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of genomic variants across 20+ crop genomes, real-time integration of distributed climate data streams, and iterative optimization of neural networks predicting flowering time and stress tolerance. HPC resources are essential for scaling these analyses beyond proof-of-concept trials to operationalize models across diverse production systems. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genetic markers associated with drought resilience in citrus rootstocks, (2) predictive algorithms for optimizing protected cultivation schedules in ornamental nurseries, and (3) open-source tools for simulating pest dispersal under varying management scenarios. By reducing trial-and-error in field testing, this work will shorten breeding cycles for stress-tolerant varieties while providing actionable intelligence for adaptive crop management—critical steps in safeguarding horticultural productivity under climate change.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific principles related to the cultivation of garden and ornamental plants, including fruits, vegetables, flowers, and landscape and nursery crops. Includes instruction in specific types of plants, such as citrus; breeding horticultural varieties; physiology of horticultural species; and the scientific management of horticultural plant development and production through the life cycle.

abstract: The increasing complexity of patient care demands in modern healthcare systems necessitates data-driven approaches to optimize clinical decision-making and resource allocation. Registered nurses, as frontline providers, require tools to predict patient outcomes, personalize interventions, and mitigate risks in dynamic care environments. However, existing predictive models in nursing often lack the computational power to integrate multidimensional datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time sensor data, and socio-behavioral factors—at the scale necessary for actionable insights. This project seeks to address this gap by developing machine learning (ML) frameworks tailored to nursing-specific challenges, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating predictive models for adverse event prevention (e.g., sepsis, falls, medication errors) using time-series analysis of EHR data and wearable device streams, and (2) simulating nurse staffing patterns through agent-based modeling to identify optimal care delivery strategies under resource constraints. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer models for clinical note analysis, LSTM networks for temporal data) and parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess intervention scalability. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project will enable rapid iteration of complex models across multi-terabyte datasets while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy standards through federated learning approaches. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for clinical nursing practice, evidence-based staffing recommendations, and novel methodologies for integrating HPC into nursing informatics research. This work aims to advance precision nursing care while establishing computational pipelines that bridge gaps between nursing theory, big data analytics, and real-world implementation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for estimating high-dimensional psychometric models, addressing critical limitations in existing approaches for analyzing large-scale behavioral and educational assessment data. Traditional estimation techniques for multidimensional item response theory (MIRT) and cognitive diagnostic models (CDMs) face prohibitive computational demands when applied to datasets with thousands of items and millions of respondents, leading to intractable runtime or approximations that sacrifice accuracy. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized Bayesian estimation algorithms via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and variational inference frameworks. These methods will be optimized for distributed-memory architectures to efficiently partition data and model parameters across nodes, reducing memory bottlenecks while maintaining Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling fidelity. A series of simulation studies will evaluate computational scalability, parameter recovery, and model fit across varying sample sizes, item dimensions, and missing data mechanisms. Additionally, we will develop open-source software integrating these algorithms with GPU-accelerated linear algebra operations to enable practical adoption by the research community. The expected outcomes include (1) novel computational workflows for fitting complex psychometric models to massive datasets, (2) empirically validated benchmarks for trade-offs between estimation accuracy and runtime in distributed computing environments, and (3) publicly accessible tools that democratize access to advanced quantitative methods. By addressing computational barriers in high-dimensional measurement models, this work will enhance the rigor of large-scale test validation processes, support more nuanced investigations of respondent behavior, and expand the methodological toolkit for quantitative psychology research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the memory-intensive demands of Bayesian hierarchical modeling and enabling timely completion of simulation experiments across diverse psychometric conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale computational analysis of Spanish dialectal and literary variation across temporal, geographic, and sociocultural contexts. While Spanish is among the most widely spoken languages globally, its regional diversification—from Medieval Castilian to contemporary Latin American dialects—remains understudied at scale due to the technical challenges of processing heterogeneous textual corpora, including historical manuscripts, modern digital media, and transcribed oral narratives. Current methodologies in Spanish philology and dialectology often rely on manual annotation or small-sample statistical models, limiting the scope of interdisciplinary inquiry into linguistic evolution, semantic shifts, and sociolinguistic patterns. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods framework combining natural language processing (NLP), neural machine translation, and phonetic alignment algorithms to analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning eight centuries of Spanish language use. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on diachronic corpora to detect syntactic and lexical changes, applying graph-based clustering to map dialect continua across Iberian and Latin American regions, and simulating phonetic drift using spectral analysis of annotated speech recordings. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing computationally intensive workflows, such as fine-tuning multilingual embeddings for archaic spellings or processing high-resolution audio datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible repository of annotated linguistic features correlated with historical events and migration patterns; (2) predictive models of dialectal divergence under sociopolitical scenarios; and (3) open-source tools for automated paleographic transcription of early modern manuscripts. By bridging computational linguistics with Hispanic studies, this work aims to redefine the scale of inquiry in Spanish philology while providing actionable resources for educators, policymakers, and digital humanities scholars invested in preserving linguistic diversity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Spanish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Castilan; Latin American and regional Spanish dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in optimizing autonomous robotic systems for dynamic, unstructured environments. As robotics applications expand into logistics, infrastructure inspection, and hazardous material handling, traditional control architectures often fail to balance real-time responsiveness with the precision required for complex tasks. The research focuses on developing a scalable framework for multi-agent robotic coordination and adaptive manipulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations in simulation fidelity, decision-making latency, and system-level optimization. Key computational challenges include real-time path planning under uncertainty, distributed task allocation across heterogeneous robot teams, and high-dimensional parameter optimization for compliant manipulators. The proposed methodology combines parallelized physics-based simulation using Gazebo and MuJoCo with reinforcement learning (RL) workflows accelerated through GPU clusters. Large-scale parameter sweeps will train RL policies for gripper-object interaction scenarios, while distributed optimization algorithms will resolve conflicts in multi-agent coordination. HPC resources will enable 1) massively parallel simulation of edge-case environmental conditions, 2) accelerated training of vision-based control models through tensor decomposition techniques, and 3) system-wide validation of safety protocols via digital twin implementations. Expected outcomes include novel benchmarking datasets for dexterous manipulation, open-source optimization tools for reconfigurable robot teams, and quantitative guidelines for trading computational overhead against operational reliability in field deployments. By establishing reproducible workflows for HPC-augmented robotic system design, this work aims to reduce development cycles for industrial robotics solutions while improving the energy efficiency of autonomous operations. The requested computing resources will directly support 12+ concurrent simulation environments, enable batch processing of 10⁴-10⁵ training episodes daily, and facilitate comparative analysis of control architectures across multiple fidelity levels.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using robots. Includes instruction in the principles of robotics, design and operational testing, system maintenance and repair procedures, robot computer systems and control language, specific system types and applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing large-scale cultural discourse data to enhance the study and practice of cultural journalism. As digital platforms expand the volume and diversity of cultural content—from multimedia reviews to social media commentary—journalists face challenges in identifying patterns, biases, and emerging narratives across fragmented sources. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process such datasets efficiently, limiting the depth of critical analysis. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to apply natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning (ML) techniques to cultural journalism datasets. These include archives of arts criticism, multimedia reviews, and real-time social media streams related to visual and performing arts, film, music, and digital media. Key computational tasks will involve sentiment analysis of critical reception over time, topic modeling to map thematic shifts in cultural coverage, and network visualization to trace the influence of critics, institutions, and platforms on public discourse. Additionally, we aim to develop a multimodal analysis pipeline integrating text, image, and audio data from arts journalism to study how interdisciplinary narratives are constructed. The scale of data—spanning millions of articles, images, and social media posts—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are only feasible with HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include open-access tools for journalists to analyze cultural trends computationally, a public database of annotated cultural discourse datasets, and scholarly insights into the evolving role of criticism in digital ecosystems. This work bridges computational methods with humanistic inquiry, empowering cultural journalists to produce more nuanced, data-informed critiques while advancing academic research on media, aesthetics, and public engagement.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to be journalists who critically examine current culture as expressed through the visual and performing arts, design, film, music, radio, television, dance, theater, and written text. Includes instruction in arts criticism, art and entertainment reporting, cultural critique, investigative reporting, newspaper reporting, photojournalism, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in computational research on Bengali (Bangla) linguistics, with a focus on dialectal variation and historical philology. Despite Bengali’s status as the seventh most spoken language globally, large-scale quantitative analyses of its regional dialects and historical text corpora remain underdeveloped due to computational limitations. The research problem centers on mapping phonetic, syntactic, and lexical divergences across Bengali dialects and tracing their evolution through digitized pre-modern texts, tasks requiring intensive processing of unstructured linguistic data. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for low-resource languages, to analyze spoken and written corpora spanning six major dialects and texts from the 15th–19th centuries. Key methods involve training dialect classification models using phonetic transcriptions, applying diachronic word embedding algorithms to track semantic shifts, and simulating language change through agent-based models. These workflows demand parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including audio recordings, annotated manuscripts, and lexical databases, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The requested HPC resources will enable efficient execution of distributed training for deep learning models, large-scale text normalization, and phonetic alignment across heterogeneous data types. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Bengali dialect boundaries, a diachronic corpus with semantic change annotations, and open-access tools for low-resource NLP applications. This work will advance scholarly understanding of Bengali’s linguistic history, support preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and provide computational frameworks applicable to other under-resourced languages. By bridging gaps between traditional philology and modern NLP, the project aims to establish a foundation for data-driven humanities research in Bengali studies while contributing methodologies to the broader field of computational linguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bengali language (Bangla) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Danish dialectal variation and its historical evolution, a critical gap in Scandinavian linguistics. While Danish dialects and historical texts offer rich insights into sociolinguistic change, traditional manual methods struggle to process the growing corpus of digitized texts, audio recordings, and metadata spanning the 19th century to the present. The research problem centers on modeling complex phonological, morphological, and lexical patterns across time and geography, which requires large-scale parallel processing and machine learning frameworks. The project will employ NLP techniques, including transformer-based models, to analyze digitized texts from regional archives, historical dictionaries, and transcribed oral histories. Computational workflows will be designed to map phonetic shifts (e.g., the transition from the Insular Danish *kirkæ* to Modern Standard Danish *kirke*) and syntactic changes across dialects, using distributed training to optimize neural networks for low-resource language tasks. Phonetic alignment algorithms will process spoken dialect corpora, while graph-based methods will trace lexical diffusion networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialect features, dynamic visualizations of language change, and models capable of identifying understudied regional variants. These resources will support philological research, language preservation initiatives, and applications in Danish NLP tools, such as improved dialect-aware speech recognition systems. By integrating computational rigor with linguistic expertise, this project aims to redefine methodologies in Danish studies while demonstrating the value of HPC for minority language research in the humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Danish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Health professions education faces increasing demands to optimize training strategies that balance clinical competency, adaptive learning, and equitable outcomes across diverse populations. Current approaches to curriculum design and evaluation often rely on limited datasets or simplified models that inadequately capture the complexity of clinical learning environments, interprofessional dynamics, and longitudinal skill development. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets and simulate large-scale training scenarios. The research will integrate anonymized student performance metrics, clinical simulation logs, preceptor evaluations, and demographic data from a multi-institutional consortium of health professions programs. Machine learning models will be developed to predict trajectories of clinical reasoning development, identify hidden biases in assessment tools, and simulate the impact of adaptive curricula on learner outcomes under variable resource constraints. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing to analyze qualitative feedback, graph-based algorithms to map interprofessional collaboration patterns, and agent-based modeling to test interventions in virtual clinical training ecosystems. The project requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize iterative model training, and run high-fidelity simulations of educational scenarios involving thousands of virtual learners and instructors. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for optimizing competency-based curricula, evidence-based strategies to reduce disparities in clinical skill acquisition, and open-source tools for simulating health professions education systems. These computational advances will empower educators to make data-driven decisions in curriculum design, resource allocation, and adaptive assessment strategies at scale, ultimately strengthening the pipeline of clinical educators equipped to address evolving healthcare challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on education and administration leadership skills for clinical educators across health professions and specialties. Includes instruction in academic leadership, assessment, clinical decision making, curriculum development, ethics, primary care education, program evaluation, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: The poultry industry faces critical challenges in optimizing production efficiency, disease resistance, and sustainability while meeting growing global protein demands. Current limitations in understanding the complex interactions between avian genetics, gut microbiota dynamics, and nutritional interventions hinder progress. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through advanced genomic and microbiomic modeling. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of poultry breeds with machine learning-driven analyses of gut microbial ecosystems. Using whole-genome sequencing data from broiler and layer populations, we will identify genetic markers linked to disease resilience and feed efficiency. Concurrently, metagenomic datasets from poultry gut microbiomes will be analyzed to model microbial community responses to dietary additives and environmental stressors. These datasets will inform agent-based simulations of host-microbiome interactions under varying nutritional regimes. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallel processing for alignment of terabase-scale sequencing data, Bayesian hierarchical modeling of genotype-phenotype associations, and dynamic flux balance analysis of microbial metabolic networks. By coupling these approaches, we aim to predict optimal genetic selection criteria and feed formulations that maximize growth performance while reducing antibiotic dependence. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the project's data volume (>500 TB raw sequencing data), complex model integration, and iterative simulations across biological scales. Expected outcomes include predictive models for precision poultry nutrition, candidate genes for selective breeding programs, and a computational toolkit for optimizing hatchery environments. This work will provide transformative insights into avian systems biology, directly supporting the development of sustainable poultry production strategies that align with global food security priorities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of poultry animals and the production and handling of poultry products. Includes instruction in avian sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, hatchery design, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: The variability in patient responses to pharmacotherapy poses a significant challenge in clinical, hospital, and managed care settings, where optimized drug regimens are critical to outcomes. Current approaches to dose individualization often rely on population averages or limited patient-specific data, leading to suboptimal efficacy or toxicity risks. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-resolution computational models of drug pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) tailored to diverse patient populations. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-scale data, including electronic health records, genomic biomarkers, and real-world drug monitoring results, into predictive frameworks. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to identify nonlinear relationships between patient covariates (e.g., renal/hepatic function, pharmacogenomic profiles) and drug behavior. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model drug-receptor interactions under physiological conditions, incorporating genetic variants affecting protein structure. These computational workflows will be validated against clinical trial data from oncology and psychiatric pharmacy cohorts, where narrow therapeutic indices demand precise dosing. The HPC environment is essential for managing the iterative parameter estimation required for population PK/PD modeling, parallel processing of genomic data, and large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models enabling dynamic dose adjustments for drugs with high interpatient variability, such as immunosuppressants and chemotherapeutics, and (2) a decision-support framework to guide therapeutic drug monitoring in real-time clinical workflows. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on advancing evidence-based, patient-specific care through computational innovation, with potential applications in antimicrobial stewardship, transplant pharmacy, and chronic disease management. By bridging mechanistic pharmacology with clinical informatics, the project aims to reduce adverse drug events and improve therapeutic outcomes in complex care environments.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Clinical, Hospital, and Managed Care Pharmacy
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to deliver specialized pharmacy services and produce pharmaceutical products in clinical settings in conjunction with other health care professionals. Includes instruction in biostatistics; clinical pharmacokinetics; biopharmaceutics; neuropharmacology; pharmacodynamics; drug metabolism; clinical sampling and research design; drug delivery systems; chemotherapy; pharmacotherapy; clinical pharmacy management; medical and research ethics; and applications to nuclear, nutrition support, oncology, psychiatric, and therapeutic pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate unresolved questions in the spectral properties of automorphic forms and their connections to arithmetic structures in pure number theory. A central focus is the computational exploration of eigenvalues of Laplacians on certain high-dimensional locally symmetric spaces associated with congruence subgroups. These eigenvalues encode deep arithmetic information but remain intractable to analytical methods alone due to the combinatorial complexity of their modular embeddings and the exponential growth of matrix coefficients in higher-rank groups. The research will employ a hybrid numerical-symbolic approach, combining optimized C++ implementations of trace formula algorithms with parallelized eigenvalue solvers for hyperbolic PDEs discretized on fundamental domains. High-performance computing resources are essential for handling the large-scale linear algebra operations (matrix diagonalization for sparse matrices of dimension >10^6) and distributed memory requirements of character variety calculations. Key objectives include verifying conjectured bounds on the asymptotic distribution of Laplace eigenvalues in congruence covers of SL(n,Z)\SL(n,R)/SO(n) for n ≥ 3, and establishing new experimental evidence for the arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity conjecture in these settings.
