Successful execution would provide the first systematic computational framework for studying spectral reciprocity laws beyond rank 1, while advancing numerical techniques for automorphic representation theory. The resulting datasets and algorithms will be made publicly available through modular arithmetic repositories, creating foundational resources for collaborative work in Langlands program numerics. This work directly addresses multiple problems highlighted in the NSF-DMS 2025 Priority Areas for Pure Mathematics, particularly regarding computational tools for non-abelian class field theory.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the analysis of quantities, magnitudes, forms, and their relationships, using symbolic logic and language. Includes instruction in algebra, calculus, functional analysis, geometry, number theory, logic, topology and other mathematical specializations.

abstract: Theatrical productions involve complex, dynamic interactions between spatial design, performer movement, and audience perception that remain challenging to optimize through traditional rehearsal methods alone. This project seeks to develop computational models for simulating and analyzing multidimensional production elements through high-performance computing (HPC). The research problem centers on the lack of integrated tools to quantitatively evaluate how staging decisions—such as actor blocking, set configurations, and lighting designs—collectively impact audience engagement and narrative clarity across diverse performance spaces. To address this, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, motion-capture data from rehearsals and historical productions will be used to train agent-based models that simulate performer trajectories and audience sightline obstructions in parametrized virtual venues. Second, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will iteratively propose staging adjustments that balance artistic intent with spatial efficiency, using reinforcement learning to optimize for metrics derived from dramaturgical principles and crowd-sourced viewer feedback. These simulations will require parallelized rendering of 3D environments and real-time physics calculations to model acoustics, lighting propagation, and multi-view spectator perspectives at scale. By leveraging GPU clusters and distributed memory systems, the project aims to produce adaptive tools that assist directors in prototyping productions computationally before physical rehearsals begin. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying directorial choices, a repository of annotated performance simulations for pedagogical use, and evidence-based guidelines for staging in non-traditional venues. This work bridges performing arts practice with computational analytics, offering methods to preserve artistic nuance while reducing resource-intensive trial-and-error in theatrical workflows. Successful implementation could transform how productions are planned in an era of increasingly constrained budgets and hybrid digital-live performance formats.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the planning, design, preparation, and production of plays and other theatrical entertainment programs. Includes instruction in theatrical design, program management, dramatic production, rehearsal management, personnel management and casting, actor coaching, directing concepts and techniques, theater history, scene work, script interpretation, business management, marketing, public relations, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the acoustic and biomechanical interactions inherent in advanced stringed instrument performance. While traditional pedagogical methods for stringed instruments rely on qualitative assessments of tone production, articulation, and expressive phrasing, the complex physical dynamics underlying these elements—including string vibration, bow contact mechanics, and performer motor control—remain insufficiently quantified. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing computational models that simulate real-world performance scenarios at high temporal and spatial resolutions. These models will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for instrument-body resonance, fluid-structure interaction simulations for bow-string friction dynamics, and machine learning (ML) techniques to correlate biomechanical sensor data (e.g., motion capture, electromyography) with perceptual outcomes in recorded performances. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve sub-millisecond temporal resolution in simulations, enabling the identification of micro-variations in technique that distinguish expert-level artistry. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database of performance-optimized physical models for violins, cellos, and related instruments; (2) ML-driven diagnostic tools for personalized feedback in pedagogical contexts; and (3) novel insights into the biomechanical efficiency of historically significant performance practices. The resource request targets GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and high-memory nodes for FEA, with an estimated 200,000 core-hours required annually. This work advances the performing arts by establishing quantitative frameworks for artistic mastery while fostering interdisciplinary innovation between computational physics and music pedagogy. Results will directly inform curriculum development in the Stringed Instruments program and provide a foundation for future studies on injury prevention and ergonomic design for musicians.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individual to master a stringed instrument and performing arts as solo, ensemble and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the complex interplay between urban environmental stressors, socioeconomic factors, and population health outcomes through an integrative data analytics framework. While prior studies have examined isolated environmental or social determinants of health, this research addresses a critical gap by modeling dynamic, multiscale interactions between heterogeneous datasets—including real-time sensor networks (air quality, noise, temperature), anonymized electronic health records, and spatially resolved socioeconomic indices—to identify emergent patterns of community-level health risks. The computational challenge lies in harmonizing high-dimensional, temporally staggered data streams spanning disparate domains while accounting for spatial autocorrelation and latent confounding variables. We propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial-temporal dependencies, Bayesian hierarchical modeling for uncertainty quantification across scales, and agent-based simulations to test intervention scenarios. HPC resources are essential for training GNNs on petabyte-scale urban sensor datasets, executing parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across socioeconomic gradients, and optimizing hyperparameters through distributed evolutionary algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include a novel open-source analytics pipeline for multimodal urban health data, identification of high-risk “hotspots” where environmental and socioeconomic stressors synergistically amplify health disparities, and predictive models to evaluate equitable mitigation strategies. This work advances interdisciplinary methodologies at the nexus of environmental science, public health, and computational social science, providing actionable insights for policymakers while establishing scalable frameworks for data integration challenges common to smart city initiatives worldwide.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data analytics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The design of high-performance buildings necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize energy efficiency, structural integrity, and environmental sustainability across complex systems. Current limitations in simulating multi-scale interactions—such as urban microclimates, building envelope performance, and integrated mechanical systems—hinder the ability to holistically evaluate design alternatives. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale simulations and machine learning workflows for architectural engineering applications. The research focuses on two primary objectives: (1) developing coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) models to assess building resilience under extreme weather and seismic loads, and (2) training generative AI models to automate the design of energy-efficient HVAC and daylighting systems using parametric inputs. High-resolution 3D urban datasets, sensor-derived environmental data, and material performance databases will be integrated into a unified simulation framework, requiring parallel processing for stochastic weather modeling and topology optimization. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed computing to reduce simulation times from weeks to hours, enabling iterative design testing at unprecedented scales. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for architects and engineers to rapidly prototype low-carbon building systems, validated against physical prototypes in lab environments. By bridging gaps between architectural design and computational engineering, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in sustainable construction, reduce lifecycle energy consumption in urban developments, and establish scalable methods for resilient infrastructure planning. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive multi-objective optimizations central to this research, which aligns with global priorities for climate-adaptive built environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance pharmacoeconomic and regulatory decision-making models for optimizing drug formularies and evaluating policy impacts. Current formulary design and reimbursement strategies often rely on static cost-effectiveness analyses, which inadequately capture dynamic factors such as regional prescribing patterns, patient adherence variability, and evolving market competition. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-stakeholder interactions (e.g., prescribers, insurers, patients) under varying regulatory and market conditions. The ABM will incorporate granular data from national insurance claims, electronic health records, and drug pricing databases to model formulary adoption, prescribing behavior, and patient outcomes at scale. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify predictors of policy compliance gaps and forecast long-term cost trajectories under hypothetical reimbursement policies. HPC resources are critical due to the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across thousands of agents and the need for high-dimensional optimization of formulary structures. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for formulary managers to prioritize drugs balancing clinical benefit, cost, and equity, as well as policy scenarios quantifying trade-offs between access restrictions and population health outcomes. This work will directly inform state-level Medicaid formulary reforms and provide a template for evaluating emerging regulatory challenges, such as biosimilar adoption incentives and specialty drug pricing caps. By enabling rapid, data-driven policy testing, the project aligns with the program’s focus on advancing evidence-based pharmacy administration and regulatory strategies in complex healthcare systems.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of translation practices across diverse sociocultural and historical contexts. Translation Studies, as a multidisciplinary field, requires the integration of large-scale multilingual corpora, sociolinguistic metadata, and contextual variables to analyze how cultural, institutional, and temporal factors shape translation outcomes. Existing methodologies often lack the computational capacity to process heterogeneous datasets—spanning literary, technical, and business translations—while modeling the nonlinear interactions between linguistic features and extratextual influences. The proposed research will develop scalable computational workflows to systematically examine these dynamics. Key methods include the deployment of neural machine translation (NMT) models fine-tuned on domain-specific corpora, coupled with graph-based algorithms to map semantic shifts and cultural adaptations across translated texts. Parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process multilingual datasets, while transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT variants) will classify stylistic, pragmatic, and ideological patterns in historical and contemporary translations. HPC resources are essential for training these models on terabytes of text, enabling comparative analyses across languages, genres, and time periods. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for quantifying the impact of sociocultural variables on translation accuracy and creativity, (2) open-access tools for cross-domain translation quality assessment, and (3) novel insights into how institutional norms and power dynamics manifest in translated texts. By bridging computational scalability with humanistic inquiry, this work will advance theoretical models of translation while supporting practical applications in multilingual communication, archival digitization, and AI-driven translation technologies. The project aligns with Translation Studies’ interdisciplinary mandate, offering methodologies applicable to literary analysis, technical documentation, and global business contexts without reliance on adjacent fields excluded by the funding guidelines.
cip_definition: A multidisciplinary program that prepares individuals to explore the historical, social, institutional and cultural facets of translation. Includes instruction in general and literary translation, business translation, technical translation, and other specific applications of linguistic skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive workplace design in response to dynamic organizational needs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between spatial configurations, occupant behavior, and operational efficiency. Traditional facility planning methods rely on static benchmarks or heuristic evaluations, which struggle to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating occupancy patterns, evolving health and safety protocols, and heterogeneous employee preferences. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate environmental psychology principles, real-time sensor data, and multi-objective optimization to generate workspace layouts that balance productivity, well-being, and resource efficiency. Using agent-based modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, the project will analyze how spatial parameters (e.g., desk density, circulation pathways, shared amenities) interact with human factors (e.g., collaboration frequency, noise sensitivity) and environmental conditions (e.g., air quality, thermal comfort). HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations across thousands of hypothetical scenarios, enabling probabilistic assessments of design resilience under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., energy use vs. social connectivity) and identifies Pareto-optimal solutions for facility managers. This work bridges gaps between data science, behavioral economics, and architectural design, offering a novel methodology for post-pandemic workspace strategy. By advancing computational approaches to facility planning, the project aims to establish evidence-based standards for adaptive environments while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional, policy-adjacent domains. Results will be validated against empirical data from partner organizations, with open-source model components to encourage broader adoption in workplace innovation research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance forensic psychology research focused on improving risk assessment models for individuals navigating the criminal justice system. Current risk assessment tools often rely on static, demographic factors or clinician-administered scales, which may lack sensitivity to dynamic behavioral patterns, contextual stressors, and intervention-related changes. To address this gap, we propose analyzing large-scale, multimodal datasets—including electronic health records, legal histories, and real-time behavioral monitoring data—to identify nuanced predictors of violence, recidivism, and treatment responsiveness. Computational challenges arise from the volume, heterogeneity, and temporal granularity of these data, which require advanced machine learning techniques to integrate structured and unstructured inputs (e.g., clinical notes, court transcripts). HPC resources will enable the training of deep learning models, such as transformer-based architectures for natural language processing of forensic interviews, and recurrent neural networks to model longitudinal behavioral trajectories. Additionally, agent-based simulations will be employed to test hypothetical intervention scenarios in diverse virtual populations. The project aims to produce validated, open-source algorithms that improve the accuracy and fairness of forensic risk assessments while reducing biases tied to overgeneralized demographic proxies. Outcomes will directly inform the development of decision-support tools for legal professionals and ethically grounded intervention protocols tailored to individual risk profiles. By integrating computational rigor with forensic psychology’s applied focus, this work bridges gaps between data-driven insights and real-world practice, ultimately supporting equitable outcomes in legal settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical, counseling, school, and neuropsychology skills to the provision of psychological services within the criminal justice and civil legal systems, including consultation, assessment, and interventions. Includes instruction in the epidemiology of mental/behavioral disorders, risk factors for violence and criminality, profiling and patterning, psychological testing, prediction and intervention measurement, forensic assessment, criminal and civil law and procedures, secure environments, forensic treatment and intervention skills, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical need for advanced computational tools to analyze complex speech patterns in individuals with neurodegenerative communication disorders, such as primary progressive aphasia (PPA) and Parkinsonian syndromes. Current clinical assessments in speech-language pathology rely heavily on subjective perceptual evaluations and time-consuming manual acoustic analyses, limiting scalability and precision in tracking disease progression or therapy outcomes. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a machine learning framework to automate the detection of subtle, subperceptual speech biomarkers from high-resolution audio and articulatory kinematic data. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets encompassing >10,000 hours of speech samples from diverse patient cohorts, paired with longitudinal clinical metadata. Computational workflows will integrate parallelized feature extraction (including nonlinear dynamic measures of vocal fold vibration and articulatory coordination) with deep neural networks trained to identify disease-specific signatures across phonetic, prosodic, and fluency domains. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive preprocessing of raw waveform data, optimizing hyperparameters for temporal convolutional networks, and validating models through large-scale cross-database replication studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for quantifying speech degradation trajectories with millisecond-level temporal resolution, enabling earlier intervention windows and personalized therapy targets. By establishing quantitative links between computational speech markers and neuropathological staging, this work aims to advance tele-rehabilitation monitoring systems while providing foundational insights into the neurocomputational mechanisms of speech motor control. The resulting infrastructure will support future investigations into speech plasticity across acquired and congenital communication disorders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of personality dynamics by integrating multi-level data on trait-behavior interactions, neurophysiological correlates, and environmental feedback loops. Personality psychology has long grappled with the challenge of modeling the temporal stability and context-dependent variability of traits, particularly when accounting for biological mechanisms (e.g., neurotransmitter systems) and social reinforcement patterns. Traditional statistical approaches struggle to handle the non-linear interactions, high-dimensional longitudinal data, and recursive individual-environment transactions central to these phenomena. We propose developing agent-based models and dynamical systems frameworks to simulate how enduring personality characteristics emerge from and adapt to intra-individual neurocognitive processes (e.g., dopaminergic reward sensitivity) and inter-individual social evaluations. The computational pipeline will implement hierarchical Bayesian inference to estimate latent trait-state networks from multimodal datasets, including experience-sampling surveys, functional neuroimaging meta-analyses, and behavioral task performance metrics. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across 50,000+ simulated agents with individualized neural architectures, processing decade-spanning longitudinal data from three established cohort studies (total N > 15,000), and conducting parameter space explorations of trait development under varying environmental contingencies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating personality-environment co-evolution, (2) novel insights into mechanistic boundaries between major theoretical frameworks (e.g., reinforcement sensitivity theory vs. socioanalytic models), and (3) empirically grounded hypotheses about neurocomputational moderators of trait malleability. By enabling simultaneous modeling of biological, cognitive, and social timescales, this work aims to bridge gaps between dispositional, process-oriented, and interpersonal approaches in personality psychology while establishing computational best practices for the field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the unique organization of fairly permanent characteristics that set the individual apart from other individuals and, at the same time, determine how others respond to that individual. Includes instruction in Freudian, Skinnerian, Rogerian, and Ellisonian psychology; neo-Freudian psychology; psychological systems, neurophysiology, and psychopharmacology.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the precision of rehabilitation protocols for patients recovering from musculoskeletal injuries by leveraging computational modeling to predict biomechanical responses to physical therapy interventions. Current clinical practices rely heavily on generalized protocols and iterative adjustments based on observable progress, which can delay optimal outcomes. To address this, we propose developing patient-specific musculoskeletal simulations that integrate individualized anatomical data, movement patterns, and tissue healing timelines. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large-scale datasets from motion capture systems, electromyography, and medical imaging, which will inform finite element models of muscle, tendon, and joint dynamics. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to identify predictive markers of recovery efficiency and risks of re-injury. The computational pipeline will simulate thousands of therapy scenarios, varying parameters such as exercise intensity, range of motion, and load distribution, to identify personalized intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for generating adaptive rehabilitation plans that dynamically respond to patient progress, reducing recovery times and improving functional outcomes. This work aligns with the educational goals of the Physical Therapy Technician/Aide program by providing a data-driven tool to support clinical decision-making, enabling technicians to better anticipate patient needs and optimize therapy delivery under the supervision of licensed physical therapists. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models that would otherwise be computationally intractable, ensuring scalability for future multicenter clinical validation studies. By bridging computational innovation and hands-on rehabilitation practice, this project aims to elevate the role of technical support staff in advancing evidence-based care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of physical therapists, and to perform routine functions in support of physical therapy and rehabilitation. Includes instruction in applied kinesiology, basic function of the human body, communication skills, principles and procedures of physical therapy, physical therapy modalities, and professional ethics.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment planning for complex malocclusions and craniofacial anomalies requires precise understanding of biomechanical interactions between orthodontic appliances, dentition, and bone remodeling processes. Current clinical methods rely on generalized force systems and static imaging, which inadequately capture patient-specific anatomical variability and dynamic tissue responses. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling with machine learning to optimize treatment predictability. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct three-dimensional finite element models derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans, incorporating heterogeneous material properties of periodontal ligaments, alveolar bone, and orthodontic hardware. Multiphysics simulations will quantify stress-strain distributions during tooth movement under various force regimens, while coupled bone remodeling algorithms will predict long-term tissue adaptation. Concurrently, a deep learning pipeline will analyze longitudinal clinical datasets to identify patterns linking biomechanical parameters to treatment outcomes. The computational scale necessitates HPC capabilities due to the need for parallel processing of nonlinear, time-dependent simulations across thousands of voxelized anatomical elements, as well as training neural networks on high-dimensional clinical imaging and treatment response data. Expected outcomes include predictive models that correlate appliance configuration with biological responses, enabling virtual treatment testing and personalized force system optimization. This work will advance precision orthodontics by reducing clinical trial-and-error approaches, potentially shortening treatment durations and minimizing adverse outcomes such as root resorption. The developed framework will be disseminated as an open-source tool for biomechanical analysis in dentistry, with implications for improving care standards in complex cases requiring interdisciplinary management.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and techniques involved in the prevention and correction of dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid edge-cloud infrastructures demands adaptive resource management strategies that transcend traditional static allocation models. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing computational and network resource distribution in dynamic, heterogeneous environments where IoT devices, edge nodes, and cloud systems operate under fluctuating workloads and strict latency constraints. Current approaches in network and system administration often rely on reactive scaling or oversimplified predictive models, leading to suboptimal utilization rates and service degradation during demand spikes. We propose developing an autonomous resource orchestration framework that integrates graph-based network topology analysis with real-time telemetry from distributed systems. The computational methodology combines temporal graph neural networks to model evolving device dependencies with multi-agent reinforcement learning for decentralized decision-making. This approach requires high-performance computing resources to simulate large-scale network environments (10,000+ nodes) while training machine learning models on parallelized workflows. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for neural network training and distributed memory systems for network emulation at operational scales. Expected outcomes include a novel resource allocation algorithm capable of maintaining sub-100ms decision latency in simulated smart city deployments, dynamic storage tiering strategies that reduce redundant data transfers by 30-40%, and failure prediction models that improve fault tolerance through proactive resource reservation. Success metrics will be validated against industrial IoT and emergency response communication scenarios, providing system administrators with concrete benchmarks for next-generation infrastructure management. The developed tools will be released as open-source modules for integration with existing network monitoring platforms, advancing capabilities in adaptive system administration while establishing performance baselines for AI-driven resource management in critical infrastructure applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: Understanding the systemic interplay between metabolic regulation and immune activation during chronic inflammatory diseases remains a critical challenge in biomedical research. Traditional experimental approaches often fail to capture the dynamic, multi-organ interactions that drive disease progression and treatment resistance. This project seeks to develop a large-scale computational model integrating metabolic pathways, immune signaling networks, and tissue-specific responses to investigate system-level dysregulations in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease. The proposed framework will employ differential equation-based modeling to simulate real-time crosstalk between hepatic metabolic processes, circulatory cytokine dynamics, and immune cell recruitment across affected tissues. High-performance computing resources are essential to solve millions of coupled equations simultaneously, parameterize models using heterogeneous clinical datasets, and perform sensitivity analyses across physiological timescales. Expected outcomes include identification of critical regulatory nodes governing inflammatory persistence, prediction of combinatorial therapeutic targets addressing both metabolic and immunological components, and generation of patient-specific in silico platforms for treatment optimization. By elucidating emergent properties of systemic inflammation, this work aims to advance precision medicine strategies for complex chronic diseases while providing a scalable computational framework applicable to diverse biomedical research contexts.
cip_definition: A general, program that focuses on the integrative scientific study of biological issues related to health and medicine, or a program in one or more of the biomedical sciences that is undifferentiated as to title. Includes instruction in any of the basic medical sciences at the research level; biological science research in biomedical faculties; and general studies encompassing a variety of the biomedical disciplines.

abstract: The study of strongly correlated quantum systems remains a central challenge in modern physics due to the exponential growth of computational complexity with system size. Classical simulations of such systems—particularly those involving out-of-equilibrium dynamics or high-dimensional entanglement—are often intractable with conventional methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance numerical simulations of quantum many-body systems using tensor network algorithms optimized for parallel architectures. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) simulating non-equilibrium phases in one- and two-dimensional spin lattices under time-dependent perturbations, and (2) characterizing entanglement growth and thermalization processes in disordered quantum systems. These investigations will employ matrix product states (MPS) and projected entangled pair states (PEPS) frameworks, combined with density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) methods, adapted for GPU-accelerated clusters. A key innovation involves developing hybrid CPU-GPU workflows to manage memory-intensive tensor contractions and optimize scalability for systems exceeding 100 qubits. The computational demands are substantial, requiring multi-node parallelism, distributed memory management, and petascale storage for wavefunction snapshots. Expected outcomes include new insights into dynamical phase transitions in quantum spin systems, quantitative predictions of thermalization timescales in engineered quantum materials, and benchmarks for near-term quantum simulators. By pushing the boundaries of simulable system sizes, this work will provide foundational data for testing theoretical conjectures in quantum statistical mechanics and guide experimental efforts in quantum computing platforms. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours, supplemented by high-memory nodes and fast interconnects, is critical to achieving the necessary numerical precision and temporal resolution. Results will be disseminated through open-source code releases, enabling broader community access to the optimized algorithms developed during this project.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of matter and energy, and the formulation and testing of the laws governing the behavior of the matter-energy continuum. Includes instruction in classical and modern physics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, mechanics, wave properties, nuclear processes, relativity and quantum theory, quantitative methods, and laboratory methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive, data-driven framework to optimize community health interventions by modeling the dynamic interplay between social determinants of health (SDOH), individual behavioral patterns, and resource accessibility. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of generalized intervention strategies in heterogeneous populations, where overlapping socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental factors create complex barriers to care. Current approaches often rely on static demographic data, failing to account for real-time behavioral feedback or spatially varying resource constraints. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled system integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), geospatial analytics, and network optimization. The ABM component will simulate population-level health decision-making processes using synthetic cohorts calibrated to regional SDOH datasets, while graph neural networks will map multi-scale interactions between community needs and service availability. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution geosocial data from public databases and anonymized community partner records, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable sensitivity analyses to identify critical leverage points for interventions and generate adaptive resource allocation templates. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for community health workers to prioritize outreach strategies under resource constraints, dynamically adjust referral pathways based on emerging needs, and quantify intervention equity impacts through counterfactual modeling. This work bridges computational social science and health services research, offering a novel methodology to transform community liaison practices from reactive to proactive systems. By coupling behavioral realism with operational scalability, the framework aims to reduce service fragmentation in underserved populations while maintaining methodological rigor for cross-community reproducibility.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as facilitators, advocates, and referral professionals linking health care and related social services with affected recipient communities. Includes instruction in public and community health, human and social services, health services administration, group counseling, health education, group advocacy, cross-cultural and multilingual communication, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent collective phenomena in strongly correlated quantum systems through large-scale numerical simulations, addressing critical gaps in understanding phase transitions and non-equilibrium dynamics in regimes where analytical methods are intractable. The research focuses on two interconnected thrusts: (1) simulating quantum spin lattices with frustrated geometries to characterize exotic magnetic phases and their transitions under varying interaction strengths, and (2) modeling non-equilibrium transport in disordered fermionic systems to elucidate the interplay between many-body localization and thermalization. The computational approach combines tensor network methods—specifically matrix product states (MPS) and projected entangled pair states (PEPS)—with hybrid quantum Monte Carlo techniques optimized for massively parallel architectures. These methods will be deployed on high-performance computing clusters to handle system sizes exceeding 1000 particles, with custom MPI-based parallelization strategies to manage memory constraints and accelerate tensor contractions. Key challenges include mitigating entanglement growth in real-time evolution simulations and improving sampling efficiency for high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include the identification of universal scaling laws near quantum critical points, quantitative predictions of dynamical phase boundaries, and open-source release of optimized simulation frameworks for the broader physics community. The results will advance fundamental knowledge of quantum matter while providing benchmarks for experimental platforms in ultracold atomic systems and solid-state devices. Successful execution requires dedicated allocations of GPU nodes for tensor operations and CPU cores for ensemble averaging, with an estimated 250,000 node-hours to complete the proposed simulations. This work bridges critical theoretical gaps in quantum statistical mechanics and demonstrates how scalable computational resources can unlock new regimes of exploration in strongly interacting systems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of matter and energy, and the formulation and testing of the laws governing the behavior of the matter-energy continuum. Includes instruction in classical and modern physics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, mechanics, wave properties, nuclear processes, relativity and quantum theory, quantitative methods, and laboratory methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical evolution of ethical frameworks in medical decision-making by analyzing large-scale, multilingual corpora of primary sources spanning religious texts, philosophical treatises, medical literature, and patient narratives from 1600–1950. While qualitative scholarship has explored localized case studies, there remains a critical gap in systematically mapping how cultural, spiritual, and scientific values intersected to shape care practices across temporal and geographic boundaries. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to process over 10 million pages of digitized materials through natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical language variants and OCR imperfections. Custom transformer models will classify ethical themes (e.g., autonomy, beneficence, sanctity of life) while tracking semantic shifts in key terms like “healing,” “suffering,” and “duty” across epochs. Graph neural networks will model the diffusion of ideas between medical, religious, and literary communities. By integrating computational text analysis with hermeneutic frameworks from health humanities, this work aims to 1) identify previously unrecognized patterns in the prioritization of ethical principles during major medical paradigm shifts, 2) map how colonial exchanges and technological innovations reconfigured value systems, and 3) generate publicly accessible annotated datasets bridging historical context with modern AI/ML workflows. The scale and linguistic complexity of the corpus necessitate HPC resources for distributed training of domain-specific language models, large-scale sentiment and topic coherence analysis, and 3D visualization of concept networks across time. Outcomes will provide empirical foundations for contemporary debates on culturally responsive care while demonstrating methodological innovations for computational humanities. This interdisciplinary approach advances both health humanities scholarship and NLP techniques for historical texts, with implications for medical education, policy, and AI ethics.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: The development of advanced materials with tailored optoelectronic and mechanical properties is critical for next-generation photonic devices and molecular electronics. However, the rational design of such materials—particularly hybrid organic-inorganic systems and semiconductor nanowires—is hindered by the complexity of predicting how nanoscale structural features, such as interfacial bonding, defects, or lattice strain, influence macroscopic behavior. Experimental trial-and-error approaches remain costly and time-intensive, while existing computational models often lack the resolution or scalability to address multiscale phenomena. This project seeks to overcome these limitations through high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulations to map structure-property relationships in two target systems: (1) self-assembled molecular arrays for chemical sensing and (2) gallium nitride (GaN) nanowires with engineered dopant profiles for enhanced optoelectronic efficiency. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations will parameterize electronic interactions and defect energetics, while machine-learned interatomic potentials will enable large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess thermal stability and strain propagation. These methods will be integrated with evolutionary algorithms to screen >10,000 candidate configurations for optimal charge transport, optical absorption, and mechanical resilience. The scale of these simulations—requiring thousands of concurrent cores for MD trajectories exceeding 100 ns and DFT models with >1,000 atoms—necessitates HPC resources. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for doping strategies in GaN nanowires to minimize non-radiative recombination and design rules for π-conjugated molecular assemblies to amplify sensor response times. Results will directly guide experimental synthesis efforts at our collaborator’s lab, accelerating the development of materials for energy-efficient photodetectors and high-sensitivity chemical sensor arrays. By bridging atomic-scale insights with device-level performance, this work aims to establish a computational pipeline for materials discovery that reduces reliance on empirical approaches.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis and study of organic or inorganic materials and their electronic, magnetic, optical or mechanical properties. Includes instruction in advanced materials for photonics, lasers, chemical sensors and arrays or nanochemistry; semiconductor nanowires; and molecular electronics.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance precision medicine in pediatric gastroenterology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-modal datasets from children with digestive disorders. Chronic abdominal pain, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and biliary atresia represent significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their heterogeneous presentations, poorly understood molecular mechanisms, and variable treatment responses. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, underscoring the need for patient-specific predictive models. This project will integrate genomic, metabolomic, microbiome, and electronic health record data from a multicenter cohort of 2,500 patients to identify subtype-specific biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Computational challenges include processing whole-genome sequencing data, resolving high-dimensional interactions between host genetics and gut microbial communities, and training machine learning models to predict disease progression or complications like stricturing Crohn’s disease. HPC resources will enable genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with gene-environment interaction terms, longitudinal microbiome trajectory modeling via Bayesian hierarchical frameworks, and dynamic simulations of mucosal immune-metabolic networks. A key innovation involves developing federated learning pipelines to preserve patient privacy while aggregating data across institutions. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for stratifying patients into molecularly defined subgroups, (2) validated predictive algorithms for treatment response (e.g., anti-TNF therapy in IBD), and (3) mechanistic insights into microbiome-host crosstalk in biliary atresia pathogenesis. By addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in multi-omics integration, this work will directly inform the design of targeted clinical trials and personalized monitoring strategies, ultimately reducing diagnostic delays and improving outcomes for children with complex gastrointestinal conditions. The requested resources will support containerized workflows for scalable data processing, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-scale parameter sweeps for mechanistic model optimization.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the digestive systems of infants, children, and adolescents; includes treatment of conditions such as abdominal pain, ulcers, diarrhea, cancer, and jaundice, and performance of complex diagnostic and therapeutic procedures using lighted scopes to see internal organs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in organizational decision-making under complex, dynamic environments. A critical challenge in business administration lies in optimizing strategic and operational decisions when faced with incomplete information, rapidly shifting market conditions, and interdependencies among stakeholders. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the scale, nonlinearity, and stochasticity inherent in such scenarios, limiting their predictive accuracy and practical utility. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-agent simulation framework integrated with machine learning (ML) techniques to model decision-making processes across hierarchical organizational structures. The computational approach will involve large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate risk propagation, resource allocation efficiency, and emergent network behaviors under varying constraints. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be deployed to train adaptive decision policies, while graph neural networks will analyze interdependencies among departments, suppliers, and customers. The HPC environment is essential to manage the parallel processing demands of simulating thousands of agents with heterogeneous behavioral rules, as well as to support the iterative training of ML models on synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., supply chain logs, financial transaction records). Expected outcomes include actionable insights into resilience-building strategies for organizations, data-driven frameworks for real-time decision support, and scalable benchmarks for evaluating management policies. By quantifying trade-offs between centralized and decentralized decision architectures, this research aims to contribute novel methodologies to management theory while providing practitioners with tools to enhance operational agility. The project aligns with broader priorities in business administration, including sustainable resource use, crisis response optimization, and adaptive leadership strategies in volatile markets.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, organize, direct, and control the functions and processes of a firm or organization. Includes instruction in management theory, human resources management and behavior, accounting and other quantitative methods, purchasing and logistics, organization and production, marketing, and business decision-making.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving cultural narratives and transnational identity formation within Latinx digital communities, with a focus on Mexican-American/Chicano and Puerto Rican diasporas. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital platforms—including social media, bilingual digital archives, and community-driven storytelling initiatives—shape collective memory, linguistic hybridity, and resistance practices among these populations. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of multilingual, multimedia data produced daily across decentralized online spaces. This project will employ computational text analysis, image recognition, and network mapping to examine over 10TB of curated data from public forums, digitized oral histories, and visual art collections. Natural language processing (NLP) models will be fine-tuned to detect code-switching patterns and semantic shifts in Spanglish/Espanglish corpora, while computer vision algorithms will analyze iconography in digital murals and protest art to trace transnational cultural motifs. Graph-based methods will map intercommunity knowledge exchange across U.S. and Caribbean/Latin American nodes. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of heterogeneous data types and iterative model training, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include: 1) a publicly accessible annotated dataset of diasporic digital cultural production; 2) network models revealing how decentralized communities sustain shared identity amid geographic dispersion; and 3) computational frameworks for ethically engaged analysis of marginalized digital spaces. By centering Latinx epistemologies in its technical design, this work advances culturally responsive digital humanities methodologies while preserving community agency over data interpretation. Results will inform pedagogical tools for heritage studies programs and support advocacy organizations in documenting cultural resilience strategies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Hispanic-American, Puerto Rican, Latinx, and Mexican-American/ Chicano Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic American immigrant populations within the U.S. and Canada, including Mexican-American Studies, Cuban American Studies, Puerto Rican Studies, and others.

abstract: Law enforcement intelligence analysis faces escalating challenges due to the exponential growth of heterogeneous data sources, including financial records, digital communications, surveillance footage, and geospatial data. Traditional analytical tools struggle to integrate and process these datasets efficiently, leading to delays in actionable insights and operational planning. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for real-time, multimodal intelligence analysis. The research will focus on optimizing the integration of structured and unstructured data, enhancing predictive modeling of criminal networks, and automating compliance checks with legal and regulatory standards. Key computational challenges include scaling graph-based link analysis to identify covert relationships, processing geospatial data for dynamic threat mapping, and training machine learning models on encrypted or sensitive datasets without compromising evidentiary integrity. The project will leverage distributed computing architectures to parallelize data ingestion, employ GPU-accelerated deep learning for pattern recognition in multimedia evidence, and implement privacy-preserving federated learning techniques for cross-agency collaboration. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform capable of processing petabytes of multimodal law enforcement data, reducing case resolution times by enabling real-time analytics, and improving the accuracy of predictive policing models through high-fidelity simulations of criminal network dynamics. By validating the framework against historical case data from partner agencies, this research aims to establish benchmarks for computational efficiency and legal admissibility in intelligence workflows. The resulting tools will provide law enforcement personnel with enhanced decision-support capabilities while ensuring compliance with constitutional and procedural safeguards, directly contributing to public safety and the ethical advancement of intelligence-driven policing.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the preparation of law enforcement personnel to perform intelligence and surveillance operations and to analyze and use data collected via such operations. Includes instruction in the intelligence cycle, information sources, data retrieval, digital investigation, financial investigations, document analysis, external sources, geographic information systems, link analysis, operation planning and security, case management, applicable law and regulations, and case preparation.

abstract: Mental health disorders present complex challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, heterogeneous symptom profiles, and variable treatment responses. Current approaches to predicting disease trajectories or optimizing personalized interventions are limited by the inability to integrate high-dimensional data—including neuroimaging, genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and socio-environmental datasets—into unified computational models. This project seeks to address this gap by developing machine learning frameworks to analyze multi-modal mental health data, with the goal of identifying predictive biomarkers, stratifying risk, and informing precision nursing interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets from regional healthcare systems and national psychiatric cohorts, encompassing over 50,000 patients with depression, schizophrenia, and substance use disorders. Computational workflows will include deep learning architectures (e.g., graph neural networks for neuroimaging connectomics, natural language processing for clinical notes) and ensemble methods to model interactions between biological, psychological, and social determinants. A key innovation involves federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy while aggregating data across institutions. The project also incorporates dynamic simulations of crisis intervention scenarios to evaluate resource allocation strategies for acute psychiatric care. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for relapse risk and treatment resistance, which will be translated into clinical decision support tools for psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners. By enabling real-time analysis of complex datasets, HPC resources are critical to overcoming computational bottlenecks in training these models and ensuring scalability to diverse populations. This work advances nursing science by establishing a data-driven framework to personalize care planning, reduce trial-and-error prescribing, and mitigate mental health disparities. The resulting open-source tools and models will be disseminated to the nursing research community to foster collaborative innovation in mental health informatics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to promote mental health and provide nursing care to patients with mental, emotional or behavioral disorders, in mental institutions or other settings. Includes instruction in psychopathology, behavioral health, counseling and intervention strategies, psychoeducation, mental health assessment and dual diagnosis, stabilization and management of psychotic illness, psychiatric care and rehabilitation, substance abuse, and crisis intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing demand for computationally intensive processes in the creation and optimization of dynamic, data-driven commercial art. Contemporary advertising design increasingly relies on generative algorithms, real-time rendering of high-fidelity 3D graphics, and large-scale analysis of consumer engagement patterns—tasks that exceed the capabilities of standard workstations. The research focuses on developing a framework for simulating hybrid digital-physical media workflows, integrating machine learning models trained on consumer response datasets with physics-based simulations of traditional printmaking techniques (e.g., lithography, silkscreen). By deploying GPU-accelerated neural networks, we aim to automate the iterative refinement of advertising content across multiple platforms while preserving the tactile qualities associated with manual artistic processes. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of high-resolution asset libraries (>8K textures), real-time style transfer across heterogeneous media formats, and predictive modeling of cross-cultural aesthetic preferences using terabyte-scale visual corpora. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for parametric design adaptation, reducing production timelines for multi-channel campaigns by 40–60%, and quantitative models correlating computational design variables with audience retention metrics. This work bridges gaps between traditional visual arts pedagogy and emerging computational demands in advertising, enabling artists to scale handcrafted aesthetics for global digital markets while maintaining creative intent. The requested HPC resources will specifically support distributed rendering workloads, hyperparameter optimization for generative adversarial networks (GANs), and large-scale A/B testing of AI-generated design variants through cloud-based consumer panels.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via illustrations and other forms of digital or printed media. Includes instruction in concept design, layout, paste-up, and techniques such as engraving, etching, silkscreen, lithography, offset, drawing and cartooning, painting, collage, and computer graphics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the impact of teacher pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) on student outcomes in secondary mathematics education, using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets. While prior research has established correlations between teacher knowledge and student achievement, the mechanisms underlying these relationships remain poorly quantified, particularly for advanced mathematical concepts such as algebraic reasoning and calculus foundations. The research problem centers on identifying scalable, data-driven predictors of effective mathematics teaching practices and their dynamic interactions with student cognition. We propose a mixed-methods computational approach integrating three components: (1) agent-based modeling of classroom discourse patterns derived from natural language processing (NLP) of lesson transcripts, (2) hierarchical Bayesian networks trained on longitudinal student assessment data, and (3) network analysis of teacher professional development trajectories using state-level administrative records. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of over 2.5 TB of structured and unstructured data from 300+ classrooms, including video annotations, standardized test results, and teacher licensure histories. Computational challenges include real-time simulation of student-teacher interaction matrices and variational inference for high-dimensional parameter spaces in Bayesian models. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for optimizing mathematics teacher training interventions, with particular attention to equity in resource allocation across diverse school districts. The models will generate actionable insights about critical leverage points in teacher education programs, such as the relative impact of content-focused pedagogy courses versus classroom mentoring experiences. By establishing quantitative links between specific components of teacher preparation and student learning gains, this work aims to inform data-driven policy decisions in mathematics education while advancing computational methodologies for educational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach mathematics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing personalized ophthalmic lens and frame design using advanced computational modeling to improve visual outcomes and patient comfort in populations with complex anatomical or optical needs. Current methods for fitting corrective eyewear rely on generalized measurements and manual adjustments, which may fail to account for subtle variations in facial asymmetry, tissue biomechanics, or dynamic interactions between lenses, frames, and anatomical structures during prolonged wear. We propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity biomechanical simulations of facial soft tissue deformation, optical ray-tracing models, and machine learning to predict optimal lens positioning and frame geometry tailored to individual patients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the execution of finite element analysis (FEA) models incorporating anatomically accurate 3D facial scans, material properties of frame components, and lens prescriptions to simulate pressure distribution, slippage patterns, and optical performance under real-world conditions. Concurrently, a deep neural network trained on a synthetic dataset of virtual fittings will accelerate the identification of design parameters that minimize visual distortion while maintaining comfort. The project will validate predictions against clinical data from 200 patients with challenging fitting requirements, including post-surgical craniofacial anatomy and high-prescription myopia with astigmatism. Outcomes will include an open-source computational toolkit for opticians to simulate and visualize fitting outcomes prior to fabrication, reducing iterative adjustments and material waste. By bridging ophthalmic optics, soft tissue biomechanics, and computational engineering, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in precision opticianry, enhancing both clinical efficiency and patient-specific optical correction. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space and multi-physics simulations inherent to this personalized approach.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: Agricultural Teacher Education faces growing demands to integrate data-driven agricultural practices into vocational curricula, yet educators often lack accessible tools to model complex agroecosystems or analyze real-world agricultural datasets in classroom settings. This project seeks to develop a computational platform enabling instructors to simulate crop management scenarios, analyze precision agriculture data, and visualize outcomes for pedagogical use. The research problem centers on bridging the gap between rapidly evolving computational agricultural practices and the technical capacity of vocational educators to teach these concepts effectively. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to construct scalable models of crop growth, soil health dynamics, and climate interactions using machine learning algorithms and agent-based simulations. These models will process heterogeneous datasets—including satellite imagery, sensor networks, and historical yield records—to generate region-specific case studies for instructional design. Computational workflows will optimize parameter space exploration for diverse farming scenarios while maintaining interpretability for non-specialist educators. Expected outcomes include an open-access web interface that allows teachers to adjust simulation parameters, visualize multi-year agricultural outcomes, and export lesson-ready datasets. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform vocational agricultural education by equipping instructors with research-grade computational tools tailored to classroom needs, thereby enhancing student competencies in data-driven decision-making. Successful implementation requires HPC resources to handle concurrent simulations across multiple geographic contexts, high-resolution climate modeling, and training neural networks on agricultural time-series data. This work aligns with national priorities for modernizing agricultural education while explicitly avoiding administrative or general education research foci to maintain alignment with teacher training objectives in technical agriculture.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational agricultural programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural transmission and adaptation among Arctic Indigenous communities through the computational analysis of multilingual textual archives, oral histories, and ethnographic records. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital representations of cultural knowledge intersect with contemporary identity formation in rapidly changing Arctic social-ecological systems. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for low-resource languages to analyze a corpus of over 500,000 pages of digitized materials spanning seven Indigenous languages and three colonial languages. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to identify patterns in intergenerational knowledge transfer, semantic shifts in cultural concepts, and multimodal relationships between textual narratives and visual cultural symbols. Spatial-temporal analysis will map the diffusion of cultural practices across 23 Arctic communities using graph neural networks, incorporating historical climate data and land-use records. The computational workflow requires distributed memory parallelism for large-scale semantic clustering and GPU acceleration for deep learning tasks involving high-dimensional embeddings of linguistic and visual data. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative framework for assessing cultural resilience thresholds in Arctic populations, a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking cultural artifacts to community-specific ontologies, and methodological advances in computational cultural studies. Results will inform collaborative heritage preservation initiatives while adhering to Indigenous data sovereignty principles. The requested resources are essential for processing heterogeneous data at scales unachievable through conventional methods, enabling novel insights into how Arctic communities maintain cultural continuity amid environmental and technological transformations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Arctic region.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in the preservation, classification, and accessibility of large-scale multimedia archival collections within digital libraries. As libraries increasingly digitize diverse materials—including historical texts, images, audio recordings, and video—existing cataloging systems struggle to manage the volume, variety, and complexity of these unstructured datasets. Traditional manual or semi-automated methods are prohibitively slow, error-prone, and ill-equipped to handle multilingual or multimodal content. The research problem centers on developing scalable computational workflows to automate metadata extraction, semantic tagging, and cross-referencing across heterogeneous archival formats, enabling libraries to optimize resource allocation and enhance user access. The computational approach integrates machine learning (ML) models, including transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for text analysis, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image and video recognition, and graph-based algorithms to map contextual relationships within and between collections. These models will be deployed on HPC clusters to parallelize training across GPU nodes, process petabytes of data efficiently, and support real-time inference for dynamic querying. The project will also explore federated learning techniques to maintain data privacy across collaborating institutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive archival management, validated on digitized collections from partner libraries, which reduces manual curation labor by an estimated 60–80% while improving search accuracy and cross-collection discoverability. By enabling libraries to manage rapidly expanding digital assets effectively, this work aims to democratize access to cultural heritage materials, support interdisciplinary research in humanities and education, and establish scalable precedents for computational resource allocation in library science. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the computational intensity of multimodal ML training, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale data integration tasks inherent to this domain.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interplay between community support networks, resource allocation strategies, and family resilience outcomes in underserved populations. While traditional social services research relies on qualitative assessments or small-scale quantitative surveys, this work addresses a critical gap: the inability to simulate complex, multi-layered interactions between policy interventions, socioeconomic variables, and longitudinal family outcomes at scale. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with machine learning, we will create a high-fidelity simulation environment that captures heterogeneous family units, community organizations, and environmental stressors across urban and rural contexts. The computational approach leverages anonymized administrative data from 12 regional service providers (spanning housing, healthcare, and education) alongside demographic datasets to parameterize agents representing families, social workers, and institutions. Key technical challenges include optimizing parallelized simulations of 100,000+ agent interactions, implementing adaptive decision trees for service utilization patterns, and validating models against longitudinal outcome studies through probabilistic sensitivity analysis. By employing high-performance computing resources, we aim to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in modeling stochastic social behaviors across multi-year timescales. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to identify optimal intervention timing in family crisis cycles, quantify resource distribution trade-offs under budget constraints, and simulate emergent effects of policy changes on community-level well-being metrics. This work establishes a novel methodology for evidence-based decision-making in family services, bridging computational social science with practical resource allocation challenges while maintaining strict ethical safeguards for data privacy and algorithmic transparency.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and implementation of public, private, and voluntary support services for individuals, families, and localities and that prepares individuals to function in a variety of occupations promoting family life, and family/community development. Includes instruction in family systems, human development, social services, community social and economic development, social policy, voluntary sector activities, and outreach and community education.

abstract: Urban horticulture systems face unique challenges due to spatial constraints, heterogeneous microclimates, pollution exposure, and soil degradation in cities, which limit crop productivity and ecological resilience. Current models for optimizing urban horticulture practices lack the resolution to account for dynamic interactions between plant physiology, soil biogeochemistry, and built-environment factors at scale. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate urban horticultural ecosystems and identify strategies that maximize yield, nutrient efficiency, and environmental sustainability. We will integrate geospatial data, multi-omics datasets from urban crop varieties, and IoT sensor feeds capturing real-time soil-air-water conditions across Los Angeles community gardens.
