The requested resources are essential for handling memory-intensive NLP tasks, training domain-specific language models, and ensuring reproducibility across heterogeneous archival sources.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, related borderlands and island groups, and including emigrant and immigrant groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize real-time biomechanical feedback systems for wearable assistive devices used in neuromuscular rehabilitation. Patients with acquired mobility impairments (e.g., post-stroke or spinal cord injury) often rely on sensor-augmented orthoses or exoskeletons to regain functional movement, but current systems lack adaptive responsiveness to physiological fatigue, tissue stress, or compensatory movement patterns. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational limitations of existing edge devices, which cannot process high-resolution electromyography (EMG), inertial measurement unit (IMU), and pressure sensor data streams while simultaneously running personalized biomechanical models. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining federated learning for patient-specific movement pattern recognition and finite element modeling (FEM) to simulate soft tissue strain under dynamic loading conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for two phases: (1) training deep neural networks on aggregated, anonymized movement datasets from heterogeneous patient populations, and (2) running iterative FEM simulations to establish safe torque thresholds for assistive actuators across anatomical variations. The pipeline will integrate GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition for real-time sensor fusion and surrogate modeling to reduce FEM computational costs by 85-90% for embedded deployment. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive assistive device control that dynamically balances mobility restoration with injury prevention, validated through digital twin simulations of 500+ unique musculoskeletal anatomies. This work bridges gaps between clinical rehabilitation practice, biomechatronics, and computational physiology, offering a paradigm shift in personalized assistive technology development while addressing critical HPC challenges in edge-cloud co-processing for medical IoT systems.
cip_title: Allied Health and Medical Assisting Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health and medical assisting services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Immunopathologic disorders, including autoimmune diseases and transplant rejection, involve complex, dynamic interactions between immune cells, signaling pathways, and host tissues that remain incompletely understood. Current clinical strategies for diagnosis and immunotherapy often lack precision due to the heterogeneous nature of these conditions and the limitations of reductionist experimental models. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing multi-scale computational models of immune dysregulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate molecular, cellular, and systemic interactions in immunologic diseases. We will integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data from patient-derived samples, proteomic profiles of inflammatory mediators, and clinical metadata to construct agent-based models (ABMs) of autoimmune effector responses and allograft rejection dynamics. These simulations will map spatial and temporal patterns of immune cell infiltration, cytokine crosstalk, and tissue damage under varying therapeutic interventions. A parallelized computational pipeline will employ machine learning to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response from high-dimensional datasets, enabling patient stratification. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of these models, which involve >10^6 interacting cellular agents and stochastic simulations across parameter spaces encompassing genetic, epigenetic, and environmental variables. Expected outcomes include: (1) mechanistic insights into failure modes of current immunotherapies, (2) in silico optimization of combination therapies targeting checkpoint inhibitors and cytokine networks, and (3) predictive algorithms for graft survival timelines in transplant recipients. The models will be validated against longitudinal clinical datasets from collaborating transplant centers and autoimmune disease registries. By bridging molecular mechanisms with clinical phenotypes through large-scale simulation, this work aims to establish computational frameworks for personalized immunotherapy design and real-time treatment adaptation, directly addressing the program’s focus on advancing diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in immunopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment and laboratory management of immunologic diseases. Includes instruction in diagnostic surgical pathology, management of organ transplantation and immunotherapy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational frameworks to model emergent properties in complex biological networks, with a focus on systems-level interactions that cannot be adequately captured by reductionist experimental approaches. A critical challenge in computational biology is the integration of multi-omics datasets (e.g., transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic) into predictive models that account for nonlinear dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and stochasticity in cellular systems. Current tools struggle with scalability and parameter estimation for large-scale networks, limiting their utility in uncovering system-wide regulatory mechanisms. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining stochastic differential equation (SDE) modeling, agent-based simulations, and machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization. The SDE framework will model global biochemical reaction networks, while agent-based methods will simulate spatially resolved cellular microenvironments. ML algorithms, including variational autoencoders and Bayesian neural networks, will enable efficient parameter inference from noisy, high-dimensional datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational complexity: stochastic simulations across parameter spaces will require parallelized workflows on GPU-accelerated nodes, and ML training will leverage distributed computing for hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for scalable, multi-scale biological network modeling, (2) novel insights into feedback mechanisms driving metabolic adaptation in stress-response pathways, and (3) a publicly accessible database of pre-trained ML models for parameter estimation in diverse biological contexts. This work will advance computational methodologies for systems biology, providing a foundation for predicting emergent behaviors in synthetic biology applications and disease states. The requested HPC allocation will directly support large-scale simulations (>10^6 CPU core-hours), distributed data storage for petabyte-scale outputs, and real-time analytics pipelines to iteratively refine models against experimental data from collaborating labs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computational theoretical approaches to understanding biological systems, including computational models of biological processes, computational management of large-scale projects, database development and data-algorithm development, and high-performance computing, as well as statistical and mathematical analyses.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the critical challenge of improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in surgical pathology through the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven computational framework for automated analysis of complex histopathological images. Pathologist Assistants (PAs) play a vital role in tissue specimen processing and preliminary diagnosis, but manual microscopic evaluation remains time-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability, particularly in borderline or rare cases. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate deep learning models on a curated dataset of whole-slide images (WSIs) encompassing diverse neoplastic and non-neoplastic conditions. The computational pipeline will integrate convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers to identify morphological patterns, quantify cellular features, and correlate these with clinical outcomes. Key innovations include the development of a hybrid model architecture optimized for multi-scale feature extraction from gigapixel WSIs and the integration of weakly supervised learning to mitigate annotation bottlenecks. Computational workflows will be designed to align with PA workflows, emphasizing interpretability through attention mapping and uncertainty quantification. Expected outcomes include a scalable AI tool to assist PAs in rapid specimen triage, anomaly detection, and quantification of diagnostically relevant biomarkers. The project will further contribute novel open-source datasets annotated with PA-relevant diagnostic criteria. By reducing repetitive analytical tasks and enhancing precision in tissue assessment, this research has the potential to transform pathological practice, accelerate diagnostic throughput, and improve patient outcomes in oncological and non-oncological surgical contexts. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities for distributed training across GPU nodes, large-scale image preprocessing, and validation against multi-institutional data—resources beyond typical clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pathologists, to assist in the performance of autopsies, obtaining and preparing surgical specimens, preparing autopsy reports, and interacting with other clinicians, officials, and individuals. Includes instruction in anatomy; physiology; medical terminology; general, systemic, forensic, and pediatric pathology; autopsy procedures; surgical technique; medical photography; tissue preparation; record keeping and laboratory administration; interpersonal skills; and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized, data-driven interventions in occupational therapy (OT). A critical challenge in OT practice lies in efficiently integrating complex, multi-modal datasets—including clinical assessments, sensor-based movement analytics, environmental scans, and patient-reported outcomes—to design interventions tailored to individual needs. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model the dynamic interactions between patient-specific factors (e.g., motor control, cognitive load) and environmental contexts, limiting the precision and scalability of therapeutic solutions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning, biomechanical simulation, and agent-based modeling. Large-scale datasets from wearable sensors, electronic health records, and 3D environmental mappings will be processed to train predictive models identifying optimal intervention parameters for diverse patient populations. Finite element simulations will evaluate stress distributions in assistive devices under real-world usage scenarios, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize adaptive strategies for environmental modifications. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of these tasks, particularly for parallel processing of high-resolution movement data, iterative optimization of multi-objective models, and real-time rendering of immersive virtual environments for patient testing. Expected outcomes include validated computational tools to predict intervention efficacy, reduce trial-and-error in device customization, and simulate the longitudinal impacts of environmental adaptations on patient independence. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making, enhance the evidence base for OT practices, and accelerate the translation of research into scalable technologies that improve quality of life for individuals with functional limitations. By bridging computational innovation and therapeutic practice, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for precision rehabilitation in occupational therapy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist patients limited by physical, cognitive, psychosocial, mental, developmental, and learning disabilities, as well as adverse environmental conditions, to maximize their independence and maintain optimum health through a planned mix of acquired skills, performance motivation, environmental adaptations, assistive technologies, and physical agents. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, psychology, sociology, patient assessment and evaluation, standardized and non-standardized tests and measurements, assistive and rehabilitative technologies, ergonomics, environmental health, special education, vocational counseling, health education and promotion, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and behavioral correlates of art creation as a precursor to therapeutic intervention, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets. While art therapy is recognized for its clinical potential, the mechanisms by which preparatory art-making activities—such as those in pre-art therapy curricula—influence emotional regulation and cognitive processing remain poorly quantified. Current studies lack integrative frameworks to model the dynamic interplay between biometric signals, creative output, and self-reported psychological states. To address this gap, we propose a computational study combining electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, motion-capture data, and semantic analysis of art products generated by participants during structured pre-therapeutic exercises. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in high-dimensional data that predict transitions from stress states to cognitive flexibility, a hypothesized precursor to therapeutic readiness. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of temporal biometric data (e.g., 256-channel EEG sampled at 1 kHz across 100+ participants) alongside computer vision analysis of art products using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Graph-based models will map relationships between physiological markers, gaze patterns, brushstroke kinematics, and emergent symbolic content in artworks. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated pipeline for fusing heterogeneous art therapy-relevant datasets, (2) predictive models linking specific art-making behaviors to neurodynamic signatures of emotional regulation, and (3) visualization tools to annotate therapeutic progressions in multidimensional parameter space. This work will establish quantitative foundations for optimizing pre-art therapy training protocols while advancing computational methods for studying embodied creative cognition. By situating art-based interventions within a systems neuroscience framework, the project bridges health sciences, affective computing, and visual cognition—offering novel infrastructure for personalized mental health strategies that precede formal clinical art therapy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in predicting reaction pathways and selectivity for complex organic transformations involving transient intermediates and solvent-dependent dynamics. Despite advances in synthetic organic chemistry, the mechanistic understanding of multi-step reactions—particularly those involving radical species, zwitterionic intermediates, or solvent-caged interactions—remains limited, hampering the rational design of efficient catalytic systems and sustainable synthetic routes. We propose a computational strategy combining density functional theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and machine learning (ML) to map free energy landscapes, characterize short-lived intermediates, and quantify solvent effects on reaction trajectories. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the scale of these simulations, which involve thousands of conformational samplings for solvated systems, non-adiabatic transitions in photochemical processes, and ensemble-based uncertainty quantification for ML-predicted reaction outcomes. The study will focus on two model systems: (1) stereoselective cycloadditions mediated by chiral organocatalysts, where solvent polarity modulates transition state stabilization, and (2) nickel-catalyzed C–H functionalization reactions, where competing oxidative addition pathways depend on ligand dynamics and solvent coordination. By integrating explicit solvation models with enhanced sampling techniques, we aim to resolve long-standing discrepancies between experimental yields and computational predictions. The resulting datasets will train graph neural networks to predict solvent-catalyst-reactivity relationships, enabling rapid screening of reaction conditions. This work will advance fundamental knowledge of dynamic effects in organic reactivity while providing open-access tools for optimizing green chemistry protocols and pharmaceutical synthesis. The requested computing resources will directly support parameterization efforts for industrially relevant transformations, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in catalyst design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of hydrocarbon compounds and their derivatives. Includes instruction in molecular conversion and synthesis, molecular synthesis and design, the molecular structure of living cells and systems, the mutual reactivity of organic and inorganic compounds in combination, the spectroscopic analysis of hydrocarbon compounds, and applications to specific problems in research, industry, and health.

abstract: Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of cancer treatment, yet optimizing the balance between tumor control and healthy tissue sparing requires highly precise, patient-specific modeling of radiation interactions with biological systems. Current limitations in computational power restrict the resolution and complexity of such models, particularly when integrating multi-scale radiobiological effects, dynamic treatment responses, and real-time adaptive planning. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational framework for simulating ionizing radiation delivery and its biological impacts at unprecedented spatial, temporal, and mechanistic detail. The research will employ Monte Carlo methods to model radiation transport through heterogeneous tissues, capturing secondary particle interactions and dose deposition with sub-millimeter accuracy. Concurrently, a coupled radiobiological model will simulate cellular responses to radiation, incorporating DNA damage kinetics, repair pathways, and microenvironmental factors such as hypoxia. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize beam configurations and fractionation schedules based on these simulations, while finite element analysis will predict mechanical changes in tumors and organs at risk during treatment. The HPC environment is critical for managing the extreme computational load of these interconnected models, which involve terabytes of imaging data, stochastic simulations with >10^9 particle histories, and iterative optimization across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for estimating tumor control probabilities and normal tissue complication risks under diverse radiotherapy scenarios, as well as open-source algorithms for automated, biologically guided treatment planning. This work directly addresses the clinical need for personalized, biologically informed radiation regimens and has the potential to reduce toxicities while improving local control rates in cancers with complex anatomic or radiobiological challenges. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as a foundation for future studies exploring novel radiation modalities and combination therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of ionizing radiation to treat patients with cancer and other diseases. Includes instruction in treatment planning, instrument design and operation, radiation physics and radiobiology. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing dynamic production systems in manufacturing environments, addressing the challenge of balancing efficiency, cost, and resilience under stochastic demand and supply chain disruptions. Traditional operations management approaches often rely on static models or simplified heuristics that fail to capture the interdependencies between production scheduling, inventory management, equipment maintenance, and workforce allocation in complex, multi-stage systems. We propose a multi-method simulation approach integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and reinforcement learning to analyze emergent system behaviors under variable operating conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across realistic production scenarios, train machine learning models on heterogeneous operational data streams, and validate optimization policies through computationally intensive Monte Carlo simulations. The computational workflow will model plant floor operations at granular temporal resolutions (sub-minute intervals) while incorporating macro-level variables such as supplier lead times and market demand volatility. Expected outcomes include (1) adaptive scheduling algorithms that minimize downtime during equipment failures or material shortages, (2) predictive maintenance policies optimized for total cost of ownership, and (3) decision-support tools for capacity planning under uncertainty. Results will advance both theoretical understanding of complex production systems and practical implementation of Industry 4.0 strategies, with particular significance for small-to-medium manufacturers lacking resources for physical prototyping. The computational infrastructure will enable sensitivity analyses across 10,000+ scenario variations, substantially exceeding the capabilities of desktop-scale optimization tools. By quantifying tradeoffs between lean manufacturing principles and buffer stock requirements in turbulent environments, this work aims to establish evidence-based guidelines for resilient operations management in the post-pandemic supply chain landscape.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and direct the physical and/or technical functions of a firm or organization, particularly those relating to development, production, and manufacturing. Includes instruction in principles of general management, manufacturing and production systems, plant management, equipment maintenance management, production control, industrial labor relations and skilled trades supervision, strategic manufacturing policy, systems analysis, productivity analysis and cost control, and materials planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of microbial dynamics in complex food matrices, addressing critical gaps in food safety and preservation. Foodborne pathogens and spoilage microorganisms pose significant risks to public health and economic stability, yet current predictive models often fail to account for the heterogeneous physicochemical conditions within multi-component food systems. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and cannot rapidly explore the vast parameter space of microbial interactions with variable moisture, pH, temperature, and nutrient gradients. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM), and machine learning (ML) to simulate microbial growth, metabolite production, and cross-species competition in spatially resolved food environments. HPC resources will enable high-throughput simulations of microbial communities within 3D-reconstructed food matrices, parameterized using experimental data from microscopy and hyperspectral imaging. Parallelized workflows will assess the impact of processing variables (e.g., thermal treatments, antimicrobial delivery systems) on microbial resilience. ML algorithms will identify emergent patterns in simulation outputs to refine predictive accuracy and guide targeted experimental validation. Expected outcomes include a validated computational platform for optimizing food processing parameters, reducing spoilage-related waste, and mitigating pathogen risks. This work will provide novel insights into microenvironmental drivers of microbial behavior, directly supporting the development of safer, more sustainable food preservation strategies. By bridging computational and experimental food science, the project aims to establish scalable methodologies for predictive microbiology, with translational benefits for industry and regulatory decision-making.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in food sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators serving students with speech or language impairments. A critical challenge in this field is the dynamic, individualized nature of language development and intervention efficacy. Traditional methods for designing and adjusting individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual observation and static assessment data, limiting educators’ ability to predict student progress or optimize interventions in real time. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale linguistic datasets, longitudinal student performance records, and machine learning (ML) models to simulate and predict language acquisition patterns under varying intervention strategies. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze speech samples from students with diverse impairments (e.g., phonological disorders, aphasia) and generate synthetically augmented training data to account for low-resource scenarios. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models, will be trained to identify subtle patterns in language development trajectories and correlate them with intervention outcomes. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments to test the scalability of personalized strategies under resource constraints. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of audio and textual data, train complex ML models with hyperparameter optimization, and run high-fidelity simulations iteratively. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access toolset for educators to dynamically adjust IEP targets based on predictive analytics, (2) a repository of anonymized speech datasets with synthetic augmentations, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for deploying computational tools in special education settings. By bridging gaps between special education practice and computational innovation, this work aims to reduce IEP design latency, improve intervention personalization, and empower educators with scalable, equity-focused resources.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Speech or Language Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study and design of educational services for children or adults with speech and language impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with speech and language impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with speech disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing personalized care plans for individuals with developmental disabilities. Current approaches to designing interventions often rely on static, generalized protocols that inadequately account for the dynamic interplay of biological, behavioral, and environmental factors unique to each client. The research problem centers on overcoming computational barriers to analyzing heterogeneous datasets—including longitudinal behavioral logs, biometric sensor data, and socio-environmental context records—to generate adaptive, real-time recommendations for caregivers. The computational approach integrates machine learning techniques, such as federated learning for privacy-preserving data aggregation and transformer-based models for temporal pattern recognition in unstructured caregiver notes. Agent-based simulations will model the cascading effects of intervention adjustments across client-caregiver ecosystems, requiring parallelized computation to iteratively test hypotheses under diverse scenarios. By synthesizing data from distributed community service providers, this project aims to produce a scalable decision-support tool that identifies optimal intervention windows, predicts adverse behavioral outcomes, and prioritizes resource allocation for high-need clients. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for developmental services that balances ethical constraints (e.g., autonomy preservation) with operational efficiency gains. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the stochasticity inherent in human behavior modeling and enabling low-latency inference in real-world care settings. This work bridges gaps between disability studies, applied psychology, and computational social science, offering a template for data-driven innovation in non-clinical support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply practical knowledge and skills to support individuals with a variety of physical, mental or developmental disabilities in a family or community setting. Includes instruction in health care, basic nutrition, pharmacology, nursing, autism, mental health, psychology, sociology, behavioral analysis, communication, intervention, counseling and community services, and developmental services, such as literacy and life skills training.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of next-generation parametric design workflows in architectural technology, with a focus on optimizing building performance and construction efficiency. Traditional architectural design processes often rely on iterative, manual adjustments to balance aesthetic, structural, and environmental criteria—a time-intensive approach that limits exploration of complex design spaces. The proposed research addresses this bottleneck by integrating real-time physics-based simulations, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and multi-objective optimization algorithms into a unified computational framework. Key challenges include the need for parallelized evaluation of thousands of design variants under dynamic environmental conditions, as well as the training of AI models on heterogeneous datasets spanning material properties, climate profiles, and historical architectural precedents. The computational workflow will utilize distributed computing architectures to simultaneously analyze structural integrity (via finite element methods), energy efficiency (through computational fluid dynamics), and constructability (using automated rule-based systems) at urban-scale resolutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for AI-assisted architectural design that reduces simulation time by orders of magnitude compared to conventional software, enabling rapid prototyping of sustainable building solutions. This work bridges gaps between architectural practice, computational geometry, and environmental informatics, offering novel methodologies for data-driven design decision-making while maintaining fidelity to architectural intent. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive 3D model processing, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the integration of real-world sensor data from smart building systems into generative design pipelines. By democratizing access to advanced simulation capabilities typically restricted to engineering domains, this project aims to redefine technological workflows in architectural practice and education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist architects in developing plans and related documentation and in performing architectural office services. Includes instruction in architectural drafting, computer-assisted drafting and design, construction methods and materials, environmental systems, building codes and standards, structural principles, cost estimation, planning documentation, visual communication skills, display production, and architectural office management.

abstract: Hearing aid personalization remains a critical challenge in audiological rehabilitation, as conventional fitting protocols often rely on population-averaged prescriptive formulas that inadequately address individual variations in cochlear damage patterns, neural processing deficits, and listening environment demands. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating biophysical cochlear models with machine learning to optimize hearing aid parameter selection at the individual level. The research will address two core limitations: (1) current clinical tools lack the resolution to map specific cochlear pathologies to frequency-specific amplification needs, and (2) real-world listening environments introduce complex nonlinear interactions between amplified signals and residual auditory function that cannot be captured by threshold-based fitting approaches. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of cochlear mechanics using finite element models incorporating patient-specific otoacoustic emission data and histological patterns of hair cell loss. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on synthetic auditory nerve spiking patterns derived from these simulations to predict optimal gain-frequency responses across diverse noise environments. A multi-objective optimization layer will balance speech intelligibility metrics with perceptual comfort constraints derived from psychoacoustic models. The computational pipeline will be validated against electrophysiological data from human temporal bone specimens and behavioral outcomes from 120 clinical hearing aid users. By establishing quantitative relationships between cochlear microstructure, neural coding fidelity, and amplification benefits, this work aims to create the first patient-specific hearing aid optimization platform that adapts to both biological constraints and environmental acoustics. Successful implementation could reduce the trial-and-error period in hearing aid fittings by 40-60% while improving speech recognition scores in noisy environments by 15-20%, significantly advancing rehabilitation outcomes for individuals with sensorineural hearing loss.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to test the hearing of, and to select, fit and dispense appropriate hearing aids for, patients. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of the ear, hearing testing, hearing aid fitting and technology, health promotion and rehabilitation, counseling and communication, business management, and professional ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolving legal and administrative frameworks governing transnational religious institutions, with a focus on computational modeling of compliance strategies across heterogeneous jurisdictions. As religious organizations increasingly operate in globalized, digitally mediated contexts, they face complex challenges in harmonizing canon law, civil legal obligations, and organizational governance structures. The project addresses a critical gap in understanding how computational approaches can map tensions between religious autonomy and state regulations, particularly regarding data sovereignty, intellectual property management, and cross-border operational logistics. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the research will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze 150+ years of digitized ecclesiastical administrative records, international legal texts, and interfaith policy documents. Agent-based modeling will simulate decision-making processes in multi-jurisdictional scenarios, while graph neural networks will map historical patterns of conflict resolution and policy adaptation. Expected outcomes include 1) a computational framework for predicting regulatory friction points in religious administration, 2) quantitative analysis of successful mediation strategies across diverse legal systems, and 3) open-source tools for optimizing compliance workflows in faith-based institutions. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational social science, legal informatics, and organizational theory, offering novel insights into the digital transformation of religious governance structures. By quantifying previously qualitative aspects of canon-civil law interactions, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying institutional religiosity in computational humanities while providing practical resources for administrators navigating 21st-century legal landscapes. The scale of textual analysis and complexity of multi-agent simulations necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing of multilingual documents and real-time adaptation of governance models across parametric legal scenarios.
cip_title: Religious Institution Administration and Law, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious institution administration and law, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay of solvent effects and reaction mechanisms in multi-step organic transformations. A critical challenge in synthetic chemistry lies in predicting how solvation environments modulate reaction pathways, particularly for systems where competing transition states and solvent-solute interactions lead to divergent outcomes. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve these transient intermediates, while conventional computational models often oversimplify solvation effects or lack the accuracy required for predictive design. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) framework coupled with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations to map free-energy landscapes and solvent reorganization dynamics during key reaction steps. The study will focus on nucleophilic aromatic substitution and catalytic asymmetric cycloaddition reactions, where solvent polarity and hydrogen-bonding networks are hypothesized to control selectivity. The computational workflow will integrate density functional theory (DFT) for QM regions, polarizable force fields for MM solvent shells, and enhanced sampling techniques to capture rare events. These simulations demand significant HPC resources due to the large system sizes (>500 atoms), necessity for long time-scale sampling (≥100 ns aggregate), and iterative optimization of collective variables. Expected outcomes include atomistic insights into solvent-mediated kinetic control, validation of mechanistic hypotheses through comparison with experimental kinetic data, and the development of transferable solvent descriptors for reaction prediction. The results will advance fundamental understanding of solvation effects in organic chemistry and provide a computational toolkit for rational solvent selection in synthesis. This work directly aligns with broader efforts to reduce trial-and-error in chemical discovery, with potential applications in pharmaceutical and sustainable chemistry. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the required statistical fidelity and explore the multidimensional parameter space governing these complex systems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of matter, including its micro- and macro-structure, the processes of chemical change, and the theoretical description and laboratory simulation of these phenomena.

abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) are a diverse group of genetic disorders characterized by disruptions in biochemical pathways, leading to complex clinical presentations and heterogeneous outcomes. Current diagnostic and management strategies often rely on iterative biochemical testing and gene-specific analyses, which can delay interventions and fail to fully elucidate disease mechanisms in atypical cases. This project proposes to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive, multi-omics models for rapid diagnosis and personalized therapeutic optimization. We will integrate whole-exome sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, and longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 1,200 patients with suspected IEMs using machine learning frameworks. Computational workflows will prioritize variant pathogenicity, map metabolic network perturbations, and simulate biochemical responses to dietary or pharmacologic interventions. Key steps include the deployment of federated learning architectures to harmonize data across collaborating institutions, molecular dynamics simulations to assess enzyme stability in novel variants, and genome-scale metabolic modeling to predict flux redistribution under therapeutic perturbations. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale data integration, iterative model training, and computationally intensive simulations requiring parallelized processing. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for clinicians to accelerate diagnosis, reduce diagnostic odysseys, and identify patient-specific treatment thresholds. This work will also advance understanding of metabolic network resilience and genotype-phenotype discordance in rare IEMs. By enabling resource-intensive analyses impractical on local infrastructure, the requested allocation will directly support translational innovations in a field where timely, precision-driven care significantly impacts patient survival and quality of life.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and medical management of individuals with inborn errors of metabolism, including the provision of direct care and consultative care for individuals of all ages.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of evaluating the efficacy of large-scale educational interventions using advanced computational methods. Educational evaluation increasingly relies on complex, multi-source datasets—including longitudinal student performance metrics, demographic records, and qualitative feedback—to assess program outcomes. Traditional statistical tools often struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale or model non-linear relationships between intervention components and student outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The framework will employ ensemble models to combine structured quantitative data (e.g., standardized test scores, attendance) with unstructured qualitative data (e.g., open-ended teacher surveys) processed via natural language processing (NLP) techniques. A key innovation involves simulating counterfactual scenarios through agent-based modeling to estimate intervention impacts under varying socioeconomic conditions. The computational demands of training these models on statewide K-12 datasets (N ≈ 2.5 million students) and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and parallelized workflows. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated open-source toolkit for causal inference in educational program evaluation, 2) scalable pipelines for merging administrative and text-based data, and 3) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing intervention designs across diverse school districts. By enabling faster, more granular analysis of equity-related outcomes (e.g., achievement gaps by socioeconomic status), this work aims to advance methodological standards in evaluation research while directly informing state-level policy decisions on resource allocation for Title I programs. The requested computing resources will support both the initial model development phase and ongoing validation studies using real-time data from 12 partner school districts.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for generating information about educational programs, personnel and methods, and the analysis of such information for planning purposes. Includes instruction in evaluation theory, evaluation research design and planning, administering evaluations and related data collection activities, data reporting requirements, data analysis and interpretation, and related economic and policy issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive analytics framework for optimizing law enforcement resource allocation in dynamic urban environments. While traditional approaches to patrol distribution and incident response rely on historical crime statistics and heuristic decision-making, these methods often fail to adapt to real-time variables such as shifting population density, transient event-driven risks (e.g., protests, festivals), and multi-jurisdictional coordination challenges. The proposed computational model integrates heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial crime reports, traffic patterns, social media activity, and emergency service call logs—to simulate urban risk landscapes and test allocation strategies under diverse scenarios. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between law enforcement units, civilian populations, and environmental factors, while graph neural networks will analyze temporal-spatial dependencies in incident patterns. A key innovation involves coupling real-time data assimilation with ensemble forecasting to quantify uncertainty in resource deployment outcomes. The computational demands of this approach necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized scenario testing, hyperparameter optimization of machine learning models, and large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that identifies high-probability intervention points for crime prevention, reduces emergency response latency, and balances proactive community engagement with reactive enforcement needs. By addressing the computational gap between theoretical public administration frameworks and operational realities, this project aims to advance evidence-based policing strategies while maintaining ethical oversight through embedded fairness audits of algorithmic recommendations. The resulting open-source framework will provide law enforcement agencies with scalable, adaptable tools to improve public safety outcomes without expanding budgetary or personnel resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply theories and practices of organization management and criminal justice to the administration of public law enforcement agencies and operations. Includes instruction in law enforcement history and theory, operational command leadership, administration of public police organizations, labor relations, incident response strategies, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address systemic inefficiencies in medical insurance claim processing, with a focus on optimizing accuracy, compliance, and reimbursement timelines. A critical challenge in medical billing lies in the analysis of vast, heterogeneous datasets spanning claim records, payer policies, regulatory guidelines, and clinical documentation. Manual or legacy software-driven approaches often fail to detect subtle patterns in claim denials, coding errors, or evolving compliance risks, leading to revenue loss and administrative burdens for healthcare providers. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes the development of machine learning (ML) models trained on de-identified historical claims data (millions of records), payer-specific policy documents, and federal/state regulatory texts. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of structured and unstructured data, including natural language processing (NLP) to map clinical notes to billing codes and semantic analysis of policy updates. Computational simulations will model claim adjudication workflows under varying regulatory scenarios to identify bottlenecks. Additionally, reinforcement learning algorithms will be deployed to optimize coding recommendations in real time, reducing denials. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable predictive framework to flag high-risk claims prior to submission, dynamic compliance monitoring tools, and data-driven insights into payer-specific reimbursement trends. By integrating these computational tools with existing billing software ecosystems, the project aims to reduce claim rejection rates by an estimated 15–25%, accelerate reimbursement cycles, and enhance adaptability to regulatory changes. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on advancing technical proficiency in insurance operations while contributing novel methodologies to bridge gaps between healthcare data science and billing practice. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the project’s data volume, model complexity, and need for rapid iteration in a regulated healthcare environment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and manage the medical and health insurance operations in a medical office, health care facility, health maintenance organization, or insurance provider. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes; health insurance law, policy, and regulations; insurance records and paperwork administration; insurance office administration; health/medical insurance software applications; personnel supervision; business mathematics; billing and collection procedures; medical terminology; and communications skills.

abstract: Preventable patient harm remains a persistent challenge in healthcare systems, driven by complex interactions among clinical workflows, human factors, and organizational structures. Current approaches to risk mitigation often rely on retrospective analyses, limiting proactive intervention. This project seeks to develop predictive, systems-based computational models to identify latent risks and optimize safety protocols in real-world clinical environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-source data—including electronic health records, adverse event reports, and sensor-derived workflow metrics—to simulate healthcare processes and human-system interactions at scale. Agent-based modeling will be employed to replicate clinician decision-making, patient flow, and equipment utilization patterns, while machine learning techniques will analyze historical harm events to forecast high-risk scenarios. A federated learning framework will ensure privacy-preserving analysis across institutional datasets. Computational demands include large-scale parameter optimization for simulation calibration, real-time processing of streaming clinical data, and natural language processing of unstructured incident reports. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of modifiable risk factors in medication administration and diagnostic workflows, (2) quantitative evaluation of proposed safety interventions through in silico trials, and (3) development of adaptive clinical decision support tools to reduce human error. By enabling granular analysis of systemic vulnerabilities, this work will advance evidence-based strategies for harm prevention while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the heterogeneous data volumes (>10 TB multimodal inputs) and computational complexity (10^6+ parallelized simulations) required to model healthcare ecosystems with sufficient fidelity. Results will directly inform quality improvement initiatives across partner health systems, with projected applications in reducing hospital-acquired infections, diagnostic errors, and perioperative complications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of transformative mechanisms and evidence-based protocols to reduce preventable patient harm and improve clinical outcomes. Includes instruction in healthcare quality, patient safety, research methods, program evaluation, epidemiology, legal and regulatory compliance, systems thinking, human factors engineering, and risk management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven framework to optimize personalized learning strategies for students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Educators face significant challenges in designing individualized education plans (IEPs) that account for the heterogeneous learning profiles, sensory sensitivities, and communication needs of autistic students. While evidence-based practices exist, their effective customization requires analyzing complex, multimodal datasets—including behavioral observations, academic performance metrics, and physiological responses—that exceed the processing capabilities of conventional systems. The research problem centers on identifying scalable computational methods to model student-teacher interactions, predict intervention outcomes, and generate adaptive teaching recommendations. The proposed approach integrates machine learning (ML) with agent-based simulations to analyze anonymized datasets from classroom settings, wearable sensors, and existing ASD intervention studies. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of reinforcement learning models to iteratively refine teaching strategies across diverse virtual student profiles. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be deployed to extract patterns from unstructured data, such as teacher journals and therapy session transcripts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating ASD learning environments, predictive models linking specific instructional tactics to skill acquisition rates, and actionable insights into real-time adaptation of pedagogical techniques. By quantifying the impact of individualized instructional variables—such as task sequencing, sensory scaffolding, and feedback timing—this work aims to empower educators with empirically validated decision-support tools. The project aligns with teacher education goals by creating translatable resources for training professionals in data-informed ASD instruction, ultimately advancing equitable access to tailored educational experiences.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of abdominal and pelvic imaging modalities, such as multiparametric MRI and spectral CT, has created a critical need for advanced computational tools to improve diagnostic precision and streamline clinical workflows. Current manual and semi-automated approaches for analyzing large volumetric datasets are time-intensive, prone to variability, and ill-equipped to handle the integration of multi-modal imaging with clinical data. This project proposes the development of a deep learning framework to automate the detection, segmentation, and quantitative analysis of abdominal pathologies, including hepatic tumors, inflammatory bowel disease, and pelvic organ prolapse. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte imaging repositories from three institutional cohorts (n=2,100 patients) and public datasets, train 3D convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms, and validate models against histopathological and longitudinal clinical outcomes. Key computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data formats, optimizing memory-intensive processing of high-resolution dynamic imaging sequences, and implementing federated learning protocols to enable multi-institutional collaboration while preserving data privacy. The proposed framework will leverage GPU-accelerated pipelines for distributed training and inference, with containerized deployment to ensure reproducibility. Successful implementation is expected to yield validated algorithms for lesion characterization, treatment response prediction, and automated report generation, significantly reducing diagnostic turnaround times while improving inter-reader consistency. By enabling granular analysis of radiomic features across diverse patient populations, this work aims to establish new quantitative biomarkers for abdominal disorders and support precision medicine initiatives. The requested HPC infrastructure will directly address scalability barriers in translating computational radiology innovations to clinical practice, ultimately enhancing diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes in abdominal imaging.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the abdomen and pelvis in adults and children.

abstract: Therapeutic radiologic physics faces a critical challenge in optimizing radiation dose delivery while minimizing toxicity to adjacent healthy tissues, particularly for complex tumor geometries and heterogeneous patient anatomies. Current treatment planning systems rely on simplified dose calculation algorithms that may underestimate dose deposition uncertainties in scenarios involving high-density implants, tissue interfaces, or charged particle beams. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity, GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulation framework for radiation transport modeling to improve the accuracy of dose prediction in clinically challenging cases. The computational approach will implement Geant4-based simulations with patient-specific CT-derived phantoms, incorporating dynamic motion modeling for thoracic and abdominal tumors. Machine learning methods will be integrated to generate surrogate models for rapid sensitivity analyses of beam parameters, enabling efficient exploration of multi-criteria optimization spaces. High-performance computing resources are essential to process the required 10⁹–10¹⁰ particle histories per simulation, manage terabyte-scale datasets from 4DCT imaging, and train deep neural networks on heterogeneous radiation response patterns. Expected outcomes include validated models for proton beam range uncertainty reduction in titanium implant scenarios, optimized fluence maps for spatially fractionated grid therapy, and open-source tools for GPU-accelerated secondary electron tracking. The resource-intensive simulations will directly inform clinical protocol development at our institution’s proton therapy center, with particular significance for pediatric and re-irradiation cases where millimeter-scale dose precision impacts outcomes. By establishing a computational pipeline linking first-principles physics modeling to treatment planning system inputs, this work aims to bridge the gap between research-grade dose calculation accuracy and clinically feasible implementation timelines. Results will be disseminated through the OpenDose collaboration to support benchmarking efforts across therapeutic radiologic physics programs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physical aspects of the therapeutic applications of x-rays, gamma rays, electron, and other charged particle beams, neutrons, and radiations from sealed radionuclide sources; and with the equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamics of socio-cultural polarization in protracted conflicts, integrating behavioral psychology, sociolinguistics, and network science. The research addresses a critical gap in conflict resolution: the inability to systematically analyze how micro-scale interpersonal communications aggregate into macro-scale adversarial narratives that sustain conflict cycles. Current models often oversimplify cultural variables or lack temporal resolution to capture feedback loops between communication patterns and group identity formation. We propose an adaptive agent-based modeling (ABM) system that simulates multi-layered interactions across three dimensions: 1) individual cognitive biases in threat perception, 2) community-level information diffusion through multilingual discourse networks, and 3) institutional influences on collective memory formation. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel execution of 10^4-10^5 agent simulations across parameter spaces exploring 15+ cultural, economic, and geopolitical variables derived from empirical case studies (e.g., post-conflict reconciliation processes in Southeast Asia and the Sahel). Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model outputs against ground-truthed social media datasets and historical reconciliation timelines. The computational architecture combines graph neural networks for modeling influence propagation with interpretable AI techniques to identify critical intervention thresholds in conflict escalation pathways. Expected outcomes include a novel metric for quantifying narrative toxicity in intercultural dialogues and predictive tools to assess the resilience of peacebuilding initiatives under different policy scenarios. By enabling multiscale analysis of cultural transmission mechanisms in conflict systems, this work aims to provide conflict mediators with evidence-based strategies to disrupt pathological communication patterns while preserving cultural identity. The resulting open-source framework will be designed for scalability to diverse conflict contexts, with particular attention to computational ethics through participatory model co-development with conflict-affected communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of national, intergroup and interpersonal conflicts. Includes instruction in theories of conflict, mediation and negotiation, understanding of the ethical, cultural and power dynamics that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the integration of multi-omics data for predicting patient-specific responses to emerging therapies in complex diseases. Despite progress in precision medicine, a critical gap remains in unifying heterogeneous biological datasets—such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—into predictive models that account for individual variability in disease progression and treatment outcomes. Traditional computational tools struggle with the scale, dimensionality, and noise inherent in these datasets, limiting their clinical utility. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning framework optimized for HPC environments to identify cross-modal biomarkers and simulate therapeutic interactions at unprecedented resolution. The computational pipeline will include dimensionality reduction techniques, graph-based neural networks to model biological networks, and physics-informed simulations of molecular dynamics. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to reduce processing times for large-scale datasets (e.g., 10,000+ patient records with multi-omics profiles) from weeks to days while improving model accuracy. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel biomarker combinations for neurodegenerative and autoimmune diseases, validated through retrospective clinical data, and open-source tools for scalable multi-omics analysis. This work will directly support translational research in underserved disease areas and provide a template for resource-efficient computational approaches in health sciences. Access to HPC resources is essential to overcome memory and speed constraints inherent in consumer-grade hardware, ensuring reproducibility and enabling real-time collaboration across institutions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical professional preparation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of neurodegenerative disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets through large-scale computational modeling of multi-omics data, neuroimaging, and patient-derived clinical datasets. Neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis exhibit complex molecular and cellular interactions that remain poorly understood, limiting the development of precision therapies. Current analytical approaches struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning genomics, proteomics, functional MRI, and longitudinal electronic health records while accounting for individual variability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model disease progression dynamics and identify biomarkers. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures, will be trained on multi-institutional datasets to map spatiotemporal patterns of neurodegeneration. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize misfolded protein interactions at atomic resolution, leveraging GPU-accelerated workflows to screen potential small-molecule inhibitors. Concurrently, finite element modeling of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics will assess how vascular dysfunction contributes to protein aggregation. These parallel computational pipelines require significant resources due to the scale of data (50+ TB of neuroimaging, 10,000+ whole genomes) and the iterative nature of simulations. Allocated HPC resources will enable rapid processing of diffusion tensor imaging, exome-wide association studies, and in silico drug screening across millions of conformations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel genetic risk loci, predictive models of clinical progression, and prioritized therapeutic compounds for experimental validation. This work will establish a scalable computational infrastructure for neurology research, bridging molecular mechanisms with patient-specific phenotypes to accelerate translational discovery. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with clinical insights, the project aims to advance personalized therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative diseases with high unmet need.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of all types of disease or impaired function of the brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, muscles and autonomic nervous system, as well as the blood vessels that relate to these structures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research in Armenian, a historically rich yet understudied language with complex dialectal diversity and a literary tradition spanning millennia. The primary research problem centers on the lack of large-scale, data-driven analyses of Armenian linguistic evolution, dialectal variation, and stylistic features in classical and modern texts. Existing studies rely on manual methods, limiting the scope and reproducibility of findings, particularly for under-resourced dialects and premodern corpora. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational approach. First, we will construct a unified digital corpus of Armenian texts spanning the 5th to 21st centuries, integrating existing digitized manuscripts, modern publications, and transcribed oral histories. Second, we will develop parallelized NLP pipelines to automate morphological tagging, syntactic parsing, and semantic analysis across dialects, utilizing transformer-based models adapted for low-resource scenarios. Third, machine learning techniques—including phylogenetic modeling and variational autoencoders—will be applied to trace linguistic divergence patterns and quantify literary stylistic shifts. The scale of data (estimated at 15 TB of text and metadata) and the computational intensity of training cross-dialectal models necessitate HPC resources for distributed storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory batch processing. Anticipated outcomes include the first probabilistic map of Armenian dialectal divergence, a quantitative framework for dating undigitized manuscripts via linguistic features, and open-access tools for automated analysis of Classical Armenian morphology. These results will significantly enhance philological research, support endangered dialect preservation, and enable comparative studies with other Indo-European languages. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for studying linguistically complex, historically layered texts while advancing Armenian studies’ capacity for data-driven scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by Armenians. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to advance fire prevention and safety planning in complex urban environments through high-fidelity computational modeling of fire spread dynamics and human evacuation behavior. Traditional fire risk assessments often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the interplay between building geometries, ventilation systems, combustible materials, and crowd movement during emergencies. This limitation hinders the development of optimized safety protocols for high-density structures such as mixed-use towers, underground transit hubs, and heritage buildings with unique architectural constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop a coupled simulation framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for fire-smoke propagation and agent-based modeling (ABM) for occupant egress. The CFD component will employ large-eddy simulations to resolve turbulent combustion and toxic plume dispersion at sub-meter scales across multi-story domains, while the ABM module will incorporate cognitive decision-making algorithms calibrated to behavioral studies of evacuees under sensory impairment. A key innovation lies in dynamically linking these models to enable real-time feedback between fire conditions and occupant movement, a computationally intensive process requiring parallelized solvers and distributed memory architectures. The project will validate simulations against full-scale experimental fire datasets and historical incident reports, then apply the framework to case studies of high-risk urban infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for identifying latent vulnerabilities in emergency evacuation routes, data-driven recommendations for staggered evacuation protocols, and evidence-based guidelines for retrofitting legacy structures with adaptive smoke control systems. By addressing critical gaps in scenario-specific fire safety planning, this work aims to reduce preventable casualties and economic losses while informing next-generation building codes tailored to evolving urban design challenges.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science and technology to problems of reducing fire risk, limiting loss, supervising substance removal, conducting safety inspections and investigations, and advising on matters of safety procedures and fire prevention policy. Includes instruction in fire behavior, fire simulation, structural risk assessment, materials analysis, detection and suppression systems, smoke management, supply and evacuation, public education, legal aspects of fire prevention, and related research and communications methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to optimize large-scale geospatial data processing for applications in surveying engineering, with a focus on improving the accuracy and efficiency of terrestrial and aerial surveying workflows. Modern surveying tasks increasingly rely on high-resolution LiDAR, photogrammetric point clouds, and multi-sensor satellite data, which generate massive datasets requiring intensive processing. Current methods for feature extraction, surface modeling, and alignment often struggle with computational bottlenecks when handling datasets spanning hundreds of square kilometers, particularly when integrating real-time GPS corrections and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. The proposed research will implement parallelized algorithms for point cloud registration, least-squares adjustment, and machine learning-based feature classification using GPU-accelerated computing. Key objectives include developing a scalable workflow for error propagation modeling in multi-sensor systems and creating adaptive meshing techniques to reduce computational overhead in digital terrain model generation. High-performance computing resources are essential to train deep neural networks for automated detection of survey control points and to run Monte Carlo simulations assessing positional uncertainty under varying environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for photogrammetric bundle adjustment optimized for distributed memory architectures and a validated protocol for resource-efficient processing of hyperspectral-topographic fused datasets. This work will directly benefit infrastructure planning, cadastral surveying, and natural hazard monitoring by enabling faster processing of centimeter-accurate geospatial models while maintaining rigorous error control. The computational infrastructure will also support educational initiatives in geospatial data science for civil and environmental engineering applications.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the determination of the location, elevations, and alignment of natural and manmade topographic features. Includes instruction in property line location, surveying, surface measurement, aerial and terrestrial photogrammetry, remote sensing, satellite imagery, global positioning systems, computer applications, and photographic data processing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the long-term efficacy of Montessori pedagogical strategies in diverse classroom environments. Montessori education emphasizes individualized, self-directed learning trajectories, yet the dynamic interplay between student autonomy, material design, and instructor interventions remains understudied at scale. Current research relies heavily on observational studies, which struggle to isolate variables or predict outcomes across heterogeneous student populations. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate classroom interactions under varying Montessori parameters (e.g., material sequencing, instructor-student ratios, mixed-age group dynamics). The ABM will represent students as autonomous agents governed by behavioral rules derived from empirical Montessori training literature, while reinforcement learning algorithms will simulate adaptive instructor decision-making. High-fidelity simulations will require parallelized computation to iteratively test hypotheses across thousands of virtual classrooms, incorporating real-world datasets on student development metrics. Key objectives include (1) identifying material configurations that optimize self-directed skill acquisition, (2) quantifying the impact of environmental factors (e.g., spatial layout, class size) on collaborative learning outcomes, and (3) generating predictive models to inform Montessori teacher training protocols. HPC resources are critical for managing the stochasticity and combinatorial complexity inherent in modeling individualized learning pathways at cohort scales. Outcomes will provide actionable insights for refining Montessori teacher education programs, with particular emphasis on balancing structure and flexibility in lesson planning. By bridging computational social science and teacher education, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for evidence-based improvements in Montessori pedagogy.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Maria Montessori and her followers.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the historical and sociolinguistic dynamics of Spanish and Portuguese dialectal variation across Latin America and the Iberian Peninsula. The research problem centers on the computational complexity of modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical shifts in large, multi-regional corpora, which include digitized historical texts, contemporary speech recordings, and transcribed oral narratives. Traditional methods struggle to process such voluminous and heterogeneous datasets, limiting the scale and precision of analyses.
