cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles and techniques of art and computer-assisted imaging, graphics, and animation to create visual materials to facilitate the recording and dissemination of biomedical knowledge for educational, research, and clinical purposes. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, histology, embryology, neuroanatomy, medical terminology, artistic media and techniques, illustration techniques, three-dimensional modeling, prosthetics, data display design, exhibit design and production, medical photography, multimedia, computer graphics and animation, digital imaging, business management, production technology, and instructional design.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC) into jewelry arts research to address material science and design challenges inherent in traditional craft practices. While jewelry creation relies on empirical knowledge of material behaviors—such as metal fatigue during forming, thermal gradients in enameling, or stress distribution in complex wearable pieces—these processes often involve iterative trial-and-error, material waste, and limited predictive insight. This research proposes leveraging finite element analysis (FEA), lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to model physical and aesthetic outcomes of jewelry fabrication techniques. HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of metal alloy interactions under varying forming conditions, simulate microstructural evolution during electroforming, and predict crack propagation in gemstone settings. Additionally, generative AI models will be trained on historical and contemporary jewelry datasets to propose structurally optimized, artistically coherent designs. The project will validate computational predictions through physical prototyping, correlating simulation data with empirical measurements of hardness, tensile strength, and surface finish. Expected outcomes include an open-access framework for computational jewelry design, reducing material waste in prototyping by 30-50%, and novel hybrid workflows combining algorithmic pattern generation with handcrafting. By bridging computational materials science and studio practice, this work aims to expand creative possibilities in jewelry arts while establishing quantitative metrics for durability and wearability in ornamental objects. The resource-intensive nature of multi-physics simulations and 3D generative modeling necessitates HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale datasets and iterate complex geometries, tasks unfeasible on local workstations. This interdisciplinary approach positions jewelry arts as a testbed for computational creativity research, with potential applications in sustainable craft practices and customizable wearable technologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by fashioning jewelry from gems, other stones, and precious metals. Includes instruction in design concepts, electroforming, enameling, gemology, lapidary technique and art, metal and non-metal casting and molding, metal coloring, metalsmithing and finishing, personal style development, photo etching, and stone cutting and polishing.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the physicochemical dynamics of ultra-high-dilution (UHD) homeopathic remedies using advanced computational modeling to elucidate potential mechanisms underlying their purported therapeutic effects. Despite widespread clinical use, homeopathic solutions—prepared through iterative dilution and succussion—lack a robust physicochemical explanatory framework, particularly at dilutions beyond Avogadro’s limit where solute concentrations approach zero. The central research problem lies in characterizing nanoscale structural or dynamic changes in solvent (water/ethanol) systems that may arise during potentization, which could mediate bioactivity despite the absence of original solute molecules. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model solvent behavior under varying dilution/succussion conditions, focusing on hydrogen-bond network rearrangements, nanobubble formation, and ephemeral solute-solvent interfacial effects. Quantum mechanical calculations will assess localized electronic or vibrational perturbations in water clusters, while machine learning algorithms will analyze large datasets from simulated and experimental Raman/FTIR spectra to identify spectral signatures correlated with succussion parameters. This integrative methodology requires significant computational power due to the need for long-timescale MD simulations (µs-ms range), ab initio accuracy in quantum analyses, and high-dimensional pattern recognition. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of persistent solvent structural anomalies induced by potentization, (2) development of predictive models linking manufacturing variables to solution properties, and (3) foundational data for designing empirical validation studies. By applying cutting-edge computational techniques to homeopathy’s core methodological mystery, this work aims to bridge gaps between traditional homeopathic claims and modern material science, potentially revealing novel solvent-mediated mechanisms relevant to low-dose bioregulation. Results could inform optimized remedy production protocols and stimulate interdisciplinary dialogue at the interface of nanotechnology, fluid dynamics, and alternative medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of homeopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic system using naturally occurring substances in highly diluted forms to mimic symptoms of illness and trigger autoimmune responses, based on the law of similars and other principles derived from the work of Samuel Hahnemann and others. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, toxicology, philosophy and theory of homeopathy, casetaking and case analysis, repertory, material medica, constitutional typing, proving, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing complexity of analyzing large-scale audiovisual media datasets in the context of evolving broadcast and streaming platforms. As media production and consumption patterns shift toward nonlinear, algorithm-driven distribution, researchers face challenges in systematically evaluating how aesthetic, technical, and narrative elements interact with audience engagement metrics across heterogeneous datasets. Traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to process terabyte-scale archives of video, audio, and metadata while maintaining temporal synchronization and context-aware interpretation. Our research will develop computational workflows to examine 10,000+ hours of broadcast television and streaming content using parallelized machine learning models optimized for multimodal analysis. Key technical objectives include implementing GPU-accelerated pipelines for scene segmentation, speech-to-text transcription, visual composition classification, and cross-platform audience behavior pattern recognition. The computational framework will integrate natural language processing for script analysis, computer vision for framing and lighting assessment, and graph-based network models to map production team structures against creative outcomes. By deploying containerized environments on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve scalable processing of legacy analog recordings and modern 4K/UHD digital assets while preserving metadata integrity. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible toolkit for media studies researchers to analyze production techniques at unprecedented scale, 2) empirical insights into how technical constraints historically shaped genre evolution in television, and 3) predictive models correlating real-time production decisions with longitudinal audience retention metrics. This work will advance media scholarship by enabling systematic analysis of industry-scale datasets while training communication students in computational humanities methodologies, thereby bridging critical media theory with emergent technical demands in the digital content ecosystem.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, methods, and techniques used to plan, produce, and distribute audio and video programs and messages, and that prepares individuals to function as staff, producers, directors, and managers of radio and television shows and media organizations. Includes instruction in media aesthetics; planning, scheduling, and production; writing and editing; performing and directing; personnel and facilities management; marketing and distribution; media regulations, law, and policy; and principles of broadcast technology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying Reiki therapy, with a focus on characterizing how directed energy practices influence cellular and systemic physiological states. Despite widespread anecdotal reports of therapeutic benefits, the absence of robust empirical models explaining Reiki’s interaction with biological systems hinders its integration into evidence-based care frameworks. We propose a computational study combining biofield modeling, physiological signal analysis, and machine learning to quantify energy transfer dynamics and their correlation with measurable health outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable multiscale simulations of electromagnetic field interactions with cellular ion channels and mitochondrial activity, informed by experimental data from electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV) monitoring, and bioimpedance measurements collected during Reiki sessions. Concurrently, graph neural networks will analyze temporal patterns in practitioner-recipient energy exchange datasets to identify potential biomarkers of efficacy. The computational pipeline will integrate finite element modeling of human biofields, molecular dynamics simulations of redox-sensitive proteins, and topological analysis of autonomic nervous system responses. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model mapping Reiki intervention parameters (e.g., hand positions, duration) to physiological response profiles, (2) identification of quantifiable electromagnetic signatures associated with therapeutic effects, and (3) optimization of treatment protocols for specific stress-related pathologies. By establishing a biophysical foundation for energy medicine modalities, this work aims to bridge traditional healing practices with modern systems biology paradigms, potentially informing new non-invasive therapeutic strategies for chronic pain, anxiety disorders, and immune dysregulation. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of biofield-body interactions and achieving sufficient temporal resolution in multiscale simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical, emotional, and spiritual balance and healing through the manipulation of the body's energy field to increase healing energy. Includes instruction in the history and philosophy of Usui Reiki, attunement, empowerment, self-treatment, direct and distance healing techniques, healing symbols, aura clearing, Reiki meditation, practice management, and related Reiki systems such as Lightarian, Urevia, and Magnified Healing.

abstract: The graphic and printing industry faces increasing demands for high-quality, customizable products while balancing efficiency and sustainability. Current production workflows often rely on trial-and-error adjustments to manage variables such as substrate compatibility, ink behavior, and equipment performance, leading to material waste and operational delays. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and optimize digital printing processes at scale. The research will develop computational frameworks to simulate dynamic interactions between inks, substrates, and printer hardware under diverse environmental conditions. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-modal datasets—including sensor data from printing equipment, high-resolution image outputs, and material property databases—to predict optimal print parameters, detect defects in real time, and recommend maintenance interventions. Additionally, HPC-enabled rendering pipelines will be designed to accelerate the processing of complex variable-data print jobs, enabling rapid iteration for personalized designs. By integrating these computational tools, the project aims to reduce waste by 20–30% in test scenarios, improve color accuracy across substrates, and shorten production cycles. Outcomes will advance the integration of data-driven decision-making into graphic communications training programs, equipping operators with predictive tools to enhance precision and adaptability in industrial workflows. The resource request prioritizes GPU nodes for neural network training and parallelized simulation tasks, as well as high-memory nodes for large-scale image analysis. This work bridges gaps between traditional print production practices and emerging computational methodologies, fostering innovation in a sector critical to global communication and media ecosystems.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamic interactions between neural circuit activity and behavioral outputs using large-scale computational modeling of spiking neural networks (SNNs). A central challenge in physiological psychology lies in bridging microscale neural processes—such as synaptic plasticity and neurotransmitter dynamics—with macroscale behavioral phenomena like decision-making, learning, and stress responses. Current models often oversimplify network complexity or lack biological fidelity, limiting their predictive power. To address this gap, we propose developing biologically constrained SNN simulations that integrate empirical data from rodent electrophysiology and optogenetic manipulation studies. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate networks of 100,000+ neurons with realistic connectivity profiles, incorporating region-specific dynamics of the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, and ventral tegmental area. Computational workflows will use parallelized simulations via the NEST simulator, coupled with parameter optimization algorithms to explore how neuromodulatory systems (e.g., dopamine, cortisol) reconfigure network states during aversive and reward-based learning tasks. Machine learning pipelines will analyze emergent patterns in multi-scale output data, identifying critical thresholds for phase transitions in network behavior. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific synaptic adaptation rules to behavioral resilience under stress, as well as open-source tools for simulating neurotransmitter diffusion in extracellular space. This work will advance theoretical frameworks in psychobiology by quantifying how molecular and cellular processes propagate through neural systems to shape behavior, while providing methodological innovations for computational neuroscience. The requested HPC resources are essential given the memory-intensive nature of whole-brain-scale simulations and the need for rapid iteration across neurobiological parameter spaces.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the biological bases of behavior.

abstract: Military Command and Control (C3) systems face escalating challenges in managing multi-domain operations, where real-time integration of heterogeneous data streams, dynamic threat assessment, and coordinated decision-making across distributed nodes are critical. Existing frameworks struggle with scalability, latency, and adaptability under contested or resource-constrained environments, particularly when balancing mission objectives with cybersecurity risks and interoperability mandates. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation environment for testing and optimizing next-generation C3 architectures using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on modeling large-scale, multi-agent operational scenarios that integrate artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision support systems, adversarial cyber-physical threats, and electromagnetic spectrum dynamics. Computational methods will include parallelized discrete-event simulations, Monte Carlo-based risk analysis, and graph-theoretic optimization algorithms to evaluate system resilience, latency thresholds, and human-automation trust metrics. A key innovation involves coupling reinforcement learning models with federated learning frameworks to enable adaptive C3 policies without centralized data aggregation, addressing both performance and security constraints. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of scenario parameters, including terrain variability, network topology disruptions, and adversarial tactics, while maintaining the granularity required for joint all-domain operations. Expected outcomes include a validated suite of computational tools for assessing C3 system readiness under emergent threat paradigms, quantifiable benchmarks for human-machine teaming efficacy, and protocols for resource allocation in degraded communications environments. This work will directly inform modernization priorities for decentralized command systems, offering a pathway to enhance situational awareness and decision velocity in complex operational theaters. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project bridges a critical gap between theoretical C3 advancements and their practical implementation, ensuring scalability and robustness in future defense architectures.
cip_title: Command & Control (C3, C4I) Systems and Operations (MILITARY)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational use of information and decision systems in support of battlefield, theatre, and global strategic operations. Includes instruction in applied mathematics and statistics, computer systems, real-time analysis and decision systems, surveillance and navigation systems, information and communications technology, information security, situational awareness, system integration, joint operations and applications to specific command problems and services.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of hypnotherapeutic interventions by developing data-driven computational models to simulate neural and psychological dynamics during hypnotic states. Despite evidence supporting hypnosis as a therapeutic tool, the mechanisms underlying its efficacy—particularly how hypnotic suggestion modulates neural activity, emotional regulation, and pain perception—remain poorly characterized. Current clinical practice relies on heuristic frameworks, limiting personalized protocol optimization. To address this gap, we propose integrating neuroimaging data (fMRI, EEG) from hypnotherapy sessions with machine learning and dynamic systems modeling to identify biomarkers of hypnotic responsiveness and predict treatment outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale neuroimaging datasets, train deep neural networks for pattern recognition in brain activity, and simulate whole-brain dynamics under varying hypnotic conditions. The computational pipeline will include three phases: (1) preprocessing and feature extraction from multi-modal neuroimaging data using GPU-accelerated tools, (2) development of patient-specific models linking hypnotic induction parameters to neural and behavioral responses via reinforcement learning algorithms, and (3) large-scale parameter space exploration to optimize virtual patient cohorts representing diverse clinical profiles. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for mapping suggestion-induced neuroplasticity, predictive models for tailoring hypnotherapy protocols to individual client needs, and open-access tools for quantifying therapeutic dose-response relationships. This work will provide the first quantitative bridge between hypnosis theory and clinical practice, enabling data-informed refinement of training standards and ethical guidelines. By elucidating neurocomputational signatures of effective therapeutic suggestion, the project aims to establish hypnotherapy as a precision intervention within integrative healthcare, with potential applications in chronic pain management, trauma recovery, and psychosomatic disorders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to employ the controlled inducement of altered states of consciousness, or trance, to reduce pain, resolve emotional conflicts, and enhance communications as part of diagnostic and treatment programs. Includes instruction in the principles of hypnosis and suggestion, induction and deepening, post-hypnotic suggestion, awakening techniques, regression, pacing and leading, resistance transformation, client testing and management, practice management and regulation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Furniture design and manufacturing face growing demands for sustainability, material efficiency, and performance optimization, yet traditional prototyping and testing methods remain resource-intensive and slow to adapt to these challenges. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that simulate material behavior, structural integrity, and ergonomic performance in furniture systems. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) optimizing composite and bio-based material formulations for strength, weight, and environmental impact through molecular dynamics simulations, and (2) predicting long-term wear patterns and failure modes in furniture assemblies using finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning-based predictive modeling. By integrating multi-scale simulations—from molecular interactions to macroscopic stress distributions—we aim to reduce reliance on physical prototyping while improving design precision. The computational workflow will employ open-source simulation tools (e.g., LAMMPS, CalculiX) enhanced with custom Python scripts for parametric design exploration, automated mesh generation, and data-driven optimization. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for material selection, digitally optimized joinery designs that minimize waste during manufacturing, and a framework for simulating user interaction effects on furniture longevity. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in digital fabrication courses while providing open-access simulation templates for small-scale manufacturers. The requested HPC resources are critical to handle the 3D transient simulations and large parameter spaces inherent to this multi-physics approach, enabling rapid iteration unachievable with local computing infrastructure. This work bridges computational engineering with craft-based manufacturing, positioning furniture design as a testbed for sustainable innovation in applied technical fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare and execute furniture design projects, assemble and finish furniture articles or subassemblies, repair furniture, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: Healthcare facility operations rely heavily on efficient administrative workflows to ensure timely patient care, but manual processes for scheduling, order transcription, and resource coordination remain prone to inefficiencies and errors. This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize ward clerk workflows by analyzing patterns in patient intake, staff availability, and procedural scheduling across diverse hospital units. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven tools to predict and mitigate workflow bottlenecks in dynamic healthcare environments. Using anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data and historical unit operation logs from partner institutions, we will employ machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate patient flow scenarios and evaluate the impact of alternative scheduling strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning years of operational records, including free-text nursing orders requiring natural language processing (NLP) for automated classification. Computational experiments will test reinforcement learning models for adaptive staff assignment and GPU-accelerated simulations of emergency department intake patterns under varying patient volumes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce procedural delays, algorithms to prioritize time-sensitive orders, and visual dashboards for real-time workload monitoring. By quantifying relationships between administrative decisions and patient throughput, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for health unit coordination training programs. The scalability of these models will be validated across simulated urban, rural, and specialty care settings, with potential to reduce preventable care delays by 15-20% in pilot units. Results will inform curriculum updates for health unit coordinator certification programs while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy regulations through synthetic data generation techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized home furnishing design and installation processes through advanced simulation, machine learning, and generative modeling. Current methods for space planning, material selection, and aesthetic coordination rely heavily on manual iteration, limiting scalability and adaptability to diverse client needs, spatial constraints, and sustainability goals. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges by training deep neural networks on multimodal datasets—including 3D room scans, textile performance metrics, client preference surveys, and environmental impact profiles—to predict optimal furniture layouts, material pairings, and decorative configurations. Agent-based models will simulate long-term wear patterns and ergonomic interactions across upholstery materials, while finite element analysis will assess stress distributions in custom-built furnishings. A parallelized workflow will integrate these components into a real-time visualization tool, enabling installers to test thousands of design permutations against client-specific criteria. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support system that reduces material waste by 15-20% through predictive sustainability analytics, improves client satisfaction via adaptive personalization algorithms, and establishes quantitative metrics for evaluating aesthetic coherence in hybrid physical-digital design spaces. The computational infrastructure will also enable the creation of an open-access repository of simulated home environments, advancing research in human-centered spatial interaction beyond traditional empirical methods. By bridging computational design, behavioral analytics, and material science within the home furnishings domain, this project aims to redefine industry standards for efficiency, customization, and ecological responsibility in residential spaces.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in home furnishings and decorations. Includes instruction in selecting, purchasing, and designing home furnishings, decorations, and equipment; floral design; accessory construction; textiles; and upholstery.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize collision repair processes and material performance in automotive applications using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Modern vehicle structures increasingly incorporate advanced materials—such as high-strength steels, aluminum alloys, and composite plastics—each with distinct mechanical behaviors under stress. Traditional repair methodologies, however, often rely on empirical guidelines that may not account for complex interactions between heterogeneous materials, adhesives, and environmental factors during post-collision restoration. This research addresses the critical gap in predictive modeling of repair outcomes, particularly for multi-material assemblies subjected to dynamic loads. Leveraging HPC capabilities, the project will implement finite element analysis (FEA) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model stress distribution, crack propagation, and adhesive bonding efficacy across scales, from macroscopic structural components to microscale material interfaces. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation datasets to correlate repair parameters (e.g., heating cycles, clamping forces, paint curing times) with long-term durability metrics. Additionally, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate spray-painting processes under varying booth conditions to optimize finish quality and reduce material waste. By integrating these computational approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights for refining repair protocols, improving training simulations for technicians, and informing material selection in collision-resistant designs. Outcomes will include open-access predictive tools for estimating repair feasibility, a digital twin platform for non-destructive repair validation, and data-driven guidelines for emerging materials like carbon-fiber-reinforced polymers. This work directly supports the Autobody/Collision and Repair Technology field by bridging empirical practice with computational innovation, enhancing both technical education and industry standards for sustainable, efficient vehicle restoration.
cip_title: Autobody/ Collision and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, reconstruct and finish automobile bodies, fenders, and external features. Includes instruction in structure analysis, damage repair, non-structural analysis, mechanical and electrical components, plastics and adhesives, painting and refinishing techniques, and damage analysis and estimating.

abstract: The increasing complexity of patient-specific data in musculoskeletal rehabilitation presents a significant challenge in developing optimized, personalized treatment plans. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, leading to variable patient outcomes and inefficiencies in resource utilization. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create a computational framework integrating biomechanical modeling, machine learning, and multi-modal data analysis. The research will utilize patient-derived datasets, including motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging, to construct dynamic simulations of musculoskeletal function under varying therapeutic interventions. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify patterns predictive of optimal recovery trajectories, while parallelized finite element modeling will quantify tissue-level responses to mechanical loading. The computational demands of processing high-resolution imaging data, coupled with the need for real-time parameter optimization in complex models, necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for efficient execution. Expected outcomes include the development of a predictive tool capable of recommending patient-specific rehabilitation protocols, thereby reducing trial-and-error treatment adjustments. The project will also generate novel insights into biomechanical adaptation processes during recovery, with potential applications in prosthetic design and injury prevention strategies. By bridging computational advances with clinical practice in allied health, this work aims to establish a scalable methodology for data-driven decision-making in rehabilitation sciences, ultimately improving therapeutic efficacy and patient quality of life.
cip_title: Allied Health Diagnostic, Intervention, and Treatment Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health diagnostic, intervention, and treatment professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Acoustic wave propagation in complex environments presents significant challenges due to the interplay of heterogeneous media, boundary interactions, and frequency-dependent attenuation. This project seeks to advance the modeling of broadband acoustic signals in underwater environments with irregular seabed topography and stratified water columns, where traditional analytical methods fail to capture nonlinear scattering and ducting effects. The primary research problem involves resolving the multiscale physics of acoustic wave interactions with dynamic seafloor sediments and fluid-solid interfaces, which are critical for applications such as marine navigation, ecosystem monitoring, and underwater communication systems. To address this, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for wave propagation with discontinuous Galerkin (DG) techniques to handle material discontinuities and complex boundaries. The model will incorporate viscoelastic seabed properties derived from experimental datasets and simulate frequency-dependent attenuation using convolutional perfectly matched layers (CPML). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of 3D simulations across a broad frequency range (10 Hz – 100 kHz), requiring parallelized solvers and adaptive mesh refinement to optimize memory allocation. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source codebase for hybrid FDTD-DG acoustics simulations, new insights into sediment-wave energy transfer mechanisms, and parametric studies of ducting efficiency under varying thermocline conditions. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation sonar systems and contribute to international efforts in mitigating anthropogenic noise impacts on marine ecosystems. The requested resources will enable simulations at biologically and industrially relevant scales, surpassing the limitations of current laboratory-scale models. This work bridges gaps between theoretical acoustics, computational physics, and applied environmental research, with broader implications for medical ultrasonography and non-destructive testing methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of sound, and the properties and behavior of acoustic wave phenomena under different conditions. Includes instruction in wave theory, the acoustic wave equation, energy transformation, vibration phenomena, sound reflection and transmission, scattering and surface wave phenomena, singularity expansion theory, ducting, and applications to specific research problems such as underwater acoustics, crystallography, and health diagnostics.

abstract: Early childhood education is critical for cognitive, social, and emotional development, yet designing effective, individualized pedagogical strategies for diverse learners remains a complex challenge. Traditional observational and survey-based methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multivariate interactions between teaching practices, child behavior, and environmental factors in preschool classrooms. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets and simulate learning environments, enabling data-driven insights into optimal teaching approaches. The research will integrate video recordings of classroom interactions, child developmental assessments, and environmental sensors (e.g., audio, motion tracking) from 50+ preschool classrooms. Computational pipelines will process these terabyte-scale datasets using machine learning models to classify teacher-child engagement patterns, predict learning outcomes, and identify contextual factors influencing instructional efficacy. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom dynamics under varying pedagogical strategies, with parameters informed by empirical data. These simulations will require parallelized computation to iteratively test thousands of scenarios, evaluating how small-group activities, play-based learning, or differentiated instruction affect developmental trajectories. By combining real-world data with synthetic environments, the project aims to uncover scalable strategies for personalizing early education. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking specific teaching behaviors to child skill acquisition, (2) a framework for simulating instructional interventions, and (3) open-source tools to help educators analyze classroom interactions. This work will directly inform teacher training programs by quantifying the impact of pedagogical choices, ultimately supporting equitable, evidence-based practices in preschool education. The scale of data processing, complexity of machine learning workflows, and iterative nature of simulations necessitate HPC resources to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in formal settings prior to beginning regular elementary school, usually ranging in age from three to six years (or grade one), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized, data-driven skincare protocols through computational modeling of skin biomechanics and treatment efficacy. While esthetic practices traditionally rely on manual assessment and standardized procedures, emerging demand for hyper-personalized care—driven by diverse skin types, environmental stressors, and genetic factors—requires scalable analytical tools to optimize outcomes. The research addresses a critical gap in esthetic training and practice: the absence of predictive frameworks to simulate how skin responds to combinations of treatments (e.g., chemical peels, microdermabrasion, LED therapy) under variable biological and environmental conditions. Using finite element modeling (FEM) and agent-based simulations, we will create multiscale models of epidermal and dermal layers, integrating empirical data from clinical skin assessments, histology, and biometric sensors to parameterize tissue elasticity, hydration dynamics, and inflammation pathways. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of treatment interactions across heterogeneous virtual skin cohorts, accounting for variables such as age, ethnicity, and microbiome composition. Machine learning algorithms will then identify optimal treatment sequences and predict adverse reactions. Expected outcomes include a computational toolkit for estheticians to design tailored regimens and a public dataset of simulated skin response profiles, fostering evidence-based practice. By bridging esthetic expertise with computational biomedicine, this work pioneers a novel interdisciplinary niche, enhancing both the precision of skincare interventions and the scientific rigor of non-clinical aesthetic training. The project’s computational demands—particularly its need for GPU-accelerated simulations and large-scale parameter optimization—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically relevant resolution and scalability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cleanse, depilate, massage, and beautify the human body and to function as licensed estheticians and skin care specialists.  Includes instruction in skin anatomy, physiology, and health; principles of nutrition; decontamination and infection control; health and safety; facial and body massage; body wrapping and spa treatments; temporary hair removal including waxing and tweezing; color and skin analysis; client consultation and care; applicable laws and regulations; business practices; and sometimes related alternative healing regimens.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systemic interactions of traditional herbal compounds used in non-canonical therapeutic practices, specifically focusing on their synergistic effects in managing chronic inflammatory conditions. While plant-derived therapies are integral to many alternative medical traditions, their mechanisms of action remain poorly characterized due to the complexity of multi-compound interactions and the lack of scalable computational frameworks to model their polypharmacology. Current research in this niche is hindered by limited capacity to integrate multi-omics datasets (e.g., metabolomic, proteomic) with patient-reported outcome metrics from heterogeneous, small-scale clinical studies. The proposed research will address this gap by developing a computational pipeline to simulate compound-target networks, predict bioavailability, and map emergent anti-inflammatory pathways across tissue types. Machine learning models will be trained on curated phytochemical libraries and validated against existing in vitro data to prioritize high-potential herbal formulations for experimental testing. Molecular dynamics simulations will further resolve time-dependent binding behaviors of multi-compound systems at scale. By employing GPU-accelerated algorithms and parallelized workflows, this approach aims to overcome the high-dimensionality and combinatorial complexity inherent to traditional polyherbal therapies. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel synergistic compound clusters, predictive biomarkers for personalized herbal regimen design, and a publicly accessible database linking traditional use cases to mechanistically supported therapeutic profiles. This work will provide a foundational computational platform for evaluating alternative medical interventions with rigor comparable to conventional drug discovery pipelines, thereby advancing integrative health strategies while respecting the epistemological frameworks of traditional knowledge systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s large-scale simulations, which require >100,000 core-hours for ensemble docking experiments and terabytes of storage for multi-layered omics integration.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medical Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medical support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and development necessitates advanced computational tools to model molecular interactions, optimize pharmacokinetic properties, and predict therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address the challenge of identifying multi-target inhibitors for neurodegenerative diseases, where traditional experimental approaches are time-intensive and limited in exploring vast chemical and conformational spaces. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid computational strategy integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven virtual screening, and free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to systematically evaluate candidate molecules. The research will utilize GPU-accelerated MD simulations to characterize dynamic binding mechanisms of lead compounds with amyloid-beta and tau protein targets implicated in Alzheimer’s disease. Concurrently, an ensemble ML model trained on structural and physicochemical descriptors will screen a curated library of 1.2 million small molecules to prioritize candidates with optimal polypharmacological profiles. FEP workflows will then refine binding affinity predictions for top candidates, enabling atomistic resolution of ligand-target interactions. This computationally intensive pipeline requires parallelized processing of terabytes of simulation data, necessitating access to HPC clusters with high-memory nodes and scalable GPU architectures. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel dual-target inhibitors with enhanced blood-brain barrier permeability and reduced off-target effects, accelerating preclinical development. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated protein-ligand trajectories and ML models tailored for neurodegenerative drug discovery. By integrating computational biophysics and cheminformatics, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for rational polypharmacology design, directly addressing critical gaps in pharmaceutical sciences for complex neurological disorders.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Pharmacy, Pharmaceutical Sciences, and Administration, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial control and measurement systems demands advanced computational tools to optimize instrumentation design, calibration, and real-time performance. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-physics simulation frameworks for next-generation instrumentation systems. A core challenge lies in modeling the interplay between sensor hardware, signal processing algorithms, and environmental variables (e.g., thermal fluctuations, electromagnetic interference) in large-scale industrial environments. Traditional lab-based testing methods are insufficient to capture these dynamic, multi-parameter interactions efficiently. The proposed research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate sensor behavior under extreme operating conditions, coupled with machine learning models to predict calibration drift and failure modes. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of distributed sensor networks, automated control systems, and multi-sensor fusion algorithms at unprecedented scales. Expected outcomes include (1) optimized sensor designs with reduced sensitivity to environmental noise, (2) predictive maintenance algorithms to enhance system reliability, and (3) open-source simulation templates for industrial instrumentation testing. These advancements will directly address critical bottlenecks in precision measurement for energy, manufacturing, and aerospace applications, where minor instrumentation errors can propagate into significant operational risks. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to reduce iterative prototyping costs by 40-60% and accelerate the deployment of robust instrumentation solutions. The resulting datasets and models will be integrated into the Instrumentation Technology curriculum, providing students with hands-on experience in computational design workflows for smart measurement systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing control and measurement systems and procedures. Includes instruction in instrumentation design and maintenance, calibration, design and production testing and scheduling, automated equipment functions, applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision animal nutrition by modeling the molecular interactions between dietary components and metabolic pathways in livestock. A critical challenge in animal nutrition lies in optimizing feed formulations that balance nutrient bioavailability, cost efficiency, and environmental sustainability. Traditional experimental approaches to assess nutrient metabolism are resource-intensive and limited in their capacity to explore the combinatorial complexity of feed additives, genetic variability, and gut microbiome interactions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML), and genome-scale metabolic network models. MD simulations will characterize the binding affinities and structural dynamics of key enzymes involved in nutrient metabolism (e.g., lipases, proteases) when exposed to novel feed additives. Concurrently, ML models trained on existing datasets of animal growth performance, nutrient absorption rates, and microbiome profiles will predict optimal feed compositions under varying physiological conditions. These components will inform a multi-scale metabolic model simulating nutrient flux across tissues, enabling predictions of how specific dietary interventions affect muscle development, milk production, or methane emissions in cattle. The HPC resources will be essential for running large-scale simulations, processing high-dimensional omics data, and iteratively training ML models. Expected outcomes include identifying synergistic feed additive combinations, elucidating mechanisms behind nutrient-gene-microbiome interactions, and generating actionable guidelines for precision feeding strategies. This work aligns with agricultural priorities to enhance livestock productivity while reducing environmental footprints. By bridging molecular-scale insights with whole-animal physiology, the project will provide a transformative toolkit for designing next-generation feeds, directly contributing to sustainable animal agriculture and food security.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a machine learning framework to optimize the design of individualized education plans (IEPs) for elementary students with disabilities, addressing the challenge of efficiently integrating heterogeneous data to personalize instruction. Current IEP development relies heavily on manual analysis of student performance, behavioral observations, and diagnostic assessments—a process that strains educator capacity and may overlook subtle patterns in multisource data. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models on structured and unstructured data from 5,000+ anonymized IEPs, longitudinal academic records, and sensor-based engagement metrics (e.g., eye-tracking, response latency) collected across 15 special education classrooms. Computational workflows will process natural language notes, time-series behavioral logs, and curriculum-aligned assessment scores to identify cross-modal predictors of skill acquisition rates. A transformer-based architecture will then recommend targeted accommodations, scaffolded objectives, and intervention strategies tailored to individual learner profiles. Validation will involve simulating IEP efficacy across synthetic cohorts representing diverse disabilities, socioeconomic factors, and classroom contexts. By automating data synthesis and pattern detection, this approach aims to reduce IEP preparation time by 30–50% while improving the granularity of skill progression targets, as measured by post-implementation student growth metrics. The resulting open-source toolkit will provide educators with real-time decision support, dynamically adjusting recommendations based on ongoing student data. This work directly addresses critical gaps in special education practice by enhancing the scalability of evidence-based personalization, ultimately fostering more equitable outcomes for neurodiverse learners. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets, training complex models with cross-validation, and running large-scale simulations to ensure robustness across educational settings.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Elementary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the elementary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for elementary special education; and teaching elementary education subject matter.

abstract: Pediatric critical care involves managing life-threatening, dynamic physiological derangements in children, where timely, personalized interventions are crucial. Current predictive models for outcomes such as sepsis, multi-organ failure, or response to therapies remain limited by their inability to integrate high-dimensional, time-varying clinical data (e.g., vital signs, biomarkers, imaging) with patient-specific factors (e.g., developmental stage, genetic predispositions). This project aims to develop and validate multiscale computational models to predict clinical trajectories and optimize therapeutic strategies in critically ill children. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate electronic health records, real-time biosensor data, and multi-omics profiles from a retrospective cohort of 2,500 pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) patients to train machine learning models. Key computational challenges include processing heterogeneous data streams at scale, resolving time-dependent interactions between organ systems, and quantifying uncertainty in individualized predictions. Our approach combines mechanistic models of cardiopulmonary and immune dynamics with deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based time-series analysis, graph neural networks) to capture both physiological first principles and data-driven patterns. HPC resources will enable parallelized parameter optimization, large ensemble simulations, and sensitivity analyses across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for early detection of septic shock and respiratory decompensation, validated against prospective PICU data, and a computational framework to simulate patient-specific responses to interventions like vasoactive titrations or ventilator adjustments. This work addresses a critical gap in precision medicine for pediatric critical care by providing tools to reduce trial-and-error decision-making, ultimately improving survival and recovery in this vulnerable population. The scale of data assimilation and model complexity necessitates HPC capabilities beyond institutional computing infrastructure, particularly for real-time applications requiring low-latency processing.
cip_definition: Research focused on advanced life support for children, from the term or near-term neonate to the adolescent. This includes critical care management of life-threatening organ system failure in both medical and surgical patients and support of vital physiological functions.

abstract: The retail industry faces increasing complexity due to dynamic consumer behavior, supply chain volatility, and the need for real-time decision-making across omnichannel platforms. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between these factors, limiting their utility in optimizing inventory, pricing, and workforce management. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate retail ecosystems at scale, integrating heterogeneous data streams such as point-of-sale transactions, online shopping patterns, and supply chain logistics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ agent-based modeling to represent individual consumer decision-making processes, coupled with deep reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize resource allocation strategies. The simulations will incorporate stochastic demand forecasting, multi-echelon inventory dynamics, and labor scheduling constraints under varying market conditions. By parallelizing these simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to explore scenario spaces orders of magnitude larger than current single-node implementations allow, enabling robust sensitivity analyses and prescriptive insights. Expected outcomes include the identification of adaptive replenishment policies to minimize stockouts during demand surges, data-driven staffing models that balance service quality and labor costs, and dynamic pricing strategies responsive to real-time competitor actions. The computational tools developed will be validated against historical data from partner retail organizations, with open-source release planned to benefit smaller enterprises lacking in-house analytics capacity. This work will advance retail management scholarship by bridging macro-scale operational optimization with micro-scale behavioral realism, while providing actionable strategies to enhance resilience in an increasingly competitive sector. The scale of data integration and concurrent simulation required to achieve these objectives necessitates dedicated HPC resources to ensure feasible runtime and model fidelity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operations of a wide variety of retail businesses, including department stores; independent and chain stores; fashion, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical establishments; and online retail businesses. Includes instruction in retail management, merchandise management, customer service management, marketing, organizational behavior, accounting, finance, business law, and personnel management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving dynamics of cultural hybridity in Canadian diasporic literature and digital media through large-scale textual analysis, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multilingual, multi-modal datasets. The research addresses a gap in understanding how diasporic communities in Canada negotiate cultural identity across generations, particularly through vernacular creative expressions in non-institutional digital spaces (e.g., community archives, social media, and self-published works). Current scholarship relies heavily on qualitative close readings, limiting scalability and comparative analysis across linguistic groups. Our computational approach employs transformer-based natural language processing models fine-tuned for code-switched text (e.g., Punjabi-English, Arabic-French), network analysis of intertextual references across 150,000+ digitized works, and geospatial mapping of cultural themes using metadata from independent publishing platforms. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training custom multilingual BERT models on terabyte-scale corpora, enabling parallel processing of heterogeneous data formats (text, audio transcripts, image OCR), and running iterative simulations of cultural transmission patterns across virtual community networks. Expected outcomes include the first longitudinal dataset tracking vernacular cultural production in 15+ immigrant communities from 1980–present, computational frameworks for analyzing hybrid literatures without anglocentric bias, and visualizations of transcultural exchange hotspots informing cultural policy. This work advances Canadian Studies by bridging digital humanities methods with critical ethnic studies, offering scalable tools to preserve marginalized narratives and analyze intersectional identity formation beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Canada and its Pre-Columbian, colonial, and pre-federation predecessors, including immigrant flows and related borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced graphic design workflows, particularly in the development of immersive, interactive media and AI-driven generative art. Current design tools struggle to efficiently process high-resolution 3D models, real-time dynamic rendering, and machine learning–based creativity support systems, creating bottlenecks in iterative design exploration and limiting scalability for complex projects. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework that integrates physically based rendering (PBR), generative adversarial networks (GANs), and agent-based interaction modeling. The research will focus on optimizing GPU-accelerated pipelines for training custom GANs on large datasets of design artifacts (e.g., typography, branding systems, UI/UX patterns), enabling rapid prototyping of AI-generated design variations while maintaining human-in-the-loop creative control. Concurrently, distributed computing resources will be employed to simulate real-time viewer interactions in augmented/virtual reality environments, using particle systems and ray tracing to model light/material behaviors at unprecedented spatial resolutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scalable generative design experimentation, quantitative benchmarks for HPC-accelerated creative workflows, and case studies demonstrating resource-efficient approaches to producing adaptive branding systems and data-driven multimedia installations. This work aims to establish new methodological standards for computational creativity in graphic design while reducing hardware barriers to cutting-edge digital art production, with potential applications in education, commercial design pipelines, and interactive exhibition technologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic and computer techniques to the interpretation of technical and commercial concepts. Includes instruction in computer-assisted art and design, printmaking, concepts sketching, technical drawing, color theory, imaging, studio technique, still and life modeling, multimedia applications, communication skills and commercial art business operations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, high-bandwidth digital media delivery in evolving 5G and edge computing environments, a critical bottleneck for communications technology providers aiming to scale immersive content (e.g., augmented reality, ultra-high-definition streaming) while maintaining quality of service (QoS). Current simulation tools lack the capacity to model dynamic, large-scale user networks with sufficient granularity to predict congestion points or evaluate adaptive bitrate algorithms under heterogeneous device conditions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating multi-platform media ecosystems, integrating network traffic patterns, user interaction data, and device-specific rendering constraints. The computational approach will leverage parallelized discrete-event simulations to model millions of concurrent user nodes across geographically distributed edge servers, coupled with machine learning workflows to predict QoS degradation triggers. By deploying this framework on HPC clusters, we aim to achieve two outcomes: (1) generate predictive models for bandwidth allocation and latency minimization in mixed-reality environments, and (2) create an open dataset of simulated edge network stress scenarios to inform adaptive encoding standards. The project directly supports communications technology innovation by enabling data-driven infrastructure planning and content optimization, with implications for reducing operational costs and improving accessibility of high-density media. Requested HPC resources will be prioritized for parallel simulation jobs and GPU-accelerated training of anomaly detection models, which require terabyte-scale memory handling and low-latency inter-node communication to maintain temporal fidelity across simulated user cohorts. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and integrated into graduate-level curricula on media systems management.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to function as workers and managers within communications industries. Includes instruction in business economics; basic management; principles of interpersonal and mediated communications; radio, television, and digital media production; and related aspects of technology and communications systems.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment planning requires precise understanding of biomechanical interactions between dental appliances and craniofacial tissues, yet current methods rely on generalized force systems that inadequately account for patient-specific variations in bone density, periodontal ligament properties, and craniofacial morphology. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate tooth movement dynamics under multifactorial physiological conditions, enabling personalized orthodontic interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct finite element models integrating cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) data, intraoral scans, and biomechanical tissue properties obtained via micromechanical testing. Multiscale simulations will resolve interactions between orthodontic forces, alveolar bone remodeling, and root resorption risks at micron-level spatial resolutions over clinically relevant timescales. Machine learning algorithms will be implemented to optimize appliance configurations by iteratively analyzing simulated treatment outcomes across parameter spaces encompassing >10^6 variable combinations. Computational workflows will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from retrospective cases of complex malocclusion treated with fixed and removable appliances. The anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-source simulation platform for predicting tooth movement trajectories with submillimeter accuracy, (2) quantitative thresholds for force application that minimize root resorption in osteopenic patients, and (3) AI-generated treatment plans demonstrating ≥30% reduction in projected treatment duration compared to conventional methods. By establishing computational biomechanics as a decision-support tool in orthodontics, this work addresses critical gaps in precision treatment planning while providing foundational insights into mechanobiological responses of craniofacial tissues. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling the >500 TB of multimodal data and parallel processing requirements inherent to real-time simulation of heterogeneous biological systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the guidance of growing dental structures and the correction of misalignments, disproportionate growth, and traumas caused by genetics, disease, injuries, and dysfunctional behaviors. Includes instruction in craniofacial growth and development, malocclusion, design and fabrication of orthodontic appliances, craniofacial alignment, physiological function and analysis, cephalometrics, model analysis, space analysis, surgical orthodontics, cleft lip and palate, and treatment planning and management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models for optimizing industrial control and measurement systems, addressing challenges in real-time data processing, system calibration, and adaptive instrumentation design. Current methods for tuning sensor arrays and control algorithms in dynamic environments—such as manufacturing plants or energy distribution networks—are limited by the computational complexity of reconciling high-dimensional sensor data with physical system constraints. This work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-sensor networks under variable operational conditions, enabling the design of robust calibration protocols and predictive maintenance frameworks. Key computational tasks include finite element modeling of sensor-environment interactions, Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification for measurement systems, and parallelized optimization of control parameters using evolutionary algorithms. The proposed models will integrate machine learning techniques to identify latent patterns in time-series sensor data, improving anomaly detection accuracy while reducing false-positive rates in industrial monitoring applications. By scaling these simulations across HPC nodes, the project aims to generate validated instrumentation templates for adaptive pressure and temperature control systems, with applications in process manufacturing and renewable energy infrastructure. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for automated instrumentation design, a database of performance-optimized sensor configurations, and generalized protocols for minimizing calibration drift in harsh operating environments. This work directly addresses gaps in scalable, data-driven instrumentation practices, with potential to reduce system downtime and energy waste in industrial settings. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the iterative, large-scale simulations required to achieve statistical significance in system response predictions and to accelerate the transition from prototype models to field-deployable solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing control and measurement systems and procedures. Includes instruction in instrumentation design and maintenance, calibration, design and production testing and scheduling, automated equipment functions, applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology faces persistent challenges in balancing spatial resolution, scan time, and signal-to-noise ratio, particularly when imaging dynamic physiological processes or complex vascular structures. Current clinical protocols often require trade-offs that limit diagnostic accuracy or patient throughput. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing and validating a high-performance computing (HPC)-optimized pipeline for real-time MRI image reconstruction and artifact correction. The proposed work will leverage parallelized algorithms to process raw k-space data using compressed sensing and deep learning-based reconstruction models, significantly reducing computational bottlenecks inherent in iterative reconstruction methods. A hybrid approach integrating physics-driven constraints with convolutional neural networks will be implemented to mitigate motion artifacts and improve resolution in time-resolved angiography studies. Clinical MRI datasets spanning neurological, cardiovascular, and oncological applications will be used for training and validation. The computational workflow will be containerized for deployment across heterogeneous HPC architectures, with particular attention to memory optimization for large 4D (3D+time) datasets. Expected outcomes include a 5-10x acceleration in reconstruction times compared to conventional GPU-accelerated clinical systems, enabling near-real-time processing of high-resolution volumetric scans. Successful implementation could advance capabilities for intraprocedural monitoring during image-guided interventions and improve detection of small vascular abnormalities. The project will additionally generate open-source tools for MRI technologist education, bridging gaps between advanced computational methods and clinical training protocols. By demonstrating the feasibility of HPC-driven workflow enhancements in MRI, this research aims to establish a framework for translating cutting-edge computational imaging techniques into routine clinical practice while maintaining compliance with AART standards for technologist training and operational safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals who are AART-certified radiological technicians to utilize MRI technology to obtain still and moving images of various vascular structures in the human body that aid the physician in the diagnosis or treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in MRI imaging, sectional anatomy and pathology, MRI technology, MRI techniques and procedures, MRI physics, and clinical training.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on leadership dynamics within complex human systems. While leadership studies have traditionally relied on qualitative case analyses or small-scale quantitative surveys, these methods struggle to model the adaptive, nonlinear interactions that define leadership emergence and effectiveness in large, dynamic groups. The research problem centers on understanding how contextual variables (e.g., crisis scenarios, cultural heterogeneity) and individual traits (e.g., decision-making styles, communication patterns) interact to shape collective outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with network analysis and machine learning. The ABM framework will simulate diverse leadership scenarios using parameters derived from foundational theories (e.g., transformational leadership, situational leadership) and real-world organizational data. Agents will be programmed with behavioral rules reflecting competing leadership philosophies, enabling systematic testing of hypotheses about collaboration, conflict resolution, and authority negotiation. HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations to realistic group sizes (10,000+ agents) and running iterative sensitivity analyses across multidimensional parameter spaces. Concurrently, graph neural networks will analyze emergent interaction patterns to identify latent predictors of leadership efficacy. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model of leadership adaptability in sociotechnical systems, (2) evidence-based insights into how resource constraints or power imbalances affect group resilience, and (3) open-source tools for simulating leadership interventions in policy-relevant contexts. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for studying leadership as a complex adaptive system, with applications to organizational design, crisis management training, and cross-cultural collaboration strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the universal phenomenon of leadership in human groups. Includes instruction in general or multidisciplinary leadership theory, practice and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance chiropractic research by modeling the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of spinal adjustments. While chiropractic care is widely utilized for musculoskeletal health, the precise mechanisms underlying its therapeutic outcomes—particularly how vertebral adjustments influence neural signaling, soft tissue response, and systemic health—remain incompletely understood. Current clinical studies often rely on static imaging or manual assessments, which lack the resolution to capture dynamic, multi-scale interactions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of spinal segments, machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of patient biomechanical data, and simulations of neural network responses to mechanical stimuli. The FEM component will model stress-strain distributions in vertebral joints and surrounding tissues under varying adjustment protocols, while ML algorithms will process motion capture data from clinical sessions to identify patterns linked to therapeutic outcomes. Concurrently, neural simulations will predict how localized mechanical forces modulate afferent signaling and central nervous system activity. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of biomechanical datasets, the iterative nature of parameter optimization in FEM, and the real-time processing demands of ML training. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of spinal adjustment efficacy based on patient-specific biomechanics, (2) mechanistic insights into the relationship between adjustment techniques and neurophysiological responses, and (3) an open-access computational toolkit for optimizing chiropractic interventions. By elucidating the biophysical underpinnings of care, this work aims to enhance clinical decision-making, reduce trial-and-error in treatment design, and strengthen the evidence base for chiropractic in integrative healthcare. The requested HPC allocation will directly support these large-scale simulations, enabling transformative advances in both chiropractic research and patient-centered practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of chiropractic, a health care and healing system based on the application of non-invasive treatments and spinal adjustments to alleviate health problems caused by vertebral misalignments affecting bodily function as derived from the philosophy of Daniel Palmer. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, chiropractic theory and science, postural and spinal analysis, diagnostic radiology and ultrasound, adjustment technique, patient counseling, professional standards and ethics, and practice management.
