abstract: The development of adaptive assistive technologies for individuals with motor impairments remains limited by the inability to dynamically personalize device parameters to user-specific biomechanical and neurological profiles. Current approaches rely on static, population-level models that fail to account for real-time physiological fluctuations or complex movement pathologies. This project seeks to establish a computational framework integrating high-fidelity musculoskeletal simulations with machine learning to optimize assistive device actuation patterns in response to individualized neuromuscular signals. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallel execution of finite element models simulating human-device interaction across diverse anatomical geometries and impairment severities, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms trained on multimodal data streams (EMG, inertial sensors, motion capture). By leveraging GPU-accelerated environments, the team will iteratively refine neural networks capable of predicting optimal torque profiles for lower-limb exoskeletons under variable gait conditions. The resulting models will be validated against experimental data from 25 participants with post-stroke hemiparesis, assessing improvements in metabolic efficiency and movement symmetry compared to conventional prescription methods. This work aims to establish a scalable pipeline for real-time personalization of rehabilitation technologies, reducing reliance on manual calibration while addressing the combinatorial complexity inherent in adaptive human-machine systems. Outcomes will directly inform the design of next-generation exoskeletons and neuroprosthetics, advancing the translation of computational biomechanics into clinical practice.
cip_title: Assistive/ Augmentative Technology and Rehabilitation Engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of psychology, engineering, and occupational therapy to the design and implementation of technological interventions and systems to promote patient rehabilitation and function. Includes instruction in ergonomics, seating and mobility design, universal and near environment systems design, rehabilitation research, rehabilitation biomechanics, access and communications design, microprocessor-based technologies, neurological trauma, standards and testing, and service delivery management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing need for advanced computational tools in nursing education to improve predictive modeling of student success and patient care outcomes. While Pre-Nursing Studies programs focus on foundational health sciences and clinical readiness, current pedagogical strategies lack robust, data-driven methods to personalize training or simulate complex clinical scenarios at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework to analyze multidimensional student performance data—including academic metrics, simulation lab results, and psychosocial assessments—and predict readiness for professional nursing programs. Additionally, we aim to create high-fidelity, agent-based simulations of patient care environments to evaluate decision-making under realistic clinical constraints. These tasks require high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the volume of input data (historical records from 15,000+ students across 10 institutions) and the computational complexity of training deep neural networks for outcome prediction. Simulations will model dynamic variables such as patient acuity, staffing ratios, and interdisciplinary team interactions, necessitating parallel processing for real-time scenario generation. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms identifying at-risk students for targeted interventions, (2) optimized simulation protocols for clinical training, and (3) a scalable computational platform adaptable to evolving nursing curricula. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will enhance the precision of pre-nursing education, directly contributing to improved student outcomes and, ultimately, higher-quality patient care through better-prepared nursing candidates. The computational pipelines developed will be shared openly with allied health programs, extending the project’s impact across health professions education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in Nursing.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic relationship between digital communication platforms and emergent linguistic phenomena, focusing on how decentralized, large-scale online interactions drive rapid syntactic and semantic shifts in understudied multilingual contexts. While traditional sociolinguistic frameworks have examined language change in physical communities, the computational demands of analyzing real-time, cross-platform digital discourse—particularly in low-resource languages and non-standard dialects—remain a critical barrier. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process terabytes of timestamped textual data from social media, messaging apps, and collaborative platforms across five linguistically diverse regions, targeting communities with limited prior documentation of their digital linguistic practices. A hybrid methodology combining transformer-based neural architectures for morphosyntactic annotation, agent-based modeling of lexical diffusion networks, and graph-theoretic analysis of semantic field evolution will be implemented. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle code-switching patterns, non-Latin scripts, and platform-specific orthographic variations, with iterative model training conducted on GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for detecting latent grammatical innovations in noisy, multilingual digital corpora; (2) quantitative models correlating platform affordances (e.g., character limits, reaction features) with rates of semantic change; and (3) an open-access repository of annotated datasets representing under-resourced digital language varieties. By elucidating the computational signatures of online language adaptation, this work aims to advance theoretical understanding of how technosocial systems shape linguistic diversity while providing practical tools for educators and developers working with marginalized language communities in digital spaces. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive graph computations, parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams, and large-scale comparative simulations across linguistic subsystems.
cip_title: Linguistic, Comparative, and Related Language Studies and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in linguistic, comparative, and related language studies and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic pricing strategies for small businesses operating in highly volatile markets, where traditional analytical tools fail to account for real-time data streams and complex interdependencies between consumer behavior, competitor actions, and supply chain fluctuations. Small enterprises often lack the computational infrastructure to process large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—such as social media trends, live transaction logs, and competitor pricing feeds—necessary to adapt pricing models at the speed required for competitive advantage. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this study will develop a machine learning framework integrating reinforcement learning and agent-based modeling to simulate market dynamics and test adaptive pricing algorithms under diverse scenarios. The computational approach will involve parallelized training of deep reinforcement learning agents on historical and synthetic datasets, augmented by real-time data ingestion to refine decision policies. Agent-based models will emulate interactions between small businesses, consumers, and competitors within a virtual marketplace, enabling the exploration of emergent pricing behaviors and systemic risks. Expected outcomes include scalable, open-source tools for small businesses to deploy adaptive pricing strategies with minimal computational overhead, as well as insights into the resilience of different pricing models under supply chain shocks or demand volatility. By bridging gaps in computational economics and entrepreneurship, this project aims to democratize access to advanced analytics for small enterprises, fostering equitable competition in data-driven markets. The use of HPC is critical to manage the complexity of simulating thousands of concurrent market agents, processing terabyte-scale datasets, and iterating pricing algorithms with low-latency responsiveness—tasks infeasible with conventional infrastructure. Results will contribute to interdisciplinary research at the intersection of behavioral economics, operations research, and machine learning, while directly supporting entrepreneurial agility in rapidly evolving sectors.
cip_title: Entrepreneurial and Small Business Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in enterprise management and entrepreneurship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Bovine Respiratory Disease Complex (BRDC) poses significant challenges to livestock health and agricultural productivity, driven by multifaceted interactions between viral and bacterial pathogens, host immune responses, and environmental stressors. Current gaps in understanding disease mechanisms and predicting clinical outcomes stem from limitations in analyzing complex biological datasets and modeling dynamic host-pathogen systems. This project proposes an integrated computational approach to investigate BRDC pathogenesis and optimize intervention strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Leveraging multi-omics datasets—including whole-genome sequencing, metatranscriptomics, and host proteomics from infected cattle—we will develop machine learning models to identify genetic markers of pathogen virulence and host susceptibility. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural interactions between viral envelope proteins and host receptors, enabling virtual screening of small-molecule inhibitors. These computational workflows require significant parallel processing capabilities and large-scale memory allocation to manage terabytes of sequencing data, simulate nanosecond-scale protein dynamics, and train deep neural networks. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for BRDC risk stratification, a curated database of pathogen genomic variants linked to clinical outcomes, and candidate compounds for therapeutic development. By elucidating critical pathways in disease progression, this work will advance precision veterinary medicine and inform targeted prevention protocols. The project also provides pre-veterinary students with training in computational biology, bridging gaps between traditional veterinary education and data-driven agricultural research. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to overcome current computational bottlenecks, ensuring robust analysis of biological complexity while fostering translational outcomes for animal health and sustainable livestock management.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in veterinary medicine.

abstract: Statistical analysis of high-dimensional and complex datasets presents significant computational challenges, particularly in settings requiring uncertainty quantification or model-based inference. This project seeks to develop and implement scalable Bayesian methods for high-dimensional statistical learning, with applications to large-scale biomedical and environmental datasets. The research addresses two critical bottlenecks: (1) efficient sampling from posterior distributions in models with millions of parameters, and (2) robust model comparison techniques for hierarchical models with complex dependency structures. The computational approach combines adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms with variational inference techniques, leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed computing paradigms. Key innovations include the development of parallel tempered MCMC chains with automated tuning mechanisms, gradient-based variational approximations for structured latent variable models, and distributed implementations of Bayesian stacking for model averaging. Proposed implementations will utilize Python-based frameworks augmented with CUDA-optimized kernels for critical computational routines, with validation performed through synthetic datasets and case studies in genomic epidemiology and spatial extreme value analysis. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable systematic benchmarking against existing methods, large-scale simulation studies to assess frequentist properties of Bayesian procedures, and analysis of whole-genome sequencing data with complex phenotypic interactions. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for large-scale Bayesian computation, theoretical insights into the scalability of approximate inference methods, and applied contributions to statistical methodology for high-dimensional biomarker studies. This work directly addresses the growing need for statistically rigorous yet computationally feasible approaches to modern data challenges, with particular emphasis on maintaining uncertainty quantification at scale. Successful implementation will provide both methodological advances in computational statistics and practical tools for researchers working with massive, complex datasets across scientific domains.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and statistics or a specialization which draws from mathematics and statistics. Includes instruction in calculus, linear algebra, numerical analysis and partial differential equations, discrete mathematics, probability theory, statistics, computing, and other related topics.

abstract: Cellular morphology analysis in cytopathology remains a cornerstone of early cancer detection, yet current diagnostic workflows rely heavily on manual microscopic evaluation by cytotechnologists, a process prone to variability and scalability challenges. This project proposes the development of a deep learning framework to automate the identification of subtle cellular anomalies in cytological specimens, with a focus on understudied precursor lesions of pancreaticobiliary malignancies—a diagnostically challenging area with high clinical urgency. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to train three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) on volumetric digitized slide data from thin-layer liquid cytology samples, integrating z-stack microscopy imaging to capture subcellular spatial relationships often missed in traditional 2D analysis. The computational workflow will process multi-terabyte whole-slide image datasets, implementing distributed training protocols to optimize model convergence while preserving rare anomaly signatures through synthetic data augmentation. A novel graph-based attention mechanism will be developed to mimic cytotechnologists' hierarchical evaluation patterns, prioritizing regions of interest while maintaining whole-slide context. Validation will involve benchmarking against consensus annotations from expert cytopathologists and correlating algorithmic predictions with longitudinal patient outcomes. Successful implementation could establish a paradigm shift in cytopathology screening by enabling rapid, quantitative analysis of high-dimensional cytomorphological features, potentially identifying novel digital biomarkers for early malignancy prediction. The proposed computational pipeline would also provide an open-source toolkit for adaptive model refinement, allowing integration with diverse laboratory information systems. By bridging computational pathology with clinical cytotechnology practice, this work addresses a critical gap in diagnostic oncology while advancing computational methods for high-content cytological data analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with pathologists to detect changes in body cells that may indicate, and permit diagnosis of, the early development of cancers and other diseases. Includes instruction in biochemistry, microbiology, applied mathematics, microscopy, slide preparation, identification of cellular structures and abnormalities, and laboratory procedures and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and cultural evolution of liturgical music in underrepresented religious traditions through computational analysis, focusing on how acoustic, melodic, and lyrical patterns correlate with communal worship practices. While existing scholarship often prioritizes textual or historical analysis of religious music, this study adopts an interdisciplinary computational humanities approach to analyze large-scale audio datasets, ethnographic recordings, and historical scores from lesser-studied traditions, including Indigenous and diasporic rituals. The core research problem lies in identifying how sonic elements—such as rhythm, pitch, and timbre—mediate spiritual experiences and communal participation, and how these elements adapt to sociocultural shifts, technological change, or environmental constraints. To address this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze terabytes of audio data using machine learning models trained to detect acoustic features, semantic themes in lyrics, and performative context. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate the diffusion of musical practices across virtual communities, incorporating variables like migration, oral transmission, and intercultural contact. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated liturgical music, predictive models of cultural transmission, and frameworks for quantifying the relationship between musical complexity and participatory worship dynamics. These results will advance scholarly understanding of music’s role in sustaining religious identity amid globalization, while offering preservation strategies for endangered traditions. The scale of audio processing, parallelized simulations, and deep learning tasks necessitates HPC capabilities, as traditional computing infrastructure cannot handle the project’s data volume or real-time analysis demands. By integrating computational methods with ethnomusicology and anthropology, this research bridges a critical gap in studies of religious practice, offering novel tools for interdisciplinary humanities scholarship.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious music and worship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in credit risk assessment frameworks by integrating high-dimensional, non-traditional data sources with dynamic macroeconomic indicators, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome computational bottlenecks in real-time decision systems. Traditional credit scoring models rely on static financial histories and fail to adapt to rapidly evolving market conditions or incorporate unstructured data such as transactional behavior patterns, supply chain interdependencies, and sentiment signals from financial communications. The proposed computational approach employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex relationships between borrowers, lenders, and interconnected financial entities, while deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract risk-relevant insights from regulatory filings, customer service interactions, and collateral documentation. Agent-based simulations will further test systemic stability under stress scenarios involving cascading defaults. HPC resources are critical for training multi-modal machine learning architectures on terabyte-scale datasets spanning 10 years of global credit transactions, insurance claims, and real estate collateral records, as well as for optimizing hyperparameters across distributed GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include a prototype AI-driven credit allocation platform capable of reducing Type I/II errors in default prediction by 15–20% compared to industry-standard models, alongside computational frameworks to quantify ethical trade-offs in algorithmic lending. The project aims to provide financial institutions with tools to enhance credit accessibility for underserved sectors while maintaining portfolio resilience, directly supporting the integration of ESG (environmental, social, governance) metrics into automated credit management systems. By advancing scalable methods to process heterogeneous financial data, this work bridges gaps between computational finance, regulatory technology, and ethical AI—a niche with growing relevance as credit systems confront climate-related disruptions and geopolitical volatility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and/or manage operations concerning personal and corporate credit, collateral, loan processing, and related financial agency communications. Includes instruction in general finance and banking principles, insurance, real estate, taxation, business law and regulations, quantitative methods, financial computer systems applications, database management, communications skills, business and office management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands in advanced drafting and design engineering workflows, particularly for complex, multi-scale simulations and generative design optimization. Traditional computational tools often struggle with the high-dimensional parameter spaces and real-time iterative modeling required for modern engineering applications, such as optimizing additive manufacturing processes or simulating multi-physics systems in smart infrastructure. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale parametric studies, topology optimization, and machine learning-driven design exploration. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and graph-based neural networks to model material behaviors, thermal stresses, and fluid-structure interactions across diverse engineering scenarios. These methods will be integrated into a unified computational framework using containerized workflows to maximize scalability on HPC clusters. Key outcomes include the development of adaptive meshing algorithms to reduce simulation overhead and the creation of a generative AI pipeline for automated design refinement. The project will validate these tools through case studies in aerospace component design and sustainable building systems, collaborating with industry partners to benchmark performance against conventional methods. By providing open-access computational workflows optimized for parallel architectures, this work aims to democratize access to advanced simulation capabilities for academic and small-industry users. The requested HPC resources will directly support training the next generation of design engineers in computational techniques while accelerating the translation of theoretical models into practical, resource-efficient engineering solutions. Anticipated impacts include reduced prototyping costs, improved energy efficiency in manufactured systems, and enhanced educational resources for computational design curricula.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in drafting/design engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic processes for hydrocarbon upgrading is hindered by the multiscale nature of reaction networks, which span molecular interactions to reactor-scale hydrodynamics. Current computational models struggle to integrate these scales due to prohibitive resource demands, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable coupled molecular dynamics (MD) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of catalytic systems under industrially relevant conditions. By employing hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization, we will resolve atomic-scale surface reactions while capturing macroscale transport phenomena in multiphase reactor environments. Machine learning surrogates will accelerate parameter estimation for rate constants and adsorption equilibria, informed by quantum mechanics calculations on key intermediates. The resulting multiscale framework will predict catalyst performance metrics (e.g., selectivity, deactivation) and optimize reactor configurations for methane pyrolysis—a promising pathway to low-carbon hydrogen production. Successful implementation will provide a validated computational toolkit for accelerating the design of intensified chemical processes, directly supporting energy transition goals through reduced computational trial-and-error. Access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory architectures is critical for managing the 10^6-core-hour requirements of cross-scale simulations spanning nanoseconds to process timescales. This work bridges a critical gap in process systems engineering by enabling first-principles prediction of catalytic reactor behavior, with potential applications in petrochemicals, carbon capture, and renewable fuel synthesis.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Infectious diseases caused by microbial agents such as viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites remain a critical global health challenge, necessitating rapid and precise identification of pathogens to guide clinical interventions. Traditional microbiological methods, while foundational, often struggle with the complexity and variability of microbial genomes, slow turnaround times, and the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational workflows for analyzing large-scale genomic and metagenomic datasets derived from clinical samples. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating machine learning models to predict antimicrobial resistance (AMR) patterns from pathogen genome sequences and (2) optimizing metagenomic classification pipelines to detect co-infections and rare pathogens in complex patient samples. Computational methods will include the deployment of neural networks trained on curated genomic databases, probabilistic modeling for strain-level identification, and parallelized alignment algorithms to process sequencing data from multi-pathogen communities. The HPC infrastructure will enable the handling of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce analysis runtime from days to hours, and improve the resolution of microbial community dynamics in infections. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel genetic markers linked to AMR in priority pathogens such as *Staphylococcus aureus* and *Candida auris*, as well as scalable tools for real-time diagnostics in clinical settings. By integrating genomic data with patient metadata, this work aims to enhance the accuracy of microbial diagnostics, inform targeted treatment strategies, and contribute to global surveillance efforts for emerging infectious diseases. The requested computing resources are critical to managing the computational burden of these analyses, ensuring reproducibility, and enabling translational impact in clinical microbiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the isolation and identification of microbial agents that cause infectious disease, including viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing urban park design and management through computational modeling of human-environment interactions in high-density recreational spaces. As cities face increasing pressure to balance green space accessibility with ecological sustainability, traditional planning frameworks struggle to account for dynamic variables such as shifting visitor demographics, climate-driven vegetation stress, and real-time infrastructure usage patterns. The research employs agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate visitor behavior, resource consumption, and landscape wear patterns across temporal scales. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-source data streams—including anonymized mobile device location pings, IoT sensor networks from smart park infrastructure, and satellite-derived vegetation health indices—at metropolitan-scale resolutions. By developing a predictive digital twin framework capable of testing hypothetical management interventions, the project aims to identify design configurations that maximize equitable access while minimizing maintenance costs and environmental degradation. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for park administrators and novel metrics for quantifying recreational space resilience under climate change scenarios. This computationally intensive approach bridges urban planning, human geography, and environmental informatics, offering evidence-based strategies for maintaining vital public spaces in rapidly urbanizing regions. The proposed models will undergo validation against observational data from three municipal park systems, with particular focus on predicting emergent congestion patterns during peak usage periods and long-term soil compaction risks. Results will directly inform municipal decision-making processes while advancing methodological innovations in the computational analysis of leisure space dynamics.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Facilities Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in parks, recreation, and leisure facilities management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Mental health counseling faces a critical challenge in predicting and optimizing treatment outcomes for clients with complex, intersecting psychosocial needs. Current approaches to personalized intervention design rely on static clinical guidelines and limited demographic data, which fail to account for dynamic behavioral patterns, real-time environmental stressors, and nuanced interpersonal dynamics that influence therapeutic progress. This project proposes to address this gap by developing a computational framework that integrates multimodal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), ecological momentary assessments (EMAs), and semi-structured session transcripts—to model client-counselor interactions and predict intervention efficacy. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze linguistic markers in session dialogues, coupled with graph neural networks (GNNs) to map temporal relationships between life events, emotional states, and therapeutic strategies. A federated learning architecture will be implemented to preserve client confidentiality while training models across distributed datasets from community mental health clinics. The computational pipeline will additionally incorporate agent-based modeling to simulate how micro-level counseling decisions propagate to long-term mental health outcomes across diverse socioeconomic contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to identify clients at risk of treatment stagnation, (2) dynamic intervention recommendations tailored to individual resilience profiles, and (3) quantitative insights into how counselor communication styles mediate client engagement. By bridging computational psychiatry with counseling practice, this work aims to establish a scalable infrastructure for data-driven mental health care while advancing methodological innovation in the analysis of therapeutic processes. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional data fusion, iterative model training across heterogeneous datasets, and large-scale validation required to ensure clinical relevance and equity in algorithmic recommendations.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide evaluations, referrals, and short-term counseling services to help people prevent or remediate personal problems, conflicts, and emotional crises. Includes instruction in human development, psychopathology, individual and group counseling, personality theory, career assessment, patient screening and referral, observation and testing techniques, interviewing skills, professional standards and ethics, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the intergenerational transmission of cultural narratives within Asian-American communities through large-scale textual and multimedia data. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how diasporic identities are preserved, adapted, or renegotiated across generations in digital and analog spaces, particularly in understudied subgroups such as Hmong-American and Filipino-American communities. Current scholarship lacks systematic methods to process the vast quantities of multilingual community archives, oral histories, social media content, and grassroots publications that capture these dynamic processes. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment and thematic analysis across multiple languages (e.g., Tagalog, Hmong, English code-switching patterns) with computer vision techniques to examine visual narratives in family photographs, community art, and short-form video content. Custom transformer models will be trained on curated corpora of Asian-American cultural production, while graph-based algorithms will map connections between historical migration patterns and contemporary digital storytelling practices. The scale of data—spanning 50,000+ digitized items from 15 community archives and 10TB of social media data—necessitates GPU-accelerated processing for transformer model fine-tuning and distributed storage solutions for metadata harmonization. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for quantifying cultural hybridity in diasporic contexts, 2) interactive visualizations of narrative evolution tied to geopolitical events and policy changes, and 3) public APIs to enable community organizations to query patterns in their own archival materials. By computationally modeling how trauma, resilience, and identity negotiation manifest across mediums and generations, this work will provide empirical grounding for theoretical debates about cultural preservation in Asian-American studies while developing reusable tools for ethnic-specific digital humanities research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of Asian population groups who have immigrated to the United States and Canada, or sought refugee asylum, from the colonial period to the present, and including Chinese-Americans, Japanese-Americans, Korean-Americans, Vietnamese-Americans, Cambodian-Americans, and others.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic customer engagement strategies in tourism and travel services through the integration of real-time behavioral analytics and hyper-personalized marketing simulations. The tourism sector faces challenges in balancing operational efficiency with individualized customer experiences, particularly as fluctuating demand, seasonal trends, and heterogeneous traveler preferences strain traditional marketing models. Current approaches often rely on static segmentation or heuristic-based decision-making, limiting responsiveness to real-time data streams from booking platforms, social media, and IoT-enabled hotel systems. To address this gap, we propose developing an adaptive computational framework that combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate multi-channel customer interactions at scale. The ABM component will emulate traveler decision pathways influenced by demographic variables, situational constraints, and real-time pricing signals, while DRL agents will iteratively optimize promotional offers, room allocation policies, and service bundling strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets from 12+ tourism partners (encompassing ~2.3 million annual transactions) and executing parallelized simulations across diverse market scenarios. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to model cross-customer influence networks and containerized microservices for A/B testing virtual campaigns. Expected outcomes include a predictive dashboard for dynamic pricing elasticity thresholds and evidence-based guidelines for automating personalized upselling interventions. By quantifying trade-offs between operational resource allocation and customer lifetime value metrics, this work aims to establish scalable decision-support tools for mid-tier hospitality businesses lacking enterprise-grade analytics infrastructure. The project will contribute methodological innovations in applying swarm intelligence paradigms to service operations while addressing sector-specific challenges in perishable inventory management and experience-driven consumer behavior.
cip_title: Tourism and Travel Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide direct retail services to hotel and motel clients and customers in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in the principles of hotel/motel operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, and basic office management.

abstract: Health system pharmacy administration faces critical challenges in optimizing medication therapy management (MTM) for complex patient populations, particularly in balancing efficacy, safety, and cost under dynamic clinical conditions. Current approaches to protocol design and real-time decision support often rely on static guidelines that inadequately account for patient heterogeneity, evolving biomarker data, and multi-drug interactions. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and optimize MTM strategies across diverse patient cohorts. The research will integrate electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacogenomic profiles, and real-time physiological monitoring data to train machine learning models predicting individual drug response trajectories. These models will inform Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of hypothetical therapy adjustments under varying clinical constraints (e.g., renal function fluctuations, drug shortages). A novel optimization algorithm will identify Pareto-optimal treatment protocols balancing clinical outcomes, adverse event risks, and institutional costs. The computational workflow requires HPC capabilities for parallel processing of large-scale EHR datasets (>1 million patient-years), high-dimensional parameter space exploration in pharmacodynamic modeling, and real-time recalibration of ensemble models. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for personalized dose adjustment in high-risk medications (e.g., anticoagulants, antimicrobials), quantitative evidence for revising health-system-wide pharmacy protocols, and open-source software enabling adaptive MTM optimization. This work will directly address gaps in clinical decision support for precision medication management, with potential to reduce adverse drug events by 15-30% in target populations while maintaining cost-effectiveness. The requested computing resources are essential for achieving sufficient model granularity and validation rigor to meet regulatory standards for clinical implementation.
cip_definition: Research focused on Health System Pharmacy Administration

abstract: Pediatric pathologies, particularly those manifesting during fetal development and early childhood, present unique diagnostic challenges due to the dynamic interplay of genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors. Current limitations in understanding the molecular trajectories of these diseases stem from the complexity of multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and histopathological imaging) and the computational demands of integrating such data at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of pediatric disease mechanisms, focusing on rare developmental disorders and therapy-resistant pediatric cancers. The research will employ a multi-modal computational approach, integrating bulk and single-cell sequencing data with spatially resolved histopathology images to map disease-specific molecular networks. Machine learning frameworks, including graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures, will be trained to identify cross-modal biomarkers and predict cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of high-resolution whole-slide imaging data, performing large-scale genomic variant prioritization, and simulating developmental pathways using systems biology models. HPC resources will enable parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, distributed model training, and in silico hypothesis testing, which are infeasible on local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel diagnostic signatures for congenital anomalies, stratification markers for pediatric tumor subtypes, and mechanistic insights into dysregulated developmental pathways. These findings will be validated against clinical cohorts and experimental models, with the goal of translating computational predictions into targeted molecular assays. By establishing scalable analytical pipelines for pediatric pathology, this work aims to advance precision diagnostics and therapeutic strategies for understudied childhood diseases, while generating publicly accessible tools for the research community. The requested computing resources are critical to overcoming current bottlenecks in data integration and model optimization, ensuring robust, reproducible analyses that bridge computational discovery and clinical application.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory diagnosis of diseases that occur during fetal growth, infancy, and child development, based on knowledge of general pathology, normal growth and development, and pediatric medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and fitting of personalized ophthalmic prosthetics and corrective lenses using biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Current opticianry practices rely on static anatomical measurements and generalized optical corrections, which often fail to account for dynamic factors such as micro-movements of ocular implants, tear film dynamics, or tissue deformation under mechanical stress from contact lenses. To address this, we propose integrating high-resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT) data, finite element modeling (FEM), and real-time sensor feedback from smart contact lens prototypes into a unified computational platform. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate the multiphysics interactions between ocular tissues, prosthetic materials, and optical surfaces at micron-scale resolutions across diverse patient anatomies. Machine learning models will be trained on a curated dataset of 10,000+ de-identified patient scans to predict optimal lens curvature, material stiffness, and edge profiles that minimize corneal abrasion risks while maximizing optical clarity. A parallelized optimization algorithm will iteratively refine designs using feedback from coupled optical-ray-tracing and biomechanical stability simulations. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific lens designs that reduce adaptation periods by 40% compared to conventional methods, as well as novel metrics for quantifying dynamic fit quality. This work bridges opticianry, computational biomechanics, and materials science, offering a paradigm shift from reactive adjustments to predictive, physics-informed prosthetics customization. The resulting open-source tools will enable opticians to leverage computational insights during clinical decision-making, advancing precision eye care for patients with complex ocular geometries or post-surgical anatomical variations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to address critical challenges in precision medicine by integrating multi-omics data with clinical and imaging datasets. The research problem centers on the computational limitations of current methods for analyzing heterogeneous biomedical data, which often fail to capture complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and phenotypic variables. These bottlenecks hinder the identification of robust biomarkers and predictive models for chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disorders and type 2 diabetes. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement advanced machine learning models, including graph neural networks and federated learning architectures, optimized for multi-modal data fusion. The computational workflow will process large-scale genomic sequences (whole exome and RNA-seq), electronic health records (EHRs), and high-resolution medical imaging data from diverse patient cohorts. Key methodological innovations include parallelized feature extraction pipelines, federated model training across distributed clinical datasets to preserve privacy, and dynamic resource allocation for hyperparameter optimization. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive operations, enabling rapid iteration of deep learning architectures, and scaling analyses to population-level datasets (>100,000 patients). Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for disease progression and treatment response, open-source tools for reproducible multi-omics integration, and novel computational biomarkers with clinical interpretability. This work will directly advance translational informatics by providing researchers and clinicians with scalable methods to derive actionable insights from complex biomedical data. The requested computing resources will support critical path experiments in GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale simulation of biological networks, and validation against longitudinal health outcomes. By addressing computational barriers in multi-omics research, this project aims to accelerate the development of precision diagnostics and contribute to evidence-based decision support systems in clinical care.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to health and/or biomedical research,  and the development of advanced database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in biomedical and/or health sciences; information science and technology; social and behavioral sciences; biomedical/health information science and technology; human factors and socio-technical systems;  applied social, behavioral, and information science and technology; and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying manual somatic bodywork therapies, such as Rolfing/Structural Integration and Hellerwork, using advanced computational modeling. Despite widespread clinical use, the field lacks rigorous quantitative frameworks to explain how these modalities interact with fascial networks, neuromuscular feedback loops, and autonomic regulation. Current limitations stem from the complex, multiscale nature of these interactions—spanning molecular signaling in connective tissues to whole-body postural dynamics—which cannot be adequately analyzed through traditional experimental methods alone. We propose developing a high-resolution finite element model of human myofascial anatomy integrated with neural control systems to simulate tissue deformation patterns, stress propagation, and autonomic responses during therapeutic interventions. The model will incorporate patient-specific MRI-derived fascial architecture data, viscoelastic material properties from ex vivo tensile testing, and neural circuit parameters from existing electrophysiological datasets. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize parameter space exploration and identify critical therapeutic leverage points. High-performance computing resources are essential for running large-scale simulations of nonlinear tissue behavior under varying load conditions, as well as for training predictive models that map manual input parameters (e.g., force vectors, velocity) to systemic physiological outcomes (e.g., heart rate variability, cytokine profiles). Expected outcomes include the first quantitative framework for predicting optimal pressure-depth relationships in fascial manipulation, evidence-based criteria for sequencing multi-modal interventions, and mechanistic insights into how manual therapies modulate inflammatory pathways via mechanotransduction. This work will establish computational foundations for personalized somatic therapy protocols while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of biomechanics, systems biology, and manual medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in medical billing workflows, specifically the high rates of claim denials and delayed reimbursements that burden healthcare providers and insurers. Current processes for verifying insurance eligibility, coding diagnoses, and reconciling payer requirements remain error-prone due to fragmented data systems, evolving regulatory policies, and heterogeneous payer-specific rules. We propose developing a machine learning (HPC) framework to automate and optimize claim adjudication by integrating multi-modal data streams: structured electronic health records (EHR), unstructured clinical documentation, payer policy databases, and historical claims outcomes. High-performance computing resources are critical to process terabytes of longitudinal claims data spanning 10+ years from partner healthcare networks, train transformer-based models for context-aware coding suggestions, and simulate denial risk under dynamic policy scenarios. Computational workflows will include natural language processing (NLP) to extract billing-relevant context from clinician notes, graph neural networks to model interdependencies between diagnosis codes and payer-specific reimbursement criteria, and reinforcement learning to iteratively refine claim submission strategies. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive denial risk dashboard for medical billers, an open-source tool for automated code validation against real-time payer rules, and a policy impact simulator to quantify how proposed regulatory changes might affect revenue cycles. By reducing manual claim reviews and resubmissions, this research aims to decrease administrative costs by an estimated 15–20% in pilot healthcare systems while improving compliance transparency. The computational pipelines developed will establish scalable methods for adaptive billing analytics in an era of rapidly shifting healthcare reimbursement landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and manage the medical and health insurance operations in a medical office, health care facility, health maintenance organization, or insurance provider. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes; health insurance law, policy, and regulations; insurance records and paperwork administration; insurance office administration; health/medical insurance software applications; personnel supervision; business mathematics; billing and collection procedures; medical terminology; and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of simulating large-scale, multi-threat homeland security scenarios to enhance national preparedness and infrastructure resilience. Current computational models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between physical infrastructure, cyber networks, and human decision-making during complex emergencies, such as coordinated cyber-physical attacks, cascading infrastructure failures, or climate-aggravated disasters. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an integrated high-performance computing (HPC) framework capable of modeling hybrid threat scenarios with unprecedented spatial, temporal, and operational granularity. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, stochastic optimization, and machine learning to simulate (1) adversarial behavior patterns in cyber and physical domains, (2) real-time critical infrastructure interdependencies (e.g., power grids, transportation systems), and (3) emergency response coordination under uncertainty. The HPC environment will enable parallelized execution of multi-scale simulations, incorporating terabyte-scale datasets from historical incidents, IoT sensors, and synthetic threat landscapes. Key innovations include adaptive graph neural networks to predict cascading failures in interdependent systems and physics-informed reinforcement learning to optimize resource allocation during evolving crises. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for federal and state agencies to stress-test defense protocols, quantify systemic vulnerabilities, and prioritize mitigation investments. The computational outputs will directly inform updates to the National Infrastructure Protection Plan and regional disaster response frameworks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work will advance predictive capabilities for emerging asymmetric threats while establishing scalable methodologies for security-critical simulations. Successful implementation requires dedicated access to HPC resources supporting 10,000+ core-hour workloads, large-memory nodes for graph-based analytics, and high-throughput data pipelines for real-time scenario perturbation testing.
cip_definition: A program focusing on security policy, planning and operations dedicated to the protection of U.S. territory, assets, infrastructure, institutions and citizens from external threats. Includes instruction in national security policy, government relations, intelligence, law enforcement, security technology, communications and information technology, homeland security planning and operations, disaster planning and applications to specific threat scenarios.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of industrial and commercial piping systems, including fire protection sprinkler networks, through high-fidelity computational modeling and simulation. Current practices in pipefitting and sprinkler system design rely heavily on empirical guidelines, simplified analytical models, and iterative physical testing, which can lead to suboptimal material usage, energy inefficiency, and unanticipated failure modes under dynamic operational or emergency conditions. To address these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating multiphysics simulations to analyze fluid dynamics, thermal stresses, and structural integrity in complex piping networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of system behavior under diverse scenarios, including transient flow regimes, water hammer effects, and extreme thermal gradients in steam or high-temperature systems. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will be coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) to evaluate interactions between fluid flow characteristics, pipe material responses, and joint performance. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize system layouts, component sizing, and material selection while adhering to safety codes and standards. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from lab-scale piping testbeds and historical failure case studies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish predictive models that reduce design iteration cycles, improve failure resistance in sprinkler systems during fire events, and minimize resource waste in pipe network installations. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for vocational training programs and a database of optimized design templates for common industrial configurations, directly enhancing both educational resources and industry practices in pipefitting technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, install, and test industrial and commercial piping systems and automatic fire and exposure protection systems. Includes instruction in water systems, steam systems, heating and cooling systems, lubricating systems, piping materials, installation tools operation and maintenance, valve installation and repair, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the integration and analysis of multi-domain intelligence data to enhance real-time strategic decision-making in military operations. The core research problem lies in the growing complexity of synthesizing heterogeneous data streams—including signals intelligence (SIGINT), geospatial intelligence (GEOINT), open-source intelligence (OSINT), and operational telemetry—into cohesive, actionable insights. Current manual and semi-automated methods struggle to scale with the volume, velocity, and variety of modern intelligence inputs, leading to latency and incomplete threat assessments. To address this, the project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid machine learning architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing, graph neural networks, and anomaly detection algorithms. These methods will be trained on classified and synthetic datasets to model adversarial intent, identify cross-domain threat patterns, and predict escalation scenarios. A key innovation involves dynamically weighting intelligence sources based on real-time reliability metrics and contextual relevance to mission objectives. The computational demands of processing petabytes of unstructured data, maintaining low-latency inference pipelines, and simulating multi-theater conflict scenarios necessitate distributed GPU-accelerated workflows and in-memory data architectures. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of reducing decision cycle times by 40-60% in simulated operational environments, quantified through A/B testing against legacy tools. The research will also yield novel benchmarks for evaluating AI-driven intelligence fusion under uncertainty, contributing to broader methodological advances in computational strategic studies. By enabling rapid, evidence-based prioritization of threats and resources, this work aims to strengthen situational awareness and adaptive planning in contested, information-dense environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the management, analysis and use of national-level, theatre-level, and international intelligence and related policy issues. Includes instruction in intelligence organization and management, strategic uses of intelligence, management of intelligence systems and assets, command and control, joint intelligence operations, electronic and signals intelligence, threat assessment and estimation, intelligence analysis and reporting, counterintelligence, and studies of specific regions and situations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of embedded systems in IoT and edge computing applications necessitates advanced methodologies for hardware-software co-design. Traditional approaches often struggle to balance performance, energy efficiency, and scalability, leading to suboptimal system configurations. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a novel framework for optimizing embedded system architectures. The research will employ large-scale simulations to model interactions between hardware components and software algorithms under varying workloads. Machine learning techniques, including neural networks and genetic algorithms, will be integrated to predict optimal resource allocation strategies and identify system bottlenecks. Additionally, FPGA-based prototyping emulated on HPC clusters will enable rapid iteration and testing of candidate designs. The computational demands of these tasks—such as parallelized circuit simulation, real-time data processing for adaptive algorithms, and multi-objective optimization—require access to HPC infrastructure with robust processing capabilities and distributed memory systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for co-design optimization, demonstrated through case studies on edge computing nodes and IoT sensor networks. The project aims to reduce development cycles by 30–40% while improving energy efficiency by 20% compared to existing methodologies. By providing insights into efficient hardware-software integration, this research will contribute to the development of next-generation embedded systems capable of supporting advanced applications in smart infrastructure and industrial automation. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the intensive computational workloads inherent in simulating complex electronic systems and training data-driven models at scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational limitations hindering real-time, high-resolution analysis of dynamic vascular structures using 4D flow MRI. While 4D flow MRI provides unparalleled insights into hemodynamic patterns critical for diagnosing cerebrovascular pathologies, aneurysms, and congenital heart defects, existing processing pipelines struggle with the massive datasets (often exceeding 10 GB/study) and the computational demands of resolving submillimeter spatiotemporal features. Current clinical workflows rely on time-averaged metrics, discarding potentially diagnostic transient flow phenomena. We propose developing a GPU-accelerated computational framework to enable voxel-wise, time-resolved hemodynamic profiling by integrating compressed sensing reconstruction with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). The framework will leverage high-performance computing resources to train PINNs on synthetic flow datasets generated through computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of patient-specific vascular geometries, then fine-tune models on clinical 4D flow MRI data. Key innovations include a hybrid architecture combining convolutional networks for spatial feature extraction with recurrent modules for temporal coherence, regularized by Navier-Stokes-derived loss functions. This approach aims to overcome noise amplification and undersampling artifacts while preserving physiological flow patterns. Successfully implemented, the platform could reduce MRI acquisition times by 40-60% through optimized k-space sampling strategies validated via virtual MRI simulations. The computational outputs will be integrated into an open-source toolkit for quantitative hemodynamic analysis, providing clinicians with novel biomarkers for early detection of flow-mediated vascular remodeling. By bridging MRI physics, biomechanics, and deep learning, this work advances precision imaging capabilities for complex vascular pathologies beyond the scope of conventional radiological techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals who are AART-certified radiological technicians to utilize MRI technology to obtain still and moving images of various vascular structures in the human body that aid the physician in the diagnosis or treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in MRI imaging, sectional anatomy and pathology, MRI technology, MRI techniques and procedures, MRI physics, and clinical training.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision dentistry through the development of a computational framework for modeling oral microbiome dynamics and their interactions with host immune responses. The oral microbiome plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of dental caries, periodontal disease, and systemic conditions, but its complex, time-dependent behavior under varying clinical interventions remains poorly understood. Current limitations stem from the inability to integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with patient-specific factors (genetics, diet, treatment history) at scale. To address this, we propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach to simulate microbial community shifts and host-pathogen interactions under clinically relevant scenarios. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of longitudinal microbiome datasets from ongoing clinical cohorts of high-caries-risk patients, employing neural ordinary differential equations to model metabolic networks and immune signaling pathways. Parallelized molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate how dental materials and antimicrobial agents influence biofilm mechanics and virulence factor expression. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to identify predictive biomarkers of dysbiosis, optimize personalized treatment schedules via reinforcement learning, and simulate the efficacy of novel bioactive dental composites. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time risk stratification in dental EHR systems and a validated in silico platform for testing preventive strategies without lengthy clinical trials. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models and large-scale parameter sweeps in sensitivity analyses—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. This research directly aligns with national priorities to reduce oral health disparities through computationally driven innovation, offering transformative potential for both clinical decision-making and mechanistic studies in dental medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of dentistry/dental medicine, encompassing the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases, disorders, and conditions of the oral cavity, maxillofacial area, and adjacent structures and their impact on the human body and health. Includes instruction in the basic biomedical sciences, occlusion, dental health and prevention, oral pathology, cariology, operative dentistry, oral radiology, principles of the various dental specialties, pain management, oral medicine, clinic and health care management, patient counseling, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The rapid evolution of dynamic web ecosystems demands scalable solutions to optimize resource allocation while balancing performance, security, and sustainability. Current web hosting infrastructures struggle to adapt to heterogeneous user demands, particularly for multimedia-rich applications requiring real-time personalization and low-latency delivery. This project proposes a novel computational framework to model and automate adaptive resource distribution across distributed web servers, integrating predictive analytics with energy-aware load balancing. The research focuses on developing machine learning models trained on multi-modal traffic patterns—including user interaction metadata, content type variability, and network latency metrics—to forecast server workloads and preemptively allocate computational resources. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating large-scale web environments under diverse stress scenarios, enabling parallelized testing of optimization algorithms that dynamically adjust CPU-GPU task partitioning, caching strategies, and edge-server coordination. The computational workflow will employ containerized microservices to emulate real-world web architectures, with Kubernetes orchestration scaled across HPC nodes to assess fault tolerance and energy efficiency. Expected outcomes include a benchmark dataset for web resource management, open-source tools for intelligent traffic routing, and quantitative guidelines for minimizing carbon footprints in data-intensive hosting environments. By bridging gaps between systems administration, environmental informatics, and human-computer interaction, this work aims to establish best practices for next-generation webmaster workflows while addressing understudied challenges in sustainable web infrastructure. The proposed methods could reduce server energy consumption by an estimated 15–30% in simulated high-traffic scenarios, with implications for improving accessibility and cost-effectiveness in academic, governmental, and enterprise web ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and maintain web servers and the hosted web pages at one or a group of web sites, and to function as designated webmasters. Includes instruction in computer systems and networks, server installation and maintenance, web page design and editing, information resources management, web policy and procedures, Internet applications of information systems security, user interfacing and usability research, and relevant management and communications skills.

abstract: The discovery and development of bioactive compounds from natural sources remain constrained by the vast structural diversity of natural products and the inefficiency of traditional bioassay-guided approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the identification of pharmacologically relevant compounds from plant, microbial, and marine-derived extracts through integrative computational strategies. We aim to address key bottlenecks in natural product drug discovery, including the prediction of bioactive metabolites, elucidation of structure-activity relationships, and prioritization of compounds for experimental validation. The computational workflow will employ molecular docking and virtual screening against disease-relevant protein targets (e.g., antimicrobial resistance proteins, oncogenic kinases), complemented by molecular dynamics simulations to assess binding stability and conformational dynamics. Machine learning models trained on curated phytochemical libraries and bioactivity datasets will predict novel bioactive scaffolds, while cheminformatics pipelines will analyze mass spectrometry and NMR spectral data to dereplicate known compounds and annotate unknowns. HPC resources will enable large-scale quantum mechanical calculations to model enzymatic interactions and predict biosynthetic pathways for prioritized leads. By integrating these approaches, the project will generate prioritized compound libraries for experimental testing, reducing reliance on resource-intensive trial-and-error methods. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel antimicrobial and anticancer candidates, insights into molecular mechanisms of ethnobotanically reported medicinal plants, and optimized protocols for computational bioprospecting. The requested computing infrastructure is critical to handle the terabytes of spectral data, perform millions of compound-target simulations, and train deep neural networks on complex phytochemical datasets—tasks infeasible with standard laboratory computing resources. This work will establish a scalable framework for natural product research, bridging computational innovation with experimental pharmacognosy to advance therapeutic discovery.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the relationship between large-scale neural circuit dynamics and cognitive dysfunction in neurodegenerative disorders, with a focus on Alzheimer’s disease. Despite advances in molecular and cellular neuroscience, a critical gap remains in understanding how synaptic and cellular pathologies propagate to disrupt network-level activity, leading to memory deficits. To address this, we propose integrating multiscale neurobiological data—including in vivo electrophysiology, structural connectivity maps, and molecular profiles of synaptic degradation—into a high-fidelity computational model of the hippocampus-prefrontal cortex network. The model will simulate neural population dynamics under healthy conditions and progressive neurodegenerative states, incorporating biophysically realistic neuron models and data-driven synaptic failure rates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of simulating 500,000+ neurons with spatially explicit connectivity, ion channel distributions, and activity-dependent plasticity rules. Simulations will run on GPU-accelerated nodes using the NEURON simulation environment, with parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds of synaptic loss that precipitate network instability. Machine learning pipelines will analyze simulation outputs to extract biomarkers of early network dysfunction, correlating them with behavioral outcomes from transgenic mouse models. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying network-level signatures predictive of cognitive decline prior to overt neurodegeneration and (2) mapping vulnerable circuit motifs that amplify pathological activity. This work will advance translational neuroscience by linking molecular-scale pathology to systems-level dysfunction, providing a computational framework to evaluate therapeutic strategies targeting network resilience. The requested resources will support 18 months of large-scale simulations, data assimilation, and model validation, enabling unprecedented resolution of spatiotemporal neural dynamics in disease progression. Results will be disseminated through open-source model releases and collaborations with experimental labs validating predictions in preclinical studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary scientific study of the molecular, structural, physiologic, cognitive, and behavioral aspects of the brain and nervous system. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, molecular and biochemical bases of information processing, behavioral neuroscience, biology of neuropsychiatric disorders, and applications to the clinical sciences and biomedical engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to advance fire safety in modern urban environments by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate fire dynamics, suppression systems, and structural failure thresholds in complex building architectures. The research addresses a critical gap in predictive tools for fire behavior in structures incorporating mixed-use designs, energy-efficient materials, and renewable energy systems—configurations that challenge conventional fire protection frameworks. Current models rely on simplified assumptions about fuel loads, airflow patterns, and material thermal degradation, limiting their applicability to contemporary construction practices. To overcome these limitations, the proposed work will implement parallelized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) to resolve multi-scale interactions between fire propagation, active suppression systems (e.g., water mist, gaseous agents), and load-bearing structural components. High-performance computing resources will enable parametric studies of fire scenarios across diverse architectural layouts, material composites, and ventilation configurations at temporal resolutions below 0.1 seconds. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to optimize sensor placement and real-time hazard prediction using simulation-derived training datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for fire department response planning, improved guidelines for fire-resistant material integration in sustainable building designs, and adaptive risk assessment frameworks for structures with integrated photovoltaic arrays or lithium-ion battery storage. By bridging fire science, materials engineering, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive fire systems design in next-generation urban infrastructure.
