cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and practice of firefighting systems, building construction and related resources as applied to fire prevention, control, and mitigation. Includes instruction in fire hydraulics and dynamics, fire protection structures and systems design, fire behavior and combustion, fire protection hydraulics and water supply, fire protection equipment and systems, building construction for fire protection, and fire apparatus.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of personalizing cosmetic treatments while minimizing damage to hair and skin, a persistent issue in cosmetology due to the biological and structural diversity of clients. Current approaches rely heavily on generalized product formulations and heuristic techniques, often resulting in suboptimal outcomes or unintended harm. To bridge this gap, the research proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity biophysical modeling, machine learning (ML), and large-scale data analytics to predict hyper-personalized treatment plans. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will simulate molecular interactions between common cosmetic agents (e.g., dyes, relaxers) and keratin structures across diverse hair types, informed by spectroscopic and microscopic datasets. Concurrently, a convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on 3D-scanned hair and skin samples to classify texture, porosity, and damage levels, enabling real-time recommendations during client consultations. A parallelized optimization algorithm will then iteratively refine treatment parameters (e.g., chemical concentrations, exposure times) to balance efficacy with safety thresholds. The computational pipeline will be validated against empirical data from partnered salons, incorporating feedback loops to enhance model accuracy. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive tool for licensed cosmetologists, reducing trial-and-error practices and fostering evidence-based decision-making. By elucidating microstructure-level dynamics of cosmetic interventions, the project also aims to establish foundational datasets for understudied hair types, addressing biases in existing beauty technology. The scalability of the models will further support future research into sustainable formulation design and virtual training environments, advancing both the scientific rigor and ethical standards of cosmetology practice.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to cut, trim, and style scalp, facial, and body hair; apply cosmetic preparations; perform manicures and pedicures; massage the head and extremities; and prepare for practice as licensed cosmetologists in specialized or full-service salons.  Includes instruction in hair cutting and styling, manicuring, pedicuring, facial treatments, shampooing, chemical applications, esthetics, shop management, sanitation and safety, customer service, and applicable professional and labor laws and regulations.

abstract: Gifted and talented students require highly individualized educational strategies to nurture their unique abilities, yet designing effective, scalable interventions remains a significant challenge. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning models that analyze multidimensional student data—including academic performance, psychometric assessments, and creative portfolios—to generate personalized learning pathways. Current methods for identifying giftedness and tailoring instruction often rely on manual, time-intensive processes, limiting educators’ capacity to address diverse needs efficiently. By integrating computational techniques with educational theory, this research aims to automate and refine the identification of gifted learners and the design of adaptive curricula. The computational approach will involve training deep neural networks on longitudinal datasets to predict student outcomes under varying pedagogical strategies, alongside agent-based modeling to simulate classroom dynamics and intervention efficacy. These models will require large-scale parallel processing to manage high-dimensional data and iterative optimization. The anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-source framework for generating evidence-based, individualized education plans (IEPs) for gifted students, (2) insights into the interplay between cognitive, social, and emotional factors in talent development, and (3) scalable tools to assist educators in dynamically adjusting instructional content. By enabling rapid analysis of complex educational datasets, HPC resources will facilitate real-time feedback mechanisms and robust validation of intervention strategies across diverse student populations. This work directly addresses gaps in teacher preparation for gifted education by providing empirically grounded computational tools that enhance pedagogical decision-making. The results will advance the integration of data-driven methodologies into special education practices, ultimately supporting equitable access to tailored learning experiences for high-ability students.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of the Gifted and Talented
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults exhibiting exceptional intellectual, psychomotor or artistic talent or potential, or who exhibit exceptional maturity or social leadership talents, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying gifted and talented students, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising gifted and talented students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Occupational medicine research requires robust computational approaches to address the complex interplay between workplace environments, occupational exposures, and health outcomes. This project seeks to develop predictive models to assess the long-term impacts of heterogeneous occupational hazards—such as chemical exposures, ergonomic stressors, and psychosocial factors—on worker health. Existing epidemiological methods often struggle to integrate multimodal data (e.g., sensor-derived exposure metrics, electronic health records, and workplace safety reports) or account for time-varying interactions between risk factors. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining machine learning (ML) and multiscale simulation. First, federated learning techniques will harmonize privacy-sensitive occupational health datasets from multiple institutions. Next, graph neural networks will model dynamic relationships between workplace conditions and subclinical biomarkers (e.g., inflammatory markers, pulmonary function trends). Agent-based simulations will then project how interventions like modified work schedules or ventilation upgrades alter long-term health risks across diverse worker populations. The computational workload necessitates parallelized training of deep learning architectures, large-scale optimization of intervention scenarios, and real-time analysis of streaming sensor data. Access to HPC resources with GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage will enable processing datasets spanning 10+ years of occupational health records (n > 200,000 workers) and high-resolution environmental monitoring. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identification of critical exposure thresholds for respiratory and musculoskeletal disorders, (2) predictive tools to prioritize workplace interventions, and (3) open-source software for scalable occupational risk analytics. This work will advance precision prevention strategies in occupational medicine, directly supporting the development of evidence-based workplace safety policies and reducing the burden of work-related illness.
cip_definition: Research focused on the maintenance of the health of workers, the ability to perform work, the arrangements of work, and the physical and chemical environments of the workplace. Includes instruction in data collection and management and the administration and regulation of occupational medical services. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing real-time communication workflows in frontline receptionist systems, with a focus on enhancing service quality and operational efficiency in high-volume business environments. Traditional receptionist workflows—spanning call routing, visitor management, and information dissemination—often face inefficiencies due to unpredictable demand patterns, cognitive overload among staff, and inconsistent adherence to organizational communication protocols. This project addresses these challenges by modeling dynamic interaction networks and simulating decision-making processes under variable stress and resource constraints. Using anonymized call logs, visitor logs, and sentiment analysis datasets from corporate reception hubs, we will train transformer-based models to predict optimal response strategies, automate routine tasks, and flag high-priority interactions requiring human intervention. Computational experiments will employ agent-based modeling to simulate receptionist-caller dynamics across diverse scenarios, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine task prioritization and scheduling policies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing multimodal data (audio, text, temporal patterns) at scale, enabling parallelized training of context-aware recommendation systems. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for reducing caller wait times, improving sentiment outcomes by 15-25% in simulated environments, and generating adaptive workflow templates customizable to specific organizational needs. By bridging computational linguistics, behavioral operations research, and queueing theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for intelligent receptionist systems that balance automation with human-centric service delivery, offering scalable solutions for healthcare facilities, enterprise campuses, and crisis response centers where frontline communication directly impacts organizational reputation and operational resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform frontline public relations duties for a business, organization, or answering service. Includes instruction in telephone answering techniques, responding to information requests, keeping caller and/or visitor records, placing business calls, operating telephone switchboards and/or other communications equipment, relaying incoming and interoffice calls, schedule maintenance, and public relations skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the reconstruction and analysis of complex crime scenes through advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. Despite advances in forensic science, reconstructing multi-layered criminal events—such as those involving digital evidence, biological traces, and ballistic data—remains time-intensive and error-prone due to the volume, diversity, and interdependency of evidence types. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach integrating agent-based modeling, Bayesian networks, and deep learning to automate evidence correlation and scenario generation. The computational model will simulate interactions between suspects, victims, and environmental factors using parallelized Monte Carlo methods to iteratively test hypotheses against physical evidence datasets (e.g., DNA methylation patterns, 3D bullet trajectory scans, and digital device logs). A neural network trained on historical crime scene data will prioritize plausible reconstructions, reducing the solution space by orders of magnitude. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time rendering of dynamic crime scenarios and employ distributed memory systems to manage terabyte-scale case file repositories from partner law enforcement agencies. Expected outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for forensic analysts that decreases reconstruction time by 40–60% while improving accuracy in multi-evidence cases, as validated against ground-truth case resolutions. By enabling rapid, data-driven crime scene analysis, this work directly supports homeland security priorities in combating organized crime and terrorism, where complex evidence patterns demand computationally intensive solutions. The resource request focuses on 12-month access to HPC infrastructure capable of sustained petaflop performance, large-memory nodes for graph-based evidence networks, and secure storage compliant with criminal justice data standards.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of clinical and criminal laboratory science, investigative techniques, and criminology to the reconstruction of crimes and the analysis of physical evidence. Includes instruction in laboratory science, laboratory procedures, criminology and police science, evidentiary testing and analysis, computer applications, record-keeping, reconstruction techniques, evidence handling and storage, and applications to specific types of evidence and crimes.

abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing involves complex, multi-physics processes that require precise control of equipment parameters to optimize yield, minimize defects, and meet evolving industry standards. Current challenges include modeling plasma etching and chemical vapor deposition (CVD) processes at atomic scales, predicting defect formation during lithography, and optimizing equipment performance under dynamic manufacturing conditions. These tasks demand high-resolution simulations that integrate quantum mechanical, fluid dynamic, and thermal effects—computations that exceed the capacity of standard workstations. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale models of semiconductor fabrication processes. Computational workflows will combine density functional theory (DFT) for surface reaction modeling, finite element analysis (FEA) for equipment-scale thermal and stress simulations, and machine learning (ML) to bridge time and length scales. A central focus is simulating plasma etching dynamics in reactive ion etchers, where ion energy distributions and radical species concentrations will be modeled using particle-in-cell (PIC) and direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) methods. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on simulation data to predict defect hotspots in photolithography patterns. The HPC environment will enable large parameter sweeps to identify optimal process conditions, reducing experimental trial-and-error. Expected outcomes include validated models for process optimization, predictive maintenance protocols for fabrication equipment, and open-source simulation tools for the semiconductor research community. By linking atomic-scale phenomena to equipment-level performance, this work aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices, reduce material waste, and accelerate the development of next-generation chips. The requested resources will also support training graduate students in computational materials science and HPC-driven manufacturing analytics, aligning with industry demands for skilled technologists in semiconductor fabrication.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to operate and monitor equipment for the fabrication of semiconductors or microchips from silicon wafers, and to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair the specialized equipment used in this process. Includes instruction in AC and DC circuits, digital fundamentals, solid state devices, manufacturing processes, vacuum principles and technology, industrial electronics, quality assurance, and semiconductor manufacturing technology.

abstract: Blood transfusion safety and efficacy rely on precise antigen-antibody compatibility assessments, optimized donor-recipient matching, and robust predictive models for adverse reactions. Current methods for antibody identification, particularly in patients with complex serologies or rare blood types, remain time-intensive and error-prone due to manual interpretation of agglutination patterns and limited computational tools. This project proposes to develop machine learning (ML) models and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to enhance immunohematology workflows, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical bottlenecks. We will train deep neural networks on multi-institutional datasets—including historical donor-recipient pairing outcomes, antigenic profiles, and hemolytic reaction records—to predict high-risk incompatibilities and automate antibody rule-outs. Concurrently, all-atom MD simulations will characterize the structural dynamics of clinically significant erythrocyte antigens (e.g., Rh, Kell, Duffy systems) under varying storage conditions, informing improved preservation protocols. The computational pipeline will integrate genomic data from blood donors to model population-specific antigen frequencies, optimizing inventory management for diverse patient demographics. HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale immunohematology datasets, running parallelized MD trajectories across antigen-antibody complexes, and deploying ensemble ML architectures with hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for antibody identification, predictive metrics for transfusion-related complications, and evidence-based guidelines for blood component storage. By bridging computational biology with blood bank operations, this work aims to reduce diagnostic delays, minimize wastage of rare blood products, and improve outcomes for transfusion-dependent patients. The developed frameworks will be validated against prospectively collected clinical data from partner blood centers, ensuring translational relevance for health professions training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying drug-receptor interactions remain incompletely resolved, particularly for membrane-bound receptors that exhibit dynamic conformational states and complex allosteric modulation. A critical challenge in molecular pharmacology is predicting how structural and energetic features of ligand binding influence receptor activation, signaling bias, and downstream therapeutic or adverse effects. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model ligand-receptor binding thermodynamics and kinetics at an atomistic scale, focusing on G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) implicated in cardiovascular and neurological disorders. Current limitations in experimental approaches—such as static crystal structures or low-resolution binding assays—fail to capture the dynamic solvent-mediated interactions and intermediate conformational states that dictate drug efficacy. To address this, we will perform ensemble-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using explicit solvent models to map free energy landscapes of receptor-ligand complexes across multiple pharmacologically relevant states. Adaptive sampling algorithms and Markov state models will identify metastable binding intermediates and allosteric networks. Parallelized free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations will quantify the relative binding affinities of structurally analogous ligands with divergent signaling profiles. These computational workflows require extensive GPU-accelerated simulations (>1 microsecond aggregate sampling per system) and large-scale parameter optimization, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking ligand chemical features to receptor signaling bias, (2) identification of novel allosteric sites for selective drug design, and (3) validation of computational predictions against in vitro pharmacodynamic data from collaborating labs. By elucidating dynamic determinants of drug action, this work will advance rational design of targeted therapies with improved efficacy and reduced off-target toxicity, directly addressing unmet needs in precision pharmacology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biochemical and biophysical characteristics of drugs at the molecular level and their interaction with, and effects on, biological macromolecules and cellular structures and processes. Includes instruction in molecular biology and biophysics; pharmacology of signal transduction, transmitters, and protein synthesis and release; receptors, protein interaction and binding; drug discovery and recognition; molecular toxicology; drug design; pharmacodynamics; developmental genetics; and studies of therapeutic strategies.

abstract: Soil health and fertility are critical determinants of agricultural productivity, yet predicting soil behavior across spatial and temporal scales remains a grand challenge due to the complex interplay of physical, chemical, and biological processes. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to model soil-plant-microbe interactions under varying agronomic management practices, with a focus on optimizing nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration in croplands. The research addresses a key gap in current soil models, which often oversimplify microbial mediation of nutrient fluxes or fail to capture heterogeneous soil structures at submeter scales. We propose to integrate mechanistic models of soil hydrology (e.g., 3D water flow using Richards’ equation), nutrient transport-reaction networks, and genome-informed microbial community dynamics into a coupled simulation environment. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these processes at relevant scales, employing parallelized finite element solvers for soil physics and agent-based modeling for microbial ecosystems. Machine learning workflows will parameterize models using geospatial soil databases, hyperspectral imagery, and long-term experimental data from row-crop systems. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive maps of nitrogen and phosphorus availability under precision irrigation regimes, (2) quantification of trade-offs between soil carbon storage and nitrous oxide emissions under cover cropping, and (3) open-source simulation tools for optimizing tillage and fertilizer strategies. The computational demands are substantial, requiring >10,000 core-hours monthly for ensemble simulations across soil textures and climate scenarios. By bridging pore-scale microbiology to field-scale agronomy, this work will provide actionable insights for sustainable intensification of food production while advancing computational methods for soil science. Results will directly inform USDA-NRCS conservation planning tools and contribute to climate-smart agriculture frameworks.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that generally focuses on the scientific classification of soils, soil properties, and their relationship to agricultural crops. Includes instruction in soil chemistry, soil physics, soil biology, soil fertility, morphogenesis, mineralogy, hydrology, agronomy, and soil conservation and management.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in mathematics teacher education by investigating how large-scale computational modeling can enhance the understanding of effective pedagogical strategies and student learning outcomes. A persistent gap exists in quantitatively linking teacher instructional practices—especially those involving technology integration, differentiated instruction, and formative assessment—to longitudinal student performance in mathematics. Traditional qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods lack the capacity to analyze multi-dimensional educational datasets, which include student assessment records, classroom observation metrics, and teacher professional development histories. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled frameworks to model interactions between teacher behaviors, curricular variables, and student achievement trajectories. The computational approach integrates machine learning algorithms, network analysis, and agent-based simulations to identify patterns in instructional effectiveness across diverse classroom contexts. For example, reinforcement learning models will be trained on statewide K–12 mathematics performance data to simulate adaptive teaching strategies, while graph-based methods will map the diffusion of evidence-based practices within teacher professional learning communities. These models require processing terabytes of structured and unstructured educational data, necessitating parallelized computing architectures for efficient parameter optimization and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide teacher educators in designing targeted professional development programs, as well as generative models that forecast the impact of policy interventions on equitable access to high-quality mathematics instruction. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in teacher preparation programs, ultimately contributing to improved STEM educational equity and student success at scale. The resulting computational frameworks will be disseminated as open-source tools for broader applications in science and mathematics education research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach mathematics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of dynamic, granular forecasting models for real-time market sentiment analysis in decentralized digital asset markets. Traditional business statistics methods struggle to process the high-velocity, unstructured data generated by blockchain-based trading platforms, social sentiment feeds, and cross-platform liquidity pools, which exhibit nonstationary patterns and complex network dependencies. The proposed computational framework integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) with Bayesian hierarchical time-series models to capture latent relationships between micro-level trader behaviors and macro-level market volatility. By parallelizing graph embedding computations across GPU clusters and optimizing memory-intensive Monte Carlo simulations for HPC architectures, the project aims to overcome scalability barriers in existing econometric toolkits. Key challenges include developing adaptive sampling algorithms to handle streaming ledger data and creating hybrid CPU-GPU workflows for simultaneous parameter estimation across heterogeneous datasets (order books, social media APIs, on-chain transaction graphs). Success metrics will focus on reducing prediction error rates for 15-minute volatility windows compared to conventional ARIMA and GARCH models, while maintaining computational feasibility for sub-second updates. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source library for high-frequency decentralized finance (DeFi) analytics, with applications to risk management systems and regulatory stress-testing frameworks. This work bridges gaps between computational economics, distributed systems research, and business statistics by formalizing methods to quantify emergent market behaviors in blockchain ecosystems—a critical need as traditional financial metrics fail to address the combinatorial complexity of Web3 markets. Resource requests emphasize GPU node allocation for deep learning components and high-memory nodes for large graph processing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-efficiency, low-emission diesel engines necessitates advanced computational modeling to optimize engine performance and reduce environmental impact. Traditional experimental methods for analyzing combustion dynamics, thermal management, and mechanical wear in diesel engines are time-intensive and costly, limiting rapid iteration and innovation. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate multi-physics interactions within modern diesel engines, with a focus on combustion efficiency, emissions control, and component durability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to resolve complex phenomena such as turbulent fuel-air mixing, soot formation, and heat transfer in exhaust aftertreatment systems at unprecedented resolution. The computational framework will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress and thermal deformation predictions, and machine learning algorithms to identify optimal operating parameters under diverse load conditions. Large-scale parametric studies will evaluate the impact of fuel injection timing, exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) rates, and piston-cylinder geometry on engine performance metrics. Validated against experimental data from industry partners, these models will enable predictive maintenance strategies by correlating sensor data with simulated degradation patterns in critical components like turbochargers and fuel injectors. The outcomes will directly inform curriculum updates in Diesel Mechanics Technology programs, bridging computational engineering with hands-on technician training. By accelerating the design of cleaner, more reliable diesel systems, this research supports the transition to sustainable heavy-duty transportation and power generation infrastructure. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for these simulations, which involve millions of mesh elements and transient analyses spanning thousands of engine cycles. The project’s open-source models and datasets will serve as a foundational resource for both academic institutions and small-to-medium enterprises in the diesel technology sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain diesel engines in vehicles such as automobiles, buses, ships, trucks, railroad locomotives, and construction equipment; as well as stationary diesel engines in electrical generators and related equipment.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced computational framework for analyzing the pedagogical and structural challenges faced by foreign-trained lawyers adapting to U.S. legal education and practice. While existing programs for foreign lawyers focus on doctrinal instruction, there is a critical gap in understanding how systemic differences in legal reasoning, cultural assumptions, and educational methodologies impact learning outcomes. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze multilingual legal corpora, including case law, academic publications, and student assessments from comparative law programs. By training transformer-based models on parallel datasets spanning common law (U.S./Canada) and civil law systems, the research aims to identify latent patterns in legal argumentation that create barriers for foreign learners. A novel computational jurisprudence component will simulate hybrid legal reasoning scenarios through agent-based modeling, testing how practitioners navigate conflicting doctrinal frameworks. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale legal texts across multiple languages, optimizing complex ML architectures for low-resource legal language tasks, and running high-fidelity cultural-cognitive simulations. Expected outcomes include 1) a predictive model of conceptual transfer difficulties in transnational legal education, 2) an open-access toolkit for adaptive curriculum design, and 3) quantitative insights into the epistemic boundaries of legal acculturation processes. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, legal pedagogy, and cognitive anthropology, offering a template for data-driven reforms in transnational professional education while advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM HPC applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares lawyers educated outside the United States to understand U. S. or Canadian law and jurisprudence.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying music therapy interventions for individuals with cognitive and emotional disorders. While music therapy has demonstrated clinical efficacy in improving outcomes for conditions such as autism spectrum disorder, depression, and dementia, the precise neural and psychological processes driving these benefits remain poorly characterized. A key challenge lies in analyzing multimodal datasets—including high-density EEG, fMRI, and real-time behavioral response metrics—collected during therapeutic sessions to model complex brain-body interactions. This requires computational workflows capable of integrating time-series data across spatial and temporal scales while accounting for individual variability in music perception and affective processing. We propose developing a pipeline using machine learning (e.g., recurrent neural networks) and dynamical systems modeling to identify patterns in neurophysiological data that predict therapeutic responsiveness. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter optimization for these models, parallel processing of cohort-level datasets from ongoing clinical trials, and simulations of hypothesized entrainment mechanisms between auditory processing networks and emotional regulation systems. Additionally, we will employ natural language processing to analyze therapist-client interaction logs, correlating linguistic markers with physiological and behavioral outcomes. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated computational framework for predicting optimal music therapy protocols based on individual neurocognitive profiles, (2) identification of biomarkers linking specific musical elements (e.g., tempo, tonal structure) to emotional and cognitive outcomes, and (3) open-source tools for real-time adaptive music generation in therapeutic contexts. This work will provide the first quantitative models of music therapy’s mechanistic pathways at scale, directly informing personalized intervention strategies while establishing computational methods as critical infrastructure for music therapy research. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-memory nodes for whole-brain network simulations, and high-throughput processing of longitudinal multimodal datasets from 500+ participants across three clinical studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in association with a rehabilitation team or in private practice, to use music in therapeutic relationships to address the physical, psychological, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of clients. Includes instruction in music theory and performance, human growth and development, biomedical sciences, abnormal psychology, disabling conditions, patient assessment and diagnosis, treatment plan development and implementation, clinical evaluation, record-keeping, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Aerospace Ground Equipment (AGE) systems are critical to sustaining military aviation and space operations, yet their operational reliability is challenged by complex, interdependent stressors including thermal cycling, fluid dynamics, corrosion, and mechanical wear. Traditional maintenance models, reliant on static schedules or reactive protocols, struggle to address the nonlinear degradation patterns caused by these multi-physics interactions, leading to unplanned downtime, safety risks, and resource inefficiencies. This project proposes the development of a predictive digital twin framework for AGE systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-scale simulations, sensor-derived operational data, and machine learning (ML) models. The research will focus on modeling electrochemical corrosion propagation in high-humidity environments, coupled with thermal-fluid interactions in hydraulic and cooling subsystems. HPC resources will enable finite element analysis (FEA) for microstructural corrosion prediction, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for evaluating coolant flow efficiency under degraded seals, and ensemble ML algorithms trained on historical maintenance logs and real-time telemetry. Key innovations include adaptive meshing techniques to resolve localized corrosion hotspots and graph neural networks to model interdependencies between subsystem failures. The resulting framework will provide dynamic risk assessments, prioritize maintenance interventions, and simulate “what-if” scenarios for equipment configuration adjustments. Outcomes aim to reduce AGE maintenance-related downtime by 20–30%, extend service lifecycles, and inform next-generation corrosion-resistant material specifications. By bridging computational materials science, fluid dynamics, and predictive analytics within a military-specific operational context, this project addresses a critical gap in infrastructure resilience, directly supporting strategic readiness and lifecycle cost reduction goals. The scalability of the digital twin architecture will further offer a template for adaptive maintenance in other austere or high-stakes operational environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology, and maintenance of ground-based systems and equipments used to support aviation flight operations and space operations. Includes instruction in computer science, electronics, basic sciences and quantitative methods, air conditioning and refrigeration, corrosion control, fluid power, hazardous materials, industrial safety, maintenance management, vehicle and equipment operation, and applications to specific ground support systems.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to sustainable power generation, yet their efficiency and reliability are challenged by dynamic environmental conditions, aging infrastructure, and the integration of modern control systems. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and optimize hydroelectric turbine performance and maintenance protocols under variable operational scenarios. Current analytical tools lack the resolution to capture complex fluid-structure interactions, sediment erosion patterns, and real-time stress distributions in turbines, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and energy losses. To overcome these limitations, the proposed research will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate multiphysics interactions within hydroelectric systems at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict component degradation and failure risks using historical sensor data and simulated wear patterns. The HPC environment is essential to process terabytes of sensor data, execute parallelized simulations of turbine clusters, and train predictive models with hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for hydroelectric turbines, predictive maintenance algorithms to reduce unplanned downtime, and optimized turbine designs that enhance energy output by 10–15% under low-flow conditions. These advancements will directly inform technician training programs, equipping future professionals with data-driven repair strategies and system diagnostics. By bridging computational modeling with applied hydroelectric technology, this project aims to strengthen the resilience of renewable energy infrastructure while reducing operational costs and environmental impacts.
cip_title: Hydroelectric Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address communication inefficiencies in multilingual community health liaison services, which hinder equitable access to care for linguistically diverse populations. While community health workers (CHWs) serve as critical bridges between healthcare systems and marginalized groups, existing protocols lack data-driven tools to optimize cross-cultural dialogue, particularly in low-resource languages. We propose a computational linguistics framework to analyze real-world CHW-client interactions, aiming to identify linguistic and paralinguistic patterns that predict successful outcomes in care coordination. The research will utilize anonymized audio recordings and transcripts from community health agencies serving refugee and immigrant populations, encompassing over 20 languages and dialects. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to extract semantic features, emotional valence, and pragmatic markers (e.g., code-switching frequency, rapport-building sequences) from these interactions. Machine learning models will then correlate these features with client health behavior outcomes (medication adherence, follow-up completion) derived from longitudinal electronic health records. Due to the complexity of multimodal data and the need for real-time processing in eventual tool deployment, high-performance computing resources are required to train transformer-based architectures on GPU clusters and perform large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include 1) a predictive model identifying high-impact communication strategies across linguistic contexts, 2) an open-source toolkit for adaptive feedback during CHW training simulations, and 3) computational evidence informing policy on resource allocation for language services in community health programs. This interdisciplinary approach advances health equity research by integrating computational social science with community health practice, offering novel methods to quantify and enhance the impact of frontline health liaison work.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as facilitators, advocates, and referral professionals linking health care and related social services with affected recipient communities. Includes instruction in public and community health, human and social services, health services administration, group counseling, health education, group advocacy, cross-cultural and multilingual communication, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the technical and artistic dimensions of barbering through computational modeling and data-driven analysis. While traditional barbering practices rely on empirical skill development, emerging challenges—such as optimizing hair and scalp health under diverse biological conditions, predicting long-term outcomes of chemical treatments, and personalizing styling techniques for complex hair textures—require sophisticated simulations beyond manual experimentation. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) developing biomechanical models of hair-scalp interactions to quantify stress distributions during cutting, styling, and chemical applications, and (2) training machine learning algorithms on 3D-scanned hair morphology datasets to recommend individualized techniques that balance aesthetic goals with structural integrity. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for simulating shear forces during scissor work, molecular dynamics for evaluating product interactions with keratin structures, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to visualize style outcomes across ethnic hair types. By correlating simulation results with clinical data on hair damage and customer satisfaction metrics, the models will establish evidence-based thresholds for tool pressure, product concentrations, and thermal exposure. The scale of these analyses—encompassing millions of hair fiber simulations and high-resolution scalp topography mappings—necessitates parallelized GPU computing and large-memory nodes. Outcomes will include open-access predictive tools for barbers to previsualize style impacts, a safety protocol framework for regulatory agencies, and adaptive training modules that integrate real-time simulation feedback into licensure programs. This work positions computational barbering as a novel interdisciplinary domain intersecting dermatology, materials science, and ethnocultural aesthetics, offering a paradigm shift from craft-based tradition to precision-driven practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shave and trim facial/neck hair and beards, cut and dress hair, fit hairpieces, give facial and scalp massages, apply cosmetic treatments, and to prepare for licensure as professional barbers at various levels.  Includes instruction in facial shaving; beard and mustache shaping and trimming; shampooing; hair cutting; hair styles and styling art; facial treatments and massage; chemical applications; hair and scalp anatomy and physiology; hairpiece and toupee fitting; equipment operation; health and safety; customer service; and shop business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamics of intractable sociopolitical conflicts, integrating behavioral, cultural, and environmental variables to predict de-escalation pathways. Traditional conflict analysis often relies on qualitative or linear quantitative models, which struggle to capture the nonlinear, adaptive interactions among stakeholders, resource constraints, and historical grievances that perpetuate violence. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach augmented by machine learning (ML) to simulate multiscale conflict systems—from individual decision-making to systemic feedback loops. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large-scale datasets (demographic records, historical conflict timelines, environmental stressors) and run millions of stochastic simulations exploring intervention scenarios. The computational pipeline will combine network analysis to map power hierarchies and information diffusion, reinforcement learning to model adaptive negotiation strategies, and dynamical systems theory to identify tipping points. Validation will leverage historical case studies (e.g., post-civil war reconciliation processes) and real-time data from partner NGOs operating in active conflict zones. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for simulating conflict trajectories under varying policy interventions (e.g., resource redistribution, third-party mediation protocols) and quantifying the resilience of proposed solutions to external shocks. This work bridges computational social science, peace studies, and complexity theory, offering a novel platform for stress-testing conflict resolution strategies in silico before real-world implementation. By elucidating how localized interactions scale to systemic outcomes, the project aims to advance evidence-based frameworks for reducing conflict recidivism—a growing priority in global security and humanitarian policy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of national, intergroup and interpersonal conflicts. Includes instruction in theories of conflict, mediation and negotiation, understanding of the ethical, cultural and power dynamics that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on adaptive leadership decision-making in complex organizational environments. Organizational leaders face dynamic challenges requiring rapid analysis of multi-dimensional data—including team performance metrics, financial constraints, and stakeholder feedback—to optimize strategic outcomes. However, existing models for leadership decision-making often oversimplify interactions between variables or fail to account for real-time environmental shifts, limiting their practical utility. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models to simulate organizational ecosystems under varying leadership strategies. These models will integrate behavioral datasets from case studies, employee surveys, and historical organizational performance records to represent hierarchical and networked decision-making structures. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations to test how adaptive leadership approaches—such as dynamic resource reallocation, conflict mediation protocols, and communication frameworks—impact organizational resilience, innovation, and efficiency across thousands of parameterized scenarios. Sensitivity analyses will identify critical thresholds where leadership interventions yield disproportionate outcomes, while machine learning techniques will uncover latent patterns in decision-making efficacy. Outcomes will provide empirically grounded insights into scalable leadership strategies for mitigating systemic risks, balancing competing priorities, and fostering collaboration in uncertain environments. The computational tools developed will be shared as open-source frameworks for leadership training and organizational design, bridging gaps between theoretical leadership models and data-driven practice. By quantifying the cascading effects of leadership choices in silico, this work aims to equip leaders in business, non-profit, and public sectors with evidence-based strategies to navigate complexity, ultimately enhancing organizational agility and long-term sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying Asian Bodywork Therapy (ABT) techniques, with a focus on optimizing pressure-point stimulation protocols for chronic pain management. While ABT modalities such as acupressure and Shiatsu are empirically associated with therapeutic benefits, the lack of high-resolution, multiscale models hinders systematic analysis of how manual interventions interact with tissue dynamics, neural signaling, and systemic physiological responses. Current clinical studies rely on coarse outcome measures, leaving critical gaps in understanding dose-response relationships, force distribution patterns, and long-term neuromodulatory effects. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling of deep tissue deformation, machine learning analysis of clinical biomechanical data, and dynamic simulations of autonomic nervous system modulation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable three core components: 1) Multi-layered tissue modeling using patient-specific MRI-derived anatomies to simulate pressure propagation across fascial planes and myofascial chains; 2) Bayesian optimization of treatment parameters (angle, duration, rhythm) through iterative analysis of 10,000+ documented ABT sessions paired with biomarker data (heart rate variability, cytokine levels); and 3) Whole-body neural network simulations mapping afferent signal cascades from mechanoreceptor activation to central pain processing pathways. The computational pipeline will process 15TB of multimodal data, including motion-captured practitioner kinematics, ultrasound elastography, and longitudinal patient-reported outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for ABT protocol personalization, quantitative safety thresholds for vulnerable anatomical regions, and mechanistic insights into ABT’s role in regulating inflammatory responses. By establishing the first HPC-enabled platform for ABT research, this work aims to bridge traditional East Asian medical principles with contemporary computational biomedicine, offering evidence-based frameworks to enhance clinical training and interdisciplinary rehabilitation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being based on Chinese medical principles through one or more of the traditional bodywork therapies of Asia. Includes instruction in acupressure, AMMA(r) Therapy, Chi Nei Tsang, Five Element Shiatsu, Integrative Eclectic Shiatsu, Japanese Shiatsu, Jin Shin Do(r) Bodymind Acupressure(tm), Macrobiotic Shiatsu, Anma Therapy, Thai massage, Tui na, Zen Shiatsu, Qigong, Okazaki(r) Restorative Massage, principles of Western and Chinese medicine, patient counseling and observation, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale epidemiological study analyzing the intersection of social determinants, environmental exposures, and health outcomes across diverse populations. Public health interventions often face challenges in accounting for multi-level, dynamic interactions between socioeconomic factors (e.g., income inequality, access to care), environmental risks (e.g., air pollution, urban heat islands), and disease burden. Traditional statistical models struggle to capture these complex, non-linear relationships at granular spatial and temporal scales. Our research aims to develop an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and geospatial analytics to simulate population health dynamics under varying policy scenarios. The ABM will simulate individual and community-level behaviors, while ML algorithms trained on linked electronic health records, satellite-derived environmental data, and census-tract socioeconomic indicators will predict emergent health disparities. Computational demands include parallelized model calibration across thousands of parameter combinations, real-time integration of high-resolution environmental datasets (~10 TB), and sensitivity analyses to quantify uncertainty. Expected outcomes include identifying priority intervention zones for reducing cardiovascular disease incidence in underserved urban areas and generating open-source tools for scalable health equity modeling. This work directly supports evidence-based policymaking by enabling rapid scenario testing for resource allocation, disaster preparedness, and climate adaptation strategies. HPC resources are critical due to the need for distributed memory processing to handle the ABM’s scale (>1 million agents) and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models on heterogeneous data streams. Results will be disseminated through public health agencies and peer-reviewed platforms to inform equitable prevention programs.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and evaluate public health care services; to function as public health professionals in public agencies, the private sector, and other settings; and to provide leadership in the field of public health. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, public health principles, preventive medicine, health policy and regulations, health care services and related administrative functions, public health law enforcement, health economics and budgeting, public communications, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the computational modeling of melodic and rhythmic structures in sacred music traditions across diverse religious contexts, with a focus on understudied oral and manuscript-based repertoires. While sacred music’s role in ritual practice is well documented, the structural interplay between theological frameworks, cultural exchange, and musical innovation remains underexplored. The research addresses this gap by analyzing large-scale datasets of liturgical chants, hymns, and instrumental works from traditions including Syriac Christian chant, Jain devotional music, and Indigenous diasporic sacred practices, many of which exist only in fragmented or non-digitized forms. A high-performance computing (HPC) approach is critical due to the need to process heterogeneous data types—audio recordings, symbolic notation, and textual annotations—while accounting for temporal, geographic, and doctrinal variables. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns in melodic contour, rhythmic complexity, and text-setting relationships, leveraging GPU-accelerated spectro-temporal analysis and transformer-based architectures for cross-modal alignment. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model the hypothetical transmission of musical motifs across historical trade and pilgrimage routes, integrating ethnographic and musicological metadata to test hypotheses about intercultural influence. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access repository of annotated sacred music corpora, a computational framework for analyzing music-theological interactions, and visualizations of stylistic convergence/divergence across traditions. By bridging computational musicology, cultural anthropology, and digital humanities, this work aims to advance scholarly understanding of how sacred music evolves as both an artistic and spiritual practice while providing tools for preserving endangered repertoires. The project’s scale—processing over 50,000 audio excerpts and 10,000 pages of manuscript images—necessitates HPC resources for data storage, parallelized feature extraction, and large-language model fine-tuning, which cannot be feasibly executed on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, theory, composition, and performance of music for religious or sacred purposes, and that prepares individuals for religious musical vocations such as choir directors, cantors, organists, and chanters.

abstract: Emerging zoonotic diseases increasingly threaten global health, driven by environmental change, habitat fragmentation, and shifting species interactions. Current predictive models often lack integration of ecological dynamics with epidemiological processes, limiting their ability to forecast spillover risks in heterogeneous landscapes. This project aims to develop a spatially explicit, multiscale framework to quantify how ecological community structure and land-use change modulate pathogen transmission at wildlife-human interfaces. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will parameterize agent-based models (ABMs) with empirical data from longitudinal wildlife surveys, remote sensing, and pathogen genomic sequences across tropical agroforestry systems. The ABMs will simulate host movement, resource competition, and cross-species contact rates under scenarios of deforestation and climate variability. Concurrently, Bayesian phylodynamic models will reconstruct pathogen spread histories using viral phylogenies and environmental covariates. A key innovation involves coupling these approaches through approximate Bayesian computation (ABC), iteratively refining ecological parameters to align simulated outbreak patterns with observed phylogeographic and epidemiological data. This integration requires computationally intensive parameter sweeps and likelihood-free inference methods, necessitating parallelized processing and large-scale memory allocation. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical ecological thresholds that amplify spillover risk, (2) high-resolution risk maps for priority regions, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive surveillance in changing ecosystems. By unifying ecological and epidemiological theory with advanced computational workflows, this work will advance predictive capacity for pre-emergent zoonoses while addressing scalability challenges in complex systems modeling. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling terabyte-scale environmental datasets, running stochastic simulations across parameter spaces, and performing iterative model comparisons—tasks infeasible on standard laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of epidemiology and biostatistics or a specialization which draws from epidemiology and biostatistics. Includes instruction in biostatistics, disease and injury determinants, epidemiology, health services research, pathology, spatial analysis, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance elementary teacher preparation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize instructional strategies for diverse student populations. A critical challenge in elementary education is designing teaching practices that adapt to varied learning needs across foundational subjects (e.g., literacy, numeracy, science). Traditional methods of evaluating instructional efficacy—such as classroom observations or small-scale trials—are resource-intensive and limited in scalability. This research proposes a computational approach to simulate classroom dynamics under different pedagogical scenarios, enabling rapid, data-driven insights into how teaching methods interact with student attributes. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to represent students as autonomous agents with distinct learning profiles, incorporating variables such as prior knowledge, engagement levels, and socioemotional traits. Teachers will be modeled as agents deploying strategies aligned with evidence-based frameworks (e.g., differentiated instruction, inquiry-based learning). Simulations will assess how variations in strategy timing, sequencing, and personalization affect learning outcomes across synthetic classrooms mirroring real-world demographic and academic diversity. HPC resources are essential to parallelize thousands of simulations, each requiring real-time interactions among dozens of agents, while machine learning pipelines will analyze emergent patterns to identify optimal strategy combinations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for prototyping teaching practices, (2) actionable guidelines for tailoring instruction to heterogeneous classrooms, and (3) open-access datasets linking strategy choices to predicted learning gains. By bridging computational modeling and teacher education, this work aims to equip educators with empirically grounded tools to address complex classroom realities, ultimately supporting equitable learning experiences in elementary settings.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the elementary grades, which may include kindergarten through grade eight, depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all elementary education subject matter.

abstract: Parent education programs face a critical challenge in addressing the heterogeneous needs of families across diverse cultural, socioeconomic, and developmental contexts. Existing curricula often adopt generalized frameworks that inadequately account for dynamic family interactions, community-specific stressors, or the evolving developmental trajectories of children. This project proposes to develop a computational model to optimize personalized parent education strategies by integrating high-dimensional data on family dynamics, cultural practices, and community resources. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze longitudinal datasets from parent-child interactions, demographic surveys, and program outcome metrics, which include multimodal data (text, audio, and behavioral coding) from 15,000 families across five global regions. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks and transformer-based natural language processing, will be employed to model relational patterns between parenting behaviors, child developmental outcomes, and contextual factors such as access to social services or community support networks. Agent-based simulations will further test hypothetical intervention scenarios, evaluating how tailored educational content might propagate through family-community ecosystems. The computational pipeline will require distributed processing of unstructured data, parallelized simulation runs, and real-time visualization of complex network dynamics, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to identify culturally adaptive parenting strategies, (2) evidence-based guidelines for modular curriculum design that responds to localized needs, and (3) open-source tools enabling educators to simulate program impacts prior to implementation. By bridging developmental psychology, data science, and educational design, this work aims to establish a scalable methodology for advancing equity in parent support systems while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in non-traditional, human-centric research domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, coordinate, and teach parent education programs and services that address the cultural, emotional, intellectual, physical and social needs of children and parents. Includes instruction in child development, cultural diversity in schools, child behavior, family development, family-community partnerships, family dynamics, interpersonal relationships, parent-child relationships, and social services.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic infectious diseases present complex challenges requiring advanced computational tools to model disease dynamics, predict transmission risks, and evaluate intervention strategies. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support the development of multi-scale models integrating host-pathogen-environment interactions, with a focus on diseases such as bovine tuberculosis (Mycobacterium bovis) and avian influenza in mixed-use agricultural systems. Current limitations in predicting outbreak trajectories stem from incomplete data on pathogen evolution, heterogeneous host immunity, and environmental drivers of transmission. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning (ML) to analyze high-dimensional datasets spanning genomic, epidemiological, and ecological variables. The ABM component will simulate disease spread across spatially explicit landscapes incorporating livestock, wildlife, and human populations, while ML algorithms will identify patterns in longitudinal metagenomic data from field samples to detect emerging antibiotic resistance markers. Parallelized molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate structural changes in viral envelope proteins associated with cross-species transmission. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across >10,000 simulated outbreak scenarios, Bayesian inference of transmission networks, and real-time integration of sensor data from agricultural IoT devices monitoring animal movements. Expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying high-risk interfaces of zoonotic spillover, optimized vaccine deployment strategies based on adaptive viral evolution forecasts, and mechanistic insights into pathogen adaptation at wildlife-livestock boundaries. These results will directly inform surveillance protocols and targeted biosecurity measures, advancing the program’s mission to mitigate economic losses in agriculture and reduce pandemic risks. By leveraging computational scaling to address biological complexity, this work bridges critical gaps in translating basic pathogen biology into actionable prevention frameworks for veterinary and public health stakeholders.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of zoonotic infectious diseases, disease mechanisms, and prevention and treatment strategies. Includes instruction in disease pathogenesis, vector biology, mycobacterial infection, blood parasites, retroviruses, food-borne diseases, new infectious agents, ecotoxicology, mechanisms of disease transfer, antibody resistance, comparative pathology, communicable diseases, and disease prevention and eradication.

abstract: Interventional radiology (IR) relies on real-time, multimodal imaging to guide minimally invasive therapies, yet current computational limitations hinder the integration of high-resolution imaging data with dynamic physiological models for personalized procedural planning. This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing image-guided interventions—such as embolization, stent placement, and thrombolysis—by developing a computational framework that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate patient-specific vascular anatomy, device-tissue interactions, and hemodynamic outcomes. The research problem centers on the inability of conventional systems to rapidly process large-scale, multi-modal datasets (e.g., CT, MRI, fluoroscopy) and predict procedural outcomes in clinically relevant timeframes. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining deep learning for real-time image segmentation, finite element modeling for simulating device deployment and vessel mechanics, and computational fluid dynamics to predict post-procedural blood flow patterns. These models will be integrated into a unified platform, enabling iterative simulation of interventions prior to their execution. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational load of 3D image processing, multi-physics simulations, and ensemble modeling across heterogeneous patient datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for procedural success metrics (e.g., stent patency, embolization completeness) and a deployable tool for pre-procedural planning that reduces intraoperative time, radiation exposure, and complication rates. The significance lies in advancing precision IR by bridging real-time imaging with predictive computational modeling, ultimately improving patient outcomes in therapies for vascular, oncologic, and traumatic conditions. This work will also establish an open-source framework for reproducible research in image-guided intervention optimization, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational disciplines.
cip_definition: Research focused on image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages. Does NOT require prior completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dissemination patterns and public reception of science, health, and environmental journalism in digital media ecosystems. The research problem centers on understanding how complex scientific information is communicated, amplified, or distorted across social platforms, news outlets, and multimedia channels, particularly during crises such as disease outbreaks or climate-related events. Current methods lack the capacity to process multimodal data—including text, video, and interactive content—at the scale required to identify misinformation trends, sentiment shifts, or audience engagement disparities across demographic groups. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling to map information flows and simulate their societal impacts. The NLP pipeline will process multilingual news corpora and social media datasets to classify scientific accuracy, detect framing biases, and track narrative evolution over time. Network models will visualize how journalistic outputs interface with advocacy groups, policymakers, and public stakeholders, while agent-based simulations will test how targeted communication strategies could mitigate misinformation. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on terabyte-scale datasets, conducting real-time sentiment analysis during breaking news cycles, and running parallelized simulations of information diffusion. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into optimizing science communication for public trust, tools to prioritize underreported environmental health risks, and a publicly accessible dashboard for journalists to visualize discourse trends. By bridging computational scalability with journalistic ethics, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based reporting and empower communities to navigate complex scientific issues.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on reporting on science, health, or environmental policy issues; investigating environmental problems and their causes; and public relations. Includes instruction in communication law, health reporting skills, interactive journalism, integrated marketing communication, journalism methods, media ethics, persuasion and political communication, science, health and the environment, social marketing, and video journalism.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular and biomechanical mechanisms underlying impaired osseointegration of dental implants in patients with metabolic bone disorders, a critical yet understudied intersection of oral biology, bioengineering, and computational systems biology. While implant failure rates remain elevated in populations with osteoporosis, diabetes, or rare skeletal dysplasias, current diagnostic tools lack predictive power at the microstructural and cellular levels. We propose to develop multiscale computational models integrating patient-specific bone microarchitecture data (μCT scans), single-cell RNA sequencing of peri-implant osteoprogenitor cells, and dynamic finite element analysis to simulate mechanobiological responses during early implant healing. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-terabyte histomorphometric datasets, machine learning-driven pattern recognition in bone remodeling trajectories, and agent-based modeling of osteoclast-osteoblast coupling under pathological metabolic conditions. The computational framework will be validated against longitudinal clinical cohorts with matched imaging and biopsy data. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for implant success probability based on subclinical bone quality parameters, identification of mechanosensitive gene networks amenable to therapeutic targeting, and optimized implant surface designs informed by simulated load distribution patterns in compromised bone. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between clinical oral pathology and computational mechanobiology, offering novel strategies to personalize implant dentistry while advancing fundamental understanding of craniofacial bone adaptation in systemic disease states.
cip_title: Oral Biology and Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the growth, development, diseases, healing properties, and neurological components of the oral cavity, related tissues and organs, and associated craniofacial areas. Includes instruction in oral microbiology microanatomy, craniofacial pain, humoral aspects of disease, etiology and histology of caries, plaque ecology, wound healing, oral disease epidemiology, oral manifestations of systemic disease, lesions, normal and pathologic physiology, and related molecular and physical studies.

abstract: In the rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, nursing professionals face increasing demands to deliver high-quality care while managing complex patient needs. This project seeks to address critical challenges in clinical decision-making and patient outcome optimization through advanced computational modeling. The research focuses on developing predictive analytics tools to identify patients at risk of adverse events, such as sepsis or falls, using large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets. Current approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multidimensional data—including vital signs, medication histories, and nursing notes—in real time. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models capable of processing heterogeneous data streams with high dimensionality. Our methodology includes the development of ensemble learning frameworks and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) tailored to temporal clinical data. These models will be validated against retrospective EHR data from diverse healthcare settings, ensuring generalizability across populations. The computational workflow will utilize distributed computing paradigms for feature extraction, model training, and real-time inference, requiring significant memory and processing capabilities provided by HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include deployable risk prediction tools that empower nursing staff to prioritize interventions proactively, potentially reducing hospital-acquired complications by 15–20%. Furthermore, this research will establish scalable computational pipelines adaptable to emerging healthcare technologies, strengthening the integration of data-driven decision support in nursing education and practice. By bridging gaps between clinical expertise and advanced analytics, this project aims to enhance both patient outcomes and nursing workforce efficiency in acute care environments.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
