Multiscale simulations will bridge quantum mechanical precision at electrode-electrolyte boundaries with mesoscale Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Stokes solvers, enabling the first unified computational framework for predicting emergent electrokinetic phenomena in angstrom-scale channels. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of variable confinement geometries (0.5-5 nm), electrolyte compositions, and surface functionalizations across relevant thermodynamic ensembles. Expected outcomes include fundamentally new design principles for voltage-gated nanofluidic membranes capable of exceeding classical permselectivity limits, with direct applications in osmotic energy harvesting and electrochemical carbon capture. The developed computational toolkit will establish protocols for simulating quantum-hydrodynamic coupling in non-equilibrium nanoscale systems, filling a critical gap between condensed matter physics and nanoengineering. By elucidating how subnanometer interfacial structuring modulates both ionic and electronic transport pathways, this work aims to enable predictive design of energy conversion architectures that leverage atomic-scale confinement effects beyond existing paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: The increasing complexity of audio engineering tasks—such as real-time spatial audio rendering, machine learning-driven sound synthesis, and high-fidelity acoustic simulations—demands computational resources beyond the capabilities of standard workstations. Current tools for music production and audio processing often struggle with latency, scalability, and precision when handling multichannel immersive audio formats, nonlinear acoustic modeling, or large datasets required for training generative audio models. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these limitations by enabling parallelized, large-scale computations critical for advancing research in audio engineering technology. The primary research problem centers on optimizing computational workflows for real-time audio processing and high-resolution acoustic simulations while maintaining perceptual fidelity and creative flexibility. Proposed computational methods include GPU-accelerated finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for room acoustics modeling, distributed computing frameworks for real-time multichannel audio effects processing, and training deep neural networks for tasks such as automated source separation and timbre transfer. These approaches will leverage MPI and CUDA architectures to parallelize tasks such as wave propagation calculations and real-time digital signal processing (DSP) chain optimizations. Additionally, the project will develop open-source tools to integrate HPC-driven workflows with industry-standard digital audio workstations (DAWs), bridging the gap between research and practical applications. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for low-latency spatial audio rendering, validated acoustic models for immersive sound environments, and publicly accessible datasets for machine learning in audio engineering. This work will directly benefit music production education by providing students with access to cutting-edge computational tools, while advancing research in areas such as virtual reality audio, AI-assisted mixing, and adaptive acoustic systems. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current bottlenecks in processing speed and data throughput, enabling innovations that align with industry demands for higher-quality, computationally efficient audio technologies.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the mixing, recording, and production of music. Includes instruction in acoustics, audio mixing, audio production, audio recording, computer composition of music, music theory, digital devices, and sound technology.

abstract: The development of next-generation polymeric materials with tailored dynamic and adaptive properties requires a fundamental understanding of how molecular-scale interactions govern macroscopic behavior under variable environmental conditions. This project addresses the challenge of predicting and optimizing stimuli-responsive polymer networks for applications in smart packaging and biomedical devices, where traditional trial-and-error experimental approaches are limited by cost, time, and the complexity of multi-physics interactions. We propose an integrated computational framework combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD), machine learning (ML)-accelerated free energy calculations, and finite element analysis (FEA) to bridge length- and time-scale gaps between molecular rearrangements and bulk material response. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate polymer networks with chemically heterogeneous motifs, quantify entropy-driven phase transitions under thermal/mechanical stress, and map these results to continuum-scale models of viscoelastic behavior. The computational workflow will parameterize force fields using quantum-mechanical data, simulate network reorganization processes across microseconds (via CG-MD on GPU clusters), and train graph neural networks to predict structure-property relationships for diverse monomer compositions. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for designing polymers with programmable shape-memory effects and environmental degradation profiles, reducing experimental iteration cycles by >60%. This multidisciplinary approach intersects polymer physics, computational chemistry, and materials informatics, advancing the rational design of sustainable adaptive materials while establishing new methodologies for cross-scale modeling in soft matter systems. The requested allocations will enable large-scale parameter sweeps (>10^4 simulation instances) to decode non-equilibrium polymer dynamics—a critical step toward energy-efficient manufacturing of stimuli-responsive materials for circular economy applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the structure and processing of polymeric materials and how these relate to properties and performance. Combines instruction in both Polymer science and engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the preservation and analysis of endangered Indigenous languages and oral traditions, with a focus on communities within the American Indian/Native American Studies framework. Despite the critical role of language in sustaining cultural identity, many Indigenous languages face extinction due to historical marginalization, limited documentation, and the complexities of intergenerational transmission. Current digitization efforts are fragmented, and existing computational tools often fail to address the unique morphological, syntactic, and contextual nuances of these languages. This research proposes the development of a scalable, community-centered computational platform to aggregate, process, and analyze linguistic data from dispersed archives, oral histories, and contemporary recordings. Machine learning models—particularly transformer-based architectures—will be trained to recognize phonetic patterns, translate semantic structures, and identify cultural references embedded in narratives. HPC resources are essential for handling the heterogeneous datasets (audio, text, video) and optimizing neural networks for low-resource language contexts. Collaborative frameworks will integrate tribal protocols for data sovereignty, ensuring ethical access and use. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository co-designed with participating communities, tools for language revitalization initiatives, and novel methodologies for interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of Indigenous knowledge systems and computational linguistics. By centering Indigenous epistemologies in algorithmic design, this project aims to counteract the erasure of cultural heritage while contributing scalable technical frameworks for similar global efforts. The requested computing infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times, and support real-time collaboration with Indigenous partners, thereby addressing both technical and community-driven research imperatives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the American Indian, Aleut, Inuit, Hawaiian and other native peoples of the Americas from earliest times until the present, with particular emphasis on U.S. and Canadian populations and their problems but including reference to Caribbean and Latin American native peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in analyzing large-scale, cross-cultural musical datasets to uncover patterns in improvisational practices and their sociocultural evolution. Despite advances in digital musicology, existing tools struggle to process high-resolution audio data across diverse genres (e.g., jazz, global folk traditions, experimental electronic music) at the scale required for statistically robust insights. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop parallelized machine learning models for feature extraction, temporal alignment, and stylistic classification of improvisational structures. Audio datasets comprising over 20,000 recordings will be processed using GPU-accelerated spectral analysis and transformer-based architectures to model nonlinear relationships between melodic, rhythmic, and timbral elements. Computational models will be validated against ethnographic metadata and historical records to correlate musical patterns with cultural migration and technological innovation. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable framework for analyzing improvisation as a dynamic cultural practice, (2) open-source tools for real-time comparative analysis of musical spontaneity across traditions, and (3) new methodologies for preserving intangible cultural heritage through computational musicology. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as simultaneous processing of multichannel audio streams and training neural networks on heterogeneous musical corpora. Results will advance scholarly understanding of music as a fluid, adaptive system while providing performing artists with historically informed models for contemporary practice. This work bridges computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, establishing infrastructure for future interdisciplinary research at the intersection of music performance, artificial intelligence, and cultural studies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in music, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel framework for real-time, adaptive narrative generation in immersive multiplayer environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational challenges of dynamic storytelling at scale. Current narrative systems in games often rely on pre-scripted events or limited decision trees, resulting in repetitive or predictable player experiences. This research proposes a hybrid approach combining procedural content generation with transformer-based language models (LLMs) to create branching narratives that evolve organically based on player decisions, in-game events, and emergent group dynamics. The computational challenge lies in maintaining narrative coherence across thousands of simultaneous player interactions while generating contextually appropriate dialogue, quest structures, and world-state modifications in real time. The proposed solution involves a distributed architecture using GPU-accelerated LLM inference for localized narrative decisions and a centralized HPC cluster to manage global narrative consistency through graph-based story state tracking. Resource requests focus on parallel processing capabilities for 1) training specialized LLMs on game-specific lore and interaction patterns, 2) simulating large-scale player behavior datasets to stress-test narrative stability, and 3) optimizing low-latency communication between narrative subsystems. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for dynamic narrative integration in commercial game engines, quantitative metrics for measuring player engagement in adaptive stories, and novel algorithms for balancing computational efficiency with narrative complexity. This work bridges gaps between computational linguistics, game design, and distributed systems, offering implications for educational simulations, interactive theater, and AI-assisted creative writing beyond entertainment contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: The study addresses critical gaps in computational resources for Khmer language research, which currently lacks robust tools for large-scale textual analysis despite the language’s rich literary heritage and complex morphology. Existing digital corpora are limited in scope and fail to represent historical texts, regional dialects, and non-literary materials, hindering advancements in philological studies, lexicography, and comparative literature. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to process and analyze diverse Khmer textual sources, including palm-leaf manuscripts, printed literature, and modern digital publications. Computational methods will integrate adaptive optical character recognition (OCR) models for digitizing pre-modern scripts, deep learning architectures for semantic and syntactic annotation, and distributed computing techniques to map lexical and stylistic evolution across six centuries of Khmer writing. The OCR component will address unique challenges posed by Khmer’s conjunct consonants and vowel diacritics in historical orthography, employing convolutional neural networks trained on a newly curated dataset of annotated manuscript images. Parallelized text processing pipelines will extract phonological, morphological, and discourse features at scale, enabling quantitative analysis of linguistic change and intertextual relationships. Expected outcomes include the first multidialectal, diachronic Khmer corpus with machine-readable metadata, an open-source toolkit for Khmer NLP tasks, and empirical insights into the influence of Sanskrit-Pali borrowings on literary registers. By overcoming current computational barriers to handling Khmer’s linguistic complexity and fragmented textual record, this research will empower scholars to investigate previously intractable questions about language standardization, literary canon formation, and cultural identity. The infrastructure developed will serve as a template for computational humanities research on other low-resource languages with non-Latin scripts, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between linguists, historians, and computer scientists.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Khmer language as spoken in Cambodia. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of emergent intergroup conflicts in fragmented societies, with a focus on identifying scalable strategies for de-escalation and reconciliation. Traditional conflict resolution frameworks often rely on qualitative case studies or small-scale simulations, limiting their capacity to predict nonlinear outcomes in complex, multi-actor systems. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational models that integrate behavioral psychology, sociopolitical network analysis, and geospatial data to simulate conflict propagation under varying governance and intervention scenarios. The core computational challenge lies in simulating millions of agent interactions across heterogeneous populations while incorporating real-world datasets on historical grievances, resource distribution, and communication patterns. We propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture both micro-level decision-making and macro-level systemic feedback loops. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing simulations across diverse parameter spaces—including intervention timing, third-party mediation strategies, and misinformation spread—and for training GNNs on high-dimensional datasets spanning conflict records, social media traces, and satellite imagery. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible simulation framework for testing conflict mitigation policies in silico, (2) quantitative thresholds for early warning indicators of systemic destabilization, and (3) evidence-based insights into how localized de-escalation tactics can be optimized to prevent regional conflict spillover. By bridging computational social science with peace studies, this work aims to provide policymakers and NGOs with actionable tools to address 21st-century conflicts characterized by rapidly evolving digital ecosystems and transnational ideological networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of international and inter-group conflicts. Includes instruction in peace research methods and related social scientific and psychological knowledge bases.

abstract: The efficient and sustainable extraction of subsurface resources through well drilling requires precise modeling of complex geological systems, fluid dynamics, and equipment performance under variable operational conditions. Current industry-standard simulations often rely on simplified assumptions about subsurface heterogeneity, multiphase flow dynamics, and drill bit-rock interactions, leading to suboptimal well placement, increased risk of mechanical failure, and environmental hazards. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models to optimize drilling processes and improve predictive accuracy in heterogeneous formations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-physics framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for drill string stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for borehole fluid behavior, and machine learning (ML) to assimilate real-time sensor data from drilling operations. The models will be calibrated against field data from active drilling sites, including lithological logs, pressure-temperature profiles, and equipment telemetry. Key computational challenges include resolving millimeter-to-kilometer spatial scales, coupling transient thermal-mechanical-hydraulic processes, and achieving near-real-time model updates during drilling. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of cores, reducing runtime for iterative design optimizations from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for adaptive drilling parameter selection, risk mitigation strategies for fractured or unstable formations, and open-source tools for well efficiency benchmarking. This work directly supports the program’s mission to advance technical training in drilling technologies while addressing critical industry needs for cost-effective, environmentally responsible resource extraction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, maintain, repair, and operate well drilling equipment; locate, drill, construct, and develop water, gas, and oil wells; and test and monitor wells to ensure adequate flow. Includes applications to home, business, and industrial uses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the quantitative analysis of ballet movement, with a focus on optimizing choreographic innovation and dancer training protocols. While ballet pedagogy and performance have historically relied on qualitative observation, the research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational tools to model the biomechanical complexity of ballet techniques or to systematically analyze choreographic patterns across historical repertoires. Current methods for capturing movement data—such as wearable sensors or video annotation—produce high-dimensional datasets that exceed the processing capabilities of standard workstations, particularly when simulating ensemble interactions or longitudinal training adaptations. This project proposes a computational framework integrating motion capture data from professional dancers, biomechanical simulations of ballet-specific movements (e.g., grand jeté, fouetté turns), and machine learning models trained to identify stylistic signatures in choreographic sequences. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of musculoskeletal simulations to assess injury risk factors under varying kinematic conditions, as well as real-time rendering of ensemble choreography in virtual environments for compositional experimentation. A key innovation involves translating Labanotation scores into spatially annotated datasets, facilitating the computational comparison of stylistic variations across ballet traditions (e.g., Vaganova vs. Bournonville schools). Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automating movement quality assessment, predictive models to personalize training regimens, and a digital archive of annotated choreographic works. By bridging computational modeling and embodied practice, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for dance research—enhancing the preservation of artistic heritage while providing evidence-based strategies for performance optimization. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated deep learning workflows, high-fidelity biomechanical simulations, and the storage of multi-terabyte motion capture libraries, which are critical to achieving statistical robustness in this understudied domain.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to express ideals and feelings through interpretation of classical dance choreography. Includes instruction in ballet exercise, solo and ensemble dance, history of ballet, ballet choreography, Laban notation, ballet technique, and interpretations of specific styles and schools.

abstract: Medical toxicology faces critical challenges in predicting and mitigating complex toxic exposures, which often involve dynamic interactions between multiple drugs, environmental toxins, and patient-specific factors. Current clinical tools lack the capacity to model these multidimensional interactions at scale, particularly for emerging synthetic drugs, chemical mixtures, or novel toxicants where human data are sparse. This project seeks to develop computational models to predict toxicity mechanisms, optimize treatment protocols, and identify risk biomarkers by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, toxicogenomics databases, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) parameters, and molecular dynamics simulations of toxin-receptor interactions. Machine learning frameworks will be trained to identify patterns in drug-drug-environment interactions linked to adverse outcomes, while parallelized molecular simulations will characterize binding affinities of understudied synthetic opioids and environmental neurotoxicants. A key focus is simulating large-scale virtual populations to assess how genetic polymorphisms, comorbidities, and polypharmacy influence toxicity thresholds—a task requiring HPC due to the combinatorial complexity of variables. Expected outcomes include predictive models for acute multi-substance overdose management, a toxicity risk stratification tool for clinical use, and mechanistic insights into novel toxicant actions. These resources will address urgent gaps in medical toxicology, such as improving antidote development for emerging synthetic drugs and personalizing treatments for chemically exposed populations. The computational infrastructure will also support real-time toxicity surveillance by analyzing regional poison control center data streams, enhancing preparedness for mass exposure events. By bridging clinical data with molecular-scale simulations, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in overdose response, chemical threat mitigation, and precision toxicology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians who specialize in the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and monitoring of injury and illness from exposures to drugs and chemicals, as well as exposures to biological and radiological agents. Important areas include acute drug poisoning; adverse drug events; drug abuse, addiction, and withdrawal; chemicals and hazardous materials; terrorism preparedness; venomous bites and stings; and environmental and workplace exposures.

abstract: Healthcare administrative workflows are increasingly strained by the growing complexity of patient scheduling, resource coordination, and compliance tracking in multidisciplinary clinical environments. Traditional rule-based systems for managing these tasks often lack the flexibility to adapt to dynamic operational demands, leading to inefficiencies that delay care and increase costs. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven framework to optimize real-time decision-making in medical administrative workflows, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze heterogeneous datasets spanning electronic health records (EHRs), staff schedules, equipment availability, and regulatory constraints. The research problem centers on creating scalable computational models capable of predicting administrative bottlenecks—such as conflicting specialist appointments or equipment overutilization—while adhering to privacy-preserving data governance standards. Computational methods will integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) to model interdependencies among clinical actors and resources, combined with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate adaptive scheduling policies under uncertainty. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of these models on multi-institutional datasets, including temporal, textual, and structured data from EHR audit logs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating clinic-wide administrative scenarios and generating prioritized task lists for medical secretarial teams, dynamically adjusted using real-time data streams. The significance lies in bridging the gap between operational research and frontline healthcare administration, offering a novel computational paradigm to reduce preventable delays in care delivery. By focusing on the understudied intersection of healthcare operations and AI-driven workflow optimization, this work addresses an emerging niche in health sciences, with potential applications in specialty care coordination, telehealth triage systems, and compliance-aware resource allocation.
cip_title: Medical Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing physicians and nurses, health care facilities and services administrators, and other health care professionals. Includes instruction in business and medical communications, medical terminology, principles of health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize air traffic management (ATM) systems under dynamically changing conditions, addressing the growing complexity of airspace operations due to increasing global air traffic. Current air traffic control (ATC) strategies often rely on static models and human-driven decision-making, which struggle to adapt to real-time variables such as weather disruptions, emergency rerouting, and fluctuating demand. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale air traffic scenarios, integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms and real-time data assimilation to improve predictive routing and conflict resolution. By modeling airspace as a dynamic network, the project will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate probabilistic outcomes of traffic flow management decisions under uncertainty, including turbulence, equipment failures, and communication delays. Additionally, graph neural networks (GNNs) will be trained on historical and synthetic flight data to identify optimal sequencing and spacing strategies for congested airspace sectors. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for rapid, iterative simulations across thousands of concurrent flights and the training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and low-latency interconnects. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of reducing flight delays by 15–20% in simulated high-density scenarios, as well as novel metrics for quantifying airspace resilience. This work will directly inform FAA training protocols and contribute to open-source ATC simulation tools, enhancing the adaptability of next-generation aviation systems. Results will be validated against operational data from the FAA’s Enhanced Traffic Management System (ETMS), ensuring translational relevance for both policymakers and aviation technology developers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to air-traffic management and control, usually with additional training at the FAA Flight Control Center in a cooperative education program. Includes instruction in flight control, the use of radar and electronic scanning devices, plotting of flights, radio communication, interpretation of weather conditions affecting flights, flight instrumentation used by pilots, and maintenance of flight-control center or control-tower log books.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-resourced Slavic, Baltic, and Albanian languages, focusing on their morphological complexity and dialectal variation. While computational linguistics has made significant strides in modeling high-resource languages, many languages within the Slavic-Baltic-Albanian continuum lack robust digital tools and datasets, hindering automated text processing, historical linguistic analysis, and the preservation of endangered dialects. The research problem centers on developing scalable, language-specific models for morphological disambiguation and dialect classification, tasks that require processing large, heterogeneous corpora spanning multiple orthographic traditions and historical periods. The computational approach integrates rule-based systems with neural architectures (e.g., transformer-based models fine-tuned on manually annotated data) to handle agglutinative morphology and phonological shifts. Parallelized workflows will be implemented to process digitized texts, archival recordings, and dialect maps, with iterative model training optimized for GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include open-source NLP pipelines for Albanian and Baltic languages, a comparative database of South Slavic dialect features, and computational evidence for contested phylogenetic relationships within the Slavic-Baltic subgroup. These resources will enable scholars to analyze textual and spoken data at unprecedented scales, supporting interdisciplinary research in historical linguistics, sociolinguistics, and digital humanities. The project’s demands—including large-scale parallel corpus processing, hyperparameter optimization for low-resource language models, and geospatial analysis of dialect data—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve runtime efficiency and methodological reproducibility. By bridging gaps in digital infrastructure for these languages, the work aims to catalyze new research trajectories while preserving linguistic diversity through computationally accessible resources.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic, Baltic, and Albanian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Slavic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Respiratory care therapy faces a critical challenge in personalizing mechanical ventilation strategies for patients with heterogeneous lung pathologies, such as acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Current clinical protocols rely on generalized algorithms, which often fail to account for dynamic, patient-specific biomechanical factors, leading to suboptimal outcomes and ventilator-induced lung injury. This project proposes a computational framework to model individualized respiratory mechanics and predict optimal ventilator settings by integrating high-fidelity simulations of lung airflow, tissue deformation, and gas exchange. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) simulations, informed by patient-specific thoracic CT scans, pulmonary function tests, and real-time ventilator data. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational cost by training surrogate models on simulation outputs, enabling rapid parameter optimization for clinical decision support. Key deliverables include an open-source software pipeline for simulating multiscale lung mechanics and a validated predictive model for recommending personalized positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) and tidal volume settings. The computational demands are significant, requiring parallelized processing of 3D meshes with >10 million elements, iterative solvers for nonlinear fluid-structure interactions, and large-scale hyperparameter tuning for neural networks. Successfully linking patient-specific lung dynamics to ventilator responses could revolutionize precision respiratory care, reducing morbidity associated with mechanical ventilation. This work bridges clinical respiratory therapy, biomechanical engineering, and computational science, offering a novel paradigm for resource allocation in critical care environments while advancing foundational knowledge in cardiopulmonary pathophysiology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize the design and testing of energy-efficient computer hardware systems, addressing the growing demand for high-performance, low-power computing architectures in edge computing and embedded applications. Current simulation tools for hardware component interaction—particularly in multi-processor systems and heterogeneous peripheral interfaces—struggle to balance accuracy with computational efficiency, leading to protracted design cycles and suboptimal resource allocation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid modeling approach combining finite element analysis for thermal-electrical behavior with discrete-event simulations of data flow dynamics. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize multi-physics simulations across varying scales of hardware granularity, from transistor-level electronic characteristics to system-wide thermal management. Key computational challenges include resolving time-step disparities between electrical and thermal models, optimizing memory usage for large-scale component arrays, and validating results against physical prototyping data from industry partners. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for rapid hardware configuration testing, a database of energy-optimal architectures for IoT-grade processors, and predictive models for fault tolerance in high-density peripheral interconnects. By reducing iterative prototyping costs and enabling data-driven design choices, this work aims to accelerate the development of sustainable, application-specific hardware systems while providing hands-on training in HPC-aided engineering for students in computer hardware technology. The requested computing resources will directly support GPU-accelerated finite element solvers and distributed memory simulations, which are critical for achieving the project’s resolution targets within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: Clinical psychology requires advanced tools to address the complexity of psychological disorders, particularly in predicting treatment outcomes and understanding heterogeneous patient responses. Current approaches often struggle to integrate high-dimensional data—such as neuroimaging, genomic variants, and real-time behavioral metrics—due to computational limitations. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive models that optimize treatment personalization for major depressive disorder (MDD) and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). The research will employ multi-modal data from 1,500 patients, including functional MRI scans, polygenic risk scores, electronic health records, and ecological momentary assessments (EMA). Computational workflows will combine deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models for temporal symptom tracking and 3D convolutional networks for neuroimaging analysis, with Bayesian hierarchical frameworks to account for individual- and population-level variability. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in treatment effect estimates, and hyperparameter optimization across 50,000+ model configurations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms predicting CBT and SSRI response probabilities with >80% cross-validated accuracy, (2) dynamic biomarkers linking default mode network connectivity to relapse risk, and (3) open-source software for clinical decision support integrating these models. By enabling rapid analysis of interactions between neurocognitive profiles, genetic predispositions, and therapeutic interventions, this work will directly inform stepped-care protocols while reducing the societal burden of treatment-resistant cases. The computational infrastructure requested is essential to overcome memory and processing constraints inherent in federated learning across multi-site datasets, ensuring clinically actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical psychology, involving the analysis, diagnosis, and clinical treatment of psychological disorders and behavioral pathologies. Includes instruction in clinical assessment and diagnosis, personality appraisal, psychopathology, clinical psychopharmacology, behavior modification, therapeutic intervention skills, patient interviewing, personalized and group therapy, child and adolescent therapy, cognitive and behavioral therapy, supervised clinical practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying plant responses to combined abiotic stresses, with a focus on drought and soil salinity—two interconnected challenges threatening global crop productivity. While prior studies have characterized plant stress responses under isolated conditions, real-world agricultural systems often expose plants to concurrent stressors, triggering nonlinear physiological and genomic interactions that remain poorly resolved. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets (genome, transcriptome, and metabolome) from maize (Zea mays) and soybean (Glycine max) subjected to combinatorial stress treatments. A hybrid computational pipeline will integrate machine learning-based feature selection, dynamic network modeling, and comparative genomics to identify conserved regulatory modules and stress-specific adaptive pathways. Bulk RNA-seq data from controlled-environment experiments will be supplemented with publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize structural changes in key stress-responsive proteins under varying ionic and osmotic conditions. The computational workload necessitates large-scale parallel processing for Bayesian network inference, GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures for pattern recognition in hyperspectral imaging data, and high-memory nodes for genome assembly tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model of core signaling hubs governing cross-stress adaptation, (2) candidate gene targets for breeding programs aimed at stress-resilient crops, and (3) open-source tools for multi-scale integration of plant phenomic and genomic data. By elucidating emergent properties of stress combination responses, this work will advance fundamental knowledge in plant systems biology while directly informing translational efforts to mitigate climate-related agricultural losses. The requested allocation of 250,000 CPU-core hours and 50 TB of temporary storage will support data-intensive workflows spanning 18 months, enabling analyses impractical on local institutional clusters.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plant sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of collective escape behaviors in mixed-species animal groups using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate complex, multi-scale interactions. While collective behavior has been studied in single-species contexts, the role of interspecific differences in sensory perception, locomotion, and decision-making algorithms during predator avoidance remains poorly understood. We propose developing a novel, modular agent-based model (ABM) that integrates species-specific biomechanical constraints, environmental heterogeneity, and real-world data on sensory thresholds (e.g., visual fields of birds, lateral line sensitivity in fish) to simulate cross-taxa interactions. The HPC framework will enable parallelized simulations of >10^5 agents across parameter spaces governing group composition, threat detection latency, and evasion strategies. Computational challenges include optimizing neighbor-detection algorithms for polydisperse groups and validating model outputs against 3D movement datasets from drone-recorded wild mixed flocks. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in species ratios that stabilize or destabilize group cohesion under predation and quantifying energy trade-offs in escape trajectories. This work will provide foundational insights into how biodiversity within animal collectives influences survival strategies—a pressing concern in conservation biology amid shifting species distributions. The resulting open-source code will offer a unique tool for zoologists studying niche ecological interactions beyond traditional single-species paradigms. Resource allocation is requested for GPU-accelerated nodes to manage memory-intensive spatial computations and iterative parameter sweeps across biologically plausible scenarios.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in zoology/animal biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives within South Asian literary and digital media texts and their influence on diaspora identity formation. The research addresses the challenge of analyzing vast, multilingual textual corpora spanning pre-colonial manuscripts, post-colonial literature, and contemporary online forums, which are critical to understanding shifting cultural discourses across temporal and geographical boundaries. Current methodologies in South Asian Studies lack scalable tools to process these heterogeneous datasets, limiting insights into how narratives adapt in diasporic contexts. To overcome this, the project employs computational textual analysis, leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to identify thematic patterns, semantic shifts, and cross-linguistic influences. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on low-resource South Asian languages, conducting large-scale topic modeling across centuries of texts, and performing network analysis of narrative diffusion through migration pathways. The computational workflow includes preprocessing digitized archives using OCR correction pipelines, aligning multilingual embeddings, and applying dynamic topic models to trace continuity and change in cultural motifs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated texts, visualization tools for narrative mapping, and quantitative frameworks linking linguistic features to socio-cultural identity markers. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this research will provide novel insights into the resilience and adaptation of South Asian cultural narratives, offering scholars a model for interdisciplinary studies of global diasporas. The project’s findings aim to inform cultural preservation initiatives and diaspora community engagement strategies while advancing methodological synergies between area studies and digital humanities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of South Asia, defined as including Afghanistan, India, the Maldives, Myanmar (Burma), Pakistan, and Sri Lanka and related borderlands and island groups; and including the study of migration patterns and overseas diasporas.

abstract: Understanding the ecological and evolutionary drivers of zoonotic disease spillover remains a critical challenge in epidemiology, particularly as anthropogenic environmental change alters species interactions and pathogen transmission dynamics. This project seeks to model how landscape fragmentation, climate variability, and host community composition jointly influence spillover risk for emerging viral pathogens at wildlife-human interfaces. We propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that integrates spatially explicit habitat data, host movement ecology, and viral phylogenetics to simulate transmission pathways under multiple environmental scenarios. The computational approach requires high-performance computing resources to handle three key components: (1) parameterization of multi-host contact networks using GPS tracking data from 12 reservoir species (totaling >5TB movement trajectories), (2) parallelized simulation of 10^6 possible transmission trees incorporating host immune competence and viral mutation rates, and (3) Bayesian inference of landscape features associated with spillover hotspots across different ecological contexts. By coupling evolutionary models of viral adaptation with ecological networks of host species distributions, this work will advance predictive capacity for identifying high-risk interfaces where preventive health measures could mitigate outbreak potential. Expected outcomes include novel metrics for quantifying spillover vulnerability across heterogeneous landscapes, identification of key host species contributing to cross-species transmission, and projections of how climate-mediated range shifts may alter disease emergence patterns through 2100. The computational framework will be designed for scalability to other pathogen systems, providing an open-source tool for analyzing complex eco-epidemiological interactions. This research directly addresses the National Institutes of Health priority to understand environmental determinants of infectious disease emergence while supporting public health planning through spatially targeted surveillance strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of disease, disability, and trauma patterns within and across populations and the development of health management mechanisms to prevent and control disease outbreaks and injurious behaviors. Includes instruction in biostatistics, biochemistry, molecular biology, immunology, disease and injury determinants, genetic disease and disability factors, behavioral studies, health services research, environmental disease and injury factors, and population studies.

abstract: The integration of ethical reasoning and humanities into health professions education remains a critical yet underexplored area, particularly in understanding how complex sociocultural dynamics influence decision-making among trainees. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to analyze large-scale qualitative and quantitative datasets from interdisciplinary health education contexts, including simulation-based training, reflective narratives, and longitudinal assessments of ethical competency. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to systematically evaluate unstructured textual data—such as student journals, patient interaction transcripts, and ethics case discussions—for patterns in moral reasoning, bias, and contextual sensitivity. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate educational environments to assess how variable curricula, institutional policies, and cultural factors interact to shape trainee outcomes. These computational approaches require the parallel processing capabilities of HPC to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train deep learning architectures, and run iterative simulations with dynamic parameter adjustments. Expected outcomes include the identification of pedagogical strategies that robustly enhance ethical decision-making, predictive models linking specific educational interventions to competency development, and a publicly accessible framework for analyzing humanities-based health education data. By elucidating the multidimensional drivers of ethical formation in health professions training, this work will inform curriculum design, accreditation standards, and policies aimed at fostering equitable, culturally responsive care. The requested HPC allocation will enable the scalability, speed, and reproducibility necessary to advance this emerging intersection of computational social science and health professions education.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop and optimize advanced computer-aided design and drafting (CAD/CADD) workflows for complex engineering systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current CAD/CADD tools face limitations in efficiently simulating high-fidelity, multi-physics models—such as those involving structural, thermal, and fluid dynamic interactions—due to computational bottlenecks. These constraints hinder real-time design iteration, scalability for large-scale systems (e.g., aerospace components, renewable energy infrastructure), and the integration of generative design algorithms that require intensive parallel processing. To address this, the research will implement distributed computing frameworks to accelerate parametric modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Custom scripts will automate mesh generation, topology optimization, and performance validation across HPC clusters, while machine learning models will be trained to predict design failures and propose material or geometric optimizations. The project will also explore GPU-accelerated rendering for immersive 3D visualization of multi-disciplinary systems. Outcomes aim to reduce simulation runtime by 40–60% compared to traditional workstations, enable real-time collaborative editing of terabyte-scale CADD projects via cloud-HPC hybrid architectures, and establish scalable workflows for AI-driven generative design. Success will directly benefit engineering education by integrating HPC-based CAD/CADD modules into the curriculum, preparing students to tackle industry challenges in sustainable infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, and robotics. The resource allocation will support benchmarking, algorithm development, and open-source toolkits to democratize HPC access for academic CAD/CADD research.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the structural and cultural dynamics of congregational hymnody across underrepresented religious traditions using computational methods, with a focus on patterns of melodic adaptation and lyrical transmission in diasporic communities. While existing scholarship has cataloged liturgical music within major traditions, the evolution of hymns in marginalized or syncretic practices—such as Indigenous Christian blends, Afro-Caribbean spirituals, or post-Soviet Baptist communities—remains understudied due to the scale and complexity of cross-cultural analysis required. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze a multilingual corpus of over 20,000 hymn texts and 15,000 audio recordings spanning 150 years, integrating optical music recognition (OMR), semantic network analysis, and phylogenetic modeling. Custom machine learning pipelines will identify melodic motifs and lyrical adaptations, tracing regional variations against historical migration data and ethnographic records. By parallelizing feature extraction across audio and textual datasets, the computational workflow will map how theological narratives and musical practices mutate in response to sociopolitical pressures, linguistic shifts, and interfaith contact. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated hymns, statistical models of cultural retention thresholds in displaced communities, and a framework for quantifying the interplay between musical complexity and congregational participation. This work bridges ethnomusicology, diaspora studies, and digital humanities, offering methodological innovations for analyzing cultural resilience through performative worship traditions. The scale of data processing—requiring GPU-accelerated OMR, distributed NLP for low-resource languages, and Monte Carlo simulations of transmission pathways—necessitates HPC resources to achieve feasible runtime for iterative model training and large-scale comparative analysis.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious music and worship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: We propose to develop an integrated computational framework to investigate the resilience of aquatic ecosystems under compounding stressors, focusing on how species interactions and evolutionary adaptations mediate responses to nutrient shifts and climate-driven disturbances. Current models often oversimplify biotic feedbacks or neglect co-evolutionary dynamics, limiting predictions for real-world communities. Our project addresses this gap by coupling agent-based simulations of organismal interactions (e.g., predator-prey dynamics, competition) with phylogenetic comparative methods to evaluate how historical adaptation influences contemporary ecological stability. The study will parameterize models using empirical data from long-term lake monitoring, experimental mesocosms, and paleoecological records of regime shifts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale spatial heterogeneity in nutrient gradients and simulate evolutionary trajectories across 10^3–10^5 generation timescales. Key computational challenges include parallelizing individual-based simulations across dynamic landscapes, optimizing matrix operations for Lotka-Volterra extensions incorporating heritable trait variation, and conducting sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces representing >200 species pairs. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of trophic network structures that confer resilience to simultaneous warming and eutrophication, (2) quantification of co-evolution’s role in delaying ecosystem collapse, and (3) paleo-validated thresholds for critical nutrient loads under varying thermal scenarios. Results will directly inform watershed management strategies while advancing theoretical integration of ecological and evolutionary timescales. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes will enable parameter sweeps across biologically realistic ranges currently infeasible on local clusters, particularly for stochastic simulations requiring >10^4 replicates to assess extinction probabilities. This work bridges organismal physiology, community ecology, and evolutionary history—a synthesis demanding computational scale beyond conventional ecological modeling tools.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions of small-scale biological systems, such as organisms, to each other, to complex and whole systems, and to the physical and other non-biological aspects of their environments. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry; landscape and/or marine/aquatic dynamics; decomposition; global and regional elemental budgets; biotic and abiotic regulation of nutrient cycles; ecophysiology; ecosystem resilience, disturbance, and succession; community and habitat dynamics; organismal interactions (co-evolution, competition, predation); paleoecology; and evolutionary ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to investigate the emergent dynamics of urban microclimates under varying environmental and anthropogenic stressors, integrating multi-physics simulations with real-world sensor data. Rapid urbanization has intensified localized climate extremes, such as urban heat islands and anomalous airflow patterns, yet existing models often decouple human mobility, built-environment thermal properties, and atmospheric processes. Our research addresses this gap by coupling agent-based crowd dynamics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and heat transport models within a unified simulation environment. The computational approach leverages adaptive mesh refinement to resolve meter-scale variations in temperature and airflow while capturing city-wide patterns through GPU-accelerated parallelization. Machine learning techniques will be applied to assimilate heterogeneous datasets—including IoT sensor networks, satellite thermal imagery, and pedestrian movement traces—into the simulation pipeline, enabling dynamic calibration of boundary conditions. High-performance computing resources are critical to manage the combinatorial complexity of modeling transient interactions between physical systems (e.g., building materials, vegetation) and human activities (e.g., traffic, urban infrastructure use) across diurnal and seasonal cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify the efficacy of heat mitigation strategies—such as green infrastructure placement or reflective surface materials—under diverse climate scenarios. The framework will advance interdisciplinary methodologies for urban resilience planning, bridging civil engineering, environmental science, and social dynamics modeling. By enabling granular analysis of microclimate feedback loops, this work will provide actionable insights for policymakers addressing climate adaptation in densely populated regions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of computing and its application for solving challenges in science and engineering fields, with a focus on principles from mathematics, science, engineering and computing.

abstract: This project seeks to address unresolved questions in computational complexity theory, particularly the classification of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) within the polynomial hierarchy. While CSPs are foundational to artificial intelligence, optimization, and formal verification, the tractability boundaries for many CSP classes remain ambiguous, impeding both theoretical understanding and practical algorithm design. The core challenge lies in systematically analyzing the solvability of CSPs under varying constraint types and structural parameters, a task that demands exhaustive exploration of exponentially large problem spaces. To achieve this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining automated theorem proving, large-scale Monte Carlo simulations, and statistical phase transition analysis. The project will deploy parallelized SAT solvers and custom algebraic closure algorithms on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to process millions of synthetically generated CSP instances. Each instance will be evaluated for satisfiability, solution-space structure, and runtime complexity across different constraint languages and graph topologies. Memory-intensive components will leverage distributed computing to manage the combinatorial explosion inherent in higher-order CSP variants. The computational results will be paired with formal methods to either prove or probabilistically validate conjectures about polynomial-time reducibility and completeness relationships. Successful execution will yield a refined complexity classification framework, potentially resolving open questions regarding the dichotomy conjecture for infinite-domain CSPs. This work is expected to advance the mathematical foundations of computation, with secondary benefits for automated reasoning systems and algorithm optimization. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the exponential scaling of key parameters, necessitating teraflop-scale processing and petabyte-scale distributed memory for statistically robust conclusions. Outcomes will be disseminated through theoretical computer science venues and open-source algorithm libraries.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical techniques underlying computing, including the theory of computation, and logic in computer science and artificial intelligence.

abstract: Neuropathological research faces critical challenges in integrating high-dimensional datasets from histopathological imaging, molecular profiling, and clinical phenotypes to diagnose and understand neurological and neuromuscular diseases. Current diagnostic workflows for nerve biopsies and post-mortem tissues rely on labor-intensive, subjective analyses of structural and cellular anomalies, which lack the resolution to disentangle complex molecular drivers of diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer’s disease, and inflammatory neuropathies. This project proposes a computational pathology pipeline to quantify and model multi-scale neuropathological features, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabyte-scale imaging datasets and perform integrative analyses. We will develop deep learning models, including 3D convolutional neural networks and graph-based architectures, to analyze whole-slide imaging (WSI) of nerve biopsies and electron microscopy datasets, capturing subcellular pathologies such as axonal degeneration, protein aggregates, and inflammatory infiltrates. These imaging datasets will be integrated with spatially resolved transcriptomic profiles and clinical metadata using probabilistic graphical models to identify disease-specific signatures. HPC resources are essential for training large-scale models on distributed GPU clusters, parallel processing of multi-modal data, and running iterative simulations to infer molecular-pathological correlations. Expected outcomes include (1) automated tools for detecting and grading neuropathological features with subcellular precision, (2) predictive models linking spatial transcriptomic patterns to disease progression, and (3) open-source pipelines for scalable analysis of neuropathology data. This work will advance objective, data-driven diagnostic criteria for rare neurological disorders and provide a framework for biomarker discovery. The requested computing resources will enable handling unprecedented data volumes from ongoing collaborations with seven clinical centers, directly supporting translational research to improve patient stratification and therapeutic targeting.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory analysis of nerve tissues and the clinical diagnosis of neurological and neuromuscular diseases. May included related research in nerve biopsies and necropsies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop adaptive computational tools to optimize individualized education program (IEP) design for K–12 students with orthopedic and physical health impairments. Current IEP development relies heavily on qualitative assessments and manual data integration, which limits scalability and fails to systematically account for dynamic factors such as fluctuating mobility, assistive technology use patterns, and environmental accessibility barriers. To address this gap, we propose creating machine learning models trained on multimodal datasets—including anonymized student health records, classroom sensor data on physical interactions, and longitudinal academic performance metrics—to predict optimal instructional strategies and accommodations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing high-dimensional data from wearable movement trackers (sampled at 100Hz) and school-wide Internet of Things (IoT) systems that monitor classroom accessibility in real time. Computational workflows will include biomechanical simulations of student-device interactions using finite element modeling, natural language processing of IEP text corpora to identify underutilized accommodations, and reinforcement learning agents trained in synthetic classroom environments. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source framework for generating evidence-based IEP recommendations with quantified confidence intervals, (2) physics-informed neural networks capable of forecasting fatigue risks during school activities, and (3) synthetic data generators to model rare impairment subtypes. This work directly supports teacher preparation programs by providing scalable tools to analyze complex student needs while maintaining compliance with IDEA accessibility standards. The requested resources will enable processing an anticipated 350TB of multimodal training data and parallelized hyperparameter optimization across 10,000+ model configurations, which cannot feasibly be implemented on local institutional clusters.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Orthopedic and Other Physical Health Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with orthopedic and other health impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying physically disabled students, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with orthopedic and other health impairments, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized care plans for elderly patients with multiple chronic conditions, a population often underrepresented in clinical trials despite their complex healthcare needs. Current approaches to predicting adverse events—such as polypharmacy complications, falls, or hospital readmissions—rely on generalized models that fail to account for the heterogeneity of aging-related physiological changes, social determinants of health, and comorbidities. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models capable of integrating multi-modal geriatric health data, including longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), medication histories, wearable device outputs, and patient-reported outcomes. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing large-scale EHR datasets (spanning 10+ years) to extract geriatric-specific features, followed by training ensemble ML algorithms to identify risk patterns and simulate interventions. Deep learning architectures will be tested for their ability to model temporal relationships in medication adherence and disease progression, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will parse unstructured clinical notes for social and cognitive risk factors. The HPC environment is essential for managing data volumes (>100 TB), parallelizing hyperparameter tuning across thousands of model iterations, and conducting real-time simulations of care pathway outcomes. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for adverse event risk stratification, optimized medication reconciliation protocols accounting for age-related pharmacokinetic changes, and dynamic care plan recommendations adaptable to individual patient trajectories. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of geriatric-specific datasets, this work will advance evidence-based precision nursing practices, inform policy for aging populations, and reduce preventable complications in vulnerable elderly patients.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal analysis in Tribal and Indigenous Law, a specialized interdisciplinary domain intersecting jurisprudence, Indigenous governance, and human rights. The research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing the vast, unstructured corpus of legal texts—including treaties, court decisions, tribal codes, and international human rights documents—that shape Indigenous legal sovereignty and policy outcomes. Traditional legal research methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these materials, particularly when identifying longitudinal trends, cross-jurisdictional inconsistencies, or gaps in the enforcement of Indigenous rights. To address this, the project employs natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to automate the extraction of legal concepts, map relationships between case law and socio-political outcomes, and model the impact of historical precedents on contemporary tribal governance. Custom algorithms will be developed to recognize culturally specific terminology and contextualize legal narratives within Indigenous frameworks, requiring training on curated datasets of tribal court opinions, federal Indian law rulings, and oral histories. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of multilingual text, optimizing deep learning models for low-resource languages, and conducting large-scale simulations of policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated legal decisions, predictive tools to assess the viability of tribal litigation strategies, and visualizations of treaty-based land rights disputes incorporating geospatial and temporal data. By integrating computational rigor with Indigenous legal epistemologies, this research aims to empower tribal governments, legal practitioners, and advocacy organizations with data-driven insights to navigate complex jurisdictional landscapes and strengthen protections for Indigenous rights. The project establishes a novel methodological framework for computational legal studies while centering ethical considerations in the use of technology for Indigenous-centered scholarship.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting federal Indian law, tribal law and policy, and Indigenous peoples' human rights.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cultural and behavioral impacts of algorithmic content curation in digital media ecosystems, with a focus on how platform-driven recommendations shape collective perceptions of social and political issues. As media industries increasingly rely on machine learning systems to personalize content, critical questions arise about the relationship between algorithmic bias, media literacy, and cultural polarization. The research employs a mixed-methods computational approach to analyze large-scale datasets of user engagement metrics, platform-recommended content, and semantic patterns across three major social media platforms. A high-performance computing (HPC) allocation is required to process multi-terabyte datasets encompassing timestamped user interactions, video/audio transcripts, and platform metadata over a 5-year period. Computational methods include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for cross-platform sentiment analysis, graph-based network modeling of information diffusion patterns, and transformer-based models fine-tuned to detect emerging narrative frameworks in visual and textual media. The analysis will integrate computational media criticism frameworks with quantitative behavioral metrics to map how recommendation algorithms amplify specific cultural discourses while suppressing others. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel dataset mapping algorithmic content prioritization to demographic engagement patterns, 2) computational models identifying platform-specific amplification biases in cultural representation, and 3) visual analytics tools for tracing the evolution of media narratives across hybrid digital ecosystems. This research addresses critical gaps in media studies’ capacity to analyze platformized cultural production at scale, with potential applications for media literacy initiatives, platform governance debates, and interdisciplinary frameworks for studying computational cultural systems. The requested resources will enable processing of temporally dense, multimodal media data that exceeds the capabilities of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis and criticism of media institutions and media texts, how people experience and understand media content, and the roles of media in producing and transforming culture. Includes instruction in communications regulation, law, and policy; media history; media aesthetics, interpretation, and criticism; the social and cultural effects of mass media; cultural studies; the economics of media industries; visual and media literacy; and the psychology and behavioral aspects of media messages, interpretation, and utilization.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to optimize the integration of heterogeneous combat systems within dynamic, multi-domain operational environments. Modern military platforms increasingly rely on interconnected sensor, weapon, and decision-support subsystems operating across air, land, sea, cyber, and space domains. However, existing simulation tools struggle to model the emergent behaviors and latency-sensitive interactions of these systems at scale, particularly when accounting for adversarial actions, environmental variability, and human-in-the-loop decision-making. The research problem centers on creating a computational environment capable of simulating networked combat systems with sufficient granularity to identify integration bottlenecks, evaluate resilience against electronic warfare threats, and predict cascading failures in contested scenarios. The proposed approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize multi-resolution simulations combining agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning-driven surrogate models. Key computational challenges include real-time synchronization of physics-based subsystem models (e.g., radar cross-section calculations, missile intercept kinematics) with strategic-level command-and-control logic, while maintaining the fidelity required for tactical relevance. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation architecture compatible with existing military digital engineering tools, quantitative metrics for combat system interoperability under stress conditions, and AI-assisted optimization techniques for rapid configuration of mission-specific system-of-systems architectures. By enabling large-scale exploration of design tradeoffs and failure modes early in the acquisition lifecycle, this work aims to reduce integration risks in next-generation combat systems while informing joint interoperability standards.
