The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of threat scenarios, supporting million-core-hour parametric studies across hardware configurations, and validating results against classified benchmark data through approved secure computing protocols.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of systems engineering and system architecture to the design and construction of modern combat systems and their integration with each other, with host platforms and with other forces into network-centric warfighting systems. Includes instruction in systems engineering, computer programming, chemical systems, biological systems, material systems, human factors, combat environments, sensor systems, threat and system risk assessment, conventional and unconventional weapons, combat simulation, reliability and maintenance, testing, engineering project management, strategic planning and applications to aerospace, ground, and naval combat systems.

abstract: The study of planetary atmospheres and their interaction with magnetospheric and space environments remains a critical challenge in understanding the evolution and habitability of planetary systems. This project seeks to advance high-resolution modeling of ion-neutral coupling and atmospheric escape processes in the upper atmospheres of gas giants and exoplanets, with a focus on non-equilibrium dynamics driven by extreme stellar and magnetospheric forcing. Current models lack the spatial resolution and coupled physics required to capture the multi-scale interactions between neutral atmospheric layers, ionospheric currents, and plasma transport—a gap that limits predictive capability for atmospheric mass loss and its role in planetary evolution. To address this, we propose a novel computational framework integrating a 3D general circulation model with a magnetohydrodynamic solver, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The model will resolve sub-meter-scale turbulence in the thermosphere-ionosphere boundary while maintaining global-scale coupling, enabled by adaptive mesh refinement and hybrid CPU-GPU parallelization. Simulations will be validated against Juno and Cassini mission data for Jupiter and Saturn, then extended to hypothetical exoplanet regimes with varying orbital distances and stellar activity levels. The project requires access to HPC resources capable of sustaining 200,000+ core-hours per simulation, with petabyte-scale data output for spectral analysis and machine learning-driven parameterization of small-scale processes. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of atmospheric escape rates under extreme space weather conditions, (2) identification of instability thresholds governing large-scale magnetosphere-atmosphere energy transfer, and (3) publicly accessible datasets for comparative planetary climate studies. These results will directly inform the interpretation of JWST observations and ESA’s upcoming ARIEL mission, while advancing fundamental knowledge of how planetary atmospheres evolve under diverse astrophysical conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets and their planetary systems, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, moons, ring systems, gas clouds, magnetospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting and modeling the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) through advanced computational approaches. Despite advances in early detection, OSCC prognosis remains highly variable due to the complex interplay of tumor microenvironment heterogeneity, genomic instability, and host immune responses. Traditional experimental methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multiscale biological processes driving tumor evolution, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-omics data and simulate disease mechanisms. The research will employ a hybrid computational framework combining bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data with spatially resolved proteomic profiles from clinical biopsy samples. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to identify predictive signatures of metastasis and treatment resistance. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate cell-cell interactions within tumor-immune ecosystems, parameterized by patient-derived data. These computational workflows require massive parallelization for parameter optimization, 3D spatial reconstruction of tumor architectures, and probabilistic inference across terabyte-scale datasets. The integration of HPC resources will enable the creation of a scalable digital twin platform to test personalized therapeutic strategies in silico. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for risk stratification, predictive models of therapeutic response, and mechanistic insights into immune evasion pathways. This work will provide a paradigm for computationally driven precision oncology in oral cancers, with implications for clinical trial design and real-time adaptive treatment planning. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to bridge critical gaps between molecular discovery and clinical translation in head and neck oncology, ultimately improving survival rates and quality of life for patients with advanced OSCC.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of intergenerational family resilience in marginalized communities through advanced computational modeling. The research problem centers on understanding how non-linear interactions between cultural, socioeconomic, and psychological factors shape family adaptation strategies in contexts of systemic inequality—a gap in current human development frameworks that rely heavily on static, survey-based methodologies. By developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating multigenerational decision-making processes, we aim to capture emergent patterns of resilience that traditional longitudinal studies cannot observe due to temporal and ethical constraints. The model will integrate qualitative data from oral histories and community narratives with quantitative socioeconomic datasets, employing machine learning techniques to calibrate agents' behavioral rules and validate against real-world outcomes. Computational challenges include managing high-dimensional parameter spaces, simulating stochastic interactions across heterogeneous agent populations, and analyzing time-series data for phase transitions in resilience trajectories. The HPC environment is critical for running large-scale sensitivity analyses and parallelized scenario testing, enabling exploration of counterfactual interventions (e.g., policy changes, community support programs) at population levels. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for identifying leverage points in family support systems, predictive insights into how localized stressors cascade across generations, and actionable metrics for culturally grounded resilience assessment. This work bridges computational social science with human development theory, offering a template for studying complex adaptive systems in under-researched populations while advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM disciplines. Results will be disseminated through open-access simulation tools and partnerships with community organizations to inform equitable program design.
cip_title: Human Development, Family Studies, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in human development, family studies, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time analysis of multi-modal clinical data streams to predict acute neurological events in critically ill patients. Current clinical decision-support systems struggle to integrate high-frequency physiological waveforms (e.g., EEG, intracranial pressure), discrete electronic health record (EHR) data, and unstructured imaging reports into unified predictive models. Our research addresses this gap by creating a machine learning architecture optimized for heterogeneous temporal medical data, targeting early detection of seizures and stroke in neurocritical care settings. The computational approach combines transformer-based models for time-series physiological data, vision-language models for radiology text-image correlation, and graph neural networks to model interdependencies between clinical variables. We will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage three key challenges: 1) processing terabyte-scale continuous monitoring data from 10,000+ patient stays, 2) training multi-modal architectures with attention mechanisms across disparate data types, and 3) implementing temporal alignment algorithms for asynchronous clinical events. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallel training of model components and high-memory nodes for assembling population-scale knowledge graphs. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for clinical temporal data fusion and validated predictive models demonstrating ≥15% improvement in early event detection compared to current clinical standards. Successful implementation could enable closed-loop monitoring systems that reduce neurological injury through timely intervention while establishing computational methods for other acute care scenarios. This work advances medical informatics by creating novel approaches for streaming health data integration, directly supporting the NIH's emphasis on AI-driven critical care innovations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to medical research and clinical information technology support, and the development of advanced imaging, database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in computer science, health information systems architecture, medical knowledge structures, medical language and image processing, quantitative medical decision modeling, imaging techniques, electronic medical records, medical research systems, clinical decision support, and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: The study of regional dialects in Romanian remains critically under-resourced, particularly in computational approaches capable of processing the scale and complexity of linguistic data required for robust analysis. Current limitations in processing power restrict the ability to systematically analyze phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variations across dialects, which are essential for understanding language evolution and its sociocultural drivers. This project proposes to address these gaps by employing high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a comprehensive dialectal corpus and train machine learning models for dialect classification and change modeling. The research will integrate heterogeneous data sources, including spoken language recordings, digitized historical texts, and modern written corpora, utilizing parallelized workflows for phonemic alignment, feature extraction, and semantic annotation. Computational methods will include transformer-based models to identify dialect-specific patterns and graph-based algorithms to map contact-induced changes between regional varieties. The scale of data—spanning terabytes of audio and text—and the computational intensity of training deep neural networks on non-standard linguistic features necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated dialectal data, predictive models for dialect classification, and quantitative insights into the dynamics of language contact in Romania’s multilingual regions. By enabling large-scale, interdisciplinary analysis of Romanian dialects, this project will advance philological research methodologies, support preservation efforts for endangered linguistic varieties, and inform the development of regionally inclusive NLP tools. The integration of HPC resources is critical to overcoming existing computational bottlenecks, ensuring that findings are both linguistically nuanced and statistically robust, thereby positioning Romanian dialectology at the forefront of digital humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Romanian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance mechanistic studies of drug-induced mitochondrial toxicity, a critical yet understudied area in pharmacological safety assessment. Current predictive models for mitochondrial dysfunction rely heavily on static in vitro assays, which fail to capture dynamic drug-metabolite interactions or tissue-specific metabolic contexts. We propose a computational framework integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling with quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations to resolve spatiotemporal patterns of drug bioactivation and subsequent mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) inhibition. The research will focus on three structurally diverse therapeutics with known mitochondrial liabilities: linezolid, valproic acid, and amiodarone. Molecular dynamics simulations will model drug interactions with ETC Complex I and III isoforms across hepatic, cardiac, and neuronal cellular environments, accounting for tissue-specific pH gradients, lipid compositions, and redox states. Ab initio calculations will quantify electron transfer interference at flavin mononucleotide and ubiquinone binding sites. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated PBPK models will simulate organ-specific accumulation patterns using human ADME data. The computational pipeline requires extensive parallelization due to the need for 1) multi-scale sampling (µs-scale MD trajectories paired with ms-scale PBPK simulations), 2) combinatorial analysis of 27 tissue-drug-time permutations per compound, and 3) iterative parameter optimization against clinical pharmacokinetic datasets. Expected outcomes include the first predictive atlas of tissue-selective mitochondrial toxicity thresholds and identification of critical redox-sensitive residues governing ETC susceptibility. This work will establish a computational toxicology platform to prioritize drug candidates with improved mitochondrial safety profiles, directly addressing FDA guidelines on preclinical metabolic risk assessment. Successful implementation requires dedicated HPC allocation for large-scale molecular simulations (>200,000 core-hours) and high-memory nodes for hybrid QM/MM workflows.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacology and toxicology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing social service delivery systems for vulnerable populations. Social work interventions, such as child welfare case management and disability counseling, involve complex, dynamic interactions between clients, providers, and policy constraints. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model these systems at scale, limiting the ability to predict service gaps or evaluate policy impacts in real time. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that simulates service access patterns, resource allocation decisions, and longitudinal client outcomes across heterogeneous populations. The ABM will integrate anonymized administrative data from multiple agencies (e.g., foster care placements, unemployment claims, and mental health service utilization) to parameterize agents representing clients, social workers, and institutions. Computational demands arise from simulating millions of agent interactions over multi-year time horizons while incorporating stochastic variables like economic shocks or staffing shortages. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to test intervention scenarios—such as reallocating caseworkers during crisis events or adjusting eligibility thresholds—with statistically robust sample sizes. Expected outcomes include identifying resource distribution strategies that reduce service delays for high-risk groups and generating predictive metrics to guide proactive policy adjustments. By quantifying trade-offs in equity, cost, and administrative burden, this work aims to provide actionable tools for social service administrators while advancing computational social work as a methodological discipline. The project will also produce open-source code to help non-technical stakeholders visualize system dynamics, fostering collaboration between researchers and practitioners in public administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional practice of social welfare administration and counseling, and that focus on the study of organized means of providing basic support services for vulnerable individuals and groups. Includes instruction in social welfare policy; case work planning; social counseling and intervention strategies; administrative procedures and regulations; and specific applications in areas such as child welfare and family services, probation, employment services, and disability counseling.

abstract: Next-generation wireless communication systems demand unprecedented computational resources to model complex electromagnetic interactions and optimize network performance under dynamic conditions. This project addresses the challenge of designing energy-efficient, high-throughput massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems operating in millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) frequency bands. Current simulation tools struggle with the spatial-temporal scale and nonlinearities inherent in these environments, limiting the exploration of optimal antenna configurations and beamforming strategies. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework combining full-wave electromagnetic simulations using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods with machine learning-driven optimization. The FDTD component will model wave propagation in complex urban environments with sub-wavelength accuracy, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively adjust beamforming coefficients and power allocation to maximize spectral efficiency. This approach requires distributed-memory parallelization for large-scale electromagnetic computations and GPU-accelerated training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets. Access to high-performance computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of antenna elements, channel realizations, and interference scenarios that are infeasible on local clusters. Expected outcomes include validated design principles for scalable mmWave/THz arrays, open-source simulation tools for the research community, and quantitative guidelines for balancing energy consumption with quality-of-service metrics in dense urban deployments. The computational infrastructure developed through this project will directly support the advancement of 6G technologies while providing a template for cross-layer optimization in next-generation communication hardware.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronics, and Communications Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Agricultural business operations face increasing complexity due to volatile market dynamics, climate variability, and the need for sustainable resource allocation. This project seeks to develop a computational decision-support framework to optimize agricultural supply chains, predict commodity price fluctuations, and evaluate operational sustainability. Current approaches often rely on static models with limited capacity to integrate high-dimensional datasets (e.g., real-time market trends, climate projections, and soil health metrics) or account for stochastic disruptions. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational workflow will train recurrent neural networks on historical commodity pricing and climate data to forecast short- to medium-term market trends, while agent-based simulations will model interactions among producers, distributors, and retailers under diverse risk scenarios. A parallelized optimization engine will then identify resilient resource allocation strategies that balance profitability, carbon footprint, and water-use efficiency. Key computational challenges include processing multi-terabyte datasets from USDA databases, IoT-enabled farm sensors, and global trade records, as well as managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-objective optimization across spatially distributed agricultural systems. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in price forecasts and supply chain vulnerabilities. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for agribusiness planners, validated against case studies in Midwestern U.S. corn-soybean systems and California specialty crop networks. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing operational risks, improving market responsiveness, and advancing sustainability goals in commercial agriculture. By integrating computational scalability with domain-specific constraints, the project aims to bridge critical gaps between agricultural business theory and data-driven decision-making in rapidly evolving food systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage agricultural businesses and agriculturally related operations within diversified corporations. Includes instruction in agriculture, agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, finance, marketing, planning, human resources management, and other managerial responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of patient outcomes in clinical support workflows, a critical challenge in allied health and medical assisting services. The research addresses the growing complexity of patient triage and resource allocation in outpatient and emergency care settings, where variability in patient acuity, staffing constraints, and evolving clinical protocols create inefficiencies that impact care quality. Current approaches to workflow optimization rely on retrospective data analyses or simplified heuristic models, which lack the capacity to integrate real-time multi-modal data (e.g., electronic health records, sensor-derived vitals, imaging metadata) or adapt to dynamic operational conditions. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework capable of simulating patient flow scenarios and predicting bottlenecks using high-dimensional datasets. The computational approach will involve training ensemble models on historical patient interaction data (demographics, diagnostic codes, time-to-service metrics) and validating them against synthetic datasets generated via agent-based modeling. HPC resources will enable parallelized hyperparameter optimization, large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to account for operational uncertainty, and real-time inference testing under varying resource constraints. Key outcomes include a deployable decision-support tool for medical assistants and clinic managers, designed to recommend optimal patient prioritization and staff assignment strategies. The project’s significance lies in its potential to reduce wait times, improve resource utilization, and mitigate clinician burnout in high-volume care environments. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with clinical workflows, this work aligns with broader efforts to enhance precision in medical operational decision-making while maintaining compliance with evolving healthcare standards. All models and simulation pipelines will be made accessible to the allied health research community to support reproducibility and scalability across care settings.
cip_title: Allied Health and Medical Assisting Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in allied health and medical assisting services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The optimization of drug therapy in veterinary medicine is challenged by the vast physiological and pathological variability across animal species, which complicates the extrapolation of pharmacological data from traditional model organisms. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive, species-specific pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) models for domesticated animals, including companion animals and livestock. A key research problem is the lack of robust computational frameworks that integrate interspecies differences in drug metabolism, tissue distribution, and disease mechanisms to guide dosing regimens. To overcome this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of clinical datasets, and molecular dynamics simulations of drug-target interactions. PBPK models will incorporate anatomical, physiological, and biochemical parameters specific to dogs, cats, horses, and cattle, calibrated using in vivo pharmacokinetic data from veterinary clinical trials. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify patterns in electronic health records to predict individual patient responses to drugs under varying conditions, such as renal impairment or obesity. Molecular dynamics simulations will elucidate structural variations in drug-binding sites across species, informing the repurposing of human pharmaceuticals for veterinary use. The integration of these methods requires HPC resources to manage large datasets, perform parallelized simulations, and optimize complex models. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for dose individualization, reduced adverse drug reaction risks, and improved therapeutic efficacy in target species. This work will advance precision veterinary medicine by establishing a computational pipeline for rational drug selection and dosing, directly addressing gaps in veterinary clinical pharmacology. The resulting models will also contribute to comparative pharmacology knowledge, with potential translational implications for human drug development.
cip_definition: Research on how to apply advanced knowledge of the chemical properties and biological effects of drugs to rational drug therapy in animal patients. Includes instruction in the comparative pharmacology of principal drug groups, pharmacokinetics, basic mechanisms and features of diseases occurring in domesticated animals, the role of drugs in modifying the disease process, and specific skills critical to the practice of clinical pharmacology.

abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and related autoimmune rheumatic diseases present complex, heterogeneous pathobiology driven by dynamic interactions between genetic, immune, and environmental factors. Current treatment strategies remain suboptimal due to variable patient responses and limited biomarkers for predicting disease progression or therapeutic efficacy. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing a computational framework integrating multi-omics data with clinical phenotypes to model disease mechanisms and predict personalized treatment outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze longitudinal genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from 1,200 RA patients across three international cohorts. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to identify predictive signatures of treatment response to biologic therapies. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate immune-stromal cell interactions in synovial tissue under varying genetic and therapeutic conditions. These computational workflows require parallel processing capabilities to manage high-dimensional datasets (>500 TB) and iterative simulations across parameter spaces. The HPC environment will enable scalable deployment of containerized pipelines for data harmonization, feature selection, and model validation while ensuring reproducibility. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for anti-TNF and JAK inhibitor responses, (2) mechanistic insights into synovial microenvironment dynamics driving treatment resistance, and (3) open-source tools for omics integration in rheumatic disease research. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs for targeted therapies and advance computational rheumatology by establishing a template for translating complex molecular data into actionable clinical decision-support frameworks. Resource allocation is critical to achieve computational scalability and meet time-sensitive milestones aligned with ongoing patient recruitment.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rheumatology

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in mammography technology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enhance diagnostic accuracy, optimize imaging protocols, and improve quality assurance (QA) processes. Despite advancements in breast cancer screening, variability in image interpretation, inconsistent QA practices, and the physical limitations of imaging systems persist. These issues contribute to false positives, false negatives, and patient discomfort during procedures. To overcome these barriers, we propose a computational research initiative combining large-scale mammographic image analysis, machine learning (ML), and physics-based simulations. The project will utilize HPC resources to process and analyze high-resolution mammograms from diverse patient populations, training deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect subtle malignancies and reduce diagnostic subjectivity. Simultaneously, Monte Carlo simulations will model X-ray photon transport through breast tissue to optimize imaging parameters (e.g., kVp, mAs) for improved lesion visibility while minimizing radiation dose. Finite element analysis will simulate breast compression mechanics to evaluate positioning protocols that balance patient comfort and image quality. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will synthesize anatomically realistic mammographic phantoms to augment training datasets and validate QA metrics. The computational demands of these tasks—including terabyte-scale image processing, iterative model training, and complex multiphysics simulations—necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallelization and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include validated ML models for lesion classification, evidence-based imaging parameter recommendations, and automated QA tools to detect equipment calibration drift. By integrating these innovations into clinical workflows and educational programs, this research aims to standardize mammography practices, reduce diagnostic variability, and improve early cancer detection rates. The project will also provide a scalable computational framework adaptable to emerging technologies, such as digital breast tomosynthesis, ensuring long-term impacts on patient outcomes and radiographer training.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered radiographers to become registered mammographers. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, mammography instrumentation, mammography positioning, principles and procedures of mammography, and quality assurance.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Burmese language studies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze and model the linguistic and literary structures of Burmese texts. Despite its rich literary tradition and unique grammatical features, Burmese remains understudied in computational linguistics due to limited digitized corpora and a lack of language-specific tools. The research problem centers on overcoming these barriers to enable large-scale textual analysis, syntactic parsing, and diachronic studies of Burmese literature, which are currently infeasible with standard computing resources. The project will compile and preprocess a diverse corpus spanning classical to modern Burmese texts, including rare manuscripts, using OCR and manual transcription. Computational methods will include the development of custom NLP pipelines for Burmese, integrating transformer-based models for syntactic and semantic analysis, and applying graph-based algorithms to map intertextual relationships in literary works. HPC resources are essential to train language models on distributed GPU clusters, process terabytes of text data, and run parallelized simulations to model language evolution across historical periods. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, annotated Burmese corpus with metadata, a suite of computational tools tailored to Burmese philology, and novel insights into stylistic shifts in Burmese literature linked to sociohistorical contexts. These resources will significantly advance research capabilities in Burmese studies, enabling quantitative literary analysis, cross-linguistic comparisons, and applications in language education or preservation. By democratizing access to scalable computational methods, this project aims to position Burmese language research within broader digital humanities discourse while preserving the linguistic heritage of Myanmar.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Burmese language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance diagnostic accuracy and workflow efficiency in medical sonography by developing advanced computational tools for real-time ultrasound image analysis. Current clinical practice relies heavily on manual interpretation of sonographic data, which is time-intensive and subject to interoperator variability, particularly when detecting subtle pathologies such as early-stage tumors or microvascular abnormalities. To address these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models capable of automating image segmentation, anomaly detection, and quantitative biomarker extraction from dynamic ultrasound datasets. The computational workflow will involve processing high-resolution 3D/4D ultrasound volumes and Doppler血流 data using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers optimized for temporal-spatial feature recognition. These models will be trained on a multi-institutional dataset of annotated cases spanning hepatic, cardiac, and obstetric applications, with federated learning techniques to maintain patient privacy. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale of this data (estimated at 250 TB), enabling rapid hyperparameter optimization, and simulating real-time inference scenarios across diverse clinical hardware. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive sonographic analysis, validated against ground-truth diagnostic findings, that reduces manual measurement errors by ≥30% in pilot trials. The project will further generate benchmark datasets for rare pathologies, addressing a gap in sonography AI research. By integrating computational advances with clinical workflows, this work aims to standardize diagnostic criteria, improve early disease detection, and provide ultrasound technicians with decision-support tools that complement their expertise—ultimately enhancing patient care quality in resource-constrained settings.
cip_title: Diagnostic Medical Sonography/ Sonographer and Ultrasound Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to utilize medical ultrasound techniques to gather sonographic data used to diagnose a variety of conditions and diseases. Includes instruction in obtaining, reviewing, and integrating patient histories and data; patient instruction and care; anatomic, physiologic and pathologic data recording; sonographic data processing; sonography equipment operation; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Somatic bodywork therapies, such as Rolfing/Structural Integration and lymphatic drainage, are increasingly utilized for managing chronic pain and stress-related disorders, yet their biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to quantify how manual interventions alter tissue dynamics, neural signaling, and systemic stress responses. Current clinical studies face limitations in capturing real-time biophysical changes during therapeutic touch, while existing biomechanical models lack the resolution to map complex interactions between fascial networks, interstitial fluid flow, and autonomic nervous system activity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to integrate finite element modeling of myofascial deformation with agent-based simulations of cellular mechanotransduction and machine learning analysis of multimodal physiological data (high-density EMG, HRV, and cytokine profiles). The computational framework will process terabyte-scale datasets from motion-captured practitioner techniques, tissue ultrasound imaging, and wearable biosensors collected across 200 clinical sessions. Key challenges include optimizing parallelized solvers for viscoelastic tissue behavior under dynamic loading conditions and training neural networks to detect patterns linking specific manual pressures/durations to biomarker signatures. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive models identifying optimal force vectors for fascial release in different anatomical regions, (2) quantitative biomarkers for assessing treatment efficacy in fibromyalgia patients, and (3) open-source tools enabling personalized therapy design based on individual tissue compliance profiles. This interdisciplinary approach bridges manual therapy traditions with computational biomechanics, offering a novel paradigm for evidence-based standardization in somatic practices while advancing fundamental knowledge about human tactile neurobiology. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations and large-scale data integration critical for translating empirical bodywork knowledge into validated computational health solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in the design and optimization of heterogeneous computing architectures for next-generation embedded systems, which face escalating demands from real-time data processing and machine learning applications. Current simulation tools struggle to model the dynamic interactions between hardware components (e.g., FPGAs, ASICs) and software workloads in multi-core environments, particularly under scalability constraints. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity, parallelized simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze hardware-software co-design strategies at unprecedented scales. The computational approach integrates cycle-accurate emulation of reconfigurable logic, memory hierarchy modeling, and workload scheduling algorithms within a modular, MPI-based architecture. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize parameter spaces for latency, power consumption, and thermal management across simulated edge-computing scenarios. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for design space exploration, while distributed memory clusters will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses of system-level trade-offs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of optimized hardware configurations for edge AI applications, a lightweight open-source simulation toolkit for embedded system designers, and novel scheduling heuristics tailored for heterogeneous architectures. This work will directly advance the development of energy-efficient, adaptive computing systems for autonomous devices and IoT networks, while providing foundational insights into the scalability of hardware-software co-optimization methods. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving statistically robust results across diverse use cases, as local computational infrastructure cannot support the required concurrency levels or memory bandwidth for billion-cycle simulations. By validating theoretical models against empirical performance limits, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for real-time embedded system design in computer engineering practice.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Palliative care research faces critical challenges in integrating complex, multimodal datasets to improve patient-centered outcomes. Current approaches often lack the computational capacity to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and patient-reported outcomes in tandem, limiting the ability to predict disease trajectories or personalize interventions. This project proposes the development of a machine learning (ML) framework to model multidimensional palliative care data, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in data integration, model training, and validation. The research will utilize de-identified EHRs from three tertiary healthcare systems (n ≈ 150,000 patients), paired with genomic biomarkers of symptom burden and longitudinal quality-of-life surveys. A hybrid neural architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing for clinical notes, convolutional networks for imaging-derived pain assessments, and survival analysis modules will be implemented to predict 6-month mortality risks, hospitalization events, and optimal care pathways. Computational workflows will leverage distributed training across GPU nodes to manage memory-intensive tasks, including federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across institutions. Validation will involve prospective clinical trials comparing model-guided palliative care referrals against standard protocols. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for temporal phenotyping of palliative care needs, risk stratification algorithms deployable in clinical settings, and evidence-based frameworks for resource allocation in hospice programs. By enabling real-time analysis of petabyte-scale datasets, this HPC-driven approach aims to reduce latency in palliative care delivery, decrease unnecessary invasive interventions, and improve alignment between patient preferences and treatment plans. The computational infrastructure will support reproducibility through containerized pipelines and benchmark datasets for future research in value-based care optimization.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in optimizing dynamic decision-making workflows for executive assistants (EAs), who operate at the intersection of complex scheduling, stakeholder coordination, and real-time information synthesis. While modern tools like calendar software and communication platforms exist, they lack predictive capabilities to manage nonlinear, high-stakes interactions common in executive support roles. The core research problem involves modeling the latent dependencies between executive priorities, stakeholder behaviors, and organizational constraints to develop adaptive workflow systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining temporal graph neural networks (TGNNs) with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). The TGNN component will process historical communication logs, meeting transcripts, and scheduling patterns to map context-sensitive decision pathways, while MARL agents simulate negotiation scenarios across competing priorities (e.g., conflicting stakeholder requests, crisis response timelines). Computational experiments will utilize anonymized datasets from partner organizations containing 5+ years of EA activity records, requiring distributed training across GPU nodes to handle irregular time-series data and sparse event matrices. Key innovations include developing attention mechanisms for cross-modal alignment of textual communications with calendar entities and implementing differential privacy safeguards during model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a probabilistic framework for anticipating scheduling conflicts and resource bottlenecks 48–72 hours in advance, (2) quantitative metrics for "strategic alignment" between EA actions and executive intent, and (3) open-source tools for ethical AI-assisted workflow prioritization. This work bridges computational social science with operational business processes, offering novel insights into human-in-the-loop automation for strategic support roles. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling the MARL environment to realistic complexity levels and achieving sub-second inference times during live prototype testing with participating EA professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and/or personal secretaries for business executives and top management. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, public relations, scheduling and travel management, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, conference and meeting recording, report preparation, office equipment and procedures, office supervisory skills, and professional standards and legal requirements.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the integration of decentralized blockchain protocols with ecological economics in accounting systems—a novel interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of accounting, sustainability, and distributed ledger technologies. Traditional accounting frameworks struggle to dynamically quantify and verify ecological externalities (e.g., carbon footprints, biodiversity impacts) in real time, particularly for complex supply chains. This project addresses this gap by designing a high-fidelity simulation environment to test hybrid blockchain architectures that automate the tracking of ecological-economic data flows while ensuring auditability, scalability, and compliance with evolving sustainability reporting standards. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate stakeholder interactions across supply networks, cryptographic validation mechanisms for multi-party data reconciliation, and machine learning to predict regulatory compliance risks under varying ecological scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the parallel processing demands of large-scale blockchain network simulations, optimize consensus algorithms for energy efficiency, and train predictive models on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., IoT sensor data, financial ledgers, ecological inventories). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating sustainable accounting systems, benchmarks for blockchain-driven ecological auditing, and scalability analyses to inform policy and corporate governance. By bridging distributed systems engineering with sustainability accounting, this work aims to advance computational methods for transparent, real-time ecological accountability in business operations—a pressing need as global regulations shift toward mandatory environmental disclosure frameworks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in accounting, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to optimize resource allocation strategies for complex, multi-stakeholder R&D programs through computational modeling of dynamic project management scenarios. A critical challenge in R&D management lies in balancing competing priorities—such as budget constraints, technical uncertainty, and interdisciplinary team coordination—while maintaining agility in rapidly evolving research environments. Traditional static allocation models often fail to account for stochastic variables like shifting project timelines, emergent risks, or variable resource yields from partnerships. To address this gap, we propose developing an adaptive decision-support framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate large-scale R&D portfolios under diverse constraints. Agent-based modeling will capture interactions between heterogeneous stakeholders (research teams, funding bodies, regulatory entities), while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes across thousands of scenario permutations. Machine learning techniques will then identify allocation patterns that maximize research output metrics while minimizing systemic risks. The computational workload requires HPC resources due to the need for simultaneous optimization of nonlinear variables across multiple temporal and organizational scales, with individual simulations involving >10^6 decision nodes. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for real-time resource reallocation in R&D programs, quantitative risk propagation models for multi-project systems, and scalability benchmarks for managing distributed innovation networks. This work will advance evidence-based practices in research administration by enabling data-driven tradeoff analyses between short-term operational efficiency and long-term strategic investment in scientific enterprises. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules and case studies demonstrating computational gains over conventional project management tools in pharmaceutical development and clean energy consortium contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in clinical laboratory diagnostics by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance the analysis of complex biomedical datasets. Clinical laboratories face increasing demands to process high-volume, multidimensional data from advanced diagnostic tools, such as next-generation sequencing, mass spectrometry, and high-resolution imaging. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the scale and complexity of these datasets, leading to delays in pathogen identification, antimicrobial resistance profiling, and biomarker discovery. This research aims to develop and optimize machine learning models and bioinformatics pipelines to accelerate and refine the interpretation of clinical data, with a focus on improving diagnostic accuracy and operational efficiency in medical laboratory settings. The computational approach will involve training deep neural networks on genomic and proteomic datasets to predict antimicrobial resistance patterns in bacterial pathogens, as well as deploying scalable clustering algorithms to classify rare hematologic anomalies from flow cytometry data. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will be integrated to model enzyme-substrate interactions in point-of-care diagnostic assays, enabling the virtual optimization of assay sensitivity. By utilizing HPC resources, these computationally intensive tasks—including large-scale parallel processing of sequencing data and GPU-accelerated model training—will be executed efficiently. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for real-time analysis of laboratory data, validated predictive models for clinical pathogen behavior, and novel computational workflows that reduce turnaround times for critical tests. This work will directly support clinical laboratory technicians in making data-driven decisions, ultimately enhancing patient care through faster, more accurate diagnostic results. The project also aims to establish a framework for integrating HPC capabilities into routine laboratory education and training, preparing future technicians to harness advanced computational resources in evolving healthcare environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists/medical technologists, to perform routine medical laboratory procedures and tests and to apply preset strategies to record and analyze data. Includes instruction in general laboratory procedures and skills; laboratory mathematics; medical computer applications; interpersonal and communications skills; and the basic principles of hematology, medical microbiology, immunohematology, immunology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis.

abstract: Pediatric musculoskeletal disorders, such as early-onset scoliosis, developmental hip dysplasia, and growth plate injuries, present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of skeletal development and the need for treatments that preserve growth potential. Current surgical and non-surgical interventions rely heavily on generalized protocols, which may not account for patient-specific biomechanical, genetic, and metabolic factors influencing outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing predictive computational models to optimize treatment personalization and improve long-term functional outcomes in pediatric orthopedic patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal clinical datasets, simulate musculoskeletal growth trajectories, and model biomechanical responses to interventions. A hybrid computational approach will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) of bone and soft tissue mechanics with machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal electronic health records, imaging data, and biomechanical sensor outputs. Key objectives include identifying biomarkers of treatment resistance in scoliosis bracing, optimizing implant design for growth-friendly spinal devices, and predicting risk of post-traumatic growth arrest in physeal fractures. HPC resources are essential to handle the high dimensionality of patient-specific data, perform real-time simulations of skeletal adaptation under varying load conditions, and iteratively refine models using Bayesian optimization frameworks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for clinical decision support, novel insights into mechanobiological drivers of pediatric skeletal development, and open-source computational templates for simulating growth-modulating interventions. This work has the potential to reduce revision surgery rates, minimize radiation exposure from repeated imaging, and establish a paradigm for data-driven precision orthopedics in pediatric populations. By aligning computational modeling with clinical workflows, the project aims to translate theoretical insights into actionable strategies for managing complex musculoskeletal disorders in children.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, surgical and non-surgical treatment, and management of musculoskeletal diseases, abnormalities and trauma in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Norwegian dialectal variation and its historical evolution, a critical gap in current Scandinavian linguistics research. Norwegian dialects exhibit exceptional diversity due to geographical, social, and historical factors, yet large-scale, data-driven studies remain limited by the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous linguistic data. The proposed research will develop and apply machine learning models to analyze multi-modal datasets, including digitized historical texts (e.g., Old Norse manuscripts, 19th-century records), contemporary spoken corpora, and dialect atlas annotations. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) techniques for morphological tagging, syntactic parsing, and phonetic feature extraction, with geospatial modeling to map dialect boundaries and their shifts over time. A key innovation involves training transformer-based models on non-standardized orthographies and oral transcripts to identify patterns in grammaticalization and lexical borrowing across regions. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale of data (≥50 TB of audio and text), parallelizing feature extraction across thousands of dialect samples, and optimizing neural architectures for low-resource language scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible Norwegian Dialect Evolution Repository, computational tools for automatic dialect classification, and quantitative insights into the impact of language policy (e.g., Nynorsk vs. Bokmål) on regional speech practices. This work will directly support endangered dialect preservation efforts and inform technology applications such as Norwegian-language speech recognition systems adaptable to diverse dialects. By bridging traditional philological methods with computational linguistics, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for data-intensive research in minority language studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Norwegian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time data integration and analysis across heterogeneous medical devices within clinical office environments, a challenge exacerbated by proprietary software architectures and variable data formats. While modern medical offices rely on interconnected devices for diagnostics, monitoring, and record-keeping, latency and interoperability limitations often delay critical decision-making. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing an adaptive middleware framework optimized via high-performance computing (HPC) to enable seamless, low-latency data synthesis from diverse sources such as imaging systems, wearable sensors, and electronic health records (EHRs). The computational approach will involve parallelized data normalization algorithms to harmonize structured and unstructured inputs, coupled with machine learning models trained on simulated clinical workflows to predict and mitigate system bottlenecks. HPC resources will be critical for both training these models on large-scale synthetic datasets (emulating multi-device environments) and for deploying containerized microservices that dynamically allocate computational workloads based on real-time demand. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in data processing latency compared to existing commercial solutions, validated through benchmarking against simulated patient care scenarios. The project will further produce open-source modules for edge-device communication protocols, designed to comply with HIPAA security standards and adaptable to legacy systems. By enhancing the speed and reliability of cross-platform data integration, this work aims to improve clinical operational efficiency, reduce software maintenance costs, and support timely diagnostic interventions in resource-constrained medical offices. Success metrics will prioritize scalability across small-to-medium practices, with iterative feedback from partner clinics guiding usability refinements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: The integration of high-performance computing (HPC) resources into dental hygiene research is critical to address the growing complexity of oral microbiome dynamics and their implications for disease prevention and treatment. Current clinical approaches in dental hygiene often rely on generalized protocols for managing conditions such as periodontal disease, dental caries, and oral-systemic health interactions. However, emerging evidence highlights the need for personalized strategies that account for patient-specific microbial communities, genetic factors, and behavioral patterns. This project proposes to leverage HPC resources to analyze large-scale genomic, metagenomic, and clinical datasets from diverse patient populations, enabling the identification of microbial biomarkers, host-microbe interactions, and risk profiles associated with oral pathologies. Computational workflows will include machine learning models to predict disease progression, agent-based simulations of biofilm formation under varying hygienic conditions, and comparative genomics to track antibiotic resistance genes in oral pathogens. By simulating the efficacy of preventive interventions—such as antimicrobial agents or probiotic treatments—across virtual patient cohorts, this research aims to optimize treatment guidelines and patient education frameworks. The outcomes will directly inform clinical training programs, enabling dental hygienists to implement data-driven, personalized care plans. Additionally, the project will generate open-access tools for visualizing microbial risk factors, empowering patients to engage proactively in their oral health. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to process multi-terabyte datasets and execute computationally intensive models within feasible timeframes. This work bridges gaps between computational biology and clinical dental hygiene, advancing preventive care paradigms while addressing health disparities through scalable, evidence-based solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean teeth and apply preventive materials, provide oral health education and treatment counseling to patients, identify oral pathologies and injuries, and manage dental hygiene practices. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, microbiology, and pathology; dental hygiene theory and techniques; cleaning equipment operation and maintenance; dental materials; radiology; patient education and counseling; office management; supervised clinical training; and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address the urgent challenge of optimizing crop resilience and productivity under climate variability by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between plant genetics, environmental stressors, and agricultural management practices. Current approaches to predicting crop performance often rely on simplified models that fail to integrate multi-scale data, such as genomic traits, soil health dynamics, and real-time climate projections. This limitation hinders the development of actionable strategies for farmers and breeders. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework that combines machine learning (ML) with mechanistic crop growth simulations to analyze terabyte-scale datasets spanning genomic sequences, historical yield records, and hyperlocal weather patterns. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of high-resolution climate models (e.g., downscaled CMIP6 data) alongside genotype-by-environment interaction studies, simulating crop responses under thousands of potential scenarios. Key tasks include training deep neural networks to identify stress-tolerant genetic markers in staple crops like wheat and maize, parameterizing process-based models for regional soil-plant-atmosphere feedbacks, and optimizing irrigation and fertilization schedules via reinforcement learning. The outcomes will provide (1) predictive tools to prioritize crop varieties for breeding programs under projected climate conditions, (2) region-specific management recommendations to reduce yield gaps, and (3) open-source software for scalable agricultural analytics. By integrating heterogeneous data streams into a unified modeling platform, this work will advance precision agriculture and directly support stakeholders in adapting to rapidly changing environmental conditions, thereby enhancing food security and sustainable production.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and practice of agricultural research and production and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of practical agricultural problems. Includes instruction in basic animal, plant, and soil science; animal husbandry and plant cultivation; soil conservation; and agricultural operations such as farming, ranching, and agricultural business.

abstract: Livestock production systems face mounting challenges in balancing efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare under dynamic environmental and market conditions. This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize feed formulation, disease resilience, and breeding strategies in cattle, leveraging multi-omics data integration and physiological simulations. Current approaches often rely on simplified linear models or phenotypic data alone, limiting their capacity to address complex gene-environment interactions or predict emergent metabolic outcomes. To overcome these barriers, we propose a computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), dynamic models of nutrient utilization, and machine learning to identify biomarkers linked to feed efficiency and methane emission traits. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process whole-genome sequencing data from 2,000 cattle, integrate longitudinal metabolomic and microbiome datasets, and train deep neural networks on high-dimensional phenotypic records. Mechanistic models of rumen fermentation and nutrient partitioning will be parameterized using differential equations solved across biologically realistic timescales, requiring parallelized simulations to test millions of variable combinations. Anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for personalized feed regimes that reduce enteric methane production by ≥15% while maintaining growth rates, (2) genomic selection markers for disease resilience validated through in silico gene network perturbation studies, and (3) open-source tools for scalable livestock data analysis. The computational workflows will directly inform experimental trials at university research farms, enabling rapid translation to production settings. By addressing critical bottlenecks in data integration and predictive modeling, this work aims to establish a decision-support framework that advances precision livestock management while mitigating environmental impacts. The requested HPC allocation will enable computationally intensive tasks—including population-scale genomic analyses, agent-based herd simulations, and Bayesian optimization of breeding indices—that are infeasible with existing campus computing infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of livestock animals and the production and handling of meat and other products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, range science, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: The safety and efficiency of in-flight emergency response protocols are critical to airline operations, yet current training methodologies often rely on static scenarios that may not fully capture the dynamic complexities of real-world emergencies. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating diverse in-flight emergency scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model passenger behavior, crew coordination, and environmental variables at scale. The research problem centers on the gap between traditional training paradigms and the stochastic, high-stakes nature of actual emergencies, where factors such as cabin layout, passenger demographics, and real-time decision-making significantly impact outcomes. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques, the proposed approach will simulate evacuation processes, turbulence-induced injuries, and emergency equipment deployment under varying conditions. HPC resources will enable the parallel execution of thousands of simulations to identify optimal crew response strategies, evaluate the effectiveness of existing protocols, and generate data-driven recommendations for procedural improvements. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for airline training programs, predictive models to assess risk probabilities in novel scenarios, and evidence-based guidelines for resource allocation during emergencies. By integrating computational rigor with operational insights, this project aims to advance the technical foundations of flight attendant training, ultimately enhancing passenger safety and operational resilience in the aviation industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the performance of a variety of personal services conducive to the safety and comfort of airline passengers during flight, including verifying tickets, explaining the use of safety equipment, providing passenger services, and responding to in-flight emergencies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural underpinnings of cognitive-communication disorders (CCD) in individuals with traumatic brain injury (TBI) using advanced computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC). CCD—characterized by deficits in attention, memory, and discourse coherence—arises from diffuse axonal injury and disrupted network connectivity, yet the dynamic interplay between structural damage, functional reorganization, and behavioral outcomes remains poorly understood. Current clinical assessments lack precision in predicting recovery trajectories, and rehabilitation strategies are often generalized rather than personalized. To address this gap, we propose integrating multimodal neuroimaging (diffusion tensor imaging, resting-state fMRI) with behavioral data from 150 TBI patients to construct patient-specific computational models of large-scale brain networks. These models will simulate neural dynamics under varying degrees of structural disruption and test hypotheses about compensatory mechanisms. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of imaging data, running parallelized simulations of whole-brain network activity using biologically informed neural mass models, and applying machine learning to identify biomarkers of CCD severity. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework linking TBI-induced structural damage to functional communication deficits, (2) predictive models of recovery patterns based on early post-injury network characteristics, and (3) prototype algorithms for optimizing non-invasive neuromodulation protocols tailored to individual network profiles. By elucidating how distributed neural systems adapt to injury, this work will advance the development of biologically grounded interventions for CCD, directly addressing the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders’ priority of integrating basic neuroscience with clinical translation. The requested computing resources will enable scaling beyond pilot studies, fostering innovation in neurorehabilitation for an understudied population with chronic communication challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution and enforcement of transnational environmental treaties, a critical yet computationally underexplored area in international law. Traditional legal scholarship often struggles to systematically evaluate the dynamic interplay between treaty language, state compliance patterns, and geopolitical variables across decades and jurisdictions. This research addresses that gap by developing a computational framework to model how subtle linguistic shifts in treaty drafting influence long-term adherence and dispute resolution outcomes. The project will process a corpus of over 10,000 multilateral environmental agreements, national implementation reports, and related case law using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for legal texts. These will be integrated with geopolitical datasets covering economic indicators, regime types, and environmental monitoring metrics. Agent-based modeling simulations will then test hypotheses about how specific treaty provisions—such as monitoring mechanisms or differentiated responsibilities—affect compliance trajectories under varying global scenarios. A machine learning pipeline will identify linguistic and structural features in treaties that correlate with successful enforcement, controlling for confounding variables like state capacity and international power dynamics. By enabling analysis at scales and complexities impractical through manual methods, this approach aims to uncover previously unrecognized patterns in treaty effectiveness while advancing computational legal studies methodologies. The outcomes will provide actionable insights for treaty drafters and international organizations seeking to design more resilient environmental governance frameworks. This work also demonstrates the transformative potential of HPC in addressing grand challenges at the intersection of law, policy, and global sustainability.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law affecting relations between nations, the behavior of international organizations, and the international activities of private citizens and organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize animal training protocols through advanced machine learning (ML) and behavioral simulation techniques. Traditional animal training methodologies often rely on generalized, trial-and-error approaches, which may not account for the nuanced variability in individual animal cognition, species-specific learning patterns, or contextual factors influencing training efficacy. The research problem centers on creating adaptive, data-driven strategies that can predict optimal training pathways for diverse animals and tasks while minimizing stress and maximizing retention. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process high-dimensional datasets—including behavioral metrics, physiological signals (e.g., heart rate, cortisol levels), and environmental variables—and to train complex ML models that simulate dynamic human-animal interactions. The computational approach integrates reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks to iteratively refine training protocols based on simulated outcomes, alongside agent-based models that emulate individual animal decision-making under varying stimuli. These models will be validated against empirical data from canine search-and-rescue training programs and equine athletic conditioning regimes. The expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to identify individualized training schedules, (2) a taxonomy of species- and task-specific learning thresholds, and (3) open-source software to assist trainers in designing evidence-based protocols. By bridging computational science and animal behavior studies, this work aims to advance the precision and welfare standards of animal training practices, with applications spanning service animal programs, conservation initiatives, and competitive sports. The scalability of these models, enabled by HPC, will also provide a foundation for future research into cross-species cognitive plasticity and ethical human-animal collaboration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach and exercise animals for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes. Includes instruction in animal psychology, health, and safety; human-animal interaction; learning and behavior styles associated with different breeds and species; and the technical and pedagogical aspects of training animals for such specific functions as obedient household pets, performing show animals, animal athletes, caregiving (e.g., seeing-eye dogs), search and rescue, and police/security work.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of hemodynamic instability during minimally invasive cardiovascular procedures, such as transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVR) or coronary angioplasties.
