Current clinical practice relies on static imaging and empirical thresholds to guide device selection and procedural planning, which often fails to account for dynamic, patient-specific biomechanical interactions. These limitations contribute to post-procedural complications, including paravalvular leaks or stent malpositioning. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating real-time fluoroscopic imaging data with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate device-tissue interactions under physiologically accurate flow conditions. The research will utilize anonymized patient datasets (CT/MRI angiograms, intraoperative pressure tracings) to construct 3D cardiovascular geometries, which will be parameterized for material properties and boundary conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across a range of physiological states (rest, exercise, arrhythmia) and device configurations, optimizing computational efficiency for near-real-time clinical applicability. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce model complexity by identifying key predictors of procedural success from simulation outputs. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for hemodynamic instability, which could inform intraoperative decision-making and pre-procedural planning tools. This work bridges gaps in cardiovascular technology by advancing patient-specific modeling beyond traditional imaging, offering a novel computational lens to refine device deployment strategies. Success would directly enhance the precision of cardiovascular technologists' workflows, reducing complication rates and improving long-term outcomes for patients undergoing structural heart interventions. The scalability of this approach could further support the development of adaptive training simulators for cardiovascular technologists, integrating biomechanical feedback into educational platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform invasive, noninvasive, and peripheral examinations of the cardiovascular system at the request of physicians to aid in diagnoses and therapeutic treatments. Includes instruction in reviewing and recording patient histories and clinical data, patient care, investigative and examination procedures, diagnostic procedures, data analysis and documentation, physician consultation, equipment operation and monitoring, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study of Japanese cultural identity as reflected in historical textual and visual materials. The research problem centers on analyzing the evolution of regional narratives and aesthetic motifs across Japan’s early modern period (1603–1868), a time of significant sociocultural transformation. Existing scholarship on this era relies heavily on manual analysis of primary sources, limiting the scale at which patterns can be identified in diverse materials such as Edo-era woodblock prints, travelogues, and regional folklore records. This project addresses this gap by employing computational methods to systematically examine relationships between textual themes, visual iconography, and geographic diffusion across a corpus of over 50,000 digitized items from institutional archives. A hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques will be implemented. Transformer-based models fine-tuned on classical Japanese texts will extract thematic clusters from travel diaries and folk tales, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will classify recurring visual elements in ukiyo-e prints and regional maps. Spatial analysis pipelines will then map these features against historical trade routes and administrative boundaries to model cultural exchange dynamics. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of high-resolution image data and large-language model inference across multilingual texts, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and scalable storage. Expected outcomes include an open-access dataset linking cultural artifacts to geotemporal metadata, a methodological framework for interdisciplinary digital humanities research, and new insights into how local identities were negotiated amid centralized governance. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across heterogeneous sources, this project aims to redefine scholarly approaches to Japanese cultural history while demonstrating the value of HPC infrastructure for area studies beyond conventional computational social science applications.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Japan, and related island groups and coastal neighbors.

abstract: Dental implantology faces significant challenges in optimizing implant design, placement protocols, and long-term biomechanical performance due to the complex interplay between implant structures, bone remodeling, and patient-specific anatomical factors. Traditional experimental approaches and low-resolution computational models are insufficient to capture the dynamic, multiscale interactions at the bone-implant interface, particularly under diverse physiological loading conditions. This project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate and analyze the biomechanical behavior of dental implants across spatial and temporal scales. Leveraging patient-specific 3D models derived from clinical CT scans, we will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to evaluate stress distribution, micromotion, and osseointegration patterns in heterogeneous bone substrates. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict optimal implant geometries, surgical trajectories, and prosthetic loading profiles based on simulated outcomes. The computational workflow will further model bone remodeling dynamics using agent-based approaches to assess long-term stability under cyclic masticatory forces. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC clusters, the project aims to generate predictive insights into failure mechanisms, soft-tissue integration, and graft resorption rates at a population scale. Anticipated outcomes include clinically validated protocols for implant placement in atrophic maxillae, data-driven design principles for porous implant surfaces, and adaptive treatment planning tools that account for biomechanical variability across demographic groups. This work will advance precision in implant dentistry by bridging computational innovation with translational clinical workflows, ultimately reducing postoperative complications and improving prosthetic longevity. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial resolution, parametric diversity, and statistical power required to address the multifactorial nature of implant success in real-world populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical bottlenecks in the design and optimization of next-generation energy storage systems, specifically solid-state batteries, through high-fidelity computational modeling. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve atomistic-scale ion transport mechanisms and interfacial degradation phenomena, which limit energy density and cycle life. To overcome these challenges, this project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) simulations. These methods will model ion diffusion dynamics across heterogeneous electrode-electrolyte interfaces under varying thermal and mechanical conditions. The simulations will utilize optimized parallelized codes (LAMMPS and Quantum ESPRESSO) to handle systems exceeding 1 million atoms, requiring multi-node GPU-accelerated architectures for feasible runtime. Concurrently, machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict stable material configurations, reducing the combinatorial search space for experimental validation. The computational workflow will integrate adaptive sampling techniques and automated job scheduling to maximize resource efficiency. Expected outcomes include atomistic insights into degradation pathways, validated descriptors for interface stability, and open-access datasets linking material properties to performance metrics. This work will directly inform the synthesis of durable solid-state battery prototypes, accelerating the transition to sustainable energy technologies. By enabling unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution of complex electrochemical processes, the project will establish a scalable computational framework applicable to other materials-intensive engineering domains, from photovoltaics to catalytic systems. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the project’s terabyte-scale data generation and iterative multiscale modeling, which exceeds the capacity of local cluster resources.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the operational complexity inherent in small-scale brewery and brewpub ecosystems, where dynamic variables such as raw material variability, energy-intensive production processes, and hyper-localized consumer preferences intersect. Traditional business optimization models often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between brewing science parameters (e.g., fermentation kinetics, ingredient quality degradation) and business-critical factors like real-time demand shifts or sustainability goals. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision framework that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including IoT sensor outputs from brewing equipment, regional sales trends, and environmental impact metrics—into a unified simulation environment. The computational approach will leverage agent-based modeling to simulate supply chain resilience under disruptions (e.g., hop shortages), coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize production scheduling amid fluctuating energy costs and carbon taxation policies. A second component will employ graph neural networks to analyze customer behavior patterns from point-of-sale and social media data, enabling predictive modeling of seasonal demand spikes and localized marketing efficacy. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU clusters, the system will generate prescriptive insights for resource allocation at temporal resolutions unachievable through conventional methods. Anticipated outcomes include a 15-20% reduction in perishable waste through just-in-time malt procurement strategies, dynamic pricing models tailored to micro-market taste preferences, and energy consumption profiles that align brewing cycles with renewable energy availability. This interdisciplinary fusion of computational biology, operations research, and consumer analytics aims to establish a replicable template for data-driven decision-making in craft beverage industries, particularly enhancing the viability of small breweries operating within tight margin constraints. The project’s open-source tools and datasets will further contribute to academic and industry understanding of sustainable, adaptive business models in agro-industrial niches.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market breweries and brewpubs. Includes instruction in brewing science, food services management, logistics and distribution, business networking, personnel management, business planning and capitalization, brewing industry operations, marketing, alcohol and liquor law and regulations, finance, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze systemic disparities in criminal case outcomes through advanced computational modeling of legal text data. The study focuses on identifying latent biases and procedural inefficiencies within criminal law by examining large-scale datasets of judicial opinions, plea agreements, sentencing memoranda, and appellate records. A core challenge lies in processing unstructured legal texts at scale to detect patterns in judicial decision-making, statutory interpretation, and the application of procedural rules across jurisdictions. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques—including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal corpora—with network analysis to map citation patterns and evolutionary trends in criminal procedure. Custom machine learning pipelines will be developed to classify case outcomes, predict procedural delays, and quantify disparities tied to demographic or jurisdictional factors. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models on terabytes of legal documents and running parallelized simulations of alternative procedural frameworks. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible framework for analyzing bias in criminal case processing, 2) evidence-based recommendations for procedural rule modifications, and 3) novel metrics for evaluating the equitable application of criminal laws. By bridging computational methods with legal theory, this work aims to establish reproducible techniques for large-scale legal analytics while addressing pressing questions about fairness and efficiency in criminal justice systems. The project demonstrates how HPC capabilities can advance sociolegal research in ways traditional doctrinal analysis cannot, offering transformative potential for both academic inquiry and policy reform.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting criminal law and trial procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an optimized framework for real-time embedded system design and validation, addressing the growing complexity of edge computing devices in industrial IoT applications. Current simulation tools struggle to model the interplay between energy efficiency, thermal constraints, and computational performance at scale, particularly when accounting for heterogeneous hardware architectures and variable network conditions. Our research will implement a hybrid computational approach combining discrete-event simulation for system-level interactions with finite element analysis for thermal-electronic modeling. The proposed high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallel execution of multi-fidelity simulations across parameter spaces encompassing processor configurations, sensor networks, and power delivery systems. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to automate design space exploration, targeting Pareto-optimal solutions that balance computational throughput with energy consumption. Expected outcomes include a modular simulation platform capable of predicting system behavior under realistic operational constraints, validated against physical prototype measurements from our lab’s embedded systems testbed. The resource allocation will directly support critical investigations into thermal-aware task scheduling algorithms and failure prediction models for edge computing hardware. This work aims to provide practical design guidelines for next-generation industrial control systems while advancing simulation methodologies in computer engineering technology. Successful implementation could reduce development cycles for energy-constrained embedded devices by 30-40% through virtual prototyping optimization, with potential applications in smart manufacturing and distributed sensor networks. The requested computing resources are essential given the combinatorial complexity of modeling multi-core embedded architectures interacting with 100+ node sensor arrays, requiring sustained parallel processing capabilities beyond our current institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to enhance the protection of cultural and archaeological resources by analyzing patterns of illicit activity and environmental degradation. Despite advances in remote sensing and site monitoring, heritage protection agencies lack robust computational tools to proactively identify at-risk sites or optimize resource allocation for surveillance and intervention. The project addresses this gap by integrating geospatial, socio-economic, and historical crime data into a machine learning pipeline to forecast threats such as looting, vandalism, and unauthorized construction. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning satellite imagery, regional archaeological inventories, and law enforcement records, which vary widely in resolution, format, and temporal scope. Computational methods will include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for automated detection of site disturbances in time-series satellite imagery, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model illicit artifact trafficking networks, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between environmental factors and human behaviors. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps for ABM calibration, real-time fusion of heterogeneous data streams, and ensemble forecasting under multiple climate change and policing scenarios. Expected outcomes include a risk-assessment toolkit that prioritizes sites for patrols or conservation funding, validated against case studies from partnering heritage agencies in high-risk regions. By bridging computational criminology, heritage science, and environmental modeling, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven cultural resource protection while advancing methodologies for sparse, irregular datasets common in non-STEM fieldwork. Results will be disseminated through an open-access web platform optimized for use by non-technical stakeholders in law enforcement and cultural preservation.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement principles and techniques to the protection of cultural resources and the investigation of related crimes. Includes instruction in cultural resources law, archaeological standards of value, site damage assessment, evidence collection, surveillance techniques, investigative techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) and co-occurring psychiatric conditions present a complex interplay of genetic, neurobiological, environmental, and behavioral factors that challenge existing treatment frameworks. Current approaches often fail to account for the heterogeneity of these interactions, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multidimensional datasets spanning neuroimaging, genomic profiles, electronic health records (EHRs), and real-time behavioral data. The research aims to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response, classify patient subtypes, and simulate the dynamic effects of psychosocial and pharmacological interventions. A key focus is the development of machine learning models to analyze functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data from individuals with opioid use disorder and comorbid depression, integrating these with polygenic risk scores and longitudinal relapse patterns. Computational pipelines will employ federated learning techniques to preserve privacy while harmonizing data across six clinical sites. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate how socioenvironmental factors—such as access to care and social networks—interact with neurocognitive vulnerabilities to influence recovery trajectories. The scale of these analyses, involving >10 TB of multimodal data and millions of stochastic simulations, necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing, large-scale parameter optimization, and real-time analytics. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for personalizing SUD treatment based on individual neurogenetic and contextual profiles, (2) mechanistic insights into relapse pathways in dual-diagnosis populations, and (3) open-source tools for simulating policy interventions targeting treatment disparities. By elucidating the systems-level architecture of addiction and comorbidity, this work will inform clinical guidelines and advance precision psychiatry approaches for high-risk populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation and treatment of individuals with alcohol, drug, or other substance-related disorders, and of individuals with the dual diagnosis of substance-related and other psychiatric disorders.

abstract: The increasing complexity of public health challenges, such as emerging infectious diseases and health disparities, demands advanced computational tools to model dynamic systems and inform intervention strategies. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate disease transmission and evaluate the efficacy of public health policies under diverse demographic and socioeconomic conditions. A critical barrier to progress is the computational expense of scaling ABMs to realistic population sizes while incorporating granular data on mobility patterns, healthcare access, and social determinants of health. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize simulations across thousands of agents and optimize parameter space exploration using machine learning techniques. The computational workflow will integrate anonymized electronic health records, census data, and geospatial mobility traces to construct synthetic populations representative of urban and rural regions in the study area. Sensitivity analyses will assess how variations in contact rates, vaccine hesitancy, and resource allocation influence outbreak trajectories. By deploying GPU-accelerated deep learning models, we aim to reduce runtime for scenario testing by over 70% compared to traditional CPU-based approaches. Anticipated outcomes include actionable insights into optimal resource deployment during epidemics, validated against historical COVID-19 response data. This work will produce an open-source computational toolkit for public health agencies, enabling rapid, data-driven decision-making in future crises. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieving the necessary scale and fidelity for these simulations, which cannot feasibly run on local institutional clusters due to memory and node limitations. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and partnerships with regional health departments, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance translational research in underserved communities.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public health, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in bioethics research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, large-scale datasets related to clinical decision-making, health equity, and ethical dilemmas in emerging medical technologies. Current studies in bioethics often rely on qualitative or small-sample analyses, limiting their ability to model systemic biases, forecast long-term societal impacts, or evaluate trade-offs in resource allocation under diverse ethical frameworks. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ computational modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and multi-agent simulations to examine patterns in clinical ethics consultations, public health policy outcomes, and patient autonomy conflicts documented in electronic health records, institutional reports, and global bioethics repositories. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including unstructured text from clinical narratives and policy documents, as well as the simulation of population-level ethical scenarios (e.g., triage protocols during resource scarcity, AI-driven diagnostics in culturally diverse contexts). Machine learning models will be trained to identify latent biases in historical ethics committee decisions, while discrete-event simulations will test the resilience of proposed ethical guidelines under demographic and epidemiological shifts. Expected outcomes include the development of open-access predictive tools to support ethics review boards, evidence-based frameworks for equitable AI deployment in healthcare, and scalable models for assessing the justice implications of genetic editing technologies. By integrating computational rigor with normative analysis, this work aims to advance translational bioethics, providing stakeholders with empirically grounded strategies to navigate moral complexity in rapidly evolving medical landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: Veterinary radiology faces unique challenges in optimizing diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy due to the anatomical and physiological diversity of animal species, coupled with the limited availability of species-specific imaging protocols. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing computational frameworks to automate the analysis of radiologic data and simulate radiation therapies tailored to heterogeneous anatomies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models on multi-modal imaging datasets (CT, MRI, and radiography) from diverse companion and livestock animals, enabling the identification of disease biomarkers and anatomical variations that influence diagnostic interpretation. Concurrently, Monte Carlo simulations will model radiation dose distributions for targeted radionuclide therapies, incorporating species-specific tissue attenuation properties and dynamic physiological parameters. These simulations will inform treatment planning systems to minimize off-target radiation exposure while ensuring therapeutic efficacy. The computational workflows will require parallel processing to manage large-scale image datasets (>100,000 annotated studies) and iterative, high-fidelity physics simulations. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for automated lesion detection in veterinary imaging, validated dosimetry models for novel radiotherapeutic agents, and a computational pipeline adaptable to rare or underrepresented species. By integrating machine learning and physics-based modeling, this project aims to bridge gaps in veterinary radiologic research, directly improving clinical decision-making and treatment outcomes. The HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the necessary scale, speed, and precision for these analyses, which cannot be feasibly conducted on local computing systems due to memory constraints and processing times. Results will be disseminated through veterinary radiologic societies and collaborative platforms to accelerate innovation in this specialized clinical domain.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radiologic imaging and therapies to diagnose and treat animal diseases and health problems. May included related research in the use and handling of equipment for radionuclides detection and application.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and performance of energy-efficient building systems through high-performance computing (HPC). Urbanization and climate change demand structures that minimize environmental impact while maintaining resilience, but current design workflows struggle to balance complex, interdependent variables such as thermal efficiency, structural integrity, and airflow dynamics. Traditional simulations often oversimplify multi-physics interactions or are computationally prohibitive, limiting innovation in sustainable architectural solutions. To address this, we propose an HPC-driven approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model building systems at unprecedented resolution and scale. High-fidelity simulations will capture coupled heat transfer, mechanical stress, and ventilation dynamics across diverse urban microclimates, while ML algorithms iteratively optimize material selection, geometric configurations, and passive energy strategies. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of large parametric datasets and real-time visualization of 3D structural-thermal models, facilitating rapid design iteration. Key outcomes include validated predictive models for energy consumption and load-bearing capacity, a generative design toolkit for architects and engineers, and actionable guidelines for retrofitting existing buildings. By resolving computational bottlenecks, this work will advance the integration of performance-driven design into architectural practice, directly supporting decarbonization goals and adaptive reuse of urban infrastructure. The requested resources will also train students in HPC applications for architectural engineering, bridging technical skills gaps in the emerging sustainable construction sector. This project aligns with national priorities for smart cities and positions architectural engineering as a critical field for scalable climate resilience solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: Medical imaging generates complex, high-dimensional datasets that challenge conventional computing resources, particularly in large-scale radiology research. Current limitations in processing speed, algorithmic scalability, and data integration hinder the development of advanced tools for quantitative image analysis, which are critical for improving diagnostic accuracy, prognostic modeling, and personalized therapeutic strategies. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these barriers by enabling the deployment of deep learning architectures and multi-modal image fusion techniques tailored to radiological data. The research will focus on optimizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models for automated segmentation of pathological features in volumetric MRI and CT datasets, which require intensive GPU memory and parallelized processing. Additionally, we will develop computational pipelines to integrate imaging data with clinical metadata using distributed storage systems and containerized workflows, ensuring scalability and reproducibility. Key challenges include managing terabyte-scale datasets across heterogeneous modalities, reducing training times for 3D neural networks, and implementing federated learning frameworks to enable multi-institutional collaboration while preserving data privacy. The anticipated outcomes include validated models for early detection of neurodegenerative diseases and tumor progression, open-source tools for efficient radiomic feature extraction, and a scalable infrastructure for real-time image analysis in clinical research. By addressing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to accelerate the translation of imaging biomarkers into practice, ultimately enhancing precision diagnostics and expanding the role of artificial intelligence in radiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Radiology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Danish philology and literature, addressing critical gaps in large-scale analysis of linguistic evolution and literary patterns. While Danish language studies have traditionally relied on manual textual analysis, the increasing availability of digitized historical texts, contemporary corpora, and dialect recordings presents an opportunity—and a challenge—to systematically analyze linguistic change, dialectal variation, and literary trends at scale. Current limitations in processing power restrict the scope of such studies, particularly for tasks requiring parallelized text processing, complex statistical modeling, or machine learning applications. This project proposes a multi-phase computational approach. First, a diachronic corpus spanning 16th-century texts to modern digital communications will be constructed, integrating OCR-cleaned manuscripts, annotated literature, and dialectal audio transcripts. NLP pipelines will be developed to handle historical orthography and dialectal features, employing transformer-based models for tasks like lemmatization, syntactic parsing, and semantic role labeling. Second, phylogenetic methods adapted from computational biology will be applied to model dialect evolution, requiring Bayesian inference frameworks optimized for HPC architectures. For literary analysis, graph neural networks will map character interactions and thematic networks across canonical Danish novels, while transformer models fine-tuned on genre-specific corpora will trace stylistic shifts. The computational demands of training these models on heterogeneous data, coupled with the need for rapid iteration across hyperparameters, necessitate dedicated HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative atlas of Danish dialect convergence, an open-access computational toolkit for Danish philology, and new models linking literary style to sociohistorical context. These resources will empower researchers to test long-standing hypotheses about language standardization and literary innovation while providing infrastructure for future studies. By bridging computational methods and Danish studies, this project aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven humanities research in under-resourced languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Danish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Soil health and fertility are critical determinants of agricultural productivity, yet the complex interactions between soil physicochemical properties, microbial communities, and crop performance remain poorly quantified. This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of soil-microbial-plant systems by integrating high-resolution biogeochemical data with spatially explicit agent-based simulations. The primary research challenge lies in scaling mechanistic models of nutrient cycling (e.g., nitrogen, phosphorus) and microbial metabolic processes from microscale soil aggregates to field-level heterogeneity, which requires resolving nonlinear feedbacks across orders of magnitude in spatial and temporal scales. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid modeling framework combining lattice Boltzmann methods for pore-scale water-nutrient transport, individual-based microbial community simulations, and machine learning surrogates for crop root exudate dynamics. This approach will utilize existing soil metagenomic datasets from Midwest agricultural systems (5 TB) and generate new 3D soil structure scans via X-ray microtomography. The computational workflow will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations across parameter spaces representing diverse management practices (tillage, cover cropping) and climate scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated open-source model capable of predicting soil carbon sequestration potential under varying agricultural interventions, (2) quantitative maps of microbial functional redundancy linked to crop resilience, and (3) optimization protocols for fertilizer application timing informed by real-time sensor data assimilation. By elucidating how microscale soil processes propagate to macroscale agroecosystem functions, this work will provide critical decision-support tools for enhancing sustainable intensification of food production systems. The scale of parameter sweeps (>10^6 core-hours) and memory demands of 4D soil moisture-nutrient coupling (>128 GB/node) necessitate dedicated HPC allocations beyond typical campus cluster capacities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the soil sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address challenges in developing adaptive assistive technologies for individuals with physical disabilities by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current approaches often lack the computational power to model complex interactions between biomechanical systems, neural control mechanisms, and patient-specific factors, leading to suboptimal device personalization and rehabilitation outcomes. The research will employ multiscale computational models integrating real-time motion capture data, electromyographic (EMG) signals, and clinical assessments to simulate and predict individual responses to prosthetic and therapeutic interventions. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed on HPC clusters to optimize control parameters for assistive devices, enabling dynamic adaptation to user behavior and environmental conditions. Additionally, large-scale simulations will investigate the biomechanical and neuromuscular effects of various rehabilitation protocols across diverse patient populations. The computational demands of processing high-dimensional datasets, training predictive models with millions of parameters, and running parallelized simulations necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for personalized device calibration, data-driven guidelines for intervention timing and intensity, and open-source tools for rehabilitation science. This work aims to advance the precision and efficacy of therapeutic technologies while establishing computational methodologies that bridge gaps between clinical practice and theoretical models in rehabilitation research. By addressing both technical and translational challenges, the project has the potential to significantly improve functional independence and quality of life for individuals with disabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with people who have learning disabilities, mental illness, and physical disabilities in a clinical, educational, or institutional setting. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, assistive technology, case management, counseling techniques, cultural diversity, disability assessment and measurement, ethics, psychological and physiological aspects of disability, rehabilitation services, rehabilitation science, and vocational counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and physiological mechanisms underlying Asian Bodywork Therapy (ABT), an understudied domain within integrative health sciences. ABT modalities, such as acupressure, Shiatsu, and Tui na, are hypothesized to influence tissue remodeling, neural signaling, and systemic homeostasis through controlled manual stimuli. However, the multiscale interactions between therapeutic force application, cellular responses, and clinical outcomes remain poorly quantified due to limitations in modeling complex biological systems. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing computational frameworks that integrate tissue biomechanics, mechanotransduction pathways, and patient-specific variability. A multi-modal approach will be employed, combining finite element modeling of soft tissue deformation under ABT techniques with agent-based simulations of cellular responses to mechanical stimuli. Machine learning algorithms will analyze high-resolution clinical datasets (including pressure-mapped treatment sessions and pre/post-therapy biomarker profiles) to identify predictive patterns linking technique parameters to therapeutic outcomes. The computational pipeline will require HPC capabilities for large-scale parameter optimization, real-time simulation of nonlinear tissue dynamics, and ensemble modeling of heterogeneous population data. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for ABT protocol optimization, mechanistic insights into dose-response relationships in manual therapies, and predictive models of treatment efficacy across diverse patient phenotypes. By elucidating the systems-level effects of ABT, this work aims to establish an evidence-based foundation for personalized treatment planning while advancing computational methodologies for studying manual therapies. The project’s interdisciplinary nature—synthesizing traditional medicine principles with computational biology and AI-driven analytics—represents a novel contribution to health sciences, with potential applications in rehabilitation science, neuromodulation research, and precision wellness initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being based on Chinese medical principles through one or more of the traditional bodywork therapies of Asia. Includes instruction in acupressure, AMMA(r) Therapy, Chi Nei Tsang, Five Element Shiatsu, Integrative Eclectic Shiatsu, Japanese Shiatsu, Jin Shin Do(r) Bodymind Acupressure(tm), Macrobiotic Shiatsu, Anma Therapy, Thai massage, Tui na, Zen Shiatsu, Qigong, Okazaki(r) Restorative Massage, principles of Western and Chinese medicine, patient counseling and observation, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling complex decision-making processes in educational leadership and policy implementation using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Educational organizations operate within dynamic, interconnected systems where policy outcomes depend on nonlinear interactions between stakeholders, institutional structures, and external constraints. Traditional analytical frameworks often oversimplify these interdependencies, limiting their utility for predicting the efficacy of leadership strategies or policy interventions. To overcome this, we propose a computational study integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), network analysis, and machine learning to simulate organizational behavior and policy diffusion within educational systems. The research will utilize large-scale administrative datasets, including longitudinal records of district-level decision-making, policy adoption timelines, and workforce dynamics, to parameterize models that capture the adaptive behaviors of leaders, educators, and governing bodies. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of simulating millions of agent interactions across diverse policy scenarios, as well as to train predictive models that identify leverage points for sustainable organizational change. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for testing hypothetical policy interventions, metrics to quantify resilience in educational leadership structures, and actionable insights into optimizing resource allocation during systemic transitions such as funding reforms or demographic shifts. By bridging computational social science with education leadership theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for organizational development and policy design, directly supporting the program’s focus on adaptive leadership in complex educational environments.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Organizational Leadership and Policy Development with an emphasis on education. Includes instruction on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, education administration and supervision, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate the cascading impacts of emerging technologies on national security decision-making processes, with a focus on adaptive statecraft in contested environments. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of traditional analytical tools to account for the dynamic interplay between rapidly evolving technologies (e.g., AI-driven disinformation, quantum computing vulnerabilities, autonomous systems proliferation) and the cognitive, institutional, and geopolitical factors shaping policy responses. Using National Security Policy Studies as an anchor, we propose an agent-based modeling approach that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including historical policy archives, real-time threat indicators, and technology adoption forecasts—to simulate decision pathways under conditions of radical uncertainty. High-performance computing resources are required to manage large-scale parameter space exploration, optimize multi-agent reinforcement learning architectures, and process classified/non-classified document corpora through natural language processing pipelines. The computational model will feature modular components representing state/non-state actors, technology diffusion networks, and feedback loops between strategic perception and capability development. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation environment for stress-testing policy assumptions, identifying critical leverage points in technology governance, and generating probabilistic forecasts of systemic risks arising from human-technological co-evolution. This work bridges computational social science with strategic studies, offering novel methodologies to analyze how adaptive policy frameworks might mitigate emergent threats while maintaining ethical and legal constraints. The resource request supports parallelized simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, enabling policymakers to explore second- and third-order effects of technological disruption at scales impractical for conventional analytical methods.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and application of intelligence, diplomacy, military power, and related tools of statecraft to national defense policy formulation and power projection. Includes instruction in history, political theory, public policy analysis, civil-military relations, military and defense studies, homeland security, leadership, threat scenarios, regional and local issues, alliance and coalition issues, defense budgeting and economics, intelligence, and strategy.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex sociocultural and logistical dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in diverse urban contexts. While church planting is traditionally guided by theological frameworks, its practical implementation intersects with spatial demographics, migration patterns, community network formation, and intercultural communication—areas underexplored in computational humanities. The primary research problem centers on identifying scalable, data-driven models to optimize site selection, resource allocation, and contextual adaptation strategies for new congregations, particularly in hyper-diverse cities experiencing rapid demographic shifts. Using anonymized global census data, geospatial analytics, and ethnographic records from 15 transnational church planting networks, the project will apply agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate community engagement outcomes under varying theological, ethical, and operational parameters. Machine learning algorithms will further classify historical success/failure patterns across 500+ documented cases, correlating theological approaches with sociodemographic variables. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution geotemporal datasets, managing stochastic elements in ABM simulations, and integrating qualitative ethnographic data into quantitative predictive frameworks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support toolkit for religious organizations, prioritizing ethical considerations in algorithmic recommendations. The project advances interdisciplinary humanities scholarship by formalizing computational methodologies for missiological studies while addressing gaps in how emerging technologies engage with faith-based community development. Results will be disseminated through open-access repositories and a peer-reviewed paper analyzing the epistemic tensions between computational modeling and theological agency in mission contexts. This work underscores the role of HPC in bridging applied humanities research with complex real-world challenges in pluralistic societies.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: Understanding the transport and fate of contaminants in heterogeneous aquifers is critical for safeguarding groundwater resources, yet existing models struggle to resolve complex subsurface interactions across scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, three-dimensional reactive transport model to simulate contaminant migration in fractured sedimentary aquifers impacted by legacy industrial pollution. The computational framework will integrate hydrogeological data (e.g., borehole logs, hydraulic conductivity measurements), geochemical reaction networks, and stochastic fracture network representations to capture coupled flow, solute transport, and biogeochemical processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the multiscale nature of the problem: parallelized finite element simulations will resolve meter-to-kilometer spatial heterogeneity, while machine learning algorithms will optimize parameterization using field-derived tracer datasets. The model will be validated against contaminant concentration profiles and isotopic signatures from a contaminated site in the Great Lakes Basin. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of dominant mechanisms controlling heavy metal mobility under varying redox conditions, (2) probabilistic forecasts of plume evolution under climate-driven hydrological changes, and (3) an open-source computational workflow adaptable to other sedimentary basins. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and scalable memory architectures, this work will achieve unprecedented spatial resolution for reactive transport models in complex geological media, reducing uncertainties in remediation planning. The requested resources will support ensemble simulations (>10⁴ core-hours) to quantify parameter sensitivity and scenario-based risks. Results will directly inform groundwater management strategies for post-industrial regions while advancing computational geosciences through the integration of mechanistic modeling and data assimilation techniques.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ancient biodiversity patterns and extinction dynamics across major geologic intervals. A critical challenge in paleontology lies in resolving the complex interplay of biotic and abiotic factors that shaped evolutionary trajectories in deep time, particularly during mass extinctions and recovery phases. Current limitations stem from the computational intensity required to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as fossil occurrence records, geochemical proxies, and sedimentary basin models—at high spatial and temporal resolutions. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining agent-based ecosystem simulations, Bayesian hierarchical models, and machine learning-driven image analysis of fossil morphology. The agent-based models will reconstruct paleocommunity interactions under variable climatic and tectonic scenarios, while Bayesian methods will quantify uncertainties in stratigraphic age correlations and extinction rates. Concurrently, convolutional neural networks will automate the analysis of microfossil imagery from digitized thin sections, enabling rapid taxonomic identification and trait quantification. These parallel workflows will be iteratively refined using paleoclimate simulations run on HPC clusters, which are essential for resolving feedbacks between carbon cycle perturbations, ocean-atmosphere chemistry, and biotic turnover. Expected outcomes include novel constraints on the drivers of the Permian-Triassic and Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction events, as well as scalable tools for synthesizing paleontological and geologic data. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work will provide a quantitative foundation for testing macroevolutionary hypotheses and contextualizing modern biodiversity loss within deep-time perspectives. The computational pipelines developed will be shared openly to support broader paleontological research, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration across geosciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of extinct life forms and associated fossil remains, and the reconstruction and analysis of ancient life forms, ecosystems, and geologic processes. Includes instruction in sedimentation and fossilization processes, fossil chemistry, evolutionary biology, paleoecology, paleoclimatology, trace fossils, micropaleontology, invertebrate paleontology, vertebrate paleontology, paleobotany, field research methods, and laboratory research and conservation methods.

abstract: Dental materials play a critical role in restorative and prosthetic treatments, yet their long-term performance and biocompatibility remain limited by gaps in understanding atomic-scale interactions, stress distribution under dynamic oral conditions, and degradation mechanisms. This project seeks to advance the development of next-generation dental composites and ceramics by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model material behavior across multiple scales. The research will address two core challenges: (1) predicting interfacial failure between resin-based composites and dentin due to hydrolytic degradation and cyclic mechanical loading, and (2) optimizing the nanostructure of zirconia ceramics to balance fracture toughness with wear resistance. Molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to characterize water diffusion dynamics and bond dissociation energies at adhesive-dentin interfaces, while finite element analysis will model stress concentrations in multi-layered prosthetic systems under mastication forces. Machine learning workflows will accelerate the exploration of dopant configurations in yttria-stabilized zirconia to identify compositions that resist low-temperature degradation without compromising optical properties. These computational approaches require large-scale parallel processing to manage systems containing >1 million atoms, iterative mechanical loading simulations across 10^5 cycles, and high-throughput screening of 500+ hypothetical material variants. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for material selection in clinical scenarios, validated protocols for accelerating aging tests, and candidate formulations for bioactive composites with enhanced interfacial stability. By elucidating failure mechanisms invisible to experimental observation alone, this work will directly inform the design of durable, biocompatible materials, reducing the need for invasive retreatment procedures. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in local computing infrastructure, enabling the complex multi-physics simulations required to bridge atomic-scale interactions with clinically relevant performance metrics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize industrial operations under dynamic constraints, addressing critical challenges in production efficiency, resource allocation, and environmental sustainability. Industrial systems are characterized by complex interdependencies among supply chain logistics, production scheduling, energy consumption, and quality control, further complicated by uncertainties such as fluctuating demand, equipment failures, and regulatory changes. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture these multidimensional, stochastic interactions at scale. To overcome these limitations, the research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach integrating agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. The computational model will simulate large-scale industrial networks, incorporating real-time data streams from IoT sensors, historical production logs, and market forecasts. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning and neural networks, will be employed to adaptively refine decision policies for scenarios such as just-in-time inventory management, predictive maintenance scheduling, and low-carbon production routing. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the parallel processing demands of millions of agent interactions, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and iterative optimization across heterogeneous objectives (e.g., cost minimization, waste reduction, workforce safety). Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of generating Pareto-optimal operational strategies under conflicting constraints, validated through case studies in automotive manufacturing and chemical processing industries. By bridging engineering principles with advanced computational analytics, this work aims to advance industrial management practices, enabling data-driven resilience in volatile markets while aligning with sustainability goals. The resulting open-source framework will provide a benchmark for integrating HPC into operational research, with potential applications in smart manufacturing and circular economy initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of engineering principles to the planning and operational management of industrial and manufacturing operations, and prepares individuals to plan and manage such operations. Includes instruction in accounting, engineering economy, financial management, industrial and human resources management, industrial psychology, management information systems, mathematical modeling and optimization, quality control, operations research, safety and health issues, and environmental program management.

abstract: Rural populations face significant health disparities, including limited access to healthcare resources and higher burdens of chronic and infectious diseases. These disparities are compounded by geographic isolation, socioeconomic factors, and heterogeneous population distributions, which complicate the design of effective public health interventions. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing computational models to predict disease spread, optimize resource allocation, and evaluate intervention strategies tailored to rural settings. A critical barrier to progress is the lack of scalable, high-resolution models capable of integrating sparse, multi-source health data with geographic, demographic, and environmental variables. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based simulations, machine learning pipelines, and geospatial analyses. The agent-based framework will simulate disease transmission dynamics across synthetic rural populations, incorporating mobility patterns, healthcare access thresholds, and social determinants of health. Machine learning models will be trained on regional electronic health records, census data, and environmental sensor datasets to identify risk clusters and forecast outbreak trajectories. Geospatial tools will map healthcare deserts and model the impact of mobile clinics or telemedicine expansion. These computational workflows require parallel processing capabilities to manage large parameter spaces, stochastic simulations, and real-time data integration. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into cost-effective intervention strategies for rural regions, validated models for policymakers, and open-source tools to support adaptive public health planning. The project’s computational demands—including multi-terabyte datasets, millions of parallelized simulations, and iterative model calibration—necessitate HPC infrastructure for storage, processing speed, and scalability. By bridging clinical research with computational innovation, this work aims to reduce rural health inequities and establish a framework for data-driven decision-making in resource-limited settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rural Health

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance protocols for industrial machinery and mechanical systems, addressing the critical challenge of unplanned downtime in manufacturing and transportation sectors. Traditional maintenance strategies often rely on static schedules or reactive measures, leading to inefficient resource use, costly operational interruptions, and premature equipment failures. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a multi-physics modeling approach integrated with machine learning (ML) to simulate wear, fatigue, and failure modes in mechanical components under diverse operational conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, which will capture complex interactions between thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamic stresses in real-world systems. These simulations will generate datasets to train ML models that predict component degradation rates and optimal intervention windows. The computational workflow will also incorporate real-time sensor data from case studies involving hydraulic systems, gearboxes, and combustion engines to validate model accuracy. By leveraging parallel processing capabilities, the project aims to reduce simulation runtime by 60–70% compared to conventional computing infrastructure, enabling rapid iteration of scenarios such as variable load cycles and environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for dynamically adjusting maintenance schedules, minimizing downtime, and extending equipment lifespans. The results will provide actionable insights for technicians and engineers, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical repair workflows. This work will advance the integration of computational methodologies into vocational training programs, fostering data-driven decision-making in maintenance professions. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the development of open-source simulation modules and benchmark datasets, contributing to the broader adoption of predictive analytics in technology and technical fields.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of tools, equipment, and machines.

abstract: Aquaculture systems face critical challenges in optimizing feed efficiency and environmental conditions to enhance growth rates while minimizing ecological impacts. Current empirical approaches for feed formulation and hydrodynamic management are resource-intensive, lack generalizability across species and systems, and fail to account for dynamic interactions between biological, chemical, and physical factors. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating hydrodynamic modeling, nutrient transport simulation, and machine learning to predict optimal feeding strategies and tank configurations for intensive fish farming. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 3D simulations of water flow patterns, dissolved oxygen distribution, and waste accumulation under varying stocking densities and feeding regimes. Coupled agent-based models will track individual fish growth metrics based on localized environmental conditions and feed availability. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulation outputs to identify nonlinear relationships between operational parameters (e.g., feed composition, aeration rates, stocking density) and production outcomes. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from recirculating aquaculture systems raising tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), with sensor measurements tracking real-time water quality and fish biometrics. Successful implementation will yield predictive models that reduce feed waste by an estimated 15-20% while maintaining growth targets, directly addressing economic and sustainability barriers in commercial aquaculture. The scalable framework will be adaptable to other finfish species and production systems, providing a template for data-driven decision-making in aquatic livestock management. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle complex multiphysics interactions and large parameter spaces, this research aims to establish computational tools that advance precision aquaculture practices without expanding natural resource extraction.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, culture, propagate, harvest, and market domesticated fish, shellfish, and marine plants, both freshwater and saltwater. Includes instruction in the basic principles of aquatic and marine biology; health and nutrition of aquatic and marine life; design and operation of fish farms, breeding facilities, culture beds, and related enterprises; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biological systems demands advanced computational tools to model multi-scale interactions and predict emergent behaviors. This project seeks to address the challenge of simulating spatially resolved, dynamic host-microbiome-environment networks, which remain poorly understood due to the combinatorial explosion of variables and nonlinear feedback mechanisms. Current methods lack the resolution to integrate heterogeneous data types—including metagenomic, metabolomic, and environmental flux data—while maintaining temporal granularity. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with Bayesian network inference, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The ABM component will simulate individual microbial and host cell behaviors at micrometer resolution, while the Bayesian network will probabilistically integrate omics-scale datasets to parameterize system-wide interactions. Scalability will be achieved through MPI-parallelized simulations, with adaptive mesh refinement to focus computational resources on high-gradient regions of the spatial domain. We will leverage GPU acceleration for parameter optimization via stochastic gradient descent, targeting a 50-fold reduction in runtime compared to existing CPU-bound implementations. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental datasets from synthetic microbial communities, with iterative refinement of force fields and interaction rules. Successful implementation will enable predictive modeling of community resilience to environmental perturbations, offering insights into dysbiosis mechanisms and candidate intervention strategies. This work will produce an open-source software package optimized for HPC clusters, filling a critical gap in tools for multi-omics integration in complex biological systems. Resource allocation requests include 200,000 CPU-core hours, 10,000 GPU-hours, and 50 TB of temporary storage to accommodate high-frequency checkpointing during large-scale parameter sweeps. Outcomes will advance computational methodologies at the intersection of dynamical systems theory and biological network analysis, with applications in ecological resilience and synthetic community design.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_title: Biomathematics, Bioinformatics, and Computational Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biomathematics, bioinformatics, and computational biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of neurodevelopmental trajectories in children with early-onset psychiatric disorders. A critical challenge in clinical child psychology is identifying reliable biomarkers and behavioral patterns that predict long-term outcomes for conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), early-onset anxiety, and disruptive mood dysregulation disorder. Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture the dynamic, multidimensional interactions between genetic, neuroimaging, and longitudinal behavioral data. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models integrating high-dimensional datasets, including functional MRI (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data from a longitudinal cohort of 800 children aged 6–12. Computational demands are substantial, as models will process terabytes of neuroimaging data while training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to detect temporal patterns in behavioral time-series data. HPC resources will enable parallelized preprocessing of neuroimaging pipelines using tools like FSL and FreeSurfer, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale hyperparameter optimization to improve predictive accuracy. The project will also employ explainable AI techniques to identify clinically interpretable features driving risk stratification. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for identifying children at highest risk of chronic symptom trajectories, (2) a scalable computational framework for multimodal data integration in developmental psychopathology research, and (3) open-source tools to help clinicians prioritize personalized interventions. By combining developmental theory with advanced computational methods, this work aims to bridge the gap between research and practice in clinical child psychology, offering actionable insights for early intervention while adhering to ethical standards for predictive analytics in pediatric populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the developmental processes of children and associated disorders and that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical child psychology. Includes instruction in developmental neuropsychology, child psychopathology, testing of children and adolescents, pediatric psychology, psychosocial variables in child development, clinical skills, family therapy, behavioral assessment and intervention, clinical skills, consultation, professional standards and ethics, and applications to topics such as infancy, childhood, and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced simulation frameworks for optimizing next-generation integrated circuit (IC) designs under the constraints of emerging semiconductor technologies. As transistor geometries shrink below 5 nm, conventional design methodologies face challenges in predicting quantum tunneling effects, thermal dissipation, and process variation impacts, leading to suboptimal performance and reliability. Current open-source electronic design automation (EDA) tools lack the scalability and precision required for these nanoscale regimes, necessitating high-fidelity computational models. The research will employ physics-based TCAD (Technology Computer-Aided Design) simulations coupled with machine learning surrogates to analyze device behavior across process corners, operating temperatures, and layout-dependent stress effects. A central focus involves parallelizing finite-element meshing workflows and Monte Carlo variability analyses across high-performance computing (HPC) nodes to reduce simulation turnaround times from weeks to days. The computational workflow will integrate open-source device simulators (e.g., GDSII-to-TCAD pipelines) with custom Python-based optimization routines targeting power-performance-area-reliability (PPAR) tradeoffs. Anticipated outcomes include validated compact models for 3 nm FinFET and nanosheet transistor architectures, which will be disseminated as parameterized design rule check (DRC) templates for academic and industry collaborators. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale design space exploration (>10^6 parameter combinations) to derive robust analog/mixed-signal circuit topologies resilient to manufacturing uncertainties. By bridging the gap between semiconductor physics and system-level IC design, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of advanced nodes in low-power IoT and edge-AI applications while reducing reliance on proprietary EDA toolchains. Results will directly inform curriculum updates in the institution’s IC design courses, providing students with hands-on experience in cutting-edge design-for-manufacturing (DFM) techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to design circuits in microelectronics. Includes instruction in circuit design, circuit layout, circuit analysis, computer-aided drafting, and semi-conductor technologies.

abstract: Urban stormwater management systems are increasingly challenged by climate change-induced precipitation variability, leading to amplified risks of combined sewer overflows (CSOs) and contaminant mobilization in receiving waters. Current design standards, reliant on historical rainfall patterns, inadequately address the non-stationarity of hydrologic regimes, resulting in compromised water quality and public health hazards. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to optimize adaptive stormwater infrastructure under uncertain climate futures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will couple hydrodynamic models (EPA SWMM, HEC-RAS 2D) with contaminant transport algorithms to simulate fine-scale spatiotemporal dynamics of runoff, sediment-bound pollutants, and pathogen dispersal across urban watersheds. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate models using real-time sensor data from municipal networks and identify cost-effective green-gray infrastructure configurations under ensemble climate projections (CMIP6). Computational demands arise from the need to execute millions of scenario iterations across decadal horizons at meter-scale spatial resolution, requiring parallelized processing of large geospatial datasets and multi-objective optimization workflows. Anticipated outcomes include (1) risk-informed thresholds for infrastructure retrofitting in flood-vulnerable communities, (2) predictive tools for evaluating pathogen exposure hotspots during extreme wet weather events, and (3) open-source decision support frameworks enabling municipalities to prioritize interventions balancing hydraulic capacity, ecological preservation, and environmental justice considerations. The HPC resources will enable previously intractable analyses of distributed stormwater systems as complex adaptive systems, directly advancing the program’s mission to develop engineering solutions for pollution control and protective living environments amidst climatic uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of non-textual symbolic communication in decentralized digital communities, focusing on the emergence and evolution of visual-iconographic systems within niche online platforms. As digital spaces increasingly prioritize multimodal interaction, communities are developing complex visual languages—such as emoji sequences, custom avatars, and procedural generative art—that transcend conventional linguistic frameworks.
