This work directly supports the program’s focus on bridging healthcare and social services by providing computational methods to quantify the impact of community-led advocacy and counseling initiatives. The requested resources will enable iterative model calibration using real-world data from a partnered network of 27 community health organizations, ensuring translational relevance for improving mental health access in linguistically diverse populations.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as facilitators, advocates, and referral professionals linking health care and related social services with affected recipient communities. Includes instruction in public and community health, human and social services, health services administration, group counseling, health education, group advocacy, cross-cultural and multilingual communication, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in scalable, evidence-based methods for training pre-service computer science (CS) educators to effectively teach computational thinking in diverse K-12 classrooms. While demand for CS education grows, teacher preparation programs often lack tools to model dynamic classroom interactions, simulate student learning trajectories, or evaluate the efficacy of pedagogical interventions under varied conditions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate CS classroom environments, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources for large-scale parallelization. The research will leverage existing datasets from classroom observations and standardized assessments to parameterize student and teacher agents with behavioral and cognitive attributes reflective of real-world populations. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about how specific instructional strategies (e.g., unplugged activities, debugging scaffolds) interact with student prior knowledge, engagement patterns, and problem-solving heuristics. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize intervention parameters across simulated demographic and resource-constrained scenarios. The project’s computational demands stem from 1) Monte Carlo simulations spanning thousands of unique classroom configurations, 2) real-time adaptation of agent policies via reinforcement learning, and 3) sensitivity analyses to identify robust teaching practices. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for CS teacher educators, evidence-based guidelines for personalizing pedagogy in heterogeneous classrooms, and predictive models linking instructional choices to longitudinal skill development. By enabling data-driven refinement of teacher training protocols at unprecedented scale, this work aims to directly enhance the quality and adaptability of computer education delivery in schools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach computer education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in transpersonal and spiritual psychology, specifically investigating how contemplative practices and altered states of consciousness influence therapeutic outcomes in counseling. A core challenge in this field is the multidimensional analysis of subjective experiences—such as meditation-induced shifts in self-perception, psychosomatic responses during healing rituals, or neural correlates of therapeutic trance—which generate complex datasets spanning biometric, qualitative, and behavioral domains. Current methodologies lack the capacity to integrate these heterogeneous data streams at scale, limiting insights into the mechanisms underlying spiritually informed counseling interventions. The proposed research will employ machine learning models to identify latent patterns in multimodal datasets, including electroencephalography (EEG) recordings of meditative states, motion-capture data from expressive movement therapies, and natural language processing (NLP) of client narratives describing transcendent experiences. Agent-based modeling will simulate group counseling dynamics to explore how shared spiritual frameworks enhance emotional resilience. Computational power is critical for processing high-resolution neurophysiological data in real time during ritual practices and for training deep learning architectures on ethically sourced, culturally diverse case studies. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific contemplative techniques to measurable psychological outcomes, validated models of consciousness states relevant to transpersonal counseling, and open-source tools for clinicians to personalize spiritually integrated therapies. By bridging advanced computation with transpersonal paradigms, this work aims to establish empirical foundations for non-ordinary states of consciousness in therapeutic contexts while maintaining rigorous respect for the phenomenological depth of spiritual experience. The results will directly inform curriculum development in spiritual psychology programs and provide scalable methods for evaluating the efficacy of emerging mind-body-spirit interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to pursue spiritual and psychological practices for counseling. Includes instruction in emotional intelligence, expressive movement, healing practices and rituals, human consciousness, movement and meditation, psychosomatic connection, spiritual systems and wellness, transpersonal counseling, and therapeutic trance.

abstract: Adult and continuing education (ACE) institutions face persistent challenges in optimizing program delivery, including dynamic enrollment patterns, heterogeneous learner needs, and constrained operational budgets. Current administrative decision-making often relies on retrospective analyses or generalized heuristics, limiting responsiveness to rapidly evolving demands. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model ACE program ecosystems and simulate resource allocation strategies under variable constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling to represent interactions between administrators, instructors, adult learners, and community stakeholders across multiple temporal and spatial scales. The computational architecture will integrate institutional datasets (enrollment records, course completion rates, staffing patterns) with geospatial community needs assessments and demographic projections. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent patterns in program efficacy metrics, while Monte Carlo simulations will test the robustness of allocation strategies against stochastic variables such as funding fluctuations and workforce availability shifts. A key innovation involves network analysis of cross-institutional collaboration pathways to quantify resource-sharing efficiencies. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for three core tasks: 1) large-scale parameter space exploration for optimization algorithms, 2) real-time simulation of intervention scenarios during stakeholder workshops, and 3) ensemble forecasting of long-term program sustainability. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that enables ACE administrators to evaluate trade-offs in personnel deployment, facility utilization, and program portfolio management. This work will advance computational applications in education leadership by establishing quantitative frameworks for adaptive administration, directly addressing the tension between static institutional structures and the fluid nature of adult learning demands. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the multivariate complexity of ACE systems, enabling simulations at fidelity levels impractical on conventional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of administering programs and facilities designed to serve the basic education needs of undereducated adults, or the continuing education needs of adults seeking further or specialized instruction, and that prepares individuals to serve as administrators of such programs. Includes instruction in adult education principles, program and facilities planning, personnel management, community and client relations, budgeting and administration, professional standards, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive instructional tools for students with specific learning disabilities (SLDs), such as dyslexia, dyscalculia, and dysgraphia. Current educational technologies often lack the computational capacity to dynamically model the heterogeneous learning profiles of students with SLDs, limiting their ability to personalize interventions in real time. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations by creating machine learning frameworks that can process multimodal educational data—including behavioral, cognitive, and performance metrics—to predict optimal instructional strategies for individual learners. The computational approach involves training ensemble models on large-scale datasets of student interactions, diagnostic assessments, and longitudinal outcomes. These datasets will integrate anonymized records from partner school districts, augmented by synthetically generated data simulating diverse SLD profiles. HPC resources are critical for executing parallelized hyperparameter optimization, validating models via cross-district generalization tests, and running agent-based simulations of classroom scenarios to stress-test intervention efficacy. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for mapping SLD subtypes to evidence-based teaching strategies, (2) open-source tools for generating individualized learning plans with embedded progress-monitoring algorithms, and (3) a simulation environment to train educators in deploying adaptive technologies. The project’s significance lies in its potential to scale data-driven personalization in special education—a field traditionally reliant on manual, resource-intensive methods—while maintaining alignment with legal and pedagogical standards for SLD instruction. By coupling HPC-enabled analytics with teacher input, this work aims to bridge gaps between special education research, computational innovation, and classroom practice, ultimately fostering more equitable access to tailored learning supports.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Specific Learning Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with specific learning disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with specific learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with specific learning disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex challenges in Talmudic Studies, a field requiring advanced analysis of multilayered legal, ethical, and philosophical texts. The research problem centers on the computational modeling of Talmudic hermeneutics—specifically, the systematic reconstruction of legal reasoning across dispersed textual loci. Traditional methods of manual comparison struggle to map the interplay of dialectical arguments, cross-references, and historical commentaries spanning centuries. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning (ML) to identify patterns in argumentation, trace conceptual dependencies, and quantify shifts in interpretive methodologies. Key tasks include training custom transformer models on digitized Talmudic texts (e.g., Mishnah, Gemara, and major commentaries) to recognize legal syllogisms and ethical axioms, followed by graph-based network analyses to visualize how specific jurisprudential principles evolve across time and cultural contexts. A parallel focus involves processing high-resolution scans of rare manuscripts to detect marginal annotations and textual variants using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), enabling large-scale comparative studies of scribal traditions. These computational workflows demand significant GPU-accelerated processing for training deep learning models and handling terabytes of unstructured text and image data. The expected outcomes include (1) an open-access digital corpus of annotated Talmudic arguments linked to their philosophical and legal underpinnings, (2) quantitative frameworks for assessing the influence of sociohistorical factors on rabbinic discourse, and (3) novel tools for scholars to simulate hypothetical legal scenarios based on reconstructed hermeneutic principles. By integrating computational rigor with traditional Talmudic scholarship, this project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in religious studies while preserving the intellectual dynamism of rabbinic thought for contemporary ethical and jurisprudential challenges.
cip_definition: A program focused on intense study of the Talmud that fosters values, critical thinking, and scholarship skills; prepares students for entry into a broad spectrum of graduate and professional schools; and prepares students for entry into a variety of careers including the Rabbinate. Includes instruction in Jewish law, Jewish jurisprudence, ethics, philosophy, and related disciplines.

abstract: Reproductive health in animals is critical for sustainable agriculture, species conservation, and translational insights into human medicine. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying reproductive pathologies—including placental insufficiency, fetal growth restriction, and perinatal mortality—remain poorly characterized due to the complexity of gestational systems and multifactorial disease etiologies. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics) from livestock species with clinical phenotypes to identify predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets for reproductive disorders. A central challenge is the computational demand of analyzing high-dimensional datasets spanning millions of genetic variants, time-series gene expression profiles from maternal-fetal tissues, and high-resolution imaging of placental vasculature. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources for three core tasks: (1) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to pinpoint genetic variants linked to preterm birth and dystocia; (2) dynamic Bayesian network modeling to reconstruct gene regulatory pathways driving placental development; and (3) deep learning-based segmentation of 3D ultrasound datasets to quantify fetal-maternal hemodynamic interactions. These analyses require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, stochastic simulations of molecular networks, and training of convolutional neural networks with millions of parameters—tasks infeasible on local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved genetic loci associated with gestational resilience, predictive models for early diagnosis of subclinical endometritis in dairy cattle, and open-source tools for automated fetal monitoring. By elucidating mechanisms of reproductive success and failure across species, this work will directly inform clinical interventions to improve neonatal survival rates, optimize breeding programs, and advance comparative studies of maternal-fetal health. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the statistical power and temporal resolution required for translational impact in theriogenology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of diseases and health problems affecting the reproductive systems of animals, and the comprehensive care and treatment of parent animals, animal fetuses and newborn or newly hatched animals throughout the gestation period.

abstract: The apparel and textile industry faces mounting pressure to reconcile rapid production demands with sustainable practices, particularly in resource-intensive dyeing processes that account for 20% of global wastewater. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing low-impact dyeing systems through high-performance simulations of molecular dye-fiber interactions and process parameter analysis. Current trial-and-error approaches to reducing water and chemical use lack precision in predicting outcomes across diverse textile substrates and dye chemistries, leading to suboptimal environmental and economic tradeoffs. We propose a hybrid methodology integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of dye adsorption kinetics with machine learning (ML)-driven predictive modeling of industrial-scale dye bath parameters. The MD component will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to simulate cellulose-protein-polymer interfacial behaviors across 50+ natural/synthetic fiber types, while ML models trained on spectral data and process variables will identify energy-minimized dyeing conditions. Initial benchmarks indicate that simulating a single fiber-dye system at nanoscale resolution requires 8,000+ core-hours due to the need for replica exchange molecular dynamics across temperature and pH gradients. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from pilot-scale dye baths measuring color fastness, water consumption, and effluent toxicity. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of optimized dyeing profiles for common textile blends and a decision-support tool that reduces water use by 30-45% compared to conventional methods. By establishing quantitative relationships between molecular interactions and macroscopic process efficiency, this research aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices while maintaining technical feasibility for small-to-medium enterprises.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and production of textile products and related processes and systems. Includes instruction in functional and aesthetic design, human factors research, production planning, manufacturing processes, quality assessment, and distribution systems.

abstract: Healthcare environments significantly influence patient outcomes, staff efficiency, and operational costs, yet the design of these spaces often relies on generalized guidelines rather than evidence-based, hyper-localized insights. This project addresses the critical gap in understanding how dynamic, real-time interactions between environmental variables (e.g., spatial layout, airflow, lighting, noise) and human behaviors (e.g., patient movement, care workflows) impact healing outcomes. Traditional architectural simulations lack the computational power to model these multidimensional, nonlinear relationships at scale. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated simulation framework combining agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to optimize healthcare environment design. Agent-based models will simulate patient and staff movement patterns, while CFD will analyze environmental factors such as airborne pathogen dispersion and thermal comfort. ML algorithms will iteratively refine design parameters by correlating simulated environments with real-world health outcome data from electronic medical records (EMRs) and sensor networks. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing large-scale spatial datasets, running parallelized simulations across diverse design scenarios, and training predictive models with high-dimensional inputs. Expected outcomes include actionable design principles for reducing hospital-acquired infections, minimizing patient stress through sensory-aware layouts, and improving care team efficiency. This work will establish a computational foundation for data-driven healthcare architecture, enabling rapid prototyping of adaptive environments tailored to evolving clinical needs. By bridging architecture, healthcare, and computational science, the project advances a novel paradigm for evidence-based design that prioritizes human health at the intersection of built and biological systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing persuasive communication strategies in digital public relations and advertising campaigns. The rapid evolution of digital platforms has created vast, dynamic datasets that traditional analytical tools struggle to process efficiently. Current methods for analyzing audience engagement, sentiment, and message diffusion across social media, search engines, and multimedia channels are limited in scalability, hindering the ability to model real-time campaign performance or predict emergent trends. This research addresses this gap by employing computational methods to analyze multi-modal communication data—including text, image, and video content—at unprecedented speed and scale. The project will develop machine learning models to identify patterns in audience behavior, simulate message dissemination networks, and test the efficacy of personalized advertising content. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment analysis, graph-based algorithms to map influencer networks, and reinforcement learning to iteratively refine campaign strategies. HPC resources are critical for training large-scale neural networks, processing terabytes of unstructured data, and running parallelized simulations of communication scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time adaptive messaging, predictive tools for audience segmentation, and evidence-based insights into how cultural, linguistic, and contextual factors shape persuasive communication in digital environments. Results will directly inform best practices for PR and advertising professionals while advancing theoretical understanding of computational persuasion. By enabling the analysis of cross-platform communication ecosystems at scale, this work bridges the gap between applied communication research and data-driven strategy development, offering transformative potential for both academic inquiry and industry practice.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on organizational communication, public relations, and advertising; and that prepares individuals to function in a wide range of public and private sector positions requiring the skills of persuasive communication. Includes instruction in communications, public relations, and advertising theory; principles and techniques of persuasion; message/image design; marketing strategy; professional writing; public speaking and multi-media presentation skills; digital communications; and applied research.

abstract: The study of Japanese dialects presents significant challenges due to their phonological, morphological, and syntactic diversity, compounded by the scarcity of comprehensive computational resources tailored to regional linguistic variations. Traditional approaches often rely on manual analysis, limiting scalability and depth. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to conduct large-scale comparative analyses of Japanese dialects, utilizing both historical texts and contemporary speech corpora. The research will develop computational models to map phonetic, lexical, and grammatical features across dialects, employing machine learning techniques such as neural networks and clustering algorithms. These models will process audio recordings digitized from archival sources and modern datasets, integrating speech recognition adapted for dialectal specificity. Additionally, phylogenetic methods will be applied to reconstruct historical relationships between dialects, providing insights into their evolution. The use of HPC is critical for handling the extensive data volumes and complex computations required for parallel processing of multimodal linguistic data. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialect features, visualization tools for linguistic divergence, and predictive models of language change. This research will enhance understanding of Japan’s linguistic heritage, support preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and inform developments in natural language processing technologies tailored to regional Japanese variations. By bridging traditional philological methods with advanced computational techniques, the project aims to establish a new paradigm in the study of Japanese linguistics, with implications for educational resources, sociolinguistic policy, and cross-cultural communication technologies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Japanese language. Includes instruction in philology; Ancient, Medieval, and Modern Japanese; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation within Canadian Indigenous and immigrant communities through large-scale textual and visual data. Focusing on understudied pre-federation and 20th-century archival materials—including digitized oral histories, multilingual newspapers, and community artwork—the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how intersecting cultural, ethnic, and gender identities have been negotiated in Canada’s pluralistic landscape. Traditional humanities methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these multimodal datasets, which span over 10 terabytes and include unstructured text in English, French, and Indigenous languages, as well as high-resolution image scans. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for historical dialects, computer vision techniques for pattern recognition in visual artifacts, and network analysis to map cross-community influences. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle non-Latin scripts and low-resource languages, while privacy-preserving federated learning protocols will ensure ethical handling of sensitive Indigenous materials. By parallelizing workflows across GPU nodes, the project aims to identify longitudinal trends in cultural self-representation, trace the diffusion of narrative motifs across demographic groups, and quantify shifts in gendered symbolism post-1960s multiculturalism policies. Expected outcomes include the first longitudinal dataset of Canadian intercultural discourse dynamics, open-source tools for heritage language NLP, and visualizations of identity negotiation processes at unprecedented temporal and spatial resolutions. These results will directly inform curricula in Canadian cultural studies and provide evidence-based frameworks for contemporary policy discussions on cultural preservation and inclusive nation-building. The scale of data processing—requiring weeks of sustained computation for transformer model training and hyperparameter optimization—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve research objectives within feasible timelines.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Canada and its Pre-Columbian, colonial, and pre-federation predecessors, including immigrant flows and related borderlands and island groups.

abstract: The increasing complexity of urban environments demands innovative approaches to environmental design that integrate dynamic socio-spatial patterns, ecological resilience, and human behavioral data. Traditional design methodologies often rely on static models or simplified simulations, limiting their capacity to address interconnected challenges such as climate adaptability, resource efficiency, and community well-being in real-world contexts. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate multi-scalar interactions between built environments, human activity, and environmental systems using high-performance computing (HPC). Leveraging agent-based modeling, real-time sensor data assimilation, and generative adversarial networks (GANs), the research will analyze how micro-scale design interventions—such as green infrastructure placement or material selection—propagate effects across urban networks over time. The computational workflow will integrate geospatial datasets, climate projections, and anonymized mobility patterns to generate adaptive design scenarios that optimize for carbon neutrality, thermal comfort, and spatial equity. By parallelizing parametric design exploration across HPC clusters, the project aims to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution urban models with 10^6+ interacting agents and fine-grained environmental variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dynamic spatial analysis, validated against case studies in three climate-vulnerable cities, and a novel metrics framework quantifying design impacts on systemic resilience. This work bridges gaps between architectural practice, computational social science, and urban ecology, offering scalable methods to inform policy and participatory design processes in an era of rapid environmental change. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations and enabling iterative machine learning training cycles that traditional workstations cannot support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design public and private spaces, indoor and outdoor, for leisure, recreational, commercial, and living purposes, and for professional practice as environmental designers and architects. Includes instruction in the design and planning of public and private open spaces and their relationship to buildings and other aspects of the built environment; facilities management; related aspects of interior design and architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to advance bicycle mechanics and repair technology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical challenges in the design, durability, and maintenance of human-powered vehicles. While empirical methods dominate current repair practices, the increasing complexity of modern bicycle systems—such as lightweight composite frames, adaptive gear mechanisms, and aerodynamic components—demands a computational approach to optimize performance and longevity. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive models for stress distribution, material fatigue, and dynamic load responses in bicycle components under real-world conditions, which limits the development of data-driven repair protocols and preventive maintenance strategies. To address this, the project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model mechanical and aerodynamic stresses across bicycle frames, drivetrains, and wheel assemblies. These simulations will integrate multi-physics datasets, including material properties, environmental factors, and usage patterns, to predict failure points and optimize component geometries. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to analyze large-scale sensor data from instrumented bicycles, identifying correlations between riding conditions and wear rates. The computational workflows will require HPC resources to manage the high-resolution meshing, iterative solvers, and parallel processing needed for accurate, large-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for component failure, validated repair guidelines for emerging materials (e.g., carbon fiber, titanium alloys), and open-access tools to assist technicians in diagnosing complex mechanical issues. By bridging computational engineering with practical repair techniques, this research aims to elevate industry standards, reduce maintenance costs, and enhance the safety and efficiency of human-powered transportation systems.
cip_title: Bicycle Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain bicycles and other human-powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication, adjustments of moving parts, and wheel building.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to analyze the impacts of climate variability and policy interventions on agricultural resource allocation and productivity across heterogeneous regions. A critical challenge in agricultural economics is modeling spatially explicit decision-making under uncertainty, particularly as climate change exacerbates risks for producers and complicates policy design. Current approaches often rely on aggregated data or simplified assumptions, limiting their capacity to capture localized interactions between environmental conditions, market dynamics, and farmer behavior. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale agent-based model (ABM) integrated with econometric estimation techniques, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate decision processes across millions of individual agents and diverse geographies. The ABM will incorporate historical climate data, crop yield projections, and real-world policy scenarios (e.g., subsidy structures, carbon pricing) to evaluate how resource allocation efficiency and regional resilience evolve under stochastic shocks. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations and machine learning-based parameter optimization to account for uncertainty in climate forecasts and market responses. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for training neural networks on high-dimensional agricultural survey datasets and CPU clusters for large-scale equilibrium simulations. Expected outcomes include policy-relevant insights into the cost-effectiveness of adaptive interventions, such as crop insurance schemes or precision agriculture incentives, across differing agroecological zones. By enabling granular analysis of nonlinear system behaviors, this work aims to advance methodological tools for agricultural economics while directly informing strategies to enhance sustainability and equity in resource use. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of iteratively solving dynamic stochastic models at fine spatial resolutions, a task infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics to the analysis of resource allocation, productivity, investment, and trends in the agricultural sector, both domestically and internationally. Includes instruction in economics and related subfields as well as applicable agricultural fields.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation and decision-making processes in secondary school administration through advanced computational modeling. School principals must balance complex variables—such as budget constraints, staff distribution, facility usage, student demographics, and safety protocols—to create equitable and effective learning environments. Traditional manual or spreadsheet-based approaches often fail to account for dynamic interactions between these variables, leading to suboptimal resource distribution and reactive (rather than proactive) policy adjustments. This research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model school administration scenarios, integrating real-world data on student enrollment, staff workloads, budget allocations, and facility capacities. Agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of administrative decisions on outcomes such as student achievement gaps, staff retention, and emergency response efficiency. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical datasets to identify patterns in resource utilization and predict the downstream effects of policy changes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these simulations across diverse school contexts (urban, rural, high-need) and running iterative optimizations under varying constraints. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., budget cuts vs. extracurricular programming) and generates actionable recommendations for equitable resource distribution. This tool will undergo validation through partnerships with three school districts, comparing model outputs to observed administrative outcomes. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform school leadership practices by embedding computational rigor into strategic planning, enabling principals to anticipate challenges, allocate resources with evidence-based precision, and uphold ethical standards of educational equity. Results will be disseminated through a cloud-based platform accessible to school administrators, alongside training modules for integrating computational analytics into leadership workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the junior high, secondary, or senior high school (7-12) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of secondary schools. Includes instruction in secondary school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing catalytic reaction systems for sustainable chemical manufacturing by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial catalytic processes, particularly those involving complex multi-phase reactors or non-ideal fluid dynamics, often suffer from inefficiencies due to incomplete understanding of coupled transport phenomena, reaction kinetics, and surface interactions at scale. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in resolving spatiotemporal heterogeneities, while existing computational models struggle to integrate atomistic catalyst behavior with reactor-scale fluid dynamics. This project aims to develop a multi-scale computational framework combining quantum mechanical calculations of active sites, molecular dynamics simulations of interfacial processes, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of reactor hydrodynamics. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of density functional theory (DFT) calculations to screen catalyst candidates, coupled with GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods for turbulent reactive flow simulations. Key objectives include identifying optimal operating conditions for CO₂ hydrogenation reactors, elucidating pore-scale mass transfer limitations in hierarchical zeolite catalysts, and predicting long-term catalyst deactivation patterns. Expected outcomes include validated open-source simulation tools for hybrid continuum-microkinetic modeling and actionable insights into designing energy-efficient catalytic systems. The computational demands—including O(10⁵) core-hours for ensemble uncertainty quantification and petascale data management for 4D reactor simulations—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation. Successful implementation will advance fundamental knowledge of reactive transport in complex media while directly supporting decarbonization efforts in chemical production. This work aligns with national priorities in sustainable manufacturing and provides a template for integrating machine learning with multi-physics simulations in chemical engineering research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of integrating large-scale clinical and patient-generated data into evidence-based nursing practice to improve care delivery and patient outcomes. Despite the growing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), wearable device metrics, and population health datasets, nurses often lack the computational tools and infrastructure required to analyze these complex, multidimensional datasets efficiently. This limits the ability to derive actionable insights for real-time clinical decision-making and the implementation of tailored interventions. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model patient care trajectories, predict adverse health events, and simulate the impact of nursing-led interventions in diverse clinical scenarios. The project will utilize machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in EHR data from 50,000+ de-identified patient records, focusing on risk factors for hospital-acquired infections and preventable readmissions in acute care settings. Agent-based modeling will then simulate the effects of evidence-based nursing protocols—such as tailored discharge planning or dynamic staffing adjustments—on patient outcomes and healthcare costs. These computational approaches require HPC resources due to the scale of data, the need for parallel processing to optimize model training, and the complexity of simulating multi-agent healthcare environments. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive tools to prioritize high-risk patients, actionable frameworks for scaling nurse-driven innovations, and open-access computational models to guide practice changes. By enabling rapid analysis of heterogeneous datasets and virtual testing of interventions, this work will empower nursing leaders to implement data-driven strategies that enhance care quality, reduce disparities, and align with evolving healthcare system demands. The project directly supports the program’s focus on translating research into practice by providing a computational foundation for evidence-based innovation in nursing.
cip_definition: A practice-focused program that prepares registered nurses for increasingly complex evidence-based nursing practice, including translating research into practice, evaluating evidence, applying research in decision-making, and implementing viable clinical innovations to change practice. Includes instruction in healthcare delivery systems, health economics and finance, health policy, research methods, translating evidence into practice, concepts in population health, and nursing leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for modeling the dynamic interplay between urban microclimate systems and airborne pollutant dispersion in complex, heterogeneous environments. Traditional models often decouple atmospheric processes, built infrastructure, and human activity, leading to gaps in predicting hyperlocal air quality risks under climate variability. Our interdisciplinary approach integrates computational fluid dynamics (CFD), agent-based modeling (ABM), and real-time sensor data assimilation to resolve multiscale interactions—from turbulent airflow around buildings to population mobility patterns—that drive pollution exposure disparities. The research addresses a critical gap in urban sustainability science, where existing tools lack the resolution and coupling necessary to inform equitable climate adaptation policies. The computational workflow employs GPU-accelerated large-eddy simulations (LES) to resolve microclimate turbulence at meter-scale resolution, coupled with parallelized ABMs simulating pedestrian movement and indoor-outdoor pollutant exchange. Machine learning surrogates will reduce the cost of parametric sweeps across urban morphologies and emission scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of identifying high-risk zones in real cities and testing mitigation strategies, such as green infrastructure placement or traffic rerouting. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to simultaneously resolve fine-grained physical processes and city-scale patterns over multi-day cycles, requiring scalable memory and parallel efficiency. Results will provide actionable insights for urban planners and public health agencies, bridging environmental engineering, social science, and climate resilience. This work underscores the role of HPC in tackling emergent, spatially nested challenges where traditional disciplinary boundaries limit solution-oriented innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of scientific computing and its application. Includes instruction in scientific visualization, multi-scale analysis, grid generation, data analysis, applied mathematics, numerical algorithms, high performance parallel computing, and numerical modeling and simulation with applications in science, engineering and other disciplines in which computation plays an integral role.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance formal and computational approaches to long-standing problems in philosophical logic. The research focuses on automating the analysis of complex logical systems, particularly non-classical logics (e.g., modal, intuitionistic, and paraconsistent logics), to evaluate their consistency, expressive power, and applicability to interdisciplinary problems. A central challenge is the combinatorial explosion inherent in modeling higher-order reasoning processes, especially when integrating multiple logical frameworks or scaling proofs to systems with recursive or infinitary rules. Traditional computational methods struggle with these tasks due to memory and processing constraints, necessitating distributed computing architectures. The project will develop parallelized algorithms to simulate proof-search strategies across heterogeneous logical systems, implement automated model-checking for large-scale semantic structures, and optimize theorem-proving heuristics using machine learning techniques. Key computational tools include custom SAT solvers adapted for non-classical logics, distributed graph databases for representing proof networks, and GPU-accelerated simulations of possible-worlds semantics. Outcomes will include (1) a publicly accessible repository of verified formal proofs for understudied logical systems, (2) benchmarks quantifying the resource requirements of automated reasoning in decidable and semi-decidable fragments, and (3) novel methods for detecting meta-logical properties (e.g., compactness, interpolation) in large axiomatic systems. This work will directly support philosophical research on the limits of formal systems, the epistemology of mathematical reasoning, and the interplay between logic and empirical sciences. By providing scalable tools for analyzing logical complexity, the project bridges gaps between theoretical philosophy and computational science, offering resources applicable to AI safety research, formal verification, and foundations of mathematics. The requested HPC allocation will enable simulations exceeding 10^8 inference steps, concurrent testing of 50+ logical configurations, and real-time collaboration across philosophy, computer science, and mathematics research teams.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of valid inference, argument, and sound reasoning. Includes instruction in Classical logic, properties of argument, validity, proof, fallacies, formal and material logic, symbolic and mathematical logic, analysis, specific schools of logic, and applications to problems in other academic disciplines and professional fields.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Armenian linguistics, focusing on the analysis of diachronic language variation and the structural evolution of Armenian dialects. The primary research problem lies in the fragmented digital infrastructure for Armenian language studies, particularly for historical and dialectal texts, which limits large-scale quantitative analysis. Current scholarship relies heavily on manual methods, restricting the scope of inquiry into phonological, morphological, and syntactic shifts across centuries of literary production and oral traditions. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to process, annotate, and analyze digitized corpora spanning Classical Armenian (Grabar), Middle Armenian, and modern Eastern/Western dialects. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for automated morphological segmentation, syntactic parsing of non-standardized orthographies, and dialect classification using ensemble methods. The scale of data—encompassing over 10,000 digitized texts from medieval manuscripts to contemporary sources—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized processing, distributed storage, and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive computational atlas of Armenian dialectal features, a publicly accessible NLP pipeline tailored for historical Armenian texts, and quantitative insights into contact-induced changes between Armenian and neighboring languages. This work will enhance philological research by enabling data-driven hypotheses about language change, while providing interdisciplinary methodologies applicable to under-resourced languages. By bridging computational linguistics and Armenian studies, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for preserving linguistic heritage and expanding access to non-dominant literary traditions.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by Armenians. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Brewing science faces significant challenges in optimizing fermentation processes, which are central to product consistency, flavor profile development, and operational efficiency. Traditional experimental approaches to strain selection, metabolic pathway analysis, and process parameter tuning are time-intensive and limited in their ability to resolve the complex interplay of microbial dynamics, biochemical reactions, and environmental variables. This project proposes a computational framework to model and simulate yeast metabolism and microbial interactions during fermentation at an unprecedented resolution. Leveraging genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and non-Saccharomyces species, we will integrate multi-omics data (transcriptomics, metabolomics) with dynamic fluid dynamics simulations to predict metabolic fluxes, substrate utilization, and byproduct formation under varying brewing conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational load of these multi-scale simulations, which involve solving systems of differential equations across spatial and temporal scales, from intracellular enzyme kinetics to vessel-scale nutrient gradients. Machine learning techniques will further refine parameter optimization, enabling rapid iteration of strain engineering targets and process variables. Expected outcomes include identifying yeast strain combinations and fermentation protocols that minimize off-flavor compounds, enhance ethanol yield, and improve temperature resilience. This work will advance precision brewing methodologies, reduce production waste, and provide a transferable computational toolkit for microbial community management in fermentation-dependent industries. By bridging systems biology with brewing technology, the project aligns with the agricultural sciences' mandate to innovate food production systems while addressing industry demands for scalability and sustainability.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of beer brewing operations. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, malting, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the precision and efficiency of forensic pathology workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in integrating multi-modal autopsy data and automating complex analyses. Traditional methods for determining cause of death, reconstructing trauma patterns, and correlating pathological findings with legal evidence remain labor-intensive and prone to subjective interpretation, particularly when handling large-scale datasets from post-mortem imaging, toxicology, genomics, and crime scene documentation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning, probabilistic modeling, and multi-physics simulations. Deep learning architectures, such as 3D convolutional neural networks, will be trained on anonymized post-mortem CT and MRI datasets to automate the detection of subtle injuries, hemorrhage patterns, and tissue decomposition markers. Bayesian networks will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including histopathology, metabolomics, and environmental variables—to model probabilistic cause-of-death pathways. Additionally, finite element simulations will reconstruct biomechanical trauma scenarios, such as ballistic impacts or blunt force injuries, to quantify force distributions and validate injury mechanisms. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize model training across GPU nodes, and execute iterative simulations with high spatial-temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for pathologists to visualize predictive analytics, generate court-admissible statistical reports, and standardize autopsy interpretations across jurisdictions. By reducing turnaround times and enhancing evidentiary rigor, this work aims to strengthen the role of forensic pathology in public health surveillance and legal accountability, particularly in cases involving mass disasters or suspected criminal negligence. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the scalability, reproducibility, and interoperability required for translational impact in both academic and operational forensic medicine contexts.
cip_definition: Research focused on the performance of medical autopsies, the analysis of human remains and crime scenes, and the legal follow-up and responsibilities of public pathologists.

abstract: Antibiotic resistance poses a critical challenge in modern medicine, driven by mutations in bacterial enzymes that reduce drug efficacy. This project employs high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and dynamic mechanisms underlying resistance in β-lactamase enzymes, which confer resistance to β-lactam antibiotics. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will characterize the conformational changes and binding free energy differences between wild-type and clinically observed mutant variants when interacting with antibiotics. These simulations, conducted using GROMACS and AMBER, require extensive computational resources due to the microsecond-scale sampling needed to capture rare enzymatic events. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained on simulation-derived datasets to predict mutation-induced alterations in substrate binding and catalytic efficiency. The integration of HPC-driven simulations and predictive analytics aims to identify novel drug targets or adjuvant strategies to restore antibiotic effectiveness. Outcomes will include atomistic insights into resistance mechanisms, validated predictive frameworks for mutation impact assessment, and a publicly accessible database of enzyme dynamic profiles. This work bridges computational biophysics and clinical medicine, directly addressing a pressing public health issue while providing pre-medical students with interdisciplinary training in computational methods. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the scale of simulations (>50,000 core-hours) and large datasets (>100 TB), enabling robust statistical analysis and model validation. By linking molecular-level findings to therapeutic applications, this project advances translational research in antimicrobial development and equips future physicians with skills to engage with data-driven medical innovation. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journals and integrated into pre-medical curricula to highlight the role of computational tools in modern healthcare challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in medicine, osteopathic medicine, or podiatric medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize human-robot collaborative workflows in industrial manufacturing environments, a critical challenge as industries increasingly adopt automation while retaining hybrid human-machine systems. Current methods for modeling these interactions struggle to account for dynamic human factors, such as ergonomic constraints, cognitive load variability, and real-time task reallocation, particularly at scale. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized multi-agent simulations that integrate discrete-event manufacturing process models with biomechanical and behavioral human performance data. The computational approach will employ reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively optimize task scheduling and resource allocation across heterogeneous workcells, while adhering to safety protocols and productivity targets. By running thousands of concurrent simulations through HPC-enabled parameter sweeps, we aim to identify robust optimization strategies that adapt to workforce skill variances, equipment availability fluctuations, and production demand scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of prescriptive analytics for layout redesign and workforce training prioritization. This work will provide quantitative insights into cost-benefit tradeoffs for different levels of automation integration, directly addressing the Industrial Technology program's focus on practical implementations of optimization theory and organizational behavior analysis. The requested computing resources will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling human-machine systems, advancing decision-support tools for industrial planners while fostering workforce-centric automation strategies. Results will be validated through partnerships with regional manufacturers implementing Industry 4.0 upgrades, ensuring translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of industrial engineers and managers. Includes instruction in optimization theory, human factors, organizational behavior, industrial processes, industrial planning procedures, computer applications, and report and presentation preparation.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into industrial systems design is critical for addressing complex, large-scale optimization challenges in modern manufacturing and logistics. This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for real-time, data-driven decision-making in multiprocess production systems, where stochastic demand, machine reliability, and energy constraints create dynamic interdependencies. Current analytical models struggle to balance trade-offs between throughput, energy efficiency, and maintenance costs at enterprise scales, particularly when incorporating high-resolution sensor data from IoT-enabled equipment. We propose a two-stage computational approach combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for adaptive scheduling with mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) for strategic resource allocation. The DRL component will train neural networks on historical operational data to predict equipment degradation patterns, while the MINLP layer optimizes system-wide objectives under uncertainty. Implementing this framework requires high-performance computing resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of simultaneous job-shop scheduling (10,000+ decision variables) and the computational intensity of neural network training across multi-terabyte datasets. Anticipated outcomes include a novel hybrid algorithm that reduces energy waste by 12-18% and downtime by 20-25% in simulated automotive assembly use cases, validated against industry benchmarks. The work will advance industrial engineering methodologies by demonstrating how HPC-enabled predictive-prescriptive analytics can co-optimize sustainability and productivity metrics in cyber-physical production systems. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits to support broader adoption of scalable optimization techniques in smart manufacturing initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of air traffic management systems, driven by rising global air travel demand and evolving operational constraints, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize safety, efficiency, and scalability. Current air traffic control (ATC) methodologies rely on heuristic models and static protocols that struggle to adapt to dynamic variables such as weather disruptions, heterogeneous aircraft performance, and real-time rerouting requirements. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate and optimize next-generation ATC decision-making processes. The research will focus on integrating real-time flight data, weather patterns, and airspace constraints into a scalable, agent-based simulation environment to model traffic flow management, conflict detection, and resolution strategies. Computational methods will include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic risks, machine learning models for predictive traffic pattern analysis, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to balance competing priorities such as fuel efficiency, delay minimization, and safety margins. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale scenario testing across diverse airspace configurations, including extreme-density scenarios and edge cases involving simultaneous system failures. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for operational improvements under variable conditions, validated machine learning architectures for adaptive traffic prediction, and open-source simulation tools to support FAA modernization initiatives. By leveraging distributed computing resources, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical ATC research and deployable solutions, providing a foundation for data-driven policy updates and automated decision-support systems. The results will directly inform ongoing efforts to enhance the National Airspace System’s capacity and resilience while maintaining stringent safety standards in an era of unprecedented aviation growth.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to air-traffic management and control, usually with additional training at the FAA Flight Control Center in a cooperative education program. Includes instruction in flight control, the use of radar and electronic scanning devices, plotting of flights, radio communication, interpretation of weather conditions affecting flights, flight instrumentation used by pilots, and maintenance of flight-control center or control-tower log books.

abstract: Musculoskeletal neoplasms present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their molecular heterogeneity, dynamic interactions with surrounding tissues, and variable responses to existing therapies. Current approaches to treatment planning and outcome prediction often rely on static clinical or imaging data, which inadequately capture the complex biomechanical and biological interplay driving tumor progression and therapy resistance. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing integrative computational models that simulate tumor behavior across molecular, cellular, and tissue-level scales. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to create multi-omics network models to identify genomic and proteomic drivers of tumor aggressiveness and metastasis, coupled with biomechanical finite element models to predict tumor-induced bone remodeling and biomechanical failure risks under therapeutic loads. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to multimodal datasets—including radiomics, histopathology, genomics, and patient-specific biomechanics—to stratify patients by predicted treatment response and optimize personalized therapy regimens. Key computational challenges include managing terabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing multi-physics simulations, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. The HPC infrastructure will enable iterative model calibration using evolutionary algorithms and large-scale parameter sweeps to account for biological variability. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for sarcoma progression, tools to simulate radiotherapy and surgical outcomes in silico, and actionable biomarkers for therapy personalization. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs and advance precision oncology by bridging computational discovery with translational applications. By quantifying previously intractable interactions between tumor biology and biomechanics, the project aims to reduce complications such as pathologic fractures and improve survival rates for patients with advanced musculoskeletal cancers.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal neoplasm, and the application of cancer therapy regimes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, personalized fitness training frameworks through computational biomechanical modeling and large-scale physiological data analysis. Current fitness programming often relies on generalized protocols that inadequately account for individual variability in biomechanics, metabolic response, and long-term adaptation, leading to suboptimal outcomes or injury risks. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating motion capture data, wearable sensor outputs, and physiological profiles to simulate and optimize individualized exercise regimens. The research will utilize finite element analysis (FEA) to model musculoskeletal stress patterns across diverse body types during high-intensity interval training (HIHT) and resistance exercises, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict metabolic efficiency and recovery dynamics. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling to simulate population-level interactions within virtual training environments, enabling the identification of emergent patterns in group fitness adherence and performance. The computational pipeline will process multi-modal datasets, including 3D kinematic sequences (1000+ fps), electromyography signals, and real-time metabolomic data streams from a cohort of 500 participants. By deploying GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures on HPC clusters, we aim to reduce simulation times for complex biomechanical interactions from weeks to hours, facilitating rapid iteration of training variables. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for injury risk mitigation, optimized load progression algorithms, and dynamically adjustable nutrition-exercise coupling models. This work will establish a foundational computational toolkit for fitness technicians to design hyper-personalized programs, bridging gaps between exercise science, data-driven decision-making, and client-specific adaptability. The resource-intensive nature of concurrent multi-scale simulations (molecular stress responses to macro-level movement patterns) necessitates HPC capabilities beyond typical institutional infrastructure, particularly for memory-intensive genomic-metabolic correlation analyses. Results will be disseminated through open-source training optimization plugins compatible with industry-standard fitness software, enhancing accessibility for non-computational practitioners.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced computational models for optimizing customer service management (CSM) operations in dynamic, large-scale environments. A critical challenge in CSM is balancing resource allocation—such as staffing, training, and technology investments—with fluctuating customer demand, multi-channel service delivery, and real-time performance metrics. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these variables or the high-dimensional data generated by modern customer relationship management (CRM) systems. The proposed research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to replicate complex customer service ecosystems, incorporating real-world data on customer behavior, employee performance, and operational constraints. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning, will be integrated to identify adaptive strategies for workforce scheduling and service process optimization. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, significantly reducing computation time compared to conventional systems. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify the impact of resource allocation decisions on key performance indicators (e.g., first-call resolution rates, service wait times) and a decision-support framework for managers to evaluate trade-offs between service quality, operational costs, and employee satisfaction. By bridging gaps in CSM theory and practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for managing customer service teams in sectors with high transaction volumes, such as telecommunications and e-commerce. The computational tools developed will be made available to the broader business research community, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in service operations management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and monitor customer service performance and manage frontline customer support services, call centers/help desks, and customer relations. Includes instruction in customer behavior, specialized information technology and systems management, developing and using customer service databases, user surveys and other feedback mechanisms, strategic and performance planning and analysis, operations management, personnel supervision, and communications and marketing skills.

abstract: Healthcare systems worldwide face growing challenges in delivering equitable, efficient, and high-quality care, particularly for populations affected by socioeconomic disparities. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the dynamic interactions between patient behaviors, systemic resource allocation, and evolving policy environments. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to model multilevel determinants of healthcare utilization and outcomes at scale. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze integrated datasets spanning electronic health records (EHRs), insurance claims, census data, and community-level social determinants of health. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate patient care-seeking behaviors, provider decision-making, and policy scenarios under varying resource constraints. Machine learning techniques, including ensemble models and natural language processing, will identify latent patterns in unstructured clinical notes and predict care gaps for high-risk subgroups. Geospatial analysis will map service availability against population needs to quantify access disparities. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the ABM simulations across diverse demographic cohorts and the integration of terabyte-scale datasets—necessitate parallel processing, distributed memory architectures, and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize clinic placement, staffing, and preventive care investments, as well as policy-relevant insights into cost-quality tradeoffs under alternative reimbursement models. By enabling real-time scenario testing across billions of agent interactions and years of simulated time, this HPC-driven approach will advance health services research methodologies while directly informing efforts to reduce care inequities. The resulting models and pipelines will be shared via public repositories to support reproducibility and scalability in resource allocation research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on basic and applied inquiry, that examines access to, and the use, costs, quality, delivery, organization, financing, and outcomes of health care services to produce new knowledge about the structure, processes, and effects of health services for individuals and populations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Baltic languages, with a focus on Latvian, Lithuanian, and the extinct Curonian language. The research problem centers on the scarcity of digitized linguistic resources and the computational complexity of modeling morphologically rich, low-resource languages, which limits advancements in philological studies, historical linguistics, and applications such as machine translation. Current tools optimized for high-resource languages (e.g., English) perform poorly on Baltic languages due to their intricate inflectional systems, dialectal variations, and fragmented historical corpora. This project proposes the development of scalable computational pipelines to automate the analysis of Baltic texts across multiple historical periods and genres. Methods include training transformer-based language models on newly digitized corpora of Old Lithuanian manuscripts and Curonian substrate texts, employing parallelized algorithms for morphological segmentation, and applying phylogenetic modeling to trace diachronic sound shifts. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of digitized archival material, running large-scale comparative simulations of language evolution, and optimizing neural architectures for real-time dialect classification. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access digital lexicons and annotated corpora for understudied Baltic variants, (2) computational models quantifying the influence of Curonian on regional Latvian dialects, and (3) a framework for adapting NLP tools to morphologically complex languages. The results will advance scholarly understanding of Baltic language development, support preservation initiatives for endangered linguistic heritage, and enable practical applications in cross-lingual information retrieval for Baltic-speaking communities. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, this project bridges a critical gap in resources for Baltic studies while demonstrating methodologies transferable to other low-resource language families.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of the Baltic peoples, including, but not limited to, the modern languages of Latvian and Lithuanian, and extinct languages such as Old Prussian and Curionian. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives in pre-modern Russian societies through computational analysis of textual and visual artifacts from medieval and early modern periods. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how localized storytelling traditions, religious iconography, and interregional exchanges shaped collective identities across the territories of historical Rus'. Current scholarship relies heavily on manual analysis of limited source materials, leaving broader patterns of cultural transmission understudied. The proposed work will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted to Old East Slavic and Church Slavonic texts, combined with computer vision methods for analyzing iconographic patterns in digitized religious frescoes and illuminated manuscripts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing over 15TB of multispectral imaging data from deteriorated manuscripts, training transformer-based language models on rare textual corpora, and running spatial network analyses to map cultural diffusion pathways. The computational pipeline will integrate weakly supervised classification of narrative motifs, cross-modal alignment of textual and visual elements, and graph-based modeling of cultural influence networks across time and space.
