Expected outcomes include the first large-scale digital inventory of narrative motifs in pre-Petrine Russian culture, quantitative evidence for previously hypothesized Byzantine and Baltic cultural transfers, and open-source tools for paleographic feature extraction. By enabling systematic analysis of previously inaccessible materials, this work will provide new insights into the formation of Russian cultural identity while demonstrating how computational methods can advance area studies research. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for cultural heritage datasets, and parallel processing of high-resolution artifact imagery.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Russian Federation and its Soviet, Czarist, and medieval predecessors and related borderlands.

abstract: Wildfire dynamics present a critical challenge to fire protection and emergency response, with complex interactions between fire behavior, fuel variability, and atmospheric conditions driving rapid, unpredictable spread. Current predictive models often lack the resolution and computational scalability to account for these multi-physics interactions in real time, particularly under dynamic weather scenarios or in heterogeneous terrain. This project seeks to advance wildfire simulation capabilities by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a coupled fire-atmosphere modeling framework. The proposed work integrates large-eddy simulation (LES) for turbulent plume dynamics, physics-based fire spread algorithms, and high-resolution fuel moisture mapping to resolve sub-meter-scale processes influencing fire progression. Computational workflows will parallelize model components across GPU and CPU architectures, optimizing runtime for ensemble simulations that quantify uncertainties in ignition sources, wind patterns, and suppression strategies. By coupling these simulations with machine learning-driven data assimilation techniques—using real-time satellite imagery and sensor networks—the framework aims to improve the accuracy of short-term fire spread predictions. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source wildfire modeling toolkit validated against historical fire case studies (e.g., 2018 Camp Fire, California) and experimental burn data. This research will directly support firefighting resource allocation, evacuation planning, and risk assessment for wildfire-prone communities. The HPC resources requested are essential to manage the computational load of multi-parameter ensembles and the storage demands of petabyte-scale output datasets. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with the U.S. Forest Service and state emergency management agencies, providing actionable tools to enhance situational awareness during active fire events.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Chiropractic care, rooted in the relationship between spinal alignment and nervous system function, lacks a comprehensive biomechanical and neurophysiological understanding of how specific adjustments influence systemic health. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a multi-scale computational model to simulate the immediate and cascading effects of spinal manipulations on neural signaling, musculoskeletal dynamics, and autonomic regulation. Current clinical studies and in vitro experiments are limited in resolving real-time, system-wide interactions, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate heterogeneous data—including MRI-derived spinal geometries, neural activity datasets, and biomechanical force profiles—into a unified simulation framework. The research will employ finite element modeling to simulate vertebral segment mechanics under adjustment forces, coupled with dynamic neural network models to predict central nervous system (CNS) responses. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated and clinical data to identify patterns linking adjustment parameters (e.g., force vector, velocity) to physiological outcomes such as pain modulation, inflammatory marker changes, or autonomic balance. HPC resources are critical for managing the computational intensity of iterative simulations across variable patient anatomies and for training predictive models on multi-terabyte datasets encompassing retrospective clinical records and motion-capture biomechanics. Expected outcomes include a validated in silico platform for optimizing adjustment protocols, a mechanistic framework explaining how localized biomechanical interventions propagate systemic effects, and predictive tools for personalizing chiropractic care based on patient-specific spinal kinematics and neural responsiveness. This work aims to advance chiropractic science from an empirically guided practice to a quantitatively grounded discipline, bridging biomechanics, neuroscience, and clinical therapeutics. By elucidating the biophysical underpinnings of spinal adjustments, the project will inform safer, more effective treatment strategies and foster interdisciplinary collaborations to position chiropractic within integrative healthcare models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of chiropractic, a health care and healing system based on the application of non-invasive treatments and spinal adjustments to alleviate health problems caused by vertebral misalignments affecting bodily function as derived from the philosophy of Daniel Palmer. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, chiropractic theory and science, postural and spinal analysis, diagnostic radiology and ultrasound, adjustment technique, patient counseling, professional standards and ethics, and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of scopist workflows through advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. Scopists, who edit court reporter transcripts to ensure legal precision, face challenges in managing high volumes of text with strict deadlines while maintaining contextual accuracy in specialized legal terminology. Traditional computer-aided transcription (CAT) tools lack adaptive learning capabilities, leading to repetitive manual corrections and inconsistent error detection. This research proposes an ML-driven system to automate context-aware error identification, optimize real-time editing workflows, and improve alignment between machine shorthand inputs and finalized transcripts. The computational approach involves training transformer-based language models on domain-specific corpora of legal transcripts, annotated with common scopist corrections (e.g., homophone errors, procedural terminology mismatches, and punctuation inconsistencies). High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of training data, hyperparameter optimization for domain-adapted models, and simulation of real-world editing scenarios through synthetic transcript generation. The project will benchmark performance against industry-standard CAT software using metrics including error reduction rates, edit turnaround time, and semantic coherence scores. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for intelligent transcript augmentation, demonstrated to reduce manual intervention by ≥40% in pilot legal domains while maintaining 99.5%+ accuracy thresholds required for court-admissible documents. By integrating computational linguistics with legal documentation practices, this work addresses a critical gap in paraprofessional legal technology, offering scalable solutions to enhance access to justice through improved transcription quality and resource efficiency. The resulting models and datasets will provide foundational resources for future research at the intersection of computational linguistics, professional training systems, and legal process optimization.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to perform editing and word processing on a court reporter transcript to ensure the accuracy of the transcripts. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcriptioning, machine shorthand, and computer-aided transcription software.

abstract: This project seeks to address the compounding challenges of rural community resilience in the face of climate change, economic transitions, and shifting demographic patterns through advanced computational modeling. Rural sociologists have historically relied on qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods to study social dynamics, but these approaches struggle to capture the complexity of multi-level, longitudinal interactions between environmental stressors, migration, agricultural practices, and institutional policies. We propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) integrated with spatial demographic data to simulate decision-making processes among rural households, agricultural producers, and local governance bodies across a 50-year horizon. The ABM will incorporate dynamically linked modules for land-use changes, population aging, labor market fluctuations, and climate vulnerability indices derived from downscaled regional projections. A parallelized parameter exploration framework will assess how varying policy interventions—including broadband infrastructure investments, adaptive agricultural subsidies, and community health service expansions—affect systemic outcomes related to population retention, economic stability, and environmental stewardship. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing resources due to the stochastic nature of agent interactions across 10^5 simulated households, high-resolution geospatial data layers (1km² grid cells), and ensemble runs accounting for climate scenario uncertainty. Expected outcomes include identifying critical leverage points for rural development policies, generating open-source simulation tools tailored to rural sociology applications, and establishing scalable methods to integrate Census microdata with environmental datasets. By advancing computational social science capabilities in rural contexts, this work will provide empirically grounded insights to support communities navigating structural transitions while contributing novel methodologies to bridge sociological theory with complex systems analysis.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the structure and function of rural societies. Includes instruction in sociological theory, research methods, statistics, sociology of agriculture, community development, social and economic development, demography, rural poverty, gender roles in rural societies, and environmental sociology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and personalized pharmacotherapy demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in optimizing drug efficacy, minimizing adverse effects, and understanding molecular interactions at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale computational models for predicting drug-target interactions, pharmacokinetic profiles, and polypharmacy risks. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) employing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the binding mechanisms of novel therapeutics to disease-specific protein targets, including those with high conformational flexibility or mutation-driven resistance, and (2) applying machine learning (ML) frameworks to analyze large-scale pharmacogenomic datasets, enabling the identification of patient-specific factors influencing drug response variability. Computational workflows will integrate quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods for modeling enzymatic reactions, hybrid ML-MD pipelines for virtual screening of compound libraries, and graph neural networks to predict drug-drug interaction risks in multi-medication regimens. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized MD simulations and distributed computing architectures for training deep learning models on heterogeneous biomedical data, including electronic health records, structural proteomics, and metabolomics datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of lead compounds with improved selectivity for neurodegenerative disease targets, predictive models for dose optimization in renal-impaired populations, and open-source tools for real-time polypharmacy risk assessment in clinical pharmacy practice. By addressing computational bottlenecks in simulating complex biological systems and analyzing high-dimensional healthcare data, this work aims to advance precision pharmacy paradigms while providing a scalable framework for accelerating therapeutic development and improving medication safety outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent or employed practice of preparing and dispensing drugs and medications in consultation with prescribing physicians and other health care professionals, and for managing pharmacy practices and counseling patients. Includes instruction in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmacy practice, pharmacy administration, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the optimization of flexible manufacturing systems (FMS) through high-fidelity computational modeling, addressing the challenge of dynamically balancing productivity, energy efficiency, and resource utilization in multi-process industrial environments. Current FMS scheduling methods struggle to account for real-time variability in machine performance, material flow bottlenecks, and energy demand fluctuations, particularly in small-batch production scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-scale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation for system-level logistics, finite element analysis for machine tool thermal deformation modeling, and reinforcement learning algorithms for adaptive scheduling. By coupling these components at scale, the model will capture interdependencies between toolpath accuracy, machine degradation, and energy consumption patterns across heterogeneous production cells. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate stochastic disruptions and training decision-making agents under diverse operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of recommending real-time adjustments to production schedules while maintaining <2% energy overconsumption thresholds. This work will directly support the development of next-generation industrial control systems that autonomously reconcile throughput targets with sustainability metrics. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for FMS simulation, enabling smaller manufacturers to adopt data-driven optimization without proprietary software dependencies. The computational infrastructure requested will also facilitate benchmarking emerging quantum-inspired annealing algorithms against classical optimization methods, informing future hybrid approaches for industrial decision-support systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in industrial production technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the molecular-level understanding of reaction mechanisms in complex catalytic systems, with a focus on enzyme-like behavior in non-equilibrium environments. A central challenge in physical chemistry lies in accurately modeling the interplay of quantum mechanical effects, solvent dynamics, and conformational changes that govern catalytic efficiency and selectivity. Traditional computational approaches often compromise either on electronic structure accuracy or system size, limiting predictive power for biologically relevant timescales. We propose a hybrid multiscale framework combining density functional theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and machine learning-accelerated free energy sampling to study model systems of chiral organocatalysts and metalloenzyme active sites. The computational workflow will leverage explicit solvation models and advanced path-sampling techniques to map free energy landscapes for competing reaction pathways. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the >10,000-core-hour simulations required for statistically robust sampling of rare events, including proton-coupled electron transfers and stereoselective transition states. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative predictions of kinetic isotope effects for validation against ultrafast spectroscopy experiments, (2) identification of solvent-mediated collective motions that lower activation barriers, and (3) generalizable protocols for optimizing catalyst design through electrostatic preorganization principles. The results will address fundamental gaps in modeling entropy-enthalpy compensation phenomena and provide new benchmarks for simulating enzymatic fidelity without empirical force fields. By bridging quantum accuracy with mesoscale sampling, this work aims to establish predictive computational strategies for complex chemical systems, with potential applications in green chemistry and biomimetic catalyst development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of understanding and predicting the behavior of chemical systems ranging from nuclear particles to atoms, molecules, clusters, biological materials and macroscopic assemblies. Includes instruction in quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, reaction dynamics, group theory, collision theory, and polymer science.

abstract: Montessori education emphasizes child-centered, self-directed learning within carefully prepared environments, yet the dynamic interplay between teacher interventions, environmental design, and student outcomes remains underexplored at scale. This project seeks to model how variations in Montessori classroom practices influence developmental trajectories, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-agent interactions and analyze longitudinal datasets. The research problem centers on identifying computationally intensive patterns in Montessori pedagogy—such as the timing of teacher guidance, material sequencing, and spatial organization—that correlate with optimal cognitive, social, and motor skill development in early childhood. A hybrid computational approach will be employed: (1) Agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom ecosystems, capturing stochastic interactions among students, teachers, and materials under diverse pedagogical scenarios; (2) Machine learning analysis of anonymized observational datasets spanning 5,000+ hours of classroom video, using natural language processing to code teacher-student dialogues and computer vision to track material usage patterns. These methods require parallelized processing of high-dimensional data and Monte Carlo simulations to account for variability in child behavior. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to optimize Montessori teacher training protocols by quantifying how specific instructional strategies mediate learning outcomes. The project will produce open-source tools for simulating classroom dynamics, enabling teacher educators to test hypothetical interventions in silico before implementation. By bridging Montessori theory with computational modeling, this work aims to advance evidence-based teacher education while preserving the pedagogical integrity of Montessori methods.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Maria Montessori and her followers.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian hierarchical models to analyze high-dimensional, spatially correlated datasets in environmental and biomedical research. A key challenge in modern statistical analysis is the computational intractability of inferring complex, multi-level models with thousands of parameters, particularly when integrating non-Gaussian response variables, latent spatial processes, and non-parametric components. Traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods suffer from slow convergence and high memory demands under these conditions, limiting their utility for real-world decision-making. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) for global parameter exploration with variational inference for localized approximation of posterior distributions. The implementation will leverage GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory parallelism to optimize sampler efficiency, using the Stan probabilistic programming language and custom CUDA kernels for low-level performance tuning. A central focus is the development of a novel preconditioning strategy for stochastic gradient descent within variational algorithms, aimed at reducing bias in high-dimensional settings. The project will validate methods using synthetic datasets with known ground truth and apply them to two case studies: (1) modeling disease spread across urban networks using anonymized mobile health data (≈10^6 observations), and (2) estimating extreme weather event risks from multi-source climate model outputs (≈1TB). Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for efficient hierarchical model fitting, theoretical insights into convergence properties of hybrid samplers in sparse data regimes, and policy-relevant risk estimates for public health planning. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential for benchmarking against existing MCMC approaches at scale, with preliminary tests indicating a 40x speedup potential through optimized parallelization. This work bridges critical gaps in computationally sustainable statistics, enabling broader adoption of Bayesian methods in data-rich scientific domains.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: Family medicine research faces unique challenges in addressing the heterogeneous needs of diverse patient populations, particularly in understanding multifactorial health outcomes influenced by social, genetic, and environmental determinants. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for chronic disease management in primary care settings, with an emphasis on multimorbidity patterns in underserved communities. The research problem centers on the computational limitations of analyzing large-scale electronic health records (EHRs) integrated with geospatial and socioeconomic data, which are critical for identifying disparities in care delivery and outcomes. Current methods struggle to process multimodal datasets at the resolution required for personalized risk stratification in family medicine contexts. To address this, we will implement a hybrid machine learning framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model patient-provider interaction networks and transformer-based architectures to interpret longitudinal EHRs. The computational workflow will include federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across collaborating clinics while training models on aggregated datasets. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 10+ terabytes of structured and unstructured data, including clinical notes, insurance claims, and community health surveys. Key outcomes will include (1) validated algorithms predicting 5-year risks of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and depression comorbidity with >85% AUC, (2) geospatial heatmaps identifying high-priority intervention zones, and (3) open-source tools for scalable primary care analytics. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform resource allocation in family medicine by enabling data-driven prioritization of preventive care strategies. Results will directly inform clinic-level decision-making for over 200 primary care practices in our health network while establishing computational methods adaptable to other primary care research initiatives. This work represents a critical step toward equitable precision medicine in community health settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Family Medicine

abstract: Pediatric endocrine disorders, including diabetes, growth hormone deficiencies, and adrenal dysfunctions, exhibit complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often rely on generalized protocols, which may inadequately address individual variability in disease progression and treatment response. This project seeks to address this gap by developing patient-specific predictive models of endocrine function and treatment outcomes using high-dimensional clinical, genomic, and metabolomic datasets. The primary challenge lies in integrating multi-scale biological data while accounting for dynamic hormonal feedback systems and developmental changes during childhood and adolescence—a task requiring computational resources beyond conventional clinical research infrastructure. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to implement multiscale computational models combining mechanistic simulations of hormone-receptor interactions with machine learning approaches. These models will analyze longitudinal patient data from electronic health records (n ≈ 10,000) and multi-omics profiles (whole-genome sequencing, proteomics, and steroid metabolomes) from a prospective cohort of 500 patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia and growth disorders. Computational workflows will include Bayesian hierarchical modeling to account for age-dependent endocrine parameters, deep learning architectures for pattern recognition in time-series hormone data, and agent-based simulations of pituitary-adrenal axis dynamics. The HPC environment is critical for training complex neural networks, running parallelized pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic simulations across developmental stages, and performing genome-wide association studies with gene-environment interaction terms. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for optimizing glucocorticoid dosing schedules in adrenal insufficiency, (2) identification of novel biomarkers for early detection of treatment-related metabolic complications, and (3) open-source computational tools for simulating endocrine maturation trajectories. By enabling precision dosing and risk stratification, this work aims to reduce long-term sequelae of pediatric endocrine disorders while establishing a computational framework adaptable to other hormone-mediated developmental conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of endocrine diseases and the regulation of hormone balance in childhood and adolescence.

abstract: Wind energy systems are critical to sustainable energy infrastructure, yet optimizing their installation, operation, and maintenance remains a significant technical challenge. Current industry practices rely on static models and limited datasets, which often fail to account for dynamic environmental factors, complex turbine wake interactions, and real-world wear patterns. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational tools that enhance the precision and efficiency of wind energy system design and repair workflows. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating site-specific wind flow patterns and turbine wake effects to optimize turbine placement and energy output, (2) modeling mechanical stress and material degradation in turbine components under variable operational conditions, and (3) training machine learning algorithms to predict equipment failures using multi-source sensor data. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will be conducted using open-source solvers, coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessments. Machine learning workflows will integrate time-series data from operational turbines to identify failure precursors. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities, large-scale memory allocation, and GPU acceleration to manage high-resolution meshes, iterative parameter sweeps, and real-time data assimilation. The expected outcomes include validated predictive models for turbine performance and lifespan, actionable maintenance schedules to reduce downtime, and open-access simulation templates for educational use in wind energy technician training programs. By bridging computational innovation with practical technician training, this project aims to advance both the technical rigor and workforce readiness critical to expanding wind energy adoption.
cip_title: Wind Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair wind energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of multi-omics data with clinical electrophysiology for personalized management of chronic neurological disorders, focusing on epilepsy and Parkinson’s disease. Current approaches to optimizing neuromodulation therapies (e.g., deep brain stimulation) rely on static anatomical or phenomenological biomarkers, often overlooking dynamic interactions between genetic, molecular, and real-time neural circuit activity. The research addresses this gap by developing computational models that unify patient-specific genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles with high-density intracranial EEG (iEEG) and wearable sensor data. A hybrid machine learning framework will be implemented, combining graph neural networks to model brain network dynamics and variational autoencoders to identify latent multi-omics signatures predictive of therapeutic response. Computational workflows will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale neurophysiological datasets, GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures, and large-scale simulations of biologically constrained neural networks. Key challenges include scaling Bayesian inference for probabilistic integration of heterogeneous data streams and mitigating computational bottlenecks in real-time closed-loop stimulation modeling. Anticipated outcomes include a novel open-source pipeline for biomarker discovery, validated against retrospective clinical trial data, and predictive models to guide adaptive neuromodulation parameter tuning. This work bridges computational neuroscience, systems biology, and clinical neuroengineering, directly supporting translational objectives by enabling data-driven personalization of neuromodulation therapies. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive omics analyses, iterative model optimization, and validation against multi-site electrophysiology repositories, ultimately accelerating the translation of multi-scale biological insights into clinically actionable tools.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares clinicians to direct a broad range of scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge into clinical practice, and bridge clinical science with laboratory investigations. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, and scientific writing.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for neuromusculoskeletal disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific biomechanical and neurological interactions. Current rehabilitation protocols often adopt generalized approaches, leading to variable functional outcomes due to the complex interplay of tissue healing, neural adaptation, and biomechanical loading across diverse patient populations. To address this, we propose developing multiscale computational models that integrate neuromuscular activation patterns, joint kinematics, and tissue remodeling processes at unprecedented resolution. These models will be parameterized using patient data from motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging, requiring iterative simulations to optimize rehabilitation prescriptions. A key computational challenge involves solving coupled partial differential equations for soft tissue mechanics and neural signal propagation across anatomically accurate domains, necessitating GPU-accelerated finite element analysis and machine learning-based surrogate modeling. Additionally, we will employ ensemble machine learning techniques to analyze high-dimensional clinical datasets (demographics, biomarkers, treatment histories) from our institution’s rehabilitation registry, aiming to identify predictors of optimal intervention timing and dosage. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to quantify uncertainty in model predictions and validate against longitudinal outcome data from ongoing clinical trials in post-stroke mobility recovery and spinal cord injury rehabilitation. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for virtual testing of rehabilitation strategies, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice. This work will directly inform the design of adaptive rehabilitation protocols that dynamically respond to individual recovery trajectories, potentially decreasing time to functional independence by 15-30% in modeled cohorts. The requested resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale multimodal datasets and computationally intensive multiscale simulations within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, etiology, treatment, prevention and rehabilitation of neuromusculo-skeletal, cardiovascular, pulmonary and other system disorders common to patients of both sexes and all ages. May included related research in physical examinations, design and prescription of rehabilitation strategies and the supervision of rehabilitation teams.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of real-time sports media communication and audience engagement across digital platforms. As the sports media landscape becomes increasingly data-driven, there is a critical need to understand how multimedia content—such as live broadcasts, social media interactions, and audience analytics—shapes public perception and engagement. Traditional methods of media analysis struggle to process the scale and complexity of modern sports communication datasets, which include high-volume video streams, geolocated social media posts, and real-time sentiment metrics. This research aims to address this gap by developing computational models to evaluate how multimodal content influences audience behavior and brand outcomes in sports. Using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques, the project will process unstructured text, audio, and video data from sources like live game broadcasts, fan forums, and influencer platforms. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these datasets, including training machine learning models to detect patterns in audience sentiment, topic trends, and visual storytelling techniques. Additionally, network analysis will map the flow of information between athletes, media outlets, and fans to identify key influencers and communication bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for optimizing media strategies, such as timing and framing of content to maximize engagement, as well as a publicly accessible toolkit for sports communication professionals to analyze their own datasets. By integrating computational methods with media theory, this work will advance the academic understanding of digital sports communication while providing practical tools for industry stakeholders. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the project’s data volume and computational intensity, ensuring robust, scalable analyses that would be infeasible with standard computing resources.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for communicating about sports in a variety of formats, media, and contexts; and that prepares individuals to be sports reporters and writers, photojournalists, radio and television announcers, producers and directors, recreational sports promoters, and public relations specialists. Includes instruction in sports writing, photography, broadcast journalism, sports production, game rules, media and public relations, and sports promotion.

abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of disease registry data present significant challenges in deriving actionable insights for public health decision-making. Current approaches to managing and analyzing these datasets are constrained by computational limitations, particularly in processing large-scale, heterogeneous data types (e.g., clinical records, genomic data, and population-level demographics) while ensuring compliance with privacy and interoperability standards. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable computational workflows for integrating, analyzing, and modeling disease registry data. The primary research problem centers on enabling real-time analytics and predictive modeling of multimorbidity patterns across diverse populations, which traditional systems struggle to support due to latency and scalability bottlenecks. The proposed computational approach combines distributed data processing frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark) with machine learning models optimized for GPU-accelerated environments to identify disease clusters, forecast epidemiological trends, and evaluate intervention scenarios. Key tasks include parallelizing data ingestion pipelines for registry updates, implementing federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across jurisdictions, and simulating disease spread under varying public health policies using agent-based models. The integration of HPC resources will enable iterative refinement of predictive algorithms and large-scale validation against historical registry data. Expected outcomes include a reproducible computational framework for enhancing the granularity and speed of disease surveillance, as well as novel metrics for assessing risk stratification in underrepresented populations. This work will directly support healthcare agencies in optimizing resource allocation during outbreaks and improve the fidelity of registry-derived evidence for policymaking. By advancing computational methods tailored to disease registry ecosystems, the project aims to establish a benchmark for scalable, ethical data management practices in public health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to find, interpret, and record demographic and medical information on individuals for healthcare agencies and disease registries. Includes instruction in anatomy, data management, disease registry organization and operations, epidemiology, ethics, fundamentals of disease coding and staging, medical terminology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, physiology, quality management, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize individualized educational strategies for students with intellectual disabilities (ID). Despite advances in special education pedagogy, educators face persistent challenges in efficiently designing personalized interventions that account for the heterogeneous cognitive, behavioral, and sensory profiles of students with ID. Current methods for creating individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual, time-consuming assessments and trial-and-error adjustments. This research proposes a computational approach to model learning trajectories and predict intervention outcomes by analyzing multimodal educational data, including student response patterns, behavioral logs, and longitudinal academic performance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large-scale datasets from diverse student populations, train machine learning models to identify predictors of skill acquisition, and simulate the efficacy of tailored instructional sequences under varying constraints. The project will integrate reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically adapt proposed interventions based on simulated student interactions, coupled with agent-based modeling to explore how different classroom resource allocations (e.g., assistive technology configurations, educator-to-student ratios) influence outcomes. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, these simulations will iteratively test thousands of scenario permutations, enabling the identification of robust, generalizable strategies for IEP design. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework to assist educators in generating data-driven IEP recommendations, reducing the time and subjectivity inherent in manual processes. The models will also quantify the impact of specific resource limitations (e.g., limited access to speech-generating devices) on achievable learning goals, informing policy discussions about equitable resource distribution. This work bridges educational theory and computational analytics, offering a scalable methodology to enhance evidence-based practices in special education while respecting the complexity of individual learner needs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with intellectual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with intellectual disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising mentally handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of creating large-scale, algorithmically driven digital artworks that integrate real-time interactivity and immersive environments. As contemporary visual arts increasingly rely on generative systems, 3D modeling, and high-resolution simulations, artists face technical barriers in rendering complex datasets, training machine learning models for creative applications, and synchronizing multi-sensory outputs in installations. The proposed research will develop a computational workflow leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable the creation of dynamic, data-responsive artworks that transcend the limitations of consumer-grade hardware. Key methods include parallelized rendering of 4K/8K volumetric visualizations using GPU clusters, distributed training of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for texture synthesis and style transfer, and real-time physics simulations for interactive installations. The project will also explore hybrid pipelines combining traditional studio practices—such as 3D-scanned physical sculptures—with computational fluid dynamics simulations to generate evolving digital forms. By utilizing HPC resources, the research aims to achieve sub-millisecond latency in interactive systems, process terabyte-scale cultural heritage datasets for AI-driven art historical analysis, and optimize neural radiance fields (NeRFs) for gallery-scale augmented reality experiences. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible toolkit for artists adopting HPC workflows, a series of exhibitions demonstrating computationally intensive artworks, and methodological insights into scaling aesthetic practices within distributed computing architectures. This work bridges gaps between computational aesthetics and studio art production, offering new frameworks for resource-intensive creative research while expanding the technical literacy of visual arts communities. The project’s interdisciplinary significance lies in its potential to redefine scalability in digital artmaking and establish best practices for integrating advanced computing into arts curricula and collaborative research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally function as creative artists in the visual and plastic media. Includes instruction in the traditional fine arts media (drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, CAD/CAM) and/or modern media (ceramics, textiles, intermedia, photography, digital images), theory of art, color theory, composition and perspective, anatomy, the techniques and procedures for maintaining equipment and managing a studio, and art portfolio marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to predict and mitigate pre-analytical errors in clinical laboratory testing, a critical but understudied factor impacting diagnostic accuracy. Pre-analytical errors—such as sample mislabeling, improper storage, or hemolysis—account for up to 70% of laboratory mistakes, yet existing quality control systems primarily target analytical phases. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets, including historical lab error reports, environmental sensor logs from sample transport systems, and real-time spectral data from pre-processing equipment. A hybrid neural network architecture will integrate time-series sensor data with image-based hemolysis detection algorithms, trained on a curated dataset of 500,000+ de-identified specimens from three tertiary care laboratories. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional spectral arrays (10^6 data points/specimen) and temporal modeling of sample handling workflows. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training of ensemble models across GPU nodes, with iterative validation against prospective clinical data. Expected outcomes include a real-time error prediction system that flags high-risk specimens prior to analysis, reducing unnecessary reagent use and diagnostic delays. This work bridges clinical laboratory science with computational analytics, advancing precision in diagnostic stewardship while establishing novel benchmarks for AI-driven quality assurance in laboratory medicine. Successful implementation could decrease repeat testing rates by an estimated 15-20% in participating health systems, directly enhancing patient care efficiency and reducing healthcare costs.
cip_title: Clinical Laboratory Science/ Medical Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conduct and supervise complex medical tests, clinical trials, and research experiments; manage clinical laboratories; and consult with physicians and clinical researchers on diagnoses, disease causation and spread, and research outcomes. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, immunology, immunohematology, physiological relationships to test results, laboratory procedures and quality assurance controls, test and research design and implementation, analytic techniques, laboratory management, data development and reporting, medical informatics, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the empirical understanding of art therapy interventions through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal clinical and artistic data. While art therapy is recognized for its capacity to address mental, emotional, and developmental disorders, the field lacks robust quantitative frameworks to systematically evaluate how specific artistic media, creative processes, or therapeutic interactions correlate with clinical outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating anonymized patient-generated art, session transcripts, and longitudinal behavioral health data from art therapy clinics. Machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines, will be trained to identify visual and linguistic patterns in artwork and dialogue that predict therapeutic progress across diverse demographics. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-resolution art images, feature extraction from temporal sequences of artistic expression, and ensemble modeling to account for individualized patient trajectories. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothesized neurocognitive mechanisms underlying art therapy’s impact, such as emotion regulation or neural plasticity, using biologically informed parameters. The computational demands of processing terabytes of image data, training complex models with cross-validation, and running iterative simulations necessitate scalable storage, GPU acceleration, and distributed computing. Outcomes will include open-source tools for art therapists to quantitatively assess interventions, predictive frameworks linking artistic engagement to symptom reduction, and mechanistic insights into art therapy’s therapeutic pathways. By bridging data-driven computational methods with clinical art therapy practice, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based protocols, inform personalized treatment planning, and establish scalable infrastructure for future translational research in creative arts therapies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use drawing and other art media forms to assess, treat, and rehabilitate individuals with mental, emotional, developmental, or physical disorders. Includes instruction in art, history and theory of art therapy, art therapeutic techniques, psychopathology, patient assessment and diagnosis, cultural diversity issues, legal and ethical practice issues, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-accuracy geospatial data in land management, infrastructure development, and environmental monitoring necessitates advanced computational methods to process large-scale surveying datasets efficiently. Current workflows for analyzing terrestrial LiDAR, photogrammetric, and satellite-derived geospatial data face limitations in scalability and precision when handling complex terrain models, high-resolution point clouds, and real-time deformation monitoring. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize algorithms for automated error correction, 3D feature extraction, and geodetic network adjustment. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) parallel processing of multi-sensor LiDAR datasets to reduce registration and classification time while maintaining sub-centimeter accuracy; (2) GPU-accelerated least-squares adjustment of large geodetic networks with >10^6 observation equations; and (3) machine learning-driven simulation of terrain deformation patterns using finite element analysis integrated with real-time GNSS data streams. By implementing distributed computing frameworks such as Apache Spark for point cloud processing and CUDA-optimized solvers for matrix computations, the project aims to achieve a 10-20x speedup compared to conventional desktop-based workflows. Validation will involve benchmarking against ground truth data from established surveying projects and comparison with existing commercial software packages. The outcomes will advance the precision and scalability of geospatial data processing in surveying applications, directly benefiting infrastructure resilience planning and natural hazard mitigation efforts. Additionally, the developed open-source computational workflows will be disseminated to the surveying community, fostering collaboration and enabling resource-constrained organizations to leverage HPC capabilities. This work will also serve as a foundation for training surveying technology students in computational geomatics, bridging the gap between traditional surveying practices and modern high-performance computational methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the delineation, determination, planning and positioning of land tracts, land and water boundaries, land contours and features; and the preparation of related maps, charts and reports. Includes instruction in applied geodesy, computer graphics, photointerpretation, plane and geodetic surveying, mensuration, traversing, survey equipment operation and maintenance, instrument calibration, and basic cartography.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic manufacturing systems through the development of a computational framework for real-time resource allocation and production scheduling under uncertainty. Modern manufacturing environments face challenges such as fluctuating demand, machine downtime, and supply chain disruptions, which traditional static scheduling models fail to resolve efficiently. To tackle this, we propose a hybrid approach integrating discrete-event simulation, stochastic optimization, and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to model complex interactions between production lines, workforce dynamics, and material flow. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train MARL agents across thousands of simulated scenarios, optimize hyperparameters via parallelized grid searches, and solve large-scale mixed-integer linear programming models for capacity planning. The computational framework will leverage historical production data and real-time sensor inputs from a partner automotive assembly plant to simulate facility-specific constraints, including maintenance schedules, energy consumption limits, and labor agreements. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool that reduces idle time by 15-20%, improves on-time order fulfillment rates, and dynamically adjusts schedules in response to disruptions. The project will contribute novel methodologies to operations management literature by bridging simulation-based optimization with adaptive machine learning, offering scalable solutions for Industry 4.0 environments. Results will be disseminated through open-source code repositories and case studies demonstrating computational efficiency gains in large-scale manufacturing settings. Access to HPC resources will enable the exploration of high-fidelity models that capture interdependencies across supply chain tiers, advancing both academic research and practical applications in smart manufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and direct the physical and/or technical functions of a firm or organization, particularly those relating to development, production, and manufacturing. Includes instruction in principles of general management, manufacturing and production systems, plant management, equipment maintenance management, production control, industrial labor relations and skilled trades supervision, strategic manufacturing policy, systems analysis, productivity analysis and cost control, and materials planning.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of neurodevelopmental trajectories in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) by integrating large-scale neuroimaging, genetic, and behavioral datasets. A critical challenge in developmental and behavioral pediatrics is the heterogeneity of symptom presentation and treatment response, which limits the precision of diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks. Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture complex, non-linear interactions between biological, environmental, and clinical variables. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to apply machine learning models and network-based analyses to multi-modal data from the ABCD Study and institutional cohorts (n ≈ 10,000 participants). Computational workflows will include feature selection algorithms to identify biomarkers predictive of developmental outcomes, graph theoretical analyses of functional brain connectivity, and ensemble classifiers to stratify subtypes based on longitudinal behavioral data. GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures will be employed to model temporal patterns in developmental milestones and treatment adherence metrics. The scale of data integration—spanning terabyte-level neuroimaging files, whole-genome sequencing, and electronic health records—necessitates distributed computing, parallelized processing, and high-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of reproducible neural and genetic signatures associated with differential responses to behavioral therapies, (2) predictive models for early detection of developmental regression, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for phenotype stratification in pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders. By elucidating mechanisms underlying clinical heterogeneity, this work aims to inform personalized intervention strategies and improve functional outcomes for children with ASD/ADHD. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing data dimensionality, reducing model training times from months to days, and enabling real-time validation across diverse cohorts.
cip_definition: Research focused on Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics

abstract: The efficient operation of heavy earthmoving equipment is critical to construction productivity, safety, and environmental impact. However, optimizing equipment workflows under dynamic site conditions—such as variable soil mechanics, terrain instability, and energy consumption patterns—remains a complex, understudied challenge. Current training protocols and operational guidelines rely heavily on generalized best practices rather than data-driven, site-specific models, leading to suboptimal fuel efficiency, equipment wear, and project timelines. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and analyze earthmoving operations in diverse environments, enabling predictive optimization of equipment use. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will model multi-body interactions between heavy equipment (e.g., crawler tractors, hydraulic excavators) and granular/soil materials using discrete element method (DEM) simulations coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress evaluation. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify patterns in operational efficiency across thousands of simulated scenarios, incorporating variables such as soil moisture, slope gradients, and operator behavior. The computational pipeline will also evaluate energy consumption and emissions profiles under different task allocations, supporting sustainability goals. By scaling these simulations across HPC clusters, we aim to generate a dataset of unprecedented resolution, capturing transient dynamics of blade-soil interactions, load distribution during digging cycles, and real-time equipment response to geotechnical feedback. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for optimizing task sequencing, a digital twin toolkit for operator training, and evidence-based recommendations for adaptive maintenance schedules to reduce downtime. This work will advance the integration of computational engineering into heavy equipment education and industry practice, bridging the gap between traditional operational training and cutting-edge simulation-driven insights. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and partnerships with equipment manufacturers to ensure translational impact.
cip_title: Construction/ Heavy Equipment/ Earthmoving Equipment Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate and maintain a variety of heavy equipment, such as a crawler tractors, motor graders and scrapers, shovels, rigging devices, hoists, and jacks. Includes instruction in digging, ditching, sloping, stripping, grading, and backfilling, clearing and excavating.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the precision, sustainability, and scalability of taxidermy practices through computational modeling and data-driven optimization. While taxidermy traditionally relies on manual craftsmanship, emerging challenges—such as replicating biomechanically accurate poses, predicting long-term material degradation, and minimizing waste in specimen preparation—require interdisciplinary solutions that integrate biological data, materials science, and computational analytics. The research will focus on three core objectives: (1) developing finite element analysis (FEA) models to simulate stress distribution in reconstructed specimens under environmental variables (e.g., humidity, temperature), (2) training machine learning algorithms to correlate historical specimen preservation data with optimal tanning chemical ratios, and (3) creating 3D parametric models for customizable armature designs that adapt to anatomical datasets from scanned specimens. These computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated simulations for real-time rendering of dynamic poses and Bayesian optimization to refine material formulations. By digitizing and analyzing decades of taxidermy records, the project aims to establish predictive frameworks that reduce trial-and-error inefficiencies while preserving artisanal nuance. Outcomes will include open-source tools for pose simulation, a database linking specimen taxa to preservation parameters, and protocols for integrating computational feedback into manual workflows. This work bridges gaps between craft traditions and computational innovation, offering scalable solutions for taxidermists facing evolving ethical, environmental, and technical demands. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large volumetric datasets from micro-CT scans of specimens and iterating complex multiphysics models, which are infeasible on local hardware. Ultimately, the project aspires to position computational taxidermy as a niche interdisciplinary field, enhancing both artistic expression and scientific rigor in biodiversity preservation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to reproduce life-like three-dimensional representations of living animals for permanent display using elements of the deceased specimen(s) as well as artificial materials, and to manage taxidermy services and businesses. Includes instruction in specimen grading and selection, caping and fleshing, preservation procedures, tanning, drying, measurements, form and armature construction, carpentry and woodworking, molding and casting, drawing, sculptural techniques, painting and finishing techniques, basic business operations, customer communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of digital memes as dynamic cultural artifacts in shaping contemporary sociopolitical narratives, an underexplored area at the intersection of media studies, cultural anthropology, and computational social science. While memes are recognized as influential vectors of communication, their lifecycle, cross-platform mutation, and impact on collective identity formation remain poorly understood due to the scale and complexity of multimodal data involved. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze a curated corpus of 10 million meme instances (images, videos, and associated metadata) across social media platforms from 2015–2025. Computational methods will integrate computer vision (via convolutional neural networks) to track visual motif evolution, natural language processing (Transformer models) to map textual hybridization patterns, and temporal network analysis to model meme dissemination pathways. A novel aspect involves developing graph-based algorithms to quantify cultural "virality" thresholds and identify latent communities of practice behind meme reinterpretation. The project requires GPU-accelerated nodes for parallel processing of image-text pairs and 100TB of scalable storage for longitudinal analysis. Expected outcomes include 1) a taxonomy of meme-driven narrative frameworks in transnational contexts, 2) computational models correlating meme mutation rates with real-world cultural events, and 3) open-source tools for ethical large-scale cultural analytics. This work will advance humanities scholarship by establishing quantitative frameworks to study emergent digital folklore, while providing policymakers and educators with evidence-based insights into meme-mediated discourse. The resource-intensive nature of analyzing ephemeral, high-volume multimedia content necessitates HPC capabilities beyond typical departmental infrastructure, positioning this project as a pioneering effort in computational cultural studies.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any single instructional program in liberal arts and sciences, general studies and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Soil systems are complex, heterogeneous environments where physical, chemical, and biological processes interact across spatial and temporal scales, influencing nutrient cycling, water retention, and carbon dynamics. However, predicting these interactions—particularly under changing environmental conditions—remains a critical challenge due to limitations in resolving multiscale phenomena experimentally. This project seeks to advance understanding of soil biogeochemical processes through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale modeling. We propose to develop and validate a coupled reactive transport framework integrating molecular-scale simulations of mineral-organic interactions, pore-scale fluid dynamics, and field-scale soil hydrology. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will parameterize free energy landscapes for ion exchange and organic matter adsorption on clay surfaces, while finite element models resolve pore network geometry and reactive transport. These outputs will inform macroscale hydrological models incorporating soil structure heterogeneity and microbial activity. The computational demand arises from the need to simulate thousands of stochastic pore-scale domains, perform ensemble MD runs across mineralogical compositions, and iteratively optimize parameters using machine learning. By leveraging GPU-accelerated HPC resources, we aim to quantify how microscale processes propagate to observable soil behavior, such as nutrient leaching or carbon stabilization. Outcomes will provide predictive tools for optimizing soil management practices, including precision fertilizer application and soil amendment strategies under climate variability. This work directly supports agricultural sustainability by bridging molecular mechanisms to field-scale outcomes, addressing urgent needs in food security and climate-resilient soil systems. The resulting open-source models will enable researchers to explore soil chemistry-physics interactions at unprecedented resolution, fostering innovation in soil health monitoring and intervention design.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and physical principles to research and analysis concerning the nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instruction in soil and fluid mechanics, mineralogy, sedimentology, thermodynamics, geomorphology, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: Soil microbial communities play a critical role in agricultural productivity through nutrient cycling, pathogen suppression, and soil structure modulation. However, predicting their functional dynamics under varying management practices remains a major challenge due to the complexity of biotic and abiotic interactions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model soil microbiome responses to agricultural interventions, integrating multi-omics data with physicochemical soil properties. Current limitations in computational scalability prevent the analysis of terabyte-scale metagenomic datasets from longitudinal field experiments, hindering mechanistic insights into community assembly and metabolic networks. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining genome-resolved metagenomics, agent-based modeling, and machine learning to simulate microbial community trajectories across soil types and management regimes. Metagenomic sequencing data from replicated field trials—comparing organic, conventional, and integrated practices—will be processed through containerized bioinformatics workflows optimized for parallelization. Network inference algorithms will map cross-kingdom interactions, while physics-informed neural networks will predict moisture and nutrient flux impacts on community stability. Agent-based models, parameterized with strain-level genomic traits, will simulate emergent behaviors at plot-to-landscape scales. The HPC environment is essential for deploying ensemble models across parameter spaces and temporal resolutions impractical for local clusters. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking microbial guild dynamics to crop yield variations and soil carbon retention metrics. This resource will enable the design of microbiome-informed soil management strategies, directly addressing agricultural sustainability challenges. By resolving scale-dependent interactions in soil systems, the project aims to advance precision agriculture tools while contributing computational methodologies adaptable to other microbial ecosystems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on application of microbiological theory and methods to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions, and the biological components and effects of soil management strategies. Includes instruction in microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, soil chemistry and physics as related to biological characteristics, and environmental science.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) represent a critical public health challenge, with treatment outcomes often hindered by the complex interplay of genetic, neurobiological, and socioenvironmental factors. Current approaches to predicting treatment response and optimizing intervention strategies lack the computational power to integrate multi-dimensional datasets, limiting personalized care. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that bridge these gaps, enhancing precision in addiction counseling. We propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze large-scale datasets, including genomic data, electronic health records, and real-time behavioral data from wearable devices. ML algorithms will identify biomarkers and psychosocial predictors of treatment adherence and relapse, while ABM simulations will model population-level dynamics of substance use spread and recovery within social networks. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-resolution neuroimaging data, running parallelized simulations of intervention scenarios, and training deep learning models on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel risk stratification profiles, optimized intervention timing strategies, and dynamic models of counselor-client interactions that improve therapeutic outcomes. By integrating computational psychiatry with clinical counseling frameworks, this research will provide actionable insights for tailoring evidence-based interventions, training counselors in data-informed decision-making, and allocating community resources efficiently. The project aligns with the program’s mission to advance addiction science through interdisciplinary innovation, directly contributing to reduced relapse rates and enhanced quality of life for individuals and families affected by SUDs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to help prevent substance abuse, counsel individuals and families with drug and alcohol problems, and perform intervention and therapeutic services for persons suffering from addiction. Includes instruction in individual and group counseling skills, psychology of addiction, sociology, crisis intervention, substance abuse identification methodologies, substance abuse treatment modalities, substance abuse prevention and treatment resources, pharmacology and behavioral aspects of abused substances, treatment evaluation, patient observation and education, group dynamics, professional standards and ethics, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven instructional tools for students with specific learning disabilities (SLDs). Current challenges in special education include the time-intensive process of designing individualized interventions and the limited scalability of traditional diagnostic and pedagogical methods. To address this, we propose a computational approach that integrates multimodal student data—including academic performance records, behavioral observations, and neuropsychological assessment results—to model learning trajectories and predict optimal intervention strategies. Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on anonymized longitudinal datasets from K-12 students with SLDs (e.g., dyslexia, dyscalculia) to identify patterns in skill acquisition and barriers to learning. Computational simulations will then test the efficacy of hypothetical intervention sequences under varied conditions, enabling rapid iteration of strategies tailored to individual learner profiles. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (spanning 10,000+ student-years of records) and running complex, parallelized models that account for dynamic interactions between cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors. Expected outcomes include 1) predictive frameworks to assist educators in prioritizing intervention targets during Individualized Education Program (IEP) development, 2) a simulation toolkit for pre-service teacher training that models student responses to evidence-based strategies, and 3) open-source code for scalable analysis of special education data. By reducing the computational bottlenecks inherent in processing heterogeneous educational data, this work aims to bridge gaps between educational research and classroom practice, ultimately enhancing the capacity of educators to deliver timely, personalized support for students with SLDs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Specific Learning Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with specific learning disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with specific learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with specific learning disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the precision and efficiency of industrial radiologic technologies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex radiation-matter interactions and optimize nondestructive testing (NDT) workflows. Current limitations in simulating real-world radiologic processes—such as x-ray fluorescence analysis, gamma-ray tomography, and real-time thickness monitoring—stem from the computational intensity of modeling stochastic particle interactions, multi-scale material behaviors, and dynamic industrial environments. Traditional methods often rely on simplified approximations that reduce accuracy, particularly when analyzing heterogeneous materials or operating near detection limits. To address this, we propose developing a multi-physics computational framework combining Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations, finite element analysis for material response, and machine learning-driven inverse modeling. The HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of GPU-accelerated Geant4 simulations for tracking high-energy photon interactions, coupled with ANSYS-based stress-strain predictions in materials undergoing radiographic inspection. A convolutional neural network will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to automate defect detection in NDT imaging, reducing human error in industrial quality control. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for optimizing radioisotope source configurations, improved defect classification accuracy in composite materials, and adaptive algorithms for continuous thickness monitoring in high-speed manufacturing. By integrating these computational tools, the project aims to establish a digital twin platform for industrial radiologic systems, enabling virtual prototyping of inspection protocols and real-time decision support. This work will directly enhance the reliability of infrastructure inspection in energy and aerospace sectors while providing open-source simulation modules to strengthen education in radiologic technology programs. The requested computing resources are critical for managing petabyte-scale datasets from synchrotron collaborations and achieving the millisecond-scale latency required for closed-loop thickness control systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of industrial and research testing equipment using radioisotopes.
