Includes instruction in x-ray analysis of materials, nondestructive testing and inspection of materials, and continuous measurement of paper or metal thickness.

abstract: The study of bioacoustic pattern formation in insects represents an underexplored niche at the intersection of biomechanics, behavioral ecology, and nonlinear dynamics. Many insects produce complex acoustic signals for communication without specialized sound-producing organs, relying instead on interactions between body structures, muscle activation, and environmental feedback. This project seeks to model the self-organizing mechanisms underlying these acoustic behaviors in non-model arthropods, particularly stridulating beetles and tremulating spiders, whose signal generation lacks dedicated anatomical adaptations. The central challenge lies in simulating multi-scale physical interactions—from exoskeletal resonances to limb kinematics—and their coupling with neural control networks under natural conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for implementing iterative, agent-based simulations that integrate finite-element modeling of chitinous structures, fluid-structure interactions during motion, and reinforcement learning algorithms modeling adaptive signal optimization. Each simulation will parameterize species-specific morphologies derived from micro-CT scans and incorporate field-recorded environmental variables (substrate vibrations, airflow). Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of universal physical constraints governing acoustic signal emergence in anatomically generalized species, (2) quantification of selective pressures driving convergence in signaling strategies across phylogenetically distant taxa, and (3) predictive frameworks for how anthropogenic noise pollution disrupts non-specialized acoustic communication systems. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated physics engines for real-time simulation of elastic wave propagation and machine learning libraries to train neural networks mimicking evolutionary optimization processes. By bridging zoology, materials science, and complex systems theory, this work will establish new paradigms for understanding the evolution of biological signaling in the absence of dedicated sensory organs while providing scalable models for bio-inspired acoustic engineering applications.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the biology of animal species and phyla, with reference to their molecular and cellular systems, anatomy, physiology, and behavior. Includes instruction in molecular and cell biology, microbiology, anatomy and physiology, ecology and behavior, evolutionary biology, and applications to specific species and phyla.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational design of next-generation heterogeneous catalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis. A critical challenge in engineering chemistry lies in optimizing catalytic materials to enhance reaction efficiency, selectivity, and stability under industrial conditions, particularly for processes central to petrochemical refining and renewable energy applications. Traditional experimental approaches to catalyst development are resource-intensive and often fail to resolve atomic-scale reaction mechanisms or predict long-term material degradation. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and machine learning (ML)-driven surrogate models. These methods will enable high-throughput screening of transition metal alloys and metal-organic framework (MOF) catalysts, with a focus on surface reactivity, adsorption energetics, and thermal stability. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of simulating complex reaction pathways (e.g., C–H activation, CO₂ hydrogenation) across diverse catalytic surfaces and operating conditions. Large-scale DFT calculations will parametrize ML models to predict catalytic performance metrics, while AIMD simulations will probe dynamic behavior under realistic temperature and pressure regimes. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel catalyst candidates with reduced noble metal content, atomistic insights into deactivation mechanisms, and validated protocols for accelerating materials discovery. This work aligns with broader goals of reducing energy consumption in chemical manufacturing and enabling carbon-neutral processes. By integrating computational chemistry with engineering principles, the project will establish a predictive pipeline for catalyst design, directly supporting advancements in chemical and petroleum engineering. The requested resources will sustain ongoing simulations of 10,000+ material configurations, enabling data generation at scales inaccessible via laboratory experimentation alone.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of chemical principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, such as development of electronic materials, solid-state science and technology, polymers, ceramics, and biomaterials. Includes instruction in physical chemistry, organic chemistry, materials science, chemical processes and systems, chemical reaction engineering, biochemical engineering, engineering mathematics, classical and modern physics, and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the synergistic effects of multi-modal holistic therapies on neuroimmune signaling pathways using computational modeling and large-scale data integration. Despite growing interest in integrative health approaches—such as combined mindfulness, herbal interventions, and somatic practices—the mechanisms underlying their systemic interactions remain poorly understood. A key challenge lies in disentangling the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between these therapies, physiological stress responses, and immune modulation, which operate across multiple temporal and biological scales. To address this, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale model integrating transcriptomic, metabolomic, and clinical data from longitudinal studies of chronic stress patients undergoing personalized integrative regimens. The computational framework will combine network analysis, agent-based modeling of immune cell populations, and machine learning to identify critical nodes where combined therapies exert amplified or emergent effects. This requires processing complex datasets spanning cortisol rhythms, cytokine profiles, epigenetic aging markers, and patient-reported outcomes (n ≈ 2.5 TB initial dataset). Key technical hurdles include real-time parameter optimization for cross-domain interactions and simulating whole-body pharmacokinetics of herbal compounds with neural feedback loops. Expected outcomes include: 1) predictive models of therapy sequencing for optimal neuroimmune regulation, 2) identification of biomarkers signaling synergistic versus additive effects, and 3) a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for testing hypothetical treatment combinations. The work directly addresses a gap in evidence-based frameworks for personalized integrative health, while advancing computational methods for analyzing emergent properties in complex, patient-specific interventions. Successful implementation will require HPC resources for parallelized model training, large-memory nodes for genome-scale network analyses, and GPU acceleration for deep learning components.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the holistic interconnectedness of physical, psychological, social, spiritual, and environmental well-being and that integrates aspects of alternative, complementary, and conventional medicine to alleviate illness and promote, maintain, and optimize wellness. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, alternative diagnostic and healing methods, aromatherapy, biofeedback, energy medicine, environmental psychology, ethics, health coaching, herbal medicine, mind-body medicine, mindfulness, nutrition, somatic bodywork, and stress management.

abstract: This project seeks to address computational bottlenecks in the creation and optimization of dynamic, high-resolution visual content for emerging graphic communications platforms. As demand grows for immersive, real-time media in areas such as augmented reality (AR) advertising, interactive digital publications, and adaptive branding systems, existing workflows struggle to process complex vector-raster hybrid assets at scale. The research focuses on developing parallelizable algorithms for intelligent asset optimization, leveraging machine learning to automate format conversion, resolution scaling, and color space harmonization across multi-device ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of industry-standard design files (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite outputs) and for simulating rendering performance across heterogeneous end-user hardware configurations. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic quality-of-service predictions with graph-based representations of design element interdependencies, enabling predictive optimization before asset deployment. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for automated graphic system adaptability, reducing manual rework in cross-platform publishing by an estimated 40-60% based on preliminary benchmarks. This work directly responds to industry needs identified through partnerships with digital media publishers and AR development studios, who require scalable solutions for maintaining visual fidelity across increasingly fragmented display technologies. The requested computing resources will enable comparative analysis of optimization strategies at unprecedented parameter scales, particularly for temporal design elements in motion graphics. By establishing computational best practices for next-generation graphic workflows, this project aims to bridge persistent gaps between creative production pipelines and technical deployment constraints in communication design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in graphic communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for real-time regulatory compliance auditing in decentralized financial ecosystems. The proliferation of blockchain-based transactions, smart contracts, and tokenized assets has created a critical gap in accounting practices: traditional auditing tools cannot efficiently analyze the velocity, complexity, and interdependencies of decentralized financial data streams. This research addresses the challenge of automating compliance verification—such as anti-money laundering (AML) checks, tax liability tracing, and asset custody validation—across heterogeneous blockchain networks while adhering to jurisdictionally fragmented regulatory standards. The computational approach combines graph neural networks (GNNs) to model transactional networks with transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) to dynamically map regulatory texts to on-chain activity patterns. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of multi-modal models on petabytes of transactional data (e.g., Ethereum, Solana) synchronized with global regulatory databases. Key innovations include a anomaly detection system that flags non-compliant subgraphs in real time and a protocol-agnostic compliance scoring engine. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for auditors to simulate regulatory scenarios across virtualized ledger environments, significantly reducing manual review workloads. The project will advance accounting methodologies for web3 economies by creating auditable machine learning pipelines that maintain chain-of-custody integrity while scaling with transaction volume. This work bridges accounting ethics, cryptographic verification, and computational social science—offering a template for next-generation assurance services in decentralized finance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the profession of accounting and to perform related business functions. Includes instruction in accounting principles and theory, financial accounting, managerial accounting, cost accounting, budget control, tax accounting, legal aspects of accounting, auditing, reporting procedures, statement analysis, planning and consulting, business information systems, accounting research methods, professional standards and ethics, and applications to specific for-profit, public, and non-profit organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurocognitive and behavioral correlates of contemplative practices using advanced computational modeling to bridge gaps between subjective experiential reports and objective physiological data. While prior research has established basic neural signatures of meditation and mindfulness, fundamental questions remain about how individual differences in cognitive traits, cultural context, and practice modalities shape the dynamic interplay between conscious experience, attention regulation, and autonomic nervous system responses. The study will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets—including high-density EEG recordings, heart rate variability metrics, and first-person phenomenological annotations—collected from 200 participants engaged in diverse contemplative protocols. A novel computational pipeline will integrate dynamical systems modeling to characterize phase transitions in attentional states, machine learning classifiers to map neural patterns to self-reported experiential qualities, and network neuroscience approaches to identify practice-specific functional connectivity profiles. Crucially, the HPC environment will enable large-scale simulations testing theoretical frameworks about metacognitive resource allocation during sustained introspection, as well as Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify cross-cultural variations in contemplative efficacy. Expected outcomes include a validated computational ontology for classifying contemplative states, predictive models linking neurophysiological markers to training outcomes, and open-source tools for real-time biofeedback in contemplative interventions. By synthesizing methods from computational neuroscience, anthropology of consciousness, and cognitive phenomenology, this work aims to establish a rigorous empirical foundation for understanding how contemplative practices modulate human cognition—a critical step toward developing personalized mental health interventions and advancing interdisciplinary dialogue between science and contemplative traditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophical, psychological, and scientific bases of human contemplative experience. Includes instruction in cognitive science, meditation, mindfulness, neuroscience, philosophy, psychology, and religion.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of anthropogenic impacts on terrestrial hydrological systems and their feedbacks with biogeochemical cycles, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, multi-scale interactions between land use, subsurface hydrology, and contaminant transport. Rapid urbanization and agricultural intensification have altered natural hydrologic pathways, increasing risks of groundwater contamination and ecosystem degradation. However, existing models often lack the spatial resolution and computational capacity to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution satellite remote sensing, geophysical surveys, and long-term geochemical monitoring—into predictive frameworks. To address this gap, we propose a coupled modeling approach combining 3D hydrogeological simulations with machine learning-driven analysis of spatial-temporal biogeochemical data. The HPC resources will enable (1) parallelized finite element modeling of subsurface flow and contaminant dispersion at meter-scale resolution across watersheds and (2) training of convolutional neural networks to identify contaminant source zones from multi-spectral satellite imagery and ground-based sensor arrays. By dynamically linking these components within an HPC-optimized workflow, the project will quantify how evolving land management practices alter contaminant mobility under projected climate scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include improved predictive capacity for pollutant thresholds in vulnerable aquifers, spatially explicit risk maps for stakeholders, and open-source computational tools for scaling process-based hydrology to regional systems. This work directly supports sustainable groundwater management goals while advancing methodological integration of GIS, remote sensing, and physical modeling—a critical need in Earth and Environmental Sciences research. The requested allocation will provide essential capacity for data assimilation, model calibration, and uncertainty quantification across billion-cell domains, which exceed the limits of institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Gay/Lesbian Studies by analyzing large-scale cultural and textual datasets that document LGBTQ+ community formation, resistance, and cultural production from the mid-20th century onward. The research problem centers on the fragmented and often ephemeral nature of historical LGBTQ+ materials, which complicates efforts to systematically trace thematic shifts in identity discourse, artistic expression, and community-building strategies. Current methodologies in queer historiography and cultural studies rely heavily on qualitative close readings, limiting scalability and the identification of macro-level patterns. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, machine learning, and network modeling to process digitized archives of LGBTQ+ periodicals, oral histories, visual art metadata, and literary works. Key tasks include training custom NLP models to detect evolving terminologies related to identity and activism, mapping thematic networks across time and geographic regions, and visualizing the intersection of artistic movements with sociopolitical events. HPC resources are critical for handling the volume and complexity of multilingual, multimedia datasets (e.g., 50,000+ pages of scanned newsletters, 10,000+ art metadata entries) and for running resource-intensive processes like transformer-based topic modeling and graph-based community detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of analyzed materials, new frameworks for quantifying cultural resilience in marginalized communities, and data-driven insights into how subcultural narratives influenced broader societal perceptions of LGBTQ+ rights. By integrating computational methods with queer theory, this project aims to redefine scalability in humanities-focused LGBTQ+ research while preserving the nuance of lived experiences. The results will directly inform curricula in Gender and Sexuality Studies and provide replicable tools for researchers examining under-documented sociocultural movements.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on homosexuality in history, society, politics, and cultural life; usually with an emphasis on the modern emergence of gays and lesbians as a sociocultural minority movement, the identification of social, literary, and artistic themes and the definition of, and public policy and legal issues surrounding, the gay and lesbian community.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop dynamic, agent-based simulations of emergency scenarios in K-12 educational environments, addressing gaps in traditional school safety protocols. Current approaches often rely on static models or historical data, failing to account for real-time behavioral variability, spatial complexities, and evolving threats. By simulating crowd dynamics during emergencies—such as fires, active shooter events, or natural disasters—this research aims to model interactions between building layouts, student-staff population densities, and individual decision-making patterns under stress. Computational methods will integrate geospatial data from school blueprints, behavioral parameters derived from crisis psychology literature, and stochastic event triggers to generate thousands of scenario iterations. Machine learning algorithms will optimize agent behavior rules, while parallel computing will enable scalable simulations across diverse virtual environments. The project will validate models against empirical evacuation studies and anonymized incident reports. Expected outcomes include identifying critical bottlenecks in existing safety designs, quantifying the impact of architectural modifications on evacuation efficiency, and generating evidence-based recommendations for adaptive emergency response protocols. By bridging computational modeling, behavioral science, and educational facility design, this work advances a novel framework for proactive risk mitigation in schools, directly supporting the “school safety and health issues” pillar of Education, General. The proposed HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, real-time agent interactions, and large-scale scenario testing required to produce actionable insights for policymakers and school administrators.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory and practice of learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methodologies for analyzing and simulating material behaviors, structural dynamics, and cultural patterns in traditional craft practices. While craft disciplines such as textile weaving, ceramic glazing, and woodworking rely on embodied knowledge and manual techniques, emerging computational tools present opportunities to model complex interactions between materials, tools, and environmental factors. The research problem centers on bridging gaps between empirical craft practices and data-driven modeling, particularly in scenarios where traditional experimentation is resource-intensive, time-consuming, or limited in scalability. For example, simulating the nonlinear stress-strain relationships in handwoven textiles under dynamic loads or predicting pigment dispersion in layered glazes requires iterative, high-resolution simulations. The project proposes a hybrid approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML)-based pattern recognition, and agent-based modeling to replicate artisan decision-making processes in digital environments. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of multi-material systems, training of neural networks on high-dimensional datasets of historical craft artifacts, and 3D rendering of intricate design geometries. Outcomes will include open-source computational tools tailored to craft practitioners, enabling predictive modeling of material outcomes and generative design exploration. Additionally, the project aims to digitize and analyze underrepresented folk art traditions through large-scale pattern clustering, identifying culturally significant motifs while respecting ethical frameworks for data sovereignty. By integrating computational rigor with craft epistemologies, this work seeks to expand creative possibilities for artisans, enhance pedagogical resources for craft preservation, and foster interdisciplinary dialogues between technical computing and tactile art forms. The requested HPC allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed data processing, and storage for terabyte-scale artifact libraries, which are computationally prohibitive on local infrastructure.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Crafts/ Craft Design, Folk Art and Artisanry
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the aesthetics, techniques, and creative processes for designing and fashioning objects in one or more of the handcraft or folk art traditions, and that prepares individuals to create in any of these media.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance precision and sustainability in taxidermy practice through advanced modeling of organic material degradation, biomechanical stress distribution in reconstructed specimens, and environmental interaction simulations. Traditional taxidermy relies on empirical, labor-intensive techniques for preserving and mounting specimens, with limited quantitative tools to predict long-term structural stability or material interactions under varying display conditions. The research problem centers on addressing these gaps by creating predictive models to optimize preservation methods, armature design, and environmental resilience, thereby reducing material waste and improving the longevity of taxidermy artifacts. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress patterns in taxidermy forms under dynamic loads, machine learning algorithms to correlate tissue preservation efficacy with chemical treatment variables, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model humidity and temperature effects on organic-composite material interfaces. Multiscale 3D scans of avian and mammalian specimens will inform anatomically accurate digital twins, enabling iterative virtual prototyping of armatures. The computational workflow will integrate open-source biomechanics libraries with custom Python-based tools for parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of material property profiles for taxidermy substrates, predictive analytics pipelines for treatment protocol selection, and GPU-accelerated visualization tools for training taxidermists in virtual sculpting workflows. By establishing quantitative frameworks for historically qualitative practices, this interdisciplinary effort bridges craft traditions with computational material science, offering scalable solutions for ethical specimen use, artifact conservation, and climate-resilient design in cultural heritage contexts. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling high-resolution volumetric datasets, parallelized degradation simulations across heterogeneous material matrices, and real-time rendering of complex biological geometries during interactive modeling phases.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to reproduce life-like three-dimensional representations of living animals for permanent display using elements of the deceased specimen(s) as well as artificial materials, and to manage taxidermy services and businesses. Includes instruction in specimen grading and selection, caping and fleshing, preservation procedures, tanning, drying, measurements, form and armature construction, carpentry and woodworking, molding and casting, drawing, sculptural techniques, painting and finishing techniques, basic business operations, customer communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of dynamic, adaptive simulation tools for theatrical production design, addressing the growing complexity of integrating real-time environmental, acoustic, and visual effects in live performance spaces. Current workflows in technical theatre rely on fragmented software and manual adjustments, limiting the ability to model interactions between variables such as moving set pieces, variable acoustics, and programmable lighting in a unified virtual environment. This research aims to create a computational framework that simulates these interdependent systems at scale, enabling predictive analysis of design choices under performance conditions. The core challenge lies in modeling real-time physical interactions (e.g., sound wave propagation through morphing set geometries, light scattering across kinetic surfaces) while maintaining the low-latency response required for iterative design testing. Proposed methods include parallelized finite element analysis for acoustic simulations, GPU-accelerated ray tracing for lighting interactions, and agent-based modeling for crowd-sourced sightline validation across auditorium configurations. By deploying these computationally intensive processes on HPC clusters, the project will generate datasets correlating material properties, spatial configurations, and equipment parameters with perceptual outcomes (e.g., audience sightline clarity, acoustic intelligibility). Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for theatre designers to optimize resource allocation during pre-production, reducing material waste and technical rehearsals. The work also advances performative computing applications by formalizing metrics for human-centric environmental simulation, with potential cross-disciplinary impacts in immersive entertainment and experiential architecture. This computational approach directly supports the program’s mission to integrate emerging technologies into theatrical practice while preserving artistic intentionality in technically constrained environments.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Technical Theatre/ Theatre Design and Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic, technical and dramatic principles and techniques to the communication of dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through technical theatre methods. Includes instruction in set design, lighting design, sound effects, theatre acoustics, scene painting, property management, costume design, and technical direction and production and use of computer applications to support these functions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting biodiversity loss and ecosystem destabilization under accelerating habitat fragmentation and climate change in tropical rainforests. Current conservation models often fail to integrate fine-scale species interactions, landscape connectivity, and epidemiological risks into unified frameworks, limiting their utility for adaptive management. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop spatially explicit, multi-agent simulation models that integrate empirical data on 127 vertebrate species across a 50,000 km² fragmented Amazonian landscape. The computational approach will couple individual-based models of animal movement and population dynamics with network analyses of habitat corridors and disease transmission risks influenced by human-wildlife interface zones. Machine learning pipelines will process remote sensing data (30m resolution) to parameterize vegetation shifts and anthropogenic disturbance gradients from 2000–2025. Each simulation will incorporate evolutionary adaptations in thermal tolerance thresholds derived from comparative genomics analyses of historical climate stressors. The HPC environment is essential for running ensemble simulations across 500+ climate scenarios while maintaining the <100m spatial granularity required to model microhabitat refugia. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone habitat patches with disproportionate impacts on regional biodiversity persistence, (2) predictive maps of zoonotic disease hotspots linked to fragmentation-induced wildlife displacement, and (3) optimization algorithms for corridor networks that balance species movement needs with epidemiological containment. Results will directly inform the Amazon Sustainable Landscapes Program’s $60M conservation strategy while advancing theoretical frameworks for resilience thresholds in coupled human-natural systems. The computational workflows will be packaged into open-access modules to strengthen HPC capacity in under-resourced tropical ecology research communities.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences to the specific problems of biodiversity, species preservation, ecological sustainability, and habitat fragmentation in the face of advancing human social, economic, and industrial pressures. Includes instruction in ecology, environmental science, biological systems, extinction theory, human-animal and human-plant interaction, ecosystem science and management, wetland conservation, field biology, forest and wildlife biology, and natural history.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision manufacturing processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model, simulate, and optimize advanced fabrication techniques. Precision production trades rely on the integration of technical illustration, material science, and multi-axis machining to create components with sub-millimeter tolerances. However, current methods for predicting tool wear, thermal deformation, and material behavior during high-speed machining lack the resolution and scalability needed for next-generation applications, particularly when working with advanced alloys or composite materials. Traditional experimental approaches are cost-prohibitive and time-intensive, while existing computational models fail to capture the multi-physics interactions inherent to these processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate machining dynamics at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of tool-workpiece interactions across diverse material systems, incorporating real-time thermal gradients, stress distributions, and microstructural evolution. A convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on simulation outputs to predict optimal machining parameters, minimizing defects while maximizing tool lifespan. The project will validate models against experimental data from CNC milling and laser engraving processes, iteratively refining predictive accuracy. Outcomes will include open-source simulation workflows tailored for precision production applications and a database of validated material response profiles. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping, this research aims to reduce material waste by an estimated 15–20% in small-batch manufacturing scenarios while improving the precision of complex geometries. The computational tools developed will directly support workforce training programs in advanced manufacturing, providing interactive visualization modules for technical illustration integration. This work establishes a foundation for data-driven process optimization in precision trades, addressing a critical need in industries transitioning to smart manufacturing paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in creating products using precision crafting and technical illustration.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to optimize resource allocation in large-scale, dynamic manufacturing systems under uncertainty. Modern manufacturing environments face challenges in balancing production efficiency, energy consumption, and operational costs while adapting to fluctuating demand, supply chain disruptions, and equipment variability. Traditional analytical methods often fail to address the combinatorial complexity and real-time decision-making requirements of these systems. We propose a hybrid approach combining parallelized discrete-event simulation, stochastic optimization models, and machine learning to enable responsive, data-driven resource allocation. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simultaneously evaluate thousands of production scenarios through massively parallel simulations coded in Julia and Python. These simulations will incorporate probabilistic models of machine failures, material flow constraints, and workforce availability derived from industrial case studies. Multi-objective optimization algorithms—including modified branch-and-bound and genetic algorithms—will then identify Pareto-optimal solutions for resource distribution across production lines. A neural network surrogate model will be trained on simulation outputs to enable rapid scenario evaluation during operational deployment. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the exponential state space of manufacturing systems with >50 interdependent workstations and hourly decision intervals over quarterly planning horizons. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for optimizing equipment utilization, labor scheduling, and energy use in flexible manufacturing environments, with validation planned through collaboration with automotive component manufacturers. Results will advance the integration of operations research methods with HPC capabilities in industrial engineering, providing a template for responsive manufacturing system design that could reduce idle time by 15-25% and energy waste by 10-20% in target applications. The computational framework and datasets will be made available to the manufacturing research community through open-source repositories.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, and implementation of manufacturing systems. Includes instruction in materials science and engineering, manufacturing processes, process engineering, assembly and product engineering, manufacturing systems design, and manufacturing competitiveness.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociolinguistic dynamics of understudied sign languages in digitally mediated environments, focusing on how emerging technologies shape language evolution and accessibility for Deaf communities. While sign languages are critical to cultural identity and communication, many remain under-documented, particularly in regions with limited institutional support. The research addresses two interrelated gaps: (1) the absence of large-scale computational models capable of analyzing visual-spatial linguistic features in real-time interactions, and (2) the need to quantify how digital platforms influence sign language vitality and intergenerational transmission. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will process multimodal datasets—including video recordings of naturalistic sign language use, motion-capture data, and user-generated content from Deaf-led online communities—to identify patterns in lexical innovation, grammatical variation, and cross-sign language contact. Computational methods will integrate 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial-temporal feature extraction, graph-based algorithms to model community interaction networks, and agent-based simulations to project language shift scenarios under varying technological adoption rates. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for sign language corpus analysis, predictive models of lexical convergence in digital contexts, and empirically grounded recommendations for inclusive platform design. By centering computational rigor on marginalized linguistic systems, this work advances interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of language preservation, human-computer interaction, and social equity, offering methodological innovations applicable to other embodied communication modalities. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the project’s terabyte-scale visual data and computationally intensive simulations, which exceed the capacity of standard university computing clusters.
cip_title: Linguistic, Comparative, and Related Language Studies and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in linguistic, comparative, and related language studies and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of legal texts, policies, and historical records central to Tribal and Indigenous law. The research addresses a critical gap in legal scholarship: the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze the complex interplay between federal Indian law, tribal legal systems, and Indigenous rights frameworks. Traditional legal research methods, which rely heavily on manual case review and qualitative interpretation, struggle to systematically map the evolution of legal doctrines, identify patterns in judicial decision-making, or trace the sociolegal impacts of colonial legal structures on Indigenous communities. To address this, the project proposes an interdisciplinary computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning (ML) to process large corpora of legal documents, treaties, court opinions, and tribal codes. Key objectives include developing custom NLP pipelines to extract relational data (e.g., citations, jurisdictional overlaps, treaty violations) and training ML models to detect latent biases or inconsistencies in judicial reasoning across federal-tribal legal interfaces. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale and complexity of datasets, which span centuries of legal texts and multilingual Indigenous language materials requiring advanced preprocessing. Anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-access computational toolkit for legal scholars and tribal policymakers to analyze precedent networks and policy impacts, (2) data visualizations illuminating systemic disparities in federal-tribal case law, and (3) a foundational dataset for comparative studies on Indigenous rights recognition. By integrating computational rigor with critical legal theory, this work aims to empower Tribal nations with evidence-based strategies for legal advocacy and policy reform while establishing a methodological precedent for computational legal studies in underrepresented juridical traditions.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting federal Indian law, tribal law and policy, and Indigenous peoples' human rights.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of computational analytics into pre-professional art therapy training and research. While art therapy traditionally emphasizes qualitative, human-centered analysis of creative expression, emerging computational methods offer novel ways to analyze patterns in art-based interventions, correlate therapeutic outcomes with visual or behavioral data, and model the neurocognitive impacts of art-making. However, pre-art therapy programs currently lack infrastructure to explore these approaches at scale. This project addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to analyze large datasets of digitized artwork, biometric data, and clinical outcomes from art therapy sessions. Using GPU-accelerated machine learning models, we will train neural networks to identify visual and compositional features in artwork (e.g., color use, spatial organization, symbolic content) that correlate with self-reported mental health metrics and physiological markers (e.g., heart rate variability, EEG recordings). Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how iterative art-making processes may influence stress regulation pathways. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale multimedia datasets, optimize deep learning architectures, and run parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models linking artistic choices to therapeutic effects, (2) open-source tools for quantitative art therapy analysis, and (3) foundational datasets to bridge computational and clinical art therapy research. By embedding computational literacy into pre-art therapy training, this work aims to equip future practitioners with data-informed strategies for personalizing interventions while maintaining the humanistic core of the discipline. The requested HPC allocation will directly support model training, data storage, and scalable processing—critical needs for pioneering this interdisciplinary synthesis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: Maternal and child health outcomes are shaped by complex interactions between biological, social, and environmental determinants, yet existing models often fail to capture these multidimensional relationships at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large, integrated datasets spanning clinical records, socioeconomic indicators, environmental exposures, and public health program participation across diverse populations. The research will develop computational models to identify critical risk factors for adverse pregnancy outcomes, childhood chronic conditions, and disparities in healthcare access. Using machine learning algorithms optimized for HPC environments, including ensemble methods and neural networks, we will analyze longitudinal data from 2.5 million maternal-child dyads across five U.S. regions. These analyses will be coupled with agent-based simulations to model the population-level impacts of proposed interventions, such as nutritional support programs or prenatal care policy changes. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to manage high-dimensional data integration, real-time geospatial mapping of health resource availability, and sensitivity analyses across simulated scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize high-risk populations, evidence-based frameworks for tailoring community health initiatives, and policy simulations quantifying the potential health equity impacts of legislative proposals. By elucidating how structural determinants interact with biological factors, this work will provide novel insights for reducing perinatal mortality, addressing childhood obesity disparities, and optimizing resource allocation in public health systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale health data while maintaining privacy-preserving federated learning architectures across institutional partners. This project directly aligns with national maternal health equity goals and advances computational methodologies for translational public health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in understanding the electronic structure and reactivity of transition metal complexes with non-innocent ligands, a class of compounds central to catalytic processes and energy storage applications. These systems exhibit complex multiconfigurational electronic ground states and dynamic ligand-metal interactions that are poorly described by conventional computational methods, limiting predictive design of novel inorganic catalysts. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve short-lived intermediates or disentangle overlapping spectroscopic signatures, necessitating advanced theoretical approaches. This project will employ high-level ab initio calculations, including multireference methods such as CASSCF and NEVPT2, to model electronic states and spin-crossover phenomena in iron- and cobalt-based coordination complexes. Density functional theory (DFT) with hybrid functionals will supplement these calculations for geometry optimizations and thermodynamic analyses. To address solvent and solid-state effects, explicit solvent molecular dynamics simulations and periodic boundary condition models will be implemented. The computational workflow requires significant resources due to the need for large active spaces (up to 18 orbitals), relativistic corrections for heavy atoms, and statistical sampling of configurational space. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into redox-induced ligand non-innocence in catalytic cycles, (2) predictive models for tuning metal-ligand charge transfer transitions via substituent effects, and (3) validation of computed spectroscopic parameters (XAS, EPR) against experimental collaborators’ data. The requested high-performance computing allocation will enable systematic studies across diverse ligand architectures, providing fundamental guidelines for designing air-stable coordination complexes with targeted redox potentials and photophysical properties. This work directly advances inorganic chemistry by bridging gaps between synthetic approaches, quantum mechanical descriptions, and functional material development, with potential applications in sustainable oxidation catalysis and next-generation battery materials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the elements and their compounds, other than the hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Includes instruction in the characterization and synthesis of non-carbon molecules, including their structure and their bonding, conductivity, and reactive properties; research techniques such as spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and photoelectron analysis; and the study of specific compounds, such as transition metals, and compounds composed of inorganic and organic molecules.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the diachronic evolution of syntactic structures across understudied Romance languages and dialects using computational modeling, with a focus on identifying cross-linguistic patterns of grammaticalization and contact-induced change. The central challenge lies in analyzing large, heterogeneous corpora spanning medieval manuscripts, modern regional variants, and oral narratives—materials that are often fragmentary, non-standardized, or available only in low-resolution scans. To address this, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and dialectal texts, including custom transformer-based models for morphological disambiguation and dependency parsing across Occitan, Sardinian, and Rhaeto-Romance varieties. These models will be trained on newly digitized materials from archival sources alongside existing corpora, requiring distributed computing for hyperparameter tuning and ensemble learning. A second computational strand will apply agent-based modeling to simulate language contact scenarios between Romance and non-Romance languages in medieval Mediterranean trade networks, incorporating sociolinguistic variables derived from historical records. The project’s HPC requirements stem from the need to process terabyte-scale textual data, run parallelized phylogenetic analyses of syntactic features, and execute thousands of contact scenario simulations with varying parameters. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a computational framework for analyzing non-standard Romance languages, 2) evidence-based revisions to existing models of syntactic change in contact situations, and 3) open-access tools for paleographic digitization workflows. This work bridges computational linguistics with philological scholarship, offering new methodologies for analyzing linguistic variation while addressing critical gaps in Romance language documentation. The resource-intensive nature of training domain-specific NLP models on historical texts and running large-scale simulations of language evolution makes HPC infrastructure essential to achieving these objectives.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Romance languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the emergent dynamics of decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) operating in blockchain ecosystems, with a focus on governance efficiency and resource allocation transparency. While DAOs represent a transformative business model, their rapid evolution and technical complexity have outpaced traditional accounting and management methodologies, creating gaps in auditing practices, decision accountability, and performance evaluation. The study addresses this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate DAO operations at scale, integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with real-time blockchain data streams. Researchers will construct multi-agent simulations that replicate token-based voting mechanisms, treasury management workflows, and smart contract interactions, incorporating stochastic variables for market volatility and participant behavior. Parallelized network analysis will map governance influence patterns, while machine learning models trained on historical DAO proposal data will predict systemic risks such as voter apathy or fund misallocation. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets from Ethereum and Solana blockchains, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time consensus protocol emulation. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of DAO governance failure modes, a toolkit for quantifying decentralization metrics, and adaptive frameworks for auditing algorithmically managed assets. By bridging distributed systems research with accounting theory, this work aims to establish protocols for regulatory-compliant DAO financial reporting while advancing computational methods for analyzing emergent organizational structures in Web3 ecosystems. The project directly supports the integration of technical blockchain literacy with strategic management competencies, addressing a critical need in modern accounting and business education.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and business administration/management that prepares individuals to function as accountants and business managers.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern engineering and architectural projects demands advanced computational tools capable of handling high-fidelity simulations and large-scale design optimizations. Current drafting and design workflows often rely on simplified models due to limitations in processing power, which can lead to suboptimal material usage, structural inefficiencies, or delayed project timelines. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable real-time, multi-physics simulations and generative design processes within drafting and design applications. The research will focus on developing and validating computational workflows that integrate finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven topology optimization. These methods will be applied to case studies in modular construction, aerospace component design, and sustainable urban planning, where iterative testing of high-resolution models is critical. Key computational tasks include parallelized meshing algorithms, distributed solving of partial differential equations, and GPU-accelerated rendering of 3D simulations. The project will utilize open-source frameworks such as CalculiX and OpenFOAM, augmented by custom Python scripts for automation and data analysis. Expected outcomes include scalable templates for cloud-based HPC workflows, benchmarks comparing traditional and HPC-enhanced design cycles, and open-access datasets demonstrating efficiency gains in material usage and energy performance. By reducing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to democratize access to advanced simulation tools for educational institutions and small firms, fostering innovation in drafting pedagogy and industry practices. The requested computing resources will support parametric studies involving 10,000+ design permutations per project phase, enabling statistically robust conclusions about the trade-offs between computational cost and design precision. Successful implementation will provide a foundation for future interdisciplinary research in smart manufacturing and digital twin technologies, aligning with broader goals of sustainability and resilience in engineered systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the pedagogical training of pre-service and in-service general science teachers by modeling the integration of cross-disciplinary science concepts in classroom settings through advanced computational simulations. A critical challenge in science teacher education is equipping educators to cohesively teach interconnected biological, physical, and Earth science content while addressing persistent misconceptions and varied student learning trajectories. Current training methods rely heavily on qualitative observation and self-reporting, which lack the scalability and granularity to systematically analyze how teachers develop, adapt, or struggle with interdisciplinary instructional strategies. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate classroom interactions, incorporating variables such as teacher content knowledge, pedagogical decisions, student prior knowledge, and real-time feedback. These models will be parameterized using empirical data from classroom observations, student assessments, and teacher reflections collected across partner teacher preparation programs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations that explore how nuanced adjustments to teacher training frameworks—such as modifying the sequencing of pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) modules or optimizing feedback mechanisms—affect simulated student outcomes. Machine learning techniques will further identify patterns in emergent teacher decision-making behaviors across diverse virtual classroom scenarios. The resulting computational toolkit will provide teacher educators with evidence-based insights into designing targeted interventions that improve educators’ ability to teach integrated science concepts effectively. By bridging computational modeling and science education research, this project aims to advance the rigor and adaptability of teacher preparation programs, ultimately supporting K-12 students in building coherent, interdisciplinary scientific literacy.
cip_title: Science Teacher Education/ General Science Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general science programs, or a combination of the biological and physical science subject matter areas, at various educational levels.

abstract: Veterinary anesthesiology faces significant challenges in optimizing anesthetic protocols across diverse species, breeds, and physiological conditions. Current approaches often rely on generalized guidelines, which may inadequately address individual variability in drug metabolism, hemodynamic responses, and pain sensitivity, leading to increased risks of complications during surgery, critical care, or obstetric procedures. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model and predict patient-specific anesthetic outcomes. The research will integrate pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, machine learning (ML), and multi-omics data to simulate individualized responses to anesthetic agents under varying clinical scenarios, including specialized surgeries, fluid therapy regimens, and comorbid conditions. Computational models will incorporate species-specific physiological parameters, electronic health records, and real-time monitoring data (e.g., cardiovascular dynamics, respiratory metrics) to predict optimal dosing, fluid management, and pain control strategies. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, Bayesian inference for uncertainty quantification, and ensemble modeling to account for interspecies and intraindividual variability. Additionally, the project will simulate rare adverse events, such as drug-induced hypotension or hypoxemia, to refine safety protocols. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for tailored anesthesia plans, a decision-support tool for clinicians, and open-access datasets linking genomic markers to drug sensitivity. By enhancing precision in veterinary anesthesia, this work aims to reduce perioperative morbidity, improve recovery times, and establish scalable computational methodologies for translational research in veterinary pain management and critical care. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical to handling the computational complexity of multi-dimensional datasets and achieving real-time analytics for clinical applicability.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical animal care and the care of pain problems. May included related research in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: Rangeland ecosystems, critical for global food security and biodiversity, face increasing stressors from climate variability, invasive species encroachment, and unsustainable grazing practices. Current management frameworks often lack the predictive capacity to balance agricultural productivity with ecological resilience due to the complex, nonlinear interactions among vegetation dynamics, hydrology, herbivore behavior, and soil processes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, spatially explicit modeling platform to simulate rangeland responses to management interventions under diverse climatic scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate agent-based models of livestock grazing patterns with process-based biogeochemical simulations (CENTURY model variants) and machine learning-driven analysis of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2, UAV hyperspectral imaging). The computational framework will parameterize vegetation-soil feedbacks at unprecedented 1m² resolution across watershed-scale domains (>10,000 km²), incorporating stochastic climate projections from CMIP6 ensembles. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in forage productivity predictions and graph neural networks to model invasive plant dispersal pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of climate-resilient grazing regimes that optimize livestock carrying capacity while maintaining perennial grass cover, (2) predictive maps of soil carbon sequestration potential under alternative restoration strategies, and (3) open-source tools for real-time decision support in drought planning. By enabling simultaneous analysis of ecological, hydrological, and socioeconomic variables across temporal scales, this HPC-driven approach will advance precision rangeland management paradigms, directly supporting the agricultural community’s adaptive capacity in water-limited environments. The resulting datasets and models will be disseminated through partnerships with USDA Extension services and the Rangeland Analysis Platform.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of rangelands, arid regions, grasslands, and other areas of low productivity, as well as the principles of managing such resources for maximum benefit and environmental balance. Includes instruction in livestock management, wildlife biology, plant sciences, ecology, soil science, and hydrology.

abstract: Pediatric emergency medicine requires precise, evidence-based protocols to address the unique physiological and developmental characteristics of infants and children during critical care scenarios. Current clinical decision-making tools often rely on generalized guidelines that do not fully account for dynamic variables such as age-specific vital sign ranges, comorbidity interactions, or rare disease presentations. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing predictive computational models to optimize emergency interventions for pediatric patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-source clinical datasets, simulate emergent physiological responses, and generate risk-stratified treatment recommendations. Data from electronic health records, including vital signs, laboratory results, imaging, and outcomes from 15,000+ pediatric emergency visits, will be integrated into machine learning frameworks to identify critical predictors of deterioration and recovery. Agent-based modeling will simulate patient responses to interventions under varying physiological conditions, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in treatment outcomes. Computational demands are substantial due to the need for real-time processing of high-dimensional data, iterative model training, and large-scale simulations of rare events. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for sepsis, traumatic brain injury, and respiratory failure, which will prioritize time-sensitive interventions tailored to patient-specific factors. By enabling rapid analysis of complex, heterogeneous datasets, this work aims to reduce diagnostic delays, minimize treatment complications, and improve survival rates in pediatric emergencies. The resulting models and simulation tools will be disseminated as open-source resources to support clinical decision-making systems worldwide, bridging a critical gap in precision medicine for acute pediatric care.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage emergencies in infants and children.

abstract: Cancer progression is driven by dysregulated molecular signaling and endocrine interactions at the subcellular level, yet the dynamic mechanisms underlying these processes remain poorly understood. Experimental approaches alone are limited in resolving the spatiotemporal complexity of ion channel activity, transporter-mediated metabolite flux, and hormonal signaling that collectively influence tumorigenesis. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multi-scale computational models of molecular and endocrine networks in cancer cells, with a focus on ovarian and prostate carcinomas. The research will integrate molecular dynamics simulations to characterize ion channel conformations under hormonal stimuli, coupled with kinetic modeling of intracellular signaling cascades (e.g., GPCR-mediated pathways) that regulate proliferation and metastasis. A systems physiology framework will map cross-talk between endocrine signals, membrane transport dynamics, and downstream effectors such as calcium-dependent transcription factors. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds in signaling fidelity and simulate tumor microenvironmental stressors. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how dysregulated transport proteins and hormonal feedback loops drive therapeutic resistance, as well as predictive models of signaling plasticity in cancer cells. This work will establish a computational platform for probing subcellular physiological dynamics in oncology, with potential applications in targeting transport machinery or hormonal regulators to restore homeostatic signaling. By bridging molecular physiology with cancer biology, the project aims to advance precision oncology strategies through computationally guided hypotheses for experimental validation.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of dynamic interactive processes and biochemical communications at the subcellular level. Includes instruction in ion channels and transporters, molecular signaling pathways, endocrine control and regulation, genetic information transfer, homeostasis and molecular control systems, electrophysiology and sensory mechanisms, protein synthesis, and applicable research methods and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and optical interactions of customized contact lenses designed to correct complex corneal irregularities, such as those seen in keratoconus or post-surgical ectasia. Current lens design relies on static topographic maps and empirical fitting processes, which often fail to account for dynamic interactions between the lens, tear film, and deforming corneal tissue during eye movement or environmental stress. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive, patient-specific tools to optimize lens geometry and material properties for irregular corneas, leading to suboptimal visual outcomes and prolonged fitting timelines. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiphysics pipeline integrating finite element modeling of corneal biomechanics, computational fluid dynamics of the tear film interface, and ray-tracing simulations of optical performance under real-world kinematic conditions. The models will be parameterized using clinical data from corneal topography, optical coherence tomography, and in vivo lens movement tracking. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate inverse design workflows, enabling rapid iteration of lens parameters to meet patient-specific biomechanical and optical targets. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for optometrists to virtually test lens designs prior to fabrication, reducing clinical trial-and-error. The project will also yield new insights into strain distribution patterns in diseased corneas during lens wear, informing future materials research. By bridging optometric practice with computational engineering, this work aims to advance precision vision correction tools for structurally compromised eyes, a growing clinical population underserved by conventional approaches.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of optometry and that focuses on the principles and techniques for examining, diagnosing and treating conditions of the visual system. Includes instruction in prescribing glasses and contact lenses, other optical aids, corrective therapies, patient counseling, physician referral, practice management, and ethics and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Ukrainian linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in scalable language processing and textual modeling for under-resourced languages. The primary research problem centers on the limited availability of tools for large-scale analysis of Ukrainian linguistic phenomena, including dialectal variation, historical semantic shifts, and syntactic patterns in literary texts. Existing computational models for Slavic languages often exclude Ukrainian or rely on insufficient datasets, hindering progress in both theoretical linguistics and applied domains like machine translation or educational technology. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational approach. First, we will compile and preprocess a corpus of digitized Ukrainian texts spanning dialects, historical periods (19th century to present), and genres (prose, poetry, folklore), integrating optical character recognition for archival materials. Second, we will implement transformer-based neural networks (e.g., BERT architectures) optimized for Ukrainian using PyTorch, training models on HPC clusters to perform tasks such as dialect classification, automated metrical analysis of poetry, and detection of loanword integration patterns. Third, graph-based methods will map semantic networks in modern Ukrainian literature, analyzing conceptual evolution across socio-political contexts. The scale of data (anticipated 10TB+ of textual and audio recordings) and complexity of deep learning architectures necessitate HPC resources for distributed training, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale parallelism. Expected outcomes include the first open-source Ukrainian language model fine-tuned for literary analysis, a dialect atlas with computational isogloss mapping, and quantitative frameworks for tracking neologisms in post-2014 media. These resources will directly benefit philological research, language preservation initiatives, and developers of Ukrainian NLP tools, while establishing methodological precedents for computationally rigorous study of lesser-resourced languages in the humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Ukrainian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict risks to cultural and archaeological heritage sites using advanced geospatial analytics, machine learning, and agent-based simulations. Despite legal protections, heritage sites globally face escalating threats from looting, urban encroachment, and environmental degradation. Current risk assessment methods rely heavily on manual field surveys and qualitative data, limiting scalability and real-time responsiveness. To address this gap, we propose integrating heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution satellite imagery, historical looting incident reports, regional socioeconomic indicators, and climate vulnerability metrics—into a unified predictive model. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabytes of geospatial data, training deep learning algorithms to detect subtle site disturbances, and simulating dynamic interactions between environmental stressors, illicit networks, and site vulnerability. Agent-based models will simulate looting behaviors under varying enforcement scenarios, while graph neural networks will map trafficking networks using open-source artifact market data. The computational pipeline will prioritize interoperability with existing cultural resource management databases, enabling automated risk alerts and adaptive policy testing. Expected outcomes include a scalable tool for prioritizing site monitoring efforts, quantifying the efficacy of protection strategies, and reconstructing dispersal patterns of looted artifacts. By bridging computational criminology, heritage science, and geoinformatics, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for proactive cultural resource protection, offering law enforcement and policymakers data-driven strategies to mitigate site loss. The project will also generate open-access codebases and training modules to empower under-resourced regions with limited technical capacity, fostering equitable adoption of computational tools in heritage crime prevention.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement principles and techniques to the protection of cultural resources and the investigation of related crimes. Includes instruction in cultural resources law, archaeological standards of value, site damage assessment, evidence collection, surveillance techniques, investigative techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and metabolic determinants of personalized exercise adherence in sedentary populations, a critical yet understudied factor in long-term health outcomes. While public health frameworks broadly address physical activity promotion, individual variability in biomechanics, neuromuscular efficiency, and metabolic response remains a barrier to designing universally effective exercise regimens. We aim to develop a computational model integrating motion capture data, physiological biomarkers, and psychological self-reports to predict optimal exercise modalities for sustaining adherence. The research problem centers on resolving how idiosyncratic physiological constraints interact with behavioral preferences to influence compliance, particularly in populations with obesity or early-stage metabolic syndrome. Using HPC clusters, we will process high-resolution biomechanical datasets from wearable sensors (sampled at 200 Hz) and merge these with metabolomic profiles derived from mass spectrometry. Machine learning pipelines will train on these multimodal datasets to identify latent patterns linking biomechanical efficiency, perceived exertion, and biochemical markers of exercise adaptation. Agent-based modeling will then simulate long-term adherence scenarios under varying exercise prescriptions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for tailoring exercise interventions to individual biomechanical and metabolic phenotypes, with potential applications in workplace wellness programs and community health initiatives. By quantifying previously intangible interactions between physiology and behavior, this work could redefine how health systems operationalize "personalized" exercise guidance, moving beyond generic recommendations toward computationally optimized prescriptions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the terabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing complex simulations, and iterating neural network architectures within feasible timeframes.
