cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to assume roles as health/wellness professionals in private business and industry, community organizations, and health care settings. Includes instruction in personal health, community health and welfare, nutrition, epidemiology, disease prevention, fitness and exercise, and health behaviors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the digital preservation and analysis of Latinx cultural narratives across media, with a focus on Mexican-American/Chicano and Puerto Rican diasporic communities. The research addresses a critical gap in accessible computational methodologies for analyzing large-scale, multilingual, and multimodal cultural archives—such as community oral histories, independent film, and social media—that reflect the dynamic interplay of identity, migration, and resistance within these groups. Current tools for text, audio, and visual analysis often fail to account for code-switching, regional vernaculars, or culturally specific symbolism, limiting their utility for Latinx studies. To address this, the project will deploy machine learning models optimized for Spanish-English code-switched speech-to-text transcription, alongside computer vision pipelines trained to recognize iconography in Chicano art and community murals. These workflows will be integrated into a scalable digital repository hosted on HPC infrastructure, enabling semantic search, network analysis of thematic trends, and geospatial mapping of cultural production across decades. Computational demands include GPU-accelerated training of multilingual transformer models, large-scale metadata processing, and high-throughput rendering of 3D-scanned cultural artifacts. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible platform for scholars and community stakeholders to engage with digitized collections, as well as new computational frameworks tailored to the linguistic and cultural nuances of Latinx materials. By centering technical innovation in service of community-driven narratives, this project aims to reshape digital humanities methodologies while safeguarding marginalized cultural knowledge against erasure. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data and ensure equitable access to tools that amplify Latinx voices in academic and public discourse.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Hispanic-American, Puerto Rican, Latinx, and Mexican-American/ Chicano Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic American immigrant populations within the U.S. and Canada, including Mexican-American Studies, Cuban American Studies, Puerto Rican Studies, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to advance earth science education by developing and deploying high-resolution computational models to simulate complex Earth systems for use in teacher training and K-12 classrooms. A critical challenge in earth science pedagogy is the lack of accessible, interactive tools that accurately represent dynamic processes such as climate feedbacks, hydrological cycles, and tectonic activity. Existing educational models often oversimplify these systems, limiting students’ ability to engage with authentic scientific practices like hypothesis testing and data-driven decision-making. To address this gap, we propose creating a suite of scalable, GPU-accelerated Earth system simulations optimized for educational contexts. These simulations will integrate real-world datasets from satellite observations, ground-based sensors, and paleoclimate archives, downscaled to regional resolutions relevant to classroom case studies. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will run ensemble climate models under varying parameters to generate probabilistic outputs, which will be packaged into modular, age-appropriate virtual labs. Concurrently, machine learning methods will analyze patterns in how pre-service teachers adapt these tools for lesson design, identifying computational bottlenecks and pedagogical misconceptions. The project will also leverage distributed computing to host collaborative modeling exercises, enabling cross-institutional cohorts of educators to compare localized climate projections or geologic hazard scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access computational curricula aligned with Next Generation Science Standards, (2) a framework for integrating HPC-derived datasets into teacher training programs, and (3) benchmarks for scaling geoscientific modeling tasks across heterogeneous classroom technologies. By grounding earth science instruction in cutting-edge computational research, this work aims to enhance spatial reasoning skills and systems thinking among both educators and students, while fostering familiarity with computational tools critical to modern geoscience careers. The requested resources are essential for managing the high-throughput simulations, real-time data assimilation, and large-scale user testing required to validate the educational efficacy of these models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach earth science programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The structural organization of macromolecular assemblies underpins critical cellular processes, yet dynamic transitions in these systems remain poorly understood due to limitations in resolving transient conformational states. This project seeks to elucidate the mechanistic basis of ATP-dependent chaperone-mediated protein folding through large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and integrative modeling. Current experimental techniques struggle to capture millisecond-scale conformational changes in these multi-subunit complexes, creating a critical gap in understanding how energy transduction drives substrate remodeling. We propose an HPC-driven approach combining all-atom MD simulations of the HSP90 chaperone system with enhanced sampling techniques to map free energy landscapes of nucleotide-induced allostery. Simulations will be parameterized using experimental data from collaborative cryo-EM studies, employing iterative refinement to reconcile conformational sampling with density maps. A second focus involves developing coarse-grained models of client protein-chaperone interactions to investigate folding pathways under crowding conditions mimicking cellular environments. These simulations require massive parallelization to achieve biologically relevant timescales while maintaining atomic-level precision for key functional residues. The requested resources will enable 1) multi-microsecond trajectories of full-length chaperone complexes (≥500,000 atoms), 2) Markov state model analysis of conformational ensembles, and 3) machine learning-assisted identification of allosteric networks. Expected outcomes include resolving nucleotide cycling mechanics in HSP90, predicting client-specific folding trajectories, and establishing a computational framework for studying multidomain protein folding in physiologically relevant conditions. This work will advance fundamental knowledge of chaperone-mediated proteostasis while providing methodological innovations for coupling cryo-EM with dynamic simulations. Results will directly inform ongoing experimental studies of chaperone mutations linked to neurodegenerative diseases and cancer, potentially identifying new targets for therapeutic intervention. The computational models and protocols developed will be disseminated as open-source tools for the structural biology community.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of submolecular and molecular components and assemblies of living systems and how they are organized into functional units such as cells and anatomic tissues. Includes instruction in glycoprotein, carbohydrate, protein, and nucleic acid structures and chemistry; cytoskeletal structure; nuclear and intracellular structures; molecular recognition; molecular chaperones; transcription and folding; multicellular organization; microtubules and microfilaments; cell differentiation; immunophysics; and DNA sequencing.

abstract: Cancer progression is driven by dynamic interactions between tumor cells and their microenvironment, yet the mechanisms by which heterogeneous cell populations adapt to metabolic and mechanical stressors remain poorly understood. This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to model tumor-stroma crosstalk in physiologically relevant microenvironments, with a focus on hypoxia-driven phenotypic plasticity in breast cancer. Current experimental models struggle to capture the spatiotemporal complexity of tumor ecosystems, particularly how localized nutrient gradients and extracellular matrix remodeling influence collective cell behaviors. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based model integrating single-cell metabolic states, paracrine signaling, and biomechanical tissue properties. The model will parameterize experimentally derived data on oxygen consumption rates, lactate-mediated endothelial activation, and collagen fiber alignment in murine xenografts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate evolving cell populations across biologically relevant timescales (weeks to months) while resolving subcellular decision-making processes. Each simulation will track >10^6 interacting agents with differential equations governing proliferation, migration, and survival thresholds under resource competition. Sensitivity analyses will quantify how microenvironmental perturbations alter metastatic potential. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of stromal-derived factors that stabilize tumor cell subpopulations resistant to metabolic therapies, and 2) predictive maps of matrix stiffness thresholds that trigger collective invasion. This work will provide the first computational platform capable of testing how physiological stressors at the tissue scale (e.g., intermittent hypoxia) emerge from subcellular adaptations in cancer and stromal cells. The requested resources will enable parameter optimization through ensemble simulations, significantly advancing our ability to model patient-specific tumor ecosystems for therapeutic targeting.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_title: Physiology, Pathology, and Related Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physiology, pathology, and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of laboratory diagnostics, driven by high-throughput testing and multi-omics data integration, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize workflows and improve diagnostic accuracy. This project seeks to address challenges in clinical laboratory efficiency and precision by developing machine learning (ML) models to automate anomaly detection in waived testing results and enhance predictive analytics for test selection. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), including hematological, biochemical, and point-of-care test results, alongside contextual metadata (e.g., patient demographics, pre-analytical variables). Our computational approach will focus on training deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based models, to identify patterns indicative of pre-analytical errors, instrument drift, or clinically significant outliers. Parallelized workflows will be implemented to process heterogeneous data streams, while Bayesian optimization will fine-tune hyperparameters for robustness across diverse laboratory settings. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between common anticoagulants and blood samples to refine phlebotomy protocols. The expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time quality control in waived testing, predictive algorithms to guide test utilization, and evidence-based recommendations for minimizing pre-analytical errors. By integrating HPC-driven insights with laboratory workflows, this research aims to reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve resource allocation in clinical laboratories, and strengthen competency-based training for laboratory personnel. The project will also provide a framework for embedding computational literacy into medical laboratory education, bridging traditional skills with data science applications. Successful implementation will advance precision in laboratory diagnostics while addressing growing demands for scalable solutions in healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians or laboratory scientists or technologists, to perform waived testing procedures (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988), phlebotomy, and other duties in support of laboratory teams. Includes instruction in clinical procedures, various laboratory tests, laboratory mathematics, computer technology, equipment operation and maintenance, sterilization and safety, communications skills, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: Agricultural supply chains face growing challenges from market volatility, climate variability, and logistical inefficiencies, which complicate inventory management, procurement, and distribution for retailers and wholesalers. Traditional analytical tools struggle to integrate real-time data across spatial and temporal scales, limiting adaptive decision-making. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model and optimize agricultural supply chain networks, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation under uncertainty. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions among producers, distributors, retailers, and consumers, incorporating heterogeneous datasets such as historical sales, weather forecasts, transportation costs, and crop yield predictions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to forecast regional demand fluctuations and supply disruptions, while mixed-integer linear programming techniques will optimize distribution routes and inventory thresholds. Computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations, assessing trade-offs between cost, resilience, and sustainability metrics. By enabling granular, data-driven insights into procurement timing, warehouse placement, and pricing strategies, this project aims to reduce operational waste, minimize stockouts, and improve profit margins for agricultural suppliers. The resulting models will be validated against case studies from midwestern U.S. grain and livestock supply chains, with scalability assessments for global applications. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software tools for supply chain analytics and evidence-based policy recommendations to stabilize market access for small-scale agricultural retailers. This work bridges computational innovation with practical agribusiness management, advancing the resilience of agricultural economies in the face of compounding stressors.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize training protocols for working animals, with a focus on service dogs and search-and-rescue canines. Current training methodologies rely heavily on iterative, trial-and-error approaches that lack systematic personalization, leading to variable success rates and prolonged training timelines. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the interplay between animal behavior, environmental variables, and trainer interventions. The project will utilize anonymized datasets spanning biometric markers (e.g., heart rate, cortisol levels), behavioral logs from training sessions, and longitudinal outcome data from 2,000+ working dogs. These datasets will inform agent-based simulations that map individual learning trajectories under varying stressors, reward schedules, and task complexities. Machine learning models, including recurrent neural networks and reinforcement learning architectures, will be trained to predict optimal conditioning strategies for specific animal-trainer dyads. Computational demands include large-scale parameter space exploration, real-time sensor data integration, and ensemble modeling to account for breed-specific cognitive profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive toolset for identifying training regimens that minimize stress while accelerating skill acquisition, (2) quantitative metrics to assess animal readiness for advanced roles, and (3) open-source simulation templates adaptable to non-canine species. By bridging ethology, behavioral psychology, and computational analytics, this work aims to establish a data-driven paradigm for animal training that enhances operational outcomes while prioritizing welfare. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s iterative modeling needs, which require parallel processing of multidimensional datasets and validation across heterogeneous training scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach and exercise animals for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes. Includes instruction in animal psychology, health, and safety; human-animal interaction; learning and behavior styles associated with different breeds and species; and the technical and pedagogical aspects of training animals for such specific functions as obedient household pets, performing show animals, animal athletes, caregiving (e.g., seeing-eye dogs), search and rescue, and police/security work.

abstract: This research seeks to address the challenge of dynamically simulating large-scale, heterogeneous virtual environments where human-agent interactions are governed by evolving behavioral patterns and environmental stressors. Traditional simulations often rely on static rule sets or oversimplified cognitive models, limiting their capacity to capture emergent collective behaviors in scenarios such as crowd evacuations, distributed teamwork in augmented reality (AR), or adaptive human-in-the-loop training systems. The project proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating neurosymbolic behavior modeling, real-time environmental stochasticity, and multi-modal sensory feedback loops. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallel execution of agent cognition engines—combining transformer-based natural language processing for social dynamics, spiking neural networks for stress-response modeling, and physics-informed reinforcement learning for spatial navigation. A novel distributed rendering pipeline will synchronize visual, auditory, and haptic outputs across GPU clusters to maintain sub-20ms latency for human participants in VR testbeds. The computational architecture employs containerized microservices to manage heterogeneous workloads, with Kubernetes orchestration scaling agent populations across nodes based on interaction density metrics. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation platform capable of sustaining 10,000+ agents with individualized cognitive profiles in photorealistic environments, quantitative metrics for behavioral emergence thresholds, and a dataset correlating physiological sensor data from human subjects with simulated agent stress responses. This work advances the integration of cognitive science principles into scalable virtual environments, with applications in disaster preparedness training, collaborative AR system design, and ethical AI development through human-centered simulation. The requested resources will specifically support the distributed training of multi-agent reinforcement learning policies and the optimization of ray-traced environment rendering across hybrid CPU/GPU architectures.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles of applied visual simulation technology and the application of quantitative analyses to human-computer interaction. Includes instruction in object-oriented programming, artificial intelligence, computer communications and networks, computer graphics, virtual worlds and simulation systems, probability, statistics, stochastic modeling, data analysis, human-performance evaluation, and human-behavior modeling.

abstract: Sterilization efficacy in healthcare settings is critical for preventing surgical site infections and ensuring patient safety, yet current practices in sterile processing technology (SPT) face challenges in predicting microbial resistance and optimizing instrument reprocessing protocols. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model microbial survival dynamics under varying sterilization parameters and simulate the efficacy of decontamination workflows. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate heat, moisture, and chemical dispersion patterns within sterilization chambers to identify inefficiencies in equipment design or operational protocols. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze large-scale datasets from microbial genomic sequences, sterilization logs, and environmental monitoring systems to predict pathogen resistance trends and correlate them with procedural variables. The integration of these computational approaches will enable the development of adaptive, data-driven models for optimizing sterilization cycles, reducing resource waste, and minimizing human error in SPT workflows. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for refining sterilization guidelines, a predictive tool for identifying high-risk instrument batches, and a framework for real-time monitoring of sterilization efficacy in clinical environments. By addressing the intersection of computational modeling and SPT practices, this research aims to advance infection control standards, reduce healthcare-associated infections, and support the training of sterile processing professionals through evidence-based protocol enhancements. The scale and complexity of multi-parameter simulations and genomic data analysis necessitate HPC resources to achieve statistically robust results within operationally relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean, sterilize, and assemble surgical instruments, equipment, and supplies for use in operating rooms and other medical and surgical facilities. Includes instruction in sterilization; infection control; decontamination; and surgical instrumentation processing, distribution, and record-keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making in aviation operations management under dynamic constraints, with a focus on improving efficiency and safety in airport ground operations and air traffic flow. The aviation industry faces growing pressures from increasing air traffic volumes, environmental regulations, and operational costs, necessitating advanced analytical tools to balance competing priorities. Current optimization models often lack the resolution to address real-time variability in factors such as weather, gate availability, and ground crew workflows. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system coupled with discrete-event simulations to model complex interactions between aircraft, ground services, and air traffic control. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on historical flight data, airport layouts, and stochastic disturbance scenarios, enabling the system to adaptively allocate resources such as gate assignments, refueling schedules, and de-icing crew deployment. Computational challenges include managing large-scale mixed-integer programming problems with time-dependent constraints and parallelizing simulations across heterogeneous scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce taxiway congestion, minimize fuel waste during ground delays, and improve turnaround time reliability. The project will also quantify trade-offs between operational efficiency metrics and CO2 emissions, providing actionable insights for aviation managers. Successful implementation could inform both operational protocols for airport authorities and strategic planning tools for aviation enterprises, contributing to scalable solutions for sustainable growth in the sector. By integrating business administration principles with computational modeling, this work bridges critical gaps in data-driven decision support systems for aviation operations management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the management of aviation industry operations and services. Includes instruction in airport operations, ground traffic direction, ground support and flightline operations, passenger and cargo operations, flight safety and security operations, aviation industry regulation, and related business aspects of managing aviation enterprises.

abstract: Agroecological systems require the integration of complex biological, environmental, and socioeconomic factors to optimize sustainability and productivity. However, current modeling frameworks often lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between crop genotypes, soil microbiomes, and management practices at scale, limiting their utility for predicting system outcomes under climate variability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational model to simulate agroecosystem dynamics, with a focus on crop-soil-microbe interactions and their response to diverse agricultural management strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate process-based crop models, microbial community metagenomic data, and spatially explicit soil health metrics to predict nutrient cycling efficiency, pest resilience, and yield stability across heterogeneous landscapes. Machine learning methods will be applied to parameterize models using multi-year field datasets from experimental agroecological plots, including crop rotations, cover cropping, and reduced tillage systems. The computational workflow will employ parallelized simulations to evaluate thousands of management scenarios under projected climate conditions, quantifying trade-offs between productivity, soil carbon sequestration, and input use efficiency. By coupling genomic, edaphic, and agronomic data at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales, this work will advance understanding of resilience mechanisms in diversified farming systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable modeling toolkit for optimizing management decisions, identification of genotype-by-management combinations that enhance sustainability, and open-access datasets to support broader agroecological research. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the high dimensionality of ecological datasets, running iterative simulations, and enabling real-time analytics for stakeholder-driven scenario testing. This project directly aligns with the program’s mission to develop computationally informed, ecologically sound solutions for agricultural challenges while prioritizing economic viability and resource efficiency.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of quantum-inspired metamaterials for energy-efficient thermal regulation in compact electronics, an emerging niche at the intersection of nanoscale engineering, statistical thermodynamics, and machine learning. As device miniaturization increases power density, managing heat dissipation without bulky cooling systems remains a critical challenge. Traditional thermal metamaterial design relies on trial-and-error approaches limited by the computational cost of modeling non-periodic, multiscale structures with coupled electron-phonon interactions. This work proposes a hybrid methodology combining lattice Boltzmann simulations, density functional tight-binding (DFTB) calculations, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to predict thermal transport in disordered meta-structures under high electromagnetic fields. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-fidelity surrogate models that bridge quantum-scale electron scattering events with continuum-level heat transfer phenomena. Key innovations include adaptive meshing algorithms for irregular geometries and a reinforcement learning agent trained on distributed GPU clusters to explore topology-property relationships across 10^6+ design candidates. Expected outcomes include validated models of tunable thermal conductivity in non-equilibrium systems and a generative design toolkit for metamaterials achieving >50% reduction in hotspot temperatures compared to conventional heat spreaders. The resource request supports large-scale parameter sweeps (O(10^4) core-hours) and memory-intensive GNN training on 3D voxel datasets (TB-scale storage). By establishing computational workflows for quantum-thermal material discovery, this research addresses a critical gap in next-generation electronics cooling while advancing algorithmic strategies for multiscale engineering systems beyond classical continuum approximations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to engineering practice and research. Includes instruction in engineering and science fundamentals, advanced mathematics, algorithms, computer languages, and software engineering design.

abstract: Dental caries and periodontal diseases remain highly prevalent globally, disproportionately affecting marginalized populations despite established preventive measures. Emerging evidence suggests oral microbial dysbiosis interacts with systemic conditions (e.g., diabetes, cardiovascular disease) through complex host-microbiome-metabolite networks, but current analytical frameworks lack resolution to model these interactions at population scales. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets from a longitudinal cohort study (n=2,400) exploring bidirectional relationships between oral microbiome dynamics, epigenetic modifications, and metabolic syndrome markers in underserved urban populations. Computational challenges include processing 45TB of metagenomic sequencing data, integrating heterogeneous datasets (16S rRNA, shotgun metagenomics, plasma metabolomics, epigenetic clocks), and implementing dynamical systems models to identify critical transition states in disease progression. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to predict community-specific caries risk thresholds based on microbial interaction networks and social determinants of health covariates. A novel agent-based model will simulate the population-level impact of targeted microbiome-modifying interventions (e.g., pH-stabilizing nanotherapies) on oral health disparities. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone microbial taxa driving oral-systemic disease synergies, (2) computational tools for personalized caries prevention strategies in public health dentistry, and (3) policy-relevant simulations of intervention scalability across diverse community dental infrastructures. This work requires HPC capabilities for parallelized metagenomic assembly (using MetaSPAdes and HUMAnN3), GPU-accelerated deep learning (PyTorch geometric for graph-based microbiome networks), and large-scale parameter sweeps in epidemiological modeling (Repast4Py). By bridging computational biology and dental public health paradigms, the project aims to establish a framework for precision prevention strategies that address oral health inequalities through microbiome-informed community programming.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of dental disease prevention and control, community dental health promotion, and prepares dentists and public health professionals to function as dental health specialists. Includes instruction in preventive dentistry, the relationship of oral disease to health and quality of life, patient and practitioner behavior, dental epidemiology, nutrition and dental health, dental care policy and delivery, oral health program planning and administration, biostatistics, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational documentation and analysis of understudied Indigenous languages of the Pacific region, with a focus on Papuan and Polynesian language families. Despite their cultural significance, many languages in these groups remain under-resourced in digital corpora, hindering both preservation efforts and comparative linguistic research. The primary challenge lies in processing large, heterogeneous datasets—including legacy audio recordings, transcribed texts, and field notes—while accounting for complex morphosyntactic structures and dialectal variations. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable pipelines for automated speech recognition (ASR), morphological parsing, and cross-linguistic alignment. Computational workflows will integrate transformer-based models fine-tuned on existing Pacific language corpora, phylogenetic algorithms for reconstructing proto-language features, and GPU-accelerated batch processing of audio data. Key innovations include adapting low-resource NLP techniques to Oceanic languages’ agglutinative morphology and developing probabilistic models to infer semantic relationships in oral narratives. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access repository of computationally enhanced linguistic resources for 10+ endangered languages, 2) novel insights into contact phenomena between Papuan and Austronesian languages in Melanesia, and 3) community-facing tools for language revitalization, such as interactive dictionaries and pedagogical applications. The scale of data—anticipated at 50TB of audio-text pairs and 1M+ annotated lexical entries—necessitates distributed storage and parallelized computation unavailable on local infrastructure. By bridging computational linguistics with Pacific language scholarship, this project aims to advance both methodological frameworks for linguistic analysis and equitable access to digital preservation technologies for Indigenous communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Australian/ Oceanic/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages native to Papua/New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and the island groups of the Pacific Ocean, including, but not limited to, the Papuan languages, the Australian languages, the Micronesian languages, and the Polynesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in optimizing food processing techniques for improved nutritional retention and safety. A critical challenge in food science lies in modeling the complex interactions between processing parameters (e.g., temperature, pressure, enzymatic activity) and the physicochemical properties of agricultural products. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and limited in their ability to predict outcomes across diverse food matrices. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML) to model the degradation pathways of micronutrients during thermal processing and storage. The study will focus on key vitamin complexes (e.g., B-group vitamins in fortified cereals) and plant-based proteins, examining how processing variables influence stability, bioavailability, and potential toxin formation. Large-scale MD simulations will parameterize time-dependent molecular interactions under varying thermal and mechanical stresses, while ML models trained on these datasets will predict optimal processing conditions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the high-dimensional data generated by these simulations, enabling parallel computation of multi-scale models, and iteratively refining predictive algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated computational toolkit to guide the design of energy-efficient processing methods that minimize nutrient loss and mitigate safety risks. This work will directly inform industry practices, reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, and support the development of scalable strategies for sustainable food production. By linking molecular-scale phenomena to macroscopic food quality metrics, the project bridges gaps in predictive modeling for agricultural product engineering, with broader implications for addressing global nutrition security.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of converting raw agricultural products into processed forms suitable for direct human consumption, and the storage of such products. Includes instruction in applicable aspects of the agricultural sciences, human physiology and nutrition, food chemistry, agricultural products processing, food additives, food preparation and packaging, food storage and shipment, and related aspects of human health and safety including toxicology and pathology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal landscape governing workplace algorithmic accountability, with a focus on disparities in employment outcomes linked to automated decision-making systems (ADMS). As organizations increasingly deploy ADMS for hiring, performance evaluation, and workforce management, legal frameworks struggle to address emergent challenges, including bias amplification, transparency deficits, and compliance conflicts between anti-discrimination statutes and data privacy regulations. The study will computationally model multi-jurisdictional legal texts—including court opinions, administrative rulings, and legislative proposals—alongside HR policy documents and ADMS audit reports to identify systemic gaps in regulatory coherence. A hybrid natural language processing (NLP) pipeline will be developed, combining transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned on legal corpora) with graph neural networks to map citation networks, concept drift in statutory interpretation, and cross-regulatory tensions. Computational legal realism methods will be adapted to simulate how hypothetical ADMS configurations might fare in adversarial litigation scenarios under differing judicial philosophies. The project requires HPC resources to manage the scale and complexity of (1) processing terabytes of unstructured legal and organizational texts, (2) training domain-specific language models with attention mechanisms optimized for statutory logic, and (3) running Monte Carlo simulations of policy impact under 50-state regulatory variance. Anticipated outcomes include a public knowledge graph of algorithmic employment law risk factors, a toolkit for proactive HR compliance auditing, and theoretical contributions to computational legal studies through novel metrics for quantifying regulatory uncertainty in sociotechnical systems. By enabling granular analysis of how ADMS-related liabilities manifest across jurisdictions and organizational contexts, this work aims to inform both legal scholarship and evidence-based HR policy formulation in an era of rapidly advancing workplace technologies.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing next-generation telecommunications networks, particularly in dense urban environments where high user density and heterogeneous devices strain existing infrastructure. Current network management strategies struggle to balance real-time demand fluctuations, dynamic resource allocation, and energy efficiency while maintaining low latency for applications like augmented reality and IoT-enabled systems. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate scalable machine learning models for adaptive network slicing in 5G/6G environments. The computational workflow will involve large-scale simulations of multi-tenant network architectures using discrete-event modeling and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess traffic patterns across varying spatial-temporal conditions. Additionally, we will train graph neural networks (GNNs) on synthetic and real-world datasets to predict optimal resource distribution across virtualized network slices, incorporating constraints from quality-of-service metrics and energy consumption profiles. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of digital signal processing pipelines for interference mitigation in millimeter-wave bands, utilizing GPU-accelerated Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) implementations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for dynamic spectrum sharing, optimized beamforming configurations, and energy-aware routing protocols that reduce baseline power consumption by 18-22% in simulated scenarios. These results will provide actionable insights for telecom operators deploying software-defined networks and contribute open-source tools for stochastic network modeling. By bridging algorithmic innovation with practical deployment constraints, this work aims to advance the scalability and sustainability of urban telecommunications infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to help design and implement telecommunications systems. Includes instruction in communications protocol, data networking, digital compression algorithms, digital signal processing, Internet access, object-oriented and relational databases, and programming languages.

abstract: Child abuse pediatrics requires integrating complex, multidimensional data to improve diagnostic accuracy, inform legal consultations, and optimize prevention strategies. Current approaches often rely on fragmented datasets and subjective clinical judgments, leading to inconsistencies in abuse identification and case management. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework that synthesizes heterogeneous data sources—including electronic health records, social services reports, forensic imaging, and legal documentation—to enhance decision-making in child abuse cases. The research problem centers on the need for robust, data-driven tools that can identify patterns indicative of abuse, predict outcomes, and evaluate intervention efficacy at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large, sensitive datasets while maintaining privacy compliance, perform advanced statistical modeling, and simulate longitudinal outcomes of abuse prevention programs. Computational methods will include machine learning algorithms (e.g., ensemble classifiers, natural language processing) to analyze unstructured clinical narratives and imaging data, network analysis to map interactions among multidisciplinary teams and community agencies, and agent-based modeling to simulate the systemic impact of prevention strategies. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data, iterative model training across diverse abuse scenarios, and real-time validation against historical case outcomes. Expected outcomes include predictive models to distinguish abusive from accidental injuries with higher specificity, computational tools to optimize forensic workflows for multidisciplinary teams, and evidence-based simulations to guide policy on prevention program allocation. By integrating disparate data streams into a unified analytical platform, this project aims to advance the precision of abuse diagnostics, reduce biases in legal consultations, and provide scalable solutions for managing complex cases. The requested computing resources will directly support the development of open-source tools tailored for child abuse pediatrics, fostering collaboration across clinical, legal, and social service domains while adhering to ethical standards for sensitive data use.
cip_definition: Research on how to accurately diagnose abuse, consult with community agencies on child safety, provide expertise in courts of law, treat consequences of abuse and neglect, direct child abuse and neglect prevention programs and participate on multidisciplinary investigative teams, and manage child abuse cases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven computational framework to optimize the accuracy and efficiency of medical insurance coding processes, addressing systemic challenges in claim denials and compliance errors. Medical coding involves translating complex clinical documentation into standardized codes, a task prone to human error due to evolving coding guidelines, intricate payer-specific rules, and the volume of healthcare data. Inaccuracies result in claim rejections, delayed reimbursements, and regulatory risks. Current software tools lack adaptability to dynamic coding environments, particularly for specialized or rare medical cases. To address this, we propose training machine learning (ML) models on heterogeneous datasets—including de-identified electronic health records (EHRs), insurance claim histories, and updated coding manuals—to predict code assignments while flagging discrepancies and compliance risks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multimodal data (structured codes, unstructured clinical notes, and imaging reports) at scale, enabling natural language processing (NLP) for text extraction, graph-based algorithms to model code dependencies, and ensemble models to reconcile conflicting guidelines across insurance providers. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated clusters to train transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned on medical corpora) for context-aware code suggestions and deploy federated learning techniques to maintain patient privacy. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive coding tool that reduces manual review time by ≥40% and decreases claim denial rates by ≥25% in simulated billing workflows. The computational pipeline will also generate synthetic datasets to benchmark coding variability under diverse insurance policies, providing actionable insights for curriculum updates in medical coding education. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with domain-specific coding practices, this work aims to establish scalable, standards-compliant solutions that enhance both operational efficiency and educational training methodologies in health information management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized data entry, classification, and record-keeping procedures related to medical diagnostic, treatment, billing, and insurance documentation. Includes instruction in medical records and insurance software applications, basic anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, fundamentals of medical science and treatment procedures, data classification and coding, data entry skills, and regulations relating to Medicare and insurance documentation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize hybrid event logistics by modeling dynamic, multi-stakeholder decision-making under uncertainty. The proliferation of hybrid (in-person/virtual) events post-pandemic has introduced unprecedented complexity in resource allocation, requiring simultaneous coordination of physical venue constraints, digital platform scalability, attendee preferences, and real-time risk mitigation (e.g., network latency, last-minute capacity changes). Current industry tools rely on static heuristics ill-suited to these interdependent variables. We propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach coupled with multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to simulate 10,000+ concurrent agent interactions across spatial, temporal, and technical domains. High-performance computing resources are critical to handle 1) large-scale parameter spaces encompassing venue blueprints, attendee mobility patterns, and vendor service-level agreements; 2) real-time Monte Carlo simulations of contingency scenarios (e.g., sudden bandwidth demands, weather disruptions); and 3) GPU-accelerated neural architecture search for adaptive scheduling policies. The computational model will integrate anonymized historical data from 15 corporate event partners (≈2.3 million participant-hours) with synthetic data generators for emerging edge cases. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that reduces vendor overtime costs by 12-18% (95% CI), improves attendee engagement equity between physical/digital cohorts, and decreases carbon footprint through optimized load-balancing of distributed micro-events. This work bridges operations research, behavioral economics, and distributed systems engineering, establishing computational social science methodologies as a critical tool for next-generation event planning ecosystems. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules and a novel benchmark dataset for hospitality informatics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, budget, and implement conferences, meetings, and other special events in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in principles of meeting and event planning; special event management; budgets and finance; site selection; contracts, vendors, and negotiations; marketing and promotions; food and beverage management; audio-visual basics and meeting technology; and hospitality law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociocultural dynamics of fan engagement in professional sports, with a focus on identifying patterns of collective behavior, identity formation, and emotional contagion across digital and physical spaces. While sports fandom is a globally significant cultural phenomenon, its computational modeling remains underdeveloped due to the complexity of integrating heterogeneous data streams—including social media interactions, biometric feedback from wearable devices, archival records, and real-time event metadata—into a unified analytical framework. The research problem centers on disentangling how localized fan rituals, historical team legacies, and digital platforms co-produce emergent collective identities that influence both online communities and in-person attendance. Computational methods will include large-scale network analysis to map transnational fan communities, agent-based modeling to simulate crowd behavior during live events, and natural language processing (NLP) to quantify sentiment and narrative evolution across multilingual platforms. Deep learning architectures will be trained to detect cross-cultural variations in fan symbolism and ritualistic practices, while GPU-accelerated simulations will model hypothetical scenarios of fan response to rule changes, team relocations, or geopolitical conflicts. The project’s interdisciplinary approach bridges cultural anthropology, digital humanities, and behavioral psychology, requiring HPC capabilities to manage petabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive workflows. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph of global sports fandom, predictive models of fan retention under demographic shifts, and frameworks for mitigating toxic behaviors in digital fan spaces. By advancing computational methods tailored to sports studies, this work aims to establish new standards for analyzing cultural systems that operate at the intersection of tradition, technology, and mass participation.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological, sociological, and historical aspects of sport and physical activity. Includes instruction in theory of sport, sport psychology, sport in American society, gender and race/ethnicity and sport, and sports history.

abstract: The increasing complexity of marine propulsion and energy systems, driven by global demands for operational efficiency and stringent environmental regulations, necessitates advanced computational tools to model, optimize, and predict system behavior. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for hybrid marine propulsion systems integrating diesel engines, electrical storage, and waste-heat recovery technologies. A critical challenge lies in balancing real-time energy demands, thermal management, and emissions control under dynamic operational conditions, such as variable loads and harsh marine environments. Traditional analytical methods and low-resolution simulations fail to capture the multi-physics interactions between mechanical, electrical, and thermal subsystems, limiting predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, coupled simulations of fluid dynamics, combustion processes, and electromechanical systems. Agent-based modeling will simulate component interactions, while machine learning algorithms will optimize control strategies using real-world operational data. The HPC environment is essential for resolving microsecond-scale combustion events, turbulent flow in heat exchangers, and system-wide energy transfers simultaneously, which would otherwise be computationally intractable. Expected outcomes include predictive models for hybrid system performance under diverse scenarios, validated against experimental data from lab-scale marine engine testbeds. These models will inform the design of adaptive control systems to reduce fuel consumption by 10–15% and nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions by 20% compared to conventional configurations. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular code libraries to support future research in marine energy systems. By advancing computational capabilities in marine engineering, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of sustainable technologies in maritime industries, aligning with global decarbonization goals while maintaining operational reliability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in shipboard mechanical and electrical engineering and the maintenance and operation of marine engines, including gas, diesel, and steam engines. Includes instruction in automation, diesel-powered systems, electrical circuits and systems, engine performance, hydraulics, manufacturing, motor-powered systems, refrigeration and air-conditioning, steam-powered systems, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural production and transnational identity formation of Latinx communities in the U.S., with a focus on Mexican-American/Chicano and Puerto Rican diasporic narratives. The research problem centers on analyzing large-scale, multilingual textual and audiovisual archives—including community newspapers, oral histories, digital media, and literature—to identify patterns of cultural resilience, hybridity, and resistance across generational and geographic divides. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these datasets, which span decades and incorporate code-switching, vernacular expressions, and non-standardized Spanish-English dialects. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) tailored for mixed-language corpora, network analysis to map thematic and discursive connections across communities, and machine learning models to trace evolving representations of identity in creative works. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on custom Latinx linguistic datasets, parallel processing of multimedia files, and visualizing dynamic cultural networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated materials, computational tools optimized for Latinx cultural analytics, and new interdisciplinary frameworks for studying intersectional identity in diasporic contexts. By bridging computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to amplify underrepresented narratives, inform culturally responsive pedagogy, and empower community-driven research partnerships. The work aligns with the program’s mission to center Latinx epistemologies while innovating methodologies for preserving and interpreting cultural heritage in the digital age.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Hispanic-American, Puerto Rican, Latinx, and Mexican-American/ Chicano Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic American immigrant populations within the U.S. and Canada, including Mexican-American Studies, Cuban American Studies, Puerto Rican Studies, and others.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the adaptive reuse of underutilized urban spaces in response to dynamic socioeconomic and environmental pressures, a critical challenge in contemporary urban planning. Traditional planning tools often struggle to account for the complex, nonlinear interactions between policy interventions, community behavior, and spatial constraints, particularly in rapidly changing neighborhoods. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with geospatial machine learning to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes and their cascading impacts on urban form. The model will incorporate high-resolution datasets including property records, mobility patterns, environmental sensor data, and community survey responses to capture both quantitative metrics and qualitative values associated with space utilization. Key computational challenges involve scaling heterogeneous data assimilation across metropolitan regions while maintaining granular temporal resolution, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized scenario testing. The framework will enable planners to evaluate "what-if" scenarios for vacant lot activation, infrastructure retrofitting, and zoning flexibility under varying climate and economic conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for participatory planning that quantifies trade-offs between development intensity, social equity, and ecological resilience. By bridging computational social science with spatial planning practice, this work advances methodological innovation at the intersection of urban informatics and community-driven design. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated training of vision-transformer models for aerial image analysis and large-scale ABM simulations across 10^5 agent populations, directly addressing scalability barriers in current urban digital twin applications. Results will inform pilot projects in three partner cities undergoing post-industrial transition, demonstrating how computational planning tools can foster more responsive and inclusive urban regeneration strategies.
detailed_field: City/ urban, community, and regional planning
cip_title: City/ Urban, Community, and Regional Planning
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of planning, analysis, and architecture to the development and improvement of urban areas and surrounding regions, and to function as professional planners. Includes instruction in principles of architecture; master plan development; service, communications, and transportation systems design; community and commercial development; zoning; land use planning; applied economics; policy analysis; applicable laws and regulations; and professional responsibilities and managerial duties.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of minimizing food waste in full-service restaurant operations while maintaining customer satisfaction and profitability—a complex optimization problem exacerbated by volatile demand patterns, perishable inventory constraints, and dynamic consumer preferences. Traditional forecasting methods often fail to account for the high-dimensional interactions between seasonal trends, local events, real-time foot traffic, and supply chain disruptions. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates probabilistic machine learning, agent-based simulation, and multi-objective optimization. The computational model will synthesize heterogeneous data streams—including historical sales, weather forecasts, event calendars, and IoT-derived kitchen workflow metrics—to generate daily demand predictions with quantified uncertainty. These predictions will drive a parallelized Monte Carlo simulation engine to evaluate thousands of inventory procurement and prep schedules, optimizing for waste reduction, ingredient freshness, and service speed. The HPC infrastructure will enable real-time sensitivity analyses across 3–12 month horizons while incorporating stochastic variables like supplier delays and last-minute group reservations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system capable of reducing food waste by 15–25% in simulated mid-scale restaurant environments, alongside generalized insights about perishable inventory risk mitigation under demand uncertainty. By leveraging parallel GPU architectures to accelerate deep reinforcement learning components, this work aims to establish a scalable template for data-driven resource allocation in food service enterprises, directly contributing to both operational sustainability and financial resilience in the hospitality sector.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide food and/or lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage, and control; hotel and restaurant facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; facilities management; marketing and sale promotion strategies; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotel, motel, and/or restaurant operations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 52.0902.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time media transmission in dynamic communication networks, where fluctuating user demand and heterogeneous data types strain traditional resource allocation strategies. As streaming services, immersive media (e.g., VR/AR), and ultra-high-definition content proliferate, existing infrastructure often fails to balance latency, bandwidth efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale communication networks and simulate traffic patterns under varying load conditions. Computational methods include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate network performance metrics, machine learning algorithms trained on historical usage data to predict congestion points, and graph-based optimization techniques to dynamically allocate bandwidth and storage resources. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to develop adaptive frameworks that minimize latency while maintaining service quality across diverse media formats. Outcomes will include open-source tools for network operators to simulate deployment scenarios, alongside predictive models for proactive resource management. This work will directly inform scalable solutions for next-generation communication systems, reducing operational costs and enhancing user experience in media delivery. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the scale and complexity of network simulations, which require terabytes of traffic data and thousands of concurrent node interactions to accurately reflect real-world conditions. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and communications technology conferences, bridging academic research and practical infrastructure advancements.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to function as workers and managers within communications industries. Includes instruction in business economics; basic management; principles of interpersonal and mediated communications; radio, television, and digital media production; and related aspects of technology and communications systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing sustainability and operational efficiency in large-scale resort ecosystems through advanced computational modeling. Resorts face increasing pressure to reduce environmental impact while maintaining profitability and guest satisfaction, yet existing decision-making frameworks often rely on static, siloed data that fails to account for dynamic interactions between energy systems, guest behavior, and environmental conditions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation platform that integrates real-time data streams from IoT sensors, weather forecasts, and guest activity patterns to model resort-wide resource flows. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate guest decision-making with Monte Carlo methods to assess uncertainty in energy demand and renewable generation. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical datasets to predict peak resource utilization, while multi-objective optimization techniques will balance trade-offs between carbon emissions, operational costs, and service quality. High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets from participating resorts, run parallelized simulations of alternative sustainability strategies, and optimize complex systems encompassing water treatment, waste management, and smart grid integration. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that enables resort operators to test circular economy interventions—such as adaptive pricing for off-peak renewable energy use or AI-driven waste sorting systems—before physical implementation. The project will generate novel insights into the scalability of green technologies in hospitality contexts, with particular significance for island resorts facing climate vulnerabilities. By creating a computational framework that quantifies both environmental and business impacts of sustainability initiatives, this research aims to establish new standards for data-driven resource allocation in the $300 billion global resort industry while advancing methodological integration of complex systems theory in hospitality analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market comprehensive vacation facilities and services and related products. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, hotel/motel management, restaurant and food services management, facilities planning, leisure studies, recreation administration, marketing, recreation equipment and grounds operations and maintenance, business finance, insurance and taxation, event management and guest services, personnel management, travel and logistics management, safety and health services, professional standards and ethics, and applications to specific vacation types and locations.

abstract: Clinical laboratory testing is a cornerstone of modern healthcare, yet the growing complexity and volume of diagnostic data pose challenges for timely and accurate interpretation. This project seeks to address bottlenecks in clinical laboratory workflows by developing machine learning models to automate the analysis of high-dimensional data from routine tests, including hematology panels, microbiological cultures, and urinalysis. Current manual and semi-automated methods for anomaly detection, pathogen identification, and result correlation are labor-intensive and prone to human error, particularly in resource-constrained settings. We propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate deep learning architectures on multi-modal laboratory datasets. These datasets will integrate structured numerical results (e.g., complete blood counts, metabolic panels) with unstructured data such as microscopic images of blood smears and bacterial cultures. Neural networks, including convolutional and transformer-based models, will be optimized to identify patterns predictive of conditions such as sepsis, antibiotic resistance profiles, and renal dysfunction. The scale of data—encompassing tens of thousands of historical patient records and high-resolution images—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are infeasible with local institutional computing infrastructure. Successful implementation will yield two key outcomes: (1) an open-source toolkit for real-time laboratory data analysis, capable of flagging critical results and suggesting differential diagnoses, and (2) validated benchmarks for integrating predictive analytics into laboratory information systems. This work will directly enhance the training of clinical laboratory technicians by incorporating computational diagnostics into the curriculum, while improving patient outcomes through faster, more precise test interpretation. The requested HPC allocation will support data storage, preprocessing, and iterative model development, ensuring scalability and reproducibility for future clinical validation studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists/medical technologists, to perform routine medical laboratory procedures and tests and to apply preset strategies to record and analyze data. Includes instruction in general laboratory procedures and skills; laboratory mathematics; medical computer applications; interpersonal and communications skills; and the basic principles of hematology, medical microbiology, immunohematology, immunology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and chemical interactions between permanent cosmetic pigments and human skin tissues, with the goal of improving safety, longevity, and aesthetic outcomes in cosmetic tattooing. Despite the growing demand for permanent makeup and medical tattooing (e.g., scar camouflage, areola restoration), there remains a critical gap in understanding how pigment composition, particle size, and application techniques influence long-term stability and biocompatibility. Current industry standards rely on anecdotal evidence, with limited quantitative modeling of pigment migration, degradation kinetics, or inflammatory responses. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of pigment-skin interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) of dermal stress during needle insertion, and machine learning (ML) models trained on longitudinal clinical data. MD simulations will map binding affinities between common organic/inorganic pigments and collagen/elastin networks, while FEA models will quantify tissue trauma under varying needle geometries and motor speeds. Concurrently, ML algorithms will correlate these computational outputs with real-world outcomes using a dataset of 5,000+ anonymized client cases (provided by collaborating clinics) to identify risk factors for pigment fading or granuloma formation. The HPC environment is essential for handling the high-resolution 3D skin models, parallelized simulation workflows, and large-scale data integration required. Anticipated outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for pigment selection, needle configurations, and aftercare protocols, as well as a predictive tool for artists to customize techniques based on individual skin typology. By bridging cosmetic art with computational biomedicine, this work aims to establish a foundational framework for safer, more durable aesthetic outcomes while advancing regulatory science in an understudied domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to prepare and apply permanent markings, color, and cosmetic products to the face and body for aesthetic or clinical purposes; to remove unwanted markings; and to function as licensed permanent makeup artists and tattooists.  Includes instruction in client consultation; sterilization and sanitation; skin anatomy, diseases, and disorders; skin preparation and anesthetics; color theory; machine theory and operation; needle selection; applications such as eyebrows, eyeliners, lips, lipliners, beauty marks, and blemish/mark removal; after care; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized assistive technologies for individuals with physical and cognitive disabilities. Current methods for optimizing assistive devices—such as prosthetics, exoskeletons, and adaptive communication tools—often rely on generalized design frameworks, which may not account for the nuanced biomechanical, sensory, or psychosocial needs of diverse users. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline integrating high-fidelity biomechanical simulations, machine learning (ML), and multi-modal clinical data analysis. The research will focus on two aims: (1) modeling human-device interactions using physics-based simulations to predict strain, fatigue, and usability outcomes across anatomies and disability types, and (2) training ML algorithms on aggregated datasets (e.g., motion capture, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes) to identify patterns linking device configurations to functional improvements. Simulations will employ finite element analysis and musculoskeletal modeling via OpenSim, scaled across parameter spaces representing variations in body morphology, disability severity, and activity contexts. ML workflows will utilize convolutional and recurrent neural networks to process temporal-spatial data from clinical trials. HPC resources are critical for managing the computational intensity of parallelized simulations, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to guide device customization, reducing iterative prototyping time by 40–60%, and open-source tools to help clinicians match assistive technologies to patient-specific needs. This work directly aligns with rehabilitation science priorities by enhancing evidence-based, equitable access to adaptive technologies, while advancing computational methods tailored to the heterogeneity of disability experiences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with people who have learning disabilities, mental illness, and physical disabilities in a clinical, educational, or institutional setting. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, assistive technology, case management, counseling techniques, cultural diversity, disability assessment and measurement, ethics, psychological and physiological aspects of disability, rehabilitation services, rehabilitation science, and vocational counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to address the complex dynamics of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) propagation in aquatic ecosystems, a critical yet understudied nexus of environmental microbiology, hydrology, and public health. Traditional models often isolate biological, chemical, or physical drivers, neglecting their synergistic effects under climate variability and anthropogenic pressures. Our research aims to develop an integrative, multi-scale computational framework to predict AMR hotspots by coupling hydrodynamic transport, microbial community interactions, and contaminant dispersion across watersheds. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatially explicit simulations of water flow, sediment transport, and bacterial gene exchange at catchment scales, while concurrently modeling population-level genomic adaptation using stochastic agent-based methods. Parallelized numerical solvers will integrate real-world hydrological data, climate projections, and metagenomic datasets to quantify how agricultural runoff, urban wastewater, and extreme weather events modulate horizontal gene transfer and resistance persistence. Machine learning techniques will identify emergent patterns from petabyte-scale simulation outputs, enabling predictive mapping of high-risk zones. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source computational platform for AMR risk assessment, validated against field observations from partnered watershed studies. This work will advance predictive capabilities for mitigating AMR spread, directly informing land-use policies and water management strategies. By bridging ecological complexity with computational innovation, the project exemplifies interdisciplinary science addressing a grand challenge in global health and environmental sustainability.
