cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of scientific computing and its application. Includes instruction in scientific visualization, multi-scale analysis, grid generation, data analysis, applied mathematics, numerical algorithms, high performance parallel computing, and numerical modeling and simulation with applications in science, engineering and other disciplines in which computation plays an integral role.

abstract: Agricultural business operations increasingly rely on data-driven decision-making to optimize productivity, supply chain efficiency, and resource use. However, scaling analytical workflows to address complex, dynamic challenges—such as real-time crop yield forecasting, market trend modeling, and precision agriculture system optimization—requires computational resources beyond the capacity of standard institutional infrastructure. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy machine learning models integrating heterogeneous agricultural datasets, including high-resolution satellite imagery, IoT sensor outputs, historical yield records, and commodity pricing databases. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing spatially explicit, temporally dense datasets to generate actionable insights for farm management and agribusiness planning. Methods will focus on parallelized data preprocessing, distributed training of deep learning architectures (e.g., convolutional neural networks for image analysis, transformer models for time-series forecasting), and large-scale simulations of climate-resilient cropping strategies under market volatility scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory partitions, the team will quantify trade-offs between input costs, environmental factors, and profit margins across diverse agricultural systems. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for predictive analytics in crop selection, risk assessment frameworks for supply chain disruptions, and optimized irrigation scheduling algorithms compatible with precision agriculture platforms. This work will directly enhance the operational efficiency of agricultural businesses while providing students in Agricultural Business Technology with hands-on experience in computational agriculture methodologies. The requested resources will enable scaling analyses to regional levels, supporting evidence-based policy recommendations and technology adoption strategies for small-to-medium agribusiness enterprises.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized support functions related to agricultural business offices and operations and to operate agricultural office equipment, software, and information systems. Includes instruction in basic agricultural business principles, office management, equipment operation, standard software, and database management.

abstract: The fabrication and repair of musical instruments rely heavily on empirical methods, with outcomes dependent on artisan expertise and iterative physical prototyping. While effective, this approach limits systematic exploration of material properties, structural dynamics, and acoustic interactions, particularly for complex or novel designs. This project proposes the integration of high-performance computing (HPC) to advance instrument design and repair through computational modeling and simulation. The research focuses on two interconnected challenges: (1) optimizing vibrational behavior in acoustic instruments by analyzing material-structure-sound relationships, and (2) developing predictive frameworks for aging and damage in both acoustic and electric instruments. A multi-physics computational approach will be employed, combining finite element analysis (FEA) for structural resonance, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for air-coupled systems in wind instruments, and machine learning (ML) to correlate simulation data with empirical acoustic measurements. HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of material composites (e.g., alternative woods, bio-based polymers), geometric variations, and environmental stressors. For electric instruments, electromagnetic simulations will model pickup configurations and signal degradation in aging components. The computational pipeline will be validated against laser vibrometry measurements and acoustic testing in controlled environments. Expected outcomes include predictive models for instrument performance across design parameters, a digital toolkit for virtual prototyping, and data-driven guidelines for repairing historical instruments while preserving tonal integrity. By bridging traditional craftsmanship with computational engineering, this work aims to reduce material waste in fabrication, extend instrument lifespans through precision repair strategies, and democratize access to advanced instrument design capabilities. The resource-intensive nature of coupled multiphysics simulations—requiring parallelized solvers, high memory bandwidth, and GPU acceleration—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve the resolution and iteration scales needed for actionable insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and tune acoustic and electric musical instruments. Includes instruction in methods and equipment for making musical instruments, electronic instrument amplification systems, techniques of cleaning, and methods of tuning musical instruments.

abstract: The optimization of chemical manufacturing processes is hindered by the complex interplay of reaction kinetics, transport phenomena, and thermodynamic equilibria, which are computationally prohibitive to model at industrial scales using conventional methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale simulations of catalytic reactor systems and separation processes central to petroleum refining and pharmaceutical production. The research will integrate quantum chemical calculations for catalyst surface interactions, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for reactor-scale hydrodynamics, and machine learning algorithms to predict process bottlenecks and optimize operating conditions. A key focus is modeling transient behaviors in fluidized bed reactors and membrane-based separations, where traditional steady-state assumptions fail to capture dynamic inefficiencies. The computational workflow will utilize parallelized solvers in OpenFOAM and LAMMPS, coupled with custom Python-based optimization frameworks, to reduce simulation timescales from weeks to days while maintaining atomistic resolution in critical regions. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting catalyst deactivation pathways, optimizing energy consumption in distillation sequences, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions in methane reforming processes. By enabling high-fidelity virtual prototyping, this work will directly address scalability challenges in sustainable chemical manufacturing, particularly for carbon capture and hydrogen production systems. The requested HPC resources will support large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and the training of neural networks on heterogeneous datasets spanning molecular dynamics trajectories and plant-scale sensor data. Successful implementation will provide open-access simulation tools for the chemical processing community, reduce reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches, and accelerate the translation of laboratory-scale innovations to industrial deployment. This project aligns with broader goals of enhancing process safety, minimizing environmental footprints, and training the next generation of computational researchers in science-driven industrial problem-solving.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of chemical processing equipment in industries such as chemical manufacturing, petroleum refining, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and waste water treatment. Includes instruction in mathematics, chemistry, and physics; computer applications; chemical and refinery plant operations, processes, and equipment; safety, health, and environment; instrumentation; troubleshooting; and applications to specific industries.

abstract: This project seeks to develop adaptive, real-time procedural content generation (PCG) systems for interactive game environments by integrating player behavior modeling with high-fidelity physics simulations. While procedural techniques are widely used to automate game asset creation, existing methods often lack dynamic responsiveness to individual player interactions, resulting in environments that feel static or disconnected from gameplay. This research addresses the challenge of balancing computational efficiency with real-time adaptability, particularly in complex 3D environments where player actions influence terrain deformation, object interactions, and non-player character (NPC) behaviors. The core computational methodology combines deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for player preference prediction with parallelized fluid dynamics and granular material simulations. High-performance computing resources will enable the simultaneous execution of multiple physics engines alongside DRL training cycles, allowing iterative optimization of environment generation algorithms under varying player interaction scenarios. Key technical hurdles include minimizing latency between player input and environmental response while maintaining visual fidelity, as well as ensuring scalable synchronization between discrete simulation modules. The project will validate outcomes through automated playtesting frameworks that measure emergent player engagement metrics across generated environments. Successful implementation could establish new paradigms for responsive PCG systems, reducing development costs for open-world games while enhancing player immersion through environments that evolve meaningfully in response to individual playstyles. This work bridges gaps between computational creativity, human-computer interaction, and real-time physics simulation—advancing game design capabilities through tightly integrated applications of machine learning and high-performance computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in urban public transportation systems by developing a computational framework to optimize multimodal network design and dynamic resource allocation under fluctuating demand. Public transit agencies face challenges in balancing operational costs, environmental impact, and service quality, particularly as cities integrate emerging mobility technologies (e.g., ride-sharing, microtransit) with traditional fixed-route systems. Existing planning tools often lack the scalability to model city-scale networks or the flexibility to account for real-time disruptions and behavioral shifts. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-objective optimization model that simultaneously evaluates infrastructure investments, fleet deployment strategies, and pricing policies across transportation modes. Agent-based simulations will capture traveler decision-making patterns using synthetic populations derived from census data, GPS traces, and transit smart card records. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical datasets to predict demand variability under different economic and environmental scenarios. Computational experiments will focus on metropolitan regions with documented last-mile connectivity gaps and congestion bottlenecks. The HPC environment is critical for running parallelized simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, enabling sensitivity analyses of factors such as energy costs, equity constraints, and carbon emission targets. Expected outcomes include a decision support toolkit for transit agencies to evaluate trade-offs between capital expenditures, service frequency adjustments, and technology adoption timelines. Results will advance academic understanding of scalability challenges in mobility system modeling while providing actionable insights for public-private partnership structures in transportation management. This work directly aligns with transportation policy innovation goals in business administration by quantifying risk-mitigation strategies for large-scale infrastructure projects.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, policy, law, and practices required to administrate and operate public transportation facilities, networks, services, and systems. Includes instruction in demand analysis and forecasting, environmental planning, facilities design and construction, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, multi- and intermodal transportation systems, project management, public administration, public policy, transportation economics, transportation law, transportation operations, transportation systems, and transportation technologies.

abstract: Forensic nursing practice requires the integration of complex biological, legal, and contextual data to support victim care and criminal investigations. However, current methods for analyzing forensic evidence—such as injury documentation, toxicology reports, and crime scene data—often rely on manual processes or siloed computational tools, limiting scalability and accuracy. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to analyze multimodal forensic datasets, including wound patterns, genomic data from sexual assault cases, and longitudinal health records. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) creating machine learning models to classify injury mechanisms and predict associated health risks using 3D imaging and biomechanical simulations; (2) optimizing genomic sequence analysis pipelines to rapidly identify forensic biomarkers in drug-facilitated crimes; and (3) integrating natural language processing (NLP) to extract temporal and spatial relationships from clinical notes, law enforcement reports, and court documents. These tasks demand parallel processing, large-scale data storage, and GPU acceleration to handle high-resolution images, whole-genome sequencing data, and unstructured text. The proposed HPC resources will enable the development of predictive tools to guide evidence collection, improve the reliability of medicolegal testimony, and identify patterns in interpersonal violence. Outcomes will include open-source algorithms tailored to forensic nursing workflows, validated through collaborations with hospital forensic teams and legal agencies. By enhancing the precision and efficiency of forensic data analysis, this project aims to advance trauma-informed care practices, reduce investigative timelines, and strengthen the scientific rigor of nursing contributions to criminal justice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the law and forensic science to nursing practice and collaborate with other professionals for the care of victims and the prosecution of criminals. Includes instruction in advanced physical assessment, evidence collection and preservation, forensic anthropology, legal testimony, medicolegal investigation, pathophysiology, pathohistology, pharmacology, and violence prevention.

abstract: The sustainable transformation of lignocellulosic biomass into high-value wood products and pulp-derived materials requires precise understanding of molecular-scale interactions and process-structure-property relationships. Current limitations in experimental characterization hinder the optimization of energy-intensive industrial processes such as chemical pulping, fiber modification, and composite manufacturing. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that bridge atomic-scale phenomena with macroscopic material behavior. Molecular dynamics simulations will investigate lignin depolymerization kinetics and cellulose microfibril interactions during pulping, while finite element analysis will predict mechanical performance of engineered wood composites under hygrothermal stresses. Machine learning models trained on integrated simulation and experimental datasets will identify optimal processing parameters for targeted material properties. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallelization to manage complex polymer networks (exceeding 10^6 atoms), stochastic fiber arrangements in composites, and high-dimensional optimization landscapes. Anticipated outcomes include predictive frameworks for reducing thermal energy consumption in kraft pulping by 15-20%, designing formaldehyde-free adhesives with improved moisture resistance, and accelerating development of cellulose-based nanomaterials for packaging applications. By enabling virtual prototyping of biorefinery processes and advanced wood products, this research will directly support conservation-oriented resource utilization, reduced carbon footprints in forest product industries, and circular economy transitions. The requested HPC allocations will facilitate time-resolved simulations of delignification reactions, parametric studies of composite durability, and neural network training across diverse wood species—tasks infeasible with institutional computing infrastructure. Results will be validated through partnerships with pulp mills and composite manufacturers, ensuring translational impact for sustainable material innovation.
cip_title: Wood Science and Wood Products/ Pulp and Paper Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the analysis of the properties and behavior of wood and wood products and the development of processes for converting wood into paper and other products. Includes instruction in wood classification and testing, product development, manufacturing and processing technologies, and the design and development of related equipment and systems.

abstract: The increasing availability of large-scale genomic and health data presents unprecedented opportunities to address complex questions in public health genetics. However, current analytical frameworks struggle to model the multidimensional interactions between genetic, environmental, and sociodemographic factors that drive population-level health disparities. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced computational models investigating the polygenic and environmental determinants of cardiometabolic diseases in underserved populations. Using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics from diverse biobanks (n > 1.5 million individuals) paired with geospatial environmental exposure data, we will implement machine learning architectures to identify gene-environment interactions influencing disease risk. Computational workflows will integrate Bayesian hierarchical models, deep neural networks for epistasis detection, and agent-based simulations of intervention scenarios. The scale of these analyses—requiring iterative processing of terabyte-scale datasets, combinatorial testing of >10^12 potential SNP pairs, and stochastic simulations across parameter spaces—necessitates parallelized GPU/CPU workflows with large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of novel interaction effects modifying disease penetrance in specific environmental contexts, 2) development of open-source tools for ethical analysis of sensitive genotype-phenotype-environment data, and 3) policy-relevant models quantifying how targeted genetic risk mitigation could reduce health inequities. By elucidating mechanisms through which genetic susceptibilities interact with structural determinants of health, this work will directly inform precision public health strategies while advancing computational methods for responsible translation of genomic discoveries. The requested resources will enable critical scaling of our proof-of-concept analyses to nationally representative datasets, ensuring statistical power to detect effects in marginalized communities often underrepresented in genetic studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to respond to the complex social, legal, ethical, and public health policy implications generated by genetic research. Includes instruction in biochemical genetics of complex diseases, bioethics, chromosomes and human disease, genetic counseling, genetic epidemiology, gene mapping, human population genetics, and the molecular basis of human inherited disease.

abstract: Orthopedic conditions, particularly those affecting load-bearing joints, present complex biomechanical challenges that are difficult to model using conventional experimental methods. Current limitations in predicting long-term outcomes of surgical interventions or implant performance stem from an incomplete understanding of multiscale tissue mechanics and patient-specific variability. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate musculoskeletal dynamics, bone remodeling, and implant-tissue interactions under physiologically realistic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling to capture mechanobiological processes across spatial scales, from cellular responses to whole-joint biomechanics. Patient-specific anatomical data, including CT and MRI-derived geometries, will inform model parametrization, while machine learning techniques will optimize computational efficiency by identifying reduced-order representations of high-dimensional datasets. The proposed simulations will quantify stress-shielding effects in orthopedic implants, predict bone adaptation patterns post-surgery, and evaluate the biomechanical consequences of anatomical variations across diverse patient populations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for implant failure risk, data-driven guidelines for personalized surgical planning, and mechanistic insights into osteoarthritis progression. The computational demands of this work necessitate HPC infrastructure due to the requirement for parallel processing of large-scale multiphysics simulations (10^6-10^7 elements per model), ensemble runs for population-level analysis, and iterative optimization of machine learning architectures. Successful implementation will provide clinical researchers with an open-source simulation platform to test intervention strategies in silico, potentially reducing costly postoperative complications and accelerating the development of next-generation orthopedic treatments.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to enhance the detection and analysis of manipulated visual media in photojournalism, addressing growing ethical challenges in an era of AI-generated and altered content. As digital manipulation techniques become increasingly sophisticated, photojournalists and news organizations face mounting difficulties in verifying the authenticity of images and videos, undermining public trust. Traditional manual verification methods are insufficient for large-scale, real-time analysis, particularly in crisis reporting. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining deep learning models for forensic analysis with metadata pattern recognition to identify tampering artifacts across still and video journalism. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train vision transformers (ViTs) on a curated dataset of 2.3 million authenticated and manipulated journalistic images, including synthetic examples from generative adversarial networks (GANs) and diffusion models. Concurrently, distributed computing frameworks will analyze temporal-spatial relationships in video metadata at scale. Key technical challenges include developing lightweight detection models deployable in field reporting environments and creating temporal alignment algorithms for video authentication. Expected outcomes include an open-source verification toolkit optimized for photojournalistic workflows, benchmark datasets for ethical AI development in media, and new computational metrics for assessing manipulation likelihood. The project directly supports photojournalism's professional ethics by advancing verification capabilities while maintaining the computational demands of high-resolution media analysis. By utilizing HPC resources for parallel processing of terabyte-scale visual datasets and complex model training, this work bridges computational photography and journalistic practice, offering novel methods to preserve documentary integrity in digital journalism. Results will be disseminated through journalism industry partnerships and computational media ethics forums, providing critical infrastructure for combating misinformation while respecting legal and ethical constraints on media analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of still and motion photography in journalism and prepares individuals to function as news photographers and photographic editors. Includes instruction in photography, journalism, studio procedures and techniques, camera and equipment operation and technique, news editing, print and film editing, news scene composition, subject surveillance, media law and policy, news team field operations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model wildfire propagation and suppression dynamics, addressing critical gaps in current fire behavior prediction systems. Wildfires present a growing threat to ecosystems, infrastructure, and public safety, exacerbated by climate change and urban expansion into wildland interfaces. Existing models often lack the spatial granularity and integration of real-time environmental variables necessary to predict fire spread in complex terrains or under rapidly shifting weather conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled atmosphere-fire numerical model that integrates computational fluid dynamics (CFD), fuel moisture dynamics, and stochastic ignition scenarios at meter-scale resolution. The framework will utilize parallelized simulations to account for multi-scale interactions between fireline behavior, localized wind patterns, and fuel heterogeneity, validated against historical fire perimeter data and controlled burn experiments. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to identify high-risk ignition zones and optimize resource deployment strategies. By enabling near-real-time scenario testing for fire departments and land managers, this research aims to improve tactical decision-making during active fire incidents and long-term risk mitigation planning. Expected outcomes include an open-source modeling toolkit for fire agencies, enhanced predictive accuracy for fire spread under extreme weather conditions, and data-driven recommendations for fuel management prioritization. The computational demands of resolving fine-scale physics and running ensemble forecasts for probabilistic risk assessment necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large memory capacity. This work will directly support firefighter safety, community resilience, and evidence-based policy in wildfire-prone regions, while advancing computational methodologies for fire science within the homeland security domain.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the dynamics of intergenerational caregiving networks and their impact on family resilience in rapidly aging populations. Traditional qualitative and survey-based methods in human development research struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions, feedback loops, and adaptive behaviors that characterize these complex social systems. Our work addresses this gap by employing agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate caregiving ecosystems across diverse cultural and socioeconomic contexts. The research integrates longitudinal demographic data, household economic surveys, and psychosocial metrics from public repositories with ethnographic case studies to parameterize multi-scale models. Computational challenges include simulating thousands of autonomous agents with heterogeneous decision-making algorithms, tracking resource flows across kinship networks, and analyzing emergent patterns through temporal graph metrics. HPC resources will enable sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces, Monte Carlo simulations to assess intervention scenarios, and machine learning approaches to identify critical leverage points for policy design. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of caregiving network stability under demographic and economic stressors, (2) evidence-based criteria for tailoring community support programs to kinship structures, and (3) open-source tools for simulating culturally situated family dynamics. By bridging computational social science with human development theory, this work advances methodological capacity to study relational systems that defy traditional disciplinary boundaries. The results will inform interventions addressing the global care crisis while establishing scalable computational workflows for family studies research. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale graph database management, and comparative analysis of terabyte-scale synthetic population datasets.
cip_title: Human Development, Family Studies, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in human development, family studies, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of pharmacological mechanisms underlying traditional Chinese herbal formulae, with a focus on multi-component interactions and their systemic effects on human physiology. While Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has long utilized complex herbal combinations to treat diseases holistically, the molecular basis of their efficacy remains underexplored due to the combinatorial complexity of bioactive compounds and the lack of scalable computational frameworks. Current limitations in processing power and algorithmic efficiency hinder systematic analysis of herb-herb and herb-protein interactions at the scale required for clinically relevant formulae. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow integrating cheminformatics, molecular docking, and machine learning to model the polypharmacology of classical TCM prescriptions. Molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to study dynamic interactions between herbal compounds and target proteins implicated in immune regulation, metabolic homeostasis, and inflammation—key pathways in TCM diagnostic frameworks. Network pharmacology approaches will map multi-target effects, while generative AI models will predict synergistic herb combinations based on historical texts and modern pharmacopeia. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from collaborator labs, including metabolomic and proteomic studies of patient samples. By enabling large-scale virtual screening of herbal libraries and dynamic modeling of formula-body interactions, this work aims to identify novel bioactive candidates, elucidate synergistic principles of herbal配伍 (compatibility), and establish predictive frameworks for optimizing personalized TCM treatments. Outcomes will bridge empirical TCM knowledge with modern systems biology, providing a foundation for evidence-based herbology and fostering innovation in integrative medicine. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the terabytes of simulation data, training deep learning models on compound-target networks, and iterating complex multi-scale analyses within project timelines.
cip_title: Traditional Chinese Medicine and Chinese Herbology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Chinese herbal medicine, a system based on the use of nutrition, natural products, and prescribed medical formulae to treat imbalances in the state of bodily health as defined in the Nei Ching Su Wen and other authorities. Includes instruction in the basic Western medical sciences, history and theory of Chinese medicine, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbology, herbal prescription preparation, herbal patent medicine, herbal pharmacology, Chinese internal medicine and gynecology, febrile diseases, food therapy, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting individual variability in drug response by integrating metabolomic and proteomic data with patient-specific physiological parameters, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of computational biology and precision health. Current approaches to drug response modeling often rely on population-level averages, neglecting the complex interplay between dynamic cellular processes and systemic factors such as organ function or circadian rhythms. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing a multiscale computational framework that simulates drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics at cellular, tissue, and whole-organism levels using individualized biological data. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized agent-based models of hepatic drug metabolism coupled with finite element analyses of vascular transport. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic datasets generated through these simulations to identify patterns linking molecular signatures with clinical outcomes. The computational workflow will incorporate real-world electronic health record data (de-identified and ethically approved) to validate predictions regarding drug clearance rates and adverse event risks. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of predicting patient-specific drug responses with greater accuracy than current clinical tools, particularly for populations with non-standard metabolic profiles. This work will advance personalized treatment strategies while providing a novel educational resource for pre-pharmacy students to explore systems pharmacology concepts through interactive computational modules. The HPC resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of biological networks and enabling rapid iteration of predictive models across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Successful implementation could transform early-phase drug candidate evaluation and inform precision dosing guidelines for special populations often excluded from traditional clinical trials.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, hyper-personalized merchandising strategies in fragmented omnichannel retail environments. Traditional marketing operations frameworks struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between consumer micro-segments, dynamic inventory constraints, and context-dependent pricing signals across hybrid physical-digital platforms. The project will develop a computational architecture combining agent-based modeling, multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, and transformer-based demand forecasting to simulate decision cascades in systems with >10^6 interacting variables. Key innovations include the integration of stochastic geospatial traffic patterns with individual psychographic profiles derived from multimodal behavioral data (transaction logs, IoT sensor feeds, social sentiment streams). Computational experiments will quantify trade-offs between inventory allocation efficiency, margin preservation, and customer lifetime value under rapid market shifts. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across heterogeneous scenario trees while maintaining sub-minute latency for prescriptive analytics. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support framework for automated merchandising policy adaptation, validated against real-world datasets from partner organizations in specialty retail and direct-to-consumer manufacturing. This work advances both business practice—by enabling granular profitability optimization in complex sales ecosystems—and computational social science methodology through its synthesis of graph neural networks with discrete-event simulation at unprecedented scale. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated training of attention mechanisms for cross-channel influence mapping and distributed memory architectures for global constraint satisfaction in mixed-integer optimization subproblems.
cip_title: Specialized Merchandising, Sales, and Marketing Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sales, marketing, and distribution operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework that optimizes personalized learning and career pathways for students with intellectual disabilities enrolled in Comprehensive Transition and Postsecondary (CTP) programs. Despite the demonstrated success of CTP programs in fostering academic, social, and vocational growth, a critical challenge lies in systematically tailoring interventions to individual needs while accounting for the dynamic interplay of academic progress, social integration, independent living skill development, and employment readiness. Current program evaluations rely on fragmented datasets and static analyses, limiting the ability to forecast long-term outcomes or adapt support strategies in real time. To address this gap, we propose a multidisciplinary computational approach integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and network analysis. Agent-based models will simulate student interactions within academic, social, and vocational environments, capturing emergent behaviors and systemic barriers. Machine learning algorithms, trained on longitudinal datasets encompassing academic performance, employment tracking, and behavioral assessments, will identify patterns predictive of successful transitions to independent living and gainful employment. Network analysis will map resource allocation efficacy across program components. These computationally intensive methods require HPC resources to manage large-scale simulations, hyperparameter optimization for predictive models, and real-time data processing from diverse sources (e.g., wearable sensors for skill practice monitoring, digital portfolios). Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for educators to customize interventions, predictive metrics for proactive resource allocation, and evidence-based insights into the systemic factors most critical to student success. By bridging computational social science and educational praxis, this project aims to advance equity in postsecondary outcomes for students with intellectual disabilities while establishing a replicable framework for data-driven program design in disability studies.
cip_definition: A comprehensive transition and postsecondary (CTP) program that provides students with intellectual disabilities with academic enrichment, socialization, independent living skills, self-advocacy skills, and integrated work experiences and career skills that lead to gainful employment.

abstract: Communication disorders arising from neurological impairment, such as aphasia or dysarthria, present complex challenges in diagnosis and treatment due to heterogeneous neural substrates and dynamic interactions between cognitive, linguistic, and motor systems. Current neurocomputational models often oversimplify these interactions, limiting their clinical utility for personalized intervention design. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating neuroimaging, speech acoustics, and behavioral data to model impaired communication networks in individuals with acquired brain injuries. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement biologically constrained neural network models that simulate cortical-subcortical interactions during speech-language tasks, informed by patient-specific diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and functional MRI connectivity maps. Machine learning pipelines will analyze high-dimensional speech kinematic datasets (electromagnetic articulography, vocal tract imaging) alongside neural activity patterns to identify compensatory mechanisms underlying functional recovery. Computational demands include large-scale parameter optimization for individualized neural models, real-time simulation of coupled oscillatory networks governing speech motor control, and multimodal data fusion across temporal resolutions (millisecond-scale articulatory kinematics to second-range fMRI). Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of communication impairment subtypes based on network dysfunction patterns, predictive models of treatment responsiveness, and open-source tools for simulating neuromodulation strategies targeting language-motor interfaces. This work bridges gaps between systems neuroscience and clinical speech-pathology by quantifying how distributed neural dynamics shape communicative function—a critical step toward precision rehabilitation. HPC resources are essential given the need to process terabytes of neuroimaging and speech sensor data, execute computationally intensive brain network simulations, and train deep learning architectures for cross-modal feature extraction within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of translational research using animal models necessitates advanced computational approaches to address limitations in data integration and predictive accuracy. Current methods for analyzing high-throughput genomic, proteomic, and phenomic datasets in laboratory animals are constrained by computational bottlenecks, particularly in multi-omics integration and dynamic modeling of disease progression. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable framework for real-time analysis of longitudinal datasets from murine and zebrafish models of neurodegenerative diseases and metabolic syndromes. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble methods) to identify cross-species biomarkers and simulate therapeutic interventions through agent-based modeling. Parallelized molecular dynamics simulations will characterize conserved protein interaction networks underlying disease phenotypes across species. The integration of colony management data, including breeding records and environmental variables, will enable predictive modeling of experimental reproducibility using multivariate regression techniques. By utilizing GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures, this project aims to overcome current limitations in processing latency, enabling the analysis of terabyte-scale datasets within biologically relevant timeframes. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel translational biomarkers, optimization of experimental animal use through predictive welfare assessment models, and generation of open-source tools for ethical data-driven experimental design. These advancements will directly enhance the translational validity of preclinical studies while aligning with the 3Rs principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) through computational hypothesis testing. The requested resources will support critical infrastructure for comparative pathobiology research, bridging computational science and laboratory animal medicine.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: Welding processes are inherently complex, involving multiphysics interactions between thermal, mechanical, and metallurgical phenomena that influence joint integrity and performance. Current experimental and analytical methods struggle to fully resolve these interactions at the scales required to predict defects, optimize parameters for advanced materials (e.g., high-entropy alloys, polymer composites), or validate novel hybrid welding techniques. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop high-fidelity, multiscale models of welding systems. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) simulating transient heat transfer and fluid dynamics in molten weld pools under varying process conditions (e.g., laser-arc hybrid welding, friction stir welding), (2) predicting microstructure evolution and residual stress distributions in dissimilar material joints, and (3) integrating machine learning workflows to accelerate parameter optimization for additive manufacturing applications. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for thermomechanical modeling, phase-field simulations for microstructure prediction, and coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-discrete element modeling (DEM) for powder-bed fusion processes. These simulations will be validated against experimental data from in-situ monitoring systems, including high-speed imaging and synchrotron X-ray diffraction. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to overcome memory and processing constraints that currently limit spatial-temporal resolution in welding simulations, particularly for large-scale or multi-pass welds. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce trial-and-error in welding procedure development, insights into defect formation mechanisms in next-generation materials, and frameworks for real-time simulation-aided control of robotic welding systems. The results will directly support curriculum development in computational welding engineering and provide industry partners with validated models to enhance quality assurance protocols under ASME and AWS standards. This work aligns with national priorities in advanced manufacturing, emphasizing sustainable process optimization and the integration of digital twins into smart manufacturing systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the design and engineering of welding and joining systems and the implementation of welding processes. Includes instruction in materials science; computer-aided design; welding design; welding processes; welding metallurgy; automation and robotics; and codes, inspections, testing, and quality assurance.

abstract: Somatic bodywork therapies, such as Rolfing/Structural Integration and lymphatic drainage, are increasingly utilized to address chronic pain, postural dysfunction, and stress-related conditions. However, the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly quantified, hindering evidence-based optimization and integration into broader healthcare frameworks. This project proposes a computational biomechanics study to model multiscale tissue responses to manual therapy techniques, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome current limitations in simulating complex, dynamic interactions between applied mechanical forces and biological systems. The research will develop patient-specific finite element models integrating MRI/CT-derived anatomical data, viscoelastic tissue properties, and neural feedback loops to simulate how targeted manual interventions alter fascial strain distributions, fluid dynamics in lymphatic networks, and proprioceptive signaling. A parallel machine learning pipeline will analyze clinical outcome datasets (pain scales, mobility metrics) to identify predictive patterns linking intervention parameters to therapeutic efficacy. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further investigate pressure propagation during hydrotherapy and colon hydrotherapy protocols. By resolving submillisecond tissue deformation dynamics and system-wide physiological cascades, this multiscale approach addresses critical gaps in understanding dose-response relationships and safety thresholds for diverse somatic modalities. Anticipated outcomes include predictive frameworks for personalizing force application patterns, biomarkers for real-time efficacy monitoring, and mechanistic insights into how manual therapies modulate autonomic nervous system activity. The computational tools developed will establish a foundation for rigorous quantitative evaluation of somatic practices, enabling their systematic refinement and evidence-based inclusion in interdisciplinary pain management and rehabilitation strategies. This work requires HPC resources to manage high-resolution 3D simulations, optimize neural network architectures across therapy subtypes, and perform parameter sensitivity analyses at clinically relevant scales.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote physical and emotional balance and well-being through the application of skilled touch principles and techniques. Includes instruction in therapeutic massage and other hands-on touch methods, anatomy and physiology, structural/functional integration and various holistic health systems (Rolfing/Structural Integration, colon hydrotherapy, Breema, Hellerwork, lymphatic drainage, Rosen Method, hydrotherapy, and others), client counseling, practice management, and applicable regulations and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary scholarship in African-American/Black history and literature by analyzing large-scale textual and historical datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in computational approaches to studying the cultural, social, and political narratives of the African diaspora in North America and the Caribbean. While traditional humanities methods have produced foundational insights, the volume and complexity of archival materials—including digitized newspapers, oral histories, slave narratives, and 20th-century literary works—require scalable computational tools to uncover patterns, connections, and underrepresented voices across time and geography. The project will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) models, machine learning classifiers, and network analysis algorithms to trace thematic shifts, linguistic evolution, and cross-regional influences within Black diasporic texts. Key computational tasks include topic modeling of abolitionist writings from 1780–1865, sentiment analysis of Harlem Renaissance poetry and prose, and geospatial mapping of migration narratives in Caribbean literature. These analyses will integrate with historical datasets such as census records, fugitive slave advertisements, and colonial trade documents to contextualize literary production within socioeconomic and political frameworks. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on non-standardized historical text corpora, processing multilingual sources (e.g., Creole, French, Spanish), and running iterative simulations to validate hypotheses about cultural transmission. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated texts, visualizations of intertextual networks across diasporic regions, and new methodological frameworks for computational humanities scholarship. By bridging literary analysis, historiography, and data science, this project aims to deepen understanding of how Black intellectual traditions have shaped—and been shaped by—transnational systems of power, resistance, and collective memory. The findings will support curricular innovation in African-American studies while providing scalable computational models for future interdisciplinary research on marginalized narratives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and operational efficiency of high-power laser systems, addressing critical challenges in thermal management and beam quality degradation. High-power lasers are integral to applications such as precision manufacturing, medical device development, and telecommunications; however, thermal-induced optical distortions and nonlinear effects limit their performance and reliability. Traditional experimental approaches to mitigate these issues are costly and time-intensive, necessitating a robust computational framework to accelerate innovation. The proposed research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions within laser systems, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for thermal-structural modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cooling system optimization, and wave optics simulations to assess beam propagation under dynamic thermal loads. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to analyze simulation outputs and identify optimal parameter combinations for minimizing thermal aberrations while maximizing energy efficiency. The computational workflow will leverage parallel processing to manage large-scale datasets and complex interdependencies across physical domains. Expected outcomes include predictive models for real-time thermal management, validated design protocols for next-generation laser resonators, and a scalable simulation toolkit to guide experimental validation. By reducing reliance on iterative trial-and-error prototyping, this work will lower development costs and enhance the safety and precision of laser-based systems. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations required for accurate modeling of nonlinear optical phenomena and transient thermal behavior, enabling advancements in laser technology with direct commercial and research applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using lasers and other optical for commercial or research purposes. Includes instruction in laser and optical principles, testing and maintenance procedures, safety precautions, specific applications to various tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of diet-related chronic diseases necessitates precision nutrition strategies tailored to individual metabolic, genetic, and lifestyle factors. However, current approaches for designing personalized dietary interventions lack the computational power to integrate multidimensional data—including metabolomic profiles, gut microbiome composition, and real-time dietary intake—at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that optimize dietary recommendations for diverse populations. The research will utilize large datasets from longitudinal cohort studies, clinical trials, and public health registries, encompassing variables such as nutrient absorption kinetics, inflammatory biomarkers, and behavioral patterns. Computational methods will include machine learning algorithms to identify nonlinear relationships between dietary components and health outcomes, agent-based modeling to simulate population-level dietary adherence scenarios, and genome-scale metabolic reconstructions to predict individual nutrient utilization efficiencies. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data and iterative model training, which are infeasible on local infrastructure due to memory and runtime constraints. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for dynamically adjusting dietary plans based on real-time biomarker feedback, validated against clinical outcomes in subsamples of diabetic and cardiovascular patient populations. This work will advance the field of dietetics by providing evidence-based tools to improve the precision of nutrition interventions, reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, and inform policy decisions about population-level dietary guidelines. The resulting models and pipelines will be disseminated through open-access platforms to support translational research in clinical and community nutrition settings. By bridging computational innovation with nutritional science, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven dietetics that addresses both individual health needs and public health priorities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to integrate and apply the principles of the food and nutrition sciences, human behavior, and the biomedical sciences to design and manage effective nutrition programs in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in human nutrition; nutrient metabolism; the role of foods and nutrition in health promotion and disease prevention; planning and directing food service activities; diet and nutrition analysis and planning; supervision of food storage and preparation; client education; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community-driven decision-making processes by modeling the complex dynamics of resource allocation in underserved populations. Community organizations often operate with limited data and tools to predict how socioeconomic variables, policy changes, and service delivery strategies intersect, leading to inefficient resource distribution and inequitable outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) that simulates community behavior, resource flows, and the impact of advocacy interventions across diverse demographic and geographic contexts. The ABM will integrate anonymized administrative data (e.g., public housing records, social service utilization) with synthetic population datasets to capture heterogeneity in community needs and behaviors. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters and identify nonlinear relationships between variables such as funding cycles, volunteer engagement, and access barriers. The scale of analysis—spanning multi-year timelines and thousands of simulated agents—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized simulations and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework to test hypothetical policy scenarios, such as the ripple effects of expanding childcare subsidies or redistributing food aid, with granular spatial and temporal resolution. This work will provide community organizations with evidence-based tools to prioritize interventions, anticipate unintended consequences, and advocate for systemic reforms. By bridging computational social science with participatory action research, the project aims to democratize access to advanced modeling tools in non-technical sectors, fostering equity in public service design and delivery.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, principles, and practice of organizing and providing services to communities. May prepare individuals to apply such knowledge and skills in community service positions.

abstract: The increasing volatility of global supply chains due to climate-related disruptions necessitates advanced computational tools to model and mitigate systemic risks. Traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to simulate complex, multi-tiered networks under dynamic environmental stressors. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating agent-based modeling, climate projection data, and reinforcement learning to optimize adaptive strategies for supply chain resilience. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will parameterize heterogeneous agents—including suppliers, logistics providers, and policymakers—within a globally distributed network, incorporating stochastic climate events (e.g., floods, wildfires) and their cascading economic impacts. The computational workflow will involve large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure propagation and machine learning-driven optimization to identify robust intervention points. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for businesses to evaluate climate risk exposure, prioritize investments in redundancy, and design decentralized response protocols. By bridging operations management, climate science, and computational engineering, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive supply chain governance in an era of escalating environmental uncertainty. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the terabytes of geospatial and transactional data, parallelizing millions of scenario iterations, and training deep reinforcement learning models to navigate high-dimensional decision spaces. This interdisciplinary approach advances computational business analytics by addressing a pressing, understudied niche: the integration of climate resilience into strategic supply chain design, offering actionable insights for industries ranging from agriculture to manufacturing.
cip_title: Business, Management, Marketing, and Related Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business, management, marketing and related support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The development of novel therapeutics remains a critical challenge in pharmaceutical sciences, particularly for diseases with complex etiologies such as neurodegenerative disorders and antimicrobial resistance. Traditional experimental approaches are often limited by high costs, lengthy timelines, and the inability to fully capture the dynamic interactions between drug candidates and their biological targets at atomic resolution. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive modeling. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) elucidating the binding mechanisms and conformational dynamics of lead compounds with target proteins implicated in Alzheimer’s disease and multidrug-resistant bacterial infections, and (2) developing predictive models to optimize drug pharmacokinetics and toxicity profiles. All-atom MD simulations, utilizing software such as GROMACS and AMBER, will be performed to simulate protein-ligand systems over microsecond timescales, requiring extensive parallelization and GPU acceleration. Concurrently, neural network architectures will be trained on multi-omic datasets—including structural proteomics, chemical libraries, and clinical toxicity data—to identify novel candidates with enhanced specificity and safety. The integration of these computational approaches will enable rapid in silico screening of millions of compounds, significantly narrowing the experimental search space. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the computational burden of these analyses, which involve terabytes of trajectory data and iterative model optimization. The anticipated outcomes include the identification of high-priority therapeutic candidates for experimental validation, atomistic insights into target engagement mechanisms, and publicly accessible ML models to guide future drug discovery efforts. This work aligns with broader goals of accelerating translational research and reducing the attrition rate of clinical drug candidates, ultimately contributing to advancements in precision medicine and global health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the basic sciences that underlie drugs and drug therapy and that prepares individuals for further study and/or careers in pharmaceutical science and research, pharmaceutical administration and sales, biotechnology, drug manufacturing, regulatory affairs, and related fields. Includes instruction in mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, statistics, pharmaceutics, pharmacology and toxicology, dosage formulation, manufacturing, quality assurance, and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to evaluate the economic and ecological trade-offs of invasive species management policies using a novel integration of dynamic computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC). Invasive species impose significant costs on ecosystems and local economies, but policy responses—such as eradication, containment, or adaptive management—require balancing uncertain ecological outcomes with budgetary constraints and regional economic impacts. Existing models often lack the spatial resolution, temporal scope, or behavioral realism to capture feedback between policy incentives, landowner decision-making, and species spread. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) coupled with a spatial ecological simulator, calibrated using high-resolution environmental and socioeconomic data from the Great Lakes region. The ABM will simulate landowner responses to subsidies, fines, or collective action requirements under varying ecological conditions, while the ecological module predicts invasive spread dynamics influenced by management actions. HPC resources are critical to support the model’s computational demands, including parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess policy robustness across climate scenarios, optimization algorithms to identify cost-effective management pathways, and Bayesian calibration using historical invasion datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of how policy design interacts with ecological thresholds to drive regional cost-benefit ratios, (2) identification of leverage points for improving cross-jurisdictional cooperation, and (3) open-source tools for scalable, spatially explicit policy analysis. Results will directly inform state and federal agencies engaged in invasive species policy renewal, offering evidence-based strategies to mitigate biodiversity loss while minimizing economic disruptions. By advancing computational methods for coupled human-environment systems, this work also contributes methodological innovations to environmental economics, enhancing the field’s capacity to address complex, large-scale resource management challenges.
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Economics (NATURAL RESOURCES/ CONSERVATION SCIENCES)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic concepts and methods to the analysis of issues such as air and water pollution, land use planning, waste disposal, invasive species and pest control, conservation policies, and related environmental problems. Includes instruction in cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, evaluation and assessment of alternative resource management strategies, policy evaluation and monitoring, and descriptive and analytic tools for studying how environmental developments affect the economic system.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of U.S. constitutional jurisprudence through large-scale legal text analysis and network modeling. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in judicial reasoning across pivotal Supreme Court cases, particularly those involving shifts in constitutional interpretation that defy traditional doctrinal categorization. Existing scholarship often relies on manual case analysis or small-sample qualitative methods, limiting the ability to systematically trace how legal concepts interact, mutate, or stabilize over multi-decadal timescales. We propose a computational legal analytics framework combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with dynamic network modeling to process a curated corpus of 50,000+ federal court opinions (1790–2024), with particular focus on First Amendment and Due Process Clause jurisprudence. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect semantic relationships between legal concepts, while temporal graph networks will map how citation patterns and conceptual dependencies evolve alongside sociopolitical changes. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of heterogeneous legal texts (PDFs, OCR outputs, metadata), GPU-accelerated model training for domain-specific legal language understanding, and iterative simulation of competing doctrinal development hypotheses. Expected outcomes include: 1) a novel taxonomy of constitutional argumentation pathways, 2) quantitative metrics for measuring doctrinal stability during constitutional "tipping points," and 3) open-source tools for legal temporal network analysis. By bridging computational social science methodologies with constitutional theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying legal change as a complex adaptive system, with implications for legal education, judicial analytics, and predictive modeling of jurisprudential trends. The scale of textual data and need for real-time simulation of multi-century legal interactions necessitates dedicated HPC resources beyond typical humanities computing infrastructure.
cip_title: American/ US Law/ Legal Studies/ Jurisprudence
cip_definition: An advanced, professional program of the U.S. legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an ethically informed computational framework to model the systemic impacts of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven triage systems in critical care settings, addressing gaps in accountability and equity when deploying autonomous decision-making tools. While AI triage algorithms promise efficiency gains during resource-constrained scenarios (e.g., pandemics, mass casualty events), their ethical implications remain underexplored, particularly concerning biases in training data, opacity in prioritization logic, and downstream effects on vulnerable populations. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will simulate dynamic hospital networks under crisis conditions, integrating multi-agent models to represent patient populations, clinician behaviors, and institutional policies. The computational pipeline will combine discrete-event simulations for resource flows, deep reinforcement learning to train adaptive triage algorithms, and counterfactual analysis to evaluate how different ethical paradigms (utilitarian, egalitarian, prioritarian) influence outcomes across demographic subgroups. Simulations will be parameterized using real-world critical care datasets, anonymized EHRs, and synthetic data augmentation to represent edge cases. Sensitivity analyses will quantify how algorithmic transparency requirements or audit mechanisms affect system-wide fairness metrics. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of scenario-based equity impact assessments for AI triage systems, (2) evidence-based recommendations for embedding procedural justice safeguards in algorithm design, and (3) novel metrics quantifying trade-offs between efficiency and distributive fairness under crisis protocols. By bridging computational modeling with normative ethics analysis, this work aims to establish reproducible methods for anticipatory ethics evaluation of clinical AI systems, directly informing policy frameworks for accountable implementation in emergency medicine.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods in sustainable fashion design, addressing the urgent need to reduce material waste and energy consumption in apparel production. Traditional design processes rely heavily on physical prototyping, which is resource-intensive and environmentally detrimental. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate material behavior, optimize pattern cutting, and automate design iterations, thereby minimizing physical trials. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) will be applied to simulate fabric draping, stress distribution, and textile interactions under diverse environmental conditions. Machine learning (ML) algorithms, trained on datasets of historical textile performance and consumer trends, will generate adaptive design solutions that balance aesthetics, structural integrity, and sustainability. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be employed to create virtual prototypes, enabling rapid visualization and modification of designs in immersive 3D environments. The project will integrate these computational approaches into an open-access toolkit tailored for fashion educators and industry professionals. Anticipated outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in material waste during prototyping, validated through comparative case studies, and a framework for real-time collaboration between designers and engineers. By merging advanced computation with creative design workflows, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for environmentally conscious apparel production while enhancing pedagogical resources in fashion education. The scalability of these methods, dependent on HPC capabilities for parallel processing of large datasets and complex simulations, underscores the necessity of robust computing infrastructure to achieve timely, impactful results.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional design of commercial fashions, apparel, and accessories, and the management of fashion development projects. Includes instruction in apparel design; accessory design; the design of men's', women's', and children's' wear; flat pattern design; computer-assisted design and manufacturing; concept planning; designing in specific materials; labor and cost analysis; history of fashion; fabric art and printing; and the principles of management and operations in the fashion industry.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern engineered systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address multidisciplinary design challenges that integrate mechanical, electrical, and software subsystems under conflicting performance requirements. Current approaches for system-level optimization and reliability analysis struggle to balance computational efficiency with fidelity when coordinating heterogeneous models or resolving trade-offs between scalability, energy efficiency, and manufacturability. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multi-domain engineering design optimization, leveraging parallelized simulation workflows and machine learning to overcome existing bottlenecks. The research will focus on two interconnected thrusts: (1) implementing distributed, GPU-accelerated finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics solvers to model physical interactions between subsystems at scale, and (2) deploying evolutionary algorithms with surrogate models to navigate high-dimensional design spaces while satisfying cross-domain constraints. Key innovations include adaptive meshing techniques for coupled systems, automated requirement conflict resolution through sensitivity clustering, and uncertainty quantification methods tailored for multi-physics interfaces. The computational workflows will be validated through case studies in aerospace component integration and renewable energy system design, where traditional sequential optimization methods fail to account for emergent behaviors in interconnected systems. Anticipated outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation wall-time for complex assemblies compared to existing commercial tools, along with novel metrics for quantifying design flexibility in multi-objective scenarios. By enabling rapid exploration of system architectures under real-world constraints, this work will advance computational capabilities for next-generation smart infrastructure, robotics, and sustainable manufacturing systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive simulations, training data-driven surrogate models, and maintaining reproducibility across parameter studies involving >10^4 design permutations.
