cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenges of analyzing and simulating large-scale visual art datasets, with a focus on understanding evolving aesthetic patterns and enabling generative digital art creation. The proliferation of digitized art collections and the growing complexity of computational art practices demand advanced analytical tools capable of processing high-resolution imagery, video, and multidimensional design data. Current methods for style classification, cultural trend analysis, and dynamic art generation are constrained by the limitations of standard computing infrastructure when handling terabyte-scale datasets and real-time generative algorithms. This project will employ parallelized neural networks to map stylistic relationships across historical and contemporary visual media, including paintings, photography, and digital installations. A hybrid approach combining convolutional autoencoders for feature extraction and transformer architectures for cross-modal analysis will be implemented to identify latent aesthetic connections between disparate artistic movements. Simultaneously, generative adversarial networks (GANs) and physics-based simulations will be developed to model material interactions in mixed-media artworks and prototype immersive digital environments. The computational workflow will utilize distributed GPU clusters for training large vision-language models on curated art corpora, while MPI-based frameworks will orchestrate parameter studies exploring design variations in 3D-rendered artworks. Expected outcomes include new quantitative frameworks for art historical analysis, open-source tools for computational creativity, and scalable pipelines for preserving complex digital artworks. By bridging art studies with computational science, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for cultural analytics while supporting artists and institutions in navigating technologically mediated creative practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale, speed, and complexity in both analytical and generative dimensions of this research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of the visual arts. Includes instruction in art, photography, and other visual communications media.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling and predictive analytics in casino operations management, with a focus on optimizing dynamic decision-making under uncertainty. The gaming industry faces unique challenges in balancing operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer experience, particularly in real-time scenarios involving variable player behavior, fluctuating demand for gaming services, and evolving security threats. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to capture the complexity of interdependent variables—such as game floor traffic patterns, dealer scheduling, surveillance system coordination, and anti-fraud measures—that influence casino performance. The proposed work will develop agent-based simulation frameworks to model multi-scale interactions between patrons, staff, and gaming systems, integrating stochastic processes to represent probabilistic outcomes inherent to casino environments. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning and anomaly detection algorithms, will be applied to historical operational data and synthetic datasets generated through Monte Carlo methods. These computational tools will enable scenario testing for resource allocation strategies, security protocol optimization, and regulatory risk assessment at unprecedented resolution. The project will further investigate ethical implications of automated decision-support systems in gaming contexts through parallelizable simulation ensembles. By creating adaptive models that account for jurisdictional variations in gaming law and cultural factors influencing patron behavior, this research aims to establish new computational standards for operational analytics in the casino services domain. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools for industry stakeholders, evidence-based recommendations for balancing profitability with responsible gaming practices, and methodological advances in applying HPC to service-oriented, regulated entertainment ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on casino operations and services. Includes instruction in casino operations, casino security and surveillance, casino dealing, principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize complex, dynamic systems inherent to the bartending profession, with a focus on operational efficiency, customer interaction patterns, and labor management in high-volume hospitality environments. While bartending is traditionally viewed as a manual service occupation, the integration of computational modeling introduces novel methodologies to address challenges such as real-time demand forecasting, inventory waste reduction, and staff scheduling under variable conditions. The core research problem centers on the lack of data-driven frameworks for predicting beverage trends, managing perishable inventory, and balancing labor costs with service quality—issues exacerbated by fluctuating customer demographics, seasonal demand shifts, and regulatory constraints. To address these challenges, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate customer flow, beverage preferences, and staff-customer interactions, informed by anonymized point-of-sale (POS) datasets and ethnographic observations from partner establishments. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze historical sales data and external factors (e.g., local events, weather patterns) to predict inventory needs and optimize procurement cycles. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to reflect real-world complexity, enabling parallel processing of thousands of stochastic scenarios to identify robust operational strategies. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for bar managers to dynamically adjust staffing and inventory orders, a predictive model for emerging beverage trends, and a taxonomy of customer interaction archetypes to inform staff training programs. By bridging computational social science with hospitality management, this work aims to establish a precedent for data-centric decision-making in service industries, reducing resource waste while enhancing both economic sustainability and customer satisfaction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally prepare mixed alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and related products and manage bars, lounges, and beverage service operations in the hospitality industry.  Includes instruction in mixology, oenology, accounting and cash management, inventory and cellar management, bar and lounge management, applicable laws and regulations, customer service, and labor/employment regulations.

abstract: Sterile processing departments (SPDs) are critical for preventing surgical site infections, yet current sterilization validation methods rely on generalized protocols that may not account for microbial biofilm resilience or device-specific complexities. This project addresses the challenge of predicting sterilization failure risks in real-world clinical settings by developing a computational framework to model microbial survival dynamics under diverse sterilization conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of biofilm-agent interactions with machine learning (ML) models trained on experimental sterilization data from surgical instruments. The computational pipeline will simulate heat, chemical, and radiation-based sterilization processes at atomistic and mesoscopic scales, capturing spatial heterogeneity in device geometries and microbial colonization patterns. Multiscale models will be validated against experimental biofilm viability assays and clinical sterilization failure records. Key innovations include the development of graph neural networks to predict residual contamination risks based on instrument topology and microbial metagenomic data, as well as agent-based models to optimize sterilization workflow parameters. The HPC environment is essential for handling the high-dimensional data from 3D instrument scans, time-resolved sterilization sensor streams, and genomic databases of sterilization-resistant pathogens. Expected outcomes include a risk stratification tool for SPDs to prioritize reprocessing validation for high-risk instrument categories and a digital twin platform for simulating protocol modifications. This work bridges computational microbiology, materials science, and healthcare operations engineering, offering a paradigm shift from compliance-based to risk-predictive sterile processing. Successful implementation could reduce instrument-related healthcare-associated infections by an estimated 15-30%, while providing foundational insights into the biophysics of extreme microbial persistence.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean, sterilize, and assemble surgical instruments, equipment, and supplies for use in operating rooms and other medical and surgical facilities. Includes instruction in sterilization; infection control; decontamination; and surgical instrumentation processing, distribution, and record-keeping.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing personalized rehabilitation interventions for individuals with physical disabilities by leveraging advanced computational modeling and machine learning. Current clinical practices often rely on generalized protocols that fail to account for the complex interplay of biomechanical, physiological, and psychosocial factors influencing patient outcomes. This project aims to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model patient-specific responses to therapeutic interventions, enabling data-driven customization of rehabilitation plans. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including motion-capture biomechanics, wearable sensor data, electronic health records, and patient-reported outcomes, to construct multi-scale models of disability progression and recovery. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing these large, multimodal datasets and executing computationally intensive simulations. Key computational methods include finite element analysis of musculoskeletal stress during rehabilitative exercises, deep learning algorithms to predict intervention efficacy across diverse patient subgroups, and agent-based modeling of long-term functional adaptation. The project will also employ probabilistic causal inference techniques to disentangle confounding variables in real-world rehabilitation settings. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide clinicians in selecting optimal assistive technologies, exercise regimens, and vocational counseling strategies tailored to individual patient profiles. By quantifying how specific interventions modify disability trajectories, this work will advance precision rehabilitation science and inform the design of next-generation assistive devices. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models at unprecedented resolution, directly addressing scalability barriers in existing rehabilitation research. This project aligns with the program’s focus on integrating disability assessment, assistive technology, and evidence-based practice, with potential to transform clinical decision-making while reducing healthcare disparities through equitable, personalized care paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with people who have learning disabilities, mental illness, and physical disabilities in a clinical, educational, or institutional setting. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, assistive technology, case management, counseling techniques, cultural diversity, disability assessment and measurement, ethics, psychological and physiological aspects of disability, rehabilitation services, rehabilitation science, and vocational counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic efficacy of multi-compound Chinese herbal formulations in modulating immune-inflammatory pathways. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) herbal prescriptions, such as Yin Qiao San and Xue Fu Zhu Yu Tang, are clinically recognized for treating complex conditions like chronic inflammatory disorders, yet their polypharmacological actions remain poorly characterized at a systems level. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational limitations of analyzing multi-target, multi-pathway interactions between hundreds of bioactive phytochemicals and human proteomes. We propose an integrative computational strategy combining molecular dynamics simulations, network pharmacology, and machine learning to model herb-derived compound interactions with immune-related proteins (e.g., TNF-α, IL-6, NLRP3). Molecular docking and binding affinity calculations will be performed across curated libraries of 1,200+ TCM compounds using AutoDock-GPU and GROMACS, followed by ensemble-based simulations to assess dynamic binding behaviors. A heterogeneous graph neural network will integrate results with transcriptomic data from public repositories to predict system-level immunomodulatory effects. This workflow requires HPC capabilities to manage the scale of combinatorial simulations (estimated 250,000+ GPU core-hours) and the complexity of network analyses across 15+ immune signaling pathways. Expected outcomes include the identification of key synergistic compound clusters, mechanistic validation of formula design principles (e.g., "sovereign-minister-assistant" hierarchy), and predictive models for optimizing herbal combinations. The results will advance the systems-level understanding of TCM polypharmacy, provide a computational framework for evaluating herbal safety and efficacy, and bridge traditional knowledge with modern molecular pharmacology. This work directly supports ongoing in vitro validation studies of prioritized compounds in macrophage models, with potential implications for developing targeted immunomodulatory therapies derived from herbal medicine paradigms.
cip_title: Traditional Chinese Medicine and Chinese Herbology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Chinese herbal medicine, a system based on the use of nutrition, natural products, and prescribed medical formulae to treat imbalances in the state of bodily health as defined in the Nei Ching Su Wen and other authorities. Includes instruction in the basic Western medical sciences, history and theory of Chinese medicine, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbology, herbal prescription preparation, herbal patent medicine, herbal pharmacology, Chinese internal medicine and gynecology, febrile diseases, food therapy, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing room acoustics simulations in variable listening environments, a critical challenge in audio engineering. Current methods for predicting and correcting acoustic anomalies in spaces such as recording studios, concert halls, and immersive audio installations rely on simplified geometrical models or empirical approximations, often leading to suboptimal sound reinforcement and mixing decisions. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled workflow combining finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning to model high-resolution, frequency-dependent wave propagation in complex 3D environments. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers to simulate broadband acoustic behavior at audible frequencies (20 Hz–20 kHz), incorporating material absorption profiles, diffraction effects, and spatially distributed transducer arrays. A neural network trained on synthetic and experimental impulse response data will then map simulation outputs to actionable acoustic treatment recommendations. The computational demands are substantial: each full-spectrum room simulation requires teraflop-scale processing to resolve wavelengths down to 1.7 cm at 20 kHz across spaces exceeding 10,000 m³. By utilizing HPC resources, we aim to reduce per-iteration simulation times from weeks to hours, enabling parametric studies of design variables like surface geometry, absorber placement, and loudspeaker configurations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolbox for real-time auralization of proposed acoustic modifications and a database of validated room impulse responses for training AI-assisted mixing systems. This work will directly benefit audio engineering education and industry practice by providing physics-informed tools to predictably control low-frequency standing waves, midrange comb filtering, and high-frequency diffusion—addressing a longstanding gap between theoretical acoustics and practical sound engineering workflows.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the mixing, recording, and production of music. Includes instruction in acoustics, audio mixing, audio production, audio recording, computer composition of music, music theory, digital devices, and sound technology.

abstract: Nursing education faces a critical challenge in preparing educators to design and evaluate clinical training programs that address rapidly evolving healthcare demands, including complex patient care scenarios and interdisciplinary collaboration. Traditional teaching methods often lack the capacity to model dynamic, high-stakes clinical environments or to personalize instruction for diverse learner needs. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate clinical training scenarios, optimize curriculum design, and assess educator and student competencies in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will build agent-based models to replicate multi-patient clinical workflows, integrate machine learning algorithms to analyze historical educational outcomes, and employ natural language processing to evaluate reflective practice in simulated debrief sessions. The simulations will incorporate variables such as patient acuity, staffing ratios, and learner skill levels, generating datasets that capture interactions between instructional strategies, student performance, and contextual factors. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale simulation outputs, train predictive models for competency gaps, and enable real-time adaptation of virtual scenarios during training. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for nurse educators to iteratively refine clinical instruction methods, predictive analytics to identify at-risk learners, and evidence-based guidelines for scaling simulation-based training across institutions. This work will advance nursing education research by providing a data-driven approach to address variability in clinical preparedness, ultimately improving the quality of nurse training programs and patient care outcomes. The computational infrastructure developed here will also serve as a foundation for future studies on adaptive learning systems in healthcare education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to teach in academic and clinical settings, including staff development. Includes instruction in advanced nursing practice, nursing role development, curriculum and instruction, program and course design, clinical instruction, and evaluation of learning.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the structural evolution of ritual practices across underrepresented religious traditions using advanced computational methods. While ritual sequences are central to theological and communal identity, their development and transmission remain poorly understood, particularly in non-canonical or marginalized traditions. The study focuses on ritual data from late-antique Mediterranean mystery cults and early medieval esoteric Buddhist communities, which lack comprehensive comparative analysis due to fragmented records and disciplinary silos. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze digitized liturgical manuals, iconographic inscriptions, and ethnographic records, applying sequence alignment algorithms—adapted from bioinformatics—to model ritual “phylogenies” and trace cross-cultural influences. Natural language processing (NLP) tools will extract semantic and syntactic patterns from multilingual primary sources, while agent-based modeling will simulate the diffusion of ritual elements under varying sociohistorical constraints. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of textual corpora (over 50,000 pages of manuscripts), the complexity of multi-layer network analyses, and the iterative parameter testing required for robust phylogenetic inference. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated ritual sequences, visualization tools for interdisciplinary collaboration, and new theoretical frameworks for understanding how ritual innovation intersects with theological adaptation. By bridging computational archaeology, anthropology, and religious studies, this project aims to establish methodologies for analyzing nonlinear cultural dynamics in theological contexts, offering insights into the resilience and transformation of minority religious practices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in theological studies and religious vocations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Commercial fishing operations face critical challenges in balancing economic viability with sustainable resource management, particularly as environmental variability and regulatory constraints intensify. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize fishing strategies, minimize bycatch, and enhance compliance with dynamic regulatory environments. The research problem centers on the integration of real-time environmental data, vessel performance metrics, and species distribution models to generate actionable decision-support tools for commercial fishermen. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a coupled modeling system combining hydrodynamic simulations, machine learning-based fish stock predictions, and Monte Carlo methods to evaluate fleet deployment scenarios under varying oceanographic and policy conditions. Key computational tasks include processing multi-terabyte datasets from satellite remote sensing, electronic monitoring systems, and historical catch records, as well as simulating gear-specific interactions with target and non-target species at fine spatial scales (1–10 km resolution). The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized parameter optimization for gear configuration algorithms and ensemble forecasting of seasonal fishing effort distribution. Expected outcomes include predictive models for reducing fuel consumption and bycatch rates by 15–30%, validated against field data from partner fishing cooperatives. Additionally, the project will produce open-access tools for simulating regulatory impacts on catch efficiency, supporting adaptive policy design. By bridging gaps between ecological data, operational logistics, and regulatory compliance, this work aims to advance both the economic resilience of commercial fisheries and the long-term sustainability of marine ecosystems. The scalability of the computational framework will permit future expansion to global fisheries, emphasizing technology-driven solutions for a critical sector within the blue economy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as commercial fishermen, fishing operations supervisors or in related fishing industry operations. Includes instruction in fishing vessel operation; fishing equipment operation and maintenance; equipment repair; catch identification, sorting, and storage; safety procedures; record keeping; and applicable legal regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to evaluate the long-term impacts of standardized testing policies on educational equity across diverse demographic groups and geographic regions. Despite widespread implementation, the heterogeneous effects of these policies on marginalized student populations remain poorly understood due to the complexity of intersecting variables, including funding disparities, curricular adaptations, and differential access to support resources. To address this gap, the study will employ multilevel longitudinal modeling to analyze decade-spanning datasets encompassing standardized test scores, district-level policy timelines, and socioeconomic indicators from 12 U.S. states. The computational demands of this analysis necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage three core challenges: (1) processing over 15 terabytes of structured and unstructured educational records, (2) executing iterative imputation algorithms to address systemic missing data in historical policy implementation records, and (3) running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to project equity outcomes under alternative policy scenarios. The research team will utilize distributed computing frameworks to optimize hierarchical Bayesian models that account for temporal autocorrelation and spatial dependencies across districts. Expected outcomes include identification of policy design features most strongly associated with reduced achievement gaps, particularly for English language learners and students from low-income households. By enabling rapid sensitivity analyses of hypothetical policy adjustments, this computational approach will provide actionable evidence for minimizing unintended consequences of accountability systems. The project will deliver open-access tools for visualizing policy impact trajectories, supporting education stakeholders in designing context-specific interventions that align with equity goals. This work advances methodological innovation in education policy analysis through scalable computational techniques for causal inference in complex, multi-jurisdictional systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to education and educational systems at the local, state, national, and international levels. Includes instruction in social and cultural issues in education, contemporary educational policies, history of education, economics of education, international and comparative education, education and social change, educational research and evaluation methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in sustainable printing workflow optimization through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve complex challenges in the graphic communications industry. Current methods for optimizing print production—spanning material selection, ink behavior prediction, energy consumption, and supply chain logistics—often rely on oversimplified models that fail to account for real-world variability, leading to costly overproduction, resource waste, and environmental impact. The research problem centers on developing a dynamic, multi-scale simulation framework to model printing processes under diverse operational constraints, integrating variables such as substrate interactions, machine calibration tolerances, and workforce scheduling. The computational approach combines machine learning for predictive quality control, fluid dynamics simulations to analyze ink dispersion on heterogeneous materials, and agent-based modeling to evaluate logistical workflows. These methods require parallelized processing to handle large datasets from print production environments, including real-time sensor inputs and historical defect records. HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated scenarios, stochastic optimization of job scheduling, and sensitivity analyses for eco-friendly material substitutions. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of recommending optimal configurations for specific print jobs, reducing trial runs by an estimated 30–40%, and a comparative analysis of sustainable material performance under operational stresses. The project will also produce open-access datasets on energy-efficient press configurations, contributing to industry-wide benchmarks for carbon footprint reduction. By bridging gaps between empirical print management practices and computational scalability, this work aims to advance academic training in printing operations, equipping students with data-driven methodologies while addressing pressing environmental and economic challenges in graphic communications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical and managerial knowledge and skills to the processes and procedures of managing printing operations from initial design through finished product distribution. Includes instruction in the principles of graphic communications design and production; quality control; printing operations management; computerization; printing plant management; business finance and marketing; logistics and distribution; personnel supervision and leadership; and professional standards in the graphic communications industry.

abstract: Quantum turbulence in superfluid systems presents a critical challenge in advancing technologies reliant on macroscopic quantum phenomena, such as next-generation quantum sensors and energy-efficient superconducting devices. Current experimental limitations in observing dynamic vortex interactions at ultralow temperatures hinder the development of predictive models for defect formation and turbulence dissipation. This project seeks to establish a computational framework integrating time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations with multiscale hydrodynamic models to simulate quantum vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluid helium-4 and helium-3 mixtures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the femtosecond-scale interactions across micron-scale domains, requiring massively parallel simulations with adaptive meshing techniques. The research will employ spectral methods for vortex core resolution and machine learning algorithms to identify emergent turbulence patterns from petabyte-scale output data. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for quantum fluid dynamics, quantitative predictions of vortex entanglement thresholds under varying thermal gradients, and design guidelines for stabilizing superconducting circuits against flux noise. By bridging quantum mechanical principles with continuum-scale engineering analysis, this work aims to enable breakthrough applications in quantum computing hardware and ultra-low-loss energy storage systems, while advancing fundamental understanding of non-equilibrium phenomena in quantum matter.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the use of physics principles in the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems and other scientific applications. Includes instruction in high- and low-temperature phenomena, computational physics, superconductivity, applied thermodynamics, molecular and particle physics applications, and space science research.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of high-performance metal alloys for extreme operational environments, addressing critical gaps in predicting microstructural evolution under combined thermal, mechanical, and chemical stresses. Current experimental methods to optimize alloy compositions and processing parameters are time-intensive and costly, while conventional computational tools lack the resolution to capture atomistic-scale defect dynamics and their mesoscale consequences. We propose a multiscale simulation framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and phase-field modeling to correlate atomic-scale solute interactions, dislocation propagation, and grain boundary stability with macroscale mechanical properties. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale MD simulations of dislocation networks in multicomponent alloys (10^6–10^8 atoms) over nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales, coupled with machine learning-driven phase-field models to predict creep resistance and fatigue crack propagation in polycrystalline systems. Key objectives include parameterizing strain-rate sensitivity in novel refractory alloys, quantifying environmental degradation mechanisms in sulfide-containing environments, and identifying thermodynamically stable nanoprecipitate distributions for strengthening. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated DFT (VASP) and scalable MD (LAMMPS) codes, with automated data pipelines to cross-validate models against synchrotron X-ray diffraction and electron backscatter diffraction datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for alloy design, reducing reliance on iterative physical testing, and accelerating the development of materials for mining infrastructure, energy generation systems, and heavy machinery. By resolving the multiscale interplay between processing-induced microstructures and degradation pathways, this work will directly inform sustainable manufacturing protocols and failure-resistant material specifications for industrial applications. The requested HPC allocation is critical to achieving the necessary statistical sampling across compositional and parametric spaces, enabling transformative insights into metallurgical systems that are inaccessible via laboratory-scale characterization alone.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and metallurgical principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of metal components of structural, load-bearing, power, transmission, and moving systems; and the analysis of engineering problems such as stress, creep, failure, alloy behavior, environmental fluctuations, stability, electromagnetic and thermodynamic characteristics, optimal manufacturing processes, and related design considerations.

abstract: Critical care management of adult and geriatric patients presents unique challenges due to the heterogeneity of aging physiology, multimorbidity, and variable responses to interventions. A key unmet need is the development of personalized predictive models for sepsis progression and multiorgan dysfunction in critically ill older adults, as existing tools lack granularity to account for complex interactions between immunosenescence, comorbidities, and dynamic biomarker profiles. This project proposes to address this gap by integrating high-dimensional clinical data (electronic health records, continuous vital sign streams) with multi-omics profiles (transcriptomic, proteomic) from a prospective cohort of 1,200 critically ill patients aged ≥55. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support three core aims: (1) training ensemble machine learning models on temporal patient trajectories using GPU-accelerated frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch), (2) performing genome-scale network analyses to identify age-specific inflammatory pathways via distributed computing, and (3) optimizing real-time risk prediction pipelines for clinical deployment. The analysis will leverage federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across collaborating ICUs while handling petabyte-scale multimodal datasets. Computational validation will include sensitivity analyses for model robustness across frailty phenotypes and pharmacogenomic subgroups. Expected outcomes include the first open-source predictive architecture specifically validated for geriatric critical care populations, with preliminary results demonstrating ≥15% improvement in sepsis prediction accuracy over existing scores (SOFA, qSOFA) in retrospective validation cohorts. The requested allocation of 200,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster with high-memory nodes and GPU arrays will enable the iterative model refinement required for this precision medicine approach. Successful implementation could inform targeted escalation protocols and generate foundational insights into the systems biology of critical illness in aging populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Critical Care

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized physical therapy interventions by modeling patient-specific biomechanical responses to therapeutic exercises. Despite advances in physical therapy practice, current protocols often rely on generalized guidelines that do not fully account for individual variations in anatomy, neuromuscular control, or tissue healing. This limitation can lead to suboptimal recovery trajectories, particularly for patients with complex conditions such as stroke-related mobility impairments or post-surgical musculoskeletal deficits. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate biomechanical interactions during therapeutic exercises, enabling data-driven customization of treatment plans. Using musculoskeletal modeling software (OpenSim) and finite element analysis, we will create patient-specific digital twins derived from clinical motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging data. Machine learning algorithms will then iteratively predict optimal exercise parameters—such as joint angle ranges, resistance levels, and movement velocities—to maximize functional gains while minimizing injury risks. The computational workflow requires parallel processing to manage high-resolution simulations across diverse anatomical datasets and stochastic optimization of treatment variables. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for clinicians to tailor rehabilitation protocols, potentially reducing recovery times and improving long-term patient mobility metrics. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets correlating computational predictions with clinical outcomes, fostering innovation in physical therapy research. By integrating HPC-driven insights into clinical decision-making, this work aims to bridge the gap between theoretical biomechanics and applied therapeutic practice, enhancing the precision of physical therapy interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physical therapist, to implement physical therapy treatment care plans, train patients, conduct treatment interventions, use equipment, and observe and record patient progress. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, behavioral sciences, biomechanics, clinical documentation, clinical pathology, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing demand for personalized prosthetic and orthotic devices requires advanced computational tools to optimize biomechanical performance, patient comfort, and long-term usability. Current design workflows often rely on static, population-level data, limiting their ability to address dynamic physiological changes, heterogeneous patient anatomies, and real-world functional demands. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and predict the biomechanical interaction between assistive devices and patient-specific anatomy under dynamic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-modal patient data—including gait analysis, musculoskeletal modeling, medical imaging, and material stress-strain profiles—into a unified simulation environment. Finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) algorithms will be employed to model tissue-device interfaces, predict pressure distribution during ambulation, and iteratively optimize device geometry and material properties. The computational pipeline will also incorporate reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive device behavior in response to real-time sensor data, such as changes in gait patterns or residual limb volume. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in parametric design exploration and enable rapid prototyping of patient-specific solutions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for reducing pressure-related injuries in prosthetic users, a data-driven framework for custom orthotic stiffness tuning in neuromuscular disorders, and open-source tools for simulating device fatigue under cyclic loading. This work addresses a critical gap in orthotic/prosthetic research by bridging clinical expertise with scalable computational innovation, ultimately advancing the development of next-generation assistive technologies that improve mobility and quality of life for individuals with limb loss or musculoskeletal impairments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize adaptive sales strategies in dynamic, multi-agent environments, with a focus on enhancing real-time decision-making in complex sales ecosystems. Traditional sales training frameworks often rely on static scenarios or simplified role-playing exercises, which fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between sales professionals, heterogeneous customer personas, and rapidly shifting market conditions. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based computational model that simulates high-stakes sales negotiations across diverse industries, incorporating behavioral economics principles, real-world transactional data, and probabilistic decision trees. The model will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to analyze historical sales call transcripts, customer relationship management (CRM) metadata, and psychometric profiles to generate synthetic yet realistic buyer personas with evolving preferences. Computational challenges include parallelizing thousands of concurrent negotiation simulations, training reinforcement learning agents to identify optimal persuasion strategies under uncertainty, and quantifying the cascading effects of micro-level interactions on macro-level sales funnel performance. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to test counterfactual scenarios, including the impact of emerging technologies like AI-assisted sales tools on human-agent collaboration dynamics. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting strategy effectiveness across customer segments, data-driven recommendations for adaptive sales training modules, and metrics quantifying the relationship between computational resource allocation and model predictive accuracy. This interdisciplinary approach bridges cognitive science, operations research, and machine learning to advance evidence-based methodologies in sales operations—a critical yet understudied domain where computational modeling has remained underutilized relative to its transformative potential.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to possess the skills associated with direct promotion of products and services to potential customers and to function as independent sales representatives and managers. Includes instruction in consumer psychology, image projection, public speaking and interpersonal communications, sales organization and operations, customer relations, professional standards and ethics, and applicable technical skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing additive manufacturing (AM) processes through high-fidelity simulations of multi-physics interactions during material deposition. Current AM techniques, particularly in polymer and composite systems, suffer from defects such as warping, delamination, and inconsistent layer adhesion due to poorly understood thermal gradients and stress dynamics. Existing experimental approaches are costly and time-intensive, while simplified computational models lack the resolution to capture critical localized phenomena. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a parallelized finite element model that couples transient thermal analysis, viscoelastic stress evolution, and material phase transitions at micrometer-scale resolutions. The model will integrate experimental calibration data from in-situ thermal imaging and mechanical testing to refine boundary conditions. Key computational challenges include managing the high spatial-temporal resolution required for defect prediction (exceeding 10^8 degrees of freedom) and implementing adaptive meshing strategies to track moving heat sources. The simulations will be validated against synchrotron X-ray tomography data of defect formation in printed specimens. Successful implementation will enable predictive optimization of process parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed, cooling rates) for novel material formulations, reducing trial-and-error prototyping by an estimated 60%. Outcomes will be disseminated as open-source workflow templates to support broader adoption of simulation-driven AM process design. This work directly aligns with national priorities in advanced manufacturing while avoiding overlap with excluded engineering disciplines through its exclusive focus on process simulation rather than material development or end-use structural analysis. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated computations and large-scale parameter sweeps essential for establishing statistically robust process-property relationships.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the ecological drivers of zoonotic disease emergence and spillover risk under shifting land-use and climate conditions, with a focus on pathogens at the wildlife-livestock-human interface. Current predictive models often oversimplify host-pathogen-environment interactions, neglecting evolutionary dynamics in reservoir species and spatially heterogeneous transmission pathways. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework integrating high-resolution ecological, epidemiological, and environmental data to simulate multi-host disease systems across dynamic landscapes. The computational approach will combine (1) spatial network analyses of habitat connectivity and fragmentation using satellite-derived land cover data, (2) individual-based simulations of host movement and interspecies contact patterns, and (3) evolutionary algorithms modeling pathogen adaptation to changing host communities. The framework will be parameterized using 20 years of surveillance data from Southeast Asian bat populations (a hotspot for emerging coronaviruses) paired with climate projections and agricultural expansion maps. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing petabyte-scale remote sensing datasets, running parallelized simulations across thousands of landscape change scenarios, and conducting sensitivity analyses of complex ecological feedback loops. Expected outcomes include predictive risk maps identifying regions vulnerable to cross-species transmission under different climate pathways, quantitative estimates of evolutionary selection pressures on viral traits, and an open-source modeling toolkit for analyzing environmental drivers of disease emergence. This work will advance fundamental understanding of how anthropogenic landscape alteration interacts with pathogen evolution to influence spillover potential, directly informing One Health strategies for surveillance prioritization and preventive intervention.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of disease, disability, and trauma patterns within and across populations and the development of health management mechanisms to prevent and control disease outbreaks and injurious behaviors. Includes instruction in biostatistics, biochemistry, molecular biology, immunology, disease and injury determinants, genetic disease and disability factors, behavioral studies, health services research, environmental disease and injury factors, and population studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a cross-linguistic analysis of narrative structures in understudied literary traditions, focusing on 19th- and 20th-century works in Arabic, Japanese, and Nahuatl. While comparative literature has long relied on close reading and manual textual analysis, the scale and linguistic complexity of these corpora—spanning diverse grammatical systems, non-Latin scripts, and translation variants—pose challenges that demand computational scalability. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in narrative temporality and focalization across these traditions, which remain underrepresented in existing transnational literary studies due to resource-intensive manual methods. Using a mixed-methods approach, we will deploy multilingual transformer models (fine-tuned for historical texts) to automate the detection of narrative devices, supplemented by graph-based algorithms to map intra- and intertextual relationships across approximately 10,000 primary texts and their translations. Computational demands include parallel processing for tokenizing heterogenous orthographies, training language-specific embeddings, and running large-scale topic modeling across multilingual feature spaces. The pipeline integrates Python-based NLP libraries with custom scripts for diachronic stylometric analysis, requiring GPU-accelerated workloads to handle memory-intensive operations on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative framework for comparing nonlinear narrative strategies across these literatures, shedding light on how linguistic structures influence cross-cultural conceptions of time and perspective. Results will be disseminated through an open-access web platform visualizing narrative networks, alongside traditional scholarly publications. By bridging computational linguistics and literary theory, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for analyzing global literatures while preserving the nuance of original language contexts—a critical step toward decolonizing comparative literary studies through technologically inclusive approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in predicting multi-organ toxicity caused by environmental and pharmaceutical agents, a challenge complicated by the dynamic interplay between toxin pharmacokinetics, tissue-specific susceptibility, and delayed pathophysiological outcomes. Current experimental models struggle to resolve these complex, system-wide interactions, particularly for toxins with non-linear dose-response relationships or those requiring metabolic activation. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multi-scale computational models integrating molecular toxicokinetic data with organ-level physiological networks. Agent-based modeling will simulate toxin distribution and metabolism across hepatic, renal, and nervous systems, parameterized by existing in vitro and in vivo datasets on priority chemicals such as halogenated hydrocarbons and organophosphate derivatives. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess inter-individual variability in detoxification capacity, incorporating polymorphisms in cytochrome P450 enzymes and membrane transporter proteins. A second computational arm will apply molecular dynamics simulations to predict structural interactions between reactive toxin metabolites and critical biomolecules, including albumin, glutathione, and extracellular matrix components, to identify sequestration or bioactivation hotspots. These simulations will utilize GPU-optimized force fields calibrated against crystallographic data from toxin-adducted proteins. The integration of these approaches aims to generate predictive maps of toxin fate and injury propagation across biological scales, enabling identification of early biomarkers and countermeasure targets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational framework for simulating multi-organ toxicity scenarios, validated against clinical and toxicological databases. This work will directly inform the design of safer chemicals, improve antidote development strategies, and reduce reliance on animal testing for systemic toxicity assessments. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter spaces, iterative model optimization, and large-scale sensitivity analyses required to achieve these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of poisons and other biohazards; their interactions with organisms and their food and respiratory systems; and their prevention, management, and counteraction. Includes instruction in toxicological biochemistry, toxic agents and transporters, toxin fate, toxicokinetics and metabolism, toxin classification, molecular toxic mechanisms, extracellular matrices and cell function, bacterial pathogenesis and mutagenesis, pathophysiology and apoptosis, cell stress and injury, studies of specific toxins, and studies of specific organ systems and physiological functions in relation to toxicological problems.

abstract: The proliferation of digital learning tools necessitates advanced computational methods to optimize adaptive educational media design, particularly for scalable, personalized learning environments. Current approaches struggle to balance real-time learner analytics with dynamic content adjustments, especially in resource-constrained settings. This project seeks to address this gap by developing and testing machine learning (ML) models and agent-based simulations to automate the design of responsive educational media. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep reinforcement learning algorithms on multimodal educational datasets—including eye-tracking, interaction logs, and performance metrics—to predict optimal content adaptation pathways. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate diverse learner populations interacting with prototype media, enabling rapid iteration of design parameters under varying pedagogical scenarios. The computational intensity of training multi-input neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets and running large-scale parallel simulations necessitates access to GPU clusters and distributed memory systems. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for embedding real-time adaptability into educational media, (2) optimized algorithms for balancing personalization with cognitive load management, and (3) open-source tools for simulating learner-media interactions. This work directly advances the Educational/Instructional Media Design field by providing evidence-based computational strategies to enhance the efficacy of digital learning tools while maintaining scalability. Findings will inform the development of next-generation adaptive learning systems capable of serving heterogeneous populations in both formal education and informal learning contexts. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s goals, as standard computing infrastructure cannot support the concurrent model training, hyperparameter optimization, and population-level simulations required for robust validation.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing technology for educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: The upholstery industry faces critical challenges in optimizing material performance, structural integrity, and sustainability while balancing cost and labor efficiency. Traditional methods for evaluating materials (e.g., foams, textiles, springs) and design configurations rely heavily on physical prototyping, which is time-consuming, resource-intensive, and limited in predictive accuracy. This project proposes a computational framework to model and simulate the mechanical behavior of upholstered systems under dynamic loads, environmental stressors, and long-term wear. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain dynamics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and moisture transport in padding materials, and machine learning (ML) models trained on empirical data to predict degradation patterns. Key objectives include optimizing spring configurations for load distribution in furniture, predicting foam compression fatigue over time, and digitally prototyping sustainable material composites. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these simulations across thousands of parameter combinations (e.g., material densities, stitch patterns, humidity levels) and iterating generative design algorithms to minimize waste in cutting processes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for lifespan estimation of upholstered products, data-driven guidelines for eco-material adoption, and open-source simulation templates to democratize advanced computational methods in small-scale upholstery enterprises. By reducing reliance on physical trials, this work aims to lower production costs, extend product durability, and advance circular economy practices in the field. The computational workflows developed here will also serve as a foundational framework for future research on smart textiles and adaptive ergonomic designs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install springs, filling, padding, covering and finishing on items such as furniture, automobile seats, caskets, mattresses, and bedsprings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across Latin America and the Caribbean through large-scale textual and visual analysis. The research problem centers on the fragmented preservation of regionally significant, non-institutionalized cultural outputs—including community-produced zines, oral history transcripts, and grassroots visual media—which are often dispersed across physical archives or digitized in unstructured formats. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to systematically analyze these materials at scale, limiting interdisciplinary insights into how marginalized communities negotiate cultural memory and identity in postcolonial contexts. The project will employ computational text mining, multimodal neural networks, and geospatial network analysis to process multilingual corpora (Spanish, Portuguese, Creole, and indigenous languages) and image datasets from 15 countries, spanning 1945–2020. Custom transformer models will be fine-tuned to recognize vernacular linguistic patterns and cross-modal semantic relationships, while graph-based algorithms will map the diffusion of narrative themes across diasporic networks. Computational workflows will integrate privacy-preserving federated learning techniques to accommodate ethically sensitive materials. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-access repository of computationally enriched cultural metadata for the region, revealing understudied transnational connections in grassroots cultural production. The work will directly support emerging scholarship in decolonial digital humanities while providing a template for ethically grounded HPC applications in area studies. Resource requests emphasize GPU nodes for model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous data types, and scalable memory for cross-regional network simulations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced control frameworks for autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments, a core challenge in mechatronics and automation engineering. Current limitations in real-time sensor fusion, adaptive decision-making, and multi-objective optimization hinder the deployment of robust robotic systems for applications such as precision manufacturing, agile logistics, and human-robot collaboration. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale simulations of complex electro-mechanical systems, coupled with machine learning-driven control strategies. Computational models will integrate multi-body dynamics, vision-based perception networks, and distributed sensor-actuator systems using parallelized finite element analysis and digital twin frameworks. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to optimize control policies for hybrid systems involving both discrete event-driven tasks and continuous motion planning. Key outcomes include validated control architectures for redundant manipulators and mobile robot fleets, with emphasis on fault tolerance and energy efficiency. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of system prototypes through hardware-in-the-loop testing, reducing development cycles for industrial partners. This work directly supports curriculum development in embedded robotics by generating case studies on computational constraints in real-time systems. By bridging simulation-to-deployment gaps in multi-agent automation, the project aims to advance scalable solutions for small-to-medium enterprises adopting Industry 4.0 technologies. Resource allocation will specifically target GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory nodes for virtual prototyping of complex mechatronic assemblies.
cip_title: Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in the support of engineers to the design, development, and operational evaluation of autonomous, computer-controlled, electro-mechanical systems. Includes instruction in computer and software engineering, control engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and robotics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational frameworks for modeling systemic risk in hyperconnected financial ecosystems. Modern financial systems are characterized by dense, dynamic interdependencies among institutions, markets, and digital infrastructures, yet existing risk assessment tools struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback loops and cascading failures inherent to these networks. The study addresses this gap by designing a hybrid agent-based and network-theoretic model that integrates real-time transactional data, adaptive behavioral rules for institutional agents, and stochastic shock propagation mechanisms. The computational approach combines graph neural networks (GNNs) to model latent interdependencies with Monte Carlo simulations to quantify tail-risk scenarios, requiring iterative optimization across terabyte-scale datasets. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive graph operations for networks exceeding 10^6 nodes and achieving subsecond latency for crisis scenario simulations. The HPC implementation will utilize parallelized graph processing frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark GraphX) and GPU-accelerated tensor operations to enable daily recalibration of risk metrics under varying macroeconomic conditions. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a novel metric for real-time systemic vulnerability scoring, 2) an open-source toolkit for regulatory stress testing, and 3) empirical insights into network interventions that mitigate contagion risks in decentralized finance (DeFi) environments. This work aims to provide financial regulators and institutional stakeholders with computationally robust tools to anticipate and manage systemic disruptions, particularly in emerging contexts where traditional risk models fail to account for blockchain-mediated transactions and AI-driven trading ecosystems. The requested resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution to inform evidence-based policymaking in complex financial networks.
cip_title: Management Sciences and Quantitative Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business quantitative methods and management science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Aircraft structural integrity and maintenance efficiency are critical to aviation safety, yet current methodologies for predicting airframe component fatigue and failure rely heavily on empirical models and periodic inspections, which can be time-intensive and insufficient for real-time decision-making. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) to predict stress distribution, fatigue life, and failure modes in airframe components under operational conditions. The research will focus on common structural materials such as aerospace-grade aluminum alloys and composite laminates, simulating complex load scenarios—including cyclic stresses, thermal gradients, and vibration—to identify critical weak points and degradation patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational demands of multi-scale FEA models, which require meshing fine geometric details of airframe joints, fasteners, and repaired sections, as well as processing terabytes of sensor-derived operational data for ML training. Parallelized solvers will accelerate iterative simulations, while deep neural networks will be trained to correlate simulated stress profiles with historical maintenance records and non-destructive testing (NDT) data. Expected outcomes include predictive models that optimize inspection intervals, reduce unplanned downtime, and extend component service life by 15–20%. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated airframe behavior under varied conditions, serving as a benchmark for validating experimental results. By bridging computational mechanics with maintenance logistics, this work aims to advance proactive maintenance strategies in aviation, directly supporting FAA guidelines for condition-based maintenance. The requested HPC allocation will enable scalable, high-throughput simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, ensuring robust validation of predictive algorithms critical to airworthiness certification and technician training programs.
cip_title: Airframe Mechanics and Aircraft Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all aircraft components other than engines, propellers, avionics, and instruments. Includes instruction in layout and fabrication of sheet metal, fabric, wood, and other materials into structural members, parts, and fittings, and replacement of damaged or worn parts such as control cables and hydraulic units.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual analysis of understudied multilingual manuscripts and print materials from the 17th–19th centuries. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural exchange, linguistic adaptation, and textual variance across globalized networks of knowledge production during this period. Existing scholarship has been limited by the computational demands of processing heterogeneous, non-Latin script materials (e.g., Arabic, Devanagari, and CJK scripts) at scale, as well as the need to integrate qualitative close-reading methods with quantitative analyses of semantic shifts and material features. The proposed work addresses these challenges through a hybrid computational approach combining transformer-based multilingual language models, optical character recognition (OCR) correction pipelines optimized for historical typography, and graph-based network analysis to trace textual reuse. HPC resources are critical for training custom OCR models on distributed GPU clusters, fine-tuning multilingual embeddings for low-resource historical languages, and executing parallelized text alignment algorithms across terabytes of digitized corpora. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of aligned textual variants, visualizations of transnational textual networks, and a methodological framework for computationally assisted comparative textual scholarship. By enabling the integration of marginalized non-Western materials into broader narratives of intellectual history, this project aims to reshape understandings of early modern knowledge circulation while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for computational humanities. The scalability of the tools developed will also provide a template for future studies requiring HPC-supported analysis of complex, multilingual textual ecosystems.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in digital humanities and textual studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The ocean’s chemical and physical systems are critical regulators of global climate, yet their responses to anthropogenic forcing remain poorly resolved at regional and decadal scales. This project seeks to advance understanding of coupled physical-chemical processes—including circulation-driven nutrient redistribution, air-sea gas exchange, and acidification feedbacks—using high-resolution modeling frameworks. A key challenge lies in capturing the interplay between fine-scale dynamics (e.g., submesoscale turbulence, coastal upwelling) and biogeochemical cycles, which operate across disparate spatiotemporal scales. Current models often oversimplify these interactions, limiting predictive accuracy for scenarios such as deoxygenation or carbon sequestration. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach leveraging a nested modeling system that integrates regional ocean circulation (ROMS) with a reactive transport model (RTM) for carbonate chemistry and nutrient speciation. The RTM will incorporate novel parameterizations of microbial mediation and particle-driven solute fluxes, informed by recent observational datasets. Simulations will resolve 3D hydrodynamic-ecological coupling at sub-kilometer resolution in critical regions (e.g., eastern boundary upwelling systems, Arctic shelf seas), with boundary conditions derived from global CMIP6 projections. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute ensemble runs spanning parameter uncertainties and climate scenarios, as well as to assimilate high-frequency sensor data from autonomous platforms. Anticipated outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into how sub-grid physical processes modulate alkalinity and dissolved inorganic carbon budgets, (2) improved projections of pH and oxygen variability under IPCC pathways, and (3) open-source model enhancements for community use. By elucidating scale-dependent feedbacks between ocean physics and chemistry, this work will directly inform climate mitigation strategies and marine resource management. The requested allocation supports 250,000 core-hours on GPU-accelerated nodes for model spin-up, sensitivity analyses, and scenario testing, enabling simulations impractical on local clusters due to memory and parallelism constraints.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical components, mechanisms, structure, and movement of ocean waters and their interaction with terrestrial and atmospheric phenomena. Includes instruction in material inputs and outputs, chemical and biochemical transformations in marine systems, equilibria studies, inorganic and organic ocean chemistry, oceanographic processes, sediment transport, zone processes, circulation, mixing, tidal movements, wave properties, and seawater properties.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid cloud-edge computing environments has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource management frameworks capable of addressing dynamic, heterogeneous workloads. Current approaches to resource allocation in multi-tiered IT service architectures often rely on static policies or isolated optimization metrics, leading to suboptimal utilization, energy inefficiency, and service-level agreement (SLA) violations during workload spikes. This project proposes the development of a context-aware resource orchestration system that integrates real-time telemetry data with predictive workload characterization to enable autonomous decision-making across infrastructure layers. The research will employ a combination of graph neural networks (GNNs) to model service dependencies and reinforcement learning (RL) agents trained on hybrid simulated-physical testbeds to optimize compute, storage, and network resources simultaneously. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three key components: 1) Large-scale simulation of multi-tenant cloud-edge environments using containerized workload generators, 2) Parallel training of ensemble ML models across diverse infrastructure scenarios, and 3) Evolutionary optimization of allocation policies through massively parallelized Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS). Expected outcomes include a novel framework for SLA-aware resource negotiation that dynamically balances energy consumption, latency constraints, and hardware heterogeneity metrics. The work will advance IT service management through measurable improvements in resource utilization efficiency (targeting 25-40% reductions in idle capacity) while maintaining sub-millisecond response time consistency across distributed nodes. By addressing the computational intensity of co-optimizing physical and virtual resource layers in modern service architectures, this research provides foundational insights for next-generation IT infrastructure automation, particularly relevant to organizations managing hybrid cloud deployments with strict sustainability requirements. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for adaptive infrastructure provisioning, directly contributing to operational efficiency in sectors reliant on complex, distributed computing ecosystems.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced cinematography workflows, particularly in rendering high-fidelity virtual environments and processing volumetric video data for immersive storytelling. While emerging technologies like neural radiance fields (NeRF) and real-time ray tracing enable unprecedented visual realism, their application in film production remains constrained by the limitations of consumer-grade hardware. Current workflows struggle with the latency and scale required to manipulate complex 3D scene reconstructions or dynamically adjust lighting simulations during interactive previsualization. This research proposes developing a GPU-accelerated pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to optimize two critical phases: 1) training diffusion models for AI-assisted texture synthesis across multi-resolution film assets, and 2) parallel processing of light field data captured from on-set volumetric video rigs. By containerizing photogrammetry processing tools (e.g., AliceVision Meshroom) and implementing distributed rendering through OpenImageIO, we aim to reduce scene reconstruction times for 8K footage by 60-75% compared to single-workstation benchmarks. A secondary focus involves prototyping a web-based interface for remote collaboration, allowing directors and cinematographers to iteratively refine virtual camera paths and depth-of-field parameters through HPC-powered simulation. The computational methodology integrates PyTorch-based neural networks for automated depth map refinement with physics-based light transport models rendered through Arnold on multi-GPU nodes. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for scalable virtual production, validated through comparative testing on both synthetic and live-action short film datasets.
