This work will provide quantitative benchmarks for HPC utilization in cinematographic contexts while advancing practical techniques for maintaining artistic intent under computationally intensive workflows. Results will be disseminated through film festivals and VIS/VR conferences to bridge gaps between media production communities and high-performance computing resources.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the making and producing of films and videos. Includes instruction in theory of film, film technology and equipment operation, film production, film directing, film editing, cinematographic art, film audio, techniques for making specific types of films and/or videos, media technologies, computer image making, multi-media production, and the planning and management of film/video operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize emergency medical services (EMS) system design and real-time decision-making through advanced computational modeling of dynamic resource allocation under uncertainty. A critical challenge in prehospital emergency care is balancing fluctuating demand patterns, geographic resource distribution, and time-sensitive clinical outcomes, particularly during mass casualty incidents or in wilderness EMS environments. Traditional static allocation models often fail to account for complex variables such as multi-casualty triage protocols, variable transport times, and competing priorities in tiered-response systems. To address this gap, we propose developing an ensemble machine learning framework integrated with discrete-event simulation to model EMS operations at metropolitan and regional scales. The computational approach will leverage historical EMS incident data, geospatial information systems, and synthetic scenario generation to train predictive models for demand forecasting, optimal unit deployment, and casualty outcome prediction. High-performance computing resources are essential for several components: 1) Parallel processing of Monte Carlo simulations across 10,000+ scenario variations incorporating weather, traffic, and disaster-scale events; 2) Training deep reinforcement learning agents on multi-objective optimization tasks balancing response times, clinician expertise matching, and resource preservation; 3) Real-time optimization of a digital twin environment simulating concurrent EMS incidents across an entire state-level service area. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of existing EMS records and prospective testing with regional EMS providers. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for strategic resource placement, dynamic dispatch algorithms adaptable to crisis conditions, and evidence-based frameworks for medical oversight policy. The computational models will specifically address wilderness EMS challenges through terrain-adaptive routing optimizations and mass casualty management through clustered resource reallocation strategies. By enabling large-scale simulation of EMS system performance under diverse operational constraints, this work aims to advance both the scientific understanding of complex emergency care systems and practical implementations of data-driven prehospital medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the leadership and medical oversight of pre- and out-of-hospital emergency care systems with advanced competencies in Emergency Medical System (EMS) system design, administration, and clinical care. Includes instruction in clinical aspects of EMS, medical oversight of EMS, mass casualty management, disaster planning and operations, wilderness EMS systems, and quality management and research.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing psychosocial intervention strategies in acute care settings, a critical yet understudied domain within clinical medical social work. The research addresses the challenge of personalizing patient-centered care plans that integrate clinical health data with dynamic psychosocial variables—such as caregiver availability, socioeconomic barriers, and mental health comorbidities—which are often siloed or analyzed in isolation. Current approaches to risk stratification in hospital social work rely on static heuristics, leading to inefficient resource allocation and suboptimal patient outcomes. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining federated learning and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient trajectories across heterogeneous datasets while preserving privacy. The ABM will incorporate multi-modal inputs, including structured electronic health records (EHRs), unstructured clinician notes processed via natural language processing (NLP), and real-time social determinants of health data from community partners. HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations to model population-level interactions across 10,000+ virtual agents, each with unique behavioral parameters derived from empirical datasets. The computational workflow will iteratively train deep reinforcement learning models to identify intervention timing and modality (e.g., crisis counseling, discharge coordination) that maximize 30-day post-discharge outcomes. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of 15,000+ historical cases from three health systems, with model performance evaluated against metrics including care plan adherence, readmission rates, and cost-effectiveness. This work is expected to produce the first open-source toolkit for adaptive intervention design in medical social work, directly addressing healthcare disparities by computationally encoding equity-aware decision protocols. The project’s outcomes will provide hospital systems with evidence-based strategies to allocate scarce social work resources while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational social science and precision health.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the specialized professional practice of social work, in collaboration with other health care professionals, in hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in social work, psychiatric case work, clinical interviewing techniques, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient testing and evaluation, patient and family counseling, social rehabilitation, patient care planning, record-keeping, and support services liaison.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the genomic and environmental drivers of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in livestock populations. Despite advances in veterinary diagnostics, the emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens in agricultural animals remains a pressing challenge, with direct implications for food security, animal welfare, and zoonotic disease risks. Current limitations in modeling complex host-pathogen-environment interactions—particularly at the scale of regional livestock systems—hinder the development of targeted mitigation strategies. To bridge this gap, we propose an integrative computational framework combining whole-genome sequencing data from bacterial isolates (Escherichia coli, Salmonella spp.) with geospatial, husbandry, and climate datasets across three high-density livestock regions. Machine learning models (e.g., graph neural networks, gradient-boosted decision trees) will be trained to identify genomic markers and husbandry practices associated with resistance gene transmission. Concurrently, agent-based epidemiological simulations will model AMR spread under varying climate and management scenarios. The scale of analysis—encompassing 50,000+ genomes, 10-year environmental time series, and multi-agent simulations for populations exceeding 1 million animals—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallelized data processing, large-model training, and stochastic simulation ensembles. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize high-risk resistance pathways, optimize biosecurity protocols, and inform regional AMR surveillance frameworks. By elucidating the interplay between pathogen genomics, management practices, and environmental stressors, this work will directly support evidence-based interventions to reduce antimicrobial use while maintaining animal health. The proposed computational workflows will be shared as open-source tools to enable similar analyses in under-resourced agricultural systems, amplifying the project’s impact on global veterinary health priorities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the study, prevention, and control of diseases in agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in environmental science, pharmacology, animal population studies, genetics, animal physiology and diet, disease prevention, treatment methodologies, and laboratory and testing procedures.

abstract: The increasing demand for rapid and accurate diagnostic imaging in clinical settings necessitates advancements in ultrasound technology, particularly in the context of real-time 3D/4D sonographic data processing. Current ultrasound systems face limitations in soft tissue contrast resolution and artifact reduction, especially when imaging complex anatomical structures or pathologies such as diffuse liver disease or early-stage tumors. This project proposes the development of a deep learning (DL)-enhanced computational framework to optimize ultrasound image reconstruction and analysis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address latency and scalability challenges. The research will focus on creating adaptive algorithms that integrate raw radiofrequency ultrasound data with biomechanical tissue models to improve edge detection, noise suppression, and quantitative parameter mapping (e.g., elastography, hemodynamic flow patterns). HPC clusters will be employed to train convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures on multi-institutional datasets comprising diverse patient demographics, pathological conditions, and transducer configurations. Parallel computing will enable rapid iteration of hybrid models combining physics-based simulations with data-driven learning, while GPU-accelerated workflows will facilitate validation of real-time processing pipelines. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for sonographers that automates image quality scoring, reduces inter-operator variability in scan interpretation, and enhances diagnostic confidence for borderline cases. The project bridges gaps between medical imaging physics, computational biomechanics, and clinical sonography practice, establishing a foundation for AI-assisted ultrasound systems capable of adaptive learning across evolving hardware platforms. By addressing computational bottlenecks in high-frame-rate 3D ultrasound processing, this work aims to expand access to precision sonographic diagnostics in resource-constrained settings while maintaining compliance with medical device cybersecurity and patient privacy standards.
cip_title: Diagnostic Medical Sonography/ Sonographer and Ultrasound Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to utilize medical ultrasound techniques to gather sonographic data used to diagnose a variety of conditions and diseases. Includes instruction in obtaining, reviewing, and integrating patient histories and data; patient instruction and care; anatomic, physiologic and pathologic data recording; sonographic data processing; sonography equipment operation; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cultural narratives of illness and contemporary clinical ethical frameworks using large-scale textual analysis and machine learning. Despite growing recognition of how sociocultural contexts shape health experiences, systematic analyses of narrative artifacts (literature, patient testimonials, historical medical texts) remain limited, particularly in their capacity to inform bioethical paradigms. The research addresses this gap by developing computational models to identify and analyze recurrent themes, metaphors, and ethical dilemmas across diverse textual corpora spanning fiction, medical case studies, and oral histories. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will apply transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) techniques to process multilingual texts (English, Spanish, Mandarin) and multimodal data (transcribed audio, digitized manuscripts) from curated repositories. Custom algorithms will classify ethical conflicts (e.g., autonomy vs. beneficence) and trace their evolution across cultural and temporal contexts. A hybrid approach combining unsupervised topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and network graph analytics will map relationships between narrative structures and normative ethical frameworks. The computational pipeline will be validated against annotated datasets co-developed with medical humanities scholars. Expected outcomes include an open-access annotated corpus of health-related narratives, a visualization platform for exploring ethical theme prevalence across demographics, and evidence-based recommendations for integrating narrative analysis into clinical ethics training. By bridging hermeneutic traditions in medical humanities with scalable computational methods, this work aims to advance understanding of how cultural narratives inform ethical decision-making in medicine, ultimately contributing to more context-sensitive approaches in patient care and policy development. The project’s scale—processing over 10TB of unstructured text and requiring GPU-accelerated model training—necessitates dedicated HPC resources to achieve rigorous, reproducible results within the proposed timeline.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of family health outcomes, addressing gaps in personalized care strategies for family practice nursing. Family health dynamics are shaped by complex, interdependent variables—including genetic predispositions, socio-environmental factors, and longitudinal health behaviors—that challenge traditional analytical methods. Current approaches often fail to integrate these multi-dimensional datasets at scale, limiting the ability to forecast risks or optimize interventions for diverse family structures. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework that combines machine learning (ML) and network analysis to model family health trajectories. The project will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from primary care systems, merged with publicly available socio-economic and environmental data, to train predictive algorithms. Key computational tasks include feature engineering for temporal health events, graph-based modeling of family relationship impacts, and simulation of intervention scenarios across synthetic family cohorts. HPC resources are critical to manage the high dimensionality of datasets, accelerate hyperparameter tuning for ML models, and enable large-scale Monte Carlo simulations assessing care pathway efficacy. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for identifying at-risk families, predicting deteriorations in chronic conditions, and recommending tailored prevention strategies. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making for nurse practitioners, bridging gaps between population-level data and individualized family care. By demonstrating the role of computational analytics in family nursing, the project aims to establish a precedent for data-driven primary care innovation while advancing methodological synergies between nursing practice and computational science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model ethical decision-making processes in critical care settings, where conflicting values, scarce resources, and time-sensitive interventions create complex moral dilemmas. While existing bioethics research relies heavily on qualitative analysis, this study integrates computational social science, normative ethics, and clinical data to simulate stakeholder interactions and evaluate the outcomes of differing ethical frameworks. The primary research problem centers on the lack of scalable, evidence-based tools to predict how variations in ethical reasoning—such as utilitarian versus rights-based approaches—affect resource allocation fairness, patient outcomes, and clinician well-being in high-stakes environments like emergency departments or organ transplant networks. Using high-performance computing resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate dynamic interactions among patients, providers, and institutional policies under resource-constrained scenarios. These ABMs will incorporate real-world data on triage protocols, historical allocation decisions, and demographic variables, paired with probabilistic representations of ethical principles derived from philosophical literature. Machine learning techniques will then analyze emergent patterns to identify decision pathways that optimize both moral coherence and clinical efficacy. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations to account for cultural, legal, and situational variability. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool for ethically informed resource allocation planning and a quantitative taxonomy of moral trade-offs in critical care. This work addresses a gap in applied bioethics by providing empirically grounded, computationally robust methods to navigate conflicts between autonomy, justice, and beneficence—advancing both theoretical ethics and practical policy design in rapidly evolving healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized care pathways for adults with complex chronic conditions, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease, through advanced computational modeling of patient-specific health trajectories. Current approaches to designing care plans often rely on generalized guidelines, which may inadequately account for dynamic interactions between comorbidities, medication regimens, and individual risk factors. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework to predict adverse health events and simulate the long-term impacts of tailored nursing interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-modal datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), longitudinal biomarker data, and patient-reported outcomes from a cohort of 15,000 adults. A hybrid neural architecture—combining temporal convolutional networks for EHR sequence modeling and graph-based methods to represent comorbid condition interactions—will be trained to forecast hospitalization risks and treatment response variability. Parallelized agent-based simulations will then model the systemic effects of nurse-led interventions, such as medication adherence support or targeted health education, under diverse physiological and socioeconomic scenarios. Computational outputs will inform the creation of adaptive decision-support tools for nurses, designed to prioritize high-risk patients and refine care strategies in real time. This work is expected to advance precision nursing by elucidating how individualized computational risk stratification can improve care coordination and resource allocation in adult health settings. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the scale of data integration, the complexity of simulating multi-organ pathophysiology, and the need for rapid, high-fidelity modeling to guide clinical workflows. Outcomes will directly contribute to evidence-based strategies for reducing preventable complications in adult populations while establishing a scalable computational framework for nursing research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide general care for adult patients. Includes instruction in adult primary care, adult pathophysiology, clinical management of medication and treatments, patient assessment and education, patient referral, and planning adult health maintenance programs.

abstract: Global food security is increasingly challenged by climate variability, population growth, and geopolitical disruptions, necessitating advanced predictive tools to optimize agricultural systems across diverse regions. This project seeks to address critical gaps in modeling crop-climate interactions and adaptive management strategies for staple crops under varying international agrobiomes. Current models often lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale data—spanning genomics, agroecology, and socio-economic decision-making—which limits their utility for guiding policy and on-ground practices. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable, geospatial modeling framework that simulates crop performance, pest dynamics, and resource-use efficiency under projected climate scenarios. The computational approach will combine process-based crop models, machine learning algorithms trained on global agricultural datasets (e.g., FAOSTAT, TerraClimate), and agent-based models to capture farmer decision-making in response to market and environmental stressors. Key innovations include the integration of genomic data to simulate climate-resilient crop traits and the coupling of biophysical models with international trade dynamics to assess cross-border food distribution impacts. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing simulations across thousands of climate-realized futures, calibrating models with high-resolution satellite imagery, and iterating complex optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for prioritizing crop varieties and management practices in vulnerable regions, such as sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, as well as open-access tools for policymakers to evaluate trade-offs between yield stability, economic viability, and environmental sustainability. By bridging computational agroinformatics with on-farm applicability, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary research in global agricultural systems while strengthening capacity for data-driven resilience planning.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of agricultural management and scientific principles to the problems of global food production and distribution, and to the study of the agricultural systems of other countries. Includes instruction in agricultural economics; comparative agricultural systems; international agribusiness and law; third-world development studies and economic development; and global applications of climate, soil, water resources, ecological and environmental studies, and animal and plant sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in nurse anesthesia by modeling patient-specific responses to anesthetic agents. A critical challenge in anesthesia practice is the variability in drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics across individuals, which contributes to adverse events such as intraoperative awareness, postoperative delirium, or hemodynamic instability. Current dosing protocols rely on population averages, but factors like genetic polymorphisms, comorbidities, and polypharmacy necessitate personalized approaches. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and physiological simulations to predict individualized anesthetic requirements. The project will develop machine learning models trained on retrospective EHRs from 50,000+ surgical cases, including anesthesia records, vital sign trajectories, and postoperative outcomes. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will characterize how genetic variants in drug-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYP2B6, CYP3A4) influence propofol and opioid metabolism. These components will be unified in a multiscale model optimized via HPC-enabled parameter sweeps to account for interactions between genetic, physiological, and clinical variables. The computational workflow will require parallel processing for large-scale genomic simulations, distributed training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data, and sensitivity analyses across simulated patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimal anesthetic dosing and real-time risk stratification tools deployable in perioperative settings. Successful validation against prospective clinical data could transform anesthesia practice by reducing trial-and-error dosing and mitigating adverse events. This work will also establish a scalable infrastructure for integrating -omics data into nurse anesthesia research, addressing a critical gap in the field. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of multiscale modeling and enable rapid iteration of predictive algorithms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on maternal and child health (MCH) disparities by modeling the complex interplay of social, environmental, and biological factors influencing health outcomes. Despite progress in public health, inequities persist in maternal mortality, preterm birth, and childhood developmental outcomes, particularly among marginalized populations. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to account for dynamic, multi-level determinants (e.g., socioeconomic conditions, healthcare access, environmental exposures) operating across spatial and temporal scales. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) and machine learning frameworks to simulate population-level health trajectories and identify intervention leverage points. The ABMs will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, geospatial environmental data, and longitudinal social surveys, to represent individual and community interactions within evolving policy contexts. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian inference for model calibration and ensemble machine learning to predict risk factors for adverse outcomes. HPC resources are essential due to the scale of data (millions of patient records, high-resolution environmental layers) and the computational intensity of simulating stochastic interactions across diverse synthetic populations. Parallelized simulations will enable sensitivity analyses to test hypothetical policy scenarios, such as expanded prenatal care access or pollution reduction initiatives. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of modifiable risk factors contributing to MCH disparities, (2) predictive tools to prioritize high-risk populations for targeted interventions, and (3) policy-relevant insights into the cost-efficacy of intervention strategies. By enabling large-scale, multi-domain simulations, this project will advance precision public health approaches in MCH, with potential applications to state and federal health agencies collaborating on this research. The requested resources will support model training, validation, and real-time scenario testing, which are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the dynamic interplay between neurocognitive development and environmental influences during early childhood. The core research problem centers on modeling how children’s evolving neural architectures—particularly in prefrontal and limbic regions—interact with environmental stimuli (e.g., caregiver interactions, educational media) to shape developmental trajectories of executive function and emotion regulation. Traditional computational approaches in developmental psychology have been constrained by the inability to process high-dimensional datasets (e.g., longitudinal fMRI, eye-tracking, and ecological momentary assessment data) while simulating complex, bidirectional child-environment interactions. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating deep neural networks with agent-based modeling. The neural network component will analyze multimodal neurobehavioral data from a longitudinal cohort (N=500, ages 3–8) to identify latent patterns of brain-behavior-environment covariation. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate how individual differences in neurocognitive maturation interact with stochastically varying environmental inputs to predict developmental outcomes. HPC resources are critical for three tasks: (1) training graph convolutional networks on neuroimaging connectomes with temporal dependencies, (2) running large-scale parameter sweeps to test developmental hypotheses across simulated environments, and (3) employing Bayesian optimization to refine models against empirical behavioral data. Expected outcomes include the first computational models capable of jointly representing neural plasticity, environmental complexity, and their nonlinear interactions during sensitive developmental periods. These tools will enable novel predictions about optimal intervention timing and content for enhancing cognitive-emotional development, while advancing methodological paradigms in developmental science. All models and pipelines will be made open-source to catalyze computationally intensive research across developmental psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from infancy through childhood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: Environmental pollution control systems require precise modeling to optimize their design and operation, yet current computational approaches often lack the resolution to capture complex, multi-scale interactions between physicochemical processes and fluid dynamics. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-fidelity simulations of pollutant dispersion and treatment in engineered systems. The research focuses on two interconnected areas: (1) simulating turbulent airflow and particulate transport in industrial-scale air quality control systems, and (2) modeling reactive transport in advanced wastewater treatment reactors. Computational methods will integrate finite volume-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with machine learning algorithms to accelerate parameter calibration and uncertainty quantification. Large-eddy simulation (LES) frameworks will resolve subgrid-scale turbulence-chemistry interactions, while graph neural networks will predict optimal reactor configurations under variable pollutant loads. The simulations will incorporate real-world sensor data from partner municipalities and industrial facilities to ensure practical relevance. By utilizing HPC resources, this work aims to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks that limit traditional single-node simulations, enabling kilometer-scale domain analyses with millimeter-level resolution. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for scrubber efficiency, biofilm reactor performance, and emergency response scenarios for chemical spills. These tools will provide environmental engineers with actionable insights to design adaptive pollution control infrastructure, reducing energy consumption and operational costs while meeting stringent regulatory standards. The project will also train undergraduate environmental engineering technology students in HPC workflows, bridging gaps between computational methods and applied environmental system management. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large dataset storage, and iterative model testing over an 18-month period.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using indoor and outdoor environmental pollution control systems. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project investigates the cultural and ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence (AI) integration in clinical decision-making through computational analysis of historical, literary, and patient-generated texts. While AI adoption in medicine accelerates, debates about its alignment with patient values, biases in training data, and the erosion of humanistic care remain unresolved. We propose a mixed-methods approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning with hermeneutic frameworks from medical humanities to analyze three corpora: 1) 19th-21st century medical ethics literature (450,000+ texts), 2) contemporary patient narratives from online forums (10 million posts), and 3) AI training datasets used in diagnostic systems. Using transformer-based models (BERT, GPT-4 architecture), we will perform cross-temporal semantic mapping of "clinical judgment" across professional vs. lay sources, identify value-laden language in AI documentation, and detect narrative patterns excluded from machine learning pipelines. High-performance computing resources are essential for training domain-specific language models on heterogeneous historical data, running parallel sentiment analysis across 12 languages, and simulating iterative dialogue between ethical frameworks and patient narratives through reinforcement learning. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible ontology mapping tensions between technical and humanistic conceptions of care, an audit framework for bias detection in AI training corpora, and generative models that synthesize patient narratives with clinical guidelines. This work bridges computational social science and medical epistemology, offering novel methods to foreground humanistic values in health technology design while advancing NLP techniques for analyzing temporally layered discourse.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the scientific understanding of Ayurvedic pharmacological synergies and therapeutic mechanisms through computational modeling and multi-omics integration. Despite the widespread use of Ayurvedic polyherbal formulations in managing chronic and complex diseases, their molecular mechanisms—particularly the synergistic interactions between phytochemicals, human proteins, and metabolic pathways—remain poorly characterized. Traditional reductionist approaches often fail to capture the holistic, multi-target nature of these formulations, necessitating advanced computational frameworks to model their systemic effects. The proposed research will employ molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and network pharmacology to analyze interactions between 50+ prioritized Ayurvedic herbs (from texts such as Charaka Samhita) and human proteomic targets linked to inflammation, oxidative stress, and immune regulation. Machine learning models will be trained on curated datasets of phytochemical properties, clinical outcomes, and historical Ayurvedic case records to predict formulation efficacy across diverse prakriti (constitutional) types. Additionally, genomic and metabolomic data from ongoing clinical studies on Ayurvedic detoxification (Panchakarma) therapies will be integrated to identify biomarker signatures of therapeutic response. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabytes of structural biology data, running parallelized simulations of multi-compound interactions, and optimizing neural networks for personalized treatment predictions. Expected outcomes include validated computational models of Ayurvedic synergy, novel biomarkers for treatment stratification, and a publicly accessible database linking traditional formulations to modern pharmacological targets. By bridging Ayurvedic principles with systems biology, this work aims to establish a rigorous computational foundation for evidence-based integration of Ayurveda into global healthcare paradigms, while preserving its holistic philosophical framework.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The pharmaceutical industry faces increasing complexity in market dynamics, driven by evolving regulatory landscapes, heterogeneous patient populations, and competitive pressures. Traditional marketing and management strategies often struggle to integrate multi-dimensional data—including electronic health records, sales trajectories, social media sentiment, and supply chain variables—to inform real-time decision-making. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to optimize pharmaceutical marketing strategies and resource allocation using high-performance computing (HPC). The research problem centers on modeling the interplay between drug efficacy, pricing, promotional efforts, and patient access while accounting for regional healthcare policies and competitor behavior. Leveraging HPC resources, we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate market responses under diverse scenarios, machine learning algorithms to predict sales trends from multi-source datasets, and network analysis to identify critical stakeholders in drug adoption pathways. Large-scale parallel processing will enable the integration of terabyte-scale datasets, including anonymized patient records and global sales data, while reducing runtime for complex optimization tasks from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to quantify the impact of marketing interventions, identify high-value patient segments, and optimize promotional budgets across therapeutic areas. This work will provide actionable insights for pharmaceutical managers to allocate resources efficiently, mitigate risks in product launches, and align marketing strategies with patient outcomes. By bridging computational scalability with domain-specific challenges in pharmaceutical management, this project aims to advance data-driven decision-making in healthcare industries, ultimately supporting equitable drug access and sustainable business practices.
cip_definition: A program that combines the study of basic and pharmaceutical sciences with marketing and management studies; and that prepares individuals for careers in pharmaceutical sales, marketing, management, and related fields within the health care industry. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, pharmaceutics, pharmacology, health care systems, issues and structure of pharmaceutical industry, management, pharmaceutical marketing, pharmaceutical and medical product management, and legal issues.

abstract: The dynamics of fault system interactions and their role in earthquake nucleation remain poorly understood due to the computational challenges of simulating multi-fault networks at tectonic timescales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution 3D computational model to investigate stress transfer and rupture cascades within geometrically complex fault systems. The research will integrate geophysical datasets from active fault zones with a hybrid finite-discrete element approach to simulate fault interactions over decadal to millennial timescales. Simulations will track stress accumulation, frictional weakening, and rupture propagation across fault networks with variable geometries and rock properties. The computational framework will leverage parallelized solvers to handle the non-linear contact mechanics and high strain-rate gradients inherent to fault rupture processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve the necessary spatial resolution (meter-scale fault segments) and temporal scope (10^3–10^5 years) while capturing system-scale emergent behaviors. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how fault network topology influences earthquake clustering and maximum magnitude potential, with implications for seismic hazard assessment in tectonically active regions. The project will also generate open-source tools for scalable fault interaction modeling, enabling community-driven advances in dynamic rupture simulations. By resolving the computational barriers to simulating multi-fault systems, this work aims to bridge gaps between short-term geodetic observations and long-term geological records of fault activity, ultimately improving probabilistic forecasts of earthquake sequences. The requested HPC allocation will support iterative model development, parameter space exploration, and ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainties in fault system behavior.
cip_title: Geological and Earth Sciences/ Geosciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in geological and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Tamil philology and dialectology, addressing critical gaps in the analysis of Tamil’s historical evolution and regional variations. While Classical and Modern Tamil have been extensively studied through traditional methods, the computational modeling of linguistic shifts, dialectal divergence, and sociolinguistic influences remains underdeveloped due to the scale and complexity of datasets. The research problem centers on analyzing large, multi-regional corpora spanning 2,000 years, including digitized palm-leaf manuscripts, modern literary texts, and oral recordings, to map phonetic, syntactic, and semantic changes across time and geography. Key challenges include processing non-standardized orthographies, managing code-switching phenomena in texts, and detecting subtle dialectal features in audio data. The proposed computational approach integrates neural language models trained on Tamil-specific corpora, phonetic alignment algorithms for cross-dialect comparisons, and graph-based methods to trace lexical diffusion pathways. HPC resources will enable the parallelization of these tasks, particularly for transformer-based models fine-tuned to handle archaic Tamil forms, and the storage of intermediate outputs from terabyte-scale text and speech datasets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Tamil linguistic variants, predictive models of dialectal intelligibility, and tools for automated dating of undetermined historical texts. These results will directly support philological research, language preservation initiatives, and educational applications, such as dialect-aware pedagogical tools. By bridging computational linguistics with Tamil scholarship, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for under-resourced Dravidian languages while advancing interdisciplinary connections between humanities research and high-performance computing.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Tamil language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Classical and Modern Tamil; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable, adaptive framework for simulating and countering AI-driven cyber-physical attacks in contested military networks. Current defense paradigms struggle to model the convergence of cyber deception tactics, autonomous malware propagation, and adversarial machine learning—particularly when targeting integrated command-and-control systems across heterogeneous edge devices. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create multi-domain digital twins that replicate network topologies, electromagnetic warfare conditions, and adversarial behavior patterns observed in modern hybrid conflicts. Computational methods will combine graph neural networks for vulnerability propagation analysis, Monte Carlo simulations of zero-day exploit cascades, and real-time adversarial reinforcement learning agents trained to identify emergent attack vectors. Key technical challenges include maintaining low-latency synchronization across distributed simulations of 100,000+ node networks while integrating hardware-in-the-loop validation for tactical radios and satellite terminals. Anticipated outcomes include predictive metrics for infrastructure fragility under coordinated cyber-electronic attacks, automated countermeasure generation protocols, and an open-source threat library documenting simulated adversarial TTPs (tactics, techniques, and procedures). This work directly addresses the DoD's need for proactive cyber resilience frameworks that account for evolving quantum-resistant cryptography requirements and AI-enhanced electronic warfare capabilities. By enabling large-scale, dynamic modeling of cross-domain effects between cyber and physical battle spaces, the proposed computational approach will inform next-generation defensive architectures and accelerate the development of autonomous response systems compliant with international norms of proportionality in cyber operations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: The increasing complexity of nanoscale systems demands advanced computational tools to bridge the gap between atomic-level interactions and emergent mesoscale behaviors in engineered nanomaterials. This project addresses the challenge of predicting and optimizing thermal transport in hybrid nanoparticle assemblies, where conventional continuum models fail to capture quantum confinement effects and interface-dominated phonon scattering. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve real-time energy dissipation pathways in these systems, limiting the design of efficient nanoscale thermal management solutions for next-generation optoelectronic and energy conversion devices. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating first-principles density functional theory (DFT), machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics (ML-MD), and stochastic lattice Boltzmann methods (SLBM) to model heat transfer across hierarchical nanostructures. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to perform large-scale simulations of gold-silicon core-shell nanoparticles and graphene-oxide superlattices, systems with tunable interface geometries that experimental collaborators are synthesizing. Key innovations include developing neural network potentials trained on DFT datasets to extend MD simulation timescales while preserving quantum mechanical accuracy, coupled with adaptive meshing algorithms to link atomistic results to SLBM continuum predictions. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative maps of thermal conductivity as a function of nanoparticle size, interface roughness, and lattice strain, (2) open-source software modules for automated multiscale parameter transfer, and (3) design rules for anisotropic thermal metamaterials with programmable heat flux directionality. This work will advance fundamental understanding of nanoscale energy transport while providing critical computational tools for engineering thermal interfaces in quantum dot solar cells and neuromorphic computing architectures. The requested GPU-accelerated computing resources are essential for handling the >10^6-atom MD systems and teraflop-scale DFT calculations required to achieve statistical significance across parameter space variations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the engineering of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across engineering disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate morphosyntactic variation across under-documented South Asian languages through computational modeling, addressing critical gaps in linguistic typology and resource development. While South Asia hosts extraordinary linguistic diversity, many languages—particularly minority and non-dominant varieties—lack robust digital corpora or systematic structural analyses. Traditional manual methods struggle to process the scale and complexity of these languages’ agglutinative morphology, clause-chaining syntax, and dialectal continua. To overcome these challenges, the research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to train transformer-based models on a newly assembled multilingual corpus spanning Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Tibeto-Burman, and Austroasiatic languages. Parallelized pipelines will process digitized texts, oral narratives, and archival materials, extracting grammatical features (e.g., case marking, verb serialization) and simulating contact-induced changes via agent-based models. Custom attention mechanisms will adapt existing NLP tools to handle script normalization, code-switching patterns, and non-linear morphological segmentation. The computational workflows require distributed memory architectures to manage terabyte-scale datasets and GPU-accelerated training for deep learning tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) probabilistic typological maps of morphosyntactic traits across the region, (2) open-access tools for low-resource language analysis, and (3) evidence-based models of language change under shifting sociolinguistic pressures. By integrating computational linguistics with field-based data, this work advances theoretical understanding of South Asia’s linguistic ecosystems while supporting endangered language preservation and NLP applications for marginalized communities. The requested HPC resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations, optimize model architectures, and democratize access to underrepresented languages through public APIs and annotated corpora.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: South Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in South Asian languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational design processes in generative and interactive visual media, addressing the challenge of scaling complex, algorithm-driven artistic workflows. Current methods for generating high-fidelity digital art, dynamic 3D environments, or AI-augmented design prototypes are constrained by the computational limits of consumer-grade hardware, particularly when handling real-time interaction, multi-modal data integration, or high-dimensional generative algorithms. The proposed research focuses on developing and optimizing a suite of computational tools for parametric design, neural network-driven asset synthesis, and immersive environment simulation. Key objectives include training custom diffusion models for material and texture generation, deploying agent-based systems for adaptive user interaction in virtual installations, and simulating physics-based behaviors in large-scale digital fabrication workflows. HPC resources will enable parallelized rendering of 4K-8K visual outputs, distributed training of generative adversarial networks (GANs) on heterogeneous datasets spanning historical design archives and sensor-captured environmental inputs, and real-time optimization of interactive media frameworks using GPU-accelerated physics engines. Anticipated outcomes include novel methodologies for bridging procedural content generation with human-in-the-loop design refinement, significantly reducing iteration times for complex artistic projects. The work aims to establish scalable pipelines for computationally intensive visual arts practices while contributing open-source tools to the digital design community. By addressing resource barriers in processing multimodal inputs and generating hyper-detailed outputs, this research has implications for sustainable design innovation, cross-disciplinary media art, and the integration of machine learning into applied arts pedagogy.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in design and applied arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the historical transmission and adaptation of medical knowledge across global networks during the 19th and early 20th centuries, with a focus on how socio-economic disparities influenced the adoption of biomedical technologies. The study addresses a critical gap in the historiography of medicine by systematically analyzing large-scale, multilingual archival materials—including medical journals, institutional records, and correspondence—to trace the diffusion of surgical practices, diagnostic tools, and public health policies between colonial powers and colonized regions. A key challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, unstructured historical data spanning multiple languages and geographic contexts, which requires advanced computational methods. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract semantic patterns from digitized texts, network analysis to map knowledge exchange pathways, and geospatial modeling to visualize regional disparities in medical resource distribution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on historical medical terminology, conducting large-scale sentiment and thematic analyses across temporal scales, and running iterative simulations of knowledge diffusion under varying socio-economic parameters. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously undocumented epistemic hierarchies in colonial medicine, quantitative evidence linking infrastructure investments to therapeutic outcomes, and an open-access digital repository of annotated historical datasets. By integrating computational social science methods with traditional historiographic approaches, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven historical inquiry while contributing new perspectives on the relationship between medical globalization and health inequities. The requested computing resources will enable processing of over 500,000 pages of primary source materials and support the development of customizable analysis pipelines for future interdisciplinary studies in the history of medicine.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution and socio-economic context of medical theories, education, practices, and technologies; and on the history of diseases, therapeutics, patients, and healers. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of the historiography of medicine; the history of science, medicine, and technology; and of research methods in the history of medicine.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in clinical esthetics through computational modeling of skin biomechanics and treatment outcomes. The esthetics field faces a critical gap in evidence-based protocols for personalized skin interventions, particularly in post-operative care and advanced dermatological esthetics. Current methods rely heavily on generalized guidelines, with limited capacity to predict individual responses to treatments such as chemical peels, microdermabrasion, or lymphatic drainage techniques. To address this, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of skin tissue dynamics, agent-based simulations of cellular responses to esthetic treatments, and machine learning (ML) models trained on clinical and biometric datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D skin scans, real-time fluid dynamics simulations for product absorption studies, and probabilistic analysis of treatment efficacy across diverse skin types and conditions. Key challenges include optimizing biomechanical parameters for heterogeneous skin layers and validating models against longitudinal clinical data from partner dermatology clinics. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing treatment sequences, reducing adverse reactions, and tailoring interventions to individual healing trajectories. This work will establish a novel computational paradigm for esthetic medicine, bridging gaps between empirical practice and quantitative analysis. By enabling data-driven personalization of care, the project aims to elevate clinical standards, improve patient outcomes in post-operative settings, and inform the development of next-generation esthetic technologies. The computational frameworks generated will also serve as foundational resources for educational programs, fostering integration of computational literacy into esthetician training curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and body with advanced chemical and cosmetic preparations and esthetic medical treatments, and to function as licensed master or medical estheticians in dermatologists' and plastic surgeons' offices as well as in salons and spas. Includes instruction in advanced anatomy and physiology, skin properties and disorders, sanitation and infection control, advanced facial treatments, spa body treatments, advanced extractions, corrective makeup, chemical peels, microdermabrasion, lymphatic drainage and advanced massage techniques, pre- and post-operative esthetic skin care, client/patient evaluation and care, applicable laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for integrating multi-modal biomedical data with dynamic 3D medical illustrations to enhance precision in oncological visualization and decision support. The research addresses a critical gap in current clinical informatics systems, which often lack the capacity to synthesize high-resolution imaging, genomic data, and real-time physiological metrics into interactive, spatially contextualized models. Traditional approaches to medical illustration and data interpretation remain siloed, limiting their utility in complex cases such as heterogeneous tumor microenvironments. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline leveraging generative adversarial networks (GANs) and agent-based modeling to simulate cellular-scale interactions within patient-specific anatomical reconstructions. The computational workflow will process raw data from histopathology slides, single-cell RNA sequencing, and functional MRI scans, aligning these inputs with biomechanical constraints derived from finite element analysis. By deploying distributed GPU-accelerated training and multi-scale optimization algorithms on HPC clusters, the project aims to generate adaptive 3D visualizations that dynamically update in response to simulated treatment perturbations. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for collaborative annotation of hybrid data-illustration models, validated against retrospective glioblastoma datasets. The resource-intensive nature of iteratively rendering high-fidelity environments—requiring petabytes of memory bandwidth and parallelized tensor operations—necessitates access to advanced computing infrastructure. Success in this interdisciplinary effort could redefine standards for precision medicine workflows, offering clinicians an intuitive interface to explore spatiotemporal relationships between molecular heterogeneity, drug penetration, and structural deformation in solid tumors.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in medical illustration and informatics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in computational complexity theory by investigating the scalability and practical limitations of quantum-inspired algorithms for solving NP-hard problems. While such algorithms—including simulated annealing variants and tensor network contractions—have shown theoretical promise in approximating solutions to combinatorial optimization problems, their empirical behavior under large-scale, real-world problem instances remains poorly understood. A core challenge lies in analyzing the trade-offs between algorithmic precision, computational resource requirements, and problem dimensionality, particularly as instances scale beyond classical simulation capabilities. To address this, we propose a dual mathematical-computational approach: (1) developing novel complexity-theoretic models to quantify the asymptotic resource costs of these algorithms under non-uniform input distributions, and (2) implementing large-scale simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to empirically validate theoretical predictions. The computational work will focus on parallelized simulations of algorithm behavior across problem sizes ranging from 10³ to 10⁷ variables, leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed memory architectures. Key metrics will include time-to-solution convergence, memory overhead patterns, and error propagation dynamics in approximation schemes. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the exponential state-space growth inherent to these simulations, particularly when benchmarking against classical baselines like branch-and-bound algorithms. Expected outcomes include new complexity classifications for quantum-inspired methods, optimized implementation strategies for emerging computing architectures, and practical guidelines for algorithm selection in applied mathematics contexts. By bridging theoretical complexity analysis with large-scale empirical validation, this work aims to establish rigorous performance boundaries for next-generation optimization algorithms while advancing methodological frameworks for computational resource analysis in theoretical computer science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical techniques underlying computing, including the theory of computation, and logic in computer science and artificial intelligence.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of organic contaminant behavior in heterogeneous environmental systems, with a focus on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and chlorinated pesticides in soil-water matrices. A critical challenge in environmental chemistry lies in elucidating the molecular-scale interactions governing contaminant adsorption, transformation, and transport across dynamic interfaces, as experimental methods alone struggle to resolve transient reaction pathways or multi-phase interactions at scale. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to quantify free energy barriers for contaminant degradation, sorption affinities at mineral-organic interfaces, and diffusion coefficients in porous soil aggregates. These simulations will parameterize a reactive transport model to predict long-term contaminant fate under varying hydrological and geochemical conditions. The HPC environment is essential due to the system complexity: DFT calculations require thousands of CPU hours to map potential energy surfaces for defluorination reactions, while MD simulations of interfacial processes demand GPU-accelerated sampling across microsecond timescales. By coupling computational outputs with laboratory-derived spectroscopic data, we aim to identify dominant transformation products and critical environmental factors influencing contaminant persistence. The resulting models will provide mechanistic insights into site-specific remediation strategies, such as optimized sorbent deployment or enhanced microbial degradation. This work directly addresses gaps in risk assessment frameworks by establishing computational workflows to prioritize high-concern contaminants and evaluate intervention efficacy under climate-driven hydrological extremes. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution of contaminant dynamics at environmentally relevant scales, bridging molecular-scale chemistry with field-scale predictions to support regulatory and mitigation efforts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of natural systems (air, water, and soil) through the use of chemical techniques and instrumentation, with an emphasis on the movement and fate of pollutants and chemical aspects of contaminant remediation. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; aquatic, soil, and atmospheric chemistry; environmental engineering; environmental toxicology; and analytical methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in digital literacy and multimedia composition within professional and technical communication. The core research problem addresses the scalability and generalizability of automated usability testing frameworks for complex, multimodal documents (e.g., interactive technical manuals, AI-driven knowledge bases). Current methods for evaluating user engagement and comprehension in such documents rely on small-scale manual analyses, limiting their applicability to diverse audiences and emerging formats like augmented reality (AR) guides. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models trained on large-scale interaction datasets—including eye-tracking patterns, clickstream data, and semantic annotations—to predict usability issues and optimize document design. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for text analysis, computer vision techniques for layout assessment, and graph-based algorithms to model user navigation paths. These methods require HPC resources due to the volume of multimodal data (∼50 TB of annotated user interactions) and the iterative nature of training deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models for context-aware readability scoring. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated usability benchmarking, validated against human expert evaluations, and a corpus of annotated technical documents optimized for accessibility compliance. This work will directly inform pedagogy in professional writing programs by providing evidence-based frameworks for teaching data-driven document design, while enabling industry partners to deploy scalable solutions for maintaining clarity in rapidly evolving technical communication environments. The project bridges computational humanities and user experience research, advancing scholarly understanding of how algorithmic methods can complement human-centered writing practices.
cip_title: Professional, Technical, Business, and Scientific Writing
cip_definition: A program that focuses on professional, technical, business, and scientific writing; and that prepares individuals for academic positions or for professional careers as writers, editors, researchers, and related careers in business, government, non-profits, and the professions. Includes instruction in theories of rhetoric, writing, and digital literacy; document design, production, and management; visual rhetoric and multimedia composition; documentation development; usability testing; web writing; and publishing in print and electronic media.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance composite materials in industries such as renewable energy and medical technology necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize their design, manufacturing, and repair processes. Current challenges include predicting delamination, fiber-matrix interfacial failures, and environmental degradation in complex composite structures, which are difficult to address through experimental methods alone. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate composite behavior under operational stresses, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning (ML) to predict failure modes and optimize material architectures. The computational framework will focus on wind turbine blade composites and carbon fiber-reinforced medical prostheses, emphasizing resin infusion processes, curing dynamics, and repair protocols. By leveraging parallelized solvers and GPU-accelerated ML algorithms, the models will analyze terabyte-scale datasets from microstructural imaging and in-situ sensor networks to correlate processing parameters with mechanical performance. Key deliverables include predictive tools for minimizing void formation during mold-based manufacturing and identifying optimal repair strategies for damaged composites. The outcomes will directly support curriculum development in composite materials technology, providing students with case studies in computational design and virtual prototyping. Access to HPC resources is critical due to the high dimensionality of multiphysics simulations and the need for real-time parameter optimization in digital twin environments. This research will advance the integration of computational tools into composite technology workflows, reducing reliance on trial-and-error methods and accelerating the development of durable, cost-effective materials for sustainable energy and healthcare applications.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and use of composite materials in aircraft technology, automotive technology, boats, medical prostheses, and wind turbines. Includes instruction in computer-aided design and drafting, composite materials and processes, composite maintenance, composite manufacturing, composite repair, material science, and mold manufacturing and production.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in multi-level teacher education by modeling and analyzing the efficacy of adaptive teaching strategies across diverse classroom environments. A critical challenge in teacher preparation is designing training frameworks that equip educators to address the cognitive, social, and developmental variability inherent in teaching students at multiple grade levels (e.g., K-5, 6-8). Existing studies lack granular computational models to simulate how pedagogical approaches interact with factors such as student age, subject complexity, and classroom diversity. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based simulations that replicate multi-age classroom dynamics, integrating real-world data from partner school districts on student performance, teacher interventions, and longitudinal outcomes. These simulations will parameterize variables including instructional pacing, differentiated content delivery, and assessment feedback loops, enabling the testing of hypothetical teaching strategies under varied conditions. Machine learning methods will then identify optimal strategy combinations for target educational levels. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (10,000+ simulated classrooms with 20-30 agents each), the need for parallelized parameter sweeps, and the complexity of training neural networks on high-dimensional interaction data. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based insights into how specific instructional practices succeed or falter when applied across developmental stages, (2) a publicly accessible repository of simulated classroom scenarios for teacher training programs, and (3) predictive tools to help educators tailor strategies for mixed-level classrooms. By bridging computational modeling and teacher education, this work aims to transform how multi-level teaching competencies are developed, directly supporting the preparation of versatile educators capable of addressing 21st-century classroom diversity.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at more than one educational level, such as a combined program in elementary/secondary, early childhood/elementary, elementary/middle school, or junior high/high school teacher education.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive swarm robotics systems in dynamic, unstructured environments—a challenge at the intersection of distributed control, nonlinear dynamics, and real-time resource allocation. Swarm robotics, while promising for applications ranging from environmental monitoring to disaster response, faces critical bottlenecks in scalability and adaptability when deployed in complex settings with unpredictable obstacles, communication constraints, and conflicting objectives. Traditional control strategies often fail to balance computational efficiency with emergent coordination, particularly when scaling to hundreds or thousands of agents. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for decentralized decision-making, multi-fidelity surrogate modeling to predict emergent swarm behaviors, and physics-informed reinforcement learning to adaptively optimize task-specific objectives. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale swarms in realistic 3D environments, train deep learning models on heterogeneous sensorimotor data streams, and iteratively refine control policies through parallelized evolutionary algorithms. Key innovations include the development of lightweight, transferable GNN architectures for edge computation and a novel metric for quantifying swarm resilience under stochastic perturbations. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for swarm simulation, validated control paradigms that maintain stability despite agent attrition or environmental shifts, and generalized design principles for engineering robust collective systems. This work bridges gaps between theoretical swarm intelligence and practical engineering deployment, with potential applications in infrastructure inspection, precision agriculture, and emergency response—domains requiring autonomous systems capable of self-organization without centralized oversight. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of swarm interactions and enabling real-time policy updates at scale.
