cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to solve a wide variety of practical problems in industry, social organization, public works, and commerce. Includes instruction in undifferentiated and individualized programs in engineering.

abstract: Binocular vision disorders, such as strabismus and amblyopia, present complex challenges in diagnosis and management due to their multifactorial etiology involving neural, muscular, and anatomical interactions. Current clinical assessments rely on static measurements that fail to capture the dynamic, system-level behavior of oculomotor control, limiting personalized treatment strategies. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating high-fidelity biophysical modeling of the oculomotor system with machine learning to simulate and predict adaptive responses to orthoptic therapies. The research will address two gaps: (1) the lack of dynamic models linking neural signaling to ocular muscle coordination in pathological conditions and (2) the need for predictive tools to optimize prismatic, surgical, or vision therapy interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of coupled neural oscillators governing vergence and version eye movements, calibrated against high-resolution ocular coherence tomography (OCT) and electrooculography (EOG) datasets from pediatric and adult cohorts. Parallelized finite element modeling will map mechanical stress distributions in extraocular muscles under simulated surgical adjustments, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine therapeutic protocols based on simulated neuroplastic outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated multiscale model of oculomotor adaptation and an open-source tool for simulating patient-specific treatment responses. This work will advance orthoptics by establishing a computational paradigm to quantify dynamic binocular interactions, reduce trial-and-error in clinical decision-making, and identify novel biomarkers for early intervention in acquired or congenital eye alignment disorders. The computational infrastructure will support future integration of real-time eye-tracking data and generative AI for adaptive therapy design, positioning orthoptics at the forefront of precision medicine in ophthalmologic care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists, to analyze, evaluate, and treat specific disorders of vision, eye movement, and eye alignment in children and adults. Includes instruction in eye anatomy, neuroanatomy, physiology, pharmacology, ophthalmic optics, diagnostic testing and measurement, orthoptic treatment therapy, systemic ocular diseases and disorders, principles of surgery, examination techniques, patient education, child psychology and development, learning disabilities, medical writing, and record-keeping.

abstract: This research investigates the evolving role of cyber-enabled influence operations in shaping diplomatic negotiations between state actors, a critical yet understudied dimension of modern international relations. As states increasingly leverage hybrid tactics—including disinformation campaigns, algorithmic manipulation of public discourse, and strategic data leaks—to gain advantage in bilateral and multilateral talks, traditional frameworks for analyzing diplomatic power dynamics fail to account for the computational scale and complexity of these interactions. The project employs a mixed-methods approach combining large-scale text analysis of diplomatic communiqués, social media datasets, and leaked documents with agent-based modeling to simulate how cyber influence strategies impact negotiation outcomes. High-performance computing resources are required to process multilingual textual corpora spanning state-aligned media outputs, official policy documents, and covert coordination networks identified through metadata analysis. Machine learning models will classify rhetorical patterns and escalation signals, while network analysis will map the diffusion of narrative elements across state and non-state actors. The computational simulations will stress-test existing theories of deterrence and credibility under conditions of asymmetric cyber capability, incorporating real-world data on recent diplomatic crises. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying the "latent pressure" exerted by cyber influence campaigns during formal negotiations, identification of early-warning signatures for diplomatic breakdowns attributable to hybrid tactics, and policy-relevant metrics for assessing the strategic value of cyber assets in national security prioritization. By bridging computational social science with international security studies, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding how emergent technologies are reshaping the foundational mechanics of statecraft.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a predictive modeling framework for optimizing staffing, resource allocation, and care quality in long-term care (LTC) facilities. The growing demand for LTC services, driven by aging populations and complex care needs, has intensified pressures on administrators to balance operational efficiency with regulatory compliance and patient-centered outcomes. Current decision-making tools often rely on static, historical data or simplified heuristics, limiting their ability to adapt to dynamic factors such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff turnover, and evolving policy requirements. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and discrete-event simulation (DES) to analyze multi-source datasets, including electronic health records, staffing logs, and financial reports. HPC resources are essential to process these high-dimensional datasets (spanning thousands of patient-years and facility variables) and execute parallelized simulations exploring "what-if" scenarios under diverse constraints (e.g., budget limits, infection outbreaks, or regulatory changes). The ABM component will simulate interactions among patients, staff, and institutional policies, while ML algorithms will identify patterns in care outcomes and operational bottlenecks. DES will model facility workflows to quantify the impact of interventions like adjusted staff-to-patient ratios or redesigned care pathways. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that enables LTC administrators to dynamically forecast resource needs, mitigate risks of understaffing, and prioritize investments in training or technology. By quantifying trade-offs between cost, compliance, and care quality, this work aims to advance evidence-based management practices in LTC settings while informing policy discussions on sustainable aging-care systems. The scalability of the framework, enabled by HPC, will support future extensions to regional or national-level analyses of LTC infrastructure resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of nursing homes, assisted living facilities, adult day care, home health services, and other long term care settings and agencies serving the elderly and disabled. Includes instruction in social and clinical aspects of aging, health care delivery systems, nursing home administration, assisted living administration, aging policy and government programs, ethics, business management, financial management, human resource management, marketing, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, culturally responsive language-learning tools for multilingual K-12 classrooms. Current digital platforms often fail to account for the intersectional linguistic, cultural, and cognitive profiles of learners in diverse educational settings, leading to suboptimal pedagogical outcomes. To address this gap, we propose building a machine learning framework that dynamically models student interactions, language proficiency trajectories, and sociocultural context variables. The research will utilize anonymized multimodal datasets from partner school districts, including longitudinal assessment scores, classroom dialogue transcripts, and teacher feedback logs. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for dialect and code-switching pattern analysis, graph neural networks to map cross-linguistic transfer mechanisms, and agent-based simulations of classroom interaction dynamics. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on low-resource languages spoken by student populations (e.g., Indigenous languages, heritage dialects) and for running large-scale parameter sweeps to optimize adaptive tutoring algorithms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating culturally situated language exercises and a predictive dashboard to help teachers allocate differentiated resources. By computationally modeling how multicultural identity negotiation intersects with language acquisition, this work aims to provide evidence-based strategies for teacher preparation programs while advancing methodological frameworks at the intersection of educational equity and computational linguistics. The proposed HPC allocation will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining the privacy-preserving federated learning architecture required for sensitive educational data.
cip_title: Bilingual, Multilingual, and Multicultural Education, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in bilingual, multilingual, and multicultural Education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated computational framework for optimizing sustainable urban real estate development under dynamic socio-environmental constraints. The core challenge lies in balancing rapid urbanization with climate resilience, affordability, and community well-being—a multidimensional problem requiring simultaneous analysis of interdependent variables such as shifting land-use regulations, evolving market demands, carbon emission targets, and infrastructure strain. Traditional modeling tools often silo these factors, leading to fragmented decision-making. To address this, the project proposes a novel agent-based simulation platform that combines generative urban design algorithms, real-time economic forecasting, and participatory stakeholder behavior modeling. The computational approach will integrate geospatial datasets (e.g., zoning maps, flood risk projections), machine learning models trained on historical development patterns, and Monte Carlo methods to simulate thousands of development scenarios across diverse policy and climate futures. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to metropolitan-level granularity while maintaining sub-neighborhood spatial resolution and hourly temporal resolution over decadal time horizons. Expected outcomes include a dynamic risk-assessment tool that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, equity, and ecological impact, as well as generative design prototypes for mixed-use developments adaptable to regional climate scenarios. By enabling rapid iteration through complex design-policy permutations, this work aims to advance evidence-based frameworks for public-private development partnerships, particularly in underserved communities facing disproportionate climate vulnerability. The resulting open-source models will provide municipal planners and developers with actionable insights to navigate conflicting priorities in urban growth, setting a precedent for computational resource integration in non-traditional, policy-adjacent applied research domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create and redevelop housing, offices, retail centers, and industrial sites. Includes instruction in architectural design and construction, historic preservation, landscape architecture, urban planning and design, business, real estate and land use law, public policy, and engineering.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare workflows and communication demands in inpatient units has highlighted critical inefficiencies in traditional Health Unit Coordinator (HUC) practices, particularly in managing real-time data streams, prioritizing interdisciplinary communications, and mitigating errors during high-stress periods. This project proposes a computational approach to model, analyze, and optimize HUC workflows by integrating electronic health record (EHR) metadata, interdepartmental communication logs, and sensor-derived patient flow data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop agent-based simulations to map decision-making patterns under varying clinical loads and apply natural language processing (NLP) to classify communication urgency in transcribed orders and messages. A machine learning pipeline will identify predictors of workflow bottlenecks and latent risks in task sequencing, using federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across participating hospital systems. The computational framework will be validated against observational datasets from six acute care units, encompassing over 200,000 discrete HUC interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dynamic task prioritization, a risk-aware alert system for order transcription errors, and generative AI tools to simulate training scenarios for emergent care contexts. By quantifying the relationship between administrative efficiency and patient throughput, this research aims to establish evidence-based standards for HUC training programs while providing scalable computational tools to reduce cognitive load and improve care coordination. The project bridges healthcare operations research, human factors engineering, and clinical informatics, offering a novel pathway to enhance the resilience of frontline administrative roles in modern healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the performance and reliability of alternative fuel vehicle (AFV) systems, with a focus on hybrid-electric powertrains and compressed natural gas (CNG) storage solutions. A critical challenge in AFV technology is balancing energy efficiency, emissions reduction, and system durability under diverse operating conditions. Current diagnostic and design methods rely heavily on empirical testing, which is time-intensive and limited in exploring the full parameter space of multi-fuel systems. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex interactions between mechanical, thermal, and electrical components in AFVs. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model CNG tank stress profiles during rapid refueling cycles, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess hybrid battery pack thermal management under extreme climates. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to predict failure modes in retrofitted AFV electrical systems. The simulations will incorporate real-world driving patterns, fuel mixtures, and aging effects on materials. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to accelerate parameter optimization for conversion kits and generate predictive maintenance frameworks adaptable to varying vehicle platforms. Expected outcomes include validated digital twins of AFV subsystems, open-source simulation tools for technician training programs, and design guidelines for improving the safety of aftermarket conversions. This research will directly support the development of standardized protocols for AFV retrofitting while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. The computational resources will enable scaling to fleet-level analyses, providing actionable insights for policymakers and automotive technicians working toward sustainable transportation infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the maintenance of alternative fuel vehicles and the conversion of standard vehicles to AFV status. Includes instruction in electrical vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles, hybrid fuel technology, electrical and electronic systems, engine performance, diagnosis and repair, and conversion/installation.

abstract: The proposed research addresses critical gaps in understanding the multifactorial etiology of reproductive failures in domestic livestock, focusing on the interplay between genomic, metabolic, and environmental factors that contribute to conditions such as recurrent pregnancy loss, subfertility, and perinatal mortality. Despite advances in theriogenology, predictive models capable of integrating large-scale omics data (e.g., transcriptomics, proteomics, metagenomics) with real-time sensor-based physiological monitoring remain underdeveloped, limiting early diagnostics and targeted interventions. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex datasets spanning 10,000+ genomes from cattle and swine cohorts, longitudinal health records, and environmental variables (temperature, humidity, pathogen load) to identify predictive biomarkers and mechanistic pathways. Machine learning frameworks, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be deployed to model nonlinear interactions between host genetics, microbial communities, and stressors during gestation. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate structural perturbations in key reproductive proteins (e.g., anti-Müllerian hormone, uterine serpins) linked to mutations prevalent in affected populations. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing of ~500 TB of raw sequencing data, iterative model training across multiple nodes, and real-time integration of IoT-enabled livestock health monitors. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive risk stratification tool for reproductive failures deployable in clinical veterinary settings, (2) novel biomarkers for early detection of subclinical infections impacting fetal development, and (3) atomistic insights into mutation-driven functional deficits in reproductive proteins, informing future therapeutic design. By resolving scalability bottlenecks in multi-modal data integration, this work will establish a computational framework to advance precision theriogenology, directly supporting sustainable livestock production and animal welfare goals. The requested HPC allocation is essential for achieving the project’s objectives within biologically relevant timescales, given the iterative nature of deep learning workflows and the need for high-throughput simulation runs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of diseases and health problems affecting the reproductive systems of animals, and the comprehensive care and treatment of parent animals, animal fetuses and newborn or newly hatched animals throughout the gestation period.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the pedagogical training of health occupations educators through advanced computational modeling of instructional strategies and competency development. Health occupations teachers must integrate evolving clinical practices with evidence-based teaching methods, yet existing training frameworks often lack data-driven approaches to optimize curriculum design or predict learner outcomes. The research problem centers on the need to analyze complex, multi-modal educational datasets—including simulated clinical training performance, student engagement metrics, and longitudinal competency assessments—to identify patterns that improve instructional efficacy. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models that correlate teaching interventions with learner proficiency across diverse healthcare specializations. These models will process large-scale datasets from virtual simulation platforms, video-recorded teaching demonstrations, and standardized assessment results to quantify the impact of specific pedagogical techniques. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom dynamics under varying instructional scenarios, enabling the exploration of adaptive teaching strategies for heterogeneous learner populations. The computational demands of training deep neural networks on high-dimensional educational data (e.g., natural language processing of reflective teaching journals, computer vision analysis of clinical skill demonstrations) necessitate distributed computing architectures. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for personalizing health occupations teacher training and evidence-based guidelines for sequencing clinical-pedagogical content. By identifying computationally intensive patterns in teaching effectiveness, this work aims to directly improve the quality of vocational health education, ultimately strengthening the preparedness of healthcare professionals entering clinical settings. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the scale and complexity of analyzing multi-institutional training datasets while maintaining the granularity required for discipline-specific insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational health occupations programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The physics of entangled polymer systems under non-equilibrium conditions presents unresolved challenges in understanding the interplay between chain dynamics, topological constraints, and macroscopic material response. While prior studies have characterized linear viscoelastic behavior in melts, the nonlinear regime—critical for applications involving flow-induced crystallization, fracture, or processing—remains poorly predicted due to computational limitations in capturing multi-scale dynamics. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate coarse-grained polymer models under large deformation, explicitly resolving entanglement interactions and strain-rate-dependent relaxation mechanisms. Using a hybrid approach combining slip-spring models and non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD), we will quantify the evolution of entanglement density, orientation, and stress propagation in bidisperse melts and lightly crosslinked networks. Simulations will span time scales from segmental relaxation (10⁻⁹ s) to terminal flow (10⁻³ s) using GPU-accelerated algorithms optimized for parallel architectures. Key deliverables include parametrizing a constitutive model for strain-hardening in entangled systems and identifying universal scaling relationships between entanglement spacing, strain rate, and dissipative losses. The computational workflow will utilize the LAMMPS framework with custom modifications to track topological constraints in real time. Expected outcomes will advance fundamental knowledge of how molecular-scale entanglements govern macroscopic failure modes and energy dissipation in polymer fluids, directly informing experimental efforts to design polymers with tailored nonlinear viscoelasticity. By bridging atomistic insights to continuum-level predictions, this work addresses a critical gap in polymer physics while demonstrating scalable methodologies for simulating complex fluids on HPC platforms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanical, optical, and transport properties of polymers with respect to the underlying physics and physical chemistry of polymers in melt, solution, and solid state

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance the analysis of clinical laboratory data, addressing critical bottlenecks in processing complex datasets generated during routine diagnostics. Clinical laboratories face growing demands to interpret high-dimensional data from hematology, microbiology, and urinalysis tests, particularly as multi-parametric assays and genomic screening become integrated into standard workflows. Traditional analysis methods, reliant on manual interpretation or limited computational tools, struggle to efficiently identify subtle patterns or correlations in these datasets, potentially delaying diagnostic insights. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models optimized for HPC environments to automate the classification of pathological anomalies, predict antimicrobial resistance profiles, and stratify patient risk based on multi-omics data. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing raw laboratory data (e.g., flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, and next-generation sequencing outputs), training ensemble models on annotated clinical datasets, and validating predictions against gold-standard diagnostic outcomes. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization for deep neural networks, and real-time simulations of microbial growth dynamics under varying treatment conditions. Expected outcomes include scalable algorithms for rapid detection of aberrant hematologic parameters, predictive tools for guiding personalized antimicrobial therapies, and a cloud-based interface to disseminate models for clinical validation. By integrating HPC-driven analytics into laboratory training modules, this project will equip future technicians with skills in computational biomarker discovery and foster interdisciplinary collaboration between laboratory medicine and data science. The results aim to reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve accuracy in detecting low-prevalence pathogens, and inform resource allocation strategies for clinical laboratories adopting precision medicine approaches.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists/medical technologists, to perform routine medical laboratory procedures and tests and to apply preset strategies to record and analyze data. Includes instruction in general laboratory procedures and skills; laboratory mathematics; medical computer applications; interpersonal and communications skills; and the basic principles of hematology, medical microbiology, immunohematology, immunology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis.

abstract: Pharmaceutical marketing and management decisions require integration of complex, multidimensional data spanning clinical outcomes, market dynamics, and regulatory constraints. Current approaches often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the nonlinear interactions between drug characteristics, prescriber behavior, payer policies, and patient adherence. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate pharmaceutical market ecosystems, enabling data-driven optimization of product launch strategies, pricing models, and post-marketing surveillance. The research will leverage real-world datasets including anonymized electronic health records, insurance claims, social media sentiment analysis, and historical market performance data for comparable therapeutics. Machine learning techniques—including graph neural networks to model stakeholder networks and transformer-based architectures for longitudinal prescription pattern analysis—will be implemented alongside agent-based simulation platforms. These computational tools will be deployed to investigate three interconnected challenges: (1) predicting regional variations in adoption rates for novel therapies under different reimbursement scenarios, (2) optimizing sales force allocation through geospatial-temporal demand forecasting, and (3) quantifying the market impact of adverse event reporting patterns. The scale of data integration (anticipated at 50+ TB from heterogeneous sources) and the need for multi-parameter sensitivity analyses across thousands of simulated market scenarios necessitate high-performance computing resources. Expected outcomes include an open-source modeling toolkit for pharmacoeconomic analysis, validated against retrospective case studies of FDA-approved drugs, and decision support frameworks to address ethical considerations in targeted marketing practices. This work directly supports the program's mission to advance evidence-based management strategies at the intersection of pharmaceutical science and healthcare commerce, with potential applications in workforce training modules and industry partnership initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that combines the study of basic and pharmaceutical sciences with marketing and management studies; and that prepares individuals for careers in pharmaceutical sales, marketing, management, and related fields within the health care industry. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, pharmaceutics, pharmacology, health care systems, issues and structure of pharmaceutical industry, management, pharmaceutical marketing, pharmaceutical and medical product management, and legal issues.

abstract: Advances in neuroradiology hinge on the ability to process and interpret complex, multimodal imaging data to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes for neurological disorders. Current clinical workflows face challenges in integrating high-resolution structural MRI, functional MRI (fMRI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and perfusion-weighted imaging (PWI) data into unified predictive models. These limitations hinder the identification of subtle biomarkers for early-stage neurodegenerative diseases, cerebrovascular anomalies, and pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop deep learning models for multimodal neuroimaging analysis. The project will focus on three objectives: (1) creating automated pipelines for preprocessing and co-registering heterogeneous neuroimaging datasets, (2) training 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to detect cross-modal spatial-temporal patterns linked to pathologies, and (3) validating models against clinical outcomes using longitudinal patient data from institutional databases. The scale of data—encompassing >10,000 imaging studies from 2,500 patients—and the computational demands of 3D voxel-wise analysis necessitate GPU-accelerated workflows and distributed memory parallelization. HPC resources will enable rapid hyperparameter optimization, ensemble model training, and uncertainty quantification via Monte Carlo dropout techniques. Successful implementation will yield tools for quantifying microstructural changes in multiple sclerosis, predicting aneurysm rupture risk from hemodynamic features, and differentiating tumor progression from treatment effects in glioma patients. By automating labor-intensive segmentation tasks and uncovering latent imaging biomarkers, this work aims to reduce diagnostic variability and support personalized treatment planning. The computational infrastructure developed will be shared with collaborating institutions, fostering scalable translational research in neuroradiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the brain, spine, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and head and neck in adults and children.

abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias present a significant diagnostic challenge due to their transient nature and the subtlety of electrophysiological signatures in early-stage pathologies. While electrocardiograph (ECG) technology remains central to detection, conventional analysis methods struggle to identify nuanced, non-linear patterns in high-resolution ECG data, particularly in underrepresented populations with atypical cardiac phenotypes. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a machine learning framework capable of analyzing multi-lead ECG waveforms at unprecedented temporal and spatial resolutions. The research focuses on integrating raw, unprocessed signal data from ambulatory ECG monitors with patient-specific biomechanical simulations to identify latent arrhythmogenic substrates. Computational workflows will employ three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) trained on petabyte-scale datasets of dynamic cardiac vector loops, coupled with finite element modeling of myocardial strain patterns derived from concurrent echocardiography data. Key challenges include optimizing GPU-accelerated pipelines for real-time feature extraction from prolonged (72+ hour) recordings and addressing class imbalance in rare arrhythmia subtypes through synthetic data generation via generative adversarial networks (GANs). Expected outcomes include a novel diagnostic tool for early detection of paroxysmal conduction abnormalities and a publicly accessible repository of simulated arrhythmia profiles correlated with demographic variables. The project’s computational demands—particularly for parallel processing of time-frequency analyses and large-scale hyperparameter optimization—necessitate cluster-based HPC infrastructure with high-memory nodes and specialized accelerators for deep learning tasks. By bridging gaps between clinical electrophysiology, computational biomechanics, and artificial intelligence, this work aims to establish a paradigm for personalized arrhythmia risk stratification while advancing methodological standards for resource-intensive biomedical signal processing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Soil systems represent complex interfaces where microbial communities interact dynamically with organic and inorganic constituents, driving critical biogeochemical processes. However, predicting these interactions at scale remains a challenge due to the nonlinear feedbacks between soil chemistry, microbial metabolism, and environmental variables. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational model integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, soil chemistry datasets, and reaction-transport dynamics to simulate microbial-mediated carbon and nutrient cycling in agricultural soils. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize and validate a spatially explicit, multi-agent model that couples microbial metabolic networks with soil pore-scale chemistry. Key objectives include (1) simulating the impacts of soil organic matter composition on microbial community assembly and function, (2) quantifying redox-driven nutrient fluxes under varying moisture regimes, and (3) identifying chemical-microbial synergies that enhance soil fertility and carbon sequestration. Computational workflows will utilize agent-based modeling frameworks (e.g., INDISIM-Soils) and genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) constrained by empirical soil metagenomic and spectroscopic data from Midwest agricultural sites. HPC capabilities are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of microbial interactions, scaling simulations to field-relevant spatial domains, and performing sensitivity analyses across diverse soil types. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize soil amendment strategies, reduce fertilizer dependency, and inform climate-resilient agricultural practices. By bridging microbial ecology and soil chemistry through advanced computation, this work will advance fundamental understanding of soil biogeochemical thresholds while directly supporting sustainable land management goals in agroecosystems. The requested resources will enable terabyte-scale data integration, parallelized simulation of 10^5+ microbial agents, and iterative model refinement via machine learning approaches, collectively addressing a critical gap in soil health forecasting capacity.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and microbiological theories and methods (in combination) to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instructional combination of microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of patient-specific biomechanical models for optimizing dental implant osseointegration in osteoporotic bone. While dental implants are a cornerstone of restorative dentistry, their long-term success in patients with systemic bone loss remains inconsistent due to poorly understood mechanobiological interactions between implant surfaces, local bone microstructure, and systemic metabolic factors. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the multiscale complexity of bone remodeling dynamics, necessitating a computational framework integrating microstructural bone imaging data, mechanoregulatory tissue differentiation algorithms, and stochastic modeling of cellular responses. The proposed research will employ finite element analysis derived from high-resolution cone-beam CT scans to model strain energy distributions at bone-implant interfaces, coupled with agent-based simulations of osteoclast/osteoblast activity modulated by systemic osteoporosis biomarkers. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify critical topological implant features that maximize strain compatibility with deteriorating trabecular architectures. By parallelizing these multiscale simulations across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to generate predictive models that account for both mechanical and biological variables influencing osseointegration failure. Expected outcomes include a novel computational pipeline for virtual implant prototyping, validated against longitudinal clinical radiomics data from retrospective patient cohorts. This work will establish a paradigm for computationally driven personalized implantology, reducing revision surgeries through data-driven design optimization while advancing fundamental understanding of bone-implant crosstalk in metabolic bone disease. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petascale imaging datasets and executing complex multiphysics simulations impractical on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program that generally prepares dentists in one or more of the oral sciences and advanced/graduate dentistry specialties.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the modeling and optimization of urban infrastructure resilience under climate-driven stressors using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Aging transportation networks, water distribution systems, and flood mitigation structures face increasing risks from extreme weather events, yet existing simulation tools struggle to integrate multi-physics interactions at city scales. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework coupling finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity, hydrodynamic models for flood propagation, and machine learning (ML)-based surrogate models to accelerate scenario testing. The research will develop parallelized workflows using open-source codes (e.g., OpenFOAM, SWMM) enhanced with graph neural networks to capture interdependencies between infrastructure components. Key challenges include resolving spatiotemporal conflicts between millimeter-scale material degradation processes and kilometer-scale urban hydrological systems while maintaining computational feasibility. HPC resources will enable parametric studies of 10,000+ stormwater management scenarios, optimizing green-gray infrastructure retrofits under probabilistic precipitation forecasts. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin prototype for mid-sized cities, reduced-order models for rapid risk assessment, and open-access datasets quantifying failure cascades across transportation and water networks. This work directly supports climate adaptation planning by providing engineers and policymakers with scalable tools to prioritize investments in critical infrastructure hardening. The requested computing allocations will allow unprecedented resolution in simulating coupled hydraulic-structural systems, overcoming memory and runtime barriers that currently limit conventional single-node simulations.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for simulating and optimizing industrial automation systems, with a focus on addressing the challenges of real-time control, energy efficiency, and system reliability in complex manufacturing environments. Current limitations in simulating multi-domain systems—such as integrated electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components—stem from the computational intensity of modeling interactions between programmable logic controllers (PLCs), sensor-actuator networks, and physical processes. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable high-fidelity, parallelized simulations of automation systems at scale. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) developing modular digital twins of industrial systems using physics-based modeling tools (e.g., MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS Twin Builder) coupled with discrete-event simulations of control logic; (2) deploying machine learning algorithms to optimize PLC code and predictive maintenance schedules through iterative, large-scale parameter sweeps; and (3) validating models against real-world data from collaborative industry partners. By harnessing GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work will facilitate the exploration of edge cases and failure modes impractical to test physically, such as cascading faults in robotic assembly lines or transient responses in hybrid energy systems. Expected outcomes include novel control strategies for reducing energy consumption in variable-speed drive systems, robust fault-detection algorithms for hydraulic actuators, and a publicly accessible repository of benchmark models for the automation research community. This project will directly enhance the educational mission of the Automation Engineer Technology program by integrating HPC-driven case studies into advanced robotics and process control courses, while providing industry stakeholders with tools to accelerate the adoption of sustainable, resilient automation technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, installing, calibrating, modifying and maintaining automated systems. Includes instruction in computer systems; electronics and instrumentation; programmable logic controllers (PLCs); electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control systems; actuator and sensor systems; process control; robotics; applications to specific industrial tasks; and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the detection and interpretation of complex financial anomalies in large-scale transactional datasets, with applications to real-time auditing processes. Traditional auditing methods often struggle to identify subtle, systemic irregularities in high-volume, heterogeneous data environments, particularly in cross-border transactions or decentralized financial ecosystems. The proposed work leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized machine learning models capable of processing terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining the chain of evidence required for regulatory compliance. Key computational challenges include optimizing graph-based anomaly detection algorithms to map multi-hop transaction networks, integrating temporal-spatial analysis of financial flows, and simulating adversarial evasion tactics to stress-test audit models. The project will employ hybrid architectures combining GPU-accelerated deep learning for pattern recognition and CPU-driven agent-based simulations to model evolving fraud strategies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive audit sampling, a benchmark dataset of synthetically generated transaction networks with embedded anomalies, and performance metrics comparing computational efficiency against conventional auditing software. By enabling near-real-time analysis of dynamic financial systems, this research aims to reduce false-positive rates in anomaly detection by at least 40% while maintaining audit trail integrity, ultimately supporting more proactive risk mitigation in global supply chains and cryptocurrency transaction monitoring. The scalability of the proposed methods will be validated through partnerships with fintech auditing firms, focusing on use cases involving blockchain-based assets and multi-jurisdictional tax compliance datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, including certified accountants, to perform independent internal and external appraisals to evaluate organizational financial and operational activities, ensure compliance with laws and policies, safeguard assets, and promote effective planning and resource allocation. Includes instruction in advanced accounting, audit tools and techniques, sampling, risk and control, audit planning, audit function management, law and regulations, environmental auditing, information technology applications, professional standards and ethics, and specific industry and service sector problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing wastewater treatment systems and enhancing water recycling efficiency through advanced computational modeling. Current treatment methods often struggle to balance energy consumption, cost, and effectiveness, particularly when managing complex contaminants such as emerging organic pollutants and microplastics. Traditional experimental approaches to system design and process optimization are resource-intensive and fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale interactions within treatment systems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity simulations of fluid dynamics, reactive transport, and microbial community interactions in wastewater environments. The study will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-physics models that couple computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with biogeochemical reaction networks, enabling granular analysis of treatment processes across spatial and temporal scales. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter calibration, identify optimal operational conditions, and predict system performance under varying influent compositions. Key objectives include simulating membrane fouling dynamics in real-time, optimizing aeration strategies in biological reactors, and evaluating the feasibility of hybrid treatment-recycling systems for decentralized applications. The computational demands of these tasks—including large-scale matrix operations, parallelized CFD solvers, and ensemble modeling for uncertainty quantification—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing energy use in treatment plants, strategies to enhance contaminant removal efficiency by 20-30%, and scalable models for adaptive water recycling systems in water-stressed regions. By bridging gaps between process engineering and computational science, this work aims to advance sustainable water management practices, reduce operational costs, and support regulatory decision-making for next-generation wastewater infrastructure.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of doctrinal evolution across Buddhist philosophical traditions, with a focus on Madhyamaka, Yogacara, and Zen textual corpora. While Buddhist studies has historically relied on close textual and philological methods, the scale and linguistic complexity of primary sources—spanning multilingual manuscripts, commentaries, and ritual texts—present challenges for systematic comparative analysis. This research aims to address these limitations by developing computational workflows to identify patterns in philosophical argumentation, trace conceptual shifts across historical periods, and map cross-cultural transmission routes. Key objectives include training multilingual natural language processing (NLP) models on digitized Buddhist texts in Classical Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit; implementing semantic network analysis to compare doctrinal frameworks; and simulating textual transmission pathways through agent-based modeling. The proposed computational architecture will integrate optical character recognition for non-Latin scripts, transformer-based language models fine-tuned on Buddhist philosophical terminology, and graph databases to represent intertextual relationships. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable pipeline for analyzing understudied commentarial traditions, 2) quantitative evidence for doctrinal hybridization processes in East Asian Buddhism, and 3) open-access tools for computational religious studies. By combining HPC capabilities with domain-specific hermeneutics, this project will enable novel investigations into how Buddhist philosophical concepts were reinterpreted across cultural contexts while establishing methodological frameworks for large-scale comparative analysis in religious studies. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, parallel processing of multi-terabyte text corpora, and storage of high-resolution manuscript images, addressing critical bottlenecks in processing premodern religious texts at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy preached by Siddartha Gautama, the Buddha, in ancient India and subsequently interpreted by his disciples and apostles; together with the intellectual, cultural, social, and ritual developments of the faith and its branches. Includes instruction in Buddhist sacred literature (Tripitaka, etc.) and study of one or more of the main branches including Early Buddhism, Hinayana, Theravada, Madhyamaka, Yogacara, Pure Land, Shingon, Tendai, Nichiren Shu, Zen, Tibetan, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and deploy computational tools to enhance the accessibility and preservation of non-textual cultural heritage materials within digital archives, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in large-scale multimedia data processing. As libraries and archives increasingly digitize diverse collections—including audiovisual recordings, born-digital art, and complex multimedia artifacts—existing cataloging and retrieval systems struggle to manage the volume, heterogeneity, and technical demands of these materials. Traditional metadata creation workflows, often manual and labor-intensive, are ill-suited for dynamic or non-textual content, leading to gaps in discoverability and long-term preservation. This research proposes an interdisciplinary computational approach combining machine learning (ML), signal processing, and semantic analysis to automate metadata extraction, enhance content classification, and enable cross-collection searchability for under-described materials. HPC resources will be critical for training ML models on multimodal datasets (e.g., audio spectrograms, image frames, embedded textual features) and optimizing feature extraction pipelines for time-based media. The project will focus on developing scalable workflows for processing petabytes of archival data, integrating domain-specific ontologies from library science to improve model interpretability and alignment with archival standards. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for automated metadata generation, a framework for HPC-assisted preservation of format-obsolete digital artifacts, and novel interfaces for cross-institutional querying of multimedia archives. By bridging gaps between computational scalability and archival practice, this work aims to empower libraries and cultural institutions to democratize access to historically marginalized or technically complex collections, ensuring their usability amid rapidly evolving digital preservation challenges. The computational workflows and models produced will be validated using test cases from partner institutions, focusing on Indigenous oral history archives and experimental digital art collections, with results disseminated through both library science and HPC research communities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist professional librarians and archivists. Includes instruction in principles, systems, processes, and procedures of library and archive operation; library resources and services; processes of acquisition, cataloging, storage, and display systems; discovery and retrieval of requested materials; and management of books, periodicals, and other documents and records.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of analyzing large-scale economic and business datasets in journalism, where traditional computational tools are increasingly inadequate for real-time, data-driven storytelling. Business and economic journalists face challenges in efficiently processing heterogeneous data—such as global financial markets data, corporate disclosures, social media sentiment, and macroeconomic indicators—while maintaining analytical rigor and meeting tight deadlines. This research proposes the development of a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to automate data ingestion, cleaning, and analysis workflows for investigative and explanatory reporting. The methodology integrates natural language processing (NLP) to extract insights from unstructured text (e.g., earnings calls, regulatory filings), machine learning models to detect patterns in market trends and corporate behavior, and interactive visualization tools to communicate findings across multimedia platforms. Key computational tasks include parallel processing of terabyte-scale historical financial datasets, sentiment analysis of news archives, and real-time simulation of economic policy impacts using agent-based models. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for training deep learning models on textual corpora and deploy containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated business data journalism, case studies demonstrating HPC-enabled investigative reporting techniques, and pedagogical resources for training journalists in computational storytelling. By enhancing the capacity to synthesize complex economic information rapidly, this work aims to elevate the precision and impact of business journalism while fostering public understanding of economic systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming latency and scalability barriers inherent in analyzing cross-sectoral, high-velocity data, thereby bridging the gap between academic research tools and industry-grade journalism practices.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares students to gather, analyze, and synthesize verbal and visual information to communicate stories related to business and economics across multiple media platforms. Includes instruction in accounting, business, business and economic reporting, business law, economics, finance, financial accounting and reporting, ethics, journalistic research methods and resources, and journalism skills and techniques.

abstract: This research project addresses the challenge of optimizing dynamic pricing and personalized marketing strategies in hospitality and recreation operations through advanced computational modeling. Traditional approaches in this domain often rely on static segmentation or heuristic pricing rules, which fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between customer behavior, real-time demand fluctuations, and multi-channel marketing impacts. The project proposes developing an agent-based simulation framework integrated with machine learning (ML) to model complex decision pathways of customers across digital platforms, physical venues, and seasonal recreation ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle large-scale simulations incorporating heterogeneous data streams—including IoT sensor outputs from recreational facilities, social media sentiment trajectories, and transactional histories—while maintaining sub-second latency requirements for scenario testing. The computational architecture will combine graph neural networks to map customer journey interdependencies with reinforcement learning agents that simulate adaptive pricing responses under variable capacity constraints. Key outcomes include predictive models quantifying the marginal impact of hyper-localized promotions on revenue per available unit (RevPAU) in hybrid hospitality-recreation environments, as well as an open-source optimization toolkit for real-time marketing operations. By enabling granular analysis of emergent behaviors in multi-stakeholder leisure ecosystems, this work aims to advance computational marketing science while addressing critical gaps in yield management for experience-driven industries. The requested resources will support parallelized training of ensemble ML models, storage and processing of terabyte-scale synthetic customer datasets, and validation against proprietary industry benchmarks from partner organizations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide marketing services in the hospitality and leisure fields. Includes instruction in hospitality operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, basic office management, retail sports, recreation equipment, food and beverage.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize instructional strategies for postsecondary STEM courses by modeling the relationship between teaching methods, learner engagement, and educational outcomes through large-scale computational analysis. Despite advances in learning science, many instructors lack evidence-based frameworks to dynamically adapt course designs across diverse classroom contexts. The research problem centers on identifying computationally detectable patterns in multimodal educational datasets—including LMS interaction logs, formative assessment performance, and classroom observation metrics—to guide real-time pedagogical adjustments. We propose developing machine learning models trained on anonymized datasets from 150+ university courses (spanning physics, biology, and engineering disciplines) to cluster effective teaching practices under varying enrollment sizes, student preparedness levels, and modality constraints (in-person/hybrid/online). The computational approach combines natural language processing of syllabus artifacts, temporal graph analysis of discussion forum interactions, and agent-based simulations of motivation dynamics. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing >50TB of heterogeneous data, running parallelized hyperparameter optimization for deep neural networks predicting student success, and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses on instructional design variables. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for quantifying alignment between course structures and evidence-based andragogical principles, (2) predictive models to help instructors prioritize syllabus modifications, and (3) generative AI prototypes that recommend personalized teaching strategies based on institutional context and learner analytics. By establishing computational links between micro-level classroom decisions and macro-level educational outcomes, this work aims to advance discipline-specific teacher development while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for educational data stewardship. The resource-intensive simulations and large-language model fine-tuning required for this research necessitate GPU-accelerated computing clusters capable of sustained throughput for complex ensemble modeling tasks.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dynamic, multimodal information systems in healthcare necessitates novel approaches to optimize data integration and decision-making processes. This project addresses the challenge of modeling and simulating large-scale, heterogeneous clinical data flows to improve the responsiveness and accuracy of real-time clinical decision support systems (CDSS). Current systems struggle with latency and fragmentation due to siloed electronic medical records (EMRs), wearable device streams, and imaging databases, leading to suboptimal patient outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate information pathways across distributed healthcare networks, incorporating temporal, spatial, and semantic variability in data exchange. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling of institutional data-sharing behaviors with graph-theoretic analysis of information flow bottlenecks. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess millions of potential routing configurations under diverse clinical scenarios, while machine learning models—trained on synthetic and de-identified patient data—will predict optimal data aggregation strategies. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration over hyperparameters governing network topology, privacy constraints, and emergency prioritization protocols. Expected outcomes include a scalable informatics architecture that reduces CDSS latency by 40–60% in simulated trauma care workflows and identifies critical interoperability gaps in multi-hospital systems. This work will provide a foundation for designing adaptive, context-aware healthcare information systems that balance speed, accuracy, and regulatory requirements. The computational tools developed will be generalized to other high-stakes domains requiring real-time integration of distributed, sensitive data streams, such as disaster response coordination or precision public health initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract:
This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational tools for analyzing art-based therapeutic interventions, a critical step in bridging gaps between pre-professional training and clinical art therapy practice. Art therapy relies on subjective interpretation of visual artifacts to assess emotional, cognitive, and psychological states, but current methods lack scalable, data-driven frameworks to quantify patterns in creative expression. To address this, we propose a computational study using machine learning (ML) and image analysis techniques to identify biomarkers in artwork correlated with mental health indicators. The research problem centers on the need for objective, reproducible metrics to evaluate therapeutic progress in art-based interventions, which could enhance training for pre-art therapy students and inform clinical best practices.  

The project will employ convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze a curated dataset of digital artwork created by participants in structured art therapy sessions, paired with anonymized psychological assessments. HPC resources will enable large-scale processing of high-resolution images, extraction of visual features (e.g., color distribution, brushstroke intensity, spatial composition), and training of ML models to detect associations between these features and diagnostic labels. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will also model the physical process of art creation (e.g., paint flow, material interactions) to explore how sensory experiences during art-making influence therapeutic outcomes.  

Expected outcomes include a validated framework for quantifying therapeutic art attributes and open-source tools to assist pre-professionals in interpreting art-based interventions. By integrating computational rigor with art therapy principles, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven pedagogical resources, ultimately improving readiness for advanced clinical training. The requested HPC allocation is essential to handle the project’s data volume (~10 TB of image/video data) and computational demands, including parallelized model training and real-time simulation of art-creation dynamics. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary journals and collaborations with art therapy accreditation bodies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of quantum-enhanced acoustic metamaterials (QEAMs) for next-generation vibration isolation systems, an emerging niche at the intersection of quantum engineering, nanomechanics, and wave dynamics. Traditional acoustic metamaterials face limitations in adaptive tuning and energy dissipation under dynamic multiscale loads. By integrating quantum-engineered nanostructures—such as phononic crystals with embedded superconducting qubits—into macroscopic metamaterial frameworks, we aim to create systems capable of real-time, self-adjusting vibrational control via quantum-acoustic interactions. The central research problem lies in modeling the nonlinear coupling between quantum degrees of freedom and macroscopic mechanical resonances, a multiscale challenge requiring high-fidelity simulations of hybrid quantum-classical dynamics. The computational approach combines density functional theory (DFT) for quantum subsystem characterization, finite element modeling (FEM) for mesoscale phonon transport, and tensor network algorithms for simulating entanglement dynamics across scales. These methods will be implemented through custom MPI-accelerated workflows on GPU clusters to handle the exponential scaling of quantum state spaces alongside large structural domains. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of quantum-enhanced damping mechanisms, (2) optimized QEAM architectures for ultra-low-frequency vibration suppression (<10 Hz), and (3) open-source tools for hybrid quantum-mechanical co-design. Success will enable breakthrough applications in precision instrumentation (e.g., gravitational wave detectors) and adaptive infrastructure, while establishing computational frameworks for engineering quantum-coherent macroscopic systems. The project directly addresses NSF’s priority area of "Quantum Leap" by translating quantum phenomena into functional engineering solutions, operating outside classical disciplinary boundaries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of regional oral traditions and their influence on contemporary Canadian literary forms. Despite the centrality of oral narratives—including Indigenous storytelling, maritime folklore, and immigrant cultural memory—to Canada’s literary identity, their structural and thematic relationships to written works remain understudied at scale. Current scholarship relies on manual close reading or small-sample computational analyses, limiting systematic comparisons across time, genre, and geography. To address this gap, we propose a computational literary studies approach using natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based network modeling to map intertextual connections between transcribed oral histories (e.g., archival recordings, community compilations) and published Canadian literature from the 19th century to the present. The project will process a multilingual corpus of 50,000+ texts, including rare francophone and Indigenous language materials digitized through partner archives. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models to identify stylistic and thematic patterns in low-resource languages, as well as for constructing large-scale citation networks that trace motifs across oral and written traditions. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a public dataset linking oral and literary works through shared narrative structures, 2) computational models adaptable to underrepresented Canadian dialects, and 3) new frameworks for analyzing how regional orality shapes national literary aesthetics. By enabling the first large-data study of Canada’s oral-written continuum, this work will redefine scholarly understandings of authorship, genre, and cultural transmission in Canadian literature while establishing scalable methods for interdisciplinary humanities computing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and optimize multimodal corporate communication strategies in dynamic, globalized environments. While corporate communications play a critical role in organizational success, existing frameworks often fail to account for the real-time interplay between linguistic patterns, visual media, cultural variables, and stakeholder network dynamics. The computational complexity of modeling these interdependent factors at scale—particularly across multilingual datasets and evolving digital platforms—exceeds the capacity of conventional analytical tools. This project proposes the development of an adaptive neural architecture combining transformer-based language models, computer vision algorithms, and graph neural networks to simulate communication impact across heterogeneous stakeholder ecosystems. The computational workflow will process terabyte-scale datasets comprising internal memos, social media interactions, crisis response transcripts, and visual branding materials, while incorporating real-time cultural sentiment metrics and geopolitical event data. Key challenges include implementing attention mechanisms that weight communication elements across modalities, optimizing distributed training for temporal network embeddings, and validating model outputs against organizational performance metrics. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting communication cascade effects, identifying latent cultural biases in content dissemination, and generating adaptive messaging recommendations during crisis scenarios. By enabling granular analysis of communication efficacy across spatial, temporal, and cultural dimensions, this research aims to establish computational benchmarks for strategic corporate communications while addressing critical gaps in scalability and predictive accuracy. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive multimodal fusion tasks, parallelized hyperparameter optimization across communication scenarios, and large-scale simulations of stakeholder network evolution. Results will provide actionable insights for optimizing global communication pipelines while advancing methodological integration between computational linguistics, organizational behavior, and decision science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has transformative potential for rapid prototyping and customized production, but current methods for selecting process parameters rely heavily on empirical trial-and-error, leading to material inefficiencies and suboptimal mechanical properties. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multiphysics interactions during AM processes and predict optimal printing parameters for diverse materials and geometries. The research will employ coupled finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics models to resolve thermal gradients, residual stresses, and microstructure evolution at high spatial and temporal resolutions. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to correlate simulated behaviors with experimental defect data, enabling adaptive parameter optimization. By utilizing HPC resources, the team will scale simulations across thousands of core-hours to capture complex interactions in industrial-scale components, validated through synchronized physical experiments. The anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for AM parameter prediction, reducing material waste by an estimated 30–50% in pilot studies, and enhancing mechanical performance through microstructure control. This work addresses a critical bottleneck in AM adoption by providing a systematic, computationally driven approach to process design, with broad implications for manufacturing sectors reliant on high-precision, low-waste production methodologies. The requested computing resources will enable the high-fidelity modeling required to bridge the gap between laboratory-scale AM research and industrial implementation, directly advancing engineering technologies in scalable digital manufacturing.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering technologies and engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized learning pathways for students with intellectual disabilities enrolled in Comprehensive Transition and Postsecondary (CTP) programs. Despite the growing emphasis on inclusive education, there remains a critical gap in data-driven tools that dynamically integrate academic, social, and vocational progress to support personalized interventions. The research problem centers on the complexity of synthesizing heterogeneous data—such as skill acquisition rates, behavioral interactions, employment training outcomes, and longitudinal well-being metrics—into actionable insights for educators and program coordinators. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale agent-based simulations and machine learning models. These computational methods will simulate student trajectories under varying program configurations, identify predictors of successful transition to employment, and optimize resource allocation for skill-building activities. The agent-based models will incorporate anonymized student data, including academic performance, social engagement logs, and workplace training evaluations, to replicate the multifaceted interactions within CTP ecosystems. Concurrently, neural networks will analyze unstructured data (e.g., mentorship notes, self-assessment journals) to detect patterns in self-advocacy development and barriers to independent living. The computational intensity of processing multimodal datasets—spanning terabyte-scale records from 15+ partner institutions—necessitates parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated training pipelines. Expected outcomes include a predictive dashboard for educators to tailor support strategies, evidence-based recommendations for program design, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit to model the long-term impacts of policy changes on employment equity. By bridging computational science and inclusive education research, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for enhancing CTP efficacy while advancing interdisciplinary discourse on equitable resource distribution in postsecondary transitions.
cip_definition: A comprehensive transition and postsecondary (CTP) program that provides students with intellectual disabilities with academic enrichment, socialization, independent living skills, self-advocacy skills, and integrated work experiences and career skills that lead to gainful employment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to identify college students at risk of academic disengagement or mental health crises by analyzing multimodal datasets from counseling services, academic records, and anonymized student interaction logs.
