Despite growing demands on student support systems, current approaches often rely on self-referrals or late-stage interventions, leaving gaps in proactive care. The research will integrate structured data (e.g., GPA trends, service utilization) with unstructured data from counseling session transcripts and advising notes using natural language processing (NLP) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process these large-scale datasets (anticipated at 50+ TB), train deep learning models for longitudinal risk prediction, and simulate intervention outcomes across diverse student subpopulations. Computational workflows will employ transformer-based architectures for text analysis, graph neural networks to model social support networks, and ensemble methods to account for temporal academic patterns. The project will validate models against historical student outcomes from three partner institutions, ensuring generalizability through federated learning approaches. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for higher education institutions to prioritize counseling outreach, optimize resource allocation, and personalize support strategies. By enabling real-time analysis of complex student data, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in student affairs, reduce equity gaps in service access, and establish computational social science methodologies within college counseling research. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and secure data processing compliant with FERPA regulations.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to address persistent inefficiencies in multi-stage manufacturing systems by developing a scalable computational framework to optimize process parameters, resource allocation, and quality control in complex production environments. Traditional trial-and-error approaches for balancing throughput, energy consumption, and defect rates struggle to account for dynamic interactions between machining operations, material variability, and automated quality inspection systems. We propose a hybrid simulation-optimization methodology leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model discrete manufacturing processes at unprecedented resolution. The computational approach integrates three components: 1) finite element analysis (FEA) of cutting tool performance under variable workpiece conditions, 2) agent-based modeling of production line dynamics, and 3) machine learning-driven predictive quality control using synthetic image datasets of manufactured components. By parallelizing these typically sequential analyses, we aim to reduce simulation wall times from weeks to hours while maintaining micron-scale spatial resolution critical for precision manufacturing applications. The HPC environment will enable sensitivity analyses across 10^4 parameter combinations to identify robust operating windows for composite material machining processes. Expected outcomes include validated digital twin prototypes for CNC machining cells, predictive maintenance algorithms for tool wear compensation, and open-source process optimization templates compatible with industrial PLC systems. This work directly supports workforce development in advanced manufacturing by generating case studies for computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) instruction while providing scalable computational tools for small-to-medium enterprises adopting Industry 4.0 technologies. The requested resources will accelerate parameter optimization cycles critical for emerging applications in automotive lightweighting and medical device manufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the identification and resolution of production problems in the manufacture of products. Includes instruction in machine operations, production line operations, engineering analysis, systems analysis, instrumentation, physical controls, automation, computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), manufacturing planning, quality control, and informational infrastructure.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling and simulation techniques for optimizing sustainable material design and fabrication processes in leatherworking and upholstery. Traditional methods in these fields rely heavily on trial-and-error experimentation, which is time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in addressing modern challenges such as material sustainability, structural durability, and ergonomic design. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a multiscale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model the behavior of leather and synthetic upholstery materials under diverse environmental and mechanical conditions. The MD simulations will focus on microstructural interactions within collagen fibers and synthetic polymer matrices to predict tensile strength, moisture resistance, and degradation patterns. Concurrently, FEA will simulate macroscopic stress distributions in upholstery designs to optimize load-bearing performance and ergonomic comfort. ML algorithms will iteratively refine material parameters and fabrication workflows based on simulation outputs, reducing waste and energy consumption. The computational intensity of these methods—particularly the parallel processing demands of MD and FEA—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for scalability and efficiency. Expected outcomes include predictive models for sustainable material blends, data-driven guidelines for eco-friendly fabrication, and open-source simulation tools tailored for leatherworking applications. By bridging computational science with traditional craft, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for precision and sustainability in the field, with potential cross-disciplinary impacts in bio-material engineering and circular manufacturing.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in leatherworking and upholstering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding population dynamics under rapidly evolving environmental, social, and public health stressors. Traditional demographic models often struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between migration, fertility, mortality, and spatial redistribution, particularly when incorporating high-dimensional data from satellite imagery, mobile device tracking, and longitudinal surveys. The research will develop and validate a scalable computational framework to simulate population responses to multi-scale shocks, such as climate-induced displacement, pandemic recovery disparities, and urbanization pressures. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with Bayesian hierarchical models, the project will simulate individual and household decision-making processes across diverse geographic and socioeconomic contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of iteratively parameterizing millions of agents, processing petabyte-scale geospatial inputs, and running ensemble projections under uncertainty. Parallelized algorithms will optimize spatial microsimulations across GPU clusters, while machine learning pipelines will identify latent patterns in heterogeneous demographic datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible library of modular code for demographic ABMs, (2) high-resolution projections of migration corridors under climate scenarios for vulnerable regions, and (3) probabilistic estimates of policy impacts on fertility transitions. By enabling real-time assimilation of emerging data streams—such as crisis-driven migration flows—the framework will advance capacity for adaptive policy planning. The requested resources will support comparative analyses across 15+ countries, leveraging census microdata and Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) harmonized over three decades. Validation against historical counterfactuals will quantify model robustness. This work directly addresses methodological limitations in current population projections by formalizing complex feedback between individual behaviors and structural constraints, with particular attention to gender disparities in migration accessibility. The computational tools developed will provide foundational infrastructure for the demography community to explore "what-if" scenarios through accessible, replicable workflows.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of population models and population phenomena, and related problems of social structure and behavior. Includes instruction in population growth, spatial distribution, mortality and fertility factors, migration, dynamic population modeling, population estimation and projection, mathematical and statistical analysis of population data, population policy studies, and applications to problems in economics and government planning.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance pedagogical strategies in vocational sales and marketing operations education by developing a simulation-based training platform for teacher candidates. A critical challenge in preparing educators for marketing and distribution programs is the limited access to scalable, dynamic tools that replicate real-world market complexities. Current methods often rely on static case studies or theoretical models, which fail to capture the adaptive decision-making required in evolving markets. To address this gap, we propose the creation of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation environment that models multi-stakeholder market interactions, consumer behavior trends, and supply chain dynamics. The computational demands of this project necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support three core components: 1) large-scale parallelized simulations of market scenarios with thousands of interacting agents, 2) machine learning-driven analysis of historical sales data to generate realistic training datasets, and 3) real-time visualization of emergent market patterns for pedagogical reflection. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing, we will train deep reinforcement learning models to simulate adaptive consumer and competitor behaviors, enabling teacher candidates to practice instructional strategies in responsive virtual environments. The expected outcomes include a modular simulation toolkit aligned with industry-recognized marketing frameworks (e.g., STP, 4Ps) and evidence-based metrics for assessing teaching effectiveness in scenario-based learning. This resource will directly support 120+ annual teacher candidates in the program while generating anonymized interaction data for refining simulation fidelity. The project advances vocational teacher education by bridging computational social science with pedagogical design, ultimately preparing instructors to cultivate data-driven decision-making skills in marketing students. Successful implementation will establish a replicable model for integrating HPC resources into competency-based teacher training programs.
cip_title: Sales and Marketing Operations/ Marketing and Distribution Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational sales and marketing operations/marketing and distributive education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the challenge of scalable statistical inference for high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets, which are increasingly common in fields such as epidemiology, environmental monitoring, and genomics. Traditional methods for Bayesian hierarchical modeling and nonparametric regression struggle with computational inefficiency when applied to modern large-scale data, limiting their utility in real-world applications. This project seeks to develop and validate novel computational algorithms that leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these limitations. Specifically, we aim to implement parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers optimized for distributed memory architectures, alongside GPU-accelerated variational inference techniques for spatial-temporal models. These approaches will be tested on multi-terabyte datasets comprising climate sensor records and genomic sequences, where dimensionality and complex dependency structures necessitate efficient memory management and rapid iteration. The computational workflow will require access to HPC clusters with multi-core nodes, high-bandwidth interconnects, and GPU arrays to enable simultaneous chain execution, large-scale matrix operations, and real-time convergence diagnostics. Anticipated outcomes include (1) open-source software packages for scalable Bayesian inference, (2) methodological advances in uncertainty quantification for high-dimensional parameter spaces, and (3) applied insights into climate pattern dynamics and genetic association studies. By reducing runtime for complex models from weeks to days, this work will democratize access to cutting-edge statistical tools for researchers lacking specialized computing infrastructure. The requested resources—250,000 CPU core-hours, 50,000 GPU hours, and 50 TB of temporary storage—are essential for benchmarking against existing methods and ensuring statistical validity through exhaustive sensitivity analyses. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journals and integrated into graduate-level computational statistics curricula, bridging gaps between theoretical methodology and practical implementation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Musculoskeletal rehabilitation protocols often lack personalization due to the complex interplay of biomechanical, physiological, and clinical factors influencing recovery outcomes. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model patient-specific responses to physical therapy interventions, with the goal of optimizing treatment plans for individuals recovering from orthopedic injuries or surgeries. The research problem centers on the high variability in patient recovery trajectories, which current generalized protocols fail to address efficiently, potentially prolonging rehabilitation timelines or increasing reinjury risks. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multiscale biomechanical simulations integrating individualized anatomical data, tissue healing dynamics, and movement biomechanics. Patient-specific models will be constructed from clinical imaging (MRI/CT), motion capture data, and electronic health records using finite element analysis and musculoskeletal modeling tools. Machine learning algorithms will then predict optimal intervention parameters by analyzing simulated outcomes across thousands of virtual treatment scenarios. Computational demands are substantial due to the need for parallel processing of high-resolution anatomical datasets, real-time optimization of multiparameter rehabilitation variables, and sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform capable of recommending personalized exercise regimens, load progression schedules, and mobility targets. This work aims to advance precision rehabilitation science by bridging computational modeling with clinical decision-making, potentially reducing trial-and-error approaches in physical therapy practice. The requested HPC resources will enable the scaling of simulations to diverse patient populations, accelerating the translation of insights into clinical guidelines. Successful implementation could inform new standards for adaptive rehabilitation protocols in pre-physical therapy education and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in physical therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, data-driven simulation platform to enhance training and operational decision-making for commercial vehicle operators and instructors. The core research problem lies in the limitations of traditional training methods, which often lack scalable, adaptive scenarios to address diverse real-world challenges—such as dynamic traffic conditions, cargo-loading efficiency, and emergency response protocols. Additionally, the growing volume of telematics data from modern commercial vehicles remains underutilized in refining instructional strategies or optimizing fleet operations. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a computational framework integrating real-time vehicle dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven scenario generation, and large-scale logistics optimization. The platform will simulate complex driving environments—including variable weather, mechanical failures, and cargo configurations—using physics-based models accelerated via parallel computing. ML algorithms will analyze historical driver performance and telemetry data to generate personalized training modules, while optimization routines will model efficient routing and load distribution across fleets. By deploying these computationally intensive tasks on HPC infrastructure, we aim to achieve real-time interactivity for trainees and instructors, as well as rapid analysis of fleet-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation tool for adaptive skill development, predictive models for identifying high-risk operational patterns, and open-source optimization algorithms for freight logistics. This work will directly support safer, more efficient training protocols and operational standards in the commercial transportation sector, bridging gaps between theoretical instruction and practical, data-informed decision-making. The scalability of the platform, enabled by HPC, will allow future expansion to emerging technologies such as autonomous freight systems and electric vehicle fleet management.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: The increasing complexity of interior design challenges—such as optimizing spatial functionality, material sustainability, and human-centered experiential quality—demands advanced computational tools to bridge creativity and technical precision. This project seeks to develop a scalable, AI-driven framework for simulating and evaluating dynamic interior environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address limitations in traditional design workflows. Current methods for modeling lighting, acoustics, and ergonomic flow rely on simplified approximations or compartmentalized analyses, which fail to capture the interdependent variables inherent in real-world spaces. By integrating parametric design algorithms, finite element analysis (FEA), and generative adversarial networks (GANs), this research will enable real-time, multi-physics simulations of interior spaces under diverse operational scenarios (e.g., fluctuating occupancy, adaptive lighting, or material wear). The computational pipeline will process high-resolution 3D scans, environmental sensor data, and user behavior datasets to iteratively refine design solutions that balance aesthetic intent, structural efficiency, and occupant well-being. Key objectives include automating compliance checks against building codes, predicting long-term material performance under stress, and generating data-driven alternatives for sustainable furnishings. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing GPU-accelerated rendering, training deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, and running parallelized optimization loops for complex spatial configurations. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for interior designers, validated through case studies in healthcare and educational facilities. This work will advance the field by establishing a methodological bridge between visual creativity and quantitative analysis, fostering evidence-based design practices while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. By addressing scalability challenges in simulating heterogeneous design variables, the project aims to set new benchmarks for computational efficiency and ecological responsibility in the built environment.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional planning, designing, equipping, and furnishing of residential and commercial interior spaces. Includes instruction in computer applications, drafting, and graphic techniques; principles of interior lighting, acoustics, systems integration, and color coordination; furniture and furnishings; textiles and their finishing; the history of interior design and period styles; basic structural design; building codes and inspection regulations; and applications to office, hotel, factory, restaurant and housing design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized intervention frameworks for motor speech disorders, specifically dysarthria, through multimodal data integration and computational modeling. Dysarthria, a neurological speech impairment affecting articulation, prosody, and intelligibility, presents significant heterogeneity across individuals due to varying etiologies (e.g., stroke, Parkinson’s disease, cerebral palsy). Current clinical assessment tools rely heavily on subjective perceptual analysis, limiting the granularity of treatment customization. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline combining high-resolution acoustic signal processing, articulatory kinematic data, and patient-specific biomechanical modeling. The research problem centers on resolving the computational bottlenecks in analyzing large-scale, temporally dense datasets (electromagnetic articulography, vocal tract MRI, and speech audio) while simulating vocal tract dynamics under differing neuromuscular conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, training of deep neural networks for pattern recognition in disordered speech, and finite element modeling of vocal tract structures to predict optimal therapeutic targets. Methods include the deployment of convolutional-recurrent hybrid architectures for acoustic-articulatory feature mapping, GPU-accelerated biomechanical simulations, and federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy in multi-institutional data collaborations. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform for clinicians to generate patient-specific motor speech profiles, predict treatment response trajectories, and optimize intervention parameters. This work bridges computational neurology, biomechanics, and clinical speech-language pathology, offering a novel paradigm for precision rehabilitation. The scalability of the proposed models will also provide a foundation for future research into real-time adaptive therapies using wearable sensor technologies, directly supporting the evolving role of Speech-Language Pathology Assistants in data-driven clinical and research settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community psychology research focused on modeling systemic inequities and optimizing community-based intervention strategies. Social problems such as disparities in mental health access, cultural stressors in marginalized populations, and fragmented social service systems are inherently complex, involving dynamic interactions between individuals, institutions, and environments. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to account for these multi-level, nonlinear relationships, limiting the scalability and precision of interventions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), network analysis, and machine learning to simulate community ecosystems and evaluate intervention scenarios. The ABM component will simulate individual and organizational behaviors within spatially defined communities, parameterized using demographic data, social determinant of health metrics, and existing survey data on service utilization. Network analysis will map resource allocation patterns and service accessibility gaps across community systems, while machine learning techniques will identify predictive markers of intervention efficacy from longitudinal datasets. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of these parallelized simulations, which require iterative parameter tuning across thousands of scenarios to model diverse community contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of leverage points for improving mental health equity in under-resourced communities, (2) predictive models to prioritize intervention strategies based on localized social ecologies, and (3) open-source tools for simulating community-specific social change dynamics. By enabling large-scale, data-driven exploration of systemic interventions, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in community psychology while contributing methodological innovations for computational social science. Results will inform resource allocation policies, preventive care frameworks, and cross-sector partnerships aimed at reducing cultural stress and fostering equitable social change.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply psychological principles to the analysis of social problems, and the implementation of intervention strategies for addressing these problems. Includes instruction in social ecology, primary and secondary prevention of social pathologies, social intervention strategies and tactics, large group counseling, social services systems behavior, creating settings, cultural stress, and the dynamics of social change.

abstract: Occupational exposure to hazardous substances and unsafe work practices remains a critical public health challenge, with existing risk assessment frameworks often limited by sparse data and simplistic modeling approaches. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational platform to model complex occupational exposure scenarios, integrate multi-source sensor data, and predict health risks in dynamic industrial environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate interactions between workers, equipment, and environmental hazards (e.g., airborne particulates, chemical leaks, ergonomic stressors) across diverse industries. The computational framework will ingest real-time sensor data from wearable devices, industrial IoT systems, and environmental monitors to parameterize exposure gradients and workplace behaviors. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in dose-response relationships, while graph neural networks will identify latent patterns in large-scale occupational injury datasets. Key challenges include scaling mechanistic toxicokinetic models across heterogeneous worker populations and optimizing computational fluid dynamics simulations for aerosol dispersion in complex workspaces. Expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for high-exposure scenarios, AI-driven recommendations for adaptive safety interventions, and open-source tools for probabilistic exposure assessment. This work will directly address gaps in current industrial hygiene practices by enabling data-driven, scenario-specific hazard mitigation strategies while advancing computational methodologies for occupational health research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive simulations, training deep learning models on multi-terabyte datasets, and maintaining computational fidelity across spatial-temporal scales relevant to workplace exposure dynamics. Project results will inform regulatory decision-making, safety protocol optimization, and targeted worker health monitoring systems, ultimately contributing to reduced occupational morbidity in high-risk industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares public health specialists to monitor and evaluate health and related safety standards in industrial, commercial, and government workplaces and facilities. Includes instruction in occupational health and safety standards and regulations; health-related aspects of various occupations and work environments; health hazard testing and evaluation; test equipment operation and maintenance; industrial toxicology; worker health and safety education; and the analysis and testing of job-related equipment, behavior practices, and protective devices and procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized musculoskeletal biomechanics models for optimizing prehabilitation strategies in individuals transitioning from injury recovery to physical therapy. Current prehabilitation protocols often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for individual variability in tissue healing rates, neuromuscular adaptation, and biomechanical load distribution. This limitation contributes to suboptimal outcomes, including prolonged recovery times or secondary injuries. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific imaging data, dynamic motion capture, and finite element modeling (FEM) to simulate tissue stress patterns during prehabilitation exercises. The project will utilize machine learning algorithms to analyze multimodal datasets—including MRI-derived musculoskeletal geometries, electromyography (EMG) signals, and kinetic measurements—to predict individualized load thresholds and movement modifications. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution 3D biomechanical models, running Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in tissue response predictions, and training neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for clinicians to design adaptive prehabilitation regimens, reducing the risk of overloading healing tissues while promoting functional recovery. By bridging computational biomechanics and clinical decision-making, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for precision prehabilitation, directly supporting the transition from injury management to evidence-based physical therapy readiness. The scalability of the framework will enable future extensions to diverse patient populations, including those with complex comorbidities affecting musculoskeletal health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in physical therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize personalized motor rehabilitation protocols by integrating biomechanical modeling, wearable sensor data, and machine learning to address variability in patient recovery trajectories. Traditional rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized exercise regimens, which fail to account for individual differences in biomechanics, neuromuscular adaptation, and real-time physiological feedback. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that dynamically adjusts task difficulty and therapeutic targets for patients recovering from musculoskeletal injuries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of high-resolution motion capture data, electromyography signals, and inertial measurement unit outputs from wearable sensors during rehabilitation sessions. These datasets will train physics-informed neural networks to simulate patient-specific joint kinematics, muscle activation patterns, and fatigue thresholds. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine exercise parameters—such as resistance, range of motion, and repetition frequency—to maximize functional gains while minimizing injury risk. The computational pipeline will be validated against clinical outcomes from a pilot cohort of 30 participants undergoing post-surgical knee rehabilitation. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for adaptive rehabilitation planning, capable of providing real-time decision support to rehabilitation aides during therapeutic interventions. This work will advance precision rehabilitation by translating complex biomechanical data into actionable clinical insights, empowering aides to deliver targeted, evidence-based care. The scalability of the framework will also establish a foundation for future studies exploring its application in neurological and geriatric rehabilitation contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and other therapeutic professionals, and to perform routine functions in support of rehabilitation. Includes instruction in roles and responsibilities of rehabilitation providers, basic function of the human body, disabling conditions, therapeutic skills, client management, and communication skills.

abstract: The increasing complexity of personalized nutrition interventions necessitates advanced computational tools to model dynamic interactions between dietary components, metabolic pathways, and patient-specific factors. Current clinical nutrition practices often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual variability in nutrient absorption, genetic predispositions, or comorbidities. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate and optimize personalized nutrition plans for patients with chronic metabolic disorders, such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease. The research will integrate multi-omic data (genomic, metabolomic, and microbiome profiles) with real-time dietary intake logs and electronic health records to predict patient-specific responses to nutritional interventions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these heterogeneous datasets to identify biomarkers of nutrient efficacy and toxicity, while mechanistic models of nutrient metabolism will simulate tissue-specific metabolic fluxes under varying dietary conditions. The computational workflow will require large-scale parallelization to handle high-dimensional data and iterative optimization of diet plans across diverse patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for designing precision nutrition regimens, validated through retrospective analysis of clinical trial data and prospective pilot studies. This resource will enable nutritionists to dynamically adjust macronutrient ratios, micronutrient supplementation, and meal timing based on individualized metabolic thresholds, thereby improving therapeutic outcomes. The project also aims to generate open-access tools for diet-disease interaction modeling, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational domains. By leveraging HPC resources, this work addresses a critical need for data-driven approaches in clinical nutrition, with potential applications in hospital food service optimization, telehealth nutrition counseling, and public health policy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of dietetics and the biomedical and nutrition sciences to design and manage effective nutrition programs as part of clinical treatment and therapy programs, and to manage health care facility food services. Includes instruction in human nutrition, nutrient metabolism, the role of foods and nutrition in health promotion and disease prevention, nutrition as a treatment regime, planning and directing hospital food service programs, diet and nutrition analysis and planning, supervision of food storage and preparation, special diets, client education, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: Chromosomal structural variants (SVs) are implicated in numerous genetic disorders, cancers, and transplant rejection risks, yet their detection and interpretation remain challenging in clinical cytogenetics. Current diagnostic workflows rely on labor-intensive techniques like karyotyping and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), which lack resolution for sub-microscopic variants or complex rearrangements. Optical genome mapping (OGM), an emerging high-resolution cytogenetic technology, generates terabyte-scale genomic imaging datasets but lacks standardized computational pipelines for automated SV detection and clinical annotation. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled machine learning framework to classify pathogenic SVs from OGM data, addressing critical bottlenecks in scalability and diagnostic accuracy. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated image processing to analyze raw molecule maps, followed by distributed computing workflows to align data to reference genomes, detect breakpoints, and integrate multi-omics evidence (e.g., epigenetic signatures, gene expression). A convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on a curated dataset of clinical OGM results paired with patient outcomes to prioritize variants of uncertain significance. The computational framework will incorporate population genomics databases and mechanistic models of genomic instability to predict variant pathogenicity. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce analysis times from days to hours while improving sensitivity for complex SVs below 10 kbp. Expected outcomes include an open-source analysis toolkit validated against gold-standard cytogenetic methods, a reference database of clinically annotated SVs, and novel biomarkers for leukemia relapse risk prediction. This work bridges gaps between computational genomics and clinical diagnostics, enabling rapid, high-resolution genome analysis for precision medicine applications. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing data-intensive OGM processing, optimizing deep learning architectures, and scaling validation across thousands of clinical samples.
cip_title: Cytogenetics/ Genetics/ Clinical Genetics Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform analyses of the human genome and chromosomes for the research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes instruction in chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms that underpin complex cognitive processes, such as working memory and decision-making, requires analyzing large-scale brain networks with high spatiotemporal resolution. Current limitations in computational power restrict the ability to model dynamic interactions across distributed neural systems or integrate multimodal neuroimaging data (e.g., fMRI, EEG) at the scale necessary to capture population-level activity. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational neuroscience framework that bridges neural dynamics with cognitive function. The research will employ whole-brain biophysical models to simulate resting-state and task-evoked activity, informed by subject-specific structural connectivity derived from diffusion tensor imaging. These simulations will be optimized using Bayesian inference to fit empirical fMRI and electrophysiological datasets, enabling the exploration of parameter spaces governing excitatory-inhibitory balance and long-range coupling. Concurrently, machine learning pipelines will be developed to decode cognitive states from high-density EEG recordings, leveraging HPC capabilities for feature extraction and real-time pattern classification. The integration of modeling and empirical data aims to identify critical network hubs and oscillatory mechanisms that sustain cognitive operations. Expected outcomes include predictive models of cognitive load in healthy aging and mechanistic insights into network destabilization in conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease. By enabling the analysis of terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, this project will establish an open-access resource for testing hypotheses about large-scale brain organization. The results will advance foundational knowledge in cognitive neuroscience and provide a computational toolkit for translating basic research into clinical biomarkers of neurocognitive health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the neural mechanisms underlying cognition.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of how biomechanical and optical aberrations in corneal and lenticular tissues contribute to visual dysfunction in aging and disease. A critical gap persists in modeling the multiscale interactions between tissue microstructure, light scattering, and neural processing, particularly under dynamic conditions such as accommodation or ocular surface trauma. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element modeling of ocular biomechanics with Monte Carlo simulations of light propagation through anatomically accurate, patient-derived ocular geometries. High-resolution optical coherence tomography and aberrometry data from clinical cohorts will inform spatially resolved material properties and boundary conditions. The computational pipeline will simulate how microstructural changes (e.g., collagen fibril disorganization in keratoconus, lenticular protein aggregation in cataracts) alter intraocular light scatter and retinal image quality. Machine learning surrogates will then map these physical outputs to perceptual outcomes using psychophysical datasets of contrast sensitivity and glare disability. By leveraging GPU-accelerated parallelization, we aim to establish the first coupled biomechanical-optical-neural model capable of resolving subcellular structural perturbations to functional vision loss. This resource-intensive approach is necessary to capture nonlinear interactions across spatial scales (nanometers to centimeters) and temporal domains (milliseconds to decades). Anticipated outcomes include predictive biomarkers for early-stage ocular pathology, quantitative frameworks for personalized refractive surgery planning, and mechanistic insights into environmental impacts on age-related vision decline. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter space exploration at clinically relevant resolutions, overcoming current limitations in single-scale modeling that hinder translational applications. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for vision science and clinical ophthalmology communities.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of vision, visual processes, and related phenomena and clinical research and treatment modalities. Includes instruction in ocular anatomy and physiology, microbiology of the eye, electrophysiology, neurophysiology, corneal physiology, photochemistry, psychophysics, visual biophysics and motor systems, sensory mechanisms and photoreception, eye circulation and metabolism, geometric and physical optics, ocular development across the life span, visual stimuli and perception, color vision, eye motility, biometrics and measurement techniques, visual pathology, and environmental issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and mitigating privacy breaches in large-scale healthcare data ecosystems. As healthcare organizations increasingly adopt distributed cloud platforms and interoperable systems, the attack surface for sensitive health data expands, creating vulnerabilities that existing threat models and compliance tools often fail to anticipate. The research problem centers on the insufficiency of conventional risk assessment methods to model multi-step adversarial attacks that exploit interactions between legacy systems, third-party applications, and emerging data-sharing architectures. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining graph-based anomaly detection, adversarial machine learning simulations, and cryptographic protocol stress-testing. Computational workflows will model hospital networks as dynamic heterogeneous graphs (5-10 million nodes) to identify latent vulnerabilities in access control hierarchies. Parallel Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic risks of re-identification attacks on partially de-identified datasets under varying compliance regimes. Cryptographic penetration testing will employ GPU-accelerated brute-force and side-channel attacks to evaluate post-quantum encryption candidates for health data at rest. The HPC environment is critical for maintaining requisite scale in simulating hospital network topologies (OpenMPI), training graph neural networks on anonymized insurance claim datasets (200+ TB, PyTorch Distributed), and optimizing lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes (CUDA). Expected outcomes include an open-source risk quantification toolkit that predicts breach likelihoods 12-18 months ahead of current compliance audit cycles, plus evidence-based recommendations for hardening hybrid cloud architectures. By enabling real-world simulation of coordinated cyber-physical attacks on health data infrastructures, this work aims to advance proactive privacy preservation strategies while maintaining computational feasibility for resource-constrained healthcare providers.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain present complex clinical challenges due to the intricate biomechanics of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and heterogeneous patient presentations. Current diagnostic and treatment strategies often rely on generalized approaches, leading to variable outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific computational models to simulate TMJ biomechanics and predict treatment responses for TMD, orofacial pain, and sleep apnea interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to overcome the computational demands of multi-scale modeling, integrating high-resolution diagnostic radiography data, neurobiological pain pathway analyses, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning algorithms. The research will construct anatomically accurate 3D TMJ models derived from clinical CT and MRI scans, incorporating tissue-level mechanical properties, dynamic loading conditions during mandibular movement, and neurobiological pain signaling mechanisms. Concurrently, machine learning frameworks will analyze longitudinal patient datasets to identify biomechanical, phenotypic, and neurophysiological predictors of therapeutic success for intraoral appliances and other interventions. The integration of these computational approaches will enable real-time simulations of treatment scenarios, optimizing device designs and personalized intervention parameters. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for TMD progression and treatment efficacy, quantitative guidelines for customizing oral appliances in obstructive sleep apnea management, and mechanistic insights into biomechanical contributors to chronic orofacial pain. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance precision medicine in TMD care, reducing the trial-and-error paradigm in clinical practice. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources to support broader research collaboration, ultimately improving patient outcomes through data-driven clinical decision-making and enhanced understanding of pain neurobiology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to evaluate, diagnose, and treat of a wide variety of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain disorders as well as the treatment of sleep apnea and snoring with intraoral appliances. Includes instruction in head and neck anatomy, physical diagnosis and evaluation, orofacial pain, neurobiology of pain and analgesia, and diagnostic radiography.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of public resource allocation in multi-level governance systems. A critical challenge in public administration is optimizing limited resources across competing priorities while balancing equity, efficiency, and political feasibility. Traditional analytical tools often oversimplify the interdependencies between policy actors, fiscal constraints, and socioeconomic variables, limiting their predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models that simulate decision-making processes among municipal, state, and federal entities under varying policy scenarios. The models will integrate empirical datasets—including historical budget allocations, demographic trends, and service delivery outcomes—with machine learning techniques to identify patterns in resource prioritization. HPC capabilities are essential for running thousands of parallel simulations that account for nonlinear feedback loops, stochastic variables (e.g., economic shocks), and heterogeneous stakeholder preferences. Key computational tasks include parameter calibration using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, real-time visualization of fiscal trade-offs, and sensitivity analysis of equity-focused allocation rules. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework to evaluate how decentralized decision-making structures affect distributive justice in areas such as emergency response funding and educational infrastructure investment. The results will provide actionable insights for designing adaptive resource allocation mechanisms that align with public administration ethics while maintaining computational reproducibility. By bridging policy informatics with administrative theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based governance in an era of increasing fiscal uncertainty and complex public needs.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Administration and Public Policy and with an emphasis the administration and management of public policies. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; research methods; role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation; and resource allocation.

abstract: The variability in patient responses to pharmacotherapy remains a critical challenge in clinical medicine, often leading to suboptimal therapeutic outcomes and adverse drug reactions. While genomic and proteomic factors are known contributors, their complex interactions with clinical variables are poorly understood, necessitating advanced computational approaches to unravel multifactorial determinants of drug efficacy and toxicity. This project aims to develop a high-dimensional predictive model integrating multi-omics data, electronic health records, and real-world pharmacovigilance datasets to identify patient-specific therapeutic optimization strategies. We propose a two-stage computational framework: first, leveraging machine learning algorithms to map genotype-phenotype associations influencing drug metabolism and target engagement, and second, employing agent-based simulations to model drug behavior across heterogeneous virtual patient populations. The scale of data integration—spanning 50,000+ patient records, 10 million+ pharmacogenomic variants, and longitudinal treatment response metrics—requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized model training, large-scale parameter optimization, and stochastic simulation ensembles. Key computational challenges include managing sparse, high-dimensional datasets, resolving multicollinearity in predictive features, and quantifying uncertainty in rare adverse event predictions. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source tool for precision dosing recommendations in anticoagulant and oncology therapies, (2) quantitative estimates of genetic and non-genetic contributors to interindividual variability for 20 high-risk medications, and (3) simulation-derived thresholds for therapeutic drug monitoring biomarkers. This work will directly address NIH priorities in pharmacogenomics implementation by providing clinically actionable decision support models, while advancing computational methods for therapeutic optimization in polypharmacy populations. Successful execution depends on HPC capacity for sustained memory-intensive workflows (>1 TB RAM/node) and GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pharmacotherapy

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing workforce training interventions in dynamic organizational environments through advanced computational modeling. Traditional approaches to human resources development (HRD) often rely on static, survey-based metrics or qualitative assessments, which struggle to capture the complexity of real-time skill acquisition, team interactions, and evolving workplace demands. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation platform that integrates psychometric data, real-time performance metrics, and organizational network structures to model the cascading effects of training programs on productivity and employee retention. The computational framework will employ agent-based modeling to represent heterogeneous employee behaviors, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate adaptive training pathways under resource constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large-scale datasets from participating organizations—including longitudinal skill assessments, collaboration patterns, and operational KPIs—while running parallel simulations to test intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool capable of identifying optimal training intervals, content personalization strategies, and team restructuring recommendations tailored to rapidly shifting industry needs. This work advances HRD by introducing a systems-level, data-driven methodology that accounts for emergent organizational behaviors, moving beyond traditional one-size-fits-all training paradigms. The resulting models will be validated against case studies from technology-driven sectors facing acute skill obsolescence pressures, with implications for improving ROI on training investments and mitigating turnover in knowledge-intensive industries. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-source modules to enable broader applications in workforce analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply integrated training, organizational development, and career planning and counseling skills to the design, management, and evaluation of programs to improve individual productivity, employability, and job satisfaction and organizational effectiveness. Includes instruction in psychology; organizational behavior; principles of adult education; occupational counseling; skill testing and evaluation; program design; consulting practice; organizational development; and applications to issues such as training, management development, customer service, and total quality management.

abstract: Marriage and family therapy (MFT) research faces challenges in modeling the dynamic, nonlinear interactions within family systems, which traditional statistical methods often oversimplify. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop large-scale computational models that simulate complex family interactions and predict therapeutic intervention outcomes. The research integrates agent-based modeling to represent family members as autonomous agents with distinct behavioral, emotional, and communication profiles, enabling the simulation of thousands of interaction scenarios across diverse demographic and clinical contexts. These simulations will identify critical leverage points for interventions and systemic patterns linked to conditions such as relational distress, intergenerational trauma, and comorbid mental health disorders. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze multimodal datasets—including longitudinal therapy transcripts, biometric data, and clinical outcomes—to detect latent patterns in therapeutic efficacy. Natural language processing (NLP) will be applied to session dialogues to quantify how specific communication strategies influence emotional attunement and conflict resolution. The scale of these analyses—requiring parallelized simulations, real-time NLP of high-dimensional text data, and training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets—necessitates HPC infrastructure for efficient computation and storage. Expected outcomes include predictive models to optimize intervention timing, personalize treatment plans, and forecast systemic risk factors for relapse. By bridging systemic therapy frameworks with computational social science, this work aims to advance evidence-based MFT practices, reduce trial-and-error in clinical decision-making, and establish scalable methods for evaluating family dynamics. The resulting tools could transform training paradigms for therapists and inform policy guidelines for equitable mental health resource distribution, particularly for underserved populations with limited access to long-term care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of marriage and family therapy, involving the diagnosis of cognitive, affective, and behavioral domain disorders, both mental and emotional, within the context of marriage and family systems and the application of short- and long-term therapeutic strategies in family group contexts. Includes instruction in psychotherapy, family systems and studies, small group intervention and therapy, marital problems, depression, identification of psychopathologies and behavioral disorders, holistic health care, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model adversarial decision-making processes in dynamic homeland security threat scenarios, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation for critical infrastructure protection. Existing threat assessment models often lack granularity in simulating adaptive adversaries who adjust strategies based on evolving countermeasures, environmental conditions, or socio-political factors. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based simulation platform integrating game-theoretic principles, behavioral economics, and network vulnerability analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale, parallelized simulations that account for stochastic variables—such as attacker priorities, infrastructure interdependencies, and real-time intelligence updates—across thousands of scenario permutations. The computational architecture will employ reinforcement learning algorithms to model adversary adaptation, coupled with Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in threat pathways. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for high-risk attack vectors, a decision-support tool for prioritizing defensive investments, and policy-relevant insights into the cost-benefit tradeoffs of layered security strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial, cyber-physical, and open-source intelligence—the project aims to advance computational social science methodologies within homeland security applications. The resulting models will be validated against historical incident data and red-team exercises, providing a scalable framework for agencies to stress-test contingency plans against emergent asymmetric threats. This work bridges computational modeling and security policy by offering empirically grounded, dynamic risk assessments that traditional qualitative approaches cannot achieve, ultimately strengthening evidence-based planning for critical infrastructure resilience.
cip_definition: A program focusing on security policy, planning and operations dedicated to the protection of U.S. territory, assets, infrastructure, institutions and citizens from external threats. Includes instruction in national security policy, government relations, intelligence, law enforcement, security technology, communications and information technology, homeland security planning and operations, disaster planning and applications to specific threat scenarios.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory allocation strategies in global consumer markets, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational complexity of modeling real-time consumer decision-making across heterogeneous retail environments. Traditional merchandising models struggle to account for the interplay between cultural preferences, regional economic conditions, and rapidly shifting purchasing behaviors in omnichannel retail ecosystems. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate behavioral data, supply chain variables, and promotional feedback loops at scale—a task requiring iterative, resource-intensive computations. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate millions of consumer agents interacting with adaptive pricing algorithms under diverse market conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of DRL policies across GPU clusters while managing ABM simulations of cross-regional retail networks. Key datasets include multi-terabyte transaction logs from partner retailers, social media sentiment streams, and geo-tagged economic indicators. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of generating region-specific merchandising strategies that balance profitability with inventory sustainability. The project will advance computational retail science by demonstrating how HPC can resolve latency challenges in real-time promotion optimization, particularly for perishable or seasonal goods. Results will be validated against historical sales data from three multinational retailers, with potential to reduce excess inventory costs by 12-18% in pilot markets. This work establishes a methodological bridge between consumer behavior theory and large-scale computational experimentation, offering a template for HPC applications in non-traditional domains requiring rapid, data-driven merchandising adaptations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on product and service promotion from the perspective of individual and family consumers and that prepares individuals to function as consumer management and marketing consultants in for-profit and non-profit enterprises. Includes instruction in applied market research, consumer behavior, product sourcing and distribution, profitability, customer feedback and evaluation methods, promotion and retailing campaign development, and applications to specific domestic and international consumer markets.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in developing advanced autonomous systems capable of real-time decision-making in dynamic, unstructured environments. As mechatronic and robotic systems grow in complexity—integrating multi-sensor fusion, high-dimensional control, and AI-driven perception—the demand for scalable, high-fidelity simulations and optimization frameworks exceeds the capabilities of standard computing infrastructure. The proposed research focuses on optimizing cooperative robotic swarms for industrial automation and disaster response scenarios, where decentralized agents must adapt to rapidly changing conditions while maintaining energy efficiency and task prioritization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the computational approach integrates parallelized physics-based simulations (via Gazebo and ROS 2), Monte Carlo-based robustness testing, and evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective controller optimization. Additionally, real-time neural network training for vision-based terrain classification and path planning will be accelerated using GPU clusters. The project will deploy containerized workflows to manage heterogeneous computational tasks, including finite element analysis for compliant mechanism design and digital twin synchronization. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for fault-tolerant swarm coordination, validated through large-scale parametric studies, and open-source simulation tools tailored for resource-constrained edge robotics. By overcoming latency and scalability barriers, this work will directly support the development of resilient autonomous systems for manufacturing and emergency services, while establishing a benchmark for HPC-driven prototyping in robotics engineering. The requested resources—multi-node CPU clusters with high memory bandwidth and dedicated GPU partitions—are critical to achieving the required iteration speed and model fidelity, enabling rapid transition from simulation to physical prototype testing.
cip_title: Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in the support of engineers to the design, development, and operational evaluation of autonomous, computer-controlled, electro-mechanical systems. Includes instruction in computer and software engineering, control engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the scientific understanding of Ayurvedic pharmacological formulations and their mechanisms of action in chronic disease management. Despite the widespread use of multi-component herbal formulations in Ayurveda, their synergistic biochemical interactions and systemic effects remain poorly characterized due to the complexity of phytochemical diversity, multi-target engagement, and non-linear pharmacokinetics. Traditional in vitro and in vivo methods face limitations in modeling these dynamic processes at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational systems biology approach integrating molecular docking, dynamic simulations, and machine learning to map interactions between Ayurvedic herb-derived compounds and human protein targets implicated in metabolic, inflammatory, and neurodegenerative disorders. Molecular dynamics simulations will model binding affinities and conformational changes in target proteins such as AMPK, NF-κB, and acetylcholinesterase when exposed to prioritized compounds from herbs like Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) and Turmeric (Curcuma longa). Network pharmacology models will identify potential synergistic pathways across formulations described in classical texts like the Charaka Samhita. Concurrently, multi-omics data integration (genomic, metabolomic) from ongoing clinical studies on rheumatoid arthritis and type 2 diabetes patients will be analyzed using HPC-enabled bioinformatics pipelines to correlate computational predictions with therapeutic outcomes. The computational workload requires large-scale parallel processing for ensemble molecular simulations, genomic association mapping, and high-dimensional data integration across 10,000+ phytochemicals and 500+ human targets. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for Ayurvedic formulation efficacy, mechanistic insights into polyherbal synergy, and biomarker discovery for personalized treatment optimization. This work will establish a bridge between Ayurvedic empirical knowledge and modern computational biology, fostering evidence-based integration of traditional medicine into global healthcare paradigms while preserving its philosophical foundations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop computational tools to analyze the efficacy of art therapy interventions for individuals with mental health disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Art therapy relies heavily on qualitative interpretation of visual artifacts (e.g., drawings, paintings) to assess emotional states and therapeutic progress. However, manual analysis of these artifacts is time-intensive and subjective, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and computer vision techniques to quantitatively evaluate artistic elements—such as color use, line intensity, compositional balance, and symbolic content—across large datasets of patient-generated artwork. The project will curate a multimodal dataset comprising digitized art therapy session outputs, anonymized patient metadata, and clinician annotations. Deep learning models (e.g., convolutional neural networks, vision transformers) will be trained to detect patterns correlating artistic features with diagnostic profiles and treatment outcomes. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) methods will analyze session transcripts to cross-reference verbal narratives with visual data. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of image data, the need for parallelized model training across thousands of artworks, and the complexity of multimodal fusion algorithms. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolset for automated art therapy artifact analysis, (2) evidence-based insights into how specific artistic behaviors correlate with symptom alleviation or exacerbation, and (3) a scalable framework for longitudinal tracking of patient progress. This work will enhance clinical decision-making by providing art therapists with data-driven adjuncts to traditional assessments, while advancing computational methods for interdisciplinary mental health research. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in bridging qualitative therapeutic practices with quantitative analytics, fostering personalized, adaptive art therapy interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use drawing and other art media forms to assess, treat, and rehabilitate individuals with mental, emotional, developmental, or physical disorders. Includes instruction in art, history and theory of art therapy, art therapeutic techniques, psychopathology, patient assessment and diagnosis, cultural diversity issues, legal and ethical practice issues, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model biomechanical interactions between implantable neurostimulation devices and dynamic neural tissues, addressing a critical gap in the design of next-generation neuromodulation therapies. Current devices often fail to account for microscale mechanical strain caused by natural tissue movement (e.g., vascular pulsatility, spinal flexion), leading to inflammatory responses or loss of therapeutic efficacy over time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will create multiscale finite element models integrating 1) patient-specific anatomical reconstructions from ultra-high-resolution MRI datasets, 2) dynamic tissue deformation patterns derived from intraoperative motion capture, and 3) material behavior simulations of novel viscoelastic electrode coatings. The computational pipeline will employ coupled fluid-structure interaction solvers to simulate chronic mechanical stress patterns across neural interfaces over simulated 12-month periods. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize device geometries through evolutionary algorithms, balancing mechanical compliance with electrical performance metrics. Successful validation against longitudinal animal model histology data will enable predictive modeling of human-device biocompatibility. This work directly addresses the unmet need for durable bioelectronic therapies in treating drug-resistant neurological disorders, with particular relevance to spinal cord stimulation and deep brain stimulation technologies. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration at clinically relevant timescales, reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping. Outcomes will include an open-source simulation toolkit for neurodevice development and quantitative design guidelines to minimize tissue-device mechanical mismatch, potentially extending functional implant lifetimes by 40-60% compared to current standards.
cip_definition: Any program in medicine, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding plant-pathogen interactions that limit crop resilience, with a focus on molecular mechanisms underlying host resistance and pathogen virulence. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture the dynamic, multi-scale complexity of these interactions, particularly the integration of genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data across plant developmental stages and environmental conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model pathogen effector protein binding dynamics with host receptors, predict virulence adaptation pathways, and identify candidate resistance genes in staple crops. Key methodologies include molecular dynamics simulations of protein-ligand interactions using GPU-accelerated AMBER workflows, machine learning-driven genomic variant analysis via convolutional neural networks trained on pan-genome datasets, and agent-based modeling of pathogen population evolution under selective pressure. These computationally intensive workflows will integrate heterogeneous datasets from CRISPR-edited plant lines, field pathogenomics surveys, and time-resolved metabolomics. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of >50 TB of multi-omics data, parallel execution of 10⁶ simulation replicates, and ensemble modeling across genomic diversity panels. Expected outcomes include predictive models of co-evolutionary trajectories in plant-pathogen systems, validated resistance gene candidates for soybean and wheat, and an open-source computational pipeline for virulence prediction. This work directly addresses urgent agricultural challenges posed by emerging fungal pathogens, with potential to accelerate development of durable crop protection strategies while reducing reliance on chemical controls. By bridging molecular-scale computational biology with applied crop improvement objectives, the project advances precision agriculture capabilities critical for global food security under climate change scenarios.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Animal/ Plant/ Veterinary Science and Related Fields, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural, animal, plant, or veterinary science and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to optimize the impact of teaching assistants (TAs) in diverse educational environments through computational modeling of real-time student-TA interaction patterns. While TAs play a critical role in bridging instructional gaps, their effectiveness is often constrained by heterogeneous student needs, variable TA preparedness, and the dynamic nature of classroom or virtual learning settings.
