Existing frameworks for TA support lack granular, data-driven strategies to adaptively match TA interventions to individual or group learning trajectories. To address this, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that integrates multimodal educational data—including discourse analysis, student performance metrics, and behavioral logs—to model TA decision-making processes and predict optimal support strategies. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom microdynamics with reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms trained on historical interaction datasets. These models will be validated against real-world observations from STEM discussion sections and online learning platforms. The HPC environment is essential for scaling simulations to thousands of parallel scenarios, enabling the analysis of complex variable interactions (e.g., TA pedagogical style, student cognitive load, and problem-solving pacing) that cannot be feasibly tested in physical settings. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to guide TA training programs, a toolkit for dynamically allocating TA resources based on real-time learner needs, and evidence-based insights into how TA-student interaction patterns correlate with conceptual mastery. By leveraging computational power to decode the “black box” of TA efficacy, this research aims to advance personalized educational support in ways that are both scalable and equitable, offering a novel interdisciplinary contribution to the science of learning assistance.
cip_definition: Any teaching assistant/aide program, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying therapeutic massage techniques. Despite the widespread clinical use of massage therapy for pain management, injury recovery, and stress reduction, the field lacks robust quantitative models to predict how specific manual interventions—such as pressure, duration, and directionality—affect tissue dynamics, inflammatory responses, and neural feedback loops. Current experimental methods are limited in spatial and temporal resolution, hindering the ability to optimize protocols for diverse patient populations. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models integrating musculoskeletal anatomy, soft tissue mechanics, and autonomic nervous system responses. These models will simulate the effects of common modalities (e.g., deep tissue massage, myofascial release) using finite element analysis and agent-based modeling frameworks. High-resolution MRI datasets and motion-capture recordings of certified practitioners will parameterize the simulations, while machine learning algorithms will identify patterns linking technique variables to therapeutic outcomes (e.g., reduced muscle stiffness, improved blood flow). HPC resources are critical to handle the computational complexity of modeling nonlinear tissue deformation, real-time feedback between mechanical stimuli and biochemical cascades, and population-scale variability in anatomy or pain thresholds. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to personalize massage protocols for conditions such as chronic low back pain and post-surgical rehabilitation, as well as interactive training modules for students to visualize biomechanical impacts of technique adjustments. By bridging empirical practice with computational innovation, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based standards in massage therapy, enhance clinical training, and inform interdisciplinary collaborations in rehabilitation sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being to clients through the application of manual techniques for manipulating skin, muscles, and connective tissues. Includes instruction in Western (Swedish) massage, sports massage, myotherapy/trigger point massage, myofascial release, deep tissue massage, cranio-sacral therapy, reflexology, massage safety and emergency management, client counseling, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Transportation law faces mounting complexity as emerging technologies and climate adaptation demands strain legacy regulatory frameworks. This project addresses the critical gap in predictive tools to analyze how liability structures and right-of-way governance impact infrastructure investment patterns across interconnected transportation modes. By developing a computational legal architecture model (CLAM), we propose to map cascading effects of regulatory decisions through three phases: (1) Automated parsing of international maritime case law, FAA advisories, and cross-border rail agreements using transformer-based NLP models to identify latent conflict points in operational standards; (2) Multi-agent reinforcement learning simulations evaluating how autonomous vehicle liability precedents influence port automation adoption rates; (3) Graph neural network analysis of 40 years of surface transportation board rulings to quantify judicial reasoning patterns affecting public-private partnership risk calculations. The research requires HPC resources to manage petascale document corpora, parallelize millions of hypothetical regulatory change scenarios, and train multimodal embeddings that align legal semantics with engineering reliability metrics. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative framework for assessing transportation policy trade-offs between innovation incentives and systemic risk mitigation, particularly crucial for governing AI-driven logistics networks. This computational jurisprudence approach establishes a methodology to proactively evaluate legal structures’ resilience to technological disruption—a critical capability as transportation law increasingly mediates between urban planning imperatives, decarbonization timelines, and global supply chain vulnerabilities.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting land, sea, air, and space transportation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and behavioral dynamics of human operators interacting with complex, safety-critical systems, such as air traffic control interfaces or emergency response platforms. Traditional experimental methods often struggle to capture the multi-layered interactions between decision-making heuristics, environmental stressors, and system feedback loops in real time. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling framework leveraging agent-based simulations (ABS) and machine learning (ML) to analyze how individual and team performance emerges under varying task demands and system constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across simulated scenarios, enabling the exploration of rare but consequential events (e.g., cascading errors) and the identification of resilience-enhancing design principles. The ABS will integrate empirical data from eye-tracking, physiological monitoring, and behavioral task performance to calibrate agent decision policies, while ML pipelines will classify patterns of adaptive vs. maladaptive system interactions. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to model populations of heterogeneous agents interacting with dynamic systems at unprecedented granularity, reducing computational bottlenecks inherent in sequential Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for predicting human-system performance trade-offs under uncertainty, with applications to interface design, training protocol optimization, and error mitigation in high-risk domains. This work advances Human Factors Psychology by bridging theoretical models of cognitive workload with data-driven, systems-level analyses, while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in scaling experimental psychology research beyond lab-based paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to understand of interactions among humans and other elements of a system. Includes instruction in applying theory, principles, data and methods to design in order to optimize human well-being and overall system performance.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in personalized patient care planning and real-time clinical decision support for registered nurses (RNs) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multidimensional health data. Despite advancements in electronic health records (EHRs) and wearable monitoring devices, nursing workflows often lack computational tools to dynamically integrate patient-specific data—such as vital signs, medication adherence, psychosocial factors, and longitudinal health trends—into actionable care plans. This limitation contributes to delayed interventions, suboptimal resource allocation, and preventable adverse events. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework optimized for HPC environments to process terabyte-scale EHR datasets and sensor-derived streams. The framework will employ ensemble models combining recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal pattern detection, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map inter-patient contagion risks in hospital units, and natural language processing (NLP) to extract insights from nursing notes. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in predicted patient trajectories under varying staffing and intervention scenarios. By integrating these components into a dashboard prototype, the system will provide RNs with real-time risk stratification and prioritized care recommendations. Computational demands necessitate HPC resources due to the scale of federated EHR datasets (>500,000 patient records across six hospitals), the need for hyperparameter optimization across competing models, and latency-critical inference during simulated clinical workflows. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for sepsis progression, fall risk, and medication complication alerts, alongside open-source tools for nursing informatics. This work aims to establish a computational foundation for data-driven nursing science, directly supporting the quadruple aim of enhancing patient outcomes, improving care team efficiency, reducing costs, and promoting clinician well-being.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data in clinical diagnostics necessitates advanced computational approaches to integrate heterogeneous datasets and uncover molecular mechanisms underlying genetic diseases. Current methods for analyzing cytogenetic (e.g., karyotyping, chromosomal microarray) and molecular genetic (e.g., exome sequencing, epigenetic profiling) data often operate in silos, limiting their ability to resolve variants of uncertain significance (VUS) or identify multi-scale genomic contributors to disease phenotypes. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a unified computational framework to harmonize multi-modal genetic data, correlate structural and sequence-level variants with clinical outcomes, and prioritize pathogenic mechanisms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale genomic datasets, including whole-genome sequencing from patient cohorts and public repositories (e.g., gnomAD, ClinVar), and to perform integrative analyses across terabase-scale data. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks trained on variant interaction networks and attention-based architectures for phenotype-genotype association, will be deployed to identify predictive patterns in complex datasets. Custom pipelines will align and annotate cytogenetic findings with mutational signatures, non-coding regulatory elements, and 3D chromatin conformation data. Statistical frameworks will assess the combinatorial effects of rare variants and structural rearrangements. The anticipated outcomes include improved classification of VUS, discovery of novel biomarkers for genetic disorders, and scalable tools to guide clinical reporting. By leveraging HPC capabilities for parallelized data processing and model training, this work aims to advance precision diagnostics and reveal mechanistic insights into conditions such as developmental disorders, cancer predisposition syndromes, and inherited metabolic diseases. The developed resources will be disseminated as open-source software to support the broader clinical genetics community.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and disorders present complex molecular landscapes that challenge conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. Current limitations in integrating multi-omics data with clinical outcomes hinder the development of precision strategies for diseases such as acute myeloid leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and lymphoma. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and clinical datasets from multicenter cohorts. The research will focus on three primary aims: (1) identifying novel molecular subtypes through unsupervised clustering of multi-omics data, (2) developing machine learning models to predict treatment resistance and disease progression, and (3) simulating clonal evolution patterns in hematologic malignancies using agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will employ containerized pipelines for variant calling, chromatin accessibility analysis, and single-cell RNA-seq processing, followed by integrative analysis using tensor decomposition and graph neural networks. The HPC environment is critical for managing datasets exceeding 500 TB, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks such as whole-genome simulations, and optimizing hyperparameters for deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include the discovery of predictive biomarkers for therapy response, a publicly accessible computational framework for hematologic disease subtyping, and mechanistic insights into microenvironment-driven clonal selection. These results will directly inform the design of upcoming clinical trials assessing risk-adapted therapies. By enabling rapid analysis of high-dimensional data at unprecedented scale, this project will advance precision hematology and provide a template for translating complex computational findings into clinically actionable tools. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated workloads, distributed storage, and scalable memory configurations to accommodate iterative model training and validation across diverse patient populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the mechanisms and therapy of diseases of the blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lymph, including patient management, diagnostic tests, biopsies, and other procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of diagnostic ambiguity in complex autoimmune disorders, where overlapping clinical presentations and heterogeneous biomarker profiles often delay accurate classification. Current laboratory methods rely on sequential, manual interpretation of immunoassay, proteomic, and flow cytometry data, creating bottlenecks in analysis and limiting the integration of multi-modal datasets. We propose developing an artificial intelligence-driven framework to automate and enhance the interpretation of clinical laboratory data through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multimodal fusion. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures to process temporal immunofluorescence patterns, mass spectrometry profiles, and single-cell cytometry data in parallel, identifying latent correlations across disparate datatypes. Computational workflows will be trained on a retrospective cohort of 15,000+ de-identified patient records with confirmed autoimmune diagnoses, then validated against prospectively collected samples. Key innovations include a novel attention-based neural network for cross-dataset feature alignment and a simulation module modeling antibody-antigen binding dynamics at scale to predict epitope spreading patterns. Expected outcomes include a clinically deployable decision-support tool that reduces diagnostic turnaround time by ≥40% while improving classification accuracy for rare autoimmune subtypes (target AUC: 0.92 vs. current 0.78 benchmark). The computational pipelines developed will be optimized for containerized deployment in clinical laboratory information systems, directly enhancing medical laboratory technicians' interpretive capabilities without disrupting existing workflows. By establishing an HPC-powered bridge between high-dimensional laboratory data and actionable diagnostic insights, this work aims to redefine precision in autoimmune diagnostics while demonstrating scalable infrastructure for emerging clinical omics applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists/medical technologists, to perform routine medical laboratory procedures and tests and to apply preset strategies to record and analyze data. Includes instruction in general laboratory procedures and skills; laboratory mathematics; medical computer applications; interpersonal and communications skills; and the basic principles of hematology, medical microbiology, immunohematology, immunology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociolinguistic and cultural impacts of 19th-century missionary print media on Indigenous Pacific Islander communities, a niche interdisciplinary area within missiology and digital humanities. Missionary-produced texts—including vernacular translations, educational materials, and religious tracts—played a pivotal role in mediating colonial encounters, yet their large-scale linguistic patterns and semantic networks remain underexplored due to the volume and fragmentation of archival sources. The research problem centers on disentangling how these texts both preserved and transformed Indigenous knowledge systems, while negotiating power asymmetries. Computational methods will be applied to a corpus of digitized missionary publications (15,000+ pages in English and Polynesian languages), combining NLP techniques—such as topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and word embedding—with network analysis to map lexical borrowing, conceptual hybridization, and paratextual framing strategies. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual OCR outputs, training custom transformer models for low-resource languages, and simulating semantic shifts across temporal and geographic axes. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for analyzing historical intercultural texts, (2) visualizations of how mission presses reconfigured Indigenous epistemologies through lexical innovation, and (3) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric narratives of cultural erasure by highlighting bidirectional adaptation in missionary-Indigenous discourse. The project will produce an open-access database and computational toolkit tailored for missiological research, enabling scholars to interrogate the complex interplay of religion, language, and colonialism at unprecedented scale. By integrating HPC-driven humanities methodologies with mission studies, this work advances interdisciplinary frameworks for decolonial historiography while expanding the technical frontiers of digital missiology.
cip_title: Missions/ Missionary Studies and Missiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in missions, missionary studies, and missiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing drug therapy regimens in complex clinical populations through advanced computational modeling, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current methodological limitations. Current approaches to personalized pharmacotherapy often fail to account for the dynamic interplay between patient-specific factors—such as genetic polymorphisms, organ dysfunction, drug-drug interactions, and comorbidities—and the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) properties of medications. This gap leads to suboptimal dosing strategies, particularly in high-risk populations receiving multi-drug regimens for conditions like cancer, psychiatric disorders, or organ transplantation. We propose to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, machine learning (ML), and stochastic simulation techniques to predict individualized therapeutic outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of large electronic health record (EHR) datasets (n > 50,000 patients) from partner health systems, coupled with genomic and proteomic data, to parameterize population PK/PD models. Bayesian hierarchical modeling will address heterogeneity in drug response, while molecular dynamics simulations will explore drug-receptor interactions for targeted therapies. Computational workflows will be validated against clinical trial data and real-world therapeutic drug monitoring outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms for dose optimization in hepatic/renal impairment, tools to mitigate adverse drug events in polypharmacy scenarios, and open-source models for chemotherapy pharmacokinetics in obese patients. This work directly supports precision medicine initiatives in clinical pharmacy by enabling data-driven decisions at the point of care, with particular significance for antimicrobial stewardship programs and oncology support services. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational intensity of multi-omic integration, large-scale parameter sensitivity analyses, and real-time simulations required for clinical translation. Project outcomes will advance therapeutic decision support systems and inform institutional protocols for high-risk medication management.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Clinical, Hospital, and Managed Care Pharmacy
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to deliver specialized pharmacy services and produce pharmaceutical products in clinical settings in conjunction with other health care professionals. Includes instruction in biostatistics; clinical pharmacokinetics; biopharmaceutics; neuropharmacology; pharmacodynamics; drug metabolism; clinical sampling and research design; drug delivery systems; chemotherapy; pharmacotherapy; clinical pharmacy management; medical and research ethics; and applications to nuclear, nutrition support, oncology, psychiatric, and therapeutic pharmacy.

abstract: The administration of anesthetic agents requires precise titration to balance efficacy with patient safety, yet current protocols rely on generalized dosing models that inadequately account for dynamic intraoperative variables, including real-time biometric fluctuations and pharmacogenomic heterogeneity. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a machine learning framework to predict individualized anesthetic requirements using high-dimensional physiological, genomic, and pharmacokinetic data. The research will integrate multimodal inputs—including continuous electroencephalogram (EEG) waveforms, hemodynamic trends, and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiles—to model interpatient variability in drug metabolism and sedation depth. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets (>10 TB) from retrospective electronic health records and prospective intraoperative monitoring systems, enabling parallelized training of deep neural networks and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations. Key computational challenges include optimizing time-series analysis of EEG data to detect subclinical arousal states and resolving stochastic differential equations for real-time drug distribution modeling. The resulting predictive algorithms will be validated against clinical outcomes in a simulated surgical environment, with performance metrics compared to standard dosing protocols. Successfully linking patient-specific biological signatures to anesthetic responsiveness will advance precision sedation practices, reducing postoperative complications such as delirium and hemodynamic instability. This work bridges computational neuroscience, systems pharmacology, and clinical anesthesiology, establishing a novel paradigm for data-driven perioperative care. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to deliver an open-source software toolkit for anesthesiologist assistants to dynamically adjust anesthetic regimens, enhancing both patient safety and procedural efficiency in diverse surgical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance protocols for high-precision electromechanical systems, such as semiconductor manufacturing equipment and aerospace components, by leveraging advanced computational modeling and machine learning. Current maintenance strategies often rely on static schedules or reactive repairs, leading to unplanned downtime, accelerated component wear, and costly over-maintenance. The study will develop a dynamic, data-driven framework to optimize maintenance intervals and failure prediction accuracy through multi-physics simulations and real-time sensor analytics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale datasets from embedded sensors, environmental monitors, and historical maintenance logs while executing parallelized simulations of component degradation under diverse operational conditions. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for stress modeling in micron-scale components, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal cycling effects, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map interdependencies between subsystems. A federated learning architecture will be implemented to preserve data privacy across collaborating industrial partners while training anomaly detection models. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework capable of reducing unplanned downtime by ≥30% in pilot manufacturing systems, a physics-informed machine learning model for wear prediction with <5% mean absolute error, and generalized protocols for adaptive maintenance in multi-vendor environments. The proposed HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 10^4+ operational scenarios, real-time hybrid simulations integrating IoT data streams, and comparative benchmarking against traditional reliability-centered maintenance approaches. This work aims to establish scalable computational tools that advance precision maintenance practices while reducing lifecycle costs for critical infrastructure systems.
cip_title: Precision Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision systems maintenance and repair, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of workplace team performance under varying organizational structures and stress conditions. Industrial and organizational psychology research faces challenges in capturing the nonlinear, multilevel interactions between individual behaviors, group dynamics, and institutional policies using traditional statistical methods. The proposed study will develop agent-based computational models to simulate how communication patterns, reward systems, and hierarchical configurations influence collective problem-solving efficiency and employee well-being. By parameterizing agents with empirically derived psychological profiles—including stress response curves, motivation thresholds, and decision-making heuristics—the simulations will explore emergent outcomes across thousands of organizational scenarios. Computational workflows will integrate machine learning techniques to identify critical leverage points for optimizing team composition and adaptive leadership strategies in high-pressure environments. The scale of analysis requires HPC capabilities to manage parallelized simulations of 10,000+ agent interactions across heterogeneous workplace contexts, coupled with real-time optimization of multi-objective outcomes (productivity vs. burnout risks). Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for designing resilient team structures in hybrid work environments and evidence-based guidelines for AI-assisted human resource allocation systems. This work bridges gaps between micro-level behavioral theories and macro-level organizational effectiveness, offering novel computational tools for studying complex psychosocial systems. Results will inform interventions to mitigate workplace stress while maintaining operational performance, with direct applications to workforce management in healthcare, technology, and emergency response sectors. The requested resources will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling how institutional policies propagate through human behavioral networks, advancing both methodological innovation and practical organizational strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and group behavior in institutional settings, applications to related problems of organization and industry, and that may prepare individuals to apply such principles in industrial and organizational settings. Includes instruction in group behavior theory, organizational theory, reward/punishment structures, human-machine and human-computer interactions, motivation dynamics, human stress studies, environmental and organizational influences on behavior, alienation and satisfaction, and job testing and assessment.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern construction practices by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize material performance, structural resilience, and energy efficiency in building systems. Current methods for evaluating construction materials and designs often rely on physical prototyping or simplified computational models, which can overlook complex interactions between variables such as thermal stress, load distribution, and environmental exposure. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-physics simulation framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model building systems under diverse real-world conditions. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of composite materials (e.g., insulated concrete forms, cross-laminated timber) and modular construction assemblies, simulating scenarios like seismic activity, extreme weather, and long-term wear. Additionally, generative design algorithms will iteratively explore geometries and material configurations to minimize waste while meeting safety codes. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times from weeks to days, allowing rapid iteration of sustainable designs. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for predicting material lifespan under climate stressors, data-driven guidelines for retrofitting aging structures, and open-source tools to help small-scale contractors adopt simulation-driven design. This work aligns with industry demands for decarbonization and disaster-resilient infrastructure, offering computational strategies to reduce construction costs and environmental impacts. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations, ML training on terabyte-scale sensor datasets from smart buildings, and high-fidelity visualization of structural failures. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with vocational training programs to bridge gaps between computational research and hands-on construction education.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the building, inspecting, and maintaining of structures and related properties. May include instruction in masonry, carpentry, electrical and power transmission installation, building/construction finishing, management, inspection and other construction-related applications.

abstract: Emerging technologies increasingly demand interfaces that adapt to users’ dynamic cognitive and perceptual states, yet current design paradigms rely on static models of human behavior. This project addresses the challenge of creating real-time adaptive interfaces through computational modeling of individual neurocognitive processes during human-technology interaction. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to develop a framework that integrates multimodal data streams—including eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and interaction logs—to predict and respond to shifts in user attention, cognitive load, and decision-making strategies. The research problem centers on the computational latency and complexity of processing heterogeneous biosignals at scale, which existing consumer-grade systems cannot support. Our approach combines graph neural networks to model temporal dependencies in neurophysiological data with reinforcement learning agents that simulate interface adaptations. These models will be trained on a corpus of user studies involving diverse task environments, from healthcare decision-support systems to immersive educational platforms. HPC resources are critical for three components: (1) parallel processing of high-frequency biosignal data to achieve real-time inference, (2) large-scale hyperparameter optimization for personalized adaptation policies, and (3) agent-based simulations of population-level interface interactions under stochastic cognitive load scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dynamic interface personalization validated through controlled user experiments, with measurable improvements in task accuracy and cognitive ergonomics. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience and interaction design, offering a foundation for ethically aligned technologies that respect cognitive diversity. By prioritizing HPC-driven adaptability, the project advances human-centered design paradigms beyond reactive interfaces toward systems that co-evolve with users’ situated needs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the drivers of hominin dispersal and adaptive strategies during the Pleistocene epoch by integrating large-scale archaeological, paleoenvironmental, and genomic datasets. A critical challenge in paleoanthropology lies in reconciling fragmented material evidence—such as lithic assemblages, fossil remains, and sediment records—with dynamic climatic and ecological conditions to model behavioral and migratory patterns. Existing studies often lack the computational capacity to synthesize spatially and temporally discontinuous datasets or to simulate complex interactions between environmental variables and hominin decision-making. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), Bayesian chronological analysis, and geospatial machine learning. Agent-based simulations will test hypotheses about resource exploitation, mobility, and social learning under variable climatic conditions simulated via paleoclimate proxy data. Concurrently, Bayesian methods will refine site chronologies, while neural networks trained on global paleoenvironmental reconstructions will predict undiscovered site locations and evaluate habitat suitability. These computationally intensive workflows require parallel processing to manage stochastic ABM iterations across millennia, high-resolution climate datasets (>10 TB), and uncertainty-aware chronological modeling. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and large-memory CPUs for population genetics analyses derived from ancient DNA datasets. Anticipated outcomes include novel insights into the interplay of environmental volatility, technological innovation, and demographic expansion in Homo sapiens and archaic hominins. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and databases, providing a scalable toolkit for simulating human-environment dynamics. This work directly advances anthropological research by enabling quantitatively robust, cross-disciplinary approaches to human evolution, with broader implications for understanding adaptive responses to ecological change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human beings, their antecedents and related primates, and their cultural behavior and institutions, in comparative perspective. Includes instruction in biological/physical anthropology, primatology, human paleontology and prehistoric archeology, hominid evolution, anthropological linguistics, ethnography, ethnology, ethnohistory, socio-cultural anthropology, psychological anthropology, research methods, and applications to areas such as medicine, forensic pathology, museum studies, and international affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural production and identity formation within Polish and Polish diaspora communities through computational analysis of large-scale textual and visual datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in Polish Studies: the lack of systematic, data-driven approaches to understanding how cultural narratives have evolved across time, particularly in response to geopolitical shifts, migration waves, and transnational exchanges. Current scholarship often relies on close readings of individual texts or localized case studies, limiting the capacity to identify macro-level patterns in cultural expression. To overcome these constraints, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze multilingual corpora spanning Polish literary works, periodicals, and archival materials from the 19th century to the present. Concurrently, computer vision methods will be applied to digitized collections of Polish art, folk art, and material culture to trace visual motifs and their sociocultural contexts. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on historical Polish-language texts, which present unique challenges due to lexical shifts and non-standard orthographies. Further computational demands arise from graph-based network analyses mapping connections between cultural producers, institutions, and transnational nodes across partitioned Poland and its diaspora communities. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable computational framework for cross-temporal analysis of cultural narratives in Polish Studies, 2) identification of previously unrecognized patterns in the relationship between borderland experiences and artistic production, and 3) open-access tools for semantic annotation of historical Polish texts. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this research will enable novel interdisciplinary perspectives on how cultural practices have sustained collective memory and shaped identity in Polish contexts, while establishing infrastructure for future large-scale digital scholarship in the field.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Poland and the current and historical inhabitants of the Polish lands, including borderlands, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of user engagement with algorithmically curated multimedia content across decentralized digital platforms, a critical challenge in contemporary digital communication. As decentralized platforms (e.g., blockchain-based social networks, peer-to-peer media-sharing systems) gain prominence, their reliance on distributed algorithms to personalize content raises questions about transparency, ethical design, and unintended behavioral outcomes. Existing studies lack scalable methods to analyze real-time, cross-platform interactions at the intersection of algorithmic design, user behavior, and content diffusion. To address this gap, the research employs high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale, dynamic networks of user-content interactions and simulate algorithmic curation processes. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate user decision-making under varying algorithmic conditions, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map content propagation pathways, and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze multimedia metadata and user-generated text. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets spanning synthetic and real-world platform data (e.g., activity logs, multimedia metadata). HPC resources are essential for training GNNs on evolving network topologies, running thousands of ABM iterations to test ethical design parameters, and performing real-time sentiment analysis on user feedback. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework to evaluate transparency in decentralized algorithmic systems, (2) evidence-based guidelines for mitigating echo chamber effects in peer-to-peer content distribution, and (3) open-source tools for simulating user-algorithm interactions at scale. The project will directly inform policy discussions on decentralized media governance and provide practitioners with actionable insights for designing ethically aligned multimedia platforms. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances computational communication research methods while addressing urgent sociotechnical challenges in digital media ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, critical evaluation, and regulation of new electronic communication technologies using computer applications; and that prepares individuals to function as developers and managers of digital communications media. Includes instruction in computer and telecommunications technologies and processes; design and development of digital communications; marketing and distribution; digital communications regulation, law, and policy; the study of human interaction with, and use of, digital media; and emerging trends and issues.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural dynamics of legislative networks and their impact on policy stability and reform in fragmented political systems. A critical challenge in political science lies in understanding how interactions among legislators, committees, and external stakeholders shape legislative outcomes, particularly in environments with polarized or unstable coalitions. While existing qualitative and statistical approaches offer partial insights, they struggle to model the nonlinear, adaptive behaviors of political actors operating within complex institutional constraints. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), natural language processing (NLP), and dynamic network analysis to simulate multi-level legislative decision-making processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across heterogeneous agent populations, process terabytes of parliamentary speech and voting records, and analyze time-evolving network structures. The ABM component will simulate strategic bargaining and coalition formation under varying electoral rules, while NLP tools will quantify ideological positions from legislative text to parameterize agent preferences. Network analysis will then map how institutional design mediates the relationship between individual preferences and collective outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of institutional configurations that mitigate legislative gridlock, (2) predictive models of coalition stability under exogenous shocks, and (3) methodological advancements in scaling political simulations to national-level legislatures. By leveraging parallelized computing for ensemble simulations and GPU-accelerated text analysis, this work will provide novel insights into the computational study of political institutions, with implications for comparative governance and institutional design. The requested resources will enable processing of multi-modal datasets across 15 legislative contexts, supporting over 50,000 simulation runs to establish statistically robust patterns.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dental restorative materials are critical for maintaining oral health, yet their long-term performance is limited by interfacial failure between the material and tooth structure, microbial colonization, and mechanical fatigue. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize these materials are time-intensive and fail to capture the complex multiscale interactions between material properties, biofilm dynamics, and biomechanical stress. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model the behavior of novel bioactive dental composites under simulated oral conditions, integrating molecular-scale interactions, mesoscale mechanical response, and microbial community dynamics. The research will employ molecular dynamics simulations to investigate interfacial adhesion mechanisms between composite resins and hydroxyapatite, finite element analysis to predict stress distribution in restored teeth under cyclic loading, and agent-based modeling to simulate competitive biofilm formation on material surfaces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these multiscale phenomena, particularly for simulating time-dependent viscoelastic behavior of polymer matrices (10^6+ atoms over nanosecond timescales) and parallelized parametric studies of geometric variations in cavity restorations. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal filler particle geometries for stress redistribution, predictive models of interfacial degradation kinetics, and biofilm-resistant surface topographies. This work will establish a computational pipeline for accelerating the design of next-generation dental materials with enhanced durability and antimicrobial properties, directly addressing the $5 billion annual global cost of restorative procedure failures. By bridging materials science, computational biomechanics, and microbial ecology, the project advances an emerging paradigm in precision dental biomaterials while providing open-source simulation tools for the research community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize clinical decision-making for patient cohorts with complex, multi-morbidity profiles, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current computational limitations in nursing research. Despite advances in evidence-based practice, clinical nurse leaders (CNLs) face challenges in personalizing care plans for patients with intersecting chronic conditions, as manual analysis of heterogeneous electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time physiological monitoring streams remains impractical. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable tools to identify dynamic risk patterns and simulate intervention outcomes across diverse patient populations. The proposed computational approach integrates machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze multi-source healthcare datasets from three regional hospital systems, encompassing 250,000+ de-identified patient records. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data—including unstructured clinical notes, medication histories, and wearable device outputs—using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines and deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer models) to extract latent risk factors. ABM simulations will then model care coordination scenarios under resource constraints, evaluating how staffing ratios, protocol adjustments, and patient education strategies affect 30-day readmission rates. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool that identifies high-risk patients and recommends tailored care pathways, validated through retrospective analysis and pilot testing in two clinical sites. The project’s significance lies in its potential to advance data-driven nursing practice, reduce algorithmic bias in triage systems, and establish computational methods for CNLs to rapidly test hypotheses about care delivery optimization. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work addresses critical gaps in translating large-scale healthcare data into actionable clinical insights, directly supporting the CNL role in improving patient outcomes through precision nursing interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: This research project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies and inaccuracies in medical insurance coding processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive framework. Medical coding, a critical interface between clinical care and billing systems, faces challenges due to the complexity of evolving code sets (e.g., ICD-11, CPT), heterogeneous electronic health record (EHR) data structures, and human error in code assignment. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) and deep learning architectures to analyze multi-modal clinical documentation—including provider notes, imaging reports, and procedural summaries—to predict optimal code combinations. By training transformer-based models on de-identified datasets spanning 10 million patient encounters from diverse healthcare systems, the computational approach will focus on semantic context extraction, code conflict resolution, and real-time compliance checks against Medicare and third-party payer policies. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and simulation of coding scenarios under varying regulatory constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated AI-assisted coding tool that reduces claim denials by ≥25%, identifies documentation gaps contributing to coding ambiguities, and dynamically adapts to annual coding updates. This work bridges health informatics, computational linguistics, and reimbursement policy analysis, offering a novel pathway to enhance financial sustainability for healthcare institutions while maintaining coding education relevance in an increasingly automated landscape. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, secure data storage compliant with HIPAA and HITECH standards, and scalable deployment architecture for integration with existing coding software ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized data entry, classification, and record-keeping procedures related to medical diagnostic, treatment, billing, and insurance documentation. Includes instruction in medical records and insurance software applications, basic anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, fundamentals of medical science and treatment procedures, data classification and coding, data entry skills, and regulations relating to Medicare and insurance documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to analyze the spatiotemporal dynamics of urban heat islands (UHIs) and their intersection with socioeconomic vulnerability, public health outcomes, and energy infrastructure resilience. UHIs—localized regions of elevated temperature in urban areas—exacerbate heat-related morbidity, strain energy grids, and disproportionately impact marginalized communities. Existing studies often address these factors in isolation, neglecting feedback loops between environmental stressors, infrastructure decay, and adaptive capacity. Leveraging heterogeneous datasets, including high-resolution satellite thermal imagery, anonymized health records, utility outage reports, and demographic surveys, we aim to model the cascading effects of UHIs across disciplinary boundaries. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to map interdependencies among physical, biological, and social systems with agent-based simulations of heat mitigation strategies. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing petabyte-scale geospatial data, optimizing hyperparameters across multi-modal architectures, and running ensemble simulations at city-block resolution over decadal timescales. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital twin platform for scenario testing, identification of high-priority intervention zones where thermal exposure intersects with infrastructural fragility, and predictive metrics for healthcare utilization during extreme heat events. By bridging climatology, urban economics, and epidemiology through scalable data integration, this work will provide policymakers with actionable tools to prioritize equitable climate adaptation measures while reducing computational barriers for cross-domain causal inference. The resource allocation will directly support the development of open-source analytics pipelines to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for complex urban system modeling.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data analytics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dairy production systems face critical challenges in optimizing milk yield, quality, and safety while minimizing economic and environmental costs. A key bottleneck lies in understanding the dynamic interactions between microbial communities in raw milk, processing environments, and final dairy products, which govern spoilage, pathogen persistence, and fermentation efficiency. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the complexity of these spatially and temporally variable systems. This project proposes an integrative computational framework to model microbial ecology and metabolic networks across dairy production stages. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable agent-based simulations of microbial population dynamics under varying processing conditions (e.g., pasteurization temperatures, storage durations) and genomic-scale flux balance analyses to predict metabolite exchange influencing product characteristics. Machine learning models trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metabolomic profiles from longitudinal sampling) will identify critical control points for quality assurance. The computational workflow will leverage containerized pipelines for reproducible analysis of sequencing data, coupled with GPU-accelerated neural networks to resolve patterns in high-dimensional sensor data from dairy processing equipment. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking operational parameters to microbial risks and product traits, validated through targeted lab experiments. This research will provide actionable insights for designing precision intervention strategies, reducing food waste from spoilage, and enhancing the safety of dairy products. By bridging gaps between microbial ecology, process engineering, and data science, the project advances computational capabilities in dairy science while addressing industry needs for sustainable innovation. Successful implementation requires HPC infrastructure capable of parallel processing for large-scale simulations (>10^6 agent interactions), high-memory nodes for genome-scale metabolic reconstructions, and scalable storage for petabyte-level multi-omics datasets.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: The safe and effective application of anesthesia requires precise, individualized approaches to manage physiological variability, drug interactions, and perioperative risks. Current models for predicting adverse events, optimizing drug dosing, or personalizing pain management protocols are limited by their reliance on simplified clinical variables or single-modality data, which fail to capture the complex interplay of genetic, pharmacodynamic, and real-time physiological factors. This project seeks to develop high-resolution computational models integrating multi-omics data, real-time vital sign streams, and electronic health records to advance predictive analytics in anesthesia and perioperative care. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct machine learning frameworks to analyze large-scale datasets from 10,000+ surgical cases, including genomic markers of drug metabolism, intraoperative hemodynamic trends, and postoperative pain outcomes. Ensemble models will identify risk signatures for hypotension, respiratory depression, and chronic post-surgical pain, while pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic simulations will optimize dosing strategies for patients with rare comorbidities or polypharmacy. Agent-based modeling will simulate emergent critical events (e.g., malignant hyperthermia) to refine crisis protocols. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated training for deep learning architectures and parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification in heterogeneous populations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for intraoperative instability, personalized analgesic regimens, and decision-support algorithms for anesthesia providers. By enabling rapid analysis of multimodal data, HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in traditional single-node systems. This work will directly inform clinical trials and practice guidelines, reducing preventable complications in vulnerable surgical populations. All models and pipelines will be shared via open-source platforms to foster collaboration in perioperative research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical patient care, and the care of pain problems. Includes instruction in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: Nursing practice faces a critical translational gap between research evidence and real-world clinical implementation, particularly in managing complex health conditions influenced by multi-dimensional patient data. This project addresses the challenge of integrating high-dimensional datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic biomarkers, and real-time patient monitoring streams—into actionable clinical decision-support tools for nurses. Traditional computing methods lack the capacity to process these heterogeneous data streams efficiently, limiting the scalability of predictive models and simulations of clinical outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models and agent-based simulations (ABS) that optimize evidence-based intervention strategies. The computational workflow includes preprocessing terabyte-scale EHR data to identify patterns in patient deterioration, training ensemble ML models to predict sepsis and hospital-acquired pressure injuries, and simulating the impact of nurse staffing ratios on intervention efficacy using ABS. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing model training across thousands of parameters, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in clinical scenarios, and analyzing genomic-epigenomic interactions influencing patient responses to nursing interventions. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for early risk detection, validated simulation frameworks to guide staffing and policy decisions, and scalable pipelines for integrating multi-omics data into nursing practice. By enabling rapid analysis of billion-row datasets and computationally intensive simulations, this project will advance precision nursing interventions, reduce unwarranted clinical variation, and provide a replicable computational infrastructure for future nursing research. The findings will be disseminated through interoperable clinical dashboards and training modules for nursing leaders, directly supporting the program’s mission to translate research into practice through innovation.
cip_definition: A practice-focused program that prepares registered nurses for increasingly complex evidence-based nursing practice, including translating research into practice, evaluating evidence, applying research in decision-making, and implementing viable clinical innovations to change practice. Includes instruction in healthcare delivery systems, health economics and finance, health policy, research methods, translating evidence into practice, concepts in population health, and nursing leadership.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of intercultural communication and identity negotiation in digitally mediated spaces, with a focus on mitigating polarization in multicultural urban environments. While prior studies have examined demographic or survey-based trends in diversity, this work addresses a critical gap: simulating how real-time, large-scale interactions between culturally diverse groups influence the emergence of inclusive or divisive social norms. The research integrates computational sociology, network science, and linguistic anthropology to analyze how micro-level communicative behaviors—such as code-switching, narrative framing, and symbolic gesture exchange—scale into macro-level patterns of social cohesion or fragmentation. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate populations with heterogeneous cultural attributes (e.g., values, communication styles, identity salience) interacting within dynamic social networks, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process multilingual corpora from social media and community forums to parameterize agent behaviors. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing thousands of stochastic simulations across diverse demographic and policy scenarios (e.g., varying levels of institutional support for multiculturalism, migration rates, or economic inequality). Expected outcomes include (1) identifying leverage points where targeted intercultural interventions (e.g., moderated dialogue platforms, algorithmic fairness adjustments) could reduce polarization, and (2) developing open-source tools for policymakers to visualize how systemic inequalities amplify cultural tensions in specific urban contexts. By bridging granular behavioral data with societal-scale dynamics, this project advances computational methods for diversity studies while providing actionable insights for fostering intercultural resilience in increasingly complex, digitally connected societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: Personalized dietary planning for individuals with specific nutritional needs requires balancing complex variables, including medical requirements, cultural preferences, budget constraints, and sensory acceptability. Current manual approaches to meal optimization are labor-intensive, prone to suboptimal outcomes, and lack scalability. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to automate and enhance meal planning processes for dietitians, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges. The research will focus on integrating multi-objective optimization algorithms with machine learning models trained on diverse datasets, including nutritional databases, clinical guidelines, patient health records, and food preference surveys. Key computational tasks include large-scale combinatorial optimization to generate meal combinations that meet nutrient targets, predictive modeling of patient acceptance and adherence, and simulations of long-term health outcomes under varying dietary scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration across high-dimensional parameter spaces, real-time adaptation to dynamic constraints (e.g., ingredient availability), and validation through Monte Carlo simulations of population-level dietary impacts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dietitian assistants that optimizes meal plans 50–100x faster than manual methods while improving adherence rates by quantitatively incorporating patient preferences. The project will further contribute novel datasets mapping regional food costs to nutritional density, supporting equity-focused meal planning. By computationally addressing the trade-offs between clinical efficacy, practicality, and patient satisfaction, this work aims to establish evidence-based protocols for scalable, personalized nutrition interventions. Successful implementation could reduce healthcare costs associated with diet-related chronic diseases while enhancing the operational capacity of dietetic professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: Urban educational leaders face persistent challenges in equitably allocating resources to address the complex needs of diverse student populations, yet data-driven strategies for optimizing decision-making remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to model the multidimensional impacts of resource distribution patterns on academic outcomes in urban K-12 systems through computational simulations of district-scale operational scenarios. Leveraging anonymized administrative datasets from three major metropolitan school districts (enrollment >150,000 students each), we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between funding allocations, staffing policies, community partnerships, and student performance metrics across heterogeneous urban contexts. High-performance computing resources are required to process longitudinal datasets spanning 10+ years, train machine learning classifiers identifying at-risk student subgroups, and run Monte Carlo simulations evaluating 50,000+ allocation scenarios accounting for variables including socioeconomic disparities, multilingual learner populations, and infrastructure constraints. Computational experiments will quantify how different leadership strategies affect equity indicators such as advanced course access gaps and chronic absenteeism rates. The hybrid methodology combines network analysis of community resource maps with predictive analytics on intervention effectiveness. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source computational framework for simulating urban education resource policies, (2) evidence-based thresholds for cost-effective staffing ratios in Title I schools, and (3) optimization algorithms balancing equity priorities with budgetary realities. By enabling large-scale analysis of systemic interactions often obscured in traditional policy analyses, this work aims to provide urban education leaders with decision-support tools grounded in complex systems science. The computational infrastructure will support ongoing collaboration with partner districts to validate models against real-world implementation data, ultimately advancing leadership capacity to transform urban educational systems through data-informed resource stewardship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on issues and problems specific to the educational needs of populations and communities located in metropolitan, inner city, and related areas and prepares individuals to provide educational services and administrative leadership in urban contexts. Includes instruction in multicultural education, at-risk studies, urban sociology, multilingual education, urban studies and planning, human services, health services and nutrition, cross-cultural communication, diversity studies, safety and security, and urban educational administration and leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate emergent behavioral dynamics in heterogeneous populations during homeland security crises, with a focus on scenarios involving disinformation propagation and decentralized threat coordination. Current models often oversimplify socio-cultural variables or lack granularity to address the interplay between digital communication networks and real-world collective behavior, limiting their utility for proactive threat mitigation. The research will integrate agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and multilayer network analysis to capture how ideologically fragmented groups adapt to security interventions in digitally mediated environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale simulations that incorporate 1) real-time social media data streams, 2) cognitive bias parameters derived from experimental psychology studies, and 3) geospatial constraints on physical mobilization patterns. The computational architecture will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to analyze cross-platform information cascades alongside reinforcement learning agents that simulate adversarial adaptation strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to identify tipping points in crisis escalation trajectories and evaluate the resilience of communication protocols used by emergency responders. By bridging computational social science with security informatics, this work aims to advance decision-support systems for managing hybrid threats that exploit the sociotechnical vulnerabilities of modern interconnected societies. The resulting models will be validated against historical case studies of coordinated disruption campaigns and stress-tested through scenario-based war-gaming exercises with homeland security stakeholders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in energy system monitoring and optimization by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to advance the development of scalable, high-fidelity simulation frameworks. Current approaches to energy loss detection and system calibration often rely on simplified models or static datasets, limiting their ability to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, intermittent renewable generation, and sensor network performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational workflow integrating real-time sensor data with physics-informed machine learning models to simulate energy flows across heterogeneous systems, including commercial buildings, industrial processes, and distributed renewable networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel execution of multi-scale simulations, testing thousands of operational scenarios to identify optimal instrumentation configurations, calibration intervals, and energy conservation strategies. Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent thermal-electrical interactions in building HVAC systems, automating anomaly detection in smart meter networks, and optimizing demand-response protocols under grid constraints. By validating these models against empirical data from partnered utility providers, the project aims to produce adaptive algorithms for minimizing energy waste while maintaining system reliability. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for predictive maintenance of monitoring infrastructure, data-driven guidelines for retrofitting legacy systems, and a digital twin platform to support decarbonization planning. This work directly aligns with national priorities for energy resilience, offering translational benefits for reducing operational costs and greenhouse gas emissions in urban and industrial sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing energy-efficient systems or monitoring energy use. Includes instruction in principles of energy conservation, instrumentation calibration, monitoring systems and test procedures, energy loss inspection procedures, energy conservation techniques, and report preparation.

abstract: Pain management in palliative care remains a critical challenge due to the heterogeneity of patient responses, complex interactions between biological and psychosocial factors, and the limited personalization of therapeutic strategies. Current approaches often rely on trial-and-error protocols, leading to delays in effective symptom control and increased risks of adverse effects. To address this, we propose a computational research project leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that optimize individualized pain management plans. This project integrates multi-modal clinical data—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, neuroimaging, and real-time sensor data—with mechanistic models of pain pathways and drug pharmacokinetics-pharmacodynamics (PK/PD). Advanced machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models, will be employed to identify patient subgroups, predict treatment responses, and simulate intervention outcomes across diverse scenarios. The computational demands of processing large-scale datasets, training complex models, and running iterative simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to ensure feasibility and scalability. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for stratifying patients based on biopsychosocial risk factors, (2) optimized dosing algorithms for opioids and adjuvant therapies that minimize side effects, and (3) predictive tools to guide clinical decision-making in dynamic care settings. By bridging data-driven insights with clinical practice, this work aims to reduce the burden of undertreated pain, enhance quality of life for palliative care patients, and provide a template for computationally guided precision medicine in symptom management. The proposed HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of models, validation against retrospective cohorts, and eventual translation into prospective clinical trials.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care/Pain Management

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern industrial production systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize efficiency, reduce waste, and enhance scalability. Current simulation and optimization methods often fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, equipment degradation, and real-time supply chain disruptions, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and operational inefficiencies. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy large-scale, multi-agent simulations coupled with machine learning-driven predictive analytics. The computational framework will model interconnected production processes at unprecedented resolution, integrating real-time sensor data from manufacturing environments to dynamically adjust workflows, predict maintenance needs, and optimize energy consumption. Key methodologies include parallelized discrete-event simulation for production line modeling, distributed training of neural networks for anomaly detection in equipment performance, and evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective optimization of resource distribution. The proposed work will enable the analysis of system-wide interactions across entire production ecosystems, from raw material handling to final product assembly, while maintaining computational tractability.
