Expected outcomes include validated models for adaptive production scheduling under uncertainty, predictive maintenance protocols with quantified reliability improvements, and decision-support tools for sustainable resource utilization. By providing scalable computational approaches tailored to industrial production challenges, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for operational agility and energy efficiency in advanced manufacturing environments, directly contributing to the competitiveness and environmental stewardship of domestic production infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in industrial production technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of dialectal variation in modern Catalan, with a focus on understudied regional and sociolinguistic dynamics. Despite Catalan’s status as a medium-sized European language with rich dialect diversity, comprehensive computational models of its phonetic, lexical, and morphosyntactic variability remain underdeveloped, particularly for non-standard registers and informal communication contexts. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and phonetic alignment algorithms, to analyze a 20-million-word multimodal corpus comprising oral histories, social media data, and regional literature. Key computational challenges include training domain-specific language models for low-resource Catalan dialects, automating the detection of contact-induced innovations from neighboring languages, and simulating diachronic shifts in lexical usage across geographic micro-regions. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution audio data (via spectral clustering and formant analysis), optimizing dialect classification models through distributed hyperparameter tuning, and handling memory-intensive alignment tasks across heterogeneous text sources. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for Catalan dialectometry, a geolocative prediction model for text attribution, and a phonetically annotated corpus to support cross-disciplinary research in Catalan philology. By integrating computational rigor with traditional linguistic scholarship, this project aims to redefine methodological standards for regional language studies while providing actionable insights for language preservation initiatives and educational resource development in Catalan-speaking territories. The scalability of the framework will also establish a template for computational approaches to other minority languages with complex dialect landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Catalan language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of immersive audio environments and real-time spatial sound processing in modern audio engineering demands computational resources beyond the capabilities of standard workstations. This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling high-fidelity acoustic spaces and optimizing real-time audio signal chains for applications in virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and interactive media. Current limitations in simulating intricate acoustic behaviors—such as wave diffraction, frequency-dependent absorption, and dynamic source-listener interactions—restrict the accuracy and scalability of audio spatialization tools. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for room acoustics and GPU-accelerated machine learning models for adaptive audio effect processing. The FDTD approach will enable physically accurate modeling of 3D wave propagation in complex geometries, while neural networks trained on large datasets of impulse responses and audio samples will automate parameter optimization for hybrid analog-digital signal chains. Key computational tasks include distributed-memory parallelization of FDTD solvers for large-scale acoustic spaces, CUDA-based implementation of real-time convolutional reverberation algorithms, and training variational autoencoders to map perceptual characteristics to DSP parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source framework for scalable acoustic simulation, (2) latency-optimized spatial audio rendering pipelines deployable on consumer-grade hardware, and (3) new insights into the relationship between computational precision and perceptual quality in immersive soundscapes. This work will directly benefit audio engineering education by providing case studies in HPC-aided acoustic design, while advancing industry capabilities in next-generation audio production tools. The requested computing resources are essential for handling memory-intensive wave simulations (>10^8 grid points) and reducing training times for deep learning models from weeks to days, enabling iterative experimentation critical to both technical and artistic dimensions of the research.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the mixing, recording, and production of music. Includes instruction in acoustics, audio mixing, audio production, audio recording, computer composition of music, music theory, digital devices, and sound technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision care strategies for geriatric dental patients by analyzing complex interactions between aging-related systemic conditions, oral microbiome dynamics, and treatment outcomes. Older adults often present with multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and age-related oral changes that complicate dental care, yet current clinical guidelines lack robust predictive tools to optimize interventions. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating large-scale genomic, metabolomic, and electronic health record (EHR) datasets from geriatric cohorts to model disease progression and therapeutic responses. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify biomarkers associated with elevated risks of caries, periodontal disease, and implant failure in aging populations, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize how age-altered salivary proteins influence oral pathogen adhesion. A key innovation involves federated learning frameworks to analyze distributed EHR data across institutions while preserving patient privacy. The computational workload necessitates HPC infrastructure due to the scale of multi-omics integration (>10 TB heterogeneous data), iterative model training for rare outcome prediction, and real-time simulations of microbial biofilms under varying physiological conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive risk stratification tools for clinicians, mechanistic insights into aging-related oral dysbiosis, and generative AI prototypes for personalized treatment planning. By elucidating pathways linking systemic health, oral ecology, and therapeutic efficacy, this research aims to establish data-driven guidelines that improve functional outcomes and quality of life for geriatric patients. The requested resources will enable rapid processing of computationally intensive workflows, including parallelized genomic alignment, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-scale agent-based biofilm modeling, which are infeasible on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of geriatric patients. Includes instruction in aging, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, geriatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and patient management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic financial decision-making in households facing economic volatility, a core concern within Family Resource Management Studies. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how families adapt resource allocation strategies under stressors such as income instability, unexpected expenses, or shifting access to public support systems. Existing models often rely on static or simplified assumptions about household behavior, limiting their ability to capture the nonlinear interactions between financial constraints, psychological factors, and policy interventions. To overcome these limitations, the project employs a multi-agent simulation framework that integrates behavioral economics principles, real-world financial datasets, and stochastic modeling of income and expense shocks. Each agent represents a household with heterogeneous attributes, including savings rates, debt profiles, risk tolerance, and awareness of public assistance programs. The computational approach requires iterative optimization to simulate millions of potential decision pathways across diverse demographic and economic scenarios, necessitating parallelized processing for parameter calibration and sensitivity analysis. By incorporating machine learning techniques to identify patterns in adaptive financial behaviors, the model aims to predict which combinations of household characteristics and external conditions lead to sustainable resource management versus financial distress. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for simulating policy impacts on household resilience, evidence-based insights into the effectiveness of targeted financial literacy interventions, and publicly accessible synthetic datasets reflecting complex decision-making dynamics. The results will directly inform the design of adaptive financial counseling frameworks and contribute to methodological innovation in non-STEM applications of HPC, demonstrating the transformative potential of computational social science in family resource management research.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and implementation of policies and processes contributing to successful individual and family resource management. Includes instruction in financial goal-setting and strategies; household income, assets, and debt management; preventing and resolving financial difficulties; and the use of relevant public resources.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for large-scale, interdisciplinary R&D programs, addressing a critical challenge in research management: balancing efficiency, innovation, and risk under dynamic constraints. While traditional project management tools excel in predictable environments, they often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between technical uncertainty, personnel expertise, and shifting organizational priorities inherent in complex R&D ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose an agent-based modeling approach combined with multi-objective optimization to simulate decision pathways across thousands of scenario permutations. The computational model will integrate historical R&D performance data, real-time project metrics, and probabilistic risk assessments to evaluate trade-offs between short-term deliverables and long-term innovation potential. Key variables include budget elasticity, team composition dynamics, and technology readiness levels across concurrent projects. By implementing parallelized genetic algorithms and Monte Carlo methods on HPC infrastructure, we aim to overcome computational bottlenecks in solving high-dimensional optimization problems that exceed the capabilities of conventional systems. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies the impact of resource allocation choices on program-wide KPIs, validated through case studies from pharmaceutical development and clean energy innovation partnerships. This work will contribute novel methodologies to the emerging field of computational research management, providing actionable insights for aligning R&D investments with strategic organizational goals while maintaining adaptive capacity. The requested computing resources are essential for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution to model enterprise-level R&D portfolios, with potential applications extending to government research agencies and cross-sector innovation consortia.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze dynamic, multimodal behavioral data from teletherapy sessions, addressing the critical challenge of objectively quantifying therapeutic alliance—a key predictor of mental health outcomes. While therapeutic alliance is traditionally assessed via subjective surveys, our approach integrates speech, facial expression, and linguistic patterns captured in video recordings to model clinician-client interactions in real time. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to evaluate and optimize communication strategies in mental health services, particularly in underserved regions reliant on telehealth. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will process and synchronize terabytes of audiovisual data from diverse teletherapy cohorts (e.g., individuals with anxiety disorders and autism spectrum conditions). Deep learning models, including transformer-based architectures for speech-text fusion and 3D convolutional networks for temporal facial affect analysis, will be trained to identify micro-level interaction features correlated with alliance metrics. Computational workflows will leverage distributed GPU acceleration for hyperparameter optimization and ensemble model validation across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolbox for granular alliance analytics and evidence-based guidelines to personalize communication training for clinicians. By bridging behavioral neuroscience, clinical psychology, and artificial intelligence, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for enhancing digital mental health interventions. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the project’s scale, enabling parallel processing of sensitive data under institutional review board protocols while maintaining low-latency pipelines for eventual real-time feedback applications.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in therapeutic recreation (TR) by developing computational models to optimize personalized intervention plans for individuals with disabilities. Current TR practices rely on generalized frameworks to design recreational activities that address physical, cognitive, or emotional health goals. However, these frameworks often lack granularity to account for dynamic interactions between individual patient factors (e.g., medical history, psychosocial needs, activity preferences) and therapeutic outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning-driven approach to analyze multimodal datasets, including electronic health records, patient-reported outcomes, and real-time biometric data (e.g., heart rate, motion sensors), to identify patterns predictive of intervention efficacy. HPC resources will enable the processing of large-scale datasets and the training of ensemble models that integrate reinforcement learning to simulate patient responses under varying therapeutic scenarios. Additionally, agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate social dynamics in group-based TR interventions, assessing how peer interactions influence adherence and outcomes. The computational pipeline will be validated using retrospective data from clinical TR programs, with iterative feedback from licensed recreational therapists. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool to recommend patient-specific activity modifications, a deeper understanding of mechanistic links between recreational modalities and health outcomes, and a framework for dynamically adapting interventions based on real-time data. This work will provide novel computational methodologies tailored to TR, a field underrepresented in data-driven health research, while directly supporting the development of precision therapeutic strategies to enhance quality of life for individuals with disabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, organize, and direct recreational activities designed to promote health and well-being for patients who are physically, mentally, or emotionally disabled. Includes instruction in the foundations of therapeutic recreation, leisure education and counseling, program planning, therapeutic recreational modalities, basic anatomy and physiology, psychology, medical terminology, human growth and development, patient observation and evaluation, special needs populations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the documentation, analysis, and revitalization of endangered Uralic languages, with a focus on under-resourced varieties such as Karelian, Ludic, and Eastern Sami. The core challenge lies in processing and modeling complex linguistic data—including historical texts, modern recordings, and dialectal variations—that exhibit non-standard orthographies, agglutinative morphology, and sparse digital representation. Traditional methods struggle to manage the scale and intricacy of these datasets, particularly when analyzing cross-dialectal phonological shifts or syntactic patterns across centuries of literary production. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining rule-based morphological parsers, transformer-based language models, and phylogenetic algorithms adapted for linguistic divergence modeling. HPC resources will enable the parallel training of custom neural architectures on distributed corpora spanning 15 Uralic languages, while iterative alignment algorithms will reconstruct proto-forms and trace contact-induced changes. Expected outcomes include 1) the first computationally derived atlas of sound correspondences across Samoyedic and Finno-Permic branches, 2) an open-source toolkit for automated morphological segmentation of Uralic texts, and 3) a diachronic corpus platform linking medieval birchbark manuscripts to contemporary speech samples through machine-translation-informed annotation. These resources will directly support Indigenous language revitalization initiatives while offering new methodologies for computational historical linguistics. The project’s scale—processing over 10 TB of multimodal data, including legacy field recordings and digitized archives—necessitates GPU-accelerated workflows for speech recognition on low-resource languages and transformer fine-tuning across distributed memory systems. By bridging documentary linguistics with HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to redefine theoretical understandings of Uralic morphosyntactic stability while producing practical resources for communities, educators, and researchers working with critically endangered languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Uralic languages, including, but not limited to, Finnish, Estonian, Karelian, and Sami. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to model the nonlinear, time-dependent mechanical behavior of hierarchically structured soft materials under dynamic loading, with a focus on applications in vascular biomechanics. Current approaches to simulating such systems face significant challenges in capturing multiscale interactions—from molecular-scale polymer chain dynamics to macroscale tissue deformation—while maintaining computational efficiency. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid particle-continuum method that integrates coarse-grained molecular dynamics with finite element analysis, enabling coupled simulations of fluid-structure interaction (FSI) and viscoelastic material response. Key innovations include adaptive resolution techniques to bridge spatiotemporal scales and GPU-accelerated solvers for real-time parameter optimization. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from collaborative studies on arterial tissue mechanics, with particular attention to aneurysm progression under pulsatile flow. Successful implementation will advance predictive capabilities for tissue remodeling in cardiovascular pathologies and establish a generalizable platform for simulating hierarchical materials in energy-absorbing structures or biomedical devices. By addressing critical gaps in multiscale mechanics and HPC-driven FSI, this work aims to provide open-source tools for the computational mechanics community, enabling high-fidelity simulations that inform both fundamental biomechanics and the design of bioinspired engineering systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to the application of mechanics. Incudes instruction in method development in solid, fluid mechanics and materials simulations with application to biomechanics and mechanics in medicine, multiphysics, fracture mechanics, multiscale mechanics, particle and meshfree methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and simulate the resilience of urban critical infrastructure networks against hybrid cyber-physical threats, with a focus on interdependencies between law enforcement operations, emergency response systems, and civil infrastructure. While existing research often examines technical vulnerabilities in isolation, this work addresses the gap in modeling cascading failures across socio-technical systems where digital attacks (e.g., ransomware, IoT compromises) intersect with physical disruptions (e.g., coordinated protests, arson). The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to execute large-scale agent-based simulations that integrate real-world datasets—including urban traffic patterns, emergency call logs, and infrastructure interdependency maps—with synthetically generated threat scenarios. Computational methods will combine network theory to model infrastructure connectivity, machine learning to predict adversarial behavior patterns, and discrete-event simulation to assess operational impacts on first responders. Key outcomes will include a risk prioritization toolkit identifying choke points in hybrid threat response workflows and probabilistic models quantifying how delayed law enforcement mobilization amplifies systemic vulnerabilities. By enabling multi-domain scenario testing at metropolitan scales, this work aims to provide actionable insights for optimizing resource allocation during concurrent cyber-physical crises. The HPC environment is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of threat vectors, simulating millions of agent interactions, and processing high-resolution spatiotemporal data streams in near-real time. Results will directly inform training protocols and contingency planning for agencies operating at the intersection of cybersecurity and physical security, ultimately strengthening community resilience against emerging asymmetric threats.
cip_title: Homeland Security, Law Enforcement, Firefighting and Related Protective Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, law enforcement, firefighting, and related protective services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into architectural design processes has the potential to revolutionize how buildings are conceived, optimized, and operated. However, existing tools for building performance analysis often operate in silos, limiting their ability to holistically address interdependent factors such as energy efficiency, thermal comfort, acoustic quality, and material lifecycle impacts. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multi-objective building system optimization, with a focus on retrofitting historic structures—a domain requiring specialized balance between preservation mandates and modern performance standards. The research problem centers on the computational complexity of simulating coupled physical phenomena (e.g., heat transfer, airflow, sound propagation) across heterogeneous materials and irregular geometries typical of older buildings. Current workflows struggle to model these interactions at sufficient resolution while maintaining practical simulation timescales. To address this, the project will implement a hybrid computational strategy combining finite element analysis (FEA) for localized structural and thermal behavior with graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on HPC-generated datasets to predict system-wide performance outcomes. Parametric design exploration will be accelerated through distributed Monte Carlo sampling, enabling rapid identification of retrofit solutions that minimize energy use without compromising heritage integrity. Validation will involve comparative case studies using 3D-scanned building data and sensor-collected post-retrofit performance metrics. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for architects and preservationists, alongside new insights into material compatibility and system interdependencies in heritage contexts. By leveraging HPC resources to overcome scale-resolution tradeoffs, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for sustainable building interventions that harmonize technological innovation with cultural and historical preservation imperatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of advanced technology to building design and construction, retrofitting existing buildings, and efficient operation of buildings, including lighting and daylight design, acoustics, solar design, building conservation, and energy-conscious design. Includes instruction in architecture, building technology, civil and structural engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental control systems, sustainability, and computer tools and applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing real-time, data-driven advertising campaigns in multi-platform digital environments. The proliferation of fragmented media channels, dynamic consumer behavior datasets, and the need for instantaneous campaign adjustments present a computational challenge: traditional analytics tools cannot efficiently process the scale and velocity of data required to inform adaptive advertising strategies. This research aims to develop machine learning models that predict cross-platform consumer engagement patterns by analyzing terabyte-scale datasets, including social media interactions, search histories, and real-time bidding logs. The computational approach will involve training neural networks on consumer response sequences, employing natural language processing to decode sentiment in user-generated content, and simulating A/B test scenarios for ad creative variations across millions of virtual audience segments. These tasks demand parallelized GPU computing for model training and distributed memory systems for large-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include a framework for optimizing ad spend allocation in real time, reducing latency in personalized content delivery, and quantifying the impact of microtargeting on brand perception metrics. By enabling faster iteration of campaign elements and more precise audience segmentation, this work addresses critical gaps in advertising efficacy measurement while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational communication and marketing science. The requested resources will support the processing of streaming data pipelines, reduce runtime for complex consumer journey simulations by 60–75%, and facilitate the development of open-source tools for ethical audience analytics, directly benefiting academic research in digital advertising strategy.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: Small internal combustion engines (ICEs) powering portable equipment, such as lawnmowers and chainsaws, face increasing demands for improved efficiency, reduced emissions, and extended operational lifespans. However, optimizing these engines remains challenging due to the complex interplay of combustion dynamics, mechanical wear, and thermal management in compact designs. Traditional experimental approaches are costly and time-intensive, limiting rapid iteration. This project proposes a computational research initiative to model small ICE systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, enabling high-fidelity simulations of engine performance under diverse operating conditions. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) developing multi-physics models integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion and emissions analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) for component stress prediction, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to correlate sensor data with maintenance needs; (2) validating models against experimental data from engine test benches; and (3) identifying design and operational modifications to enhance efficiency and durability. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational intensity of resolving turbulent combustion at microscales, simulating thermal gradients in engine components, and training ML models on large datasets of engine performance metrics. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing fuel injection timing, air-fuel ratios, and material selection for high-stress components, as well as data-driven diagnostic tools for early fault detection. By bridging advanced computational methods with practical small engine mechanics, this work aims to provide actionable insights for manufacturers and technicians, reduce environmental impacts, and equip students with skills in computational problem-solving—a novel integration of HPC-driven research into technical education for small engine repair. The project’s open-source models and case studies will serve as a resource for the broader small engine technology community.
cip_title: Small Engine Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain small internal-combustion engines used on portable power equipment such as lawnmowers, chain saws, rotary tillers, and snowmobiles.

abstract: Child development is shaped by dynamic interactions between individual cognitive processes, social environments, and evolving cultural contexts. However, existing models often oversimplify these interactions by treating them as static or unidirectional, limiting their capacity to predict long-term outcomes or inform interventions. This project proposes a computational framework to simulate and analyze the emergence of self-regulation skills in children aged 3–8 years, integrating neurocognitive, behavioral, and sociolinguistic data within a unified agent-based modeling (ABM) paradigm. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how nonlinear feedback loops between caregiver communication patterns, peer interactions, and neural maturation jointly influence developmental trajectories. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of these multiscale simulations, which will parameterize thousands of synthetic agents using real-world developmental datasets, including longitudinal eye-tracking records, naturalistic audio recordings of caregiver-child dyads, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data. Bayesian optimization methods will be deployed to iteratively refine model parameters, while graph neural networks will identify latent interaction patterns predictive of self-regulation milestones. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating developmental cascades in diverse sociocultural contexts, (2) evidence-based criteria for identifying at-risk profiles through computational biomarkers, and (3) actionable insights for tailoring community programs that align with neurodevelopmental sensitive periods. By bridging developmental science with computational modeling, this work advances theoretical frameworks for understanding emergent complexity in child development while providing scalable tools to inform policy and practice. The requested HPC allocation will directly support parallelized simulation runs, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale sensitivity analyses that are computationally infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the intellectual, social, emotional, and biological development of children and the planning and design of related human services. Includes instruction in parent-child relations, parenting practices, special needs of children, parental and environmental influences on child development, external support services, and related public policy issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing risk management and educational outcomes in outdoor education programs. While outdoor education emphasizes experiential learning in dynamic environments, program leaders face challenges in balancing safety, participant engagement, and environmental stewardship—a complex interplay influenced by variables such as weather patterns, group dynamics, terrain variability, and skill progression. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to curriculum design and risk assessment are resource-intensive and may fail to account for nonlinear interactions between these factors. To address this gap, we propose an interdisciplinary computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), geospatial analysis, and machine learning (ML). The ABM component will simulate participant interactions and decision-making during activities like rock climbing or wilderness expeditions, incorporating physiological data (e.g., fatigue thresholds) and environmental inputs from real-time satellite datasets. ML algorithms will analyze historical incident reports and instructor evaluations to identify latent risk factors and predict optimal intervention thresholds. Geospatial tools will map terrain-specific hazards and route viability under varying climatic conditions. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, we aim to generate probabilistic risk profiles and adaptive curriculum recommendations tailored to specific cohorts and ecosystems. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for outdoor educators to test scenarios virtually, reducing field trial risks while preserving the spontaneity essential to experiential learning. This work bridges computational social science, environmental informatics, and pedagogical theory, establishing a novel methodology for data-driven decision-making in non-traditional educational settings. The computational framework may also inform policy development for wilderness access management and contribute to broader discourse on human-environment interaction in education.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work as an educator, instructor or facilitator in parks, recreational facilities, camps and other outdoor settings. Includes instruction in leadership skills, wilderness survival skills, first aid, group processes, counseling techniques, environmental studies and instruction in recreational activities such as rock climbing, ropes courses, backpacking, kayaking and canoeing.

abstract: Healthcare systems face growing pressure to optimize operational efficiency amid dynamic patient influx, yet existing administrative frameworks often lack the computational tools to model complex, real-time decision-making scenarios. This project seeks to address the challenge of adaptive resource allocation in emergency departments (EDs) through the development of a machine learning-driven simulation platform. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train neural networks on multi-modal clinical and operational data—including patient triage logs, staff schedules, and equipment utilization patterns—to predict bottlenecks and simulate intervention outcomes. Agent-based modeling will be employed to represent interactions between patients, providers, and physical resources under varying demand scenarios, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize allocation strategies. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of heterogeneous datasets spanning millions of time-stamped ED events from three regional hospital networks, necessitating GPU-accelerated training and large-scale memory resources. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for identifying critical inflection points in ED throughput and evidence-based protocols for dynamic staff redeployment and inventory management. By integrating operational research with clinical informatics, this work aims to establish a novel computational paradigm for healthcare administration that balances efficiency metrics with patient care quality indicators. Successful implementation could reduce average wait times by 15-25% in pilot sites while providing generalizable methods for real-time resource optimization in complex care environments. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC-enabled analytics in bridging gaps between frontline healthcare delivery and strategic administrative decision-making.
cip_title: Health and Medical Administrative Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of polypharmacology-driven drug interactions and their implications for therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. A critical challenge in pharmacology is predicting how drugs with multi-target effects—particularly those used in combination therapies—interact dynamically with biological systems to produce synergistic, additive, or antagonistic outcomes. Traditional experimental methods are limited in scalability and temporal resolution, especially when evaluating complex pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) relationships across diverse physiological conditions. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to map the behavior of multi-target drugs in heterogeneous biological environments. PBPK models will simulate drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) across virtual patient populations, while MD simulations will resolve atomistic interactions between drugs and off-target proteins implicated in adverse effects. ML algorithms, trained on curated datasets of drug-target affinities and clinical toxicity reports, will predict high-risk drug combinations and optimize dosing regimens. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale of simulations, which involve millions of atomic trajectories, and to process high-dimensional PK-PD datasets spanning genetic, metabolic, and demographic variables. Expected outcomes include predictive models for drug-drug and drug-protein interactions, identification of repurposable drugs with minimized polypharmacological risks, and actionable insights into personalized dosing strategies. This work will directly inform preclinical drug development and clinical trial design, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in therapeutic optimization. By prioritizing computational toxicology and pharmacodynamic profiling, the project aligns with the program’s focus on drug safety and mechanistic pharmacology while avoiding overlap with excluded biological subfields.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drug interactions on biological systems and organisms and the sources, chemical properties, biological effects, and therapeutic uses of drugs. Includes instruction in pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, drug therapeutics, drug action, bodily responses to drug events, biochemical proliferation and differentiation, apoptosis, cell biology, medicinal chemistry, and studies of specific drugs and drug interactions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and fabrication of complex 3-D printed structures with adaptive material properties, addressing challenges in precision, structural efficiency, and scalability. Current approaches to multi-material 3-D modeling struggle to balance high-resolution simulations with real-world manufacturability, particularly for applications requiring dynamic responses to environmental stimuli (e.g., temperature, load). To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-scale, multi-physics simulations that integrate finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven topology optimization. The computational workflow will model material behavior at microstructural levels while maintaining macro-scale performance targets, with iterative feedback between simulated outcomes and experimental 3-D printing parameters. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated lattice generation algorithms and neural networks trained on coupled thermal-mechanical datasets to predict deformation patterns in functionally graded materials. Expected outcomes include validated digital twins for 3-D printed components in aerospace and biomedical contexts, reducing prototyping iterations by 40-60% through predictive simulation. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the project's computational demands, including parallel processing of billion-element meshes, distributed training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, and real-time rendering of high-precision 3-D models for virtual testing environments. Successful implementation will advance the integration of computational design with additive manufacturing, enabling resource-efficient production of customized, performance-optimized structures while establishing a scalable platform for future research in smart material systems. This work will directly support curriculum development in advanced 3-D modeling courses, providing students with access to cutting-edge computational tools and datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing hydrocarbon recovery from complex subsurface reservoirs by leveraging advanced computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Conventional reservoir simulation tools often struggle to accurately capture the multiphase fluid dynamics, heterogeneous geological properties, and coupled thermal-hydro-mechanical processes inherent in unconventional oil and gas formations. This limitation hinders the design of efficient enhanced oil recovery (EOR) strategies, particularly in low-permeability reservoirs where marginal gains in extraction efficiency have significant economic and operational implications. To overcome these barriers, this project will develop a high-fidelity, multi-scale reservoir simulator integrating machine learning-assisted parameterization of fracture networks, dynamic fluid-rock interaction models, and uncertainty quantification frameworks. The computational workflow will employ finite volume methods for solving governing equations of multiphase flow, coupled with graph neural networks to model fracture propagation and fluid pathways at the meter-to-micron scale. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across diverse geological scenarios, utilizing petrophysical data from target formations in the Permian Basin as case studies. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for evaluating EOR techniques (e.g., CO₂ injection, surfactant flooding) under realistic operational constraints, with particular emphasis on optimizing energy-water-carbon tradeoffs. The resulting models will provide actionable insights for field development planning while advancing fundamental understanding of coupled processes in fractured porous media. By achieving grid resolutions below 1 meter across kilometer-scale domains—computationally infeasible on conventional systems—this work will establish new benchmarks for reservoir simulation fidelity. Successful implementation will directly support petroleum technology innovation through improved recovery forecasts, reduced environmental footprint of extraction operations, and enhanced decision-making tools for subsurface engineers. The project will additionally generate open-source modules for reservoir characterization, fostering collaboration across petroleum technology and computational geoscience communities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of oil and natural gas extraction and processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of petroleum extraction and related geology, petroleum field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, laboratory analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, environment and safety monitoring procedures for oil/gas fields and facilities, facility inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven strategies for improving school counseling interventions that address systemic inequities in student mental health and academic outcomes. School counselors face growing challenges in identifying at-risk students and tailoring support within diverse K–12 populations, yet existing tools often rely on static, small-scale datasets that fail to capture complex, intersecting factors such as socioeconomic barriers, cultural dynamics, and longitudinal behavioral trends. To address this, our interdisciplinary team will analyze multi-year, de-identified student records—including academic performance, attendance, disciplinary incidents, and anonymized counselor notes—from urban and rural school districts. Using natural language processing (NLP), we will extract insights from unstructured counselor narratives to quantify the efficacy of specific therapeutic approaches. Concurrently, graph neural networks (GNNs) will model student support networks and their impact on resilience metrics, while reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms will simulate intervention pathways optimized for equitable resource allocation. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model training, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks to prioritize students needing proactive support, (2) actionable benchmarks for culturally responsive counseling practices, and (3) open-source tools to help counselors visualize intervention trade-offs in real time. By integrating computational social science with counselor education, this work aims to transform how training programs prepare practitioners to address inequities through scalable, evidence-based strategies. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with state education agencies and the American School Counselor Association to maximize translational impact.
cip_title: Counselor Education/ School Counseling and Guidance Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the theory and principles of guidance and counseling to the provision of support for the personal, social, educational, and vocational development of students, and the organizing of guidance services within elementary, middle and secondary educational institutions. Includes instruction in legal and professional requirements, therapeutic counselor intervention, vocational counseling, and related sociological and psychological foundations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate genomic prediction and optimization of complex traits in agricultural and horticultural crops. Traditional plant breeding approaches face challenges in efficiently integrating multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, and phenomic) to predict genotype-environment interactions and identify optimal genetic combinations for stress resilience and yield improvement. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in analyzing large-scale genomic data from diverse plant populations, which limits the speed and precision of marker-assisted selection and genomic selection pipelines. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with machine learning models to identify key genetic markers and epistatic interactions linked to drought tolerance and disease resistance in staple crops. High-dimensional genomic datasets from wheat and tomato breeding lines will be analyzed using distributed computing workflows to train deep neural networks for trait prediction, coupled with evolutionary algorithms to simulate selective breeding outcomes under varying environmental scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale sequencing data, reduce runtime for iterative model training, and facilitate large-scale simulations of crop populations across virtual agroclimatic zones. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for genomic selection prioritization, validated predictive models for trait heritability, and optimized breeding strategies for releasing climate-resilient cultivars. By reducing computational constraints, this project aims to shorten breeding cycles by up to 40% compared to conventional methods, directly supporting food security goals. The resources will also enhance training for graduate students in computational plant breeding, bridging gaps between agricultural genomics and data science. All tools and datasets will be shared via public repositories to advance collaborative innovation in crop improvement.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural plant health, the development of new plant varieties, and the selective improvement of agricultural plant populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, agronomy, plant protection, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in the creation and analysis of large-scale, dynamic visual communication systems. As digital media complexity grows—driven by demands for real-time interactivity, high-resolution rendering, and adaptive user experiences—traditional design workflows struggle to efficiently process multimodal datasets or simulate user interactions at scale. The research focuses on optimizing generative design algorithms and immersive environment simulations, which require parallelized computation to handle iterative prototyping, 3D scene synthesis, and AI-driven aesthetic evaluation. Key computational tasks include training machine learning models for automated layout optimization, rendering photorealistic previews of interactive media, and simulating crowd-sourced visual perception data across diverse demographic parameters. These processes demand significant GPU capacity, distributed memory systems, and fast inter-node communication to reduce latency in feedback loops between design iteration and user testing. Outcomes will advance methodologies for data-driven visual storytelling, enabling designers to rapidly prototype accessible, user-centric interfaces and dynamic branding systems. The project also aims to establish scalable frameworks for evaluating aesthetic impact and usability in virtual environments, with applications in augmented reality (AR) advertising, educational media, and digital product visualization. By integrating HPC into visual communication pipelines, this work bridges gaps between computational efficiency and creative experimentation, offering new tools for cross-disciplinary collaboration in media design. Resource allocation will directly support benchmarking studies, open-source tool development, and the creation of a public repository of optimized design templates validated through computational experimentation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that focuses on the general principles and techniques for effectively communicating ideas and information, and packaging products, in digital and other formats to business and consumer audiences, and that may prepare individuals in any of the applied art media.

abstract: Neurodevelopmental disabilities (NDDs) in children, including autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, and genetic syndromes, present complex, heterogeneous challenges requiring personalized interventions. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies are limited by an incomplete understanding of the interplay between genetic, neuroimaging, and behavioral data. This project seeks to address these gaps by integrating multi-modal datasets to identify biomarkers and predictive models of treatment response. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic sequences, functional MRI (fMRI) data, and longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) from a cohort of 2,000 children with NDDs. Key computational challenges include processing high-dimensional neuroimaging data (≈50 TB), performing genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with rare variant analysis, and training machine learning models to link dynamic behavioral trajectories to neurobiological features. The proposed workflow involves cloud-based preprocessing of fMRI using containerized pipelines (e.g., FMRIPREP), distributed computing for parallelized genomic analyses (PLINK2, REGENIE), and GPU-accelerated deep learning (PyTorch) to develop multimodal predictive frameworks. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of novel neurodevelopmental subtypes based on integrated genetic-functional brain networks, (2) predictive algorithms for motor or cognitive outcomes in cerebral palsy and autism, and (3) open-source tools for EHR-derived behavioral phenotyping. By clarifying mechanisms underlying treatment variability, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches for NDDs. The scale of data harmonization and model training necessitates HPC capabilities, as baseline tests on a 500-subject subset required 12,000 CPU-hours and 4 TB of memory for preliminary analyses. Successfully linking multi-omics, neuroimaging, and real-world clinical data at this scale will provide a template for computationally intensive translational research in pediatric neurodevelopment.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat children having developmental delays or learning disorders, including those associated with visual and hearing impairment, developmental delays, cerebral palsy, spina bifida, autism, and other chronic neurologic conditions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic performance environments in live theater through computational modeling of spatial, acoustic, and temporal interactions. The central challenge lies in analyzing how complex variables—such as actor movement trajectories, audience positioning, and reverberation patterns—collectively shape emergent perceptual experiences that defy traditional linear analysis. Current methods in theater studies lack the capacity to simulate these multidimensional relationships at scale, particularly when accounting for real-world constraints like irregular venue architectures or adaptive lighting systems. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models that integrate motion-capture data from rehearsals, acoustic propagation algorithms tailored to historic theater spaces, and machine learning techniques to identify non-obvious correlations between staging choices and audience response metrics. The computational workflow will require parallelized processing to manage high-resolution spatial datasets (3D lidar scans of performance venues) and real-time acoustic simulations across variable audience sizes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing sightline equity in nontraditional staging configurations, dynamic acoustic profiling for understudied regional theaters, and generative models that propose staging adaptations based on historical performance archives. By enabling systematic investigation of nonlinear interactions in theatrical environments, this work aims to establish new methodologies for evidence-based stagecraft while preserving the ephemeral art form’s material history through digital twin technologies. The requested HPC allocation is critical for scaling simulations beyond single-scene analyses, with projected computations exceeding 10,000 core-hours to model full productions across multiple venue types.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Dramatic/ Theatre Arts and Stagecraft, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dramatic/theatre arts and stagecraft, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding and mitigating disparities in access to allied health services across diverse populations. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies and inequities in healthcare delivery systems, particularly in underserved regions, where complex interactions between socio-economic, geographic, and clinical factors limit timely access to care. Current analytical approaches often oversimplify these multidimensional challenges, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and intervention strategies. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), geospatial data, and socio-demographic datasets to model the dynamics of healthcare access and utilization. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be employed to identify predictive patterns of service gaps and simulate the impact of targeted interventions. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale datasets, training high-dimensional models, and running iterative simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime and accuracy. Expected outcomes include the development of a scalable, open-source tool for health systems to prioritize resource distribution, optimize staffing models, and forecast demand for allied health services. By elucidating the interplay of systemic barriers, this work aims to advance health equity while providing a methodological blueprint for data-driven decision-making in public health. The project also aligns with pedagogical goals by creating training modules for health sciences students in computational epidemiology and resource modeling, fostering interdisciplinary skills at the intersection of healthcare and data science. Outcomes will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and collaborations with regional health networks to validate models in real-world settings, ensuring translational impact.
cip_title: Health Services/ Allied Health/ Health Sciences, General
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health services occupations that prepares individuals for either entry into specialized training programs or for a variety of concentrations in the allied health area. Includes instruction in the basic sciences, research and clinical procedures, and aspects of the subject matter related to various health occupations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing acoustofluidic systems, an emerging interdisciplinary niche combining fluid dynamics, acoustics, and microfabrication to enable precise manipulation of microscale particles and fluids via sound waves. Current acoustofluidic device designs face challenges in scalability and efficiency due to the complex interplay of acoustic forces, viscous effects, and geometric constraints, which are difficult to model with conventional experimental or low-fidelity computational tools. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multiphysics interactions at unprecedented resolution, enabling predictive design of next-generation devices. The computational approach integrates finite element modeling (FEM) and lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) to capture high-frequency acoustic wave propagation, fluid-structure interactions, and particle trajectories in three-dimensional geometries. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate parameter optimization, targeting applications in advanced manufacturing, such as non-contact microassembly or pharmaceutical encapsulation. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for large-scale parallel simulations and parameter sweeps, requiring over 500,000 core-hours to resolve multiscale phenomena across relevant spatial (µm–mm) and temporal (ns–ms) regimes. Expected outcomes include validated open-source simulation tools, generalized design principles for acoustofluidic systems, and demonstration of a novel device configuration capable of manipulating sub-10 µm particles with >90% efficiency. This work will advance the engineering of acoustofluidic technologies by bridging gaps between theoretical models and real-world performance, with potential translational impacts in microfluidics, lab-on-a-chip systems, and smart materials processing. By addressing computational bottlenecks in modeling wave-matter interactions, the project also contributes methodological innovations to the broader engineering community working on multiphysics problems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Vascular and Interventional Radiology (VIR) relies on minimally invasive, image-guided therapies to treat complex conditions, yet challenges persist in optimizing procedural efficacy and reducing complications. Current limitations stem from the inability to model dynamic, patient-specific interactions between vascular anatomy, medical devices (e.g., stents, catheters), and physiological parameters in real time. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate these interactions, enabling predictive analytics for procedural planning and device optimization. The research will integrate patient imaging data (CT, MRI, fluoroscopy) with biomechanical and hemodynamic simulations to analyze device-tissue interactions under diverse anatomical and pathological conditions. Key computational methods include fluid-structure interaction (FSI) modeling to assess blood flow and device deformation, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain predictions in vascular walls, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to correlate simulation outputs with clinical outcomes from retrospective procedural datasets. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution imaging inputs, execute parallelized simulations across thousands of vascular geometries, and train ML models on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for stent migration risk, embolization efficacy, and post-procedural thrombosis, (2) a computational framework to guide personalized device selection, and (3) open-source tools for simulating image-guided therapies. By bridging computational engineering and clinical VIR practice, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error approaches in interventions, improve patient safety, and establish a foundation for AI-driven procedural innovations. The requested computing allocation will directly support time-sensitive simulations critical for upcoming clinical validation studies and grant applications targeting NIH R01 funding.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists with additional training in image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing the design and operational efficiency of next-generation power electronics systems, with a focus on applications in renewable energy integration and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Current limitations in device-level thermal management and system-wide energy loss prediction hinder the reliability and performance of high-power converters, particularly under dynamic load conditions. To address this, we propose a hybrid simulation approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) for component-level electrothermal modeling with system-level neural network surrogates trained on multiphysics datasets. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute parallelized 3D FEA simulations across diverse material configurations and switching frequencies, generating training data for physics-informed graph neural networks. Key computational challenges include resolving microsecond-scale transient behaviors in wide-bandgap semiconductor devices while maintaining system-scale simulation fidelity across thousands of interconnected components. The proposed workflow will utilize MPI-based domain decomposition for distributed FEA computations and GPU-accelerated training of neural operators to predict thermal hotspots and harmonic distortions under real-world operating profiles. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for power electronics co-design and validated performance benchmarks for gallium nitride-based converter topologies. This work will directly support the development of more compact, efficient power conversion systems critical for decarbonization infrastructure, while advancing computational methods applicable to coupled electrothermal-aging phenomena in power electronics. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the memory-intensive multiscale simulations and achieving statistically significant results across the target parameter space within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronic engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for the documentation and analysis of under-resourced Turkic, Uralic-Altaic, Caucasian, and Central Asian languages, many of which face endangerment or lack robust digital tools. The research problem centers on the challenges of modeling complex morphological structures and dialectal variations in these languages, which are characterized by agglutinative morphology, vowel harmony, and intricate syntactic features. Traditional methods struggle to process large-scale corpora or generate accurate computational models due to resource constraints, hindering efforts to preserve linguistic diversity and advance typological studies. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining parallelized corpus analysis, neural machine translation (NMT) tailored for low-resource languages, and phylogenetic algorithms to trace historical linguistic relationships. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing digitized texts and audio recordings (including legacy field notes and contemporary speech samples) using GPU-accelerated pipelines, training transformer-based models on distributed clusters to handle morphological segmentation and syntactic parsing, and simulating language evolution patterns across Altaic and Caucasian subgroups. Expected outcomes include open-access computational lexicons, dialect maps, and machine-readable grammars for five focus languages (e.g., Tuvan, Udmurt, and Georgian Mingrelian), as well as a comparative framework for evaluating areal linguistic features. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive tasks such as probabilistic alignment of cognate sets. By enabling large-scale cross-linguistic analysis, this work will significantly advance theoretical understanding of language contact in Central Eurasia while providing practical tools for communities engaged in language revitalization. Results will be disseminated through an interactive platform for researchers and a workshop on computational methods for endangered language documentation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Turkic, Uralic-Altaic, Caucasian, and Central Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the Turkic, Uralic-Altaic, Caucasian, and Central Asian languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Fungal pathogens pose a significant threat to global health and food security, with rising antifungal resistance complicating treatment strategies. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding fungal pathogenesis and environmental drivers of resistance by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex host-fungus-environment interactions. Current experimental methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multiscale nature of these systems, particularly the interplay between fungal phenotypic plasticity, host immune evasion mechanisms, and variable environmental stressors. We propose a dual computational approach: (1) agent-based modeling of fungal growth and dissemination within host tissues, integrating empirical data on fungal morphogenesis, host histopathology, and antifungal pharmacokinetics; and (2) dynamic systems models simulating environmental selection pressures on antifungal resistance across ecological niches. These models will incorporate heterogeneous datasets spanning clinical isolates, soil microbiome compositions, and climatic variables to identify key predictors of treatment failure and resistance emergence. The scale of parameter space exploration—encompassing thousands of fungal strains, host conditions, and environmental scenarios—necessitates parallelized computing for sensitivity analyses and optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for resistance risk assessment, identification of high-risk environmental reservoirs for zoonotic pathogens, and mechanistic insights into fungal stress adaptation strategies. By elucidating context-dependent virulence factors, this work will directly inform surveillance priorities and antifungal stewardship programs. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations at biologically relevant spatiotemporal resolutions, which are computationally prohibitive on standard infrastructure, advancing both fundamental mycology and translational applications in clinical and agricultural settings.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of fungi, lichenous plants, eukaryotic microorganisms, myxomycetes, and plasmodiophorales and their relationship to diseases in higher plants, animals, and human beings as well as to pharmacologically useful products. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; histopathology; fungal growth and behavior; environmental mycology; antifungal sensitivity; mycoses; pathogens and pathogenesis; pharmacological properties; and computer and laboratory research methods.

abstract: Vocational rehabilitation counseling aims to optimize outcomes for individuals with disabilities through personalized interventions, yet current methods for job matching and intervention planning often rely on static, population-level data. This project addresses the critical need for dynamic, individualized decision-support tools that integrate real-time client data, labor market trends, and longitudinal health metrics. We propose developing machine learning models to predict vocational success and simulate intervention scenarios using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will utilize anonymized client records (e.g., functional assessments, employment histories) and regional labor datasets to train natural language processing models for extracting psychosocial factors from clinical notes, graph neural networks to model client-service provider interactions, and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize multi-step rehabilitation plans. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional data from 50,000+ client cases, managing temporal dependencies in longitudinal outcomes, and conducting sensitivity analyses across diverse disability subgroups. HPC resources are essential for parallelized hyperparameter tuning of deep learning architectures, large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of intervention pathways, and real-time optimization of resource allocation strategies under constrained clinical settings. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework identifying clients at risk of vocational discontinuation, (2) evidence-based thresholds for adjusting counseling frequency based on biomarker trends, and (3) open-source tools for simulating the systemic impacts of policy changes on employment equity. By enabling granular analysis of complex client-environment interactions, this work will advance precision rehabilitation practices while maintaining rigorous ethical standards through embedded model auditing protocols. The computational infrastructure developed will directly support 15+ ongoing studies on disability-inclusive workforce development, creating a scalable resource for the vocational rehabilitation research community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel and assist disabled individuals and recovering patients in order to achieve their greatest physical, mental, social, educational, and vocational potential. Includes instruction in patient evaluation and testing, rehabilitation program planning, patient support services and referral, job analysis, adjustment psychology, rehabilitation services provision, patient counseling and education, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Maritime environments face unprecedented challenges from climate change, geopolitical shifts, and increasing human activity. This project addresses the urgent need to model the complex interactions between environmental change and maritime policy in the Arctic region, where melting sea ice is opening new shipping routes with significant economic, ecological, and security implications. Traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to integrate large-scale oceanographic data, historical shipping patterns, and policy frameworks, necessitating advanced computational approaches. This research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a coupled modeling system that simulates ice melt dynamics, projects future shipping traffic using machine learning algorithms, and assesses environmental risks such as oil spills and habitat disruption. By synthesizing satellite-derived sea ice data, historical vessel tracking records, and regulatory databases, the project will generate high-resolution simulations to evaluate policy scenarios under varying climate trajectories. The computational workflow leverages parallel processing to manage petabytes of heterogeneous data and employs agent-based modeling to capture the decision-making processes of maritime stakeholders. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for policymakers to balance economic opportunities with environmental preservation, a publicly accessible database of Arctic maritime scenarios, and novel methodologies for interdisciplinary maritime research. This work will advance the understanding of feedback loops between human activities and marine ecosystems, providing a foundation for evidence-based governance in a rapidly changing region of global strategic importance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, science, policy issues, and literature of the ocean. Includes instruction in maritime history, maritime law, maritime literature, oceanography, maritime security, and maritime politics.

abstract: Cardiovascular complications in cancer patients, particularly those undergoing radiation or chemotherapy, represent a critical yet underexplored intersection of cardiovascular physiology and oncology.
