This project seeks to model the multiscale mechanisms by which anti-cancer therapies disrupt cardiac and vascular homeostasis, with a focus on chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity and radiation-associated microvascular dysfunction. Current experimental models struggle to capture the dynamic interplay between systemic drug distribution, tissue-specific metabolic stress, and adaptive cellular responses. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating hemodynamic simulations at the organ level with agent-based models of cardiomyocyte and endothelial cell behavior under therapy-induced oxidative stress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatiotemporal variations in drug diffusion, oxygen radical production, and calcium handling across millions of cardiac cells while accounting for patient-specific vascular geometries derived from clinical imaging. The model will incorporate time-resolved MRI data from breast cancer and lymphoma cohorts to parameterize systemic circulation and regional perfusion changes. Machine learning pipelines will identify patterns in clinical datasets linking therapy regimens to early electrophysiological biomarkers of dysfunction. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of cardiotoxicity risk based on treatment protocols, vascular topology, and metabolic profiles, enabling personalized dose optimization. This work will advance understanding of how cancer therapies perturb cardiovascular resilience at subcellular to systemic scales, with direct implications for mitigating heart failure in oncology patients. The computational platform will also serve as a community resource for testing interventions targeting microvascular permeability, neural regulation of cardiac output, and mitochondrial adaptation—key pathways in cardiovascular-oncology research. Successful execution requires large-scale parallelization of coupled differential equations governing ion transport, fluid dynamics, and cellular energetics, necessitating dedicated HPC allocation for GPU-accelerated simulations and high-memory node utilization.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate cross-cultural literary dynamics through computational analysis of multilingual textual corpora, with a focus on understudied interactions between 20th-century Arabic, Chinese, and Russian modernist movements. While traditional comparative methods have identified thematic parallels across these traditions, the scale and linguistic complexity of primary sources—including novels, poetry, and critical essays in their original languages—have hindered systematic analysis of stylistic evolution and transnational influence networks. To address this gap, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) and graph-theoretical models on high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure to process approximately 15,000 digitized texts (25TB) spanning Arabic, Mandarin, and Russian. Computational workflows will integrate transformer-based multilingual embeddings (e.g., BERT variants) for cross-lingual semantic alignment, combined with stylometric feature extraction at scale. Network analysis modules will map citation patterns and lexical innovation transfer across authors and regions, while unsupervised clustering methods will detect emergent thematic shifts tied to historical exchange events. A critical technical challenge involves optimizing OCR post-correction pipelines for diverse non-Latin scripts under noise conditions typical of archival materials. The project’s computational outcomes—including an open-source framework for multilingual literary network analysis—will advance understanding of how decentralized modernist movements developed shared aesthetic strategies despite linguistic and geopolitical barriers. By enabling pattern detection across previously inaccessible corpora, this research will provide new models for studying global literary modernity while demonstrating scalable digital humanities methodologies for non-Anglophone traditions. Resource requests emphasize GPU nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory nodes for large-scale graph computations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern engineering systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in multi-system integration, design optimization, and performance validation. This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing the coordination of heterogeneous systems in large-scale engineering applications, such as renewable energy microgrids or autonomous vehicle networks. Current approaches often rely on compartmentalized simulations that inadequately capture interdependencies between mechanical, electrical, and control subsystems, leading to suboptimal designs and costly iterative prototyping. To overcome these limitations, the research will implement coupled multi-physics simulations using finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, and agent-based modeling integrated through a unified optimization pipeline. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to manage the computational intensity of these multi-scale simulations, which involve millions of degrees of freedom and require iterative evaluations across conflicting design objectives. The proposed workflow will leverage parallelized evolutionary algorithms and gradient-based optimization methods to navigate high-dimensional parameter spaces while maintaining physical constraints. A key innovation involves implementing adaptive mesh refinement and reduced-order modeling techniques to balance accuracy with computational efficiency during exploratory design phases. The research will validate results against experimental data from collaborating industry partners in two case studies: 1) thermal-structural optimization of concentrated solar power receivers, and 2) resilience analysis of distributed sensor networks for smart infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly available library of modular simulation components, quantitative benchmarks for system integration efficiency, and design guidelines for managing requirement conflicts in cyber-physical systems. The broader impact lies in enabling computationally tractable exploration of novel engineering architectures that harmonize traditionally incompatible subsystems, potentially reducing development cycles by 30-50% in cross-domain design challenges. This work will establish methodological foundations for next-generation engineering design tools capable of handling exponentially growing system complexity through targeted HPC utilization.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to engineering problems involving marrying or coordinating multiple dissimilar systems to carry out single functions or achieve common purposes, organizing system components for maximum flexibility and utility, planning engineering projects involving multiple tasks and design solutions, planning design testing and evaluation procedures, resolving specification and requirement conflicts, and choosing among competing theoretical solutions. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 14.2901.

abstract: Medical imaging technologies, such as x-ray, ultrasound, and electromagnetic radiation-based modalities, generate increasingly complex, high-dimensional datasets that challenge conventional computational resources. This project seeks to develop advanced image reconstruction and analysis pipelines for diagnostic radiology, with a focus on optimizing real-time processing of multi-modal imaging data while minimizing radiation exposure and artifacts. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in dynamic, image-guided interventions, where latency in processing high-resolution 3D/4D datasets can impact diagnostic accuracy and treatment outcomes. We propose a hybrid high-performance computing (HPC) approach combining GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures for noise reduction and resolution enhancement with Monte Carlo simulations of radiation-tissue interactions. The computational workflows will integrate adaptive neural networks trained on heterogeneous clinical imaging data (CT, MRI, PET) to enable cross-modal feature extraction and anomaly detection. Resource-intensive components include large-scale optimization of inverse problems in limited-angle tomography, parallelized finite-difference time-domain modeling of electromagnetic wave propagation in anatomical structures, and patient-specific dosimetry calculations for interventional radiology protocols. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of physics-informed machine learning models through distributed training across multiple nodes, leveraging containerized workflows for reproducibility. Expected outcomes include: 1) clinically validated algorithms for dose reduction in pediatric CT protocols without loss of diagnostic quality, 2) automated tools for artifact correction in MRI-guided focused ultrasound therapies, and 3) open-source frameworks for real-time multi-modal image fusion in interventional radiology suites. This work will directly address computational barriers to precision imaging in oncology, neurology, and cardiovascular disease management, with particular emphasis on translating validated models into clinical trial pipelines through containerized deployment in hospital HPC environments.
cip_definition: Research on how to utilize x-ray, ionizing radiation, radionuclides, ultrasound, electromagnetic radiation, and image-guided intervention to diagnose and treat disease. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: Healthcare facilities face increasing challenges in managing patient flow, resource allocation, and administrative efficiency, particularly in dynamic clinical environments. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize ward coordination tasks—such as scheduling, resource distribution, and real-time communication—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies inherent in manual or siloed systems for managing patient admissions, procedure scheduling, and staff-task alignment, which contribute to delays, errors, and suboptimal resource utilization. Current approaches often lack predictive capabilities and adaptability to fluctuating demands. This project proposes a hybrid computational model integrating machine learning (ML) for demand forecasting, agent-based simulations to model patient-staff interactions, and natural language processing (NLP) to automate the transcription and prioritization of medical orders. HPC resources are critical for training ML models on large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets, running parallelized simulations of ward operations under diverse scenarios, and processing real-time data streams from hospital communication systems. The computational pipeline will utilize anonymized EHRs, historical admission logs, and simulated emergency scenarios to validate model robustness. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for patient admission surges, dynamic scheduling algorithms to reduce procedural wait times, and NLP-driven error reduction in order transcription. These tools aim to enhance operational efficiency, minimize administrative burdens on clinical staff, and improve patient outcomes through timely care delivery. The results will inform scalable protocols for health unit coordinators and contribute open-source modules for task automation in healthcare education programs. By addressing computational gaps in ward management, this project aligns with broader efforts to modernize healthcare administration through data-driven decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving cultural and spatial dynamics of Indigenous storytelling traditions within the Pacific Northwest’s coastal regions. The study addresses a critical gap in regional studies by examining how oral histories, documented in multilingual archives (including Indigenous languages, English, and French), intersect with environmental and socio-cultural changes over the past two centuries. Existing methodologies struggle to process the scale and complexity of these heterogeneous datasets, which include digitized oral recordings, ethnographic field notes, and georeferenced ecological records. To overcome these challenges, the project employs a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text and audio analysis, geospatial machine learning to map narrative motifs against environmental shifts, and network models to trace the diffusion of stories across communities. HPC resources are essential to train transformer-based NLP models on low-resource Indigenous languages, process high-resolution spatial data correlating storytelling sites with hydrological changes, and simulate network interactions at scale. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas visualizing story pathways and environmental pressures, alongside computational tools adaptable to other multilingual, place-based cultural analyses. This work will advance scholarly understanding of how Indigenous narratives encode adaptive knowledge, offering insights for cultural preservation initiatives and cross-regional comparative studies. By centering computational scalability and interdisciplinary data integration, the project aims to establish a replicable model for analyzing cultural resilience in geographically bounded communities, directly contributing to the regional studies field’s capacity to bridge humanities-driven inquiry with data-intensive methodologies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the defined geographic subregions and subcultures within modern and historical countries and societies. Includes such topics as Acadian Studies, French Canadian and Quebec Studies, Southern (U.S.) Studies, New England Studies, Southwestern Studies, Northern Studies, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of quantifying and optimizing movement therapy interventions through advanced computational modeling of neuromuscular and biomechanical processes. Movement therapy relies on nuanced, individualized interactions between practitioners and clients to enhance somatic awareness and functional movement patterns. However, current methods for assessing therapeutic efficacy remain largely qualitative, limiting scalability and evidence-based refinement of techniques. We propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework to model neuromuscular responses to therapeutic touch and guided movement, integrating motion capture data, electromyography (EMG), and pressure sensor inputs from clinical sessions. High-performance computing resources will enable the creation of multi-scale models that correlate external biomechanical forces with internal tissue strain, proprioceptive feedback, and cortical activation patterns derived from existing neuroimaging datasets. Machine learning approaches will identify critical kinematic and temporal features predictive of therapeutic outcomes across diverse populations, including individuals with chronic pain or movement disorders. The computational pipeline will also simulate hypothetical intervention scenarios to test mechanistic hypotheses about sensorimotor integration during therapy. By bridging embodied therapeutic practices with systems biology and computational neuroscience, this work aims to establish predictive biomarkers for treatment efficacy, inform personalized intervention protocols, and generate open-access tools for movement educators. Expected outcomes include a novel ontology for classifying movement therapy modalities based on computational signatures and a proof-of-concept platform for virtual therapy prototyping. This interdisciplinary approach advances the scientific rigor of somatic practices while preserving their human-centered ethos, offering new pathways to validate and innovate within movement-based therapeutic traditions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use functional and expressive integration strategies to help promote somatic awareness and optimal psychophysical functioning. Includes instruction in skilled touch techniques, kinesthetic awareness processes, movement observation, patterning, client assessment and guidance, verbal and nonverbal communication, practice management, professional standards and ethics, and specific therapeutic and educational modalities

abstract: Sustainable forest management requires balancing timber production with ecological conservation, a challenge exacerbated by climate variability, shifting species distributions, and complex socio-economic demands. Current models for optimizing harvest schedules, predicting growth yields, and assessing ecological impacts lack the resolution and integration needed to address these multidimensional factors at landscape scales. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate forest growth, harvesting operations, and long-term sustainability outcomes under dynamic environmental and management scenarios. The research will integrate remote sensing data, machine learning-driven species distribution models, and agent-based simulations of harvesting workflows to quantify trade-offs between production efficiency, carbon sequestration, and biodiversity preservation. Computational workflows will process multi-terabyte LiDAR and hyperspectral datasets to parameterize forest structure and health metrics, while parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will evaluate millions of potential harvest strategies across synthetic and real-world forest landscapes in the Pacific Northwest. Key innovations include coupling discrete-event logging system models with ecophysiological growth projections, enabling fine-grained analysis of how equipment selection, road networks, and processing technologies influence both economic returns and ecosystem resilience. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive spatial analyses, reducing runtime for iterative optimization algorithms, and scaling validation across heterogeneous forest types. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools that enable stakeholders to visualize trade-offs in near-real time, prioritize climate-adaptive silviculture practices, and mitigate habitat fragmentation risks. By bridging industrial forestry operations with ecological forecasting, this work aims to establish computationally rigorous protocols for sustainable resource allocation in working forests under 21st-century environmental uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of forestry principles to the production, harvesting, and processing of forest resources and that prepares individuals to perform associated technical and managerial functions. Includes instruction in forest production and utilization, industrial forestry, agroforestry, transplantation, timber harvesting, selection and identification of trees, processing technologies and systems, equipment operations and maintenance, and related management skills.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing concrete mixtures and finishing techniques to meet evolving demands for durability, sustainability, and cost efficiency. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to material formulation and structural performance analysis are resource-intensive and fail to account for the complex, multiscale interactions between concrete components, environmental conditions, and mechanical stresses. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive computational models that simulate concrete behavior from molecular interactions to macroscopic structural performance. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will model the hydration kinetics of cementitious materials, aggregate distribution, and crack propagation under varying thermal and load conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on experimental datasets—including compressive strength tests, rheology measurements, and environmental exposure trials—to identify correlations between mix design parameters (e.g., water-cement ratio, additive concentrations, curing time) and performance outcomes. These models will enable parametric optimization of concrete formulations for specific climates and structural applications, reducing material waste and energy consumption. HPC resources are critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelizing multiscale simulations, and processing hyperspectral imaging data of curing processes. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for concrete finishing workflows, open-access predictive tools for mix design optimization, and novel insights into the role of nanoscale additives in enhancing durability. By integrating computational advancements with applied concrete technology, this research will directly support workforce training initiatives in the Concrete Finisher program, equipping students with data-driven methodologies to advance sustainable construction practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to prepare, construct, and finish buildings, components, and related structures using compound masonry mixtures of stone, gravel, sand, cement, and water. Includes instruction in site preparation, applied mathematics, mixing formulas and applications, job estimation, concrete design, finishing techniques, mold preparation, reinforcement installation, site safety, and equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation relies on the precise integration of biomechanical principles with patient-specific anatomical and functional demands. However, current computational models for simulating the biomechanical behavior of dental implants, prostheses, and associated tissues lack the resolution to predict long-term performance under dynamic physiological conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing multiscale, patient-specific computational models to optimize prosthodontic device design and treatment planning. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform finite element analysis (FEA) of stress distribution in bone-implant systems, molecular dynamics simulations of interfacial interactions between implant surfaces and biological tissues, and machine learning-driven predictive modeling of clinical outcomes. Key challenges include modeling the heterogeneous viscoelastic properties of bone and soft tissues, simulating micro-scale osseointegration processes, and integrating real-world data from intraoral scans, CBCT imaging, and occlusal force sensors. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across multiple spatial and temporal scales, significantly reducing computational bottlenecks inherent in conventional single-node systems. Expected outcomes include (1) validated computational frameworks for predicting biomechanical failure risks in implant-supported prostheses, (2) optimized surface topography designs for enhanced osseointegration in compromised bone conditions, and (3) AI-driven treatment planning algorithms that account for patient-specific factors such as bone density, occlusal patterns, and systemic health parameters. This work will provide novel insights into the mechanobiological principles governing prosthodontic success while establishing scalable computational workflows for personalized restorative dentistry. The resulting tools aim to reduce prosthetic complications, improve functional and aesthetic outcomes, and inform evidence-based clinical guidelines—advancing the field toward data-driven, precision prosthodontics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the restoration and maintenance of teeth, oral function, and aesthetic form through the use of single or compound materials, structures, and artificial devices. Includes instruction in implant dentistry, surgical procedures, denture design and fabrication, fixed and removable prosthodontics, restorative techniques, occlusion therapy and devices, geriatric dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

abstract: Genetic counseling faces a critical challenge in accurately interpreting complex genomic data to assess disease risk and guide patient decisions. Current clinical tools often rely on simplified models that prioritize single-gene or panel-based analyses, neglecting the cumulative effects of structural variants, epigenetic modifiers, and polygenic interactions. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to integrate multi-omics data—including whole-genome sequencing, methylation profiles, and chromatin accessibility data—with clinical histories to improve risk prediction for hereditary conditions such as cardiomyopathies and neurodevelopmental disorders. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale genomic datasets from diverse populations, train ensemble models to identify combinatorial genetic and epigenetic risk factors, and simulate population-specific variant penetrance. Computational workflows will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, GPU-accelerated deep learning for feature selection, and distributed computing for genome-wide association meta-analyses. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model that quantifies multifactorial risk with higher precision than existing clinical tools, (2) identification of novel regulatory elements or structural variants contributing to variable expressivity in understudied populations, and (3) an open-access decision-support toolkit for genetic counselors to generate patient-specific risk visualizations. By bridging gaps between genomic complexity and clinical interpretability, this work aims to empower counselors to address inequities in variant interpretation, reduce diagnostic odysseys for rare diseases, and personalize preventive care recommendations. The HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the project’s computational demands, including petabyte-scale data storage, parallelized model training across >10,000 genomes, and real-time sensitivity analyses during patient consultations.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel patients and families concerning inherited genetic disorders and diseases; assess risk factors and planning options associated with potential and actual inherited conditions; and serve as patient advocates and provide referral services in relation to private and public support services. Includes instruction in clinical/medical genetics, methods of genetic testing, interviewing and counseling skills, genetic and support services delivery, principles of public health, medical ethics, law and regulations, patient advocacy, and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cognitive development, social-environmental factors, and neural maturation during adolescence using computational modeling approaches that require high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Adolescence is marked by dynamic, non-linear changes in decision-making, emotion regulation, and social cognition, but existing longitudinal studies often struggle to disentangle the temporal dependencies and multi-level interactions driving these processes. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate neurocognitive development under varying environmental conditions, informed by empirical data from a 5-year longitudinal cohort (n=1,200 adolescents, ages 12-17) assessing behavioral, fMRI, and ecological momentary assessment metrics. The ABM framework will incorporate reinforcement learning algorithms to model how individual differences in neural reward sensitivity interact with peer influence dynamics and family environment variables. A parallel computational pipeline will apply graph-based network analysis to resting-state fMRI data, examining how functional connectivity patterns predict developmental trajectories of risk-taking behavior. Given the combinatorial complexity of modeling thousands of interacting variables across developmental timepoints, HPC resources are essential for parameter space exploration, Monte Carlo simulations, and Bayesian network inference. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of computational signatures predicting transitions between developmental stages, (2) validation of mechanistic hypotheses about critical periods in social-cognitive development, and (3) open-source tools for simulating intervention effects on developmental pathways. This work will advance methodological innovation in developmental psychology by creating scalable frameworks to study emergent phenomena in adolescent development, while providing foundational insights into how multi-system interactions shape normative and atypical maturation processes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from adolescence to adulthood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in floral supply chain management and post-harvest flower quality degradation, critical challenges facing commercial floriculture enterprises. Despite advances in cold chain logistics, significant losses persist due to dynamic environmental factors, suboptimal storage protocols, and reactive delivery planning. We propose developing a computational framework integrating plant physiology models, real-time sensor data, and logistics optimization to minimize waste while maintaining floral product integrity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-modal datasets—including hyperspectral imaging of flower senescence patterns, regional climate forecasts, and transportation network variables—at operational scales. Machine learning models will predict species-specific vase life under diverse temperature and humidity regimes, while parallelized routing algorithms will optimize delivery schedules across fluctuating urban demand zones. A novel aspect involves coupling cellular-level metabolic simulations of cut flowers with macro-level supply chain dynamics, requiring iterative parameter tuning across biological and operational timescales. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support system for florists to simulate preservation strategies, automate climate-controlled routing, and forecast regional inventory needs. By quantifying trade-offs between energy use, transportation costs, and product quality at unprecedented resolution, this work aims to reduce post-harvest losses by 15–30% in modeled scenarios while maintaining profit margins. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a template for perishable agricultural supply chain optimization, with particular relevance to temperature-sensitive horticultural products. Successful implementation could transform floristry management practices through data-driven preservation protocols and responsive logistics, strengthening the economic and environmental sustainability of floral enterprises.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage commercial and contract florist enterprises, supply and delivery services, and flower catering services. Includes instruction in the applicable principles of plant science; purchasing, storage, and delivery systems; floral design and arranging; and principles of business management.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance and durable bicycles necessitates advanced methodologies to optimize design and maintenance protocols. Traditional approaches in bicycle mechanics rely heavily on empirical testing, which is resource-intensive and limits the exploration of innovative materials and geometries. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that simulate mechanical stresses, aerodynamic performance, and material behavior in bicycles. Key focus areas include finite element analysis (FEA) of frame and component integrity under dynamic loads, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to evaluate aerodynamic efficiency, and machine learning-driven optimization of spoke tension distribution in wheel building. These simulations will incorporate real-world data from sensor-equipped bicycles to validate models and predict wear patterns, enabling proactive maintenance strategies. The scale and complexity of multi-physics simulations—requiring simultaneous analysis of structural, fluid, and material interactions—demand HPC capabilities for parallel processing and large dataset management. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for component failure, optimized aerodynamic profiles for competitive cycling, and data-driven guidelines for wheel construction that enhance durability. By integrating computational insights with practical repair techniques, this research aims to bridge the gap between theoretical advancements and hands-on technician training, fostering innovation in bicycle technology. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular simulation tools, providing educational resources for technical programs focused on sustainable transportation solutions.
cip_title: Bicycle Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain bicycles and other human-powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication, adjustments of moving parts, and wheel building.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing emergent collective behaviors in decentralized information systems, with a focus on ethically aligned decision-making in multi-agent networks. The research addresses the challenge of modeling how large-scale, heterogeneous systems—such as distributed sensor networks or crowdsourced data platforms—achieve coherence without centralized control, particularly when ethical constraints (e.g., fairness, privacy, transparency) dynamically influence agent interactions. Current models often oversimplify ethical parameters as static inputs, neglecting their adaptive interplay with system-wide goals. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with mechanism design theory, implemented via high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate systems at unprecedented scale. Agent behaviors will be encoded using message-passing GNN architectures, while optimization processes will integrate game-theoretic principles to balance global efficiency with local ethical compliance. The computational workload involves iterative simulations across parameter spaces spanning network topologies, agent rationality models, and constraint violation penalties, necessitating GPU-accelerated parallel processing and distributed memory management. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable library for simulating ethical decision-making in decentralized systems, (2) quantitative metrics for trade-offs between ethical adherence and operational efficiency, and (3) identification of critical thresholds where system-wide ethical alignment emerges from local interactions. This work will provide foundational tools for designing responsible distributed AI systems in domains such as community-driven disaster response networks and privacy-preserving federated learning architectures, where traditional optimization frameworks fail to capture complex sociotechnical dynamics. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving statistical significance in results given the high dimensionality of modeled systems and stochastic nature of agent interactions.
cip_title: Computer and Information Sciences and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer and information sciences and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and operational efficiency of wind turbine systems, addressing critical challenges in aerodynamic performance, structural reliability, and grid integration. Wind energy systems are subject to complex, dynamic environmental loads and variable power generation patterns, which complicate efforts to maximize energy output while minimizing mechanical fatigue and maintenance costs. Current design tools often rely on simplified assumptions or static datasets, limiting their ability to predict turbine behavior under real-world conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-physics interactions across temporal and spatial scales. Large-eddy simulations (LES) will resolve turbulent airflow around turbine blades at high resolution, while coupled FEA models will assess structural responses to aerodynamic and inertial forces. Concurrently, ML algorithms trained on historical operational data will identify patterns in wind variability and mechanical wear, enabling predictive maintenance strategies. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of parametric studies (e.g., blade geometry optimization, material fatigue analysis) and the need for ensemble simulations capturing diverse atmospheric conditions. Expected outcomes include validated models for (1) aerodynamically efficient blade designs tailored to regional wind regimes, (2) fatigue-resistant tower and drivetrain configurations, and (3) adaptive control algorithms to stabilize power output during grid fluctuations. By integrating these results, the project aims to reduce levelized energy costs by 8–12% for mid-sized wind farms while extending turbine lifespans. These advancements will directly support curriculum development in wind energy technology, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-aided renewable energy research. The generated datasets and open-source simulation tools will be shared with industry partners to accelerate the translation of computational insights into field-deployable solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing wind-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in wind energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of legal transcript editing performed by scopists, a specialized role critical to judicial documentation integrity. Current scopist workflows rely heavily on manual review of court reporter transcripts, a process challenged by the exponential growth in digital court proceedings, complex legal terminology, and the need for real-time error correction in high-stakes environments. The research problem centers on overcoming limitations in existing computer-aided transcription (CAT) software, which lacks robust machine learning capabilities to autonomously detect contextual inconsistencies, misheard terminology, or syntax errors in machine shorthand outputs. To address this, we propose a hybrid natural language processing (NLP) model trained on domain-specific legal corpora, including appellate court records, deposition transcripts, and specialized glossaries, to identify and flag discrepancies between raw stenographic data and contextually appropriate legal language. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallel processing of multi-speaker audio-text alignment, dynamic legal lexicon updating, and probabilistic error detection across terabyte-scale transcript datasets. By implementing transformer-based architectures optimized for low-latency inference, the system aims to reduce scopists’ manual correction time by 40–60% while maintaining 99.5% terminological accuracy across diverse jurisdictional requirements. Expected outcomes include an open-source API for real-time editorial suggestions and a novel evaluation metric for legal transcript fidelity that accounts for rhetorical nuance, precedent-specific phrasing, and procedural formalities. This work bridges computational linguistics with legal documentation practices, offering scalable solutions for courts adapting to remote proceedings and AI-augmented stenography tools, while preserving human oversight essential for judicial accountability.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to perform editing and word processing on a court reporter transcript to ensure the accuracy of the transcripts. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcriptioning, machine shorthand, and computer-aided transcription software.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social network structures and demographic behaviors using large-scale computational simulations. The research problem centers on understanding how evolving social ties—such as kinship, friendship, and professional connections—influence population-level outcomes like migration patterns, fertility decisions, and household formation. Traditional survey-based methods struggle to capture the recursive feedback between individual agency and structural constraints at scale, particularly across heterogeneous populations. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) that simulates life-course decisions within dynamic, multi-layered social networks. The model will integrate demographic microdata, longitudinal social tie metrics, and empirically derived behavioral rules to explore emergent phenomena under varying policy and environmental scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational demands of simulating millions of interacting agents across decadal time horizons, while maintaining granular detail in network evolution and decision pathways. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for network topology updates, implementing adaptive sampling techniques for rare demographic events, and validating model outputs against census and panel study benchmarks. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how localized network disruptions (e.g., workforce automation, climate migration) propagate through social systems to alter demographic trajectories. The results will advance theoretical frameworks in computational sociology while providing actionable evidence for policymakers addressing population aging and spatial inequality. By open-sourcing the optimized ABM framework, this work will also create a reusable resource for studying complex social systems across disciplines.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sociology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of cancer-related muscle dysfunction by integrating computational modeling with exercise physiology to investigate how tumor biology and systemic metabolic stress impair skeletal muscle adaptation. Cancer patients frequently exhibit severe muscle wasting and impaired recovery, yet the molecular-to-systemic mechanisms linking tumor-induced physiological stress to maladaptive exercise responses remain poorly characterized. We propose to develop a multiscale computational framework simulating interactions between tumor-secreted factors, host metabolism, and skeletal muscle protein turnover during exercise. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the integration of dynamic physiological datasets—including proteomic profiles of muscle biopsies from breast cancer survivors, in vivo cytokine trajectories during exercise, and longitudinal metabolic measurements—into agent-based models of muscle fiber networks. These models will parameterize tumor-driven disruptions to anabolic signaling pathways (e.g., mTOR activation thresholds) and predict how exercise dosage modulates proteostasis under varying oncogenic stress conditions. A second computational layer will employ finite element analysis to simulate tissue-level oxygen diffusion limitations caused by cancer-associated anemia during sustained activity. Validation will utilize clinical datasets measuring exercise-induced changes in muscle cross-sectional area and systemic inflammatory markers across cancer stages. The HPC scale required stems from stochastic modeling of heterogeneous cell populations (10⁵–10⁶ agents) coupled with iterative optimization of differential equation systems representing whole-body energetics. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms identifying patient-specific exercise thresholds that maximize hypertrophic responses while minimizing catabolic risk, directly informing clinical trials in oncological exercise rehabilitation. This work bridges exercise physiology and cancer biology by quantifying how malignancy alters fundamental principles of muscle plasticity, with translational potential to refine exercise prescriptions in oncology care.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in physical or motor activity, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in muscular and skeletal anatomy; molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction; fuel utilization; neurophysiology of motor mechanics; systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others); fatigue and exhaustion; muscle and body training; physiology of specific exercises and activities; physiology of injury; and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: Clinical and translational research increasingly relies on the integration of heterogeneous, high-dimensional datasets—including multi-omics profiles, electronic health records (EHRs), and medical imaging—to bridge gaps between laboratory discoveries and clinical applications. However, existing computational resources at our institution are insufficient to support large-scale analyses of these complex datasets, particularly for projects requiring parallel processing, real-time analytics, or machine learning model training. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable three interrelated aims: (1) develop predictive models of treatment response in autoimmune diseases by integrating genomic, proteomic, and longitudinal EHR data; (2) simulate population-level disease spread under varying clinical intervention scenarios using agent-based epidemiological modeling; and (3) optimize natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for automated extraction of clinically relevant variables from unstructured physician notes and imaging reports. Computational workflows will leverage containerized environments for reproducibility, with GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer models) applied to multimodal data fusion. Statistical power calculations estimate that cohort analyses will require processing >10 TB of data across 20,000 patient records, necessitating scalable storage and distributed computing frameworks. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers for personalized immunotherapy, validated simulation tools for public health decision-making, and open-source NLP utilities tailored to clinical text. These resources will directly support six active NIH-funded studies while enhancing institutional capacity for data-driven medical education initiatives. By enabling rapid analysis of sensitive health data in secure, HIPAA-compliant environments, this allocation will advance translational research infrastructure critical for training clinician-scientists in computational methodologies. The project aligns with national priorities for precision medicine and addresses urgent needs in resource allocation for health professions education, where few platforms currently support both research and training in clinical computational analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares medical and health clinicians to combine knowledge from scientific or clinical or translational studies, translate scientific knowledge, improve medical education, and bridge laboratory and clinical science into clinical practice. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, Information technology, biostatistics, epidemiology, grant writing, management and analysis of clinical data, clinical and translational research law and policy, responsible conduct of research, medical education and scientific writing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a computational framework to optimize radiation dose delivery and image quality in diagnostic radiography, addressing critical challenges in patient safety and diagnostic accuracy. Current protocols for X-ray imaging rely on generalized exposure parameters, which may lead to unnecessary radiation exposure or suboptimal image quality, particularly for patients with atypical anatomies or medical conditions. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven approach to personalize imaging protocols by integrating patient-specific anatomical data, real-time sensor feedback, and historical imaging outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep learning models on large, heterogeneous datasets of radiographic images, patient metadata, and radiation dose records. These models will predict optimal exposure settings (kVp, mAs, collimation) and positioning adjustments tailored to individual patient morphologies. Concurrently, Monte Carlo simulations will model radiation scatter and absorption patterns across diverse anatomical regions, requiring parallelized computation to iteratively refine dose distribution predictions. The computational pipeline will also incorporate generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize realistic training data for rare clinical scenarios, mitigating data scarcity issues. Expected outcomes include a validated software toolset that recommends patient-specific protocols, reducing median radiation dose by an estimated 15-20% while maintaining diagnostic utility, as quantified by contrast-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index metrics. This work will provide radiographers with evidence-based decision support, advancing precision in medical imaging. The resulting datasets and models will be disseminated as open educational resources for radiologic science programs, enhancing training in dose optimization strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges computational innovation with clinical radiography practice, directly aligning with institutional priorities in health professions education and patient-centered care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical imaging services to patients and attending health care professionals. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, patient positioning, radiographic technique, radiation biology, safety and emergency procedures, equipment operation and maintenance, quality assurance, patient education, and medical imaging/radiologic services management.

abstract: Musculoskeletal neoplasms present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneity, complex molecular landscapes, and variable responses to therapies. Current approaches to diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment optimization rely on histopathological and imaging data, which often fail to capture the dynamic interplay of genomic, proteomic, and microenvironmental factors driving tumor behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating multi-omics data, longitudinal imaging, and clinical outcomes. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating predictive models of tumor progression and treatment response using machine learning algorithms trained on genomic sequencing, radiomics, and patient-specific biomechanical data, and (2) simulating the effects of combination therapies—including targeted agents, immunotherapies, and radiation—to identify optimal treatment regimens. Computational workflows will involve large-scale data harmonization, deep learning for feature extraction from histopathology slides and MRI/CT scans, and agent-based modeling of tumor-immune interactions. HPC resources are critical for managing petabytes of multimodal data, running parallelized simulations, and training complex neural networks. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early metastasis detection, patient-specific therapy recommendations, and a publicly accessible computational platform for simulating treatment scenarios. This work will advance precision oncology by enabling dynamic, data-driven decision-making, reducing trial-and-error in therapy selection, and providing a framework to accelerate translational discoveries in musculoskeletal oncology. The proposed models and tools will be validated against retrospective clinical datasets, with findings directly informing prospective trials at our institution.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal neoplasm, and the application of cancer therapy regimes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize supply chain efficiency and resilience in agricultural retail and wholesale systems, addressing critical challenges in product distribution, inventory management, and demand forecasting. Agricultural supply chains are increasingly strained by climate volatility, fluctuating input costs, and shifting consumer demands, yet existing decision-support tools often lack the computational power to integrate multi-scale datasets or model dynamic interactions between stakeholders. The research will develop a computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to analyze spatial-temporal patterns in farm supply procurement, storage, and distribution. Key datasets include historical sales records, weather data, transportation logistics, and real-time market signals from agricultural cooperatives. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risk under diverse climate and economic scenarios, the project will identify optimal inventory allocation strategies and evaluate the cost-benefit tradeoffs of regional distribution hubs. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution geospatial data, train predictive models on multi-year transactional datasets, and simulate complex supply networks across thousands of nodes. Expected outcomes include scalable algorithms for adaptive inventory management and decision-support dashboards to help retailers minimize waste, reduce transportation costs, and mitigate stockout risks during peak demand periods. This work will directly benefit agricultural suppliers, wholesalers, and farmers by enhancing the robustness of supply chains critical to food security and farm profitability. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools and partnerships with state agricultural extension programs, ensuring translational impact for stakeholders operating in resource-constrained environments.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) present complex challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, involving neurobiological, psychological, and sociocultural determinants. Current treatment personalization remains limited by a lack of integrative computational frameworks capable of modeling dynamic interactions between these factors. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to simulate and predict individual treatment trajectories in addiction counseling, integrating real-world clinical data, neuroimaging-derived biomarkers, and behavioral patterns. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational limitations of existing predictive models, which often oversimplify temporal and contextual variables critical to relapse risk and therapeutic response. We will employ a hybrid computational approach combining mechanistic modeling of neural reward circuitry (via differential equations informed by fMRI and EEG data) with machine learning analysis of longitudinal clinical records, including counselor notes, patient-reported outcomes, and ecological momentary assessments. GPU-accelerated parameter optimization and ensemble learning techniques will be implemented to handle high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets while maintaining interpretability for clinical translation. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a scalable computational framework for identifying patient-specific vulnerability signatures across biological and psychosocial domains, (2) predictive models of intervention effectiveness under varying contextual stressors, and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating hypothetical counseling strategies in silico. This work addresses a critical gap in addiction science by enabling precision counseling approaches grounded in systems-level computational psychiatry. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the iterative model training, large-scale parallel simulations, and integration of multimodal data streams required to capture the dynamic complexity of SUD recovery processes. Successful implementation could transform treatment planning by providing counselors with empirically validated computational tools to optimize intervention timing and modality selection.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to help prevent substance abuse, counsel individuals and families with drug and alcohol problems, and perform intervention and therapeutic services for persons suffering from addiction. Includes instruction in individual and group counseling skills, psychology of addiction, sociology, crisis intervention, substance abuse identification methodologies, substance abuse treatment modalities, substance abuse prevention and treatment resources, pharmacology and behavioral aspects of abused substances, treatment evaluation, patient observation and education, group dynamics, professional standards and ethics, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the dynamics of multi-faith spiritual care in crisis environments, a critical but understudied aspect of chaplaincy studies. Chaplains operating in settings such as disaster response, conflict zones, or emergency healthcare must navigate complex ethical dilemmas, rapidly evolving interpersonal dynamics, and diverse cultural-religious expectations. Current training models rely primarily on qualitative case studies, limiting scalability and generalizability. Our research addresses this gap by creating a high-fidelity simulation environment using agent-based modeling (ABM) to study decision-making patterns and intervention outcomes across heterogeneous populations. The computational model will integrate ethnographic data from chaplain field reports, psychological profiles, and historical records of crisis interventions to generate synthetic populations with varying faith traditions, trauma responses, and social networks. High-performance computing resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps analyzing how variables such as interfaith competency levels, team composition, and crisis duration impact care efficacy. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent patterns in simulated interactions, particularly around ethical boundary negotiation and culturally adaptive counseling strategies. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for chaplain training programs, quantitative metrics for evaluating multi-faith intervention protocols, and evidence-based recommendations for optimizing resource allocation in crisis chaplaincy teams. By bridging computational social science with practical theology, this work aims to advance both methodological innovation in humanities research and the operational preparedness of spiritual care providers in high-stakes environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide caregiver, pastoral, and spiritual support in an institutional, hospice, military, or sports setting. Includes instruction in global, healthcare, prison, and sports chaplaincy; addiction, crisis, disaster, family, marriage, grief, and loss counseling; ethics; leadership; multi-cultural, multi-faith contexts; and worship.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of dynamic resource optimization in large-scale, multi-venue event ecosystems using computational modeling and simulation. While traditional event planning relies on static schedules and heuristic vendor allocation, modern hybrid and decentralized events—such as conferences spanning physical venues, virtual platforms, and satellite hubs—require real-time coordination of interdependent variables, including attendee flow, vendor capacity, energy consumption, and emergency response logistics. The project will develop a high-fidelity agent-based model (ABM) integrated with stochastic optimization algorithms to simulate scenarios involving 50,000+ concurrent participants across heterogeneous event nodes. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model spatial-temporal dependencies between venues, Monte Carlo methods to assess risk propagation in supply chain disruptions, and reinforcement learning to optimize vendor routing under capacity constraints. High-performance computing resources are critical for parameter sensitivity analysis across 10^6 possible configurations and real-time scenario testing during model training. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of recommending adaptive resource allocation strategies that reduce operational costs by 15-25% in simulated events while maintaining attendee satisfaction metrics. The framework will also quantify cascading failure risks in event ecosystems—a novel contribution to hospitality risk management literature. By bridging computational social science with event operations, this work establishes a methodological foundation for data-driven resilience planning in an industry increasingly shaped by complex, technology-mediated participant experiences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, budget, and implement conferences, meetings, and other special events in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in principles of meeting and event planning; special event management; budgets and finance; site selection; contracts, vendors, and negotiations; marketing and promotions; food and beverage management; audio-visual basics and meeting technology; and hospitality law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in large-scale, data-driven analysis of sociocultural and historical dynamics in translation practices. While translation studies has traditionally relied on qualitative, case-based methods, the increasing availability of digitized multilingual corpora—spanning literary, technical, and commercial texts—presents an opportunity to systematically analyze patterns of linguistic transfer, ideological shifts, and institutional influences across time and geographies. However, processing these heterogeneous datasets (e.g., parallel texts, translation metadata, paratextual commentaries) at scale requires advanced computational capabilities beyond local infrastructure. The research will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and contemporary translation data, including transformer-based models fine-tuned to detect stylistic anomalies, semantic distortions, and sociolinguistic biases in translated works. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model how translation norms emerge through interactions between translators, institutions, and audiences, incorporating real-world data on publishing trends and geopolitical contexts. By integrating machine learning, network analysis, and computational linguistics, this project aims to uncover systemic factors shaping translation outcomes—such as the impact of colonial histories on technical translation practices or the role of digital platforms in homogenizing literary translation. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for corpus-based translation analysis, a public repository of annotated multilingual datasets, and empirically grounded frameworks for evaluating equity in global translation workflows. The computational demands—training multilingual models on terabytes of text, running thousands of simulation iterations with parameter variations, and cross-referencing results against sociohistorical databases—necessitate HPC support for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workflows. Findings will advance interdisciplinary scholarship in translation theory while informing practical strategies for ethical translation policy and technology design.
cip_definition: A multidisciplinary program that prepares individuals to explore the historical, social, institutional and cultural facets of translation. Includes instruction in general and literary translation, business translation, technical translation, and other specific applications of linguistic skills.

abstract: Oral health disparities persist across populations due to uneven access to preventive and curative dental services, compounded by complex socioeconomic, geographic, and behavioral factors. Current public health strategies often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between these variables, limiting the precision of interventions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate population-level oral health outcomes under varying service delivery scenarios, enabling data-driven policy recommendations. The research will integrate anonymized electronic health records, demographic surveys, and environmental data from public health databases to model disease progression, resource allocation efficiency, and intervention impacts at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations that represent millions of individuals with heterogeneous risk profiles, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict emergent patterns of dental caries, periodontal disease, and service utilization. Computational workflows will optimize parallel processing for parameter sensitivity analyses and scenario testing, such as evaluating the cost-effectiveness of community fluoride programs or mobile clinic deployments in underserved regions. Geospatial analytics will further map service gaps and forecast demand under demographic shifts. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into optimal intervention timing, resource distribution, and policy adjustments to reduce inequities. By quantifying trade-offs between preventive and reactive care strategies, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in dental public health. The scalability of the models will also provide a adaptable toolkit for addressing oral health challenges in diverse global contexts, with implications for reducing systemic healthcare costs and improving population-level oral health outcomes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the formulation and delivery of public preventive and curative dental health services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary study examining the dynamics of socio-cultural resilience in urban environments facing rapid environmental and demographic change. While traditional approaches in urban studies often silo qualitative social data, quantitative environmental metrics, and historical-cultural analyses, this research integrates these domains through computational modeling to identify patterns and feedback loops that influence community adaptability. The core challenge lies in processing heterogeneous datasets—including ethnographic interviews, geospatial records, climate projections, and archival materials—to construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating decision-making processes among stakeholders under varying stress scenarios. Current pilot simulations on local clusters have been limited by scale, struggling to handle the combinatorial complexity of multi-layered interactions across 10,000+ agents and decade-long time horizons. Access to HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across parameter spaces, Bayesian calibration of model outputs against real-world case studies, and machine learning-driven sensitivity analyses to prioritize key variables. Methodologically, the project bridges computational social science, environmental humanities, and urban informatics, employing Python-based frameworks (Mesa, PyTorch) for model development and R Shiny for interactive visualization of results. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for policymakers to test intervention strategies, alongside scholarly contributions to theories of cultural resilience that account for nonlinear systemic behaviors. By quantifying how intangible factors like collective memory or identity influence adaptation thresholds, this work aims to inform equitable urban planning frameworks that balance infrastructure demands with cultural preservation. The requested computing allocation directly supports scaling these computationally intensive workflows, which are critical to capturing the emergent, cross-disciplinary phenomena central to the research questions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Maternal and child health (MCH) disparities persist globally, driven by complex interactions between biological, socioecological, and structural determinants. This project seeks to model these multifactorial influences on adverse pregnancy outcomes and pediatric health inequities using advanced computational methods, with a focus on identifying intervention points for policy and clinical practice. Current analytical approaches often oversimplify dynamic interactions across individual, community, and systemic levels, limiting their utility in real-world decision-making. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with machine learning to simulate population-level health trajectories under varying policy and resource allocation scenarios. The ABM will incorporate longitudinal data from national health surveys, electronic health records, and geospatial environmental exposures, capturing bidirectional relationships between socioeconomic factors, healthcare access, and biological risk. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity of these simulations, which involve millions of autonomous agents with heterogeneous attributes interacting across temporally varying conditions. Parallelized parameter sweeps will assess how systemic factors (e.g., prenatal care funding, nutrition programs) modulate disparities in preterm birth, maternal mortality, and early childhood developmental delays. Complementary analyses will apply multilevel Bayesian regression to quantify uncertainty in intervention effects across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for simulating MCH policy impacts, granular maps of regional risk factors, and cost-effectiveness rankings of intervention strategies. By enabling high-resolution modeling of causal pathways at scale, this work will provide actionable insights for optimizing resource allocation in under-resourced communities. The requested computational infrastructure will support data integration, model calibration, and sensitivity analyses that exceed the capacity of local computing clusters, directly advancing translational research at the intersection of computational epidemiology and health equity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-regional communication and ideological exchange in 19th-century Latin America by analyzing large-scale archival datasets, including digitized newspapers, personal correspondence, and government records from Mexico to Argentina. The central research problem lies in tracing how political ideas—such as liberalism, federalism, and anti-colonialism—circulated among urban centers and rural areas during post-independence state formation. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to systematically map these flows across multilingual sources (Spanish, Portuguese, and Indigenous languages) or quantify their impact on regional governance structures. To address this, we propose a computational approach leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis. Custom transformer models will be trained to detect ideological concepts, semantic shifts, and multilingual terminology in over 500,000 pages of text, while temporal graph algorithms will model the diffusion of ideas through geographic and social networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing heterogeneous, noisy historical data at scale, particularly for parallelized OCR correction of degraded documents, training multilingual NLP pipelines, and running iterative simulations of network propagation. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory CPUs for constructing dynamic networks with temporal edge weighting. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated texts, interactive visualizations of idea circulation patterns, and quantitative metrics assessing the influence of key cities as ideological hubs. By integrating computational methods with archival research, this work aims to reveal previously obscured connections between intellectual movements and institutional changes, offering new frameworks for understanding the contested construction of national identities in postcolonial Latin America.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking areas of the world, including the Iberian, Latin American, and Lusophone worlds.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis of architectural heritage conservation through computational modeling and machine learning, addressing gaps in current methods for documenting and interpreting vulnerable historic structures. Traditional approaches to architectural history and conservation often rely on manual archival research, physical surveys, and static 2D representations, which struggle to account for dynamic environmental stressors, material decay patterns, or the spatial complexity of historic sites. Our research proposes an interdisciplinary computational framework integrating 3D LiDAR scans, multispectral imaging, and environmental sensor data from three at-risk 19th-century industrial complexes in understudied regions.
