Using HPC-enabled workflows, we will process terabyte-scale datasets to construct dynamic digital twins that simulate decay mechanisms under varying climate scenarios, while training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to identify subtle patterns of structural degradation across archival imagery. The computational pipeline will automate the alignment of heterogeneous data sources—historical blueprints, geospatial records, and real-time monitoring inputs—enabling probabilistic modeling of intervention outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for predictive conservation planning, validated against physical surveys, and a novel visualization platform that layers temporal, material, and socio-technical data onto immersive 3D models. By bridging architectural historiography with computational engineering methods, this work aims to establish new standards for data-driven preservation strategies while interrogating how algorithmic analysis can reshape historical narratives about industrial heritage. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations of large-scale structures and optimizing machine learning models across distributed GPU nodes, tasks infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Architectural History, Criticism, and Conservation, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural history, criticism, and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable decision-support platform for education entrepreneurs to optimize resource allocation in innovative learning ventures, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic educational ecosystems. Education entrepreneurs face complex challenges in balancing financial sustainability, equitable access, and pedagogical impact, particularly when scaling interventions across diverse contexts. Current planning tools lack the capacity to integrate real-time data on market dynamics, funding volatility, and learner outcomes, resulting in suboptimal resource distribution and missed opportunities for systemic impact. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling framework simulating interactions between stakeholders (e.g., schools, investors, policymakers) and variables such as funding cycles, enrollment patterns, and operational costs. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of scenarios, including Monte Carlo analyses of risk exposure under fluctuating economic conditions and machine learning-driven sensitivity testing of business model pivots. The computational architecture will incorporate heterogeneous datasets—from philanthropic investment trends to regional education infrastructure metrics—to train predictive models identifying high-leverage intervention points. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation engine capable of forecasting 3-year financial and educational outcomes under user-defined constraints, with applications in venture capital due diligence, philanthropic grant strategy, and adaptive project management for education startups. By quantifying trade-offs between profitability and equity in resource allocation decisions, this work aims to advance evidence-based entrepreneurship practices while maintaining computational reproducibility standards for public benefit. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated parameter optimization and validation against historical case studies of failed/persistent education ventures, requiring ~200,000 core-hours for initial development and benchmarking. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and integrated into a graduate-level curriculum on computational decision-making in education leadership.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create, fund, and manage innovations in education. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, the design of learning environments, the economics of education, entrepreneurship, evaluation, finance, human-centered design, investing, resource management, project management, and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to simulate fire dynamics and suppression strategies in complex built environments, addressing critical gaps in predicting fire behavior under real-world conditions. Current fire modeling tools often rely on simplified assumptions that neglect coupled phenomena such as turbulent combustion, heat transfer to structural elements, and the interaction of suppression agents with evolving fire plumes. These limitations hinder the design of optimized fire protection systems and evidence-based emergency response protocols. To overcome these challenges, we propose a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve multi-scale, multi-physics processes inherent in fire scenarios. Large-eddy simulations (LES) will model turbulent combustion and soot formation using detailed chemical kinetics, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict heat-induced structural degradation. Coupled agent-based modeling will simulate occupant evacuation dynamics influenced by real-time fire spread predictions. The computational workflow will integrate experimental data from bench-scale fire tests to validate submodels for water mist suppression efficiency and toxic gas dispersion. Machine learning techniques will be employed to accelerate parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification across millions of simulated scenarios. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this research aims to produce predictive tools that inform next-generation fire codes, improve the resilience of building materials, and enable AI-driven decision support systems for fireground operations. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation modules for the fire science community, risk assessment guidelines for high-occupancy structures, and training datasets for firefighter situational awareness technologies. The requested computing resources will directly support the parallelized execution of 3D transient simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (<1 cm) and temporal scales (<10 ms), which are computationally infeasible with existing institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: Health services research faces growing challenges in analyzing large-scale, multi-dimensional datasets to evaluate healthcare delivery and outcomes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding how structural inequities and care fragmentation impact health outcomes across diverse populations. The research will integrate electronic health records (EHRs), insurance claims, and socioeconomic datasets to model longitudinal care pathways and quantify disparities in access, costs, and quality. A key computational challenge lies in processing terabyte-scale datasets with temporal, spatial, and hierarchical dependencies while preserving privacy through federated learning architectures. The proposed approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for clinical text mining, graph neural networks to map patient-provider networks, and agent-based simulations to test intervention scenarios. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of distributed EHR data across 12 healthcare systems, training of deep learning models on GPU clusters, and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to estimate policy impacts. Expected outcomes include identifying high-risk patient subgroups with underutilized preventive services, optimizing resource allocation for chronic disease management, and simulating the effects of telehealth expansion on rural-urban outcome disparities. By scaling methods that are computationally infeasible on local infrastructure, this work will provide actionable evidence for health systems and policymakers to reduce inequities. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to advance reproducible health services research, with particular emphasis on validating models across heterogeneous populations. This project directly aligns with public health priorities by enabling data-driven strategies to improve care coordination, cost efficiency, and equity in real-world service delivery.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on basic and applied inquiry, that examines access to, and the use, costs, quality, delivery, organization, financing, and outcomes of health care services to produce new knowledge about the structure, processes, and effects of health services for individuals and populations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in tool and die manufacturing by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize the design and fabrication of metal-forming tools, dies, and fixtures. Traditional methods for developing these components rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and empirical adjustments, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to predict complex material behaviors under dynamic thermal and mechanical stresses. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning (ML), and generative design algorithms. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model high-strain processes such as stamping, forging, and extrusion, with a focus on predicting tool wear, residual stresses, and microstructural evolution in workpiece materials. ML models will be trained on simulation and experimental data to identify optimal machining parameters, material selections, and tool geometries, while generative design methods will automate the exploration of lightweight, high-strength die configurations. These computationally intensive workflows demand HPC resources to achieve the necessary scale, resolution, and speed for practical industry applications. The outcomes will include validated predictive models for tool longevity, reduced material waste through virtual prototyping, and data-driven design guidelines for complex dies. Successfully demonstrating this approach will advance precision in tool and die manufacturing, lower production costs, and enhance the durability of components in sectors such as automotive and aerospace. Additionally, the project will integrate HPC-based workflows into the Tool and Die Technology curriculum, equipping students with skills in computational modeling and digital manufacturing—a critical step in modernizing technical education for Industry 4.0 challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate machine tools used in the forming of metal components, as well as the fabrication of special tools, dies, jigs and fixtures used in cutting, working and finishing metal components.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the role of dynamic biomechanical forces in regulating cellular behavior during musculoskeletal tissue regeneration, with a focus on understudied connective tissues such as the meniscus. Current regenerative strategies often fail to account for the complex, time-varying mechanical cues that drive cell differentiation and extracellular matrix remodeling in these load-bearing tissues. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate mechanotransduction pathways across cellular, tissue, and organ levels. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallelization of stochastic ABM simulations capturing individual cell responses to mechanical stimuli, coupled with FEA modeling of evolving tissue-scale stress distributions under physiological loading conditions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs by identifying key mechanobiological parameter combinations that maximize predictive accuracy. The resulting models will be validated against in vitro experiments measuring real-time strain patterns and gene expression profiles in engineered meniscal constructs. Expected outcomes include the first predictive platform for optimizing dynamic mechanical conditioning protocols in tissue engineering bioreactors, with potential applications in personalized rehabilitation strategies and implant design. By elucidating how spatially heterogeneous mechanical microenvironments influence regenerative outcomes, this work advances fundamental understanding of mechanobiology while addressing a critical clinical need for functional tissue repair solutions. The computational infrastructure will support the development of open-source tools for mechanoregulated tissue engineering, fostering collaboration across biomechanics, computational biology, and orthopedic surgery domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Licensed Practical/Vocational Nurses (LPNs/LVNs) play a critical role in patient care, yet clinical workflows often lack data-driven tools to optimize their decision-making in dynamic care environments. This project addresses the challenge of predicting patient deterioration in acute care settings, where delays in recognizing early warning signs can lead to adverse outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop machine learning (ML) models that analyze multimodal clinical data—including vital signs, medication administration records, and nurse-reported observations—to identify high-risk patients in real time. Current approaches rely on static protocols, which do not adapt to individual patient trajectories or contextual factors such as staffing constraints. The computational workload involves processing heterogeneous datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), requiring parallelized pipelines for data cleaning, feature engineering, and temporal analysis. Deep learning architectures, such as transformer-based models and recurrent neural networks, will be trained on historical patient data to detect subtle patterns preceding clinical deterioration. HPC resources are essential to manage the scale of EHR data (spanning millions of patient-hours), optimize hyperparameters via distributed computing, and validate models across diverse patient subgroups. The outcomes will include an open-source predictive framework tailored for integration into LPN workflows, providing actionable alerts to prioritize interventions. This research directly aligns with nursing science by enhancing LPNs’ capacity to deliver proactive care, potentially reducing hospital-acquired complications and readmissions. By simulating care scenarios under varying resource conditions, the models will also inform training programs on adaptive clinical judgment. The project underscores the transformative role of computational methods in nursing practice, bridging data science and hands-on patient care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in providing general nursing care under the direction of a registered nurse, physician or dentist. Includes instruction in taking patient vital signs, applying sterile dressings, patient health education, and assistance with examinations and treatment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for modeling dynamic consumer decision-making under volatile economic conditions, with a focus on heterogeneous household consumption patterns. Traditional consumer economics models often rely on simplified assumptions about rationality, market homogeneity, and static preferences, limiting their ability to capture complex behavioral interactions in real-world scenarios characterized by inflationary shocks, supply chain disruptions, and rapid technological change. The research will implement a hybrid agent-based and machine learning approach to simulate millions of individualized consumer agents operating within a high-dimensional economic environment. Computational challenges include parallelizing preference learning algorithms across diverse demographic cohorts, optimizing differential equations for intertemporal budget constraints under uncertainty, and analyzing emergent consumption patterns through network analysis of cascading demand shifts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter calibration using granular microdata from consumer expenditure surveys, price indices, and digital transaction traces while maintaining privacy-preserving data protocols. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for policymakers to stress-test fiscal interventions, forecast sector-specific demand elasticity, and evaluate equity implications of inflation mitigation strategies. By integrating behavioral heterogeneity with macroeconomic shocks, this work aims to advance predictive modeling in consumer economics while establishing computational best practices for ethical large-scale consumer data utilization in non-STEM domains. The resource request prioritizes GPU-accelerated nodes for deep reinforcement learning components and high-memory nodes for multi-agent simulation workloads.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of micro- and macro-economic theory to consumer behavior and individual and family consumption of goods and services. Includes instruction in modeling, economic forecasting, indexing, price theory, and analysis of individual commodities and services and/or groups of related commodities and services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize alloy design and processing parameters for high-performance metallurgical applications, addressing the challenge of efficiently predicting microstructural evolution and mechanical properties under industrial-scale manufacturing conditions. Traditional experimental approaches to alloy development are resource-intensive and time-consuming, particularly for complex multi-phase systems used in aerospace, automotive, and energy sectors. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for atomic-scale defect analysis, phase-field modeling (PFM) for mesoscale grain boundary dynamics, and machine learning (ML) to accelerate property prediction across processing variables. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the computational demands of these coupled models, which require parallelized simulations across thousands of processing scenarios, large-scale thermodynamic database integration, and real-time adaptive mesh refinement for phase transformations. The research will focus on nickel-based superalloys and advanced high-strength steels, correlating simulated microstructures with experimental data from partner industrial labs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing heat treatment schedules, reducing trial runs in physical testing by 40-60%, and identifying novel alloy compositions with enhanced corrosion resistance and fatigue life. This work will advance computational metallurgy capabilities in academic-industrial collaborations while training students in HPC-aided materials design. The resulting open-source simulation workflows will provide the metallurgical technology community with adaptable frameworks for addressing sustainable manufacturing challenges, including energy-efficient processing and recyclable alloy development. Successful implementation requires dedicated GPU nodes for ML training and CPU cores for concurrent PFM/MD simulations, enabling parametric studies impractical on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and metallurgists engaged in developing and using industrial metals and manufacturing processes. Includes instruction in principles of metallurgy, related manufacturing systems, laboratory techniques, testing and inspection procedures, instrument calibration, system and equipment maintenance and repair, applications to specific processes, and report preparation.

abstract: Infant and toddler mental health is shaped by dynamic interactions between biological, psychological, and environmental factors, yet current methods to model these complex systems remain limited. This project seeks to develop predictive computational models of early childhood mental health outcomes by integrating high-dimensional datasets, including behavioral observations, genetic markers, caregiver-reported measures, and neural activity data (e.g., EEG). A key challenge lies in analyzing non-linear, time-dependent relationships across these modalities at scale, particularly when identifying early risk factors for conditions such as anxiety, attachment disorders, or developmental delays. To address this, we propose using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning architectures—including recurrent neural networks and transformer-based models—on longitudinal datasets from 5,000+ children enrolled in regional mental health programs. These models will simulate developmental trajectories under varying biopsychosocial conditions, enabling the identification of critical intervention windows and personalized risk profiles. Computational workflows will prioritize ethical data handling, with federated learning techniques to maintain participant confidentiality across multi-institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms to predict mental health vulnerabilities with higher accuracy than existing screening tools, (2) a framework for simulating the systemic impacts of caregiver-focused or community-level interventions, and (3) open-source tools to help clinicians interpret model outputs in practice. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process multimodal data and optimize complex models, this work aims to advance precision approaches in infant mental health services while contributing methodological innovations to the broader field of developmental psychopathology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide mental health services to infants, toddlers, and preschoolers and their families. Includes instruction in developmental psychology, cognitive and biological development, social and emotional development, research methods, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize workforce ecosystems in multi-platform labor markets, a novel interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of human capital analytics, computational social science, and decision theory. Traditional human resources frameworks struggle to account for the dynamic interdependencies between permanent employees, gig workers, automated systems, and AI collaborators in modern organizational networks. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to quantify how micro-level interactions among heterogeneous workforce agents—including skill complementarity, task delegation patterns, and cross-system dependencies—propagate through organizations to impact macro-level outcomes such as operational resilience, innovation capacity, and ethical risk exposure. Using agent-based modeling and multilayer network analysis, the project will simulate large-scale workforce ecosystems under varying conditions of market volatility, technological disruption, and policy constraints. Computational experiments will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess emergent properties across thousands of synthetic organizations, integrating real-world HR datasets on performance metrics, collaboration patterns, and attrition rates. The HPC environment is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of modeling 10^5+ agent interactions across multiple temporal and organizational scales while maintaining granular individual behavioral parameters. Expected outcomes include a decision support framework for strategic workforce architecture optimization, novel metrics for quantifying hybrid human-AI team robustness, and evidence-based policy recommendations for governing decentralized labor platforms. By advancing computational methods to analyze next-generation workforce dynamics, this research addresses a critical gap in contemporary human resources science while providing practical tools for managing organizational complexity in an era of increasingly fluid labor markets.
cip_title: Human Resources Management and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in human resources management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing reliance on space-based systems for military operations necessitates advanced tools to model and mitigate risks posed by adversarial threats, such as electronic warfare, cyber intrusions, and kinetic attacks on orbital assets. Current simulation frameworks lack the fidelity to evaluate the resilience of heterogeneous satellite constellations operating in dynamic, contested environments. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to simulate multi-domain threats against military space systems, integrating orbital mechanics, network vulnerability analysis, and adversarial behavior modeling. The research will employ agent-based modeling to represent satellite constellations, ground stations, and threat actors, with Monte Carlo methods assessing system degradation under stochastic attack scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to identify critical failure pathways and optimize defensive resource allocation. The computational demands of concurrently modeling high-fidelity physics-based interactions (e.g., signal jamming, debris propagation) and strategic decision-making processes across thousands of parallelized scenarios require dedicated HPC resources. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for quantifying mission-level impacts of space system disruptions, predictive tools for prioritizing infrastructure hardening measures, and tactical playbooks for maintaining operational continuity during attacks. This work bridges gaps between traditional space operations research and emerging computational security methodologies, offering military planners novel insights into protecting next-generation architectures like proliferated low-Earth orbit networks. By leveraging scalable HPC infrastructure, the project aims to advance decision superiority in space systems command and control while informing future acquisitions and doctrine.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and operation of missiles, satellites and other space-based systems for military purposes. Includes instruction in the military applications of space, space technology, aerospace engineering, systems architecture, orbital mechanics, launch and retrieval systems, ground support systems, satellite communications, and space-based sensor systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance understanding of biomechanical and biochemical interactions within dental pulp and periradicular tissues during endodontic disease progression and treatment. A critical challenge in endodontics lies in predicting how microscale variations in tissue morphology, bacterial biofilm dynamics, and biomechanical stress distribution influence treatment efficacy, particularly in complex root canal systems. Current clinical models lack the resolution to capture these multiscale interactions, limiting personalized treatment optimization. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating three-dimensional finite element analysis (FEA) of root canal biomechanics, agent-based modeling of pulpal biofilm communities, and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. High-resolution micro-CT scans of extracted teeth with diverse anatomical configurations will inform patient-specific FEA models simulating fluid dynamics during irrigation, stress distribution during instrumentation, and thermal profiles during obturation. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate microbial population dynamics under varying antimicrobial treatment conditions, incorporating spatial constraints from FEA outputs. Machine learning algorithms will analyze integrated datasets to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment success and optimize clinical parameter selection. The computational intensity of simultaneously resolving micron-scale anatomical features, stochastic microbial interactions, and nonlinear material properties necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized simulations and large-scale data synthesis. Expected outcomes include the first multiscale model linking microanatomical variability to clinical outcomes, predictive tools for irrigation protocol optimization, and a publicly accessible database of simulated treatment scenarios. This work bridges computational biology and clinical endodontics, offering novel insights into disease mechanisms while advancing data-driven strategies for precision endodontic care. Successful implementation will establish a computational paradigm applicable to other dental specialties addressing complex tissue-microbe-biomechanics interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the morphology, physiology, and pathology of human dental pulp and periradicular tissues, and prepares dentists to diagnose and treat internal diseases and injuries of teeth. Includes instruction in theory and practice of endodontics; pulpal disease; relationship of endodontic conditions to other dental/oral health issues; endodontic operative technique; and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and operational decision-making in correctional facilities, addressing systemic inefficiencies in staffing, inmate healthcare delivery, and crisis response protocols. Corrections administration faces unique challenges due to dynamic variables such as fluctuating inmate populations, heterogeneous security risks, and constrained budgets, which traditional management strategies often address reactively. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to build predictive models that integrate real-world data on inmate behavior, staff performance metrics, facility logistics, and historical incident reports. Agent-based modeling will simulate complex interactions between stakeholders under varying scenarios, while machine learning techniques will identify patterns in resource utilization bottlenecks and predict outcomes of policy adjustments. A key innovation involves adapting graph neural networks to map interdependencies between operational units (e.g., healthcare, security, rehabilitation programs) and quantify how localized decisions propagate through the system. The computational workload requires parallel processing of large-scale, sensitive datasets—including anonymized inmate records spanning 10+ years from three state systems—to maintain temporal and spatial resolution in simulations. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating optimized staffing schedules, emergency response plans, and resource distribution strategies tailored to facility-specific constraints. By modeling the cascading effects of administrative choices, this research aims to reduce operational costs while improving safety outcomes for staff and inmates. The project will demonstrate how advanced computing can address critical gaps in corrections management, offering a transferable methodology for resource-constrained public administration domains. Results will be disseminated through corrections policy forums and computational social science venues to bridge disciplinary divides.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: This project seeks to address the evolving challenges of digital content management and ethical decision-making in the publishing industry through advanced computational analysis. As digital publishing grows in scale and complexity, publishers face difficulties in optimizing workflows, predicting market trends, and navigating ethical dilemmas related to content curation and copyright compliance. Traditional analytical tools are insufficient for processing the vast, heterogeneous datasets generated by global eBook platforms, social media engagement metrics, and digital rights management systems. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines capable of analyzing multi-terabyte datasets spanning decades of publishing records, reader interactions, and legal disputes. Computational methods will include sentiment analysis of reader feedback to predict demand, network analysis to map author-publisher collaboration patterns, and simulation of digital distribution strategies under varying copyright regimes. Additionally, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to detect potential ethical conflicts in publishing contracts or content moderation decisions. The scale of data—encompassing millions of titles across multiple languages and formats—requires distributed computing architectures for efficient processing. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for dynamic pricing models, automated rights clearance workflows, and ethics-aware recommendation systems tailored to academic and trade publishing contexts. By quantifying historical trends in copyright disputes and content removal requests, the project will also generate novel insights into systemic biases in publishing workflows. These results aim to equip publishers with data-driven strategies for balancing commercial objectives with professional standards, ultimately strengthening trust in digital publishing ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process of managing the creation, publication, and distribution of print and electronic books and other text products and prepares individuals to manage the editorial, technical, and business aspects of publishing operations. Includes instruction in product planning and design, editing, author relations, business and copyright law, publishing industry operations, contracting and purchasing, product marketing, electronic publishing and commerce, history of publishing, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Marine engineering systems, particularly shipboard power and propulsion systems, face increasing demands for efficiency, reliability, and environmental compliance. Current computational models for optimizing these systems often lack the resolution to capture complex multiphysics interactions—such as fluid-structure-thermal coupling in marine diesel engines or dynamic loads on hybrid electric propulsion systems—limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-fidelity simulations of integrated marine engineering systems. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of combustion dynamics and emissions in variable-speed marine diesel engines under transient operating conditions; (2) finite element analysis (FEA) of mechanical and thermal stresses in shipboard power distribution networks incorporating renewable energy storage; and (3) machine learning-driven optimization of marine refrigeration and HVAC systems for energy-efficient operation. The computational workflows will leverage coupled solvers and adaptive meshing techniques to resolve multiscale phenomena, while GPU-accelerated algorithms will enable parametric studies of system configurations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for minimizing fuel consumption in heterogeneous engine fleets, strategies for mitigating vibration-induced failures in marine electrical infrastructure, and frameworks for real-time performance monitoring of shipboard thermal systems. By integrating HPC capabilities with experimental data from lab-scale marine engine testbeds, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in the digital twin development for next-generation vessels. The resource allocation will directly support the validation of simulation results against operational data from industry partners, accelerating the translation of computational insights into practical marine engineering solutions. This project will advance the marine technology field by establishing scalable computational methods for sustainable maritime infrastructure while training students in cutting-edge HPC applications for marine system design and optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in shipboard mechanical and electrical engineering and the maintenance and operation of marine engines, including gas, diesel, and steam engines. Includes instruction in automation, diesel-powered systems, electrical circuits and systems, engine performance, hydraulics, manufacturing, motor-powered systems, refrigeration and air-conditioning, steam-powered systems, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of stylistic and thematic evolution in American literature from the Colonial Era to the 20th century. Traditional literary scholarship often relies on close reading of select texts, limiting the scope of analysis to curated corpora. This research addresses the challenge of systematically tracing patterns across vast, heterogeneous collections of U.S. literary works—including novels, essays, and oral tradition transcriptions—to identify understudied connections between regional dialects, genre conventions, and sociocultural shifts. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic role labeling, dynamic topic modeling, and stylometric clustering. These methods will process digitized texts from repositories such as the HathiTrust Digital Library and the American Antiquarian Society’s archives, requiring parallelized workflows to handle ~50TB of unstructured data. Key tasks include training custom word embeddings to capture historical linguistic nuances, deploying distributed algorithms for network analysis of intertextual influence, and applying neural architectures to map sentiment trajectories in response to events like the Civil War or industrialization. HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, reducing runtime for iterative model training, and enabling scalable storage solutions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated texts with metadata on stylistic features and thematic tags, as well as visualizations of literary trends across time and geography. The project aims to reveal how marginalized voices (e.g., Indigenous oral traditions, early African American narratives) influenced canonical literary movements—a question difficult to address at this scale without computational support. By bridging digital humanities and American literary studies, this work will provide a replicable framework for data-driven inquiry into cultural production, offering new empirical foundations for theoretical debates about nationalism, regionalism, and identity in U.S. literature.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the United States from the Colonial Era to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of producing high-fidelity, real-time animations and interactive visual effects for applications in entertainment, virtual production, and immersive media. While advancements in animation tools have expanded creative possibilities, rendering photorealistic 3D environments with dynamic physics, complex particle systems, and AI-driven character interactions remains constrained by the latency and scalability of consumer-grade hardware. This bottleneck limits experimentation with emerging techniques such as neural rendering, volumetric capture integration, and multi-user virtual reality (VR) experiences. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize rendering workflows, optimize physics-based simulations, and train machine learning models for procedural asset generation. The project will focus on two primary objectives: (1) developing a scalable pipeline for real-time ray tracing of large-scale animated scenes using distributed rendering nodes, and (2) implementing GPU-accelerated fluid and cloth simulations that interact with AI-controlled virtual agents in VR environments. Computational methods will include adaptive mesh refinement for optimizing geometry processing, neural network-based denoising of path-traced outputs, and hybrid CPU-GPU task scheduling to minimize frame latency. Outcomes will be validated through benchmark testing against industry-standard animation packages and user studies measuring perceptual realism in interactive demos. Successful implementation will enable novel approaches to virtual production pipelines, reduce iteration times for complex effects, and provide students with hands-on experience deploying HPC solutions in media creation. The resource allocation will directly support 12 graduate students and faculty across six courses while generating open-source optimization frameworks tailored to animation workflows. This work aims to bridge the gap between academic research in communication technologies and professional animation practices, fostering innovation in storytelling through computationally intensive visual media.
cip_title: Animation, Interactive Technology, Video Graphics, and Special Effects
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use computer applications and related visual and sound imaging techniques to manipulate images and information originating as film, video, still photographs, digital copy, soundtracks, and physical objects in order to communicate messages simulating real-world content. Includes instruction in specialized camerawork and equipment operation and maintenance, image capture, computer programming, dubbing, CAD applications, and applications to specific commercial, industrial, and entertainment needs.

abstract: Clinical child psychology faces a critical challenge in understanding the complex, dynamic interactions between neurodevelopmental processes and behavioral outcomes in pediatric mental health disorders. Current approaches often struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets—including neuroimaging, behavioral assessments, and genetic markers—limiting insights into mechanisms underlying conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and childhood anxiety. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that map longitudinal trajectories of brain-behavior relationships in children aged 5–12. The research will utilize resting-state and task-based fMRI data, coupled with ecological momentary assessment (EMA) metrics and clinical diagnostic profiles, to model how neural network connectivity evolves alongside symptom severity and psychosocial stressors. Computational methods will include multilevel Bayesian modeling to account for nested data structures, graph theory-based network analyses to identify biomarkers of risk and resilience, and machine learning pipelines to predict individualized treatment responses. HPC resources are essential for processing large neuroimaging datasets (>10 TB), parallelizing computationally intensive simulations of neural circuit dynamics, and training deep learning architectures on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include the identification of transdiagnostic neurocognitive signatures linked to developmental psychopathology, which could inform early intervention strategies and personalized therapeutic approaches. By integrating clinical expertise with scalable computational tools, this work aims to advance precision medicine in pediatric mental health, bridging gaps between neurodevelopmental theory and clinical practice. The project aligns with the program’s focus on developmental neuropsychology and ethical, evidence-based care, while avoiding overlap with non-clinical psychology subfields.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the developmental processes of children and associated disorders and that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical child psychology. Includes instruction in developmental neuropsychology, child psychopathology, testing of children and adolescents, pediatric psychology, psychosocial variables in child development, clinical skills, family therapy, behavioral assessment and intervention, clinical skills, consultation, professional standards and ethics, and applications to topics such as infancy, childhood, and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the analysis of electroencephalographic (EEG) data through advanced computational methods to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in clinical neurophysiology. EEG recordings are critical for diagnosing epilepsy, sleep disorders, and neurological injuries, but manual interpretation remains time-intensive and subject to variability. Current computational approaches struggle with artifact contamination, low signal-to-noise ratios, and the complexity of modeling dynamic brain activity across large patient cohorts. To address these challenges, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled pipeline for automated EEG analysis. The pipeline will integrate machine learning models trained on multi-institutional EEG datasets to detect epileptiform discharges, classify sleep stages, and isolate pathological patterns. Computational workflows will include artifact removal via parallelized independent component analysis, feature extraction using wavelet transforms, and deep learning architectures (e.g., convolutional and recurrent neural networks) optimized for temporal-spatial EEG data. HPC resources will enable the processing of high-density EEG recordings (256+ channels) at scale, reduce latency in real-time monitoring simulations, and facilitate hyperparameter tuning for model optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for rapid, standardized EEG interpretation with quantified improvements in sensitivity and specificity compared to manual methods. The project will also generate open-source tools for signal preprocessing and anomaly detection, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational domains. By bridging gaps in neurodiagnostic technology, this work aims to accelerate diagnosis timelines, reduce clinician workload, and support precision medicine applications in neurology. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC resources can transform electrophysiological data analysis, directly aligning with the program’s focus on advancing patient care through technological innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to study and record electrical activity in the brain and nervous system for purposes of patient monitoring and supporting diagnoses. Includes instruction in patient communication and care; taking and abstracting patient histories; application of recording electrodes; EEG, EP, and PSG equipment operation and procedural techniques; and data recording and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of speech-language pathology (SLP) screenings and assessments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale speech datasets. Current clinical protocols for identifying communication disorders often rely on manual, time-intensive evaluations by speech-language pathologists (SLPs) and their assistants (SLPAs), which can limit scalability and introduce subjective variability. To address this, we propose developing computational models capable of automating the detection of speech and language anomalies in diverse populations. The research will utilize a corpus of de-identified speech samples from individuals with disorders such as aphasia, dysarthria, and childhood apraxia, alongside typical speakers, to train machine learning algorithms. These models will process acoustic features (e.g., pitch, articulation rates) and linguistic patterns (e.g., syntactic complexity, semantic coherence) using neural networks optimized via HPC clusters. The computational workflow will involve parallelized feature extraction, hyperparameter tuning, and validation against clinical diagnoses to ensure robustness. By integrating these tools into a user-friendly interface, SLPAs could conduct preliminary screenings with greater consistency, allowing SLPs to focus on nuanced diagnostic and therapeutic tasks. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for disorder classification, open-source tools for speech analysis, and benchmarks for computational efficiency in processing real-world clinical data. This work holds significance for reducing disparities in access to SLP services, particularly in underserved regions, while advancing research on the neurocomputational underpinnings of communication disorders. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive training processes, which exceed the capacity of standard institutional infrastructure. Successful implementation will bridge gaps between computational research and clinical practice, fostering innovation in health professions education and patient care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug development pipelines necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in optimizing therapeutic efficacy, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory compliance. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate computational workflows central to preclinical drug design and industrial process optimization. A key focus is the integration of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML) models to predict drug-target binding affinities, stability under industrial-scale production conditions, and potential metabolic degradation pathways. Current in silico methods for these tasks are limited by the computational expense of simulating large protein-ligand systems or microbial expression vectors over biologically relevant timescales. By parallelizing MD simulations across GPU nodes, we aim to model conformational dynamics of plasmid-derived biologics and small-molecule drug candidates at unprecedented resolution. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on existing pharmacokinetic datasets to predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties, with model validation performed using molecular docking results. A second component focuses on optimizing microbial strain engineering for industrial drug synthesis through genome-scale metabolic modeling. Constraint-based reconstruction and analysis (COBRA) of bacterial and fungal systems will be scaled using distributed computing to identify gene knockout targets that maximize yield while minimizing byproduct formation. These computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from partner pharmaceutical labs. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of virtual screening pipelines, reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error experimentation. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for candidate drug prioritization, strain design blueprints for scalable synthesis, and quality control protocols informed by stability simulations. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on bridging pharmacological science and industrial management by providing computational tools to de-risk translational processes, streamline intellectual property strategy through early patentability assessments, and enhance regulatory compliance via in silico quality assurance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific application of pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and industrial management to the development, production, marketing, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. Includes instruction in industrial microbiology, plasmids, expression vectors, protein chemistry, assay and evaluation, drug synthesis and purification, quality control, industrial management, production security, patent procedures, intellectual property regulations and issues, patent enforcement and defense, and research design and testing.

abstract: The proposed research aims to develop a multiscale computational framework to investigate the evolutionary dynamics of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) under environmental stress, a critical challenge in genomics and evolutionary biology. Current models often fail to integrate stochastic gene expression, epigenetic modifications, and population-level selection pressures in a unified system, limiting predictive insights into adaptive mechanisms. To address this gap, we will construct a hybrid agent-based model (ABM) coupled with partial differential equations (PDEs) to simulate GRN behavior across intracellular, cellular, and population scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity of network interactions, simulate large populations over evolutionary timescales, and perform parameter sensitivity analyses. The ABM will incorporate stochastic reaction-diffusion processes for transcription factor dynamics, while PDEs model nutrient gradients and spatial competition in heterogeneous environments. Parallelized algorithms will optimize runtime for ensemble simulations, and machine learning tools will identify emergent patterns in adaptation strategies. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how stress-induced mutagenesis and epigenetic plasticity jointly shape evolvability in GRNs, with applications to antibiotic resistance and cancer progression. This work will produce open-source software for scalable GRN simulations, enabling the broader community to test hypotheses about evolutionary trade-offs and resilience thresholds. By bridging molecular-scale stochasticity with population-level selection, the project advances mathematical foundations for predicting adaptation in dynamic environments, directly supporting goals in synthetic biology and precision medicine. The requested computing allocation will enable 10⁶ core-hours for parameter exploration across biologically realistic regimes, which is infeasible with local cluster resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to genomics, molecular modeling, structural biology, ecology, evolutionary biology and systems of analysis of neurobiology, physiology, and metabolism. Includes instruction in computational mathematics, chaos and nonlinear systems, perturbation methods, evolutionary biology, molecular biology, bioinformatics, and neurobiology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex legal and regulatory frameworks governing urban land development, with a focus on identifying systemic inefficiencies and unintended consequences in zoning, environmental compliance, and property rights adjudication. The project addresses a critical gap in computational legal studies: the lack of scalable, data-driven models to simulate interactions between evolving land-use policies, stakeholder behavior, and market outcomes. By integrating large-scale legal text corpora (including court decisions, municipal codes, and regulatory filings) with geospatial and economic datasets, we aim to develop a novel computational framework that maps how legal constraints propagate through real estate development ecosystems. The methodology combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques for semantic analysis of regulatory documents, agent-based modeling to simulate developer and municipal decision-making, and network analysis to trace cascading legal impacts across jurisdictions. Key challenges include processing terabytes of unstructured legal texts, training domain-specific language models for statutory interpretation tasks, and running iterative policy scenario simulations at metropolitan-scale resolution. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a predictive tool for assessing litigation risks associated with contested zoning reforms, 2) identification of regulatory bottlenecks in climate-resilient infrastructure permitting, and 3) quantitative evidence supporting harmonization of cross-jurisdictional land-use policies. This work bridges computational law and urban planning, offering a template for data-intensive legal research with direct applications to sustainable development governance. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive NLP pipelines and parallelized policy simulations that cannot feasibly run on conventional infrastructure.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for verifying the reliability and security of complex, distributed software systems through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Modern software systems, particularly those deployed in cloud-native or edge computing environments, face challenges in maintaining functional correctness under dynamic workloads, adversarial inputs, and heterogeneous hardware configurations. Traditional verification methods struggle with the combinatorial explosion of possible system states, while existing machine learning-based approaches often lack formal guarantees. Our research will employ probabilistic model checking enhanced with neural symbolic reasoning to address these limitations, requiring significant computational resources to manage state-space complexity. The proposed methodology integrates discrete-event simulation, Markov decision processes, and graph neural networks within a high-performance computing (HPC) environment to enable parallel evaluation of system behaviors across multiple fidelity levels. Key innovations include a hybrid architecture that partitions verification tasks between CPU clusters (for exhaustive state exploration) and GPU-accelerated nodes (for neural-guided abstraction refinement). The project will utilize MPI-based distributed computing for large-scale parameter sweeps and leverage containerized workflows to manage heterogeneous software dependencies. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for probabilistic software verification, quantitative benchmarks comparing computational efficiency against existing methods, and novel insights into trade-offs between verification completeness and resource allocation in distributed systems. By enabling more rigorous analysis of safety-critical software components in autonomous systems and IoT networks, this work aims to advance software engineering practices while contributing methodological innovations at the intersection of formal methods and machine learning. Successful implementation requires access to HPC resources capable of supporting memory-intensive simulations across 100+ concurrent nodes, with estimated compute needs of 250,000 core-hours annually.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, analysis, verification, validation, implementation, and maintenance of computer software systems using a variety of computer languages. Includes instruction in discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, computer science, managerial science, and applications to complex computer systems.

abstract: This project seeks to resolve how microbial metabolic networks dynamically interact with mineral weathering processes across spatial and temporal scales, bridging gaps between microbial ecology, geochemistry, and reactive transport modeling. A critical challenge in geobiology lies in predicting how microbial communities influence silicate weathering rates—a process central to global carbon cycling and climate regulation over geological timescales. Existing models often oversimplify microbial dynamics or mineral surface reactivity, limiting their ability to capture feedbacks between microbial evolution, community assembly, and geochemical fluxes. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based microbial simulations with high-resolution mineral surface reaction models. The approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to couple individual-based models of microbial metabolism (tracking energy allocation, extracellular enzyme production, and population dynamics) with lattice Boltzmann simulations of dissolution-precipitation reactions at mineral-fluid interfaces. This hybrid method will resolve pore-scale geochemical gradients and cell-mineral interactions while scaling to meter-sized systems over millennial timescales. Key computational challenges include managing stochastic microbial processes alongside deterministic reactive transport equations and optimizing parallelization for heterogeneous workflows. The project will utilize existing codebases (e.g., BioFVM for microbial dynamics, Chombo-Crunch for reactive transport) adapted via custom CUDA kernels and MPI-based task distribution. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of how microbial evolutionary trajectories alter weathering kinetics under varying climatic forcings, (2) identification of tipping points in community-mineral coevolution that drive regime shifts in carbon sequestration, and (3) open-source tools enabling reactive transport models to incorporate adaptive microbial behavior. Results will advance predictive models of Earth’s biogeochemical cycles and inform strategies for enhanced weathering-based climate interventions. The computational demands—requiring >500,000 core-hours for ensemble simulations across parameter spaces—necessitate HPC resources to achieve statistically robust insights into this nonlinear, multiscale system.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of how living things interact with geological systems. Includes instruction in evolution of Earth systems, geochemistry, geology, geomicrobiology, marine chemistry, paleobiology, paleoecology, paleontology, and petrology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling and synthesizing immersive, multidimensional soundscapes that integrate cultural, spatial, and temporal dynamics. Sound arts research faces a critical challenge in simulating and rendering complex acoustic environments that reflect diverse cultural narratives while maintaining technical precision, particularly in real-time interactive contexts. Current tools for spatial audio design and dynamic sound synthesis are limited by the computational demands of high-fidelity wave propagation modeling, machine learning–driven soundscape generation, and multi-channel spatialization. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these bottlenecks through parallelized acoustic simulation, large-scale neural network training for generative sound models, and real-time distributed processing for interactive installations. Computational methods will include finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations of 3D reverberation profiles, transformer-based models trained on ethnographically curated sound databases, and GPU-accelerated spatial audio engines for multichannel diffusion. The research will produce novel algorithms for culturally situated sound design, validated through collaborations with performing artists and public installations. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for adaptive soundscape generation, a repository of annotated computational models linking acoustic parameters to cultural contexts, and performance benchmarks for HPC-driven audio art. By enabling the creation of large-scale, dynamically responsive sound works that integrate technical rigor with cultural specificity, this project aims to expand the methodological possibilities of sound arts while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between performing arts, computational acoustics, and critical sound studies. The requested resources will directly support GPU node allocations for neural network training, high-memory nodes for wave simulation, and low-latency networking for distributed real-time audio processing across campus performance spaces.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on sound as a form of cultural expression, and its relationship to other disciplines such as computer programming, performance, and video. Includes instruction in acoustics; arranging, composing, and editing music; music theory; musicology; orchestration and scoring; and sound design.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociotechnical dynamics of AI-driven urban surveillance systems through a computational lens, integrating policy analysis, ethical frameworks, and large-scale behavioral simulations. As cities globally adopt artificial intelligence for public safety and infrastructure management, the interplay between algorithmic decision-making, civic trust, and regulatory efficacy remains understudied. The research problem centers on modeling how heterogeneous sociopolitical values—embedded in urban populations—interact with automated surveillance architectures, potentially amplifying biases or eroding public consent. Using high-performance computing resources, we will develop agent-based models simulating multi-stakeholder decision networks (citizens, municipal authorities, AI developers) across diverse demographic and governance contexts. These models will incorporate real-world datasets on policy adoption rates, anonymized mobility patterns, and public sentiment metrics derived from social media. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess emergent outcomes under varying ethical constraint parameters (e.g., transparency thresholds, accountability mechanisms) to quantify trade-offs between surveillance efficacy and societal equity. The computational framework will enable sensitivity analyses at unprecedented scale, testing how localized cultural norms and legacy infrastructures mediate the global proliferation of surveillance technologies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of scenario projections to inform adaptive governance frameworks, alongside novel metrics for evaluating "algorithmic accountability thresholds" in urban policy contexts. By bridging computational social science with Science and Technology Studies, this work aims to establish predictive tools for anticipating second-order societal impacts of intelligent systems while advancing methodological integration across technical and humanistic domains.
detailed_field: History/ philosophy of science, technology, and society
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the contemporary social and public policy ramifications of science and technology, the interrelationship of science and engineering with the public policy process, and the social and ethical dimensions of scientific and technological enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of immersive audio production in the Recording Arts Technology field, where traditional workstations struggle to process high-channel-count spatial audio and real-time acoustic simulations. Emerging formats like 6DoF (six degrees of freedom) sound for augmented/virtual reality require dynamic, latency-sensitive processing of dozens of audio streams alongside physics-based reverberation modeling—tasks that exceed the capabilities of standard systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable workflows for next-generation spatial audio production. The research will employ parallelized digital signal processing algorithms optimized for GPU clusters, enabling real-time convolution of complex impulse responses for environmental acoustics and AI-driven source separation for immersive mixing. A key focus involves adapting machine learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) to train neural networks on HPC infrastructure for tasks such as automated dialogue enhancement in multi-mic field recordings and adaptive noise reduction in live broadcast scenarios. The project will validate these methods through case studies simulating large-scale concert acoustics and interactive game audio environments. Successful implementation will provide practitioners with open-source tools for efficient high-density audio rendering, reducing post-production timelines for film and interactive media by an estimated 40%. Outcomes will advance the field’s capacity to handle increasingly complex auditory experiences while establishing best practices for HPC integration in non-STEM media disciplines. All developed code and benchmark data will be shared through industry partnerships and the AES Audio Engineering Society’s research portal, directly supporting the program’s mission to bridge technical innovation with creative practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of sound recordings as finished products or as components of film/video, broadcast, live, or mixed media productions. Includes instruction in sound equipment operation and maintenance; music, dialogue, and sound effects recording; soundtrack editing; dubbing and mixing; sound engineering; tape, disk, and CD production; digital recording and transmission; amplification and modulation; and working with producers, editors, directors, artists, and production managers.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of synaptic connectivity alterations in driving hyperexcitability within hippocampal circuits implicated in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE). Despite advances in understanding cellular mechanisms of TLE, the relationship between micro-scale synaptic pathology and macro-scale network dysfunction remains poorly characterized. We aim to bridge this gap by constructing a biophysically detailed computational model of the hippocampal CA1 circuit, integrating experimental data from rodent models of epilepsy. The model will simulate thousands of neurons with morphologically realistic dendritic structures and dynamic synaptic properties, incorporating pathological features such as interneuron loss and axonal sprouting. Large-scale parallel simulations will quantify how these alterations perturb excitation-inhibition balance, promoting seizure-like synchronization. Machine learning approaches will then analyze simulation outputs to identify critical connectivity patterns and dynamic biomarkers of hyperexcitability. This work requires HPC resources to manage the computational intensity of simulating multi-compartment neurons with high temporal resolution, as well as to perform parameter space explorations across diverse network configurations. Expected outcomes include a mechanistic framework linking synaptic-level changes to emergent network pathology in TLE, validated against in vivo electrophysiological recordings. By pinpointing circuit nodes most sensitive to intervention, this research could inform targeted neuromodulatory therapies for drug-resistant epilepsy. The project underscores the necessity of HPC in modern neuroanatomical research, enabling hypothesis-driven modeling at scales unachievable with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular studies of neuronal and glial cells and circuits, neural transmitters and receptors, neuronal signaling processes, membrane and synapse structure and communication, autonomic function, nervous system circuitry and mapping, and anatomical and functional basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling the dynamics of cross-cultural information transmission in decentralized networks, integrating methods from information theory, sociocultural anthropology, and complex systems analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how nonlinear cultural variables—such as semantic ambiguity, social hierarchy biases, and ritualized communication practices—influence the fidelity and evolution of information across heterogeneous populations. Current models often oversimplify cultural context as noise or static variables, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios like public health messaging or heritage preservation. The proposed work will employ agent-based simulations to map how multi-layered cultural parameters interact with network topologies, using a novel adaptive encoding system that represents information as context-dependent semantic graphs. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating 10^5–10^6 agents with dynamically evolving rule sets, each incorporating individual and community-level cultural priors. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess stability thresholds for information propagation across synthetically generated cultural landscapes, validated against ethnographic datasets spanning oral traditions, digital folklore, and crisis communication patterns. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for predicting information distortion hotspots in culturally fragmented populations and optimization strategies for designing context-aware communication protocols. The computational architecture will also enable reverse-engineering cultural signatures from observed information diffusion patterns, with applications in misinformation mitigation and intercultural resource allocation. By bridging technical and humanistic approaches to information dynamics, this work aims to establish new metrics for evaluating cultural resilience in socio-technical systems while advancing methodological integration across computational social science and digital humanities domains.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on computing, computer science, and information science and systems. Such programs are undifferentiated as to title and content and are not to be confused with specific programs in computer science, information science, or related support services.

abstract: The increasing complexity of next-generation wireless communication systems necessitates advanced computational methods to address challenges in resource allocation, interference management, and energy efficiency. Current analytical models struggle to capture the dynamic behavior of large-scale heterogeneous networks operating at millimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing distributed antenna systems and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in ultra-dense urban environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement parallelized electromagnetic wave propagation models using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods coupled with multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for stochastic channel modeling with distributed optimization techniques to balance spectral efficiency and power consumption across dynamically changing topologies. By scaling these simulations to networks exceeding 10,000 nodes—a magnitude beyond current experimental testbeds—we aim to identify fundamental tradeoffs between latency, reliability, and energy use in extreme-density scenarios. The resulting datasets and validated models will provide critical insights for 6G protocol development while establishing open-source tools for massive MIMO beamforming optimization. This work directly addresses the computational bottlenecks preventing real-time adaptation in software-defined radios and lays the foundation for energy-aware network architectures capable of supporting emerging applications in augmented reality and industrial IoT. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential for achieving the required simulation throughput and enabling parameter space exploration at unprecedented scales.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronics, and Communications Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing patient care efficiency and safety in settings reliant on health aides, attendants, and orderlies. Despite their pivotal role in routine care delivery, resource constraints, variable patient acuity, and dynamic workflows often lead to suboptimal staffing decisions, delayed interventions, and preventable adverse events. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model care delivery processes, predict patient needs, and simulate intervention outcomes. Using anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data spanning 50,000+ patient encounters, we will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate interactions between health aides, patients, and environmental factors across diverse clinical scenarios.
