These models will integrate real-time patient vital signs, mobility metrics, and care task logs to identify patterns predictive of deterioration or unmet needs. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms (e.g., recurrent neural networks, gradient-boosted trees) will be trained to forecast staffing requirements and prioritize tasks under fluctuating workloads. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, running parallelized simulations across 10,000+ parameter combinations, and validating models against historical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for proactive patient monitoring, (2) evidence-based guidelines for task delegation and shift scheduling, and (3) open-source simulation tools to train health aides in high-risk scenarios. By elucidating the relationship between care processes and patient outcomes, this work will directly inform curriculum updates for health aide training programs and institutional policies aimed at reducing preventable harm. The scalability of our computational approach offers transformative potential for resource-limited settings where health aides serve as frontline caregivers.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic workflow allocation in decentralized clerical environments through advanced computational modeling, addressing inefficiencies in task prioritization and resource distribution within modern hybrid office settings. Traditional clerical support systems often rely on static hierarchies or manual oversight, struggling to adapt to fluctuating demands, heterogeneous skill sets among personnel, and real-time operational disruptions. The study will develop an adaptive framework using agent-based modeling and reinforcement learning to simulate complex interactions between administrative workers, digital tools, and evolving task queues. High-performance computing resources are required to process multi-dimensional datasets capturing communication patterns, equipment usage logs, and task completion metrics across distributed office networks. The computational architecture will integrate discrete-event simulation with natural language processing analysis of email/chat corpora to model decision-making processes under varying constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for intelligent task routing, evidence-based thresholds for automated delegation triggers, and quantifiable benchmarks for cross-training effectiveness in general office occupations. By bridging computational social science with operational analytics, this work aims to establish new paradigms for responsive administrative support systems that balance human judgment with machine learning optimization. The resulting models will provide actionable insights for configuring adaptive office technologies while preserving the critical role of clerical workers' situational expertise in unstructured problem-solving scenarios.
cip_title: General Office Occupations and Clerical Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide basic administrative support under the supervision of office managers, administrative assistants, secretaries, and other office personnel. Includes instruction in typing, keyboarding, filing, general business correspondence, office equipment operation, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to enhance the creation of dynamic, interactive medical visualizations for surgical planning, patient education, and biomedical research. Current methods for generating high-fidelity 3D anatomical models and simulations face limitations in scalability, real-time interactivity, and integration of multimodal datasets (e.g., MRI, CT, histology). Medical illustrators require tools capable of processing large-scale biomedical data while maintaining anatomical precision and artistic adaptability—a challenge compounded by the increasing complexity of clinical and educational demands. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize two parallel workflows: (1) AI-driven segmentation and rendering of volumetric medical imaging data using deep learning architectures (3D U-Net, GANs) trained on annotated clinical datasets, and (2) physics-based simulations of tissue deformation and fluid dynamics for procedural animations in virtual surgical training environments. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid processing of terabyte-scale imaging repositories through distributed GPU-accelerated pipelines, while supporting iterative model refinement via parameter sweeps for biomechanical simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating patient-specific anatomical models with automated texture mapping, real-time interactive visualizations for VR/AR platforms, and validated benchmarks for computational efficiency in medical animation workflows. This work will directly benefit surgical training programs and patient communication initiatives while establishing new best practices for computationally intensive medical illustration processes. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations, maintaining data security compliance for sensitive medical images, and enabling collaborative access for interdisciplinary teams spanning clinical experts, computer scientists, and medical illustrators.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles and techniques of art and computer-assisted imaging, graphics, and animation to create visual materials to facilitate the recording and dissemination of biomedical knowledge for educational, research, and clinical purposes. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, histology, embryology, neuroanatomy, medical terminology, artistic media and techniques, illustration techniques, three-dimensional modeling, prosthetics, data display design, exhibit design and production, medical photography, multimedia, computer graphics and animation, digital imaging, business management, production technology, and instructional design.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment planning relies on accurately predicting the biomechanical response of craniofacial structures to applied forces, yet current methods often depend on generalized clinical protocols that fail to account for individual variations in bone density, periodontal ligament properties, and craniofacial growth patterns. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model patient-specific orthodontic tooth movement and optimize treatment outcomes using advanced biomechanical simulations. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of static, population-averaged treatment approaches by integrating dynamic, patient-specific data into predictive models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the computational complexity of simulating interactions between teeth, alveolar bone, and orthodontic appliances at biologically relevant spatial and temporal scales. The proposed computational approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) with machine learning algorithms to analyze cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans, intraoral scans, and clinical force data from 200 patients undergoing orthodontic treatment. HPC-enabled parallel processing will facilitate the creation of multi-scale models that incorporate micromechanical bone remodeling processes, viscoelastic periodontal ligament behavior, and nonlinear material properties of orthodontic appliances. Machine learning components will iteratively refine model parameters using longitudinal treatment outcome data, enabling real-time adjustments to force magnitude and direction in simulated treatment plans. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for estimating tooth movement trajectories under varying biomechanical conditions and identifying patient-specific risk factors for root resorption or delayed treatment progress. This work will advance personalized orthodontics by enabling clinicians to simulate treatment scenarios, optimize appliance design, and mitigate adverse outcomes prior to clinical intervention. The computational framework will also provide foundational insights into the biomechanical drivers of craniofacial adaptation, with potential applications in surgical orthodontics and cleft palate rehabilitation. Successful implementation requires access to HPC resources capable of handling terabytes of 3D image data and supporting GPU-accelerated simulations with submillimeter spatial resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the guidance of growing dental structures and the correction of misalignments, disproportionate growth, and traumas caused by genetics, disease, injuries, and dysfunctional behaviors. Includes instruction in craniofacial growth and development, malocclusion, design and fabrication of orthodontic appliances, craniofacial alignment, physiological function and analysis, cephalometrics, model analysis, space analysis, surgical orthodontics, cleft lip and palate, and treatment planning and management.

abstract: The increasing demand for precision in equine hoof care necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize farriery practices, which currently rely heavily on empirical knowledge and manual craftsmanship. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical interactions between horseshoes, hoof morphology, and equine locomotion through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled modeling and simulation. Traditional approaches to corrective shoeing and gait analysis lack the granularity to account for dynamic, three-dimensional stress distributions or material behavior under varying load conditions, leading to suboptimal outcomes in hoof health and performance. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain modeling of hoof-shoe systems, machine learning (ML)-driven gait pattern recognition, and thermodynamic simulations of metal forging processes. The FEA component will model hoof tissue response to different shoe geometries and alloys, calibrated using micro-CT scan data of equine hooves. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze motion-capture datasets from equine gait laboratories to identify correlations between shoeing modifications and biomechanical efficiency. A parallel computational study will simulate coal- and gas-based forging environments to optimize thermal profiles for producing durable, customized shoes. By leveraging HPC resources, these computationally intensive models—which require iterative parameter adjustments and high-resolution volumetric meshes—can be executed at scales unachievable with local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for farriers to preemptively address pathologies like laminitis, data-driven guidelines for alloy selection, and energy-efficient forging protocols. This interdisciplinary effort merges veterinary biomechanics, materials science, and computational engineering, establishing a novel paradigm for evidence-based farrier science while preserving the artisan traditions central to the field. The resulting open-access models and datasets will serve as foundational resources for both practitioners and educators in this specialized domain.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to become specialists in equine hoof care (farriers). Includes instruction in equine science, equine health and first aid, general horseshoeing, corrective horseshoeing, gait analysis, and metal forging techniques using gas or coal.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized care coordination for patients with complex, overlapping chronic conditions in community-based health settings. Health aides, who serve as frontline support in these environments, often lack access to real-time computational tools to integrate and interpret heterogeneous patient data streams—including wearable sensor outputs, electronic health record snippets, and patient-reported symptom logs—into actionable insights. The research aims to develop a machine learning (ML) framework that dynamically synthesizes these multimodal datasets to predict acute health event risks (e.g., falls, medication non-adherence crises) and recommend preemptive interventions. A core innovation lies in adapting transformer-based architectures, typically used in natural language processing, to model temporal patterns in sparse, irregularly sampled physiological and behavioral data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train these models on synthetic datasets mirroring real-world noise and missingness, followed by validation on de-identified data from community health partnerships. Computational workflows will prioritize low-latency inference to enable integration with mobile health aide platforms. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source pipeline for lightweight model deployment and evidence-based guidelines for health aide workflows that balance predictive accuracy with interpretability. By focusing on the understudied intersection of edge computing, temporal ML, and community health operations, this work aims to bridge a critical gap in decision support tools for non-specialist caregivers, ultimately reducing preventable hospitalizations in underserved populations. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for parallelized hyperparameter optimization and large-scale synthetic data generation—necessitate GPU-accelerated clusters and scalable storage solutions, aligning with HPC infrastructure capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and assistance to patients under the direct supervision of other health care professionals, and/or to perform routine maintenance and general assistance in health care facilities and laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural and biomechanical underpinnings of speech motor control deficits in acquired communication disorders, with a focus on post-stroke dysarthria and apraxia of speech. Current understanding of how cortical reorganization interacts with articulatory kinematics during recovery remains limited, hindering the development of personalized neuromotor rehabilitation protocols. The research employs a multimodal approach integrating high-density electroencephalography (EEG), dynamic electromagnetic articulography (EMA), and computational modeling to map disrupted sensorimotor networks and simulate compensatory articulatory strategies. A critical barrier is the need to process terabyte-scale neuroimaging datasets synchronized with submillisecond kinematic data while running biophysically realistic neural network models of speech motor planning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address three core challenges: (1) real-time processing of cortical oscillatory dynamics during speech production using time-frequency decomposition across 128 EEG channels, (2) biomechanical inverse modeling of EMA-derived tongue/jaw movement trajectories to estimate muscle activation patterns, and (3) reinforcement learning simulations to optimize model parameters for predicting treatment-responsive patient subtypes. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition for feature extraction from spatiotemporal data matrices and implement multiscale modeling pipelines using Message Passing Interface (MPI) frameworks. Expected outcomes include a novel computational taxonomy of speech motor impairment phenotypes tied to specific neuromotor compensation mechanisms and an open-source platform for simulating articulatory- neural coupling dynamics. This work will advance precision rehabilitation tools for communication disorders while establishing scalable methods for analyzing high-dimensional sensorimotor datasets in clinical populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: Sustainable management of natural resource-based tourism requires understanding complex, dynamic interactions between ecological systems, visitor behavior, and socio-economic priorities. Current models often lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale environmental data (e.g., habitat health, climate projections) with granular human activity patterns (e.g., trail use, seasonal visitation trends), limiting the ability to forecast trade-offs between conservation goals and tourism demands. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a spatially explicit, agent-based modeling framework to simulate visitor behavior, ecological impacts, and economic outcomes under diverse climate and management scenarios. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize models using high-resolution GPS tracking data from visitors, remote sensing datasets (e.g., vegetation cover, erosion risk), and longitudinal socio-economic records from regional tourism operators. Computational workflows will employ machine learning to identify nonlinear relationships between environmental conditions and visitation patterns, coupled with Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainties in long-term ecosystem service projections. By simulating thousands of policy interventions—such as trail rerouting, carrying capacity adjustments, or fee structure changes—the models will identify strategies that minimize ecological degradation while maintaining equitable access and economic viability. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools for public land managers, validated against field data from three case study regions in vulnerable alpine and coastal ecosystems. These tools will advance adaptive management practices by enabling real-time scenario testing, with particular relevance to mitigating climate-driven disruptions to tourism systems. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to process terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and execute parallelized simulations across heterogeneous landscapes, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Results will directly inform state and federal tourism policies while contributing methodological innovations to computational ecology and recreation science.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Recreation and Tourism
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, and manage tourism in a natural resource setting, with an emphasis on applying environmentally sound, culturally sensitive, and economically sustainable principles. Includes instruction in environmental studies; natural resource management and interpretation; tourism planning, management, and policies; public land use management and policies; communications; marketing; and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the real-time coordination mechanisms underlying ensemble musical performance through advanced computational modeling. Despite extensive study of individual musicianship, the dynamic interplay between performers—encompassing auditory, visual, and gestural cues—remains poorly quantified. Traditional analytical methods lack the temporal resolution and scalability to model these complex interactions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal performance data, including synchronized motion capture, high-fidelity audio recordings, and physiological sensor inputs from live ensemble sessions. Machine learning techniques, such as recurrent neural networks and dynamic time warping algorithms, will be employed to identify patterns of synchronization, leadership dynamics, and error correction strategies among performers. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets and real-time simulation of interaction scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for ensemble coordination, validated against expert assessments and historical performance archives. This research will advance the understanding of collaborative musicianship, offering pedagogical tools to optimize rehearsal strategies and performance resilience. Additionally, the computational pipelines developed may be adapted to study interaction dynamics in broader creative contexts, reinforcing the role of music performance as a critical domain for human behavior research.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to master musical instruments and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers. Includes instruction on one or more specific instruments from various instrumental groupings.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern graphic communications production processes, particularly the high material waste, energy consumption, and quality inconsistencies associated with traditional and digital printing methods. While advancements in prepress, press, and postpress technologies have expanded production capabilities, optimizing parameters such as ink viscosity, substrate compatibility, and press speed remains challenging due to the complex interplay of physical, chemical, and mechanical variables. This research proposes a computational framework to model and simulate multi-phase printing workflows, including offset lithography, flexography, and digital imaging, to identify optimal process configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) of fluid dynamics in ink transfer, machine learning-driven predictive modeling of color consistency across substrates, and Monte Carlo simulations of postpress finishing outcomes under variable environmental conditions. By integrating real-world sensor data from press equipment with synthetic datasets generated through computational models, the project aims to develop adaptive algorithms that reduce trial-and-error calibration in production settings. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-access simulation tools for the graphic communications community, empirically validated guidelines for sustainable material usage, and a predictive dashboard for minimizing energy consumption in high-volume print runs. This work will directly support the graphic communications industry’s transition to data-driven, environmentally conscious practices while maintaining fidelity in color reproduction and tactile quality—critical factors in packaging, publishing, and branded media. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-resolution 3D rendering, parallelized fluid dynamics computations, and iterative training of neural networks required to achieve these objectives at production-relevant scales.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the manufacture and distribution or transmission of graphic communications products. Includes instruction in the prepress, press, and postpress phases of production operations and processes such as offset lithography, flexography, gravure, letterpress, screen printing, foil stamping, digital imaging, and other reproduction methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of adaptive learning environments through large-scale simulation of student interaction patterns, with the goal of identifying scalable strategies for personalizing education in heterogeneous classrooms. While advances in educational technology have enabled dynamic content delivery, existing systems often struggle to balance real-time adaptability with computational efficiency, particularly in under-resourced schools where device availability and network reliability vary widely. The research problem centers on developing lightweight machine learning (ML) models capable of predicting optimal intervention points in student workflows without requiring continuous cloud connectivity or high-end hardware. Using anonymized interaction datasets from open-source learning platforms, we will train ensemble models combining recurrent neural networks with graph-based attention mechanisms to map temporal dependencies in student problem-solving behaviors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized hyperparameter optimization across simulated classroom scenarios, varying parameters such as device latency, student-to-device ratios, and intermittent connectivity. The computational approach further involves agent-based modeling to test how localized edge computing architectures could distribute model inference tasks across classroom devices. Expected outcomes include a framework for deploying adaptive ML systems in low-infrastructure environments, accompanied by benchmarks quantifying trade-offs between model accuracy and resource consumption. By addressing the computational barriers to equitable implementation of personalized learning technologies, this work contributes to educational studies through its focus on the sociotechnical intersection of pedagogy, resource constraints, and algorithmic efficiency. Results will inform both the design of future educational tools and policy discussions surrounding technology integration in diverse school environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory, practice, organization of, and public policies in education. Includes instruction in learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of dynamic extracellular vesicle (EV) membrane microdomains in mediating cell-to-cell communication during cardiovascular calcification, a process with poorly understood molecular drivers. While EVs are recognized as critical mediators of pathological mineralization, the biophysical mechanisms governing their selective cargo loading and targeting in calcific microenvironments remain opaque. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate EV membrane reorganization at atomic resolution under varying calcium-phosphate concentrations, integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning-driven analysis of EV surface protein clustering patterns. Multi-scale models will map temporal changes in lipid-protein interactions across >10^6 lipid molecules and embedded receptors (e.g., annexins), simulating systems exceeding 20 million atoms over microsecond timescales. Concurrently, graph neural networks will predict emergent clustering behaviors from simulation trajectories, identifying stable microdomain architectures that correlate with in vitro EV uptake assays in calcifying vascular cells. The computational workflow requires parallelized MD codes (NAMD, GROMACS) optimized for GPU clusters and distributed training of deep learning models on terabytes of trajectory data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking EV membrane dynamics to pathological mineralization efficiency, with potential applications in developing EV-based diagnostic markers or engineered vesicles for targeted calcium chelation. This interdisciplinary approach bridges nanoscale biophysical modeling with clinical cardiovascular research—a niche not fully addressed by traditional bioinformatics or molecular biology paradigms—while advancing computational methods for membrane systems biology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the molecular and cellular basis of disease, and the application of this knowledge to the development of new clinical and diagnostic tools, medications, and therapies. Includes instruction in cell biology, molecular biology, physiology, pharmacology, biochemistry, genetics, pathology, molecular immunology, research and quantitative methods, and biomedical research computing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of legislative decision-making and coalition dynamics in multiparty democracies. A central challenge in political science is understanding how institutional rules, party preferences, and strategic interactions shape policy outcomes. Existing models often simplify computational constraints, limiting their ability to simulate complex bargaining processes or analyze large-scale voting records. This project addresses these gaps by developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate legislative negotiations under varying electoral systems and party configurations. The ABMs will incorporate game-theoretic decision rules, historical voting data, and ideological positioning derived from manifesto texts. Additionally, machine learning methods will be applied to identify latent coalition patterns in cross-national legislative datasets spanning 25 democracies. Computational demands arise from the need to run thousands of parallel simulations with heterogeneous agents, process high-dimensional text corpora for ideological scaling, and train ensemble models on sparse, imbalanced voting records. The requested HPC resources will enable parameter space exploration, real-time sensitivity testing, and validation against historical case studies. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for predicting coalition stability under institutional reforms, (2) empirical insights into the trade-offs between proportionality and governance efficiency in electoral system design, and (3) open-source tools for computational legislative analysis. By integrating formal theory with large-scale computational experiments, this work aims to enhance scholarly understanding of how political institutions mediate representation and conflict resolution. The results will inform debates about constitutional engineering in transitioning democracies while demonstrating novel applications of HPC in political behavior research.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the systematic study of political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in political philosophy, political theory, comparative government and politics, political parties and interest groups, public opinion, political research methods, studies of the government and politics of specific countries, and studies of specific political institutions and processes.

abstract: The study of emergent electronic phases in strongly correlated quantum materials under extreme thermodynamic conditions presents fundamental challenges in condensed matter physics. This project focuses on investigating the interplay between non-equilibrium lattice distortions and collective charge ordering phenomena in transition metal oxides using advanced computational methods. The central research problem involves understanding how strain-mediated phonon coupling modulates competing electronic instabilities near quantum critical points, where conventional density functional theory (DFT) approaches often fail to capture crucial many-body effects. We propose a multiscale computational framework combining large-scale DFT+U calculations with tensor network simulations to model electron-phonon interactions in prototypical nickelate and cuprate systems. The workflow integrates ab initio molecular dynamics for lattice thermalization with exact diagonalization of effective Hubbard models, requiring petascale computing resources to handle the exponential scaling of quantum state spaces. Key objectives include quantifying strain-dependent modifications to charge density wave coherence lengths, mapping phase diagrams under tunable uniaxial stress, and identifying universal signatures of phonon-entangled quantum criticality. The computations will leverage GPU-accelerated architectures for massively parallel tensor contractions and distributed memory systems for configuration-space sampling across defect ensembles. Successful completion will provide critical insights into manipulating correlated electron states through mechanical stimuli, potentially revealing new pathways for controlling quantum materials in strain-engineered devices. This work directly addresses open questions in the CMMP community regarding the microscopic origins of electronically soft phases while developing computational methodologies applicable to broader classes of frustrated quantum systems. The requested resources will enable unprecedented system sizes (up to 10^4 atoms) and temperature resolutions (<1K) essential for resolving competing energy scales in these complex materials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of macroscopic physical phenomena and properties that arise from basic microscopic interactions. Includes instruction in low-temperature and solid-state physics, x-ray physics, liquids and soft materials, including the study of semiconductors, metals, superliquids, magnets, superconductors, glasses, gels, polymers, colloids, neural networks, and macromolecules.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize the design and operational efficiency of wind turbine arrays in complex terrain using high-fidelity computational modeling, a critical challenge in expanding wind energy adoption. Current industry tools for wind farm layout optimization rely on simplified wake models and static atmospheric data, limiting their accuracy in predicting energy losses due to turbulent interactions in non-uniform landscapes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for microscale turbulence analysis with mesoscale weather model data to capture site-specific atmospheric dynamics. The computational workflow will integrate open-source computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software (e.g., OpenFOAM) with custom Python-based optimization algorithms to evaluate turbine placement configurations under varying wind regimes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve turbulent flow structures at meter-scale resolutions across multi-kilometer domains while iterating through thousands of potential layouts. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for wake-induced power losses in topographically diverse regions and a decision-support tool that balances energy output with infrastructure costs. This work directly supports regional wind energy developers aiming to site projects in underserved mountainous areas, where poor layout choices can reduce array efficiency by 15–25%. By leveraging HPC capabilities to account for real-world complexity, the project aims to reduce levelized energy costs through improved capacity factors while providing students in Wind Energy Technology with hands-on experience in cutting-edge computational methods. The resulting datasets and workflow templates will be shared through public repositories to advance collaborative research in renewable energy systems integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing wind-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in wind energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and generating complex polyphonic compositions through the integration of music theory principles and machine learning techniques. The core research problem lies in the limitations of existing computational tools to model nonlinear harmonic progressions, intricate rhythmic interactions, and timbral evolution in contemporary orchestral works, particularly those employing extended tonality and spectral composition techniques. Current approaches often simplify vertical sonorities or temporal development in ways incompatible with advanced compositional practices. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid methodology combining graph-based representations of harmonic relationships, temporal convolutional networks for rhythm analysis, and transformer architectures for large-scale formal planning. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to train models on a curated dataset of 20th/21st-century orchestral scores (encoded in MusicXML and MIDI) synchronized with corresponding audio renderings (96kHz/24bit). Key computational challenges include real-time spectral analysis of composite timbres across orchestral sections, parallel processing of multi-movement structural dependencies, and GPU-accelerated rendering of dynamic score visualizations. The project will implement distributed computing pipelines to handle memory-intensive tasks such as comparative analysis of orchestration strategies across 10,000+ annotated score segments. Expected outcomes include: 1) An open-source analysis toolkit capable of identifying non-traditional voice leading patterns and microtonal relationships in complex scores; 2) Generative models that preserve composer-specific orchestral idioms while exploring novel timbral combinations; 3) Quantitative frameworks for assessing spectral tension/release in post-tonal works. These resources will enable new research directions in computational musicology while providing composition students with AI-assisted tools for experimenting with extended techniques. The requested computing resources are essential for managing the project's multi-terabyte dataset, training memory-intensive neural networks on polyphonic structures, and running real-time simulations of acoustic interactions in virtual orchestral environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the principles of sound manipulation as applied to the creation of music, and the techniques of creating and arranging music. Includes instruction in aural theory, melody, counterpoint, complex harmony, modulation, chromatics, improvisation, progressions, musical writing, instrumentation, orchestration, electronic and computer applications, studies of specific musical styles, and development of original creative ability.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and optimization of multi-physics simulation frameworks for industrial manufacturing processes. A critical challenge in engineering support roles lies in accurately modeling complex interactions between thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamic systems during production—a task hindered by the computational intensity of high-fidelity simulations. Current methods often rely on simplified assumptions or reduced-order models, limiting predictive accuracy for parameter-sensitive applications such as additive manufacturing or composite material fabrication. To address this, the proposed research will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) workflows to simulate coupled thermo-mechanical phenomena at unprecedented resolution scales. The computational approach will integrate open-source solvers (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCS) with custom Python-based optimization algorithms to iteratively refine process parameters like laser power in 3D printing or resin infusion rates in composite molding. Simulations will employ adaptive meshing and distributed memory architectures to manage the nonlinear, transient nature of these systems. Anticipated outcomes include validated models for predicting defect formation under varied manufacturing conditions, enabling data-driven adjustments to reduce material waste and energy consumption. By scaling these workflows across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce simulation wall-clock times by 60–75% compared to existing single-node implementations, making iterative design optimization feasible for small-to-medium enterprises. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and open-access simulation toolkits, directly supporting workforce training in computational engineering technologies. This work bridges gaps between academic research and industrial practice, providing actionable insights for sustainable manufacturing innovation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in a wide variety of projects. Includes instruction in various engineering support functions for research, production, and operations, and applications to specific engineering specialties.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time computational modeling of American Sign Language (ASL) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the multimodal and spatiotemporal complexity of sign language discourse. Current automated interpretation systems struggle with the nuanced integration of manual gestures, non-manual markers (e.g., facial expressions, body shifts), and linguistic prosody—features that require simultaneous processing of high-dimensional visual, kinematic, and semantic data. Our research focuses on developing machine learning pipelines to model these interactions at scale, using synchronized multi-camera video corpora of naturalistic ASL dialogues. The computational approach combines 3D pose estimation, optical flow analysis, and transformer-based architectures trained to detect linguistic and paralinguistic patterns across sequential and concurrent channels. HPC resources are essential for processing petabytes of video data, running parallelized feature extraction workflows, and iteratively training deep neural networks capable of temporal alignment between continuous signing streams and their English gloss equivalents. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel computational framework for segmenting and annotating ASL discourse structures at sub-second resolution, (2) open-source tools for analyzing the coordination of articulatory features in sign language production, and (3) foundational models to support next-generation assistive technologies for Deaf communities. By advancing the computational linguistics of visual-spatial languages, this work will directly enhance interpreter training through data-driven feedback systems while informing equitable AI-mediated communication solutions. The scale of multimodal analysis required to capture ASL’s linguistic complexity necessitates GPU-accelerated environments and distributed storage systems unavailable in local computing infrastructures, positioning HPC access as critical to achieving translation fidelity comparable to human interpreter performance.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as simultaneous interpreters of American Sign Language

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of Venus’s super-rotating atmosphere, where winds circulate up to 60 times faster than the planet’s rotation. Despite decades of study, the mechanisms sustaining this phenomenon—particularly the role of small-scale waves, turbulence, and cloud-driven dynamics—remain poorly resolved in global models. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC) study using a next-generation Venus General Circulation Model (VGCM) to simulate atmospheric processes across scales, from planetary-wide circulation to sub-kilometer convective eddies. The VGCM integrates radiative transfer, cloud microphysics, and momentum transport schemes, optimized for Venus’s dense, CO2-dominated atmosphere with sulfuric acid cloud layers. Simulations will employ a variable-resolution grid, targeting <5 km resolution in the cloud deck and equatorial regions, where wave-mean flow interactions are critical. This demands petascale computational resources due to the model’s high spatial-temporal resolution and 3D coupling of chemistry and dynamics over simulated durations exceeding 100 Venus days (∼22 Earth months). Data output will be postprocessed using Lagrangian tracer analysis and spectral decomposition to isolate energy transfers between atmospheric waves and zonal jets. Expected outcomes include identifying dominant mechanisms driving angular momentum redistribution, quantifying the impact of cloud radiative effects on jet stability, and resolving discrepancies between current models and observational data from Akatsuki and past missions. By elucidating the dynamics of an extreme atmospheric regime, this work will refine fundamental theories of planetary climate, inform the interpretation of exoplanet observations, and support future Venus missions. The project’s scale necessitates access to HPC systems capable of sustaining large MPI-parallelized simulations, with an estimated requirement of 500,000 core-hours and 200 TB of storage for ensemble runs and sensitivity analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets and their planetary systems, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, moons, ring systems, gas clouds, magnetospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of public infrastructure projects necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize design, testing, and maintenance processes. Current methodologies in civil engineering technologies often rely on simplified models or empirical data, which may inadequately capture the nonlinear behavior of materials, dynamic environmental interactions, or long-term structural performance. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop high-fidelity simulations of civil infrastructure systems, including bridges, dams, and transportation networks. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating multiscale computational models that integrate real-time sensor data from field testing with physics-based simulations to predict structural responses under extreme loads; (2) implementing machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in material degradation and optimize maintenance schedules; and (3) automating the generation of compliance reports and specifications through cloud-based collaboration tools. By utilizing parallelized finite element analysis and data assimilation techniques, the project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in analyzing large-scale structures while improving the accuracy of safety assessments. Expected outcomes include a modular computational framework adaptable to diverse project types, validated protocols for hybrid physical-digital testing workflows, and open-access datasets to benchmark predictive models. The integration of HPC capabilities will enhance the capacity of civil engineering technologists to deliver resilient infrastructure solutions while minimizing resource waste and operational downtime. This work directly aligns with national priorities for sustainable infrastructure development and climate adaptation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of civil engineers engaged in designing and executing public works projects such as highways, dams, bridges, tunnels and other facilities. Includes instruction in site analysis, structural testing procedures, field and laboratory testing procedures, plan and specification preparation, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the design and performance of advanced masonry systems, addressing critical gaps in understanding how material composition, structural geometry, and environmental stressors interact at scale. Traditional masonry design relies heavily on empirical data and standardized codes, which often fail to account for the complex, nonlinear behavior of composite masonry structures under dynamic loads or extreme conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), discrete element methods (DEM), and machine learning to simulate masonry systems from the micro-scale interactions of mortar joints and brick interfaces to the macro-scale performance of entire walls or facades. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of parametric studies evaluating thousands of material combinations (e.g., recycled aggregates, bio-based binders) and geometric configurations. Simulations will incorporate real-world variables such as thermal cycling, moisture ingress, and seismic activity, validated against experimental data from partner institutions. Key outcomes include predictive models for crack propagation, load distribution, and long-term durability, enabling the design of masonry systems with enhanced resilience and sustainability. This work will directly inform updates to masonry codes and training materials, addressing workforce needs in modern construction practices. By leveraging HPC, the project aims to reduce reliance on physical prototyping, accelerate the adoption of novel materials, and provide open-source simulation tools for educators and practitioners. The results will advance decarbonization efforts in construction by optimizing low-carbon masonry solutions and preserving historic structures through improved failure prediction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the laying and/or setting of exterior brick, concrete block, hard tile, marble and related materials, using trowels, levels, hammers, chisels, and other hand tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, blueprint reading, structural masonry, decorative masonry, foundations, reinforcement, mortar preparation, cutting and finishing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The industrial production of specialty chemicals requires precise control over reaction kinetics and transport phenomena to optimize yield and ensure safety. However, empirical methods for process development are often resource-intensive and fail to capture complex multiphase interactions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that bridge molecular-level reaction dynamics with reactor-scale fluid flow and heat transfer. Using quantum mechanical calculations (DFT) and reactive molecular dynamics, we will simulate reaction pathways and catalyst behavior under industrially relevant conditions. These results will inform continuum-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, incorporating turbulence and multiphase flow effects, to predict system performance across varying operating parameters. Machine learning techniques will be employed to analyze simulation datasets, identify optimal process conditions, and reduce computational expense through surrogate modeling. The integration of these methods aims to establish a predictive framework for designing efficient, scalable reaction systems with minimized environmental impact. Expected outcomes include validated models for key industrial processes, such as catalytic upgrading of bio-derived intermediates and solvent recycling systems, which will be disseminated through open-source tools to support broader adoption in the chemical manufacturing sector. Access to HPC resources is critical to handle the computational intensity of coupled simulations and enable parametric studies at realistic production scales. This work aligns with industry priorities to enhance sustainability and operational safety while reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in social service delivery by developing computational models to optimize resource allocation and intervention strategies for vulnerable populations. Social work systems—such as child welfare, homelessness support, and disability services—involve complex, dynamic interactions between individuals, institutions, and policies. Existing decision-making tools often lack the capacity to simulate multi-level, real-world complexities, resulting in inefficient resource distribution and inequitable outcomes. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze how systemic factors (e.g., funding constraints, caseload dynamics, policy changes) interact with individual needs and behaviors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations that incorporate granular demographic data, historical service utilization patterns, and stochastic variability across diverse populations. These simulations will model hypothetical policy scenarios, such as shifts in housing subsidies or mental health service eligibility, to predict their downstream effects on service accessibility and client outcomes. Concurrently, ML algorithms will process administrative datasets to identify latent risk factors and prioritize interventions for high-need subgroups. By integrating ABM and ML on an HPC platform, the project will generate actionable insights into how adaptive resource allocation can mitigate service gaps and reduce disparities. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable modeling framework for evaluating social policies, evidence-based recommendations for agency-level decision-making, and open-source tools to help practitioners simulate local service networks. This work bridges computational social science and social work practice, offering transformative potential to enhance equity in publicly administered services while advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional practice of social welfare administration and counseling, and that focus on the study of organized means of providing basic support services for vulnerable individuals and groups. Includes instruction in social welfare policy; case work planning; social counseling and intervention strategies; administrative procedures and regulations; and specific applications in areas such as child welfare and family services, probation, employment services, and disability counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in optimizing multi-stage industrial production systems through the development of a high-fidelity computational framework for simulating and predicting process interdependencies. Current approaches to modeling complex production lines—particularly those integrating additive manufacturing, precision machining, and automated quality control—are limited by computational scalability when accounting for real-world variables such as tool wear, material heterogeneity, and energy consumption patterns. The research will employ hybrid simulation techniques combining discrete event simulation (DES) for system-level logistics, finite element analysis (FEA) for component-level stress-strain behavior, and machine learning (ML) models trained on historical production data to capture nonlinear relationships between process parameters and output quality. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing these coupled simulations at necessary resolutions, given the need to simultaneously resolve micrometer-scale material deformation in manufacturing tools while simulating months of factory-level operational data. The computational workflow will leverage distributed-memory parallelism for DES-FEA integration and GPU-accelerated tensor operations for ML surrogate models. Anticipated outcomes include predictive metrics for bottleneck reduction in mixed-material production lines and a digital twin framework capable of recommending real-time adjustments to machining parameters under dynamic supply chain conditions. This work aims to advance adaptive manufacturing systems that minimize material waste and energy use while maintaining tolerances for aerospace and medical device applications. Successful implementation will provide open-source simulation tools to bridge the gap between academic research in production optimization and industry-ready solutions, with particular relevance to small-to-medium enterprises adopting Industry 4.0 technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in industrial production technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for analyzing dynamic, multi-source geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) data to model and predict emergent security threats influenced by human-environment interactions. The research addresses a critical gap in current GEOINT workflows: the integration of real-time socio-cultural data (e.g., social media trends, population mobility patterns) with traditional physical geography datasets (e.g., satellite imagery, climate models) to anticipate asymmetric risks in conflict zones or disaster scenarios. Existing methods struggle with the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of these data streams, particularly when modeling at hyper-local scales with temporal granularity under 24 hours. To overcome these barriers, the project proposes a hybrid high-performance computing (HPC) architecture combining graph-based spatial network analysis, transformer models for unstructured text interpretation, and GPU-accelerated raster algebra. Key innovations include a spatiotemporal attention mechanism to weight disparate data sources by predictive relevance and a distributed computing pipeline optimized for ingesting streaming data from open-source intelligence (OSINT) platforms. The framework will be validated against three historical case studies involving rapid urbanization impacts on conflict escalation, cross-border migration patterns during droughts, and infrastructure vulnerability to coordinated disinformation campaigns. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for probabilistic threat surface modeling, benchmark datasets linking human terrain variables to observed security outcomes, and performance metrics quantifying the trade-offs between computational resolution and prediction accuracy in time-sensitive scenarios. By enabling near-real-time fusion of human geography factors with physical landscape data, this work aims to advance methodological rigor in security-focused geospatial analytics while providing resource-efficient strategies for intelligence prioritization in resource-constrained environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to analyze security and intelligence problems using a geographic perspective by relating human actions to cultural, political, economic, social, and physical landscapes. Includes instruction in aerial photography analysis, cartography, geographic information systems (GIS), physical geography, remote sensing, spatial programming, and quantitative methods in geographic research.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution and efficacy of digital communication strategies in lay ministry training programs, focusing on their role in fostering community resilience and spiritual engagement. While lay ministry has historically relied on in-person pastoral practices, the rise of hybrid and fully remote ministry models—accelerated by global shifts in communication norms—demands a computational approach to evaluate how digital tools reshape theological education, congregational dynamics, and cross-cultural outreach. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in pastoral communication effectiveness across diverse demographics, particularly in underrepresented or geographically dispersed communities, where traditional ministry frameworks may lack scalability. Using natural language processing (NLP), the project will analyze multimodal datasets (text, audio, and video) from lay ministry training sessions, public sermons, and virtual congregational interactions to model how theological concepts are linguistically adapted across contexts. Agent-based modeling will simulate community response to different communication strategies, incorporating variables such as cultural literacy, socioeconomic factors, and digital access disparities. These computational methods will enable the identification of adaptive frameworks for training lay ministers in technologically mediated environments. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated ministry communication datasets, predictive models for optimizing pastoral training curricula, and evidence-based recommendations for equitable digital ministry practices. By bridging computational linguistics, social simulation, and practical theology, this research aims to advance the capacity of lay ministry programs to address 21st-century spiritual needs while preserving theological coherence across rapidly changing communicative landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained individuals to serve as lay pastors, religious educators, youth leaders, and other professional positions open to the laity in local churches and other settings. Includes instruction in bible studies, theology, spirituality, pastoral counseling, foundations of ministry, effective communication, and church leadership.

abstract: Understanding the multi-scale interactions between soil minerals, organic matter, fluid dynamics, and microbial activity is critical for advancing sustainable soil management practices. However, experimental approaches alone struggle to capture the complexity of these processes, particularly across spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to integrate molecular-scale simulations, pore-scale fluid dynamics modeling, and machine learning to predict soil behavior under varying agricultural management scenarios. The primary research problem centers on quantifying how soil amendments and environmental stressors influence nutrient retention, water permeability, and carbon sequestration in heterogeneous soil matrices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of ion exchange and organic-mineral interactions at atomic resolution, coupled with 3D lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations of water and solute transport in digitally reconstructed soil pore networks. These simulations will parameterize machine learning models trained to predict macroscale soil properties, such as hydraulic conductivity and cation exchange capacity, using inputs from molecular and pore-scale data. The computational workflow requires parallelized GPU-accelerated MD simulations (via GROMACS or LAMMPS), high-memory nodes for LBM-based fluid dynamics (Palabos), and distributed training of neural networks (TensorFlow/PyTorch) on heterogeneous soil datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks linking soil amendment chemistry to water-nutrient dynamics, validated against experimental X-ray tomography and spectroscopy data. This work will advance mechanistic models of soil biogeochemical cycles, directly informing strategies to optimize soil fertility, mitigate nutrient leaching, and enhance climate resilience in agricultural systems. By bridging atomic-scale processes to field-scale outcomes, the project will provide a scalable computational toolkit for soil scientists, reducing reliance on resource-intensive empirical trials. The requested HPC resources will enable the high-throughput simulations and data integration necessary to address these computationally demanding, multi-disciplinary challenges.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and physical principles to research and analysis concerning the nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instruction in soil and fluid mechanics, mineralogy, sedimentology, thermodynamics, geomorphology, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of linguistically informed neural models for low-resource language processing by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Despite progress in natural language processing (NLP), current systems struggle to generalize across typologically diverse languages, particularly those with limited digital corpora or complex morphological and syntactic structures. The research addresses this gap by integrating formal linguistic theories—such as principles of syntactic dependency hierarchies and semantic role labeling—into transformer-based architectures. The computational approach involves training hybrid models that combine unsupervised pre-training on multilingual text with structured linguistic constraints derived from annotated treebanks and grammars. To achieve scalability, the project will implement distributed training pipelines on GPU clusters, optimizing for parallel processing of large-scale linguistic datasets spanning 50+ languages. Key challenges include dynamically encoding language-specific grammatical rules into attention mechanisms and evaluating cross-linguistic transfer learning under varying data scarcity conditions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for iterating on model architectures (e.g., graph-augmented transformers), running comparative ablation studies, and processing high-dimensional embeddings across multilingual layers. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for low-resource language analysis, a framework for incorporating linguistic typology into neural models, and empirically grounded insights into the interaction between machine learning and human language universals. This work has implications for both computational linguistics—by testing theoretical predictions at scale—and NLP applications—by improving machine translation and information extraction systems for underrepresented languages. The requested resources will directly support 15,000+ GPU hours for model training, distributed storage for petabyte-scale linguistic corpora, and real-time computation for syntactic-semantic parsing experiments. By bridging formal linguistics and deep learning, the project aims to establish reproducible methods for resource-efficient, cross-linguistic NLP while contributing interdisciplinary benchmarks to the HPC community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationship between computer and human language and computational techniques applied to natural language. Includes instruction in computer programming, human languages, linguistic analysis, logic, natural language processing, semantics, machine learning, psycholinguistics, software engineering, and syntax.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the formation and evolution of cultural identities across South Asia and its diasporas through computational analysis of multilingual textual corpora. Existing scholarship often relies on manual close readings or region-specific studies, limiting the scope to trace transnational cultural exchanges and linguistic hybridity at scale. The research employs high-performance computing to process and analyze digitized collections of vernacular literature, historical documents, and oral histories spanning eight South Asian languages, including lesser-studied dialects. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for cross-lingual semantic analysis, transformer-based models to detect intertextual references, and network graphs mapping the circulation of narrative motifs across linguistic boundaries. By parallelizing tasks such as optical character recognition correction for non-Latin scripts, named entity recognition in low-resource languages, and topic modeling across temporal-spatial axes, the project overcomes processing bottlenecks inherent in conventional humanities computing. Anticipated outcomes include identifying previously undocumented pathways of cultural transmission between coastal Sri Lankan Tamil communities and Myanmar’s Rohingya diaspora, as well as quantifying the influence of 19th-century Urdu poetic forms on modern Bengali feminist discourse. These findings will advance interdisciplinary understanding of how multilingualism and migration have shaped collective memory in South Asia, while developing open-source tools for computational regional studies. The resource request supports GPU-intensive model training, large-scale text alignment across scripts, and storage for petabyte-scale archival datasets.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of South Asia, defined as including Afghanistan, India, the Maldives, Myanmar (Burma), Pakistan, and Sri Lanka and related borderlands and island groups; and including the study of migration patterns and overseas diasporas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance psychodynamic research by enabling large-scale computational modeling of therapeutic processes and patient outcomes. Psychoanalytic practice relies on nuanced interpretation of unstructured clinical data—including therapy transcripts, dream reports, and longitudinal case studies—to uncover unconscious dynamics. However, traditional qualitative methods face limitations in analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, hindering systematic exploration of patterns in transference, defense mechanisms, and symptom evolution. This research aims to address these gaps by developing machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to quantify psychodynamic phenomena and simulate therapeutic interactions. Proposed computational workflows include training transformer-based models on anonymized therapy transcripts to identify linguistic markers of transference and resistance, applying graph neural networks to model symptom networks in personality disorders, and implementing agent-based simulations to test theoretical frameworks linking early attachment patterns to adult relational behaviors. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of multimodal data (text, audio, clinical scales) and optimizing deep learning architectures through hyperparameter tuning. Expected outcomes include (1) validated computational proxies for core psychoanalytic concepts, (2) predictive models correlating intervention strategies with symptom trajectories, and (3) open-source tools to support clinicians in treatment personalization. By bridging psychodynamic theory with data-driven methods, this work will enhance empirical foundations for psychoanalytic practice while preserving its humanistic depth, ultimately contributing to more rigorous training protocols and evidence-based refinements of therapeutic techniques. The scalability of these approaches will also enable cross-cultural analyses of psychodynamic processes, addressing a longstanding gap in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung. Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The integration of biofield therapies, such as Reiki and therapeutic touch, with conventional medical practices remains limited by a lack of mechanistic understanding of how subtle energy interactions influence physiological systems. This project seeks to model biofield dynamics and their systemic effects on human health using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate interactions between electromagnetic fields, cellular activity, and neuroendocrine pathways. Current research in energy medicine relies heavily on clinical outcomes, leaving a critical gap in biophysical and computational frameworks that explain observed therapeutic effects. We propose a multi-scale computational approach combining finite element modeling of biofield-generated electromagnetic patterns with agent-based simulations of cellular response networks. These models will integrate empirical data from biofeedback devices, electroencephalography (EEG), and metabolomic profiling to parameterize energy transfer mechanisms and downstream physiological cascades. Machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in multi-omics datasets to correlate biofield modulation with stress reduction, immune response, and autonomic nervous system regulation. HPC resources are essential for handling the high dimensionality of spatiotemporal simulations, optimizing stochastic models of energy-body interactions, and processing heterogeneous clinical datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models of biofield efficacy under varying physiological states, validated against experimental data from mindfulness and energy therapy trials. This work will establish a computational foundation for optimizing personalized biofield interventions, advancing evidence-based integration of energy medicine into holistic health frameworks. By elucidating mechanisms underlying mind-body-environment interactions, the project aims to bridge gaps between traditional healing paradigms and modern systems biology, fostering interdisciplinary innovation in integrative health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the holistic interconnectedness of physical, psychological, social, spiritual, and environmental well-being and that integrates aspects of alternative, complementary, and conventional medicine to alleviate illness and promote, maintain, and optimize wellness. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, alternative diagnostic and healing methods, aromatherapy, biofeedback, energy medicine, environmental psychology, ethics, health coaching, herbal medicine, mind-body medicine, mindfulness, nutrition, somatic bodywork, and stress management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive maintenance and performance optimization in motorcycle systems through computational modeling and data-driven analysis. Modern motorcycles incorporate complex mechanical, electrical, and fuel systems whose interactions are challenging to analyze empirically, particularly under dynamic operating conditions. Traditional diagnostic methods often rely on iterative manual inspections, which are time-intensive and may fail to anticipate latent faults. This research addresses these limitations by developing physics-based simulations of critical subsystems—including combustion dynamics, thermal management, and vibration-induced wear—paired with machine learning models trained on operational telemetry and historical failure data. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model airflow in cooling systems and exhaust gas behavior, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess stress distribution in engine components under varying loads. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in component lifespan predictions. Additionally, a neural network trained on sensor data from instrumented motorcycles will identify early warning signatures of ignition system degradation or carburetor malfunctions. The integration of these approaches requires significant computational resources due to the high dimensionality of parameter spaces, transient simulation timescales, and iterative model calibration. By deploying these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to generate actionable insights into failure prevention, fuel efficiency optimization, and adaptive maintenance scheduling. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation templates for common motorcycle architectures and a predictive maintenance algorithm validated against empirical repair records. This work will directly support technician training programs by providing data-driven diagnostic tools and enhancing curricular materials with interactive computational case studies. The results will bridge gaps between traditional mechanical repair practices and modern computational engineering, fostering innovation in motorcycle maintenance education and industry standards.
cip_title: Motorcycle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain motorcycles and other similar powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication and cooling systems, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuel systems and adjustments of moving parts.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the emergent dynamics of decentralized information processing in colonial marine invertebrates, a novel interdisciplinary niche bridging organismal biology, complex systems theory, and distributed computing. While neuronal computation is well-studied, many sessile marine colonies (e.g., bryozoans, tunicates) exhibit coordinated group behaviors—such as synchronized feeding currents or colony-wide threat responses—without centralized neural control. This project addresses the critical knowledge gap in understanding how these systems achieve distributed decision-making through localized cell-to-cell signaling and hydrodynamic interactions. We will develop a high-resolution 3D agent-based model integrating individual zooid behavior, mechanochemical signaling cascades, and fluid dynamics at colony scales. The computational framework will employ smoothed particle hydrodynamics coupled with stochastic reaction-diffusion processes to simulate signal propagation through both biological tissue and surrounding water. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the nonlinear interactions across 10^4-10^5 individual zooids in realistic flow regimes, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of cores.
