Validation will leverage published experimental data on response thresholds and propagation speeds in Botryllus schlosseri colonies. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of critical parameters enabling reliable distributed computation in noisy aquatic environments, 2) quantitative comparison of efficiency trade-offs between neural and non-neural biological computing systems, and 3) bio-inspired design principles for robust decentralized networks in marine robotics. This work establishes a new paradigm for studying computation in non-neural multicellular systems while advancing fundamental knowledge about the evolutionary constraints and capabilities of biological distributed intelligence.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the biological and biomedical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of multiscale phenomena in environmental systems demands advanced computational approaches to resolve interactions spanning molecular to macroscopic scales. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the dynamic behavior of hybrid organic-inorganic materials under extreme environmental conditions, particularly those relevant to sustainable energy and pollution mitigation. Current experimental methods struggle to capture real-time, atomistic-level processes in these systems, while existing computational models lack the resolution and scalability to predict emergent properties across spatiotemporal domains. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-method computational framework combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), machine learning (ML)-accelerated free energy sampling, and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. These methods will be integrated through a custom workflow manager to enable cross-validation between quantum-mechanical calculations and mesoscale predictions. The research requires high-performance computing resources to handle three core tasks: 1) AIMD simulations of interfacial reactions at solid-liquid boundaries (10,000+ atoms, ~1 ns trajectories), 2) training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of molecular configurations, and 3) ensemble-based analysis of phase transition kinetics across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations. The requested allocation of 750,000 CPU-core hours and 200 TB of temporary storage will support these computationally intensive workflows. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models of material degradation pathways under operational stresses and optimized designs for environmentally stable composites. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation packages and partnerships with experimental groups validating computational predictions. This work establishes a template for data-driven discovery in understudied material systems central to advancing green technologies, while pushing the boundaries of heterogeneous computing strategies in molecular modeling.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in science technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical informatics research faces significant challenges in integrating and analyzing heterogeneous, large-scale datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, genomic data, and real-time sensor outputs—to derive actionable insights for patient care. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the volume, velocity, and complexity of these data, limiting the development of predictive models and decision-support tools. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance clinical informatics methodologies. The primary research problem involves optimizing multi-modal data integration and analysis to improve predictive accuracy in diagnosing and managing complex conditions such as sepsis and metabolic syndrome. The computational approach will employ distributed machine learning frameworks, including federated learning for privacy-preserving analysis of multi-institutional EHRs, and deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer models, convolutional neural networks) to process temporal, imaging, and genomic data. HPC resources will enable parallelized hyperparameter tuning, large-scale simulations of disease progression models, and real-time analytics for streaming physiological data. Additionally, graph-based algorithms will map patient-specific biomarker interactions to identify novel risk stratification patterns. The project will validate these methods using retrospective datasets from three academic health systems and prospectively pilot them in a critical care setting. Expected outcomes include the development of scalable computational pipelines for multi-modal clinical data, open-source tools for reproducible analysis, and validated predictive models with improved sensitivity and specificity compared to existing approaches. By addressing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to advance personalized treatment strategies, reduce clinician cognitive load, and inform resource allocation in clinical workflows. The requested HPC infrastructure—particularly GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory capacity systems—is critical to achieving the necessary throughput for training complex models and simulating population-level health outcomes within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on Clinical Informatics

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize personalized learning pathways for adult learners in continuing education programs. Adult learners exhibit diverse educational backgrounds, skill levels, and career-oriented goals, creating challenges in designing adaptive curricula that balance flexibility with structured skill development. Existing approaches often rely on static competency frameworks or manual instructor assessments, which struggle to scale efficiently across hybrid and online learning environments. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven framework to analyze multimodal learner data—including interaction logs, assessment performance, and self-reported feedback—to dynamically predict individual knowledge gaps and recommend targeted content adjustments. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on longitudinal datasets from three adult education platforms (total ~2.3 million anonymized learner interactions) while preserving privacy through federated learning architectures. Computational experiments will compare the efficacy of graph neural networks for modeling prerequisite skill hierarchies against temporal convolutional networks for sequencing learning objectives. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating real-time pedagogical recommendations, validated against outcomes from 12 existing continuing education cohorts. The models aim to reduce time-to-proficiency in workforce-relevant skills by adaptively aligning content with learners' evolving needs while maintaining instructor oversight capabilities. Successful implementation could provide evidence-based frameworks for scaling personalized adult education in resource-constrained settings, particularly for programs targeting career transitions or technological upskilling. This work directly supports the program's mission to improve teaching strategies for adult learners through data-informed approaches while adhering to ethical AI principles in educational technology.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_title: Adult and Continuing Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach adult students in various settings, including basic and remedial education programs, continuing education programs, and programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ethical reasoning in complex, large-scale moral dilemmas, particularly those arising in emerging technologies and sociotechnical systems. While traditional ethical analysis relies on qualitative, case-based methods, the increasing scale and interconnectivity of modern moral problems—such as algorithmic bias, climate justice, or biomedical AI—demand tools capable of modeling dynamic interactions between ethical principles, contextual variables, and stakeholder priorities. The research problem centers on developing computational frameworks to systematically analyze how competing ethical theories (e.g., utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics) resolve conflicts in high-dimensional scenarios where outcomes depend on non-linear relationships and probabilistic uncertainties. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, Bayesian networks, and constrained optimization techniques to simulate decision landscapes under diverse ethical paradigms. Agent behaviors will be encoded with rule sets derived from philosophical literature, while environmental variables will incorporate empirical data from case studies in technology ethics and policy. HPC resources are essential for iteratively testing model robustness across parameter spaces encompassing millions of potential scenario configurations and ethical weighting schemes. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible library of simulated moral dilemmas annotated with ethical trade-offs, (2) quantitative metrics for comparing theoretical approaches’ coherence under scalability pressures, and (3) visualizations of how hybrid ethical frameworks might address gaps in traditional theories when applied to systemic challenges. By bridging formal ethics with computational social science methods, this work aims to provide philosophers and policymakers with evidence-based tools for navigating morally pluralistic, rapidly evolving problem domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the theory of moral good and its application to various theoretical and practical problems. Includes instruction in ethical theory, history of ethics, belief and value systems, ethical constructs, and applications to specific topics, issues and problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing adaptive manufacturing systems in high-variability production environments, a critical challenge in modern engineering technologies. Traditional approaches struggle to dynamically balance resource allocation, process sequencing, and quality control under rapidly changing product specifications and material constraints. We propose to address this gap through a hybrid simulation-optimization methodology leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational model will integrate discrete-event simulation with multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to simultaneously optimize production throughput, energy efficiency, and equipment utilization. Key innovations include the implementation of distributed Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty quantification in material supply chains and the development of GPU-accelerated neural networks for real-time defect prediction. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable parallel execution of 10⁴-10⁵ parametric simulations across diverse manufacturing scenarios, significantly exceeding the capacity of current institutional computing resources. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source toolkit for adaptive manufacturing system design, (2) quantitative benchmarks for reconfigurable production line performance under stochastic demand, and (3) novel convergence criteria for multi-scale optimization in hybrid human-robot workflows. This work will directly support emerging applications in customized medical device manufacturing and on-demand aerospace component repair, while advancing fundamental computational methodologies in engineering systems optimization. Resource allocation requests include 200,000 CPU-core hours and 50 TB of temporary storage to accommodate large-scale sensitivity analyses and high-dimensional parameter spaces characteristic of modern smart manufacturing challenges.
cip_definition: Any programs in engineering-related technologies and technicians, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to optimize the resilience of urban transportation networks under climate-driven hydrological stressors. Increasingly frequent extreme precipitation events exacerbate flooding risks, disrupting critical infrastructure and amplifying economic losses. Current models often lack the spatial granularity and dynamic coupling of hydrological, structural, and traffic flow processes needed to assess cascading failures in complex urban systems. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating 2D hydrodynamic flood modeling, finite element analysis of bridge and pavement integrity, and agent-based transportation network simulations. The framework will leverage GPU-accelerated shallow water equations solvers (using Clawpack and ANSYS Fluent) to model surface water dynamics at 1-meter resolution across a 200 km² testbed region, coupled with machine learning surrogates to predict infrastructure degradation thresholds under hydraulic loading. Concurrently, a parallelized MATSim implementation will simulate traffic rerouting behaviors during flood propagation. The integration of these modules requires high-performance computing resources to manage the computational intensity of transient, multi-physics simulations and large-scale optimization tasks. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to identify high-risk infrastructure chokepoints, evaluate adaptive mitigation strategies (e.g., green stormwater infrastructure placement), and inform climate-resilient urban planning policies. The research directly aligns with national priorities for sustainable infrastructure adaptation, with particular relevance to coastal cities experiencing compound flooding threats. Successful implementation will provide open-source computational workflows to advance coupled human-infrastructure-environment modeling capabilities within civil and environmental engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures. Combines instruction in civil and environmental engineering.

abstract: The increasing complexity of histologic data, driven by high-resolution whole-slide imaging and multi-modal tissue analyses, presents challenges in efficiently correlating structural biomarkers with molecular and functional phenotypes. Current manual and semi-automated approaches in histotechnologic workflows struggle to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial transcriptomics, and 3D electron microscopy reconstructions—limiting diagnostic precision and discovery of novel tissue-based disease signatures. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging deep learning and topological data analysis (TDA) to automate the identification of multiscale histologic patterns and their contextual relationships to subcellular omics data. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process petabytes of whole-slide images from neurodegenerative disease cohorts, paired with single-cell resolution proteomic and metabolic profiles. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will be trained to segment tissue regions of interest, while graph-based TDA methods will model spatial interactions between cellular clusters and extracellular matrix components. Parallelized workflows will align these outputs with mass spectrometry imaging datasets to construct probabilistic maps of disease progression biomarkers. The computational pipeline will incorporate quality control modules simulating histotechnologist decision-making patterns, ensuring clinical interpretability. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for integrative histologic-omics analysis, validated against gold-standard manual annotations, and novel insights into tissue-level heterogeneity in early-stage neurodegeneration. This work bridges gaps between traditional histotechnologic expertise and emerging computational pathology paradigms, offering scalable solutions for precision diagnostics while maintaining alignment with ethical standards for automated tissue analysis. Successful implementation will enhance the role of histotechnologists in data-driven biomarker discovery and provide a template for resource allocation in specialized health science computation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, at the request of physicians, researchers, and laboratory scientists, to identify tissue structures and cell components and relate these findings to physiological functions and to the detection and diagnosis of diseases and other abnormalities. Includes instruction in medical chemistry, histochemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, medical informatics, applied mathematics, electron microscopy, instrumentation, quality control procedures, data recording and analysis, laboratory administration, medical terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Clinical decision-making for complex patient populations requires integrating multidimensional data to optimize pharmacotherapeutic outcomes and minimize adverse effects. However, current approaches often rely on generalized guidelines that fail to account for dynamic interactions between patient-specific factors, such as comorbidities, polypharmacy, genetic variability, and social determinants of health. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model individualized pharmacotherapeutic strategies for high-acuity patients under the care of Clinical Nurse Specialists (CNSs). Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) data, and genomic datasets to identify predictors of treatment response and toxicity. Machine learning models, including ensemble methods and graph neural networks, will be trained to simulate drug-drug and drug-disease interactions across heterogeneous patient subgroups. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will explore how care coordination workflows and nurse-led interventions influence clinical outcomes in virtual patient cohorts. The computational pipeline will be validated against retrospective CNS case data from three academic medical centers. This work requires HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize computationally intensive PK/PD simulations, and run iterative optimization algorithms for treatment personalization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to support CNSs in tailoring pharmacotherapy for patients with multimorbidity, reducing preventable adverse drug events by 15-20% in pilot implementations. The models will also generate evidence to inform health system policies on nurse-led medication management protocols. By bridging clinical expertise with advanced analytics, this project aims to establish a scalable paradigm for data-driven CNS practice while addressing critical gaps in precision pharmacotherapy for complex care populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver direct patient and client care in clinical settings. Includes instruction in clinical pharmacotherapeutics, advanced clinical practice, holistic nursing, nursing practice and health care policy, administration and consultation services, health assessment, patient stabilization and care, and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying music therapy interventions for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a population with high heterogeneity in treatment response. Despite clinical evidence supporting music therapy’s efficacy in improving social communication and emotional regulation, the lack of mechanistic understanding limits personalized protocol development. The research problem centers on identifying dynamic brain-body interactions during structured music therapy sessions and modeling their relationship to therapeutic outcomes. Multimodal data—including high-density EEG, heart rate variability, motion capture, and acoustic feature extraction—will be collected from 50 participants during therapist-guided improvisation tasks. Computational challenges include real-time synchronization of terabyte-scale datasets, nonlinear analysis of neurophysiological time series, and machine learning-driven pattern recognition across disparate modalities. HPC resources will enable (1) large-scale parallel processing of EEG source localization via finite element modeling, (2) GPU-accelerated training of hybrid neural networks (CNNs + LSTMs) to decode emotion expression from biometric and musical features, and (3) agent-based simulations of therapist-client interaction dynamics. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific music elements (tempo, timbre, harmonic complexity) to individualized neural engagement patterns, validated against behavioral metrics. The computational models will inform the development of adaptive music therapy protocols that automatically adjust auditory stimuli based on real-time physiological feedback. By bridging music neuroscience, computational psychiatry, and therapeutic practice, this work aims to establish quantitative biomarkers for treatment personalization while advancing methodological standards for data-intensive research in creative arts therapies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in association with a rehabilitation team or in private practice, to use music in therapeutic relationships to address the physical, psychological, cognitive, emotional, and social needs of clients. Includes instruction in music theory and performance, human growth and development, biomedical sciences, abnormal psychology, disabling conditions, patient assessment and diagnosis, treatment plan development and implementation, clinical evaluation, record-keeping, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The study of morphogenesis and cell differentiation during embryonic development remains a central challenge in developmental biology. A critical gap exists in understanding how multicellular aggregates integrate biochemical signaling with mechanical forces to establish robust tissue architecture. This project aims to develop a computational framework to model the spatiotemporal dynamics of cell-cell interactions and force transmission during early embryogenesis, focusing on gastrulation events in vertebrate model systems. Current limitations in analyzing tissue-scale biomechanical feedback require high-resolution simulations of collective cell behaviors that are intractable with standard computing resources. We propose to implement a hybrid agent-based model coupled with continuum mechanics, parameterized by live-cell imaging data from avian and amphibian embryos. The computational approach will integrate cell polarity dynamics, adhesion receptor trafficking, and actomyosin contractility into a 3D viscoelastic model to predict emergent tissue deformation patterns. High-performance computing resources will enable simulations at biologically relevant scales (10^4-10^5 cells) with subcellular spatial resolution and minute-level temporal resolution across developmental time windows. Validation will leverage quantitative comparisons to in vivo perturbation experiments targeting cytoskeletal regulators and cell adhesion molecules. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in mechanical coupling that ensure faithful germ layer segregation, (2) predictive maps of stress distribution during primitive streak formation, and (3) mechanistic insights into how local cell shape changes propagate to orchestrate global tissue remodeling. This work will establish a scalable computational platform for analyzing developmental robustness, with direct implications for understanding congenital malformations caused by disrupted morphogenetic processes. The requested resources will support iterative model refinement through parallelized parameter space exploration and high-throughput simulation analyses that exceed local computing capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of embryology, development, and growth of animals and human beings. Includes instruction in fertilization, oogenesis, histogenesis, gastrulation, and cell differentiation; embryological development including organ and pattern formation, morphogenesis, gene regulation, cell lineage, and fate maps; disease and defect studies; transgenic and evolutionary models of growth and development; and applications to specific organisms and phyla.

abstract: The integration of ocular biomechanics and computational modeling offers transformative potential for understanding dynamic interactions between the cornea, tear film, and external stressors—a critical yet understudied area in vision health. This project seeks to develop high-resolution, multi-physics models of the human corneal surface to simulate real-time responses to environmental factors (e.g., air quality, digital screen exposure) and mechanical forces (e.g., contact lens wear). Current clinical models rely on static measurements, limiting predictive insights into cumulative microtrauma or dehydration effects that precede conditions like dry eye syndrome or corneal ectasia. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis coupled with fluid-structure interaction simulations to map strain distributions, tear film stability, and metabolic exchange under variable physiological and environmental conditions. Patient-specific corneal topography data from optical coherence tomography and Scheimpflug imaging will parameterize models, while machine learning algorithms will optimize computational efficiency by identifying key variables driving biomechanical responses. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to quantify risk thresholds for subclinical corneal damage and personalized tolerance metrics for contact lens materials. By bridging gaps between ophthalmology, mechanical engineering, and environmental health, this work will establish a novel computational platform to advance preventive strategies in ocular surface health—a priority for pre-optometry education and future clinical innovation. The project’s scale necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing of 3D transient simulations, which exceed the capacity of local workstations due to the complexity of non-linear material behaviors and terabyte-scale datasets generated by high-temporal-resolution analyses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in optometry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical and literary datasets in theatre studies, addressing gaps in understanding the evolution of dramaturgical practices, collaborative networks, and cultural transmission across periods and regions. Traditional humanities methodologies often struggle to process the volume and complexity of global theatre archives, play texts, production records, and critical reviews. This research will apply computational text analysis, network modeling, and machine learning to identify patterns in dramatic literature, track the circulation of theatrical conventions, and map relationships between playwrights, companies, and audiences. Key tasks include training NLP models to detect stylistic shifts in playwriting across centuries, constructing multilayer networks to model influence among theatre practitioners, and simulating the diffusion of performance techniques using geospatial data. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual corpora (spanning 16th–20th-century European, Asian, and colonial theatres), running iterative simulations of artistic collaboration dynamics, and handling high-dimensional metadata on productions. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated theatre datasets, new computational workflows for performing arts research, and evidence-based theories about how socioeconomic factors shaped theatrical innovation. By bridging computational methods with theatre historiography, this project aims to advance interdisciplinary frameworks for analyzing cultural heritage at scale while preserving context-sensitive humanistic interpretation. The results will inform scholarly debates on canon formation, intercultural exchange, and the role of theatre in public discourse, offering tools to reinterpret marginalized works and practitioners within broader historical narratives.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the history, literature, theory, and analysis of written plays, theatrical productions, and theatre methods and organization. Includes instruction in historical method; critical theory; literary analysis; the study of themes and archetypes in dramatic literature; the history of acting, directing, and technical theatre; and the study of specific historical and cultural styles and traditions.

abstract: Palliative care and pain management require personalized treatment strategies to address the complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors influencing patient outcomes. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may fail to account for individual variability in pain perception, treatment response, and disease progression. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating multimodal patient data—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, and longitudinal symptom reports—to identify predictive biomarkers and optimize dynamic treatment regimens. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational challenges of analyzing high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets while preserving clinical interpretability. To address this, we will implement machine learning models (e.g., Bayesian hierarchical clustering, recurrent neural networks) and causal inference methods to model temporal relationships between interventions and outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on a cohort of 15,000+ palliative care patients, enabling parallel processing of genomic association studies, real-time simulation of treatment pathways, and sensitivity analyses across diverse demographic subgroups. Key computational steps include dimensionality reduction of multi-omics data, reinforcement learning for adaptive treatment recommendation systems, and validation through in silico clinical trials. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for opioid response phenotypes, (2) dynamic decision-support tools for titrating multimodal therapies, and (3) mechanistic insights into neuroimmune pathways influencing refractory pain. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle complex interactions at scale, this work aims to advance precision palliative care, reduce trial-and-error prescribing, and establish a computational infrastructure for translating large-scale clinical data into actionable treatment protocols. The results will directly inform the design of a forthcoming multicenter clinical trial evaluating algorithm-guided pain management strategies.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care/Pain Management

abstract: This project addresses the critical challenge of strategically allocating resources in educational entrepreneurship to maximize the scalability and sustainability of innovative learning initiatives. Entrepreneurs in education must navigate complex, dynamic systems involving diverse stakeholders, fluctuating funding landscapes, and heterogeneous regional demands, yet lack robust tools to model the long-term impacts of operational decisions. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that integrates agent-based modeling, machine learning, and econometric analysis. The platform will simulate interactions among key actors—such as philanthropic organizations, investors, school networks, and policymakers—across varying market conditions and regulatory environments. By processing multi-source datasets (e.g., historical venture performance, demographic trends, and investment patterns), the model will identify optimal business strategies for resource allocation, risk mitigation, and market expansion. Computational experiments will focus on testing human-centered design adaptations, evaluating financial resilience under funding volatility, and forecasting the educational and economic outcomes of scalable interventions. HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty analysis, and train predictive models on large-scale, real-world education venture data. Anticipated outcomes include actionable frameworks for balancing educational impact with financial viability, data-driven tools for adaptive project management, and policy insights to incentivize equitable innovation ecosystems. This work will provide education entrepreneurs and stakeholders with evidence-based strategies to design financially sustainable interventions, ultimately enhancing the reach and efficacy of transformative educational models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create, fund, and manage innovations in education. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, the design of learning environments, the economics of education, entrepreneurship, evaluation, finance, human-centered design, investing, resource management, project management, and marketing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding and treatment of complex communication disorders through integrative computational modeling of auditory and speech-language processes. A critical challenge in audiology and speech-language pathology lies in disentangling the multifactorial interactions between auditory processing deficits, neural language pathways, and compensatory mechanisms in individuals with overlapping disorders, such as those with hearing loss and aphasia. Current clinical models often address these domains in isolation, limiting the personalization of therapeutic interventions. To address this gap, we propose developing a multimodal computational framework that integrates neuroimaging data (fMRI, EEG), speech acoustics, and auditory-evoked potentials to simulate dynamic interactions between auditory and language networks under varying conditions of sensory deprivation and rehabilitation. The project will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze large-scale datasets from clinical populations, alongside biophysically informed neural network models to simulate pathological and treatment-induced plasticity. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution neuroimaging datasets, optimizing complex model parameters, and running real-time simulations of therapeutic scenarios (e.g., cochlear implant programming paired with language therapy). Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers predictive of cross-modal rehabilitation success, the generation of patient-specific intervention protocols, and the creation of open-source tools for simulating communication disorder trajectories. By bridging computational neuroscience with clinical practice, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for optimizing dual-qualified clinician training and improving functional outcomes for patients with co-occurring auditory and speech-language impairments. The proposed computational workflows will also provide a foundation for future studies exploring bidirectional relationships between hearing health and language recovery in neurodegenerative and acquired brain injury contexts.
cip_title: Audiology/ Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathology/ Pathologist
cip_definition: An integrated program that prepares individuals to work as both audiologists and speech-language pathologists. Includes instruction in a variety of communication disorder studies, audiology, speech pathology, language acquisition, and the design and implementation of comprehensive therapeutic and rehabilitative solutions to communications problems.

abstract: The proposed research addresses a critical gap in radiation protection protocols by investigating the complex interplay of low-dose, mixed-radiation fields in occupational and environmental settings. Current risk models, which primarily rely on linear extrapolations from high-dose exposures, inadequately capture the biological effects of prolonged, low-dose exposure to heterogeneous radiation types (e.g., alpha, beta, gamma, neutron). This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multiscale simulation framework integrating radiation transport, cellular response dynamics, and probabilistic risk assessment. Monte Carlo N-Particle (MCNP) simulations will model radiation interactions at the subcellular level across diverse exposure scenarios, while agent-based modeling will simulate DNA damage repair mechanisms and tissue-level responses. Machine learning algorithms will analyze terabyte-scale datasets generated by these simulations to identify nonlinear dose-response patterns and predict long-term health risks. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental radiobiology data from in vitro cell cultures exposed to controlled radiation mixtures. By quantifying the synergistic effects of mixed radiation fields on genomic instability and carcinogenic potential, this research aims to establish evidence-based thresholds for radiation safety in emerging contexts such as nuclear decommissioning sites, space travel, and advanced radiotherapy facilities. The outcomes will directly inform the development of adaptive radiation monitoring systems and personalized dosimetry strategies, bridging the gap between theoretical health physics and practical safety implementations. Access to HPC resources is essential due to the iterative nature of radiation transport simulations, the combinatorial complexity of mixed-field analyses, and the need for real-time uncertainty quantification across billions of particle histories. This interdisciplinary approach advances radiation protection science by providing a computational toolkit to address 21st-century challenges in occupational and environmental health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health physicists, occupational safety and health specialists, and public health officials, to monitor and control radiation exposure and implement preventive measures in health care, work, and natural environments. Includes instruction in radiation physics, environmental radioactivity, radiological instrumentation, electronics of radiation detection equipment, radioactive waste management and control, safety and handling procedures, decontamination procedures, radioactivity testing and analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation propagation in decentralized digital media ecosystems using advanced computational modeling. While prior research has focused on centralized social networks, the rapid growth of federated platforms, encrypted messaging apps, and blockchain-based media presents new challenges for understanding how unverified claims gain traction across technically and culturally disparate communities. The research problem centers on developing a framework to simulate cross-platform information flows while accounting for heterogeneous moderation policies, algorithmic recommendation systems, and user agency. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques with multi-agent network modeling to analyze three terabyte-scale datasets: 1) longitudinal content archives from Mastodon instances, 2) Telegram channel metadata, and 3) blockchain transaction records tied to decentralized social platforms. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to classify content types and rhetorical strategies, while parallelized graph algorithms will map temporal-spatial patterns in cross-platform sharing. The HPC resources are essential for processing encrypted network traffic patterns through probabilistic data structures, running evolutionary optimization of agent-based models, and maintaining versioned datasets across the project lifecycle. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for simulating polycentric information ecosystems, empirical insights into vulnerability thresholds for misinformation amplification in decentralized networks, and actionable metrics for platform designers seeking to balance free expression with community safeguards. By advancing computational methods tailored to emergent media architectures, this work aims to reshape theoretical paradigms in digital communication studies while providing practical resources for stakeholders addressing next-generation misinformation challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication and media studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Aging populations present complex challenges that intersect social structures, health outcomes, and environmental interactions. This project investigates the dynamic relationship between social connectivity patterns and cognitive resilience in older adults, leveraging computational models to simulate longitudinal social networks and their impact on cognitive health trajectories. While prior gerontological research has established correlations between social engagement and cognitive function, the causal mechanisms and nonlinear interactions—such as feedback loops between isolation, health behaviors, and community resource access—remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) integrating individual-level cognitive decline algorithms with macro-scale social and environmental datasets. The model will simulate diverse aging populations across varying community contexts (e.g., urban/rural divides, access to public infrastructure) over decadal timescales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-terabyte longitudinal datasets (e.g., health surveys, geospatial activity traces) and execute parallelized simulations testing thousands of parameter combinations. Machine learning techniques will identify critical inflection points where policy interventions (e.g., transportation systems, community center placements) could amplify cognitive resilience. By quantifying how micro-level social interactions scale to population-level outcomes, this research aims to generate actionable insights for equitable aging-in-place initiatives. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation framework for gerontological policy testing and empirically grounded thresholds for cost-effective community investments. The computational demands—including memory-intensive network analyses and real-time calibration of neural network-based cognitive models—exceed the capacity of standard institutional clusters, necessitating HPC support for both scalable computation and robust sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences and psychology.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in resource allocation for technology-driven supply chains, a critical challenge in science and technology management. As industries increasingly adopt complex, multi-stakeholder production systems, traditional linear optimization models fail to account for dynamic variables such as real-time demand fluctuations, sustainability constraints, and cross-organizational dependencies. The research aims to develop an adaptive decision-support framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale, non-linear resource allocation scenarios. Leveraging agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations, the computational approach will integrate operational data from partner manufacturing firms with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) metrics to evaluate trade-offs between cost efficiency, risk mitigation, and regulatory compliance. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning supplier networks, IoT-enabled production logs, and market forecasts while maintaining the low-latency requirements of iterative scenario testing. Expected outcomes include a validated machine learning model for predictive resource allocation under uncertainty and a benchmarking tool to assess organizational readiness for AI-driven operational decision-making. Results will advance management strategies for technology-intensive industries by quantifying how computational scalability impacts strategic planning outcomes. The project will also generate open-access simulation templates to help small and mid-sized enterprises adopt data-driven resource management practices. By bridging computational science with operations management theory, this work aligns with the program’s focus on developing technical and analytical competencies for leading technology-based organizations in evolving regulatory and competitive landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop science, technical, and business skills required for management of people and systems in technology-based industries, government agencies, and non-profit organizations. Includes instruction in computer applications, general management principles, production and operations management, project management, quality control, safety and health issues, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing radar system performance in contested electromagnetic environments, where adversarial signal degradation, spectrum congestion, and emerging electronic warfare tactics threaten operational effectiveness. Current radar resource management strategies struggle to adapt to dynamic, multi-threat scenarios due to computational limitations in real-time signal processing and decision-making algorithms. Our research proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex radar-environment interactions across tactical networks. The computational approach integrates physics-based radar propagation models with machine learning techniques to predict and mitigate interference patterns, while testing adaptive waveform allocation strategies under varying threat conditions. By simulating large-scale scenarios involving coordinated radar networks, mobile platforms, and adversarial countermeasures, the project aims to identify optimal resource allocation protocols that balance detection accuracy, spectral efficiency, and anti-jamming resilience. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for dynamic spectrum sharing, improved signal classification architectures resistant to deception techniques, and quantifiable performance benchmarks for next-generation radar systems operating in multi-domain battle spaces. This work bridges the gap between traditional radar engineering and modern computational warfare requirements, offering actionable insights for maintaining electromagnetic superiority without requiring hardware modifications. The requested computing resources will enable parametric studies across 10^6+ scenario variations, dramatically accelerating the development cycle for tactical radar enhancements while maintaining operational security constraints inherent to military research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of air, sea and ground-based radar systems. Includes instruction in electronic principles and digital techniques, transistors and solid-state component theory, radar systems; maintenance technology, data processing systems, wiring and circuit schematics, maintenance management, safety procedures, and applications to specific systems and services.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing dynamic portfolio strategies under systemic risk shocks influenced by climate transition pathways. Traditional portfolio models often inadequately capture nonlinear interdependencies between asset classes, regulatory shifts, and climate-related financial stressors, particularly during abrupt market realignments. The study addresses this gap by integrating agent-based market simulations with forward-looking climate scenario analysis—synthesizing granular financial data, geopolitical risk indicators, and probabilistic climate policy timelines. Computational challenges include real-time optimization of multi-objective portfolios (balancing returns, decarbonization targets, and tail risk exposure) across high-dimensional parameter spaces, requiring Monte Carlo simulations with adaptive Bayesian learning algorithms. HPC resources will enable parallelized testing of hedging strategies against stochastic climate pathways from IPCC AR6 datasets, coupled with sentiment analysis of regulatory announcements using transformer-based NLP models. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for stress-testing investment portfolios against climate-driven regime shifts, with open-source release of modular code for scenario weighting and liquidity-adjusted risk propagation. This work aims to advance practical methods for aligning securities valuation with transition physics while addressing computational bottlenecks in multi-horizon, multi-agent financial systems. The requested resources directly support iterative model training, hyperparameter tuning across 10,000+ simulated market epochs, and validation against historical crisis periods (2008, 2020) to quantify robustness improvements over conventional mean-variance approaches.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage assets placed in capital markets, and related technical operations. Includes instruction in security analysis, debt and equity analysis, investment strategies, securities markets, computer-assisted research, portfolio management, portfolio performance analysis, and applications to specific investment problems and business situations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex interactions between culinary techniques, ingredient properties, and sensory outcomes in understudied regional cuisines. The culinary arts lack a systematic framework for predicting how variations in preparation methods—such as fermentation durations, thermal gradients during cooking, or mechanical processing of ingredients—affect molecular stability, textural evolution, and flavor profiles in culturally significant dishes. Current experimental approaches are resource-intensive and limited in scalability, leaving gaps in preserving culinary heritage and innovating sustainable practices. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning-driven sensory prediction models, and agent-based simulations of traditional cooking workflows. Datasets will include physicochemical properties of rare ingredients, ethnographic records of preparation practices, and multi-sensor evaluations of dish outcomes. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of protein denaturation, starch retrogradation, and lipid oxidation under diverse thermal and mechanical conditions, while neural networks trained on gastronomic datasets will map these processes to qualitative sensory descriptors. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing traditional techniques under resource constraints, a digital repository of at-risk culinary practices, and frameworks for adapting heritage methods to modern sustainability goals. By bridging computational science and culinary ethnography, this work aims to establish a novel interdisciplinary domain that supports cultural preservation, food security, and innovation in gastronomic sciences. The scalability of this approach will be validated through case studies on fermented legume-based dishes from Southeast Asia and slow-cooked meat preparations from West Africa, prioritizing cuisines with limited prior quantitative analysis.
cip_title: Culinary Arts and Related Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary arts and related services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of stylistic and thematic patterns in understudied English prose fiction from the 18th to early 20th centuries, leveraging computational text analysis to address gaps in traditional literary historiography. While canonical works from this period have been extensively analyzed, vast archives of non-canonical novels—including serialized fiction, regional narratives, and genre hybrids—remain underexplored due to their scale and fragmented preservation. The research problem centers on identifying latent aesthetic and ideological shifts within this corpus that challenge existing models of literary periodization. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based embeddings and dynamic topic modeling, to a curated dataset of 5,000 digitized texts drawn from open-access repositories like HathiTrust and Project Gutenberg. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training custom word embeddings on archaic lexical structures, running iterative clustering algorithms across multidimensional stylistic features (syntax, diction, metaphor density), and visualizing longitudinal trends through GPU-accelerated dimensionality reduction. Expected outcomes include 1) the identification of previously unrecognized subgenres and stylistic cohorts within marginalized literary production, 2) quantitative evidence for how industrial capitalism influenced narrative pacing and focalization techniques, and 3) an open-access toolkit for diachronic style analysis optimized for historical Englishes. By bridging computational methods with critical hermeneutics, this work aims to recalibrate scholarly understanding of literary innovation while demonstrating how HPC-enabled distant reading can productively complicate traditional close-reading paradigms in English studies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in English language literature, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation strategies for boutique hotels facing volatile demand patterns influenced by localized events, environmental factors, and shifting traveler preferences. Traditional revenue management systems struggle to account for hyperlocal variables—such as neighborhood construction timelines, microclimate-driven tourism trends, or transient social media activity—that disproportionately impact small-to-midsize lodging operations. The project will employ high-performance computing resources to train multi-agent reinforcement learning models that simulate guest decision-making processes, competitor pricing behaviors, and operational constraints specific to boutique properties. By integrating real-time data streams from municipal APIs, weather sensors, and anonymized mobility datasets, the models will predict optimal room pricing, staffing allocations, and amenity investment thresholds at 15-minute intervals across a 12-month forecasting horizon. Computational challenges include resolving stochastic demand shocks through Monte Carlo simulations, optimizing non-linear utility functions for diverse traveler segments, and validating model outputs against proprietary transaction datasets from 40 participating hotels. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that enables independent hoteliers to dynamically adjust strategies without relying on corporate franchise systems, potentially reducing revenue leakage by 8-12% in pilot implementations. The work advances computational hospitality research by bridging operations management, behavioral economics, and urban informatics, while providing scalable methods for resource-constrained businesses in the experience economy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage and control; hotel facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; marketing and sales promotion; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotels and motel operations.

abstract: Electrocardiograph (ECG) technology remains a cornerstone of cardiac diagnostics, yet the growing complexity of arrhythmia patterns and the integration of multimodal physiological data present challenges for real-time, high-fidelity analysis. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to enhance ECG interpretation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic cardiac electrical activity in heterogeneous patient populations. The research addresses the critical gap in existing ECG analysis tools, which often rely on static thresholds and population-averaged metrics, limiting their ability to detect subtle, patient-specific anomalies in real-world clinical settings. Using anonymized ECG datasets paired with hemodynamic and demographic metadata, we will train physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to simulate personalized cardiac conduction pathways. These models will integrate nonlinear dynamics of ion channel behavior and tissue-specific conductivity, calibrated via inverse problem-solving approaches accelerated by GPU parallelization. A second computational layer will employ federated learning to refine detection algorithms for rare arrhythmias while preserving data privacy across collaborating institutions. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to assess model robustness under physiological variability, such as electrolyte imbalances or medication effects, which are poorly characterized in conventional ECG analysis. Expected outcomes include an open-source software toolkit for adaptive ECG interpretation, validated against clinical outcomes in a retrospective cohort, and a novel biomarker library linking simulated conduction abnormalities to early signs of structural heart disease. This work bridges computational cardiology and clinical ECG practice, offering a scalable platform to advance precision diagnostics in resource-constrained environments. By transcending traditional heuristic methods, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for ECG technology that dynamically adapts to individual patient physiology, ultimately reducing diagnostic latency and improving therapeutic targeting for complex cardiac conditions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize error detection and correction in high-volume, heterogeneous data entry workflows using adaptive pattern recognition and real-time user behavior modeling. While modern microcomputer applications provide foundational tools for data processing, repetitive manual entry tasks—common in fields like healthcare, logistics, and archival digitization—remain prone to inconsistencies arising from human fatigue, cognitive biases, and contextual ambiguities in source materials. Traditional quality assurance methods rely on post hoc validation, creating latency and inefficiency. Our research proposes a dynamic system that integrates keystroke dynamics, temporal workflow patterns, and semantic context analysis to predict and mitigate errors during data ingestion. The approach combines stochastic process modeling with transformer-based natural language processing adapted for structured and semi-structured data formats. High-performance computing resources are critical to train ensemble models on synthetically generated datasets replicating diverse entry scenarios (e.g., handwritten text digitization, spreadsheet population from audio transcripts) and to simulate real-time inference across distributed user environments. Expected outcomes include 1) a probabilistic error classification system that adapts to individual user patterns, 2) an open-source middleware library for augmenting existing data entry platforms with low-latency corrective feedback, and 3) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational pre-validation against conventional manual review in accuracy and throughput. By addressing the intersection of human-computer interaction, applied information theory, and operational ergonomics, this work aims to establish scalable quality control standards for legacy and emerging data entry ecosystems while reducing the cognitive and temporal burdens on operators. The requested resources will enable large-scale parallelism for simulating edge-case scenarios and optimizing model interoperability across heterogeneous microcomputer architectures.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform basic data and text entry using standard and customized software products. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, personal computer and work station operation, reading draft texts and raw data forms, audio and tape dictation, and various interactive software programs used for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing school-based interventions for enhancing social-emotional learning (SEL) and academic engagement in K–12 students. A critical challenge in educational psychology is modeling the dynamic, multi-level interactions between student traits, instructional practices, and intervention components that collectively shape learning outcomes. Traditional statistical methods often oversimplify these interdependencies, limiting the ability to predict how interventions perform across diverse classroom contexts. To address this, we propose developing computational models that integrate agent-based simulations with longitudinal educational datasets. The agent-based framework will represent students, teachers, and school environments as interactive entities, parameterized using empirical data on developmental trajectories, behavioral patterns, and intervention response metrics from 15 regional school districts. Machine learning pipelines will then analyze simulated and real-world data to identify context-sensitive predictors of intervention efficacy. HPC resources are essential for scaling these computationally intensive tasks: parallelized simulations will explore thousands of scenarios varying classroom compositions, intervention timing, and implementation fidelity, while deep learning architectures will process multimodal data (e.g., academic records, behavioral surveys, teacher reports). Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model linking intervention design to context-dependent student outcomes and (2) actionable guidelines for tailoring counseling strategies and SEL programs to specific school environments. This work directly supports the program’s mission to improve educational processes through psychological research, offering novel tools to bridge the gap between individualized counseling principles and systemic educational practices. By elucidating how interventions interact with classroom ecosystems, the project aims to empower educators with evidence-based strategies for fostering equitable student development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: Actuarial risk models increasingly face challenges in capturing complex, interdependent risks (e.g., climate-related catastrophes, pandemic shocks, or systemic financial disruptions) due to limitations in computational scalability and the integration of heterogeneous data sources. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for dynamic, multi-scale risk modeling that addresses these gaps. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks of traditional actuarial methods, which struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces, real-time stochastic simulations, and the fusion of structured (claims data) and unstructured (environmental sensor data, socio-economic indicators) datasets. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo-based stochastic optimization, agent-based modeling, and hybrid machine learning architectures to simulate emergent risk scenarios under non-stationary conditions. Key methodologies include parallelized nested simulation for liability valuation, GPU-accelerated gradient descent for capital allocation optimization, and graph neural networks to model contagion effects in interconnected risk portfolios. The proposed HPC resources will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses across 10^6+ parameter combinations, reduce simulation wall-time for multi-year horizon models from weeks to hours, and facilitate the integration of terabyte-scale external datasets (e.g., satellite imagery for flood risk mapping). Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible actuarial simulation library optimized for distributed-memory architectures, (2) quantitative evidence for regulatory capital adjustments under climate stress scenarios, and (3) improved risk-adjusted pricing models for parametric insurance products. This work will directly enhance the actuarial community’s capacity to address systemic risks through computationally rigorous tools while providing a template for HPC adoption in solvency testing and enterprise risk management applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical analysis of risk, and their applications to insurance and other business management problems. Includes instruction in forecasting theory, quantitative and non-quantitative risk measurement methodologies, development of risk tables, secondary data analysis, and computer-assisted research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in optimizing the design and control of advanced electromechanical systems, such as automated manufacturing assemblies, robotic actuators, and energy-efficient servomechanical drives. Current physical prototyping and experimental validation workflows for these systems are resource-intensive, time-consuming, and limited in their ability to explore complex parameter spaces. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation framework that integrates electromechanical dynamics, thermal behavior, and control system interactions. The computational approach will employ finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and electromagnetic modeling, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management simulations. Dynamic system responses will be analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink co-simulations, while machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify optimal control strategies and material configurations. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and real-time digital twin implementations for systems requiring microsecond-scale temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for electromechanical component degradation, optimized control algorithms for energy-efficient operation, and a modular simulation toolkit for rapid prototyping of hybrid systems. This work will directly support ongoing research in smart manufacturing and renewable energy integration, while providing undergraduate researchers in Electromechanical Engineering Technology with hands-on experience in computational engineering methods. The resulting open-source models and datasets will advance the field’s capacity to design resilient, adaptive systems, reducing reliance on physical testing by an estimated 40–60% in targeted applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize sustainable fabric selection and style coordination in fashion consulting, addressing gaps in data-driven decision-making for eco-conscious apparel design. The research problem centers on the lack of integrated tools that dynamically reconcile aesthetic, functional, and environmental criteria—such as material durability, carbon footprint, and client-specific style preferences—across diverse use cases, from everyday wear to event-based consultations. Current manual approaches rely on heuristic expertise, limiting scalability and consistency in an industry increasingly pressured to meet sustainability benchmarks. To address this, we propose a hybrid machine learning and simulation pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Deep learning models trained on textile property datasets (e.g., tensile strength, biodegradability) and historical client preference data will predict optimal fabric combinations, while agent-based simulations will model long-term wear patterns and environmental impact under varying climatic and usage conditions. A reinforcement learning module will iteratively refine style recommendations based on simulated client feedback loops. The computational intensity arises from processing high-resolution 3D fabric drape simulations, real-time lifecycle assessment calculations, and multi-objective optimization across thousands of material-client-scenario permutations. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for personalized, sustainability-optimized fashion consulting, validated against industry partner datasets, and a novel benchmarking tool for quantifying trade-offs between aesthetic priorities and ecological impacts. This work bridges computational sustainability, human-centered design, and textile science, offering a template for data-driven innovation in non-traditional HPC domains while advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) within the fashion sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in apparel and fashion selection, style coordination, customer sales and consulting, fabric selection, clothing specifications, and contract buying activities. Includes instruction in supplying regular clothing needs or acting as a consultant for special events such as weddings.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to optimize decision-making for agribusinesses facing dynamic risks from climate variability, market fluctuations, and supply chain disruptions. Current agricultural business models often rely on static or compartmentalized data, limiting their ability to adapt to real-time challenges such as extreme weather events, commodity price volatility, or livestock disease outbreaks. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a scalable, multi-agent simulation platform that synthesizes heterogeneous datasets—including historical climate records, real-time satellite imagery, IoT sensor outputs from farm equipment, and global market trends—into predictive analytics. The computational approach will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between stakeholders (e.g., producers, distributors, retailers) and hybrid machine learning techniques to forecast short- and long-term agricultural outcomes. Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in yield predictions, while graph-based algorithms will optimize logistics for resilient supply chains. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to reduce model runtime by 70–80% compared to existing tools, enabling near-real-time scenario testing for farm managers and corporate planners. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool for evaluating trade-offs in resource allocation, risk mitigation strategies, and sustainability metrics. The framework will be validated through case studies focused on midwestern U.S. grain cooperatives and poultry supply networks in Southeast Asia, with results directly applicable to improving operational efficiency, reducing financial losses from disruptions, and balancing profitability with environmental stewardship. This work bridges computational innovation and agribusiness management, offering scalable solutions to enhance food system resilience in a rapidly changing global economy.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage agricultural businesses and agriculturally related operations within diversified corporations. Includes instruction in agriculture, agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, finance, marketing, planning, human resources management, and other managerial responsibilities.

abstract: Infertility and reproductive endocrine disorders, such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, and diminished ovarian reserve, represent complex clinical challenges with multifactorial etiologies involving genetic, hormonal, and metabolic dysregulation. Current approaches to understanding these conditions often lack the capacity to integrate large-scale, multi-dimensional data, limiting insights into their underlying mechanisms and the development of personalized treatment strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and clinical metadata, through advanced machine learning and network analysis techniques. Computational models will be developed to simulate dynamic endocrine interactions and predict individual responses to ovarian stimulation protocols in assisted reproductive technology (ART). Additionally, high-throughput image analysis pipelines will be deployed to quantify follicular development patterns from ultrasound data, correlating morphological features with hormonal profiles and cycle outcomes. The utilization of HPC will enable the processing of terabytes of heterogeneous data, iterative training of deep neural networks for biomarker discovery, and large-scale in silico experiments testing hypothetical therapeutic interventions. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel molecular signatures associated with infertility subtypes, predictive algorithms for optimizing ART protocols, and mechanistic insights into ovarian aging pathways. By bridging computational innovation with clinical data, this research aims to advance precision medicine in reproductive endocrinology, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy, treatment personalization, and success rates for patients experiencing infertility.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage complex problems relating to reproductive endocrinology and infertility.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural production and digital archiving practices of marginalized racial and ethnic communities in North America. The research problem centers on the limited accessibility and fragmented preservation of community-generated media—such as zines, oral histories, and grassroots publications—that document lived experiences of resistance, identity formation, and collective memory. Traditional methods of analyzing these materials are constrained by the scale of data, the need for multimodal analysis (text, image, audio), and the ethical complexities of handling culturally sensitive content. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, machine learning-assisted image recognition, and network analysis to map patterns in cultural narratives, visual symbolism, and intercommunity collaborations across digitized collections. Key tasks include training custom NLP models to identify themes in non-standardized vernacular texts, developing image classifiers to trace recurring visual motifs in self-published art, and constructing temporal networks to analyze shifts in activist discourse from the 1960s to the present. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of high-resolution archival scans, optimizing deep learning architectures for low-resource language varieties (e.g., Indigenous languages, African American Vernacular English), and running iterative simulations to validate network models. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for ethically engaged ethnic studies research, new frameworks for decentralizing archival authority through community-led metadata practices, and interdisciplinary findings on how marginalized groups have navigated cultural erasure through grassroots media. By scaling qualitative insights across larger corpora while maintaining nuanced attention to context, this work aims to reshape methodologies in ethnic studies and inform contemporary debates on equitable digital stewardship.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
