cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary and comparative study of the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of North American racial and ethnic groups, including African Americans, American Indians/Native Americans, Hispanic Americans, and Asian Americans.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance pedagogical strategies for vocational-technical educators by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze complex, dynamic classroom interactions. Technical teacher education faces a critical challenge: traditional training methods often fail to capture the nuanced interplay between hands-on skill demonstration, real-time problem-solving, and adaptive instruction required in technical disciplines such as engineering, manufacturing, or information technology. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates vocational teaching environments using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML). The ABM component will integrate heterogeneous agents (students, instructors, and equipment) with variable skill levels, learning behaviors, and environmental constraints, while ML algorithms will identify patterns in instructional effectiveness across simulated scenarios. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale parameter spaces—including diverse student backgrounds, technical task complexities, and pedagogical interventions—and to run iterative simulations that reflect real-world variability. Expected outcomes include a validated model for predicting optimal teaching strategies under resource-limited conditions, a dataset of scenario-based training modules for technical educators, and a tool for assessing the impact of adaptive teaching methods on student competency development. By quantifying how technical instruction succeeds or fails in simulated environments, this research will provide evidence-based frameworks to improve vocational teacher preparation programs, directly aligning with the program’s goal of advancing equitable, high-quality technical education. The computational outputs will be disseminated as open-source resources to support curriculum design and instructor training in secondary and postsecondary technical education systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational technical education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize AI-driven workflow automation tools for administrative support roles by analyzing complex, unstructured communication patterns in hybrid office environments. The proliferation of asynchronous communication platforms (email, chat systems, collaborative documents) has created bottlenecks in task prioritization and delegation, particularly when managing cross-departmental requests with conflicting urgency signals. Current rule-based automation systems fail to adequately interpret contextual nuances in stakeholder communications, leading to inefficient resource allocation in calendaring, document routing, and meeting coordination. This study proposes developing a multimodal natural language processing (NLP) framework trained on anonymized organizational datasets—including email threads, project management logs, and meeting transcripts—to predict optimal task handling pathways. The computational approach combines transformer-based language models with temporal graph neural networks to map request-response patterns across communication channels while preserving confidentiality through differential privacy techniques. High-performance computing resources are required for three critical phases: 1) Parallel processing of terabyte-scale historical communication data to establish baseline interaction patterns, 2) Federated learning across simulated departmental knowledge domains, and 3) Real-time optimization testing through discrete event simulations modeling 10,000+ concurrent workflow scenarios. Expected outcomes include a probabilistic decision-support system that reduces administrative latency in complex request handling by 35-50% compared to current industry-standard tools, as measured through simulated stress tests and validated against human expert benchmarks. The research bridges computational linguistics with organizational behavior theory, offering novel insights into human-AI collaboration dynamics in modern administrative ecosystems. Successful implementation could redefine competency frameworks for administrative professionals by introducing evidence-based metrics for evaluating automation-assisted workflow efficiency.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: The discovery of bioactive natural products with therapeutic potential remains challenging due to the structural complexity of natural compounds and the limitations of empirical screening approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the identification, optimization, and mechanistic characterization of bioactive molecules derived from plant, microbial, and marine sources. Computational methods including molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning will be employed to virtually screen large natural product libraries against disease-relevant biological targets, with particular emphasis on antimicrobial resistance and oncology-related protein systems. Quantum mechanical calculations will complement MD simulations to investigate enzyme-substrate interactions in biosynthetic pathways, guiding the engineering of novel analogs with improved pharmacokinetic properties. A cheminformatics pipeline will be developed to integrate ethnobotanical data with metabolomic profiles and predicted ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) parameters, enabling prioritization of lead candidates for experimental validation. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of density functional theory calculations for 3D structure refinement and the training of graph neural networks on >500,000 natural product structures to predict bioactivity landscapes. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel chemotypes with validated biological activity, computational frameworks for rational natural product analog design, and open-access tools for the pharmacognosy community. This work will advance methodologies in computational pharmacognosy while addressing pressing needs for new therapeutic entities derived from nature's chemical diversity.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of integrated building systems modeling tools for sustainable architectural design. Current approaches to optimizing energy efficiency, structural resilience, and environmental performance in buildings often rely on fragmented simulations that inadequately capture the interdependencies between mechanical, thermal, and structural systems. This limitation hinders the ability to holistically evaluate design trade-offs in complex urban environments. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework coupling finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-physics interactions within building systems at unprecedented resolution. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of building prototypes under dynamic environmental loads, integrating real-world climate data and material behavior models. Key tasks include validating a coupled FEA-CFD model for predicting heat transfer and airflow in mixed-use structures, training ML surrogates to accelerate parametric design optimization, and conducting probabilistic risk assessments of structural failures under extreme weather scenarios. The computational workflow will utilize open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCS) alongside custom Python-based optimization routines, requiring distributed memory architectures for large-scale matrix computations and GPU acceleration for neural network training. Expected outcomes include a novel digital twin methodology for building performance analysis, actionable insights into climate-adaptive design strategies, and open-access datasets quantifying energy-structure-environment synergies. By enabling high-fidelity, system-level simulations, this research will directly support architects and engineers in creating next-generation buildings that balance operational efficiency, safety, and environmental stewardship. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational intensity of 3D transient simulations and ML model development, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of architects, engineers and planners engaged in designing and developing buildings, urban complexes, and related systems. Includes instruction in design testing procedures, building site analysis, model building and computer graphics, engineering drawing, structural systems testing, analysis of prototype mechanical and interior systems, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of adaptive real-time systems in industrial automation demands computational frameworks capable of dynamically balancing latency, accuracy, and resource constraints. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing embedded control logic for multi-agent robotic systems operating in unpredictable environments, where traditional static programming models fail to account for fluctuating sensor noise, variable communication bandwidth, and heterogeneous hardware capabilities. Leveraging a novel hybrid approach combining online evolutionary algorithms with lightweight containerized simulation kernels, the research aims to develop a self-tuning framework that autonomously reconfigures control parameters and task allocation strategies during runtime. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for parallelizing the training of context-aware reinforcement learning models that predict environmental disturbance patterns, as well as for large-scale validation of emergent swarm behaviors across thousands of simulated production scenarios. The computational workflow involves iterative optimization cycles using GPU-accelerated parameter sweeps, coupled with real-time physics-based emulation of material handling workflows on CPU clusters. Expected outcomes include an open-source middleware toolkit for adaptive edge computing in smart manufacturing environments, validated through digital twin simulations mirroring operational data from collaborating industry partners. This work bridges gaps between industrial control systems and distributed computing by establishing methodologies for runtime-adaptive programming in resource-constrained cyber-physical environments, with potential applications in agile production lines and disaster response robotics. Successful implementation will provide a template for embedding HPC-driven optimization directly into operational technology stacks without compromising deterministic execution requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of general computer programming to the solution of specific operational problems and customization requirements presented by individual software users and organizational users. Includes training in specific types of software and its installation and maintenance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content in the global arts and entertainment industries. As generative AI tools rapidly disrupt creative sectors, legal systems worldwide face challenges in reconciling intellectual property (IP) laws, attribution standards, and ethical guidelines with emerging technologies. The study will focus on comparative jurisdictional analyses of copyright, moral rights, and liability frameworks across 50+ countries, combining large-scale text mining of legal databases, policy documents, and litigation records with network analysis of cross-border regulatory influences. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) models trained to detect semantic patterns in statutory texts and judicial decisions, machine learning classifiers to predict legislative trends, and agent-based simulations modeling stakeholder interactions (creators, platforms, regulators). The project requires HPC capabilities to process multilingual legal corpora exceeding 10TB, optimize transformer-based architectures for low-resource legal languages, and run complex simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include a predictive mapping of regulatory divergence points in AI-content governance, identification of transnational policy harmonization opportunities, and an open-access toolkit for benchmarking legal risks in AI-driven creative workflows. By integrating computational social science with arts law scholarship, this work aims to address critical gaps in adaptive legal infrastructure for algorithmic creativity while establishing a replicable framework for data-driven analysis of emergent issues at the technology-law interface.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of biomechanical forces in cancer progression and metastasis, with a focus on tumor microenvironment dynamics. Despite evidence that mechanical properties of tissues influence cancer cell behavior, the mechanisms linking mechanical stress, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and metastatic spread remain poorly understood. Traditional experimental models struggle to isolate and quantify these multiscale interactions, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose to develop high-fidelity biomechanical models to simulate tumor-ECM interactions under physiological stress conditions, specifically examining how interstitial pressure, ECM stiffness, and fluid shear stress drive cellular invasion and vascular dissemination. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) to model tissue-scale strain distributions and agent-based modeling (ABM) to track individual cell responses to mechanical cues. These multiscale simulations will integrate empirical data from 3D bioprinted tumor models and patient-derived histology to parameterize ECM viscoelasticity and cell adhesion dynamics. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and real-time feedback between tissue deformation and cellular decision-making. Expected outcomes include identifying critical mechanical thresholds that trigger metastatic phenotypes and predicting how ECM-targeted therapies could alter tumor mechanics to suppress invasion. This work will establish a predictive framework for evaluating biomechanical drivers of cancer progression, directly informing translational strategies to disrupt metastasis. The requested HPC resources are essential for executing large-scale simulations, reducing computational bottlenecks in solving coupled solid-fluid mechanics equations, and enabling parameter sensitivity analyses across biologically relevant timescales. By bridging biomechanics and oncology, this project aims to advance mechanistic understanding of cancer mechanobiology while providing open-source computational tools for the broader research community.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, anatomical, and mechanical structure and function of the mechanical aspects of biological systems. Includes courses in anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, mechanics, measurement and instrumentation, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for real-time, immersive visualization of dynamic, high-dimensional environmental and urban datasets, integrating heterogeneous data streams from climate sensors, satellite imagery, and social media feeds. Existing visualization tools struggle to reconcile the temporal, spatial, and semantic complexity of such datasets, limiting their utility for cross-domain decision-making in sustainability planning and disaster response. The research addresses this gap by creating adaptive visualization pipelines that combine topological data analysis, perceptual modeling, and machine learning-driven dimensionality reduction. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support the parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, GPU-accelerated rendering of 3D temporal geospatial models, and real-time simulation of user interaction patterns across multi-modal interfaces (AR/VR, web dashboards). Computational workflows will leverage distributed memory architectures to optimize feature extraction from unstructured data and employ graph-based algorithms to map latent correlations between environmental variables and human activity metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for resource-efficient, perception-aware visual analytics, validated through case studies on coastal flood resilience and urban heat island mitigation. By unifying computational scalability with cognitive design principles, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for visual inference in data-rich, time-sensitive scenarios, directly benefiting researchers in environmental science, public health, and urban design. The requested HPC allocation will enable benchmarking at biologically relevant scales—such as simulating crowd movement during extreme weather events—while ensuring low-latency responsiveness for stakeholder-driven exploratory analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and derive meaning from data by using visual presentation tools and techniques. Includes instruction in cognitive science, computer programming, data management, data visualization theory, graphic design, infographics, perceptual psychology, statistics, and visual design.

abstract: Forest operations face critical challenges in balancing ecological preservation with the demand for efficient timber production, particularly as climate variability intensifies and regulatory frameworks evolve. Traditional forest harvesting optimization models often rely on static environmental parameters or simplified spatial assumptions, limiting their ability to adapt to dynamic conditions such as soil moisture fluctuations, habitat fragmentation risks, and real-time equipment performance data. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize forest harvesting systems under spatially and temporally variable constraints. The research will integrate multi-source geospatial data (LiDAR, satellite imagery, IoT-enabled soil sensors) with agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between harvesting machinery, forest ecosystems, and environmental conditions at unprecedented scales. Machine learning techniques will be applied to predict equipment wear patterns and energy consumption across diverse terrain types, while constraint programming will address multi-objective optimization of extraction routes that minimize soil compaction, carbon emissions, and canopy disturbance. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated parallel processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets encompassing multi-year environmental observations and detailed forest structural inventories. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool capable of generating adaptive harvesting plans that respond to real-time environmental feedback, reducing operational costs by an estimated 15-20% while maintaining compliance with biodiversity protection thresholds. The HPC resources will enable sensitivity analyses across 10^6+ parameter combinations to identify critical thresholds in system resilience, providing novel insights into the coupled dynamics of mechanized forestry operations and ecosystem health. This work bridges gaps between precision forestry, ecological engineering, and industrial systems optimization, offering a replicable methodology for sustainable resource extraction in climate-vulnerable regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and forestry principles to the design of mechanical devices and processes for efficient forest management, timber production and related forest logistics systems. Includes instruction in forest products processing, forest management, forest harvesting, timber structure design, production analysis, road and bridge construction, vehicle adaptation and design, and harvesting equipment design.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolution of dramatic texts and performance practices across distinct historical periods and cultural contexts through large-scale computational analysis. The central challenge lies in synthesizing and interpreting heterogeneous datasets—including play scripts, production records, historical reviews, and sociopolitical archives—to identify patterns in theatrical innovation, thematic shifts, and the transmission of artistic conventions. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to manage the scale and complexity of this data, particularly when analyzing multi-lingual works or tracking nonlinear influences among global theatre traditions. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical texts, network analysis to map creative collaborations and influence trajectories, and machine learning models to classify stylistic features across genres and eras. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training transformer-based models on curated corpora of dramatic literature (15th–20th centuries), processing non-standardized archival materials via optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines, and simulating agent-based models of theatrical dissemination. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts and performance metadata, quantitative frameworks for cross-cultural theatrical comparison, and visualizations tracing the diffusion of techniques like ensemble acting or experimental staging. By integrating computational methods with theatre historiography, this work aims to reveal previously underexamined connections between artistic practices and their historical contexts, offering new methodologies for performance studies while preserving the interpretive nuance central to the humanities. The project’s computational tools will also be adapted for pedagogical use, enabling students to engage dynamically with theatre history through data-driven inquiry.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the history, literature, theory, and analysis of written plays, theatrical productions, and theatre methods and organization. Includes instruction in historical method; critical theory; literary analysis; the study of themes and archetypes in dramatic literature; the history of acting, directing, and technical theatre; and the study of specific historical and cultural styles and traditions.

abstract: Modern diagnostic radiology relies on advanced imaging technologies to detect and treat diseases with precision, yet the computational demands of processing high-resolution multimodal imaging data—such as dynamic CT, MRI, and ultrasound—remain a critical bottleneck. This project seeks to address the challenge of real-time, patient-specific analysis of complex imaging datasets during image-guided interventions, where delays in processing can compromise clinical decision-making. Specifically, we aim to develop a scalable computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and fluid dynamics modeling to optimize the delivery of targeted therapies using radionuclides and electromagnetic radiation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep neural networks on multi-terabyte repositories of clinical imaging data, simulate radiation transport in heterogeneous tissues, and model transient biomechanical responses during ultrasound-mediated drug delivery. Key computational tasks include GPU-accelerated 3D image segmentation, finite element analysis of dose distributions, and parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of photon-electron interactions in anatomically realistic phantoms. The proposed workflows will leverage containerized environments to ensure reproducibility across heterogeneous imaging platforms. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated ML pipeline for predicting optimal intervention pathways based on patient-specific imaging biomarkers, (2) open-source tools for real-time adaptive radiotherapy planning, and (3) quantitative models linking ultrasound cavitation dynamics to enhanced permeability in tumor vasculature. By enabling rapid, large-scale analysis of spatial-temporal imaging data, this work will advance personalized therapeutic strategies in oncology and vascular diseases while reducing ionizing radiation exposure. The requested HPC allocation will directly support time-sensitive computations that cannot feasibly be performed on local clinical workstations, bridging the gap between research prototypes and translatable clinical tools.
cip_definition: Research on how to utilize x-ray, ionizing radiation, radionuclides, ultrasound, electromagnetic radiation, and image-guided intervention to diagnose and treat disease. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between multigenerational family communication patterns and emerging adult identity development using computational social science methods. While prior work in family systems has emphasized qualitative or survey-based approaches, this study addresses a critical gap by modeling how nonlinear, time-dependent interactions within family networks (e.g., parent-child-grandparent triads) influence psychosocial outcomes. The research problem centers on identifying computational signatures of adaptive versus maladaptive identity formation processes through analysis of longitudinal interaction data from 300 families, including multimodal behavioral (video-recorded discussions), linguistic (transcribed narratives), and physiological (heart rate variability) datasets. A high-performance computing (HPC) resource allocation is essential to implement agent-based models that simulate family communication dynamics across developmental timescales, integrating reinforcement learning architectures to capture how interpersonal feedback loops shape self-concept. Computational challenges include real-time natural language processing of dyadic emotional tone, network analysis of cross-generational influence hierarchies, and Bayesian inference models quantifying uncertainty in developmental trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for predicting identity coherence scores based on simulated family interaction patterns, (2) identification of computational biomarkers indicating resilience to intergenerational conflict, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing developmental cascades in family systems. By bridging developmental psychology with complex systems science, this work advances theoretical understanding of how micro-level interpersonal processes macro-scale identity outcomes, while providing methodological innovations for studying relational dynamics in HDFS research. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of >10TB of multimodal data and parallelized simulation of 50,000+ family interaction scenarios with varying cultural and socioeconomic parameters.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling and optimizing the integration of neural correlates of attention into adaptive human-computer interfaces (HCIs), a niche interdisciplinary domain bridging cognitive neuroscience, real-time data processing, and interactive system design. The core challenge lies in addressing the latency-reliability trade-off inherent in processing high-density electroencephalography (EEG) data streams to dynamically adjust interface parameters, such as information density or response thresholds, based on users’ fluctuating cognitive states. Current methods lack the computational efficiency to handle real-time multivariate EEG analysis while simultaneously running predictive models of user engagement, limiting the scalability of neuroadaptive systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for spatiotemporal feature extraction from sensor-level brain activity with lightweight reinforcement learning agents that optimize interface configurations. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to: 1) Train GNNs on our existing 12-terabyte multimodal dataset of EEG-recorded attention states during complex visualization tasks, 2) Simulate distributed processing pipelines for latency-critical components using containerized microservices, and 3) Conduct large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal architectures under varying noise profiles and computational constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for neuroadaptive interface development, quantitative benchmarks for real-time cognitive state classification, and novel insights into the computational resource requirements for maintaining sub-200ms closed-loop latency in multi-user scenarios. This work advances the emerging field of neurally-grounded human-computer collaboration while providing methodological innovations in edge-cloud hybrid computing for physiological data streams.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive language learning tools for English and French as second languages (ESL/FSL). A critical challenge in language education lies in addressing the heterogeneous needs of learners, particularly in optimizing individualized feedback and scaffolding in digital learning environments. Traditional methods often rely on static content or limited datasets, resulting in subpersonalized interventions. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to model learner interactions, predict linguistic development patterns, and dynamically adjust instructional content. The research will utilize anonymized learner corpora—comprising written, spoken, and multimodal interactions from diverse ESL/FSL classrooms—to train deep neural networks capable of parsing syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic errors in real time. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional linguistic data (e.g., speech waveforms, annotated texts) and scaling transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT, GPT variants) to handle low-resource language pairs and dialectal variations in French. Additionally, reinforcement learning frameworks will be deployed to simulate longitudinal language acquisition trajectories, enabling the system to recommend context-aware pedagogical strategies. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating adaptive language exercises, validated against classroom efficacy metrics, and a corpus annotated with error-tagged learner data. This work bridges computational linguistics and teacher education by providing instructors with actionable insights into learner progression while demonstrating how HPC can catalyze innovation in language pedagogy. The tools developed will prioritize scalability for under-resourced educational contexts, aligning with broader goals of equity in language education.
cip_title: Teaching English or French as a Second or Foreign Language, Other
cip_definition: Any program in teaching English or French as a second or foreign language, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural and environmental drivers of collective decision-making in wild meerkat (Suricata suricatta) groups using high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic interactions between individual cognition, social hierarchies, and ecological pressures. Despite extensive behavioral studies, the computational mechanisms by which meerkats integrate sensory input, memory, and social cues to reach group consensus during critical tasks—such as coordinating vigilance, foraging, or burrow relocation—remain poorly understood. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling framework that simulates neural networks encoding individual decision-making processes (e.g., risk assessment, signal interpretation) and scales these to emergent group behaviors. The model will incorporate empirical field data on meerkat movement, vocalizations, and environmental conditions collected via GPS collars and bioacoustic sensors. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across parameter spaces (e.g., varying group sizes, predation threats, resource distributions) and to train deep reinforcement learning algorithms that optimize agent behavior against empirical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of neural circuit motifs that stabilize or destabilize group coordination under ecological stress, (2) predictive maps of decision-making bottlenecks in fragmented habitats, and (3) open-source tools for simulating cross-species social cognition. By bridging ethology, computational neuroscience, and complex systems theory, this work will advance understanding of how modular neural architectures scale to collective intelligence—a gap in behavioral biomedicine with implications for conservation strategy and bio-inspired swarm robotics. The project’s computational demands necessitate sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and large-memory processors for high-resolution spatial agent interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the psychological and neurological bases of animal sensation, perception, cognition, behavior, and behavioral interactions within and outside the species. Includes instruction in ethology, behavioral neuroscience, neurobiology, behavioral evolution, cognition and sensory perception, motivators, learning and instinct, hormonal controls, reproductive and developmental biology, community ecology, functional behavior, and applications to specific behaviors and patterns as well as to specific phyla and species.

abstract: This project seeks to evaluate the cost-effectiveness and long-term health economic impacts of novel therapeutic interventions using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on optimizing pharmaceutical resource allocation in dynamic healthcare systems. The research problem centers on the limitations of traditional pharmacoeconomic models, which often oversimplify real-world heterogeneity in patient populations, treatment adherence patterns, and evolving market conditions. We propose developing a high-fidelity simulation framework integrating individual-level decision trees, Markov cohort models, and system dynamics approaches to capture multi-scale interactions between pharmaceutical interventions, healthcare utilization, and economic outcomes. The computational workload requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage three core components: (1) Bayesian probabilistic sensitivity analysis across 10,000+ parameter combinations for uncertainty quantification in cost-effectiveness models, (2) parallel processing of agent-based simulations modeling 10^6 synthetic patients with individualized treatment pathways and adverse event risks, and (3) optimization algorithms for formulary design under budget constraints using mixed-integer programming. Datasets will include merged electronic health records (2.5M+ patients), insurance claims databases, and pharmaceutical pricing data across multiple payers. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source modeling platform for comparative effectiveness research, sensitivity analyses identifying key cost drivers in specialty drug markets, and policy simulations quantifying the economic impact of value-based pricing mechanisms. This work will directly inform formulary decision-making processes while advancing methodological capabilities in pharmaceutical outcomes research through scalable computational approaches. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving sufficient model granularity and computational throughput to generate actionable insights for healthcare payers, providers, and regulatory stakeholders.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics and policy analysis to the study of the relationship of pharmacy services and pharmaceutical processes and products to the health care system and their impact on health care organizations. Includes instruction in health economics, pharmacoeconomics, health care systems, health care organization and management, statistics and biostatistics, outcomes research, health care policy, pharmacy services, and pharmaceutical industry operations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize clinical workflow efficiency and patient triage in outpatient care settings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in healthcare management. Outpatient facilities face mounting challenges in balancing resource allocation, staffing demands, and patient wait times, particularly as demographic shifts and chronic disease prevalence increase clinical workloads. Traditional scheduling systems often fail to adapt to real-time variables such as patient acuity, provider availability, and equipment utilization, leading to bottlenecks and suboptimal care delivery. To address this, we propose a machine learning model trained on multimodal clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), historical appointment logs, and sensor-derived patient flow metrics—to dynamically predict demand and recommend staffing or resource adjustments. The computational approach combines recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal pattern recognition with agent-based modeling to simulate patient-provider interactions under diverse operational scenarios. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of anonymized patient data, running parallelized simulations, and iteratively refining model hyperparameters via grid search optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool capable of reducing average patient wait times by 20–30% and improving clinician utilization rates in pilot clinics. The project also aims to identify systemic inefficiencies in diagnostic testing workflows through cluster analysis of procedural delays. By integrating clinical operations management with computational modeling, this work will provide actionable insights for healthcare administrators while advancing methodologies for scalable, ethical AI applications in medical settings. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for non-technical clinical staff, fostering equitable access to data-driven management strategies.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize clinical workflow efficiency in multi-specialty outpatient facilities through the development of a high-resolution simulation framework powered by machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling. Current healthcare management strategies often rely on static scheduling templates and retrospective data, leading to bottlenecks in patient flow, underutilization of staff and equipment, and increased wait times. The research addresses this gap by integrating real-time electronic health record (EHR) data, wearable device outputs, and environmental sensor feeds to dynamically model patient-provider interactions, resource availability, and facility-specific constraints. A hybrid computational approach will be employed: 1) Graph neural networks will predict patient movement patterns and service time variability across specialties such as radiology, physiotherapy, and point-of-care testing, and 2) Parallelized discrete-event simulations will test allocation strategies for clinical assistants, shared diagnostic equipment, and procedure rooms under diverse operational scenarios. The framework will be trained and validated using de-identified datasets from three academic medical centers encompassing 2.8 million patient encounters. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale temporal EHR data, running ensemble ML models with hyperparameter optimization across 500+ simulation parameters, and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses to account for rare clinical events and seasonal demand fluctuations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that enables facility managers to simulate the impact of staffing changes, equipment purchases, and workflow redesigns prior to implementation. By reducing computational barriers to precision health operations management, this work aims to establish new standards for data-driven clinical environment optimization while advancing methodological approaches for real-time healthcare system modeling.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize dispute resolution strategies across complex, multi-party scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations of traditional analytical methods. Dispute resolution processes in settings such as labor negotiations, international diplomacy, or corporate mergers involve dynamic interactions among stakeholders with competing priorities, cultural differences, and asymmetric information. Existing theoretical models often fail to capture the nonlinear feedback loops, behavioral biases, and context-dependent decision-making inherent in these systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), game-theoretic simulations, and natural language processing (NLP). The ABM component will simulate thousands of negotiation trajectories using empirically derived behavioral profiles, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize mediation strategies under varying constraints. NLP tools will analyze historical arbitration transcripts and treaty documents to identify linguistic patterns correlated with successful outcomes, informing model parameters. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to realistic participant numbers (50+ agents per scenario), parallelizing scenario testing, and processing large textual datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated dispute resolution benchmarks, (2) quantitative metrics for predicting negotiation breakdown risks, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive mediation protocols. By bridging computational social science with conflict resolution theory, this work aims to provide practitioners with data-driven tools to de-escalate high-stakes disputes while advancing methodological innovation in multidisciplinary computational humanities research. The project’s scale—encompassing 10,000+ simulation hours and terabyte-scale text analysis—necessitates cluster computing infrastructure with GPU acceleration and distributed memory capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation diffusion across digital media platforms using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale communication networks and analyze real-time interaction data. The rise of algorithmically amplified content and decentralized information ecosystems has complicated efforts to track and mitigate false narratives, posing critical challenges to public discourse and democratic processes. While prior studies have examined discrete cases of misinformation, gaps remain in understanding how platform-specific affordances, user behavior, and network structures interact to accelerate or inhibit viral spread. The research will employ computational methods including natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of multi-platform content, agent-based modeling to simulate information cascades under varying network topologies, and temporal network analysis to identify tipping points in dissemination patterns. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of social media data, training transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants) for context-aware misinformation detection, and running parallelized simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting misinformation hotspots based on real-time network metrics, evidence-based recommendations for platform-level intervention strategies, and open-access tools to help researchers analyze cross-platform communication flows. By advancing computational approaches to studying media ecosystems, this work will contribute to communication theory on digital publics while addressing urgent societal concerns about information integrity. The scalability of methods developed through this project will support future interdisciplinary collaborations at the intersection of communication studies, data science, and computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, and that spans the study of mass communication/media studies, old and new media technologies, social and political applications, and speech communication and rhetoric. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; media social science and criticism; and quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing decentralized cyber-physical production systems (CPPS) in the context of distributed additive manufacturing networks. Emerging applications in on-demand, geographically dispersed manufacturing—such as disaster-response part fabrication or customized medical device production—require dynamic coordination of heterogeneous resources (3D printers, material stocks, logistics) across fluctuating demand and supply chains. Traditional centralized optimization methods struggle with real-time adaptability, scalability, and resilience to localized disruptions, creating a critical gap in applied engineering solutions. The research will combine agent-based modeling, distributed constraint optimization, and federated machine learning to create a hierarchical decision-making architecture. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale CPPS networks (10,000+ nodes) with multi-physics interactions, including thermal-structural deformation during printing, material flow bottlenecks, and energy consumption trade-offs. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will evaluate robustness under stochastic demand shocks, while graph neural networks trained on HPC clusters will predict optimal resource reallocation strategies. Key innovations include a digital twin interoperability layer for mixed-fidelity simulations and privacy-preserving data sharing protocols between distributed nodes. Outcomes will yield open-source tools for resilient production system design, validated against real-world case studies in distributed aerospace tooling and rural healthcare supply chains. The work advances applied engineering by bridging gaps between discrete-event simulation, real-time control systems, and sustainable lifecycle management, with direct implications for Industry 4.0 scalability. Successful implementation could reduce production downtime by 15-30% in decentralized networks and provide a template for adaptive resource allocation in other critical infrastructure domains.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles inherent to engineering to the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of the coupled physical and chemical processes governing fluid-rock interactions in active fault zones, with implications for seismic hazard assessment and subsurface resource management. A critical challenge in geoscience is predicting how fluid migration modulates stress accumulation and release along faults, as existing models struggle to integrate multi-scale datasets spanning mineralogical, geomechanical, and hydrological processes. We propose to develop high-resolution 3D numerical simulations coupling reactive transport with poroelastic stress evolution to quantify how fluid chemistry, fracture network geometry, and heterogeneous rock properties influence fault stability. The computational approach leverages finite element methods with adaptive meshing to resolve meter-scale fault core structures within kilometer-scale domains, incorporating experimentally derived reaction rates for fault gouge minerals. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the nonlinear solver requirements, parallelized workflows for stochastic fracture network generation, and petabyte-scale output from time-dependent multiphysics simulations. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework to assess how CO2-rich fluids or engineered injections alter fault friction parameters, with applications to earthquake forecasting and geothermal energy optimization. By bridging pore-scale geochemical processes with field-scale geomechanical behavior, this work will provide novel constraints on the role of fluids in triggering both natural and induced seismicity. The resulting open-source codebase will enable community-driven enhancements to fault dynamics models, directly supporting risk mitigation strategies for subsurface development projects. Successful implementation requires dedicated GPU nodes for matrix solvers, large-memory nodes for ensemble simulations, and high-throughput storage for global sensitivity analyses across tectonic settings.
cip_title: Geological and Earth Sciences/ Geosciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in geological and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the performance and sustainability of medium/heavy commercial vehicles through advanced computational modeling of hybrid and electric powertrain systems. As the transportation industry transitions toward electrification, thermal management of high-capacity battery systems in commercial trucks remains a significant barrier to efficiency, safety, and operational longevity. Current experimental approaches to battery thermal analysis are resource-intensive and limited in capturing dynamic real-world operating conditions. To overcome this, we propose developing high-fidelity multiphysics models using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate heat generation, dissipation, and thermal stress in battery packs under varied load cycles, ambient temperatures, and charging scenarios. These models will integrate electrochemical-thermal coupling to predict cell-level behavior and system-wide interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the complex, transient phenomena at appropriate spatial and temporal scales while accounting for heterogeneous materials and irregular geometries inherent to commercial vehicle battery enclosures. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter optimization and identify failure-prone operating regimes. The computational outcomes will be validated against experimental data from partnered industry collaborators. Successful completion of this work will provide actionable insights for designing next-generation thermal management systems, reducing energy waste, mitigating thermal runaway risks, and extending battery service life in heavy-duty applications. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping, this project aims to lower development costs for manufacturers and accelerate the adoption of sustainable freight technologies, directly supporting emissions reduction targets in the transportation sector.
cip_title: Medium/ Heavy Vehicle and Truck Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the specialized maintenance and repair of trucks, buses, and other commercial and industrial vehicles. Includes instruction in diesel engine mechanics, suspension and steering, brake systems, electrical and electronic systems, preventive maintenance inspections, drive trains, gasoline engine mechanics, HVAC systems, and auxiliary equipment installation and repair.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in the United States, with a focus on the interplay between immigrant communities and dominant national discourses from the 19th century to the present. Traditional methods in American Studies struggle to systematically process the vast, heterogeneous textual and visual archives—including newspapers, literary works, oral histories, and public media—that reflect these dynamics. By applying computational text analysis, image recognition, and network modeling at scale, this research aims to identify patterns in how marginalized groups negotiated cultural belonging and how these negotiations influenced broader conceptions of “American” identity. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, such as transformer-based models for semantic shift detection and multilingual sentiment analysis, with geospatial mapping to track regional variations in discourse. HPC resources are critical for training custom machine learning models on terabytes of digitized primary sources, enabling efficient processing of non-Latin script materials (e.g., Yiddish, Chinese) and image datasets that have been underrepresented in prior studies. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for interdisciplinary cultural analysis, new insights into the role of diasporic press in shaping regional identities, and an open-access repository of annotated datasets. This work will advance methodological innovation in digital humanities while addressing gaps in public understanding of how pluralistic narratives have historically contested and redefined U.S. cultural boundaries. The project’s computational demands—particularly parallelized processing of high-resolution historical images and GPU-accelerated NLP workflows—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve timely, replicable results.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the United States and its Pre-Columbian and colonial predecessors, and including the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an automated framework for detecting accounting anomalies in large-scale financial datasets by integrating machine learning (ML) with domain-specific accounting principles. The increasing volume and complexity of financial data, coupled with evolving regulatory requirements, pose significant challenges for traditional audit and compliance methods. Current approaches often lack scalability, struggle with real-time analysis, and fail to effectively integrate unstructured data sources (e.g., transaction notes, emails) with structured ledger entries. To address these limitations, we propose a computational pipeline leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model transactional relationships and contextual metadata. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and optimize models on multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10+ years of anonymized corporate financial records, including text, temporal sequences, and entity networks. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams, dynamic graph construction for evolving transaction networks, and hyperparameter optimization for imbalanced classification tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable anomaly detection system capable of flagging fraudulent patterns with higher precision than rule-based or shallow ML methods, (2) quantifiable metrics comparing model performance across accounting subdomains (e.g., receivables vs. tax compliance), and (3) open-source tools for temporal graph representation learning tailored to financial data. By bridging accounting semantics with advanced computational techniques, this work aims to establish reproducible benchmarks for AI-driven financial oversight while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of audit science and scalable machine learning. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive graph computations and enabling rapid iteration across model architectures, directly supporting the program’s mission to innovate at the convergence of accounting practice and computational systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines accounting with computer science and/or computer studies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model and predict the spread of wildfires in complex urban-wildland interfaces, a critical challenge for homeland security and emergency response. Wildfires increasingly threaten communities, infrastructure, and ecosystems, yet existing predictive models lack the spatial granularity and integration of real-time environmental variables needed to support dynamic evacuation planning and resource deployment. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement coupled atmosphere-fire behavior simulations at unprecedented scales. The computational approach integrates the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model with a physics-based fire-spread algorithm, enhanced by machine learning techniques to assimilate real-time data from satellite imagery, IoT sensors, and historical fire databases. This hybrid model will resolve fire dynamics at 10-meter spatial resolution, capturing interactions between terrain, vegetation, microclimate, and built environments. HPC resources are essential to manage the extreme computational demands of ensemble simulations, which will quantify uncertainties in fire progression under varying weather scenarios and mitigation strategies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible predictive tool for emergency managers, validated against case studies from recent megafires in fire-prone regions. The project will also generate risk assessment datasets to inform land-use policies and preemptive resource allocation. By advancing the fidelity and speed of wildfire simulations, this work aims to reduce loss of life, property damage, and economic disruption, directly supporting homeland security priorities in disaster resilience and community preparedness. The scalability of the framework will enable future adaptation to other cascading hazards, such as post-fire flooding or industrial accidents in critical infrastructure zones.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The rapid evolution of telecommunications infrastructure, driven by emerging technologies such as 5G, edge computing, and IoT, has introduced unprecedented complexity in network resource allocation. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing dynamic resource distribution in multi-stakeholder telecom ecosystems, where conflicting priorities—such as latency minimization, energy efficiency, and regulatory compliance—create computationally intractable trade-offs. Traditional operations research methods struggle to scale with the real-time demands of modern networks, particularly when incorporating heterogeneous data streams and security constraints inherent to distributed systems. This research proposes a novel computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, graph neural networks, and multi-objective reinforcement learning to simulate and optimize resource allocation strategies under uncertainty. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep learning models on synthetic network topologies reflecting diverse urban and rural deployment scenarios, while parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will evaluate policy outcomes across regulatory, technical, and business continuity dimensions. The computational workflow will process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing network traffic patterns, cybersecurity threat landscapes, and energy consumption profiles. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of generating Pareto-optimal allocation strategies that balance profit maximization for telecom providers with public service obligations mandated by spectrum licensing agreements. This interdisciplinary approach bridges telecommunications engineering, computational economics, and regulatory policy analysis, offering a quantitative foundation for managing next-generation networks. The project’s computational artifacts—including open-source simulation modules and pre-trained models—will enable telecom operators and policymakers to test infrastructure investment strategies under evolving technological and market conditions, ultimately supporting more resilient and equitable connectivity frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business skills to design, implement, and manage the voice, video, and data networking systems of organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications concepts and technologies, network operations and management, wireless communications and mobile computing, cybersecurity, regulation and public policy, business practices and management, and written and oral communications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the performance, durability, and environmental compliance of medium/heavy-duty commercial vehicles, with a focus on diesel engine systems and hybrid-electric drivetrain integration. The research addresses a critical industry challenge: balancing engine efficiency and torque requirements with stringent emissions regulations and lifecycle costs. Current diagnostic and optimization methods rely heavily on physical prototyping and static datasets, which are time-intensive, costly, and insufficient for capturing the dynamic interactions between engine components, aftertreatment systems, and emerging hybrid technologies. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining 3D combustion simulation, machine learning-driven predictive maintenance models, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. Large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model in-cylinder combustion processes and exhaust gas recirculation dynamics at microsecond resolution, while reinforcement learning techniques will train predictive models for component wear and failure modes using heterogeneous datasets from onboard sensors and maintenance logs. These workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization cycles that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The requested HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across engine calibration profiles, hybrid battery thermal management strategies, and aftertreatment regeneration schedules to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for heavy-duty powertrains, predictive maintenance algorithms with 15-20% improved accuracy over current industry standards, and optimized hybrid configurations demonstrating 8-12% fuel savings in simulated duty cycles. This work will directly support curriculum modernization in vehicle diagnostics and emission control strategies while providing students with hands-on experience in HPC applications for transportation technology.
cip_title: Medium/ Heavy Vehicle and Truck Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the specialized maintenance and repair of trucks, buses, and other commercial and industrial vehicles. Includes instruction in diesel engine mechanics, suspension and steering, brake systems, electrical and electronic systems, preventive maintenance inspections, drive trains, gasoline engine mechanics, HVAC systems, and auxiliary equipment installation and repair.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance clinical decision-making and operational efficiency in medical assistant workflows through the development of predictive computational models for patient triage and resource optimization. Medical assistants play a critical role in managing patient intake, preliminary diagnostics, and administrative coordination in high-volume clinical environments. However, manual triage processes and static resource allocation strategies often lead to bottlenecks, delayed care, and uneven staff workloads. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets, including historical patient demographics, symptom profiles, diagnostic results, and clinic operational logs. Machine learning models—such as gradient-boosted decision trees and neural networks—will be trained to predict patient acuity levels, anticipated procedure durations, and resource requirements (e.g., equipment, staffing). Concurrently, discrete-event simulations will model clinic workflows under varying patient volumes to identify optimal scheduling and resource distribution strategies. The computational demands of processing multi-terabyte EHR datasets, coupled with the need for real-time inference in simulated environments, necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized training, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale scenario testing. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for clinic administrators to dynamically adjust staffing and resource allocation based on predictive insights, reducing patient wait times by an estimated 20–30% in pilot testing. Additionally, the project will generate novel benchmarks for clinical workflow efficiency, contributing to the broader integration of computational tools in medical assistant education and practice. By aligning HPC-driven analytics with frontline clinical operations, this work aims to improve patient care quality while reducing systemic inefficiencies in outpatient healthcare delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical office administrative services and perform clinical duties including patient intake and care, routine diagnostic and recording procedures, pre-examination and examination assistance, and the administration of medications and first aid. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology; medical terminology; medical law and ethics; patient psychology and communications; medical office procedures; and clinical diagnostic, examination, testing, and treatment procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to integrate advanced computational modeling and simulation techniques into the creation and analysis of sculptural forms, addressing the challenge of scaling material experimentation and structural optimization in three-dimensional art. Traditional sculptural processes rely on iterative physical prototyping, which is resource-intensive and limits exploration of complex geometries or unconventional material behaviors. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this work aims to develop a predictive framework for simulating material interactions, stress distributions, and dynamic form-generation processes. Key computational methods include finite element analysis (FEA) for evaluating structural integrity in large-scale installations, agent-based modeling to simulate emergent textures in mixed-media assemblages, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to explore form-language variations across cultural and historical datasets. These simulations will be validated against physical prototypes created using clay, metal, and biodegradable composites, with sensor data from deformation and environmental stress tests informing model refinement. The project also proposes developing an open-source toolset to bridge sculptural design workflows with HPC-driven analysis, enabling artists to previsualize material outcomes under diverse conditions. Expected outcomes include novel methods for sustainable material reuse informed by computational lifecycle analysis, optimized fabrication workflows for public art installations, and a cross-disciplinary framework for evaluating aesthetic resonance through data-driven spatial metrics. By merging computational rigor with artistic intuition, this work aims to expand the conceptual and technical boundaries of sculpture while fostering dialogue between visual arts and computational science. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling high-resolution 3D meshes, real-time physics simulations, and machine learning training tasks that exceed the capacity of local workstations, ensuring scalability and reproducibility in computational art research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by creating three-dimensional art works. Includes instruction in the analysis of form in space; round and relief concepts; sculptural composition; modern and experimental methods; different media such as clay, plaster, wood, stone, and metal; techniques such as carving, molding, welding, casting, and modeling; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time control and coordination of heterogeneous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments. A critical challenge in mechatronics and automation lies in managing complex interactions between perception, decision-making, and actuation components across multiple robotic agents with varying capabilities, particularly when executing collaborative tasks under latency constraints. Traditional control architectures often struggle to balance computational efficiency with the precision required for robust operation in uncertain conditions. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach combining physics-based digital twins, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and distributed model predictive control. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train neural networks on large-scale sensorimotor datasets, simulate multi-body dynamics with high-fidelity contact modeling, and solve constrained optimization problems across temporal and spatial scales. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized finite element analysis for simulating soft robotic actuators, GPU-accelerated deep learning for adaptive perception modules, and distributed computing paradigms for scalable task allocation algorithms. Expected outcomes include novel control strategies that enable resilient coordination of robot teams in applications ranging from precision agriculture to infrastructure inspection, validated through both virtual and physical prototypes. The resulting open-source framework will provide the research community with tools to explore complex robotic behaviors beyond current computational limitations, while advancing methodologies for co-designing robotic hardware and control systems through large-scale parameter space exploration. This work directly addresses national priorities in advanced manufacturing and resilient infrastructure by developing computationally tractable solutions for deployable automation systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer controlled electro-mechanical systems and products with embedded electronics, sensors, and actuators; and which includes, but is not limited to, automata, robots and automation systems. Includes instruction in mechanical engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, computer and software engineering, and control engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Arabic linguistic variation and historical language change. While Arabic boasts a rich literary tradition and dynamic dialectal diversity, large-scale comparative studies of its linguistic evolution—spanning Classical Arabic, Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), and regional dialects—remain limited due to the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous textual and spoken corpora. Current methodologies struggle to efficiently analyze morphological, syntactic, and semantic shifts across time, geography, and sociocultural contexts, particularly when handling the non-standardized orthography and phonological variation inherent to dialectal forms. This project proposes a multi-phase computational approach to model these variations. First, we will compile and preprocess a corpus of digitized classical texts, MSA publications, and transcribed dialectal speech from diverse regions (e.g., Levantine, Gulf, Maghrebi). Using NLP tools optimized for Semitic languages, we will perform automated morphological parsing, syntactic annotation, and semantic role labeling across these datasets. Parallel GPU-accelerated workflows will train transformer-based language models to detect diachronic and synchronic patterns, supported by phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct historical relationships between dialects. Second, we will integrate sociolinguistic metadata to simulate language contact scenarios and quantify the impact of geopolitical and cultural factors on lexical borrowing and grammatical convergence. The scale of data (estimated at 50 TB of text and audio) and the iterative nature of model training necessitate HPC resources for distributed storage, parallel processing, and high-memory computation. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible repository of annotated Arabic corpora with cross-dialectal and diachronic tags; (2) computational models elucidating pathways of linguistic change between Classical Arabic, MSA, and vernaculars; and (3) open-source tools for dialect identification and historical text dating. These resources will advance scholarly understanding of Arabic’s linguistic ecology while supporting applications in language education, heritage preservation, and NLP systems tailored to under-resourced Arabic varieties.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Arabic language. Includes instruction in philology; Classical Arabic; Modern Standard Arabic; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interplay of cultural identities and transnational networks in the Balkan Peninsula from the late Ottoman period to the early 20th century.
