This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models capable of analyzing multi-source datasets at scale. By employing ensemble learning techniques and neural networks, we aim to identify patterns associated with adverse health outcomes in chronic conditions prevalent among underserved populations, such as diabetes and hypertension. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model the impact of various intervention strategies on community health metrics, accounting for variables like access to care and patient compliance. The computational demands of processing terabytes of structured and unstructured data, coupled with the need for real-time analytics in clinical settings, require the parallel processing capabilities and large memory infrastructure of HPC systems. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms integrated into a decision support tool for PAs, enabling personalized treatment recommendations and proactive management of at-risk populations. This research will contribute to reducing health disparities by equipping PAs with data-driven insights, ultimately improving patient outcomes and optimizing resource allocation in settings where physician supervision is limited. The scalability of the models will also support broader public health initiatives aimed at preventive care and chronic disease management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice medicine, including diagnoses and treatment therapies, under the supervision of a physician. Includes instruction in the basic medical and clinical sciences and specialized preparation in fields such as family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, gynecology, general surgery, psychiatry, and behavioral medicine; the delivery of health care services to homebound patients, rural populations, and underserved populations; and community health services.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of climate-driven hydrological changes and their cascading impacts on terrestrial ecosystem resilience and biogeochemical cycles. As shifting precipitation patterns and intensified drought regimes increasingly stress regional water resources, predicting feedbacks between surface hydrology, vegetation dynamics, and soil carbon-nutrient cycling remains a critical challenge. To address this, we propose developing a high-resolution, process-based model integrating surface-subsurface hydrology, plant-soil interactions, and soil biogeochemistry. The model will leverage parallel computing architectures to simulate coupled water-carbon-nitrogen dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes at unprecedented spatial resolutions (100 m scale) over decadal timescales. Satellite remote sensing data (Sentinel-2, Landsat, GRACE-FO) will be assimilated to constrain soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and vegetation productivity, while machine learning techniques will optimize parameterization of subgrid-scale processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational load of multi-year ensemble simulations across diverse climate scenarios and to process large geospatial datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying regions at risk of hydrological regime shifts, quantifying thresholds for ecosystem transitions (e.g., forest to grassland), and mapping hotspots of soil carbon vulnerability under altered moisture regimes. The results will directly inform water resource management strategies and climate adaptation planning for agricultural and natural landscapes. By elucidating terrestrial system responses to hydroclimatic stressors, this work will contribute foundational knowledge to Earth system models while providing scalable computational frameworks for regional resilience assessments. The requested allocation supports iterative model development, large-scale data assimilation, and scenario analysis critical for addressing interlinked water, ecosystem, and climate challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction of the Earth's oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial systems. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate high-performance computing (HPC) into advanced printmaking research to address the computational challenges of simulating, optimizing, and innovating traditional and hybrid print-based processes. Traditional printmaking techniques, such as lithography, intaglio, and serigraphy, involve complex interactions between materials, tools, and environmental conditions, which constrain the scalability, reproducibility, and creative exploration of multi-layered or large-format works. Current limitations in manually predicting ink behavior, substrate interactions, or the emergent effects of layered prints hinder artistic experimentation and technical precision. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a computational framework leveraging HPC resources to model material dynamics, generate algorithmic design patterns, and simulate print outcomes under variable parameters. High-resolution fluid dynamics simulations will be employed to predict ink absorption and bleeding across diverse paper and fabric substrates, while generative adversarial networks (GANs) will train on historical and contemporary print corpuses to propose novel compositional strategies. Additionally, Monte Carlo methods will optimize press configurations and registration alignment for multi-plate workflows, reducing trial iterations in physical studios. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of high-dimensional data, real-time rendering of intricate textures, and large-scale parameter sweeps—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include a suite of open-source tools for artists to previsualize print interactions digitally, alongside a repository of simulated material datasets to inform sustainable practice. This work aims to expand the technical and expressive boundaries of printmaking, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between computational science and studio art, while preserving traditional craft through adaptive technological integration.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by rendering art concepts onto surfaces and transferring images, via ink or dyes, onto paper or fabric. Includes instruction in monochrome and color printing; tonality; chemistry; equipment set-up and maintenance; techniques such as serigraphy, lithography, intaglio, woodcut, block, stencil, relief, etching, and composite; and personal style development.

abstract: The project seeks to address foundational questions in mathematical logic, specifically in model theory, recursion theory, and set theory, through advanced computational methods. A central challenge in these areas involves the complexity of determining the decidability of axiomatic systems, the structural properties of recursively enumerable sets, and the consistency of large cardinal axioms. Traditional analytical approaches often encounter intractable combinatorial complexity when investigating these problems, necessitating the application of high-performance computing (HPC) techniques. This research proposes to develop and implement scalable algorithms to explore the decidability boundaries of first-order theories, analyze the computational density of Turing degrees in the arithmetic hierarchy, and simulate forcing constructions to assess the consistency strength of extended set-theoretic frameworks. Computational models will be constructed using automated theorem provers and custom-built enumeration software, optimized for parallel processing on HPC clusters. Large-scale simulations will systematically test conjectures regarding the existence of minimal models for certain non-well-founded theories and the stratification of algorithmically random sequences. The expected outcomes include resolving open questions about the finite axiomatizability of selected algebraic structures, characterizing the distribution of computably enumerable sets within hyperarithmetical hierarchies, and providing empirical evidence for the independence of specific combinatorial principles under enhanced cardinal axioms. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to advance the theoretical understanding of logical systems' limits and interrelations, offering new methodological paradigms for pure mathematical research. The results will contribute to the broader logic community by clarifying foundational uncertainties and enabling more precise metamathematical classifications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study foundations of mathematics, including model theory, recursion theory and set theory.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the optimization of supply chain resilience strategies under climate-induced disruptions through computational economic modeling, addressing a critical gap in traditional managerial economics frameworks. While firms increasingly face climate-related risks, existing models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between economic decision-making, resource allocation, and stochastic environmental shocks. The project will develop an agent-based simulation platform to model multi-tier supply networks under varying climate scenarios, integrating firm-level cost-benefit analyses with macroeconomic shock propagation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parallel simulations that incorporate heterogeneous agent behaviors, non-linear price adjustments, and probabilistic disruption events across geographies and industries. The computational framework will leverage econometric calibration using historical supply chain disruption data and climate projection datasets, enabling validation against real-world cases. Expected outcomes include identifying economically viable adaptation strategies—such as dynamic inventory buffering, supplier diversification thresholds, and contingency pricing mechanisms—that balance short-term efficiency with long-term resilience. The project will further produce sensitivity analyses quantifying how regulatory environments and market competition modulate the effectiveness of resilience investments. By bridging environmental uncertainty modeling with microeconomic decision theory, this research aims to advance managerial economics methodologies while providing actionable insights for firms navigating climate volatility. The HPC component directly supports the iterative optimization of agent-based parameters and high-dimensional scenario testing, which are computationally intractable with conventional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics principles to the analysis of the organization and operation of business enterprises. Includes instruction in monetary theory, banking and financial systems, theory of competition, pricing theory, wage and salary/incentive theory, analysis of markets, and applications of econometrics and quantitative methods to the study of particular businesses and business problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of producing high-resolution, data-intensive documentary films by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Contemporary documentary workflows increasingly integrate 4K/8K video, immersive 360° footage, and machine learning-driven tools for tasks such as automated scene analysis, archival material restoration, and real-time collaborative editing. However, these processes strain conventional computing systems, leading to prohibitive render times, inefficient processing of large audiovisual datasets, and limitations in deploying advanced computational methods during post-production. This research proposes a hybrid computational approach combining distributed rendering frameworks, GPU-accelerated neural networks, and cloud-based parallel processing to optimize resource-intensive tasks. Key objectives include developing scalable pipelines for training custom vision models to detect thematic patterns in archival footage, implementing adaptive compression algorithms for heterogeneous media formats, and simulating interactive documentary environments using real-time ray tracing. The project will utilize HPC clusters to benchmark performance gains in processing terabyte-scale datasets, enabling comparative analysis of workflow efficiency across traditional and computationally augmented methodologies. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools tailored for documentary creators, reducing barriers to advanced computational techniques while maintaining artistic intent. By bridging gaps between media production and computational scalability, this work aims to expand creative possibilities for nonfiction storytelling, support preservation of aging audiovisual archives, and establish best practices for integrating HPC resources into arts-driven research. The results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, workshops for documentary practitioners, and integration into visual arts curricula, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational and media disciplines.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce nonfiction film and video. Includes instruction in film and video writing, directing, and production; film studies; history of the documentary; research techniques; videography; editing; and business aspects of film production.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework to optimize dynamic tariff and customs compliance strategies in cross-border supply chains, with a focus on mitigating delays caused by fluctuating trade policies and heterogeneous regulatory environments. Current approaches to customs risk assessment and toll fee forecasting rely on static models that inadequately account for real-time geopolitical shifts, multi-jurisdictional legal conflicts, or emergent smuggling patterns. The proposed computational system will integrate machine learning with discrete-event simulation to model complex interactions between shippers, customs authorities, and transportation networks across 57 major international trade corridors. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel execution of Monte Carlo simulations incorporating 1) natural language processing of real-time regulatory updates from 200+ government sources, 2) agent-based modeling of cargo inspection processes, and 3) neural network predictions of bottleneck formation in multimodal transport hubs. The simulation environment will process terabyte-scale historical clearance datasets alongside synthetic scenarios testing proposed tariff structures and inspection protocols. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool capable of recommending optimal declaration strategies under uncertainty, reducing computational latency in compliance checks by 40-60% compared to current industry benchmarks. This work addresses critical gaps in adaptive revenue management for customs-dependent economies while advancing computational methods for policy-sensitive logistics optimization. Successful implementation could inform both private-sector transportation cost reduction strategies and public-sector modernization initiatives for electronic customs systems.
cip_title: Traffic, Customs, and Transportation Clerk/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform duties associated with managing revenue-based customs, traffic, or transportation services, such as control of domestic and international traffic, toll roads and waterways, and to assist in the dispatch and control of fleet-based traffic for businesses and public services. Includes instruction in record-keeping; preparation of customs and transportation documentation; operation of communications equipment; basic transportation operations management; tariffs, rates and fares; revenue collection and change-making; and interpretation of customs or transportation regulations and related legislation, policies, and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in predictive maintenance and operational optimization of industrial electronic systems. Industrial electronics, critical to manufacturing automation and process control, increasingly relies on complex sensor networks and real-time data analytics. However, existing methods for fault detection and performance modeling often lack the scalability to handle high-dimensional data streams from modern industrial equipment, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and unplanned downtime. To address this gap, the research will develop machine learning (ML) frameworks and multiphysics simulations to model equipment degradation, predict failures, and optimize energy efficiency in industrial electronic systems. Key computational tasks include training deep neural networks on time-series sensor data (e.g., voltage, temperature, vibration) to identify early failure signatures, coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to evaluate thermal and electromagnetic stresses in power electronics components. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of large datasets from distributed manufacturing sites, iterative hyperparameter tuning for ML models, and high-fidelity simulations of electronic circuits under dynamic operational conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms with reduced false-positive rates, digital twin prototypes for industrial motor drives and programmable logic controllers (PLCs), and energy-optimized control strategies for variable-frequency drives. By integrating computational modeling with empirical validation using lab-scale industrial electronics testbeds, this work aims to bridge the gap between data-driven insights and practical implementation in manufacturing environments. The results will directly benefit industries reliant on automated systems by minimizing downtime, extending equipment lifespan, and reducing energy consumption. Additionally, the project will support workforce development by incorporating HPC-driven case studies into the Industrial Electronics Technology curriculum, preparing technicians to engage with advanced analytics tools in Industry 4.0 applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair electrical/electronic equipment used in industry and manufacturing. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of brass instrument performance through high-fidelity computational modeling of aeroacoustic interactions between players and their instruments. Despite the rich history of brass pedagogy and performance, the precise mechanisms by which player biomechanics, airflow dynamics, and instrument acoustics collectively shape timbre, intonation, and projection remain poorly quantified. Current analytical methods often rely on simplified physical models or empirical observations, limiting their capacity to disentangle complex nonlinear interactions. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element modeling (FEM) of structural vibrations, and biomechanical simulations of embouchure dynamics. Large-scale simulations will model airflow through instrument bores under varying lip kinematics, valve configurations, and mouthpiece geometries, capturing turbulence, pressure wave propagation, and resonance modes at sub-millisecond temporal resolution. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze multimodal performance data—including motion-capture recordings of embouchure gestures, sensor-based airflow measurements, and spectral audio features—to identify correlations between physiological control parameters and acoustic outcomes. The computational workload necessitates parallelized GPU-accelerated processing for real-time visualization of multiphysics interactions and parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated predictive models linking specific performance techniques (e.g., double tonguing, pitch bending) to acoustic signatures; (2) a digital twin framework for virtual prototyping of instrument modifications; and (3) data-driven pedagogical tools to visualize embouchure efficiency and airflow management. By bridging computational engineering with performing arts practice, this work aims to establish new paradigms for optimizing brass performance pedagogy, instrument design, and interpretive creativity while preserving the idiomatic nuances central to artistic expression.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a brass instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the systemic impacts of policy interventions on recidivism rates within correctional systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in predictive accuracy and scalability. Current approaches to evaluating criminal justice policies often rely on static statistical models or localized case studies, which struggle to account for dynamic interdependencies between socioeconomic factors, institutional practices, and individual behavioral outcomes. The proposed work integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning to simulate heterogeneous populations of justice-involved individuals, correctional staff, and community resources across multi-year timelines. By parameterizing agents using anonymized administrative data—including criminal histories, program participation, and post-release outcomes—the framework will test hypotheses about how policy changes (e.g., rehabilitative program funding, parole supervision protocols) propagate through complex, adaptive systems. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to represent state-level populations (∼100,000 agents) and enabling Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty across diverse demographic and geographic scenarios. Additionally, graph neural networks will be trained on simulation outputs to identify latent risk factors and optimal intervention points. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for policymakers to assess the long-term fiscal and social impacts of proposed reforms before implementation. This work bridges computational social science and criminal justice research, offering a novel methodology to address entrenched challenges in reducing recidivism while ensuring equitable resource allocation. The project’s computational demands—particularly parallelized simulation workflows and large-scale parameter optimization—require dedicated HPC infrastructure to achieve timely results, with potential applications in evidence-based policy design and correctional system cost-benefit analysis.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general study of criminal justice and corrections. Includes instruction in criminology, criminal justice, correctional science, forensic science, law enforcement, psychology, and ethics.

abstract: Nursing science faces critical challenges in integrating complex, high-dimensional datasets—including electronic health records, biometric sensor data, and patient-reported outcomes—to inform precision care strategies. While advancements in clinical data acquisition present opportunities to refine nursing interventions, existing analytical tools lack the capacity to model dynamic, multi-scale interactions between patient physiology, care protocols, and environmental factors. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that optimize clinical decision-making in acute and chronic care settings. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating predictive machine learning frameworks to identify early signatures of patient deterioration in critical care nursing contexts, and (2) simulating the impact of nurse staffing patterns and workflow adjustments on care quality metrics through agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will integrate real-time vital sign streams, longitudinal medication administration records, and nurse-patient interaction logs from three tertiary care hospitals. Deep learning architectures will be trained on GPU clusters to detect nonlinear patterns in physiological time series predictive of sepsis or delirium onset, while parallelized discrete-event simulations will model care delivery systems under varying resource constraints. The anticipated outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for proactive nursing interventions, evidence-based staffing recommendations to reduce adverse events, and open-source tools for scalable analysis of clinical workflow efficiency. By leveraging HPC capabilities to analyze nursing-sensitive outcomes at unprecedented resolution, this work will advance methodological frameworks for data-driven nursing science while directly addressing operational challenges in modern healthcare systems. The requested resources will enable processing of petabyte-scale clinical datasets and iterative model optimization that exceeds the capabilities of local computing infrastructure, ultimately supporting translational advances in evidence-based nursing practice.
cip_definition: A research program that focuses on the study of advanced clinical practices, research methodologies, the administration of complex nursing services, and that prepares nurses to further the progress of nursing research through experimentation and clinical applications.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the evidence-based understanding of somatic bodywork therapies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model biomechanical and neurophysiological interactions during therapeutic interventions. Somatic bodywork modalities, such as myofascial release and neuromuscular re-education, are widely practiced, yet the mechanisms underlying their therapeutic efficacy remain poorly quantified. A key challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets—including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and autonomic nervous system biomarkers—to map how manual techniques influence tissue dynamics, proprioceptive feedback, and systemic stress responses. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining musculoskeletal modeling, finite element analysis, and machine learning. Patient-specific biomechanical models will simulate soft tissue deformation and force transmission during therapy sessions, validated against experimental kinematic and pressure data. Concurrently, neural network architectures will analyze time-series physiological data (e.g., heart rate variability, galvanic skin response) to identify patterns correlating manual interventions with parasympathetic activation. HPC resources are critical for managing the high dimensionality of these datasets, enabling parallelized simulations of diverse anatomical regions, and training predictive models on multi-modal clinical data. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative biomarkers linking specific manual techniques to measurable physiological outcomes, (2) optimized force-delivery parameters for individualized treatment protocols, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing therapist-client biomechanical interactions. By bridging gaps between empirical practice and computational validation, this work aims to establish a foundational platform for standardizing somatic therapies, informing educational curricula, and guiding regulatory frameworks. The requested computing infrastructure will directly support 5–10 concurrent users across three institutions, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between somatic practitioners, biomechanists, and data scientists.
cip_title: Somatic Bodywork and Related Therapeutic Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in somatic bodywork and related therapeutic services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing administrative workflow efficiency in dynamic office environments, with a focus on mitigating bottlenecks in document management, communication scheduling, and task prioritization. Administrative professionals in secretarial and assistant roles increasingly face complex, data-dense workflows due to the proliferation of digital communication tools and hybrid work models. Traditional time-management strategies often fail to account for real-time variables such as shifting priorities, multi-channel requests, and document versioning conflicts. This project addresses the computational challenge of modeling these variables to generate adaptive workflow recommendations. Using anonymized datasets of email threads, calendar interactions, and document-editing histories from corporate environments, we will train transformer-based models to predict task-critical paths and simulate resource allocation scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of temporal graphs representing workflow dependencies, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively refine scheduling policies. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of dynamically reprioritizing tasks based on real-time input streams, reducing latency in document processing cycles, and automating conflict resolution in multi-stakeholder requests. This work bridges computational scalability gaps in office management research, offering a quantitative framework to enhance decision-making in administrative roles. By integrating NLP for request parsing and graph neural networks for workflow modeling, the project advances interdisciplinary intersections between business communication theory and computational logistics. Results will provide actionable insights for developing next-generation office management tools, with potential applications in training AI-augmented administrative systems and redefining productivity metrics for hybrid work environments.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for modeling emergent communication patterns in decentralized multi-agent systems, with applications to resilient infrastructure design and bio-inspired robotics. The core problem lies in understanding how adaptive, context-aware communication protocols can self-organize in resource-constrained environments where traditional network architectures fail—a challenge observed in both distributed sensor networks responding to natural disasters and collective robotic systems operating in unstructured terrains. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement a hybrid approach combining neuromorphic computing paradigms with evolutionary optimization to simulate populations of >10^5 heterogeneous agents. The computational model integrates spiking neural networks for real-time signal processing, multi-objective genetic algorithms for protocol optimization, and graph-based topological analysis to quantify system resilience. Key innovations include the development of energy-efficient communication primitives using event-driven computation and the creation of a novel metric space for evaluating protocol adaptability under dynamic constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible benchmark dataset of emergent communication scenarios, (2) quantitative guidelines for designing self-stabilizing network architectures in critical infrastructure applications, and (3) open-source tools for simulating bio-inspired communication strategies at unprecedented scale. By bridging gaps between distributed computing, complex systems theory, and adaptive control, this work aims to establish foundational principles for next-generation autonomous systems while advancing computational methodologies for studying emergence in artificial ecosystems. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration across biologically plausible timescales, requiring sustained petascale capabilities for evolutionary optimization cycles and terabyte-scale memory bandwidth for neural population simulations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to optimize the design of sustainable, high-performance synthetic fibers with tailored mechanical and thermal properties. A central challenge in textile engineering lies in predicting how molecular-scale interactions and processing parameters (e.g., extrusion rates, temperature gradients, polymer chain alignment) collectively influence fiber performance metrics such as tensile strength, elasticity, and degradation resistance. Traditional trial-and-error experimental approaches are resource-intensive and fail to capture the nonlinear interdependencies between synthesis variables and macroscopic behavior. To address this, we propose integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model fiber production across atomic, mesoscopic, and continuum scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale MD simulations of polymer melt dynamics during spinning, coupled with FEA modeling of stress distribution in fiber networks under cyclic loading. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify correlations between simulated structural features (e.g., crystallinity, cross-link density) and experimental data on fiber durability. The resulting predictive models will guide the synthesis of novel bio-based polyamide fibers with reduced environmental footprint, targeting applications in recyclable technical textiles and heat-resistant protective gear. By elucidating process-structure-property relationships, this work aims to accelerate the development of fibers that balance performance demands with circular economy principles. The computational pipeline will be openly shared to support broader innovation in textile engineering, reducing reliance on petrochemical feedstocks and energy-intensive prototyping. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities to manage terabytes of simulation data, parallelize iterative optimization tasks, and train deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets spanning nanosecond-scale molecular events to bulk material responses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to test and manufacture fibers and fiber products, both synthetic and natural; to develop new and improved fibers, textiles and their uses; and to the analysis of related engineering problems such as structural factors, molecular synthesis, chemical manufacturing, weaves, strength and stress, useful life, dyes, and applications to composite systems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern munitions systems, characterized by advanced materials, integrated guidance technologies, and multi-physics operational environments, demands high-fidelity computational modeling to address critical challenges in safety, reliability, and lifecycle management. This project seeks to develop a predictive framework for evaluating degradation mechanisms in high-explosive ordnance storage systems under variable environmental and operational stresses. Traditional empirical methods lack the resolution to capture nonlinear interactions between hygrothermal aging, microstructural corrosion, and energetic material stability, particularly in hybrid munitions incorporating both conventional and additive-manufactured components. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) for material decomposition pathways, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress propagation in composite casings, and machine learning (ML) models trained on historical failure datasets. The computational workflow will couple these layers through adaptive meshing and surrogate modeling techniques to enable probabilistic risk assessments across decade-long storage timelines. Key innovations include the development of a custom solver for reactive transport phenomena in confined munitions environments and the incorporation of real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled storage facilities via digital twin integration. Anticipated outcomes include predictive metrics for critical failure thresholds, optimized storage protocols for mixed-origin ordnance stockpiles, and a decision-support tool for maintenance prioritization. This research directly addresses gaps in next-generation ordnance stewardship, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to preemptive lifecycle management while maintaining alignment with evolving safety regulations. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the petascale datasets generated by coupled multi-physics simulations and enabling the parametric studies required to account for global climate variability's impact on munitions depot resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of ground or sea-based weapons systems, ordinance and munitions. Includes instruction in basic sciences, electronics, systems technology, fluid power, computer science, conventional weapons systems, nuclear weapons systems, munitions systems, storage and safety, equipment operation, guidance and control systems, hazardous materials, corrosion control, nondestructive testing and quality control, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project proposes to investigate the heterogeneous impacts of non-tariff barriers (NTBs) on bilateral trade flows and global welfare using a high-dimensional structural gravity model augmented with firm-level dynamics. Despite their growing prominence in international trade policy, NTBs—such as technical standards and sanitary regulations—remain poorly quantified due to data granularity challenges and computational limitations in modeling their sector-specific effects across diverse economic contexts. We aim to develop a novel computational framework integrating disaggregated UN Comtrade data, WTO regulatory records, and firm heterogeneity parameters to estimate NTB ad valorem equivalents (AVEs) at the 6-digit HS code level. The analysis will employ a Bayesian hierarchical model with random coefficients to account for unobserved heterogeneity across 150 countries and 5,000 product categories. Given the model’s scale—featuring over 10 million parameters and sparse matrix operations—high-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for parallelized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling via Stan, reducing estimation time from months to days. The computational workflow will optimize memory allocation for sparse tensor contractions and implement domain decomposition strategies across GPU clusters. Anticipated outcomes include the first globally comprehensive NTB elasticity database, enabling counterfactual analysis of multilateral regulatory harmonization scenarios. Results will inform trade negotiation priorities by identifying sectors where NTB reductions could yield disproportionate welfare gains. This work advances methodological capabilities in trade policy simulation while addressing critical gaps in evidence-based international economic governance. The resource request supports 12 months of large-scale computations on GPU-enabled nodes, with open-source release of optimized code to facilitate reproducibility in structural trade modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study and analysis of international commercial behavior and trade policy. Includes instruction in international trade theory, tariffs and quotas, commercial policy, trade factor flows, international finance and investment, currency regulation and trade exchange rates and markets, international trade negotiation, and international payments and accounting policy.

abstract: Traumatic injuries and critical illness present complex, dynamic pathophysiological states that challenge conventional analytical approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive multiscale models integrating heterogeneous clinical, multi-omics, and physiological time-series data from trauma patients. The primary research problem centers on the inability of current risk stratification tools to account for nonlinear interactions between host response, organ dysfunction, and therapeutic interventions in critical care settings. We propose a computational framework combining ensemble machine learning with mechanistic dynamical systems modeling to address this gap. Clinical data from electronic health records (EHRs), including high-frequency vital sign streams, laboratory trends, and imaging biomarkers, will be fused with longitudinal genomic and proteomic profiles using graph-based data integration techniques. Parallelized Bayesian optimization will train predictive models for sepsis progression, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multi-organ failure on GPU-accelerated nodes. Mechanistic models of inflammatory cascades and oxygen transport dynamics will be implemented using differential equation solvers, with parameter estimation performed via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods at scale. The HPC environment is essential for processing >10 TB of multimodal patient data, enabling real-time simulation of competing physiological trajectories across hypothesized intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early deterioration detection, personalized dynamic treatment regime optimization, and mechanistic insights into trauma-induced immunomodulation. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs for targeted immunotherapies and resuscitation protocols while establishing a scalable computational infrastructure for precision critical care research. By elucidating critical transition states in trauma pathophysiology through large-scale data synthesis, the project aims to reduce preventable deaths in the golden hour of trauma care and improve long-term outcomes for survivors of critical illness.
cip_definition: Research focused on Trauma and Critical Care

abstract: The study of anatomical structures in veterinary medicine is increasingly reliant on high-resolution imaging and multi-scale modeling to understand disease mechanisms and therapeutic interventions. However, existing computational resources are insufficient to process large-scale datasets, such as 3D electron microscopy volumes of neural tissues or dynamic simulations of molecular interactions in pathological conditions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the structural and functional interplay in animal tissues, with a focus on neurodegenerative diseases in domestic species. Using GPU-accelerated deep learning, we will automate segmentation of synaptic ultrastructure and axonal pathways from terabyte-scale imaging datasets. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model conformational changes in proteins implicated in equine neuroaxonal dystrophy, a disorder with poorly understood etiology. These simulations will integrate cryo-EM data and electrophysiological parameters to predict how structural variants alter ion channel function. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of multi-modal data, including histology, proteomics, and biomechanical strain patterns in musculoskeletal tissues. Expected outcomes include identifying novel biomarkers for early disease diagnosis, mapping neural circuit vulnerabilities to metabolic stress, and validating computational predictions through experimental collaborations. By bridging cellular anatomy to systemic pathophysiology, this work will establish scalable computational frameworks for veterinary neuroanatomy research, with translational applications in targeted drug design and rehabilitative therapies. The requested resources will directly support the development of open-access tools for the veterinary community, enhancing diagnostic precision and treatment strategies for neurological and musculoskeletal disorders in both companion and livestock animals.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of small and large animal cellular, organ, tissue, and body systems and their relation to physiologic function, disease, and therapeutic treatment. Includes instruction in histology, ultrastructure, molecular biology, biochemistry, developmental biology, neuroscience, electrophysiology, electron microscopy, computer imaging, and applications to specific species.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the quantitative analysis of large-scale historical datasets related to military decision-making, logistics, and societal impacts during conflicts from the 18th to 20th centuries. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in operational effectiveness and resource allocation across diverse geopolitical contexts, particularly in understudied theaters of war. Traditional historiography often relies on qualitative case studies, limiting systematic comparisons of how variables such as terrain, supply chain resilience, and command hierarchies influenced outcomes. To address this, the project will integrate digitized archival records—including troop deployments, supply inventories, and communication networks—with geospatial data and climate reconstructions. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling to simulate battlefield dynamics, network analysis to map hierarchical decision-making structures, and machine learning techniques to detect shifts in strategic priorities across multi-theater campaigns. A key innovation involves applying natural language processing to officer correspondence and after-action reports, enabling the quantification of leadership behavior and its correlation with operational outcomes. By parallelizing these analyses across HPC nodes, the project aims to process over 10 million pages of text and 500,000 georeferenced events within a feasible timeframe. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking military operational data with socio-economic indicators, predictive models of logistical bottlenecks in historical conflicts, and visualizations of decision cascades in multi-front wars. These results will provide new frameworks for understanding the interplay between institutional constraints and adaptive strategies in military history, while demonstrating how computational humanities methods can enrich traditional historiographical approaches. The resource allocation will directly support scalability testing of spatial-temporal analytics pipelines and validation of models against established historical scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the history of warfare and military institutions in their operational, politico-economic and socio-cultural contexts; including airpower history, naval history, and military history. Includes instruction in military organization, military operations, the history of technology, leadership and biography, military psychology and behavior, international relations and politics, economics, aspects of general and regional history, cultural history and anthropology, historiography, and applicable quantitative methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in workforce education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize adaptive training systems for diverse learner populations. Workforce education programs must balance rapidly evolving industry demands with heterogeneous learner needs, yet existing instructional design frameworks lack the computational power to simulate large-scale, dynamic interactions between training variables (e.g., skill gaps, learning modalities, and real-time labor market shifts). The research problem centers on developing predictive models to personalize competency-based training while maintaining scalability for institutions serving thousands of learners annually. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning, we will simulate learner trajectories across virtual training environments parameterized by industry-specific skill requirements, demographic factors, and cognitive load thresholds. These simulations will integrate real-time labor market data from API feeds and historical program completion records to test hypotheses about optimal resource allocation for hybrid (online/in-person) training ecosystems. The HPC infrastructure is essential for running parallelized Monte Carlo experiments to evaluate 10,000+ permutations of instructional strategies under varying economic scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated framework for dynamically aligning workforce curricula with regional employer needs, (2) predictive metrics to identify at-risk learners before skill deficiencies escalate, and (3) open-source tools for simulating the fiscal and pedagogical impacts of emerging technologies (e.g., AR/VR trainers) in workforce development contexts. By enabling computationally intensive analysis of multivariate educational datasets, this work will provide actionable insights for designing equitable, future-ready training programs that reduce time-to-competency in high-demand fields such as advanced manufacturing and healthcare.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills in various settings, and to various age groups.

abstract: This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving dynamics of Women’s Ministry programs in diverse cultural and denominational contexts, with a focus on mapping spiritual leadership patterns, community-building practices, and gendered theological frameworks. The research problem centers on the lack of large-scale, data-driven studies examining how non-ordained women navigate spiritual authority, foster collective resilience, and adapt ministry strategies amid shifting socioreligious landscapes. While qualitative case studies dominate existing scholarship, computational methods remain underutilized in decoding complex interactions between theological training, lived experience, and program efficacy. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will process unstructured textual data (oral histories, ministry training manuals, sermon transcripts) and structured survey responses from 15,000+ participants across 200 global congregations. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will identify latent themes in spiritual mentorship practices, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will model relational networks within ministry cohorts. Agent-based simulations will test how variations in curriculum design and leadership structures impact long-term community outcomes. Key computational challenges include managing multilingual sacred text corpora, preserving contextual nuance in theological discourse analysis, and scaling dynamic network models to simulate decade-long ministry lifespans. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of Women’s Ministry archetypes, predictive tools for optimizing lay counseling training modules, and an open-access repository of annotated ministry interaction datasets. By bridging computational social science and practical theology, this work aims to empower faith communities with evidence-based strategies for cultivating inclusive spiritual leadership while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for studying emergent religious practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on niche theological lexicons and executing large-scale cultural simulations impractical on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained women to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to other women in local churches, parachurch organizations, and other settings. Includes instruction in foundations of women's ministry, women's ministry in the local church, spiritual formation, women's evangelism and discipleship, bible study and theology, homiletics, lay counseling, women's issues, and leadership training.

abstract: Healthcare facilities face increasing demands to optimize resource allocation and patient care efficiency, particularly in settings reliant on health aides who perform critical supportive roles. This project seeks to address the challenge of dynamically matching health aide staffing and task schedules to real-time patient needs while minimizing operational costs and maximizing care quality. Current methods often rely on static schedules or heuristic adjustments, which can lead to inefficiencies in rapidly changing clinical environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning-driven simulation framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation with reinforcement learning (RL) to model patient flow, health aide workflows, and facility resource constraints. The RL agent will be trained on synthetic datasets reflecting diverse clinical scenarios—including variable patient admission rates, acuity levels, and task priorities—to learn adaptive scheduling policies. HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations across thousands of parallelized training episodes, enabling the exploration of complex state-action spaces that would be computationally intractable on conventional systems. Additionally, we will incorporate real-world data from partner healthcare institutions to validate model generalizability. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for care delivery efficiency (e.g., reduced patient wait times, optimized aide workload distribution) and operational cost savings. The resulting framework will provide decision-support tools to improve health aide training programs by integrating scenario-based simulations, while offering healthcare administrators actionable insights into staffing and resource management. This work bridges a critical gap between computational optimization and frontline healthcare operations, with potential applications in long-term care, outpatient clinics, and resource-constrained settings where health aides play pivotal roles.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and assistance to patients under the direct supervision of other health care professionals, and/or to perform routine maintenance and general assistance in health care facilities and laboratories.

abstract: Higher education institutions face growing demands to evaluate program efficacy and equity using increasingly complex, multi-source datasets. Traditional analytical methods often fail to integrate unstructured data (e.g., student feedback, course evaluations) with structured metrics (e.g., retention rates, learning assessments) at scale, limiting actionable insights. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for evaluating higher education programs by leveraging advanced machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze heterogeneous datasets. The research will address two core questions: (1) How can large-scale, mixed-method data be systematically processed to identify predictors of program effectiveness? (2) What computational strategies enable real-time equity assessments across diverse student populations? High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train transformer-based NLP models on qualitative text data from millions of course evaluations and institutional surveys, while simultaneously running ensemble ML models on structured longitudinal data (e.g., enrollment, graduation, and employment records). GPU-accelerated clusters will be used to optimize hyperparameter tuning for deep learning architectures and enable parallel processing of sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for program evaluators, validated computational workflows for bias detection in evaluation metrics, and predictive models linking curricular interventions to equity outcomes. By scaling analysis beyond conventional statistical approaches, this work aims to advance evidence-based policy design and provide institutions with adaptive frameworks to address systemic inequities in higher education.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for generating information about educational programs in higher education, staff and methods, and the analysis of such information for planning purposes outside of institutional research. Includes instruction in evaluation theory, evaluation research design and planning, administering evaluations and related data collection activities, data reporting requirements, data analysis and interpretation, and related economic and policy issues in higher education.

abstract: Mental health disorders in elderly populations, such as late-life depression, dementia-related neuropsychiatric symptoms, and treatment-resistant geriatric schizophrenia, present complex etiological pathways involving genetic, neurobiological, and environmental interactions. Current diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks often lack precision due to the heterogeneity of aging-related comorbidities and the limited integration of multimodal data. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, neuroimaging, and electronic health record (EHR) datasets. The primary research objective is to identify biomarkers and computational phenotypes that predict disease progression and treatment response in geriatric psychiatric disorders. A multi-omics approach will integrate whole-genome sequencing, epigenetic profiles, and structural/functional MRI data from a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 patients aged 65+. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to detect cross-modal associations between genetic risk variants, neuroanatomical changes, and clinical outcomes. Computational workflows will parallelize image processing via containerized pipelines to analyze terabytes of diffusion tensor imaging data, while federated learning frameworks will enable privacy-preserving analysis of distributed EHRs across collaborating institutions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with age-stratified covariates, and for reducing runtime during hyperparameter optimization of deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models for personalized intervention strategies, the identification of novel therapeutic targets linked to neuroinflammation pathways in aging, and open-source tools for scalable geriatric psychiatry analytics. This research aims to advance precision medicine in geriatric mental health by elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment variability and informing clinical guidelines for data-driven, patient-specific care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of mental and emotional disorders in the elderly, and to improve the psychiatric care of the elderly both in health and in disease.

abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) represent a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by disruptions in biochemical pathways, leading to complex clinical presentations and variable treatment responses. Current diagnostic and management strategies often rely on fragmented clinical and biochemical data, limiting the ability to predict disease progression or optimize therapies. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (genomic, metabolomic, proteomic) with clinical records to identify predictive biomarkers and model metabolic network perturbations in IEMs. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets, perform genome-scale metabolic reconstructions, and apply machine learning algorithms to uncover genotype-phenotype correlations. Key computational steps include variant prioritization using deep learning models trained on population and disease-specific genomic data, dynamic flux balance analysis to simulate metabolic dysregulation under varying physiological conditions, and unsupervised clustering of patient cohorts to stratify disease subtypes. The project will utilize existing clinical datasets from [Institution]’s metabolic clinic, encompassing over 1,500 patients with confirmed IEMs, and will validate models against longitudinal outcomes. By enabling rapid analysis of complex datasets, HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of these tasks, particularly the iterative optimization required for metabolic network modeling and high-dimensional data integration. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool for early diagnosis of rare IEMs using multi-omics signatures, (2) in silico models to guide personalized dietary and pharmacological interventions, and (3) publicly accessible computational workflows for the metabolic genetics community. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making, reduce diagnostic odysseys, and advance precision medicine approaches for IEMs, ultimately improving outcomes for patients with these complex disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and medical management of individuals with inborn errors of metabolism, including the provision of direct care and consultative care for individuals of all ages.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven decision-making framework to optimize resource allocation and improve student outcomes in higher education institutions (HEIs). Despite growing financial pressures and demands for equitable access, many HEIs rely on static, legacy models for budgeting, staffing, and program evaluation. This research addresses the critical gap in dynamic, scalable computational tools capable of simulating institutional policies, forecasting enrollment trends, and modeling the cascading impacts of resource decisions on student retention and academic success. Using anonymized institutional data spanning admissions records, course evaluations, financial reports, and student support interactions, we propose implementing agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate multi-year scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process heterogeneous datasets (5+ TB) and train ensemble models that integrate demographic, academic, and operational variables. The computational workflow will involve three phases: (1) preprocessing longitudinal institutional data using distributed data-parallel methods, (2) developing parallelized ABM simulations to test resource allocation strategies under demographic and funding uncertainties, and (3) applying interpretable ML classifiers to identify predictors of student attrition and program viability. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for HEI administrators to evaluate trade-offs in strategic planning, such as the equity implications of budget cuts or the cost-benefit analysis of student success initiatives. By quantifying how targeted investments in faculty staffing, advising systems, or infrastructure correlate with graduation rates, this research aims to advance evidence-based leadership practices while addressing computational challenges unique to higher education’s complex, interdependent systems. The project’s scalable architecture will enable adoption by diverse institutions, fostering more responsive and equitable resource distribution in higher education administration.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in four-year colleges, universities and higher education systems, the study of higher education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in higher education economics and finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; college student services; research on higher education; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the legal and regulatory dynamics shaping equitable access to digital health technologies (DHTs) across diverse populations. While DHTs—such as AI-driven diagnostics, telehealth platforms, and wearable devices—promise transformative health outcomes, their integration into healthcare systems raises complex legal questions involving privacy, liability, algorithmic bias, and disparities in technology adoption. Existing research in health law often relies on manual case reviews or qualitative policy analyses, limiting scalability and the ability to model systemic interactions between legal frameworks, socio-economic variables, and health equity outcomes. This project will develop computational legal analytics tools to process large-scale datasets, including judicial opinions, federal/state regulations, health outcome databases, and demographic records, to identify patterns in legal barriers or facilitators of DHT accessibility. Using natural language processing (NLP) models tailored to legal text, we will classify precedents related to DHT liability and data governance, while graph-based network analyses will map correlations between jurisdictional legal stances, technology adoption rates, and disparities in health outcomes. Agent-based modeling will simulate how hypothetical policy interventions (e.g., revised FDA guidance on AI transparency or state-level reimbursement laws for telehealth) might propagate through healthcare ecosystems. The HPC environment is critical for training domain-specific NLP architectures on multi-terabyte legal corpora, running parallelized policy simulations, and managing high-dimensional datasets linking legal, clinical, and demographic variables. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for predicting the equity impacts of health technology regulations and actionable insights for policymakers seeking to align innovation incentives with equitable access imperatives. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science and health law, offering novel methodologies to address gaps in evidence-based health technology governance.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies and regulations affecting the health care industry, health professions, health services and insurance industries, and patients.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing complex industrial systems under uncertainty, with applications in supply chain resilience, healthcare operations, and sustainable energy distribution. Industrial systems increasingly face disruptions from demand volatility, resource constraints, and dynamic interdependencies between human and automated processes. Existing optimization methods struggle to balance real-time decision-making with long-term strategic planning, particularly when modeling stochastic events or multi-objective trade-offs. We propose a hybrid approach combining high-fidelity discrete-event simulation, parallelized stochastic optimization, and machine learning-based scenario generation to address these challenges. The computational workload involves solving large-scale mixed-integer linear programs with embedded Markov decision processes, requiring distributed memory architectures for scenario tree evaluations and Monte Carlo sampling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable iterative refinement of risk-aware scheduling policies through GPU-accelerated deep reinforcement learning agents trained on synthetic and real-world operational datasets. Key innovations include adaptive decomposition algorithms to partition problem spaces across nodes and a novel convergence criterion for non-stationary environments. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for resilience planning in multi-echelon networks, validated through case studies on medical supply distribution during crisis events and cross-sector resource sharing in circular economies. The research will advance methodological integration of prescriptive analytics and simulation-based digital twins in industrial engineering, directly supporting NSF’s priorities for cybermanufacturing and intelligent systems. Resource allocation will prioritize GPU node hours for neural network training and MPI-enabled clusters for distributed optimization tasks, with an estimated need for 250,000 core-hours annually. Results will be disseminated through open-source code repositories and industry partnerships to bridge academic research and practical implementation gaps.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: Dental biofilms are complex microbial communities implicated in oral diseases such as caries and periodontitis, yet their dynamic interactions with preventive agents remain poorly understood at mechanistic levels. This project seeks to model the resilience of oral biofilms to common antimicrobial treatments used in dental hygiene, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate biofilm behavior under varying clinical conditions. Current experimental models struggle to capture the spatial, temporal, and metabolic heterogeneity of biofilms, limiting the optimization of treatment protocols. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and molecular dynamics (MD) to simulate biofilm architecture, interspecies interactions, and response to chlorhexidine, fluoride, and emerging nano-scale preventive agents. The ABM layer will model population-level behaviors, including extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) production and nutrient gradients, while MD simulations will resolve atomic-scale interactions between antimicrobial compounds and bacterial cell membranes. This approach requires HPC resources due to the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across thousands of microbial agents and nanosecond-scale molecular trajectories. Expected outcomes include identifying biofilm vulnerabilities to combinatorial treatments, predicting evolutionary pathways of antimicrobial resistance, and optimizing agent delivery strategies to enhance clinical efficacy. The results will directly inform evidence-based guidelines for personalized preventive care, supporting dental hygienists in tailoring patient-specific interventions. By bridging computational microbiology and clinical dental hygiene, this project addresses a critical gap in translational oral health research, offering a novel paradigm to combat biofilm-mediated diseases through in silico hypothesis testing. The proposed work will generate open-access simulation tools adaptable to broader biofilm studies, fostering interdisciplinary innovation at the intersection of health sciences and computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to clean teeth and apply preventive materials, provide oral health education and treatment counseling to patients, identify oral pathologies and injuries, and manage dental hygiene practices. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, microbiology, and pathology; dental hygiene theory and techniques; cleaning equipment operation and maintenance; dental materials; radiology; patient education and counseling; office management; supervised clinical training; and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying real-time second language (L2) processing by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While traditional methods in second language acquisition (SLA) research—such as behavioral experiments, surveys, or neuroimaging—provide valuable insights, they are constrained by limited scalability, temporal resolution, and capacity to model dynamic interactions across multimodal data (e.g., eye-tracking, EEG, production corpora). To overcome these limitations, the proposed research employs large-scale computational modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate and analyze the complex processes involved in L2 comprehension and production. The project will integrate psycholinguistic datasets from diverse learner populations, including longitudinal records of syntactic development, phonological processing, and cross-linguistic interference patterns. These datasets will feed into neural network models trained to replicate human-like language acquisition trajectories, with parallelized simulations running on HPC clusters to test hypotheses about critical periods, transfer effects, and individual variability. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be deployed to parse and annotate multilingual learner corpora, enabling real-time analysis of error patterns and proficiency milestones. The computational demands of training deep learning architectures, managing terabyte-scale multimodal data, and conducting Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic linguistic outcomes necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying cognitive thresholds for L2 grammatical internalization, (2) data-driven frameworks for optimizing pedagogical interventions based on learner-specific cognitive profiles, and (3) open-access tools for scalable analysis of L2 development metrics. By bridging computational neuroscience and applied linguistics, this work aims to advance theoretical models of language plasticity while offering empirically grounded strategies for personalized language instruction. The requested resources will directly support the generation of publishable findings and grant proposals targeting interdisciplinary funding agencies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, and maintenance of second languages. Includes instruction in language pedagogy, use, analysis and processes.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying cross-species transmission and virulence of emerging zoonotic pathogens in livestock, with a focus on influenza A viruses (IAVs) and coronaviruses. These pathogens pose significant threats to animal health, agricultural economies, and public health due to their rapid evolution, host adaptability, and pandemic potential. Current limitations in predicting spillover events stem from an incomplete integration of multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with population-level epidemiological models, a task requiring computational resources beyond typical laboratory capabilities. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze terabyte-scale datasets from longitudinal surveillance of infected poultry and swine populations, incorporating whole-genome sequencing, host immune response profiles, and environmental metadata. Machine learning frameworks will identify genetic markers associated with host tropism and antiviral resistance, while agent-based models simulate transmission dynamics under varying husbandry conditions. Phylogenetic reconciliation methods will reconstruct viral evolutionary histories to pinpoint drivers of cross-species jumps. The computational workflow will utilize parallelized pipelines for alignment of nanopore sequencing data, Bayesian inference of selection pressures, and network analysis of host-pathogen protein interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models of strain-specific virulence, spatially explicit risk maps for outbreak hotspots, and a curated database of pathogen-host molecular interactions. These resources will enable proactive surveillance strategies, inform vaccine target selection, and refine biosecurity protocols for livestock systems. By leveraging HPC capabilities to bridge molecular and population scales, this work will advance diagnostic precision, reduce economic losses from emergent epizootics, and mitigate zoonotic threats at the human-animal interface.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the development and process of disease in domestic and wild animals and applications to diagnosis, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in pathogenesis, immunoparasitology, viral therapy, inherited metabolic diseases, environmental toxicology, anatomical and clinical pathology, necropsy and biopsy techniques, clinical laboratory analysis, pathological interpretation, and disease diagnosis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate entrepreneurial ecosystems, enabling educators in business and innovation teacher education programs to design data-driven pedagogical strategies. Current approaches to teaching entrepreneurship often rely on static case studies or theoretical models, which fail to capture the dynamic, interdependent variables influencing real-world business outcomes. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build large-scale agent-based simulations that replicate market interactions, resource allocation dynamics, and innovation diffusion processes.
