These simulations will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including regional economic indicators, startup success metrics, and behavioral patterns from entrepreneurial networks—to create adaptive scenarios reflecting diverse industry contexts. Machine learning models will then analyze simulation outputs to identify critical success factors and failure modes for early-stage ventures. A parallel computational effort will focus on optimizing curriculum design through natural language processing (NLP) of longitudinal student feedback and competency assessments, correlating instructional methods with measurable skill acquisition in business modeling and opportunity recognition. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent interactions, real-time parameter tuning across thousands of simulation instances, and training predictive models on high-dimensional educational data. Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for entrepreneurship educators, evidence-based frameworks for teaching adaptive decision-making in uncertain markets, and predictive analytics templates to personalize instruction based on emerging competency gaps. By grounding teacher education in computationally validated models of entrepreneurial systems, this research aims to bridge the gap between classroom instruction and the rapidly evolving demands of innovation-driven economies.
cip_title: Business and Innovation/ Entrepreneurship Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational business, innovation, and entrepreneurship programs at various educational levels. Includes instruction in business administration, business development, finance, idea generation, investing, logistics, management, and marketing.

abstract: Aging populations present complex social dynamics that remain understudied due to the interplay of cognitive decline, shifting interpersonal networks, and environmental adaptations. This project seeks to model how micro-level social interactions among older adults aggregate into macro-level community resilience patterns, with a focus on mitigating isolation and cognitive deterioration. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will simulate longitudinal social networks across diverse aging populations, incorporating individual-level data on cognitive capacity, mobility constraints, and communication preferences. The computational framework integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture bidirectional relationships between individual behaviors and evolving group structures. Unique challenges include scaling dynamic network analyses across decade-long synthetic cohorts (N ≈ 1M agents) and calibrating models using multimodal data from wearables, community surveys, and care facility records. HPC resources will enable parallelized parameter space exploration to account for heterogeneity in cultural norms around aging, regional resource disparities, and crisis scenarios (e.g., pandemic-induced isolation spikes). Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for simulating aging-related social dynamics, identification of critical leverage points for community interventions, and predictive metrics for early-stage resilience decline. By bridging gerontology with computational social science, this work addresses a methodological gap in modeling lifespan social processes while providing actionable insights for age-friendly infrastructure design. The resource-intensive nature of iteratively training GNNs on stochastic ABM outputs necessitates dedicated GPU nodes and large-memory processors to manage high-dimensional interaction histories. Results will advance both theoretical frameworks for aging-in-context and practical tools for policymakers aiming to optimize social support systems in rapidly aging societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences and psychology.

abstract: Chiropractic care relies on precise spinal adjustments to address vertebral misalignments and their systemic effects, yet the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying optimal clinical outcomes remain incompletely understood. Current experimental and clinical methods lack the resolution to model the complex, dynamic interactions between spinal structures, neural pathways, and adjustment forces in patient-specific contexts. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models of spinal biomechanics and simulate the effects of chiropractic interventions. Using anonymized patient imaging data (MRI, CT) and clinical records, we will construct finite element models of spinal segments to analyze load distribution, tissue deformation, and joint kinematics during manual adjustments. These models will integrate neural network simulations to predict how biomechanical changes influence proprioceptive feedback and autonomic nervous system activity. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will process longitudinal clinical datasets to identify patterns linking adjustment techniques, patient demographics, and health outcomes. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated solvers for finite element analysis and distributed computing frameworks for large-scale data analytics. By coupling mechanistic simulations with data-driven inference, this research aims to establish predictive relationships between adjustment parameters, biomechanical responses, and therapeutic efficacy. Expected outcomes include optimized adjustment protocols for specific vertebral misalignment patterns, personalized treatment planning tools, and a foundational computational framework for hypothesis testing in chiropractic research. The project will enhance evidence-based practice by providing quantitative insights into adjustment mechanisms while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in advancing chiropractic science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of chiropractic, a health care and healing system based on the application of non-invasive treatments and spinal adjustments to alleviate health problems caused by vertebral misalignments affecting bodily function as derived from the philosophy of Daniel Palmer. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, chiropractic theory and science, postural and spinal analysis, diagnostic radiology and ultrasound, adjustment technique, patient counseling, professional standards and ethics, and practice management.

abstract: Wildfire behavior prediction and forensic investigation require advanced computational tools to address the growing complexity of fire dynamics in changing ecosystems. Current operational models struggle to integrate real-time data streams—including hyperlocal meteorology, heterogeneous fuel distributions, and human activity patterns—into actionable forecasts or post-event reconstructions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model fire spread under multi-scale environmental variability and quantify uncertainty in arson investigation scenarios. The computational approach combines coupled atmosphere-fire physics (WRF-Fire) with machine learning techniques to assimilate satellite-derived fuel moisture data, LiDAR terrain maps, and historical ignition records. Parallelized ensemble simulations will quantify probabilistic fire pathways under varying suppression strategies, while graph-based anomaly detection algorithms will analyze spatial-temporal ignition clusters to differentiate natural from human-caused fires. By scaling to 10-meter resolution across 100,000+ acre domains, the framework aims to reduce false-positive rates in arson detection by 40% compared to current forensic methods and improve 6-hour containment probability forecasts by 25% under extreme weather conditions. The HPC implementation will optimize GPU-accelerated fluid dynamics solvers for buoyant plume interactions and employ distributed memory architectures to handle petabyte-scale outputs from multi-agent evacuation simulations. Outcomes will directly inform next-generation decision support systems for firefighting resource allocation, including airborne deployment prioritization and dynamic firebreak placement. The open-source tools developed will enable agencies to reconcile conflicting observational datasets during active incidents and provide court-admissible probabilistic evidence in wildfire arson cases, addressing critical gaps in both operational response and environmental justice.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science, firefighting and investigation to the prevention, control and mitigation of wildland fires and the analysis of causes. Includes instruction in fire science and behavior, wildland environments, meteorology, wildland fire hydraulics and dynamics, water and chemical supply systems, wildland firefighting operations, airborne firefighting, firebreak engineering, communications systems, wildland arson, forensic procedures, wildland fire prevention, investigation techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of forensic evidence analysis, particularly in cases involving complex biological mixtures, degraded samples, or ambiguous crime scene patterns. A critical challenge in forensic science is the reliable interpretation of trace evidence—such as multi-contributor DNA profiles, bloodstain patterns in dynamic environments, or chemically altered materials—where traditional analytical methods often struggle to resolve uncertainties or integrate multi-modal datasets. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement probabilistic modeling, machine learning, and large-scale simulations tailored to forensic applications. Key computational tasks include the development of Bayesian networks for DNA mixture deconvolution, agent-based simulations of blood spatter dynamics under variable environmental conditions, and deep learning models for automated comparison of toolmarks or fracture patterns. These methods require iterative parameter sampling, high-dimensional data integration, and validation against empirical datasets, all of which demand substantial parallel processing capabilities. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, we aim to reduce analysis times from weeks to hours while improving statistical confidence in evidence interpretation. The outcomes will directly support forensic practitioners in generating reproducible, court-admissible results, particularly in high-stakes cases involving terrorism, mass disasters, or cold case reinvestigations. Additionally, this work will establish open-source computational frameworks that adhere to forensic ethics standards, enabling transparent peer validation and reducing risks of algorithmic bias. The requested HPC resources will enable scaling to real-world forensic datasets, including 3D crime scene reconstructions and multi-omics forensic biomarkers, thereby bridging gaps between laboratory research and operational forensic workflows in homeland security contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the physical, biomedical, and social sciences to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence, human testimony and criminal suspects. Includes instruction in forensic medicine, forensic dentistry, anthropology, psychology, entomology, pathology, forensic laboratory technology and autopsy procedures, DNA and blood pattern analysis, crime scene analysis, crime scene photography, fingerprint technology, document analysis, witness and suspect examination procedures, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Floriculture enterprises face critical challenges in optimizing perishable inventory management while maintaining artistic and commercial viability. Current industry practices rely on heuristic decision-making for floral design trends, greenhouse climate control, and delivery logistics, resulting in substantial economic losses from unsold inventory (15-25% sector-wide) and suboptimal product quality. This project proposes a computational framework integrating machine learning, fluid dynamics simulations, and logistics optimization to transform floriculture operations. We will develop convolutional neural networks trained on multi-year floral arrangement images and consumer preference data to forecast design trends with spatial-temporal resolution. Parallelized computational fluid dynamics simulations will model microclimate conditions across commercial greenhouses, optimizing energy-efficient environmental controls for diverse species using GPU-accelerated lattice Boltzmann methods. A mixed-integer linear programming solver enhanced with quantum-inspired annealing will dynamically route delivery vehicles while balancing floral perishability rates, traffic patterns, and real-time order updates. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets of historical sales, IoT sensor feeds, and street-level imagery, enabling daily retraining of prediction models. Expected outcomes include a 22-35% reduction in floral waste through improved demand forecasting, 18% energy savings in greenhouse operations via adaptive climate modeling, and 27% faster delivery times through neural combinatorial optimization. The resulting decision-support system will be validated through partnerships with three regional floral cooperatives, providing scalable solutions for small businesses facing climate volatility and market pressures. By establishing computational workflows at the intersection of aesthetic analytics and agricultural engineering, this research advances precision floriculture management while preserving artistic expression in horticultural commerce.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage commercial and contract florist enterprises, supply and delivery services, and flower catering services. Includes instruction in the applicable principles of plant science; purchasing, storage, and delivery systems; floral design and arranging; and principles of business management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the dynamic interactions between macroeconomic policy and heterogeneous agent behavior under uncertainty. Traditional macroeconomic models often rely on representative agent frameworks, which obscure distributional effects and limit the analysis of how policy shocks propagate across diverse households and firms. To address this gap, the study employs a large-scale heterogeneous agent New Keynesian (HANK) model calibrated to U.S. economic data, integrating granular household-level consumption, savings, and labor supply decisions. The computational challenge lies in solving high-dimensional dynamic stochastic optimization problems with recursive preferences, asymmetric information, and occasionally binding constraints—tasks that require parallelized solving algorithms and significant memory allocation. The project will utilize MPI-based parallelization to distribute equilibrium computation across nodes, alongside GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods for simulating forward-looking expectations under multiple stochastic shock scenarios. Key outcomes include quantifying the distributional impacts of monetary and fiscal policy interventions, assessing the role of household heterogeneity in amplifying or dampening macroeconomic volatility, and generating policy-relevant insights into the design of stabilization mechanisms. By enabling faster parameter space exploration and robustness checks across alternative model specifications, HPC resources are critical to achieving convergence in equilibrium solutions and ensuring numerical stability. The results aim to inform debates on macroeconomic resilience and equitable policy design, while advancing computational methods for heterogeneous agent modeling in economics. This work aligns with the program’s focus on resource allocation under scarcity by rigorously analyzing trade-offs in policy instruments under complex, real-world constraints.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the systematic study of the production, conservation and allocation of resources in conditions of scarcity, together with the organizational frameworks related to these processes. Includes instruction in economic theory, micro- and macroeconomics, comparative economic systems, money and banking systems, international economics, quantitative analytical methods, and applications to specific industries and public policy issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the long-term impacts of Waldorf/Steiner pedagogical practices on multidimensional learning outcomes. While qualitative studies have documented the holistic benefits of Waldorf education, there remains a critical gap in understanding how its unique pedagogical elements—such as arts-integrated curricula, epoch-based learning, and developmental stage alignment—interact dynamically to influence cognitive, emotional, and social development. The research problem centers on capturing these complex, nonlinear relationships at scale, which traditional observational methods cannot adequately address. To achieve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations that replicate classroom ecosystems under Steiner-inspired pedagogical conditions. The ABM framework will integrate empirical data from existing Waldorf schools, including student engagement metrics, teacher intervention patterns, and longitudinal performance data. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters and identify emergent patterns across simulated multiyear educational trajectories. Key computational challenges include managing large parameter spaces for individualized learning pathways, parallelizing simulations to test diverse pedagogical scenarios, and processing multimodal output data (e.g., social network dynamics within student cohorts). Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model to assess how variations in Steiner teaching strategies influence developmental milestones, enabling data-informed refinements to teacher training programs. The project will also produce open-source tools for visualizing pedagogical interactions, designed for accessibility by educator-researchers without computational expertise. By bridging Waldorf’s humanistic traditions with advanced computational analytics, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based practices in Steiner teacher education while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in studying complex pedagogical systems.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Rudolf Steiner and his followers.

abstract: Nursing science faces critical challenges in advancing evidence-based practice, including the need to analyze complex, high-dimensional datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), wearable devices, and multi-omic profiles to optimize patient outcomes. Traditional statistical methods are insufficient to model the nonlinear interactions between patient-specific variables, environmental factors, and dynamic care protocols. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models that predict patient deterioration risks and personalize nursing interventions in acute care settings. Using a longitudinal dataset of 250,000+ EHR entries from a tertiary hospital, we will employ deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models, recurrent neural networks) to integrate temporal clinical data, free-text nursing notes, and sensor-derived mobility metrics. Computational workflows will include federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy while training models across distributed datasets. A parallelized simulation framework will test hypothetical intervention scenarios, quantifying how staffing ratios or protocol adjustments affect clinical outcomes. The HPC environment is essential for managing GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and real-time inference tasks across multi-node clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for sepsis, pressure injury, and falls, validated against prospective clinical data; (2) open-source tools to automate nursing workload-intensity calculations; and (3) a computational platform for simulating nurse-patient interactions under resource constraints. This work will directly inform staffing policies, reduce adverse events, and establish a template for data-driven nursing research. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project bridges gaps between clinical expertise and computational innovation, enabling scalable solutions to challenges in care delivery and health equity.
cip_definition: A research program that focuses on the study of advanced clinical practices, research methodologies, the administration of complex nursing services, and that prepares nurses to further the progress of nursing research through experimentation and clinical applications.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and customer sentiment integration in tourism and travel service operations through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the unique challenges of real-time decision-making in hospitality marketing. Traditional pricing models in hotel and motel operations often fail to adapt to hyperlocal demand fluctuations, seasonal volatility, and real-time consumer sentiment derived from social media, reviews, and IoT-enabled guest interactions. The research problem centers on developing a machine learning framework that synthesizes heterogeneous data streams—including booking patterns, sentiment analysis from multilingual reviews, and environmental sensors tracking occupancy and service usage—to generate adaptive pricing and personalized marketing strategies. Computational methods will involve graph neural networks to model interdependencies between service touchpoints (e.g., spa bookings, restaurant reservations) and transformer-based natural language processing for real-time sentiment tracking across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts. Agent-based simulations will test operational scenarios under stochastic demand shocks, such as weather disruptions or regional events, requiring parallelized computations to evaluate millions of parameter combinations. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training multi-modal models on terabyte-scale datasets spanning five years of global hotel operations and simulating decision pathways at sub-minute latency for operational relevance. Expected outcomes include a deployable API for dynamic price-tier adjustments and service bundling recommendations, validated against historical revenue data from partner hotels. The research aims to advance computational hospitality science by establishing a methodological bridge between granular operational data and macro-scale market trends, directly addressing efficiency gaps in travel services marketing while contributing open-source tools for resource-constrained small and mid-sized hospitality enterprises.
cip_title: Tourism and Travel Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide direct retail services to hotel and motel clients and customers in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in the principles of hotel/motel operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, and basic office management.

abstract: Ocular diseases in animals present unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to species-specific anatomical variations, limited biomarkers, and the complexity of pathophysiological mechanisms. This project seeks to advance precision veterinary ophthalmology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model ophthalmic disease progression, optimize surgical interventions, and identify therapeutic targets. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) developing machine learning models to predict postoperative outcomes in canine cataract surgery using multimodal data (optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure dynamics, and proteomic profiles), and (2) simulating biomechanical interactions during corneal ulcer healing across species using finite element analysis. Current clinical approaches rely on generalized treatment protocols, which fail to account for individual variability in wound healing kinetics or species-specific corneal biomechanics. The computational workflow integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image segmentation, federated learning frameworks to aggregate multi-institutional data while preserving privacy, and GPU-accelerated fluid-structure interaction models to simulate tear film dynamics and stromal remodeling. By analyzing >50 TB of historical surgical records and high-resolution imaging data, the models will identify predictive features for surgical complications and establish species-specific thresholds for safe intraocular pressure modulation during procedures. Anticipated outcomes include a validated computational platform for pre-surgical risk stratification and a publicly accessible database of corneal biomechanical properties across 15+ animal species. This work addresses critical gaps in veterinary ophthalmic care by enabling data-driven personalization of treatment plans, reducing postoperative morbidity in companion animals, and providing translational insights into comparative ocular pathology. The scale of 3D biomechanical simulations and federated training across distributed datasets necessitates HPC resources to achieve clinically relevant throughput and model fidelity.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders in animals, and related ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in animal eye surgery.

abstract: Somatic psychology emphasizes the integration of bodily experiences and movement practices to address psychological distress, yet the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying these interventions remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by analyzing high-dimensional, multimodal datasets from movement-based therapeutic sessions (e.g., authentic movement, yoga, Tai Chi) to model dynamic mind-body interactions. The research problem centers on identifying reproducible patterns in autonomic, kinematic, and self-reported affective data that correlate with therapeutic outcomes in somatic counseling contexts. A computational pipeline will be developed to process synchronized biometric data streams (motion capture, heart rate variability, electrodermal activity) and qualitative session transcripts using time-series analysis, network modeling, and natural language processing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these datasets: individual sessions generate over 10 GB of multimodal data at 100+ Hz sampling rates, necessitating parallelized preprocessing, real-time feature extraction, and large-scale simulations of hypothesized body-mind feedback loops. Machine learning models will be trained to predict intervention efficacy based on early-session biomarkers, enabling personalized somatic therapy design. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for quantifying embodied therapeutic processes, (2) open-source tools for analyzing movement-biometric datasets in counseling research, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing body-centered interventions in applied psychology settings. By bridging somatic practices with advanced computational methods, this work aims to establish empirical foundations for holistic trauma and stress interventions while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in advancing non-clinical psychological research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on a holistic approach to solving interpersonal issues and psychological problems. Includes instruction in authentic movement, body-mind balance and integration, contact improvisation, dance, Pilates, Tai Chi, relaxation techniques, and Yoga.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for simulating the dynamic behavior of dense granular systems under extreme shear conditions—a critical yet understudied problem with implications for industrial processes, geophysical flows, and advanced manufacturing. While granular materials exhibit complex solid- and fluid-like behaviors, existing simulation tools struggle to resolve the multiscale interactions between particle-scale mechanics, mesoscale force chains, and system-level rheology, particularly in regimes where rapid deformation induces jamming-to-flow transitions. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining discrete element method (DEM) simulations with graph neural network (GNN)-accelerated continuum approximations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale DEM simulations (10^7+ particles) to generate training data for the GNN architecture, which will learn latent representations of stress transmission and contact network evolution. The framework will integrate these components within a multiphysics solver, leveraging adaptive mesh refinement to locally resolve critical regions of high shear. Validation will utilize experimental datasets from collaborative shear cell studies. Successful implementation will provide a scalable tool for predicting flow instabilities and energy dissipation patterns in granular systems, directly informing the design of next-generation additive manufacturing powder spreaders, landslide mitigation systems, and planetary regolith excavation technologies. The computational methodologies developed—particularly the fusion of particle-based and data-driven techniques—will advance the broader field of computational mechanics by offering a template for bridging microscale discontinuities and macroscale continuum assumptions in heterogeneous material simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to the application of mechanics. Incudes instruction in method development in solid, fluid mechanics and materials simulations with application to biomechanics and mechanics in medicine, multiphysics, fracture mechanics, multiscale mechanics, particle and meshfree methods.

abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into modern power grids presents complex challenges due to the inherent variability of solar and wind resources, coupled with evolving demand patterns and aging infrastructure. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize grid stability, energy storage utilization, and cost-effective dispatch strategies in hybrid energy systems. Current models often oversimplify spatiotemporal interactions between distributed generation assets, storage technologies, and demand-side management, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios with high renewable penetration. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach combined with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to simulate and optimize grid operations at unprecedented resolution. The computational framework will integrate real-world weather data, equipment performance curves, and stochastic demand profiles to generate adaptive control policies for grid operators. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train the MARL-PINN hybrid model, which requires parallelized simulations of thousands of interacting agents across multi-year operational horizons. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor operations for neural network training and employ MPI-based distributed computing for large-scale scenario analysis. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for grid resilience planning, novel insights into storage sizing under climate uncertainty, and quantifiable metrics for balancing renewable integration with infrastructure upgrade costs. This work directly supports national priorities for decarbonizing energy systems while maintaining grid reliability, with potential applications ranging from microgrid design to regional transmission planning. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at scales impractical for local clusters, particularly for sensitivity analyses examining how evolving technology costs and extreme weather events impact optimal system configurations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric patients exhibit significant variability in treatment responses due to interactions between developmental, genetic, and environmental factors, complicating the delivery of optimized care. Traditional clinical approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may inadequately address individual patient needs, potentially leading to suboptimal outcomes or adverse effects. This project proposes to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that integrate multi-dimensional data, enabling personalized, predictive strategies for pediatric nursing. The research will focus on common pediatric conditions such as asthma, congenital heart defects, and type 1 diabetes, where dynamic treatment adjustments are critical. Using machine learning algorithms, we will analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and socio-environmental datasets to identify patterns influencing disease progression and therapeutic efficacy. Agent-based simulations will model patient-specific responses to interventions, while real-time optimization frameworks will test hypothetical treatment adjustments to minimize risks. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, training complex neural networks, and executing parallelized simulations at scale—tasks infeasible with standard clinical computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to stratify patients by risk of complications, decision-support systems for nurses to tailor medication dosages and monitoring schedules, and evidence-based insights into modifiable factors affecting recovery. By translating computational findings into clinical workflows, this work aims to reduce hospital readmissions, mitigate treatment side effects, and improve long-term health outcomes for pediatric populations. The project underscores the transformative potential of computational science in advancing precision nursing, offering a scalable framework to bridge data-driven research and bedside care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care for children from infancy through adolescence. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting physicians, patient examination and referral, and planning and delivering health maintenance and health education programs.

abstract: The increasing complexity of high-dimensional datasets in laboratory medicine—including multi-omics profiles, high-resolution medical imaging, and real-time clinical laboratory data—poses significant challenges for traditional analytical methods. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing scalable computational workflows to integrate and analyze heterogeneous datasets, with the goal of improving diagnostic accuracy, prognostic modeling, and therapeutic decision-making. A central focus is the creation of predictive models that link laboratory-derived biomarkers to clinical outcomes in patients with complex, multifactorial diseases such as sepsis and autoimmune disorders. The proposed work will leverage machine learning (ML) algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to identify latent patterns in high-dimensional data from electronic health records (EHRs), mass spectrometry, and flow cytometry. Computational challenges include managing data sparsity, addressing class imbalance in rare disease cohorts, and ensuring model interpretability for clinical translation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training large-scale models on multi-terabyte datasets, optimizing hyperparameters via distributed computing, and validating results through computationally intensive permutation testing. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for harmonizing laboratory and clinical data streams, (2) validated ML models for early detection of sepsis progression using proteomic and metabolomic signatures, and (3) a computational framework to assess the cost-effectiveness of novel biomarker panels in diverse healthcare settings. By enabling rapid analysis of complex datasets, this work will directly inform precision medicine strategies while providing a template for resource-efficient data integration in clinical laboratories. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale data integration, ensuring reproducibility and scalability across future studies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied medical research and related techniques, equipment, data systems, and research design. Includes instruction in the management of medical laboratories in research and healthcare facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize rehabilitation program delivery and resource allocation in correctional facilities through predictive modeling and simulation. Correctional systems face persistent challenges in balancing security, rehabilitation outcomes, and operational costs, yet lack data-driven tools to model complex interactions between staffing patterns, facility logistics, and inmate behavioral dynamics. Our research addresses this gap by integrating anonymized historical inmate records, facility operation datasets, and psychological assessment metrics into a novel agent-based model (ABM) that simulates decision pathways for both incarcerated individuals and administrative staff. The ABM will be coupled with machine learning classifiers trained on longitudinal recidivism data to evaluate how adjustments in program scheduling, counselor-to-inmate ratios, and educational resource distribution affect projected rehabilitation success rates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10+ years from three state correctional departments, run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations testing 50,000+ policy scenarios, and train deep reinforcement learning models that identify optimal intervention timing. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between budgetary constraints and evidence-based rehabilitation practices, as well as generative models capable of projecting facility-specific outcomes under staffing shortages or population surges. By translating behavioral theories and operational data into computational parameters, this work establishes a methodological bridge between correctional psychology and systems engineering. The resulting tools will be validated through partnerships with three mid-sized correctional institutions, with potential to reduce trial-and-error policy implementation while maintaining compliance with ethical constraints on inmate data usage. This interdisciplinary approach demonstrates how computational social science methodologies can address pressing operational challenges in non-traditional HPC domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making processes in contested, multi-domain Command and Control (C2) environments, with a focus on mitigating cognitive overload and adversarial misinformation in real-time operational scenarios. Current C2 systems struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams—including signals intelligence, cyber threat indicators, and distributed sensor inputs—while maintaining human operator situational awareness under time-critical constraints. The research employs a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, graph-based anomaly detection, and adaptive reinforcement learning to simulate decision pathways under variable threat landscapes and resource limitations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale simulations of multi-echelon command structures, train machine learning models on synthetic datasets reflecting adversarial deception tactics, and analyze emergent patterns in decision latency across escalating conflict scenarios. Key computational challenges include real-time graph processing for threat network mapping, parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of battlefield outcomes, and federated learning architectures to preserve operational security during model training. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support toolkit that quantifies trade-offs between automation and human judgment, probabilistic models of misinformation propagation in C2 networks, and benchmark metrics for resilient communication protocols under electronic warfare conditions. This work addresses a critical gap in next-generation C2 system design by bridging theoretical operations research with practical constraints of modern military operations, ultimately aiming to reduce decision cycle times while maintaining auditability and human oversight. The computational framework will be iteratively tested against historical exercise data and hypothetical multi-domain conflict scenarios co-developed with operational partners.
cip_title: Command & Control (C3, C4I) Systems and Operations (MILITARY)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational use of information and decision systems in support of battlefield, theatre, and global strategic operations. Includes instruction in applied mathematics and statistics, computer systems, real-time analysis and decision systems, surveillance and navigation systems, information and communications technology, information security, situational awareness, system integration, joint operations and applications to specific command problems and services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the design and optimization of next-generation laser systems and optical devices for industrial and scientific applications. A critical challenge in laser and optical technology lies in modeling nonlinear light-matter interactions, beam propagation in complex media, and thermal-optical effects with sufficient fidelity to guide experimental development. Traditional analytical methods and small-scale simulations often fail to capture the multi-physics dynamics inherent to high-power laser systems, photonic integrated circuits, and ultrafast optical phenomena, leading to costly trial-and-error prototyping cycles. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for electromagnetic wave propagation, custom finite element analysis (FEA) for thermo-optic coupling, and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms. These methods will be applied to three key objectives: (1) simulating nonlinear frequency conversion in quasi-phase-matched optical crystals for mid-infrared laser sources, (2) optimizing femtosecond laser pulse shaping in dispersive media for precision micromachining, and (3) modeling mode-locking dynamics in fiber lasers with complex cavity architectures. The HPC environment is essential for resolving micron-scale spatial features and picosecond temporal dynamics across centimeter-scale optical systems, requiring parallelized computation across thousands of cores for parameter space exploration. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for nonlinear optical processes, optimized laser configurations for specific material processing applications, and open-source simulation tools tailored to photonic device engineering. By bridging computational photonics with experimental laser development, this work aims to reduce design iteration times by 40-60% while enabling performance breakthroughs in laser efficiency, pulse control, and system miniaturization. The resulting capabilities will directly support research in quantum optics, advanced manufacturing, and biomedical imaging within the Laser and Optical Technology program.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using lasers and other optical for commercial or research purposes. Includes instruction in laser and optical principles, testing and maintenance procedures, safety precautions, specific applications to various tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: Veterinary dermatology faces significant challenges in diagnosing and managing complex, multifactorial skin diseases in animals, such as chronic allergic dermatitis, autoimmune disorders, and integumentary cancers. These conditions often involve intricate interactions between genetic, immunological, and environmental factors, necessitating advanced computational approaches to unravel their pathophysiology. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support large-scale genomic, proteomic, and microbiome analyses aimed at identifying biomarkers and therapeutic targets for refractory dermatologic conditions in companion animals. A central focus involves integrating multi-omics datasets from canine and feline patients with clinical metadata to model disease progression and treatment responses. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to classify subtypes of cutaneous lymphoma and predict outcomes of immunomodulatory therapies, while molecular dynamics simulations will characterize interactions between novel biologics and species-specific immune receptors. Additionally, HPC-enabled image analysis pipelines will process high-resolution histopathology and confocal microscopy data to quantify morphological features associated with treatment resistance. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of sequencing data, running parallelized simulations across thousands of ligand-receptor pairs, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved transcriptional pathways in allergic skin disease, validation of cross-species therapeutic targets, and development of open-source diagnostic tools for veterinary practitioners. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will advance precision medicine in veterinary dermatology, reduce reliance on empirical treatment protocols, and provide translational insights into human dermatopathologies. Resource allocation will directly enable scalable data integration and accelerate discovery timelines for critical care applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: Musculoskeletal neoplasms present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneity, variable treatment responses, and high recurrence rates. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often rely on generalized protocols that inadequately account for tumor-specific molecular profiles or dynamic microenvironmental interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics data, clinical records, and advanced imaging for predictive modeling of tumor behavior and therapeutic outcomes. The research will focus on three aims: (1) developing machine learning frameworks to identify genomic and transcriptomic signatures predictive of metastasis and drug resistance in osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma; (2) simulating tumor-immune microenvironment dynamics using agent-based models to optimize combination therapies; and (3) creating radiomic pipelines to correlate MRI/CT-derived features with histopathologic and molecular subtypes. Computational workflows will employ large-scale genomic datasets from public repositories (e.g., TCGA, TARGET), institutional biobanks, and prospective clinical cohorts. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of whole-genome sequencing data, GPU-accelerated deep learning for image analysis, and stochastic modeling of treatment response trajectories. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for personalized neoadjuvant therapy selection, mechanistic insights into tumor-stromal crosstalk, and non-invasive imaging biomarkers for early recurrence detection. By bridging computational oncology with clinical practice, this work aims to reduce therapeutic trial-and-error, improve survival rates, and establish scalable frameworks for precision musculoskeletal oncology. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to managing data complexity, ensuring reproducibility, and achieving translational milestones within clinically relevant timelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal neoplasm, and the application of cancer therapy regimes.

abstract: Plant diseases pose escalating threats to global food security, particularly under climate change-driven shifts in pathogen biogeography and host susceptibility. Current predictive models inadequately capture the spatiotemporal complexity of polycyclic pathogen spread across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes, especially when integrating dynamic host-pathogen-environment interactions at multiple scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based computational framework to simulate epidemic emergence in staple crops, with an initial focus on soil-borne fungal pathogens in wheat systems. The model will integrate (1) spatially explicit soil microbiome metagenomic data, (2) real-time weather pattern projections, and (3) genetically diverse host resistance profiles to quantify emergent disease dynamics. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized execution of >10^6 parameter combinations across simulated landscapes, incorporating stochastic weather events and evolving pathogen populations through deep reinforcement learning algorithms. Key innovations include the implementation of hybrid neural networks to predict microenvironment-specific infection probabilities and GPU-accelerated cellular automata modeling for rhizosphere-level microbial community interactions. Expected outcomes include identification of critical leverage points for preemptive disease management through sensitivity analyses across biological, agronomic, and climatic variables. The framework will generate open-access risk projection maps with 1km² resolution, enabling targeted surveillance for high-risk pathogen genotype × environment combinations. This computational approach advances phytopathology by bridging molecular-scale host-microbe interactions with landscape-scale epidemiological patterns, providing a novel platform to optimize resilience in ecologically intensified cropping systems. Successful implementation will require sustained access to GPU clusters and distributed memory architectures to manage petabyte-scale outputs from coupled biological-physical simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model and optimize hybrid auction formats that integrate live, in-person bidding with decentralized digital participation—a growing trend in auctioneering driven by advances in real-time communication technologies. The research addresses a critical challenge in modern auction management: dynamically balancing bidder engagement, price discovery, and operational efficiency when coordinating simultaneous physical and virtual bid streams across heterogeneous asset categories (e.g., fine art, agricultural equipment). Current auction theory lacks robust models for these hybrid environments, particularly when accounting for latency effects, bidder psychology across modalities, and multi-commodity interactions. To bridge this gap, we will implement a high-performance agent-based simulation platform leveraging historical auction data from partner firms (2018-2023) encompassing 12,000+ transactions. The computational architecture will combine parallelized bid stream processing with reinforcement learning agents trained to emulate human bidder behavior under different auctioneer pacing strategies. Key innovations include a GPU-accelerated environment for real-time simulation of 10,000+ concurrent participants and a novel metric space for quantifying bid "momentum" transfer between physical and digital channels. Expected outcomes include empirically validated protocols for optimal bid sequencing, technology-mediated bidder onboarding workflows, and dynamic reserve price adaptation algorithms. These computational tools will directly address pain points identified in preliminary surveys of 147 professional auctioneers, particularly the need for decision support systems that preserve auctioneer autonomy while mitigating the cognitive load of hybrid event management. By establishing quantitative benchmarks for emerging auction formats, this work aims to enhance the economic efficiency of asset redistribution markets while maintaining the performative elements central to auctioneering practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional careers as auctioneers and auction managers, and for meeting applicable state licensing requirements. Includes instruction in bid calling, public speaking, ringworking, auction techniques, salesmanship skills, auction clerking and cashiering, auction advertising, working independently or with auction houses, contracts and agency, applicable sales law, and managing both general auctions and auctions specializing in commodities such as antiques, consignments, farm equipment, industrial equipment, real estate, livestock, and automobiles.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-resourced Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages, focusing on both ancient textual corpora and modern dialectal variations. A central challenge in this field is the fragmented digital infrastructure for languages such as Akkadian, Aramaic, and modern Arabic dialects, which limits large-scale linguistic analysis. Existing corpora are often sparse, non-standardized, or restricted to specific historical periods, hindering comprehensive studies of syntactic evolution, dialectal divergence, and cross-linguistic contact. To address this, the project proposes the development of scalable computational pipelines for text processing, morphological annotation, and semantic modeling. HPC resources will enable the training of transformer-based machine learning models on distributed datasets to identify phonological, syntactic, and lexical patterns across millennia of language evolution. Key tasks include the automated parsing of cuneiform script digitizations, dialect classification using neural networks, and phylogenetic modeling of Semitic language diversification. The computational demands—including parallel processing of terabyte-scale text corpora, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-memory simulations of language contact scenarios—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of open-access annotated corpora, novel insights into the diffusion of grammatical features across ancient Near Eastern languages, and tools for dialect preservation in endangered speech communities. This work will provide a methodological framework for integrating computational linguistics with philological scholarship, bridging gaps between traditional text-based analysis and data-driven approaches. The results will support broader interdisciplinary applications, from improving OCR accuracy for historical manuscripts to informing language revitalization efforts in collaboration with regional stakeholders.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Middle/ Near Eastern and Semitic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages of the ancient and modern Middle/Near East, Western Asia, North Africa, and Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the molecular and cellular dynamics underpinning immune evasion strategies employed by persistent viral pathogens, with a focus on herpesviruses. A critical gap exists in understanding how chronic antigen exposure reshapes T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire diversity and effector function, particularly in immunocompromised contexts. To address this, we will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze TCR sequencing datasets from longitudinal patient cohorts, integrating single-cell transcriptomic profiles to map clonal expansion trajectories and functional exhaustion markers. Molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between viral immune-modulatory proteins (e.g., CMV US28, EBV BILF1) and host chemokine receptors, leveraging all-atom and coarse-grained approaches to identify conformational states exploitable for therapeutic intervention. Agent-based modeling will simulate spatial immune cell interactions in lymphoid tissue microenvironments during latent infection, incorporating stochastic variation in cytokine gradients and cell motility parameters. These computational workflows require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets and GPU-accelerated simulations exceeding the capacity of local institutional clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of TCR repertoire collapse linked to viral reactivation risk, (2) structural blueprints for allosteric inhibitors of viral G protein-coupled receptors, and (3) mechanistic insights into how stromal cell networks sustain viral reservoirs. The resource allocation will directly enable parameter sweeps across 10^4–10^5 simulated immune cell populations, significantly advancing translational goals in targeted immunotherapy and vaccine design for chronic viral infections. This work bridges immunology and computational biophysics while remaining distinct from excluded fields by focusing on host-pathogen interface mechanisms rather than general bioinformatics tool development or genomic-scale analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on scientific study of the biological mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of disease, host-pathogen interactions, and host response to disease. Includes instruction in antigen and antibody structure and function, effector mechanisms, receptors, histocompatibility, host-pathogen recognition, disease modeling, autoimmune systems, antibody formation, cytotoxic responses, regulation of immune response, virulence determinants, intercellular signaling, immunosuppression, immunotherapy, immunogenetics, disease markers, transplantation, antibody humanization, and microbial pathogenesis.

abstract: The integration of computational modeling into physical therapy rehabilitation planning remains underexplored, particularly in optimizing personalized interventions for patients with musculoskeletal impairments. Current clinical practices rely heavily on generalized protocols, which may not account for individual biomechanical variability, leading to suboptimal recovery timelines. This project seeks to address this gap by developing high-fidelity computational models that simulate patient-specific motor function and tissue response to therapeutic interventions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process large-scale datasets from motion capture systems, electromyography, and medical imaging to construct multiscale biomechanical models of the lower extremities. These models will integrate machine learning algorithms to predict optimal rehabilitation strategies based on individualized factors such as injury severity, joint kinematics, and muscle activation patterns. Key computational challenges include real-time simulation of neuromuscular feedback loops, finite element analysis of soft tissue stress distributions during therapeutic exercises, and sensitivity analyses to evaluate intervention efficacy across diverse patient cohorts. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the computational intensity of parallelized simulations and training predictive algorithms on heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for generating adaptive rehabilitation protocols, which will be disseminated as an open-access tool for clinical educators and physical therapy technicians. By bridging computational advances with applied rehabilitation science, this project aims to enhance evidence-based decision-making in clinical settings, reduce trial-and-error in treatment planning, and improve functional recovery outcomes. Additionally, the project will support the development of training modules to familiarize physical therapy students with computational tools, fostering interdisciplinary skills in data-driven patient care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of physical therapists, and to perform routine functions in support of physical therapy and rehabilitation. Includes instruction in applied kinesiology, basic function of the human body, communication skills, principles and procedures of physical therapy, physical therapy modalities, and professional ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) on resource-constrained edge devices by developing a co-design framework that optimizes both algorithmic efficiency and hardware execution. While advances in deep learning have enabled state-of-the-art performance across domains, the computational and energy costs of modern DNNs remain prohibitive for real-time edge applications, such as autonomous systems and IoT devices. Existing approaches often treat model architecture design and hardware optimization as isolated tasks, leading to suboptimal trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and power consumption. This work proposes an interdisciplinary computational methodology integrating neural architecture search (NAS), hardware-aware quantization, and energy-efficient accelerator design. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale parallel simulations of candidate architectures across heterogeneous computing platforms, iteratively refining models using multi-objective optimization techniques. Key computational steps include distributed training of surrogate models for rapid architecture evaluation, hardware-in-the-loop simulations to assess latency and energy profiles, and reinforcement learning-driven exploration of the joint design space. The project’s outcomes will include (1) energy-optimized DNN architectures tailored for edge deployment, (2) an open-source framework for hardware-algorithm co-design, and (3) empirical benchmarks quantifying trade-offs across accuracy, latency, and power for emerging edge devices. By bridging computer science (algorithmic innovation) and computer engineering (hardware optimization), this work aims to advance the development of sustainable, scalable intelligent systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the computational complexity of multi-fidelity simulations and enabling rapid iteration across design parameters, which would be infeasible on local infrastructure. Results will directly benefit applications in smart healthcare, robotics, and distributed sensor networks, while contributing methodological advances to interdisciplinary computing research.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze ethical decision-making processes in complex, real-world professional environments, with a focus on identifying and mitigating systemic biases in organizational policies. Despite advances in ethical theory, practical applications often struggle to account for dynamic, multi-stakeholder scenarios where competing values and power imbalances complicate outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale simulations of ethical dilemmas across healthcare, corporate governance, and environmental policy contexts. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to represent diverse actors (e.g., professionals, institutions, communities) and their interactions under varying ethical frameworks (utilitarian, deontological, care ethics). Machine learning techniques will then identify patterns in emergent ethical conflicts and evaluate the efficacy of intervention strategies. A key innovation is the integration of empirical datasets—such as historical case law, public health records, and corporate ethics reports—to ground simulations in observed behavior. The computational demands of this approach are significant: ABM scalability requires parallel processing to manage thousands of concurrent agents, while NLP-driven analysis of unstructured ethical case texts necessitates GPU-accelerated transformers. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated ethical scenarios with annotated decision trees, (2) quantitative metrics for assessing bias and fairness in organizational ethics protocols, and (3) predictive models to guide policy redesign in high-stakes domains like AI governance and crisis triage systems. By bridging normative ethics with data-driven systems analysis, this work aims to equip practitioners with tools to navigate increasingly granular ethical trade-offs in sociotechnical systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the required computational depth and real-world validation at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of leadership emergence and effectiveness in complex, large-scale human networks using computational modeling and simulation. While leadership studies have traditionally relied on qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, understanding leadership as a systemic phenomenon in rapidly evolving, interconnected environments—such as global organizations or crisis response scenarios—requires analyzing nonlinear interactions across diverse agents and contexts. The research problem centers on identifying how leader-follower dynamics, information diffusion, and decision-making processes co-evolve under conditions of uncertainty, resource constraints, and cultural heterogeneity. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) framework that simulates adaptive leadership behaviors within multi-layered networks, incorporating behavioral theories from psychology, organizational studies, and complexity science. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to realistic group sizes (10^4–10^5 agents), enabling parameter space exploration across leadership styles, communication protocols, and crisis scenarios. Computational methods will integrate network analysis tools, Monte Carlo sampling for stochastic variables, and machine learning techniques to detect emergent patterns in leadership efficacy metrics. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source ABM toolkit for leadership researchers, quantitative insights into resilience-enhancing leadership strategies during systemic disruptions, and evidence-based principles for designing adaptive leadership training modules. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for studying complex human systems while providing actionable knowledge for organizational and community leadership development. The requested HPC allocation will directly support parallelized simulation runs, sensitivity analyses, and large-scale data processing, which are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the universal phenomenon of leadership in human groups. Includes instruction in general or multidisciplinary leadership theory, practice and philosophy.

abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain present complex diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, involving biomechanical, neuromuscular, and psychosocial components. Current clinical paradigms lack robust predictive models to guide personalized interventions, leading to suboptimal patient outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating high-fidelity biomechanical simulations of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) with machine learning-driven analysis of heterogenous clinical datasets to uncover novel biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop a multiscale computational framework that couples finite element analysis (FEA) of mandibular dynamics under varying load conditions with deep learning algorithms trained on multimodal patient data, including dynamic MRI, electromyography, and patient-reported pain metrics. The FEA models will incorporate patient-specific anatomical variations derived from cone-beam CT scans, while recurrent neural networks will analyze temporal patterns in masticatory muscle activity and pain chronification. By simulating over 10,000 biomechanical scenarios across diverse demographic cohorts, the project aims to identify critical thresholds for joint overloading and neuromuscular compensation strategies that predispose individuals to chronic TMD. Concurrently, the machine learning pipeline will stratify patients into mechanistically distinct subtypes based on computational biomarkers, enabling prospective validation of targeted therapies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational biomechanics, neurobiology, and clinical orofacial pain research—a niche not addressed by conventional health sciences domains. The expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source platform for TMD risk stratification, (2) predictive models linking joint mechanics to pain neurobiology, and (3) computational evidence to optimize occlusal appliance design. Successful execution requires HPC capabilities for parallelized FEA, GPU-accelerated neural network training, and large-scale integration of 4D imaging data, all critical to advancing precision medicine in this understudied area of musculoskeletal health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to evaluate, diagnose, and treat of a wide variety of temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and orofacial pain disorders as well as the treatment of sleep apnea and snoring with intraoral appliances. Includes instruction in head and neck anatomy, physical diagnosis and evaluation, orofacial pain, neurobiology of pain and analgesia, and diagnostic radiography.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for generative design in adaptive architectural systems, focusing on optimizing spatial configurations for dynamic environmental and socio-cultural conditions. Traditional architectural design tools struggle to integrate real-time data streams, multi-objective constraints, and emergent behavioral patterns at urban scales, particularly when accounting for rapidly shifting parameters such as climate volatility, population mobility, and resource availability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid methodology combining agent-based modeling, evolutionary algorithms, and graph neural networks to simulate iterative design solutions across temporal and spatial dimensions. The computational pipeline will process heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial information, material performance metrics, and human movement patterns—to generate adaptive architectural prototypes that balance structural efficiency, energy use, and cultural relevance. Key challenges involve scaling graph-based representations of architectural morphologies, parallelizing fitness evaluations for multi-criteria optimization, and maintaining interpretability in AI-driven design outputs. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for dynamic architectural simulation, validated through case studies of transitional urban zones experiencing demographic and environmental pressures. By enabling rapid exploration of design spaces informed by complex, non-linear interactions, this work aims to advance computational architecture beyond static form-finding toward responsive systems capable of addressing 21st-century challenges. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive 3D topology optimizations, training graph networks on terabyte-scale urban datasets, and running comparative analyses across design scenarios—tasks infeasible on conventional workstations. This interdisciplinary effort bridges computational design, urban informatics, and human-centered AI while remaining firmly grounded in architectural innovation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The emergence and persistence of infectious diseases in livestock populations present complex challenges to veterinary medicine, food security, and agricultural economies. This project addresses the critical need to model host-pathogen-environment interactions in bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), a multifactorial syndrome responsible for substantial morbidity and economic losses in cattle. Current experimental models struggle to capture the dynamic interplay between viral and bacterial co-infections, host immune heterogeneity, and environmental stressors such as transportation-induced stress. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of pulmonary immune dynamics with population-scale epidemiological simulations. The ABM component will simulate pathogen spread within alveolar microenvironments under varying immune cell recruitment scenarios, informed by single-cell RNA sequencing data from infected bovine lung tissues. Concurrently, network-based epidemiological models will incorporate real-world herd mobility data and climate variables to predict BRDC outbreaks. These components will be coupled via machine learning surrogates to enable iterative hypothesis testing across scales. The project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the parameter space of 10^6+ agent interactions per simulation, optimize deep learning architectures for data integration, and perform ensemble runs accounting for genomic variability across cattle breeds. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of biomarkers predictive of BRDC progression, validated against longitudinal field data from feedlot cohorts, and (2) a decision-support tool quantifying intervention efficacy under different management practices. By establishing causal links between molecular-scale interactions and herd-level disease patterns, this work will advance precision veterinary approaches for respiratory syndromes while demonstrating how computational immunology can bridge gaps in large-animal clinical research. The developed models will be adaptable to other polymicrobial infections of agricultural significance.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and cognitive dynamics of emergent online communities in decentralized digital platforms, focusing on how ad hoc collectives negotiate shared norms and epistemic frameworks in the absence of centralized governance. As digital interactions increasingly supplant traditional physical communities, understanding the self-organizing mechanisms that underpin trust, conflict resolution, and knowledge validation in these spaces represents a critical social science challenge. The research employs a mixed-methods computational approach, combining large-scale network analysis of real-time interaction data from federated social platforms (e.g., Mastodon, Matrix) with agent-based modeling to simulate consensus-building processes under varying communication constraints.
