High-performance computing resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets of timestamped user interactions, training graph neural networks to detect latent community boundaries, and running parallelized simulations of norm-formation scenarios across diverse synthetic populations. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of emergent governance patterns in decentralized digital spaces, (2) quantitative metrics for predicting community fragmentation or resilience based on early interaction networks, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing epistemic alignment processes in real-time collaboration environments. By bridging computational social science with network theory and cognitive modeling, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding how human social systems adapt to radically decentralized digital environments—a pressing concern as Web3 technologies and AI-mediated communication redefine collective human behavior. Results will inform both theoretical frameworks for studying post-institutional sociality and practical designs for next-generation collaborative platforms.
cip_definition: Any program in general social sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between household consumption patterns and economic volatility through the lens of multi-agent simulation modeling. While traditional consumer economics research relies on aggregated survey data or static econometric models, this study proposes a computational framework to simulate heterogeneous household decision-making under fluctuating economic conditions. The research problem centers on understanding how micro-level consumption behaviors—shaped by variables such as income instability, intergenerational resource sharing, and localized retail market dynamics—aggregate into macro-level economic resilience or fragility. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will develop a scalable agent-based model (ABM) incorporating 1) demographic data from longitudinal household surveys, 2) geospatial retail ecosystem mappings, and 3) stochastic economic shock generators. The computational architecture will parallelize decision trees across 500,000+ autonomous household agents, each with adaptive consumption strategies influenced by machine learning-derived behavioral templates. Key methodological challenges include optimizing memory allocation for real-time market feedback loops and validating emergent phenomena against historical recession/recovery cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive insights into critical thresholds for consumption-driven economic instability and actionable frameworks for adaptive retail business strategies. By bridging computational social science with consumer economics, this work advances theoretical understanding of complex system dynamics in household-market interactions while providing practical tools for business leaders and policymakers in human sciences domains. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of cross-scale interactions between individual decision-making, household networks, and macroeconomic forces within experimentally varied crisis scenarios.
cip_title: Business Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationship between the economy and the consuming individual and family. Includes instruction in consumption theory and practice, the production and distribution of retail goods and services, and the management of business enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to address persistent inefficiencies in high-volume manufacturing systems, particularly those arising from dynamic process interdependencies and unpredictable material behavior, which lead to production bottlenecks, energy waste, and quality inconsistencies. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the complexity of modern computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) environments, especially when integrating real-time sensor data, machine learning-driven quality control, and multi-objective optimization. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining discrete event simulation, finite element analysis (FEA), and reinforcement learning (RL) to model and optimize manufacturing systems at unprecedented resolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations of production line interactions while simultaneously resolving micron-scale material deformation phenomena during machining processes. The computational workflow will integrate ANSYS Mechanical for FEA-based toolpath stress analysis, Python-based RL agents for adaptive scheduling, and GPU-accelerated digital twin environments to evaluate energy consumption and throughput under stochastic demand scenarios. By leveraging distributed memory architectures, we aim to reduce simulation wall-clock time for multi-stage production systems by 85% compared to current single-node benchmarks, enabling rapid iteration of design-for-manufacturing strategies. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for tool wear propagation across heterogeneous machining centers and an open-source optimization toolkit for minimizing thermal distortion in additive manufacturing workflows. This work will directly support industry partnerships focused on sustainable manufacturing, providing actionable insights for reducing scrap rates in aerospace component production by an estimated 22%. The requested resources will also facilitate workforce development by integrating HPC-based case studies into advanced manufacturing courses, training students in cyber-physical system optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the identification and resolution of production problems in the manufacture of products. Includes instruction in machine operations, production line operations, engineering analysis, systems analysis, instrumentation, physical controls, automation, computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), manufacturing planning, quality control, and informational infrastructure.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in computational research on the Albanian language, particularly its Gheg and Tosk dialects. While Albanian’s historical development and dialectal variation have long been subjects of linguistic study, the lack of large-scale computational models limits progress in understanding its structural evolution, sociolinguistic dynamics, and applications in modern contexts. Current tools for Albanian—such as morphological analyzers, dialect classifiers, and diachronic corpora—are underdeveloped compared to those for widely studied languages, hindering interdisciplinary research and practical implementations. This project proposes to develop a suite of NLP-driven resources, including dialect-aware neural models and probabilistic phylogenetic frameworks, to analyze linguistic divergence, contact effects, and standardization processes. Computational workflows will integrate digitized texts, transcribed spoken corpora, and historical manuscripts, with a focus on tokenization challenges posed by orthographic variation in pre-20th century sources. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on distributed Albanian language data (∼10 TB), optimizing dialect classification algorithms via hyperparameter tuning, and simulating language change using agent-based models at scale. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational dialect atlas of Albanian, an annotated diachronic corpus spanning the 15th–21st centuries, and statistically robust reconstructions of sound change trajectories. These resources will enable novel research in Albanian philology, support educational tools for heritage language preservation, and inform policy decisions on language standardization. By bridging computational linguistics and Albanian studies, this project aims to establish a methodological framework adaptable to other under-resourced languages while advancing the program’s mission to expand scholarly and technological engagement with Albanian.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Albanian language. Includes instruction in Albanian/Illyrian philology; Ghegg and Tosk dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The discovery of novel bioactive natural products with therapeutic potential is hindered by the complexity of plant metabolomes and limitations in traditional bioassay-guided isolation methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the identification of medicinally relevant compounds from plant extracts through integrative computational metabolomics and molecular modeling. The research will focus on resolving spectral data from LC-MS/MS and NMR analyses of understudied medicinal plants with ethnobotanical significance, combined with virtual screening against disease-relevant protein targets. A multi-tiered computational workflow will be implemented: (1) Molecular networking of MS/MS spectra using GNPS-platform tools to map compound families and prioritize unknown features; (2) Density functional theory (DFT)-assisted NMR prediction for stereochemical elucidation of complex secondary metabolites; (3) GPU-accelerated molecular docking of in silico-generated compound libraries against validated therapeutic targets in cancer and infectious diseases. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale spectral datasets, quantum chemical calculations for 3D structure optimization, and ensemble docking simulations across multiple target conformations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel lead compounds with predicted bioactivity, improved annotation of plant metabolite databases, and development of machine learning models correlating spectral signatures with pharmacological potential. This computational-phytochemical integration addresses critical bottlenecks in natural product drug discovery by enabling systematic evaluation of chemical diversity while reducing reliance on resource-intensive bioassays. The resource allocation will directly support the training of pharmacy students in computational pharmacognosy methods and advance structure-activity relationship studies for plant-derived medicinal agents. Project results will contribute to both pharmaceutical development and the scientific validation of traditional plant medicines through modern computational approaches.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical mechanisms underpinning plant-parasitic nematode invasion of root systems, a process responsible for billions of dollars in annual agricultural losses. Current understanding of nematode root penetration focuses on biochemical interactions, leaving critical gaps in knowledge about the physical forces and structural adaptations enabling these organisms to breach plant tissues. We propose a computational study integrating high-resolution finite element analysis (FEA) and fluid-structure interaction (FSI) modeling to simulate the dynamic mechanical interplay between nematode stylets (spear-like mouthparts) and root cell walls under varying soil conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 3D simulations of stylet kinematics, stress distribution during penetration, and the role of soil moisture gradients in modulating root tissue resistance. Multiscale models will parameterize stylet morphology from micro-CT scans of economically significant species (e.g., *Meloidogyne incognita*) and incorporate experimentally derived viscoelastic properties of root cells. The simulations will identify mechanical failure thresholds of plant tissues and optimize nematode attack strategies, revealing evolutionary adaptations that enhance parasitic efficiency. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking nematode morphometrics to invasion success, with applications in designing nematode-resistant crop architectures and biomimetic tools for precision agriculture. By bridging biomechanics and parasitology, this work establishes a novel computational paradigm for understanding physically driven host-pathogen interactions, offering translational insights distinct from conventional biochemical control approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between instructional design, learner cognition, and socio-cultural contexts in digital learning environments. A critical challenge in the learning sciences is understanding how real-time, multi-modal data—such as eye-tracking, interaction logs, and physiological responses—can inform adaptive instructional strategies that improve learning outcomes across diverse populations. Current analytical methods struggle to integrate these heterogeneous, high-volume datasets while accounting for temporal dependencies and contextual variables. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework leveraging machine learning (ML) and network analysis to model learning processes at scale. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning models on longitudinal interaction data from 15,000+ learners across three MOOC platforms, incorporating linguistic, behavioral, and assessment metrics. Agent-based simulations will further test hypotheses about how instructional interventions propagate effects in social learning networks. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of unstructured data (video annotations, forum discussions), optimizing hyperparameters for time-series prediction models, and running parallelized simulations of classroom-scale learning communities. Outcomes will include (1) a validated ML pipeline for predicting learner engagement and performance in real time, (2) evidence-based principles for culturally responsive course design, and (3) open-source tools for simulating instructional scenarios. By enabling rapid iteration of virtual learning experiments and large-scale pattern detection, this work aims to advance theoretical models of situated learning while providing practical frameworks for equitable educational technology. The requested GPU nodes and distributed memory architecture are essential for handling memory-intensive natural language processing tasks and complex system simulations that cannot feasibly run on local infrastructure.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the multiple aspects of learning in different environments, including specific aspects of the content to be mastered, cognitive aspects of the student, the instructional environment and materials, the preparation and activities of the instructor, socio-cultural and linguistic components, and assessment outcomes. Includes instruction in the social, organizational, and cultural dynamics of learning; learning and cognition; learning strategies; educational psychology; educational testing and measurement; instructional design and technology; and statistical design of educational research.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of how horticulture therapy interventions mediate physical and mental health outcomes through complex biological, psychological, and environmental interactions. Current research in horticulture therapy is constrained by fragmented datasets and limited computational tools to model the dynamic interplay between plant-derived biochemical stimuli, participant physiology, and therapeutic garden design. To address this gap, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and multi-omics analysis to simulate and predict therapeutic efficacy across diverse populations. Agent-based models will simulate real-time interactions between participants and therapeutic garden environments, incorporating variables such as plant volatile organic compound (VOC) emission rates, microbiome exchanges, and behavioral responses. Machine learning algorithms will analyze longitudinal datasets from clinical trials, including biometric sensor data (e.g., cortisol levels, heart rate variability) and psychological assessments, to identify biomarkers of therapeutic success. Concurrently, genomic and metabolomic data from both plants and participants will be integrated to elucidate molecular pathways underlying observed health outcomes. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations, enabling parallel processing of high-resolution environmental datasets, and training predictive models on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include the development of evidence-based design principles for therapeutic gardens, personalized intervention protocols tailored to specific neurological or physical conditions, and a predictive toolset for optimizing horticulture therapy workflows. This research will establish a foundational computational platform for the field, bridging gaps between empirical horticultural science and clinical practice while fostering data-driven standards for therapeutic efficacy. By quantifying the mechanisms of people-plant interactions, this work aims to expand access to non-pharmacological interventions and improve quality of life for individuals with chronic health challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on plant science and horticulture techniques to achieve measurable physical and mental health outcomes for individuals with physical or mental challenges. Includes instruction in abnormal psychology, adult development and aging, botany, facilities design, horticultural therapy, plant pathology, people-plant relationships, and psychology.

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) is critical for mitigating neurological injury during high-risk surgeries, yet current systems lack robust computational frameworks to integrate multimodal neural signals with real-time predictive analytics. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform for advanced analysis of intraoperative neurophysiological data, including electrocorticography (ECoG), electromyography (EMG), and somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs). The primary research challenge lies in overcoming latency and scalability limitations inherent to existing neuromonitoring workflows, which rely on threshold-based alerts and discrete signal interpretation. These methods lack the capacity to synthesize complex spatial-temporal patterns or anticipate subclinical neural degradation. Our approach combines adaptive signal processing, machine learning (ML)-driven anomaly detection, and biophysical modeling to create a dynamic risk stratification system. HPC resources will be utilized to parallelize computationally intensive tasks, including: (1) real-time preprocessing of high-density neural time series (sampling rates >10 kHz) across multiple modalities, (2) training of graph neural networks (GNNs) to model functional connectivity shifts in cortical-subcortical networks, and (3) Monte Carlo simulations of ischemic cascades in patient-specific vascular models derived from preoperative angiograms. The proposed infrastructure will enable intraoperative prediction of adverse events (e.g., stroke, spinal cord ischemia) with a target latency of <500 ms, exceeding current clinical standards. Anticipated outcomes include a validated computational pipeline for detecting early biomarkers of neurological compromise and a proof-of-concept interface for surgeon feedback. This work bridges gaps between neuroengineering, data science, and surgical practice, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to proactive neuromonitoring. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project addresses critical limitations in processing speed and model complexity that have hindered previous attempts at predictive IONM systems. Successful implementation could reduce postoperative neurological complications by an estimated 15-25% in complex neurosurgical and orthopedic cases, while establishing a scalable framework for integrating multimodal physiological data in time-sensitive clinical environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate the resilience of critical sociotechnical systems in hybrid threat environments—scenarios where physical infrastructure vulnerabilities intersect with disinformation campaigns and cyber-physical attacks. Traditional homeland security risk assessments often treat these domains in isolation, limiting their capacity to predict cascading failures in increasingly interconnected systems. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this project will integrate agent-based modeling, dynamic network analysis, and natural language processing to simulate multi-vector threats across urban transportation networks, energy grids, and digital communication ecosystems. The computational approach will process real-world datasets spanning infrastructure sensor logs, social media activity, and historical incident reports to parameterize threat propagation pathways under varying conditions. Key challenges include scaling graph-based algorithms to model interdependencies across 10^6+ nodes, optimizing real-time sentiment analysis of disinformation trends, and simulating stochastic failure cascades in GPU-accelerated environments. Expected outcomes include a modular simulation platform capable of identifying latent systemic vulnerabilities, stress-testing mitigation strategies, and quantifying the efficacy of cross-domain response protocols. This work addresses a critical gap in homeland security preparedness by providing policymakers and infrastructure operators with tools to anticipate emergent risks at the intersection of physical and informational systems. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology—bridging computational social science, cybersecurity, and infrastructure engineering—offers a novel paradigm for analyzing hybrid threats while remaining distinct from established domains such as public administration or multidisciplinary studies. Successful implementation will advance both theoretical frameworks for complex system resilience and practical strategies for adaptive threat mitigation in evolving risk landscapes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Occupational and environmental health nursing requires evidence-based strategies to address complex interactions between workplace exposures, worker health outcomes, and preventive interventions. This project seeks to develop predictive models for occupational health risk assessment by analyzing multidimensional datasets, including longitudinal electronic health records, environmental sensor data, and occupational exposure registries. A critical challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous data sources—spanning chemical exposure levels, biometric measurements, and work history variables—while accounting for temporal patterns, dose-response relationships, and confounding factors such as comorbidities or non-occupational exposures. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to apply machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks and time-series analysis, to model exposure-health outcome pathways. The project will utilize federated learning approaches to preserve data privacy across collaborating clinical sites while training models on aggregated datasets. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle high-dimensional data (e.g., real-time particulate matter measurements paired with spirometry results) and simulate intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include risk stratification tools to identify workers at elevated risk for respiratory, musculoskeletal, or stress-related conditions, as well as decision support algorithms for personalized preventive care plans. By enabling large-scale analysis of spatiotemporal health patterns, this work will advance occupational health surveillance capabilities and inform targeted workplace safety policies. The requested computing resources are essential for managing memory-intensive simulations, iterative model training, and validation across diverse worker populations, ultimately supporting nurses in optimizing clinical interventions and resource allocation in occupational health practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver nursing health care services to workers and worker populations in clinical settings and at job sites. Includes instruction in public and community health, occupational safety and health, occupational health surveillance, case management, fitness for duty testing, medication, allergies and immunization, emergency and ambulatory care, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize bicycle component durability and performance under dynamic mechanical stress, addressing a critical gap in data-driven repair protocols for modern human-powered vehicles. While traditional bicycle repair relies on empirical techniques, the increasing complexity of materials (e.g., carbon fiber composites, additive-manufactured alloys) and variable usage patterns demands predictive tools to guide maintenance decisions. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in bicycle systems, including stress distribution in frames under load, wear patterns in drivetrain components, and aerodynamic efficiency across riding conditions. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will be implemented at scale to analyze microstructural failures in components, validated against experimental data from strain gauges and wear-testing rigs. A machine learning pipeline will concurrently process terabyte-scale datasets from IoT-enabled bicycles to correlate sensor data (torque, vibration, environmental conditions) with component degradation rates. The computational workflow requires parallelized simulations across thousands of cores to achieve the resolution needed for sub-millimeter defect detection in heterogeneous materials. Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms capable of identifying failure risks 20-30% earlier than current diagnostic methods and a material optimization framework for 3D-printed replacement parts. This research will directly enhance technician training programs by providing evidence-based thresholds for part replacement and lubrication schedules, while the open-source simulation tools developed will enable small repair shops to access advanced diagnostic capabilities. By integrating HPC-driven insights with hands-on repair education, this work bridges the gap between traditional bicycle mechanics and computational engineering, fostering innovation in sustainable transportation technologies.
cip_title: Bicycle Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain bicycles and other human-powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication, adjustments of moving parts, and wheel building.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and cultural evolution of European urban centers between 1500 and 1800, a period marked by rapid demographic growth, economic transformation, and shifting political frameworks. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of urbanization and their correlation with socioeconomic factors—such as trade networks, institutional development, and technological innovation—across diverse regions, including the Mediterranean, Western Europe, and the Baltic. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to synthesize the vast, fragmented datasets required for such comparative analysis, including digitized municipal records, tax registers, migration logs, and cartographic materials. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, geospatial modeling, and network analysis tools to process multilingual archival sources, map demographic shifts, and reconstruct economic interactions at scale. Machine learning classifiers will be trained to categorize qualitative data from civic chronicles and guild records, enabling systematic analysis of cultural narratives alongside quantitative trends. The HPC environment is critical for handling the volume and complexity of these datasets, which include over 10 million structured and unstructured records from 30 repositories, as well as high-resolution georeferenced maps. Expected outcomes include (1) a dynamic, open-access database of urban indicators, (2) visualizations of regional interconnectedness and resource flows, and (3) statistical models testing hypotheses about the role of institutions in mitigating crises like famine or plague. By integrating computational methods with archival research, this project aims to advance transnational perspectives on early modern European history, offering new insights into how cities shaped—and were shaped by—broader societal transformations. The findings will contribute to scholarly debates on state formation, economic resilience, and the longue durée impacts of urbanization, while demonstrating the value of HPC-driven methodologies in historical research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of European society, culture, and institutions from the origins to the present. Includes instruction in European historiography, European history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of microbial metabolic networks for optimizing bioproduction processes in biotechnology. A critical challenge in industrial biotechnology is the design of microbial strains with enhanced capabilities for producing biofuels, pharmaceuticals, or biochemicals. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to strain optimization are time-consuming and costly, while existing computational tools often lack the resolution to predict complex interactions between genetic modifications, metabolic fluxes, and environmental conditions. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs), dynamic flux balance analysis (DFBA), and machine learning to predict strain behavior under industrial bioreactor conditions. The project will utilize HPC resources to perform large-scale parameter sweeps, simulate genetic perturbation scenarios, and train deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics). Key computational workflows will employ parallelized implementations of constraint-based reconstruction and analysis (COBRApy) and molecular dynamics simulations for enzyme engineering. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel gene knockout targets for improving succinic acid production in *Escherichia coli* and a publicly available dataset of simulated metabolic responses to nutrient gradients. This work will directly support downstream experimental validation in our lab’s bioreactor platform, reducing the experimental design cycle by months. By enabling high-resolution modeling of microbial systems, the requested resources will accelerate the development of sustainable biomanufacturing processes, with broader implications for renewable energy and precision fermentation industries. The project also aims to establish best practices for integrating HPC into biotechnology curricula, training students in computational biology tools essential for next-generation biotech careers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of biologists and biotechnologists in research, industrial, and government settings. Includes instruction in fermentation technology, cell culturing, protein purification, biologic synthesis, assaying and testing, quality control, industrial microbiology, bioprocessing, chromatography and bioseparation, genetic technology, laboratory and hazardous materials safety, and computer applications.

abstract: Avionics systems in modern aircraft are increasingly complex, integrating advanced sensors, communication networks, and adaptive control algorithms. Maintaining these systems requires predictive diagnostics and real-time performance analysis, but current methods struggle with the computational demands of processing high-dimensional sensor data and simulating failure scenarios across diverse operating conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable framework for predictive maintenance modeling and fault-tolerant avionics system simulation. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) training machine learning models to detect anomalies in multi-modal sensor streams (e.g., inertial measurement units, radar altimeters, and datalink telemetry) and predict component degradation, and (2) running high-fidelity simulations of avionics hardware-software interactions under environmental stressors such as electromagnetic interference, thermal cycling, and vibration. Computational methods will include parallelized finite element analysis for component stress modeling, federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across maintenance networks, and agent-based simulations of fault propagation in integrated modular avionics architectures. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory processing, the project aims to reduce model training times for large-scale maintenance datasets by 60-75% compared to conventional systems while enabling real-time simulations of aircraft-wide failure scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for predictive maintenance scheduling, a validated library of fault injection models for avionics training systems, and quantitative reliability benchmarks for next-generation aircraft electronics. This work will directly support curriculum modernization in avionics maintenance education while providing actionable strategies to improve fleet readiness and reduce unscheduled downtime in aviation operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft operating, control, and electronic systems. Includes instruction in flight instrumentation, aircraft communications and homing systems, radar and other sensory systems, navigation aids, and specialized systems for various types of civilian and military aircraft.

abstract: Law enforcement agencies face escalating challenges in managing digital evidence and records due to the exponential growth of heterogeneous data sources, including body-worn cameras, IoT devices, and multimedia submissions from the public. Existing record-keeping systems often lack the scalability, interoperability, and security required to handle these datasets efficiently, risking procedural delays, data integrity breaches, and compliance failures. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to optimize evidence lifecycle management through advanced data structuring, predictive analytics, and privacy-preserving automation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will employ graph-based databases to model complex relationships in case files, apply natural language processing (NLP) to automate metadata tagging of unstructured reports, and simulate blockchain-inspired protocols for audit trail integrity. A key innovation involves training federated machine learning models on distributed evidence repositories to identify patterns in storage access and chain-of-custody workflows without centralizing sensitive data. Computational experiments will benchmark system performance under multi-jurisdictional data-sharing scenarios and stress-test encryption schemes against adversarial attacks. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic evidence prioritization, anomaly detection in access logs, and risk-aware storage allocation algorithms. These resources aim to reduce administrative bottlenecks in law enforcement operations, enhance compliance with evolving data privacy regulations, and mitigate vulnerabilities in digital evidence handling. By integrating computational scalability with domain-specific legal and operational constraints, this work seeks to establish a replicable model for modernizing public safety infrastructure in an era of data-driven policing.
cip_title: Law Enforcement Record-Keeping and Evidence Management
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and procedures for managing records in police or other security offices, including storing and retrieving evidence and related data. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, office management, report preparation, organizational software, database software, physical and digital evidence properties, controlled storage and retrieval, investigative file inventories, case management, security systems, and communications skills.

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems face escalating threats from adversarial actors seeking to exploit vulnerabilities in interconnected physical and cyber networks. Traditional risk assessment methods often struggle to model the scale, nonlinear interactions, and cascading failures inherent in modern infrastructure, particularly when addressing coordinated multi-vector attacks. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework to quantify systemic risks and evaluate mitigation strategies for power grids, transportation networks, and communication backbones. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized Monte Carlo simulations that capture probabilistic threat scenarios, dynamic interdependencies between cyber-physical components, and adaptive attacker-defender interactions. Computational models will integrate real-world infrastructure topology data, machine learning-driven anomaly detection algorithms, and game-theoretic decision engines to simulate threat propagation under varying defense postures. Key innovations include the creation of a multi-resolution modeling architecture to balance granularity with computational tractability, and the incorporation of adversarial reinforcement learning agents to stress-test infrastructure resilience. Expected outcomes include (1) vulnerability heatmaps identifying critical failure pathways across infrastructure sectors, (2) quantitative evaluation of defense-in-depth strategies under resource constraints, and (3) predictive metrics for infrastructure robustness against emerging attack vectors. The HPC implementation will enable unprecedented simulation scale, modeling infrastructure networks with >10^6 interdependent nodes while maintaining sub-second time resolution for cyber-physical event cascades. Results will directly inform national infrastructure protection standards and provide decision-support tools for prioritizing security investments. This work advances computational homeland security capabilities by creating a validated platform for infrastructure risk analysis that accounts for modern threat landscapes’ complexity, adaptability, and cross-domain impacts.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing complex, multi-domain systems under uncertainty, with applications in industrial operations and supply chain management. A critical challenge in systems engineering lies in coordinating interdependent subsystems—such as logistics networks, production workflows, and human resource allocations—while accounting for stochastic demand, resource variability, and dynamic constraints. Existing methods often simplify these interdependencies or rely on deterministic assumptions, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios. To address this gap, the research integrates stochastic optimization, agent-based simulation, and machine learning techniques within a high-performance computing (HPC) environment. The computational approach will employ mixed-integer programming and Monte Carlo methods to model uncertainty, coupled with parallelized metaheuristics to efficiently explore large solution spaces. Agent-based models will simulate interactions between subsystems, capturing emergent behaviors in logistics and production systems. The HPC infrastructure will enable iterative scenario testing across heterogeneous parameters, including demand fluctuations, equipment failures, and sustainability constraints (e.g., energy use, waste reduction). Expected outcomes include a modular optimization toolkit for designing resilient industrial systems, validated through case studies in manufacturing and distribution networks. The project will quantify trade-offs between cost, robustness, and sustainability metrics, providing actionable insights for decision-makers. By leveraging distributed computing architectures, the framework will scale to systems with 10^4–10^5 variables, surpassing the capabilities of conventional solvers. Results will advance methodologies in systems engineering by bridging gaps between prescriptive optimization and adaptive, data-driven modeling. The resource allocation request supports GPU-accelerated simulations, large-memory nodes for in-memory data processing, and high-throughput job scheduling to manage concurrent optimization runs. This work aligns with industrial engineering priorities in operational efficiency and resource allocation, with potential applications in healthcare logistics, smart manufacturing, and circular economy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems solutions to a wide variety of engineering problems, including the integration of human, physical, energy, communications, management, and information requirements as needed, and the application of requisite analytical methods to specific situations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the linguistic and structural evolution of rabbinic responsa literature (She’elot u-Teshuvot) across temporal, geographic, and cultural boundaries. While traditional scholarship in Rabbinical Studies has focused on manual close reading of these legal-ethical texts, the sheer volume of material—spanning over 1,500 years and tens of thousands of documents—presents a barrier to systemic analysis of patterns in halachic reasoning, rhetorical strategies, and cross-cultural influence. The project addresses this gap by developing a computational pipeline to process digitized responsa in Hebrew and Aramaic, integrating natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for rabbinic textual structures (e.g., citation chains, argument-counterargument frameworks) with geospatial-temporal network analysis. Custom algorithms will trace the diffusion of legal concepts through Jewish diaspora communities, identify syntactic markers of cultural adaptation in ritual guidance, and quantify shifts in ethical priorities relative to historical crises such as forced migrations or technological disruptions. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on non-standard orthography and abbreviations in manuscript sources, running large-scale graph analyses of citation networks, and simulating probabilistic models of decision-tree influences across rabbinic schools. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access annotated corpus of 10,000+ responsa enriched with computational metadata, 2) visualization tools mapping doctrinal development against external historical datasets, and 3) quantitative frameworks to contextualize contemporary rabbinic discourse within longitudinal patterns of legal-ethical reasoning. By bridging computational humanities and rabbinic textual tradition, this work aims to provide scholars and religious practitioners with new methodologies for understanding Judaism’s adaptive legal-ethical systems while preserving the interpretive nuance central to Rabbinical Studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as Rabbis. Includes instruction in Talmud, Halacha, Liturgy and Rituals, Rabbinical Thought, Jewish Ethics, Jewish Education, Pastoral Counseling and Homiletics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in process safety risk assessment by developing advanced computational models to simulate complex accident scenarios in high-risk industrial environments. Traditional risk analysis methods often rely on static datasets and simplified assumptions, limiting their ability to predict cascading failures or dynamic interactions between human, technical, and environmental factors. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating probabilistic risk assessment, real-time sensor data, and machine learning to model nonlinear accident pathways in chemical processing, energy production, and hazardous material storage systems. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale Monte Carlo simulations that account for spatial-temporal variables, equipment degradation patterns, and human operator responses under stress conditions. Key computational components include agent-based modeling of workforce interactions, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of chemical release dispersion, and Bayesian network analysis for updating risk probabilities with streaming operational data. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive toolkit capable of identifying latent risks in process designs, optimizing safety-critical control parameters, and quantifying the effectiveness of proposed mitigation strategies under diverse failure modes. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing of rare but catastrophic events—such as multi-equipment cascade failures or extreme weather impacts—this work will provide actionable insights for designing inherently safer processes while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. The resulting models and datasets will be shared with industrial partners through an open-access portal, fostering collaboration between academic researchers and process safety practitioners. Successful implementation of this project has the potential to transform risk management practices across multiple sectors, ultimately reducing workplace injuries, environmental harm, and economic losses associated with process safety incidents.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing methods to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in design for injury prevention, engineering for process safety, environmental psychology, function-based risk analysis, fundamentals of industrial engineering, operations research, probability and statistics, risk assessment and reduction, and safety engineering.

abstract: Understanding the evolutionary relationships among taxa is a fundamental challenge in systematic biology, particularly when conflicting phylogenetic signals arise from incomplete lineage sorting, hybridization, or convergent evolution. This project seeks to resolve persistent uncertainties in the phylogeny of [specific clade or group], a lineage marked by rapid diversification and complex biogeographical histories. Current morphological and molecular datasets yield conflicting topologies, impeding taxonomic clarity and hindering downstream analyses of trait evolution and biogeographic patterns. To address this, we propose a computationally intensive approach integrating genome-scale data with mechanistic models of lineage diversification. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze ultraconserved elements (UCEs) and transcriptome datasets from over 500 specimens, representing 90% of the extant diversity in the clade. Phylogenetic inference will employ Bayesian and maximum-likelihood frameworks (e.g., ExaBayes, IQ-TREE) to evaluate concatenated and coalescent-based species trees, while accounting for heterotachy and site-specific rate variation. Model testing will utilize stepping-stone sampling and machine learning-driven partitioning schemes to optimize parameter space exploration. To assess robustness, we will simulate trait evolution under alternative topologies using agent-based models in SLiM and compare empirical biogeographic data against these outputs. The scale of data—terabases of sequence data, thousands of loci, and complex hierarchical models—necessitates parallelized computation, extensive memory nodes, and GPU acceleration for likelihood calculations. Successful resolution of these relationships will directly inform taxonomic revisions under the International Code of Phylogenetic Nomenclature, clarify historical biogeographic pathways linked to [specific geological/climatic event], and provide a framework for predicting lineage vulnerability to contemporary environmental change. All pipelines and optimized code will be made publicly available via a dedicated repository, enhancing reproducibility in systematics. This project underscores the critical role of HPC in tackling phylogenomic complexity, advancing both methodological and empirical frontiers in evolutionary biology.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate solvent-mediated reaction dynamics in complex chemical systems using high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome current limitations in simulating multi-scale interactions. While solvent effects critically influence reaction pathways and kinetics, traditional computational methods struggle to reconcile quantum mechanical accuracy with the statistical sampling required for solvated environments, particularly for systems involving large biomolecules or ionic solutions. The research will employ hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations combined with enhanced sampling techniques, such as metadynamics and path-integral molecular dynamics, to model solvent reorganization and proton transfer processes in enzymatic and aqueous-phase reactions. These simulations will integrate density functional theory (DFT) for electronic structure calculations with classical force fields, enabling atomistic resolution of reactive events while accounting for long-range solvent polarization and entropy effects. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated HPC resources to perform large-scale parallel simulations across multiple time and length scales, with data-driven approaches optimizing reaction coordinate analysis. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into solvent-driven catalytic efficiency in enzymes like carbonic anhydrase and the role of water networks in acid-base equilibria. The resulting datasets and adaptive sampling protocols will advance predictive modeling of solvent effects on reaction rates and selectivity, with applications in biocatalyst design and sustainable chemistry. By addressing the computational bottleneck of sampling solvation dynamics at quantum accuracy, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for simulating chemically complex environments, bridging gaps between theoretical models and experimental observables in physical chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of understanding and predicting the behavior of chemical systems ranging from nuclear particles to atoms, molecules, clusters, biological materials and macroscopic assemblies. Includes instruction in quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, reaction dynamics, group theory, collision theory, and polymer science.

abstract: Chronic wound healing remains a critical challenge in clinical medicine, with persistent inflammation, infection, and impaired tissue regeneration contributing to prolonged recovery, high healthcare costs, and patient morbidity. Current therapeutic strategies lack precision due to incomplete understanding of the dynamic molecular, cellular, and biomechanical interactions within wound microenvironments. This project proposes a computational approach to model the multiscale processes underlying chronic wound pathophysiology and predict patient-specific healing trajectories. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate high-dimensional clinical data—including longitudinal multi-omics (transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic), microbiomic, and host immune profiles—with spatially resolved tissue biomechanics simulations. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular interactions (e.g., fibroblast-macrophage crosstalk, microbial dynamics), while finite element analysis will map mechanical stress distributions in wound beds. Deep learning architectures will be trained on these synthetic datasets alongside real-world electronic health records to identify predictive biomarkers and optimize treatment parameters. The computational pipeline will be validated against prospective clinical cohorts of diabetic foot ulcers and pressure injuries. By leveraging HPC capabilities for parallelized simulation, large-scale parameter optimization, and federated learning across heterogeneous datasets, this work aims to uncover mechanistic drivers of healing stagnation and generate actionable insights for personalized wound care. Expected outcomes include a predictive decision-support tool for clinicians, novel biomarkers for targeted therapies, and mechanistic hypotheses to guide wet-lab experimentation. This resource-intensive computational framework addresses a critical gap in wound care research, where traditional reductionist approaches fail to capture systemic complexity. Successful implementation could transform therapeutic paradigms, reducing healing times and healthcare burdens for millions of patients globally.
cip_definition: Research focused on Wound Care

abstract: The development of novel therapeutics requires precise understanding of drug-target interactions, metabolic pathways, and off-target effects, yet conventional experimental methods remain resource-intensive and slow. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to accelerate the rational design of small-molecule inhibitors targeting kinase enzymes implicated in neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. Kinases are critical regulators of cellular signaling, but their structural plasticity and conserved ATP-binding sites complicate selective drug design. We propose an integrative computational strategy combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, and machine learning (ML)-guided virtual screening to map allosteric binding pockets and optimize lead compounds. Large-scale MD simulations (μs-ms timescales) will model conformational dynamics of target kinases, while FEP workflows will quantify binding affinities of designed analogs. An ML model trained on kinase-ligand interaction datasets will predict selectivity and toxicity profiles, enabling prioritization of candidates for synthesis. The HPC environment is essential to manage the computational load of these workflows, which involve millions of atomic trajectories and iterative quantum mechanical calculations. Expected outcomes include the identification of 3-5 high-affinity, selective kinase inhibitors with reduced off-target activity, as well as publicly accessible datasets of kinase conformational states and binding energetics. This work will advance methodologies for targeting structurally dynamic proteins and provide a framework for computationally driven drug discovery in understudied kinase families. By integrating biophysical simulations with data-driven prioritization, the project aims to reduce experimental attrition rates and accelerate the translation of therapeutic candidates into preclinical testing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemistry to the study of biologically and clinically active substances, biological and pharmacological interactions, and the development of associated research methods, techniques, and clinical trial procedures. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular graphics, rational drug design, toxicology, molecular biology, pharmacology, enzyme mechanisms, receptor theory, neurochemistry, drug metabolism, drug synthesis, biological mechanisms of drug action, research tools and techniques, and laboratory safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time control and fault tolerance in industrial automation systems through high-fidelity simulation and machine learning (ML)-enhanced modeling. Modern automated systems, such as those integrating programmable logic controllers (PLCs), sensor-actuator networks, and robotic manipulators, require rigorous testing under diverse operational scenarios to ensure reliability. However, physical prototyping and real-world validation are cost-prohibitive and limited in scalability. This research proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-physics automation environments, including hydraulic, pneumatic, and electromechanical subsystems. The project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) for stress and thermal modeling of mechanical components, coupled with discrete-event simulations to replicate PLC logic and communication latency in distributed control systems. Additionally, reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to optimize control policies for adaptive fault recovery and energy efficiency. Key outcomes include predictive models for system degradation under dynamic loads, a digital twin platform for rapid prototyping of automation workflows, and data-driven recommendations for hardware-software co-design. The computational demands of parallelized simulations, real-time sensor data integration, and large-scale ML training necessitate access to HPC resources with GPU acceleration and distributed memory architectures. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for reducing downtime in manufacturing systems and enhance the scalability of automation solutions for small-to-medium enterprises. This work aligns with the Automation Engineer Technology program’s focus on practical, industry-relevant tools by advancing simulation-driven design methodologies accessible to engineering technologists.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, installing, calibrating, modifying and maintaining automated systems. Includes instruction in computer systems; electronics and instrumentation; programmable logic controllers (PLCs); electric, hydraulic and pneumatic control systems; actuator and sensor systems; process control; robotics; applications to specific industrial tasks; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in practical and vocational nursing education and practice through advanced computational modeling of patient care scenarios. A central problem in nursing training and clinical decision-making is the lack of personalized, real-time tools to simulate complex patient interactions, particularly for high-acuity cases requiring rapid intervention. Existing educational models often rely on static scenarios, limiting students’ exposure to dynamic physiological changes or unpredictable care environments. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The platform will integrate multi-modal data from electronic health records, wearable sensors, and nursing workflow studies to generate adaptive patient avatars with physiologically accurate responses to interventions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on clinical datasets to model patient trajectories under varying care strategies, while Monte Carlo methods will simulate probabilistic outcomes of nursing actions. The computational intensity of parallelized scenario generation and real-time feedback systems necessitates HPC infrastructure for both model training and deployment. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation framework capable of hosting 10,000+ concurrent users, enabling scalable training for nursing students and continuing education for practicing vocational nurses. This work will directly enhance clinical preparedness by quantifying the impact of nursing decisions on patient safety metrics such as fall risk reduction and early sepsis recognition. By providing data-driven insights into competency gaps, the project aims to establish new standards for evidence-based nursing education while reducing reliance on resource-intensive live simulations. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools tailored for nursing programs, fostering broader adoption of computational methods in healthcare training.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing hybrid marine propulsion systems through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations in simulating dynamic, multi-physics interactions. Hybrid systems combining diesel, electric, and energy storage technologies are increasingly vital for reducing emissions and improving efficiency in maritime operations. However, existing models struggle to capture transient behaviors, thermal-electrical coupling, and wear patterns under variable loads, leading to suboptimal designs and operational risks. To resolve this, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion and exhaust analysis, finite element modeling (FEM) for mechanical stress prediction in engine components, and machine learning (ML) to correlate sensor data with system degradation. These workflows will be coupled via a co-simulation architecture to model real-world operating scenarios, including extreme weather and rapid load shifts. HPC resources are essential due to the need for high-fidelity, parallelized simulations spanning milliseconds to years of operational time, requiring iterative optimization of 10,000+ parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for hybrid marine propulsion systems, predictive maintenance algorithms to extend component lifespans, and design guidelines for emission reduction. The project directly supports the Marine Engineering Technology program’s focus on shipboard system optimization by providing students and researchers with tools to explore next-generation propulsion architectures. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation templates and industry partnerships, advancing workforce training in maritime sustainability. This work fills a critical gap in scalable computational methods tailored to marine energy systems, distinct from terrestrial or aerospace applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in shipboard mechanical and electrical engineering and the maintenance and operation of marine engines, including gas, diesel, and steam engines. Includes instruction in automation, diesel-powered systems, electrical circuits and systems, engine performance, hydraulics, manufacturing, motor-powered systems, refrigeration and air-conditioning, steam-powered systems, and welding.

abstract: Radiation therapy is a cornerstone of cancer treatment, requiring precise delivery of therapeutic doses to tumor volumes while minimizing exposure to surrounding healthy tissues. Current treatment planning systems rely on simplified dose calculation algorithms and manual optimization processes, which can lead to suboptimal plans in complex anatomical scenarios. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for automated, patient-specific radiation therapy treatment planning, integrating Monte Carlo dose simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization. The research problem centers on addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in Monte Carlo methods—which provide gold-standard dose accuracy but are prohibitively resource-intensive—and the need for adaptive planning that accounts for interfraction anatomical changes. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo photon transport simulations (using tools such as GATE/Geant4) with deep reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively optimize beam angles, weights, and collimator configurations. High-fidelity patient datasets, including 4D CT imaging and radiobiological parameters, will be processed through this pipeline. The HPC resources will enable parallel execution of thousands of simulated treatment scenarios, coupled with distributed training of neural networks to identify Pareto-optimal plans balancing target coverage, organ-at-risk sparing, and delivery efficiency. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework capable of generating clinically acceptable treatment plans within 30 minutes—a 10x improvement over conventional workflows—while maintaining dosimetric accuracy within 2% of ground-truth Monte Carlo predictions. This work has significant potential to advance personalized radiotherapy by enabling real-time adaptive planning and dose escalation strategies for radioresistant tumors. The computational infrastructure will also support the creation of a public repository of simulated treatment planning challenges, fostering collaboration across medical physics and radiation oncology communities.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurocognitive and psychosomatic mechanisms underlying transpersonal counseling interventions, with a focus on therapeutic trance and meditative practices, to advance evidence-based frameworks for spiritual psychology. Despite growing interest in integrating spiritual systems into counseling, there remains a critical gap in understanding how these practices modulate consciousness, emotional regulation, and somatic responses at scale. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets, including electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and qualitative self-report data from participants engaged in guided therapeutic trance and mindfulness-based rituals. Agent-based modeling will simulate collective consciousness dynamics in group healing practices, while machine learning pipelines will identify patterns linking specific interventions to psychospiritual outcomes (e.g., transcendent experiences, emotional integration). A novel computational framework will be developed to map transient states of altered consciousness during rituals, correlating neural oscillations with phenomenological reports. The project’s computational demands arise from processing high-resolution temporal neurophysiological data (≈10 TB across 200 participants), running parallelized simulations of consciousness networks, and training transformer models on qualitative narratives to decode spiritual meaning-making. Expected outcomes include predictive models of intervention efficacy, optimized protocols for personalized transpersonal counseling, and a publicly accessible database of annotated spiritual practice biomarkers. By bridging first-person experiential data with third-person computational analysis, this work aims to establish empirical foundations for spiritual psychology while respecting its phenomenological complexity, ultimately enhancing the rigor and accessibility of transpersonal approaches in applied counseling contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to pursue spiritual and psychological practices for counseling. Includes instruction in emotional intelligence, expressive movement, healing practices and rituals, human consciousness, movement and meditation, psychosomatic connection, spiritual systems and wellness, transpersonal counseling, and therapeutic trance.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in zoonotic and livestock pathogens poses a critical challenge to veterinary medicine and public health. Current methods for predicting resistance patterns and optimizing treatment protocols in animals are limited by the scale and complexity of genomic, epidemiological, and pharmacological datasets. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to predict AMR emergence in veterinary pathogens and evaluate targeted intervention strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-omics data (whole-genome sequencing, metagenomics) from bovine and porcine clinical isolates with pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models to identify genetic determinants of resistance and simulate drug efficacy under varying dosing regimens. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on curated datasets spanning 10,000+ pathogen genomes and associated clinical metadata to predict resistance phenotypes from genotypic signatures. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will characterize interactions between veterinary antimicrobials and mutated bacterial targets, enabling atomistic insights into resistance mechanisms. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro susceptibility testing data from partner veterinary diagnostic labs. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for AMR risk stratification in livestock populations, (2) optimized treatment guidelines for common veterinary pathogens, and (3) an open-access framework for rapid analysis of emerging resistance patterns. By bridging large-scale genomic data with clinical decision-making, this work aims to enhance evidence-based antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary practice while providing training opportunities for pre-veterinary students in computational biology methods. The proposed HPC resources are essential for managing petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing molecular simulations across multiple nodes, and reducing runtime for iterative model training from weeks to days.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in veterinary medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community health outcomes through the development of predictive models for disease spread and intervention efficacy in underserved populations. Public health nurses play a critical role in mitigating health disparities, yet resource allocation decisions are often constrained by limited access to real-time, spatially resolved data and computational tools capable of modeling complex social determinants of health. The research problem centers on optimizing community-level interventions—such as vaccination campaigns, health education initiatives, and chronic disease management programs—by integrating dynamic demographic, environmental, and behavioral data into actionable predictive frameworks. Current models lack granularity in representing transient populations, cultural health practices, and overlapping risk factors, which are essential for tailoring interventions in rural and urban settings. To address this gap, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) techniques to simulate population-level health behaviors and forecast intervention outcomes under varying resource scenarios. ABM will capture individual interactions within community networks, while ML algorithms will analyze longitudinal electronic health records, geospatial data, and socioeconomic indicators to identify high-risk clusters and prioritize outreach. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across large, heterogeneous populations and iterating thousands of parameter combinations to assess robustness. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework to guide public health agencies in deploying nurses and materials efficiently, particularly in regions with limited infrastructure. The project will also generate open-access tools for real-time scenario testing, enabling community health workers to adapt strategies during emerging crises. By bridging computational innovation with frontline nursing practice, this work aims to reduce preventable hospitalizations, improve health equity, and strengthen evidence-based decision-making in resource-constrained environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to promote health and provide preventive and curative nursing services for groups or communities under the supervision of a public health agency. Includes instruction in community and rural health, family therapy and intervention, disease prevention, health education, and community health assessment.

abstract: The integration of alternative and complementary medicine (ACM) into modern healthcare systems is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of many therapies, particularly those involving multi-component herbal formulations or non-pharmacological interventions. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the complex biochemical and physiological interactions underlying ACM modalities. Current challenges include the combinatorial complexity of herbal compounds, the dynamic nature of biofield therapies (e.g., acupuncture, energy healing), and the need to analyze multi-omics datasets from clinical studies of ACM interventions. We propose a computational pipeline combining molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning-based network pharmacology, and multiscale biophysical modeling to investigate two primary foci: (1) the polypharmacology of Traditional Chinese Medicine herbal formulations in modulating neuro-immuno-endocrine pathways, and (2) the systemic effects of bioelectrical interventions on cellular redox states. Molecular docking and free energy calculations will be performed on GPU-accelerated nodes to screen >10,000 natural compound-target pairs, while ensemble simulations will characterize time-dependent interactions in representative herbal extract mixtures. For biofield modeling, finite element methods will simulate electromagnetic field interactions with ion channels and cytoskeletal structures across spatial scales. The required computational resources include access to parallelized CPU clusters for long-timescale simulations (≥1ms), high-memory nodes for genome-scale metabolic network analyses, and secure storage for integrating proteomics/transcriptomics data from collaborating clinical sites. Expected outcomes include predictive models of ACM therapy efficacy, identification of synergistic herbal combinations, and quantitative frameworks for personalizing energy-based therapies. This work will establish computational foundations for evidence-based integration of ACM modalities while advancing methodologies for studying complex, system-level healthcare interventions.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, Other
