Includes instruction in general circulation patterns, weather phenomena, atmospheric predictability, parameterization, numerical and statistical analysis, large- and mesoscale phenomena, kinematic structures, precipitation processes, and forecasting techniques.

abstract: The increasing availability of large-scale genomic data in clinical genetics presents significant challenges in efficiently analyzing and interpreting genetic variants to provide timely diagnoses and personalized management strategies. Current computational approaches often struggle with the scale and complexity of whole-genome sequencing datasets, particularly when integrating multi-omics data or modeling gene-environment interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable pipelines for variant prioritization, pathogenicity prediction, and genotype-phenotype correlation. We will employ machine learning algorithms trained on diverse population datasets to improve the identification of clinically actionable variants, including structural variants and non-coding regulatory elements. Advanced computational workflows will be implemented to enable parallel processing of genomic data across thousands of cases, significantly reducing analysis time while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Additionally, we will utilize HPC capabilities to perform large-scale simulations of genetic inheritance patterns in family-based studies, enhancing our ability to provide precise recurrence risk estimates. The integration of epigenetic profiling data and electronic health records through graph-based analytics will further elucidate the clinical relevance of rare variants. Expected outcomes include the development of optimized computational frameworks that accelerate diagnostic workflows, improve variant interpretation accuracy by ≥30% compared to existing methods, and enable discovery of novel disease-associated loci. These advancements will directly enhance clinical decision-making for genetic disorders, reduce time-to-diagnosis for rare diseases, and inform targeted counseling strategies. The requested computing resources will also support the creation of open-access tools for the clinical genetics community, facilitating broader implementation of precision medicine approaches in routine care.
cip_definition: Research on how to provide comprehensive diagnostic, management, and counseling services for individuals and families at risk for clinical disorders with a genetic basis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize psychosocial intervention strategies for patients with complex chronic illnesses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal clinical and social determinant data. While clinical social workers routinely assess psychosocial risk factors—such as housing instability, caregiver support, and health literacy—these variables are rarely systematically integrated with biomedical data to forecast patient outcomes. The research addresses this gap by analyzing de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 250,000+ patients, including structured diagnostic codes, unstructured social work notes, and community resource utilization patterns. A hybrid natural language processing (NLP) pipeline will extract latent psychosocial stressors from clinical narratives, while graph neural networks model dynamic interactions between medical comorbidities, care access barriers, and intervention timing. Computational challenges include scaling transformer-based architectures to process longitudinal patient narratives and simulating intervention impact via agent-based models calibrated to real-world social work workflows. The HPC environment is critical for training large language models on unstructured text corpora and running ensemble predictive simulations across diverse demographic subgroups. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated risk stratification tool identifying patients likely to benefit from proactive social work interventions, (2) quantitative evidence linking specific intervention sequences to reduced hospital readmissions in high-risk populations, and (3) an open-source framework for simulating resource allocation trade-offs in safety-net health systems. By computationally formalizing decision-making processes in clinical social work, this work aims to advance precision care coordination while providing a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into psychosocial research domains traditionally underserved by computational methods.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the specialized professional practice of social work, in collaboration with other health care professionals, in hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in social work, psychiatric case work, clinical interviewing techniques, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient testing and evaluation, patient and family counseling, social rehabilitation, patient care planning, record-keeping, and support services liaison.

abstract: The growing complexity of computational workflows in commercial photography, driven by ultra-high-resolution imaging (8K+), multi-spectral capture, and AI-enhanced post-processing, has exposed critical limitations in conventional computing infrastructure. This project addresses the challenge of processing terabyte-scale visual datasets while maintaining artistic fidelity and meeting industry turnaround expectations. Current methods for tasks such as neural style transfer, computational lighting simulation, and batch processing of RAW files become prohibitively slow when handling modern medium-format digital captures or frame-accurate video sequences. We propose deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a hybrid pipeline combining distributed GPU rendering, containerized machine learning workflows, and memory-optimized preprocessing nodes. The research will focus on three key areas: 1) Parallel implementation of non-destructive editing operations across massive image stacks using PyTorch and OpenCL, 2) Photorealistic virtual staging through real-time ray tracing accelerated by multi-GPU architectures, and 3) Semantic segmentation of commercial product imagery at scale using vision transformers fine-tuned on proprietary datasets. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce processing times for complex compositing workflows by 70-90% compared to desktop workstations while enabling previously impractical techniques like iterative generative AI refinement across 10,000+ image campaigns. Outcomes will include optimized algorithms for photographic applications, performance benchmarks for heterogeneous computing clusters in visual media production, and a reproducible framework for cloud-native photography workflows. This work advances the integration of computational arts methodologies within commercial practice, providing artists with tools to push creative boundaries while maintaining technical feasibility for client-driven projects. The resource allocation will directly support both algorithmic development and large-scale testing using real-world datasets from active industry collaborations.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: Agricultural productivity faces mounting challenges from climate variability, emerging pests, and shifting disease pressures, necessitating advanced computational tools to optimize resilience and yield. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that integrate genomic, environmental, and agronomic data for precision crop management. The research focuses on analyzing complex interactions between plant genotypes, pathogen evolution, and dynamic environmental conditions, which exceed the capacity of standard computing infrastructure due to the scale and heterogeneity of datasets. We will employ machine learning frameworks, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), to process multispectral satellite imagery, soil sensor data, and genomic sequences from staple crops such as wheat and soybean. These models will be trained to identify genetic markers associated with stress tolerance and predict disease outbreak risks under projected climate scenarios. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model pest population dynamics and spread patterns across diverse agricultural landscapes. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, stochastic parameter sampling, and iterative optimization of predictive algorithms. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for recommending region-specific crop varieties, planting schedules, and integrated pest management strategies. This work will directly support agricultural extension services and policymakers in mitigating yield losses while reducing reliance on broad-spectrum agrochemicals. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to advance translational agriculture through data-driven decision tools, fostering climate adaptation and food security. Results will be disseminated via open-access platforms to ensure accessibility for stakeholders in public agricultural services.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general agricultural sciences and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Therapeutic applications of targeted radionuclide therapy (TRT) require precise dosimetry to maximize tumor control while sparing healthy tissues. Current clinical dose estimation methods often rely on simplified analytical models that inadequately capture patient-specific anatomical variability, heterogeneous radionuclide biodistribution, and radiation transport phenomena at sub-organ scales. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, patient-specific dosimetry framework using Monte Carlo (MC) simulations to address these limitations. The primary research problem lies in overcoming the computational barriers to performing full-body, time-resolved MC dose calculations that integrate dynamic biokinetic data, high-resolution anatomical imaging, and detailed radiation transport physics. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute GPU-accelerated MC simulations (using tools such as GATE/Geant4) on voxelized phantoms derived from patient CT/MRI datasets. Biokinetic models of radiopharmaceutical distribution, informed by serial SPECT/CT imaging, will be coupled with radiation transport simulations to model dose deposition over time. A sensitivity analysis will quantify uncertainties introduced by approximations in tissue composition, radionuclide redistribution, and photon/electron interactions. The project will validate simulations against physical phantom measurements and clinical dosimetry data. Successful implementation will yield a scalable pipeline for generating 3D dose maps with sub-millimeter resolution, enabling the identification of dose-response thresholds for normal tissues and tumors. Expected outcomes include optimized TRT planning protocols for prostate cancer and neuroendocrine tumor patients, reducing toxicity risks while improving tumor targeting. This work will establish a foundational computational resource for advancing personalized radionuclide therapy, with broader implications for radiopharmaceutical development and radiation safety protocol refinement. The requested HPC allocation is critical due to the project’s scope: an estimated 200,000 core-hours are required to simulate 50 patient cases with multiple timepoints, necessitating parallelized workflows across high-memory nodes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the therapeutic and diagnostic applications of radionuclides (except those used in sealed sources for therapeutic purposes); and in the use of equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: Mental health counseling relies on nuanced interpersonal dynamics to drive therapeutic outcomes, yet the relationship between counselor language patterns and client progress remains poorly quantified. This project proposes a computational linguistics framework to analyze therapeutic interactions at scale, aiming to identify linguistic markers predictive of clinical improvement in short-term counseling contexts. The research problem centers on the lack of empirically validated, real-time decision-support tools for counselors working with clients experiencing acute emotional crises. Current manual coding methods for session analysis are labor-intensive and fail to capture complex temporal patterns in dialogue. To address this, we will develop machine learning models trained on anonymized transcript datasets from diverse counseling sessions (n ≈ 50,000 interactions), incorporating paralinguistic features, topic trajectories, and therapeutic alliance metrics. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: 1) Processing natural language data through transformer-based architectures to model counselor-client turn-taking dynamics, 2) Running parallelized simulations of conversational pathways using reinforcement learning to optimize intervention timing, and 3) Conducting high-dimensional clustering of linguistic phenotypes across demographic and diagnostic subgroups. The computational pipeline will integrate psycholinguistic theory with deep learning techniques, requiring iterative training of neural networks on GPU clusters to handle the temporal and contextual complexity of therapeutic dialogues. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of linguistic adaptation strategies that correlate with measured client outcomes, visualized through dynamic interaction maps. This work bridges counseling psychology with computational social science, potentially yielding (a) evidence-based guidelines for language pattern optimization in crisis interventions, (b) an open-source toolkit for real-time session analysis, and (c) novel metrics for evaluating counselor training efficacy. By establishing quantitative links between micro-level linguistic choices and macro-level therapeutic success, this research could transform competency standards in mental health counseling while maintaining strict ethical safeguards for client privacy and clinical judgment autonomy.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide evaluations, referrals, and short-term counseling services to help people prevent or remediate personal problems, conflicts, and emotional crises. Includes instruction in human development, psychopathology, individual and group counseling, personality theory, career assessment, patient screening and referral, observation and testing techniques, interviewing skills, professional standards and ethics, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis of multiscale electrophysiological data in clinical neurodiagnostics, with a focus on improving the detection and interpretation of subtle neurological biomarkers. Current electroneurodiagnostic (END) workflows rely heavily on visual inspection of electroencephalographic (EEG) and evoked potential (EP) recordings, a process limited by inter-rater variability and the challenge of identifying transient or spatially diffuse anomalies in high-dimensional data. The research problem centers on developing automated, adaptive algorithms capable of integrating raw EEG/EP signals with patient-specific clinical metadata (e.g., medication history, comorbidities) to predict neurological dysfunction earlier and with greater specificity. Computational methods will combine time-frequency analysis, graph-based network modeling of neural connectivity, and hybrid machine learning architectures (convolutional neural networks coupled with attention mechanisms) trained on a curated dataset of >10,000 hours of annotated recordings from diverse neurological pathologies. HPC resources are critical for three phases: 1) parallel processing of long-term monitoring data to establish baseline population models, 2) iterative optimization of dynamic neural networks that adapt to individual patient electrophysiology, and 3) real-time simulation of clinical deployment scenarios requiring sub-second latency for potential intraoperative applications. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework that quantifies spatially distributed neural network instability—a proposed precursor to overt seizures and post-traumatic encephalopathies—with demonstrable improvements over conventional amplitude-based metrics. This work bridges clinical neurophysiology, computational neuroscience, and edge computing, aiming to translate theoretical advances in network neuroscience into practical tools for END technologists. Success would enhance diagnostic precision in understudied conditions such as subclinical seizure propagation and mild traumatic brain injury, while establishing scalable methodologies for integrating HPC-driven analytics into routine END workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to study and record electrical activity in the brain and nervous system for purposes of patient monitoring and supporting diagnoses. Includes instruction in patient communication and care; taking and abstracting patient histories; application of recording electrodes; EEG, EP, and PSG equipment operation and procedural techniques; and data recording and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the electronic structure and reactivity of transition metal complexes with non-innocent ligands, a critical area in inorganic chemistry with implications for catalysis and energy storage. A central challenge in modeling these systems lies in accurately capturing their complex bonding interactions, which involve strong electron correlation effects, relativistic contributions, and dynamic solvent interactions. Conventional density functional theory (DFT) methods often fail to describe multi-configurational electronic states or spin-crossover behavior, necessitating advanced computational approaches. The proposed work will employ multi-reference wavefunction methods (CASSCF, NEVPT2) combined with relativistic DFT to model ground and excited states of iron and cobalt complexes with redox-active ligands. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will further probe solvent-driven structural fluctuations and their impact on electron transfer kinetics. These calculations will be validated against experimental X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) spectra to establish predictive frameworks for ligand design. The HPC resources will enable the systematic screening of ligand modifications to tune metal-ligand cooperativity, targeting complexes with enhanced catalytic activity for nitrogen fixation. Expected outcomes include new mechanistic insights into bond activation pathways and the development of open-source computational workflows for inorganic chemists to prioritize synthetic targets. This work addresses a critical gap in the rational design of next-generation catalysts by bridging the divide between qualitative bonding models and quantitative, dynamic descriptions of inorganic reactivity. The requested computing allocation will directly support the generation of high-quality reference data for understudied transition metal systems, fostering progress in sustainable chemistry and renewable energy technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the elements and their compounds, other than the hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Includes instruction in the characterization and synthesis of non-carbon molecules, including their structure and their bonding, conductivity, and reactive properties; research techniques such as spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and photoelectron analysis; and the study of specific compounds, such as transition metals, and compounds composed of inorganic and organic molecules.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cybersecurity threats and the dynamic nature of organizational risk landscapes demand advanced computational tools to optimize cybersecurity resource allocation. Traditional cost-benefit frameworks often fail to account for evolving adversarial tactics, interdependencies between digital assets, and the nonlinear impacts of security failures across interconnected business ecosystems. This project proposes a novel computational framework to model multi-stakeholder cybersecurity investment strategies under conditions of asymmetric information and adaptive threat actors. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will develop agent-based simulations that integrate game-theoretic decision models with real-world data on cyber-attack patterns, network vulnerabilities, and organizational workflows. The computational architecture will simultaneously process threat intelligence feeds, simulate attacker-defender interactions across scalable network topologies, and quantify cascading operational impacts using stochastic optimization techniques. Key innovations include the incorporation of machine learning to predict emergent attack vectors and dynamic resource reallocation algorithms that balance prevention, detection, and response capabilities. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for optimizing cybersecurity budgets across heterogeneous assets and actionable insights into resilience thresholds for critical business functions. The research bridges gaps between computational economics, network science, and information security management, advancing methodological approaches to cyber risk quantification while addressing pressing operational challenges in resource-constrained environments. By utilizing HPC capabilities to handle large-scale parallel simulations and high-dimensional optimization spaces, this work will establish scalable models for proactive cybersecurity governance, directly supporting the IRM program's focus on integrating technology management with strategic organizational planning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of information technology, computer systems management, and business operations to the planning, management, and evaluation of information services in organizations. Includes instruction in telecommunications, systems planning and integration, information policy, information security, contracting and purchasing, budgeting, information technology, operations management, human resources, communications skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Bengali linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in digital methodologies for non-Latin script languages. The primary research problem centers on the scarcity of scalable tools for analyzing syntactic, morphological, and semantic patterns in historical and contemporary Bengali texts, particularly across dialects such as Chittagonian, Sylheti, and Rarhi. Existing computational models for Bengali—often adapted from English-centric frameworks—struggle with the language’s diglossic variations, complex verb morphology, and script-specific challenges, limiting their utility for large-scale philological or sociolinguistic studies. Our work proposes a dual computational approach: (1) developing machine learning pipelines to automate the parsing and annotation of digitized Bengali texts spanning pre-modern manuscripts to modern social media corpora, and (2) implementing comparative dialectometry using graph-based algorithms to map linguistic shifts across temporal and regional axes. The HPC infrastructure will enable training transformer-based models on distributed GPU nodes to handle the 500GB+ multilingual corpus, while parallelized workflows will optimize resource-intensive tasks like morphological segmentation and collocation analysis. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for diachronic Bengali corpus linguistics, a geotagged dialect atlas with interactive visualization capabilities, and a neural architecture fine-tuned for low-resource Bengali variant identification. These resources will directly support interdisciplinary scholarship in Bengali philology, enable quantitative studies of literary style evolution, and provide frameworks for applied linguistic projects in education and technology localization. By addressing computational bottlenecks in processing non-standardized orthographies and morphosyntactic structures, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies that can inform similar efforts for other under-resourced South Asian languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bengali language (Bangla) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in perishable goods supply chain optimization for multi-location restaurant franchises, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic inventory allocation, waste reduction, and demand forecasting. The food services industry faces unique challenges due to the perishable nature of ingredients, fluctuating regional demand patterns, and complex logistics networks spanning centralized kitchens, third-party distributors, and individual outlets. Traditional inventory management systems often fail to account for real-time variables such as weather disruptions, localized consumer behavior shifts, or supplier reliability, resulting in annual food waste costs exceeding 10% of revenue for many operators. The proposed computational framework integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning to simulate multi-echelon supply chain interactions at scale, incorporating heterogeneous data streams including point-of-sale trends, IoT sensor readings from storage facilities, and transportation latency metrics. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, optimizing just-in-time delivery schedules while maintaining compliance with food safety regulations. A novel graph neural network architecture will be trained on historical spoilage patterns and external datasets (e.g., climate, economic indicators) to predict stockout risks and surplus accumulation at hyperlocal levels. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of reducing perishable inventory waste by 15-25% in test franchise networks, with adaptable modules for pricing elasticity analysis and crisis response planning. The computational workflows will be containerized for industry deployment, advancing operational resilience in food services while establishing transferable methodologies for perishable goods management across adjacent sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market restaurants, food services in hospitality establishments, food service chains and franchise networks, and restaurant supply operations. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, food services management, wholesale logistics and distribution, franchise operations, business networking, personnel management, culinary arts, business planning and capitalization, food industry operations, marketing and retailing, business law and regulations, finance, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The development of next-generation polymer materials with tailored properties requires precise control over polymerization kinetics, chain architecture, and mesoscale morphology. However, experimentally mapping the vast design space of monomer chemistries, reaction conditions, and processing parameters remains prohibitively time-intensive. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to establish a multiscale simulation framework that bridges quantum-scale molecular interactions, polymerization reaction dynamics, and continuum-scale material behavior. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations will parameterize force fields for novel monomer systems, while kinetic Monte Carlo methods will model chain growth mechanisms under varying reactor conditions. These outputs will feed into coarse-grained dissipative particle dynamics simulations to predict phase-separated morphologies in block copolymer systems, with particular focus on stimuli-responsive polymers for targeted drug delivery applications. Concurrently, finite element modeling will correlate simulated nanostructures with bulk viscoelastic properties under thermomechanical loads. Machine learning models trained on this multiscale dataset will identify predictive relationships between synthetic parameters and functional performance. The computational workflow demands parallelized execution across GPU-accelerated nodes for quantum calculations and large-scale morphology sampling, supplemented by high-memory nodes for handling polymer network trajectory data. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source framework for in silico polymer design, (2) optimized reaction pathways for synthesizing branched copolymers with enhanced toughness and thermal stability, and (3) morphology-property maps guiding the development of self-healing elastomers. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, this work aims to accelerate the creation of sustainable polymer alternatives to conventional petroleum-based materials while advancing computational methodologies for complex chemical engineering systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of synthesized macromolecular compounds and their application to specific engineering uses, including the development of industrial materials with tailored properties, the design of lightweight structural components, the use of liquid or solid polymers, and the analysis and control of polymerization processes.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predictive modeling for nanoscale thermal transport in hybrid quantum-material systems, an emerging area at the intersection of nanoscale engineering, quantum physics, and computational science. Current models for heat dissipation in nanodevices rely on simplified bulk approximations or single-material frameworks, failing to capture the complex, non-equilibrium dynamics of hybrid systems such as 2D material heterostructures coupled to quantum dots or superconducting resonators. These limitations hinder the design of energy-efficient nanoelectronics and quantum technologies, where thermal management at interfaces governs performance and stability. To overcome this gap, we propose a multiscale computational approach integrating first-principles density functional theory (DFT), non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) methods, and machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics (ML-MD) simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve atomic-scale phonon scattering, interfacial thermal resistance, and quantum confinement effects across heterogeneous material boundaries at experimentally relevant scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-optimized codes for DFT (VASP) and MD (LAMMPS), coupled with custom Python-based ML force fields trained on ab initio datasets to extend simulation timescales. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for predicting thermal transport in hybrid nanosystems, new insights into interfacial phonon engineering for heat mitigation in quantum devices, and design guidelines for next-generation thermal interfaces in superconducting qubit arrays. This work bridges a critical gap between quantum device engineering and nanoscale thermal sciences, with potential applications in cryogenic computing, photonic-integrated circuits, and energy-efficient nanoelectronics. The requested resources will enable simulations spanning 10^4–10^6 atoms over nanosecond timescales, exceeding the capabilities of current local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the integration and predictive analysis of multi-domain intelligence data for military decision-making. Modern intelligence operations require synthesizing vast, heterogeneous datasets—including signals intelligence (SIGINT), human intelligence (HUMINT), geospatial data, and open-source information—to identify emerging threats and optimize resource deployment. However, traditional analytical tools struggle with the scale, velocity, and unstructured nature of these data streams, particularly in dynamic operational environments. This research addresses the critical gap in scalable, real-time processing and pattern recognition across classified and unclassified sources, enabling proactive threat anticipation. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement distributed machine learning models, graph-based network analysis, and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to military intelligence workflows. Key computational challenges include federated learning across secure data silos, anomaly detection in temporally evolving networks, and semantic extraction from multilingual, noisy text. By parallelizing these tasks across GPU clusters and optimizing memory-intensive graph traversals, the framework aims to reduce latency in situational awareness products from hours to minutes. Expected outcomes include an open architecture toolkit for adaptive intelligence fusion, validated against historical operational datasets, and novel algorithms for identifying latent adversarial tactics. Success will provide military planners with a unified platform to simulate threat scenarios, assess resource allocation trade-offs, and prioritize collection assets. This work bridges computational scalability with domain-specific operational constraints, advancing the intelligence community’s capacity to preempt asymmetric threats while maintaining rigorous security and chain-of-command protocols. The requested HPC resources will enable benchmarking at operationally relevant data scales, ensuring translational impact for joint all-domain command and control (JADC2) initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of intelligence acquisition, analysis and exploitation. Includes instruction in intelligence organizations, the intelligence cycle, intelligence operations planning, intelligence analysis and reporting, intelligence methods, electronic and signals intelligence, operations and communications security, human intelligence management, intelligence chain of command, information exploitation and psychological warfare, and the relationship to national security policy and strategy.

abstract: The dynamic behavior of silicate minerals under extreme pressure-temperature conditions governs critical geomorphological processes, including metamorphic reactions, crustal deformation, and mantle dynamics. However, quantitative models of silicate phase transitions and their kinetic pathways remain limited due to the computational expense of simulating atomic-scale interactions across geologically relevant spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance multiscale modeling of silicate systems, focusing on coupled quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations of olivine-group mineral transformations. These minerals dominate ultramafic rocks and play key roles in lithospheric rheology, yet their dislocation-mediated deformation mechanisms under shear stress—particularly at subduction zone interfaces—are poorly constrained. We propose to implement hybrid QM/MM simulations using CP2K and LAMMPS software packages, with QM regions treated via density functional theory (DFT) to model bond-breaking/reforming events, while MM regions employ classical force fields to capture long-range strain effects. Simulations will track dislocation nucleation and migration in forsterite (Mg2SiO4) under varying P-T conditions (0–10 GPa, 300–1500 K), requiring >1 million CPU-hours to achieve nanosecond-scale trajectories across 100,000+ atom systems. Parallel tempering methods will enhance conformational sampling of rare events. Outcomes will include (1) atomistic mechanisms for shear-induced amorphization in olivine, (2) rate constants for dislocation creep under lithospheric stresses, and (3) predictive relationships between defect geometries and macroscopic viscosity. These results will directly inform field-based studies of mantle xenoliths and improve constitutive models for tectonic simulations. The computational framework developed will be extensible to other silicate systems, addressing fundamental gaps in linking micro-scale mineral physics to planetary-scale geodynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the silicates and other substances formed by chemical and physical geomorphological processes.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of herbal compounds used in traditional medicine systems, focusing on their interactions with host immune and metabolic pathways. Despite widespread use, the polypharmacological nature of these compounds—acting through multiple targets and pathways—remains poorly characterized due to the complexity of their bioactive constituents and the lack of scalable computational frameworks to model their systemic effects. We propose an integrative approach combining network pharmacology, machine learning, and multiscale molecular dynamics simulations to map interactions between 200+ phytochemicals (from 15 prioritized medicinal plants) and human proteomes associated with inflammation and metabolic regulation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale virtual screening (2M+ ligand-receptor pairs), ensemble docking simulations, and dynamic network analysis of protein-ligand complexes under physiological conditions. Density functional theory calculations will optimize force field parameters for rare phytochemicals lacking existing molecular descriptors. Concurrently, graph neural networks will predict plant-compound-target networks using curated ethnopharmacological databases and transcriptomic datasets from preclinical models. The computational pipeline will be validated through in vitro assays measuring cytokine modulation and metabolomic profiling in immune cell cultures treated with candidate compounds. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved signaling motifs targeted by traditional herbal formulations, (2) a publicly accessible database of optimized molecular models for understudied phytochemicals, and (3) predictive frameworks for evaluating plant-derived combinations in silico. This work addresses critical gaps in evidence-based validation of traditional medical knowledge while advancing computational methods for complex natural product research, with potential applications in precision phytotherapy and cross-cultural pharmacognosy.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of biomedical systems, such as adaptive prosthetics and biohybrid devices, demands high-resolution modeling to capture multiscale interactions between biological tissues, synthetic materials, and dynamic physiological environments. Current limitations in computational power restrict the ability to simulate these systems at clinically relevant spatiotemporal scales, hindering the optimization of device functionality and patient-specific design. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multi-physics framework for simulating biomechanical, electrochemical, and fluid-structure interactions in bioengineered systems. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) creating patient-specific models of neuromuscular-prosthetic interfaces to predict stress distributions, metabolic activity, and long-term tissue remodeling under cyclic loading, and (2) optimizing the design of soft robotic assistive devices through coupled fluid dynamics and machine learning algorithms that account for real-time physiological feedback. Computational methods will integrate finite element analysis, agent-based modeling, and convolutional neural networks trained on high-resolution imaging datasets (MRI, micro-CT) to capture anatomical variability. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations across multiple fidelity scales, reducing runtime for complex optimization tasks from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for reducing implant failure rates, a computational pipeline for personalized prosthetic design, and open-source tools for simulating biohybrid systems. These advances will directly support translational research in rehabilitation engineering and contribute to the development of adaptive biomedical devices that dynamically respond to physiological changes. The requested computing resources are critical for handling datasets exceeding 100TB, executing GPU-accelerated deep learning workflows, and maintaining the iterative optimization cycles required for clinically actionable results.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: Dental diseases remain a significant public health burden, disproportionately affecting underserved populations due to complex interactions between biological, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the multidimensional nature of these disparities, limiting the design of targeted interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that elucidate the drivers of oral health inequities and optimize community-level prevention strategies. The research will integrate large-scale datasets, including national dental health surveys, electronic health records, and geospatial socioeconomic indicators, to analyze patterns of caries, periodontal disease, and access to care. Machine learning approaches, such as ensemble classifiers and graph neural networks, will be applied to identify risk clusters and forecast disease trajectories across diverse populations. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate the long-term impacts of proposed public health interventions, such as fluoridation programs or teledentistry expansion, under varying policy and resource allocation scenarios. Computational workflows will require parallel processing to manage the heterogeneity and volume of data (spanning millions of patient records and environmental variables) and to iteratively refine models through sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-priority regions for preventive care investment, predictive tools to guide early intervention in at-risk populations, and evidence-based frameworks for evaluating the cost-effectiveness of community dental programs. By enabling granular analysis of multifactorial influences on oral health, this work aims to advance equity-focused policy design and strengthen the integration of computational epidemiology into dental public health training curricula. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current limitations in processing capacity, ensuring robust validation of models, and scaling analyses to address both local and global oral health challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of dental disease prevention and control, community dental health promotion, and prepares dentists and public health professionals to function as dental health specialists. Includes instruction in preventive dentistry, the relationship of oral disease to health and quality of life, patient and practitioner behavior, dental epidemiology, nutrition and dental health, dental care policy and delivery, oral health program planning and administration, biostatistics, and research methods.

abstract: Fermentation processes in food production are governed by complex microbial interactions that remain poorly understood, limiting the optimization of product quality, consistency, and innovation. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the dynamic, multiscale nature of microbial communities, substrate utilization, and metabolite production in heterogeneous fermentation environments. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-resolution computational model of microbial consortia in fermented food systems, with a focus on cereal-based (e.g., beer, sourdough) and dairy fermentations. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of key fermentative microorganisms (e.g., *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*, *Lactobacillus* spp.) with spatiotemporal simulations of substrate diffusion, pH gradients, and microbial competition/cooperation. Machine learning methods will be applied to multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic) from experimental fermentations to identify critical regulatory nodes in community behavior. The computational framework will enable stochastic simulations of batch and continuous fermentation processes at unprecedented scale, incorporating 10^4-10^5 microbial agents with species-specific metabolic constraints. Key deliverables include predictive models linking starter culture composition to fermentation kinetics, off-flavor risks, and post-processing shelf-life indicators. This work will directly support three ongoing experimental studies on (1) reducing biogenic amine production in plant-based fermented proteins, (2) optimizing mixed-culture brewing fermentations for novel flavor profiles, and (3) accelerating strain selection for acid-tolerant probiotics in dairy systems. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling the combinatorial parameter space of microbial interactions, running parallelized flux balance analyses, and training deep neural networks on fermentation time-series data. Outcomes will provide a transformative toolkit for both academic research and industry applications, enabling data-driven design of fermentation protocols that enhance product safety, sensory qualities, and process efficiency while reducing trial-and-error experimentation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of fermented food production. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how large-scale computational analysis can advance understanding of genre evolution in digital writing environments, particularly as traditional text-based genres adapt to multimodal, interactive formats. While existing scholarship has qualitatively examined shifts in genres like blogs, podcasts, and interactive narratives, the scale and complexity of digital writing across platforms necessitate quantitative approaches to identify patterns in rhetorical strategies, structural innovation, and audience engagement. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning to analyze a corpus of 30,000 digital texts spanning 2010–2023, sourced from open-access repositories, social media, and web archives. Computational methods will include semantic network analysis to map rhetorical moves, transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) to classify hybrid genre features, and sentiment analysis to correlate stylistic choices with reader feedback metrics. High-performance computing resources are critical for training custom NLP models on heterogeneous data (text, metadata, hyperlinks) and processing multimodal elements, including embedded images and dynamic content, which require parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated feature extraction. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of emergent digital genres based on computational rhetorical analysis, (2) models predicting successful genre adaptation strategies across contexts, and (3) open-access tools for writers to visualize genre conventions and audience expectations. By bridging computational methods with writing studies, this project will provide empirically grounded insights into how digital technologies reshape compositional practices, offering practical applications for writing pedagogy, professional communication, and inclusive design in public-facing genres.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on writing for applied and liberal arts purposes. Includes instruction in writing and document design in multiple genres, modes, and media; writing technologies; research, evaluation, and use of information; editing and publishing; theories and processes of composing; rhetorical theories, traditions, and analysis; communication across audiences, contexts, and cultures; and practical applications for professional, technical, organizational, academic, and public settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the distribution of prime gaps in arithmetic progressions, a foundational problem in analytic number theory with implications for conjectures such as the Hardy-Littlewood prime tuples conjecture. While theoretical bounds on gaps between primes in arithmetic progressions exist, explicit computational verification for large moduli remains incomplete due to the prohibitive scale of required calculations. Specifically, the research will focus on characterizing the minimal gaps between consecutive primes within progressions of the form \(a \mod q\) for large \(q\), where existing asymptotic results may not capture fine-grained behavior. The computational approach involves deploying a distributed, high-performance sieve algorithm to generate and analyze primes across extensive ranges (\(10^{12}\) and beyond) for multiple residue classes. The sieve will be optimized for parallel execution across multi-node clusters, leveraging MPI for task distribution and shared-memory architectures for local sieving. Memory-efficient storage structures will be developed to manage prime tables, while probabilistic primality tests will validate candidate gaps. Anticipated outcomes include empirical datasets quantifying gap distributions for previously inaccessible moduli, potentially identifying deviations from expected asymptotic trends. These results could refine conjectural models of prime distributions in arithmetic progressions and inform theoretical work on error terms in related analytic estimates. The project’s computational demands—terabyte-scale data generation, intensive modular arithmetic operations, and parallel scalability—necessitate dedicated high-performance computing resources. Successful execution will advance both algorithmic methods in computational number theory and foundational knowledge of prime number phenomena.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of integers, integer-valued functions, including combinatorics.

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems—spanning energy grids, transportation networks, and communication systems—are increasingly targeted by sophisticated cyber-physical attacks that exploit interdependencies between digital and physical components. Existing risk assessment and mitigation frameworks often fail to model these complex interactions at scale, leaving gaps in contingency planning and redundancy strategies. This project seeks to address this challenge by developing an integrated computational platform to simulate multi-domain infrastructure interdependencies, quantify cascading failure risks, and evaluate adaptive defense strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct a multi-agent simulation environment that integrates cyberattack dynamics, physical system vulnerabilities, and human operational responses. Agent-based models will represent infrastructure nodes (e.g., power substations, data centers) with granular threat propagation rules, while graph-theoretic methods will map dependency networks across sectors. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical threat intelligence and real-time sensor data to parameterize adversarial behavior patterns and adaptive attack scenarios. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations to assess millions of potential attack-defend permutations, requiring large-scale CPU/GPU clusters for ensemble modeling and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for identifying critical failure pathways in interconnected infrastructure systems, (2) probabilistic risk metrics to prioritize infrastructure hardening investments, and (3) AI-driven mitigation protocols for rapid response to cross-domain threats. Results will directly inform policy recommendations for redundancy planning and sector-specific security standards, while the simulation toolkit will be made available as an open-source resource for infrastructure operators and homeland security agencies. By bridging computational modeling with operational security practices, this work aims to advance the resilience of national infrastructure against emerging asymmetric threats.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: Emergency and trauma nursing requires rapid, evidence-based decision-making under high-stakes conditions, yet current clinical tools for predicting patient deterioration or optimizing intervention timing remain limited. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating real-time patient data with machine learning models to support clinical decision-making in emergency and trauma care. The primary challenge lies in processing heterogeneous data streams—including vital signs, imaging, and injury patterns—within the narrow time windows critical for trauma outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate ensemble models that synthesize multimodal data at scale, enabling dynamic risk stratification and treatment pathway recommendations. Using retrospective electronic health records from Level I trauma centers (n ≈ 25,000 cases), we will implement neural networks to predict hemorrhagic shock progression and sepsis risk, while agent-based modeling will simulate resource allocation scenarios under varying ER congestion levels. Computational demands are substantial: model training requires iterative optimization across 10+ hyperparameters, and trauma simulations involve parallel processing of 10^6+ patient-flow permutations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for acute deterioration in trauma patients, deployable via bedside clinical decision support systems, and (2) evidence-based protocols for staffing and resource distribution during mass casualty events. This work directly addresses gaps in trauma nursing practice by translating large-scale computational analysis into actionable clinical tools, with potential to reduce time-to-intervention for critical conditions. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the throughput and latency requirements necessary to mirror real-world ER environments, ensuring models are both accurate and operationally feasible.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver advanced, direct patient care in emergency and trauma settings. Includes instruction in advanced health assessment, pharmacology, physiology, emergency management, trauma conditions, trauma assessments and acute care.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how habitat fragmentation and shifting climatic conditions interact to shape the evolutionary trajectories and population viability of keystone species in temperate forest ecosystems. As anthropogenic landscape modification accelerates, understanding the long-term adaptive capacity of ecologically critical species is vital for predicting ecosystem resilience. We propose an integrative computational framework combining individual-based population simulations with spatially explicit environmental data to model adaptive responses under scenarios of varying climate gradients and habitat connectivity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute these simulations at biologically relevant spatial and temporal scales, incorporating stochastic demographic processes, gene flow dynamics, and selection pressures across heterogeneous landscapes. The models will integrate empirical data from field studies on dispersal behavior, fecundity, and heritable phenotypic traits, parameterized using Bayesian calibration techniques. By simulating millions of agent interactions over multi-generational timescales, we aim to identify thresholds of habitat connectivity and climate variability beyond which local adaptation fails to track environmental change. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of genetic diversity loss, estimates of time-to-extinction probabilities under alternative management scenarios, and mechanistic insights into trait-environment feedback loops. These results will directly inform regional conservation strategies targeting functional biodiversity maintenance in fragmented landscapes. The computational workflows developed will also provide a scalable template for assessing climate-driven eco-evolutionary dynamics in other biome types, advancing theoretical frameworks at the intersection of landscape ecology and evolutionary rescue biology.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_title: Ecology, Evolution, Systematics and Population Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ecology, evolution, and systematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Cutaneous diseases, including psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and melanoma, involve complex interactions between genetic, immunological, and environmental factors. Current gaps in understanding disease heterogeneity and treatment resistance limit the development of personalized therapies. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-omics datasets and simulate molecular pathways underlying dermatologic pathologies. The research will integrate bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from patient-derived skin biopsies, genomic variant databases, and spatially resolved proteomic profiles to identify disease-specific cellular states and dysregulated signaling networks. Machine learning models will be trained on these datasets to classify subtypes of chronic inflammatory skin conditions and predict drug response variability. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between therapeutic agents (e.g., biologics, small-molecule inhibitors) and target proteins under varying inflammatory microenvironments, enabling in silico screening of optimized compounds. A parallel computational pipeline will employ agent-based modeling to study immune cell trafficking and keratinocyte dynamics in lesional skin, parameterized by longitudinal clinical imaging data. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale data storage, accelerating genome-wide association studies via parallelized statistical frameworks, and performing real-time analysis of high-resolution histopathology images using deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early disease detection, computationally validated drug candidates for refractory cases, and predictive algorithms to guide therapeutic selection. These results will be disseminated through open-source tools for dermatological data analysis, fostering reproducibility in computational dermatology. By bridging large-scale data science with mechanistic modeling, this work aims to advance precision dermatology and improve outcomes for patients with complex or treatment-resistant skin diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on diseases of the skin, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May also include research on dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, sexually transmitted diseases, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics datasets—spanning genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and clinical phenotyping—poses a critical challenge in identifying actionable biomarkers for personalized treatment of complex diseases. While existing tools can analyze individual data layers, integrating heterogeneous, high-dimensional datasets to uncover systemic pathophysiological mechanisms remains computationally intractable with conventional infrastructure. This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable real-time integration of multi-omics data with dynamic clinical variables, facilitating precision diagnostics and therapeutic optimization. The research will employ hybrid machine learning architectures, including graph neural networks to model cross-omics interactions and transformer-based models for temporal clinical data fusion. Federated learning protocols will be implemented to support privacy-preserving analysis across distributed healthcare datasets. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for large-scale tensor operations, reducing dimensionality without losing biologically relevant signal, and ensuring interpretability of cross-modal feature attributions. The HPC environment will be critical for benchmarking these methods against synthetic and real-world datasets, including a curated repository of longitudinal multi-omics profiles from patients with autoimmune disorders. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for adaptive multi-omics integration, validation of novel combinatorial biomarkers for disease subtyping, and a proof-of-concept decision support module for predicting individualized treatment responses. By addressing the computational bottlenecks in multi-scale health data synthesis, this work aims to advance translational informatics paradigms, bridging the gap between high-throughput biomarker discovery and clinically deployable AI tools. The resource request aligns with the program’s focus on scalable, ethical health informatics solutions, emphasizing interoperability and human-AI collaboration in dynamic care environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to health and/or biomedical research,  and the development of advanced database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in biomedical and/or health sciences; information science and technology; social and behavioral sciences; biomedical/health information science and technology; human factors and socio-technical systems;  applied social, behavioral, and information science and technology; and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory allocation strategies for multi-industry vehicle parts markets (automotive, marine, aviation) under stochastic supply chain disruptions and shifting consumer preferences. Traditional inventory models fail to address the unique challenges of these sectors, where parts compatibility matrices, seasonal demand volatility, and geographically fragmented distribution networks intersect with emergent factors like electric vehicle retrofitting trends and marine electrification regulations. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid simulation-optimization approach combining agent-based modeling of distributor-retailer-customer networks with reinforcement learning algorithms. Agent behaviors will be parameterized using historical transaction data from 12 industry partners and real-time IoT sensor feeds tracking parts utilization patterns. Monte Carlo simulations will stress-test inventory policies against climate-related logistics delays and regulatory shock scenarios, while graph neural networks will map cross-industry demand spillover effects. Computational demands arise from the need to process terabyte-scale telematics datasets, simulate 10^6+ agent interactions across heterogeneous market environments, and solve high-dimensional optimization problems with non-convex constraints. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of prescriptive inventory recommendations at 24-hour refresh cycles, probabilistic risk assessments for parts portfolio management, and novel metrics quantifying resilience-efficiency tradeoffs in multi-modal distribution systems. This work will provide the first unified computational model addressing interdependencies between legacy combustion engine part markets and emerging electric vehicle retrofit ecosystems, offering actionable insights for 3,000+ small-to-midsize distributors participating in the National Vehicle Parts Alliance consortium.
cip_title: Vehicle and Vehicle Parts and Accessories Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of replacement parts and other end-use supplies in the automotive, marine, and aviation industries. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, principles of vehicular technologies, storage and distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical diagnostics, driven by advancements in multi-omics technologies and large-scale biomedical data, necessitates robust computational infrastructure to support research in clinical laboratory science. This project seeks to address critical bottlenecks in analyzing high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles—to improve the accuracy and efficiency of disease diagnosis and monitoring. Current methods for integrating heterogeneous clinical data often lack scalability, leading to delays in identifying actionable biomarkers and validating laboratory-developed tests (LDTs). To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning (ML) models capable of processing multi-omics data in real time. Our computational approach will focus on ensemble learning techniques and neural networks to identify patterns across disparate datasets, while parallelized workflows will enable rapid validation of candidate biomarkers against clinical outcomes. Key tasks include the deployment of containerized pipelines for data harmonization, feature selection, and model training, utilizing frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch. Additionally, we will simulate large-scale virtual cohorts to assess the generalizability of diagnostic algorithms across diverse patient populations. The use of HPC will allow iterative refinement of models with minimal latency, ensuring compliance with clinical turnaround time requirements. Expected outcomes include the development of a scalable computational platform for biomarker discovery, validated ML models for early detection of sepsis and hematologic malignancies, and open-source tools to enhance reproducibility in clinical laboratory research. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation diagnostic protocols, reduce reliance on manual interpretation, and advance precision medicine initiatives. By bridging computational innovation with clinical laboratory practice, the project aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, optimize laboratory workflows, and ultimately improve patient outcomes through data-driven decision-making.
cip_title: Clinical Laboratory Science/ Medical Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conduct and supervise complex medical tests, clinical trials, and research experiments; manage clinical laboratories; and consult with physicians and clinical researchers on diagnoses, disease causation and spread, and research outcomes. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, immunology, immunohematology, physiological relationships to test results, laboratory procedures and quality assurance controls, test and research design and implementation, analytic techniques, laboratory management, data development and reporting, medical informatics, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in simulating complex mechanical systems for advanced Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CAD/CADD) applications. Current workflows in mechanical drafting often rely on iterative physical prototyping and simplified computational models to predict system behavior, leading to prolonged development cycles, material waste, and suboptimal designs under multifactorial stress conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven topology optimization to model high-fidelity mechanical assemblies. The project will focus on optimizing parametric designs for industrial machinery components subject to dynamic thermal, vibrational, and structural loads. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of design permutations, coupled with real-time visualization of deformation patterns and failure modes at micron-scale resolutions. Key computational challenges include managing multi-physics couplings in GPU-accelerated environments, automating geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) validation through distributed computing, and training neural networks on terabyte-scale simulation datasets to predict optimal material distributions. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in computational runtime compared to current workstation-based workflows, enabling rapid iteration of ASME Y14.5-compliant designs. The research will produce open-source tools for automated blueprint generation and stress analysis visualization, directly enhancing technical communication in cross-disciplinary engineering teams. By integrating HPC capabilities into mechanical drafting pedagogy, this project aims to bridge the gap between traditional CAD techniques and Industry 4.0 demands, equipping students with skills in large-scale simulation and data-driven design optimization. Results will be validated against physical prototypes in collaboration with regional manufacturing partners, with potential applications in renewable energy systems and precision aerospace components.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance geography teacher education by integrating high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing need for spatial data literacy and advanced geospatial analysis skills in K–12 classrooms. Despite the increasing availability of large-scale geospatial datasets (e.g., satellite imagery, climate models, urban sensor networks) and computational tools, geography educators often lack training in leveraging these resources to teach complex spatial phenomena. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing scalable computational workflows that enable pre-service and in-service teachers to analyze, visualize, and interpret geospatial data efficiently. The project will design and implement HPC-driven modules focused on three domains: (1) simulating landscape changes under climate scenarios using agent-based modeling, (2) processing high-resolution remote sensing data to assess urbanization patterns, and (3) automating the generation of customizable, region-specific teaching materials from global geospatial datasets. Computational methods will include parallelized spatial statistics, machine learning for pattern detection in heterogeneous datasets, and GPU-accelerated rendering of 3D terrain models. These workflows will be optimized for classroom accessibility, allowing educators to run analyses via user-friendly interfaces while abstracting backend HPC complexities. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools and curricular resources that empower geography teachers to incorporate real-world computational geoscience into their pedagogy. By demonstrating how HPC can democratize access to large-scale spatial analysis, this work aims to elevate spatial reasoning skills among students, foster interdisciplinary connections between geography and computational science, and prepare educators to address emerging challenges such as climate resilience and sustainable development. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform geography education from a static, map-based discipline into a dynamic, data-driven field that aligns with 21st-century scientific and societal demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: The construction industry faces increasing demands for sustainable, high-performance building materials that balance structural integrity, energy efficiency, and environmental impact. Traditional experimental approaches to material development are resource-intensive and time-consuming, limiting the exploration of novel composites and innovative designs. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a computational framework for the rapid optimization of next-generation construction materials. The research will employ multi-scale finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate mechanical behavior under dynamic loads, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models to assess thermal and hygrothermal performance. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to analyze simulation datasets, identifying key material parameters and predicting optimal compositions. HPC resources are critical to manage the high computational demands of these simulations, which involve complex, non-linear interactions across multiple physical domains and require iterative parametric studies. The project will generate a validated database of material properties for emerging composites, such as bio-based polymers and fiber-reinforced ceramics, and establish predictive models to guide their application in energy-efficient building systems. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for construction trades, enabling educators and industry partners to explore material behaviors in virtual environments. By accelerating the transition to sustainable materials, this research aims to reduce construction-related carbon emissions and enhance the resilience of built infrastructure, directly aligning with global priorities in climate action and sustainable development.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in construction trades, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and biochemical interactions of cosmetic treatments on heterogeneous skin types, aiming to optimize personalized skincare protocols. Despite advances in esthetic practices, the dynamic relationship between treatment variables (e.g., product formulations, massage techniques, environmental factors) and client-specific skin responses remains poorly quantified. Current protocols rely heavily on generalized guidelines, leading to variable outcomes for individuals with diverse skin textures, sensitivities, or ethnic backgrounds. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale skin behavior under varying treatment conditions. A hybrid approach integrating finite element modeling (FEM) for mechanical stress analysis during manual therapies (e.g., lymphatic drainage, deep-tissue massage) will be paired with agent-based modeling to predict biochemical diffusion rates of topical agents across stratified skin layers. Machine learning algorithms will train on heterogeneous datasets comprising clinical skin assessments, hyperspectral imaging, and longitudinal treatment logs to identify predictive biomarkers for adverse reactions or optimal efficacy. Computational workflows will be validated against in vitro 3D skin models and retrospective client data from partner spas.
