Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of dynamically adjusting treatment parameters (pressure, product viscosity, duration) based on real-time client biometrics, reducing trial-and-error in practice. This work bridges esthetic science with computational biophysics, offering a novel paradigm for precision skincare that enhances safety and personalization while addressing gaps in non-engineering, non-biomedical research infrastructure for beauty wellness professions. The scalability of these models will further enable investigations into underrepresented skin phenotypes and emerging cosmetic technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cleanse, depilate, massage, and beautify the human body and to function as licensed estheticians and skin care specialists.  Includes instruction in skin anatomy, physiology, and health; principles of nutrition; decontamination and infection control; health and safety; facial and body massage; body wrapping and spa treatments; temporary hair removal including waxing and tweezing; color and skin analysis; client consultation and care; applicable laws and regulations; business practices; and sometimes related alternative healing regimens.

abstract: The development of advanced structural materials with tailored mechanical properties requires a fundamental understanding of defect dynamics at atomic and microstructural scales. Current experimental techniques face limitations in resolving real-time evolution of dislocations, grain boundaries, and voids under complex thermo-mechanical loads, particularly in multi-phase systems. This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate defect-mediated deformation mechanisms in polycrystalline alloys, integrating atomistic and mesoscale models to bridge critical gaps in predicting failure initiation. Using large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will quantify dislocation nucleation and interaction energies in heterogeneous microstructures with explicit grain boundaries, while phase-field models will capture longer-term coarsening and crack propagation behaviors. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated LAMMPS for MD and in-house phase-field solvers optimized for adaptive mesh refinement, enabling concurrent multi-scale simulations across 10^6–10^9 atom ensembles and millimeter-scale microstructures. Key challenges include managing memory constraints during cross-scale data transfer and achieving strong scaling for iterative solute diffusion calculations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework correlating local defect configurations with macroscopic yield strength and fatigue resistance in titanium-aluminide composites. The resource request targets 250,000 node-hours on a GPU-equipped cluster, with 2 TB of high-speed storage for trajectory analysis. Results will inform the design of next-generation high-temperature alloys for aerospace applications, directly addressing the materials science community’s need for predictive tools that bypass trial-and-error prototyping. By resolving the spatiotemporal limits of existing models, this work aims to establish computational protocols for defect engineering in additive manufacturing processes, with open-source release of optimized simulation workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical and scientific principles to the analysis and evaluation of the characteristics and behavior of solids, including internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, compound materials, and research on industrial applications of specific materials.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy-efficient building designs and construction workflows through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations. The construction industry faces increasing pressure to reduce energy consumption and carbon footprints while maintaining cost-effectiveness and structural integrity. However, traditional methods for evaluating building performance—such as manual load calculations, static energy models, and physical prototyping—are time-intensive, lack granularity, and struggle to account for dynamic interactions between structural systems, HVAC efficiency, and regional climate variability. To address these limitations, this research will employ HPC resources to run multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress testing, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow and thermal modeling, and machine learning algorithms to predict material performance under varying environmental conditions. Large datasets from existing building projects, including sensor-derived thermal profiles, material properties, and regional weather patterns, will inform these models. The simulations will assess novel construction materials, hybrid HVAC configurations, and modular building designs to identify optimal solutions that balance energy efficiency, durability, and cost. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin framework for real-time performance prediction of residential and commercial structures, validated against physical prototypes. This work will directly advance the Building Construction Technology field by enabling data-driven decision-making in design phases, reducing iterative testing costs, and providing actionable insights for sustainable code-compliant construction. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational load of parallelized simulations, which require terabytes of memory and thousands of core-hours to process high-resolution 3D models and stochastic climate datasets. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools tailored for construction technicians, fostering industry adoption of simulation-driven practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to residential and commercial building construction and remodeling. Includes instruction in construction equipment and safety; site preparation and layout; construction estimating; blueprint reading; building codes; framing; masonry; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning; electrical and mechanical systems; interior and exterior finishing; and plumbing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and gendered dynamics of Polish diaspora communities through the analysis of digitized archival materials, oral histories, and multimedia artifacts. While existing scholarship has mapped broad migration patterns, significant gaps remain in understanding how localized cultural practices, gender roles, and intergenerational memory have evolved within dispersed Polish communities since the mid-20th century. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the scale and heterogeneity of available data, including multilingual texts, audio recordings, and visual media from institutional and community archives. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of textual records, computer vision techniques to identify visual motifs in photographs and folk art, and network modeling to trace transnational connections across diaspora nodes. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect gendered language patterns and cultural references in Polish, Ukrainian, and Yiddish sources, while graph algorithms will map shifting community structures against geopolitical events. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to process over 500,000 digitized items from 15 collections within a 12-month period—a task infeasible on standard computing systems. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing cultural transmission pathways, computational models for intersectional analysis in Slavic studies, and new methodologies for ethically engaging with fragmented or contested heritage materials. This work will provide the first large-scale computational framework for analyzing Polish diasporic identity formation, offering insights into how cultural preservation interacts with gender dynamics in displaced communities. Results will directly inform curricular development in digital Polish studies and support collaborative preservation initiatives with diaspora organizations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Poland and the current and historical inhabitants of the Polish lands, including borderlands, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: In modern tool and die manufacturing, empirical approaches to designing complex dies, molds, and fixtures often result in prolonged development cycles, material inefficiencies, and unpredictable tool failure. This project addresses these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models that simulate metal-forming processes with unprecedented fidelity. The research integrates multi-physics simulations—including finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD)—to capture thermal gradients, stress distributions, and microstructural evolution during stamping, forging, and injection molding. Machine learning algorithms will further optimize tool geometry, material selection, and process parameters by analyzing large datasets derived from simulations and experimental trials. The computational intensity of these coupled models, particularly the need for high-resolution meshing, nonlinear material behavior analysis, and real-time iterative optimization, necessitates HPC resources to enable parallel processing and efficient data management. Anticipated outcomes include predictive frameworks for minimizing defects (e.g., cracking, springback) and extending tool lifespan through wear-resistant design optimizations. By reducing reliance on physical prototyping, this work aims to lower production costs and lead times, particularly for small-batch and custom manufacturing. Additionally, the project will advance workforce training in tool and die technology by developing open-source simulation tools tailored for educational use, bridging computational methodologies with hands-on technical curricula. The integration of HPC-driven modeling into traditional manufacturing workflows is expected to enhance precision, scalability, and sustainability in the field, positioning tool and die technicians to meet evolving industry demands for high-tolerance components in aerospace, automotive, and energy sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate machine tools used in the forming of metal components, as well as the fabrication of special tools, dies, jigs and fixtures used in cutting, working and finishing metal components.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and sustainable well drilling practices necessitates advanced computational modeling to optimize drilling operations, mitigate risks, and reduce environmental impacts. Current industry challenges include unpredictable subsurface conditions, wellbore instability, and equipment failures, which lead to costly downtime and environmental hazards. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity simulations of drilling processes in heterogeneous geological formations to improve predictive accuracy for drill bit performance, fluid dynamics, and fracture propagation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement coupled geomechanical and hydrodynamic models that integrate real-time sensor data from drilling sites with machine learning (ML) algorithms. The computational framework will utilize finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate multiphase interactions between drilling fluids, rock matrices, and equipment under varying pressure and temperature regimes. ML components will train on historical drilling data and simulation outputs to predict optimal drilling parameters, such as weight-on-bit, rotational speed, and mud viscosity, while identifying early signs of equipment wear or formation collapse. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these simulations to field-relevant dimensions, resolving millimeter-scale drill bit interactions with kilometer-scale geological features, and iterating across probabilistic subsurface scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for drillers to minimize non-productive time, extend equipment lifespan, and prevent groundwater contamination. By enabling precise, data-driven adjustments during drilling, this research will advance the technical rigor of well construction practices, reduce operational costs by an estimated 15–20%, and align with global sustainability goals by lowering the ecological footprint of hydrocarbon and water extraction. The resulting open-source models and datasets will serve as a foundational resource for future innovations in drilling technology education and industry workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, maintain, repair, and operate well drilling equipment; locate, drill, construct, and develop water, gas, and oil wells; and test and monitor wells to ensure adequate flow. Includes applications to home, business, and industrial uses.

abstract: Maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes are shaped by complex biological, social, and environmental interactions that challenge traditional analytical methods. Current approaches often fail to integrate multi-dimensional data—such as clinical, genomic, and socioeconomic variables—limiting the capacity to predict adverse outcomes or tailor interventions effectively. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address these gaps through advanced computational modeling. The research will focus on analyzing large-scale datasets, including electronic health records, geospatial public health data, and longitudinal cohort studies, to identify risk factors for preterm birth, maternal morbidity, and disparities in pediatric health outcomes. Machine learning techniques, such as ensemble models and neural networks, will be applied to develop predictive tools for early risk stratification. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model community-level impacts of policy interventions, such as nutrition programs or prenatal care expansions, on health equity. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, optimizing hyperparameters in complex models, and executing computationally intensive simulations across diverse demographic scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for clinical use, actionable insights into intervention scalability, and open-source computational tools for MCH research. By integrating multi-disciplinary data with advanced analytics, this work aims to advance precision public health strategies, reduce inequities, and inform policy decisions to improve health trajectories for vulnerable populations. The requested computing infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of models, ensure reproducibility, and support the translation of research findings into scalable maternal and child health solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of terrorist network dynamics and threat evolution, addressing critical gaps in counterterrorism intelligence and operational planning. Terrorist organizations increasingly exploit decentralized structures, encrypted communications, and adaptive financing strategies, rendering traditional analytical methods insufficient for real-time threat assessment. The study will integrate multi-source datasets—including dark web activity, financial transaction records, and social media metadata—to develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating terrorist network behaviors under varying counterterrorism scenarios. Computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale unstructured data, training graph neural networks (GNNs) to detect latent network relationships, and running Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in threat trajectories. HPC resources will enable parallelized ABM executions across parameter spaces capturing cultural, psychological, and geopolitical variables, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze multilingual extremist content for sentiment and intent patterns. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for identifying network resilience points, forecasting regional threat hotspots, and optimizing resource allocation for border security and cyberdefense operations. By mapping financial flow interdependencies and communication cascade effects, the models will inform policies to disrupt recruitment cycles and weapon procurement channels. This work directly supports the Homeland Security mission to mitigate asymmetric threats through data-driven decision-making, with model outputs designed for integration into existing incident command systems and joint operations platforms. The computational infrastructure will be shared with partner agencies to enhance collaborative threat analysis capabilities, establishing a foundation for adaptive, AI-enhanced counterterrorism strategies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the study of terrorism as a global and national threat and the methods for analyzing and countering it. Includes instruction in psychology, cultural studies, terrorist history and organization, terrorist capabilities, terrorist finance and international money-laundering, threat assessment, intelligence operations, incident command systems, border security, emergency response, joint operations, surveillance and communications systems, cyberterrorism, weapons of mass destruction, counterterrorist operations, and applications to specific terrorist organizations and threats.

abstract: Cybersecurity defense strategies increasingly rely on dynamic, data-driven policy frameworks to address evolving threats, yet existing approaches often lack the computational rigor to model complex, large-scale adversarial behaviors in real-world systems. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a high-fidelity simulation environment to evaluate the efficacy of cybersecurity policies under diverse threat scenarios, with a focus on resilience metrics and adaptive response protocols. The research problem centers on the absence of scalable, empirically validated models that capture the interdependencies between human decision-making, organizational infrastructure, and adversarial innovation in cyberspace. Current policy evaluation tools struggle to incorporate real-time threat intelligence or simulate multi-vector attacks across distributed networks, limiting their utility for strategic planning. To address this, we propose a multi-layered computational framework combining agent-based modeling, graph-theoretic network analysis, and machine learning techniques to simulate threat propagation, policy interventions, and cascading systemic impacts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations of nation-state and non-state actor behaviors, analyzing petabyte-scale datasets of historical cyber incidents, and training neural networks to predict policy outcomes under uncertainty. The computational architecture will integrate game-theoretic adversarial models with probabilistic risk assessment algorithms, enabling policymakers to stress-test defense strategies against emergent attack patterns. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of validated policy simulation templates, quantitative metrics for cyber resiliency across critical infrastructure sectors, and adaptive policy recommendations informed by scenario-based sensitivity analyses. This work aims to advance cybersecurity governance by establishing a methodological foundation for evidence-based defense strategy formulation, directly supporting the development of standards for proactive vulnerability reduction and post-incident recovery. The requested resources will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling the socio-technical dimensions of cyber conflicts, ultimately contributing to more robust, agile, and empirically grounded defense policies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the intergenerational transmission and digital preservation of Indigenous Pacific cultural narratives through computational analysis of multimodal datasets, including oral histories, visual art, and linguistic records. While Pacific communities have rich traditions of storytelling as vehicles for cultural knowledge, the impacts of colonialism, globalization, and climate migration have fragmented these practices, risking irreversible loss of intangible heritage. Existing scholarship lacks scalable methodologies to systematically analyze patterns in narrative structures, symbolic motifs, and language use across dispersed communities. To address this gap, we propose deploying natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques on a corpus of over 50,000 digitized records—including transcribed oral histories from 15 Pacific language groups, high-resolution scans of tapa cloth and carvings, and ethnographic field notes—held by partnering cultural institutions. High-performance computing resources are critical for training transformer-based models to identify cross-cultural narrative archetypes, semantically map region-specific metaphors related to ecological knowledge, and detect visual motifs in art that correlate with oral traditions. The computational pipeline will integrate community-defined ontologies to ensure culturally grounded interpretation. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing connections between narrative elements, ecological practices, and migration histories, as well as language-specific NLP tools for Indigenous educators. This work advances Pacific cultural studies by enabling large-scale comparative analysis while supporting community-led preservation initiatives. The requested resources will accelerate processing times for complex multimodal data by 70%, making feasible the identification of subtle patterns across terabytes of culturally significant materials.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Australasia and the Pacific Ocean, related island groups and bordering coastal regions, and including pre- and post-colonial migration patterns.

abstract: This project seeks to advance counseling psychology research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets of therapeutic interactions and client outcomes. Despite growing evidence that client-counselor dynamics and intervention timing significantly influence therapeutic success, existing studies are limited by small sample sizes and simplistic analytical methods. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating natural language processing (NLP), dynamic systems modeling, and machine learning to identify patterns in counselor-client interactions that predict resilience, symptom reduction, or premature termination. The dataset comprises anonymized longitudinal therapy transcripts (n=15,000+ sessions), client self-reports, and physiological markers (e.g., heart rate variability) from diverse populations receiving counseling for anxiety, depression, and trauma. HPC resources are critical to process speech-to-text outputs, train transformer-based models for emotion and alliance tracking, and simulate interaction trajectories using differential equations. A key innovation involves modeling therapeutic microprocesses—such as shifts in client emotional valence following specific counselor reflections—at scale, while accounting for contextual factors like cultural identity and session frequency. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly available computational framework for optimizing counseling strategies in real-world settings, (2) predictive models to guide personalized intervention timing, and (3) new insights into how ruptures and repairs in the therapeutic relationship manifest across demographic groups. By bridging counseling theory with data-driven methods, this work aims to establish best practices for computationally enhanced psychotherapy research while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for privacy and bias mitigation. Results will directly inform training protocols for counselors and adaptive digital tools to support clinical decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of psychological counseling, involving the rendering of therapeutic services to individuals and groups experiencing psychological problems and exhibiting distress symptoms. Includes instruction in counseling theory, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient/counselor relationships, testing and assessment methods and procedures, group therapy, marital and family therapy, child and adolescent therapy, supervised counseling practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: Maternal and neonatal health outcomes are profoundly influenced by complex interactions between biological, environmental, and clinical factors. Despite advances in prenatal and neonatal care, adverse outcomes such as preterm birth, intrauterine growth restriction, and neonatal sepsis remain significant challenges, particularly in underserved populations. Current risk prediction models often lack precision due to oversimplified variable interactions and limited integration of high-dimensional data, including genomics, proteomics, and real-time physiological monitoring. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to model multifactorial risks and optimize personalized care pathways using advanced machine learning (ML) and high-performance computing (HPC). The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records, longitudinal biomarker profiles, and geospatial environmental exposures—to train ensemble ML models capable of identifying high-risk pregnancies and neonates. Agent-based modeling will simulate clinical decision pathways under varying resource constraints to evaluate intervention scalability in low-resource settings. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of large-scale data integration, hyperparameter optimization for deep neural networks, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing model robustness. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early detection of perinatal complications, open-access decision support tools for clinicians, and policy-relevant insights into equitable resource allocation. By leveraging computational power to unravel complex biological-clinical interactions, this work aims to reduce disparities in maternal and neonatal outcomes while advancing nursing practice through data-driven, precision care strategies. The proposed models and tools will be disseminated via collaborations with clinical partners and repositories supporting reproducible research in maternal-child health.
cip_title: Maternal/ Child Health and Neonatal Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide prenatal care to pregnant women and to mothers and their newborn infants. Includes instruction in perinatal and newborn health assessment, stabilization, and care; pathophysiology of pregnancy, fetuses, and the newborn; clinical management of high-risk pregnancies and newborns; perinatal and neonatal technology and clinical procedures; and patient education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex challenges in international law through computational legal analysis, focusing on the dynamics of treaty compliance and state behavior in emerging domains such as cybersecurity and cross-border data governance. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on qualitative case studies or manual text analysis, limiting scalability and the ability to model systemic interactions. By contrast, this research integrates large-scale legal text corpora—including treaties, case law, diplomatic correspondence, and policy documents—with computational methods to analyze patterns of state practice, predict compliance risks, and simulate negotiation outcomes. The core computational challenge involves processing multilingual, unstructured legal texts to construct relational databases of obligations, reservations, and dispute resolution mechanisms. Natural language processing (NLP) models will be trained to identify nuanced legal arguments and temporal shifts in state positions, while agent-based modeling will simulate strategic interactions between states and non-state actors under varying geopolitical scenarios. Network analysis will map dependencies between overlapping legal regimes (e.g., trade agreements intersecting with human rights frameworks) to assess fragmentation or convergence in international norms. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses across decades of legal data and enabling real-time simulations of multilateral negotiation strategies. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for legal practitioners to quantify compliance probabilities, visualize treaty conflicts, and optimize drafting strategies for complex agreements. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between legal theory and data-driven policy design, offering novel methodologies to address 21st-century challenges where traditional legal frameworks struggle to adapt—such as regulating AI-driven disinformation or jurisdictional conflicts in decentralized digital ecosystems. By advancing computational legal analytics, this project aims to enhance the agility and predictive capacity of international law in an increasingly interconnected world.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law affecting relations between nations, the behavior of international organizations, and the international activities of private citizens and organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border information operations in geopolitical crises using computational social science methods, with a focus on real-time data integration and network analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how state and non-state actors exploit decentralized communication platforms to manipulate public perception during emerging conflicts, particularly in understudied regions where digital infrastructure intersects with fragile governance. Current models of information warfare analysis remain siloed, lacking capacity to process multilingual unstructured data at scale or model adaptive adversarial strategies in dynamic environments. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment and narrative detection in 15 languages, temporal network analysis of coordinated account behavior, and agent-based modeling to simulate crisis escalation pathways. The computational framework will ingest heterogeneous data streams—including social media posts, encrypted messaging app metadata, and satellite-derived mobility patterns—to identify latent signatures of hybrid threat campaigns. Leveraging GPU-accelerated transformer models and distributed graph databases, the system will enable near-real-time detection of influence operation patterns across terabyte-scale datasets. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of three case studies: maritime territorial disputes in Southeast Asia, election interference patterns in post-Soviet states, and humanitarian crisis narratives in the Sahel region. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational disinformation research, novel metrics for assessing information resilience in national security frameworks, and predictive models of cross-platform narrative diffusion. By advancing methodological integration between social network analysis, security studies, and AI-driven linguistics, this work aims to establish new standards for evidence-based policy responses to next-generation information threats.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the environmental and biological variables influencing human decomposition processes in diverse settings, a critical yet understudied area in mortuary science. Current methods for estimating postmortem intervals (PMIs) and optimizing body preservation techniques rely on empirical data with limited adaptability to variable conditions, leading to inaccuracies in forensic analysis and resource-intensive trial-and-error approaches in mortuary practice. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that account for complex interactions between microbial activity, tissue biochemistry, and environmental factors such as soil composition, humidity, and temperature gradients. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a multi-scale simulation approach integrating finite element analysis for thermodynamic processes in burial environments, agent-based modeling for microbial community dynamics, and machine learning to correlate decomposition patterns with contextual variables. The computational pipeline will be trained and validated against a curated dataset of decomposition timelines from diverse geographic and climatic conditions, including rare edge cases critical for forensic applications. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool for PMI estimation with quantified uncertainty intervals and evidence-based guidelines for preservation protocol adjustments in non-standard scenarios. This work bridges gaps between forensic taphonomy, computational biology, and mortuary operations, offering a novel resource for both academic research and applied funeral service contexts. The scalability of the models will also provide a foundation for future studies on eco-friendly burial practices and disaster victim identification workflows. By employing HPC to manage the high-dimensional parameter space and stochastic elements inherent to decomposition systems, this project advances computational capabilities in a specialized domain traditionally underserved by quantitative methods.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in funeral service and mortuary science not listed above.

abstract: Pediatric rheumatic diseases, including juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), pediatric collagenopathies, and musculoskeletal injury sequelae, exhibit significant clinical and molecular heterogeneity, complicating diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment optimization. Current approaches rely on generalized protocols that often fail to address individual variability in disease mechanisms or therapeutic response. This project proposes to address these challenges by integrating multi-modal clinical, imaging, genomic, and proteomic datasets to identify patient-specific molecular drivers and predictive biomarkers. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform large-scale analyses of whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, and longitudinal proteomic data from a multi-center cohort of 1,200 patients. Machine learning models (unsupervised clustering, graph neural networks) will stratify patients into mechanistically distinct subgroups, while dynamical systems modeling will simulate intracellular signaling pathways to predict treatment outcomes. A key focus involves simulating collagen-protein interactions in connective tissue disorders using molecular dynamics (MD) frameworks to assess mutation-specific impacts on tissue integrity. Computational demands include parallelized MD simulations (NAMD/AMBER) across >10,000 GPU-hours, training deep learning models on terabyte-scale multi-omics data, and Bayesian network inference for causal pathway discovery. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms to match patients with optimal biologic or small-molecule therapies, (2) novel biomarkers for early detection of treatment-resistant subtypes, and (3) atomistic insights into collagen misfolding in Ehlers-Danlos syndromes. These results will directly inform three ongoing clinical trials and refine diagnostic criteria under development by the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance. By leveraging HPC capabilities to resolve molecular complexity at scale, this work aims to advance precision medicine paradigms in pediatric rheumatology, reducing long-term disability through timely, individualized interventions.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose and treat diseases of joints, muscle, bones, and tendons in children and young adults, including arthritis, back pain, muscle strains, common athletic injuries, and collagen diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that optimize institutional decision-making in community college administration. Community colleges face complex challenges in balancing resource allocation, student success initiatives, and operational efficiency amid fluctuating enrollment, funding constraints, and evolving workforce demands. Current administrative strategies often rely on fragmented data or heuristic approaches, limiting their ability to predict outcomes of policy changes or resource distribution. To address this gap, the proposed research will integrate large-scale institutional datasets—including enrollment patterns, student performance metrics, financial records, and staffing data—into agent-based models and machine learning frameworks. These models will simulate scenarios such as the impact of targeted advising interventions on retention, the effects of budget reallocations on program viability, and the relationship between faculty workload policies and student completion rates. HPC resources are critical to process heterogeneous datasets at scale, train predictive algorithms, and run parallelized simulations that account for dynamic variables across multi-campus systems. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools to help administrators visualize trade-offs in real-time decision-making, identify high-impact interventions, and model long-term systemic risks. By enabling data-driven policy design, this work aims to enhance institutional agility, equity, and sustainability in community college leadership. The project will also contribute methodological advances in applying computational modeling to higher education administration, fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration between data science and educational leadership practices.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of administering community and junior colleges and related postsecondary systems, the study of community and junior colleges as objects of applied research, and that may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in community and junior college finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; student services; research on community and junior colleges; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex dynamics of early childhood learning environments, with a focus on optimizing pedagogical strategies for children aged 0–8 years. Early childhood education involves multifaceted interactions between instructional methods, developmental stages, and contextual factors (e.g., socioemotional, linguistic, and cognitive variability), yet existing research often relies on small-scale observational studies or simplified statistical models. These approaches struggle to capture the nonlinear, high-dimensional relationships influencing learning outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate classroom interactions at scale. The ABM component will represent individualized learner “agents” with parameters derived from real-world developmental data (e.g., attention spans, language acquisition rates, motor skills), while ML algorithms will identify patterns in multimodal datasets (e.g., video recordings of classrooms, standardized assessments, teacher logs). HPC resources are critical to support parallelized simulations of diverse classroom configurations, enabling rapid iteration of hypothetical teaching interventions (e.g., play-based vs. structured curricula) across virtual cohorts. Additionally, neural networks will be trained to predict how developmental trajectories respond to pedagogical adjustments, accounting for variables such as bilingualism, disability accommodations, and socio-economic disparities. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into the scalability of evidence-based teaching practices, personalized learning pathway recommendations, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for teacher training programs. By quantifying the impact of instructional choices on emergent classroom dynamics, this work aims to advance equitable, developmentally responsive teaching strategies while reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in real-world settings. The proposed computational pipeline will require significant memory allocation and GPU nodes to manage large-scale data processing and real-time visualization of simulation outputs.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students ranging in age from infancy through eight years (grade three), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern software systems necessitates advanced testing methodologies to ensure reliability and security. Traditional automated testing frameworks often struggle with scalability and efficiency, particularly when handling large-scale applications with extensive codebases and diverse user interactions. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven testing framework that leverages parallel processing and machine learning to optimize test case execution and prioritization. The research will focus on designing distributed algorithms capable of concurrently executing thousands of test cases across HPC clusters, coupled with predictive models trained on historical testing data to identify high-impact test scenarios dynamically. Computational workloads will be managed using containerization and orchestration tools to ensure scalability across heterogeneous environments. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to reduce testing time by orders of magnitude while maintaining comprehensive coverage, particularly for applications in critical domains such as healthcare and cybersecurity. The outcomes will include an open-source testing toolkit optimized for HPC infrastructures, empirical benchmarks comparing performance gains against conventional methods, and guidelines for adapting machine learning techniques to resource-constrained testing environments. This work will directly contribute to the field of software engineering by enabling faster development cycles, reducing operational costs, and enhancing the robustness of mission-critical systems. The requested computing resources will support large-scale simulations, model training on multi-terabyte datasets, and validation across real-world software projects.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in developing, implementing, and evaluating computer software and program applications. Includes instruction in computer programming, programming languages, databases, user interfaces, networking and warehousing, encryption and security, software testing and evaluation, and customization.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model and optimize real-time adaptive learning environments mediated by teacher assistants (TAs) in linguistically diverse K-12 classrooms. The research addresses the challenge of scaling personalized support for multilingual students, where TAs must dynamically balance instructional tasks, language translation, and behavioral cues across fluid classroom conditions. Existing tools lack predictive capacity to guide TA interventions in ways that harmonize with primary lesson flow, particularly in mixed-ability groups. We will employ high-performance computing resources to train multimodal machine learning models on synthesized datasets of classroom interactions (audio, video, and text transcripts), simulating scenarios where TAs navigate competing demands across pedagogical, linguistic, and socioemotional dimensions. Agent-based modeling will map decision trees for optimal TA response timing and modality selection, incorporating variables such as student engagement metrics, language proficiency levels, and lesson complexity thresholds. Parallelized simulations will stress-test intervention strategies across virtual classroom configurations, evaluating outcomes through computational metrics of learning equity and instructional coherence. The project further aims to prototype a low-latency recommendation system that processes real-time classroom data streams to suggest context-aware TA actions. By leveraging GPU-accelerated neural architecture search and hyperparameter optimization, we intend to reduce inference latency below thresholds that disrupt human instruction cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive models of TA effectiveness in multilingual settings, open-source simulation tools for training program development, and computational evidence for resource allocation strategies that amplify TA impacts without overburdening educators. This work bridges gaps between educational practice, cognitive science, and computational modeling, offering novel methods to study classroom dynamics at scale while respecting the nuanced human interactions central to learning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist a teacher in regular classroom settings or in providing instruction and supervision to special student populations, such as bilingual/bicultural students, special education students, adult learners, and students learning English. Includes instruction in techniques of general classroom supervision, maintaining order, assisting with lessons and carrying out related assignments.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable food systems necessitates innovative approaches to optimize post-harvest storage and reduce spoilage, which accounts for significant global food losses. Traditional empirical methods for designing storage facilities struggle to account for the complex interactions between environmental variables, crop physiology, and microbial growth. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model multi-physics processes in post-harvest environments, enabling the design of adaptive storage systems tailored to diverse climatic conditions and crop types. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), heat and mass transfer simulations, and machine learning algorithms to predict spatial-temporal variations in temperature, humidity, and gas composition within storage units. The framework will incorporate real-world data from IoT sensors monitoring existing facilities, allowing for validation and iterative model refinement. Key outcomes include predictive models for spoilage risk assessment, optimization algorithms for dynamic climate control, and scalable digital twins of storage infrastructures. By enabling precision management of post-harvest environments, this research aims to reduce food waste by up to 30% in target systems, enhance energy efficiency of cooling technologies, and provide open-source tools for global agricultural stakeholders. The computational demands of resolving fine-scale physical interactions across large, heterogeneous datasets necessitate access to HPC resources for parallelized simulations, big data analytics, and AI-driven optimization. This work bridges gaps between agricultural engineering, computational science, and sustainability, offering transformative potential for food supply chain resilience in the face of climate change and population growth.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems, equipment and facilities for production, processing, storage, handling, distribution and use of food, feed, and fiber. Includes applications to aquaculture, forestry, human and natural resources.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address high-dimensional, non-convex optimization problems arising in machine learning and data science. A key challenge in training modern neural networks or solving large-scale inverse problems is navigating complex, noisy optimization landscapes with numerous local minima. Traditional gradient-based methods often stagnate in these settings, while stochastic or metaheuristic approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs when applied to high-dimensional systems. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid framework integrating stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics with parallel tempering techniques, enhanced by algebraic topology tools to characterize landscape connectivity. The research will implement and test these algorithms on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, leveraging distributed memory architectures for parallel sampling and ensemble-based exploration of parameter spaces. Key innovations include adaptive temperature scheduling via reinforcement learning and the application of persistent homology to map metastable regions in optimization trajectories. The computational workload involves large-scale matrix computations, Monte Carlo simulations, and topological data analysis, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and high-throughput interconnects. Expected outcomes include robust optimization algorithms with demonstrably faster convergence rates on benchmark tasks such as training transformer-based models and solving ill-posed imaging problems. By unifying probabilistic sampling, geometric analysis, and parallel computing, this work aims to advance both theoretical understanding of non-convex optimization and practical tools for data-intensive applications. The resulting software will be released as an open-source library optimized for HPC environments, with potential impacts in autonomous systems, computational biology, and climate modeling. Successful implementation requires allocation of 200,000 node-hours to evaluate scalability on problems exceeding 10^6 dimensions, alongside storage for terabyte-scale optimization trajectory datasets.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and computer science or a specialization which draws from mathematics and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of groundwater contamination risks in anthropogenically altered watersheds. Human activities such as industrial discharge, agricultural runoff, and urbanization increasingly interact with subsurface geological systems, creating complex contamination pathways that challenge existing monitoring and mitigation frameworks. Current models often lack the spatial resolution and integration of multi-scale geochemical, hydrological, and anthropogenic data required to predict contaminant transport in heterogeneous aquifers. To address this gap, we propose developing a coupled reactive transport model that simulates fluid flow, solute dispersion, and geochemical interactions across dynamically evolving subsurface environments. The model will integrate high-resolution LiDAR-derived topography, borehole lithology data, and time-series contaminant concentrations from field sensors, processed via GPU-accelerated geospatial analytics. Computational demands include parallelized finite element simulations of 3D Darcy flow with adaptive meshing, Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification for heterogeneous permeability fields, and machine learning-driven parameter optimization using TensorFlow-based workflows. HPC resources are critical to resolve meter-scale geological features across watershed-scale domains (>100 km²) while capturing decade-long temporal trends. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for identifying contamination hotspots, assessing remediation strategies under climate variability, and informing land-use policies to safeguard groundwater resources. This work will directly support environmental regulators and water management agencies by providing actionable, data-driven tools to mitigate risks to drinking water supplies and ecosystems. The open-source code and workflows developed will be shared via public repositories to advance collaborative research in environmental geoscience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the environmental implications of geological processes and human activities on Earth. Includes instruction in environmental/natural resource management, geographic information systems (GIS), geology, hydrology, regulatory agency compliance, hazard identification and mitigation, environmental law, environmental policy, and sustainability studies.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic administrative workflow optimization within decentralized organizational environments, a critical yet understudied challenge in business operations support. Traditional secretarial and administrative systems rely on static, rule-based protocols that struggle to adapt to real-time fluctuations in task complexity, resource availability, and cross-departmental coordination. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an adaptive workflow engine powered by machine learning and agent-based modeling, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale organizational environments and train predictive models. The computational approach integrates three components: (1) a transformer-based natural language processing pipeline to analyze unstructured communication data (emails, meeting notes, project briefs) for task prioritization signals, (2) a graph neural network to model interdependencies across 500+ concurrent administrative processes, and (3) a reinforcement learning framework to optimize resource allocation decisions under uncertainty. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing for parallelized scenario testing across synthetic and real historical datasets (spanning 2.5 million task records from 12 multinational corporations), the system will predict workflow bottlenecks with sub-15-minute granularity while maintaining 99.9% service-level agreement compliance. Expected outcomes include a novel benchmarking toolkit for quantifying administrative efficiency and an open-source framework for intelligent process orchestration. This work bridges computational social science with operations research, offering transformative potential for organizations managing hybrid workforces and rapidly evolving compliance landscapes. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive simulations of enterprise-scale workflows and achieving the millisecond-level inference speeds required for real-time decision support in production environments.
cip_title: Business Operations Support and Secretarial Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in administrative and secretarial services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize medical office workflow efficiency and patient data management using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Medical offices face growing challenges in balancing administrative tasks—such as scheduling, billing, and electronic health record (EHR) management—with patient care demands. Existing software tools often lack adaptability to dynamic clinic environments, leading to inefficiencies that impact both staff productivity and patient outcomes. This research will address these gaps by analyzing anonymized clinic operational datasets (e.g., appointment logs, EHR access patterns, and billing timelines) to model workflow bottlenecks. Leveraging HPC resources, we will implement parallelized agent-based simulations to replicate multi-staff medical office environments under varying patient loads and regulatory constraints. Machine learning models, trained on historical data, will predict no-show probabilities and prioritize task automation pathways. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be deployed to analyze unstructured clinical notes for integration with structured EHR data, enhancing interoperability. The computational scale of these tasks—particularly the simulation of clinic networks and NLP processing across millions of text entries—necessitates HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and accuracy. Outcomes will include predictive tools for resource allocation, such as dynamic staff scheduling algorithms and task prioritization protocols, validated against real-world clinic performance metrics. This work will directly support the training of Medical Office Assistant students by generating open-access, simulated training modules that reflect computationally optimized workflows. By bridging healthcare administration education with advanced computational methods, the project aims to reduce administrative burdens in clinical settings, improve patient data accessibility, and establish scalable models for clinic operations research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers and other professionals, to perform routine administrative duties in a medical, clinical, or health care facility/system office environment. Includes instruction in general office skills, data processing, office equipment operation, principles of medical record-keeping and business regulations, medical/clinical office procedures, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and evaluate machine learning models that optimize individualized instruction for middle school students with disabilities. Special education teachers face significant challenges in tailoring curricula to diverse learning needs while adhering to time and resource constraints. Traditional methods for designing individualized education plans (IEPs) rely on manual data analysis, which limits scalability and real-time adaptation. To address this, we propose a computational framework that integrates multimodal student data—including academic performance, behavioral logs, and sensory input from classroom environments—to generate dynamic, evidence-based recommendations for instructional strategies. The research will utilize neural networks and reinforcement learning algorithms to model student engagement, predict learning barriers, and simulate intervention outcomes under varied instructional conditions. High-performance computing is essential for processing large-scale datasets (spanning thousands of anonymized student records) and training complex models that account for heterogeneous learning profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source tool for generating adaptive lesson plans aligned with IEP goals, (2) quantitative insights into how specific disabilities correlate with optimal teaching modalities (e.g., visual vs. kinesthetic), and (3) a benchmark dataset for future research in special education analytics. By reducing the cognitive load on teachers and enabling data-driven personalization at scale, this work aims to improve academic outcomes for students with learning disabilities while advancing computational pedagogy as a transformative domain within teacher education. The project’s computational outputs will be validated through partnerships with six middle school special education programs, ensuring practical relevance and ethical alignment with classroom needs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Junior High/ Middle School Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in junior high/middle school. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for middle school special education; and principles of middle school instruction in specific subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of modeling complex interactions between urban microclimates, energy consumption patterns, and socioeconomic disparities using advanced data science techniques. Urban heat island effects, energy demand fluctuations, and community vulnerability metrics are typically studied in isolation, despite their interconnected impacts on climate resilience. Our research integrates heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution satellite thermal imagery, smart meter energy records, demographic surveys, and real-time IoT sensor networks—to develop a unified predictive framework that captures these multidimensional relationships. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model spatial dependencies with agent-based simulations of human-environment interactions, requiring iterative optimization across temporal scales from minutes to decades. Key challenges include processing petabyte-scale geospatial time series, resolving conflicting data resolutions through novel resampling algorithms, and maintaining interpretability in cross-domain feature engineering. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parallelized training of hybrid machine learning architectures, large-scale sensitivity analyses of mitigation scenarios, and 3D visual analytics of urban systems dynamics. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for cities to simulate the equity implications of heat mitigation strategies, such as green infrastructure placement or cooling center allocation, while accounting for feedback loops between energy systems and localized climate effects. This work advances data science methodology through its development of scalable techniques for fusing physical and social datasets, while providing actionable insights for sustainable urban planning. By bridging domains that traditionally operate in silos—climate science, energy engineering, and public policy—the project demonstrates how modern computational resources can tackle emergent, multidimensional problems at the science-society interface.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis of large scale data sources from the interdisciplinary perspectives of applied statistics, computer science, data storage, data representation, data modeling, mathematics, and statistics. Includes instruction in computer algorithms, computer programming, data management, data mining, information policy, information retrieval, mathematical modeling, quantitative analysis, statistics, trend spotting, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing leadership decision-making in international schools, where administrators must navigate complex, culturally diverse environments with varying regulatory frameworks, resource constraints, and stakeholder expectations. Existing approaches often rely on qualitative or localized data, limiting their scalability and applicability across global contexts. To bridge this gap, this research proposes a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate and analyze the impact of administrative decisions on institutional outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations that model interactions among diverse stakeholders—including staff, students, families, and policymakers—across hypothetical and real-world scenarios. These simulations will incorporate dynamic variables such as cultural norms, funding models, policy compliance, and crisis response strategies. Concurrently, ML algorithms will be trained on anonymized global datasets of school performance metrics, leadership surveys, and demographic trends to identify patterns and predict decision outcomes. The computational workflow will also leverage natural language processing (NLP) to analyze institutional policies and communication patterns across multilingual contexts. Outcomes will include a predictive toolset for evaluating resource allocation strategies, a taxonomy of decision-making risks and opportunities in cross-cultural settings, and evidence-based frameworks for adaptive leadership training. By quantifying the systemic effects of administrative choices, this project aims to enhance the capacity of international school leaders to foster equitable, resilient, and high-performing educational environments. The requested HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of millions of simulation iterations and the analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, which are computationally infeasible with standard infrastructure. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on applied research in global education leadership, offering scalable methodologies to address pressing challenges in international school administration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in international schools, the study of international education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in culture in the classroom, educational leadership, globalization, instructional design and technology, international research methods, evaluation, and education policy.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of chronic conditions among adult populations, coupled with the complexity of managing comorbidities, presents significant challenges in delivering personalized and effective nursing care. Traditional approaches to clinical decision-making often rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for individual patient variability, dynamic health trajectories, or the interplay of biological, behavioral, and environmental factors. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to model patient-specific health risks and optimize evidence-based interventions using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will leverage longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from diverse adult populations, including demographics, physiological metrics, treatment histories, and self-reported outcomes, to train machine learning models capable of predicting decompensation events (e.g., acute exacerbations of heart failure, uncontrolled diabetes) and simulating intervention outcomes. Computational methods will include ensemble learning for risk stratification, agent-based modeling to simulate care pathways under varying clinical scenarios, and Bayesian networks to quantify uncertainty in treatment responses. By parallelizing these analyses across HPC nodes, the project aims to efficiently process terabytes of multi-modal data and generate real-time decision support tools for nurses. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early intervention, dynamic care plans tailored to individual risk profiles, and scalable protocols for integrating predictive analytics into nursing workflows. This work will advance the precision of adult health nursing by bridging gaps between population-level evidence and patient-centered care, ultimately reducing preventable hospitalizations and improving long-term health outcomes. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the computational intensity of modeling heterogeneous datasets and ensuring the translational validity of these tools in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide general care for adult patients. Includes instruction in adult primary care, adult pathophysiology, clinical management of medication and treatments, patient assessment and education, patient referral, and planning adult health maintenance programs.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of decentralized decision-making in hybrid human-AI supply chain networks, an emerging interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of computational economics, behavioral operations, and machine learning. Traditional supply chain models often assume centralized control or homogeneous agent behavior, failing to capture the complexity of modern systems where human stakeholders and autonomous AI tools co-evolve under asymmetric information. The core research problem involves quantifying how trust, cognitive biases, and adaptive learning algorithms influence system-wide resilience and efficiency in such environments. To address this, we propose a multi-method computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), graph neural networks (GNNs), and inverse reinforcement learning. The ABM component will simulate interactions among 10^5+ heterogeneous agents (human decision-makers, contractual AI systems, and legacy software tools) across dynamically evolving supply networks. GNNs will be employed to analyze emergent topological patterns and predict cascading failure risks, while inverse reinforcement learning techniques will infer latent reward structures from observed human-AI negotiation behaviors. High-performance computing resources are critical for three aspects: 1) Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore parameter spaces across diverse crisis scenarios (geopolitical shocks, demand volatility), 2) Training of attention-based graph transformers on petabyte-scale synthetic interaction logs, and 3) Real-time optimization of incentive mechanisms through evolutionary algorithms with population sizes >10^4. Expected outcomes include a novel metric framework for assessing organizational "hybrid intelligence quotient" (HIQ) and actionable insights for designing AI-augmented governance protocols that balance human expertise with machine speed. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scale in modeling socio-technical supply chain ecosystems, advancing both academic understanding of human-AI collaboration dynamics and practical tools for next-generation operational resilience. Resulting datasets and model architectures will be made available through a curated open-access repository to support replication in related interdisciplinary business contexts.
cip_title: Business, Management, Marketing, and Related Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business, management, marketing and related support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of high-fidelity, real-time simulation tools for optimizing aerodynamics and thermal management in motorsports vehicles, addressing critical gaps in current computational approaches. While computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) are widely used in motorsports engineering, existing methods struggle to balance accuracy with the speed required for rapid design iteration, particularly for complex interactions between airflow, heat dissipation, and vehicle dynamics. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop coupled CFD-FEA models that simulate transient aerodynamic loads and thermal behavior under race conditions, incorporating real-world variables such as turbulent wake effects from nearby vehicles and dynamic heat transfer in braking systems. Open-source solvers like OpenFOAM and Code_Aster will be parallelized to leverage GPU-accelerated clusters, enabling parametric studies of wing configurations, duct geometries, and cooling system layouts at unprecedented resolution. Validation will occur through comparison with wind tunnel data and telemetry from track testing. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predicting aerodynamic downforce and component temperatures with sub-second latency, directly applicable to endurance racing and electric vehicle thermal management. The project will also generate open datasets to support curriculum development in vehicle simulation courses. By bridging the gap between high-accuracy modeling and practical design workflows, this work aims to reduce reliance on physical prototyping while improving race vehicle performance margins—a critical need for smaller teams with limited testing budgets. The requested computing resources will enable the exploration of design spaces that are currently computationally prohibitive, fostering innovation in a field where incremental gains determine competitive success.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: Clinical research trials generate increasingly complex datasets from diverse sources, including electronic medical records, multi-omics platforms, wearable devices, and patient-reported outcomes. Managing and analyzing these data at scale presents a critical bottleneck in trial efficiency, particularly when balancing rigorous regulatory requirements with the need for real-time insights to inform adaptive trial designs. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational pipelines for optimizing clinical trial workflows, enhancing data integrity, and enabling predictive analytics. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning models to predict patient enrollment feasibility and attrition risks using historical trial data and demographic variables; (2) implementing parallelized simulation frameworks to evaluate virtual patient cohorts under different trial protocols; and (3) establishing secure, scalable infrastructure for federated analysis of distributed clinical trial data while maintaining regulatory compliance. Computational methods will integrate Python-based machine learning libraries (TensorFlow, scikit-learn) with R-based statistical models, containerized using Docker for reproducibility. Large-scale genomic and proteomic datasets from ongoing oncology trials will serve as primary test cases. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for patient stratification, optimized trial stop/go decision thresholds, and containerized workflow templates compatible with institutional review board requirements. The HPC resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte datasets, reduce analysis latency from weeks to hours for critical safety endpoints, and support GPU-accelerated deep learning for biomarker discovery. By bridging computational innovation with clinical research operations, this work aims to establish best practices for data-driven trial management while providing Clinical Research Coordinator trainees with hands-on experience in HPC applications. The resulting frameworks will be disseminated through open-source repositories and integrated into the program’s curriculum, strengthening workforce readiness in an era of increasingly complex, data-intensive clinical research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers as clinical research administrators or clinical research coordinators where they work under the supervision of a Principal Investigator to organize, coordinate and administer clinical research trials. Includes instruction in pharmacology, medical terminology, foundations of clinical research, project management, ethics, research design and data management, and legal and regulatory compliance .

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between family dynamics and early childhood developmental outcomes using advanced computational modeling techniques. Traditional approaches in Early Childhood and Family Studies (ECFS) often struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets—spanning socio-economic indicators, parental mental health metrics, child behavioral assessments, and longitudinal developmental trajectories—into a unified analytical framework. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns and predictive relationships within these heterogeneous data streams to better understand how familial risk and protective factors influence developmental trajectories in children aged 0–6 years. To address this, we propose a multi-modal computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources.
