Machine learning pipelines will be developed to harmonize structured (e.g., survey responses, clinical evaluations) and unstructured data (e.g., natural language processing of caregiver interviews, video-coded parent-child interactions). Graph neural networks will model relational dynamics within family systems, while time-series analyses will track developmental milestones against evolving family contexts. Agent-based simulations will further explore how hypothetical interventions might alter long-term outcomes under varying socio-environmental conditions. The scale of data integration—targeting 10,000+ families across diverse demographics—necessitates distributed computing architectures for efficient feature extraction, model training, and validation. Expected outcomes include the identification of critical inflection points in early development where targeted family support could mitigate adverse outcomes, as well as open-source tools for scalable analysis of developmental datasets. By bridging computational methodologies with developmental theory, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for evidence-based family intervention strategies, advancing both methodological innovation and practical applications in ECFS.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the development and learning of children from birth to six years old within the context of the family. Includes instruction in child abuse and neglect, child and infant growth and development, early childhood education, early childhood language and literacy, early childhood math and science, early childhood special education, family literacy, family sociology, family and marriage relations, assessment and measurement, psychology, and psychopathology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay of legal, demographic, and policy data in the domain of family, child, and elder law—a field situated at the intersection of legal practice, social equity, and lifespan development. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how algorithmic bias and systemic inequities manifest within legal decision-making systems, particularly in cases involving custody disputes, elder care allocation, and child welfare interventions. Current legal databases, while extensive, lack the computational frameworks necessary to model longitudinal outcomes or simulate the cascading effects of policy changes on vulnerable populations. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) to parse unstructured court records and legal opinions, paired with agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making processes under varying policy conditions. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage large-scale datasets (spanning millions of anonymized case records) and to run iterative simulations that account for multivariate factors such as socioeconomic status, geographic disparities, and temporal shifts in judicial precedent. Additionally, graph neural networks will be trained to identify latent patterns in judicial rulings that correlate with demographic variables, enabling a quantitative assessment of equity in legal outcomes. The anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for legal researchers, designed to predict the downstream impacts of proposed legislation on family dynamics and intergenerational equity. By integrating computational social science methods with legal scholarship, this work aims to advance evidence-based reforms in family law, offering policymakers and practitioners actionable insights to mitigate systemic biases. The scalability of the proposed models will also establish a foundation for future interdisciplinary studies at the nexus of law, ethics, and computational analytics.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting domestic relations across the lifespan.

abstract: Healthcare systems face persistent challenges in dynamically allocating resources during crises, such as surges in demand or supply chain disruptions, due to the inherent complexity of modeling interdependent variables in real-world settings. This project seeks to develop an adaptive decision-support framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize resource distribution—including staff, equipment, and facility capacity—across multi-institutional healthcare networks. Current approaches often rely on static models that fail to account for real-time data streams, spatial inequities, or cascading operational bottlenecks. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient flow and staff interactions, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map inter-facility dependencies, and reinforcement learning (RL) to iteratively refine allocation policies. The ABM module will incorporate electronic health record (EHR) data, supply chain telemetry, and regional epidemiological forecasts, while the GNN-RL system will optimize for competing objectives such as minimizing wait times, balancing clinician workloads, and reducing costs. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations across thousands of scenarios, train deep learning models on heterogeneous datasets spanning 15+ hospital systems, and solve high-dimensional optimization problems with latency constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for proactive resource redistribution, predictive metrics for identifying vulnerability hotspots, and policy guidelines for crisis-responsive healthcare management. By bridging operations research, AI, and organizational theory, this work aims to advance computational methods in health administration while directly addressing systemic inefficiencies exacerbated by public health emergencies and demographic shifts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, plan, and manage health care operations and services within health care facilities and across health care systems. Includes instruction in planning, business management, financial management, public relations, human resources management, health care systems operation and management, health care resource allocation and policy making, health law and regulations, and applications to specific types of health care services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced robotic control systems for dynamic, unstructured environments using high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical limitations in real-time adaptability and energy efficiency. Current robotic systems struggle with latency and computational overhead when processing multimodal sensor data (e.g., LiDAR, vision, proprioceptive feedback) in unpredictable scenarios, such as disaster response or agricultural field operations. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining reinforcement learning (RL) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to optimize control policies and predictive maintenance protocols. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of two primary tasks: (1) training RL agents in simulated environments with variable terrain, obstacle density, and sensor noise profiles, and (2) solving inverse dynamics problems via PINNs to refine actuator torque predictions under partial system observability. Simulations will leverage NVIDIA GPU clusters for accelerated deep learning workflows, while multi-body dynamics models will run on CPU-based nodes using the ROS 2 framework with Gazebo integration. Expected outcomes include a validated control architecture capable of reducing decision latency by 40-60% compared to conventional model-predictive approaches, alongside energy-optimal pathfinding algorithms that adapt to hardware degradation patterns. The resulting open-source datasets and benchmarking tools will directly support robotics researchers in testing multi-agent collaboration strategies and failure recovery protocols. This work addresses a critical gap in deployable field robotics by providing computationally tractable solutions for systems that must balance real-time responsiveness with long-term operational reliability under resource constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using robots. Includes instruction in the principles of robotics, design and operational testing, system maintenance and repair procedures, robot computer systems and control language, specific system types and applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cardiac surgical interventions requiring extracorporeal circulation demands advanced tools to optimize perfusion strategies and mitigate risks associated with hemodynamic instability. Current clinical protocols for managing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) rely on generalized guidelines, which may inadequately address patient-specific physiological variability. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating patient hemodynamic data, fluid dynamics modeling, and machine learning to predict real-time perfusion requirements and reduce complications such as thromboembolism or organ hypoperfusion. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate multiphase blood flow through 3D-reconstructed vasculature and extracorporeal circuits under diverse physiological conditions, incorporating variables like viscosity, shear stress, and oxygen transport. A hybrid approach will combine computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine predictive models of optimal pump flow rates, anticoagulant dosing, and circuit pressure thresholds. The workflow will utilize anonymized intraoperative datasets (e.g., arterial pressure waveforms, blood gas analyses) from 500+ perfusion cases to train and validate models. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of forecasting perfusion-related complications with >85% accuracy 30 minutes prior to clinical manifestation, enabling proactive intervention. By establishing quantitative correlations between circuit dynamics and end-organ perfusion metrics, this research aims to advance personalized perfusion strategies, reduce reliance on empirical protocols, and improve neurological outcomes in cardiac surgery patients. The computational models will also inform the design of next-generation perfusion devices through virtual prototyping of cannula geometries and oxygenator configurations. This interdisciplinary effort bridges clinical perfusion practice with computational engineering, addressing a critical gap in precision perfusion medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to operate extracorporeal circulation and autotransfusion equipment during medical procedures and surgeries where the support or temporary replacement of a patient's own respiratory or circulatory system is required. Includes instruction in equipment selection and operation, physician and medical team consultation, patient condition monitoring, procedural techniques, and principles of respiratory and circulatory physiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Deaf Studies, with a focus on analyzing large-scale linguistic and cultural datasets central to American Sign Language (ASL) and the U.S. deaf community. The research problem centers on the lack of computational tools capable of processing multimodal ASL data—including video corpora, historical records, and sociolinguistic annotations—at the scale required to uncover patterns in language evolution, cultural transmission, and community-driven advocacy. Current methods for analyzing ASL’s spatial-kinetic structure and its intersection with cultural narratives remain constrained by limited processing power, hindering progress in documenting linguistic diversity and preserving deaf heritage. The proposed work will employ parallelized computational workflows to process terabytes of annotated video data, integrating computer vision techniques for sign recognition, natural language processing for gloss alignment, and graph-based models to map historical shifts in ASL usage across generations. These methods will be applied to two primary datasets: a longitudinal corpus of ASL narratives from the 20th century and a contemporary collection of digital media produced by deaf creators. By optimizing these workflows on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to achieve sublinear scaling in runtime for feature extraction and pattern detection tasks, enabling previously intractable analyses of temporal and geographic variation in ASL. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access repository of processed ASL datasets with metadata aligned to sociocultural contexts, (2) computational models identifying critical junctures in the standardization of ASL grammar, and (3) visualizations of community networks that underpinned civil rights mobilization. This work will provide novel resources for deaf education, linguistic research, and cultural preservation while demonstrating how HPC can address unique challenges in minority language studies—specifically, the need to balance computational rigor with community-centered interpretations of deaf-centric data.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the sociological, historical and linguistic aspects of the deaf and hearing impaired, and that prepares individuals to work with the deaf and hearing impaired. Includes instruction in American Sign Language, deaf studies, American deaf culture, structure of American Sign Language, history of the American deaf community, and civil rights of deaf people.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive computational framework to optimize private security patrol routes and threat response protocols in dynamic urban environments. Traditional security strategies often rely on static schedules and historical crime data, which fail to account for real-time variables such as shifting crowd densities, transient infrastructure vulnerabilities, and emerging behavioral patterns in adversarial actors. To address this gap, the research integrates agent-based modeling, geospatial risk mapping, and machine learning to simulate complex security scenarios and iteratively refine resource deployment. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-modal data streams—including IoT sensor feeds, anonymized mobility traces, and environmental context markers—while training deep reinforcement learning models to predict high-risk zones and recommend patrol adjustments with low-latency decision-making. The computational pipeline will feature parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to stress-test proposed strategies against synthetic threat landscapes, enabling probabilistic assessments of coverage gaps and response efficacy. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for generating context-aware patrol schemas that balance deterrence visibility with covert surveillance needs, alongside predictive analytics dashboards to assist human operators in interpreting model recommendations. By bridging operational security practices with computational dynamic systems theory, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for next-generation loss prevention services, with potential applications in critical infrastructure protection, event security, and hybrid human-AI patrol systems. The project’s computational demands necessitate sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and distributed memory clusters for large-scale spatial-temporal simulations, which cannot feasibly be executed on local institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine inspection, patrol and crime prevention services for private clients. Includes instruction in the provision of personal protection as well as property security.

abstract: Occupational therapy interventions for motor impairments rely heavily on observational assessments, which may overlook subtle biomechanical inefficiencies or compensatory patterns. This project seeks to address the gap in objective, data-driven tools to optimize personalized therapeutic task design for individuals with neuromuscular conditions, such as post-stroke hemiparesis or cerebral palsy. By integrating inertial measurement unit (IMU) data from patient movement trials with computational modeling, we aim to develop a predictive framework for identifying movement strategies that maximize functional independence while minimizing injury risk. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of high-frequency kinematic datasets from 200 participants across impairment severity levels, coupled with musculoskeletal simulations using OpenSim to quantify joint loading and muscle activation patterns. Machine learning models (convolutional neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees) will be trained to correlate movement features with clinical outcomes, including task completion efficiency and therapist-rated safety. The computational pipeline will further simulate adaptive equipment configurations and task modifications to recommend patient-specific adjustments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for occupational therapist assistants to quantitatively assess movement quality during therapeutic activities, reducing trial-and-error in intervention design. This interdisciplinary approach bridges rehabilitation science, biomechanics, and computational analytics, offering a novel methodology to advance precision in occupational therapy practice. The project’s scalability to other neuromotor populations and potential integration with real-time biofeedback systems underscore its broader impact on rehabilitative care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in healthcare administration by developing computational tools to optimize workflows in medical office settings. Medical office assistants and specialists manage high volumes of patient data, appointment scheduling, and resource coordination, yet existing protocols often rely on static, manual processes that struggle to adapt to dynamic patient needs or operational disruptions. To tackle this, we propose a data-driven approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and refine administrative workflows. The research will focus on three key areas: (1) constructing agent-based models to simulate patient intake, scheduling conflicts, and staff-task interactions; (2) applying discrete-event simulation to identify bottlenecks in real-time resource allocation; and (3) training machine learning algorithms on historical clinic data to predict no-show rates and optimize appointment templates. These computational methods require HPC capabilities to process large-scale datasets from electronic health records, handle parallelized simulations of multi-clinic networks, and iteratively test optimization strategies under diverse scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for reducing patient wait times, dynamic scheduling algorithms adaptable to urgent care demands, and resource allocation frameworks that balance staff workloads. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform administrative training paradigms by integrating computational literacy into medical office education, equipping future professionals with evidence-based strategies to improve healthcare efficiency. By bridging gaps between healthcare operations research and frontline administrative practices, this work aims to reduce operational costs, enhance patient satisfaction, and support scalable solutions for clinics managing resource constraints. Results will be validated through partnerships with regional healthcare providers, ensuring practical applicability for medical office specialists.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers and other professionals, to perform routine administrative duties in a medical, clinical, or health care facility/system office environment. Includes instruction in general office skills, data processing, office equipment operation, principles of medical record-keeping and business regulations, medical/clinical office procedures, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to simulate urban fire dynamics and optimize emergency response strategies under complex, real-world conditions. Despite advances in fire science, existing models often fail to account for the interplay between heterogeneous urban infrastructure, evolving fire behavior, and human evacuation patterns, leading to suboptimal resource deployment during crises. The research addresses this gap by integrating high-fidelity simulations of fire spread, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for smoke dispersion, and agent-based modeling (ABM) for crowd movement into a unified, scalable platform. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, particularly when modeling large-scale urban environments with diverse building materials, ventilation systems, and real-time meteorological data. The computational approach leverages parallelized solvers and adaptive mesh refinement to balance accuracy and efficiency, while machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs associated with uncertainty quantification across thousands of stochastic scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolset for fire departments to simulate disaster scenarios, test mitigation strategies, and prioritize infrastructure retrofits. The framework will also inform policy by identifying vulnerabilities in current fire codes related to modern urban design trends, such as high-density mixed-use developments and green building materials. By bridging fire science, urban planning, and emergency management, this work aims to reduce civilian and responder risks while enhancing community resilience. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across fire intensity, occupancy types, and suppression tactics at unprecedented resolution, providing actionable insights for fire-safe urban development.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design, installation, and maintenance of hybrid renewable energy systems through high-fidelity simulations and predictive modeling. As energy systems grow more complex—integrating solar, wind, storage, and grid interfaces—the need for precision in installation practices and failure prediction becomes critical. Current methods often rely on static guidelines or reactive maintenance, leading to inefficiencies and downtime. This research addresses these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic energy system behaviors under variable environmental and load conditions. Computational workflows will simulate component interactions, degradation patterns, and fault propagation across photovoltaic arrays, wind turbines, and battery systems using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Machine learning models trained on synthetic and field-collected data will predict equipment failures and recommend preemptive maintenance schedules. Additionally, the project will develop digital twin prototypes for real-time performance monitoring, integrating IoT sensor data streams with physics-based simulations. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal installation configurations for diverse geographic and climatic contexts, reducing trial-and-error in field deployments. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools for technicians to visualize stress points in energy systems, predictive maintenance algorithms tailored for small-scale renewables, and a database of failure thresholds for common components. By bridging computational modeling with applied technical training, this work aims to advance workforce readiness in deploying resilient, efficient energy infrastructure while providing a scalable framework to support the renewable energy transition.
cip_title: Energy Systems Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: The development of advanced materials with tailored electronic and mechanical properties is critical for next-generation optoelectronic and energy-harvesting technologies. A key challenge in materials chemistry lies in predicting and optimizing the behavior of nanostructured semiconductors under operational stresses, particularly for systems such as transition metal chalcogenide nanowires and hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites. These materials exhibit complex structure-property relationships influenced by defects, interfacial strain, and dynamic lattice interactions, which are difficult to resolve experimentally at the nanoscale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multiscale simulations that bridge quantum mechanical effects, mesoscale carrier dynamics, and macroscopic mechanical responses. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations will parameterize electronic band structures and defect energetics, while machine-learned interatomic potentials will enable large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model strain-induced phase transitions and degradation pathways. Charge transport properties will be evaluated via nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) methods coupled with kinetic Monte Carlo sampling to account for disorder effects. The computational workflow will target two material systems: (1) doped ZnO nanowires for ultraviolet photodetectors, focusing on dopant clustering impacts on carrier mobility, and (2) lead-free perovskite analogs for solar cells, quantifying ion migration barriers under mechanical bending. By correlating atomic-scale features with device-scale performance metrics, this work aims to establish design rules for synthesizing robust, high-efficiency materials. The HPC resources are essential for managing the ∼10^4-atom MD systems, iterative NEGF configurations, and high-throughput screening of ∼500 candidate compounds. Expected outcomes include predictive models for degradation-resistant nanowire architectures and strain-tolerant perovskite derivatives, directly informing experimental synthesis efforts in our group. These advances could enable flexible optoelectronics with enhanced longevity and efficiency, supporting applications in wearable sensors and scalable solar energy conversion.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis and study of organic or inorganic materials and their electronic, magnetic, optical or mechanical properties. Includes instruction in advanced materials for photonics, lasers, chemical sensors and arrays or nanochemistry; semiconductor nanowires; and molecular electronics.

abstract: Emerging digital marketing ecosystems require adaptive strategies to optimize cross-platform budget allocation amidst rapidly shifting consumer engagement patterns. Traditional analytical models struggle to process the high-dimensional data generated by real-time bidding systems, social media interactions, and evolving platform algorithms, leading to suboptimal resource deployment. This project proposes the development of a reinforcement learning framework enhanced by high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-platform marketing environments and identify dynamic budget allocation policies. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including clickstream data, demographic variables, and contextual ad performance metrics—to train deep reinforcement learning agents capable of navigating complex reward landscapes across competing platforms. Computational experiments will leverage parallelized architecture to run millions of simulated campaign scenarios, incorporating temporal dynamics and competitive response patterns. Key challenges involve managing sparse reward signals in high-action spaces and optimizing model inference latency for near-real-time decision support. The expected outcomes include a scalable optimization engine that reduces customer acquisition costs by at least 18% compared to static allocation baselines while maintaining adaptability to platform policy changes. By employing GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed experience replay buffers, the project aims to demonstrate how HPC infrastructures can enable novel marketing operations paradigms that balance exploration-exploitation tradeoffs at unprecedented scales. The resulting methodologies will provide actionable insights for omnichannel campaign management and establish computational benchmarks for next-generation marketing resource allocation systems.
cip_title: Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Operations, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general process and techniques of direct wholesale and retail buying and selling operations and introduces individuals to related careers. Includes instruction in the principles of entrepreneurial economics, basic sales skills, the distribution channels for goods and services, and supervised practical application experiences.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in mathematical logic—specifically in model theory and computability theory—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address problems intractable to classical analytical methods. A core challenge in modern logic involves analyzing the structural complexity of uncountable models, classifying degrees of unsolvability in recursion-theoretic hierarchies, and resolving open questions about the consistency and independence of axiomatic systems. Such problems require the systematic exploration of vast solution spaces, verification of combinatorial or infinitary constructions, and iterative testing of conjectures across parameterized scenarios, all of which exceed the computational limits of standard workstations. The proposed work will employ custom algorithms to automate the generation and analysis of mathematical structures, including fine-structure models of set theory, non-well-founded trees for independence proofs, and priority argument simulations for degree-theoretic classifications. These algorithms will integrate symbolic computation, parallelized search heuristics, and proof-assistant frameworks (e.g., Lean 4 or Coq) to ensure formal correctness. HPC resources will enable large-scale Monte Carlo simulations for stochastic model construction, distributed computation of consistency thresholds in forcing extensions, and efficient SAT-solving for propositional encodings of logical satisfiability problems. Expected outcomes include resolving conjectures in the stability hierarchy of infinitary theories, characterizing the computational density of Turing degrees below 0', and producing open-access datasets of axiomatic consistency results. By bridging proof-theoretic rigor with computational scalability, this project aims to expand the methodological toolkit of pure logic research while contributing foundational insights to areas such as algorithmic meta-mathematics and the philosophy of mathematical practice. The requested resources will directly support the parallelization of memory-intensive tasks, with an estimated need for 50,000 core-hours and 2 TB of distributed memory to accommodate iterative model-checking and proof-tree generation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study foundations of mathematics, including model theory, recursion theory and set theory.

abstract: The increasing demand for high-integrity welded joints in advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, and robotic automation requires precise control of welding processes under complex multi-physics conditions. However, traditional experimental methods and low-fidelity simulations struggle to resolve dynamic interactions between thermal gradients, phase transformations, residual stresses, and molten pool behavior at the spatiotemporal scales relevant to industrial applications. This project seeks to address these challenges through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled modeling of arc welding processes, with a focus on optimizing parameter selection and predicting defect formation in multi-pass steel welds. A coupled computational framework will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer and stress evolution, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for melt pool dynamics, and machine learning (ML) for rapid parameter optimization. High-resolution simulations will capture microstructural changes during rapid solidification using CALPHAD-based phase prediction tools, while parallelized thermal-mechanical models will quantify distortion and residual stress accumulation across sequential weld passes. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of 3D transient simulations with adaptive meshing, particularly when analyzing the effects of process variables (e.g., travel speed, current waveform) on defect susceptibility metrics like hot cracking indices. Validation will leverage experimental data from in-situ monitoring systems, including high-speed imaging and acoustic emission sensors. Expected outcomes include a predictive digital twin framework capable of reducing trial-and-error prototyping by 40-60% for complex joint configurations, as well as new insights into process-structure-property relationships for emerging wire-arc additive manufacturing applications. By enabling atomistic-to-macroscale simulations on timescales aligned with industrial R&D cycles, this work will directly support workforce training in computational welding engineering and advance the adoption of AI-driven process control systems in welding technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the design and engineering of welding and joining systems and the implementation of welding processes. Includes instruction in materials science; computer-aided design; welding design; welding processes; welding metallurgy; automation and robotics; and codes, inspections, testing, and quality assurance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Italian dialectal variation and its historical evolution, a critical yet underexplored area in Italian linguistics. Traditional dialectology relies on manual comparison of phonetic, lexical, and morphosyntactic features across regions, a process limited in scalability and precision when applied to large corpora spanning centuries. Our work addresses this gap by developing automated methods to map and quantify linguistic shifts in digitized texts and speech recordings from diverse Italian dialects, including those underrepresented in existing studies. The project employs neural language models fine-tuned on historical and contemporary dialectal data to identify patterns of divergence and convergence, supplemented by phylogenetic algorithms to model evolutionary relationships. A key innovation involves integrating geographic information systems (GIS) with linguistic features to visualize spatial-temporal dynamics of dialectal change. The computational demands are significant: training transformer-based models on heterogeneous, multilingual text corpora (15th–21st centuries) requires parallelized processing of terabytes of data, while phylogenetic simulations and geospatial analyses necessitate high-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated dialectal features linked to geographic and historical metadata, (2) predictive models of language contact effects in border regions, and (3) methodological frameworks for computational philology applicable to other low-resource languages. This work will enable unprecedented granularity in tracing Italy’s linguistic diversity, offering insights into sociocultural influences on language change. By bridging digital humanities and Italian studies, the project aims to reshape pedagogical tools for dialect preservation and inform policy supporting minority languages. The scale of data processing and model training involved makes HPC resources indispensable to achieving these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Italian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in supervisory decision-making processes within K-12 educational settings by developing computational models to optimize resource allocation and instructional leadership strategies. School administrators face complex challenges in balancing personnel assignments, professional development investments, and curricular alignment amid dynamic institutional constraints. Traditional qualitative approaches to these problems often lack scalability and predictive precision, particularly in diverse or under-resourced districts. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a two-phase computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, an agent-based modeling framework will simulate interactions between administrators, teachers, and students across varied demographic and resource scenarios, incorporating longitudinal data on staffing patterns, student outcomes, and budget parameters from state education databases. Second, machine learning techniques will analyze the simulation outputs to identify patterns in effective supervisory strategies, with particular attention to equity in resource distribution and curriculum implementation fidelity. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of modeling thousands of interdependent variables across multi-year timescales in simulated school systems. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs in supervisory approaches and predicts the downstream impacts of leadership decisions on instructional quality metrics. This work will provide education administrators with evidence-based frameworks for strategically allocating human and material resources while maintaining compliance with instructional standards. By bridging computational social science with educational leadership theory, the project aims to advance data-driven supervision practices that enhance curricular coherence and operational efficiency in diverse educational contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise instructional and support personnel at the school building, facility or staff level. Includes instruction in the principles of staffing and organization, the supervision of learning activities, personnel relations, administrative duties related to departmental or unit management, and specific applications to various educational settings and curricula.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions rely on personalized strategies to optimize patient independence, yet current methods for assessing environmental adaptations and assistive technologies remain limited by subjective or lab-based evaluations. This project addresses the critical need for data-driven, dynamic models to simulate real-world interactions between individuals with disabilities and their environments, enabling evidence-based recommendations for adaptive tools and home modifications. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop a computational framework integrating biomechanical movement analysis, environmental sensor datasets, and machine learning (ML) to predict functional outcomes under diverse scenarios. The research will utilize anonymized motion-capture data from clinical OT assessments (n=500+ participants) to train deep neural networks that model upper-limb kinematics during activities of daily living (ADLs). Concurrently, physics-based simulations will replicate home environments in a virtual space, testing how assistive devices (e.g., reachers, adaptive utensils) and architectural modifications (e.g., ramp angles, counter heights) influence task performance metrics. HPC capabilities are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of environmental configurations, and optimizing ML architectures via distributed training. Expected outcomes include: 1) a predictive tool to recommend personalized assistive technologies based on individual motor patterns and environmental constraints, 2) quantitative guidelines for home modifications that reduce injury risks while maximizing independence, and 3) open-source simulation modules for OT practitioners to virtually test intervention strategies. By bridging computational modeling and rehabilitation science, this work will establish a novel paradigm for precision occupational therapy, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice while advancing adaptive design innovation. The scalability of the framework will support future expansions into neurological recovery trajectories and population-level accessibility analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist patients limited by physical, cognitive, psychosocial, mental, developmental, and learning disabilities, as well as adverse environmental conditions, to maximize their independence and maintain optimum health through a planned mix of acquired skills, performance motivation, environmental adaptations, assistive technologies, and physical agents. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, psychology, sociology, patient assessment and evaluation, standardized and non-standardized tests and measurements, assistive and rehabilitative technologies, ergonomics, environmental health, special education, vocational counseling, health education and promotion, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of disease registry data, driven by heterogeneous multi-modal datasets (genomic, clinical, socio-environmental), demands advanced computational infrastructure to enable real-time analytics and predictive modeling. Current registry systems often rely on static, siloed datasets, limiting their ability to integrate emerging data types or support dynamic risk stratification for rare diseases. This project seeks to develop a scalable, machine learning-driven framework for harmonizing and analyzing high-dimensional registry data, with a focus on optimizing early detection of atypical disease progression patterns in autoimmune disorders. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address three core challenges: (1) processing unstructured clinical notes and imaging data at scale using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision pipelines, (2) training ensemble models to predict treatment-resistant disease phenotypes by integrating longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data with sparse multi-omics datasets, and (3) implementing federated learning architectures to enable cross-registry collaboration while maintaining data privacy compliance. Computational workflows will utilize containerized environments on GPU clusters for deep learning tasks, with Spark-based distributed processing for feature engineering across terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive registry data management, validated predictive models for identifying high-risk autoimmune cohorts 6-12 months earlier than current standards, and benchmarking data on HPC resource requirements for real-time registry analytics. This work bridges gaps between clinical informatics, computational biomedicine, and data engineering, offering a template for next-generation registry systems capable of supporting precision public health initiatives without relying on traditional population-health methodologies. Results will directly inform the development of a pilot registry for rare autoimmune diseases in partnership with three academic medical centers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to find, interpret, and record demographic and medical information on individuals for healthcare agencies and disease registries. Includes instruction in anatomy, data management, disease registry organization and operations, epidemiology, ethics, fundamentals of disease coding and staging, medical terminology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, physiology, quality management, and statistics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems demands advanced methodologies to optimize diagnostics, maintenance, and repair processes. Traditional approaches, which rely heavily on manual inspection and static failure prediction models, often lack the precision to address dynamic operational stressors such as thermal fluctuations, mechanical wear, and transient electrical loads. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and analyze failure mechanisms in electrical equipment, enabling data-driven predictive maintenance strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will employ multiphysics simulations—integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal behavior—to replicate real-world operating conditions of critical components like circuit boards, motor drives, and power distribution systems. These simulations will generate large datasets characterizing component degradation under diverse stress profiles. Machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), will then be trained on this data to identify early failure signatures and predict remaining useful life. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational intensity of iterative simulations and optimizing hyperparameters for the machine learning models. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive maintenance toolkit that reduces unplanned downtime in industrial and commercial electrical systems, as well as actionable insights into material and design improvements for fault-tolerant equipment. This work will directly inform curriculum enhancements in electrical repair technology programs, equipping technicians with advanced diagnostic proficiencies aligned with Industry 4.0 standards. By bridging computational engineering with applied repair methodologies, the project aims to elevate the precision and sustainability of electrical infrastructure management.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modern plumbing systems, including inefficiencies in water distribution, energy consumption, and susceptibility to leaks or pressure failures in complex piping networks. Traditional design and maintenance approaches often rely on static codes and empirical guidelines, which may not account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, aging infrastructure, or climate-driven stressors. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models for optimizing plumbing system performance, resilience, and sustainability. The research will employ multiphysics simulations, including computational fluid dynamics (CFD), to analyze turbulent flow, pressure gradients, and thermal interactions in large-scale residential and commercial systems. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to predict failure risks by training on synthetic and real-world datasets of pipe corrosion, joint stress, and water quality degradation. Additionally, graph-based algorithms will model network topologies to identify optimal layouts that minimize resource waste while adhering to safety standards. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the high resolution required for 3D pipe geometry simulations, the combinatorial complexity of network optimization, and the iterative nature of predictive analytics. Outcomes will include open-access tools for simulating system behavior under diverse operational scenarios, data-driven recommendations for code updates, and training modules to enhance plumbing education with digital twin technologies. By enabling precise, scalable analysis of plumbing infrastructure, this work aims to reduce water and energy waste in building systems, lower maintenance costs, and support the transition to sustainable urban water management practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice as licensed plumbers by applying technical knowledge and skills to lay out, assemble, install, and maintain piping fixtures and systems for steam, natural gas, oil, hot water, heating, cooling, drainage, lubricating, sprinkling, and industrial processing systems in home and business environments. Includes instruction in source determination, water distribution, waster removal, pressure adjustment, basic physics, technical mathematics, blueprint reading, pipe installation, pumps, welding and soldering, plumbing inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) and pediatric cardiopulmonary diseases represent complex, heterogeneous conditions requiring personalized approaches to diagnosis and management. Current clinical strategies often rely on generalized risk models, which inadequately account for patient-specific anatomical, hemodynamic, and genetic variability. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating high-fidelity cardiovascular simulations, machine learning, and multi-omics data to predict disease progression and optimize therapeutic interventions in pediatric patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct patient-specific 3D models from cardiac MRI/CT data, simulate hemodynamics using computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and analyze longitudinal clinical datasets. Deep learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns in imaging, electronic health records, and genomic data associated with adverse outcomes in hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) and pulmonary hypertension. Multi-scale models will evaluate surgical planning scenarios, such as Fontan procedure modifications, by simulating postoperative hemodynamics across virtual patient cohorts. The computational pipeline will also integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data from pediatric myocardium samples to map molecular pathways driving disease heterogeneity. By coupling these approaches, the project aims to generate predictive tools for risk stratification, identify novel biomarkers, and establish a platform for in silico testing of treatment strategies. The proposed work addresses critical gaps in translating complex datasets into actionable clinical insights, with potential to reduce invasive procedures and improve long-term outcomes. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities to manage large-scale simulations (>10,000 core-hours), optimize machine learning architectures, and process multi-terabyte imaging/genomic datasets. Outcomes will advance precision medicine in pediatric cardiology by enabling data-driven, individualized care while fostering computational methods applicable to other congenital and acquired cardiovascular disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases and disorders of the cardiovascular and cardiopulmonary systems of infants, children, and adolescents. May include related research in public health and community medicine issues.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic pathogens at the interface of wildlife, livestock, and human populations present complex challenges to global public health and food security. Current epidemiological models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic, multi-host transmission networks, environmental drivers, and heterogeneous data sources, limiting their utility in predicting outbreak trajectories or optimizing intervention strategies. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to model zoonotic disease transmission dynamics, with a focus on pathogens impacting both animal health and food safety (e.g., Salmonella, avian influenza). Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement spatially explicit agent-based models (ABMs) integrating real-world datasets on livestock movements, wildlife habitat overlap, climate variables, and genomic surveillance data. These models will simulate pathogen spread across species barriers, incorporating stochastic transmission events, host immunity landscapes, and anthropogenic factors such as agricultural practices. Parallelized parameter sweeps and Bayesian calibration methods will be used to infer transmission pathways and identify high-risk spatiotemporal interfaces. Additionally, machine learning approaches will analyze model outputs to prioritize surveillance targets and forecast intervention efficacy under varying scenarios. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the ABMs operating at regional scales with millions of agents and the integration of high-dimensional genomic and environmental data—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and storage. Outcomes will advance predictive capacity for zoonotic hotspots, inform One Health policies to mitigate cross-species transmission, and provide actionable insights for veterinary public health practitioners. This work will also establish an open-source toolkit for adaptive disease modeling, enhancing collaborative responses to emerging threats at the intersection of animal and human health.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, and Public Health
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the prevention and control of communicable animal diseases, diseases affecting humans, and prepares veterinarians to function as public health specialists. Includes instruction in animal epidemiology, biostatistics, food safety and quality assurance, food toxicology, zoonotic and infectious diseases, disease vectors and transference, production medicine, animal health, veterinary public health practice, and inspection and evaluation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for the analysis of understudied African languages and their oral and written literatures. Despite the continent’s linguistic diversity—encompassing over 2,000 languages—many remain underrepresented in digital corpora, hindering advances in comparative linguistics, dialectology, and the preservation of endangered oral traditions. Current tools for automated text and speech analysis are often ill-suited to African languages due to structural complexities such as agglutinative morphology, tonal systems, and non-Latin scripts. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop scalable pipelines for processing multilingual datasets, including digitized oral narratives, historical manuscripts, and contemporary texts across Niger-Congo, Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan language families. Computational methods will include the training of transformer-based models for low-resource machine translation, phonological pattern recognition using parallelized acoustic analysis, and graph-based algorithms to map syntactic and semantic shifts in literature across time and dialects. By optimizing these workflows for distributed memory architectures, the project aims to process terabytes of heterogeneous data (audio, text, and video) while integrating community-sourced annotations from native speakers. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for cross-linguistic African language analysis, a federated database of annotated literary works, and empirically grounded insights into the evolution of narrative structures in Sahelian oral traditions. These resources will directly support philological research, pedagogical tool development, and the decolonization of linguistic technologies, ensuring equitable access to computational methods for Africanist scholars and speech communities. The project’s scale—spanning 40+ languages and 15 TB of primary data—necessitates HPC infrastructure to manage memory-intensive tasks, reduce latency in model training, and enable real-time collaboration across geographically dispersed research teams.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the African continent, including, but not limited to, Bantu languages, Nilo-Saharan languages, Niger-Congo languages, Khoisan languages, and the Chadic and Ethiopic languages of the Hamito-Semitic language family. Includes instruction in philology, dialects, and oral and written literatures.

abstract: Occupational safety in high-risk industrial environments requires advanced predictive models to anticipate and mitigate hazards arising from complex interactions between human workers, machinery, and environmental factors. Current risk assessment tools often rely on static datasets or simplified simulations, limiting their ability to model dynamic scenarios with multiple concurrent variables. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework for simulating workplace safety risks using agent-based modeling (ABM) and multi-physics simulations. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create scalable models that integrate real-time sensor data, ergonomic stressors, equipment failure probabilities, and chemical exposure dynamics. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic risk outcomes across diverse industrial configurations, while finite element analysis will model localized hazards such as structural collapses or ventilation failures in confined spaces. Validation will utilize historical incident datasets from manufacturing and construction sectors. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical to handle the computational demands of simulating thousands of interacting agents and physics-based systems at sub-second temporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for scenario-based hazard prediction, quantitative risk prioritization metrics, and optimized safety protocol recommendations tailored to variable workplace conditions. This work directly addresses gaps in proactive occupational safety planning, with potential applications in regulatory compliance, workforce training, and emergency preparedness. By enabling computationally intensive simulations previously infeasible on local clusters, the project aims to advance data-driven decision-making in occupational health, reducing preventable workplace injuries through predictive analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining job-related health and safety standards. Includes instruction in safety engineering principles, inspection and monitoring procedures, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, applications to specific work environments, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing administrative decision-making in early childhood education programs through advanced computational modeling. Early childhood administrators face dynamic pressures, including fluctuating enrollment, evolving regulatory requirements, and constrained budgets, which demand agile, data-informed strategies to allocate resources effectively. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model complex interactions between these variables at scale, leading to suboptimal program outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that integrates real-world data on enrollment trends, staffing patterns, facility costs, and compliance metrics. The platform will employ agent-based modeling to simulate program operations under diverse scenarios, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify predictive patterns in administrative outcomes. By leveraging HPC resources, the project will process large, multi-source datasets and run thousands of simulations to evaluate the impact of varying resource allocation strategies on program quality, financial sustainability, and regulatory adherence. Key outputs include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between staffing investments, facility expansions, and budget adjustments, as well as evidence-based guidelines for balancing competing priorities in early childhood program administration. This work will advance the field of educational leadership by introducing computational methods to a domain traditionally reliant on qualitative heuristics, empowering administrators to proactively address systemic challenges. The outcomes will directly inform policy discussions on equitable resource distribution and program scalability, with potential applications in state-level early childhood systems. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for these large-scale simulations, enabling rapid iteration and sensitivity analyses that would be infeasible with standard computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on early childhood educational program administration and prepares individuals to serve as a principal or director of an early childhood educational program. Includes instruction in early childhood education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, early childhood growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Ancient and Byzantine Greek textual corpora, addressing critical gaps in the scalable study of linguistic evolution, stylistic patterns, and intertextuality across millennia of Greek literature. While traditional philological methods have yielded foundational insights, the manual analysis of large, diachronic datasets remains prohibitively time-intensive, limiting systematic investigation of language change, authorial attribution, or the diffusion of literary motifs. This project will develop and apply computational workflows to analyze digitized texts spanning Archaic Greek poetry, Classical historiography, Koine biblical and patristic writings, and Byzantine chronicles. Key objectives include training machine learning models to detect syntactic and morphological shifts between dialects (e.g., Attic to Koine), quantifying stylistic divergence in disputed authorship cases, and mapping intertextual networks across genres using semantic embedding techniques. Custom NLP pipelines will be designed to handle non-standard orthography, fragmentary inscriptions, and manuscript variants, integrating existing lexica (e.g., LSJ, TLG) with context-aware neural architectures. The scale of data—corpora exceeding 100 million tokens, including multispectral imaging outputs from papyri—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which local workstations cannot support. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a diachronic corpus annotated for linguistic features, (2) open-source tools for Greek philology optimized for HPC environments, and (3) quantitative evidence resolving longstanding debates, such as the linguistic stratification of the Septuagint or the chronology of hagiographical texts. By bridging computational linguistics and classical scholarship, this work will establish reproducible frameworks for analyzing premodern languages at scale, with implications for pedagogy, critical editing, and the digital preservation of Greek literary heritage.
cip_title: Ancient/ Classical Greek Language and Literature
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Greek language and literature from its origins through the fall of the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, Attic and Hellenistic dialects, Koine (Biblical) Greek, and Medieval or Byzantine Greek.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare data ecosystems, driven by advances in interoperable health information exchange and artificial intelligence applications, has amplified vulnerabilities in patient privacy protection. Existing anonymization frameworks often fail to account for combinatorial re-identification risks arising from multimodal data integration across distributed networks. This project seeks to develop and validate a dynamic privacy-risk assessment platform capable of simulating large-scale healthcare data linkage attacks while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct a synthetic health data environment mirroring real-world patient demographics, clinical variables, and socio-geographic markers across 50 million simulated patient records. Computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks to model potential adversarial inference pathways and probabilistic re-identification surfaces across heterogeneous data types, including genomic markers, wearable device outputs, and longitudinal electronic health record data. The parallelized architecture will enable simultaneous evaluation of multiple attack vectors under varying threat models while preserving differential privacy constraints through GPU-accelerated cryptographic computations. Validation phases will benchmark performance against current de-identification standards using federated learning approaches across simulated healthcare institutions. Expected outcomes include a risk stratification framework that quantifies re-identification probabilities in emerging data-sharing contexts and an open-source toolkit for adaptive anonymization policy testing. This work addresses critical gaps in healthcare information security by providing computational tools to proactively identify privacy erosion points in next-generation health data infrastructures, ultimately supporting the development of more robust patient privacy preservation strategies in complex, interconnected care environments.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural and gendered identities within European colonial and postcolonial migrant communities through computational analysis of multilingual textual and visual archives. The research problem centers on the scarcity of large-scale, comparative studies examining how intersecting identities—shaped by colonialism, migration, and intercultural contact—were represented and contested in European diasporic communities between 1850 and 1950. Existing scholarship relies heavily on fragmented case studies, limiting systematic cross-regional and temporal analysis. To address this gap, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques on a corpus of 250,000+ digitized primary sources, including personal correspondence, community newspapers, and visual materials from underrepresented groups in French, Dutch, and British colonial contexts. Key computational tasks include multilingual sentiment analysis to trace emotional narratives of displacement, topic modeling to identify evolving discourses of belonging, and network analysis to map transnational cultural exchanges. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing non-Latin script materials (e.g., Jawi texts), training custom transformer models for historical language variants, and managing the spatial-temporal linking of heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing identity negotiation patterns across colonial hierarchies and gender divides, 2) quantitative evidence challenging Eurocentric periodizations of cultural assimilation, and 3) methodological frameworks for computationally analyzing intersectionality in historical contexts. By enabling processing at scales unachievable through manual methods, this work will provide new insights into how marginalized communities navigated European imperial structures while preserving distinct cultural practices—a critical foundation for contemporary debates on multiculturalism and postcolonial memory.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the European Continent, including the study of European migration patterns and colonial empires.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance geography teacher education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze spatial learning processes in simulated classroom environments. A critical challenge in geography education is the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to evaluate how novice teachers adapt pedagogy to diverse student needs when teaching complex geospatial concepts. Traditional training often relies on limited observational feedback, hindering personalized skill development. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate student-teacher interactions during geography lessons, incorporating variables such as spatial reasoning ability, cultural context, and prior knowledge. These models will integrate real-world geospatial datasets (e.g., climate patterns, demographic distributions) to create dynamic, scenario-based learning environments. HPC resources are essential to execute thousands of parallel simulations, testing how different instructional strategies affect student outcomes under varied conditions. Machine learning techniques will then identify patterns in effective teaching practices across simulated scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for assessing geography teaching efficacy, (2) evidence-based guidelines for tailoring instruction to student demographics, and (3) open-access training modules that prepare educators to interpret and respond to heterogeneous spatial learning needs. By bridging computational modeling and teacher education, this work will provide novel tools to improve geography instruction at scale, particularly in underserved regions where classroom diversity and resource limitations pose significant challenges. The requested resources will support data storage for multi-terabyte geospatial datasets, GPU-accelerated ABM simulations, and distributed training of deep learning models to analyze emergent patterns in pedagogical decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach geography at various grade levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding spatial and temporal population dynamics affecting public health infrastructure planning in aging populations. While demographic shifts are well-documented at macro scales, localized projections integrating real-time migration, mortality, and fertility data remain computationally constrained, limiting actionable insights for policymakers. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model subnational population changes at unprecedented granularity (census tract level) across a 20-year horizon, combining agent-based microsimulation with Bayesian hierarchical spatial-temporal models. The research will integrate multi-source data, including U.S. Census microdata, Medicare utilization records, and georeferenced vital statistics, to simulate individual life-course trajectories while accounting for spatial dependencies and uncertainty propagation. Computational challenges include parallel processing of 100+ million agent interactions per simulation year, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) parameter estimation for high-dimensional spatial models, and real-time visualization of uncertainty metrics through GPU-accelerated geospatial analytics. The HPC environment is essential for scaling ensemble simulations across parameter spaces, reducing runtime from estimated 18 months on local clusters to 6 weeks via distributed memory parallelism and optimized memory handling for terabyte-scale demographic datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source tools for adaptive demographic forecasting under policy scenarios, (2) vulnerability indices identifying regions at risk of healthcare infrastructure mismatches, and (3) validation frameworks comparing model projections against emerging migration patterns observed in the 2020s post-pandemic era. This work directly supports evidence-based decision-making for hospital capacity planning, geriatric service allocation, and regional workforce development strategies, while advancing methodological integration of demographic microsimulation with spatially explicit uncertainty quantification.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the practical application of demographic methods and materials for decision-making in business, education, health, and government. Includes instruction in statistics, research methods, geographic information systems, and demographic methods and techniques.

abstract: Critical care nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to manage patients with life-threatening conditions, yet current clinical tools for predicting patient deterioration or optimizing care plans lack the computational power to integrate multimodal, high-frequency data streams. This project seeks to address this gap by developing machine learning models capable of synthesizing real-time physiological data, electronic health records (EHRs), and longitudinal clinical outcomes to predict hemodynamic instability and sepsis in intensive care unit (ICU) patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale datasets from multiple ICUs, including high-resolution vital sign waveforms (e.g., ECG, arterial pressure), laboratory results, and nurse-documented assessments. Computational workflows will integrate time-series analysis, natural language processing for clinical notes, and ensemble learning techniques to identify early warning patterns. A key innovation involves training adaptive models that account for patient-specific variability in physiological responses, which requires iterative optimization across thousands of parallel simulations. The HPC environment is essential for handling the volume (terabytes of waveform data) and velocity (real-time processing demands) inherent to critical care datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for clinical deployment, which could reduce unplanned interventions and improve nurse-led triage accuracy. Additionally, the project will generate open-source tools for critical care data harmonization, enabling future research in nursing science. By enhancing predictive capabilities at the bedside, this work aligns with the priority of advancing evidence-based, patient-centered care in critical care nursing while addressing computational challenges unique to high-acuity clinical environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide specialized care to patients with life-threatening problems, including those in intensive care facilities and on life support. Includes instruction in adult, neonatal, and pediatric critical care; technical skills; patient monitoring and assessment; normal and abnormal readings; and troubleshooting.

abstract: The integration of advanced computational methods into traditional leatherworking and upholstery practices presents an opportunity to revolutionize material design, sustainability, and performance. This project seeks to address the lack of predictive models for leather and upholstery material behavior under mechanical stress, environmental exposure, and aging—a challenge that current trial-and-error approaches fail to resolve efficiently. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop multi-scale simulations that bridge molecular interactions, textile microstructure, and macroscopic mechanical properties.
