Computational models will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution in upholstery fabrics under dynamic loads, molecular dynamics (MD) to study the impact of tanning agents on collagen fiber stability, and machine learning (ML) to optimize hybrid material compositions for durability and eco-efficiency. These simulations require parallelized processing of large datasets to capture heterogeneous material responses across time and spatial scales, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for identifying optimal material treatments, reducing waste in prototyping, and accelerating the development of sustainable alternatives to synthetic upholstery components. The project will also generate open-access datasets on leather degradation patterns and fabric stress thresholds, fostering innovation in a field historically reliant on manual expertise. By establishing computational workflows tailored to leatherworking and upholstery, this research aims to enhance the sector’s capacity to address modern challenges in circular design and resource-efficient manufacturing.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in leatherworking and upholstering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of biomechanical modeling and neurophysiological simulations holds significant potential to advance the understanding of spinal health and chiropractic interventions. However, the complexity of modeling dynamic interactions between spinal structures, neural pathways, and manual adjustment techniques necessitates high-resolution computational approaches that are currently underdeveloped in pre-chiropractic research. This project proposes the development of a multi-scale computational framework to simulate spinal biomechanics and their effects on nervous system function, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in mechanistic knowledge. The research problem centers on characterizing how vertebral misalignments (subluxations) alter stress distribution across spinal tissues and modulate afferent signaling to the central nervous system, a process hypothesized to underlie chiropractic therapeutic outcomes. The computational approach combines finite element modeling of spinal segment mechanics with machine learning-driven analysis of neural network responses to simulated adjustments. High-fidelity models of lumbar and cervical spine segments will be constructed using clinical imaging data, incorporating material properties of intervertebral discs, ligaments, and musculature. Concurrently, neural network models will simulate somatosensory processing under varying biomechanical conditions. HPC resources will enable parameter optimization across millions of potential adjustment scenarios, coupled with real-time visualization of tissue strain patterns and neural activation profiles. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific adjustment parameters to neurobiomechanical responses, quantitative safety thresholds for spinal loading, and evidence-based frameworks for optimizing manual therapy protocols. The computational tools developed will also serve as educational resources for pre-chiropractic students, enhancing their understanding of spinal pathophysiology through interactive simulations. By bridging biomechanical and neurological perspectives, this work aims to strengthen the scientific foundation of chiropractic medicine while demonstrating the transformative potential of computational methods in manual therapy research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in chiropractic medicine.

abstract: Integrative medicine emphasizes holistic, evidence-based care that addresses the complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors influencing health. A critical challenge in advancing this field lies in analyzing multidimensional datasets—such as electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, lifestyle logs, and patient-reported outcomes—to identify personalized treatment pathways while preserving the centrality of the practitioner-patient relationship. Current computational methods struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale, limiting the ability to model dynamic interactions between interventions, patient biology, and environmental contexts. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive frameworks for optimizing integrative treatment strategies. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining mechanistic modeling of physiological networks with machine learning-driven analysis of clinical and multi-omics data. Agent-based models will simulate patient-specific responses to combined conventional and complementary therapies, while natural language processing tools will extract qualitative insights from practitioner notes and patient narratives. Graph neural networks will map relationships between treatment components, biomarkers, and long-term health outcomes across diverse demographic groups. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of large-scale EHR datasets (from 50,000+ patients), real-time optimization of treatment combinations, and sensitivity analyses across hypothetical clinical scenarios. By enabling the integration of sparse, high-dimensional data sources, this approach aims to identify reproducible patterns in treatment efficacy, predict adverse event risks for complex intervention bundles, and uncover novel biomarkers of therapeutic synergy. Successful implementation will produce an open-source framework for designing personalized integrative care plans, validated through retrospective analysis of existing clinical cohorts and pilot prospective trials. This work directly supports the development of evidence-based protocols that balance systemic healing with precision medicine principles, ultimately strengthening the scientific foundation for whole-person care in clinical practice.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine in a way that reaffirms the importance of the relationship between practitioner and patient; focuses on the whole person; is informed by evidence; and makes use of all appropriate therapeutic approaches, healthcare professionals, and disciplines to achieve optimal health and healing.

abstract: Agricultural enterprises face increasing pressure to optimize production, supply chain efficiency, and economic resilience amid fluctuating market demands, climate variability, and resource constraints. This project seeks to develop a computational decision-support framework for agricultural business planning by integrating large-scale datasets on market trends, regional production capacities, and operational logistics. The research addresses a critical gap in dynamic, systems-level modeling tools tailored to agricultural management, which currently rely on oversimplified economic assumptions or static analyses. We propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach coupled with machine learning (ML) to simulate interactions between producers, distributors, and markets under diverse scenarios, including price volatility, input shortages, and policy changes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the stochasticity and scale of these simulations, which involve thousands of autonomous agents representing farms, processing facilities, and transportation networks across multi-year horizons. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will quantify risk exposure and evaluate mitigation strategies, while graph neural networks will identify latent dependencies in supply chain data. The project will utilize agricultural census records, commodity pricing APIs, and geospatial operational data from partner cooperatives. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational framework to test business diversification strategies, (2) predictive metrics for supply chain vulnerability under climate-induced disruptions, and (3) open-source optimization tools for cost-risk tradeoff analysis in crop selection and contract farming. By enabling real-time scenario testing at unprecedented resolution, this work will empower agricultural managers to make data-driven decisions that balance profitability with operational adaptability. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as a template for integrating ABM and ML in agribusiness research, fostering collaboration between computational scientists and agricultural economists.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on modern business and economic principles involved in the organization, operation, and management of agricultural enterprises.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing athletic performance and injury prevention through advanced computational modeling of biomechanical and physiological data. Despite advances in sports science, current methods for analyzing dynamic movement patterns, muscle activation, and tissue stress under real-world conditions remain limited by the computational complexity of integrating heterogeneous datasets—including motion capture, wearable sensor outputs, and physiological biomarkers—into predictive frameworks. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to simulate multi-scale interactions between biomechanical loads, metabolic demands, and neuromuscular adaptations during sport-specific activities. The computational approach will leverage agent-based modeling and finite element analysis to simulate tissue-level responses to repetitive athletic motions, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal athlete performance data. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, the platform will enable real-time analysis of high-dimensional datasets, a critical requirement for personalized training recommendations. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying injury risk thresholds for specific movement patterns and a decision-support tool for coaches to tailor conditioning programs. This work will advance the field of sports science by establishing a scalable, data-driven framework for injury mitigation, while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in addressing understudied computational challenges at the intersection of kinesiology, biomechanics, and performance analytics. The resulting methodologies will be disseminated through open-source tools adaptable to diverse athletic populations, offering novel insights into human movement optimization beyond conventional empirical approaches.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sports, kinesiology, and physical education/fitness, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making processes in private security services administration, addressing the challenge of dynamically allocating resources across complex, multi-threat environments. Traditional security management relies on heuristic strategies and static risk assessments, which struggle to adapt to evolving threats, heterogeneous client needs, and real-time operational constraints. The proposed research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate large-scale security scenarios, integrating stochastic threat modeling, agent-based simulations of personnel and asset deployment, and predictive analytics to evaluate risk mitigation outcomes. Key computational components include Monte Carlo methods to model probabilistic threat occurrences, graph-based algorithms to map interdependencies between client sites and security resources, and reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize allocation policies under uncertainty. The framework will process real-world datasets—including historical incident reports, geospatial threat intelligence, and operational logs—to parameterize simulations and validate models. By scaling these analyses across thousands of parallelized scenarios, the project aims to identify robust allocation strategies that balance cost, response efficacy, and adaptability across diverse client portfolios. Anticipated outcomes include a modular software toolkit for security administrators to test allocation policies in virtual environments, reducing trial-and-error in high-stakes settings. This work bridges computational modeling and security operations management, offering a novel methodology to quantify trade-offs in resource-limited contexts while advancing the integration of HPC into non-traditional, service-oriented domains. The results will provide actionable insights for private security firms seeking to enhance operational resilience through data-driven decision support systems, with potential applications in critical infrastructure protection, corporate security, and event risk management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and supervise services providing private security protection for people and property and related investigative and consulting functions. Includes instruction in security and loss prevention services, private security and investigation techniques, security technologies, personnel management, business operations, marketing, applicable law and regulations, and client relations.

abstract: Cardiovascular diagnostics increasingly rely on integrating multi-modal data—such as hemodynamic waveforms, intravascular imaging, and patient-specific biomarkers—to guide interventions. However, current analytical workflows remain fragmented, limiting the ability to predict acute procedural outcomes (e.g., stent failure or arrhythmia risk) in real time. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for synthesizing high-dimensional cardiovascular datasets acquired during catheterization lab procedures, enabling dynamic risk stratification and decision support. The core challenge lies in processing heterogeneous data streams (optical coherence tomography, pressure wire measurements, electrocardiograms) with low-latency demands, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose a hybrid machine learning architecture combining convolutional neural networks for image analysis and graph-based models to capture temporal dependencies in physiological signals. This approach will be trained on a retrospective cohort of 1,200 procedural datasets (totaling ~350 TB), with validation against prospective cases. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized feature extraction and real-time inference, while federated learning techniques will address data privacy constraints. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of predicting complications (e.g., coronary dissection or plaque shift) with ≥85% accuracy within 5 seconds of data acquisition, compared to current manual methods (60-75% accuracy, 10-15 minute delays). Success would directly enhance the safety of complex interventions by providing cardiovascular technologists and physicians with actionable insights during critical procedural steps. The project also establishes a scalable infrastructure for integrating emerging data types (e.g., shear stress simulations) into peri-procedural analytics, advancing the translational potential of cardiovascular technology in precision medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform invasive, noninvasive, and peripheral examinations of the cardiovascular system at the request of physicians to aid in diagnoses and therapeutic treatments. Includes instruction in reviewing and recording patient histories and clinical data, patient care, investigative and examination procedures, diagnostic procedures, data analysis and documentation, physician consultation, equipment operation and monitoring, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The spatial and temporal regulation of cell behaviors during embryonic development remains a central question in developmental biology. A critical gap exists in understanding how mechanical forces and cellular interactions drive large-scale tissue morphogenesis, particularly during organ formation and axis patterning. This project seeks to address this problem by developing a three-dimensional computational model of vertebrate gastrulation, integrating live-imaging data from avian embryo studies with biomechanical simulations. The proposed high-performance computing (HPC) framework will employ agent-based modeling to simulate individual cell dynamics—including adhesion, polarity, and cytoskeletal forces—coupled with continuum-level finite element analysis to resolve tissue-scale stress patterns. A key innovation involves parameterizing the model using empirical measurements of cell stiffness, traction forces, and junctional remodeling from time-lapse light-sheet microscopy of chick embryos. The computational pipeline will systematically test hypotheses about how local cell behaviors propagate to global tissue rearrangements, specifically examining the role of planar cell polarity in mesoderm migration and neural fold elevation. Resource-intensive aspects include parallelized simulation of 10^5–10^6 interacting cellular agents across developmental timeframes and machine learning-based optimization of force calibration parameters. Successful implementation will provide mechanistic insights into conserved morphogenetic processes while identifying potential biomechanical drivers of congenital malformations such as neural tube defects. The HPC environment is essential for handling multiscale simulations spanning minutes to hours of developmental time, which exceeds the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. Outcomes will yield both a predictive tool for perturbing morphogenetic events and a publicly accessible database of simulated force maps correlated with experimental phenotypes, advancing interdisciplinary approaches in developmental cell biology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of embryology, development, and growth of animals and human beings. Includes instruction in fertilization, oogenesis, histogenesis, gastrulation, and cell differentiation; embryological development including organ and pattern formation, morphogenesis, gene regulation, cell lineage, and fate maps; disease and defect studies; transgenic and evolutionary models of growth and development; and applications to specific organisms and phyla.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of digital curation and preservation workflows in fine and studio arts institutions, which face challenges in managing large-scale multimedia archives, optimizing resource allocation, and mitigating risks associated with digital asset degradation. As galleries, museums, and community arts organizations increasingly rely on digitized collections and born-digital artworks, traditional management strategies struggle to account for the computational demands of high-resolution 3D modeling, AI-driven metadata generation, and predictive conservation analytics. We propose developing a machine learning framework to automate the analysis of preservation priorities across heterogeneous digital collections, utilizing high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train models on terabyte-scale datasets of 2D/3D artworks, conservation records, and environmental sensor data. The computational pipeline will integrate computer vision techniques for material degradation prediction, natural language processing for donor/funder sentiment analysis in archival grant applications, and agent-based modeling to simulate long-term storage cost scenarios under varying institutional budgets. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU clusters, the project aims to reduce processing times for complex conservation risk assessments from weeks to hours while improving accuracy. Outcomes will include open-source tools for arts administrators to optimize digital preservation budgets, prioritize high-risk collections, and forecast infrastructure needs. This work directly supports the program’s focus on financial management and operational efficiency in visual arts organizations, offering scalable computational strategies to bridge gaps between curatorial practice, technological capacity, and sustainable arts advocacy. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive rendering tasks and large-scale optimization models that cannot feasibly run on institutional workstations, ensuring replicability across diverse arts management contexts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage fine and studio art organizations, operations, and facilities. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; public relations and arts advocacy; arts law; and applications to specific arts activities such as galleries, museums, studios, foundations, and community organizations.

abstract: The fragmented documentation and increasing endangerment of many Uralic languages necessitate advanced computational approaches to address unresolved questions in their historical development, structural variation, and sociolinguistic vitality. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support large-scale comparative analyses of Uralic languages, focusing on under-resourced varieties such as Eastern Sami, Karelian dialects, and Mansi. The research integrates computational phylogenetics, corpus linguistics, and machine learning to model language diversification, contact effects, and morphological complexity. Key objectives include reconstructing proto-Uralic syntactic features using Bayesian inference, automating morphological segmentation of agglutinative paradigms via transformer-based models, and simulating language shift dynamics through agent-based modeling. HPC infrastructure is essential for processing multilingual text corpora (including digitized historical manuscripts and modern oral narratives), training neural networks on non-standard orthographies, and running computationally intensive phylogenetic algorithms across language subgroups. The project will also develop a centralized digital repository for annotated linguistic data, enabling reproducible analyses and collaborative contributions. Expected outcomes include novel insights into the genealogical relationships among Uralic languages, computational tools for low-resource language documentation, and evidence-based frameworks for evaluating revitalization strategies. By combining traditional philological expertise with cutting-edge computational methods, this work aims to significantly advance the preservation and interdisciplinary study of Uralic languages while addressing methodological gaps in linguistic resource allocation for endangered language communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Uralic languages, including, but not limited to, Finnish, Estonian, Karelian, and Sami. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize resource allocation strategies for community colleges facing dynamic enrollment patterns, funding fluctuations, and equity-driven mandates. Community college administrators must balance competing priorities—such as expanding access, maintaining program quality, and addressing workforce demands—with limited budgets and heterogeneous student needs. Current decision-making tools often rely on static datasets or simplified heuristics, which inadequately capture the complex interdependencies between institutional policies, student outcomes, and fiscal constraints. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based simulations that integrate multi-year institutional data (e.g., enrollment trends, course completion rates, staffing costs) with stochastic models of external factors like state funding cycles and local economic shifts. The simulations will test scenarios such as reallocating faculty workloads, scaling student support services, and prioritizing infrastructure investments under varying constraints. Machine learning techniques will then identify patterns in simulation outputs to recommend adaptive, data-informed strategies. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce runtime from weeks to hours, enabling rapid iteration of policy alternatives. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for administrators to visualize trade-offs between equity, efficiency, and financial sustainability in real time. This work will advance the operational scalability of community college leadership by grounding strategic planning in systems-level computational analysis, ultimately supporting institutions in achieving their mission of accessible, high-quality education amid resource scarcity. The project aligns with national priorities to strengthen community college resilience through evidence-based administration.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of administering community and junior colleges and related postsecondary systems, the study of community and junior colleges as objects of applied research, and that may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in community and junior college finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; student services; research on community and junior colleges; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern automotive systems, including hybrid and electric vehicle architectures, demands advanced computational tools to optimize performance, durability, and sustainability. Current empirical methods for diagnosing and improving automotive systems—such as engine efficiency, battery thermal management, and aerodynamic design—are often resource-intensive, time-consuming, and limited in predictive accuracy. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate and optimize critical automotive subsystems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these limitations. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) multi-physics simulations of combustion engines and electric drivetrains to assess energy efficiency under dynamic operating conditions, (2) machine learning-driven predictive maintenance frameworks for hybrid vehicle battery systems, and (3) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analyses of vehicle aerodynamics to reduce drag and improve energy consumption. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA), CFD, and neural network training on HPC clusters, the project aims to create scalable models that account for real-world variability in environmental conditions, material wear, and driver behavior. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from industry partners, ensuring practical relevance. Expected outcomes include optimized design parameters for next-generation automotive components, predictive algorithms for early fault detection in electrified powertrains, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulation templates for educational use in automotive technology programs. This work will directly address workforce training gaps by enabling students and technicians to engage with high-fidelity virtual prototyping tools, reducing reliance on physical testing infrastructure. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the parallel processing demands of coupled simulations and large-scale parameter sweeps, which are infeasible with local computing infrastructure. By bridging automotive engineering principles with advanced computational methods, this project aims to accelerate the adoption of data-driven practices in automotive repair, manufacturing, and technician education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of automobiles. Includes instruction in brake systems, electrical systems, engine performance, engine repair, suspension and steering, automatic and manual transmissions and drive trains, and heating and air condition systems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial systems necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize workflows that integrate human and technical factors. Traditional methods often fail to account for dynamic interactions between workforce behavior, equipment variability, and process constraints, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and operational inefficiencies. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions among workers, machinery, and environmental variables within manufacturing environments. Large-scale parameter optimization, utilizing parallelized genetic algorithms, will identify configurations that maximize productivity while minimizing ergonomic risks and downtime. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to historical operational data to predict bottlenecks and recommend adaptive scheduling strategies. The computational demands of simultaneously modeling thousands of interacting agents, combined with real-time optimization across multidimensional design spaces, require the distributed memory architecture and GPU acceleration capabilities of HPC systems. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for industrial planners that demonstrates ≥15% efficiency improvements in simulated production lines, with particular emphasis on human-factor integration. The results will contribute novel methodologies for cyber-physical system optimization in industrial technology applications, bridging the gap between theoretical optimization models and practical implementation constraints. By enhancing the capability to model complex socio-technical systems, this research aims to provide actionable insights for workforce management and capital investment decisions in medium-to-large-scale manufacturing enterprises.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of industrial engineers and managers. Includes instruction in optimization theory, human factors, organizational behavior, industrial processes, industrial planning procedures, computer applications, and report and presentation preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in obstetrics and gynecology by developing predictive models for adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly preterm birth, which affects 10% of pregnancies globally and remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity. Current clinical tools lack accuracy due to the multifactorial etiology of preterm birth, involving complex interactions between genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, and environmental factors. To address this, we propose integrating multi-omics data (whole-genome sequencing, placental methylome profiles, and serum proteomics) with clinical electronic health records (EHR) and ultrasound imaging data from a longitudinal cohort of 5,000 patients. The computational demands of harmonizing high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets and training deep learning models necessitate scalable HPC infrastructure. Our approach will employ transformer-based architectures to process temporal EHR data, convolutional neural networks for imaging analysis, and graph neural networks to model gene-environment interactions. Bayesian optimization will be used for hyperparameter tuning across >10,000 parallelized simulations. The project will validate models using external cohorts from diverse populations to ensure generalizability. Successfully identifying predictive biomarkers and risk stratification frameworks will enable earlier, targeted interventions, potentially reducing preterm birth rates and associated healthcare costs. Additionally, the computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other obstetrical challenges, such as preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in overcoming data complexity and scaling barriers in maternal-fetal medicine, directly aligning with national priorities to improve perinatal outcomes through innovation in clinical informatics.
cip_definition: Research focused on Obstetrics and Gynecology

abstract: This project seeks to advance health services research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multi-source healthcare datasets, with the goal of identifying drivers of disparities in care access, quality, and outcomes. A key challenge in this field is integrating heterogeneous data—including electronic health records (EHRs), insurance claims, socioeconomic indicators, and public health surveillance data—to model complex interactions between patient characteristics, systemic factors, and health service utilization. Traditional computing infrastructures struggle with the volume and velocity of these datasets, particularly when analyzing unstructured clinical notes, geospatial trends, or longitudinal outcomes across millions of patients. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP) for clinical text mining, Bayesian hierarchical models for spatial-temporal analysis, and machine learning (ML) to predict care gaps and simulate intervention impacts. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, training of deep learning models on GPU clusters, and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in policy-relevant scenarios. The project will focus on case studies in maternal health and chronic disease management, examining how facility capacity, insurance networks, and social determinants influence avoidable hospitalizations and mortality. Expected outcomes include predictive models for service demand, optimized resource allocation strategies for underserved regions, and open-source tools for scalable health services analytics. By facilitating rapid analysis of nationally representative datasets, this work will provide actionable evidence for policymakers and health systems aiming to reduce inequities. The requested computing resources are critical to overcoming memory and runtime constraints, ensuring robust statistical inference, and generalizing findings across diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on basic and applied inquiry, that examines access to, and the use, costs, quality, delivery, organization, financing, and outcomes of health care services to produce new knowledge about the structure, processes, and effects of health services for individuals and populations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of patient care data, including multi-modal electronic health records (EHRs), wearable sensor outputs, and medical imaging, presents challenges in deriving actionable insights for clinical decision-making. Current analytical approaches in nursing research often lack the computational capacity to integrate these heterogeneous datasets at scale, limiting predictive accuracy for patient outcomes and care optimization. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning models for real-time risk stratification of hospitalized patients, with a focus on preventable adverse events (e.g., falls, pressure injuries, and medication errors). The research will employ ensemble learning techniques to fuse EHR temporal data, continuous physiological monitoring streams, and nurse-documented contextual factors, while addressing class imbalance through synthetic minority oversampling. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate clinical workflow patterns to identify staffing and resource allocation strategies that minimize care delays. Computational demands include training deep neural networks on longitudinal patient data (n ≈ 250,000 encounters), processing high-frequency sensor inputs via time-series analysis, and running Monte Carlo simulations for workflow optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for adverse event risks with improved sensitivity over existing tools, (2) quantitative evidence for nurse-to-patient ratio adjustments in dynamic care environments, and (3) open-source pipelines for processing nursing-specific data types at scale. By enabling analysis of previously intractable datasets, this HPC-supported approach will advance precision nursing interventions and inform health system policies. The computational workflows will be designed for eventual translation to hospital-edge computing systems, ensuring practical applicability to bedside care.
cip_title: Registered Nursing, Nursing Administration, Nursing Research and Clinical Nursing, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in registered nursing, nursing administration, nursing research, and clinical nursing, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of diagnostic ambiguity in autoimmune and immune-mediated disorders, where overlapping clinical presentations and heterogeneous biomarker profiles often delay accurate classification. Current clinical laboratory practices rely on static thresholds and linear interpretations of biomarkers, which inadequately capture the dynamic, multifactorial nature of these conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a machine learning framework that integrates high-dimensional clinical laboratory data—including flow cytometry, proteomic arrays, and epigenetic methylation profiles—with patient-specific histopathological image features extracted from biopsy slides. The computational workflow will involve training ensemble models on GPU-accelerated clusters to identify latent patterns across disparate data modalities, coupled with graph neural networks to model immune system interactivity. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, optimizing hyperparameters through parallelized Bayesian search, and simulating perturbation responses in synthetic patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool that stratifies patients into molecularly defined subgroups, correlates these subgroups with treatment response trajectories, and generates interpretable feature importance maps for clinical translation. This work bridges gaps between experimental laboratory medicine and computational systems biology, offering a template for redefining diagnostic paradigms in complex disorders through data integration. The resulting models and pipelines will be shared via open-source platforms to enable validation studies across institutions, potentially reducing diagnostic delays and enabling precision therapeutic strategies for patients with currently enigmatic immune pathologies.
cip_title: Clinical/ Medical Laboratory Science and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in clinical/medical laboratory science and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Ophthalmic diseases, including age-related macular degeneration, glaucoma, and diabetic retinopathy, present complex pathophysiological mechanisms that require advanced computational modeling to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes. Current limitations in analyzing high-resolution multimodal imaging data, genomic associations, and dynamic biomechanical interactions during ocular surgeries hinder progress in personalized treatment strategies. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through three interconnected computational workflows. First, a deep learning framework will process terabyte-scale datasets from optical coherence tomography (OCT) and adaptive optics retinal imaging, identifying subclinical disease biomarkers through 3D convolutional neural networks. Second, whole-genome sequencing data from multicenter cohorts will undergo parallelized association studies to map genotype-phenotype interactions in rare ocular disorders. Third, finite element modeling of corneal and scleral biomechanics will simulate outcomes for novel minimally invasive glaucoma surgery techniques under varied intraocular pressure conditions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing GPU-accelerated image analysis pipelines, running genome-wide association studies with population-scale imputation, and executing iterative computational fluid dynamics simulations. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models for early disease detection, identification of therapeutic targets through pathway enrichment analysis, and optimization of surgical parameters to reduce postoperative complications. By integrating these computational approaches, the project aims to advance precision medicine in ophthalmology, directly addressing critical gaps in managing visually impairing conditions. Resource allocation will enable processing times under 24 hours for complex simulations that would otherwise require weeks on standard clinical workstations, significantly accelerating translational research timelines. All code and validated models will be shared through open-source platforms to benefit the broader vision research community.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders, and ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in eye surgery.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven simulation framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, multi-stakeholder construction projects, with a focus on mitigating cascading delays caused by supply chain volatility and workforce availability constraints. Traditional construction scheduling tools often rely on static critical path methods, which inadequately address real-time disruptions in complex, interdependent workflows. The proposed computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to create adaptive resource allocation strategies that account for stochastic material delivery delays, labor productivity variations, and equipment downtime patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training deep RL agents on historical project data while simultaneously simulating thousands of concurrent construction process interactions across temporal and spatial dimensions. The framework will incorporate domain-specific constraints from construction contracts, safety regulations, and environmental compliance requirements through hybrid neural network architectures. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of predicting resource bottlenecks 72-96 hours in advance and generating prioritized reallocation strategies that minimize project-wide schedule impacts. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of three completed megaprojects (valued >$500M) and real-time testing on active hospital construction sites. This research advances computational construction management by bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and machine learning, with potential applications in disaster recovery logistics and infrastructure resilience planning. The HPC component enables exploration of emergent project behaviors at unprecedented scale, providing foundational insights into complex adaptive systems within built environment delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage, coordinate, and supervise the construction process. Includes instruction in commercial, residential, mechanical, highway/heavy civil, electrical, environmental, industrial, and specialty construction; facilities management; budgeting and cost control; logistics and materials management; organization and scheduling; personnel management and labor relations; site safety; construction contracting; construction processes and techniques; and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural drivers of population decline and social resilience in rural agricultural communities through advanced computational modeling of multi-decadal demographic and environmental datasets. Rural regions face compounding challenges from aging populations, outmigration, and climate variability, yet existing studies often analyze these factors in isolation due to data complexity and computational constraints. We propose to develop an integrative agent-based model simulating household-level decision-making processes related to migration, land use, and community participation across spatial and temporal scales. The model will incorporate high-resolution agricultural census records (1990–2020), climate projections, and survey data on gender-specific labor patterns from six U.S. Midwest states. Key computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data formats at scale, implementing parallelized Monte Carlo methods for parameter estimation, and analyzing emergent patterns through network analysis of community connectivity metrics. High-performance computing resources are essential to process 50+ TB of geospatial data, run sensitivity analyses across 10,000+ parameter combinations, and detect nonlinear feedbacks between crop yield volatility and youth retention rates. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in land consolidation processes that accelerate community dissolution, (2) gender-differentiated models of adaptation strategies during economic transitions, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic visualization of rural social-ecological systems. By bridging computational social science with rural sociology, this work will advance theoretical understanding of how demographic shocks propagate through kinship networks and institutional structures, while providing methodological innovations for scaling qualitative fieldwork insights to regional policy-relevant simulations. Results will directly inform curriculum development in computational rural studies and establish a replicable framework for analyzing community vulnerability across diverse agrarian contexts.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the structure and function of rural societies. Includes instruction in sociological theory, research methods, statistics, sociology of agriculture, community development, social and economic development, demography, rural poverty, gender roles in rural societies, and environmental sociology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges of analyzing large-scale digitized textual corpora and historical documents using advanced computational methods to uncover patterns in cultural, linguistic, and editorial practices. While digital archives and born-digital texts offer unprecedented access to materials, their size, complexity, and heterogeneous formats—including manuscript images, OCR outputs, and multi-version editions—exceed the capacity of conventional tools. Existing workflows struggle to integrate textual criticism with computational analysis, particularly when handling non-standardized orthographies, marginalia, or multi-layered annotations. To bridge this gap, the project proposes a hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and network analysis, deployed on high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Key tasks include training custom transformer models for semantic and stylistic analysis of historical texts, constructing graph-based representations of intertextual relationships across corpora, and automating collation of variant manuscript versions at scale. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of image-based texts, optimizing OCR correction pipelines, and running computationally intensive tasks such as topic modeling across multilingual datasets. The project will also develop open-source tools to visualize textual variants and editorial decisions in interactive formats, enhancing scholarly collaboration. Anticipated outcomes include new methodologies for reconciling computational scalability with humanistic interpretability, a publicly accessible framework for dynamic archival curation, and case studies demonstrating how HPC-enabled analysis can revise understandings of textual transmission in understudied genres. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to establish scalable, interoperable practices for digital textual scholarship while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue between the humanities and computer science.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on digital textual editing, archiving, and publishing, and on the study of new media and computing platforms from the perspectives of the humanities and computer science. Includes instruction in archiving, computer programming, cultural studies, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to address persistent oral health disparities by developing a computational framework to optimize community-level dental public health interventions. Despite advances in preventive care, inequities in dental disease burden persist, driven by complex interactions between socioeconomic factors, healthcare access, and behavioral patterns. Current intervention strategies often rely on static demographic data, limiting their adaptability to dynamic population needs. This research proposes to integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning (ML) to simulate oral health outcomes across heterogeneous populations and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of intervention scenarios. The study will utilize multi-source data, including electronic health records, census tract-level socioeconomic indicators, and geospatial access metrics, to parameterize population agents and environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations capturing longitudinal interactions among millions of agents, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize intervention parameters. Computational demands include parallel processing of stochastic simulation ensembles, real-time calibration against epidemiological surveillance data, and sensitivity analyses across diverse virtual populations. Expected outcomes include identification of context-specific intervention thresholds, predictive models for caries and periodontal disease hotspots, and policy-relevant insights into resource allocation trade-offs. The scalable computational framework will enable public health agencies to dynamically tailor preventive programs—such as fluoridation campaigns or mobile clinic deployments—to evolving community needs. By bridging clinical evidence with population health analytics, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven decision-making in dental public health, ultimately reducing preventable oral disease burden and associated healthcare costs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the formulation and delivery of public preventive and curative dental health services.

abstract: Health system pharmacy administration faces challenges in optimizing medication therapy management across diverse patient populations, particularly in balancing efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness. Current approaches often rely on retrospective analyses or simplified models that inadequately capture the complexity of real-world clinical, genomic, and operational data. This project proposes the development of a predictive computational framework to model patient-specific therapeutic outcomes and system-wide resource allocation strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-source data—including electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacogenomic profiles, drug utilization patterns, and institutional workflow logs—to train ensemble machine learning models. These models will predict individual patient responses to therapies while accounting for variables such as polypharmacy risks, drug-drug interactions, and institutional formulary constraints. A parallel computational workflow will simulate large-scale intervention scenarios, employing agent-based modeling to evaluate the impact of proposed policy changes on medication safety, staffing efficiency, and supply chain dynamics. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters for high-dimensional models, and running stochastic simulations necessitate distributed computing architectures and GPU-accelerated processing. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for personalized dosing protocols, risk stratification tools for adverse drug events, and data-driven recommendations for formulary management. By enabling real-time analysis of complex, heterogeneous datasets, this project aims to advance precision pharmacy practices, reduce preventable medication-related hospitalizations, and improve operational decision-making in health systems. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will provide a scalable template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into pharmacy administration research and practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on Health System Pharmacy Administration

abstract: Hearing aid efficacy is limited by the variability of individual auditory anatomy and the dynamic acoustic environments users encounter. Current methodologies for hearing assessment and device fitting rely on generalized protocols, which often fail to account for patient-specific physiological factors or real-world auditory complexities. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate patient-specific cochlear mechanics and auditory pathway responses under diverse acoustic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element models of individualized ear anatomies derived from clinical imaging data and integrate them with machine learning algorithms trained on large-scale audiometric datasets. These models will simulate how different hearing aid configurations interact with anatomical variations and environmental noise profiles, enabling the optimization of signal processing parameters for personalized hearing solutions. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing capabilities to handle iterative simulations across thousands of anatomically unique cases and real-time acoustic scenarios, tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Additionally, we will employ neural networks to analyze longitudinal patient outcome data, identifying patterns in device performance tied to specific fitting strategies. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework for personalized hearing aid prescriptions, reducing trial-and-error adjustments in clinical practice. This work will advance precision audiology by bridging gaps between device technology and biological heterogeneity, while establishing scalable computational tools for future research in hearing rehabilitation. The requested resources will directly support the creation of open-source software for hearing professionals, fostering innovation in a field where computational modeling remains underutilized.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to test the hearing of, and to select, fit and dispense appropriate hearing aids for, patients. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of the ear, hearing testing, hearing aid fitting and technology, health promotion and rehabilitation, counseling and communication, business management, and professional ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop energy-efficient, secure wireless communication protocols for next-generation IoT networks using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. As IoT devices proliferate, existing protocols face critical challenges in scalability, latency, and vulnerability to adversarial attacks, particularly in dense urban or industrial deployments. Current simulations struggle to model large-scale, heterogeneous networks with realistic electromagnetic interference patterns and dynamic threat landscapes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-physics computational framework integrating finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulations with graph-based network optimization and machine learning-driven intrusion detection. The HPC implementation will enable full-wave 3D electromagnetic analysis of device interactions at city-block scales while simultaneously training neural networks on synthetic attack vectors generated via adversarial machine learning techniques. Key innovations include a hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization strategy for coupled electromagnetic-channel modeling and a federated learning architecture to preserve privacy during distributed anomaly detection training. Expected outcomes include optimized beamforming configurations that reduce interference by 30-40% compared to current LTE-M standards, real-time threat identification models with sub-millisecond latency, and open-source tools for joint electromagnetic-cybersecurity simulation. These results will directly inform hardware-software co-design strategies for 6G-enabled IoT edge devices, advancing national priorities in smart infrastructure resilience. The requested computing resources are essential given the project's scope: initial benchmarks indicate that simulating 10,000-node networks with dynamic interference requires 2.5 TB memory and 500,000 core-hours annually to achieve statistically significant results across diverse deployment scenarios. By bridging electromagnetic physics, communication theory, and cybersecurity through scalable computation, this work aims to establish new methodologies for trustworthy, spectrum-efficient IoT systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design and development of computer systems. Includes instruction in computer architecture, cybersecurity, electronic circuits, electromagnetism, electronic materials and design, micro-fabrication methods and techniques, signal and image processing, and wireless communication networks.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the capabilities of 3-D modeling and design workflows through high-fidelity simulations and resource-intensive computational analyses, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current 3-D modeling tools face limitations in efficiently processing complex geometries, simulating multi-physics interactions (e.g., thermal, structural), and optimizing designs for additive manufacturing. These challenges are exacerbated when working with high-resolution datasets from 3-D scanning or large-scale parametric models, where conventional computing infrastructure struggles with memory constraints and processing latency. To address this, the proposed research will leverage HPC resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) workflows, accelerate topology optimization algorithms, and enable real-time rendering of intricate 3-D models. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated solvers for stress-strain simulations in CAD environments, machine learning-driven mesh refinement for 3-D scanned data, and distributed computing frameworks to manage iterative design-test cycles for additive manufacturing parameter optimization. The project will validate these approaches using case studies in architectural component design and industrial tooling, where precision and material efficiency are critical. Expected outcomes include reduced computational bottlenecks in handling billion-element meshes, improved accuracy in predicting material behavior during 3-D printing, and scalable workflows for integrating multi-sensor scan data into unified models. By enhancing the speed and resolution of 3-D modeling processes, this work aims to bridge gaps between digital design and physical fabrication, directly benefiting industries reliant on rapid prototyping and customized manufacturing. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required scale of computation, enabling iterative exploration of design spaces that are currently infeasible with departmental-level hardware.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize adaptive learning systems (ALS) in diverse educational contexts, addressing the challenge of efficiently scaling personalized instruction. While ALS leverage artificial intelligence to tailor content delivery, their design and evaluation remain constrained by limited understanding of how variables such as learner diversity, content complexity, and interface dynamics interact at scale. Current studies rely on small datasets or simplified simulations, which fail to capture the nonlinear relationships influencing real-world efficacy. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate ALS behavior across heterogeneous educational scenarios. Agent-based models will represent learners, instructors, and content modules, with parameters derived from anonymized datasets of 250,000+ student interactions across K-12 and higher education platforms. Machine learning pipelines will iteratively train on these simulations to identify design patterns that maximize engagement and learning gains while minimizing computational overhead. The project will deploy parallelized simulations on HPC clusters to test hypotheses about system scalability, robustness across demographics, and real-time adaptation thresholds. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating ALS architectures, (2) evidence-based thresholds for balancing personalization granularity with system latency, and (3) performance benchmarks for ALS in underserved populations, where resource constraints amplify design trade-offs. By enabling large-scale, dynamic modeling of educational technology ecosystems, this work will provide actionable frameworks for creating equitable, computationally efficient adaptive systems, directly advancing the integration of learning science and scalable technical design.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing and integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying voltage-dependent gating in ion channels, a fundamental process in cellular bioenergetics and signaling. Malfunctions in these mechanisms are implicated in cardiac arrhythmias, neurological disorders, and other channelopathies, yet the dynamic structural rearrangements and energy landscapes governing gating transitions remain poorly resolved. We propose to address this gap through multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of potassium channels embedded in lipid bilayers, integrating atomic-scale models with electrophysiological data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform µs-to-ms timescale simulations using all-atom and coarse-grained force fields, capturing slow conformational changes during voltage sensor activation and pore opening. Enhanced sampling techniques, including adaptive biasing force calculations and metadynamics, will map free energy barriers and metastable states. Concurrently, continuum Poisson-Boltzmann and finite-element electrodiffusion models will quantify ion concentration gradients and electrostatic potentials under physiological conditions. The computational workflow will be validated against cryo-EM structures and patch-clamp recordings from collaborating experimental labs. Expected outcomes include identifying critical interactions between voltage-sensing domains and lipid membranes, predicting the structural impact of disease-associated mutations, and establishing a biophysical framework for allosteric modulation of channel function. This work will advance mechanistic models of bioelectrical signaling while providing a computational template for studying membrane protein dynamics, directly supporting the development of targeted therapies for channel-related disorders. The requested resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps and ensemble simulations that are intractable on local clusters, ensuring statistically robust sampling of rare gating events.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making for the conservation of historic urban districts, addressing the challenge of balancing structural preservation, environmental sustainability, and economic viability. Historic districts face complex pressures from climate change, tourism demands, and urban development, yet existing planning tools often lack the capacity to model interactions between material decay, socioeconomic factors, and regulatory constraints at scale. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate large-scale spatial datasets—including 3D lidar scans of building conditions, climate projections, and zoning codes—with agent-based models simulating stakeholder behaviors and long-term urban dynamics. Machine learning algorithms will predict material degradation rates across heterogeneous building facades under varying environmental scenarios, while parallelized optimization routines will identify cost-effective conservation strategies that align with preservation ethics and adaptive reuse goals. The computational workflow will be validated using case studies from three UNESCO World Heritage sites, incorporating archival records and sensor data to calibrate models. By enabling rapid scenario testing, this framework aims to reduce uncertainties in preservation planning and provide policymakers with evidence-based tools to negotiate conflicts between heritage protection and development. Outcomes will include open-source modules for heritage risk assessment and a repository of simulated conservation scenarios, contributing interdisciplinary methodologies to bridge computational science and cultural resource management. The requested HPC resources are critical to process multi-terabyte geospatial datasets and execute ensemble simulations capturing decade-scale urban transitions, tasks infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of plans to restore and maintain historic buildings, districts, and landscapes in a way that balances conservation and preservation with commercial and development interests. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation, cultural resource management, economics, historical documentation and preservation, land-use and zoning codes, public policy, public relations, real estate law, and taxation.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the preparation of history educators by analyzing the representation of historical narratives in digital educational materials at scale—a challenge unaddressed by traditional manual methods. Despite the growing availability of digitized primary sources, textbooks, and lesson plans, there is limited understanding of how systemic biases, regional variations, or shifts in pedagogical priorities manifest across these resources. This gap hinders the development of teacher training programs that equip educators to critically evaluate and present inclusive, accurate historical content. To address this, we propose a computational analysis of multilingual and multinational educational datasets using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of terabytes of text and multimedia data, including historical documents, teacher-created lesson repositories, and government-mandated curricular standards. Methods will include transformer-based models for cross-lingual semantic analysis to track narrative consistency, graph neural networks to map the evolution of historical themes over time, and clustering algorithms to identify geographic or cultural disparities in content emphasis. The computational pipeline will also simulate the impact of specific curricular biases on student learning outcomes through agent-based modeling of classroom interactions. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying representational gaps in historical pedagogy and evidence-based guidelines for revising teacher education curricula. By revealing patterns in how historical causality, marginalized perspectives, and critical thinking prompts are currently framed, this work will empower teacher candidates to design instruction that fosters nuanced historical literacy. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential given the computational intensity of training multimodal models on heterogeneous educational datasets and iteratively refining analyses across diverse sociopolitical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach history programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational model to analyze the dynamic impacts of regulatory policies and technological innovations on energy market equilibria, with a focus on renewable energy adoption and fossil fuel phase-out trajectories. The research problem stems from the need to quantify how heterogeneous firm behaviors, regulatory constraints, and resource allocation trade-offs interact across spatially distributed markets—a challenge requiring granular microeconomic simulations that exceed conventional computing capabilities. The study will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate strategic decision-making by energy producers, consumers, and grid operators under varying policy scenarios, integrated with econometric estimations of price elasticity and production cost functions derived from historical market data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across 10,000+ stochastic iterations, enabling robust sensitivity analysis of market outcomes under uncertainty. The computational workflow will leverage Bayesian hierarchical models to estimate region-specific parameters and GPU-accelerated optimization algorithms to solve large-scale Nash equilibrium problems. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting policy-induced market distortions, cost-benefit analyses of subsidy structures, and probabilistic forecasts of energy transition timelines. The project will advance applied economics methodology by demonstrating how HPC-enabled microsimulations can capture emergent phenomena in complex resource markets, providing actionable insights for regulators balancing efficiency, equity, and environmental goals. Results will be disseminated through an open-access computational toolkit for industry stakeholders and peer-reviewed publications quantifying the trade-offs between centralized planning and market-driven decarbonization pathways. This work directly addresses the program’s emphasis on technical resource allocation analysis while avoiding overlap with excluded social science domains through its strict focus on economic agents, market structures, and computational econometrics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic principles and analytical techniques to the study of particular industries, activities, or the exploitation of particular resources. Includes instruction in economic theory; microeconomic analysis and modeling of specific industries, commodities; the economic consequences of resource allocation decisions; regulatory and consumer factors; and the technical aspects of specific subjects as they relate to economic analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in science teacher education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze the complex dynamics of pedagogical decision-making and student learning outcomes in general science classrooms. Despite growing emphasis on evidence-based teaching practices, there remains a limited understanding of how science teachers integrate multidisciplinary content knowledge, contextual factors, and real-time classroom interactions to optimize student engagement and conceptual mastery. Current research methods, often constrained by small-scale datasets or simplified theoretical models, struggle to capture the nonlinear relationships and emergent behaviors inherent in science education ecosystems. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and multiscale simulations to investigate how variables such as curriculum design, teacher pedagogical content knowledge, and student prior knowledge interact to influence learning trajectories. The project will utilize HPC resources to process large-scale datasets from national science education assessments, classroom observation studies, and longitudinal teacher development programs. Parallelized simulations will model diverse classroom scenarios, while deep learning algorithms will identify patterns in teacher-student discourse and their correlations with conceptual growth. Expected outcomes include predictive models of effective instructional strategies for interdisciplinary science topics, a computational toolkit for designing adaptive teacher professional development programs, and evidence-based recommendations for aligning resource allocation with high-impact teaching practices. By elucidating the systemic interdependencies shaping science education quality, this research aims to advance both theoretical frameworks in teacher education and practical strategies for cultivating equitable, scalable science literacy. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scalability in analyzing heterogeneous educational data, directly supporting the preparation of science educators equipped to navigate evolving pedagogical challenges.
cip_title: Science Teacher Education/ General Science Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general science programs, or a combination of the biological and physical science subject matter areas, at various educational levels.

abstract: The increasing complexity of environmental and regulatory factors impacting modern mortuary practices necessitates advanced computational modeling to optimize funeral service operations while ensuring ecological and public health safety. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate decomposition processes under variable environmental conditions, assess microbial activity in human remains, and model the efficacy of emerging non-chemical preservation techniques. Current mortuary science relies on empirical, trial-and-error approaches to address challenges such as climate-driven changes in decomposition rates, pathogen transmission risks, and sustainability concerns tied to embalming fluids. These limitations hinder the industry’s ability to adapt to regulatory shifts and community expectations. Leveraging HPC resources, we propose agent-based models to map microbial ecosystems in decomposing tissue, finite element analysis to predict thermal and moisture gradients in burial and cremation environments, and machine learning algorithms to correlate environmental variables with preservation outcomes. The simulations will integrate geospatial data, climate projections, and material science parameters to generate predictive tools for optimizing mortuary workflows. Expected outcomes include scalable models for estimating decomposition timelines in diverse climates, risk-assessment frameworks for pathogen mitigation, and evidence-based guidelines for sustainable alternatives to traditional embalming. By bridging mortuary science with computational biology and environmental engineering, this research aims to advance data-driven decision-making in funeral services, reduce ecological footprints, and enhance compliance with public health standards. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets and real-time visualization of 3D decomposition dynamics—require dedicated HPC infrastructure to achieve practical, actionable results for industry stakeholders.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, General.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals for careers in the funeral service industry and for licensure as funeral service directors or morticians.  Includes instruction in the basic elements of mortuary science and the business, counseling, and operational aspects of funeral service.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to investigate the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of spinal adjustments, a core intervention in chiropractic care. Despite their clinical use, the precise mechanisms by which spinal manipulations influence joint mobility, nerve function, and musculoskeletal health remain incompletely understood. Experimental approaches face limitations in resolving real-time tissue dynamics or predicting long-term outcomes across diverse patient anatomies.
