To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) to simulate spinal adjustments at multiple scales. Patient-specific anatomical models will be constructed from anonymized medical imaging data, incorporating vertebrae, intervertebral discs, ligaments, and surrounding soft tissues. Multiphysics simulations will quantify stress distribution, joint kinematics, and neural responses during manipulation. Concurrently, ML algorithms trained on clinical datasets will identify patterns linking adjustment parameters to therapeutic outcomes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the computational burden of high-resolution simulations, iterative model optimization, and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models of adjustment efficacy and safety, which could inform personalized treatment protocols and reduce trial-and-error approaches in clinical training. By elucidating biomechanical principles underlying chiropractic techniques, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based practice, enhance educational resources for pre-chiropractic students, and contribute to interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computational biology and manual therapy. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated simulations, data storage for terabyte-scale anatomical datasets, and parallel processing for ML training, enabling advancements in both foundational knowledge and translational applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in chiropractic medicine.

abstract: Agricultural machinery plays a critical role in ensuring food security and operational efficiency, yet challenges persist in optimizing the performance, durability, and environmental impact of complex systems such as diesel engines, hydraulic actuators, and precision agriculture equipment. Current empirical methods for testing design modifications or operational parameters are time-intensive, costly, and limited in scalability. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-physics computational models that simulate the interplay of mechanical, thermal, and fluid dynamics processes in agricultural machinery under real-world operating conditions. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms, we will model combustion efficiency in diesel engines, stress distribution in tillage implements, and fluid behavior in hydraulic systems under variable loads and environmental conditions. Sensor data from field trials and IoT-enabled equipment will inform boundary conditions and validate simulations. The HPC environment is essential to handle large datasets, parallelize simulations across diverse scenarios, and train ML models to predict component wear, optimize fuel-air mixtures, and recommend maintenance schedules. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for designing more efficient machinery, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and extending equipment lifespans. This work will directly support agricultural equipment manufacturers, technicians, and farmers by providing data-driven strategies to lower operational costs and enhance sustainability. By integrating computational modeling with agricultural mechanics, the project bridges a critical gap between traditional equipment maintenance practices and advanced digital tools, fostering innovation in a sector vital to global food systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural Mechanics and Equipment/ Machine Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to maintain and repair specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment and vehicles. Includes instruction in the principles of diesel, combustion, electrical, steam, hydraulic, and mechanical systems and their application to the maintenance of terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos; irrigation and pumping equipment; dairy, feeding, and shearing operations; and processing systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced computer-aided design (CAD) and drafting workflows in engineering technology applications, particularly for complex 3D solids modeling and simulation tasks. Current CAD software tools face scalability limitations when handling high-fidelity geometric models, multi-physics simulations, or real-time collaborative design iterations, leading to productivity bottlenecks in engineering design processes. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing and optimizing parallelized computational workflows leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) implementing distributed computing frameworks to accelerate finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations integrated with CAD geometry processing, and (2) creating machine learning-enhanced algorithms for automated design optimization and error detection in large-scale assembly models. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for rendering-intensive tasks and MPI-based parallelization for parametric design studies. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation runtime for typical mechanical systems, improved accuracy in stress analysis for composite materials, and scalable solutions for collaborative CAD environments. These advancements will directly benefit engineering technology education by enabling students to work with industry-scale models and simulations, while providing a foundation for resource-efficient design methodologies applicable to renewable energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing systems. The computational workflows and benchmarking data generated will be made available as open educational resources to support CAD/CADD programs nationwide.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: Pediatric patients with complex chronic conditions, such as congenital disorders or severe asthma, require personalized care strategies that balance developmental needs, treatment efficacy, and long-term health outcomes. Current clinical decision-making tools often lack the capacity to integrate multi-modal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, and socio-environmental factors—to predict individualized treatment responses. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model pediatric health trajectories and optimize care plans using advanced machine learning (ML) and simulation techniques. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of traditional statistical methods in handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets and capturing dynamic interactions between biological, behavioral, and clinical variables. We propose a two-phase computational approach: first, training ensemble ML models on retrospective EHR data from 50,000+ pediatric patients to identify risk factors and predict treatment outcomes; second, building agent-based simulations to test hypothetical intervention scenarios in virtual patient cohorts. These simulations will incorporate developmental physiology, medication pharmacokinetics, and caregiver behavior patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the scale of data processing, parallelize model training across thousands of parameters, and run stochastic simulations with probabilistic uncertainty quantification. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for adverse event risk stratification in children under 12, (2) optimized medication dosing schedules tailored to developmental stages, and (3) a open-source simulation platform for testing nurse-led intervention strategies. By enabling data-driven personalization of pediatric care, this work aims to reduce hospital readmissions, improve quality-of-life metrics, and inform equitable resource allocation in underserved populations. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a scalable resource for future nursing research in precision health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care for children from infancy through adolescence. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting physicians, patient examination and referral, and planning and delivering health maintenance and health education programs.

abstract: The integration of multi-scale data in dermatopathology presents significant computational challenges due to the volume and heterogeneity of histopathological images and molecular datasets. Current analytical approaches lack the capacity to efficiently process and correlate these data, limiting advancements in diagnostic precision and mechanistic understanding of skin diseases. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable machine learning frameworks for multimodal data integration. Focused on conditions such as melanoma, psoriasis, and cutaneous lymphomas, the research will combine high-resolution whole-slide imaging, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and clinical metadata to identify diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. A key innovation involves training deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract spatial and morphological features from gigapixel histopathology images, which will be cross-referenced with genomic variants and immune microenvironment profiles using graph-based neural architectures. Computational workflows will employ distributed processing for image segmentation, feature alignment, and network optimization, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory environments to manage terabytes of imaging data and sparse high-dimensional omics matrices. Validation will involve retrospective cohorts with annotated clinical outcomes, with prospective deployment planned for validating automated diagnostic pipelines. Successfully linking microscopic phenotypes to molecular drivers will enable more accurate subclassification of morphologically ambiguous lesions and reveal novel therapeutic targets. Additionally, the project will establish reproducible, containerized workflows to democratize access to advanced computational tools for dermatopathology laboratories, directly enhancing training and diagnostic standardization. By addressing critical bottlenecks in data synthesis, this work aims to transform integrative diagnostics, accelerate translational research, and improve patient stratification in dermatologic care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical and microscopic diagnosis and analysis of skin diseases and disorders. May included related research in laboratory administration and the supervision and training of support personnel.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated many-body systems through advanced numerical simulations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current computational limitations. The research focuses on understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations, entanglement, and symmetry-breaking effects in two-dimensional lattice models, which are analytically intractable due to their exponential complexity. Key objectives include mapping phase diagrams of frustrated spin systems, characterizing dynamical response functions under non-equilibrium conditions, and identifying universal scaling behavior near quantum critical points. The computational approach combines tensor network methods—specifically, density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and projected entangled-pair states (PEPS)—with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations to mitigate the sign problem in fermionic systems. These methods will be optimized for parallel execution across distributed-memory architectures, with adaptive algorithms to manage memory constraints during tensor contractions. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations of lattice sizes exceeding 100×100 sites, surpassing the capabilities of existing local clusters. Expected outcomes include new insights into the stability of topological spin liquids, predictions of exotic magnetic ordering in transition metal compounds, and benchmarks for experimental studies of quantum materials. The project will also develop open-source software tools for efficient simulation of correlated systems, enhancing reproducibility in computational physics. By addressing gaps in our understanding of quantum matter, this work aims to advance theoretical frameworks for designing quantum technologies and guide the synthesis of novel materials with tailored entanglement properties. Successful execution of these simulations requires sustained access to petascale computing infrastructure, including high-memory nodes for tensor storage and GPU acceleration for iterative diagonalization routines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the theories that explain the fundamental structure of our world and the universe and which draws from physics and astronomy. Includes instruction in astronomy, calculus, cosmology, differential equations, electricity, magnetism, data analysis, physics, quantum mechanics, space science, spectroscopy, and thermal physics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the cognitive and pedagogical factors influencing the effectiveness of psychology instruction at the secondary school level. Despite the growing emphasis on evidence-based teaching practices, there remains a critical gap in understanding how dynamic interactions between teacher pedagogical strategies, student cognitive profiles, and curricular content shape learning outcomes in psychology education. The research problem centers on the complexity of these multivariate relationships, which traditional experimental methods struggle to capture due to high-dimensional data requirements and nonlinear dependencies. To address this, we propose a two-phase computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, we will implement agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations to replicate classroom interactions, integrating empirical data from teacher surveys, student assessments, and classroom observations. These simulations will parameterize variables such as instructional pacing, concept sequencing, and individual differences in metacognitive skills. Second, we will apply machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, to analyze longitudinal datasets of student performance and identify predictive patterns in knowledge retention. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling these computationally intensive processes, particularly for running parallelized ABM iterations across diverse virtual classroom configurations and training models on multimodal educational data. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated simulation environment for testing hypothetical teaching interventions, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing instructional design in psychology teacher preparation programs, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive lesson planning. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of pedagogical effectiveness, this work aims to advance personalized teacher training strategies while contributing novel computational methodologies to STEM education research. The requested resources will directly support the iterative refinement of models, enable large-scale sensitivity analyses, and reduce runtime constraints associated with complex educational datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: Our research addresses the challenge of simulating ultrafast reaction dynamics in complex molecular systems, where quantum mechanical effects and solvent interactions critically influence outcomes. Traditional computational methods struggle with the high dimensionality and electron-nuclear coupling inherent in these processes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement advanced ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations combined with machine learning-accelerated quantum mechanical potentials. By utilizing massively parallel architectures, we aim to achieve the necessary scalability to model systems such as photoactive catalysts and solvated biomolecules over experimentally relevant timescales. The computational framework will integrate time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) for electronic excitations with path-integral techniques to account for nuclear quantum effects. These simulations will elucidate the interplay between solvent dynamics and nonadiabatic transitions in determining reaction pathways and yields. Expected outcomes include predictive models for solvent-mediated charge transfer efficiencies and a quantitative understanding of quantum coherence effects in multistep reactions. The results will provide fundamental insights into designing efficient photocatalytic systems and inform synthetic strategies for controlling reaction selectivity. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the computational cost of multi-scale simulations, which require millions of core-hours to sample rare events and converge quantum dynamical observables. This work bridges critical gaps in our ability to simulate chemically relevant systems at quantum mechanical accuracy, advancing methodologies in computational physical chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of understanding and predicting the behavior of chemical systems ranging from nuclear particles to atoms, molecules, clusters, biological materials and macroscopic assemblies. Includes instruction in quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, reaction dynamics, group theory, collision theory, and polymer science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze large-scale textual datasets generated in English language arts (ELA) classrooms, with the goal of identifying patterns in instructional efficacy and student writing development. While teacher education programs emphasize pedagogical strategies for teaching composition and literary analysis, there remains a critical gap in empirically mapping how specific instructional interventions correlate with measurable improvements in student writing complexity, coherence, and genre adaptability. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume and linguistic nuance required for such analysis. To address this, we propose leveraging natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to evaluate anonymized student writing samples (n ≈ 250,000) collected over a 10-year period from diverse secondary classrooms, paired with metadata on instructional approaches. The research will employ transformer-based models (e.g., BERT, GPT-4) fine-tuned for educational linguistics to quantify syntactic complexity, rhetorical structure, and vocabulary adaptation across genres. Concurrently, graph neural networks will model the relationship between pedagogical strategies (e.g., scaffolded peer review, genre-based pedagogy) and longitudinal writing outcomes. High-performance computing resources are essential for training domain-specific language models, processing high-dimensional textual data, and running iterative simulations to identify optimal instructional pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible computational toolkit for ELA teacher educators to diagnose writing development challenges, (2) evidence-based frameworks for sequencing writing instruction across modalities, and (3) scalable metrics for assessing the impact of teacher training programs on classroom outcomes. By bridging computational linguistics with teacher education, this work aims to transform how writing pedagogy is studied and taught, ensuring pre-service teachers can leverage data-driven insights to support diverse learners.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach English grammar, composition and literature programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Abdominal radiology faces significant challenges in diagnosing complex pathologies due to the heterogeneity of anatomical structures, overlapping disease presentations, and limitations in conventional imaging analysis. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing advanced computational tools for automated, high-precision analysis of abdominal and pelvic imaging data, with a focus on improving early detection and characterization of malignancies, inflammatory conditions, and congenital anomalies. A critical barrier is the computational demand of processing high-resolution multi-modal imaging datasets (CT, MRI, PET) while integrating clinical and genomic data for personalized risk stratification. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate deep learning models optimized for abdominal anatomy. The computational workflow will include (1) federated learning across multi-institutional datasets to enhance model generalizability while preserving data privacy, (2) 3D convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms for lesion detection and segmentation in pediatric and adult populations, and (3) radiomic feature extraction pipelines to quantify spatial-temporal disease patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid processing of >50,000 annotated clinical cases and synthetic data generated through generative adversarial networks (GANs) to address class imbalances. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for differentiating indeterminate lesions, predictive models for treatment response in hepatocellular carcinoma, and open-source tools for quantitative imaging biomarker discovery. This work will directly impact clinical decision-making by reducing diagnostic delays and inter-reader variability, particularly for rare entities in pediatric abdominal imaging. The requested computing resources are essential given the project’s scale: initial benchmarks indicate a requirement for GPU-accelerated nodes with >1 PB of storage to manage the iterative training of ensemble models and whole-organ simulation workloads. Successful implementation will establish a computational framework adaptable to emerging imaging technologies in abdominal radiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the abdomen and pelvis in adults and children.

abstract: Understanding the impacts of climate change on watershed systems is critical for sustainable natural resource management, yet existing models often lack the resolution to capture complex interactions between hydrological processes, land-use changes, and extreme weather events. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate watershed dynamics under varying climate scenarios, with a focus on predicting water availability, sediment transport, and pollutant dispersion in the rapidly changing Pacific Northwest watersheds. The research will integrate multi-scale datasets, including satellite-derived land cover, regional climate projections, and in-situ hydrological measurements, to parameterize a coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical model. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale spatial heterogeneities (≤100m resolution) and temporal variability across decadal scales, leveraging parallelized simulations to evaluate mitigation strategies such as riparian buffer restoration and adaptive reservoir management. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs associated with uncertainty quantification, enabling probabilistic assessments of intervention efficacy under ensemble climate pathways. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into watershed resilience thresholds, optimized conservation planning maps for regional stakeholders, and open-source tools for scalable hydrologic modeling. By advancing predictive capabilities at the intersection of climatology, geomorphology, and resource management, this work will directly inform state and tribal natural resource policies while contributing methodological innovations to environmental computational science. The requested allocation of 200,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster will support the iterative model calibration, large-ensemble climate simulations, and machine learning workflows required to address these interdisciplinary challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of the physical environment and the solution of environmental problems, including subjects such as abating or controlling environmental pollution and degradation; the interaction between human society and the natural environment; and natural resources management. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, geosciences, climatology, statistics, and mathematical modeling.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing decentralized wastewater treatment systems to improve water recycling efficiency and pollutant removal under variable operational conditions. Current systems often struggle with dynamic influent loads, inconsistent removal of emerging contaminants (e.g., pharmaceuticals, microplastics), and energy-intensive processes, limiting scalability in resource-constrained settings. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a high-resolution computational framework integrating hydrodynamic modeling, reactive transport simulations, and machine learning (ML) to predict system behavior and identify control strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute multiphysics simulations capturing granular fluid-structure interactions in biofilm reactors, chemical kinetics of advanced oxidation processes, and transient microbial community dynamics. Coupled ML models will leverage simulation outputs and real-world sensor data to forecast treatment performance under diverse scenarios, enabling adaptive process optimization. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental pilot-scale data, including spectral imaging of biofilm architectures and high-frequency water quality measurements. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for simulating treatment units, predictive algorithms for energy-efficient contaminant removal, and open-access datasets characterizing reactor hydrodynamics. This work will directly inform the design of modular, automated treatment systems with enhanced resilience to fluctuating wastewater compositions, reducing operational costs and expanding safe water reuse in urban and agricultural contexts. By integrating HPC-driven modeling with empirical data, the project advances actionable strategies for sustainable water management aligned with circular economy principles.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and sociolinguistic mechanisms underlying second language (L2) acquisition through advanced computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. A critical challenge in the field is understanding how individual differences—such as prior linguistic knowledge, cognitive load, and social context—interact with instructional interventions to shape language learning trajectories. Existing studies often rely on small datasets or simplified models, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic, nonlinear processes inherent in L2 development. To address this gap, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets (e.g., learner corpora, eye-tracking data, and longitudinal proficiency assessments) and simulate complex acquisition processes. Computational methods will include deep learning models to identify patterns in language production across proficiency levels, agent-based simulations to explore social network effects on L2 retention, and Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify variability in learning outcomes. These approaches require parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of annotated linguistic data and iterative parameter tuning for cognitive models. The expected outcomes include (1) novel insights into how neurocognitive constraints and social interactions co-determine L2 mastery, (2) predictive frameworks for personalizing language pedagogy based on learner profiles, and (3) open-source tools for scalable analysis of multilingual datasets. By integrating psycholinguistic theory with computational rigor, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for language education while establishing a methodological bridge between humanities-driven SLA research and data-intensive computational science. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the project’s scope, enabling rapid experimentation with high-dimensional models and reproducibility across diverse learner populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, and maintenance of second languages. Includes instruction in language pedagogy, use, analysis and processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Urdu linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in scalable text processing and dialectal modeling. Urdu, a South Asian language with rich literary traditions and diverse regional dialects, presents unique challenges due to its complex morphosyntax, Perso-Arabic script, and code-switching tendencies. Current tools for automated Urdu text analysis remain underdeveloped, limiting large-scale studies of historical texts, dialect variation, and stylistic trends. Our research aims to develop a computational pipeline for analyzing Urdu corpora spanning classical poetry, modern prose, and colloquial speech. Key objectives include training transformer-based models for morphological disambiguation, dialect classification, and semantic parsing of Urdu texts, as well as deploying distributed computing frameworks to process multi-terabyte datasets of digitized manuscripts and oral narratives. The project will employ parallelized workflows to compare linguistic features across genres and temporal periods, enabling quantitative studies of stylistic evolution and dialectal divergence. Additionally, we will simulate language contact scenarios to model Urdu’s historical interactions with Persian, Sanskrit, and English. The computational demands of these tasks—including GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous text sources, and high-memory nodes for graph-based semantic analyses—necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include open-source NLP tools tailored for Urdu, a geotagged dialect corpus with phonological annotations, and quantitative frameworks for literary stylometry. This work will provide unprecedented scalability in Urdu philological research, support digital preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and establish methodological foundations for computational humanities scholarship in under-resourced languages. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary collaborations with linguists, literary scholars, and regional archives.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Urdu language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Urdu; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced predictive models and simulations for optimizing operational efficiency and customer experience in casino environments. While casino operations intersect with hospitality, entertainment, and risk management, the computational challenges inherent in modeling complex, real-time decision-making processes—spanning game dynamics, staffing logistics, and customer behavior—remain underexplored. Traditional analytical tools are insufficient for handling the scale, variability, and interdependencies of data streams generated by modern casino ecosystems, including player tracking systems, slot machine telemetry, and surveillance networks. This research addresses this gap by constructing a multi-layered computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to analyze spatial, temporal, and behavioral patterns. Key objectives include simulating crowd flow to minimize congestion, optimizing game floor layouts for revenue maximization, and predicting equipment maintenance needs to reduce downtime. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution datasets (e.g., terabyte-scale transaction logs and video analytics outputs) and iterative testing of hypothetical scenarios under varying constraints, such as regulatory changes or seasonal demand fluctuations. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for resource allocation, such as dynamic staff scheduling algorithms and real-time anomaly detection systems to mitigate fraud. By advancing computational methods tailored to casino operations, this project aims to establish a benchmark for data-driven decision-making in the gaming industry while contributing novel methodologies to computational social science and operational research domains. The scalability of the proposed models may also inform resource optimization strategies in analogous service-oriented environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in casino operations and services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the biomechanical and physiological effects of manual massage therapies on soft tissue microenvironments, addressing a critical gap in evidence-based frameworks for optimizing therapeutic outcomes. While manual therapies like myofascial release and deep tissue massage are widely practiced, their mechanisms at cellular and molecular scales remain poorly characterized due to the complexity of tissue deformation dynamics and heterogeneous biological responses. Current clinical protocols rely on empirical approaches, limiting personalization and reproducibility. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational platform integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of tissue mechanics with agent-based simulations of cellular mechanotransduction. High-resolution MRI-derived anatomical datasets will inform 3D FEM simulations of pressure propagation across muscle, fascia, and connective tissues under varying massage parameters (e.g., force vectors, duration). Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate mechanosensitive pathways in fibroblasts and immune cells to predict cytokine signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling. HPC resources are essential to resolve spatiotemporal interactions across these scales, requiring parallelized solvers for large deformation analyses and Monte Carlo sampling of biological variability. Machine learning pipelines will then identify optimal parameter combinations for target outcomes, such as reducing fibrosis or improving perfusion. Validation will utilize motion-capture-driven robotic massage actuators paired with ultrasonography and biomarker assays in human participants. By bridging biomechanics and systems biology, this work aims to establish predictive models for therapy personalization, reduce trial-and-error in practice, and elucidate mechanobiological links between manual interventions and tissue healing. The resulting computational tools will provide a foundation for advancing precision in therapeutic massage, with translational potential for rehabilitation sciences and chronic pain management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being to clients through the application of manual techniques for manipulating skin, muscles, and connective tissues. Includes instruction in Western (Swedish) massage, sports massage, myotherapy/trigger point massage, myofascial release, deep tissue massage, cranio-sacral therapy, reflexology, massage safety and emergency management, client counseling, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 10% of the global population, with heterogeneous progression rates and treatment responses that remain poorly understood. This project aims to develop predictive multi-scale models of CKD progression by integrating clinical, genomic, and imaging data to identify patient-specific drivers of renal functional decline. Current limitations stem from the computational complexity of analyzing longitudinal multi-modal datasets spanning molecular pathways, tissue remodeling, and systemic physiological changes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on linked electronic health records (n=35,000 patients), whole-genome sequences, and renal histopathology images from three prospective cohorts. Key computational challenges include (1) parallelized processing of high-resolution digital pathology slides using convolutional neural networks to quantify fibrosis and microvascular injury, (2) Bayesian network inference to map genotype-phenotype interactions across 2.1 million genetic variants, and (3) dynamic systems modeling of electrolyte homeostasis perturbations using differential equations parameterized by individual patient data. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive whole-slide image analyses, accelerating genome-wide association studies through distributed computing, and simulating multi-compartment kidney models at scale. Expected outcomes include a validated prognostic platform that predicts 5-year CKD trajectories with >85% accuracy, identifies novel biomarkers for rapid progression, and generates personalized therapeutic targets via in silico drug screening. This resource will enable clinically actionable stratification of CKD subphenotypes and advance precision nephrology through computational integration of diverse data layers. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads, high-memory nodes for genomic analyses, and scalable storage for petabyte-scale medical imaging archives.
cip_definition: Research focused on Nephrology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches in pediatric critical care, where clinical outcomes remain highly variable due to developmental, genetic, and environmental factors. A key challenge lies in integrating multi-omic data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with real-time clinical variables—such as vital signs, treatment responses, and developmental trajectories—to predict individualized risks of sepsis, organ failure, or neurodevelopmental impairment in critically ill children. Current predictive models, largely derived from adult populations, fail to account for the dynamic biological processes unique to pediatric growth stages. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining large-scale data integration, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning. Longitudinal clinical data from electronic health records (n≈10,000 patients) will be merged with single-cell RNA sequencing and plasma proteomics from a prospective cohort of neonates and children admitted to intensive care. Dimensionality reduction techniques and federated learning will address heterogeneity and missing data, while mechanistic models of immune-metabolic pathways, parameterized using patient-specific omics, will simulate pathophysiological responses under varying treatment conditions. Graph neural networks will then identify critical nodes in cross-scale biological networks predictive of clinical deterioration or recovery. These outputs will train ensemble models to stratify patients by risk and optimize intervention timing. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of omics datasets, large-scale parameter sweeps in mechanistic models, and distributed training of deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include actionable predictive tools for pediatric intensivists, reducing trial-and-error approaches to life-support decisions. By elucidating developmental stage-specific disease mechanisms, this work will also inform targeted therapeutic discovery. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to accelerate translational research in pediatric medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the comprehensive care and treatment of all aspects of human growth and development from conception through fetal life, infancy, childhood and adolescence, including preventive and therapeutic regimes. May included related research in behavioral aspects of illness, related family and community medicine issues, and emergency and critical care procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic analysis of dialectal and sociolinguistic variation in Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian (BCS) languages. While these languages share significant overlap, their regional and social dialects exhibit complex divergences in phonology, morphology, and syntax, compounded by historical, political, and cultural influences. Traditional manual analysis struggles to systematically map these variations across large, heterogeneous corpora, particularly when analyzing spoken language data or informal digital communication (e.g., social media). The proposed research will develop and apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to automate the identification and classification of dialectal features across three key dimensions: lexical choice, morphosyntactic patterns, and code-switching behaviors. Using transformer-based models fine-tuned on a curated multilingual corpus of contemporary and historical BCS texts (including transcribed oral histories, literature, and online forums), we will train dialect classification systems and conduct gradient dialectometry to quantify linguistic boundaries. Computational demands are significant due to the scale of data (10+ TB of text and audio requiring automatic alignment), the need for parallel processing of non-standard orthographies, and the iterative training of deep neural networks for low-resource language tasks. HPC resources will enable rapid experimentation with model architectures, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale inference across distributed datasets. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for BCS dialect analysis, a geotagged linguistic atlas visualizing regional variation, and novel methodologies for computational dialectology applicable to under-resourced languages. This work directly supports pedagogical tools for language learners and educators while contributing to broader debates about language standardization and identity in multilingual societies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian Languages and Literatures
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bosnian, Serbian and/or Croatian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address a foundational challenge in normative ethics: evaluating the scalability and coherence of moral frameworks when applied to complex, dynamic systems. Traditional philosophical methods, which often rely on abstract thought experiments or localized case studies, struggle to model the emergent behaviors and unintended consequences that arise when ethical principles are operationalized at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational approach using agent-based modeling (ABM) and large-scale simulation to analyze how deontological, consequentialist, and virtue-based ethical systems perform in scenarios involving distributed agency, resource allocation conflicts, and recursive decision-making. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for this work, as simulating populations of 10^4 to 10^6 autonomous agents—each with distinct ethical reasoning modules, memory structures, and social interaction protocols—requires parallel processing capabilities and significant memory allocation. The computational model will incorporate evolutionary game theory elements to track the propagation of ethical norms across generations of agents, while Monte Carlo methods will assess stability under stochastic environmental pressures. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of failure modes for classical ethical systems in scaled environments, (2) quantitative metrics for comparing the resilience of moral frameworks, and (3) open-source tools enabling philosophers to parameterize and test theoretical models computationally. By grounding abstract ethical debates in rigorous simulation, this project aims to advance methodological innovation in moral philosophy while providing actionable insights for applied ethics in domains such as AI governance and climate policy. The requested computing resources will directly support iterative model development, validation against historical case data, and sensitivity analyses across ethical parameters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Philosophy, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the critical challenge of scalable, high-fidelity multi-physics integration in computational engineering, a domain not confined to traditional disciplinary boundaries but essential for advancing next-generation engineering systems. Current approaches to coupling disparate physical models—such as thermal, fluid, structural, and electromagnetic phenomena—often rely on static, manually tuned interfaces that introduce inefficiencies, inaccuracies, and scalability bottlenecks in high-performance computing (HPC) environments. This project aims to develop a novel, adaptive computational framework that dynamically optimizes multi-physics coupling through a hybrid approach combining domain decomposition, machine learning (ML)-driven parameterization, and asynchronous parallelization. The framework will leverage graph-based representations to model interactions between physical domains, enabling automated load balancing and adaptive resolution scaling across heterogeneous HPC architectures. Key computational innovations include the integration of reinforcement learning to predict optimal coupling intervals and error tolerance thresholds, reducing synchronization overhead while maintaining numerical stability. The research will validate the framework using benchmark problems from emerging engineering applications such as plasma-assisted manufacturing and hypersonic material degradation, where tightly coupled multi-physics interactions defy conventional single-domain simulation tools. Anticipated outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in wall-clock time for coupled simulations compared to existing monolithic solvers, demonstrated on petascale systems via weak and strong scaling studies. By providing an open-source, modular toolkit for adaptive multi-physics integration, this work will empower interdisciplinary engineering research in areas requiring complex system-level simulations, from energy-material interfaces to bioelectronic device design, without dependence on domain-specific solvers. The results will advance computational engineering methodologies by bridging gaps between algorithmic innovation, HPC resource utilization, and cross-domain model interoperability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to engineering practice and research. Includes instruction in engineering and science fundamentals, advanced mathematics, algorithms, computer languages, and software engineering design.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic fiber-fluid interactions in sustainable textile dyeing processes—a niche interdisciplinary domain bridging textile science, environmental chemistry, and computational fluid dynamics. Conventional dyeing methods are resource-intensive, with up to 30% of synthetic dyes remaining unfixed, leading to wastewater contamination. While experimental studies have explored low-impact dye chemistries, the microscale mechanics of dye diffusion in heterogeneous fiber assemblies under turbulent conditions remain poorly understood. This gap limits the development of optimized dyeing protocols that minimize water and energy use without compromising colorfastness. The project proposes a multiscale computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of dye-fiber interfacial interactions, lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) models for pore-scale fluid transport in yarn structures, and machine learning (ML)-accelerated parameter optimization. MD simulations will quantify binding energies and kinetic barriers for novel bio-based dyes interacting with modified cellulose and protein fibers. LBM simulations will resolve turbulent flow patterns and local shear forces within 3D-scanned fiber geometries, informing macroscale mass transfer coefficients. A convolutional neural network trained on simulation data will predict optimal temperature, pressure, and flow conditions for maximal dye uptake. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high dimensionality of coupled physicochemical processes, with MD and LBM simulations requiring parallelized GPU computing and petascale data workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated computational toolkit for virtual prototyping of closed-loop dyeing systems, identification of non-intuitive process parameters to reduce water use by 20-40% in pilot trials, and foundational insights into turbulence-mediated transport in fibrous media. By integrating computational textile science with green chemistry principles, this work aims to establish a paradigm for resource-efficient textile manufacturing while expanding HPC applications in non-traditional engineering domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and processing of fibers, yarns, whole fabrics, dyes, and finishes, both natural and synthetic. Includes instruction in the chemical and physical properties of textile materials; end-use analysis; interior furnishing applications; and industrial applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance quantitative modeling of lithospheric deformation processes in tectonically active regions. A critical challenge in understanding continental dynamics lies in resolving the multi-scale interactions between crustal stress regimes, fault network evolution, and magma intrusion events over geological timescales. Existing models often simplify rheological complexities or operate at resolutions insufficient to capture emergent behaviors linking localized deformation (e.g., fault slip) to regional-scale strain patterns. We propose to develop coupled thermo-mechanical simulations using a parallelized finite element framework that integrates visco-elasto-plastic rheologies, fracture mechanics, and magma migration dynamics. The computational approach will combine adaptive mesh refinement with distributed-memory parallelism to achieve kilometer-scale resolution across domain sizes exceeding 1,000 km, enabling the first 3D models capable of bridging seismic cycle timescales with million-year tectonic evolution. Key targets include quantifying how pre-existing crustal heterogeneity influences strain localization in orogenic systems and assessing feedbacks between magma-assisted lower crustal flow and upper crustal faulting. Simulations will be validated against geodetic, seismicity, and structural geology datasets from the Himalayan-Tibetan collision zone. The requested HPC allocation will support parameter space exploration across varying thermal gradients, strain rates, and melt fraction scenarios. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive frameworks for interpreting surface deformation signals in terms of evolving subsurface rheological states, (2) open-source release of optimized computational routines for lithospheric modeling, and (3) high-resolution synthetic datasets to inform field-based studies of continental dynamics. By elucidating the interplay between mechanical and thermal processes in deforming lithosphere, this work aims to transform strategies for assessing seismic hazards and interpreting geological archives of past tectonic events.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and the behavior of the solids, liquids and gases comprising it. Includes instruction in historical geology, geomorphology, and sedimentology, the chemistry of rocks and soils, stratigraphy, mineralogy, petrology, geostatistics, volcanology, glaciology, geophysical principles, and applications to research and industrial problems.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize patient intake and discharge workflows in medical reception settings through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Despite the critical role of receptionists in healthcare efficiency, current workflows often suffer from unpredictable patient arrival patterns, inconsistent data entry practices, and communication bottlenecks between administrative and clinical teams. To address these challenges, we propose developing an agent-based simulation framework that models patient flow, staff interactions, and resource utilization in real-world clinical environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and validate these simulations using de-identified historical data from electronic health records (EHRs), including check-in times, triage logs, and discharge rates. Machine learning techniques will be applied to predict peak service demands and identify latent inefficiencies in staff scheduling or patient routing. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) tools will analyze transcribed patient-receptionist interactions to quantify communication patterns that correlate with service quality metrics. The computational workflow will integrate discrete-event simulation for queue management with reinforcement learning algorithms to test adaptive staffing policies under dynamic conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for minimizing patient wait times, data-driven recommendations for training protocols in medical reception programs, and open-source tools for simulating clinic-specific workflow adjustments. This research directly supports the educational goals of medical reception programs by bridging theoretical training with empirically validated operational strategies. The scale of EHR datasets (spanning millions of anonymized patient encounters) and the combinatorial complexity of simulating multi-agent clinic interactions necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized model training and large-scale parameter optimization. Findings will be disseminated through healthcare administration conferences and integrated into competency-based curricula for medical reception training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, nurses, or physicians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in medical office and health care facility procedures, medical terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: Clinical research trials generate increasingly complex, high-dimensional datasets from diverse sources, including electronic health records, multi-omics platforms, wearable devices, and imaging systems. However, the integration and analysis of these heterogeneous data streams remain a critical bottleneck, limiting the ability to derive actionable insights in real time. This project seeks to address this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate scalable computational workflows for clinical trial data harmonization, predictive modeling, and regulatory-compliant analysis. The research problem centers on overcoming computational limitations in processing large-scale, multimodal datasets while adhering to stringent ethical, legal, and privacy requirements inherent to clinical research. We propose a hybrid approach combining federated learning frameworks for decentralized data analysis, GPU-accelerated machine learning models for patient stratification, and simulation-based methods for optimizing trial design. These workflows will be tested using retrospective data from oncology and neurology trials (n ≈ 15,000 patients) to evaluate their capacity to reduce computational runtime, improve prediction accuracy of adverse events, and enhance reproducibility. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of imaging datasets, real-time integration of streaming sensor data, and secure, auditable environments for handling protected health information. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated data quality control, validated pipelines for multi-site trial coordination, and benchmarks for ethical AI deployment in clinical research settings. By addressing computational barriers, this project aims to accelerate evidence generation in trials, reduce administrative overhead for research coordinators, and establish scalable frameworks for next-generation, data-driven clinical research. The requested resources will directly support training initiatives for clinical research coordinator trainees, embedding computational proficiency into their core skill set.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers as clinical research administrators or clinical research coordinators where they work under the supervision of a Principal Investigator to organize, coordinate and administer clinical research trials. Includes instruction in pharmacology, medical terminology, foundations of clinical research, project management, ethics, research design and data management, and legal and regulatory compliance .

abstract: This project seeks to advance tactical decision-making in naval operations by addressing critical gaps in high-resolution coastal oceanographic modeling under dynamically complex, data-sparse conditions. Military operations in littoral zones face heightened risks due to rapidly evolving bathymetric features, sediment transport, and nonlinear interactions between tides, currents, and wind-driven waves—phenomena poorly captured by existing operational models optimized for open-ocean scenarios. The research will develop a multi-physics modeling framework integrating hydrodynamic, sedimentological, and acoustic propagation components at sub-100-meter resolutions, explicitly targeting scenarios such as amphibious landings, mine countermeasures, and submarine evasion in contested near-shore environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the team will implement a nested modeling approach using the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) coupled with customized sediment resuspension and acoustic attenuation modules, validated against classified observational datasets from recent exercises. Parallelized ensemble simulations will quantify uncertainty in predicting shallow-water thermocline formation and bottom roughness effects on sonar performance, with machine learning techniques applied to reduce computational overhead in surrogate modeling. Anticipated outcomes include a validated capability to forecast 72-hour windows of acoustic transparency/opacity in operationally relevant timelines, directly informing mission planning tools for undersea navigation and sensor deployment. The resource request prioritizes GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning workflows and large-memory nodes to handle high-resolution bathymetric data assimilation. By bridging gaps between geophysical processes and tactical constraints, this work aims to establish new standards for environmental awareness in joint littoral operations, with potential spillover applications to search-and-rescue planning and infrastructure resilience against storm surge. Collaborative partnerships with naval meteorology units ensure transition pathways for model outputs into active decision-support systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of physical oceanography as applied to the naval tactical and strategic environment and the support of military operations. Includes instruction in atmospheric thermodynamics and radiation propagation, air-ocean fluid dynamics, ocean waves, nearshore environments and processes, ocean acoustics, ocean analysis, tactical oceanography, prediction, and related quantitative and experimental methods.

abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing involves complex physical and chemical processes that require precise control to optimize yield, performance, and cost. A critical challenge lies in modeling multiphysics phenomena—such as thermal stress during rapid thermal processing (RTP), plasma dynamics in etching, and defect propagation in crystalline structures—which are computationally intensive and influence device reliability at scale. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale simulations that bridge atomic-level interactions with continuum-scale manufacturing processes. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) simulating defect formation in silicon wafers under varying process conditions using molecular dynamics (MD) and finite element analysis (FEA), and (2) training machine learning (ML) models to predict optimal process parameters for minimizing defects while maximizing throughput. The computational workflow will integrate open-source tools (LAMMPS, OpenFOAM) with custom Python-based ML pipelines to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of process variables, material properties, and real-time sensor data. HPC resources are essential to handle the parallelized MD simulations of nanoscale interactions (10^6–10^9 atoms) and the iterative optimization of ML hyperparameters across thousands of experimental permutations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting thermal gradient-induced wafer warpage, a framework for coupling ML with multiphysics simulations, and a publicly accessible dataset of process-structure-property relationships. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation semiconductor fabrication protocols, reducing trial-and-error experimentation in industrial settings. By elucidating the interplay between process variables and defect mechanics, this work aims to advance foundational knowledge in semiconductor manufacturing technology while providing students with hands-on training in computational modeling and data-driven materials engineering. The project aligns with national priorities to strengthen domestic semiconductor production capabilities through innovation in advanced manufacturing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to operate and monitor equipment for the fabrication of semiconductors or microchips from silicon wafers, and to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair the specialized equipment used in this process. Includes instruction in AC and DC circuits, digital fundamentals, solid state devices, manufacturing processes, vacuum principles and technology, industrial electronics, quality assurance, and semiconductor manufacturing technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex dynamics of family systems undergoing Medical Family Therapy (MFT) for chronic illness management. Chronic illnesses introduce multidimensional stressors that disrupt family communication, emotional regulation, and relational patterns, yet existing therapeutic models lack granular tools to predict how these variables interact over time. Current qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, interdependent nature of family responses to illness, limiting the personalization of interventions. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate family systems under varying therapeutic scenarios. The ABM component will represent individual family members as autonomous agents with dynamic behavioral rules informed by clinical data on stress responses, communication styles, and cultural values. These agents will interact within a simulated environment reflecting disease progression stages (e.g., diagnosis, treatment, remission/recurrence) and therapeutic interventions. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze anonymized longitudinal datasets from MFT sessions—including speech patterns, physiological markers (e.g., heart rate variability), and therapy outcomes—to identify predictive signatures of intervention efficacy. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to thousands of virtual families, enabling sensitivity analyses of cultural, socioeconomic, and clinical variables while maintaining computational fidelity. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model that identifies high-risk family interaction patterns and optimizes intervention timing and content. This work will advance systemic therapy practices by providing empirically grounded, computationally derived insights into family resilience mechanisms, ultimately informing adaptive therapeutic protocols tailored to diverse medical and psychosocial contexts. The project bridges clinical psychology, systems biology, and computational science, establishing a novel paradigm for data-driven family therapy research.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with patients and their families who are experiencing emotional, physical, relational and spiritual difficulties related to acute and chronic illnesses. Includes instruction in cultural context, ethics, family dynamics, family therapy, gender, human development, marriage counseling, psychopathology, research design and methods, sexuality, and systems thinking.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop computational frameworks for optimizing quantum-enhanced sensing networks (QESNs), an emerging interdisciplinary domain merging quantum physics, distributed systems engineering, and machine learning. Current quantum sensing technologies face scalability challenges when deployed in networked configurations, limiting their real-world utility in applications such as precision navigation, infrastructure health monitoring, or distributed environmental sensing. The project addresses the critical engineering challenge of modeling and optimizing QESNs under realistic noise, latency, and resource constraints—a problem requiring high-dimensional parameter space exploration beyond the capabilities of classical computing resources. The computational approach combines quantum circuit simulations using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) methods with graph-based network optimization algorithms accelerated by GPU-parallelized Monte Carlo sampling. A custom HPC workflow will integrate existing quantum simulation libraries (e.g., QuTiP) with novel topology optimization routines designed for heterogeneous quantum-classical networks. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for QESN performance prediction under dynamic operating conditions, (2) machine learning-derived heuristics for resource allocation in hybrid quantum-classical sensor arrays, and (3) benchmark data correlating network topology with metrological gain in multi-parameter estimation tasks. The research will advance engineering methodologies for distributed quantum systems, providing foundational insights for future hardware implementations while maintaining compatibility with classical sensor infrastructures. By leveraging high-performance computing to bridge quantum theory and network engineering constraints, this work aims to establish scalable design principles for next-generation sensing systems that transcend the limitations of standalone quantum devices. Successful implementation will directly benefit engineering education initiatives by generating case studies and modular codebases for pre-engineering curricula focused on emerging technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission or transfer to a baccalaureate-level program in any of the fields of engineering.

abstract: The integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into fashion and apparel design research is critical to addressing the growing complexity of sustainable material innovation, dynamic consumer customization, and efficient production workflows. Traditional design methods struggle to balance aesthetic, functional, and environmental demands, particularly when simulating intricate fabric behaviors, optimizing material usage, or scaling personalized design solutions. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging HPC to model textile properties, automate pattern generation, and simulate production processes at unprecedented resolution. Advanced machine learning models will be trained on multimodal datasets—including textile mechanics, historical fashion trends, and consumer preference data—to predict material performance and design viability under diverse conditions. Physics-based simulations will replicate fabric drape, stress, and environmental impact across virtual prototypes, while generative adversarial networks (GANs) will explore energy-efficient, waste-minimized pattern configurations. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities to iteratively refine designs, assess lifecycle sustainability, and generate real-time customization options. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit for designers to rapidly prototype eco-conscious apparel, reduce physical sampling waste by 40–60%, and enable mass customization without compromising production efficiency. The project also aims to establish open-access datasets and computational workflows tailored to fashion research, bridging gaps between artistic creativity and technical precision. By deploying HPC resources, this work will advance the field’s capacity to meet global sustainability targets while fostering innovation in smart textiles and adaptive wearable technologies. Results will be disseminated through academic publications, industry partnerships, and integration into interdisciplinary design curricula, positioning computational methods as a cornerstone of next-generation fashion education and practice.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional design of commercial fashions, apparel, and accessories, and the management of fashion development projects. Includes instruction in apparel design; accessory design; the design of men's', women's', and children's' wear; flat pattern design; computer-assisted design and manufacturing; concept planning; designing in specific materials; labor and cost analysis; history of fashion; fabric art and printing; and the principles of management and operations in the fashion industry.

abstract: The proposed research project aims to address inefficiencies in multi-stage industrial production systems through advanced computational modeling and optimization. Modern manufacturing environments face challenges in synchronizing interdependent processes—such as material flow, machine scheduling, and quality control—under dynamic constraints like fluctuating demand, equipment degradation, and energy variability. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions and stochastic behaviors inherent in these systems, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and reduced throughput. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity digital twin framework using hybrid simulation techniques, integrating discrete-event simulation, agent-based modeling, and real-time data assimilation to optimize production line performance. The computational approach will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate millions of scenario permutations, coupled with multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal solutions balancing cost, energy use, and cycle time. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of modeling 10+ interdependent production stages with <1-second temporal resolution, requiring sustained calculations across thousands of cores for ensemble simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of recommending adaptive control policies under uncertainty, validated through case studies with automotive component manufacturers. The research will advance methodological integration of digital twin technologies in industrial systems while providing actionable insights to reduce production waste by an estimated 12-18% in target sectors. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules and industry partnerships, bridging gaps between academic research and practical implementation in smart manufacturing. Successful execution of this work relies on access to HPC clusters with GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning-enhanced optimization and large-memory nodes for handling high-dimensional parameter spaces in near-real-time analyses.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in industrial production technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Genomic structural variations (SVs) are critical drivers of phenotypic diversity and disease susceptibility, yet their detection and functional annotation remain technically challenging in non-model organisms and complex populations. Current reference-based methods often fail to resolve large or repetitive SVs, limiting our understanding of their role in gene regulation and adaptation. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-throughput computational framework to identify and characterize SVs using long-read sequencing data from diverse maize (Zea mays) populations and human cohorts with unresolved Mendelian disorders. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a hybrid approach combining de novo assembly, graph-based genome alignment, and population-scale haplotype phasing to resolve complex SVs with base-pair precision. Custom algorithms will integrate epigenomic data (ATAC-seq, Hi-C) to predict SV impacts on chromatin architecture and regulatory element disruption. A key innovation involves training an ensemble machine learning model to prioritize pathogenic SVs by synthesizing population frequency, evolutionary conservation, and multi-omics features. The computational pipeline will be optimized for parallel processing across thousands of genomes, requiring large-scale memory allocation and GPU acceleration for deep learning components. Successful implementation will produce the first pan-genome resource for maize structural variation, reveal novel regulatory mechanisms underlying agronomic traits, and identify diagnostic SVs in undiagnosed genetic disorders. These outputs will advance genomic research by providing scalable tools for SV analysis while addressing critical gaps in linking genome structure to functional outcomes across eukaryotic species.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of whole genome sequences and patterns of gene expression. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular biology, genetics, protein technologies, genomic sciences and techniques, bioinformatics, and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in physical retail operations through the development of a real-time, adaptive framework for optimizing in-store customer flow and staff allocation using high-performance computing (HPC). Despite advancements in e-commerce, brick-and-mortar retailers face persistent challenges in dynamically aligning staffing levels and product placement with fluctuating in-store traffic patterns, which are influenced by factors such as time-of-day demand peaks, localized promotional events, and external environmental conditions. Traditional heuristic-based approaches lack the computational capacity to process multimodal data streams—including IoT sensor feeds, point-of-sale systems, and computer vision-derived foot traffic analytics—at the scale and speed required for actionable insights. The proposed research will leverage agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate customer movement and purchasing behavior under diverse scenarios, integrated with reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to iteratively optimize staff deployment and inventory staging. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations and training RL models on high-resolution spatiotemporal datasets. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of reducing customer wait times by 15–20%, increasing cross-selling opportunities through predictive product placement, and minimizing labor cost overruns via shift scheduling aligned with real-time demand signals. By bridging computational modeling and retail operations, this work aims to enhance the agility of physical retailers in adapting to rapidly changing consumer behaviors while maintaining cost efficiency.
