The resulting framework will be validated against empirical data from partner retail chains, with open-source release of non-proprietary computational modules to support broader industry adoption.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations associated with retail sales in a variety of settings. Includes instruction in over-the-counter and other direct sales operations in business settings, basic bookkeeping principles, customer service, team/staff leadership and supervision, floor management, and applicable technical skills.

abstract: Occupational therapy interventions rely on personalized strategies to enhance patient engagement in daily activities, yet current methods for predicting intervention efficacy lack granularity in modeling dynamic interactions between patient-specific biomechanical, cognitive, and environmental factors. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating wearable sensor data, biomechanical simulations, and reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize task-specific interventions for individuals with upper limb motor impairments. The research problem centers on the inability of traditional clinical assessments to account for real-time physiological variability and environmental context when designing therapeutic activities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal data streams—including inertial measurement units, electromyography, and 3D motion capture—from a cohort of 120 patients undergoing occupational therapy. Computational workflows will employ OpenSim for musculoskeletal modeling to simulate limb dynamics under varying task demands, coupled with RL algorithms trained on individualized reward functions that prioritize motor learning efficiency and pain reduction. Sensitivity analyses will quantify how subtle changes in task parameters (e.g., object weight, workspace layout) impact therapeutic outcomes. Expected outcomes include a predictive model capable of generating adaptive intervention blueprints that respond to patient progress and contextual factors, validated against longitudinal functional independence measures. This work bridges health sciences and computational engineering, advancing evidence-based practices for occupational therapist assistants by providing data-driven tools to personalize therapeutic task progression. The computational infrastructure will enable scaling to diverse impairment populations while maintaining the low-latency processing required for eventual translation to real-time clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of occupational therapists, to direct patient participation in skill-enhancing, learning, and motivational tasks; correct or diminish pathologies; and to provide direct health education and promotion services. Includes instruction in human life span development, occupational therapy principles and practice skills, treatment planning and implementation, record-keeping and documentation, patient education and intervention, activity and program direction, and assistive services management.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in personalized financial planning tools for households by integrating high-dimensional behavioral data with dynamic economic modeling. Current tools often rely on static demographic profiles or oversimplified assumptions about decision-making, limiting their applicability to diverse family structures and evolving economic conditions. The project will develop a computational framework to simulate household financial behaviors under variable stressors, such as income volatility, healthcare costs, and intergenerational resource transfers. Using anonymized transaction records from partnered financial institutions (N ≈ 2.5 million households), combined with longitudinal survey data on consumption patterns and family lifecycle transitions, we will train agent-based models to capture nonlinear relationships between socioeconomic factors and financial resilience. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing petabyte-scale financial datasets, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of long-term financial outcomes, and optimizing machine learning architectures that account for temporal dependencies in household decision sequences. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source predictive engine capable of generating adaptive financial planning recommendations for heterogeneous family configurations, (2) quantitative thresholds for intervention efficacy in debt mitigation strategies across cultural and socioeconomic subgroups, and (3) novel metrics for assessing intertemporal trade-offs in multi-generational household resource allocation. By bridging computational social science with consumer economics, this work aims to advance evidence-based tools for financial educators and family service providers while establishing methodological foundations for complex systems analysis in human sciences research. The requested resources will enable comparative analysis of model performance across hardware configurations, ensuring scalability for future integration with real-time financial counseling platforms.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Business Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences business services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Livestock production systems face critical challenges in balancing efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare under growing global demand. A key bottleneck lies in optimizing feed formulations to meet nutritional requirements while minimizing environmental impacts, such as methane emissions. Current approaches rely on static nutritional models that inadequately account for dynamic interactions between host genetics, gut microbiota, and feed components. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating multi-omics data to predict methane output, nutrient utilization, and growth metrics in cattle. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct genome-scale metabolic models of bovine microbiomes, parameterized via metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from cattle trials. These models will be coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal data (feed intake, weight gain, gas emissions) to simulate outcomes under diverse dietary and genetic scenarios. Parallelized simulations will explore combinatorial feed additives, prebiotics, and genetic selection strategies, enabling rapid in silico screening of interventions. The computational pipeline will also incorporate climate variables and economic constraints to recommend region-specific solutions. Expected outcomes include identifying feed formulations that reduce enteric methane emissions by ≥15% without compromising productivity, as well as genetic markers for low-emission breeding lines. By translating complex biological interactions into predictive models, this work will provide a scalable tool for precision livestock management, directly supporting climate-smart agriculture goals. The proposed HPC resources are essential to handle the computational load of microbiome-host modeling, which involves millions of reaction fluxes, and to iteratively train deep learning architectures on heterogeneous datasets. This project bridges gaps between systems biology and applied animal science, offering a transformative approach to sustainable livestock production.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of livestock animals and the production and handling of meat and other products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, range science, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for adaptive real-time processing of heterogeneous data streams in distributed edge-fog-cloud continuum architectures, addressing the growing inefficiency of static data pipelines in dynamic, resource-constrained environments. Current approaches struggle to balance latency, energy consumption, and computational accuracy when handling multimodal IoT data streams (e.g., environmental sensor networks, mobile health devices) with variable temporal-spatial resolutions and QoS requirements. The research will implement a reinforcement learning-driven resource orchestrator that autonomously redistributes processing tasks across edge, fog, and cloud layers based on real-time network conditions, data criticality, and energy availability. The computational methodology combines lightweight containerization for task modularity with hybrid quantum-classical neural networks to optimize feature extraction from high-dimensional time-series data. High-performance computing resources are essential for simulating large-scale distributed networks (10,000+ virtual nodes) during framework training and validation, particularly for modeling latency propagation and energy trade-offs under peak load scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source middleware capable of reducing end-to-end processing latency by 40% compared to static edge-cloud partitioning, while maintaining 95% energy efficiency across fluctuating workloads. The project will validate the framework through two case studies: wildfire risk prediction using multi-spectral satellite imagery coupled with ground sensor data, and wearable-based physiological signal processing for critical care triage. Results will contribute novel benchmarking metrics for adaptive data processing systems and establish design patterns for QoS-aware resource allocation in fragmented computing environments. By bridging gaps between distributed systems theory and practical data pipeline optimization, this work aims to advance computational strategies for next-generation cyber-physical systems requiring guaranteed real-time responses amidst infrastructure variability.
cip_title: Data Processing and Data Processing Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master and use computer software programs and applications for inputting, verifying, organizing, storing, retrieving, transforming (changing, updating, and deleting), and extracting information. Includes instruction in using various operating system configurations and in types of data entry such as word processing, spreadsheets, calculators, management programs, design programs, database programs, and research programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systemic mechanisms underlying electroacupuncture (EA) as a neuromodulatory intervention for chronic neuropathic pain—a niche at the intersection of bioengineering, computational neuroscience, and traditional medicine. Despite promising clinical evidence, the biophysical and neurodynamic principles of EA remain poorly characterized, limiting its integration into standardized care protocols. Current gaps include an incomplete understanding of how EA’s electrical stimuli interact with peripheral nerve bioelectricity to influence central pain-processing networks, particularly in heterogeneous patient populations. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating finite element modeling of stimulus propagation through tissue layers, dynamic systems modeling of neural circuit responses, and machine learning-driven analysis of patient-specific electrophysiological datasets. The finite element component will simulate electric field distributions in anatomically realistic tissue models derived from MRI data, while neural network models will map stimulus parameters (frequency, intensity) to pain-modulatory outcomes via dopaminergic and opioidergic pathways. Concurrently, graph-based machine learning algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers from high-density EEG recordings and autonomic response data collected in a pilot clinical cohort. These computationally intensive tasks demand HPC capabilities to manage large parameter spaces, real-time multiscale data integration, and iterative optimization of hybrid models. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for personalizing EA parameters and a mechanistic atlas of EA-induced neuroplasticity. By elucidating dose-response relationships and neural decoding strategies unique to bioelectrical therapies, this work aims to establish a quantitative bridge between empirical practice and systems-level pathophysiology, advancing both the scientific rigor and clinical applicability of electroacupuncture in pain management.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medical Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medical support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and performance of high-power laser systems, addressing critical challenges in beam quality control, thermal management, and nonlinear optical effects. Current experimental approaches to mitigate thermal lensing, mode instability, and spectral broadening in high-energy laser systems are resource-intensive and time-consuming, particularly when scaling to next-generation applications in materials processing, telecommunications, and medical devices. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multiphysics simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model coupled optical-thermal-mechanical phenomena in laser gain media, beam delivery optics, and nonlinear frequency conversion crystals. The computational workflow integrates finite element analysis (COMSOL Multiphysics) for thermal-structural modeling with GPU-accelerated beam propagation methods (Python-based custom code) to simulate dynamic interactions across spatial scales from microns to meters and temporal scales from nanoseconds to continuous wave operation. Machine learning techniques will be applied to extract reduced-order models from the simulation datasets, enabling rapid performance prediction for novel laser architectures. The HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across laser diode configurations, cooling geometries, and nonlinear crystal orientations that would otherwise require prohibitive experimental iterations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting beam degradation thresholds in high-power fiber lasers, optimized thermal management strategies for ultrashort pulse amplification systems, and predictive tools for efficiency enhancement in optical parametric oscillators. These results will directly inform the design of compact, energy-efficient laser systems for industrial cutting/welding applications and tunable sources for spectroscopic sensing. By integrating computational modeling with experimental validation, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift in laser development workflows, reducing prototyping costs by an estimated 30–50% while accelerating performance optimization cycles. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution in coupled-domain simulations and to train robust machine learning models on the terabyte-scale datasets generated.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using lasers and other optical for commercial or research purposes. Includes instruction in laser and optical principles, testing and maintenance procedures, safety precautions, specific applications to various tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: Healthcare unit management faces critical challenges in optimizing staffing and resource allocation amidst dynamic patient care demands, particularly in acute care settings. Traditional scheduling approaches rely on retrospective data and static protocols, often failing to adapt to real-time variability in patient acuity, admission surges, or staff availability. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient flow, predict short-term care demands, and simulate staffing configurations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research integrates anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), real-time bed telemetry, and staff competency matrices to develop agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate unit operations under diverse scenarios. Machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and graph convolutional networks (GCNs), will analyze temporal patterns in patient admissions, transfers, and discharge trajectories. Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes of staffing decisions under constraints such as nurse-patient ratios, skill mix requirements, and unexpected absenteeism. The computational pipeline will be validated against historical operational data from three tertiary care facilities, with sensitivity analyses quantifying the impact of predictive accuracy on resource utilization metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that enables ward supervisors to dynamically optimize staff deployment, reduce overtime costs, and maintain care quality during demand fluctuations. By bridging operations research, predictive analytics, and healthcare management, this work addresses a critical gap in adaptive resource allocation strategies for modern clinical units. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling simulations across multi-unit hospital systems and achieving the granular temporal resolution required for minute-to-minute operational decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nursing or medical service administrators, to supervise and coordinate the operations of one or more patient care units in hospitals or other health care facilities. Includes instruction in planning and initiating administrative procedures, personnel supervision, interpersonal skills, general and/or specialized health care operations and procedures, and consultation with other medical, nursing, and administrative team members.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and sustainability of multilayer packaging materials, addressing critical gaps in current industry practices where material performance, cost, and environmental impact are often balanced through trial-and-error approaches. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive tools to efficiently simulate interactions between packaging layers (e.g., barrier films, adhesives, structural components) under dynamic real-world conditions, such as variable temperatures, mechanical stresses, and chemical exposures during transportation and storage. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach integrating multiscale modeling techniques. Molecular dynamics simulations will analyze interfacial adhesion and permeability at the atomic level, while finite element analysis will evaluate macroscale mechanical integrity and thermal response. Machine learning models, trained on experimental and simulated data, will identify optimal material combinations and layer geometries to meet target performance metrics (e.g., oxygen transmission rates, compressive strength) while minimizing material waste and carbon footprint. The computational workflow will also incorporate lifecycle assessment databases to quantify environmental impacts of proposed designs. By leveraging HPC resources, we aim to reduce simulation times for complex multilayer systems by two orders of magnitude compared to existing single-node solutions, enabling rapid iteration across thousands of material permutations. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive toolkit for packaging designers, validated prototypes of bio-based multilayer films with 30% reduced material use, and a framework for automating compliance checks against evolving global packaging regulations. This work directly supports the packaging industry’s transition toward circular economy principles by enabling data-driven design of recyclable, high-performance materials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific, technological, design, and business principles to the development of packages and packaging materials, including raw material production, conversion of raw materials into usable forms, design, distribution, and post-use recycling and reuse. Includes instruction in principles of packaging, materials sciences, distribution and transportation, engineering and technology, graphic design, packaging regulations, and business and marketing.

abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders, including osteoarthritis, traumatic injuries, and spinal pathologies, represent a leading cause of global disability. Current diagnostic workflows in radiology rely heavily on qualitative image interpretation, which can lead to variability in detection, grading, and treatment planning. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing quantitative, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven tools to analyze musculoskeletal imaging data, with an emphasis on automating the detection of subtle pathological features and predicting disease progression. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate deep learning models on multi-institutional datasets of MRI, CT, and radiographs encompassing diverse patient populations and pathologies. Key computational challenges include processing high-resolution 3D volumetric data, harmonizing heterogeneous imaging protocols across sites, and optimizing model generalizability. The project will implement a hybrid architecture combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for localized feature extraction and transformer-based models to capture long-range spatial dependencies in musculoskeletal structures. Computational workflows will be parallelized across GPU nodes to accelerate model training and enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Additionally, federated learning frameworks will be tested to facilitate privacy-preserving collaborations across institutions. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for automated lesion segmentation, joint space quantification, and fracture risk prediction, validated against expert radiologist annotations. These tools aim to reduce diagnostic variability, enable earlier intervention, and support personalized treatment strategies. By integrating HPC capabilities with clinical radiology expertise, this work seeks to establish a scalable computational framework for advancing precision medicine in musculoskeletal care. Successful implementation will provide a template for translating computationally intensive AI models into clinically actionable tools, directly addressing unmet needs in the diagnosis and management of complex musculoskeletal conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders or injuries of the joints, bones, muscles, and spine in adults and children.

abstract: The study of Hindu theological and philosophical traditions involves analyzing vast corpora of Sanskrit texts, spanning millennia. Traditional scholarly methods face challenges in systematically tracking doctrinal evolution, intertextual influences, and conceptual networks across this extensive literature. This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analysis of primary Hindu scriptures, including the Vedas, Upanishads, and key philosophical commentaries. Leveraging natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for classical Sanskrit, we will develop computational models to map semantic shifts in core concepts (e.g., dharma, moksha) across historical periods and school affiliations. Network analysis will be applied to trace citation patterns and argumentative relationships between philosophical texts, while transformer-based architectures will assist in identifying previously unrecognized thematic connections across genres. The scale of data—encompassing over 100,000 shlokas (verses) with multiple commentary layers—requires significant parallel processing capabilities for tokenization, dependency parsing, and semantic role labeling specific to Sanskrit's morphological complexity. Expected outcomes include: (1) quantitative models of philosophical concept development through Hindu intellectual history, (2) visualizations of intertextual networks demonstrating transmission pathways between scholastic traditions, and (3) an open-access annotated corpus supporting future computational humanities research in Hindu Studies. By integrating advanced computing with theological inquiry, this project aims to generate novel insights into Hinduism's intellectual heritage while establishing methodological frameworks for digitally-aided religious studies research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the group of South Asian theologies and philosophies collectively known as Hinduism; together with the religious history and cultural and social manifestations of the faith. Includes instruction in Hindu theology and philosophy (dharma); literature (Vedas, Upanishads, Epics, and commentaries); the Hindu Pantheon, sects, and movements; schools and disciplines; and related arts and sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing hearing assistive technologies for complex auditory environments through advanced computational modeling of neural auditory processing. Current hearing aids and cochlear implants often underperform in dynamic, noisy settings due to limitations in real-time signal processing and a poor understanding of how individual neurophysiological variability influences device efficacy. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating biophysically detailed models of the auditory pathway with machine learning to simulate how diverse neural populations process amplified or electrically stimulated signals. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations capturing the nonlinear interactions between cochlear mechanics, neural synchrony, and cortical adaptation across heterogeneous virtual patient cohorts. The computational pipeline will leverage finite element modeling of cochlear dynamics, spiking neural networks for auditory nerve encoding, and transformer-based architectures to predict cortical responses to time-varying acoustic scenes. By training these models on electrophysiological data from animal studies and human electroencephalography (EEG) recordings, we aim to develop personalized noise-suppression algorithms that adapt to both environmental acoustics and user-specific neuroplasticity patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for auditory neurotechnology testing and evidence-based design principles for next-generation adaptive hearing devices. This work intersects computational neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and clinical audiology, offering a paradigm shift from population-averaged hearing solutions to precision audiological interventions. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ neural configurations and millisecond-resolution simulations of auditory processing chains—tasks intractable on local clusters. Success in this endeavor could significantly improve quality of life for the 466 million individuals globally with disabling hearing loss by enabling technologies that maintain efficacy in real-world listening environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose and treat hearing loss and other disorders involving the ear, advise patients on means to use their remaining hearing, and select and fit hearing aids and other devices. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of hearing, hearing measurement, auditory pathology, middle and inner ear analysis, rehabilitation therapies and assistive technologies, and pediatric and other special applications.

abstract: Plant breeding programs face significant challenges in efficiently developing climate-resilient cultivars due to the complex genetic architectures underlying stress tolerance traits and the need to optimize genomic selection models for diverse environments. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the identification of genetic markers and predictive models for drought and heat resilience in staple crops, focusing on sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) as a case study. The research will integrate large-scale genomic datasets (whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq) with high-resolution environmental data to model genotype-by-environment interactions. Machine learning pipelines, including convolutional neural networks and gradient-boosted regression trees, will be trained on genomic and phenomic data from field trials across multiple agroecological zones. Population genomic simulations will evaluate selection strategies under projected climate scenarios. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling for Bayesian genomic prediction, and distributed computing for multi-trait optimization. Outcomes will include open-source predictive models for trait heritability under stress conditions, optimized breeding schedules for genetic gain, and a curated database linking candidate genes to adaptive phenotypes. This work will directly inform breeding pipelines at partner institutions, reducing the iteration time for cultivar development by enabling in silico pre-screening of crossing schemes. By addressing computational bottlenecks in analyzing complex plant-environment systems, the project aims to establish a scalable framework for precision breeding across crops, enhancing agricultural sustainability under climate change.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural plant health, the development of new plant varieties, and the selective improvement of agricultural plant populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, agronomy, plant protection, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems through large-scale numerical simulations, addressing critical gaps in understanding how collective interactions drive macroscopic quantum phases. The research focuses on simulating two-dimensional lattice models, such as Hubbard-type systems, to elucidate mechanisms behind high-temperature superconductivity and quantum spin liquid behavior—problems intractable to analytical methods due to their exponential computational complexity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ tensor network algorithms, including density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and projected entangled-pair states (PEPS), optimized for parallel architectures to handle system sizes beyond current state-of-the-art limits. These methods will be augmented by custom hybrid Monte Carlo techniques to incorporate dynamical electron-phonon coupling effects, a key underexplored factor in stabilizing unconventional superconducting orders. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for tensor contractions and distributed memory systems for variational optimization, requiring petabytes of storage for wavefunction data and Green’s function calculations. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative phase diagrams mapping the interplay of spin fluctuations, lattice dynamics, and doping in cuprate-inspired models, (2) identification of universal signatures of quantum criticality via finite-temperature scaling, and (3) open-source release of optimized code for simulating non-Abelian quasiparticles in frustrated geometries. By resolving debated mechanisms in quantum material behavior, this work will directly inform experimental efforts to engineer high-T_c superconductors and topological qubits. The requested HPC allocation will enable unprecedented resolution of multi-scale quantum correlations, advancing foundational physics knowledge while developing computational tools adaptable to broader strongly interacting systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the theories that explain the fundamental structure of our world and the universe and which draws from physics and astronomy. Includes instruction in astronomy, calculus, cosmology, differential equations, electricity, magnetism, data analysis, physics, quantum mechanics, space science, spectroscopy, and thermal physics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced digital arts research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, real-time rendering and simulation of interactive multimedia environments. Current limitations in local computing infrastructure restrict the ability to process high-resolution 3D models, dynamic particle systems, and AI-driven generative art in real time, hindering the exploration of complex, immersive narratives in digital storytelling and experiential design. The proposed research will employ GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines, distributed computing frameworks, and machine learning models to optimize workflows for procedural asset generation, photorealistic lighting simulations, and multi-user virtual environments. Key computational challenges include parallelizing physics-based simulations for interactive installations, training custom diffusion models for texture synthesis, and deploying low-latency networked systems for collaborative VR experiences. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to reduce iterative design cycles, enhance the fidelity of real-time visualizations, and scale interactive systems to support experimental formats such as city-scale augmented reality and AI-augmented performance art. Outcomes will include a suite of open-source tools for optimizing digital arts workflows on HPC architectures, case studies demonstrating novel applications of computational methods in generative design, and a public exhibition of interactive works exploring themes of human-AI co-creation. This work bridges technical innovation with artistic practice, advancing methodologies for computationally intensive digital arts while contributing to broader interdisciplinary dialogues about the role of scalable computing in creative industries. The requested resources will directly support 12-18 months of development and testing, enabling researchers to push the boundaries of digital expression while training students in cutting-edge computational art techniques.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the use of computerized digital images as the primary medium of expression in the visual and performing arts, and that may prepare individuals for a wide variety of careers using new media, including graphic design, digital animation, motion graphics, 3D visualization, game and interactive media design, music and sound design, video production, web design, photography, and other fields.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting and mitigating structural degradation in historic buildings through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Historic structures, often composed of heterogeneous materials such as timber, stone, and lime mortar, are subject to complex environmental stressors, including moisture infiltration, thermal cycling, and pollutant exposure. Traditional preservation methods rely on manual inspections and localized interventions, which lack the capacity to model long-term, system-wide interactions between materials and environmental factors. This research proposes a computational framework to simulate multi-physical degradation processes across entire structures, integrating historical construction data, environmental sensor inputs, and material science datasets. Finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to predict stress distribution, crack propagation, and material fatigue under varying climatic scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze spatial-temporal patterns of decay from 3D laser scan datasets and archival imagery. The scale and resolution required for these simulations—encompassing micrometer-scale material interactions and building-scale structural dynamics—necessitate HPC resources for parallel processing, large-memory computation, and high-throughput data management. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk zones in historic buildings, optimized conservation strategies to prioritize interventions, and a publicly accessible database of material degradation profiles. By bridging architectural history, materials engineering, and computational science, this project aims to advance evidence-based preservation practices, reduce costs associated with reactive repairs, and extend the lifespan of culturally significant structures. The integration of HPC-driven analytics into heritage conservation represents a novel interdisciplinary contribution, offering scalable methodologies applicable to diverse historic sites globally.
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on architectural design and building techniques for historic and restored structures, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing linguistic and cultural diversity in K-12 classrooms presents significant challenges for educators tasked with fostering inclusive, equitable learning environments. Current teacher training frameworks lack robust, data-driven tools to model dynamic interactions between language acquisition, cultural identity, and pedagogical strategies in multilingual settings. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to simulate classroom interactions and analyze patterns in multilingual educational outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to process and synthesize large-scale datasets spanning anonymized student performance metrics, teacher intervention logs, and longitudinal sociolinguistic surveys from diverse school districts. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze code-switching patterns in classroom transcripts, agent-based modeling to simulate teacher-student communication dynamics, and neural networks to identify predictors of academic success for emergent bilingual students. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model training across heterogeneous data types, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to optimize instructional strategies for culturally sustaining pedagogy, (2) open-source tools for real-time analysis of multilingual classroom discourse, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for teacher education programs to address implicit biases in cross-cultural communication. By quantifying how specific teaching practices mediate equity gaps, this work aims to transform the preparation of educators serving multilingual populations. The resulting models will be validated against observational studies in partner school districts, ensuring translational relevance for curriculum design and policy reform. This project directly aligns with national priorities to advance educational equity through computational innovation in teacher training.
cip_title: Bilingual, Multilingual, and Multicultural Education, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in bilingual, multilingual, and multicultural Education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized rehabilitation protocols for patients with complex musculoskeletal injuries, focusing on optimizing therapeutic exercise parameters through biomechanical modeling. Current physical therapy practices often rely on generalized protocols that may not account for individual variations in tissue healing rates, neuromuscular adaptation, or biomechanical load tolerance. This gap contributes to suboptimal recovery trajectories, particularly in patients with multi-joint injuries or comorbidities such as connective tissue disorders. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific musculoskeletal simulations with machine learning to model tissue response to therapeutic exercise. High-resolution motion capture data, electromyography, and medical imaging will inform anatomically accurate models of individual patients, while finite element analysis will simulate load distribution across healing tissues. Machine learning algorithms will iteratively refine exercise parameters (e.g., range of motion, resistance levels) based on simulated tissue strain patterns and predicted remodeling outcomes. The computational intensity of running thousands of parallelized simulations to explore parameter spaces necessitates HPC resources, particularly for calibrating multi-scale models that link cellular-level healing processes to macroscopic biomechanical performance. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for injury-specific exercise optimization and an open-source toolkit to assist physical therapy technicians in designing adaptive rehabilitation plans. This work bridges computational biomechanics and clinical rehabilitation science, offering a novel paradigm for precision physical therapy that could reduce recovery times and improve functional outcomes while providing technicians with evidence-based decision-support tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in rehabilitation services under the supervision of physical therapists, and to perform routine functions in support of physical therapy and rehabilitation. Includes instruction in applied kinesiology, basic function of the human body, communication skills, principles and procedures of physical therapy, physical therapy modalities, and professional ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize predictive maintenance frameworks for next-generation military aerospace ground equipment (AGE) using high-fidelity simulations of equipment degradation under operational stress. Current maintenance protocols rely on static schedules or reactive diagnostics, leading to unplanned downtime, resource inefficiencies, and risks to mission-critical operations. To address this, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) model trained on multiphysics simulations of thermal, vibrational, and corrosion-induced failures in AGE components such as hydraulic test stands, nitrogen servicing carts, and cryogenic cooling units. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize these simulations across diverse environmental conditions (e.g., desert, maritime, arctic) and operational loads, generating the terabyte-scale datasets required to capture rare failure modes. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and corrosion dynamics, and time-series analytics to map sensor data to simulated degradation pathways. The resulting ML model will predict remaining useful life (RUL) of components with quantified uncertainty, enabling condition-based maintenance aligned with mission readiness requirements. Outcomes include a digital twin framework adaptable to emerging AGE systems, validated against field data from three active U.S. Air Force bases. This work bridges gaps between legacy maintenance practices and data-driven decision-making, directly supporting the U.S. Department of Defense’s priorities for sustainment modernization. By reducing unnecessary maintenance cycles and mitigating catastrophic failures, the project aims to decrease lifecycle costs by an estimated 12–18% per platform while enhancing operational safety in contested logistics environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology, and maintenance of ground-based systems and equipments used to support aviation flight operations and space operations. Includes instruction in computer science, electronics, basic sciences and quantitative methods, air conditioning and refrigeration, corrosion control, fluid power, hazardous materials, industrial safety, maintenance management, vehicle and equipment operation, and applications to specific ground support systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational photography research focused on enhancing the precision and scalability of AI-driven image synthesis and restoration techniques. A critical challenge in contemporary photographic practice lies in efficiently processing ultra-high-resolution (UHR) imagery (e.g., 50+ megapixel datasets) while preserving artistic intent, especially when applying neural networks for style transfer, artifact removal, or generative augmentation. Traditional workflows struggle with memory constraints and processing latency when handling UHR images or iterative training of complex models, limiting their utility in creative applications. To address this, the project proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) optimized for parallelized training, multi-scale image decomposition algorithms, and domain-specific data augmentation pipelines. HPC resources will enable distributed training of GAN architectures across GPU nodes, accelerating experimentation with attention mechanisms and loss functions tailored to aesthetic outcomes. Additionally, large-scale simulations of optical phenomena (e.g., light diffraction, spectral filtering) will be conducted to generate synthetic training data for rare or impractical photographic scenarios. Outcomes will include open-source tools for adaptive resolution-aware image processing, a benchmark dataset linking computational parameters to perceptual quality metrics, and novel methods for preserving metadata integrity during AI-assisted editing. This work aims to bridge computational efficiency and artistic control, empowering photographers to explore complex digital manipulations without sacrificing technical fidelity. The requested resources will directly support iterative model training, hyperparameter optimization, and validation against terabyte-scale archives of historical and contemporary photographic works, ensuring robust evaluation across diverse visual styles and mediums.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of communicating information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the creation of images on photographic film, plates, and digital images and that may prepare individuals to be professional photographic artists. Includes instruction in camera and equipment operation and maintenance, film and plate developing, light and composition, films and printing media, color and special effects, photographic art, photographic history, use of computer applications to record or enhance images and applications to the photography of various subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize radiopharmaceutical imaging protocols for rare oncologic and neurodegenerative conditions using advanced computational modeling, addressing critical limitations in spatial resolution and quantitative accuracy of positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT). Current clinical workflows rely on generalized protocols that inadequately account for patient-specific anatomical variability, tracer kinetics, or detector physics, leading to suboptimal diagnostic sensitivity for small lesions or early-stage disease. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate and iteratively refine imaging parameters across diverse virtual patient phantoms. Monte Carlo simulations (GATE/Geant4) will model photon transport and detector response at unprecedented scale, incorporating individualized CT-derived anatomical data, radiopharmaceutical biodistribution models, and noise characteristics. Machine learning architectures (3D convolutional neural networks) will then analyze simulated datasets to identify protocol adjustments that maximize lesion detectability while minimizing radiation exposure. The computational workflow will be validated against physical phantom experiments and retrospective clinical data. By leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized simulation batches and distributed training of deep learning models, this approach aims to establish patient-adaptive imaging protocols that improve diagnostic confidence in complex cases. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for protocol optimization, quantitative benchmarks for novel tracer applications, and a computational pipeline adaptable to emerging detector technologies. This work bridges nuclear medicine physics with computational oncology, offering a paradigm shift toward precision nuclear imaging that enhances diagnostic accuracy while maintaining ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) safety principles—a critical advancement for managing rare diseases with limited therapeutic windows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to employ radioactive and stable nuclides in diagnostic evaluations and therapeutic applications while monitoring for patient health and safety. Includes instruction in nuclear physics, health physics, instrumentation and statistics, biochemistry, immunology, radiopharmacology, radiation biology, clinical nuclear medicine, radionuclide therapy, computer applications, safety regulations, equipment operation, quality control, laboratory procedures, taking patient histories, patient evaluation and monitoring, emergency first aid, administration and record-keeping, and personnel supervision.

abstract: The commercial poultry industry faces persistent challenges from infectious diseases such as avian influenza, Newcastle disease, and bacterial infections, which threaten animal welfare, food security, and public health. Current strategies for disease prevention and management are hindered by gaps in understanding pathogen evolution, host-pathogen interactions, and the influence of environmental and genetic factors on disease transmission. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and analyze large-scale datasets, enabling data-driven interventions. The research integrates epidemiological surveillance data, whole-genome sequencing of pathogens and poultry populations, and environmental variables to investigate disease spread dynamics, genetic resistance markers, and optimal biosecurity protocols. Computational methods include agent-based modeling to simulate disease transmission across poultry flocks under varying management practices, machine learning algorithms to identify risk factors for outbreaks, and phylogenetic analyses to track pathogen evolution and zoonotic potential. Additionally, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be conducted to pinpoint genetic variants linked to disease resilience in poultry. The scale of these datasets—spanning millions of genomic sequences, high-resolution environmental metrics, and real-time flock health records—necessitates HPC infrastructure for efficient processing, storage, and parallelized computation. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into targeted vaccination strategies, genetic selection for disease-resistant poultry lines, and early-warning systems for outbreak prediction. By enhancing the precision and scalability of these analyses, the project aims to reduce economic losses in the poultry sector, mitigate antimicrobial use, and minimize zoonotic spillover risks. This work aligns with broader goals of advancing sustainable livestock production and global health security through translational clinical research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the commercial poultry industry, providing services and technical support pertaining to prevention, diagnosis, and management of disease; epidemiology; genetics; and nutrition.

abstract: Interventional radiology (IR) faces critical computational challenges in optimizing image-guided therapies, where real-time integration of multimodal imaging data (fluoroscopy, CT, MRI) is essential for navigating devices and monitoring interventions. Current workflows lack the processing speed and analytical depth required to handle high-resolution, dynamic datasets, leading to suboptimal procedural planning, increased radiation exposure, and limited personalization. This project proposes to address these limitations by deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable computational frameworks for three core objectives: (1) real-time fusion and enhancement of multi-modal imaging streams to improve device tracking accuracy, (2) patient-specific hemodynamic simulations to predict outcomes of embolization and stent placement, and (3) AI-driven predictive models for intraprocedural complication risk assessment. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated deformable image registration, finite element modeling of vascular biomechanics, and federated learning techniques trained on heterogeneous clinical datasets. These workflows will be validated against retrospective IR cases (n=250) and prospectively tested in a pilot cohort (n=30) undergoing complex embolotherapy. The anticipated outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in image processing latency, predictive tools with >85% accuracy in forecasting thromboembolic events, and open-source simulation pipelines for preprocedural device optimization. By enabling rapid, data-rich decision-making, this work aims to elevate the precision of minimally invasive interventions, reduce adverse events, and establish reproducible computational standards for IR innovation. The scale of imaging data (>15 TB/post-processing case) and the iterative demands of deep learning and multiphysics simulations necessitate dedicated HPC infrastructure. This project will directly advance the translational potential of computational IR while fostering scalable solutions for resource-constrained clinical environments.
cip_definition: Research focused on image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages. Does NOT require prior completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: Pediatric cardiovascular diseases, particularly congenital heart defects (CHDs) and cardiomyopathies, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to anatomical variability, developmental dynamics, and limited predictive models for long-term outcomes. Current approaches often rely on generalized clinical criteria, which may inadequately address individual patient complexity. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific predictive models for postoperative outcomes and disease progression in pediatric cardiology. The research will integrate multi-modal datasets, including high-resolution cardiac MRI/CT imaging, electronic health records (EHR), and longitudinal genomic data, to characterize hemodynamic and molecular factors influencing surgical success and cardiac remodeling. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model blood flow dynamics in 3D-reconstructed patient cardiac geometries, while machine learning pipelines will analyze heterogeneous clinical and omics data to identify prognostic biomarkers. The HPC environment is critical for handling the computational intensity of large-scale simulations, parallel processing of imaging datasets (>10,000 high-resolution images), and training deep learning models on multi-terabyte EHR repositories. Expected outcomes include the development of a validated computational framework for predicting postoperative complications (e.g., right ventricular failure in tetralogy of Fallot repairs) and optimizing surgical intervention timing in CHDs. This work will also establish open-source tools for pediatric cardiac simulation, enabling reproducible hemodynamic analysis across institutions. By advancing precision medicine in pediatric cardiology, the project aims to reduce reoperation rates, improve long-term functional outcomes, and inform risk-stratified follow-up protocols. The computational infrastructure will additionally support future investigations into population-level trends through integration with public health databases, bridging gaps between individualized care and community health strategies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases and disorders of the cardiovascular and cardiopulmonary systems of infants, children, and adolescents. May include related research in public health and community medicine issues.

abstract: This project proposes a computational investigation into the biomechanical and neurophysiological interactions underlying spinal manipulation therapies (SMTs), with a focus on optimizing force delivery parameters for chiropractic interventions. While SMTs are widely utilized in chiropractic care, the mechanistic relationships between specific adjustment techniques, vertebral joint dynamics, and resultant neural modulation remain poorly characterized. This gap limits the development of evidence-based, patient-specific protocols. We aim to address this by integrating multiscale biomechanical modeling with neural signal simulation to analyze how variations in force magnitude, vector, and rate influence spinal tissue responses and downstream autonomic nervous system activity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be employed to execute finite element models of lumbar spinal segments under dynamic loading conditions, incorporating heterogeneous material properties derived from clinical imaging data. Concurrently, we will simulate afferent signaling patterns through biophysically detailed models of mechanosensitive dorsal root ganglia neurons, coupling mechanical strain data from the structural simulations to predict neural activation thresholds. Machine learning approaches will then identify optimal force parameter combinations that maximize predicted neurobiomechanical efficacy while minimizing tissue stress concentrations. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from motion capture and surface electromyography recordings collected during controlled chiropractic adjustments. By establishing a predictive framework linking adjustment mechanics to physiological outcomes, this work seeks to advance precision in chiropractic technique selection and force calibration. The project’s outcomes have potential to inform clinical training programs, reduce trial-and-error approaches in manual therapy, and contribute foundational knowledge to the emerging field of computational neuromusculoskeletal health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in chiropractic medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision metal working processes through high-fidelity computational modeling of thermo-mechanical interactions in advanced machining and additive manufacturing systems. The research addresses a critical gap in real-time predictive capabilities for minimizing microstructural defects—such as residual stress, tool wear, and phase transformations—that arise during high-speed machining of refractory alloys and laser-based metal deposition. Current analytical models struggle to account for the multi-physical coupling of heat transfer, plastic deformation, and rapid solidification dynamics at micrometer scales, particularly under extreme thermal gradients. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for bulk deformation, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for grain boundary interactions, and machine learning-driven optimization of process parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these models, which require parallelized simulations across 10^4–10^6 mesh elements, iterative solver algorithms for non-linear material behavior, and GPU-accelerated training of neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets from in-situ sensor arrays. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating toolpath strategies, energy input profiles, and cooling rates with final part integrity, enabling first-time-right manufacturing for aerospace and medical components. The computational workflows will be validated against synchrotron X-ray diffraction data and high-speed thermographic measurements. By establishing open-source simulation templates for the precision metal working community, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error prototyping cycles by 40–60% while providing a foundation for AI-enhanced process planning in vocational training programs. The requested allocation of 200,000 core-hours and 4 TB of temporary storage will directly support monthly simulation batches through 2024–2025, with scalability testing for industrial-grade part geometries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision metal work, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Chiropractic care relies on evidence-based approaches to diagnose and treat musculoskeletal disorders, yet the biomechanical mechanisms underlying spinal adjustments remain incompletely understood. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to simulate spinal joint dynamics during manual manipulation and evaluate their physiological effects on surrounding tissues. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the complex interactions between vertebral kinematics, soft tissue deformation, and neural response patterns at clinically relevant timescales. The research will integrate anatomical datasets from pre-chiropractic cadaver studies, patient-specific motion capture, and finite element modeling to construct a biomechanical framework of the lumbar spine. Molecular dynamics simulations will then analyze load transmission through facet joints and intervertebral discs under varying adjustment protocols. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify predictive relationships between adjustment parameters (e.g., force vectors, velocity) and therapeutic outcomes, such as pain reduction or range-of-motion improvements. Expected outcomes include validated computational workflows to optimize adjustment techniques, reduce trial-and-error in clinical training, and establish quantitative safety thresholds for spinal loading. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will advance the precision of chiropractic interventions while providing a foundational tool for educational simulations in pre-chiropractic curricula. The resulting models and datasets will be shared openly to support reproducibility and interdisciplinary collaboration in musculoskeletal research. This project aligns with the program’s mission to bridge foundational science and clinical practice, offering students hands-on exposure to computational biomechanics as part of modern chiropractic training.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in chiropractic medicine.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and analyze dynamic simulations of caregiver-child interaction patterns within early childhood education environments. The study addresses a critical gap in scalable, evidence-based training tools for child care providers, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid decision-making under resource constraints (e.g., staff-to-child ratios, diverse developmental needs). Current training models rely heavily on static case studies or limited real-world observations, which fail to capture the complex, multivariate nature of child care environments. Our computational approach combines agent-based modeling with reinforcement learning to simulate realistic, culturally responsive caregiving scenarios across demographic variables, developmental stages, and regulatory frameworks. The models will integrate real-world data from anonymized child care center logs, developmental milestone databases, and environmental sensor datasets to generate adaptive training modules. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of interaction timelines across thousands of simulated hours, natural language processing for dialogue pattern analysis in caregiver-child communications, and real-time optimization of scenario difficulty levels. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform that identifies critical decision thresholds in caregiving quality and predicts longitudinal impacts of training interventions on developmental outcomes. By quantifying traditionally qualitative aspects of caregiving (e.g., emotional attunement, conflict resolution styles) through computational metrics, this work aims to establish new standards for competency evaluation in child care certification programs. The requested HPC resources will enable parameter space exploration across 15+ interaction variables simultaneously while maintaining the low-latency requirements essential for responsive scenario generation. This interdisciplinary initiative bridges developmental psychology, educational theory, and computational social science, offering a novel framework to enhance workforce preparedness in early childhood education through data-driven simulation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be primary providers of home, family, residential, or institutional-based child care services. Includes instruction in child growth and development, nutrition, recreation, planning and supervision of play and learning activities, child abuse and neglect prevention, parent-child relationships, and applicable legal and administrative requirements.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-modal biomedical data—including genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and medical imaging datasets—presents significant challenges in developing predictive models for precision medicine. Current approaches often lack scalability when integrating heterogeneous data types, leading to suboptimal performance in clinical decision support systems. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design and train advanced machine learning models capable of synthesizing large-scale, multi-source health data. The research will focus on optimizing deep learning architectures, such as graph neural networks and transformer-based models, to process EHR temporal sequences, genomic variants, and high-resolution imaging data in parallel. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive operations across distributed nodes, accelerating hyperparameter optimization via parallelized Bayesian methods, and implementing federated learning frameworks to preserve data privacy across institutional boundaries. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated clusters and scalable storage systems to handle datasets exceeding 500 TB, including publicly available biobank data and institutional de-identified patient records. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for cross-modal feature fusion, validated against clinical endpoints such as disease progression prediction and treatment response stratification. By enabling efficient analysis of previously intractable datasets, this work will advance the development of robust, interpretable decision systems for personalized care. The computational infrastructure will also support the creation of open-source tools for scalable health data integration, benefiting the broader biomedical informatics community. This project aligns with national priorities in translational health AI and addresses critical gaps in computational methods for real-world, data-driven healthcare innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to health and/or biomedical research,  and the development of advanced database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in biomedical and/or health sciences; information science and technology; social and behavioral sciences; biomedical/health information science and technology; human factors and socio-technical systems;  applied social, behavioral, and information science and technology; and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of companion animal diseases, coupled with the need for precision in surgical planning and therapeutic interventions, demands advanced computational approaches to bridge gaps in clinical veterinary practice. This project seeks to develop high-performance computing (HPC)-driven models to optimize the diagnosis, treatment, and postoperative management of small animals, with a focus on oncology, orthopedics, and metabolic disorders. Current challenges include predicting tumor metastasis dynamics, personalizing bone fracture repair strategies, and modeling drug pharmacokinetics in diverse breeds—problems that require resource-intensive simulations exceeding the capacity of standard clinical computing infrastructure. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating species-specific anatomical data, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, medical imaging, and genomic profiles. HPC resources will enable finite element modeling of biomechanical stress in orthopedic implants, agent-based simulations of cancer-immune interactions, and real-time optimization of anesthesia protocols using reinforcement learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for metastatic risk stratification in canine mast cell tumors, breed-specific guidelines for implant design in feline femoral fractures, and generative models for synthetic contrast-enhanced CT images to reduce diagnostic radiation exposure. By leveraging parallelized computing, these models will address critical bottlenecks in veterinary translational research, such as scaling patient-specific simulations across large cohorts and validating computational predictions against clinical outcomes. The project will establish an open-access repository of validated computational workflows tailored to veterinary applications, fostering collaboration between clinical researchers and computational scientists. This work directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance evidence-based companion animal care through innovation, with potential impacts on reducing postoperative complications, improving survival rates in oncology cases, and refining personalized treatment protocols in diverse small animal populations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Small/ Companion Animal Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of companion and household animals. Includes instruction in avian medicine, pet care, companion animal medicine, pathophysiology, small animal diseases, small animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a federated machine learning framework to model patient-specific metabolic responses to combination therapies, integrating multi-omics data with real-time wearable sensor inputs. While precision medicine increasingly leverages genomic and proteomic data, predicting dynamic physiological outcomes—particularly for patients with complex comorbidities—remains limited by fragmented data integration and computational inefficiencies in modeling nonlinear, high-dimensional interactions. Current approaches often silo biochemical, behavioral, and treatment response data, neglecting temporal resolution and inter-system feedback loops critical for personalized dosing. We propose a hybrid graph neural network (GNN) architecture optimized for heterogeneous biomedical data streams, including metabolomic time series, electronic health record parameters, and continuous glucose/activity monitoring. The model will be trained on a distributed dataset of 12,000+ patients with metabolic syndrome comorbidities, utilizing high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage federated learning across encrypted health data nodes while preserving privacy. Computational challenges include scaling transformer-based attention mechanisms for cross-modal feature alignment and simulating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic interactions through differentiable ordinary differential equation solvers embedded in the GNN. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting glycemic variability and adverse event risks under proposed treatment regimens, with clinical validation planned via retrospective cohort analysis and in silico trials. Successful implementation will advance the integration of dynamic biosensor data into precision treatment planning, directly addressing computational bottlenecks in multi-scale health informatics. This work requires GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized model training, high-memory instances for large-scale graph processing, and secure enclave capabilities to maintain HIPAA compliance during federated updates. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source modules for adaptive therapy optimization, filling a critical gap in real-time, data-driven clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer science and software engineering to health and/or biomedical research,  and the development of advanced database, and decision systems. Includes instruction in biomedical and/or health sciences; information science and technology; social and behavioral sciences; biomedical/health information science and technology; human factors and socio-technical systems;  applied social, behavioral, and information science and technology; and informatics aspects of specific research and practice problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing behavioral interventions in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA). A critical challenge in ABA is efficiently tailoring evidence-based interventions to the heterogeneous needs of individuals with developmental disabilities and autism, particularly when managing large-scale, longitudinal datasets that capture complex behavioral patterns, environmental variables, and intervention outcomes. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model the dynamic, non-linear interactions between these factors, limiting the personalization and timeliness of care. To address this, we propose a computational approach integrating machine learning (ML) and network analysis to identify predictive biomarkers of intervention success from multimodal data, including structured observational coding, ecological momentary assessments, and wearable sensor outputs. HPC resources will enable the training of deep learning models on high-dimensional time-series data, parallelized simulations of behavioral trajectories under varying intervention parameters, and real-time optimization of intervention protocols via reinforcement learning. The computational pipeline will prioritize interpretability to align with ABA’s emphasis on functional assessment and ethical practice. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for predicting individual responses to specific intervention strategies, (2) generative models to simulate the long-term impacts of behavioral supports, and (3) open-source tools to help practitioners dynamically adjust interventions based on real-time data. By reducing computational bottlenecks in analyzing large behavioral datasets, this work aims to accelerate the translation of ABA research into precision-based practices, ultimately improving quality of life for individuals with developmental disabilities. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data storage, and collaborative tools for interdisciplinary teams working at the intersection of behavior analysis and computational psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principles of learning and behavior to enhance the development, abilities, and choices of children and adults; and that prepares individuals to address the behavioral needs of individuals, especially those with developmental disabilities and autism. Includes instruction in behavior analysis and learning, behavioral and functional assessment, developmental psychology, applied behavioral analysis in developmental disabilities and autism, applied behavioral analysis in mental health and aging, research methods, evaluation of interventions, and professional and ethical issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic executive support logistics, a critical yet underexplored area within business operations. Executive assistants (EAs) face complex challenges in optimizing schedules, resource allocation, and crisis response for high-level stakeholders, particularly in environments with competing priorities, real-time disruptions, and multi-layered confidentiality constraints. Traditional rule-based scheduling tools often fail to account for the nuanced interpersonal dynamics, contextual adaptability, and predictive demands inherent to executive support. This project proposes the development of a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and reinforcement learning to simulate and optimize decision-making processes in executive assistance scenarios.
