High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets of anonymized executive communication patterns, calendar interactions, and historical crisis resolution logs, while training adaptive models that account for variables such as stakeholder preferences, organizational hierarchies, and real-time geopolitical or market disruptions. The computational pipeline will include clustering algorithms to categorize emergent priorities, Monte Carlo simulations for risk-weighted scenario planning, and NLP-driven sentiment analysis to prioritize communications. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for proactive resource allocation, a benchmarking toolkit for evaluating EA operational efficiency, and open-source simulation modules tailored to executive support training. By bridging computational social science with operational logistics, this work aims to establish quantitative frameworks for a domain traditionally governed by qualitative heuristics, offering scalable solutions to enhance strategic decision support in executive roles. Results will be tested against real-world case studies from partnered corporate and nonprofit organizations, with potential applications in AI-assisted workflow design and cross-sector competency standards for executive support professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and/or personal secretaries for business executives and top management. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, public relations, scheduling and travel management, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, conference and meeting recording, report preparation, office equipment and procedures, office supervisory skills, and professional standards and legal requirements.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving dynamics of digital content distribution and consumer engagement in visual arts and media industries. The rapid growth of online platforms, generative AI tools, and immersive media technologies has created complex challenges for arts organizations and creative enterprises, particularly in predicting market trends, optimizing resource allocation, and mitigating risks associated with digital rights management. Current analytical models lack the capacity to process multimodal datasets—including image metadata, user interaction logs, and cross-platform engagement metrics—at scales required for actionable insights. This project will develop machine learning pipelines to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of digital art transactions, social media interactions, and virtual exhibition attendance records. Computational methods will include computer vision models for style trend detection, graph neural networks to map creator-consumer networks, and agent-based simulations of digital art market behaviors. By integrating these approaches on HPC infrastructure, the research aims to identify patterns in emerging media consumption, forecast demand for hybrid physical-digital art experiences, and model the financial viability of AI-assisted creative workflows. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for arts managers to simulate audience development strategies, assess intellectual property risks in AI-generated content, and optimize pricing models for digital collectibles. The computational framework will address critical gaps in arts management practice, particularly in adapting to Web3 ecosystems and multisensory media formats, while maintaining ethical constraints around cultural equity and creator compensation. Results will be disseminated through a cloud-based dashboard for arts organizations and peer-reviewed publications on computational cultural analytics.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Arts, Entertainment, and Media Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage various aspects of the visual arts, performing arts, and entertainment media industries. Includes instruction in business and financial management, marketing and fund-raising, labor relations for the arts, event promotion and management, product and artist management, and applicable law.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamics of decentralized, algorithmically mediated social trust in hybrid digital-physical communities, a phenomenon emerging at the intersection of socio-technical systems and grassroots organizational behavior. As traditional institutions decline, new trust networks—spanning mutual aid collectives, decentralized governance protocols, and crisis-response micro-communities—are forming through novel interactions between human social cognition and machine learning systems. The research problem centers on modeling how these hybrid communities develop shared epistemologies and coordinate action despite lacking centralized authority, particularly examining how algorithmic tools both scaffold and distort trust-building processes. Using a mixed-methods computational approach, we will analyze multi-platform interaction data (text, transaction logs, and federated governance decisions) from three case studies spanning urban cooperatives and digital nomad networks. High-performance computing resources are required to implement large-scale network analysis across temporal graphs capturing human and algorithmic actor relationships, coupled with transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned to detect implicit trust signaling in multilingual, multimodal communications. Agent-based modeling will simulate how micro-level interactions between human bias parameters and algorithmic recommendation systems generate macro-level trust patterns, validated against ethnographic fieldwork. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying "algorithmic social capital" and predictive models of trust cascade failures in decentralized organizations. This work advances sociological understanding of 21st-century institutional emergence while developing computational anthropology methodologies for studying embedded AI-human systems. Results will inform the design of socially sustainable decentralized technologies and policy approaches to governing adaptive socio-algorithmic networks.
cip_definition: A program that combines sociology and anthropology to study how society is organized, the origins and development of social institutions, social change, social organizations, race, class, gender and culture.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to analyze and optimize decision-making processes in music management, with a focus on predictive modeling for audience engagement, resource allocation in event promotion, and dynamic pricing strategies for music products. The research addresses the growing complexity of data-driven management in the music industry, where large-scale datasets from streaming platforms, social media, and ticket sales require advanced analytical methods. Traditional approaches often struggle to integrate multimodal data (e.g., audio metadata, consumer behavior metrics, geographic trends) in real time, limiting adaptive strategies for emerging artists and small-to-mid-sized music organizations. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC) framework leveraging machine learning and agent-based modeling. The computational pipeline will process terabyte-scale datasets to train ensemble models predicting regional demand for live events, simulate the impact of marketing variables on merchandise sales, and identify optimal contract terms for artist-fan engagement platforms. GPU-accelerated clustering algorithms will classify audience segments based on streaming patterns and demographic cross-correlations, while Monte Carlo methods will assess financial risk in tour planning scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these analyses across heterogeneous datasets and enabling real-time parameter optimization via parallelized workflows. Outcomes will include open-source software modules for music management analytics, validated against case studies from independent record labels and music festivals. By integrating computational social science methods with industry-specific challenges, this work aims to democratize data-driven tools for non-profit music organizations and reduce operational uncertainties in artist promotion. The project will also contribute interdisciplinary insights into how computational resource allocation can support creative industries within academic programs focused on visual arts, media, and design.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage music organizations, operations, facilities, and personnel. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; music products merchandising; artist agency and promotion; music law; and applications to specific activities such as managing theaters, recording studios and companies, bands and other ensembles, individual artists, and music organizations.

abstract: The integration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) with modern computational approaches presents a unique opportunity to decode the complex mechanisms underlying herbal formulae, which often exhibit polypharmacological effects through multi-component, multi-target interactions. Despite the widespread use of TCM in global health contexts, the systems-level biological processes modulated by herbal combinations remain poorly characterized, limiting their acceptance in evidence-based frameworks. This project seeks to address this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model the dynamic interactions between bioactive compounds in classical Chinese herbal formulae and human proteomic networks, with a focus on Qi-regulating formulations used in metabolic and immune dysregulation syndromes. Leveraging molecular docking simulations, machine learning-driven network pharmacology, and multi-omics integration, we will systematically analyze 50 prioritized formulae from the *Jin Gui Yao Lue* and *Shang Han Lun* classics. Computational workflows will be designed to account for TCM-specific parameters, including herb processing methods, dosage ratios, and meridian tropism, while cross-referencing with Western biomedical ontologies. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale virtual screening of over 10,000 phytochemicals against disease-relevant protein targets, coupled with dynamic network analysis to identify synergistic nodes and emergent therapeutic pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of herb-herb-host interaction networks, (2) mechanistic hypotheses for clinically observed formula efficacy in managing Xiao Ke (wasting-thirsting) syndromes, and (3) a novel computational framework that bridges TCM theory with systems biology. This research will provide unprecedented resolution into the "Jun-Chen-Zuo-Shi" (monarch-minister-assistant-ambassador) hierarchy of herbal combinations, while establishing computational pipelines for validating traditional knowledge through contemporary bioinformatics paradigms. The requested resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of herbal formulae and achieving statistically robust results across multiple scales of biological organization.
cip_title: Traditional Chinese Medicine and Chinese Herbology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Chinese herbal medicine, a system based on the use of nutrition, natural products, and prescribed medical formulae to treat imbalances in the state of bodily health as defined in the Nei Ching Su Wen and other authorities. Includes instruction in the basic Western medical sciences, history and theory of Chinese medicine, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbology, herbal prescription preparation, herbal patent medicine, herbal pharmacology, Chinese internal medicine and gynecology, febrile diseases, food therapy, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing volume and heterogeneity of signals intelligence (SIGINT) data from multi-domain sensors—including radar, acoustic arrays, and electro-optical systems—present significant challenges for real-time processing and actionable geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) extraction. Traditional computational architectures struggle with the latency and scalability demands of integrating disparate sensor streams, particularly in contested environments where rapid decision-making is critical. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework optimized for multi-modal SIGINT fusion and adaptive signal exploitation. Leveraging distributed memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated processing, the proposed framework will implement novel algorithms for real-time feature extraction, cross-domain correlation, and anomaly detection across terahertz-frequency radar returns, underwater acoustic signatures, and hyperspectral infrared datasets. The computational approach integrates graph-based signal representation with machine learning models trained on phenomenology-specific datasets to enable context-aware processing in dynamic operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for concurrent processing of petabyte-scale SIGINT collections, reducing analyst burden through automated pattern recognition and predictive threat modeling. The research will advance computational methodologies for next-generation intelligence architectures, directly supporting enhanced situational awareness and time-sensitive decision processes in joint military operations. By bridging the gap between raw sensor data and tactical intelligence products, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for processing efficiency and analytical fidelity in emerging multi-intelligence fusion environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational aspects of collecting, processing and exploiting remote-sensed, radar, acoustic and other forms of signals intelligence. Includes instruction in applied physics, wave propagation and capture, radar systems, acoustics and underwater systems, infrared systems, synthetic aperture systems, collection and processing systems, signal phenomenology, signal analysis and exploitation, and applications to specific intelligence problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing school counseling interventions through predictive analytics and large-scale longitudinal data analysis. School counselors face increasing demands to address students’ academic, social-emotional, and career development needs, yet limited empirical guidance exists on how to tailor interventions to diverse student populations or forecast long-term outcomes of counseling strategies. The research problem centers on analyzing complex, multi-source datasets—including student academic records, behavioral surveys, and counseling session metadata—to identify patterns in intervention efficacy, equity gaps in service access, and factors influencing post-secondary readiness. Computational methods will include machine learning models (e.g., gradient-boosted decision trees, neural networks) to predict intervention outcomes across demographic subgroups, natural language processing (NLP) to analyze counselor-student interaction logs for linguistic markers of therapeutic progress, and agent-based simulations to model the systemic impact of proposed counseling frameworks. The scale of data—spanning 10+ years of anonymized records from 50+ K-12 institutions—requires HPC capabilities for distributed processing, hyperparameter tuning, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing statistical robustness. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive toolkit to prioritize interventions for at-risk students, (2) equity-focused benchmarks for counseling resource allocation, and (3) generative AI prototypes to assist counselors in personalizing communication strategies. By integrating computational social science with counselor education, this work aims to establish data-driven best practices for scaling evidence-based guidance services while addressing heterogeneity in student needs. The requested resources will enable iterative model training on sensitive educational data within secure, high-memory nodes while maintaining compliance with FERPA and institutional review protocols.
cip_title: Counselor Education/ School Counseling and Guidance Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the theory and principles of guidance and counseling to the provision of support for the personal, social, educational, and vocational development of students, and the organizing of guidance services within elementary, middle and secondary educational institutions. Includes instruction in legal and professional requirements, therapeutic counselor intervention, vocational counseling, and related sociological and psychological foundations.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in veterinary administrative workflows through the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support system optimized for veterinary practice management. Veterinary administrative professionals, including executive assistants and secretaries, face complex challenges in scheduling, client communication, and compliance tracking due to the unique integration of medical, regulatory, and business requirements in veterinary settings. Existing generic office management tools lack domain-specific adaptations for veterinary terminology, ethical protocols, and multi-species care coordination, leading to workflow fragmentation and preventable errors. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate machine learning models capable of automating context-aware task prioritization, dynamic scheduling adjustments, and compliance documentation audits. A hybrid computational architecture combining natural language processing (NLP) for client communication analysis, graph neural networks for interleaved task dependencies, and reinforcement learning for adaptive resource allocation will be developed. The models will be trained on a curated dataset of anonymized veterinary administrative records, including appointment logs, client interaction transcripts, and regulatory inspection reports from 200+ practices. Computational experiments will focus on optimizing real-time processing of heterogeneous data streams while maintaining strict privacy-preserving protocols required for veterinary client-patient confidentiality. Anticipated outcomes include a prototype system demonstrating reduced administrative processing times, improved compliance accuracy, and enhanced predictive capacity for workload balancing in veterinary settings. Successful implementation could establish novel benchmarks for AI applications in veterinary administration, with potential translational benefits for other healthcare-adjacent administrative domains. This work highlights the critical role of specialized computational tools in supporting non-clinical veterinary professionals, bridging gaps between operational efficiency, regulatory demands, and quality of care imperatives.
cip_title: Veterinary Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Veterinary Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing veterinarians, veterinary health care facilities and services administrators, and other veterinary professionals. Includes instruction in business and veterinary communications, veterinary terminology, principles of veterinary health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of diagnosing and managing multifactorial diseases in veterinary patients—such as chronic kidney disease, endocrine disorders, and age-related comorbidities—demands advanced computational tools to integrate heterogeneous data and improve clinical decision-making. Traditional approaches in veterinary internal medicine often rely on static diagnostic criteria and generalized treatment protocols, which fail to account for dynamic interactions between genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model disease progression, optimize diagnostic accuracy, and predict treatment responses in companion animals. Leveraging anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-time biometric sensor outputs from diverse animal populations, we will employ machine learning algorithms to identify predictive biomarkers and simulate disease pathways. Key computational tasks include large-scale data integration, ensemble model training for phenotype classification, and agent-based modeling of intrahospital disease transmission dynamics in referral settings. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets, running parallelized simulations of pharmacodynamic interactions across species, and validating models against clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include validated decision-support tools for early disease detection, personalized therapeutic recommendations, and evidence-based protocols for managing aging-related conditions. This work will directly enhance the precision of general medical services in veterinary practice, reduce diagnostic delays, and improve the management of non-surgical clinical cases. By establishing scalable computational methods tailored to veterinary data structures, the project also aims to address gaps in species-specific clinical research, ultimately supporting translational advancements in animal and human health.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of general medical services to animals with a wide range of non-surgical clinical problems. May included related research in behavioral aspects of diseases, animal diagnosis, animal aging, and referral procedures.

abstract: Early childhood education relies on dynamic teacher-child interactions that significantly influence developmental and academic outcomes. However, traditional observational methods and small-scale analyses lack the granularity and scalability needed to identify patterns across diverse contexts. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets (video, audio, and longitudinal assessments) from early childhood classrooms, employing machine learning (ML) techniques to model interaction dynamics. By processing thousands of hours of classroom footage with computer vision and natural language processing algorithms, we aim to quantify nuanced aspects of teacher responsiveness, emotional tone, and instructional strategies. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how variations in these factors propagate through classroom ecosystems, affecting collective skill acquisition and socioemotional development. The computational intensity of training deep neural networks on multimodal data and running large-scale simulations necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workloads. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for embedding HPC-driven analytics into teacher education programs, (2) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing real-time teacher decision-making, and (3) open-source tools to help educators visualize and interpret interaction patterns in their own classrooms. This work will bridge gaps between educational theory and data-informed practice, equipping early childhood educators with scalable strategies to personalize instruction and foster equitable learning environments. The requested resources will directly support advancing computational pedagogy as a critical domain within teacher preparation.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students ranging in age from infancy through eight years (grade three), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance our understanding of the dynamical evolution of dwarf galaxies within dark matter-dominated environments. A critical unresolved challenge in astrophysics is reconciling observed kinematic and morphological properties of dwarf galaxies with predictions from cosmological simulations, particularly discrepancies in dark matter density profiles and star formation histories. To address this, we propose a suite of high-resolution, multi-physics simulations that integrate baryonic physics—including star formation, supernova feedback, and metal enrichment—with high-fidelity dark matter structure formation. The simulations will utilize adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques via the ENZO code, coupled with custom subgrid models for interstellar medium processes, to resolve scales from galactic (~10 kpc) down to star-forming regions (~1 pc). This multi-scale approach demands significant computational resources due to the dynamic range required, including parallelized gravitational N-body solvers, radiative hydrodynamics, and frequent data output for transient phenomena analysis. The requested allocation will enable parameter studies across dark matter profiles (e.g., cold vs. self-interacting models) and environmental conditions (tidal interactions, gas accretion). Anticipated outcomes include refined constraints on dark matter particle properties, mechanisms driving observed diversity in dwarf galaxy populations, and publicly released simulation datasets for cross-comparison with JWST and Rubin Observatory surveys. By resolving the interplay between baryonic feedback and dark matter dynamics at unprecedented scales, this work will directly inform theoretical frameworks for galaxy formation and test paradigms of hierarchical structure growth in the Lambda-CDM cosmology. The computational scale—requiring ~2 million core-hours and 200 TB of storage—is essential to achieve the spatial/temporal resolution necessary for statistically robust conclusions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in astronomy and astrophysics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the modeling and optimization of resilient urban transportation networks under dynamic stressors, including population growth, climate variability, and evolving mobility technologies. Current simulation frameworks struggle to capture the interdependencies between infrastructure degradation, traffic flow patterns, and real-time decision-making at metropolitan scales, limiting their utility for adaptive planning. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining agent-based modeling, finite element analysis, and graph-theoretic network optimization. The computational workflow will integrate multi-resolution datasets—spanning traffic sensor feeds, material fatigue models, and socioeconomic mobility patterns—into a coupled simulation platform. Parallelized finite element solvers will assess pavement and bridge deterioration under probabilistic climate scenarios, while GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize traffic signal control and rerouting strategies in response to simulated disruptions. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these analyses to city-level networks with sub-meter spatial resolution and sub-minute temporal resolution, which exceeds the capacity of conventional workstations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for quantifying trade-offs between infrastructure maintenance investments, congestion mitigation, and equity in transportation access. Results will inform the development of digital twin tools for municipal planners, enabling proactive adaptation to systemic shocks. By leveraging distributed memory architectures and scalable optimization libraries, this work will also contribute methodological advances in computationally intensive civil systems analysis. The resource request supports 12 months of large-scale simulations on GPU- and CPU-based clusters, including parametric studies across 10+ metropolitan templates. This project aligns with national priorities for sustainable urban infrastructure and provides open-source computational tools to the civil engineering community.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in civil engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Neuromuscular disorders represent a heterogeneous group of conditions with complex molecular mechanisms, variable clinical presentations, and limited therapeutic options. A critical barrier to advancing precision medicine in this field is the integration and analysis of multi-modal data—including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical datasets—to identify biomarkers, stratify patient subtypes, and predict disease progression. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through large-scale computational modeling and artificial intelligence-driven approaches. We will develop machine learning frameworks to integrate multi-omics data from patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), hereditary neuropathies, and congenital myopathies, leveraging publicly available datasets (e.g., ALS Consortium, ClinVar) and institutional biorepositories. Key computational tasks include whole-genome sequencing variant prioritization using graph-based neural networks, dynamic modeling of neuromuscular junction protein interactions via molecular dynamics simulations, and unsupervised clustering of clinical-electrophysiological patterns to redefine phenotypic classifications. The analysis will employ containerized workflows (Singularity/Nextflow) to ensure reproducibility, with GPU-accelerated deep learning models (PyTorch, TensorFlow) for feature extraction from high-dimensional data. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel genotype-phenotype correlations, predictive models for disease trajectories, and candidate therapeutic targets validated through in silico docking studies. By elucidating shared molecular pathways across distinct neuromuscular disorders, this work aims to accelerate translational insights into personalized treatment strategies. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of processing terabytes of sequencing data, running iterative simulations, and training complex models, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters. This project aligns with national priorities in neuromuscular research and has direct implications for improving diagnostic accuracy, prognostic stratification, and therapeutic development for patients with these debilitating conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of disorders of nerve, muscle, or neuromuscular junction, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, peripheral neuropathies, various muscular dystrophies, congenital and acquired myopathies, inflammatory myopathies, and neuromuscular transmission disorders.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the long-term impacts of colonial legal and administrative frameworks on contemporary political behavior and institutional trust in post-colonial states, integrating computational historical analysis with political science theory. The central challenge lies in analyzing fragmented, multilingual archival records (e.g., colonial legislation, court proceedings, and correspondence) alongside modern political surveys and institutional performance data to identify path-dependent relationships between historical governance patterns and current socio-political dynamics. We propose a multi-scale computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of historical documents, agent-based modeling to simulate institutional legacy transmission across generations, and network analysis to map how colonial-era administrative structures evolved into modern governance networks. High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabytes of digitized archival materials across seven languages using transformer-based NLP models, run complex simulations capturing century-scale societal interactions, and analyze multilayer networks connecting historical actors to contemporary institutions. The project will develop novel computational methods for temporal knowledge graph construction, addressing sparse data interpolation challenges through probabilistic modeling of historical events. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for quantifying institutional continuity/rupture across colonial and post-colonial periods, 2) identification of critical junctures where policy interventions could have altered present-day political trajectories, and 3) predictive models assessing how specific historical governance practices (e.g., indirect rule, legal pluralism) correlate with modern patterns of political participation and state legitimacy. By creating interoperable digital archives and analytical tools, this work will enable comparative studies of decolonization processes while providing policymakers with evidence-based insights into addressing systemic inequities rooted in historical institutions.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and political science or a specialization which draws from history and political science. Includes instruction in comparative government and politics, historiography, historical research methods, political science, political theory, records administration, and systematic study of political institutions and behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural and regional identities within Italian diaspora communities through the computational analysis of historical texts, oral histories, and multimedia archives. The research problem centers on understanding how localized traditions, dialects, and collective memories were preserved, adapted, or transformed across generations of migration, particularly in North and South American contexts from the late 19th to mid-20th centuries. Current methodologies in cultural studies lack scalable tools to systematically analyze the vast, multilingual corpus of personal correspondence, community newspapers, and audio recordings that document these transnational experiences. To address this gap, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical Italian dialects and English-Italian code-switching patterns, alongside network analysis to map the circulation of cultural narratives across migrant networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on fragmented, noisy textual data, as well as for running large-scale simulations of cultural transmission dynamics using agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include the development of a novel computational framework for diasporic cultural analysis, identification of key factors influencing identity retention in migrant enclaves, and geotemporal visualizations of cultural exchange hotspots. The findings will contribute to interdisciplinary scholarship on cultural memory and ethnic identity formation while providing open-access tools for analyzing underrepresented narratives in Italian diasporic heritage. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to overcome current limitations in processing heterogeneous historical sources at scale, offering new insights into how migration shaped modern conceptions of Italianness beyond national borders.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of modern Italy and its predecessors on the Italian Peninsula, including the overseas migrations of Italian peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of quantum-coherent processes in photosynthetic protein complexes under non-equilibrium conditions, integrating principles from quantum biophysics, photochemistry, and condensed matter physics. While quantum effects in biological systems have been studied in isolated contexts, the interplay between coherent energy transfer, environmental decoherence, and protein conformational fluctuations remains poorly understood. The central challenge lies in modeling these multiscale interactions across temporal (femtoseconds to milliseconds) and spatial (angstroms to micrometers) scales, requiring unprecedented computational synthesis of quantum dynamics, molecular mechanics, and mesoscale environmental perturbations. The research will employ hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations combined with tensor network algorithms optimized for photosynthetic exciton systems, executed on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to achieve the necessary parallelization of multidimensional parameter spaces. Key innovations include adaptive sampling protocols to track rare conformational states influencing coherence lifetimes and machine learning-driven dimensionality reduction for analyzing simulation trajectories. Expected outcomes include predictive models of how specific protein architectures protect quantum coherence under physiological noise, with implications for bio-inspired quantum material design and synthetic biology applications. The computational framework will also enable exploration of nonequilibrium control strategies using tailored electromagnetic fields to enhance coherent energy transport—a potential gateway to novel photonic technologies. By bridging quantum physics with structural biology and nonlinear dynamics, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding life’s potential exploitation of quantum phenomena while establishing scalable computational methodologies for studying complexity across biological and quantum systems. Resource allocation is essential for handling the project’s teraflop-scale demands, particularly for GPU-accelerated quantum dynamical calculations and large-scale Monte Carlo sampling of conformational landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that is either a general synthesis of one or more of the biological and physical sciences, or a specialization which draws from the biological and physical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the safety and efficiency of next-generation nuclear reactor designs, with a focus on addressing challenges in thermal-hydraulic behavior and neutron transport under extreme operating conditions. Current reactor simulations often rely on simplified approximations due to computational limitations, leading to conservative design margins that hinder performance improvements. To overcome this, we propose a multi-physics framework integrating high-fidelity Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for coolant flow modeling, and machine learning-driven uncertainty quantification. The research problem centers on resolving coupled neutronic-thermal-mechanical interactions in molten salt reactor configurations, where traditional codes struggle with complex phase changes and time-dependent material properties. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations at reactor-scale resolution, including 3D full-core models with <1 mm mesh precision for localized boiling detection. The computational workflow will leverage OpenMC for neutronics, OpenFOAM for CFD, and custom Python-based AI/ML pipelines for surrogate model training. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for transient scenarios, such as rapid power excursions or coolant loss events, enabling safer cladding material selection and optimized fuel cycle management. This work directly supports the development of inherently safer reactor designs by reducing reliance on empirical safety factors, potentially lowering capital costs for advanced nuclear systems. Successful implementation will yield publicly accessible datasets and open-source code extensions, fostering collaboration in nuclear computational research. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated architectures will accommodate the project’s need for ensemble simulations across parametric design spaces, with individual runs requiring up to 24 hours on 256 nodes. Results will be disseminated through the Journal of Nuclear Technology and inform regulatory guidance documents on multiphysics verification benchmarks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of research scientists and operating engineers engaged in the running of nuclear reactors, and in nuclear materials processing and disposal. Includes instruction in basic nuclear physics and nuclear engineering, monitoring and safety procedures, radioactive materials handling and disposal, equipment maintenance and operation, and record keeping.

abstract: The rapid expansion of multi-omics datasets and high-resolution ecological sensor networks presents unprecedented opportunities to model complex biological systems, yet integrating these heterogeneous data streams remains a critical bottleneck. This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework combining interpretable machine learning (ML) and network-based data mining to uncover hidden interactions between microbial communities, environmental stressors, and ecosystem resilience in rapidly changing Arctic watersheds. Current approaches struggle with sparse temporal alignment, cross-scale dependencies (molecular to landscape-level), and non-linear feedback loops inherent in these systems. We propose an adaptive ensemble method leveraging multi-task graph neural networks (GNNs) with attention mechanisms to process metagenomic, geochemical, and remote sensing data while preserving ecological interpretability. The framework will implement hybrid sampling techniques to address extreme class imbalances in rare microbial taxa observations and employ causal discovery algorithms to disentangle correlation from mechanistic drivers. Computational challenges include training memory-intensive GNNs on terabyte-scale spatiotemporal graphs and optimizing hyperparameter searches across interdependent biological and physical variables. The project requires high-performance computing resources for parallelized model training, distributed storage of evolving graph structures, and real-time visualization of high-dimensional latent spaces. Expected outcomes include 1) open-source tools for dynamic ecological network inference, 2) predictive models identifying early-warning signals for critical transitions in permafrost-derived water systems, and 3) a benchmark dataset linking microbial functional traits to landscape-scale methane flux patterns. By bridging gaps between microbial ecology, climate science, and explainable AI, this work aims to provide actionable insights for environmental managers while advancing methodological integration across disciplinary data paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of data mining and machine learning. Includes instruction in naive Bayes rule, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, decision tree learning, neural nets, network science, optimization, statistical computing, and graphical models and methods.

abstract: The increasing complexity of supply chain dynamics in the automotive, marine, and aviation aftermarkets necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize inventory management and distribution strategies. This research addresses the challenge of integrating real-time telematics and IoT data from connected vehicles and equipment into predictive demand forecasting models for replacement parts. Traditional inventory systems in vehicle parts marketing rely on historical sales data and static regional demand patterns, often leading to inefficiencies in storage, delayed fulfillment, and excess waste. This project proposes a novel computational framework that synthesizes high-frequency sensor data (e.g., engine performance metrics, component wear patterns) with customer behavior analytics to predict part failure risks and regional demand spikes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process terabytes of streaming telematics data, train deep learning models on temporal-spatial demand signals, and simulate multi-echelon inventory networks under dynamic scenarios. The computational pipeline includes graph neural networks to model interdependencies between parts failure cascades and transformer-based architectures for cross-modal fusion of structured sales data with unstructured service logs. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for regional distribution centers, enabling proactive stock rebalancing and dynamic pricing adjustments. The project’s significance lies in bridging the gap between vehicular IoT ecosystems and business operations, reducing supply chain waste by an estimated 15–20% in pilot sectors, while improving service-level agreements for commercial and consumer clients. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances interdisciplinary research at the intersection of operational analytics, embedded systems data, and sustainable logistics—a niche yet critical domain for next-generation vehicle parts marketing.
cip_title: Vehicle and Vehicle Parts and Accessories Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of replacement parts and other end-use supplies in the automotive, marine, and aviation industries. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, principles of vehicular technologies, storage and distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to optimize diagnostic workflows in clinical laboratory settings by integrating real-time biosensor data with machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics. Clinical laboratory assistants (CLAs) perform critical tasks such as waived testing and phlebotomy, yet current protocols rely on static decision trees for sample prioritization, leading to inefficiencies in high-throughput environments. To address this, we propose a dynamic, adaptive system that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal data streams—including biosensor outputs (e.g., pH, temperature), sample metadata, and historical workflow patterns—to predict and mitigate bottlenecks. The research problem centers on the lack of real-time adaptability in laboratory workflows, which contributes to delayed turnaround times and increased pre-analytical error rates. Our computational approach involves three phases: (1) simulating laboratory workflows using agent-based modeling to identify inefficiencies under variable conditions, (2) training deep reinforcement learning models on synthetic and retrospective clinical data to generate adaptive scheduling algorithms, and (3) deploying these models in a cloud-HPC hybrid environment for real-time inference and validation. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and high-memory nodes for large-scale simulation of workflow scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive system that reduces sample processing delays by ≥20% and decreases pre-analytical errors by ≥15% in simulated environments, with potential for integration into laboratory information systems (LIS). This work bridges gaps between clinical laboratory science, computational optimization, and real-time data analytics, offering a novel tool to enhance the precision and efficiency of CLA-driven workflows while maintaining compliance with CLIA regulations. The scalability of this framework may also inform future applications in resource-limited settings or emerging point-of-care testing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians or laboratory scientists or technologists, to perform waived testing procedures (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988), phlebotomy, and other duties in support of laboratory teams. Includes instruction in clinical procedures, various laboratory tests, laboratory mathematics, computer technology, equipment operation and maintenance, sterilization and safety, communications skills, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: Understanding the dynamics of contaminant transport in heterogeneous aquifers is critical for safeguarding groundwater resources, yet existing models struggle to resolve fine-scale geological variability and transient hydrologic processes. This project seeks to advance predictive capabilities for contaminant migration—particularly arsenic and nitrate species—in complex aquifer systems by integrating high-resolution 3D hydrogeological modeling with reactive transport simulations. The research will employ parallelized finite-element models (e.g., MODFLOW coupled with PHT3D) to simulate coupled groundwater flow, solute advection-dispersion, and geochemical interactions across scales. Stochastic methods will quantify uncertainty in hydraulic conductivity fields and redox zonation, informed by geophysical and borehole data from two case study aquifers in arsenic-affected regions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve meter-scale heterogeneity across domains exceeding 100 km², execute ensemble simulations for parameter sensitivity analysis, and optimize machine learning surrogates to accelerate Monte Carlo-based risk assessments. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for coupling stochastic hydrostratigraphic models with reactive transport codes, (2) improved quantification of timescales for contaminant mobility under pumping-induced hydraulic gradient shifts, and (3) probabilistic risk maps identifying vulnerable zones in target aquifers. The computational workflows will be containerized for community reuse via HydroShare. By advancing the integration of HPC-driven stochastic modeling with geochemical realism, this work will directly inform managed aquifer recharge strategies and wellfield management policies, addressing a critical need for predictive tools in regions where groundwater contamination threatens drinking water security. The project aligns with national priorities on water resource resilience while demonstrating how compute-intensive hydrologic models can transition into operational decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the occurrence, circulation, distribution, chemical and physical properties, and environmental interaction of surface and subsurface waters, including groundwater. Includes instruction in geophysics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, chemical physics, geomorphology, mathematical modeling, hydrologic analysis, continental water processes, global water balance, and environmental science.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making processes during critical incident response operations, such as hostage rescues, active shooter scenarios, and coordinated terrorist threats. While traditional approaches rely on static protocols and human intuition, the dynamic, high-stakes nature of these events demands adaptive tools capable of integrating real-time data streams, environmental variables, and behavioral predictions. The core challenge lies in modeling complex, multi-agent interactions under uncertainty while accounting for psychological, logistical, and tactical constraints unique to law enforcement emergencies. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the project will implement a hybrid simulation architecture combining agent-based modeling, game-theoretic decision trees, and machine learning-driven risk assessment. The computational models will incorporate anonymized historical incident data, 3D geospatial reconstructions of real-world venues, and behavioral datasets derived from de-escalation training simulations. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will stress-test response strategies across thousands of scenario permutations, evaluating outcomes through metrics including civilian survivability rates, operational timeline efficiency, and resource deployment precision. A novel component involves integrating natural language processing to analyze negotiation transcripts and predict perpetrator escalation patterns. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system prototype that generates probabilistic action pathways during live incidents and an after-action analysis toolkit for identifying procedural bottlenecks. The computational intensity of simultaneously processing IoT sensor data, biometric inputs, and environmental variables necessitates cluster-scale resources for both training deep reinforcement learning models and running multi-parameter sensitivity analyses. By bridging computational social science with operational tactics, this work aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for critical incident management while advancing methodological frameworks for HPC applications in public safety domains.
cip_title: Critical Incident Response/ Special Police Operations
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for dealing with police emergencies such as hostage situations, bomb threats, barricades and terrorist incidents. Includes instruction in crisis management, command procedures, incident containment, information collection and debriefing, first responder negotiation, victim and criminal psychology, site survey and surveillance, special weapons and tactics, interagency communications and joint operations, pre-confrontation and contingency planning, assault and rescue operations, security and crowd control, media relations, and post-operation procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that simulate the efficacy of individualized interventions for young children with disabilities in early childhood special education (ECSE) settings. A critical challenge in ECSE is the dynamic, heterogeneous nature of learning needs among children aged 0–5, which complicates the design of effective, personalized educational strategies. Existing approaches to creating individualized education plans (IEPs) rely on manual, time-intensive assessments and trial-and-error adjustments, often leading to delays in addressing evolving needs. This research addresses the gap by constructing predictive models that integrate behavioral, cognitive, and environmental data to forecast intervention outcomes. The computational approach employs machine learning (ML) algorithms, including reinforcement learning and ensemble methods, to analyze longitudinal datasets comprising child performance metrics, intervention types, and contextual factors (e.g., classroom environment, caregiver interactions). Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between children, educators, and interventions under diverse scenarios, enabling the identification of optimal strategies for specific developmental profiles. HPC resources are essential to process high-dimensional datasets (e.g., video-based behavioral coding, sensor data) and execute parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for predicting intervention efficacy, (2) actionable insights into tailoring IEPs to mitigate developmental delays, and (3) open-source tools to assist educators in dynamically adjusting teaching strategies. By bridging computational analytics and ECSE practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based, data-driven decision-making in special education, ultimately improving learning trajectories for children with disabilities during critical early developmental windows.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Early Childhood Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to infant and pre-school age children with special learning needs or disabilities, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Urban environments are increasingly shaped by the interplay of digital platforms and physical infrastructure, yet the socio-spatial implications of location-based social media (LBSM) on public space utilization remain poorly understood. This project addresses the critical gap in modeling how real-time, data-driven interactions on platforms like Foursquare and Pokémon GO influence collective behavior patterns, strain shared resources, and reshape equitable access to urban amenities. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a multi-agent simulation framework integrating anonymized LBSM datasets, pedestrian mobility traces, and geospatial inventories of public infrastructure across three mid-sized cities. The computational model will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to map dynamic preference cascades, coupled with reinforcement learning agents that adapt their movement patterns based on evolving social feedback loops. Spatial-temporal analytics will quantify emergent congestion hotspots and "digital deserts" where offline amenities fail to meet digitally amplified demand. By parallelizing sentiment analysis of 12 million geotagged posts across GPU clusters, the system will identify latent thresholds where virtual interactions trigger physical space saturation. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for municipal planners to simulate platform-induced crowd dynamics during urban design processes, alongside policy frameworks for regulating locative media impacts on public space equity. This interdisciplinary approach advances computational urban science by bridging social media analytics with spatial justice theory, offering novel methodologies for managing hybrid digital-physical environments in smart cities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of social science principles to the study of urban institutions and the forces influencing urban social and political life. Includes instruction in urban theory, the development and evolution of urban areas, urban sociology, principles of urban and social planning, and the politics and economics of urban government and services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive, high-dimensional data visualization framework to address the challenge of interpreting complex, heterogeneous datasets emerging from cross-domain scientific collaborations. As interdisciplinary research increasingly integrates diverse data types—from spatially resolved environmental sensor streams to temporally dynamic genomic or social network data—existing visualization tools struggle to balance computational efficiency with perceptual effectiveness. Our work focuses on creating a scalable pipeline that couples topological data analysis with perceptually optimized rendering, enabling researchers to identify latent patterns across disparate data modalities. The computational approach combines GPU-accelerated dimension reduction algorithms, dynamic graph processing, and cognitive load-aware visual encoding strategies, all orchestrated through a distributed workflow manager. High-performance computing resources will be critical for three components: (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets using persistent homology calculations to extract multi-scale features, (2) real-time rendering of 3D/4D visualizations with adaptive level-of-detail adjustments based on user interaction patterns, and (3) machine learning-driven optimization of visual parameter spaces through large-scale A/B testing of perceptual efficacy. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that reduces interpretative bias in multidisciplinary science by maintaining mathematical rigor while respecting human visual cognition constraints. The resource will be validated through case studies in climate-epidemiology modeling and materials science-biointerface research, where it will enable discovery of cross-domain correlations previously obscured by disciplinary visualization conventions. This work bridges gaps between computational topology, perceptual psychology, and domain sciences, advancing the capacity for visual analytics to drive convergence research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and derive meaning from data by using visual presentation tools and techniques. Includes instruction in cognitive science, computer programming, data management, data visualization theory, graphic design, infographics, perceptual psychology, statistics, and visual design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research on understudied Iranian languages, with a focus on historical phonology and morphological analysis. The primary research problem centers on modeling sound changes and morphological shifts across ancient, medieval, and modern Iranian languages—including Avestan, Middle Persian, and modern dialects like Balochi and Zazaki—to reconstruct proto-forms and trace contact-induced changes. Current methodologies rely on manual comparative analysis, which is time-intensive and limited in handling the combinatorial complexity of linguistic variables across time and geography. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models trained on digitized corpora of annotated texts, inscriptions, and lexical databases. Computational workflows will include neural sequence-to-sequence models for simulating sound change processes, graph-based algorithms for identifying shared morphological patterns, and probabilistic clustering to detect substrate influences from neighboring language families. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these analyses to encompass over 50,000 lexical items and 200+ morphological paradigms across 15 languages, as well as enabling parallelized simulations of diachronic developments under varying sociolinguistic parameters. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible database of reconstructed proto-Iranian forms with confidence metrics, 2) computational tools for automated morphological parsing of under-resourced Iranian languages, and 3) new insights into language contact dynamics between Iranian languages and Semitic, Turkic, and Indo-Aryan families. This work will directly support endangered language preservation initiatives and provide a scalable framework for computational historical linguistics in under-documented language families. The requested resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte text corpora and reduce runtime for iterative model training from months to days, making computationally intensive Bayesian phylogenetic analyses feasible for the first time in Iranian linguistic studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages used in ancient, medieval, and modern Iran and its border regions, including modern Persian, Avestan/Old Persian, and related modern and extinct languages. Includes instruction in applications of modern Persian and other languages in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to sustainable power generation, yet optimizing their efficiency, longevity, and environmental compatibility remains a complex challenge. Current limitations in predicting dynamic stressors, sediment-induced turbine wear, and flow variability across seasonal conditions hinder the development of adaptive maintenance protocols and high-efficiency turbine designs. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model hydroelectric system performance under multifactorial operational and environmental conditions. The research will employ multiscale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to analyze turbulent flow interactions with turbine blades, coupled with machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on historical sensor data from operational dams. These models will predict wear patterns, identify failure risks in real time, and simulate the impact of novel composite materials on component durability. Additionally, HPC-driven optimization algorithms will evaluate configurations for turbine arrays to maximize energy output while minimizing ecological disruption. The computational workflow will integrate hydro-mechanical simulations with geospatial data to assess site-specific installation challenges, such as sediment transport in reservoir systems. By correlating simulation outputs with field data from partner hydroelectric facilities, this research aims to establish predictive maintenance frameworks and design guidelines that extend infrastructure lifespans and reduce unplanned downtime. Outcomes will include open-source tools for technicians to simulate repair scenarios and optimize component replacements, directly supporting workforce training and operational decision-making. Access to HPC resources is essential to process high-resolution 3D simulations, train ML models on terabyte-scale datasets, and run iterative optimization analyses. This work will advance the integration of computational modeling into hydroelectric system management, fostering resilient, data-driven practices for sustainable energy infrastructure.
cip_title: Hydroelectric Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing high-performance composite materials for extreme environments by leveraging advanced computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current experimental approaches to designing materials with tailored thermal stability, mechanical strength, and corrosion resistance are limited by the cost and time required to test combinatorial variations in composition, microstructure, and processing conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and phase-field modeling to predict the evolution of material properties under coupled thermal-mechanical-chemical loads. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of atomic-scale defect interactions in metal-ceramic interfaces, mesoscale modeling of grain boundary dynamics in polycrystalline alloys, and parametric studies of processing parameters such as sintering temperatures and cooling rates. These simulations will generate datasets linking synthesis conditions to microstructure-property relationships, which will inform machine learning models to accelerate materials discovery. The outcomes will directly support experimental efforts to develop next-generation composites for energy storage systems and high-temperature industrial applications, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches. By resolving atomic-scale mechanisms of interfacial degradation and phase transformations, this work will advance fundamental knowledge of materials behavior in aggressive environments while providing actionable design guidelines for industry partners. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the high computational cost of ab initio calculations across multiple alloy systems, the memory demands of 3D phase-field simulations at experimentally relevant scales, and the parallel processing required for sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations. Successful completion of this project will establish a validated computational pipeline for accelerated materials development, with potential applications in sustainable manufacturing and decarbonization technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and materials science principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and related processes used in manufacturing in a wide variety of settings; the synthesis of new industrial materials, including marrying and bonding composites; analysis of materials requirements and specifications; and related problems of system design dependent on materials factors.

abstract: Pediatric dentistry faces unique challenges in managing the dynamic oral health needs of children and patients with disabilities, particularly in optimizing treatment protocols that account for developmental variability and physiological constraints. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop patient-specific computational models that simulate biomechanical interactions and disease progression in pediatric dentition. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive tools to evaluate the long-term efficacy of restorative materials and preventive interventions under varying biomechanical and biochemical conditions inherent to growing patients. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling (ABM), we will simulate stress distributions in primary and mixed dentition during mastication, as well as the spatiotemporal dynamics of caries formation influenced by dietary, microbiological, and behavioral factors. High-resolution 3D imaging data from clinical cohorts will inform anatomically accurate models, while machine learning algorithms will integrate heterogeneous datasets to predict treatment outcomes across diverse patient subgroups. The computational workflows will require parallel processing capabilities to manage the scale of parametric simulations and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of material properties and intervention strategies that minimize restoration failure rates and caries recurrence in pediatric populations. By establishing a computational framework for treatment optimization, this research aims to reduce invasive procedures, improve patient compliance, and inform evidence-based guidelines for managing oral health in vulnerable populations. The HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational throughput for these multiscale, multimodal analyses, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: Critically ill patients in intensive care units (ICUs) often present with complex, rapidly evolving multi-organ dysfunction, making timely prognosis and treatment selection challenging. Existing predictive models frequently lack accuracy due to their inability to integrate high-dimensional, time-sensitive physiological data and account for dynamic inter-organ interactions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create predictive models that synthesize multimodal clinical data, including real-time vital signs, laboratory results, imaging biomarkers, and treatment response histories. Machine learning techniques, particularly deep neural networks with attention mechanisms, will be employed to model temporal patterns and cross-modal dependencies across organ systems. Bayesian methods will quantify prediction uncertainty, while agent-based modeling will simulate critical care interventions under varying physiological constraints. The computational infrastructure will process terabytes of electronic health records from five tertiary care centers, requiring parallelized data pipelines and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include validated risk stratification tools for sepsis-associated organ failure, personalized ventilation strategies in acute respiratory distress syndrome, and optimized fluid resuscitation protocols. By enabling real-time analysis of complex clinical trajectories, this research aims to reduce mortality through earlier targeted interventions while providing a scalable computational platform for critical care innovation. The proposed HPC resources are essential given the need for rapid iteration across model architectures, sensitivity analyses of therapeutic simulations, and validation against emerging ICU datasets. This work bridges computational scalability with clinical translatability, offering a paradigm shift in data-driven critical care management.
cip_definition: Research focused on the management of care for patients with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. Includes instruction in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures and post-discharge care of former critical care patients.

abstract: Aquaculture systems face critical challenges in optimizing production efficiency, disease management, and environmental sustainability due to the complex interactions between biological, chemical, and physical factors in aquatic environments. This project seeks to develop predictive models to enhance aquaculture productivity by integrating multi-scale data on species physiology, water quality dynamics, and farm operational parameters. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) simulating metabolic responses of key aquaculture species (e.g., Atlantic salmon, Pacific white shrimp) to variable feeding regimes and environmental stressors, and (2) modeling pathogen transmission dynamics within high-density culture systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to implement agent-based models that track individual organism behavior, population-level interactions, and water chemistry changes at temporal resolutions impractical for conventional computing systems. Machine learning approaches will be applied to optimize feed conversion ratios and predict disease outbreak thresholds using historical production data and real-time sensor inputs from partner aquaculture facilities. The computational workflow will leverage parallel processing to run ensemble simulations evaluating climate change scenarios, including warming temperatures and shifting oxygen gradients. Expected outcomes include decision-support tools for adaptive feeding schedules, early warning systems for pathogen detection, and hydrodynamic models to inform sustainable farm siting. By quantifying trade-offs between growth performance, disease risk, and environmental impacts, this work will directly address industry needs for precision aquaculture management while advancing computational methods for biological systems modeling. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter calibration across multiple species and production systems, significantly accelerating research timelines compared to traditional experimental approaches.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, culture, propagate, harvest, and market domesticated fish, shellfish, and marine plants, both freshwater and saltwater. Includes instruction in the basic principles of aquatic and marine biology; health and nutrition of aquatic and marine life; design and operation of fish farms, breeding facilities, culture beds, and related enterprises; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: Dental implantology faces a critical challenge in predicting long-term biomechanical stability due to the complex interplay between implant design, bone remodeling, and patient-specific anatomical factors. Current clinical methods rely on static imaging and empirical protocols, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between mechanical stress distributions, cellular bone adaptation, and soft tissue integration. This project proposes a computational framework to model the multiscale biomechanical and biological processes governing osseointegration and peri-implant tissue remodeling. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop patient-specific finite element models derived from cone-beam CT data, integrated with agent-based simulations of osteoblast-osteoclast activity and mechanobiological feedback loops. The models will incorporate time-dependent variables such as occlusal loading patterns, micromotion at the bone-implant interface, and systemic factors (e.g., bone density, metabolic rates) to predict long-term outcomes under diverse physiological conditions. A machine learning pipeline will optimize parameter space exploration, enabling probabilistic risk assessment for implant failure modes including marginal bone loss and prosthetic complications. The computational workflow will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from 300+ implant cases with 5-year follow-up. By establishing predictive relationships between biomechanical stimuli and biological responses, this research aims to generate actionable guidelines for implant selection, surgical planning, and load management protocols. The resulting framework will advance precision in implant dentistry while providing a template for computational biomechanics applications in other medical device integration challenges. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-resolution multiphysics simulations, large-scale parameter optimization, and complex data assimilation required for this real-time adaptive modeling approach.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.
