abstract: Pediatric dermatological disorders, such as atopic dermatitis, acne vulgaris, and congenital ichthyoses, present unique therapeutic challenges due to developmental differences in skin biology, immune responses, and pharmacokinetics in young populations. Current treatment paradigms often extrapolate from adult studies, resulting in suboptimal efficacy and safety profiles. This project aims to address this gap by developing computational models to identify pediatric-specific therapeutic targets and predict personalized treatment outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omic data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) from pediatric cohorts with clinical datasets, including electronic health records and longitudinal treatment responses. Machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to map disease subtypes to molecular pathways and drug mechanisms, accounting for age-stratified variations in skin physiology. Molecular dynamics simulations will further model drug interactions with pediatric-specific skin barrier proteins and immune receptors to optimize dosing and formulation. Key challenges include scaling these analyses across heterogeneous datasets (>50 TB) and achieving real-time predictions for clinical decision support. The HPC infrastructure is critical for parallel processing of large-scale simulations, hyperparameter optimization of predictive models, and federated learning across multi-institutional data repositories. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for treatment stratification, predictive models for adverse event risk, and a computational framework for repurposing existing therapies for pediatric populations. This work will directly inform ongoing clinical trials in pediatric dermatology and provide a scalable platform for precision medicine in understudied populations. By integrating computational and clinical research, the project seeks to improve therapeutic precision, reduce trial-and-error prescribing, and address disparities in pediatric dermatologic care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the treatment of specific skin disease categories, with emphasis on those diseases which predominate in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: Emergency and trauma nursing requires rapid, data-driven decision-making in high-stakes environments where patient outcomes depend on timely interventions. However, current clinical practices often rely on generalized protocols that may not account for the dynamic interplay of patient-specific variables, such as evolving physiological states, injury complexity, and resource availability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing predictive computational models to optimize trauma care pathways and real-time decision support for emergency nurses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze multi-modal clinical datasets—including electronic health records, real-time vital sign streams, imaging metadata, and trauma registry data—to identify patterns predictive of patient deterioration, complications, or optimal intervention timing. Machine learning methods, such as ensemble classifiers and time-series analysis, will be applied to model nonlinear relationships between patient covariates and outcomes. Additionally, agent-based simulations will test hypothetical resource allocation strategies under varying emergency department conditions (e.g., mass casualty events, staffing constraints). The computational scale of training models on heterogeneous datasets spanning 250,000+ trauma cases, coupled with real-time simulation of care workflows, necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to flag high-risk patients during triage, (2) evidence-based recommendations for personalized resuscitation protocols, and (3) simulation-validated strategies for dynamic staff and equipment allocation. By integrating these tools into clinical workflows, this research aims to reduce preventable complications in trauma care, improve survival rates for critically injured patients, and provide a computational framework adaptable to evolving emergency nursing practices. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-source tools to support reproducibility in healthcare operations research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver advanced, direct patient care in emergency and trauma settings. Includes instruction in advanced health assessment, pharmacology, physiology, emergency management, trauma conditions, trauma assessments and acute care.

abstract: Dairy production systems face critical challenges in optimizing animal health, feed efficiency, and operational sustainability amid rising global demand and environmental constraints. Traditional empirical approaches to dairy management often lack the resolution to model complex, dynamic interactions between genetic traits, nutritional protocols, microbial activity in rumen and processing environments, and facility design parameters. This project proposes the development of a multi-scale computational framework to simulate dairy herd productivity and operational efficiency under variable management scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the integration of agent-based herd models with mechanistic representations of nutrient metabolism, microbial community dynamics, and facility-specific environmental controls. Machine learning workflows will parameterize these models using farm-scale sensor data (e.g., automated milking systems, RFID-based health monitors) and genomic datasets from dairy cattle microbiomes. Computational experiments will evaluate feed formulation strategies, heat stress mitigation protocols, and disease transmission risks under climate variability scenarios. The framework will also simulate energy and waste management outcomes for different housing and processing facility designs. By coupling biological, environmental, and operational datasets at unprecedented scales, this work aims to identify management practices that simultaneously enhance milk yield, animal welfare, and resource efficiency. The resulting decision-support tools will be validated through partnerships with three working dairy farms, providing actionable insights for producers. This project addresses a critical gap in precision dairy science by enabling systems-level optimization—a task computationally infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will directly inform extension programs and industry guidelines, strengthening the resilience of dairy production systems while maintaining compliance with evolving safety and operational regulations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the selection and care of dairy animals and associated dairy farm and processing facilities and operations. Includes instruction in basic animal and dairy science; dairy animal nutrition and health; design and operation of dairy housing, feeding, and processing facilities and equipment; and related issues of safety, sanitation, shipping and handling, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This research project addresses the critical need to analyze the evolving representation of gender and cultural identity in Korean visual media through computational methods. While existing scholarship has qualitatively examined these themes in select case studies, the scale and complexity of contemporary media production—spanning decades of film, television,k-dramas, and webtoons—require quantitative approaches to identify systemic patterns and underrepresented narratives. The study will employ computer vision techniques to process over 50,000 hours of visual media, utilizing pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for scene composition analysis, character positioning, and symbolic element detection. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract and contextualize dialogue from subtitles and scripts, with transformer models fine-tuned for Korean linguistic nuances to assess gendered language patterns. High-performance computing resources are essential for training multimodal architectures that synchronize visual and textual feature extraction, particularly given the need for parallel processing of high-resolution video frames and large language model inference. The computational workflow will integrate temporal analysis to map historical shifts in representation against sociocultural milestones, enabling three-dimensional visualization of cultural narrative trajectories. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of an open-access annotated media corpus, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural content at scale, and evidence-based insights into how marginalized identities are constructed across mainstream and alternative media platforms. This methodology advances Korean studies by enabling systematic analysis of cultural production trends while maintaining sensitivity to context-specific meanings—a critical balance often challenging to achieve in computational humanities approaches. The project’s technical innovations will also contribute to developing culturally aware AI tools for media analysis beyond this disciplinary context.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Korea, including related island groups and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing clinical workflows and patient outcomes through advanced computational modeling of multi-modal health data. Despite the growing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic datasets, healthcare systems struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data sources for real-time decision support. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to improve resource allocation in clinical settings, reduce diagnostic delays, and personalize care pathways for patients with complex chronic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, machine learning techniques—including graph neural networks and transformer architectures—will be applied to de-identified EHR data from [Institution/Partner Network] to identify patterns in care delivery bottlenecks and comorbidities. Second, discrete-event simulation models will be developed to test interventions for clinic scheduling, staff deployment, and equipment utilization under varying patient volumes. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including time-series vital sign data, radiology reports, and administrative operation logs. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for simulating clinic operations under different resource constraints, predictive models for early identification of high-risk patients, and evidence-based recommendations for balancing clinical efficiency with care quality. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on medical management and clinical specialization by creating scalable tools to enhance both administrative decision-making and patient-facing care coordination. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of complex models that cannot run efficiently on local clinical systems, particularly for Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of operational scenarios. Results will be disseminated through healthcare informatics conferences and adapted into training modules for clinical assistant education programs.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The safe and effective administration of anesthesia requires precise management of drug interactions, patient-specific physiological variability, and real-time clinical decision-making. However, existing pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models often fail to account for the complex interplay of genetic, demographic, and comorbidity-related factors that influence anesthesia outcomes, leading to suboptimal dosing protocols and heightened risks of adverse events. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to predict individualized anesthetic responses and optimize perioperative care strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale simulations of drug metabolism, machine learning-driven analysis of electronic health records (EHRs), and agent-based modeling of physiological systems. The computational pipeline will process large datasets spanning patient genomics, real-time vital sign monitoring, and historical anesthesia outcomes to identify predictors of hemodynamic instability, prolonged recovery, or drug toxicity. Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic dosing outcomes under diverse clinical scenarios, while neural networks will refine predictive models using retrospective EHR data from over 50,000 anesthesia cases. The proposed work will enable the creation of a decision-support tool for nurse anesthetists, offering real-time dosing adjustments based on patient-specific risk profiles. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for propofol, rocuronium, and opioid responses in high-risk populations, as well as open-source computational workflows for simulating anesthesia-related physiological interactions. By elucidating the mechanistic drivers of interpatient variability, this research aims to reduce postoperative complications, enhance recovery precision, and establish a paradigm for data-driven anesthesia practice. The scale of genomic, proteomic, and hemodynamic data analysis necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically actionable processing speeds, enabling iterative model training and large-scale parameter sweeps that are infeasible with standard computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate dysregulated molecular signaling pathways in cancer progression, with a focus on ion channel and transporter dynamics within tumor microenvironments. Despite emerging evidence linking aberrant ion channel activity to metastatic behavior and therapy resistance, the systems-level integration of these processes with endocrine and homeostatic control mechanisms remains poorly understood. The research problem centers on identifying how spatial and temporal variations in ion flux, coupled with hormonal signaling, drive phenotypic plasticity in solid tumors. Computational models will integrate experimental data from electrophysiological recordings, proteomic profiles of signaling complexes, and live-cell imaging of calcium dynamics to simulate subcellular communication networks. Agent-based modeling will map the stochastic interactions of ion channels (e.g., TRP families, voltage-gated channels) with G-protein-coupled receptors and hypoxia-responsive transporters, while finite element analysis will resolve electrochemical gradients across tumor niches. These multi-scale simulations will require parallelized processing of high-dimensional datasets (>50 TB) and iterative parameter optimization using machine learning frameworks. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maps of signaling nodes that govern therapeutic escape in pancreatic and breast cancer models, validated through collaborative wet-lab experiments. The computational workflows will also generate open-access tools for simulating crosstalk between endocrine hormones and ion transport machinery, addressing a critical gap in molecular physiology research. By elucidating how dysregulated electrochemical gradients rewire homeostatic checkpoints, this work aims to identify targetable vulnerabilities for precision oncology. The requested HPC allocation will enable the execution of computationally intensive simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, directly supporting the development of mechanistic frameworks for cancer-specific physiological dysregulation.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of dynamic interactive processes and biochemical communications at the subcellular level. Includes instruction in ion channels and transporters, molecular signaling pathways, endocrine control and regulation, genetic information transfer, homeostasis and molecular control systems, electrophysiology and sensory mechanisms, protein synthesis, and applicable research methods and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on cultural and intellectual networks in Medieval and Renaissance Europe through the integration of large-scale textual, artistic, and archival datasets. The core research problem lies in the fragmented and siloed nature of surviving materials—such as manuscripts, correspondence, liturgical records, and artistic works—which has limited scholars’ ability to trace transnational exchanges of ideas, materials, and aesthetic practices at scale. Current manual methods struggle to analyze correlations across multilingual texts, visual motifs, and socio-geographic metadata, particularly when handling terabytes of digitized materials from repositories across Europe. To address this, the project will deploy computational workflows including natural language processing (NLP) for Latin and vernacular texts, graph-based network analysis to map connections between individuals and institutions, and computer vision techniques to detect stylistic patterns in illuminated manuscripts and early printed books. HPC resources are essential to train transformer models on low-resource historical languages, process high-resolution multispectral imagery of degraded documents, and run iterative simulations testing hypotheses about the diffusion of artistic techniques. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated datasets, dynamic visualizations of patronage networks across 14th–16th-century Europe, and machine learning tools tailored to paleographic analysis. By enabling quantitative and qualitative synthesis across disciplines, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of how cultural production intersected with political, religious, and economic systems during transformative historical periods. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for 3D artifact scans, and parallelized text analysis across a corpus exceeding 50,000 documents.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the Medieval and/or Renaissance periods in European and circum-Mediterranean history from the perspective of various disciplines in the humanities and social sciences, including history and archeology, as well as studies of period art and music.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural correlates of auditory processing disorders (APDs) in pediatric populations using multimodal neuroimaging and machine learning approaches, with the goal of developing predictive models to personalize therapeutic interventions. While APDs affect 3–7% of children and are linked to speech-language delays, current diagnostic frameworks rely on behavioral assessments with limited sensitivity to neurobiological heterogeneity. Our research will integrate high-density electroencephalography (EEG), functional MRI (fMRI), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data to map aberrant connectivity patterns in auditory-linguistic networks. The computational challenges involve processing terabytes of neuroimaging data, synchronizing temporal-spatial features across modalities, and training deep learning architectures to classify APD subtypes. We propose using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a three-stage pipeline: (1) preprocessing raw data with GPU-accelerated signal filtering and artifact removal, (2) employing graph theoretical models to characterize network topology changes, and (3) developing hybrid convolutional-recurrent neural networks to predict intervention outcomes based on baseline neural signatures. This approach requires parallelized processing of large-scale datasets and iterative model optimization impractical on local clusters. Anticipated outcomes include identifying neurophysiological biomarkers for early APD detection, stratifying patients by predicted responsiveness to auditory training versus neuromodulation therapies, and generating simulated neural network models to test intervention mechanisms. The project bridges gaps between computational neuroscience and clinical audiology by establishing a framework for data-driven rehabilitation strategies, with potential applications to acquired communication disorders in aging populations. Successful implementation will advance precision health paradigms in speech-language pathology while demonstrating scalable HPC workflows for neuroimaging analytics in resource-constrained clinical research settings.
cip_title: Audiology/ Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathology/ Pathologist
cip_definition: An integrated program that prepares individuals to work as both audiologists and speech-language pathologists. Includes instruction in a variety of communication disorder studies, audiology, speech pathology, language acquisition, and the design and implementation of comprehensive therapeutic and rehabilitative solutions to communications problems.

abstract: Dental diseases remain a significant global public health burden, disproportionately affecting underserved populations due to systemic inequities in access to care. Current approaches to optimizing preventive service delivery—such as community fluoride programs or school-based dental screenings—often rely on static epidemiological data, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between population demographics, behavioral factors, and resource constraints. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model the cost-effectiveness and equity impacts of alternative public health strategies for dental disease prevention. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale, spatially explicit simulations integrating multi-source data, including census tract demographics, disease prevalence maps, and healthcare utilization patterns. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to simulate individual and community-level decision-making under varying policy scenarios, such as mobile clinic deployments or targeted oral health education campaigns. Machine learning algorithms will further refine parameter estimation for disease progression and intervention efficacy using longitudinal electronic health record data from public health clinics. Computational demands arise from the need to simultaneously model millions of agents across diverse geographies, incorporate stochastic variability in outcomes, and perform sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimized resource allocation strategies that maximize population-level caries reduction while minimizing disparities in access. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will enable local health departments to tailor preventive programs to community-specific needs. By quantifying trade-offs between cost, equity, and clinical impact, this work aims to provide policymakers with evidence-based tools to transform dental public health planning from reactive to proactive, data-driven decision-making.
cip_definition: Research focused on the formulation and delivery of public preventive and curative dental health services.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance precision medicine in companion animal oncology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model tumor heterogeneity and predict treatment outcomes. Despite progress in veterinary oncology, therapeutic responses in dogs and cats remain highly variable due to complex genomic, proteomic, and microenvironmental factors in tumors. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, often leading to suboptimal efficacy or adverse effects. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating single-cell RNA sequencing data from canine and feline tumors with clinical metadata to identify predictive biomarkers and simulate therapeutic responses. The project will employ machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks, to model spatial tumor-immune interactions, and agent-based simulations to replicate dynamic drug penetration in heterogeneous tumor architectures. These analyses require processing multi-terabyte datasets and iteratively training models with hyperparameter optimization, necessitating HPC resources for parallelized computation and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive models for veterinary oncologists to tailor chemotherapy and immunotherapy regimens, reducing trial-and-error prescribing. The work will also establish cross-species tumor atlases, contributing to comparative oncology research by highlighting conserved therapeutic targets. By bridging computational biology and clinical veterinary medicine, this project aims to improve survival rates and quality of life for companion animals while generating scalable tools for translational research in small animal surgical and medical specialties.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Small/ Companion Animal Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of companion and household animals. Includes instruction in avian medicine, pet care, companion animal medicine, pathophysiology, small animal diseases, small animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize radiation therapy treatment planning while minimizing secondary cancer risks associated with stray radiation exposure—a critical public health concern in medical physics. Current protocols prioritize tumor targeting but lack robust models to predict long-term carcinogenic effects on healthy tissues, particularly for pediatric and genetically susceptible populations. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating Monte Carlo radiation transport modeling with patient-specific genomic and radiobiological data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations of radiation dose deposition at sub-millimeter resolution across heterogeneous anatomical phantoms, coupled with probabilistic risk models informed by population-level epidemiological datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these outputs to identify dose-distribution patterns that balance therapeutic efficacy with lifetime risk thresholds. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for rapid Monte Carlo iterations and CPU clusters for large-scale parameter sweeps across radiation types, energy levels, and patient demographics. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide clinical decision-making, reduce secondary malignancy rates, and inform public health guidelines on radiation safety. By openly sharing optimized codebases and risk-assessment modules, this work will empower broader research into radiation-related health disparities. The project’s scale—requiring ~200,000 core-hours for sensitivity analyses of 10+ cancer types and 3D dose reconstructions from historical treatment data—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. Results will advance precision radiology while addressing a systemic challenge in public health: mitigating unintended consequences of life-saving medical technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics, nuclear science, and engineering physics to diagnostic, treatment, and therapeutic processes and public health protection. Includes instruction in radiation biophysics, biophysics, health effects of natural and artificially induced radiation, hazard evaluation, environmental radioactivity, nuclear physics, engineering physics, radiobiology, medical radiology, calibration and dosage theory, computer applications and medical informatics, and specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address gaps in large-scale literary analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to examine patterns of stylistic and thematic evolution across a curated corpus of 50,000 English-language literary texts from the 18th century to the present. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically track nuanced linguistic features—such as syntactic complexity, metaphor density, or semantic shifts in key lexemes—across such vast temporal and generic ranges. By developing custom natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for literary analysis, this research will quantify how specific stylistic devices correlate with historical events, cultural movements, and genre innovations. The computational workload involves training transformer-based models to recognize literary features in prose, poetry, and drama, followed by graph-based network analyses to map influence and innovation trajectories. HPC resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte text datasets, running parallelized feature-extraction tasks, and iteratively refining models through hyperparameter tuning. Expected outcomes include: (1) identifying previously unrecognized clusters of stylistic innovation in underrepresented 19th-century serialized fiction; (2) publishing an open-access dataset tagging literary devices across the corpus; and (3) developing modular, reusable codebases for GPU-accelerated literary analysis. This work will provide quantitative foundations for new theoretical frameworks in periodization studies while demonstrating how computational methods can complement qualitative scholarship. By making tools and datasets publicly available, the project aims to lower barriers to computational literary analysis, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration within digital humanities. Resource requests focus on GPU nodes for model training and high-memory CPU nodes for large-scale text graph construction.
cip_title: English Language and Literature/ Letters, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in English language and literature, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation in distributed edge computing networks, which are critical for latency-sensitive applications such as industrial automation and real-time sensor systems. Current approaches often struggle to balance computational load, energy efficiency, and latency in dynamic environments with heterogeneous devices. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive scheduling algorithms and machine learning-driven predictive modeling. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale edge networks with varying topologies, workloads, and hardware constraints. Agent-based models will emulate device interactions, while Monte Carlo simulations will assess robustness under stochastic demand patterns. Parallelized optimization routines will iteratively refine task allocation strategies, minimizing latency and energy consumption. Additionally, neural networks trained on synthetic datasets will predict resource requirements for emergent workloads. The computational intensity of simulating thousands of nodes, coupled with the need for rapid convergence in multi-objective optimization, necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with GPU acceleration and distributed memory capabilities. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for dynamic resource management in edge environments, validated against industrial IoT and smart manufacturing use cases. This work will contribute novel methodologies for real-time decision-making in distributed systems, directly advancing computer engineering technologies for Industry 4.0 applications. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits to enable community-driven improvements in edge computing efficiency and reliability.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop advanced computational models to enhance threat detection and resilience planning for critical infrastructure systems vulnerable to cyber-physical attacks. As infrastructure networks grow in complexity and interconnectivity, traditional risk assessment methods struggle to account for cascading failures, adversarial machine learning exploits, and dynamic threat landscapes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model infrastructure interdependencies, attacker behaviors, and mitigation strategies. The computational approach integrates graph neural networks to represent infrastructure topology, reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive adversaries, and fluid dynamics models to predict physical cascades (e.g., power grid failures impacting water distribution). HPC resources are essential for executing millions of parallelized attack-defend scenarios across heterogeneous infrastructure datasets, enabling probabilistic risk quantification at unprecedented resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source algorithmic toolkit for identifying system-specific vulnerabilities, optimizing defense resource allocation, and stress-testing incident response protocols under realistic constraints. By enabling granular analysis of emerging threats like AI-driven cyberattacks or climate-aggravated physical disruptions, this work aims to advance predictive security analytics for transportation, energy, and communication systems. The resulting models will provide actionable insights for infrastructure operators and policymakers, bridging the gap between theoretical security science and operational resilience requirements. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale graph computations, with an estimated need for 200,000 node-hours to validate the framework against real-world infrastructure case studies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in security science and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing burden of vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases in resource-limited regions underscores the urgent need for advanced computational tools to model complex disease dynamics and optimize intervention strategies. Current approaches often fail to capture the multiscale interactions between pathogens, vectors, human populations, and environmental drivers, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative, spatially explicit models of disease transmission for pathogens such as malaria, dengue, and chikungunya. The research will combine agent-based modeling, machine learning, and genomic epidemiology to simulate transmission dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes, incorporating real-world data on vector ecology, climate variability, host immunity, and human mobility. Key computational challenges include parameterizing large-scale models with genomic datasets from pathogen surveillance, optimizing spatiotemporal resolution for regional forecasts, and quantifying uncertainty in intervention outcomes. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to explore scenarios such as vaccine deployment strategies, insecticide resistance evolution, and climate-driven shifts in vector habitats. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to identify high-risk transmission hotspots, evaluate the durability of vaccine-induced immunity, and prioritize targeted vector control measures. By integrating high-resolution genomic and environmental data, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of pathogen adaptation and spillover risks. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to support public health decision-making in endemic regions. This project directly addresses critical gaps in tropical disease management, with potential to reduce morbidity and mortality through data-driven, precision public health interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative architectural design frameworks that integrate cultural, ecological, and historical data into real-time spatial simulations. Traditional architectural workflows often rely on static, siloed datasets, limiting the ability to dynamically model complex interactions between built environments, localized cultural narratives, and shifting ecological conditions. The research addresses this gap by creating a computational pipeline that synthesizes heterogeneous data—including oral histories, geospatial climate projections, and material heritage records—into adaptive 3D design models. Using a combination of agent-based modeling, graph neural networks (GNNs), and parametric design tools, the project will simulate how architectural forms evolve in response to socio-cultural priorities and environmental stressors. Key computational challenges include optimizing mesh generation for irregular heritage site geometries, parallelizing climate impact simulations across multi-decadal timelines, and training GNNs on sparse, non-uniform cultural datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify design solutions that balance structural resilience with community-defined cultural values. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for culturally responsive generative design, validated through case studies in post-disaster reconstruction contexts. By bridging architectural practice with computational ethnography and ecological forecasting, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for ethically grounded, data-driven design—one that prioritizes the integration of intangible heritage and participatory decision-making into computationally intensive workflows. The resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed database management for cross-disciplinary datasets, and the development of hybrid AI-human interfaces for collaborative design iteration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of architecture and to conduct research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in architectural design, history, and theory; building structures and environmental systems; project and site planning; construction; professional responsibilities and standards; and related cultural, social, economic, and environmental issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of psychodynamic processes in therapeutic interactions through computational modeling and large-scale natural language processing (NLP). Traditional psychoanalytic research has relied on qualitative case studies and manual coding of clinical sessions, limiting scalability and reproducibility. The proposed research addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to analyze longitudinal therapy transcripts, quantify patterns in transference-countertransference dynamics, and model the emergence of unconscious conflict resolution during treatment. Using anonymized datasets comprising over 10,000 hours of psychotherapy session transcripts across diverse clinical populations, we will implement neural language models to identify latent linguistic markers of defense mechanisms, emotional valence shifts, and therapeutic alliance fluctuations. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate dyadic patient-therapist interactions under varying psychodynamic principles to test hypotheses about optimal intervention timing. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-dimensional text data, training transformer-based architectures on therapeutic dialogue, and running parallelized simulations of complex interpersonal dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated NLP pipeline for automated detection of clinically relevant psychodynamic phenomena, (2) computational evidence linking specific interaction patterns to treatment outcomes, and (3) open-source tools enabling real-time analysis of therapeutic process variables. By bridging psychoanalytic theory with computational psychiatry methods, this work aims to establish quantitative foundations for psychodynamic research while providing clinicians with data-driven insights into intervention efficacy. The project represents a novel convergence of depth psychology and artificial intelligence, addressing core challenges in mental health care personalization and mechanistic understanding of psychotherapy.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung. Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) present complex challenges requiring personalized intervention strategies, yet current approaches often lack the computational power to model multifaceted interactions between biological, psychological, and social factors. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize treatment personalization by analyzing high-dimensional datasets, including electronic health records, neuroimaging data, and real-time behavioral metrics from wearable devices. The research problem centers on identifying dynamic predictors of treatment adherence and relapse risk that traditional statistical methods cannot capture due to computational limitations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ agent-based modeling to simulate patient trajectories under varying intervention scenarios, combined with machine learning (ML) techniques to integrate genetic, epigenetic, and environmental data. Computational workflows will include parallelized training of ensemble ML models to handle imbalanced datasets common in SUD research, as well as large-scale network analysis to map social determinants of health influencing recovery outcomes. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning applications in natural language processing of clinical notes and time-series analysis of physiological monitoring data. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for predicting individual-level responses to evidence-based therapies, (2) open-source tools for real-time risk stratification using federated learning architectures, and (3) novel insights into dose-response relationships between counseling modalities and neurocognitive recovery patterns. By enabling rapid iteration of complex models across diverse virtual cohorts, this HPC-supported approach aims to advance precision medicine in addiction counseling, potentially reducing trial-and-error treatment selection and improving long-term recovery rates. All models and pipelines will be shared with the research community to accelerate computational innovation in behavioral health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to help prevent substance abuse, counsel individuals and families with drug and alcohol problems, and perform intervention and therapeutic services for persons suffering from addiction. Includes instruction in individual and group counseling skills, psychology of addiction, sociology, crisis intervention, substance abuse identification methodologies, substance abuse treatment modalities, substance abuse prevention and treatment resources, pharmacology and behavioral aspects of abused substances, treatment evaluation, patient observation and education, group dynamics, professional standards and ethics, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, leveraging manual techniques to diagnose, treat, and prevent illness by enhancing the body’s natural self-regulatory mechanisms. Despite its clinical use, the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying OMT’s therapeutic effects remain poorly characterized, limiting evidence-based optimization of treatment protocols. This project proposes a computational framework integrating multiscale modeling, machine learning, and large-scale clinical data analysis to elucidate how OMT modulates physiological systems. The primary research problem centers on resolving the gap between observed clinical outcomes and the mechanistic basis of OMT, particularly in chronic musculoskeletal pain and systemic inflammatory conditions. To address this, we will develop biophysical models simulating OMT-induced tissue strain and its propagation across anatomical scales, coupled with molecular dynamics simulations to predict mechanotransduction pathways activated by manual forces. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze electronic health records (EHRs) from osteopathic clinics to identify patterns in treatment efficacy, patient demographics, and comorbidity interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of these tasks, including finite element modeling of musculoskeletal structures, molecular-scale protein interaction networks, and high-dimensional EHR datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific OMT techniques to quantifiable changes in inflammatory biomarkers, tissue remodeling, and patient-reported pain metrics. These results will advance the precision of OMT application in clinical practice and provide a foundational computational platform for future studies in osteopathic research. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to bridge clinical observations with mechanistic insights, fostering evidence-based refinement of osteopathic principles and enhancing therapeutic strategies for complex, multifactorial health conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on Osteopathic Medicine

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing tactical decision-making in dynamic combat environments through advanced simulation and predictive analytics. Current approaches to military operations planning often rely on static models that inadequately account for real-time sensor data, adversarial adaptation, and cascading logistical constraints. The central challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous data streams—including satellite imagery, unmanned system telemetry, and intelligence reports—into adaptive decision-support tools capable of operating under latency-sensitive conditions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale, agent-based simulations that model multi-domain operations (MDO) across air, land, maritime, and cyber theaters. These simulations will incorporate machine learning techniques to predict adversary behavior patterns, evaluate resource allocation tradeoffs, and stress-test contingency plans under probabilistic threat scenarios. Key computational components include parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification, graph neural networks for modeling inter-theater dependencies, and evolutionary algorithms for optimizing supply chain resilience. The anticipated outcomes include a novel decision architecture that reduces cognitive load on human operators while maintaining ethical oversight controls, as well as quantifiable metrics for assessing mission risk in contested environments. By enabling rapid iteration of complex scenarios that mirror emerging hybrid warfare paradigms, this work aims to advance both theoretical frameworks for military operations research and practical tools for enhancing strategic agility. The requested computing resources will directly support the development of containerized simulation modules, validation against historical conflict datasets, and sensitivity analyses across diverse operational parameters. Results will inform next-generation command-and-control systems while contributing methodological innovations to the interdisciplinary study of military technology management.
cip_title: Military Technology and Applied Sciences Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on applied military science, military operations, intelligence gathering, military technology, and national security. Includes instruction in computer science, engineering, ethics, field training, leadership, military strategy, logistics, management skills, and politics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance strategies for aging aircraft airframe components, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model structural degradation in complex materials and operational environments. Current maintenance protocols rely heavily on static schedules and manual inspections, which may fail to account for dynamic stress factors, material fatigue variability, or environmental corrosion patterns. To address this, the research will employ multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning algorithms to predict failure risks in critical components such as sheet metal structures, composite panels, and hydraulic systems. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to simulate wear under diverse conditions—including vibration spectra, thermal cycles, and moisture exposure—while training neural networks on historical maintenance data and sensor-derived strain measurements. The computational pipeline will prioritize scalability to handle high-resolution 3D models of airframe segments, with validation against experimental data from controlled fatigue tests and field-reported defect cases. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify remaining useful life of components, identify high-risk zones for targeted inspections, and recommend adaptive maintenance intervals. By reducing unplanned downtime and extending service lifetimes of airframes, this work aims to enhance operational safety while lowering long-term maintenance costs for aviation operators. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for stochastic simulations and real-time data assimilation, which are infeasible on local clusters due to memory and processing constraints. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for aircraft maintenance technicians, fostering data-driven decision-making in the industry.
cip_title: Airframe Mechanics and Aircraft Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all aircraft components other than engines, propellers, avionics, and instruments. Includes instruction in layout and fabrication of sheet metal, fabric, wood, and other materials into structural members, parts, and fittings, and replacement of damaged or worn parts such as control cables and hydraulic units.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of singularity formation and geometric structure evolution in high-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under curvature-driven flows, with a focus on Ricci and mean curvature flow. A central challenge in geometric analysis lies in characterizing the behavior of such flows as singularities develop, particularly in dimensions four and higher, where analytical methods alone struggle to resolve the intricate interplay between topology, curvature, and metric evolution. The research will employ large-scale numerical simulations to model these nonlinear PDE systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to discretize geometric flows on adaptive meshes, track emerging singular structures, and analyze their stability. Key computational components include implementing parallelized finite element schemes on manifold meshes, optimizing tensor field operations for distributed memory architectures, and applying topological data analysis to classify singularity types. The simulations will test conjectures about singularity stratification in non-compact settings and quantify the role of initial metric anisotropies in flow convergence. Expected outcomes include new criteria for flow existence in constrained topologies, refined conjectures on singular set Hausdorff dimensions, and datasets mapping flow behaviors to manifold invariants. Results will directly inform ongoing work in geometric PDE regularity theory and provide numerical evidence to guide formal proofs in scenarios where current analytical tools are insufficient. By coupling geometric analysis with scalable computational methods, this work aims to uncover universal patterns in high-dimensional geometric flows, with potential implications for problems in mathematical relativity and low-dimensional topology. The project requires HPC resources due to the memory-intensive nature of high-dimensional manifold discretizations and the need for long-time integration of stiff, nonlinear systems at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties, measurements, and relationships pertaining to points, lines, angles, surfaces, and solids. Includes instruction in global analysis, differential geometry, Euclidian and Non-Euclidian geometry, set theory, manifolds, integral geometry, and applications to algebra and other topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for individualized neuromotor rehabilitation strategies, focusing on rare neuromuscular disorders that lack standardized therapeutic protocols. Current clinical approaches to these conditions—such as inherited neuropathies or mitochondrial myopathies—are often generalized, leading to suboptimal patient outcomes due to the high variability in disease progression and biomechanical adaptation. The research aims to address this gap by integrating multiscale computational modeling with patient-specific neuroimaging, electromyography (EMG), and motion-capture data to simulate neuromuscular dynamics and predict personalized intervention efficacy. A hybrid computational framework will be developed, combining finite element modeling of musculoskeletal structures, dynamical systems theory to map neural control mechanisms, and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize therapeutic parameters. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high dimensionality of datasets, real-time feedback loops in simulated interventions, and stochastic optimization processes requiring parallelized computation. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for generating patient-specific rehabilitation protocols, validated through retrospective clinical data and pilot prospective case studies. This work bridges computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and clinical neurology, offering a paradigm shift toward precision rehabilitation for underserved patient populations. The computational tools and datasets generated will be made available to the research community, fostering collaboration in niche neuromuscular disease research and accelerating translational applications in clinical settings.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The emergence and spread of infectious diseases in livestock populations pose significant threats to animal welfare, agricultural productivity, and public health. Current approaches to modeling disease dynamics often lack the resolution to account for complex interactions between host behavior, pathogen evolution, and environmental variables, limiting their utility in real-world intervention planning. This project seeks to develop high-resolution, multi-scale computational models to predict disease transmission risks in heterogeneous livestock populations, with a focus on pathogens exhibiting zoonotic potential. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate agent-based modeling, machine learning, and genomic epidemiology datasets. Agent-based simulations will capture individual animal movement, contact networks, and management practices across diverse farming systems, while deep learning architectures will analyze pathogen genomic data to identify emergent virulence or antimicrobial resistance traits. Spatial-temporal models will incorporate regional climate and land-use data to forecast outbreak hotspots. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of large-scale genomic datasets (e.g., bacterial whole-genome sequencing from surveillance programs) and real-time parameter optimization for dynamic models simulating populations exceeding 1 million individual agents. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive frameworks to prioritize surveillance in high-risk animal populations, (2) identification of genetic markers associated with cross-species transmission events, and (3) quantitative evaluation of mitigation strategies such as targeted vaccination or biosecurity protocols. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of host-pathogen-environment interactions at unprecedented scales, this work will advance precision veterinary medicine and inform One Health policies. The developed models will be shared via open-source platforms to support adaptive disease management in agricultural communities, directly contributing to enhanced animal health outcomes and reduced economic losses from epizootic events.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary or animal health technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize clinical workflows in Licensed Practical/Vocational Nurse (LPN/LVN) training environments, with the goal of improving patient safety and educational outcomes. A critical challenge in LPN/LVN education is the limited availability of data-driven tools to simulate complex clinical scenarios, assess trainee decision-making under pressure, and predict how workflow inefficiencies contribute to errors. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create large-scale, agent-based simulations of clinical settings, incorporating variables such as patient acuity, staffing ratios, and trainee skill progression. These simulations will integrate real-world electronic health record (EHR) data from partner healthcare institutions, anonymized and processed using natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract patterns in nursing documentation, medication administration, and interprofessional communication. Machine learning models will then identify high-risk scenarios where workflow bottlenecks or knowledge gaps correlate with near-miss events or suboptimal care. A parallel computational effort will focus on virtual reality (VR)-enhanced training modules, rendered via GPU-accelerated clusters, to simulate high-stakes clinical interactions while capturing real-time trainee biometric data (e.g., eye tracking, stress indicators) for adaptive learning analytics. The computational demands of processing multimodal datasets (EHRs, biometric streams, 3D environments) and running millions of parallelized training scenarios necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models for individualized competency assessments, optimized clinical rotation schedules based on trainee performance patterns, and evidence-based recommendations for workflow redesign in ambulatory care settings. By bridging computational science and nursing education, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for reducing preventable errors and enhancing the preparedness of LPN/LVN trainees in evolving healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in providing general nursing care under the direction of a registered nurse, physician or dentist. Includes instruction in taking patient vital signs, applying sterile dressings, patient health education, and assistance with examinations and treatment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the impacts of rapid environmental change on multispecies community dynamics and ecosystem resilience. A critical challenge in environmental biology lies in disentangling how shifting abiotic conditions—such as temperature extremes, altered precipitation regimes, and habitat fragmentation—interact with biotic processes to drive population declines, community restructuring, and ecosystem function loss. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, context-dependent interactions among species and environmental drivers at ecologically relevant scales. To address this, we propose developing spatially explicit, hierarchical Bayesian models that integrate long-term ecological monitoring data, remote sensing inputs, and experimental climate manipulation datasets. These models will simulate population viability, interspecific interactions, and nutrient cycling processes under projected environmental scenarios, explicitly accounting for uncertainty in parameter estimates and stochastic disturbances. The computational workflow will involve parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for model calibration, agent-based simulations of species movement and resource competition, and machine learning techniques to identify tipping points in ecosystem stability. By coupling fine-scale process-based models with regional-scale environmental covariates, this approach will quantify how biodiversity buffers against—or amplifies—ecosystem responses to concurrent stressors. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for prioritizing conservation efforts in vulnerable communities, identifying keystone species that disproportionately affect resilience, and forecasting feedbacks between ecological change and environmental processes. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, processing terabytes of multispectral imagery and sensor network data, and executing ensemble simulations across diverse climate and land-use scenarios. Results will directly inform adaptive management strategies for ecosystems facing unprecedented rates of environmental change while advancing methodological integration in ecological forecasting.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the origins, functions, relationships, interactions, and natural history of living populations, communities, species, and ecosystems in relation to dynamic environmental processes. Includes instruction in biodiversity, molecular genetic and genomic evolution, mesoscale ecology, computational biology and modeling, conservation biology, local and global environmental change, and restoration ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the mechanistic drivers of urban wildlife adaptation through high-resolution, individual-based simulations of behavioral plasticity in avian species occupying heterogeneous urban landscapes. Urbanization imposes novel selective pressures—such as artificial light, noise pollution, and fragmented green corridors—that challenge traditional wildlife behavioral paradigms. However, existing models lack the spatial granularity and temporal resolution to disentangle adaptive behaviors from stochastic responses in dynamic urban matrices. We propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate fine-scale decision-making processes in urban birds (e.g., Corvus brachyrhynchos, Passer domesticus) across diurnal cycles and seasonal transitions. The ABM will integrate empirical data from GPS tracking, LiDAR-derived 3D habitat structure, and anthropogenic disturbance gradients to parameterize agents’ sensory perception thresholds, energy budgets, and risk-assessment heuristics. Computational workflows will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to test hypotheses on how microhabitat selection trade-offs (e.g., foraging efficiency vs. anthropogenic stress) scale to population-level fitness outcomes under varying urban planning scenarios. Machine learning pipelines will analyze emergent patterns in terabyte-scale simulation outputs to identify critical tipping points in habitat connectivity and resource availability. This work will advance predictive frameworks for urban wildlife management by quantifying nonlinear interactions between behavioral adaptation and landscape configuration, directly informing conservation policies aimed at balancing biodiversity persistence with urban development. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatiotemporal resolution and stochastic ensemble sizes, enabling unprecedented mechanistic insight into urban ecological resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological principles to the study of vertebrate wildlife, wildlife habitats, and related ecosystems in remote and urban areas. Includes instruction in animal ecology; adaptational biology; urban ecosystems; natural and artificial habitat management; limnology; wildlife pathology; and vertebrate zoological specializations such as mammalogy, herpetology, ichthyology, ornithology, and others.

abstract: Autoimmune rheumatic diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus, exhibit substantial heterogeneity in treatment response, driven by poorly understood molecular mechanisms. Current clinical tools lack the resolution to predict patient-specific outcomes, leading to prolonged trial-and-error therapeutic approaches. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omics data—including single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomics, and longitudinal clinical data—to identify predictive biomarkers and mechanistic drivers of treatment resistance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the scale and complexity of these datasets, which encompass terabytes of genomic information and high-dimensional clinical variables from a multicenter cohort of 1,200 patients. Computational workflows will include unsupervised clustering to stratify patient subtypes, supervised machine learning models to predict drug response, and network-based analyses to elucidate dysregulated immune pathways. Custom pipelines will be developed to harmonize disparate data types, mitigate batch effects, and prioritize candidate biomarkers using permutation-based significance testing. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of computationally intensive tasks, such as genome-wide association studies and Bayesian network inference, which are infeasible on local servers due to memory and runtime constraints. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early prediction of non-response to biologic therapies, a validated patient stratification model deployable in clinical settings, and mechanistic insights into immune pathway crosstalk underlying treatment resistance. This work will directly inform personalized therapeutic strategies, reduce healthcare costs associated with ineffective treatments, and advance computational methodologies for translational rheumatology. By leveraging scalable HPC resources, this project bridges critical gaps between large-scale data analytics and clinical decision-making, fostering precision medicine in autoimmune disease management.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rheumatology

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the role of spatially organized mechanical forces in regulating cellular dynamics and tissue-scale architecture, with a focus on epithelial systems. A critical gap persists in understanding how subcellular force generation, mediated by actomyosin networks and adhesion complexes, integrates across scales to drive collective cell behaviors such as polarity establishment, junction remodeling, and tissue folding. Traditional experimental approaches lack the spatiotemporal resolution to track force propagation in real time, while existing computational models often oversimplify cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions. To address this, we will develop a multiscale, agent-based computational framework that couples discrete cellular mechanics with continuum descriptions of extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of epithelial monolayers (>10,000 cells) incorporating realistic cell geometries, dynamic actomyosin contractility, and ECM feedback. The model will integrate empirical data from live-cell microscopy and traction force microscopy, parameterizing force transduction at cadherin-based junctions and integrin-mediated adhesions. Key deliverables include quantification of energy dissipation patterns during tissue morphogenesis, prediction of stress transmission pathways underlying mechanical homeostasis, and identification of failure modes in adhesion cooperativity that precede tissue disorganization. This work will directly inform experimental studies exploring how mechanical perturbations contribute to histopathological changes in epithelial barriers. The requested computational resources are essential given the iterative nature of parameter space exploration (e.g., stiffness gradients, adhesion kinetics) and the need for parallelized simulation batches to statistically resolve emergent behaviors. Outcomes will advance fundamental knowledge of mechanotransduction in cellular systems while providing a predictive toolkit for analyzing tissue-scale responses to mechanical stimuli, with potential applications in developmental biology and epithelial repair mechanisms.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure, function, and regulation of cells as individual units and as components of larger systems. Includes instruction in cell chemistry, cellular dynamics, cellular replication and reproduction, cell anatomy, membrane function, organelles, cell adhesion and extracellular matrices, cell dynamics and motility, meiosis and mytosis, signal transduction, regulation, recognition and defense mechanisms, the cell cycle, cell metabolism and respiration, gene expression, and studies of cell types and characteristics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and behavioral impacts of complex tax code provisions on compliance strategies and economic decision-making. Contemporary tax systems, particularly in the U.S., are characterized by multilayered statutes, administrative rulings, and judicial interpretations that create dynamic interactions between legal constraints, taxpayer behavior, and macroeconomic outcomes. Traditional legal analysis and econometric modeling often fail to capture the nonlinear feedback loops and scalability challenges inherent in these systems. To address this gap, the research employs agent-based modeling (ABM) frameworks to simulate taxpayer decision-making under varying regulatory scenarios, integrating granular tax code data, historical audit outcomes, and socioeconomic variables. Computational legal parsing tools will preprocess tax statutes and case law into machine-readable rule sets, while HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelized simulations across diverse demographic and economic agent profiles. The project further applies graph-based algorithms to map interdependencies between tax provisions, identifying systemic vulnerabilities to strategic avoidance or unintended fiscal consequences. Expected outcomes include predictive models quantifying how specific code amendments might influence compliance rates, revenue projections, and distributional equity at scale. These insights aim to provide policymakers with evidence-based tools to evaluate trade-offs between tax complexity, enforcement efficiency, and economic growth. By bridging computational modeling and legal analysis, this work establishes a methodological foundation for simulating emergent behaviors in regulatory ecosystems, advancing tax law scholarship beyond doctrinal or case-study approaches into data-driven, systems-oriented inquiry.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of tax law and taxation procedures in U.S. or Canadian jurisdictions affecting individuals and corporations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing the performance and reliability of complex electromechanical systems through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Electromechanical systems, such as automated servomechanical actuators and hybrid industrial automation platforms, require precise integration of mechanical dynamics, electronic control systems, and embedded sensor feedback. Traditional design and testing methods rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is resource-intensive and limits exploration of design trade-offs. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation framework that models coupled electromechanical behaviors at scale. The computational approach will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and thermal dynamics, circuit simulation for power electronics and control systems, and data-driven optimization algorithms to identify parameter sets that balance efficiency, durability, and responsiveness. HPC-enabled parallelism will allow systematic exploration of design variables—including material properties, actuator geometries, and PID control parameters—under diverse operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for electromechanical system performance, reduced prototyping cycles for industrial partners, and optimized control strategies for energy-efficient operation. This work will directly support curriculum development in electromechanical system diagnostics and smart manufacturing, while providing students with hands-on experience in computational engineering tools. The resource allocation will enable simulations at unprecedented resolution, capturing transient electromechanical interactions critical for next-generation automation systems in sectors such as precision robotics and adaptive manufacturing. Results will be disseminated through industry workshops and open-access model libraries to bridge gaps between academic research and applied electromechanical technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Integrative medicine faces a critical challenge in synthesizing complex, multi-modal data—including patient histories, genomic profiles, lifestyle factors, and clinical outcomes—to inform personalized, evidence-based care. Current analytical methods often struggle to integrate these heterogeneous datasets at scale, limiting the ability to identify patterns that could optimize therapeutic strategies and improve patient outcomes. This project proposes to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that bridge clinical, molecular, and psychosocial data. The research will focus on three aims: (1) constructing predictive models to identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit from specific integrative therapies, (2) analyzing longitudinal interactions between treatment modalities and patient-reported outcomes, and (3) simulating the systemic effects of multi-component interventions on health trajectories. Computational methods will include machine learning (e.g., ensemble classifiers, graph neural networks) to handle high-dimensional data, network analysis to map relationships between therapeutic variables, and agent-based modeling to simulate patient-practitioner decision-making dynamics. Large-scale datasets from electronic health records, genomic repositories, and prospective clinical cohorts will be harmonized using federated learning frameworks to preserve privacy while enabling cross-institutional analysis. The HPC environment is essential for managing computationally intensive tasks such as genome-wide association studies, real-time optimization of treatment combinations, and parallelized validation of model robustness. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for treatment responsiveness, actionable frameworks for tailoring integrative care plans, and scalable tools to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of holistic interventions.
