By elucidating how diverse therapeutic approaches interact at individual and population levels, this work will advance the evidence base for integrative medicine, directly supporting clinical decision-making and policy development. The project underscores the transformative role of HPC in enabling precision approaches to whole-person care, with implications for reducing healthcare disparities and improving resource allocation in complex chronic disease management.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine in a way that reaffirms the importance of the relationship between practitioner and patient; focuses on the whole person; is informed by evidence; and makes use of all appropriate therapeutic approaches, healthcare professionals, and disciplines to achieve optimal health and healing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex sociocultural and spatial dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in urban environments. While church planting is a well-established practice within Christian missiology, existing studies often rely on qualitative case studies or small-scale surveys, limiting their capacity to model multifactorial interactions at scale. The computational challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets—including demographic patterns, historical congregational growth rates, community engagement metrics, and geospatial information—to identify predictive variables for sustainable church establishment. Using agent-based modeling (ABM), we will simulate urban ecosystems to test hypotheses about how localized social networks, migration trends, and institutional resource allocation interact with theological and ethical frameworks. A parallel NLP pipeline will process unstructured textual data from historical church planting manuals, sermon corpora, and ethnographic interviews to detect evolving semantic patterns in missiological strategies. By combining these approaches on an HPC cluster, the project aims to generate probabilistic maps of optimal planting locations, adaptive leadership models, and risk assessment frameworks for multicultural contexts. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for missiological researchers, validated against historical case data from 20th-century urban church planting movements. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational social science, human geography, and practical theology, offering a novel evidence-based paradigm for religious organizations navigating rapidly secularizing urban landscapes. The scalability of HPC resources is critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space and enabling real-time sensitivity analyses, which are impractical on conventional infrastructure. Results will advance both academic discussions in digital humanities and applied strategies for faith communities seeking culturally responsive growth models.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale communication datasets and simulate strategic communication scenarios in real time, addressing gaps in data-driven decision-making for organizational messaging. Current approaches to crisis communication, audience engagement, and cross-platform media strategy often rely on fragmented or delayed analyses, limiting the agility of responses to dynamic public discourse. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to optimize message dissemination, assess risk during crises, and evaluate the longitudinal impact of strategic communication campaigns across digital and traditional media ecosystems. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to parse multilingual social media content, news archives, and organizational communication logs, combined with network analysis to map information diffusion patterns. Machine learning models (e.g., transformer-based architectures) will be trained to identify emerging crises, predict audience sentiment shifts, and recommend adaptive messaging strategies. Agent-based simulations will test hypothetical scenarios, such as misinformation outbreaks or brand reputation threats, to refine organizational response protocols. The scale of data—encompassing terabytes of text, video metadata, and real-time API streams—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-memory workloads. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for communication managers to simulate campaign impacts, a framework for proactive crisis detection, and evidence-based insights into cross-platform audience behavior. By bridging computational scalability with communication theory, this work aims to advance adaptive, ethically informed strategies that align organizational goals with rapidly evolving media landscapes. The requested resources will directly support the development of reproducible, large-scale analyses critical to addressing modern challenges in strategic communication.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the critical thinking, analysis, and practical skills essential to developing and implementing communication strategies that advance organizations goals and missions. Includes instruction in communication management, crisis communication, communications law, digital and traditional marketing strategies, media relations, social media strategies, strategic communication, traditional and emerging media, and writing for the media.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Islamic theological and juridical discourse through computational text mining and network analysis of classical Arabic texts. The research problem centers on tracing doctrinal developments across time, regions, and schools of thought in Islam, as reflected in foundational works (e.g., Qur’anic exegeses, hadith commentaries, legal treatises) and later scholarly debates. Current scholarship relies heavily on manual close reading, limiting the scale at which patterns, influences, and conceptual shifts can be systematically identified, particularly across multilingual corpora spanning 14 centuries. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining optical character recognition (OCR) correction for digitized manuscripts, semantic embedding models tailored to classical Arabic, and graph-based network analyses to map intellectual lineages and thematic divergences. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training transformer-based language models on curated datasets of primary sources (∼10^7 words) and secondary literature, as well as for running large-scale simulations of textual transmission and influence networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) a searchable database linking key doctrinal concepts to their temporal, geographic, and sectarian contexts; (2) quantitative visualizations of epistemological shifts in Islamic philosophy; and (3) open-source tools for Arabic-script manuscript processing. By enabling systematic analysis at unprecedented scales, this work aims to reveal understudied connections between early Islamic thought and later scholastic traditions while providing a replicable computational framework for interdisciplinary religious studies. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multilingual text corpora, and parallelized network analysis workflows requiring ∼25,000 core-hours over 12 months.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Islam as preached by the Prophet Muhammad in 6th century Arabia and subsequently interpreted and elaborated by Islamic scholars and others; together with the cultural and social milieu related to the faith in various periods, localities, and branches. Includes instruction in Islamic scripture and related written authorities and commentaries

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in cosmetology through computational modeling of hair structure and chemical interaction dynamics. The research problem centers on the lack of mechanistic understanding of how cosmetic treatments—such as coloring, perming, and keratin smoothing—alter hair at the molecular level, leading to unpredictable outcomes in texture, strength, and aesthetic longevity. Current cosmetology practices rely heavily on empirical trial-and-error approaches, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to account for the diverse biological variability of hair across demographics. To address this gap, the project will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the behavior of hair keratin proteins under varying chemical and mechanical stress conditions. Simulations will integrate physicochemical parameters (e.g., pH, temperature, and oxidative agent concentrations) to predict structural changes in hair fibers during common salon procedures. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze simulation outputs to identify optimal treatment protocols that minimize damage while maximizing desired aesthetic effects. This computational approach will be validated against experimental data from atomic force microscopy and tensile strength testing of treated hair samples. The outcomes will yield predictive frameworks for personalized cosmetic interventions, reducing reliance on hazardous overprocessing and enabling the design of safer, more effective products. By bridging cosmetology with computational biophysics, this work establishes a novel interdisciplinary niche, offering cosmetologists evidence-based tools to enhance client outcomes while advancing curricular innovation in cosmetology education. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the high-throughput simulations required to capture the complexity of hair-chemistry interactions at scale.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to cut, trim, and style scalp, facial, and body hair; apply cosmetic preparations; perform manicures and pedicures; massage the head and extremities; and prepare for practice as licensed cosmetologists in specialized or full-service salons.  Includes instruction in hair cutting and styling, manicuring, pedicuring, facial treatments, shampooing, chemical applications, esthetics, shop management, sanitation and safety, customer service, and applicable professional and labor laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research focused on understudied South Asian languages, particularly historical and low-resource languages of the Indian subcontinent. The core challenge lies in analyzing complex morphosyntactic structures, dialectal variations, and cross-linguistic influences in these languages, which often lack digitized corpora or computational tools tailored to their unique grammatical features. Current methods, optimized for Indo-European languages with rigid word-order systems, fail to account for the agglutinative morphology, free word order, and script-specific encoding challenges prevalent in many South Asian languages. To address this gap, the project will employ parallelized natural language processing (NLP) workflows to process digitized historical texts, oral narratives, and modern publications in languages such as Sindhi, Kashmiri, and Odia. Computational tasks include training transformer-based models for syntactic parsing, developing unsupervised clustering algorithms to map dialectal phonemic variations, and simulating language contact effects through agent-based modeling. These methods require large-scale distributed computing to handle terabyte-scale multilingual datasets, optimize hyperparameters for low-resource language models, and run iterative simulations of linguistic change. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated analysis of agglutinative South Asian languages, a publicly accessible corpus of annotated historical texts, and novel insights into language convergence patterns across the subcontinent. The project will directly support endangered language preservation efforts and provide methodological frameworks for computational research on non-Western language systems, filling critical gaps in both linguistics and digital humanities scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: South Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages, literatures, and linguistics of the peoples of the Indian subcontinent and associated borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing precision machining processes through advanced computational modeling and simulation, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Traditional machining workflows often rely on iterative physical testing to mitigate tool wear, thermal deformation, and vibration-induced inaccuracies, leading to material waste, energy inefficiency, and extended production timelines. The proposed research will develop a multi-physics simulation framework to model interactions between cutting tools, workpiece materials, and machine dynamics under diverse operating conditions. Leveraging finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), the framework will integrate material science datasets (e.g., stress-strain behavior, thermal conductivity) with real-time sensor data emulation to predict tool life, surface finish quality, and dimensional stability. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to recommend adaptive machining parameters, reducing trial-and-error adjustments. HPC resources are essential to resolve the high-resolution, transient simulations required for multi-axis machining scenarios, which involve non-linear material behaviors and micron-scale tolerances. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for machining systems, enabling virtual prototyping and process optimization without physical waste. This work will advance smart manufacturing capabilities for industries reliant on high-precision components (e.g., aerospace, medical devices), while providing Machine Tool Technology students with access to cutting-edge computational tools for workforce training. The project’s open-source simulation modules and datasets will serve as a community resource for further innovation in machining efficiency and sustainability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, manufacture, assemble, test, and repair parts, mechanisms, machines, and structures in which materials are cast, formed, shaped, molded, heat treated, cut, twisted, pressed, fused, stamped or worked.

abstract: Hearing aid technology faces critical challenges in adapting to complex auditory environments, where users often experience difficulty distinguishing speech from background noise. Current hearing aid algorithms, while effective in controlled settings, struggle to dynamically process real-world acoustic variability, leading to suboptimal user outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing advanced machine learning models that simulate and optimize hearing aid signal processing in diverse, noisy environments. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate neural networks on large-scale datasets of real-world acoustic scenes, including multi-speaker environments, transient noises, and non-stationary soundscapes. Computational models will integrate patient-specific audiometric data, cognitive profiles, and subjective preference metrics to personalize hearing aid parameter optimization. Key methodological steps include (1) generating synthetic auditory scenes via physics-based acoustic simulations, (2) implementing deep learning architectures for real-time noise suppression and spatial audio enhancement, and (3) conducting virtual trials through auditory pathway modeling. The scale of data processing—involving terabytes of high-fidelity audio samples and thousands of parallel simulations—necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed training, hyperparameter optimization, and statistical validation across heterogeneous patient populations. Expected outcomes include novel algorithmic frameworks for adaptive gain control and spectral enhancement that outperform conventional hearing aid processing strategies in computational benchmarks. Success metrics will evaluate improvements in speech intelligibility scores and listening effort reduction across simulated environments. This work aims to establish computationally derived design principles for next-generation hearing aids while creating open-source tools for audiological research. Results will directly inform clinical practice guidelines for hearing instrument specialists and contribute to the evidence base for personalized hearing rehabilitation strategies. The project further demonstrates how computational audiology can bridge gaps between theoretical acoustics, clinical practice, and assistive technology development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to test the hearing of, and to select, fit and dispense appropriate hearing aids for, patients. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of the ear, hearing testing, hearing aid fitting and technology, health promotion and rehabilitation, counseling and communication, business management, and professional ethics.

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation relies on the design of oral prostheses that balance biomechanical stability, functional performance, and biocompatibility. Current approaches to optimizing these devices face challenges in predicting long-term outcomes due to the complex interplay of patient-specific anatomical variations, dynamic occlusal forces, and material degradation. Traditional experimental methods are limited in resolving these multiscale interactions efficiently, creating a need for advanced computational modeling to accelerate innovation. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for evaluating and optimizing prosthodontic devices, including dental implants, removable dentures, and maxillofacial prostheses. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate biomechanical stress distribution under physiologically realistic masticatory loads, coupled with machine learning (ML) algorithms to iteratively refine device geometries and material compositions. Patient-specific inputs, derived from clinical CT/CBCT imaging and intraoral force measurements, will inform model parameters to capture heterogeneity in bone density, soft tissue resilience, and occlusal patterns. Multi-physics simulations will assess interfacial stress concentrations, micromotion at the bone-implant interface, and fatigue behavior of prosthetic materials. HPC capabilities are essential to manage the computational intensity of these simulations, which involve millions of mesh elements and non-linear material properties, while enabling large-scale parameter sweeps for ML-driven optimization. Expected outcomes include validated computational protocols for predicting prosthesis failure modes, data-driven design guidelines to minimize bone resorption and soft tissue irritation, and a digital twin platform for virtual prototyping of patient-matched devices. This work will advance prosthodontic research by reducing reliance on iterative physical testing, shortening device development cycles, and improving clinical success rates through personalized biomechanical solutions. The resulting computational tools will be disseminated to the clinical research community to support evidence-based design standards in restorative dentistry.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and techniques of constructing oral prostheses, and the restoration and maintenance of oral function by the replacement of missing teeth and other oral structures with such artificial devices.

abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) operate in high-stakes, time-sensitive environments where clinical decision-making directly impacts patient outcomes. Current protocols for prehospital care rely on generalized guidelines, which may not adequately account for dynamic patient conditions, resource constraints, or rare clinical scenarios. This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize real-time decision support for EMT paramedics by analyzing heterogeneous datasets, including electronic patient care reports, vital sign telemetry, geospatial data, and historical outcomes. The primary research challenge lies in integrating multimodal data streams under time-critical constraints to generate actionable recommendations without compromising patient privacy or overburdening field personnel. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train machine learning models on large-scale EMS datasets (spanning 500,000+ anonymized cases) and simulate emergency scenarios via agent-based modeling. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures for predictive analytics (e.g., deterioration risk stratification), natural language processing to extract insights from unstructured narrative reports, and discrete-event simulations to evaluate protocol efficiency. Federated learning techniques will be employed to address data siloing across EMS agencies while maintaining HIPAA compliance. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated decision-support framework capable of operating on edge devices in low-bandwidth environments, (2) evidence-based refinements to triage and resource allocation protocols, and (3) open-source simulation tools for training paramedics in rare high-acuity scenarios. By leveraging HPC-enabled large-scale modeling, this work aims to reduce cognitive load during emergencies, improve adherence to evolving clinical guidelines, and ultimately enhance survival rates for time-critical conditions such as trauma, stroke, and cardiac arrest. The resulting computational infrastructure will serve as a replicable platform for prehospital care research across diverse EMS systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the remote supervision of physicians, to recognize, assess, and manage medical emergencies in prehospital settings and to supervise Ambulance personnel. Includes instruction in basic, intermediate, and advanced EMT procedures; emergency surgical procedures; medical triage; rescue operations; crisis scene management and personnel supervision; equipment operation and maintenance; patient stabilization, monitoring, and care; drug administration; identification and preliminary diagnosis of diseases and injuries; communication and computer operations; basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: Palliative care research faces significant challenges in predicting patient trajectories and optimizing individualized care plans due to the complex interplay of biological, psychosocial, and clinical factors influencing outcomes. Current approaches often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic symptom evolution, treatment responses, and heterogeneous patient needs. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to integrate multimodal data—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, real-time symptom reports, and social determinants of health—into predictive models for personalized palliative care. The research will employ machine learning techniques such as recurrent neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models to analyze longitudinal datasets from 15,000+ patients across six palliative care cohorts. These models will identify critical predictors of symptom burden, quality-of-life trajectories, and end-of-life decision-making patterns while accounting for missing data and temporal dependencies. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for model training, stochastic simulations of care pathways, and sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of complex algorithms that would be infeasible with standard clinical computing resources. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools to guide early interventions for high-risk patients, dynamic decision-support systems for clinicians, and stratification frameworks for clinical trial enrollment. By elucidating modifiable factors in palliative care outcomes, this work aims to reduce preventable suffering, optimize resource allocation, and establish scalable computational methodologies for future research in patient-centered care. The proposed models and pipelines will be disseminated through open-source platforms to foster collaboration across palliative care research networks.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of multi-scale atmospheric wave interactions and their role in modulating severe weather events and upper atmospheric dynamics. A critical gap persists in resolving how mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) interact with gravity waves and larger-scale solar wind perturbations, particularly during geomagnetic storms. These coupled processes influence ionospheric variability and tropospheric storm intensity but remain poorly quantified due to computational limitations in simulating cross-scale feedbacks. To address this, we propose high-resolution numerical simulations using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model with thermosphere-ionosphere extension (WACCM-X). The simulations will resolve turbulence and boundary layer dynamics at sub-kilometer horizontal grid spacing while incorporating real-time solar wind data to capture magnetosphere-ionosphere-atmosphere coupling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational demands of (1) nested domains spanning 10 km to 100 m resolution, (2) ensemble forecasting under varying geomagnetic conditions, and (3) assimilation of radar and satellite remote sensing data. The project will leverage GPU-optimized model configurations and parallelized workflows to process petabytes of 4D atmospheric state variables. Expected outcomes include improved parameterizations of gravity wave momentum transfer in weather-climate models and quantifiable linkages between solar wind variability and convective system intensification. Results will directly benefit the development of coupled space-weather-forecasting frameworks and inform climate resilience strategies reliant on accurate severe weather prediction. The scale of these multi-physics simulations—requiring 2.5 million core-hours and 400 TB of storage—exceeds institutional capabilities, necessitating allocation of national HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the processes governing the interactions, movement, and behavior of atmospheric phenomena and related terrestrial and solar phenomena. Includes instruction in cloud and precipitation physics, solar radiation transfer, active and passive remote sensing, atmospheric electricity and acoustics, atmospheric wave phenomena, turbulence and boundary layers, solar wind, geomagnetic storms, coupling, natural plasma, and energization.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of personalizing pain management in hospice and palliative care through advanced computational modeling of dynamic pain trajectories. Despite the critical need for effective symptom control in patients with advanced illness, current approaches rely on static assessments and reactive adjustments, often failing to account for the nonlinear interplay of physiological, psychosocial, and pharmacological factors. We propose to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating time-series electronic health record (EHR) data, continuous biosensor metrics, and patient-reported outcomes to model pain progression and treatment response. The research will employ machine learning architectures, including transformer-based temporal models and hybrid neural-pharmacokinetic systems, to predict individualized pain dynamics. Agent-based modeling will simulate patient-specific responses to opioid and non-opioid interventions under varying clinical scenarios, while federated learning techniques will enable multi-institutional data collaboration without compromising privacy. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated clusters for real-time optimization of dosing schedules and risk stratification for adverse events such as respiratory depression. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source predictive toolset for clinicians to proactively adjust therapies based on simulated trajectories, validated against a longitudinal dataset of 1,200 palliative care patients. This work bridges gaps in precision palliative medicine by introducing systems-level computational approaches to a domain traditionally dependent on qualitative assessment, with potential to reduce preventable suffering in terminal illness while maintaining ethical alignment with patient-centered care goals. The HPC resources are essential for handling the scale of multimodal data fusion, parallelized parameter exploration in pharmacological simulations, and deployment of privacy-preserving distributed learning across partner hospice networks.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Khmer-language texts, addressing critical gaps in digital scholarship for Cambodian literature and linguistics. Despite the rich cultural and linguistic heritage of Khmer, there remains a scarcity of digitized corpora and computational tools tailored to its unique morphological and syntactic structures. This limits scholarly access to large-scale textual analysis, machine-readable historical manuscripts, and applications in education or technology. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to process, annotate, and analyze Khmer texts across genres—from classical literature to modern media—enabling systematic inquiry into linguistic evolution, stylistic patterns, and sociocultural themes. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for Khmer’s non-Latin script and agglutinative morphology, including custom tokenization models and neural architectures for semantic segmentation. Optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines will be trained on diverse Khmer scripts, including palm-leaf manuscripts, to digitize understudied historical works. These workflows will be parallelized across HPC nodes to manage large datasets, reduce processing times for training language models, and enable comparative analyses of textual features at scale. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, annotated corpus of premodern and contemporary Khmer texts, alongside reusable NLP tools for the research community. The project will generate new insights into diachronic shifts in literary conventions, lexical borrowing, and the relationship between language use and cultural identity. By creating infrastructure for computational Khmer studies, this work supports interdisciplinary scholarship, language preservation, and applications in educational technology, such as adaptive learning systems for Khmer literacy. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive tasks in corpus construction and computationally demanding model training, ensuring the project’s feasibility and scalability.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Khmer language as spoken in Cambodia. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate the behavioral dynamics of adversarial decision-making in hybrid threat environments, where physical and cyber elements intersect with human cognitive factors. The research addresses a critical gap in security science: current risk assessment tools often treat human adversaries as static actors, neglecting adaptive strategies influenced by real-time feedback, misinformation, or cultural context. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to create agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate cognitive architectures, game-theoretic principles, and machine learning to capture the nonlinear evolution of adversarial intent across multiple operational domains. The computational approach will combine discrete-event simulations with neural network-driven pattern recognition to analyze how adversaries might exploit systemic vulnerabilities in interconnected infrastructure, accounting for psychological biases, resource constraints, and deception tactics. Key innovations include the development of multi-resolution modeling techniques to bridge individual decision-making scales with organizational behavior, and the implementation of ensemble simulation workflows to quantify uncertainty in threat prediction. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmark dataset of adversarial behavior scenarios, validated through retrospective analysis of historical security breaches, and predictive metrics for resilience planning in critical systems. This work will provide security practitioners with novel analytical tools to anticipate emergent threat patterns in an era of increasingly sophisticated hybrid operations, while advancing methodological paradigms for computational social science applications in security contexts. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling simulations to realistic complexity levels, enabling parallelized scenario testing across diverse parameter spaces that reflect the multidimensional nature of modern security challenges.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in modeling reactive transport and phase equilibria during magma crystallization and hydrothermal alteration, processes central to ore formation and crustal evolution. Current geochemical models struggle to resolve coupled fluid-rock interactions at the spatial and temporal scales relevant to natural systems, particularly in multi-phase, multicomponent systems with kinetic barriers. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating parallelized finite element simulations of reactive transport with machine learning-accelerated thermodynamic modeling. The computational workflow will couple existing geochemical software (e.g., CHiMaD, ThermoCalc) with custom Fortran/Python codes to solve conservation equations for mass and energy while dynamically updating phase assemblages and fluid compositions across 3D domains. High-resolution simulations will target two scenarios: (1) fractional crystallization of basaltic magmas with volatile exsolution, and (2) wallrock alteration in porphyry copper systems. Both scenarios require petabyte-scale storage for mineral reaction network databases and GPU-optimized linear algebra routines to handle stiffness in rate equations. The HPC implementation will leverage adaptive mesh refinement and distributed memory parallelism (MPI) to achieve meter-scale resolution across kilometer-scale geological domains. Expected outcomes include quantitative predictions of ore metal partitioning during magma differentiation, validated against natural samples from the Chilean Andes, and probabilistic maps of alteration zonation patterns useful for mineral exploration. By bridging atomic-scale reaction kinetics with reservoir-scale fluid flow, this work will advance theoretical geochemistry while providing open-source tools for simulating multi-phase reactive transport. The requested computational resources (10,000+ CPU-core-hours/month, 200 TB storage) are essential given the >10⁶ degree-of-freedom systems and iterative parameter optimization via neural network surrogates, which exceed the capabilities of local university clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the igneous, metamorphic, and hydrothermal processes within the earth and the mineral, fluid, rock, and ore deposits resulting from them. Includes instruction in mineralogy, crystallography, petrology, volcanology, economic geology, meteoritics, geochemical reactions, deposition, compound transformation, core studies, theoretical geochemistry, computer applications, and laboratory studies.

abstract: Critically ill surgical patients, particularly those with polytrauma or multi-organ dysfunction, present complex clinical challenges due to the dynamic interplay of physiological, biochemical, and treatment-related variables. Existing predictive models for outcomes such as sepsis progression, organ failure, or mortality often lack the resolution to capture nonlinear interactions between organ systems or adapt to patient-specific heterogeneity. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to predict individualized clinical trajectories and optimize intervention strategies in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multimodal data from electronic health records (laboratory results, vital signs), waveform analytics (continuous hemodynamic monitoring), and imaging-derived biomarkers into a multiscale modeling framework. Machine learning approaches, including ensemble neural networks and Bayesian adaptive algorithms, will be coupled with mechanistic models of systemic inflammation, coagulation dysregulation, and organ crosstalk. The computational workflow will prioritize scalability to accommodate heterogeneous datasets from 15,000+ retrospective cases and prospective validation cohorts. HPC resources will enable parallelized parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses across 100+ variables, and real-time simulation of treatment scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for early identification of sepsis-associated cardiac dysfunction, probabilistic forecasts of acute kidney injury progression, and decision-support algorithms for personalized fluid resuscitation. By quantifying uncertainty in dynamic clinical states, these models aim to reduce delayed interventions and mitigate iatrogenic risks in critical care. The computational infrastructure developed will be shared via an open-source platform, enabling collaborative refinement across trauma centers. This work directly addresses the National Academies’ call for data-driven precision approaches in acute care surgery and has the potential to redefine risk stratification paradigms in surgical critical care training and practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares surgeons in the diagnosis, treatment, and support of critically ill and injured patients, particularly trauma victims and patients with multiple organ dysfunction.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the computational challenges of solving high-dimensional stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) arising in multiphysics systems, such as fluid-structure interactions with uncertain parameters. Traditional numerical methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs due to the curse of dimensionality and the need for repeated sampling in stochastic domains. This project will develop and implement scalable hybrid algorithms that combine adaptive sparse grid collocation with parallelized multilevel Monte Carlo methods, optimized for heterogeneous computing architectures. The computational approach integrates domain decomposition strategies for spatial discretizations, leveraging distributed-memory parallelism via MPI, with GPU-accelerated tensor operations for stochastic basis function evaluations. A novel feature includes dynamic load-balancing algorithms to address irregular computational workloads caused by localized mesh refinements and spatially correlated uncertainty fields. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable large-scale simulations of 3D turbulent flow coupled with elastic structures, targeting systems exceeding 10^8 degrees of freedom. Expected outcomes include a quantitative framework for error propagation analysis in stochastic multiphysics systems and open-source software modules compatible with the PETSc and FEniCS ecosystems. This work will advance computational mathematics by establishing new performance benchmarks for mixed-precision iterative solvers in stochastic settings while providing methodological insights for uncertainty-aware simulations in applied domains such as aerospace engineering and biomechanics. The resource-intensive nature of the project necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes with high memory bandwidth and low-latency interconnects to achieve strong scaling across thousands of concurrent processes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the theory, architecture, and design of computers, computational techniques, and algorithms. Includes instruction in computer theory, cybernetics, numerical analysis, algorithm development, binary structures, combinatorics, advanced statistics, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict safety risks in dynamic industrial environments, with a focus on optimizing real-time hazard mitigation strategies. Industrial safety management faces challenges in anticipating accidents caused by complex interactions between human operators, equipment, and environmental factors. Traditional risk assessment methods often rely on static models or historical data, limiting their ability to address emerging risks in modern, adaptive manufacturing systems. To address this gap, we propose an integrated simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-agent interactions, ergonomic stressors, and process deviations at scale. The computational model will combine agent-based simulations of worker behavior with finite element analyses of equipment stress and computational fluid dynamics models of environmental contaminants. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify risk patterns from synthetic and real-world sensor datasets, enabling predictive analytics for accident prevention. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-resolution spatial-temporal data, running parallelized simulations across diverse hazard scenarios, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous input streams. Expected outcomes include a validated risk prediction toolkit capable of recommending context-aware safety interventions, such as adaptive equipment shutdown protocols or dynamic personnel routing. This work will advance industrial safety technology by enabling proactive, data-driven decision-making in complex operational settings, with potential applications in chemical processing, automated manufacturing, and warehouse logistics. Results will be disseminated as open-source modules for safety simulation, contributing to academic research and industry practices in occupational health. The requested computing resources will support the creation of large-scale digital twins for safety testing, reducing reliance on physical prototypes and enabling the exploration of high-consequence, low-probability events that are infeasible to study experimentally.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing and enforcing industrial safety standards to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in industrial processes, industrial hygiene, injury prevention, toxicology, ergonomics, risk analysis, system and process safety, safety performance measurement, human factors, human behavior, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing processes involve complex interactions between material properties, equipment dynamics, and environmental conditions, requiring precise control to minimize defects and maximize yield. Current challenges in optimizing processes such as chemical vapor deposition, plasma etching, and photolithography stem from limited insights into multiphysics phenomena at micro- and nanoscales, particularly under high-vacuum and high-temperature conditions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and analyze critical manufacturing steps, enabling data-driven process optimization. The research will employ multiscale computational models integrating molecular dynamics (MD) for atomic-scale interactions during thin-film deposition, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for reactor-scale gas flow and thermal gradients, and machine learning (ML) to correlate simulated parameters with real-world process outcomes. These models will be validated against experimental data from industrial partners, including in-line metrology and defect inspection results. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal equipment settings, predict failure modes in vacuum systems, and reduce trial-and-error experimentation. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for defect formation mechanisms, a digital twin framework for process troubleshooting, and recommendations for equipment calibration under varying operational constraints. This work will directly support workforce training in semiconductor manufacturing technologies by generating open-access simulation tools and case studies for educational use. By bridging computational modeling with industrial applications, the project aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices, reduce material waste, and enhance the reliability of next-generation semiconductor devices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to operate and monitor equipment for the fabrication of semiconductors or microchips from silicon wafers, and to troubleshoot, maintain, and repair the specialized equipment used in this process. Includes instruction in AC and DC circuits, digital fundamentals, solid state devices, manufacturing processes, vacuum principles and technology, industrial electronics, quality assurance, and semiconductor manufacturing technology.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of emergency medical services (EMS) through advanced computational modeling of ambulance deployment strategies in dynamic urban environments. Emergency Care Attendants (ECAs) face critical challenges in optimizing response times amid variable factors such as traffic patterns, incident location density, and fluctuating patient acuity levels. Traditional dispatch protocols often rely on static geographic zones or historical averages, which fail to adapt to real-time conditions, potentially delaying life-saving interventions. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework that integrates real-time traffic data, historical emergency call records, and probabilistic patient outcome models. The framework will employ agent-based modeling to simulate thousands of concurrent emergency scenarios, varying parameters such as ambulance fleet size, base station locations, and priority dispatch algorithms. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in time-sensitive patient outcomes, enabling predictive analytics for resource allocation. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of parallelized simulations required to model metropolitan-scale emergency networks and the complex optimization of multi-objective decision-making (e.g., minimizing response times while balancing crew fatigue and fuel efficiency). Validation will utilize retrospective EMS datasets from partner agencies, comparing simulated outcomes to real-world performance metrics. Expected outcomes include the creation of adaptive dispatch algorithms that dynamically adjust to emerging conditions, as well as a publicly accessible training module for ECAs to practice decision-making in computationally generated high-pressure scenarios. This work has the potential to reduce median emergency response times by an estimated 15-20% in test regions, directly improving survival rates for time-critical conditions such as cardiac arrest and severe trauma. Results will be disseminated through EMS software partnerships and integrated into EMT-Ambulance training curricula to bridge research innovation with frontline practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist licensed EMTs, under the supervision of a physician, to prepare and transport ill or injured patients, and to operate emergency vehicles and equipment such as life support units. Includes instruction in first aid and emergency medicine field techniques, patient stabilization and care, medical field communications, equipment operation and maintenance, emergency vehicle operation, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Aging populations face increasing risks of psychiatric disorders such as late-life depression, dementia-related psychosis, and Alzheimer’s disease–associated neuropsychiatric symptoms. Current diagnostic frameworks and treatment strategies for these conditions lack precision, partly due to the heterogeneous biological and psychosocial factors influencing geriatric mental health. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multimodal neuroimaging, genomic, and electronic health record (EHR) data to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment response and disease progression in elderly patients. The computational complexity of analyzing high-dimensional datasets, which include longitudinal structural/functional MRI scans, polygenic risk scores, and dynamic EHR entries, necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Specifically, we propose developing machine learning models to disentangle interactions between neuroanatomical changes, genetic vulnerabilities, and clinical outcomes. Deep neural networks will be trained to classify patient subtypes using fused imaging-genomic data, while survival analysis models will evaluate time-to-event outcomes (e.g., cognitive decline, medication discontinuation) from EHRs. These tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale neuroimaging data, genome-wide association study (GWAS) pipelines, and iterative model validation across hyperparameter spaces—workflows impractical without HPC clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for individualized treatment selection in geriatric depression and dementia-related psychosis, (2) novel biomarkers linking neuroinflammation-related genetic variants to longitudinal symptom trajectories, and (3) open-source tools for multimodal data integration in aging research. By elucidating mechanisms of psychiatric resilience and vulnerability in older adults, this work aims to advance precision geriatric psychiatry, reduce trial-and-error prescribing practices, and inform targeted interventions. The requested computing resources will enable scalable analyses critical to transforming large, complex datasets into clinically actionable knowledge for an underserved population.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of mental and emotional disorders in the elderly, and to improve the psychiatric care of the elderly both in health and in disease.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational methods to address challenges in real-time processing and fusion of multi-modal signals intelligence (SIGINT) and geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) data within contested operational environments. Contemporary military intelligence workflows face critical bottlenecks in synthesizing high-volume, heterogeneous data streams—including radar, acoustic, electromagnetic, and overhead imagery—under latency constraints. Existing tools often rely on sequential processing architectures or simplified physical models, limiting their capacity to resolve ambiguities in cluttered or adversarial signal environments. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC) framework leveraging GPU-accelerated parallel processing and machine learning (ML) to enable near-real-time correlation of spatially and temporally dispersed signals. The computational approach integrates adaptive signal decomposition algorithms with physics-informed neural networks trained on synthetic and operational datasets, explicitly accounting for terrain occlusion, atmospheric propagation effects, and adversarial countermeasures. Key innovations include a dynamic resource allocation module to prioritize computational effort based on mission-critical signals and a federated learning architecture to maintain model efficacy in bandwidth-constrained environments. The project will validate the framework using simulated and operational datasets, including multi-sensor collections from distributed airborne and maritime platforms. Anticipated outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in processing latency for target resolution tasks, improved discrimination of low-probability-of-intercept signals, and tools to visualize multi-domain signal interactions at tactically relevant scales. By bridging gaps between traditional SIGINT/GEOINT processing pipelines and modern HPC capabilities, this work aims to enhance situational awareness and decision-making superiority in complex electromagnetic battlespaces, directly supporting operational readiness and mission success.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, technology and operational aspects of collecting, processing and exploiting remote-sensed, radar, acoustic and other forms of signals intelligence. Includes instruction in applied physics, wave propagation and capture, radar systems, acoustics and underwater systems, infrared systems, synthetic aperture systems, collection and processing systems, signal phenomenology, signal analysis and exploitation, and applications to specific intelligence problems.

abstract: The proposed research aims to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying enzyme catalysis in understudied metabolic pathways critical to cellular homeostasis. Despite advances in structural biology, dynamic features of enzyme-substrate interactions—particularly transient conformational states and solvent-mediated proton transfer processes—remain poorly resolved experimentally. This project will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced by free energy calculations to model catalytic cycles of two target enzymes: a flavin-dependent oxidoreductase implicated in redox stress response and a metal-dependent hydrolase involved in lipid metabolism. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform millisecond-scale all-atom simulations with explicit solvent, which are required to capture rare but mechanistically pivotal transitions, such as cofactor rearrangements and proton-coupled electron transfer events. Systems will be parameterized using quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) approaches to accurately model reactive intermediates and transition states. Concurrently, Markov state models will be constructed to map free energy landscapes and identify kinetic bottlenecks in catalysis. Expected outcomes include (1) atomic-level insights into how conserved active-site residues orchestrate multistep reactions, (2) predictive models of mutations that alter catalytic efficiency, and (3) validation of hypothesized solvent participation in proton relays. Results will address longstanding questions in enzymology regarding the interplay between protein dynamics and chemical reactivity, while providing a framework to guide rational enzyme engineering. The proposed work directly aligns with foundational goals in biochemistry and molecular biology by bridging gaps between static structural data and functional mechanisms. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical due to the computational intensity of multi-tiered sampling (≥500,000 core-hours) and the need for parallelized analysis of terabyte-scale trajectory datasets. This project will yield broadly applicable methodologies for studying enzymatic systems inaccessible to conventional experimental techniques.
cip_definition: A program of study that combines the biological sub-disciplines of biochemistry and molecular biology. Includes instruction in general biology, general and organic chemistry, physics, biochemistry, molecular biology, immunology, microbiology, genetics, and cellular biology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision production processes through the development of a high-fidelity computational framework for optimizing multi-material additive manufacturing (AM). Current AM workflows struggle with defects arising from thermal stress gradients and material incompatibilities, particularly in complex geometries requiring heterogeneous material deposition. These limitations hinder the adoption of AM for high-value applications in aerospace, biomedical devices, and energy systems. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-physics modeling approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate coupled thermal-structural phenomena at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational framework will integrate finite element analysis for heat transfer modeling, phase-field methods for material interface dynamics, and machine learning algorithms for real-time parameter optimization. By parallelizing these computationally intensive workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to achieve micron-scale resolution across centimeter-scale build volumes while maintaining practical simulation timescales. The project will validate models against experimental data from in-situ monitoring systems, creating feedback loops to improve predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include a publicly available simulation toolkit for multi-material AM optimization, quantitative guidelines for mitigating defect formation, and a database of validated process parameters for niche alloys and polymer-ceramic composites. This work will directly advance the precision production community's capacity to manufacture next-generation components with tightly controlled material properties while reducing trial-and-error prototyping costs by an estimated 40-60%. Successful implementation requires sustained access to HPC resources capable of handling petascale datasets generated by coupled multi-physics simulations, including dedicated GPU nodes for deep learning components and high-memory nodes for handling heterogeneous material property matrices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision production, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance survey methodology by addressing a critical gap in understanding how latent cognitive processes during question-response tasks influence measurement error, particularly in cross-cultural and multilingual contexts. Traditional approaches to survey design often rely on post-hoc statistical adjustments to mitigate bias, but they inadequately account for real-time cognitive and linguistic factors that shape respondents’ comprehension, retrieval, and reporting behaviors. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating cognitive modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and large-scale simulation to dynamically model response pathways under varying survey conditions. The research will develop agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate respondents’ decision-making processes during surveys, incorporating individual differences in working memory, semantic understanding, and cultural framing. These models will be trained and validated using existing multilingual survey datasets with paradata (e.g., response times, click patterns) and linked to experimental manipulations of question wording, format, and translation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support the parallelized execution of millions of ABM instances across diverse demographic and linguistic parameter spaces, as well as the training of transformer-based NLP models to detect subtle linguistic ambiguities in survey instruments. The computational pipeline will employ multilevel regression and structural equation modeling to quantify interactions between cognitive load, question features, and measurement error. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for optimizing survey design through pre-test simulations, empirically grounded guidelines for cross-cultural questionnaire adaptation, and novel metrics for assessing cognitive validity in survey items. By elucidating the cognitive mechanisms underlying response bias, this work aims to enhance the accuracy and equity of survey data collection in heterogeneous populations, with applications spanning public health, education, and policy evaluation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on survey research design to gather data about behaviors, demographics, opinions, and data analysis to answer complex questions. Includes instruction in the analysis of survey data, cross-cultural and multi-population survey methodology, data collection methods, modes of survey analysis, quantitative analysis, questionnaire design, research design, sampling, survey error, and structural equation modeling.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of language processing deficits in acquired communication disorders, such as aphasia, through large-scale computational modeling of neural network dynamics. Aphasia, often resulting from stroke or traumatic brain injury, disrupts language comprehension and production, yet the precise neural mechanisms underlying these impairments remain poorly characterized. Traditional neuroimaging and behavioral studies are limited in spatial-temporal resolution and the ability to simulate pathological neural activity. To address this, we propose developing biologically constrained spiking neural network (SNN) models to simulate language processing pathways under both healthy and lesioned conditions. These models will integrate structural connectivity data from neuroimaging repositories, simulate lesion effects via targeted node inactivation, and predict functional disruptions using dynamic systems theory. The computational demands of simulating large-scale SNNs with millions of neurons and synaptic connections necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized simulation, parameter optimization, and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include identifying critical network hubs whose dysfunction predicts clinical symptom profiles and generating testable hypotheses for neuromodulation therapies. By mapping model-predicted deficits to behavioral data from aphasia patients, this work will bridge computational neuroscience and clinical practice, offering a framework for personalized rehabilitation strategies. The requested HPC resources will enable the iterative training of network architectures, storage of multi-terabyte simulation outputs, and deployment of machine learning pipelines to analyze emergent network properties. This project aligns with the Health Professions’ mission to translate cutting-edge computational tools into clinically actionable insights, with broader implications for understanding neuroplasticity in communication disorders.
cip_title: Communication Disorders Sciences and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications disorders sciences and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of traditional herbal medicine with modern computational approaches presents a critical challenge due to the complexity of multi-compound botanical formulations and their dynamic interactions with human physiological systems. While such formulations are central to many alternative medical systems, their mechanisms of action remain poorly characterized, limiting scientific validation and optimization. This project seeks to address this gap by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model the polypharmacological effects of a curated library of 500 plant-derived compounds, focusing on their synergistic interactions within inflammation-related pathways. Leveraging molecular docking, machine learning-based binding affinity prediction, and dynamic network pharmacology, the research will simulate compound-target interactions across proteome-scale datasets to identify key bioactive agents and their cooperative effects. The computational pipeline integrates AlphaFold-predicted protein structures, molecular dynamics simulations for conformational sampling, and Bayesian network analysis to map multi-target modulation patterns. HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative, high-throughput processing of over 10^6 potential compound-target pairs, requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated simulations and distributed memory architectures for large-scale graph-based network analyses. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel synergistic herbal combinations with predicted anti-inflammatory properties, validated through subsequent in vitro testing. The project will generate an open-access database of compound interaction profiles, bridging traditional knowledge systems with computational systems biology. By establishing a framework for analyzing complex botanical formulations at molecular resolution, this work aims to advance evidence-based integration of alternative medicine into contemporary healthcare paradigms while contributing computational methodologies applicable to other understudied therapeutic modalities.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the theories, science, and practice of alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems. Includes instruction in understanding acupuncture, herbal medicine, naturopathy, homeopathy, and other alternative and complementary medicine modalities; mind-body therapies; nutrition; comparison of conventional and alternative medicine; and medical ethics; and may include training in specific alternative and complementary medicine modalities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive toxicology and pharmacology in veterinary medicine, addressing critical gaps in understanding species-specific drug and toxicant interactions. Current limitations in experimental approaches hinder the efficient evaluation of xenobiotic metabolism, pharmacodynamic variability, and mechanisms of toxicity across diverse animal species. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling. The project will focus on three key areas: (1) simulating interactions between veterinary drugs, pesticides, and ion channels/enzymes in species such as canines, bovines, and avian models; (2) predicting interspecies differences in metabolic pathways using genomic data and enzyme structure modeling; and (3) optimizing antidote efficacy through virtual screening of compound libraries against toxin targets. HPC resources are essential for large-scale MD simulations (exceeding 10^6 atom systems), parallelized ML training on toxicogenomic datasets, and population PK modeling across anatomical variations in livestock and companion animals. Expected outcomes include identifying genetic biomarkers of drug resistance in parasites, elucidating neurotoxic mechanisms of agricultural pesticides in non-target species, and accelerating the design of species-specific detoxification protocols. By enabling high-resolution simulations of complex biological systems, this work will provide foundational insights into interspecies toxicological responses, directly supporting the development of safer therapeutics and environmental risk mitigation strategies for veterinary and agricultural applications. The generated models and datasets will be shared via open-access platforms to foster collaborative innovation in veterinary pharmacology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of specific environmental and food hazards affecting domestic and wild animals and the development and action of chemical antidotes and treatments. Includes instruction in small and large animal toxicology and pharmacology, neurotoxicology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, neuropharmacology, xenobiotics, drug resistance, pesticides, toxicological pathology, genetic and molecular toxicology, environmental toxicology, drug and toxicant analysis and evaluation, and environmental radiology.

abstract: Grapevine health and productivity are challenged by dynamic biotic and abiotic stressors, necessitating advanced predictive tools to optimize vineyard management. Current approaches lack the computational capacity to integrate multi-scale data, from genomic markers to regional climate patterns. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework combining large-scale genomic analysis, machine learning, and multi-environment simulation models. By analyzing tera-scale genomic datasets from *Vitis vinifera* cultivars, alongside high-resolution environmental data, we aim to identify genetic loci associated with resilience to pathogens such as powdery mildew and abiotic stressors like drought. Concurrently, deep learning algorithms will be trained on historical pest incidence records and microclimate data to forecast disease outbreaks at subregional scales. HPC-enabled agent-based models will simulate vineyard management strategies under varying climate scenarios, evaluating their impact on yield, fruit quality, and input costs. The integration of these computational approaches will enable the development of precision viticulture tools that recommend cultivar selection, treatment timing, and resource allocation tailored to specific terroirs. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive models for grower decision support, novel insights into grapevine stress response mechanisms, and optimized protocols for sustainable winegrape production. This research directly addresses critical challenges in viticultural sustainability and economic viability, providing computational resources to bridge the gap between genomic potential and field-scale agricultural practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific and agribusiness principles to the production of grapes, the making of wine, and the wine business. Includes instruction in grapes and wines of the world; grape production; winemaking technology; plant biology; chemistry; food science, safety, and packaging; soil science; pest management; and marketing and business management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize complex operational dynamics in multi-location restaurant enterprises, focusing on real-time decision-making under uncertainty. The research problem centers on the challenge of balancing perishable inventory management, labor scheduling, and customer demand fluctuations across geographically dispersed kitchens and dining facilities—a task complicated by variables such as seasonal menu changes, supply chain disruptions, and heterogeneous regional consumption patterns. Traditional operations research methods have proven inadequate for these nonlinear, high-dimensional optimization problems due to their reliance on static assumptions and inability to process real-time data streams from point-of-sale systems, IoT-enabled kitchen equipment, and third-party delivery platforms. The proposed computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation, agent-based modeling, and reinforcement learning to create an adaptive decision-support framework. By parallelizing thousands of scenario iterations across HPC nodes, the models will account for spatial-temporal dependencies between locations, employee skill variability, and dynamic customer behavior patterns derived from historical transaction datasets spanning 12 million meals. Expected outcomes include a novel optimization engine capable of recommending coordinated purchasing, staffing, and menu engineering strategies at 15-minute intervals while maintaining nutritional guidelines and profit margins. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of operational data from three national casual dining chains and prototype deployment in a live test environment with 42 locations. The computational intensity stems from simultaneously optimizing 78 interdependent variables across 72-hour planning horizons, requiring teraflop-scale processing to achieve practical runtime thresholds. Successful implementation could reduce food waste by an estimated 18-22% and labor costs by 12-15% in participating enterprises while providing a template for AI-driven resource allocation in hospitality management. This work bridges gaps between culinary operations, behavioral economics, and computational logistics, establishing a framework for data-intensive decision-making in food service ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage food and beverage preparation and service operations, restaurant facilities, and catering services.  Includes instruction in food/beverage industry operations, cost control, purchasing and storage, business administration, logistics, personnel management, culinary arts, restaurant and menu planning, executive chef functions, event planning and management, health and safety, insurance, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Sleep disorders present complex challenges in diagnosis and treatment, requiring precise analysis of multidimensional physiological data. Current polysomnography workflows rely on manual scoring of sleep stages and events, a time-intensive process prone to inter-rater variability. This project seeks to develop an automated, high-resolution framework for interpreting polysomnographic data through advanced computational modeling. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets encompassing electroencephalography, respiratory effort signals, oxygen saturation, and limb movement data from 5,000 retrospective patient studies. A hybrid machine learning architecture combining transformer-based temporal analysis with graph neural networks will be implemented to model interdependencies between physiological subsystems during sleep cycles. The computational pipeline will address three core challenges: 1) real-time detection of microarousals and transitional sleep states, 2) identification of subclinical patterns predictive of circadian rhythm dysregulation, and 3) spatial-temporal mapping of autonomic nervous system fluctuations during REM sleep. By utilizing GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition and distributed training across HPC nodes, the models will process high-density EEG signals (256-channel) at millisecond resolution while maintaining clinical interpretability through attention mechanism visualization. Validation will employ a novel adversarial validation protocol comparing model outputs against consensus scores from international sleep experts. Anticipated outcomes include a validated computational framework capable of identifying previously undetectable biomarkers for narcolepsy subtypes and non-apnea sleep fragmentation syndromes. This resource will enable personalized sleep architecture profiling, potentially reducing diagnostic latency for rare sleep disorders by 40-60% while establishing scalable infrastructure for future studies integrating genomics and wearable sensor data streams.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in equine health and performance optimization through advanced computational modeling of large-scale genomic and biomechanical datasets. A key problem in modern horse husbandry is the need to balance selective breeding for desirable athletic traits with minimizing genetic predispositions to musculoskeletal injuries and metabolic disorders. Current approaches rely on limited phenotypic correlations, which fail to capture complex gene-environment interactions or biomechanical stress patterns during training. We propose developing machine learning models to analyze whole-genome sequencing data from 5,000 sport horses alongside longitudinal health records, integrating this with 3D motion-capture-derived biomechanical simulations of gait dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte genomic datasets using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and training neural networks to predict injury risks based on combined genetic, kinematic, and training load factors. Additionally, finite element analysis simulations will model bone and tendon stress distributions across different disciplines (racing, dressage, jumping) to establish evidence-based conditioning protocols. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of candidate genes associated with injury resilience, 2) predictive algorithms for optimizing individual training regimens, and 3) biomechanically validated standards for discipline-specific facility design. These computational tools will enable data-driven decisions in breeding programs and stable management while improving equine welfare.
