The scale of genomic analysis, complexity of multi-physics biomechanical modeling, and need for real-time parameter optimization in machine learning workflows necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and parallel processing capabilities beyond typical institutional resources. This work bridges quantitative biology and precision equine management, advancing both animal science research methodologies and practical applications for sustainable horse industry operations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Horse Husbandry/ Equine Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the selection, breeding, care, and maintenance of work, athletic, and show horses; and to manage horse farms, stables, tracks and related equipment and operations. Includes instruction in applicable principles of animal science, care, and health; stable and track management; design and operation of facilities and equipment; and related issues such as regulations, business management; and logistics.

abstract: The sustainable management of natural resources under accelerating climate change and anthropogenic pressures requires advanced predictive modeling to inform conservation strategies. This project addresses critical gaps in understanding how complex, large-scale interactions between climate variables, hydrological systems, and terrestrial ecosystems influence biodiversity patterns and resource availability at regional scales. Current models often oversimplify spatial heterogeneity or fail to integrate multi-temporal datasets spanning decades, limiting their utility for adaptive management. We propose to develop a high-resolution computational framework leveraging remotely sensed data (30m resolution), historical climate records, and species occurrence databases to simulate ecosystem responses under multiple climate scenarios (RCP 4.5, 6.0, 8.5). The research employs coupled hydrodynamic and species distribution models (SDMs) with machine learning techniques to predict shifts in habitat suitability for 200+ keystone species and quantify cascading impacts on watershed health. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process 80TB of multispectral imagery, run ensemble microclimate simulations at 1km² granularity, and optimize neural networks for ecological pattern recognition. Parallelized workflows using MPI will accelerate Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses assessing uncertainty in soil-carbon feedback loops and precipitation regime changes. Expected outcomes include: (1) spatially explicit vulnerability maps identifying conservation priority zones in critical biomes; (2) open-source algorithms for real-time drought-flood risk assessment integrating USGS streamflow data; and (3) predictive metrics quantifying trade-offs between forest carbon sequestration capacity and water resource sustainability. By enabling unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution in coupled human-natural system modeling, this work will directly support state agencies in revising habitat conservation plans and allocating climate resilience funding. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a replicable framework for interdisciplinary resource management studies across diverse ecological regions.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the studies and activities relating to the natural environment and its conservation, use, and improvement. Includes instruction in subjects such as climate, air, soil, water, land, fish and wildlife, and plant resources; in the basic principles of environmental science and natural resources management; and the recreational and economic uses of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in intellectual property (IP) law, specifically focusing on the computational analysis of patent litigation dynamics and their implications for innovation policy. The exponential growth of global patent filings, coupled with the increasing complexity of patent disputes involving emerging technologies (e.g., AI-generated inventions, CRISPR-based biotech innovations), has created a pressing need for advanced computational tools to model litigation risks, predict case outcomes, and assess systemic biases within IP adjudication systems. Traditional legal research methods struggle to process the scale and interdependencies of multi-jurisdictional patent data, including millions of litigation records, patent office decisions, and technology-specific claim language. This project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze patent claim construction trends across U.S., European, and Asian jurisdictions, combined with graph-based network analysis to map relationships between litigants, expert witnesses, and technical subject matter. Machine learning models will be trained on historical litigation datasets to identify predictors of case outcomes, while agent-based simulations will evaluate how proposed policy reforms might impact innovation ecosystems. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for NLP corpus analysis (patent texts, court opinions), high-memory nodes for graph database operations linking 10M+ legal entities, and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible computational framework for assessing patent litigation risks in emerging technology sectors, (2) evidence-based policy recommendations for balancing patent enforcement with open innovation principles, and (3) novel methodologies for applying HPC resources to complex legal system analysis. By bridging computational science and IP law, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven legal research while informing critical debates about how intellectual property regimes can adapt to 21st-century technological realities.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations related to copyrights, patents, trademarks, trade secrets, and related issues. Includes instruction in patent law, copyright law, trademark law, intellectual property licensing and litigation, and applications such as art and entertainment law, communications law, information technology law, sports law, and chemical and biotech patent law.

abstract: Agricultural and food product processing faces critical challenges in optimizing efficiency, preserving nutritional quality, and ensuring safety while scaling operations to meet global demand. Traditional experimental approaches to evaluate processing parameters—such as thermal treatments, mechanical operations, and storage logistics—are resource-intensive and limited in their ability to predict complex interactions between variables. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale processes in agricultural product transformation, with a focus on nutrient retention, microbial safety, and energy efficiency. We will develop physics-based simulations (e.g., computational fluid dynamics for thermal processing, discrete element modeling for granular flow during drying) coupled with machine learning to predict outcomes under varying operational conditions. Key applications include optimizing pasteurization protocols for dairy products to minimize heat damage while ensuring pathogen reduction, and simulating starch-protein interactions in plant-based meat alternatives to improve texture and shelf stability. Large-scale parameter sweeps will identify optimal processing windows, reducing experimental trial costs by 40–60%. The HPC environment is essential for handling high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets, parallelizing multibody simulations, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous data (e.g., hyperspectral imaging, rheological measurements). Outcomes will provide actionable insights for designing energy-efficient processing systems, mitigating post-harvest losses, and enhancing the nutritional profile of value-added products. This work aligns with global food security priorities by advancing scalable, data-driven solutions for sustainable agricultural processing. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated computations and large-memory nodes to manage datasets exceeding 50 TB, enabling unprecedented resolution in modeling agricultural processing systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, inspect, store, process, and package agricultural products in the form of human food consumables, animal or plant food, or other industrial products. Includes instruction in the nutrient and industrial properties of various agricultural products; logistics and storage procedures; chemical and mechanical processing operations; packaging; safety and health requirements; and related technical and business principles.

abstract: Land use planning requires balancing complex socio-economic needs with environmental sustainability, particularly under intensifying pressures from urbanization and climate change. Current decision-making tools often lack the capacity to integrate high-resolution spatial data, dynamic environmental feedbacks, and stakeholder priorities at regional scales. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing land use strategies that maximize ecosystem resilience, economic viability, and equitable resource access. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to parameterize and run spatially explicit agent-based models simulating land use change under diverse climate, policy, and market scenarios. These models will integrate geospatial datasets (e.g., soil health, hydrological networks, biodiversity corridors) with econometric projections and participatory inputs from regional planners. Machine learning techniques will identify non-linear relationships between land use patterns and outcomes such as carbon sequestration, flood risk, and agricultural-urban land value trade-offs. Computational demands arise from fine-grained spatial simulations (1 km² resolution) across multi-decadal time horizons, requiring parallelized model ensembles to quantify uncertainties. Outcomes will include open-source tools for scenario testing, policy briefs on cost-effective conservation-development balances, and a decision support system prioritizing adaptive management in vulnerable watersheds. By enabling rapid analysis of trade-offs between competing land use objectives, this work will directly inform state and municipal climate adaptation plans while advancing computational methods for coupled human-natural systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving sufficient temporal and spatial granularity to guide actionable policies, reducing reliance on heuristic approaches in land use governance.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Land Use Planning and Management/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how public and/or private land and associated resources can be preserved, developed, and used for maximum social, economic, and environmental benefit. Includes instruction in natural resources management, natural resource economics, public policy, regional and land use planning, environmental impact assessment, applicable law and regulations, government and politics, principles of business and real estate land use, statistical and analytical tools, computer applications, mapping and report preparation, site analysis, cost analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to advance predictive modeling and risk assessment in building inspection processes. Current inspection protocols often rely on reactive, manual evaluations, which can miss latent structural vulnerabilities or material degradation patterns. To address this, the research will integrate computational simulations with real-world inspection data to create predictive models capable of identifying high-risk failure points in residential and commercial structures. The core computational challenge lies in processing large-scale datasets—including 3D building scans, material property databases, and historical inspection records—while simulating complex physical behaviors (e.g., stress distribution, moisture intrusion, thermal expansion) under diverse environmental conditions. Leveraging HPC resources, we will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) models to assess structural integrity across multi-physics domains, combined with machine learning algorithms trained on failure case histories to prioritize inspection targets. The workflows will utilize open-source tools like OpenFOAM and TensorFlow, optimized for distributed computing architectures to handle iterative simulations and probabilistic risk calculations. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational platform that quantifies failure probabilities for critical building components, identifies inspection priorities based on dynamic risk thresholds, and generates actionable reports for inspectors. This system aims to reduce oversight gaps in aging infrastructure, improve compliance with evolving building codes, and mitigate safety hazards. By transitioning inspection practices from periodic checklists to data-driven, predictive analytics, the project aligns with national efforts to enhance urban resilience and adaptive building management. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary computational scale, enabling rapid scenario testing across heterogeneous building types and environmental variables while maintaining fidelity to real-world inspection constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply industrial, labor, and governmental standards and laws to the oversight of construction projects and the maintenance of completed buildings and other structures. Includes instruction in construction processes and techniques, materials analysis, occupational safety and health, industry standards, building codes and specifications, blueprint interpretation, testing equipment and procedures, communication skills, accident investigation, and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance costume design processes by integrating dynamic simulation, material behavior modeling, and historical data analysis. Costume designers face challenges in predicting how fabrics and materials will interact with performers’ bodies under varied movement conditions, particularly for complex productions requiring period-accurate designs or physically demanding performances. Traditional prototyping methods are time-intensive and resource-heavy, limiting iterative experimentation. This research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate fabric dynamics, stress distributions, and ergonomic interactions in virtual environments, enabling rapid, data-driven design iterations. The computational approach will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for material deformation modeling, machine learning algorithms trained on historical costume datasets to predict stylistic and functional constraints, and motion capture data to simulate performer-specific biomechanical interactions. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce simulation times for multi-layered garments and large ensembles from weeks to hours. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for simulating costume performance metrics (e.g., durability, mobility, thermal comfort) and a database linking historical design patterns to computational parameters. This work will empower designers to optimize aesthetics and functionality while minimizing physical prototyping waste, advancing sustainability in theatrical production. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time rendering of 3D garment simulations and high-memory nodes for processing large-scale motion datasets. By bridging computational engineering and performing arts, this project establishes a novel paradigm for interdisciplinary research in costume design, with potential applications in education, archival preservation, and adaptive design for diverse body types.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and select costumes for characters in theatre and the performing arts and to serve as part of a production team. Includes instruction in costume design, script analysis, theory and criticism, period styles, history of costume, stage makeup, rendering, and costume construction.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and fitting of patient-specific orthotic and prosthetic devices using high-performance computing (HPC). Current clinical practices rely heavily on manual adjustments and static biomechanical models, which often fail to account for dynamic, individualized factors such as tissue compliance, gait variability, and real-time pressure distribution. These limitations contribute to suboptimal device performance, prolonged fitting processes, and increased risk of secondary musculoskeletal complications. To address this, we propose integrating multi-scale biomechanical simulations, machine learning (ML), and patient-specific sensor data to predict device-patient interactions under dynamic conditions. HPC resources will enable finite element analysis (FEA) modeling of tissue-device interfaces at unprecedented resolution, coupled with ML-driven optimization of device geometry and material properties. Sensor-derived gait and pressure data from wearable devices will inform boundary conditions for simulations, ensuring alignment with real-world biomechanical loads. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine designs by minimizing interfacial stresses, maximizing functional alignment, and incorporating patient-reported comfort metrics. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for generating patient-optimized orthotic/prosthetic designs, reducing iterative fitting sessions by 30–50%, and improving long-term user mobility outcomes. This work bridges gaps in personalized assistive device design by merging clinical orthotics/prosthetics with computational engineering, advancing a niche area within health sciences that remains underserved by traditional analytical methods. The resulting open-source tools will empower clinicians to leverage computational insights during device customization, fostering translation of HPC-driven innovation into routine care. By addressing the intersection of biomechanics, materials science, and data science, this project establishes a paradigm for computational resource applications in specialized health technology domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: The proliferation of decentralized, user-driven information ecosystems—such as community-maintained knowledge repositories and crowdsourced crisis response platforms—has created urgent challenges in ensuring the integrity and resilience of dynamically evolving data. Traditional centralized moderation and verification frameworks struggle to adapt to the scale, real-time demands, and distributed governance of these systems. This project seeks to model and analyze emergent self-correction behaviors in such environments, leveraging computational social science methods to identify design principles that enhance organic error detection without stifling participatory engagement. The research employs large-scale agent-based simulations to replicate heterogeneous user interactions, misinformation diffusion patterns, and collaborative editing dynamics within synthetic information networks. These simulations integrate empirical data from case studies of existing platforms, including temporal metadata and user reputation graphs, to parameterize agent decision-making algorithms. High-performance computing resources are critical for executing millions of parallelized simulation runs across diverse network topologies and incentive structures, enabling sensitivity analyses of variables such as trust thresholds, information velocity, and subcommunity formation. Machine learning techniques will then identify robust correlations between platform design features (e.g., transparency mechanisms, contribution weighting systems) and resilience metrics like misinformation decay rates and collective consensus stability. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for evaluating the self-regulatory capacity of decentralized information systems, with applications to the development of adaptive tools for community stewards and policymakers. The work bridges informatics, human-computer interaction, and computational social science, offering novel insights into sustaining information quality in increasingly democratized digital spaces while preserving open collaboration norms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the drivers of phylogenetic discordance and biogeographic patterns in a hyper-diverse clade of tropical angiosperms, integrating large-scale molecular, morphological, and ecological datasets to resolve longstanding uncertainties in evolutionary relationships and diversification processes. A major challenge in systematic biology is reconciling conflicting phylogenetic signals arising from incomplete lineage sorting, hybridization, and convergent trait evolution, particularly in lineages with rapid radiations. To address this, we will employ a computational pipeline combining Bayesian species-tree inference, divergence-time estimation, and comparative methods to analyze genome-scale sequence data (targeted enrichment sequencing), fossil-calibrated trait matrices, and historical biogeographic reconstructions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the project’s scope: datasets include ~2,000 loci across 500+ species, 10,000+ morphological character states, and probabilistic biogeographic models requiring iterative likelihood calculations across millions of tree topologies. Key computational steps include parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for multilocus coalescent models, machine learning-assisted morphological homology assessments, and likelihood-based tests for trait-dependent diversification. The requested resources will enable efficient processing of these analyses, which are otherwise computationally intractable on standard laboratory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a robust, time-calibrated phylogeny resolving contentious nodes in the focal clade, (2) identification of ecological and biogeographic factors correlated with diversification rate shifts, and (3) novel protocols for integrating high-dimensional morphological data into phylogenomic frameworks. This work will advance systematic theory by clarifying how heterogeneous evolutionary processes shape taxonomic diversity in tropical hotspots, while providing open-access computational workflows and a curated database of phenotypic characters to support future studies. Results will directly inform conservation prioritization by identifying evolutionarily distinct lineages in threatened ecosystems.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational modeling of multifactorial ophthalmic diseases, with a focus on optimizing diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for conditions such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration. Current clinical decision-making often relies on static, population-level data, which inadequately captures the dynamic interplay of genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors driving disease progression. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multi-omics integration and personalized risk prediction. The research will leverage federated learning architectures to aggregate anonymized patient data from collaborating optometric clinics, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, visual field tests, and longitudinal electronic health records. Computational workflows will combine deep learning models for image segmentation (e.g., retinal layer thickness quantification) with mechanistic modeling of intraocular pressure dynamics and vascular perfusion metrics. A key innovation involves implementing hybrid graph neural networks to map patient-specific biomarker interactions across temporal and spatial scales. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter optimization for these models while maintaining compliance with healthcare data privacy standards through containerized processing environments. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for disease progression trajectories and a cloud-based decision support tool prototype for clinicians. This resource will directly enhance the precision of optometric care delivery while establishing a scalable computational paradigm for ophthalmic research. The project’s open-source tools and de-identified datasets will be disseminated through partnerships with professional associations, creating infrastructure to advance computational optometry education and practice standards. By bridging HPC capabilities with clinical optometric workflows, this work aims to reduce preventable vision loss through earlier, more individualized interventions.
cip_title: Ophthalmic and Optometric Support Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ophthalmic and optometric support services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced control strategies for autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments, with a focus on optimizing real-time decision-making under computational and energy constraints. The core challenge lies in balancing the high-dimensional sensorimotor processing required for adaptive locomotion and manipulation with the limited onboard computational resources typical of mobile mechatronic platforms. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining physics-informed neural networks for predictive system modeling and distributed optimization algorithms for multi-objective control allocation. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex multi-body dynamics scenarios, train deep reinforcement learning agents through massively parallelized trial batches, and validate control policies across stochastic environmental conditions. Key computational tasks include finite element analysis of compliant actuator arrays, Monte Carlo-based robustness testing of sensor fusion pipelines, and real-time optimization of redundant manipulator trajectories using GPU-accelerated quadratic programming solvers. Expected outcomes include a scalable control architecture that dynamically allocates computational resources based on task criticality, reducing latency in perception-action cycles by 30-50% compared to conventional centralized approaches. The work will directly contribute to enabling resource-efficient autonomous systems for industrial inspection and disaster response applications, while advancing methodological integration of embedded real-time computing with model-based control theory. HPC support is essential given the project’s need for large-scale parameter space exploration, concurrent simulation of heterogeneous robotic fleets, and data-intensive training of multimodal perception models—tasks exceeding the capacity of local laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer controlled electro-mechanical systems and products with embedded electronics, sensors, and actuators; and which includes, but is not limited to, automata, robots and automation systems. Includes instruction in mechanical engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, computer and software engineering, and control engineering.

abstract: Occupational safety and health (OSH) professionals face growing challenges in predicting and mitigating workplace risks due to the complexity of modern industrial environments, where dynamic interactions between personnel, equipment, and hazardous materials complicate traditional risk-assessment models. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate workplace hazard scenarios, optimize safety protocols, and predict emergent risks in real time. The research will focus on modeling exposure to chemical, physical, and ergonomic hazards across diverse settings, including manufacturing, construction, and chemical processing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute agent-based simulations coupling human behavioral dynamics with environmental factors, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of airborne contaminant dispersion, and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics. These multi-scale simulations will integrate real-world sensor data from partner industries to validate and refine models. Key computational challenges include managing large datasets from IoT-enabled safety devices, parallelizing stochastic risk-assessment algorithms, and achieving near-real-time feedback for proactive hazard intervention. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for OSH training and decision support, predictive tools to identify high-risk scenarios before they manifest, and data-driven recommendations for optimizing safety engineering controls. The project will directly advance the program’s mission by equipping safety professionals with evidence-based computational tools to preempt workplace injuries and illnesses, reduce regulatory compliance costs, and adapt safety strategies to evolving industrial technologies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work addresses critical gaps in current OSH methodologies, which often rely on static, retrospective analyses ill-suited to dynamic work environments. All models and datasets will be made available as open-source resources to foster collaboration across academia and industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining job-related health and safety standards. Includes instruction in safety engineering principles, inspection and monitoring procedures, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, applications to specific work environments, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the longitudinal impacts of parent education programs on family dynamics and child development outcomes, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multidimensional interactions. Parent education services aim to enhance caregiving practices and family resilience, yet existing evaluations often rely on small-scale qualitative studies or simplified quantitative metrics that inadequately capture nonlinear relationships between program variables (e.g., cultural adaptation of curricula, parental stress levels, and child behavioral outcomes). The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate heterogeneous family systems under varying intervention scenarios, incorporating real-world data on socioeconomic, cultural, and psychological factors. The computational approach integrates machine learning techniques with dynamic systems modeling to identify critical leverage points in program design. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets from regional parent education initiatives—encompassing demographic records, pre/post-intervention surveys, and third-party social service metrics—the models will simulate how micro-level interactions between caregivers, children, and educators propagate to macro-level outcomes over time. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, perform sensitivity analyses across diverse virtual populations, and optimize intervention strategies via parallelized Monte Carlo simulations. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive toolkit for program administrators to tailor parent education content to specific community needs, prioritize resource allocation, and forecast long-term impacts on child well-being metrics. By mapping the cascading effects of program variables in culturally nuanced contexts, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in family support systems while demonstrating the transformative potential of computational social science in non-STEM domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, coordinate, and teach parent education programs and services that address the cultural, emotional, intellectual, physical and social needs of children and parents. Includes instruction in child development, cultural diversity in schools, child behavior, family development, family-community partnerships, family dynamics, interpersonal relationships, parent-child relationships, and social services.

abstract: Audio engineering technology faces growing challenges in achieving high-fidelity, low-latency processing for real-time applications such as immersive soundscapes, live performance augmentation, and adaptive acoustic environments. This project seeks to develop advanced computational models for audio signal manipulation and spatialization that require high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inherent complexities in temporal resolution, multi-channel synchronization, and nonlinear acoustic phenomena. The research will implement parallelized algorithms for machine learning-based audio synthesis using generative adversarial networks (GANs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), optimized through GPU-accelerated frameworks. Concurrently, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations will model wave propagation in complex environments at unprecedented spatial resolutions, enabling precise prediction of room acoustics and material interactions. These computational approaches will be validated against experimental data from controlled studio environments and field recordings. The integration of HPC resources will allow simultaneous optimization of psychoacoustic parameters and physical acoustic modeling at scales impractical for desktop computing. Expected outcomes include novel hybrid architectures for real-time audio processing, open-source tools for spatial audio rendering, and fundamental insights into the relationship between computational precision and perceptual audio quality. This work will directly advance capabilities in music production, virtual/augmented reality systems, and intelligent audio interfaces while establishing methodological frameworks for computational audio engineering. The requested resources will support critical benchmarks in processing efficiency, including sub-millisecond latency targets for interactive applications and high-resolution acoustic simulations exceeding 10 million grid points, which are essential for next-generation audio technologies.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the mixing, recording, and production of music. Includes instruction in acoustics, audio mixing, audio production, audio recording, computer composition of music, music theory, digital devices, and sound technology.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of glacial retreat dynamics and their impact on landscape evolution through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled modeling of ice-sheet hydrology and sediment transport. Current models of glacial systems often simplify subglacial processes, limiting their ability to predict how meltwater drainage and bedrock erosion interact to influence ice flow stability and post-glacial landform development. To address this gap, we propose a coupled numerical framework integrating 3D ice dynamics, distributed subglacial hydrology, and sediment advection—processes that operate across scales from meters to kilometers. The model will leverage finite-element discretization and parallelized solvers to resolve feedbacks between basal water pressure, sediment lubrication, and ice velocity at unprecedented spatial resolution (10–100 m grid scales) across multi-decadal timescales. Simulations will be validated against geomorphological field data from deglaciated regions in Alaska and Greenland, including sediment flux estimates and landform morphology. The computational demands of this approach are substantial, requiring access to HPC resources for ensemble runs to quantify parameter sensitivity and uncertainty under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a mechanistic understanding of how sediment availability modulates ice sheet response to warming, (2) predictive maps of erosion hotspots that drive fjord formation and sediment deposition, and (3) open-source model components for community use. Results will inform projections of landscape resilience and hydrogeological changes in glaciated regions, with direct relevance to water resource management and geohazard mitigation. The scale-resolving simulations proposed are computationally intractable without HPC allocation, as individual transient runs demand ~200,000 core-hours to capture nonlinear process couplings across 50+ years of modeled time.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origin and evolution of topographic features created by physical, chemical or biological processes operating at or near the Earth's surface, including glaciers.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and model the acquisition of French grammatical structures among second language (L2) learners, with the goal of informing adaptive pedagogical strategies. A key challenge in teaching French as a foreign language lies in addressing persistent errors in complex grammatical areas such as verb conjugation, gender agreement, and syntactic negation. Traditional pedagogical assessments often lack the granularity to identify nuanced, learner-specific error patterns across diverse cohorts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets of learner interactions—including written assignments, speech recordings, and real-time classroom response data—from over 5,000 intermediate-level students. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be optimized to annotate errors, classify their linguistic sources, and map developmental trajectories using transformer-based models. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model the efficacy of different instructional interventions under varying learner profiles. The computational workload necessitates parallelized processing of text and audio data, large-scale parameter sweeps for simulation calibration, and training of ensemble models to predict error persistence. Expected outcomes include (1) a corpus of annotated learner errors with associated pedagogical recommendations, (2) evidence-based guidelines for personalizing grammar instruction based on learner cognition patterns, and (3) open-source tools for automated error detection integrated into teacher training modules. By elucidating the dynamics of French grammatical acquisition at unprecedented scale, this work aims to equip educators with data-driven strategies to reduce fossilized errors and accelerate proficiency. The project directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance French language teaching through innovative, empirically grounded methodologies.
cip_title: Teaching French as a Second or Foreign Language
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching French to students who are not proficient in French or who do not speak, read, or write French, and prepares individuals to serve as teachers and administrators.

abstract: Interior design faces growing complexity in balancing aesthetic, functional, and environmental demands within residential and commercial spaces, particularly as sustainability standards and user-centric design expectations escalate. Current workflows struggle to integrate multi-physics simulations—such as lighting, acoustics, thermal dynamics, and material performance—into iterative design processes, often relying on fragmented tools or oversimplified approximations. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable holistic, real-time analysis of interior environments, optimizing spatial configurations, material selections, and systems integration under dynamic constraints. The research will develop parallelized workflows using ray-tracing algorithms for photorealistic lighting simulations, finite element analysis (FEA) for acoustic and thermal modeling, and machine learning (ML) to predict occupant comfort metrics across diverse design scenarios. By coupling these methods within a parametric design platform, the system will iteratively generate and evaluate thousands of design variants, correlating aesthetic choices (e.g., color coordination, furniture layouts) with quantifiable performance data (energy efficiency, ergonomic compliance). HPC resources are critical to process high-resolution 3D models, simulate complex interactions between design variables, and train ML models on heterogeneous datasets spanning historical style databases, textile properties, and building code regulations. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable simulation toolkit for interior designers, validated against physical prototypes, that reduces reliance on trial-and-error approaches while enhancing compliance with sustainability certifications. This work bridges gaps between traditional design practices and computational engineering, offering new methodologies to address spatial equity, adaptive reuse, and climate-responsive interiors. The resulting open-source frameworks will be tested on case studies ranging from mixed-use urban developments to healthcare environments, with implications for advancing evidence-based design pedagogy and industry standards.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional planning, designing, equipping, and furnishing of residential and commercial interior spaces. Includes instruction in computer applications, drafting, and graphic techniques; principles of interior lighting, acoustics, systems integration, and color coordination; furniture and furnishings; textiles and their finishing; the history of interior design and period styles; basic structural design; building codes and inspection regulations; and applications to office, hotel, factory, restaurant and housing design.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing crop yield and resilience under increasing environmental stressors, including climate variability, emerging pest resistance, and soil degradation. Traditional approaches to modeling crop responses to these variables often lack the resolution to account for complex interactions between genomic traits, microclimate conditions, and agronomic practices. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating high-throughput genomic data, real-time environmental sensor inputs, and multi-scale crop growth models. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify genotype-environment-management (G×E×M) interactions predictive of stress tolerance and yield outcomes, while agent-based models will simulate pest and pathogen spread under projected climate scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of hyperspectral imaging data from field trials, execute parallelized genomic prediction models across diverse crop varieties, and run ensemble climate simulations at regional scales. Expected outcomes include the development of a decision-support tool for dynamically optimizing irrigation, fertilization, and pest management strategies, validated against experimental data from partner farms. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets linking crop genomic markers to stress resilience traits, enabling faster breeding cycles. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance precision agriculture frameworks that enhance resource efficiency, reduce chemical inputs, and stabilize production in variable climates, directly supporting food security priorities. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other staple crops, amplifying their long-term impact across agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cultivate grain, fiber, forage, oilseed, fruits and nuts, vegetables, and other domesticated plant products. Includes instruction in basic principles of plant science, health, and nutrition as applied to particular species and breeds; soil preparation and irrigation; pest management; planting and harvesting operations; product marketing; and applicable issues of safety, regulation, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of understudied Semitic languages, focusing on morphosyntactic variation across modern and historical dialects of Aramaic, Geʿez, and Neo-Arabic. While these languages hold significant cultural and historical value, their complex morphological systems and limited digital corpora pose challenges for traditional linguistic analysis. Current tools, optimized for widely spoken languages, fail to capture the intricate root-and-pattern structures and dialectal diversity characteristic of Semitic languages. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to develop scalable algorithms for automated morphological parsing, syntactic annotation, and dialect classification. Using transformer-based models adapted for low-resource scenarios, we will process multilingual textual datasets spanning epigraphic inscriptions, medieval manuscripts, and modern speech recordings. Parallelized workflows will enable large-scale comparative analyses of linguistic features across temporal and geographic dimensions, while GPU-accelerated training will optimize model performance for agglutinative morphologies. The computational pipeline will integrate variational autoencoders to reconstruct unattested proto-forms and simulate language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for Semitic language processing, a diachronic corpus annotated with syntactic trees and morphological features, and quantitative models of language change dynamics. These resources will empower scholars to test hypotheses about language diffusion in the Near East while preserving endangered linguistic heritage. The project’s computational demands—including terabyte-scale dataset storage, distributed training across multilingual models, and real-time simulation of language evolution pathways—necessitate dedicated HPC resources beyond standard institutional capacities. By bridging computational linguistics and Semitic philology, this work aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing non-configurational languages while advancing digital humanities infrastructure for under-resourced linguistic traditions.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Middle/ Near Eastern and Semitic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical training environments face challenges in balancing educational quality with patient safety, particularly in high-stakes, unpredictable clinical scenarios. Traditional simulation-based training methods are resource-intensive and struggle to replicate the dynamic decision-making required in real-world settings. This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven clinical training platform that generates adaptive, personalized simulation scenarios using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on optimizing scenario complexity, learner assessment granularity, and ethical constraints in AI-generated clinical training modules. We propose a computational approach combining reinforcement learning (RL) agents with multi-scale physiological modeling to simulate patient responses, clinical workflow interactions, and educator feedback systems. The platform will integrate natural language processing for real-time analysis of learner-clinical instructor dialogues and computer vision techniques for procedural skill assessment. HPC resources will enable parallel training of multiple RL agents across diverse clinical specialties (emergency medicine, surgery, critical care) while maintaining the fidelity required for educational validity. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying clinical reasoning development through interpretable AI metrics, predictive models of competency trajectory across training phases, and evidence-based guidelines for AI-mediated scenario personalization. This work addresses a critical gap in health professions education by creating scalable, data-driven tools that enhance clinical decision-making training without compromising patient care standards. The computational infrastructure will support validation studies comparing AI-generated simulations with traditional methods across six clinical disciplines, ultimately advancing our understanding of how adaptive technologies can transform competency assessment and curriculum design in health professions education.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on education and administration leadership skills for clinical educators across health professions and specialties. Includes instruction in academic leadership, assessment, clinical decision making, curriculum development, ethics, primary care education, program evaluation, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of chronic lifestyle-related conditions has highlighted the need for personalized health optimization strategies that integrate real-time physiological, behavioral, and environmental data. Current approaches to individualized wellness planning lack the computational capacity to model complex, dynamic interactions between biometric signals, activity patterns, and contextual factors at scale. This project proposes the development of an adaptive digital twin framework to simulate personalized health trajectories and optimize intervention strategies using high-resolution data from wearable devices, geospatial inputs, and multi-omics profiles. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to implement agent-based modeling and hybrid machine learning architectures capable of processing heterogeneous temporal datasets (sampled at 1-100Hz across modalities) while maintaining individual privacy constraints. Computational challenges include synchronizing irregular time-series streams, resolving feature interactions across biological scales (e.g., heart rate variability to microbiome composition), and implementing reinforcement learning for dynamic intervention adjustments. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition techniques and federated learning protocols to address these challenges while scaling to cohorts of 10,000 simulated individuals. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for predicting individualized responses to lifestyle modifications, identification of novel digital biomarkers for metabolic resilience, and optimization algorithms for timing nutrition/exercise interventions based on circadian and contextual factors. This work will provide a foundation for next-generation wellness tools that empower health professionals to design data-driven, adaptive prevention strategies while addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in multi-scale health modeling. Successful implementation will directly inform the development of scalable decision-support systems for use in corporate wellness programs, fitness platforms, and community health initiatives.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to assume roles as health/wellness professionals in private business and industry, community organizations, and health care settings. Includes instruction in personal health, community health and welfare, nutrition, epidemiology, disease prevention, fitness and exercise, and health behaviors.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate community-level interventions addressing systemic inequities in access to social services, with a focus on housing instability and mental health disparities. Social work research faces unique challenges in evaluating multi-agency interventions due to the dynamic interactions between individuals, institutions, and policies. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture nonlinear feedback loops, resource allocation trade-offs, and emergent outcomes in complex social systems. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build large-scale simulations that integrate anonymized administrative data from public health departments, homeless shelters, and community mental health providers. The ABM will model decision-making processes of individuals navigating service systems alongside organizational behaviors under varying policy constraints. Computational demands arise from the need to simulate heterogeneous populations (N ≈ 100,000 agents) with detailed interaction rules, longitudinal time horizons (10+ simulated years), and sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations. The model will be implemented using Python-based Mesa frameworks optimized for parallel processing, with validation against longitudinal outcomes data from three urban counties. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for improving service coordination, quantifying threshold effects in resource allocation, and generating policy test scenarios for crisis response systems. This work directly supports evidence-based decision-making in public administration by creating a virtual laboratory to assess equity impacts of proposed interventions before implementation. The requested computing resources are essential given the memory-intensive nature of tracking multidimensional disadvantage indicators across large populations and the need for rapid iteration with community partners.
cip_definition: Any program providing instruction in social work and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Diseases of the ear and temporal bone, such as Meniere’s disease, vestibular schwannomas, and otosclerosis, present significant clinical challenges due to the complex anatomy and physiological variability of the inner ear. Current treatment strategies often rely on generalized approaches, which may fail to account for patient-specific biomechanical, hydrodynamic, or neurophysiological factors that influence disease progression and therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop patient-specific computational models of the inner ear and temporal bone, enabling precision medicine approaches for neurotological disorders. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating high-resolution finite element models of the cochlea, vestibular system, and surrounding structures to simulate biomechanical responses to surgical interventions or implantable devices, and (2) integrating fluid-structure interaction simulations with clinical imaging and electrophysiological data to predict functional outcomes of therapies for hearing and balance disorders. Computational workflows will utilize patient-derived CT/MRI data to construct anatomically accurate models, while machine learning algorithms will analyze multimodal datasets to identify biomarkers of disease progression. The scale and resolution required for these simulations—particularly the need to resolve micron-scale structures and millisecond-level dynamic processes—demand significant parallel processing capabilities and large-scale memory allocation, necessitating HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive frameworks to optimize cochlear implant placement, improve vestibular prosthesis design, and personalize surgical planning for tumor resection. By bridging computational biomechanics with clinical neurotology, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven treatment personalization, reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. The resulting models and tools will be disseminated to the broader research community, fostering collaboration in computational otology and accelerating translational innovations for hearing and balance disorders.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat diseases of the ear and temporal bone, including disorders of hearing and balance.

abstract: This project seeks to address the scalability challenges inherent in deploying adaptive learning technologies for diverse educational contexts. While personalized learning systems show promise in improving student outcomes, their effectiveness is constrained by computational limitations in processing high-dimensional, multimodal data—including interaction logs, biometric signals, and multimedia artifacts—in real time. Current systems often rely on simplified student models that fail to capture the complexity of individual learning pathways, particularly in large-scale or heterogeneous classrooms. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for dynamic learner modeling and intervention design. The computational approach integrates deep reinforcement learning architectures to model student knowledge states and predict optimal instructional sequences, trained on terabyte-scale datasets of anonymized student interactions from existing learning management systems. Parallelized simulations will test the efficacy of adaptive interventions across synthetic classroom environments representing varied demographic, curricular, and technological conditions. The HPC infrastructure will enable 1) rapid retraining of models as new data streams are incorporated, 2) hyperparameter optimization for context-specific implementations, and 3) real-time sensitivity analyses of proposed pedagogical strategies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scalable learning analytics, validated through benchmarking against traditional adaptive systems using metrics of learning gain, engagement, and equity of outcomes. This work will advance evidence-based practices for AI-driven educational technologies while establishing computational pipelines for ethical, large-scale experimentation in digital learning environments. By demonstrating how HPC resources can overcome current bottlenecks in educational data science, the project aims to foster new collaborations between learning researchers and computational scientists.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, computer applications, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Slavic cultural and linguistic heritage through the lens of digital humanities. The research focuses on identifying and mapping understudied patterns in the migration and adaptation of Slavic cultural narratives across time and space, particularly within diasporic communities. Traditional methods in Slavic Studies have been limited by the scale and complexity of multilingual textual corpora, fragmented archival materials, and non-linear cultural exchange dynamics. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze digitized collections of folklore, oral histories, and literary works in multiple Slavic languages (e.g., Ukrainian, Serbian, and Czech) alongside metadata from diaspora publications and community records. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for cross-lingual semantic alignment, network analysis of narrative motifs, and geospatial modeling of cultural diffusion pathways. These methods require HPC infrastructure to manage large-scale parallel processing of heterogeneous datasets (spanning 10+ TB), optimize multilingual model training, and run iterative simulations of cultural transmission scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized transnational narrative networks, a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated materials, and methodological frameworks for computationally tracing non-institutional cultural preservation practices. By integrating computational rigor with area-specific expertise, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of how diasporic Slavic communities negotiate cultural identity in transnational contexts while establishing scalable tools for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of cultural studies and data science.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Slavic peoples inhabiting Europe, Asia, and in immigrant groups elsewhere, including the study of the emergence and migration patterns of Slavic culture, languages, and populations.

abstract: The rapid advancement of semiconductor technologies demands increasingly sophisticated integrated circuit (IC) designs that balance power efficiency, thermal management, and performance in nanoscale architectures. However, traditional circuit simulation and optimization tools struggle to model quantum effects, process variations, and electromagnetic interactions at sub-10nm nodes with sufficient accuracy, leading to suboptimal designs and prolonged development cycles. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, multi-physics simulations and machine learning-driven design automation. The research will focus on developing a computational framework that integrates finite-element analysis for thermal and electromagnetic modeling, Monte Carlo simulations for statistical variation analysis, and neural networks to accelerate design space exploration. Key objectives include optimizing transistor-level layouts to mitigate leakage currents, predicting interconnect crosstalk in 3D-stacked ICs, and automating analog circuit synthesis under process-voltage-temperature (PVT) constraints. HPC resources are critical to parallelize computationally intensive tasks such as parameter sweeps across thousands of design variants, transient simulations of mixed-signal circuits, and training of surrogate models for real-time performance prediction. Expected outcomes include novel design methodologies that reduce power consumption by 15–20% in target applications such as edge-computing devices and 5G transceivers, as well as open-source tools to bridge the gap between academic research and industrial design flows. By enabling high-fidelity simulations of emerging materials (e.g., gallium nitride) and non-von Neumann architectures, this work will advance the scalability of IC design tools while providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-accelerated electronic design automation, fostering workforce readiness in semiconductor innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to design circuits in microelectronics. Includes instruction in circuit design, circuit layout, circuit analysis, computer-aided drafting, and semi-conductor technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and physiological mechanisms underlying yoga therapy interventions for chronic musculoskeletal pain management. While yoga therapy is increasingly integrated into clinical care, its biomechanical efficacy remains undercharacterized due to the complexity of modeling dynamic, multi-joint postures and their systemic effects. Current limitations in computational power restrict simulations to isolated muscle groups or static poses, failing to capture real-time interactions between neuromuscular activation, joint kinematics, and cardiovascular responses during therapeutic yoga sequences. Our research will develop a multiscale computational framework integrating finite element modeling of connective tissue stress distribution, agent-based simulations of proprioceptive feedback loops, and computational fluid dynamics of hemodynamic adaptations during sustained asanas. These models will be parameterized using motion capture data from certified yoga therapists and synchronized biometric data (EMG, pulse transit time) collected during therapeutic sessions. Machine learning algorithms will identify posture-specific load redistribution patterns and predict individualized risk-benefit thresholds for patients with degenerative joint conditions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the high dimensionality of spatiotemporal data across scales, enabling real-time coupling of musculoskeletal dynamics with autonomic nervous system responses. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive platform for optimizing yoga therapy protocols based on patient-specific biomechanical profiles, advancing the evidence base for yoga as a precision intervention. This work bridges computational physiology and integrative health paradigms, establishing a novel methodological framework for quantifying mind-body therapies in clinical contexts while addressing critical gaps in non-pharmacological pain management research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional instructors in the spiritual and physical therapy of Yoga in private, institutional, and clinical settings. Includes instruction in the principles of Ayurveda, philosophy of Yoga, warm-up and progressive exercises, breathing exercises, meditation, Yamas and Niyamas, instructional techniques, posture adjustment, student/client counseling and assessment, advanced Yoga disciplines and styles, business practices, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation in K-12 school districts through computational modeling of administrative decision-making processes. School systems face dynamic pressures, including fluctuating enrollments, budget constraints, and equity mandates, yet traditional analytical tools often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between these variables. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework to model how district-level policies—such as staffing ratios, facility investments, and curriculum mandates—propagate through school networks and influence long-term outcomes. The model will integrate historical administrative data (e.g., budget records, student performance metrics, and staffing patterns) with machine learning techniques to predict emergent behaviors under varying policy scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to running thousands of parallel simulations that account for stochastic variables like demographic shifts and funding volatility, enabling sensitivity analyses at a scale impractical on local infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool that identifies resource allocation strategies to balance equity, efficiency, and academic performance. This work will advance leadership practices in educational administration by providing empirically grounded frameworks for anticipating second-order effects of policy choices. By quantifying trade-offs in multi-objective optimization problems inherent to district management, the project aims to reduce trial-and-error decision-making and foster data-driven governance. The computational pipeline developed here will be adaptable to diverse administrative contexts, offering a template for integrating systems thinking into educational leadership.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in education administration and supervision, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of micro-scale mechanical systems in modern horology and jewelry design demands advanced computational tools to model material behaviors, optimize precision manufacturing, and predict long-term performance. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the simulation of micromechanical interactions within watch components and jewelry structures, particularly those involving sub-millimeter parts, heterogeneous material interfaces, and dynamic stress patterns. Current limitations in desktop computing restrict the resolution and timescales achievable when modeling phenomena such as crystalline lattice deformation in gemstone settings, wear patterns in escapement mechanisms, or thermal gradients during laser soldering of delicate alloys. Our research will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate atomic-scale adhesion in brazing joints, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution mapping in engraved surfaces, and machine learning (ML)-accelerated optimization of casting parameters for precious metal alloys. These simulations will integrate experimental data from micro-CT scans of historical timepieces and spectroscopic analysis of failed jewelry components to validate computational models. The HPC environment will enable parametric studies across material combinations (e.g., steel-titanium interfaces in watch cases) and operational conditions (e.g., temperature cycling impacts on lubricant viscosity in gear trains). Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for material fatigue in micro-engraving tools, generative design algorithms for weight-optimized bracelet links, and digital twins of antique watch movements to guide restoration protocols. By bridging traditional craftsmanship with computational engineering, this work aims to establish new standards for precision in horological component lifespan prediction and jewelry structural integrity assessment, while developing open-source simulation toolkits tailored to artisan manufacturing contexts. The requested resources will directly support 12 novel case studies across horological complications and avant-garde jewelry forms, with implications for conserving heritage techniques and advancing sustainable material use in luxury goods production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make repairs, and maintain timepieces, time-measuring devices, and jewelry items. Includes instruction in mechanical timekeeping systems, digital timekeeping systems, timesetting, casting, engraving, polishing, stonesetting, soldering, fine microscopic work, equipment and tool maintenance, redesign and restyling techniques, and customer relations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven optimization framework to enhance decision-making efficiency in executive support systems, focusing on dynamic scheduling, communication prioritization, and resource coordination for high-level administrative workflows. While current tools for executive assistants rely on static rulesets or manual input, the increasing complexity of multi-stakeholder engagements, real-time data streams, and geographically distributed operations demands computational approaches capable of adaptive, context-aware planning. The core challenge lies in modeling hierarchical priorities (e.g., strategic corporate objectives vs. individual executive preferences) while balancing constraints such as privacy protocols, cross-departmental dependencies, and emergent disruptions. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose a hybrid architecture combining federated learning for confidential data handling, graph neural networks to map evolving stakeholder relationships, and multi-objective reinforcement learning for scenario simulation. Computational experiments will utilize anonymized historical datasets of executive meeting logs, communication patterns, and enterprise resource calendars to train models that predict optimal intervention points in scheduling conflicts, automate context-sensitive task delegation, and simulate the downstream effects of administrative decisions on organizational workflows. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for ethical AI-assisted executive support, validated through benchmark comparisons against traditional methods in simulated crisis response and cross-continental event coordination scenarios. By quantifying how computational resource allocation correlates with administrative agility in high-stakes business environments, this work aims to establish new metrics for evaluating AI readiness in executive operations—a critical yet understudied factor in organizational resilience. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale parallelism for hyperparameter optimization across diverse corporate governance models and real-time stress-testing of decision pipelines under synthetic disruption scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and/or personal secretaries for business executives and top management. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, public relations, scheduling and travel management, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, conference and meeting recording, report preparation, office equipment and procedures, office supervisory skills, and professional standards and legal requirements.

abstract: The management of surgical and medical conditions in large animals presents unique challenges due to their physiological complexity, limited species-specific datasets, and the economic implications of suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to address the high variability in post-surgical recovery and treatment efficacy in food animals and equines by developing predictive computational models to optimize clinical decision-making. A critical barrier lies in integrating multi-modal data—including high-resolution imaging, real-time biometrics, genomic markers, and longitudinal health records—into actionable insights. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning (ML) models on heterogeneous datasets from bovine, porcine, and equine patients. These models will identify risk factors for complications such as post-operative infections, anesthetic adverse events, and delayed healing, while simulating outcomes under varying treatment protocols. Computational workflows will include deep learning for image analysis (e.g., CT/MRI-based lesion localization), graph neural networks to model disease progression, and ensemble methods to account for interspecies anatomical and metabolic differences. The scale of data (10+ TB of imaging, 100,000+ clinical records) and the need for real-time parameter optimization in iterative simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated training. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide personalized surgical planning, targeted prophylactic interventions, and early complication detection, directly reducing morbidity and mortality in production and sport animals. By establishing an open-access computational framework, this work will advance translational veterinary research, enhance food security through improved livestock health, and provide a template for data-driven precision medicine in non-model species.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Large Animal/ Food Animal and Equine Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of herd, work, sport, and food animals. Includes instruction in equine medicine, swine and dairy medicine, food animal medicine, pathophysiology, large animal diseases, large animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: The spread of invasive ant species poses significant ecological and economic threats, disrupting native ecosystems and agricultural systems worldwide.
