Current predictive models often fail to capture the nuanced role of microclimatic variability—such as transient temperature gradients and soil moisture fluctuations—in shaping invasive ant colonization success. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, spatiotemporal modeling framework to quantify how microclimatic dynamics at sub-meter scales influence the establishment and spread of invasive ant populations in heterogeneous landscapes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning (ML)-driven environmental data assimilation to simulate colony behavior, resource foraging, and interspecies competition under dynamically varying microhabitat conditions. Field-collected data on ant movement, nest-site selection, and local climate parameters will inform model parameterization, while remote sensing datasets (LiDAR, thermal imaging) will provide substrate for spatially explicit microclimate layers. Computational workflows will parallelize millions of agent interactions across thousands of simulated hectares, requiring GPU-accelerated optimization for real-time scaling. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of invasion risk under current and projected climate scenarios, validated through field trials, and a publicly accessible toolkit for land managers to prioritize containment efforts. This work bridges entomology, landscape ecology, and computational physics, advancing both theoretical understanding of insect-environment interactions and practical strategies for invasive species mitigation. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling the combinatorial complexity of biotic-abiotic feedback loops at ecologically relevant resolutions, enabling unprecedented granularity in ecological forecasting.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of insect species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and neurocognitive effects of movement therapy interventions on individuals with functional movement disorders. Despite growing evidence for movement therapy’s role in enhancing somatic integration, the lack of predictive models linking specific therapeutic movements to neurophysiological outcomes limits personalized application. Current clinical assessments rely on subjective observation and coarse metrics, failing to capture the dynamic interplay between motor patterns, proprioceptive feedback, and cortical adaptation. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal data—including high-density motion capture, electromyography (EMG), electroencephalography (EEG), and patient-reported outcomes—from a longitudinal cohort undergoing movement education protocols. Computational workflows will integrate machine learning (convolutional neural networks and recurrent architectures) to identify latent movement signatures predictive of therapeutic progress, coupled with biomechanical simulations to quantify energy efficiency and joint loading patterns. A parallelized finite element model will simulate soft tissue strain during therapeutic maneuvers, informing safety thresholds for diverse populations. By correlating kinematic data with neural oscillatory patterns, we aim to map how movement repetition induces neuroplastic changes in sensorimotor networks. The resulting models will establish a taxonomy of movement qualities (e.g., fluidity, symmetry, timing) tied to functional outcomes, enabling therapists to optimize interventions via computational feedback. This work will yield open-source tools for real-time movement analysis, a biomechanical database of therapeutic movement standards, and predictive algorithms to guide dosage and progression in movement therapy. The outcomes will advance precision in somatic education, reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, and provide foundational computational methods for emerging research at the intersection of movement science and neurorehabilitation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use functional and expressive integration strategies to help promote somatic awareness and optimal psychophysical functioning. Includes instruction in skilled touch techniques, kinesthetic awareness processes, movement observation, patterning, client assessment and guidance, verbal and nonverbal communication, practice management, professional standards and ethics, and specific therapeutic and educational modalities

abstract: Electromechanical systems are increasingly complex, integrating mechanical, electrical, and control components to meet demands for automation, energy efficiency, and precision. A critical challenge lies in modeling and optimizing these systems under dynamic, real-world conditions, where nonlinear interactions between domains lead to computationally intensive simulations that exceed the capabilities of standard computing resources. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, multiphysics simulations of advanced electromechanical systems, such as hybrid robotic actuators and energy-harvesting devices. The research will focus on developing coupled finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models to study thermal, structural, and electromagnetic behaviors concurrently. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter optimization and predictive maintenance algorithms. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers in ANSYS Mechanical and COMSOL Multiphysics, with custom Python scripts for data integration and control system emulation. Expected outcomes include validated models for high-torque, low-latency servo mechanisms and thermally stable power electronics, which will inform prototype development and testing. By resolving multiphysics bottlenecks in simulation scalability, this work aims to reduce iterative design cycles by 40–60% compared to traditional methods. The results will advance electromechanical system reliability and energy efficiency, with direct applications in smart manufacturing, renewable energy infrastructure, and autonomous robotics. Furthermore, the project will provide training for undergraduate and graduate students in HPC-driven engineering design, strengthening institutional expertise in computational electromechanics. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the tera-scale datasets and real-time co-simulation demands inherent to this multidisciplinary research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Radiation therapy efficacy is critically dependent on precise tumor targeting and optimal dose distribution, yet current treatment planning systems often oversimplify tumor heterogeneity, leading to suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. This project addresses the challenge of integrating spatially resolved radiobiological parameters derived from multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) into Monte Carlo-based radiation transport simulations to model dose deposition in heterogeneous tumors. The computational complexity of simulating radiation interactions at voxel-level resolution across entire tumor volumes—while incorporating dynamic biological factors such as hypoxia and cellular proliferation rates—exceeds the capacity of standard clinical workstations. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable framework for multi-scale, multi-modal treatment optimization. The workflow will involve (1) processing high-resolution mpMRI datasets to map sub-regional radiosensitivity, (2) implementing GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations (using Geant4/GATE) to model linear energy transfer distributions in geometrically complex tumors, and (3) applying evolutionary optimization algorithms to iteratively refine dose painting prescriptions. Initial validation will utilize retrospective data from 50 glioblastoma patients treated with volumetric modulated arc therapy, comparing simulated dose distributions against clinical outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include a validated pipeline for biologically adaptive radiation therapy planning that reduces normal tissue toxicity by ≥15% in simulated models while maintaining target coverage. This work bridges radiomics, computational oncology, and advanced treatment delivery, directly addressing the limitations of current one-size-fits-all radiation prescription paradigms. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the ∼1 PB of imaging data and 10^6 core-hour computations required to establish clinically feasible optimization timelines. Successful implementation could redefine precision standards in radiation oncology, particularly for tumors with pronounced intra-lesional variability.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Pediatric infectious diseases present unique challenges due to the dynamic interplay between evolving pathogens, developmental immune responses, and variable drug pharmacokinetics in children. Current clinical models often fail to account for the heterogeneity of pediatric populations, particularly in cases involving complex host conditions, antimicrobial resistance, or rare pathogens, leading to suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive, patient-specific models for optimizing treatment strategies in pediatric infections. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating host multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic), pathogen genomes, and longitudinal clinical data from a diverse cohort of 1,500 pediatric patients with severe or recurrent infections. Machine learning algorithms will identify biomarkers associated with treatment failure or adverse drug reactions, while agent-based models will simulate host-pathogen interactions across developmental stages to predict disease trajectories. Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models, parameterized using pediatric physiological data, will evaluate drug efficacy and toxicity thresholds in virtual patient cohorts. These models will be validated against real-world clinical outcomes from partner children’s hospitals. HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale datasets, training deep neural networks, and executing parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide antibiotic selection, dosing adjustments, and immunomodulatory interventions in complex cases, reducing trial-and-error prescribing. The project will also generate open-access computational workflows for pediatric infectious disease research, addressing a critical gap in age-specific therapeutic development. By bridging clinical data with scalable computational modeling, this work aims to improve survival rates, mitigate long-term complications, and establish a paradigm for precision medicine in pediatric infectious diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases in children; and to effect a better outcome for pediatric infections with complicated courses, underlying diseases that predispose to unusual or severe infections, unclear diagnoses, uncommon diseases, and complex or investigational treatments.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic evolution of Swedish dialects and their sociolinguistic interfaces using advanced computational methods, with a focus on modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variation across historical and contemporary corpora. Despite Sweden’s rich dialectal diversity, systematic large-scale analyses of regional language change—particularly under the influence of urbanization, digital communication, and language policy—remain underexplored due to the technical challenges of processing heterogeneous, unstructured text and speech data. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on a curated multilingual corpus spanning 19th-century manuscripts, modern regional speech recordings, and social media texts. Computational workflows will integrate dialectometric clustering, neural machine translation for historical orthographies, and prosodic feature extraction from audio data, enabling comparative analyses across temporal, geographic, and sociodemographic axes. Key challenges include managing non-standard orthographies in pre-20th-century texts, aligning audio recordings with dialect-specific phonetic inventories, and scaling semantic role labeling for low-resource Swedish variants. The HPC environment is critical for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, fine-tuning large language models, and running iterative simulations of language contact scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated Swedish dialect features, (2) quantitative models correlating linguistic shifts with extralinguistic factors (e.g., migration patterns, education policies), and (3) novel methods for diachronic dialectology applicable to minority languages globally. By bridging computational linguistics with Swedish philology, this work aims to redefine scholarly approaches to language preservation and policy while providing infrastructure for cross-disciplinary humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Swedish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Contemporary studies of literary genre evolution remain constrained by the manual analysis of limited text corpora, hindering comprehensive insights into cross-genre influences and historical development patterns. This project seeks to address this gap by employing large-scale computational analysis to examine stylistic and structural features across a corpus of 10,000 English-language literary works spanning four centuries. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the research will implement natural language processing pipelines to extract syntactic patterns, thematic clusters, and narrative frameworks at scale. Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures and unsupervised clustering algorithms, will be trained to identify latent genre markers and trace their diachronic trajectories. The computational demands of processing multi-gigabyte text datasets, parallelizing feature extraction across thousands of documents, and iteratively optimizing neural network parameters necessitate dedicated HPC infrastructure with GPU acceleration and distributed storage capabilities. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized genre hybridizations, quantitative models of stylistic diffusion between literary movements, and interactive visualizations mapping temporal shifts in genre boundaries. By bridging computational methods with literary theory, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for macroanalytic scholarship in English literary studies while providing open-access tools for reproducible textual analysis in the humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on literature from one or more genres, cultures or traditions. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and studies of various types of literary text.

abstract: This project addresses the critical need for advanced computational tools to analyze the morphological, syntactic, and sociolinguistic complexity of under-resourced Iranian languages, including Middle Persian, Balochi, and Kurdish dialects. Current research in Iranian linguistics is constrained by limited digital corpora and the absence of scalable computational models capable of processing these languages’ unique typological features, such as nonconcatenative morphology and contact-induced variation. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and train transformer-based language models on heterogeneous textual data spanning historical manuscripts, modern literature, and oral narratives. Computational workflows will integrate unsupervised segmentation algorithms to handle script variation and morphological complexity, while graph-based methods will model dialect continua and language contact dynamics across the Iranian cultural sphere. The scale of data—encompassing digitized clay tablets, multilingual parallel texts, and endangered language recordings—requires distributed storage solutions and GPU-accelerated processing for efficient batch training and hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include the first open-source NLP toolkit for Middle Persian, enabling automated translation and semantic analysis of Zoroastrian texts, and probabilistic models quantifying the influence of substrate languages on regional Persian varieties. These resources will advance scholarly access to pre-Islamic literary traditions and support minority language revitalization efforts. By enabling large-scale comparative analysis, this project will generate new insights into language change across the Iranian plateau, with methodological implications for computational historical linguistics. The requested HPC infrastructure is indispensable for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as attention mechanism computations across long textual sequences, and for replicating experiments across diverse language subsets. Results will be disseminated through interoperable digital archives and integrated into pedagogical tools for Iranian studies, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between linguists, computer scientists, and cultural heritage stakeholders.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages used in ancient, medieval, and modern Iran and its border regions, including modern Persian, Avestan/Old Persian, and related modern and extinct languages. Includes instruction in applications of modern Persian and other languages in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to simulate and optimize the application and performance of cosmetic prosthetics and makeup under dynamic real-world conditions, addressing a critical gap in predictive modeling for the makeup artistry field. Current methods for testing prosthetic adhesion, cosmetic longevity, and environmental resilience rely heavily on physical trials, which are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in their ability to account for diverse physiological and environmental variables. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this work will model the biomechanical interactions between prosthetic materials, biological tissues (e.g., skin elasticity, sweat gland activity), and external factors (e.g., temperature, humidity, motion). The computational approach integrates multi-physics simulations—combining finite element analysis for stress-strain dynamics, computational fluid dynamics for sweat and sebum dispersion, and ray-tracing for photorealistic rendering under varied lighting conditions—to predict outcomes such as prosthetic displacement, makeup degradation, and visual continuity. Machine learning models will further refine these simulations using empirical data from clinical and theatrical case studies to enhance predictive accuracy. The expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools enabling artists to virtually test designs and materials, reducing physical prototyping by an estimated 60–80%. This work holds significance for both creative and clinical domains, offering applications in film production (e.g., real-time prosthetic durability forecasting), medical prosthetics (e.g., optimizing biocompatible adhesives), and inclusive beauty technology (e.g., tailoring solutions for diverse skin types). By bridging computational science and aesthetic practice, the project establishes a novel interdisciplinary niche, advancing methodological rigor in a field traditionally dominated by manual techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally apply cosmetic makeup preparations and perform complete and specialized appearance makeovers including hairdressing, wig work, masking, temporary prosthesis applications, cosmetic applications, and related costuming for leisure or for professional stage, camera, clinical, or security purposes.  Includes instruction in period and contemporary hairstyling and costuming; wig work and hairpiece application; synthetic hair and masks; cosmetic preparations and treatments; makeup artistry; attachment, removal, and camouflaging of prostheses; health and safety; client consultation and care; pre- and post-production operations; set and crew conduct and relations; script, instruction, and prescription interpretation; labor relations; and business practices.

abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical laboratory data, driven by high-throughput genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic technologies, has created a critical bottleneck in translating raw biomedical data into actionable diagnostic and therapeutic insights. Current analytical workflows struggle to integrate multi-modal datasets—such as pathogen genomic sequences, mass spectrometry outputs, and patient-specific immunological profiles—while maintaining the speed and accuracy required for clinical decision-making. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable computational pipelines for real-time analysis of heterogeneous clinical data. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) optimizing machine learning models to predict antimicrobial resistance patterns from bacterial whole-genome sequencing data, and (2) creating dynamic simulations of host-pathogen interactions to refine diagnostic protocols for sepsis and other acute conditions. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks for feature extraction from sequencing data, parallelized molecular dynamics simulations to model protein-ligand interactions, and ensemble classifiers to reconcile disparate data types into unified diagnostic scores. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to reduce analysis times for complex microbiological assays from days to hours while improving predictive accuracy through large-scale validation against retrospective clinical datasets. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for clinical laboratories, validated predictive models for antibiotic resistance in priority pathogens, and a framework for integrating real-time computational analytics into laboratory information systems. This work will directly enhance the precision and efficiency of clinical testing, support data-driven antibiotic stewardship, and provide a template for implementing HPC-driven innovation in routine laboratory operations. The resource allocation will enable critical benchmarking against existing clinical algorithms and facilitate the translation of research prototypes into robust, regulatory-compliant tools for diagnostic applications.
cip_title: Clinical Laboratory Science/ Medical Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conduct and supervise complex medical tests, clinical trials, and research experiments; manage clinical laboratories; and consult with physicians and clinical researchers on diagnoses, disease causation and spread, and research outcomes. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, immunology, immunohematology, physiological relationships to test results, laboratory procedures and quality assurance controls, test and research design and implementation, analytic techniques, laboratory management, data development and reporting, medical informatics, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate dysregulated molecular transport and signaling mechanisms underlying cancer cell metabolic adaptation, with a focus on ion channel-transporter networks and their role in tumor microenvironment interactions. Despite evidence linking aberrant activity of voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs) and solute carriers (SLCs) to therapy-resistant cancer phenotypes, the dynamic coupling between these membrane proteins and downstream effector pathways remains poorly characterized at subcellular resolution. We propose to develop multiscale computational models integrating cryo-EM structural data, live-cell imaging datasets of calcium transients, and phosphoproteomic profiles from patient-derived glioblastoma samples. High-performance computing resources will enable 1) molecular dynamics simulations of VGCC conformational states under hypoxic conditions, 2) spatial stochastic modeling of calcium-microdomain-dependent kinase activation cascades, and 3) Bayesian network inference of microenvironmental stress-induced signaling adaptations across single-cell trajectories. Our computational framework will specifically interrogate how cooperative interactions between calcium flux and amino acid transport systems sustain mTORC1 activity in nutrient-deprived tumors. The models will be iteratively refined using experimental validation data from 3D glioblastoma organoids subjected to ion channel pharmacological perturbation. This work aims to establish a predictive map of critical nodes in membrane signaling architectures that maintain cancer cell homeostasis, with potential to identify novel targets for disrupting metabolic plasticity in treatment-resistant malignancies. By resolving spatiotemporal constraints on molecular physiological networks at unprecedented resolution, the project will advance computational methodologies for analyzing dynamic subcellular processes while generating open-source simulation tools adaptable to broader studies of transport-driven signaling in epithelial cancers.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of dynamic interactive processes and biochemical communications at the subcellular level. Includes instruction in ion channels and transporters, molecular signaling pathways, endocrine control and regulation, genetic information transfer, homeostasis and molecular control systems, electrophysiology and sensory mechanisms, protein synthesis, and applicable research methods and technologies.

abstract: Public horticulture faces critical challenges in optimizing plant selection and management strategies for urban environments under dynamic climate conditions, resource constraints, and diverse public needs. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that integrate plant physiology, environmental variables, and socioeconomic data to guide sustainable urban horticulture planning. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate species performance across heterogeneous urban microclimates while balancing educational, aesthetic, and ecological priorities. We will employ agent-based modeling to simulate plant-environment interactions at city scales, incorporating real-world datasets on soil properties, historical climate patterns, projected urban heat island effects, and public usage patterns of green spaces. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on horticultural performance data (growth rates, pest resistance, water needs) and public engagement metrics from botanical gardens and urban farms. Computational workflows will parallelize parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated growing scenarios, enabling rapid sensitivity analyses of management strategies under climate uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that identifies regionally optimized plant portfolios and quantifies tradeoffs between horticultural viability, resource efficiency, and educational value. The models will also predict how specific outreach interventions (e.g., interpretive signage, volunteer programs) correlate with community engagement levels. By enabling high-resolution analysis of socio-ecological systems in public horticulture, this work aims to advance evidence-based landscape design while demonstrating how computational approaches can bridge traditional horticultural science and community-centered program development. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project’s spatial-temporal complexity, with simulations requiring >10,000 core-hours to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning biological, environmental, and social domains.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on combining traditional horticulture and public education and outreach. Includes instruction in botany, soil science, plant science, agricultural economics, leadership, and business.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, multi-stakeholder decision-making in decentralized business ecosystems enabled by blockchain-based smart contracts. As organizations increasingly adopt distributed ledger technologies for supply chain coordination, dynamic pricing, and cross-institutional governance, existing computational models struggle to scale to the complexity of continuously evolving, trustless networks with conflicting stakeholder incentives. The project will develop agent-based simulation frameworks to model emergent behaviors in these systems, incorporating game-theoretic reward mechanisms, stochastic market dynamics, and privacy-preserving data-sharing protocols. Computational demands arise from the need to simulate thousands of autonomous agents operating under Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus rules while maintaining cryptographic audit trails. Proposed methods include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing, evolutionary algorithms to optimize incentive structures, and graph neural networks to predict network congestion patterns. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for designing resilient decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) and quantified metrics for trade-offs between transaction finality speeds, incentive alignment costs, and system vulnerability surfaces. By advancing computational modeling capabilities at the intersection of distributed systems theory and operational business processes, this work aims to establish performance benchmarks for next-generation enterprise blockchain implementations while informing protocol standardization efforts. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations of large-scale networks (>10^4 nodes) and enabling rapid iteration cycles for machine learning components trained on synthetic transaction graphs.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the resilience of small business ecosystems under dynamic economic shocks, such as supply chain disruptions, regional crises, or rapid market shifts. While small businesses are critical to economic stability, their capacity to adapt to volatile conditions remains poorly understood due to the complex interdependencies between localized markets, resource availability, and digital infrastructure. Traditional analytical methods lack the granularity and scalability to simulate real-time decision-making across heterogeneous small business networks. This project addresses this gap by developing an agent-based computational framework to simulate thousands of small business entities interacting within a multi-layered economic environment. Each agent will incorporate decision-making algorithms informed by real-world data on cash flow constraints, supplier relationships, customer behavior, and e-commerce adoption. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations to test how varying levels of access to capital, digital tools, or policy interventions (e.g., emergency grants, tax relief) impact system-wide recovery rates. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to identify critical leverage points for enhancing adaptive capacity. Outcomes will include predictive models to forecast small business vulnerability under different crisis scenarios, as well as optimization strategies for resource allocation at regional and sectoral levels. By integrating computational social science with business operations research, this work aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers, nonprofit organizations, and small business owners to prioritize investments in technologies, training, and safety nets. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to process high-resolution datasets (e.g., transaction records, geospatial logistics) and execute millions of stochastic simulations to capture nonlinear system behaviors. Results will advance interdisciplinary methodologies for small business resilience planning while directly supporting evidence-based strategies to mitigate economic fragility in underserved communities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing need to prepare technology and industrial arts educators to integrate emerging computational tools—such as augmented reality (AR), generative AI, and advanced simulation software—into pedagogical practices. While these technologies hold transformative potential for design-based learning in industrial arts (e.g., prototyping, manufacturing systems), existing teacher education programs lack scalable frameworks to model their effective use in K–12 classrooms. A critical barrier is the absence of adaptive, data-driven methods to simulate how novice teachers implement such tools in dynamic classroom environments. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to model and analyze technology integration scenarios. The platform will leverage agent-based modeling to simulate classroom interactions, machine learning to assess instructional efficacy from multimodal datasets (e.g., student design portfolios, teacher feedback logs), and real-time rendering for AR/VR-based lesson prototyping. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale behavioral data, optimize generative AI workflows for curriculum personalization, and parallelize simulations across diverse pedagogical contexts. Outcomes will include (1) predictive models identifying effective strategies for teaching technology-assisted design processes and (2) an open-access repository of simulated classroom scenarios for educator training. This work will directly enhance industrial arts teacher readiness to employ advanced technologies while establishing a computational foundation for iterative, evidence-based curriculum design in vocational-technical education. By aligning HPC capabilities with hands-on pedagogical research, the project aims to redefine how teacher education programs prepare instructors to navigate rapidly evolving technological landscapes.
cip_title: Technology Teacher Education/ Industrial Arts Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach technology education/industrial arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of narrative structures and thematic patterns in American literature across three centuries, with a focus on underrepresented regional and oral traditions. While existing scholarship has mapped broad literary movements through close reading, computational limitations have hindered systematic analysis of stylistic and thematic shifts at scale. This study addresses this gap by applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to a curated corpus of 15,000 texts, including novels, essays, folk tales, and transcribed oral narratives from diverse geographic and cultural contexts (1700–2000). The research problem centers on identifying how sociopolitical transformations—such as westward expansion, industrialization, and civil rights movements—are reflected in linguistic innovation, narrative fragmentation, and the persistence of regional vernaculars. The computational approach will employ transformer-based models for semantic role labeling and sentiment analysis to track syntactic complexity and emotional valence shifts, while graph-based algorithms will map intertextual networks of influence among authors and traditions. A key innovation involves training domain-specific embeddings using HPC resources to account for archaic spellings, dialectical variations, and nonstandard orthographies in oral histories. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU nodes, the project aims to process terabytes of text data, enabling comparative analysis of macro-trends alongside micro-scale case studies (e.g., Appalachian ghost stories versus Harlem Renaissance manifestos). Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated texts, visualization tools for temporal-geographic literary patterns, and quantitative evidence challenging canonical periodizations of American literary history. This work will provide humanities scholars with new methodologies to interrogate scale in literary analysis while recentering marginalized voices in national narrative formation. The computational demands of training custom models on heterogeneous historical texts necessitate the requested HPC infrastructure to achieve both granularity and scope.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the United States from the Colonial Era to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing undersea sensor network performance within dynamic and contested maritime environments. Modern Undersea Warfare (USW) systems rely on distributed sensor arrays to detect, classify, and track submerged threats, but current simulation frameworks struggle to model the interplay of acoustic propagation, environmental variability, and adversarial counter-detection tactics at operationally relevant scales. This project aims to develop a high-fidelity computational model integrating real-time oceanographic data, adaptive signal processing algorithms, and probabilistic threat behavior patterns to enhance sensor deployment strategies and operational resilience. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute massively parallelized simulations of multi-physics scenarios, including thermocline fluctuations, biologics-generated noise, and coordinated swarm threats. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize sensor placement and fusion algorithms under constraints of energy efficiency and stealth requirements. By coupling hydrodynamic models with reinforcement learning architectures, the framework will enable autonomous adaptation to evolving battlefield conditions. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for rapid sensor network reconfiguration in response to environmental shifts or adversarial interference, as well as predictive metrics for system effectiveness across diverse ocean basins. This work bridges gaps between traditional undersea systems engineering and emerging computational decision-support paradigms, offering a novel approach to maintaining acoustic superiority in increasingly complex undersea domains. The requested HPC allocation will support parameter space exploration across 10^6+ scenario permutations, enabling statistically robust conclusions about system performance thresholds. Successful implementation will provide the USW community with a scalable tool for evaluating next-generation sensor concepts while informing platform acquisition and doctrine development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, engineering design and military concepts that govern the operational employment of underwater sensors and weapons systems. Includes instruction in acoustics, electrical, and mechanical engineering; mathematics; meteorology; oceanography; physics; operations analysis; human factors; computer science; and robotics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling hyper-personalized consumer decision pathways in fragmented digital markets, integrating real-time neuromarketing data with multi-platform behavioral analytics. The core problem lies in the inadequacy of traditional marketing models to capture the non-linear, context-dependent nature of modern consumer choices shaped by augmented reality interfaces, algorithmic recommendation systems, and cross-channel micro-moments. Our approach combines high-frequency eye-tracking datasets (500Hz temporal resolution) from mixed-reality shopping experiments with distributed social media engagement traces across 14 platforms, creating multi-terabyte streams requiring synchronized processing. We propose implementing a hybrid architecture leveraging GPU-accelerated transformer models for attention pattern recognition alongside agent-based simulations of marketplace emergence, with computational demands necessitating sustained access to high-memory nodes and parallel file systems. The workflow will employ federated learning techniques to maintain data privacy across commercial partners while training predictive models of micro-conversion events. Expected outcomes include a dynamic graph neural network architecture capable of forecasting purchase propensity at sub-second latency across heterogeneous touchpoints, validated against experimental control groups exposed to adaptive content variations. This work aims to establish computational benchmarks for next-generation marketing systems that respect cognitive load boundaries while optimizing experiential relevance, with potential applications in ethical AI design for attention economies. The scale of spatiotemporal data integration and need for real-time multi-agent simulation of 10^6 synthetic consumers across empirically calibrated digital twins requires dedicated HPC resources beyond conventional cloud capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to undertake and manage the process of developing consumer audiences and moving products from producers to consumers. Includes instruction in buyer behavior and dynamics, principle of marketing research, demand analysis, cost-volume and profit relationships, pricing theory, marketing campaign and strategic planning, market segments, advertising methods, sales operations and management, consumer relations, retailing, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision woodworking techniques through computational modeling and simulation, addressing challenges in material behavior prediction and toolpath optimization. Traditional woodworking methods rely on empirical adjustments and manual testing, which are time-intensive and limited in accounting for complex variables such as anisotropic grain structures, moisture dynamics, and tool-material interactions. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale finite element models (FEM) that simulate cutting forces, thermal effects, and deformation in real time. These models will integrate material datasets from experimental wood samples, including density maps, hygrothermal properties, and stress-strain responses under varying conditions. Machine learning algorithms will further refine predictive accuracy by correlating simulation outputs with empirical machining data collected via sensor-equipped CNC routers. The computational workflow will also optimize toolpath generation through parallelized genetic algorithms, minimizing waste and maximizing surface quality. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible simulation framework for woodworking applications, validated protocols for adaptive machining parameters, and predictive tools to reduce material defects in complex joinery or curved assemblies. By bridging computational science with craft practice, this work aims to enhance sustainability through reduced material waste, enable novel design possibilities in architectural woodworking, and provide educational resources for integrating computational methods into technical woodworking curricula. The scale of data processing (terabyte-level voxel datasets for grain modeling) and the need for real-time parametric simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve practical runtime performance.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in woodworking, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing prevalence of diet-related metabolic disorders in companion animals, such as obesity and diabetes, highlights critical gaps in understanding species-specific nutrient metabolism and its interaction with health outcomes. Current empirical models fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale relationships between dietary components, host physiology, and the gut microbiome, limiting the development of precision nutrition strategies. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to construct mechanistic, multi-omics models of nutrient metabolism in dogs and cats. We will integrate species-specific genomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic data to simulate nutrient absorption, hepatic processing, and systemic utilization under varying dietary conditions. A hybrid computational approach will combine differential equation-based systems biology models with machine learning to predict metabolic fluxes, microbiome-mediated nutrient transformations, and their collective impact on biomarkers of health. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses across diverse physiological states (e.g., age, disease status), and probabilistic simulations of dietary interventions. The computational framework will be validated against clinical datasets from feeding trials measuring postprandial metabolite profiles, gut microbiota composition, and inflammatory markers. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal nutrient ratios for mitigating metabolic dysfunction, predictive tools for personalized diet formulation, and mechanistic insights into species-specific differences in nutrient requirements. This work will directly inform evidence-based clinical guidelines for therapeutic diets, reducing reliance on trial-and-error nutritional management. By resolving complex interactions between diet, metabolism, and animal health at unprecedented resolution, the project advances veterinary nutrition into a computationally driven paradigm with translational implications for both companion and production animals.
cip_definition: Research focused on the chemical nature of food substances; the processes by which animals ingest, digest, absorb, transport, utilize and excrete food and nutrients; and their relation to animal behavior and health.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing resource allocation for youth social service programs through advanced computational modeling. Youth service administrators face complex decision-making processes when balancing limited resources, diverse community needs, and variable program effectiveness across demographic groups. Traditional evaluation methods often struggle to account for the multidimensional nature of risk factors, service interactions, and longitudinal outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an agent-based simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model service delivery systems at scale. The computational model will integrate anonymized administrative data from child welfare agencies, educational institutions, and community partners, incorporating variables such as socioeconomic status, family dynamics, service utilization patterns, and developmental outcomes. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters and identify non-linear relationships between intervention types, dosage, timing, and youth outcomes. The HPC environment will enable simultaneous execution of thousands of simulation scenarios to test hypothetical resource allocation strategies under different demographic and budgetary conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that quantifies projected impacts of funding distribution choices across multiple outcome measures: academic achievement, juvenile justice system involvement, mental health service accessibility, and long-term economic self-sufficiency. This computational approach will provide unprecedented capacity to analyze equity implications of allocation policies while maintaining strict confidentiality standards through synthetic data generation techniques. The results will directly inform state-level youth service reform initiatives and establish a replicable methodology for evidence-based administration in non-profit and public agency settings. By bridging computational social science with public administration practice, this project aims to enhance the effectiveness of youth services while advancing computational methods for social policy analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and implement social services for children, youth, and families. Includes instruction in child development and psychology, adolescence, family studies, social work, social services administration, juvenile and family law, program and facilities planning, youth leadership, counseling, probation, casework, applicable procedures and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting landscape-scale ecosystem responses to compounding stressors, including climate change, habitat fragmentation, and resource extraction. Current models often oversimplify interactions between hydrological systems, biodiversity dynamics, and anthropogenic disturbances, limiting their utility for adaptive management. We propose developing an integrated computational framework to simulate coupled ecological-hydrological processes across heterogeneous landscapes at high spatial-temporal resolution (1 km² grids, daily timesteps). The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized agent-based models for wildlife population dynamics alongside physically based hydrological models (e.g., ParFlow-CLM), with machine learning techniques to optimize parameterization across scales. Key challenges include resolving feedback loops between surface water availability, species dispersal patterns, and human infrastructure development in multi-scenario analyses. The computational workflow requires handling petabytes of multi-source geospatial data, including remote sensing inputs (Landsat, Sentinel-2), climate projections (CMIP6), and regional biodiversity databases. Expected outcomes include 1) novel algorithms for scaling ecological processes across organizational levels, 2) predictive maps of ecosystem service vulnerabilities under alternative management scenarios, and 3) open-source tools for dynamic habitat connectivity assessments. This work directly supports conservation prioritization in critical ecoregions facing rapid environmental change, with immediate applications to protected area network design in collaboration with state and federal agencies. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving sufficient model complexity and ensemble sizes to quantify uncertainty in coupled human-natural systems, enabling decision-relevant projections at policy-relevant scales. Results will advance computational ecology methods while providing actionable insights for balancing resource use with biodiversity preservation in complex landscapes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing maternal-fetal health outcomes in community-based midwifery care. Despite growing evidence supporting the safety of midwife-led care for low-risk pregnancies, systemic gaps persist in predicting and mitigating risks during natural births, particularly in underserved populations. Current clinical decision-making relies on static risk stratification models that inadequately account for dynamic, patient-specific factors such as maternal biomechanics, real-time fetal positioning, and environmental stressors. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating biomechanical modeling, machine learning, and multi-omics data analysis to predict labor progression and obstetric complications. The research will utilize 3D pelvic floor simulations derived from anonymized MRI datasets and stochastic models of uterine contractility patterns, requiring parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging data. Recurrent neural networks will be trained on longitudinal electronic health records from midwifery practices (n≈50,000 births) to identify subtle predictors of dystocia or hemorrhage. Additionally, metagenomic analysis of maternal microbiome samples (n=2,000) will investigate associations between microbial communities and preterm labor risk. The computational intensity of simultaneously running finite element analyses, deep learning workflows, and genome assembly pipelines necessitates HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized birth planning, validated through retrospective clinical data and prospective pilot studies with partnering midwifery clinics. By creating open-source tools for dynamic risk assessment, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based practice in direct-entry midwifery while maintaining its philosophy of low-intervention care. The resource demands reflect the need to process heterogeneous biological, imaging, and clinical data at scales previously unexamined in midwifery research, ultimately bridging computational innovation with equitable perinatal care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide pre-natal, natural birth, and immediate postpartum care to pregnant women in jurisdictions licensing direct (non-nursing) training for midwives. Includes instruction in basic obstetrics, women's health, fetal development, childbirth education, maternal nutrition and health, labor support, natural childbirth, postpartum support, prebirth counseling and risk screening, management of obstetric emergencies, patient referral, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance teacher professional development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze the efficacy of adaptive instructional strategies in diverse classroom environments. A critical challenge in teacher education is the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate how nuanced teaching behaviors—such as real-time feedback, differentiated instruction, and culturally responsive practices—impact student engagement and learning outcomes. Traditional observational studies are constrained by small sample sizes, manual coding, and limited generalizability. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom dynamics under varied pedagogical strategies. Large-scale datasets of teacher-student interactions (video, audio, and text transcripts from K-12 classrooms) will be processed using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to identify behavioral patterns. These patterns will inform the parameterization of ABMs, which will simulate how modifications to teacher strategies propagate through student networks, affecting collective learning. HPC resources are essential to train deep learning models on multimodal data (requiring GPU-accelerated processing) and to run thousands of parallelized ABM iterations, enabling robust sensitivity analyses across demographic and contextual variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking specific teaching practices to equity-focused student outcomes, (2) open-access tools for teacher educators to visualize and test strategy adaptations in virtual environments, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for personalized professional development programs. By quantifying the systemic impacts of teaching methods at scale, this work aims to transform how teacher preparation programs design clinical training and support data-informed instructional decision-making.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Levels and Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education and professional development, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to evaluate the longitudinal impacts of higher education programs on student outcomes and institutional performance. Current evaluation methodologies often rely on static, aggregated datasets and simplified statistical models, which struggle to account for the dynamic, multi-source nature of modern educational data (e.g., learning analytics, demographic trends, policy shifts) or to model complex causal relationships. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations to enable real-time, high-dimensional evaluation of program efficacy, equity, and economic sustainability. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including student performance records, institutional budgets, employment metrics, and qualitative policy documents—using natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based data fusion techniques. Machine learning models will then analyze temporal and spatial patterns in these integrated datasets to identify critical predictors of program success, simulate policy impacts under varying economic conditions, and quantify biases in evaluation metrics. Computational demands include training transformer-based NLP architectures on unstructured policy texts, running agent-based simulations of enrollment and funding scenarios, and conducting Bayesian network analyses to map interdependencies between institutional variables. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive higher education evaluation, validated against historical data from 15 U.S. institutions, and policy briefs quantifying trade-offs in resource allocation strategies. By enabling granular, computationally intensive analyses of equity-efficiency tensions in higher education, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making for accreditors, policymakers, and institutional leaders while establishing methodological benchmarks for evaluation research in resource-constrained environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for generating information about educational programs in higher education, staff and methods, and the analysis of such information for planning purposes outside of institutional research. Includes instruction in evaluation theory, evaluation research design and planning, administering evaluations and related data collection activities, data reporting requirements, data analysis and interpretation, and related economic and policy issues in higher education.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of persuasive communication in digital media environments through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal discourse. As digital platforms increasingly shape public opinion, understanding how rhetorical strategies—such as argumentation frameworks, emotional appeals, and nonverbal cues—interact across text, audio, and visual modalities remains a critical challenge. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the scale and complexity of modern communication ecosystems, necessitating advanced computational tools. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze a corpus of 10 million social media posts, political speeches, and multimedia content from diverse cultural contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models to detect rhetorical patterns, sentiment trajectories, and cross-modal coherence at scale, while maintaining sensitivity to contextual factors like audience demographics and platform-specific norms. Parallel processing will enable real-time simulation of information diffusion networks to model how persuasive messages evolve through user interactions. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of effective multimodal rhetorical strategies in digital persuasion, (2) predictive models linking specific communication patterns to audience engagement metrics, and (3) open-source tools for ethical discourse analysis. These contributions will advance rhetorical theory by quantitatively testing classical frameworks against contemporary digital practices while providing evidence-based guidance for communication professionals addressing societal challenges like misinformation and polarization. The project’s scale—requiring simultaneous analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, complex neural network architectures, and dynamic network simulations—fundamentally depends on HPC capabilities for distributed processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-memory data handling beyond conventional computing infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific, humanistic, and critical study of human communication in a variety of formats, media, and contexts. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of interpersonal, group, organizational, professional, and intercultural communication; speaking and listening; verbal and nonverbal interaction; rhetorical theory and criticism; performance studies; argumentation and persuasion; technologically mediated communication; popular culture; and various contextual applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between urban recreational spaces and socio-environmental equity, a niche interdisciplinary domain within Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Studies. Despite the critical role parks play in community health and ecological resilience, current planning frameworks lack granular computational tools to simulate long-term outcomes of design decisions under shifting demographic and climatic conditions. The research problem centers on developing predictive models that integrate heterogeneous datasets—including geospatial park usage patterns, vegetation health metrics, and socioeconomic vulnerability indices—to evaluate how park allocation strategies affect equitable access and environmental justice in urban landscapes. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and geospatial temporal analysis, the project will simulate scenarios of park development, maintenance, and programming under varying budget constraints and climate projections. Computational workflows will process high-resolution satellite imagery, anonymized mobility data, and municipal infrastructure records to parameterize models, requiring parallelized processing for large-scale spatial datasets. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support framework that quantifies trade-offs between recreational resource allocation, canopy cover expansion, and neighborhood-level equity metrics. By coupling machine learning optimization techniques with participatory planning principles, the project aims to advance computational methods for leisure studies while generating actionable insights for municipalities addressing climate adaptation and social inclusion mandates. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the iterative, multi-agent simulations and scaling analyses across diverse urban typologies, enabling real-time visualization of complex system interactions that traditional planning tools cannot capture. This work bridges computational social science, urban ecology, and public policy, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional research domains focused on community well-being.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles underlying recreational and leisure activities, and the practices involved in providing indoor and outdoor recreational facilities and services for the general public.

abstract: Dental occlusal dysfunction remains a significant clinical challenge, with traditional restorative approaches relying on static models that inadequately represent dynamic masticatory forces. This project proposes to develop a real-time biomechanical simulation framework for optimizing CAD/CAM restorative designs in digital dentistry, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational complexity of modeling time-dependent occlusal interactions. Current limitations in simulating temporomandibular joint kinematics, intraoral soft tissue deformation, and material fatigue in ceramic restorations restrict the predictive accuracy of digital treatment planning systems. We will employ multiscale finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning-driven surrogate modeling to predict stress distribution patterns across dental restorations under physiologically realistic loading conditions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 4D intraoral scan data (sequential DICOM/CBCT volumes) and iterative optimization of prosthetic geometries through automated design space exploration. The computational workflow integrates patient-specific biomechanical parameters derived from dynamic stereophotogrammetry with material science datasets for modern dental composites. Validation will occur through in vitro testing using sensor-embedded typodonts and retrospective analysis of 150 clinical cases with long-term follow-up. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of reducing restorative failure rates by 30-40% through predictive design optimization, along with novel quantitative metrics for occlusal load distribution. This research will establish computational thresholds for real-time chairside simulation in dental CAD software while advancing fundamental understanding of biomechanical failure modes in digitally fabricated restorations. The developed models may further inform regulatory standards for AI-assisted dental device design, addressing a critical gap in personalized digital dentistry infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of digital and CAD/CAM technology in dental treatment. Includes instruction in digital diagnostic and treatment planning techniques, CAD/CAM restoration, and patient management.

abstract: The reactivity of silicate minerals governs critical geochemical and physical processes shaping Earth’s surface and subsurface environments. However, modeling the coupled effects of silicate weathering, fluid transport, and mechanical deformation at scales spanning atomic interactions to landscape evolution remains a fundamental challenge due to computational limitations. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of silicate-dominated systems by developing high-resolution, multiscale models of mineral-fluid interactions under varying thermodynamic and stress conditions. The research will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to quantify atomic-scale dissolution-precipitation kinetics and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to refine interatomic potentials for silicate-water interfaces. These data will parameterize continuum-scale reactive transport models, implemented using the open-source software CrunchTope, to simulate weathering fronts and fracture propagation in heterogeneous rock matrices. A key innovation involves coupling geochemical reaction networks with discrete element method (DEM) simulations to resolve feedbacks between chemical weathering and mechanical breakdown. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from laboratory mesocosms and field observations of weathering profiles in granitic terrains. This project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the iterative multiscale simulations, particularly the massively parallel MD runs (using LAMMPS) and high-resolution DEM domains with >10^6 particles. Anticipated outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into rate-limiting steps during silicate weathering, (2) predictive frameworks for fracture network development in engineered geothermal systems, and (3) improved scaling relationships for global biogeochemical models. By integrating atomistic and continuum approaches, this work will provide novel constraints on how silicates regulate terrestrial carbon cycling, soil formation, and subsurface hydrology over geologic timescales. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of storage will enable these computationally intensive simulations, fostering advances in geomorphology, environmental geology, and sustainable resource management.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the silicates and other substances formed by chemical and physical geomorphological processes.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in precision medicine by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between multi-omics data, clinical variables, and environmental factors in heterogeneous patient populations. Current approaches to personalized treatment planning often fail to account for the dynamic interplay of these variables, particularly in understudied cohorts, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project will develop scalable computational frameworks to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets with real-world clinical data, enabling predictive modeling of disease progression and therapeutic responses. Using machine learning algorithms optimized for distributed computing architectures, we will train ensemble models to identify biomarkers and stratify patients based on risk profiles. The HPC infrastructure will support parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, feature selection, and cross-validation, while enabling large-scale simulations of molecular pathways to contextualize observed clinical patterns. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive data integration in precision health, validated predictive models for cardiovascular and metabolic disorders, and a publicly accessible repository of annotated multi-omics datasets. This work will directly inform clinical decision-support systems under development in partnership with regional health networks, bridging translational research gaps. By advancing computational methods for health data synthesis, the project aligns with institutional priorities to expand interdisciplinary training in health analytics, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-driven biomedical research. The requested resources are essential to manage terabyte-scale datasets and reduce runtime for iterative model training, which is infeasible on local clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical professional preparation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing rehabilitation outcomes in juvenile corrections programs. Despite advances in correctional methodologies, juvenile recidivism remains a persistent challenge, with limited computational tools available to analyze complex, multi-dimensional datasets spanning behavioral, socioenvironmental, and institutional factors. Current approaches often rely on static risk assessments that fail to dynamically integrate real-time data streams, such as educational progress, mental health indicators, or community engagement metrics. This project addresses this gap by employing machine learning (ML) and network analysis techniques to identify patterns in longitudinal datasets from juvenile justice systems, including anonymized records of behavioral interventions, family dynamics, and post-release outcomes. Computational workflows will prioritize ethical AI practices, including bias mitigation in training data and interpretable model design. Key technical challenges include processing heterogeneous data formats (e.g., case notes, sensor data from electronic monitoring systems) and simulating intervention scenarios through agent-based modeling. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to test hypothetical rehabilitation pathways and quantify their probabilistic impacts on recidivism reduction. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive risk stratification and resource allocation recommendations tailored to individualized rehabilitation plans. By integrating computational social science with correctional practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in juvenile justice systems while establishing a methodological template for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of public policy, behavioral analytics, and high-performance computing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to specialize in the provision of correction services to underage minor populations. Includes instruction in corrections, juvenile delinquency, juvenile development and psychology, juvenile law and justice administration, social services, record-keeping procedures, and communication skills.

abstract: Pediatric airway disorders, including complex congenital malformations and acquired obstructions, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to the dynamic nature of developing respiratory anatomy and the risks of invasive interventions. Current clinical assessments often rely on static imaging or subjective evaluations, which may inadequately capture functional deficits. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model pediatric upper airway biomechanics, integrating patient-specific anatomical data with multiphysics simulations of airflow, tissue deformation, and fluid-structure interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process 3D reconstructions from dynamic CT/MRI scans of 200+ patients (ages 0-12) with conditions such as laryngomalacia, subglottic stenosis, and tracheobronchomalacia. The computational pipeline will employ finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics using open-source solvers (e.g., FEBio, OpenFOAM), optimized for parallel processing to handle meshes exceeding 10 million elements. Machine learning models will concurrently analyze clinical metadata to identify predictors of surgical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) validated simulations quantifying airflow resistance and collapse risk across diagnoses, (2) a predictive tool for optimizing surgical planning (e.g., comparing single-stage reconstruction vs. conservative approaches), and (3) open-access benchmark datasets of pediatric airway biomechanics. This work addresses a critical gap in objective metrics for airway dysfunction severity, with potential to reduce revision surgeries and improve personalized treatment protocols. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the need for rapid iteration of multiscale models, with an estimated 250,000 core-hours required for parameter sensitivity analyses and validation against spirometry/endoscopy data. By coupling computational modeling with clinical AI, this project aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in pediatric otolaryngology while establishing scalable methods for studying rare childhood airway disorders.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose, treat and manage disorders of infants and children that include congenital and acquired conditions involving the aerodigestive tract, nose and paranasal sinuses, the ear, and other areas of the head and neck; this includes special skills in the diagnosis, treatment, and management of childhood disorders of voice, speech, language, and hearing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content in the global arts and entertainment industries. As generative AI tools rapidly transform creative sectors, unresolved questions about copyright ownership, attribution, liability, and ethical compliance have created systemic uncertainty for stakeholders.
