Traditional legal research methods struggle to map the transnational, cross-industry impacts of these technologies due to the sheer volume of case law, licensing agreements, and policy drafts emerging from diverse jurisdictions. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis algorithms to process multilingual legal documents, contractual templates, and regulatory proposals from 50+ jurisdictions, identifying patterns in legislative approaches and liability allocation. Custom machine learning models will simulate hypothetical disputes across scenarios such as AI-remixed music catalogs, synthetic actor performances, and algorithmically generated visual art, assessing how existing intellectual property doctrines might adapt to novel creative workflows. By integrating legal text corpora with datasets tracking real-world AI adoption rates in entertainment sectors, the computational framework will quantify gaps between policy development and industry practices. Anticipated outcomes include a dynamic visualization platform for policymakers to test regulatory interventions and a risk-assessment toolkit for creative professionals navigating AI integration. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational legal analytics with arts industry needs, offering empirically grounded insights to stabilize an increasingly fragmented governance landscape while preserving creative autonomy in the algorithmic age. The scale of data processing and complexity of multi-agent simulations necessitate HPC capabilities to achieve legally rigorous, actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting the sports, fashion, entertainment, arts, and media industries.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the cultural and textual dynamics of Irish identity formation across historical and diasporic contexts. The research problem centers on the fragmented nature of primary source materials—including digitized manuscripts, newspapers, folklore collections, and emigrant correspondence—which span multiple centuries, geographies, and formats. Traditional humanities methodologies struggle to systematically trace patterns of cultural transmission, linguistic evolution, or thematic continuity within such large, heterogeneous datasets. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning to identify latent connections between Irish cultural production in Ireland and diaspora communities (e.g., North America, Australia) from the 18th to early 20th centuries. Key tasks include training custom transformer models on historical Irish English and Gaelic texts to detect semantic shifts in concepts like “community,” “exile,” or “heritage”; constructing co-occurrence networks to map the dissemination of literary motifs and oral traditions; and applying spatial-temporal modeling to correlate linguistic patterns with migration waves. The scale of data—over 500,000 pages of text and 10,000 archival records—requires distributed computing for parallelized text extraction, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale graph analytics. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated datasets, visualizations of cultural exchange pathways, and statistical frameworks for quantifying narrative persistence in diasporic contexts. This work aims to advance interdisciplinary Irish Studies by bridging qualitative cultural analysis with computational rigor, offering new insights into how collective memory and identity were negotiated across dispersed populations. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume and complexity, enabling methods impractical on local infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Ireland and the Irish Diaspora, from the early Christian period to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between international human rights policies and transnational governance frameworks, with a focus on identifying systemic bottlenecks that impede effective implementation across diverse geopolitical contexts. Traditional policy analysis methods often struggle to account for the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between state and non-state actors, as well as the cascading effects of policy decisions across jurisdictional boundaries. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating natural language processing of multilateral agreements, agent-based modeling of policy adoption processes, and network analysis of institutional interdependencies. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process multilingual policy documents from over 150 national and supranational entities, simulate emergent outcomes of concurrent policy interventions at regional and global scales, and model the diffusion of governance innovations through international organizations. Computational challenges include parsing legal texts with contextual semantic analysis, optimizing parallel simulations of 10^6+ agent interactions, and maintaining temporal consistency in longitudinal network models spanning three decades of policy development. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of policy implementation barriers, predictive models of cross-jurisdictional policy convergence, and evidence-based recommendations for improving coordination mechanisms in transnational human rights initiatives. The resulting computational tools and datasets will be made available through an open-access policy analytics portal, enabling replication studies and comparative analyses across other domains of international public policy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to relationships among nations and among governments and non-governmental entities. Includes instruction in international politics, governance, financial policy, and security affairs; globalization; economic and social policies of developing nations; and applications to specific public policy topics such as labor and employment, immigration, and human rights.

abstract: The global fashion industry faces increasing pressure to optimize live and virtual presentation strategies that balance consumer engagement, operational efficiency, and environmental impact. This project addresses the computational challenge of simulating and predicting outcomes for hybrid (physical-digital) fashion modeling events, where dynamic variables such as audience attention patterns, model choreography, real-time garment physics, and sustainability metrics intersect. Current industry practices rely on heuristic decision-making, leading to resource-intensive trial-and-error processes in event design. We propose developing an agent-based modeling framework enhanced by computer vision and reinforcement learning to simulate audience reactions, model movement efficiency, and material waste patterns under diverse staging scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal datasets—including 3D garment simulations, eye-tracking data from past shows, and environmental impact metrics—while training neural networks to identify pareto-optimal configurations that maximize aesthetic impact and minimize carbon footprint. The computational pipeline will integrate real-time rendering engines with discrete-event simulation tools, requiring parallel processing of terabyte-scale spatial-temporal data streams. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between creative choices and sustainability benchmarks, potentially reducing material waste in set construction by 15-30% and improving audience retention metrics for virtual shows. This research establishes a novel computational foundation for data-driven fashion presentation design, bridging operational research, behavioral analytics, and environmental science within the business context of modeling program optimization. Results will be validated through partnerships with three Milan-based fashion houses implementing 2025 hybrid show formats.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to present and display fashion, apparel, and accessories products in wholesale and retail settings, either on the person or via props and natural or artificial settings. Includes instruction in modeling skills, health and cosmetic principles, fashion show management, display design and production, and applicable aspects of advertising and fashion photography.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for modeling the dynamic interactions between corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures and real-time financial market reactions. While ESG metrics are increasingly critical to investor decision-making, current accounting practices struggle to quantify their nonlinear, time-dependent impacts on market volatility, liquidity, and firm valuation. The project addresses this gap by integrating heterogeneous datasets—including SEC filings, ESG rating databases, social media sentiment, and high-frequency trading data—to analyze how granular ESG factors propagate through global markets. Computational methods will combine natural language processing (NLP) for extracting latent ESG themes from unstructured disclosures, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map inter-firm ESG influence networks, and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate investor behavior under evolving regulatory scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of petabyte-scale financial time series data and probabilistic uncertainty quantification across thousands of concurrent market simulations. Expected outcomes include a novel risk assessment tool that identifies ESG-driven financial tipping points and a publicly accessible dataset linking ESG disclosure patterns to market microstructure effects. This work bridges accounting theory with computational social science, offering practitioners a systematic approach to evaluate ESG strategies in volatile markets while advancing methodological integration of AI/ML techniques in fiduciary analytics. The resource-intensive nature of modeling cross-scale interactions—from firm-level disclosures to systemic market shocks—necessitates specialized computing capabilities beyond conventional cloud infrastructure.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and business administration/management that prepares individuals to function as accountants and business managers.

abstract: Orthoptic disorders, such as strabismus and amblyopia, involve complex interactions between neurophysiological pathways governing eye alignment, binocular vision, and sensorimotor adaptation. Current clinical assessments often rely on static, behaviorally observable metrics, limiting insight into the dynamic neural processes underlying these conditions. This project proposes to address this gap by developing computational models of cortico-midbrain oculomotor networks to simulate aberrant circuitry in orthoptic pathologies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-modal datasets—including high-density electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking kinematics, and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) tractography—into a unified biophysical modeling framework. A primary focus is simulating how disruptions in cerebellar-parietal feedback loops contribute to adaptive failures in vergence control, a mechanism implicated in decompensated strabismus. The computational pipeline will employ large-scale neural population models using NEURON and NetPyNE, optimized for parallel processing to handle real-time simulations of interareal connectivity across timescales (milliseconds to months). Machine learning classifiers will be trained on simulated and clinical datasets to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment resistance in amblyopia. By mapping maladaptive plasticity pathways, this work aims to advance personalized therapeutic strategies, such as optimizing prism adaptation protocols or neurostimulation targets. Outcomes will include open-source tools for simulating orthoptic dysfunction, enabling hypothesis-driven refinement of diagnostic criteria and intervention timing. The computational demands of modeling whole-brain networks with cellular resolution necessitate HPC allocation to achieve clinically translatable throughput. This interdisciplinary approach bridges systems neuroscience, clinical ophthalmology, and computational modeling, offering a novel paradigm to investigate dynamic neural substrates of visual disorders that evade traditional analytic methods.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists, to analyze, evaluate, and treat specific disorders of vision, eye movement, and eye alignment in children and adults. Includes instruction in eye anatomy, neuroanatomy, physiology, pharmacology, ophthalmic optics, diagnostic testing and measurement, orthoptic treatment therapy, systemic ocular diseases and disorders, principles of surgery, examination techniques, patient education, child psychology and development, learning disabilities, medical writing, and record-keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize precision meat-cutting workflows in commercial settings through advanced simulation and predictive modeling. The research addresses inefficiencies in traditional meat processing, which relies heavily on manual expertise and static guidelines, leading to variable yield rates, energy waste, and suboptimal equipment utilization. By integrating high-fidelity physics-based simulations with machine learning, we aim to model the biomechanical properties of diverse meat products (e.g., beef, pork, poultry) under varying blade geometries, cutting speeds, and refrigeration conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate tissue deformation and stress distribution during cutting, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to map thermal gradients in storage environments. Parallelized reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine cutting protocols to maximize yield while minimizing energy consumption and tool wear. Additionally, genomic and proteomic datasets from livestock sources will be analyzed to predict muscle fiber orientation and fat marbling patterns, informing adaptive cutting strategies. The computational pipeline will be validated against empirical data from sensor-equipped cutting stations, tracking outcomes such as waste reduction, ergonomic safety metrics, and shelf-life extension. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision support toolkit for butchers, dynamically optimized cutting templates for automated machinery, and predictive models for regulatory compliance in meat handling. By bridging gaps between computational mechanics, materials science, and food technology, this work establishes a novel interdisciplinary paradigm for advancing precision in meat processing—a critical yet underexplored domain in non-STEM vocational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, cut, and package animal meat products in commercial establishments and to function as licensed meat cutters/butchers.  Includes instruction in product recognition for beef, veal, lamb, pork, poultry, and fancy and smoked meats; retail and wholesale cutting and specialty cuts; packaging and counter display; shop safety; meat sanitation, storage and rotation; quality control; meat handling laws and regulations; and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance strategies for complex vehicle systems through advanced computational modeling and machine learning. Traditional diagnostic methods in vehicle maintenance often rely on reactive or rule-based approaches, leading to unplanned downtime, costly repairs, and suboptimal resource allocation. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation framework to model wear patterns, failure modes, and component interactions across diverse vehicle subsystems, including hybrid/electric powertrains, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and legacy combustion systems. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets comprising real-world telemetry, sensor logs, maintenance records, and material degradation metrics. Computational methods will include finite element analysis for structural fatigue modeling, computational fluid dynamics for thermal management systems, and graph neural networks to map interdependencies between components. Parallelized training of ensemble machine learning models will enable probabilistic failure forecasting at scale, while sensitivity analyses will identify critical maintenance thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive maintenance toolkit optimized for commercial repair workflows, validated through partnerships with fleet operators and dealerships. The project aims to reduce diagnostic errors by 25–40% in pilot studies and establish computational benchmarks for lifecycle assessment of emerging vehicle technologies. By integrating HPC-driven insights with technician training modules, this work bridges gaps between data science and hands-on repair practices, fostering innovation in a traditionally hardware-focused field. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter optimization, and the development of adaptive digital twins for next-generation vehicle architectures.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Understanding how rapid environmental change reshapes species interactions and evolutionary trajectories remains a critical challenge in ecology and evolutionary biology. Current models often simplify either ecological dynamics or evolutionary processes, limiting their ability to predict biodiversity outcomes under scenarios like climate warming or habitat fragmentation. This project addresses this gap by developing an integrative framework to simulate eco-evolutionary feedbacks in multi-species communities. We propose using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize and run individual-based models that track phenotypic and genetic variation, population dynamics, and species interactions across heterogeneous landscapes. These models will incorporate empirical data from long-term field studies on plant-pollinator networks and predator-prey systems, scaling from individual traits to community-level responses. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for spatially explicit simulations with >10^6 individuals, integrating adaptive landscapes with demographic stochasticity, and analyzing high-dimensional output to identify emergent patterns. Expected outcomes include quantifying how gene flow and selection interact with ecological competition to determine resilience to environmental stressors, predicting tipping points in ecosystem stability, and mapping geographic regions where evolutionary rescue is most likely to buffer biodiversity loss. Results will advance theoretical understanding of eco-evolutionary dynamics while providing actionable insights for conservation prioritization. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across climate scenarios, genetic architectures, and interaction networks that are infeasible on local clusters, directly supporting hypothesis testing and model validation. This work aligns with the program’s mission to link evolutionary mechanisms with ecological consequences, offering a scalable computational approach to address pressing challenges in biodiversity science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how evolution shapes biodiversity, and how organisms interact with each other and their environments. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: Medical staff credentialing and privileging processes are critical for ensuring healthcare quality, yet current methodologies remain labor-intensive, fragmented, and prone to delays that jeopardize institutional compliance and patient safety. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven decision support system to optimize credential verification, risk prediction, and compliance monitoring for healthcare facilities. The research will leverage federated learning architectures to analyze multi-source data—including licensure records, malpractice claims, peer references, and procedural competency metrics—while preserving data privacy across institutions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of structured and unstructured data, train deep neural networks on longitudinal credentialing outcomes, and simulate accreditation scenarios under dynamic regulatory constraints. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing for automated extraction of provider qualifications from heterogeneous documents, graph analytics to map inter-institutional credentialing patterns, and reinforcement learning to model adaptive privileging policies. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for real-time risk stratification of applicant portfolios, predictive alerts for credential expiration or noncompliance, and generative AI tools to streamline audit documentation. This work addresses an unmet need in healthcare operations by transforming static, manual workflows into proactive, data-driven processes. Success would directly enhance medical staff service efficiency, reduce administrative overhead, and mitigate institutional liability—advancing a specialized niche in health systems technology with implications for workforce management and regulatory interoperability. The HPC environment is indispensable for managing the computational complexity of cross-institutional data harmonization and enabling rapid iteration of models that balance accuracy, interpretability, and compliance with evolving healthcare standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform credentialing, privileging, personnel management, and accreditation compliance services for hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in medical staff organization and management, medical terminology, credentialing and re-credentialing, health care accreditation and regulatory standards, health care law, meeting and negotiation management, and office information systems management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing additive manufacturing (AM) processes using high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical challenges in production efficiency, material waste, and part quality. Despite advancements in AM technologies, inconsistencies in process parameters—such as laser power, scan speed, and layer thickness—lead to defects like porosity, residual stress, and dimensional inaccuracies, particularly in complex geometries. Current experimental approaches to parameter optimization are time-intensive and costly, while existing computational models often lack the resolution or multi-physics integration needed to predict outcomes reliably. This research proposes a hybrid approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and optimize AM processes at scale. High-fidelity simulations will model heat transfer, melt pool dynamics, and solidification behavior across diverse material systems (e.g., metals, polymers) and printing configurations. ML algorithms will then iteratively refine parameter sets using simulation outputs and experimental validation data. The HPC environment is essential to manage the computational burden of these multi-scale, coupled simulations, which require parallel processing of millions of mesh elements and real-time data integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models for defect minimization, a parameter optimization toolkit adaptable to industry-standard AM hardware, and a publicly accessible dataset linking process variables to part properties. This work will directly support manufacturing industries in reducing material waste by up to 20% and improving production throughput, while advancing academic understanding of multi-physics interactions in AM. The computational framework will also serve as a template for addressing optimization challenges in other manufacturing domains, such as CNC machining and composite fabrication.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the identification and resolution of production problems in the manufacture of products. Includes instruction in machine operations, production line operations, engineering analysis, systems analysis, instrumentation, physical controls, automation, computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), manufacturing planning, quality control, and informational infrastructure.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational advertising, specifically addressing the challenge of optimizing real-time, cross-platform ad campaign performance in dynamic consumer environments. Modern advertising requires rapid analysis of vast datasets—including social media interactions, consumer behavior metrics, and real-time bidding logs—to deliver personalized content while balancing ethical, budgetary, and brand consistency constraints. Existing methods struggle to process these heterogeneous data streams at scale, limiting predictive accuracy and adaptability. The proposed research will develop machine learning models to simulate and predict consumer responses across diverse media channels, integrating natural language processing for ad copy analysis, computer vision for visual ad element optimization, and reinforcement learning for adaptive budget allocation. Agent-based modeling will simulate large-scale consumer networks to test campaign scenarios under varying market conditions. These computationally intensive tasks demand parallelized processing, GPU acceleration, and large-memory nodes to handle terabyte-scale datasets and complex model training workflows. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for real-time ad performance prediction, actionable insights into cross-platform audience engagement patterns, and open-source tools for ethical targeting parameter optimization. The project will directly support graduate-level coursework in data-driven advertising strategy and provide empirical foundations for three peer-reviewed studies on computational advertising efficiency. By enabling rapid iteration of campaign simulations that mirror real-world complexity, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical advertising models and practical industry needs while adhering to emerging privacy standards. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for multi-objective optimization tasks, which would be infeasible on local infrastructure.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creation, execution, transmission, and evaluation of commercial messages in various media intended to promote and sell products, services, and brands; and that prepares individuals to function as advertising assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in advertising theory, marketing strategy, advertising design and production methods, campaign methods and techniques, media management, related principles of business management, and applicable technical and equipment skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the complex interplay of environmental, demographic, and socio-political factors in the development and decline of ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern civilizations (ca. 3000–100 BCE). Current scholarship faces significant challenges in synthesizing disparate datasets—including paleoclimate proxies, settlement patterns, epigraphic records, and material culture distributions—at spatiotemporal scales necessary to test hypotheses about systemic resilience and cultural transformation. The proposed computational framework integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with geospatial analysis and Bayesian statistical methods to simulate human-environment interactions across multi-century timelines. Key objectives include reconstructing agricultural productivity under variable climate conditions, modeling trade network dynamics using archaeological provenance data, and analyzing demographic shifts through mortuary and settlement records. HPC resources are critical for running ensemble simulations that account for uncertainty in fragmentary historical datasets, as well as processing high-resolution LiDAR and multispectral imagery to identify previously undocumented archaeological features. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital platform for testing competing theories of societal collapse, open-access datasets correlating environmental and cultural variables, and methodological advancements in computational archaeology. By bridging disciplinary gaps between ancient history, environmental science, and complex systems theory, this project aims to establish new paradigms for studying long-term human adaptation while providing infrastructure for future collaborative research in antiquity studies. The computational demands of simultaneously processing terabyte-scale geospatial datasets, running thousands of parallelized simulation iterations, and applying machine learning classifiers to textual corpora necessitate dedicated HPC allocation beyond typical humanities computing capacities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Western and Non-Western cultures and related topics in the periods of Pre-history and Antiquity. Includes such disciplines as ancient languages, archeology, history, art history, geography, population studies, environmental studies, religious studies, and the social sciences.

abstract: The biological effects of ionizing radiation arise from complex molecular interactions that induce DNA damage, protein dysfunction, and oxidative stress, yet the precise mechanisms driving these outcomes remain incompletely resolved. This project seeks to advance mechanistic understanding of radiation-induced biomolecular perturbations by integrating atomistic simulations with kinetic modeling to study damage formation and repair dynamics in biophysically relevant systems. A central focus involves simulating radiation-induced ionization tracks in chromatin environments to quantify clustered DNA lesion formation and associated protein-DNA crosslinking events, which are critical drivers of genomic instability. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model the structural evolution of DNA-protein complexes (e.g., nucleosomes bound to repair enzymes) under radiation-mimetic conditions, while quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) approaches will resolve electron transfer processes that mediate oxidative damage to nucleic acids and proteins. Parallel kinetic Monte Carlo simulations will analyze competitive repair pathways for complex lesions, incorporating experimentally derived rate constants for base excision repair and homologous recombination proteins. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the computational cost of multi-scale modeling across spatial (Ångström to micrometer) and temporal (femtosecond to hour) scales. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for lesion persistence based on radiation quality (e.g., linear energy transfer) and chromatin conformation, as well as identification of molecular vulnerabilities that influence cellular radiosensitivity. This work will provide foundational insights into radiation biology by bridging molecular-scale damage events with organismal outcomes, with potential applications in optimizing therapeutic radiation regimens and mitigating off-target effects in healthy tissues.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the effects of radiation on organisms and biological systems. Includes instruction in particle physics, ionization, and biophysics of radiation perturbations, cellular and organismic repair systems, genetic and pathological effects of radiation, and the measurement of radiation dosages.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in construction site management by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to optimize real-time decision-making for resource allocation, risk mitigation, and schedule adherence. Construction projects face dynamic challenges, including fluctuating material costs, labor shortages, safety incidents, and environmental disruptions, which often lead to delays, budget overruns, and rework. Traditional management tools lack the computational capacity to integrate multi-source data—such as IoT sensor feeds, weather forecasts, equipment telemetry, and workforce productivity metrics—into actionable insights at scale. This research proposes a computational approach combining agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to create a digital twin of active construction sites. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of large datasets to simulate thousands of scenario permutations, evaluating the impact of variables like crew scheduling adjustments, equipment reallocations, or safety protocol changes. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical project data to predict bottlenecks and recommend preemptive interventions. Key outcomes include a scalable decision-support system capable of reducing project delays by modeling cascading impacts of disruptions and optimizing resource distribution across multiple concurrent sites. The computational framework will also incorporate safety analytics, using real-time worker positioning data and accident history to dynamically flag high-risk zones. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to advance adaptive construction management practices, reduce rework through predictive analytics, and improve compliance with safety and diversity standards. The resulting tools will be validated against case studies from commercial and infrastructure projects, with potential applications in training next-generation site managers via immersive simulation environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise, manage, and inspect construction sites, buildings, and associated facilities. Includes instruction in site safety, personnel supervision, labor relations, diversity training, construction documentation, scheduling, resource and cost control, bid strategies, rework prevention, construction insurance and bonding, accident management and investigation, applicable law and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in the operational readiness and sustainability of military Aerospace Ground Equipment (AGE) systems through advanced computational modeling and optimization. AGE systems—including power generators, hydraulic test units, and environmental control systems—face dynamic operational stressors such as thermal cycling, corrosion, and mechanical wear, exacerbated by deployment in austere environments. Traditional maintenance protocols rely on static schedules or reactive measures, leading to inefficiencies, unplanned downtime, and safety risks. This project proposes a predictive maintenance framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning (ML), and real-time sensor data analytics to model equipment degradation and optimize maintenance workflows. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-scale phenomena, such as electrochemical corrosion propagation in composite materials under variable humidity and temperature, or fluid-structure interactions in hydraulic systems during rapid pressure transients. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be coupled with ML models trained on historical maintenance records and sensor datasets to identify failure precursors. The computational workflow will also evaluate energy efficiency trade-offs in hybrid power systems, simulating scenarios where renewable energy integration reduces fossil fuel dependence without compromising mission-critical reliability. Outcomes include predictive degradation models for high-priority AGE components, actionable maintenance thresholds, and a digital twin prototype for real-time operational decision support. By transitioning from time-based to condition-based maintenance, this research aims to reduce lifecycle costs, enhance equipment availability, and mitigate risks associated with aging infrastructure. The interdisciplinary approach bridges computational engineering, materials science, and military logistics, advancing a specialized niche in defense-related infrastructure optimization that aligns with emerging priorities in sustainable military operations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology, and maintenance of ground-based systems and equipments used to support aviation flight operations and space operations. Includes instruction in computer science, electronics, basic sciences and quantitative methods, air conditioning and refrigeration, corrosion control, fluid power, hazardous materials, industrial safety, maintenance management, vehicle and equipment operation, and applications to specific ground support systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genetic and environmental determinants of complex diseases in diverse populations, with a focus on advancing equity in public health genetics. Genetic research increasingly highlights polygenic risk scores (PRS) and gene-environment interactions as critical drivers of disease susceptibility, yet existing models often lack generalizability across ancestrally diverse cohorts, perpetuating health disparities. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS), multi-omic data (genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic), and environmental exposure datasets from public biobanks. Machine learning models will be trained to identify population-specific risk variants and optimize PRS calibration while accounting for structural biases in genomic datasets. The scale of data—spanning millions of genetic variants, electronic health records, and geospatial environmental variables—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallelized processing, large-memory simulations, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include (1) validated, ancestry-informed risk prediction tools for conditions such as cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes, (2) mechanistic insights into gene-environment interplay in understudied populations, and (3) open-access computational pipelines to support ethical translation of genetic findings into public health practice. By elucidating genetic risk architectures within diverse social and environmental contexts, this work aims to directly inform equitable screening guidelines, precision prevention strategies, and policy discussions on the ethical use of polygenic risk tools. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome computational bottlenecks in handling multi-terabyte datasets and enable reproducible, large-scale analyses that bridge genetic discovery and population health implementation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to respond to the complex social, legal, ethical, and public health policy implications generated by genetic research. Includes instruction in biochemical genetics of complex diseases, bioethics, chromosomes and human disease, genetic counseling, genetic epidemiology, gene mapping, human population genetics, and the molecular basis of human inherited disease.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of subsurface fluid dynamics in heterogeneous petroleum reservoirs, addressing critical challenges in optimizing extraction efficiency and reducing environmental risks. Current reservoir simulation tools struggle to resolve fine-scale geological heterogeneities and multiphase flow interactions with sufficient accuracy, limiting their utility in real-world field management. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework that integrates high-resolution geological data, dynamic fluid behavior, and stress-sensitive fracture networks to improve predictions of hydrocarbon recovery and reservoir stability. The proposed approach combines finite element modeling (FEM) for geomechanical deformation with parallelized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate multiphase flow across spatially variable permeability fields. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters using historical production data and core sample analyses, reducing computational overhead while maintaining fidelity to physical constraints. HPC resources are essential to execute these simulations at the requisite spatiotemporal scales, enabling the use of stochastic ensembles to quantify uncertainty in reservoir performance under varying operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for reservoir engineers, optimized well placement strategies to mitigate gas coning and water encroachment, and predictive metrics for fracture propagation risks during enhanced oil recovery (EOR) operations. The project will also generate novel datasets correlating microseismic monitoring signals with simulated stress distributions, supporting early detection of casing failures or subsidence. By bridging gaps between reservoir characterization and operational decision-making, this work aims to reduce non-productive drilling time, extend field lifespans, and minimize environmental impacts through data-driven resource management. The computational workflows developed will be integrated into petroleum technology curricula, training students in advanced HPC applications for subsurface systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of oil and natural gas extraction and processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of petroleum extraction and related geology, petroleum field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, laboratory analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, environment and safety monitoring procedures for oil/gas fields and facilities, facility inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize energy-efficient building designs and construction workflows through high-fidelity simulations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. A critical challenge in residential and commercial construction is balancing structural integrity, material costs, and energy performance while adhering to evolving building codes and sustainability standards. Traditional modeling tools struggle to integrate multi-physics parameters—such as thermal dynamics, load-bearing capacity, and HVAC system efficiency—across complex, real-world building geometries. This research will address these limitations by deploying finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model building performance under diverse environmental and operational conditions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of large-scale 3D structural and energy models, incorporating variable inputs like regional climate data, material properties, and mechanical system configurations. Machine learning techniques will further refine predictive accuracy by identifying patterns in simulation outputs to recommend cost-optimal design adjustments. The project will validate results against empirical data from case studies of low-energy residential buildings and commercial retrofits. Outcomes will include an open-access toolkit for construction professionals to simulate energy use, thermal comfort, and material stress during the design phase, reducing iterative prototyping costs and accelerating compliance with green building certifications. By integrating computational rigor into construction workflows, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in the industry, lowering carbon footprints and operational costs for built environments. The scalability of the proposed methods will also support future research into smart materials and net-zero energy construction systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to residential and commercial building construction and remodeling. Includes instruction in construction equipment and safety; site preparation and layout; construction estimating; blueprint reading; building codes; framing; masonry; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning; electrical and mechanical systems; interior and exterior finishing; and plumbing.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical dynamics of connective tissue remodeling in chronic tendinopathy using multiscale computational modeling, a niche area intersecting computational biology, biophysics, and clinical medicine. Chronic tendon disorders affect millions globally, yet the mechanisms driving pathological tissue adaptation—particularly the interplay between cellular mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix degradation, and aberrant load distribution—remain poorly quantified. Current clinical interventions lack personalization due to gaps in understanding how microscale tissue properties influence macroscale mechanical failure. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations of collagen fibril deformation, agent-based models of fibroblast activity, and finite element analysis of tendon macrostructure. These models will be parameterized using multi-omics datasets (proteomics, transcriptomics) from patient-derived tendon samples and validated against biomechanical testing data. The computational workflow requires parallelized execution of coupled simulations across spatial and temporal scales, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure to handle terabytes of spatially resolved mechanical and biological data. Expected outcomes include predictive maps linking localized cellular responses to tissue-scale mechanical vulnerabilities, identification of novel biomarkers for early pathology detection, and optimization of load-modulation strategies for rehabilitation. By elucidating mechanobiological drivers of tendinopathy, this work aims to advance precision rehabilitation frameworks while demonstrating the utility of HPC in bridging molecular-scale biology to organ-level clinical phenomena. The developed models will be disseminated as open-source tools for the biomechanics community, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in understudied musculoskeletal pathologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of human cognitive workload dynamics in complex human-machine systems through computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability limitations in existing frameworks. Human factors research often relies on cognitive architectures (e.g., ACT-R, QN-MHP) to simulate decision-making and attention allocation, but these models struggle to replicate real-time interactions in large-scale systems with multiple concurrent tasks, such as aviation control interfaces or emergency response coordination platforms. The research problem centers on improving the fidelity and granularity of workload predictions under dynamic, high-stakes conditions, where traditional methods lack the computational power to model interactions at sufficient resolution. The proposed approach integrates parallelized cognitive simulations with machine learning techniques to optimize parameter spaces and validate models against empirical behavioral datasets (e.g., eye-tracking, response latency). HPC resources will enable the simultaneous execution of thousands of agent-based simulations across diverse scenarios, scaling to systems with >50 interactive elements and sub-second temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework to predict workload thresholds and system bottlenecks, validated through iterative comparison with experimental data from controlled lab studies on multitasking performance. This work will directly inform design principles for adaptive interfaces that mitigate cognitive overload in critical environments, contributing foundational insights into the limits of human attention allocation. By bridging gaps between theoretical cognitive models and real-world system complexity, the project aims to enhance the methodological toolkit of human factors psychology while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in behavioral research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to understand of interactions among humans and other elements of a system. Includes instruction in applying theory, principles, data and methods to design in order to optimize human well-being and overall system performance.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize irrigation system design and operational efficiency in water-scarce agricultural regions through advanced computational modeling. Current irrigation management practices often rely on generalized guidelines, leading to overwatering, energy waste, and reduced crop yields due to inadequate spatial or temporal resolution in water delivery. To address this, we propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework that integrates heterogeneous soil moisture data, real-time weather patterns, crop-specific water requirements, and hydraulic dynamics of irrigation infrastructure. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize finite element models of soil-water transport, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on multispectral satellite imagery and IoT sensor datasets from experimental farm sites. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of 3D hydrological simulations at sub-field scales (~1m resolution) and reinforcement learning optimizations for adaptive pumping schedules across distributed drip irrigation networks. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying energy-efficient irrigation thresholds under variable climate conditions and a decision-support system for infrastructure upgrades. By simulating millions of scenario combinations—factoring in crop rotations, aquifer depletion rates, and photovoltaic-powered pumping alternatives—the project will generate actionable insights for reducing water use by 15-25% in test regions while maintaining yields. The resulting computational framework will be scalable to diverse agricultural landscapes, supporting the program’s mission to advance precision irrigation technologies. This work directly addresses the urgent need for data-driven irrigation strategies in aridification-prone regions, with potential applications in training future agricultural technologists and informing policy on sustainable water allocation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in the field of agricultural technology and irrigation. Includes instruction in irrigation and drainage methodologies, pumping and delivery systems, system design and evaluation, and principles of installation and repair of irrigation systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamics of family systems under evolving sociocultural and economic pressures, with a focus on understanding resilience and adaptation mechanisms in non-traditional family structures. While family systems theory has historically relied on qualitative or small-scale quantitative studies, the complexity of modern family networks—including multigenerational households, blended families, and caregiver networks—demands large-scale, dynamic simulations to capture nonlinear interactions and emergent behaviors. The research problem centers on the lack of computational tools capable of integrating heterogeneous data (e.g., demographic records, time-use surveys, and qualitative narratives) to simulate family decision-making processes over extended temporal scales. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate family units as adaptive systems. Agents will be parameterized using behavioral data from longitudinal studies, incorporating variables such as role fluidity, resource allocation preferences, and stress-response thresholds. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters against empirical datasets, while network analysis tools will identify critical nodes and pathways influencing system stability. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of hypothetical scenarios to account for regional sociocultural variability and policy interventions. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable open-source toolkit for family systems simulation, (2) evidence-based insights into intervention points for enhancing family resilience during socioeconomic disruptions, and (3) novel metrics for quantifying relational interdependence within family networks. By bridging computational social science with family systems theory, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for studying kinship structures as complex adaptive systems, with potential applications in social work, education, and community health planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biochemical and genomic data in diagnosing inherited metabolic disorders necessitates advanced computational tools to uncover patterns, predict pathogenicity, and optimize diagnostic workflows. Current approaches for interpreting multi-omics datasets (e.g., metabolomic, enzymatic, and exome sequencing data) face limitations in scalability and integration, particularly when analyzing rare variants or heterogeneous patient cohorts. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to enhance the interpretation of biochemical genetic data and improve diagnostic accuracy. Leveraging HPC resources, we will build machine learning models trained on multi-institutional datasets to classify variants of uncertain significance in genes associated with metabolic pathways, predict biochemical phenotype-genotype correlations, and simulate enzyme kinetics under diverse mutational scenarios. Computational workflows will integrate structural modeling (via molecular dynamics simulations) with Bayesian networks to assess variant impacts on protein function and metabolic flux. Additionally, we will optimize pipelines for high-throughput analysis of mass spectrometry data to identify novel biomarkers in complex patient samples. The scale of these tasks—including the processing of terabyte-scale spectral datasets and millions of molecular dynamics time steps—requires parallelized computing, GPU acceleration, and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated decision-support tool for variant interpretation in clinical biochemical genetics, (2) publicly accessible databases linking computational predictions to clinical phenotypes, and (3) optimized protocols for rapid multi-omics data integration in diagnostic settings. This work will directly enhance the capability of clinical laboratories to resolve ambiguous cases, reduce diagnostic odysseys for patients with rare disorders, and provide a template for computational resource utilization in precision laboratory medicine. Resource allocation requests include 200,000 CPU-core hours, 50 TB of temporary storage for intermediate data, and access to GPU nodes for deep learning and molecular modeling tasks.
cip_definition: Research on how to perform and interpret biochemical analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases, and to serve as a consultant regarding laboratory diagnosis of a broad range of inherited disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to assess the impacts of climate change and anthropogenic land-use patterns on biodiversity in critical forest ecosystems, with a focus on identifying conservation priorities in rapidly changing regions. Current models often lack the resolution and integration of socio-environmental drivers necessary to inform adaptive management strategies. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run spatially explicit, dynamic simulations that couple ecological niche models, climate projections, and land-use change data at unprecedented scales. The computational approach will integrate multi-decadal remote sensing datasets, species occurrence records, and regional climate models (RCMs) within a Bayesian hierarchical framework to quantify uncertainty in biodiversity responses. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify non-linear relationships between ecosystem health metrics and stressors such as temperature extremes, habitat fragmentation, and resource extraction patterns. These workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and iterative parameter optimization, necessitating HPC capabilities. The resulting models will predict shifts in species distributions and ecosystem services under multiple climate scenarios, enabling the identification of regions most vulnerable to cascading biodiversity loss. Outcomes will directly support conservation planning by highlighting corridors for assisted species migration and zones requiring urgent policy intervention. By quantifying trade-offs between economic development and ecological resilience, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in environmental decision-making tools. The scalability of the framework will allow future adaptation to other ecosystems, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration across environmental science, computational modeling, and policy analysis. Successful implementation will provide stakeholders with actionable, data-driven strategies to mitigate anthropogenic impacts on natural resources while addressing socio-economic realities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on environment-related issues using scientific, social scientific, or humanistic approaches or a combination. Includes instruction in the basic principles of ecology and environmental science and related subjects such as policy, politics, law, economics, social aspects, planning, pollution control, natural resources, and the interactions of human beings and nature.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenges of analyzing and processing large-scale visual datasets in photojournalism, where ethical accuracy, real-time reporting, and narrative authenticity are paramount. As photojournalists increasingly rely on high-resolution still and motion imagery—including 360-degree video, drone footage, and augmented reality overlays—traditional workflows struggle to manage the computational demands of editing, verifying, and ethically contextualizing content under time-sensitive conditions. This research proposes the development of an AI-assisted computational pipeline to automate resource-intensive tasks such as detecting manipulated media, reconstructing 3D scenes from crowd-sourced imagery, and optimizing multi-format storytelling workflows. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the training of deep learning models on diverse, ethically sourced photojournalistic datasets, including conflict zones and disaster environments, while preserving chain-of-custody metadata critical to journalistic integrity. Parallelized processing will be applied to simulate real-world scenarios, such as rapid forensic analysis of suspected deepfakes or dynamic recompilation of multi-angle footage for interactive news platforms. Outcomes will include open-source tools for photojournalists to validate visual authenticity, reduce biases in AI-augmented editorial decisions, and streamline the integration of immersive media into deadline-driven reporting. The project aligns with the program’s emphasis on ethical standards and field operations, offering scalable solutions to enhance transparency in visual storytelling while maintaining compliance with media law and policy frameworks. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge the gap between computational innovation and journalistic practice, ensuring photojournalists can meet evolving demands without compromising procedural rigor or public trust.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of still and motion photography in journalism and prepares individuals to function as news photographers and photographic editors. Includes instruction in photography, journalism, studio procedures and techniques, camera and equipment operation and technique, news editing, print and film editing, news scene composition, subject surveillance, media law and policy, news team field operations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of hypnotherapy’s neurocognitive mechanisms and optimize therapeutic protocols. While hypnotherapy is increasingly recognized for its clinical potential in pain management, emotional regulation, and behavioral modification, its efficacy remains variable across individuals, and the underlying neural and psychological processes are poorly characterized. A key challenge lies in modeling the dynamic interactions between hypnotic suggestion, brain activity, and behavioral outcomes, which involve complex, high-dimensional datasets spanning neuroimaging, physiological signals, and patient-reported metrics. This research will employ computational neuroscience and machine learning approaches to address these gaps. First, we will develop biophysical network models simulating cortical and subcortical activity during hypnotic states, calibrated using resting-state fMRI and EEG data from clinical cohorts. Second, reinforcement learning algorithms will be applied to personalize suggestion strategies based on real-time psychophysiological feedback (e.g., heart rate variability, galvanic skin response). Third, large-scale Bayesian inference methods will identify predictors of hypnotic susceptibility by integrating multimodal data (genetic, cognitive, neuroanatomical) from diverse populations. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model optimization, and high-fidelity simulations of brain-network dynamics—all necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models of therapeutic responsiveness, data-driven guidelines for optimizing induction techniques, and novel biomarkers for monitoring trance depth. By elucidating the neurocomputational principles of hypnosis, this work will enhance the reproducibility and precision of hypnotherapy interventions, ultimately improving clinical outcomes in chronic pain, anxiety, and trauma-related disorders. The project will also establish an open-access computational toolkit for the hypnotherapy research community, fostering collaboration and methodological standardization in this emerging interdisciplinary field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to employ the controlled inducement of altered states of consciousness, or trance, to reduce pain, resolve emotional conflicts, and enhance communications as part of diagnostic and treatment programs. Includes instruction in the principles of hypnosis and suggestion, induction and deepening, post-hypnotic suggestion, awakening techniques, regression, pacing and leading, resistance transformation, client testing and management, practice management and regulation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Parasitic infections remain a critical global health challenge, with complex host-parasite interactions often driving pathogenicity and treatment resistance. This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying immune evasion by parasitic protozoa, particularly *Plasmodium* and *Trypanosoma* species, which exhibit sophisticated strategies to circumvent host defenses. A central challenge lies in modeling the dynamic interplay between parasite surface proteins and host immune factors at scale, as experimental approaches alone struggle to capture the rapid conformational changes and evolutionary adaptations involved. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework leveraging molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning to predict antigenic variation patterns and binding affinities of parasite-derived ligands. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform large-scale MD simulations of key parasite proteins (e.g., *Plasmodium* PfEMP1 variants) interacting with host receptors under varying biochemical conditions. These simulations will be coupled with phylogenetic analyses of parasite populations to identify conserved epitopes vulnerable to targeted interventions. Additionally, we will develop predictive models of drug resistance emergence by analyzing genomic and proteomic datasets from field isolates. The computational pipeline will utilize GPU-accelerated workflows for real-time analysis of terabyte-scale simulation outputs. Expected outcomes include identifying novel molecular targets for therapeutic disruption of immune evasion and generating predictive maps of antigenic diversity to guide vaccine design. This work directly aligns with parasitology’s focus on ecological exploitative relationships and chemotherapeutic development, while avoiding overlap with excluded fields such as general biochemistry or genomics. By elucidating evolutionary drivers of host-parasite conflict, the project aims to advance translational strategies for mitigating disease burden in endemic regions. Access to HPC resources will enable the execution of computationally intensive simulations that are currently infeasible with local infrastructure, significantly accelerating progress toward these goals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biological organisms living in ecologically exploitative and competitive relationships with host organisms, and the role of parasites in causing injury, disease, and environmental damage. Includes instruction in vector biology, immunoparasitology, medical parasitology, molecular biology of parasitical associations, veterinary and comparative parasitology, chemotherapeutics, and ecological and systematic parasitology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a critical gap in Disability Studies: the large-scale analysis of cultural and narrative patterns shaping societal perceptions of disability. While qualitative methods dominate the field, computational approaches are underutilized in examining how disability is represented across expansive digital archives, including literature, media, legal texts, and artistic works. The research problem centers on identifying systemic biases, evolving discourses, and intersectional dynamics within these sources at a scale unachievable through manual analysis. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and semantic network mapping, to analyze multilingual corpora comprising millions of texts and metadata from disability-related publications, advocacy materials, and creative works. Concurrently, computer vision algorithms will process visual art and media collections to classify representations of disability, accessibility symbolism, and embodied diversity. These computational workflows require HPC resources to manage distributed data storage, parallelize model training across GPU nodes, and optimize memory-intensive tasks such as cross-modal analysis linking textual and visual datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of historical and contemporary narrative trends influencing disability stigma or empowerment, a publicly accessible toolkit for computational Disability Studies, and frameworks for ethically centering disability perspectives in AI model design. By integrating HPC-driven insights with critical disability theory, this work aims to redefine methodological norms in cultural and group studies while directly informing advocacy strategies for inclusive representation. The resource allocation will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, advancing interdisciplinary scholarship that bridges humanities inquiry with computational social science.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature, meaning, and consequences of what it is to be defined as disabled and explores the historical, cultural, economic, physiological, and socio-political dynamics of disability. Includes instruction in disability rights, legal issues, and public policy; literature, philosophy, and the arts; and/or research in the social sciences, education, and health sciences addressing social and experiential aspects of disability.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural memory formation in digital spaces through the lens of power asymmetries and transnational data flows. As digital platforms increasingly mediate cultural production and preservation, traditional archival methods fail to capture the scale, interactivity, and algorithmic curation inherent to contemporary cultural datasets. The research addresses this gap by analyzing multimodal digital archives—including social media corpora, decentralized content repositories, and institutionally hosted collections—to map how hegemonic narratives emerge and circulate across geopolitical boundaries. Using high-performance computing (HPC), the team will apply natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks to trace semantic shifts, attribution patterns, and metadata hierarchies within 15+ terabyte datasets spanning six languages. Computational critical discourse analysis will be enhanced through transformer-based models fine-tuned on postcolonial and feminist theory frameworks, enabling systematic detection of epistemic erasures and platform-induced biases in cultural representation. A novel adaptive sampling algorithm will prioritize underrepresented voices in training data to counteract structural marginalization in machine learning workflows. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational methodology for interrogating cultural power relations in digital ecosystems, visualized through interactive spatial-temporal network graphs. The work will produce the first longitudinal study of algorithmic gatekeeping in UNESCO’s endangered language archives while developing open-source tools for ethical large-scale cultural analytics. By synthesizing critical theory with distributed computing techniques, this project establishes an interdisciplinary paradigm for studying techno-cultural systems, requiring HPC resources for parallelized text processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and cross-regional data federation. Results will inform policy frameworks for equitable digital heritage preservation and provide humanities scholars with replicable computational workflows for power structure analysis.
cip_title: Cultural Studies/ Critical Theory and Analysis
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the analysis and critique of culture in its varied forms, including values, ideas, belief systems, and expressive acts, and the relationship between cultural forms, everyday life, and structures of power. Includes instruction in anthropology, communications, history, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, and sociology, as well as recent theories and methodologies such as semiotics, deconstruction, postcolonial studies, gender theory, and ethnography.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the compositional history and transmission of pseudepigraphical texts associated with biblical traditions through advanced computational modeling, a task requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While traditional textual criticism relies on manual analysis of manuscript variants, our research addresses the challenge of modeling complex, non-linear textual relationships across thousands of variants in understudied parabiblical materials (e.g., Enochic literature, Testamentary texts). The computational problem involves analyzing multidimensional data—including linguistic patterns, intertextual allusions, and scribal markers—to reconstruct plausible transmission pathways and identify previously unrecognized compositional strata. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for ancient Semitic languages and Koine Greek, we will process digitized corpora from the Dead Sea Scrolls, Septuagint, and early Jewish pseudepigrapha. Graph neural networks will then map textual dependencies, while phylogenetic algorithms adapted from bioinformatics will model branching relationships across manuscript traditions. A key innovation involves training transformer-based models on curated datasets to detect subtle stylistic shifts indicative of redactional layers, addressing longstanding debates about textual unity and authorship. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the scale of data (∼10 TB of high-resolution manuscript images and transcriptions) and the computational intensity of ensemble modeling approaches. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible digital corpus of annotated textual variants, 2) probabilistic models of compositional development for three target pseudepigrapha, and 3) new computational frameworks for analyzing ancient textual plurality. This work bridges biblical studies, computational linguistics, and cultural heritage informatics, offering methodological advances for understanding the dynamic textual landscapes that shaped early Jewish and Christian thought.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Christian and/or Jewish Bible and related literature, with an emphasis on understanding and interpreting the theological, doctrinal, and ethical messages contained therein. May include preparation for applying these studies in various religious vocations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze nonlinear dynamics in heterogeneous agent macroeconomic models with stochastic shocks, a problem intractable to closed-form solutions due to high-dimensional state spaces and path-dependent interactions. Traditional equilibrium analyses often rely on restrictive homogeneity assumptions or linear approximations that fail to capture emergent complexity in financial networks, labor market frictions, and climate-economic feedback loops. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to implement massively parallelized Monte Carlo simulations coupled with numerical continuation methods, enabling systematic exploration of bifurcation thresholds and resilience regimes in coupled economic-ecological systems. The computational architecture will combine agent-based modeling techniques with stochastic optimal control solvers, operating across multiple scales from microeconomic decision rules to macroeconomic stability metrics. Key challenges include adaptive meshing for value function iteration in 8+ dimensional state spaces and Bayesian estimation of nonlinear impulse responses using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of early-warning indicators for critical transitions in debt-climate cascades, (2) quantitative assessment of policy intervention efficacy under deep uncertainty, and (3) open-source modular code for heterodox economic system simulation. The HPC resources requested are essential for achieving statistical significance across parameter sweeps (>10^5 parallelized runs), maintaining numerical stability in stiff differential-algebraic systems, and storing petabyte-scale output for topological data analysis. This interdisciplinary synthesis of dynamical systems theory, computational statistics, and economic modeling aims to establish new standards for complexity-aware policy design while advancing numerical methods for high-dimensional economic systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical methods to the development of economic theory, models, and quantitative analysis. Includes instruction in data analysis, applied business economics, calculus, econometrics, linear algebra, microeconomic theory, probability, and statistical methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize high-power laser systems for industrial and scientific applications, addressing critical challenges in beam quality control, thermal management, and nonlinear optical effects. Current experimental approaches to mitigate performance-limiting factors such as thermal lensing and Brillouin scattering remain resource-intensive and iterative, while existing simulations often oversimplify multiphysics interactions in laser cavities and beam delivery systems.
