We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for electromagnetic wave propagation with coupled thermal-fluid dynamics models to capture the complex interplay between optical, thermal, and mechanical phenomena in solid-state and fiber laser architectures. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate parameter space exploration for novel resonator designs and cooling configurations. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for Maxwell's equations and custom Python-based post-processing pipelines to analyze mode stability, power scalability, and beam profile degradation under realistic operating conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for laser system optimization that reduce prototype development cycles by 30-50%, as well as open-source simulation tools for nonlinear optical effects in gain media. These results will directly support next-generation laser applications in precision manufacturing, lidar systems, and quantum photonics research. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale 3D simulations of full laser assemblies—currently infeasible on departmental clusters—while maintaining the temporal resolution required to model ultrafast optical phenomena. Successful implementation will provide both fundamental insights into thermal-optic coupling mechanisms and practical design guidelines for industry partners, advancing the Laser and Optical Technology program's mission to bridge theoretical innovation with applied engineering solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using lasers and other optical for commercial or research purposes. Includes instruction in laser and optical principles, testing and maintenance procedures, safety precautions, specific applications to various tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: Endocrine disorders such as diabetes, obesity, and thyroid dysfunction arise from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility, environmental factors, and metabolic dysregulation. While advances in high-throughput technologies have enabled large-scale generation of multi-omics data, integrating these heterogeneous datasets to uncover disease mechanisms remains computationally prohibitive. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular drivers of polygenic endocrine disorders. We propose a computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), deep learning-based analysis of epigenomic and transcriptomic data, and dynamic network modeling of metabolic pathways. These methods will be applied to a cohort of 10,000 patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity, integrating genomic variants, DNA methylation profiles, single-cell RNA sequencing, and longitudinal clinical data. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, training of multimodal neural networks for predictive phenotyping, and stochastic simulations of hormone-receptor interactions under varying metabolic states. The HPC environment is essential for enabling scalable data integration, reducing model training times from weeks to days, and performing millions of molecular dynamics simulations to identify allosteric binding sites. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel genetic-epigenetic interactions influencing insulin resistance, predictive models of diabetes progression, and candidate therapeutic targets for adrenal dysfunction. This research will provide a computational foundation for precision endocrinology, enabling data-driven stratification of patient subgroups and optimization of hormone-based therapies. The requested resources will directly support the development of open-source tools for endocrine research, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational domains.
cip_definition: Research on disorders of the internal (endocrine) glands such as the thyroid and adrenal glands, and to deal with disorders such as diabetes, metabolic and nutritional disorders, obesity, pituitary diseases, and menstrual and sexual problems. Requires prior completion of a residency program in internal medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze the pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) of pre-service chemistry teachers, with a focus on identifying gaps in their ability to translate complex chemical concepts into effective classroom instruction. A critical challenge in chemistry teacher education is the lack of data-driven tools to systematically evaluate how trainees internalize and contextualize abstract topics such as molecular interactions, reaction mechanisms, and thermodynamics. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate classroom scenarios, model trainee decision-making processes, and generate predictive analytics on instructional effectiveness. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) to replicate student-teacher dynamics, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to visualize chemical processes for educational use cases, and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze lesson plans and dialogue patterns from teaching practicums. These methods will be combined in a unified workflow using Python-based frameworks (e.g., MDAnalysis, Mesa) scaled across multiple nodes to handle large datasets of training assessments, video recordings, and curricular materials. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model correlating specific PCK deficiencies with measurable instructional behaviors, (2) dynamic visualizations of chemical phenomena optimized for pedagogical clarity, and (3) a repository of simulated teaching scenarios for training purposes. The project will directly enhance the Chemistry Teacher Education program by providing evidence-based strategies to refine course content, address individualized learning needs, and improve the integration of computational literacy into teacher preparation. By bridging molecular-level understanding with classroom practice, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for using HPC resources in discipline-specific teacher development, ultimately supporting secondary students’ engagement with chemistry through better-prepared educators.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach chemistry programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of microbial community dynamics in engineered biosystems, with applications in sustainable bioremediation and bioenergy production. Microbial consortia drive critical biochemical processes in systems such as anaerobic digesters and bioelectrochemical reactors, but their complex interactions—spanning metabolic cross-feeding, spatial heterogeneity, and environmental stressors—remain poorly understood. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve these multi-scale, nonlinear interactions, limiting predictive design of robust biosystems. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-agent modeling framework that integrates genome-scale metabolic networks, dynamic flux balance analysis, and spatially explicit agent-based simulations. This framework will capture individual microbial behavior, metabolite exchange, and community-level emergent properties under varying operational conditions (e.g., substrate gradients, pH fluctuations). HPC resources are essential to parameterize models using large-scale omics datasets, perform stochastic simulations of communities exceeding 10^5 cells, and conduct sensitivity analyses across high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of key design principles for stabilizing microbial consortia in continuous-flow systems, (2) predictive models linking reactor configuration to community function, and (3) open-source simulation tools for optimizing biosystem performance. The results will directly inform ongoing experimental work on bioaugmentation strategies for heavy-metal contaminated wastewater treatment, as well as the design of syntrophic communities for enhanced biogas production. By bridging gaps between systems biology and bioprocess engineering, this computational work will accelerate the development of scalable, adaptive biosystems critical to addressing environmental and energy challenges.
detailed_field: Biological/ biosystems engineering and biomedical technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and management of biological systems; and includes applications to biology, biochemistry, ecology, and microbiology. Includes instruction in organic chemistry; microbiology; biochemistry; chemical, biological, biochemical, and process engineering; thermodynamics; process control; kinetics and reactor design; electric circuits; biosystem modeling; and bioelectronics and instrumentation.

abstract: The management of diseases affecting the inner ear and temporal bone remains challenging due to the complex microanatomy and biomechanical interactions underlying auditory and vestibular function. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized anatomical models, which may not adequately capture patient-specific pathophysiology or predict individualized treatment outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multiscale computational models of the human temporal bone and its neurotological systems. High-resolution imaging data from clinical CT and MRI scans will be integrated into finite element models simulating mechanical, acoustic, and fluid-structure interactions within the cochlea, semicircular canals, and associated neural structures. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to optimize model parameters using retrospective clinical datasets, enabling predictive analyses of surgical interventions, implant design optimization, and drug delivery systems. The computational workflows will be validated against intraoperative findings and post-treatment outcome data from collaborating neurotology clinics. By enabling submillimeter-scale simulations of pathological processes—such as otosclerosis, Meniere’s disease, and superior canal dehiscence—this research aims to uncover mechanistic insights into disease progression and treatment resistance. The anticipated outcomes include the development of patient-specific surgical planning tools, virtual testing platforms for implantable devices, and predictive models for non-invasive therapies. This work will provide a computational foundation for advancing precision medicine in neurotology, with direct implications for improving functional outcomes in hearing restoration and vestibular rehabilitation. The scale of these simulations necessitates HPC resources, as individual models may require >10^6 core-hours to resolve multiphysics interactions across anatomical scales while maintaining clinical relevance.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat diseases of the ear and temporal bone, including disorders of hearing and balance.

abstract: The increasing complexity of health datasets and the demand for precision in predictive modeling necessitate advanced computational resources to address critical public health challenges. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal health data—including electronic health records, genomic sequences, and socioenvironmental variables—to identify risk factors and optimize intervention strategies for chronic diseases in underserved populations. A key challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets with varying spatial, temporal, and structural resolutions while accounting for biases and missing data. Traditional computing infrastructures lack the capacity to process these datasets efficiently, limiting the scalability and reproducibility of analyses. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for relational data integration, Bayesian hierarchical models for uncertainty quantification, and agent-based simulations to model population-level health outcomes under diverse intervention scenarios. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization for machine learning models, and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to assess robustness. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for federated learning across distributed health datasets, (2) predictive models linking polygenic risk scores with environmental exposures to forecast disease incidence, and (3) open-source tools for simulating resource allocation strategies in low-resource settings. This work will directly inform public health policies by quantifying the cost-effectiveness of targeted interventions, while advancing methodological innovations in health data science. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the project’s aims within a clinically relevant timeframe, as local clusters lack sufficient GPU nodes and memory bandwidth to handle the proposed workloads. By enabling rapid iteration of complex models, this allocation will accelerate discoveries in population health optimization and translational research.
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between urban built environments and psychological well-being, with a focus on loneliness, stress, and restorative experiences in densely populated regions. While prior studies highlight correlations between environmental features (e.g., green spaces, communal areas) and mental health outcomes, the dynamic mechanisms underlying these relationships—particularly across diverse sociocultural groups—remain poorly quantified. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling framework integrating agent-based simulations (ABS) with machine learning-driven analysis of multi-modal datasets, including geospatial records, anonymized mobile device mobility traces, and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data from 5,000 participants across 15 global cities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale ABS scenarios that simulate daily routines, social interactions, and environmental exposures for synthetic populations calibrated to real-world demographic and psychological profiles. Concurrently, graph neural networks will analyze temporal patterns in mobility and self-reported well-being data to identify context-dependent predictors of environmental stress buffering. The computational pipeline will leverage parallelized processing for (1) parameter space exploration in ABS experiments testing urban design interventions and (2) training of attention-based models to detect subtle environment-behavior linkages across subgroups. Outcomes will yield a validated predictive toolkit for assessing how spatially embedded stressors and resources interact with individual differences to shape mental health trajectories. This work directly supports applied environmental psychology goals by enabling evidence-based recommendations for equitable urban planning and personalized therapeutic landscape design. The requested resources will overcome current limitations in modeling complex person-environment systems at scale, advancing translational applications in community counseling and preventive mental health infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of behavioral interactions between human beings and the environment in individual and group contexts, and ways to improve them. Includes instruction in contextual theory; statistics; physiological, social, and psychological responses to natural and technological hazards and disease; environmental perception and cognition; loneliness and stress; and psychological aspects of environmental design and planning.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze doctrinal transmission and philosophical synthesis across Buddhist traditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges of scale and complexity in sacred text analysis. While Buddhist studies has produced extensive scholarship on individual traditions, comparative analyses of cross-school doctrinal evolution remain limited by the manual examination of vast, multilingual corpora spanning 2,500 years. This research will computationally process digitized primary sources—including the Pali Tipitaka, Chinese Āgamas, Tibetan Kangyur/Tengyur, and Mahayana sutras—along with their commentaries in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and other Asian languages. The computational approach integrates transformer-based language models fine-tuned for Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit and literary Chinese, graph neural networks to map concept diffusion across schools, and phylogenetic algorithms to model textual genealogies. HPC resources are critical for training cross-lingual embeddings across 10+ historical languages, running large-scale topic modeling on over 50,000 texts, and simulating doctrinal network formation through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal correlations between Theravada Abhidhamma and Yogācāra philosophical systems, 2) quantitative models of ritual-textual interdependence in Vajrayana traditions, and 3) an open-access knowledge graph visualizing the development of key concepts like pratītyasamutpāda (dependent origination) across 15 Buddhist branches. By enabling systematic analysis of pan-Buddhist intellectual exchange at unprecedented scale, this work will provide new empirical foundations for understanding Buddhism as a dynamic, interconnected philosophical system rather than discrete schools. The computational pipelines developed will establish reproducible methods for textual analysis in religious studies, with potential applications to other tradition-based philosophical systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy preached by Siddartha Gautama, the Buddha, in ancient India and subsequently interpreted by his disciples and apostles; together with the intellectual, cultural, social, and ritual developments of the faith and its branches. Includes instruction in Buddhist sacred literature (Tripitaka, etc.) and study of one or more of the main branches including Early Buddhism, Hinayana, Theravada, Madhyamaka, Yogacara, Pure Land, Shingon, Tendai, Nichiren Shu, Zen, Tibetan, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, and others.

abstract: The development of advanced materials with tailored properties for extreme environments remains a critical challenge in materials science, particularly for multi-component systems such as high-entropy alloys (HEAs) and ceramics. These materials exhibit exceptional mechanical, thermal, and chemical stability but require precise control of atomic-scale interactions and phase behavior. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve the complex interplay of entropy, enthalpy, and kinetic effects in these systems, limiting predictive design. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model atomic-scale interactions, phase stability, and defect dynamics in multi-component materials under extreme thermal and mechanical conditions. The research will employ density functional theory (DFT) to calculate thermodynamic properties and interatomic potentials, coupled with large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study microstructural evolution and deformation mechanisms. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to accelerate the exploration of composition-property relationships and identify promising candidate systems. Simulations will target systems with 10^4–10^6 atoms, requiring parallelized computations across thousands of cores to achieve the necessary spatial and temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for phase stability in HEAs under high stress, mechanistic insights into dislocation and crack propagation in multi-component ceramics, and a curated database of computed properties for 50+ novel compositions. These results will guide experimental synthesis efforts funded by a related grant, reducing trial-and-error approaches. The computational workflows developed will be shared via open-source platforms to enable broader community use. By bridging atomic-scale modeling with macroscale performance predictions, this work aims to advance the design of materials for next-generation energy, aerospace, and manufacturing applications. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational cost of multi-million-atom MD simulations and high-throughput DFT screening, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in materials sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for urban microclimate optimization in dense, mixed-use environments. Traditional environmental design approaches often rely on static climate data or simplified simulations, which inadequately capture dynamic interactions between built forms, vegetation, human activity, and localized weather patterns. The proposed work addresses this gap by creating a computational framework that integrates real-time sensor data, parametric urban geometry, and machine learning to simulate hyperlocal thermal comfort, airflow, and energy use at neighborhood scales. Using GPU-accelerated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and agent-based modeling, the project will analyze how design interventions—such as façade retrofits, green infrastructure placement, and pedestrian pathway configurations—affect microclimatic conditions under diverse seasonal and diurnal scenarios. A key innovation involves coupling these simulations with generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on global climate datasets to predict emergent microclimate behaviors in underrepresented urban typologies. The computational intensity of modeling 3D urban canyons at sub-meter resolution, combined with stochastic human movement patterns and multi-physics interactions, necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing and large-scale data aggregation. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for designers to evaluate climate-responsive strategies during early-stage planning, with applications for reducing urban heat island effects, improving outdoor thermal comfort, and lowering cooling energy demands. By bridging architectural design, urban ecology, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish scalable methods for evidence-based environmental design in rapidly urbanizing regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design public and private spaces, indoor and outdoor, for leisure, recreational, commercial, and living purposes, and for professional practice as environmental designers and architects. Includes instruction in the design and planning of public and private open spaces and their relationship to buildings and other aspects of the built environment; facilities management; related aspects of interior design and architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: Mental health disorders present complex challenges requiring personalized interventions, yet psychiatric nursing practice lacks robust tools to predict individual patient outcomes or optimize treatment plans. This project seeks to develop computational models that identify patterns in patient responses to psychiatric nursing interventions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets. The research focuses on integrating electronic health records (EHRs), patient-reported outcomes, and behavioral data (e.g., sleep patterns, medication adherence) from individuals with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder. Machine learning algorithms, including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, will be applied to model longitudinal trajectories of symptom severity, crisis events, and recovery milestones. A key innovation involves simulating the impact of nurse-led interventions (e.g., psychoeducation strategies, crisis de-escalation techniques) through agent-based modeling, which requires parallel computing to account for heterogeneous patient profiles and care settings. Computational demands are substantial due to the need to process high-dimensional temporal data (>10,000 patient-years) and perform sensitivity analyses across demographic and clinical variables. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide treatment prioritization, risk stratification for relapse, and dynamic decision-support systems for psychiatric nurses. By elucidating how specific nursing actions correlate with stabilization rates and quality-of-life metrics, this work will advance evidence-based practices in mental health nursing. The models will be validated against prospective clinical data from three community mental health centers, with results disseminated through open-source tools tailored for nursing researchers. This project directly addresses the NIH’s emphasis on computational psychiatry while prioritizing nurse-driven care mechanisms, ultimately aiming to reduce trial-and-error approaches in mental health management and improve resource allocation in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to promote mental health and provide nursing care to patients with mental, emotional or behavioral disorders, in mental institutions or other settings. Includes instruction in psychopathology, behavioral health, counseling and intervention strategies, psychoeducation, mental health assessment and dual diagnosis, stabilization and management of psychotic illness, psychiatric care and rehabilitation, substance abuse, and crisis intervention.

abstract: Veterinary emergency and critical care medicine faces significant challenges in predicting outcomes and optimizing treatment strategies for animals with acute, life-threatening conditions such as sepsis, polytrauma, or toxicologic emergencies. Current clinical decision-making relies on static protocols and limited predictive tools, which often fail to account for the dynamic interplay of multi-organ dysfunction, patient-specific physiologic variability, and time-sensitive interventions. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model critical illness trajectories and simulate treatment responses in veterinary patients using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate species-specific physiological data, electronic health records, and biomarker dynamics to construct multiscale models that capture cellular, organ-level, and systemic responses to acute insults. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to retrospective datasets from veterinary intensive care units (ICUs) to identify predictive signatures of organ failure progression. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model the effects of fluid resuscitation, vasopressor regimens, and extracorporeal therapies under varying physiologic conditions. The HPC environment is essential for running parallelized simulations of heterogeneous patient cohorts, optimizing treatment parameters via iterative in silico trials, and processing high-frequency monitoring data in near-real time. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for early detection of decompensation, validated computational protocols for crisis scenarios, and a decision-support tool to personalize resuscitation strategies. This work will advance the understanding of critical illness pathophysiology in diverse animal species while establishing a platform for translating computational insights into improved clinical workflows. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce mortality in veterinary ICUs, enhance resource allocation during emergencies, and provide a scalable framework for future studies in veterinary translational medicine.
cip_title: Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Medicine
cip_definition: Research focused on the emergency treatment and management of care for animals with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. May included related research in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures, and long-term care of critically diseased animals.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of coupled human-natural systems in the context of climate adaptation and sustainable resource management. A critical challenge in environmental policy lies in balancing ecological resilience with socioeconomic demands, particularly as climate change exacerbates uncertainties in resource availability. Traditional models often oversimplify dynamic feedbacks between land-use decisions, biodiversity shifts, and hydrological regimes, limiting their utility for regional-scale policy design. To address this gap, we propose developing an integrated computational framework that combines agent-based modeling, machine learning-enhanced ecosystem simulations, and high-resolution spatial analysis. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of multi-scale datasets, including satellite-derived land cover time series, species distribution records, and stakeholder behavior patterns across a case study region in a climate-vulnerable watershed. Key computational tasks include parameterizing stochastic climate scenarios, training neural networks to predict habitat fragmentation thresholds, and optimizing adaptive management strategies through evolutionary algorithms. By quantifying trade-offs between conservation targets and resource extraction pathways under varying policy interventions, this work aims to generate decision-support tools for prioritizing cost-effective, ecologically viable management plans. The expected outcomes include publicly accessible codebases for coupled human-environment modeling, peer-reviewed insights into threshold behaviors of managed ecosystems, and policy briefs addressing scalability challenges in regional climate adaptation frameworks. Access to HPC resources is essential given the project’s reliance on ensemble simulations across 10,000+ parameter combinations, real-time integration of large geospatial datasets (>100 TB), and computationally intensive sensitivity analyses. This work directly supports the program’s mission by bridging technical gaps in resource management planning while fostering interdisciplinary methodologies for environmental governance.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Management and Policy, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, manage, and evaluate programs to protect and regulate natural habitats and renewable natural resources. Includes instruction in the principles of wildlife and conservation biology, environmental science, animal population surveying, natural resource economics, management techniques for various habitats, applicable law and policy, administrative and communications skills, and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the evidence-based integration of Yoga Therapy and Ayurvedic principles into personalized health interventions. Despite growing clinical interest in Yoga and Ayurveda for managing chronic conditions such as chronic pain, anxiety, and metabolic disorders, a critical gap remains in understanding how individualized practices—tailored to biomechanical, physiological, and dosha-based profiles—elicit measurable therapeutic outcomes. Current studies often rely on generalized protocols, neglecting the dynamic interplay between posture sequences, breathwork, and individual anatomical or metabolic variability. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining biomechanical modeling, multi-omics data integration, and machine learning to simulate and predict personalized Yoga Therapy outcomes. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of musculoskeletal stress distributions during complex asana sequences, optimized via finite element analysis, while parallelized workflows will process genomic, metabolomic, and wearable sensor data to identify biomarkers linked to therapeutic efficacy. Neural networks trained on clinical datasets will map interactions between Ayurvedic dosha assessments, practice modifications, and patient-reported outcomes, enabling probabilistic recommendations for condition-specific protocols. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for designing adaptive Yoga Therapy regimens, validated through partnerships with clinical Yoga therapists. This work will establish a novel paradigm for precision mind-body interventions, bridging ancient practices with computational biomedicine. By quantifying the mechanistic basis of Yoga’s therapeutic effects, the project aims to elevate its clinical credibility, inform accreditation standards, and expand access to personalized, data-driven holistic care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional instructors in the spiritual and physical therapy of Yoga in private, institutional, and clinical settings. Includes instruction in the principles of Ayurveda, philosophy of Yoga, warm-up and progressive exercises, breathing exercises, meditation, Yamas and Niyamas, instructional techniques, posture adjustment, student/client counseling and assessment, advanced Yoga disciplines and styles, business practices, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in large-scale, cross-cultural analyses of folklore as dynamic expressions of collective identity and creativity. While folklore studies have traditionally relied on qualitative methods, the increasing availability of digitized oral histories, folk narratives, and performance records from diverse communities presents an opportunity to systematically investigate patterns of aesthetic adaptation and cultural transmission. However, analyzing these heterogeneous datasets—spanning multilingual texts, audiovisual materials, and ethnographic metadata—requires computational resources beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations to trace motif distributions across regional folklore corpora. Concurrently, graph-based algorithms will model the nonlinear dissemination of narrative elements through social and kinship networks inferred from ethnographic records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on fragmented or non-standardized textual data, running multilevel simulations of cultural exchange dynamics, and processing high-resolution audiovisual materials documenting performative traditions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable framework for identifying understudied intersections between gender roles and genre evolution in folk narratives; (2) computational evidence for how marginalized communities reconfigure shared folklore motifs during cultural disruptions; and (3) open-access tools tailored for ethically sourcing and analyzing Indigenous knowledge systems. By enabling the integration of previously siloed regional collections, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for preserving intangible cultural heritage while centering the agency of tradition-bearers in large-scale analyses. The requested resources directly support the program’s mandate to investigate creativity as a socially embedded practice, offering new paradigms for studying cultural resilience without relying on anthropological or sociological paradigms.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec

abstract: This project seeks to investigate unresolved conjectures in algebraic topology and geometric group theory through large-scale computational experiments, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The central research problem focuses on characterizing the homotopy types of certain non-positively curved simplicial complexes and their relationship to the rigidity properties of infinite discrete groups. While theoretical advances have established partial classification frameworks, critical cases remain intractable due to the combinatorial complexity of higher-dimensional cell structures and the exponential growth of configuration spaces. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational strategy combining symbolic algebra, discrete Morse theory, and distributed homology computations. Key steps include (1) generating exhaustive datasets of simplicial complexes up to dimension 6 with bounded vertex degrees, (2) implementing parallelized algorithms to compute persistent homology and automorphism group actions, and (3) applying machine learning techniques to identify patterns in spectral sequences derived from these complexes. The computational workflow will leverage MPI-based task distribution for large-scale parameter sweeps and GPU acceleration for matrix reduction in homology calculations. Expected outcomes include the discovery of counterexamples to a longstanding conjecture about $CAT(0)$ cube complexes, new bounds on the cohomological dimension of Thompson-like groups, and an open-source software library for high-dimensional complex analysis. This work will provide the first systematic computational exploration of homotopy phenomena in this geometric regime, offering insights into the deep interplay between local combinatorial structures and global topological properties. The requested resources are essential due to the $O(n^4)$ memory scaling in intermediate steps of our spectral sequence analysis and the need to simultaneously maintain thousands of complex instances in memory during Monte Carlo sampling of configuration spaces. Results will directly impact multiple areas of pure mathematics, including geometric group theory, algebraic K-theory, and manifold topology.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the analysis of quantities, magnitudes, forms, and their relationships, using symbolic logic and language. Includes instruction in algebra, calculus, functional analysis, geometry, number theory, logic, topology and other mathematical specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of maintaining precision in manufacturing and construction quality control (QC) processes, where traditional statistical methods struggle to handle the scale and complexity of modern sensor-driven data streams. Current QC systems often rely on offline sampling and manual inspections, leading to delayed defect detection, increased waste, and inefficiencies in high-throughput environments. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a real-time, computational quality control framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating multi-physics simulations of manufacturing processes to predict defect formation under variable conditions, and (2) training machine learning models for adaptive anomaly detection in heterogeneous production data. Computational methods will include parallelized finite element analysis for simulating material stresses in additive manufacturing, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic failure modeling, and deep neural networks trained on terabyte-scale sensor datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of complex simulations across diverse manufacturing scenarios while supporting distributed training of ensemble models for real-time quality prediction. Expected outcomes include an open-source QC analytics toolkit optimized for HPC architectures, validated against industrial case studies in precision machining and composite material fabrication. By enabling near-instantaneous analysis of high-dimensional process data, this work aims to reduce defect rates by an estimated 15–30% in partner manufacturing systems while decreasing computational latency for quality assessments by 80% compared to current cloud-based solutions. The project will directly enhance the scalability of automated QC systems, providing technical education programs with advanced computational case studies for curriculum development in quality assurance technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining consistent manufacturing and construction standards. Includes instruction in quality control systems management principles, technical standards applicable to specific engineering and manufacturing projects, testing procedures, inspection procedures, related instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of pediatric diseases, combined with the growing volume of multi-modal clinical data, presents a critical challenge in identifying biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and personalized treatment strategies for children. Current analytical approaches often struggle to integrate genomic, proteomic, imaging, and electronic health record (EHR) data at scale, limiting insights into disease mechanisms and heterogeneity. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced computational pipelines for multi-omic integration, predictive modeling, and dynamic simulation of pediatric disease progression. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) identifying molecular signatures associated with treatment-resistant pediatric cancers using whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, and longitudinal EHR data, and (2) simulating neurodevelopmental trajectories in preterm infants through agent-based models informed by brain imaging and metabolomic profiles. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures (e.g., graph neural networks, transformers) for cross-modal data fusion, Bayesian hierarchical models to account for developmental variability, and large-scale parameter optimization for mechanistic simulations. These analyses demand significant parallel processing capabilities, distributed memory management for terabyte-scale datasets, and GPU acceleration for training complex models. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel prognostic biomarkers, predictive models of therapeutic response, and optimized intervention strategies tailored to developmental stages. By enabling the synthesis of disparate data types at unprecedented resolution, this work will advance understanding of pediatric disease pathophysiology while providing a scalable framework for data-driven clinical decision support. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current computational bottlenecks, ensuring rigorous statistical validation and translational applicability of findings to improve outcomes in pediatric populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Medicine

abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that movement and mind-body therapies (MMBT) modulate neurophysiological and biomechanical processes, but the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain poorly quantified. This project addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic, whole-body movement practices—such as those in somatic education or trauma-informed embodied therapies—induce systemic changes in neural plasticity, autonomic regulation, and motor coordination. Current limitations stem from the inability to integrate high-dimensional datasets (motion capture, EEG, heart rate variability, respiratory dynamics) with temporal precision at the millisecond scale, a computational challenge requiring parallel processing capabilities. We propose developing a novel framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to model bidirectional body-brain networks during complex MMBT sequences. The research will employ multiscale simulations combining musculoskeletal modeling (OpenSim) with dynamic causal modeling of neural oscillations (FieldTrip), augmented by machine learning pipelines to identify latent biomarkers of therapeutic efficacy. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling to simulate neurocognitive adaptation processes across repeated therapy sessions, incorporating individualized anatomical constraints derived from participant-specific MRI data. The computational workload necessitates GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time signal fusion and stochastic optimization of personalized intervention parameters. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated open-source toolkit for analyzing MMBT-induced neurobiomechanical coupling, (2) predictive models identifying optimal movement sequences for specific clinical subpopulations (e.g., chronic pain, PTSD), and (3) quantitative evidence supporting standardized dosing parameters in embodied therapies. By resolving current bottlenecks in processing multimodal embodiment data, this work will establish computational foundations for precision-prescription paradigms in mind-body medicine, while advancing HPC applications in understudied areas of integrative health research.
cip_title: Movement and Mind-Body Therapies and Education, Other

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of computational models for optimizing coating material performance in architectural and industrial painting applications. The central challenge lies in predicting the long-term durability, adhesion, and environmental resilience of paints, lacquers, and wall coverings under diverse climatic and structural conditions. Traditional empirical testing methods are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to account for complex variables such as fluctuating humidity, temperature gradients, and substrate interactions. To address this, the project will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model interactions between coating materials and substrates at atomic scales, combined with finite element analysis (FEA) to evaluate macroscopic mechanical and thermal stresses. Machine learning techniques will further be integrated to correlate simulation data with experimental results, enabling predictive optimization of material formulations and application protocols. By simulating scenarios ranging from extreme weather exposure to chemical degradation, the models will identify failure thresholds and ideal coating compositions for specific use cases. The computational workflow demands significant parallel processing capabilities due to the multi-scale nature of the simulations and the need for high-resolution spatial-temporal data. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of material performance profiles, predictive tools for selecting coatings based on environmental and structural parameters, and evidence-based recommendations for updating industry standards on surface preparation and application practices. This work directly supports the painting and wall covering industry’s transition toward sustainable, high-performance materials while reducing reliance on trial-and-error methodologies. The integration of HPC-driven insights into technical training programs will also enhance pedagogical approaches for emerging professionals in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to finish exterior and interior structural surfaces by applying protective or decorative coating materials, such as paint, lacquer, and wallpaper. Includes instruction in surface preparation; selecting, preparing, and applying paints and other coatings; hanging wallpaper; equipment operation and maintenance; finish selection; safety and clean-up; environmental effects on finishes; adhesion properties; and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic number theory and arithmetic geometry by addressing computational challenges inherent to studying class groups, Selmer groups, and rational points on higher-genus curves. The central problem involves developing scalable algorithms to analyze invariants of algebraic structures associated with number fields and elliptic curves, with applications to longstanding conjectures such as the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and the Cohen-Lenstra heuristics. Current methods for computing étale cohomology groups, regulator constants, or Tate-Shafarevich groups face exponential complexity when scaling to degrees or conductors relevant to theoretical predictions, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The proposed computational approach combines optimized implementations of p-adic cohomology algorithms, distributed parallelization of lattice-based attacks on Diophantine equations, and hybrid CPU-GPU architectures for sieving in quadratic form spaces. Key tasks include enumerating isomorphism classes of abelian extensions with prescribed ramification, computing Hecke eigenvalues for automorphic forms over totally real fields, and verifying divisibility properties in Iwasawa modules. These methods will leverage existing libraries (PARI/GP, SageMath) alongside custom C++/MPI codes for distributed memory models. Expected outcomes include the first large-scale verification of stability patterns in Tamagawa numbers under base change, empirical bounds for ranks of Jacobians of genus-2 curves, and open datasets of class group structures for fields of degree ≥6. The results will directly inform conjectures in Galois deformation theory and refine asymptotic models in analytic number theory. By overcoming memory and runtime barriers in exact arithmetic, this work will enable algebraic techniques to address problems previously accessible only through analytic or probabilistic approximations, strengthening synergies between computational experimentation and theoretical innovation in pure mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the expression of quantities and their relationships by means of symbols, vectors, matrices, and equations, and the properties of integers. Includes instruction in algebraic structures, quadratic and automorphic forms, combinatorics, linear algebra, and algebraic geometry.

abstract: Irrigation systems are critical to global agricultural productivity, yet their efficiency is increasingly challenged by variable climate conditions, water scarcity, and heterogeneous soil properties. Current approaches to irrigation management often rely on generalized models that fail to account for localized, real-time environmental dynamics, leading to overuse of water resources and suboptimal crop yields. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize irrigation scheduling and system design at field scales. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-source datasets—including soil moisture telemetry, hyper-local weather forecasts, and crop-specific evapotranspiration rates—into a coupled hydrological-machine learning model. The model will dynamically adjust irrigation parameters (e.g., timing, volume, delivery methods) in response to real-time environmental feedback while accounting for infrastructure constraints such as pump capacity and pipe network hydraulics. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate system robustness under diverse climate scenarios and geospatial variability. Key outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool for precision irrigation management and predictive metrics for infrastructure upgrades under projected climate extremes. By enabling site-specific optimization of water use efficiency, this research aims to reduce agricultural water consumption by an estimated 15–25% in test regions while maintaining or improving crop yields. The scalability of the framework will be validated across representative agricultural zones in semi-arid and temperate climates, ensuring broad applicability to irrigation system operators, agronomists, and technology developers. Access to HPC resources is essential to process terabytes of sensor-derived and remote-sensing data, execute complex parameter optimizations, and deliver actionable insights within operational timeframes. This project aligns with the Irrigation Management Technology program’s goals by advancing data-driven methodologies for sustainable agricultural water use and resilient infrastructure design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize autonomous agricultural machinery operations under variable field conditions, addressing inefficiencies in current mechanized systems that lead to excessive energy use and suboptimal crop management. A key challenge in agricultural automation is the dynamic interaction between machinery, soil properties, and crop variability, which existing deterministic control systems struggle to adapt to in real time. To overcome this, we propose a machine learning-driven simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-scale interactions between autonomous vehicles, sensor networks, and agroecological systems. The computational approach integrates three components: (1) physics-based simulations of soil-tool dynamics using finite element modeling, (2) reinforcement learning algorithms trained on synthetic field environments to optimize path planning and implement control, and (3) uncertainty quantification through Monte Carlo methods to account for spatial heterogeneity in soil moisture and crop density. By parallelizing these computationally intensive workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, the platform will enable real-time scenario testing at unprecedented spatial resolutions (1 cm scale) across hectare-sized virtual fields. Expected outcomes include adaptive control policies that reduce fuel consumption by 15-20% compared to conventional systems while maintaining yield targets, validated through digital twin comparisons with field data from partner farms. The resulting open-source framework will provide researchers with tools to simulate next-generation agricultural robotics, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance sustainable mechanization strategies. Access to HPC resources is critical due to the need for massive parallelization in training deep reinforcement learning models and running high-fidelity soil mechanics simulations, tasks that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the digital preservation and computational analysis of large-scale historical datasets, with a focus on enhancing public access to historical resources and improving decision-making for heritage management. Public history institutions, including archives, museums, and municipal governments, increasingly face challenges in managing fragmented, unstructured, or deteriorating historical records, such as civic documents, oral histories, and community-led archival initiatives. Traditional methods struggle to process these materials at scale, particularly when extracting patterns, linking dispersed datasets, or modeling historical trends. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating machine learning (ML) and geospatial analysis to automate the digitization, classification, and contextualization of heterogeneous historical sources. Key tasks include training ML models to transcribe handwritten 19th-century municipal records, applying natural language processing (NLP) to identify temporal and thematic connections across oral history collections, and developing interactive geospatial visualizations of urban development patterns using historical maps and census data. These workflows require HPC resources to handle terabyte-scale datasets, optimize parallel processing of image and text files, and support iterative model training. Outcomes will include a publicly accessible digital repository with enhanced metadata, tools for community historians to query linked datasets, and predictive models to prioritize preservation efforts for at-risk materials. By integrating computational methods with public history praxis, this project aims to democratize access to historical resources, strengthen collaborative stewardship between academic and public institutions, and provide scalable frameworks for addressing data-intensive challenges in heritage conservation. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving these goals, enabling analyses that are infeasible with standard computing resources while maintaining ethical standards for data transparency and community engagement.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of history and administrative skills to the recording of public events and the management of related historical resources. Includes instruction in historical research methods, the planning and administration of public history projects, and applications to specific problems in public organizations, government agencies, foundations, and other facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to understand the impacts of climate-driven hydrological variability on freshwater microbial and macroinvertebrate community dynamics in temperate lake systems, with a focus on predicting ecosystem resilience under future environmental scenarios. Freshwater communities face unprecedented stressors from shifting thermal regimes, nutrient loading, and extreme precipitation events, yet their adaptive responses and cascading effects on ecosystem function remain poorly resolved at regional scales. To address this gap, we propose integrating high-resolution environmental sensor data, historical species occurrence records, and process-based ecological models to simulate multi-trophic interactions across spatially heterogeneous habitats. The computational approach employs agent-based modeling frameworks to represent microbial metabolic networks, invertebrate life history strategies, and resource competition dynamics under varying oxygen, temperature, and dissolved organic carbon conditions. These models will be coupled with hydrodynamic projections from regional climate models to assess community stability thresholds and biogeochemical feedbacks. The scale of analysis—encompassing 12 lake districts across glaciated terrains in North America and Europe—necessitates high-performance computing resources for parallelized simulations of 10^6+ individual agent interactions, Bayesian calibration of trait-based parameters, and machine learning-driven pattern detection in multi-terabyte environmental datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of keystone taxa maintaining ecosystem functions under hypoxia stress, (2) predictive maps of biodiversity hotspots vulnerable to hydrological regime shifts, and (3) open-source modular code for simulating microbial-metazoan energy transfer efficiencies. By resolving how fine-scale habitat heterogeneity buffers against climatic extremes, this work will directly inform watershed management strategies and provide a computational framework for prioritizing conservation efforts in freshwater systems facing rapid environmental change.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of regional Italian dialect variation and its historical-literary intersections. While Italian dialects and regional linguistic practices have been studied extensively through traditional philological methods, large-scale quantitative analyses remain underdeveloped due to the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous textual and spoken corpora spanning diverse time periods and geographic regions. The research problem centers on mapping dialectal evolution in relation to sociohistorical shifts (e.g., post-unification standardization efforts) and identifying latent stylistic patterns in regional literature that resist mainstream Tuscan-based Italian norms. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and non-standard texts, including tokenization models adapted for orthographic variation, graph-based algorithms for semantic network analysis, and transformer-based architectures fine-tuned on dialect-specific corpora. These methods will be applied to a curated multilingual dataset comprising 19th–21st-century literature, transcribed oral histories, and digitized archival materials from Lombardy, Sicily, and Veneto. Parallelized workflows will enable comparative sentiment analysis, lexical diffusion modeling, and the identification of morphosyntactic features that correlate with extralinguistic factors such as urbanization rates and educational policy changes. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access computational toolkit for Italian dialect studies, high-resolution visualizations of dialect convergence/divergence patterns, and statistically grounded insights into how regional identity is encoded in linguistic variation. By enabling the processing of previously intractable datasets, this project aims to bridge gaps between computational linguistics and traditional philological scholarship while informing contemporary efforts to preserve endangered dialects. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, including training domain-specific language models and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to validate diachronic linguistic hypotheses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Italian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational models for simulating language acquisition dynamics in bilingual and multilingual classrooms. A critical challenge in bilingual education lies in understanding how learners with diverse linguistic backgrounds and proficiencies interact within adaptive instructional environments, particularly when teachers employ strategies that integrate translanguaging or code-switching. Existing models often oversimplify these interactions, failing to account for the real-time cognitive load fluctuations, cross-linguistic interference, or sociocultural factors influencing communication. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent simulation framework that models student-teacher and peer interactions at scale, incorporating psycholinguistic data, individualized language proficiency metrics, and dynamic classroom discourse patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized execution of thousands of agent-based simulations, each parameterized with empirical data from classroom observations, eye-tracking studies, and language assessment tools. Machine learning components will iteratively refine interaction rules and pedagogical strategies through reinforcement learning, optimizing for measurable outcomes such as metalinguistic awareness and cross-language transfer. Computational demands are substantial due to the need for real-time natural language processing (NLP) of simulated dialogues, multimodal data integration (gesture, prosody), and high-dimensional optimization of instructional variables. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for identifying optimal translanguaging strategies under specific classroom demographics, as well as an open-access toolkit for teacher training programs to simulate intervention scenarios. This work directly advances bilingual educator preparation by providing evidence-based, computationally derived insights into complex multilingual pedagogy challenges that are infeasible to study through traditional experimental designs alone.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to bilingual/bicultural children or adults, and/or the design and implementation of educational programs having the goal of producing bilingual/bicultural individuals. Includes preparation to serve as teachers and administrators in bilingual/bicultural education programs.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of insurance law in the context of evolving regulatory frameworks and litigation trends. Insurance law, while a specialized legal domain, intersects with computational challenges due to the volume of case law, statutory texts, and policy documents, as well as the need to model probabilistic outcomes of legal disputes and regulatory enforcement. The core research problem lies in understanding how algorithmic tools can map the cascading effects of legal precedents and regulatory changes on insurance markets, particularly in scenarios involving emerging risks (e.g., climate-related liabilities, cybersecurity breaches) that lack established judicial guidance. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to parse and classify legal texts, agent-based modeling to simulate stakeholder decision-making under varying regulatory conditions, and probabilistic graphical models to quantify litigation risks. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage large-scale text corpora (e.g., decades of court opinions, international regulatory filings) and to run iterative simulations that account for multi-jurisdictional legal variability. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting regulatory compliance costs, identifying systemic vulnerabilities in insurance contract design, and generating evidence-based recommendations for legislative reforms. By bridging computational methodologies with doctrinal legal analysis, this project aims to advance the emerging field of computational legal studies while providing actionable insights for policymakers, insurers, and legal practitioners navigating increasingly complex risk landscapes. The scalability of HPC resources is critical to handling the heterogeneous data types and stochastic modeling inherent to this interdisciplinary work.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: Motor recovery following neurological or musculoskeletal injuries exhibits significant variability across individuals, complicating the development of personalized rehabilitation protocols. Current clinical assessments often lack the granularity to predict long-term outcomes or optimize therapeutic interventions dynamically. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets—including high-resolution motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and neuroimaging data—collected from patients undergoing rehabilitation. Computational modeling techniques, such as machine learning-driven trajectory prediction and finite element simulations of tissue remodeling, will be employed to identify biomarkers of recovery and simulate patient-specific responses to therapeutic stimuli. The scale of data integration (spanning terabytes of heterogeneous clinical and biomechanical records) and the computational intensity of iterative simulations necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale parameter optimization. Anticipated outcomes include the development of predictive algorithms to stratify patients by recovery potential, the generation of biomechanically informed intervention guidelines, and open-source tools for real-time therapy adaptation. By bridging computational advances with clinical rehabilitation practice, this work aims to establish a framework for data-driven therapeutic personalization, ultimately improving functional outcomes and reducing healthcare costs through targeted resource allocation. The requested resources will enable the execution of complex, multi-layered analyses that are otherwise infeasible on local infrastructure, directly supporting innovations in rehabilitation science and scalable therapeutic decision-making.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rehabilitation and therapeutic professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Forest ecosystems face increasing pressures from climate change, invasive species, and shifting land-use patterns, necessitating advanced predictive tools to inform sustainable management. Current models often lack the spatial resolution or computational scalability to integrate multi-scale ecological processes with socio-economic factors. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a coupled modeling framework that simulates forest dynamics under diverse climate and management scenarios. The research will integrate remote sensing data, species distribution models, and agent-based simulations to quantify interactions between forest growth, disturbance regimes (e.g., wildfires, pest outbreaks), and resource extraction decisions. Key computational challenges include processing high-resolution LiDAR datasets (~10 TB), calibrating probabilistic models of tree mortality, and running ensemble climate projections at regional scales. The HPC environment will enable parallelized parameter optimization via Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods and GPU-accelerated machine learning to identify non-linear relationships in ecological time-series data. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of forest vulnerability to compound stressors under IPCC climate scenarios, (2) decision-support metrics for balancing carbon sequestration targets with timber yield optimization, and (3) open-source code packages for scalable forest simulation. By resolving fine-grained ecological processes within landscape-scale models, this work will advance adaptive management strategies that maintain biodiversity while addressing economic and conservation priorities. The requested computing resources are critical for overcoming memory-intensive analyses of 3D forest structure data and achieving the temporal resolution needed to inform real-world management cycles.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to manage and develop forest areas for economic, recreational, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in forest-related sciences, mapping, statistics, harvesting and production technology, natural resources management and economics, wildlife sciences, administration, and public relations.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, with diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning relying heavily on the interpretation of complex, multi-modal data. Current clinical workflows for analyzing hemodynamic parameters, imaging datasets (e.g., echocardiography, angiography), and electrophysiological signals face challenges in integrating heterogeneous data sources efficiently, limiting real-time decision-making and personalized care. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a computational pipeline for advanced cardiovascular data synthesis and predictive modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three aims: (1) creating multi-scale simulations of cardiovascular dynamics to model disease progression in conditions such as atherosclerosis and heart failure, (2) training deep learning algorithms to automate the detection of anomalies in high-resolution imaging and waveform data, and (3) optimizing predictive models for patient-specific treatment outcomes using ensemble machine learning techniques. These tasks require parallelized processing of large datasets (>100 TB), including 4D flow MRI, intravascular ultrasound, and continuous electrocardiographic monitoring data, which exceed the capacity of local institutional servers. The HPC infrastructure will enable GPU-accelerated model training, finite element simulations of blood flow, and real-time integration of clinical parameters for risk stratification. Expected outcomes include validated computational tools to enhance diagnostic precision, reduce analysis time for complex cases, and identify novel biomarkers for early disease detection. The pipeline will be disseminated as open-source software to support translational cardiovascular research, with direct applications in training technologists to interpret AI-augmented diagnostics. By bridging computational innovation and clinical practice, this work aims to advance both the technical capabilities and educational frameworks within cardiovascular technology programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform invasive, noninvasive, and peripheral examinations of the cardiovascular system at the request of physicians to aid in diagnoses and therapeutic treatments. Includes instruction in reviewing and recording patient histories and clinical data, patient care, investigative and examination procedures, diagnostic procedures, data analysis and documentation, physician consultation, equipment operation and monitoring, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the precision and innovation of baking and pastry arts through computational modeling of complex biochemical and physical processes inherent to artisanal and commercial baking. Traditional baking relies heavily on experiential knowledge and iterative experimentation, limiting the scalability of recipe optimization, consistency in product quality, and adaptation to novel dietary or sustainability constraints. To address these challenges, this research proposes the development of a multi-scale simulation framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) models of dough fermentation, heat and mass transfer simulations during baking, and machine learning (ML)-driven predictive analytics for texture and flavor outcomes. The MD component will simulate enzymatic activity and gas diffusion in dough matrices under varying ingredient ratios and environmental conditions, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will analyze heat distribution patterns in commercial ovens to minimize energy waste and optimize crust formation. Concurrently, ML algorithms will process experimental and simulated datasets to correlate ingredient combinations, processing parameters, and sensory outcomes, enabling predictive recipe design. HPC resources are critical to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize stochastic simulations, and train deep learning models on heterogeneous data (e.g., 3D crumb structure imaging, moisture gradients). Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for bakers to prototype recipes virtually, reduce trial-and-error resource costs, and customize products for dietary needs without compromising traditional quality. By bridging culinary arts with computational science, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven gastronomy, enhancing both the sustainability and creativity of professional baking practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares  individuals to serve as professional bakers and pastry specialists in restaurants or other commercial baking establishments.  Includes instruction in bread and pastry making, bread and pastry handling and storage, cake and pastry decorating, baking industry operations, product packaging and marketing operations, and counter display and service.

abstract: Gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary diseases, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), are driven by complex molecular interactions that remain poorly characterized. Current clinical strategies often lack precision due to heterogeneous disease manifestations and incomplete understanding of underlying mechanisms. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets and build predictive models of disease progression and therapeutic response. We will integrate bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, microbiome metagenomics, and spatially resolved transcriptomic data from clinical cohorts of patients with HCC and IBD. Computational workflows will include deconvolution of tumor microenvironment heterogeneity, network-based modeling of host-microbiome interactions, and deep learning approaches to identify imaging biomarkers from histopathology slides. These analyses require large-scale data processing, iterative machine learning model training, and simulation of dynamic biological networks—tasks that exceed the capacity of standard computing infrastructure. The HPC resources will enable parallelized execution of bioinformatics pipelines, storage of multi-terabyte datasets, and deployment of GPU-accelerated neural networks. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel molecular subtypes of HCC linked to immune evasion mechanisms, predictive signatures of IBD treatment resistance, and microbiome-derived metabolites associated with disease flares. By mapping context-specific pathways, this work aims to advance personalized therapeutic strategies and generate clinically actionable biomarkers. All tools and datasets will be made available to the research community, fostering broader translational innovation in gastroenterology and hepatology.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology and Hepatology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing the socio-spatial dynamics of informal urban settlements, a critical yet understudied dimension of contemporary architectural and urban research.
