Informal settlements—often characterized by self-organized construction, adaptive material practices, and complex social networks—present unique challenges for conventional architectural analysis due to their dynamic morphologies and lack of standardized data. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to model and visualize these environments, integrating heterogeneous data sources (e.g., satellite imagery, crowd-sourced mapping, ethnographic records) to generate actionable insights for equitable urban design and policy. Computational workflows will combine machine learning for pattern recognition in spatial-temporal datasets, agent-based modeling to simulate resident-driven development processes, and 3D parametric modeling to reconstruct settlement geometries at scale. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution geospatial data, running iterative simulations of growth scenarios under varying resource constraints, and enabling real-time collaborative visualization of results through cloud-based platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for architects and planners to engage with informal urbanization as a site of design innovation, rather than solely a technical or policy challenge. The project bridges architectural theory, computational social science, and urban data analytics, offering a methodological advance for studying non-formalized built environments while contributing to debates on sustainable urban futures. By situating computational rigor within a human-centered framework, this work aims to expand the disciplinary boundaries of architectural studies and demonstrate the value of HPC in addressing complex, socially embedded design problems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of architecture, cities, landscapes, designed objects, ornament, architectural photography, and material culture in diverse places and time periods, and the social and aesthetic dimensions of contemporary architecture, landscapes, and cities, emphasizing issues of sustainable environments, new forms of urbanism, and the use of digital media for visualization and analysis. Includes instruction in the fundamentals of architecture, design, environmental and sustainability studies, historic preservation, landscape architecture, studio art, and urban affairs and planning.

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems—encompassing energy grids, transportation networks, and communication frameworks—are increasingly interdependent and vulnerable to cascading failures from cyber-physical threats. Traditional risk assessment models often lack the granularity to simulate dynamic interactions between physical infrastructure components and their cyber counterparts, particularly under evolving adversarial tactics such as AI-driven attacks or IoT-based exploits. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-fidelity, multi-layered simulation environment to model infrastructure interdependencies, predict failure propagation pathways, and evaluate mitigation strategies under diverse threat scenarios. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale agent-based simulations, integrating real-world data on infrastructure topologies, threat intelligence feeds, and stochastic hazard models. Computational methods include network theory to map node criticality, machine learning algorithms to identify latent vulnerabilities in operational technology (OT) systems, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify systemic risks under uncertainty. By simulating coordinated cyber-physical attacks on hybrid infrastructure models, the project aims to identify chokepoints, test redundancy protocols, and optimize contingency responses. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for dynamic risk prioritization, adaptive threat detection benchmarks, and policy-ready insights on hardening infrastructure resilience against asymmetric threats. The HPC environment is essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing complex scenario analyses, and achieving near-real-time predictive analytics for critical decision-making. This work directly supports national security objectives by advancing computational tools for infrastructure operators and policymakers, enabling proactive defense measures in an era of escalating hybrid threats. Results will be validated through partnerships with infrastructure agencies and disseminated via open-source threat modeling toolkits to foster cross-sector collaboration.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive urban microclimate modeling frameworks tailored for understudied informal settlements. Rapid urbanization in regions with limited infrastructural governance has led to environments where conventional design principles fail to address hyperlocal thermal, airflow, and material dynamics. Current simulation tools, optimized for regulated urban contexts, lack the flexibility to incorporate transient variables such as improvised building materials, informal green spaces, and socially driven spatial adaptations. The research problem centers on creating a computational model that dynamically integrates these factors to predict microclimatic outcomes and inform community-led design interventions. Using a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning, the project will simulate interactions between human behavior, material improvisation, and environmental fluxes at neighborhood scales. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of high-resolution 3D urban datasets, real-time calibration against ground-sensor networks, and iterative scenario testing across diverse climatic regimes. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit capable of running on heterogeneous architectures, a repository of parametric design strategies optimized for informal settlement contexts, and evidence-based guidelines for low-cost thermal mitigation. By bridging gaps between participatory design, fluid dynamics, and adaptive systems modeling, this work aims to establish a new computational paradigm for equitable environmental design—one that prioritizes resource-constrained communities while generating transferable insights for climate-responsive urban planning. The scalability of the proposed methods could redefine how non-canonical urban forms are analyzed, offering pathways to integrate grassroots design intelligence into computational workflows traditionally dominated by formal engineering frameworks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental design, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of identifying and interpreting pathogenic genetic variants underlying complex Mendelian disorders and genetically heterogeneous diseases, such as inherited cardiomyopathies and neurodevelopmental syndromes. Despite advances in sequencing, pinpointing causal variants remains difficult due to extensive locus heterogeneity, variable penetrance, and the lack of scalable frameworks to integrate clinical, genomic, and functional data. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 10,000 patients with undiagnosed genetic disorders, alongside matched controls, to disentangle contributions of rare coding and noncoding variants. Computational workflows will prioritize candidate variants through a multi-tiered approach: (1) population-scale filtering using allele frequency thresholds from diverse genomic databases; (2) integration of clinical phenotype data with gene-specific mutation profiles using machine learning models trained on known disease-gene associations; (3) predictive scoring of variant pathogenicity via comparative analysis of evolutionary conservation, splice-site disruption, and regulatory element overlap. Epistatic interactions and modifier effects will be evaluated using graph-based algorithms to model gene network perturbations. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing these analyses across massive datasets, enabling rapid genotype-phenotype correlation and reducing computational bottlenecks in variant annotation. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel disease-associated loci, refined diagnostic criteria for genetically unresolved cases, and a publicly accessible variant prioritization toolkit optimized for clinical genetics workflows. This work will directly enhance diagnostic yield in medical genetics, inform targeted therapeutic strategies for monogenic disorders, and advance methods for interpreting noncoding variation in rare disease contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of human genetics from the standpoint of medical applications such as clinical diagnosis, genetic engineering and therapy, transplantation, and the study of genetic diseases and disabilities and their defense. Includes instruction in human molecular genetics; genetic factors causing disease; changes in gene expression during development, differentiation, and pathogenesis; recombinant DNA; gene therapy; clinical genetics; genetic epidemiology; immunogenetics; cytogenetics; and genetics of specific disorders and diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and optimization of next-generation aerospace propulsion systems, with a focus on hybrid-electric architectures. The integration of electric propulsion components into traditional gas turbine engines introduces complex multi-physics challenges, including unsteady fluid-structure interactions, thermal management constraints, and coupled electromagnetic-aerodynamic effects. Current experimental approaches are limited in resolving these phenomena at relevant scales, while existing computational models lack the fidelity to capture transient behaviors across disparate time and spatial domains. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and dynamic system modeling. High-fidelity LES (Large Eddy Simulation) will model turbulent combustion and flow separation in hybrid combustors, coupled with conjugate heat transfer analysis for thermal stress prediction in critical components. GPU-accelerated solvers will enable parametric studies of electric motor-generator configurations under varying flight conditions, while reduced-order models will bridge component-level simulations with full-system performance optimization. The computational workload demands distributed-memory parallelism and large-scale data handling capabilities due to the billion-cell meshes required for resolving boundary layer physics and the need for ensemble runs across design permutations. Expected outcomes include validated performance maps for hybrid propulsion subsystems, identification of optimal power management strategies for reduced emissions, and predictive models for component degradation under cyclic thermal loading. These results will directly inform prototype testing protocols and certification pathways for sustainable aviation technologies, accelerating the translation of theoretical concepts into field-deployable solutions. By advancing simulation-driven design in aerospace engineering technology, this work aims to reduce reliance on costly physical iterations while improving the reliability of emerging propulsion systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. Includes instruction in aircraft/spacecraft systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize school-level decision-making for elementary and middle school administrators by modeling the impacts of resource allocation strategies on student outcomes and operational efficiency. School leaders face complex challenges in balancing budgetary constraints, staffing needs, facility usage, and student support services, yet lack accessible tools to simulate how these variables interact dynamically. To address this gap, we propose building agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate school ecosystems under varying resource distribution scenarios. These models will integrate anonymized longitudinal data from district records (e.g., student performance metrics, staff retention rates, facility maintenance costs) and environmental parameters (e.g., enrollment fluctuations, community socioeconomic profiles). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the parallel processing required for large-scale simulations, which will test thousands of allocation permutations across multi-year timelines. Machine learning techniques will then identify patterns linking specific resource decisions to outcomes such as academic growth, equity gaps, or operational cost efficiency. The resulting predictive analytics dashboard will provide administrators with evidence-based guidance for strategic budgeting, staffing, and program investments. By translating computational insights into actionable leadership practices, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in K-7 educational administration, directly supporting the program’s focus on effective school management. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools tailored to elementary/middle school contexts and a framework for evaluating policy impacts on developmental milestones in childhood and early adolescence. This project bridges computational social science and educational leadership, offering novel methodologies to address systemic challenges in school administration.
cip_title: Elementary and Middle School Administration/ Principalship
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the elementary and middle school (K-7) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of elementary and middle schools. Includes instruction in elementary and/or middle school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, childhood and pre-adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the complex interplay between historical maritime activities, contemporary ocean governance, and environmental change through advanced computational modeling. Maritime ecosystems and policy frameworks are influenced by dynamic, multi-scale interactions spanning centuries of human-ocean engagement, yet existing studies often lack the integrative tools to analyze these relationships systematically. Our research will develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal model to reconstruct historical shipping patterns, correlate them with long-term ecological shifts (e.g., sediment deposition, species migration), and evaluate their implications for modern maritime security and resource management. The computational approach integrates digitized archival records (logbooks, trade ledgers), satellite-derived oceanographic data, and agent-based simulations to map the evolution of shipping corridors and their environmental footprints since the 18th century. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process petabytes of heterogeneous data, run multi-decadal simulations of vessel traffic under varying climatic conditions, and apply machine learning algorithms to identify policy-relevant patterns in maritime conflict and cooperation. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of historical and projected maritime activity hotspots, predictive models of piracy risk zones under climate-driven route changes, and evidence-based frameworks for balancing jurisdictional disputes in emerging Arctic shipping lanes. By bridging historical analysis with computational oceanography, this work will provide policymakers, ecologists, and maritime historians with a shared analytical platform to anticipate cascading challenges—from illegal fishing to territorial disputes—in an era of rapid oceanic transformation. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology also advances methodological synergies between digital humanities and environmental sciences, establishing scalable protocols for temporal-spatial data fusion in maritime studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, science, policy issues, and literature of the ocean. Includes instruction in maritime history, maritime law, maritime literature, oceanography, maritime security, and maritime politics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the co-evolution of scientific instrumentation and theoretical frameworks across the 19th and 20th centuries, with a focus on how material practices in laboratories influenced the conceptualization of phenomena such as electromagnetic fields and quantum indeterminacy. Traditional historiography often prioritizes textual analysis, leaving gaps in understanding the reciprocal relationship between experimental tools and epistemic shifts. To address this, we propose a computational approach integrating digitized laboratory notebooks, instrument blueprints, patent records, and correspondence archives into a unified analytical framework. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process and correlate heterogeneous datasets spanning >10 million pages of text, 50,000 technical diagrams, and spatiotemporal metadata from 150 global institutions. Machine learning models—including transformer-based architectures for semantic analysis of handwritten texts and graph neural networks to map citation networks between instrument designs and theoretical publications—will be deployed to identify patterns in technological adoption and conceptual innovation. Statistical topology methods will further analyze how geometric representations in schematics correlate with shifts in ontological commitments within research communities. The computational pipeline requires parallelized workflows for feature extraction, unsupervised clustering of epistemic paradigms, and dynamic network visualization. Expected outcomes include: (1) a quantitative model of feedback loops between material culture and theory formation, (2) identification of previously overlooked "epistemic thresholds" where instrumental constraints catalyzed paradigm changes, and (3) an open-access knowledge graph linking artifacts to conceptual lineages. By bridging computational humanities with history of science, this work aims to establish a new methodology for studying material-epistemic dynamics at scale, with implications for contemporary philosophy of technoscientific practice.
detailed_field: History/ philosophy of science, technology, and society
cip_title: History and Philosophy of Science and Technology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution of scientific theories, science applications and technologies, and the scientific, medical, and technological disciplines, as well as the philosophy of science and its historical socio-economic context. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of philosophical inquiry; historiography of science; history of science, medicine, and technology; and research methods in the history of the scientific and engineering disciplines, including mathematics.

abstract: Emergency Medicine requires rapid, data-driven decision-making in high-stakes environments, yet existing predictive models for critical outcomes such as sepsis, trauma mortality, or acute decompensation often lack the speed and accuracy needed for real-time clinical use. This limitation stems from the complexity of integrating heterogeneous, high-dimensional data—including electronic health records, continuous vital sign streams, imaging, and biomarker trends—into scalable computational frameworks. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning models capable of processing multimodal data in near real-time. The project will employ distributed computing architectures to parallelize data ingestion, preprocessing, and model training across large retrospective datasets from diverse emergency department (ED) populations. Deep neural networks and ensemble methods will be optimized to identify subtle, time-dependent patterns predictive of deterioration or intervention needs. Validation will involve simulating real-world deployment by testing inference latency and accuracy under high-throughput conditions mirroring ED patient volumes. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational burden of training on terabytes of temporally aligned data, hyperparameter optimization across thousands of concurrent jobs, and stress-testing models under synthetic load scenarios. Successful implementation will yield clinically validated tools for early risk stratification, enabling proactive interventions during the "golden hour" of emergency care. Anticipated outcomes include a 15–20% improvement in prediction accuracy for life-threatening events compared to existing protocols, as well as a framework for deploying adaptive models that evolve with shifting patient populations. This work has the potential to reduce preventable morbidity, optimize resource allocation during surge events, and establish a blueprint for computationally intensive clinical analytics in time-sensitive care settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Emergency Medicine

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize customer interaction dynamics in decentralized financial service platforms, a rapidly evolving niche within digital banking. Traditional customer service frameworks in banking are increasingly strained by the scale and complexity of decentralized systems, which integrate blockchain technologies, AI-driven chatbots, and real-time multi-currency transactions. The computational challenge lies in simulating hyper-realistic, concurrent user interactions across global networks while accounting for stochastic variables such as regional regulatory constraints, fluctuating asset valuations, and behavioral anomalies in user decision-making. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and graph neural networks (GNNs), we will construct a scalable simulation environment to test adaptive customer service protocols under scenarios of market volatility, cybersecurity threats, and cross-jurisdictional compliance conflicts. The ABM agents will represent heterogeneous users, institutional stakeholders, and regulatory bodies, each governed by unique behavioral parameters derived from anonymized transaction datasets and sentiment analysis of customer support logs. GNNs will map emergent network effects and interdependencies between service efficiency, trust metrics, and financial risk exposure. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations across thousands of agent permutations and to train models on high-dimensional time-series data spanning terabytes of transactional and interaction records. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into resilience thresholds for decentralized service architectures, predictive frameworks for preempting systemic customer experience failures, and optimized resource allocation strategies for hybrid human-AI support systems. This work will provide financial institutions with empirically grounded tools to enhance service scalability in decentralized ecosystems while maintaining regulatory and operational stability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform a wide variety of customer services in banks, insurance agencies, savings and loan companies, and related enterprises. Includes instruction in communications and public relations skills, business equipment operation, and technical skills applicable to the methods and operations of specific financial or insurance services.

abstract: The dynamic interplay between macromolecular structure and energy transduction underpins critical biological processes, yet mechanistic understanding of these phenomena remains limited by the temporal and spatial resolution of experimental methods. This project seeks to address this gap by employing large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the structural dynamics of energy-transducing complexes in respiratory and photosynthetic systems. Specifically, we aim to resolve how proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanisms in cytochrome c oxidase and photosystem II are governed by transient conformational states and hydration dynamics. A key challenge lies in modeling the microsecond-to-millisecond timescales required to observe functionally relevant transitions in these supramolecular assemblies. To overcome this, we will implement adaptive sampling algorithms and Markov state models on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, enabling efficient exploration of free energy landscapes across multiple reaction coordinates. The simulations will integrate experimental constraints from cryo-EM density maps and time-resolved spectroscopic data through Bayesian inference frameworks. This computational approach demands substantial resources due to the need for atomic-resolution modeling of 500k-1M atom systems over aggregated simulation times exceeding 100 μs. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved water-mediated proton transfer pathways in oxidoreductases, (2) quantification of coupling between redox-driven conformational changes and proton motive force generation, and (3) predictive models for engineering artificial energy transduction systems. The proposed work directly advances molecular biophysics by bridging structural snapshots with dynamic mechanistic models, while providing open-access trajectory datasets to guide experimental validation. Successful implementation will require dedicated GPU nodes for accelerated MD and >1 PB of high-throughput storage for trajectory analysis. These computational insights into biological energy conversion principles have broad relevance for understanding mitochondrial disorders and developing bioinspired energy technologies.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: The increasing complexity of autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize control strategies and ensure real-time adaptability. Current approaches for multi-robot coordination, sensor fusion, and path planning often rely on simplified models or offline simulations, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios where latency, scalability, and uncertainty are critical challenges. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate novel algorithms for distributed, real-time control of heterogeneous robotic systems. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) implementing parallelized simulations of multi-agent interactions in physics-based virtual environments to test swarm intelligence algorithms under variable constraints, (2) training machine learning models for adaptive sensor fusion using large-scale datasets from lidar, vision, and inertial measurement units, and (3) optimizing embedded control code through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing accelerated by GPU-accelerated computation. Computational methods will include hybrid agent-based modeling frameworks, Monte Carlo optimization for robustness testing, and neural network architectures optimized for low-latency inference. By enabling high-fidelity simulations of complex mechatronic systems and reducing the computational bottleneck in algorithm development, this work aims to advance the design of scalable, resilient automation solutions for industrial logistics and collaborative robotics. The requested HPC resources will directly support the parallel execution of thousands of simulation instances, reduce model training times through distributed computing, and facilitate the transition from simulation to physical prototypes. Outcomes are expected to contribute open-source tools for robotic system co-design and demonstrate quantifiable improvements in task completion times and energy efficiency for autonomous material handling applications.
cip_title: Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in the support of engineers to the design, development, and operational evaluation of autonomous, computer-controlled, electro-mechanical systems. Includes instruction in computer and software engineering, control engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced machine learning framework for detecting anomalies in large-scale health insurance claims data, with a focus on identifying complex fraud patterns and adjudication inefficiencies. The research addresses a critical gap in current claims examination methodologies, which often rely on rule-based systems that struggle to adapt to evolving fraud tactics or process multimodal data (e.g., clinical narratives, billing codes, provider networks) efficiently. The computational approach integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) to model provider-patient interactions as dynamic networks, transformer-based architectures for temporal analysis of claim sequences, and multimodal fusion techniques to synthesize structured and unstructured data. By processing historical claims datasets spanning 50 million records—including text-based clinical justification documents and billing metadata—the framework will identify latent correlations and suspicious patterns that evade conventional detection methods. The HPC environment is essential for training models at scale, optimizing hyperparameters across distributed nodes, and simulating claim adjudication scenarios under varying regulatory constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for probabilistic fraud risk scoring, validated against active investigations by partner insurance regulators, and a novel benchmarking dataset for claims analysis research. This work will directly enhance the operational efficiency of claims examiners by providing interpretable, real-time decision support, while advancing computational methods for ethical AI in healthcare compliance. The project’s interdisciplinary integration of health informatics, computational linguistics, and regulatory analytics represents a novel contribution to understudied challenges at the intersection of insurance operations and healthcare delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized investigatory, analytical, evaluative, and consultative functions related to health/medical insurance operations and their regulation. Includes instruction in health and medical insurance processes and procedures, health insurance law and regulations, health care industry law, record-keeping, analytic and investigatory techniques, evaluation methods, field operations methods, office procedures, related software applications, oral and written communications skills, interviewing techniques, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for heavy equipment using high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in current diagnostic and repair practices. Heavy machinery in industries such as mining, construction, and agriculture often suffers unplanned downtime due to mechanical failures in critical systems like hydraulics, drivetrains, and engine components. Traditional maintenance relies on reactive strategies or static schedules, leading to costly operational interruptions and premature part replacements. To overcome these limitations, this research will integrate sensor data from equipment telemetry, historical failure records, and multiphysics simulations to create machine learning models capable of predicting component degradation with high spatiotemporal resolution. The computational approach involves training deep neural networks on HPC clusters to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, including vibration spectra, thermal imaging, and fluid dynamics profiles from hydraulic systems. Finite element analysis simulations will model stress distributions in load-bearing components under diverse operating conditions, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize maintenance schedules based on risk-reward tradeoffs. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the parallel processing demands of 3D multiphysics simulations and the hyperparameter tuning required for robust predictive models. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that reduces unplanned downtime by 30–50% in field-tested scenarios, extends component lifespans through condition-based interventions, and provides real-time failure risk visualizations for technicians. The project will also generate open-access datasets of annotated equipment sensor logs paired with simulation results, creating new benchmarking resources for the heavy equipment maintenance community. By fusing computational engineering with operational data, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift from schedule-driven to predictive, physics-informed maintenance strategies in vocational technical fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the field maintenance and repair of heavy equipment, and in the general maintenance and overhaul of such equipment. Includes instruction in inspection, maintenance, and repair of tracks, wheels, brakes, operating controls, pneumatic and hydraulic systems, electrical circuitry, engines and in techniques of welding and brazing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neural and biomechanical underpinnings of apraxia of speech (AOS), a motor planning disorder characterized by impaired speech production. Current diagnostic frameworks for AOS rely heavily on subjective clinical assessments, leading to variability in diagnosis and treatment. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating neuroimaging, computational biomechanics, and machine learning to develop objective biomarkers for AOS. The research will utilize multimodal datasets, including high-resolution functional MRI (fMRI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and 3D vocal tract kinematics captured during speech tasks. Computational challenges arise from the need to model dynamic interactions between cortical activation patterns, white matter connectivity, and articulatory muscle coordination—a process requiring real-time processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative simulations of neural-mechanical coupling. HPC resources will enable the deployment of graph neural networks (GNNs) to map disrupted network topology in speech-related brain regions and finite element models (FEMs) to simulate vocal tract dynamics under varying neuromotor constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model linking specific neural circuit abnormalities to articulatory kinematics, (2) automated classification algorithms to differentiate AOS from related disorders, and (3) open-source tools for optimizing speech motor rehabilitation protocols. By bridging gaps between computational neuroscience and speech motor control theory, this work aims to establish a novel framework for precision assessment of motor speech disorders, with potential applications in neurorehabilitation technology and adaptive therapeutic interfaces. The scale of data integration and the complexity of real-time biomechanical simulations necessitate the parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workflows uniquely afforded by HPC infrastructure.
cip_title: Communication Disorders Sciences and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications disorders sciences and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and integrate fragmented historical datasets from pre-colonial to post-colonial Africa, addressing the challenge of reconstructing holistic narratives from dispersed and heterogeneous sources. Despite Africa’s rich historical record, critical gaps persist due to the ephemerality of oral traditions, uneven preservation of archival materials, and the spatial disconnect between archaeological evidence and documentary accounts. The research will focus on three core datasets: digitized colonial administrative records from British and French archives (1880–1960), georeferenced archaeological surveys of Iron Age settlements in West and East Africa, and transcribed oral histories from 20th-century anticolonial movements. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) to identify semantic patterns in colonial texts, machine learning classifiers to cross-reference oral histories with archaeological site data, and network analysis to model the diffusion of cultural practices across diasporic communities. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based NLP models on low-resource African languages, processing high-resolution LiDAR scans of settlement sites, and simulating large-scale agent-based models of trade networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of integrated datasets, visualizations of shifting political and cultural boundaries, and quantitative frameworks to assess the impact of environmental change on social structures. By bridging disciplinary silos, this project aims to advance methodologies for decentralized historiography while centering African agency in narratives of state formation, resistance, and cultural exchange. The computational tools developed will provide a template for analyzing understudied regions and empower collaborative research with African institutions, addressing longstanding inequities in data sovereignty and scholarly infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of one or more peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara (and including the African diasporas overseas) from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing adaptive learning systems in engineering education through advanced computational modeling of student cognitive engagement. While personalized learning platforms are increasingly deployed in technical curricula, their design remains largely heuristic, with limited integration of real-time cognitive load dynamics or multi-modal learning analytics. The research problem centers on developing a high-fidelity simulation framework to model the interplay between instructional content complexity, learner cognitive states, and knowledge retention patterns in engineering problem-solving contexts. The computational approach combines neuromorphic machine learning architectures with discrete event simulation techniques to create a digital twin ecosystem for engineering education scenarios. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel execution of multiple agent-based learning models incorporating physiological response proxies (eye-tracking patterns, interaction latency metrics) and conceptual mastery trajectories across diverse engineering domains. The simulation environment will process synthetic cohorts representing varied demographic and cognitive profiles, iterating through different pedagogical strategies and content delivery modalities. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for optimal challenge pacing in engineering instruction and a generative AI toolkit capable of proposing context-aware curriculum adaptations. This work bridges educational neuroscience, computational pedagogy, and engineering systems design, offering novel methodologies for quantifying the cognitive ergonomics of technical education. The resulting framework aims to establish new standards for evidence-based engineering education resource development while providing foundational insights into the neurocognitive dimensions of engineering problem acquisition. By leveraging large-scale parameter space exploration enabled through HPC, this project addresses a critical gap in data-driven engineering education research, with potential applications ranging from adaptive credentialing systems to augmented reality-enhanced technical training platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach engineering and/or engineering subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in general engineering principals or at least one specific engineering discipline and in educational curriculum, instruction, pedagogy.

abstract: Dental prostheses, such as crowns, bridges, and dentures, require precise biomechanical compatibility to ensure long-term functionality and patient comfort. Current design and fabrication workflows rely heavily on manual adjustments and generic material specifications, which can lead to suboptimal fit, premature failure, or patient discomfort. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework to optimize the design and material composition of dental prostheses using patient-specific anatomical and biomechanical data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to model the complex interactions between prosthetic devices, oral tissues, and dynamic occlusal forces at unprecedented resolution. The research will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution mapping, machine learning algorithms to predict optimal geometric configurations, and multi-physics simulations to evaluate the performance of novel ceramic-polymer composite materials under physiological conditions. Key computational challenges include resolving micron-scale surface topography in 3D intraoral scans, simulating time-dependent material fatigue, and iterating designs across diverse patient datasets. The outcomes will establish predictive models for prosthesis longevity and biomechanical performance, enabling data-driven customization in dental laboratory workflows. By reducing trial-and-error prototyping and material waste, this approach has the potential to lower production costs while improving clinical outcomes. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will provide dental technologists with actionable insights for personalized prosthesis design, bridging gaps between digital dentistry, materials science, and biomechanical engineering. Successful implementation of this interdisciplinary methodology could redefine standards in prosthetic dental care, particularly for patients with complex anatomical needs or systemic conditions affecting oral tissue resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of dentists, to design and construct dental prostheses such as caps, crowns, bridges, dentures, splints, and orthodontic appliances. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, dental materials, ceramics technology, impressions, complete dentures, partial dentures, orthodontics, crowns and bridges, sculpture, bonding and assembly techniques, and equipment operation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into clinical neurophysiology to address the computational challenges of analyzing large-scale, multimodal electrophysiological datasets. Current clinical workflows for diagnosing and monitoring disorders such as epilepsy, neuromuscular diseases, and autonomic dysfunction rely on labor-intensive, time-limited interpretations of electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and nerve conduction studies (NCS). These methods often fail to leverage the full spatiotemporal complexity of high-density recordings or longitudinal data, limiting insights into disease progression and treatment response. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing automated, machine learning-driven pipelines for real-time and retrospective analysis of neurophysiological signals. The computational workflows will include (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale EEG/EMG datasets to detect subtle epileptiform patterns or neuromuscular junction abnormalities; (2) dynamic network modeling of multi-channel EEG to map seizure propagation pathways in drug-resistant epilepsy; and (3) federated learning frameworks to pool anonymized data across institutions while preserving privacy, enabling robust biomarker discovery. These tasks demand HPC resources due to the need for GPU-accelerated deep learning, high-memory nodes for whole-brain signal decomposition, and scalable storage for multi-center datasets. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for automated spike detection in EEG, predictive models of neuromuscular degeneration from EMG/NCS time series, and open-source tools for reproducible neurophysiology analytics. By translating computational advances into clinical workflows, this work aims to enhance diagnostic precision, enable personalized neuromodulation therapies, and establish scalable infrastructure for collaborative research in neurological disorders. The requested computing resources will directly support training of clinical researchers in computational methods, bridging the gap between electrophysiology and data science in patient care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous system disorders using a combination of clinical evaluation and electrophysiologic testing such as electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and nerve conduction studies (NCS).

abstract: Herbalism has long relied on empirical knowledge of plant-derived compounds for therapeutic applications, yet systematic validation of multi-compound interactions, bioavailability, and mechanisms of action remains a critical gap. This project seeks to computationally model the polypharmacological effects of traditional herbal formulations used in Western and Indigenous herbal medicine traditions, focusing on their modulation of neuroinflammatory pathways implicated in chronic pain and age-related cognitive decline. Current limitations in predicting synergistic or antagonistic interactions among hundreds of phytochemicals—particularly when combined with modern pharmaceuticals—require advanced computational approaches to address safety and efficacy concerns. We propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning-driven metabolomic network analysis, and agent-based models of blood-brain barrier permeation. High-performance computing resources will enable the analysis of 50+ herbal species from the Appalachian materia medica tradition, each represented by 200-500 phytochemicals, against multi-omic datasets of neuroinflammatory targets. This will involve parallelized docking simulations (AutoDock-GPU, OpenMM), dynamic pharmacophore refinement, and ensemble learning to predict herb-drug interaction risks. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for identifying high-priority herbal candidates for experimental validation, (2) quantitative safety profiles for traditional formulations in common clinical use, and (3) an open-access database mapping 10,000+ phytochemicals to neuroinflammatory pathway targets. By establishing computational workflows tailored to herbalism's unique polycompound challenges, this research aims to bridge traditional ecological knowledge with contemporary systems pharmacology, addressing critical gaps in evidence-based integration of herbal therapies into mainstream healthcare. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated simulations and large-scale data integration tasks impractical on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to utilize the materia medica and clinical practices of Western, Native American, African, Australasian, and other herbal medicine traditions to prevent and cure illness and temporary physical disorders. Includes instruction in basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; nutrition; terminology and materia medica; therapeutic herbalism; herbal pharmacy; botanicals and ethnobotany; wildcrafting and harvesting; labeling and dispensing phytotherapy; counterindications; practice management; consultation skills; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational challenges of modeling high-frequency, cross-jurisdictional financial transaction ecosystems to evaluate real-time regulatory compliance and systemic risk in decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms. As blockchain-based financial instruments and smart contracts proliferate, traditional accounting frameworks struggle to dynamically audit complex, automated transactions spanning multiple legal and fiscal regimes. The study proposes a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and graph neural network (GNN) approach to simulate interaction networks between autonomous smart contracts, liquidity pools, and regulatory boundaries at scale. High-performance computing resources are required to process terabyte-scale transaction histories from public blockchain ledgers while simultaneously training GNNs to detect emergent compliance gaps and cascading risk patterns. The computational workflow will integrate parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of market shock scenarios with temporal graph embeddings that capture evolving relationships between DeFi protocols, tokenized assets, and off-chain accounting events. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for predictive auditing of automated financial agreements, 2) quantitative metrics for jurisdictional arbitrage risks in cross-chain transactions, and 3) optimized graph sampling techniques to reduce computational overhead in large-scale compliance verification. This work bridges distributed systems engineering with forensic accounting principles, offering regulatory bodies and financial institutions tools to monitor algorithmic markets while preserving blockchain networks' decentralized benefits. The resulting models will be validated against real-world case studies involving interoperable DeFi platforms and central bank digital currency (CBDC) pilot programs, with performance benchmarks comparing CPU-GPU resource configurations for different network topologies.
cip_definition: An integrated or combined program in accounting and finance that prepares individuals to function as accountants and financial managers or analysts.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of architectural design paradigms across the 20th century through computational analysis of large-scale spatial and stylistic datasets, with a focus on understudied transnational exchanges between non-Western and Western architectural movements. Traditional methods in architectural historiography rely on qualitative case studies, limiting the capacity to identify macro-scale patterns or quantify the diffusion of design principles. The research problem centers on developing a reproducible framework to analyze digitized architectural drawings, photographs, and textual critiques using machine learning and spatial analytics, enabling systematic comparisons of formal language, material innovations, and theoretical influences across geographic and cultural contexts. High-performance computing resources will be critical for processing terabyte-scale visual archives, training convolutional neural networks to classify stylistic features, and running graph-based algorithms to map professional networks and intellectual lineages. Key computational challenges include adapting computer vision techniques to heterogeneous historical imagery and developing geotemporal visualizations that integrate socio-political metadata with design characteristics. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated architectural elements, quantitative models tracing the adoption of specific design strategies in response to geopolitical events, and interactive tools for visualizing contested narratives in architectural criticism. By bridging computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in architectural history while challenging Eurocentric periodizations through data-driven analysis of marginalized contributions to global modernism. The resource request supports GPU-intensive model training, large-memory nodes for graph computations, and scalable storage for collaborative annotation workflows.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the aesthetic, technical, and social development of the built environment and the architectural profession from earliest times to the present. Includes instruction in the principles of architecture and related fields; art history; historiography of architecture; architectural theory and criticism; related aspects of the history of technology and social and economic history; and various period, cultural, and stylistic specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of understanding the complex interactions between auditory processing deficits and speech-language pathologies in patients with communication disorders. Current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches often treat auditory and speech-language impairments as separate domains, limiting the development of integrated interventions. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets, including audiometric assessments, speech acoustics, neuroimaging, and longitudinal clinical records. The research will employ machine learning models to identify cross-modal biomarkers of co-occurring auditory-speech dysfunction, with a focus on neurodegenerative and pediatric populations. Computational models of neural networks involved in auditory-language integration will be developed using biologically plausible simulations, informed by dynamic causal modeling of functional MRI data. These simulations will test hypotheses about compensatory mechanisms in patients with acquired or congenital communication disorders. The scale of data integration—spanning terabytes of high-resolution neuroimaging, real-time speech signal processing, and population-level clinical data—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallel processing, large-memory workloads, and GPU-accelerated deep learning. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to personalize combined audiological and speech-language therapies, (2) a computational framework for simulating intervention outcomes across heterogeneous patient profiles, and (3) open-source tools for correlating subcortical auditory pathway integrity with speech production metrics. By elucidating the computational principles underlying integrated auditory-speech rehabilitation, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in dual-trained audiology-speech pathology care while establishing scalable methods for analyzing complex communication disorders. Results will directly inform the development of next-generation diagnostic protocols and multimodal therapeutic strategies within clinical training programs.
cip_title: Audiology/ Audiologist and Speech-Language Pathology/ Pathologist
cip_definition: An integrated program that prepares individuals to work as both audiologists and speech-language pathologists. Includes instruction in a variety of communication disorder studies, audiology, speech pathology, language acquisition, and the design and implementation of comprehensive therapeutic and rehabilitative solutions to communications problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of high-resolution, high-fidelity media production in photographic and film/video workflows, particularly as formats such as 8K video, virtual production environments, and AI-driven post-processing become industry standards. Current workflows in the Photographic and Film/Video Technology field struggle to efficiently process ultra-high-definition media, simulate complex lighting environments, or train machine learning models for automated editing and effects due to limited access to scalable computing resources. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize three core tasks: (1) real-time rendering of virtual sets with dynamic lighting simulations using ray-tracing algorithms, (2) parallel processing of large-scale image/video datasets for AI-assisted color grading and restoration, and (3) generative adversarial network (GAN) training for synthetic media generation in previsualization workflows. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated rendering via OpenCL and CUDA frameworks, distributed processing of media files using Apache Spark, and iterative model training with TensorFlow and PyTorch. The project will benchmark performance gains against current industry-standard workstations to quantify efficiency improvements in processing times, energy use, and output quality. Expected outcomes include open-source workflow templates for educational use, validated benchmarks for HPC integration in media production curricula, and novel techniques for reducing computational bottlenecks in collaborative film/video pipelines. By enabling scalable testing of emerging technologies like neural rendering and virtual production, this work will directly support student and faculty research in advanced cinematography, archival media preservation, and adaptive storytelling tools, bridging technical training with creative innovation in communication and journalism disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation and maintenance of camera and lighting equipment and the production of finished still, video, and film products under the supervision of photographers, directors, and editors. Includes instruction in equipment setup and maintenance; lighting; power supplies; studio and film set tasks such as camera operator, grip, and best boy; plate and negative handling and development; laboratory procedures; and digital software applications.

abstract: Hemodialysis is a life-sustaining therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease, yet variability in treatment efficacy and complications such as intradialytic hypotension remain significant challenges. Current protocols rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for patient-specific physiological dynamics, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model hemodialysis processes at high resolution, integrating patient-specific data to predict treatment responses and optimize dialysate composition, flow rates, and session duration. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale physiological systems, including vascular dynamics, solute transport across semipermeable membranes, and electrolyte equilibration. Patient data from electronic health records—such as blood pressure trends, serum electrolyte levels, and dialysis machine parameters—will inform boundary conditions for finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics models. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify patterns in historical data and refine predictive models. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing to manage large datasets, iterative parameter optimization, and real-time sensitivity analyses, which exceed the capabilities of local institutional servers. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for hemodialysis efficacy and adverse event risk, (2) personalized treatment recommendations to minimize complications, and (3) open-source tools to support clinical decision-making for dialysis technologists. By bridging gaps between empirical protocols and individualized care, this work aims to improve patient outcomes while providing dialysis technologists with advanced training resources rooted in computational biomedicine. The HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required scale and precision, enabling simulations that replicate complex biophysical interactions over clinically relevant timescales. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journals and integrated into renal technology curricula to enhance evidence-based practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance diagnostic and therapeutic precision in radiology by developing computational models to optimize multi-modal imaging analysis and radiation dose delivery. Current limitations in real-time processing of high-resolution imaging data—including dynamic contrast-enhanced X-ray, diffusion-weighted MRI, and 4D ultrasound—hinder the ability to delineate subtle pathological features or adapt therapies during image-guided interventions. Additionally, the interplay between patient-specific anatomy and radiation dosimetry in emerging techniques, such as radiopharmaceutical therapies and hyperthermic ablation, remains inadequately modeled for clinical translation. To address these challenges, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating machine learning (ML) and physics-based simulations. First, a deep convolutional neural network will be trained on multi-institutional datasets to segment tumors and critical structures across heterogeneous imaging modalities, leveraging distributed GPU nodes for accelerated model optimization. Second, Monte Carlo simulations of ionizing radiation transport and ultrasound wave propagation will be implemented using parallelized computation to predict dose deposition and thermal effects in patient-specific 3D anatomies derived from CT/MRI. These models will be validated against phantom experiments and retrospective clinical cases. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale imaging repositories, enabling submillimeter-resolution simulations, and reducing iterative computation times from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for real-time adaptive treatment planning, validated protocols to minimize off-target radiation exposure in novel radionuclide therapies, and quantitative biomarkers for early treatment response assessment. By unifying imaging analytics with biophysical modeling, this work aims to establish a scalable computational foundation for personalized radiologic care, directly addressing variability in interventional outcomes and enhancing the safety of advanced radiotherapeutic approaches.
cip_definition: Research on how to utilize x-ray, ionizing radiation, radionuclides, ultrasound, electromagnetic radiation, and image-guided intervention to diagnose and treat disease. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of cross-cultural narrative patterns in global folklore traditions, with a focus on gendered and community-based storytelling practices. Folklore Studies has long grappled with the challenge of systematically analyzing vast, heterogeneous collections of oral histories, folktales, and performative traditions while preserving their contextual richness. Current manual coding and qualitative methods struggle to address the scale of digitized archival materials now available, limiting researchers’ ability to identify nuanced patterns in aesthetic expression across cultures. Our interdisciplinary team proposes the development of a computational pipeline combining natural language processing (NLP), graph-based motif detection, and community-validated semantic analysis to examine how gender roles and communal identity are negotiated through recurring narrative structures. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of multilingual corpora spanning 15,000+ transcribed narratives from underrepresented cultural groups, while supporting iterative machine learning models trained to recognize culturally specific metaphor systems and performance markers. Custom graph algorithms will map relationships between tale types, character archetypes, and moral frameworks across regional traditions. By integrating computational outputs with ethnographic insights from collaborating cultural bearers, this approach addresses critical gaps in scalability and bias reduction for comparative folklore analysis. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph of cross-cultural narrative correlations, new methodological frameworks for ethically computing with community-based cultural data, and evidence-based insights into how marginalized groups employ folklore as adaptive resistance. The project will significantly enhance the capacity of cultural studies researchers to trace aesthetic innovation at previously unattainable scales while maintaining interpretive fidelity to localized meaning-making practices.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of creativity and aesthetic expression in everyday life, as expressed in narrative, literature, performing arts, culture, work, family and community.

abstract: This project seeks to characterize the structural organization of multisensory integration hubs in the mammalian thalamus, with a focus on resolving unresolved synaptic connectivity patterns that underlie neurological disorders such as autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. A critical barrier in mapping these circuits lies in analyzing the ultrastructure of thalamic nuclei at synaptic resolution across large tissue volumes—a task requiring petabyte-scale imaging datasets from serial electron microscopy and correlated light-electron microscopy. Current open-source tools for automated reconstruction of neural circuits are insufficiently optimized for the anisotropic resolution and staining variability inherent to thalamic datasets, necessitating custom computational pipelines. We request high-performance computing (HPC) resources to deploy a hybrid workflow combining GPU-accelerated deep learning for voxel-wise synapse classification, distributed CPU-based morphological tracing of long-range axonal projections, and graph-theoretical analysis of synaptic motifs. The proposed pipeline will process 50 TB of initial imaging data (3,000 coronal sections from murine thalamus), leveraging SLURM-managed parallelization for iterative model training and multi-scale registration. Validation will involve ground-truth comparison with manual reconstructions from the anterior pulvinar nucleus. This resource-intensive approach is expected to 1) generate the first connectome of thalamocortical circuits involved in multisensory processing, 2) identify pathognomonic alterations in synaptic bouton distribution in a transgenic ASD mouse model, and 3) release open-access thalamus-specific segmentation models to address a critical gap in neuroanatomical toolkits. Outcomes will directly inform mechanistic studies of sensory processing deficits and provide a computational framework for ultrastructural analysis of subcortical regions. The project’s scale—processing datasets orders of magnitude larger than existing thalamic connectomics efforts—is unfeasible without dedicated HPC infrastructure for memory-intensive graph computations and teravoxel image stitching.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates or the nervous system of invertebrates. Includes instruction in cellular and circuit anatomy, mapping of neuronal pathways, anatomical distribution and mapping of neuronal signaling molecules and their receptors, and the anatomical basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of corneal biomechanical adaptations in response to specialty contact lens designs using high-fidelity computational modeling. While modern optometric practice relies on empirical fitting approaches for irregular corneas (e.g., keratoconus, post-surgical cases), the biomechanical interplay between lens geometry, ocular surface strain, and long-term tissue remodeling remains poorly characterized. Current clinical paradigms lack predictive tools to optimize lens parameters for individual corneal stiffness profiles, often leading to iterative fitting processes and suboptimal visual outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing a multiscale finite element model integrating patient-specific corneal topography, viscoelastic tissue properties, and fluid-structure interaction dynamics under varying lens geometries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve micron-scale deformations across entire corneal surfaces while simulating multi-hour wear cycles at physiological timescales. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for nonlinear material behavior and machine learning surrogates to map strain distributions to clinical outcomes using retrospective fitting data from 850+ patients. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to recommend lens curvature, edge lift, and material rigidity based on pre-fit corneal biomechanics, reducing trial-and-error adjustments by ≥40% in silico. This interdisciplinary approach bridges optometric clinical practice with computational biomechanics, offering a paradigm shift toward precision contact lens design. Successful validation against optical coherence tomography and tonometry datasets could establish the first clinically deployable model of corneal-lens biomechanical compatibility, directly enhancing therapeutic outcomes for complex ocular surface disorders. The proposed HPC implementation will require parallelized execution across 200+ nodes to manage memory-intensive 3D meshing and real-time parameter optimization, exceeding the capabilities of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of optometry and that focuses on the principles and techniques for examining, diagnosing and treating conditions of the visual system. Includes instruction in prescribing glasses and contact lenses, other optical aids, corrective therapies, patient counseling, physician referral, practice management, and ethics and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in keyboard performance practice through computational analysis of large-scale performance datasets. The research problem centers on understanding the relationship between technical execution, expressive interpretation, and pedagogical outcomes in keyboard performance. While traditional analysis methods rely on manual observation or small-sample studies, this project will develop machine learning models to analyze multi-modal performance data—including audio recordings, MIDI kinematics, and motion-capture gestures—across diverse repertoire and skill levels. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) processing and synchronizing heterogeneous performance data using signal processing and time-series alignment algorithms; (2) training neural networks to detect patterns linking technical parameters (e.g., keystroke velocity, pedal timing) to expressive outcomes (e.g., phrasing, dynamic shaping); and (3) creating simulation environments to model the biomechanical demands of advanced keyboard works. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling terabyte-scale datasets from international performance archives, enabling parallel processing of high-dimensional feature spaces, and supporting iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include new analytical frameworks for quantifying performance excellence, data-driven insights into technical development pathways, and generative models that assist pedagogues in creating personalized training regimens. By bridging computational musicology and performance pedagogy, this research aims to establish evidence-based benchmarks for keyboard education while preserving artistic individuality. The resource request supports both proposed work in model development and ongoing analysis of historical performance corpora, with potential applications in adaptive learning systems and augmented practice technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the piano, organ, or related keyboard instruments and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in piano and keyboard pedagogy, ensemble playing, accompanying, service playing, repertoire, keyboard and pedal skills, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: Agricultural systems face increasing pressure to adapt to climate variability while maintaining productivity and sustainability. Current challenges include optimizing crop yields under fluctuating environmental conditions, improving pest and disease resistance in staple crops, and enhancing soil health management. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-resolution computational model integrating genomic, phenotypic, and environmental data to predict adaptive traits in key crops under diverse climate scenarios. The research will leverage machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-omic datasets (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) from wheat and soybean cultivars, combined with spatially explicit soil composition data and historical climate records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process terabytes of sequencing data, train neural networks on genotype-environment-phenotype associations, and run ensemble climate simulations at regional scales. The computational workflow will employ parallelized genomic prediction models, Bayesian inference for trait heritability analysis, and agent-based simulations of pest population dynamics under projected temperature and precipitation regimes. Expected outcomes include identifying genetic markers linked to drought tolerance, generating risk maps for emerging crop pathogens, and optimizing fertilizer application protocols using reinforcement learning. This work will provide actionable insights for breeding programs and precision agriculture, enabling data-driven decisions to improve crop resilience. By quantifying trade-offs between yield maximization and resource conservation, the project aims to advance sustainable agricultural practices while addressing food security challenges. The proposed HPC allocation will directly support scalable analyses that are infeasible on local clusters, reducing model training times from weeks to days and enabling high-fidelity simulations of agricultural systems across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and practice of agricultural research and production and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of practical agricultural problems. Includes instruction in basic animal, plant, and soil science; animal husbandry and plant cultivation; soil conservation; and agricultural operations such as farming, ranching, and agricultural business.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize computer-aided design (CAD) and drafting processes for complex, multi-disciplinary engineering projects, with a focus on addressing scalability challenges in parametric modeling and simulation. Current CAD/CADD systems often struggle to efficiently manage high-resolution 3D geometries, dynamic design iterations, and multi-physics simulations—particularly when handling large assemblies or real-time collaborative environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA), automate topology optimization, and accelerate generative design algorithms. The research will employ GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed computing frameworks to enable rapid evaluation of design alternatives under constraints such as material efficiency, structural integrity, and manufacturability. Key computational methods include the development of machine learning models for predictive design validation and the implementation of adaptive meshing techniques to reduce computational overhead in multi-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for cloud-based CAD collaboration, reduced iteration times for complex assemblies, and benchmark data quantifying the relationship between computational resource allocation and design optimization efficiency.
