This work will directly benefit engineering technology education by providing case studies and workflows that integrate HPC into CAD/CADD curricula, while offering industry-relevant tools for energy-efficient design processes. The resource allocation will support parametric studies involving 10,000+ variable design spaces, real-time rendering of assemblies exceeding 1 million components, and comparative analyses of optimization algorithms. By bridging the gap between conventional CAD workflows and HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish best practices for resource-aware design in engineering technology applications, with potential impacts across manufacturing, architectural systems, and industrial equipment development.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: Aging populations face complex psychological challenges influenced by intersecting biological, cognitive, and sociocultural factors. While counseling interventions for older adults aim to enhance mental health and cognitive resilience, variability in treatment efficacy remains poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by modeling the dynamic interplay between psychosocial stressors, neurocognitive aging, and intervention outcomes using advanced computational methods. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze longitudinal datasets from community-dwelling older adults (N ≈ 15,000), integrating behavioral assessments, ecological momentary assessments (EMA), and structural neuroimaging biomarkers. Machine learning pipelines will identify multivariate predictors of counseling response, while agent-based modeling will simulate how age-related changes in social networks interact with community-based mental health interventions. Computational demands include processing high-dimensional neuroimaging data (7T MRI), training ensemble models on imbalanced longitudinal outcomes, and running large-scale sensitivity analyses for intervention parameters. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive workflows and parallelizing computationally demanding tasks, such as Bayesian network analysis of time-varying risk factors. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for personalizing counseling strategies based on individual neurocognitive and social profiles, (2) simulation tools to optimize the timing and delivery of preventative interventions, and (3) open-source computational models linking geropsychological theory to applied practice. By clarifying mechanisms of resilience in later life, this work will directly inform the development of scalable, evidence-based counseling approaches tailored to aging populations’ needs. The requested resources will enable transformative advances in geropsychology research, bridging methodological gaps between individual-level clinical observations and population-level mental health trends.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychology of aging and of elderly individuals and populations, with reference to growth and decline across the life span. Includes instruction in gerontology, developmental and adult psychology, age-related development and decline of cognitive processes, age-related psychological and neurological disorders, social and personality development in aging populations and individuals, and applications to the clinical treatment and care of older adults.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design, fabrication, and acoustic optimization of musical instruments through high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulations and material analysis. Traditional instrument crafting relies heavily on empirical trial-and-error methods, which are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict complex acoustic behaviors. The research problem centers on overcoming these constraints by modeling the nonlinear interactions between materials, structural geometries, and sound propagation in both acoustic and electric instruments. Key challenges include simulating high-resolution vibrational modes in irregular instrument bodies, optimizing material composites for durability and tonal quality, and analyzing airflow dynamics in wind instruments under varying performance conditions. To address these, the project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, augmented by machine learning algorithms trained on acoustic datasets from historical and experimental instruments. These models will integrate material property data (e.g., wood grain anisotropy, metal fatigue patterns) and performance metrics (e.g., frequency response, harmonic distortion) to predict optimal fabrication parameters. The HPC environment is critical for handling the multi-physics complexity of these simulations, which require parallel processing of large-scale meshes and real-time parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for luthiers and repair technicians to preemptively identify stress points in instrument designs, reduce material waste, and customize instruments for specific acoustic profiles. Additionally, the project will generate open-access computational workflows tailored to instrument fabrication, bridging gaps between traditional craftsmanship and data-driven innovation. By enabling precise virtual prototyping, this work aims to enhance the sustainability of rare materials, expand access to high-quality instrument repair, and support the development of novel hybrid acoustic-electric instruments. The requested computing resources will directly contribute to reducing computational bottlenecks in simulating multi-scale physical interactions, ensuring robust validation against experimental data from collaborative workshops.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and tune acoustic and electric musical instruments. Includes instruction in methods and equipment for making musical instruments, electronic instrument amplification systems, techniques of cleaning, and methods of tuning musical instruments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the dynamic interactions between Polarity Therapy interventions and the Human Energy Field (HEF), as conceptualized in Randolph Stone’s integrative framework. Despite the growing clinical interest in energy-based therapies, the biophysical and computational foundations of HEF modulation remain understudied, limiting evidence-based optimization of Polarity Therapy protocols. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational tools to simulate how Polarity Therapy techniques—such as bodywork, yoga, and nutritional interventions—influence HEF patterns and correlate with physiological outcomes. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational model integrating quantum-inspired energy field simulations with physiological data from clinical studies. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of HEF perturbations using finite element analysis, coupled with machine learning pipelines to identify patterns in multimodal datasets (e.g., bioelectrical measurements, patient-reported outcomes, and motion-capture data from Polarity Yoga sessions). Key computational challenges include optimizing tensor-based representations of energy flow pathways, validating model predictions against empirical data, and ensuring real-time visualization for practitioner feedback. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for simulating Polarity Therapy’s effects on HEF dynamics, predictive models linking specific interventions to therapeutic outcomes, and mechanistic insights into energy field rebalancing. This work will advance the evidence base for Polarity Therapy by bridging energy medicine principles with computational biomedicine, while providing practitioners with actionable tools to personalize treatments. The project’s scale—requiring ~200,000 core-hours for initial simulations and 50 TB of storage for heterogeneous datasets—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve timely results. Successful implementation will position Polarity Therapy as a innovator in computational energy medicine, with broader implications for integrative health research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote health and well-being through application of the integrative therapeutic system based on the Human Energy Field theory developed by Randolph Stone. Includes instruction in polarity theory and principles, energy-based and orthodox anatomy and physiology, polarity processing, polarity bodywork, polarity yoga, energetic nutrition, energetic evaluation and assessment, client communication, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of embodied cognition in actor training through large-scale computational analysis of performance data. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically evaluating how nuanced physiological and vocal behaviors—such as gesture dynamics, breath patterns, and prosodic variations—contribute to the perceived authenticity of dramatic performances. Traditional pedagogical methods rely heavily on subjective observation, limiting the scalability and granularity of feedback for emerging performers. To address this, the project will employ machine learning models trained on multimodal datasets comprising motion-capture recordings, biometric sensor data, and audio-video archives of classical and contemporary theatrical works. Computational methods will include 1) biomechanical simulation of movement efficiency across different acting techniques using rigid-body dynamics models, 2) spectral analysis of vocal timbre variations correlated with emotional valence annotations, and 3) transformer-based natural language processing to map script semantic content to observed physical/vocal choices. These parallelizable workflows demand significant GPU-accelerated processing for real-time rendering of 3D movement reconstructions and distributed training of recurrent neural networks on terabyte-scale performance corpora. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models identifying biomechanically sustainable practices for demanding physical theater techniques, data-driven frameworks for optimizing vocal projection strategies in acoustic performance spaces, and open-source tools enabling quantitative benchmarking of stylistic consistency in script interpretation. By bridging computational analytics with performance praxis, this work aims to establish new methodologies for preserving embodied knowledge in acting pedagogy while reducing injury risks associated with intensive training regimens. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional sensor data and simulating audience perception models at scales unachievable through conventional laboratory infrastructure.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the achievement of naturalistic and believable behavior in imaginary circumstances. Includes instruction in voice and acting speech, stage dialects, movement, improvisation, acting styles, theatre history, script interpretation, and actor coaching.

abstract: Dental resin composites, widely used in restorative procedures, face critical challenges in long-term performance due to hydrolytic degradation and biofilm adhesion at the tooth-restoration interface. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve the dynamic, multiscale interactions between material chemistry, mechanical stress, and microbial activity that drive clinical failure. This project proposes an integrated computational framework to model degradation pathways and microbial colonization in dental composites, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome scale and complexity barriers. Molecular dynamics simulations will quantify water diffusion kinetics and hydrolysis reactions within methacrylate-based matrices under oral cavity conditions. Concurrently, finite element analysis will predict stress distribution in restored teeth during mastication, coupled with phase-field modeling to simulate crack propagation in aged composites. A novel agent-based model will explore how surface degradation products influence Streptococcus mutans biofilm formation. These multiscale simulations will be iteratively validated against experimental data from micro-CT and biofilm assays. By synthesizing materials science, microbiology, and biomechanics, this approach will establish predictive relationships between composite formulation, environmental stressors, and clinical failure modes. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational intensity of coupled physicochemical-biological models across relevant spatiotemporal scales (nanometers to millimeters; picoseconds to years). Expected outcomes include a digital twin platform for accelerated material optimization, reducing empirical trial cycles by 40-60%. This work addresses a critical gap in personalized restorative dentistry by enabling data-driven design of composites that balance mechanical resilience, degradation resistance, and antimicrobial properties. The computational framework will also provide foundational insights into oral microbiome-material interactions, advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of bioengineering and computational health sciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the neural and physiological underpinnings of communication disorders, with a focus on complex, understudied conditions such as acquired apraxia of speech and dysarthria in neurodegenerative diseases. Current clinical assessments for these disorders lack precision in mapping multidimensional deficits—such as speech motor planning errors, prosodic variability, and respiratory-phonatory coordination—to their neuroanatomical and biomechanical correlates. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multimodal data, including high-density electroencephalography (EEG), dynamic MRI of vocal tract kinematics, and respiratory plethysmography, acquired from a cohort of 120 participants with heterogeneous communication impairments. Machine learning models, including 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph-based neural architectures, will be developed to analyze spatiotemporal patterns across these datasets. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training these models on terabyte-scale neuroimaging and biomechanical data, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized grid searches, and simulating biophysical models of speech motor control. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of novel biomarkers linking specific neural oscillatory profiles to articulatory kinematics, (2) predictive models for stratifying patients into intervention-responsive subgroups, and (3) open-source tools for real-time analysis of speech physiology data in clinical settings. By enabling large-scale integration of heterogenous data types, this work will establish a computational foundation for personalized therapies in communication disorders while advancing methods at the intersection of clinical neuroscience and speech biomechanics. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for raw and processed datasets, and scalable deployment of analytic pipelines.
cip_title: Communication Disorders Sciences and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications disorders sciences and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of high-impact weather events underscore the need for improved predictive understanding of multi-scale atmospheric processes. Current numerical weather prediction (NWP) models struggle to resolve critical interactions among cloud microphysics, boundary layer turbulence, and radiative transfer, particularly in regions of complex terrain or oceanic-atmospheric coupling. This project seeks to advance the representation of these processes through high-resolution simulations enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to employ a coupled atmosphere-ocean modeling framework, integrating the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model with hydrodynamic ocean components, to investigate mesoscale convective systems and their modulation by aerosol-cloud interactions and sea surface temperature variability. The computational approach will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve turbulent eddies and cloud dynamics at sub-kilometer scales while maintaining global energy consistency. Ensemble simulations will quantify uncertainties in precipitation thresholds and storm intensification pathways under varying aerosol loading and thermodynamic profiles. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameterization schemes for ice-phase microphysics and subgrid-scale turbulence. The requested HPC resources will support petabytes of distributed storage for multi-terabyte initial condition datasets and thousands of core-hours for concurrent sensitivity experiments. Expected outcomes include new insights into precipitation efficiency of extreme storms, improved representation of cloud-radiative feedbacks in climate models, and optimized data assimilation workflows incorporating satellite-based lidar and radar observations. By addressing critical scale-aware modeling challenges, this work aims to enhance predictive skill for severe weather events while advancing fundamental knowledge of energy transfer mechanisms within the atmospheric boundary layer. The developed frameworks will be disseminated as community-ready tools to support next-generation NWP and climate modeling initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the processes governing the interactions, movement, and behavior of atmospheric phenomena and related terrestrial and solar phenomena. Includes instruction in cloud and precipitation physics, solar radiation transfer, active and passive remote sensing, atmospheric electricity and acoustics, atmospheric wave phenomena, turbulence and boundary layers, solar wind, geomagnetic storms, coupling, natural plasma, and energization.

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) is critical for preventing neurological injury during high-risk surgeries, yet current methods face challenges in real-time processing of complex neurophysiological data and predictive accuracy. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced machine learning (ML) models capable of analyzing multimodal neuromonitoring signals—including high-density EEG, EMG, and somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs)—with enhanced temporal resolution and spatial specificity. The primary research problem centers on the computational demands of integrating heterogeneous, high-volume data streams in real time while detecting subtle neurophysiological changes predictive of postoperative deficits. Existing clinical systems often rely on threshold-based alerts with limited sensitivity, risking delayed intervention. To overcome this, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, HPC resources will be used to parallelize preprocessing pipelines for noise reduction, feature extraction, and time-frequency analysis across terabytes of historical IONM data. Second, we will train deep neural networks (DNNs) using GPU-accelerated frameworks to identify patterns associated with emerging neural compromise, incorporating attention mechanisms to prioritize critical signal components. Validation will involve retrospective testing against surgical outcomes and prospective pilot integration with intraoperative systems. The expected significance lies in creating a scalable platform for early detection of neurological insults, potentially reducing complications such as stroke or paralysis. Outcomes will include open-source algorithms optimized for HPC environments, validation benchmarks for ML in IONM, and preliminary data supporting FDA-cleared device development. By enabling rapid analysis of multidimensional datasets beyond the capacity of clinical workstations, this project aims to advance precision in neuromonitoring and establish computational workflows adaptable to evolving neurotechnologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the neurocognitive and emotional correlates of art-making processes in pre-clinical populations, with the goal of establishing objective biomarkers for art therapy efficacy. Current art therapy research relies heavily on qualitative assessments, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this gap, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating high-density electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking data, and digital art process recordings (e.g., brushstroke kinematics, color choice dynamics) from participants engaged in structured art tasks. The primary computational challenge involves modeling multivariate time-series data across disparate modalities (neural, behavioral, and artistic) at millisecond resolution, requiring alignment of temporal patterns and identification of cross-modal signatures predictive of therapeutic outcomes. High-performance computing resources will enable the implementation of custom recurrent neural network architectures optimized for temporal fusion of heterogeneous data streams, alongside large-scale permutation testing to validate robustness. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated pipeline for quantifying art-making behaviors as multidimensional time-evolving signals, 2) predictive models linking specific neurodynamic patterns during creative expression to post-intervention psychological state improvements, and 3) open-source tools for visualizing art process biomarkers. This work will establish quantitative foundations for art therapy assessment while advancing computational methods for analyzing creative cognition. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training across >10,000 parameter combinations, storage/processing of petabyte-scale multimodal datasets, and parallelized statistical validation—capabilities unattainable with standard laboratory infrastructure. By bridging computational neuroscience and expressive therapies, this project aims to transform art therapy from a subjective practice to an evidence-based intervention modality.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: Chronic pain represents a complex, multifactorial challenge with significant variability in patient-specific pathophysiology and treatment response. Current approaches to pain management often rely on generalized protocols, leading to suboptimal outcomes and prolonged reliance on trial-and-error prescribing. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model patient-specific pain pathways and predict individualized therapeutic responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including dynamic functional MRI (fMRI), electrophysiological recordings, multi-omics profiles (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic), and longitudinal electronic health records—to construct mechanistic models of pain signaling networks. A key innovation lies in synthesizing these data layers into a unified graph-based representation that maps interactions between genetic predispositions, neuroinflammatory markers, and neural circuit dynamics. Machine learning models will be trained to identify latent biomarkers of treatment efficacy, with a focus on non-opioid therapies such as neuromodulation protocols and targeted pharmacogenomic interventions. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Bayesian optimization for parameter estimation in biophysical neural models, coupled with federated learning architectures to preserve patient privacy across collaborating institutions. The anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide clinician selection of therapies based on patient-specific neural and molecular profiles, (2) mechanistic insights into interindividual variability in pain chronification, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for simulating intervention impacts across biological scales. By bridging systems biology with clinical pain neuroscience, this work aims to advance precision pain medicine while reducing reliance on broadly ineffective or high-risk treatments. The scale of data integration and real-time simulation of neural ensemble dynamics necessitates access to HPC resources for distributed memory processing and GPU-accelerated deep learning, which are unavailable in local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A post-residency program of study that prepares physicians in the diagnosis, management, and treatment of acute and chronic pain. Includes instruction in anesthesiology, pain assessment, pain classification and diagnosis, pain neuroscience, palliative and end-of-life care, physical medicine and rehabilitation, psychiatry of pain, pain pharmacology, public policy, and legal issues of pain management.

abstract: Rangeland ecosystems, characterized by low productivity and high climatic variability, face increasing pressure from overgrazing, climate change, and competing land-use demands. Current management strategies often lack predictive precision due to the complex interactions between vegetation dynamics, soil hydrology, and grazing patterns. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, spatially explicit modeling framework to simulate rangeland resilience under alternative management scenarios, with a focus on optimizing livestock carrying capacity while maintaining ecological integrity. The research integrates multi-source data, including satellite-derived vegetation indices, soil moisture sensors, historical climate records, and field-measured forage biomass, into a coupled process-based and machine learning model. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale heterogeneity across large spatial extents (≥10,000 km²) and to perform ensemble simulations that account for stochastic climate projections and grazing regimes. Key computational challenges include parameterizing ecohydrological feedbacks in semi-arid soils, training convolutional neural networks to predict forage quality from hyperspectral imagery, and running Monte Carlo analyses to quantify uncertainty in long-term rangeland productivity. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold conditions for vegetation community transitions under drought stress, (2) spatially adaptive grazing management maps to balance livestock nutrition requirements with grassland recovery rates, and (3) open-source tools for real-time decision support in rotational grazing systems. By enabling computationally intensive scenario testing at ecologically relevant scales, this work will provide a mechanistic basis for sustainable management policies in agro-pastoral systems, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance resource efficiency in low-productivity landscapes. The requested HPC allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale geospatial data processing, and the deployment of interactive visualization platforms for stakeholder engagement.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of rangelands, arid regions, grasslands, and other areas of low productivity, as well as the principles of managing such resources for maximum benefit and environmental balance. Includes instruction in livestock management, wildlife biology, plant sciences, ecology, soil science, and hydrology.

abstract: Soil microbiomes play a critical role in agricultural productivity through nutrient cycling, plant-microbe interactions, and resilience to environmental stressors. However, predicting and managing these complex microbial communities remains challenging due to the scale of genomic diversity, nonlinear dynamics of microbial networks, and context-dependent responses to soil management practices. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of soil microbial community assembly and function under varying agricultural management regimes. We will integrate genome-resolved metagenomics, biogeochemical data, and agent-based modeling to simulate microbial interactions at micrometer-to-meter scales across soil matrices. Computational workflows will include (1) large-scale metagenomic assembly and annotation of soil microbiomes from long-read sequencing data, (2) dynamic flux balance analysis to predict metabolic interactions in rhizosphere communities, and (3) spatially explicit simulations of microbial dispersal and nutrient exchange in soil aggregates. These analyses require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte sequencing datasets, iterative optimization of genome-scale metabolic models, and high-resolution 3D simulations of soil microenvironments—tasks infeasible without dedicated HPC infrastructure. The resulting models will be validated against experimental data from controlled mesocosm studies and field trials evaluating cover cropping, tillage, and organic amendment strategies. By resolving how management practices alter microbial functional traits and community stability, this work will advance our ability to design soil health interventions that optimize crop productivity while reducing synthetic fertilizer inputs. The computational frameworks developed will provide scalable tools for linking microbial ecology to agroecosystem outcomes, addressing a critical gap in sustainable agriculture research. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the project’s goal of translating soil microbiome complexity into actionable management principles for agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on application of microbiological theory and methods to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions, and the biological components and effects of soil management strategies. Includes instruction in microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, soil chemistry and physics as related to biological characteristics, and environmental science.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of electrocardiographic (ECG) signal analysis through advanced computational modeling, addressing limitations in traditional methods for detecting cardiac arrhythmias and abnormalities. Despite the widespread use of ECG technology, challenges persist in analyzing high-volume, noisy datasets from ambulatory monitoring systems and wearable devices, particularly in distinguishing subtle pathological patterns from artifacts or benign variations. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on large-scale, heterogeneous ECG datasets to improve automated rhythm classification and anomaly detection. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of multi-lead ECG recordings, including publicly available databases and de-identified clinical data from partner institutions. Deep learning architectures, such as convolutional and transformer-based networks, will be optimized for parallelized training on GPU clusters to identify temporal and spatial features indicative of arrhythmias, ischemic events, and conduction disorders. Signal preprocessing pipelines will integrate noise reduction techniques and domain adaptation strategies to enhance model generalizability across diverse patient populations and recording devices. The project will further simulate cardiac electrical activity using finite-element modeling to generate synthetic ECG waveforms for augmenting training data and validating detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time ECG analysis, validated against expert clinician interpretations, with potential integration into clinical workflows and educational platforms. By improving diagnostic precision and reducing latency in identifying critical cardiac events, this research aims to directly support patient care and advance training in electrocardiograph technology. The scalability of these computational methods will also provide a foundation for future innovations in personalized cardiovascular monitoring, aligning with broader goals of improving health outcomes through technology-driven clinical decision support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized lower-limb prosthetics through biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Current prosthetic devices often lead to secondary musculoskeletal complications, such as osteoarthritis or chronic pain, due to suboptimal load distribution during movement. Traditional design approaches rely on static anatomical measurements and population-level averages, neglecting dynamic, patient-specific biomechanical interactions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating motion capture data, medical imaging, and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution across residual limb tissues and adjacent joints under real-world activity conditions. High-resolution simulations will model tissue deformation, pressure gradients, and joint kinetics at a granularity impractical for standard computing infrastructure. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will iteratively optimize prosthetic component parameters—such as socket geometry and material compliance—to minimize peak stresses while maintaining functional mobility. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations across diverse gait patterns, body weights, and activity levels, enabling the generation of adaptive prosthetic designs tailored to individual biomechanical profiles. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for prosthetic-related stress mitigation, an open-source optimization toolkit for clinical engineers, and preliminary evidence of reduced complication rates in patient case studies. By bridging computational biomechanics, materials science, and clinical rehabilitation, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for patient-specific prosthetic development, directly addressing unmet needs in musculoskeletal health and assistive technology innovation. The computational pipelines developed may also inform broader applications in orthotic design and post-surgical rehabilitation planning.
cip_title: Health Professions and Related Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health professions and related clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of corneal biomechanics in the context of early-stage keratoconus, a progressive thinning disorder of the cornea that severely impacts visual acuity. While clinical diagnostics for keratoconus rely on static structural imaging, emerging evidence suggests that dynamic biomechanical properties—such as tissue deformation under intraocular pressure or external forces—play a critical role in disease progression. Traditional experimental methods to assess these properties are limited by ethical and practical constraints in human studies, creating a gap in predictive modeling for personalized interventions. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific corneal topography data, derived from optical coherence tomography (OCT), with finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate multi-scale biomechanical behavior under physiological and pathological conditions. The FEA models will incorporate anisotropic hyperelastic material properties, regional thickness variations, and viscoelastic effects, calibrated against ex vivo experimental datasets. Machine learning algorithms will then be applied to identify biomechanical risk markers predictive of rapid progression, enabling stratification of pre-symptomatic patients. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of 3D FEA simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, as well as to train deep neural networks on the resulting high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for keratoconus progression and a computational toolkit for optimizing corneal cross-linking protocols, a common treatment to stiffen weakened corneal tissue. This work bridges optometry, computational biomechanics, and machine learning, offering a novel paradigm for early intervention in corneal ectatic disorders and laying a foundation for patient-specific therapeutic design in vision science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in optometry.

abstract: The development of advanced polymeric materials for extreme-environment applications—such as aerospace, deep-sea exploration, or next-gen energy systems—requires a fundamental understanding of how multiscale polymer dynamics respond to coupled stressors (e.g., high radiation, pressure, and thermal cycling). Current experimental methods struggle to isolate these interacting effects at relevant spatiotemporal scales, while existing computational models often oversimplify hierarchical material behavior, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to bridge this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate the nonlinear, nonequilibrium dynamics of engineered polymers under multifactorial stress conditions. Using a hybrid computational framework, we integrate coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) to capture mesoscale chain reorganization, finite element analysis (FEA) for continuum-level mechanical response, and machine learning (ML)-accelerated parameterization to link atomistic-scale chemical degradation pathways (via quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics simulations) to macroscopic failure modes. The HPC environment is critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of concurrent stressors across disparate time scales (nanoseconds to hours) and spatial resolutions (Ångströms to micrometers). Key objectives include identifying design rules for radiation-resistant elastomers in orbital infrastructure and optimizing self-healing hydrogels for high-pressure submersible seals. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source simulation toolkit for multifactorial polymer degradation prediction, (2) mechanistic insights into stressor coupling effects on viscoelastic energy dissipation, and (3) accelerated discovery of three polymer formulations with tailored extreme-environment performance. By unifying materials chemistry, continuum mechanics, and data science approaches, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for computationally driven polymer design, reducing reliance on iterative physical prototyping. The requested resources will enable large-scale parametric studies (>10^6 core-hours) to resolve rare events and stochastic interactions central to polymer failure, directly supporting national priorities in advanced materials resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the structure and processing of polymeric materials and how these relate to properties and performance. Combines instruction in both Polymer science and engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in precision manufacturing workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize toolpath generation and material behavior prediction in subtractive and additive manufacturing processes. Current approaches to precision production trades, particularly in CNC machining and 3D printing, rely on iterative physical prototyping and simplified computational models that inadequately account for dynamic thermal, mechanical, and material interactions. This results in prolonged development cycles, material waste, and suboptimal product performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-physics simulation framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) models to predict tool wear, residual stresses, and microstructure evolution during fabrication. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across diverse manufacturing scenarios, processing high-resolution sensor data from in-situ monitoring systems to train neural networks for real-time process adjustments. Computational workloads will include parametric optimization of machining parameters (e.g., feed rates, spindle speeds) and layer-by-layer thermal history modeling for metal additive manufacturing, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes for ML inference and distributed memory clusters for large-scale FEA/CFD coupling. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of reducing prototyping iterations by 40–60% in precision machining applications and improving dimensional accuracy in complex additive components by 15–25%. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—particularly the need to resolve micron-scale features across macro-scale workpieces—necessitates access to HPC architectures with petascale storage and low-latency interconnects. Results will advance data-driven decision-making in precision production trades while providing open-source simulation templates to bridge gaps between academic research and industry adoption. This work directly supports workforce development in advanced manufacturing by integrating HPC workflows into technical curricula for precision production specialists.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in creating products using precision crafting and technical illustration.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of silicate melt behavior in magmatic systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of multicomponent phase equilibria and reactive transport. A critical gap persists in modeling the coupled effects of volatile species (e.g., H2O, CO2) and trace elements on melt crystallization kinetics at pressures and temperatures relevant to planetary crust formation. Traditional thermodynamic models often oversimplify non-ideal mixing in silicate melts, leading to inaccuracies in predicting mineral stability fields and melt-vapor partitioning. To address this, we propose an integrated computational approach combining atomistic-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using density functional theory (DFT) with mesoscale phase-field modeling. The MD simulations will parameterize melt structure and diffusion properties under varying fugacities of volatiles, while phase-field models will simulate crystal growth/dissolution dynamics in multicomponent systems. These datasets will inform machine learning-driven optimization of existing geochemical software (e.g., MELTS) to improve predictive capacity for disequilibrium processes. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of quantum mechanical calculations (VASP) across thousands of cores, coupled with GPU-accelerated phase-field simulations of polycrystalline textures. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of silicate melt properties validated against experimental studies, (2) open-source modules for modeling volatile-bearing magmatic systems, and (3) new constraints on timescales of magma reservoir evolution prior to volcanic eruptions. By resolving microscale controls on macroscale geochemical signals preserved in igneous rocks, this work will enhance interpretations of planetary differentiation processes and volcanic hazard forecasting. The computational demands—particularly the need for teraflop-scale processing of 3D reactive transport models with >10^7 grid points—necessitate dedicated allocation of HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemical properties and behavior of the silicates and other substances forming, and formed by geomorphological processes of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in chemical thermodynamics, equilibrium in silicate systems, atomic bonding, isotopic fractionation, geochemical modeling, specimen analysis, and studies of specific organic and inorganic substances.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance protocols for hybrid renewable energy systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex failure modes and optimize repair strategies. Current maintenance frameworks for integrated solar-wind-storage systems often rely on generalized schedules or reactive approaches, leading to costly downtime, component degradation, and safety risks. The computational challenge lies in analyzing terabyte-scale sensor datasets—capturing thermal, vibrational, and electrical parameters—while simulating multi-physics interactions across heterogeneous energy infrastructure. Our team will develop machine learning models trained on historical failure data and synthetic scenarios generated through finite element analysis (FEA) of stress accumulation in photovoltaic arrays, wind turbine bearings, and lithium-ion battery cells. HPC resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify failure probabilities under variable environmental and operational conditions, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to prioritize maintenance actions. Key deliverables include a fault-propagation graph database for cross-system dependency mapping and an adaptive scheduling tool that reduces unplanned outages by ≥30% in simulated microgrid test cases. By integrating time-series forecasting with materials degradation models, this work aims to establish scalable protocols for condition-based maintenance in next-generation energy systems. The computational outputs will be validated against empirical data from three partner solar-wind farms, with open-source code and benchmark datasets disseminated to advance research in energy infrastructure resilience. This project directly supports workforce training initiatives by generating case studies for technician education programs focused on data-driven repair decision-making.
cip_title: Energy Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale cultural and textual datasets central to advancing interdisciplinary research in Women’s Studies. The research problem focuses on identifying and mapping transnational feminist discourse across digital archives of literature, art, and grassroots media produced by women and gender-diverse communities between 1970 and 2010. Current scholarship lacks systematic computational methods to trace the evolution of feminist thought across linguistic, geographic, and cultural boundaries, particularly in underrepresented regions. This project addresses this gap by employing natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal network analysis to examine over 10,000 digitized texts, artworks, and oral histories from open-access repositories and institutional collections. Computational workflows will be designed to detect thematic patterns, semantic shifts in feminist terminology, and cross-cultural citation networks while preserving contextual nuance. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to recognize culturally specific expressions of gender-based resistance and solidarity in multilingual materials, with attention to regional dialects and non-dominant linguistic forms. Image analysis pipelines will extend this work to visual media, using convolutional neural networks to catalog recurring symbolic motifs in feminist art. The scale of data and complexity of multilingual, multimedia analysis necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-model training, and high-memory storage. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible interactive atlas of feminist cultural production, 2) computational frameworks for ethically grounded feminist digital humanities research, and 3) new insights into how marginalized communities navigated intersecting oppressions during global feminist movements. By integrating computational rigor with intersectional feminist theory, this project aims to redefine methodological norms in Women’s Studies, offering tools to recover historically silenced voices and challenge Eurocentric periodizations of feminist history. Resource allocation will directly support GPU-intensive model training, distributed storage for sensitive data, and scalable visualization of results.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of women, and the development of modern feminism in relation to the roles played by women in different periods and locations in North America and the world. Programs may focus on literature, philosophy, and the arts as much as on social studies and policy.

abstract: The increasing demand for physician assistants (PAs) in diverse clinical settings necessitates innovative approaches to optimize PA education and readiness. A critical gap lies in understanding how large-scale biomedical datasets and patient outcomes can inform predictive models to enhance clinical decision-making training for pre-PA students. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal health data—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic datasets, and longitudinal patient outcomes—to identify patterns in disease progression, treatment efficacy, and risk factors. The computational approach integrates machine learning (ML) algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, to model complex interactions between genetic, demographic, and clinical variables. These models will be trained on curated datasets spanning 500,000+ anonymized patient cases from public repositories (e.g., MIMIC-IV, UK Biobank) and synthetic data simulating rare clinical scenarios. Computational workflows will prioritize scalability, with distributed training across GPU nodes to handle high-dimensional data and hyperparameter optimization. Key outcomes include (1) predictive tools for identifying high-risk patient subgroups, (2) a framework for simulating clinical decision pathways under resource constraints, and (3) open-source educational modules integrating these models into pre-PA curricula. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform pre-PA training by grounding pedagogical strategies in data-driven clinical patterns, thereby improving students’ preparedness for real-world diagnostic and ethical challenges. Access to HPC resources is essential to process terabytes of raw data, reduce model training times from weeks to days, and enable iterative testing of hypothetical clinical scenarios. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with PA program directors and clinical informatics conferences, fostering broader adoption of computational tools in health professions education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional physician assistant program.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the cognitive and linguistic processes underlying second language acquisition (SLA) among adult learners in English as a Second Language (ESL) programs. While existing research emphasizes sociocultural and pedagogical factors, the computational modeling of real-time language processing—particularly the interplay between syntactic complexity, semantic retention, and cross-linguistic interference—remains underexplored. To bridge this gap, we propose a large-scale computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze longitudinal datasets of learner interactions, including written essays, spoken dialogue transcripts, and reading comprehension assessments. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to extract syntactic structures, lexical diversity metrics, and error patterns, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer-based models will simulate incremental language production and comprehension. Parallelized simulations will model the impact of母语 (L1) transfer on English morphosyntactic development across diverse language pairs (e.g., Mandarin-English, Spanish-English). The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the scale of multimodal data (over 10,000 learner hours), the complexity of training multilingual models with attention mechanisms, and the need for real-time analysis in virtual ESL classroom simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for identifying at-risk learners based on computational biomarkers, (2) evidence-based strategies for personalized curriculum design targeting syntactic and semantic bottlenecks, and (3) open-source NLP tools optimized for SLA research. By integrating computational linguistics with applied ESL pedagogy, this work aims to advance both theoretical models of interlanguage development and practical interventions for postsecondary ESL programs.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English for those for whom English is not their mother tongue. Includes instruction in the use of basic communication skills to develop and transmit ideas and thoughts in English as well as specialized programs that focus on the development of proficiency in English sufficient to meet specific occupational or academic demands. Note: These programs are for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential. For second language programs that are not for academic credit towards a postsecondary credential, see 32.0109.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable framework for optimizing the reliability and performance of distributed, real-time software systems through advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. Modern software systems increasingly rely on decentralized architectures to meet demands for low latency and fault tolerance, but existing design tools struggle to model emergent behaviors in large-scale, heterogeneous deployments. The research will address this gap by creating a high-fidelity simulation environment that integrates discrete-event modeling, probabilistic verification, and reinforcement learning to predict system outcomes under dynamic workloads and partial failures. The computational approach will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to explore state spaces efficiently, while graph neural networks will be trained to identify optimal resource allocation strategies across distributed nodes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for two aspects: (1) executing millions of parameterized simulation runs to capture rare failure modes in complex interaction networks, and (2) training deep learning models on terabyte-scale synthetic datasets representing diverse infrastructure configurations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for architecture-aware software optimization, validated against industrial case studies in edge computing and IoT control systems. The work will advance software engineering practices by providing empirically grounded methods to quantify trade-offs between consistency, availability, and resource utilization in distributed environments. Results will directly inform curriculum enhancements in concurrent system design and fault-tolerant software courses, while the computational artifacts will serve as a community resource for reproducible research in performance engineering. This project requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and high-memory CPUs for large-scale discrete-event simulations, with an estimated need for 200,000 core-hours over 12 months to achieve statistically significant results across target use cases.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, analysis, verification, validation, implementation, and maintenance of computer software systems using a variety of computer languages. Includes instruction in discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, computer science, managerial science, and applications to complex computer systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing health education pedagogy through computational modeling of dynamic student learning patterns and behavioral outcomes. Current approaches to training health educators often rely on static curricula that do not account for the complex interplay between instructional strategies, sociocultural factors, and evolving public health priorities. We propose developing an adaptive simulation framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model how different teaching methodologies influence long-term health literacy and decision-making in diverse student populations. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling with machine learning techniques to simulate classroom environments, incorporating real-world datasets on adolescent health behaviors, regional health disparities, and educational outcome metrics. By parallelizing thousands of simulated teaching scenarios across demographic contexts, the models will identify pedagogical strategies that maximize knowledge retention and positive health behavior adoption. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the stochastic nature of human learning processes, which requires iterative parameter optimization across multidimensional spaces encompassing cognitive, emotional, and social learning dimensions. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics toolkit that informs the design of evidence-based health education curricula and a novel competency assessment system for teacher trainees. This work will advance health teacher education by enabling data-driven personalization of instructional methods while maintaining scalability for widespread implementation. The resulting computational framework will be disseminated as an open-access resource for educator preparation programs, potentially impacting public health outcomes through improved training of next-generation health educators.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach health education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance clinical and translational research in cardiovascular disease (CVD) heterogeneity, a critical barrier to personalized treatment. Despite advances in risk stratification, a significant proportion of patients exhibit unpredictable disease progression or treatment responses, likely due to underexplored molecular and cellular interactions. To address this, we propose integrating multi-omics data (genomics, proteomics, single-cell transcriptomics) with clinical outcomes from a longitudinal cohort of 5,000 CVD patients. The computational workflow will employ machine learning models to identify dynamic biomarkers of disease subphenotypes, coupled with mechanistic network simulations to map how genetic variants and immune-inflammatory pathways converge to drive clinical variability. Key challenges include processing >50 TB of raw sequencing data, scaling graph-based neural networks for multi-modal integration, and running agent-based simulations of cellular interactions across 10,000+ parameter combinations. Access to HPC resources with parallelized GPU nodes and large-memory CPUs is essential to complete these tasks within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework linking molecular signatures to CVD trajectories, (2) validated subnetworks as therapeutic targets, and (3) open-source tools for clinical biomarker discovery. By clarifying mechanisms of heterogeneity, this work will directly inform the design of adaptive clinical trials and precision therapies, bridging a persistent gap between bench research and patient care. The requested resources will accelerate analyses that are intractable with standard hospital computing infrastructure, ensuring robust, reproducible results for translation into practice.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated clinical science program that prepares clinicians to conduct clinical and translational research in various areas. Note: programs that prepare clinicians to conduct research in specific scientific fields should report under the relevant CIP code series (e.g., Series 26 Biological and Biomedical Sciences).

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing decentralized quality control in distributed manufacturing networks using privacy-preserving federated learning (FL) models. Modern manufacturing systems increasingly rely on geographically dispersed production nodes, creating challenges in maintaining consistent product quality while adhering to data privacy regulations. Traditional centralized machine learning approaches face latency, security, and scalability limitations when applied to these environments. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulation platform to design and evaluate FL architectures that enable real-time anomaly detection across networked facilities without raw data exchange. The research will parameterize heterogeneous manufacturing environments, simulate multi-node FL workflows, and test neural network architectures under varying communication constraints and data distributions. Computational experiments will leverage parallelized training of deep learning models on GPU clusters to assess convergence rates, robustness to adversarial perturbations, and trade-offs between model accuracy and network latency. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for FL deployment in industrial quality assurance, validated against real-world datasets from partner automotive and electronics manufacturers. By advancing scalable, privacy-aware machine learning for distributed systems, this work aims to reduce defect rates by 15–30% in pilot implementations while maintaining compliance with evolving data sovereignty standards. The project bridges gaps in applied systems engineering, computational statistics, and cybersecurity, offering a template for HPC-enabled innovation in next-generation smart manufacturing ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles inherent to engineering to the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern masonry systems, which integrate advanced materials like high-performance concrete, fiber-reinforced composites, and adaptive thermal barriers, demands a deeper understanding of their structural and environmental behavior under dynamic loads. Traditional empirical methods for evaluating masonry performance are limited in predicting nonlinear stress distributions, long-term durability under climate variability, or the impact of novel material combinations. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing computational models to simulate multi-scale masonry behavior, optimize material configurations, and predict failure mechanisms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) simulations, which require parallel processing to handle the high-resolution meshing and iterative load-testing scenarios inherent to heterogeneous masonry assemblies. Computational workflows will integrate machine learning algorithms to identify correlations between material properties, mortar composition, and environmental exposure data, enabling predictive analytics for masonry performance. Key objectives include modeling seismic resilience in decorative masonry façades, analyzing thermal bridging effects in insulated structural masonry systems, and optimizing reinforcement strategies for sustainable masonry-infilled concrete frames. The scale of these simulations—involving millions of elements and multiphysics interactions—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and data storage. Outcomes will provide actionable insights for advancing masonry codes and standards, reducing material waste through computational prototyping, and enhancing energy efficiency in building envelopes. This work will also support educational initiatives by generating open-access datasets for masonry technology curricula, bridging hands-on training with computational literacy in the masonry trades. By integrating HPC-driven research with applied masonry science, the project aims to position computational modeling as a transformative tool for innovation in this historically craft-based field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the laying and/or setting of exterior brick, concrete block, hard tile, marble and related materials, using trowels, levels, hammers, chisels, and other hand tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, blueprint reading, structural masonry, decorative masonry, foundations, reinforcement, mortar preparation, cutting and finishing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the diachronic and synchronic variations of Korean dialects, with a focus on phonetic, syntactic, and lexical evolution. Despite the rich diversity of Korean dialects, comprehensive studies remain limited due to the challenges of processing large-scale historical and contemporary speech/text corpora. The primary research problem involves modeling dialectal divergence patterns and quantifying the influence of socio-geographic factors on language change, which requires computationally intensive analyses of multi-register datasets spanning pre-modern to modern Korean. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for unsupervised dialect classification, dynamic phonetic alignment algorithms for comparing archaic and modern phonological systems, and agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about language contact effects. A custom corpus of digitized historical texts (15th–19th centuries) and contemporary spoken/written data from under-documented regional dialects will be processed using GPU-accelerated pipelines to extract phonological, morphological, and syntactic features. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning models on heterogeneous data (≈50 TB), running parallelized comparative analyses across 20+ dialect groups, and performing Monte Carlo simulations of language change scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first computational atlas of Korean dialect evolution, a publicly accessible database of annotated linguistic features, and predictive models of language shift in minority dialect communities. This work will provide novel insights into the mechanisms of Korean language variation, directly supporting preservation efforts for endangered dialects and informing applied domains such as speech technology localization and heritage language pedagogy. By bridging traditional philological methods with cutting-edge computational linguistics, the project aims to establish a framework for data-driven humanities research in Korean studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized motor rehabilitation frameworks for individuals with neurological impairments, a critical focus area within pre-occupational therapy education and practice. Current rehabilitation protocols often adopt generalized approaches, which fail to account for the heterogeneity in neural recovery patterns, sensorimotor deficits, and patient-specific environmental contexts. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating multimodal neuroimaging, biomechanical movement data, and machine learning to model patient-specific motor learning processes. The research will analyze high-resolution functional MRI (fMRI) and motion capture datasets from stroke survivors to identify neural correlates of motor adaptation, combined with biomechanical simulations of upper-limb task performance under varying environmental constraints. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to predict optimal therapeutic task progressions tailored to individual neurophysiological profiles and functional goals. The computational workflow demands significant parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization in biomechanical simulations, as well as GPU-accelerated training of neural networks on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework that maps neuroplasticity dynamics to personalized rehabilitation strategies, thereby informing clinical decision-making and enhancing pre-occupational therapy curricula with data-driven approaches to intervention design. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational neuroscience, rehabilitation engineering, and occupational therapy, offering a novel paradigm for optimizing motor recovery while aligning with emerging trends in precision rehabilitation. The project’s success hinges on HPC capabilities to manage computationally intensive simulations and machine learning workflows, which are infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying biofield therapies—such as Qi Gong and Therapeutic Touch—which purportedly modulate physiological states through non-invasive energy interactions. Despite anecdotal and clinical evidence of their effects on pain, inflammation, and stress, the fundamental principles of energy transfer, field dynamics, and cellular response remain poorly characterized. A critical barrier is the lack of multiscale computational models capable of simulating low-energy bioelectromagnetic interactions within biologically relevant systems. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven study integrating quantum mechanical, molecular dynamics, and continuum-level electromagnetic simulations. These models will map how externally applied energy fields (e.g., low-frequency electromagnetic waves or simulated "healing" waveforms) interact with ion channels, cell membranes, and tissue networks, focusing on mitochondrial voltage gradients, ATP production, and redox signaling pathways. Simulations will be parameterized using experimental data from in vitro bioelectric assays and validated against high-resolution biosensor measurements. The HPC framework will enable parallelized optimization of field parameters (frequency, amplitude, spatial distribution) and probabilistic analysis of emergent tissue-scale effects. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of plausible biophysical pathways for biofield-induced cellular modulation, (2) predictive models linking therapeutic parameters to specific physiological responses, and (3) a scalable computational platform for designing targeted energy-based interventions. By elucidating mechanisms at the intersection of biophysics and alternative medicine, this work aims to establish a quantitative foundation for optimizing biofield therapies, addressing skepticism about their scientific plausibility while advancing computational tools for studying subtle energy interactions in biological systems. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics (Amber, GROMACS), finite element electromagnetic modeling (COMSOL), and custom Python-based multiscale integration workflows requiring ~500,000 core-hours and large-memory nodes for terascale datasets.
cip_title: Energy and Biologically Based Therapies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative, complementary, and somatic health and therapeutic services not elsewhere classified (bioenergetics, cranio-sacral therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Qi Gong, and others).

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the dynamic evolution of decentralized terrorist networks and their adaptive responses to counterterrorism interventions. While traditional approaches to counterterrorism often rely on static network analyses or qualitative assessments, this study addresses a critical gap by integrating computational social science, behavioral psychology, and systems dynamics to simulate how terrorist organizations reorganize under pressure. The research focuses on three interconnected challenges: (1) identifying latent patterns in organizational restructuring after leadership decapitation strikes, (2) quantifying the impact of resource disruption (e.g., financial sanctions) on operational capabilities, and (3) modeling the emergence of hybrid threats combining physical attacks with cyber-enabled disinformation campaigns. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making hierarchies, graph neural networks to analyze dark web communication patterns, and ensemble machine learning techniques to process multilingual extremist content from decentralized platforms. The project will utilize distributed computing architectures to manage heterogeneous datasets spanning encrypted messaging logs, cryptocurrency transaction ledgers, and geospatial incident reports. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for predicting organizational resilience thresholds, a risk assessment toolkit for evaluating intervention trade-offs, and actionable insights into counter-network strategies that minimize unintended escalatory effects. By enabling large-scale parallel simulations of multi-domain threat scenarios, the requested HPC resources are essential for advancing predictive capabilities in counterterrorism operations while maintaining ethical AI governance standards. This work bridges technical and policy-oriented research, offering a template for computational social science applications in national security domains.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the study of terrorism as a global and national threat and the methods for analyzing and countering it. Includes instruction in psychology, cultural studies, terrorist history and organization, terrorist capabilities, terrorist finance and international money-laundering, threat assessment, intelligence operations, incident command systems, border security, emergency response, joint operations, surveillance and communications systems, cyberterrorism, weapons of mass destruction, counterterrorist operations, and applications to specific terrorist organizations and threats.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address operational inefficiencies in food service management, focusing on the optimization of dining room workflows, staff allocation, and customer satisfaction. Despite advances in hospitality technology, many restaurants struggle to balance dynamic variables such as fluctuating customer demand, real-time staff performance, and post-pandemic sanitation protocols. Traditional manual or rule-based approaches often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these factors, leading to suboptimal resource use, prolonged wait times, and inconsistent service quality. To resolve this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), discrete-event simulation (DES), and reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate and analyze complex dining room ecosystems. The ABM component will model customer behavior, including arrival patterns, seating preferences, and meal duration variability, while DES will map staff movements, table turnover, and sanitation workflows. RL algorithms will then iteratively optimize staff-task assignments and seating policies under constraints such as labor costs and hygiene compliance.
