By scaling these simulations across HPC clusters, we will generate granular insights into high-efficiency service configurations under diverse scenarios (e.g., peak hours, special events). Expected outcomes include a predictive decision-support tool capable of recommending adaptive staffing levels, table layouts, and workflow prioritization in real time. This tool will be validated against empirical data from partner restaurants, with success metrics including reduced customer wait times (target: 15–20%), improved staff utilization rates, and enhanced compliance with safety protocols. The project bridges computational modeling and hospitality management, offering a novel application of HPC to a non-traditional domain while advancing operational sustainability in food service industries.
cip_title: Food Service, Waiter/Waitress, and Dining Room Management/Manager.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve food to customers in formal or informal settings.  Includes instruction in the nutritional, sensory, and functional properties of food and its ingredients; food services principles; table and counter services; dining room operations and procedures; service personnel supervision and management; communication skills; business math; safety; and sanitation.

abstract: Emerging antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens poses a critical threat to global health, particularly in low-resource settings where empirical treatment guidelines remain prevalent. This project seeks to address the urgent need for computationally driven strategies to predict AMR evolution, optimize treatment regimens, and inform clinical decision-making. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating clinical patient data, bacterial genomic sequencing, and molecular dynamics simulations to model resistance mechanisms and predict drug efficacy across diverse populations. The computational pipeline will leverage machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-omic datasets from 15,000+ clinical isolates (spanning WHO priority pathogens) and correlate genetic markers with phenotypic resistance patterns. Molecular dynamics simulations will then model interactions between antimicrobial agents and mutated bacterial targets, enabling atomic-level insights into resistance pathways. These outputs will feed into a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model optimized for HPC parallelization to simulate drug performance under varying host physiologies and dosing strategies. The scale of genomic data, complexity of simulations, and need for real-time analysis of evolving resistance trends necessitate access to HPC resources for efficient data processing, storage, and large-scale parameter sweeps. Expected outcomes include predictive models of region-specific AMR emergence, actionable biomarkers for rapid diagnostics, and personalized therapeutic recommendations deployable via point-of-care platforms. By bridging clinical data with computational biology, this work aims to reduce AMR-associated mortality, prolong drug efficacy, and provide a scalable framework for adaptive treatment guidelines in resource-variable healthcare systems. Successful implementation will directly support WHO AMR containment goals while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in addressing global health disparities.
cip_definition: Research focused on Global Health

abstract: The increasing demand for precision and durability in horological and jewelry components necessitates advanced computational approaches to overcome limitations in traditional empirical methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address two interconnected challenges: (1) optimizing microstructural properties of novel alloys for watch springs and jewelry settings to enhance fatigue resistance and tribological performance, and (2) simulating complex mechanical interactions in miniature horological systems under extreme environmental conditions. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve atomic-scale material behaviors and predict long-term wear patterns in these microscale components, particularly when accounting for multivariate stressors such as temperature fluctuations, humidity, and mechanical load cycling. The proposed computational workflow integrates molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model grain boundary dynamics in proprietary alloys, coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) of stress distribution in multi-axis escapement mechanisms. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to identify optimal geometric tolerances for jewel bearings and predict failure modes in soldered joints under nanoscale deformation. These multi-scale simulations require parallel processing capabilities to handle system sizes exceeding 10 million atoms (MD) and transient thermal-structural coupling across micron-scale geometries (FEA). Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for material selection in horological applications, validated against microhardness testing and chronometric stability measurements, as well as generative algorithms for designing topology-optimized jewelry components compatible with additive manufacturing. By bridging computational materials science with artisanal craftsmanship, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for precision engineering in heritage technologies, reducing prototyping costs by an estimated 40% while enabling unprecedented structural complexity in decorative and functional elements. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary spatial-temporal resolution in these simulations, which would be computationally intractable on local cluster infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make repairs, and maintain timepieces, time-measuring devices, and jewelry items. Includes instruction in mechanical timekeeping systems, digital timekeeping systems, timesetting, casting, engraving, polishing, stonesetting, soldering, fine microscopic work, equipment and tool maintenance, redesign and restyling techniques, and customer relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational framework for analyzing systemic interactions between criminal justice policies, socioeconomic disparities, and recidivism outcomes. Despite the critical role of data-driven modeling in criminal justice reform, existing tools often oversimplify complex feedback loops between institutional decision-making, community dynamics, and individual behavioral patterns. The research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based simulation environment that integrates heterogeneous datasets—including historical incarceration records, demographic variables, and programmatic intervention outcomes—to model how localized policy changes propagate through interconnected social and legal systems. Computational challenges include processing multi-terabyte datasets with temporal-spatial granularity, calibrating probabilistic models of decision-making by justice system actors, and simulating long-term societal impacts under varying policy scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations, Bayesian network inference, and machine learning-driven parameter optimization at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating criminal justice policy trade-offs, validated against real-world recidivism data from three U.S. states. This work aims to provide policymakers with evidence-based insights into unintended consequences of sentencing reforms, resource allocation for diversion programs, and equity implications of risk assessment algorithms. By bridging computational social science with correctional science, the project establishes a methodological foundation for analyzing criminal justice systems as complex adaptive systems, while adhering to ethical guidelines for sensitive data usage. The requested resources directly support scalability requirements for national-level simulations, reducing runtime for ensemble models from estimated weeks on conventional clusters to days, thereby accelerating iterative policy analysis cycles.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general study of criminal justice and corrections. Includes instruction in criminology, criminal justice, correctional science, forensic science, law enforcement, psychology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize trauma triage decision-making in emergency nursing through advanced computational modeling of patient outcomes under time-sensitive, high-acuity conditions. Emergency departments (EDs) face critical challenges in rapidly prioritizing care for trauma patients, particularly during mass casualty incidents or resource-constrained scenarios. Current triage protocols rely on static scoring systems that inadequately account for dynamic patient variables, overlapping injuries, or real-time resource availability. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework trained on multi-institutional trauma registries, including high-dimensional data from 250,000+ patient encounters (e.g., vital sign trajectories, injury patterns, interventions, and outcomes). The research will employ neural architecture search to identify optimal model architectures for predicting deterioration risk and intervention time sensitivity, while incorporating stochastic simulations of ED resource availability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multimodal clinical data at scale, running parallelized hyperparameter optimizations, and executing Monte Carlo simulations of triage scenarios under varying constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) a real-time decision support tool that dynamically updates triage priorities based on evolving patient states and system capacity, (2) quantitative evidence for modifying existing triage protocols, and (3) open-source simulation modules for training emergency nurses in resource allocation strategies. The computational models will be validated against retrospective outcomes data and pilot-tested through prospective observational studies in three Level I trauma centers. By integrating clinical expertise with ML-driven predictive analytics, this work aims to reduce preventable mortality in trauma care while providing emergency nurses with evidence-based tools to manage complex triage decisions under uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver advanced, direct patient care in emergency and trauma settings. Includes instruction in advanced health assessment, pharmacology, physiology, emergency management, trauma conditions, trauma assessments and acute care.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in somatic bodywork therapies by analyzing multimodal datasets to quantify physiological and biomechanical responses to therapeutic interventions. Somatic bodywork—including manual therapies, movement re-education, and touch-based modalities—is widely practiced, yet evidence-based frameworks for optimizing treatment protocols remain underdeveloped. Current limitations stem from the complexity of modeling dynamic interactions between therapeutic techniques, tissue biomechanics, and patient-specific physiological states. This research addresses these gaps by integrating motion capture data, electromyography (EMG), wearable sensor outputs, and patient-reported outcomes into computational models to simulate and predict therapeutic efficacy. The primary computational challenge involves processing high-dimensional, time-series datasets to identify patterns in neuromuscular activation, fascial strain, and proprioceptive feedback across diverse patient populations. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of finite element simulations to model tissue deformation under varying therapeutic loads, coupled with machine learning algorithms to classify optimal intervention parameters. A secondary aim involves developing real-time feedback systems for training practitioners, requiring GPU-accelerated rendering of biomechanical simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking specific manual techniques to short- and long-term clinical outcomes, (2) open-source tools for visualizing biomechanical effects of somatic interventions, and (3) datasets correlating objective physiological measures with subjective therapeutic experiences. By bridging empirical somatic practice with computational rigor, this work will establish a foundation for evidence-based protocol design, enhance educational standards in therapeutic services, and enable personalized treatment strategies. The scale of data processing—projected to require 50+ TB of storage and sustained multi-core computations for iterative model training—necessitates dedicated HPC infrastructure beyond typical institutional capacities. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary health informatics platforms to foster collaboration between somatic practitioners and computational researchers.
cip_title: Somatic Bodywork and Related Therapeutic Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in somatic bodywork and related therapeutic services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing large-scale, stochastic industrial systems under dynamic constraints, with applications in supply chain resilience and process integration. The research addresses the challenge of designing adaptive systems capable of responding to disruptions such as material shortages, demand fluctuations, and energy variability. Current analytical models struggle to balance real-time decision-making with long-term strategic planning, particularly when handling high-dimensional uncertainty or nonlinear interactions between subsystems. The proposed work combines mixed-integer programming, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to model multi-echelon networks, integrating production scheduling, inventory management, and logistics coordination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to solve these computationally intensive problems within practical timeframes. Parallelized algorithms will be implemented to accelerate scenario-based optimization, leveraging distributed computing frameworks for Monte Carlo simulations of disruption scenarios. A key innovation involves embedding graph neural networks within decomposition methods to predict bottleneck propagation across interconnected systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision support tool that identifies robust resource allocation policies and quantifies trade-offs between efficiency and resilience metrics. The results will advance fundamental methodologies in operations research by addressing state-space explosion in stochastic optimization, with direct applications to semiconductor manufacturing and pharmaceutical distribution case studies. By enabling rapid evaluation of mitigation strategies for systemic risks, this work aims to reduce operational downtime costs by an estimated 15–25% in modeled systems. The computational infrastructure will also support open-source code development for reproducible industrial engineering research, fostering collaboration on complex system optimization challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Combines instruction in industrial and systems engineering.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the long-time behavior of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in geometric analysis and mathematical physics, with a focus on high-dimensional settings where analytical methods alone are insufficient. The central challenge lies in characterizing stability, blow-up phenomena, and convergence properties of solutions to equations such as the Schrödinger-Poisson system and geometric flows with nonlocal terms. These systems exhibit intricate dependencies on initial data and parameter configurations, particularly in dimensions ≥4, necessitating large-scale numerical simulations to complement theoretical analysis. The computational approach integrates adaptive spectral methods with wavelet-based multiresolution techniques to efficiently discretize high-dimensional domains while preserving critical structural features like conservation laws and symmetries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations across distributed memory architectures, leveraging GPU acceleration for tensor contraction operations inherent to high-dimensional function representations. Key objectives include quantifying phase transitions in solution stability under parameter variations, identifying dimension-dependent regularity thresholds, and validating conjectures about energy concentration mechanisms in critical regimes. Expected outcomes include new criteria for global existence of solutions, optimized algorithms for functional-analytic computations in high dimensions, and open-source software tools for adaptive wavelet-based PDE solvers. The results will advance foundational understanding of nonlinear dynamics in functional spaces while providing methodological innovations applicable to problems in harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory. This work requires sustained access to HPC clusters with multi-node GPU support, large memory nodes (>1TB), and parallel file systems to manage petascale datasets generated by long-time horizon simulations. Computational benchmarks indicate a need for approximately 500,000 core-hours to achieve sufficient resolution across parameter studies, with data analysis workflows incorporating topological data analysis to detect persistent patterns in solution landscapes. The proposed resource allocation will directly support both numerical verification of theoretical predictions and the discovery of new phenomena guiding future analytical investigations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and behavior of equations, multivariate solutions, functions, and dynamic systems. Includes instruction in differential equations, variation, approximations, complex variables, integrals, harmonic analysis and wavelet theory, dynamic systems, and applications to mathematical physics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between tumor microenvironmental factors and metastatic progression in epithelial cancers. A critical barrier in oncology lies in understanding how spatial heterogeneity in oxygen tension, extracellular matrix (ECM) composition, and paracrine signaling collectively drive cancer cell migration, invasion, and colonization of distant tissues. Traditional experimental models struggle to capture the multiscale, nonlinear interactions between these variables, limiting the identification of context-specific vulnerabilities in metastatic cascades. To address this, we propose a spatially resolved, 3D agent-based computational model simulating tumor cell behavior under physiologically relevant biophysical constraints. The model will integrate empirical data from patient-derived xenograft systems, including hypoxia gradients, collagen fiber alignment, and cytokine diffusion profiles, to parameterize cancer cell decision-making processes such as epithelial-mesenchymal transition, matrix remodeling, and collective migration. HPC resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across microenvironmental conditions, track emergent tumor subpopulations, and statistically validate model predictions against histological and intravital imaging datasets. Expected outcomes include the identification of microenvironmental "tipping points" that promote metastatic dissemination and the prediction of combinatorial therapeutic strategies targeting stromal co-evolution. By bridging tumor physiology with computational dynamics, this work aims to advance mechanistic insights into metastasis and inform the development of microenvironment-modulating therapies. The requested allocation will support parallelized simulations across 10,000+ core-hours, enabling iterative refinement of the model and high-resolution analysis of tumor-ECM feedback loops at scales inaccessible to conventional in vitro systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of carcinogens; the onset of malignancy in cells, tissues, blood, and organs; the genetics of cancer; the anatomy and physiology of cancer cells; and the study of cancer behaviors and treatments. Includes instruction in gene expression; oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes; viral genes and cancer proliferation; regulation of signal transduction; cancer proteins; hormonal and growth factors in cancer cells; tumor promotion, progression, and metastasis; carcinogen receptors and metabolism; carcinogen ecology; immunological targeting; and studies of genetic, chemical, radiologic and other treatment therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between cellular architecture and extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions during tissue morphogenesis, with a focus on how mechanical forces and adhesion dynamics guide spatial organization in epithelial systems. A critical gap exists in understanding how subcellular structural adaptations—such as cytoskeletal rearrangements and focal adhesion turnover—translate to multicellular patterning in heterogeneous environments. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with continuum mechanics to simulate cell-ECM feedback loops across scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these systems, where individual cell agents (1,000–10,000 cells per simulation) will be modeled with dynamic membrane receptors, strain-dependent cytoskeletal responses, and force-sensitive ECM remodeling behaviors. Each cell agent will interact with a discretized ECM substrate, governed by partial differential equations capturing local stiffness, ligand density, and deformation. Parallelized simulations will run parameter sweeps to test hypotheses on how ECM heterogeneity influences collective cell migration and tissue boundary formation. Validation will leverage experimental datasets from live-cell imaging of avian embryonic epithelia and ECM proteomic profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying mechanochemical thresholds that stabilize tissue architecture, (2) predicting ECM modifications that disrupt pathological adhesion in fibrotic models, and (3) generating open-source simulation tools for visualizing 3D cell-ECM force networks. This work will advance foundational knowledge in histogenesis and provide a computational pipeline for designing biomimetic scaffolds in regenerative medicine. The scale of parameter space exploration and real-time visualization of terabyte-level simulation data necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure, which are unavailable in our current local computing environment.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure, function, and regulation of cells as individual units and as components of larger systems. Includes instruction in cell chemistry, cellular dynamics, cellular replication and reproduction, cell anatomy, membrane function, organelles, cell adhesion and extracellular matrices, cell dynamics and motility, meiosis and mytosis, signal transduction, regulation, recognition and defense mechanisms, the cell cycle, cell metabolism and respiration, gene expression, and studies of cell types and characteristics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern architectural designs demands advanced computational tools to optimize energy efficiency, structural integrity, and material usage while adhering to evolving sustainability standards. Current architectural drafting workflows, reliant on conventional CAD/CADD software, face limitations in simulating large-scale or highly detailed building systems, particularly when evaluating dynamic environmental interactions or iterative design alternatives. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable, physics-informed simulation frameworks for architectural design optimization. The research will focus on two interconnected computational workflows: (1) parametric modeling and finite element analysis (FEA) for structural performance prediction under multi-hazard scenarios, and (2) energy performance simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and building energy modeling (BEM) to assess thermal and airflow dynamics. Machine learning techniques will be applied to automate the exploration of design parameter spaces, identifying configurations that balance aesthetic, functional, and sustainability criteria. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of resource-intensive tasks such as daylighting analysis, material lifecycle assessment, and generative design iterations across diverse climate zones. By interfacing CAD/CADD platforms with HPC clusters through custom scripting APIs, the project aims to create a seamless workflow for architectural drafters to access advanced simulation capabilities without compromising design intent. Expected outcomes include quantifiable improvements in simulation accuracy for complex architectural systems, reduced computational bottlenecks in design iteration cycles, and validated models for sustainable material optimization. The developed framework will provide architectural practitioners and educators with a template for integrating high-fidelity computational analysis into standard drafting workflows, advancing the field’s capacity to address challenges in energy-efficient construction and resilient design. This work directly aligns with institutional priorities in engineering technology education by bridging architectural design pedagogy with cutting-edge computational methodologies.
cip_title: Architectural Drafting and Architectural CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations for architectural and related construction projects. Includes instruction in basic construction and structural design, architectural rendering, architectural-aided drafting (CAD), layout and designs, architectural blueprint interpretation, building materials, and basic structural wiring diagramming.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time decision-making in high-stress military operational environments, leveraging advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. Traditional decision-support systems often struggle to account for the dynamic interplay of human cognitive limitations, environmental unpredictability, and mission-critical constraints. Our research addresses this gap by modeling complex scenarios—such as urban reconnaissance or contested logistics operations—where rapid adaptation to emergent threats and resource limitations is paramount. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based simulations that integrate behavioral data from military training exercises with real-time sensor inputs, environmental variables, and adversarial action-reaction dynamics. These simulations will train reinforcement learning models to identify optimal decision pathways under uncertainty while minimizing cognitive overload for personnel. Key computational challenges include scaling neural architecture searches for time-sensitive predictions, parallelizing scenario variations to cover low-probability/high-impact events, and validating models against classified operational datasets in secure virtual environments. The expected outcomes include a prototype decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive contingency plans with quantified risk profiles, as well as generalized insights into human-machine collaboration under stress. This work bridges military operational theory, cognitive science, and computational systems engineering, offering a novel approach to enhancing mission resilience in asymmetric conflict environments. By utilizing HPC resources to simulate thousands of interdependent variables across operational timelines, the project aims to advance both applied military readiness and interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and human factors analysis.
cip_title: Military Technologies and Applied Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military technologies and applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of complex molecular interactions in materials science, a critical area within science-related technologies. The research addresses a fundamental challenge: accurately simulating dynamic, multiscale processes in novel material systems, such as self-assembling polymers or catalytic nanoparticles, where experimental characterization alone is insufficient to resolve rapid or atomic-scale behaviors. Traditional computational methods struggle with the spatial and temporal scales required to capture these phenomena, limiting predictive design capabilities. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using optimized force fields with machine learning (ML)-accelerated free energy calculations. The MD simulations will employ GPU-optimized software (e.g., LAMMPS, GROMACS) to model systems comprising millions of atoms over microsecond timescales, while ML surrogate models will predict thermodynamic properties from subsets of simulation data, reducing computational cost. The HPC resources will enable parallel execution of parameterized simulations across diverse material compositions and environmental conditions (temperature, pressure), generating datasets to train and validate the ML algorithms. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models for predicting phase behavior and reaction pathways in target material systems, (2) open-source workflows integrating MD and ML tools for broader scientific use, and (3) actionable insights for designing materials with enhanced catalytic or mechanical properties. By bridging gaps between atomistic simulations and macroscale material performance, this work will directly support experimental collaborations in energy storage and nanotechnology. The requested resources—including GPU nodes for ML training and high-memory CPUs for large-scale MD—are essential to handle the iterative, data-intensive nature of this research, which demands rapid processing of terabyte-scale simulation outputs. Results will advance both computational methodology and practical material innovation, aligning with the program’s mission to integrate technical skills with scientific research.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of scientific research and development. Includes instruction in standard laboratory practices and procedures; techniques for analysis, testing and inspection; laboratory instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance; laboratory and materials handling safety; and computer applications.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the coevolution of biomechanical and biochemical signaling in hybrid biological-physical systems, focusing on the self-organization of synthetic cell-matrix composites under dynamic environmental stimuli. This project bridges evolutionary developmental biology, soft matter physics, and nonlinear dynamical systems to address a critical gap in understanding how spatially heterogeneous mechanical forces and chemical gradients jointly govern emergent multicellular patterning in artificial tissues. The central challenge lies in modeling multiscale feedback loops—where subcellular signaling cascades influence macroscopic matrix remodeling, which in turn alters local stress fields and nutrient diffusion—a process requiring high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations of coupled reaction-diffusion-advection systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement hybrid computational frameworks combining lattice Boltzmann methods for fluid-structure interactions, agent-based models for cellular decision-making, and finite element analysis for continuum-scale mechanics. Unique algorithmic developments will focus on adaptive mesh refinement to capture boundary instabilities at cell-matrix interfaces and machine learning-accelerated parameter optimization for rare-event sampling. Expected outcomes include predictive models of synthetic morphogenesis in mechanically active biomaterials, with applications to programmable tissue engineering and adaptive soft robotics. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scaling to simulate >10^6 interacting cellular agents within viscoelastic matrices across physiologically relevant timescales (hours-days). By establishing open-source simulation tools for this emerging interdisciplinary niche, the project aims to catalyze convergence between developmental biology, active matter physics, and synthetic biology communities, while providing benchmark datasets for data-driven discovery of universal principles in hybrid living-nonliving systems.
cip_definition: A program that is either a general synthesis of one or more of the biological and physical sciences, or a specialization which draws from the biological and physical sciences.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the interplay between dietary composition, metabolic adaptation, and health outcomes in companion animals, with a focus on optimizing therapeutic diets for chronic conditions such as obesity and renal disease. Current nutritional models often rely on generalized physiological assumptions, failing to account for individual variability in nutrient absorption, microbiome-host interactions, and genetic predispositions. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multi-scale, mechanistic models integrating species-specific genomic, metabolomic, and clinical data. These models will simulate nutrient flux across tissues, predict microbiome-mediated metabolite production, and quantify dynamic responses to dietary interventions. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify patterns in high-dimensional datasets from longitudinal veterinary trials, enabling the stratification of metabolic phenotypes and personalized nutrient recommendations. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized simulations to explore parameter spaces governing nutrient-gene interactions and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationships in heterogeneous populations. By coupling agent-based modeling of gut microbial communities with whole-body metabolic networks, the project aims to predict how tailored dietary modifications alter disease trajectories. Expected outcomes include validated predictive frameworks for diet optimization, open-access tools for veterinary clinicians, and novel biomarkers linking nutrient utilization to health status. This work will advance precision veterinary nutrition by establishing computational methods to reconcile individual biological complexity with clinical dietary guidelines, ultimately improving the management of diet-responsive disorders in diverse animal populations. The scale of data integration and real-time simulation demands HPC resources to achieve clinically actionable resolution within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the chemical nature of food substances; the processes by which animals ingest, digest, absorb, transport, utilize and excrete food and nutrients; and their relation to animal behavior and health.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical drivers of corneal ectatic disorders, such as keratoconus, through advanced computational modeling. Current clinical assessments rely on static anatomical measurements, which poorly predict disease progression or therapeutic outcomes. To overcome this, we propose developing patient-specific, dynamic finite element models (FEMs) of corneal tissue behavior under physiological stress, integrating multimodal imaging data (Scheimpflug tomography, optical coherence tomography) and intraocular pressure dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets, simulate nonlinear anisotropic tissue responses at micron-scale resolution, and perform probabilistic analyses of biomechanical failure thresholds. Machine learning pipelines will be trained on these simulations to identify subclinical biomarkers of instability and optimize personalized cross-linking treatment protocols. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for real-time iterative modeling and uncertainty quantification across heterogeneous patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform for stratifying progression risk in early-stage keratoconus and a virtual testing environment for novel refractive surgery approaches. By bridging optometric imaging, computational biomechanics, and HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to transform the paradigm of corneal disease management from reactive to proactive, reducing vision loss through earlier intervention. The resource request supports the development of open-source tools for clinical translation, enabling optometry practitioners to integrate computational insights into diagnostic workflows without requiring specialized hardware.
cip_title: Ophthalmic and Optometric Support Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ophthalmic and optometric support services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize adaptive logistics planning for large-scale construction projects under supply chain volatility, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic resource allocation strategies. Construction logistics—particularly in multi-phase projects like industrial plants or urban infrastructure—face compounding risks from material shortages, labor variability, and geopolitical disruptions. Traditional linear scheduling tools inadequately capture these interdependencies, leading to cascading delays and cost overruns. The proposed study will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate decentralized decision-making across suppliers, contractors, and transport networks under stochastic conditions. Using HPC resources, the team will parameterize a multi-agent system reflecting real-world constraints (e.g., equipment availability, carbon emission limits, just-in-time delivery tolerances) and train RL policies to minimize project-wide downtime. The computational workflow will process terascale datasets from historical project records, IoT-enabled job sites, and global supply chain APIs to calibrate risk profiles. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of forecasting disruption propagation and recommending real-time adjustments to procurement routes, workforce deployment, and inventory buffers. By quantifying trade-offs between resilience and efficiency in resource allocation, this work aims to advance adaptive capacity in construction management—a critical need in an era of climate and geopolitical uncertainties. The HPC component is essential for parallelizing thousands of stochastic simulations, enabling near-real-time policy updates during model training. Results will be validated against case studies from offshore wind farm construction, where logistical complexity and regulatory constraints exacerbate scheduling challenges. This interdisciplinary approach bridges operations research, computational sustainability, and construction systems engineering, offering a novel paradigm for data-driven resilience in capital projects.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage, coordinate, and supervise the construction process. Includes instruction in commercial, residential, mechanical, highway/heavy civil, electrical, environmental, industrial, and specialty construction; facilities management; budgeting and cost control; logistics and materials management; organization and scheduling; personnel management and labor relations; site safety; construction contracting; construction processes and techniques; and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis of multi-scale interactions between climate variability, agricultural productivity, and market dynamics in domestic and international contexts. A critical challenge in agricultural economics lies in modeling complex, non-linear relationships across heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution climate projections, spatially disaggregated crop yields, and global commodity trade flows—while accounting for stochastic shocks and adaptive decision-making by farmers, policymakers, and supply chain actors. Current methods often rely on simplified assumptions due to computational constraints, limiting their capacity to inform resilient resource allocation strategies. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating dynamic stochastic economic models with machine learning techniques to simulate adaptive behaviors under diverse climate and market scenarios. The project will employ parallelized econometric estimation of panel data spanning 40 years of agricultural production, trade, and environmental variables across 150 countries, coupled with agent-based modeling to capture decentralized decision-making. HPC resources are essential for scaling Bayesian hierarchical models to process terabytes of satellite-derived land-use data and for running Monte Carlo simulations evaluating the fiscal and welfare impacts of climate-adaptive policies. Expected outcomes include empirically grounded insights into optimal investment thresholds for drought-resistant infrastructure, price stabilization mechanisms for volatile global markets, and spatially explicit risk maps to guide regional agricultural subsidies. By enhancing the granularity and robustness of agricultural economic models, this work will directly contribute to evidence-based policies that balance productivity, sustainability, and equity in resource allocation. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source packages to support reproducible research in the field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics to the analysis of resource allocation, productivity, investment, and trends in the agricultural sector, both domestically and internationally. Includes instruction in economics and related subfields as well as applicable agricultural fields.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems, a rapidly growing but understudied domain within Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law. The proliferation of blockchain-based financial instruments, smart contracts, and autonomous governance protocols has created novel challenges for traditional regulatory paradigms, particularly in areas such as liability attribution, jurisdictional conflicts, and compliance automation. The project aims to address the critical gap in systematic, data-driven analysis of how emergent DeFi architectures interact with existing legal doctrines, focusing on case law, regulatory enforcement patterns, and transactional data spanning multiple jurisdictions. Computational methods will include large-scale natural language processing (NLP) of judicial opinions, regulatory filings, and smart contract codebases to identify latent legal risk factors, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate the systemic impacts of proposed regulatory interventions on decentralized networks. Graph analytics will map cross-jurisdictional regulatory arbitrage pathways, while cryptographic techniques will anonymize sensitive transactional datasets for ethical analysis. The HPC environment is essential for processing multi-terabyte legal corpora, training domain-specific large language models (LLMs) to detect regulatory signal in unstructured text, and running parallelized simulations of market behaviors under varying legal constraints. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for assessing compliance exposure in DeFi projects, quantitative metrics for evaluating regulatory fragmentation across jurisdictions, and open-source tools for automated audit trail reconstruction in blockchain transactions. By integrating computational social science methodologies with doctrinal legal analysis, this interdisciplinary project aims to establish new paradigms for proactive regulatory design in algorithmically governed financial systems while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of legal scholarship and high-performance computing.
cip_title: Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law and process related to the regulation of businesses and the financial services industry. Includes instruction in corporate law, antitrust law, securities law and regulation, negotiation, incorporation, partnerships, trusts, and related topics

abstract: The built environment faces escalating demands to balance energy efficiency, structural resilience, and occupant well-being amid climate change and urbanization. Current design practices often treat building systems—such as HVAC, envelope performance, and load-bearing structures—in isolation, leading to suboptimal solutions. This project proposes a computational framework to holistically optimize architectural systems through high-fidelity, multi-physics simulations. The research will integrate energy modeling, structural mechanics, and airflow dynamics to evaluate interdependent performance metrics in diverse climatic and operational scenarios. Central challenges include resolving scale disparities between component-level details (e.g., thermal bridging in wall assemblies) and whole-building responses, as well as managing the combinatorial complexity of design parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms at scale. Proposed workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for real-time parametric studies and employ surrogate models to reduce computational costs during iterative design exploration. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of identifying Pareto-optimal solutions that minimize embodied carbon while maximizing operational efficiency and seismic performance. The project will also generate benchmark datasets for atypical building geometries, addressing gaps in existing codes and standards. By enabling rapid evaluation of novel materials and adaptive systems, this work aims to advance data-driven decision-making in architectural engineering, directly supporting the development of next-generation sustainable infrastructure. Resource allocation will specifically target memory-intensive CFD simulations of natural ventilation patterns and distributed computing for uncertainty quantification across urban microclimate models.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials, systems, and methods used to construct and equip buildings intended for human habitation or other purposes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to address inefficiencies in real-time language interpretation and technical translation, particularly for low-resource languages paired with English or French. Current neural machine translation (NMT) systems struggle with context retention, domain-specific terminology, and the syntactic complexity of simultaneous interpretation, especially in scenarios requiring bidirectional or multi-speaker processing. To overcome these limitations, we propose training large-scale transformer-based architectures on augmented multilingual corpora, integrating parallel text, speech, and contextual metadata from government, healthcare, and legal domains. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing terabytes of speech-text aligned data, optimizing dynamic vocabulary adaptation algorithms, and simulating real-time interpretation scenarios through parallelized inference tasks. The computational workflow will involve contrastive fine-tuning of pretrained language models (e.g., mBART, Whisper) using domain-adapted Canadian parliamentary proceedings, Indigenous language oral histories, and technical manuals in French/English pairs. Memory-intensive attention mechanisms will be refined to handle code-switching patterns and rare morphological forms in target languages such as Inuktitut and Plains Cree. Expected outcomes include open-source translation frameworks with 15-20% improved BLEU/TER scores over existing systems for Indigenous language pairs, plus latency-optimized interpretation models deployable on edge devices. This work will directly support Canada’s multilingual policy infrastructure while establishing computational best practices for preserving linguistic diversity through AI-assisted translation technologies. The requested GPU nodes and distributed storage systems will enable critical experiments in cross-modal alignment and low-latency simultaneous interpretation that standard cluster configurations cannot sustain.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be professional interpreters and/or translators of documents and data files, either from English or (Canadian) French into another language or languages or vice versa. Includes intensive instruction in one or more foreign languages plus instruction in subjects such as single- and multiple-language interpretation, one- or two-way interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, general and literary translation, business translation, technical translation, and other specific applications of linguistic skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of optimizing neural network architectures for real-time, resource-constrained edge computing systems. As embedded and IoT devices increasingly rely on machine learning for applications such as autonomous navigation and industrial automation, the need for energy-efficient, low-latency inference models has become critical. However, designing architectures that balance accuracy, computational complexity, and hardware compatibility requires iterative exploration of hyperparameters, layer configurations, and quantization strategies at scales impractical for local computing resources. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to systematically evaluate thousands of neural network variants through parallelized training and inference simulations. Using a hybrid approach combining evolutionary algorithms, Monte Carlo sampling, and gradient-based optimization, the project will map the Pareto frontier of performance trade-offs across heterogeneous hardware profiles (e.g., FPGA, ASIC, and low-power GPUs). Computational workflows will employ distributed TensorFlow and PyTorch frameworks with CUDA acceleration to manage large-scale hyperparameter sweeps, while custom benchmarking tools will profile memory usage, power consumption, and thermal characteristics via hardware-in-the-loop emulation. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source framework for generating hardware-aware neural architectures, (2) optimized model templates for common edge computing use cases, and (3) quantitative guidelines for balancing model compression techniques with accuracy retention. The computational scale required—involving simultaneous training of >500 models with up to 100M parameters each—necessitates access to GPU clusters with high-speed interconnects and multi-node scaling capabilities. Results will advance the development of deployable AI systems in critical domains such as precision agriculture, smart manufacturing, and robotics, while contributing methodological innovations to the field of automated neural architecture search.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into existing power grids presents complex challenges due to the intermittent nature of wind and solar generation, which can destabilize grid reliability and efficiency. This project addresses the critical need for advanced computational tools to optimize hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) that combine hydrogen electrolysis, fuel cells, and battery technologies. Current models for HESS coordination lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between electrochemical, thermal, and grid-scale phenomena, particularly under rapid load fluctuations. To overcome this gap, we propose developing a multi-physics, multi-timescale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational approach integrates quantum-informed molecular dynamics to model catalyst degradation in electrolyzers, finite element analysis for thermal management in fuel cell stacks, and reinforcement learning algorithms for real-time grid dispatch optimization. These components will be coupled through a modular architecture enabling bidirectional data exchange across scales, with validation against experimental datasets from pilot-scale HESS installations. The HPC environment is essential to manage the computational burden of simulating 10^6+ degree-of-freedom systems over operational timelines spanning milliseconds to seasonal cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive models for component lifespan under variable loading, optimized control policies for hydrogen-battery hybridization, and open-source software tools for grid operators. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation storage systems capable of supporting 80%+ renewable penetration targets while reducing levelized storage costs by an estimated 30%. By bridging molecular-scale material behavior with grid-scale dynamics, the project advances foundational methodologies for cross-scale energy systems engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of energy generation, storage, conversion, and distribution systems. Includes instruction in conventional and alternative/renewable energy systems, electrical power systems, and electrical system design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop novel computational methods to analyze the existence and regularity of solutions to nonlocal elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs) with fractional diffusion operators in high-dimensional settings. Such equations arise in modeling anomalous transport phenomena and interface dynamics in heterogeneous media, but their rigorous mathematical treatment remains limited due to the complexity of nonlocal operators and the curse of dimensionality. Current analytical approaches struggle to characterize solution smoothness or stability when spatial dimensions exceed three, while numerical methods face prohibitive computational costs. To address this, we propose a hybrid analytical-computational framework combining theoretical analysis with large-scale numerical experiments. The core computational component will implement parallelized spectral-Galerkin discretizations using hierarchical basis functions adapted to fractional operator eigenstructures, coupled with tensor network decompositions to mitigate dimensionality challenges. High-performance computing resources will enable systematic parameter studies across dimensions 4–10, probing scaling relationships between fractional order, domain geometry, and solution regularity. Validation will occur via comparison to exact solutions in symmetric domains and convergence analysis against mesh refinements. Expected outcomes include (1) new conjectures on the dimensional dependence of Hölder regularity bounds for nonlocal PDEs, (2) optimized algorithms for high-dimensional fractional operators, and (3) open-source spectral solvers compatible with distributed-memory architectures. Results will advance foundational knowledge in PDE theory while providing computational tools for subsequent studies of nonlinear nonlocal systems. The project requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for matrix exponential computations and large-scale linear algebra, alongside high-memory nodes for storing multidimensional basis function coefficients. This work bridges abstract analysis and practical computation, leveraging HPC to explore regimes inaccessible to purely theoretical methods.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of theoretical and applied mathematics to the solution of functional problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, numerical statistics, optimization, operational research, signal analysis, wavelets, image processing, fuzzy sets, spline, stochastic analysis, integral equations, differential equations, and partial differential equations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven pedagogical frameworks for K-12 teacher education. A critical challenge in modern teacher preparation is designing instruction that equitably addresses the diverse cognitive, cultural, and linguistic needs of students while integrating emerging technologies. Current approaches often rely on static models of classroom interaction, which fail to account for the dynamic, multivariate nature of learning environments. To address this gap, we propose building a computational platform that simulates classroom ecosystems through agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML). The ABM component will parameterize student agents using empirical data on learning behaviors, developmental stages, and sociocultural contexts, while ML algorithms will analyze real-world classroom interaction datasets to identify patterns in teacher responsiveness and student engagement. HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations to thousands of virtual classrooms, enabling the exploration of "what-if" scenarios across demographic variables, instructional strategies, and technology integration models. The computational outputs will inform the design of a teacher training module focused on adaptive decision-making, with an emphasis on culturally sustaining practices and AI-augmented teaching tools. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated classroom interaction data, (2) evidence-based guidelines for embedding computational thinking into teacher education curricula, and (3) predictive models linking specific teaching strategies to equity-oriented learning outcomes. By bridging computational analytics with pedagogical theory, this work aims to equip educators with dynamic, scalable tools to navigate the complexities of 21st-century classrooms, ultimately contributing to more personalized and inclusive educational experiences.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education that prepares individuals to be effective educators or trainers. Includes instruction in school reform and design; arts and technology in the classroom; theories of teaching and learning; adult and adolescent development; race, class, and gender dynamics; and the history and future of education in America.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance vocational rehabilitation counseling research by modeling complex, multidimensional factors influencing employment outcomes for individuals with disabilities. Current vocational rehabilitation practices rely on static, population-level data to guide client-counselor decision-making, which often fails to account for dynamic interactions between personal, environmental, and systemic variables such as fluctuating health conditions, workplace accommodations, labor market trends, and policy changes. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate individualized vocational pathways using heterogeneous datasets, including longitudinal client health records, employer requirements, regional economic indicators, and psychosocial assessments. These simulations will integrate machine learning algorithms to identify critical intervention points and predict long-term employment success under varying scenarios. Computational demands are significant due to the need for parallel processing of high-dimensional data (e.g., 10,000+ simulated agents with 50+ dynamic attributes each) and iterative optimization of model parameters. The HPC environment will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses to evaluate how systemic factors like healthcare access, employer incentives, and counselor caseloads interact with individual characteristics such as disability type, skill development trajectories, and social support networks. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework to inform personalized rehabilitation planning, a policy-testing toolkit for stakeholders, and open-source computational workflows tailored for rehabilitation research. By quantifying nonlinear relationships in vocational recovery processes, this work aims to improve evidence-based practices for counselors while advancing methodological innovation in rehabilitation science through computationally intensive, systems-level modeling approaches.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel and assist disabled individuals and recovering patients in order to achieve their greatest physical, mental, social, educational, and vocational potential. Includes instruction in patient evaluation and testing, rehabilitation program planning, patient support services and referral, job analysis, adjustment psychology, rehabilitation services provision, patient counseling and education, applicable law and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Tamil linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in the digital study of Classical and Modern Tamil. Despite Tamil’s rich literary history and status as a classical language, computational tools tailored to its unique morphosyntactic structures, dialectal variations, and historical texts remain underdeveloped. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, interoperable frameworks for analyzing Tamil’s linguistic evolution, stylistic patterns in literature, and dialectal diversity—challenges compounded by the computational complexity of processing agglutinative morphology and non-Latin scripts. To address this, the project will deploy parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Tamil, including neural models for dialect classification, rule-based morphological analyzers for Classical Tamil, and transformer-based architectures for cross-era stylistic comparison. These methods will process digitized corpora spanning 2,000 years of Tamil texts, including inscriptions, Sangam poetry, and modern media, alongside spoken dialect recordings. Computational workflows will be designed to quantify linguistic shifts, map dialect boundaries, and identify literary motifs, with validation against philological scholarship. The HPC environment is essential for training large language models on low-resource Tamil datasets, running exhaustive parameter searches for optimal dialect clustering, and handling high-dimensional textual data. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for Tamil NLP, annotated multilingual corpora, and interactive visualizations of linguistic and literary trends. This work will enable novel interdisciplinary inquiries into Tamil’s historical development, support preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and provide frameworks for applying computational methods to other under-resourced Dravidian languages. By integrating advanced computing with traditional Tamil scholarship, the project aims to bridge methodological gaps in humanities research while fostering digital literacy in Tamil studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Tamil language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Classical and Modern Tamil; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing pollution control systems in urban-industrial environments. A critical challenge in environmental engineering technology lies in efficiently mitigating airborne particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, which exhibit complex dispersion dynamics influenced by meteorological variables, topography, and heterogeneous emission sources. Current models often lack the spatiotemporal resolution and computational scalability to inform real-time control strategies for industrial scrubbers, filtration systems, and sensor-based monitoring networks. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating large-eddy simulation (LES) for microscale atmospheric transport, machine learning (ML) emulators trained on sensor-derived pollution datasets, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. The LES component will resolve turbulence and plume interactions at sub-meter scales across domains exceeding 10 km², while ML models will assimilate real-time sensor data to dynamically adjust emission control parameters. HPC resources are essential to parallelize LES computations across thousands of cores, manage petabyte-scale datasets from IoT-enabled pollution sensors, and iteratively optimize system responses through genetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated digital twin platform for simulating pollution scenarios under variable climate conditions, (2) adaptive control protocols for reducing energy consumption in industrial filtration systems by 15–20%, and (3) open-source tools for environmental technicians to deploy localized mitigation strategies. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on applied engineering solutions by bridging computational fluid dynamics with practical pollution control technologies, while providing students with training in scalable environmental data science workflows. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling urban pollution hotspots, directly supporting regulatory compliance and community health objectives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using indoor and outdoor environmental pollution control systems. Includes instruction in environmental safety principles, testing and sampling procedures, laboratory techniques, instrumentation calibration, safety and protection procedures, equipment maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive maintenance and energy efficiency optimization in residential and commercial appliances, including refrigeration systems, laundry units, and cooking appliances. A critical challenge in appliance repair and installation is the lack of data-driven frameworks to anticipate mechanical failures or energy inefficiencies in aging or complex systems. Traditional diagnostics rely on static guidelines or reactive troubleshooting, which can lead to increased downtime, resource waste, and consumer costs. To address this gap, we propose developing physics-informed machine learning models that simulate appliance performance under diverse operational conditions, material stresses, and environmental factors. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling in components like compressor valves or heating elements, coupled with time-series forecasting to predict wear patterns. High-resolution sensor data from field deployments (e.g., temperature, vibration, power draw) will train neural networks to correlate real-world usage patterns with failure risks. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across thousands of appliance configurations and rapidly iterate multi-physics models that account for thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamics interactions. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance toolkit that enables technicians to prioritize repairs, reduce energy waste by up to 20% in malfunctioning units, and extend appliance lifespans. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular simulation templates tailored to common appliance architectures, fostering innovation in technician training programs and sustainable appliance design. By bridging computational modeling with applied repair technologies, this work aims to elevate technical standards in the field while supporting global energy conservation goals.
cip_title: Appliance Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, install, and service major gas, electric, and microwave consumer appliances such as stoves, refrigerators, dryers, water heaters, washers, dishwashers, and commercial units such as ice makers and coffee makers.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the acoustic and biomechanical interactions between brass instrumentalists and their instruments through high-fidelity computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address limitations in real-time physical simulations. While brass performance pedagogy emphasizes empirical approaches to embouchure control, airflow dynamics, and resonant feedback, the nonlinear coupling of lip vibration, bore acoustics, and player physiology remains poorly quantified. Current experimental methods struggle to isolate variables or resolve sub-millisecond interactions, hindering the development of predictive models for advanced performance techniques. The proposed research will implement finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model time-dependent pressure waves in trumpet and horn bores under physiologically realistic lip kinematics derived from motion-capture data. Machine learning workflows will optimize parameter spaces linking mouthpiece geometry, material properties, and player-controlled variables to spectral output. HPC resources are critical for executing coupled multiphysics simulations at 1 µs temporal resolution across 10+ octave harmonic series configurations, a computational load exceeding real-time capabilities by six orders of magnitude. Expected outcomes include the first open-source framework for simulating player-instrument co-adaptation effects, validated against laser vibrometry and high-speed Schlieren imaging data. Results will advance fundamental understanding of transient regimes in brass acoustics while providing pedagogical tools to diagnose performance bottlenecks. The resource allocation will directly support 12-18 months of large-scale parametric studies, with generated datasets informing both musical instrument design and computational arts research at the intersection of embodied cognition and physical sound synthesis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a brass instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized athletic training regimens through the integration of biomechanical modeling, physiological data analytics, and machine learning. Current training programs often rely on generalized protocols that fail to account for individual variability in biomechanics, metabolic responses, and recovery dynamics, leading to suboptimal performance gains and heightened injury risks. To address this gap, the research proposes a computational framework that synthesizes motion capture data, wearable sensor outputs, and physiological biomarkers to model athlete-specific adaptations in real time. The core computational challenge involves simulating high-dimensional interactions between musculoskeletal dynamics, tissue stress responses, and metabolic load distributions across diverse athlete profiles. Agent-based modeling will be employed to replicate population-level training outcomes, while deep reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize individualized exercise prescriptions by iteratively balancing performance targets with injury risk thresholds. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations, enabling parallel processing of heterogeneous datasets and reducing latency in model training and validation. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive toolset for coaches and sports scientists to design dynamically adaptive training programs, alongside open-source computational workflows that bridge gaps between sports science and data-driven decision-making. By quantifying previously intractable relationships between training variables and athlete outcomes, this work aims to establish a foundational platform for precision sports science, with potential applications in rehabilitation, talent development, and injury prevention across amateur and elite athletic populations.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on activities and principles that promote physical fitness, achieve and maintain athletic prowess, and accomplish related research and service goals. Includes instruction in human movement studies, motivation studies, rules and practice of specific sports, exercise and fitness principles and techniques, basic athletic injury prevention and treatment, and organizing and leading fitness and sports programs.

abstract: This project investigates the mechanosensory mechanisms underlying plant responses to acoustic vibrations, an underexplored area at the intersection of botany, biophysics, and computational engineering. While prior studies suggest that specific sound frequencies influence seed germination and root growth, the biophysical principles governing these morphogenetic responses remain poorly characterized. Our research aims to model how vibrational energy propagates through plant tissues and triggers cellular signaling cascades, bypassing traditional molecular signaling pathways. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will simulate wave interactions across multiscale plant architectures, integrating finite element analysis of tissue mechanics with machine learning-driven pattern recognition in time-resolved growth imaging datasets. The computational framework will parameterize species-specific traits, including cellulose microfibril orientation and organ geometry, to predict resonance behaviors and strain-activated ion channel dynamics. Experimental validation will employ laser Doppler vibrometry and microelectrode arrays in model species (Arabidopsis thaliana, Zea mays). By resolving how plants transduce acoustic energy into biomechanical signals, this work will establish predictive models for optimizing acoustic treatments to enhance stress resilience in crops. The requested resources will enable large-scale simulations of vibration-tissue interactions across 3D mesophyll networks and probabilistic analyses of emergent growth patterns under variable acoustic regimes. Outcomes will advance fundamental knowledge of non-canonical sensory modalities in plants while providing a computational toolkit for developing sustainable agricultural technologies based on targeted mechanostimulation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in botany/plant biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Sleep disorders, affecting millions globally, present complex diagnostic challenges due to the multidimensional nature of polysomnographic (PSG) data, which includes electroencephalography, electromyography, respiratory signals, and oximetry. Traditional analysis methods rely on manual scoring and linear statistical approaches, limiting the ability to detect subtle, nonlinear patterns predictive of disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy, or insomnia. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a scalable computational framework to automate and enhance PSG analysis through machine learning (ML) and high-dimensional signal processing. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on a retrospective dataset of 10,000+ de-identified PSG studies, integrating time-series biosignals with clinical metadata. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of multi-channel signals at scale, optimizing hyperparameters for temporal convolutional networks, and implementing federated learning protocols to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. The project will validate models against expert-annotated hypnograms and clinical outcomes, assessing accuracy in sleep stage classification, event detection (e.g., apneas, limb movements), and disorder prediction. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for automated PSG scoring, reducing inter-rater variability and clinician workload. Additionally, the discovery of novel electrophysiological biomarkers could advance personalized interventions. HPC resources are critical to manage the dataset’s size (>50 TB), enable rapid iteration of complex models, and support real-time inference simulations for eventual clinical integration.
