This work aligns with national priorities to improve sleep health infrastructure and demonstrates how computational innovation can transform diagnostic paradigms in allied health professions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing secure, scalable software systems in distributed computing environments, where traditional development and testing frameworks struggle to balance performance, security, and adaptability. The research focuses on developing a novel computational framework to automate vulnerability detection in large-scale software applications while simulating real-world stress conditions. Current methods for dynamic code analysis and penetration testing lack the efficiency to handle modern, heterogeneous systems with real-time data streams, leading to gaps in identifying zero-day exploits or performance bottlenecks. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid approach combining machine learning-driven static analysis with parallelized, high-fidelity simulations of networked environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train deep learning models on curated datasets of vulnerable code patterns, optimize encryption protocols through combinatorial testing, and emulate multi-node deployments under variable loads. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated anomaly detection algorithms and containerized microservice orchestration to model attack surfaces across diverse architectures. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated security auditing, performance profiling, and resilience testing in cloud-native systems. This work will advance software engineering practices by enabling proactive identification of vulnerabilities and scalability limits, reducing post-deployment risks. The requested HPC allocation will support large-scale parallelism for codebase analysis, cryptographic brute-force simulations, and distributed load testing, which are infeasible on local clusters. By integrating computational efficiency with robust security testing, this project aims to bridge critical gaps in software reliability for data-intensive applications in healthcare, finance, and IoT domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in developing, implementing, and evaluating computer software and program applications. Includes instruction in computer programming, programming languages, databases, user interfaces, networking and warehousing, encryption and security, software testing and evaluation, and customization.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the ethical and educational implications of artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated clinical communication training in health professions education. While AI-driven simulations are increasingly used to train healthcare providers in technical skills, their role in developing nuanced, ethically informed communication competencies—such as navigating cultural sensitivities, delivering adverse diagnoses, or addressing patient mistrust—remains underexplored. The research problem centers on the gap in scalable, evidence-based tools to evaluate how AI-generated patient interactions influence trainees’ ethical reasoning and communication strategies. To address this, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform that integrates large-language models (LLMs), multimodal sentiment analysis, and reinforcement learning to simulate dynamic, culturally diverse patient scenarios. The computational workflow will involve training ethically calibrated LLMs on anonymized clinical dialogue datasets and synthetic edge cases representing complex moral dilemmas. Agent-based modeling will simulate longitudinal interactions between trainee cohorts and AI patients, tracking decision-making patterns and communication outcomes under varying ethical constraints. Parallelized sentiment and semantic analysis pipelines will process speech, text, and behavioral data from simulations to quantify alignment with evidence-based communication frameworks. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the real-time generation of context-aware patient responses, running thousands of parallel simulation instances, and training deep reinforcement learning models to adapt scenarios based on trainee performance metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of ethically annotated simulation datasets, a validated computational framework for assessing communication competency development, and evidence-based guidelines for integrating AI tools into ethics-focused health professions curricula. This work will advance interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of clinical education, computational ethics, and AI systems design, offering scalable solutions to cultivate humanistic care in technologically mediated healthcare environments.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling and optimization of industrial-scale chemical production processes, with a focus on enhancing energy efficiency and reducing environmental impacts. Current challenges in Chemical Engineering Technology include the computational limitations of simulating multiphase reactor dynamics, heterogeneous catalysis, and real-time process control under variable industrial conditions. These limitations hinder the development of scalable, sustainable chemical manufacturing systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for reactor-scale flow and heat transfer analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate catalyst-surface interactions, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to optimize process parameters. The CFD models will resolve turbulent fluid behavior and species transport in large-scale reactors, while MD simulations will probe atomic-scale mechanisms of catalytic activity and degradation. ML frameworks will integrate these datasets to predict optimal operating conditions, such as temperature gradients and feedstock ratios, balancing production efficiency with emissions control. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high dimensionality of these simulations, particularly the parallel processing demands of coupled CFD-MD workflows and the training of deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include validated models for industrial reactor design, actionable insights into catalyst longevity, and adaptive control strategies for minimizing energy consumption in continuous chemical processes. This work aligns with the Chemical Engineering Technology program’s emphasis on applied industrial problem-solving, offering transferable computational tools for educators and industry partners. Successful implementation will directly support curriculum development in process simulation and provide a foundation for collaborative research on sustainable chemical manufacturing, addressing pressing needs in environmental compliance and operational cost reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing strategies in hybrid auction environments, where real-time, multi-platform bidding intersects with specialized commodity markets (e.g., industrial equipment, rare collectibles). The core research problem lies in addressing the inefficiencies of current auctioneering models, which struggle to adapt pricing mechanisms to volatile bidder behavior, cross-platform competition, and heterogeneous asset valuations at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach to simulate hyperrealistic auction ecosystems, incorporating stochastic bidder networks, temporal valuation shifts, and regulatory constraints derived from sales law parameters. The computational model will process terascale datasets of historical auction transcripts, bid timing patterns, and post-auction market outcomes to train adaptive agents capable of predicting optimal bid-calling sequences, reserve price adjustments, and anti-collusion safeguards. By parallelizing agent interactions across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to evaluate millions of auction scenario permutations, identifying robust strategies that maximize auction house revenue while preserving bidder participation incentives. Expected outcomes include an open-source auction simulation toolkit validated against real-world data from automotive and agricultural equipment auctions, as well as predictive metrics for platform-specific revenue leakage risks. This work bridges computational economics and auctioneering practice, offering empirically grounded solutions for emerging challenges in decentralized digital auctions and high-stakes specialty markets. The HPC infrastructure is critical for maintaining temporal fidelity in agent training cycles and scaling scenario testing across diverse regulatory jurisdictions, directly addressing the computational intensity of modeling asynchronous, multi-lot auction events.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional careers as auctioneers and auction managers, and for meeting applicable state licensing requirements. Includes instruction in bid calling, public speaking, ringworking, auction techniques, salesmanship skills, auction clerking and cashiering, auction advertising, working independently or with auction houses, contracts and agency, applicable sales law, and managing both general auctions and auctions specializing in commodities such as antiques, consignments, farm equipment, industrial equipment, real estate, livestock, and automobiles.

abstract: Diabetes mellitus represents a complex, multifactorial disorder with profound global health impacts, yet the mechanisms underlying its heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Current therapeutic strategies often fail to account for individual variability in disease progression, treatment response, and complication risk, highlighting the need for integrative approaches to unravel its pathophysiological complexity. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal clinical, genomic, and metabolomic datasets from a longitudinal cohort of 15,000 patients with type 2 diabetes. The research will develop machine learning models to identify subtype-specific biomarkers and predict individualized risks of microvascular complications. Computational challenges include integrating high-dimensional datasets (whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal HbA1c measurements, and serum metabolomics) while addressing missing data and temporal dependencies. A hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for biological network integration and transformer-based architectures for temporal pattern recognition will be implemented. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate candidate protein-metabolite interactions implicated in subtype-specific pathways. The scale of data processing (~2 PB) and the iterative nature of deep learning model training necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized workflows, GPU-accelerated computations, and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a clinically actionable stratification framework for diabetes subtyping, (2) predictive models for complication risks with validated accuracy (>85% AUC), and (3) mechanistic insights into dysregulated pathways amenable to therapeutic targeting. By bridging large-scale data science with clinical translation, this work aims to advance precision medicine paradigms in diabetes care, potentially reducing trial-and-error treatment approaches and complication-related healthcare burdens. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the project’s resolution of complex interactions across biological scales within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on Diabetes

abstract: The safe and efficient management of blood products is critical in transfusion medicine, yet challenges persist in predicting component degradation, optimizing storage conditions, and minimizing alloimmunization risks. Current methodologies rely on static guidelines and retrospective analyses, which lack the granularity to address dynamic biological variability and complex donor-recipient interactions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that enhance blood component quality assessment and transfusion outcomes. Using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations, we will investigate the biophysical changes in red blood cell membranes and platelet activation pathways under varying storage conditions. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will be applied to multi-omic datasets (genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) from donors and recipients to identify biomarkers associated with adverse transfusion reactions and alloimmunization events. These computational approaches will integrate real-time sensor data from blood storage units to dynamically adjust preservation protocols. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of high-resolution temporal data, running parallelized simulations across thousands of storage scenarios, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous biomedical datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for component shelf-life extension, personalized transfusion protocols based on recipient immunoprofiles, and optimized storage conditions that reduce waste by 20–30%. By translating computational insights into clinical workflows, this research aims to strengthen blood supply resilience, improve patient safety, and advance evidence-based practices in transfusion medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for the maintenance of an adequate blood supply, blood donor and patient-recipient safety, and appropriate blood utilization. Includes directing the preparation and safe use of specially prepared blood components, including red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma constituents, and marrow or stem cells for transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational approach to analyzing the evolution of legal language in non-binding advisory texts, such as model statutes, public legal guides, and community-generated policy frameworks. While legal informatics often focuses on binding precedents or statutory law, non-professional legal materials—critical for public legal literacy, advocacy, and grassroots policy design—remain understudied. The research addresses a gap in understanding how these materials adapt to shifting societal values, particularly in decentralized contexts where formal legal training is absent. Using a corpus of 15 million words spanning community-led legal education documents, NGO toolkits, and collaborative policy drafts from 2000–2023, the project employs transformer-based NLP models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned for legal semantics) to map semantic shifts, conceptual fragmentation, and cross-jurisdictional borrowing patterns. Computational challenges include processing heterogeneous, multilingual texts with irregular structure and inferring latent normative frameworks through attention mechanism analysis. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing large-scale embedding generation, training domain-specific language models, and running iterative simulations of legal concept diffusion across networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible toolkit for quantifying alignment between non-professional legal advice and formal legal systems, (2) evidence-based strategies to improve participatory policy design, and (3) novel metrics for assessing the "accessibility drift" of legal guidance materials over time. By bridging computational linguistics and non-hierarchical legal theory, this work aims to empower communities in co-creating legally coherent yet accessible governance frameworks, with implications for legal education technology and civic tech platforms.
cip_definition: Any program in non-professional legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenges of analyzing large-scale multimedia news datasets in broadcast journalism, where the volume, velocity, and complexity of audiovisual content demand advanced computational tools. Traditional methods for evaluating news accuracy, bias, and audience engagement struggle to keep pace with real-time data streams, multi-platform distribution, and emerging formats like immersive 360-degree video. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable framework for automated content analysis, ethical auditing, and production optimization. The research will employ machine learning models trained on diverse broadcast datasets—including news clips, live streams, and social media feeds—to identify patterns in editorial decision-making, detect synthetic or manipulated media, and model audience response across demographics. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing for transcript analysis, computer vision for frame-by-frame metadata extraction, and network analysis to trace information diffusion. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce processing times for terabyte-scale archives from weeks to hours, enabling unprecedented longitudinal studies of broadcast trends. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for newsrooms to audit algorithmic bias in automated captioning systems, simulate the impact of ethical editing choices on audience trust, and optimize resource allocation during breaking news events. This work will advance scholarly understanding of computational journalism while providing practical resources for educators training students in data-driven storytelling and media ethics. The proposed HPC infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive video processing and ensuring reproducibility in multi-modal experiments, ultimately supporting broadcast journalism’s evolving role in evidence-based public discourse.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for reporting, producing, and delivering news and news programs via radio, television, and video/film media; and that prepares individuals to be professional broadcast journalists, editors, producers, directors, and managers. Includes instruction in the principles of broadcast technology; broadcast reporting; on- and off-camera and microphone procedures and techniques; program, sound, and video/film editing; program design and production; media law and policy; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize safety and efficiency in mobile crane operations through advanced dynamic load modeling and real-time simulation. Mobile crane operations involve complex interactions between machinery, environmental conditions, and load dynamics, yet existing predictive models often lack the resolution to account for multi-variable stressors such as wind shear, ground stability, and sudden load shifts. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating high-fidelity simulations that integrate structural mechanics, fluid dynamics, and operator decision-making patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large-scale datasets from crane sensors, lidar-scanned worksites, and historical incident reports while running parallelized simulations of load trajectories under diverse operational scenarios. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) to model crane structural responses, machine learning algorithms trained on operator behavior data, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risk probabilities. The project will also develop a digital twin platform to test emergency protocols virtually, reducing reliance on physical prototypes. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to alert operators of instability risks, optimized load capacity charts adaptive to real-time environmental variables, and data-driven recommendations for updates to crane operation standards (e.g., ANSI/ASME B30.5). By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to reduce equipment failure rates and workplace accidents while improving training protocols for crane operators. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and partnerships with crane certification bodies, offering transformative benefits to construction, logistics, and heavy manufacturing industries reliant on mobile crane operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to hoist and swing loads via complex rotating machinery that is driver operated. Includes instruction in crane operational characteristics, load and capacity chart usage, emergency control skills, safety, specific types of mobile cranes and loading devices, applicable codes and standards, and applications to particular types of jobs and loads.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced computational framework for optimizing franchise network performance in dynamic market environments. Franchise systems face unique challenges due to their decentralized structure, geographic dispersion, and interdependencies between franchisors and franchisees. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between operational variables (e.g., supply chain logistics, local consumer behavior, and brand consistency) and external factors (e.g., regional economic shifts or competitive landscapes). The proposed study addresses this gap by creating a multi-agent simulation model that integrates real-world transactional data, demographic trends, and macroeconomic indicators to predict system-wide outcomes under varying operational strategies. The computational approach combines graph theory to map franchise network topology, reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive decision-making by franchisees, and Monte Carlo methods to quantify risk exposure across different scenarios. By employing HPC capabilities, the project will process terabytes of heterogeneous data from franchise management platforms, social media sentiment analyses, and public economic databases, enabling near-real-time scenario testing at unprecedented scale. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics toolkit capable of identifying optimal resource allocation strategies for franchise expansion, crisis response protocols for economic disruptions, and dynamic pricing models sensitive to local market conditions. This work will contribute novel methodologies to the understudied computational dimension of franchise operations, offering practical tools for enhancing the resilience of franchise systems while advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of business analytics, complex systems theory, and distributed decision-making architectures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and operate franchises. Includes instruction in legal requirements, set-up costs and capitalization requirements, financing, and applications to specific franchise opportunities.

abstract: Pulmonary diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with complex pathophysiological mechanisms that span molecular, cellular, and organ-level interactions. Traditional experimental approaches often struggle to capture these multiscale dynamics, necessitating advanced computational methods to integrate heterogeneous data and model disease progression. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models of pulmonary physiology and pathology, focusing on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), and pulmonary malignancies. The research will employ patient-derived clinical imaging, genomic data, and physiological measurements to construct spatially resolved models of lung tissue remodeling, airflow dynamics, and tumor microenvironment interactions. Large-scale simulations will quantify the impact of genetic variants, cellular signaling pathways, and biomechanical forces on disease trajectories. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to multi-omic datasets to identify predictive biomarkers and optimize therapeutic targeting. The computational workflows require parallelized processing of high-resolution medical images (≥10 TB datasets), stochastic modeling of molecular networks, and real-time coupling of fluid dynamics with tissue deformation simulations—tasks feasible only with HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting treatment responses in COPD, mechanistic insights into IPF progression, and in silico screening of anticancer drug combinations for pulmonary tumors. By integrating clinical data with computational biology, this work aims to accelerate the translation of mechanistic discoveries into personalized therapeutic strategies, ultimately improving prognostic accuracy and patient outcomes in pulmonary medicine. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling lung pathophysiology, fostering innovation at the intersection of clinical research and computational science.
cip_definition: Research focused on pulmonary physiology and the treatment of lung diseases, pulmonary malignancies, related vascular diseases, respiratory disorders, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, and pulmonary pathology.

abstract: The development of advanced polymers with tailored functionalities requires a detailed understanding of molecular-scale interactions, yet predicting the behavior of complex polymer systems remains a significant challenge. Experimental approaches alone struggle to resolve dynamic processes such as polymerization kinetics, phase transitions, or the effects of monomer sequence on bulk properties. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale polymer systems, enabling the rational design of materials for applications such as biodegradable plastics, responsive hydrogels, and conductive polymers. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) modeling polymerization mechanisms and kinetics for novel monomer systems using quantum mechanical (QM) and molecular dynamics (MD) methods, and (2) predicting the thermomechanical and interfacial properties of resulting polymers through coarse-grained and all-atom simulations. Key computational challenges include simulating long-timescale polymerization reactions, capturing entropy-driven phase transitions in block copolymers, and analyzing solvent-polymer interactions under varied thermodynamic conditions. The simulations will employ software packages such as LAMMPS and GROMACS, augmented by custom scripts to analyze bond formation dynamics and network percolation thresholds. Access to HPC resources is critical due to the need for large-scale parallelization, extended simulation timescales (microseconds to milliseconds), and high-resolution sampling of free energy landscapes. Expected outcomes include identifying monomer sequences that optimize mechanical resilience in thermoplastic elastomers, elucidating design rules for redox-active polymers in energy storage devices, and establishing computational workflows to accelerate polymer discovery. This work will provide foundational insights into structure-property relationships while reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, directly supporting sustainable polymer innovation in alignment with industrial and environmental priorities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: Maintaining the reliability and efficiency of modern energy systems demands advanced predictive and diagnostic capabilities, yet current maintenance practices often rely on reactive or schedule-based approaches that result in unnecessary downtime, resource waste, and safety risks. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize maintenance and repair protocols for heterogeneous energy infrastructure, including wind turbines, photovoltaic arrays, and grid-scale battery systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate multi-physics simulations (e.g., thermal, mechanical, and electrochemical degradation models) with machine learning algorithms trained on historical failure datasets and real-time sensor inputs. Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent material stresses across varying operational conditions, automating anomaly detection in terabyte-scale sensor datasets, and optimizing repair schedules via combinatorial optimization algorithms. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulation of degradation pathways at component and system levels, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively refine maintenance strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive fault classification models with quantified uncertainty bounds, physics-informed digital twins for critical infrastructure, and adaptive decision-support tools for prioritizing repairs under resource constraints. By transitioning maintenance paradigms from heuristic to data-driven approaches, this work aims to reduce operational costs by an estimated 15–20% in modeled systems while extending asset lifespans. The resulting computational toolkit will be disseminated as open-source modules to support workforce training programs in energy systems technology, directly aligning with the program’s mission to advance technical proficiency in next-generation maintenance practices. This project’s integration of HPC-driven analytics with applied energy systems repair represents a novel cross-disciplinary contribution to sustainable infrastructure management.
cip_title: Energy Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the efficacy of school-based counseling interventions in fostering social-emotional learning (SEL) outcomes among K-12 students. Current research lacks scalable methods to model the dynamic interplay between intervention strategies, individual differences, and contextual factors in diverse educational environments. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models that simulate student interactions, counselor decision-making processes, and SEL progression over time. These models will integrate longitudinal datasets encompassing student behavioral records, demographic variables, and intervention fidelity metrics from multiple school districts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps, calibrate models using Bayesian optimization techniques, and conduct Monte Carlo simulations assessing intervention robustness across heterogeneous populations. Machine learning pipelines will further analyze simulated and empirical data to identify critical intervention components and moderators of effectiveness. The anticipated outcomes include a validated computational framework for predicting intervention impacts under varying school conditions and evidence-based guidelines for personalizing counseling approaches. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will provide novel insights into how multi-level factors interact to shape SEL development, directly informing the design of equitable, data-driven counseling practices in educational psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution and cross-jurisdictional influence of medieval religious legal systems, with a focus on understudied canonical traditions outside the Roman Catholic mainstream. While canonical studies traditionally emphasize textual analysis of ecclesiastical decrees, this project addresses a gap in computational approaches to modeling how non-Roman canon laws—such as those of the Armenian Apostolic Church, Coptic Orthodox Church, and Syriac Christian communities—developed networked relationships with secular legal systems and neighboring religious traditions. The core challenge lies in processing fragmentary, multilingual primary sources (Syriac, Armenian, Ge‘ez, and Arabic) spanning the 6th–14th centuries, which require advanced optical character recognition (OCR) correction, semantic tagging, and spatial-temporal alignment. The computational methodology combines natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource historical languages with graph neural networks to reconstruct legal influence networks. Key tasks include training custom transformer models on canonical corpora to detect intertextual legal citations, developing a geospatial database of legal dissemination nodes, and simulating the diffusion of norms through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include 1) the first quantitative map of cross-cultural legal borrowing between Eastern Christian canon laws and Islamic fiqh systems in medieval Anatolia and Mesopotamia, 2) a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking canonical provisions to socio-political contexts of enforcement, and 3) novel metrics for measuring the "resilience" of religious legal principles under shifting political regimes. By integrating computational historiography with canon law studies, this work aims to establish a framework for analyzing legal pluralism in premodern religious societies while advancing digital humanities methodologies for non-Latin script historical texts. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized OCR of 50,000+ manuscript images, alignment of heterogeneous temporal taxonomies, and graph computations across ~1 billion potential node relationships—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime for iterative model training and large-scale network analysis.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, theology, and philosophy of religious, church, and ecclesiastical law and that prepares individuals to serve as professional canonists.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and control of active matter systems, a rapidly emerging interdisciplinary field at the intersection of statistical physics, soft matter engineering, and autonomous systems. Active matter—composed of self-propelled units such as synthetic colloidal particles or biohybrid microswimmers—exhibits collective behaviors with transformative potential for applications in targeted material transport, adaptive infrastructure, and microrobotics. However, engineering these systems requires overcoming significant challenges in predicting and directing their nonequilibrium dynamics across scales. Current models struggle to bridge microscale interactions and macroscale functionality, particularly in complex, heterogeneous environments. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning-augmented hydrodynamic simulations, and topology optimization. Large-scale parallelized simulations will resolve particle-scale interactions in experimentally relevant systems (10^5–10^6 agents) while neural operators accelerate the exploration of parameter spaces governing emergent patterns. The computational pipeline will integrate open-source molecular dynamics tools with custom optimization libraries to identify optimal external field configurations and particle designs for desired transport or assembly outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform for active matter engineering, generalized design principles for controlling collective behaviors under noise, and predictive models for system response to dynamic stimuli. This work will provide foundational insights for engineering autonomous matter-based systems beyond conventional robotics paradigms, with potential applications in environmental remediation, precision agriculture, and smart material logistics. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary spatiotemporal resolution and statistical sampling to advance this nascent engineering discipline.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission or transfer to a baccalaureate-level program in any of the fields of engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to enhance real-time analysis of multi-source intelligence data in military strategic decision-making. Modern military intelligence operations face challenges in rapidly integrating heterogeneous data streams—including signals intelligence (SIGINT), human intelligence (HUMINT), and geospatial intelligence (GEOINT)—into actionable insights. Existing tools often struggle with latency, data volume, and the complexity of correlating disparate formats, leading to delayed or incomplete situational assessments. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a dynamic, adaptive system capable of processing unstructured and semi-structured data at scale while maintaining stringent security protocols. The computational approach combines graph-based analytics to map relational patterns across entities and events, machine learning models for anomaly detection in temporal datasets, and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract latent connections from multilingual textual reports. These components will be integrated into a containerized architecture optimized for parallel processing, enabling real-time updates to threat assessments and predictive scenario modeling. The project will validate the framework using synthetic datasets replicating multi-domain conflict scenarios, with iterative testing against historical intelligence gaps identified in post-operational reviews. Anticipated outcomes include a reduction in analytical latency for time-sensitive decisions, improved accuracy in identifying cross-domain threats, and a novel methodology for quantifying uncertainty in fused intelligence products. By advancing the computational infrastructure available to strategic intelligence analysts, this work aims to strengthen the agility of military planning processes in contested environments, directly supporting national security priorities. The HPC resources requested are critical for training domain-specific ML models, simulating large-scale data ingestion workflows, and stress-testing the system’s ability to handle classified data tiers within secure virtualized environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the management, analysis and use of national-level, theatre-level, and international intelligence and related policy issues. Includes instruction in intelligence organization and management, strategic uses of intelligence, management of intelligence systems and assets, command and control, joint intelligence operations, electronic and signals intelligence, threat assessment and estimation, intelligence analysis and reporting, counterintelligence, and studies of specific regions and situations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale multimedia datasets in journalism research, addressing the growing challenge of misinformation detection and narrative tracking across decentralized media ecosystems. Traditional journalism research methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and variety of digital content—including text, images, and video—generated by social platforms, news outlets, and user communities. The research problem centers on developing scalable computational tools to identify emerging disinformation campaigns, map the diffusion of narratives, and assess bias in multimedia reporting. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis, computer vision techniques for image and video verification, and graph-based network modeling to trace cross-platform content sharing. Deep learning models, including transformer architectures and multimodal neural networks, will be trained on heterogeneous datasets comprising social media posts, historical news archives, and fact-checking databases. HPC resources are critical for handling parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters for complex models, and simulating information diffusion dynamics in near-real time. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for journalists to detect synthetic media, visualize narrative networks, and prioritize high-risk content for manual review. The project aims to advance computational journalism methodologies by establishing reproducible pipelines for auditing media ecosystems at scale, with implications for improving public trust in journalism and supporting evidence-based policy responses to misinformation. By integrating HPC-driven insights with traditional reporting practices, this work will empower news organizations to address evolving ethical challenges in the digital age while maintaining rigorous standards of accountability.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in journalism, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, yet the biomechanical mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects on musculoskeletal conditions remain incompletely characterized. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to simulate OMT-induced tissue responses and optimize treatment protocols. A key challenge is integrating patient-specific anatomical variability with dynamic biomechanical forces during manual interventions, which requires high-resolution modeling of musculoskeletal structures and real-time simulation of tissue deformation. To achieve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement finite element analysis (FEA) frameworks coupled with machine learning-driven parameter optimization. The project will utilize clinical imaging data (MRI/CT) from a cohort of 150 patients with chronic lower back pain to construct anatomically detailed models of the lumbar spine, surrounding soft tissues, and fascial networks. These models will simulate OMT maneuvers under varying force vectors, durations, and frequencies, with outputs validated against motion capture and electromyography data collected during clinical OMT sessions. The computational pipeline will employ GPU-accelerated solvers to handle nonlinear tissue mechanics and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess parameter sensitivity across diverse physiological scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of biomechanical predictors of OMT efficacy, (2) quantification of dose-response relationships for specific techniques, and (3) development of a predictive tool for personalizing OMT protocols based on individual biomechanical profiles. By elucidating mechanistic pathways at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, this work will advance evidence-based application of OMT while establishing a computational framework for future studies on manual therapies. The scale of data integration (≥10^6 mesh elements per model) and need for rapid iteration across parameter spaces (≥50,000 simulations) necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to ensure clinically relevant throughput and model fidelity.
cip_definition: Research focused on Osteopathic Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cultural and experiential dimensions of disability through computational analysis of large-scale textual and visual datasets, with a focus on identifying patterns in disability representation across digital media, literature, and advocacy materials. The research problem centers on the lack of systematic, data-driven studies examining how disability narratives—shaped by intersecting identities such as race, gender, and class—evolve in public discourse and artistic expression. Traditional qualitative methods in Disability Studies face scalability limitations when analyzing expansive corpora, hindering comprehensive insights into systemic biases, erasures, or transformative narratives. To address this, the project employs natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze multilingual texts, images, and audiovisual materials from sources including digital archives, social media platforms, and disability-led art collections. Key computational tasks include sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and multimodal network analysis to map relationships between discursive themes, visual symbolism, and socio-cultural contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training transformer-based models on disability-specific lexicons, processing terabyte-scale datasets, and running iterative simulations to assess the robustness of findings across diverse subcommunities. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for analyzing disability representation at scale, identifying gaps in mainstream narratives, and highlighting counternarratives that challenge ableist paradigms. The project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in Disability Studies by integrating computational social science with humanities-driven inquiry, offering new tools for activists, artists, and policymakers to evaluate and amplify equitable representations of disability. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will generate empirically grounded insights into how disability is constructed, contested, and reimagined in global digital ecosystems.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature, meaning, and consequences of what it is to be defined as disabled and explores the historical, cultural, economic, physiological, and socio-political dynamics of disability. Includes instruction in disability rights, legal issues, and public policy; literature, philosophy, and the arts; and/or research in the social sciences, education, and health sciences addressing social and experiential aspects of disability.

abstract: The proposed research addresses unresolved questions in the statistical mechanics of turbulent fluid systems, focusing on energy cascades and intermittency in non-equilibrium regimes. Traditional analytical models struggle to capture the multi-scale, nonlinear interactions governing these phenomena, particularly in three-dimensional flows with variable boundary conditions. This project will employ high-resolution direct numerical simulations (DNS) of the Navier-Stokes equations to resolve inertial-range dynamics across spatial and temporal scales inaccessible to laboratory experiments. A hybrid spectral-finite difference method will be implemented to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, with adaptive mesh refinement targeting regions of high vorticity. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed-memory parallelism to achieve the necessary scale, requiring access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources with dedicated nodes for sustained petascale workloads. Key objectives include quantifying anomalous scaling exponents in turbulent kinetic energy spectra, characterizing rare extreme events contributing to intermittency, and validating recently proposed universality classes for dissipation field structures. Data analysis pipelines will employ wavelet-based techniques and machine learning classifiers to identify coherent structures in simulation outputs. Expected outcomes include new empirical constraints for theoretical models of turbulent transport, with implications for improving subgrid-scale parameterizations in weather prediction and fusion plasma confinement systems. The generated datasets will be made publicly available through a curated repository, supporting reproducibility and cross-disciplinary comparisons. By resolving long-standing discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental observations, this work aims to advance fundamental understanding of turbulence while demonstrating the critical role of HPC resources in tackling computationally intractable problems in classical physics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Public sector decision-making faces increasing complexity due to evolving societal needs, fiscal constraints, and interconnected policy challenges. This project seeks to advance evidence-based policy design by developing computational models to simulate multi-stakeholder interactions and evaluate dynamic trade-offs in public resource allocation. The research focuses on optimizing equity-efficiency balances in social service delivery systems, particularly in contexts such as emergency response resource distribution, healthcare access in underserved regions, and cross-agency budget prioritization. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will implement agent-based modeling frameworks to capture the behavior of governmental entities, community organizations, and individual beneficiaries under varying policy scenarios. Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations will assess systemic outcomes across demographic, economic, and institutional variables, while natural language processing techniques will analyze historical policy documents and public feedback data to inform model parameters. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing capabilities to manage 1) fine-grained simulations of decision cascades across jurisdictional boundaries, 2) real-time sensitivity analyses for multi-objective optimization problems, and 3) machine learning-driven pattern recognition in unstructured administrative data. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify the second-order effects of funding allocation choices, identify latent inequities in service delivery networks, and test crisis response protocols under resource scarcity conditions. By integrating computational social science methods with public administration theory, this work aims to provide actionable frameworks for improving institutional adaptability and democratic accountability in resource governance. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from municipal partnership networks and support over 10,000 concurrent policy simulations, significantly advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational modeling and participatory policymaking.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Administration and Public Policy and with an emphasis the administration and management of public policies. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; research methods; role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation; and resource allocation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary study of cultural resilience and identity formation within marginalized North American communities, with a focus on Indigenous oral histories and African American digital archives. The research problem centers on the fragmented preservation and analysis of culturally significant materials—such as oral narratives, community-generated media, and ephemeral art—which are often dispersed across non-standardized repositories or exist in computationally demanding formats (e.g., audiovisual recordings, multilingual texts). Traditional qualitative methods struggle to synthesize these large, heterogeneous datasets, limiting opportunities to trace cross-generational patterns of cultural adaptation and resistance. To address this, the project will deploy computational text analysis, speech-to-text algorithms, and multimodal machine learning models to process and interrelate diverse sources at scale. Custom NLP pipelines will be developed to handle code-switching, dialectal variations, and culturally specific metaphors in oral histories, while graph-based analytics will map the evolution of narrative themes across time and geographies. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models, parallelizing metadata extraction from terabyte-scale audiovisual corpora, and simulating network dynamics of cultural dissemination. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit tailored for Ethnic Studies researchers, enriched annotated datasets documenting intersectional identity practices, and visualizations elucidating how marginalized communities navigate cultural erasure. By integrating computational rigor with critical ethnic studies frameworks, this work aims to establish new methodologies for ethically engaging with non-dominant knowledge systems while centering the voices of historically underrepresented groups. The project’s scalability and open-access deliverables will support broader scholarly efforts to decolonize digital humanities infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary and comparative study of the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of North American racial and ethnic groups, including African Americans, American Indians/Native Americans, Hispanic Americans, and Asian Americans.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational film and media studies through large-scale analysis of cinematic datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in the field: the lack of systematic, data-driven methodologies for analyzing historical and contemporary media artifacts at scale. Traditional approaches to film theory and criticism rely on manual close readings of select works, limiting the scope of analysis and hindering the identification of macro-level patterns across genres, periods, or cultural contexts. To overcome these limitations, this project will develop and deploy machine learning models to process and analyze a curated corpus of 10,000+ films and associated metadata, including visual content (color palettes, shot compositions, lighting), audio features, subtitles, and production records. Computational methods will include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for frame-level feature extraction, transformer-based models for narrative structure analysis, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map evolving stylistic influences across global cinema. The HPC infrastructure is essential for training multi-modal architectures on high-resolution video data, conducting parallelized experiments across temporal and geographic dimensions, and storing intermediate representations of terabyte-scale media files. Expected outcomes include 1) quantitative frameworks for tracking the diffusion of cinematic techniques through history, 2) interactive visualization tools for exploring transnational aesthetic networks, and 3) open-source pipelines to enable computational media analysis across humanities disciplines. By bridging film studies with scalable computational methods, this work aims to redefine how scholars contextualize cultural artifacts, while providing practical resources for preserving and interpreting the rapidly expanding corpus of digital media heritage.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program in the visual arts that focuses on the study of the history, development, theory, and criticism of the film/media arts, as well as the basic principles of filmmaking and film production.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of patient care outcomes in practical nursing settings. A critical challenge in nursing practice is optimizing staffing workflows and clinical decision-making under dynamic, resource-constrained conditions. Traditional methods for predicting patient deterioration or allocating nursing staff often rely on static protocols, which may not account for real-time variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff availability, or emerging health data from wearable sensors. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework trained on multimodal datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), nurse-patient interaction logs, and real-time biometric monitoring data. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of temporally structured, heterogeneous data to train deep learning models (e.g., transformer-based architectures and time-series forecasting networks) capable of predicting short-term patient risks and recommending adaptive staffing adjustments. HPC resources are essential for parallelized hyperparameter tuning, large-scale simulation of care scenarios, and validation across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool to assist nurse managers in proactive resource allocation and a validated model for early detection of patient decompensation in vocational nursing contexts. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with nursing expertise, this work aims to reduce preventable adverse events, improve nurse workload equity, and establish scalable computational methods for personalized care planning in non-hospital settings. The results will directly inform competency-based training frameworks for nursing assistants and contribute novel computational strategies to the nursing science literature.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a computational framework for modeling teacher decision-making processes in diverse classroom environments, with the goal of improving personalized professional development tools for educators. A critical challenge in teacher education lies in understanding how educators dynamically adapt instructional strategies to heterogeneous student needs, particularly in inclusive classrooms where cognitive, linguistic, and cultural variability requires real-time pedagogical adjustments. Current training simulations lack the granularity to capture nuanced interactions between teacher actions, student responses, and learning outcomes. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate millions of classroom scenarios across parameterized student profiles, curriculum structures, and pedagogical interventions. The computational model will integrate empirical data from classroom observations, student assessment records, and teacher self-reports to train deep reinforcement learning agents that emulate teacher behavior patterns. Multi-node parallelization will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds in class composition, resource availability, and instructional tactics that influence educational equity outcomes. Expected outputs include (1) a validated simulation engine for predicting how specific professional development strategies impact teacher adaptability, and (2) generative AI tools that propose customized training modules based on individual educators' simulated performance gaps. By quantifying complex classroom dynamics through massively parallel simulations, this work aims to establish an evidence base for optimizing competency-based teacher development programs at scale. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of classroom interactions and achieving statistical power in analyzing emergent patterns across demographic subgroups. Outcomes will directly inform the design of adaptive learning systems for teacher education programs seeking to enhance inclusive pedagogical practices.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Levels and Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education and professional development, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The controlled use of explosives in construction, mining, and demolition demands high precision to balance efficiency, safety, and environmental impact. Current empirical models for blast design often rely on oversimplified assumptions about rock fragmentation, shockwave propagation, and structural response, leading to suboptimal outcomes such as overbreak, flyrock, or incomplete fracturing. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate blasting dynamics in complex geological environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to integrate multi-physics simulations coupling fracture mechanics, granular material behavior, and transient fluid-structure interactions. These simulations will account for heterogeneous rock properties, explosive charge geometries, and site-specific boundary conditions. Advanced numerical methods, including smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) and discrete element modeling (DEM), will be implemented to capture crack propagation, debris dispersion, and energy dissipation at multiple scales. Machine learning techniques will further optimize blast parameters by analyzing simulation outputs against field data. The project will validate models using controlled experimental blasts, incorporating high-speed imaging and seismic monitoring. Outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing collateral damage, improving fragmentation efficiency, and reducing hazardous byproducts. By enabling precise, scenario-specific blast designs, this work will enhance safety protocols, lower operational costs, and support sustainable resource extraction practices. The computational demands of these simulations—requiring terabytes of memory, parallelized solvers, and weeks of runtime—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Successful implementation will advance academic understanding of explosive-material interactions while providing actionable insights for industry stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in using a variety of explosive materials to aid in the construction process. Includes instruction in safety procedures for storing, handling, placement, charge power determination, drilling, pounding, building demolition, preparing rocky surfaces for building foundations and demolition of explosives.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing multi-stage manufacturing processes with complex material behavior and dynamic operational constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability challenges in real-time production systems. Traditional simulation tools struggle to model interactions between machine tool dynamics, thermal deformation in additive manufacturing, and adaptive quality control systems at scale, particularly when integrating real-time sensor data from production lines. The proposed work will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for micro-scale material deformation, discrete-event simulation for factory-floor logistics, and machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets spanning tool wear patterns, energy consumption metrics, and in-process inspection results. By deploying these hybrid models on HPC clusters using MPI-based parallelization, the research aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in simultaneous optimization of machining parameters, robotic assembly sequences, and predictive maintenance schedules. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated digital twin simulations for rapid scenario testing and graph neural networks to model interdependencies between production subsystems. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support system capable of recommending parameter adjustments under fluctuating demand scenarios while maintaining ISO 28400 quality standards. This work will directly benefit small-to-medium manufacturers adopting Industry 4.0 technologies by providing open-source computational templates for scalable process optimization. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sensitivity studies across 10,000+ core-hour simulations, significantly advancing the precision and applicability of virtual manufacturing frameworks in industrial settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to the identification and resolution of production problems in the manufacture of products. Includes instruction in machine operations, production line operations, engineering analysis, systems analysis, instrumentation, physical controls, automation, computer-aided manufacturing (CAM), manufacturing planning, quality control, and informational infrastructure.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize vehicle emission inspection protocols and improve diagnostic accuracy for aging emission control systems. Current inspection methods rely heavily on standardized test cycles and static thresholds, which inadequately capture real-world emission variability, especially in older vehicles with deteriorating components. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale interactions between engine performance, exhaust aftertreatment systems, and sensor outputs under diverse operating conditions. A hybrid approach will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of catalytic converter efficiency, machine learning algorithms trained on historical inspection data, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in fault detection. The CFD models will resolve spatially resolved chemical reactions within catalytic substrates, while recurrent neural networks will correlate transient sensor patterns (e.g., O2 sensor waveforms) with specific emission system failures. By parallelizing these computations across thousands of scenarios, we aim to establish dynamic, vehicle-specific emission thresholds that account for component wear and environmental factors. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool for inspection stations to prioritize high-risk vehicles, reducing false pass/fail rates by an estimated 40%. Additionally, the simulations will inform technician training modules by visualizing failure progression in virtual emission systems. This work directly supports regulatory compliance with evolving emission standards and reduces the environmental health burden of undetected high emitters. The computational demands—particularly the need for GPU-accelerated CFD solvers and distributed training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve practical runtime for operational deployment.
cip_title: Vehicle Emissions Inspection and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to test, repair, service, and maintain vehicle emission systems in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of intercultural conflict resolution and cooperation in digitally mediated environments using large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis. As globalized societies increasingly rely on virtual platforms for cross-cultural collaboration, tensions arising from divergent communication norms, values, and power asymmetries pose challenges to equitable participation. Traditional social science methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, adaptive interactions that characterize these complex systems. The research will develop computational models to simulate how culturally situated agents negotiate shared goals under conditions of linguistic bias, information inequality, and competing identity narratives. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to parameterize agents using empirical data from ethnographic studies (e.g., conflict resolution styles, trust-building rituals) and scale simulations to reflect realistic population diversity. Neural networks will be trained on multilingual dialog corpora to emulate culturally coded communication patterns, while graph-theoretic methods will analyze emergent alliance structures and polarization thresholds. The computational framework integrates anthropological theories of ritual interaction, sociological models of social capital, and psychological principles of intergroup attribution bias. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for identifying critical intervention points in cross-cultural collaborations and generative algorithms for designing inclusive digital deliberation spaces. By quantifying how micro-level cultural exchanges propagate to macro-level group outcomes, this work aims to inform policies addressing systemic inequities in education, remote work, and transnational governance. The resource-intensive nature of simulating millions of culturally contextualized interactions across parameter spaces necessitates parallelized computing architectures to achieve statistical robustness. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation toolkits tailored for intercultural studies researchers.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the formation and evolution of intersectional identities within diasporic communities through the analysis of large-scale, multilingual textual and multimedia archives. While prior studies have examined cultural identity through qualitative frameworks, the scale and complexity of digital ethnocultural records—spanning social media, oral histories, and community-generated content—demand computational methods to identify patterns, semantic shifts, and network dynamics across temporal and spatial axes. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations, combined with multimodal network analysis to trace how gender, ethnicity, and cultural practices are negotiated in hybridized diasporic spaces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training transformer-based models on terabyte-scale datasets, enabling parallel processing of heterogeneous data types (text, audio, visual), and simulating agent-based models of cultural transmission. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational framework for analyzing identity construction in fragmented, multilingual archives; (2) empirical insights into how generational trauma and resilience manifest in digital cultural production; and (3) open-source tools for ethical data stewardship aligned with community-based participatory research principles. By advancing computational methods tailored to marginalized cultural datasets, this work aims to redefine scholarly approaches to studying identity formation while directly supporting heritage preservation initiatives in partner communities. The requested GPU nodes and distributed storage infrastructure will facilitate processing timelines impossible with existing campus resources, particularly for transformer fine-tuning and hyperparameter optimization across 50+ linguistic varieties.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Area, Ethnic, Cultural, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in area, ethnic, cultural, gender, or group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing and simulating the evolution of vernacular architectural typologies in under-documented regions. Traditional architectural historiography often relies on qualitative, manual analysis of physical structures and archival records, limiting scalability and the ability to model dynamic cultural, environmental, and socio-economic influences on design practices over time. Our research addresses this gap by developing a hybrid methodology combining 3D spatial analytics, machine learning (ML)-driven pattern recognition, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to reconstruct and visualize architectural adaptation processes across multi-century timelines. The computational workflow integrates heterogeneous datasets—including LiDAR scans of extant structures, fragmented historical maps, climate records, and ethnographic archives—to train ML models that identify correlations between material choices, structural forms, and contextual stressors. ABM simulations will then test hypotheses about how communities iteratively modified building practices in response to factors such as resource scarcity, trade networks, or demographic shifts. HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale geospatial datasets, optimizing deep learning architectures for image-based feature extraction, and running ensemble simulations across parameterized historical scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational architectural heritage analysis, a publicly accessible digital repository of simulated typological lineages, and new interdisciplinary frameworks for studying vernacular architecture as a dynamic system rather than a static artifact. By bridging computational scalability with humanities-driven inquiry, this project aims to redefine preservation priorities for at-risk structures and inform culturally responsive conservation policies in rapidly urbanizing regions.
cip_title: Architectural History, Criticism, and Conservation, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural history, criticism, and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze the sociocultural and spatial dynamics influencing the success of church planting initiatives in urban environments, a critical but underexplored area within mission-oriented theology and practical ministry. While church planting traditionally relies on qualitative ethnographic and theological frameworks, this research introduces a computational humanities approach to model how demographic shifts, community networks, and cultural adaptation strategies intersect with congregational growth. The central problem addressed is the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to predict viable locations for new congregations or evaluate the long-term sustainability of planting strategies across diverse urban contexts. By integrating geospatial data, census metrics, social media activity, and historical church growth patterns, the project will employ machine learning algorithms to identify latent variables affecting community receptivity and resilience. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between hypothetical planting strategies and localized socioreligious ecosystems, testing hypotheses about optimal outreach methods, leadership structures, and intercultural engagement. HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning multiple cities, running parallelized simulations of decade-long growth scenarios, and training deep learning models on unstructured textual data from mission reports and congregational surveys. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive analytics framework to guide denominational planting investments and an open-access repository of computational models linking theological principles with urban sociology. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges gaps between empirical social science, digital humanities, and applied theology, offering novel tools for faith communities navigating 21st-century urbanization challenges while preserving the humanistic core of religious vocation. The project’s computational artifacts aim to set a precedent for data-informed decision-making in religious studies without reducing spiritual praxis to purely quantitative metrics.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to establish congregations of Christians in new locations. Includes instruction in models of church planting, church multiplication strategies, church leadership, evangelism, missiology, Christian ethics, and mission-oriented theology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of ecological opportunity and functional trait evolution in driving adaptive radiations across deep time, with a focus on resolving long-standing questions about the tempo and mode of morphological diversification in extinct and extant vertebrate clades.
