A key challenge in testing macroevolutionary hypotheses lies in integrating complex, multidimensional datasets—including fossil-derived morphometric data, phylogenetic comparative models, and biomechanical simulations—to disentangle the effects of selective pressures, developmental constraints, and stochastic processes. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based evolutionary simulations with high-resolution phylogenetic paleobiological analyses. Agent-based models will simulate adaptive landscapes under varying ecological scenarios, while parallelized Bayesian methods will infer evolutionary rate shifts and trait correlations from 3D cranial and postcranial morphological datasets spanning 50+ million years across multiple radiations (e.g., Cenozoic mammals, Mesozoic archosaurs). Computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis will be employed to quantify functional consequences of craniodental evolution in key lineages. The scale of these analyses—requiring iterative model testing across thousands of simulated evolutionary trajectories and processing of terabyte-scale micro-CT datasets—necessitates high-performance computing resources. Expected outcomes include (1) novel metrics for identifying ecological triggers of adaptive radiation in the fossil record, (2) a refined understanding of how locomotor and feeding biomechanics constrain evolutionary pathways, and (3) open-source tools for integrating paleontological and neontological data in macroevolutionary synthesis. By bridging theoretical models with empirical trait datasets, this work will advance predictive frameworks for how organisms evolve under shifting environmental pressures, with implications for conservation biology and systematic prioritization in rapidly changing ecosystems. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale phylogenetic inference, and optimized storage for multidimensional morphological datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic, developmental, functional, and morphological patterns and processes, and theoretical principles; and the emergence and mutation of organisms over time. Includes instruction in molecular and morphological systematics; genetics and development; evolutionary transformation; paleobiology and paleontology; morphogenesis; mutation; locomotor, biomechanical and craniodental form and function; evolutionary theory; and systematic biology.

abstract: Documentary production is increasingly reliant on advanced computational tools to manage high-resolution media, complex data integration, and interactive storytelling techniques. However, existing consumer-grade hardware and software often fail to support the scale and complexity of modern documentary workflows, particularly when handling 4K/8K video processing, machine learning (ML)-driven archival analysis, or real-time immersive rendering. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through three interconnected research strands: (1) developing scalable algorithms for automated video segmentation and metadata tagging across large historical archives, (2) training custom ML models to analyze visual and auditory patterns in documentary footage for ethical bias detection, and (3) prototyping interactive documentary environments using real-time neural rendering techniques. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallel processing of video frames, distributed storage systems for managing petascale media libraries, and cloud-based rendering clusters to test viewer interactions in virtual production pipelines. The research builds on open-source frameworks like FFmpeg and PyTorch but extends them to address domain-specific needs, such as preserving temporal context in oral history interviews during automated transcript synchronization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for documentary-specific HPC workflows, peer-reviewed studies on computational ethnography methods, and case studies demonstrating how resource-intensive techniques—such as simulating archival footage degradation for preservation research—can deepen historical analysis. By bridging gaps between media studies and computational science, this project aims to establish new best practices for data-driven storytelling while training documentary students in HPC literacy, ensuring they can ethically harness emerging technologies in nonfiction media production.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce nonfiction film and video. Includes instruction in film and video writing, directing, and production; film studies; history of the documentary; research techniques; videography; editing; and business aspects of film production.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance quantitative models of sediment flux and stratigraphic architecture in terrestrial basins, with a focus on resolving uncertainties in the feedbacks between tectonic deformation, climate variability, and sedimentary system response. Current stratigraphic models struggle to simulate the multiscale interactions driving basin-filling processes over geologic timescales, particularly in settings where high-resolution stratigraphic data reveal complex, nonlinear responses to external forcings. To address this, we propose a coupled modeling framework integrating 3D stratigraphic forward modeling (SFM) with machine learning (ML)-based parameter optimization. The SFM component will simulate sediment erosion, transport, and deposition using physics-based hydrodynamics and sediment mechanics, while ML algorithms will iteratively refine boundary conditions and process rates through comparison with field-derived stratigraphic datasets (e.g., grain size trends, paleocurrent indicators, and basin geometry). Computational workflows will parallelize ensemble model runs across HPC nodes to explore parameter space efficiently, requiring ~50,000 core-hours for sensitivity analyses and model calibration. Key challenges include handling high-resolution spatial datasets (10^6–10^7 grid cells) and coupling time-dependent tectonic subsidence/uplift patterns with stochastic climate forcing. Expected outcomes include: (1) improved quantification of sediment routing system sensitivity to tectonic-climate perturbations, (2) validation of model predictions against well-constrained field examples from Cenozoic rift basins, and (3) open-source release of optimized ML-SFM code to enable community-driven testing of stratigraphic hypotheses. This work will directly inform interpretations of sedimentary archives used in hydrocarbon exploration, paleoenvironmental reconstruction, and assessments of landscape response to modern climate change. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary spatial-temporal resolution and computational throughput to advance beyond current model limitations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of sedimentary rocks and the processes that shaped the surface of the Earth and how those processes have interacted to control the Earth system.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized learning pathways for middle school students, addressing the challenge of diverse learning needs in mixed-ability classrooms. Despite advances in differentiated instruction, teachers often lack tools to dynamically predict student performance trajectories or design interventions that account for interrelated cognitive, behavioral, and socio-emotional factors. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate heterogeneous data—including standardized assessment results, formative feedback, and engagement metrics—to support educators in crafting adaptive instructional strategies. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble machine learning models on multi-year datasets from 15,000+ students across diverse school districts. Computational methods will include natural language processing of open-response student work, graph neural networks to map concept mastery dependencies, and agent-based simulations to test intervention impacts under varying classroom conditions. Key challenges involve scaling feature engineering for sparse educational data and parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across learning domains. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool that quantifies the probable efficacy of instructional choices for subpopulations, enabling teachers to proactively adjust lesson plans and resource allocations. By simulating millions of potential learning sequences, this work aims to identify high-yield pedagogical strategies that balance curricular requirements with individual learner needs. The resulting models could reduce trial-and-error in classroom practice while providing empirical insights into how specific interventions propagate through student networks. This work directly supports teacher education by transforming complex educational data into actionable guidance, ultimately aiming to improve both pedagogical decision-making and equity in middle school learning outcomes.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Junior High/ Intermediate/ Middle School Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the middle, intermediate or junior high grades, which may include grades four through nine by regulation.

abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients face complex nutritional challenges due to metabolic dysregulation, yet current dietary guidelines lack precision in addressing individual variability in nutrient metabolism and microbiome interactions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for personalized nutrition strategies in CKD by integrating multi-omics data, dynamic metabolic modeling, and patient-specific clinical parameters. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze longitudinal metabolomic, gut microbiome, and genomic datasets from a cohort of 500 CKD patients, coupled with real-time continuous glucose and uremic toxin monitoring. A systems biology approach will be employed to construct mechanistic models of nitrogen and phosphorus metabolism, simulating interactions between dietary intake, microbial fermentation, and host metabolic pathways. Machine learning algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers of nutritional response, while in silico trials will test the efficacy of tailored dietary interventions under varying physiological conditions. Key computational challenges include large-scale optimization of nonlinear metabolic networks, stochastic modeling of microbiome-host crosstalk, and high-dimensional data integration across temporal scales. The expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific nutrient prescriptions that minimize uremic toxicity while maintaining nutritional adequacy, alongside open-source tools for simulating diet-microbiome-metabolome dynamics in renal impairment. This work addresses a critical gap in clinical nutrition by moving beyond population-level recommendations to computationally driven, precision dietary management. Successful implementation could reduce CKD progression rates and dialysis dependency, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-enabled nutritional metabolomics in chronic disease care. Resource allocation will support data storage, parallelized model calibration, and large-ensemble simulations across heterogeneous patient subgroups.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of dietetics and the biomedical and nutrition sciences to design and manage effective nutrition programs as part of clinical treatment and therapy programs, and to manage health care facility food services. Includes instruction in human nutrition, nutrient metabolism, the role of foods and nutrition in health promotion and disease prevention, nutrition as a treatment regime, planning and directing hospital food service programs, diet and nutrition analysis and planning, supervision of food storage and preparation, special diets, client education, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of drug-resistant pathogens necessitates the rapid development of novel antimicrobial agents with enhanced efficacy and selectivity. Traditional experimental approaches for drug discovery are often time-consuming and resource-intensive, particularly when addressing complex biological targets such as multi-drug efflux pumps or mutation-prone viral proteases. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the rational design of next-generation antimicrobial compounds through advanced computational chemistry methods. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) elucidating atomistic mechanisms of drug-target interactions and resistance-conferring mutations using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, and (2) employing machine learning (ML)-enhanced virtual screening to identify lead compounds from large chemical libraries. All-atom MD simulations will model dynamic behavior of target proteins (e.g., bacterial β-lactamases, viral polymerases) and their complexes with inhibitors at microsecond timescales, while FEP will quantify binding affinity changes caused by resistance mutations. Concurrently, graph neural networks trained on existing drug-target interaction data will predict binding poses and prioritize compounds for synthesis. The computational workflow demands significant HPC resources due to the need for parallelized sampling of conformational states (≥50 replicas per system), processing of multi-terabyte simulation datasets, and screening of >10 million compounds across GPU-accelerated docking platforms. Expected outcomes include the identification of 3-5 high-potential antimicrobial candidates for experimental validation, structural insights into resistance mechanisms to guide future drug optimization, and publicly shared ML models for target-specific virtual screening. This work directly addresses critical gaps in antimicrobial development while establishing computational frameworks that could be adapted to other therapeutic areas within medicinal chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemistry to the study of biologically and clinically active substances, biological and pharmacological interactions, and the development of associated research methods, techniques, and clinical trial procedures. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular graphics, rational drug design, toxicology, molecular biology, pharmacology, enzyme mechanisms, receptor theory, neurochemistry, drug metabolism, drug synthesis, biological mechanisms of drug action, research tools and techniques, and laboratory safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing pedagogical strategies for social science teacher candidates by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the longitudinal impacts of training interventions on instructional efficacy. Social science education requires teachers to navigate complex, interdisciplinary content and diverse classroom dynamics, yet existing teacher education programs often lack data-driven frameworks to predict how specific training methods translate to real-world teaching outcomes. The proposed research will develop computational models to simulate how variations in curricular emphasis, practicum experiences, and mentorship structures affect teacher candidates’ ability to design inclusive, inquiry-based social science lessons. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques, we will analyze multi-year datasets from 15 partner teacher preparation programs, incorporating variables such as candidate demographics, mentor feedback, and K-12 student performance metrics. HPC resources are critical for processing these heterogeneous datasets (totaling ~50 TB) and running parallelized simulations that test thousands of training scenarios under differing socioeconomic and institutional constraints. Expected outcomes include identifying key leverage points in social science teacher development pathways and generating predictive tools to personalize training modules based on candidate strengths and contextual needs. By elucidating the nonlinear relationships between training inputs and teaching competencies, this work aims to advance evidence-based reforms in teacher education, ultimately improving secondary students’ civic engagement and critical analysis of societal systems. The computational framework will be made accessible to education researchers, enabling scalable replication studies across disciplinary domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific social science subjects and programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the resolution and accuracy of structural variant (SV) detection in clinical cytogenetics by integrating high-throughput imaging data from karyotyping and fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) with whole-genome sequencing. Current SV detection methods face limitations in resolving complex rearrangements, such as balanced translocations or low-level mosaicism, due to fragmented data analysis pipelines and insufficient computational power for multimodal data integration. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabyte-scale imaging datasets (including high-resolution metaphase spreads and interphase FISH signals) alongside genomic sequencing data. A hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) and graph-based algorithm will be trained to identify subtle cytogenetic anomalies by correlating spatial chromosomal patterns from imaging with sequencing-derived breakpoint data. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of high-dimensional image stacks, real-time alignment of heterogeneous data types, and scalable storage for population-level cytogenetic archives. The anticipated outcomes include a validated pipeline for detecting SVs with >95% concordance across modalities, reducing manual analysis time by 70%, and identifying previously undetectable mosaic variants in retrospective leukemia samples. This work will provide open-source tools for automated cytogenetic annotation, enabling clinical labs to standardize SV reporting and improve diagnostic accuracy for congenital disorders and hematologic malignancies. By bridging computational genomics and imaging informatics, the project addresses a critical gap in precision cytogenetics, with implications for guiding targeted therapies and refining risk stratification in cancer genomics.
cip_title: Cytogenetics/ Genetics/ Clinical Genetics Technology/ Technologist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform analyses of the human genome and chromosomes for the research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes instruction in chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of hypersonic reentry dynamics and thermal protection systems (TPS) for spacecraft, addressing critical gaps in simulating high-speed, high-enthalpy flows and material responses under extreme aerothermal loads. Current models struggle to resolve multiscale phenomena, such as turbulence-chemistry interactions in partially ionized boundary layers and ablation-induced surface degradation, which compromise the accuracy of TPS design predictions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity framework combining direct numerical simulation (DNS) of reacting flows, discrete element method (DEM) modeling of material erosion, and machine learning-accelerated coupling between fluid and structural solvers. The DNS component will resolve micron-scale boundary layer features using a compressible Navier-Stokes solver with finite-rate chemistry, validated against experimental shock tube data. The DEM approach will model carbon-carbon composite degradation at the fiber-matrix level under combined thermal and shear stresses. A neural operator surrogate will bridge the disparate timescales between fluid and solid domains, enabling full-system predictions over mission-relevant durations. This work demands high-performance computing resources for three primary tasks: 1) petascale simulations of transitional hypersonic boundary layers (requiring >100 million core-hours on adaptive meshes), 2) GPU-optimized DEM computations tracking >10^6 discrete material elements, and 3) distributed training of physics-informed neural networks on multi-terabyte simulation datasets. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting TPS recession rates with <5% error relative to flight data, open-source tools for coupled aerothermal-structural analysis, and fundamental insights into nonequilibrium surface catalysis effects. These advances will directly inform next-generation spacecraft design for lunar return missions and crewed Mars exploration vehicles, while establishing computational best practices for multiphysics problems in extreme aerospace environments.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering, general
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their systems; applied research on flight and orbital characteristics; and the development of systems and procedures for the launching, guidance, and control of air and space vehicles.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for adaptive typographic systems that dynamically optimize readability, aesthetic coherence, and cross-platform compatibility in digital publishing. Current tools for computer typography and composition lack the computational capacity to efficiently model the interplay between variable font rendering, responsive layout parameters, and user-specific accessibility needs at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate and evaluate typographic compositions across millions of contextual permutations. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate user interactions with text under diverse conditions (e.g., screen resolutions, ambient lighting, cognitive load) and use genetic algorithms to iteratively refine typographic rulesets. This approach requires parallelized processing of large datasets—including font metrics, eye-tracking data, and device specifications—to generate predictive models for optimal typeface selection, kerning, and line spacing. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for real-time adaptive typography, validated against user studies and industry-standard design workflows. The project’s significance lies in advancing computational typography beyond static design paradigms, enabling automated, context-aware composition that enhances accessibility for diverse readers while reducing manual labor in publishing pipelines. By leveraging HPC resources, this work will address latency challenges in rendering complex layouts and support the training of machine learning models to predict design efficacy across communication platforms. Results will directly benefit journalism and digital media sectors by providing scalable solutions for personalized content delivery, aligning with evolving demands in multi-device publishing environments.
cip_title: Computer Typography and Composition Equipment Operator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to design and execute page formats, layouts and text composition, and to make typographical selections using computer graphics and other computer-assisted design programs.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics and textual analysis in Vietnamese language studies. While Vietnamese is spoken by over 90 million people globally, computational tools tailored to its tonal, syntactic, and dialectal complexity remain underdeveloped compared to widely studied languages like English. This gap hinders large-scale analysis of historical and contemporary Vietnamese texts, limiting insights into linguistic evolution, sociocultural trends, and regional dialect variation. The project aims to address this by constructing a scalable corpus of Vietnamese texts spanning pre-modern Chữ Nôm scripts to modern digital media, then applying neural language models and phonetic alignment algorithms to analyze linguistic patterns. Key computational challenges include training transformer-based models on non-Latin scripts with diacritics, optimizing grapheme-to-phoneme conversion for six major dialects, and performing diachronic sentiment analysis on literature across political eras. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale text datasets, distributed training of deep learning architectures, and high-memory phonetic alignment tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source NLP tools for Vietnamese dialect classification and historical text normalization, (2) quantitative maps of lexical and semantic shifts in 20th-century literature, and (3) a public corpus with metadata linking linguistic features to sociocultural contexts. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this work will provide new methodologies for preserving endangered dialectal forms, enhance machine learning applications for Vietnamese language technologies, and offer empirically grounded perspectives on how linguistic changes reflect Vietnam’s modern sociohistorical trajectory. The requested resources are critical given the computational intensity of processing tonal embeddings and aligning cross-dialectal speech corpora, tasks infeasible on standard academic infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Vietnamese language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of mobile cranes in dynamic environments remains a critical challenge in construction and industrial settings, particularly as infrastructure projects grow in scale and complexity. Current training protocols and operational guidelines often rely on static load charts and simplified assumptions, which inadequately account for real-world variables such as fluctuating wind loads, dynamic load oscillations, terrain instability, and operator decision-making under stress. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity, multi-physics simulation framework to model mobile crane operations under diverse environmental and operational conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate wind-crane interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress prediction, and machine learning algorithms to model operator behavior and adaptive control strategies. These components will be coupled within a real-time digital twin environment, enabling scenario testing across thousands of parameter combinations, including extreme or rare events impractical to replicate physically. The computational intensity of resolving fine-scale fluid-structure interactions, coupled with the need for Monte Carlo-style probabilistic risk assessments, necessitates parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows and large-scale data processing capabilities. Expected outcomes include predictive models for load stability thresholds, optimized emergency response protocols, and AI-driven decision-support tools for operators. The results will directly inform updates to industry safety standards, enhance simulator-based training modules, and provide a quantitative basis for crane configuration planning in complex job sites. By bridging gaps between theoretical load capacities and real-world operational dynamics, this work aims to reduce accident rates and improve efficiency in crane-dependent industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to hoist and swing loads via complex rotating machinery that is driver operated. Includes instruction in crane operational characteristics, load and capacity chart usage, emergency control skills, safety, specific types of mobile cranes and loading devices, applicable codes and standards, and applications to particular types of jobs and loads.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of dynamically integrating live performance, choreographic complexity, and technical production elements in theatre and dance. While interdisciplinary collaboration is central to performance creation, traditional rehearsal and design processes often struggle to simulate the real-time interplay between performers, interactive technologies, and environmental variables (e.g., lighting, acoustics, spatial configurations). This limitation hinders the ability to iteratively test and optimize multidimensional performance systems before live staging. The proposed work employs agent-based modeling and physics-driven simulations to computationally represent performer movement, audience sightlines, and environmental feedback loops. Motion-capture data from dance ensembles will inform machine learning models that predict choreographic trajectories, while parallelized rendering frameworks will simulate dynamic stage environments under variable technical parameters. These computational experiments aim to identify optimal alignments between artistic intent and technical feasibility, reducing production risks and expanding creative possibilities. Additionally, the project will prototype real-time interactive systems using HPC-enabled edge computing, where sensor-driven inputs from performers trigger adaptive lighting, sound, or projection responses during live workshops. Outcomes will include open-source tools for simulating performance ecosystems and a framework for quantifying aesthetic-impact metrics (e.g., audience engagement, spatial perception) through computational analysis. By bridging performance practice with scalable computational methods, this work advances the capacity of theatre and dance artists to innovate within complex, technology-mediated environments while preserving the embodied integrity of live performance. The requested resources are critical for handling large-scale datasets, running high-fidelity simulations, and reducing latency in interactive systems, enabling novel research at the intersection of performing arts and computational modeling.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on integrating the studies of dance and theatre arts to provide perspectives in all facets of production, performance, and critical engagement. Includes instruction in acting, aesthetics, choreography, costume design, criticism, dance, improvisation, music analysis, playwriting, theatre performance history, scene design, stage lighting, and technical theatre.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Celtic languages, with a focus on modeling linguistic evolution, dialectal variation, and cross-language contact phenomena. Despite the rich textual and oral traditions of Celtic languages, their historical fragmentation, divergent revitalization trajectories, and complex sociolinguistic dynamics pose significant barriers to systematic study. Current limitations in processing digitized corpora—spanning Old Irish glosses, Middle Welsh poetry, Modern Scottish Gaelic speech, and reconstructed Proto-Celtic forms—require scalable computational methods to analyze phonological shifts, morphosyntactic patterns, and lexical borrowing across time and space. The project proposes a multi-modal approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), phylogenetic modeling, and corpus linguistics to (1) automate the alignment of diachronic textual data, (2) simulate language contact scenarios using agent-based models, and (3) train neural architectures for low-resource machine translation between modern Celtic languages. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of fragmented manuscript data, Bayesian inference of language divergence timelines, and comparative analysis of regional dialects (e.g., Munster vs. Connacht Irish; Breton’s Vannetais variety). Expected outcomes include a unified digital repository of annotated Celtic language corpora, probabilistic reconstructions of unattested proto-language features, and open-source tools for dialect classification. These results will advance philological research on Celtic literary traditions, inform language revitalization initiatives, and refine theoretical frameworks for minority language preservation in computational contexts. By addressing scalability constraints in handling non-standard orthographies and sparse data, this work will also contribute methodological innovations to computational historical linguistics broadly.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by the Celtic peoples of the British Isles, Continental Europe, and Asia Minor, including, but not limited to, modern languages such as Irish, Scots Gaelic, Welsh, and Breton; and extinct or revived languages such as Cornish, Manx, Galatian, and others. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and assembly processes of prefabricated metal structures, addressing inefficiencies in current industry practices that rely on generalized codes and manual trial-and-error methods. Metal building systems must balance structural integrity, material efficiency, and compliance with evolving safety regulations, yet existing approaches often fail to account for dynamic environmental loads, localized material variability, and complex interactions between prefabricated components. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale modeling strategy leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate structural responses to combined wind, seismic, and thermal loads across diverse building configurations, while discrete element modeling (DEM) will assess assembly-stage behaviors such as bolt slippage and panel-to-frame interactions. Machine learning models trained on HPC-generated datasets will identify optimal component geometries and assembly sequences, reducing material waste and labor costs. The computational workflow will integrate probabilistic methods to quantify uncertainties in material properties and fabrication tolerances, ensuring robustness against real-world variability. By coupling these approaches, the project aims to establish predictive guidelines for code-compliant designs that minimize steel usage without compromising safety margins. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for vocational training programs, enabling students to virtually test assembly scenarios and analyze code-driven design tradeoffs. The resource-intensive nature of parametric studies—requiring thousands of parallelized simulations to map performance across design spaces—necessitates HPC capabilities. Successful implementation will advance metal construction sustainability while bridging gaps between academic instruction and industry computational practices, equipping graduates with data-driven problem-solving skills aligned with modernized building standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to construct industrial, storage, and commercial metal structures using prefabricated framing and siding components. Includes instruction in sheet metal working, ironworking, assembly and fastening techniques, blueprint reading, site preparation, structural design principles, safety, and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven computational framework to enhance the precision and diagnostic utility of ultrasound imaging by addressing variability in sonographer technique and image interpretation. Despite the widespread use of diagnostic medical sonography, inconsistencies in transducer manipulation, anatomical structure identification, and real-time decision-making during scans contribute to interoperator variability, which can impact diagnostic accuracy. To mitigate this, we propose a multi-modal machine learning approach that integrates live ultrasound video feeds, biomechanical modeling of transducer pressure and motion, and patient-specific anatomical data to generate adaptive guidance for sonographers during examinations. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on a curated dataset of 3D/4D ultrasound sequences paired with synchronized transducer kinematics from diverse clinical scenarios (e.g., cardiac, abdominal, and musculoskeletal imaging). Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model soft tissue deformation under varying transducer pressures, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize scan protocols based on real-time feedback. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for quantitative assessment of sonographer technique, AI-generated quality metrics for ultrasound image sequences, and personalized pressure-motion profiles to improve visualization of challenging anatomical targets. By establishing computational standards for ultrasound acquisition quality, this work aims to reduce diagnostic uncertainties in borderline cases and enhance training paradigms for emerging sonography technologies, including portable and point-of-care systems. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-frame-rate ultrasound video streams (>10 GB/exam), running parallelized tissue deformation simulations, and enabling federated learning across multiple institutions while maintaining patient data privacy.
cip_title: Diagnostic Medical Sonography/ Sonographer and Ultrasound Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to utilize medical ultrasound techniques to gather sonographic data used to diagnose a variety of conditions and diseases. Includes instruction in obtaining, reviewing, and integrating patient histories and data; patient instruction and care; anatomic, physiologic and pathologic data recording; sonographic data processing; sonography equipment operation; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic and high-consequence livestock diseases present complex challenges to global food security, animal welfare, and public health. Current limitations in predicting disease dynamics arise from the need to integrate multi-scale data—including genomic, environmental, and socio-economic factors—while accounting for uncertainties in transmission pathways and host-pathogen interactions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework to simulate disease spread across heterogeneous animal populations and evaluate targeted intervention strategies. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize models using geospatial livestock density data, metagenomic sequences of priority pathogens (e.g., avian influenza viruses, antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella), and contact network analyses derived from animal movement records. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks, will be applied to identify critical control points in disease transmission chains and optimize resource allocation for vaccination, surveillance, or biosecurity measures. Sensitivity analyses will assess how climate variability and anthropogenic land-use changes modulate outbreak risks. The project will also generate open-access predictive tools to support real-time decision-making for veterinary public health practitioners. By enabling large-scale ensemble simulations and probabilistic risk assessments, this work aims to reduce the economic burden of livestock epidemics and mitigate zoonotic spillover events. Outcomes will directly inform national animal disease preparedness plans and provide a training resource for epidemiology students to engage with advanced computational methodologies. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the iterative model calibration, parallel processing of multi-terabyte genomic datasets, and spatially explicit scenario analyses required for robust, evidence-based veterinary policy development.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, and Public Health
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the prevention and control of communicable animal diseases, diseases affecting humans, and prepares veterinarians to function as public health specialists. Includes instruction in animal epidemiology, biostatistics, food safety and quality assurance, food toxicology, zoonotic and infectious diseases, disease vectors and transference, production medicine, animal health, veterinary public health practice, and inspection and evaluation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of religious syncretism and ideological adaptation across historically interconnected faith communities through computational analysis of textual, ethnographic, and historical datasets. The central research problem revolves around identifying patterns of doctrinal exchange, semantic evolution in sacred texts, and sociopolitical factors influencing religious hybridity—questions traditionally limited by manual analysis of sparse or fragmented sources. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose a multi-modal approach combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling (ABM), and network analysis. NLP pipelines will process multilingual corpora spanning early Christian, Islamic, and Zoroastrian texts to detect conceptual overlaps and terminological shifts, while ABM simulations will test hypotheses about how environmental pressures and social networks shape theological innovation. Network graphs will map historical interfaith contact zones against doctrinal borrowing events, incorporating geospatial and temporal metadata. The computational scale required—processing over 50,000 pages of digitized manuscripts, simulating populations of 10^5 agents with culturally parameterized belief systems, and analyzing multiplex networks across 15 centuries—necessitates parallelized workflows and large-memory nodes. Anticipated outcomes include a quantitative framework for modeling religious change, identification of understudied syncretic pathways in Near Eastern traditions, and open-access tools for computational religious studies. This work aims to advance phenomenological approaches to belief systems by integrating hermeneutic analysis with data-driven methods, offering new insights into the adaptive mechanisms of religious traditions in pluralistic societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature of religious belief and specific religious and quasi-religious systems. Includes instruction in phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature and art of religion; mythology; scriptural and textual studies; religious history and politics; and specific studies of particular faith communities and their behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical computational bottlenecks in law enforcement intelligence analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the scalability and precision of cross-jurisdictional crime pattern detection. Law enforcement agencies increasingly rely on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including digital transaction records, geospatial surveillance inputs, unstructured social media data, and encrypted communications—to identify emerging threats. However, existing analytical tools struggle to process these multimodal datasets efficiently, particularly when analyzing real-time or near-real-time information across large geographic regions. The research problem centers on developing adaptive computational workflows that automate the fusion of structured and unstructured data while maintaining chain-of-custody integrity and compliance with legal constraints. The proposed methodology combines natural language processing for entity extraction from incident reports, graph neural networks for dynamic link analysis across decentralized datasets, and privacy-preserving federated learning techniques to enable secure multi-agency collaboration. HPC resources will be critical for training models on synthetic datasets replicating jurisdictional data silos, optimizing distributed computing architectures for time-sensitive queries, and stress-testing scalability using petabyte-scale simulations of metropolitan-area crime networks. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for ethical large-scale intelligence correlation, validated through partnerships with regional task forces, that reduces false positive rates in threat detection by ≥40% compared to conventional methods. The project further aims to establish computational benchmarks for processing encrypted multimedia evidence without decryption, addressing both technical and legal challenges in modern digital forensics. By bridging gaps between computational scalability and domain-specific operational requirements, this work will provide law enforcement agencies with tools to prioritize actionable intelligence while maintaining constitutional safeguards.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the preparation of law enforcement personnel to perform intelligence and surveillance operations and to analyze and use data collected via such operations. Includes instruction in the intelligence cycle, information sources, data retrieval, digital investigation, financial investigations, document analysis, external sources, geographic information systems, link analysis, operation planning and security, case management, applicable law and regulations, and case preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze patterns of textual transmission and intertextuality across ancient Near Eastern legal and ritual texts, with a focus on their influence on the compositional frameworks of biblical law codes (e.g., Exodus 20–23, Deuteronomy 12–26). While biblical studies has traditionally relied on philological and comparative methods, the scale and complexity of extant cuneiform and early alphabetic corpora—spanning over 3,000 texts from Mesopotamia, Ugarit, and Egypt—require computational approaches to identify subtle linguistic, structural, and thematic parallels. The research problem centers on quantifying the degree to which biblical legal materials reflect adaptive reuse of prior traditions versus innovative theological-ethical formulations, a question complicated by fragmentary evidence and subjective interpretive practices. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for morphologically rich Semitic languages, we will apply transformer-based models fine-tuned on aligned bilingual corpora to detect syntactic and semantic correspondences. Graph network analysis will map citation-like relationships between legal clauses, while phylogenetic algorithms adapted from bioinformatics will model textual evolution across cultural boundaries. The HPC environment is critical for training custom word embeddings, processing high-resolution 3D scans of damaged tablets via computer vision-assisted transcription, and running Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic dependencies between texts. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated parallel texts, a computational typology of legal reuse strategies, and quantitative frameworks to contextualize biblical law within broader ancient Near Eastern jurisprudence. By bridging computational humanities and comparative religion, this project aims to establish reproducible methods for analyzing cultural transmission in fragmentary textual traditions while offering new insights into the compositional history of biblical literature.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Christian and/or Jewish Bible and related literature, with an emphasis on understanding and interpreting the theological, doctrinal, and ethical messages contained therein. May include preparation for applying these studies in various religious vocations.

abstract: The installation and structural performance of transparent building materials, such as glass and plexiglass, present unique challenges in modern architectural design, particularly as demand grows for larger, more complex glazing systems in energy-efficient structures. Traditional empirical methods for evaluating stress distribution, thermal behavior, and failure modes in these materials are limited in scalability and precision, especially when applied to non-standard geometries or dynamic environmental conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate the mechanical and thermal performance of advanced glazing systems under real-world operational stresses. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate multi-physics interactions—including wind loading, thermal expansion, and impact resistance—across diverse architectural configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve these computationally intensive models at scale, enabling parametric studies of material thickness, joint design, and anchoring systems across millions of mesh elements. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize installation parameters by training on simulation-derived datasets, reducing trial-and-error in field applications. The outcomes will include predictive frameworks for identifying failure-prone glazing designs, data-driven guidelines for retrofit projects in aging buildings, and open-access simulation tools tailored for vocational training programs. By bridging computational engineering with glazier trade practices, this work aims to enhance the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of transparent building enclosures while informing updates to industry codes and standards. The requested computing resources will support parallelized simulations across 500+ cores, reducing runtime for iterative design optimization from weeks to days, and enabling the processing of hyperspectral thermal imaging data collected from field validation studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair fixtures, sheets, windows, and skylights made of glass, plexiglass, and other transparent materials. Includes instruction in site measurement, job analysis and estimation, material cutting and trimming, window and door installation, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling complex, nonlinear interactions between human cultural dynamics and ecological systems to improve predictive accuracy in environmental management. Traditional ecological models often overlook localized socio-cultural factors—such as community resource-use practices, informal governance structures, or culturally mediated responses to policy—that significantly influence ecosystem outcomes. We propose an interdisciplinary framework integrating ecological sensor data, ethnographic surveys, and social media analytics to quantify these interactions at scale. The research will develop a hybrid computational architecture combining agent-based modeling (ABM), graph neural networks (GNNs), and Bayesian hierarchical models to capture feedback loops between cultural behaviors (e.g., seasonal harvesting traditions) and biophysical processes (e.g., species population dynamics). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) parallelized ABM simulations of human-environment interactions across diverse cultural and ecological scenarios; (2) training GNNs on heterogeneous data streams (10+ TB of spatiotemporal ecological data paired with socio-cultural indicators); and (3) global sensitivity analyses to identify leverage points for culturally informed conservation strategies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible library of adaptable cultural-ecological modules for environmental modeling and novel metrics quantifying "cultural resonance" in policy effectiveness. This work bridges anthropology, conservation biology, and computational social science, offering a template for embedding human complexity into sustainability science while advancing scalable methods for multimodal data integration. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes will enable parameter exploration at resolutions necessary to inform UNESCO Biosphere Reserve management protocols, with direct applications to 15 partnered Indigenous-led conservation initiatives.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data analytics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in practical nursing and patient care through the development of predictive computational models to optimize clinical decision-making. Nursing professionals often face high-stakes scenarios requiring rapid, data-informed interventions, yet existing tools for predicting patient deterioration, readmission risks, or adverse events remain limited in accuracy and scalability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this research will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), real-time vital sign streams, and longitudinal patient demographic data. The computational approach will integrate ensemble learning techniques and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model temporal patterns in patient data, enabling early identification of at-risk individuals. Parallel processing capabilities will be utilized to train models across multi-dimensional datasets, including unstructured clinical notes and sensor data from wearable devices, while ensuring robustness through cross-validation and sensitivity analyses. The project will also simulate patient care scenarios to evaluate how predictive insights can be operationalized in vocational nursing workflows. Expected outcomes include deployable risk-stratification tools that empower nursing staff to prioritize interventions, reduce preventable complications, and improve resource allocation in acute and long-term care settings. By bridging data science and nursing practice, this work aims to advance evidence-based care protocols and inform curriculum updates for nursing education programs. The scale and complexity of multimodal health data necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve computationally intensive model training, hyperparameter optimization, and real-time inference testing. Successful implementation will demonstrate the transformative potential of integrating computational analytics into nursing workflows, ultimately enhancing patient outcomes and supporting healthcare system efficiency.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized engagement strategies in digital children’s and youth library services, addressing the challenge of effectively tailoring resources to diverse developmental needs and interaction patterns. While libraries increasingly adopt digital tools, there is a critical gap in data-driven methods to dynamically adapt content, interfaces, and recommendations for young users, particularly for neurodiverse populations and multilingual learners. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets—including anonymized interaction logs, voice queries, gesture inputs, and digital artifact creation patterns—from library platforms serving youth aged 3–18. Computational methods will combine graph neural networks to map resource connectivity, transformer-based models for natural language and visual processing, and agent-based simulations to test engagement scenarios. Key challenges include ethical AI design to prioritize privacy-preserving techniques, real-time adaptation to developmental stages, and cross-cultural accessibility modeling. The project will produce open-source tools for librarians to simulate service outcomes, predict resource demand cycles, and generate inclusive engagement templates. Anticipated outcomes include evidence-based frameworks for adaptive digital library design, benchmarks for equitable AI in youth services, and scalable models for hybrid (physical/digital) programming. By integrating computational social science with library practice, this work aims to advance the capacity of youth-focused libraries to serve as inclusive, adaptive learning ecosystems in rapidly evolving digital landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide library and information services and programming for children and young adults. Includes instruction in information needs of children and young adults, resources and services for children and young adults, literature for youth, storytelling, multi-ethnic materials, library management, and information technology for librarians.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing digital printing workflows by modeling the interactions between variable substrate materials, dynamic ink deposition, and equipment performance. The graphic and printing industry faces growing demands for high-throughput, customizable production, yet traditional trial-and-error approaches to process calibration remain resource-intensive and environmentally costly. Current research lacks robust predictive tools to account for the nonlinear behavior of hybrid printing systems, particularly when integrating sustainable substrates or adaptive color management protocols. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Finite element analysis will model mechanical stress distributions in novel biodegradable substrates during high-speed printing, while computational fluid dynamics simulations will characterize ink transfer dynamics across diverse nozzle geometries and rheological profiles. Machine learning models trained on experimental datasets will predict color consistency under variable humidity and temperature conditions, with reinforcement learning algorithms iteratively optimizing press configurations. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of high-resolution 3D substrate meshes (10⁶–10⁷ elements) and real-time analysis of multi-spectral imaging data streams. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support system for predictive maintenance scheduling and substrate-ink pairing recommendations, validated through physical trials on industrial-grade equipment. By reducing material waste through virtual prototyping and enabling energy-efficient process parameter optimization, this research directly supports the graphic communications industry’s transition toward sustainable manufacturing practices. The project will also generate open-access educational modules demonstrating computational modeling applications in press operations, enhancing workforce training in emerging digital workflow strategies. Resource requests emphasize GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and high-memory nodes for handling large-scale spectral datasets, with an estimated 200,000 core-hours required for initial model development and validation phases.
cip_title: Graphic and Printing Equipment Operator, General Production
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, prepare, and execute a variety of commercial and industrial graphic communications jobs. Includes instruction in the operation and maintenance of mechanical, electronic, and digital graphic, printing, and finishing equipment; and related processes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing defect detection and safety assurance in advanced manufacturing systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current quality control methods in industrial settings often rely on manual inspections or traditional statistical process control, which struggle to handle the complexity, scale, and real-time demands of modern production lines. This research addresses the critical need for adaptive, automated systems capable of identifying subtle defects and predicting safety risks in heterogeneous manufacturing environments. The proposed approach integrates multi-modal sensor data—including high-resolution imaging, thermal signatures, and vibration metrics—with physics-informed machine learning models to detect anomalies and forecast system failures. Computational workflows will leverage distributed deep learning architectures for real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, coupled with finite element simulations to model stress propagation and material fatigue in critical components. HPC resources are essential to train ensemble models on diverse defect scenarios, optimize hyperparameters via large-scale grid searches, and simulate failure modes under varying operational conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source software toolkit for adaptive quality control, validated against experimental data from collaborating manufacturing partners, and a predictive safety dashboard for operational risk mitigation. This work will advance the integration of computational modeling and sensor-driven analytics in industrial safety systems, with potential applications in aerospace, automotive, and medical device manufacturing. By reducing false positives in defect detection and improving failure prediction accuracy, the project aims to lower production waste, enhance worker safety, and inform revised industry standards for AI-assisted quality assurance. The requested computing resources will enable iterative model refinement at scales impractical on local clusters, directly supporting the development of robust, generalizable solutions for next-generation manufacturing challenges.
cip_title: Quality Control and Safety Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in quality control and safety technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias present a significant clinical challenge due to their complex mechanisms and variable patient-specific manifestations. Current approaches to predicting arrhythmia susceptibility and optimizing therapies, such as catheter ablation, often rely on generalized anatomical or electrical models that inadequately capture individual variability in cardiac structure, tissue heterogeneity, and dynamic electrophysiological behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific computational models of cardiac electrophysiology to predict arrhythmia dynamics and guide precision therapies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support large-scale simulations of heart rhythm disorders, integrating high-resolution imaging data (e.g., cardiac MRI or CT), intracardiac electroanatomic mapping, and biophysically detailed cellular models. The computational workflow will involve finite element modeling of myocardial geometry, parameterization of ion channel kinetics and fibrosis distribution from clinical data, and simulation of arrhythmia initiation/perpetuation using monodomain reaction-diffusion equations. Machine learning methods will be applied to analyze simulation outputs and identify predictive biomarkers of arrhythmia recurrence or treatment success. The project will leverage parallel computing to perform sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces and conduct population-scale simulations to evaluate phenotypic variability. Expected outcomes include the creation of validated, open-source tools for patient-specific arrhythmia modeling, optimized criteria for selecting ablation targets in atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, and novel mechanistic insights into how fibrosis patterns or genetic channelopathies modulate arrhythmia risk. This work has direct translational significance, with potential to improve procedural outcomes, reduce healthcare costs from repeat interventions, and advance personalized management strategies in clinical electrophysiology. The scale of data processing, iterative model optimization, and multi-dimensional simulations necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for feasible computation times, enabling clinically relevant discovery within a research timeline.
cip_definition: Research focused on, within the subspecialty of cardiovascular disease, which prepares physicians in intricate technical procedures to evaluate heart rhythms and determine appropriate treatment.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze evolving narrative structures, thematic patterns, and representations of identity in anglophone children’s and adolescent literature across the 20th and 21st centuries. While qualitative studies of individual texts or authors dominate the field, large-scale computational analysis remains underutilized, limiting scholars’ ability to trace macro-level trends in genre development, cultural values, and audience engagement. This project will apply natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to a curated corpus of over 50,000 primary texts, including novels, picture books, and award-winning titles, alongside paratextual data (reviews, publisher catalogs). Computational methods will identify shifts in linguistic complexity, recurring motif clusters, and demographic representation patterns across age categories, historical periods, and geographic regions. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models to classify genre hybrids (e.g., eco-fiction, verse novels) and to map semantic networks connecting character archetypes, plot devices, and moral frameworks. Additionally, GPU-accelerated text mining will enable sentiment analysis of protagonist agency and emotional tonality at scale, addressing gaps in scholarship regarding evolving depictions of childhood adversity. Outcomes will include an open-access annotated dataset, visualizations of thematic evolution, and statistical models linking literary trends to educational policies and publishing industry data. By bridging computational literary studies with youth literature research, this project aims to inform inclusive curriculum design, library collection practices, and evidence-based discussions about canon formation. The requested resources will support processing multi-terabyte text corpora, running parallelized semantic analyses, and iteratively refining classification algorithms to account for the unique linguistic and narrative conventions of literature for young audiences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scholarly study of children's and adolescent literature and that may enhance the professional work of teachers, librarians, publishers, booksellers, and creative writers. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, studies of various types of literary text, book artists, and children's films.

abstract: Financial crime and fraud networks have grown increasingly sophisticated, leveraging complex transactions, multi-jurisdictional operations, and encrypted communication channels to evade detection. Traditional forensic accounting methods struggle to analyze the scale and interconnectedness of modern financial data, particularly when addressing fraud schemes involving cryptocurrency, shell companies, or transnational money laundering. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for large-scale financial network analysis to identify hidden fraud patterns, trace illicit asset flows, and model evolving money laundering tactics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process heterogeneous datasets—including banking transaction records, corporate ownership graphs, blockchain ledgers, and unstructured communications—using a hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP), temporal graph analytics, and anomaly detection algorithms. Computational methods will include transformer-based NLP models to extract entities and relationships from financial documents, dynamic network analysis to map asset concealment pathways, and deep learning architectures trained on historical fraud cases to predict emerging risk patterns. HPC capabilities will enable iterative simulation of money laundering networks under varying regulatory scenarios, as well as real-time analysis of terabyte-scale financial datasets. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for forensic investigators to reconstruct complex fraud schemes, quantify concealed asset networks, and prioritize high-risk transactions. This research will advance computational forensics by addressing critical gaps in processing speed, multi-modal data integration, and adaptive pattern recognition—directly supporting homeland security objectives to disrupt terrorist financing and organized financial crime. The developed models and workflows will be validated against active investigations in partnership with regulatory agencies, with open-source components shared to strengthen public-sector forensic capabilities.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of conducting investigations into financial crime, terrorist activity, and the analysis and use of accounting data as evidence. Includes instruction in the principles of accounting, investigative auditing, computer investigations, accounting system documents and software, business corruption, criminal and terrorist financial networks, international money markets and movement, net worth analysis, financial fraud, exposing concealed assets, records seizure, fraud and money laundering statutes, fraud case initiation, case management, and case presentation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of turbulent transport and instability mechanisms in magnetically confined high-temperature plasmas, with direct applications to optimizing magnetic confinement fusion devices. A persistent challenge in plasma physics is the accurate prediction of anomalous energy and particle losses caused by microturbulence and large-scale magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities, which degrade confinement and limit reactor efficiency. Current fluid-based models often fail to capture critical kinetic effects, while fully kinetic simulations remain prohibitively expensive for reactor-relevant scales. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational approach combining gyrokinetic theory, nonlinear MHD simulations, and data-driven reduced-order modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be leveraged to perform high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations using a hybrid Particle-in-Cell (PIC) and spectral code, resolving both ion-gyroscale turbulence and macroscopic MHD modes within a unified framework. The simulations will incorporate realistic magnetic geometries, collisional effects, and boundary conditions representative of tokamak plasmas. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate the identification of instability thresholds and turbulence saturation mechanisms from petabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include improved predictive models for heat flux profiles under varying magnetic configurations, quantitative criteria for suppressing edge-localized modes (ELMs), and optimized turbulence control strategies via resonant magnetic perturbations. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation fusion devices, reducing computational uncertainties in plasma confinement predictions. The requested HPC allocation will enable unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution in coupled MHD-gyrokinetic simulations, overcoming memory and scalability limitations of current workflows. Resultant datasets and open-source simulation tools will be disseminated to the plasma physics community, fostering collaborative advances in fusion energy research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of properties and behavior of matter at high temperatures, such that molecular and atomic structures are in a disassociated ionic or electronic state. Includes instruction in magnetohydrodynamics, free electron phenomena, fusion theory, electromagnetic fields and dynamics, plasma and non-linear wave theory, instability theory, plasma shock phenomena, quantitative modeling, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize mineral liberation processes during comminution, addressing inefficiencies in energy consumption and resource recovery in mineral processing systems. Current empirical models for predicting particle fracture dynamics in crushers and grinding mills lack the resolution to account for heterogeneous ore textures, mineralogical interfaces, and micro-crack propagation—factors critical to minimizing overgrinding and maximizing liberation efficiency. We propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating discrete element method (DEM) for granular flow, finite element analysis (FEA) for particle-scale stress modeling, and machine learning (ML) to bridge microstructural data with macro-scale operational parameters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the coupled physics across 10^6–10^8 particles in industrial-scale mill simulations, requiring parallelized solvers and GPU-accelerated workloads. The computational workflow will leverage open-source codes (e.g., LAMMPS, MFEM) augmented by custom ML models trained on 3D X-ray CT datasets of ore samples to predict fracture pathways. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework capable of optimizing mill rotational speeds, feed rates, and liner designs for specific ore types, targeting a 15–20% reduction in specific energy consumption while maintaining target liberation grades. The resource request supports GPU node allocations for DEM-FEA coupling and CPU-heavy batches for Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification across mineralogical datasets. This work aligns with global efforts to decarbonize mining operations and advances computational granular mechanics in mineral systems, with open-source toolkits to be disseminated to the mining engineering community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of mineral extraction, processing and refining systems, including open pit and shaft mines, prospecting and site analysis equipment and instruments, environmental and safety systems, mine equipment and facilities, mineral processing and refining methods and systems, and logistics and communications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic logistics networks for multi-modal transportation systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations, addressing inefficiencies in resource allocation under real-world uncertainties. Current models struggle to integrate variable factors such as fluctuating demand, traffic disruptions, and environmental constraints at scale, leading to suboptimal routing, energy waste, and delayed deliveries. We propose developing a hybrid computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to analyze interactions between freight carriers, infrastructure nodes, and environmental conditions. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of large-scale networks, incorporating real-time data streams on weather, traffic, and commodity flows. Reinforcement learning algorithms will train decision-making agents to balance cost, emissions, and delivery deadlines, while graph-based optimization methods will iteratively refine routing and load distribution strategies. Key deliverables include a scalable digital twin of regional freight networks and adaptive algorithms for real-time resource allocation. Expected outcomes include a 15-30% reduction in empty cargo miles and a 10-20% decrease in fuel consumption across simulated scenarios, with validation against case studies from port logistics and intermodal hubs. By quantifying trade-offs between economic and sustainability metrics, this work aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers and logistics operators. The computational demand—terabyte-scale datasets, millions of agent interactions per simulation, and hyperparameter tuning for machine learning models—necessitates GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Results will advance adaptive logistics planning and inform infrastructure investment strategies in rapidly urbanizing regions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in transportation and materials moving, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in patent law through the development of a computational framework for analyzing patent validity and litigation trends. The exponential growth of patent filings, coupled with the increasing complexity of technical disclosures and prior art, has strained traditional legal analysis methods. Current tools for patent examination and litigation risk assessment lack the capacity to efficiently process large-scale, unstructured datasets spanning global patent databases, legal texts, and technical literature.
