This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution, agent-based forest resilience simulation framework. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model forest dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes at unprecedented scales, incorporating variables such as species composition, soil moisture gradients, historical disturbance patterns, and projected climate scenarios. Computational workflows will integrate remote sensing data (LiDAR, multispectral imagery), field-collected forest inventory datasets, and machine learning algorithms to parameterize individual tree agents and simulate interactions across millions of agents over decadal timescales. Key objectives include quantifying tipping points in ecosystem stability, identifying silvicultural strategies that optimize carbon sequestration and biodiversity, and forecasting post-disturbance recovery trajectories under varying management interventions. The HPC environment is critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of ecological processes, enabling parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess uncertainty, and processing petabyte-scale geospatial inputs. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive forest management, empirically validated risk maps for regional stakeholders, and policy-relevant insights into climate resilience trade-offs. By bridging computational ecology and operational forestry, this work will provide a replicable framework for data-driven decision-making in forest technology, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance resource management through innovation. Results will be disseminated via partnerships with state forestry agencies and integrated into curricular modules on computational natural resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist foresters in the management and production of forest resources. Includes instruction in woods and field skills, tree identification, timber measurement, logging and timber harvesting, forest propagation and regeneration, forest fire-fighting, resource management, equipment operation and maintenance, record-keeping, sales and purchasing operations, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern printing press operations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize press setup, material usage, and operational workflows. Traditional methods for calibrating printing presses—such as adjusting ink viscosity, pressure, and substrate alignment—often rely on iterative manual testing, leading to material waste, prolonged downtime, and inconsistent output quality. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate and refine these processes computationally, reducing reliance on physical trials. By integrating sensor data from press operations with material science parameters, the project aims to create a dynamic framework for real-time decision support in press configuration. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) to model ink dispersion across substrates under variable press conditions, machine learning algorithms trained on historical press performance data to predict optimal settings, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in operational outcomes. HPC resources are critical for handling large datasets from press sensors, running parallelized simulations, and iterating complex models efficiently. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital toolset for operators to minimize waste (e.g., paper, ink) and energy consumption while maintaining print quality. The project also aims to establish correlations between substrate properties and press parameters, enabling adaptive workflows for diverse materials. By bridging computational modeling with hands-on press operations, this work will advance technical training in communication and journalism fields, providing operators with data-driven strategies to enhance productivity and sustainability in print media production. Results will be disseminated through industry partnerships and integrated into instructional modules, fostering innovation in a traditionally analog discipline.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate, and maintain printing presses.

abstract: Neurologic disorders in pediatric populations, ranging from neonatal encephalopathies to adolescent-onset epilepsy, present complex etiologies and heterogeneous clinical presentations that challenge diagnosis and treatment. Current approaches to understanding these disorders often rely on fragmented analyses of clinical, imaging, or genomic data, limiting the ability to identify integrative biomarkers or predictive models. This project proposes to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multimodal computational framework for analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets in child neurology. The research will focus on integrating neuroimaging (MRI, fMRI), genomic sequencing, electronic health records, and longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 1,200 patients with neurodevelopmental and acquired neurologic disorders. Computational methods will include the development of machine learning pipelines for feature extraction, graph-based neural networks to model disease progression, and Bayesian hierarchical models to account for age-dependent variability in neurodevelopment. Key challenges include processing high-dimensional imaging data, harmonizing disparate data types, and scaling analyses across developmental stages. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of imaging datasets, optimization of deep learning architectures through distributed training, and large-scale simulations to validate statistical models. Expected outcomes include the identification of subtype-specific biomarkers for early-onset epilepsy, predictive models for neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonatal brain injury, and open-source tools for pediatric neurology data integration. This work will directly inform clinical trial design and personalized therapeutic strategies while advancing computational methods for pediatric neuroimaging and multi-omics analysis. The requested resources are critical due to the computational intensity of processing terabytes of imaging data, the need for rapid iteration in model training, and the scalability requirements for population-level analyses in this understudied domain. By bridging clinical child neurology with advanced computational approaches, this project aims to accelerate translational discoveries in pediatric neurologic care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of neurologic disorders of the neonatal period, infancy, early childhood, and adolescence. Requires training in neurology with additional training in child neurology.

abstract: Respiratory care therapy faces critical challenges in optimizing treatment protocols for patients with complex pulmonary conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for individual variability in lung mechanics, disease progression, or response to mechanical ventilation. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity computational framework integrating patient-specific physiological data with multi-scale biomechanical models to simulate respiratory dynamics and predict optimal therapeutic strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large clinical datasets—including electronic health records, imaging data, and real-time ventilator outputs—and perform parallelized simulations of lung mechanics, gas exchange, and ventilator interactions. Computational models will employ finite element analysis to capture regional lung deformation and fluid-structure interactions, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in heterogeneous patient responses. By simulating scenarios such as tidal volume adjustments, positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration, and recruitment maneuvers, the framework aims to generate personalized ventilation strategies that minimize alveolar strain and improve oxygenation. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for clinicians to tailor respiratory interventions, reducing the risk of ventilator-associated complications and enhancing recovery trajectories. The project’s computational demands necessitate HPC resources due to the scale of parameter optimization, real-time data assimilation, and the need for ensemble simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts. This work will advance respiratory care by bridging clinical practice with computational precision medicine, ultimately contributing to evidence-based protocols that address gaps in current therapeutic decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: The study of complex reaction mechanisms in catalytic systems presents significant challenges due to the interplay of dynamic electronic and structural factors that govern reactivity. Traditional experimental techniques often struggle to resolve transient intermediates or quantify subtle energy barriers, particularly in multi-step processes involving open-shell species or solvent effects. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale quantum chemical simulations of industrially relevant homogeneous catalytic cycles. The research will employ density functional theory (DFT) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to map free energy landscapes, characterize short-lived intermediates, and analyze solvent-solute interactions in iron-catalyzed C–H functionalization reactions. These computational methods require intensive parallelization to handle the explicit solvation models, non-adiabatic transitions, and statistical sampling necessary for convergence. The requested HPC resources will enable the use of multi-reference wavefunction methods to address multi-configurational electronic states in key transition metal intermediates, a critical capability beyond standard DFT approaches. Expected outcomes include the identification of rate-determining factors in catalytic selectivity, the prediction of solvent effects on reaction trajectories, and the development of generalized protocols for simulating spin-crossover events in solution-phase organometallic systems. This work will provide atomistic insights into tuning catalyst efficiency, directly supporting experimental collaborators in synthesizing improved catalytic architectures. By establishing scalable computational workflows for modeling dynamic catalytic systems, the project aims to advance predictive capabilities in reaction design while contributing open-access tools for the computational chemistry community.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of matter, including its micro- and macro-structure, the processes of chemical change, and the theoretical description and laboratory simulation of these phenomena.

abstract: Statistical inference in complex, high-dimensional models remains a fundamental challenge in modern statistics, particularly when analyzing large-scale datasets with intricate dependence structures. This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian nonparametric methods for high-dimensional inference under model misspecification, with applications to multi-source biomedical data integration. Traditional Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms become computationally prohibitive in such settings due to slow mixing, high memory demands, and costly likelihood evaluations. We propose to implement and benchmark hybrid sampling strategies that combine Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics, and variational inference frameworks. These methods will be optimized for distributed-memory architectures using MPI-based parallelism to enable efficient exploration of posterior distributions with >10^5 parameters. Key computational challenges include designing adaptive preconditioning schemes for gradient-based samplers, developing sparse approximation techniques for Gaussian process priors, and implementing fault-tolerant checkpointing for long-running chains. The project will leverage existing genomic and neuroimaging datasets from collaborative studies on Alzheimer’s disease progression, where joint modeling of longitudinal cognitive scores, MRI-derived biomarkers, and high-dimensional proteomics requires novel statistical approaches. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for large-scale Bayesian computation using PyMC and Julia-based custom kernels, (2) theoretical guarantees on sampler convergence rates in misspecified models, and (3) clinically interpretable models of neurodegenerative disease trajectories with uncertainty quantification. The requested high-performance computing resources—particularly GPU nodes and high-memory CPU partitions—are essential for benchmarking methodological innovations against state-of-the-art alternatives at biologically relevant data scales. This work will advance statistical computing infrastructure while addressing critical gaps in modeling complex biomedical processes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mathematics and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of phytochemical interactions in multi-herb formulations, a cornerstone of traditional herbal medicine systems. Despite the widespread use of polyherbal therapies in clinical herbalism, the molecular mechanisms underlying their synergistic or antagonistic effects remain poorly characterized due to the combinatorial complexity of bioactive compounds. Current research is constrained by limited computational capacity to model interactions across large phytochemical datasets or simulate dynamic biological responses. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline integrating cheminformatics, molecular docking, and machine learning to analyze multi-herb interactions at scale. The project will curate a repository of phytochemical structures from ethnobotanical databases, cross-referenced with pharmacological and ethnomedical annotations. Molecular dynamics simulations will model compound-target interactions for human proteins implicated in inflammation, immune response, and metabolic regulation, while deep learning architectures will predict herb-herb synergies and contraindications. HPC resources are critical for managing the high-throughput screening of ~10,000 phytochemical permutations, parallelized docking simulations, and training predictive models on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database of predicted herb interaction networks, (2) validated computational frameworks for optimizing traditional formulations, and (3) toxicity risk assessments for common herbal combinations. This work will provide empirical support for evidence-based herbal practice, bridging traditional knowledge systems with modern computational biology. By elucidating the systems-level behavior of complex herbal therapies, the project aims to enhance clinical decision-making, inform regulatory standards, and foster innovation in personalized phytotherapy protocols. The requested computing resources will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling herbal pharmacodynamics, directly addressing a critical bottleneck in contemporary herbal medicine research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to utilize the materia medica and clinical practices of Western, Native American, African, Australasian, and other herbal medicine traditions to prevent and cure illness and temporary physical disorders. Includes instruction in basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; nutrition; terminology and materia medica; therapeutic herbalism; herbal pharmacy; botanicals and ethnobotany; wildcrafting and harvesting; labeling and dispensing phytotherapy; counterindications; practice management; consultation skills; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-resourced African languages by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model linguistic structures and oral literatures at scale. Despite the rich diversity of African languages—encompassing over 2,000 distinct languages across major phyla such as Niger-Congo, Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan—many remain under-documented and under-analyzed due to limited computational resources and tools tailored to their unique morphosyntactic, tonal, and discourse features. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks in processing large corpora of oral narratives, dialectal variations, and non-linear morphological systems, which are often incompatible with existing natural language processing (NLP) frameworks optimized for Indo-European languages. To address this, the project will deploy parallelized algorithms on HPC clusters to train machine learning models for automated morphological segmentation, tonal pattern recognition, and cross-dialectal similarity mapping. These models will be trained on curated datasets of annotated texts and audio recordings from languages such as isiZulu (Bantu), Oromo (Cushitic), and !Xun (Khoisan), incorporating both written and oral sources. Additionally, graph-based computational methods will be used to model the structural relationships in oral narratives, enabling the identification of culturally significant motifs and their diffusion across linguistic boundaries. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale simulations of language contact scenarios, shedding light on historical linguistic processes in the Sahel and Great Lakes regions. Expected outcomes include open-access computational tools for African language analysis, a scalable digital repository of annotated oral literatures, and novel insights into the typological diversity of African languages. By advancing computational methods for these understudied languages, the project aims to support revitalization efforts, inform pedagogical frameworks, and contribute to global linguistic theory. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks, such as training transformer-based models on low-resource languages, and for reducing processing times in comparative phylogenetic analyses from months to days.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the African continent, including, but not limited to, Bantu languages, Nilo-Saharan languages, Niger-Congo languages, Khoisan languages, and the Chadic and Ethiopic languages of the Hamito-Semitic language family. Includes instruction in philology, dialects, and oral and written literatures.

abstract: The rapid digitization of visual arts and media ecosystems has created complex challenges in understanding audience engagement, content valuation, and sustainable distribution models at scale. Current arts management practices often rely on limited datasets and qualitative methods, struggling to account for the nonlinear interactions between digital platforms, generative AI art markets, and evolving consumer behavior. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze terabyte-scale datasets from global online art marketplaces, social media platforms, and immersive media installations using high-performance computing resources. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns in cross-cultural aesthetic preferences, while network analysis techniques will map the diffusion pathways of visual trends through digital communities. Agent-based simulations will test resource allocation strategies for hybrid physical-digital exhibitions, incorporating real-time data streams from augmented reality interfaces. The computational architecture will employ parallel processing to handle heterogeneous data types, including 3D asset metadata, blockchain-based provenance records, and eye-tracking datasets from virtual gallery environments. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing exhibition curation cycles, dynamic pricing tools for algorithmically generated art, and risk assessment frameworks for emerging media formats. By establishing quantitative relationships between computational creativity metrics and audience retention rates, this research aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in cultural institutions while preserving artistic innovation. The results will provide arts managers with scalable strategies to navigate decentralized creation ecosystems, address digital preservation challenges, and ethically leverage generative AI in visual culture stewardship. This interdisciplinary approach demonstrates how advanced computing can bridge gaps between data science, design theory, and arts administration in the post-digital era.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Arts, Entertainment, and Media Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage various aspects of the visual arts, performing arts, and entertainment media industries. Includes instruction in business and financial management, marketing and fund-raising, labor relations for the arts, event promotion and management, product and artist management, and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of ethical frameworks and cultural narratives surrounding end-of-life care across diverse historical, literary, and medical datasets. While qualitative scholarship in health humanities has richly documented shifting societal attitudes toward mortality, existing studies are often limited in scale, relying on manual analysis of localized case studies or small corpora. This research addresses the challenge of synthesizing patterns across vast, heterogeneous sources—including digitized medical archives, philosophical texts, patient narratives, and modern social media—to trace how cultural, religious, and ethical discourses intersect with clinical practices over time. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for semantic analysis of historical documents, transformer-based models to identify ethical argument structures in contemporary bioethics literature, and network analysis to map the diffusion of narratives across genres and periods. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models on centuries-spanning textual data, running large-scale sentiment and thematic clustering algorithms, and simulating probabilistic models of discourse evolution. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive visualization platform that highlights temporal and cultural divergences in end-of-life values, as well as computational frameworks adaptable to other topics in medical humanities. By bridging quantitative scalability with humanistic interpretability, this work aims to inform policy debates, clinical ethics training, and public engagement initiatives while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-enabled approaches in health humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that explores the ethical, historical, literary, philosophical, and religious dimensions of medicine or health. Includes instruction in art, cultural studies, economics, ethics, history, literature, medical anthropology, philosophy, religion and spiritual thought, science and technology, visual art, and writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven strategies for optimizing resource allocation and operational efficiency in visual arts organizations. Fine and studio arts institutions—including galleries, museums, and community arts programs—face persistent challenges in balancing financial sustainability, audience engagement, and equitable access to cultural resources. Traditional management approaches often rely on static datasets or qualitative assessments, limiting the ability to model dynamic variables such as visitor behavior, spatial utilization, or the impact of digital outreach campaigns. This research proposes the development of computational models to simulate resource distribution, predict engagement outcomes, and evaluate the efficacy of arts programming under varying constraints. Using anonymized historical data from partner institutions (e.g., attendance records, demographic surveys, and spatial layouts), we will employ agent-based modeling to map visitor flows through physical and virtual exhibition spaces. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns in donor behavior and fundraising campaign performance, while network analysis will model stakeholder interactions within regional arts ecosystems. These methods require HPC capabilities to process high-dimensional datasets, run iterative simulations, and generate real-time visualizations for scenario testing. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for arts administrators to forecast budgetary needs, optimize staffing and facility use, and assess the community impact of programming. By integrating computational rigor with arts management praxis, this project aims to bridge gaps between institutional decision-making and evolving public expectations, fostering resilient, data-informed strategies for cultural sustainability. The results will be disseminated through open-access platforms to support small and mid-sized arts organizations, advancing equity in resource access across the visual arts sector.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage fine and studio art organizations, operations, and facilities. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; public relations and arts advocacy; arts law; and applications to specific arts activities such as galleries, museums, studios, foundations, and community organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms governing symbiotic interactions between eukaryotic hosts and their microbial partners, with a focus on horizontal gene transfer (HGT) dynamics and coevolutionary adaptation. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale genomic datasets and simulating complex evolutionary processes hinder our understanding of how genetic material is exchanged across species boundaries and how such exchanges influence host-microbe symbiosis. We propose to employ high-performance computing resources to conduct comparative genomic analyses across diverse host-symbiont systems, reconstruct phylogenetic networks to trace HGT events, and perform population genetic simulations modeling coevolutionary scenarios. These computational approaches will process terabyte-scale metagenomic and whole-genome sequencing data, utilizing optimized algorithms for alignment, variant calling, and network inference. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained to predict functional outcomes of horizontally acquired genes and identify epigenetic modification patterns associated with symbiotic states. The integration of these methods will enable the identification of conserved genetic modules involved in cross-species interactions, quantification of selection pressures driving HGT, and characterization of epigenetic regulation in maintaining symbiotic relationships. Expected outcomes include a comprehensive framework for analyzing host-microbe genetic crosstalk, novel insights into the role of HGT in shaping eukaryotic genomes, and predictive models of symbiont adaptation under environmental stress. This research will advance fundamental knowledge in microbial and eukaryotic genetics while providing computational tools applicable to studying genetic exchange in natural ecosystems and engineered biological systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of viruses, infectious agents, organelles, nuclear genomes, eubacteria, archaebacteria, and eukaryotic organisms. Includes instruction in molecular genetics and evolution, parasitic and symbiotic interaction at the genetic level, epigenetic phenomena, microbial interactions, and genomics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in German philology and dialectology through large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary German language corpora. The core research problem centers on the dynamic evolution of German dialects and their sociolinguistic interactions, particularly in understudied regional varieties and their adaptation to modern technological contexts. Traditional manual methods for analyzing phonetic, morphological, and syntactic shifts across time and geography are limited in scalability, hindering comprehensive insights into patterns of language change. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to process and analyze multilingual textual datasets spanning 15th-century manuscripts to present-day digital communications. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on dialect-specific corpora to automate phonetic transcription alignment, detecting syntactic innovations in regional vernaculars, and simulating contact-induced language change under varying sociocultural parameters. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s data volume—over 10 TB of digitized texts, audio recordings, and annotated linguistic metadata—and for running computationally intensive tasks such as parallelized corpus comparisons, neural network training, and agent-based simulations of language diffusion. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access dialect maps visualizing linguistic divergence, a publicly available NLP toolkit optimized for historical German variants, and new empirical insights into the resilience of dialects in digital communication platforms. This work will significantly enhance interdisciplinary methodologies in humanities computing, providing tools applicable to language preservation initiatives, educational resource development, and cross-disciplinary studies of language-technology interfaces. By bridging philological scholarship with advanced computational resources, the project aims to redefine the scope of dialectological research while addressing contemporary challenges in multilingual data processing.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the German language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the impact of spatially embedded social dynamics on housing accessibility and equity through computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex interactions between demographic shifts, policy frameworks, and built environments. Despite growing recognition of housing as a critical determinant of human well-being, existing models often oversimplify the interdependencies between socio-cultural preferences, regulatory constraints, and urban morphology. Our research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based model (ABM) that integrates granular demographic data, geospatial layers of housing stock, and dynamic policy scenarios to analyze how emergent behaviors—such as informal cohabitation practices or transient occupancy patterns—affect equitable resource distribution in urban and rural contexts. The computational framework will utilize parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate millions of agent interactions across diverse temporal scales, requiring significant memory allocation and multi-node processing capabilities. A hybrid machine learning pipeline will further analyze simulated outcomes against real-world housing inequity metrics, identifying leverage points for policy intervention. By bridging computational social science with architectural theory, this work aims to produce a novel evidence base for designing adaptive housing systems that respond to non-linear societal challenges, including climate migration and digital nomadism. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation tools for policymakers and a repository of scenario-driven housing equity indices, advancing interdisciplinary discourse at the intersection of human environments, technology, and social justice. This project’s scale and data complexity necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve the resolution required for actionable insights, positioning it as a pioneering effort in computational housing studies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in housing and human environments, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in warehouse operations and maintenance by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex logistical workflows, predict equipment failures, and optimize inventory management. Modern warehousing faces dynamic challenges, including fluctuating demand, equipment downtime, and the need for real-time decision-making, which traditional analytical methods struggle to address due to computational limitations. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate warehouse operations under varying demand scenarios, integrating real-world data on inventory turnover, equipment performance, and labor allocation. Concurrently, machine learning (ML) algorithms will be trained on historical maintenance records and sensor data from forklifts, conveyor systems, and automated storage/retrieval systems to predict equipment failures and recommend preemptive maintenance schedules. A parallel computational framework will optimize inventory routing and storage allocation using mixed-integer linear programming (MILP), balancing spatial constraints, energy consumption, and labor costs. These computational tasks demand HPC resources due to their scale: ABM simulations will model thousands of concurrent agents (e.g., workers, robots, inventory units), while ML training and MILP solvers require distributed computing to handle high-dimensional datasets and complex constraint matrices. Outcomes will include predictive maintenance benchmarks, adaptive inventory routing algorithms, and open-source simulation tools tailored for warehouse technicians. By integrating computational modeling with operational data, this project aims to advance decision-support systems for warehouse personnel, reduce unplanned downtime by up to 30%, and lower storage costs through dynamic spatial optimization. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in warehousing technology programs, bridging gaps between traditional maintenance practices and data-driven operational strategies.
cip_title: Parts and Warehousing Operations and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain inventory control, care for inventory, and make minor repairs to warehouse equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of labor negotiation processes in industries undergoing rapid automation and AI integration. While traditional labor-management frameworks emphasize static variables such as wages and benefits, emerging challenges—such as algorithmic scheduling, gig work platforms, and AI-driven productivity monitoring—introduce complex, dynamic interdependencies that defy conventional analytical methods. The research problem centers on quantifying how these technological shifts alter power asymmetries between workers and employers during collective bargaining, particularly in sectors like logistics, healthcare, and manufacturing. Using agent-based modeling (ABM), we will simulate negotiation scenarios under varying technological, economic, and policy conditions. Computational agents will represent workers, unions, employers, and regulatory bodies, each programmed with adaptive decision-making algorithms informed by real-world labor dispute datasets and behavioral economics principles. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parallel simulations to explore "what-if" scenarios, such as the impact of universal basic income policies on strike behaviors or the role of predictive analytics in preempting grievances. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify emergent patterns in negotiation outcomes, including tipping points for worker mobilization or management concession strategies. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework to forecast labor relations risks in technologically disrupted industries, as well as policy recommendations for balancing innovation with equitable labor practices. By integrating computational social science with industrial relations theory, this project addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital transformation redefines workplace governance. The results will provide stakeholders with evidence-based tools to navigate contentious labor issues in an era of accelerating technological change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on employee-management interactions and the management of issues and disputes regarding working conditions and worker benefit packages, and that may prepare individuals to function as labor or personnel relations specialists. Includes instruction in labor history, policies and strategies of the labor movement, union organization, labor-management negotiation, labor law and contract interpretation, labor economics, welfare and benefit packages, grievance procedures, and labor policy studies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern distributed networks has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource allocation strategies, particularly under dynamic workloads and heterogeneous infrastructure conditions. Traditional network management frameworks often rely on static thresholds or reactive measures, which struggle to balance performance, energy efficiency, and fault tolerance in real time. This project proposes the development of a bio-inspired, self-organizing resource orchestration system designed for large-scale, multi-domain LAN/WAN environments. Leveraging decentralized swarm intelligence algorithms, the system will autonomously optimize computational and bandwidth resources across hybrid cloud-edge architectures while maintaining compliance with organizational service-level agreements. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate network topologies mirroring real-world enterprise deployments, including stochastic traffic patterns, hardware failures, and security incidents. Agent-based modeling will be employed to evaluate emergent behaviors of the proposed algorithms under varying scales (10,000–1,000,000 nodes), with comparative analysis against conventional software-defined networking controllers. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify system resilience against cascading outages, while GPU-accelerated neural networks will predict optimal resource distribution during peak demand scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for proactive anomaly detection, dynamic load redistribution without service interruption, and energy-aware provisioning that reduces idle resource consumption by 30–50% in simulated environments. The research directly addresses the operational challenges of maintaining performance parity during infrastructure upgrades, a persistent pain point in system migration workflows. Successful validation could redefine standards for autonomous network management, particularly for organizations managing distributed computing resources across evolving technological ecosystems.
cip_title: System, Networking, and LAN/ WAN Management/ Manager
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to oversee and regulate the computer system and performance requirements of an entire organization or network of satellite users. Includes instruction in performance balancing; redundancy; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) network management; system migration and upgrading; outage control; problem diagnosis and troubleshooting; and system maintenance, budgeting, and management.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize hemodialysis treatment outcomes by developing a high-resolution computational model of solute transport and fluid dynamics in dialyzers, integrating patient-specific physiological variables to predict and mitigate complications such as intradialytic hypotension. Current dialysis protocols rely on generalized parameters, which often fail to account for dynamic interactions between blood flow, membrane characteristics, and individual patient biochemistry. This limitation contributes to suboptimal toxin clearance and cardiovascular instability during treatment. We propose a multi-scale simulation framework combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with machine learning to analyze how variations in dialyzer fiber geometry, flow rates, and patient biomarkers (e.g., serum albumin levels, hematocrit) influence treatment efficacy. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 3D simulations of blood-dialysate interactions across millions of hollow fibers under physiologically realistic pulsatile flow conditions, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify personalized operational thresholds. The computational pipeline will be validated against clinical data from 200 anonymized dialysis sessions, including real-time pressure measurements and post-treatment lab results. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive model for optimizing dialyzer selection and flow parameters to reduce adverse events, as well as a novel metric for quantifying membrane fouling dynamics that could inform next-generation dialyzer designs. By bridging gaps between biomedical engineering, computational modeling, and renal replacement therapy, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift toward precision hemodialysis—a critical need as patient populations grow increasingly diverse in age, comorbidities, and vascular access viability. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the terabyte-scale datasets and parallelized simulations required to capture these complex biophysical interactions at clinically relevant resolutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer hemodialysis treatments to patients with renal failure under the supervision of a nurse or physician. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, dialysis prescription interpretation, dialysate preparation, extracorporeal circuit and dialyzer set-up and maintenance, equipment monitoring, patient preparation, taking vital signs, documentation and communication, venipuncture and local anesthesia administration, emergency intervention, safety and sanitation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of biomechanical stress in the progression of tendinopathies, a pervasive yet poorly understood class of musculoskeletal disorders. Tendinopathies, characterized by chronic pain and functional impairment, lack targeted therapies due to gaps in understanding how tissue-level mechanical forces interact with cellular signaling pathways to drive pathological remodeling. Traditional experimental models struggle to capture the dynamic, multiscale nature of these interactions, necessitating a computational approach. We propose to develop a multiscale finite element model integrating tissue-scale biomechanics with agent-based simulations of tenocyte behavior under varying load conditions. The model will incorporate empirical data from transcriptomic profiling of human tendon samples and high-resolution imaging of collagen fiber deformation patterns. HPC resources will enable parameter optimization across millions of simulated load cycles, coupled with machine learning-driven analysis of emergent patterns in extracellular matrix degradation and inflammatory signaling. Expected outcomes include identification of critical mechanical thresholds for pathological transitions and predictive biomarkers for early intervention. By bridging biomechanics, cell biology, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish a framework for mechanistically informed therapies, reducing reliance on palliative treatments. The computational pipeline developed will also serve as a template for investigating other load-sensitive tissues, advancing interdisciplinary innovation in musculoskeletal health.
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health sciences.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize resource use while maintaining profitability and sustainability. However, the complexity of interactions between environmental variables, management practices, and economic factors challenges traditional decision-making approaches. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model and optimize agricultural production operations at scale. By integrating real-time sensor data, historical climate records, and crop growth simulations, the research aims to generate actionable insights for precision agriculture applications. The computational approach leverages machine learning algorithms to predict crop yields under varying irrigation, fertilization, and pest management strategies, while parallelized simulations assess the economic and environmental trade-offs of different operational plans. High-performance computing resources are essential to process multi-terabyte datasets, train complex neural networks, and execute millions of scenario iterations within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include scalable models for site-specific management recommendations, reducing input waste and enhancing yield stability. Furthermore, the framework will enable scenario testing for emerging challenges such as climate variability and market fluctuations, providing agribusiness stakeholders with robust tools for strategic planning. By advancing data-driven decision-making in agricultural operations, this research contributes to the sustainable intensification of food production systems, aligning with global efforts to address food security and resource efficiency.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general planning, economics, and use of facilities, natural resources, equipment, labor, and capital to produce plant and animal products, and that may prepare individuals for work in farming, ranching, and agribusiness.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern manufacturing systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize processes, manage stochastic demand, and minimize resource waste. This project seeks to address critical challenges in manufacturing system design and operations by developing a scalable, high-fidelity simulation framework integrated with optimization algorithms. The research focuses on multi-objective decision-making under uncertainty, including dynamic production scheduling, facility layout optimization, and supply chain resilience. Key computational challenges involve handling large-scale combinatorial problems, real-time stochastic event modeling, and high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to distributed manufacturing networks. The proposed work leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized discrete-event simulations, enabling the evaluation of millions of production scenarios with varying material flows, machine failure rates, and demand patterns. Optimization will employ distributed metaheuristic algorithms, including asynchronous genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization, to identify Pareto-optimal solutions for throughput maximization, energy consumption reduction, and lead time minimization. The computational framework will integrate industrial data streams through digital twin architectures, requiring real-time synchronization between physical systems and simulation instances. Expected outcomes include novel methodologies for adaptive resource allocation in cloud manufacturing environments and predictive models for bottleneck mitigation in hybrid human-robot assembly lines. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of system-wide manufacturing interdependencies, this research aims to advance operational efficiency metrics while maintaining scalability for industry adoption. The requested HPC resources will directly support the development of open-source tools for manufacturing system optimization, contributing to academic knowledge in industrial engineering while addressing practical challenges in sustainable production. Results will be validated through case studies with automotive component manufacturers, providing benchmarks for computational performance and economic impact assessment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, and implementation of manufacturing systems. Includes instruction in materials science and engineering, manufacturing processes, process engineering, assembly and product engineering, manufacturing systems design, and manufacturing competitiveness.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced numerical frameworks to investigate quantum field theories (QFTs) in curved spacetime geometries, a foundational problem at the intersection of theoretical physics and differential geometry. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how quantum fluctuations interact with non-trivial gravitational backgrounds, particularly in regimes where perturbative methods fail. Key challenges include solving coupled Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations in highly symmetric yet non-stationary spacetimes, modeling vacuum polarization effects, and characterizing renormalized stress-energy tensors near causality boundaries. To tackle these problems, we propose a hybrid computational strategy combining spectral methods for spacetime discretization, lattice-based Monte Carlo sampling for path integral evaluation, and adaptive mesh refinement for resolving high-curvature regions. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize large-scale tensor network contractions, optimize gradient flows in variational quantum simulations, and store multi-terabyte datasets of field configurations. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative predictions for particle production in dynamical horizon formation scenarios, (2) non-perturbative bounds on semiclassical gravity’s domain of validity, and (3) open-source software tools for covariant QFT simulations. These results will directly inform theoretical models of quantum-gravitational phenomena while advancing numerical relativity techniques. The requested allocation—targeting GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures—is essential given the exponential scaling of Hilbert space dimensions in spatially extended quantum systems and the need for high-precision floating-point operations in solving hyperbolic partial differential equations. This work bridges mathematical physics with computational science, offering new pathways to analyze strongly correlated quantum fields in geometric backgrounds beyond analytic approximation schemes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and mathematical formulation and evaluation of the physical laws governing, and models describing, matter-energy phenomena, and the analysis of related experimental designs and results. Includes instruction in classical and quantum theory, relativity theory, field theory, mathematics of infinite series, vector and coordinate analysis, wave and particle theory, advanced applied calculus and geometry, analyses of continuum, cosmology, and statistical theory and analysis.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics datasets in comparative biomedical research necessitates advanced computational tools to model disease mechanisms and optimize experimental animal use. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in analyzing large-scale genomic, proteomic, and physiological data from murine and porcine models of human cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the integration of heterogeneous datasets, hindering the identification of conserved molecular pathways and predictive biomarkers. Our computational approach employs parallelized workflows for genome-wide association studies (GWAS), machine learning-based feature selection, and multi-scale mechanistic modeling to resolve genotype-phenotype relationships across species. Agent-based simulations will further evaluate how genetic diversity and environmental variables influence disease penetrance in controlled animal colonies, enabling predictive optimization of breeding strategies and experimental protocols. By leveraging GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks, we aim to develop predictive models of drug-induced cardiotoxicity and metabolic syndrome progression, validated against high-resolution imaging and functional genomics data. The proposed work will advance translational insights into conserved disease pathways while refining ethical frameworks for experimental animal use through data-driven reductions in sample sizes and invasive procedures. Outcomes will include open-source tools for cross-species data integration, colony management simulations, and AI-driven experimental design recommendations tailored to veterinary researchers. This project bridges critical gaps in computational comparative medicine, supporting both biomedical discovery and the ethical imperatives central to laboratory animal science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the preservation and accessibility of dynamic, born-digital cultural artifacts, a critical yet under-resourced area within library science. As libraries and archives increasingly steward complex digital objects—such as interactive media, algorithmically generated content, and ephemeral web-based materials—traditional preservation frameworks struggle to model the behavior, dependencies, and decay risks inherent in these artifacts. The research problem centers on developing computational models to simulate the lifecycle of dynamic digital objects under varying preservation strategies, enabling data-driven decision-making for long-term stewardship. The project employs a hybrid methodology combining agent-based modeling to replicate interactions between digital objects and their technical ecosystems, machine learning to predict degradation patterns, and graph-based analytics to map dependencies in software and hardware environments. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage large-scale simulations of multi-decadal preservation scenarios, parallel processing for training predictive models on heterogeneous datasets (including emulation logs, format migration records, and web archive metadata), and high-memory nodes for analyzing complex dependency networks. Expected outcomes include a toolkit for quantifying preservation risks in dynamic digital collections, optimized strategies for allocating institutional resources to at-risk materials, and a publicly accessible dataset documenting simulated preservation pathways. The work bridges library science, computational forensics, and digital humanities, offering a novel framework for safeguarding culturally significant digital content against technological obsolescence. By integrating HPC-driven insights into archival practice, the project aims to advance the scalability of digital preservation efforts while informing the development of next-generation archival standards for emergent media formats.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of hospital operations, driven by fluctuating patient volumes, resource constraints, and dynamic care pathways, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize administrative decision-making. This project focuses on developing a high-fidelity simulation framework to model patient flow and resource allocation within emergency departments (EDs), where inefficient triage and staffing practices contribute to bottlenecks, prolonged wait times, and clinician burnout. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to create a multi-scale, adaptive model integrating real-time electronic health record (EHR) data, staff scheduling variables, and equipment utilization patterns to predict and mitigate operational inefficiencies. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient-clinician interactions, discrete-event simulation (DES) for process mapping, and machine learning (ML) to identify latent predictors of congestion. Key innovations include the incorporation of stochastic demand forecasting—accounting for seasonal illness trends and emergent public health events—and dynamic resource reallocation algorithms that adjust staffing and bed availability in response to simulated scenarios. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of thousands of parameter combinations to identify optimal operational strategies under diverse conditions, including surge capacity planning. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for hospital administrators, capable of reducing average ED wait times by 15-25% in pilot simulations while maintaining staff workload equity. This work bridges gaps between health systems engineering and clinical operations management, offering a scalable framework adaptable to other high-acuity care settings. By aligning computational modeling with frontline administrative needs, the project aims to enhance both patient outcomes and institutional resilience, providing a template for data-driven governance in rapidly evolving healthcare environments.
cip_title: Hospital and Health Care Facilities Administration/ Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial principles to the administration of hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, and other health care facilities. Includes instruction in facilities planning, building and operations management, business management, financial management and insurance, fund-raising and marketing, public relations, human resources management and labor relations, health care facilities operations, principles of health care delivery, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Child and adolescent mental health disorders, including anxiety, depression, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), represent a growing public health crisis, with significant heterogeneity in symptom presentation, treatment response, and long-term outcomes. Current diagnostic frameworks and intervention strategies lack precision, partly due to limited integration of multimodal biological, behavioral, and environmental data. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale neuroimaging, genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and real-time mobile sensor datasets from a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 participants (ages 8–18). The computational demands of integrating these heterogeneous data types—including voxel-based morphometry MRI analyses, whole-genome sequencing, and natural language processing of clinical notes—exceed the capacity of standard clinical research infrastructure. We propose developing a machine learning pipeline using federated learning architectures to preserve data privacy while training predictive models for illness trajectories and treatment outcomes. Graph neural networks will map dynamic interactions between neurodevelopmental markers and environmental stressors, while Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify uncertainty in personalized risk stratification. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biobehavioral subtypes of depression and ADHD, validated against 12-month functional outcomes, and a scalable computational framework for optimizing intervention timing. By enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, HPC resources will directly accelerate translational insights, with the potential to transform clinical practice through data-driven diagnostic tools and adaptive treatment algorithms. This work aligns with national priorities in precision mental health, offering a paradigm to reduce long-term disability by computationally targeting mechanisms underlying illness heterogeneity.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of developmental, behavioral, emotional, and mental disorders of childhood and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to analyze the efficacy of multimodal communication strategies in secondary education classrooms, with a focus on improving pedagogical training for pre-service Communication Arts and Literature teachers. A critical challenge in teacher education is understanding how diverse instructional techniques—such as interactive storytelling, debate facilitation, and peer review workflows—impact student engagement and learning outcomes across varied demographic contexts. While qualitative studies dominate this field, the scale and complexity of classroom interaction data (e.g., transcribed dialogues, written feedback, and multimedia artifacts) require advanced computational methods to identify patterns and predictors of successful teaching practices. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to process and analyze large datasets comprising audio/video recordings of classroom activities, student writing samples, and teacher feedback logs from 50+ partner schools. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for sentiment analysis and discourse structure identification, will be applied to evaluate linguistic and paralinguistic features of teacher-student interactions. Concurrently, network analysis will map the relationship between specific instructional approaches (e.g., scaffolded writing exercises) and longitudinal student performance metrics. The computational pipeline will integrate these multimodal inputs to generate adaptive simulations of classroom scenarios, enabling pre-service teachers to virtually test and refine communication strategies in diverse simulated environments. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for quantifying the impact of rhetorical choices on learning outcomes, (2) evidence-based recommendations for personalizing communication pedagogy, and (3) open-access training modules incorporating computational insights into existing teacher education curricula. By bridging computational linguistics with classroom praxis, this work aims to equip educators with data-driven tools to address evolving challenges in literacy education and intercultural communication.
cip_title: Communication Arts and Literature Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to teach oral expression, literature, and writing to students at various education levels. Includes instruction in interpersonal communication, intercultural communication, language learning, listening instructional techniques, public speaking, reading instructional techniques, writing instructional techniques, and practical teaching experience.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the theoretical understanding of computational hardness in approximation algorithms for NP-hard optimization problems, with a focus on bridging gaps between asymptotic complexity bounds and empirical algorithmic behavior. While polynomial-time approximation algorithms for problems such as traveling salesman, vertex cover, and set cover are well-characterized theoretically, their practical performance under realistic input regimes—particularly at scales encountered in modern applications—remains underexplored. This gap limits the ability to predict algorithm efficacy in real-world scenarios where input structures and size interact with hidden constants and lower-order terms. To address this, we propose a computational study combining theoretical analysis with large-scale empirical validation. Our methodology involves (1) generating synthetic and real-world-derived problem instances across multiple dimensions (size, density, constraint structure), (2) implementing state-of-the-art approximation algorithms with instrumentation to track hidden constants and memory-access patterns, and (3) executing parallelized performance analyses across parameterized input spaces. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the combinatorial explosion of test cases, particularly for problems where instance spaces grow exponentially with input size. We will employ distributed-memory parallelism for batch simulations and shared-memory architectures for fine-grained algorithm profiling. Expected outcomes include: (a) quantitative models relating theoretical complexity measures to practical runtime distributions, (b) identification of phase transitions where asymptotic bounds become practically relevant, and (c) an open-source benchmarking suite for complexity-aware algorithm evaluation. Results will directly contribute to the refinement of complexity-theoretic models while providing practitioners with evidence-based guidelines for algorithm selection. The computational demands—processing petabytes of performance telemetry across millions of instances—necessitate cluster-scale resources with high-core-count nodes and fast interconnects to ensure feasible completion timelines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computability theory, complexity theory, and the nature of computation.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the role of algorithmic curation in shaping cultural narratives across digital media platforms, with a focus on how large-scale computational methods can reveal patterns in content dissemination, audience engagement, and ideological framing. As media ecosystems become increasingly dominated by platform-specific algorithms, understanding their impact on cultural production and consumption requires analyzing vast datasets—including social media posts, video metadata, and user interaction logs—that exceed the capacity of conventional computing resources. The study will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process multi-modal data (text, video, network structures) from platforms like YouTube, TikTok, and X (Twitter), utilizing natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis, computer vision techniques for visual rhetoric assessment, and graph-based modeling to trace information diffusion pathways. By integrating computational critical media analysis with cultural theory, the project aims to identify how algorithmic systems prioritize certain narratives, amplify specific stakeholders, and reinforce or disrupt cultural hierarchies. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for auditing platform algorithms’ cultural impacts, evidence-based insights into the relationship between media economics and content bias, and methodological advancements in applying HPC to humanistic media research. These results will inform policy discussions on platform accountability, support media literacy initiatives, and provide scholars with tools to critically assess the infrastructural dimensions of digital culture. The requested computing resources are essential for handling terabyte-scale datasets, training machine learning models on heterogeneous media formats, and simulating cross-platform narrative propagation in iterative scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis and criticism of media institutions and media texts, how people experience and understand media content, and the roles of media in producing and transforming culture. Includes instruction in communications regulation, law, and policy; media history; media aesthetics, interpretation, and criticism; the social and cultural effects of mass media; cultural studies; the economics of media industries; visual and media literacy; and the psychology and behavioral aspects of media messages, interpretation, and utilization.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance biomechanical modeling and motor skill analysis in physical education and coaching contexts. A critical challenge in training pedagogy is the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to optimize movement patterns for diverse learners. Traditional observational methods often fail to capture the complex, dynamic interactions between biomechanical variables (e.g., joint kinematics, muscle activation) and environmental factors (e.g., equipment, terrain) that influence skill acquisition. To address this, we propose developing computational models to simulate and analyze sport-specific movements under varying physiological and contextual conditions. The research will utilize motion capture datasets from collegiate athletes and physical education students, integrating them with musculoskeletal simulations via OpenSim and machine learning algorithms to identify biomechanical inefficiencies and predict optimal training adjustments. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional data (including 3D motion trajectories, electromyography signals, and force plate measurements) and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about technique modifications. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for personalizing coaching interventions based on individual biomechanical profiles, (2) a computational toolkit to visualize movement adaptations in real-time educational settings, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for sequencing motor skill instruction across sports like basketball, swimming, and track. By bridging computational biomechanics with pedagogical practice, this work aims to enhance the precision of physical education curricula and reduce injury risks in novice learners. The scalability of these models will also support future research on inclusive adaptations for athletes with disabilities, aligning with broader educational equity goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physical education programs and/or to coach sports at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time encrypted data query processing for decentralized business intelligence systems, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of cybersecurity, quantum-inspired algorithms, and distributed database architectures. As organizations increasingly adopt hybrid cloud-edge infrastructures, conventional encryption methods create latency bottlenecks when analyzing sensitive operational data across fragmented networks, limiting the agility of decision-support systems. The study proposes a novel computational framework leveraging lattice-based homomorphic encryption combined with quantum annealing-inspired optimization to enable secure, parallelized query execution on distributed business datasets. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-node environments with varying data locality constraints, testing neural network-based workload predictors against combinatorial optimization models for query routing. Key objectives include developing a GPU-accelerated library for privacy-preserving aggregate operations and benchmarking against traditional federated learning approaches using synthetic datasets modeling supply chain logistics and cross-institutional financial transactions. Expected outcomes include quantifiable performance metrics for encrypted join operations at petabyte scale and adaptive resource allocation strategies for heterogeneous computing clusters. This work aims to advance the state of practice in secure distributed analytics, directly supporting compliance-driven industries requiring both rigorous data protection and subsecond response times for complex business queries. The computational intensity of simulating quantum annealing effects on classical hardware and the need for massively parallel encryption/decryption cycles necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with specialized cryptographic acceleration capabilities. Successful validation of the framework could inform new standards for responsive security architectures in management information systems, particularly for organizations operating in regulated verticals with strict data sovereignty requirements.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in high-resolution digital imaging workflows for platemaking and graphic reproduction, a critical challenge in the communication and journalism sectors where rapid, high-quality print and digital media production is essential. Current workflows struggle with processing large-scale, high-fidelity image datasets (often exceeding 10 terabytes per project) due to computational bottlenecks in color calibration, raster image processing (RIP), and imposition planning. These limitations result in prolonged production times, suboptimal resource use, and increased material waste during plate alignment testing. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy parallelized algorithms for real-time image optimization, multi-stage RIP simulations, and AI-driven imposition planning. The computational approach will integrate GPU-accelerated rendering for color-space transformations, distributed computing frameworks for dynamic error-correction in plate alignment, and machine learning models trained on historical production data to predict optimal ink coverage and substrate interactions. By scaling these resource-intensive simulations across HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce iterative testing phases by 40–60%, minimize material waste in platemaking by 30%, and enable direct-to-press workflows for ultra-high-resolution (6000+ dpi) hybrid print-digital products. The outcomes will directly benefit academic programs training platemaking specialists by providing a scalable computational framework for teaching advanced digital imaging techniques, while offering industry partners in publishing and packaging a replicable model for sustainable, cost-effective production. This work bridges a critical gap in non-STEM computational research by demonstrating how HPC can transform traditional graphic arts workflows, aligning with broader efforts to digitize and decarbonize the print media sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare film, digital data, and surfaces to reproduce printed or graphic images. Includes instruction in platemaking, stripping, camerawork, imposition, digital imaging, computer direct-to-plate and direct-to-press, and related processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance consumer advocacy through the development of a predictive modeling framework that evaluates product safety risks and ecological impacts across dynamic consumption patterns. Despite regulatory frameworks, consumers remain vulnerable to poorly understood risks from emerging products, particularly those intersecting with sustainability challenges. Current analytical methods struggle to integrate real-time consumer feedback, longitudinal product safety data, and environmental impact metrics at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational system combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling (ABM), and lifecycle assessment (LCA) simulations. The NLP component will analyze unstructured consumer complaint data from public databases and social media to identify latent risk signals. ABM will simulate decision-making patterns among diverse consumer demographics, while LCA modules will quantify ecological footprints of products under varying usage scenarios. HPC resources are critical to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, train deep learning models for anomaly detection, and run Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic risks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for advocacy groups to prioritize high-risk products, forecast regulatory gaps, and quantify trade-offs between product safety and environmental sustainability.
