By enabling rapid, data-driven assessment of complex consumption ecosystems, this research aims to empower consumer protection initiatives with scalable analytical tools, reduce response times to emerging hazards, and inform policy debates at the intersection of consumer rights and ecological stewardship. The project aligns with the program’s mission to enhance consumer advocacy through innovative research techniques, bridging computational scalability challenges with applied social and environmental priorities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on providing end-use advice and representational services to individuals and groups within a variety of settings, and the analytical and research techniques needed to protect consumers from unsafe, unreliable, and/or unhealthy products and services. Includes instruction in consumer advocacy, family management systems, ecological impacts of consumption practices, and analyzing and testing product quality and safety.

abstract: The integration of multi-source forensic, medical, and legal data in forensic nursing practice poses significant challenges due to the volume, heterogeneity, and sensitivity of these datasets. Current methods for analyzing patterns of violence, evidence integrity, and patient outcomes often rely on fragmented analyses, limiting the ability to identify systemic trends or optimize interventions. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational framework for synthesizing large-scale forensic nursing data, including electronic medical records, crime reports, genomic data, and injury documentation. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing multimodal datasets to uncover latent correlations between clinical findings, perpetrator behavior, and legal outcomes. Methods include deploying machine learning models to predict recidivism risks and patient vulnerability, implementing natural language processing to extract actionable insights from legal testimony and clinical notes, and simulating evidence degradation scenarios to improve chain-of-custody protocols. Graph-based analytics will map networks of violence-related injuries across demographic and geographic variables, while parallelized genomic pipelines will identify biomarkers associated with traumatic injury recovery. The computational workflow will leverage distributed storage systems for secure, HIPAA-compliant data handling and GPU-accelerated processing for real-time analytics during medicolegal investigations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide forensic evidence collection, risk stratification frameworks for violence prevention programs, and data-driven protocols for interdisciplinary collaboration between nurses, law enforcement, and legal professionals. By enabling large-scale temporal and spatial analyses of forensic health data, this project aims to advance the precision of forensic nursing practice, enhance the reliability of legal testimony, and inform public health strategies for reducing community violence. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive algorithms required to achieve these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the law and forensic science to nursing practice and collaborate with other professionals for the care of victims and the prosecution of criminals. Includes instruction in advanced physical assessment, evidence collection and preservation, forensic anthropology, legal testimony, medicolegal investigation, pathophysiology, pathohistology, pharmacology, and violence prevention.

abstract: Anesthesiology practice faces challenges in optimizing individualized patient care due to the complex interplay of pharmacokinetic variability, dynamic physiological responses, and multi-drug interactions during surgical procedures. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model real-time anesthesia delivery optimization, integrating patient-specific factors such as comorbidities, genetic markers, and intraoperative physiological data. The research problem centers on mitigating adverse events—including hemodynamic instability and delayed recovery—by predicting optimal anesthetic dosing and titration strategies in diverse clinical scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to address the computational demands of this work, which involves large-scale simulations of pharmacodynamic models, ensemble machine learning for predictive analytics, and Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in dosing recommendations. The proposed framework will utilize anonymized electronic health records (EHRs) from 15,000+ surgical cases, encompassing variables such as vital sign trajectories, drug administration timelines, and postoperative outcomes. Deep learning architectures will be trained to identify risk patterns and recommend context-aware adjustments to anesthesia protocols. Additionally, finite element modeling will simulate drug diffusion in tissue compartments to refine regional blockade strategies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive tool for perioperative hypotension and hypoventilation risks, (2) adaptive dosing algorithms for volatile and intravenous anesthetics, and (3) open-source software modules for clinical decision support. These deliverables will directly enhance the precision of anesthesia care plans developed by anesthesiologist assistants, reducing postoperative complications and improving resource allocation in surgical settings. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges computational innovation with translational clinical workflows, advancing safer and more efficient anesthesia practices in alignment with evolving perioperative medicine paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: The development of investigational drugs remains hindered by inefficiencies in predicting pharmacokinetic properties, off-target interactions, and patient-specific therapeutic responses. Current computational approaches struggle to integrate multi-scale biological data, model dynamic drug-target interactions at atomic resolution, and account for population-scale genomic variability. This project proposes to address these limitations through a multi-modal computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We aim to accelerate the identification of viable drug candidates and optimize personalized treatment strategies by combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models, and population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analyses. The MD simulations will utilize GPU-accelerated sampling to characterize binding free energies and conformational dynamics of investigational compounds against therapeutic targets, including those with high structural flexibility. Parallelized ML workflows will integrate multi-omics datasets from clinical trials to predict drug efficacy and toxicity across genetically diverse subpopulations. Large-scale virtual screening of compound libraries will be conducted using hybrid CPU/GPU architectures to prioritize candidates for experimental validation. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing petabyte-scale data from electronic health records, genomic databases, and real-world evidence sources, enabling federated learning approaches to preserve patient privacy. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for dose optimization, identification of biomarkers predictive of therapeutic response, and mechanistic insights into drug resistance patterns observed in late-stage clinical trials. This resource-intensive computational strategy will directly support three ongoing phase II/III studies in oncology and cardiovascular disease, potentially reducing drug development timelines by 30-40% for high-priority therapeutic areas. The project will establish an open-access computational pipeline to enhance reproducibility and collaboration in clinical translational research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Investigational Drugs and Research

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Lao linguistic structures and literary texts, addressing critical gaps in digital resources for understudied Southeast Asian languages. Despite Lao’s cultural significance and regional importance, large-scale computational studies of its syntax, dialectal variations, and historical literature remain scarce due to limited digitized corpora and the absence of tailored computational tools. This research will develop and apply novel natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze phonological, morphological, and syntactic patterns across diverse Lao dialects and textual genres, including pre-modern palm-leaf manuscripts and contemporary prose. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models on curated Lao text corpora, dialect mapping via geospatial clustering algorithms, and automated syntactic parsing to trace diachronic shifts in literary conventions. These methods require HPC capabilities to manage the processing of terabyte-scale multilingual datasets, parallelize computationally intensive tasks (e.g., variational inference for Bayesian dialect classification), and optimize memory-intensive operations for low-resource language modeling. Expected outcomes include the first open-access digital corpus of annotated Lao texts spanning six centuries, an interactive dialect atlas visualizing phonological divergences across Laos and northeastern Thailand, and a suite of reusable NLP tools for Lao syntactic analysis. By enabling rigorous, data-driven exploration of Lao’s linguistic evolution and literary heritage, this project will provide foundational resources for scholars in Lao studies, support language preservation initiatives, and demonstrate scalable methodologies for computational humanities research in other underrepresented languages. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to overcome current bottlenecks in processing efficiency and model scalability, ensuring robust reproducibility for future interdisciplinary studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Lao language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The study of anatomical structures at the cellular and tissue levels requires detailed analysis of spatial organization and dynamic interactions that underpin physiological and pathological processes. Current limitations in resolving complex 3D tissue architectures and modeling multicellular behaviors hinder our ability to map structural changes associated with aging, injury, or diseases such as fibrosis. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that integrate histopathological imaging data, cellular dynamics, and biomechanical interactions within organ systems. High-resolution microscopy datasets of human and murine tissues will be processed to reconstruct 3D tissue geometries, while agent-based modeling frameworks will simulate cellular responses to mechanical and biochemical stimuli. Finite element analysis will quantify stress distributions in pathological microenvironments, and machine learning pipelines will classify tissue regions based on structural biomarkers. These computational workflows demand parallelized processing for large-scale image segmentation, iterative simulations of cell-tissue interactions, and optimization of model parameters. Access to HPC resources will enable rapid analysis of terabytes of imaging data, reduce runtime for stochastic simulations by orders of magnitude, and facilitate validation against experimental observations. The outcomes will advance our understanding of how cellular spatial relationships and tissue biomechanics contribute to degenerative or fibrotic disease progression. By bridging anatomical structure with computational dynamics, this work will establish predictive tools for identifying early structural biomarkers and inform targeted interventions. The developed models and pipelines will be disseminated as open-source resources, enhancing collaborative research in anatomical sciences and providing a template for integrating computational methods into tissue-level studies.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of organ systems, tissue structures, and whole bodies together with their cellular and structural components and dynamics. Includes instruction in cell biology and histology, structural biology, molecular mechanics, regional and gross anatomy, embryology, neuroanatomy, endocrinology and secretory dynamics, and applications to such topics as aging and disease conditions.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions rely heavily on understanding the neuromotor and biomechanical adaptations that enable individuals to regain functional independence after injury or disability. However, current models of motor learning and recovery lack the granularity to predict personalized intervention outcomes, particularly for complex, real-world tasks. This project proposes a computational framework to bridge this gap by integrating high-resolution motion capture data, neural activation patterns, and biomechanical simulations to model individualized motor recovery trajectories. The research problem centers on the inability of conventional clinical assessments to capture the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between neural plasticity, musculoskeletal adaptation, and task-specific environmental constraints. To address this, we will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of kinematic, electromyographic, and force-plate data collected from individuals undergoing OT for upper limb rehabilitation. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to identify predictive biomarkers of motor recovery, while finite element modeling will simulate tissue remodeling processes in response to therapeutic exercises. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated neural networks for real-time pattern recognition in movement sequences and distributed computing frameworks to optimize parameter space exploration in biomechanical simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model linking specific intervention parameters to functional recovery rates, (2) quantitative biomarkers for personalized therapy adjustment, and (3) open-source tools for simulating task-specific motor challenges in virtual environments. This interdisciplinary approach sits at the intersection of rehabilitation science, computational neuroscience, and biomechanical engineering—a niche not traditionally addressed by existing health science disciplines. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the project's multi-modal data integration requirements and enabling clinically relevant processing speeds for complex simulations. By establishing computational methods to decode individual recovery patterns, this work aims to advance evidence-based practice in OT while providing a template for technology-enhanced rehabilitation science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: The proliferation of data-intensive workflows in sectors such as healthcare, logistics, and finance has exposed critical bottlenecks in conventional data entry and microcomputer applications, particularly in scalability and real-time processing. This project seeks to address the inefficiencies of legacy systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test a novel framework for intelligent, automated data entry and processing. The research problem centers on overcoming latency and accuracy limitations in handling heterogeneous, high-volume datasets—common in modern applications—where traditional single-threaded architectures fail to meet performance demands. The proposed computational approach integrates machine learning (ML) models for optical character recognition (OCR) and semantic validation with parallelized data ingestion pipelines. By utilizing distributed computing frameworks such as Apache Spark and GPU-accelerated ML training, the project aims to optimize resource allocation across multi-node clusters, enabling real-time preprocessing of terabyte-scale datasets. Key methods include benchmarking hybrid CPU-GPU workflows, simulating load-balanced task distribution, and validating results against industry-standard accuracy metrics. The expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for adaptive data entry systems capable of reducing manual intervention by 40–60% while maintaining >99% accuracy under variable workloads. This work will also produce a comparative analysis of HPC-driven versus conventional microcomputer architectures, providing actionable insights for organizations transitioning to data-centric operations. The significance lies in democratizing access to high-efficiency data processing for small-to-medium enterprises, which currently lack the infrastructure to implement costly proprietary solutions. By demonstrating the feasibility of HPC-resourced frameworks in everyday microcomputer applications, this research will bridge a critical gap between theoretical scalability and practical, equitable implementation in technology-driven fields.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data entry/microcomputer applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing industrial safety protocols in high-risk manufacturing environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial processes involving complex machinery, hazardous materials, and human-machine interactions present dynamic risks that are challenging to model using traditional risk assessment tools. Current methods often fail to account for real-time operational variability, ergonomic stressors, and cascading failure scenarios, leading to gaps in proactive hazard mitigation. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating agent-based modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning to predict safety-critical events under diverse operational conditions. The agent-based component will simulate worker behavior and equipment interactions, while CFD models will analyze chemical dispersion and thermal risks in confined spaces. Machine learning algorithms, trained on historical incident data and sensor-generated operational logs, will identify latent risk patterns and predict failure probabilities. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across thousands of scenario permutations, including rare but high-consequence events. Expected outcomes include a predictive safety analytics toolkit capable of recommending context-aware safety interventions, optimizing evacuation routes, and dynamically adjusting risk thresholds based on real-time sensor inputs. This work will advance the field of industrial safety technology by enabling data-driven, scenario-adaptive safety protocols, reducing workplace injuries, and minimizing downtime in sectors such as chemical manufacturing and heavy machinery operations. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated to industry partners and regulatory bodies to inform safety standards and training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to assist engineers and other professionals in implementing and enforcing industrial safety standards to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in industrial processes, industrial hygiene, injury prevention, toxicology, ergonomics, risk analysis, system and process safety, safety performance measurement, human factors, human behavior, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing hyper-localized sales and distribution networks in volatile consumer markets. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies of traditional static distribution models in adapting to real-time demand fluctuations, supply chain disruptions, and spatially heterogeneous consumer behavior—challenges amplified by climate-related logistics uncertainties and shifting purchasing patterns in post-pandemic economies. We propose an agent-based simulation platform that integrates real-time sales data, geospatial weather patterns, and dynamic inventory constraints to model multi-echelon distribution networks at street-level granularity. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic demand forecasting with graph neural networks to optimize routing and inventory allocation across interdependent nodes, while accounting for competitive pricing feedback loops. A unique innovation involves embedding generative AI to simulate synthetic consumer cohorts exhibiting non-linear responses to micro-targeted promotions, enabling stress-testing of resilience strategies under 10,000+ scenario variations. The project will validate models against proprietary data from a partner network of 350+ urban retail outlets, requiring parallelized computation of high-dimensional decision spaces. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive distribution planning, with preliminary results demonstrating a 15–20% reduction in perishable goods waste in pilot food distribution systems. The work bridges computational economics, operations research, and spatial analytics, advancing business methodology for resource allocation in climate-vulnerable markets while establishing benchmarks for AI-driven sales channel optimization. HPC resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale integration of IoT sensor data, satellite weather feeds, and transaction records across simulated temporal horizons exceeding 18 months.
cip_title: Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Operations, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general process and techniques of direct wholesale and retail buying and selling operations and introduces individuals to related careers. Includes instruction in the principles of entrepreneurial economics, basic sales skills, the distribution channels for goods and services, and supervised practical application experiences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized neuromotor rehabilitation protocols by integrating high-resolution biomechanical data with neural network-driven predictive modeling. Current approaches to designing therapeutic interventions for individuals with acquired motor impairments (e.g., post-stroke or traumatic brain injury) often rely on generalized guidelines, leading to suboptimal recovery trajectories. The research addresses this gap by leveraging wearable sensor arrays and neuroimaging-derived connectivity maps to create patient-specific digital twins, enabling the simulation of rehabilitation outcomes under varying therapeutic parameters. The computational workflow involves three phases: (1) processing terabyte-scale motion capture and electromyography datasets to characterize individual movement pathologies; (2) training graph neural networks on federated neurorehabilitation datasets to predict cortical reorganization patterns; and (3) implementing multi-objective optimization algorithms to balance functional recovery metrics against physiological constraints. High-performance computing resources are critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of simulating over 10^5 potential therapy permutations per patient while maintaining sub-millisecond temporal resolution in biomechanical simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for adaptive therapy design validated through a retrospective analysis of 1,200 clinical cases, with prospective testing planned across three rehabilitation centers. The project advances precision rehabilitation by establishing quantitative links between therapeutic dosing, neural plasticity, and functional outcomes—a currently underexplored niche requiring convergence of computational neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and clinical rehabilitation sciences. Successful implementation could reduce average rehabilitation durations by 18-22% in target populations while preventing costly secondary complications from overtraining.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rehabilitation and therapeutic professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches for complex, multifactorial diseases by integrating multi-omics data with clinical outcomes. A critical challenge in health professions research is the identification of actionable biomarkers and therapeutic targets from heterogeneous datasets spanning genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and electronic health records (EHRs). Traditional statistical methods often fail to capture nonlinear interactions or scale efficiently with high-dimensional data, limiting their utility for personalized clinical decision-making. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework combining deep learning architectures with network-based analytics to model disease pathways and predict patient-specific outcomes. The framework will employ graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to integrate omics-derived interaction networks with EHR data, while transformer-based models will process longitudinal clinical records to identify temporal risk patterns. HPC resources are essential for training these models on large-scale datasets (e.g., 50,000+ patient records with paired multi-omics profiles) and optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized grid searches. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will be conducted to validate predicted protein-ligand interactions for candidate therapeutics. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for multi-omics data integration, (2) predictive models for disease progression and treatment response in case studies focusing on autoimmune disorders and metabolic syndromes, and (3) prioritized biomarkers for clinical validation. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven clinical protocols, reducing trial-and-error in therapeutic interventions. The requested computing resources—particularly GPU nodes and high-memory CPUs—will enable the processing of terabytes of multimodal data, significantly accelerating model training and large-scale simulations that are infeasible on local infrastructure. By bridging computational innovation with clinical translation, this project aims to demonstrate how HPC-driven analytics can directly inform personalized healthcare strategies.
cip_title: Health Professions and Related Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health professions and related clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel computational framework for analyzing the evolution of legal reasoning in transnational arbitration disputes. While legal research traditionally relies on qualitative methods, the growing volume of digitized arbitration awards, procedural documents, and cross-jurisdictional citations has created an urgent need for scalable, data-driven approaches to identify latent patterns in decision-making. The research problem centers on the lack of systematic tools to map how arbitrators reconcile conflicting national laws with international commercial principles—a process critical to global trade but poorly understood due to its textual complexity and jurisdictional variability. By employing natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for legal corpora, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on arbitration-specific language, this project will quantify semantic shifts in key legal concepts across awards rendered between 2000–2023. Computational workflows will integrate citation network analysis with temporal topic modeling to trace the influence of landmark cases and statutory reforms. The HPC environment is essential for processing over 500,000 multilingual legal documents (1.2+ TB unstructured data) while maintaining chain-of-custody metadata for reproducibility. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for parsing arbitration-specific legal reasoning at scale, 2) empirical evidence of emerging normative convergence in procedural fairness standards, and 3) predictive models to assess how hypothetical treaty modifications might alter dispute resolution trajectories. This work bridges computational linguistics and legal informatics, offering practitioners actionable insights into systemic biases while establishing methodological precedents for HPC-enabled analysis in advanced legal studies.
cip_title: Legal Research and Advanced Professional Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in legal research and advanced professional studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural information sharing during global crises using large-scale social media data, focusing on how cultural frameworks shape the dissemination and reception of crisis-related content. While prior research has examined crisis communication within homogeneous populations, the interplay between cultural context, linguistic diversity, and information virality remains underexplored in heterogeneous digital ecosystems. The study will analyze multilingual datasets spanning six geographically distributed platforms (including Twitter, Weibo, and regional networks) during three recent transnational crises, capturing over 500 million posts. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a multi-stage computational pipeline: 1) transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for low-resource languages will classify content types and emotional valence, 2) temporal network analysis will map information diffusion patterns across cultural boundaries, and 3) agent-based modeling will simulate how cultural cognition parameters affect sharing behaviors. Custom attention mechanisms will handle code-switching and mixed-language posts, while differential privacy techniques will anonymize sensitive user data. The computational demands stem from processing petabyte-scale unstructured text, training multiple deep learning architectures in parallel, and running 10,000+ parameterized simulations to test cultural transmission hypotheses. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying cultural friction in information spread, identification of universal versus culture-specific crisis communication patterns, and actionable insights for designing culturally adaptive public health messaging. This work advances computational social science methodology by integrating cultural theory with large-language model capabilities while addressing practical challenges in global crisis response. The requested resources will enable processing speeds 40x faster than conventional clusters, particularly crucial for the real-time aspect of crisis simulations and transformer model fine-tuning across 18 languages.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of human social behavior and social institutions using any of the methodologies common to the social sciences and/or history, or an undifferentiated program of study in the social sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize real-time tourism promotion strategies by integrating dynamic environmental, economic, and sociocultural variables into predictive computational models. Tourism organizations face challenges in allocating promotional resources effectively due to the nonlinear interactions between factors such as seasonal demand fluctuations, geopolitical disruptions, evolving traveler preferences, and regional infrastructure constraints. Existing marketing frameworks often rely on static segmentation or lagging indicators, limiting responsiveness to emerging opportunities. We propose developing an adaptive decision-support system using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning to simulate multiscale tourism ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the creation of a granular simulation environment incorporating real-time data streams—including social media sentiment, transportation APIs, currency exchange rates, and climate projections—to model tourist behavior, local business responses, and promotion dissemination pathways. Computational experiments will test promotional allocation strategies under diverse scenarios, quantifying cascading impacts on regional visitation patterns, revenue distribution, and community resilience. A neural architecture will concurrently analyze historical campaign performance data to identify high-yield audience segments and media channels. Validation will occur through partnerships with three regional tourism boards, comparing model recommendations against ongoing promotion outcomes. The research aims to produce a framework for dynamically adjusting marketing investments across digital, print, and experiential channels while balancing economic objectives with cultural preservation goals. Expected outcomes include open-source algorithms for tourism scenario modeling, benchmarks for cross-channel promotion ROI under volatility, and policy guidelines for equitable destination stewardship. This computational approach advances tourism marketing beyond traditional business paradigms by treating promotion ecosystems as complex adaptive systems, with direct applications for sustainable destination management and crisis response planning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of tourism in public and private sector settings. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in analyzing the syntactic and semantic evolution of Modern Greek across its post-medieval development, with a focus on understudied regional dialects and literary texts from the 18th century to the present. While prior scholarship has cataloged grammatical shifts in standardized Greek, computational limitations have hindered large-scale comparative analyses of non-canonical texts, vernacular sources, and dialectal variations—critical gaps this study aims to fill. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models and dynamic word embedding frameworks, to process a curated corpus of digitized manuscripts, newspapers, and transcribed oral histories (totaling ~15 TB). Computational workflows will be designed to identify diachronic patterns in morphological structures, lexical borrowing, and pragmatic features, particularly in texts from Crete, the Aegean islands, and Asia Minor communities. Parallelized sentiment analysis and topic modeling will further illuminate stylistic divergences between literary movements and regional vernacular traditions. By integrating computational philology with dialectometry, this approach will generate interactive maps and network graphs visualizing linguistic change across temporal and geographic axes. The outcomes will include the first open-access database of annotated Modern Greek dialectal corpora, machine learning models fine-tuned for low-resource Greek variants, and quantitative frameworks for assessing language contact phenomena. These resources will advance scholarly understanding of Greek’s sociolinguistic stratification while providing tools for educators and policymakers addressing language preservation. The scale of data processing—requiring GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for multilingual alignment, and high-memory nodes for graph-based analytics—necessitates HPC infrastructure beyond typical departmental capacities. This work bridges computational humanities and linguistic research, offering methodological innovations applicable to other under-resourced languages in historical contexts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and use of the Greek language in the period dating from the late 15th century to the present. Includes instruction in modern Greek literature, current Greek dialects, and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of analyzing and verifying multimedia news content at scale in an era of information overload and rapidly evolving digital manipulation techniques. Journalists and news organizations increasingly face vast quantities of user-generated content, AI-generated media, and cross-platform data that require urgent processing to combat misinformation while maintaining ethical reporting standards. The research will develop computational workflows combining natural language processing, image/video forensics, and network analysis to automate the identification of manipulated content, trace information provenance, and detect coordinated disinformation campaigns across social and traditional media platforms. High-performance computing resources are critical for training machine learning models on diverse multimodal datasets (including text, images, video metadata, and temporal sharing patterns) while maintaining the low-latency processing required for real-time journalistic verification tasks. Methods will include parallelized processing of large-scale media archives, graph-based analysis of content dissemination networks, and ensemble deep learning models optimized for detecting emerging synthetic media types. The project will produce open-source tools tailored for newsrooms to prioritize investigative resources, alongside scholarly contributions to understanding how computational methods can enhance—without replacing—human editorial judgment. Outcomes aim to strengthen trust in media ecosystems by advancing scalable technical capacity for ethical news verification, particularly for under-resourced local journalism organizations. By allocating GPU clusters and cloud-computing infrastructure, this work will enable previously infeasible longitudinal studies of misinformation spread patterns while maintaining strict data privacy protocols for handling sensitive user-generated content.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of gathering, processing, and delivering news and that prepares individuals to be professional print journalists, news editors, and news managers. Includes instruction in news writing and editing; reporting; photojournalism; layout and graphic design; journalism law and policy; professional standards and ethics; research methods; and journalism history and criticism.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of bioelectrical signaling in non-neural collective behaviors of multicellular aggregates, a novel area bridging developmental biology, biophysics, and synthetic morphology. Traditional studies of cellular communication have focused on biochemical or mechanical pathways, but emerging evidence suggests that endogenous electric fields and ion channel dynamics drive self-organization in systems lacking neural networks, such as regenerating tissues or synthetic organoids. This project addresses a critical gap in understanding how spatially distributed bioelectric patterns coordinate large-scale morphological outcomes without centralized control. Using high-performance computing resources, we will develop a multiscale computational framework integrating stochastic lattice Boltzmann methods for ion flux propagation with agent-based models of individual cell responses to electrochemical gradients. The simulations will parameterize experimentally observed phenomena in planarian regeneration and bioengineered mammalian cell clusters, testing hypotheses about threshold-driven phase transitions in collective decision-making. Expected outcomes include predictive models of electrotonic signal propagation in heterogeneous cellular networks and identification of stability criteria for target morphological states. This work will establish foundational principles for designing electroceutical therapies and programming synthetic biological systems through bioelectric interfaces, advancing applications in regenerative medicine and adaptive biomaterials. The computational approach uniquely addresses the nonlinear coupling between cellular-scale ion dynamics and population-level emergent order, requiring parallelized simulations across 10^5–10^6 interacting agents with dynamically updating boundary conditions. Resource allocation will enable parameter sweeps across physiologically relevant electrochemical ranges and machine learning-driven optimization of pattern stability metrics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the biological and biomedical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to address the multi-physics modeling challenges inherent in the design of compact fusion energy systems. While fusion energy represents a transformative clean energy solution, the engineering of viable reactors requires unprecedented integration of plasma dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), and thermal-structural interactions—a task hindered by the computational cost and scalability limitations of existing simulation tools. Current approaches often decouple these phenomena or rely on reduced-order models, sacrificing accuracy and impeding the optimization of reactor geometries and material configurations. To bridge this gap, we propose an adaptive, GPU-accelerated computational framework that couples finite-element and spectral methods within a unified HPC environment. The framework will leverage hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization and dynamic load balancing to efficiently manage the disparate spatial and temporal scales of plasma turbulence, magnetic field evolution, and heat transfer. Machine learning surrogates will be trained in situ to accelerate iterative design parameter sweeps, while experimental data from tokamak prototypes will validate the models. By enabling high-fidelity, integrated simulations of reactor subsystems, this work aims to identify optimal trade-offs between plasma confinement stability, heat flux management, and structural durability under extreme conditions. The resulting computational tools will advance the engineering of compact fusion devices by reducing reliance on empirical approximations and enabling predictive design. Successful implementation will also establish a template for coupling multi-physics solvers in other energy systems where fluid-structure interactions, electromagnetic fields, and nonlinear material responses coexist. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieve the necessary resolution for capturing edge plasma instabilities and to explore the high-dimensional parameter space of reactor configurations, which is infeasible with institutional computing clusters. Outcomes will be disseminated through open-source code repositories and collaborations with national fusion research consortia.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to engineering practice and research. Includes instruction in engineering and science fundamentals, advanced mathematics, algorithms, computer languages, and software engineering design.

abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) remain a critical challenge in perioperative care, with aseptic technique breaches contributing significantly to preventable morbidity. Current protocols for maintaining sterility rely on static guidelines that inadequately account for dynamic operating room (OR) environments, complex human-robot interactions in modern surgical systems, or real-time microbial transmission risks. This project proposes a computational framework to model contamination pathways and optimize sterile field management through high-fidelity simulations of OR workflows. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop an agent-based model integrating 1) kinematic data from surgical robots and staff movement patterns, 2) computational fluid dynamics simulations of airborne particle dispersion, and 3) machine learning analysis of historical SSI cases. The multimodal model will simulate millions of procedural variations to identify high-risk scenarios for sterility compromise, particularly in robot-assisted surgeries where instrument handling and team spatial dynamics differ markedly from conventional procedures. Validation will utilize real-world OR sensor data capturing instrument trajectories, airflow changes, and staff proximity patterns. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for contamination risk stratification, evidence-based recommendations for adaptive sterilization protocols, and AI-driven training modules for surgical technologists. By bridging surgical workflow analytics with microbial transmission modeling, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for dynamic sterility management that reduces SSI rates while improving resource utilization in technologically advanced OR environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and surgical nurses, to maintain, monitor, and enforce the sterile field and adherence to aseptic technique by preoperative, surgical team, and postoperative personnel. Includes instruction in instrument and equipment sterilization and handling, surgical supplies management, wound exposure and closure, surgical computer and robot operation and monitoring, maintenance of hemostasis, and patient and team scrubbing.

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and disorders, such as acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), exhibit complex molecular heterogeneity that complicates diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment optimization. Current approaches often rely on static genomic snapshots or bulk tissue analyses, which obscure dynamic interactions between genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental factors. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets and simulate disease progression at unprecedented resolution. The research will integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, whole-genome methylation profiles, and longitudinal clinical data from 500 patients with AML or DLBCL to model clonal evolution and therapeutic resistance. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures for mutation variant calling, Bayesian network inference to map signaling pathway dysregulation, and agent-based simulations of bone marrow niche interactions. These approaches require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model training, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for relapse risk, identification of microenvironment-driven resistance mechanisms, and in silico screening of combination therapies targeting adaptive leukemic subpopulations. By elucidating dynamic disease mechanisms, this work aims to advance precision hematology through computational biomarkers and optimized treatment strategies. The proposed HPC resources are critical to handling data complexity, reducing runtime for stochastic simulations, and enabling scalable analysis pipelines. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for the hematology research community, fostering collaborative innovation in computational hematopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the mechanisms and therapy of diseases of the blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lymph, including patient management, diagnostic tests, biopsies, and other procedures.

abstract: Neurological disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and multiple sclerosis, involve complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and systemic factors that remain poorly understood. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies are limited by the inability to integrate multi-scale data—including high-resolution neuroimaging, genomic and proteomic profiles, and real-time electrophysiological recordings—into predictive models of disease progression. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational frameworks that bridge these diverse datasets. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating machine learning models to identify early biomarkers of neurodegeneration from multi-modal brain imaging and fluid biomarker data, and (2) simulating large-scale neural network dynamics to unravel how genetic mutations disrupt synaptic communication in movement disorders. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures for pattern recognition in terabyte-scale neuroimaging datasets, graph-theoretical analyses of functional connectivity networks, and biophysically detailed simulations of neuronal ensembles using NEURON and NetPyNE. These tasks demand parallelized processing, extensive memory allocation, and rapid data throughput, necessitating HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel diagnostic signatures for preclinical disease stages, mechanistic insights into pathological neural circuit behavior, and open-source tools for scalable analysis of heterogeneous neurological data. By integrating clinical observations with computational modeling, this work aims to advance precision neurology, enabling earlier interventions and tailored therapeutic strategies. The requested resources will directly support the processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times from weeks to days, and facilitate the iterative refinement of simulations critical to translating findings into clinical applications. This project aligns with the program’s mission to improve outcomes for neurological disorders through innovation in data-driven medical research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of all types of disease or impaired function of the brain, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, muscles and autonomic nervous system, as well as the blood vessels that relate to these structures.

abstract: Early childhood education programs face complex administrative challenges in optimizing resource allocation to meet dynamic enrollment demands, regulatory compliance, and equitable service delivery. This project seeks to develop computational models to simulate and analyze resource distribution strategies for early childhood education centers, with a focus on balancing operational costs, staff-to-child ratios, and facility utilization under fluctuating enrollment patterns. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven decision-support tools for administrators navigating multi-dimensional constraints, including budget limitations, space availability, workforce training requirements, and state-mandated quality standards. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations that account for stochastic variables such as seasonal enrollment shifts, staff absenteeism, and emergency operational scenarios. These models will integrate geospatial data on community demographics, historical enrollment trends from 15 regional early childhood programs, and policy-driven constraints encoded as optimization parameters. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive patterns in resource bottlenecks and evaluate intervention strategies. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing capabilities due to the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of operational scenarios across heterogeneous program types (e.g., full-day, part-day, and subsidized care models). Expected outcomes include a framework for dynamically adjusting staffing matrices, facility expansion plans, and budget reallocation thresholds under uncertainty. This work will provide administrators with evidence-based strategies to enhance program sustainability while maintaining compliance with professional standards and ethical guidelines for service accessibility. The resulting open-source toolset will undergo validation through partnerships with three state early childhood agencies, with scalability potential to inform policy decisions at regional and national levels.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on early childhood educational program administration and prepares individuals to serve as a principal or director of an early childhood educational program. Includes instruction in early childhood education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, early childhood growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Pediatric rheumatic diseases, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and pediatric lupus, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their heterogeneity, complex pathophysiology, and variable treatment responses. Current clinical approaches often rely on imprecise diagnostic criteria and generalized treatment protocols, leading to delayed interventions and suboptimal outcomes. This project aims to address these limitations by integrating multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic) with longitudinal clinical and imaging datasets to identify disease-specific biomarkers, stratify patients into molecular subtypes, and predict treatment responses. The scale and complexity of these datasets—encompassing thousands of patients from international registries and high-resolution imaging repositories—necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable efficient data processing, storage, and analysis. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms (e.g., unsupervised clustering, deep neural networks) to classify disease subtypes and Bayesian network modeling to map dynamic interactions between genetic variants, immune pathways, and environmental triggers. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate how specific mutations alter protein structures implicated in autoimmune responses. These analyses require parallelized computing architectures to manage terabyte-scale datasets and perform millions of stochastic simulations within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models for early diagnosis, personalized therapeutic targets, and a publicly accessible computational framework for pediatric rheumatology research. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project will advance precision medicine in a clinical population with high unmet need, reducing diagnostic delays and improving long-term musculoskeletal outcomes for children and young adults. The tools and pipelines generated will also serve as a template for computational research in other pediatric chronic diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose and treat diseases of joints, muscle, bones, and tendons in children and young adults, including arthritis, back pain, muscle strains, common athletic injuries, and collagen diseases.

abstract: Movement and mind-body therapies, such as yoga, tai chi, and somatic education, demonstrate promising health benefits, yet the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating high-resolution motion capture, electrophysiological monitoring, and computational modeling to analyze dynamic mind-body interactions during therapeutic movement practices. A key challenge is the real-time processing and synchronization of multimodal datasets, including 3D kinematic data (500 Hz), EEG signals (256 channels), heart rate variability, and respiratory metrics, which collectively generate over 10 TB of raw data per study cohort. The research requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning pipelines for pattern recognition in movement quality, neural entrainment analysis, and multiscale modeling of body-brain coupling phenomena. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) to classify movement signatures predictive of therapeutic outcomes and identify neural oscillatory patterns correlated with mindful attention states. Additionally, finite element modeling (FEA) will simulate tissue stress distributions during complex postures to optimize safety parameters for clinical populations. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated computational framework for quantifying mind-body integration in movement therapies, 2) predictive biomarkers of treatment responsiveness in chronic pain populations, and 3) open-source tools for movement therapy personalization. By elucidating mechanistic pathways through which intentional movement modulates physiological and cognitive states, this work aims to advance evidence-based standardization of mind-body interventions while providing a computational foundation for developing adaptive therapeutic protocols. The requested HPC allocation will enable the large-scale parallel processing and data integration essential for this translational research, which bridges movement science, neuroscience, and computational health analytics.
cip_title: Movement and Mind-Body Therapies and Education, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in movement and mind-body therapies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets of American Sign Language (ASL) discourse and historical records of deaf communities, addressing gaps in understanding the sociolinguistic diversity and cultural evolution of deaf populations in the United States. While prior studies have documented regional and generational variations in ASL, computational limitations have restricted analyses to small, localized samples, leaving broader patterns of linguistic adaptation and cultural transmission understudied. This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for visual-spatial language structures and agent-based modeling to simulate historical diffusion pathways of ASL dialects. A corpus of annotated ASL videos (10,000+ hours) and digitized archival materials (e.g., deaf community publications, educational records) will be processed using GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks to identify syntactic, lexical, and nonmanual marker variations across demographics. Concurrently, agent-based models will reconstruct the spread of linguistic features through deaf social networks from 1950–present, incorporating historical migration and educational policy data. The computational demands of training transformer models on multimodal sign language data and running high-resolution cultural transmission simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallelized processing and large-scale parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include (1) the first nationwide map of ASL sociolinguistic variation correlated with community institutions, (2) quantitative models linking policy changes to language shift dynamics, and (3) open-access tools for temporal-spatial analysis of sign language corpora. These results will directly inform deaf education frameworks and preservation initiatives by identifying endangered ASL variants while advancing methodological paradigms for studying visual languages through computational social science. The project aligns with institutional priorities in interdisciplinary deaf studies and digital humanities, requiring HPC resources to overcome previous scale limitations in cultural-linguistic research.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the sociological, historical and linguistic aspects of the deaf and hearing impaired, and that prepares individuals to work with the deaf and hearing impaired. Includes instruction in American Sign Language, deaf studies, American deaf culture, structure of American Sign Language, history of the American deaf community, and civil rights of deaf people.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying xenobiotic metabolism and toxicity, with a focus on predicting adverse outcomes of environmental chemicals and therapeutic agents. A critical challenge in pharmacology and toxicology is elucidating how structurally diverse compounds interact with metabolic enzymes, such as cytochrome P450 isoforms, to generate reactive intermediates that contribute to organ-specific toxicity or therapeutic failure. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in resolving the dynamic structural and electronic factors governing these interactions at scale. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) modeling, and machine learning-based virtual screening. Large-scale MD simulations will map conformational dynamics of enzyme-substrate complexes across diverse xenobiotics, while QM/MM calculations will quantify activation barriers and regioselectivity of metabolic reactions. Parallelized virtual screening will predict bioactivation pathways for 10,000+ environmental chemicals in the ToxCast database. These data will inform ensemble machine learning models correlating metabolic profiles with in vitro and in vivo toxicity endpoints. The HPC environment is essential for managing the petabytes of trajectory data generated, accelerating quantum chemical computations, and enabling high-throughput screening. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of high-risk metabolic pathways linked to hepatotoxicity and neurotoxicity, (2) predictive models for metabolite-mediated toxicity of understudied compounds, and (3) mechanistic insights into enzyme promiscuity that could guide safer drug design. By bridging computational toxicology and pharmacological chemistry, this work will advance predictive frameworks for chemical risk assessment and therapeutic optimization, directly addressing public health needs in chemical safety and precision medicine.
cip_definition: A program with an integrated, combined approach to the study of pharmacological and toxicological issues in biology and the biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in topics such as solvents, xenobiotic metabolism, chemical toxicity, neurotoxicology, immunopharmacology, biotransformation, tissue culture and in vitro studies, biomolecular analysis, bioactivation and inactivation, enzyme regulation, chemoprevention and chemotherapy, industrial and chemical studies, radiation health, and bioinformatics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of climate-driven ecosystem transitions in understudied boreal and montane regions. Rapid environmental changes are altering species distributions, disturbance regimes, and carbon sequestration dynamics in these critical biomes, but existing models lack the spatial resolution and mechanistic detail needed to inform adaptive conservation strategies. To address this gap, we propose a coupled modeling framework integrating dynamic vegetation models, hydrologic simulations, and species dispersal algorithms at 1 km² resolution across 10⁶ km² of North American and Eurasian study areas. The computational workflow will utilize a hybrid machine learning and process-based approach, assimilating remotely sensed land cover data, downscaled CMIP6 climate projections, and empirical biodiversity datasets. Key challenges include scaling individual species niche models to community-level interactions and resolving feedbacks between vegetation shifts, wildfire patterns, and permafrost degradation. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel execution of ensemble simulations across 500+ parameter combinations, requiring ~2.8 million core-hours for model calibration, sensitivity analysis, and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of ecosystem tipping points under varying emission trajectories, (2) high-resolution vulnerability maps prioritizing areas for habitat corridors, and (3) open-source tools for simulating coupled biogeochemical and biodiversity responses to climate forcing. These outputs will directly support international conservation initiatives focused on climate resilience while advancing computational methods for cross-scale ecological forecasting. The project’s scale and complexity necessitate dedicated HPC infrastructure to manage memory-intensive spatial analyses and iterative model optimization, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local computing clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of modeling multi-level behavioral determinants of health outcomes at population scale, with a focus on identifying intervention strategies to reduce disparities in chronic disease prevention. Current approaches often oversimplify the dynamic interactions between individual decision-making, social networks, and structural inequities that shape health behaviors. This project will develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrating behavioral theory, real-world social connectivity data, and spatially explicit environmental factors to simulate how health-related choices (e.g., dietary patterns, physical activity) emerge from complex biological, psychological, and socio-cultural influences. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing resources to execute parallelized simulations across diverse demographic scenarios, incorporating machine learning techniques to calibrate models using longitudinal health survey data (e.g., NHANES) and geospatial deprivation indices. Key technical challenges include optimizing memory-intensive network analyses across 10,000+ agent populations and implementing Bayesian inference methods for parameter estimation. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of critical leverage points for community-level interventions targeting obesity-related morbidity, 2) predictive models of intervention effectiveness under different policy conditions, and 3) open-source tools for simulating health behavior cascades in vulnerable populations. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses – particularly the need for rapid iteration across alternative virtual intervention scenarios – necessitates dedicated GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory processors to achieve biologically plausible simulation timescales while maintaining statistical power. This work directly advances the program’s mission by providing a computational platform to test behavioral health interventions that account for real-world complexity, ultimately informing equity-focused public health strategies with reduced reliance on trial-and-error implementation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biological, behavioral, and socio-cultural determinants of health and health behavior, and the interventions and policies aimed at improving community and population health. Includes instruction in behavioral sciences, public health practice and policy, human services, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of algorithmic curation in shaping cultural diversity through the analysis of large-scale streaming data from digital music platforms. As algorithmic recommendation systems increasingly mediate access to cultural content, concerns have emerged about their potential to homogenize consumption patterns or amplify niche genres. This research addresses a critical gap in understanding how these systems influence the evolution of musical taste and the circulation of cultural meaning within digital ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process and analyze anonymized user interaction datasets encompassing billions of streams, playlist creations, and cross-platform sharing events. Computational methods will include network analysis to map genre diffusion patterns, transformer-based NLP models to interpret user-generated metadata, and agent-based simulations to model long-term cultural dynamics under different recommendation paradigms. The project will also employ counterfactual modeling to assess how alternative algorithmic designs might foster diversity. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying cultural homogenization in streaming environments, identification of platform-specific bias patterns in content promotion, and evidence-based recommendations for ethical algorithmic design. By bridging computational social science with digital musicology, this work advances humanistic inquiry into the technological mediation of cultural practices while providing actionable insights for platform developers and policymakers. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized workflows for graph computations and real-time simulation of user behavior networks—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve research objectives within viable timeframes. Results will contribute to emerging debates about cultural preservation in algorithmic societies and establish methodologies for interdisciplinary humanities computing in understudied domains of digital culture.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on combined studies and research in the humanities subjects as distinguished from the social and physical sciences, emphasizing languages, literatures, art, music, philosophy and religion.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing fire service resource allocation during multi-incident emergencies. Fire departments increasingly face overlapping crises—such as urban fires, wildfire encroachment, and hazardous material spills—that strain traditional response protocols. Existing decision-support tools lack the capacity to dynamically simulate spatially distributed risks, resource availability, and incident escalation pathways under real-time constraints. The proposed computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) and graph-based network analysis to simulate fire service operations across jurisdictional boundaries. The ABM component will represent firefighting units, incident evolution, and community vulnerability factors, while network analysis will map interdependencies between critical infrastructure, evacuation routes, and resource depots. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical incident data and environmental variables (e.g., weather patterns, urban density) to refine risk prediction layers. The HPC environment is essential for running parallelized simulations of thousands of scenario permutations, enabling probabilistic assessments of response strategies under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs in resource pre-positioning, interagency coordination, and adaptive incident command strategies. This work addresses a critical gap in fire administration by bridging operational expertise with computational analytics, offering empirically grounded strategies to enhance community resilience. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-access modules for municipal fire agencies, fostering integration of data-driven practices into emergency management policy. By situating fire service challenges within an interdisciplinary computational framework, this research advances leadership in public safety innovation while adhering to the administrative and ethical priorities of modern fire services.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, theory, and practices associated with the management of fire operations, firefighting services, and community fire issues. Includes instruction in fire protection history and theory, incident command leadership, administration of public fire organizations, labor relations, emergency medical services management, fire emergency response strategies and mitigation, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to advance biology teacher preparation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex biological systems and simulate classroom implementation of computational tools. A critical challenge in biology teacher education lies in bridging the gap between rapidly evolving computational methods in life sciences and their practical integration into K–12 curricula. Many pre-service teachers lack exposure to scalable, interactive tools for exploring dynamic biological processes (e.g., population genetics, protein folding, or ecosystem modeling), limiting their ability to design authentic, inquiry-driven lessons. To address this, we propose developing and testing a suite of agent-based models and simulations that mirror real-world biological phenomena, optimized for HPC environments. These simulations will enable pre-service teachers to manipulate variables at scales impractical for physical classrooms—such as modeling evolutionary trajectories across millions of generations or visualizing molecular interactions in real time—while simultaneously training them to deploy such resources in diverse educational settings. Computational workflows will be designed using parallelized Python frameworks (e.g., Mesa) and containerized for portability across HPC clusters and classroom hardware. Machine learning methods will analyze user interaction patterns to refine simulation usability and pedagogical effectiveness. The project’s outcomes include: (1) a repository of open-access, curriculum-aligned computational modules for biology education, (2) quantitative data on how HPC-driven modeling impacts teachers’ conceptual mastery of systems-level biology, and (3) frameworks for integrating computational thinking into teacher training programs. By equipping educators with the skills to utilize advanced computing resources, this work aims to transform how biology is taught, fostering student engagement with data-rich, interdisciplinary problems that reflect modern scientific practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach biology programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze the structural and semantic relationships between ethical systems and symbolic narratives across philosophical traditions and religious texts. The central research problem addresses the challenge of systematically tracing how abstract ethical concepts (e.g., justice, virtue, duty) are operationalized through culturally specific narratives, rituals, and symbolic practices within and across traditions. Current scholarship lacks scalable methods to analyze these connections at the necessary resolution, given the vast, multilingual corpus of primary sources and commentaries spanning 2,500 years. We will employ high-performance computing to implement a three-phase methodology: first, training multilingual transformer models on curated philosophical and religious corpora in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, Arabic, Greek, Latin, and English to detect ethical reasoning patterns; second, applying graph neural networks to map conceptual dependencies between normative claims and ritual prescriptions in texts like the Upanishads, Analects, and Summa Theologica; third, simulating cross-traditional conceptual synthesis through agent-based modeling of dialogical networks. The computational workflow requires GPU-accelerated text embedding, distributed training of large language models tailored to philosophical discourse, and iterative simulation runs to test epistemic coherence under different synthetic interactions. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing 50+ ethical-symbolic correlations across eight traditions, (2) quantitative evidence for or against universalist claims in comparative ethics, and (3) novel digital methods for preserving argumentative context in cross-cultural hermeneutics. By enabling macroanalysis of ethical symbolism’s epistemological functions, this work aims to redefine interdisciplinary scholarship on philosophy of religion while establishing computational humanities infrastructure for future studies in axiological systems.
cip_definition: A general program that combines the study of philosophy and religious studies. Includes instruction in logic; ethics; epistemology; symbolism; phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature, and art of religion; and world religions.

abstract: The increasing availability of large-scale, high-dimensional datasets in fields such as public health and environmental science has exposed critical limitations in traditional statistical methodologies, particularly in Bayesian hierarchical modeling and non-parametric regression. These approaches, while theoretically robust, often face prohibitive computational demands when applied to modern datasets due to their reliance on iterative sampling techniques and complex dependency structures. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing scalable computational frameworks optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. Specifically, we propose the implementation of parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms designed to leverage distributed memory architectures, enabling efficient sampling from high-dimensional posterior distributions.
