Additionally, we will investigate adaptive Monte Carlo methods combined with stochastic gradient-based variational inference to reduce convergence times in hierarchical models. The computational workflows will be integrated with non-parametric bootstrap resampling techniques, parallelized across multiple nodes to handle massive datasets. By utilizing HPC resources, this research aims to overcome existing bottlenecks in statistical computation, facilitating the analysis of datasets that are currently intractable due to size or complexity. The expected outcomes include novel algorithmic implementations that bridge statistical theory with computational efficiency, validated through case studies in climate modeling and epidemiological surveillance. These advancements will not only expand the applicability of Bayesian and non-parametric methods but also provide open-source tools to the statistical community, fostering reproducible research in data-intensive domains. The project underscores the critical role of HPC in advancing modern statistical methodology, ensuring that theoretical rigor keeps pace with the growing scale of real-world data challenges.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address challenges in analyzing high-dimensional, sparse biological datasets with complex error structures, a recurring problem in biometry and biometric applications. Traditional statistical tools often struggle with computational inefficiency or convergence issues when applied to such data, particularly in contexts like longitudinal studies of dynamic biological systems or spatially resolved multi-omics datasets. The proposed research will focus on advancing Bayesian hierarchical modeling frameworks and machine learning techniques optimized for sparse data, integrating adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, variational inference, and ensemble neural networks. Key computational challenges include efficiently estimating high-dimensional parameter spaces, managing memory-intensive covariance matrices in spatial-temporal models, and enabling real-time uncertainty quantification. To overcome these barriers, the project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize model fitting across multi-node clusters, implement distributed GPU-accelerated deep learning pipelines, and optimize memory allocation for large-scale matrix operations. A central innovation involves developing open-source software tools that automate resource-aware algorithm selection based on data sparsity and error complexity. The expected outcomes include (1) novel computational workflows for analyzing unbalanced longitudinal datasets in agricultural trait monitoring, (2) improved inference methods for sparse spatial proteomics data, and (3) benchmarked performance gains in model runtime and accuracy compared to existing biostatistical packages. Successful implementation will provide the broader biometry community with scalable, interoperable resources for complex biological data analysis, directly benefiting applications such as precision agriculture yield optimization and environmental stress response modeling. The requested HPC allocation is critical for testing computational architectures, validating statistical properties through large-scale simulations, and ensuring reproducibility across diverse biological use cases.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics and other computational methods to the study of problems in the biological sciences and related fields in agriculture and natural resources. Includes instruction in computational biology, mathematical statistics, matrix algebra, applied calculus, experimental design, linear modeling, sampling theory, stochastic processes, spatial and temporal analysis, longitudinal analysis, sparse/unbalanced data and complex error, and applications to such topics as population genetics, animal breeding, forest genetics, population dynamics, wildlife biometry, ecology, and agricultural and natural resource management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate data-driven, computationally intensive models to optimize individualized learning strategies for elementary students with disabilities, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of scalability in special education research. Current methods for designing personalized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual, time-intensive assessments and trial-and-error adjustments, which often fail to account for the complex interplay of cognitive, behavioral, and environmental factors affecting learning outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework that integrates multimodal student data—including academic performance metrics, behavioral observation logs, and speech-language pathology reports—to predict optimal instructional interventions. Using natural language processing (NLP), we will analyze unstructured text from IEPs and teacher narratives to identify patterns in successful intervention strategies. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom dynamics under varying instructional conditions to evaluate the scalability of interventions across diverse learner profiles. The computational demands of training deep learning models on large-scale, longitudinal datasets (spanning 5+ years of anonymized student records) and running high-fidelity simulations necessitate parallelized computing and GPU acceleration. Outcomes will include an open-source tool for generating evidence-based intervention recommendations and a simulated classroom environment to train educators in adaptive teaching practices. This work directly supports the program’s focus on improving pedagogical methods for special education by providing teachers with scalable, data-informed strategies to address heterogeneous learning needs. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model refinement, which are infeasible on standard institutional infrastructure. Results will advance both the technical understanding of computational education research and the practical implementation of equitable, individualized instruction in K-5 special education classrooms.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Elementary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the elementary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for elementary special education; and teaching elementary education subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize sustainable and ergonomic design workflows in home furnishings and equipment installation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in material selection, spatial planning, and consumer customization. Current practices rely on manual iteration and generalized guidelines, which often result in resource waste, suboptimal user comfort, and limited scalability for personalized solutions. The research will integrate parametric design algorithms, biomechanical simulations, and lifecycle assessment models to analyze complex variables such as material durability, human ergonomics, and environmental impact. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) will evaluate stress distributions in modular furniture systems under diverse usage scenarios, while agent-based modeling will simulate spatial interactions in dynamic home environments. Machine learning techniques will be applied to consumer preference datasets to identify latent patterns in aesthetic and functional priorities across demographics. By parallelizing these workflows on HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in multi-objective optimization tasks, enabling real-time feedback for designers and installers. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating resource-efficient design prototypes, predictive models for longevity of upholstery textiles under mechanical wear, and a decision-support system balancing cost, sustainability, and user well-being. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational engineering, human-centered design, and environmental science, offering novel methodologies for an industry traditionally underserved by advanced analytics. The resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated simulations of textile-microstructure interactions and large-scale optimization runs exploring trade-offs between circular economy principles and manufacturing feasibility. Results will be validated through partnerships with vocational training centers, ensuring translational impact on workforce development in the home furnishings sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in home furnishings and decorations. Includes instruction in selecting, purchasing, and designing home furnishings, decorations, and equipment; floral design; accessory construction; textiles; and upholstery.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the comparative analysis of ethical frameworks across religious and philosophical traditions. The central problem lies in systematically identifying, categorizing, and modeling patterns in moral reasoning within large, multilingual textual corpora spanning diverse cultural contexts. While qualitative methods dominate the humanities, the scale and complexity of cross-tradition analysis—encompassing texts from Classical Greek philosophy, Mahayana Buddhist sutras, Abrahamic theological commentaries, and modern secular ethics—require computational augmentation to detect latent semantic structures and longitudinal shifts. The proposed approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned for ancient and specialized religious vocabularies, with network analysis to map conceptual relationships. Computational workflows will be designed to handle non-Latin scripts, ambiguous metaphorical language, and fragmentary historical sources, while ethical guardrails will ensure culturally sensitive interpretation of sacred texts. Key tasks include parallel processing of digitized manuscripts, training custom embeddings for domain-specific terminology, and simulating argumentative coherence across traditions using graph-based models. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a scalable computational framework for cross-cultural philosophical analysis, 2) quantitative evidence supporting or challenging existing theories about universal versus culturally contingent ethical principles, and 3) publicly accessible datasets linking moral concepts to their contextualized interpretations. By bridging hermeneutic scholarship with computational rigor, this work aims to demonstrate how HPC can expand the methodological horizons of philosophy and religious studies while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between the humanities and data sciences. The requested resources are critical for managing memory-intensive NLP pipelines and iterative model training across heterogeneous textual datasets exceeding 10TB in aggregate.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in philosophy and religion, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of U.S. constitutional jurisprudence through computational legal analytics, focusing on the interplay between judicial decision-making patterns and sociopolitical dynamics. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on qualitative analysis of case law, limiting scalability and obscuring systemic trends across large corpora of judicial opinions. This study addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to quantitatively map shifts in legal reasoning within Supreme Court opinions, with emphasis on how implicit biases, textual ambiguity, and historical context influence interpretations of constitutional principles. The project employs natural language processing (NLP) techniques to parse over 50,000 pages of federal court decisions, concurrences, and dissents, spanning 1950–2023, augmented by metadata on judicial appointments, legislative changes, and public opinion data. Machine learning models (including transformer-based architectures and graph neural networks) will be trained to identify latent patterns in argumentation strategies, semantic drift in key constitutional terms, and network effects among judicial citations. A novel contribution involves simulating hypothetical decision pathways using generative AI to model how alternative doctrinal frameworks might impact precedent formation under varying sociopolitical conditions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database linking quantified legal reasoning metrics to historical events, (2) predictive models of jurisprudential evolution under emerging constitutional challenges, and (3) methodological advancements in computational legal theory. By bridging data science and constitutional hermeneutics, this work aims to provide policymakers and legal practitioners with evidence-based tools to anticipate systemic impacts of judicial nominations and constitutional challenges while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for analyzing law as a complex adaptive system. The scale of textual analysis, parallelized model training, and real-time simulation of multi-variable legal scenarios necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve operational feasibility.
cip_title: American/ US Law/ Legal Studies/ Jurisprudence
cip_definition: An advanced, professional program of the U.S. legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the structure and dynamics of neutron-rich nuclei through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled ab initio nuclear theory. Neutron-rich systems near the drip line exhibit complex many-body phenomena—such as enhanced pairing correlations, shell evolution, and collective excitations—that challenge existing nuclear models. Current approaches, which often rely on phenomenological interactions or truncated model spaces, struggle to predict properties like binding energies, transition strengths, and reaction cross-sections for these nuclei. This work proposes large-scale computations using chiral effective field theory (χEFT) nucleon-nucleon interactions to systematically model medium-mass nuclei (A ≈ 50–100) with controlled uncertainty estimates. The research will deploy coupled-cluster and in-medium similarity renormalization group (IM-SRG) methods to solve the many-body Schrödinger equation in expanded harmonic oscillator basis spaces, explicitly incorporating three-nucleon forces and continuum effects. These calculations will leverage HPC resources to diagonalize matrices with dimensions exceeding 10^9, requiring optimized MPI/OpenMP parallelization across thousands of cores. Key outcomes include predictions of ground-state energies, excitation spectra, and beta-decay rates for isotopes relevant to r-process nucleosynthesis, as well as benchmarks against recent FRIB experimental data. The project will also advance numerical methods for handling the computational complexity of open quantum systems near the drip line. By bridging χEFT with observed nuclear properties, this work aims to refine foundational nuclear models, inform future experiments, and enhance predictive capabilities for astrophysical processes and rare isotope applications. The requested computing allocation will support 20M core-hours on a GPU-accelerated system for matrix construction and iterative solvers, alongside 500 TB of storage for intermediate wavefunction data and cross-code validation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of atomic nuclei. Includes instruction in nuclear reaction theory, quantum mechanics, energy conservation, nuclear fission and fusion, strong and weak forces, nuclear modeling, nuclear decay, nucleon scattering, pairing, photon and electron reactions, the physics of nuclear effects, statistical methods, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of high-resolution digital imaging and prepress design workflows, which are increasingly limited by conventional computing infrastructure. As the complexity of graphic design projects escalates—driven by 4K/8K media, non-destructive editing layers, and real-time collaborative workflows—existing tools struggle to maintain efficiency during resource-intensive tasks such as raster image processing, vector rendering, and dynamic typographic simulations. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and test optimized algorithms for parallelized image compositing, GPU-accelerated font rendering, and AI-driven layout optimization. By leveraging distributed computing frameworks, we aim to reduce processing times for multi-gigabyte design files by orders of magnitude while maintaining print-ready color accuracy and resolution fidelity. Additionally, the project will prototype machine learning models trained on design pattern datasets to automate repetitive prepress tasks, such as bleed margin calibration and color space conversion, which currently require manual intervention. The computational workflows will be validated against industry-standard Adobe Creative Cloud and Affinity Suite benchmarks, with performance metrics focusing on throughput, latency, and energy efficiency. Successful implementation is expected to yield open-source tools for scalable desktop publishing pipelines, directly benefiting graphic design education and small-to-medium print enterprises. This work will also contribute new methodologies for integrating HPC capabilities into non-STEM disciplines, demonstrating how computational resource allocation can advance creative workflows traditionally excluded from high-performance infrastructure discussions. Outcomes will be disseminated through design technology conferences and partnerships with digital imaging software developers to influence next-generation tool development.
cip_title: Prepress/ Desktop Publishing and Digital Imaging Design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the layout, design and typographic arrangement of printed and/or electronic graphic and textual products. Includes instruction in printing and lithographic equipment and operations, computer hardware and software, digital imaging, print preparation, page layout and design, desktop publishing, and applicable principles of graphic design and web page design.

abstract: Developmental education programs aim to address systemic inequities in postsecondary readiness by equipping educators with evidence-based strategies to support underprepared learners. However, optimizing instructional interventions remains challenging due to the dynamic, multivariate nature of learning processes and the limited scalability of traditional classroom studies. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models of student learning trajectories in developmental education contexts. Using anonymized institutional datasets encompassing demographic, behavioral, and performance metrics from 15 community colleges, we will implement agent-based modeling to simulate how combinations of instructional strategies (e.g., adaptive scaffolding, metacognitive feedback loops) interact with learner characteristics in virtual classroom environments. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess intervention efficacy across diverse synthetic cohorts, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze discussion forum interactions from existing online developmental courses to refine model parameters. The computational workflow will integrate differential equation systems modeling knowledge retention and reinforcement learning agents representing student decision-making. HPC capabilities are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space (>10^6 combinations), multiscale temporal resolutions (minute-to-semester timescales), and ensemble simulations required for robust statistical inference. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold effects in intervention timing and sequencing, (2) predictive frameworks for personalizing developmental curricula, and (3) open-source tools enabling educators to simulate localized strategy implementations. By mapping complex interactions between pedagogy and learner variability, this work will provide actionable insights for designing equitable, scalable developmental instruction while advancing computational education research methodologies.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach educational strategies for assisting students who are perceived as underprepared for the academic rigor of college-level coursework at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational frameworks for optimizing next-generation energy storage systems and hybrid computer architectures, addressing critical bottlenecks in efficiency and reliability at the intersection of electrical engineering and computer science. Emerging energy storage technologies, such as superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) and solid-state battery arrays, require high-fidelity modeling of multi-physics interactions—including thermal dynamics, electromagnetic field behavior, and material degradation—under variable load conditions. Concurrently, heterogeneous computing systems integrating classical and quantum processing units demand novel resource allocation strategies to balance energy consumption, latency, and fault tolerance in real-time applications. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining large-scale parallelized finite element simulations, tensor network-based quantum circuit emulation, and reinforcement learning-driven optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 1) distributed electromagnetic-thermal co-simulation of SMES systems across 10^4+ mesh elements using GPU-accelerated solvers, 2) time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (t-DMRG) simulations of quantum-classical interface protocols, and 3) multi-objective neural architecture search for adaptive task scheduling in heterogeneous compute clusters. The computational workflows will leverage containerized environments with MPI-OpenMP hybrid parallelism and dynamic resource scaling to manage memory-intensive tensor operations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for energy storage capacity fade under high-frequency cycling, open-source frameworks for quantum-classical co-design, and energy-aware scheduling algorithms demonstrating >30% efficiency gains in simulated smart grid test cases. By bridging materials modeling, quantum computing emulation, and distributed system optimization, this work aims to advance both methodological capabilities in scientific computing and the practical deployment of sustainable energy-compute infrastructures. The requested HPC allocations are essential for achieving the required numerical precision and parametric exploration scale within tractable timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components computer theory, computing problems and solutions, including electrical power generation systems; the design of computer systems and user interfaces; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification. c and the design of computer systems and user interfaces

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern printing operations by developing data-driven optimization models for resource allocation, production scheduling, and quality control in commercial printing workflows. Despite advances in digital printing technologies, many facilities struggle with balancing cost, speed, and environmental impact due to complex variables including substrate diversity, ink chemistry constraints, and fluctuating client demands. Current analytical tools often fail to account for real-time process interdependencies or the scale of multi-stage production systems. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate plant-wide operations through discrete-event simulation frameworks enhanced by machine learning algorithms trained on historical production data. Computational experiments will focus on three key areas: 1) dynamic scheduling under equipment failure scenarios, 2) waste reduction through predictive ink viscosity modeling, and 3) energy consumption optimization across hybrid analog/digital workflows. Large-scale parallelization will enable simultaneous evaluation of thousands of parameter combinations through Monte Carlo methods, while neural networks trained on GPU clusters will identify nonlinear relationships between press configurations and output quality metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit for printing managers, validated through industry partnerships with three regional commercial printers. The computational approach will advance sustainable practices in graphic communications by reducing material waste by an estimated 15-20% in test scenarios and improving equipment utilization rates. By applying HPC capabilities to traditionally non-technical domains, this work bridges critical gaps between operational research and practical printing management challenges while establishing computational reproducibility standards for the graphic arts industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical and managerial knowledge and skills to the processes and procedures of managing printing operations from initial design through finished product distribution. Includes instruction in the principles of graphic communications design and production; quality control; printing operations management; computerization; printing plant management; business finance and marketing; logistics and distribution; personnel supervision and leadership; and professional standards in the graphic communications industry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize mineral extraction processes in underground mining environments, with a focus on improving efficiency while minimizing environmental disruption. A critical challenge in modern mining is balancing economic viability with ecological sustainability, particularly in complex geological settings where traditional methods struggle to predict dynamic rock behavior, ore distribution, and groundwater interactions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-physics simulations integrating geomechanical modeling, computational fluid dynamics, and machine learning-driven ore grade prediction. The computational approach will utilize finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress redistribution during excavation, coupled with discrete fracture network models to map fluid flow through fractured rock systems. Concurrently, convolutional neural networks will process historical drilling data and real-time sensor inputs to refine resource estimation accuracy. These interdependent models require parallelized computing architectures to handle the terabyte-scale datasets typical of mine-scale simulations, including 3D lithological maps and continuous monitoring data streams. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across safety thresholds, extraction sequences, and equipment configurations that are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying optimal cut-and-fill sequences, real-time risk assessment modules for mine collapse prevention, and dynamic resource allocation strategies that reduce waste by 15–20% compared to conventional methods. By creating a digital twin capability for mining operations, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for sustainable resource extraction, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance technical solutions in mineral development. The resulting open-source framework will be validated against case studies from copper and rare earth element mines, with implications for reducing energy consumption and water usage across the mining sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic project scheduling under uncertainty, a critical challenge in business project management. Traditional scheduling tools often fail to account for real-world complexities such as fluctuating resource availability, interdependent task delays, and probabilistic risk impacts, leading to cost overruns and timeline deviations. We propose a hybrid computational approach integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to model large-scale projects with hundreds of interdependent tasks and stochastic variables. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute parallelized simulations that capture diverse risk scenarios across construction, product development, and IT implementation case studies drawn from industry partners. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical project data (including task durations, resource allocation patterns, and risk registers) to train predictive models for delay propagation and bottleneck identification. The computational workflow will incorporate integer programming to balance cost, time, and quality constraints while maintaining human-interpretable scheduling logic. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that enables project managers to visualize trade-offs between competing objectives under uncertainty, assess resilience of different scheduling strategies, and dynamically reallocate resources. By enabling rapid analysis of complex scheduling scenarios that would be computationally intractable on standard hardware, this research aims to advance evidence-based project management practices. The results will contribute methodological innovations in computational project management while addressing practical needs for adaptive scheduling in business environments characterized by volatile markets and supply chain disruptions. Successful implementation will be validated through comparative analysis against traditional critical path methods using industry benchmarks for schedule adherence and resource utilization efficiency.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply quantitative and qualitative knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage projects in a wide range of fields and occupations. Includes instruction in project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing real-time digital content delivery across heterogeneous networks, a critical issue for media producers and streaming platforms aiming to balance quality, accessibility, and resource efficiency. As demand for high-resolution video, immersive audio, and interactive digital media surges, existing adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithms often fail to dynamically account for fluctuating global network conditions, device diversity, and user engagement patterns. This results in suboptimal viewer experiences, inflated infrastructure costs, and excess energy consumption. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing machine learning (ML)-driven ABR models trained on large-scale datasets of viewer interactions, network performance metrics, and multimedia content attributes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-node content delivery networks (CDNs) under diverse geographic and demographic scenarios, process terabytes of streaming logs, and iteratively train deep reinforcement learning agents. Computational workflows will include parallelized network emulation using tools like Mininet, distributed training of neural networks across GPU clusters, and real-time analytics of A/B test outcomes. The scale of data—spanning millions of concurrent streams, varying resolutions (4K/8K), and emerging formats like volumetric video—necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve timely results. Expected outcomes include open-source ABR algorithms that reduce latency by 15–30%, improve quality-of-experience (QoE) metrics by 20%, and decrease bandwidth waste in edge computing environments. This work will directly benefit media technology researchers and industry partners, while advancing scholarly understanding of computational methods in digital communication systems. Findings will be disseminated through communications conferences and journals, with potential applications in next-gen 5G/6G streaming infrastructure and equitable access initiatives for underserved regions.
cip_title: Radio, Television, and Digital Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in radio, television, and digital communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and semantic evolution of non-binding legal instruments—such as memoranda of understanding, soft law agreements, and community-led dispute resolution frameworks—across decentralized governance systems. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable computational tools to map how non-enforceable legal texts accumulate normative influence over time, particularly in contexts where formal legal infrastructure is absent or hybridized with informal practices (e.g., digital communities, transnational environmental coalitions). Current scholarship relies on manual textual analysis, limiting the scope to small corpora and obscuring macro-scale patterns in language adaptation, cross-referential networks, and clause repurposing. To address this gap, the project will employ transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned on a novel dataset of 15,000+ non-professional legal documents, spanning grassroots organizations, open-source governance charters, and cross-cultural mediation protocols. Computational workflows will include dynamic topic modeling to track conceptual shifts across temporal and cultural boundaries, graph neural networks to visualize interdependencies between clauses, and contrastive learning to identify latent normative hierarchies within ostensibly neutral frameworks. The HPC environment is critical for training large-scale embeddings on heterogeneous, multilingual texts and simulating iterative revisions under hypothetical governance scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible toolkit for quantifying the “normative weight” of non-binding legal language, (2) evidence-based frameworks for improving participatory drafting processes in non-jurisdictional contexts, and (3) novel metrics to assess the durability and adaptability of informal legal systems. By bridging computational linguistics and non-professional legal theory, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven governance design in emergent, decentralized communities.
cip_definition: Any program in non-professional legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing community-based social service delivery through computational modeling of complex, large-scale human systems. The research problem centers on the challenge of designing equitable, data-driven interventions in contexts such as homelessness prevention, substance use treatment access, and crisis response, where dynamic interactions between individuals, institutions, and policies create emergent outcomes that defy traditional analytical methods. Current approaches often rely on static demographic data or oversimplified statistical models, limiting their ability to account for real-world variables like spatial inequities, service network capacity constraints, and behavioral feedback loops. The proposed work will develop agent-based simulation models that integrate anonymized administrative records (e.g., housing assistance applications, public health referrals) with synthetic population datasets to replicate service ecosystems at urban and regional scales. Computational experiments will test how varying resource allocation strategies—such as shifting funding thresholds for eligibility programs or reconfiguring multidisciplinary care teams—affect long-term service gaps and systemic disparities. Machine learning methods will be applied to calibrate models using historical service utilization patterns and identify high-impact leverage points for intervention. By simulating millions of agent interactions across diverse demographic profiles and policy scenarios, this approach will quantify trade-offs between efficiency, accessibility, and equity in human services design. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools for local agencies to evaluate proposed programs pre-implementation and evidence-based frameworks for prioritizing resources in multi-stakeholder environments. The project represents a novel integration of computational social science methodologies into applied human services research, with potential to transform how public administrators model the cascading effects of systemic interventions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and provision of human and social services to individuals and communities and prepares individuals to work in public and private human services agencies and organizations. Includes instruction in the social sciences, psychology, principles of social service, human services policy, planning and evaluation, social services law and administration, and applications to particular issues, services, localities, and populations.

abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the supporting structures of teeth, is driven by complex interactions between dysbiotic microbial communities, host immune responses, and genetic and environmental factors. Current clinical strategies often fail to predict disease progression or personalize therapeutic interventions due to gaps in understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of host-microbe crosstalk at the gingival interface. This project seeks to address this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that integrate single-cell transcriptomic data, spatially resolved metabolomic profiles, and biomechanical simulations of periodontal tissue remodeling. A hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, deep learning for pattern recognition in microbial metagenomic datasets, and finite element analysis will be employed to simulate the evolution of periodontal microenvironments under inflammatory stress. The computational framework will be trained and validated using longitudinal clinical data, including 3D intraoral scans, cytokine profiles, and microbial sequencing from a cohort of 200 patients with stage III/IV periodontitis. Key objectives include identifying nonlinear signaling thresholds that trigger irreversible bone loss, mapping metabolic networks linking specific pathobionts to tissue degradation phenotypes, and predicting patient-specific responses to biomechanical interventions such as occlusal adjustment. By elucidating mechanistic drivers of periodontitis heterogeneity, this work aims to generate actionable biomarkers for early intervention and computational tools to optimize regenerative therapies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing stochastic simulations, and iterating complex neural networks. Outcomes will advance precision periodontics by bridging molecular-scale discovery with clinical decision-making, while establishing a computational pipeline adaptable to other oral-inflammatory pathologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance trauma counseling interventions through the development of a multimodal computational framework for analyzing neurobiological and psychosocial correlates of trauma recovery. Current limitations in trauma treatment stem from a poor understanding of how individual differences in neurocognitive resilience interact with therapeutic modalities, particularly in populations with complex trauma histories. To address this, we propose integrating dynamic computational models of neural network plasticity with large-scale, longitudinal datasets capturing psychophysiological markers (e.g., EEG, heart rate variability) and clinical outcomes from trauma-focused therapies. The research will employ machine learning architectures to identify latent patterns in heterogeneous data streams, simulating how trauma-related neuroadaptations influence therapeutic response trajectories. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional neuroimaging data, running parallelized agent-based models of memory reconsolidation processes, and optimizing neural network architectures for personalized outcome prediction. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to stratify individuals by probable response to specific trauma interventions (e.g., EMDR, somatic experiencing) and mechanistic insights into how relational trauma alters default mode network connectivity. By bridging computational neuroscience with clinical counseling practice, this work aims to establish data-driven protocols for optimizing crisis intervention timing, dosing, and modality selection—advancing precision medicine in trauma care while reducing trial-and-error approaches that prolong patient suffering. The computational tools developed will be open-sourced to support replication studies in underrepresented populations, including veterans and survivors of systemic violence.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on understanding elements of traumatic exposure, trauma-sensitive care, and crisis intervention. Includes instruction in disaster response, grief and loss counseling, crisis intervention and management, trauma counseling, neurobiology of trauma, PTSD and combat-related trauma, relational trauma and treatment of trauma-related disorders.

abstract: Agricultural enterprises face increasing pressure to optimize production efficiency, resource allocation, and supply chain resilience under dynamic environmental and market conditions. While precision agriculture technologies generate vast datasets—from soil sensors to equipment telemetry—many agricultural businesses lack the computational capacity to integrate these high-dimensional datasets with economic models for real-time decision support. This project proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to analyze heterogeneous agricultural data streams, simulate market and production scenarios, and recommend risk-informed management strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between farm operations, commodity markets, and logistics networks under stochastic climate and pricing conditions. Machine learning ensembles will be trained on historical yield, weather, and market data to predict regional production trends and price volatility, while mixed-integer programming will optimize multi-objective decisions such as planting schedules, input purchasing, and contract negotiations. Computational workflows will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainties in crop yields, input costs, and export demand cycles. The project will validate models using anonymized operational data from partner agribusinesses in the Midwest U.S., focusing on corn and soybean systems. By integrating agronomic, economic, and logistical variables at previously infeasible scales, this research aims to produce adaptive decision-support tools that help agricultural enterprises mitigate financial risks, reduce input waste, and align production with market opportunities. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations of regional supply chains, hyperparameter tuning of machine learning models across thousands of cores, and iterative optimization runs requiring low-latency parallel processing. Outcomes will advance computational methods in agricultural business analytics while providing open-source workflow templates to help small- and medium-sized enterprises adopt data-driven management practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on modern business and economic principles involved in the organization, operation, and management of agricultural enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in enhancing crop resilience to abiotic stressors, such as drought and soil salinity, which threaten global food security. Traditional breeding and experimental approaches are limited by the complexity of plant stress-response networks, which involve dynamic gene regulatory interactions, metabolic pathways, and epigenetic modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrative computational framework combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), transcriptomic network modeling, and machine learning-driven predictive simulations. The research will utilize large-scale genomic datasets from staple crops (e.g., rice, wheat) subjected to stress conditions, alongside environmental and phenotypic data. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-omics datasets to identify candidate genes and regulatory elements linked to stress tolerance. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate crop growth under variable climatic scenarios, integrating genetic, physiological, and environmental parameters to predict trait performance. These computational workflows require substantial memory and processing power due to the dimensionality of genomic data, the iterative nature of machine learning optimization, and the stochasticity inherent in multi-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-priority genetic targets for breeding programs, predictive models for stress-resilient crop phenotypes, and open-source tools for scalable genomic analysis. By accelerating the discovery of adaptive traits, this work aims to directly inform precision breeding strategies, reduce agricultural losses under climate change, and contribute to sustainable food systems. The requested computing resources are essential to manage data complexity and deliver actionable insights within biologically relevant timelines.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Animal/ Plant/ Veterinary Science and Related Fields, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural, animal, plant, or veterinary science and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between personality traits, neurophysiological markers, and contextual behavioral responses through computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome existing methodological limitations. Traditional personality psychology frameworks—such as Freudian, Skinnerian, and Rogerian models—often rely on static, reductionist assessments, limiting their ability to capture the temporal and multi-layered complexity of personality as a system. To address this, we propose developing an integrative agent-based model (ABM) that simulates how stable personality characteristics interact with situational variables and neurophysiological processes (e.g., stress-response pathways, dopaminergic activation) to shape behavior. The ABM will incorporate parameters derived from empirical datasets, including longitudinal behavioral studies, functional neuroimaging, and psychopharmacological interventions, to test competing hypotheses about trait-state interactions. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to optimize model fit and identify nonlinear patterns in high-dimensional data. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations across diverse theoretical scenarios (e.g., trait activation thresholds, reinforcement learning dynamics) and conducting Bayesian parameter estimation with large posterior distributions. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework that reconciles divergent theories of personality structure and generates testable predictions about individual differences in adaptive and maladaptive behaviors. This work will provide novel insights into the neurocomputational mechanisms underlying personality, bridging gaps between psychodynamic, behavioral, and physiological perspectives. The resulting open-source tools and simulated datasets will serve as a resource for the broader research community, enabling hypothesis-driven exploration of personality dynamics at unprecedented granularity. By integrating historically siloed theories within a unified computational architecture, this project aims to advance personality psychology into a new era of data-intensive, theory-generative science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the unique organization of fairly permanent characteristics that set the individual apart from other individuals and, at the same time, determine how others respond to that individual. Includes instruction in Freudian, Skinnerian, Rogerian, and Ellisonian psychology; neo-Freudian psychology; psychological systems, neurophysiology, and psychopharmacology.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision metal fabrication processes in machine shop applications by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize machining dynamics. Traditional trial-and-error approaches to toolpath planning, cutting parameter selection, and thermal management in subtractive manufacturing often lead to material waste, tool wear, and suboptimal surface finishes. To address these challenges, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate multi-physics interactions during machining operations. High-fidelity models will analyze stress distributions, heat generation, and material deformation for common alloys (e.g., steel, titanium) under varying spindle speeds, feed rates, and coolant conditions. ML algorithms will process experimental sensor data (vibration, temperature, force) from CNC machines to validate and refine simulations. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these resource-intensive simulations across thousands of parameter combinations and enabling real-time predictive analytics. Expected outcomes include optimized machining parameter sets to minimize tool wear and energy consumption, predictive models for surface integrity, and a publicly accessible database of simulation results. This work will directly support small-scale manufacturing enterprises and vocational training programs by providing data-driven guidelines to improve machining efficiency and part quality. The integration of computational modeling into machine shop workflows represents a novel cross-disciplinary advance, bridging traditional manufacturing practices with Industry 4.0 methodologies. All developed tools and datasets will be disseminated through partnerships with regional technical colleges to enhance curriculum development in machine shop technology programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and modify metal parts in support of other manufacturing, repair or design activities, or as an independent business.

abstract: This project addresses the challenge of automating real-time auditing processes in large-scale financial systems, a critical need in modern accounting that demands integration with advanced computational methods. Traditional auditing frameworks struggle to efficiently analyze high-volume transactional data streams, particularly in decentralized or blockchain-based environments, leading to latency in anomaly detection and compliance risks. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a hybrid machine learning and cryptographic verification system optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The research will implement distributed graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex transactional networks across terabyte-scale datasets while leveraging zero-knowledge proofs for privacy-preserving validation of suspicious patterns. Computational workflows will be parallelized across GPU clusters to enable sub-second analysis intervals, with iterative model training incorporating adversarial samples to improve robustness against evolving financial fraud tactics. The project will further design a novel consensus mechanism tailored for auditing smart contracts, requiring large-scale simulations of Byzantine fault tolerance scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework that reduces false positive rates in anomaly detection by at least 40% compared to existing tools while maintaining interpretability for regulatory compliance. This work will advance interdisciplinary methodologies at the accounting-computer science interface by establishing scalable benchmarks for real-time audit automation and contributing optimized tensor operations for financial graph processing. The resulting infrastructure will directly benefit both academic researchers studying decentralized finance and enterprises requiring auditable, low-latency transaction systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines accounting with computer science and/or computer studies.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the emergence and stability of decentralized economic equilibria in dynamic, heterogeneous-agent systems with adaptive learning mechanisms. Traditional equilibrium models in mathematical economics often rely on representative agents or static expectations, limiting their ability to capture complex interactions in systems where agents exhibit heterogeneous preferences, incomplete information, and time-varying behavioral rules. The project addresses this gap by constructing a high-dimensional stochastic game-theoretic model where agents dynamically update strategies via reinforcement learning, constrained by evolving network structures and resource availability. The computational approach combines large-scale Monte Carlo simulations with numerical solutions to coupled Fokker-Planck equations, enabling the study of phase transitions in equilibrium formation under stochastic shocks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of agent interactions, Bayesian estimation of time-varying parameters, and sensitivity analyses across multi-dimensional policy spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative criteria for equilibrium robustness in decentralized markets with adaptive agents, (2) scalable algorithms for simulating learning dynamics in heterogeneous populations, and (3) empirically testable predictions about systemic risk propagation in networked economies. The results will advance interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of stochastic control theory, behavioral economics, and complexity science, with applications to policy design for digital market regulation and climate-resilient infrastructure planning. By integrating mathematical rigor with computational scalability, this work aims to bridge theoretical gaps in dynamic equilibrium analysis while providing open-source tools for reproducible, data-driven economic modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical methods to the development of economic theory, models, and quantitative analysis. Includes instruction in data analysis, applied business economics, calculus, econometrics, linear algebra, microeconomic theory, probability, and statistical methods.

abstract: Modern agricultural operations face increasing complexity due to the need to integrate heterogeneous data streams—such as weather patterns, soil health metrics, crop yields, livestock biometrics, and market fluctuations—into actionable management decisions. Current analytical tools often lack the capacity to process these multidimensional datasets at scale, limiting the ability to optimize operational efficiency, financial planning, and long-term sustainability. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision-support framework for farm and ranch management. The research will focus on creating agent-based models that simulate farm operations under variable environmental and economic conditions, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict outcomes of management strategies. These models will incorporate real-time data from IoT sensors, historical yield records, and regional market trends to evaluate resource allocation scenarios, including labor distribution, equipment use, capital investment, and risk mitigation. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle large-scale spatial-temporal datasets and stochastic simulations of climate variability, pest outbreaks, and commodity price shifts. By leveraging HPC resources, the project aims to generate predictive insights into optimal planting schedules, livestock rotation plans, and financial hedging strategies while accounting for regulatory constraints and estate planning considerations. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for adaptive farm management, validated against empirical data from partner agricultural enterprises. This work will advance precision agriculture by enabling dynamic, data-driven decision-making at the enterprise level, directly contributing to improved profitability and resilience in farm operations. The scalability of the proposed framework will also support policy analyses on the economic impacts of agricultural subsidies or climate adaptation programs, fostering broader interdisciplinary collaboration in agricultural sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage farms, ranches, and similar enterprises. Includes instruction in applicable agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, taxation, capitalization, purchasing, government programs and regulations, operational planning and budgeting, contracts and negotiation, and estate planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the Catalan language, with a focus on analyzing dialectal variation and historical linguistic evolution. Catalan, spoken by over 10 million people across diverse regions, exhibits significant dialectal fragmentation and sociolinguistic complexity. Traditional methods in Catalan philology and dialectology struggle to efficiently process large-scale textual corpora or model subtle linguistic changes across time and geography. This project addresses these limitations by applying machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to three interconnected objectives: (1) training dialect identification models using historical and contemporary texts to map regional linguistic boundaries; (2) conducting diachronic analyses of morphological and syntactic shifts in Catalan literature from the medieval era to the modern period; and (3) developing a computational framework to simulate language contact effects between Catalan and co-official languages in multilingual communities. The proposed workflow involves preprocessing digitized texts (including OCR-corrected manuscripts and modern publications) using NLP pipelines, followed by distributed training of transformer-based models for feature extraction and classification. HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s data volume (over 20 TB of text and metadata), optimizing hyperparameters for low-resource language models, and running parallelized simulations of language change. Expected outcomes include open-access datasets of annotated Catalan dialects, a web-based visualization tool for dialectometry, and novel computational methods adaptable to other minority languages. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional Catalan studies, this research aims to deepen understanding of the language’s resilience and variability while providing resources to support its technological integration in domains like education and automated translation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Catalan language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of sustainable urban development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-dimensional interactions between environmental, economic, and social variables in real estate projects. Traditional planning tools often fail to dynamically integrate real-time data streams such as climate projections, population mobility patterns, and fluctuating market demands, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and missed opportunities for resilience. The proposed work employs an interdisciplinary computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and geospatial analysis to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes, predict long-term viability of development scenarios, and optimize site design under constraints of carbon neutrality and community equity. By processing large-scale datasets—including satellite imagery, municipal infrastructure records, and demographic surveys—the HPC environment enables iterative testing of hybrid urban forms (e.g., mixed-use districts, green corridors) at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support platform that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, ecological impact, and social benefit across development timelines. This tool aims to empower developers, municipalities, and community organizations to collaboratively prioritize projects that balance growth with sustainability imperatives. The computational demands of parallelized scenario analysis, coupled with the need for AI-driven pattern recognition in heterogeneous data sources, necessitate access to advanced GPU clusters and distributed storage systems. Successful implementation will advance methodological synergies between real estate practice and computational urban science while addressing critical gaps in adaptive planning for climate-resilient cities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create and redevelop housing, offices, retail centers, and industrial sites. Includes instruction in architectural design and construction, historic preservation, landscape architecture, urban planning and design, business, real estate and land use law, public policy, and engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to advance image-guided therapeutic interventions in Vascular and Interventional Radiology (VIR) by developing computational models to optimize device navigation, predict procedural outcomes, and personalize treatment strategies. Despite the growing use of minimally invasive techniques such as stent placement, embolization, and thrombolysis, challenges persist in navigating complex vascular anatomies, mitigating complications like thrombosis or vessel perforation, and tailoring therapies to individual hemodynamic conditions. Current clinical workflows rely heavily on static imaging and empirical decision-making, limiting precision in dynamic, patient-specific scenarios. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity simulations of blood flow, device-tissue interactions, and real-time imaging data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element modeling of vascular networks derived from patient CT/MRI datasets, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective procedural outcomes. The models will simulate hemodynamic changes during device deployment, predict stress distributions in vessel walls, and identify risk thresholds for adverse events. A parallel computational pipeline will process multi-modal imaging data (fluoroscopy, sonography) to enhance real-time guidance through adaptive registration and deformation tracking. By leveraging HPC capabilities, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in solving Navier-Stokes equations for pulsatile flow and enable rapid parameter optimization for clinical deployment. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for stent malposition or embolic material dispersion, a prototype decision-support system for intraprocedural planning, and open-source simulation templates for the VIR community. This work has the potential to improve procedural success rates, reduce radiation exposure from prolonged imaging, and establish a foundation for computationally driven precision medicine in interventional radiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists with additional training in image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages.

abstract: Ophthalmic diagnostics and treatment planning increasingly rely on advanced imaging modalities such as optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus photography, and visual field testing, generating large-scale datasets that challenge conventional analysis workflows. This project seeks to address the critical bottleneck in processing and interpreting complex ophthalmic data by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform for automated, real-time analysis of multimodal ocular imaging. The research problem centers on the limitations of existing clinical software, which often lacks the computational capacity to integrate heterogeneous data streams—such as volumetric OCT scans, dynamic perimetry results, and angiographic sequences—into unified diagnostic models. To overcome this, we propose a computational pipeline leveraging distributed GPU-accelerated machine learning frameworks to train deep neural networks on curated datasets of de-identified patient imaging (n > 50,000 studies). Key objectives include optimizing 3D convolutional architectures for detecting early biomarkers of diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma in OCT volumes, implementing federated learning protocols to maintain patient privacy across collaborating institutions, and creating an interactive visualization interface for technician-guided validation of automated findings. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of ensemble models combining structural and functional data while maintaining sub-second latency for clinical deployment. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms achieving ≥95% sensitivity in lesion detection benchmarks, a 40% reduction in analysis time compared to manual workflows, and open-source tools to enhance ophthalmic technician training through simulated diagnostic scenarios. By bridging computational innovation with clinical workflows, this project aims to establish scalable infrastructure for next-generation ocular health monitoring while advancing the technical competencies required for modern ophthalmic practice. Resource allocation will directly support data storage needs (>500 TB), parallelized model training across 50+ GPUs, and secure multi-institutional data sharing capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist ophthalmologists and optometrists in examining and treating patients with vision problems, vision disorders, and eye diseases. Includes instruction in taking patient histories, administering directed treatments and topical medications, diagnostic test procedures and equipment operation, anatomical and functional ocular measurements, patient care and instruction, ophthalmic and surgical equipment maintenance, safety and sterilization procedures, and office administrative procedures.

abstract: Mammography remains a critical tool for early breast cancer detection, yet challenges persist in optimizing image quality, diagnostic accuracy, and patient comfort during compression. Current protocols rely on generalized compression techniques and static image analysis, which may inadequately address anatomical variability or early-stage lesion detection in dense breast tissue. This project proposes a computational biomechanics and machine learning approach to advance mammographic imaging by integrating patient-specific tissue modeling and AI-driven image enhancement. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop finite element models simulating breast tissue deformation under varying compression protocols, informed by anonymized clinical datasets (including 3D mammograms and patient biodemographics). Concurrently, deep learning architectures will be trained on multi-institutional mammography datasets to identify subtle lesion patterns in heterogeneous tissue, with a focus on reducing false negatives in dense breasts. Computational workflows will merge these components to generate personalized compression recommendations and enhance lesion visibility through real-time image post-processing. The scale of data—high-resolution volumetric imaging, multi-parametric tissue properties, and longitudinal patient records—necessitates distributed computing for parallelized model training and large-scale biomechanical simulations. Expected outcomes include optimized, patient-specific compression parameters to reduce discomfort while maintaining diagnostic efficacy, and an open-source AI framework for adaptive image analysis. This interdisciplinary integration of biomechanics, oncology, and computational imaging science addresses a critical niche in radiological technology, with potential to directly improve clinical workflows and early detection rates. Successful implementation could establish a paradigm for personalized mammography protocols, reducing recall rates and advancing precision screening strategies for diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered radiographers to become registered mammographers. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, mammography instrumentation, mammography positioning, principles and procedures of mammography, and quality assurance.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design of next-generation hypersonic vehicles by addressing critical challenges in modeling turbulent reacting flows and coupled aerothermal-structural phenomena under extreme flight conditions. Current computational tools struggle to resolve the multiscale, multiphysics interactions inherent in high-enthalpy boundary layers, combustion instabilities in scramjet engines, and ablation processes in thermal protection systems. These limitations hinder the development of robust predictive models for vehicle performance and survivability. We propose a high-fidelity computational framework combining direct numerical simulation (DNS) of compressible turbulence, finite-element-based conjugate heat transfer analysis, and machine learning-accelerated chemistry reduction techniques. The framework will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layer dynamics at Mach 10+ conditions while coupling to material response models for carbon-carbon composites. The computational workload necessitates access to high-performance computing resources due to the extreme resolution requirements (exceeding 10^9 grid points) for DNS of turbulent combustion and the iterative nature of fluid-structure interaction simulations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for shock-boundary layer interaction with finite-rate chemistry effects, optimized fuel injection strategies for scramjet flameholding, and probabilistic ablation maps for heatshield design. These results will directly inform ongoing experimental efforts at our hypersonic wind tunnel facility and enable physics-based design rules for thermal management systems in reusable orbital vehicles. The generated datasets will be curated into a community-accessible repository to support verification/validation benchmarks for the aerospace community. Successful completion will reduce reliance on empirical safety margins in vehicle design, potentially enabling lighter thermal protection systems and expanded mission envelopes for both atmospheric entry vehicles and air-breathing hypersonic platforms.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematic principles to the design, technology, and development of systems and equipment used in aerospace and astronautical operations. Includes instruction in basic and applied sciences related to astronomy and astronautics, control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: The design and optimization of multiphase chemical reactors and separation systems require resolving complex interactions between fluid dynamics, heat and mass transfer, and reaction kinetics across multiple scales. Current computational tools struggle to accurately model these processes due to limitations in handling the coupled physics, high dimensionality, and transient phenomena inherent to industrial-scale systems. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate multiphase reactive flows in gas-liquid-solid systems, with a focus on catalytic slurry reactors and membrane-based separations. The proposed work will employ large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with discrete element method (DEM) for particle tracking, reactive transport equations, and machine learning-accelerated closure models for interfacial phenomena. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale boundary layers, track millions of catalyst particles, and simulate reactor hydrodynamics at practical operating conditions. Simulations will leverage parallelized solvers and adaptive mesh refinement to balance accuracy and computational cost. Key outcomes include predictive models for mass transfer coefficients in slurry reactors, optimized membrane module designs to mitigate fouling, and scalable strategies for integrating reaction kinetics with turbulent multiphase flows. The resulting computational tools will enable virtual prototyping of energy-efficient chemical processes, reducing reliance on costly empirical pilot-scale testing. This work directly supports the development of sustainable chemical manufacturing systems, with applications in carbon capture, petrochemical refining, and electrochemical synthesis. By advancing multiscale modeling capabilities in chemical engineering, the project aims to bridge critical gaps between laboratory-scale observations and industrial process scalability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems employing chemical processes, such as chemical reactors, kinetic systems, electrochemical systems, energy conservation processes, heat and mass transfer systems, and separation processes; and the applied analysis of chemical problems such as corrosion, particle abrasion, energy loss, pollution, and fluid mechanics.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate advanced computational modeling with traditional printmaking techniques to investigate the dynamic interactions between ink viscosity, substrate porosity, and pressure application in multi-layer printing processes. Traditional printmaking relies on iterative, trial-and-error experimentation to achieve desired visual outcomes, which is time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in its capacity to predict complex material behaviors.
