The research problem centers on bridging this gap by developing physics-informed machine learning models to simulate ink transfer mechanics across diverse printmaking methods, including lithography, intaglio, and relief printing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize these simulations at scale, incorporating variables such as humidity, temperature, and tool geometry, while resolving micron-scale fluid dynamics at the ink-substrate interface. The computational approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate ink flow under variable pressures, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on high-resolution scans of historical and experimental prints to predict aesthetic outcomes. By correlating simulation data with empirical results from controlled print trials, the models will identify optimal parameter combinations for achieving specific tonal gradients, texture fidelity, and registration accuracy. Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit tailored for printmaking education and practice, reducing material waste and expanding creative possibilities through predictive modeling. The project also aims to publish novel insights into the rheological properties of mixed-media inks under non-uniform pressure, advancing interdisciplinary discourse at the intersection of computational materials science and visual arts. This work positions computational resource allocation as a critical enabler for innovation in tactile art disciplines, fostering new methodologies for preserving traditional craft knowledge through digital frameworks.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by rendering art concepts onto surfaces and transferring images, via ink or dyes, onto paper or fabric. Includes instruction in monochrome and color printing; tonality; chemistry; equipment set-up and maintenance; techniques such as serigraphy, lithography, intaglio, woodcut, block, stencil, relief, etching, and composite; and personal style development.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and development necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in predicting drug-target interactions, optimizing pharmacokinetic properties, and understanding mechanisms of drug resistance. Traditional experimental approaches are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to explore the vast chemical and biological space required for modern therapeutics. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply multiscale computational models that bridge molecular simulations, machine learning, and systems pharmacology. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) employing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize binding dynamics and allosteric effects of small molecules with protein targets implicated in chronic diseases and antimicrobial resistance, and (2) training graph neural networks on large-scale chemical and genomic datasets to predict off-target interactions and toxicity profiles. The MD simulations will utilize GPU-accelerated workflows to achieve microsecond-scale sampling of conformational changes, while machine learning models will integrate heterogeneous data sources, including electronic health records and high-throughput screening data, to improve predictive accuracy. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental assays conducted in collaboration with pharmaceutical chemists and pharmacologists. By enabling rapid virtual screening of compound libraries and patient-specific pharmacokinetic modeling, this work aims to accelerate the identification of lead candidates, reduce late-stage attrition rates, and support personalized dosing strategies. Access to HPC resources is critical for managing the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive tasks inherent to these analyses. Outcomes will advance computational pharmacy methodologies, with direct applications in rational drug design, precision medicine, and the development of therapies for underserved clinical populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent or employed practice of preparing and dispensing drugs and medications in consultation with prescribing physicians and other health care professionals, and for managing pharmacy practices and counseling patients. Includes instruction in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmacy practice, pharmacy administration, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary study of textual transmission and cultural evolution across premodern and early modern manuscripts. A central challenge in textual studies lies in reconstructing the genealogical relationships (stemmatology) and material histories of fragmented or corrupted texts, particularly when analyzing large, multilingual corpora with complex variant networks. Traditional manual collation and analysis methods are insufficient for processing the scale of data required to model textual lineages, trace cross-cultural influences, or identify patterns in scribal practices across centuries. To address this, the project will deploy computational workflows integrating machine learning, phylogenetic modeling, and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze digitized manuscripts and print materials. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on multilingual textual variants to detect scribal errors and intentional revisions, applying graph-theoretical algorithms to reconstruct stemmata for understudied manuscript traditions, and employing computer vision tools to automate paleographic analysis of handwriting styles in digitized codices. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale image and text datasets, iterative model training across distributed nodes, and high-memory simulations for phylogenetic tree generation. The computational outputs will enable the identification of previously unrecognized textual relationships, enhance the accuracy of critical editions, and map the circulation of specific motifs across geotemporal boundaries. Outcomes will be integrated into an open-access platform for collaborative textual criticism, providing scholars with scalable tools for data-driven literary and historical analysis. By bridging computational scalability with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to transform the study of textual materiality, offering new methodologies for preserving cultural heritage and interrogating the sociopolitical contexts of textual production.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interconnected histories of digital or print texts and manuscripts for cultural and literary study. Includes instruction in archiving texts, bibliography, book and literary history, cultural studies, codicology, paleography, stemmatology, and textual criticism.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational challenges of optimizing real-time decision-making in sustainable fashion show logistics, a niche intersection of operations management, environmental science, and digital modeling within the business of fashion. The core problem lies in minimizing material waste and carbon footprint during live events while maintaining artistic integrity and commercial viability. Current industry practices rely on heuristic approaches that fail to account for dynamic variables such as last-minute design changes, model availability, and venue-specific constraints, leading to inefficient resource use. To overcome this, we propose developing a machine learning framework enhanced by multi-agent simulation systems to model complex interactions between creative workflows, supply chain parameters, and sustainability metrics. The computational approach will integrate three key components: 1) a generative adversarial network trained on historical show data to predict material flow bottlenecks, 2) discrete-event simulations of backstage operations under varying crisis scenarios, and 3) quantum-inspired annealing algorithms for real-time resource reallocation. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing high-dimensional data from IoT sensors embedded in garments, managing parallel simulation instances across diverse venue configurations, and reducing latency in decision support outputs. Expected outcomes include a predictive model that reduces textile waste by 30-40% per event while maintaining production timelines, along with an open-source toolkit for ethical AI integration in creative industries. The results will advance computational sustainability methodologies in business contexts that balance artistic vision with operational efficiency, particularly relevant as the $2.5B global fashion events industry faces increasing pressure to meet net-zero commitments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to present and display fashion, apparel, and accessories products in wholesale and retail settings, either on the person or via props and natural or artificial settings. Includes instruction in modeling skills, health and cosmetic principles, fashion show management, display design and production, and applicable aspects of advertising and fashion photography.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable, agent-based framework for simulating emergent human-AI collaboration patterns in dynamically evolving virtual training environments. Traditional virtual training systems often rely on static scenarios or scripted AI behaviors, limiting their capacity to model adaptive human responses to unexpected, AI-driven environmental changes. The proposed work addresses this gap by integrating stochastic human-performance modeling with reinforcement learning (RL)-based environment adaptation, enabling real-time analysis of how users cognitively and behaviorally adjust to AI-induced perturbations. The computational approach combines three core components: (1) a multi-agent system representing heterogeneous human operators with psychologically grounded decision-making parameters, (2) an RL controller that dynamically modifies environmental constraints and task complexity based on real-time performance metrics, and (3) a distributed visualization engine capturing fine-grained interaction data across spatial, temporal, and physiological dimensions. High-performance computing resources are essential for simultaneously running thousands of parameterized simulations across GPU-accelerated nodes, enabling Monte Carlo sampling of human-AI interaction trajectories under varying stress profiles and environmental stochasticity. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for resilience thresholds in human-AI teaming, predictive models of skill transfer from virtual to real-world settings, and open-source tools for generating synthetic behavior datasets that account for adaptive AI influences. The resulting framework will advance simulation methodologies at the intersection of cognitive engineering and machine learning, with direct applications in emergency response training systems where humans must rapidly adapt to AI-reconfigured operational environments. By capturing nonlinear interactions between algorithmic environment modifications and human perceptual-motor adaptation, this work contributes new theoretical foundations for designing human-centered AI systems in safety-critical domains.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles of applied visual simulation technology and the application of quantitative analyses to human-computer interaction. Includes instruction in object-oriented programming, artificial intelligence, computer communications and networks, computer graphics, virtual worlds and simulation systems, probability, statistics, stochastic modeling, data analysis, human-performance evaluation, and human-behavior modeling.

abstract: Gynecologic cancers, including ovarian, endometrial, and cervical malignancies, exhibit significant molecular heterogeneity, complicating treatment optimization and biomarker discovery. Current clinical approaches often rely on generalized therapeutic strategies, which may inadequately address interpatient variability in tumor biology and treatment response. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-omics predictive models that integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data from patient cohorts, aiming to identify subtype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities and resistance mechanisms. The computational workflow will process raw sequencing data from tumor biopsies and liquid biopsies, harmonize disparate omics datasets, and apply machine learning algorithms to uncover patterns associated with clinical outcomes. Key challenges include managing large-scale data volumes (≥10 TB), executing parallelized bioinformatic pipelines for variant calling and pathway analysis, and training deep learning models to predict drug response across heterogeneous tumor subtypes. The HPC infrastructure will enable accelerated genome-wide association studies (GWAS), dynamic simulations of tumor-immune interactions, and validation of candidate biomarkers through in silico perturbation experiments. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for stratifying patients based on molecular profiles, (2) novel biomarkers predictive of platinum-based chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer, and (3) open-source tools for real-time integration of multi-omics data in clinical decision support systems. This work directly addresses the urgent need for precision medicine in gynecologic oncology by bridging computational innovation with clinical translation. Successful implementation will enhance therapeutic targeting, reduce ineffective treatment exposures, and provide a template for computational resource utilization in oncologic research. All models, code, and de-identified datasets will be shared via public repositories to foster collaborative advances in the field.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for consultation and comprehensive management of patients with gynecologic cancer, including those diagnostic and therapeutic procedures necessary for the total care of the patient with gynecologic cancer and resulting complications.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in sheet metal forming processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model, simulate, and optimize complex deformation behaviors in metal alloys. Traditional sheet metal manufacturing relies heavily on iterative physical prototyping and empirical adjustments, leading to material waste, prolonged development cycles, and suboptimal tooling configurations. While computational tools like finite element analysis (FEA) have reduced some inefficiencies, simulating high-strain forming processes—such as those involving cornice brakes, forming rolls, or squaring shears—requires resolving nonlinear material responses, anisotropic plasticity, and dynamic friction conditions at fine spatiotemporal scales. Existing simulations often oversimplify these factors due to computational limitations, resulting in unreliable predictions for novel geometries or advanced materials. This project proposes an HPC-driven framework to overcome these barriers. High-resolution FEA models will integrate multi-physics phenomena, including thermal gradients, microstructural evolution, and tool-workpiece interactions, using adaptive meshing and parallelized solvers to maintain computational tractability. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate parameter optimization for target geometries, enabling rapid exploration of forming paths and tooling designs. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from industrial partners, focusing on aerospace-grade aluminum and high-strength steel alloys. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for springback, wrinkling, and fracture risks under diverse forming conditions, as well as open-source tools to guide process design. By reducing reliance on physical trials, this research aims to lower material costs by an estimated 15–20% in prototyping phases and improve geometric accuracy for complex sheet metal components. The resulting methodologies will advance digital twin capabilities in sheetworking, supporting broader adoption of sustainable, precision-driven manufacturing practices in automotive, aerospace, and construction sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to form, shape, bend and fold extruded metals, including the creation of new products, using hand tools and machines such as cornice brakes, forming rolls, and squaring shears.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal dynamics of German-language cultural narratives across digital archives spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in the representation of regional identities, migration, and transnational cultural exchange within German-speaking Europe, as reflected in digitized literature, periodicals, and ephemera. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to address the scale and complexity of these materials, which include over 500,000 multilingual texts from repositories such as the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek and Europeana, alongside understudied diasporic publications from North America and Eastern Europe. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and geospatial analysis to trace semantic shifts, intertextual networks, and the diffusion of motifs across time and borders. Custom transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to handle historical German orthographic variations and code-switching in minority-language contexts, while graph algorithms will map connections between authors, publishers, and thematic clusters. The workflow requires distributed training of multilingual embeddings, large-scale topic modeling across GPU-accelerated frameworks, and high-memory processing of georeferenced metadata. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas visualizing cultural transmission pathways, as well as new methodologies for computational literary studies that address the unique challenges of Central European multilingual corpora. By revealing how regional identities were negotiated in transnational contexts, this work will provide German Studies scholars with data-driven insights into the historical roots of contemporary cultural debates, while demonstrating the value of HPC infrastructure for humanities research reliant on heterogeneous, temporally layered datasets.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Germany, the neighboring countries of Austria and Switzerland, the German minorities in neighboring European countries, and the historical areas of German influence across Europe and overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the analysis of large-scale, multilingual translation corpora within Translation Studies. While the field has traditionally relied on qualitative methods to examine translation practices, the increasing digitization of historical texts, audiovisual media, and institutional archives demands scalable computational tools to analyze patterns across languages, time periods, and cultural contexts. The research problem centers on identifying systemic biases, stylistic shifts, and sociocultural influences in translated works—tasks that require processing terabytes of text, audio, and visual data spanning diverse linguistic systems. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) models, unsupervised clustering algorithms, and network analysis to map translation norms, track lexical evolution, and model the diffusion of translated content across geopolitical boundaries. Custom pipelines will be developed to preprocess heterogeneous data (e.g., parallel texts, translator metadata, paratextual commentaries) while preserving contextual nuances critical to interdisciplinary analysis. GPU-accelerated transformer models will fine-tune multilingual embeddings to detect subtle pragmatic variations in literary and technical translations. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model how institutional policies and cultural hierarchies shape translation workflows. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for diachronic and synchronic translation analysis, open-access tools for corpus-based translation studies, and novel insights into how power dynamics manifest in cross-linguistic mediation. By enabling the processing of previously intractable datasets, this project aims to advance empirical methodologies in Translation Studies while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue with computational linguistics and digital humanities. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle memory-intensive tasks, including training domain-specific language models and conducting large-scale comparative analyses across 50+ language pairs, ultimately contributing to a more robust, data-driven understanding of translation as a sociocultural practice.
cip_definition: A multidisciplinary program that prepares individuals to explore the historical, social, institutional and cultural facets of translation. Includes instruction in general and literary translation, business translation, technical translation, and other specific applications of linguistic skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay between energy transition policies, legal frameworks, and land-use conflicts in transboundary river basins. As nations pursue decarbonization goals, hydropower expansion and renewable energy infrastructure development increasingly intersect with environmental protection laws, indigenous land rights, and multilateral water-sharing agreements. Traditional legal research methods struggle to model the cascading impacts of policy decisions across jurisdictions or quantify risks arising from competing regulatory priorities. This project addresses this gap by developing a computational legal analytics framework integrating three components: (1) natural language processing (NLP) of international treaties, national legislation, and judicial opinions related to water governance; (2) geospatial analysis of energy project footprints relative to protected ecosystems and ancestral territories; and (3) agent-based modeling of stakeholder decision-making under evolving legal constraints. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parallel processing of multilingual legal texts, high-resolution spatial datasets, and millions of simulation iterations exploring policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying regulatory conflict hotspots in major river systems, visualizations of legal obligation networks across governance scales, and a decision-support tool for evaluating compliance risks in energy infrastructure planning. By bridging computational social science with energy law scholarship, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in legal impact assessment while providing actionable insights for balancing climate mitigation targets with environmental justice imperatives in contested transboundary contexts.
cip_title: Energy, Environment, and Natural Resources Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing the energy industry, environmental protection, natural resources and land use, and related topics.

abstract: Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, yet the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain incompletely characterized. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to simulate OMT’s impact on neuromusculoskeletal systems and predict clinical outcomes. A critical barrier to progress is the integration of high-resolution biomechanical data with dynamic neural signaling pathways, which requires computationally intensive simulations exceeding the capacity of standard clinical workstations. This proposal requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale modeling of tissue deformation, proprioceptive feedback, and autonomic nervous system modulation during OMT techniques. Leveraging finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling, we will simulate mechanical forces applied during OMT protocols (e.g., myofascial release, high-velocity low-amplitude thrust) across anatomically detailed 3D musculoskeletal models derived from patient-specific MRI and motion capture data. Concurrently, neural network models will map mechanotransduction signals to autonomic and central nervous system responses, incorporating real-world clinical data from electromyography and heart rate variability metrics. Machine learning pipelines will identify predictive biomarkers of treatment efficacy by correlating simulated biomechanical stressors with outcomes in pain reduction, joint mobility, and inflammation markers from a retrospective dataset of 1,200 OMT cases. The HPC environment will facilitate parallel processing of these heterogeneous datasets and reduce simulation runtime from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for optimizing OMT protocols based on patient-specific anatomy and physiological states, as well as novel insights into the neurobiomechanical pathways mediating OMT’s therapeutic effects. This work will advance evidence-based osteopathic practice by providing a quantitative foundation for treatment personalization and mechanistic hypothesis generation, ultimately improving clinical outcomes in musculoskeletal pain and dysfunction.
cip_definition: Research focused on osteopathic neuromusculoskeletal diagnosis and Osteopathic Manipulative Treatment (OMT).

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of solvent effects on reaction mechanisms in organic and biocatalytic systems—a critical challenge in computational chemistry. While experimental methods provide insights into reaction outcomes, they often struggle to resolve transient intermediates, solvent-solute interactions, or dynamic electronic effects in complex environments. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining density functional theory (DFT), ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and machine learning (ML)-accelerated free energy sampling. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) quantifying how solvation microenvironments alter transition-state energetics and selectivity in asymmetric organocatalytic reactions, and (2) characterizing proton-coupled electron transfer mechanisms in metalloenzymes under physiologically relevant solvation conditions. The computational workflow will employ hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations with explicit solvent models, using adaptive sampling techniques to map free energy landscapes. For larger enzyme systems, we will implement neural network potentials trained on DFT data to enable microsecond-scale dynamics. These simulations demand substantial HPC resources due to the need for extensive conformational sampling, high-level electronic structure calculations (e.g., DLPNO-CCSD(T) benchmarks), and parallelized ML training workflows. Expected outcomes include the development of transferable solvent descriptors for predicting reaction outcomes and mechanistic insights into solvation-driven catalytic enhancements. The resulting datasets and optimized ML models will be disseminated through open-access platforms, enabling broader applications in reaction design. By bridging quantum mechanical accuracy with biologically relevant timescales, this work aims to establish predictive models that complement experimental spectroscopy and kinetic studies, with potential applications in sustainable chemistry and enzyme engineering. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the ∼500,000 core-hour computational load and managing the ∼200 TB of trajectory data generated during the project period.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principals of mathematical algorithms, statistics, and large databases to integrate chemical theory and modeling with experimental observations. Includes instruction in chemistry or a related scientific field, computer training, a familiarity with chemical principles, including conformational analysis, acid–base equilibria, physical organic chemistry, molecular structure, thermodynamics, and stereochemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of glacial landscape evolution by quantifying the coupled interactions between ice dynamics, subglacial hydrology, and sediment transport during deglaciation. Despite the critical role of these feedbacks in shaping landforms such as moraines, drumlins, and meltwater channels, existing models often treat ice flow, hydrology, and erosion processes in isolation, limiting their predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose a high-resolution, three-dimensional computational framework integrating finite element ice sheet modeling (via the Ice Sheet System Model, ISSM) with discrete element sediment transport simulations and pore water pressure dynamics. The coupled model will simulate transient glacier retreat scenarios under varying climatic forcings, resolving meter-scale bed interactions over multi-kilometer domains. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational demands of (1) parallelized solutions to Stokes flow equations with adaptive meshing near glacier termini, (2) Lagrangian tracking of subglacial sediment particles under evolving hydraulic conditions, and (3) ensemble runs assessing parameter sensitivity across glacial geologic settings (e.g., soft-bedded vs. hard-bedded systems). The simulations will be validated against field data from ongoing studies of Late Pleistocene deglaciation in the Upper Midwest (USA) and modern analog sites in Svalbard. Anticipated outcomes include new quantitative constraints on how subglacial drainage efficiency modulates ice flow instabilities during retreat and its legacy in sediment deposition patterns. This work will provide the first process-based numerical tool capable of reconstructing paraglacial landscape assemblages from first principles, with applications to paleoclimate reconstruction, glacial hazard assessment, and the interpretation of planetary cryospheric features. Successful implementation requires dedicated HPC allocations to manage memory-intensive coupled simulations exceeding 10^8 computational cells and multi-terabyte output datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origin and evolution of topographic features created by physical, chemical or biological processes operating at or near the Earth's surface, including glaciers.

abstract: The study of dynamic neural network reconfiguration during cognitive control tasks presents a critical challenge in cognitive neuroscience, as traditional approaches struggle to capture the millisecond-scale interactions across distributed brain regions. This project seeks to address this gap by investigating how transient, large-scale network dynamics underpin cognitive flexibility and adaptive decision-making. A key obstacle lies in integrating high-density electrophysiological data (e.g., intracranial EEG) with functional MRI to resolve spatiotemporal mismatches between modalities, while modeling rapid shifts in network topology. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining time-resolved graph theory, Bayesian hierarchical modeling, and biophysically constrained neural mass simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) processing terabytes of 256-channel intracranial EEG recordings with millisecond temporal precision, (2) running Monte Carlo simulations of dynamic community detection algorithms on whole-brain functional connectivity graphs, and (3) optimizing parameters for coupled oscillator models that bridge neural population dynamics with behavioral trial data. The HPC architecture will enable parallel processing of multi-scale datasets across 10,000+ core-hours, reducing computation time for iterative model fitting from months to days. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for analyzing cross-modal network dynamics, validated through behavioral experiments on cognitive flexibility in healthy adults. This work will establish quantitative links between transient network states and task-switching performance metrics, advancing theoretical models of cognitive control while providing potential biomarkers for network dysfunction in traumatic brain injury. By leveraging HPC capabilities to overcome current limitations in temporal resolution and model complexity, the project aims to transform our understanding of how distributed neural systems dynamically coordinate to support adaptive cognition.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the neural mechanisms underlying cognition.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of French dialectal and creole variation across historical and contemporary contexts. The research addresses a critical gap in Francophone linguistics: the systematic modeling of phonetic, syntactic, and lexical shifts in under-resourced French-adjacent languages, particularly Caribbean and African creoles, which face both rapid evolution and attrition. Traditional comparative methods struggle to process the scale of multi-modal data—including archival texts, modern speech corpora, and sociolinguistic metadata—required to trace these dynamics. Our team proposes a hybrid computational approach combining neural language models, phonetic alignment algorithms, and geospatial-temporal visualization to analyze over 10 TB of digitized primary sources (19th–21st centuries) and contemporary field recordings. Key objectives include training domain-specific transformer models on historical Metropolitan French corpora to detect semantic drift, developing a comparative framework for automated creole classification using parallel texts, and mapping dialect boundaries through clustering algorithms applied to phonetic feature extraction. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing distributed training of large language models, parallel processing of audio datasets via GPU-accelerated speech recognition pipelines, and running iterative simulations of language contact scenarios. Outcomes will include open-access tools for dialectometric analysis, a public repository of annotated creole corpora, and novel insights into the impact of colonial/postcolonial migration patterns on French linguistic diversity. This work directly supports preservation efforts for endangered varieties while providing methodological innovations applicable to computational humanities research on multilingualism and language change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the French language and related dialects and creoles. Includes instruction in philology; Metropolitan French; Canadian French; African and Caribbean Creoles; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Land use planning requires balancing complex interactions between environmental, economic, and social systems to optimize sustainable development. However, current models often lack the resolution or computational capacity to integrate multi-scale datasets, simulate dynamic feedbacks, or evaluate long-term scenarios under climate change and population growth. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance spatially explicit modeling of land use decisions and their impacts on ecosystem services in rapidly developing regions. We propose developing a coupled modeling framework that combines agent-based simulations of stakeholder decision-making, cellular automata for land cover change, and machine learning-driven analysis of socio-economic drivers. The framework will integrate high-resolution geospatial data (e.g., satellite imagery, soil maps, climate projections) with demographic and policy datasets to assess trade-offs between urbanization, agricultural conversion, and conservation goals. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across diverse climate and policy scenarios, calibrating models using Bayesian optimization, and processing petabyte-scale remote sensing inputs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify how land use policies affect carbon sequestration, water quality, and habitat connectivity over decadal timescales. By enabling real-time visualization of development scenarios through GPU-accelerated rendering, this work will support stakeholder engagement in regional planning processes. The computational pipelines and open-source tools developed will enhance the capacity of land use researchers to analyze complex systems, while results will inform state and federal policies aimed at minimizing ecological degradation while meeting housing and infrastructure demands. This project addresses a critical gap in scalable, data-driven approaches to sustainable land management, with direct applications in mitigating biodiversity loss and climate-driven land use conflicts.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Land Use Planning and Management/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how public and/or private land and associated resources can be preserved, developed, and used for maximum social, economic, and environmental benefit. Includes instruction in natural resources management, natural resource economics, public policy, regional and land use planning, environmental impact assessment, applicable law and regulations, government and politics, principles of business and real estate land use, statistical and analytical tools, computer applications, mapping and report preparation, site analysis, cost analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in Korea through large-scale analysis of textual and visual materials. While existing scholarship in Korean Studies has extensively examined historical and sociocultural dynamics, traditional methodologies struggle to systematically analyze the vast, fragmented corpora of premodern and modern sources—including classical manuscripts, colonial-era publications, and digital media—that reflect shifting notions of Korean identity. The research addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis, image recognition, and network modeling to identify patterns in language use, visual symbolism, and cross-media discourse across a curated dataset spanning the 15th to 21st centuries. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on classical Hanja-Hangul mixed scripts, applying computer vision techniques to analyze artistic motifs in Chosŏn-era folk paintings, and mapping semantic networks in post-division North and South Korean media. These methods require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, fine-tuning of multilingual language models, and iterative visualization of high-dimensional cultural data—tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for tracing diachronic changes in Korean cultural narratives, 2) open-access tools for processing non-standard historical Korean texts, and 3) new insights into how localized traditions interacted with transnational influences during critical junctures, such as the Imjin War or post-Korean War modernization. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish reproducible workflows for analyzing Korea’s cultural heritage at unprecedented scale while fostering collaboration between area studies scholars and data science researchers. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage of sensitive archival materials, and secure processing of copyrighted 20th-century texts under fair-use agreements.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Korea, including related island groups and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize firearm design and manufacturing processes through advanced simulations of mechanical and thermodynamic behaviors in firearm components. Traditional gunsmithing relies heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-consuming, costly, and limited in evaluating complex dynamic interactions such as barrel harmonics, chamber pressure distribution, and heat dissipation during rapid fire. To address these limitations, this research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-physics phenomena in firearms, including stress-strain relationships under cyclic loading, thermal deformation in barrels, and fluid-structure interactions in gas-operated systems. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will be implemented using open-source solvers like Code_Aster and OpenFOAM, parameterized with material properties of common firearms alloys (e.g., 4140 steel, 6061 aluminum). Machine learning models will then analyze simulation outputs to identify optimal geometries, material treatments, and manufacturing tolerances. A key innovation involves coupling these simulations with ballistic performance metrics, enabling predictive design adjustments for improved accuracy and durability. Expected outcomes include validated computational workflows to reduce prototyping iterations by 40–60%, data-driven guidelines for mitigating wear in high-stress components, and open-access templates for gunsmiths to adapt simulations to custom firearms. By integrating computational engineering with traditional craft, this work aims to elevate precision in gunsmithing while preserving artisanal customization—a critical balance in an industry where mechanical reliability and user-specific ergonomics are paramount. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the terabyte-scale datasets and parallelized computations required to achieve micron-level resolution in component stress analysis and sub-millisecond temporal fidelity in firing cycle modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and modify firearms according to blueprints or customer specifications, using specialized hand tools and machines.

abstract: Vocational sales and marketing education faces a critical challenge in bridging theoretical knowledge with dynamic, real-world applications. Current pedagogical approaches often lack scalable methods to simulate complex market environments or analyze large-scale student performance data, limiting educators’ ability to personalize instruction and predict learner outcomes. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy computational models that enhance the design and delivery of marketing and distribution teacher education programs. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) creating agent-based simulations of market ecosystems to model consumer behavior, supply chain dynamics, and competitive scenarios for use in classroom training, and (2) implementing machine learning algorithms to analyze longitudinal datasets tracking student engagement, skill acquisition, and career progression. By utilizing parallel computing architectures, the simulations will incorporate multi-agent interactions across diverse economic conditions, enabling pre-service teachers to experiment with pedagogical strategies in risk-free virtual environments. Concurrently, natural language processing techniques will be applied to qualitative feedback from teaching portfolios, while recurrent neural networks will identify patterns in quantitative performance metrics. These computational approaches will allow for the identification of optimal instructional interventions tailored to varying learner profiles. The anticipated outcomes include an open-source simulation platform adaptable to regional market contexts, predictive models for student success in certification programs, and evidence-based frameworks for competency assessment in distributive education. By integrating computational modeling with teacher training methodologies, this work aims to advance the preparation of marketing educators, ultimately strengthening the pipeline of skilled professionals in sales and distribution fields. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets and maintaining low-latency performance during concurrent simulation runs, capabilities unattainable with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Sales and Marketing Operations/ Marketing and Distribution Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational sales and marketing operations/marketing and distributive education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Phlebotomy procedures, while routine, involve complex interactions between anatomical variability, technique precision, and patient-specific factors that influence success rates and complication risks. This project seeks to optimize blood collection practices by developing computational models to simulate venipuncture dynamics, predict outcomes, and guide evidence-based protocol improvements. The primary research challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous biological data—including vascular anatomy, blood flow characteristics, and tissue biomechanics—into predictive frameworks that account for real-world clinical variability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to run multi-scale simulations coupling finite element analysis of needle-tissue interactions with machine learning models trained on anonymized phlebotomy outcome datasets (e.g., hematoma rates, sample hemolysis). These simulations will incorporate 3D vascular mapping derived from ultrasound imaging data and patient demographic variables to assess technique efficacy across diverse populations. A secondary aim involves creating virtual reality (VR)-compatible training modules that use real-time biomechanical feedback to accelerate skill acquisition among phlebotomy students. The computational workflow demands parallel processing for Monte Carlo simulations evaluating 10,000+ procedural scenarios, as well as GPU-accelerated neural networks to identify risk patterns in retrospective clinical data. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide needle insertion angle and depth based on individual patient characteristics, (2) quantitative safety thresholds for specimen handling variables like tube inversion frequency, and (3) validated VR training sequences that reduce skill competency time by ≥30% compared to traditional methods. By establishing computational phlebotomy benchmarks, this work addresses critical gaps in standardized practice guidelines while providing a scalable framework to analyze procedural outcomes across healthcare settings. The requested HPC allocation will enable the parameter space exploration necessary to account for biological diversity and operational constraints inherent in clinical phlebotomy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in ophthalmic lens fabrication by integrating computational biomechanics and adaptive optics modeling. Current lens manufacturing workflows rely on static optical corrections that may not account for dynamic ocular biomechanics, such as microfluctuations in corneal shape during eye movement or environmental stressors (e.g., temperature, humidity). These factors contribute to suboptimal visual outcomes for patients with complex prescriptions, particularly those requiring high-index or multifocal lenses. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) of lens stress distributions under simulated physiological conditions, machine learning-driven optimization of lens curvature gradients, and real-time ray-tracing simulations to evaluate optical performance across dynamic scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-resolution 3D ocular biomechanical datasets (derived from anonymized clinical tomography scans) and iteratively modeling lens behavior at micrometer-scale tolerances. Key challenges include resolving nonlinear material responses in polymer composites under rapid thermal-mechanical cycling and minimizing computational artifacts in wavefront error predictions. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for adaptive lens design, reducing trial-and-error prototyping by 40–60% in laboratory settings, and a proof-of-concept digital twin system for simulating patient-specific lens performance. This work bridges materials science, optomechanical engineering, and clinical ophthalmology, offering a paradigm shift toward dynamically optimized eyewear. Successful implementation could enhance visual acuity outcomes for patients with irregular corneas or high astigmatism while establishing computational pipelines for next-generation ophthalmic laboratory technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in acupuncture and herbal medicine by addressing the computational challenges of analyzing complex biological interactions and treatment efficacy. Despite the growing evidence supporting acupuncture and herbal therapies, mechanistic understanding remains limited due to the multi-target, multi-component nature of these interventions. Traditional research methods struggle to model the synergistic effects of herbal formulations or the dynamic physiological responses to acupuncture. This project proposes a computational approach integrating machine learning, bioinformatics, and multi-scale modeling to bridge these gaps. First, machine learning algorithms will analyze clinical datasets—including electronic health records and treatment outcomes—to identify patterns in acupuncture point selection and herb combinations correlated with therapeutic success. Second, molecular dynamics simulations will model interactions between herbal compounds and biological targets (e.g., inflammatory markers, neural receptors) to predict synergistic or adverse effects. Third, finite element modeling will simulate biomechanical and neurophysiological responses to acupuncture needle manipulation, incorporating patient-specific anatomical data to explore mechanisms of pain modulation. These computational workflows require HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of datasets, the need for parallelized simulations, and the iterative optimization of predictive models. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive tools to optimize herbal formulation design, personalized acupuncture protocols, and mechanistic hypotheses for experimental validation. By elucidating the systems-level effects of these therapies, this work aims to strengthen the evidence base for acupuncture and herbal medicine, inform clinical decision-making, and foster integration with biomedical frameworks. The requested computing resources will enable scalable, reproducible analyses critical for advancing precision in traditional medicine.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of acupuncture, a Chinese system of health care and healing based on the use of pulse diagnosis, acupuncture point selection, and needle insertion, as well as herbs and other Asian treatment modalities. Includes instruction in basic Western medical sciences, Asian philosophy, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbs, diagnostic techniques, patient observation and communication, acupuncture points and point selection, acupuncture techniques, acupuncture treatment of disease, pain management, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in veterinary pathogens presents a critical threat to animal health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. Current experimental approaches to characterize resistance mechanisms and develop targeted therapies are limited by the complexity of host-pathogen interactions and the vast genomic diversity of veterinary pathogens. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of AMR dynamics in bacterial pathogens affecting livestock, with a focus on multidrug-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* and *Escherichia coli* strains. We propose an integrative approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-enabled genomic analysis, and virtual drug screening to identify novel therapeutic targets and compounds. MD simulations will model conformational changes in key resistance-associated proteins (e.g., beta-lactamases, efflux pumps) under varying ligand-binding conditions, requiring millisecond-scale sampling enabled by GPU-accelerated nodes. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze multi-omic datasets (whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomics) from clinical veterinary isolates to predict resistance genotypes and epistatic interactions. A virtual compound library will be screened against prioritized targets using docking simulations and free-energy perturbation calculations. The scale of these analyses—involving >50,000 GPU core-hours and large-scale parallelization of genomic data processing—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic resolution maps of resistance protein dynamics, (2) predictive models linking genomic signatures to phenotypic resistance in veterinary isolates, and (3) a shortlist of lead compounds with validated binding affinities. This work will directly inform the development of narrow-spectrum antimicrobials tailored to veterinary pathogens, reducing reliance on broad-spectrum antibiotics in agriculture. By bridging computational biology and veterinary clinical science, the project aims to establish a framework for rapid, cost-effective AMR mitigation strategies while advancing computational methodologies for veterinary biomedical research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize marine vessel maintenance and repair processes, addressing inefficiencies in current trial-and-error approaches for hull integrity restoration, propulsion system balancing, and corrosion mitigation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will simulate multi-physics interactions affecting marine structures, including hydrodynamic stresses, material fatigue in composite hulls, and electrochemical degradation in saltwater environments. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model propeller performance under cavitation and debris-impact scenarios, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict stress distribution in drive shafts and welded joints. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical repair data and sensor-derived operational metrics to identify failure precursors in vessel electrical systems and steering mechanisms. The research will integrate material science datasets with real-world environmental conditions (e.g., salinity gradients, thermal cycling) to create predictive maintenance frameworks. Expected outcomes include validated models for prioritizing repair interventions, adaptive corrosion-resistance strategies for welded hull sections, and dynamic balancing protocols for propeller-shaft assemblies. By enabling data-driven decision-making, this work aims to reduce dry-dock downtime by 15-20% and extend service intervals for critical marine components. The computational workflows will be designed for scalability to accommodate diverse vessel classes, from coastal fishing craft to large cargo ships, with open-source toolkits disseminated to maritime technical training programs. This project directly supports workforce development in ship repair technology by providing actionable insights into sustainable material choices and failure-resistant engineering designs.
cip_title: Marine Maintenance/ Fitter and Ship Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair outboard and inboard engines; test, maintain, and repair steering devices and electrical systems; repair metal, wood, and fiberglass hulls and vessel components; fabricate and maintain sails; and repair and balance propellers and drive shafts.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of cultural transmission and identity formation within African diasporic communities through large-scale digital humanities approaches. The research problem centers on understanding how diasporic groups negotiate cultural continuity and adaptation in transnational contexts, particularly through digital media and vernacular archives. Existing studies lack computational scalability to process vast, unstructured datasets—such as social media content, digitized oral histories, and multimedia art—that reflect evolving cultural practices. The project employs machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to map semantic networks, sentiment trajectories, and visual motifs across multilingual, multimedia corpora from platforms like YouTube, community archives, and collaborative storytelling databases. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on low-resource African languages, detecting dialectal variations, and analyzing image-text relationships in user-generated content. Spatial-temporal modeling will further trace the diffusion of cultural narratives across diasporic nodes (e.g., Afro-Brazilian, Caribbean, and Black European communities). By parallelizing workflows across GPU nodes, the team aims to process over 10TB of heterogeneous data, enabling comparative analysis of how gender, generation, and geopolitical events shape identity articulation. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking cultural artifacts to their sociohistorical contexts, methodological advances in decolonial AI for underrepresented languages, and policy-oriented insights into digital cultural preservation. This work bridges computational scalability with critical African diaspora studies, offering new frameworks to study cultural resilience without reducing lived experiences to quantifiable metrics. The requested resources will directly support model training, large-scale graph analytics, and storage of annotated datasets, which are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara, and including the African diasporas overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of contraband distribution networks within correctional facilities, a critical yet understudied challenge in criminal justice systems. Contraband, including illicit drugs and weapons, undermines institutional safety and rehabilitation efforts, but traditional interventions often fail due to the complexity of social and logistical networks that facilitate its spread. Current research lacks scalable computational tools to simulate these networks, which involve thousands of interacting agents (e.g., incarcerated individuals, staff, visitors) and dynamic environmental factors. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with network analysis to simulate contraband flow under varying conditions. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across multiple scenarios, incorporating real-world data on facility layouts, movement patterns, and historical incident reports. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent network structures and predict high-risk interactions. The computational workflow will also test the hypothetical impacts of policy changes, such as altered visitation protocols or staff allocation strategies, on contraband reduction. Outcomes will include a validated simulation toolkit for prison administrators to proactively design interventions, as well as novel insights into the resilience of covert networks within constrained environments. By bridging criminological theory with computational social science, this project advances interdisciplinary methodologies for correctional system optimization while adhering to ethical guidelines for data anonymization and institutional confidentiality. The scalability of the approach offers potential applications to broader criminal justice contexts, including community corrections and reentry programs.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general study of criminal justice and corrections. Includes instruction in criminology, criminal justice, correctional science, forensic science, law enforcement, psychology, and ethics.

abstract: Animal infectious diseases pose significant threats to global livestock health, food security, and zoonotic disease emergence. Current limitations in understanding host-pathogen-immune system dynamics stem from the complexity of multi-omics datasets and the need for predictive models of pathogen evolution. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance comparative analyses of microbial genomes, host immune receptor diversity, and cross-species infection mechanisms in veterinary species. We propose an integrative computational framework combining bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data from bovine, avian, and porcine immune cells exposed to priority pathogens (e.g., *Mycobacterium avium* subsp. *paratuberculosis*, influenza A virus). Machine learning models will predict antigenic drift patterns in viral surface proteins, while molecular dynamics simulations (AMBER, GROMACS) will characterize host receptor binding kinetics. Phylogenomic pipelines will reconstruct transmission networks for antimicrobial-resistant *Salmonella* strains using whole-genome sequencing data from >5,000 veterinary isolates. Parallelized agent-based modeling (Repast-HPC) will simulate mucosal immune responses to fungal pathogens at cellular resolution. These computationally intensive workflows require GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning architectures (PyTorch) and >10TB memory allocation for population-scale genomic analyses. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of conserved epitopes for broad-spectrum vaccine development targeting ruminant coronaviruses, 2) predictive frameworks for strain-specific mastitis risks in dairy cattle through mammary epithelial cell transcriptomic networks, and 3) evolutionary risk scores for avian influenza host-jumping potential based on hemagglutinin structural stability metrics. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research will establish open-access computational tools for veterinary immunogenomics while addressing critical gaps in preventive strategies against economically devastating livestock diseases. Resource allocation will directly support 7 collaborative projects investigating immune evasion mechanisms in priority veterinary pathogens.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microbial causation and immunologic processes related to animal disease, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in bacteriology, mycology, virology, immune response mechanisms, humoral and cell function, cancer defenses, immune system dysfunction, immunologic diseases, parasitology, pathogenesis, and disease vectors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate mechanisms of chemical toxicity and pharmacological intervention in complex biological systems. A critical challenge in pharmacology and toxicology is predicting how xenobiotics, such as industrial solvents or chemotherapeutic agents, interact with molecular targets across tissues, particularly when metabolic biotransformation generates reactive intermediates with unpredictable toxicity. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the dynamic, multi-scale nature of these interactions, which span atomic-level enzyme-substrate binding, cellular detoxification pathways, and systemic toxicokinetics. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., cytochrome P450 isoforms) with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling. MD simulations will characterize solvent interactions and substrate specificity of enzymes under varying redox conditions, while PBPK models will extrapolate tissue-specific exposure thresholds. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of simulating large enzyme-ligand systems (≥500,000 atoms) over microsecond timescales and to optimize parameter space exploration in toxicity prediction models. Expected outcomes include identifying high-risk metabolites of common environmental toxicants, validating in silico predictions against in vitro hepatic toxicity assays, and elucidating mechanisms of chemopreventive agents that modulate bioactivation pathways. This work will advance predictive toxicology by bridging atomic-resolution insights with organism-level exposure dynamics, directly informing risk assessment strategies and the design of safer therapeutic agents. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, parallelized parameter sweeps, and large-scale data integration, enabling workflows impractical on local clusters. By prioritizing HPC-driven hypothesis testing, this project aims to reduce reliance on costly animal models and accelerate translational discoveries in environmental and pharmacological toxicity.
cip_definition: A program with an integrated, combined approach to the study of pharmacological and toxicological issues in biology and the biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in topics such as solvents, xenobiotic metabolism, chemical toxicity, neurotoxicology, immunopharmacology, biotransformation, tissue culture and in vitro studies, biomolecular analysis, bioactivation and inactivation, enzyme regulation, chemoprevention and chemotherapy, industrial and chemical studies, radiation health, and bioinformatics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of educational systems necessitates advanced tools to model and optimize administrative decision-making processes. This project seeks to address the challenge of dynamically allocating limited institutional resources—such as staffing, budgets, and facility usage—across large, heterogeneous school districts. Traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to process real-time data streams, simulate multi-year scenarios, or account for interdependent variables (e.g., shifting enrollment patterns, policy changes, and community needs). To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model resource allocation strategies under uncertainty. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) to represent stakeholder interactions, integer programming for optimization of discrete resources, and machine learning to predict emergent outcomes from historical district data. By parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations—including varying budget constraints, staffing policies, and student demographic projections—the HPC environment will enable rapid scenario testing at scale. Initial work will focus on validating models against historical data from three urban school districts (2010–2020), followed by prospective simulations to evaluate resilience of allocation strategies under demographic and fiscal stressors. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit for administrators, quantifying trade-offs between equity, cost efficiency, and academic outcomes in resource distribution. This project will advance the field of educational leadership by providing empirically grounded computational methods to navigate complex administrative challenges, directly supporting the program’s mission to equip leaders with innovative, scalable solutions for organizational management. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume (10+ TB of structured/unstructured records) and computational intensity, as single simulation iterations require ~8 hours on 128 cores for district-scale models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and techniques of administering a wide variety of schools and other educational organizations and facilities, supervising educational personnel at the school or staff level, and that may prepare individuals as general administrators and supervisors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of under-resourced East Asian languages, with a focus on historical linguistic shifts and dialectal variations in Sino-Tibetan languages. The research problem centers on the limited computational tools and corpora available for studying non-standardized or regionally specific language forms, such as archaic Chinese dialects and minority Sino-Tibetan languages spoken in Southwest China and the Himalayas. Traditional philological methods struggle to process large, fragmented textual datasets and audio recordings, hindering systematic analysis of phonetic evolution, syntactic divergence, and lexical borrowing across time and geography. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow. First, we will employ neural language models to automate the parsing and annotation of digitized historical texts, including classical Chinese manuscripts and early vernacular materials. Second, phonetic data from field recordings will be processed using GPU-accelerated acoustic analysis to map dialectal sound shifts and identify substrate influences. Third, graph-based algorithms will model contact-induced grammatical changes across language boundaries, integrating textual, phonetic, and sociolinguistic metadata. The project will utilize distributed computing frameworks to handle heterogeneous data types (text, audio, geospatial) at scale, requiring parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access computational toolkit for East Asian historical linguistics, (2) annotated corpora of endangered dialects, and (3) quantitative models of language change that challenge Eurocentric periodization frameworks. By enabling large-scale comparative analysis, this work will provide new insights into language contact phenomena in pre-modern East Asia while developing computational methods adaptable to other non-Indo-European language families. The requested HPC resources are critical for training custom transformer models, conducting high-fidelity acoustic simulations, and managing complex network analyses beyond the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: East Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages of East Asia, including, but not limited to, the Sino-Tibetan, Japanese, and Korean languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between language contact, cultural identity, and digital communication practices in endangered language communities, leveraging computational methods to analyze multimodal linguistic data at scale. While existing sociolinguistic research often focuses on spoken or written corpora, this study addresses a critical gap by integrating paralinguistic features (e.g., gesture, prosody, emoji usage) and social network patterns from digital platforms into models of language vitality. The research employs high-performance computing to process terabytes of audio-visual recordings, social media interactions, and ethnographic field notes from three Indigenous communities undergoing rapid language shift. Custom natural language processing pipelines will be developed to detect code-switching patterns, while computer vision techniques will quantify culturally significant gestural repertoires. Graph-based neural networks will model the diffusion of linguistic innovations through hybrid online-offline social networks, with agent-based simulations testing hypotheses about intervention strategies. Computational demands arise from the need to align heterogeneous data streams across temporal scales, process low-resource languages with limited NLP tools, and run iterative simulations of complex adaptive systems. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for assessing language vitality through multimodal signaling, 2) predictive models of cultural transmission pathways in digitally mediated environments, and 3) open-source tools for community-led language documentation that integrate machine learning with Indigenous data sovereignty protocols. By bridging computational linguistics, interaction analysis, and anthropological theory, this work advances our understanding of how embodied cultural practices adapt to technological change while providing actionable insights for language revitalization efforts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the anthropological, historical, and sociological context of language with a particular emphasis on language use and its role in shaping cultural and social diversity. Includes instruction in applied linguistics, data management, field methods, language heritage, socialization, structure, linguistic analysis, linguistic theory, and multilingualism.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing hardware-software co-design for energy-efficient embedded AI systems, a critical gap in deploying machine learning models on resource-constrained edge devices. Current neural architectures and deployment frameworks often fail to balance computational efficiency, latency, and power consumption, particularly when adapting to diverse hardware configurations. To tackle this, we propose a multi-objective optimization framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate, train, and evaluate neural networks under hardware-aware constraints. The computational approach combines parallelized neural architecture search (NAS) with hardware performance modeling, utilizing distributed GPU clusters to iteratively explore Pareto-optimal architectures across accuracy, latency, and energy metrics. Additionally, we will implement cycle-accurate simulations of custom accelerators using FPGA emulation workflows scaled across HPC nodes. This hybrid methodology enables rapid exploration of co-design spaces spanning algorithmic, compiler, and microarchitectural parameters. The requested resources will support large-scale distributed training of surrogate models for hardware prediction, Monte Carlo sampling of design permutations, and validation against benchmark datasets for embedded vision and sensor applications. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for hardware-in-the-loop NAS, validated Pareto fronts for edge-AI use cases, and novel accelerator architectures optimized for sparse, quantized neural networks. By bridging the simulation gap between machine learning and low-power hardware design, this work aims to advance the development of adaptive, sustainable edge computing systems. The results will directly contribute to applications in autonomous IoT, robotics, and smart infrastructure, while establishing computational workflows for future co-design research in computer engineering.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disorders present complex management challenges in internal medicine, requiring integration of multi-dimensional patient data to optimize care. Current approaches often fail to leverage the full breadth of available clinical, genomic, and behavioral data due to computational limitations, resulting in suboptimal personalization of treatment strategies. This project seeks to address this gap by developing high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive models that synthesize electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and patient-reported behavioral factors.
