By aligning computational advances with research administration priorities, the project aims to establish scalable best practices for leaders managing multidisciplinary teams in academia, government, and healthcare. Results will be disseminated through open-source modules and case studies integrated into graduate curricula, directly supporting the program’s mission to train data-proficient administrators capable of navigating 21st-century research challenges.
cip_definition: A program designed to prepare formally trained, advanced-level personnel for research administration leadership positions at colleges and universities, government agencies, hospitals, nonprofit agencies, and in industry. Includes instruction in bioethics, biostatistics, ethical, legal and regulatory consideration in clinical investigation, financial analysis, grant writing, managing and monitoring clinical trials, project management, strategic planning, and team building.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a culturally responsive, data-driven framework for optimizing instructional strategies in Tribal/First Nation K-12 classrooms through advanced computational modeling. Despite growing recognition of Indigenous pedagogies, there remains a critical gap in scalable tools that integrate Native knowledge systems, language preservation needs, and localized learning patterns into curriculum design. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal educational datasets from six Tribal school districts, including longitudinal student performance records, Indigenous language text corpora, and ethnographic observations of classroom interactions. Machine learning models will identify patterns in how students engage with STEM concepts when taught through place-based, culturally grounded methodologies versus standard approaches. A novel agent-based simulation platform will then model the cascading impacts of different instructional designs on language retention, intergenerational knowledge transfer, and academic persistence rates. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of terabyte-scale qualitative data (oral histories, elder interviews) via NLP pipelines optimized for low-resource Indigenous languages, coupled with high-dimensional parameter sweeps to test intervention scenarios in simulated classroom environments. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for educators to prototype curriculum elements that balance state standards with Tribal educational priorities, as well as evidence-based guidelines for resource allocation in rural Indigenous schools. By centering Indigenous epistemologies in computational analysis, this work aims to advance equity in AI/ML applications for education while strengthening capacity for self-determined pedagogical innovation in Native communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of instructional and advising services for American Indian, Alaska Native, and Hawaiian Native students at various learning levels and that prepares individuals to perform teaching and administrative functions in Tribal/First Nation schools. Includes instruction in the cultural traditions and social patterns, history and politics, learning styles and issues, curriculum design, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling techniques and social issues, rural education services, distance education, adult education techniques, school administration, applicable laws and regulations, and research issues.

abstract: Wildland fires pose an escalating threat to ecosystems, infrastructure, and human safety due to climate change and expanding urban-wildland interfaces. Current predictive models for fire behavior and spread lack sufficient resolution to account for dynamic interactions between fire, heterogeneous fuels, micro-terrain, and atmospheric turbulence, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making and post-fire investigation. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-performance computational framework to simulate wildland fire dynamics at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales. The research will employ coupled physics-based models integrating large-eddy simulation (LES) for turbulent combustion, pyrolysis-driven fuel decomposition, and radiative heat transfer, validated against empirical data from prescribed burns and historical fire case studies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve meter-scale fire-atmosphere interactions across landscapes spanning hundreds of square kilometers, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of cores. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameterization of fuel moisture and ember transport models using multi-source environmental data, including remote sensing inputs and real-time weather station feeds. Outcomes will include an open-source simulation toolkit for fire agencies, improved probabilistic fire spread forecasts for operational use, and enhanced forensic analysis capabilities for fire origin determination. The computational framework will also enable virtual testing of novel fire suppression strategies, such as optimized firebreak placement and drone-assisted ignition tactics. By advancing the fidelity and scalability of wildland fire modeling, this work aims to directly inform firefighter safety protocols, evacuation planning, and mitigation policies while providing academic researchers with new tools to study fire ecology and climate change impacts. The requested HPC allocation will support ensemble simulations across diverse environmental conditions, ensuring robust validation and operational relevance.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science, firefighting and investigation to the prevention, control and mitigation of wildland fires and the analysis of causes. Includes instruction in fire science and behavior, wildland environments, meteorology, wildland fire hydraulics and dynamics, water and chemical supply systems, wildland firefighting operations, airborne firefighting, firebreak engineering, communications systems, wildland arson, forensic procedures, wildland fire prevention, investigation techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical and synchronic phonetic variation across North Germanic languages using high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale acoustic and textual datasets. The research focuses on resolving ambiguities in the phonological evolution of Scandinavian languages, particularly the divergence of regional dialects in Norway, Sweden, and Denmark, and their relationship to insular Nordic varieties (e.g., Icelandic, Faroese). Current scholarship lacks comprehensive models of how vowel shifts and consonant gradation patterns propagated across these communities, partly due to computational limitations in processing heterogeneous data spanning medieval runic inscriptions, modern speech corpora, and digitized historical texts. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow. First, we will employ neural networks trained on parallelized phonetic data to detect subtle acoustic patterns in contemporary and archival speech recordings. Second, phylogenetic algorithms, adapted from computational biology, will model language diversification timelines, integrating textual evidence from Old Norse manuscripts and dialect maps. Finally, agent-based simulations will test sociolinguistic hypotheses about contact-driven changes in coastal versus inland regions. The project requires HPC resources to manage the scale of data (∼50 TB of audio, annotated texts, and metadata) and the complexity of simulations involving thousands of linguistic variables. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Nordic phonetic features, refined models of language change applicable to understudied minority varieties (e.g., Elfdalian), and methodological frameworks for cross-disciplinary computational linguistics. This work will advance the digital humanities in Scandinavian studies by enabling resource-intensive analyses previously constrained by local computing infrastructure, while contributing to broader linguistic theories of language contact and divergence.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages, literatures, and linguistics of the peoples of Scandinavia and associated Northern European island groups. Programs may involve multiple languages and language families, not be specific as to the name of the language(s) studied, or be otherwise undifferentiated.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation in technology-driven industries, where dynamic factors such as fluctuating market demands, regulatory constraints, and rapid technological advancements complicate decision-making. Traditional resource management frameworks often struggle to balance competing priorities in these environments, leading to inefficiencies and reduced innovation capacity. To overcome this, we propose developing a computational model that integrates agent-based simulations and machine learning (ML) to dynamically allocate resources across multi-project, multi-team organizations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets—including historical project timelines, budget allocations, and workforce performance metrics—and to simulate complex, real-world scenarios with varying constraints. The agent-based component will model interactions between teams, projects, and external stakeholders, while ML algorithms will identify patterns in past successes and failures to predict optimal allocation strategies under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that enables organizations to proactively adjust resource distribution in response to emerging risks and opportunities. This tool will be validated against case studies from semiconductor manufacturing and renewable energy sectors, where rapid iteration and cross-functional collaboration are critical. The project aligns with the Science/Technology Management program’s focus on bridging technical and managerial domains by providing actionable insights into balancing operational efficiency with innovation. The computational intensity of simulating thousands of allocation scenarios, coupled with real-time data integration, necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve practical runtime performance. Results will contribute to academic literature on adaptive management systems and offer organizations a framework to enhance agility in technology-intensive markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop science, technical, and business skills required for management of people and systems in technology-based industries, government agencies, and non-profit organizations. Includes instruction in computer applications, general management principles, production and operations management, project management, quality control, safety and health issues, and statistics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze emergent systemic risks in decentralized financial ecosystems, particularly those arising from the integration of autonomous algorithmic agents and hybrid human-AI decision-making processes in capital markets. Traditional risk models, which rely on static correlations and equilibrium assumptions, fail to capture the nonlinear dynamics and adaptive behaviors inherent in modern financial networks. The study addresses this gap by employing large-scale agent-based simulations to model interactions between institutional traders, retail investors, liquidity providers, and regulatory mechanisms in real-world market conditions. High-performance computing resources are essential to execute Monte Carlo experiments across multi-dimensional parameter spaces, including varying market structures, agent learning rates, and regulatory constraint scenarios. The computational architecture integrates deep reinforcement learning agents with evolutionary optimization techniques, requiring parallelized GPU-accelerated training environments to handle complex reward functions and state-action spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds for cascading liquidity failures in fragmented markets, (2) quantification of emergent volatility patterns caused by competing AI-driven trading strategies, and (3) development of stress-testing protocols for regulatory sandboxes. By leveraging distributed computing capabilities to process petabytes of order book data and alternative sentiment indicators, this research aims to establish predictive metrics for systemic instability while maintaining market efficiency. The resulting framework will provide financial institutions and policymakers with adaptive tools to navigate the computational arms race in algorithmic trading while mitigating unintended consequences of decentralized finance ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and analyze the financial and monetary aspects and performance of business enterprises, banking institutions, or other organizations. Includes instruction in principles of accounting, financial instruments, capital planning, funds acquisition, asset and debt management, budgeting, financial analysis, and investments and portfolio management.

abstract: The management of infectious diseases in non-domesticated animal populations presents significant challenges due to ecological complexity, host biodiversity, and limited access to longitudinal health data. Emerging pathogens in wildlife, such as avian influenza in migratory birds or mycobacterial infections in captive zoo species, threaten conservation efforts, animal welfare, and public health. Current predictive models often lack the resolution to account for species-specific physiological traits, behavioral interactions, and environmental stressors. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing high-resolution, multi-scale computational models to predict disease transmission dynamics and optimize therapeutic interventions for zoological species. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate genomic, ecological, and clinical datasets to simulate pathogen spread within heterogeneous animal populations. Agent-based modeling frameworks will be employed to represent individual host movement, contact networks, and immune responses across diverse habitats, from captive enclosures to migratory corridors. Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical outbreak data and electronic health records from zoological institutions to identify risk factors for disease susceptibility and treatment failure. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further model aerosolized pathogen transmission in mixed-species enclosures. The scale of these analyses—encompassing genomic sequences from 50+ species, GPS tracking data from 10,000+ individuals, and 3D enclosure geometries—necessitates parallelized processing and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide prophylactic measures, habitat design modifications, and species-specific dosing regimens for antimicrobials. This work will advance the evidence base for precision medicine in zoological health while providing a framework for One Health initiatives addressing zoonotic threats. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across ecological scenarios, sensitivity analyses of intervention strategies, and real-time model calibration using wildlife health monitoring data.
cip_definition: Research focused on the specialized treatment and care of zoo animals, performing animals, and animals living in the wild. May included related research in the principles and procedures used in the observation, diagnosis, care and treatment of illness, disease, injury, deformity, or other anomalies in non-domesticated animals.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for training pre-service German language educators. A critical challenge in German language teacher education lies in modeling the dynamic interplay between pedagogical strategies, learner variability, and linguistic complexity—particularly in morphosyntax and discourse pragmatics, which pose persistent difficulties for second-language learners. Traditional approaches to analyzing classroom interactions or designing instructional materials often rely on manual coding or static frameworks, limiting scalability and real-time adaptability. To address this, we propose a computational linguistics framework combining neural language models, agent-based simulations, and corpus-driven analysis to (1) model the relationship between instructional interventions and learner outcomes across proficiency levels and (2) generate context-sensitive feedback for teacher trainees. The project will process multimodal datasets spanning classroom recordings, learner essays, and teacher annotations using transformer-based architectures (e.g., fine-tuned BERT variants) to identify patterns in effective error correction and communicative task design. Agent-based models will simulate diverse learner-teacher interactions under varying curricular constraints, requiring parallelized computation to explore parameter spaces across sociolinguistic contexts. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for visualizing pedagogical decision pathways and a repository of synthetically augmented training scenarios calibrated to Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) competencies. By enabling large-scale analysis of teaching practices and their longitudinal impacts, this work aims to bridge gaps in evidence-based teacher preparation while preserving the dialogic nature of language instruction. The requested HPC resources are essential for training multilingual models, running complex simulations, and optimizing real-time feedback systems that balance computational efficiency with pedagogical validity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach German language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance crisis response effectiveness through advanced computational modeling of dynamic disaster scenarios, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation and decision-making under uncertainty. Current incident command systems often rely on static contingency plans, which struggle to adapt to rapidly evolving, large-scale emergencies such as cascading natural disasters or coordinated terrorist attacks. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates real-time data assimilation, agent-based simulations, and machine learning to model multi-hazard interactions, stakeholder coordination challenges, and resource distribution bottlenecks. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) generating synthetic disaster scenarios using stochastic weather models, infrastructure failure cascades, and population mobility patterns; (2) simulating emergency response workflows through massively parallel agent-based models that capture the decision-making processes of first responders, hospital networks, and civilian populations; and (3) training reinforcement learning algorithms on HPC clusters to identify adaptive resource allocation strategies that minimize response times and maximize lives saved. The models will incorporate multi-modal data streams, including satellite imagery, social media feeds, and IoT sensor networks, processed through GPU-accelerated neural networks for real-time situational awareness. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for crisis managers that enables stress-testing of emergency plans against novel threat scenarios, predictive analytics for pre-positioning critical supplies, and AI-assisted recommendations for interagency coordination. By leveraging HPC resources to handle the combinatorial complexity of simultaneous hazard impacts and human behavior dynamics, this work aims to advance incident command system theory while providing practical tools for mitigating systemic vulnerabilities in disaster response networks. The resulting framework will be validated through historical case studies of hurricane responses and live exercises with regional emergency management agencies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of the incident command system model to formulating and implementing effective response to natural and man-made disasters. Includes instruction in contingency planning, hazard and risk assessment, joint operations, law and ethics, emergency response and recovery, event mitigation, emergency rescue and medical operations, incident command, terrorism and national security issues, law enforcement, relief administration, volunteer and citizen coordination, public relations and applications to specific types of incidents.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in traffic control and flagging operations through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Current traffic management strategies in construction and maintenance zones often rely on static protocols that do not adapt dynamically to real-time variables such as fluctuating traffic volumes, driver behavior, weather conditions, or emergency scenarios. These limitations can compromise safety for workers, drivers, and pedestrians while increasing congestion and operational costs. To overcome these issues, we propose the development of a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework to model traffic flow, pedestrian movement, and flagger decision-making in complex, dynamic environments. The computational model will integrate real-world data from traffic sensors, weather reports, and historical incident logs to simulate scenarios ranging from routine freeway flagging to high-stakes emergency response operations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets, run thousands of parallel simulations with varying parameters, and train machine learning algorithms to optimize traffic control strategies. Key computational tasks include real-time pathfinding for autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions, probabilistic risk assessment for night operations, and adaptive signal optimization under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include data-driven guidelines for adaptive traffic control zone designs, predictive tools for incident prevention, and scenario-specific training modules for flagging personnel. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to reduce collision risks, improve traffic throughput in work zones, and establish a scalable framework for next-generation traffic management systems aligned with emerging smart infrastructure technologies. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in flagging certification programs and provide actionable insights for transportation agencies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to control the movement of traffic through construction and maintenance zones and to protect the safety of work crews, drivers, and pedestrians. Includes instruction in flagging duties and responsibilities, the traffic control zone, flagging signals, pavement markers, freeway flagging, utility flagging, emergency response flagging, and night traffic control.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between digital communication platforms and the preservation of marginalized sign languages, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of computational linguistics, disability studies, and sociocultural analysis. While major spoken languages dominate automated language technologies, sign languages—particularly those used by smaller deaf communities—face systemic exclusion from digital tools, exacerbating social inequities. The research addresses this gap by developing computational models to analyze and support the documentation of under-resourced sign languages, using high-volume video datasets from community-driven platforms. The core challenge lies in processing multimodal linguistic data (gestures, facial expressions, spatial syntax) at scale, which demands advanced machine learning workflows and significant computational power. The project employs a hybrid approach: (1) training vision-based transformer models on annotated sign language corpora to automate linguistic feature extraction, (2) implementing graph neural networks to map dialectal variations across regional signing communities, and (3) simulating language contact dynamics through agent-based modeling to predict attrition risks. High-performance computing resources are essential for handling the terabyte-scale video datasets, optimizing deep learning architectures with distributed training, and running parallelized simulations of language evolution scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for sign language corpus analysis, quantitative insights into the impact of digital marginalization on language vitality, and policy recommendations for equitable resource allocation in assistive technologies. By centering computational rigor on a socially urgent issue, this work advances methodological innovation in multimodal linguistics while directly addressing accessibility disparities encoded in contemporary technosocial systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the anthropological, historical, and sociological context of language with a particular emphasis on language use and its role in shaping cultural and social diversity. Includes instruction in applied linguistics, data management, field methods, language heritage, socialization, structure, linguistic analysis, linguistic theory, and multilingualism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven decision support framework for optimizing farm management strategies under dynamic environmental and economic conditions. Despite advances in precision agriculture, farmers and ranchers face persistent challenges in integrating heterogeneous datasets—such as soil health metrics, weather forecasts, commodity price trends, and livestock performance indicators—into actionable operational plans. Current models often lack the scalability to account for regional variability or the temporal resolution to adapt to rapid market shifts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build an adaptive simulation platform that combines agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning. Agent-based models will simulate farm operations at granular spatial and temporal scales, capturing interactions between management decisions (e.g., crop rotations, irrigation schedules, herd culling), stochastic environmental factors, and market volatility. Monte Carlo simulations will quantify risk profiles for alternative strategies, while neural networks trained on historical yield data and satellite imagery will predict localized outcomes under climate variability. The computational intensity arises from the need to parallelize thousands of scenario iterations across diverse agroecological zones and validate models against multi-terabyte datasets from USDA reports, IoT-enabled farm sensors, and remote sensing platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario-based resource allocation, capable of recommending optimal planting dates, input applications, and livestock management protocols tailored to real-time conditions. By quantifying trade-offs between short-term profitability and long-term sustainability at unprecedented resolution, this work aims to reduce operational risks for small-to-midsize farms while informing policy frameworks for agricultural resilience. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial fidelity and stochastic depth required for actionable insights, with preliminary simulations indicating a 40-60x speedup over existing cloud-based solutions when scaling to regional analyses.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage farms, ranches, and similar enterprises. Includes instruction in applicable agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, taxation, capitalization, purchasing, government programs and regulations, operational planning and budgeting, contracts and negotiation, and estate planning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize perioperative decision-making and surgical outcomes through predictive modeling of patient-specific risks and real-time intraoperative data integration. Surgical nursing practice faces challenges in dynamically assessing patient responses to anesthesia, blood loss, and physiological stressors during procedures, as well as predicting postoperative complications such as infections or delayed recovery. While existing clinical guidelines provide general protocols, personalized risk stratification remains limited due to the complex interplay of preoperative health status, surgical variables, and intraoperative events. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline leveraging electronic health records (EHRs), intraoperative vital sign streams, and surgical nursing documentation from a multi-site perioperative database (n ≈ 45,000 cases). The computational approach will employ ensemble models to identify risk signatures for postoperative complications and neural networks to model temporal relationships in physiological data during surgery. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing high-frequency sensor data (1Hz sampling rates across 15+ parameters), training multimodal architectures that fuse structured EHRs with unstructured nursing notes, and conducting hyperparameter optimization across 100+ model configurations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive system for sepsis, hypothermia, and hemodynamic instability risks, operable within clinical timeframes, and (2) synthetic data generation tools to simulate rare adverse events for nurse training scenarios. The project will enable evidence-based refinement of nursing interventions such as intraoperative warming protocols or vigilance windows for critical transitions. By coupling large-scale clinical data with HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to advance precision nursing practices in the operating room while maintaining rigorous attention to interpretability and ethical AI deployment standards.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the complex relationship between musical performance practices and the acoustic properties of architectural spaces through high-fidelity computational simulations. While historical and contemporary performance practices are often studied in isolation, the dynamic interaction between sound production, spatial acoustics, and performer adaptation remains underexplored due to the computational complexity of modeling real-world environments. The project will employ wave-based acoustic simulation methods, including finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) and boundary element modeling (BEM), to recreate the acoustic signatures of diverse performance venues—from Baroque churches to modern concert halls. These simulations will be coupled with machine learning techniques to analyze how performers intuitively adapt their technique to spatial acoustics, using motion-capture data of instrumentalists and vocalists. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve 3D wave propagation at audio frequencies across large volumetric meshes, requiring parallelized computations across thousands of cores to achieve real-world accuracy within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include a novel database of performer-acoustic interaction patterns and an open-source framework for virtual acoustic rehearsal environments. This work will provide new insights into the embodied cognition of musical performance while developing tools that enable artists to experience historically informed acoustic environments digitally. The computational methodologies developed may also inform future architectural designs for performance spaces, bridging artistic practice with acoustic engineering. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project addresses critical gaps in musicology and performance studies through an interdisciplinary approach that transcends traditional analytical limitations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: The increasing complexity of disease diagnostics in veterinary pathology demands advanced tools to integrate heterogeneous data types, including high-resolution histopathology imaging, multi-omics profiles, and clinical metadata. Current workflows struggle to process these datasets efficiently, limiting the ability to identify subtle patterns in disease progression, especially in cases with ambiguous morphologic features or multifactorial etiologies. This project proposes a computational pathology framework to enhance diagnostic precision by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources for large-scale analysis of animal tissue samples. The research will focus on developing machine learning models to correlate histologic features from whole-slide images (WSIs) with genomic and proteomic data from diseased tissues across species, including companion animals and livestock. Computational workflows will utilize deep learning architectures (e.g., convolutional neural networks) for WSI segmentation and feature extraction, coupled with graph-based algorithms to model molecular pathway disruptions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabytes of imaging data, iterative model training across multiple GPU nodes, and integration of spatially resolved omics datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for early detection of neoplasms and inflammatory diseases with improved classification accuracy over traditional methods, (2) identification of novel biomarker combinations for diagnostically challenging cases, and (3) open-source tools optimized for veterinary diagnostic laboratories to automate tissue analysis workflows. The project will directly address critical gaps in veterinary diagnostic capacity, with potential applications in forensic pathology and quality assurance programs. By establishing scalable computational methods for multimodal data synthesis, this work aims to advance precision veterinary medicine while providing a template for resource-efficient pathology research in resource-constrained settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of diseased animal tissues and anatomic abnormalities. May included related research in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management and quality control.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the efficacy of school counseling interventions using large-scale, multi-source student data. School counselors face increasing demands to address complex student needs—academic, social-emotional, and career development—amid limited resources. However, existing studies often rely on small samples or self-reported data, limiting actionable insights. Our research will integrate anonymized student records (e.g., academic performance, attendance, behavioral logs), counselor notes, and longitudinal survey responses to model how interventions correlate with outcomes such as academic resilience, mental health improvements, and college enrollment. A key challenge is the heterogeneous, high-dimensional nature of these datasets, which requires advanced computational methods. We propose using natural language processing (NLP) to extract themes from qualitative counselor notes, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map peer support networks, and reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate intervention strategies under resource constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train these models on district-level data spanning 50,000+ students, manage temporal dependencies in longitudinal analyses, and run multi-agent simulations of counseling workflows. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying intervention components most predictive of student success across demographic subgroups, (2) optimizing resource allocation for early intervention systems, and (3) generating open-source tools for school counselors to visualize risk factors and intervention pathways. This work will advance data-driven decision-making in counselor education by bridging gaps between qualitative practices and quantitative analytics, while adhering to ethical standards for student privacy and algorithmic fairness. By leveraging HPC capabilities, we aim to provide scalable solutions that empower counselors to address inequities and maximize student outcomes without overburdening existing systems.
cip_title: Counselor Education/ School Counseling and Guidance Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the theory and principles of guidance and counseling to the provision of support for the personal, social, educational, and vocational development of students, and the organizing of guidance services within elementary, middle and secondary educational institutions. Includes instruction in legal and professional requirements, therapeutic counselor intervention, vocational counseling, and related sociological and psychological foundations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of linguistic variation and evolution in Portuguese dialects, with a focus on the divergence and convergence between Metropolitan Portuguese and Luso-Brazilian varieties. A critical gap persists in large-scale, data-driven studies of phonological, syntactic, and lexical shifts across historical and contemporary texts, particularly in under-resourced dialects. To address this, we propose the development of a corpus-based computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to model dialectal trajectories and contact phenomena. The research will compile and digitize a multilingual corpus of historical manuscripts, transcribed oral narratives, and modern digital texts (15th–21st centuries), prioritizing underrepresented Luso-African and Brazilian vernaculars. Computational workflows will include phonetic alignment algorithms for cross-dialectal sound mapping, transformer-based models for syntactic pattern detection, and graph neural networks to trace lexical borrowing and semantic change. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific language models on terabytes of unstructured text, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks such as diachronic sentiment analysis, and simulating language contact scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative models of dialectal divergence timelines, (2) an open-access repository of annotated linguistic data, and (3) methodological frameworks for scalable philological analysis. This work will directly inform debates on language standardization, creolization processes, and pedagogical tools for Portuguese instruction. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional philology, the project aims to establish reproducible pipelines for dialect studies while preserving linguistic diversity in technology applications such as automated translation systems and speech recognition tailored to Lusophone communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Portuguese language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Metropolitan Portuguese; Luso-Brazilian Portuguese; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical grids, driven by renewable energy integration, extreme weather events, and aging infrastructure, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize grid resilience and safety. This project seeks to address critical challenges in power line maintenance and installation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and predict mechanical stresses, environmental impacts, and failure risks in overhead and underground electrical systems. Traditional analytical models often oversimplify dynamic variables such as wind loading, ice accumulation, and soil displacement, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and safety margins. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model the structural and environmental interactions of power line infrastructure. The HPC environment will enable large-scale simulations of pole and cable networks under diverse climatic and load conditions, while ML algorithms trained on historical failure data will identify patterns predictive of equipment degradation. Key objectives include quantifying the impact of high-voltage transients on insulator fatigue, optimizing trenching paths for underground cables to minimize soil instability risks, and developing predictive maintenance protocols for fibre-optic communication lines. By integrating real-time sensor data from smart grid systems into these models, the project aims to generate adaptive risk-assessment tools for lineworkers, reducing outage frequencies and enhancing workplace safety. Outcomes will include open-source simulation templates for training programs, data-driven guidelines for code updates, and a decision-support platform for infrastructure planning. This work directly aligns with the Lineworker program’s mission to advance technical education through cutting-edge tools, ensuring graduates are equipped to address emerging challenges in grid modernization and climate adaptation. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required computational granularity and scale, enabling transformative insights into the interplay between mechanical, electrical, and environmental factors in power distribution systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain and repair local, long-distance, and rural electric power cables and communication lines; erect and construct pole and tower lines; and install underground lines and cables. Includes instruction in cable installation and repair, fibre-optic technology, trenching, mobile equipment and crane operation, high-voltage installations, maintenance and inspection, safety, remote communications, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Developmental education programs are critical for addressing systemic inequities in college readiness, yet scalable, evidence-based strategies for optimizing instructional interventions remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate the longitudinal impacts of adaptive teaching practices on underprepared student cohorts, with a focus on identifying personalized instructional pathways that improve persistence and academic success. The research problem centers on the complexity of analyzing heterogeneous student data—including engagement patterns, assessment histories, and socio-cognitive factors—across diverse institutional contexts, which limits the generalizability of traditional small-scale studies. Using anonymized datasets from multi-institutional partnerships (encompassing >50,000 student records), we will implement machine learning-driven clustering to classify at-risk learner profiles and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom-scale interventions. Computational workflows will integrate dynamic Bayesian networks to evaluate how real-time adjustments to instructional design (e.g., scaffolded critical thinking activities, multimodal content delivery) affect learning outcomes under varying motivational and resource constraints. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing ABM simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, enabling sensitivity analyses of factors like class size, technology integration, and instructor feedback latency. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting the efficacy of developmental education strategies under resource-limited conditions, as well as open-source tools for generating institution-specific recommendations. This work directly addresses gaps in equitable teaching practices by quantifying how learner-centered adaptations can mitigate attrition risks, with broader implications for curriculum standardization and professional development in teacher education programs.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach educational strategies for assisting students who are perceived as underprepared for the academic rigor of college-level coursework at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone of cancer treatment, yet optimizing therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity requires precise modeling of radiation interactions with biological tissues and dynamic patient anatomy. Current clinical tools often rely on simplified approximations of radiation transport, tumor response, and normal tissue tolerance, which may limit personalization and accuracy in complex cases. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework for radiation treatment planning and outcome prediction by integrating patient-specific radiobiological models, real-time anatomical dynamics, and advanced Monte Carlo dose calculations. The primary research challenges include (1) modeling stochastic variations in radiation-induced DNA damage across heterogeneous tumor and normal tissue microenvironments, (2) simulating the interplay between fractionated radiation delivery and temporal changes in tumor oxygenation/geometry, and (3) establishing predictive relationships between multi-scale biological parameters and clinical outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to implement GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo radiation transport algorithms (based on TOPAS-nBio and Geant4-DNA) coupled with finite-element biomechanical models of organ motion and deep learning-based auto-segmentation. The computational workflow will process high-resolution 4D CT/MRI datasets (>2 TB/patient cohort) while performing parallelized parameter sweeps across radiobiological variables. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of resolving sub-millimeter dose deposition patterns under respiratory motion constraints (<1% statistical uncertainty) and probabilistic forecasts of tumor control probability/normal tissue complication probability incorporating spatial and temporal heterogeneity. This resource will enable unprecedented investigation of dose escalation strategies in moving targets, rare toxicity prediction in serial organs-at-risk, and biologically optimized fractionation schemes. By bridging computational physics with clinical radiobiology, the project aims to establish a paradigm shift toward simulation-driven personalized radiation oncology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of ionizing radiation to treat patients with cancer and other diseases. Includes instruction in treatment planning, instrument design and operation, radiation physics and radiobiology. One of two general certificates in the area of radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of narrative structures in playwriting and screenwriting, addressing the challenge of quantifying emotional and thematic coherence in dramatic texts. While traditional script development relies on subjective interpretation and iterative workshops, this research proposes a data-driven framework to model narrative dynamics, character interactions, and audience engagement patterns at scale. The core problem lies in the absence of systematic tools to analyze how micro-level creative choices—such as dialogue pacing, emotional tone shifts, or subtextual cues—cumulatively shape macro-level audience experiences. To address this, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on theatrical and cinematic scripts, to parse semantic, syntactic, and sentiment features across diverse dramatic corpora. Agent-based modeling will simulate audience response trajectories based on demographic and psychographic variables, while network analysis will map character relationship evolution within nonlinear plot structures. These computational methods require HPC capabilities to process large text datasets (spanning 10,000+ scripts), train custom language models, and run iterative simulations of narrative impact. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access toolkit for playwrights to visualize emotional arcs and predict audience engagement during script development; (2) a comparative analysis of successful vs. underperforming scripts across genres, identifying statistically significant narrative patterns; and (3) novel metrics for assessing script viability in pre-production phases. By bridging computational humanities with performing arts practice, this work aims to democratize access to advanced dramaturgical analysis while preserving the irreducibility of creative expression. The requested resources will enable processing times reduced from weeks to hours for large-scale script corpora, facilitating real-time feedback loops between human creativity and machine learning insights.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for communicating dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the composition of creative written works for the theatre, film, and/or television. Includes instruction in creative writing craft, scene writing, script development, stage and/or camera instructions, line and moment analysis, script reading, script editing, and the creation of full productions.

abstract: This project seeks to analyze the economic impacts of renewable energy integration in regional electricity markets, with a focus on policy-driven resource allocation and market efficiency. Renewable energy adoption introduces complex trade-offs between regulatory incentives, infrastructure costs, and dynamic pricing, yet existing models often oversimplify microeconomic interactions among producers, grid operators, and consumers. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution computational model that simulates decentralized decision-making under evolving policy constraints. The model will integrate heterogeneous agent behaviors, stochastic renewable generation profiles, and regulatory frameworks to evaluate how subsidy structures, carbon pricing, and transmission investments affect long-term market equilibria. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the iterative optimization required for multi-agent systems, Bayesian parameter estimation using historical market data, and Monte Carlo simulations spanning diverse policy scenarios. By parallelizing computationally intensive tasks such as solving Nash equilibria across thousands of simulated agents and calibrating high-dimensional demand-response functions, HPC will enable scalable analysis of market dynamics at a granular spatiotemporal resolution. Expected outcomes include identifying policy mixes that minimize price volatility while incentivizing renewable adoption, quantifying distributional impacts on consumer subgroups, and mapping interregional resource allocation efficiencies. Results will provide actionable insights for regulators and energy firms, advancing applied microeconomic research on transition economies. This work underscores the critical role of computational economics in addressing sustainability challenges, demonstrating how HPC-driven models can bridge theoretical principles with real-world energy systems analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic principles and analytical techniques to the study of particular industries, activities, or the exploitation of particular resources. Includes instruction in economic theory; microeconomic analysis and modeling of specific industries, commodities; the economic consequences of resource allocation decisions; regulatory and consumer factors; and the technical aspects of specific subjects as they relate to economic analysis.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in simulating emergent quantum phenomena within hybrid material systems, which exhibit complex interactions across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Traditional computational approaches struggle to capture the interplay between electronic, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom in these systems, particularly under non-equilibrium conditions. This limitation hinders progress in designing materials for next-generation energy conversion devices and quantum information technologies. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate ab initio density functional theory (DFT), real-time time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (t-DMRG) methods, and machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing computationally intensive DFT calculations on heterogeneous interfaces, while GPU-optimized tensor network algorithms will enable the study of dynamical quantum correlations in systems exceeding 1000 spin sites—a scale inaccessible to current single-node simulations. Concurrently, neural network potentials trained on-the-fly will bridge quantum-mechanical accuracy with mesoscopic timescales for defect propagation analysis. Expected outcomes include predictive models of ultrafast spin-lattice coupling in transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures and topological insulator surfaces under strain gradients. These results will directly inform experimental synthesis efforts funded by the [AGENCY] grant #XXXXX, with broader impacts on spin-caloritronic device optimization. The computational workflows developed will be disseminated as open-source modules, enhancing capability for the broader quantum materials community. Resource requests target 1.2 million core-hours on a CPU-GPU hybrid architecture, with 256-node scaling tests for tensor network algorithms and 50 TB of temporary storage for active learning datasets. This project represents a necessary convergence of numerical methods that can only be achieved through sustained access to state-of-the-art HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in science technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The study of non-adiabatic dynamics in photochemical reactions presents a fundamental challenge in chemical physics, particularly for systems where quantum coherence and electronic-vibrational coupling dictate reaction outcomes. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve ultrafast timescales and competing pathways in such processes, while computational models often rely on approximations that neglect critical quantum effects or scale poorly with system size. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform ab initio multiple spawning (AIMS) simulations combined with time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT). The research will focus on excited-state proton transfer and conical intersection dynamics in organic chromophores, systems central to photocatalytic energy conversion and light-driven molecular devices. Key objectives include mapping multidimensional potential energy surfaces, quantifying non-radiative decay rates, and identifying coherence lifetimes in solvated environments. The computational approach employs hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to parallelize trajectory propagation and electronic structure calculations, enabling millisecond-scale simulations with explicit solvent models. This methodology overcomes memory bottlenecks associated with traditional grid-based quantum dynamics by utilizing adaptive basis sets and tensor network algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include mechanistic insights into solvent-mediated decoherence and predictive guidelines for tuning reaction quantum yields through molecular design. By integrating these results with ultrafast spectroscopic data, the project aims to establish a computational framework for resolving nonequilibrium photochemical processes with sub-picosecond resolution. The requested HPC allocation will directly support 50-100 concurrent trajectories per system, scaling to >10,000 CPU-core hours per month, which is essential for achieving statistical significance in free energy estimates and convergence in quantum dynamics. This work bridges gaps between theoretical chemistry and molecular physics, offering broadly applicable tools for simulating quantum coherent phenomena in complex chemical environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of structural phenomena combining the disciplines of physical chemistry and atomic/molecular physics. Includes instruction in heterogeneous structures, alignment and surface phenomena, quantum theory, mathematical physics, statistical and classical mechanics, chemical kinetics, and laser physics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cultural narratives, social networks, and mental health outcomes in urban migrant populations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While prior qualitative studies have documented how stigma and community support shape mental health disparities, the dynamic, large-scale interactions between these factors remain understudied due to methodological limitations. We propose a mixed-methods computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP) of ethnographic interviews with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate how health-related beliefs propagate through social networks. The research will analyze 15,000+ transcribed interviews from three transnational migrant communities, employing transformer-based models to classify narratives related to trauma, coping strategies, and healthcare access. These outputs will parameterize ABMs simulating decision-making processes around mental health service utilization under varying social cohesion scenarios. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of text corpora, iterative model calibration, and parallelized simulations across 10,000+ agent networks. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in community-level support structures that buffer against systemic barriers to care, as well as a publicly accessible toolkit for cultural consensus analysis. This work advances medical anthropology by quantitatively modeling how micro-level cultural practices interact with macro-structural inequities, offering translational insights for designing community-led mental health interventions. The project also demonstrates the utility of HPC in scaling ethnographic insights to inform public health strategies without reducing cultural complexity to deterministic variables.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological, socio-cultural, psychological, and behavioral factors as they relate to health, illness, medical practices, and access to health care services. Includes instruction in ethno-medicine, urban health, international health, psychiatric and psychological anthropology, aging, and health and identity.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-documented and typologically diverse languages, focusing on cross-linguistic patterns in morphological and syntactic structures. While advances in natural language processing (NLP) have transformed research on high-resource languages, many languages—particularly those with complex agglutinative or polysynthetic morphologies—remain understudied due to a lack of tailored computational tools and scalable resources. Our research aims to develop and apply high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled methods to analyze large-scale multilingual corpora, including historical texts, transcribed oral narratives, and modern digital communications from under-resourced language communities. Key computational tasks include parallelized morphological parsing, automated alignment of dialectal variants, and probabilistic modeling of syntactic change over time. These methods will leverage GPU-accelerated machine learning frameworks to train transformer-based models on distributed datasets spanning multiple language families, enabling efficient handling of non-linear morphological rules and low-resource training scenarios. The project will also employ agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about language contact dynamics and the diffusion of grammatical features. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological analysis, this work will generate novel insights into universal and language-specific structural constraints, while contributing open-source tools for processing morphologically rich languages. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of annotated corpora, optimized NLP pipelines for under-documented languages, and interdisciplinary frameworks for modeling linguistic diversity. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative training of large language models, process terabyte-scale text and audio datasets, and run computationally intensive simulations. This research will advance both theoretical linguistics and computational methodologies, offering scalable solutions to challenges in language preservation, typological classification, and the study of linguistic evolution.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Foreign Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in geometric topology by investigating the classification and invariant properties of high-dimensional continua under continuous transformation actions. A central challenge lies in characterizing the stability of homotopy and homology structures in non-compact, infinite-dimensional spaces, where traditional analytical methods face prohibitive combinatorial complexity. The research will employ computational homology tools to analyze transformation-equivariant filtrations of spaces, with a focus on detecting persistent homotopy types and constructing algebraic invariants resistant to controlled deformations. Key computational tasks include the parallelized computation of spectral sequences arising from multi-scale cell complexes, large-scale persistence diagram comparisons across transformation orbits, and Monte Carlo sampling of configuration spaces under topological constraints. These methods require high-performance computing resources to manage memory-intensive simplicial complex representations, accelerate Gröbner basis calculations for chain complex mappings, and enable distributed processing of probabilistic invariance tests. Anticipated outcomes include a computational framework for classifying wild embeddings in dimensions ≥4, new lower bounds on the complexity of uncountable transformation groups, and conjectures regarding the decidability of certain homeomorphism problems in descriptive set theory. The results will directly contribute to open problems in geometric topology and logic, particularly the interplay between large-scale geometric properties and point-set topological constraints. By leveraging parallelized algorithms for algebraic topology computations, this work aims to bridge theoretical advances in continua theory with practical tools for handling infinite-dimensional spaces, offering methodological insights applicable to continuum theory, dynamical systems, and foundational set-theoretic topology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of unaltered geometric configurations under conditions of continuous, multi-directional transformations. Includes instruction in mathematical logic, proof theory, model theory, set theory, combinatorics, continua, homotopy, homology, links, and transformation actions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational modeling and analysis of sign language phonology, syntax, and sociolinguistic variation across American Sign Language (ASL) and other global sign languages. While sign languages exhibit complex linguistic structures comparable to spoken languages, their visual-spatial modality presents unique challenges for large-scale quantitative analysis, particularly in modeling articulatory dynamics, syntactic dependencies, and dialectal variations. Current methodologies rely on labor-intensive manual annotation of video corpora, limiting the scope of cross-linguistic comparisons and hindering progress in sign language typology. To address this, we propose developing automated pipelines using 3D motion capture data and computer vision techniques to annotate phonological parameters (handshape, movement, location) and syntactic non-manual markers across six sign languages: ASL, Auslan, LSF, Shuwa jiten, HamNoSys, and Libras (Brazilian Sign Language). HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte video datasets, GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for sign recognition, and large-scale simulations of sign language morphology using finite-state toolkits adapted for visual grammar. The project will also employ agent-based modeling to study the emergence of sociolinguistic variation in deaf communities under different demographic conditions. Outcomes will include the first cross-linguistic database of computationally annotated sign language features, open-source tools for automated sign language analysis, and empirically grounded models of sign language evolution. These resources will directly support linguistic research on understudied sign languages while informing the development of assistive technologies for deaf communities. The computational demands of processing high-resolution video data, simulating multi-agent interactions, and training deep learning models on diverse sign languages necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with parallelized storage, GPU nodes, and high-memory capacity.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Linguistics of ASL and Other Sign Languages
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and scholarly study of the development, structure, and use of American Sign Language (ASL) and other visual signed languages, both as vehicles for communication within the deaf community and in relation to spoken and written languages. Includes instruction in cognitive linguistics; ASL and sign language phonology, syntax, and morphology; sociolinguistics of the deaf community; comparative linguistics; and studies of specific sign languages, including, but not limited to, ASL, Auslan (Australian Sign Language), LSF (French Sign Language), Shuwa jiten (Japanese Sign Language), HamNoSys (German Sign Language), and Gestuno.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and simulation of complex mechanical systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current drafting and design workflows often rely on iterative, resource-intensive simulations to evaluate structural integrity, thermal behavior, and material efficiency, which can lead to computational bottlenecks when handling high-fidelity models or multi-variable optimization tasks. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations by integrating parametric modeling, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization into a unified HPC-enabled pipeline. The proposed approach will leverage parallelized solvers and distributed computing to accelerate simulations of 3D CAD models under dynamic physical conditions, such as stress distribution in aerospace components or energy flow in architectural systems. Additionally, generative design algorithms will be implemented to explore Pareto-optimal solutions balancing weight, cost, and performance metrics. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing clusters to train neural networks for predictive material behavior modeling and to automate topology optimization. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for real-time multi-physics simulations, reducing design iteration cycles by an estimated 40–60% compared to conventional methods. This work will advance drafting and design education by providing open-source computational modules for instructional use, while its applications in industry could enable more sustainable manufacturing through lightweight, resource-efficient designs. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the memory-intensive demands of high-resolution meshing and large-scale parameter sweeps, ensuring robust validation of the proposed methods across diverse engineering use cases.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid cloud-edge computing environments demands novel approaches to dynamic resource allocation that prioritize both performance and security in distributed systems. Current methodologies for managing heterogeneous resources across geographically dispersed nodes struggle to adapt to fluctuating workloads, leading to inefficiencies in energy consumption, latency, and vulnerability to orchestration-layer attacks. This project proposes the development of an adaptive resource management framework that integrates real-time network telemetry with predictive workload modeling to optimize compute, storage, and security resource distribution in multi-tenant environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a hierarchical simulation environment replicating large-scale hybrid infrastructure, incorporating agent-based models for user traffic patterns, stochastic processes for hardware failure scenarios, and machine learning classifiers to detect anomalous resource requests. Computational experiments will test reinforcement learning algorithms against traditional static allocation policies under simulated stress conditions, including distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks and sudden workload spikes. The framework will employ containerized microservices to model edge node interactions, with Kubernetes-based orchestration layers interfacing with Slurm workload managers to emulate cross-platform dynamics. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for energy-per-operation efficiency in varying network topologies, a security-aware resource allocation decision tree, and open-source tools for synthetic workload generation in hybrid infrastructure testbeds. This work addresses critical gaps in system administration practices by providing empirically validated strategies for maintaining service-level agreements while mitigating emergent security risks in next-generation network architectures. Successful implementation could reduce idle resource overhead by an estimated 30-40% in simulated environments while maintaining sub-100ms response latency thresholds, offering practical advancements for organizations managing distributed computational ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: The study of ancient ecosystems and evolutionary dynamics relies increasingly on integrating large, multidimensional datasets spanning fossil morphology, geochemistry, and stratigraphic context. However, existing computational approaches often lack the capacity to synthesize these data at scales necessary to address complex questions about extinction selectivity, biogeographic patterns, and long-term ecosystem resilience. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by developing high-resolution computational models of Triassic-Jurassic terrestrial ecosystems, a critical interval marked by mass extinction and rapid biotic recovery. We propose to utilize high-performance computing resources to implement Bayesian hierarchical models that simultaneously analyze fossil occurrence data, phenotypic trait evolution, and paleoclimatic proxies across spatial and temporal gradients. These models will be coupled with agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about trophic network stability and species dispersal under varying climatic scenarios. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of 3D fossil scan data, running Monte Carlo Markov Chain iterations for multivariate parameter estimation, and simulating ecological interactions across distributed environments. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for synthesizing paleontological data types, quantitative estimates of extinction risk factors among terrestrial vertebrates and plants, and spatially explicit reconstructions of post-extinction community assembly. By leveraging parallel processing and GPU acceleration, this research will achieve unprecedented temporal resolution in deep-time ecological modeling, providing insights into how biological systems respond to abrupt environmental change. Results will advance methodological integration in paleontology while offering empirical benchmarks for evaluating modern biodiversity loss scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of extinct life forms and associated fossil remains, and the reconstruction and analysis of ancient life forms, ecosystems, and geologic processes. Includes instruction in sedimentation and fossilization processes, fossil chemistry, evolutionary biology, paleoecology, paleoclimatology, trace fossils, micropaleontology, invertebrate paleontology, vertebrate paleontology, paleobotany, field research methods, and laboratory research and conservation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, AI-driven simulations for training clinical educators in complex decision-making scenarios. A critical gap exists in Health Professions Education: current simulation tools lack the capacity to dynamically model the nuanced, high-stakes decisions faced by clinical educators, such as balancing trainee autonomy with patient safety or addressing ethical dilemmas in interdisciplinary care teams. Traditional methods rely on static case studies or labor-intensive role-playing, which fail to capture the iterative, context-dependent nature of real-world educational leadership. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating reinforcement learning (RL) and natural language processing (NLP) to generate responsive, branching simulation environments. These environments will emulate multi-layered scenarios involving variable learner competencies, evolving patient conditions, and institutional constraints. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel training of RL agents on diverse educational trajectories, processing multimodal inputs (e.g., trainee performance metrics, simulated patient outcomes, and educator feedback logs) to optimize decision pathways. Concurrently, transformer-based NLP models will analyze historical debriefing transcripts to refine dialogue generation for simulated learners and patients, ensuring linguistic and pedagogical authenticity. The anticipated outcomes include 1) a scalable platform for prototyping competency-specific training modules, 2) quantitative benchmarks for educator decision efficiency under uncertainty, and 3) open-source tools linking simulation performance to evidence-based curriculum adjustments. By bridging computational modeling and health education theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven faculty development, ultimately enhancing the preparedness of clinical educators to navigate complex training environments while maintaining patient care standards.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on education and administration leadership skills for clinical educators across health professions and specialties. Includes instruction in academic leadership, assessment, clinical decision making, curriculum development, ethics, primary care education, program evaluation, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: Agricultural mechanization faces critical challenges in optimizing equipment performance under diverse field conditions while minimizing environmental impact. Current machinery systems often operate with static configurations, leading to inefficiencies in energy use, soil disruption, and input application. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing dynamic, data-driven control algorithms for agricultural machinery using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on integrating real-time sensor data—including soil moisture, crop health metrics, and machinery telemetry—with predictive models to enable adaptive decision-making during field operations. Computational workflows will employ machine learning techniques to analyze multi-modal datasets spanning crop phenology, soil dynamics, and historical equipment performance.
