HPC resources are essential for training neural networks on terabyte-scale agricultural datasets and simulating equipment interactions across heterogeneous landscapes at meter-scale resolution. Expected outcomes include optimized machinery control protocols that reduce fuel consumption by 15–20% and improve input-use efficiency for fertilizers and pesticides by 25% compared to conventional systems. The models will also enable scenario testing for novel equipment configurations, accelerating the design of modular implements tailored to precision agriculture applications. By leveraging parallelized simulations of soil-tool interactions and crop response dynamics, this work will provide actionable insights for manufacturers and farmers adopting smart mechanization technologies. The resulting computational framework will be disseminated as open-source tools to support benchmarking and innovation in agricultural equipment automation, directly advancing the program’s mission to integrate advanced data processing systems with sustainable mechanization practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to sell, select, and service agricultural or agribusiness technical equipment and facilities, including computers, specialized software, power units, machinery, equipment structures, and utilities. Includes instruction in agricultural power systems, planning and selecting materials for the construction of support facilities, mechanical practices associated with irrigation and water conservation, erosion control, and agricultural data processing systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Czech linguistics and literary studies, addressing critical gaps in large-scale analysis of Czech language evolution, dialect variation, and textual patterns. While Czech philology and literature have rich scholarly traditions, existing studies often rely on manual or small-scale computational methods, limiting the scope of analyses—particularly for historical texts, regional dialects, and understudied 20th-century works. The proposed research will employ NLP techniques and machine learning models to analyze multi-century corpora, including digitized historical manuscripts (14th–19th centuries), modern literary works, and dialectal recordings. Key computational tasks include morphological disambiguation of archaic Czech, semantic shift tracking across sociohistorical contexts, and dialectometric mapping using phonetic and syntactic features. These processes demand HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (15+ TB of text and audio), the complexity of transformer-based models fine-tuned for Czech, and the need for parallelized processing of heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include the first longitudinal quantification of grammatical regularization in Czech, a geotemporal model of Moravian dialect convergence, and an open-access annotated corpus of non-standard Czech texts. By enabling systematic, data-driven inquiry into language-internal variation and literary style, this work will provide novel methodologies for Slavic philology, inform language preservation efforts, and expand digital humanities infrastructure for underrepresented languages. The requested resources directly support computationally intensive workflows that cannot be executed on local hardware, ensuring rigorous analysis of patterns across millions of tokens while maintaining reproducibility. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary collaborations, open-source tools for Czech NLP, and publications bridging computational linguistics and literary theory.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Czech language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Agricultural mechanization faces critical challenges in optimizing equipment performance and operational efficiency under dynamic field conditions, particularly as precision agriculture generates increasingly complex, high-resolution datasets. Current computational models for machinery design and farm management systems struggle to integrate real-time sensor data, environmental variables, and equipment telemetry at scale, limiting their ability to inform adaptive decision-making. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-physics simulation frameworks that couple mechanized operations with agronomic processes. The computational approach will leverage finite element analysis to model soil-tool interactions across diverse soil textures and moisture levels, combined with machine learning algorithms trained on terabyte-scale datasets from IoT-enabled tractors, harvesters, and irrigation systems. Parallelized optimization routines will evaluate energy-efficient equipment configurations under 10,000+ scenario permutations, incorporating regional climate projections and crop growth models. Key deliverables include GPU-accelerated digital twins of mechanized planting and harvesting systems, validated against field trials in major cropping zones. These tools will enable predictive maintenance algorithms and autonomous equipment path planning that reduces fuel consumption by an estimated 15–20%. The research will also establish open-source libraries for agricultural machinery simulation, addressing a critical gap in scalable computational resources for the field. By bridging high-fidelity equipment modeling with farm-scale operational data, this work aims to advance intelligent mechanization systems that enhance productivity while minimizing environmental impacts—a prerequisite for sustainable intensification of global agriculture. Successful implementation requires dedicated HPC nodes with GPU clusters capable of handling 24/7 multi-node simulations, along with petabyte-scale storage for heterogeneous agricultural datasets.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of real-time analysis and optimization of corporate communication networks in large organizations, a critical yet underexplored challenge at the intersection of computational linguistics, behavioral analytics, and organizational strategy. Corporate communications generate vast unstructured datasets—including internal memos, stakeholder emails, press releases, and social media interactions—that require advanced computational methods to evaluate for consistency, sentiment alignment, and crisis response efficacy. Traditional tools lack the capacity to process multimodal data (text, audio, visual) at scale while preserving contextual nuance, leading to inefficiencies in strategic decision-making. The proposed work will develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model communication flows, simulate stakeholder response dynamics, and identify latent risks in real time. Using transformer-based neural architectures fine-tuned on industry-specific corpora, the system will perform semantic coherence checks, sentiment trajectory mapping, and anomaly detection across hierarchical communication layers. Graph convolutional networks will map interdependencies between internal teams and external partners, while reinforcement learning agents will stress-test proposed messaging strategies against simulated crisis scenarios. The computational pipeline will leverage distributed GPU clusters for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, enabling subsecond latency in critical-path analyses. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying communication network resilience, automated tools for preemptive reputation risk mitigation, and generative models to optimize cross-departmental content alignment. This work bridges a gap in applied business communication research by providing empirically grounded, computation-driven methods to enhance organizational agility in high-stakes environments. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive workloads in training domain-specific large language models and running millions of stochastic simulations for scenario validation. Results will be validated against historical corporate crisis datasets and peer-reviewed via partnerships with communications analytics firms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: This project investigates the psychological dynamics of trust formation in human-AI collaborative decision-making, a nascent area at the intersection of cognitive science, computational modeling, and ethics. As AI systems increasingly mediate high-stakes domains like healthcare and finance, understanding how users calibrate trust—particularly in contexts where AI recommendations conflict with human intuition—is critical. Current frameworks lack granularity in modeling the cognitive and emotional factors driving trust adaptation over time. To address this gap, we propose a dual-method approach combining behavioral experiments with large-scale computational simulations. Participants will engage in a series of iterative decision-making tasks with AI partners of varying reliability, with multimodal data collection (eye tracking, galvanic skin response, and behavioral logs) capturing real-time trust modulation. These empirical data will inform the development of neural network models simulating trust adaptation mechanisms under different uncertainty conditions. The computational component requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train recurrent neural networks on longitudinal interaction patterns and to run parallelized agent-based simulations exploring emergent trust dynamics in population-scale human-AI systems. Key challenges include modeling the nonlinear integration of affective states and rational risk assessment in trust decisions, as well as simulating rare but consequential trust breakdown scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework predicting trust trajectories across human-AI interaction types, identification of critical intervention points for maintaining appropriate trust calibration, and evidence-based design principles for AI transparency features. This work will establish foundational insights into the psychology of human-machine trust while advancing methodology for studying complex cognitive processes through tightly coupled empirical-computational research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the 15TB of experimental data, executing computationally intensive trust model simulations (>10,000 agent permutations), and achieving the temporal resolution required to capture micro-level trust adjustments in simulated decision cycles.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of linguistic and stylistic patterns in understudied Classical Greek and Latin texts. A central challenge in classical philology is the limited systematic analysis of textual features across fragmented or rarely examined works, such as late-antique technical treatises or fragmentary inscriptions, which often lack comprehensive literary histories. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to identify subtle linguistic continuities, intertextual borrowings, or authorship markers at scale, particularly in corpora spanning multiple centuries and genres. To address this, the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for ancient languages, including tokenization adapted for scriptio continua, morphological tagging using neural transformer models pretrained on curated classical corpora, and semantic network analysis. These methods will be deployed to trace lexical innovations, syntactic preferences, and metrical anomalies across a curated dataset of 10,000+ texts from the Packard Humanities Institute and Duke Databank of Documentary Papyri. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models, running parallelized comparative analyses across heterogeneous textual subsets, and visualizing high-dimensional stylistic data through dimensionality reduction techniques. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized stylistic clusters in post-classical Latin technical writings, a quantitative reevaluation of authorship debates surrounding pseudepigraphical works in the Greek rhetorical tradition, and an open-access toolkit for computational stylometry in ancient languages. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project aims to enhance scholarly understanding of linguistic evolution and cultural transmission in antiquity while establishing scalable methodologies for interdisciplinary humanities research.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the literary culture of the ancient Graeco-Roman world and the Greek and Latin languages and literatures and their development prior to the fall of the Roman Empire.

abstract: Reproductive health in animals is critical for sustainable agriculture, species conservation, and translational insights into human medicine. Despite advances in theriogenology, persistent challenges remain in understanding the multifactorial causes of infertility, pregnancy loss, and neonatal mortality across species. These conditions often arise from complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors that are difficult to disentangle using conventional experimental approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of reproductive pathophysiology, enabling targeted interventions. The research will integrate multi-omics datasets (genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiles from maternal, fetal, and neonatal samples) with clinical records from bovine, equine, and canine cohorts to identify biomarkers of reproductive dysfunction. Machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and graph neural networks, will be trained to classify risk factors for gestational complications and predict therapeutic responses. Agent-based modeling will simulate intrauterine microenvironments during critical developmental windows, exploring how hypoxia, nutrient gradients, and inflammatory signals influence fetal viability. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further analyze placental blood flow patterns associated with preterm birth. These models require large-scale parallel processing due to the high dimensionality of omics data, stochasticity in microenvironment interactions, and the need for parameter sensitivity analyses across species-specific physiologies. By unifying these approaches, the project aims to uncover conserved pathways in reproductive failure, propose biomarkers for early diagnosis, and optimize treatment protocols for at-risk animals. The outcomes will advance precision theriogenology, reduce economic losses in livestock industries, and inform comparative studies of human obstetric challenges. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the computational burden of iterative model training, multi-scale simulations, and data integration across terabytes of heterogeneous biological datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of diseases and health problems affecting the reproductive systems of animals, and the comprehensive care and treatment of parent animals, animal fetuses and newborn or newly hatched animals throughout the gestation period.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolving legal and administrative frameworks governing transnational religious institutions through computational analysis of multi-jurisdictional regulatory documents and case law. As religious organizations increasingly operate across national boundaries, they face complex legal challenges arising from conflicting secular laws, digital governance requirements, and shifting cultural norms. Traditional legal scholarship struggles to systematically analyze the scale and complexity of these interactions, particularly across languages and jurisdictions. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques on a corpus of 250,000+ legal documents (including court decisions, institutional policies, and legislative texts from 15 countries) to model patterns in legal conflicts, regulatory compliance strategies, and administrative decision-making processes. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on multilingual legal texts, conducting network analysis of citation patterns between judicial systems, and simulating the cascading effects of policy changes through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of recurring conflict domains in cross-border religious administration; 2) development of predictive models for legal risk assessment in institutional operations; and 3) creation of an open-access visualization platform mapping relationships between religious governance structures and secular legal systems. This computational approach advances humanistic scholarship by revealing hidden systemic interactions in religious institutional law while providing practical tools for faith-based organizations navigating complex regulatory environments. The research bridges computational legal studies, digital humanities, and organizational theory within an understudied domain of religious institutional practice.
cip_title: Religious Institution Administration and Law, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious institution administration and law, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the predictive accuracy of high-impact weather events in a changing climate by advancing the resolution and physical fidelity of regional atmospheric simulations. Current numerical weather prediction (NWP) models struggle to resolve mesoscale processes—such as convective initiation, cloud microphysics, and boundary layer interactions—that drive extreme precipitation, heatwaves, and severe storms. These limitations hinder reliable forecasts of localized extreme events, which are projected to increase in frequency and intensity under climate change. To address this, we propose a multi-scale modeling framework leveraging the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model, configured with 1-km horizontal resolution over North American hotspot regions, nested within a global climate model. The simulations will integrate novel stochastic parameterizations for subgrid-scale convection and aerosol-cloud interactions, calibrated using observational datasets from radar, satellites, and atmospheric profilers. Ensemble-based data assimilation techniques will be employed to reduce initialization uncertainties. The computational demands are substantial: each 72-hour forecast ensemble (50 members) requires ~8,000 CPU-hours, with planned multi-year climate scenario runs (RCP 4.5 and 8.5) necessitating petascale storage for output analysis. The project will utilize high-performance computing resources to parallelize model components, optimize I/O workflows, and perform Monte Carlo sensitivity experiments on parameterization schemes. Anticipated outcomes include improved understanding of scale-aware precipitation processes, quantifiable reductions in forecast spread for extreme events, and publicly accessible datasets to inform regional climate adaptation strategies. By bridging the gap between climate projections and operational forecasting scales, this work aims to provide actionable insights for mitigating weather-related risks in vulnerable communities. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the spatial granularity and ensemble sizes required for statistically robust conclusions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the prediction of atmospheric motion and climate change. Includes instruction in general circulation patterns, weather phenomena, atmospheric predictability, parameterization, numerical and statistical analysis, large- and mesoscale phenomena, kinematic structures, precipitation processes, and forecasting techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and linguistic identities across the Balkan Peninsula from the late medieval period to the early 20th century. The research addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary scholarship: the lack of systematic, large-scale computational analysis of vernacular texts, oral histories, and material culture artifacts that reflect the region’s pluralistic heritage. By integrating digitized manuscripts, ethnographic recordings, and archival records from diverse Balkan communities, the study aims to trace patterns of cultural hybridity, language contact, and identity negotiation in contexts shaped by shifting political and religious boundaries. The computational approach employs natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for historical South Slavic dialects and non-Slavic languages (e.g., Albanian, Vlach), alongside network analysis to map cross-regional transmission of narratives and symbols. A key innovation involves training custom transformer models to detect semantic shifts in religious and ethnic terminology within Ottoman tax registers, liturgical texts, and folkloric corpora. Image processing workflows will also be applied to analyze stylistic variations in ecclesiastical art and domestic material culture, correlating visual motifs with textual evidence of communal self-representation. The scale of data—over 10 million text tokens and 50,000 high-resolution artifact images—necessitates parallelized computing for dimensionality reduction, temporal-spatial modeling, and interactive visualization of results. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of Balkan cultural interfaces, methodological frameworks for computationally tracing identity formation in multi-ethnic regions, and new datasets challenging nationalist historiographies that dominate the field. By enabling granular analysis of understudied vernacular sources, this project will advance transdisciplinary dialogue in Balkan Studies while demonstrating how HPC can reshape research on cultural memory in contested borderlands.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the Balkan Peninsula and associated island groups and borderlands, Southern Slavic and non-Slavic, during the medieval, Ottoman, and modern periods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of personalized nutrition, food systems optimization, and behavioral health analytics—a niche within Foods, Nutrition, and Wellness Studies that integrates computational modeling with human-centered health outcomes. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic, individualized dietary patterns interact with socioeconomic, cultural, and physiological variables to influence long-term wellness. Traditional nutrition studies often rely on static dietary assessments or small-sample trials, limiting their ability to model complex, nonlinear relationships between food intake, metabolic responses, and lifestyle factors at scale. To overcome this, we propose developing a machine learning framework to analyze multi-modal datasets, including longitudinal dietary logs, biometric sensor data, regional food supply chain metrics, and psychosocial surveys. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional time-series data, training ensemble models to predict nutrient absorption variability across demographic subgroups, and simulating the public health impacts of culturally tailored dietary interventions under diverse socioeconomic scenarios. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter optimization for neural networks, parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of intervention efficacy, and real-time integration of heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive toolkit for personalized meal planning that accounts for user-specific constraints (e.g., budget, food accessibility), (2) evidence-based models linking localized food production practices to community health disparities, and (3) novel metrics for evaluating nutrition interventions across temporal and biological scales. By bridging computational scalability with human-factors complexity, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven wellness policy while advancing methodological innovation in non-traditional HPC applications. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, storage of petabyte-scale nutritional databases, and collaborative visualization of multidimensional wellness landscapes.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Wellness Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the role of foods and nutrition in human health and wellness. Includes instruction in nutritional care and education, the planning and provision of food services, the development of consumable food products, life-span nutrition and wellness, the principles of nutritional assessment, and food safety and food composition.

abstract: The proliferation of health-related misinformation in digital ecosystems presents a critical socio-technical challenge, undermining public trust and effective health communication. This project addresses the dynamics of misinformation propagation within decentralized, community-driven platforms (e.g., niche forums, encrypted messaging networks), where conventional content moderation tools are limited. We propose a computational framework to model how emergent narratives gain traction through the interplay of user behavior, platform affordances, and network topology, with a focus on understudied communities that exhibit distinct information-sharing norms. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the research will integrate three methodological components: (1) agent-based simulations capturing heterogeneous user decision-making when encountering contested health information, calibrated through ethnographic interviews; (2) temporal network analysis of cross-platform information diffusion patterns using anonymized interaction metadata; and (3) multimodal NLP pipelines to detect latent persuasive strategies in text, image, and audio-based misinformation. The scale of required simulations—simultaneously modeling 10^6+ agents across dynamically evolving network structures—necessitates parallelized computation and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model of context-sensitive misinformation spread and an adaptive classification system that accounts for community-specific epistemic values. Results will inform the design of targeted counter-messaging systems that preserve informational autonomy while mitigating harm, advancing theoretical understanding of trust formation in fragmented digital spaces. This work bridges information science, computational social science, and public health, offering novel methods to study socio-technical systems where centralized governance models prove inadequate.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, organization, and process of information collection, transmission, and utilization in traditional and electronic forms. Includes instruction in information classification and organization; information storage and processing; transmission, transfer, and signaling; communications and networking; systems planning and design; human interfacing and use analysis; database development; information policy analysis; and related aspects of hardware, software, economics, social factors, and capacity.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision medicine in pediatric critical care by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, multifactorial determinants of treatment response in acutely ill children. Despite standardized protocols, outcomes for conditions such as sepsis, traumatic brain injury, and acute respiratory failure remain highly variable across pediatric populations, partly due to poorly characterized interactions between developmental biology, genomic factors, and dynamic clinical parameters. Current analytic approaches lack the capacity to integrate high-dimensional data—including time-resolved electronic health records, multi-omics profiles, and multimodal imaging—while accounting for developmental stage-specific pathophysiology. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that combines mechanistic models of organ system maturation with machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous clinical datasets. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of ensemble models to predict individualized therapeutic trajectories, simulate in silico treatment perturbations, and identify critical windows for intervention. Key steps include (1) harmonizing retrospective data from 15,000+ pediatric ICU encounters, (2) implementing federated learning architectures to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions, and (3) optimizing neural differential equation models to capture time-dependent biological processes. Validation will focus on predicting hemodynamic response to fluid resuscitation in septic shock, a scenario where suboptimal decisions disproportionately affect neurodevelopmental outcomes. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for adaptive clinical decision support, directly addressing the National Institutes of Health’s priority to reduce life-course morbidity through computationally driven pediatric research. By elucidating developmental modifiers of treatment efficacy, this work aims to establish a paradigm for dynamically personalized critical care while demonstrating how HPC can overcome longstanding barriers in translating population-level evidence to individual patients.
cip_definition: Research focused on the comprehensive care and treatment of all aspects of human growth and development from conception through fetal life, infancy, childhood and adolescence, including preventive and therapeutic regimes. May included related research in behavioral aspects of illness, related family and community medicine issues, and emergency and critical care procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational modeling of sustainable textile dyeing processes, an underexplored niche at the intersection of textile science, environmental chemistry, and computational fluid dynamics. Traditional dyeing methods are resource-intensive, relying on trial-and-error approaches that consume significant water, energy, and chemicals. However, the molecular interactions between synthetic dyes and natural fibers—particularly under varying thermal, mechanical, and pH conditions—remain poorly understood, limiting the development of optimized, eco-friendly protocols. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations, reactive force field (ReaxFF) modeling, and machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization. CGMD will simulate the diffusion and binding of dye molecules across fiber surfaces at mesoscopic scales, while ReaxFF will model bond-breaking and reformation dynamics during dye-fiber attachment. Concurrently, ML algorithms will iteratively refine simulation parameters using experimental datasets spanning cotton, silk, and hemp fibers with 12 common dye classes. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space (e.g., temperature gradients, shear forces, solvent polarity) and the computationally intensive reactive simulations across 10^6+ atomic-scale timesteps. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dye uptake efficiency, colorfastness, and wastewater chemical load, validated against laboratory dyeing trials. This work will establish the first open-access computational toolkit for sustainable textile dyeing, directly addressing industry needs to reduce water consumption by 30–50% in commercial processes. By integrating computational chemistry with textile science, the project bridges a critical gap in non-engineering domains, offering a template for HPC-driven innovation in niche applied material sciences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and processing of fibers, yarns, whole fabrics, dyes, and finishes, both natural and synthetic. Includes instruction in the chemical and physical properties of textile materials; end-use analysis; interior furnishing applications; and industrial applications.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of real-time media production and distribution in the digital age by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Traditional methods for optimizing broadcast workflows and audience engagement analysis are increasingly inadequate due to the volume and velocity of multimedia data generated by streaming platforms, social media, and interactive content. The research will employ parallelized machine learning algorithms to analyze viewer interaction patterns and content performance metrics across heterogeneous datasets, including high-resolution video streams, real-time engagement logs, and multi-platform metadata. Computational modeling will simulate large-scale distribution networks to evaluate bandwidth allocation, latency minimization, and adaptive bitrate streaming under varying global demand scenarios. Additionally, GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines will be developed to prototype virtual production environments, enabling real-time synthesis of complex visual effects for live broadcasts. Anticipated outcomes include scalable frameworks for dynamic content personalization, data-driven strategies for cross-platform media scheduling, and enhanced tools for immersive storytelling in television production. By integrating computational scalability with media-specific challenges, this work aims to advance the technical capabilities of next-generation broadcast systems while informing pedagogical approaches in modern radio and television education. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale media datasets, training AI models for predictive analytics, and rendering high-fidelity virtual environments, tasks infeasible with standard computing infrastructure. This research bridges gaps between media theory and computational practice, offering actionable insights for industry professionals and academic curricula alike.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, methods, and techniques used to plan, produce, and distribute audio and video programs and messages, and that prepares individuals to function as staff, producers, directors, and managers of radio and television shows and media organizations. Includes instruction in media aesthetics; planning, scheduling, and production; writing and editing; performing and directing; personnel and facilities management; marketing and distribution; media regulations, law, and policy; and principles of broadcast technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying acupuncture needle manipulation, a core component of traditional East Asian medicine. Despite clinical evidence supporting acupuncture’s efficacy in pain modulation and tissue repair, the biophysical interactions between needle manipulation techniques (e.g., lifting-thrusting, twisting) and connective tissue microstructure remain poorly characterized. Current experimental models face limitations in resolving real-time, microscale tissue deformation and mechanotransduction signaling cascades triggered by mechanical stimuli. To address this gap, we propose multiscale computational simulations integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of needle-tissue interactions with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of force-induced cellular responses. HPC resources will enable high-resolution modeling of collagen fiber networks under dynamic mechanical loading, paired with atomistic simulations of integrin activation and downstream signaling pathways (e.g., FAK/PI3K) linked to therapeutic effects. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated datasets to identify optimal needle manipulation parameters (depth, frequency, torque) for maximizing mechanobiological responses in specific tissue types. This computational framework will be validated against in vitro measurements from collagen hydrogels and fibroblast cultures subjected to controlled needle stimuli. Outcomes will yield the first predictive model linking manual acupuncture techniques to quantifiable cellular responses, advancing the rational design of precision needling protocols. By bridging traditional practice with computational biophysics, this work aims to establish mechanistic benchmarks for acupuncture research while providing a template for integrating HPC-driven approaches into the study of complex manual therapies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of acupuncture, a Chinese system of health care and healing based on the use of pulse diagnosis, acupuncture point selection, and needle insertion, as well as herbs and other Asian treatment modalities. Includes instruction in basic Western medical sciences, Asian philosophy, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbs, diagnostic techniques, patient observation and communication, acupuncture points and point selection, acupuncture techniques, acupuncture treatment of disease, pain management, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in sustainable apparel production by developing a computational framework to optimize textile material innovation and personalized design processes. Traditional methods for textile development rely on iterative physical prototyping, which is resource-intensive, time-consuming, and environmentally detrimental. This project aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale interactions between novel biodegradable materials, advanced manufacturing techniques, and biomechanical consumer data. By integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural behavior prediction, molecular dynamics simulations for polymer degradation modeling, and machine learning algorithms trained on anthropometric datasets, the framework will enable virtual prototyping of textiles that balance durability, comfort, and environmental impact. The computational pipeline will also incorporate lifecycle assessment models to quantify carbon footprints and water usage across design iterations. Key outcomes include the generation of predictive tools for rapid material screening, the identification of optimal hybrid fibers for circular fashion systems, and data-driven guidelines for adaptive garment designs tailored to diverse body types and mobility needs. The HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space of material compositions, weave structures, and dynamic stress scenarios, which require parallelized simulations and large-scale optimization. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between computational engineering, sustainable chemistry, and consumer-centric design, offering a transformative methodology for reducing waste in the apparel industry while advancing scalable customization. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-source modules to support industry adoption and academic collaboration in ethical textile innovation.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the development of textile products and their distribution and use in terms of the psychological, social, economic, and physical needs of consumers. Includes instruction in the production, distribution, marketing, and end use of various apparel and textile products.

abstract: Pediatric clinical research faces critical challenges in understanding complex, multifactorial diseases due to the dynamic interplay of developmental biology, environmental factors, and heterogeneous patient responses. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches for pediatric sepsis, a leading cause of mortality in critically ill children. Current risk stratification and treatment protocols lack personalization, contributing to variable outcomes. We propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic), electronic health records, and longitudinal immune profiling from a multicenter cohort of 2,500 pediatric sepsis patients. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression, organ dysfunction, and therapeutic response. Bayesian hierarchical modeling will account for developmental age-specific variations in immune and metabolic pathways, while mechanistic simulations of host-pathogen interactions will explore causal drivers of clinical heterogeneity. The scale of data (≈150 TB) and complexity of models necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized data processing, distributed hyperparameter optimization, and large-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated risk stratification tool for early identification of high-risk patients, (2) computational biomarkers to guide immunomodulatory therapy selection, and (3) open-source pipelines for pediatric multi-omics integration. By enabling rapid analysis of developmental trajectories and rare patient subgroups, this HPC-driven approach will address fundamental gaps in understanding sepsis pathophysiology across maturing biological systems. Results will be disseminated through clinician-facing decision support tools and a public cloud repository for pediatric sepsis datasets, fostering translational applications in critical care.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Medicine

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-modal datasets in chemical pathology—spanning high-throughput metabolomic profiles, longitudinal patient biochemical data, and instrument-generated analytical outputs—presents a critical computational challenge. Current infrastructure struggles to integrate these heterogeneous datasets efficiently, limiting the development of predictive models for disease stratification and personalized treatment. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable advanced computational workflows for large-scale data integration, machine learning-driven biomarker discovery, and real-time simulation of metabolic pathways. The research focuses on three aims: (1) developing scalable algorithms to harmonize multi-omic data (genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) with clinical laboratory results, (2) training deep neural networks to predict adverse drug reactions and metabolic disorders using historical chemical pathology datasets, and (3) simulating enzyme kinetics and drug-metabolite interactions via parallelized molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The HPC environment is essential for managing terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters in complex neural architectures, and executing energy calculations for MD simulations across thousands of CPU cores. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for early detection of renal dysfunction and inborn errors of metabolism, as well as optimized protocols for clinical mass spectrometry data processing. By leveraging distributed computing frameworks, this work will establish a pipeline to reduce turnaround times for complex biochemical analyses by 40-60%, directly enhancing laboratory operational efficiency. The resource allocation will also support open-source tool development for reproducible analysis of chemical pathology data, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational domains. This project bridges critical gaps in data-driven chemical pathology, with implications for precision diagnostics, therapeutic monitoring, and cost-effective laboratory management.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use and interpretation of chemical analyses, chemical diagnoses and management, and the supervision of chemical pathology laboratories. May included related research in basic and applied analytical chemical pathology; instrumentation data processing and chemical laboratory management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in legal document analysis and precedent retrieval, a critical challenge in legal support services. The increasing volume of unstructured legal texts—including court opinions, briefs, and regulatory filings—has made manual review and synthesis impractical, leading to delays and inconsistencies in legal research. Traditional keyword-based search tools lack the capacity to identify nuanced patterns or contextual relationships within legal language, underscoring the need for advanced computational methods. This research proposes the development of a machine learning (ML) framework tailored to automate the extraction of legal concepts, predict case outcomes, and map citation networks across jurisdictions. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to analyze text corpora spanning millions of legal documents. Computational workflows will integrate distributed training of deep learning models, graph analytics for precedent linkage, and optical character recognition (OCR) for digitized historical records. HPC resources are essential to manage the scale of data (multi-terabyte datasets), optimize hyperparameter tuning for domain-specific language models, and parallelize tasks such as entity recognition and semantic similarity scoring. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for legal professionals to rapidly identify relevant case law, visualize argumentative trends, and assess litigation risks. By bridging computational scalability with legal domain expertise, this work aims to establish a foundation for next-generation legal support systems, reducing research costs and improving access to justice. The interdisciplinary nature of this effort—situated at the intersection of computational law, data science, and legal practice—occupies a specialized niche not addressed by existing research categories, advancing both technical methodologies and their practical application within legal services.
cip_definition: Any program in legal support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of neuroimaging data in neuroradiology—including high-resolution MRI, diffusion tensor imaging, and functional MRI—demands advanced computational methods to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic planning for neurological disorders. Current clinical workflows struggle to efficiently integrate multi-modal imaging data, quantify subtle pathological features, and predict disease progression, particularly in conditions like gliomas, multiple sclerosis, and neurodegenerative diseases. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a machine learning framework optimized for automated lesion segmentation, biomarker extraction, and predictive modeling using large-scale neuroimaging datasets. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and validate 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph-based models on multi-institutional datasets comprising over 10,000 annotated brain and spine studies. Computational workflows will include preprocessing pipelines for artifact correction, spatial normalization, and feature fusion across imaging modalities (e.g., T1-weighted, FLAIR, and perfusion MRI). HPC capabilities are critical for managing memory-intensive volumetric data, parallelizing hyperparameter optimization, and enabling rapid inference for clinical translation. Expected outcomes include (1) robust algorithms for detecting early-stage white matter lesions and tumor infiltration boundaries with submillimeter precision, (2) prognostic models linking imaging biomarkers to patient-specific outcomes, and (3) open-source tools for quantitative neuroradiology designed for integration into clinical PACS systems. By harnessing HPC resources, this project aims to reduce diagnostic variability, accelerate interpretation timelines, and establish computational standards for precision neuroradiology. The resulting frameworks will be validated against histopathological and longitudinal clinical data, with potential to redefine imaging-based decision-making in acute stroke, neuro-oncology, and pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the brain, spine, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, and head and neck in adults and children.

abstract: Clinical research trials generate vast, heterogeneous datasets from electronic medical records, wearable devices, genomic sequencing, and imaging, presenting significant challenges in integration, analysis, and regulatory compliance. Traditional computing methods struggle to efficiently process these data at scale, leading to delays in identifying adverse events, optimizing trial protocols, and validating outcomes. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for real-time, large-scale clinical trial data management and predictive analytics. The research will focus on three aims: (1) implementing parallelized pipelines to harmonize multi-modal data (clinical, omics, sensor-based) using distributed storage and Apache Spark; (2) training machine learning models to predict patient-specific intervention responses and safety risks through GPU-accelerated deep learning (TensorFlow/PyTorch); and (3) simulating trial design adjustments via agent-based modeling to minimize recruitment biases and protocol deviations. The HPC environment will enable rapid processing of terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining HIPAA/GCP compliance through encrypted workflows and audit trails. Expected outcomes include a validated platform for dynamic risk monitoring, automated FDA reporting templates, and optimized patient stratification algorithms. This work addresses critical gaps in clinical research coordination by providing coordinators with tools to manage complex trials efficiently, reduce manual errors, and improve protocol adherence. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a scalable model for multi-site trials, directly enhancing training in data-intensive clinical research methodologies. By integrating HPC capabilities with regulatory workflows, this project aims to accelerate translational discoveries while maintaining rigorous ethical and compliance standards essential for modern clinical research operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers as clinical research administrators or clinical research coordinators where they work under the supervision of a Principal Investigator to organize, coordinate and administer clinical research trials. Includes instruction in pharmacology, medical terminology, foundations of clinical research, project management, ethics, research design and data management, and legal and regulatory compliance .

abstract: The increasing complexity of electronic health records (EHRs) presents challenges in efficiently extracting clinically actionable insights from unstructured data, such as provider notes, imaging reports, and patient-generated text. Current natural language processing (NLP) methods for clinical text often underperform due to the contextual ambiguity of medical terminology, sparse documentation patterns, and privacy constraints limiting large-scale model training. This project proposes the development of a federated learning framework augmented with high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models capable of synthesizing structured and unstructured EHR data while preserving data security. The research will focus on creating a transformer-based architecture optimized for distributed clinical datasets, integrating temporal event sequences from structured records with semantic features from free-text narratives. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated clusters to pretrain language models on de-identified clinical corpora, followed by federated fine-tuning across participating healthcare institutions without raw data exchange. Key technical challenges include optimizing memory efficiency for long-sequence clinical narratives, developing differential privacy mechanisms for model weight aggregation, and validating cross-site generalizability using adversarial validation techniques. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for privacy-preserving clinical NLP, validated against benchmark tasks such as 30-day readmission prediction and incidental finding detection in radiology reports. Successful implementation could enable smaller healthcare organizations to contribute to and benefit from collective model improvement without compromising patient confidentiality. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the distributed training workloads, conducting large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and simulating federated learning environments with synthetic clinical datasets prior to real-world deployment. This work bridges gaps in health informatics by addressing both technical scalability and ethical data stewardship in next-generation medical record analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the hydrodynamic and structural performance of next-generation marine vessels operating in extreme oceanic conditions. The research addresses a critical gap in current naval architecture practices, which often rely on decoupled simulations for fluid-structure interactions (FSI), leading to inaccuracies in predicting dynamic loads and fatigue behavior for hulls subjected to nonlinear wave impacts, slamming events, and cavitation-induced vibrations. By leveraging tightly coupled multiphysics modeling, we aim to resolve bidirectional feedback between turbulent flow fields, transient structural deformations, and material responses at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational approach integrates adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) for large-eddy simulation (LES) of wave-structure interactions with parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) for anisotropic composite hull materials. Machine learning techniques will be embedded to accelerate topology optimization of hull geometries that balance hydrodynamic efficiency with damage tolerance under cyclic loading. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the exascale datasets generated by three-dimensional transient simulations across relevant timescales, from microsecond pressure pulses during cavitation collapse to multi-hour operational profiles. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for lifetime performance degradation in novel hull forms, a publicly accessible database of FSI benchmarks for marine applications, and AI-driven design guidelines that reduce fuel consumption while enhancing structural reliability. This work directly supports the development of energy-efficient vessels capable of maintaining mission-critical operations in increasingly volatile maritime environments, with potential applications ranging from autonomous underwater vehicles to offshore renewable energy infrastructure. The computational toolkit developed will be shared with the marine engineering community through open-source plugins for established naval architecture software platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of self-propelled, stationary, or towed vessels operating on or under the water, including inland, coastal and ocean environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as corrosion, power transfer, pressure, hull efficiency, stress factors, safety and life support, environmental hazards and factors, and specific use requirements.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of linguistic and stylistic patterns in Classical Latin and Ancient Greek literary corpora. A central challenge in the field is the systematic identification of diachronic and synchronic variations across vast textual datasets, which span multiple centuries and genres. Traditional manual methods are insufficient for detecting subtle, large-scale trends in syntax, meter, or vocabulary that may illuminate historical shifts in literary practices, cultural exchange, or authorial attribution. To address this, the project will develop and apply scalable natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for ancient languages, including morphological tagging, syntactic dependency parsing, and semantic vector modeling. These pipelines will process digitized texts from repositories such as the Perseus Digital Library and the Corpus Corporum, encompassing over 50,000 documents. HPC resources will enable parallelized computation of metrical analyses for Greek poetic forms, Bayesian statistical modeling of lexical changes in Latin prose, and neural network-based authorship attribution for disputed works. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized stylistic continuities between Hellenistic and Late Antique literature, refined chronologies for undated texts, and open-access tools for computational philology. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to deepen understanding of ancient literary evolution while establishing reproducible methods for interdisciplinary scholarship in the digital humanities.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the literary culture of the ancient Graeco-Roman world and the Greek and Latin languages and literatures and their development prior to the fall of the Roman Empire.

abstract: Epilepsy is a complex neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, affecting over 50 million individuals globally. Despite advances in diagnostic tools and therapies, approximately 30% of patients remain drug-resistant, and the underlying mechanisms of seizure generation and propagation remain poorly understood. Current clinical methods, such as electroencephalography (EEG) and neuroimaging, generate high-dimensional data that are challenging to analyze comprehensively using conventional computational resources. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models for improving the diagnosis, classification, and personalized treatment of epilepsy. The research will focus on integrating multimodal neuroimaging, electrophysiological data, and genetic information to identify biomarkers of epileptogenesis, predict treatment responses, and simulate seizure dynamics. A key component involves machine learning algorithms to detect subtle patterns in long-term EEG recordings and structural MRI data that correlate with seizure onset zones and network abnormalities. Additionally, we will employ computational neuroscience techniques to model large-scale neural networks, simulating how genetic mutations or structural lesions alter network excitability and synchronization. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and transcriptomic analyses will be conducted to explore genetic risk factors and their interactions with neuroimaging phenotypes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the scale and complexity of these datasets, enabling parallel processing of terabytes of neuroimaging data, real-time analysis of continuous EEG streams, and iterative optimization of predictive models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, stratification of patients into subphenotypes based on computational profiles, and in silico testing of antiepileptic drug effects on simulated neural networks. This work has the potential to transform clinical practice by providing tools for precision medicine in epilepsy, reducing diagnostic delays, and guiding targeted therapeutic interventions. By elucidating the multiscale mechanisms of epileptogenesis, the project will contribute to foundational knowledge that informs future research and therapeutic innovation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of patients with epileptic seizures or with symptoms and signs whose differential diagnosis includes epileptic seizures.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex ophthalmic diseases in companion and livestock animals, such as inherited retinal degeneration, glaucoma, and corneal pathologies, necessitates advanced computational approaches to bridge gaps in mechanistic understanding and therapeutic development. Current limitations in studying these conditions arise from the heterogeneous nature of ocular tissues, interspecies anatomical variability, and the dynamic interplay of molecular pathways driving disease progression. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models of ocular pathophysiology, enabling predictive analyses of disease mechanisms and treatment outcomes. Using clinical datasets from veterinary ophthalmology cases—including high-resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT), electroretinography, and genomic profiles—we will construct species-specific digital twins of ocular structures. These models will integrate finite element simulations of biomechanical stress in glaucoma, machine learning-based pattern recognition for early lesion detection in corneal ulcers, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate candidate drugs targeting retinal apoptosis pathways. The HPC environment is critical for handling large-scale image processing (≥10 TB of OCT data), parallelized genomic variant analysis across 1,000+ patient samples, and real-time optimization of surgical parameters in simulated cataract procedures. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved biomarkers for degenerative retinopathies, predictive algorithms for post-surgical complication risks, and in silico screening of novel neuroprotective compounds. By translating computational insights into clinical workflows, this work aims to advance precision medicine in veterinary ophthalmology, reduce invasive diagnostic procedures, and improve surgical success rates. The generated datasets and open-source computational tools will be shared via a dedicated repository, fostering collaboration across veterinary and human ophthalmic research communities.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders in animals, and related ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in animal eye surgery.

abstract: The increasing complexity of global business environments necessitates advanced methodologies for risk assessment and mitigation. Traditional risk management approaches often struggle to account for the interdependencies among diverse risk factors—such as market volatility, cybersecurity threats, and supply chain disruptions—in real-time. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computational framework for integrated risk analysis. Leveraging parallelized Monte Carlo simulations, the research will model stochastic processes underlying rare but high-impact risk events across multiple domains. Machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be employed to analyze large-scale datasets encompassing financial markets, operational logs, and cyber incident reports. Additionally, optimization algorithms will identify optimal risk mitigation strategies under uncertainty. The computational intensity of these tasks, particularly the need for real-time processing of terabyte-scale datasets and the execution of millions of stochastic scenarios, necessitates access to high-performance computing resources. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for dynamic risk assessment, capable of providing actionable insights with reduced latency compared to existing tools. This research will contribute to the academic understanding of systemic risk interactions and offer practitioners a robust tool for proactive risk management in sectors such as finance, insurance, and critical infrastructure. The proposed framework aims to enhance organizational resilience by enabling data-driven decision-making in complex, rapidly evolving risk landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles of business risk measurement, mitigation, and management. Includes instruction in business analytics, foundations of insurance and risk management, investments, life and health insurance, loss prevention, property and liability insurance risk assessment, risk control, risk financing, and security.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in reconstructing and analyzing ancient trade networks across the Mediterranean and Near East (ca. 2000 BCE–500 CE). Traditional archaeological methods struggle to synthesize vast, fragmented datasets—including textual records, ceramic distributions, isotopic analyses, and maritime archaeology findings—into dynamic models of economic interaction. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of resource exchange, cultural influence, and political dependency that shaped Bronze Age through Late Antique societies. To overcome computational limitations in handling heterogeneous spatial-temporal data at scale, the project will develop machine learning pipelines to classify trade goods from digitized excavation reports, apply network analysis algorithms to map connectivity between sites, and employ agent-based modeling to simulate trade route viability under environmental and socio-political constraints. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution satellite imagery to detect submerged ports or eroded caravan paths, as well as for running Monte Carlo simulations that account for chronological uncertainties in artifact dating. Expected outcomes include an open-access geospatial database of trade nodes and a probabilistic model of interaction spheres linking regions such as Mesopotamia, Anatolia, and the Nile Delta. This computational framework will enable hypothesis testing about the role of trade in state formation and collapse, with implications for understanding cross-cultural exchange mechanisms. By integrating archaeological, philological, and environmental data through scalable analytical tools, the project aims to establish new best practices for digital humanities research in ancient studies while providing reproducible workflows for future interdisciplinary investigations.
cip_title: Classical, Ancient Mediterranean, and Near Eastern Studies and Archaeology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the classical ancient civilizations of the ancient Near East, Europe, and the Mediterranean Sea, such as Athens, Anatolia, Egypt, Greece, Israel, Mesopotamia, North Africa, and Rome. Includes instruction in ancient languages, ancient history, archaeology, anthropology, Greek and Roman mythology, philosophy, and religion.

abstract: Livestock breeding programs require precise genomic tools to enhance traits such as disease resistance, feed efficiency, and productivity, yet current methods are limited by the computational complexity of integrating multi-omics data across large populations. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges by developing a computational framework for analyzing whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic, and metabolomic datasets from dairy cattle. The research will employ machine learning algorithms, including gradient-boosted trees and convolutional neural networks, to identify genetic variants and epigenetic markers associated with mastitis susceptibility and growth rates. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model herd-level genetic trajectories under varying selection pressures and environmental conditions. The scale of data—spanning terabytes of genomic sequences and decades of phenotypic records—necessitates parallelized processing, distributed memory architectures, and GPU-accelerated computations to achieve feasible runtime. Expected outcomes include predictive models for prioritizing breeding candidates, optimized protocols to reduce methane emissions through microbiome-linked traits, and open-source software for genomic selection in agricultural animals. By enabling rapid, large-scale analyses, this work will advance precision livestock breeding, directly contributing to sustainable animal production systems and food security. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current bottlenecks in data integration, ensuring scalable solutions that bridge genetic research and practical agricultural outcomes.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding and husbandry of agricultural animals, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural animal products. Includes instruction in the animal sciences, animal husbandry and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to assess the impacts of climate variability on critical watershed systems, addressing gaps in predicting how dynamic hydrological and ecological interactions influence water security and biodiversity conservation. Current models often lack the spatial resolution or computational capacity to capture nonlinear feedbacks between precipitation shifts, land cover changes, and species habitat viability at regional scales. To overcome these limitations, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled hydrologic-ecological model at unprecedented resolution (1 km² grid cells) across a 50,000 km² study area encompassing threatened montane and lowland ecosystems. The framework integrates satellite-derived land use data, downscaled climate projections (CMIP6), and agent-based simulations of species dispersal under habitat fragmentation. Machine learning algorithms will optimize parameter calibration across heterogeneous terrain, while parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in drought and flood scenarios under varying emission pathways. By simulating 100+ years of daily hydrological fluxes and habitat connectivity metrics, the project will identify tipping points in water availability and ecosystem resilience. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of climate refugia for endemic species, prioritized zones for watershed restoration, and open-access tools for adaptive management. The computational demands—10 TB of input data, iterative ensemble runs, and real-time visualization of multi-dimensional outputs—necessitate HPC infrastructure for memory-intensive workloads and GPU-accelerated model training. Results will directly inform regional conservation planning, providing a scalable template for assessing climate risks to natural resources in data-limited regions. This work advances computational ecology by bridging gap between process-based modeling and decision-relevant conservation analytics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of optimizing personalized rehabilitation protocols for individuals with musculoskeletal impairments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between biomechanical, physiological, and patient-specific factors. Current approaches to designing therapeutic interventions often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for the high variability in patient anatomy, injury mechanisms, or functional recovery trajectories. This project aims to develop a computational framework integrating musculoskeletal modeling, machine learning, and multi-scale simulations to predict patient responses to therapeutic exercise regimens. Using tools such as OpenSim for biomechanical analysis and custom Python-based pipelines for data assimilation, we will simulate neuromuscular activation patterns, joint loading dynamics, and tissue adaptation processes under varying therapeutic conditions. Clinical datasets—including gait analysis, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes—will inform model parameters, while machine learning algorithms will identify predictive features linking intervention parameters to functional outcomes. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational demands of iterative simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts, real-time optimization of intervention variables (e.g., exercise intensity, duration), and sensitivity analyses to quantify uncertainty in model predictions. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomechanical and physiological thresholds that maximize recovery efficiency, the development of adaptive intervention templates for common conditions (e.g., post-stroke gait dysfunction, rotator cuff injuries), and actionable insights into dose-response relationships for therapeutic exercise. This work will advance precision physical therapy by providing clinicians with evidence-based, computationally derived guidelines to tailor rehabilitation strategies, potentially reducing recovery times and improving long-term functional outcomes. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated as open-source resources to support broader research in movement science and rehabilitation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate, examine, diagnose, and alleviate physical functional impairments and limitations caused by injury or disease through the design and implementation of therapeutic interventions to promote fitness and health. Includes instruction in anatomy, behavioral sciences, biology, biomechanics, biophysical agents, care plan development and documentation, cellular histology, clinical evaluation and measurement, clinical reasoning, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, professional standards and ethics, rehabilitation psychology, and therapeutic exercise.

abstract: Dermatopathology research faces growing challenges in integrating multi-modal data—such as histopathological imaging, genomic profiles, and clinical metadata—to resolve complex diagnostic ambiguities and uncover molecular drivers of skin diseases. Current approaches often lack the computational capacity to process high-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs) alongside multi-omics datasets at scale, limiting the discovery of biomarkers and mechanisms underlying conditions like cutaneous lymphoma, autoimmune blistering disorders, and melanoma progression. This project proposes the development of a machine learning framework to unify these heterogeneous data types, enabling predictive models for disease classification and therapeutic response. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep neural networks on terabytes of WSIs, perform genome-wide association studies, and conduct spatial transcriptomic analyses within feasible timeframes. Computational workflows will include patch-based convolutional neural networks for feature extraction from WSIs, graph-based architectures to model cellular interactions in tumor microenvironments, and federated learning techniques to preserve patient privacy across collaborating institutions. Parallelized pipelines will be optimized for GPU clusters to accelerate hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. Expected outcomes include (1) novel algorithms for detecting subtle histologic patterns predictive of disease subtypes, (2) integrated multi-omics signatures linking genetic variants to inflammatory skin pathology, and (3) open-source tools for scalable digital pathology analysis. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance precision diagnostics, reduce inter-observer variability in microscopic interpretation, and identify candidate targets for personalized therapies. The resource allocation will directly support translational goals in dermatopathology, enhancing both clinical decision-making and foundational understanding of cutaneous disease mechanisms.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical and microscopic diagnosis and analysis of skin diseases and disorders. May included related research in laboratory administration and the supervision and training of support personnel.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance in-flight safety and emergency response protocols for airline flight attendants through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Current training programs and safety assessments rely heavily on static scenarios and manual evaluations, which may not account for the dynamic, high-stakes variables present during real-world emergencies such as rapid decompression, onboard fires, or medical crises.
