By integrating plasma physics simulations with astrodynamics models at unprecedented scale, this work aims to reduce computational overhead for real-time trajectory replanning by 40-60% compared to conventional methods while identifying novel resonant orbital transitions for lunar gateway station-keeping. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the generation of open-source tools for the astronautical community, with applications to upcoming NASA Artemis-era missions and commercial space logistics networks. Results will advance the foundational understanding of multi-physics coupling in spacecraft systems while demonstrating scalable co-design methodologies for propulsion and guidance subsystems.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and operational evaluation of aircraft and space vehicles. Includes instruction in control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: This project seeks to advance data-driven approaches to curriculum design by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the relationships between instructional material sequencing, learner engagement, and educational outcomes. A critical challenge in curriculum and instruction research is the lack of scalable methods to analyze complex, multidimensional interactions within learning ecosystems—such as how variations in content order, multimedia integration, and assessment timing collectively influence student mastery. Traditional experimental designs struggle to account for these nonlinear dynamics, particularly across diverse learner populations. To address this gap, we propose developing computational models that simulate curriculum efficacy under varying design parameters. The project will employ machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks and agent-based modeling, trained on anonymized longitudinal datasets from digital learning platforms (e.g., student interaction logs, formative assessment results, and content metadata). HPC resources are essential for processing these terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters across thousands of parallel simulations, and conducting sensitivity analyses to identify robust curricular patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for predicting how specific curricular adjustments affect learning trajectories, (2) evidence-based guidelines for dynamically adapting instructional materials to mitigate skill gaps, and (3) open-source tools to help educators visualize trade-offs in curriculum planning scenarios. By enabling large-scale, granular analysis of instructional design choices, this work aims to bridge the gap between curriculum theory and practical implementation, particularly in STEM education contexts where hierarchical skill dependencies are pronounced. The findings will contribute to the emerging field of computational curriculum analytics, offering a replicable methodology for optimizing educational resources in alignment with heterogeneous learner needs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the curriculum and related instructional processes and tools, and that may prepare individuals to serve as professional curriculum specialists. Includes instruction in curriculum theory, curriculum design and planning, instructional material design and evaluation, curriculum evaluation, and applications to specific subject matter, programs or educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize prosthetic and cosmetic material integration for clinical and security applications, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in realism, durability, and environmental adaptability. Traditional prosthetic design relies heavily on manual trial-and-error processes, which limit scalability and precision in addressing diverse anatomical and environmental variables. This research focuses on creating predictive models to simulate the interaction between synthetic materials (e.g., silicone, adhesives, pigments) and biological tissues under dynamic conditions, such as temperature fluctuations, moisture exposure, and prolonged wear. By employing finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML), the project will model biomechanical stress distribution, adhesive failure thresholds, and pigment degradation rates across heterogeneous skin types and environmental scenarios. High-resolution 3D scans of anatomical structures will inform simulations, while ML algorithms trained on material science datasets will predict optimal material combinations and application protocols. The computational workflow will integrate multi-physics simulations (thermal, mechanical, chemical) to evaluate real-world performance, reducing reliance on physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include a validated library of material-behavior profiles, adaptive application guidelines for practitioners, and open-source tools for simulating prosthetic-cosmetic outcomes in virtual environments. This work bridges gaps between cosmetic artistry, materials engineering, and computational modeling, offering novel solutions for medical prosthetics (e.g., post-surgical reconstruction) and security-focused disguise systems. The HPC resources are critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelized simulations, and large-scale data processing required for robust, generalizable models. Results will advance evidence-based practices in prosthetic cosmetology, enhancing accessibility and efficacy for diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally apply cosmetic makeup preparations and perform complete and specialized appearance makeovers including hairdressing, wig work, masking, temporary prosthesis applications, cosmetic applications, and related costuming for leisure or for professional stage, camera, clinical, or security purposes.  Includes instruction in period and contemporary hairstyling and costuming; wig work and hairpiece application; synthetic hair and masks; cosmetic preparations and treatments; makeup artistry; attachment, removal, and camouflaging of prostheses; health and safety; client consultation and care; pre- and post-production operations; set and crew conduct and relations; script, instruction, and prescription interpretation; labor relations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on diachronic syntactic and morphological shifts in East Asian languages, with a focus on understudied regional dialects and pre-modern textual corpora. The core research problem centers on identifying and modeling linguistic evolution across time and space, particularly in languages such as Classical Chinese, Early Middle Japanese, and Korean vernacular variants, where manual analysis of large-scale textual datasets remains prohibitively time-intensive. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the scope of corpus-based studies, hindering systematic comparisons of syntactic structures, lexical borrowing patterns, and sociolinguistic influences. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical and dialectal East Asian texts, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on pre-modern corpora. Key tasks include the development of a unified annotation framework for cross-linguistic comparison, training of dialect identification classifiers using phonological and morphological features, and large-scale simulation of language contact scenarios through agent-based modeling. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte text repositories, GPU-accelerated training of multilingual BERT variants for low-resource historical languages, and high-dimensional visualization of dialect continuum data. Expected outcomes include 1) quantitative reconstructions of syntactic change trajectories in Sino-Tibetan languages from the Tang to Qing dynasties, 2) geospatial models of Korean dialect divergence correlated with historical migration patterns, and 3) open-source NLP tools tailored for pre-modern East Asian texts. These results will provide novel insights into language change mechanisms while creating computational infrastructure to support philological research across the humanities. The project directly addresses gaps in digital resources for non-Western languages and strengthens interdisciplinary connections between computational linguistics and area studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: East Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages of East Asia, including, but not limited to, the Sino-Tibetan, Japanese, and Korean languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools for real-time spatial audio synthesis and interactive music systems, addressing the challenge of creating immersive, dynamically adaptive soundscapes for virtual/augmented reality (VR/AR) and live performance contexts. Current methods for 3D audio rendering struggle to balance high spatial precision with low latency, particularly in environments requiring real-time interaction or adaptive acoustic responses. To overcome these limitations, the research will implement parallelized physical modeling algorithms and machine learning-driven sound propagation simulations optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. Key computational tasks include GPU-accelerated finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for room acoustics, neural networks trained on spectral impulse response datasets, and distributed processing of multichannel audio streams. The project will leverage large-scale parameter sweeps to optimize hybrid models combining physics-based and data-driven approaches, enabling efficient synthesis of spatially complex auditory environments. Expected outcomes include open-source software frameworks for real-time spatial audio manipulation and novel metrics for evaluating perceptual accuracy in dynamic 3D sound fields. These tools will directly benefit music technology research by enabling new forms of computational composition and performance while advancing interdisciplinary applications in VR/AR development. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the memory-intensive wave equation simulations and large neural network architectures required to model high-frequency audio interactions at scale, tasks infeasible on standard workstations. By bridging music cognition research with computational acoustics, this work aims to establish new best practices for technology-mediated musical expression and interactive audio design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creative aspects of the blending of music and technology; and that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the composition, recording, synthesis, and performance of music; audio-visual production; scoring for film and multimedia; and software and multimedia development. Includes instruction in music theory, music history, composition, acoustics, recording technology, computer composition, electronic music synthesis, technology-based performance, 3D sound and spatial audio, and music business and law.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in educational resource allocation across multi-school districts by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize decision-making processes. School district administrators face persistent challenges in balancing budgetary constraints, equity mandates, and dynamic student needs, yet existing tools for predictive planning lack the computational capacity to integrate multi-dimensional datasets or simulate long-term outcomes at scale. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a computational framework that synthesizes district-level financial, demographic, and academic performance data with policy constraints and geographic variables. Agent-based modeling will simulate resource distribution scenarios under fluctuating enrollment, funding shifts, and policy reforms, while machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in historical allocation decisions and their impacts on student achievement gaps. HPC resources are critical to process terabytes of structured and unstructured data from state databases, district records, and community surveys, enabling real-time sensitivity analyses and probabilistic forecasting. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between allocation strategies, predicts equity impacts across student subgroups, and prioritizes interventions aligned with regional needs. By providing superintendents with evidence-based, computationally derived insights, this project aims to advance adaptive leadership practices, reduce discretionary biases in resource distribution, and foster scalable models for equitable systemic administration. The resulting framework will be validated through case studies across urban, suburban, and rural districts, establishing a replicable methodology for data-driven governance in K-12 educational systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leading and managing multi-school educational systems and school districts and prepares individuals to serve as systems administrators and district superintendents. Includes instruction in educational administration; education of students at various levels; system planning and budgeting; educational policy; educational law and regulations; public relations; professional standards and ethics; and applications to specific issues, cultural context, and geographic locales.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic relationships between vernacular creativity, cultural memory, and identity formation in diasporic communities through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal folklore archives. Despite growing digitization efforts, existing methodologies struggle to systematically analyze the complex interplay of narrative structures, performative elements, and material culture artifacts within and across communities, particularly at the scale required to identify patterns in transnational cultural transmission. The proposed research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for multilingual folktale corpora, computer vision analysis of material culture images, and network modeling of motif diffusion across geographic and temporal axes. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing over 500,000 digitized items from the Global Folklore Repository, including oral history transcripts, ritual performance videos, textile imagery, and ephemera from six migrant-descendant populations. Custom transformer models will be trained to recognize culturally specific aesthetic patterns while preserving contextual nuance, with parallelized workflows managing heterogeneous data types. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously undocumented narrative preservation strategies in gender-specific craft traditions, 2) quantitative models mapping how trauma motifs transform across generational thresholds, and 3) open-source tools for ethically grounded computational folklore analysis. By bridging scale and specificity in cultural analytics, this work aims to advance both digital humanities methodologies and practical frameworks for safeguarding intangible heritage in rapidly changing social landscapes. The computational demands of processing high-resolution multimedia artifacts, maintaining chain-of-custody metadata for culturally sensitive materials, and running iterative comparative analyses across distributed datasets necessitate dedicated GPU clusters and large-memory nodes beyond typical institutional capacities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of creativity and aesthetic expression in everyday life, as expressed in narrative, literature, performing arts, culture, work, family and community.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of nonlinear optical phenomena in complex photonic systems through large-scale computational modeling, with a focus on ultrafast laser-matter interactions and chaotic light propagation. Current experimental limitations in resolving sub-cycle optical field dynamics and spatially heterogeneous nonlinear responses hinder the optimization of high-efficiency frequency conversion devices and stable optical soliton-based communication systems. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining time-domain finite-difference methods for Maxwell’s equations with quantum-corrected nonlinear polarization models. The core challenge lies in simulating three-dimensional nanophotonic structures with femtosecond-scale temporal resolution over experimentally relevant propagation distances—a task requiring petascale computing resources due to the inherent stiffness of the coupled Maxwell-Schrödinger equations and the need for statistical ensemble modeling of chaotic regimes. Our approach leverages adaptive mesh refinement algorithms optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures to handle the disparate spatial scales in metasurface-enhanced harmonic generation systems. Key objectives include characterizing the stability boundaries of multi-pulse soliton complexes in nonlinear waveguide arrays and predicting nonlinear phase-matching conditions in heterogeneous mid-infrared frequency combs. Anticipated outcomes include new design principles for broadband optical parametric amplifiers and validated models of noise-driven polarization collapse in high-intensity propagation media. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parameter space explorations across >10^6 unique configurations, which is critical for establishing universal scaling laws in nonlinear optical systems. This work directly supports the development of next-generation optical computing architectures and terahertz spectroscopy techniques, with potential applications in quantum light source engineering and attosecond pulse control.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of light energy, including its structure, properties and behavior under different conditions. Includes instruction in wave theory, wave mechanics, electromagnetic theory, physical optics, geometric optics, quantum theory of light, photon detecting, laser theory, wall and beam properties, chaotic light, non-linear optics, harmonic generation, optical systems theory, and applications to engineering problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to resolve combustion instability mechanisms in scramjet engines, a critical challenge limiting the reliability of hypersonic propulsion systems. Current models lack the resolution to capture the coupled interactions between turbulent compressible flows, finite-rate chemistry, and unsteady heat release in scramjet combustors, particularly under high-Mach-number conditions. To address this gap, we propose large-scale, three-dimensional simulations using a hybrid LES/FGM (Large Eddy Simulation/Flamelet-Generated Manifolds) approach, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The solver will integrate compressible Navier-Stokes equations with finite-rate chemical kinetics reduced via manifold methods, enabling efficient simulation of turbulence-chemistry interactions at resolutions necessary to resolve kHz-scale instability modes. Simulations will target a representative dual-mode scramjet configuration, with boundary conditions and geometries validated against experimental data from collaborating hypersonic test facilities. The computational workflow will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to dynamically resolve shear layers and reaction zones, coupled with parallelized solvers to manage the >10^8 cell domains required for parameter sweeps across Mach 5–8 regimes. Expected outcomes include identification of instability triggering mechanisms, quantitative maps of mode growth rates under varying inlet conditions, and predictive criteria for stable operability envelopes. These results will directly inform next-generation combustor designs and active control strategies, advancing the viability of scramjet-powered vehicles for orbital launch systems and high-speed global transport. The project requires 750,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated HPC systems, supplemented by 200 TB of high-speed storage for transient flow datasets. By integrating multi-physics modeling with experimental validation, this work aims to establish a foundational framework for simulating combustion dynamics in air-breathing hypersonic systems, addressing a key barrier in aerospace propulsion research.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematic principles to the design, technology, and development of systems and equipment used in aerospace and astronautical operations. Includes instruction in basic and applied sciences related to astronomy and astronautics, control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of computational biology and systems pharmacology into Ayurvedic medicine research. A critical challenge in modernizing Ayurveda lies in systematically validating the therapeutic mechanisms of its complex herbal formulations, which often involve synergistic interactions among hundreds of bioactive compounds. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to address the combinatorial complexity of these polyherbal formulations, their multi-target effects on human physiology, and their alignment with Ayurvedic principles such as *dosha* balance and *agni* (metabolic) regulation. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning to model interactions between Ayurvedic phytochemicals and human protein targets implicated in conditions like metabolic syndrome, chronic inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale virtual screening of classical formulations documented in Sanskrit texts such as the *Charaka Samhita*, coupled with network pharmacology analyses to map formulation-specific effects onto Ayurvedic pathophysiology models. Concurrently, we will develop AI-driven pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models to predict herb-herb and herb-drug interactions, informed by traditional detoxification (*shodhana*) and preparation methods. This dual approach—grounded in both biomedical data and Ayurvedic theory—aims to establish predictive models for personalized *rasayana* (rejuvenation) therapies while preserving the holistic framework of the tradition. Expected outcomes include a curated database of Ayurvedic formulation-target interactions, computational validation of *prakriti* (constitution)-specific treatment responses, and optimized protocols for translating classical interventions into evidence-based practice. By applying advanced computational resources to decode Ayurveda’s empirical wisdom, this work will strengthen its scientific foundation, facilitate interdisciplinary dialogue, and support the development of integrative healthcare solutions validated through both traditional and modern paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Marine microbial communities play a critical role in regulating biogeochemical cycles and ecosystem health in coastal and polar environments, yet their responses to multi-stressor interactions—such as warming, acidification, and deoxygenation—remain poorly resolved at regional scales. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, three-dimensional coupled physical-biogeochemical model to simulate microbial dynamics and metabolic processes in rapidly changing polar coastal systems. The research will focus on the Western Antarctic Peninsula, a region experiencing accelerated warming and ice loss, where shifts in microbial composition could disrupt carbon export and nutrient cycling. A novel aspect of the computational approach involves integrating genomic and metagenomic datasets with a reactive transport model to parameterize taxon-specific metabolic traits and their plasticity under environmental stressors. The model will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve fine-scale heterogeneity in microbial habitats, such as ice-ocean interfaces and stratified water columns, while capturing basin-scale circulation patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to conduct ensemble simulations across decadal timescales, evaluate uncertainty in trait-based parameterizations, and resolve non-linear interactions between physical drivers and microbial feedbacks. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how microbial community structure modulates carbon sequestration efficiency under future climate scenarios and identification of tipping points in coastal polar ecosystems. The resulting open-source model framework will provide a community resource for predicting microbial-mediated biogeochemical shifts in other climate-sensitive regions. By quantifying linkages between microbial resilience and ecosystem function, this work aims to inform strategies for monitoring biodiversity loss and its cascading effects on marine food webs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of biology, chemistry, geology and physics applied to marine, estuarine and coastal environments. Includes instruction in marine biogeochemistry, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, coastal ecology, coastal ocean processes, microbial ecology, marine ecosystem modeling, and polar microbiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven simulation environment to optimize training protocols for teacher assistants (TAs) working with neurodiverse and multilingual student populations in inclusive classrooms. While TAs play a critical role in bridging gaps between instructional goals and student needs, existing training frameworks lack personalized, scenario-based tools to prepare TAs for the dynamic challenges of heterogeneous classrooms. The research problem centers on the computational modeling of high-variability classroom interactions—including non-verbal cues, language transitions, and sensory processing differences—that require real-time adaptive strategies from TAs. We propose a two-phase computational approach: (1) creating synthetic classroom cohorts using generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on multimodal educational datasets (speech, gesture, eye-tracking), and (2) implementing reinforcement learning agents that model TA decision-making processes during simulated interventions. The high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of over 10,000 unique student-TA interaction scenarios, each requiring real-time analysis of linguistic, behavioral, and environmental parameters through coupled natural language processing and computer vision pipelines. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation platform capable of generating TA training modules that adapt to individual learning trajectories, along with quantitative frameworks for assessing TA competency in managing complex classroom dynamics. This work intersects educational psychology, computational linguistics, and machine learning, offering novel methodologies for scaling specialized educator training while maintaining fidelity to the nuanced realities of diverse learning environments. The resulting tools could significantly reduce preparation time for TAs entering specialized classrooms while providing empirical insights into effective support strategies for students at the intersection of multiple learning modalities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist a teacher in regular classroom settings or in providing instruction and supervision to special student populations, such as bilingual/bicultural students, special education students, adult learners, and students learning English. Includes instruction in techniques of general classroom supervision, maintaining order, assisting with lessons and carrying out related assignments.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between digital cultural production and systemic power structures through the computational analysis of multimodal cultural datasets. As digital platforms increasingly mediate cultural expression—from social media discourse to algorithmic content curation—traditional critical frameworks struggle to scale to the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of contemporary data. The research problem centers on mapping how hegemonic narratives emerge and circulate within decentralized digital ecosystems, particularly examining the entanglement of user-generated content, platform algorithms, and geopolitical influences. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a mixed-methods approach combining large-scale natural language processing, network analysis, and visual culture analytics to process petabytes of multilingual social media posts, image-text memes, and streaming video metadata. Computational models will identify patterns in discursive framing, semiotic hybridization, and cross-platform narrative diffusion, while critical theory lenses—including intersectional feminism and postcolonial technoscience—will inform iterative model design and interpretation. Key technical challenges include developing transformer-based architectures sensitive to context-dependent cultural semantics and optimizing graph neural networks to trace ideological propagation across spatially fragmented user communities. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) a novel computational framework for critical cultural analytics that bridges hermeneutic traditions and machine learning; (2) empirical findings on how platform architectures amplify or suppress counterhegemonic cultural practices; and (3) open-source tools enabling researchers to audit algorithmic bias in cultural recommendation systems. By requiring parallelized GPU clusters for training multimodal models and distributed storage for heterogeneous data ingestion, this work both advances interdisciplinary methodologies and demonstrates how HPC infrastructure can empower humanistic inquiry into 21st-century cultural formations.
cip_title: Cultural Studies/ Critical Theory and Analysis
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the analysis and critique of culture in its varied forms, including values, ideas, belief systems, and expressive acts, and the relationship between cultural forms, everyday life, and structures of power. Includes instruction in anthropology, communications, history, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, and sociology, as well as recent theories and methodologies such as semiotics, deconstruction, postcolonial studies, gender theory, and ethnography.

abstract: Geothermal energy systems represent a critical component of renewable energy infrastructure, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by challenges in optimizing installation configurations, predicting long-term performance, and mitigating equipment degradation under variable subsurface conditions. This project seeks to address these challenges through high-fidelity computational modeling of geothermal heat exchange systems, focusing on the interplay between equipment design, geological heterogeneity, and operational parameters. The research will employ multiphysics simulations to model coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical processes in geothermal boreholes, heat pumps, and distribution networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve transient 3D simulations of heat transfer in anisotropic geological formations, stress analysis of mechanical components under thermal cycling, and machine learning-driven optimization of system layouts. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessment, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for working fluid behavior, and Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in subsurface property estimates. The project will validate models against field data from existing installations provided by industry partners. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for equipment lifespan estimation, optimized borehole spacing configurations tailored to regional geology, and decision-support frameworks for proactive maintenance scheduling. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in geothermal technician training programs, bridging the gap between field practices and computational analytics. By enabling precise virtual prototyping of geothermal systems, this work aims to reduce installation costs by 15-20% and extend functional system lifetimes, advancing the technical workforce's capacity to deploy robust geothermal solutions in diverse geological settings.
cip_title: Geothermal Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of interreligious textual and doctrinal interactions across premodern Afro-Eurasian traditions (circa 500–1500 CE). While historical religious studies have traditionally relied on close readings of key texts, the scale and linguistic diversity of extant manuscripts—spanning Arabic, Sanskrit, Syriac, and Classical Chinese—pose significant barriers to systematic comparative analysis. Current scholarship lacks robust frameworks for identifying patterns of conceptual exchange, adaptation, and polemic between traditions such as Buddhism, Islam, Christianity, and Hinduism during this formative period. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach combining multilingual natural language processing (NLP), semantic network analysis, and probabilistic topic modeling. Custom transformer-based models will be fine-tuned for low-resource historical languages using digitized corpora from partner archives, enabling cross-lingual alignment of theological and philosophical terminology. Graph-theoretic methods will then map doctrinal relationships across traditions, while temporal modeling will trace conceptual diffusion pathways. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale text collections, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable pipeline for comparative analysis of religious texts across linguistic boundaries, 2) empirical identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal interfaces between traditions, and 3) open-access visualization tools for exploring dynamic interreligious networks. By integrating computational methods with domain expertise in religious history, this project aims to advance scholarly understanding of cross-cultural theological exchange while establishing new methodologies for data-driven religious studies. The resource-intensive nature of training multilingual models and analyzing heterogeneous textual networks makes HPC infrastructure critical to achieving these objectives.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religion/religious studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize the operational efficiency and environmental performance of thermal power plants through advanced simulations of coupled thermo-fluid and chemical processes. Aging power infrastructure, coupled with increasing demands for efficiency and stringent emissions regulations, necessitates a deeper understanding of complex interactions between turbine dynamics, combustion systems, water chemistry, and pollution control mechanisms. Current empirical models lack the resolution to capture transient phenomena, such as stress-induced turbine fatigue or the real-time formation of nitrogen oxides (NOx) during load fluctuations. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-physics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization. Large-eddy simulations (LES) will resolve turbulent combustion dynamics in boiler systems, while conjugate heat transfer models will assess thermal stresses in turbine blades under cyclic loading. Concurrently, reactive transport models will evaluate corrosion and scaling in water-steam cycles, informed by aqueous chemistry datasets. A neural network trained on simulation outputs and historical plant data will identify operational parameters that minimize fuel consumption and emissions without compromising output. The computational scale requires parallelized solvers and distributed memory architectures to handle ~1 billion cell meshes and microsecond-scale timestepping over operational timelines. Expected outcomes include predictive models for turbine lifespan, optimized combustion profiles reducing NOx by 15–20%, and adaptive control strategies for hybrid plants integrating renewable energy sources. This work will provide a validated digital twin framework to support next-generation power plant design, retrofitting, and real-time operational decision-making, directly contributing to sustainable energy transitions and grid resilience. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial and temporal resolutions necessary for actionable insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and operational disparities in K-12 education systems across diverse socioeconomic contexts, with a focus on identifying policy-relevant drivers of inequitable student outcomes. While existing studies have evaluated discrete interventions, there remains a critical gap in modeling how systemic factors—such as resource distribution frameworks, teacher retention policies, and administrative decision-making hierarchies—interact dynamically to shape educational access and quality. The research employs a multi-method computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and longitudinal network analysis to simulate policy impacts across 10,000+ synthetically generated school districts, calibrated using national datasets (e.g., Civil Rights Data Collection, state accountability reports). ABM will simulate stakeholder interactions (students, educators, administrators) under varying policy regimes, while temporal network analysis will map how funding flows and information-sharing mechanisms propagate inequities over time. HPC resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity of these simulations, which involve parallel processing of over 200 billion agent interactions and real-time optimization of policy parameters via machine learning techniques. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework to predict the second-order effects of proposed education policies, validated against historical equity metrics from 15 states. Results will inform actionable recommendations for optimizing resource allocation models and institutional governance structures, directly contributing to evidence-based policymaking in education. By quantifying the emergent consequences of policy choices, this work aims to advance methodological rigor in education policy analysis while addressing urgent questions about systemic fairness in public education systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to education and educational systems at the local, state, national, and international levels. Includes instruction in social and cultural issues in education, contemporary educational policies, history of education, economics of education, international and comparative education, education and social change, educational research and evaluation methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of financial resilience in households through the development of a dynamic, agent-based simulation framework. The research problem centers on understanding how complex interactions between income volatility, debt accumulation, and adaptive financial decision-making influence long-term household stability. Traditional analytical methods in Family Resource Management Studies often rely on static or simplified models, limiting their capacity to capture nonlinear feedback loops, heterogeneous behavioral patterns, and the cascading effects of economic shocks. To address this gap, the proposed computational approach integrates granular household financial data, stochastic income modeling, and empirically derived behavioral rules to simulate decision-making processes across diverse socioeconomic cohorts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of over 100,000 agent-households under variable macroeconomic conditions, incorporating machine learning techniques to refine predictive accuracy in real-time scenario testing. Key computational challenges include optimizing memory allocation for large-scale parameter sweeps and managing latency in iterative reinforcement learning algorithms that govern agent adaptation. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in debt-to-income ratios that precipitate financial distress, (2) validation of intervention strategies to mitigate resource depletion during economic downturns, and (3) open-source tools for personalized financial planning. By quantifying the interdependencies between behavioral choices and systemic economic pressures, this project aims to establish a novel computational paradigm for household resource management research, with direct applications to financial literacy programs and policy design. The scalability afforded by HPC resources is essential to achieving the temporal resolution and cohort diversity required for robust, generalizable insights.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and implementation of policies and processes contributing to successful individual and family resource management. Includes instruction in financial goal-setting and strategies; household income, assets, and debt management; preventing and resolving financial difficulties; and the use of relevant public resources.

abstract: Women’s health outcomes are shaped by complex interactions between biological, social, and environmental factors, yet current clinical models often lack the computational power to integrate these multi-dimensional datasets at scale. This project seeks to address critical gaps in personalized care for women by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale clinical, genomic, and socio-environmental data. The research focuses on two interrelated aims: (1) developing predictive models for adverse maternal outcomes, such as preterm birth and perinatal mood disorders, by integrating electronic health records (EHRs), polygenic risk scores, and geospatial data; and (2) simulating the population-level impacts of targeted nursing interventions using agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will employ machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and neural networks, to identify risk stratification patterns and optimize intervention strategies. These models will account for sex-specific physiological pathways, pharmacotherapeutic responses, and structural determinants of health. By harnessing HPC capabilities, the project will process terabytes of heterogeneous data, perform real-time sensitivity analyses, and iteratively refine predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include scalable tools to guide evidence-based nursing practices, reduce disparities in women’s healthcare access, and inform policy decisions. This work will directly advance the capacity of women’s health nurses to deliver precision care, particularly in underserved populations, while establishing a computational framework for future studies in gender-specific health optimization. The requested resources are essential to overcome current limitations in data processing speed and model complexity, ensuring robust, reproducible findings with translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: The increasing demand for precision and safety in firearm design necessitates advanced computational tools to overcome limitations in traditional gunsmithing methods. Current approaches to optimizing firearm components—such as barrels, triggers, and gas systems—rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-intensive, costly, and constrained by material availability. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate the mechanical, thermal, and fluid dynamic behaviors of firearm systems under operational conditions. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) developing multi-physics models to predict stress distribution, heat dissipation, and internal ballistics in novel firearm designs, and (2) optimizing component geometries and material selections to enhance durability, accuracy, and safety. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for propellant gas flow modeling, and machine learning algorithms to identify material-performance correlations across datasets of metallurgical properties and historical failure cases. HPC resources are critical due to the high-resolution meshing requirements for small-scale components and the need for parallelized simulations across diverse operating parameters (e.g., ammunition types, environmental conditions). Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for rapid virtual prototyping, reducing physical testing cycles by an estimated 60–75%, and data-driven guidelines for material substitutions in response to supply chain disruptions. The project will also produce open-access simulation templates tailored to gunsmithing education, enabling students to explore advanced design principles without access to industrial-scale machinery. By integrating computational engineering into a traditionally craft-based field, this work aims to modernize gunsmithing practices, improve safety standards, and bridge gaps between technical education and emerging manufacturing technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and modify firearms according to blueprints or customer specifications, using specialized hand tools and machines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational model of adaptive neural circuitry underlying human motor learning, leveraging artificial intelligence to bridge gaps in understanding how synaptic plasticity dynamics integrate real-time sensorimotor feedback. Traditional models of motor control often oversimplify the nonlinear interactions between cortical plasticity, cerebellar error correction, and basal ganglia reinforcement mechanisms, particularly during skill acquisition in dynamic environments. To address this, we propose a hybrid spiking neural network (SNN) architecture enhanced with meta-reinforcement learning, designed to simulate multi-scale neural adaptation—from individual synaptic modifications to network-level reconfiguration. The model will integrate biologically constrained neuron models with AI-driven plasticity rules trained on multimodal data, including motion capture kinematics, electromyography, and synthetic neural activity patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate the network’s 10^6+ spiking neurons and 10^9+ dynamic synapses while maintaining millisecond temporal resolution across hours of simulated learning tasks. Computational experiments will systematically perturb sensory input latency, noise levels, and reward schedules to identify failure modes in adaptive motor control, with validation against empirical datasets from human subjects performing precision grip tasks under variable load conditions. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how neural circuits balance stability-plasticity tradeoffs during skill refinement, with translational implications for optimizing neuroprosthetic device training protocols. The project will also yield open-source tools for large-scale SNN simulations, enabling broader research into biologically inspired AI architectures for adaptive control systems. By synthesizing principles from computational neuroscience, machine learning, and biomechanics, this work advances an interdisciplinary framework for studying embodied intelligence while pushing the boundaries of resource-intensive neural simulation methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the symbolic inference, representation, and simulation by computers and software of human learning and reasoning processes and capabilities, and the computer modeling of human motor control and motion. Includes instruction in computing theory, cybernetics, human factors, natural language processing, and applicable aspects of engineering, technology, and specific end-use applications.

abstract: The increasing complexity of veterinary administrative operations, driven by evolving regulatory requirements, client expectations, and data management demands, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize workflows and decision-making. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to model and analyze large-scale administrative datasets from veterinary practices, including client interactions, appointment scheduling, billing cycles, and inventory logistics. Current systems often rely on fragmented software solutions that lack interoperability, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and compliance tracking. The research problem centers on identifying systemic bottlenecks and predicting operational risks through computational simulations that integrate heterogeneous data streams, such as electronic health records, staff performance metrics, and supply chain variables. Leveraging parallelized agent-based modeling and machine learning algorithms, the project will simulate clinic operations under varying constraints (e.g., staffing shortages, seasonal demand fluctuations) to generate adaptive resource allocation strategies. A key innovation lies in applying graph-based network analysis to map dependencies between administrative tasks and clinical outcomes, enabling proactive adjustments to workflow prioritization. The computational architecture will utilize GPU-accelerated clustering techniques to process real-time data from anonymized multi-site veterinary practices, ensuring scalability while adhering to ethical standards for data privacy. Expected outcomes include a predictive dashboard for veterinary administrators to optimize staffing schedules, inventory procurement, and compliance auditing cycles, with preliminary simulations targeting a 15–20% reduction in operational overhead. By bridging computational analytics and veterinary administrative science, this work establishes a foundation for data-driven governance in animal care facilities, addressing a critical gap in non-science and engineering research while advancing professional standards for operational efficiency in the sector.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to provide administrative support services in a veterinary office or animal care facility. Includes instruction in business office operations, customer service, principles of veterinary health care operations, record-keeping, veterinary terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the multifactorial etiology of periodontal disease, a pervasive oral health condition with systemic implications. Current clinical studies often focus on isolated factors—such as microbial composition or host immune responses—yet lack the computational capacity to integrate multi-omics datasets (genomic, metagenomic, proteomic) with clinical variables at scale. This limitation hinders the identification of predictive biomarkers and mechanistically informed treatment strategies. To address this gap, we propose a computational study analyzing longitudinal data from 500 patients with varying stages of periodontal disease, including 16S rRNA sequencing, host transcriptomics, inflammatory cytokine profiles, and electronic health records. Machine learning models (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble classifiers) will be trained to identify cross-modal signatures of disease progression and treatment resistance. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model host-pathogen interactions critical to biofilm virulence, utilizing GPU-accelerated frameworks to simulate protein-ligand binding events across microbial communities. These simulations will inform targeted antimicrobial design. The HPC environment is essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks, and enabling real-time analytics during clinical data collection. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for individualized risk stratification, (2) mechanistic insights into polymicrobial synergy driving chronic inflammation, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic integration of clinical and omics data in dental research. By elucidating pathways linking oral dysbiosis to systemic conditions (e.g., cardiovascular disease), this work will directly enhance evidence-based practices in periodontal therapy while establishing scalable methods for precision dentistry. The requested resources will support iterative model training, large-scale simulations, and secure handling of sensitive patient data, fulfilling computational demands exceeding the capacity of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program that generally prepares dentists in one or more of the oral sciences and advanced/graduate dentistry specialties.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in plant-pathogen interactions, with a focus on identifying genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying disease resistance in staple crops. Plant diseases caused by fungal and bacterial pathogens result in significant agricultural losses annually, threatening global food security. Traditional experimental approaches to dissect host-pathogen dynamics are limited by the complexity of plant immune systems and the vast genomic datasets involved. To overcome these barriers, this project proposes an integrated computational framework combining machine learning, multi-omics data integration, and mechanistic modeling. Genome-scale metabolic models of key crops (e.g., wheat, rice) and their pathogens will be reconstructed using transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets. These models will be coupled with neural networks trained on historical disease resistance phenotypes to predict candidate resistance genes and optimal gene-editing targets. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate structural interactions between plant immune receptors and pathogen effectors at atomistic resolution. The scale of these analyses—spanning terabytes of genomic data and requiring millions of CPU-hours for ensemble simulations—necessitates HPC infrastructure with parallelized workflows and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive atlas of resistance-associated genetic loci, (2) optimized gene-editing strategies for breeding programs, and (3) publicly accessible databases of plant-pathogen interaction networks. By accelerating the identification of durable disease resistance traits, this work aims to reduce reliance on chemical pesticides while enhancing crop resilience in changing climates. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other plant species, offering a transformative toolset for plant sciences research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plant sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the integration of high-performance computing (HPC) in the creation and analysis of large-scale generative visual art and interactive digital installations. Traditional computational tools for artists often face limitations in processing power, restricting the complexity and interactivity of artworks that rely on real-time data processing, dynamic simulation, or machine learning models. The research problem centers on overcoming these constraints to enable the production of intricate, algorithmically-generated visual experiences that respond to environmental inputs or user interactions with minimal latency. The computational approach involves leveraging HPC resources to parallelize rendering tasks, optimize neural network training for generative adversarial networks (GANs) tasked with producing high-resolution visual content, and simulate physical phenomena (e.g., fluid dynamics, particle systems) within virtual environments. Additionally, the project will utilize distributed computing frameworks to manage real-time data streams from IoT sensors embedded in installation spaces, facilitating adaptive artwork behaviors. Expected outcomes include the development of a scalable software toolkit for digital artists, enabling the creation of previously infeasible artworks that dynamically evolve in response to complex inputs. The research also aims to contribute novel methodologies at the intersection of computational art and media studies, offering insights into how HPC can expand the boundaries of artistic practice and interactive design. By addressing both technical and conceptual challenges, this work underscores the transformative potential of advanced computing resources in fostering innovation within visual arts and redefining audience engagement through technology-driven experiences.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Fine Arts and Art Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fine arts and art studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating computational tools into art pedagogy training by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model large-scale datasets of student-artwork interactions. Current approaches to art teacher education often rely on qualitative assessments of student progress, limiting the scalability and personalization of feedback. The proposed research will develop a computational framework to analyze digital art portfolios, behavioral data from collaborative art platforms, and temporal patterns in skill development across diverse student demographics. Using machine learning models trained on multimodal data (e.g., image features, metadata, and user interaction logs), the project will identify correlations between teaching strategies, artistic technique acquisition, and student engagement. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of image and video data, running parallelized neural networks for style recognition, and simulating classroom scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable toolset for art educators to diagnose skill gaps in real time, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adapting lesson plans to individual learning trajectories, and (3) open-access datasets linking computational art analysis to pedagogical effectiveness. By bridging art education theory with data-driven methods, this work aims to equip future art teachers with empirically validated strategies for fostering creativity in digitally mediated learning environments. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in art teacher certification programs, emphasizing adaptive instruction and the ethical use of AI tools in K-12 art classrooms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach art and art appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Greenhouse operations require precise environmental control to optimize plant growth, yet current management strategies often rely on static protocols that fail to dynamically adapt to real-time biological and environmental variability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational model to simulate and predict plant-environment interactions in controlled agricultural settings. The research problem centers on the need for adaptive, energy-efficient greenhouse systems that balance productivity with resource constraints, particularly under fluctuating external conditions such as shifting weather patterns or pest pressures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale datasets—including sensor-derived climate data, hyperspectral plant imaging, and genomic information from key crop species—into a machine learning framework. This framework will employ neural networks and agent-based modeling to predict optimal adjustments to temperature, humidity, irrigation, and lighting systems in response to real-time plant physiological states. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will further refine spatial climate distribution models to minimize energy use while maintaining growth homogeneity across greenhouse zones. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high dimensionality of sensor data, parallelizing iterative optimization algorithms, and scaling simulations to represent diverse crop species and facility designs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for dynamic climate control, validated against experimental greenhouse trials, that reduces energy consumption by 15–20% while increasing yield consistency for high-value crops. By bridging computational modeling with operational greenhouse management, this work will provide a template for data-driven automation in controlled-environment agriculture, enhancing the resilience and scalability of food production systems. The proposed resource allocation will directly support the development of open-access computational tools tailored to the needs of commercial and research greenhouse operators.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce, store, and deliver plant species in controlled indoor environments for wholesale, commercial, research, or other purposes. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science; climate, irrigation, and nutrition control equipment operation and maintenance; facilities management; inventory control; safety procedures; and personnel supervision.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and policy challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems within intellectual property (IP) law frameworks. The rapid proliferation of AI-generated content—spanning text, images, code, and inventions—has created ambiguities in existing IP regimes, particularly regarding authorship, inventorship, and infringement liability. Traditional doctrinal legal analysis struggles to keep pace with the technical complexity and scale of AI outputs, necessitating a computational approach to model interactions between emerging technologies and legal principles. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze large corpora of case law, patent filings, and regulatory documents, training machine learning models to identify patterns in judicial reasoning, predict litigation outcomes, and simulate the downstream effects of proposed policy changes. Computational simulations will model hypothetical scenarios, such as the systemic impacts of recognizing AI systems as legal authors or the economic consequences of varying infringement thresholds for AI-trained models. By integrating legal text analysis with network modeling of IP ecosystems, this research aims to quantify risks and opportunities in AI-related IP disputes while informing equitable governance frameworks. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of legal and technical data, running parallelized simulations, and optimizing deep learning architectures for legal semantic analysis. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database mapping AI-related IP conflicts, predictive tools to assist policymakers in drafting adaptive regulations, and scholarly articles proposing evidence-based reforms to balance innovation incentives with public access in the AI era. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, legal informatics, and technology policy, offering novel methodologies for addressing 21st-century IP challenges.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations related to copyrights, patents, trademarks, trade secrets, and related issues. Includes instruction in patent law, copyright law, trademark law, intellectual property licensing and litigation, and applications such as art and entertainment law, communications law, information technology law, sports law, and chemical and biotech patent law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary study at the intersection of legal systems analysis and computational modeling, focusing on the emergent field of legal informatics. The research addresses a critical gap in traditional legal scholarship: the inability to systematically model complex, large-scale interactions between legal decisions, statutory evolution, and societal outcomes over extended temporal and jurisdictional scales. By developing a computational framework to simulate the dynamic effects of judicial reasoning patterns and legislative changes, this project aims to uncover latent systemic biases, predict unintended consequences of legal reforms, and identify opportunities for optimizing judicial efficiency. The core computational challenge involves processing and analyzing terabyte-scale datasets of appellate court decisions, legislative histories, and socio-economic indicators using natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for legal text, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making cascades across hierarchical court systems. Custom machine learning architectures will be trained to classify judicial reasoning styles and detect subtle patterns in precedent citation networks, while Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes of hypothetical policy interventions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational legal analysis, novel metrics for quantifying systemic legal efficiency, and evidence-based recommendations for procedural reforms in appellate review processes. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform advanced legal research methodologies by introducing scalable, data-driven approaches to questions traditionally limited to qualitative or small-sample analysis. Successful implementation will provide scholars, policymakers, and judicial administrators with unprecedented analytical tools to evaluate the longitudinal impacts of legal structures, advancing both academic understanding and practical governance in an era of increasingly complex legal systems.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program in one or more of the legal research or advanced practice fields.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergence of decentralized trade networks in early human societies, focusing on how environmental resource distribution and social decision-making processes facilitated intergroup exchange without centralized political structures. Despite extensive ethnographic and archaeological evidence of such networks, the mechanisms driving their formation and sustainability remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with high-resolution geographic information systems (GIS) data. The ABM framework will simulate interactions between autonomous agent groups representing semi-nomadic communities, incorporating variables such as resource scarcity, mobility constraints, kinship ties, and reciprocity norms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across diverse ecological scenarios and to process spatially explicit interactions within dynamic landscapes. By systematically varying environmental productivity zones and social exchange rules, the simulations will identify critical thresholds and feedback loops that promote stable trade relationships. The outcomes will generate testable hypotheses about the archaeological signatures of early trade networks, such as artifact distribution patterns and settlement hierarchies. This research will advance anthropological theories on the coevolution of economic systems and environmental adaptation, offering a scalable framework to analyze pre-state exchange dynamics. The computational models and datasets produced will be made openly available, facilitating interdisciplinary collaborations in archaeology, complexity science, and historical ecology.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Anthropology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and dynamic drivers of social inequality in urban populations, with a focus on how micro-level interactions aggregate to produce macro-level disparities. The research problem centers on the limitations of traditional statistical methods in modeling complex, nonlinear social systems, particularly when analyzing large-scale demographic datasets that capture multidimensional variables such as income, education, migration, and access to public services. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis techniques to simulate population-scale interactions and emergent social outcomes. The computational approach will involve developing parallelized simulations using census data, longitudinal social surveys, and geospatial information systems (GIS) data to parameterize agents representing individuals and households. These simulations will test hypotheses about feedback loops between policy interventions, economic shocks, and demographic behaviors (e.g., fertility, migration). Network analysis will further examine how information diffusion and resource access within social networks reinforce or mitigate inequality. The HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to realistic population sizes (10^6–10^7 agents) and running thousands of parameterized scenarios to assess robustness. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for equitable policy design, publishing open-source simulation frameworks for sociological research, and advancing methodological integration of computational social science within demography. By clarifying how local interactions generate systemic inequalities, this work aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC-enabled modeling in sociology and population studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human social institutions and social relationships. Includes instruction in social theory, sociological research methods, social organization and structure, social stratification and hierarchies, dynamics of social change, family structures, social deviance and control, and applications to the study of specific social groups, social institutions, and social problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the urgent challenge of optimizing land use decisions in rapidly developing regions facing competing demands for conservation, urbanization, and resource extraction. Current models often fail to integrate dynamic environmental, socioeconomic, and climatic variables at sufficient spatial and temporal resolutions, limiting their utility for adaptive management. We propose developing a high-resolution, multi-agent simulation framework that couples machine learning with geospatial analytics to model land use outcomes under diverse policy and climate scenarios. The computational approach will integrate satellite imagery, hydrological data, urban growth patterns, biodiversity indices, and stakeholder behavior models within a unified HPC environment. Key methodologies include parallelized cellular automata for land cover change prediction, GPU-accelerated deep learning for habitat fragmentation analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in economic-environmental tradeoffs. The scale of data processing—terabytes of multispectral imagery, decades of climate projections, and fine-grained demographic inputs—necessitates distributed memory architectures and optimized I/O pipelines. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of identifying land use configurations that maximize carbon sequestration, water security, and economic productivity while respecting ecological carrying capacities. This work will advance computational techniques in spatial optimization and provide actionable insights for regional planners managing tradeoffs between conservation and development. By quantifying the cascading impacts of zoning policies, infrastructure investments, and conservation incentives, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for sustainable land governance in biodiversity-critical regions. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the required computational throughput for parameter sensitivity analyses and to deliver scalable, open-source models for public agency use.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Land Use Planning and Management/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how public and/or private land and associated resources can be preserved, developed, and used for maximum social, economic, and environmental benefit. Includes instruction in natural resources management, natural resource economics, public policy, regional and land use planning, environmental impact assessment, applicable law and regulations, government and politics, principles of business and real estate land use, statistical and analytical tools, computer applications, mapping and report preparation, site analysis, cost analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of food processing systems, with a focus on optimizing thermal and non-thermal preservation methods to enhance food safety, quality, and energy efficiency. A key challenge in food technology lies in predicting the complex interactions between processing parameters (e.g., temperature gradients, flow dynamics, microbial inactivation kinetics) and heterogeneous food matrices at scale. Current experimental approaches are resource-intensive and limited in resolving spatiotemporal variations, while existing simulations often oversimplify multi-physics phenomena. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model heat and mass transfer during pasteurization, drying, and high-pressure processing. High-fidelity simulations will capture turbulent flow in industrial-scale equipment, coupled with reaction kinetics of nutrient degradation and pathogen reduction. Parallelized solvers will enable parameter sweeps to identify energy-efficient processing conditions while maintaining safety standards. Additionally, ML models trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets will predict optimal packaging configurations to minimize thermal buffering and extend shelf life. The HPC environment is critical for handling the computational demands of 3D transient simulations with adaptive meshing, which require terabytes of memory and thousands of CPU-core hours per iteration.
