Expected outcomes include validated models for designing novel processing systems that reduce energy consumption by 15–20% compared to conventional methods, as well as predictive tools for mitigating quality losses in thermally sensitive products. This work aligns with global priorities to reduce food waste and decarbonize food manufacturing, directly supporting advancements in sustainable food engineering practices. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will be shared with academic and industry partners to accelerate innovation in food process optimization.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making processes in critical incident response operations, such as hostage rescues, active shooter scenarios, and coordinated terrorist attacks. Traditional training and planning tools rely on static simulations or historical case studies, which fail to account for the dynamic, high-stakes variables inherent in real-world emergencies—including evolving threat behaviors, environmental unpredictability, and multi-agency coordination challenges. The research problem centers on creating adaptive, real-time models that integrate behavioral psychology, tactical logistics, and environmental dynamics to improve operational outcomes. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate complex interactions between suspects, victims, responders, and bystanders across diverse incident scenarios. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze historical incident data, identify patterns in suspect decision-making, and predict optimal response strategies under uncertainty. Additionally, geospatial analytics will model physical environments (e.g., urban layouts, building structures) to assess tactical vulnerabilities and resource deployment efficiency. The computational pipeline will incorporate real-time data streams, such as situational updates from first responders and IoT sensors, to enable dynamic scenario adjustment. Expected outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for incident commanders to evaluate contingency plans, prioritize interventions, and mitigate collateral risks during live operations. The framework will also generate synthetic training datasets to enhance preparedness for low-probability, high-impact events. By bridging computational science with tactical emergency response, this work aims to reduce operational failure rates, improve interagency interoperability, and establish a foundation for data-driven protocols in a field traditionally reliant on heuristic approaches. The project’s computational demands—particularly parallelized ABM execution, large-scale ML training, and real-time multi-agent reinforcement learning—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve practical scalability and latency thresholds.
cip_title: Critical Incident Response/ Special Police Operations
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for dealing with police emergencies such as hostage situations, bomb threats, barricades and terrorist incidents. Includes instruction in crisis management, command procedures, incident containment, information collection and debriefing, first responder negotiation, victim and criminal psychology, site survey and surveillance, special weapons and tactics, interagency communications and joint operations, pre-confrontation and contingency planning, assault and rescue operations, security and crowd control, media relations, and post-operation procedures.

abstract: Surgical wound complications, including infection, dehiscence, and delayed healing, remain significant challenges in postoperative care, contributing to increased morbidity, healthcare costs, and patient dissatisfaction. Current clinical approaches to optimize wound management and reconstruction lack robust predictive tools to account for patient-specific biomechanical, immunological, and microbiological variables. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and finite element (FE) modeling to predict surgical wound outcomes and guide personalized reconstruction strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale clinical datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), 3D imaging, and genomic profiles—and simulate complex interactions between tissue mechanics, microbial dynamics, and immune responses. The computational pipeline will first train ML models on retrospective EHR data to identify risk factors for poor healing, followed by FE simulations of wound biomechanics under varying surgical closure techniques and physiological loads. Concurrently, agent-based models will analyze host-microbe interactions to predict infection risks. These components will be unified into a patient-specific predictive dashboard for clinical testing. The project leverages HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize FE simulations across thousands of tissue microstructures, and optimize ML hyperparameters via distributed computing. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for wound failure probability, biomechanically optimized closure protocols, and mechanistic insights into microbial-immune crosstalk. Successful implementation will advance precision medicine in surgery by enabling data-driven decision-making, reducing trial-and-error approaches, and improving patient outcomes. All models and workflows will be made open-source to foster collaboration in computational surgical research. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in bridging clinical data complexity with actionable insights for transformative patient care.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: Surgical wound healing and tissue reconstruction outcomes remain highly variable due to complex interactions between patient-specific biological factors, surgical techniques, and postoperative care. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict individualized healing trajectories or optimize reconstructive strategies, leading to preventable complications such as dehiscence, infection, and poor aesthetic outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to model multiscale wound healing dynamics and simulate reconstructive outcomes under diverse biological and biomechanical conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate patient-derived genomic, proteomic, and imaging data with mechanistic models of cellular behavior, extracellular matrix remodeling, and mechanical stress distributions. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular interactions during inflammation and proliferation phases, while finite element analyses will predict tissue deformation and perfusion in complex anatomical geometries. Machine learning pipelines will identify predictive biomarkers from multi-omics datasets and clinical records, enabling risk stratification. The computational platform will be validated against a retrospective cohort of 850 surgical cases with longitudinal wound imaging and histopathological data. By enabling real-time simulation of hypothetical surgical interventions—including flap design modifications or adjunct therapies—this resource will advance personalized decision-making in reconstructive surgery. Anticipated outcomes include a validated predictive tool for wound complication risks, biomechanical guidelines for flap design optimization, and novel biomarkers for targeted therapies. The HPC environment is critical for scaling spatially explicit simulations across anatomical variability, managing high-dimensional data integration, and enabling rapid parameter sweeps to test clinical hypotheses. This work bridges computational systems biology and surgical innovation, with potential to reduce revision surgeries, improve functional recovery, and lower healthcare costs in complex wound management.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and stylistic patterns underlying commercially successful contemporary literary works, with the goal of developing data-driven insights to inform creative writing practices. While literary analysis has traditionally relied on qualitative methods, the scale and complexity of modern publishing output—spanning thousands of novels, short stories, and poetry collections—exceeds the capacity of manual close reading. This research addresses this gap by applying computational text analysis to a curated corpus of 20,000 English-language works published between 2010–2023, including award-winning titles, bestsellers, and critically acclaimed midlist publications. Using GPU-accelerated natural language processing pipelines, we will quantify stylistic features such as syntactic complexity, lexical diversity, narrative pacing, and thematic cohesion. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer models will be trained to identify latent patterns correlating with commercial success or critical recognition, controlling for genre and demographic variables. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will simulate hybrid stylistic approaches by merging features from distinct authorial voices or subgenres. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of multi-gigabyte text datasets, fine-tuning of large language models, and iterative experimentation with generative architectures—tasks requiring dedicated HPC resources for memory-intensive batch jobs. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible web tool enabling writers to analyze their drafts against genre-specific success markers, (2) empirical frameworks for assessing market-aligned creative choices without compromising artistic integrity, and (3) new interdisciplinary methodologies bridging computational analysis and humanistic inquiry. By revealing quantifiable relationships between craft techniques and reader reception, this project aims to equip emerging writers with evidence-based strategies while stimulating scholarly debates about creativity in the algorithmic age.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process and techniques of original composition in various literary forms such as the short story, poetry, the novel, and others. Includes instruction in technical and editorial skills, criticism, and the marketing of finished manuscripts.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of quantum many-body dynamics in ultracold molecular systems, a frontier area in atomic and molecular physics where experimental and theoretical efforts are constrained by the extreme computational demands of accurately modeling correlated quantum states. Current state-of-the-art methods struggle to simulate the non-equilibrium behavior of large molecular ensembles with sufficient precision, particularly in regimes dominated by long-range dipole-dipole interactions and external field effects. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining tensor network algorithms with large-scale exact diagonalization to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for systems of up to 50 interacting polar molecules. The simulations will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize the construction and evolution of many-body wavefunctions, employing adaptive basis sets and symmetry-aware partitioning to reduce memory overhead. Key objectives include characterizing entanglement growth during collisional processes and predicting the stability of proposed quantum phases in optical lattice traps. The computational methodology will be validated against existing experimental data on Stark deceleration and rotational quenching in trapped molecular gases. Successful implementation will yield predictive models for controlling quantum state transitions in next-generation ultracold chemistry experiments, while the developed codebase will be optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures and disseminated as an open-source tool. This work directly supports national priorities in quantum information science by providing essential theoretical benchmarks for molecular qubit design. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on HPC systems will enable simulations at unprecedented scales, resolving critical open questions about the role of many-body correlations in molecular quantum dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time customer interaction systems within banking and financial support services, where conventional models struggle to balance scalability, personalization, and regulatory compliance. The increasing volume of digital transactions, coupled with demands for hyper-personalized financial advice, exposes critical bottlenecks in legacy systems. This study proposes the development of a dynamic, AI-driven interaction framework that optimizes customer engagement by integrating natural language processing (NLP), sentiment analysis, and reinforcement learning (RL). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train deep neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets of anonymized customer interactions, financial product metadata, and real-time market signals. Parallelized simulations will model diverse customer personas and interaction scenarios to refine RL policies, while GPU-accelerated inference pipelines will test low-latency response generation in simulated environments. The computational workflow includes federated learning to address data privacy constraints and graph-based analytics to map customer needs to evolving financial products. Expected outcomes include a scalable system architecture capable of reducing median service latency by 40-60% while maintaining compliance with financial regulations, as well as novel metrics for quantifying interaction quality in hybrid human-AI service pipelines. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational linguistics, behavioral economics, and distributed systems engineering, offering financial institutions a pathway to enhance customer retention and operational efficiency. The resulting models and simulation tools will be disseminated as open-source benchmarks to accelerate innovation in ethical AI applications for financial services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform a wide variety of customer services in banks, insurance agencies, savings and loan companies, and related enterprises. Includes instruction in communications and public relations skills, business equipment operation, and technical skills applicable to the methods and operations of specific financial or insurance services.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in computational methods for analyzing and optimizing the management of large-scale digital art collections and interactive media installations. As institutions increasingly adopt immersive technologies—such as augmented reality (AR), generative AI art systems, and dynamic digital archives—the need for efficient, scalable tools to curate, preserve, and adapt these works has grown urgent. Current approaches to metadata organization, user engagement analytics, and real-time content adaptation remain fragmented, often relying on underpowered systems ill-equipped for the computational demands of high-resolution visual datasets and nonlinear audience interactions. The research will employ parallelized machine learning models to classify and predict trends in digital art consumption, coupled with agent-based simulations to model visitor behavior in virtual gallery environments. Additionally, GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines will be developed to test preservation strategies for ephemeral AI-generated artworks, which require dynamic recomputation to maintain integrity over time. By integrating heterogeneous datasets—including user interaction logs, environmental sensor data, and generative art source code—the project aims to establish a framework for adaptive resource allocation in media-rich cultural institutions. Outcomes will include open-source tools for real-time analytics in art management systems, benchmarks for computational preservation of generative works, and scalable models to optimize audience engagement metrics. This work addresses a critical gap in arts management infrastructure, where traditional methods fail to accommodate the technical complexity of contemporary digital media. Access to HPC resources is essential to process multi-terabyte visual datasets, train deep learning models on temporal behavioral data, and simulate large-scale virtual environments with low-latency interactivity—tasks infeasible on standard institutional hardware. The results will inform best practices for museums, galleries, and digital archives navigating computational challenges at the intersection of artistic innovation and technological sustainability.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec

cip_definition: Any instructional program in arts, entertainment, and media management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociopolitical and economic networks of medieval Near Eastern societies through large-scale integration of fragmented historical records. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional institutions—such as trade guilds, religious endowments (waqfs), and tribal alliances—shaped governance and cultural exchange across North Africa, the Levant, and the Arabian Peninsula between the 11th and 15th centuries. Existing scholarship relies heavily on localized case studies due to the sheer volume and linguistic diversity of primary sources, including Arabic chronicles, Geniza documents, tax registers, and traveler accounts. To overcome these limitations, the project employs computational text analysis, network modeling, and geospatial visualization. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to extract named entities, relational data, and transactional references from digitized Arabic, Persian, and Syriac texts, supplemented by structured archaeological datasets. Graph-based algorithms will map interactions between urban centers, nomadic groups, and religious institutions, while agent-based models will simulate the diffusion of administrative practices under varying environmental and political conditions. These workflows demand HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train multilingual NLP models, and iteratively compute network metrics across dynamic temporal layers. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking over 50,000 historical actors and locations, quantitative reassessments of state-tribe fiscal dynamics, and visual reconstructions of pilgrimage routes as vectors for ideological transmission. By bridging computational methods with historiographical inquiry, the project aims to establish scalable frameworks for transregional analysis while challenging Eurocentric periodizations of Near Eastern history.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: The increasing demand for home-based healthcare services necessitates innovative approaches to optimize care delivery and improve outcomes for homebound populations. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model patient-caregiver interactions, predict adverse health events, and simulate the impact of personalized intervention strategies. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven tools to support home health aides (HHAs) in dynamically adapting care plans to complex, evolving patient needs, particularly for individuals with multiple chronic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate retrospective patient data (electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and caregiver notes) with agent-based modeling to simulate care scenarios across diverse demographic and clinical profiles. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns in physiological deterioration, environmental risks, and caregiver response efficacy, with a focus on variables such as infection risk, medication adherence, and emergency recognition latency. Computational experiments will evaluate the effectiveness of hypothetical intervention workflows, including adjusted visit frequencies, task prioritization protocols, and real-time decision support systems for HHAs. The scale of data processing—encompassing millions of simulated patient-days across parameterized age, morbidity, and socioeconomic strata—requires parallelized computing architectures to achieve clinically actionable resolution. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for adverse event risk stratification and an open-source toolkit for generating optimized care schedules under resource constraints. By quantifying the relationship between caregiving variables and patient outcomes, this work aims to provide evidence-based strategies for training programs, ultimately reducing hospital readmissions and improving quality of life for homebound individuals. The project’s computational demands necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory systems to handle high-dimensional optimization and sensitivity analyses within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and support services for homebound disabled, recovering, or elderly people. Includes instruction in basic nutrition, home sanitation, infection control, first aid, taking vital signs, personal hygiene, interpersonal communication skills, supervised home management, emergency recognition and referral, geriatric care, and legal and ethical responsibilities.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the biomechanical and hydrodynamic principles underlying collective locomotion in densely schooling fish, focusing on energy efficiency and emergent group dynamics. While collective behavior is well-studied ecologically, the physical constraints governing rapid, coordinated maneuvers in high-density groups remain poorly quantified. This project addresses a critical gap by modeling fluid-structure interactions at unprecedented scales, combining individual-based agent simulations with 3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to resolve turbulence and vortex shedding effects across thousands of interacting bodies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute coupled simulations using an immersed boundary method framework, where each fish is represented as a self-propelled flexible body with tunable kinematic parameters derived from empirical measurements of Pacific herring (Clupea pallasii). The computational approach integrates machine learning-assisted optimization to identify hydrodynamic regimes that minimize individual energy expenditure while maintaining group cohesion under predation-like perturbation scenarios. Expected outcomes include: 1) quantification of scaling relationships between group size, spatial organization, and metabolic savings; 2) identification of vortex-mediated communication mechanisms that enable rapid signal propagation; and 3) development of open-source simulation tools for aquatic collective motion analysis. Results will advance fundamental understanding of evolutionary adaptations for group locomotion while providing bio-inspired design principles for underwater swarm robotics. The project’s computational demands necessitate sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for CFD resolution and parallelized parameter optimization across millions of agent configurations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the biology of animal species and phyla, with reference to their molecular and cellular systems, anatomy, physiology, and behavior. Includes instruction in molecular and cell biology, microbiology, anatomy and physiology, ecology and behavior, evolutionary biology, and applications to specific species and phyla.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize workflow efficiency and client communication in veterinary reception environments through the analysis of large-scale operational data. Veterinary receptionists manage complex, dynamic workflows involving patient intake, client interactions, and administrative coordination, yet existing tools for workflow analysis in this niche field remain underdeveloped. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in appointment scheduling bottlenecks, client wait-time dissatisfaction, and miscommunication risks arising from inconsistent terminology use in client-facing interactions. Using anonymized datasets from 15 veterinary clinics—including timestamps, service codes, free-text client communications, and staff activity logs—we will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze communication efficacy and graph-based network modeling to simulate workflow scenarios. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets and running iterative agent-based simulations that test the impact of proposed interventions, such as dynamic scheduling algorithms or standardized communication templates. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for identifying high-risk workflow configurations, (2) a veterinary-specific NLP toolkit to assess clarity in client-staff exchanges, and (3) open-source simulation software tailored to small-animal practice logistics. By integrating computational social science methods with veterinary administrative practices, this work aims to establish evidence-based protocols that reduce operational inefficiencies while maintaining compliance with animal care regulations. The project bridges a gap in applied computational research for non-clinical veterinary support systems, offering scalable tools adaptable to diverse practice environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, veterinary technicians, or veterinarians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in veterinary office and animal care facility procedures, veterinary terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of neural circuit dynamics underlying adaptive and maladaptive behaviors, with a focus on anxiety-related disorders and addiction. A central challenge in behavioral neuroscience is characterizing how distributed neural populations encode, integrate, and transform information across timescales, particularly in scenarios requiring real-time behavioral adaptation. Current limitations in processing large-scale electrophysiological datasets (e.g., multi-region spike trains, local field potentials) and simulating biologically plausible neural network models hinder progress in mapping these processes. Our research integrates two computational approaches: (1) data-driven analysis of in vivo recordings from rodents performing decision-making tasks under threat-reward conflict, and (2) theory-driven simulations of cortico-limbic-striatal circuits using biologically constrained spiking neural network models. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale neural datasets through optimized machine learning pipelines for detecting cross-frequency coupling patterns and population coding dynamics. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated simulations will model circuit-level interactions between prefrontal cortical modules and subcortical structures under varying neuromodulatory states (e.g., dopamine, norepinephrine). This dual approach addresses critical gaps in relating cellular-resolution mechanisms to system-level behavioral outputs. Expected outcomes include novel computational frameworks for predicting stress-induced decision-making biases and identifying network resilience factors against addiction-related plasticity. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the need for parameter space exploration in neural models and high-dimensional data reduction—necessitates dedicated HPC support. By bridging mesoscale neural activity patterns with behavioral phenotypes, this work will provide foundational insights into the organizational principles of affective circuits while developing open-source tools for the neuroscience community. Results may inform future targets for neuromodulatory interventions in neuropsychiatric disorders, advancing experimental capabilities in computational psychiatry research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biological bases of behavior and psychological functioning, and their application to experimental and therapeutic research problems. Includes instruction in functional neuroanatomy, neural system development, biochemical neural regulatory mechanisms, neurological biophysics, memory storage and retrieval, physiology of cognition and perception, physiological bases of psychopathology and behavioral disorders, psychopharmacology, comparative psychobiology, molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, and specialized experimental design and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized facial treatment protocols by modeling the biomechanical and biochemical interactions between cosmetic formulations and heterogeneous skin phenotypes. Current facialist practices rely on heuristic, trial-and-error approaches to select products and techniques, limiting precision in addressing individual skin conditions such as elasticity variations, pore dynamics, and microbial imbalances. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-layered skin responses to therapeutic interventions, integrating domain-specific data from dermatology, cosmetic chemistry, and clinical esthetics. A hybrid computational pipeline will be constructed, combining finite element modeling of facial tissue mechanics with agent-based simulations of topical product absorption and microbiome interactions. Machine learning models trained on high-resolution imaging datasets (e.g., hyperspectral face scans, sebum secretion profiles) will predict treatment outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. The computational architecture will additionally incorporate regulatory constraints, including safety thresholds for pH gradients and antimicrobial agent concentrations as per licensing standards. By parallelizing stochastic simulations across thousands of skin phenotype permutations, this resource-intensive approach aims to establish quantitative guidelines for customizing treatment variables such as exfoliation intensity, emulsion viscosity, and massage kinematics. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool for facialists to preempt adverse reactions in sensitive clients and a generative design module proposing novel product formulations optimized for underrepresented skin types. This interdisciplinary integration of esthetic practice with computational biosimulation represents a novel paradigm in non-clinical skincare research, with potential applications in vocational training simulations and ethical AI-assisted treatment planning. The project’s computational demands necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time rendering of tissue deformation models and distributed memory clusters to manage stochastic optimization across high-dimensional parameter spaces.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and scalp with chemical and cosmetic preparations, and to function as licensed facial specialists in specialized and full service salons.  Includes instruction in facial surface anatomy; skin properties; skin decontamination and infection control; facial massage; facial makeup; facial wrapping; selection and application of creams, lotions, oils, and other chemicals and cosmetics; European and other facial techniques; client evaluation and care; applicable laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: The structural organization of cells within tissues is a fundamental aspect of anatomical development and disease, yet the mechanisms driving 3D cellular patterning remain poorly understood. This project seeks to investigate how mechanical interactions between cells and their extracellular microenvironment guide tissue morphogenesis in epithelial systems. A critical barrier to progress in this field is the inability to model dynamic, multiscale biomechanical processes across experimentally relevant spatial and temporal scales. To address this gap, we propose to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate emergent tissue-scale behaviors arising from subcellular force generation. The ABM component will parameterize individual cell behaviors—including adhesion, contractility, and polarity—using empirical data from live-cell imaging of avian and mammalian epithelial models. The FEA module will then resolve tissue-level stress distributions and strain energy landscapes, enabling prediction of deformation patterns during morphogenetic events. Computational models will be iteratively validated against experimental measurements of tissue stiffness and cellular rearrangement dynamics obtained via traction force microscopy. This work requires HPC resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of cell-cell interactions in multicellular ensembles (>10⁴ cells) and to solve nonlinear mechanical equations across heterogeneous domains. Successful implementation will provide novel insights into how local cellular mechanics propagate to orchestrate global tissue architecture, with particular relevance to congenital malformations linked to cytoskeletal defects. The resulting computational platform will be disseminated as an open-source tool for simulating tissue remodeling under physiological and pathological conditions, bridging a critical gap between cell-scale biophysics and organ-level anatomy.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_title: Cell/ Cellular Biology and Anatomical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cell/cellular biology and anatomical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Behavioral disorders in companion animals present complex challenges that often involve interactions between medical conditions, environmental factors, and learned behaviors. Current approaches to diagnosing and treating these disorders rely heavily on manual observation and trial-and-error adjustments to behavior modification plans, which can prolong patient distress and delay effective interventions. This project proposes to develop computational models that integrate multimodal data—including behavioral assessments, medical diagnostics, and pharmacological response profiles—to predict individualized treatment outcomes for animals with behavioral pathologies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large datasets derived from electronic health records, wearable sensor data tracking animal movement and physiological states, and genomic markers associated with behavioral traits. Machine learning algorithms will be trained to identify patterns linking specific medical conditions (e.g., endocrine dysfunction, neurological abnormalities) to behavioral presentations, while agent-based simulations will model the efficacy of behavior modification protocols under varying environmental and pharmacological conditions. A key innovation involves real-time optimization of treatment plans using reinforcement learning frameworks, which require iterative computation across high-dimensional parameter spaces. The computational demands of processing multimodal data streams, running parallel simulations, and training deep neural networks necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory systems. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide veterinarians in distinguishing medically driven behavioral issues from purely environmental causes, algorithms to recommend personalized behavior-drug therapy combinations, and a public dataset for benchmarking computational approaches in veterinary behavioral medicine. This work aims to reduce the average time to effective intervention, improve animal welfare, and establish a scalable framework for data-driven decision-making in veterinary behavioral practice.
cip_definition: Research on how to understand and treat the behavioral problems of animals, primarily through the application of behavior modification techniques to companion animals; may also involve diagnosis of medical conditions that can affect a pet's behavior, and the use of medication in conjunction with behavior modification therapy.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing dynamic decision-making for microbusinesses operating in volatile, hyperlocal markets—a niche intersection of computational social science, behavioral economics, and small business strategy. While traditional business administration frameworks emphasize static planning, microbusinesses (particularly those in informal sectors or gig economy platforms) require real-time adaptive strategies influenced by complex variables: fluctuating consumer sentiment, supply chain micro-disruptions, and spatially constrained resource networks. We propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework enhanced by machine learning to simulate decision pathways under multidimensional uncertainty at unprecedented resolution. The computational approach integrates heterogeneous datasets—including geolocated transaction streams, social media sentiment traces, and public infrastructure APIs—to model microbusiness ecosystems at granular temporal (minute-level) and spatial (neighborhood-scale) resolutions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for parallelized scenario testing across 10,000+ agent profiles while maintaining low-latency responsiveness for live data assimilation. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable risk-hedging framework that identifies optimal resource reallocation thresholds for microbusinesses in crisis scenarios, 2) predictive metrics for hyperlocal market stability using topological data analysis of ABM outputs, and 3) open-source tools enabling microbusiness owners to simulate personalized contingency plans via simplified computational notebooks. By bridging computational intensity with practical accessibility, this work advances both methodological frontiers in business resilience modeling and applied strategies for underserved small business populations. The resulting insights could redefine how microenterprises leverage real-time computational analytics without specialized expertise, potentially reducing failure rates in critical first-year operations by 18-22% based on preliminary pilot data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and manage independent small businesses. Includes instruction in business administration; enterprise planning and entrepreneurship; start-up; small business operations and problems; personnel supervision; capitalization and investment; taxation; business law and regulations; e-commerce; home business operations; and applications to specific sectors, products, and services.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making in dynamic, multi-stakeholder business ecosystems using advanced computational models. Modern enterprises operate in environments characterized by rapidly shifting consumer preferences, volatile supply chains, and complex regulatory landscapes, yet traditional analytical tools often fail to capture the interdependencies and nonlinear feedback loops inherent in these systems. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates agent-based modeling, stochastic optimization, and interpretable machine learning to simulate emergent behaviors across interconnected business networks. The computational approach will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to explore decision pathways under uncertainty, combined with graph neural networks to model cascading effects of strategic choices on suppliers, competitors, and consumers. A novel aspect of this work involves embedding behavioral economics principles into learning algorithms to better approximate human decision biases in market interactions. The required HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations across parameter spaces encompassing millions of agent interactions, real-world supply chain topologies, and stochastic demand scenarios derived from multimodal data streams. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for scenario testing adaptive business strategies, quantitative insights into resilience trade-offs during systemic disruptions, and methodological advances in coupling economic theory with computational learning systems. This work bridges gaps between operations research, behavioral science, and data-driven strategy formulation, offering both academic contributions to complexity-aware business analytics and practical applications for enterprises navigating rapidly evolving markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to solve business challenges. Includes instruction in machine learning, optimization methods, computer algorithms, probability and stochastic models, information economics, logistics, strategy, consumer behavior, marketing, and visual analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling the dynamics of consumer decision-making in fragmented, hyperconnected markets, where traditional marketing analytics struggle to capture nonlinear interactions between micro-influencers, algorithmic recommendation systems, and real-time sentiment shifts. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of static, survey-based models to predict emergent purchasing patterns in environments dominated by short-form video platforms, decentralized social networks, and AI-curated content ecosystems. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose implementing large-scale agent-based simulations that integrate behavioral economics principles with deep learning architectures trained on multi-platform digital trace data. The computational model will simulate 10^6+ heterogeneous agents across parameterized cultural contexts, incorporating temporal network effects from social media APIs, psychographic segmentation clusters, and stochastic shock events mimicking viral content spread. Key methodological challenges include developing adaptive attention allocation algorithms that reflect neurocognitive limits in information processing and implementing GPU-accelerated causal inference techniques to isolate platform-specific effects on conversion pathways. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying brand resilience to information cascade disruptions and predictive benchmarks for budget allocation across hybrid human-AI influencer networks. By enabling real-time simulation of competing marketing interventions at unprecedented scale, this research aims to establish computational decision theater capabilities for strategic planners—addressing a critical gap in marketing science’s capacity to navigate post-platform consumer environments. The resource request specifically supports parallelized model validation against terascale datasets from partnered e-commerce platforms and comparative analysis of emergent market structures under varying regulatory AI transparency scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to undertake and manage the process of developing consumer audiences and moving products from producers to consumers. Includes instruction in buyer behavior and dynamics, principle of marketing research, demand analysis, cost-volume and profit relationships, pricing theory, marketing campaign and strategic planning, market segments, advertising methods, sales operations and management, consumer relations, retailing, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable econometric framework for analyzing high-dimensional time-series datasets to improve forecasting accuracy in macroeconomic and financial systems. Traditional econometric models often struggle with the computational demands of large-scale datasets, nonlinear dynamics, and structural breaks, particularly when applied to real-time policy evaluation or asset pricing. The research aims to address these limitations by integrating machine learning techniques with Bayesian econometric methods, enabling robust inference in environments characterized by non-stationarity and model uncertainty. Key computational challenges include estimating high-dimensional parameter spaces via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture nonlinear temporal dependencies, and conducting counterfactual simulations under multiple policy scenarios. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize MCMC sampling, optimize hyperparameter tuning for ensemble models, and backtest forecasts across heterogeneous datasets (e.g., FRED macroeconomic indicators, global equity markets, and central bank communications). Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for efficient Bayesian model averaging in Python, validated against benchmark datasets, and empirical results quantifying the trade-offs between computational complexity and forecast precision. The work will directly inform applications such as monetary policy impact analysis, systemic risk assessment in financial networks, and real-time nowcasting of economic indicators. By enabling the analysis of datasets with thousands of interdependent time series, this research will advance methodological innovation in econometrics while providing actionable insights for policymakers and financial institutions. The requested computing resources are critical to managing the memory-intensive demands of covariance matrix estimation, distributed gradient descent for RNNs, and large-scale Monte Carlo experiments, which are infeasible on standard workstations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of mathematical and statistical analysis of economic phenomena and problems. Includes instruction in economic statistics, optimization theory, cost/benefit analysis, price theory, economic modeling, and economic forecasting and evaluation.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the integration of biophilic design principles with urban microclimate resilience through advanced computational modeling, aiming to optimize human-nature interactions in high-density built environments. Traditional architectural approaches often rely on static environmental datasets or simplified simulations, limiting their capacity to address dynamic, multi-scalar interactions between vegetation, built form, and pedestrian-scale microclimates. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a parametric framework that simulates real-time feedback loops between biological systems (e.g., urban forests, green façades) and localized atmospheric conditions across diurnal and seasonal cycles. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with machine learning-driven plant growth models, the methodology will analyze how hybrid natural-engineered systems mitigate urban heat island effects while enhancing spatial experience. Key innovations include agent-based modeling of root-soil-structure interactions at the streetscape level and GPU-accelerated ray tracing to quantify perceptual metrics like dappled light patterns under moving foliage. The computational workflow will process LiDAR-scanned urban morphologies from five climate zones, iterating through 10^6+ design variants to identify configurations that balance thermal performance, ecological viability, and aesthetic value. Expected outcomes include an open-source plugin for environmental design software that enables architects to co-optimize biological and structural systems during early-stage design. By bridging gaps between landscape ecology, atmospheric science, and architectural practice, this research advances evidence-based strategies for climate-adaptive cities while demonstrating how HPC can transform traditionally qualitative design domains into data-driven decision spaces. Resource allocation will support large-scale parallel simulations requiring 12 TB memory capacity and GPU nodes for real-time visualization of 4D environmental interactions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design public and private spaces, indoor and outdoor, for leisure, recreational, commercial, and living purposes, and for professional practice as environmental designers and architects. Includes instruction in the design and planning of public and private open spaces and their relationship to buildings and other aspects of the built environment; facilities management; related aspects of interior design and architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient, safe, and environmentally sustainable maritime operations necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize vessel performance and navigation strategies. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to analyze hydrodynamic interactions, fuel efficiency, and route optimization for commercial vessels operating in dynamic ocean environments. A critical challenge lies in integrating real-time environmental data—such as wave spectra, currents, and weather patterns—with vessel-specific parameters, including hull design, propulsion systems, and cargo loads, to model complex maritime scenarios. Traditional methods often rely on static models or simplified assumptions, limiting their predictive accuracy under variable conditions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale, multi-physics simulations using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning (ML) algorithms. The CFD component will resolve turbulent flow around vessel hulls and propellers at high spatial resolution, while ML models trained on historical voyage data will predict optimal speed profiles and routing adjustments to minimize fuel consumption and emissions. The simulations will incorporate stochastic environmental inputs to assess operational risks and resilience in diverse scenarios. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC clusters, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks associated with iterative parameter testing and ensemble forecasting. Expected outcomes include validated models for decision support systems that enable real-time operational adjustments, reducing fuel costs by an estimated 10–15% and greenhouse gas emissions by 8–12% per voyage. This work will directly inform maritime training curricula and industry best practices, bridging gaps between theoretical naval architecture and practical fleet management. The computational infrastructure will also support future research in autonomous vessel navigation and adaptive marine energy systems, aligning with global efforts to decarbonize maritime transport.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as captains, executive officers, engineers and ranking mates on commercially licensed inland, coastal and ocean-going vessels. Includes instruction in maritime traditions and law, maritime policy, economics and management of commercial marine operations, basic naval architecture and engineering, shipboard power systems engineering, crew supervision, and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of integrated computational models for evaluating the multi-scale impacts of energy transition policies on environmental sustainability and regional security. The research addresses a critical gap in current energy and environmental policy analysis: the inability to dynamically simulate interactions between heterogeneous energy systems, climate change mitigation pathways, and socio-economic outcomes at subnational to global scales. The proposed computational framework combines agent-based modeling, spatially explicit life-cycle assessment, and machine learning techniques to analyze trade-offs and synergies among decarbonization strategies, including renewable energy deployment, fossil fuel phaseout, and carbon pricing mechanisms. Key challenges include processing multi-petabyte datasets spanning energy infrastructure inventories, satellite-derived land-use patterns, and climate projections, as well as resolving non-linear feedbacks between policy decisions, technological adoption, and resource availability (e.g., water scarcity constraints on clean hydrogen production). HPC resources will enable parallelized scenario testing across 10,000+ processor cores, utilizing optimization algorithms to identify policy portfolios that maximize emissions reductions while minimizing risks to food security and energy access. Expected outcomes include a first-of-its-kind open-source policy simulation platform capable of 1 km-resolution impact mapping, validated against historical energy transitions in 15 case study regions. Results will directly inform international climate negotiations and national adaptation plans by quantifying the equity implications of competing net-zero pathways. This work aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 7 (affordable clean energy) and 13 (climate action), providing critical evidence for balancing environmental protection with energy security in resource-constrained economies.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to climate change, energy policy, environmental economics, global sustainability, and security. Includes instruction in climate change, clean energy technologies, environmental policy, environmental law, environmental economics, food security, fossil fuels, renewable and sustainable energy sources, and water issues.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interactions between large-scale brain networks that underlie cognitive flexibility—the ability to adapt behavior in response to changing environmental demands. Cognitive flexibility is impaired in numerous neuropsychiatric disorders, yet the neural mechanisms driving these impairments remain poorly understood. A key challenge lies in modeling the millisecond-scale temporal dynamics and nonlinear interactions across distributed brain regions using high-resolution neuroimaging data. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets combining task-based fMRI, magnetoencephalography (MEG), and behavioral measures from 150 participants performing cognitive flexibility paradigms. Computational workflows will integrate dynamic causal modeling (DCM) to infer directed connectivity between prefrontal, parietal, and subcortical networks, combined with time-resolved graph theory analyses to characterize network reconfiguration patterns. These methods require iterative Bayesian parameter estimation and massive parallelization of network simulations across varying cognitive load conditions. HPC resources are critical for processing petabytes of spatiotemporal data, running computationally intensive permutation testing for statistical validation, and training recurrent neural network (RNN) models to map neural dynamics to behavioral outcomes. Expected outcomes include a mechanistic framework linking transient network states to flexibility performance, identification of biomarkers predictive of clinical flexibility deficits, and open-source tools for multiscale neural dynamics analysis. This work will advance foundational knowledge of adaptive cognition while providing scalable computational pipelines for future studies of network-level dysfunction in neurological populations. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated computations, large-memory nodes for in-memory data processing, and high-throughput storage for intermediate outputs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the neural mechanisms underlying cognition.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on Albanian linguistic diversity and dialectal variation. The Albanian language features two primary dialects, Gheg and Tosk, which exhibit distinct phonological, morphological, and syntactic characteristics. Traditional comparative analyses of these dialects, as well as historical Albanian/Illyrian philology, have been limited by manual methods and small-scale corpora. This research aims to address these limitations by developing a large-scale, digitized corpus of Albanian texts spanning regional dialects, historical periods, and sociolinguistic contexts. Computational methods, including machine learning-driven dialect classification, phonetic alignment algorithms, and probabilistic models of syntactic change, will be applied to analyze patterns of divergence and convergence between Gheg and Tosk, as well as their diachronic evolution. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of textual and audio data, train deep neural networks for dialect identification, and run parallelized simulations of language change under varying sociocultural parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access digital repository of annotated Albanian dialectal data, (2) computational tools for automatic dialect classification and philological analysis, and (3) novel insights into the dynamics of language variation in underrepresented Albanian-speaking communities. These resources will support pedagogical applications, inform policy for language preservation, and enhance interdisciplinary collaborations in corpus linguistics and NLP for low-resource languages. By integrating computational rigor with Albanian philological expertise, this project bridges a critical gap in Balkan linguistic studies while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Albanian language. Includes instruction in Albanian/Illyrian philology; Ghegg and Tosk dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in postmortem interval (PMI) estimation and ecological impact modeling within funeral service and mortuary science. Traditional PMI determination relies on qualitative assessments of decomposition stages, which are prone to inaccuracies due to dynamic interactions between biological, environmental, and anthropogenic factors. Current models inadequately account for multivariate influences such as microbial community succession, soil biogeochemistry, climate variability, and embalming fluid interactions, limiting their forensic and ecological utility. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate decomposition as a complex adaptive system. The ABM module will map microbial consortia dynamics and tissue breakdown pathways under varying embalming protocols, while FEA will model heat transfer, fluid diffusion, and soil moisture gradients in burial environments. A neural network trained on multispectral imaging data from controlled decomposition studies will correlate observable tissue changes with simulated biochemical trajectories. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from longitudinal cadaver decomposition studies, environmental sensor arrays, and historical forensic case records. Validated models will be deployed as open-access tools for mortuary educators and forensic practitioners to refine PMI estimation, optimize green burial site management, and predict embalming efficacy in diverse climates. Anticipated outcomes include a novel taxonomy of decomposition pathways indexed to regional ecosystems, quantitative metrics for evaluating burial practice sustainability, and a predictive platform for mitigating public health risks in mass fatality scenarios. By bridging mortuary science with computational biology and environmental engineering, this work establishes a foundation for data-driven innovation in an industry critical to public welfare yet underrepresented in computational research.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, General.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals for careers in the funeral service industry and for licensure as funeral service directors or morticians.  Includes instruction in the basic elements of mortuary science and the business, counseling, and operational aspects of funeral service.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational philological research on the evolution of Hebrew morphosyntactic patterns across historical periods. The core challenge lies in analyzing large-scale textual corpora spanning Biblical Hebrew (including divergent pre- and post-exilic dialects) and Modern Hebrew, which require intensive processing to detect subtle linguistic shifts obscured by traditional manual methods. We propose a mixed-methods approach combining rule-based morphological parsers with transformer-based language models to automate the identification of syntactic and lexical features across 3,000+ digitized texts, including understudied post-biblical manuscripts and modern speech corpora. Computational workflows will parallelize feature extraction, train diachronic language models using temporal holdout validation, and apply phylogenetic algorithms to model dialectal divergence. A key innovation involves adapting semisupervised learning to address data sparsity in transitional-era Hebrew materials, where limited annotated training data hinders existing NLP tools. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as aligning variant-rich biblical manuscript traditions at the token level and simulating linguistic change under sociocultural parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated Hebrew syntactic constructions across eras, (2) quantitative evidence resolving scholarly debates about the chronology of specific grammatical changes (e.g., the loss of waw-consecutive forms), and (3) open-source tools for dialectometric analysis of Semitic languages. By enabling previously infeasible macro-scale comparisons, this work will advance understanding of Hebrew’s historical trajectory while developing computational methods transferable to other under-resourced languages. The requested resources directly support the program’s mandate to bridge traditional philology with contemporary computational applications in linguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hebrew language. Includes instruction in philology; Biblical Hebrew (including Pre- and Post-Exilic scripts); Modern Hebrew; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in global apparel supply chains, which contribute to overproduction, resource waste, and environmental degradation. Current models often fail to dynamically integrate real-time consumer behavior data with sustainability metrics, resulting in misaligned production cycles and excess inventory. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that optimizes textile distribution and production planning by synthesizing multi-dimensional datasets, including social media trends, historical sales, carbon footprint analyses, and regional socioeconomic factors. The computational approach employs machine learning algorithms to forecast demand fluctuations, coupled with multi-objective optimization techniques to balance cost efficiency, ethical labor practices, and ecological impact. Agent-based modeling will simulate decentralized decision-making across supply chain stakeholders, from manufacturers to consumers, to evaluate emergent outcomes under varying policy and market conditions. By leveraging parallelized computing architectures, the project will process terabyte-scale datasets and iteratively refine models to account for real-world complexity, such as geopolitical disruptions or shifting consumer preferences. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for reducing textile waste by 15-30% in simulated scenarios, identifying region-specific strategies for circular economy adoption, and generating adaptive frameworks for responsive production scaling. This work aligns with the psychological and social dimensions of consumer needs emphasized in apparel and textiles research, while advancing computational methodologies tailored to the unique challenges of non-engineering domains. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of sustainability variables and enabling rapid scenario testing, which traditional single-node systems cannot support. Successful implementation will provide a replicable model for data-driven decision-making in apparel industries, promoting economically viable transitions to sustainable practices.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the development of textile products and their distribution and use in terms of the psychological, social, economic, and physical needs of consumers. Includes instruction in the production, distribution, marketing, and end use of various apparel and textile products.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize and automate the analysis of legal administrative workflows, with a focus on identifying inefficiencies in document management, case tracking, and compliance verification within law offices. While legal administrative systems are critical to operational efficacy, their workflows often rely on manual or semi-automated processes that lack scalability and adaptability to evolving regulatory requirements. The research problem centers on modeling the complex interdependencies between legal procedural rules, document metadata, and administrative task sequences, which existing commercial software frequently handles through rigid, predefined templates. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on heterogeneous datasets comprising anonymized legal case files, timekeeping records, and jurisdictional procedural guidelines. Key computational methods include graph-based neural networks to map task dependencies and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to classify legal document types and extract context-sensitive deadlines. The project will also employ agent-based simulations to stress-test workflow adaptations under varying caseloads and regulatory scenarios. By parallelizing these processes across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce model training times from weeks to days, enabling iterative refinement of predictive algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for dynamic workflow optimization, capable of recommending context-aware task prioritization and compliance alerts tailored to specific legal practice areas. This work bridges computational efficiency with legal administrative praxis, offering a novel pathway to enhance productivity while maintaining rigorous adherence to ethical and procedural standards. The resource request directly supports scalability challenges inherent in processing legally sensitive, text-heavy datasets, which exceed the capabilities of typical office computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as legal office managers, special assistants, and legal secretaries. Includes instruction in office management, secretarial science, principles of U.S. or Canadian law, legal terminology and documentation, legal research, legal software applications, law office procedures, record-keeping, billing, applicable policies and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of gendered narratives in Japanese visual and textual media from the post-war period (1945–2000). While existing scholarship has qualitatively examined gender representation in specific media forms, such as film or literature, large-scale computational studies remain scarce due to the technical challenges of processing multilingual, multimodal datasets. This research addresses this gap by integrating natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to systematically map shifts in gender tropes, semantic associations, and visual motifs across a corpus of 50,000+ digitized texts (novels, newspapers, film scripts) and 20,000+ images (film stills, manga panels, advertisements). Computational methods will include transformer-based models fine-tuned for classical and modern Japanese text analysis, clustering algorithms to identify temporal patterns in gendered terminology, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to quantify compositional trends in visual media (e.g., spatial positioning of characters, color symbolism). The HPC environment is critical for training custom models on heterogeneous data, which requires parallelized processing of high-resolution images and context-aware NLP tasks across decades of evolving linguistic conventions. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible dataset of annotated media excerpts with metadata, (2) visualizations tracking the relationship between gendered discourse and socio-cultural events (e.g., economic shifts, feminist movements), and (3) a methodological framework for interdisciplinary computational analysis in area studies. By revealing systemic patterns in cultural production, this project aims to deepen understanding of how media both reflected and shaped gender norms in modern Japan, while demonstrating the value of HPC-driven approaches for humanities scholarship. Results will inform ongoing debates about the role of media in cultural memory and identity formation.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Japan, and related island groups and coastal neighbors.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling dynamic protein interaction networks underlying cellular signaling processes, a critical gap in systems biology that limits predictive understanding of disease mechanisms and therapeutic targeting. Current methods struggle to integrate time-resolved experimental data with structural and kinetic parameters at scale, particularly for cell-type-specific networks involving thousands of proteins. We propose developing a scalable computational framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with parallelized molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to predict context-dependent interaction kinetics. The framework will leverage existing proteomic datasets and biophysical models to train GNNs on hierarchical network features, while MD simulations parameterize energy landscapes for key interactions using enhanced sampling techniques. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) distributed training of multi-scale GNN architectures across GPU nodes, (2) ensemble MD simulations requiring >10,000 core-hours per network state, and (3) Bayesian optimization of network parameters through massively parallel sampling. The integrated pipeline will be validated against single-cell signaling datasets from published perturbation experiments. Successful implementation will produce the first open-source platform capable of simulating cell-state-specific protein interaction networks at kinetic resolution, enabling researchers to predict how genetic variants or drug candidates alter signaling flux. This resource will advance computational biology by bridging network-scale modeling with atomistic detail, with applications to precision medicine and therapeutic discovery. Allocation of 200,000 CPU-core hours and 10,000 GPU-hours will support method development, large-scale validation runs, and community tool deployment through our institutional bioinformatics portal.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer-based technologies and services to biological, biomedical, and biotechnology research. Includes instruction in algorithms, network architecture, principles of software design, human interface design, usability studies, search strategies, database management and data mining, digital image processing, computer graphics and animation, CAD, computer programming, and applications to experimental design and analysis and to specific quantitative, modeling, and analytical studies in the various biological specializations.

abstract: Forest ecosystems face increasing pressures from climate change, invasive species, and shifting disturbance regimes, necessitating advanced predictive tools to inform sustainable management strategies. Current approaches often lack the spatial resolution, temporal scope, or integration of multi-scale processes required to model complex forest dynamics under uncertainty. This project proposes to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating forest growth, disturbance interactions, and management outcomes across heterogeneous landscapes. The research will integrate multi-source remote sensing data (LiDAR, hyperspectral, and satellite imagery), climate projections, and field-based forest inventory datasets to parameterize process-based ecological models. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify patterns in historical disturbance regimes, while agent-based models will simulate forest management interventions, wildfire spread, and pest outbreaks at scales ranging from individual stands to regional landscapes. Computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to conduct sensitivity analyses and scenario testing across diverse climate pathways and management strategies. The resulting models aim to quantify trade-offs between timber production, carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and disturbance mitigation objectives. By enabling near-real-time analysis of large geospatial datasets and complex ecological interactions, this HPC resource allocation will directly support the development of adaptive management tools for public and private forest stakeholders. Anticipated outcomes include optimized harvest scheduling algorithms under climate uncertainty, improved risk assessment frameworks for wildfire-prone ecosystems, and spatially explicit maps of forest resilience indicators. These outputs will advance the integration of computational ecology into forest resources management while providing scalable methodologies for addressing pressing challenges in natural resource conservation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of forestry and natural resources management to the administration of forest lands and related resources. Includes instruction in silviculture, forest mensuration, forest protection, inventorying, biometrics, geographic information systems, remote sensing, photogrammetry, forest policy and economics, forest land use planning, fire protection and management, and related administrative skills.

abstract: Agroecological systems are critical for addressing global food security and environmental sustainability, yet optimizing these systems under dynamic climatic and socioeconomic conditions remains a formidable challenge. Current empirical approaches often fail to capture the complex interactions between crop physiology, soil biogeochemistry, pest dynamics, and farm management decisions at relevant spatiotemporal scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize multifunctional agroecosystems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate process-based crop models (e.g., APSIM), soil nutrient cycling algorithms, and agent-based representations of pest populations within a unified simulation environment. Machine learning techniques will be applied to parameterize models using heterogeneous datasets spanning long-term field trials, remote sensing products, and IoT sensor networks from experimental farms. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations across diverse climate scenarios (CMIP6 projections) and management regimes to identify robust strategies that balance yield stability, nitrogen use efficiency, and carbon sequestration potential. A novel multi-agent system will simulate farmer decision-making processes under evolving market and policy constraints.
