Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of tradeoffs between regenerative practices and short-term productivity, (2) spatially explicit recommendations for cover crop integration and pest suppression planting schedules, and (3) open-source tools for participatory design of climate-resilient polycultures. By resolving nonlinear interactions between biophysical and human dimensions at unprecedented scales, this work will advance computational agroecology while directly supporting extension programs aimed at reducing synthetic input dependency in row-crop systems. The requested computing resources are essential for managing petabyte-scale simulation outputs and implementing genetic optimization algorithms across high-dimensional parameter spaces.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: The growing complexity of air transportation systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address inefficiencies in air traffic management (ATM), environmental impact mitigation, and operational resilience. This project seeks to develop a scalable, high-fidelity simulation framework to model dynamic air traffic patterns, optimize routing under uncertainty, and evaluate the systemic effects of emerging technologies such as urban air mobility (UAM) and AI-driven decision support systems. Current methodologies lack the resolution to capture real-time interactions among thousands of aircraft, weather systems, and ground infrastructure, particularly in congested airspace. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning to analyze multi-agent decision-making, stochastic disruptions, and network-wide cascading effects. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parallelize simulations across diverse scenarios, process large-scale ADS-B and weather datasets, and train deep reinforcement learning models for adaptive traffic flow optimization. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for real-time rendering of 3D airspace interactions and employ distributed memory architectures to simulate continental-scale traffic over 24-hour cycles. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source ATM simulation toolkit, predictive metrics for congestion and emissions hotspots, and policy recommendations for integrating UAM into existing airspace. By enabling granular analysis of operational trade-offs, this work aims to reduce flight delays by an estimated 10–15%, lower fuel consumption through optimized climb/descent profiles, and inform FAA NextGen infrastructure upgrades. The requested resources will directly support 8 research personnel and 3 collaborative initiatives with aviation authorities, advancing both academic research and industry applications in sustainable air transportation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in aviation and air transportation services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize decentralized entrepreneurial ecosystems, focusing on the dynamic interplay between resource scarcity, institutional trust, and innovation outcomes in emerging markets. Traditional entrepreneurial studies often prioritize firm-level strategies or macroeconomic policies, yet lack granular computational frameworks to simulate how micro-level interactions among entrepreneurs, informal networks, and resource providers shape systemic resilience. The core research problem lies in understanding how decentralized allocation mechanisms—such as peer-to-peer resource sharing or blockchain-based trust systems—can mitigate structural bottlenecks in environments with limited institutional support. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with reinforcement learning, the project will simulate multi-agent ecosystems where entrepreneurs adaptively negotiate resource access under constraints like liquidity shortages, geopolitical instability, and asymmetric information. The computational approach integrates heterogeneous datasets, including transactional records from fintech platforms, social network analyses of entrepreneurial hubs in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, and experimental behavioral economics data. HPC resources are critical to scaling simulations to encompass 10^5–10^6 agents with real-world temporal and spatial granularity, enabling sensitivity analyses of policy interventions (e.g., tokenized incentive systems) across diverse regulatory regimes. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to identify optimal resource allocation protocols for policymakers and a decision-support tool for entrepreneurs operating in institutionally fragmented markets. By bridging computational social science, distributed systems design, and entrepreneurial theory, this work aims to advance a nascent interdisciplinary paradigm for fostering equitable growth in underserved entrepreneurial ecosystems. All models and datasets will be made open-source to catalyze further research in decentralized economic resilience.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform development, marketing and management functions associated with owning and operating a business.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying acupuncture point specificity and its systemic effects on neuro-immuno-endocrine networks. While acupuncture is empirically validated for conditions like chronic pain and inflammation, the functional basis of point specificity—why stimulating distinct anatomical loci produces divergent physiological outcomes—remains poorly characterized. Current limitations stem from the complexity of modeling dynamic, multi-scale interactions between mechanical stimulation, cellular signaling, and systemic responses. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element modeling of needle-induced tissue deformation, agent-based simulations of local immune cell behavior, and network analysis of gene expression datasets from pre/post-treatment transcriptomics. HPC resources will enable (1) multi-physics simulations of mechanotransduction pathways activated by needle manipulation techniques (e.g., lifting-thrusting), parameterized using MRI-derived tissue viscoelasticity data; (2) Bayesian network inference to identify causal links between stimulation parameters, cytokine release patterns, and autonomic nervous system activity metrics extracted from wearable device data; and (3) topology-based alignment of predicted signaling hubs with historically documented point combinations in classical texts. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of point-specific neuroimmune modulation, validated against prospective clinical data on inflammatory biomarker trajectories in osteoarthritis patients. This work will establish a quantitative bridge between traditional meridian theory and systems biology, while developing open-source tools for optimizing personalized acupuncture protocols. By resolving spatial and temporal dependencies in acupuncture’s systemic effects, the project advances precision applications of traditional medicine within integrative health paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of acupuncture, a Chinese system of health care and healing based on the use of pulse diagnosis, acupuncture point selection, and needle insertion, as well as herbs and other Asian treatment modalities. Includes instruction in basic Western medical sciences, Asian philosophy, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbs, diagnostic techniques, patient observation and communication, acupuncture points and point selection, acupuncture techniques, acupuncture treatment of disease, pain management, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The stability and sustainability of civil infrastructure and natural resource management systems are critically influenced by subsurface geological heterogeneity, which governs complex phenomena such as landslide dynamics, groundwater flow, and soil-structure interactions. Current predictive models often oversimplify these systems due to computational limitations, leading to uncertainties in hazard assessment and engineering design. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing high-resolution, multi-physics simulations of subsurface processes using advanced computational methods. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) modeling the coupled hydro-mechanical behavior of heterogeneous geological formations under dynamic loading, and (2) quantifying uncertainty in geohazard predictions through probabilistic inverse analysis. A combination of finite element modeling, discrete fracture network analysis, and machine learning techniques will be employed to integrate geophysical survey data, laboratory-scale material properties, and field-scale boundary conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatial and temporal scales required for these simulations, which involve iterative solving of nonlinear partial differential equations across domains exceeding 10^8 grid elements. Parallelized workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and ensemble-based uncertainty quantification frameworks. Expected outcomes include improved predictive tools for assessing infrastructure resilience to seismic and hydrological events, optimized strategies for subsurface resource exploration, and a publicly accessible database of validated simulation templates. This work will directly support safer and more cost-effective engineering solutions for critical challenges in transportation infrastructure, urban development, and climate adaptation, while advancing computational methodologies at the intersection of geoscience and civil engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and geological principles to the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems, including the geological evaluation of construction sites, the analysis of geological forces acting on structures and systems, the analysis of potential natural resource recovery sites, and applied research on geological phenomena.

abstract: Fungal pathogens pose significant threats to human health, agriculture, and ecosystem stability, with rising antifungal resistance complicating treatment strategies. This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying fungal pathogenesis and environmental adaptation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex datasets derived from experimental mycology. A key focus is elucidating how stress-response pathways in pathogenic fungi, such as *Candida auris* and *Aspergillus fumigatus*, modulate virulence and drug resistance under host-mimicking conditions. Traditional laboratory methods face limitations in scaling to analyze multi-omics data (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) generated from fungal cultures exposed to antifungal agents and immune system stressors. The project will employ computational workflows integrating molecular dynamics simulations to model fungal protein-ligand interactions, particularly those involving antifungal targets like lanosterol demethylase and β-glucan synthase. Parallelized pipelines will process high-throughput imaging data of fungal morphogenetic shifts (e.g., hyphal growth in host tissue), correlating structural changes with gene expression profiles. Machine learning models trained on phenotypic and environmental data will predict adaptive mutations linked to resistance. By deploying these HPC-driven approaches, the project aims to identify novel therapeutic targets, forecast resistance evolution, and characterize ecological drivers of fungal pathogenicity. Outcomes will advance understanding of host-fungal interactions, inform antifungal development, and support predictive frameworks for managing mycoses in clinical and environmental contexts. The requested computing resources are critical for handling terabyte-scale datasets, running iterative simulations, and optimizing predictive algorithms, enabling insights unattainable with standard laboratory infrastructure. This work bridges mycological research with computational innovation, addressing urgent challenges in microbial pathogenesis and antimicrobial resistance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of fungi, lichenous plants, eukaryotic microorganisms, myxomycetes, and plasmodiophorales and their relationship to diseases in higher plants, animals, and human beings as well as to pharmacologically useful products. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; histopathology; fungal growth and behavior; environmental mycology; antifungal sensitivity; mycoses; pathogens and pathogenesis; pharmacological properties; and computer and laboratory research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and visualizing large-scale participatory data generated through community-engaged art initiatives addressing environmental justice. While socially-engaged art has proven effective in mobilizing civic dialogue, existing methods struggle to synthesize complex, multimodal datasets (e.g., geospatial records, oral histories, ecological sensor data, and crowdsourced imagery) into cohesive artistic interventions. The research problem centers on creating accessible tools for artists and communities to interpret these datasets at meaningful scales, enabling data-driven storytelling that highlights inequities in urban climate resilience. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will design a pipeline integrating machine learning, geospatial analysis, and generative visual algorithms. Computational methods include training vision transformers to classify community-sourced imagery documenting environmental conditions, applying network analysis to oral history transcripts to identify shared themes, and simulating fluid dynamics models to visualize flood risk disparities across neighborhoods. These components will feed into an interactive 3D environment that artists and community members can adapt for site-specific installations. The project’s significance lies in bridging computational scalability with participatory art practices—offering new methods to amplify marginalized voices in environmental policymaking. Outcomes will include open-source tools for ethically embedding HPC workflows into socially-engaged art, a repository of annotated community datasets, and case studies demonstrating how computational analysis can deepen the impact of art-driven advocacy. By addressing technical barriers to processing heterogeneous, community-generated data, this work aims to expand the role of art as a catalyst for data literacy and environmental justice.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on using the arts to promote activism, civic dialog, community development, ecological and environmental awareness, or social justice. Includes instruction in community organizing, cultural criticism, social practice, studio art, and visual and performing arts.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) by addressing critical uncertainties in subsurface reservoir performance through high-fidelity computational modeling. Geothermal energy extraction is constrained by heterogeneous geological formations, dynamic fluid-rock interactions, and complex thermal-hydro-mechanical coupling, which challenge the efficiency and longevity of engineered reservoirs. Current simplified models often fail to capture multi-physics interactions at field-relevant scales, limiting predictive accuracy for energy output and reservoir lifespan. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate coupled thermal, hydraulic, mechanical, and chemical (THMC) processes in fractured geothermal reservoirs. The project will utilize finite element methods and discrete fracture network models to resolve pore-to-reservoir-scale phenomena, integrating machine learning techniques to optimize fracture network designs for sustained heat extraction. Parallelized simulations will employ open-source solvers (e.g., FEniCS, PyLith) adapted for geothermal-specific boundary conditions and material properties, validated against experimental data from lab-scale rock mechanics tests and field datasets from existing EGS sites. Key outcomes include predictive tools to quantify energy recovery under varying operational scenarios, identify fracture stimulation strategies that mitigate short-circuiting flow paths, and assess long-term geochemical impacts on permeability. By enabling high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations of decade-scale reservoir behavior, this work will directly inform the development of robust EGS designs, reducing exploration risks and improving economic viability for geothermal projects. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the required computational scale, with simulations targeting >1 billion grid elements to resolve fracture dynamics across spatially heterogeneous domains. Results will be disseminated through open-access datasets and integrated into geothermal technology curricula, supporting workforce training in next-generation energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of multiparametric design challenges in drafting and design workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize computational simulations and generative modeling processes. Current drafting tools often struggle with real-time rendering of intricate 3D models and dynamic simulations, particularly when handling material behavior predictions, thermal expansion analyses, or large-scale structural assemblies. These limitations hinder iterative design refinement and constrain innovation in sectors such as industrial manufacturing and architectural prototyping. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework integrating parametric design algorithms with finite element analysis (FEA) and topology optimization routines. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of design iterations across multiple variables, including material stress thresholds, geometric tolerances, and energy efficiency metrics. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict optimal design configurations, reducing manual recalibration efforts. Expected outcomes include a scalable simulation pipeline capable of resolving micron-level tolerances in complex assemblies and a 30-50% reduction in computational time for multiphysics analyses compared to current workstation-based workflows. The project will also produce open-source plugins for industry-standard CAD software, democratizing access to HPC-enhanced design validation for educational and small-scale industrial users. By bridging the gap between traditional drafting methodologies and advanced computational modeling, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for precision and efficiency in design technology education while supporting sustainable practices through optimized material usage simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance data-driven decision-making in human services program evaluation and policy design. The research addresses a critical gap in the field: the limited integration of large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., demographic records, service utilization patterns, economic indicators, and longitudinal public health data) to model community needs and optimize resource allocation. Current approaches often rely on static, siloed analyses that fail to capture dynamic interactions between socioeconomic factors, policy changes, and service outcomes. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing agent-based simulation models (ABMs) coupled with machine learning techniques to analyze multi-source datasets from three regional human services networks. The ABMs will simulate population-level behaviors and service access patterns under varying policy scenarios, while natural language processing (NLP) methods will extract insights from unstructured case management notes and policy documents. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC capabilities to process terabytes of structured and unstructured data, run parallelized simulations across diverse parameter spaces, and train predictive models for service demand forecasting. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable computational framework for evaluating equity impacts of human services interventions, 2) evidence-based recommendations for reducing disparities in service access across rural and urban populations, and 3) open-source tools to help agencies dynamically adjust resource allocation in response to shifting community needs. By enabling real-time analysis of complex, interconnected social systems, this work will provide policymakers with unprecedented capacity to test hypothetical interventions computationally before implementation. The requested resources directly support the program’s mission to integrate technological innovation with human services practice, ultimately advancing more responsive and equitable social safety nets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and provision of human and social services to individuals and communities and prepares individuals to work in public and private human services agencies and organizations. Includes instruction in the social sciences, psychology, principles of social service, human services policy, planning and evaluation, social services law and administration, and applications to particular issues, services, localities, and populations.

abstract: Ambulatory care faces growing challenges in optimizing patient outcomes and resource utilization, particularly in managing chronic diseases and preventing avoidable hospitalizations. This project seeks to develop predictive models for clinical deterioration and readmission risks using high-dimensional electronic health record (EHR) data from ambulatory settings. A key limitation of existing approaches is their reliance on static, manually curated variables, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between patient-specific factors, longitudinal treatment patterns, and social determinants of health. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework leveraging temporal graph neural networks (TGNNs) to model patient trajectories as time-evolving networks of clinical events, medications, and care interactions. The computational workflow involves preprocessing 5+ years of structured and unstructured EHR data from 250,000+ ambulatory patients, followed by distributed feature engineering and embedding of multimodal clinical data. Model training will require iterative optimization of TGNN architectures across hyperparameter spaces exceeding 10^6 configurations, necessitating GPU-accelerated computing and large-memory nodes. We will validate models against 30-day deterioration and 90-day readmission outcomes using time-stratified cross-validation, with subgroup analyses for high-risk populations (e.g., diabetes, heart failure). Expected outcomes include (1) risk prediction tools with ≥20% improved accuracy over current logistic regression baselines, (2) interpretable representations of critical transition points in ambulatory care pathways, and (3) open-source pipelines for temporal clinical data integration. This work directly supports the program’s mission by enabling proactive intervention in ambulatory settings through computationally intensive analytics that cannot feasibly run on local institutional clusters. The requested high-performance computing resources will empower clinically actionable predictions at scale while maintaining compliance with HIPAA-grade data security requirements for protected health information.
cip_definition: Research focused on Ambulatory Care

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing tacit knowledge transfer in decentralized, global organizations through advanced computational modeling of human-centric knowledge networks. While traditional knowledge management systems focus on codified information, the dynamic, context-dependent nature of tacit knowledge—critical for innovation and strategic decision-making—remains understudied at scale. The project will develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate multi-agent knowledge interactions across linguistic, cultural, and organizational boundaries, integrating natural language processing (NLP), graph neural networks (GNNs), and reinforcement learning. Computational models will process terabyte-scale datasets of cross-border collaboration patterns, communication metadata, and performance metrics from multinational corporations, accounting for latent variables such as psychological safety thresholds and power dynamics in virtual teams. The HPC infrastructure will enable real-time simulation of knowledge flow scenarios under varying organizational structures, allowing probabilistic analysis of intervention strategies to reduce information silos. Expected outcomes include a novel metric system for quantifying tacit knowledge vitality and predictive models for identifying at-risk innovation pipelines. This work bridges cognitive science, complex systems theory, and enterprise architecture, offering empirically grounded strategies for maintaining competitive advantage in distributed work environments. By leveraging parallelized agent-based modeling and large-language model fine-tuning at scale, the project advances computational organizational theory while providing practical tools for designing adaptive knowledge ecosystems in an era of hybrid work. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated training of domain-adapted transformer architectures and distributed simulations of 100,000+ node knowledge networks across multiple temporal scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of knowledge management in government agencies and corporations for the purpose of supporting stated organizational goals and objectives, and prepares individuals to function as information resource managers. Includes instruction in information technology, principles of computer and information systems, management information systems, applicable policy and regulations, and operations and personnel management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of nematode-host-environment interactions poses significant challenges in predicting the adaptive strategies of parasitic nematodes under dynamic climatic and agricultural conditions. This project seeks to address the critical gap in understanding how soil-dwelling plant-parasitic nematodes modulate their behavioral and metabolic responses to heterogeneous environmental stressors, such as fluctuating soil moisture, temperature gradients, and host root exudate profiles. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the multi-scale nature of these interactions, spanning molecular signaling, individual movement, and population-level dispersal. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate nematode navigation and decision-making processes in 3D soil microenvironments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallelization of millions of nematode agents, each governed by biomechanical constraints derived from microfluidic experiments and omics-based metabolic network models. FEA will resolve soil pore-scale hydromechanics, while reinforcement learning algorithms will train nematode agents to optimize resource acquisition and avoidance behaviors. The project will leverage existing genomic datasets from target species (e.g., *Meloidogyne incognita*) to parameterize species-specific phenotypic plasticity. Expected outcomes include a scalable simulation platform capable of predicting nematode infestation patterns under climate change scenarios, identifying vulnerabilities in pest life cycles, and informing precision biocontrol strategies. By bridging nematode physiology, soil biophysics, and computational science, this work will establish a novel paradigm for understanding parasitic nematode adaptation while providing open-source tools for the broader nematology community. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling the petabyte-scale output of coupled ABM-FEA simulations and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous spatial-temporal datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts.

abstract: This project seeks to address scalability and efficiency challenges in processing heterogeneous, high-volume datasets using advanced computational methods, with applications in domains such as real-time analytics and large-scale machine learning pipelines. While existing data processing frameworks offer foundational tools for transformation and retrieval, they often struggle with non-uniform data structures, dynamic resource allocation, and energy-efficient computation—gaps that become critical as dataset complexity and velocity increase. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a hybrid computational architecture integrating adaptive distributed computing, GPU-accelerated transformation pipelines, and machine learning-driven resource optimization. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to prototype and benchmark this architecture, focusing on parallelized data ingestion, in-memory processing of semi-structured data (e.g., JSON, XML, and graph-based formats), and dynamic workload balancing across CPU-GPU clusters. Key computational methods include the implementation of domain-specific query optimizers using constraint programming, neural network-based workload predictors trained on historical processing patterns, and fault-tolerant checkpointing mechanisms for long-running data transformation tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source framework for energy-aware, multi-modal data processing, (2) performance benchmarks comparing the proposed methods against Apache Spark and Dask in simulated high-volume scenarios, and (3) novel algorithms for minimizing data movement costs in heterogeneous computing environments. By enabling faster, more resource-efficient processing of complex datasets, this work will directly support researchers in fields requiring large-scale data integration—from genomic sequence analysis to IoT sensor networks—while advancing methodological innovations in distributed systems and computational resource management. The requested HPC resources are essential for validating scalability claims through petabyte-scale simulations and for optimizing cross-node communication protocols under realistic latency constraints.
cip_title: Data Processing and Data Processing Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master and use computer software programs and applications for inputting, verifying, organizing, storing, retrieving, transforming (changing, updating, and deleting), and extracting information. Includes instruction in using various operating system configurations and in types of data entry such as word processing, spreadsheets, calculators, management programs, design programs, database programs, and research programs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize water supply systems in urban environments, addressing inefficiencies in current plumbing infrastructure that lead to water loss, energy waste, and contamination risks. Despite advancements in pipe materials and installation techniques, systemic challenges—such as dynamic demand fluctuations, aging network configurations, and corrosion dynamics—remain poorly understood at scale. Traditional experimental methods are limited by cost, spatial constraints, and the inability to simulate multi-variable interactions in real-world systems. To overcome these barriers, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining fluid dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML), and network topology optimization. Large-scale hydraulic models will be developed using finite element analysis (FEA) to predict pressure gradients, flow rates, and sediment accumulation across heterogeneous pipe networks. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will train on synthetic and municipal datasets to identify failure-prone nodes and recommend adaptive routing strategies. These computational workflows will integrate real-time sensor data from pilot systems to refine predictive accuracy. The project requires HPC resources to manage the iterative simulation of city-scale water networks (10^4–10^5 nodes), parallelized ML training on terabyte-scale datasets, and multi-objective optimization under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital twin framework for plumbing system diagnostics, predictive maintenance protocols to reduce pipe leakage by 15–20%, and evidence-based guidelines for retrofitting legacy infrastructure. By quantifying trade-offs between water conservation, energy use, and material durability, this work aims to establish new standards for sustainable water supply management in the plumbing technology sector.
cip_title: Plumbing and Related Water Supply Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plumbing and related water supply services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Developmental-behavioral pediatrics faces a critical challenge in understanding the multifactorial origins of childhood developmental and behavioral disorders, which arise from dynamic interactions between genetic, environmental, and psychosocial factors. Current approaches often rely on static models or fragmented datasets, limiting the ability to predict individual trajectories or optimize interventions. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing a computational framework integrating longitudinal clinical data, neuroimaging, genomic variants, and environmental exposure data to model the emergence and progression of developmental-behavioral conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze heterogeneous datasets from 15,000 participants in the Developmental Health Cohort, including high-dimensional neuroimaging (resting-state fMRI, DTI), whole-genome sequencing, and real-time behavioral assessments collected via mobile platforms. Computational methods will include the implementation of deep learning architectures for time-series analysis to identify critical developmental windows, graph neural networks to model family-environment interactions, and Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify uncertainty in personalized risk predictions. A key innovation involves federated learning techniques to preserve privacy while harmonizing data across 12 clinical sites. The scale of data—requiring petabyte-scale storage and parallel processing of 10^6+ genomic variants paired with multimodal phenotypic features—necessitates HPC infrastructure for efficient GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for early identification of children at risk for developmental delays, (2) mechanistic insights into gene-environment interplay in behavioral phenotypes, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for adaptive intervention planning. This work will directly inform clinical guidelines for developmental surveillance and family-centered care strategies while advancing computational methods for precision pediatrics. The requested resources will enable processing timelines 40-60x faster than standard clinical workstations, making feasible the analysis of complex developmental trajectories that existing systems cannot resolve.
cip_definition: Research on how to assist in the prevention, diagnosis, and management of developmental difficulties and problematic behaviors in children, and in the family dysfunctions that compromise children's development; and to foster understanding and promotion of optimal development of children and families through research, education, clinical care, and advocacy efforts.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of hybrid human-artificial intelligence (AI) teams in organizational decision-making processes, leveraging computational modeling to address gaps in understanding how cognitive biases and algorithmic outputs interact in high-stakes business environments. While prior organizational behavior research has explored human team dynamics or AI tool adoption in isolation, the integration of autonomous AI agents as coequal decision-makers introduces novel challenges, including trust calibration, responsibility attribution, and emergent power structures. The research employs large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations to map how varying levels of AI transparency, human cognitive load, and incentive alignment affect group outcomes across iterative business scenarios (e.g., strategic pivots, crisis response). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations across multidimensional parameter spaces—including individual personality trait variations (modeled via neurocognitive frameworks), real-time learning feedback loops, and dynamic network topologies—at organizational scales (500–5,000 agent interactions per simulation). Machine learning techniques will analyze simulation outputs to identify critical thresholds where human-AI collaboration transitions from synergistic to adversarial, particularly examining how confirmation bias in human agents amplifies or mitigates algorithmic anchoring effects. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing hybrid team architectures, empirically grounded guidelines for AI role specialization, and computational evidence supporting interventions to reduce behavioral- algorithmic friction. This work bridges organizational psychology, behavioral economics, and complex systems science, offering actionable insights for businesses navigating the strategic integration of increasingly autonomous AI systems while advancing theoretical models of socio-technical organizational evolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior and motivations of individuals functioning in organized groups, and its application to business and industrial settings. Includes instruction in organization theory, industrial and organizational psychology, social psychology, sociology of organizations, reinforcement and incentive theory, employee relations strategies, organizational power and influence, organization stratification and hierarchy, leadership styles, and applications of operations research and other methodologies to organizational analysis.

abstract: Veterinary pathology faces critical challenges in diagnosing complex diseases through histopathological and molecular analysis, particularly when managing high-throughput data from diverse animal species. Current diagnostic workflows struggle with integrating multi-modal data—such as high-resolution histopathology images, genomic sequences, and clinical metadata—limiting the ability to detect subtle disease patterns or emerging pathogens. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enhance diagnostic accuracy, identify novel biomarkers, and streamline laboratory workflows. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning models to automate the classification of histopathological lesions in animal tissues across species, and (2) establishing a scalable bioinformatics pipeline to correlate genomic variants with tissue-level abnormalities. For the first aim, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will be trained on a curated dataset of >50,000 whole-slide images spanning common and rare veterinary pathologies, with HPC resources enabling rapid image preprocessing, distributed model training, and hyperparameter optimization. The second aim will utilize HPC clusters to process bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from diseased tissues, integrating these with histomorphometric features to identify conserved molecular pathways. Computational workflows will be containerized for reproducibility and deployed via a cloud-HPC hybrid architecture to support collaboration across veterinary diagnostic laboratories. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated lesion scoring, a public database linking genomic markers to veterinary disease phenotypes, and quality control algorithms to standardize inter-laboratory diagnostic criteria. By unifying computational pathology with veterinary medicine, this work aims to reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve early detection of zoonotic threats, and provide a template for data-driven resource allocation in clinical animal laboratories. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the project’s scale, including storage for multi-terabyte imaging datasets, GPU nodes for deep learning tasks, and high-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of diseased animal tissues and anatomic abnormalities. May included related research in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management and quality control.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic merchandising strategies in volatile retail markets by integrating real-time consumer sentiment analysis, supply chain resilience metrics, and competitive pricing dynamics. Traditional merchandising models rely on historical sales data and static supplier networks, limiting adaptability to rapid shifts in demand or disruptions. The research problem centers on creating a decision-support tool that enables buyers to simulate and evaluate purchasing strategies under uncertainty, incorporating emerging data sources such as social media trends, IoT-enabled inventory tracking, and geopolitical risk indicators. The computational approach combines three core methodologies: 1) graph neural networks to model complex dependencies between product categories, suppliers, and regional demand clusters; 2) multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate competitive market interactions; and 3) Monte Carlo optimization for risk-aware inventory allocation. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing petabytes of structured and unstructured data from 15+ sources, including live supplier APIs, satellite imagery of logistics hubs, and sentiment-coded customer reviews. Expected outcomes include a novel metric for "adaptive buying capacity" that quantifies purchasing flexibility across product lifecycles, and an open-source toolkit for scenario-based supplier negotiation training. The project will validate results against three years of transactional data from a multinational apparel retailer, with potential to reduce excess inventory costs by 18-22% in simulated crisis scenarios while maintaining 95% service-level agreements. By bridging computational social science with operations research, this work advances data-driven merchandising paradigms capable of responding to black swan events and microtrend simultaneity in post-pandemic markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional buyers of resale products and product lines for stores, chains, and other retail enterprises. Includes instruction in product evaluation, merchandising, applicable aspects of brand and consumer research, principles of purchasing, and negotiation skills.

abstract: Aging populations present complex oral health challenges influenced by comorbidities, polypharmacy, and physiological decline, complicating treatment outcomes in geriatric dentistry. Traditional clinical studies struggle to disentangle these multifactorial interactions, limiting the development of personalized therapeutic strategies. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between systemic health, pharmacological agents, and oral disease progression in older adults. Using a hybrid computational approach, we will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate biological and behavioral factors affecting oral health, coupled with machine learning (ML) analysis of longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and pharmacodynamic profiles. The ABM framework will parameterize variables such as salivary gland function, immune response attenuation, drug-drug interactions, and patient adherence, while ML algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers and risk clusters from heterogeneous datasets. HPC resources are critical to manage the computational load of iterative simulations across diverse geriatric cohorts and to train deep neural networks on high-dimensional data. Expected outcomes include predictive models for caries recurrence, periodontal disease exacerbation, and implant failure risk, stratified by frailty status and medication regimens. These tools will inform adaptive treatment protocols, optimize preventive interventions, and reduce iatrogenic complications in vulnerable populations. The project will also generate open-source computational workflows to support reproducibility in geriatric dental research. By bridging clinical expertise with scalable computational methods, this work aims to advance precision care paradigms for aging populations, addressing a critical gap in health professions research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of geriatric patients. Includes instruction in aging, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, geriatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and patient management.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing strategies in omnichannel retail environments through advanced computational modeling, addressing the challenge of real-time price adaptation across physical and digital sales channels. Traditional pricing models struggle to integrate heterogeneous data streams—such as real-time inventory levels, competitor pricing, localized demand signals, and customer sentiment from social media—into a unified decision framework. To bridge this gap, we propose a machine learning-driven approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate market dynamics at scale. Agent-based modeling will simulate consumer purchasing behavior under varying pricing scenarios, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in demand forecasting. Neural networks trained on historical transaction data and real-time API feeds will predict elasticity thresholds, enabling adaptive pricing recommendations. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including geospatial sales data, IoT-enabled shelf inventory updates, and unstructured social media inputs. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for optimizing margin preservation and inventory turnover in rapidly shifting markets, with validation against live A/B tests in partner retail networks. This research fills a critical gap in merchandising operations by enabling sub-hourly price adjustments responsive to micro-market conditions, advancing both computational economics and retail analytics. The HPC infrastructure is essential for reducing latency in model retraining and ensuring robustness in multi-agent simulations, which are infeasible on commodity hardware.
cip_title: General Merchandising, Sales, and Related Marketing Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in merchandising, sales, and related marketing operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) and breaches in aseptic technique remain critical challenges in modern operating rooms, contributing to patient morbidity, extended hospital stays, and increased healthcare costs. While current protocols in surgical technology emphasize manual adherence to sterility standards, dynamic intraoperative environments—including variations in personnel movement, equipment placement, and robotic device usage—introduce complex variables that are difficult to model using traditional observational methods. This project proposes a computational approach to simulate and optimize sterile field integrity in real-world surgical settings. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop a multi-agent simulation framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airborne particle dispersion, machine learning (ML) to analyze historical data on contamination events, and discrete-event simulation to evaluate the impact of workflow modifications. The model will incorporate real-world inputs from motion-captured surgical team movements, environmental sensor data (temperature, airflow, humidity), and robotic system telemetry from da Vinci surgical platforms. By simulating millions of intraoperative scenarios across diverse surgical specialties, we aim to identify high-risk configurations and generate predictive insights for sterility protocol enhancements. Expected outcomes include evidence-based recommendations for operating room layout optimization, personnel movement patterns, and adaptive sterile field monitoring systems capable of responding to dynamic environmental changes. This research bridges gaps between surgical technology practice, environmental engineering, and computational modeling, offering a novel paradigm for data-driven aseptic technique optimization. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the scale of 4D spatial-temporal simulations, training ML models on heterogeneous datasets, and achieving the resolution required for actionable clinical insights. Results will directly inform next-generation surgical assistive technologies and contribute to reducing preventable SSIs through computational risk prediction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and surgical nurses, to maintain, monitor, and enforce the sterile field and adherence to aseptic technique by preoperative, surgical team, and postoperative personnel. Includes instruction in instrument and equipment sterilization and handling, surgical supplies management, wound exposure and closure, surgical computer and robot operation and monitoring, maintenance of hemostasis, and patient and team scrubbing.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting ecosystem resilience to compounding stressors, including climate change, habitat fragmentation, and anthropogenic land-use shifts. Current conservation models often lack the spatial resolution and temporal scalability needed to simulate dynamic interactions between ecological processes and human activities across heterogeneous landscapes. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale ecological feedback loops. The model will integrate remote sensing data (Lidar, multispectral imagery), climate projections (CMIP6), and regional biodiversity datasets to quantify how habitat connectivity, species migration thresholds, and resource availability co-evolve under alternative management scenarios. Computational challenges include parameterizing probabilistic species distribution models across 10^6+ grid cells, parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations to assess uncertainty in climate-vegetation interactions, and optimizing memory usage for large-scale spatial graph analyses of habitat networks. HPC resources will enable iterative calibration against empirical data from long-term ecological research sites while maintaining sub-kilometer spatial resolution across watershed-scale domains (≥50,000 km²). Expected outcomes include (1) identification of priority conservation corridors resilient to mid-21st-century climate scenarios, (2) quantification of tipping points in ecosystem service provision under varying land-use policies, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive management of coupled human-natural systems. By resolving fine-grained ecological dynamics within computationally tractable regional simulations, this work will provide actionable insights for maintaining biodiversity hotspots and critical ecosystem functions. The proposed computational framework will advance predictive ecology by bridging gaps between process-based models and decision-relevant spatial scales, directly supporting regional conservation planning efforts mandated under the Global Biodiversity Framework.
cip_title: Natural Resources Conservation and Research, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources conservation and research, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The structural dynamics and energy transduction mechanisms of macromolecular assemblies remain poorly understood despite their central role in cellular function. This project seeks to characterize the conformational landscapes and transient interaction networks governing ATP-dependent macromolecular complexes, with a focus on systems implicated in membrane transport and redox-coupled proton pumping. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve rapid, stochastic transitions between functional states or quantify the collective motions driving allosteric communication. To address this gap, we propose multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations integrating microsecond-scale all-atom sampling with coarse-grained models, enhanced by Markov state analysis and machine learning-driven dimensionality reduction. These simulations will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to track energy propagation pathways in systems exceeding 500,000 atoms, including the vacuolar ATPase rotary motor and cytochrome bc1 complex. Quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) hybrid calculations will further map electron transfer kinetics in metalloenzyme active sites. The computational workflow requires GPU-accelerated MD packages (AMBER, NAMD) and custom analysis pipelines optimized for distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved mechanical coupling motifs in rotary ATPases, (2) quantitative models of proton motive force generation in respiratory complexes, and (3) predictive frameworks for engineering photoactivatable proton pumps. By elucidating how supramolecular architecture directs energy conversion, this work will advance fundamental understanding of bioenergetic regulation while providing mechanistic insights relevant to neurodegenerative disease pathways and synthetic bioengineering. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours enables statistically robust sampling of rare conformational transitions across biological replicates, a critical requirement for deriving principles applicable to diverse macromolecular machines.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: The development of advanced polymeric fibers with tailored mechanical and thermal properties requires a fundamental understanding of how molecular-scale interactions govern macroscopic behavior. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve the dynamic interplay between polymer chain orientation, crystallinity, and intermolecular forces under processing conditions, limiting the rational design of next-generation fibers. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and coarse-grained simulations that elucidate the relationship between polymer architecture, processing parameters, and fiber performance. The computational framework will focus on semi-crystalline polymers, including polyamides and polyolefins, simulating their behavior during melt spinning and post-drawing stages. Atomistic MD will model chain alignment and stress-induced crystallization under strain rates and thermal gradients representative of industrial processes. Coarse-grained models will extend these insights to longer timescales, capturing mesoscale morphological evolution. Additionally, machine learning interatomic potentials will be trained on ab initio datasets to improve the accuracy of interfacial interactions between polymer chains and additives, such as nanofillers or compatibilizers. The anticipated outcomes include predictive models linking molecular design to fiber strength, elasticity, and thermal stability, enabling computational screening of novel polymer systems prior to synthesis. These results will directly inform collaborative experimental efforts to optimize eco-friendly fiber production, reducing reliance on trial-and-error methods. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the need for parallelized simulations across multiple length scales, requiring significant memory and processing power to handle systems exceeding 1 million atoms and microsecond trajectories. This work advances the broader goal of sustainable materials innovation by accelerating the discovery of high-performance fibers for applications in lightweight composites, smart textiles, and biomedical scaffolds.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis, structure and properties of polymers with an emphasis on fibers. Includes instruction in polymer chemistry and synthesis, fiber and polymer physics and physical chemistry, the production, processing and properties of fibrous materials, and chemistry of dyes, finishes, and their processes.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize high-performance engine tuning and aftermarket modification processes, with the goal of reducing trial-and-error testing while improving power output, efficiency, and emissions compliance. Current methods for enhancing diesel and automotive engines rely heavily on empirical dynamometer testing and technician expertise, which are time-intensive, resource-limited, and often fail to account for multivariate interactions between fuel systems, exhaust flow dynamics, and engine control unit parameters. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining 3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of combustion chambers and exhaust systems with machine learning algorithms trained on dynamometer datasets. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of piston geometry, turbocharger configurations, and fuel injection timing across diverse operating conditions. Concurrently, finite element analysis (FEA) will model thermal and mechanical stresses in modified powertrain components to predict failure modes. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from partner automotive workshops, creating a feedback loop to refine predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include a decision-support framework for identifying optimal modification combinations, predictive maps for engine tuning under real-world load scenarios, and open-access simulation templates tailored to common aftermarket parts. This work will directly benefit technical education by providing students with virtual experimentation tools to study engine performance trade-offs, while offering industry partners reduced development cycles for performance upgrades. The requested computing resources are essential given the need for massively parallel simulations of transient combustion events and the iterative nature of machine learning model training on heterogeneous engine telemetry data.
cip_title: High Performance and Custom Engine Technician/ Mechanic
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to increase the power of diesel and automotive engines; enhance the performance of automobiles; and repair, service, and maintain high performance vehicles. Includes instruction in adding performance accessories; modifying powertrains; tuning custom engines, suspension, and exhaust systems; and using dynamometers and other diagnostic equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and manufacturing processes in upholstery through computational modeling and simulation, addressing critical challenges in material optimization, structural integrity, and ergonomic performance. Traditional upholstery methods rely heavily on empirical testing and iterative physical prototyping, which are time-consuming, resource-intensive, and limited in their ability to predict long-term material behavior under dynamic stress, environmental exposure, or repetitive use. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate the mechanical and thermal interactions of upholstery materials—including foams, textiles, springs, and composite fillings—under varied load and environmental conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution mapping, discrete element modeling (DEM) to analyze particulate filling dynamics, and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization algorithms to identify ideal material combinations. These simulations will incorporate multi-physics interactions, such as heat-moisture coupling in automotive seat fabrics or viscoelastic foam compression-recovery cycles in furniture, requiring parallelized computation to manage complex, nonlinear systems. The project will also leverage HPC to train neural networks on experimental datasets linking material properties to performance metrics, enabling predictive design frameworks. Outcomes include validated models for rapid prototyping, reduced material waste, and enhanced product longevity, directly benefiting industries reliant on custom or high-performance upholstery. Additionally, the computational workflows developed will be integrated into educational modules, equipping upholstery students with skills in digital design and simulation—a critical bridge between traditional craftsmanship and modern computational tools. By addressing both technical and educational gaps, this work aims to elevate the precision, sustainability, and innovation capacity of the upholstery field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install springs, filling, padding, covering and finishing on items such as furniture, automobile seats, caskets, mattresses, and bedsprings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social network evolution and its relationship to demographic change in urban environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations in modeling large-scale, longitudinal data. Traditional sociological studies of networks and demography often rely on static or small-scale datasets, which inadequately capture the interplay between individual mobility, life-course transitions, and macro-level population shifts. The research will develop and validate a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with demographic microsimulation to analyze how micro-level decisions—such as residential relocation or occupational changes—propagate through social networks, influencing broader patterns of segregation and community cohesion. The ABM will simulate heterogeneous agents with demographic attributes (e.g., age, education, migration status) across multi-decadal timescales, incorporating real-world urban census and geospatial data. A key innovation involves coupling network dynamics with machine learning techniques to iteratively calibrate model parameters against historical demographic trends, enabling probabilistic scenario testing. Computational demands are substantial: simulations will track millions of agents across thousands of time steps, requiring parallelized execution for parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses, and uncertainty quantification. HPC resources will also support the analysis of high-dimensional output data to identify tipping points in network fragmentation and resilience. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for sociodemographic modeling, novel insights into the feedback loops between individual agency and structural inequality, and evidence-based projections for policymakers addressing urban planning challenges. By bridging computational social science and demographic theory, this work aims to advance methodological rigor in studying population heterogeneity while addressing critical gaps in understanding how social networks mediate demographic transitions.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sociology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) results in complex, multifaceted disabilities that require interdisciplinary approaches to improve patient outcomes. Current clinical strategies for SCI management remain limited by incomplete understanding of injury heterogeneity, variable recovery trajectories, and the interplay between biological, biomechanical, and psychosocial factors. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multimodal datasets—including clinical records, neuroimaging, sensor-derived biomechanical data, and molecular profiling—into predictive models of functional recovery and treatment response. A key challenge lies in the high-dimensional integration of temporally dynamic data across scales, from cellular processes to patient-reported outcomes, necessitating advanced computational infrastructure. The research will employ machine learning frameworks, such as graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to identify biomarkers of neurological recovery and optimize personalized rehabilitation protocols. Concurrently, finite element modeling and computational fluid dynamics simulations will be applied to investigate cerebrospinal fluid dynamics post-injury, which may inform interventions for neuropathic pain and autonomic dysreflexia. These analyses require large-scale parallel processing capabilities and GPU-accelerated workloads to manage iterative model training and simulate multicompartmental biophysical systems. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for SCI data integration, validated predictive algorithms for clinical deployment, and mechanistic insights into secondary injury cascades. By enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, the requested HPC resources will directly support translational advances in SCI medicine, including the design of adaptive clinical trials and patient-specific neuroprosthetic interfaces. This work aligns with national priorities to reduce long-term disability burdens through precision rehabilitation, offering a scalable computational foundation for future studies in neurotrauma recovery.
cip_definition: Research on how to address the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and management of traumatic spinal cord injury and non-traumatic etiologies of spinal cord dysfunction, including related medical, physical, psychological, and vocational disabilities and complications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the biomechanical and cultural dynamics of dance movement across diverse traditions, addressing gaps in computational dance research. While dance is increasingly studied through interdisciplinary lenses, few projects systematically integrate large-scale motion capture datasets with cultural metadata to uncover patterns in movement semantics, kinetics, and historical evolution. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of processing high-dimensional movement data (e.g., from inertial measurement units and optical tracking systems) and linking it to qualitative cultural annotations, such as ethnographic records or Labanotation scores. Proposed methods include developing machine learning pipelines to classify dance styles, simulate biomechanical constraints in choreographic sequences, and model the diffusion of movement vocabularies across cultures using graph-based algorithms. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of motion data from over 1,000 recorded performances spanning ballet, contemporary, and traditional global dance forms, as well as agent-based simulations of choreographic decision-making under physiological and cultural parameters. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible database linking movement features to cultural contexts; (2) computational tools for choreographers to explore biomechanically sustainable movement sequences; and (3) quantitative frameworks for dance historiography, tracing how geopolitical factors shape embodied practices. This work bridges computational rigor with dance scholarship, offering new methodologies for preserving intangible cultural heritage and advancing cross-cultural dance analysis. The scale of data processing—requiring terabytes of storage and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve timely results, as traditional workstations lack the capacity to handle concurrent simulation, rendering, and analysis tasks.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to express ideas, feelings, and/or inner visions through the performance of one or more of the dance disciplines, including but not limited to ballet, modern, jazz, ethnic, and folk dance, and that focuses on the study and analysis of dance as a cultural phenomenon. Includes instruction in technique, choreography, Laban notation, dance history and criticism, and dance production.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling and optimization of ultrafast laser systems and nonlinear optical devices, critical challenges in laser and optical engineering. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve the complex spatiotemporal dynamics of high-intensity laser-matter interactions, particularly in emerging materials like metasurfaces and photonic crystals. Additionally, conventional computational tools lack the scalability to simulate multi-physics phenomena—such as thermal-optical coupling, nonlinear pulse propagation, and quantum noise effects—in integrated optoelectronic systems. To address these gaps, we propose a computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for electromagnetic wave propagation, stochastic models for photon-statistics analysis, and machine learning-assisted optimization of resonator geometries. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across laser wavelength, pulse duration, and material dispersion profiles while maintaining femtosecond-scale temporal resolution. Key objectives include (1) simulating nonlinear harmonic generation in quasi-phase-matched waveguides to improve terahertz radiation efficiency, (2) optimizing topology-designed optical cavities for low-threshold supercontinuum generation, and (3) modeling thermal dissipation in high-power vertical-external-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VECSELs). Expected outcomes include predictive design rules for compact nonlinear optical devices and validated multi-physics simulation protocols that bridge nanoscale light-matter interactions with macroscopic system performance. By enabling previously intractable simulations of ultrafast phenomena across multiple length scales, this work will directly support the development of next-generation laser systems for applications in precision manufacturing, quantum photonics, and secure free-space communications. The requested computational resources will accelerate parameter optimization cycles by 10–100x compared to existing cluster capabilities, critically enabling rapid iteration between simulation and experimental validation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of optical systems, lasers and related electronic devices. Includes instruction in wave theory and mechanics, electromagnetic applications, linear and non-linear optics, photon detecting, laser beam properties, directed energy, harmonic generation, optical systems, shielding and the design and implementation of related systems and equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of lithospheric dynamics and fault system interactions by developing high-resolution, three-dimensional computational models of crustal deformation in tectonically active regions. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting seismic hazards, as existing models often oversimplify the interplay between heterogeneous rock properties, stress accumulation, and multi-fault rupture propagation. We propose to implement a parallelized finite element framework that integrates geophysical datasets—including seismic tomography, GPS-derived strain rates, and fault geometry maps—to simulate deformation processes across spatial scales from meters to hundreds of kilometers. The computational approach leverages adaptive mesh refinement and visco-elasto-plastic constitutive relationships to capture both short-term seismic cycles and long-term tectonic evolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex fault networks at unprecedented resolution while incorporating probabilistic uncertainty quantification through ensemble modeling. Expected outcomes include new insights into stress transfer mechanisms between fault segments, improved estimates of maximum credible earthquakes for hazard assessment, and validation of hypothesized seismic gaps in understudied continental regions. The resulting models will be compared against paleoseismic records and modern geodetic observations to refine predictive capabilities. By enabling terabyte-scale simulations of coupled crust-mantle systems, this work will produce open-source tools for the geoscience community and inform infrastructure resilience planning in earthquake-prone areas. The requested allocation supports 1.2 million core-hours on GPU-accelerated nodes for matrix solvers and machine learning-assisted parameter optimization, addressing computational bottlenecks in multi-physics earth system modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and relationships between the solids, liquids and gases comprising it.

abstract: Neuromuscular disorders (NMDs), including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, muscular dystrophies, and congenital myopathies, exhibit significant clinical and molecular heterogeneity, complicating diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic development. A critical barrier to advancing precision medicine in NMDs is the integration of multi-modal clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data to identify robust biomarkers, subtype-specific pathways, and dynamic disease progression patterns. This project proposes to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets from international NMD cohorts, including whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal clinical assessments, and high-resolution muscle imaging. We will develop machine learning models to integrate these data, identifying combinatorial genetic modifiers, predictive signatures of disease trajectory, and patient-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. Computational modeling of neuromuscular junction transmission dynamics will be performed using molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate how mutations in ion channels or synaptic proteins disrupt signaling. These simulations require intensive parallel processing to resolve time-dependent conformational changes at microsecond scales. Additionally, generative AI approaches will be applied to synthesize in silico cohorts for rare NMD subtypes, augmenting statistical power for subgroup analyses. The HPC environment is essential for managing petabyte-scale data storage, enabling rapid iteration of deep neural networks, and executing computationally demanding simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for NMD progression, (2) mechanistic insights into mutation-specific pathobiology, and (3) open-access tools for multi-omics integration in neuromuscular research.
