By elucidating subtype-specific drivers of disease heterogeneity and accelerating therapeutic target discovery, this work will directly inform clinical trial design and personalized treatment strategies, addressing unmet needs in neuromuscular medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of disorders of nerve, muscle, or neuromuscular junction, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, peripheral neuropathies, various muscular dystrophies, congenital and acquired myopathies, inflammatory myopathies, and neuromuscular transmission disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in commercial vehicle operations and driver training, with a focus on optimizing safety, efficiency, and instructional outcomes. Commercial vehicle operators face complex demands, including dynamic route planning, real-time hazard response, and fuel efficiency management, while instructors require advanced tools to simulate high-risk scenarios and assess trainee performance. Current training frameworks and operational decision-support systems often lack the computational capacity to model large-scale, real-world variables such as traffic patterns, weather conditions, or vehicle telemetry data at sufficient fidelity. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale simulation platform integrating agent-based traffic modeling, vehicle dynamics analysis, and machine learning-driven risk prediction. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of fleet operations across diverse geographic and environmental conditions, coupled with probabilistic modeling of mechanical failures or driver errors. Additionally, generative AI methods will be applied to synthesize rare but critical scenarios (e.g., extreme weather, system malfunctions) for immersive virtual training modules. The computational workflow will process terabytes of historical telematics data, driver performance records, and traffic incident reports to identify risk correlations and optimize instructional content. Outcomes include predictive tools for route efficiency, personalized trainee assessment algorithms, and a scenario library for adaptive simulation-based instruction. By quantifying the impact of operational decisions and training interventions, this research aims to reduce accident rates, lower fuel consumption, and enhance the scalability of commercial driver education programs. The project will directly support curriculum modernization in commercial vehicle operator training, aligning technical education with data-driven advancements in transportation technology.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the Filipino/Tagalog language, with a focus on its morphological complexity and dialectal variations across regional and digital contexts. Despite the language’s widespread use and cultural significance, large-scale computational analyses of its structural features remain limited due to the lack of curated datasets and the resource-intensive nature of processing agglutinative morphology. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to analyze Tagalog’s morphosyntactic patterns, trace lexical evolution in literature, and map dialectal shifts in digital communication (e.g., social media, online forums). A hybrid corpus of historical texts, modern literature, and web-based sources will be compiled, requiring preprocessing of non-standard orthography and code-switching phenomena. Computational approaches will include neural sequence modeling for morphological segmentation, transformer-based dialect classification, and graph-based algorithms to track semantic changes in literature across time. These tasks demand parallelized processing, large memory allocation, and GPU acceleration to manage datasets exceeding 10 million tokens and train language-specific models. Expected outcomes include an open-access annotated corpus, a morphological analyzer for low-resource Tagalog variants, and visualizations of dialectal boundaries influenced by migration and technology. By enabling precise, data-driven insights into the language’s development and contemporary usage, this work will support pedagogical tools, language preservation efforts, and NLP applications tailored to Philippine contexts. The project underscores the role of HPC in addressing linguistic research challenges that are infeasible with traditional methods, directly contributing to the advancement of Filipino/Tagalog studies within global humanities computing.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the modern Filipino/Tagalog language as used in the Philippines. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive diagnostic tools for reading difficulties, with a focus on optimizing individualized intervention strategies for K–12 students. Despite decades of research, persistent challenges remain in efficiently identifying the root causes of reading struggles—such as phonological deficits, fluency barriers, or comprehension gaps—and aligning these diagnoses with evidence-based instructional practices. Current manual assessment methods are time-intensive, subjective, and often fail to scale across diverse learner populations. To address this, we propose a computational framework that integrates eye-tracking data, linguistic feature extraction, and machine learning models to automate and refine the diagnostic process. Large-scale datasets comprising reading performance metrics, gaze patterns, and demographic variables will be analyzed to identify latent patterns in reading behaviors. Neural networks will be trained to classify subtypes of reading difficulties, while reinforcement learning algorithms will simulate and evaluate the efficacy of hypothetical teaching interventions across varied student profiles. The computational intensity of processing high-dimensional eye-tracking data (sampled at 500Hz+) and iteratively training context-aware models necessitates HPC infrastructure for parallelized workloads and GPU-accelerated model optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable, open-source diagnostic platform that reduces assessment time and improves accuracy in pinpointing reading challenges, (2) data-driven insights into how specific instructional strategies correlate with progress across learner subgroups, and (3) generative models capable of proposing personalized lesson sequences for training scenarios in reading teacher education programs. By bridging computational analytics with pedagogical expertise, this work aims to equip educators with precision tools to transform assessment practices and tailor reading instruction, ultimately reducing disparities in literacy outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose reading difficulties and to teach reading programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to enhance the creation of adaptive, high-resolution digital illustrations through machine learning and real-time rendering, addressing the growing demand for dynamic visual content in client-driven contexts. Current illustration workflows often struggle to efficiently integrate complex client specifications—such as multi-style hybridization, contextual object placement, or material texture simulation—while maintaining artistic intent. We propose a two-phase approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources: first, training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on a curated dataset of 50,000+ annotated illustrations spanning historical and contemporary styles, material textures, and spatial compositions; second, implementing real-time neural rendering pipelines to enable iterative client-artist collaboration. The GAN architecture will utilize transformer-based attention mechanisms to parse textual and visual input constraints, requiring distributed training across multiple GPUs to handle the model’s 12-billion-parameter scale. Concurrently, physics-based simulations of traditional media (e.g., watercolor pigment dispersion, charcoal grain dynamics) will be optimized through parallel computing to generate texture libraries with microsecond temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for style-adaptive illustration generation, reducing revision cycles by enabling rapid prototyping of client-directed edits. This work bridges computational aesthetics and practical design workflows, offering empirical insights into human-AI collaborative creativity. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive rendering tasks, distributed model training, and large-scale user testing simulations—processes infeasible on local hardware. Results will be validated through partnerships with digital media studios and peer-reviewed benchmarks against industry-standard illustration tools, with potential applications in interactive book illustration, augmented reality design, and customizable asset generation for cross-platform publishing.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing food safety and shelf-life by modeling microbial dynamics in complex food matrices. Current approaches to predicting microbial growth, survival, and cross-contamination in multi-component food systems are limited by the inability of conventional computational tools to integrate heterogeneous datasets or simulate interactions at biologically relevant scales. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale, data-driven models that simulate microbial behavior under diverse food processing and storage conditions. The computational framework will integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles) with physicochemical properties of food matrices and environmental variables (e.g., temperature, pH, water activity) using agent-based modeling and hybrid machine learning techniques. These simulations will map microbial community resilience, pathogen virulence, and spoilage organism activity across spatial and temporal scales, enabling predictions of contamination risks in scenarios such as thermal processing, packaging, and cold-chain logistics. HPC resources are essential for handling the computational complexity of modeling thousands of microbial species interacting within dynamic food microenvironments, requiring parallelized simulations and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to identify processing parameters that minimize pathogen persistence while preserving nutritional quality, as well as decision-support systems for tailoring preservation strategies to food type and supply chain context. This work will advance fundamental understanding of microbial ecology in food systems while directly addressing industry needs to reduce waste and improve safety. The resulting open-source computational platform will serve as a resource for the broader food science community, enabling rapid hypothesis testing and innovation in food technology development.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in food sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Chinese linguistic diversity and classical literary texts. The research problem centers on the vast scale and structural complexity of Chinese dialects and premodern texts, which hinder systematic analysis using conventional methods. While dialectology and textual studies have long relied on manual annotation or small-scale computational tools, the volume of data—including digitized historical texts, spoken dialect corpora, and cross-regional linguistic datasets—demands advanced computational infrastructure to enable large-scale pattern recognition, phonetic modeling, and semantic mapping. The project will employ neural language models optimized for classical Chinese and dialectal speech, alongside graph-based algorithms to trace lexical and syntactic evolution across literary periods. Key tasks include training transformer architectures on Ming-Qing vernacular literature to detect stylistic shifts, applying contrastive phonemic analysis to understudied Mandarin and Wu dialect recordings, and simulating language contact effects in pidgin varieties. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of terabyte-scale text corpora, hyperparameter tuning of deep learning models, and real-time acoustic feature extraction from oral archives. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated dialectal features, predictive models of literary genre evolution, and tools for automated glossing of rare characters in medieval manuscripts. By integrating computational linguistics with Sinological scholarship, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in Chinese philology, support endangered dialect preservation, and provide scalable frameworks for analyzing non-standard linguistic phenomena. The results will directly contribute to interdisciplinary digital humanities initiatives while addressing gaps in language technologies tailored to Chinese’s unique morphological and tonal properties.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of China and associated dialects and literature. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale multimedia datasets and model the dissemination of science, health, and environmental information across digital media platforms. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how complex scientific and environmental issues are communicated to the public, particularly how journalistic framing, social media dynamics, and algorithmic biases interact to shape public perception and policy outcomes. Current methods for analyzing such communication networks are limited by the volume and heterogeneity of data (e.g., news articles, video content, social media interactions, and metadata), which require advanced computational tools to process efficiently. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to evaluate thematic patterns and sentiment in science journalism across 10+ years of global news archives. Concurrently, graph-based network analysis will map the flow of environmental health narratives between journalists, policymakers, and public stakeholders, incorporating geospatial and temporal variables to track misinformation spread during crisis events (e.g., pandemics, climate disasters). HPC resources are essential to train custom NLP models on domain-specific corpora, process terabytes of multimedia data, and simulate information diffusion scenarios using agent-based models. Expected outcomes include identifying key leverage points for improving science communication efficacy, quantifying the impact of algorithmic recommendation systems on environmental reporting accuracy, and developing open-access tools for journalists to visualize bias or gaps in coverage. By integrating computational social science methods with journalism studies, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for communicating complex scientific issues, ultimately supporting public engagement and informed decision-making in health and environmental policy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on reporting on science, health, or environmental policy issues; investigating environmental problems and their causes; and public relations. Includes instruction in communication law, health reporting skills, interactive journalism, integrated marketing communication, journalism methods, media ethics, persuasion and political communication, science, health and the environment, social marketing, and video journalism.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from Holocaust survivor testimonies, archival records, and wartime documentation, aiming to uncover latent patterns in trauma narratives, resistance networks, and perpetrator logistics. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume and heterogeneity of these materials—including text, audio, and visual sources—limiting insights into systemic behaviors, narrative evolution across survivor generations, and the spatial-temporal dynamics of genocide. The project will develop computational pipelines integrating natural language processing (NLP), geospatial mapping, and network analysis to address these gaps. Custom transformer models will be trained to identify and classify trauma-related linguistic features across multiple languages (e.g., Yiddish, German, Polish), while graph-based algorithms will reconstruct clandestine communication networks among resistance groups using fragmented archival data. HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale oral history collections (e.g., USC Shoah Foundation’s Visual History Archive) and optimizing machine learning models sensitive to context-specific ethical constraints, such as avoiding re-traumatizing language in training data. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive platform visualizing displacement routes of survivor populations, an open-source toolset for ethically aligned genocide document analysis, and novel quantitative frameworks to assess narrative consistency in war crimes testimony. By bridging historical scholarship, computational linguistics, and ethical AI, this work aims to advance methodological standards in Holocaust studies while providing scalable tools for educators and human rights organizations to analyze contemporary conflict patterns. The requested computing resources will enable iterative model training, large-scale parallel data processing, and secure handling of sensitive materials, which are infeasible with standard institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on genocide in human history with particular reference to Twentieth Century genocides such as that of the Ottoman Armenians during World War I and the Nazi Holocaust during World War II. Programs also focus on topics such as survivor studies and counseling, war crimes research and prevention, reconciliation and compensation, ethical and spiritual issues, holocaust art and literature, and legacy and effect in relation to subsequent generations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interplay between socio-economic decision-making and ecosystem resilience in rapidly urbanizing regions, with a focus on identifying policies that balance human development needs with biodiversity preservation. Current models often treat social and ecological systems as isolated entities, leading to fragmented sustainability strategies. By integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of land-use decisions, spatially explicit ecological network analysis, and machine learning-driven scenario forecasting, we aim to simulate how urban expansion, agricultural intensification, and conservation efforts co-evolve under climate uncertainty. The computational approach will combine high-resolution satellite data, demographic surveys, and species distribution records to parameterize multi-scale interactions across governance boundaries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of scenarios involving thousands of decision-making agents (e.g., households, municipalities), fine-grained ecological connectivity matrices, and multi-objective optimization over decadal timescales. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of leverage points where policy interventions can simultaneously enhance economic equity and habitat connectivity, (2) quantification of trade-offs between short-term development gains and long-term ecosystem service provision, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive governance that account for cross-system feedbacks. The project bridges computational social science, landscape ecology, and complexity theory, advancing methodological integration in sustainability science while providing actionable insights for regions facing competing pressures from population growth, food security demands, and climate-driven habitat fragmentation. Results will inform international biodiversity frameworks and regional land-use planning processes, demonstrating how computationally intensive transdisciplinary modeling can reconcile often-divergent sustainability priorities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the concept of sustainability from an interdisciplinary perspective. Includes instruction in sustainable development, environmental policies, ethics, ecology, landscape architecture, city and regional planning, economics, natural resources, sociology, and anthropology.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize casino floor operations, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation and risk mitigation in live gaming environments. The problem addressed is the lack of scalable, real-time decision-making tools for casino managers to balance operational efficiency, customer experience, and regulatory compliance amid fluctuating demand patterns and security challenges. Current industry practices rely heavily on static scheduling and human intuition, which struggle to adapt to complex variables such as patron flow, game popularity shifts, and evolving fraud tactics. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patron behaviors, staff movements, and security incidents across a parameterized virtual casino environment. High-performance computing resources are required to run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations that account for probabilistic gaming outcomes, surveillance system latency, and multi-objective optimization constraints (e.g., labor costs vs. table game coverage). Machine learning techniques will be integrated to identify patterns in historical security breach data and generate predictive alerts for anomalous activities. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit capable of testing operational scenarios at casino-scale resolution, quantitative metrics for evaluating surveillance system responsiveness, and adaptive staffing algorithms that reduce service bottlenecks by 15-20% in benchmark tests. By bridging computational systems theory with gaming operations management, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for next-generation casino resource planning while maintaining compliance with jurisdictional gaming regulations. The computational infrastructure will enable replication studies across diverse virtual floor layouts and regulatory regimes, providing a foundation for data-driven policymaking in the global gaming industry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on casino operations and services. Includes instruction in casino operations, casino security and surveillance, casino dealing, principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale historical analysis of transnational social movements in the 19th and early 20th centuries. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how ideas, networks, and organizational strategies spread across borders during this transformative period. Traditional archival methods struggle to synthesize fragmented, multilingual primary sources—including newspapers, government documents, and personal correspondence—held in dispersed digital repositories. To overcome these limitations, the project employs computational text analysis, network modeling, and geospatial mapping to identify patterns of discourse, collaboration, and ideological exchange across millions of digitized records. Key tasks include training custom natural language processing (NLP) models to handle historical languages and OCR errors, constructing dynamic network graphs to trace the evolution of activist networks, and visualizing spatial-temporal diffusion using GIS-integrated tools. The scale of data (estimated at 15 TB of text and metadata) and the complexity of multi-layered analyses necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory operations, and efficient storage management. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive database of movement actors and events, quantitative insights into the relationship between communication technologies and mobilization rates, and qualitative case studies validating computational findings against traditional historiography. By integrating computational methods with historical rigor, this project aims to redefine scholarly approaches to transnational history while providing a replicable framework for analyzing large, heterogeneous archival corpora. Results will inform contemporary discussions about grassroots organizing and cross-cultural solidarity, bridging historical scholarship with public engagement initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and interpretation of the past, including the gathering, recording, synthesizing and criticizing of evidence and theories about past events. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; studies of specific periods, issues and cultures; and applications to areas such as historic preservation, public policy, and records administration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance anthropological research on the dynamics of cultural transmission and adaptation in prehistoric human populations. A central challenge in anthropological modeling is simulating large-scale, multi-generational behavioral interactions under variable ecological and social constraints, which requires computationally intensive agent-based models (ABMs) and probabilistic analyses of sparse archaeological datasets. Current limitations in local computing infrastructure prevent the exploration of parameter spaces necessary to address key questions: How did resource volatility and social network structures interact to shape cultural resilience in early Holocene societies? What computational frameworks can best integrate heterogeneous data (e.g., artifact distributions, paleoenvironmental proxies, and ethnographic analogs) to infer decision-making processes in past populations? To address these gaps, we propose deploying scalable ABMs on HPC clusters to simulate population interactions across millennia, incorporating dynamically linked environmental, demographic, and cultural variables. Parallelized Bayesian inference methods will be applied to archaeological datasets spanning 10,000–5,000 BP from six continental regions, enabling comparative analysis of technological innovation rates under differing climate regimes. The computational workflow will utilize containerized environments for reproducibility, with iterative model calibration against radiocarbon-dated cultural sequences. Expected outcomes include: (1) quantitative estimates of threshold conditions for cultural fragmentation versus continuity in early agricultural societies, (2) open-source tools for simulating anthropogenic landscape modifications, and (3) a publicly accessible database linking archaeological signatures to simulated social processes. By enabling complex systems approaches at previously impractical scales, this work will establish new methodologies for testing anthropological theories of cultural evolution while providing frameworks to analyze modern societal resilience through long-term human-environment dynamics. The requested resources are critical for managing memory-intensive phylogenetic analyses of cultural trait diffusion and Monte Carlo simulations assessing demographic uncertainty in prehistoric contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human beings, their antecedents and related primates, and their cultural behavior and institutions, in comparative perspective. Includes instruction in biological/physical anthropology, primatology, human paleontology and prehistoric archeology, hominid evolution, anthropological linguistics, ethnography, ethnology, ethnohistory, socio-cultural anthropology, psychological anthropology, research methods, and applications to areas such as medicine, forensic pathology, museum studies, and international affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop personalized assistive and augmentative technologies (AAT) through advanced computational modeling of human-device interactions, with the goal of improving mobility and functional outcomes for individuals with neurological or musculoskeletal impairments. The research addresses a critical challenge in rehabilitation engineering: optimizing device design (e.g., exoskeletons, prosthetics, or adaptive interfaces) to account for the biomechanical variability and dynamic needs of users while minimizing iterative physical prototyping. Current approaches often rely on static anatomical measurements or generalized population data, leading to suboptimal fit, comfort, and long-term usability. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale musculoskeletal simulations integrating individualized biomechanical data, real-world movement patterns, and material stress analyses. Multibody dynamics models will be coupled with finite element analysis to predict tissue-device interface pressures, joint loading, and energy expenditure across diverse user scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will further refine predictive models by correlating simulated outcomes with clinical metrics from rehabilitation trials. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of these high-fidelity simulations, which require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets spanning anatomical geometries, sensor-derived motion capture, and device performance parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for rapidly generating patient-specific AAT design recommendations, (2) validated models linking device configurations to functional gains in activities of daily living, and (3) open-source tools to accelerate adaptive technology development. By reducing trial-and-error in device customization, this work aims to enhance access to precision rehabilitation technologies while advancing computational methods for human-centered engineering in healthcare.
cip_title: Assistive/ Augmentative Technology and Rehabilitation Engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of psychology, engineering, and occupational therapy to the design and implementation of technological interventions and systems to promote patient rehabilitation and function. Includes instruction in ergonomics, seating and mobility design, universal and near environment systems design, rehabilitation research, rehabilitation biomechanics, access and communications design, microprocessor-based technologies, neurological trauma, standards and testing, and service delivery management.

abstract: Medication-related adverse events remain a significant public health challenge, contributing to preventable patient harm and substantial healthcare costs. Current approaches to medication safety monitoring often rely on manual reporting systems or retrospective analyses, which lack the resolution to detect complex risk patterns across diverse patient populations and drug combinations. This project proposes to develop a computational framework for real-time prediction of medication-use risks by integrating multimodal clinical data, including electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacogenomic profiles, and longitudinal medication adherence patterns. The research will employ machine learning models trained on federated datasets from six health systems, encompassing over 2.5 million patient encounters. Key computational challenges include processing high-dimensional temporal data streams, managing heterogeneous data formats at scale, and preserving privacy through differential privacy techniques. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parallelized model training across GPU nodes, large-scale simulation of drug interaction networks using graph-based approaches, and validation of predictive algorithms through in silico clinical trials. Anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive analytics platform for identifying high-risk medication regimens, (2) quantitative risk stratification models validated against prospective clinical data, and (3) novel insights into context-specific risk factors for adverse drug events in vulnerable populations. By enabling rapid analysis of complex medication-use scenarios across diverse care settings, this work aims to provide clinicians with actionable decision support tools while informing health system-level medication safety protocols. The computational infrastructure developed through this project will establish a scalable framework for ongoing medication safety surveillance, adaptable to emerging therapeutic classes and evolving clinical practice patterns.
cip_definition: Research focused on Medication-Use Safety

abstract: Emerging digital communication platforms demand increasingly sophisticated tools to optimize media content delivery, user engagement, and network efficiency. This project addresses the computational challenges of modeling large-scale, dynamic interactions in hybrid communication ecosystems—particularly systems integrating real-time streaming, adaptive bitrate technologies, and audience behavior analytics. Current simulations fail to account for the nonlinear relationships between user decision-making, fluctuating bandwidth constraints, and platform-specific content moderation algorithms, limiting predictive accuracy for QoS (Quality of Service) outcomes. To resolve this, we propose developing a high-fidelity agent-based model (ABM) leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-platform communication networks with 10^6+ concurrent user agents. The model will integrate machine learning submodules trained on anonymized streaming metadata (e.g., viewer retention logs, buffering events) to predict adaptive bitrate selection patterns under variable latency conditions. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess system robustness across stochastic scenarios, including sudden traffic surges and localized network outages. Computational outputs will inform the design of a novel congestion-aware content distribution protocol, aiming to reduce latency by 15–25% in simulated real-world streaming environments compared to industry-standard TCP-based approaches. This work directly supports the Communications Technology program’s focus on advancing media production systems and infrastructure, offering empirically validated strategies for scalable content delivery. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation frameworks for educators and a white paper detailing HPC-driven optimizations for adaptive streaming services. By quantifying trade-offs between computational overhead and QoS improvements, this research will provide actionable insights for developers, telecommunications policymakers, and digital media platforms navigating bandwidth allocation challenges in 5G-adjacent networks.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to function as workers and managers within communications industries. Includes instruction in business economics; basic management; principles of interpersonal and mediated communications; radio, television, and digital media production; and related aspects of technology and communications systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the regulatory and systemic risk implications of algorithmic decision-making in corporate finance and securities trading. The rapid proliferation of machine learning models in financial operations—ranging from credit风险评估 to high-frequency trading—has created legal ambiguities under existing frameworks such as the Dodd-Frank Act, MiFID II, and SEC disclosure rules. Traditional legal analysis struggles to map the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between adaptive algorithms, market behavior, and regulatory thresholds. To address this gap, we propose a computational legal analytics framework combining agent-based market simulations, natural language processing (NLP) of regulatory texts, and graph-theoretic analysis of compliance networks. Agent-based models will simulate trading environments where heterogeneous algorithmic strategies interact under varying regulatory scenarios, generating terabyte-scale datasets on market stability and rule violations. Concurrently, transformer-based NLP models will parse and semantically cluster regulatory documents to identify latent conflicts or gaps in legal language when applied to AI-driven financial instruments. Graph analytics will then model the cascading effects of localized compliance failures across interconnected financial entities. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these simulations to realistic market participant counts (>10^5 agents) and for training domain-specific legal language models on multi-jurisdictional corpora. Expected outcomes include 1) a taxonomy of algorithmic financial practices that challenge current legal taxonomies, 2) quantitative metrics for assessing systemic compliance risks in automated markets, and 3) prototype tools for real-time regulatory stress-testing. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, legal theory, and financial engineering, offering policymakers and regulatory bodies empirically grounded strategies to modernize oversight frameworks for AI-permeated financial ecosystems.
cip_title: Banking, Corporate, Finance, and Securities Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law and process related to the regulation of businesses and the financial services industry. Includes instruction in corporate law, antitrust law, securities law and regulation, negotiation, incorporation, partnerships, trusts, and related topics

abstract: This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to evaluate the long-term impacts of public policy interventions in complex, multi-stakeholder systems, with an initial focus on urban transportation infrastructure allocation. Public policy analysis often grapples with predicting emergent outcomes from nonlinear interactions between institutional rules, individual behaviors, and physical constraints, yet existing computational tools struggle to integrate high-resolution behavioral data with system-scale dynamics. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale simulations that capture heterogeneous traveler decision-making, municipal budget cycles, and infrastructure decay processes across a synthetic metropolitan region of 1 million agents. Computational methods will combine parallelized discrete event simulation for daily mobility patterns with evolutionary algorithms to optimize policy packages under demographic and climate uncertainty. Model validation will leverage anonymized transit smartcard data and maintenance records from three U.S. cities. The project addresses critical gaps in policy evaluation methodologies by enabling real-time sensitivity analysis of equity-efficiency tradeoffs and threshold effects in infrastructure investments. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source policy simulation toolkit capable of processing petabyte-scale behavioral datasets, along with evidence-based recommendations for adaptive funding allocation mechanisms in transportation policy. By quantifying second-order effects of policy decisions at unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution, this work aims to provide policymakers with robust predictive tools for managing interdependent vulnerabilities in public infrastructure systems. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the memory-intensive nature of multi-year simulations with dynamically interacting policy levers, environmental stressors, and population mobility patterns.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues and decision processes. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, microeconomic analysis of policy issues, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: Marine ecosystems are increasingly threatened by climate-driven perturbations, including ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation, yet their nonlinear impacts on planktonic food webs and biogeochemical cycles remain poorly resolved at regional scales. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of how interacting physical, chemical, and biological processes structure pelagic community dynamics in the California Current System (CCS), a critical coastal upwelling zone supporting high biodiversity and fisheries productivity. We propose to develop a high-resolution, coupled physical-biological model integrating hydrodynamic simulations with trait-based representations of microbial and zooplankton functional groups. The model will resolve submesoscale turbulence (1–10 km), diel vertical migration, and adaptive behaviors in key taxa, which are underrepresented in existing frameworks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute ensemble simulations across multiple climate scenarios (RCP 4.5, 8.5) at spatiotemporal scales necessary to capture fine-grained biophysical interactions. Computational workflows will leverage the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) coupled to a customized Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) model with dynamic stoichiometry and trait diffusion algorithms. Machine learning tools will be applied to analyze petabyte-scale output alongside in situ genomic data and satellite-derived productivity indices. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into climate-driven shifts in plankton community composition, carbon export efficiency, and cross-trophic energy transfer. Results will directly inform adaptive management strategies for marine protected areas and fisheries in the CCS while providing an open-source modeling framework for the broader ocean sciences community. This work requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for turbulence-resolving simulations and large-memory nodes for ecological network analyses, necessitating 2.5 million core-hours and 250 TB of storage allocation annually over three years.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting oceans, coastal waters, and saltwater wetlands and their interactions with the physical environment. Includes instruction in chemical, physical, and geological oceanography; molecular, cellular, and biochemical studies; marine microbiology; marine botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; marine population dynamics and biodiversity; reproductive biology; studies of specific species, phyla, habitats, and ecosystems; marine paleocology and palentology; and applications to fields such as fisheries science and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale digital communication datasets, addressing critical gaps in understanding how evolving media ecosystems shape public discourse and social behavior. The research focuses on two interrelated problems: (1) the dynamics of misinformation propagation across hybrid media environments (social platforms, news outlets, and interpersonal networks) and (2) the computational modeling of rhetorical strategies that influence collective decision-making in polarized contexts. Current methodologies in communication studies often rely on small-scale qualitative analyses or simplified quantitative models, limiting their capacity to capture the nonlinear, multi-platform interactions characteristic of modern communication. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods framework combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling, and dynamic network analysis. NLP pipelines will process terabytes of text and multimedia content from social media APIs, legacy news archives, and public forums to identify narrative patterns, sentiment shifts, and source credibility signals. Agent-based models will simulate information diffusion across heterogeneous networks, incorporating psychological and sociological parameters derived from communication theory (e.g., selective exposure, cognitive dissonance). Network analyses will map temporal changes in influence hierarchies and cross-platform content migration. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on domain-specific corpora, running parallelized simulations across diverse demographic scenarios, and processing real-time data streams during emergent communication events (e.g., elections, crises). Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for communication researchers, empirically grounded models of resilience against misinformation, and policy-relevant insights into platform governance. By bridging communication theory with scalable computational methods, this work aims to advance the field’s capacity to study macro-level communication phenomena while maintaining theoretical rigor—a critical step in addressing 21st-century challenges to democratic discourse and social cohesion.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, and that spans the study of mass communication/media studies, old and new media technologies, social and political applications, and speech communication and rhetoric. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; media social science and criticism; and quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving regulatory and legal frameworks governing artificial intelligence (AI) applications in healthcare, a critical yet underexplored niche within Health Law. The rapid integration of AI into clinical decision-making, patient data management, and insurance risk assessment has outpaced existing legal and policy structures, creating gaps in accountability, equity, and compliance. Traditional legal research methods are insufficient to systematically evaluate the vast, dynamic corpus of case law, administrative rulings, and transnational regulatory texts shaping this domain. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based network analysis to map interjurisdictional legal conflicts, identify patterns in judicial reasoning, and model the cascading effects of emergent AI-related litigation on healthcare institutions. A custom pipeline will process multimodal data—including court opinions, regulatory guidance, and insurance claim disputes—to train transformer-based models for semantic similarity analysis and precedent retrieval. Temporal network models will track shifts in legal interpretation across federal circuits and state jurisdictions, while agent-based simulations will forecast compliance challenges under hypothetical regulatory scenarios. The computational demands of processing terabytes of unstructured legal text, coupled with the need for real-time updates to capture emergent case law, necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallelized training, large-scale graph traversal, and high-throughput simulations. Expected outcomes include a public repository of annotated legal corpora, predictive tools to assess litigation risks for healthcare AI developers, and policy recommendations to harmonize conflicting standards. By bridging computational scalability with doctrinal analysis, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for addressing complexity in health law, offering stakeholders actionable insights to navigate the legal uncertainties of AI-driven healthcare.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies and regulations affecting the health care industry, health professions, health services and insurance industries, and patients.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamic interplay between digital cultural production and systemic power structures through a computational critical theory framework. The research problem centers on mapping and modeling how marginalized communities navigate, resist, and reshape dominant cultural narratives within algorithmically mediated platforms (e.g., social media, digital archives, collaborative creative spaces). Traditional qualitative methods in cultural studies struggle to capture the scale, velocity, and nonlinear feedback loops inherent in these environments, necessitating computational approaches to trace emergent patterns across multimodal datasets. The project will employ a mixed-methods pipeline combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling, and network analysis to study three interrelated phenomena: 1) the diffusion of counter-narratives in decentralized digital communities, 2) the algorithmic amplification/reduction of intersectional identity markers in platform content moderation systems, and 3) the evolution of visual-cultural symbology in AI-generated art communities. Custom transformer models will process multilingual text and image corpora spanning 2010-2023, while graph-theoretic simulations will map power asymmetries in content dissemination networks. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of petabyte-scale datasets, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-network analysis. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for critical cultural analytics, quantitative frameworks for measuring narrative resilience in digital ecosystems, and novel visualizations of cultural hegemony dynamics across temporal scales. By integrating critical theory with scalable computational methods, this research aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for studying cultural power relations while providing empirically grounded insights into contemporary digital resistance practices. The project’s computational demands reflect the need to reconcile close hermeneutic analysis with macro-scale cultural pattern detection—a challenge central to next-generation interdisciplinary cultural studies.
cip_title: Cultural Studies/ Critical Theory and Analysis
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the analysis and critique of culture in its varied forms, including values, ideas, belief systems, and expressive acts, and the relationship between cultural forms, everyday life, and structures of power. Includes instruction in anthropology, communications, history, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, and sociology, as well as recent theories and methodologies such as semiotics, deconstruction, postcolonial studies, gender theory, and ethnography.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in optimizing energy-efficient designs for advanced hydraulic control systems used in industrial automation and heavy machinery. Current models struggle to capture the coupled thermo-fluid-structural interactions within these systems at high spatial and temporal resolutions, limiting predictive accuracy for dynamic load scenarios. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale, transient simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and multi-body dynamics within a unified framework. A parallelized solver architecture will be developed to handle the multi-physics coupling, utilizing adaptive mesh refinement and GPU-accelerated algorithms to resolve critical regions such as valve interfaces and actuator seals. The simulations will quantify energy losses attributed to turbulence, leakage, and component deformation under varying pressure cycles, enabling topology optimization of flow paths and material selections. Validation will occur through scaled experimental rigs instrumented with high-frequency pressure and strain sensors. Successful implementation will reduce computational wall time by 60% compared to existing serial approaches while maintaining sub-millisecond temporal resolution. Anticipated outcomes include a 15-20% improvement in hydraulic system efficiency for prototype configurations, directly supporting sustainability goals in manufacturing and construction equipment. The resource allocation will further enable parametric studies of 50+ design variants to establish generalized guidelines for minimizing throttling losses in proportional valves. By bridging high-fidelity simulation capabilities with real-world hydraulic system performance, this work aims to advance predictive modeling tools for next-generation fluid power systems while reducing reliance on physical prototyping.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and end-product systems used for specific uses, including machine tools, jigs and other manufacturing equipment; stationary power units and appliances; engines; self-propelled vehicles; housings and containers; hydraulic and electric systems for controlling movement; and the integration of computers and remote control with operating systems.

abstract: Pediatric dentistry faces complex challenges in understanding the multifactorial determinants of oral health disparities and treatment outcomes across diverse populations, including children with disabilities. Current clinical studies often lack the computational power to integrate high-dimensional datasets—such as electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, longitudinal behavioral patterns, and 3D craniofacial imaging—into predictive models that account for dynamic interactions between biological, environmental, and care-access variables. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for analyzing these heterogeneous datasets, enabling precision oral health strategies tailored to pediatric populations. The research will employ machine learning (ML) models, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to identify risk trajectories for early childhood caries and orthodontic complications in patients with neurodevelopmental conditions. Large-scale simulations will model the impact of socioecological factors on care adherence, while finite element analysis of dental biomechanics will optimize restorative protocols for children with physical disabilities. Computational workflows will be parallelized to process multi-institutional EHRs and imaging repositories, requiring GPU-accelerated training of deep learning architectures and distributed memory systems for genome-wide association studies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for caries progression, data-driven clinical decision support systems, and mechanistic insights into oral-systemic health interactions in medically complex pediatric cohorts. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to overcome current limitations in data integration and real-time analytics, directly informing personalized prevention programs and reducing oral health inequities. All models and pipelines will be disseminated as open-source resources to advance computational pediatric dentistry research, with translational potential to improve clinical guidelines and resource allocation for vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on primary oral health care to infants, children, and adolescents, including patients with medical, physical or mental disabilities.

abstract: Mental health disorders represent a leading cause of global disability, yet their underlying biological and environmental mechanisms remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting treatment outcomes and disentangling multifactorial contributors to psychiatric conditions, including schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and bipolar disorder, through advanced computational modeling. The complexity of integrating high-dimensional datasets—spanning genomics, neuroimaging, electronic health records, and real-time behavioral data—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in scalability and analytical precision. We propose a two-phase computational approach. First, we will develop federated machine learning models to harmonize heterogeneous datasets from 15+ international cohorts (n > 50,000 participants), preserving privacy while identifying transdiagnostic biomarkers. Second, we will implement biophysically informed neural circuit simulations to model how genetic risk variants interact with environmental stressors to alter neurodevelopmental trajectories. These simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated dynamical systems modeling to capture non-linear interactions across molecular, cellular, and circuit-level domains. HPC resources are essential for training deep learning architectures on multi-modal data, running large-scale parameter sweeps in neural models, and conducting genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analyses with iterative permutation testing. Expected outcomes include the identification of reproducible neural signatures predictive of treatment resistance in depression, stratification of psychosis risk pathways based on gene-environment interplay, and open-source tools for scalable psychiatric data integration. By elucidating mechanisms that bridge genetic susceptibility and clinical phenotypes, this work aims to advance precision psychiatry, enabling clinicians to tailor interventions based on individualized risk profiles. The requested computing infrastructure will directly support translational advances with the potential to reduce trial-and-error treatment approaches and improve functional outcomes for patients worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on Psychiatric/Mental Health

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict adversarial influence operations targeting national security decision-making processes, with a focus on emergent strategies leveraging generative AI and decentralized communication platforms. While existing scholarship on disinformation and hybrid warfare often prioritizes retrospective analysis or single-domain tactics, this research addresses a critical gap: the real-time simulation of multi-vector influence campaigns that exploit cognitive vulnerabilities in security policy ecosystems. The study employs agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between adversarial actors (state and non-state), civilian populations, and institutional decision-makers across geopolitical scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to execute large-scale parallel simulations incorporating natural language processing (NLP) for synthetic content generation, network analysis of dark web coordination patterns, and dynamic game-theoretic models of strategic deception. Key innovations include the integration of cognitive bias parameters derived from experimental psychology into decision-agent architectures, as well as machine learning classifiers trained on cross-domain escalation signatures (cyber, economic, and information operations). Outputs will quantify the resilience of policy-making infrastructures to next-generation influence tactics, identify early-warning indicators of systemic manipulation, and test countermeasure prototypes through adaptive scenario testing. The computational toolkit developed through this work will provide national security institutions with evidence-based strategies to mitigate AI-amplified information threats while preserving democratic deliberation processes. By bridging computational social science with defense policy applications, this project advances interdisciplinary methodologies for security studies in an era of algorithmic conflict.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and application of intelligence, diplomacy, military power, and related tools of statecraft to national defense policy formulation and power projection. Includes instruction in history, political theory, public policy analysis, civil-military relations, military and defense studies, homeland security, leadership, threat scenarios, regional and local issues, alliance and coalition issues, defense budgeting and economics, intelligence, and strategy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of analyzing audience engagement and media impact in sports communication, where traditional computational tools struggle to process large-scale multimedia datasets. The rise of digital platforms has transformed how sports content is created, disseminated, and consumed, generating vast volumes of unstructured data—including social media interactions, live broadcast feeds, and athlete-generated content. Current methods for evaluating audience sentiment, content virality, and cross-platform media strategies lack the capacity to integrate multimodal data (text, video, audio) efficiently, limiting actionable insights for practitioners. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for real-time and retrospective analysis of sports communication dynamics. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) to assess sentiment in fan commentary, computer vision techniques to evaluate visual storytelling patterns in broadcast footage, and graph-based algorithms to map information diffusion across social networks. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including historical broadcast archives and streaming social media APIs, to train machine learning models that identify trends in audience behavior and content effectiveness. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable toolkit for sports media professionals to optimize content strategies, predict engagement metrics, and mitigate reputational risks during live events. The research will also contribute novel methodologies to communication studies by quantifying the relationship between media formats (e.g., highlight reels, press conferences) and public perception. By utilizing HPC, this work advances the precision of sports communication analytics, offering empirically grounded strategies to enhance media production, audience targeting, and crisis communication in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for communicating about sports in a variety of formats, media, and contexts; and that prepares individuals to be sports reporters and writers, photojournalists, radio and television announcers, producers and directors, recreational sports promoters, and public relations specialists. Includes instruction in sports writing, photography, broadcast journalism, sports production, game rules, media and public relations, and sports promotion.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale patient care datasets and optimize training protocols for nursing assistants and patient care aides. The research problem centers on the growing demand for data-driven insights to improve patient outcomes and reduce preventable adverse events—such as falls, pressure injuries, or medication errors—in settings where nursing aides provide frontline care. Current approaches to training and workflow design often rely on static guidelines, with limited integration of real-world, temporally rich data from electronic health records (EHRs), wearable sensors, or staff scheduling systems. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient-staff interactions, identify risk factors, and test intervention strategies. EHR data from 15 long-term care facilities (spanning 5 years, ~2.5 million entries) will be processed using natural language processing (NLP) to extract unstructured clinical notes, while time-series data from mobility sensors will train ML models to predict patient deterioration. Concurrently, ABM simulations will model staff workflows under varying patient-to-staff ratios, enabling scenario testing for protocol adjustments. The HPC environment is critical for handling the computational load of parallelized model training, large-scale data integration, and real-time simulation of facility-wide care dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to flag high-risk patients, (2) evidence-based recommendations for staff training focused on situational awareness and decision-making under time constraints, and (3) open-source simulation templates for nursing educator use. By bridging computational analytics with hands-on care paradigms, this work aims to enhance the precision of nursing aide training programs while providing scalable methods to improve care quality in resource-constrained environments.
cip_title: Nursing Assistant/ Aide and Patient Care Assistant/ Aide
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine nursing-related services to patients in hospitals or long-term care facilities, under the training and supervision of a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing personalized counseling interventions for postsecondary students facing academic and psychosocial challenges. Current counseling practices often rely on generalized frameworks that may not adequately account for the complex, dynamic interactions between individual student characteristics, institutional contexts, and intervention outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational model integrating longitudinal student data—including academic performance, mental health surveys, and counselor session transcripts—to identify patterns in intervention efficacy across diverse student subgroups. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze unstructured counseling session data, combined with multilevel Bayesian network modeling to map relationships between intervention types, student traits, and longitudinal outcomes. Computational demands include training transformer-based NLP models on anonymized session transcripts (estimated 50,000+ documents) and running iterative simulations to test intervention scenarios across synthetic student cohorts. HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive NLP tasks and enabling rapid parameter space exploration in Bayesian networks. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive framework for matching students to optimal counseling strategies based on their profiles, 2) identification of underrecognized risk/protective factors in student persistence, and 3) open-source tools for dynamic intervention planning. Results will directly inform evidence-based practices in student support services while advancing methodological integration of computational social science approaches in education research. This work addresses a critical need for scalable, data-driven decision-making tools in student counseling—a field historically constrained by small-sample qualitative methods—and demonstrates how HPC can catalyze innovation in personalized education support systems.
cip_title: Student Counseling and Personnel Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in student counseling and personnel services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Childhood and adolescent psychiatric disorders are complex, heterogeneous conditions shaped by dynamic interactions between genetic, neurobiological, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic frameworks and treatment strategies lack sufficient precision, in part due to limitations in modeling these multidimensional relationships at scale. This project proposes to address this gap by integrating high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, neuroimaging, electronic health record (EHR), and longitudinal behavioral data—to identify biobehavioral subtypes of developmental psychiatric disorders and predict treatment outcomes. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics data from 5,000 participants in the ABCD Study, process functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data from a regional cohort of 800 youth with anxiety or mood disorders, and apply machine learning to EHR-derived treatment trajectories. Computational workflows will include genome-wide association studies (GWAS) coupled with polygenic risk score optimization, connectome-based neural network modeling, and transformer-based natural language processing to extract latent features from clinical notes. Ensemble methods will integrate these data layers to stratify patients into subtypes with distinct neurodevelopmental signatures and treatment response profiles. Anticipated challenges include managing batch effects in multi-site neuroimaging data, harmonizing temporal EHR features, and scaling interpretable machine learning models to accommodate missing data. The project’s computational demands necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks, high-memory nodes for genome-phenome association testing, and large-scale parallel processing for permutation-based significance testing in imaging analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) validated computational pipelines for multimodal data integration in developmental psychiatry, (2) novel biomarkers linking neurodevelopmental trajectories to treatment resistance in adolescent depression, and (3) a proof-of-concept decision support tool for personalized intervention selection. By elucidating mechanisms underlying clinical heterogeneity, this work aims to advance translational applications of computational psychiatry while establishing infrastructure for data-driven care models in youth mental health.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of developmental, behavioral, emotional, and mental disorders of childhood and adolescence.

abstract: Pediatric nephrology faces critical challenges in understanding the molecular and physiological drivers of heterogeneous kidney diseases, such as congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT), steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, and pediatric hypertension. Current diagnostic and prognostic tools lack precision, leading to suboptimal risk stratification and therapeutic decisions. This project proposes to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-omics data, electronic health records (EHRs), and advanced imaging biomarkers. The research will develop computational models to unravel genotype-phenotype associations, predict disease progression, and identify novel therapeutic targets. A key focus is the creation of machine learning frameworks to analyze whole-exome sequencing, transcriptomic, and epigenomic datasets from pediatric cohorts, combined with longitudinal clinical data (e.g., glomerular filtration rates, blood pressure variability, and histopathology findings). HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these complex datasets, facilitate dynamic simulations of renal hemodynamics, and support the training of deep neural networks to detect subtle imaging patterns in renal ultrasounds and DMSA scans. Additionally, agent-based models will explore immune-mediated injury mechanisms in pediatric glomerulopathies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for early detection of chronic kidney disease progression, biomarkers for personalized treatment stratification, and open-source tools for pediatric nephrology research. By elucidating disease mechanisms and optimizing clinical decision-making, this work aims to reduce long-term morbidity in children with kidney disorders. The requested computing infrastructure is essential to manage the computational intensity of multi-modal data integration, ensure reproducibility, and accelerate discoveries in a field where sample sizes are inherently limited and biological heterogeneity is high.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of infants, children, and adolescents with renal and genito-urinary problems, hypertension and disorders of body fluid physiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize the design and performance of next-generation electric and autonomous vehicles (EVs/AVs), addressing critical challenges in energy efficiency, thermal management, and safety systems. Current vehicle prototyping and physical testing workflows are time-intensive and cost-prohibitive, particularly when evaluating complex multi-physics interactions across powertrains, battery systems, and autonomous driving algorithms. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct large-scale simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven control optimization. Key objectives include modeling battery thermal runaway scenarios under extreme operating conditions, optimizing aerodynamics for reduced energy consumption in EV configurations, and validating sensor fusion algorithms for AV perception systems in simulated urban environments. The computational workflow will utilize open-source and commercial tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, ANSYS, TensorFlow) adapted for parallel processing on GPU-accelerated clusters. Expected outcomes include predictive design frameworks to reduce physical prototyping cycles by 30-40%, identification of safety-critical thermal thresholds for battery packs, and benchmark datasets for AV decision-making latency in edge cases. Results will directly inform ongoing collaborations with regional automotive manufacturers to accelerate sustainable transportation solutions. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of coupled multi-domain simulations, which require terabytes of parametric data storage, thousands of core-hours per design iteration, and real-time co-simulation capabilities for vehicle-to-infrastructure networking tests. This work will advance both academic knowledge in vehicular systems integration and industry-ready tools for agile automotive development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The integration of multimodal patient data to optimize psychotropic medication selection and dosing remains a critical challenge in psychiatric care, particularly for frontline mental health technicians managing complex cases. Current approaches rely heavily on trial-and-error protocols, contributing to prolonged treatment timelines, adverse side effects, and suboptimal outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to analyze high-dimensional clinical datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), pharmacogenomic profiles, and real-time behavioral monitoring data—to predict individualized treatment responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop machine learning models capable of identifying patterns across heterogeneous data types while accounting for ethical and regulatory constraints inherent to mental health data. The computational pipeline will incorporate federated learning techniques to preserve patient confidentiality across institutions and dynamic simulation modules to model neuropharmacological interactions. Key deliverables include an open-source predictive tool for medication efficacy estimation and a risk stratification system for adverse event prediction, both designed for integration into technician workflow platforms. Anticipated outcomes include reduced medication trial periods by 30-50% in simulated cohorts and improved detection of high-risk pharmacological interactions. This work bridges computational psychiatry and clinical operations, offering a novel decision-support mechanism for non-prescribing mental health professionals. By aligning predictive analytics with the procedural scope of psychiatric technicians, the project aims to enhance precision in treatment plan execution while maintaining human-centric care standards.
