By bridging computational methodologies with critical Black studies frameworks, this work aims to reveal previously obscured synergies between artistic movements and community resilience strategies while developing interoperable tools for cross-institutional collaborative research. The resource allocation will directly support capacity-building in digital humanities approaches within African-American studies, enabling rigorous analysis of cultural production's role in sustaining transnational Black identities amid shifting sociopolitical landscapes.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: International school administrators face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, policy implementation, and cross-cultural leadership across diverse student populations and regulatory environments. Current decision-making frameworks often rely on static datasets or qualitative insights, limiting predictive accuracy and scalability. This project proposes the development of a dynamic computational model to simulate international school ecosystems, integrating multi-source data on student demographics, cultural dynamics, fiscal constraints, and academic outcomes. The research will employ agent-based modeling to represent stakeholder interactions, coupled with machine learning techniques to analyze longitudinal institutional data from 150+ international schools. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets of student performance metrics, staff retention patterns, and cross-national policy documents while running parallel simulations of administrative decision pathways. Computational experiments will test scenarios related to equitable resource distribution, crisis response protocols, and culturally responsive leadership strategies under varying enrollment and geopolitical conditions. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics framework to identify optimal budget allocation patterns, risk-mitigated policy adoption timelines, and culturally adaptive staff development programs. The model’s sensitivity analyses will quantify how localized adjustments in leadership approaches affect systemic outcomes across different school sizes and regional contexts. By establishing quantitative relationships between administrative choices and institutional performance indicators, this work aims to advance evidence-based leadership practices in international education while demonstrating novel applications of HPC capabilities in non-STEM educational administration research. Resulting computational tools will be disseminated as open-access resources for administrator training programs and accreditation bodies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in international schools, the study of international education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in culture in the classroom, educational leadership, globalization, instructional design and technology, international research methods, evaluation, and education policy.

abstract: The increasing burden of vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases, exacerbated by climate change, urbanization, and antimicrobial resistance, demands advanced predictive tools to optimize intervention strategies. Current approaches to modeling disease dynamics often lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale data, including pathogen genomics, vector ecology, human mobility, and environmental variables. This project seeks to address this gap by developing high-resolution computational models to predict transmission patterns of malaria, dengue, and emerging arboviral diseases in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based models simulating vector-host interactions across heterogeneous landscapes, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on regional climate projections, genomic surveillance data, and real-time epidemiological reports. A parallel computational pipeline will analyze whole-genome sequencing data from clinical isolates to identify genetic markers of drug resistance and antigenic evolution in Plasmodium and dengue virus populations. These models will be validated against historical outbreak data and iteratively refined to improve predictive accuracy. The computational workload requires massive parallelization due to the stochastic nature of disease spread simulations and the volume of genomic data (>10,000 sequences). Expected outcomes include (1) spatially explicit risk maps identifying outbreak hotspots under future climate scenarios, (2) predictive metrics for strain-specific vaccine efficacy, and (3) optimized intervention timelines for vector control campaigns. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will provide actionable insights for policymakers and clinicians, enabling targeted resource allocation and adaptive management of tropical diseases. The resulting open-source tools will advance computational methodologies in tropical medicine, fostering collaboration across endemic regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced real-time animation and interactive visual effects using high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome the computational limitations of simulating hyper-realistic physics, complex particle systems, and multi-sensory environments. Current workflows in animation and interactive media struggle to render dynamic, large-scale simulations—such as fluid dynamics, cloth behavior, or crowd interactions—at cinematic quality without prohibitive processing delays. These bottlenecks hinder creative experimentation and limit the scalability of immersive experiences for applications in virtual production, gaming, and interactive storytelling. To address this, the project proposes leveraging HPC clusters to parallelize rendering tasks, optimize neural radiance field (NeRF) models for real-time 3D scene reconstruction, and train generative AI systems for automated texture synthesis. Computational methods will integrate physics-based simulations (e.g., finite element analysis for deformable objects) with machine learning frameworks to accelerate iterative design processes. The research will also explore hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to balance memory-intensive tasks (e.g., 4K/8K video compositing) with computationally demanding ray tracing. Outcomes aim to establish optimized pipelines for rendering photorealistic animations 40–60% faster than current industry standards while maintaining artistic control. The resulting workflows and open-source tools will be validated through case studies in virtual production and interactive installations, with implications for reducing production costs and enabling smaller studios to compete in high-end visual effects. By bridging computational efficiency with creative flexibility, this work will advance the technical frontiers of digital storytelling and expand access to cutting-edge tools in communication-focused fields such as journalism (e.g., data-driven 3D infographics) and experiential education. Resource requests include GPU nodes, distributed storage for terabyte-scale asset libraries, and support for mixed-precision computing to balance speed and visual fidelity.
cip_title: Animation, Interactive Technology, Video Graphics, and Special Effects
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use computer applications and related visual and sound imaging techniques to manipulate images and information originating as film, video, still photographs, digital copy, soundtracks, and physical objects in order to communicate messages simulating real-world content. Includes instruction in specialized camerawork and equipment operation and maintenance, image capture, computer programming, dubbing, CAD applications, and applications to specific commercial, industrial, and entertainment needs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the spatial and temporal dynamics of visitor behavior in urban parks, with the goal of optimizing resource allocation for equitable access and ecological sustainability. Urban parks face growing pressures from increased visitation, climate variability, and competing demands for recreational programming, yet traditional management tools lack the granularity to predict how micro-scale decisions—such as trail rerouting, event scheduling, or habitat restoration—cascade into systemic impacts. The research employs agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with high-resolution geospatial data to simulate visitor movement patterns, preferences, and interactions with park infrastructure under diverse scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the stochasticity of human decision-making at scale, integrating real-time sensor data from park Wi-Fi hotspots, environmental sensors, and anonymized mobile device traces to calibrate models. Machine learning components will identify latent patterns in visitation trends, while Monte Carlo methods assess uncertainty in long-term predictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that quantifies trade-offs between visitor experience metrics (e.g., crowding, accessibility) and ecological indicators (e.g., soil compaction, wildlife disturbance). This work bridges computational social science, landscape ecology, and operations research, advancing methodological innovation in leisure studies by introducing adaptive systems modeling to a field traditionally reliant on survey-based or qualitative approaches. The results will inform municipal park agencies in designing adaptive management strategies that balance recreational demand with conservation imperatives in rapidly urbanizing regions. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project addresses a critical gap in translating theoretical frameworks of recreational carrying capacity into actionable, data-driven policies.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles underlying recreational and leisure activities, and the practices involved in providing indoor and outdoor recreational facilities and services for the general public.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of optimizing sustainable textile design through advanced computational modeling of complex, irregular woven structures. Traditional textile design tools often rely on simplified geometric assumptions, limiting their ability to predict the performance of innovative, non-repeating patterns that incorporate recycled or biodegradable fibers with heterogeneous material properties. This project will develop and validate a high-fidelity simulation framework using finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning to model nonlinear interactions between yarn composition, weave topology, and mechanical behavior under dynamic stress conditions. The computational workflow will integrate multi-scale material datasets spanning molecular polymer dynamics, fiber-level friction coefficients, and macro-scale drape characteristics. A key innovation involves adapting graph neural networks to predict failure points in asymmetrical weave configurations informed by historical textile archives from cultural heritage collections, creating a novel bridge between traditional craft knowledge and computational design. The research requires high-performance computing resources to manage iterative simulations across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 variables, including GPU-accelerated tensor operations for real-time design feedback loops. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive model for sustainable textile engineering that reduces physical prototyping waste by 40-60%, as well as new metrics for assessing the cultural relevance of computational design outputs through embedded ethnomathematical frameworks. This work fills a critical gap in apparel research infrastructure by enabling data-driven exploration of design solutions that simultaneously address technical performance, environmental impact, and cultural preservation imperatives.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in apparel and textiles, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing dynamic risk mitigation strategies in large-scale construction projects using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Construction projects face complex, interdependent risks—such as supply chain volatility, weather disruptions, labor shortages, and regulatory changes—that evolve unpredictably over time. Traditional risk management approaches, which rely on static models and linear assumptions, struggle to address the nonlinear interactions and real-time decision-making required for modern megaprojects. The computational challenge lies in modeling thousands of risk variables across technical, environmental, and socioeconomic domains while simulating adaptive mitigation pathways under uncertainty. Leveraging HPC capabilities, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating graph neural networks (GNNs) to map risk interdependencies, multi-agent reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate stakeholder decision dynamics, and discrete-event simulations to model cascading schedule impacts. The framework will ingest real-time data streams from IoT sensors, procurement databases, and geopolitical event feeds, processed through a scalable pipeline to update risk probabilities and mitigation ROI estimates. Key innovations include a stochastic scenario generator for stress-testing contingency plans and a combinatorial optimization layer to balance cost, safety, and sustainability constraints. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool that identifies high-probability risk cascades and recommends prioritized interventions, validated against historical data from three transnational infrastructure projects. This work aims to advance computational decision support systems in construction management by addressing latency and scalability barriers in existing software, ultimately reducing average project overruns by an estimated 12–18%. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 10^6+ scenario permutations per hour, surpassing current desktop-based solutions by three orders of magnitude. Findings will contribute methodological insights to the emerging field of adaptive resilience engineering in built environment management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: The development of advanced materials for renewable energy applications is hindered by the inefficiency of traditional experimental methods, which struggle to explore vast chemical spaces. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to accelerate the discovery and optimization of next-generation photovoltaic and energy storage materials. We propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating quantum mechanical simulations, molecular dynamics, and machine learning (ML) models to predict material properties, stability, and performance. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations will be employed to screen candidate materials at the atomic scale, while large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will assess mesoscale behaviors under operational conditions. ML algorithms, trained on these datasets, will establish structure-property relationships and guide the iterative design of novel compositions. The computational demands of this approach—including massive parameter space sampling, ab initio calculations requiring thousands of CPU cores, and neural network training on GPU clusters—necessitate access to HPC resources. Expected outcomes include the identification of three promising material systems with ≥20% improved energy conversion or storage efficiency compared to existing benchmarks, validated through experimental collaborations. Additionally, the project will generate open-source software tools for automated material screening, enabling broader community adoption of computational discovery workflows. By bridging quantum-scale insights with macroscale performance predictions, this research aims to establish a paradigm shift in materials development cycles, directly supporting global transitions to sustainable energy technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in science technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the dynamic interactions between large-scale neural networks and synaptic plasticity mechanisms underlying adaptive behavior, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in simulating biologically realistic neural systems. A central challenge in neuroscience lies in bridging the gap between microscale synaptic events and macroscale network dynamics, particularly in systems where plasticity rules interact nonlinearly with spatiotemporal activity patterns. Current models either oversimplify biophysical detail or lack the scalability to capture emergent phenomena in mammalian cortical networks. To address this, we will develop a hybrid computational framework integrating biophysically detailed neuron models with empirically derived synaptic plasticity rules, simulating networks of up to 10^5 neurons with millisecond temporal resolution. The HPC implementation will utilize parallelized NEURON and NEST simulations optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters, coupled with custom algorithms for spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) parameter optimization. Resource-intensive components include Monte Carlo sampling of plasticity parameter space, real-time spike pattern analysis during learning phases, and multi-scale data integration from in vitro electrophysiology experiments. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of critical plasticity thresholds governing network stability during learning, 2) predictive models linking specific STDP variants to distinct oscillation patterns observed in vivo, and 3) open-source tools for simulating plasticity in large-scale networks. This work will directly advance our understanding of how synaptic adaptability shapes functional neural circuits, with implications for developing targeted interventions in neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by plasticity dysregulation. The requested computing resources are essential for achieving the necessary temporal and spatial resolution to capture emergent network properties inaccessible through conventional cluster computing or reduced-model approaches.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in neurobiology and neurosciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the computational analysis of understudied ancient Near Eastern languages, with a focus on reconstructing fragmented texts and modeling linguistic evolution across regional dialects. The primary research problem lies in the scarcity of computational tools capable of processing the complex morphosyntactic structures and non-Latin scripts of languages such as Akkadian, Ugaritic, and Sabaean, compounded by the fragmented nature of surviving inscriptions. Traditional manual methods struggle to scale with the growing digitization of epigraphic corpora, hindering systematic comparative analysis. The project proposes a dual computational approach: (1) training transformer-based language models on curated corpora of cuneiform and Semitic texts to automate syntactic parsing and semantic disambiguation, and (2) developing a graph-based framework to model diachronic linguistic changes across 2nd–1st millennium BCE Levantine dialects. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of high-resolution 3D scans of inscriptions (from partner institutions’ digitization initiatives) using convolutional neural networks to improve character recognition accuracy in degraded texts. Additionally, phylogenetic algorithms will be applied to trace phonological shifts between Bronze Age Canaanite dialects. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for ancient language analysis, a diachronic lexicon of Northwest Semitic variants, and probabilistic reconstructions of damaged liturgical texts from the Amarna corpus. This work will significantly advance methodological capacity in computational philology, providing scalable solutions for cross-dialectal comparison and enabling new insights into language contact phenomena in ancient Levantine scribal traditions. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks, including training multilingual models on distributed GPU clusters and processing terabyte-scale datasets of inscribed artifact imagery.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Ancient Near Eastern and Biblical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the extinct Semitic and/or Non-Semitic languages spoken in the ancient Near East, including those used to write historical Jewish and Christian religious texts. These languages include, but are not limited to, Egyptian/Coptic, Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian, Assyrian, Aramaic, Canaanite, Phoenician, Samarian, Ugaritic, Syriac, Mandean, Hattic, Elamite, Hurrian, Hittite, Urartian, Lydian, Luwian, Lycian, Palaic, Sabaean/South Arabian, and other associated languages. Includes instruction in philology, epigraphy, papyrology, numismatics, and textual studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model the dynamics of transference and countertransference in psychodynamic psychotherapy, a core yet understudied mechanism of therapeutic change. Traditional psychoanalytic research relies heavily on qualitative case studies, limiting scalability and generalizability. The computational complexity of simulating dyadic interactions—incorporating linguistic, affective, and behavioral data from therapist-patient sessions—exceeds the capacity of standard analytical tools. We propose developing a neural network framework to analyze multimodal datasets (e.g., session transcripts, vocal prosody, physiological markers) from 500+ anonymized therapy cases. The model will map patterns of transference enactment, therapist response strategies, and their correlation with clinical outcomes (e.g., symptom reduction, alliance strength). HPC resources will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional time-series data and Monte Carlo simulations to test competing psychodynamic hypotheses about intervention efficacy. A secondary aim involves generative AI to create synthetic patient profiles for therapist training, calibrated against empirical data on transference resolution. Outcomes will include open-source tools for quantifying therapeutic process variables historically deemed “unmeasurable,” advancing evidence-based frameworks for psychoanalytic practice. This work bridges computational linguistics, affective computing, and clinical theory, offering a novel paradigm to investigate how unconscious relational patterns manifest and shift in treatment—a critical step toward personalized, mechanism-driven psychotherapy.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung. Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The integration of sustainable tourism practices within natural resource settings requires advanced tools to model complex socio-ecological systems, yet current approaches often lack the computational capacity to capture dynamic interactions between visitor behavior, ecosystem resilience, and policy scenarios. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution simulation framework to optimize tourism planning while minimizing environmental degradation in protected areas. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning, we will simulate visitor movement patterns, resource utilization, and ecological impacts across diverse landscapes under varying climate and management conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-scale datasets, including geospatial layers of habitat sensitivity, real-time visitor tracking data, and climate projections, while running computationally intensive parameter sweeps to identify sustainable carrying capacities. The models will integrate stakeholder-defined thresholds for ecological disturbance and visitor satisfaction, enabling iterative testing of adaptive management strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to forecast site-specific tourism pressures under climate change, identify conflict zones between recreation and conservation goals, and evaluate trade-offs in proposed infrastructure development. Results will directly inform land management agencies and tourism operators in designing spatially explicit, data-driven policies that align with regional biodiversity targets and cultural heritage preservation efforts. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project advances the methodological rigor of sustainable tourism research, offering scalable solutions for balancing economic viability with long-term ecosystem health in natural resource-dependent communities.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Recreation and Tourism
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, and manage tourism in a natural resource setting, with an emphasis on applying environmentally sound, culturally sensitive, and economically sustainable principles. Includes instruction in environmental studies; natural resource management and interpretation; tourism planning, management, and policies; public land use management and policies; communications; marketing; and public relations.

abstract: Ornamental horticulture faces pressing challenges in optimizing plant breeding and environmental adaptation to meet evolving aesthetic, commercial, and climate-resilience demands. Current breeding programs for ornamental species, such as roses, orchids, and ornamental grasses, rely on time-consuming phenotypic evaluations and trial-and-error approaches to select traits like flower morphology, drought tolerance, and disease resistance. This project seeks to accelerate the development of novel ornamental varieties by integrating genomic prediction models with high-resolution environmental simulations, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to analyze large-scale genomic datasets (e.g., whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq) from diverse ornamental plant populations to identify candidate genes and regulatory networks associated with target traits. Concurrently, we will simulate microclimate conditions across urban and managed landscapes using fluid dynamics and radiative transfer models to predict genotype-by-environment interactions. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to link genomic and environmental data, enabling predictive selection of optimal genotypes for specific design applications and climate scenarios. The computational workflow will require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling for Bayesian genomic prediction, and iterative training of deep neural networks. Access to HPC resources is critical to manage these computationally intensive tasks within biologically relevant timeframes. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for trait heritability and plasticity in key ornamental species, (2) optimized breeding strategies to reduce trial cycles by 30–50%, and (3) open-access databases linking genomic markers to design-relevant phenotypes. This work will directly support horticultural industries in developing climate-resilient, resource-efficient ornamental varieties while advancing computational methods for complex trait prediction in non-model plant systems. Results will be disseminated through plant science journals and partnerships with commercial nurseries and landscape design firms.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on domesticated plants and plant materials used for decorative and recreational applications and prepares individuals to breed, grow, and utilize ornamental plant varieties for commercial and aesthetic purposes. Includes instruction in applicable plant science subjects, the environmental design and artistic aspects of horticultural product usage, and the management of horticultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in correctional facility resource allocation through advanced computational modeling, with the goal of optimizing rehabilitation outcomes while reducing operational costs. Despite evidence-based practices in corrections administration, facilities struggle to dynamically align staffing, programming, and infrastructure with fluctuating inmate populations and complex behavioral needs. Current decision-making relies on static protocols ill-suited to real-time operational demands, contributing to suboptimal rehabilitation rates and recidivism. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate facility operations under variable constraints, integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of inmate behavior, system dynamics models of institutional workflows, and machine learning-driven risk prediction. The ABM component will simulate individual and group interactions influenced by program participation, staff-inmate ratios, and environmental stressors, while system dynamics models will map resource flows across educational, therapeutic, and custodial functions. Machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized historical data—including inmate demographics, program completion rates, and post-release outcomes—will identify critical leverage points for intervention. By deploying these models on HPC infrastructure, we will perform multi-scale optimization analyses to test hypothetical scenarios, such as adaptive scheduling of cognitive behavioral therapy sessions or reallocation of security personnel during program hours. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of forecasting the cascading impacts of resource allocation choices on safety, rehabilitation metrics, and budgetary outcomes. This work bridges correctional theory with computational social science, offering a novel paradigm for data-driven facility management. Successful implementation could inform policy frameworks for dynamic resource distribution in correctional systems, potentially reducing recidivism by 10-15% in modeled scenarios while maintaining operational safety standards. The computational architecture developed will be scalable to diverse facility types, establishing a template for evidence-based corrections administration in an era of constrained resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision agriculture strategies for optimizing crop yield resilience under dynamic environmental stressors. A critical challenge in modern crop production is predicting how genotype-environment-management (G×E×M) interactions influence phenotypic outcomes across diverse agroecosystems. Traditional field trials and simplified statistical models lack the resolution to account for the nonlinear interactions between genetic traits, soil heterogeneity, microclimate variability, and pest pressures. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating mechanistic crop growth models, machine learning, and spatially explicit environmental datasets. The research will parameterize process-based models (e.g., APSIM, DSSAT) with high-resolution soil moisture data, drone-derived canopy imagery, and genomic markers linked to stress tolerance in staple crops. Bayesian optimization algorithms will identify management interventions that maximize yield stability under simulated drought, heat, and pest infestation scenarios. A key innovation involves coupling agent-based pest dispersal models with crop physiology simulations to evaluate integrated pest management strategies at landscape scales. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the iterative nature of ensemble climate simulations (CMIP6 downscaled projections), parameter calibration across millions of genotype-environment combinations, and real-time sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include open-source decision support tools for farmers, optimized cultivar recommendations tailored to regional climate forecasts, and dynamically updated risk maps for pest outbreaks. By elucidating G×E×M trade-offs, this work will directly inform breeding programs and sustainable intensification practices, enhancing food security while minimizing input waste. The requested HPC resources will enable the scaling of simulations to cover major U.S. agricultural regions, with methodology transferable to global cropping systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cultivate grain, fiber, forage, oilseed, fruits and nuts, vegetables, and other domesticated plant products. Includes instruction in basic principles of plant science, health, and nutrition as applied to particular species and breeds; soil preparation and irrigation; pest management; planting and harvesting operations; product marketing; and applicable issues of safety, regulation, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on cultural transmission and community resilience in Appalachia through the analysis of large-scale, unstructured datasets. Traditional methodologies in Appalachian Studies often prioritize qualitative, small-scale analyses of cultural artifacts, oral histories, and linguistic patterns, which can limit the scope of identifying region-wide trends or connections. To address this gap, the proposed research will computationally analyze digitized collections of Appalachian folk music recordings, oral history transcripts, and vernacular writings (e.g., diaries, letters) spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. These datasets, totaling approximately 15 TB, require advanced natural language processing (NLP) and audio signal processing techniques to systematically identify linguistic dialects, musical motifs, and narrative themes across diverse subregions. Computational workflows will include transformer-based models for dialect classification, graph-based network analysis to map cultural exchange patterns among communities, and unsupervised clustering algorithms to detect temporal shifts in storytelling traditions. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC nodes, the project aims to resolve bottlenecks in processing heterogeneous data formats and improve the scalability of semantic and acoustic feature extraction. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated datasets, visualizations of cultural connectivity, and statistical models quantifying the influence of migration and industrialization on Appalachian cultural practices. This work will provide novel insights into how Appalachia’s distinct identity has been preserved and transformed, offering a framework for integrating computational tools into humanities-driven regional studies. The requested resources—particularly GPU nodes for deep learning and high-memory nodes for large graph computations—are critical to achieving these objectives within the project timeline.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, sociology, culture, and economics of the Appalachian region of the United States. Includes instruction in contemporary issues in Appalachia, political economy of Appalachia, community-based research, ethnomusicology, and oral and written languages of Appalachia.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address a critical gap in the operational and educational frameworks of wine stewardship: the systematic prediction of optimal wine storage conditions and aging trajectories across diverse environmental and varietal contexts. Traditional approaches to wine program management rely on generalized guidelines and experiential knowledge, which often fail to account for the complex interplay of chemical, microbial, and environmental variables that influence wine evolution. The research problem centers on developing a predictive model that integrates multi-scale data—including regional climate patterns, cellar microclimates, wine composition analytics, and sensory outcomes—to generate dynamic, site-specific storage protocols. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations, the computational approach will simulate the degradation and maturation processes of key wine compounds (e.g., phenolics, esters) under variable temperature, humidity, and vibration conditions. Machine learning algorithms will then correlate these simulations with sensory data from historical aging benchmarks to predict quality outcomes. The project will utilize HPC resources to manage the high dimensionality of input datasets (e.g., multi-year climate records, spectral wine analyses) and the computational intensity of iterative, stochastic simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision-support tool for sommeliers and wine educators, enabling data-driven storage strategies that minimize spoilage risks and optimize sensory profiles. By bridging enology, data science, and hospitality management, this research aims to establish a novel computational paradigm for wine program sustainability, enhancing both pedagogical resources and industry practices in a field traditionally dominated by qualitative methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage wine selection, purchasing, storage, sales, and service for a variety of establishments in the hospitality industry. Includes instruction in wine production, wine regions of the world, wine tasting, food and wine matching, service techniques, and wine program management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing adaptive learning systems in educational technology through advanced computational modeling. Current adaptive platforms struggle to dynamically adjust content complexity, pacing, and modality in real time while accounting for diverse learner behaviors, cognitive states, and multimodal interaction data. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates machine learning, natural language processing, and agent-based simulations to model learner-system interactions at scale. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures to process real-time streams of eye-tracking, clickstream, and biometric data from 5,000+ simulated learners, paired with transformer-based analysis of open-response inputs. A parallelized reinforcement learning system will iteratively optimize instructional pathways using these multimodal inputs, with computational experiments comparing the efficacy of centralized versus federated learning approaches for scalability. The project requires HPC resources to manage the high-dimensional parameter space of adaptive algorithms, sustain low-latency inference during concurrent user simulations, and train foundation models on synthetic datasets representing diverse pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model for granular, real-time adaptation in digital learning environments, (2) benchmarks for resource-efficient deployment of AI-driven personalization in educational technology, and (3) open-source tools enabling researchers to simulate large-scale learning ecosystems with embedded ethical constraints. By advancing the computational infrastructure for next-generation adaptive learning, this work aims to bridge gaps between educational theory and implementable AI systems while establishing performance standards for responsible use of intensive computing in instructional design.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, computer applications, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the optimization of outdoor fitness equipment design in public parks, addressing a critical gap in equitable access to inclusive recreational infrastructure. Current park fitness equipment often fails to accommodate diverse user demographics, including varying age groups, physical abilities, and biomechanical needs, leading to underutilization or injury risks. To address this, the research will employ a multi-scale computational framework integrating biomechanical modeling, machine learning (ML), and agent-based simulations. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distributions on equipment under diverse usage scenarios, while motion-capture-derived datasets will train ML algorithms to predict kinematic outcomes for users with differing physiques and mobility constraints. Agent-based models will simulate population-level interactions with equipment layouts, incorporating behavioral data to assess accessibility and engagement patterns. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine design parameters—such as material composition, ergonomic geometry, and spatial arrangement—to maximize safety, usability, and inclusivity. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for adaptive equipment design and evidence-based guidelines for park planners to deploy configurations that serve heterogeneous communities. By bridging kinesiology, materials science, and computational social dynamics, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for data-driven recreational infrastructure that enhances public health equity. The project’s scale—requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations and large-scale ML training—necessitates HPC resources to achieve practical timelines. Results will inform municipal policy and park design standards, fostering environments that promote sustained physical activity across populations.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, Leisure, Fitness, and Kinesiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and kinesiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in digital textile pattern optimization, a critical challenge in apparel manufacturing that intersects computational design, material science, and industrial engineering. Traditional methods for generating and validating textile patterns rely on iterative manual adjustments and physical prototyping, leading to prolonged development cycles, material waste, and limited scalability for custom or adaptive designs. To overcome these constraints, the research proposes a computational framework integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate and optimize textile patterns under dynamic mechanical and aesthetic constraints. The project will develop machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets—including fabric tensile properties, historical design archives, and consumer preference metrics—to generate pattern variations that balance structural integrity, material efficiency, and stylistic coherence. Concurrently, FEA simulations will model stress distribution and drape behavior across diverse body geometries and movement scenarios, enabling virtual validation of digitally generated patterns before physical production. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-resolution textile datasets, parallelizing computationally intensive FEA workloads, and iterating GAN architectures at scale. Anticipated outcomes include a reduction in physical prototyping by 40–60%, a predictive framework for sustainable material utilization, and novel methods for mass-customized apparel production. By bridging gaps between computational design automation and industrial textile workflows, this research aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven manufacturing in non-science and engineering domains, with potential applications in adaptive fashion, wearable technology, and circular economy initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and production of textile products and related processes and systems. Includes instruction in functional and aesthetic design, human factors research, production planning, manufacturing processes, quality assessment, and distribution systems.

abstract: Livestock production systems face growing pressure to enhance efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare while meeting global food demands. A critical barrier lies in optimizing complex, interacting factors—genetics, nutrition, housing environments, and health management—across dynamic production scales. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to model these multidimensional interactions efficiently, particularly when scaling from individual animals to herd-level outcomes. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating genomic, physiological, and environmental data for predictive livestock management. Using machine learning and agent-based modeling, we will simulate interactions between genetic traits (e.g., feed efficiency, disease resilience), real-time sensor data from precision livestock farming systems (e.g., thermal imaging, activity monitors), and facility design parameters (e.g., ventilation, space allocation). Genomic datasets from cattle and poultry populations will be analyzed via genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify markers linked to stress tolerance and productivity, while finite element modeling will assess airflow and waste management in housing systems. The HPC environment is essential for training deep learning models on high-dimensional datasets (genomic sequences, sensor streams) and running parallelized simulations of herd dynamics under varying management scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize feed formulations, breeding selections, and facility designs tailored to regional climates and production goals. By resolving nonlinear interactions between biological and environmental variables, this work will advance precision livestock strategies, reduce resource waste, and inform welfare-centered policies. The computational pipeline will be shared via open-source platforms to support scalable decision-making in diverse agricultural systems, directly contributing to resilient food production frameworks under evolving climatic and market pressures.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, breed, care for, process, and market livestock and small farm animals. Includes instruction in basic animal science, animal nutrition, and animal health as applied to various species and breeds; design and operation of housing, feeding, and processing facilities; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual analysis study examining linguistic and structural patterns in understudied multilingual manuscripts from the early modern period (1500–1800). The research addresses a critical gap in digital humanities scholarship: the computational limitations of analyzing heterogeneous, non-Latin script texts at scale, which have hindered efforts to trace cross-cultural literary influences and linguistic evolution. Existing tools struggle with the volume (over 10,000 digitized manuscripts) and complexity (mix of Arabic, Ottoman Turkish, Persian, and regional dialects) of the corpus, requiring advanced computational capacity to process OCR corrections, syntactic annotations, and network-based modeling. The proposed methodology combines transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for historical languages with graph neural networks to map semantic shifts and intertextual connections across temporal and geographic axes. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale textual data, distributed training of multilingual embedding models, and dynamic visualization of manuscript networks through GPU-accelerated graph analytics. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital catalog of cross-referenced thematic motifs in early modern Eurasian texts, an open-source pipeline for multilingual manuscript analysis, and a public interactive platform showcasing diffusion patterns of narrative structures. By overcoming current bottlenecks in processing speed and model scalability, this work will establish new benchmarks for computational textual studies while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between humanities scholars and data scientists. The resource request specifically targets GPU nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for graph computations, ensuring rigorous validation of hypotheses about transregional literary exchange.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in digital humanities and textual studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational modeling of cross-linguistic syntactic variation in under-resourced languages, with a focus on Uralic and Turkic language families. The research addresses a critical gap in linguistic typology: while large-language models (LLMs) and computational tools have transformed the analysis of widely spoken languages, many low-resource languages lack sufficient digital corpora and syntactic annotations to support robust comparative studies. This limitation impedes progress in understanding universal grammar principles, contact-induced language change, and the historical development of morphosyntactic features. The project’s computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques with rule-based syntactic parsing to analyze parallel texts, oral narratives, and newly digitized archival materials across 15 target languages. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on fragmented, morphologically complex datasets and for running large-scale simulations of syntactic change under varying contact scenarios. Key tasks include the development of automated annotation pipelines for agglutinative structures, probabilistic modeling of case-marking patterns, and clustering analyses to identify areal linguistic features. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access repository of syntactically annotated corpora for Uralic and Turkic languages, (2) computational evidence supporting or revising existing hypotheses about genealogical vs. areal influences in Eurasian language evolution, and (3) methodological frameworks adaptable to other low-resource language families. By combining linguistic theory with advanced computational methods, this work will provide novel insights into language diversity while establishing scalable tools for resource-light syntactic analysis, directly supporting global efforts to document and revitalize endangered languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Foreign Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled optimization framework for resilient and sustainable supply chain networks under stochastic disruptions. Modern supply chains face compounding challenges from demand volatility, geopolitical risks, and sustainability mandates, necessitating computational tools capable of modeling complex interdependencies across procurement, production, and distribution systems. Current methods struggle to balance cost efficiency, carbon footprint reduction, and disruption mitigation at scale, particularly when handling multivariate uncertainty. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating agent-based simulation, multi-objective stochastic optimization, and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. Agent-based models will represent supplier, manufacturer, and logistics provider behaviors, while Monte Carlo methods simulate disruptions such as raw material shortages or transportation delays. A parallelized genetic algorithm will optimize inventory allocation, facility location, and routing decisions across conflicting objectives (cost, emissions, service levels). Deep reinforcement learning components will train adaptive contingency policies using historical disruption data. The scale of these simulations—encompassing thousands of agents, multi-echelon networks, and decade-long horizon analyses—requires HPC resources for tractable computation. Expected outcomes include a decision support system that identifies Pareto-optimal strategies under uncertainty, quantifies trade-offs between resilience and sustainability metrics, and prescribes dynamic reconfiguration policies. This work will advance computational logistics by demonstrating how HPC enables granular, system-wide optimization previously constrained by memory and processing limits. Results will be validated against real-world data from automotive and pharmaceutical supply chains, with open-source release of core simulation modules to benefit both academic research and industry practitioners. The project directly aligns with program goals by innovating resource allocation methodologies for complex logistical systems while addressing pressing operational and environmental challenges.
cip_title: Logistics, Materials, and Supply Chain Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and coordinate all logistical functions in an enterprise, ranging from acquisitions to receiving and handling, through internal allocation of resources to operations units, to the handling and delivery of output. Includes instruction in acquisitions and purchasing, inventory control, storage and handling, just-in-time manufacturing, logistics planning, shipping and delivery management, transportation, quality control, resource estimation and allocation, and budgeting.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamic interplay between digital pedagogies and religious education across diverse faith communities. While traditional religious education research has focused on curriculum design or qualitative assessments of classroom outcomes, this study addresses a critical gap: quantifying how emerging technologies—such as virtual reality (VR) environments, AI-driven personalized learning tools, and cross-cultural digital storytelling platforms—affect the retention, engagement, and spiritual development of learners in multi-religious contexts. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable frameworks to model complex, nonlinear interactions between pedagogical strategies, cultural variables, and learner behaviors in digitally mediated religious instruction. Using anonymized datasets from interfaith education platforms (spanning Christian, Islamic, Jewish, Hindu, and Buddhist communities), we will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze textual interactions in virtual classrooms, agent-based modeling to simulate long-term educational outcomes under varying technological interventions, and network analysis to map knowledge transfer patterns across demographic boundaries. Computational demands arise from processing multilingual sacred texts integrated with real-time behavioral data (eye-tracking, response latency) from VR sessions, requiring parallelized workflows for semantic analysis and GPU-accelerated neural networks to identify latent pedagogical efficacy markers. Expected outcomes include a predictive model for optimizing faith-specific digital curricula and a taxonomy of intercultural learning barriers in hybrid religious education spaces. By establishing quantitative bridges between computational social science and theological instruction methodologies, this work aims to inform equitable resource allocation for understudied religious minorities in increasingly technologized educational landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of providing educational services to members of faith communities, within the context of a particular religion, and that prepares individuals to serve as religious educators. Includes instruction in planning and teaching lessons, organizing and supervising instructional activities, designing and developing instructional materials, and administering religious education programs and facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on cultural and intellectual exchange across medieval and Renaissance Europe through the computational analysis of fragmented historical datasets. Traditional scholarship in this domain has been constrained by the manual processing of disparate sources—including digitized manuscripts, archival records, art inventories, and archaeological reports—limiting the scale at which patterns of transmission can be identified. The proposed research will integrate natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning to systematically analyze multilingual textual corpora, artistic iconography, and material culture data spanning the 12th to 16th centuries. Key objectives include modeling the diffusion of literary motifs, reconstructing trade and pilgrimage routes using geospatial datasets, and identifying socio-cultural hubs through dynamic network simulations. HPC resources are critical to process terabytes of high-resolution manuscript images, optimize OCR accuracy for archaic scripts, and train neural networks to detect stylistic correlations in art and architecture. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated datasets, interactive maps visualizing transnational exchange networks, and computational models that quantify the impact of specific institutions (e.g., monastic scriptoria, merchant guilds) on cultural dissemination. By bridging gaps between textual, artistic, and archaeological evidence, this project aims to reveal previously unrecognized pathways of influence, enriching scholarly debates on regional identity formation and the transmission of knowledge. The tools and methodologies developed will establish a scalable framework for computational humanities research, enabling future studies to interrogate large, heterogeneous datasets with greater precision. This work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in addressing complex historical questions that transcend disciplinary boundaries.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the Medieval and/or Renaissance periods in European and circum-Mediterranean history from the perspective of various disciplines in the humanities and social sciences, including history and archeology, as well as studies of period art and music.

abstract: Medical toxicology faces critical challenges in predicting and mitigating complex toxicological interactions, particularly in cases involving novel synthetic drugs, environmental toxins, and chemical threat agents. Current clinical decision-making relies heavily on historical data and generalized treatment protocols, which inadequately address individual variability in toxin metabolism, polymedicated patients, or exposures to uncharacterized substances. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to model toxin-host interactions, predict clinical outcomes, and optimize personalized treatment strategies using high-performance computing (HPC). Leveraging clinical data from poison control centers, electronic health records, and toxicogenomic databases, we will employ machine learning to identify biomarkers of toxicity severity and build predictive models for acute poisoning scenarios. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize binding affinities between emergent synthetic opioids and opioid receptors, as well as antidote-receptor interactions, to guide antidote development and dosing. Network pharmacology approaches will evaluate multi-toxin synergies in cases of polysubstance overdose. HPC resources are essential for processing multi-terabyte datasets, running large-scale parallelized simulations of toxin-receptor systems, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for renal/hepatic toxicity risk stratification, computational tools for rapid identification of unknown toxins via mass spectrometry pattern recognition, and simulation-based protocols for antidote administration in mass exposure events. This work will directly enhance clinical capabilities in managing complex toxicological emergencies, reduce diagnostic delays, and provide a foundation for data-driven precision toxicology. The developed models will be deployed as open-access clinical decision support tools, benefiting both acute care providers and public health preparedness initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians who specialize in the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and monitoring of injury and illness from exposures to drugs and chemicals, as well as exposures to biological and radiological agents. Important areas include acute drug poisoning; adverse drug events; drug abuse, addiction, and withdrawal; chemicals and hazardous materials; terrorism preparedness; venomous bites and stings; and environmental and workplace exposures.

abstract: The integration of multi-omics data and advanced analytical techniques in chemical pathology has generated vast, high-dimensional datasets, challenging conventional computational tools in scalability and precision. Current methods for biomarker discovery, diagnostic algorithm development, and laboratory workflow optimization often lack the capacity to process heterogeneous datasets—including metabolomic, proteomic, and clinical laboratory data—while accounting for complex biochemical interactions. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy scalable computational workflows for predictive modeling, data integration, and real-time analytics in chemical pathology. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning models to identify novel diagnostic biomarkers from multi-omics datasets, (2) simulating molecular interactions to optimize assay design for high-throughput clinical instruments, and (3) implementing AI-driven tools for error detection and resource allocation in laboratory management. Computational methods will include large-scale parallelization of molecular dynamics simulations, ensemble learning for biomarker classification, and graph-based algorithms to model laboratory workflow efficiency. HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, reduce runtime for complex simulations, and support the training of deep neural networks on integrated clinical and analytical data. Expected outcomes include the discovery of clinically actionable biomarkers for metabolic disorders, improved accuracy in automated assay validation, and data-driven protocols to minimize diagnostic turnaround times. This work will advance precision diagnostics by bridging gaps between analytical chemistry, clinical data science, and laboratory operations, directly impacting patient care through faster, more reliable pathological assessments. The computational frameworks developed will be disseminated as open-source tools to promote reproducibility and adoption in clinical laboratories globally.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use and interpretation of chemical analyses, chemical diagnoses and management, and the supervision of chemical pathology laboratories. May included related research in basic and applied analytical chemical pathology; instrumentation data processing and chemical laboratory management.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance evidence-based interventions for student behavioral challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-source educational and psychological data. School psychologists face growing demands to synthesize large-scale datasets—including academic performance metrics, behavioral assessments, socio-environmental factors, and intervention outcomes—to identify patterns and optimize support strategies. However, traditional statistical methods often fail to capture nonlinear interactions among variables or scale efficiently for longitudinal and population-level analyses. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models to predict intervention efficacy and classify risk profiles using integrated datasets from diverse school systems. Computational workflows will include feature engineering to operationalize developmental and contextual factors (e.g., classroom climate, peer dynamics), ensemble learning to model heterogeneous student trajectories, and sensitivity analyses to prioritize modifiable intervention targets. HPC resources are critical for training models on high-dimensional data spanning thousands of students, enabling parallel processing for cross-validation and real-time simulation of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool for school psychologists to generate personalized intervention recommendations and system-level insights into resource allocation. By bridging computational advances with applied psychological practice, this work aims to reduce disparities in behavioral support access and improve the scalability of data-driven decision-making in school settings. The project aligns with the ethical imperatives of school psychology by incorporating fairness-aware algorithms and stakeholder feedback loops to ensure equitable, transparent model outputs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the implementation of public policies in complex administrative systems, with a focus on improving equity and efficiency in resource distribution. The research problem centers on the challenge of simulating dynamic interactions between policy design, administrative capacity, and real-world outcomes—particularly in contexts where decentralized decision-making and multi-agency coordination introduce unpredictability. Traditional linear models often fail to account for emergent behaviors, stakeholder adaptation, or cascading delays in resource flows, limiting their utility for proactive policy adjustment. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with machine learning techniques to simulate how administrative structures, policy rules, and resource allocation mechanisms interact across hierarchical systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale simulations capturing 1) millions of agent interactions across synthetic populations representing diverse demographics, 2) probabilistic scenarios of administrative compliance and capacity constraints, and 3) multi-objective optimization of policy parameters under budgetary and equity constraints. The computational approach will leverage parallel processing to iteratively test policy implementations across virtual environments calibrated with historical data from municipal service delivery programs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that identifies administrative bottlenecks, predicts unintended consequences of policy designs, and recommends adaptive allocation strategies. This work will contribute novel methodologies to public policy analysis by bridging computational social science with public administration theory, offering actionable insights for designing robust, evidence-based policies. The requested resources will enable simulations at sufficient scale and resolution to inform real-world policy decisions while maintaining computational fidelity to complex social and administrative systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Policy and Public Administration with an emphasis on issues related to public policy. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, principles of public administration; the management of public policy; and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the design and analysis of civil infrastructure systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Civil drafting and engineering workflows increasingly rely on high-fidelity simulations to address complex challenges such as geological variability, dynamic load distributions, and environmental constraints. However, traditional CAD/CADD tools often lack the scalability to process large-scale datasets or perform real-time simulations of multi-physics systems, particularly for infrastructure projects in seismically active or environmentally sensitive regions. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML)-driven design optimization, and parametric modeling to enhance the precision and efficiency of civil engineering simulations. The project will leverage HPC resources to parallelize finite element meshing for geological stability assessments, automate topology optimization of structural components, and simulate fluid-structure interactions in drainage and flood mitigation systems. A key innovation involves integrating AI-assisted generative design algorithms with CADD workflows to iteratively refine blueprints under multi-objective constraints (e.g., material costs, carbon footprint, and seismic resilience). By deploying containerized computational environments on HPC clusters, we aim to reduce simulation runtime for large-scale urban planning scenarios by 60–75% compared to current workstation-based methods. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for GPU-accelerated civil infrastructure simulations, validated against physical scale models and field data from ongoing highway and wastewater management projects. This work will directly support curriculum development in computational civil engineering, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-aided design while advancing industry adoption of resource-efficient, data-driven drafting methodologies. The resource allocation will enable critical benchmarks of distributed memory architectures for processing LiDAR-derived terrain models and automating compliance checks against evolving building codes.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing water supply systems through advanced computational modeling, with a focus on mitigating inefficiencies and failures in urban and residential plumbing networks. Aging infrastructure, dynamic pressure fluctuations, and increasing demand for sustainable water management necessitate high-fidelity simulations to predict system behavior under diverse operational and environmental conditions. The primary research problem centers on the inability of conventional modeling approaches to capture the complex interactions between hydraulic dynamics, material degradation, and real-time demand variability at scale. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning, and network topology optimization. The CFD models will simulate transient flow phenomena, including water hammer effects and leak-induced pressure drops, across large-scale pipe networks, while machine learning algorithms will analyze historical failure data and sensor-derived operational metrics to predict vulnerability hotspots. Concurrently, graph-based optimization methods will evaluate system configurations to balance efficiency, cost, and resilience. The computational intensity of coupling these methods—particularly the need for parallelized solvers to handle millions of mesh elements in 3D pipe networks and terabytes of sensor data—requires the distributed memory and GPU acceleration capabilities of HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for proactive maintenance scheduling, validated strategies for pressure surge mitigation, and data-driven design standards to reduce water loss by an estimated 15–20% in testbed systems. By enhancing the precision of failure prediction and system optimization, this research aims to directly support sustainable water management practices, reduce infrastructure costs, and improve public health outcomes through more reliable contamination risk mitigation. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will be adaptable to diverse plumbing architectures, from municipal supply networks to high-rise building systems.
cip_title: Plumbing and Related Water Supply Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plumbing and related water supply services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address gaps in understanding the evolution of Western polyphonic compositional practices between the 14th and 16th centuries by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale musical datasets. While historical musicology has traditionally relied on manual score analysis, the sheer volume of surviving manuscripts—coupled with complex intertextual relationships between works—has hindered systematic study of stylistic transitions, regional influences, and theoretical innovations. Our research will computationally process digitized musical corpora, including the Digital Image Archive of Medieval Music and the Josquin Research Project, using optical music recognition (OMR) adapted for early notation systems. Converted symbolic data will undergo feature extraction for harmonic progressions, contrapuntal patterns, and cadential structures through custom Python pipelines integrating music21 and librosa. Machine learning models (LSTMs, transformer networks) will then identify temporal and geographic patterns in compositional techniques, trained on metadata-rich subsets before scaling to full corpora. HPC resources are critical for managing storage demands (50+ TB of high-resolution manuscript images), parallel processing of OMR workflows, and training complex models across thousands of scores. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of analyzed works, quantitative maps of stylistic diffusion across Europe, and detection of previously unrecognized theoretical treatise influences on compositional practice. By bridging computational methods with musicological expertise, this work will enable novel insights into Renaissance musical networks while establishing reproducible frameworks for computational music analysis.
