HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on heterogeneous datasets spanning slapstick, satire, and sketch comedy, as well as for real-time analysis of improvisational workflows in simulated performance environments. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for quantifying comedic “success” across contexts, (2) tools to assist writers in optimizing pacing and joke density via generative AI, and (3) datasets mapping the evolution of comedic tropes in relation to societal shifts. By bridging computational methods with performance theory, this work aims to expand scholarly understanding of comedy’s adaptive mechanisms while creating practical resources for creators. The project’s scale—processing over 10,000 hours of performance data and 50,000 textual sources—necessitates HPC capabilities to manage parallelized model training, multimodal data fusion, and high-throughput simulations of live audience interactions. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools tailored for performing arts researchers and partnerships with comedy production networks.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical, cultural, and theoretical dimensions of comedy as an art form, and the writing, performance, and production of comedy. Includes instruction in comedic storytelling, comedy production, comedy writing, history of comedy, improvisation, and sketch writing.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a machine learning-driven framework for optimizing dynamic credit risk assessment in decentralized financial ecosystems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address latency and scalability challenges inherent to real-time, multi-agent credit networks. Traditional credit management models struggle to adapt to emerging decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms and blockchain-based lending protocols, where creditworthiness must be evaluated across heterogeneous, pseudonymous entities without centralized oversight. The computational problem centers on training ensemble models to predict default probabilities using high-dimensional transaction graphs, temporal behavioral data, and cross-chain collateralization patterns—datasets that exceed the processing capabilities of conventional systems. The proposed methodology combines graph neural networks (GNNs) for modeling transactional interdependencies with transformer architectures to interpret sequential financial behaviors across 50+ blockchain networks. HPC resources will enable parallelized training on petabyte-scale datasets, Monte Carlo simulations of systemic risk propagation, and real-time stress testing of collateralization thresholds under volatile market conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source credit scoring architecture capable of processing 10M+ transactions per second with sub-second latency, validated against historical liquidation events in Ethereum-based lending pools. This work aims to establish computational benchmarks for trustless credit systems while addressing regulatory challenges in automated collateral management. The resource request targets GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads and distributed memory systems for large-scale graph computations, with particular emphasis on optimizing memory bandwidth for sparse transactional data structures. Results will provide financial institutions and protocol designers with actionable insights for balancing risk exposure and capital efficiency in algorithmically governed credit markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform and/or manage operations concerning personal and corporate credit, collateral, loan processing, and related financial agency communications. Includes instruction in general finance and banking principles, insurance, real estate, taxation, business law and regulations, quantitative methods, financial computer systems applications, database management, communications skills, business and office management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems operate under extreme thermal, mechanical, and aerodynamic stresses, leading to complex degradation patterns that challenge traditional inspection and maintenance protocols. This project seeks to address the critical need for predictive modeling of turbine engine component failures, specifically focusing on high-cycle fatigue in compressor blades and thermal degradation in combustion chambers. Current empirical methods for assessing wear and predicting failures are limited by their reliance on post-service inspections and generalized operational data, which often fail to capture localized stress dynamics or transient thermal gradients. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating high-fidelity fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations, machine learning (ML)-enabled anomaly detection, and probabilistic lifetime prediction models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multiphysics phenomena—including turbulent combustion dynamics, conjugate heat transfer, and cyclic elastoplastic deformation—at scales relevant to microstructural material behavior. Large-eddy simulations (LES) will model combustion instability effects on chamber walls, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict stress accumulation in blade root geometries under variable rotor speeds. A recurrent neural network (RNN) trained on simulation-derived datasets will correlate real-time sensor data with early failure signatures. Outcomes will include a validated digital twin framework for powerplant subsystems, enabling proactive maintenance scheduling and reducing unplanned downtime. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated failure scenarios to support curriculum advancements in powerplant diagnostics, equipping technicians with data-driven decision-making tools. By bridging computational mechanics with applied aircraft maintenance practices, this work aims to extend service intervals safely and inform next-generation engine design priorities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing community-level social service interventions through large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM). Social work practice and policy increasingly rely on evidence-based strategies to allocate limited resources effectively, yet existing tools often lack the computational power to simulate complex, dynamic interactions between individuals, service providers, and systemic inequities. The research problem centers on addressing this gap by developing a computational framework capable of modeling heterogeneous populations, service accessibility barriers, and longitudinal outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. The project will employ ABM to simulate individual and household decision-making processes, integrating real-world demographic, socioeconomic, and service utilization data from municipal and nonprofit partners. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate model parameters using historical service outcomes, while parallelized simulations will test the efficacy of hypothetical resource allocation policies across diverse community contexts. Key computational challenges include managing high-dimensional data inputs, scaling simulations to regional population levels (>1 million agents), and conducting sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations. Access to HPC resources is critical for achieving sufficient model fidelity and statistical power within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool to help social service agencies prioritize interventions with the highest predicted equity and effectiveness, particularly for marginalized populations. The project will also generate novel methodological insights into adapting computational social science approaches for applied social work research. By bridging gaps between macro-level policy analysis and micro-level service delivery realities, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven resource allocation in public and nonprofit human service systems.
cip_definition: Any program providing instruction in social work and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation propagation across digital news ecosystems using advanced computational methods. As journalists and media organizations grapple with the rapid spread of unverified claims, understanding the interplay between algorithmic content distribution, user engagement patterns, and source credibility remains a critical challenge. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-terabyte datasets comprising social media posts, news articles, and platform metadata from 2016–2023. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to classify content veracity, map diffusion networks, and identify amplification patterns across partisan media clusters. Graph-based machine learning models will trace cross-platform information cascades, while transformer architectures will assess contextual shifts in recurring narratives. The computational demands of processing heterogeneous text data at scale—including transformer fine-tuning, dynamic network analysis, and time-series modeling of engagement metrics—necessitate parallelized workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time misinformation risk assessment, neural architectures optimized for journalistic fact-checking applications, and visual analytics tools to help newsrooms prioritize debunking efforts. By clarifying how technical systems and human behaviors jointly shape viral misinformation, this work aims to strengthen evidence-based reporting practices and inform platform accountability measures. The requested resources will enable processing timelines 12–15x faster than conventional infrastructure, particularly for training multimodal models on coordinated disinformation campaigns. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools tailored for investigative journalism and policy briefs addressing content moderation governance.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in journalism, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of construction and earthmoving operations demands advanced computational tools to optimize equipment performance, safety, and environmental sustainability. Current operational protocols for heavy equipment, such as crawler tractors, motor graders, and excavators, often rely on static guidelines that fail to account for dynamic site conditions, material variability, and real-time equipment interactions. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation framework to model heavy equipment operations under diverse scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these limitations. The research will focus on three interconnected challenges: (1) simulating the multi-physics interactions between equipment, terrain, and materials (e.g., soil, rock) during tasks like excavation and grading; (2) optimizing operational parameters (e.g., blade angles, load distribution) to minimize energy consumption and wear; and (3) integrating machine learning models to predict equipment failure risks under varying workloads. Computational methods will include discrete element modeling (DEM) for granular material dynamics, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress prediction, and reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine operational strategies. Large-scale parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses will be conducted to evaluate scenarios spanning diverse soil types, weather conditions, and equipment configurations. The HPC environment is critical due to the need for parallel processing of computationally intensive simulations and the training of high-dimensional machine learning models. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for real-time decision support, data-driven protocols to extend equipment lifespan, and a virtual training platform for operators that incorporates adaptive scenarios. By bridging gaps between empirical practices and computational innovation, this work aims to advance the technical foundations of heavy equipment operation, reducing costs and environmental impacts while improving safety standards across the construction sector.
cip_title: Construction/ Heavy Equipment/ Earthmoving Equipment Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate and maintain a variety of heavy equipment, such as a crawler tractors, motor graders and scrapers, shovels, rigging devices, hoists, and jacks. Includes instruction in digging, ditching, sloping, stripping, grading, and backfilling, clearing and excavating.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the diachronic and synchronic variation of morphosyntactic structures across understudied Germanic dialects, with a focus on Low German and Frisian. The research problem centers on the lack of comprehensive, data-driven models explaining the divergence and convergence of grammatical features in these languages, particularly in relation to language contact and internal innovation. Traditional qualitative methods face limitations in processing large, heterogeneous corpora spanning medieval manuscripts, modern regional speech recordings, and digitized folklore archives. To address this, the project will employ computational linguistics techniques, including rule-based morphological parsers and transformer-based language models, to automate the annotation of syntactic patterns and inflectional morphology. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-terabyte text and audio datasets, as well as the training of custom neural architectures for detecting nuanced grammatical shifts. Statistical analyses (Bayesian phylogenetic modeling, network analysis) will then map historical relationships and contact-induced changes. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated linguistic features, predictive models of grammatical change, and peer-reviewed findings on the interplay between sociolinguistic factors and structural evolution in minority Germanic languages. This work will significantly enhance empirical foundations in Germanic linguistics, offering methodological frameworks scalable to other non-standardized languages, while directly supporting preservation initiatives for endangered dialects. The computational demands of corpus preprocessing, model training, and large-scale simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve rigorous, reproducible results within project timelines.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Germanic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Germanic languages of Western, Central, and Northern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The integration of natural therapies into evidence-based clinical practice requires a robust understanding of the complex interactions between botanical compounds, physiological systems, and patient-specific factors. Current research in naturopathic medicine faces challenges in modeling these multi-scale interactions due to the computational demands of simulating dynamic biochemical networks, predicting herb-drug interactions, and analyzing large-scale genomic or metabolomic datasets. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance three interconnected aims: (1) developing predictive models for the synergistic effects of multi-herbal formulations using molecular docking and machine learning approaches; (2) simulating longitudinal patient outcomes under naturopathic interventions through agent-based modeling of immune-endocrine crosstalk; and (3) conducting high-throughput virtual screening of phytochemical libraries against targets relevant to chronic inflammatory conditions. Computational workflows will integrate cheminformatics tools (e.g., RDKit, AutoDock Vina), systems biology frameworks (COPASI, PySB), and deep learning architectures (graph neural networks, transformers) to process heterogeneous data types, including traditional herbal pharmacopeias, multi-omics cohorts, and electronic health records. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as molecular dynamics simulations of protein-herb complexes and parallelized parameter sweeps across personalized digital twin models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel bioactive synergies in botanical medicines, validated biomarkers for naturopathic treatment responsiveness, and open-access computational tools for naturopathy research. By enabling precision modeling of holistic therapeutic mechanisms, this work aims to strengthen the evidence base for naturopathic interventions while advancing computational methodologies tailored to the unique complexity of natural medicine systems. Resource allocation will directly support 3-5 peer-reviewed publications, two open-source software packages, and a clinical decision-support prototype for personalized naturopathic care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of naturopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic approach combining medical knowledge with noninvasive natural, homeopathic, and non-Western therapies and emphasizing disease prevention, wellness, and self-healing. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, biostatistics, public and community health, laboratory and clinical diagnosis, pharmacognosy, botanical medicine, homeopathy, principles of Oriental medicine and Ayurveda, manipulative therapy, naturopathic therapeutics, therapeutic nutrition, case analysis and management, philosophy of naturopathy, patient counseling, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between cellular architecture and tissue-scale anatomical organization in developing vertebrate models. A critical gap in cell biology and anatomy lies in understanding how subcellular structural adaptations—such as cytoskeletal rearrangements, organelle positioning, and membrane remodeling—directly influence the emergence of functional tissue patterns during morphogenesis. Traditional imaging and in vitro approaches lack the capacity to integrate multiscale datasets spanning molecular, cellular, and tissue-level events in intact systems. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining 3D electron microscopy reconstructions of developing avian musculoskeletal tissues with agent-based modeling to simulate cell-matrix interactions across developmental stages. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale volumetric imaging data to map ultrastructural features (e.g., focal adhesion distributions, endoplasmic reticulum networks) within thousands of cells simultaneously. These empirical datasets will parameterize multiscale models simulating how mechanical feedback between cells and extracellular matrix components drives tissue patterning. Validation will involve comparative analysis of simulated outcomes against time-resolved light sheet microscopy of ex vivo embryonic explants. The project’s computational demands center on parallelized image segmentation, feature extraction, and iterative model optimization, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. Expected outcomes include 1) predictive frameworks linking subcellular adaptations to tissue morphogenesis, 2) identification of conserved structural motifs critical for anatomical integrity, and 3) open-source tools for correlative ultrastructure-dynamics analysis. This work will advance foundational knowledge in developmental anatomy while providing mechanistic insights into structural birth defects affecting musculoskeletal systems. By bridging cell biological principles with anatomical complexity, the research aligns directly with the program’s mission to integrate cellular dynamics into organismic and regional contexts.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cell structure, function, and dynamics within the context of organismic, regional, and gross anatomical systems. Includes instruction in molecular biology, cell biology and histology, structural biology, anatomy, embryology, endocrinology, and applications to specific systems, diseases, defects, and processes.

abstract: The increasing complexity of decentralized autonomous systems (DAS) in critical infrastructure necessitates novel approaches to real-time security auditing that traditional centralized frameworks cannot support. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity, adaptive auditing framework for DAS, leveraging large-scale simulations of adversarial scenarios to identify vulnerabilities in distributed consensus protocols and smart contract execution. The research addresses a critical gap in current auditing methodologies, which struggle to dynamically assess systems where governance is algorithmically enforced and attack surfaces evolve unpredictably. By employing agent-based modeling and graph neural networks, the project will simulate heterogeneous networks of nodes, malicious actors, and stochastic environmental perturbations at scales reflecting real-world deployments (10^4–10^6 nodes). High-performance computing resources are essential to parameterize these models using empirical data from blockchain-based energy grids and IoT supply chains, while maintaining the low-latency requirements of real-time anomaly detection. Key computational challenges include parallelizing Byzantine fault tolerance simulations across GPU clusters and optimizing memory-intensive graph analyses of transaction provenance. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for probabilistic risk assessment in DAS, quantitative benchmarks for resilience metrics in decentralized systems, and novel algorithms for detecting collusion patterns in cross-chain transactions. This work will directly inform security standards for public-sector DAS implementations, particularly in contexts where conventional auditing practices fail to address emergent trustlessness and combinatorial attack vectors. By bridging formal verification, distributed systems theory, and operational cybersecurity, the project advances foundational methodologies for next-generation information assurance.
cip_title: Computer and Information Systems Security/ Auditing/ Information Assurance
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assess the security needs of computer and network systems, recommend safeguard solutions, and manage the implementation, auditing, and maintenance of security devices, systems, and procedures. Includes instruction in computer architecture, programming, and systems analysis; networking; telecommunications; cryptography; security system auditing and design; applicable law and regulations; risk assessment and policy analysis; contingency planning; user access issues; investigation techniques; and troubleshooting.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dynamic interactions between cognitive development and environmental influences in early childhood. A critical gap in developmental psychology lies in understanding how real-world, variable inputs—such as caregiver-child interactions or multimedia exposure—shape neural and behavioral trajectories. Traditional experimental methods struggle to capture the complexity of these nonlinear, time-dependent processes. To address this, we propose a computational modeling framework integrating longitudinal behavioral datasets (e.g., eye-tracking, vocalization records) with simulated neural network architectures. The research will employ deep reinforcement learning models to simulate how developing attention systems in children (ages 1–5 years) adapt to probabilistic patterns in their environments. A key innovation involves multi-agent modeling of dyadic interactions, where caregiver behavior models dynamically influence child agent learning. HPC resources are essential for training these models at scale, given the need for parallelized simulations across diverse developmental scenarios (e.g., varying input frequencies, socioemotional contexts) and parameter spaces. The computational pipeline will incorporate empirically derived datasets from existing cohort studies, enabling validation against real-world developmental outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) identification of critical environmental structure thresholds that predict shifts in cognitive strategies, (2) probabilistic maps of developmental branching points under different caregiving conditions, and (3) open-source tools for simulating individual differences in learning trajectories. This work will provide novel insights into mechanisms underlying developmental plasticity while establishing computational methods to bridge micro-level behavioral observations and macro-level developmental theories. The requested resources will directly support intensive GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter space explorations, and Bayesian optimization of developmental pathway predictions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from infancy through childhood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to sustainable power generation, yet optimizing their efficiency and longevity remains a significant challenge, particularly in environments with high sediment load. Sediment erosion in turbine components leads to frequent maintenance, reduced energy output, and increased operational costs. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models for simulating sediment-laden flow dynamics and predicting erosion patterns in hydroelectric turbines. The research problem centers on understanding the interplay between turbulent multiphase flows, particle dynamics, and material wear in complex turbine geometries under varying operational conditions. The computational approach integrates high-fidelity fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) tools, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify erosion hotspots and optimize turbine blade designs. High-resolution 3D simulations will model sediment transport, particle-impact forces, and surface degradation mechanisms at scale, requiring parallelized solvers and large-scale data processing capabilities provided by HPC infrastructure. Validation will be conducted using experimental data from laboratory-scale hydrodynamic testing and field measurements from operational hydroelectric plants. The expected outcomes include predictive models for turbine lifespan, data-driven design recommendations to mitigate erosion, and operational guidelines to enhance energy efficiency in sediment-prone environments. This work will directly contribute to reducing downtime and maintenance costs for hydroelectric facilities while supporting the broader adoption of resilient, sustainable hydropower technology. By enabling precise simulation of previously intractable flow regimes, the requested computing resources are essential to advancing hydroelectric engineering innovation and aligning with global decarbonization goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in hydroelectric energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the empirical understanding of dance movement therapy (DMT) by modeling the dynamic interplay between creative movement, neuroanatomical activation, and psychosocial outcomes. Despite growing clinical adoption of DMT, mechanistic insights into how movement patterns influence emotional regulation, cognitive processing, and interpersonal coordination remain understudied due to the complexity of analyzing multidimensional biomechanical, physiological, and behavioral data. Our research integrates motion capture systems, wearable biosensors, and patient-reported outcomes to capture real-time movement signatures during therapeutic interventions. Computational challenges include processing high-resolution kinematic data (500 Hz sampling rates), synchronizing multimodal datasets (motion, EEG, heart rate variability), and training machine learning models to classify movement patterns predictive of therapeutic progress. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of motor control networks using neuroanatomical models, as well as graph-theoretical analyses of group therapy dynamics to quantify emergent social coordination. A key innovation involves developing generative AI models to simulate patient-specific movement trajectories, allowing therapists to predict individualized intervention adjustments. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking specific movement qualities (e.g., fluidity, symmetry) to neural activation patterns and emotional states, (2) predictive algorithms for optimizing session plans based on real-time biometric feedback, and (3) open-source tools for quantifying therapeutic alliance through dyadic movement synchrony metrics. By bridging embodied therapeutic practices with computational neuroscience methodologies, this work will establish empirically grounded protocols to enhance DMT efficacy, particularly for populations with motor impairments or trauma-related disorders. The requested resources directly address the computational demands of analyzing terabyte-scale movement datasets while ensuring ethical data governance through encrypted processing pipelines compliant with healthcare privacy standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use the therapeutic application of creative dance movement to assist in promoting client rehabilitation and physical, emotional, and mental health. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, personality development, movement and motor behavior, psychology, dance, creative expression modalities, improvisation, group psychology and leadership, client evaluation and supervision, dance therapy practice, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens pose a critical threat to global health, particularly in resource-limited settings. This project seeks to characterize the genetic and molecular mechanisms driving AMR in multidrug-resistant *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*, a priority pathogen associated with high morbidity in healthcare and community environments. Despite advances in microbial genomics, the interplay between resistance gene acquisition, host-pathogen interactions, and immune evasion remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and structural biology data to model how specific genetic elements promote resistance while modulating host immune responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process whole-genome sequencing datasets from clinical isolates, perform comparative genomics to identify resistance-associated loci, and simulate protein-ligand interactions underlying resistance phenotypes. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will be employed to analyze mutations in bacterial efflux pumps and their impact on antibiotic binding, while machine learning models will predict immune evasion strategies linked to biofilm formation and antigenic variation. This multi-scale approach will map genomic diversity to phenotypic outcomes, clarifying how AMR evolves alongside immune subversion. The expected outcomes include (1) identifying novel genetic markers predictive of resistance in *P. aeruginosa*, (2) elucidating structural determinants of antibiotic efflux, and (3) characterizing immune evasion mechanisms that sustain chronic infections. These findings will directly inform the development of targeted antimicrobial therapies and rapid diagnostic tools, addressing urgent needs in global health. The project’s computational demands—including genome-wide association studies (GWAS), MD simulations requiring millisecond-scale sampling, and neural network training on multi-omics data—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for data storage, parallel processing, and GPU-accelerated analyses. By leveraging these resources, this work aims to advance translational microbiology research and strengthen evidence-based strategies to mitigate AMR-driven infectious disease burdens.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biological, social, and behavioral factors contributing to the cause and spread of infectious diseases. Includes instruction in research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, disease mechanisms, antimicrobial resistance, immunology, and bioterrorism.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of systematically analyzing complex ethical reasoning patterns across philosophical traditions using computational methods. Traditional philosophical scholarship often relies on manual textual analysis, limiting the scale and granularity with which interconnected arguments, presuppositions, and counterarguments can be examined. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), this research aims to map structural relationships within and between ethical frameworks—such as deontological, consequentialist, and virtue-based systems—through large-scale textual analysis and simulation. The primary corpus includes digitized works from classical to contemporary philosophy, with particular attention to understudied intercultural dialogues. Computational methods will combine natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned for argument mining, with network analysis to visualize conceptual dependencies. Agent-based modeling will further simulate hypothetical ethical decision-making scenarios under varying epistemic constraints, requiring parallelized computation to test thousands of parameter combinations. These approaches demand significant memory and processing power to handle multi-terabyte datasets, train machine learning models on nuanced philosophical language, and run iterative simulations. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized argumentative patterns across traditions, quantitative metrics for comparing ethical systems, and open-source tools tailored for computational philosophy. The project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in the humanities by demonstrating how HPC can reveal latent complexities in philosophical discourse, while fostering new frameworks for cross-cultural ethical analysis. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, a public database of annotated philosophical texts, and workshops on computational approaches to humanistic research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Philosophy, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to optimize multimodal cross-border freight routing under dynamic regulatory constraints using high-performance computing (HPC) to address systemic inefficiencies in customs-triggered logistics delays. Current routing models inadequately integrate real-time updates to tariffs, trade agreements, and inspection protocols, resulting in cascading delays that cost global supply chains an estimated $140 billion annually. We propose developing a simulation framework that models freight movement across air, maritime, and terrestrial networks while dynamically incorporating jurisdictional policy changes, automated customs documentation validation, and carrier capacity constraints. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation with transformer-based natural language processing to parse regulatory texts from 190+ customs jurisdictions, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize routing decisions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 1) high-resolution geotemporal traffic data, 2) multilingual regulatory updates scraped from government portals, and 3) multi-agent simulations evaluating over 10^6 potential route permutations per shipment corridor. Expected outcomes include a predictive routing engine that reduces customs clearance times by 18-22% in simulated scenarios while maintaining compliance accuracy above 99.4%, benchmarked against historical shipment data from EU and ASEAN trade corridors. The computational toolkit will be designed for integration with existing transportation management systems, providing actionable recommendations for fleet dispatchers and customs brokers. This research fills a critical gap in adaptive logistics planning at the intersection of computational trade compliance and transportation operations, offering scalability benefits for both public customs authorities and private-sector freight forwarders navigating increasingly complex transnational regulatory environments.
cip_title: Traffic, Customs, and Transportation Clerk/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform duties associated with managing revenue-based customs, traffic, or transportation services, such as control of domestic and international traffic, toll roads and waterways, and to assist in the dispatch and control of fleet-based traffic for businesses and public services. Includes instruction in record-keeping; preparation of customs and transportation documentation; operation of communications equipment; basic transportation operations management; tariffs, rates and fares; revenue collection and change-making; and interpretation of customs or transportation regulations and related legislation, policies, and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in masonry design and structural performance under dynamic environmental stressors. Traditional masonry practices rely on empirical methods and physical testing, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in predicting long-term durability under variable conditions such as seismic activity, moisture infiltration, and thermal cycling. The research problem centers on developing predictive computational models to simulate masonry behavior at multiple scales—from molecular interactions in mortar composition to macro-scale structural integrity—enabling data-driven optimization of materials, construction techniques, and decorative designs. The computational approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element modeling (DEM) to simulate stress distribution, crack propagation, and failure mechanisms in diverse masonry assemblies, including reinforced and decorative systems. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation data to identify correlations between material properties, geometric configurations, and environmental exposure, facilitating rapid prototyping of resilient designs. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate moisture diffusion and chemical degradation in mortar matrices to inform improved mix designs. By utilizing HPC resources, this project will process large datasets encompassing parametric variations in material ratios, joint geometries, and load scenarios, which are infeasible to analyze with conventional computing. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for masonry durability, optimized guidelines for seismic-resistant and energy-efficient designs, and open-access simulation tools tailored for vocational training programs. These advancements aim to bridge gaps between traditional craftsmanship and computational innovation, enhancing the safety, sustainability, and adaptability of masonry in modern construction. The results will directly inform curriculum updates and industry standards, ensuring masons are equipped with cutting-edge, evidence-based practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the laying and/or setting of exterior brick, concrete block, hard tile, marble and related materials, using trowels, levels, hammers, chisels, and other hand tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, blueprint reading, structural masonry, decorative masonry, foundations, reinforcement, mortar preparation, cutting and finishing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address gaps in large-scale computational analysis of Norwegian linguistic diversity and literary evolution by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Norwegian dialects and historical texts present complex phonological, morphological, and syntactic variations that are challenging to systematically analyze with traditional methods due to the scale and multidimensionality of the data. The research will focus on two interrelated objectives: (1) modeling dialectal variation across modern Norwegian (Bokmål, Nynorsk, and regional dialects) using machine learning-driven phonetic and lexical analysis, and (2) tracing semantic and stylistic shifts in 19th- to 21st-century Norwegian literature through corpus linguistics and natural language processing (NLP). Computational workflows will integrate speech corpora (including the Nordic Dialect Corpus), digitized historical texts, and contemporary sources, applying transformer-based models for cross-dialect comparison and diachronic text analysis. HPC resources are essential for training custom tokenizers to handle orthographic variations in older texts, running parallelized acoustic analyses of dialect recordings, and processing multi-terabyte datasets with attention-based architectures. Expected outcomes include the first computational typology of Norwegian dialect boundaries, an open-access repository of annotated historical texts, and quantitative frameworks for detecting literary influences across eras. These resources will advance philological research, support language preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and enable robust NLP tools tailored to Norwegian’s linguistic specificity. By integrating computational methods with traditional humanities scholarship, this project aims to establish new interdisciplinary paradigms for studying lesser-resourced languages within the digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Norwegian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling and rendering large-scale, interactive sound environments for experimental artistic practice. Sound arts research increasingly relies on simulating complex acoustic phenomena, real-time processing of spatial audio, and generative sound design—tasks that demand significant processing power, memory, and parallelization. Current consumer-grade systems lack the capacity to handle high-channel-count spatial audio diffusion, dynamic wave-field synthesis, or machine learning-driven sound synthesis at the granularity required for immersive installations. The proposed research will develop computational frameworks for two interconnected strands: (1) simulating acoustic environments with wave-based algorithms to model sound propagation in non-linear, site-specific spaces, and (2) training neural networks to generate adaptive soundscapes responsive to real-time sensor inputs during live performances. Methods will include finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) acoustic simulations, GPU-accelerated spectral processing, and distributed computing approaches to synchronize audio rendering across multi-channel arrays. By utilizing HPC infrastructure, these workflows will scale to handle 3D spatial audio resolutions exceeding 256 discrete channels and latency-sensitive generative systems incorporating motion capture and environmental data streams. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for computational sound design, validated through public installations and performances, that demonstrate how HPC can expand the creative possibilities of sound as a performative medium. This work will contribute new methodologies at the intersection of auditory culture and computational arts while establishing benchmarks for resource-intensive sonic practices within performing arts research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on sound as a form of cultural expression, and its relationship to other disciplines such as computer programming, performance, and video. Includes instruction in acoustics; arranging, composing, and editing music; music theory; musicology; orchestration and scoring; and sound design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the personalization of educational interventions for students with disabilities, addressing the challenge of efficiently tailoring evidence-based strategies to highly heterogeneous learning needs. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) often rely on manual data analysis and generalized frameworks, which can limit scalability and precision in dynamic classroom settings. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from K-12 special education programs, including longitudinal academic performance metrics, behavioral logs, teacher annotations, and physiological sensor data from attention-monitoring tools. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns in student responses to specific interventions under varying conditions, such as classroom configurations, task types, and instructor scaffolding techniques. Computational simulations will test hypothetical intervention combinations across synthetic cohorts representing diverse disability profiles (e.g., autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, and developmental delays), enabling rapid iteration of strategies that maximize predicted learning gains while minimizing educator workload. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated clustering algorithms to categorize emergent student archetypes and reinforcement learning to model adaptive teaching sequences. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for generating data-driven IEP recommendations and a sensitivity analysis toolkit to evaluate intervention robustness across demographic and disability severity factors. By enabling real-time processing of complex, high-dimensional educational data, this work aims to reduce disparities in special education outcomes through computationally optimized teaching strategies while preserving the critical role of human educator judgment. The requested resources will support the parallel processing demands of training transformer-based models on sensitive, de-identified student records (≥100 TB) and running multi-agent simulations of classroom dynamics at scale.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of pharmacotherapy and the growing volume of multidimensional health data present critical challenges in optimizing medication use and patient outcomes. Current approaches in pharmacy informatics often lack the computational capacity to integrate and analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and real-world evidence efficiently, limiting the ability to predict drug responses, adverse events, and therapeutic outcomes at scale. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for personalized medication management. The research will focus on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including EHRs, pharmacogenomic profiles, and drug interaction databases—to identify patterns in medication-related outcomes across diverse patient populations. Computational methods will involve machine learning algorithms for feature selection, natural language processing to extract unstructured clinical notes, and graph-based analytics to model drug-disease-gene networks. Large-scale simulations will assess the impact of genetic polymorphisms on pharmacokinetic variability, while parallelized workflows will enable real-time risk prediction for adverse drug events. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling datasets spanning millions of patient encounters, performing iterative model training, and executing complex simulations that require terabytes of memory and thousands of CPU hours. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for dose optimization, risk stratification models for medication-related hospitalizations, and a framework for dynamic clinical decision support. These results will advance precision pharmacotherapy by enabling data-driven adjustments to treatment plans, reducing trial-and-error prescribing, and mitigating preventable harm. The resource allocation will directly support translational goals to improve medication safety and efficacy in diverse clinical settings, with implications for health system cost reduction and enhanced patient outcomes.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pharmacy Informatics

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between digital cultural production and identity formation within South Asian diasporic communities, with a focus on gender and intersectional perspectives. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital platforms—such as social media, online literary archives, and collaborative storytelling forums—shape collective memory and self-representation among displaced or migratory populations from South Asia. Current scholarship often relies on qualitative textual analysis, limiting scalability and the ability to identify longitudinal patterns across vast, multilingual datasets. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis and machine learning techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned for regional dialects and transliterated content, to analyze over 10 terabytes of user-generated text, images, and metadata from curated digital repositories. Key computational challenges include processing code-mixed content (e.g., Hindi-English, Tamil-Sinhala), detecting emergent themes in gendered narratives, and mapping transnational network connections between diasporic creators. High-performance computing resources are essential to train custom NLP pipelines for underrepresented South Asian languages, run large-scale sentiment and network analyses, and visualize spatial-temporal patterns in cultural discourse. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of diasporic digital expression, algorithmic frameworks tailored to South Asian sociolinguistic contexts, and new theoretical insights into how technology mediates cultural preservation amid displacement. By integrating computational methods with critical cultural studies, this work aims to establish a replicable model for analyzing identity dynamics in globalized digital ecosystems while centering the voices of marginalized communities. The requested resources will directly support GPU-intensive model training, parallel processing of heterogeneous data types, and secure storage for sensitive ethnographic materials, enabling a novel interdisciplinary approach to diaspora studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of South Asia, defined as including Afghanistan, India, the Maldives, Myanmar (Burma), Pakistan, and Sri Lanka and related borderlands and island groups; and including the study of migration patterns and overseas diasporas.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address operational inefficiencies in small-to-medium brewery and brewpub supply chains, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation under uncertainty. The craft brewing industry faces unique challenges, including fluctuating raw material availability, variable demand cycles, and stringent regulatory constraints, which complicate production scheduling, inventory management, and distribution logistics. Current decision-support tools often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between biological processes (e.g., fermentation timelines), perishable inventory constraints, and real-time market signals. We propose developing a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework coupled with discrete-event simulation to model these interdependent systems at scale. The computational approach will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including sensory data from IoT-enabled fermentation tanks, supplier lead times, and regional sales patterns—into a unified optimization model. HPC resources will enable parallelized scenario testing across diverse operational configurations, simulating thousands of brewery-vendor-consumer interactions under stochastic conditions (e.g., climate-induced barley yield variations, sudden regulatory changes). Sensitivity analyses will quantify the resilience of different allocation strategies, while graph neural networks will identify latent patterns in distribution network bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for adaptive capacity planning that balances production flexibility with cost efficiency, specifically tailored to breweries operating under <5,000 barrel annual production. The research will advance computational methods for perishable goods supply chains while contributing novel insights into resource allocation problems at the intersection of biochemical processes and business operations. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation modules and a decision-support dashboard designed for non-technical brewery operators, potentially reducing operational waste by an estimated 12-18% in pilot implementations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market breweries and brewpubs. Includes instruction in brewing science, food services management, logistics and distribution, business networking, personnel management, business planning and capitalization, brewing industry operations, marketing, alcohol and liquor law and regulations, finance, and ethics.

abstract: Critically ill adult and geriatric patients in intensive care units (ICUs) face high risks of mortality and long-term morbidity due to the interplay of acute illness, chronic comorbidities, and age-related physiological decline. Existing risk stratification models often fail to account for the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between genomic, clinical, and real-time physiological data that influence outcomes in this population. This project proposes to develop a predictive computational framework integrating multi-omics profiles, high-resolution vital sign streams, and electronic health record data to model personalized trajectories of critical illness and recovery. We will employ machine learning techniques, including time-series analysis, graph neural networks, and ensemble methods, to identify signatures of treatment response and decompensation risks specific to aging-associated pathophysiology. The computational demands of processing terabytes of longitudinal biosensor data, whole-genome sequences, and multimodal clinical records necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized model training, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale simulation of virtual patient cohorts. Key outcomes will include (1) predictive algorithms for sepsis progression, organ failure, and delirium in geriatric critical care populations, validated against a retrospective cohort of 15,000 ICU patients, and (2) an open-source computational workflow for real-time integration of heterogeneous critical care data streams. Successful implementation will enable clinically actionable dynamic risk stratification, potentially reducing avoidable complications through earlier targeted interventions. This work addresses a critical need for computationally intensive approaches to unravel complex phenotype-environment interactions in vulnerable aging populations, with direct implications for precision medicine in critical care settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Critical Care

abstract: Forest ecosystems face mounting pressures from climate change, invasive species, and shifting land-use patterns, necessitating advanced tools to model adaptive management strategies. Current approaches to optimizing timber production, biodiversity conservation, and carbon sequestration often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic ecological interactions or scale effectively across heterogeneous landscapes. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, spatially explicit simulation framework to evaluate multi-objective forest management scenarios under uncertainty. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate remote sensing data, species distribution models, and process-based growth simulations to quantify trade-offs between timber yield, habitat connectivity, and ecosystem resilience. The computational workflow will employ machine learning algorithms to parameterize forest regeneration patterns from LiDAR and multispectral imagery, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate disturbance regimes (e.g., pests, wildfires) and management interventions. Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes across climate projections from CMIP6 ensembles. By parallelizing computationally intensive tasks such as landscape-scale carbon flux calculations and genetic algorithm-driven harvest scheduling, the HPC environment will enable previously intractable analyses of decade-scale forest dynamics at 10-meter spatial resolution. Expected outcomes include actionable strategies for balancing economic and ecological priorities in managed forests, validated against field data from experimental timber stands. The resulting open-source tools will empower forest technologists to design adaptive management plans responsive to real-time environmental data, while advancing computational ecology methods applicable to other complex natural systems. This work directly addresses critical gaps in forest technology education and practice by bridging field-based expertise with cutting-edge computational modeling capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist foresters in the management and production of forest resources. Includes instruction in woods and field skills, tree identification, timber measurement, logging and timber harvesting, forest propagation and regeneration, forest fire-fighting, resource management, equipment operation and maintenance, record-keeping, sales and purchasing operations, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural semantic alignment in global corporate communication networks using advanced natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based computational models. As multinational corporations increasingly rely on decentralized, multilingual teams, misalignments in the interpretation of mission-critical terminology—such as “compliance,” “innovation,” or “risk”—across linguistic and cultural contexts pose operational and strategic risks. Traditional manual audits of communication artifacts are resource-intensive and fail to scale with the volume and velocity of modern digital interactions. The research will employ transformer-based language models fine-tuned on industry-specific corpora to detect semantic divergences in translated or localized internal communications, employee feedback channels, and external stakeholder messaging. A graph neural network (GNN) framework will then map how these divergences propagate through organizational communication networks, simulating their impact on decision-making latency and consensus formation. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of multilingual text data across 20+ languages, train domain-adapted embeddings, and execute dynamic network simulations at enterprise scale. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of high-risk semantic misalignment patterns correlated with cultural and syntactic variables, (2) predictive models for identifying latent misinterpretation hotspots in emerging markets, and (3) an open-source toolkit for real-time monitoring of semantic coherence in corporate communications. By bridging computational linguistics, cross-cultural management, and network science, this work aims to establish empirically grounded frameworks for mitigating communication-driven operational risks in globally distributed organizations. The requested resources will enable processing of federated datasets from seven industry partners while maintaining data sovereignty constraints, with iterative model validation against ground-truthed incident reports from participating firms.
cip_definition: Any program in business or corporate communications, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the creation and analysis of large-scale, data-driven digital artworks, addressing the growing computational demands of contemporary visual arts practices. The research problem centers on the limitations of conventional tools in rendering complex, interactive, or generative art forms—particularly those involving high-resolution 3D modeling, real-time simulation of dynamic materials, or AI-driven generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on vast art-historical datasets. Current workflows struggle to process photorealistic textures, simulate fluid interactions in mixed-media installations, or iterate generative designs at scales necessary for public art or immersive environments. To address this, the project proposes a computational framework combining parallelized rendering pipelines, physics-based simulations of material behaviors (e.g., ceramics, textiles), and machine learning models optimized for artistic collaboration. HPC resources will enable GPU-accelerated training of custom GANs on terabyte-scale datasets of historical and contemporary artworks, facilitating the synthesis of novel visual styles while preserving computational efficiency for artist-guided iteration. Additionally, finite element analysis (FEA) simulations will model stress distributions in 3D-printed sculptures, optimizing structural integrity for large-format pieces. The integration of real-time ray tracing and volumetric capture data will support interactive virtual studio environments, allowing artists to manipulate high-fidelity digital prototypes with minimal latency. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for scalable digital art production, a repository of computationally optimized material models for interdisciplinary use, and a series of public exhibitions demonstrating HPC-enabled artworks. This work aims to expand the technical and conceptual boundaries of studio practice, fostering new intersections between visual art, computational design, and material science while democratizing access to advanced tools for artists without specialized coding expertise.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally function as creative artists in the visual and plastic media. Includes instruction in the traditional fine arts media (drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, CAD/CAM) and/or modern media (ceramics, textiles, intermedia, photography, digital images), theory of art, color theory, composition and perspective, anatomy, the techniques and procedures for maintaining equipment and managing a studio, and art portfolio marketing.

abstract: This research project seeks to analyze the distributional impacts of monetary policy through a heterogeneous agent New Keynesian (HANK) model, which integrates household heterogeneity with nominal rigidities. Traditional macroeconomic models often assume representative agents, obscuring distributional consequences of policy changes. This study addresses this gap by developing a high-dimensional HANK model that captures diverse household behaviors, income dynamics, and portfolio choices. The computational complexity arises from solving for equilibrium in a high-dimensional state space, requiring iterative methods across thousands of parallelized simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the model’s scale, enabling the use of numerical optimization algorithms and Monte Carlo techniques to estimate parameters from microeconomic data. The project will simulate various monetary policy shocks—such as interest rate adjustments and quantitative easing—to assess their effects on consumption, wealth inequality, and macroeconomic stability. Expected outcomes include quantifying the heterogeneous welfare effects of policy interventions and identifying mechanisms that amplify or mitigate inequality. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance the integration of microeconomic heterogeneity into macroeconomic modeling, providing policymakers with nuanced insights for designing equitable stabilization policies. The findings will contribute to academic debates on monetary policy efficacy and inform real-world discussions on mitigating economic disparities in inflationary environments.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the systematic study of the production, conservation and allocation of resources in conditions of scarcity, together with the organizational frameworks related to these processes. Includes instruction in economic theory, micro- and macroeconomics, comparative economic systems, money and banking systems, international economics, quantitative analytical methods, and applications to specific industries and public policy issues.

abstract: Declines in honey bee health and colony stability threaten global agricultural systems dependent on pollination services. Despite advances in apiary management, the complex interactions between pathogens (e.g., Varroa destructor, deformed wing virus), pesticide exposure, nutritional stressors, and genetic factors remain poorly quantified. This project proposes a computational framework to model these multifactorial drivers of colony collapse and optimize mitigation strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including longitudinal hive sensor data, genomic sequences of pathogen-resistant bee populations, pesticide application geospatial records, and floral resource maps—into a unified agent-based model (ABM). The ABM will simulate colony dynamics across spatial scales, incorporating individual bee behavior, pathogen transmission, and seasonal management practices. Machine learning pipelines will concurrently analyze historical colony failure data to identify risk thresholds for pesticide residues and pathogen loads. A key innovation involves coupling genomic association studies with population viability analysis to predict the long-term efficacy of breeding programs targeting hygienic behavior and parasite resistance. By leveraging parallelized simulations across parameter spaces, this work will quantify trade-offs between intervention strategies (e.g., miticide rotation, supplemental feeding, queen selection protocols) under climate variability. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for beekeepers to prioritize colony health interventions, genetic markers for breeding programs, and evidence-based thresholds for pesticide use near apiaries. The computational workflows developed will be scalable to regional pollination networks, directly supporting the agricultural sector’s reliance on stable bee populations. This project addresses a critical gap in apicultural research by bridging field observations with systems-level computational analysis, enabling data-driven decisions to enhance apiary resilience and pollination security.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on improving the beekeeping industry, promoting pollination of fruits and vegetables, and bee colony expansion and maintenance. Includes instruction in apiary behavior, apiary equipment and supplies, beekeeping, bee pests and parasites, handling bees, hive set up and care, queen rearing, and seasonal management practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven adaptive support system designed to optimize the workflow of teaching assistants (TAs) in large, heterogeneous classrooms. While TAs play a critical role in scaling personalized instruction, they face challenges in efficiently addressing diverse student needs, particularly in STEM courses with high enrollment and variable learner backgrounds. Existing tools for TA support are limited to generic workflow automation, lacking the capacity to dynamically adapt to real-time classroom data or individual student-TA interactions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework that integrates multimodal data—including student forum queries, assignment submissions, and biometric feedback (e.g., eye-tracking during office hours)—to generate context-aware recommendations for TAs. The system will employ transformer-based models fine-tuned on domain-specific educational corpora and reinforcement learning algorithms to personalize TA intervention strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on large-scale, privacy-preserved datasets spanning multiple institutions (targeting 500,000+ student-TA interactions) and for simulating classroom scenarios through agent-based modeling. Computational challenges include real-time processing of unstructured educational data streams, optimizing low-latency inference for deployment in live classrooms, and ensuring algorithmic fairness across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive TA support, validated through randomized controlled trials in 15 partner courses, and a novel evaluation metric quantifying the impact of AI-augmented TA interventions on both student learning outcomes and TA workload equity. This work bridges educational practice, human-computer interaction, and machine learning, offering a scalable solution to enhance instructional support systems without requiring structural reforms to existing TA training programs.
cip_definition: Any teaching assistant/aide program, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate scalable statistical models for analyzing heterogeneous treatment effects (HTEs) in large-scale educational interventions, a critical challenge in education research. Current methods for HTE estimation struggle with high-dimensional data from modern digital learning platforms, which often include multimodal features (e.g., clickstream interactions, assessment histories, and demographic variables) across millions of observations. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining multilevel Bayesian additive regression trees (MBART) with distributed optimization techniques. The research will extend existing BART implementations to handle hierarchical data structures common in educational settings (e.g., students nested in schools) while maintaining computational tractability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling across intervention subgroups using GPU-accelerated nodes, (2) distributed cross-validation of model hyperparameters through SLURM job arrays, and (3) simulation studies comparing our approach to traditional methods under varying sample sizes (n = 10^4 to 10^7) and missing data patterns. The computational workflow will leverage containerization for reproducibility across HPC architectures. Using real-world data from three national STEM education initiatives (totaling 2.3 million student records), the project aims to identify robust predictors of intervention effect variation while controlling for institutional confounding. Expected outcomes include open-source software for HTE analysis in education, validated computational strategies for handling massive observational datasets, and evidence-based guidelines for personalizing interventions at scale. This work directly addresses the critical need for advanced statistical computing in education research, where traditional methods often fail to balance interpretability with the computational demands of modern big data. Results will inform resource allocation decisions in educational policy and provide methodological foundations for future studies in adaptive learning systems.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the analysis and solution of educational research problems, and the development of technical designs for research studies. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, research design, computer applications, instrument design, research methodologies, and applications to research problems in specific education subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the digital humanities dimension of Near and Middle Eastern Studies through the computational analysis of historical multilingual textual corpora. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding cross-regional cultural exchanges between North African, Levantine, and Arabian communities during the 12th–16th centuries, as documented in understudied Arabic, Judeo-Arabic, and Persian manuscripts. Traditional scholarship has been limited by the fragmented nature of these sources, their linguistic diversity, and the logistical challenges of manual analysis. Our work proposes a computational pipeline combining optical character recognition (OCR) optimized for cursive scripts, natural language processing (NLP) models trained on historical dialects, and network analysis to map intellectual exchanges and semantic shifts across time and space. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing approximately 15 TB of digitized manuscripts from dispersed archives, enabling parallelized OCR correction, transformer-based semantic annotation, and large-scale graph computations to trace textual transmission pathways. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital reconstruction of transregional knowledge networks connecting scholarly hubs from Cairo to Baghdad, with particular attention to marginalized voices in women’s devotional texts and merchant community records. The computational workflows will be packaged into open-source tools tailored for non-Latin scripts, addressing a longstanding technical barrier in the field. By revealing patterns of cultural adaptation and resistance, this project aims to reshape scholarly narratives about premodern connectivity while providing heritage institutions with scalable methods for preserving fragile manuscripts. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for annotated corpora, and high-memory nodes for network visualization, which are computationally prohibitive in standard academic computing environments.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, related borderlands and island groups, and including emigrant and immigrant groups.

abstract: Pediatric hematologic malignancies, such as leukemia and lymphoma, present unique clinical challenges due to their complex molecular heterogeneity and variable treatment responses. While advances in genomic profiling have identified recurrent mutations, the functional impact of these alterations on disease progression and therapeutic resistance remains poorly characterized in pediatric populations. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omics data with computational models to identify high-risk molecular subtypes and predict optimal therapeutic strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic datasets from pediatric patients enrolled in international consortia, including the Children’s Oncology Group. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to delineate clonal evolution patterns during treatment and correlate these dynamics with clinical outcomes.
