Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model the structural consequences of recurrent mutations in key oncoproteins, enabling virtual screening of small-molecule inhibitors tailored to pediatric-specific variants. A pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic framework will further optimize dosing regimens for identified compounds using population-based modeling. The computational workflow will require parallel processing capabilities to manage terabytes of sequencing data, iterative model training, and large-scale in silico drug screens. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, predictive biomarkers for treatment resistance, and personalized dosing recommendations to minimize toxicity. By elucidating the molecular drivers of therapeutic failure in pediatric hematologic cancers, this work aims to directly inform the design of upcoming clinical trials and improve survival rates for high-risk patients. The scale and complexity of these analyses necessitate robust HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically actionable insights within a translational research timeline.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Hematology-Oncology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of cultural survival and intergroup influence among Baltic, Scandinavian, and Slavic communities through computational text and artifact analysis. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural resilience and assimilation in multilingual historical records, folklore collections, and digitized material culture from the Baltic region, which remain understudied due to the scale and linguistic complexity of the source materials. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis (including Latvian, Lithuanian, Estonian, Swedish, and German) with machine learning models to map semantic shifts, narrative motifs, and symbolic representations across time and communities. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect cross-cultural borrowings and adaptations in folklore, religious texts, and early modern administrative documents, while image recognition algorithms will classify stylistic features in digitized artifacts (e.g., traditional textiles, woodcarvings) to trace regional aesthetic exchanges. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, including unstructured text corpora spanning six centuries, high-resolution artifact images, and geospatial records. The project will employ distributed training frameworks to optimize model performance across GPU nodes and utilize parallel processing for large-scale comparative analyses. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph visualizing cultural connections and conflict zones among Baltic Sea populations, as well as computational models adaptable to other minority language contexts. By revealing previously inaccessible patterns of cultural negotiation, this work aims to advance methodological frameworks for digital humanities in area studies while directly informing contemporary heritage preservation initiatives in the Baltic region.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the coastlands of the Baltic Sea, including Baltic, Germanic, Scandinavian, and Slavic populations, related borderlands and island groups, and problems of cultural survival and assimilation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and tuning of high-performance automotive engines and vehicle systems, addressing the growing complexity of modifying modern powertrains for competitive and custom applications. Current approaches to engine enhancement rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and dynamometer testing, which are costly, time-intensive, and limited in their ability to explore multidimensional design spaces. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate combustion dynamics, exhaust gas flow, thermal stress distributions, and suspension kinematics under high-load conditions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model air-fuel mixing and exhaust scavenging efficiency across custom intake and exhaust geometries, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict component fatigue in turbocharged engines operating at extreme boost pressures. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on dynamometer datasets to correlate simulated parameters with empirical power output and emissions data, enabling predictive optimization of camshaft timing, fuel injection maps, and forced induction configurations. These multi-physics simulations will account for transient interactions between modified engine subsystems, a critical gap in current single-domain modeling tools. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these resource-intensive computations across parametric variations in displacement, compression ratio, and aftermarket component combinations. Expected outcomes include a framework for virtual prototyping of performance engines, reducing physical testing cycles by an estimated 40-60%, and generating actionable insights into trade-offs between horsepower gains, drivetrain reliability, and regulatory compliance. This work will directly support curriculum development in computational engine tuning, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-driven automotive research. The resulting open-source models aim to democratize access to high-fidelity simulation tools for small-scale mechanics and custom fabricators, fostering innovation in the high-performance automotive sector.
cip_title: High Performance and Custom Engine Technician/ Mechanic
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to increase the power of diesel and automotive engines; enhance the performance of automobiles; and repair, service, and maintain high performance vehicles. Includes instruction in adding performance accessories; modifying powertrains; tuning custom engines, suspension, and exhaust systems; and using dynamometers and other diagnostic equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance intelligence analysis and decision-making processes in dynamic, high-stakes military environments by integrating heterogeneous data streams with advanced machine learning (ML) and graph analytics. Traditional intelligence workflows often struggle to synthesize fragmented data—including signals intelligence (SIGINT), human intelligence (HUMINT), and open-source intelligence (OSINT)—into actionable insights under time constraints. The research problem centers on overcoming latency, scalability, and uncertainty challenges inherent in processing multi-modal intelligence data, particularly in scenarios involving adversarial deception or information warfare. The proposed approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to deploy ensemble ML models trained on historical operational data, coupled with real-time graph-based network analysis to map adversarial intent and resource flows. Key computational methods include transformer-based natural language processing for unstructured OSINT corpus analysis, probabilistic reasoning to quantify confidence in HUMINT reports, and distributed graph neural networks (GNNs) to model threat actor relationships. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale simulations of multi-domain operational scenarios, stress-testing the framework’s ability to prioritize intelligence leads, detect emergent patterns, and generate adaptive recommendations under varying resource constraints. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of reducing analyst decision latency by 30-50% in simulated environments, validated against classified military exercise datasets. The research will also produce novel metrics for quantifying intelligence fusion efficacy in contested information environments. By bridging computational scalability with domain-specific military requirements, this work aims to establish a template for next-generation intelligence platforms that balance automation with human oversight, directly supporting strategic and tactical readiness.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of intelligence acquisition, analysis and exploitation. Includes instruction in intelligence organizations, the intelligence cycle, intelligence operations planning, intelligence analysis and reporting, intelligence methods, electronic and signals intelligence, operations and communications security, human intelligence management, intelligence chain of command, information exploitation and psychological warfare, and the relationship to national security policy and strategy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of student needs in postsecondary education demands innovative approaches to optimize counseling interventions and resource allocation. Current practices in student counseling often rely on static assessments or generalized protocols, which may fail to address the dynamic, interconnected factors influencing student well-being and academic success. This project proposes to develop a predictive modeling framework using machine learning and network analysis to identify patterns in multi-source student data (e.g., academic performance, service utilization, and anonymized counseling session transcripts) that correlate with critical outcomes such as retention, mental health crises, and career readiness. The computational approach will integrate natural language processing techniques to analyze unstructured text data from counseling interactions with structured institutional records, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets (>1 million anonymized student records across 15 partner institutions) and train complex neural architectures. A key innovation involves simulating intervention pathways through agent-based modeling to predict how tailored counseling strategies might propagate through student support networks. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for real-time analysis of longitudinal data streams and ethical AI validation processes to mitigate algorithmic bias. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for higher education institutions to prioritize at-risk populations, dynamically adjust counseling resource distribution, and evaluate intervention effectiveness through counterfactual simulations. This work advances education research by establishing computationally rigorous methods to personalize student support while maintaining strict privacy standards. Results will directly inform national best practices for data-informed counseling in the College Student Counseling and Personnel Services field, with particular relevance to underserved populations in community colleges and minority-serving institutions.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance trauma counseling research by analyzing complex interactions between neurobiological, psychological, and contextual factors influencing trauma recovery. Current trauma interventions exhibit variable efficacy, partly due to heterogeneous manifestations of trauma-related disorders such as PTSD and gaps in understanding how individual differences in neurobiology, trauma history, and social environments shape treatment outcomes. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating multimodal datasets—including neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), genetic markers, clinical assessments, and longitudinal patient-reported outcomes—to model predictors of therapeutic success. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale neuroimaging data, training machine learning (ML) models to identify subtypes of trauma response, and simulating neurodynamic changes associated with evidence-based interventions. Computational workflows will include (1) preprocessing and feature extraction from imaging data using tools such as FSL and FreeSurfer; (2) ML-driven clustering to delineate trauma phenotypes based on neural, genetic, and behavioral profiles; and (3) biophysically informed neural circuit simulations to quantify how trauma disrupts functional connectivity and how interventions may restore adaptive patterns. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to overcome limitations of traditional statistical methods in handling high-dimensional, multilevel data. Anticipated outcomes include predictive biomarkers for personalized treatment matching, mechanistic insights into trauma-related neural plasticity, and open-source computational tools for the trauma research community. This work will directly inform the development of trauma-sensitive, precision counseling frameworks while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in bridging clinical practice and computational neuroscience within health professions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on understanding elements of traumatic exposure, trauma-sensitive care, and crisis intervention. Includes instruction in disaster response, grief and loss counseling, crisis intervention and management, trauma counseling, neurobiology of trauma, PTSD and combat-related trauma, relational trauma and treatment of trauma-related disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for energy-efficient and high-performance computer hardware by optimizing thermal management and computational throughput in next-generation multi-core processors. As processor architectures scale in complexity—with increasing core counts, heterogeneous designs, and 3D integrated circuits (ICs)—traditional simulation tools struggle to model thermal-electronic interactions at sufficient fidelity. Current methods often oversimplify material properties, boundary conditions, and dynamic workloads, leading to suboptimal thermal solutions that limit device longevity and performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-physics computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cooling system design, and machine learning (ML) to predict thermal behavior under variable operational scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute these simulations at scale, as the coupled models require parallel processing of fine-grained meshes (exceeding 10^8 elements) and iterative optimization across thousands of design parameters. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers (e.g., ANSYS Mechanical, OpenFOAM) and ML libraries (TensorFlow, PyTorch) to explore novel cooling topologies, adaptive voltage-frequency scaling policies, and material configurations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting thermal runaway thresholds in 3D ICs, a dataset of optimized cooling strategies for heterogeneous architectures, and open-source tools for co-simulating electronic and thermal performance. These results will directly inform the design of energy-efficient processors for data centers and edge computing devices, reducing cooling energy costs by an estimated 15–30% compared to conventional approaches. By integrating computational modeling with hardware prototyping, this work advances the broader goal of sustainable computing while providing students in Computer Hardware Technology with hands-on experience in cutting-edge simulation-driven design methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate high-performance computing (HPC) resources into the creation and analysis of advanced metal artworks, addressing the challenge of scaling complex, data-driven design processes within traditional metal arts practices. While manual fabrication techniques remain foundational, computational tools are increasingly critical for optimizing material behavior, simulating structural integrity, and generating intricate forms that exceed the limits of conventional workflows. The research problem centers on bridging gaps between artistic intent and technical feasibility, particularly in large-scale sculptures or designs involving dynamic material interactions (e.g., thermal stresses in castings, alloy corrosion patterns). To address this, the project will deploy finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model metal flow during casting, stress distribution in welded joints, and electrochemical responses in anodized surfaces. Machine learning algorithms will also be trained on historical and experimental datasets to predict optimal fabrication parameters for novel alloys or hybrid techniques, such as combining 3D-printed wax patterns with lost-wax casting. HPC resources are essential for handling the high-resolution meshing, multi-physics simulations, and iterative generative design processes required for these tasks, which exceed the capacity of standard workstations. Expected outcomes include a suite of computational workflows tailored to metal arts, enabling artists to previsualize material outcomes, reduce physical prototyping waste, and explore geometries informed by algorithmic design. The project will yield both scholarly contributions—documenting interdisciplinary methods for computational craft—and tangible artworks exhibited in public venues, demonstrating how HPC can expand the creative and technical frontiers of metal-based artistic practice. By situating computational modeling as a complementary tool to hands-on craftsmanship, this work aims to redefine pedagogical and professional standards in the visual arts, fostering innovation at the intersection of technology and tradition.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of individual artistic expression and technical skills necessary for fabricating refined metal works. Includes instruction in aesthetics, anodizing, art history, casting, design, electroforming, enameling, metalsmithing, sculpture, two and three-dimensional design, wax carving, and welding.

abstract: Animal-assisted therapy (AAT) leverages human-animal interactions to improve outcomes for individuals with disabilities, yet the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain poorly characterized. This project seeks to address this gap by investigating dynamic neural and physiological responses during structured human-animal interactions using high-resolution multimodal datasets. The research will integrate electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), heart rate variability (HRV), and salivary cortisol measurements from 120 participants (60 neurotypical, 60 with autism spectrum disorder) during controlled sessions with therapy dogs. The primary computational challenge involves processing and analyzing terabytes of temporally synchronized, high-dimensional biological data to identify cross-modal interaction patterns predictive of therapeutic benefit. We propose developing a custom machine learning pipeline optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments, combining topological data analysis for feature extraction with recurrent neural networks to model temporal dependencies in neurophysiological responses. Concurrently, agent-based computational models will simulate hypothesized stress regulation pathways mediated by oxytocinergic and autonomic nervous system dynamics. This dual approach requires parallel processing capabilities for large-scale parameter space exploration and validation against empirical data. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of quantifiable biomarkers distinguishing effective from ineffective AAT interventions, (2) predictive models linking specific interaction characteristics (e.g., tactile engagement duration, animal-initiated eye contact) to neurophysiological modulation, and (3) open-source computational frameworks for optimizing therapy animal training protocols. By elucidating the biological substrates of human-animal therapeutic interactions, this work aims to establish an evidence-based foundation for personalizing AAT protocols while advancing computational methods for analyzing complex biosignals in heterogeneous clinical populations. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive analyses and achieving the temporal resolution required to capture millisecond-scale neurodynamic shifts during naturalistic therapy sessions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares health and human service professionals to integrate the use of animals into their treatment practices in order to facilitate change in people with mental and physical disabilities. Includes instruction in psychology, psychology of disabilities, animal behavior, animal training, the human-animal bond, integration of animals into therapeutic settings, and ethical and cultural issues.

abstract: The development of novel therapeutics is hindered by the complexity of predicting drug-target interactions and optimizing pharmacokinetic properties. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and time-consuming, necessitating advanced computational strategies. This project seeks to utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the discovery of small-molecule inhibitors targeting protein kinases implicated in inflammatory diseases. We will employ molecular dynamics simulations to model binding dynamics and free energy calculations to assess affinity and selectivity. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will be trained on multi-omics datasets to predict ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) profiles and prioritize candidates with optimal safety-efficacy ratios. The integration of these computational approaches will enable large-scale virtual screening of compound libraries, significantly reducing the experimental validation burden. Expected outcomes include the identification of lead compounds with validated kinase inhibition, computational frameworks for rapid toxicity prediction, and open-source tools for structure-based drug design. This research will advance precision pharmacotherapy by enabling data-driven optimization of drug candidates and provide a scalable platform for repurposing existing therapeutics. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale simulation data and computationally intensive training of deep neural networks, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local infrastructure. By bridging computational and experimental pharmacology, this project aims to shorten the drug development timeline and reduce costs, directly contributing to the translational goals of pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Pharmacy, Pharmaceutical Sciences, and Administration, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution and syntactic variation of understudied Semitic languages through large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary textual corpora. The primary research challenge lies in processing and analyzing vast, multilingual datasets spanning diverse dialects and time periods—including Classical Arabic, Neo-Aramaic, and Epigraphic South Arabian—which exhibit complex morphological structures and non-Latin scripts. Manual analysis of these features at scale is infeasible due to the volume of texts and the need for cross-referential pattern detection. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to deploy custom natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Semitic languages, integrating morphological parsers, syntactic dependency taggers, and semantic role labeling algorithms. Parallelized workflows will enable comparative analysis of linguistic features across temporal, geographic, and sociolinguistic dimensions, while transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to identify diachronic shifts in grammatical structures. A key innovation involves the development of graph-based representations to map contact-induced changes between Semitic and non-Semitic languages of the Near East. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital corpus of annotated texts for several endangered varieties, quantitative models of syntactic change spanning two millennia, and open-source tools for computational Semitic linguistics. These resources will significantly advance understanding of language contact dynamics in the region while providing methodological frameworks for analyzing low-resource languages with non-concatenative morphology. The requested computing resources are critical for training large language models on specialized orthographic representations and maintaining the petabyte-scale multilingual database central to this interdisciplinary inquiry.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Middle/ Near Eastern and Semitic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the transmission and transformation of cultural symbols within Chinese diaspora communities through large-scale analysis of digitized textual and visual materials. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how diasporic groups reinterpret traditional cultural motifs—such as folklore, ritual iconography, and vernacular architecture—in diverse global contexts, and how these adaptations reflect evolving notions of identity. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual textual analysis and computer vision techniques for pattern recognition in visual cultural artifacts. A corpus of 20,000+ primary sources will be processed, including community newspapers, oral history transcripts, digitized material culture collections, and social media archives spanning 15 diaspora communities from the 19th century to present. Custom transformer models will be developed to handle classical Chinese characters, regional dialects in transliterated forms, and code-mixed languages prevalent in diaspora texts. High-performance computing resources are essential for training these models on heterogeneous data, conducting cross-modal analysis between textual and visual datasets, and running spatial-temporal simulations of cultural diffusion patterns. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of understudied adaptation pathways for traditional symbols in extraterritorial contexts, 2) quantitative frameworks for analyzing cultural hybridity in diaspora studies, and 3) open-access tools for processing linguistically complex Sinophone materials. The project will advance methodological innovation in computational cultural studies while providing empirical insights into how diasporic communities negotiate heritage preservation and local integration. Results will inform scholarly debates on cultural sustainability in global migration contexts and support heritage organizations in developing more inclusive documentation strategies for transnational Chinese cultures.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of present-day China and its historical predecessors, related borderlands and island groups, and the overseas Chinese diaspora.

abstract: Palliative care research faces critical challenges in integrating complex, multimodal data to inform personalized interventions and improve patient outcomes. Current approaches often rely on fragmented analyses of electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, patient-reported outcomes, and clinician notes, limiting the ability to model dynamic symptom trajectories or predict treatment responses in advanced illness. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a scalable computational framework to analyze longitudinal palliative care datasets using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in multi-omics, clinical, and psychosocial data that correlate with palliative outcomes, including symptom burden reduction, quality-of-life metrics, and end-of-life care preferences. We propose applying machine learning architectures—including transformer-based models for temporal EHR analysis and graph neural networks for comorbidity-symptom interaction mapping—to synthesize heterogeneous data from 15,000+ patients across three health systems. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated training for deep learning models, parallelized survival analysis, and agent-based simulations of care intervention scenarios. Key technical challenges include managing high-dimensional sparse data, addressing missingness through generative imputation techniques, and ensuring model interpretability for clinical translation. The HPC environment is essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets, running ensemble model comparisons, and conducting sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing palliative care timing, personalized symptom management algorithms, and risk stratification models for proactive care planning. This work will generate open-source computational pipelines tailored to palliative care research while advancing methodological innovation in clinical decision support systems. By enabling large-scale integration of real-world data, the project aims to transform evidence-based palliative care practice and inform health system resource allocation for aging populations with serious illness.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing plant health and landscape sustainability in managed green spaces through advanced computational modeling of dynamic plant-environment interactions. Current landscaping practices rely heavily on generalized guidelines for irrigation, nutrient application, and pest management, which often fail to account for micro-scale variations in soil composition, microclimate, and plant phenology. We propose to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating agent-based modeling of plant growth with real-time environmental data assimilation to predict outcomes under diverse management scenarios. The computational approach will couple process-based models of turfgrass and ornamental species physiology with machine learning algorithms trained on hyperspectral imaging data and IoT sensor feeds from experimental plots. High-performance computing resources are essential to parameterize species-specific responses across heterogeneous landscapes, simulate water-nutrient dynamics at sub-meter scales, and conduct Monte Carlo analyses of long-term management strategies under climate uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of prescribing spatially variable irrigation schedules, fertilizer application rates, and species selection matrices that minimize resource use while maintaining aesthetic and functional requirements. By enabling precision landscaping at scale, this research will provide commercial groundskeeping operations and urban planners with evidence-based tools to reduce water consumption by an estimated 15-25%, decrease chemical inputs, and enhance climate resilience in designed landscapes. The proposed work directly advances the agricultural sciences through novel applications of computational agroinformatics to ornamental horticulture, while maintaining strict exclusion of natural ecosystem conservation aspects to align with program scope.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the thermal and power efficiency of next-generation computer processors through advanced computational modeling and simulation. As processor architectures scale toward smaller transistor sizes and higher component densities, managing heat dissipation and power distribution becomes increasingly complex, directly impacting device reliability and performance. Traditional empirical testing methods are insufficient for exploring the vast design space of modern multi-core processors and heterogenous computing units, necessitating high-fidelity simulations to guide hardware design. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model thermal gradients, material stress, and power delivery networks at the microarchitecture level. These simulations will integrate machine learning-driven optimization to iteratively refine cooling solutions, substrate materials, and power gating configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multi-physics interactions across nanometer-scale geometries and millisecond-scale operational cycles, which require parallelized solvers and large memory allocations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting thermal runaway thresholds, identifying optimal layouts for on-chip cooling structures, and proposing material interfaces to mitigate electromigration in high-current conditions. This work will directly support the development of energy-efficient processors for high-performance computing clusters and edge devices, while advancing methodologies for virtual prototyping in computer hardware design. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ design permutations, reducing reliance on physical prototyping and accelerating iteration cycles for industry partners in semiconductor manufacturing. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and collaboration with hardware testing laboratories to bridge computational predictions with empirical validation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: Hydroelectric power systems are critical to renewable energy infrastructure, yet optimizing their efficiency and sustainability remains a complex challenge due to dynamic fluid-structure interactions, sediment transport, and environmental constraints. This project seeks to advance hydroelectric energy technology by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate and optimize turbine performance, sediment management, and ecological impact mitigation in dam-reservoir systems. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve multi-scale, multi-physics phenomena, including turbulent flow through turbine runners, sediment erosion dynamics, and fish passage viability. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) frameworks such as OpenFOAM and ANSYS Fluent, we will model transient hydraulic conditions under varying operational scenarios, integrating machine learning algorithms to identify optimal turbine geometries and operational protocols. Additionally, discrete element modeling (DEM) will simulate sediment transport to evaluate long-term infrastructure wear, while agent-based models (ABMs) will assess ecological impacts on aquatic ecosystems. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from laboratory-scale hydraulic rigs and field measurements from partner hydroelectric facilities. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for turbine efficiency optimization, strategies to reduce sediment-related maintenance costs, and frameworks for environmentally sustainable dam operations. By addressing these interconnected technical and ecological challenges, this research aims to enhance the reliability, cost-effectiveness, and environmental compatibility of hydroelectric systems, supporting global transitions to low-carbon energy. The scale and resolution required for these simulations necessitate access to HPC resources to manage large datasets, parallelize computationally intensive solvers, and enable rapid parameter sweeps. Results will be disseminated through open-source code repositories, industry partnerships, and public policy briefs to maximize translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in hydroelectric energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly threatened by climate change, invasive species, and shifting disturbance regimes, necessitating advanced predictive tools to guide sustainable management. Current forest growth and yield models often lack the spatial resolution, mechanistic detail, and scalability required to address these interconnected stressors across heterogeneous landscapes. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate forest dynamics at unprecedented scales, integrating species-specific physiological responses, pest dispersal patterns, and wildfire behavior under multiple climate scenarios. Leveraging LiDAR-derived canopy structure data, satellite-based phenology time series, and regional climate projections, we will parameterize agent-based models to predict tree mortality, regeneration, and carbon sequestration patterns across a 10,000 km² study area in the northeastern United States. The computational workflow will employ parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in biotic and abiotic interactions, while machine learning surrogates will accelerate parameter optimization. Resource-intensive tasks include processing multi-terabyte remote sensing datasets, running fine-grained cellular automata for bark beetle outbreaks, and coupling hydrodynamic wildfire spread models with forest fuel moisture dynamics. Anticipated outcomes include (1) spatially explicit risk maps identifying stands vulnerable to compound disturbances, (2) optimized harvest scheduling algorithms balancing timber production and carbon storage, and (3) open-source visualization tools enabling managers to interact with scenario projections. By harnessing HPC capabilities to resolve ecological processes across scales, this work will provide forest technologists with decision-support systems that traditional single-threaded models cannot deliver. The resulting framework advances both computational ecology methods and applied forest management strategies, directly supporting climate-resilient conservation practices in line with regional sustainability goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist foresters in the management and production of forest resources. Includes instruction in woods and field skills, tree identification, timber measurement, logging and timber harvesting, forest propagation and regeneration, forest fire-fighting, resource management, equipment operation and maintenance, record-keeping, sales and purchasing operations, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of precolonial African social and political networks through large-scale spatial and temporal analysis of fragmented historical data. While Africa’s precolonial history is richly documented in diverse sources—including oral traditions, archaeological findings, traveler accounts, and colonial records—these materials remain dispersed, heterogeneous, and challenging to synthesize at continental scales. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to systematically analyze patterns of state formation, trade dynamics, or cultural diffusion across such vast, interconnected geographies and timeframes. This project addresses this gap by developing computational models to integrate and visualize multi-source data, enabling the identification of macrohistorical trends and localized interactions. Using geospatial analysis, network modeling, and machine learning techniques, we will map shifting political boundaries, trade routes, and cultural exchange networks across West and Central Africa from 1000–1800 CE. Key tasks include processing unstructured textual data (e.g., Arabic manuscripts, Portuguese colonial records) via NLP tools, georeferencing archaeological site data, and simulating trade network resilience under environmental stressors. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale of geospatial datasets, running agent-based simulations of social interactions, and training transformer models to detect linguistic and thematic patterns in multilingual corpora. Expected outcomes include an open-access interactive atlas of precolonial African polities, a repository of computationally enhanced historical datasets, and new insights into the longue durée impacts of trans-Saharan and intra-African exchange systems. By bridging computational methods with African historiographic scholarship, this project aims to reshape understandings of precolonial statecraft, mobility, and connectivity while centering African agency in global historical narratives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of one or more peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara (and including the African diasporas overseas) from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of systematically analyzing large-scale, cross-cultural music datasets to uncover patterns in melodic, rhythmic, and timbral structures across diverse musical traditions. While traditional musicological methods rely on manual transcription and comparative analysis, the volume and complexity of global audio archives—spanning field recordings, historical performances, and contemporary genres—exceed the capacity of conventional computational tools. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multimodal music data, including audio signals, metadata, and ethnographic annotations, from over 20 distinct cultural traditions. Computational workflows will integrate audio feature extraction (e.g., pitch tracking, spectrotemporal decomposition), machine learning classifiers for genre and style recognition, and network analysis to map intercultural influences. Key tasks include parallelized processing of 50,000+ audio samples using GPU-accelerated libraries, training transformer-based models on symbolic music representations, and simulating agent-based models to test hypotheses about the diffusion of musical innovations. Outcomes will advance methodological frameworks for computational ethnomusicology, enabling the identification of previously undocumented relationships between musical practices and sociocultural contexts. The project will produce open-source tools for large-scale music analysis, a curated repository of annotated datasets, and publications re-evaluating theoretical constructs such as "musical universals" through data-driven perspectives. By scaling analytical rigor to match the diversity of global music practices, this work aims to bridge gaps between qualitative ethnographic research and quantitative music information retrieval, offering new pathways to study musical change, cultural hybridity, and intangible heritage preservation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the forms and methods of music art, and the functions of music, in Western and non-Western societies and cultures. Includes instruction in music theory, musicological research methods, and studies of specific cultural styles such as jazz, folk music, rock, ethnic musical traditions, and the music of non-Western cultures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in classical philology and digital humanities, addressing challenges in analyzing fragmented and multilingual textual corpora from antiquity. The core research problem centers on reconstructing and interpreting understudied classical texts—such as papyri, inscriptions, and palimpsests—that are often physically degraded, linguistically hybrid, or dispersed across archives. Traditional manual methods struggle to efficiently process these materials at scale, particularly when analyzing syntactic patterns, cross-cultural linguistic exchange, or textual reuse across Greek, Latin, and neighboring languages. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and phylogenetics. HPC resources will enable large-scale tokenization, morphological tagging, and semantic modeling of digitized texts using transformer-based architectures fine-tuned for ancient languages. Parallelized algorithms will trace lexical and stylistic diffusion across regions and periods, while Monte Carlo simulations will test hypotheses about textual transmission pathways. A key innovation involves deploying graph neural networks to map intertextual networks in fragmentary literature, reconstructing plausible connections between works. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital corpus annotated with linguistic and historical metadata, new quantitative frameworks for assessing authorship in anonymous texts, and visualizations of cultural exchange dynamics in the ancient Mediterranean. This work will provide novel methodologies for integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, offering insights into multilingualism, textual production, and intellectual networks in antiquity. By demonstrating scalable computational approaches to classical studies, the project aims to bridge disciplinary gaps and establish best practices for HPC-driven humanities research.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Reproductive endocrinology and infertility (REI) involve complex, multifactorial disorders influenced by dynamic hormonal, genetic, and environmental interactions. A critical challenge in managing these conditions lies in disentangling heterogeneous patient data—spanning genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic, and clinical variables—to identify predictive biomarkers and personalized treatment pathways. Current analytical approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multi-omics datasets at scale or model non-linear biological interactions, limiting progress toward precision medicine in REI. This project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to address these gaps by leveraging large-scale data integration, machine learning, and dynamic systems modeling. We will analyze retrospective and prospective datasets from 15,000 patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, and unexplained infertility, including whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal hormone profiles, electronic health records, and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian hierarchical models to account for population heterogeneity, graph neural networks to map hormone-receptor interaction networks, and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize simulated treatment protocols. A key innovation involves coupling single-cell RNA-seq data from endometrial biopsies with agent-based modeling to simulate embryo implantation dynamics under varying hormonal conditions. These analyses demand parallelized processing of petabyte-scale data, stochastic parameter sampling, and real-time optimization—tasks requiring HPC resources for GPU-accelerated model training, distributed memory architectures, and high-throughput job scheduling. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for ovarian response and IVF success, (2) mechanistic insights into progesterone resistance in endometriosis, and (3) a validated computational platform for simulating patient-specific treatment adjustments. By elucidating pathophysiological pathways and enabling data-driven clinical decision-making, this work aims to advance therapeutic strategies for complex REI disorders while establishing scalable computational methodologies for reproductive medicine research.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage complex problems relating to reproductive endocrinology and infertility.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the resilience of ecological communities to climate-driven disturbances by integrating field-derived interaction networks with spatially explicit, dynamic simulations. A critical challenge in evolutionary ecology lies in predicting how interspecific relationships—such as competition, mutualism, and trophic dependencies—mediate ecosystem responses to environmental stressors. Traditional models often oversimplify biotic interactions or fail to capture nonlinear feedbacks across scales, limiting their utility for conservation planning. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that simulates community dynamics under varying climate scenarios, parameterized using empirical data from long-term monitoring of temperate forest and freshwater ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run ensembles of these computationally intensive simulations, which track individual species’ traits, interaction strengths, and dispersal constraints at fine spatial resolutions (1 km² grids) across decadal timescales. The models will incorporate paleoecological data to calibrate historical baselines and test hypotheses about co-evolutionary buffers to disturbance. Parallelized sensitivity analyses will identify key thresholds in habitat connectivity and functional diversity that govern ecosystem collapse or recovery. Outcomes will advance mechanistic understanding of how biotic networks mediate resilience, enabling predictions of community restructuring under projected warming scenarios. Results will directly inform regional habitat corridor designs and species-specific management plans. By leveraging HPC capabilities to scale from organismal physiology to landscape-level processes, this work bridges a critical gap between ecological theory and climate adaptation practice. The computational workflows and open-source tools generated will provide a template for integrating complex interaction networks into predictive ecology, with applications in conservation biology and ecosystem services planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions of small-scale biological systems, such as organisms, to each other, to complex and whole systems, and to the physical and other non-biological aspects of their environments. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry; landscape and/or marine/aquatic dynamics; decomposition; global and regional elemental budgets; biotic and abiotic regulation of nutrient cycles; ecophysiology; ecosystem resilience, disturbance, and succession; community and habitat dynamics; organismal interactions (co-evolution, competition, predation); paleoecology; and evolutionary ecology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biomedical data in laboratory animal research—spanning high-throughput sequencing, multimodal imaging, and longitudinal behavioral datasets—presents significant challenges for traditional analytical methods. Current approaches often lack the computational power to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale, limiting insights into disease mechanisms, treatment responses, and predictive modeling for translational applications. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable advanced computational workflows for analyzing large-scale datasets derived from murine and non-human primate models of neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) developing machine learning frameworks to identify biomarkers from multi-omics data (genomics, proteomics, metabolomics) correlated with disease progression; (2) implementing GPU-accelerated image analysis pipelines for whole-slide histopathology and in vivo MRI datasets; and (3) simulating host-pathogen-environment interactions in infectious disease models using agent-based modeling. Computational workflows will leverage containerized environments for reproducibility and utilize distributed computing architectures to process terabytes of raw data. Expected outcomes include novel predictive models of treatment efficacy, optimized protocols for automated pathological scoring, and quantitative frameworks for assessing environmental variables in experimental design. By integrating HPC capabilities, this work aims to address critical bottlenecks in translational animal research, enhancing both the statistical rigor of preclinical studies and the welfare of research animals through reduced experimental redundancy. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated as open-source resources to support reproducibility in laboratory animal medicine, with direct implications for accelerating therapeutic development in human clinical trials.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied veterinary research and related techniques, equipment, data systems and research design. May included related research in the management of veterinary and other animal research laboratories and health care facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision agricultural decision-making tools for extension professionals and growers. A critical challenge in agricultural systems is optimizing site-specific management practices—such as irrigation scheduling, nutrient application, and integrated pest management—under dynamic environmental conditions. Current tools often rely on generalized models that lack the resolution to account for hyperlocal variability in soil properties, microclimates, and pest population dynamics, leading to suboptimal resource use and reduced crop resilience. To address this gap, we propose developing a scalable computational framework integrating multi-source geospatial data (soil sensors, drone imagery, regional weather stations) with mechanistic crop growth models and machine learning algorithms. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-resolution datasets (1–5m spatial granularity) across thousands of simulated agricultural fields, coupled with parameter optimization for pest lifecycle models (e.g., degree-day accumulations for invasive species). This approach will generate probabilistic risk maps and real-time management recommendations tailored to individual farms. The computational workflow will prioritize interoperability with existing extension service platforms to ensure practical deployment. Anticipated outcomes include a cloud-based decision support system that reduces input costs by 15–20% in pilot regions while maintaining yield targets, as well as modular training materials for extension agents on interpreting model outputs. By scaling fine-grained analyses across diverse agroecological zones, this work will enhance the precision and adaptability of outreach services, directly supporting the Agricultural and Extension Education Services mission to deliver science-based, context-specific solutions to agricultural stakeholders.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide referral, consulting, technical assistance, and educational services to gardeners, farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and other organizations. Includes instruction in basic agricultural sciences, agricultural business operations, pest control, adult education methods, public relations, applicable state laws and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: Forest ecosystems face escalating threats from climate change, including increased drought stress, pest outbreaks, and wildfire frequency, which challenge traditional forest management frameworks. Current predictive models often lack the spatial resolution and computational scalability to integrate multi-source data—such as high-resolution remote sensing, LiDAR-derived canopy structures, and dynamic soil moisture profiles—across large, heterogeneous landscapes. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate forest resilience under climate-driven disturbances at ecologically relevant scales. Leveraging process-based forest dynamics models (e.g., ED2 or LPJ-GLM) coupled with machine learning algorithms, we will parameterize species-specific stress responses and quantify feedbacks between forest structure, disturbance regimes, and carbon cycling. The computational workflow will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to assess uncertainty in climate projections and optimize adaptive management strategies, such as selective thinning or assisted migration. Key datasets include multi-temporal satellite imagery, USDA Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) plots, and regional climate model outputs. The HPC resources will enable hyperparameter tuning for neural networks analyzing canopy mortality patterns and runtime-intensive simulations across 10^4–10^5 ha domains. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maps of forest vulnerability, identification of bioclimatic tipping points, and decision-support tools for prioritizing intervention zones. This work will advance the integration of ecological theory with computational scalability in forest management, directly informing state and federal agencies on climate-adaptive practices while contributing open-source code for large-scale forest resilience modeling. By resolving fine-grained interactions between biotic and abiotic drivers, the project aims to bridge critical gaps in spatial explicitness and computational efficiency that currently hinder actionable forest policy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of forestry and natural resources management to the administration of forest lands and related resources. Includes instruction in silviculture, forest mensuration, forest protection, inventorying, biometrics, geographic information systems, remote sensing, photogrammetry, forest policy and economics, forest land use planning, fire protection and management, and related administrative skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the therapeutic efficacy of art interventions in clinical populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process multimodal datasets. Art therapy relies on qualitative interpretation of visual and behavioral data, which limits scalability and reproducibility. To address this, we propose integrating machine learning (ML) with psychometric evaluations to quantify relationships between artistic expression, emotional states, and therapeutic outcomes. The research problem centers on identifying objective biomarkers within art therapy processes—such as color use, composition, and symbolic content in patient artwork—and correlating these with clinical metrics (e.g., symptom severity scales, physiological stress markers). Current methods lack the computational power to analyze large volumes of high-resolution visual data alongside longitudinal patient records. Our approach combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image feature extraction, natural language processing (NLP) for therapist notes, and graph-based models to map dynamic patient progress. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning architectures on terabytes of anonymized patient artwork (n ≈ 5,000 images), video recordings of sessions, and electronic health record integrations. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking specific artistic elements to therapeutic milestones in disorders such as PTSD and depression, (2) an open-source toolkit for art therapists to visualize patient progress computationally, and (3) validation of hybrid human-AI workflows to enhance clinical decision-making. By bridging art therapy’s subjective dimensions with data-driven analytics, this work aims to establish reproducible standards for treatment personalization while maintaining ethical alignment with therapeutic practices. The computational infrastructure will also support future studies on cross-cultural art symbolism and real-time biofeedback integration during art creation, advancing the field’s capacity for evidence-based innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use drawing and other art media forms to assess, treat, and rehabilitate individuals with mental, emotional, developmental, or physical disorders. Includes instruction in art, history and theory of art therapy, art therapeutic techniques, psychopathology, patient assessment and diagnosis, cultural diversity issues, legal and ethical practice issues, and professional standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the development of regional political economies in the United States from 1790 to 1860, a critical period of early nation-building and sectional conflict. The research problem centers on mapping and quantifying the interplay between agricultural production, labor systems (including enslaved labor), transportation networks, and legislative decision-making across states and territories. Traditional historiography has relied on fragmented datasets or qualitative case studies, limiting systematic comparisons of how regional economic priorities influenced federal policies and long-term socio-political divisions. To address this gap, the project will integrate digitized census records, legislative voting data, agricultural schedules, transportation maps, and newspaper corpora into a unified geospatial-temporal database. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) to extract economic discourse from newspapers, agent-based modeling to simulate legislative coalition formation, and network analysis to trace commodity flows. HPC resources are essential for processing over 10 million pages of text, running iterative simulations of political-economic scenarios, and handling high-resolution spatial datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying previously overlooked correlations between localized economic pressures and federal policy shifts, (2) visualizing the evolution of regional economic networks that preceded the Civil War, and (3) publishing an open-access database linking legislative actions to constituent economic interests. This work will provide a scalable computational framework for analyzing path dependency in American institutional development while offering new empirical insights into how material conditions shaped conflicts over sovereignty and slavery. The requested resources will enable processing at scales unachievable with standard workstations, reducing runtime for corpus analysis from months to days and supporting complex model iterations critical for robust historical inference.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of American society, culture, and institutions from the Pre-Columbian period to the present. Includes instruction in American historiography, American history sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving role of digital communication in lay ministry, specifically examining how non-ordained religious leaders navigate ethical and practical challenges in virtual pastoral care. As lay ministers increasingly adopt online platforms for spiritual guidance, community building, and crisis intervention, there is a critical need to map the linguistic, emotional, and relational patterns that define effective—or potentially harmful—digital ministry practices. The study will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze a corpus of 500,000+ anonymized text-based interactions (e.g., counseling chats, sermon comments, prayer forums) from diverse denominational contexts. Computational sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network graphs will identify recurring themes, communication strategies, and ethical dilemmas unique to digital spaces, such as maintaining spiritual authenticity in abbreviated formats or addressing misinformation in real-time discussions. HPC resources are essential for processing this unstructured, multilingual dataset while preserving nuanced theological and cultural contexts. Expected outcomes include a framework for training lay ministers in digital literacy, an open-access toolkit for ethically auditing online ministry interactions, and predictive models to flag high-risk communication scenarios. By bridging computational linguistics with practical theology, this project aims to establish scalable, evidence-based best practices for lay leaders operating at the intersection of faith and technology, ultimately strengthening community resilience in digitally mediated religious spaces.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained individuals to serve as lay pastors, religious educators, youth leaders, and other professional positions open to the laity in local churches and other settings. Includes instruction in bible studies, theology, spirituality, pastoral counseling, foundations of ministry, effective communication, and church leadership.

abstract: Cancer progression is driven by dynamic interactions between tumor cells and their microenvironment, yet the physiological mechanisms underlying these processes remain poorly understood. This project seeks to characterize how tumor-induced vascular remodeling and hypoxia influence metastatic potential and therapeutic resistance in epithelial cancers, with a focus on pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). A critical barrier is the inability of conventional experimental models to capture the multi-scale, nonlinear feedback between cellular metabolism, hemodynamic forces, and tissue-level adaptation over clinically relevant timescales. We propose to address this gap through an integrative computational physiology framework combining 1) agent-based modeling of tumor-stroma interactions, 2) lattice Boltzmann simulations of blood flow through evolving vascular networks, and 3) parameter optimization algorithms informed by time-resolved microscopy data from 3D bioprinted tumor models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatiotemporal relationships across molecular (nutrient gradients), cellular (endothelial migration), and tissue (perfusion heterogeneity) scales while accounting for patient-specific vascular architectures derived from clinical imaging. Our preliminary studies demonstrate that tumor endothelial cell metabolic reprogramming alters vascular permeability thresholds in a flow-dependent manner, but current workstation-based simulations cannot simultaneously track >10⁵ interacting agents across 72-hour developmental windows. The requested allocation would enable ensemble runs exploring therapeutic perturbation of angiogenic signaling under varying mechanical microenvironments (shear stress, interstitial pressure), with direct validation against organ-on-chip experimental data. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying hemodynamic biomarkers of early metastasis and a publicly accessible simulation platform for testing combination therapies targeting physiological vulnerabilities in treatment-resistant tumors. This work will establish computational physiology as a critical tool for bridging subcellular mechanisms to organ-level cancer phenotypes, directly supporting the development of physics-informed treatment strategies in precision oncology.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the functional dynamics, morphology, and biochemical and biophysical communications within organisms and between living systems at all levels of complexity and integration. Includes instruction in reproduction, growth, hormonal action, vascular function, respiration, digestion, sensory perception and processing, sensorimotor integration, signal encoding and conveyance, homeostasis, physical function and malfunction, evolutionary physiology, and disease processes.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and behavioral mechanisms underlying arts-based interventions for chronic pain management, an emerging interdisciplinary niche within health sciences. Chronic pain affects over 20% of adults globally, yet pharmacological treatments often yield incomplete relief or adverse side effects. While preliminary evidence suggests that structured engagement with visual arts, music, or movement modulates pain perception, the biological and cognitive pathways involved remain poorly characterized. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets from a longitudinal study of 300 participants undergoing arts-in-medicine protocols. Data streams include high-density EEG recordings (256 channels at 2kHz), dynamic facial expression analysis via 4D video, cortisol levels from saliva samples, and self-reported pain scores. Computational challenges involve real-time synchronization of heterogeneous temporal data, feature extraction from high-dimensional neuroimaging datasets, and machine learning-driven pattern recognition across disparate biological and behavioral signals. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of 50TB of raw data, implementation of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for EEG microstate classification, and agent-based modeling to simulate neural-immune interactions modulated by arts engagement. Expected outcomes include identification of biomarker signatures predictive of intervention efficacy, quantitative models linking specific artistic activities (e.g., guided painting vs improvisational dance) to distinct neuroinflammatory pathways, and an open-source computational framework for optimizing personalized arts therapies. By elucidating the systems-level mechanisms through which arts interventions alleviate chronic pain, this work aims to establish an evidence base for integrating arts modalities into mainstream pain management protocols while advancing computational methods for studying embodied, non-pharmacological health interventions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of programs that use the visual and performing arts in support of health and wellness among diverse individuals and communities. Includes instruction in dance, literary arts, music, theatre, healthcare systems, program administration, and public health.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop computational models to optimize operational decision-making in funeral service management, a field facing unique challenges due to fluctuating demand patterns, cultural diversity in service expectations, and stringent regulatory constraints. Traditional approaches to resource allocation—such as staff scheduling, inventory management for perishable goods like floral arrangements, and real-time coordination of multi-site services—often rely on static heuristics, leading to inefficiencies during periods of high demand or unexpected disruptions. To address this, we propose an agent-based simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic interactions between service providers, clients, and supply chains under variable scenarios. The computational approach integrates demographic data, historical service records, and probabilistic event triggers (e.g., public health crises) to simulate demand surges, supply bottlenecks, and staffing gaps. Machine learning techniques will be applied to refine predictive accuracy for service customization, such as estimating culturally informed preferences for memorialization practices. By parallelizing thousands of scenario iterations across HPC clusters, the project aims to generate adaptive decision-support tools that balance ethical considerations, cost constraints, and service quality. Expected outcomes include open-source optimization algorithms tailored to funeral home workflows, validated against real-world operational data from partner institutions. This work bridges a critical gap in non-STEM disciplines by introducing scalable computational methods to a sector traditionally reliant on manual processes, with potential applications in crisis response planning and ethical AI integration for sensitive service industries. The resource allocation request prioritizes GPU-enabled nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale simulations of multi-jurisdictional regulatory compliance scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional licensure as funeral directors and as managers of funeral homes, cemeteries, and related services.  Includes instruction in the sociology of death and dying, psychology of grief and grief counseling, history of funeral service, funeral direction, business law, funeral service law, funeral home management, accounting and related computer operations, and funeral services marketing and merchandising.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, installation, and maintenance of overhead and underground electrical and communication infrastructure, with a focus on improving safety, efficiency, and resilience in linework operations. Aging power grids, increasing demand for reliable broadband connectivity, and climate-driven stressors such as extreme weather necessitate innovative approaches to infrastructure planning. Current industry practices rely heavily on manual inspections and static safety margins, which lack predictive capabilities for dynamic risks like equipment fatigue, thermal expansion in high-voltage lines, or soil instability near underground cables. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in power distribution systems. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) to model mechanical stresses on utility poles and towers under wind and ice loads, machine learning algorithms trained on historical fault data to predict cable degradation patterns, and geospatial modeling to assess trenching routes for underground fiber-optic networks. Large-scale simulations will evaluate the cascading impacts of equipment failures on grid stability, while reinforcement learning frameworks will optimize real-time decision-making for emergency repairs. By coupling these models with LiDAR-derived terrain data and real-time sensor inputs, the project aims to generate adaptive risk assessment tools for lineworkers, including dynamic load-calculation systems for crane operations near live conductors and probabilistic maps of excavation hazards. Outcomes will include open-source simulation modules for training programs, validated against field data from partner utilities, and a digital twin framework to test infrastructure upgrades under climate change scenarios. This research will directly enhance the technical precision of lineworker education, reduce occupational hazards through predictive analytics, and inform standards for next-generation smart grid deployments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain and repair local, long-distance, and rural electric power cables and communication lines; erect and construct pole and tower lines; and install underground lines and cables. Includes instruction in cable installation and repair, fibre-optic technology, trenching, mobile equipment and crane operation, high-voltage installations, maintenance and inspection, safety, remote communications, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for modeling and simulating complex multiphysics systems with inherent nonlinear dynamics, a problem central to advancing predictive capabilities in applied mathematics. Traditional analytical approaches struggle to resolve the interplay of coupled physical processes—such as fluid-structure interactions, reactive transport, or phase transitions—in high-dimensional parameter spaces. To address this, we propose a hybrid numerical framework combining adaptive finite element discretizations, reduced-order modeling, and iterative solvers optimized for distributed-memory architectures.
