The research will focus on algorithm design to mitigate stiffness and memory bottlenecks inherent in multiscale simulations, leveraging parallel computing to enable efficient parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses. Key innovations include the integration of data-driven surrogate models to accelerate convergence in iterative schemes and the development of dynamic load-balancing strategies for heterogeneous computing environments. The computational workflows will be implemented using open-source libraries (e.g., PETSc, FEniCS) and tested on high-performance computing clusters to evaluate scalability. Anticipated outcomes include new error estimation techniques for coupled systems, validated against experimental datasets from collaborative engineering and geoscience projects. This work will directly support applications in renewable energy systems design and subsurface flow prediction, where high-fidelity simulations are critical but remain computationally prohibitive. By advancing the efficiency of multiphysics solvers, the project aims to bridge gaps between theoretical models and real-world deployment, while providing open-access benchmarks for the applied mathematics community. The requested computing resources are essential for handling problem sizes exceeding 1 billion degrees of freedom and for quantifying uncertainties across operational regimes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in applied mathematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of vocal performance through computational modeling and analysis of physiological, acoustic, and pedagogical data. While voice training traditionally relies on subjective mentorship and qualitative feedback, the lack of standardized, data-driven frameworks limits the scalability of personalized instruction and the understanding of biomechanical factors influencing vocal health and artistic expression. The research will address this gap by developing computational models of vocal fold dynamics, respiratory patterns, and acoustic output under varying performance conditions (e.g., repertoire demands, vocal registers, linguistic diction). High-fidelity simulations will integrate MRI-derived anatomical datasets, real-time motion capture of expressive movement, and spectral analysis of recorded performances to map correlations between physiological parameters and artistic outcomes. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in historical and contemporary vocal pedagogies, enabling the generation of adaptive training recommendations. Additionally, HPC resources will support the creation of a multimodal database for voice educators, linking performance metrics with pedagogical annotations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for injury prevention, tools to optimize rehearsal efficiency, and evidence-based frameworks for repertoire selection tailored to individual vocal profiles. By bridging computational science and performing arts methodologies, this work aims to transform vocal pedagogy into a data-enriched discipline while preserving the nuance of artistic tradition. The scalability of these tools will benefit both emerging artists and established professionals, fostering sustainable vocal practices across opera, concert, and ensemble contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the human voice and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers in concert, choir, opera, or other forms of singing. Includes instruction in voice pedagogy, diction, vocal physiology and exercise, expressive movement, repertoire, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for enhancing precision in anatomical modeling and diagnostic visualization by integrating multi-modal medical imaging data with patient-specific genomic and proteomic profiles. Current approaches to medical illustration often rely on static, population-averaged anatomical templates, limiting their utility in personalized treatment planning for complex conditions such as congenital anomalies or post-oncological reconstruction. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of dynamically reconciling high-resolution imaging data (e.g., 4D MRI, micro-CT) with heterogeneous molecular datasets to generate patient-adaptive 3D anatomical models. The proposed solution leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid pipeline combining geometric deep learning for feature extraction from imaging data, Bayesian networks for probabilistic integration of multi-omics data, and real-time physically based rendering techniques. Key computational challenges include processing petascale voxel datasets, optimizing memory-intensive tensor operations for neural network training on irregular anatomical meshes, and parallelizing radiative transfer simulations for photorealistic tissue visualization. The workflow will be validated using a cohort of 200 patients with craniofacial abnormalities, correlating model predictions with surgical outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source platform for multi-scale anatomical modeling, novel metrics for quantifying spatial concordance between molecular markers and phenotypic manifestations, and GPU-accelerated visualization modules for clinical decision support. This work bridges gaps between computational anatomy, biomedical informatics, and visual computing, with potential applications in surgical simulation, medical education, and biomarker discovery. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-distributed processing of whole-body scans, maintaining submillimeter spatial fidelity across imaging modalities, and achieving interactive frame rates during volumetric rendering of complex tissue interfaces.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in medical illustration and informatics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Reproductive cancers, such as ovarian and prostate malignancies, are tightly linked to dysregulated endocrine signaling, yet the mechanisms driving hormone-dependent tumor progression and therapy resistance remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address critical gaps in defining how dynamic hormonal interactions within the tumor microenvironment influence oncogenic pathways and treatment outcomes. We propose a computational physiology framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model spatially resolved hormone-receptor activation patterns, intracellular signaling cascades, and their integration with stromal cell dynamics. Multiscale agent-based models will simulate tumor growth under varying endocrine conditions, incorporating clinical data on serum hormone levels, receptor expression, and treatment histories from retrospective cohorts. These simulations will be validated against in vitro models of hormone-responsive cancer cell lines and patient-derived organoids. By deploying HPC resources, we will achieve the necessary scale to analyze complex, non-linear interactions between endocrine factors, cellular heterogeneity, and drug response variability. Expected outcomes include the identification of microenvironmental drivers of therapeutic resistance, predictive biomarkers for hormonal therapy efficacy, and optimized combinatorial treatment strategies. The computational pipelines developed will enable rapid hypothesis testing on hormonal perturbation effects, reducing reliance on high-cost in vivo models. This work will advance precision oncology in reproductive cancers by elucidating context-specific hormone signaling networks and providing a platform for simulating personalized treatment scenarios. Successful implementation requires dedicated HPC allocation to manage large parameter spaces, high-resolution spatial simulations, and machine learning-driven analysis of multimodal datasets.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of reproductive processes and biogenesis in animals and human beings. Includes instruction in reproductive ecology and behavior, reproductive system physiology, endocrinology, developmental biology, neuroendocrinology, evolution and types of reproductive systems, reproductive genetics, physiopathology of reproductive processes, and applications of molecular biology and biophysics to the study of reproductive physiology.

abstract: Public health education campaigns face significant challenges in tailoring interventions to diverse populations and dynamically evolving health threats, particularly when addressing disparities in health literacy and access to information. This project seeks to optimize the design and evaluation of adaptive, data-driven health promotion strategies using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral datasets. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate the spread of health behaviors through agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate demographic, sociocultural, and spatial data from national health surveys, social media, and electronic health records. These models will account for multi-level influences on health decision-making, including social networks, educational messaging efficacy, and environmental barriers. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to identify population-specific predictors of intervention success and generate personalized communication strategies. Computational experiments will test hypothetical scenarios for disease prevention campaigns (e.g., vaccination uptake, chronic disease management) across varied virtual populations, quantifying the projected impact of different educational approaches under resource constraints. The scalability of ABMs requires parallelized computing to manage complex interactions between millions of agents representing geographic and cultural subgroups. Expected outcomes include a framework for rapidly prototyping equity-focused health education strategies, predictive metrics for campaign performance, and evidence-based guidelines for allocating outreach resources. By enabling real-time simulation of intervention effects across heterogeneous communities, this work aims to advance the precision and cost-effectiveness of public health promotion while reducing evaluation timelines. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the memory-intensive nature of network-based behavioral models and the computational demands of iterative parameter optimization in high-dimensional public health datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of educational and communications principles and methods to the promotion of preventive health measures and the education of targeted populations on health issues, and prepares individuals to function as public health educators and health promotion specialists. Includes instruction in human development, health issues across the life span, population-specific health issues, principles and methods of public health education, administration of health education campaigns and programs, evaluation methods, public communications, and applications to specific public health subjects and issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary field of Culinary Science/Culinology by modeling complex interactions between food matrices, processing parameters, and sensory outcomes. Traditional approaches to recipe optimization and product development rely heavily on iterative physical experiments, which are time-intensive, resource-limited, and often fail to capture nonlinear relationships between variables such as ingredient ratios, thermal dynamics, and texture formation. The proposed research will address these challenges by developing computational models to simulate food systems at multiple scales, from molecular interactions in emulsions and gels to bulk behavior during thermal processing. Key computational methods include molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to study protein-polysaccharide binding kinetics in plant-based meat analogs, finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer modeling in sous-vide cooking, and machine learning (ML) frameworks trained on heterogeneous datasets (e.g., rheological measurements, sensory panel data) to predict optimal formulations for reduced-sodium sauces. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to establish a predictive pipeline for designing sustainable, nutritionally enhanced food products while minimizing physical prototyping. Expected outcomes include open-access algorithms tailored to culinary applications, validated models of starch-protein co-gelation under shear stress, and a decision-support tool for optimizing processing conditions in small-batch artisanal production. The work bridges gaps between food chemistry, culinary arts, and computational science, offering novel methodologies for an industry-facing discipline that lacks dedicated computational infrastructure. Access to HPC resources is critical for handling the high dimensionality of multi-omics data integration (e.g., linking proteomic profiles to textural outcomes) and achieving the millisecond-scale resolution required for simulating phase transitions in complex food colloids.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the blending of food science and the culinary arts and that prepares individuals to work as research chefs and related research and development positions in the food industry. Includes instruction in culinary arts, food chemistry, food safety and quality, food processing, nutrition, and business management.

abstract: The installation and finishing of drywall systems involve complex interactions between material properties, environmental conditions, and human technique, yet current practices rely heavily on empirical knowledge and standardized guidelines. This project seeks to advance drywall installation methodologies by developing computational models to optimize material performance, structural integrity, and labor efficiency. A critical challenge lies in predicting how factors such as humidity, temperature fluctuations, mechanical stress, and installation techniques influence the long-term durability of drywall systems. To address this, we propose a multi-physics simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model drywall behavior under diverse environmental and structural conditions. Finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate stress distribution across drywall panels and joints during installation and under load, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model moisture diffusion and thermal effects. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to identify optimal installation parameters, such as screw spacing, joint compound application thickness, and drying times. These models will integrate real-world data from embedded sensors in training environments to validate predictions. The computational scale requires HPC capabilities to manage high-resolution 3D simulations, iterative optimization workflows, and large-scale parameter sweeps. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing material waste, reducing installation errors, and enhancing compliance with safety standards. By quantifying relationships between technique and performance, this research will provide data-driven guidelines for curriculum updates in drywall education programs and contribute to the development of adaptive installation protocols. The project represents a novel integration of computational science into construction trades, with potential applications in automated quality assessment and precision drywall robotics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, tape, and plaster drywall installations in interior and exterior construction jobs. Includes instruction in drywall handling and transport, cutting and mounting, taping and spackling, finishing, job analysis and estimation, site safety, tool operation and maintenance, blueprint and specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Telemedicine has emerged as a critical tool for expanding access to care, yet challenges persist in optimizing its efficacy, particularly in integrating heterogeneous data streams and enabling real-time, data-driven clinical decisions. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a scalable computational framework to unify multi-modal patient data—including electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable device outputs, and real-time biosensor data—and apply predictive analytics to enhance diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment planning in telemedicine workflows. A key barrier is the computational complexity of processing and synthesizing high-dimensional, temporally dense datasets while adhering to privacy-preserving standards. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to deploy distributed machine learning models, federated learning architectures, and GPU-accelerated signal processing algorithms. The computational workflow will prioritize scalability to accommodate large patient cohorts and latency-sensitive applications, such as acute event prediction (e.g., sepsis, cardiac events) during remote monitoring. Validation will involve retrospective analysis of existing telemedicine datasets and prospective pilot deployments in partnership with rural healthcare networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source pipeline for federated analysis of telemedicine data across institutions, (2) optimized predictive models for early intervention in chronic disease management, and (3) benchmarking data on computational resource requirements for real-time telemedicine analytics. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation telemedicine platforms, enabling more precise, equitable, and responsive care delivery while establishing computational best practices for privacy-aware health data integration. The requested HPC resources are essential to train large-scale models, simulate multi-institutional federated learning environments, and process high-frequency biosensor streams at clinically relevant scales.
cip_definition: Research on how to bring together technology and clinical medicine to enhance the overall delivery of medical care.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic inventory optimization for vehicle replacement parts across automotive, marine, and aviation sectors, where traditional forecasting models fail to integrate real-time operational data from connected vehicles and IoT-enabled systems. The proliferation of telematics, predictive maintenance alerts, and fluctuating demand patterns—driven by environmental regulations and shifting consumer repair behaviors—creates a need for computational frameworks capable of synthesizing heterogeneous datasets at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this study will develop a multi-agent simulation environment to model decentralized supply chain networks, incorporating live sensor data, regional sales trends, and stochastic demand shocks. Machine learning models (e.g., transformer-based time-series forecasting and graph neural networks) will be trained on historical parts failure rates, customer service interactions, and supplier lead times to predict inventory bottlenecks. The computational workflow will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to assess risk under varying market conditions, while reinforcement learning agents will optimize just-in-time distribution strategies across multimodal logistics hubs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that reduces overstock waste by 15–20% and improves service-level agreements for urgent part deliveries. By bridging IoT analytics with adaptive inventory control, this project aims to establish a scalable framework for data-driven marketing operations in niche vehicle industries, directly enhancing supply chain resilience and customer retention metrics. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling terabyte-scale datasets from OEM telemetry streams and enabling low-latency model retraining in response to emergent market disruptions.
cip_title: Vehicle and Vehicle Parts and Accessories Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of replacement parts and other end-use supplies in the automotive, marine, and aviation industries. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, principles of vehicular technologies, storage and distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: The integration of advanced simulation technologies into health occupations teacher education remains underdeveloped, limiting the ability to prepare instructors for diverse, dynamic vocational training environments. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model and optimize pedagogical strategies specific to health professions education. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct large-scale, agent-based simulations of classroom and clinical training scenarios, incorporating variables such as learner proficiency, instructional methods, and real-time feedback mechanisms. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated and empirical datasets—drawn from existing vocational health education programs—to identify patterns in instructional effectiveness and student skill acquisition. The computational models will enable iterative testing of teaching interventions, predicting their impacts on learner outcomes under varying conditions. Additionally, the project will generate synthetic datasets to augment limited real-world training data, facilitating robust validation of adaptive teaching protocols. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for prototyping evidence-based teaching practices tailored to health occupations, as well as actionable insights into optimizing clinical-pedagogical integration. By enabling data-driven refinement of teacher training curricula, this research aims to enhance the preparedness of health occupations educators, ultimately improving the quality of vocational healthcare training programs. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational complexity of multi-agent simulations and large-scale data analytics, which are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational health occupations programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the evolution of rhetorical strategies in multimodal digital writing. As communication increasingly relies on hybrid texts integrating language, images, hyperlinks, and interactive elements, understanding how writers adapt compositional practices across platforms—from academic blogs to professional social media—remains a critical challenge. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to analyze the scale and complexity of such multimodal corpora, necessitating computational approaches. The research will employ NLP tools and computer vision algorithms to process and annotate a corpus of 50,000+ digital documents (e.g., online articles, multimedia essays, and organizational communication), identifying patterns in rhetorical design, audience engagement, and cross-media citation networks. Machine learning models will classify genre conventions and track shifts in persuasive techniques over time, while network analysis will map how ideas propagate through interconnected digital spaces. By integrating these computational methods, the project aims to model how writers negotiate coherence, credibility, and accessibility in fragmented, multimedia environments. Outcomes will include (1) an open-access dataset of annotated multimodal texts, (2) a framework for computationally assessing rhetorical effectiveness in hybrid genres, and (3) pedagogical tools to help students and professionals navigate digital writing demands. The requested HPC resources are essential for training models on large-scale image-text datasets, running parallelized analyses of document networks, and simulating audience interactions with dynamic content. This work bridges computational humanities and writing studies, offering empirically grounded insights into 21st-century compositional practices while advancing methodologies for interdisciplinary text analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on writing for applied and liberal arts purposes. Includes instruction in writing and document design in multiple genres, modes, and media; writing technologies; research, evaluation, and use of information; editing and publishing; theories and processes of composing; rhetorical theories, traditions, and analysis; communication across audiences, contexts, and cultures; and practical applications for professional, technical, organizational, academic, and public settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in funeral service and mortuary science, specifically addressing the optimization of postmortem logistical processes and environmental impact mitigation. The funeral service industry faces growing challenges in balancing operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and ecological sustainability, particularly in urban environments with limited burial space and evolving public health requirements. Traditional methods for managing interment logistics, embalming chemical dispersion modeling, and cemetery land-use planning remain largely manual or reliant on oversimplified heuristics, resulting in suboptimal resource allocation and environmental strain. This research proposes the development of computational models to simulate mortuary workflows, burial site utilization patterns, and chemical transport in soil systems under varying demographic and climatic scenarios. Agent-based modeling will map multi-stakeholder decision-making processes in funeral home operations, while finite element analysis will quantify groundwater contamination risks from embalming fluids. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical burial records and geographic information system (GIS) data to predict long-term cemetery capacity constraints. The computational intensity of these parallelizable simulations—particularly the three-dimensional hydrogeological modeling and large-scale optimization of burial space allocation—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parameter space exploration and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing funeral service carbon footprints, evidence-based guidelines for sustainable thanatopraxy practices, and open-source frameworks for cemetery spatial planning. By integrating computational science with mortuary science, this work aims to establish quantitative decision-support systems for an industry critical to public health and cultural practices, while creating novel methodologies applicable to other non-traditional HPC domains. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary partnerships with funeral service associations and environmental regulatory bodies.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in funeral service and mortuary science not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in personalized care for women with complex gynecological and obstetric conditions by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multidimensional health data. Women’s health nurses require advanced tools to predict risks, optimize interventions, and tailor pharmacotherapeutic plans, yet existing models often lack the computational power to integrate heterogeneous data sources such as electronic health records, genomic profiles, and longitudinal symptom reports. Our research aims to develop predictive algorithms that identify high-risk pregnancy complications, adverse responses to hormonal therapies, and patterns in chronic pelvic pain management. Using HPC resources, we will apply ensemble machine learning methods to process terabyte-scale datasets, including structured clinical variables, unstructured nursing notes, and imaging-derived biomarkers. Parallelized workflows will enable real-time feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, and validation across diverse demographic subgroups. A key innovation involves simulating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic responses to common obstetric medications under varying physiological conditions using agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include validated risk stratification frameworks and decision support tools that account for sex-specific biological factors, social determinants of health, and nursing-led intervention timelines. These resources will directly inform clinical guidelines for women’s health nurse practitioners, enhance precision in symptom management, and reduce disparities in maternal morbidity. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of multifactorial health trajectories, this work advances nursing science’s capacity to harness big data for evidence-based, patient-centered care paradigms in women’s health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex, multifactorial diseases in food animals and equine populations poses significant challenges to veterinary medicine, agricultural productivity, and food security. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often lack precision due to limited understanding of disease dynamics, host-pathogen interactions, and individual variability in treatment response. This project seeks to address these gaps through the development of multi-scale computational models to predict disease progression, optimize surgical interventions, and evaluate therapeutic efficacy in large animal populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process heterogeneous datasets—including genomic, proteomic, imaging, and herd-level epidemiological data—and to simulate complex biological systems at clinically relevant scales. Computational methods will integrate machine learning algorithms to identify biomarkers associated with disease resistance in livestock, finite element modeling to assess biomechanical stress in equine orthopedic procedures, and agent-based modeling to predict pathogen transmission within herds. These models will be validated against experimental and clinical data from bovine respiratory disease complexes, equine colic cases, and porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome outbreaks. The anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to guide personalized treatment plans, improve surgical outcomes, and inform herd management protocols. By enabling rapid, high-fidelity simulations of disease mechanisms and treatment scenarios, this research will advance evidence-based practices in large animal medicine, reduce economic losses from disease outbreaks, and enhance welfare in food-producing and sport animals. The computational frameworks developed will also serve as adaptable platforms for future studies in veterinary pharmacology, immunology, and precision surgery, fostering innovation in agricultural and veterinary sciences.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Large Animal/ Food Animal and Equine Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of herd, work, sport, and food animals. Includes instruction in equine medicine, swine and dairy medicine, food animal medicine, pathophysiology, large animal diseases, large animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: Healthcare-associated adverse events remain a significant public health challenge, contributing to preventable patient harm and systemic inefficiencies. This project seeks to develop predictive models for identifying latent risks in clinical workflows and evaluating large-scale intervention strategies using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on the limitations of current risk assessment tools, which often fail to account for complex interactions between human factors, organizational dynamics, and evolving care protocols in modern healthcare systems. We propose a multi-modal computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze structured electronic health records (EHRs), unstructured clinical notes, and incident reporting system data from 23 affiliated hospitals (n≈4.1 million encounters). Deep learning architectures will be implemented to model temporal patterns in adverse event trajectories, while natural language processing techniques will extract critical contextual features from clinician narratives. Agent-based modeling simulations will test the theoretical impact of safety interventions across heterogeneous care environments, requiring parallelized computation of >10,000 scenario permutations. The computational workflow demands significant GPU-accelerated processing for training transformer-based models on multi-site EHR data and running real-time sensitivity analyses on intervention parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for anticipating preventable harm events with temporal-spatial granularity, (2) quantitative evidence for optimizing resource allocation in safety initiatives, and (3) open-source tools for simulating care pathway modifications under different risk profiles. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for reducing preventable medical errors through data-driven approaches, with particular significance for health systems managing competing safety and operational demands. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the scale and complexity of multimodal healthcare data while maintaining necessary computational throughput for iterative model development and validation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of transformative mechanisms and evidence-based protocols to reduce preventable patient harm and improve clinical outcomes. Includes instruction in healthcare quality, patient safety, research methods, program evaluation, epidemiology, legal and regulatory compliance, systems thinking, human factors engineering, and risk management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation in community colleges through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate institutional decision-making under dynamic constraints. Community colleges operate in environments marked by fluctuating enrollment, variable funding streams, and evolving workforce demands, yet administrative strategies for resource distribution—such as faculty hiring, program expansion, or infrastructure investment—often rely on static, historical data. This limits responsiveness to real-time needs and disproportionately impacts underserved student populations. The research will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate resource allocation scenarios across interconnected domains, including academic programming, staffing, student support services, and budgetary planning. These models will integrate multi-source datasets (enrollment trends, labor market projections, demographic shifts, and state/federal policy changes) to dynamically represent institutional ecosystems. HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations, enabling the parallel processing of high-dimensional data and stochastic modeling of uncertainty across thousands of iterations. Expected outcomes include a computational framework to predict the downstream effects of resource decisions on student retention, equity metrics, and institutional sustainability. By quantifying trade-offs in scenarios such as reallocating funds to expand high-demand vocational programs or adjusting faculty workloads during enrollment surges, this work will provide actionable insights for administrators. The project aims to advance data-driven leadership practices in community college settings, offering open-source tools to model equity-centered resource strategies and fostering institutional resilience amid demographic and economic volatility.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques of administering community and junior colleges and related postsecondary systems, the study of community and junior colleges as objects of applied research, and that may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in community and junior college finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; student services; research on community and junior colleges; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of multimodal communication patterns in digital media ecosystems. The research addresses a critical gap in communication studies: the lack of scalable, dynamic models to analyze how emergent media technologies—such as algorithmically driven social platforms, immersive storytelling tools, and decentralized communication networks—reshape public discourse, polarization, and collective sensemaking. Traditional methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of contemporary digital communication data, which includes text, audio-visual content, metadata, and user interaction logs spanning terabytes of unstructured information. To overcome these limitations, the project proposes a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate and analyze communication flows across platforms. Key tasks include training domain-specific transformer models for semantic and sentiment analysis of cross-platform discourse, mapping temporal network dynamics of information diffusion, and simulating how algorithmic mediation influences opinion formation. HPC resources are essential to parallelize data preprocessing, optimize deep learning workflows, and run large-scale ABM simulations with millions of agent interactions. Expected outcomes include (1) novel computational methods for analyzing multimodal communication at scale, (2) empirical insights into how platform architectures amplify or mitigate societal divisions, and (3) open-source tools for communication researchers to study digital ecosystems. By bridging computational social science with media effects theories, this work will advance scholarly understanding of 21st-century communication challenges while informing policy debates on platform governance and digital citizenship. The requested resources will enable processing of petascale datasets from platforms like Reddit, YouTube, and Mastodon, which are otherwise computationally prohibitive to analyze holistically.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, and that spans the study of mass communication/media studies, old and new media technologies, social and political applications, and speech communication and rhetoric. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; media social science and criticism; and quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multimodal data in decentralized learning ecosystems presents critical challenges for real-time knowledge integration and decision-making. Traditional frameworks struggle to harmonize heterogeneous data streams—ranging from sensor networks to human behavioral inputs—while preserving privacy, scalability, and interpretability. This project proposes a novel computational architecture leveraging hypergraph-based neural networks and federated learning paradigms to model dynamic, context-aware interactions across distributed systems. The research focuses on optimizing resource-constrained environments, such as rural community networks or IoT-enabled agricultural systems, where latency, bandwidth, and data sovereignty constraints necessitate adaptive, edge-centric solutions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale deployments, train multi-agent reinforcement learning models, and validate the system’s ability to dynamically reallocate computational tasks across nodes under variable load conditions. Key innovations include a hybrid topology for intermittent connectivity, differential privacy mechanisms tailored for sparse temporal data, and entropy-driven prioritization of data flows. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for decentralized, ethical AI deployment in resource-limited settings, with applications in participatory environmental monitoring and crisis response coordination. The computational experiments will benchmark performance against existing edge-computing architectures using synthetic and real-world datasets from partner NGOs operating in off-grid regions. By addressing the intersection of distributed systems, ethical AI, and socio-technical resilience, this work aims to advance foundational methodologies for equitable information infrastructure while contributing actionable insights to the emergent field of community-centric computing.
cip_title: Computer and Information Sciences and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer and information sciences and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of medical imaging data and the demand for precision in clinical and educational visualization tools present significant computational challenges in medical illustration and informatics. Current workflows for processing high-resolution 3D anatomical models, dynamic simulations of physiological processes, and AI-driven diagnostic support systems are constrained by the limitations of standard computing infrastructure. These bottlenecks hinder the development of scalable, interactive platforms capable of integrating multimodal datasets (e.g., MRI, CT, and histopathology) in real time. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these limitations by enabling advanced computational workflows for large-scale medical data analysis, simulation, and visualization. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) developing GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines to automate the segmentation and annotation of complex anatomical structures across heterogeneous imaging datasets, and (2) deploying distributed computing frameworks to simulate biomechanical processes, such as blood flow dynamics or tissue deformation, within interactive 3D environments. Computational methods will include deep neural networks (e.g., transformer-based architectures for cross-modal data fusion) and finite element modeling optimized for parallel processing. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as rendering 4D surgical simulations or training generative models on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time collaborative annotation of medical images, enhanced predictive models for pathological classification, and immersive visualization modules for medical education. These advancements will directly support clinical decision-making, surgical planning, and interdisciplinary training programs, bridging gaps between data science and healthcare practice. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish a scalable infrastructure for next-generation medical illustration and informatics applications, fostering innovation in personalized medicine and translational research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in medical illustration and informatics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and promotional strategies for perishable and seasonal special products (e.g., artisanal foods, floral arrangements) using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex market interactions. The challenge lies in balancing real-time demand fluctuations, supply chain constraints, and profit margins for niche products with short shelf lives and highly variable consumer appeal. Traditional marketing models struggle to account for the nonlinear relationships between social media-driven demand spikes, localized inventory thresholds, and time-sensitive pricing adjustments. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based computational framework integrating real-time social sentiment analysis, supply chain telemetry, and consumer behavior simulations. The model will leverage GPU-accelerated machine learning to predict regional demand patterns from heterogeneous data streams (e.g., Instagram engagement metrics, weather data, local event calendars) while simultaneously optimizing pricing tiers and promotion schedules through Monte Carlo methods. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations across thousands of hypothetical market scenarios, enabling rapid sensitivity analysis for parameters like flash sale timing or influencer partnership ROI. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that reduces perishable product waste by 18-25% while maintaining premium pricing integrity, alongside novel metrics for quantifying the viral potential of visual-centric special products. This work bridges computational social science and operations research, advancing marketing analytics for small-batch producers in underserved sectors. By mapping how micro-influencer networks spatially propagate demand signals, the project will also yield methodological innovations in simulating decentralized marketing ecosystems—a critical capability as special product markets increasingly rely on hyper-localized, community-driven promotion strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of special products, including floristry, food, and home and office products. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: Pediatric critical care medicine faces significant challenges in predicting and managing life-threatening organ failure in children, where rapid clinical deterioration demands precise, individualized interventions. Current approaches rely on generalized protocols that may not account for dynamic physiological complexity, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating multimodal patient data—including high-resolution vital signs, laboratory results, imaging, and genomic markers—to model real-time risk stratification and optimize therapeutic strategies. The research problem centers on overcoming computational barriers to analyzing heterogeneous, time-sensitive datasets at scale, which is critical for advancing precision medicine in this vulnerable population. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on retrospective datasets from 5,000+ pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, capturing nonlinear interactions between organ systems during critical illness. Agent-based modeling will simulate responses to interventions under diverse physiological scenarios, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in treatment effect predictions. A novel multiscale computational architecture will link molecular pathways to systemic hemodynamics, enabling in silico testing of resuscitation protocols. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for acute respiratory distress syndrome progression and septic shock trajectories, which will be prospectively tested in a pilot clinical decision-support system. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to uncover previously intractable patterns in critical care data, reduce latency in clinical decision-making, and establish a foundation for adaptive, patient-specific care pathways. The computational infrastructure will also support open-source tool development for pediatric physiological signal processing, benefiting the broader critical care research community. Successful implementation could transform management of life-threatening pediatric illness by bridging the gap between complex pathophysiology and actionable clinical insights.
cip_definition: Research focused on advanced life support for children, from the term or near-term neonate to the adolescent. This includes critical care management of life-threatening organ system failure in both medical and surgical patients and support of vital physiological functions.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic inventory allocation and warehouse operational workflows, driven by the increasing complexity of real-time demand signals, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability constraints. Traditional inventory management models struggle to optimize spatial resource utilization, workforce routing, and multi-echelon replenishment under stochastic conditions, particularly in large-scale warehousing systems with heterogeneous parts and perishable stock. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity simulations of warehouse operations with reinforcement learning (RL) and agent-based modeling (ABM). The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize millions of scenario iterations, capturing variables such as fluctuating order volumes, robotic picker coordination, and energy consumption patterns. Key computational tasks include training multi-agent RL frameworks to minimize idle time in automated storage/retrieval systems (AS/RS), optimizing 3D bin-packing heuristics for irregularly shaped parts, and simulating emergent behaviors in human-robot collaborative workflows. The models will ingest real-world IoT data streams from warehouse sensors to refine decision policies. Expected outcomes include adaptive inventory stratification strategies to reduce carrying costs by 12–18%, dynamic zoning protocols to improve order fulfillment rates, and a scalable digital twin platform for evaluating circular economy interventions (e.g., reusable packaging integration). By bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and computational logistics, this work aims to establish a paradigm for resilient, data-driven warehousing systems that balance efficiency with environmental and social governance (ESG) metrics. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling the non-linear combinatorial complexity of these interdependent optimization problems at enterprise-grade operational scales.
cip_title: Parts, Warehousing, and Inventory Management Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide administrative, technical, and managerial support in the operation of warehouses, control of inventory, parts identification, and the performance of counter services for customers. Includes instruction in record-keeping, equipment operation, database entry, supply logistics, shop operations and math, and customer and supplier relations.

abstract: Occupational and environmental health nursing faces critical challenges in understanding complex, multifactorial relationships between workplace exposures, environmental risks, and long-term health outcomes. Current approaches often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture nonlinear interactions, temporal patterns, or population-scale variability. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing predictive computational models to assess cumulative health risks in workers exposed to dynamic combinations of chemical, physical, and psychosocial stressors. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale occupational health datasets spanning electronic health records, industrial hygiene monitoring data, environmental sensor networks, and longitudinal cohort studies. Machine learning architectures, including ensemble models and graph neural networks, will be trained to identify risk signatures for respiratory, musculoskeletal, and stress-related disorders across diverse worker populations. Computational workflows will integrate geospatial analysis of environmental exposure patterns with individual-level biometric data to optimize intervention strategies. The scale of data integration—projected to exceed 50 million worker-hours of exposure records and 200,000 health outcomes—necessitates parallelized processing and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models quantifying dose-response relationships for understudied exposure combinations, (2) decision support tools for nurse-led workplace surveillance programs, and (3) simulation frameworks to evaluate prevention strategies under varying occupational scenarios. By enabling analysis at unprecedented resolution, this research will directly inform clinical guidelines for exposure monitoring, worker fitness-for-duty assessments, and early intervention protocols. The requested computing resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale epidemiological simulations, and secure processing of sensitive health data in compliance with HIPAA standards. This work bridges computational innovation with frontline occupational health practice, advancing evidence-based nursing interventions in complex work environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver nursing health care services to workers and worker populations in clinical settings and at job sites. Includes instruction in public and community health, occupational safety and health, occupational health surveillance, case management, fitness for duty testing, medication, allergies and immunization, emergency and ambulatory care, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance technical vocational education (TVET) by developing data-driven frameworks to optimize instructional design for complex, skills-based disciplines such as advanced manufacturing, renewable energy systems, and industrial automation. A critical challenge in technical teacher education is the lack of scalable, evidence-based methods to model how learners acquire hands-on competencies in dynamic, high-stakes environments. Traditional approaches often rely on subjective assessments or oversimplified simulations, limiting their ability to inform adaptive teaching strategies. To address this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal educational datasets—including biometric sensor data, equipment telemetry from training simulations, and longitudinal performance metrics—to identify patterns in skill acquisition. Machine learning models (e.g., transformer-based architectures for temporal data, graph neural networks for procedural knowledge mapping) will be trained to predict learner trajectories and simulate the efficacy of alternative pedagogical interventions under diverse scenarios. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of time-series data from simulated welding, CNC machining, and mechatronics tasks, requiring parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated inference. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to guide instructors in personalizing technical skill development, (2) generative models for creating context-aware training simulations, and (3) open-source tools to help educators interpret complex learner analytics. By elucidating the relationship between instructional design variables and competency outcomes, this work aims to establish scalable computational methods for improving technical teacher preparation, directly supporting workforce development in high-demand STEM-vocational fields. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project’s data volume, real-time simulation requirements, and iterative model training processes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational technical education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociotechnical dynamics of urban energy transitions, focusing on how algorithmic decision-making in smart grid systems interacts with community-level equity and policy outcomes. As cities adopt AI-driven energy management platforms to optimize renewable integration, these tools risk perpetuating biases in resource allocation—prioritizing efficiency over accessibility. The research problem centers on quantifying the feedback loops between computational optimization, energy justice, and policy formulation in heterogeneous urban landscapes. Using a mixed-methods approach, we will develop agent-based models simulating energy demand patterns across socioeconomic strata, coupled with natural language processing analysis of municipal policy documents. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the multiscale nature of the simulations, which integrate real-time sensor data from urban infrastructure with synthetic populations reflecting demographic diversity. The computational framework will employ graph neural networks to model grid resilience under different policy scenarios while maintaining interpretability for stakeholder engagement. Expected outcomes include a novel metric for algorithmic equity in energy systems and an open-source toolkit that enables policymakers to assess how technical constraints in smart grid architectures might disproportionately impact marginalized communities. By bridging computational engineering with critical policy studies, this work aims to establish new methodologies for evaluating the societal embeddedness of urban technologies, particularly how optimization algorithms become de facto policy actors. The requested computing resources will enable sensitivity analyses across multiple cities’ datasets while preserving privacy through federated learning techniques. This interdisciplinary approach advances understanding of how computational systems shape—and are shaped by—societal values in the clean energy transition, offering pathways to align technical infrastructure development with principles of distributive justice.
detailed_field: History/ philosophy of science, technology, and society
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the contemporary social and public policy ramifications of science and technology, the interrelationship of science and engineering with the public policy process, and the social and ethical dimensions of scientific and technological enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of enhancing pedagogical effectiveness in Latin language instruction by developing a data-driven, adaptive learning platform tailored for pre-service Latin teachers. Despite Latin’s structural complexity and its role in fostering critical linguistic and cultural competencies, current teacher training often relies on static curricula and limited personalized feedback mechanisms. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design and train machine learning models that dynamically analyze learner interactions, predict areas of student difficulty, and generate real-time instructional recommendations for teacher candidates. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to parse and evaluate Latin syntax, morphology, and translation exercises submitted by simulated K–12 students, alongside reinforcement learning algorithms to model adaptive teaching strategies. By processing large-scale datasets of historical student performance metrics and annotated classical texts, the platform will simulate diverse classroom scenarios, enabling teacher candidates to refine their instructional techniques in a risk-free virtual environment. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling these simulations, optimizing model accuracy through iterative training, and supporting concurrent user interactions during pilot testing. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for personalized Latin teacher training, open-access datasets of annotated pedagogical interactions, and evidence-based insights into optimizing metacognitive feedback in second-language acquisition. This work directly aligns with the program’s mission to advance innovative, scalable tools for Latin education, ultimately contributing to improved student outcomes in classical language programs and fostering equitable access to high-quality Latin instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach Latin at various grade levels.

abstract: Pediatric populations exhibit dynamic physiological and developmental changes that significantly influence drug pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD), yet clinical dosing guidelines often rely on extrapolation from adult studies or limited pediatric data. This project seeks to address the critical gap in precision dosing strategies for high-risk medications in neonates, infants, and children by developing a computational framework to predict age- and development-specific drug responses. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-scale data, including electronic health records, genomic datasets, and physiological parameters, into mechanistic PK/PD models. A key challenge is the computational burden of parameter optimization across heterogeneous pediatric subgroups and the simulation of virtual patient cohorts that reflect inter-individual variability in organ maturation, body composition, and pharmacogenomic factors. The proposed approach combines nonlinear mixed-effects modeling, Bayesian machine learning, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to quantify developmental trajectories of drug metabolism and response. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of parameter estimation tasks, Monte Carlo uncertainty analyses, and sensitivity testing across maturational age bins. Expected outcomes include validated models for 3-5 high-risk medications (e.g., anticoagulants, antiepileptics) that are frequently associated with adverse drug events in pediatric care. These models will inform dose individualization algorithms based on patient-specific covariates such as gestational age, enzyme ontogeny, and genetic polymorphisms. The project aims to advance evidence-based pediatric pharmacotherapy by replacing current one-dose-fits-all approaches with computational tools that dynamically adapt to developmental physiology. Successful implementation will directly support ongoing clinical trials at our institution while generating open-access models to accelerate pediatric drug development. The scale of data integration and the need for real-time simulation of thousands of virtual patients necessitate robust HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically actionable results within project timelines.
cip_definition: Research focused on pediatric pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in post-harvest handling of perishable crops, a major contributor to global food loss, by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize storage and transport conditions for fruits and vegetables. Current empirical models fail to capture the complex interplay between produce physiology, environmental factors, and logistical constraints, particularly under variable climate scenarios. We propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), discrete element modeling (DEM), and machine learning to simulate multi-scale interactions within post-harvest systems—from cellular-level moisture transport in individual produce items to bulk airflow dynamics in stacked storage containers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these coupled phenomena across temporal and spatial scales, including parallelized simulations of heterogeneous produce loads under dynamic external conditions (e.g., fluctuating temperatures during transport). The framework will incorporate real-world sensor data from IoT-enabled storage facilities to train neural networks predicting spoilage risk, enabling adaptive control strategies. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of identifying optimal ventilation configurations, stacking patterns, and cooling schedules for diverse crop types, with preliminary simulations targeting reductions in post-harvest losses by 15-30% for citrus and leafy greens. By bridging gaps between agricultural systems engineering, biophysics, and data science, this work aims to establish scalable computational tools for sustainable food supply chains while advancing methodologies for hyper-resolution modeling of biological transport processes. The requested resources will support large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and validation against experimental datasets from collaborating food distribution networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems, equipment and facilities for production, processing, storage, handling, distribution and use of food, feed, and fiber. Includes applications to aquaculture, forestry, human and natural resources.

abstract: Fermentation processes are central to the production of diverse food products, yet optimizing microbial consortia for consistent quality, efficiency, and scalability remains a critical challenge in industrial applications. This project seeks to address gaps in predictive modeling of microbial community dynamics during food fermentation, with a focus on strain interactions, metabolic flux variability, and environmental parameter optimization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to develop multi-omics integration pipelines and agent-based models to simulate microbial ecosystems under variable fermentation conditions (e.g., temperature, pH, substrate gradients). Metagenomic data from experimental fermentations (yogurt, kimchi, and sourdough) will inform genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of key lactic acid bacteria and yeast species, while machine learning algorithms will identify metabolic bottlenecks and predict community stability thresholds. Computational workflows will include parallelized flux balance analysis, dynamic Bayesian network inference, and stochastic optimization of growth parameters across hyperscale combinatorial design spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for in silico strain selection, nutrient supplementation strategies, and process parameter tuning to minimize batch failures and off-target metabolite accumulation. By bridging gaps between lab-scale experiments and industrial-scale fermentation, this research will advance precision control in food biotechnology, reduce resource waste, and support the development of novel fermented products with enhanced nutritional or sensory profiles. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of simulating thousands of microbial interactions across multi-dimensional parameter sets, enabling real-time analytics that traditional bench methods cannot achieve. This project aligns with broader agricultural science goals by enhancing food production efficiency and safety through data-driven microbial management.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of fermented food production. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: The dynamic behavior of polymers under nanoscale confinement remains a critical unresolved challenge in polymer physics, with implications for designing advanced coatings, sensors, and energy storage systems. While experimental studies have revealed anomalous relaxation and diffusion phenomena in confined polymers, the molecular-scale mechanisms driving these behaviors—particularly the interplay of entropic constraints, interfacial interactions, and chain topology—are poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap through large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the nonequilibrium dynamics of entangled polymer melts and networks under spatially varying confinement geometries. The proposed computational approach employs coarse-grained bead-spring models with tunable surface interactions to systematically investigate how confinement length scales (1–100 nm) and interfacial adhesion energies alter chain mobility, stress relaxation spectra, and glass transition behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the broad range of timescales (ns–ms) and length scales (angstroms to micrometers) inherent to these systems, particularly for simulating experimentally relevant film thicknesses and high-molecular-weight polymers. Parallelized MD simulations will leverage optimized force-field kernels and hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to achieve the required computational throughput. Expected outcomes include predictive relationships between confinement parameters, entanglement dynamics, and viscoelastic response, offering fundamental insights into how nanoscale interfaces modulate polymer physics. These results will directly inform the design of polymer-based nanocomposites for flexible electronics and solid-state battery electrolytes, where confined polymer phases govern ion transport and mechanical stability. By elucidating universal scaling laws for confined polymer dynamics, this work will advance the physics of nonequilibrium soft matter systems while providing actionable guidelines for next-generation nanomaterials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis, structure and properties of polymers. Includes instruction in nanomaterials, biomaterials, sensors, chemistry, physics, mathematics, biochemistry, electronic and photonic polymers, polymers for energy generation and storage, coatings, structure and function of polymers, and polymer blends.

abstract: The increasing demand for advanced materials in photonics, molecular electronics, and sensor technologies necessitates the development of semiconductor nanowires with tailored electronic and optical properties. A critical challenge lies in understanding how structural defects, interfacial strain, and dopant distributions influence charge transport and excitonic behavior in these systems. Experimental characterization alone struggles to resolve atomic-scale mechanisms, particularly under dynamic operational conditions. This project seeks to address this gap through multiscale computational modeling of III-V semiconductor nanowires (e.g., InP, GaAs) and hybrid organic-inorganic interfaces relevant to light-harvesting and sensing applications. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale density functional theory (DFT) calculations to map defect formation energies, band structure modifications, and charge localization effects at strained heterojunctions. Molecular dynamics simulations parameterized by machine learning interatomic potentials will model thermal and mechanical stability during nanowire synthesis and device operation. These atomistic insights will inform mesoscale kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of electron transport under applied bias, explicitly incorporating defect-mediated scattering processes. The computational workflow will integrate the Quantum ESPRESSO, LAMMPS, and custom transport codes, requiring parallelized execution across thousands of cores to manage system sizes exceeding 10^4 atoms and microsecond-scale dynamics. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking synthesis parameters to nanowire performance metrics, such as carrier mobility and defect tolerance, which will guide experimental collaborators in optimizing vapor-liquid-solid growth conditions. The results will advance the rational design of nanowire-based photodetectors and molecular-scale sensors while establishing computational frameworks for accelerating materials discovery in nanochemistry. This work directly aligns with national priorities in energy-efficient electronics and responsive sensor arrays, with potential applications in medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis and study of organic or inorganic materials and their electronic, magnetic, optical or mechanical properties. Includes instruction in advanced materials for photonics, lasers, chemical sensors and arrays or nanochemistry; semiconductor nanowires; and molecular electronics.

abstract: This research proposes the development of a predictive computational framework to optimize emergency medical decision-making during prehospital ambulance transport, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation and real-time clinical deterioration prediction. Emergency Care Attendants (ECAs) face critical challenges in balancing time-sensitive interventions, patient stabilization, and transport logistics under resource-constrained conditions. Current protocols rely on static triage guidelines that do not account for multivariate factors such as fluctuating patient vitals, traffic patterns, or competing hospital capacities. To address this gap, we will implement a machine learning-driven simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between patient physiology, environmental variables, and operational constraints. The computational approach integrates three components: 1) agent-based modeling of ambulance workflows using historical dispatch records and telemetry data, 2) temporal convolutional neural networks trained on multimodal biosignal data (ECG, SpO2, etCO2) to predict acute deterioration risks, and 3) reinforcement learning algorithms for adaptive routing optimization incorporating real-time traffic APIs and hospital status feeds. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel execution of Monte Carlo simulations across diverse emergency scenarios (trauma, cardiac events, pediatric crises) while processing high-frequency physiological streams at scale. Expected outcomes include a validated decision support system prototype capable of recommending prioritized interventions, optimal destination selection, and resource pre-notification strategies. This work aims to establish computational evidence for next-generation EMS protocols that reduce preventable morbidity through data-driven situational awareness, directly addressing the understudied intersection of prehospital informatics, operational research, and critical care physiology. Successful implementation could transform emergency medical logistics in heterogeneous urban-rural environments while maintaining compliance with ECA scope-of-practice regulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist licensed EMTs, under the supervision of a physician, to prepare and transport ill or injured patients, and to operate emergency vehicles and equipment such as life support units. Includes instruction in first aid and emergency medicine field techniques, patient stabilization and care, medical field communications, equipment operation and maintenance, emergency vehicle operation, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Agricultural systems face escalating challenges due to climate variability, pest pressures, and the demand for sustainable intensification. This project addresses the critical need to optimize crop resilience and productivity by integrating genomic, environmental, and agronomic data into predictive models. Current limitations in processing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including high-throughput phenotyping, soil health metrics, and climate projections—hinder the development of actionable insights for precision agriculture. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning frameworks and genomic prediction models that identify genetic markers associated with stress tolerance and yield stability in staple crops. Computational workflows will process multi-terabyte datasets, combining convolutional neural networks for hyperspectral image analysis of plant traits with Bayesian algorithms for genotype-environment association studies. These models will simulate crop performance under diverse climatic scenarios, enabling the design of region-specific breeding strategies and management practices. The project’s outcomes will provide scalable tools for farmers to adopt climate-resilient cultivars and optimize input use, reducing economic and environmental risks. By enabling rapid analysis of complex interactions between crop genetics and environmental variables, HPC resources will accelerate the translation of research into public agricultural services, such as decision-support systems and extension programs. This work bridges gaps between computational agronomy and on-farm applications, directly supporting food security and sustainable agricultural practices in vulnerable regions. The proposed computational pipelines will be disseminated as open-source resources, fostering collaboration across agricultural research communities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general agricultural sciences and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research addresses the critical challenge of understanding how prolonged exposure to microgravity and radiation during spaceflight drives physiological deconditioning in astronauts, particularly focusing on musculoskeletal atrophy, cardiovascular dysfunction, and cancer risk modulation.
