While prior studies have characterized systemic responses to space environments, the integrative mechanisms linking cellular hypoxia, fluid redistribution, and radiation-induced genomic instability remain poorly quantified. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale physiological models that bridge molecular, tissue, and organ-level adaptations. A three-tiered computational framework will be implemented: (1) Finite element modeling of hemodynamic shifts and cerebrovascular autoregulation in simulated microgravity, informed by astronaut cardiovascular telemetry; (2) Agent-based simulations of muscle fiber remodeling under chronic mechanical unloading, integrating proteomic data on myokine signaling pathways; and (3) Monte Carlo simulations of cosmic radiation interactions with bone marrow microenvironments to assess leukemogenic potential. The HPC environment is essential for resolving spatiotemporal complexities across these scales, requiring parallelized execution of coupled differential equations modeling pressure-volume dynamics (10⁶-node vascular networks) and stochastic radiation damage events (10¹²-particle histories). Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for early detection of spaceflight-induced pathologies and optimized countermeasure protocols targeting mechanotransduction pathways. By elucidating cross-system vulnerabilities in aerospace physiology, this work will directly inform NASA’s Artemis program crew health standards and advance terrestrial oncology research through novel insights into hypoxia-mediated cancer progression. The requested computational allocation will enable unprecedented resolution in simulating human physiological resilience at the intersection of gravitational biology and environmental carcinogenesis.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in low and high-altitude flight and living in space and related low-pressure and low-gravity environments, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in anatomy, molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction, fuel utilization, neurophysiology of motor mechanics, systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others), fatigue and exhaustion, systemic environmental pathologies, muscle and body training, physiology of specific exercises and activities, physiology of injury, and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize procurement decision-making under uncertainty, with a focus on large-scale contract management and supplier risk assessment. Modern procurement systems must balance cost efficiency, regulatory compliance, sustainability goals, and supply chain disruptions, yet existing analytical tools often fail to integrate real-time market data, multi-tier supplier dependencies, and dynamic risk variables at enterprise scales. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex procurement networks using agent-based simulations, machine learning-driven supplier performance forecasting, and Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic risk analysis. Key computational challenges include processing heterogeneous datasets (contract terms, vendor histories, geopolitical indicators), training ensemble models to predict supply chain bottlenecks, and optimizing multi-objective procurement strategies across thousands of simulated scenarios. The HPC environment will enable parallelized execution of optimization algorithms such as genetic algorithms and integer programming to evaluate bid structures, inventory buffers, and contingency clauses under stochastic demand conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario-based contract negotiation support, quantitative metrics for supplier resilience scoring, and policy insights for automated compliance auditing in government contracting. By scaling analyses to global supply chain levels while preserving contract-specific legal and financial constraints, this work aims to advance data-driven procurement practices that reduce operational risks and adaptive costs in volatile markets. The computational infrastructure will also support benchmarking of sustainable procurement strategies through lifecycle assessment integrations, addressing critical gaps in environmental impact forecasting for acquisition workflows.
cip_title: Purchasing, Procurement/ Acquisitions and Contracts Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and/or administer the processes by which a firm or organization contracts for goods and services to support its operations, as well as contracts it to sell to other firms or organizations. Includes instruction in contract law, negotiations, buying procedures, government contracting, cost and price analysis, vendor relations, contract administration, auditing and inspection, relations with other firm departments, and applications to special areas such as high-technology systems, international purchasing, and construction.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, distributed engineering systems under uncertainty, leveraging advances in hybrid simulation and machine learning. Traditional resource allocation models in engineering management often rely on static, deterministic assumptions, leading to inefficiencies when applied to complex, adaptive systems such as smart manufacturing networks or decentralized energy grids. The research problem centers on addressing the computational limitations of existing optimization methods, which struggle to integrate real-time operational data, stochastic demand patterns, and multi-stakeholder decision-making processes. To overcome these challenges, the project proposes a two-stage approach: First, a high-fidelity agent-based simulation model will be constructed to emulate resource flows and decision pathways in distributed engineering systems. Second, a reinforcement learning architecture will be trained on this digital twin environment to derive adaptive allocation policies that balance efficiency, equity, and resilience metrics. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing resources due to the need for parallel execution of thousands of stochastic simulation scenarios, coupled with the memory-intensive nature of training deep neural networks on high-dimensional state-action spaces. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for real-time resource negotiation in engineering systems, validated through case studies on semiconductor supply chain resilience and hospital infrastructure management during demand surges. The results will advance engineering management practice by providing data-driven strategies for mitigating systemic risks in interconnected critical infrastructure networks while maintaining operational flexibility. This work bridges gaps between discrete-event simulation, decentralized optimization, and systems engineering, offering methodological contributions applicable to emerging challenges in public-private infrastructure partnerships and circular economy transitions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of management and administration principles to engineering systems and applications. Includes instruction in resource allocation theory, control theory, statistical analysis, business management and administration, and applications to specific engineering research problems.

abstract: Chronic pain disorders present a complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors, complicating diagnosis and treatment personalization. Current clinical approaches often rely on trial-and-error strategies due to insufficient understanding of pain mechanisms and heterogeneous patient responses. This project aims to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal clinical data, including neuroimaging, genomic profiles, electronic health records, and real-time sensor data from wearable devices. We propose developing machine learning models to identify biomarkers predictive of pain subtypes and treatment outcomes. Computational workflows will integrate unsupervised clustering for patient stratification, deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer networks) to process longitudinal pain reports, and genome-wide association studies coupled with functional genomic annotation to pinpoint pain-related pathways. A key innovation involves simulating neural circuit dynamics using biophysically detailed models to explore how peripheral and central sensitization mechanisms contribute to chronic pain states. These simulations will require large-scale parallel processing to iteratively test hypotheses across parameter spaces representing genetic, molecular, and clinical variables. The project will also employ federated learning frameworks to securely aggregate data from multiple institutions, preserving privacy while enhancing model generalizability. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for optimizing non-opioid pharmacotherapy, neuromodulation protocols, and behavioral interventions. By elucidating subtype-specific pain pathways, this work could reduce reliance on high-risk therapies and improve functional outcomes for diverse populations. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to advance reproducible pain research. Access to HPC resources is essential given the project’s scale, involving petabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive analyses that exceed the capacity of local clinical servers.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of the entire range of painful disorders, either as a primary physician or consultant, for patients experiencing problems with acute, chronic, and/or cancer pain in both hospital and ambulatory settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing technology-driven entrepreneurship, with a focus on algorithmic accountability, decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs), and cross-jurisdictional compliance challenges. The rapid proliferation of emerging technologies such as blockchain, generative AI, and decentralized finance has created novel legal ambiguities that traditional statutory interpretation methods struggle to address systematically. This study proposes a computational legal analytics approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis to map precedent patterns across 10 million pages of case law, administrative rulings, and international regulatory guidance. Custom transformer models will be trained to identify latent policy priorities in judicial decisions affecting startup liability, while graph neural networks will model the cascading effects of regulatory changes on innovation ecosystems. The computational workload requires parallelized processing of heterogeneous legal texts across multiple jurisdictions, necessitating GPU-accelerated clusters for transformer model training and high-memory nodes for large-scale network simulations. Expected outcomes include a dynamic visualization platform tracking regulatory risk exposure for entrepreneurial ventures and a predictive framework quantifying how hypothetical policy interventions might influence innovation rates in specific technology sectors. By bridging legal hermeneutics with computational social science methods, this project aims to establish an evidence-based paradigm for evaluating entrepreneurship law's impact on economic ecosystems while maintaining compliance with ethical AI governance standards. The resulting tools could inform legislative reforms and help startups navigate complex compliance landscapes without stifling technological experimentation.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting entrepreneurship and innovation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of global financial networks, driven by interconnected markets, decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems, and heterogeneous data streams, poses significant challenges for systemic risk assessment. Traditional models often fail to capture nonlinear dependencies, temporal volatility, and cross-domain interactions at scale. This project proposes an interdisciplinary framework integrating multilayer network theory, dynamic Bayesian inference, and adaptive machine learning to model systemic risk propagation across asset classes, geopolitical events, and emerging digital financial infrastructures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process petabytes of structured and unstructured financial data—including transaction records, sentiment signals from alternative text sources, and real-time blockchain metrics—to construct a time-evolving risk topology. Computational challenges include solving stochastic partial differential equations for contagion dynamics, training graph neural networks (GNNs) on temporal heterogeneous graphs, and optimizing ensemble models for scenario forecasting under uncertainty. The HPC environment is critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across 10,000+ synthetic market shock scenarios, enabling GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition of high-dimensional financial time series, and maintaining low-latency pipelines for real-time data assimilation. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for multilayer financial network analysis, (2) predictive early-warning indicators for cascading failures in hybrid (traditional/DeFi) systems, and (3) empirically validated stress-testing protocols that incorporate climate-related financial disclosures and geopolitical risk factors. This work bridges gaps between financial mathematics, computational social science, and climate economics, offering regulators and institutions a computationally robust platform to navigate systemic vulnerabilities in an era of escalating interdisciplinary financial risks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on financial big data modeling from algorithms to cloud-based data-driven financial technologies. Includes instruction in financial analytics, financial data processing, knowledge management, data visualization, effective decision communication, machine learning for finance, statistical inference and dynamic modeling on financial data, and project management.

abstract: Sheet metal forming processes are integral to manufacturing industries, yet optimizing these techniques for complex geometries and advanced materials remains a significant challenge. Traditional trial-and-error methods for determining optimal parameters—such as punch force, die clearance, and annealing conditions—are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to predict material behavior under extreme deformation. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop high-fidelity computational models that simulate multi-stage sheet metal forming processes, including bending, deep drawing, and hydroforming. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) modeling the anisotropic plasticity and fracture behavior of lightweight alloys (e.g., aluminum, titanium) under dynamic strain rates and temperature gradients, and (2) identifying process parameters that minimize defects such as springback, wrinkling, and tearing. A hybrid computational approach will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) using ABAQUS/Explicit with machine learning algorithms to iteratively refine predictive models. High-resolution simulations will account for microstructure evolution, contact friction, and tool-workpiece interactions, requiring parallel computing capabilities to handle meshes with >10 million elements and nonlinear material constitutive equations. Validation will utilize experimental data from industrial partners, including strain measurements via digital image correlation and post-forming microstructure characterization. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable framework for virtual process design, reducing physical prototyping by 40–60%, and a publicly accessible database of simulated forming limits for novel alloy grades. By enabling rapid optimization of energy-efficient forming pathways, this work aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices in aerospace and automotive sectors while providing pedagogical resources for sheet metal technology education. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary computational scale and resolution, as local workstations lack the capacity to resolve the coupled thermomechanical phenomena inherent to industrial-scale sheetworking operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to form, shape, bend and fold extruded metals, including the creation of new products, using hand tools and machines such as cornice brakes, forming rolls, and squaring shears.

abstract: Forensic social work practice increasingly relies on the analysis of complex, multidimensional datasets to address systemic challenges in criminal justice, mental health, and victim advocacy systems. However, existing computational tools are inadequate for modeling the interplay between individual risk factors (e.g., substance use, trauma history), institutional policies, and community-level variables at scale. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate predictive models that optimize intervention strategies for justice-involved populations with co-occurring mental health needs. The research will integrate anonymized administrative data from courts, hospitals, and social service agencies—spanning 10+ years and millions of records—to examine patterns in treatment adherence, recidivism, and service gaps. Computational workflows will employ machine learning techniques (ensemble classifiers, survival analysis) to identify high-risk subgroups and simulate the longitudinal impacts of hypothetical policy changes. Natural language processing will be applied to unstructured clinical notes and court documents to augment traditional structured data analysis. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling to test how resource allocation strategies affect outcomes across urban and rural service ecosystems with varying infrastructure. The project will establish secure data pipelines compliant with HIPAA and criminal justice privacy standards, leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized model training. Expected outcomes include a decision-support framework to guide forensic social workers in matching clients to evidence-based interventions, predictive tools for jurisdictions to anticipate treatment capacity needs, and policy briefs quantifying the cost-benefit ratios of early diversion programs. By bridging computational social science and frontline practice, this work aims to reduce systemic inefficiencies in cross-sector case management while advancing methodological paradigms for equity-focused forensic research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as social workers in correctional facilities, mental health hospitals, the justice system, substance abuse treatment programs, and victim assistance. Includes instruction in forensic social work, criminal justice administration, domestic violence, ethics, juvenile justice systems, mental illness and crime, program evaluation, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance risk assessment and counseling strategies for genetic disorders by leveraging large-scale genomic and phenotypic datasets. Genetic counseling faces a critical challenge in efficiently translating complex genomic data into actionable clinical insights, particularly for rare or multifactorial conditions with poorly characterized risk profiles. Current variant interpretation pipelines lack scalability and often fail to integrate dynamic patient-specific factors, such as family history, environmental exposures, and epigenomic modifiers. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining machine learning (ML) models, population genetics simulations, and natural language processing (NLP) of electronic health records (EHRs). The computational workflow will train ensemble ML classifiers on multi-omic datasets from public repositories (e.g., gnomAD, ClinVar) and institutional biobanks to prioritize pathogenic variants while accounting for pleiotropic effects. Parallelized coalescent simulations will model disease allele frequencies across diverse ancestries to improve risk prediction equity. NLP algorithms will automate extraction of phenotypic descriptors from unstructured clinical notes to enrich genotype-phenotype correlations. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing terabyte-scale genomic data, enabling rapid hyperparameter optimization of ML architectures, and conducting millions of stochastic simulations to quantify uncertainty in risk estimates. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for generating probabilistic risk reports that integrate molecular, demographic, and clinical data, reducing turnaround time for complex cases by ≥40%. This resource will directly support genetic counselors in delivering personalized risk communication, optimizing testing strategies, and addressing disparities in access to precision medicine. By coupling scalable computation with clinical expertise, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven counseling that bridges genomic discovery and patient care, while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for data privacy and algorithmic bias mitigation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel patients and families concerning inherited genetic disorders and diseases; assess risk factors and planning options associated with potential and actual inherited conditions; and serve as patient advocates and provide referral services in relation to private and public support services. Includes instruction in clinical/medical genetics, methods of genetic testing, interviewing and counseling skills, genetic and support services delivery, principles of public health, medical ethics, law and regulations, patient advocacy, and professional standards.

abstract: Women’s health research faces critical gaps in understanding sex-specific physiological mechanisms and their implications for disease susceptibility, progression, and treatment outcomes. A significant challenge lies in integrating large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including genomic, proteomic, hormonal, and clinical data—to uncover biomarkers and therapeutic targets for conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), gestational diabetes, and hormone-responsive cancers. Current approaches often lack the computational power to model dynamic interactions across biological scales, limiting translational insights. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support a multi-omics investigation of hormonal regulation and its disruption in women’s health disorders. Leveraging machine learning and network biology, we will analyze longitudinal datasets from clinical cohorts to identify predictive signatures of disease risk and treatment response. Agent-based models will simulate hormone-receptor interactions and cellular signaling pathways under varying genetic and environmental contexts, while federated learning frameworks will enable privacy-preserving analysis of distributed electronic health records. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle terabyte-scale data, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis of PCOS, stratification of breast cancer subtypes based on hormone signaling dynamics, and predictive models of gestational metabolic dysfunction. These results will inform clinical trials for personalized therapies and advance understanding of sex-specific disease mechanisms. By enabling scalable integration of multi-modal data, this project will establish a computational framework to address longstanding disparities in women’s health research, bridging gaps between molecular insights and clinical practice. The requested resources are essential to overcome current bottlenecks in data processing, model training, and simulation fidelity, ensuring robust, reproducible findings with direct translational relevance.
cip_definition: Research focused on Women's Health

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time, multi-objective staff scheduling in high-volume hospitality operations using high-performance computing (HPC) to address labor cost volatility and service quality challenges. Traditional scheduling methods in hotels and restaurants struggle to balance dynamic variables such as fluctuating occupancy rates, seasonal demand peaks, employee skill heterogeneity, and labor law constraints, often resulting in overstaffing, understaffing, or mismatched expertise. We propose a computational framework integrating federated learning with mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) to model workforce allocation across decentralized hospitality units while preserving operational privacy. The model will ingest real-time data streams from property management systems, IoT-enabled guest traffic sensors, and employee performance metrics to iteratively refine scheduling constraints. HPC resources are critical for solving the MILP component at scale, as the problem involves combinatorial optimization across thousands of shifting variables (e.g., labor regulations per jurisdiction, cross-trained staff availability, predictive demand curves). Parallelization will be implemented to simulate alternative scheduling scenarios under stochastic demand conditions, enabling robustness testing against historical disruption datasets (e.g., weather events, convention cancellations). Expected outcomes include an open-source scheduling engine capable of reducing labor costs by 12-18% in simulated full-service hotel environments while maintaining service quality thresholds measured through synthetic guest satisfaction scores. The project will further contribute novel benchmarking metrics for hospitality workforce agility, addressing a gap in operational analytics for an industry where labor constitutes 30-35% of total costs. Results will be validated against proprietary datasets from three regional hotel chains, with computational workflows designed for eventual integration into commercial property management systems.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to manage operations and facilities that provide food and/or lodging services to the traveling public. Includes instruction in hospitality industry principles; supplies purchasing, storage, and control; hotel and restaurant facilities design and planning; hospitality industry law; personnel management and labor relations; financial management; facilities management; marketing and sale promotion strategies; convention and event management; front desk operations; and applications to specific types of hotel, motel, and/or restaurant operations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 52.0902.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying stress adaptation in agriculturally significant plant species. Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten global crop productivity, necessitating rapid identification of genetic loci associated with drought tolerance, pathogen resistance, and nutrient-use efficiency. While advances in plant genomics have generated vast datasets—including whole-genome sequences, chromatin accessibility profiles, and methylation states for diverse cultivars—integrating these multi-omics layers to pinpoint functional regulatory elements remains computationally prohibitive using conventional resources. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze terabyte-scale genomic datasets from maize (Zea mays) and rice (Oryza sativa), focusing on structural variations and epigenetic modifications correlated with stress-responsive phenotypes. A hybrid pipeline combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with deep learning models will identify candidate cis-regulatory regions and quantify their pleiotropic effects across environments. Population genomic analyses will further reconstruct evolutionary trajectories of these loci under selective pressures. Computational demands include large-memory nodes for de novo genome assembly of non-reference cultivars, GPU-accelerated training of convolutional neural networks to predict enhancer-promoter interactions, and parallelized population genetics simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a prioritized list of haplotype-specific regulatory elements driving phenotypic variation, (2) predictive models linking epigenetic states to gene expression under stress, and (3) evolutionary inference frameworks to distinguish adaptive mutations from drift. These results will directly inform marker-assisted breeding programs and provide foundational insights into how chromatin architecture shapes plant adaptation. The scale of data (≥50 TB) and need for real-time iterative model tuning necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve biologically relevant throughput, as local clusters cannot support the concurrent genomic alignments, graph-based pangenome analyses, and population-level Bayesian computations required. This work bridges functional genomics with evolutionary theory, offering translational strategies to enhance crop resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetics of multicellular plants and fungi as related to botanical research as well as to applications in comparative genetics, ecology and evolutionary studies, clinical studies, and industrial research. Includes instruction in molecular genetics, gene expression, gene regulation, genomics, epigenetic phenomena, DNA recombination and repair, genetic interactions at the microbial and higher levels, and molecular evolution.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of criminal network evolution and decision-making processes through an innovative computational framework integrating behavioral game theory, geospatial analytics, and multi-agent systems. While traditional criminological research has examined static social structures or isolated individual choices, the complex interplay between adaptive criminal strategies, law enforcement responses, and urban environmental factors remains poorly understood at systemic scales. The research will develop a high-resolution simulation environment modeling how transient alliances form among offenders, how resource allocation strategies propagate through illicit networks, and how spatial crime patterns emerge from repeated interactions between rational actors. Computational methods include the implementation of evolutionary game theory algorithms optimized for GPU-accelerated systems, network topology analysis using graph neural networks, and assimilation of real-world crime incident data through Bayesian spatiotemporal models. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage three core challenges: 1) parallel processing of stochastic simulation ensembles capturing nonlinear societal feedback loops, 2) training deep learning architectures on sensitive, anonymized police records spanning 10 million+ incidents, and 3) real-time visualization of metropolitan-scale crime pattern forecasts. Anticipated outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for policy stress-testing, empirical insights into resilience mechanisms within urban criminal ecosystems, and predictive models of how infrastructure modifications influence offense displacement. By advancing computational criminology's capacity to model adaptive behaviors in complex social systems, this work aims to provide law enforcement agencies and urban planners with evidence-based strategies for crime prevention while maintaining rigorous ethical safeguards for data privacy and algorithmic transparency.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of crime as a sociopathological phenomenon, the behavior of criminals, and the social institutions evolved to respond to crime. Includes instruction in the theory of crime, psychological and social bases of criminal behavior, social value systems and the theory of punishment, criminal law and criminal justice systems, penology, rehabilitation and recidivism, studies of specific types of crime, social attitudes and policy, and applications to specific issues in law enforcement administration and policy.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate advanced computational modeling and simulation into the creative processes of three-dimensional sculpture, addressing the challenge of material and structural unpredictability in large-scale, experimental artworks. Traditional sculptural methods rely on iterative physical prototyping, which limits the exploration of complex forms, unconventional materials, and dynamic structural behaviors due to time, cost, and physical constraints. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for material deformation, stress distribution, and environmental interactions (e.g., wind, temperature) in virtual sculptural prototypes. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate the behavior of hybrid materials such as biodegradable composites, shape-memory alloys, and tensioned fabric systems under varying conditions. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained to propose structurally viable forms that balance aesthetic intent with physical feasibility, enabling rapid iteration of designs that push beyond conventional geometric paradigms. These computational workflows will be paired with augmented reality (AR) interfaces, allowing artists to interactively adjust parameters and visualize outcomes in real time. The project’s outcomes will include a suite of open-source tools for computational sculptural design, a dataset of material behavior simulations, and a series of physically realized artworks that demonstrate the integration of HPC-driven insights into studio practice. By bridging computational engineering and artistic experimentation, this research aims to expand the technical and conceptual boundaries of sculpture, offering new methodologies for sustainable, large-scale public art and fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between the visual arts and computational sciences.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by creating three-dimensional art works. Includes instruction in the analysis of form in space; round and relief concepts; sculptural composition; modern and experimental methods; different media such as clay, plaster, wood, stone, and metal; techniques such as carving, molding, welding, casting, and modeling; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing customer service operations in dynamic, large-scale environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Customer service management, particularly in call centers and help desks, involves complex interactions between customer behavior, real-time decision-making, and resource allocation. Traditional analytical models often fail to account for the high-dimensional data generated by these systems—including real-time service logs, customer feedback surveys, and behavioral analytics—limiting the ability to predict demand fluctuations or design adaptive staffing strategies. The proposed research will develop a computational framework to simulate and analyze customer service ecosystems, integrating heterogeneous datasets to model operational scenarios, test intervention strategies, and identify performance bottlenecks. Agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate customer interactions, service workflows, and staff responses under varying conditions, while machine learning techniques will predict emergent patterns in service demand and customer satisfaction. HPC resources are critical to support the parallel processing required for large-scale simulations, real-time data assimilation from customer relationship management (CRM) systems, and iterative optimization of staffing and workflow parameters. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for service managers, enabling data-driven adjustments to staffing schedules, escalation protocols, and training programs. The project will also generate novel insights into the relationship between operational flexibility, customer retention, and cost efficiency in service environments. By advancing computational methods tailored to customer service management, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical models and practical applications in business administration, ultimately enhancing the responsiveness and sustainability of customer-centric organizations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and monitor customer service performance and manage frontline customer support services, call centers/help desks, and customer relations. Includes instruction in customer behavior, specialized information technology and systems management, developing and using customer service databases, user surveys and other feedback mechanisms, strategic and performance planning and analysis, operations management, personnel supervision, and communications and marketing skills.

abstract: Neurodegenerative and neuromuscular diseases present complex diagnostic challenges due to heterogeneous molecular and structural alterations in nerve tissues. Current neuropathological analyses, while critical for diagnosis, often rely on subjective histopathological assessments or fragmented multi-omics data, limiting their ability to resolve spatially dynamic disease mechanisms or predict clinical trajectories. This project seeks to address these limitations by integrating high-resolution histopathological imaging, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and clinical data through advanced computational modeling, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The primary research objective is to identify spatially resolved biomarkers and mechanistic pathways underlying diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer’s disease, with a focus on nerve biopsy and necropsy-derived tissues. Computational workflows will include the development of deep learning models for automated annotation of neuropathological features in whole-slide imaging datasets, parallelized pipelines for multi-omics integration, and graph-based neural networks to model neuron-glia interaction networks. These analyses demand HPC capabilities due to the scale of data (10+ TB of imaging/sequencing data per cohort), the complexity of spatially aware machine learning architectures, and the need for iterative simulation of neurodegenerative cascades. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking histopathological signatures to molecular subtypes and disease progression, (2) open-source tools for integrative neuropathology analytics, and (3) novel hypotheses about microenvironment-specific drivers of neural degeneration. By bridging clinical neuropathology with scalable computational methods, this work aims to advance precision diagnostics and accelerate therapeutic discovery for neurological disorders. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage memory-intensive image processing, enable rapid hyperparameter optimization for deep learning models, and support large-scale comparative analyses across multi-modal datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory analysis of nerve tissues and the clinical diagnosis of neurological and neuromuscular diseases. May included related research in nerve biopsies and necropsies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the interplay of multisensory worship environments in contemporary Christian practice, with a focus on optimizing congregational engagement through dynamic integration of music, digital media, and spatial design. The central challenge lies in quantifying how real-time interactions between acoustic properties, visual projections, and participant positioning affect collective emotional and spiritual responses—a multidimensional problem requiring simultaneous processing of heterogeneous data streams. Current methodologies in worship studies rely on qualitative assessments or isolated technical metrics, lacking tools to simulate complex, adaptive systems where artistic, technological, and theological variables co-evolve during live services. The project will develop computational models using agent-based simulations to map congregation behavior patterns under varying sensory conditions, informed by anonymized motion-capture data from worship sessions and acoustic profiles of sacred spaces. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will process historical datasets of worship service recordings (audio, video, and environmental sensor logs) to identify correlations between artistic choices, technological configurations, and participant feedback metrics. HPC resources are critical for rendering 3D acoustic simulations of worship spaces with variable seating arrangements and digital projection surfaces, as well as training neural networks on the high-resolution multimodal datasets. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for worship environment design, enabling ministry teams to prototype spatial-aesthetic configurations computationally before physical implementation. The research will also yield open-source tools for analyzing real-time feedback loops between liturgical art and congregational dynamics, contributing new methodologies to the emerging field of computational humanities in sacred contexts. By bridging gaps between performing arts theory, human-computer interaction, and worship theology, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for creating inclusive, technologically integrated worship experiences while advancing interdisciplinary research at the nexus of faith traditions and digital innovation.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the use of musical and theatrical arts in Christian worship. Includes instruction in digital media, electronic hardware design and installation, music, theater, and worship theology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework to enhance the precision and efficiency of initial diagnostic image observations performed by Radiologist Assistants (RAs). While RAs play a critical role in preliminary image analysis under radiologist supervision, increasing imaging complexity and data volume risk diagnostic delays and observer variability. The proposed research addresses this challenge by creating computational tools to support RAs in detecting subtle anomalies in cross-sectional imaging, such as early-stage tumors or microvascular irregularities in CT and MRI scans. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train multimodal deep learning models on a curated dataset of 50,000 anonymized studies, integrating imaging data with structured clinical context (e.g., patient history, prior findings) to improve lesion localization and classification. A hybrid convolutional-transformer architecture will be optimized to prioritize interpretability, generating attention maps that align with RA workflows. Computational validation will involve synthetic data augmentation to simulate rare pathologies and scanner-specific artifacts, ensuring robustness across imaging protocols. Successful model development will enable real-time AI assistance during RA image evaluation, flagging regions of interest and suggesting differential diagnoses. The outcomes aim to reduce perceptual errors in initial assessments by ≥20% compared to unaided observations, as measured through blinded radiologist audits. This interdisciplinary approach bridges radiology practice, computer vision, and clinical decision science, advancing a niche yet critical component of diagnostic workflows. By deploying scalable AI tools tailored to RA competencies, the project supports safer task delegation in resource-constrained environments while maintaining rigorous diagnostic standards. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing 3D volumetric data, hyperparameter optimization across GPU nodes, and simulating real-world deployment scenarios through parallelized inference testing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to perform patient assessment, patient management, selected imaging procedures and to make initial observations of diagnostic images. Includes instruction in radiologic procedures and techniques, cross sectional anatomy, pharmacology, pathophysiology, patient assessment, patient care and management, and radiation biology.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced simulation framework for optimizing autonomous decision-making in contested air and space operational environments. Modern military aerospace operations face escalating complexity due to the proliferation of adversarial counter-space capabilities, dynamic threat landscapes, and the need for real-time coordination across heterogeneous systems (e.g., satellites, drones, manned aircraft). Traditional mission-planning tools struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between these elements at scale, particularly when accounting for cyber-physical vulnerabilities, sensor degradation, and adaptive adversarial tactics. The proposed work will employ a hybrid computational architecture combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and graph neural networks to simulate multi-domain operations under uncertainty. Key technical challenges include scaling real-time threat prediction algorithms, optimizing resource allocation for degraded communications, and validating emergent behaviors in edge-case scenarios. By integrating classified operational datasets with synthetic training environments, the framework will quantify risk trade-offs across mission timelines while adhering to strict safety and rules-of-engagement constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for joint air-space tasking orders, a repository of simulated adversarial tactics for training AI systems, and performance benchmarks for next-generation autonomous platforms. This work directly addresses the U.S. Department of Defense’s priority to enhance resilience in joint all-domain command and control (JADC2) systems while operating in electronically contested environments. The computational demands—parallelized simulations across 10^6+ scenario permutations, terabyte-scale sensor fusion, and sub-second latency requirements for reinforcement learning—necessitate dedicated HPC resources. Successful implementation will inform both near-term upgrades to existing platforms and long-term doctrinal shifts toward human-machine teaming architectures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of systems and equipment used in aerospace operations. Includes instruction in astronomy and astronautics, solid state theory, air and space operations, electronics, computer science, aviation and space flight safety, life support systems, flight operations management systems, programming, propulsion systems, weaponry, maintenance management and applications to specific systems and operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing computational demands of advanced digital arts research, particularly in the creation and optimization of large-scale, interactive, and AI-driven visual media. Current workflows in digital arts face significant bottlenecks when generating high-resolution 3D environments, simulating dynamic physics-based effects, or training generative neural networks for procedural content creation. These tasks require intensive parallel processing, real-time rendering capabilities, and vast memory allocation—requirements that exceed the capacity of standard desktop workstations. The research will focus on three core areas: (1) developing AI models for generative art and style transfer using multi-GPU training to accelerate iterative design processes; (2) simulating complex particle systems and fluid dynamics for immersive installations through distributed computing frameworks; and (3) enabling real-time interactivity in 4K/8K virtual reality (VR) environments via GPU-accelerated ray tracing and memory-optimized rendering pipelines. Computational methods will include CUDA-optimized algorithms, PyTorch-based neural networks, and MPI-parallelized simulations, validated against benchmarks in rendering efficiency and user experience metrics. The project’s outcomes aim to reduce rendering times by 60–80% for high-fidelity scenes, enable novel artistic workflows through scalable AI tools, and establish best practices for integrating HPC into digital arts pedagogy. By democratizing access to supercomputing resources, this work will empower artists and researchers to explore computationally prohibitive techniques—such as hyperrealistic real-time visuals or billion-parameter generative models—while contributing to interdisciplinary dialogues at the intersection of art, technology, and computational science. Results will directly support faculty-student collaborations, public digital exhibitions, and industry partnerships in game development and immersive media.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the use of computerized digital images as the primary medium of expression in the visual and performing arts, and that may prepare individuals for a wide variety of careers using new media, including graphic design, digital animation, motion graphics, 3D visualization, game and interactive media design, music and sound design, video production, web design, photography, and other fields.

abstract: This project seeks to advance theoretical understanding of non-perturbative phenomena in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) through large-scale numerical simulations of the strong interaction. The research focuses on resolving key uncertainties in the hadron spectrum, particularly the properties of exotic mesons and glueball candidates, which are critical for testing QCD predictions and exploring confinement mechanisms. Current experimental results from colliders present discrepancies with theoretical models, necessitating high-precision calculations of multi-quark systems and gluon dynamics that are inaccessible via perturbative methods. To address this, we employ lattice QCD simulations with dynamical fermions, utilizing improved staggered quark actions and Monte Carlo sampling techniques on fine spacetime lattices. The proposed work requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to generate statistically significant ensembles of gauge field configurations at near-physical pion masses (∼135 MeV) and lattice spacings below 0.06 fm. These configurations will enable calculations of correlation functions for exotic states using noise-reduction techniques and all-to-all propagators. Additional computational demands arise from the need to implement overlap fermions for studying chiral symmetry breaking and to analyze topological susceptibility in finite-temperature QCD matter. The requested resources will support hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization across thousands of cores, with optimized memory bandwidth for Dirac operator inversions. Expected outcomes include refined predictions for the mass hierarchy of tetraquark states, quantitative insights into gluon-mediated interactions, and improved constraints on the QCD phase diagram. These results will directly inform ongoing experiments at CERN and Jefferson Lab while advancing numerical methods for future studies of hadronic matter. The project’s computational requirements—estimated at 2.5 million node-hours annually—reflect the exponential scaling of lattice QCD with physical volume and inverse lattice spacing, necessitating dedicated allocations on tier-1 HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the basic constituents of sub-atomic matter and energy, and the forces governing fundamental processes. Includes instruction in quantum theory, field theory, single-particle systems, perturbation and scattering theory, matter-radiation interaction, symmetry, quarks, capture, Schroedinger mechanics, methods for detecting particle emission and absorption, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: The integration of multi-scale clinical laboratory data—including histopathological images, genomic profiles, and clinical metadata—remains a critical challenge in advancing diagnostic precision for complex diseases such as cancer and autoimmune disorders. Current methodologies often fail to efficiently synthesize these heterogeneous datasets, limiting the ability to identify subtle anatomic abnormalities or correlate molecular signatures with disease progression. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, integrative analysis of multimodal pathology data. The research will focus on creating machine learning models to automate the detection of diagnostically significant features in whole-slide imaging (WSI) of tissue samples, coupled with genomic variant prioritization pipelines to uncover biomarkers predictive of clinical outcomes. Computational methods will include deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for WSI segmentation, graph-based algorithms for spatial transcriptomics integration, and federated learning architectures to maintain patient privacy while aggregating data across institutional partners. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of high-resolution imaging data, train complex models with millions of parameters, and perform genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across diverse patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for automated identification of underrecognized histologic patterns in renal and hepatic biopsies, (2) predictive models linking tumor microenvironment features to immunotherapy responses, and (3) open-source tools for quality control in digital pathology workflows. The project will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in anatomic pathology while providing a template for computational pathology resource sharing. By bridging gaps between traditional morphologic analysis and modern omics technologies, this work aims to establish scalable computational strategies for personalized disease classification, ultimately reducing diagnostic turnaround times and improving reproducibility in clinical laboratories.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease and anatomic abnormalities. Includes instruction in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management, and quality control.

abstract: The growing complexity of healthcare systems demands advanced strategies to optimize nurse staffing, resource allocation, and operational workflows while maintaining patient safety and care quality. Current approaches in nursing administration often rely on static models or historical data, which fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff skill mix variability, and real-time resource constraints. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model and predict optimal staffing and resource configurations in diverse clinical scenarios. Leveraging multi-agent modeling and machine learning techniques, we will simulate hospital units under varying conditions, integrating real-world data streams (e.g., electronic health records, nurse-patient ratios, equipment availability) with probabilistic projections of patient admission patterns and staff availability. The computational framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess millions of potential staffing and scheduling combinations, evaluating outcomes related to care quality metrics, overtime costs, and nurse burnout risk factors. By incorporating temporal and spatial dependencies at scale, the models will identify resilient staffing patterns adaptable to unexpected demand surges or resource shortages. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space and achieving clinically relevant time-to-solution metrics for operational decision support. Expected outcomes include evidence-based staffing algorithms, predictive tools for resource bottleneck identification, and policy recommendations for adaptive nurse management strategies. These results will advance nursing administration research by enabling data-driven, proactive decision-making in complex healthcare environments, with potential applications to crisis response planning and value-based care initiatives. The project will also establish a template for computational nursing science methodologies that bridge operations research and clinical practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to manage nursing personnel and services in hospitals and other health care delivery agencies. Includes instruction in principles of health care administration, resource and financial management, health care law and policy, medical personnel management, and managed care operations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory management strategies for omnichannel retail systems, addressing the growing complexity of consumer behavior, supply chain disruptions, and multi-platform sales operations. While traditional retail models rely on static assumptions about demand elasticity and supplier reliability, modern retail environments require real-time adaptive decision-making under uncertainty. We propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach to simulate interactions between customer segments, inventory nodes, and pricing algorithms across physical stores, e-commerce platforms, and third-party marketplaces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating 10,000+ concurrent agents representing customers, suppliers, and logistics systems while incorporating terabyte-scale datasets of historical sales, web traffic, and supply chain records. The computational workflow will integrate deep reinforcement learning for price optimization, graph neural networks to model supply chain dependencies, and Monte Carlo methods to quantify operational risks. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for simulating multi-echelon retail systems under stochastic demand, (2) evidence-based thresholds for automated price adjustments across sales channels, and (3) predictive metrics for inventory allocation that balance warehousing costs with service-level requirements. This research will provide retail managers with scalable decision-support tools to improve profitability in hybrid sales environments while maintaining computational reproducibility—a gap in current retail management literature. The project’s HPC requirements stem from the need to run parameter sweeps across hundreds of market scenarios and validate models against decade-long temporal datasets, tasks that exceed the capacity of standard enterprise computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operations of a wide variety of retail businesses, including department stores; independent and chain stores; fashion, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical establishments; and online retail businesses. Includes instruction in retail management, merchandise management, customer service management, marketing, organizational behavior, accounting, finance, business law, and personnel management.

abstract: Surgical wound healing and tissue reconstruction outcomes remain highly variable due to complex interactions between patient-specific biological factors, surgical techniques, and postoperative care protocols. This project aims to develop predictive multiscale models integrating clinical, imaging, and molecular data to optimize personalized treatment strategies for complex surgical wounds. A critical barrier is the computational demand of analyzing high-dimensional datasets (e.g., 3D tissue perfusion imaging, single-cell transcriptomics, and longitudinal electronic health records) while accounting for biomechanical forces and cellular-scale healing dynamics. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement finite element models of wound biomechanics, agent-based simulations of microbial colonization dynamics, and machine learning architectures for risk stratification. The computational workflow will couple finite element analysis of tissue stress-strain distributions under different closure techniques with agent-based models simulating immune cell-pathogen interactions informed by patient microbiome data. Deep learning approaches will be applied to preoperative CT/MRI datasets to predict regions of poor vascularization susceptible to dehiscence. These components will feed into an ensemble model trained on outcomes from 2,350 historical cases to identify optimal closure methods and antimicrobial prophylaxis regimens. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabytes of intraoperative imaging data, running Monte Carlo simulations of wound infection probabilities, and training 3D convolutional neural networks with biologically informed regularization. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for surgical site infection risk and tissue viability thresholds, (2) open-source tools for simulating wound microenvironment dynamics, and (3) clinical decision-support algorithms to guide reconstruction planning in comorbid populations. This computational framework will address critical gaps in translating heterogeneous biological data into actionable surgical strategies, ultimately reducing revision surgeries and healthcare costs associated with wound complications.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social inequality in urban environments through the analysis of large-scale, longitudinal demographic and social interaction datasets. The research problem centers on understanding how structural factors—such as housing policies, access to education, and employment networks—interact with individual-level behaviors to reproduce or mitigate socioeconomic disparities over time. Traditional statistical methods face limitations in modeling the multi-level, non-linear relationships and feedback loops inherent in these processes, particularly when scaling to city-level populations with millions of interactions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based simulations coupled with machine learning-enhanced social network analysis. The computational approach will involve three phases: 1) processing and harmonizing census microdata, geospatial records, and social media-derived mobility patterns using distributed computing frameworks; 2) developing parallelized agent-based models that simulate decision-making processes under varying policy scenarios; and 3) applying graph neural networks to detect emergent patterns in inequality propagation across temporal networks of resource access. The simulations will be calibrated using historical data from three major metropolitan regions, enabling counterfactual analysis of intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include identifying critical leverage points for reducing spatial segregation, quantifying the compounding effects of intersectional disadvantages, and generating predictive frameworks to assess the long-term impacts of housing and education reforms. By enabling analysis at unprecedented granularity across decades of social change, this HPC-supported methodology aims to advance sociological theories of structural inequality while providing empirically grounded tools for policymakers. The computational workflows and anonymized datasets will be made available through an open-access repository to support reproducibility and collaborative development in demographic research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human social institutions and social relationships. Includes instruction in social theory, sociological research methods, social organization and structure, social stratification and hierarchies, dynamics of social change, family structures, social deviance and control, and applications to the study of specific social groups, social institutions, and social problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of spiritual resilience in digital religious communities through computational text and network analysis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale, unstructured datasets. As virtual faith-based spaces—such as prayer forums, grief support groups, and crisis counseling channels—grow in prominence, their role in shaping individual and collective spiritual well-being remains underexplored. The research problem centers on identifying linguistic, relational, and behavioral patterns that correlate with measurable outcomes in pastoral care efficacy, particularly in contexts where traditional in-person ministry is inaccessible. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to analyze sentiment, thematic clusters, and narrative structures in anonymized text corpora from moderated interfaith support platforms (spanning 2015–2023), alongside temporal network analysis to model participant engagement and community cohesion. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect subtle markers of spiritual distress or growth, while graph algorithms will map the diffusion of coping strategies and social support across decentralized networks. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale (estimated 15TB of text and metadata) and complexity of these analyses, particularly for fine-tuning large language models on domain-specific theological and counseling terminology, and for running iterative simulations of community resilience under varying sociotechnical conditions. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying pastoral impact in digital ministry contexts, actionable insights for optimizing virtual care protocols, and open-source tools tailored to ethical analysis of sensitive spiritual communication data. This work bridges computational social science, pastoral theology, and digital humanities, offering methodological innovations for studying emergent forms of religious practice while addressing urgent practical challenges in scalable, culturally competent spiritual care.
cip_title: Pastoral Counseling and Specialized Ministries, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pastoral counseling and specialized ministries, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision rehabilitation strategies for neuromusculoskeletal disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific biomechanical and physiological responses to therapeutic interventions. Current clinical tools for predicting rehabilitation outcomes lack the resolution to account for individual variations in tissue healing, neuromuscular adaptation, and functional recovery, leading to suboptimal treatment personalization. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multiscale biomechanical modeling, machine learning, and high-resolution clinical imaging data (e.g., MRI, motion capture). The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale simulations of musculoskeletal dynamics under diverse rehabilitation protocols, coupled with probabilistic machine learning to identify predictors of optimal recovery trajectories. Key computational challenges include finite element modeling of tissue remodeling, real-time optimization of assistive device parameters, and ensemble learning across heterogeneous patient datasets (demographics, injury severity, comorbidities). By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times from weeks to hours, permitting rapid iteration of virtual rehabilitation scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models linking specific therapeutic variables (e.g., load magnitude, exercise frequency) to functional milestones in stroke, spinal cord injury, and osteoarthritis populations. These tools will inform clinical decision-making by quantifying patient-specific risks of reinjury or non-recovery, while guiding the design of adaptive rehabilitation robotics. The resource request supports 1.2 million core-hours annually for three years, prioritizing scalable memory allocation for whole-body simulations and distributed training of deep neural networks on multi-modal data. This work bridges a critical gap in rehabilitation science by translating computational insights into actionable clinical protocols, ultimately reducing trial-and-error approaches in physical therapy and improving long-term patient mobility outcomes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, etiology, treatment, prevention and rehabilitation of neuromusculo-skeletal, cardiovascular, pulmonary and other system disorders common to patients of both sexes and all ages. May included related research in physical examinations, design and prescription of rehabilitation strategies and the supervision of rehabilitation teams.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing additive manufacturing (AM) processes for high-performance metallic components, where defects such as residual stresses, microstructural inhomogeneity, and geometric distortions limit reliability and scalability. Current analytical models and small-scale simulations fail to capture the complex, coupled thermal-mechanical-metallurgical interactions inherent in laser-based powder bed fusion (LPBF) processes, particularly at industrial production scales. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-physics computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and phase-field modeling to simulate melt pool dynamics, solidification behavior, and stress evolution across entire part geometries. The simulations will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve micron-scale features over macroscale build volumes, requiring parallelized solvers and adaptive meshing to manage memory and computational demands. Machine learning techniques will be applied to surrogate modeling and parameter optimization, reducing the cost of iterative design exploration. By correlating simulation outputs with experimental data from in-situ monitoring systems, the project aims to establish predictive process-structure-property relationships for nickel superalloys and titanium alloys. The outcomes will enable defect mitigation strategies, process parameter optimization, and digital twin frameworks for AM systems, directly advancing the adoption of metal additive manufacturing in aerospace and energy sectors. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution across multi-layer builds, with simulations targeting >10^8 degrees of freedom and 48-hour compute times per build iteration. This work will provide open-source simulation tools and a public dataset to accelerate innovation in computational materials engineering.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the preservation of culturally significant historic structures through the development of a computational framework to model material degradation and structural vulnerabilities in aging architectural heritage. Many historic buildings feature unique, non-standardized construction materials and methods, making their conservation challenging. Current approaches rely heavily on physical inspections and localized testing, which are time-intensive and fail to capture system-wide interactions between environmental stressors, material fatigue, and structural integrity. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning, and environmental sensor data to predict long-term degradation patterns in historic masonry, timber, and composite structures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating complex, nonlinear interactions across spatial and temporal scales—from micro-crack propagation in aged mortar to macro-scale load redistribution in vaulted ceilings. The computational workflow will leverage historical climate data, material property databases, and 3D laser scans of case-study buildings to parameterize models. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and empirical datasets to identify high-risk degradation pathways and prioritize intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolset for predicting site-specific preservation needs, reducing reliance on invasive sampling, and informing climate-resilient restoration practices. By enabling dynamic, data-driven conservation planning, this research aims to extend the lifespan of heritage structures while maintaining their historical authenticity. The project bridges computational engineering, materials science, and preservation ethics, aligning with interdisciplinary priorities in historic conservation. Successful implementation will provide preservationists with evidence-based frameworks to allocate resources efficiently, particularly for underrepresented or at-risk sites with limited prior study.
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on architectural design and building techniques for historic and restored structures, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision manufacturing processes through the development of high-fidelity computational models to optimize additive manufacturing (AM) of high-performance alloys. A critical challenge in AM is controlling defects caused by rapid thermal gradients and phase transformations during laser-based deposition. Existing analytical models lack the resolution to predict localized stress accumulation, microstructural anomalies, or porosity formation at the micron scale, particularly for complex geometries. To address this gap, we propose a multi-physics computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for thermal-stress modeling, phase-field simulations for microstructure evolution, and machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these coupled phenomena, which involve billion-element meshes and nanosecond-scale iterative calculations across multi-layer builds. Simulations will be validated against synchrotron X-ray diffraction data capturing real-time thermal and strain dynamics during laser-material interactions. The resulting models will identify process parameter combinations (e.g., laser power, scan speed, layer thickness) that minimize residual stress while maximizing tensile strength in nickel-based superalloys. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for AM process design and a database of optimized parameters for aerospace-grade materials. This work will directly support next-generation manufacturing of turbine components with reduced post-processing requirements, lowering energy costs by an estimated 15-20% compared to conventional methods. By leveraging HPC capabilities to bridge mesoscale physics and macroscale performance, the project aims to establish a computational paradigm for precision production challenges across materials systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision production, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing resource allocation across multiple concurrent projects, particularly under conditions of uncertainty such as fluctuating material costs, labor shortages, and environmental disruptions. Traditional resource management strategies often rely on static schedules and deterministic models, which fail to account for dynamic, real-world variability, leading to inefficiencies, cost overruns, and project delays. This research proposes the development of a stochastic optimization framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate multi-project resource allocation under uncertainty. The project integrates operations research, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to create adaptive decision-support tools capable of dynamically reallocating labor, equipment, and materials in response to stochastic events. Computational methods will include Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risks, parallelized genetic algorithms to explore solution spaces efficiently, and reinforcement learning to refine allocation policies iteratively. By harnessing HPC resources, the framework will process large-scale datasets—including historical project performance, real-time supply chain data, and environmental sensors—to generate probabilistic forecasts and optimize decisions at enterprise scales. Expected outcomes include a scalable software prototype that reduces idle resource time by 15–20%, minimizes emergency procurement costs by modeling contingent scenarios, and improves adherence to project timelines through proactive risk mitigation. The research will advance computational methods in construction management by bridging gaps between prescriptive analytics and operational agility, offering a novel paradigm for resource optimization in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Results will be validated against case studies from collaborative industry partners, ensuring practical relevance and scalability.
