This work positions HPC as a critical enabler of next-generation construction management tools, with implications for cost efficiency, sustainability, and resilience in global infrastructure development.
cip_definition: Any program in construction management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern hybrid energy systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize their design, operation, and resilience. This project addresses the challenge of modeling multi-source energy networks—integrating intermittent renewables, storage technologies, and demand-response mechanisms—under dynamic grid conditions and policy constraints. Existing simulation tools struggle to resolve the temporal, spatial, and stochastic variability inherent in these systems at scale, particularly when evaluating long-term performance across diverse climate scenarios and regulatory frameworks. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform parallelized, multi-objective optimization and uncertainty quantification. The framework will employ modular agent-based models to simulate component interactions, combined with machine learning surrogates to accelerate scenario evaluations. Key computational tasks include Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic risk assessment, mixed-integer linear programming for dispatch optimization, and sensitivity analyses to identify critical infrastructure dependencies. By utilizing HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce simulation wall times by 70-90% compared to existing single-node approaches while scaling to regional-level systems with >10^5 decision variables. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for hybrid energy system planning, validated against real-world microgrid data, and policy-relevant insights into cost-reliability tradeoffs under decarbonization pathways. This work will directly support curriculum development in energy systems integration for engineering technology students, bridging gaps between theoretical models and industrial-scale applications. The requested computing resources will enable unprecedented resolution in capturing grid-edge dynamics, advancing both academic research and workforce training in next-generation energy infrastructure management.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex systemic interactions in families navigating chronic illness, with the goal of advancing evidence-based interventions in Medical Family Therapy (MedFT). Current therapeutic approaches often rely on qualitative assessments of family dynamics, limiting scalability and the ability to predict longitudinal outcomes under variable biopsychosocial stressors. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate family systems as adaptive networks, integrating clinical data from patient-therapist interactions, electronic health records, and wearable biometric sensors. The ABMs will parameterize relational behaviors (e.g., communication patterns, caregiving roles), physiological markers (e.g., cortisol levels, heart rate variability), and contextual factors (e.g., healthcare access, cultural norms) to explore emergent phenomena such as resilience thresholds or cascading relational stress. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian inference to calibrate models against longitudinal observational data from 200+ families managing type 2 diabetes, a condition with well-documented systemic impacts. Sensitivity analyses will identify critical leverage points for therapeutic intervention, while machine learning pipelines will classify interaction patterns predictive of treatment adherence or emotional disengagement. HPC resources are essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter space, running stochastic simulations across diverse demographic cohorts, and processing real-time biometric streams. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for simulating family illness trajectories, (2) actionable insights into how nonlinear dynamics in relational systems modulate health outcomes, and (3) open-source tools enabling therapists to visualize probabilistic scenarios during treatment planning. By bridging systems science with relational health practices, this work aims to establish computational MedFT as a paradigm for personalized, proactive family-centered care in chronic disease management.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with patients and their families who are experiencing emotional, physical, relational and spiritual difficulties related to acute and chronic illnesses. Includes instruction in cultural context, ethics, family dynamics, family therapy, gender, human development, marriage counseling, psychopathology, research design and methods, sexuality, and systems thinking.

abstract: Infectious diseases in agricultural animal populations pose significant threats to food security, economic stability, and animal welfare. Current approaches to modeling disease spread often lack the resolution to account for complex interactions between host genetics, pathogen evolution, environmental stressors, and management practices. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate disease transmission dynamics and optimize mitigation strategies for economically critical pathogens, such as avian influenza and porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). The research will integrate multi-scale datasets, including genomic sequences, climate variables, and animal movement records, to model spatiotemporal disease risks under diverse scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support agent-based modeling of transmission pathways across heterogeneous populations and machine learning analyses to identify genetic or environmental biomarkers of outbreak susceptibility. Simulations will evaluate the efficacy of vaccination protocols, biosecurity measures, and selective breeding strategies under shifting climate conditions. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized genomic epidemiology tools to analyze pathogen evolution and host adaptation patterns across millions of pathogen genomes and host transcriptomic profiles. Expected outcomes include predictive models to prioritize high-risk regions, optimize surveillance, and design targeted interventions. By enabling rapid scenario testing at unprecedented scales, this project will provide actionable insights for reducing disease burdens in livestock systems while addressing critical gaps in translational animal health research. The resulting framework will advance capabilities to preempt emerging zoonotic threats and support sustainable agricultural practices through data-driven decision-making.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the study, prevention, and control of diseases in agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in environmental science, pharmacology, animal population studies, genetics, animal physiology and diet, disease prevention, treatment methodologies, and laboratory and testing procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between neural plasticity and cognitive flexibility using computational models that integrate neuroimaging data, behavioral experiments, and artificial neural networks. While cognitive flexibility—the ability to adapt thinking and behavior to novel stimuli—is critical to human intelligence, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Traditional approaches in neuroscience or psychology alone struggle to disentangle the multiscale interactions between synaptic-level changes, network-level dynamics, and behavioral outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework that couples spiking neural network models with reinforcement learning algorithms, calibrated against functional MRI (fMRI) and electroencephalography (EEG) data from human subjects performing cognitive flexibility tasks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale networks with biophysically realistic neuron models, optimize parameters via evolutionary algorithms, and perform Bayesian inference on hierarchical models linking neural activity to behavioral metrics. The proposed work will generate novel predictions about how neurotransmitter systems (e.g., dopamine, acetylcholine) modulate plasticity-flexibility trade-offs across developmental stages. Expected outcomes include a publicly shared toolbox for simulating cognitive flexibility impairments in neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorder) and actionable insights for designing adaptive AI systems that mimic human-like learning transitions. By bridging computational neuroscience, machine learning, and cognitive psychology, this research advances a unified theory of adaptive intelligence while providing scalable methods for cross-domain data integration—a critical need in multidisciplinary cognitive science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the mind and the nature of intelligence from the interdisciplinary perspectives of computer science, philosophy, mathematics, psychology, neuroscience, and other disciplines. Includes instruction in mathematics and logic, cognitive process modeling, dynamic systems, learning theories, brain and cognition, neural networking, programming, and applications to topics such as language acquisition, computer systems, and perception and behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize the efficiency and nutritional quality of agricultural product processing through advanced computational modeling of multi-variable systems. Current methods for thermal, mechanical, and chemical processing of plant- and animal-derived foods face challenges in balancing energy efficiency, product safety, and nutrient retention due to the complex interactions of variables such as temperature gradients, material heterogeneity, and reaction kinetics. To address this, we propose developing high-fidelity simulations of processing workflows using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will map heat and mass transfer during thermal treatments (e.g., pasteurization, drying), while discrete element method (DEM) simulations will analyze particle interactions in milling and mixing operations. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will identify optimal processing parameters by integrating experimental data on nutrient degradation kinetics, microbial inactivation rates, and energy consumption from pilot-scale trials. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these models to accommodate real-world variability in raw material properties and industrial equipment configurations, which existing reduced-order models cannot capture. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to minimize energy use while maximizing nutrient preservation in plant-based protein extraction and dairy processing case studies. These tools will be validated against experimental data from collaborating food processing facilities, with a target of reducing energy inputs by 15-20% and improving vitamin retention by 10% compared to industry benchmarks. The resulting open-access computational frameworks will enable small-to-medium enterprises to adopt precision processing strategies, enhancing food security and reducing waste in the agricultural value chain. This work aligns with national priorities to modernize food infrastructure while addressing the growing demand for sustainably processed, nutritionally dense products.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, inspect, store, process, and package agricultural products in the form of human food consumables, animal or plant food, or other industrial products. Includes instruction in the nutrient and industrial properties of various agricultural products; logistics and storage procedures; chemical and mechanical processing operations; packaging; safety and health requirements; and related technical and business principles.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of next-generation electrical power transmission systems through advanced computational modeling. The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, coupled with aging grid infrastructure and dynamic load demands, has introduced unprecedented complexity in ensuring grid stability, fault tolerance, and energy efficiency. Traditional analytical methods and small-scale simulations are insufficient to model the interdependencies between distributed energy resources, transmission line behavior under extreme weather conditions, and real-time load balancing at regional scales. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a multi-physics computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale power networks with high spatial and temporal resolution. The approach integrates finite element analysis for electromagnetic transient modeling, machine learning algorithms for predictive fault detection, and graph theory-based optimization to evaluate grid reconfiguration strategies under contingency scenarios. Key simulations will model cascading failure propagation, transient stability during renewable intermittency, and the impact of novel high-temperature superconducting materials on transmission efficiency. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve a 50-100x acceleration in simulation throughput compared to conventional workstations, enabling parametric studies across thousands of grid configurations. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for grid resilience improvement, validated control strategies for adaptive voltage regulation, and open-source simulation tools tailored for atypical transmission architectures not covered by existing software. These results will directly inform curriculum development for emerging power transmission technologies while providing actionable insights for utilities modernizing critical infrastructure. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the project's petabyte-scale datasets and complex optimization loops, which require sustained GPU-accelerated computations and distributed memory architectures.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics data in laboratory medicine presents a critical challenge for advancing precision diagnostics and disease stratification. Current methodologies struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and clinical laboratory data—into unified predictive models, particularly at scale. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework for real-time, integrative analysis of heterogeneous biomedical data to identify biomarkers and optimize diagnostic workflows. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement scalable machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, to model interactions across biological layers and clinical variables. Key steps include preprocessing raw sequencing and mass spectrometry data, training interpretable models on GPU-accelerated nodes, and validating predictions against longitudinal patient outcomes from electronic health records. The computational demand arises from the need to process terabytes of multi-omics data, perform hyperparameter optimization across thousands of model configurations, and simulate diagnostic scenarios under varying clinical constraints. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel biomarker panels for early detection of sepsis and autoimmune disorders, as well as a validated pipeline for dynamically updating diagnostic models as new data becomes available. This work will directly enhance the translational utility of laboratory data in clinical decision-making, reduce turnaround times for complex diagnoses, and establish a template for resource-efficient integration of emerging technologies in medical laboratories. The requested HPC allocation is essential to achieve the necessary computational throughput, enable large-scale parallelization, and ensure reproducibility across diverse patient cohorts. Success in this project will provide a foundation for data-driven innovations in laboratory test development and foster collaboration between computational researchers and clinical pathologists.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and practices of applied medical research and related techniques, equipment, data systems, and research design. Includes instruction in the management of medical laboratories in research and healthcare facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural identity preservation and transformation within diasporic communities through the computational analysis of multilingual textual corpora and multimedia archives. The research problem centers on understanding how digital communication platforms and transnational networks influence the evolution of cultural narratives, practices, and intergenerational knowledge transfer in underrepresented communities. Current qualitative methodologies in area studies lack scalability for analyzing vast, heterogeneous datasets spanning decades, limiting insights into longitudinal patterns and cross-regional comparisons. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods framework combining natural language processing (NLP), geospatial network modeling, and machine learning-based multimedia analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of digitized community records, social media interactions, oral history transcripts, and visual artifacts in 15+ languages. Computational workflows will include transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, graph neural networks to map transnational communication patterns, and computer vision techniques to analyze symbolic representations in visual media. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel computational model of cultural transmission pathways across digital and physical spaces, 2) open-source tools for ethically grounded analysis of culturally sensitive materials, and 3) quantitative evidence challenging assumptions about cultural homogenization in globalization studies. The project’s scale—processing over 10 million text documents and 500,000 multimedia items—requires parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated model training that only HPC infrastructure can provide. By bridging computational social science with critical area studies frameworks, this research aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing cultural change while directly supporting community-driven preservation initiatives. Results will be disseminated through an interactive platform enabling scholars and community stakeholders to explore cultural connectivity patterns through accessible data visualizations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: Any instructional program in specifically defined area studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Chronic pain remains a poorly understood condition with heterogeneous treatment responses, often necessitating trial-and-error approaches that prolong patient suffering. This project seeks to address this challenge by integrating multimodal neurobiological data to develop predictive computational models of pain perception and treatment efficacy. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will analyze large-scale datasets spanning functional neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), transcriptomic profiles of peripheral nociceptors, and longitudinal electronic health records from diverse chronic pain cohorts. Machine learning pipelines will be optimized to identify neural circuit signatures and genetic markers associated with pain phenotypes, while mechanistic simulations of neurotransmitter dynamics will model interactions between pharmacological agents and patient-specific neurophysiology. A key innovation involves federated learning frameworks to securely aggregate data across institutions, addressing sample size limitations while preserving privacy. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning for image analysis, parallelized genomic association studies, and agent-based modeling of neural network plasticity. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated classifier for predicting opioid vs. non-opioid therapy success based on baseline biomarkers, (2) dynamic maps of pain-related brain connectivity alterations under different interventions, and (3) open-source tools for simulating patient-specific drug effects on pain pathways. By bridging clinical pain neuroscience with advanced computational methods, this work aims to establish a foundation for precision pain medicine, reducing reliance on empirical treatment strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing petascale neuroimaging datasets, running comparative analyses across 10,000+ genomic loci, and maintaining iterative model training pipelines requiring months of compute time on conventional systems.
cip_definition: A post-residency program of study that prepares physicians in the diagnosis, management, and treatment of acute and chronic pain. Includes instruction in anesthesiology, pain assessment, pain classification and diagnosis, pain neuroscience, palliative and end-of-life care, physical medicine and rehabilitation, psychiatry of pain, pain pharmacology, public policy, and legal issues of pain management.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of household financial decision-making under economic volatility using advanced computational modeling techniques. The study focuses on how heterogeneous household behaviors—shaped by cultural norms, access to digital financial tools, and localized policy environments—affect resilience to macroeconomic shocks such as inflation or income disruption. While prior work in consumer economics has relied on aggregated survey data or simplified theoretical models, this project addresses a critical gap by integrating high-resolution behavioral datasets, agent-based modeling (ABM), and machine learning to simulate complex, adaptive decision networks at scale. The primary research problem revolves around identifying nonlinear feedback loops between micro-level financial choices (e.g., savings, debt management, gig economy participation) and systemic economic outcomes, particularly in underserved communities where traditional risk-mitigation frameworks are often inadequate. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will develop a modular ABM framework capable of simulating millions of agent-households with dynamically updated preference structures, calibrated using real-world transactional data and ethnographic interviews. Computational workflows will include parallelized Monte Carlo experiments to test policy interventions, natural language processing (NLP) of social media data to refine behavioral priors, and graph-based network analysis to map interdependencies between financial behaviors and community-level economic health. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for policymakers to evaluate hyper-localized economic stabilization strategies, as well as novel metrics for quantifying household financial fragility in multi-stressor scenarios. By bridging computational social science, behavioral economics, and consumer informatics, this work aims to advance methodological innovation in non-STEM domains while addressing pressing societal challenges related to economic equity and adaptive capacity. The scale and complexity of the simulations—requiring terabyte-scale data integration, real-time parameter optimization, and high-throughput scenario testing—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve research objectives within feasible timeframes.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Economics and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer economics and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the mechanisms underlying vascular remodeling in diabetic cardiovascular complications, a leading contributor to morbidity in patients with type 2 diabetes. Despite clinical evidence linking hyperglycemia and hemodynamic stress to pathological vascular changes, the integrated effects of metabolic dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered mechanical forces on arterial wall dynamics remain poorly understood. We propose a multi-scale computational framework to model vascular adaptation in diabetes, combining hemodynamic simulations with cellular-scale representations of endothelial and smooth muscle cell behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatially heterogeneous blood flow patterns in patient-specific arterial geometries derived from clinical imaging, while simultaneously simulating mechanotransduction pathways and redox signaling in vascular cells. The computational model will integrate physiological data from in vitro studies of human vascular cells exposed to diabetic conditions, including glucose variability and oxidative stress, to parameterize cellular responses to biomechanical cues. Using finite element methods and agent-based modeling, we will predict how localized alterations in wall shear stress and circumferential strain drive maladaptive remodeling in coronary and renal arteries. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds in glucose levels, blood pressure, and inflammatory markers that exacerbate vascular stiffening and luminal narrowing. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform to map disease progression under varying metabolic and hemodynamic conditions, as well as candidate mechanobiological targets to mitigate remodeling. This work will advance translational strategies for diabetic cardiovascular complications by elucidating how systemic metabolic disturbances converge with localized mechanical forces to drive tissue-level pathology, directly supporting the development of personalized interventions for high-risk patients.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: Endocrine and metabolic disorders, including type 2 diabetes, thyroid dysfunction, and obesity, are driven by complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. Current clinical models struggle to integrate multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with dynamic physiological parameters, limiting personalized treatment strategies. This project aims to develop a computational framework to model endocrine system dysregulation at scale, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to identify predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets. The primary research problem involves resolving heterogeneity in patient datasets—spanning electronic health records, longitudinal biomarker measurements, and single-cell RNA sequencing—to uncover subtype-specific mechanisms of disease progression. A hybrid machine learning and dynamical systems approach will be employed. Neural networks will classify patient subtypes using clinical and omics data, while differential equation-based models will simulate hormonal feedback loops (e.g., insulin-glucose dynamics) under genetic perturbation. Bayesian inference methods will integrate sparse, noisy clinical data with in silico simulations to refine parameter estimates. Computational demands include large-scale parameter sweeps for network stability analysis, parallelized processing of single-cell datasets (>100,000 cells per sample), and training deep learning models on multi-modal data. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of novel regulatory nodes in metabolic pathways associated with treatment resistance in diabetes, (2) predictive models linking thyroid hormone receptor variants to cardiovascular risk in hypothyroidism, and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating endocrine network perturbations. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of >10 TB of multi-omics data across 5,000 patient records, reducing simulation runtime from weeks to days. This work will advance precision endocrinology by bridging molecular mechanisms with clinical phenotypes, directly informing targeted therapies and trial design for metabolic syndromes.
cip_definition: Research on disorders of the internal (endocrine) glands such as the thyroid and adrenal glands, and to deal with disorders such as diabetes, metabolic and nutritional disorders, obesity, pituitary diseases, and menstrual and sexual problems. Requires prior completion of a residency program in internal medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the morphosyntactic and lexical divergence of Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian (BCS) languages in contemporary digital texts, a critical yet understudied area in South Slavic linguistics. While these languages share a high degree of mutual intelligibility, socio-political shifts since the 1990s have amplified regional standardization efforts, fostering subtle but consequential linguistic differentiation. Current scholarship lacks large-scale computational studies tracking these changes, particularly in informal digital communication (e.g., social media, forums), where language evolution is most dynamic. The research problem centers on identifying and modeling emergent patterns of divergence across dialects and registers, which traditional manual methods cannot feasibly address due to data volume and complexity. The project will employ computational linguistics techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on BCS corpora, dialectometric analysis, and diachronic word embedding alignment, to process multilingual and multidialectal text datasets spanning 2010–2024. HPC resources are essential for training custom neural models on terabytes of unstructured text, running parallelized comparative analyses across regional variants, and simulating lexical diffusion patterns using agent-based models. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible corpus of annotated digital BCS texts, 2) quantitative metrics of divergence rates across grammatical features, and 3) visualizations of dialect continua influenced by digital communication networks. This work will advance understanding of how digital spaces accelerate language standardization and differentiation, with applications in language preservation policy, machine translation for under-resourced South Slavic varieties, and educational tools for dialect navigation. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, the project bridges methodological gaps between humanities research and data science, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in tracking linguistic change within closely related language systems.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian Languages and Literatures
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bosnian, Serbian and/or Croatian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize image acquisition protocols in radiologic technology, addressing the critical challenge of balancing radiation dose reduction with diagnostic image quality in dynamic clinical scenarios. While modern digital radiography systems offer adjustable technical parameters (e.g., kVp, mAs, filtration), current protocol selection remains largely generalized, failing to account for patient-specific anatomical variability or real-time equipment performance factors. This limitation results in either unnecessary radiation exposure or suboptimal imaging outcomes, particularly in pediatric, geriatric, and trauma populations. We propose developing a machine learning framework trained on multi-source data—including Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport, anthropomorphic phantom measurements, and retrospective clinical image metadata—to generate adaptive, patient-specific exposure protocols. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated radiation dose distribution modeling with deep learning architectures (3D convolutional neural networks and transformer models) to predict optimal technical parameters based on patient body habitus, target anatomy, and equipment-specific modulation characteristics. High-fidelity simulations of over 10,000 virtual patient models will be generated using anatomically variable phantoms constructed from CT-derived datasets. The HPC environment is essential for managing the parallel processing demands of Monte Carlo simulations (using Gate/Geant4), training complex neural networks on terabyte-scale imaging datasets, and performing real-time parameter optimization through hybrid genetic algorithm-particle swarm optimization methods. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model capable of reducing average patient radiation dose by 15-30% while maintaining diagnostic accuracy across diverse populations, as well as an open-source toolkit for protocol optimization adaptable to various digital radiography systems. This interdisciplinary approach bridges medical physics, radiologic science, and computational engineering, advancing precision in medical imaging while addressing core safety and efficacy challenges in modern radiography practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical imaging services to patients and attending health care professionals. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, patient positioning, radiographic technique, radiation biology, safety and emergency procedures, equipment operation and maintenance, quality assurance, patient education, and medical imaging/radiologic services management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern artificial intelligence (AI) models and the demand for their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices present a critical challenge in computer science and engineering. Current approaches to optimizing neural networks for hardware efficiency often rely on iterative, manual design processes or simplified simulations that fail to capture the full heterogeneity of real-world systems. This project seeks to address this gap by developing an automated, hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) framework that integrates computational models of device-specific constraints, such as energy consumption, memory bandwidth, and latency. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a multi-objective optimization pipeline combining evolutionary algorithms, reinforcement learning, and fine-grained hardware simulations to explore vast design spaces efficiently. Key computational challenges include parallelizing architecture evaluations across diverse hardware profiles (e.g., embedded GPUs, FPGAs, and custom accelerators) and scaling simulations to account for dynamic operational environments. The proposed work will utilize distributed computing frameworks to manage large-scale parameter sweeps and employ GPU-accelerated neural network training to reduce search time. Expected outcomes include novel neural architectures optimized for specific edge computing platforms, a publicly available benchmarking suite for hardware-aware AI, and generalized principles for co-designing machine learning models with heterogeneous systems. This research will advance interdisciplinary knowledge in computer science (algorithmic optimization, machine learning) and computer engineering (hardware-software co-design), with applications in IoT, autonomous systems, and real-time analytics. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the project’s computational intensity, including the simultaneous execution of thousands of hardware simulations and the training of candidate models across multiple nodes. Successful implementation will provide a foundation for sustainable AI deployment in edge computing environments while reducing the carbon footprint associated with redundant model development.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens in livestock pose critical challenges to veterinary medicine, food security, and public health. Current diagnostic and surveillance strategies often lack the resolution to predict resistance dynamics across complex microbial communities or model transmission risks at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive frameworks for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in veterinary clinical settings, with a focus on bovine respiratory disease (BRD) in cattle—a leading cause of morbidity and economic loss in the livestock industry. We will integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic profiles) from clinical samples with epidemiological metadata to identify resistance gene networks and host-microbe interactions that drive AMR evolution. Computational workflows will employ machine learning models (e.g., graph neural networks, gradient-boosted decision trees) to classify high-risk resistance phenotypes and prioritize therapeutic targets. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate pathogen transmission under varying herd management practices, enabling the assessment of mitigation strategies. Molecular dynamics simulations will further elucidate structural mechanisms of resistance in key bacterial proteins, guiding the design of novel antimicrobial analogs. The scale of these analyses—spanning terabytes of sequencing data, thousands of simulated herd environments, and nanosecond-resolution protein simulations—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for parallel processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools for AMR emergence in veterinary pathogens, (2) optimized treatment protocols to reduce antimicrobial use, and (3) open-access datasets and models to inform One Health policies. By bridging computational innovation with veterinary clinical needs, this work aims to advance precision livestock medicine while addressing a critical gap in agricultural sustainability.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Sciences/ Veterinary Clinical Sciences, General
cip_definition: An integrated program of study in one or more of the veterinary medical or clinical sciences or a program undifferentiated as to title.

abstract: Epilepsy management remains challenged by the need for precise seizure detection and personalized treatment strategies. Current diagnostic methods, such as manual electroencephalogram (EEG) analysis, are time-consuming and subjective, while treatment selection often relies on trial-and-error due to heterogeneous patient responses. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing computational models that integrate multi-modal neuroimaging, electrophysiological data, and clinical biomarkers to predict seizure dynamics and optimize therapeutic interventions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale EEG datasets (including intracranial and scalp recordings) using machine learning architectures, such as transformer-based networks and graph neural networks, to identify latent patterns associated with seizure onset, propagation, and treatment resistance. Concurrently, we will implement biophysically realistic neural network simulations to model the effects of antiepileptic drugs and neurostimulation protocols across diverse patient-derived cellular parameters. These simulations will be calibrated using Bayesian inference frameworks, requiring parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling across thousands of computational cores. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce model training times from weeks to days, and facilitate ensemble approaches to quantify uncertainty in clinical predictions. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for automated seizure localization, a probabilistic framework for ranking patient-specific treatment efficacy, and openly shared tools for simulating seizure dynamics in silico. This work aims to advance precision medicine in epilepsy by translating computational insights into clinically actionable metrics, potentially reducing diagnostic delays and improving therapeutic outcomes for refractory cases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of patients with epileptic seizures or with symptoms and signs whose differential diagnosis includes epileptic seizures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address analytical and creative challenges in Jazz Studies through computational modeling of improvisational structures, ensemble interaction dynamics, and harmonic complexity. While traditional methods of jazz analysis rely on manual transcription and subjective interpretation, the nonlinear, real-time nature of improvisation and polyphonic ensemble interplay presents a research gap in systematically quantifying these elements at scale. The proposed work will develop machine learning models trained on a curated corpus of jazz recordings spanning blues, swing, bebop, and avant-garde subgenres. These models will identify patterns in melodic contour, rhythmic articulation, and harmonic divergence, enabling the statistical mapping of improvisational vocabularies across historical periods and individual artists. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will model ensemble interactions using multi-agent reinforcement learning frameworks to study emergent properties in collective improvisation. The computational demands of processing high-resolution audio datasets (10,000+ hours), training deep neural networks on temporal sequence data, and running parallelized simulations of interactive performance scenarios necessitate HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for computational jazz analysis, 2) quantitative frameworks for assessing stylistic evolution in improvisational practices, and 3) novel insights into the relationship between preset harmonic structures and spontaneous collective creativity. By bridging computational musicology with jazz pedagogy, this research aims to advance both analytical methodologies and performance practices while preserving the cultural nuances of jazz as an oral tradition. The requested resources will directly support the development of AI-assisted educational tools for improvisation training and contribute to interdisciplinary dialogues between performing arts and computational research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study and master the performance and composition of Jazz. Includes instruction in the history of Jazz and related musical styles such as the Blues, Jazz composition and theory, improvisation, Jazz instrument and ensemble performance, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to simulate and optimize pedagogical strategies for trade and industrial education, addressing the critical need to align vocational training with rapidly evolving industry technologies. Current teacher preparation programs often lack data-driven tools to evaluate the efficacy of hands-on training methods in high-tech environments such as automated manufacturing, smart construction systems, and renewable energy labs. The research problem centers on identifying scalable, adaptive teaching frameworks that bridge theoretical instruction and competency-based skill development in these dynamic settings. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets, including student performance metrics, real-time sensor data from industrial equipment, and behavioral feedback from virtual reality (VR) training simulations. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to model skill acquisition pathways, while agent-based simulations will test the impact of different instructional sequences on learner outcomes under variable resource constraints. The computational workflow will integrate Python-based data pipelines, parallelized optimization routines, and GPU-accelerated VR rendering to evaluate thousands of pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for tailoring trade instruction to regional industry needs, evidence-based guidelines for integrating emerging technologies into vocational curricula, and open-source tools for simulating workshop environments. By quantifying the relationship between instructional design variables and workforce readiness, this work aims to advance the precision and scalability of trade teacher education, directly supporting the development of educators capable of preparing learners for Industry 4.0 challenges. The HPC resources are essential due to the need for large-scale parameter space exploration, real-time data assimilation from distributed IoT devices, and computationally intensive physics-based simulations of industrial processes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational trades and industries programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between chronic stress-induced neuroendocrine signaling and adaptive decision-making processes in the mammalian brain using multiscale computational modeling. Chronic stress disrupts glucocorticoid receptor (GR) signaling and synaptic plasticity across corticolimbic circuits, yet how these molecular and cellular changes propagate to alter network-level computations underlying complex behaviors remains poorly understood. We propose integrating biophysically detailed models of GR-mediated gene regulation, spiking neural network simulations of prefrontal-hippocampal-amygdala circuits, and reinforcement learning frameworks to map stress-induced molecular modifications to behavioral outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for this work, as the research requires (1) large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of GR-DNA interactions under varying cortisol concentrations, (2) parallelized parameter sweeps across 10^4+ neuron network configurations to identify stress-vulnerable circuit motifs, and (3) evolutionary algorithms to optimize multi-omic data integration from transcriptomic profiles of stressed rodent models. The computational pipeline will bridge timescales from milliseconds (ion channel kinetics) to weeks (chronic stress exposure), incorporating experimental data from collaborative electrophysiology and behavioral studies. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific GR phosphorylation patterns to decision-making deficits, identification of critical network hubs for targeted interventions, and validation of novel computational biomarkers of stress resilience. This interdisciplinary approach advances biopsychology by establishing quantitative bridges between molecular neuroendocrinology and systems-level cognitive phenomena, while developing reusable computational tools for analyzing cross-scale interactions in neural systems. The requested resources will enable simulations at biological fidelity levels intractable with conventional computing, directly supporting the development of precision neuropharmacology strategies for stress-related disorders.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological and psychological linkages, especially the linkages between biochemical and biophysical activity and the functioning of the central nervous system.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in precision metal fabrication processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and optimize machining workflows. Traditional machine shop practices rely heavily on iterative trial-and-error approaches for tool path generation, material removal optimization, and thermal deformation mitigation. These methods are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited in their ability to predict complex interactions between cutting tools, workpieces, and environmental factors. To overcome these challenges, this research will employ physics-based computational models to simulate machining operations under diverse conditions. Finite element analysis (FEA) will be used to model stress distributions and thermal gradients during high-speed milling and turning, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate coolant flow and heat dissipation. Machine learning algorithms will further refine predictive models by correlating simulation data with empirical results from physical machining trials. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify optimal combinations of spindle speed, feed rate, and tool geometry for specific material classes, including high-strength alloys and composites. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to minimize material waste, reduce energy consumption, and extend tool life in precision machining applications. The computational tools developed will also support educational objectives by generating interactive visualizations of machining dynamics for instructional use. By integrating HPC-driven insights with practical machine shop operations, this project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical process optimization and real-world manufacturing constraints, benefiting small-scale workshops and industrial partners alike. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation templates and a public dataset of validated machining parameters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and modify metal parts in support of other manufacturing, repair or design activities, or as an independent business.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize operational decision-making in salon and beauty salon management through advanced data-driven modeling and simulation. The beauty industry faces unique challenges in resource allocation, including dynamic customer demand patterns, staff scheduling complexities, and inventory management for perishable cosmetic products. Traditional business management tools often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between aesthetic trends, seasonal demand fluctuations, and service delivery constraints inherent to salon operations. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create a multi-agent simulation environment that models salon ecosystems at unprecedented granularity, incorporating real-world data on customer behavior, stylist productivity metrics, and supply chain variables. The computational approach integrates machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized point-of-sale records, appointment histories, and social media trend data with discrete-event simulations of salon workflows. Key innovations include the development of a novel recommendation system for service bundling optimization and a genetic algorithm framework for adaptive staff rostering. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of forecasting local beauty trends with 85% accuracy over 6-month horizons and decision-support tools that reduce product waste by an estimated 30% through improved inventory predictions. By applying computational intensity to a traditionally non-technical field, this research aims to establish new paradigms for evidence-based beauty business management while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources in service-sector applications. The resulting open-source toolkit will provide small business owners with enterprise-level analytical capabilities, potentially benefiting an industry comprising over 1 million US businesses and $62 billion in annual revenue.
cip_definition: A program that prepares cosmetologists, hairstylists, and other personal grooming specialists to manage beauty parlors, shops, and full-service or specialized salons and to prepare for licensure as professional salon owners and operators.  Includes instruction in cosmetic services marketing and retailing; advertising and promotion; salon management; the cosmetic and salon supply industries; hiring, supervision, and labor relations; applicable business and professional laws and regulations; professional standards and image; and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing electrical systems for safety, efficiency, and reliability in residential, commercial, and industrial settings through advanced computational modeling. As modern electrical infrastructure increasingly incorporates renewable energy sources, smart grid technologies, and variable demand loads, traditional design and fault-detection methods struggle to account for dynamic operational conditions. This research proposes the development of high-fidelity simulations to model complex electrical networks, predict failure points, and evaluate compliance with evolving safety standards (e.g., NEC, IEC). Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate thermal and electromagnetic behavior in wiring systems under peak loads, machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in electrical fault data, and Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic risks in aging infrastructure. Key objectives include creating adaptive models for arc-fault detection, optimizing circuit layouts to minimize energy loss, and quantifying the impact of transient voltages on equipment longevity. The computational workflows will integrate real-world datasets from smart meters, thermal imaging, and historical maintenance records to enhance predictive accuracy. Outcomes will yield open-source tools for electricians to visualize system stress points, prioritize preventive maintenance, and validate designs against virtual stress-test scenarios. By bridging computational engineering with practical electrical work, this research aims to reduce fire risks, improve energy efficiency in mixed-source power systems, and inform updates to training protocols and code compliance frameworks. The scale of data processing and the need for real-time simulation of multi-physics interactions necessitate HPC capabilities to achieve industry-relevant resolution and reliability in results.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain, and repair electric apparatus and systems such as residential, commercial, and industrial electric-power wiring; and DC and AC motors, controls, and electrical distribution panels. Includes instruction in the principles of electronics and electrical systems, wiring, power transmission, safety, industrial and household appliances, job estimation, electrical testing and inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing industrial-scale additive manufacturing (AM) processes through advanced computational modeling and simulation. While AM technologies offer transformative potential for customized production and rapid prototyping, inconsistent part quality due to thermal stress, material anisotropy, and process parameter variability remains a significant barrier to reliable adoption. Current experimental approaches to parameter optimization are resource-intensive and lack the resolution needed to predict localized defects. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate coupled thermal-structural phenomena during metal powder bed fusion processes. The project will implement finite element analysis (FEA) at the macroscale, discrete element method (DEM) for powder dynamics, and phase-field modeling at the microstructural level, with adaptive meshing techniques to bridge scale-dependent interactions. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to identify defect-correlated process signatures and enable real-time parameter optimization. By utilizing parallel computing architectures, we aim to reduce simulation times for complex geometries by 60-70% compared to existing single-scale approaches, while achieving micron-scale resolution in critical regions. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will provide manufacturers with predictive capabilities to minimize post-processing and material waste, directly supporting sustainable manufacturing objectives. Successful implementation will advance fundamental understanding of multi-physics interactions in AM systems while delivering practical frameworks for quality assurance in aerospace tooling, medical device production, and other high-value applications. This work requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning integration and large-memory systems to handle multi-terabyte datasets from coupled simulations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering technologies and engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of persuasive communication in large-scale digital discourse through computational rhetorical analysis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in analyzing multimodal, real-time communication. While existing research has examined rhetorical strategies in static texts or small-group interactions, the proliferation of social media, streaming platforms, and AI-mediated communication necessitates new methods to parse complex, high-volume datasets integrating text, vocal patterns, and visual cues. The central research problem lies in developing scalable models to identify and evaluate rhetorical devices—such as metaphor, narrative framing, and appeals to ethos—across heterogeneous digital media formats, while accounting for contextual factors like audience engagement and cultural resonance. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques with audio-visual feature extraction, utilizing transformer-based architectures fine-tuned on rhetorical theory frameworks. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets (e.g., political livestreams, influencer content, and cross-platform debates) and training of multimodal deep learning models that correlate linguistic patterns with paralinguistic signals (prosody, facial expressions) and real-time audience metrics. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for rhetorical analysis of streaming media, 2) empirical insights into how multimodal persuasion operates in algorithmically mediated environments, and 3) theoretical advancements in digital rhetorical criticism through machine-assisted pattern discovery. This work directly supports the program’s focus on technologically mediated communication by providing scholars with methods to systematically study persuasion at scales and speeds unattainable through manual analysis, while maintaining humanistic engagement with rhetorical meaning. The requested computing infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive multimodal data pipelines and iterative model training, which exceeds the capacity of standard departmental resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific, humanistic, and critical study of human communication in a variety of formats, media, and contexts. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of interpersonal, group, organizational, professional, and intercultural communication; speaking and listening; verbal and nonverbal interaction; rhetorical theory and criticism; performance studies; argumentation and persuasion; technologically mediated communication; popular culture; and various contextual applications.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of diagnosing and optimizing medium/heavy vehicle systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive maintenance and performance modeling. Modern commercial vehicles integrate advanced technologies, including hybrid powertrains, autonomous driving subsystems, and interconnected electronic control units (ECUs), which generate vast datasets. Traditional diagnostic methods struggle to efficiently process this data, leading to unplanned downtime, increased operational costs, and safety risks. This research will develop computational models to predict component failures, optimize maintenance schedules, and simulate system interactions under diverse operational conditions. Using anonymized telemetry data from fleet vehicles—including engine performance metrics, brake system sensor outputs, and HVAC operational logs—we will train machine learning algorithms to identify failure precursors and correlate them with maintenance histories. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets, reducing training times for deep neural networks and ensemble models. Additionally, finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model thermal and mechanical stresses in diesel engines and drivetrain components under extreme loads. These simulations will validate empirical findings and refine predictive thresholds. The expected outcomes include open-source diagnostic algorithms tailored for commercial vehicle technicians, a framework for real-time data analytics in repair workflows, and optimized maintenance protocols that reduce downtime by an estimated 15–20%. By integrating HPC-driven insights into technician training programs, this work will bridge gaps between emerging vehicle technologies and workforce preparedness, fostering safer, more efficient transportation systems. The computational demands of processing high-frequency sensor data and running multiphysics simulations necessitate scalable HPC infrastructure to achieve these objectives within a 12-month timeline.
cip_title: Medium/ Heavy Vehicle and Truck Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the specialized maintenance and repair of trucks, buses, and other commercial and industrial vehicles. Includes instruction in diesel engine mechanics, suspension and steering, brake systems, electrical and electronic systems, preventive maintenance inspections, drive trains, gasoline engine mechanics, HVAC systems, and auxiliary equipment installation and repair.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework for optimizing multi-spectral signature reduction in advanced military platforms, integrating electromagnetic, acoustic, and thermal stealth considerations. Current approaches often address these domains in isolation, leading to suboptimal trade-offs between radar cross-section (RCS) minimization, acoustic dampening, and infrared suppression. The research problem centers on resolving the conflicting material and geometric requirements inherent in multi-signature management, particularly for complex platforms operating in contested environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will implement coupled multi-physics simulations combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) modeling for electromagnetic scattering, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermoacoustic interactions, and machine learning-driven topology optimization. A key innovation involves developing adaptive metamaterial models that dynamically adjust effective permittivity and permeability in response to real-time sensor feeds, requiring massive parameter space exploration. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated solvers for wave propagation analysis across frequency bands (0.1-40 GHz) and integrate experimental material characterization data from anechoic chamber tests via surrogate modeling techniques. Expected outcomes include predictive models for hybrid radar-infrared-acoustic signature trade-offs under diverse operational conditions, optimized conformal coating architectures, and a digital twin framework for evaluating stealth performance in synthetic battle-space environments. This work aims to advance the state of the art in survivability design by enabling concurrent multi-domain signature management, directly supporting next-generation platform development. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the petascale datasets generated by coupled transient simulations and for training neural networks to identify non-intuitive material configurations that balance competing stealth requirements.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of electromagnetic field theory, electro-optics and materials science to the reduction of radar, optical and acoustic signatures of weapons systems. Includes instruction in computational electromagnetics, electro-optics, acoustics, guided wave theory, radiation capture, antenna applications in layered environments, material characterization, radar cross-section analysis, sonar signature analysis, non-destructive testing, remote sensing, and applications to specific weapons systems and operational environments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized neuromuscular rehabilitation protocols through multiscale biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Current rehabilitation strategies for movement disorders (e.g., post-stroke gait impairments or degenerative neuromuscular conditions) often rely on generalized therapeutic frameworks, which inadequately address individual variability in motor control mechanisms, tissue biomechanics, and neural adaptation processes. To overcome this limitation, we propose an integrative computational framework that couples subject-specific musculoskeletal simulations with deep reinforcement learning to optimize rehabilitation outcomes. The research will utilize motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) data from clinical cohorts to construct high-fidelity models of neuromuscular function, incorporating real-time feedback loops between motor neuron activation patterns, muscle-tendon dynamics, and joint-level kinematics. A central computational challenge involves solving inverse dynamics problems across spatiotemporal scales—from milliseconds of neural signaling to weeks of adaptive motor learning—which demands parallelized finite element analysis and GPU-accelerated neural network training. HPC resources will enable the parameterization of stochastic simulations to account for biological variability and the deployment of ensemble machine learning models to predict patient-specific therapeutic responses. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source platform for dynamic rehabilitation protocol design, validated against clinical trial data, and new insights into the neurobiomechanical drivers of motor recovery. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation engineering, offering a paradigm shift toward precision therapeutics in movement disorder management. The requested computing allocation will support large-scale parameter optimization, storage of multimodal patient datasets (>500 TB), and real-time simulation rendering for clinician-end-user validation, which are infeasible with existing institutional resources.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of long-term social change in prehistoric populations through the analysis of large-scale spatiotemporal datasets, with a focus on settlement patterns, material culture distributions, and environmental interactions. The central challenge lies in processing and modeling complex, multidimensional archaeological records spanning millennia, which require computational capacities beyond standard workstations. Our team will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based models simulating population mobility and resource-use strategies under variable climatic conditions, paired with machine learning approaches to detect subtle patterns in artifact assemblages and site distributions. Spatial analyses integrating geographic information systems (GIS) data with radiocarbon-dated settlement records will reconstruct regional interaction networks, while Bayesian statistical frameworks will assess chronological uncertainties at scale. These methods demand parallel processing capabilities and substantial memory allocation due to the iterative nature of simulations involving >10^6 agent decisions per run and the processing of terabyte-scale lidar and multispectral imaging datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying previously unrecognized thresholds in settlement system resilience, modeling the feedback between ecological carrying capacity and social organization, and testing hypotheses about the pace of cultural transmission under resource stress. The project will generate open-access tools for archaeological simulation and geospatial analysis, advancing methodological integration in computational anthropology. Results will contribute to theoretical debates about human-environment coevolution while providing scalable frameworks for analyzing fragmentary, time-averaged datasets common in social science research. By leveraging HPC infrastructure, this work addresses critical gaps in studying societal complexity at intergenerational timescales, with implications for understanding modern challenges related to sustainable resource use and collective decision-making.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Anthropology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Secondary school administrators face complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, operational efficiency, and student outcomes amidst dynamic enrollment patterns, budgetary constraints, and evolving policy requirements. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model multi-variable scenarios or simulate long-term impacts of administrative strategies. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze district- and school-level administrative data, enabling evidence-based policy design for secondary school leadership. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will build agent-based models simulating student population dynamics, staff deployment patterns, and facility utilization across diverse urban and rural school systems. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical datasets—including enrollment trends, academic performance metrics, and community demographic shifts—to identify predictive relationships between resource allocation decisions and educational outcomes. Computational experiments will evaluate hypothetical interventions such as redistricting, extracurricular program expansion, and crisis response protocols under varying socioeconomic conditions. The scale of analysis requires parallel processing to manage high-dimensional data from 10+ partner school districts, encompassing 500,000+ student records and longitudinal operational metrics. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking specific administrative actions to graduation rates and equity indicators, (2) optimized decision-support tools for principals facing budget reallocation or infrastructure planning challenges, and (3) policy recommendations for scalable interventions that balance academic priorities with fiscal responsibility. By quantifying the systemic impacts of leadership decisions, this work advances computational approaches in education administration while directly addressing the National Educational Leadership Preparation (NELP) standards for data-driven school improvement. The requested HPC resources will enable previously infeasible large-scale simulations critical for generalizing findings across institutional contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the junior high, secondary, or senior high school (7-12) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of secondary schools. Includes instruction in secondary school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance physics teacher preparation by addressing the challenge of integrating computational modeling and data-driven pedagogy into physics education curricula. Many pre-service physics educators lack exposure to high-performance computing (HPC) tools, limiting their ability to design instruction that leverages modern computational methods or contextualizes complex physics concepts through simulation. To bridge this gap, we propose developing and testing a scalable suite of interactive, curriculum-aligned computational physics modules optimized for HPC environments. These modules will simulate phenomena such as quantum wavefunction behavior, many-body gravitational interactions, and thermodynamic systems under non-ideal conditions—topics often taught abstractly due to experimental or mathematical barriers. The research will employ GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulations, finite element analysis for electromagnetic field visualization, and machine learning algorithms to automate the generation of customizable, grade-appropriate visualization outputs. By running these workflows on HPC clusters, we will enable pre-service teachers to parametrically explore physical systems in real time during lesson development exercises, fostering deeper pedagogical content knowledge. Outcomes will be evaluated through pre/post assessments of 120 teacher candidates’ computational pedagogical skills and analyses of lesson plans created using the modules. The project aims to establish a replicable framework for embedding HPC-driven inquiry in physics teacher education, directly addressing the Next Generation Science Standards’ emphasis on computational thinking. Successful implementation will provide open-access resources to help future physics educators harness advanced computing tools, ultimately improving secondary students’ engagement with computationally intensive STEM concepts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between urban soundscapes and community well-being through a spatial-analytical lens, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex geosocial interactions. While noise pollution is widely studied in environmental sciences, its socio-spatial inequities—how marginalized populations disproportionately experience harmful acoustic environments—remain under-quantified in social science frameworks. This research addresses this gap by integrating georeferenced sound sensor data, demographic records, and participatory community noise assessments to analyze spatial patterns of acoustic exposure across diverse urban neighborhoods. The computational approach employs geospatial machine learning models to identify latent relationships between soundscape characteristics (e.g., decibel variability, frequency profiles) and socio-demographic variables, while agent-based modeling simulates how policy interventions (e.g., zoning changes, green infrastructure) might alter exposure disparities. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of audio data from distributed IoT sensors, training deep learning architectures on spectrogram representations, and running Monte Carlo simulations across high-resolution urban grids. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating soundscape justice in urban planning contexts, predictive maps of at-risk populations, and policy-relevant metrics for equitable noise mitigation. By centering geography’s integrative capacity to bridge physical measurements and social dynamics, this work advances methodological innovation in spatial justice research while contributing empirical insights to emerging discourses on sensory equity—a niche intersecting human geography, urban informatics, and public health. The computational outputs will be disseminated through interactive spatial dashboards for community stakeholders and open-source tools for replicating the analytical pipeline in other cities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the spatial distribution and interrelationships of people, natural resources, plant and animal life. Includes instruction in historical and political geography, cultural geography, economic and physical geography, regional science, cartographic methods, remote sensing, spatial analysis, and applications to areas such as land-use planning, development studies, and analyses of specific countries, regions, and resources.
