abstract: Traditional building inspection methodologies often depend on manual evaluations and post-construction assessments, limiting their ability to predict structural vulnerabilities proactively. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model building performance under multifactorial stressors, enabling predictive inspection workflows. The research will utilize parallelized finite element analysis to simulate structural responses to seismic activity, thermal cycling, and material fatigue across diverse construction typologies. Machine learning models, trained on heterogeneous datasets encompassing decades of inspection reports, LiDAR scans, and environmental sensor data, will identify latent risk factors correlated with code violations or premature degradation. HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale datasets and iterating complex multiphysics simulations that account for regional building code variations. The computational pipeline will automate compliance verification against evolving standards (e.g., International Building Code updates) while generating probabilistic failure forecasts for infrastructure portfolios. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source risk prioritization toolkit for inspectors, validated through case studies on hurricane-prone coastal structures and aging urban high-rises. By transforming inspection protocols from reactive checklists to predictive systems, this work aims to reduce construction-related accidents by 15-20% within a decade while optimizing maintenance budgets. The project further contributes to academic curricula by creating modular training modules on computational inspection techniques, bridging the gap between traditional trade skills and data science competencies in vocational education programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply industrial, labor, and governmental standards and laws to the oversight of construction projects and the maintenance of completed buildings and other structures. Includes instruction in construction processes and techniques, materials analysis, occupational safety and health, industry standards, building codes and specifications, blueprint interpretation, testing equipment and procedures, communication skills, accident investigation, and documentation.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in modeling nonlinear optical wave propagation in disordered media, a problem central to advancing ultrafast laser applications and topological photonic systems. Current analytical approaches struggle to predict light-matter interaction dynamics in systems with engineered disorder, particularly when combining high-intensity pulsed excitation, nonlocal nonlinearities, and wavelength-scale heterogeneities. This project will implement a hybrid computational framework integrating stochastic Maxwell-Bloch equations with machine learning-accelerated parameter optimization to simulate femtosecond-scale pulse evolution in three-dimensional disordered optical structures. The numerical approach combines finite-difference time-domain methods for electromagnetic propagation with tensor network representations of quantum optical states, enabling simultaneous tracking of classical field dynamics and photon statistics. High-performance computing resources are essential for resolving sub-cycle temporal features (< 0.1 fs) while maintaining micron-scale spatial resolution across macroscopic propagation distances (up to 10^4 wavelengths). Key deliverables include open-source software for predicting nonlinear susceptibility saturation effects in amorphous optical metamaterials and identifying disorder configurations that enhance broadband supercontinuum generation. Expected outcomes will provide fundamental insights into noise-mediated soliton formation mechanisms and enable the design of novel optical limiting devices with tailored nonlinear responses. The research directly supports experimental efforts to develop compact mid-infrared frequency combs and robust all-optical signal processing architectures. By establishing scalable computational methods for multiscale nonlinear optics problems, this work will accelerate innovation in laser engineering and quantum photonics while addressing critical gaps between nanoscale light localization theories and device-scale performance prediction. The resulting datasets and algorithms will be disseminated to advance community capabilities in modeling extreme nonlinear optical phenomena.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of light energy, including its structure, properties and behavior under different conditions. Includes instruction in wave theory, wave mechanics, electromagnetic theory, physical optics, geometric optics, quantum theory of light, photon detecting, laser theory, wall and beam properties, chaotic light, non-linear optics, harmonic generation, optical systems theory, and applications to engineering problems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing personalized care protocols delivered by health aides in non-clinical settings, such as home-based and community care. Health aides routinely collect multimodal data—including biometric readings, behavioral observations, and environmental metrics—during patient interactions, but current practices lack tools to dynamically synthesize these data into actionable insights. The computational challenge lies in integrating sparse, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., wearable sensor streams, qualitative notes, and temporal activity logs) to model patient-specific risks for acute health events, such as falls or delirium, which are often preventable with timely intervention. We propose a hybrid machine learning architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model relational dependencies between care activities and physiological parameters, and transformer-based models to process natural language documentation from aides. The HPC environment will enable large-scale simulation of care scenarios, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and real-time inference testing across synthetic and real-world datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predicting patient deterioration trajectories and generating context-aware care recommendations, validated through retrospective analysis of historical aide-collected data. By bridging gaps between frontline care documentation and computational precision health tools, this work aims to empower health aides with predictive analytics capabilities, ultimately reducing preventable adverse events in vulnerable populations. The project’s computational demands—particularly in training multi-modal models and simulating high-dimensional care pathways—necessitate scalable GPU clusters and parallelized data processing pipelines, which are central to the resource allocation request.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate advanced computational methods with traditional drawing practices to investigate the dynamic interplay between manual artistic techniques and generative digital processes. While traditional drawing emphasizes tactile media and embodied skill, contemporary tools increasingly rely on algorithmic assistance, raising questions about how computational systems can augment—rather than replace—the nuances of hand-drawn expression. The research problem centers on developing a scalable framework to simulate and analyze the biomechanical, perceptual, and aesthetic dimensions of drawing techniques, enabling systematic study of how tools, materials, and gestures influence artistic outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for modeling complex variables, including stroke dynamics, pigment dispersion in mixed media, and real-time feedback systems for generative art tools. Computational methods will involve agent-based modeling of drawing gestures, GPU-accelerated rendering of layered media interactions, and machine learning analysis of stylistic patterns across historical and experimental datasets. By simulating material behaviors (e.g., charcoal friction, ink fluid dynamics) at high spatial-temporal resolutions, the project aims to establish predictive models linking physical processes to visual outcomes. A secondary focus involves training neural networks on curated datasets of hand-drawn works to identify latent features correlating with artistic intent and viewer perception. Outcomes will include open-source tools for artists and educators to visualize technique impacts iteratively, fostering deeper engagement with both traditional and computational media. The work advances interdisciplinary research in computational aesthetics while preserving material-specific knowledge often lost in digital art pipelines. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges gaps between embodied artistic practice and data-driven innovation, offering new methodologies for creative expression and digital conservation in the visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions through representation by lines made on a surface. Includes instruction in eye-hand coordination; line, value, shape, and perspective; figure and still life drawing; the use of media such as pen and ink, pencil, charcoal, pastel, and brush; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of catalytic reaction systems critical to sustainable chemical manufacturing by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Industrial catalysts, essential for processes such as hydrocarbon reforming and carbon capture, often suffer from inefficiencies due to poorly understood atomic-scale active sites and dynamic reactor-scale transport limitations. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve these multi-scale interactions, while conventional computational models lack the fidelity to capture coupled reaction-transport phenomena across relevant spatiotemporal scales. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC), and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Atomic-level reaction pathways and activation energies will be derived via DFT, feeding into kMC models to predict catalyst surface kinetics under realistic temperature and pressure conditions. These results will inform reactor-scale CFD simulations incorporating turbulent flow, heat transfer, and species transport. Machine learning surrogates will accelerate parameter optimization across scales. The computational intensity of this approach—particularly the need for large-scale DFT ensembles and 3D transient CFD simulations—necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing and high memory bandwidth. Expected outcomes include identifying catalyst compositions with improved activity and selectivity for methane dry reforming, optimizing reactor geometries to minimize mass transfer limitations, and reducing energy consumption by 15–20% in benchmark systems. This work will provide foundational insights into bridging atomic-scale mechanisms with industrial reactor performance, directly supporting decarbonization goals in chemical production. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required simulation throughput and resolution, enabling predictive models that guide experimental validation and scale-up.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems employing chemical processes, such as chemical reactors, kinetic systems, electrochemical systems, energy conservation processes, heat and mass transfer systems, and separation processes; and the applied analysis of chemical problems such as corrosion, particle abrasion, energy loss, pollution, and fluid mechanics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into the design and evaluation of adaptive outdoor education curricula, focusing on optimizing safety, participant engagement, and environmental stewardship. Outdoor education programs face challenges in balancing experiential learning outcomes with dynamic environmental conditions, group dynamics, and risk variables. Traditional program design relies heavily on heuristic frameworks and static risk assessments, which may not account for real-time ecological shifts or nuanced participant interactions. This research addresses these limitations by developing computational models to simulate outdoor education scenarios, leveraging HPC resources to analyze multi-dimensional datasets spanning environmental sensor data, biometric feedback from participants, historical incident reports, and geospatial variables. Agent-based modeling will simulate group behavior under varying conditions (e.g., weather extremes, terrain complexity), while machine learning algorithms will identify patterns linking instructional strategies to learning outcomes and risk profiles. A key innovation involves synthesizing ecological impact metrics with pedagogical efficacy, enabling the creation of curricula that minimize environmental disruption while maximizing skill acquisition. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of high-resolution geospatial datasets and real-time parameter adjustments to model scenarios such as backcountry navigation, wilderness first response, and group conflict resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for outdoor educators, predictive risk-assessment modules, and evidence-based frameworks for dynamically adapting programs to ecological and social variables. By bridging computational analytics with experiential education theory, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision-making in outdoor education, enhancing both safety protocols and the ecological sustainability of field-based learning.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work as an educator, instructor or facilitator in parks, recreational facilities, camps and other outdoor settings. Includes instruction in leadership skills, wilderness survival skills, first aid, group processes, counseling techniques, environmental studies and instruction in recreational activities such as rock climbing, ropes courses, backpacking, kayaking and canoeing.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in real-time, immersive spatial audio processing for interactive music performances and installations. Current systems for 3D sound spatialization and dynamic audio synthesis struggle to maintain low latency and high fidelity in complex acoustic environments, particularly when integrating live inputs, adaptive machine learning models, and multi-channel spatial rendering. The research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to enable real-time processing of heterogeneous audio streams, leveraging parallelized algorithms for wave field synthesis, ambisonic encoding, and neural networks for timbral transformation. By deploying GPU-accelerated spatial audio engines and distributed computing architectures, the project aims to overcome bottlenecks in processing latency and scalability, enabling precise control of sound localization, diffusion, and spectral manipulation in dynamic performance contexts. The computational workflow will integrate physical modeling of acoustic environments, machine learning-based sound synthesis, and interactive parameter optimization, requiring access to HPC resources for large-scale simulations, training of deep learning models on high-dimensional audio datasets, and stress-testing real-time performance under variable load conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive spatial audio rendering, novel methodologies for integrating AI-driven synthesis with live performance systems, and benchmarks for computational efficiency in interactive music applications. This work will advance the technical foundations of immersive music experiences, with implications for live electronic music, virtual reality sound design, and audience-centered auditory environments. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the project’s goals, as existing local infrastructure cannot support the concurrent demands of large-scale neural network training, multi-channel audio processing, and real-time interactive latency thresholds below 10ms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creative aspects of the blending of music and technology; and that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the composition, recording, synthesis, and performance of music; audio-visual production; scoring for film and multimedia; and software and multimedia development. Includes instruction in music theory, music history, composition, acoustics, recording technology, computer composition, electronic music synthesis, technology-based performance, 3D sound and spatial audio, and music business and law.

abstract: Blood banking and transfusion medicine face critical challenges in ensuring the safety, efficacy, and equitable availability of blood products, particularly as demand grows for complex component therapies and personalized transfusion strategies. A key bottleneck lies in predicting the functional integrity of blood components during storage, as biochemical and biophysical degradation (e.g., red blood cell membrane fragility, platelet activation) directly impacts transfusion outcomes. Current quality assessment methods are reactive and lack the resolution to forecast time-dependent changes in blood products under variable storage conditions. This project proposes a computational framework to model the dynamic degradation of blood components, integrating multi-omics data, donor variability, and storage protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of cellular membrane stability under stress conditions, coupled with machine learning models trained on longitudinal metabolomic and proteomic datasets from >10,000 blood units. These models will predict degradation trajectories for individual donor units, optimizing inventory management and reducing waste. Additionally, finite element modeling of blood component transport in transfusion devices will identify design modifications to minimize shear-induced cellular damage. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized simulation workflows and distributed training of neural networks on heterogeneous datasets. Outcomes will include predictive tools for blood bank decision support, validated against clinical transfusion efficacy data, and protocols for personalized component selection in high-risk recipients. This work addresses a critical gap in transfusion science by transitioning from static, population-based storage guidelines to dynamic, unit-specific quality monitoring, directly enhancing the safety of blood products and operational efficiency of blood supply chains. Successful implementation will inform regulatory standards and reduce adverse transfusion events, particularly in resource-limited settings where supply constraints exacerbate clinical risks.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians for the maintenance of an adequate blood supply, blood donor and patient-recipient safety, and appropriate blood utilization. Includes directing the preparation and safe use of specially prepared blood components, including red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma constituents, and marrow or stem cells for transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing hydrocarbon recovery from complex subsurface reservoirs through advanced computational modeling of multiphase fluid dynamics in fractured geological systems. Traditional reservoir simulation tools struggle to accurately capture the interplay of fluid flow, geomechanical stress, and fracture propagation at field-relevant scales, particularly in unconventional reservoirs with heterogeneous rock properties. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity, parallelized numerical framework that integrates finite element methods for geomechanics with volume-of-fluid (VOF) multiphase flow simulations. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve millimeter-to-kilometer spatial scales through adaptive mesh refinement and parallel processing across thousands of cores. Machine learning techniques will be embedded to accelerate parameter calibration using historical production data and real-time sensor inputs from distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) systems. The project will validate models against experimental data from hydraulic fracturing test beds and field measurements from partner oil and gas operators. Expected outcomes include predictive tools capable of simulating reservoir behavior with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, enabling operators to optimize well placement, fracturing strategies, and production schedules. This work directly supports the sustainable development of hydrocarbon resources by reducing operational risks, minimizing environmental footprint through precision engineering, and extending the productive life of mature reservoirs. The computational framework will be made available as open-source software to advance research capabilities across mining and petroleum engineering disciplines. Successful implementation requires access to HPC infrastructure capable of handling petascale simulations, including GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning workflows and high-memory nodes for large-scale geomechanical calculations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mining and petroleum engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize material selection, installation processes, and long-term performance of carpet, tile, and flooring systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Traditional approaches to flooring installation rely heavily on empirical guidelines and manual testing, which often fail to account for complex interactions between material properties, environmental conditions, and structural dynamics. This limitation leads to inefficiencies in labor, material waste, and suboptimal durability in real-world settings. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation platform integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model the mechanical behavior of flooring materials under diverse stressors (e.g., moisture, thermal expansion, foot traffic). HPC resources will enable parametric studies of material combinations (e.g., adhesives, subfloor composites) across thousands of simulated environmental scenarios, while ML algorithms trained on these datasets will predict optimal installation parameters for specific site conditions. Additionally, the project will develop digital twins of common flooring failure modes, such as tile cracking or adhesive degradation, to inform preventative maintenance strategies. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from industry partners, including stress tests and environmental chamber trials. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of material performance metrics, predictive tools for installation planning, and interactive training modules for workers to visualize stress distributions and failure risks in virtual environments. By bridging computational engineering with trade-specific challenges, this work aims to reduce material waste by 15–20%, extend flooring system lifespans, and improve safety standards in the industry through data-driven decision support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, prepare, install, and repair carpet; linoleum; vinyl; ceramic, marble, quarry, mosaic, and terrazzo tiles; and wood materials on floors, walls, and stairs. Includes instruction in measuring, cutting, and installing materials; use of hand and power-operated equipment; estimation of material and labor costs; and safety training.

abstract: The management of chronic diseases in adult populations presents significant challenges due to the complex interplay of physiological, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors influencing patient outcomes. Current approaches to risk stratification and personalized care planning in adult health nursing often lack the precision required to address this complexity, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and preventable hospital readmissions. This project proposes the development of a predictive computational framework to optimize care strategies for adults with chronic conditions, such as heart failure or diabetes, by integrating multi-modal patient data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), including clinical measurements, medication adherence patterns, and social determinants of health, alongside longitudinal outcomes data. Machine learning models, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, will be trained to identify high-risk patients, predict decompensation events, and simulate the impact of tailored nursing interventions. Computational demands arise from the need to process heterogeneous datasets encompassing millions of data points across diverse patient cohorts while maintaining temporal resolution for trend analysis. The HPC environment will enable parallelized model training, hyperparameter optimization, and sensitivity analyses to ensure robustness across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that quantifies individualized risk profiles and recommends evidence-based care pathways. This work will advance nursing practice by providing data-driven methods to prioritize interventions, reduce avoidable hospitalizations, and allocate clinical resources more effectively. By bridging computational science and nursing research, the project aims to establish scalable frameworks for personalized adult healthcare while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in health informatics. Successful implementation will require dedicated GPU nodes and high-memory computing infrastructure to handle the computational intensity of multi-task learning architectures and large-scale simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide general care for adult patients. Includes instruction in adult primary care, adult pathophysiology, clinical management of medication and treatments, patient assessment and education, patient referral, and planning adult health maintenance programs.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interplay between multinational corporate tax strategies and evolving global tax regulations, with a focus on real-time scenario analysis under uncertainty. The increasing complexity of international tax systems—driven by initiatives like the OECD’s Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework and country-specific digital services taxes—has created a critical need for advanced tools to evaluate the fiscal and operational impacts of tax policy shifts on cross-border enterprises. Traditional analytical methods struggle to account for the combinatorial scale of jurisdictional rules, transfer pricing mechanisms, and transient market conditions, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-actor decision-making in stochastic environments. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate corporations, subsidiaries, and regulatory bodies as autonomous agents interacting within a parameter space defined by real-world tax codes, macroeconomic variables, and probabilistic policy changes. Monte Carlo methods will be integrated to assess risk exposure under diverse regulatory futures, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will map profit allocation networks across jurisdictions. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized optimization algorithms to identify tax-efficient operational configurations under constraints such as anti-avoidance laws and supply chain dependencies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating tax policy impacts at scale, validated against historical case studies involving pillar-two global minimum tax implementations. This work aims to advance computational taxation as a distinct interdisciplinary domain, providing actionable insights for policymakers designing adaptive tax regimes and corporations navigating compliance in volatile regulatory landscapes. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, iterative multi-agent simulations, and memory-intensive optimization tasks requiring GPU-accelerated compute nodes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide tax advice and management services to individuals and corporations. Includes instruction in tax law and regulations, tax record systems, individual and corporate income taxation, tax planning, partnerships and fiduciary relationships, estates and trusts, property depreciation, capital gains and losses, dispositions, transfers, liquidity, valuation, and applications to specific tax problems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of therapeutic regimens in veterinary medicine, driven by interspecies variability in drug metabolism and disease pathophysiology, necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize drug dosing and minimize adverse effects. Current pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models often fail to account for the dynamic interplay between species-specific physiological parameters, genetic polymorphisms in drug-metabolizing enzymes, and comorbidities prevalent in domesticated animals. This project proposes the development of multi-scale computational models integrating species-specific physiological data, pharmacogenomic profiles, and drug-receptor interaction dynamics to predict individualized dosing strategies for veterinary patients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the construction of population PK/PD models using Bayesian hierarchical methods and machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records from companion animals (canines, felines, equines) and pharmacokinetic data from controlled trials. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will characterize interspecies differences in drug-target binding affinities, while finite element modeling will simulate drug distribution in anatomically accurate tissue compartments. The computational framework will be validated against retrospective clinical datasets and prospectively tested through in vitro assays measuring drug clearance pathways across species. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dose individualization in patients with renal/hepatic impairment, protocols for therapeutic drug monitoring in critical care settings, and mechanistic insights into species-dependent adverse drug reactions. By leveraging HPC capabilities to manage complex parameter spaces and perform real-time optimizations, this work aims to establish a translational bridge between experimental pharmacology and clinical decision-making in veterinary practice. The resulting computational tools will be disseminated as open-access resources to support evidence-based drug therapy optimization across veterinary specialties, with potential applications in comparative translational medicine.
cip_definition: Research on how to apply advanced knowledge of the chemical properties and biological effects of drugs to rational drug therapy in animal patients. Includes instruction in the comparative pharmacology of principal drug groups, pharmacokinetics, basic mechanisms and features of diseases occurring in domesticated animals, the role of drugs in modifying the disease process, and specific skills critical to the practice of clinical pharmacology.

abstract: This project seeks to address computational challenges in estimating high-dimensional psychometric models, which are critical for advancing measurement precision in psychological research. Contemporary test construction and validation increasingly rely on complex models, such as multidimensional item response theory (MIRT) and cognitive diagnostic models (CDMs), to capture nuanced interactions between latent traits and item responses. However, parameter estimation for these models involves computationally intensive procedures, including high-dimensional integration and iterative optimization, which strain conventional computing resources. Existing software tools often employ approximations or restrictive assumptions to mitigate these demands, potentially compromising accuracy and limiting scalability. This project proposes the development and validation of parallelized Bayesian estimation algorithms optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to overcome these bottlenecks. The computational approach will leverage Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods with adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) samplers, implemented using distributed computing frameworks to enable efficient scaling across thousands of cores. Key steps include (1) simulating large-scale datasets reflecting realistic educational and psychological assessment scenarios, (2) benchmarking computational efficiency and parameter recovery against existing estimation methods, and (3) extending models to incorporate hierarchical structures for cross-population measurement invariance testing. The requested HPC resources will support intensive simulations (>100,000 CPU-hours) and empirical applications to national assessment datasets with complex sampling designs. Successful implementation will yield open-source software tools for scalable psychometric modeling, directly addressing methodological gaps in handling large respondent populations and high-dimensional latent structures. Outcomes will enhance researchers’ capacity to rigorously validate assessments while reducing computational barriers to cutting-edge quantitative techniques, with broad implications for educational testing, personality measurement, and behavioral research. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on advancing statistical methodologies for psychological science through innovative computational solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making in juvenile corrections systems by modeling the dynamic interplay of behavioral, environmental, and institutional factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. Despite advances in correctional practices, juvenile facilities often rely on static risk-assessment tools that fail to account for real-time behavioral data, situational stressors, or the heterogeneous needs of youth populations. This gap limits the ability to allocate resources effectively or predict the long-term impacts of intervention strategies. To address this, we propose an agent-based simulation platform that integrates individual-level psychological profiles, facility-specific operational constraints, and longitudinal recidivism data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the stochasticity and scalability required for these simulations, which will model thousands of synthetic agents across diverse demographic and behavioral categories. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibration and validation datasets derived from anonymized records of 15,000 juvenile cases, including behavioral logs, educational progress metrics, and post-release outcomes. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about the efficacy of targeted staffing allocations, therapeutic programming schedules, and crisis response protocols under varying resource constraints. The resulting models aim to identify cost-effective policy adjustments that reduce recidivism while maintaining facility safety. By bridging computational social science with correctional practice, this work will provide juvenile justice administrators with evidence-based tools to prioritize interventions for high-need individuals and simulate the systemic effects of resource reallocation before implementation. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation software adaptable to regional correctional contexts and a policy whiteboard outlining computational best practices for non-specialist stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to specialize in the provision of correction services to underage minor populations. Includes instruction in corrections, juvenile delinquency, juvenile development and psychology, juvenile law and justice administration, social services, record-keeping procedures, and communication skills.

abstract: This project investigates the historical evolution of educational ideologies and their relationship to societal change through computational analysis of large-scale textual corpora. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how shifting philosophical paradigms in education—such as progressivism, perennialism, and critical pedagogy—intersect with sociopolitical transformations across different historical periods and cultural contexts. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will analyze multilingual educational documents spanning 1850–2020, including policy papers, pedagogical treatises, and institutional archives from 15 countries. Advanced natural language processing techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic analysis and cross-lingual embeddings, will be employed to trace conceptual diffusion and adaptation patterns. Computational hermeneutics methods will facilitate the systematic interpretation of normative values embedded in educational discourses, while graph neural networks will model the transnational flow of educational ideas through institutional networks. The scale of analysis—processing over 10 million pages of text with temporal, geographic, and linguistic dimensions—requires distributed computing capabilities for efficient data processing and model training. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel computational framework for analyzing educational philosophy as a sociocultural phenomenon, 2) empirical insights into how specific historical events (e.g., decolonization movements, globalization) reshaped educational priorities, and 3) open-access visualization tools enabling humanistic scholars to explore complex relationships between educational theories and material social conditions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges qualitative educational research with computational social science, offering new methodological pathways for investigating education's role in societal reproduction and transformation.
cip_title: Social and Philosophical Foundations of Education
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of education as a social and cultural institution, and the educational process as an object of humanistic inquiry. Includes instruction in such subjects as the philosophy of education, history of education, educational literature, educational anthropology, sociology of education, economics and politics of education, educational policy studies, and studies of education in relation to specific populations, issues, social phenomena, and types of work.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of identity formation and cultural resilience within diasporic communities through the analysis of large-scale multilingual textual and multimedia archives. The research problem centers on understanding how intersectional identities—shaped by ethnicity, gender, and cultural hybridity—are negotiated and sustained across generations in contexts of displacement and digital globalization. Current methodologies in cultural studies often rely on qualitative close readings of limited datasets, which struggle to capture longitudinal patterns or transnational discursive networks at scale. To address this gap, we propose deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze over 15 terabytes of digitized community records, oral histories, social media interactions, and visual art collections from three diasporic groups over a 50-year period. Computational methods will include multilingual natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for sentiment and thematic analysis, network modeling of cross-cultural influence, and machine learning-assisted visual pattern recognition in multimedia artifacts. These techniques will enable the identification of previously underexamined correlations between linguistic shifts, visual symbolism, and sociopolitical events across spatial and temporal boundaries. The project expects to generate three key outcomes: 1) an open-access computational framework for analyzing intersectional identity in cultural archives, 2) new theoretical models of cultural adaptation that account for digital mediation’s role in diasporic memory practices, and 3) evidence-based recommendations for preserving intangible cultural heritage in digitization initiatives. By scaling interpretive methods while maintaining critical engagement with cultural specificity, this work aims to advance computational humanities approaches within interdisciplinary ethnic and gender studies. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing non-Latin script datasets, training custom transformer models for low-resource languages, and conducting multimodal analyses that integrate text, image, and temporal data streams.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Area, Ethnic, Cultural, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in area, ethnic, cultural, gender, or group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models for optimizing prosthetic and cosmetic application workflows in professional makeup artistry. Current methods for integrating temporary prosthetics—such as those used in film, clinical camouflage, or theatrical contexts—rely heavily on manual trial and error, leading to inefficiencies in material selection, adhesion durability, and aesthetic realism under dynamic conditions (e.g., temperature changes, movement, or prolonged wear). The research problem centers on the lack of predictive tools to simulate how prosthetic materials interact with human skin topography, sweat secretion, and environmental stressors, which limits both creative possibilities and clinical outcomes. To address this, the project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining 3D biomechanical modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate sweat dispersion and adhesive degradation, and machine learning (ML) to analyze texture-matching algorithms across diverse skin tones and lighting environments. High-resolution scans of facial geometries and material property datasets will inform finite element analysis (FEA) models, while ML frameworks will train on spectral reflectance data to predict optimal pigment blends for prosthetics. The HPC environment is critical for parallel processing of large-scale simulations, real-time rendering of dynamic interactions, and iterative training of ML models. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-access computational tools to streamline prosthetic design, reduce application time by 30–50% in test cases, and improve durability under simulated stressors. This work bridges gaps between aesthetic practice, material science, and computational engineering, offering novel methodologies for an underserved domain. By enabling data-driven decision-making in makeup artistry, the project aims to enhance accessibility to high-fidelity prosthetics in medical and low-resource entertainment contexts while establishing a framework for computational innovation in non-traditional STEM fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally apply cosmetic makeup preparations and perform complete and specialized appearance makeovers including hairdressing, wig work, masking, temporary prosthesis applications, cosmetic applications, and related costuming for leisure or for professional stage, camera, clinical, or security purposes.  Includes instruction in period and contemporary hairstyling and costuming; wig work and hairpiece application; synthetic hair and masks; cosmetic preparations and treatments; makeup artistry; attachment, removal, and camouflaging of prostheses; health and safety; client consultation and care; pre- and post-production operations; set and crew conduct and relations; script, instruction, and prescription interpretation; labor relations; and business practices.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of mechanobiological signaling in extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated intercellular communication during fibrotic disease progression. Fibrosis, characterized by pathological tissue stiffening, is a hallmark of chronic diseases in multiple organs, yet the molecular mechanisms linking mechanical cues to EV cargo sorting and recipient cell responses remain poorly understood. This project integrates computational modeling and machine learning to analyze how substrate stiffness modulates EV biogenesis, cargo composition, and functional uptake in stromal-epithelial cell networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of membrane curvature proteins (e.g., syndapins, ESCRT complexes) under varying mechanical stress conditions, coupled with stochastic modeling of EV trafficking in 3D multicellular environments. Experimental datasets—including atomic force microscopy-derived tissue stiffness maps, single-EV proteomics, and live-cell imaging of EV transfer—will parameterize and validate the models. Machine learning pipelines will identify stiffness-sensitive EV cargo clusters predictive of fibrotic progression using multi-omic datasets from patient-derived matrices. The computational framework aims to predict mechanoresponsive EV signatures that drive fibroblast activation or epithelial-mesenchymal transition, with validation via in silico perturbation of key mechanotransduction pathways (e.g., YAP/TAZ, integrin-ECM interactions). This work will establish a first-of-its-kind platform to simulate EV-mediated mechanosignaling across scales, from molecular interactions to tissue-level network behaviors. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into fibrosis propagation, predictive biomarkers for early detection, and in silico screening of anti-fibrotic therapies targeting EV dysregulation. By bridging mechanobiology, computational biophysics, and translational EV research, this project addresses an unmet need in molecular medicine, offering novel strategies to disrupt fibrosis through mechano-informed therapeutic design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the molecular and cellular basis of disease, and the application of this knowledge to the development of new clinical and diagnostic tools, medications, and therapies. Includes instruction in cell biology, molecular biology, physiology, pharmacology, biochemistry, genetics, pathology, molecular immunology, research and quantitative methods, and biomedical research computing.

abstract: The therapeutic mechanisms underlying hypnotherapy remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of standardized protocols and objective outcome measures. Current neuroimaging and behavioral studies generate complex, high-dimensional datasets that challenge conventional analytical methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neurophysiological correlates of hypnotic trance states and their relationship to therapeutic efficacy. Multimodal data—including high-density EEG, functional MRI, and real-time behavioral metrics—will be collected from participants undergoing clinically administered hypnotherapy sessions. Computational pipelines will integrate signal processing, dynamic network modeling, and machine learning to identify state-specific neural signatures and predictors of individual susceptibility. HPC capabilities will enable large-scale parallel processing of neuroimaging time series, Bayesian inference of brain-state transitions, and ensemble classification of therapeutic responsiveness across heterogeneous cohorts. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothesized cortico-thalamic interactions modulating trance depth and suggestibility. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers for hypnosis susceptibility, data-driven optimization of induction protocols, and the development of open-source tools for neurophenotypic analysis in hypnotherapy research. By elucidating the dynamical brain systems engaged during therapeutic trance, this work aims to establish empirically validated guidelines for personalized intervention strategies while advancing computational methods for studying altered states of consciousness in clinical populations. The requested resources are critical for handling the project's terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive analyses, which exceed the capacity of local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to employ the controlled inducement of altered states of consciousness, or trance, to reduce pain, resolve emotional conflicts, and enhance communications as part of diagnostic and treatment programs. Includes instruction in the principles of hypnosis and suggestion, induction and deepening, post-hypnotic suggestion, awakening techniques, regression, pacing and leading, resistance transformation, client testing and management, practice management and regulation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational philological and literary analysis of Hungarian texts, addressing critical gaps in digital scholarship for the Uralic language family. While computational methods have transformed research on Indo-European languages, Hungarian’s complex morphology, agglutinative structure, and historical textual diversity remain underexplored due to limited scalable tools and infrastructure. The research problem centers on analyzing large-scale diachronic corpora spanning medieval manuscripts to modern literature to trace linguistic evolution, dialectal variation, and stylistic trends. A key challenge lies in processing archaic orthographies and non-standardized historical forms, which require computationally intensive morphological parsing and semantic disambiguation. The project will employ neural language models (e.g., transformer-based architectures) fine-tuned on Hungarian-specific corpora, combined with rule-based morphological analyzers, to automate tokenization, lemmatization, and syntactic annotation across heterogeneous texts. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including the Magyar Elektronikus Könyvtár and curated collections of 16th–19th century print materials. Additionally, graph-based algorithms will map lexical-semantic networks to quantify stylistic shifts in literary movements, while clustering techniques will identify regional dialect features in lesser-studied vernacular sources. Expected outcomes include the first open-source pipeline for historical Hungarian NLP, a publicly accessible annotated corpus covering six centuries, and quantitative models linking linguistic change to sociocultural contexts. These resources will directly support philological research, language education, and digital preservation initiatives, while advancing methodologies for under-resourced languages in computational humanities. By integrating HPC-driven analysis with traditional literary scholarship, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for studying Hungarian language dynamics at unprecedented scale and resolution.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hungarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing generative design processes in architectural contexts that integrate cultural, environmental, and spatial data. Traditional architectural design workflows often struggle to balance complex, non-quantifiable variables—such as cultural heritage preservation, site-specific ecological impacts, and community spatial preferences—within iterative design explorations. To address this gap, the proposed research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to enable large-scale parametric simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of multi-modal datasets. The core computational challenge lies in modeling nonlinear interactions between qualitative socio-cultural inputs (e.g., historical site narratives, ethnographic surveys) and quantitative environmental metrics (e.g., energy efficiency, material lifecycle assessments) within a unified generative design system. The project will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to process relational data from urban archives and 3D-scanned heritage sites, coupled with multi-objective optimization algorithms to explore design spaces that respect both preservation imperatives and contemporary functional requirements. By parallelizing evolutionary design algorithms across HPC clusters, the team aims to reduce simulation times for large-scale architectural proposals from weeks to days, enabling rapid scenario testing for stakeholders. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational workflow for culturally informed generative design, validated through case studies in adaptive reuse of heritage structures. This work bridges computational architecture, digital humanities, and sustainability science, offering a novel methodological approach for resource-constrained design contexts where cultural significance and ecological performance must coexist. The requested HPC resources will support GPU-accelerated ML training, distributed parametric simulations, and high-resolution rendering of multi-criteria design alternatives, which are computationally infeasible on local workstations. Results will advance tools for architects working at the intersection of heritage conservation, community engagement, and low-carbon design, addressing a critical need in interdisciplinary practice.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture and related programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of understudied ancient Near Eastern languages, with a focus on reconstructing fragmented texts and modeling linguistic evolution across regional dialects. The primary research challenge lies in processing vast, heterogeneous corpora—including cuneiform tablets, epigraphic inscriptions, and papyri—that exhibit high degrees of fragmentation, orthographic variation, and undeciphered elements. Traditional philological methods struggle to systematically analyze these datasets at scale, particularly when tracing phonological shifts, syntactic patterns, or lexical borrowing between languages such as Akkadian, Ugaritic, and Syriac. To address this, the project will implement a multi-stage computational pipeline. First, high-resolution 3D scans of physical artifacts will be processed using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to enhance character recognition in degraded texts. Second, transformer-based language models, pre-trained on extant transliterated corpora, will be fine-tuned to predict missing text fragments, flag potential scribal errors, and identify dialectal features. Finally, phylogenetic algorithms will map diachronic relationships between languages, incorporating epigraphic and numismatic metadata to constrain chronological uncertainties. The HPC environment is critical for managing petabyte-scale image datasets, parallelizing computationally intensive tasks like beam search for text reconstruction, and iterating model training across multiple language families. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated texts, a toolkit for automated paleographic analysis, and probabilistic models of linguistic contact in Bronze Age Levantine societies. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological expertise, this work aims to accelerate the decipherment of poorly attested languages and provide new methodologies for cross-cultural textual studies in ancient Near Eastern scholarship.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Ancient Near Eastern and Biblical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the extinct Semitic and/or Non-Semitic languages spoken in the ancient Near East, including those used to write historical Jewish and Christian religious texts. These languages include, but are not limited to, Egyptian/Coptic, Sumerian, Akkadian, Babylonian, Assyrian, Aramaic, Canaanite, Phoenician, Samarian, Ugaritic, Syriac, Mandean, Hattic, Elamite, Hurrian, Hittite, Urartian, Lydian, Luwian, Lycian, Palaic, Sabaean/South Arabian, and other associated languages. Includes instruction in philology, epigraphy, papyrology, numismatics, and textual studies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and optimize digital resource allocation in children and youth library services, focusing on the intersection of accessibility, engagement, and developmental outcomes. Public libraries increasingly rely on digital platforms to deliver educational content, yet there is limited understanding of how algorithmic curation, interface design, and resource distribution impact equitable access for diverse youth populations. The research problem centers on identifying computational biases in existing digital library systems—such as disparities in content recommendations for neurodiverse users or underserved linguistic groups—and designing adaptive models to improve inclusivity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will process large-scale datasets comprising anonymized user interaction logs, demographic metadata, and multimodal content features (e.g., text complexity, audiovisual components). Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures for natural language processing and graph neural networks for mapping user-content interaction patterns, will be trained to simulate and predict engagement outcomes across subpopulations. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making pathways of young users under varying digital interface conditions, enabling systematic testing of proposed design interventions. Computational results will inform the development of an open-source toolkit for librarians to audit and reconfigure digital platforms, prioritizing equitable access without compromising system performance. Expected outcomes include novel metrics for quantifying engagement equity in youth-oriented digital libraries and empirically validated guidelines for balancing algorithmic efficiency with developmental appropriateness. By integrating computational social science methods with library science praxis, this work addresses a critical gap in non-STEM research infrastructure, offering scalable strategies to align emerging technologies with the ethical imperatives of youth services.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide library and information services and programming for children and young adults. Includes instruction in information needs of children and young adults, resources and services for children and young adults, literature for youth, storytelling, multi-ethnic materials, library management, and information technology for librarians.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to evaluate the long-term impacts of health policy interventions on healthcare system performance and health equity. Despite the critical role of policy simulations in shaping healthcare reform, existing models often lack the granularity to assess interactions between heterogeneous patient populations, institutional resource constraints, and evolving care delivery protocols. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a multi-scale, agent-based simulation platform that integrates electronic health records (EHRs), insurance claims data, and demographic projections. The model will simulate patient care pathways under alternative policy scenarios—such as coverage expansion, telehealth reimbursement changes, and workforce redistribution—while accounting for spatial inequities in care access and dynamic feedback loops between policy implementation and system capacity. Computational challenges include parallelization of stochastic simulations across 10,000+ synthetic patient agents, Bayesian calibration of behavioral parameters using longitudinal Medicare data, and real-time visualization of equity outcomes through geospatial dashboards. Expected outcomes include identification of policy combinations that optimize cost-effectiveness while reducing racial and socioeconomic disparities in care access. The platform will also enable sensitivity analyses to quantify resilience of proposed policies under demographic shifts and public health emergencies. By providing open-source tools for high-fidelity policy testing, this work aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in health system design while establishing scalable methods for computationally intensive policy evaluation. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, secure storage for multi-terabyte health datasets, and runtime for ensemble simulations across diverse policy parameters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to domestic and international health and health care systems. Includes instruction in contemporary health issues and policies, politics and economics of health care delivery, epidemiology, public health, comparative and global health, medical law and ethics, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing human-centric spatial experiences in interior architectural design through high-performance simulations of multisensory environmental interactions. Traditional design methods often prioritize static visual aesthetics and structural compliance, neglecting dynamic factors such as acoustic resonance, transient thermal gradients, and olfactory diffusion patterns that collectively influence occupant well-being. We propose to address this gap by creating a GPU-accelerated simulation environment that models real-time interactions between architectural geometries, material properties, and human sensory perception thresholds. The computational approach integrates ray-traced sound propagation algorithms with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of air-particle movement, coupled with psychophysical models of human sensory adaptation rates. Machine learning techniques will be employed to predict perceptual comfort zones across diverse demographic groups, using training data derived from virtual reality-based user studies. The simulation pipeline will enable parametric exploration of design variables—including surface texture arrays, ventilated partition configurations, and bio-based material composites—while maintaining real-time feedback on multisensory congruence metrics. Expected outcomes include a novel evaluation matrix for quantifying phenomenological spatial quality and an open-source toolset for adaptive interior space prototyping. By establishing quantitative relationships between geometric configurations and neurophysiological responses, this research aims to advance evidence-based design paradigms that transcend conventional sustainability metrics to address holistic human experience in built environments. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space and sub-second latency requirements of coupled multisensory simulations at architectural scales.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply architectural principles in the design of structural interiors for living, recreational, and business purposes and to function as professional interior architects. Includes instruction in architecture, structural systems design, heating and cooling systems, occupational and safety standards, interior design, specific end-use applications, and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: Pediatric hematologic malignancies, such as leukemia and lymphoma, exhibit marked genomic and molecular heterogeneity that drives treatment resistance and relapse. While advances in sequencing technologies have enabled comprehensive profiling of tumors, the integration of multi-omic data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) to uncover clinically actionable patterns remains computationally prohibitive for individual research groups without specialized infrastructure. This project proposes to address this bottleneck by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale datasets from pediatric hematology-oncology cohorts. The primary research objective is to identify molecular subtypes and predictive biomarkers associated with treatment outcomes using machine learning models trained on integrated multi-omic profiles. Computational workflows will include bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data processing, somatic variant calling from whole-genome sequencing, and proteomic network modeling. Deep learning architectures, such as graph neural networks, will be deployed to model interactions between tumor cells and the microenvironment. A key innovation involves simulating clonal evolution dynamics via agent-based models to predict relapse risk under varying therapeutic pressures. The HPC environment is critical for managing datasets exceeding 500 TB, parallelizing complex analyses across thousands of cores, and enabling real-time visualization of 3D tumor microenvironment reconstructions. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated classifier for stratifying relapse risk in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia, (2) mechanistic insights into therapy-induced microenvironment remodeling, and (3) open-source computational pipelines optimized for pediatric cancer data. These results will directly inform two ongoing clinical trials at our institution evaluating targeted therapies for high-risk subtypes. By bridging computational biology with clinical translation, this work aims to advance personalized treatment strategies and reduce disparities in outcomes for pediatric hematology-oncology patients. The requested resources will ensure scalable, reproducible analyses that are infeasible with existing institutional computing capacity.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Hematology-Oncology

abstract: Breastfeeding challenges, including inefficient milk transfer and infant anatomical variations, significantly impact maternal-infant health, yet the biomechanical dynamics underlying these issues remain poorly understood. Current clinical assessments rely on qualitative observations, limiting evidence-based interventions. This project proposes a computational approach to model the biomechanical interactions during infant suckling, integrating anatomical variability, fluid dynamics, and tissue mechanics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to develop multiscale simulations of the infant orofacial complex and mammary tissue to quantify milk flow dynamics under diverse physiological and pathological conditions. Clinical MRI datasets from lactating parents and infants will inform 3D finite element models, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will resolve pressure gradients and flow rates during feeding. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulation outputs alongside clinical metadata (e.g., latch quality, feeding duration) to identify predictive biomechanical signatures of dysfunction. The scale of this effort necessitates HPC resources: single-instance CFD simulations require >10,000 core-hours due to high-resolution meshing of deformable structures and non-Newtonian fluid behavior, while ensemble modeling across anatomical variations demands parallelized workflows. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking biomechanical parameters to feeding efficiency, (2) predictive models of intervention efficacy (e.g., frenotomy outcomes), and (3) open-access tools for quantifying suckling kinematics from clinical videos. By establishing quantitative biomarkers for lactation assessments, this work will empower lactation consultants to personalize clinical strategies, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches. The resource-intensive integration of biomechanical modeling and clinical data science represents a novel frontier in lactation support, bridging computational engineering and perinatal health to address a critical gap in evidence-based practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide lactation management services and breastfeeding support to women, and to work as a Lactation Consultant in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology of lactation, nutrition, breastfeeding techniques and technologies, common concerns and solutions, management of special situations, breastfeeding instruction, professional and legal concerns, and advocacy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of endocrine signaling dysregulation in tumor microenvironment adaptation and therapy resistance, with a focus on hormone-sensitive cancers. Despite advances in endocrine therapies, many tumors develop resistance through poorly understood mechanisms involving dynamic crosstalk between cancer cells and stromal components. The research problem centers on identifying how endocrine-driven cellular communication networks evolve during treatment, altering metabolic and secretory profiles to promote survival. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze spatially resolved transcriptomic and proteomic datasets from patient-derived xenograft models of breast and prostate cancer, capturing temporal changes in endocrine signaling pathways during therapy. Computational models will integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data with secreted protein profiles to reconstruct paracrine interaction networks between epithelial cells and fibroblasts. Agent-based simulations will map how hormone receptor activation dynamics influence collective survival behaviors under therapeutic pressure. A custom computational pipeline will employ Bayesian network inference to identify master regulatory nodes coordinating endocrine and stress-response pathways, validated through in silico perturbation experiments. Expected outcomes include predictive models of resistance-associated secretory phenotypes and candidate targets for disrupting adaptive endocrine-stromal crosstalk. This work will advance understanding of microenvironment-mediated therapy evasion while providing a computational framework to optimize combination therapies targeting both endocrine and compensatory signaling axes. The scale of multi-omic integration and need for high-resolution spatial-temporal modeling necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing of large-scale datasets (>50 TB) and iterative simulation of complex cellular systems. Outcomes will directly inform preclinical studies in hormone-driven cancers, bridging critical gaps between endocrine physiology and translational oncology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition, manufacture, and secretion of protein compounds by cells and glands and the role of endocrine substances in bodily processes. Includes instruction in protein chemistry, protein secretion, membrane biogenesis and transfer methods, cellular communication, gene and cell regulation, cytochemistry, fractionation, radioautography, and applications such as neuroendocrinology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, sparse biological datasets commonly encountered in agricultural and natural resource studies. A key challenge in these domains is the integration of multi-modal data—such as environmental sensor readings, species occurrence records, and resource management histories—into predictive models that account for complex spatial dependencies, temporal autocorrelation, and unbalanced sampling designs. Traditional biometrical approaches often struggle with computational inefficiency when handling such data structures, particularly when applying Bayesian hierarchical frameworks or ensemble machine learning techniques. To address this, we propose implementing a hybrid computational architecture combining Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling with distributed gradient boosting, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated matrix operations for covariance estimation in mixed-effects models while employing MPI-based parallelization for stochastic gradient descent in neural network components. Key deliverables include an open-source R/Python package for sparse spatiotemporal analysis and validation against empirical datasets from precision agriculture trials and wildlife population monitoring programs. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale simulations to evaluate type I/II error rates under varying missing data mechanisms, as well as parameter estimation for high-dimensional random forest models with >10^5 decision trees. Expected outcomes include robust protocols for handling non-ignorable missingness in longitudinal ecological datasets and improved uncertainty quantification in resource allocation optimization tasks. This work directly supports evidence-based decision-making in sustainable agriculture and biodiversity conservation by providing computationally feasible tools for complex error structures inherent to real-world biological systems. Successful implementation will require access to at least 50 nodes with 64 GB RAM each, GPU support for tensor operations, and scalable storage for terabyte-scale sensitivity analyses.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics and other computational methods to the study of problems in the biological sciences and related fields in agriculture and natural resources. Includes instruction in computational biology, mathematical statistics, matrix algebra, applied calculus, experimental design, linear modeling, sampling theory, stochastic processes, spatial and temporal analysis, longitudinal analysis, sparse/unbalanced data and complex error, and applications to such topics as population genetics, animal breeding, forest genetics, population dynamics, wildlife biometry, ecology, and agricultural and natural resource management.

abstract: The increasing demand for real-time photorealistic rendering in applications ranging from virtual prototyping to immersive entertainment necessitates advancements in simulating complex material-light interactions. Traditional approaches in computer graphics often rely on simplified bidirectional scattering distribution functions (BSDFs) that inadequately capture the anisotropic, multi-scale light transport phenomena observed in materials such as woven textiles, biological tissues, or metamaterials. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a scalable computational framework for simulating subsurface scattering and diffraction effects in hierarchically structured materials, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome the prohibitive computational costs of physically accurate simulations. The core challenge lies in efficiently solving the radiative transfer equation (RTE) across multiple spatial scales while preserving visual fidelity. Our approach combines Monte Carlo path tracing with adaptive wavelet-based discretization to reduce memory overhead and enable dynamic load balancing across GPU clusters. A novel hybrid algorithm will exploit temporal coherence in animated scenes by caching partial solutions for quasi-static geometry components. The computational workflow will integrate open-source rendering engines with custom CUDA kernels optimized for NVIDIA A100 GPUs, targeting a 50x speedup over existing single-GU implementations for equivalent scene complexity. Validation will employ experimentally derived refractive index datasets from collaborating materials science groups, correlating simulated output with hyperspectral imaging measurements. Successful implementation will yield open-access tools for real-time rendering of dynamically deforming heterogeneous materials, with applications in digital twin systems for manufacturing and telemedicine. This work advances the intersection of computational physics and graphics by addressing a critical bottleneck in rendering pipeline efficiency, while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration through shared HPC resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the software, hardware, and mathematical tools used to represent, display, and manipulate topological, two-, and three-dimensional objects on a computer screen and that prepares individuals to function as computer graphics specialists. Includes instruction in graphics software and systems; digital multimedia; graphic design; graphics devices, processors, and standards; attributes and transformations; projections; surface identification and rendering; color theory and application; and applicable geometry and algorithms.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) and their role in extreme precipitation events under varying climate scenarios, using high-resolution atmospheric modeling to address critical gaps in current predictive capabilities.
