By parallelizing simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, HPC resources will enable rapid exploration of intervention efficacy while accounting for stochastic physiological responses. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to guide triage and treatment prioritization in austere settings, (2) quantitative evidence for revising wilderness medicine protocols, and (3) open-source computational frameworks for simulating environmental-clinical interactions. This work will directly inform clinical training programs and emergency response planning, with potential applications in disaster medicine, military healthcare, and global health equity. The scale of required parameter space exploration, coupled with the need for high-resolution physiological modeling in transient environmental conditions, necessitates the processing power and memory allocation uniquely available through HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine with limited resources in austere environments or to provide healthcare anywhere in which environmental conditions have physiologic insult to a patient.

abstract: The rapid evolution of digital publishing has created significant challenges in analyzing large-scale content distribution networks, optimizing discoverability, and addressing ethical concerns such as copyright compliance and algorithmic bias. Traditional methods lack the capacity to process the vast, heterogeneous datasets generated by global digital publishing platforms, including e-book sales metrics, social media engagement, and unauthorized content-sharing networks. This project proposes a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze these dynamics. Using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML), we will process multilingual text corpora from digital publications and user-generated commentary to identify trends in content consumption and ethical risks, such as AI-generated plagiarism or culturally biased recommendation algorithms. Concurrently, network analysis tools will map the dissemination of copyrighted materials across peer-to-peer platforms and social media, enabling simulations of anti-piracy strategies. The scale of data—terabytes of text, images, and user interaction logs—necessitates distributed computing for efficient processing, while iterative ML model training requires GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for metadata optimization to enhance content discoverability, predictive models for copyright infringement hotspots, and evidence-based guidelines for ethical AI use in automated publishing workflows. By addressing these computational bottlenecks, the project aims to advance scholarly understanding of digital publishing ecosystems while providing industry stakeholders with scalable tools to navigate technical, legal, and ethical complexities. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on integrating technical and managerial solutions in publishing, offering a template for data-driven decision-making in a rapidly transforming field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process of managing the creation, publication, and distribution of print and electronic books and other text products and prepares individuals to manage the editorial, technical, and business aspects of publishing operations. Includes instruction in product planning and design, editing, author relations, business and copyright law, publishing industry operations, contracting and purchasing, product marketing, electronic publishing and commerce, history of publishing, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized skincare treatment protocols for clients undergoing post-operative or medically supervised esthetic care. Current approaches to designing such protocols rely heavily on trial-and-error methodologies, which can lead to suboptimal outcomes, prolonged recovery times, or adverse reactions due to the complex interplay of individual skin physiology, treatment combinations, and environmental factors. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interactions between skin biomechanics, biochemical agents (e.g., peels, serums), and therapeutic interventions (e.g., lymphatic drainage, microdermabrasion). A multi-scale computational pipeline will integrate clinical datasets, including high-resolution skin imaging, histopathological profiles, and real-time biometric sensor data, with machine learning algorithms to simulate treatment outcomes across diverse skin types and conditions. Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent diffusion processes of topical agents through stratified skin layers, predicting mechanical stress responses during manual therapies, and optimizing treatment sequences under physiological constraints. The HPC environment will enable parallelized parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated patient profiles, coupled with ensemble learning techniques to identify robust protocol templates. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for esthetic practitioners, capable of recommending personalized treatment plans that minimize recovery intervals while maximizing therapeutic efficacy. By bridging computational modeling and clinical esthetics, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for evidence-based skincare that enhances patient outcomes, reduces healthcare costs associated with complications, and advances professional standards in medical esthetics. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale data integration, and validation against clinical case studies collected through partnerships with dermatology clinics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and body with advanced chemical and cosmetic preparations and esthetic medical treatments, and to function as licensed master or medical estheticians in dermatologists' and plastic surgeons' offices as well as in salons and spas. Includes instruction in advanced anatomy and physiology, skin properties and disorders, sanitation and infection control, advanced facial treatments, spa body treatments, advanced extractions, corrective makeup, chemical peels, microdermabrasion, lymphatic drainage and advanced massage techniques, pre- and post-operative esthetic skin care, client/patient evaluation and care, applicable laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize automated defect detection and lifecycle management in building construction finishing processes. Current inspection practices rely heavily on manual assessments, which are time-consuming, subjective, and prone to human error, leading to costly delays and safety risks. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven approach using high-resolution 3D scans, thermal imaging datasets, and real-time sensor data from construction sites. The core challenge lies in processing multi-modal data streams at scale to identify subtle material defects (e.g., cracks, moisture ingress, improper insulation) while accounting for dynamic environmental factors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep convolutional neural networks on terabyte-scale image datasets and running finite element analysis simulations to model defect propagation under varying stress conditions. Parallelized workflows will integrate computer vision algorithms for anomaly detection with probabilistic models to predict failure risks across building systems. A key innovation involves developing a digital twin platform that maps defect signatures to maintenance protocols, enabling proactive resource allocation for repairs. Expected outcomes include a validated computational pipeline capable of reducing inspection time by 40-60% while improving defect classification accuracy to >95% compared to manual methods. The project will generate open-source tools for construction managers to prioritize high-risk zones in finishing workflows and extend asset lifespans. By bridging computational engineering with construction management, this work aims to establish new standards for data-driven quality control in the built environment, with potential applications in regulatory compliance and sustainable resource utilization.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of a dynamic knowledge flow optimization framework for decentralized organizational structures. As hybrid work models and digital transformation accelerate, traditional knowledge management systems struggle to adapt to fragmented, real-time decision-making environments. The research problem centers on mitigating information asymmetry and latency in distributed teams, where inefficient knowledge transfer undermines operational agility and innovation. Current approaches lack the computational granularity to model multi-agent interactions across temporal, spatial, and hierarchical dimensions simultaneously. The proposed computational methodology integrates agent-based modeling with graph neural networks to simulate knowledge propagation patterns in large-scale virtual organizations (10,000+ synthetic agents). By incorporating transformer architectures trained on anonymized corporate communication datasets, the framework will predict optimal knowledge routing paths while preserving privacy constraints. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across diverse organizational topologies and validating the model against real-world benchmarks from partner firms undergoing digital transitions. Expected outcomes include a scalable API for recommending context-aware knowledge-sharing protocols and quantifying the ROI of collaborative technologies. This work bridges computational social science with information systems design, offering novel metrics for measuring "knowledge liquidity" in decentralized enterprises. The results will directly inform adaptive governance policies for Web3-native organizations and traditional firms adopting distributed workflows, addressing a critical gap in next-generation knowledge management infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of knowledge management in government agencies and corporations for the purpose of supporting stated organizational goals and objectives, and prepares individuals to function as information resource managers. Includes instruction in information technology, principles of computer and information systems, management information systems, applicable policy and regulations, and operations and personnel management.

abstract: The increasing demand for safe and efficient nuclear energy systems necessitates advanced computational tools to address the complex multiphysics phenomena inherent to reactor design and safety analysis. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for analyzing transient multiphysics coupling in molten salt reactors (MSRs), a next-generation reactor design with inherent safety features but significant modeling challenges due to fluid-fuel interactions, delayed neutron precursor transport, and time-dependent thermal-structural feedback. Current tools for MSR simulation rely on simplified approximations that decouple neutronics, thermal-hydraulics, and structural mechanics, limiting predictive accuracy for off-normal scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose a tightly coupled computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve spatiotemporal interactions across scales. The framework will integrate Monte Carlo neutron transport (via OpenMC), computational fluid dynamics (using OpenFOAM's multiphase solver), and finite-element structural analysis (via MOOSE) through a custom coupling manager optimized for asynchronous data exchange. Machine learning surrogates will accelerate cross-scale feedback iterations, while adaptive mesh refinement will focus resolution on interface regions. Validation will employ experimental data from molten salt flow loops and existing transient benchmarks. The HPC implementation targets scalability to >10,000 cores on leadership-class systems, enabling 3D full-core transient simulations at unprecedented resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source multiphysics platform for MSR analysis, quantitative safety margins for fuel salt freezing scenarios, and optimized control strategies for flow-induced power oscillations. This work will provide foundational tools for advancing liquid-fueled reactor licensing and inform the design of inherently safe nuclear systems, supporting global decarbonization efforts. The computational methodologies developed may also extend to other nuclear–thermal-fluid applications, including fusion blanket systems and radioisotope production facilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling and manipulating nuclear energy, including nuclear power plant design, fission reactor design, fusion reactor design, reactor control and safety systems design, power transfer systems, containment vessels and structures design; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as fission and fusion processes, human and environmental factors, construction, and operational considerations.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the optimization of corporate communication strategies through advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, with a focus on enhancing the alignment of organizational messaging with stakeholder expectations across cultural and linguistic boundaries. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies in current communication workflows, where manual processes for drafting, editing, and tailoring content for diverse audiences often lead to delays, inconsistent messaging, and misalignment with stakeholder sentiment. Existing tools lack the capacity to dynamically model the interplay between linguistic nuance, cultural context, and organizational objectives at scale. To address this gap, the project proposes developing a computational framework that integrates transformer-based language models, sentiment analysis, and cross-cultural semantic mapping. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train and fine-tune models on multilingual corpora of corporate communications (e.g., press releases, internal memos, social media content) and stakeholder feedback data, while simulating real-time adaptation scenarios. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of heterogeneous text datasets, hyperparameter optimization for domain-specific language models, and probabilistic modeling of communication impact across stakeholder networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source toolkit for automated analysis and generation of context-aware business communications, (2) quantitative metrics for evaluating cross-cultural message efficacy, and (3) evidence-based frameworks for adaptive communication strategy design. The research will contribute to emerging interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of computational linguistics, stakeholder theory, and organizational behavior, while providing practical tools to reduce operational friction in global corporate communications. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to overcome scalability limitations in current NLP applications, enabling organizations to proactively address communication challenges in fast-evolving business environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to model systemic risk propagation in decentralized insurance markets, with a focus on emergent risks linked to climate-driven extreme weather events and cyber-physical disruptions. Traditional actuarial models often fail to capture nonlinear interdependencies between heterogeneous risk pools, reinsurance networks, and asset-liability cascades in modern insurance ecosystems. This gap becomes critical as novel risk-transfer instruments (e.g., parametric insurance derivatives) and AI-driven underwriting tools reshape market dynamics. We propose a hybrid agent-based model (ABM) coupled with graph neural networks (GNNs) to simulate multi-scale risk contagion across 10^6+ synthetic entities representing insurers, policyholders, and capital markets. The ABM layer will integrate geospatial climate projections (CMIP6 datasets) and stochastic cyber-attack generators, while GNNs will dynamically infer latent dependencies from real-world claims data and regulatory filings. High-performance computing resources are essential to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations across diverse climate scenarios (RCP 2.6 to 8.5) and optimize GNN architectures through hyperparameter sweeps in tensor-optimized environments. Expected outcomes include (1) a risk topology map identifying critical leverage points in insurance networks, (2) stress-testing metrics for solvency thresholds under compound disasters, and (3) an open-source toolkit for regulators to evaluate systemic stability when approving innovative insurance products. By bridging complexity science and actuarial practice, this work aims to redefine capital adequacy standards for interconnected risks while providing computational infrastructure to address 21st-century insurability challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage risk in organizational settings and provide insurance and risk-aversion services to businesses, individuals, and other organizations. Includes instruction in casualty insurance and general liability, property insurance, employee benefits, social and health insurance, loss adjustment, underwriting, risk theory, and pension planning.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in large-scale art historical analysis and conservation science. Current methods for studying artistic style evolution, material degradation, and provenance often rely on manual or localized computational approaches, which struggle to process the growing volume of high-resolution multispectral imaging data, 3D artifact reconstructions, and global archival records. The project proposes a computational framework combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for stylistic pattern detection, graph-based algorithms for mapping historical influence networks, and physics-informed machine learning models to simulate pigment degradation and environmental impacts on conservation. Key datasets include digitized collections of 15th–18th century European paintings, terabyte-scale LiDAR scans of archaeological sites, and hyperspectral imaging of deteriorating modern artworks. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU nodes, the team aims to analyze cross-cultural stylistic transfers at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, predict optimal conservation parameters for vulnerable materials, and reconstruct damaged artworks through generative inpainting models. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for art historians, validated preservation strategies for institutions managing climate-vulnerable collections, and new evidence-based narratives about understudied artistic exchanges in the early modern period. The resource-intensive nature of training domain-adapted vision models on culturally diverse artworks and running iterative conservation simulations necessitates HPC capabilities beyond typical departmental infrastructure. This work bridges computational scalability gaps in art historical research while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies at the intersection of heritage science, data-driven humanities, and ethical AI applications for cultural preservation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical development of art as social and intellectual phenomenon, the analysis of works of art, and art conservation. Includes instruction in the theory of art, art history research methods, connoisseurship, the preservation and conservation of works of art, and the study of specific periods, cultures, styles, and themes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systems-level mechanisms underlying synergistic botanical formulations used in naturopathic medicine. While naturopathy emphasizes multi-modal, natural therapies to promote self-healing, the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic interactions of complex plant-derived compounds remain poorly characterized, limiting evidence-based optimization of clinical protocols. The research addresses this gap by analyzing how polyherbal formulations modulate immune-neuro-endocrine networks, with a focus on low-dose botanical combinations that exhibit non-linear bioactivity—a phenomenon observed clinically but inadequately explained by reductionist models. Computational workflows will integrate molecular docking simulations, machine learning-driven network pharmacology, and multi-omics data fusion to map interactions between phytochemical ensembles and human proteomic targets. A novel computational framework will be developed to model entourage effects—the emergent therapeutic properties arising from compound interactions—using quantum chemistry-informed molecular dynamics simulations to assess energy landscapes of botanical mixtures. Concurrently, Bayesian network models will correlate in silico predictions with existing clinical metabolomic datasets from patients undergoing naturopathic treatments for chronic inflammatory conditions. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these analyses across thousands of potential phytochemical combinations and simulating temporal biological responses at cellular resolution. Expected outcomes include the identification of key synergistic phytochemical pairs, predictive biomarkers for treatment personalization, and a publicly accessible database linking traditional naturopathic pharmacopeia to molecular interaction profiles. By elucidating mechanisms underlying holistic therapeutic strategies, this work aims to establish a computational foundation for advancing naturopathic research methodologies while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between traditional medicine systems and computational biology. The resource request directly supports the development of open-source tools for natural product research, addressing a critical need in integrative health sciences for scalable approaches to study complex, multi-target interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of naturopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic approach combining medical knowledge with noninvasive natural, homeopathic, and non-Western therapies and emphasizing disease prevention, wellness, and self-healing. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, biostatistics, public and community health, laboratory and clinical diagnosis, pharmacognosy, botanical medicine, homeopathy, principles of Oriental medicine and Ayurveda, manipulative therapy, naturopathic therapeutics, therapeutic nutrition, case analysis and management, philosophy of naturopathy, patient counseling, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of targeted neuropharmacological therapies for neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders. Current drug discovery efforts in neuropharmacology face critical challenges, including the complexity of blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, receptor subtype selectivity, and dynamic interactions between neuromodulatory agents and adaptive neural circuits. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in resolving the spatiotemporal dynamics of drug-receptor interactions or predicting systemic effects on neural network activity. To address these gaps, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of drug candidates interacting with neuronal ion channels and neurotransmitter receptors (e.g., dopamine D3 and NMDA subtypes), coupled with pharmacodynamic network modeling. The MD component will employ all-atom simulations to quantify binding affinities and conformational changes in key CNS targets, while the network models will predict dose-dependent effects on oscillatory dynamics in cortico-striatal-thalamic circuits relevant to Parkinson’s disease and schizophrenia. HPC resources will enable large-scale virtual screening of 50,000+ BBB-permeable compounds from the ZINC15 database, accelerated using machine learning-based QSAR models trained on existing pharmacokinetic data. Parallelized simulations will map time-dependent drug distribution across multi-compartmental neuron-glial models, incorporating stochastic vesicular release and transporter kinetics. Expected outcomes include the identification of 3-5 lead compounds with optimized polypharmacology profiles, validated against in vitro electrophysiology data, and predictive models linking molecular binding kinetics to network-level therapeutic outcomes. This work will establish a computational pipeline for rational design of CNS drugs with enhanced efficacy and reduced off-target effects, directly addressing the program’s focus on mechanistic drug development for brain disorders. The requested resources are essential for handling the terabyte-scale data from multi-parametric simulations and enabling real-time iterative refinement of candidate molecules.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drugs that modify the function of the brain and central nervous system, the effects of such drugs on health, disease, perception, motor action, and behavior; and the development of countermeasures and treatment therapies. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, behavioral neuroscience, neurobiochemistry, neuropathology, the mechanisms of brain function, medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics, and studies of specific drugs and drug therapies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of undersea warfare operations demands advanced computational tools to optimize sensor deployment, autonomous system coordination, and real-time decision-making in contested environments. Current approaches to modeling underwater sensor networks and unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) swarm dynamics struggle to account for the synergistic effects of multi-domain variables, including acoustic propagation uncertainties, adversarial counter-detection tactics, and dynamic mission constraints. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to address these gaps, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale undersea scenarios with unprecedented granularity. The research integrates agent-based modeling, probabilistic game theory, and adaptive signal processing algorithms to simulate adversarial interactions between distributed sensor arrays, UUV swarms, and opposing forces under realistic oceanographic conditions. Key computational challenges include resolving multi-scale physics (e.g., turbulent flow effects on sensor performance), optimizing resource allocation in incomplete information environments, and validating emergent swarm behaviors against classified operational datasets. The HPC implementation will utilize parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification and machine learning techniques to identify optimal sensor-weapon pairing strategies across mission phases. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating undersea system resilience, quantifying the operational impact of novel autonomy protocols, and informing acquisition priorities for next-generation distributed maritime systems. By bridging tactical requirements with computational innovation, this work aims to establish new paradigms for undersea warfare resource optimization while advancing methodological approaches for modeling human-machine teaming in constrained electromagnetic environments. The resulting framework will be designed for interoperability with existing naval simulation architectures, ensuring direct relevance to current modernization priorities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, engineering design and military concepts that govern the operational employment of underwater sensors and weapons systems. Includes instruction in acoustics, electrical, and mechanical engineering; mathematics; meteorology; oceanography; physics; operations analysis; human factors; computer science; and robotics.

abstract: Hospice and palliative care research faces a critical challenge in predicting patient-centered outcomes due to the complex interplay of biological, psychosocial, and symptom-related variables in advanced illness. Existing prognostic models often lack the granularity and scalability required to inform personalized care plans, particularly for patients with multi-morbidity or rapidly evolving symptoms. This project proposes to develop a machine learning framework to analyze multi-modal clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), longitudinal symptom reports, genomic markers of pain sensitivity, and caregiver narratives—to predict trajectories of functional decline, symptom burden, and quality of life in patients receiving palliative care. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of structured and unstructured data, train deep neural networks on temporal patterns across heterogeneous datasets, and perform Bayesian optimization for dynamic risk stratification. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for extracting semantic features from clinician notes and patient-reported outcomes, federated learning to preserve privacy across six participating hospice institutions, and ensemble methods to address class imbalance in rare clinical events. The resulting models will be validated against prospective outcomes in a cohort of 2,300 patients and deployed as open-source tools for real-time decision support. This work aims to advance the precision of palliative care interventions by identifying subpopulations at risk for under-managed symptoms, optimizing the timing of hospice transitions, and elucidating biological signatures associated with end-of-life experiences. The requested HPC allocation will enable iterative model refinement at scale, reducing training times for 3D convolutional networks analyzing functional MRI correlates of delirium from weeks to days. Outcomes will directly inform clinical trial designs for personalized pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic therapies while establishing computational infrastructure for collaborative palliative care research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hospice and Palliative Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study examining the evolution of cultural identity markers in post-Soviet Central Asia and the Caucasus through computational analysis of multilingual textual and visual archives. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how linguistic, artistic, and symbolic representations of identity shifted between 1985 and 2005, particularly in digitized materials from minority communities that remain underexplored due to computational constraints. Current scholarship lacks systematic analysis of cross-regional cultural reconfigurations during this transitional period, hindered by the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources spanning Turkic, Persian, and Russian-language materials. The proposed methodology integrates transformer-based natural language processing models fine-tuned for low-resource Central Asian languages with computer vision techniques to analyze 12TB of digitized newspapers, folk art collections, and oral history transcripts. Computational workflows will be designed to trace semantic shifts in identity-related terminology, map visual motifs in textile and architectural photography, and correlate these with geopolitical changes. The pipeline requires distributed GPU-accelerated processing for training multilingual embeddings, running iterative pattern recognition algorithms on high-resolution image sets, and maintaining a knowledge graph linking cultural artifacts to sociohistorical metadata. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of identity discourse, interactive visualizations of cultural influence networks, and new methodological frameworks for computational area studies. This work will provide the first large-scale comparative analysis of identity negotiation strategies across five Central Asian and three Caucasus republics during state formation periods, offering critical insights for scholars of postcolonial cultural adaptation. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing heterogeneous data types at scale while preserving context in linguistically complex materials central to understanding Eurasian cultural dynamics.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_title: Russian, Central European, East European and Eurasian Studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the region encompassing Russia, Central Europe, Eastern Europe, and Eurasia, including the Balkan, Baltic, Caucasus, and Central Asian states that were republics of the former Soviet Union.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic task allocation and prioritization within decentralized administrative support systems, a critical yet understudied challenge in business operations. As organizations scale, traditional secretarial and operational workflows—particularly in hybrid or fully remote environments—struggle to adapt to real-time fluctuations in task urgency, resource availability, and cross-departmental dependencies. Current rule-based or manual prioritization systems often lead to bottlenecks, duplicated efforts, and suboptimal resource utilization. This study proposes a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate and optimize decision-making processes in complex administrative ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the parallel simulation of thousands of agent interactions across multi-layered organizational networks, each with unique constraints (e.g., compliance protocols, skill mismatches, time-sensitive deliverables). The computational model will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to analyze historical task logs and communications, generating synthetic training environments that reflect real-world operational ambiguity. Expected outcomes include 1) a predictive tool for identifying systemic vulnerabilities in administrative workflows, 2) adaptive prioritization algorithms that balance short-term responsiveness with long-term operational stability, and 3) quantitative metrics for evaluating the resilience of support service architectures under stress scenarios. By bridging computational social science with operational theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for intelligent resource allocation in business support functions, with potential applications extending to crisis management, regulatory compliance automation, and cross-organizational collaboration frameworks. The research will provide empirically validated strategies to enhance operational agility while reducing computational overhead compared to conventional enterprise scheduling systems.
cip_title: Business Operations Support and Secretarial Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in administrative and secretarial services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance the understanding of complex reaction mechanisms in heterogeneous catalysis, a critical area for sustainable energy and chemical synthesis. While experimental studies provide valuable insights, they often struggle to resolve transient intermediates and solvent effects at atomic resolution, particularly in multi-component systems. This project addresses these limitations by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model catalytic cycles at the quantum-mechanical level, focusing on transition metal clusters in liquid-phase environments. The primary challenge lies in accurately simulating dynamic solvent interactions and entropy contributions, which require extensive sampling of free energy landscapes. To overcome this, we will implement hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations coupled with enhanced sampling techniques, such as metadynamics and replica-exchange molecular dynamics. These methods demand substantial computational resources due to the need for large periodic boundary condition systems (500–1,000 atoms), long simulation timescales (nanosecond range), and iterative optimization of reaction coordinates. The HPC allocation will enable parallelized calculations across multiple nodes, leveraging GPU acceleration for density functional theory (DFT) computations and force field parametrization. Expected outcomes include identifying solvent-mediated pathways for CO₂ hydrogenation and ammonia synthesis, quantifying the role of entropy in rate-determining steps, and validating theoretical predictions against in situ spectroscopic data. This work will provide a predictive framework for tailoring catalyst selectivity under realistic conditions, directly informing experimental efforts to develop energy-efficient processes. Additionally, the generated datasets will be curated into an open-access repository, supporting reproducibility and community-driven method development in computational chemistry. By bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical catalysis, this project aims to accelerate the discovery of environmentally benign chemical technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemistry, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze high-dimensional, spatiotemporal datasets generated by multisensor ecological monitoring systems, integrating machine learning with domain-specific knowledge from conservation biology and environmental physics. The core challenge lies in modeling nonlinear interactions between biotic communities and microclimatic variables under rapidly shifting environmental conditions, where traditional statistical methods fail to scale or capture complex dependencies. We propose a hybrid architecture combining transformer-based attention mechanisms for cross-modal data fusion, graph neural networks (GNNs) to represent species interaction networks, and physics-informed recurrent units to embed known biogeochemical constraints. The computational workflow will process terabyte-scale inputs from LiDAR, hyperspectral imaging, and distributed sensor arrays across seven forest ecosystems, requiring distributed training of probabilistic models across GPU clusters. Key innovations include adaptive sampling strategies to handle extreme class imbalances in rare species detection and a novel loss function penalizing ecologically implausible predictions through domain knowledge graphs. Expected outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for joint biodiversity-microclimate forecasting capable of resolving subkilometer spatial gradients and subdiurnal temporal dynamics. This work addresses critical gaps in predictive ecology by enabling real-time assimilation of heterogeneous data streams, with applications ranging from wildfire resilience planning to invasive species management. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential for benchmarking model architectures at scale, optimizing hyperparameters through Bayesian neural networks, and simulating ecosystem trajectories under 50+ climate scenarios. Success will provide conservation agencies with decision-support tools that balance computational precision with interpretability constraints inherent to multidisciplinary environmental applications.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of data mining and machine learning. Includes instruction in naive Bayes rule, artificial neural networks, genetic algorithms, decision tree learning, neural nets, network science, optimization, statistical computing, and graphical models and methods.

abstract: Surgical complications and adverse events remain significant challenges in perioperative care, with current practices often relying on reactive interventions. This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize intraoperative decision-making and patient outcomes through computational modeling of multi-modal surgical data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate structured electronic health records (EHRs), real-time physiological sensor data, and instrument utilization logs from 15,000+ historical surgeries to identify risk factors for complications such as hemorrhage, infection, and anesthesia-related events. Machine learning models, including temporal convolutional networks and transformer architectures, will be trained to recognize patterns preceding adverse events, enabling proactive interventions. The computational workflow requires processing high-frequency physiological signals (500 Hz sampling rate) alongside sparse clinical observations, necessitating parallelized feature extraction and hybrid model architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) a real-time risk prediction dashboard for perioperative nurses, prioritizing critical patient metrics during surgery; (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing instrument sterilization workflows and surgical team communication patterns; and (3) synthetic data generation capabilities for nurse training simulations. By enabling millisecond-scale analysis of complex surgical datasets, the requested HPC resources will directly support advancements in anticipatory patient care, operating room efficiency, and nursing education—addressing critical gaps in perioperative practice. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for surgical nursing informatics and validation studies across three academic medical centers.
cip_title: Perioperative/ Operating Room and Surgical Nurse/ Nursing
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide care to patients before and during surgery, and provide tableside assistance to surgeons. Includes instruction in operating room safety and preparation, aseptic technique, anesthesia, patient preparation, surgical instruments and procedures, sterilization and disinfecting, surgical drugs and solutions, hemostasis, emergency procedures, and patient/family education.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic resource allocation in heterogeneous edge-to-cloud computing environments, where traditional static or centralized resource management strategies struggle to adapt to fluctuating workloads, diverse hardware architectures, and latency-critical applications. As modern networks increasingly incorporate edge devices, on-premises clusters, and multi-cloud deployments, system administrators face growing complexity in balancing computational efficiency, energy consumption, and Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. We propose developing an adaptive resource orchestration framework that leverages real-time telemetry data and machine learning to predict workload patterns, optimize task placement, and autonomously reconfigure virtualized infrastructure. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulations of hybrid network topologies with reinforcement learning models trained on multi-objective optimization criteria, including latency minimization, energy-aware scheduling, and fault tolerance. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for both training distributed ML models on historical system logs (spanning petabyte-scale operational datasets) and simulating large-scale network environments with 10,000+ node configurations. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support toolkit for system administrators, enabling proactive resource provisioning strategies that reduce service-level agreement (SLA) violations by ≥30% in simulated environments compared to conventional reactive methods. The research will further contribute open-source modules for anomaly-aware load balancing and energy-efficient container migration, validated through benchmark testing against real-world traces from scientific computing clusters and IoT-enabled smart infrastructure. By bridging gaps between autonomic computing theory and practical network administration, this work aims to establish new methodologies for managing next-generation cyberinfrastructure ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian inference methods for high-dimensional statistical models, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in uncertainty quantification for complex data. Modern statistical applications—such as epidemiological forecasting, genomic association studies, and environmental risk modeling—increasingly rely on hierarchical Bayesian frameworks to integrate heterogeneous data sources and quantify uncertainty. However, conventional Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms suffer from prohibitive computational costs when applied to models with millions of parameters or non-conjugate likelihood structures, limiting their utility in real-world settings. To overcome these challenges, this research will implement and evaluate hybrid sampling strategies that combine Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), variational inference, and distributed computing frameworks. Key innovations include the development of domain-specific preconditioning techniques for HMC to improve convergence in ill-conditioned parameter spaces and the integration of GPU-accelerated linear algebra libraries for efficient gradient computations. The project will validate these methods using synthetic datasets and case studies from public health (e.g., spatiotemporal disease transmission models) and climate science (e.g., extreme event attribution). By parallelizing likelihood evaluations and optimizing memory allocation across HPC nodes, the proposed algorithms aim to reduce wall-clock time for posterior sampling by orders of magnitude while maintaining statistical fidelity. Success will enable statisticians to fit larger, more realistic models to emerging high-dimensional datasets, advancing the reproducibility and predictive accuracy of data-driven decision-making. The outcomes will be disseminated as open-source software packages tailored for distributed memory architectures, along with benchmarking studies to guide computational resource allocation for Bayesian workflows. This work bridges critical gaps in statistical computing, empowering researchers to tackle grand challenges in science and policy without sacrificing rigorous uncertainty quantification.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and statistics or a specialization which draws from mathematics and statistics. Includes instruction in calculus, linear algebra, numerical analysis and partial differential equations, discrete mathematics, probability theory, statistics, computing, and other related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven instructional frameworks for students with intellectual disabilities (ID). A critical challenge in special education is the design of individualized learning strategies that account for the vast heterogeneity in cognitive, behavioral, and sensory profiles among students with ID. Traditional approaches often rely on generalized interventions, which may fail to optimize outcomes for learners with complex or overlapping needs. To address this, our research integrates computational modeling, machine learning, and large-scale simulations to analyze longitudinal educational datasets, including student performance metrics, behavioral logs, and individualized education plan (IEP) records. By training ensemble models on multi-modal data—spanning speech, motor skill development, and adaptive behavior assessments—we aim to identify latent patterns that predict responsiveness to specific pedagogical strategies. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom dynamics under varying intervention scenarios, enabling the exploration of “what-if” conditions for tailoring instructional pacing, scaffolding, and assistive technology integration. These simulations will account for real-world constraints, such as classroom size, resource availability, and educator-student ratios. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabytes of anonymized student data, running parallelized model iterations, and optimizing hyperparameters for predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational framework for generating evidence-based IEP recommendations, (2) predictive tools to guide educators in personalizing instructional content, and (3) open-source simulation modules for training pre-service teachers in adaptive pedagogy. By bridging computational analytics and special education practice, this work has the potential to transform how educators individualize instruction, reduce trial-and-error inefficiencies, and improve academic and functional outcomes for students with ID.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with intellectual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with intellectual disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising mentally handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation for public sector entities facing climate-related fiscal risks. As governments increasingly confront budgetary pressures from extreme weather events, shifting regulatory landscapes, and transitional climate policies, traditional static budget models fail to capture the complex interdependencies between environmental volatility, infrastructure investments, and long-term fiscal health. The project will create a high-resolution simulation platform integrating stochastic climate projections, heterogeneous agent-based modeling of municipal stakeholders, and machine learning-driven vulnerability assessments. Using historical fiscal data from coastal municipalities and climate scenario outputs from IPCC reports, we will parameterize a multi-objective optimization model that balances short-term service delivery obligations against long-term resilience investments. The computational approach leverages parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate thousands of budget pathway permutations under variable carbon pricing regimes, disaster frequency distributions, and intergovernmental funding constraints. By implementing this framework on high-performance computing infrastructure, we aim to overcome current limitations in temporal granularity and system complexity that restrict conventional econometric tools. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of real-time sensitivity analysis for public finance officers, novel metrics for climate-adjusted municipal bond risk assessment, and policy recommendations for adaptive capital budgeting processes. This work bridges computational sustainability science with public financial management, addressing a critical gap in fiscal policy tools for climate-vulnerable jurisdictions while advancing methodological innovations in resource allocation modeling under deep uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: This project addresses the computational challenges inherent in modeling the spatial-temporal structures of American Sign Language (ASL), a visual-gestural language with complex phonological, morphological, and syntactic features. Despite advancements in sign language processing, existing computational frameworks often fail to capture the simultaneous, multidimensional articulations (e.g., handshapes, facial expressions, body movements) that define ASL grammar and discourse. This limitation hinders progress in linguistic analysis, educational tool development, and the preservation of dialectal variations within Deaf communities. To bridge this gap, we propose a large-scale computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and train advanced machine learning models capable of parsing, simulating, and analyzing ASL’s dynamic visual-spatial properties. The research will utilize a corpus of 3D motion-capture and high-resolution video data from diverse ASL speakers, annotated for linguistic features. Computational methods will include the implementation of transformer-based architectures adapted for sequential spatial data, coupled with graph neural networks to model non-linear dependencies between articulators. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of multimodal data, optimizing hyperparameters across iterative model configurations, and running parallelized simulations of ASL phonological processes. Expected outcomes include the first open-source framework for fine-grained ASL structure prediction, which will enable automated annotation of undocumented ASL dialects and support the creation of responsive, AI-driven ASL tutoring systems. By advancing computational methodologies for visual language analysis, this work will contribute to linguistic theory, address resource disparities in signed language research, and promote equitable access to ASL education technologies. The scalability of the proposed models will also establish a foundation for future studies of other under-resourced sign languages globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on American Sign Language as a communication medium or language skill that is, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding how anthropogenic stressors and climate variability jointly influence the resilience of freshwater ecosystems, with a focus on trophic interactions and biodiversity dynamics in temperate lakes. Freshwater systems face accelerating threats from eutrophication, invasive species, and shifting thermal regimes, yet predicting ecosystem-scale responses remains limited by the computational complexity of integrating hydrodynamic, ecological, and evolutionary processes. We propose to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework coupling agent-based models (ABMs) of species interactions with spatially explicit hydrodynamic simulations. The ABMs will parameterize key taxa, including phytoplankton, zooplankton, and fish, using empirical data from long-term monitoring of Laurentian Great Lakes coastal wetlands, while hydrodynamic models will resolve fine-scale temperature, oxygen, and nutrient gradients under multiple climate scenarios. By simulating feedbacks between habitat heterogeneity, species dispersal traits, and population viability, this approach will quantify thresholds of ecosystem stability and identify functional traits linked to resilience. The HPC resources will enable ensemble simulations across parameter spaces (e.g., nutrient loading rates, invasive predator introduction timelines) and high-resolution 3D hydrodynamic outputs at daily timesteps over decadal horizons. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of regime shift risks for regional wetlands, identification of keystone species underpinning food-web robustness, and trait-based conservation strategies for endemic fish populations. This work will directly inform watershed management plans under development by state agencies and advance theoretical frameworks for freshwater metacommunity dynamics in heterogeneous landscapes. The computational pipeline developed will be modular and adaptable to other inland waters, providing a critical tool for prioritizing habitats in conservation networks amid rapid environmental change.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cascading impacts of landscape fragmentation on biodiversity and ecosystem resilience under shifting climatic regimes. As anthropogenic pressures and climate variability increasingly disrupt habitat connectivity, predicting how interspecific interactions and community dynamics respond remains a critical challenge in environmental biology. We propose to integrate high-resolution geospatial data on habitat configuration with mechanistic, trait-based models of species dispersal, resource competition, and trophic interactions. These simulations will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve multi-scale ecological processes across 10^4–10^6 km² landscapes at fine spatiotemporal resolutions (≤1 km², daily time steps). By parameterizing models with empirical data from long-term ecological monitoring networks, we will quantify threshold responses in metapopulation stability, cross-trophic energy transfer efficiency, and functional diversity under contrasting climate scenarios (RCP 4.5 vs. 8.5). The computational framework will employ parallelized parameter sweeps to evaluate conservation strategies optimizing corridor placement and habitat restoration. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maps of fragmentation-sensitive biodiversity hotspots, validated against field observations from three continental-scale ecosystems. This work will advance mesoscale ecological theory while providing decision-support tools for climate-adaptive land management. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling individual-based models across heterogeneous landscapes and conducting sensitivity analyses on ~10^7 parameter combinations, enabling robust uncertainty quantification. Results will directly inform regional conservation policies and UNESCO biosphere reserve planning, addressing urgent gaps in managing ecosystems under concurrent habitat loss and climatic stress.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the origins, functions, relationships, interactions, and natural history of living populations, communities, species, and ecosystems in relation to dynamic environmental processes. Includes instruction in biodiversity, molecular genetic and genomic evolution, mesoscale ecology, computational biology and modeling, conservation biology, local and global environmental change, and restoration ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform digital communication networks and their role in shaping emergent collective behaviors, using advanced computational methods to model multi-modal interactions at scale. The research problem centers on the lack of integrative frameworks for analyzing how information cascades and social influence operate across heterogeneous platforms (e.g., social media, forums, collaborative wikis), particularly when accounting for temporal, semantic, and user behavioral variables. Current methodologies often focus on single-platform analyses or rely on simplified network representations, limiting insights into the complex interdependencies driving modern digital discourse. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-dimensional computational model that integrates natural language processing (NLP), dynamic network analysis, and agent-based simulation techniques. The model will process terabyte-scale datasets spanning text, user activity logs, and platform metadata, utilizing GPU-accelerated transformer architectures for real-time semantic embedding and graph neural networks to capture evolving relational patterns. A novel agent-based component will simulate cross-platform interaction trajectories under varying incentive structures and information diffusion rules. High-performance computing resources are critical for training multi-modal deep learning models, conducting large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to test robustness, and performing hyperparameter optimization across distributed computing nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for quantifying cross-platform influence pathways, (2) identification of latent behavioral signatures predictive of large-scale opinion shifts, and (3) methodological advances in handling temporally asynchronous multi-platform data. By advancing computational social science methodologies, this work will provide foundational tools for studying emergent phenomena in digitally mediated societies, with applications ranging from misinformation resilience research to the design of participatory governance systems. The requested allocation of 200,000 CPU-core hours and 10,000 GPU-hours will enable processing of unprecedented dataset complexity while maintaining probabilistic rigor in uncertainty quantification.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of research studies, measurement of variables, data analysis, and formulation of models. Includes instruction in experimental, quasi-experimental, and case study methods; historical research; participant observation; questionnaire design; sampling theory; and statistical methods.

abstract: Pediatric respiratory diseases, including asthma, cystic fibrosis, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), are leading causes of morbidity and mortality in children, yet many pathophysiological mechanisms remain poorly understood due to developmental variability and limited pediatric-specific data. Current predictive models for disease progression and therapeutic response often rely on extrapolated adult data, which inadequately represent the dynamic growth of pediatric lungs and age-specific immune responses. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing computational models that integrate multi-omics data, longitudinal clinical records, and high-resolution medical imaging to predict respiratory outcomes in children. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale simulations of pediatric lung development, airway remodeling, and disease trajectories under varying therapeutic interventions. Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on heterogeneous datasets to identify biomarkers of early disease onset and optimize personalized treatment strategies. Agent-based models will simulate cellular interactions in developing lung tissue, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will map airflow patterns in pediatric airways under pathological conditions. These computationally intensive workflows require parallel processing capabilities and massive memory allocation to handle terabytes of imaging data, complex multi-omics integrations, and stochastic modeling of developmental variability. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for BPD progression in preterm infants, stratifications of asthma phenotypes based on developmental immune markers, and simulations of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator efficacy across age groups. The project will generate open-source computational frameworks tailored to pediatric pulmonology, enabling reproducible analysis of developmental respiratory biology. By elucidating age-specific disease mechanisms, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches for children with chronic respiratory conditions, reduce trial-and-error in clinical management, and inform guidelines for early intervention. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary scale, speed, and complexity of simulations that cannot be performed on local clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention and treatment of all respiratory diseases affecting infants, children, and young adults, based on knowledge of the growth and development of the lung, assessment of respiratory function in infants and children, and experience in a variety of invasive and noninvasive diagnostic techniques.

abstract: Pediatric rheumatic diseases, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and pediatric collagen disorders, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their clinical heterogeneity, complex pathophysiology, and variable treatment responses. Current approaches to risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making rely on limited biomarkers and subjective clinical assessments, often leading to delayed or suboptimal care. This project aims to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-modal datasets—including genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic, and longitudinal clinical data—and develop predictive models for disease progression and treatment outcomes. A key focus is identifying molecular signatures and biomechanical risk factors associated with treatment-resistant phenotypes in JIA and pediatric lupus. Computational workflows will include large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS), dynamic network modeling of immune pathways, and machine learning algorithms (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble classifiers) to analyze high-dimensional datasets from multicenter cohorts. Additionally, biomechanical simulations of joint tissue stress in pediatric patients will be performed using finite element analysis to evaluate injury susceptibility and inform rehabilitation protocols. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage datasets exceeding 100 TB and execute iterative modeling frameworks. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for early identification of high-risk patients, (2) mechanistic insights into treatment resistance pathways, and (3) open-source computational tools for pediatric rheumatology biomarker discovery. By enabling rapid, data-driven stratification of patients, this work has the potential to reduce irreversible joint damage, optimize biologic therapy selection, and improve quality of life for children with chronic musculoskeletal conditions. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s scale and complexity, which exceed the capabilities of local clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose and treat diseases of joints, muscle, bones, and tendons in children and young adults, including arthritis, back pain, muscle strains, common athletic injuries, and collagen diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing energy-efficient communication systems and electronic circuits through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Modern applications, such as 5G/6G networks, IoT devices, and low-power embedded systems, require precise design and analysis of high-frequency circuits, signal integrity, and electromagnetic compatibility. However, traditional laboratory-based prototyping and single-node simulations struggle to scale with the multi-physics demands and parameter spaces of these systems, leading to prolonged development cycles and suboptimal energy performance. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, parallelized simulations of electromagnetic wave propagation, nonlinear circuit behaviors, and thermal effects in integrated systems. The computational approach integrates finite-element analysis (FEA), finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms to model multi-layered communication channels and mixed-signal circuits under real-world operating conditions. Key objectives include simulating millimeter-wave antenna arrays for beamforming applications, analyzing crosstalk in high-density PCB layouts, and optimizing power distribution networks for minimal electromagnetic interference. The HPC environment will allow for parameter sweeps across thousands of cores, reducing simulation times from weeks to days while capturing transient phenomena and multi-scale interactions. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source simulation workflows tailored for HPC architectures, validated against experimental prototypes, and novel design guidelines for energy-constrained communication hardware. This work will directly support the training of students in computational electromagnetics and parallel algorithm development, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical engineering solutions. By accelerating the design of next-generation electronic systems, the project aims to advance sustainable technology deployment in telecommunications and industrial automation.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronic, and Communications Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of electrical, electronics and communication engineers. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, prototype development and testing, systems analysis and testing, systems maintenance, instrument calibration, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare data, including electronic health records, genomic information, and real-time patient monitoring streams, presents significant challenges for traditional computational methods in allied health research. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing clinical decision-making and resource allocation in heterogeneous patient populations. The research focuses on integrating multi-modal datasets—spanning demographic, clinical, genomic, and socioeconomic variables—to identify patterns associated with health disparities, treatment response variability, and preventable hospital readmissions. Computational methods will include large-scale machine learning pipelines for feature selection and risk stratification, parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to model healthcare system workflows, and graph-based analytics to map care coordination networks. Key objectives include creating scalable algorithms to process terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy regulations, and validating models against retrospective clinical outcomes from partner health systems. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of complex models that account for nonlinear interactions between variables, which is computationally infeasible with standard workstations. Anticipated outcomes include actionable frameworks for personalized care pathway recommendations, evidence-based tools for capacity planning in clinical settings, and open-source software packages tailored for allied health researchers. This work directly supports the program’s mission to advance translational health sciences by providing students and faculty with cutting-edge computational methodologies that bridge clinical practice and population health analytics. Successful implementation could inform policy decisions on healthcare resource distribution while establishing a replicable platform for data-driven innovation in preventive care and chronic disease management.
cip_title: Health Services/ Allied Health/ Health Sciences, General
cip_definition: A general, introductory, undifferentiated, or joint program in health services occupations that prepares individuals for either entry into specialized training programs or for a variety of concentrations in the allied health area. Includes instruction in the basic sciences, research and clinical procedures, and aspects of the subject matter related to various health occupations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in strongly correlated systems, a fundamental challenge in condensed matter physics. While experimental advances have enabled precise manipulation of quantum systems, theoretical progress remains limited by the exponential scaling of computational complexity with system size. Traditional methods, such as exact diagonalization or mean-field approximations, fail to capture emergent phenomena in large-scale systems under time-dependent perturbations. To address this gap, we propose leveraging tensor network algorithms, specifically matrix product states (MPS) and time-dependent variational principles (TDVP), to simulate the real-time evolution of one-dimensional quantum spin chains and fermionic lattices. The research will employ hybrid CPU-GPU architectures on high-performance computing clusters to optimize the contraction and renormalization steps critical for maintaining numerical precision in large bond-dimension simulations. Key objectives include characterizing thermalization dynamics in disordered Heisenberg models, identifying prethermalization plateaus in Floquet-driven systems, and quantifying entanglement growth near critical points. The computational framework will incorporate adaptive time-stepping and distributed memory parallelism to scale simulations to system sizes of ~100 lattice sites, exceeding the capabilities of existing single-node implementations. Expected outcomes include predictive insights into the stability of quantum memory in near-term quantum devices and universal scaling laws for information scrambling in nonintegrable systems. Results will be validated against ultrafast quantum simulator data from collaborating experimental groups. By providing open-source implementations of optimized tensor network libraries, this work will enhance the broader community’s capacity to model quantum matter under extreme nonequilibrium conditions, with implications for quantum computing, sensing, and the fundamental limits of statistical mechanics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the major topics, concepts, processes, and interrelationships of physical phenomena as studied in any combination of physical science disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent collective phenomena in driven-dissipative quantum systems far from equilibrium, a frontier area in modern condensed matter physics. While equilibrium quantum phase transitions are well-characterized, the interplay of quantum coherence, many-body interactions, and non-equilibrium driving in systems such as optically pumped polariton condensates remains poorly understood. The central challenge lies in simulating the real-time dynamics of these open quantum systems at experimentally relevant scales, which demands tracking entanglement growth across mesoscopic particle numbers—a task intractable to classical methods except through advanced high-performance computing (HPC). We propose large-scale numerical simulations using tensor network algorithms optimized for massively parallel architectures to compute non-stationary phase diagrams of two-dimensional driven-dissipative Bose-Hubbard models. The computational workflow will employ adaptive time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (t-DMRG) methods combined with quantum trajectories to handle dissipation, requiring distributed memory parallelism across thousands of cores for systems exceeding 100 lattice sites. Key objectives include identifying novel non-equilibrium phases, characterizing critical behavior near dynamical phase transitions, and quantifying the stability of quantum coherence under driven-dissipative conditions. These results will directly inform ongoing experiments with semiconductor microcavities and superconducting circuit arrays, while advancing computational methodologies for open quantum systems. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster will enable simulations at unprecedented scales, providing fundamental insights into how non-equilibrium quantum matter self-organizes—a question critical to the development of robust quantum technologies and the understanding of thermalization in isolated quantum systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Russian philology and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in the digital study of the Russian language and its historical development. The primary research problem centers on the computational modeling of dialectal variations in pre-modern and modern Russian texts, as well as the automated identification of stylistic and thematic patterns across large corpora of Russian literature. Existing scholarship has been limited by manual analysis methods, which struggle to scale to the vast and heterogeneous body of Russian textual sources. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational approach.
