Traditional data processing frameworks often struggle with heterogeneous formats, fluctuating data velocities, and context-dependent transformation requirements, leading to suboptimal resource utilization and latency in time-sensitive applications. This project proposes the development of an adaptive data processing architecture that integrates machine learning-driven workflow optimization with high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructures to address these limitations. The research will focus on creating dynamic pipeline reconfiguration algorithms capable of autonomously adjusting data ingestion patterns, transformation logic, and storage protocols based on real-time performance metrics and semantic content analysis. Computational methods will include the implementation of parallelized data validation kernels, graph-based dependency tracking for distributed transformations, and containerized microservices orchestrating GPU-accelerated processing nodes. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of multi-source data environments and benchmarking against conventional processing stacks. Expected outcomes include a novel framework demonstrating ≥40% improvement in throughput for mixed-structured data workloads compared to existing ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) systems, along with open-source modules for adaptive resource allocation in streaming data contexts. The project’s significance lies in enabling more responsive decision-support systems across domains such as environmental monitoring, public health informatics, and smart infrastructure management, where processing delays directly impact operational effectiveness. By optimizing computational resource utilization during peak data loads, this work aims to establish new best practices for energy-efficient data processing at scale while maintaining strict semantic consistency across distributed transformation workflows.
cip_title: Data Processing and Data Processing Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master and use computer software programs and applications for inputting, verifying, organizing, storing, retrieving, transforming (changing, updating, and deleting), and extracting information. Includes instruction in using various operating system configurations and in types of data entry such as word processing, spreadsheets, calculators, management programs, design programs, database programs, and research programs.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in machining process optimization by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between cutting tools, workpiece materials, and dynamic operating conditions. Traditional machining approaches rely heavily on empirical data and iterative physical testing, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to predict tool wear, thermal deformation, or material stress under high-speed, high-precision conditions. The proposed research will develop multi-physics computational models to simulate machining processes at unprecedented resolution, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for coolant flow and heat dissipation, and machine learning (ML) to predict tool life and surface finish quality. These simulations will account for variables such as tool geometry, material microstructures, spindle speeds, and vibration patterns, enabling the identification of optimal machining parameters for diverse alloys and composites. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational demands of these high-fidelity models, which require parallel processing of large-scale datasets and iterative optimization across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for virtual machining process design, reducing material waste and energy consumption by up to 30% in trial phases, and extending tool longevity through predictive maintenance algorithms. The project will also produce open-access datasets and modular simulation tools tailored for educational use in machine tool technology programs, bridging gaps between theoretical instruction and industrial CNC machining practices. By integrating computational modeling into machinist training and process planning, this work aims to advance precision manufacturing capabilities while fostering sustainability in small- to medium-scale production environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to plan, manufacture, assemble, test, and repair parts, mechanisms, machines, and structures in which materials are cast, formed, shaped, molded, heat treated, cut, twisted, pressed, fused, stamped or worked.

abstract: This project seeks to develop energy-efficient, secure hardware-software co-designs for next-generation edge computing devices, addressing the growing demand for low-latency, high-throughput processing in resource-constrained environments such as IoT networks and autonomous systems. Current architectures face critical bottlenecks in balancing computational performance with power consumption while maintaining robustness against emerging hardware-based security threats. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-scale computational framework combining electromagnetic circuit simulations, machine learning-driven design optimization, and hardware-aware neural architecture search. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite-element analysis of nanoscale electronic components, parallelized Monte Carlo sampling for statistical verification of side-channel attack resilience, and distributed training of graph neural networks to model device-level thermal-electronic interactions. The computational workflow integrates open-source EDA tools with custom CUDA-accelerated solvers for transient analysis of mixed-signal circuits and physics-informed generative models for materials discovery. Expected outcomes include optimized accelerator designs for real-time signal processing in 5G/6G edge nodes, validated through electromagnetic and thermal co-simulation datasets, and open-access benchmarks for secure embedded system evaluation. By leveraging HPC capabilities to bridge quantum-scale device physics with system-level performance constraints, this work aims to advance design methodologies for energy-aware, trustworthy computing platforms while reducing prototyping cycles through virtual fabrication pipelines. The resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated parameter sweeps across 10,000+ design variants and petascale storage for heterogeneous simulation outputs, enabling unprecedented exploration of tradeoffs between computational density, electromagnetic interference, and adversarial robustness in emerging electronic systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design and development of computer systems. Includes instruction in computer architecture, cybersecurity, electronic circuits, electromagnetism, electronic materials and design, micro-fabrication methods and techniques, signal and image processing, and wireless communication networks.

abstract: Effective insulation systems are critical for optimizing energy efficiency, ensuring safety, and mitigating environmental impacts in industrial and residential infrastructure. However, designing these systems requires balancing complex variables—such as material properties, thermal dynamics, structural integration, and fire resistance—that are difficult to model experimentally. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-physics interactions within insulation systems and develop predictive frameworks for material performance. The research focuses on two primary objectives: (1) creating high-resolution computational models of heat transfer, acoustic damping, and fire spread in composite insulation materials under diverse environmental conditions, and (2) optimizing asbestos abatement protocols through fluid dynamics simulations of particulate dispersion during removal processes. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate insulation behavior across scales, from microscopic material interfaces to full-scale industrial installations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to iteratively refine material configurations and predict failure thresholds. The computational workflows will integrate real-world data from thermal imaging and acoustic testing to validate models. By enabling precise virtual prototyping, this approach reduces reliance on physical trials, accelerating the development of safer, more efficient insulation solutions. The outcomes will provide actionable insights for selecting materials, designing installation protocols, and improving safety standards in asbestos handling. This work directly supports the Insulator program’s mission to advance technical training through data-driven methodologies, while contributing to broader societal goals of energy conservation and hazard mitigation. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational intensity of multi-physics simulations and large-scale parameter optimization, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply insulation materials to pipes, boilers, ducts, refrigeration systems, and related equipment to reduce the passage of heat, cold, sound, or fire. Includes instruction in insulation specifications, measuring and cutting insulating material, applying and securing insulation, installing vapor barriers, insulation system maintenance, asbestos removal and abatement, and safety training.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing trajectory planning and collision-avoidance strategies for multi-satellite constellations in low Earth orbit (LEO) under dynamic space weather conditions. The proliferation of satellite mega-constellations has intensified orbital congestion, raising risks of collisions and cascading debris generation. Current analytical methods struggle to account for real-time perturbations from atmospheric drag, gravitational anomalies, and solar radiation pressure across large fleets. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework coupling parallelized orbital mechanics simulations with machine learning-driven decision algorithms. The computational approach will integrate a high-fidelity astrodynamics model—solving Gauss’s variational equations with adaptive time-stepping—within a distributed reinforcement learning architecture. This hybrid method will simulate thousands of concurrent satellites while optimizing station-keeping and collision-avoidance maneuvers under stochastic space weather inputs derived from NASA’s OMNI datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across constellation geometries, orbital regimes, and thruster configurations, scaling to 10^4–10^5 core-hours for ensemble Monte Carlo analyses. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolset for constellation resilience planning and novel guidance policies that reduce propellant consumption by ≥15% compared to traditional rule-based approaches. The results will directly inform regulatory frameworks for space traffic management and provide actionable insights for operators of Earth observation and communication constellations. By enabling rapid, risk-aware trajectory optimization at unprecedented scales, this work aims to enhance the safety and sustainability of LEO operations while advancing computational astrodynamics methodologies for next-generation space systems.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any program in aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, or space engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address complex challenges in public administration by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the impacts of policy interventions on public service delivery efficiency. Public agencies increasingly face dynamic pressures, including fluctuating budgets, shifting demographics, and crises such as climate-related disasters, which demand agile, evidence-based decision-making. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to capture the interdependencies and nonlinear effects inherent in large-scale administrative systems. This research proposes a computational framework combining agent-based modeling, network analysis, and machine learning to simulate resource allocation strategies across interconnected domains such as emergency management, healthcare access, and infrastructure planning. The project will utilize heterogeneous datasets, including historical administrative records, real-time sensor data, and demographic surveys, to parameterize multi-agent systems representing government entities, service providers, and citizen populations. HPC resources are critical to running thousands of stochastic simulations that explore how varying policy inputs—such as funding distribution formulas, staffing policies, or cross-agency collaboration protocols—affect equity, cost-effectiveness, and operational resilience. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to identify high-risk bottlenecks in service delivery, optimize budget prioritization under uncertainty, and evaluate trade-offs between short-term efficiency and long-term systemic stability. By enabling granular, real-time scenario testing, this work aims to advance computational social science methodologies within public administration while providing actionable insights for policymakers. The results will be disseminated through open-source policy simulation templates and partnerships with municipal governments, contributing to broader efforts to enhance adaptive capacity in public sector management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as managers in the executive arm of local, state, and federal government and that focuses on the systematic study of executive organization and management. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; and research methods.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression and therapeutic resistance in cancers with high clinical relevance to pre-medical education. A critical challenge in modern medicine is the variability of treatment responses across patients, driven by complex genetic, epigenetic, and proteomic interactions. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to model these multidimensional systems efficiently. This project will employ computational methods, including molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven multi-omics integration, to analyze tumor microenvironment dynamics and drug-target interactions at scale. MD simulations will model conformational changes in oncogenic proteins (e.g., mutant KRAS, EGFR) under varying biochemical conditions, while ML algorithms will process genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from public repositories (e.g., TCGA, CPTAC) to identify predictive biomarkers of therapeutic resistance. The HPC environment is essential for managing terabyte-scale datasets, running parallelized simulations across thousands of protein conformers, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous biological data. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel allosteric binding sites for targeted therapies and a framework for stratifying patients based on computational biomarkers. This work aligns with pre-medical training objectives by bridging foundational biomedical concepts with computational tool literacy, preparing students for data-driven clinical research. Results will be disseminated through open-access platforms and integrated into undergraduate pre-medical curricula to emphasize translational applications of computational biology. The requested resources will directly support 12 months of intensive simulations and analyses, enabling scalable workflows that are infeasible on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in medicine, osteopathic medicine, or podiatric medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing multimodal transportation networks under dynamic demand and climate resilience constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome computational bottlenecks in large-scale infrastructure modeling. Urbanization and climate change necessitate transportation systems that balance efficiency, safety, and sustainability, yet existing simulation tools struggle to integrate real-time traffic data, freight logistics, and extreme weather impacts at metropolitan scales. The research will develop a parallelized computational framework combining dynamic traffic assignment models, agent-based freight movement simulations, and probabilistic flood-risk analysis. By coupling GPU-accelerated traffic microsimulations with graph neural networks trained on multi-source datasets (e.g., connected vehicle telemetry, IoT sensor feeds, and climate projections), the framework will enable scenario testing of adaptive traffic management policies, infrastructure hardening strategies, and emergency evacuation routing. The HPC environment is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of modeling 10^6+ agent interactions across 24-hour periods while maintaining sub-minute temporal resolution. Anticipated outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating tradeoffs between congestion pricing schemes, electric vehicle charging infrastructure placement, and flood-resistant highway designs. This work will provide state DOTs and metropolitan planning organizations with quantitative metrics to prioritize investments that reduce travel delay by 15-25%, lower transportation-related emissions, and enhance network robustness against 100-year flood events. The computational workflows will be open-sourced to enable replication in diverse geographic contexts, advancing scalable methods for next-generation transportation systems analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems for the physical movement of people, materials and information, including general network design and planning, facilities planning, site evaluation, transportation management systems, needs projections and analysis, and analysis of costs.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing Burmese literary texts and historical manuscripts using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques, with a focus on addressing challenges unique to the Burmese language’s morphology, syntax, and script. Burmese, a tonal language with a complex syllabic structure and a Brahmic-derived script, presents significant barriers to automated text analysis due to limited existing computational resources, sparse digitized corpora, and dialectal variations across historical periods. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and fine-tune transformer-based language models on a curated corpus of pre-modern and modern Burmese texts, including poetry, legal documents, and prose spanning the 18th–21st centuries. Key computational tasks include script normalization, tokenization tailored to Burmese’s agglutinative morphology, and semantic role labeling to trace thematic and stylistic evolution in literature. Parallelized processing will be employed to analyze syntactic patterns at scale, enabling comparative studies of regional dialects and literary forms. The project will also develop an open-access annotated corpus and NLP toolkit optimized for Burmese, addressing gaps in existing language technologies. Expected outcomes include novel insights into lexical shifts linked to sociohistorical changes, quantitative models of stylistic features in Burmese poetry, and foundational resources for low-resource language NLP. By enabling large-scale analysis of Burmese texts, this work will advance scholarship in Burmese linguistics, support digital humanities pedagogy, and inform the development of language preservation tools for endangered regional variants. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as training deep neural networks on heterogeneous text data and running distributed simulations of linguistic feature extraction across historical periods.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Burmese language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation hypersonic re-entry vehicles through high-fidelity computational modeling of aerothermal-structural interactions during atmospheric entry. Current models struggle to resolve multiscale turbulence, chemically reactive boundary layers, and transient material ablation phenomena simultaneously, limiting predictive accuracy for thermal protection system (TPS) performance. To address this, we propose a tightly coupled computational framework integrating large-eddy simulation (LES) for compressible turbulent flows, finite-rate chemistry models for air dissociation, and nonlinear thermostructural solvers for anisotropic composite materials. The workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform 3D implicit simulations at unprecedented resolutions, capturing sub-mm boundary layer features across meter-scale vehicle geometries. Adaptive mesh refinement will dynamically resolve shock interactions and localized ablation zones, while asynchronous parallelization strategies will enable efficient scaling across thousands of cores. Validation will utilize legacy wind tunnel data from arcjet tests and flight measurements from past missions. Successful implementation will produce the first open-source toolchain capable of full-cone hypersonic TPS analysis with coupled fluid-structure-chemistry effects at mission-relevant scales. Outcomes will directly inform material selection and cooling system designs for the NSF-sponsored HYPERSAT spacecraft program, reducing reliance on conservative safety margins that currently limit payload capacity. By enabling predictive modeling of extreme aerothermal environments, this work aims to accelerate the development of reusable hypersonic platforms while mitigating risks in crewed lunar return missions and Mars entry systems. The requested computing allocations will support parametric studies across Mach 8–20 regimes, requiring petascale storage for high-dimensional output datasets and dedicated GPU nodes for machine learning-assisted turbulence closure model training.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematic principles to the design, technology, and development of systems and equipment used in aerospace and astronautical operations. Includes instruction in basic and applied sciences related to astronomy and astronautics, control systems, fluid dynamics, electrical circuits systems, orbital mechanics, propulsion, remote sensing, satellites, spacecraft centers, spacecraft systems engineering, and space exploration.

abstract: Court interpreters play a critical role in ensuring equitable access to justice, yet current training frameworks lack robust tools to simulate the dynamic, high-stakes environments of legal proceedings. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational platform to model and analyze the cognitive and linguistic demands of court interpreting, with a focus on optimizing interpreter performance under stress. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will simulate multilingual courtroom scenarios integrating variables such as speech rate, emotional tone, regional dialects, and complex legal terminology. These simulations will be powered by natural language processing (NLP) models trained on multilingual legal corpora to generate contextually accurate dialogues, while reinforcement learning algorithms will evaluate interpreter responses in real time. A key innovation lies in the use of generative AI to create adaptive scenarios that evolve based on interpreter decisions, mimicking the unpredictability of live proceedings. Computational models will also assess the impact of cognitive load on error rates during simultaneous interpretation, correlating behavioral data with neural network-based predictions of decision fatigue. The project will further employ parallelized sentiment analysis to quantify how emotional valence in witness testimony affects interpreter accuracy. Outcomes include an open-source training module for court interpreters, validated through partnerships with legal training institutions, and a framework for quantifying competency metrics in high-pressure interpreting tasks. By integrating computational linguistics with cognitive modeling, this work aims to advance pedagogical strategies for legal language professionals while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-STEM domains. The resulting tools will enhance the scalability and accessibility of interpreter training, directly supporting judicial equity in multilingual contexts.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to provide accurate translation and interpretation between two or more languages for parties involved in a legal proceeding. Includes instruction in courtroom standards and procedures, court interpreting, legal terminology, consecutive interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, and sight translation.

abstract: The ocean’s mesoscale eddies play a critical role in redistributing heat, nutrients, and biogeochemical tracers, yet their impacts on regional marine ecosystems and carbon cycling remain poorly quantified due to computational limitations in resolving their dynamic, kilometer-scale features. This project seeks to advance understanding of how these eddies modulate nutrient availability and primary productivity in oligotrophic ocean regions, which are pivotal to global carbon sequestration but vulnerable to climate-driven changes. To address this, we propose high-resolution, coupled physical-biogeochemical simulations using the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) integrated with the Carbon, Ocean Biogeochemistry, and Lower Trophic (COBALT) model. The simulations will resolve eddy-driven processes at 1-3 km horizontal resolution over a decadal timescale, capturing nonlinear interactions between submesoscale turbulence, vertical nutrient fluxes, and phytoplankton community dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational load of multi-year, three-dimensional simulations across nested domains, alongside ensemble runs to assess uncertainty in biogeochemical parameterizations. Data assimilation techniques will integrate satellite-derived chlorophyll and in situ glider measurements to constrain model outputs. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how eddy-induced nutrient upwelling sustains productivity hotspots in nutrient-depleted regions and quantifies their contribution to the biological carbon pump. The results will inform parameterizations of eddy impacts in Earth system models, reducing uncertainties in projections of marine ecosystem responses to warming and stratification. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work bridges critical gaps in resolving scale-dependent processes that underpin ocean-climate interactions, with direct relevance to managing marine biodiversity and carbon sink conservation under climate change.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the ocean/marine sciences, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: This project seeks to advance teacher professional development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize adaptive learning environments for diverse classroom scenarios. A critical challenge in teacher education is preparing educators to design instruction that responds dynamically to variations in student needs, cultural contexts, and resource constraints. Traditional training methods often rely on static case studies or limited live simulations, which lack the scalability and granularity needed to explore complex, real-time decision-making processes. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates multidimensional classroom interactions, integrating variables such as student prior knowledge, engagement patterns, language barriers, and differentiated pedagogical strategies. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to replicate student-teacher dynamics, using empirical data from classroom observations and anonymized student performance metrics to parameterize agents. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning, will then be applied to iteratively refine instructional strategies within these simulations. HPC resources are essential to support large-scale parallelization of simulations across diverse demographic and socioeconomic contexts, enabling the exploration of "what-if" scenarios at a resolution impractical on standard computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated suite of simulation tools for training pre-service and in-service teachers in adaptive pedagogy, (2) data-driven insights into high-impact teaching practices under resource-limited conditions, and (3) open-source visualization modules demonstrating optimal decision pathways for common classroom challenges. By bridging computational modeling with teacher education, this work aims to create scalable, evidence-based professional development resources that enhance instructional equity and effectiveness across heterogeneous learning environments.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Levels and Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education and professional development, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance sustainable pulp and paper manufacturing by optimizing the energy-intensive pulping and bleaching processes through high-fidelity computational modeling. Current industrial methods rely on empirical correlations that inadequately capture the complex, multiscale interactions between lignocellulosic fibers, chemical reagents, and process parameters. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of lignin depolymerization, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of reactor-scale transport phenomena, and machine learning (ML)-driven surrogate models for process optimization. The MD component will simulate solvent-lignin interactions at the atomic scale using reactive force fields (ReaxFF) to identify catalytic pathways for reducing thermal degradation energy barriers. Concurrently, CFD simulations will resolve turbulent flow, heat transfer, and chemical diffusion in industrial digesters, enabling the design of spatially optimized reagent distribution systems. These high-resolution models will inform ML training datasets to develop real-time predictive controllers for minimizing chlorine dioxide usage in bleaching stages while maintaining product brightness specifications. The computational workload demands high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the need for large-scale parallel MD simulations (10^6+ atoms), transient multiphase CFD with adaptive meshing, and distributed hyperparameter tuning for neural networks. Expected outcomes include a 15-20% reduction in energy consumption for kraft pulping, a 30% decrease in bleaching chemical demand, and predictive models transferable to biorefinery operations. By elucidating fundamental process-structure-property relationships across scales, this work will provide a computational toolkit for transitioning the pulp and paper industry toward carbon-neutral manufacturing paradigms. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for MD/ML workloads and high-memory CPUs for large-domain CFD simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and manufacturing of pulp and paper products. Includes instruction in pulp and paper science, pulping and bleaching processes, paper structure and processes, pulp and paper manufacturing, coating technology, surface and colloid science, and fibers.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized treatment strategies for complex chronic conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address variability in patient responses to therapies. Despite advances in precision medicine, clinical decision-making remains constrained by the inability to efficiently integrate multi-modal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, and real-time physiological monitoring—into predictive models that account for individual patient trajectories. The proposed research will employ machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate disease progression and treatment outcomes across diverse patient cohorts. Key computational tasks include training deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment success, and simulating thousands of virtual patients under varying therapeutic regimens to evaluate efficacy and safety trade-offs. These workflows require scalable parallel processing for hyperparameter optimization, large-scale matrix operations, and Monte Carlo simulations, necessitating access to GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel combinatorial treatment pathways for type 2 diabetes and hypertension, two conditions with high interpatient variability. The resulting models will be validated against retrospective clinical data and shared via an open-source platform to enable reproducibility. By quantifying the impact of patient-specific factors on therapeutic outcomes, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice and inform adaptive intervention guidelines. The scale of data integration and the iterative nature of model refinement make HPC resources critical to achieving statistically robust results within feasible timeframes, directly advancing the translation of computational insights into actionable clinical tools.
cip_title: Health Professions and Related Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health professions and related clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying mind-body movement therapies (MBMTs), such as Feldenkrais Method and Body-Mind Centering, which lack rigorous computational frameworks to quantify their therapeutic efficacy. While clinical studies suggest benefits for chronic pain, mobility disorders, and cognitive function, the integration of real-time sensorimotor feedback, neural dynamics, and biomechanical adaptation in these practices remains poorly modeled. We propose a multiscale computational approach combining high-density electromyography (HD-EMG), motion capture, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data from 120 participants engaged in structured MBMT protocols. The core computational challenge involves developing a coupled neural-biomechanical model using hierarchical Bayesian inference to map cortical hemodynamic patterns, muscle activation synergies, and joint kinematics during therapeutic movements. High-performance computing resources are essential for three key tasks: (1) Parallelized processing of multi-terabyte sensor datasets via GPU-accelerated signal decomposition, (2) Training deep neural networks to identify cross-modal biomarkers of therapeutic responsiveness, and (3) Running massively parallel simulations of neuromotor control circuits using spiking neural network models. Expected outcomes include the first open-source computational framework for MBMT analysis, validated against psychometric and physiological outcome measures. This work will establish quantitative bridges between subjective therapeutic experiences and objective neurobiomechanical states, addressing critical gaps in evidence-based validation for movement-based mind-body therapies. The requested resources will enable parameter sensitivity analyses across 10^6 possible neural-circuit configurations and real-time feedback system prototyping at millisecond resolution. By elucidating how intentional movement modulates central-peripheral nervous system communication, this research advances fundamental knowledge in embodied cognition while providing computational tools for personalized rehabilitation protocols in underserved clinical populations, including fibromyalgia and Parkinson’s disease.
cip_title: Movement and Mind-Body Therapies and Education, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in movement and mind-body therapies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Soil microbial communities drive critical biogeochemical processes, yet their interactions with dynamic soil chemistry remain poorly quantified, limiting predictive understanding of soil carbon cycling and resilience. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating microbial genomic potential, metabolite exchange networks, and abiotic soil parameters to predict carbon stabilization mechanisms under varying agricultural management practices. Current models lack sufficient granularity to resolve species-specific metabolic contributions or feedbacks between microbial activity and soil mineralogy, particularly at scales relevant to field applications. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will construct agent-based models parameterized with multi-omics datasets (metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metabolomics) from long-term agricultural trials, combined with spectroscopic soil chemistry profiles. Parallelized simulations will map microbial functional guild interactions across spatial gradients of iron-aluminum oxides, pH, and organic matter composition, while machine learning pipelines will identify key predictors of carbon use efficiency. The computational architecture will implement dynamic flux balance analysis for microbial metabolism and finite element methods for solute transport, requiring distributed memory parallelism to handle an estimated 10^6 microbial agents interacting with 3D soil chemistry grids. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source platform for simulating microbiome-soil chemistry feedbacks, (2) quantitative linkages between specific microbial taxa, extracellular enzyme production, and organo-mineral complex formation, and (3) optimization strategies for tillage and crop rotation practices that maximize carbon sequestration via microbial- mineral synergy. By bridging molecular-scale microbial processes with field-scale soil chemistry dynamics, this work will provide actionable insights for maintaining soil health in intensive agricultural systems while advancing fundamental knowledge of terrestrial carbon-climate feedbacks.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and microbiological theories and methods (in combination) to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instructional combination of microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize furniture design and manufacturing processes through advanced simulation, material analysis, and generative design algorithms. While traditional methods rely on iterative physical prototyping and manual testing, this approach introduces significant delays and material waste. The research problem centers on overcoming these inefficiencies by creating predictive models for structural performance, ergonomic compatibility, and material utilization using high-performance computing (HPC). Key challenges include simulating complex load scenarios across diverse furniture typologies, modeling anisotropic material behaviors in wood composites, and automating design iterations to meet functional and aesthetic constraints. The computational approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling, machine learning for pattern recognition in historical design success metrics, and topology optimization algorithms to minimize material use while maintaining structural integrity. Parametric modeling tools will interface with HPC clusters to explore multi-objective design spaces, balancing factors such as manufacturing feasibility, cost, and sustainability. Expected outcomes include a scalable software pipeline that reduces prototyping cycles by 40-60% and decreases material waste by optimizing cutting patterns and joint configurations. The project will also generate open-access datasets correlating digital simulations with physical testing results, providing validation benchmarks for the furniture design community. By leveraging parallel computing resources, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven furniture engineering, with potential applications in sustainable mass customization and adaptive manufacturing systems. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter sweeps for generative design exploration, and training of neural networks for real-time design feedback—capabilities unattainable with local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare and execute furniture design projects, assemble and finish furniture articles or subassemblies, repair furniture, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of modeling systemic risk propagation in multi-stakeholder insurance networks, particularly in the context of cascading cyber-physical threats exacerbated by climate change. Traditional actuarial models, which often treat risks as isolated events, fail to capture the nonlinear interdependencies between cyber incidents, infrastructure failures, and environmental factors in modern organizational ecosystems. We propose developing a novel computational framework that integrates graph neural networks with multi-scale catastrophe modeling to simulate risk contagion across interconnected business entities, critical infrastructure systems, and insurance portfolios. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to process petabyte-scale datasets encompassing historical cyber incidents, climate projections, IoT sensor networks, and inter-organizational dependency mappings. Agent-based modeling techniques will be combined with adversarial machine learning to stress-test insurance products under compound risk scenarios while maintaining differential privacy for proprietary business data. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of identifying emerging risk accumulation points in real-time insurance markets, quantifying cascading loss potentials through adaptive reinsurance networks, and optimizing capital allocation strategies for parametric insurance products. This work aims to establish new computational benchmarks for dynamic risk pricing in complex adaptive systems, directly addressing critical gaps in next-generation enterprise risk management capabilities. The requested computing resources will enable parallel processing of 10^6 scenario permutations at unprecedented spatial-temporal resolutions, fundamentally advancing predictive analytics for systemic risk mitigation in the insurance sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage risk in organizational settings and provide insurance and risk-aversion services to businesses, individuals, and other organizations. Includes instruction in casualty insurance and general liability, property insurance, employee benefits, social and health insurance, loss adjustment, underwriting, risk theory, and pension planning.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern energy systems, driven by the integration of renewable sources and distributed generation, demands advanced computational tools to optimize grid stability and efficiency. This project seeks to develop a scalable, machine learning-enhanced framework for real-time power system optimization and fault detection, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational bottlenecks inherent in large-scale, dynamic grid simulations. Current methods for transient stability analysis and optimal power flow struggle with the non-linear, high-dimensional nature of hybrid AC/DC grids, particularly under stochastic renewable generation profiles. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid approach combining physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with parallelized finite element solvers. The PINNs will be trained on HPC clusters to approximate solutions to partial differential equations governing electromagnetic transients, while distributed optimization algorithms will handle security-constrained economic dispatch across heterogeneous computing nodes. Key computational tasks include GPU-accelerated training of deep reinforcement learning agents for adaptive grid control, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic risk assessment under cyber-physical threats, and large-scale eigenvalue analysis to identify weak modes in transmission networks. The project will utilize MPI and CUDA frameworks to parallelize time-domain simulations across 10,000+ cores, reducing wall-clock time for day-ahead scheduling from hours to minutes. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for grid resilience analytics, validated against IEEE test cases and real-world data from partner utilities. By enabling sub-second response to contingencies in systems with >50% renewable penetration, this work aims to advance the design of next-generation smart grids while contributing novel methodologies for HPC-driven interdisciplinary research in energy systems and computational engineering. Resource allocation requests focus on GPU nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory CPU nodes for sparse matrix computations in network topology optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of electrical and electronic systems and their components computer theory, computing problems and solutions, including electrical power generation systems; the design of computer systems and user interfaces; and the analysis of problems such as superconductor, wave propagation, energy storage and retrieval, and reception and amplification. c and the design of computer systems and user interfaces

abstract: Geriatric patients often present with complex, multifactorial health conditions that require integration of diverse clinical, genomic, and sensor-derived data to optimize care. Current approaches to analyzing these datasets are limited by conventional computing resources, which struggle to manage the scale, heterogeneity, and temporal resolution of geriatric health data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of geriatric health outcomes and adverse drug events, with a focus on polypharmacy risks and age-related physiological decline. The research will aggregate electronic health records, wearable device metrics, and genomic data from a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 patients aged 65+ receiving care through partner clinical sites. Machine learning pipelines will be implemented to identify multidimensional risk profiles for falls, delirium, and medication-related hospitalizations, while mechanistic models of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic interactions will simulate age-related changes in drug metabolism. Agent-based modeling will further explore how nurse-led interventions can mitigate risks in different care settings. Computational challenges include federated learning across distributed clinical datasets, real-time processing of continuous vital sign streams, and parameter optimization for physiologically based pharmacokinetic models. Outcomes will include validated predictive algorithms for geriatric syndromes, open-source tools for personalized medication reconciliation, and simulation frameworks to test care coordination strategies. By enabling large-scale integration of multimodal geriatric data, this work aims to advance precision nursing interventions, reduce preventable complications in aging populations, and inform clinical decision-support systems tailored to gerontological nursing practice. The requested HPC resources are essential for training deep learning architectures, running parallelized simulations, and maintaining secure data processing pipelines in compliance with healthcare privacy standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize the design of next-generation energy-efficient thermal systems for industrial applications, with a focus on multi-physics interactions in complex fluid-thermal-structural systems. Current challenges in predicting coupled phenomena—such as conjugate heat transfer in high-temperature environments, fluid-induced vibrations in heat exchangers, and thermally driven material degradation—limit the efficiency and reliability of industrial equipment. To address this, the research will employ large-scale parallel simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and transient structural mechanics using open-source frameworks like OpenFOAM and FEniCS. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve fine-scale turbulence models, track phase-change dynamics in working fluids, and simulate long-duration thermal cycling effects with adaptive mesh refinement. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs by identifying dominant parameters for surrogate model development. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for optimizing heat exchanger geometries, mitigating thermal stress in turbine components, and improving the lifespan of high-temperature reactors. The results will advance fundamental understanding of multi-physics coupling in mechanical systems and directly support the design of sustainable industrial equipment, reducing energy consumption in manufacturing and power generation sectors. This work requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and distributed-memory clusters for scaling transient simulations to realistic engineering timescales. The computational datasets and open-source code extensions generated will be shared with the broader engineering community to facilitate collaborative innovation in thermal system design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and end-product systems used for specific uses, including machine tools, jigs and other manufacturing equipment; stationary power units and appliances; engines; self-propelled vehicles; housings and containers; hydraulic and electric systems for controlling movement; and the integration of computers and remote control with operating systems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern communications systems, including 5G networks, IoT infrastructures, and hybrid fiber-coaxial architectures, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize installation, maintenance, and repair processes. Current simulation methods for signal propagation, network traffic analysis, and electromagnetic interference often lack the resolution or scalability required to model large-scale, heterogeneous environments accurately. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-physics simulations integrating finite-element analysis for cable system stress testing, machine learning models for predictive fault detection, and Monte Carlo methods for assessing signal reliability in dense urban deployments. Computational workflows will be designed to parallelize parametric studies of antenna placement, evaluate the thermal-electrical performance of amplification hardware under varying loads, and train neural networks on synthetic datasets representing equipment failure modes. The expected outcomes include optimized installation protocols that minimize signal attenuation, data-driven diagnostic tools for rapid fault localization, and probabilistic models to prioritize maintenance interventions in aging infrastructure. By enabling high-fidelity modeling of physical-layer phenomena and system-wide network dynamics, this research will advance technical education in communications systems by providing empirically validated frameworks for resource-efficient repairs and adaptive system design. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated tensor computations for deep learning applications and distributed-memory simulations scaling to 10^4 nodes, critical for achieving statistical significance in reliability assessments across diverse operational scenarios.
cip_title: Communications Systems Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair one- and two- way communications equipment and systems, including television cable systems and mobile or stationary communication devices. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of communications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational methods for solving inverse problems arising in the analysis of nonlinear wave propagation in heterogeneous media, with applications to seismic imaging and materials characterization. A key challenge lies in accurately reconstructing material properties from sparse, noisy observational data, which involves solving high-dimensional optimization problems governed by complex partial differential equations (PDEs). Traditional approaches suffer from prohibitive computational costs and poor convergence when applied to realistic three-dimensional geometries. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining asymptotic waveform analysis, adjoint-based optimization, and parallelized iterative solvers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to implement large-scale finite element discretizations of the governing PDEs, accelerate matrix-free linear algebra operations, and enable ensemble-based uncertainty quantification across parameter spaces. The project will extend existing open-source PDE solvers using domain decomposition techniques optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures, with adaptive mesh refinement targeting regions of high solution gradients. Validation will focus on viscoelastic wave models relevant to subsurface imaging, where multi-scale material heterogeneities dominate wave attenuation patterns. Successful implementation is expected to yield a 40-60% reduction in computational time compared to conventional full-waveform inversion methods while improving parameter recovery accuracy. Outcomes will advance inverse problem methodologies in applied mathematics by bridging asymptotic approximation theory with data-driven optimization, with direct applications to geophysical sensing and nondestructive material testing. The developed software tools will be disseminated as modular extensions to the FEniCSx framework, promoting reproducibility in computational inverse problems. This work requires access to HPC systems capable of supporting distributed memory parallelism, large-scale eigenvalue computations, and GPU-accelerated linear algebra to manage memory demands exceeding 10 TB for high-resolution 3D simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as engineering and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in natural phenomena modeling continuum mechanics, reaction-diffusion, wave propagation, dynamic systems, numerical analysis, controlled theory, asymptotic methods, variation, optimization theory, inverse problems, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: Emerging infectious diseases and multifactorial health challenges in non-domesticated animal populations present complex diagnostic and management dilemmas in zoological medicine. Current approaches often rely on extrapolation from domestic species, which inadequately addresses the physiological, ecological, and genomic diversity of wildlife, zoo, and performing animals. This project seeks to develop species-specific predictive models for disease risk assessment and therapeutic optimization through integrative analysis of multi-omics data, clinical records, and environmental variables. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to process heterogeneous datasets spanning 200+ species, including whole-genome sequencing, metagenomic profiles, longitudinal health monitoring data, and habitat telemetry. Computational workflows will employ machine learning architectures (e.g., graph neural networks, transformer models) to identify cross-species pathogen transmission networks, host immune adaptation patterns, and pharmacogenomic interactions. Key challenges requiring HPC resources include alignment of non-model organism genomes at scale, Bayesian network inference for probabilistic treatment outcome prediction, and 3D molecular dynamics simulations of drug-enzyme binding affinities across evolutionary divergent taxa. Expected outcomes include: (1) a computational framework for personalized antimicrobial dosing in megavertebrates, (2) predictive maps of zoonotic disease hotspots in fragmented wildlife habitats, and (3) open-access classifiers for early detection of stress-associated pathologies in captive populations. By enabling simultaneous analysis of clinical, ecological, and evolutionary variables across taxonomic groups, this work aims to transform evidence-based care paradigms in zoological medicine while addressing critical gaps in One Health preparedness. The requested computing resources will support containerized workflows across 50,000+ CPU-core hours annually, with GPU-accelerated components for deep learning model training and phylogenetic comparative analyses.
cip_definition: Research focused on the specialized treatment and care of zoo animals, performing animals, and animals living in the wild. May included related research in the principles and procedures used in the observation, diagnosis, care and treatment of illness, disease, injury, deformity, or other anomalies in non-domesticated animals.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized symptom management in hospice and palliative care using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Despite advances in end-of-life care, dynamic symptom control—particularly for pain, dyspnea, and delirium—remains challenging due to interpatient variability in drug metabolism, comorbid conditions, and psychosocial factors. Current protocols often rely on generalized guidelines, which fail to account for real-time physiological, pharmacological, and environmental interactions. We propose an integrative modeling approach that combines pharmacogenomic data, continuous biosensor metrics, and patient-reported outcomes to predict individualized therapeutic responses. The research will leverage machine learning algorithms trained on multi-modal datasets from palliative care EHRs (including genomic profiles, medication histories, and wearable device streams) to simulate drug pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics under diverse clinical scenarios. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale, parallelized simulations of opioid and adjuvant drug interactions across genetically stratified cohorts, as well as for optimizing neural network architectures to handle temporal patterns in symptom exacerbation and relief. Key computational challenges include resolving stochastic variations in drug efficacy linked to CYP450 polymorphisms, modeling nonlinear interactions between polypharmacy regimens and organ dysfunction, and integrating sparse, irregularly sampled hospice data into predictive workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for dynamically adjusting palliative care plans, reducing trial-and-error prescribing, and minimizing adverse events in medically fragile populations. By bridging computational pharmacology, precision medicine, and hospice care delivery, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven palliative interventions that honor patient-specific priorities while addressing the multidimensional complexity of end-of-life symptom burden. The resulting models and codebase will be shared via open-source platforms to foster collaboration in this underserved computational health niche.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: Pediatric gastrointestinal (GI) diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), eosinophilic esophagitis, and biliary atresia, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their heterogeneity, complex pathophysiology, and limited pediatric-specific biomarkers. Current approaches to diagnosis and treatment optimization rely heavily on invasive procedures and generalized protocols, which may not account for molecular and developmental variability in children. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets, including genomic, metabolomic, and endoscopic imaging data, to identify novel biomarkers and predictive models tailored to pediatric populations. The primary research problem centers on integrating large-scale, heterogeneous clinical and molecular data to uncover disease mechanisms and optimize personalized therapeutic strategies. Computational approaches will include the development of machine learning models to predict treatment response in pediatric IBD using whole-genome sequencing and longitudinal electronic health record data, as well as deep learning-based analysis of endoscopic video sequences to automate disease severity scoring and detect subtle mucosal patterns associated with early-stage pathology. These tasks require HPC resources due to the scale of genomic data (whole-genome sequences from 1,500 patients), high-resolution video processing (≈10,000 hours of endoscopic footage), and the complexity of multi-omics integration. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of genetic and metabolomic signatures predictive of treatment-resistant IBD in children, (2) a computational framework for real-time endoscopic disease classification, and (3) open-source tools for pediatric-specific GI disease stratification. The project will directly advance clinical decision-making by enabling non-invasive biomarkers and reducing diagnostic delays, while the computational pipelines will serve as a foundational resource for the pediatric gastroenterology research community. Successful implementation will depend on HPC capabilities for parallelized genome-wide association studies, 3D convolutional neural network training on endoscopic video data, and large-scale integration of clinical and multi-omics datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the digestive systems of infants, children, and adolescents; includes treatment of conditions such as abdominal pain, ulcers, diarrhea, cancer, and jaundice, and performance of complex diagnostic and therapeutic procedures using lighted scopes to see internal organs.

abstract: Veterinary practices face growing challenges in managing complex, data-intensive workflows that integrate electronic health records (EHRs), diagnostic imaging, genomic data, and real-time monitoring. Current approaches to optimizing treatment protocols, predicting disease progression, and personalizing care are limited by the computational demands of analyzing heterogeneous datasets at scale. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that enhance clinical decision-making and operational efficiency in veterinary practice. The research focuses on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to analyze multi-modal data (e.g., radiographs, EHRs, sensor data) for early disease detection and treatment outcome prediction; (2) simulating clinic-wide workflows to identify bottlenecks in emergency response and resource allocation; and (3) optimizing image analysis pipelines for high-resolution diagnostic tools, such as MRI and CT scans, to reduce processing times while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures, agent-based modeling, and parallelized image segmentation algorithms. By utilizing HPC capabilities, these analyses will scale to terabytes of data across diverse patient populations, enabling real-time insights for clinical teams. Expected outcomes include validated decision-support tools for chronic disease management, improved triage protocols for emergency care, and open-source computational workflows tailored to veterinary applications. This work will directly impact the quality of care for animal patients while providing a framework for data-driven practice management, ultimately supporting the sustainability of independent veterinary clinics in an era of increasing technological and operational complexity.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of regular and long-term care to animals, health services to owners, and the management of independent veterinary practices. May included related research in comprehensive care and specialist referral, basic surgery, emergency medical procedures, and diagnostic imaging.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of complex dispute resolution dynamics through large-scale simulations and data-driven modeling. Dispute resolution processes—such as negotiation, mediation, and arbitration—involve intricate interactions among parties with divergent priorities, cultural backgrounds, and power asymmetries. Existing analytical methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear, multidimensional nature of these interactions, particularly in cases involving large groups or multi-issue disputes. To address this gap, we propose developing computational models that simulate dispute scenarios across diverse contexts, including labor relations, cross-border business conflicts, and community mediation. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to represent parties’ decision-making behaviors under varying conditions, integrating empirical data from historical cases to calibrate agent strategies and outcomes. Machine learning techniques will further analyze patterns in dispute escalation and resolution, identifying predictors of successful outcomes. The scale of these simulations—requiring thousands of parallelized iterations to account for stochastic variability and scenario permutations—necessitates HPC resources to achieve statistically robust results. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting optimal intervention strategies in real-world disputes, tools to train practitioners in adaptive negotiation tactics, and insights into how systemic biases or structural inequities influence resolution pathways. By bridging computational social science with dispute resolution theory, this research aims to enhance the efficacy of conflict resolution mechanisms while establishing a replicable methodology for interdisciplinary studies. The project will also produce open-access datasets and simulation tools to support future research in this under-resourced domain, fostering innovation in a field critical to social and organizational stability.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: The development of safe and effective investigational drugs requires robust methods to predict pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and toxicity profiles across heterogeneous patient populations. Current approaches often rely on simplified in vitro or animal models that inadequately capture human physiological variability, leading to high attrition rates in clinical trials. This project seeks to address these limitations by integrating patient-derived multi-omics data, clinical variables, and drug-target interaction networks into predictive computational models. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of drug-receptor binding dynamics under diverse conformational states, coupled with machine learning (ML)-driven population pharmacokinetic modeling. The MD simulations will utilize GPU-accelerated frameworks to sample free energy landscapes for investigational compounds, enabling the identification of binding affinities and off-target risks. Concurrently, ML models trained on electronic health records and genomic datasets from prior clinical trials will predict inter-individual variability in drug metabolism and response. These parallel workflows will be integrated via a Bayesian inference framework to optimize dosing regimens and patient stratification strategies. The computational demands—including the analysis of terabyte-scale genomic datasets, iterative training of deep neural networks, and ensemble simulations across thousands of ligand-receptor pairs—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with parallel processing capabilities and large memory nodes. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate-specific biomarkers for adverse event risk, validated in retrospective clinical trial data, and the generation of actionable guidelines for personalized dosing in upcoming Phase II/III studies. This work aims to reduce late-stage trial failures by prioritizing patient subgroups most likely to benefit from investigational therapies while minimizing safety risks, thereby accelerating the translation of novel drugs into clinical practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on Investigational Drugs and Research

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-resourced African languages by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex linguistic structures and preserve oral literatures. While African languages exhibit rich phonological, morphological, and syntactic diversity, many remain under-documented due to limited computational tools and resources tailored to their unique features, such as tonal systems, agglutinative morphology, and non-Latin orthographies. The research problem centers on developing scalable methods to analyze these features in large corpora of spoken and written texts, including archival recordings of oral narratives, modern digital texts, and transcribed folklore from languages such as isiZulu, Oromo, and Hausa. The computational approach integrates machine learning (ML) models for automatic tonal pattern recognition, neural architectures for morphological segmentation, and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to annotate syntactic dependencies in low-resource settings. HPC resources are essential to train deep learning models on distributed clusters, process terabytes of audio data for phonetic alignment, and run parallel simulations of dialectal variation across geographic regions. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for tonal transcription, a cross-linguistic database of annotated oral narratives, and novel algorithms for morphological parsing that account for dialect diversity. These resources will empower linguists and communities to accelerate documentation efforts, while advancing theoretical frameworks for African language typology. By enabling large-scale, comparative analyses, this project aims to mitigate the risk of language attrition and expand computational linguistics methodologies beyond dominant global languages, fostering equitable technological inclusion for African linguistic heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages native to the African continent, including, but not limited to, Bantu languages, Nilo-Saharan languages, Niger-Congo languages, Khoisan languages, and the Chadic and Ethiopic languages of the Hamito-Semitic language family. Includes instruction in philology, dialects, and oral and written literatures.

abstract: Archival institutions face mounting challenges in managing exponentially growing volumes of born-digital records, particularly complex digital objects such as dynamic websites, multimedia content, and interactive media. These materials often exhibit intricate dependencies, non-standard formats, and evolving technical ecosystems, rendering traditional preservation workflows insufficient. This project seeks to develop computational methods for automating the appraisal, preservation risk assessment, and accessibility of such materials at scale. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on heterogeneous archival datasets—including file format metadata, emulation logs, and user interaction patterns—to identify at-risk digital objects and predict preservation pathways. A central focus involves simulating distributed digital preservation environments through containerized workflows to model format migration bottlenecks and storage tiering strategies under varying resource constraints. Additionally, natural language processing techniques will be applied to extract contextual relationships from unstructured finding aids and donor correspondence, enabling automated linkage between dispersed digital assets. The computational demands of processing petabyte-scale archival corpora, parallelizing format identification across millions of files, and training deep learning models on multimodal archival metadata necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory systems. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for computationally assisted digital preservation prioritization, empirically validated benchmarks for scalable emulation strategies, and novel metrics for quantifying archival integrity in complex digital collections. By bridging archival theory and computational scalability, this work aims to establish new paradigms for ensuring the longevity and accessibility of society’s increasingly dynamic digital heritage.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to identify, manage, preserve, and make available records with long-term value for documentation, legal, research, and other purposes. Includes instruction in appraisal and collection development, information and records management, archival preservation, access systems, management of electronic records, archival outreach, and legal and ethical issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and conceptual evolution of Hindu philosophical systems as articulated in classical Sanskrit texts, including the Vedas, Upanishads, and later commentarial traditions. The primary research problem centers on mapping the development of key doctrinal frameworks—such as the relationship between *dharma* (moral order), *moksha* (liberation), and sect-specific theological interpretations—across geographically and temporally dispersed sources. Current scholarship lacks systematic computational models to trace how these ideas were contested, synthesized, or reified through centuries of philosophical debate, particularly in non-linear textual traditions where intertextual influences are often implicit. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored for Sanskrit, trained on existing digitized corpora and newly encoded manuscripts, to identify semantic shifts, argumentative patterns, and citation networks. Computational workflows will integrate phylogenetic algorithms to model doctrinal divergence among *darshanas* (philosophical schools), alongside graph-based analytics to visualize the diffusion of concepts across regions and sects. HPC resources are critical for scaling these analyses to handle the syntactic complexity of Sanskrit compounds, the volume of textual variants (≈10^6 potential comparisons), and iterative simulations testing historical transmission hypotheses.
