This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy a parallelized forest ecosystem model that couples hydrologic, biogeochemical, and disturbance processes at unprecedented granularity (1 km² resolution across 10⁶-hectare landscapes). The computational framework will leverage machine learning to assimilate heterogeneous datasets, including satellite phenology time series and soil moisture networks, while mechanistic simulations will project carbon sequestration, species migration, and wildfire risk under multiple climate scenarios. Key challenges include optimizing memory-intensive canopy radiation transfer calculations and scaling agent-based tree mortality algorithms across GPU clusters. Anticipated outcomes include (1) high-resolution vulnerability maps identifying forests at greatest risk of drought-induced decline in the study region (Pacific Northwest, USA), (2) quantitative assessments of how mixed-severity fire regimes influence long-term timber yield and habitat connectivity, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive silviculture planning. By enabling near-real-time parameter sensitivity analyses across 100+ climate ensembles, the requested resources will directly address critical gaps in scaling plot-level ecological theory to operational landscapes. Results will support state and federal agencies in prioritizing conservation investments, revising harvest rotations, and designing climate-resilient reforestation protocols. This work underscores the role of computational innovation in transforming passive forest monitoring into proactive, data-driven stewardship.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to manage and develop forest areas for economic, recreational, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in forest-related sciences, mapping, statistics, harvesting and production technology, natural resources management and economics, wildlife sciences, administration, and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interplay between cultural identity and digital media in contemporary Latin America, with a focus on underrepresented Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities. While existing scholarship has documented broad sociocultural trends, granular patterns in self-representation, linguistic hybridity, and transnational digital activism remain underexplored due to the scale and complexity of multimodal datasets. The research will employ computational text analysis, image recognition, and network modeling to process a curated corpus of 500,000+ social media posts, community radio transcripts, and digitized grassroots visual art from 2010–2023 across six countries. Key computational challenges include training custom NLP models for mixed Spanish-Indigenous language content, detecting iconographic motifs in low-resolution images, and mapping cross-regional information flows through temporal graph analysis. By combining transformer-based architectures with community-engaged validation frameworks, the project aims to identify how marginalized groups negotiate cultural preservation and innovation in digitally mediated spaces. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated datasets, visualization tools for tracing discursive evolution, and evidence-based insights into decolonial digital practices. This work will advance methodological innovation at the intersection of Latin American cultural studies and computational humanities while directly supporting collaborative research with partner organizations in Guatemala, Colombia, and Brazil. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive multilingual embeddings, parallelizing large-scale network computations, and ensuring reproducible workflows across heterogeneous data types. Results will inform both academic debates on identity in the digital age and participatory policymaking for culturally sustainable technology access.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic peoples of the North and South American Continents outside Canada and the United States, including the study of the Pre-Columbian period and the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the biomechanical and hydrodynamic mechanisms underlying rapid prey capture in pelagic cnidarians, focusing on species-specific tentacle dynamics that challenge existing models of fluid-structure interaction in soft-bodied organisms. Traditional approaches in zoology have largely relied on empirical observations or simplified analytical models, which fail to capture the nonlinear material properties of gelatinous tissues and their coupling with turbulent flow regimes. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve multiscale simulations integrating hyperelastic continuum mechanics with immersed boundary methods, explicitly modeling the time-dependent deformation of tentacular networks during predatory strikes. Custom GPU-accelerated code will be developed to handle viscoelastic constitutive equations at biologically relevant Reynolds numbers (10<sup>2</sup>–10<sup>4</sup>), incorporating empirical material data from rheometry experiments on live tissue samples. Simulations will quantify energy transfer efficiency between contractile mesoglea layers and surrounding vorticity fields, addressing the fundamental question of how radial symmetry in these organisms enables ultrafast prey immobilization despite low metabolic rates. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for analyzing nonlinear biomechanical systems in understudied marine taxa, with potential applications to bioinspired soft robotics and hydrodynamic sensor design. The resource request supports 18 months of large-scale parallelized simulations across three model species, requiring 250,000 node-hours on systems capable of handling mixed-precision calculations with adaptive mesh refinement. Results will advance functional morphology studies in pelagic zoology while establishing computational tools for analyzing extreme biomechanical performance in non-model organisms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in zoology/animal biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of modeling the complex socio-spatial dynamics of urban environments to optimize the efficacy of ministry-driven community interventions. Urban ministry operates within rapidly evolving, heterogeneous neighborhoods where factors such as economic inequality, migration patterns, and digital connectivity intersect with spiritual and communal needs. Traditional qualitative approaches, while valuable, struggle to capture systemic interactions at scale. This project proposes the development of an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate urban ecosystems, integrating demographic data, geospatial activity patterns, and ethnographic datasets from ministry partners. The computational model will simulate scenarios such as the cascading effects of localized outreach programs, the diffusion of social services through informal networks, and the impact of environmental stressors on community cohesion. Machine learning techniques will be applied to anonymized service utilization records and public infrastructure datasets to identify latent variables influencing ministry outcomes. A key innovation lies in coupling sociological theories of urban marginalization with real-time mobility data and sentiment analysis from community forums, enabling dynamic feedback loops within the simulations. The HPC environment is critical for handling fine-grained spatial-temporal resolution across large metropolitan regions while maintaining the computational intensity required for multi-agent interactions. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for ministry organizations to prioritize resource allocation, anticipate emergent needs in shifting urban landscapes, and evaluate the potential reach of interventions. By bridging computational social science and theological praxis, this project aims to advance evidence-based strategies for equitable community engagement in underserved urban contexts, offering a replicable methodology for interdisciplinary humanities research at the intersection of technology and social ethics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to individuals and groups in urban communities. Includes instruction in bible study and theology, pastoral leadership and care, urban structure and context, inner city ministry, counseling ministries, family studies, homiletics, social ethics, and community organizing.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating emerging digital tools and computational methodologies into art pedagogy, a critical gap in contemporary art teacher education. While traditional approaches to art instruction emphasize manual techniques and subjective assessment, the increasing prevalence of digital art platforms, generative algorithms, and immersive technologies necessitates new pedagogical frameworks. However, the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze student interactions with these tools limits educators’ ability to adapt curricula effectively. This research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model student engagement, creativity, and skill development in digital art environments. Using anonymized datasets from classroom trials—including temporal interaction logs, multimodal artwork outputs (e.g., 3D models, digital paintings), and biometric feedback—we will train machine learning models to identify patterns in creative decision-making and technical proficiency. Computational image analysis pipelines will quantify stylistic evolution across student portfolios, while agent-based simulations will test hypothetical teaching strategies in virtual classroom environments. These methods require HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale visual datasets, parallelize neural network training for generative adversarial networks (GANs) simulating art critiques, and run iterative simulations of pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for assessing digital art competencies through computational metrics, (2) evidence-based recommendations for integrating generative AI tools into lesson plans, and (3) open-source visualization tools to help educators interpret complex learning analytics. By bridging computational analysis and art pedagogy, this work aims to equip future art teachers with empirically validated strategies to foster creativity in technology-rich classrooms, ensuring their readiness to educate students in rapidly evolving digital art landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach art and art appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of oral biofilm-mediated diseases, such as peri-implantitis and dental caries, underscores a critical gap in understanding the biomechanical and biochemical dynamics of polymicrobial communities under clinically relevant conditions. Traditional in vitro models fail to capture the complex spatiotemporal interactions between microbial species, host-derived factors, and mechanical stressors like occlusal forces or orthodontic device micro-movements. This project proposes an interdisciplinary computational framework to model oral biofilm resilience and adaptive behaviors in response to multifactorial perturbations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop a hybrid agent-based model (ABM) coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate biofilm growth, metabolite diffusion, and mechanical strain across 3D-reconstructed dental and mucosal surfaces derived from clinical imaging data. The ABM will integrate strain-specific genomic and metabolomic datasets to parameterize microbial interactions, while finite element analysis (FEA) will map stress distributions affecting biofilm detachment and virulence gene expression. Machine learning techniques will optimize model calibration against experimental biofilm assays conducted under microfluidic shear conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of biofilm vulnerability zones, identification of keystone species driving treatment resistance, and in silico testing of novel antimicrobial surface topographies. By bridging microbial ecology, biomechanics, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish a paradigm for personalized biofilm intervention strategies in restorative dentistry and orthodontics, ultimately reducing device failure rates and antibiotic overuse. The requested HPC allocation will enable simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (sub-µm scale) across clinically relevant timeframes (days to weeks), addressing a critical bottleneck in translational oral health research.
cip_title: Dental Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dental services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of noncoding structural genomic variation in shaping complex traits across diverse populations. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci linked to phenotypic variation, the functional mechanisms of noncoding structural variants—such as copy-number variations (CNVs), inversions, and translocations—remain poorly understood, particularly in non-model organisms and underrepresented human populations. Traditional methods for analyzing these variants are limited by their inability to handle the scale and complexity of population-level genomic datasets. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework integrating long-read sequencing data, chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C) datasets, and functional genomic annotations. This framework will enable allele-specific modeling of 3D genome architecture to predict how noncoding structural variants influence regulatory element activity and gene expression. The project will utilize graph-based genome representations and parallelized algorithms to process multi-terabyte datasets, with iterative simulations to assess variant effects under varying epigenetic contexts. Expected outcomes include the identification of structural variants associated with adaptive traits in plant species and human disease susceptibility loci with previously unresolved mechanisms. This work will advance the understanding of how large-scale genomic rearrangements contribute to phenotypic diversity, offering insights into evolutionary processes and precision agriculture applications. The computational tools generated will be optimized for scalability and released as open-source packages to support the broader genetics community. Successful execution of this project requires access to HPC resources capable of managing distributed memory workloads, high-throughput data storage, and GPU-accelerated modules for deep learning-based prediction of variant impacts.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in genetics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict health outcomes in family practice nursing, with a focus on optimizing personalized care strategies for diverse family units. Family practice nurses manage complex, multi-generational health data influenced by genetic, environmental, and socio-economic factors, yet existing tools often lack the capacity to integrate these variables dynamically. The research problem centers on the need for scalable, predictive models to identify at-risk populations and tailor interventions within family systems. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), demographic datasets, and real-time biometric data from wearable devices. Machine learning algorithms—including ensemble methods and graph neural networks—will be employed to model familial health trajectories, account for interdependencies among family members, and simulate the impact of targeted nursing interventions. Computational challenges include managing heterogeneous data formats, ensuring privacy-preserving data linkage, and running iterative simulations to test care scenarios. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing for training complex models, while agent-based simulations will replicate family health dynamics under varying clinical and social conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to stratify families by chronic disease risk (e.g., diabetes, hypertension) based on aggregated genetic and lifestyle factors, (2) a decision-support system for nurses to prioritize interventions, and (3) open-source code for replicable family health analytics. This work will advance nursing science by integrating computational precision into family-centric care, directly supporting the program’s emphasis on holistic practice and health assessment. The requested resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume (~50 TB of structured/unstructured EHRs) and computational demands, which exceed the capacity of local servers. Findings will inform clinical guidelines and policy recommendations for scalable family health monitoring in primary care settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how rapid environmental change influences the adaptive potential and population dynamics of interacting species in fragmented landscapes. Climate-driven shifts in temperature and precipitation are altering species’ geographic ranges, phenology, and interspecific interactions, yet predicting population resilience remains challenging due to the complex interplay between evolutionary processes, demographic stochasticity, and community-level feedbacks. We propose to develop spatially explicit, individual-based models integrating genomic, demographic, and environmental data to simulate multi-species responses under future climate scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and run these simulations at ecologically relevant scales, tracking millions of individuals across heterogeneous landscapes over multi-generational timeframes. The models will incorporate empirical data from long-term field studies on plant-pollinator networks and vertebrate predator-prey systems, including genomic markers of local adaptation, life-history traits, and dispersal behavior. Computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to evaluate how gene flow, selection, and stochastic events interact to shape population viability and range shifts. Sensitivity analyses will quantify thresholds in environmental variables that trigger destabilizing demographic or genetic effects. Outcomes will advance predictive frameworks for biodiversity conservation by identifying populations at risk of maladaptation or collapse and clarifying how evolutionary rescue might buffer some species. This work bridges evolutionary ecology and landscape demography, directly addressing the Program’s focus on diversity patterns and ecosystem dynamics. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter exploration at unprecedented resolution, overcoming current limitations in scaling population-genetic simulations to realistic community contexts. Results will inform priority-setting for habitat corridors and genetic rescue initiatives, with data products shared through open-access repositories to support broader research on population resilience.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the natural history, life cycle behavior, and ecosystem dynamics of single species and multi-species communities, and the patterns and causes of diversity within and among such populations. Includes instruction in biostatistics, population dynamics, population and quantitative genetics, RNA and DNA sequences, genomics, evolutionary ecology, natural adaptation and hybridization, geographic differentiation, life history and life cycle studies, and animal and plant demography.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the computational modeling of ensemble performance dynamics under varied conducting techniques. Conductors face the complex task of translating musical scores into cohesive performances, balancing interpretive decisions with real-time communication to musicians. Traditional methods for analyzing these processes are limited by subjective observation and small-scale experimentation. This research proposes a computational framework to simulate and evaluate the impact of conducting strategies on ensemble synchronization, expressive accuracy, and adaptive responsiveness. Using motion-capture data from professional conductors, machine learning models will be trained to correlate gestural patterns with ensemble performance metrics derived from audio-visual recordings of rehearsals. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these datasets, as well as real-time simulations of virtual ensembles responding dynamically to algorithmic conducting gestures. The project further integrates score analysis algorithms to map structural features (e.g., tempo shifts, dynamic contrasts) to optimal conducting tactics, generating actionable insights for rehearsal planning. Outcomes will include an open-source software toolkit for conducting educators and ensemble directors, offering data-driven feedback on gesture efficacy and score interpretation. By quantifying the relationship between conducting practices and performance quality, this work aims to advance pedagogical methods, enhance ensemble cohesion in professional settings, and establish a foundation for computational research in music leadership. The requested resources are critical for handling the project’s intensive workloads, including neural network training, multichannel audio analysis, and real-time simulation rendering, which exceed the capacity of standard computing infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the art of leading bands, choirs, orchestras and other ensembles in performance, and related music leadership. Includes instruction in score analysis and arranging, rehearsal and performance leadership, music coaching, arrangement and performance planning, ensemble operations management, and applications to specific school or professional ensembles.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Bengali linguistics and literary analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable large-scale text processing, dialect classification, and syntactic pattern recognition. Despite Bengali’s status as the seventh most spoken language globally, computational tools for its analysis remain underdeveloped compared to Indo-European languages with more extensive digital infrastructure. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, annotated corpora and models capable of capturing regional dialect variations, historical linguistic shifts, and stylistic features in Bengali literature. To address this, we propose building a multi-dialectal corpus of Bengali texts spanning pre-modern to contemporary eras, integrating philological annotations, and training machine learning models to analyze linguistic evolution and literary trends. Computational methods will include neural network-based dialect classifiers, transformer models for syntactic parsing, and geospatial mapping of phonetic variations using distributed computing frameworks. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of textual data, optimize parallelized training of language models, and run iterative simulations for dialect boundary identification. Expected outcomes include (1) the first open-access, computationally annotated corpus of Bengali texts with metadata on regional and historical context, (2) quantitative frameworks for tracking syntactic simplification in modern literary Bengali, and (3) dialect classification models with applications in education, speech technology, and cultural preservation. By bridging computational linguistics with Bengali philology, this work will empower interdisciplinary scholarship while developing replicable methods for under-resourced languages. The requested resources will directly support data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale text rendering for visual analytics, enabling breakthroughs in both theoretical linguistics and applied language technologies for Bengali.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bengali language (Bangla) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize electrical system safety and efficiency in complex industrial and commercial environments. Despite established electrical codes and standards, unpredictable load fluctuations, harmonic distortions, and transient faults in modern power networks continue to pose risks of equipment damage, energy waste, and hazardous failures. Traditional analytical methods struggle to account for the dynamic interactions between renewable energy integrations, smart grid technologies, and legacy infrastructure. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate multi-scale electrical systems under diverse operating conditions. Large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) models will be developed to map electromagnetic field behaviors in three-phase distribution panels, while parallelized circuit simulations will evaluate fault propagation scenarios across hybrid AC/DC microgrid architectures. Machine learning algorithms will train on synthetic datasets generated from these simulations to predict arc flash risks and optimal equipment derating strategies. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers to handle millions of transient analysis iterations, incorporating real-world variables such as aging conductor resistance and non-linear load profiles. Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance frameworks to reduce electrical fire risks, validated mitigation strategies for harmonic resonance in variable frequency drive clusters, and open-source simulation templates adaptable to regional electrical codes. By integrating HPC capabilities into electrical system analysis, this research aims to bridge theoretical training with data-driven decision support tools, enhancing both educational outcomes for electrician trainees and practical reliability for industry practitioners. The resource-intensive nature of coupled electromagnetic-thermal modeling and Monte Carlo-based reliability analyses necessitates access to high-memory nodes and scalable compute architectures to achieve industrially relevant resolution and statistical confidence.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain, and repair electric apparatus and systems such as residential, commercial, and industrial electric-power wiring; and DC and AC motors, controls, and electrical distribution panels. Includes instruction in the principles of electronics and electrical systems, wiring, power transmission, safety, industrial and household appliances, job estimation, electrical testing and inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Aircraft structural integrity and maintenance efficiency are critical to aviation safety and operational cost reduction. Current methods for assessing airframe fatigue, stress distribution, and material degradation rely heavily on physical inspections and standardized replacement intervals, which may not account for localized operational conditions or advanced composite material behaviors. This project proposes a computational approach to model multi-physics interactions in airframe structures under operational loads, enabling predictive maintenance strategies tailored to real-world wear patterns. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop finite element analysis (FEA) models to simulate stress-strain dynamics in wing assemblies, fuselage joints, and landing gear components across diverse environmental conditions. These models will integrate empirical data from material fatigue tests, aerodynamic load profiles, and corrosion rate datasets to predict failure probabilities at microstructural levels. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to optimize inspection schedules by correlating simulation outputs with historical maintenance records. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale meshing for complex geometries, iterative solvers for non-linear material responses, and high-throughput parameter sweeps to account for operational variability. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for identifying high-risk fatigue zones in aging aircraft, (2) validated digital twins for evaluating retrofit modifications, and (3) machine learning-driven maintenance protocols that reduce unplanned downtime by 15-20%. By transitioning from reactive to simulation-informed maintenance practices, this research aims to extend component lifespans while maintaining FAA compliance. The HPC resources will additionally support educational modules for training technicians in computational diagnostics, bridging traditional hands-on practices with Industry 4.0 methodologies in airframe maintenance programs.
cip_title: Airframe Mechanics and Aircraft Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all aircraft components other than engines, propellers, avionics, and instruments. Includes instruction in layout and fabrication of sheet metal, fabric, wood, and other materials into structural members, parts, and fittings, and replacement of damaged or worn parts such as control cables and hydraulic units.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in small internal-combustion engines (ICEs) used in portable power equipment, such as lawnmowers and snowmobiles, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize combustion dynamics. Small ICEs are critical to numerous industries but suffer from suboptimal fuel efficiency, elevated emissions, and mechanical wear due to incomplete combustion and turbulent flow irregularities. Traditional experimental methods to analyze these issues are costly and time-intensive, limiting the scope of iterative design improvements. This research proposes a computational approach using high-fidelity 3D simulations to resolve multiphase combustion processes, turbulent fluid dynamics, and thermal stress distributions within small engine systems. High-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will be developed using open-source frameworks (e.g., OpenFOAM), validated against experimental data from engine test benches. HPC resources are essential to manage the scale of these simulations, which involve transient, compressible flows with complex boundary conditions and fine meshing requirements. Parallelized solvers will reduce computational time for parametric studies evaluating fuel injection timing, air-fuel ratios, and piston geometry modifications. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to simulation datasets to identify predictive correlations between operational parameters and engine performance. Outcomes will include actionable insights for reducing hydrocarbon emissions, improving fuel economy by 10–15%, and extending component lifespans through thermally optimized designs. This work aligns with environmental regulations targeting small-engine emissions and supports technical training programs by providing data-driven repair protocols. The requested HPC allocation will enable the execution of over 500 simulation cases, fostering advancements in sustainable small-engine technologies and their practical maintenance.
cip_title: Small Engine Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain small internal-combustion engines used on portable power equipment such as lawnmowers, chain saws, rotary tillers, and snowmobiles.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in music management, specifically optimizing decision-making processes for music organizations and events in dynamic, data-rich environments. The research focuses on developing computational models to analyze large-scale datasets spanning music consumption patterns, marketing campaign efficacy, and logistical constraints in event management. A key problem lies in synthesizing heterogeneous data—streaming metrics, social media engagement, ticket sales, and artist contract terms—into actionable insights for stakeholders. Traditional methods struggle with the volume and velocity of these datasets, necessitating advanced computational approaches. The project will employ machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, to model audience behavior, simulate marketing scenarios, and predict revenue outcomes under varying constraints. Agent-based modeling will further test resource allocation strategies for concert logistics, venue operations, and artist-fan interaction networks. These simulations will integrate real-world variables such as regional copyright laws, labor agreements, and supply chain disruptions. By parallelizing computations across HPC clusters, the team aims to reduce model training times from weeks to days while scaling analyses to global music markets. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive budget allocation, risk-aware contract negotiation frameworks, and predictive systems for tour routing optimization. Results will be validated against historical case studies from partner music festivals and artist management firms. This work directly addresses gaps in data-driven decision support for an industry facing increasing complexity in audience fragmentation, digital platform dominance, and sustainability pressures. The computational infrastructure requested will enable transformative analyses at the intersection of arts administration, business analytics, and cultural policy, with implications for equitable resource distribution in music ecosystems.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage music organizations, operations, facilities, and personnel. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; music products merchandising; artist agency and promotion; music law; and applications to specific activities such as managing theaters, recording studios and companies, bands and other ensembles, individual artists, and music organizations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the transnational diffusion and adaptation of German-language cultural narratives across historical diasporas in Central and Eastern Europe using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural hybridity in textual and visual media produced by German-speaking minorities between 1750 and 1950—a corpus spanning millions of pages of digitized newspapers, pamphlets, personal correspondence, and artworks. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to analyze this scale of multilingual, multimedia data, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to uncover latent connections and contextualize marginalized voices within broader cultural histories. The project will employ a hybrid computational framework combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for semantic analysis of historical German dialects, computer vision techniques for iconographic classification in visual materials, and network analysis to map cultural exchange pathways. Custom machine learning pipelines will be developed to handle orthographic variations in pre-modern texts and mitigate biases in archival preservation practices. By integrating geospatial mapping tools, the analysis will visualize temporal shifts in cultural production centers and their relationship to political boundaries. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from distributed archives, training domain-specific language models, and running iterative simulations of cultural transmission dynamics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking digitized artifacts to thematic nodes (e.g., folklore adaptation, linguistic code-switching), quantitative models of cross-cultural influence, and new methodological frameworks for ethically engaged digital humanities in area studies. This work will provide unprecedented insights into how decentralized cultural networks sustained German-language identities amid state dissolution and migration, while establishing scalable protocols for computational analysis of underrepresented historical narratives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Germany, the neighboring countries of Austria and Switzerland, the German minorities in neighboring European countries, and the historical areas of German influence across Europe and overseas.

abstract: Agricultural business and management faces increasing complexity due to the integration of multi-scale data—from field-level sensor inputs to global market trends—that drive operational and strategic decisions. Current analytical tools often lack the computational power to synthesize these heterogeneous datasets in real time, limiting the ability to optimize supply chains, forecast pricing volatility, or evaluate risk under climate variability. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model decision-making processes in agribusiness systems, with a focus on enhancing resilience and profitability. Leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML), we will simulate interactions between producers, distributors, and markets under dynamic environmental and economic conditions. The ABM component will integrate geospatial data, IoT-derived crop performance metrics, and historical market records to represent stakeholder behavior, while ML algorithms will predict short- and long-term outcomes of management strategies, such as crop diversification or contract pricing adjustments. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these simulations to regional and global contexts, enabling parallel processing of millions of agent interactions and high-resolution scenario testing. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision support tool that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, sustainability, and risk mitigation for agricultural enterprises. This work will advance computational methodologies in agricultural business by bridging gaps between precision agriculture data and macroeconomic modeling, providing stakeholders with actionable insights to navigate volatile markets and resource constraints. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for ML training and large-memory nodes for ABM ensemble runs, which are infeasible on local computing clusters. By enhancing computational capacity, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven agricultural business optimization, contributing to both academic research and industry practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural business and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dairy product quality and safety are heavily influenced by microbial communities during fermentation, yet predicting their complex interactions remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model microbial dynamics in industrial dairy fermentation processes, with a focus on cheese production. Current empirical approaches cannot adequately resolve strain-level metabolic interactions or predict outcomes under varying environmental conditions, leading to inconsistencies in product quality and inefficiencies in resource use. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metabolomic) with genome-scale metabolic models of key lactic acid bacteria and spoilage organisms. Agent-based simulations will model spatial heterogeneity in microbial colonies within cheese matrices, while machine learning algorithms will identify critical parameters governing fermentation stability. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from pilot-scale fermentations, including pH, metabolite profiles, and microbial composition time series. Successful implementation will enable predictive optimization of starter culture ratios, temperature regimes, and inhibitory strategies against pathogens or spoilage microbes. This work is expected to provide novel insights into microbial resource competition and cross-feeding in dairy systems, directly addressing industry needs for improved process control and waste reduction. By establishing a scalable computational platform, this project will enhance the safety, consistency, and resource efficiency of fermented dairy products, with broader applications in microbial food ecology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of decentralized labor negotiation systems enabled by blockchain technology, an emerging area at the intersection of computational economics, industrial relations, and decentralized governance. Traditional collective bargaining models face challenges in scalability, transparency, and adaptability to gig economy structures, where fluid work arrangements and cross-border labor pools complicate centralized negotiation frameworks. We propose to develop and simulate agent-based models (ABMs) of blockchain-mediated negotiation protocols that automate contract enforcement, enable real-time stakeholder voting on labor conditions, and dynamically adjust benefits based on predictive analytics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to model large-scale, heterogeneous workforces (10,000+ agent-workers with diverse preferences) interacting with algorithmic management systems and smart contract logic under varying economic scenarios. The computational framework will integrate reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive bargaining strategies and network analysis to map emergent power structures in decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). By stress-testing these systems under simulated recessions, regulatory shifts, and sector-specific disruptions, we aim to quantify trade-offs between efficiency, equity, and resilience in next-generation labor markets. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for simulating decentralized industrial relations systems, empirical insights into computational bargaining protocol design, and policy recommendations for regulating hybrid human-AI negotiation platforms. This work addresses a critical gap in understanding how Web3 technologies might reconfigure labor-management interactions while maintaining compliance with evolving international labor standards.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on employee-management interactions and the management of issues and disputes regarding working conditions and worker benefit packages, and that may prepare individuals to function as labor or personnel relations specialists. Includes instruction in labor history, policies and strategies of the labor movement, union organization, labor-management negotiation, labor law and contract interpretation, labor economics, welfare and benefit packages, grievance procedures, and labor policy studies.

abstract: Casino dealing involves complex interactions between dealers, players, and game rules, yet computational approaches to optimize training and operational efficiency remain understudied. This project seeks to model the behavioral and procedural dynamics of casino table games using high-performance computing (HPC) to identify strategies that minimize dealer error rates and maximize game integrity. Traditional dealer training relies on experiential methods, which lack empirical validation across diverse scenarios. By simulating millions of game iterations across blackjack, craps, and roulette, this research will employ agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo methods to quantify the impact of variables such as dealer speed, procedural adherence, and stress response on game outcomes. Machine learning techniques will further analyze patterns in simulated player-dealer interactions to uncover latent factors influencing procedural consistency. The computational demands of real-time multi-agent simulations and large-scale scenario testing necessitate access to HPC resources for parallel processing and data storage. Expected outcomes include a framework for evidence-based dealer training protocols, predictive models for error prevention, and insights into game rule modifications that enhance fairness. By bridging computational analytics with casino operations, this project aims to establish a foundation for data-driven decision-making in an industry traditionally governed by heuristic practices, offering broader implications for workforce development and regulatory compliance in gaming environments.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and knowledge to become table games dealers in casinos or other recreational settings. Includes instruction in dealing techniques for Baccarat, Blackjack, Carnival Games, Craps, Poker, and Roulette.

abstract: This project seeks to advance evidence-based public policy design by developing computational models to evaluate the equity and efficiency of multi-sector policy interventions. Public policy analysis increasingly relies on simulating complex systems where decisions in one domain (e.g., education access) interact dynamically with others (e.g., healthcare funding or housing stability). However, existing tools often oversimplify these interdependencies or fail to scale to real-world population sizes, limiting their utility for actionable insights. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and network analysis. The project will simulate policy impacts across heterogeneous populations using granular administrative data (e.g., census records, service utilization patterns) to parameterize agents representing individuals, institutions, and policymakers. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for large-scale agent interactions, training predictive models to estimate behavioral responses under policy scenarios, and quantifying cascading effects across policy domains. The HPC infrastructure will enable simulations at unprecedented resolution—modeling millions of agents with geographically varying rulesets—to identify unintended consequences and equity trade-offs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for policymakers to test interventions prior to implementation, with applications to education equity, disaster response coordination, and cross-jurisdictional healthcare policies. By mapping how localized decisions propagate through interconnected systems, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error policymaking while advancing computational social science methodologies. The requested resources will support iterative model calibration, sensitivity analyses, and validation against historical policy outcomes, ensuring robustness for real-world deployment.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public policy analysis, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable, predictive framework to optimize integrated pest management (IPM) strategies for diverse cropping systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in real-time decision support for agricultural stakeholders. Current IPM models struggle to incorporate dynamic interactions between pest behavior, environmental variables, and farm-specific management practices at regional scales, limiting their utility for extension professionals advising growers. We propose a computational approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and geospatial analytics to simulate pest population dynamics under varying climate scenarios and intervention strategies. High-resolution weather data, soil health metrics, and historical pest surveillance records will be integrated into a modular platform to predict infestation risks and evaluate the efficacy of biological, chemical, and cultural control methods. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing spatially explicit simulations across thousands of farm management scenarios while maintaining fine-grained temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool for extension agents, validated through retrospective analysis of regional pest outbreaks, and probabilistic risk maps to prioritize outreach efforts. By quantifying trade-offs between yield preservation, input costs, and environmental impacts, this work will directly enhance the precision and adaptability of educational resources provided to agricultural producers. The computational pipeline will also serve as a template for future extension-focused models targeting emerging pests and climate-resilient practices, fostering data-driven agricultural education at scale.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide referral, consulting, technical assistance, and educational services to gardeners, farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and other organizations. Includes instruction in basic agricultural sciences, agricultural business operations, pest control, adult education methods, public relations, applicable state laws and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the operational dynamics of mid-sized religious institutions in multicultural urban environments, focusing on optimizing resource allocation amid shifting demographic and regulatory pressures. While religious institutions increasingly face complex administrative challenges—such as balancing budgetary constraints with community service mandates, complying with evolving nonprofit tax laws, and managing hybrid (digital/physical) engagement strategies—existing management frameworks often rely on anecdotal or static data. The project addresses this gap by constructing dynamic, agent-based simulations that integrate real-world financial, congregational, and regulatory datasets to test adaptive management strategies under uncertainty. Computational models will incorporate variables such as fluctuating donation patterns, volunteer labor dynamics, facility maintenance costs, and legal compliance risks, calibrated using anonymized operational data from 50 participating institutions. Machine learning techniques will then identify optimal decision pathways for resource allocation under scenarios including sudden membership decline, regulatory audits, or emergency fundraising needs. By simulating thousands of interdependent variables across multi-year timelines, HPC resources are critical to handling the combinatorial complexity of these nonlinear systems. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital twin framework to assist administrators in stress-testing fiscal and operational policies, alongside predictive benchmarks for sustainable staffing and program investment. The project bridges computational social science with practical theological administration, offering a novel methodology for data-driven stewardship in faith-based organizations while advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of nonprofit management, behavioral economics, and computational humanities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the business affairs and administration of religious institutions. Includes instruction in business management, principles of accounting and financial management, human resources management, taxation of religious institutions, and business law as applied to religious institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of adolescent spiritual engagement in digital and hybrid ministry environments, a niche interdisciplinary area bridging theology, developmental psychology, and computational social science. While youth ministry traditionally emphasizes in-person community-building, the proliferation of digital platforms—accelerated by global shifts in communication norms—has created complex, data-rich environments that challenge conventional pastoral strategies. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how adolescents form and express spiritual identity across social media, virtual worship spaces, and AI-driven pastoral tools, which existing qualitative frameworks struggle to model at scale. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets from ecumenical youth networks (including text, multimedia interactions, and behavioral metrics), the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) to map evolving spiritual vocabulary, agent-based modeling to simulate community formation under varying digital conditions, and network analysis to quantify the interplay between online engagement and offline spiritual practices. Computational demands include training transformer models on niche religious lexicons, running large-scale simulations of intervention strategies, and processing multi-modal data streams in near real-time to iteratively refine hypotheses. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing hybrid ministry programs, evidence-based guidelines for ethically integrating generative AI into pastoral care, and open-source tools for quantifying spiritual development markers in digital contexts. By applying computational rigor to traditionally phenomenological questions, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for studying emergent spiritual practices while addressing urgent practical challenges in youth ministry training and resource allocation. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—situated at the intersection of humanities, data science, and applied theology—exemplifies how emerging computational methods can advance specialized domains within humanities-adjacent fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to children, adolescents, and young adults. Includes instruction in child and adolescent psychology, human growth and development, family studies, communication skills, religious education, youth counseling, small group leadership, planning and organizing youth activities, volunteer supervision, and youth evangelism and worship.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of immersive, data-driven pedagogical tools for training future history educators. A persistent challenge in history teacher education is equipping pre-service teachers with the ability to critically analyze and contextualize vast historical datasets, primary sources, and conflicting narratives within limited instructional time. Traditional methods often struggle to simulate the complexity of real-world historical analysis or adapt to diverse learner needs. To address this, we propose creating a scalable computational framework that integrates machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and agent-based modeling to generate dynamic, interactive historical case studies. These simulations will model multi-perspective historical scenarios, enabling teacher candidates to practice sourcing, corroboration, and contextualization skills in adaptive virtual environments. The computational workload involves training transformer-based NLP models on curated historical texts to recognize bias and rhetorical patterns, coupled with reinforcement learning agents that simulate student reasoning during historical inquiry tasks. Large-scale parallelism will be required to optimize hyperparameters across diverse pedagogical scenarios while maintaining low-latency responses for real-time classroom applications. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that enables history education programs to simulate complex historical discourse analysis exercises, personalized feedback systems for teacher candidates, and data visualizations tracking pedagogical decision-making patterns. This work will directly enhance the preparation of history teachers by bridging gaps between theoretical training and the demands of contemporary, technology-integrated classrooms. The resource-intensive nature of simultaneously processing multimodal historical data, running parallelized pedagogical simulations, and iteratively refining adaptive learning models necessitates robust HPC infrastructure to achieve both computational efficiency and educational relevance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach history programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the precision and efficiency of ophthalmic lens fabrication by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize lens design and manufacturing processes. Current methods for producing corrective lenses rely on empirical adjustments and simplified optical models, which can lead to suboptimal visual outcomes, material waste, and prolonged production timelines. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating optical theory, patient-specific anatomical data, and advanced manufacturing parameters. High-fidelity ray-tracing simulations will model light propagation through lenses to evaluate optical performance under diverse conditions, while finite element analysis will assess structural integrity during lens surfacing, grinding, and impact resistance testing. Machine learning algorithms will further optimize lens geometry and material selection by analyzing large datasets of patient prescriptions, corneal topography, and historical fabrication outcomes. These computationally intensive tasks necessitate HPC resources to manage parallelized simulations, iterative design optimizations, and multi-parameter sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive models for personalized lens designs that minimize aberrations, enhance durability, and reduce production errors. The project will also generate open-access computational tools to streamline prescription interpretation and improve alignment between laboratory processes and clinical requirements. By advancing the integration of computational precision into ophthalmic laboratory workflows, this research aims to elevate the standard of care for corrective eyewear, reduce costs associated with trial-and-error fabrication, and support the development of next-generation lens coatings and frame materials. The results will directly benefit training programs in ophthalmic technology by providing data-driven insights into optical manufacturing principles and safety-critical testing protocols.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the computational challenges in modeling active matter systems—engineered or natural materials that exhibit autonomous motion or dynamic reorganization through energy dissipation. These systems, such as synthetic particle swarms or stimuli-responsive metamaterials, present complex multiscale interactions involving hydrodynamic, mechanical, and activity-induced forces. Existing simulation frameworks struggle to resolve the emergent collective behaviors of these systems at experimentally relevant scales due to prohibitive computational costs and limitations in coupling discrete activity models with continuum mechanics. This project will develop a scalable, hybrid computational framework combining smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), discrete element methods (DEM), and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model active matter across spatiotemporal scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallelization of particle-based solvers for systems exceeding 10^8 degrees of freedom, while machine learning surrogates will accelerate closure terms for activity-induced stress fields. Validation will leverage experimental datasets from collaborative studies on magnetically actuated colloidal assemblies. The outcomes will provide an open-source software toolkit for simulating active matter, advancing the design of adaptive materials for applications in reconfigurable robotics, energy-efficient smart composites, and programmable matter. By integrating particle methods with data-driven modeling on HPC architectures, this work will establish new benchmarks for computational mechanics in understudied, non-equilibrium systems, bridging gaps between classical continuum theories and discrete, activity-driven phenomena. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for ML integration and high-memory nodes to handle large-scale particle datasets, critical for achieving the proposed methodological innovations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to the application of mechanics. Incudes instruction in method development in solid, fluid mechanics and materials simulations with application to biomechanics and mechanics in medicine, multiphysics, fracture mechanics, multiscale mechanics, particle and meshfree methods.

abstract: The study of toxicant interactions with physiological systems requires advanced computational approaches to address the complexity of toxin transport, metabolic transformation, and organ-specific pathophysiology. Current limitations in predicting tissue-specific toxicokinetics and dynamic responses to emerging biohazards—such as environmental chemicals, pharmaceutical metabolites, or synthetic compounds—stem from oversimplified models that fail to capture multi-organ interactions or inter-individual variability in detoxification pathways. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to simulate toxin distribution, bioactivation, and adverse outcomes across heterogeneous physiological systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK) model integrated with agent-based simulations of cellular stress responses in priority organ systems (hepatic, renal, and respiratory). The framework will parameterize toxin-protein binding affinities, phase I/II metabolic rates, and transporter-mediated uptake using experimental data from in vitro assays and in vivo studies. Machine learning algorithms will optimize model calibration across diverse demographic and exposure scenarios. Computational demands include large-scale parallelization for Monte Carlo analyses of population variability and real-time coupling of organ-level models to resolve systemic feedback. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify dose-response relationships for understudied toxicants, identify susceptibility biomarkers linked to metabolic polymorphisms, and simulate countermeasure efficacy against acute toxin exposure. This work will advance precision toxicology by enabling risk assessments tailored to genetic and environmental variables, directly informing regulatory decision-making and therapeutic strategies for toxin-mediated pathologies. Successful implementation relies on HPC capabilities to manage iterative simulations, high-dimensional parameter spaces, and multi-omics data integration, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of poisons and other biohazards; their interactions with organisms and their food and respiratory systems; and their prevention, management, and counteraction. Includes instruction in toxicological biochemistry, toxic agents and transporters, toxin fate, toxicokinetics and metabolism, toxin classification, molecular toxic mechanisms, extracellular matrices and cell function, bacterial pathogenesis and mutagenesis, pathophysiology and apoptosis, cell stress and injury, studies of specific toxins, and studies of specific organ systems and physiological functions in relation to toxicological problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of biomechanical and neurocognitive mechanisms underlying dance/movement therapy (DMT) as an intervention for trauma-related psychological disorders. While DMT has shown empirical promise in clinical settings, the lack of granular, quantitative models linking specific movement patterns to therapeutic outcomes limits its integration into precision mental health frameworks. The research problem centers on decoding how dynamic, whole-body movement sequences—captured via motion sensor arrays and synchronized biometric monitoring—correlate with neural activity (EEG) and psychometric markers of emotional regulation. A computational pipeline will be developed to process multimodal data streams (kinematic, physiological, and neuroimaging) from 120 participants undergoing structured DMT protocols. High-dimensional time-series analyses, including nonlinear dynamical systems modeling and graph-theoretic network inference, will map intra- and inter-session changes in movement complexity, autonomic arousal, and functional brain connectivity. Deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models) will identify latent movement signatures predictive of therapeutic milestones, while agent-based simulations will test hypotheses about group synchrony dynamics in dyadic or ensemble DMT contexts. The scale of data integration—terabytes of high-frequency sensor inputs per subject—necessitates distributed computing for real-time preprocessing, parallelized feature extraction, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework for quantifying DMT dose-response relationships, (2) mechanistic insights into how embodied movement practices modulate trauma-related neural circuitry, and (3) open-source tools enabling reproducible movement analysis in somatic therapies. By bridging movement neuroscience, computational psychiatry, and dance therapeutics, this work aims to establish a data-driven foundation for optimizing personalized DMT protocols and expanding its recognition as an evidence-based intervention.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use the therapeutic application of creative dance movement to assist in promoting client rehabilitation and physical, emotional, and mental health. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, personality development, movement and motor behavior, psychology, dance, creative expression modalities, improvisation, group psychology and leadership, client evaluation and supervision, dance therapy practice, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Emerging antimicrobial resistance and the increasing prevalence of zoonotic pathogens pose critical challenges in veterinary medicine, necessitating advanced computational approaches to unravel complex host-microbe interactions. This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying pathogen virulence, transmission dynamics, and host adaptation in clinically relevant animal systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled analyses. We will employ comparative genomics and machine learning to identify genetic determinants of antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens affecting livestock, leveraging large-scale genomic datasets from clinical isolates. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural interactions between viral surface proteins and host receptors in key zoonotic viruses, including influenza A and coronaviruses. Agent-based models will simulate disease spread within animal populations, integrating environmental, immunological, and management factors. These computational approaches require substantial resources for genome-wide association studies (2TB RAM/node), parallelized MD simulations (>10,000 core-hours), and real-time epidemiological modeling with dynamic parameter optimization. The integration of multi-omics data through neural network architectures will predict emergent resistance patterns and potential spillover risks. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, predictive models for outbreak containment, and genomic signatures informing rapid diagnostic development. By elucidating pathogen evolution at scale, this research aims to enhance clinical decision-making in veterinary practice and strengthen One Health initiatives through computationally derived insights into animal disease processes with human health implications.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: Occupational and environmental health nurses (OEHNs) face complex challenges in assessing multifactorial workplace exposures and their long-term health impacts on workers. Current risk assessment models often rely on simplified linear associations, which inadequately capture interactions between chemical, physical, psychosocial, and biological hazards in dynamic work environments. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model cumulative exposure risks and predict adverse health outcomes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including longitudinal electronic health records, workplace sensor data, environmental monitoring reports, and employee-reported symptom logs, to construct a multidimensional exposure-health nexus. Machine learning techniques, such as ensemble models and graph neural networks, will be employed to identify nonlinear exposure-response relationships, synergistic hazard interactions, and early biomarkers of occupational illness. HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution temporal-spatial exposure data, optimizing hyperparameters across large feature spaces, and simulating intervention scenarios in virtual worker cohorts. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for identifying high-risk workers, optimizing workplace-specific preventive strategies, and informing clinical decision-making for OEHNs in case management and fitness-for-duty evaluations. The computational framework will advance occupational health surveillance by enabling real-time risk stratification and personalized intervention plans, ultimately reducing preventable work-related injuries and chronic diseases. This project aligns with the program’s focus on evidence-based occupational health nursing practice, leveraging computational innovation to address gaps in exposure assessment and health outcome prediction. By prioritizing scalability and interpretability, the models will be adaptable to diverse industries, strengthening the capacity of OEHNs to safeguard worker health in evolving occupational landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver nursing health care services to workers and worker populations in clinical settings and at job sites. Includes instruction in public and community health, occupational safety and health, occupational health surveillance, case management, fitness for duty testing, medication, allergies and immunization, emergency and ambulatory care, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the precision and customization of ophthalmic lens fabrication by integrating biomechanical modeling, optical simulation, and machine learning. Current lens manufacturing processes rely on static optical models that inadequately account for dynamic interactions between lenses, corneal biomechanics, and individual patient physiology, leading to suboptimal visual outcomes for patients with complex ocular conditions such as keratoconus or post-surgical corneas. To address this, we propose a computational framework that simulates real-time, patient-specific interactions between custom-fabricated lenses and ocular surfaces under varying mechanical and environmental conditions. The project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model corneal deformation and stress distribution, coupled with ray-tracing algorithms to predict optical aberrations introduced by lens-cornea interactions. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-modal datasets—including corneal topography, wavefront aberrometry, and patient-reported comfort metrics—to optimize lens curvature, edge design, and material properties. HPC resources are critical for resolving the computational intensity of iterative simulations across thousands of parametric combinations and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive tool for lens customization that reduces trial-and-error prototyping in laboratory settings and improves visual acuity outcomes by ≥15% in simulated cohorts. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets correlating lens design parameters with biomechanical strain metrics, fostering innovation in adaptive optics for ocular prosthetics. By bridging computational optics, materials science, and ocular biomechanics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in precision ophthalmic device fabrication, with implications for emerging fields such as augmented reality eyewear and biocompatible smart lenses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern distributed network infrastructures has exposed critical gaps in dynamic resource allocation strategies, particularly in environments where fluctuating workloads and heterogeneous hardware coexist. Traditional LAN/WAN management frameworks often rely on static performance balancing protocols, leading to suboptimal utilization during traffic spikes, prolonged outage recovery times, and inefficient energy consumption in large-scale systems. This project proposes a novel computational framework to optimize real-time resource distribution across hybrid network architectures by integrating adaptive redundancy models with predictive failure analytics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop and simulate a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system trained on synthetically generated network telemetry data, emulating diverse operational scenarios—including edge-to-cloud workflows, intermittent node failures, and asymmetric bandwidth demands. The computational approach will combine graph neural networks to model interdependencies in layered network topologies with Monte Carlo methods to assess risk during live system migrations. Key objectives include designing a decentralized decision-making protocol to minimize latency during WAN segment reconfigurations and creating a probabilistic model for preemptive resource reservation during outage events. The HPC environment is essential for scaling simulations to enterprise-grade network sizes (>50,000 nodes) while maintaining sub-second decision cycles required for real-world applicability. Expected outcomes include a benchmark dataset for adaptive network management systems, open-source algorithms for performance-aware load balancing, and quantitative guidelines for cost-performance tradeoffs in hardware upgrade cycles. This work addresses the urgent need for intelligent, self-optimizing network architectures in an era of exponentially growing data traffic and increasingly decentralized computing paradigms, with direct applications in healthcare IoT networks, smart grid systems, and emergency response communication infrastructures.
cip_title: System, Networking, and LAN/ WAN Management/ Manager
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to oversee and regulate the computer system and performance requirements of an entire organization or network of satellite users.
