This project proposes a novel computational approach inspired by collective intelligence mechanisms observed in biological systems, such as swarm dynamics and fungal mycelial networks, to design decentralized, resource-aware algorithms for autonomous network reconfiguration. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate hyper-distributed network topologies with up to 10^6 nodes, modeling stochastic environmental perturbations and multi-agent interactions. Computational experiments will integrate reinforcement learning with bio-inspired heuristics to optimize latency, fault tolerance, and energy efficiency in scenarios including disaster-response mesh networks and contested spectrum environments. Key deliverables include an open-source framework for simulating self-organizing network behaviors, quantitative benchmarks against traditional Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controllers, and theoretical insights into scalability limits of emergent coordination strategies. By bridging computational biology with network systems engineering, this work aims to establish foundational principles for next-generation adaptive telecommunications infrastructures, directly addressing gaps in resiliency and autonomy for critical applications in edge computing and IoT ecosystems. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving statistically robust results across parameter spaces infeasible to test on local clusters, enabling validation of hypotheses at scales mirroring real-world deployments.
cip_title: Computer Systems Networking and Telecommunications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer systems networking and telecommunications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop data-driven tools to optimize individualized education plans (IEPs) for students with orthopedic and other physical health impairments through advanced computational modeling. Current IEP design faces challenges in systematically addressing the heterogeneous needs of students, including mobility limitations, assistive technology dependencies, and variable health-related absences. Existing approaches often rely on qualitative assessments, which can lead to delays in identifying effective interventions. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate student outcomes under diverse educational strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal datasets—including academic performance metrics, assistive technology usage logs, and physical accessibility assessments—while training ensemble ML models to predict intervention efficacy. ABM simulations will replicate classroom dynamics, testing how environmental adaptations (e.g., desk configurations, digital tool integration) and instructional methods impact student engagement and learning. The project will utilize federated learning techniques to preserve privacy across distributed educational records from partner institutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that recommends IEP adjustments based on real-time data, prioritized accessibility features for classroom environments, and evidence-based guidelines for educators. By quantifying relationships between instructional strategies, assistive technologies, and student success, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in special education practices and improve resource allocation for students with physical impairments. The scalability of these models, enabled by HPC, will support future research on equitable AI applications in special education, ensuring tools remain adaptable to evolving policies and diverse student needs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Orthopedic and Other Physical Health Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with orthopedic and other health impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying physically disabled students, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with orthopedic and other health impairments, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Urban educational systems face complex challenges due to dynamic interactions between socio-economic disparities, institutional policies, and community needs. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the non-linear, multi-level systems influencing equity gaps in student outcomes, resource allocation efficiency, and leadership decision-making. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model urban educational ecosystems and simulate the impact of leadership strategies under diverse metropolitan conditions. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to represent stakeholders—students, educators, administrators, and community partners—within interconnected environments that reflect real-world urban contexts. Computational experiments will integrate granular datasets (e.g., demographic shifts, school funding patterns, and policy timelines) with machine learning techniques to identify high-leverage interventions for improving educational equity. A key focus will be simulating the cascading effects of district-level leadership decisions on school climate, resource distribution, and longitudinal student performance. By parallelizing simulations across varying urban configurations (e.g., differing poverty rates, multilingual populations, or safety challenges), the HPC framework will enable probabilistic scenario testing at scale, providing actionable insights for adaptive leadership practices. Expected outcomes include predictive models to optimize resource deployment in under-resourced schools, data-driven frameworks for evaluating policy trade-offs, and evidence-based recommendations for mitigating systemic inequities. This work will advance computational social science applications in education leadership while contributing open-source tools for urban administrators to simulate decision impacts in their specific contexts. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces and iterative model refinements required to address the complexity of urban educational systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on issues and problems specific to the educational needs of populations and communities located in metropolitan, inner city, and related areas and prepares individuals to provide educational services and administrative leadership in urban contexts. Includes instruction in multicultural education, at-risk studies, urban sociology, multilingual education, urban studies and planning, human services, health services and nutrition, cross-cultural communication, diversity studies, safety and security, and urban educational administration and leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance culinary innovation through the computational modeling of ingredient interactions and texture optimization in plant-based meat analogs. Despite growing demand for sustainable protein alternatives, the development of plant-based products that replicate the sensory experience of animal-derived meats remains a complex, iterative challenge. Current methods rely heavily on empirical trial-and-error, which is resource-intensive and limits rapid scalability. This research proposes a novel computational framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML), and rheological modeling to predict how plant protein matrices interact with lipids, water, and binders under varying processing conditions. By simulating shear forces, temperature gradients, and hydration dynamics at microscales, the models will identify optimal formulations and processing parameters to achieve target textures (e.g., fibrousness, juiciness). A curated dataset of ingredient properties, processing variables, and sensory outcomes from existing culinary experiments will train ML models to generalize patterns across diverse protein sources (e.g., pea, mycoprotein). The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space and real-time finite element analysis required for multi-phase system simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for chefs and food scientists to accelerate recipe development, reduce waste, and improve the fidelity of plant-based analogs. This work bridges culinary arts with computational material science, establishing a precedent for data-driven gastronomy while addressing sustainability challenges in food systems. The resulting open-access models and workflows will provide a foundation for interdisciplinary collaborations, enabling future innovations in culinary applications of HPC.
cip_title: Cooking and Related Culinary Arts, General.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of the cooking and related culinary arts, and that may prepare individuals for a variety of jobs within the food service industry.  Includes instruction in food preparation, cooking techniques, equipment operation and maintenance, sanitation and safety, communication skills, applicable regulations, and principles of food service management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary study of cultural and linguistic preservation in Tibetan communities through large-scale textual and spatial analysis. The research problem centers on the fragmented and understudied nature of historical and contemporary Tibetan-language materials, including religious manuscripts, oral histories, and diaspora community records, which are critical for understanding the evolution of Tibetan cultural identity. Traditional methods of analysis struggle to process the volume, linguistic diversity (e.g., Classical Tibetan, regional dialects), and non-standard orthographies of these materials, particularly when cross-referencing them with spatial data on migration patterns or sacred geography. To address this, the project will employ computational methods including natural language processing (NLP) tailored for low-resource languages, geospatial clustering algorithms, and network analysis to map relationships between textual themes, historical events, and cultural practices across time. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on a curated corpus of digitized manuscripts and modern publications, geolocating references to pilgrimage sites using historical maps and satellite imagery, and analyzing semantic shifts in exile community narratives. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of data (10,000+ digitized pages, multilingual metadata), the complexity of parallelizing NLP pipelines for rare language variants, and the iterative processing required for spatial-temporal modeling. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts, visualizations of cultural transmission pathways, and new insights into how Tibetan identity has been reconstituted in diasporic contexts. This work will provide scholars with tools to analyze cultural continuity and disruption at unprecedented resolution, supporting both academic research and community-led preservation initiatives. By integrating computational rigor with area studies expertise, the project aims to establish a methodological framework for studying marginalized cultural systems in resource-constrained contexts.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the optimization of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations and machine learning. Modern HVACR systems face challenges in balancing energy efficiency, reliability, and environmental compliance, particularly under dynamic operational conditions. Traditional empirical methods for system diagnostics and performance tuning are limited in scalability and fail to account for complex, multi-variable interactions inherent in advanced HVACR architectures. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging HPC resources to model thermodynamic cycles, airflow dynamics, and heat exchanger performance across diverse operating scenarios. Large-scale simulations will be conducted using fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) tools to evaluate system behavior under variable loads, refrigerant properties, and component degradation. Parallelized workflows will enable parametric studies of system configurations, optimizing coefficients of performance (COP) and fault detection thresholds. Additionally, machine learning models trained on simulation outputs and real-world sensor data will be developed to predict failure modes and recommend maintenance interventions. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the iterative solving of partial differential equations for multi-phase refrigerants and the training of deep neural networks on high-dimensional datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for energy-efficient system design, a digital twin framework for real-time diagnostics, and open-source tools to bridge computational insights with technician workflows. This research will directly inform curriculum updates in HVACR diagnostics, empowering technicians with data-driven decision-making skills while contributing to industry-wide reductions in energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
cip_title: Heating, Air Conditioning, Ventilation and Refrigeration Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, install, service and maintain the operating condition of heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration systems. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of heating, air conditioning and refrigeration systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale computational analysis of Polish linguistic and literary corpora, addressing critical gaps in diachronic and dialectal studies of the Polish language. While existing scholarship has produced foundational textual archives, the integration of advanced computational methods remains limited, particularly for analyzing morphosyntactic evolution, regional dialect variation, and stylistic patterns across centuries of Polish literature. The primary research problem centers on processing and modeling complex linguistic features in historical and contemporary Polish texts—tasks requiring significant computational capacity due to the language’s rich inflectional morphology, dialect diversity, and the scarcity of digitized resources optimized for machine learning. Proposed computational approaches include deploying NLP pipelines tailored for Polish to process multi-century textual data (14th–21st centuries), training transformer-based models for dialect classification, and implementing phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct historical language change. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale corpora, including digitized manuscripts, dialect recordings, and modern sociolectal data, while supporting GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models for semantic and stylistic analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) the first comprehensive digital atlas of Polish dialect evolution, mapping phonological and lexical shifts across time and space; (2) computational models quantifying the influence of Romantic-era literature on contemporary Polish syntax; and (3) open-access tools for morphological disambiguation and historical text normalization. These outputs will provide novel methodologies for Slavic linguistics, enhance preservation efforts for endangered regional dialects, and establish infrastructure for future computational research in Polish studies. The project’s scale—analyzing over 10 million text tokens across 40+ dialect variants—necessitates HPC capabilities unavailable through standard institutional resources, particularly for memory-intensive corpus alignment and real-time visualization of multidimensional linguistic data.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Polish language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for youth services programs, addressing systemic inefficiencies in service delivery to vulnerable populations. Current approaches to prioritizing funding, staff deployment, and program design often rely on static demographic data or qualitative assessments, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between socioeconomic factors, service accessibility, and longitudinal outcomes. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach coupled with machine learning (ML) to simulate the complex ecosystem of youth service provision. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale administrative datasets—including anonymized case records, regional poverty indices, and service utilization patterns—while training ML models to predict critical outcomes such as recidivism risk, educational attainment, and family stability. The ABM will integrate spatial-temporal data to model how policy changes, budget constraints, and community-specific variables affect service efficacy across diverse populations. Computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to run thousands of parameterized scenarios, enabling sensitivity analyses to identify high-impact intervention points. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for administrators, capable of recommending context-aware resource distribution plans that balance equity, cost-effectiveness, and compliance with juvenile justice and child welfare regulations. This work aligns with public administration priorities by bridging gaps between data-driven policymaking and on-the-ground service delivery, with potential applications in state-level program audits and federal grant allocation processes. By quantifying the cascading effects of resource decisions on multi-year outcomes, the project aims to establish a replicable computational methodology for improving youth service systems’ resilience and responsiveness to evolving community needs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and implement social services for children, youth, and families. Includes instruction in child development and psychology, adolescence, family studies, social work, social services administration, juvenile and family law, program and facilities planning, youth leadership, counseling, probation, casework, applicable procedures and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Immunopathologic diseases such as autoimmune disorders and transplant rejection arise from complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies often lack precision due to the heterogeneity of immune responses across individuals. This project aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative computational models that decode immune dysregulation mechanisms and predict patient-specific treatment outcomes. The research will analyze multi-omics datasets (including single-cell RNA sequencing, TCR repertoire profiling, and proteomics) from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and renal transplant recipients, combined with longitudinal clinical records. Machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be employed to identify immune cell subsets and signaling pathways associated with disease progression and graft rejection. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate the dynamic interplay between immune cells and allografts under varying immunosuppressive regimens. The computational demands of processing terabytes of genomic data and running stochastic simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallelized workflows and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include the discovery of predictive biomarkers for SLE flares, optimization of personalized immunotherapy schedules, and in silico evaluation of novel combination therapies to prolong transplant survival. By elucidating context-specific immune networks, this research will advance precision medicine approaches in immunopathology, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy for patients with immune-mediated diseases.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment and laboratory management of immunologic diseases. Includes instruction in diagnostic surgical pathology, management of organ transplantation and immunotherapy.

abstract: This interdisciplinary research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural exchange and transformation in digitally mediated societies, focusing on how globalized digital platforms influence localized artistic practices and community identity formation. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable methodologies to analyze complex, unstructured datasets spanning visual art, social media interactions, and ethnographic records, which are critical to understanding emergent cultural hybridity in the 21st century. To address this gap, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate and process heterogeneous data—including image repositories, multilingual textual corpora, and geospatial metadata—using a combination of computer vision, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis. Deep learning models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer architectures, will be trained to detect stylistic patterns in visual art and correlate these with sociolinguistic trends extracted from social media. Agent-based modeling will simulate cultural diffusion processes across digital and physical networks, enabling the identification of key nodes and pathways in transnational creative exchanges. The computational demands of processing terabytes of high-resolution imagery, coupled with the need for real-time analysis of streaming social data, necessitate access to GPU clusters and parallelized workflows. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for interdisciplinary cultural analytics, open-source tools for large-scale qualitative data synthesis, and empirically grounded insights into the resilience of local cultural practices amid digital globalization. These contributions will advance scholarly discourse in digital humanities, cultural studies, and computational social science while providing actionable knowledge for cultural institutions and policymakers seeking to balance technological innovation with community-led preservation efforts.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic and geometric topology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve computational bottlenecks in the analysis of high-dimensional topological invariants. A central challenge in modern topology involves characterizing the behavior of homotopy and homology groups under iterative transformations in dimensions ≥4, where manual computation becomes intractable due to exponential growth in combinatorial complexity. Current methods for studying such structures—such as spectral sequence computations for fibrations or persistent homology algorithms for infinite simplicial complexes—are constrained by memory limitations and processing speeds on standard workstations. This work proposes a hybrid computational framework integrating novel parallelized algorithms for chain complex reduction, distributed memory management for large simplicial datasets, and GPU-accelerated calculations of group extensions in Postnikov towers. Key objectives include automating the verification of conjectured relationships between higher homotopy groups of non-simply connected spaces and their covering spaces, as well as classifying transformation actions on wild embeddings of continua in ℝⁿ (n ≥5). The computational pipeline will employ a combination of symbolic computation libraries (e.g., SageMath, GAP) and custom C++/CUDA code optimized for HPC architectures, with verification against known results in low-dimensional special cases. Successful implementation will enable systematic exploration of previously inaccessible regions in the classification space of topological manifolds, directly addressing open problems in shape theory and geometric group theory. Outcomes will include publicly shared datasets of computed invariants, optimized algorithms for persistent homology in non-metrizable spaces, and a framework adaptable to related problems in set-theoretic topology. This work bridges theoretical advances in pure mathematics with cutting-edge computational techniques, offering new tools to analyze continuity and connectivity in ultrahigh-dimensional geometric configurations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of unaltered geometric configurations under conditions of continuous, multi-directional transformations. Includes instruction in mathematical logic, proof theory, model theory, set theory, combinatorics, continua, homotopy, homology, links, and transformation actions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize school-based behavioral interventions by analyzing multi-faceted student data, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address scalability challenges inherent in traditional approaches. School psychologists must evaluate complex interactions between developmental, cognitive, and environmental factors when designing interventions, yet existing tools often struggle to integrate longitudinal behavioral data, real-time classroom observations, and socioecological variables (e.g., family dynamics, school climate). Our research will employ machine learning techniques, including ensemble methods and neural networks, to model how these variables collectively influence intervention efficacy across diverse student populations. HPC resources will enable iterative training of models on large-scale datasets from partner school districts, incorporating time-series analyses of behavioral trajectories and natural language processing of qualitative case notes. A key innovation involves agent-based simulations to test hypothetical intervention scenarios, simulating how individualized strategies might propagate effects within classroom social networks. Outcomes will include (1) a framework for identifying students at risk of poor response to standard interventions, (2) decision-support tools for tailoring strategies based on developmental and contextual profiles, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for allocating school psychological resources. By addressing computational bottlenecks in analyzing high-dimensional educational data, this work aims to advance precision support strategies in school psychology while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for data privacy and algorithmic fairness. The requested computing infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s data volume (~50 TB of structured/unstructured records) and enabling real-time model validation—a necessity for translating research into practical tools usable by practitioners without computational expertise.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: Modern agricultural systems face mounting pressures from climate volatility, resource constraints, and evolving pathogen threats, necessitating rapid development of resilient, high-yielding plant varieties. Traditional breeding methods struggle to efficiently disentangle complex genotype-phenotype interactions in polygenic traits such as drought tolerance or disease resistance, particularly in perennial horticultural species with long generation cycles. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale genomic prediction and optimization of breeding pipelines for key crops, including wheat and fruit-bearing trees. We propose integrating multi-omics datasets (whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomics, and metabolomics) with environmental covariates through machine learning frameworks to model trait heritability under stress scenarios. Computational workflows will implement Bayesian neural networks for genomic selection and parallelized genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across simulated climate futures. HPC capacity is critical for training these models on terabyte-scale datasets encompassing 50,000+ plant accessions and 10 billion genomic markers. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of pleiotropic genetic regulators influencing stress-adaptive traits, (2) optimized parental selection algorithms to maximize genetic gain in multi-trait breeding objectives, and (3) open-source predictive tools for accelerating hybrid development cycles by 40-60% compared to conventional methods. The computational infrastructure will directly support marker-assisted breeding programs targeting durable resistance to emerging fungal pathogens in staple crops and enhanced water-use efficiency in orchard systems. By bridging genomic complexity with predictive analytics, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for precision plant breeding that addresses urgent food security challenges while reducing land and input requirements. Resulting models and datasets will be disseminated through agricultural extension networks to empower breeding initiatives across diverse agroecological zones.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural plant health, the development of new plant varieties, and the selective improvement of agricultural plant populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, agronomy, plant protection, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of data-driven pedagogical frameworks for bilingual and multilingual classrooms by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex language acquisition dynamics. Current approaches to designing instructional strategies for multilingual learners often rely on qualitative assessments or small-scale quantitative studies, limiting their ability to account for the interrelated cognitive, sociocultural, and linguistic variables influencing language development. To address this gap, we propose a computational study analyzing longitudinal datasets of student interactions, language proficiency metrics, and instructional materials from diverse bilingual education programs. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, we will process multilingual classroom transcripts and written work to identify patterns in code-switching, metalinguistic awareness, and cross-linguistic transfer. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how variations in instructional pacing, language allocation policies, and home-school language disparities affect long-term bilingual outcomes. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train transformer-based NLP models on low-resource languages, and run parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing language distribution in curricula, (2) predictive tools to identify at-risk multilingual learners, and (3) open-source computational frameworks for modeling bilingual pedagogies. By elucidating the nonlinear interactions between instructional variables and language development, this work will directly inform teacher preparation programs and provide scalable methods for personalizing multilingual education in heterogeneous classrooms. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional data and complex system dynamics inherent to this research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to bilingual/bicultural children or adults, and/or the design and implementation of educational programs having the goal of producing bilingual/bicultural individuals. Includes preparation to serve as teachers and administrators in bilingual/bicultural education programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic structural mechanisms underlying enzymatic catalysis in oxidoreductases, a critical class of enzymes involved in cellular redox reactions and metabolic pathways. Despite their biological importance, the atomic-level details of how conformational changes and transient intermediate states govern catalytic efficiency and substrate specificity remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental techniques struggle to capture these rapid, stochastic processes, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose to perform large-scale, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the structural dynamics of two oxidoreductases: glutathione reductase and thioredoxin reductase. These enzymes, essential for maintaining redox homeostasis, exhibit complex cofactor-mediated mechanisms that are hypothesized to depend on precise electrostatic interactions and solvent-mediated proton transfers. Simulations will integrate enhanced sampling techniques (e.g., metadynamics, replica exchange) to overcome timescale limitations and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) methods to model electron transfer events. The HPC environment is critical for achieving the required spatial-temporal resolution, as each system involves ~150,000 atoms and necessitates microsecond-scale sampling across multiple replicas. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of key residues and solvent networks that stabilize transition states, (2) characterization of allosteric communication pathways between cofactor-binding domains and active sites, and (3) thermodynamic profiles of rate-limiting steps in catalysis. These insights will advance fundamental understanding of redox enzyme mechanisms and inform the rational design of engineered variants with enhanced stability for industrial biocatalysis. The computational workflows developed will also serve as a template for studying other undercharacterized enzymes in the oxidoreductase family, bridging gaps between structural biochemistry and functional proteomics. Successful execution of this project requires robust HPC resources to manage the storage, parallel processing, and analysis of multi-terabyte simulation datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the chemistry of living systems, their fundamental chemical substances and reactions, and their chemical pathways and information transfer systems, with particular reference to carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. Includes instruction in bio-organic chemistry, protein chemistry, bioanalytical chemistry, bioseparations, regulatory biochemistry, enzymology, hormonal chemistry, calorimetry, and research methods and equipment operation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing water supply systems for resilience against contamination and variable demand using advanced computational modeling. Despite advancements in plumbing infrastructure, aging systems and emerging contaminants (e.g., Legionella, microplastics) pose persistent public health risks, particularly in complex urban networks. Traditional hydraulic models lack the resolution to predict localized stagnation, biofilm formation, or chemical disinfection efficacy at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating fluid dynamics, water quality simulations, and machine learning to analyze pipe networks at unprecedented spatiotemporal detail. The research will develop parallelized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models using OpenFOAM to simulate flow regimes, solute transport, and microbial growth dynamics in multi-branch systems under varying pressure conditions. Machine learning surrogates will reduce the computational cost of scenario testing for infrastructure retrofits, such as looped vs. branched layouts or smart valve placements. Additionally, graph neural networks will predict contamination spread patterns using synthetic training data generated from HPC simulations. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to handle millions of cell meshes for 3D pipe geometries and years of operational data. Outcomes include open-source tools for designing contamination-resistant plumbing systems, risk maps identifying high-stagnation zones in municipal networks, and evidence-based guidelines for pipe material selection. By enabling fine-grained analysis of water age, disinfectant decay, and biofilm hotspots, this work aims to reduce waterborne disease risks while improving energy efficiency in recirculation systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling simulations to real-world network sizes and informing next-generation plumbing codes and smart sensor deployment strategies.
cip_title: Plumbing and Related Water Supply Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in plumbing and related water supply services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational sculpting framework that integrates advanced material behavior simulations and generative design algorithms to expand the creative and technical possibilities of three-dimensional art. Traditional sculpture practices face limitations in prototyping complex forms, especially when working with materials that have nonlinear physical properties (e.g., metal under stress, composite media) or when designing large-scale installations requiring structural validation. To address this, we propose a hybrid methodology combining finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML)-driven generative adversarial networks (GANs), and real-time 3D topology optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing these computationally intensive processes, which involve iterative simulations of material deformation, stress distribution, and environmental interactions (e.g., wind, load-bearing capacity) at fine spatial resolutions. ML models will be trained on datasets of historical and contemporary sculptures to generate novel form proposals, while FEA will validate their feasibility under physical constraints. A key innovation lies in coupling these tools into an interactive digital workspace, enabling artists to manipulate virtual models with immediate feedback on structural and material limits. Expected outcomes include a scalable software pipeline for computational sculpting, a repository of simulated material profiles, and a series of physically optimized sculpture prototypes fabricated using additive manufacturing. This research bridges gaps between artistic intuition and engineering rigor, offering new methods to explore form, scale, and materiality while reducing reliance on resource-intensive physical trials. The project will also contribute open-source tools to the digital arts community, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between visual artists, computational scientists, and material engineers.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by creating three-dimensional art works. Includes instruction in the analysis of form in space; round and relief concepts; sculptural composition; modern and experimental methods; different media such as clay, plaster, wood, stone, and metal; techniques such as carving, molding, welding, casting, and modeling; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of consumer decision-making dynamics in digital apparel marketplaces, an under-researched area at the intersection of behavioral economics, computational social science, and digital marketing. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable models to simulate and predict how emerging technologies—such as virtual try-on systems, AI-generated fashion influencers, and blockchain-based authentication—reshape purchasing behaviors in real-time, data-rich environments. Traditional consumer behavior frameworks struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between user-generated content, algorithmic personalization, and cultural trends in globalized digital markets. To address this gap, the project proposes developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate millions of heterogeneous consumer agents interacting with dynamic digital retail ecosystems. These models will integrate natural language processing (NLP) of social media trends, computer vision analysis of virtual garment customization patterns, and reinforcement learning algorithms to capture adaptive consumer preferences. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the need for parallelized simulations across diverse demographic scenarios, real-time processing of multi-modal data streams (text, image, and transactional), and sensitivity analyses testing market resilience under supply chain disruptions. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying the impact of immersive technologies on brand loyalty, as well as open-source tools for optimizing adaptive pricing and inventory strategies in hybrid physical-digital retail environments. By bridging computational modeling with apparel marketing theory, this work aims to establish best practices for data-driven decision-making in an industry increasingly dominated by ephemeral trends and decentralized digital platforms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on marketing research and management as applied to the products and services of the apparel and textile industries. Includes instruction in applicable principles of textile and apparel design and manufacturing, sales and distribution systems, domestic and international market research, profitability, consumer research, and the design and implementation of marketing campaigns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale comparative analysis of textual variants and transmission histories across multilingual manuscript corpora. Traditional textual criticism and stemmatology face challenges in systematically evaluating relationships among thousands of manuscript witnesses, particularly when working with non-Latin scripts, fragmentary sources, or understudied textual traditions. This research addresses these limitations by developing computational workflows to model textual evolution, scribal practices, and cultural exchange networks across premodern Eurasia. The project integrates machine learning-based optical character recognition (OCR) for digitized manuscripts in Arabic, Syriac, and Greek scripts with phylogenetic clustering algorithms adapted from computational biology. By reconstructing hypothetical archetypes and mapping variant distributions across time and space, the team will test hypotheses about textual dissemination routes and the impact of translation practices on literary transmission. A key innovation involves parallelized processing of high-resolution manuscript images (≥10 TB) paired with collation of textual variants at scale, enabled by GPU-accelerated NLP pipelines. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital corpus of aligned textual variants, computational tools for cross-cultural stemmatic analysis, and quantitative models of how paratextual features (marginalia, annotations) correlate with textual instability. This work will provide humanities scholars with new methods to trace the interconnected histories of texts that circulated between medieval Islamic, Byzantine, and European manuscript cultures, while advancing interdisciplinary frameworks for computational textual scholarship. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive alignment tasks, training domain-specific OCR models, and running iterative simulations of textual transmission dynamics across distributed manuscript traditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interconnected histories of digital or print texts and manuscripts for cultural and literary study. Includes instruction in archiving texts, bibliography, book and literary history, cultural studies, codicology, paleography, stemmatology, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neural and behavioral mechanisms underlying hypnotherapy’s efficacy in modulating pain perception and emotional regulation. Despite growing clinical interest in hypnotherapy as a non-pharmacological intervention, the neurocomputational basis of its therapeutic effects remains poorly understood. Current limitations include insufficient resolution in modeling dynamic brain-state transitions during trance induction and a lack of scalable frameworks to simulate individualized therapeutic protocols. To address this, we propose a multi-modal computational approach integrating functional neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG) with behavioral data from clinical hypnotherapy sessions. HPC resources will enable the development of a biophysical neural network model optimized to simulate cortical-subcortical interactions during hypnosis, incorporating real-time feedback mechanisms and variability across patient phenotypes. Machine learning pipelines will be deployed to analyze high-dimensional datasets (spanning neural oscillations, autonomic responses, and self-reported symptom profiles) and identify predictive biomarkers of therapeutic response. Additionally, agent-based modeling will explore how therapist-client interactions influence trance depth and treatment outcomes. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across GPU clusters, we aim to generate the first large-scale, dynamic simulations of hypnotherapy processes, bridging gaps between neurobiology and clinical practice. Expected outcomes include validated computational biomarkers for optimizing hypnotic suggestion protocols, a predictive framework for personalizing interventions in chronic pain and anxiety disorders, and open-source tools for simulating neurobehavioral responses to hypnosis. This work will establish a foundation for data-driven hypnotherapy research, advancing its integration into precision health paradigms while addressing critical gaps in mechanistic understanding. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the scale, speed, and complexity of modeling brain-behavior dynamics in real-time therapeutic contexts, which cannot feasibly be achieved with standard computational resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to employ the controlled inducement of altered states of consciousness, or trance, to reduce pain, resolve emotional conflicts, and enhance communications as part of diagnostic and treatment programs. Includes instruction in the principles of hypnosis and suggestion, induction and deepening, post-hypnotic suggestion, awakening techniques, regression, pacing and leading, resistance transformation, client testing and management, practice management and regulation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the emergent dynamics of quantum-coherent processes in biological energy transfer systems, an interdisciplinary frontier bridging molecular biophysics, quantum chemistry, and condensed matter physics. While classical models dominate studies of biological systems, recent experimental evidence suggests that quantum phenomena, such as entanglement and coherence, may play critical roles in optimizing energy transport in photosynthetic complexes and enzymatic reactions. However, simulating these processes requires integrating quantum mechanical principles with large-scale biomolecular dynamics—a computational challenge unaddressed by conventional tools. The research aims to develop hybrid quantum-classical simulation frameworks to model exciton transport in pigment-protein complexes under physiologically relevant conditions. This involves coupling time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) with GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to capture transient electronic interactions across fluctuating protein scaffolds. A key innovation lies in adaptive quantum embedding algorithms that dynamically partition regions treated with quantum accuracy versus classical approximations, balancing computational cost and precision. The HPC workflow will employ scalable MPI-OpenMP parallelization for ensemble simulations across parameter spaces, including temperature gradients and electromagnetic field perturbations, to identify conditions favoring sustained coherence. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how biological systems harness quantum effects for functional advantages, validated against ultrafast spectroscopic data from collaborating experimental groups. By bridging quantum physics and molecular biology, this work could inform bio-inspired quantum materials design and advance theoretical frameworks for studying non-trivial quantum effects in living systems. The computational methodologies developed will be open-sourced to catalyze interdisciplinary research at the intersection of quantum physics and life sciences.
cip_definition: A program that is either a general synthesis of one or more of the biological and physical sciences, or a specialization which draws from the biological and physical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized neuromuscular rehabilitation strategies by modeling the dynamic interplay between biomechanical forces, neural adaptation, and tissue remodeling in patients with acquired movement disorders. Current clinical approaches to physical therapy often rely on generalized protocols, which fail to account for individual variability in motor control patterns, connective tissue properties, and neuroplastic potential. We propose to address this gap by integrating high-resolution motion capture data, electromyography (EMG), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and patient-specific musculoskeletal simulations into a unified machine learning pipeline. High-performance computing resources will be critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets spanning 3D kinematic trajectories, muscle activation timeseries, and white matter tractography from stroke survivors and spinal cord injury patients. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms will train adaptive therapy agents on simulated neuromuscular environments, while finite element modeling will predict load-dependent tissue microdamage and repair processes during repetitive therapeutic exercises. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition to identify latent movement control signatures and predict optimal exercise dosing parameters. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for estimating patient-specific recovery trajectories under varying intervention scenarios, as well as open-source tools for real-time biomechanical risk assessment during rehabilitation. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, soft tissue mechanics, and clinical decision-making in physical therapy, offering a paradigm shift toward precision neuromusculoskeletal rehabilitation. By elucidating how individualized neural reorganization patterns modulate mechanical stressors during recovery, the project aims to establish computational biomarkers for therapy response, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice and informing the development of next-generation assistive robotics interfaces.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate, examine, diagnose, and alleviate physical functional impairments and limitations caused by injury or disease through the design and implementation of therapeutic interventions to promote fitness and health. Includes instruction in anatomy, behavioral sciences, biology, biomechanics, biophysical agents, care plan development and documentation, cellular histology, clinical evaluation and measurement, clinical reasoning, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, professional standards and ethics, rehabilitation psychology, and therapeutic exercise.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility of real-time court reporting and captioning through advanced machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP). While court reporting relies on specialized skills in legal terminology, shorthand, and transcription, current tools struggle with real-time processing of complex, overlapping speech in dynamic courtroom environments, particularly in scenarios involving low-quality audio, regional dialects, or technical jargon. The research problem centers on creating adaptive computational models that can augment human court reporters by automating error detection, contextualizing ambiguous phrases, and predicting legal terminology in real time. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and fine-tune large language models (LLMs) on multimodal datasets comprising courtroom audio recordings, annotated transcripts, and legal reference materials. Computational methods will include parallelized training of transformer-based architectures optimized for low-latency inference, acoustic modeling for noise-robust speech recognition, and semantic alignment techniques to map colloquial speech to formal legal text. By simulating diverse courtroom scenarios—including multi-speaker interactions, cross-talk, and rare lexical items—the models will be stress-tested for reliability under realistic conditions. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time transcript validation, a benchmark dataset for legal speech processing, and quantifiable metrics for evaluating human-AI collaboration in court reporting workflows. This work addresses a critical gap in legal accessibility technology, aiming to reduce transcription errors, lower cognitive load for practitioners, and improve equitable access to justice for individuals with hearing impairments. The HPC infrastructure is essential due to the computational intensity of training domain-specific LLMs and the need for large-scale synthetic data generation to capture edge cases in legal proceedings.
cip_title: Court Reporting and Captioning/ Court Reporter
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to record and transcribe examinations, testimony, judicial orders and instructions, legal opinions, and other formal proceedings via print or electronic methods. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcription, shorthand, verbatim recording, equipment operation and procedures, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the formation and evolution of kinship networks among African-descended communities in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean during the 18th and 19th centuries. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how enslaved and free Black individuals navigated systemic displacement and violence to sustain familial and communal bonds, which were central to cultural resilience. Traditional archival methods struggle to reconstruct these fragmented histories due to sparse, siloed, or deliberately obscured records. To overcome these challenges, the project will aggregate digitized archival materials—including census records, plantation inventories, newspaper advertisements, and church registries—into a unified relational database. Computational methods such as social network analysis, spatial statistics, and agent-based modeling will then be applied to identify patterns of migration, kinship ties, and community formation. HPC resources are essential for processing large-scale datasets (spanning millions of entries) and running iterative simulations to test hypotheses about regional variations in social structures. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized hubs of cultural exchange, quantitative insights into how legal and geographic constraints shaped kinship practices, and visualizations of diaspora networks across time and space. The findings will advance scholarly debates about agency and resilience in African-American history while providing a methodological framework for integrating computational tools into historical research. A publicly accessible interactive atlas of kinship networks will also be developed to support educational and community engagement initiatives. By bridging archival research with data-driven inquiry, this project aims to transform our understanding of Black diasporic life and its enduring legacies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and performance assessment of complex plumbing systems in urban residential and commercial buildings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current plumbing design practices rely on static code-compliant layouts and manual hydraulic calculations, which often fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, fluid turbulence, material degradation, and thermal stress in integrated HVAC-plumbing systems. This limitation can lead to inefficiencies, increased energy consumption, and premature system failures. The research will employ parallelized fluid dynamics simulations using OpenFOAM to model transient water flow and pressure distribution in multi-story plumbing networks under diverse usage scenarios. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic and real-world sensor data to predict pipe wear patterns and optimize maintenance schedules. A key innovation involves coupling building information modeling (BIM) datasets with finite element analysis to simulate long-term stress impacts on joints and valves in hybrid metal-polymer systems. The computational workload requires HPC resources due to the need for high-resolution 3D meshing of entire building water systems, real-time parameter optimization across thousands of simultaneous usage cases, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing code compliance variations across jurisdictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for probabilistic plumbing system design, validated against experimental data from partner vocational training centers. This work will advance plumbing education by integrating computational fluid dynamics into curriculum standards while providing data-driven insights to reduce water and energy waste in next-generation sustainable buildings. The requested allocations will support GPU-accelerated simulations of full-scale building prototypes and distributed training of neural networks on heterogeneous plumbing failure datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice as licensed plumbers by applying technical knowledge and skills to lay out, assemble, install, and maintain piping fixtures and systems for steam, natural gas, oil, hot water, heating, cooling, drainage, lubricating, sprinkling, and industrial processing systems in home and business environments. Includes instruction in source determination, water distribution, waster removal, pressure adjustment, basic physics, technical mathematics, blueprint reading, pipe installation, pumps, welding and soldering, plumbing inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the design and optimization of next-generation solar energy systems, addressing critical challenges in efficiency, scalability, and grid integration. Despite rapid advancements in solar technology, persistent gaps remain in modeling the complex interactions between photovoltaic (PV) materials, energy storage systems, and dynamic grid demands. Current simulation tools struggle to resolve multi-scale phenomena—from nanoscale carrier dynamics in novel perovskite materials to system-level energy flow—under real-world operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating atomistic modeling, finite element analysis, and machine learning-driven optimization. Molecular dynamics simulations will evaluate defect tolerance and charge transport in emerging PV materials, while coupled thermal-electrical models will assess degradation mechanisms in concentrated solar power components. At the system level, reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize hybrid battery-thermal storage configurations across diverse climatic and load scenarios. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized workflows and large-scale parameter sweeps that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations at unprecedented resolution and throughput, reducing the experimental iteration cycle for material discovery by 60-80% and identifying storage-grid control policies that maximize renewable utilization under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include validated models for tandem solar cell architectures, predictive tools for long-duration storage sizing, and open-source software packages to accelerate community research. By bridging molecular-scale insights with grid-scale operational planning, this work will directly inform the development of resilient, high-efficiency solar technologies capable of meeting decarbonization targets. The computational datasets and adaptive control strategies generated will be disseminated through industry partnerships and public repositories, ensuring broad impact across the solar energy innovation ecosystem.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing solar-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in solar energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize traditional and modern woodworking processes by analyzing the mechanical behavior of wood under diverse environmental and operational conditions. Despite wood’s widespread use, its anisotropic nature, moisture sensitivity, and variable grain structures pose challenges in predicting performance during cutting, carving, or assembly. Current trial-and-error approaches in toolpath planning, joinery design, and material selection lead to inefficiencies, material waste, and suboptimal product durability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and 3D digital twin simulations. The FEA models will simulate stress distribution, vibration, and deformation during machining operations across species-specific wood datasets. ML algorithms will correlate historical craft data with simulation outputs to predict optimal tool geometries, feed rates, and clamping configurations. Concurrently, digital twins of workshop environments will test virtual prototypes under dynamic humidity and temperature conditions to evaluate long-term structural integrity. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized workflows to manage multi-scale simulations (microscopic grain interactions to macroscopic assembly dynamics) and large datasets spanning material science, traditional craft knowledge, and sensor-derived machining metrics. The HPC resources will accelerate model training, enable parametric studies of 500+ wood-tool combinations, and support real-time rendering of digital twins. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for woodworkers, predictive models to reduce material waste by 20-30% in craft production, and a framework for digitizing traditional woodworking expertise. This interdisciplinary effort bridges computational engineering and artisanal practice, offering scalable solutions to enhance precision in custom woodcraft while preserving manual techniques through data-driven refinements. Results will be disseminated via workshops for vocational training programs and partnerships with heritage craft preservation initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out and shape stock; assemble wooden articles or subassemblies; mark, bind, saw, carve, and sand wooden products; repair wooden articles, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to optimize dynamic mission planning for contested air and space operations in multi-domain environments. Current mission planning tools rely on static, pre-defined threat and resource models, which struggle to adapt to real-time changes in adversarial electronic warfare activity, weather disruptions, or satellite constellation availability. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including real-time sensor feeds, probabilistic threat assessments, and orbital mechanics constraints—into a unified decision-support system capable of generating resilient operational plans under uncertainty. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with Monte Carlo methods to simulate adversarial interactions across air, space, and cyber domains, while reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms will train adaptive decision policies on synthetic scenarios reflecting emerging counter-space capabilities and hypersonic threats. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling the ABM to thousands of concurrent agents, accelerating RL training through parallelized environment sampling, and validating models against classified historical mission datasets via secure virtual enclaves. Expected outcomes include a modular architecture for rapid scenario prototyping, quantifiable metrics for plan robustness under subsystem failures, and novel algorithms prioritizing covert satellite tasking in low-probability-of-intercept modes. This work directly supports the development of next-generation command-and-control systems by addressing computational bottlenecks in real-time resource allocation for joint all-domain operations, with implications for both tactical responsiveness and strategic deterrence posture.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of systems and equipment used in aerospace operations. Includes instruction in astronomy and astronautics, solid state theory, air and space operations, electronics, computer science, aviation and space flight safety, life support systems, flight operations management systems, programming, propulsion systems, weaponry, maintenance management and applications to specific systems and operations.

abstract: Anatomic pathology faces significant challenges in diagnosing complex diseases due to the increasing volume and intricacy of histopathological data, including high-resolution whole-slide images (WSIs) and multi-omics datasets. Current manual and semi-automated diagnostic workflows struggle with scalability, reproducibility, and integration of heterogeneous data types, leading to delays and potential diagnostic variability. This project proposes the development of a computational pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, AI-driven analysis of histopathological and molecular data. The primary research objective is to create deep learning models trained on annotated WSIs to detect subtle anatomic abnormalities—such as tumor microenvironment features or rare cytological patterns—and correlate these findings with genomic and proteomic data. The computational approach will involve three phases: (1) preprocessing and segmentation of terabyte-scale WSI datasets using distributed storage and GPU-accelerated frameworks, (2) training of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers for feature extraction and classification, and (3) integration of histomorphometric data with bulk RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics using graph-based neural networks. The HPC infrastructure will be critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simultaneous jobs, and validation against multi-institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include quantitative benchmarks for automated detection of underrecognized diagnostic patterns in renal carcinomas and gliomas, with validation against gold-standard pathologic assessments. This work aims to establish a scalable framework that reduces diagnostic turnaround times by 30-50% while identifying novel histomic-genomic correlations predictive of disease progression. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source modules, enhancing reproducibility in digital pathology research. By addressing critical bottlenecks in data processing and model training, this project will directly support precision medicine initiatives and quality improvement in anatomic pathology laboratories.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis of disease and anatomic abnormalities. Includes instruction in autopsy pathology, cytology, diagnostic surgical pathology, forensic medicine, laboratory management, and quality control.

abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) remain a critical concern in postoperative care, with breaches in sterile technique contributing to preventable complications. Current protocols for maintaining aseptic environments in operating rooms (ORs) rely on static guidelines that may not adequately address the dynamic, multifactorial risks posed by human activity, equipment interactions, and robotic surgical systems. This project proposes a computational approach to model contamination risks and optimize real-time sterile field management. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based simulations of OR workflows to quantify microbial transmission pathways influenced by personnel movement, airflow, and instrument handling. Machine learning models will be trained on retrospective SSI incidence data, surgical robot telemetry, and environmental sensor logs to predict contamination events and identify protocol vulnerabilities. Additionally, finite element analysis will assess the efficacy of sterilization techniques for robotic end-effectors and reusable instruments under varying clinical conditions. The computational framework will enable scenario testing of interventions, such as adjusted scrubbing protocols or redesigned equipment workflows, to minimize microbial load. Expected outcomes include dynamic, data-driven guidelines for sterile field maintenance, predictive tools for SSI risk stratification, and virtual training modules for surgical technologists. By integrating HPC-driven insights into surgical practice, this research aims to reduce infection rates, lower healthcare costs, and enhance patient safety. The project aligns with the Surgical Technology program’s emphasis on innovation in aseptic technique, providing a scalable computational foundation for advancing evidence-based practice and education in sterile processing and robotic surgery support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and surgical nurses, to maintain, monitor, and enforce the sterile field and adherence to aseptic technique by preoperative, surgical team, and postoperative personnel. Includes instruction in instrument and equipment sterilization and handling, surgical supplies management, wound exposure and closure, surgical computer and robot operation and monitoring, maintenance of hemostasis, and patient and team scrubbing.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of nuclear reactors requires precise modeling of complex multiphysics phenomena, including neutron transport, thermal-hydraulic behavior, and material degradation under extreme conditions. Current computational tools for simulating these coupled processes often rely on simplified models or empirical correlations due to limitations in processing power, which can introduce uncertainties in safety analyses and design optimizations. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-fidelity, multiphysics simulations of nuclear reactor systems, with a focus on advancing predictive accuracy for accident scenarios and long-term operational safety. The research will employ Monte Carlo methods for neutron transport simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal-hydraulic modeling, and finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessments. These tools will be integrated using a coupled multiphysics framework to capture real-time interactions between radiation, heat transfer, and mechanical stress. Key challenges include managing the computational expense of resolving fine spatial and temporal scales, optimizing parallelization strategies for heterogeneous architectures, and validating results against experimental data from test reactors and international benchmarks. The proposed work will enable the analysis of advanced reactor designs, such as small modular reactors (SMRs), under both normal and transient conditions, with emphasis on cladding failure thresholds, coolant flow instabilities, and fission product dispersion. Outcomes will provide actionable insights for reducing conservatism in safety margins, improving fuel cycle efficiency, and informing regulatory guidelines for next-generation nuclear systems. By utilizing HPC capabilities, this project aims to bridge critical gaps in computational nuclear engineering, supporting the development of safer, more sustainable nuclear technologies while training students in cutting-edge simulation techniques essential for the future workforce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering, knowledge and technical skills in support of engineer and other professionals operating nuclear facilities and engaged in nuclear applications and safety procedures. Includes instruction in physics, nuclear science, nuclear systems, nuclear plant and systems design, radiological safety, radiological applications, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing hyper-personalized financial planning strategies in real-time, integrating dynamic tax-code simulations, behavioral client profiling, and multi-jurisdictional regulatory constraints. Traditional financial planning tools struggle to simultaneously account for rapidly evolving tax policies, idiosyncratic client risk preferences, and cross-border investment implications, often relying on static rulesets and periodic manual updates. Our research addresses this gap by creating an adaptive system that leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to model thousands of interdependent fiscal scenarios under uncertainty, including stochastic simulations of legislative changes, nonlinear interactions between retirement accounts and estate structures, and psychometric analysis of client decision-making patterns. The computational approach combines three methodological pillars: 1) Monte Carlo-based tax efficiency optimization using parallelized gradient descent algorithms to navigate high-dimensional strategy spaces; 2) Natural language processing pipelines that parse and semantically analyze evolving regulatory documents across multiple government databases; and 3) Reinforcement learning agents trained on historical client interaction data to predict behavioral responses to proposed financial strategies. By utilizing GPU-accelerated optimization and distributed memory architectures, the system will enable real-time strategy adjustments responsive to micro- and macroeconomic shifts while maintaining audit trails for compliance verification. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational engine capable of generating Pareto-optimal financial plans that balance quantitative efficiency metrics with qualitative client preferences, validated against historical performance data from multinational wealth management firms. This research aims to establish a new paradigm for fiduciary decision support systems that proactively adapt to both external policy environments and internal client dynamics, significantly reducing the latency between regulatory changes and implementable financial strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage the financial interests and growth of individuals and institutions. Includes instruction in portfolio management, investment management, estate planning, insurance, tax planning, strategic investing and planning, financial consulting services, and client relations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive control systems for next-generation electromechanical assemblies used in industrial automation, renewable energy integration, and advanced manufacturing.
