Current systems struggle to maintain efficiency and reliability under dynamic operational conditions, particularly when integrating heterogeneous components such as servo-actuators, power converters, and real-time sensor networks. The research problem centers on modeling the nonlinear interactions between mechanical wear, thermal drift, and electrical transient responses in these systems, which existing reduced-order simulations fail to capture accurately. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework combining multi-physics finite element analysis (FEA), discrete-event system modeling, and machine learning-driven optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations of coupled electromechanical systems under thousands of operational scenarios, including stress cycles, fault conditions, and variable load profiles. Key computational challenges involve resolving microsecond-scale electrical transients alongside hour-long thermal degradation processes within unified simulations. Machine learning models will then iteratively optimize control parameters and failure prediction algorithms using simulation-derived training data. Expected outcomes include validated control strategies that reduce energy losses by 15–20% in prototype testing and predictive maintenance schedules that extend component lifetimes by 30% under cyclic loading. The developed models will be shared as open-source tools to support workforce training programs in electromechanical technology, addressing a critical need for scalable simulation resources in applied engineering education. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work bridges the gap between theoretical electromechanical principles and practical implementation constraints, directly supporting advancements in smart manufacturing infrastructure and sustainable industrial systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electromechanical technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive maintenance strategies for industrial machinery by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model wear mechanisms and failure modes in mechanical systems. Despite advancements in repair methodologies, unplanned equipment downtime remains a critical challenge in manufacturing, transportation, and energy sectors, often arising from insufficient understanding of dynamic stress interactions and material degradation under operational conditions. To address this, the research will employ multi-scale computational simulations to analyze stress distribution, fatigue behavior, and thermal effects in common mechanical components such as gears, bearings, and hydraulic systems. Finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) frameworks will be integrated to simulate component interactions across varying loads and environmental conditions, while machine learning models trained on synthetic and experimental datasets will identify failure precursors. The computational workflow requires HPC resources to manage large-scale parametric studies, real-time sensor data integration, and high-resolution 3D simulations of microstructural evolution. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to optimize maintenance intervals, reduce component replacement costs, and extend machinery service life by 15–30%. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets of simulated failure scenarios, providing a benchmark for repair training programs and diagnostic tool development. By bridging computational mechanics with practical repair protocols, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for proactive maintenance in technology-driven industries, ultimately enhancing operational safety and resource efficiency. The requested computing allocation will enable the parallel processing of multi-physics models and validation against experimental wear testing, ensuring robust translation of theoretical insights into field-applicable solutions.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of tools, equipment, and machines.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of maintaining and optimizing computer systems in heterogeneous, high-demand environments, where hardware failures and performance bottlenecks incur significant operational costs. While traditional diagnostic and repair methodologies rely on manual inspection and reactive troubleshooting, this research proposes a computational approach to model hardware behavior under stress, predict failure points, and recommend optimal configurations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will simulate workloads across diverse hardware architectures—including power supply units, memory hierarchies, and microprocessor designs—to quantify performance degradation and identify failure thresholds. Machine learning models will be trained on simulated and empirical datasets to classify fault patterns in real-time sensor data from CPUs, GPUs, and storage devices. Additionally, network simulations will evaluate peripheral integration challenges, such as latency in distributed repair diagnostics and I/O contention in multi-device environments. The computational workflows will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic failure analysis and employ containerized environments to replicate field conditions at scale. Outcomes will include predictive maintenance frameworks for technicians, validated against physical testbeds, and open-source tools for optimizing hardware configurations in educational and industrial settings. By bridging empirical repair practices with computational modeling, this work aims to reduce system downtime, extend hardware longevity, and enhance training protocols for computer technicians. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the scale of concurrent simulations, which require terabytes of synthetic telemetry data and real-time analytics across thousands of hardware permutations. This project aligns with the program’s focus on advancing technical proficiency in computer maintenance through innovation in computational problem-solving.
cip_title: Computer Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair computers and related instruments. Includes instruction in power supplies, number systems, memory structure, buffers and registers, microprocessor design, peripheral equipment, programming, and networking.

abstract: Nuclear medicine research faces critical challenges in modeling the dynamic behavior of radiopharmaceuticals and their interactions with biological systems, which are essential for advancing diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy. Current computational approaches often lack the resolution and scalability needed to simulate complex tracer kinetics, radiation dosimetry, and multi-scale physiological processes, limiting the development of optimized imaging protocols and personalized therapies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced computational models of radiopharmaceutical distribution, metabolism, and radiation transport in heterogeneous biological tissues. The research will employ Monte Carlo simulations to model radiation interactions at the molecular and cellular levels, coupled with pharmacokinetic modeling to predict tracer dynamics across organ systems. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to analyze high-dimensional imaging datasets and refine image reconstruction algorithms for positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT). The computational workflows will utilize open-source frameworks such as GATE/Geant4 for radiation transport and custom Python-based pipelines for data analysis, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of simulated and clinical imaging data. Expected outcomes include the optimization of tracer dosing protocols, improved quantification of metabolic pathways in oncology and neurology applications, and enhanced dosimetric precision for targeted alpha therapy. By enabling high-fidelity simulations of radiopharmaceutical behavior, this work will accelerate the translation of novel tracers into clinical practice, reduce patient radiation exposure, and advance theranostic strategies for precision medicine. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current computational bottlenecks, ensuring scalable and reproducible analyses that are infeasible with conventional infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the tracer principle, most often with radiopharmaceuticals, to evaluate molecular, metabolic, physiologic and pathologic conditions of the body for the purposes of diagnosis, therapy and research. Includes instruction in tracer kinetics, the biologic effects of radiation exposure, the fundamentals of the physical sciences, and the principles and operation of radiation detection and imaging systems.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize the design of immersive educational games through computational modeling and large-scale simulation, addressing the challenge of balancing engagement with pedagogical efficacy in digital learning environments. While game-based learning is increasingly adopted in K-12 and higher education, existing tools often lack empirically grounded frameworks to dynamically adapt narrative structures, interaction mechanics, and feedback systems to diverse learner needs. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate over 10,000 unique game design permutations using agent-based models that incorporate cognitive, behavioral, and affective learner profiles derived from educational psychology literature. Each simulation tracks multidimensional outcomes, including knowledge retention, problem-solving patterns, and engagement metrics, under varying conditions of narrative complexity, reward schedules, and collaborative gameplay mechanics. Machine learning techniques, particularly multi-objective optimization algorithms, will identify Pareto-optimal design configurations that simultaneously maximize learning gains and intrinsic motivation. Validation phases will cross-reference simulation results with empirical data from classroom trials involving 500+ students. The computational intensity of modeling fine-grained learner-game interactions across extended play sessions necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated neural networks for real-time parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for evidence-based educational game design and predictive models linking specific game mechanics to cognitive load and skill acquisition rates. By bridging computational game studies, learning sciences, and HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to establish new methodologies for data-informed educational content creation while advancing theoretical understanding of engagement-learning tradeoffs in digital environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, distributed engineering systems under uncertainty, with applications to cross-sector infrastructure resilience planning. Traditional resource allocation models in engineering management often rely on static, deterministic assumptions, which inadequately address the stochastic nature of supply chain disruptions, workforce variability, and emergent system interdependencies in modern infrastructure networks. The research problem centers on creating adaptive decision-support tools that integrate real-time operational data with predictive analytics to balance competing technical, economic, and organizational constraints. The computational approach combines multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with high-fidelity discrete-event simulation to model complex interactions between human decision-makers, automated systems, and environmental variables across multiple temporal scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training MARL agents on heterogeneous datasets (including IoT sensor streams, maintenance logs, and economic forecasts) while maintaining the low-latency requirements of operational decision cycles. Expected outcomes include a scalable optimization engine capable of generating Pareto-efficient resource allocation strategies under partial observability, validated through case studies in energy-water nexus management and hybrid human-robot manufacturing systems. The framework will advance engineering management theory by formalizing trade-offs between centralized control architectures and emergent coordination in socio-technical systems. Successful implementation could reduce resource waste in critical infrastructure operations by 15-30% compared to current industry benchmarks, as quantified through digital twin validation. This work bridges gaps between control theory, cognitive systems engineering, and operations management, establishing computational foundations for next-generation adaptive resource governance in engineered systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of management and administration principles to engineering systems and applications. Includes instruction in resource allocation theory, control theory, statistical analysis, business management and administration, and applications to specific engineering research problems.

abstract: The increasing complexity of product design requirements, driven by demands for sustainability, cost-efficiency, and ergonomic performance, challenges traditional iterative prototyping and manual optimization methods. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational workflows for generative design, multi-physics simulation, and lifecycle analysis in industrial design. By integrating parametric modeling with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), the research will enable rapid evaluation of structural integrity, material efficiency, and environmental impact across thousands of design permutations. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify optimal form-factor relationships while adhering to manufacturing constraints and user experience parameters. The proposed computational framework will also incorporate real-time rendering capabilities to visualize complex assemblies and interactive product behaviors under simulated operational conditions. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to process large datasets from 3D scanning, material databases, and energy consumption models, enabling predictive analytics at scale. Anticipated outcomes include novel methodologies for embedding circular economy principles into early-stage design processes, reducing physical prototyping waste by an estimated 60-75%, and establishing quantifiable metrics for aesthetic-functional tradeoffs in consumer products. This research aims to advance computational tools for the industrial design community, fostering innovation in sustainable manufacturing and user-centered product development.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via the creation of effective forms, shapes, and packaging for manufactured products. Includes instruction in designing in a wide variety of plastic and digital media, prototype construction, design development and refinement, principles of cost saving, and product structure and performance criteria relevant to aesthetic design parameters.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the synthesis and performance of sustainable, high-strength synthetic fibers with tunable thermal and mechanical properties. A key challenge in textile engineering is balancing material durability, environmental impact, and manufacturability when designing novel fiber systems. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in resolving multiscale interactions—from molecular polymer dynamics to macro-scale fiber network behavior—that govern these properties. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to predict structure-property relationships in next-generation bio-based polyamide fibers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale MD simulations (10^6+ atoms) to model polymerization kinetics and interfacial adhesion between natural additives and synthetic matrices. Concurrently, FEA will simulate stress distribution in fiber assemblies under dynamic loads, while ML algorithms trained on simulation outputs will identify optimal chemical compositions and processing parameters. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental tensile testing, differential scanning calorimetry, and microscopy data from collaborating labs. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for fiber elasticity and thermal degradation thresholds, (2) a curated database of simulated polymer-additive interactions, and (3) prototype formulations reducing petrochemical content by ≥30% without compromising strength. This work will advance computational textile science by establishing open-source tools for virtual material screening, accelerating the development of sustainable alternatives to conventional synthetic fibers. The requested resources are critical for handling the parallelized simulations and large datasets inherent to multiscale modeling, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems to test and manufacture fibers and fiber products, both synthetic and natural; to develop new and improved fibers, textiles and their uses; and to the analysis of related engineering problems such as structural factors, molecular synthesis, chemical manufacturing, weaves, strength and stress, useful life, dyes, and applications to composite systems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of stellar merger remnants and their role in producing rare astrophysical transients, such as luminous red novae and kilonovae. Despite their importance in galactic chemical evolution and gravitational wave astronomy, the complex interplay of magnetohydrodynamics, radiation transport, and nuclear processes in these systems remains poorly modeled. Current simulations often simplify radiative transfer or neglect multi-physics coupling, limiting predictive accuracy for observable signals. To address this, we propose high-resolution 3D simulations using the open-source code FLASH, enhanced with custom modules for non-equilibrium radiation transfer and microphysical equations of state. The simulations will model post-merger accretion disks, shock-driven ejecta, and their associated electromagnetic emission, incorporating relativistic corrections and neutrino-cooling effects. These calculations demand extreme computational resources due to the need for adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) to resolve turbulent mixing at multiple scales, coupled with Monte Carlo radiative transfer across 10^6–10^7 wavelength bins. We request 1.2 million node-hours on a GPU-accelerated supercomputing cluster to conduct parameter studies varying progenitor masses, metallicities, and magnetic field configurations. Anticipated outcomes include publicly released synthetic light curves and spectra for comparison with JWST and Rubin Observatory data, constraints on r-process nucleosynthesis in merger environments, and improved priors for gravitational wave follow-up campaigns. This work will directly inform observational strategies for upcoming time-domain surveys and bridge gaps between stellar astrophysics, nuclear physics, and multi-messenger astronomy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and observational study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena. Includes instruction in cosmology, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and model the temporal-spatial complexity of American Sign Language (ASL) discourse in real-time interpretation scenarios, addressing critical gaps in the efficiency and accuracy of machine-assisted translation tools. Current automated ASL processing systems struggle with the dynamic, multi-channel nature of sign language—including simultaneous manual gestures, facial expressions, and body movements—leading to latency and errors in real-world applications. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating 3D convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) and transformer-based temporal modeling to process high-resolution video streams of ASL performances. The computational workflow will involve parallelized training on GPU clusters to handle the large-scale dataset of annotated ASL interpretations (over 10,000 hours of video from diverse sociolinguistic contexts) and simulate real-time inference scenarios. Key challenges include optimizing memory usage for frame-sequence analysis and reducing computational latency to under 50 milliseconds per processed frame, a threshold necessary for seamless human-interpreter use cases. The project will validate models using motion-capture data and expert-reviewed interpretation benchmarks, measuring improvements in sign recognition accuracy and discourse coherence. Outcomes will include open-source tools for ASL computational linguistics, a public dataset of annotated interpretations, and a scalable framework for future research on low-latency sign language processing. By advancing the computational understanding of ASL’s linguistic structures, this work aims to support the development of next-generation interpretation technologies, directly benefiting Deaf communities and professional interpreter training programs. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the intensive demands of multi-modal data processing and iterative model optimization within project timelines.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as simultaneous interpreters of American Sign Language

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamical and structural behavior of complex polymer systems under non-equilibrium conditions, with a focus on physics-driven models. Polymers, particularly those with functional electronic or photonic properties, exhibit intricate phase transitions and self-assembly dynamics that are challenging to characterize experimentally. Current theoretical frameworks lack predictive power for systems involving entangled polymer chains, anisotropic interactions, or external stimuli such as electric fields—critical gaps for advancing energy-efficient optoelectronic materials. The research will employ coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations, enhanced by machine learning-accelerated free energy sampling, to model large-scale polymer assemblies (≥10^6 particles) over microsecond timescales. Key objectives include elucidating how chain topology and external field parameters govern the formation of metastable states in semiconducting polymers and quantifying the correlation between entanglement density and charge transport efficiency. The computational workflow will integrate open-source MD packages with custom GPU-optimized code for analyzing nematic order parameters and stress relaxation spectra. Anticipated outcomes include predictive design rules for polymer architectures that optimize exciton migration in photovoltaic applications and reduce energy losses in organic transistors. By resolving multiscale dynamics inaccessible to laboratory techniques, this work will advance foundational physics of soft matter systems while directly informing the development of next-generation polymeric devices for renewable energy technologies. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary spatial and temporal resolution, as preliminary benchmarks indicate that simulating experimentally relevant scales requires >50,000 core-hours per parameter set.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis, structure and properties of polymers. Includes instruction in nanomaterials, biomaterials, sensors, chemistry, physics, mathematics, biochemistry, electronic and photonic polymers, polymers for energy generation and storage, coatings, structure and function of polymers, and polymer blends.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between macromolecular conformational changes and catalytic efficiency in multienzyme complexes central to nucleotide biosynthesis. A critical gap exists in understanding how transient structural fluctuations in supramolecular assemblies, such as the purinosome, influence reaction thermodynamics and allosteric regulation. Traditional experimental techniques struggle to resolve these rapid, atomic-scale motions, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose a multi-scale molecular dynamics (MD) framework integrating enhanced sampling techniques (metadynamics, replica exchange) with hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations to map free energy landscapes governing substrate channeling and cooperative catalysis. High-performance computing resources will enable microsecond-scale simulations of full purinosome assemblies (∼1.2 million atoms) under physiological conditions, coupled with QM/MM calculations of rate-limiting phosphoryl transfer reactions. The CHARMM36 and AMBER ff19SB force fields will model protein dynamics, while the GFN2-xTB method will handle QM regions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of metastable conformational states driving metabolic flux regulation, (2) quantitative characterization of interfacial electrostatic networks that stabilize transition states, and (3) predictive models of mutation-induced dysregulation observed in nucleotide biosynthesis disorders. This work directly addresses the NIH Roadmap’s emphasis on bridging molecular structure with physiological function and will provide the first dynamic atlas of purinosome operation at chemical resolution. The requested GPU-accelerated nodes (4× NVIDIA A100 per simulation) and 500 TB parallel storage are essential for managing multi-terabyte trajectory datasets and concurrent QM/MM workloads. Results will advance fundamental knowledge of supramolecular enzyme cooperativity while informing therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic syndrome and rare inborn errors of metabolism through computational enzymology.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific relationship of physiological function to the structure and actions of macromolecules and supramolecular assemblies such as multienzyme complexes, membranes, and viruses. Includes instruction in the chemical mechanisms of regulation and catalysis, protein synthesis and other syntheses, and biomolecular chemical reactions.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of cross-cultural exchange networks in premodern Asia (c. 500–1500 CE). Traditional historiography of Asian societies often relies on fragmented textual and archaeological records, limiting systematic studies of regional connectivity. Our research addresses this gap by integrating multilingual primary sources—including Chinese court annals, Arabic trade logs, Sanskrit inscriptions, and archaeological site data—into a unified computational framework. The core challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, incomplete datasets spanning diverse formats, languages, and chronologies to reconstruct dynamic networks of trade, religious diffusion, and diplomatic interaction. We propose a multi-stage computational approach: (1) NLP-driven text analysis to extract entities, events, and temporal markers from digitized manuscripts and inscriptions; (2) network modeling to map spatial and temporal shifts in connectivity nodes using Python-based graph algorithms; and (3) agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about the role of environmental factors (e.g., monsoon patterns, Silk Road routes) in shaping institutional changes. HPC resources are critical for training transformer models on low-resource historical languages, running Monte Carlo simulations to address source uncertainty, and processing high-resolution geospatial data. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated historical records, visualizations of network evolution over time, and statistical insights into how intercultural encounters influenced state formation and religious syncretism. By bridging computational methods with historiographical inquiry, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for analyzing large-scale historical transformations, offering new perspectives on Asia’s interconnected past. The requested resources will enable processing an estimated 15 TB of primary data, reducing runtime for iterative simulations from weeks to days, and supporting version-controlled collaboration across interdisciplinary teams.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the Asian Continent from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resource allocation in large-scale R&D programs through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enhance decision-making in research management. R&D initiatives in technology-driven sectors face inherent uncertainties, including fluctuating budgets, dynamic team structures, and evolving project scopes, which complicate the alignment of resources with strategic priorities. Traditional management approaches often rely on static frameworks that inadequately account for real-time variables, leading to inefficiencies in capitalizing on emerging opportunities or mitigating risks. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the development of a dynamic simulation platform integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate R&D project ecosystems under diverse constraints. The computational model will incorporate variables such as funding cycles, personnel expertise, intellectual property landscapes, and market-driven timeline pressures. HPC resources are critical to support large-scale parallel simulations that explore thousands of scenario permutations, enabling probabilistic assessments of resource allocation strategies. Additionally, reinforcement learning algorithms will be deployed to identify adaptive policies for balancing exploratory research with product development pipelines. The platform will be validated against historical R&D performance data from collaborating industry partners in the biotechnology and advanced manufacturing sectors. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between short-term deliverables and long-term innovation capacity, as well as evidence-based guidelines for reallocating resources during project lifecycle disruptions. This work bridges computational analytics with R&D management theory, offering novel insights into sustaining competitive advantage in science-intensive enterprises while advancing methodologies for complexity-aware resource optimization in organizational leadership contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage projects, programs and organizations involving basic and applied research, or specialized technology applications, in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in all aspects of business management applied to the leadership and control of scientific, clinical, engineering and social scientific enterprises; the management of related operational, security and logistical issues; and technical competence in one or more research disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to advance research in adaptive learning systems by developing computational models to optimize personalized educational content delivery in large-scale online learning environments. A critical challenge in instructional design is the dynamic alignment of multimedia resources, assessment tools, and pedagogical strategies with diverse learner needs, particularly when operating at scale. Current systems often rely on static rulesets or simplistic recommendation algorithms, limiting their ability to process multimodal learner data (e.g., interaction logs, assessment performance, and biometric feedback) in real time. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep reinforcement learning models on heterogeneous educational datasets. The computational approach involves three phases: 1) Parallelized preprocessing of terabyte-scale learner interaction data from MOOC platforms using distributed computing pipelines, 2) Training of transformer-based architectures to model learner behavior sequences and knowledge state trajectories, and 3) GPU-accelerated simulations of virtual classroom environments to test instructional interventions. The project will utilize HPC capabilities for hyperparameter optimization across competing model architectures and large-batch training with synthetic data augmentation to improve generalization. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time adaptive content generation validated through A/B testing with 50,000+ learners across three partner online education platforms. This research will contribute novel methodologies for computational instructional design, enabling more effective scaling of personalized learning technologies while maintaining rigorous privacy-preserving data practices. The resulting models and simulation tools will be disseminated to the educational research community, providing infrastructure for future investigations into human-computer interaction patterns and cognitive load optimization in technology-mediated learning environments.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing and integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-documented Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages. Many languages in these regions remain under-resourced in terms of digitized corpora, syntactic annotations, and tools for automated processing, hindering both linguistic research and community-led preservation efforts. The project focuses on developing scalable computational methods to analyze syntactic diversity, dialectal variation, and contact-induced language change across these linguistically complex regions. Key objectives include the creation of parallelized pipelines for processing multilingual text corpora, training neural models for low-resource language tasks (e.g., morphological segmentation, dependency parsing), and simulating language evolution using agent-based models. HPC resources are essential to manage the heterogeneous datasets, which include audio recordings, transcribed oral narratives, and historical texts from over 20 languages, including Austronesian, Papuan, and Kra-Dai families. Computational workflows will integrate transformer-based architectures for cross-lingual transfer learning and Bayesian phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct dialect maps. Anticipated outcomes include open-access tools for automated annotation, a publicly accessible repository of computationally enhanced linguistic datasets, and novel insights into areal typological patterns. By enabling large-scale comparative analyses, this work aims to advance theoretical understanding of language contact dynamics in multilingual ecologies while supporting Indigenous communities in safeguarding linguistic heritage. The project’s computational outputs will be designed for interoperability with existing digital humanities platforms, ensuring broad applicability across linguistic research and pedagogy.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian and Australasian/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance digital humanities research centered on the revitalization and preservation of Indigenous languages and cultural narratives within U.S. and Canadian Native communities. Despite growing efforts to document endangered languages, many existing archives remain fragmented, under-analyzed, or inaccessible to the communities they represent. This research addresses the critical gap in computational tools capable of processing complex, non-linear Indigenous oral histories and multilingual datasets while adhering to tribal data sovereignty protocols. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations, alongside geospatial analysis of oral tradition narratives tied to ancestral landscapes. Computational workflows will integrate community-generated metadata and ethical access frameworks co-designed with tribal partners. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on distributed linguistic corpora, conducting large-scale pattern recognition in audio-visual archives, and simulating interactive 3D environments for cultural heritage education. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for Indigenous language reclamation initiatives, a federated database architecture respecting tribal data governance, and multimodal digital repositories that align with Native epistemologies. By centering computational methods on Indigenous knowledge systems, this work aims to redefine best practices in collaborative digital stewardship while providing scalable infrastructure for Native-led cultural preservation. The research directly supports academic-community partnerships in Native American Studies, offering methodological innovations at the intersection of computational linguistics, cultural geography, and decolonial digital humanities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the American Indian, Aleut, Inuit, Hawaiian and other native peoples of the Americas from earliest times until the present, with particular emphasis on U.S. and Canadian populations and their problems but including reference to Caribbean and Latin American native peoples.

abstract: Chemical processes involving heterogeneous catalysis are central to the production of fuels, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals. However, the empirical development of catalysts and reaction conditions remains time-intensive and costly. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multiscale modeling of catalytic systems, integrating quantum mechanical simulations of active sites with reactor-scale transport phenomena. Density functional theory (DFT) will be employed to elucidate reaction mechanisms and activation barriers on candidate catalyst surfaces, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) frameworks will model mass and heat transfer in industrial reactor geometries. The integration of these scales requires iterative data exchange between software packages, necessitating large-scale parallelization and significant memory allocation. HPC resources will also facilitate machine learning-assisted optimization of catalyst compositions and operating parameters by training on terabyte-scale datasets generated from combinatorial simulations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel catalyst formulations with improved selectivity for target products, reduced energy demands for hydrocarbon processing, and validated multiscale workflows adaptable to other reactive systems. This work addresses critical gaps in accelerating sustainable process engineering by replacing trial-and-error experimentation with predictive computational frameworks, directly benefiting industries reliant on catalytic technologies while minimizing environmental impacts through optimized resource utilization.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how large-scale, multilingual digital communication patterns shape intercultural understanding and conflict in global contexts, with a focus on social media and international news platforms. As cross-cultural interactions increasingly occur in digitally mediated spaces, existing analytical frameworks struggle to account for the scale, linguistic diversity, and contextual nuances of these exchanges. Our research addresses this gap by developing computational models to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of public communication across six languages (English, Mandarin, Spanish, Arabic, French, and Swahili) from platform APIs and web archives. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement natural language processing pipelines with transformer-based models fine-tuned for cross-cultural semantic analysis, sentiment detection across cultural contexts, and network analysis of information flow between linguistic communities. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of heterogeneous text data, dynamic topic modeling at scale, and GPU-accelerated training of culture-aware language models. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for identifying cultural friction points in transnational digital discourse, 2) predictive models of intercultural communication breakdowns in diplomatic and organizational settings, and 3) visual analytics tools to support intercultural training programs. This work directly supports the program’s mission by advancing evidence-based strategies for effective global communication, with applications in international journalism, cross-cultural public relations, and diplomatic communication. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the project’s multilingual data complexity, real-time processing requirements for streaming social media analysis, and iterative model training across cultural contexts—tasks that exceed the capacity of standard academic computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the specialized knowledge and skills needed for effective communication in the international community and among people of different cultures; and that prepares individuals to function at the national and international levels as journalists, public relations specialists, travel industry representatives, intercultural trainers, and/or foreign service officers. Includes instruction in journalism, communications, intercultural and international relations, marketing and public relations, and global communications policy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in casino operations using high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of balancing real-time customer demand with operational constraints. Casinos represent complex, high-stakes environments where spatial layouts, staffing, and gaming equipment must adapt to fluctuating patron behavior, regulatory requirements, and profitability targets. Traditional static planning models fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between variables such as crowd density, slot machine utilization, security response latency, and hospitality service queues. We propose an agent-based simulation platform coupled with reinforcement learning (RL) to model multi-objective decision-making under uncertainty. The computational model will integrate anonymized customer movement data (via IoT sensors), gaming transaction logs, and staff scheduling inputs to simulate scenarios ranging from routine operations to peak-hour or event-driven demand surges. HPC resources are critical to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of potential resource configurations while accounting for probabilistic outcomes in gaming revenue, regulatory compliance risks, and guest satisfaction metrics. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends optimal adjustments to floor layouts, security patrol routes, and staff deployment in near real time, validated against historical operational data from partner casinos. The project contributes to the understudied intersection of computational game theory, behavioral analytics, and service operations in gaming environments, offering a scalable framework that advances resource optimization beyond conventional hospitality management paradigms. Results will be disseminated through gaming industry partnerships and computational economics forums, demonstrating how HPC-enabled models can address niche operational challenges in regulated entertainment sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage casinos and gaming establishments. Includes instruction in business and financial management; casino operations; casino security and surveillance; hospitality, facilities, and personnel management; and principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to assess the cumulative impacts of climate change and anthropogenic stressors on coastal estuarine ecosystems, with a focus on nutrient pollution, sediment dynamics, and habitat loss. Coastal estuaries—critical transition zones between freshwater and marine environments—face unprecedented pressures from sea-level rise, altered hydrology, and land-use changes, yet existing management tools often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between physical, biogeochemical, and ecological processes. To address this gap, we propose a coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical model incorporating three-dimensional circulation, sediment transport, nutrient cycling, and benthic-pelagic interactions at spatial scales ≤100 m and temporal resolutions ≤1 hour. The model will integrate satellite-derived water quality data, in situ sensor networks, and field-collected biodiversity datasets to simulate scenarios of stormwater management, wetland restoration, and watershed development. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve fine-scale processes across multi-year simulations, particularly for parallelized parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification using ensemble techniques. Machine learning workflows will be employed to downscale global climate projections and identify thresholds of ecosystem resilience. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of hypoxia risk, sediment retention capacity, and seagrass habitat viability under multiple management regimes. This work will directly inform state and federal strategies for nutrient load reduction, wetland conservation, and adaptive flood management, while advancing computational methods for coupled human-natural systems analysis. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing of >50 TB of heterogeneous environmental data and execution of >10,000 core-hours of model runs, substantially improving decision-support tools for balancing ecological integrity with human water needs in vulnerable coastal regions.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Water, Wetlands, and Marine Resources Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of marine/aquatic biology, oceanography, natural resource economics, and natural resources management to the development, conservation, and management of freshwater and saltwater environments. Includes instruction in subjects such as wetlands, riverine, lacustrine, coastal, and oceanic water resources; water conservation and use; flood control; pollution control; water supply logistics; wastewater management; aquatic and marine ecology; aquatic and marine life conservation; and the economic and recreational uses of water resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in facial treatment protocols through the development of a computational framework for simulating and predicting skin response to cosmetic interventions. Despite the growing demand for personalized skincare, current methods in facial treatment rely heavily on generalized product formulations and manual assessment, leading to variable outcomes across diverse skin types and conditions. The project addresses this gap by integrating biophysical modeling, machine learning, and clinical data to create predictive tools that optimize treatment efficacy while minimizing adverse reactions. The computational approach involves three phases: (1) constructing a multi-layered, dynamic model of facial skin physiology using finite element analysis to simulate interactions between topical agents (e.g., chemical exfoliants, hydrating serums) and skin microstructure under varying conditions; (2) training deep neural networks on anonymized client datasets (including hyperspectral imaging, pH levels, and elasticity measurements) to classify skin states and predict treatment trajectories; and (3) validating models against in-clinic outcomes from partnered salons to iteratively refine algorithmic accuracy. HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional datasets, parallelizing finite element simulations across heterogeneous skin types, and enabling real-time parameter optimization during model training. Expected outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for facialists to design client-specific treatment plans, a repository of simulated skin response profiles for rare dermatological conditions, and evidence-based guidelines for adapting European facial techniques to non-Caucasian skin phenotypes. By bridging esthetic practice with computational biomechanics, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for data-driven skincare, reduce reliance on trial-and-error methodologies, and enhance safety standards in an industry currently lacking robust predictive frameworks. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated through open-access modules tailored for vocational training programs, fostering equitable access to advanced esthetic tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and scalp with chemical and cosmetic preparations, and to function as licensed facial specialists in specialized and full service salons.  Includes instruction in facial surface anatomy; skin properties; skin decontamination and infection control; facial massage; facial makeup; facial wrapping; selection and application of creams, lotions, oils, and other chemicals and cosmetics; European and other facial techniques; client evaluation and care; applicable laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the nonlinear dynamics of entangled polymer melts under shear flow, a problem central to predicting their viscoelastic behavior in industrial processing and functional applications. While current tube-based models capture linear viscoelasticity, they inadequately describe nonlinear responses at high deformation rates, where chain stretch, convective constraint release, and non-affine motion introduce complex coupling between chain topology and flow kinematics. This project will employ large-scale coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to resolve these multiscale phenomena, explicitly modeling entangled polymer systems with chain lengths and timescales inaccessible to atomistic simulations or experimental rheometry. Simulations will utilize a bead-spring polymer model with explicit slip-spring entanglement constraints, implemented in the LAMMPS framework, to probe the evolution of chain conformations, entanglement density, and stress relaxation under steady and transient shear. Advanced topological analysis tools, including graph-theoretic methods, will quantify time-dependent entanglement networks and their coupling to flow fields. The computational demands are substantial, requiring high-performance computing resources to simulate systems of 500–1,000 chains (each with 50–200 Kuhn steps) over microsecond timescales, alongside parallelized post-processing of terabyte-scale trajectory data. Expected outcomes include (1) validated constitutive relations for nonlinear stress-optical behavior, (2) mechanistic insights into how flow alters entanglement lifetimes and spatial distributions, and (3) predictive metrics for process-dependent material properties. By bridging molecular-scale physics to continuum-scale rheology, this work will advance first-principles models for polymer processing optimization, directly supporting applications in extrusion and injection molding while maintaining a foundational focus on nonequilibrium polymer physics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanical, optical, and transport properties of polymers with respect to the underlying physics and physical chemistry of polymers in melt, solution, and solid state

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the complex interplay between cultural dietary practices, nutrient absorption variability, and long-term health outcomes across diverse populations. While nutritional science traditionally emphasizes biochemical mechanisms, this study addresses a gap in modeling how socio-cultural factors—such as regional food preparation methods, meal timing, and ingredient combinations—influence nutrient bioavailability and metabolic responses. The computational challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous datasets, including ethnographic records of food practices, genomic data linked to enzymatic activity, and longitudinal health metrics, to build predictive models of dietary efficacy. A hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, machine learning (e.g., graph neural networks to map ingredient interaction networks), and pharmacokinetic simulations will be employed to account for multi-scale temporal and spatial variables. Key innovations include adapting computational fluid dynamics frameworks to simulate nutrient diffusion in gut microbiomes under varying dietary patterns and developing culturally contextualized embeddings for food-item classification. The project requires HPC resources to manage large-scale parameter sweeps across demographic variables, optimize stochastic models of meal sequencing effects, and validate predictions against global nutritional databases. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for designing culturally adaptive dietary recommendations, a novel framework for quantifying "nutritional resilience" in aging populations, and insights into how traditional food practices modulate metabolic disease risk. This work bridges computational social science, precision nutrition, and public health, offering a paradigm shift from one-size-fits-all dietary guidelines to context-aware nutritional strategies.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foods, nutrition, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a multidisciplinary investigation into the transnational circulation and adaptation of cultural narratives across linguistic, historical, and geopolitical boundaries. While traditional methods in cultural studies and comparative literature have relied on close reading and manual archival analysis, the scale and complexity of contemporary digital cultural archives—spanning millions of texts, images, and multimedia artifacts—demand computational approaches to identify patterns, trace influences, and analyze discursive shifts. The research problem centers on how ideological frameworks embedded in literary and cultural texts migrate and mutate within and across marginalized communities, particularly in postcolonial and diasporic contexts. To address this, the project will deploy natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for multilingual and multimodal corpora, including under-resourced languages, to perform large-scale sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network mapping of narrative structures. Additionally, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to detect intertextual and transmedial references, enabling systematic comparison of adaptations in film, visual art, and digital media. Computational workflows will integrate Python-based frameworks (e.g., spaCy, Gensim) with custom algorithms for diachronic analysis, executed across parallelized environments to manage memory-intensive tasks. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital humanities toolkit for tracing cultural transmission, open-access datasets of annotated cross-media narratives, and new theoretical insights into the role of hybridized aesthetics in resisting hegemonic discourses. By coupling computational power with interdisciplinary scholarship, this work aims to redefine methodologies for analyzing cultural production in an era of globalized digital exchange, while ensuring equitable access to HPC resources for non-STEM fields. The results will inform pedagogical practices, archival digitization initiatives, and public humanities projects focused on decolonial epistemologies.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of cultural studies and comparative literature or a specialization which draws from cultural studies and comparative literature. Includes instruction in anthropology, comparative linguistics, cultural studies, history, literary criticism, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, sociology, and textual studies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of animal health data—including genomic, proteomic, and clinical imaging datasets—presents a critical challenge in veterinary diagnostics and care optimization. Current methods for integrating and analyzing these heterogeneous datasets are computationally limited, leading to delays in disease detection, treatment personalization, and epidemiological modeling. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to address these bottlenecks by leveraging machine learning (ML) and multi-omics integration. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating predictive models for zoonotic disease transmission risks in livestock populations using spatiotemporal datasets and deep learning architectures, and (2) optimizing treatment protocols for companion animals through real-time analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) and biomarker profiles. Computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) for training neural networks on anonymized EHRs from veterinary clinics, genomic sequences from pathogen surveillance programs, and high-resolution imaging data from diagnostic radiography and histopathology. Parallelized pipelines will be developed to handle species-specific biological variability and missing data inherent in clinical veterinary settings. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, running ensemble models for uncertainty quantification, and simulating disease spread dynamics under varying intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for rapid pathogen variant analysis, decision-support systems for antimicrobial stewardship, and predictive risk maps for regional disease outbreaks. These resources will directly enhance veterinary training programs by integrating computational literacy into clinical curricula and providing students with hands-on access to advanced analytics platforms. By bridging gaps between veterinary medicine and computational biology, this work aims to improve diagnostic accuracy, reduce treatment costs, and advance preventive care strategies across diverse animal populations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary/ Animal Health Technology and Veterinary Assistant
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of veterinarians, laboratory animal specialists, and zoological professionals, to provide patient management, care, and clinical procedures assistance as well as owner communication. Includes instruction in animal nursing care, animal health and nutrition, animal handling, clinical pathology, radiology, anesthesiology, dental prophylaxis, surgical assisting, clinical laboratory procedures, office administration skills, patient and owner management, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Clinical cytogenetics faces growing challenges in analyzing complex genomic and cytogenetic data to diagnose genetic disorders, guide organ transplant compatibility, and optimize cancer treatment strategies. Current methodologies, including karyotyping, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), and molecular genetic profiling, generate vast multi-modal datasets—such as high-resolution chromosomal images, spatial gene expression maps, and sequencing outputs—that demand advanced computational resources for integration and interpretation. Traditional analysis pipelines lack the scalability to process these data efficiently, limiting the resolution of structural variants, mosaic anomalies, and epigenetic interactions critical for clinical decision-making. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a unified computational framework for large-scale cytogenetic data analysis. The proposed workflow will deploy machine learning models to automate the detection of chromosomal aberrations in karyotype and FISH images, integrate these findings with whole-genome sequencing and transcriptomic data via graph-based algorithms, and simulate spatial chromatin dynamics in cancer cells to predict clonal evolution. HPC capabilities are essential for training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale imaging repositories, performing parallelized genomic variant calling across thousands of samples, and running molecular dynamics simulations of chromosomal rearrangements. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for identifying diagnostic biomarkers of transplant rejection risk, subclonal cancer populations, and rare constitutional abnormalities with higher sensitivity than current clinical standards. The resource will also enable real-time photomicrography analysis during time-sensitive procedures like hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. By bridging computational bottlenecks in multi-omics data synthesis, this project aims to establish new standards for precision in genetic disease diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and transplant compatibility assessment, directly impacting patient outcomes in leukemia, solid tumors, and congenital disorders. All tools will be containerized for clinical deployment, ensuring translation of HPC-driven insights into routine diagnostic workflows.
cip_definition: The clinical research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in optimizing treatment strategies for infectious diseases in low-resource global health settings. Despite advances in clinical interventions, diseases such as HIV, tuberculosis (TB), and malaria continue to impose disproportionate burdens in regions with limited healthcare infrastructure. Key challenges include predicting pathogen evolution, optimizing multidrug regimens to minimize resistance, and tailoring interventions to heterogeneous patient populations. To overcome these barriers, we propose an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling, Bayesian inference, and machine learning to simulate disease transmission dynamics, treatment outcomes, and healthcare resource allocation at scale. The project will utilize clinical datasets from multinational cohorts, including genomic, demographic, and treatment adherence data, to parameterize models reflecting real-world variability in host-pathogen interactions and healthcare access. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of simulations to test thousands of intervention scenarios, including adaptive drug rotation policies, targeted vaccine deployment, and community-level screening protocols. Sensitivity analyses will identify high-impact variables driving treatment success, while neural networks trained on simulation outputs will predict optimal strategies under resource constraints. Expected outcomes include actionable guidelines for balancing efficacy, cost, and equity in frontline clinical settings, as well as open-source tools for rapid scenario testing by public health stakeholders. By quantifying trade-offs between individualized care and population-level priorities, this work aims to reduce preventable mortality and advance health equity in line with global sustainability goals. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a scalable platform for future studies on emerging pathogens and antimicrobial resistance crises.
cip_definition: Research focused on Global Health

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance costume design workflows through advanced simulation, data-driven historical analysis, and collaborative digital prototyping. While traditional costume design relies heavily on physical prototyping and manual research, current methods struggle to efficiently integrate complex variables such as fabric behavior under dynamic performance conditions, historical pattern accuracy, or real-time collaborative adjustments across production teams. The proposed research addresses these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale interactions between textiles, movement, and environmental factors (e.g., lighting, humidity) in virtual performance spaces. Physics-based simulations will predict fabric drape, wear, and movement for diverse materials under staged choreography, while machine learning models trained on historical costume databases will identify period-accurate design elements from digitized archives. A cloud-enabled collaborative platform will allow designers, directors, and technicians to iteratively refine 3D costume renderings in shared virtual environments, reducing reliance on physical mock-ups. Computational demands include GPU-accelerated rendering for real-time visualization, parallelized simulations for material stress testing, and large-language-model-assisted script analysis to automate costume plot generation. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating costume-performance interactions, a validated database of computationally annotated historical designs, and protocols for reducing material waste in prototyping. By bridging computational methods with artistic practice, this work aims to establish new standards for interdisciplinary collaboration in performing arts while preserving craft-specific knowledge through digital preservation. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the terabyte-scale datasets and complex multi-physics models required for this integrative approach.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and select costumes for characters in theatre and the performing arts and to serve as part of a production team. Includes instruction in costume design, script analysis, theory and criticism, period styles, history of costume, stage makeup, rendering, and costume construction.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between environmental change, host-pathogen dynamics, and emerging infectious disease risk in human populations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Rapid urbanization, climate shifts, and habitat fragmentation are altering ecological networks and evolutionary pressures on zoonotic pathogens, yet scalable models integrating these processes remain underdeveloped. We propose to build spatially explicit, multiscale simulation frameworks to analyze how landscape connectivity, wildlife migration patterns, and anthropogenic stressors jointly influence cross-species transmission hotspots. Agent-based models will incorporate empirical data on reservoir host distributions (e.g., rodents, bats), vector ecology, and human mobility across three regions with accelerating spillover events: Southeast Asia, the Amazon Basin, and East Africa. Phylogenetic comparative methods will be adapted to assess pathogen trait evolution under simulated environmental gradients, avoiding genomic sequence analysis to align with program scope. A novel feature integrates adaptive behavioral responses in human communities—such as changes in land use or healthcare access—as dynamic feedbacks altering transmission pathways. The computational workflow requires parallelized parameter sweeps across >10^5 ecological scenarios, Bayesian inference for model calibration, and real-time visualization of epidemic trajectories. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of high-risk interfaces where land-use change amplifies evolutionary selection for human-adapted pathogens, 2) predictive maps of outbreak vulnerability under multiple climate projection scenarios, and 3) quantitative evaluation of ecological intervention strategies targeting wildlife-livestock-human contact networks. By coupling evolutionary ecology principles with epidemiological modeling at unprecedented spatial granularity, this work will provide actionable insights for preventing spillover events while advancing theoretical frameworks for planetary health. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive landscape layers, optimizing stochastic simulation kernels, and enabling iterative model refinement through ensemble machine learning techniques.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of disease, disability, and trauma patterns within and across populations and the development of health management mechanisms to prevent and control disease outbreaks and injurious behaviors. Includes instruction in biostatistics, biochemistry, molecular biology, immunology, disease and injury determinants, genetic disease and disability factors, behavioral studies, health services research, environmental disease and injury factors, and population studies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize dynamic pricing strategies for multi-tenant hospitality ecosystems, integrating real-time data from transportation networks, event-driven demand fluctuations, and cross-industry partnerships (e.g., airlines, local attractions). The hospitality industry faces mounting complexity in revenue management due to the interdependency of lodging, dining, and ancillary services across spatially distributed properties, compounded by volatile demand patterns influenced by external factors like weather, geopolitical events, and shifting consumer preferences. Traditional linear optimization models fail to capture these nonlinear, high-dimensional interactions, particularly when scaling to enterprise-level portfolios with thousands of properties and heterogeneous customer segments. We propose a computational framework combining reinforcement learning (RL) with multi-agent simulation to model competitive and cooperative decision-making among hospitality providers, transportation operators, and third-party platforms. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training of RL agents across diverse market scenarios, incorporating terabyte-scale datasets spanning historical booking patterns, social media sentiment, and IoT-derived foot traffic metrics. Key computational challenges include managing asynchronous updates across geographically partitioned simulations and optimizing memory allocation for sparse, high-frequency input streams. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for adaptive pricing and resource allocation, validated against industry benchmarks for occupancy rates and profit margins. This work will advance computational methodologies for hospitality systems by formalizing a network-aware pricing paradigm, with implications for resilience planning in tourism-dependent economies. The resulting models and open-source simulation toolkit will be disseminated through industry partnerships, bridging gaps between operations research, behavioral economics, and distributed computing in hospitality contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain significant global health challenges, particularly among infants born preterm or with complex congenital conditions. Current approaches to predicting adverse outcomes and optimizing therapeutic strategies are limited by the inability to integrate high-dimensional, multi-modal data—including genomic, proteomic, electrophysiological, and clinical parameters—into actionable models. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to analyze longitudinal datasets from neonates in high-risk clinical scenarios, with the goal of identifying early biomarkers of organ dysfunction and enabling personalized treatment strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and integrate heterogeneous data streams from electronic health records, wearable biosensors, and multi-omics platforms. Machine learning models, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to predict outcomes such as bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, and sepsis. Parallelized computational fluid dynamics simulations will model cardiorespiratory physiology in preterm infants with congenital heart defects, optimizing ventilation strategies under varying hemodynamic conditions. The scale of data—anticipated to exceed 500 TB from a multi-center cohort of 2,000 neonates—and the complexity of real-time biosignal analysis necessitate HPC infrastructure for efficient storage, distributed processing, and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for neonatal intensive care decision support, mechanistic insights into pathophysiology through network analysis of multi-omics data, and open-source computational tools for neonatal physiological modeling. This work will directly inform clinical trials targeting high-risk subgroups and contribute to a precision medicine framework for neonatal-perinatal care, ultimately reducing morbidity through earlier, data-driven interventions. The requested computing resources are essential to overcome current limitations in processing latency and model generalizability, ensuring translational impact across diverse patient populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physiology of the normal neonate, the pathophysiology of the sick infant, and the diagnosis and management of problems of the newborn infant, including consulting with obstetricians to plan for the care of women with high-risk pregnancies.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the evolution of Italian cultural identity across transnational diaspora communities through the computational analysis of multilingual textual and visual archives. The study addresses a critical gap in Italian cultural studies: the lack of systematic, large-scale analyses of how migrant and descendant communities negotiate Italian identity through locally produced media, literature, and organizational records. While existing scholarship relies on localized case studies, this project will process and analyze over 250,000 digitized pages of newspapers, personal correspondence, and institutional documents from Italian communities in North America, South America, and Australia (1880–1980), alongside contemporary social media data from transnational digital networks. The computational approach combines multilingual natural language processing (NLP) for Italian, English, Spanish, and Portuguese texts with computer vision techniques to examine visual materials. Custom transformer-based models will be developed to detect semantic shifts in cultural references across generations and geographic contexts, while graph neural networks will map the transnational circulation of narratives and symbols.
