The project will advance academic understanding of computational approaches to organizational management while delivering practical solutions that enhance operational efficiency, reduce overhead costs, and improve employee satisfaction in business administration contexts. Results will be disseminated through open-source optimization frameworks and case studies demonstrating measurable improvements in office management outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and manage the operations and personnel of business offices and management-level divisions. Includes instruction in employee supervision, management, and labor relations; budgeting; scheduling and coordination; office systems operation and maintenance; office records management, organization, and security; office facilities design and space management; preparation and evaluation of business management data; and public relations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing systemic financial risk propagation in multi-layered market networks, integrating heterogenous data from derivatives, credit markets, and shadow banking activities. Traditional risk management models struggle to capture the nonlinear interdependencies between regulated financial institutions and less transparent sectors, particularly during stress events where liquidity constraints and collateral calls create cascading failures. The proposed work addresses this gap by constructing dynamic network models that simulate cross-sector risk transmission pathways under varying macroeconomic scenarios, incorporating machine learning-calibrated agent behaviors and regulatory boundary conditions. The computational approach combines graph neural networks with Monte Carlo stress testing, requiring high-performance computing resources to handle three critical challenges: (1) processing real-time streaming data from disparate financial subsystems at scale, (2) resolving complex network interdependencies through iterative graph convolutions, and (3) running ensemble simulations that account for path-dependent market reactions across multiple timescales. Expected outcomes include a novel risk propagation metric quantifying contagion susceptibility in hybrid financial ecosystems, scenario analysis tools for monitoring emergent vulnerabilities in derivative collateral chains, and sensitivity benchmarks comparing centralized versus decentralized risk mitigation strategies. By leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed memory architectures, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities for systemic crisis prevention while establishing computational best practices for next-generation financial network analysis. The resulting tools will provide institutions and regulators with actionable insights into cross-market risk amplification mechanisms that conventional value-at-risk models currently overlook.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the strategies used to define and manage acceptable financial risk for companies. Includes instruction in banking and bank regulations, derivative securities, interest rate and credit markets, financial engineering of systematic risk, and equity, bond, futures, and options markets.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between urban soundscapes, environmental stressors, and population health outcomes using advanced data science methods and high-performance computing (HPC). Urban noise pollution, a growing public health concern, exhibits complex spatiotemporal patterns influenced by infrastructure, human activity, and environmental policies. However, existing studies often lack the resolution and computational power to model these interactions at city-wide scales while integrating heterogeneous datasets—including acoustic sensor networks, mobility traces, health records, and socio-demographic indicators. The research will develop a novel computational framework to (1) analyze terabyte-scale audio streams using deep neural networks for sound event recognition, (2) fuse multi-source geospatial data to quantify cumulative noise exposure, and (3) simulate noise propagation and mitigation scenarios through physics-informed machine learning. Leveraging GPU-accelerated computing, we will process distributed acoustic monitoring data from 50+ city nodes in near real-time, train domain-adapted audio classifiers on urban sound taxonomy, and apply graph-based algorithms to model noise diffusion across built environments. Agent-based models will then assess how noise exposure gradients correlate with stress-related health disparities across demographic groups. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for urban soundscape analytics, high-resolution noise-health risk maps, and evidence-based policy recommendations for equitable noise mitigation. By bridging acoustics, public health, and urban informatics through scalable computational methods, this work addresses critical gaps in environmental epidemiology while advancing methodologies for large-scale sensor data integration—a capability directly dependent on HPC resources for parallel processing, large memory allocation, and distributed storage.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis of large scale data sources from the interdisciplinary perspectives of applied statistics, computer science, data storage, data representation, data modeling, mathematics, and statistics. Includes instruction in computer algorithms, computer programming, data management, data mining, information policy, information retrieval, mathematical modeling, quantitative analysis, statistics, trend spotting, and visual analytics.

abstract: Special education administrators face complex challenges in equitably allocating limited resources to meet the diverse needs of students with disabilities while complying with federal mandates and optimizing educational outcomes. Traditional decision-making frameworks often rely on static, district-level data, which inadequately capture the dynamic interactions between student needs, resource availability, and program efficacy. This project proposes the development of a computational modeling platform to simulate resource allocation scenarios across heterogeneous student populations and evaluate their impacts on individualized education program (IEP) compliance, academic progress, and systemic equity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate multi-year special education datasets, including student disability profiles, service delivery logs, staffing patterns, and budget allocations. These ABMs will simulate how variations in resource distribution—such as specialist staffing ratios, assistive technology investments, or professional development schedules—affect longitudinal outcomes for students with high- and low-incidence disabilities. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify non-linear relationships between allocation strategies and compliance risks or achievement gaps. The computational intensity of modeling thousands of individualized student trajectories across hundreds of schools necessitates parallel processing and large-scale data storage capabilities provided by HPC systems. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool to help administrators prospectively assess the equity and feasibility of resource plans, evidence-based guidelines for aligning budgets with disability-specific service demands, and a publicly accessible dataset linking allocation patterns to IEP outcomes. This work bridges computational analytics and special education leadership, offering novel methods to advance data-driven administration while adhering to legal and ethical obligations in supporting vulnerable student populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage programs for exceptional students and their parents. Includes instruction in special education theory and practice, special education program development, evaluation and assessment in special education, state and federal law and regulations, managing individual education plans, problems of low- and high- disability students, mainstreaming, special education curricula, staff management, parent education, communications and community relations, budgeting, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolving role of digital media platforms in shaping cultural narratives and public opinion during sociopolitical crises, with a focus on large-scale, cross-platform content analysis. While existing scholarship has explored media effects through qualitative or small-scale quantitative methods, the scale, diversity, and real-time nature of contemporary digital media necessitate computational approaches to analyze patterns across billions of texts, images, and videos. The research problem centers on how algorithmic content prioritization and user engagement dynamics interact with cultural context to amplify or suppress specific narratives, particularly in multilingual and transnational contexts. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for multilingual sentiment analysis and topic modeling, alongside computer vision tools for meme and visual rhetoric analysis. Network analysis will map cross-platform information diffusion, while high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets from social media APIs, broadcast archives, and web scraping initiatives. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of platform-specific amplification patterns for crisis-related content, 2) a computational framework for assessing cultural bias in algorithmic content curation, and 3) longitudinal models of narrative evolution across media types and geopolitical contexts. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized ingestion of streaming media, GPU-accelerated deep learning for multimodal analysis, and distributed storage for petascale datasets—necessitates HPC infrastructure beyond conventional departmental resources. Results will advance media ecology theory while providing actionable insights for policymakers addressing platform governance and crisis communication strategies. This computationally intensive approach bridges critical media studies with data science, establishing new methodologies for analyzing digital culture at societal-scale resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the analysis and criticism of media institutions and media texts, how people experience and understand media content, and the roles of media in producing and transforming culture. Includes instruction in communications regulation, law, and policy; media history; media aesthetics, interpretation, and criticism; the social and cultural effects of mass media; cultural studies; the economics of media industries; visual and media literacy; and the psychology and behavioral aspects of media messages, interpretation, and utilization.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between environmental stressors, agricultural adaptation, and demographic shifts in rural communities using advanced computational methods. Rural populations face compounding challenges from climate variability, economic precarity, and outmigration, yet existing studies often lack the granularity to model these multidimensional interactions at scale. We propose to analyze longitudinal datasets spanning environmental metrics (soil health, precipitation trends), agricultural census records, and demographic surveys across five U.S. states using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques. The ABM framework will simulate household decision-making processes related to land use, livelihood strategies, and migration, incorporating heterogeneous agent priorities derived from gender, age, and socioeconomic status. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process terabytes of geospatial data, run thousands of parameterized simulations, and apply deep learning models to identify nonlinear relationships between ecological conditions and community resilience. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational model mapping thresholds of environmental change that trigger demographic transitions, (2) identification of gender-differentiated adaptation strategies in farm households, and (3) predictive analytics quantifying how localized infrastructure investments could mitigate displacement risks. By integrating sociological theory with computational social science methods, this research will advance methodological innovation in rural sociology while generating policy-relevant knowledge about sustainable development pathways. The requested resources will enable processing of restricted-access microdata through secure virtual environments, ensuring compliance with IRB protocols while maintaining computational efficiency. Results will be disseminated through open-access repositories to support comparative studies on rural vulnerability and community-led adaptation frameworks.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the structure and function of rural societies. Includes instruction in sociological theory, research methods, statistics, sociology of agriculture, community development, social and economic development, demography, rural poverty, gender roles in rural societies, and environmental sociology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing energy efficiency and operational reliability of next-generation hybrid and electric vehicles (HEVs/EVs) through high-fidelity computational modeling. Current design processes for vehicular systems—particularly powertrain integration, battery thermal management, and autonomous control algorithms—rely on fragmented simulations that inadequately capture multi-physical interactions under real-world conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a unified simulation framework integrating electro-thermal battery models, drivetrain dynamics, and machine learning-based energy management systems. The computational approach will employ multi-scale finite element analysis to predict lithium-ion battery degradation under variable load cycles, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to optimize thermal regulation systems. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to devise adaptive control strategies that balance power distribution between electric motors and internal combustion engines in hybrid configurations. By simulating entire vehicle systems at unprecedented resolution across diverse environmental and operational scenarios, this work aims to identify design configurations that extend battery lifespan by 15–20% while reducing energy waste in transitional power states. The anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for rapid virtual prototyping of sustainable automotive systems, reducing reliance on physical testing. This resource allocation will directly support the Automotive Engineering Technology program’s mission to advance practical, scalable solutions for emerging transportation challenges, with implications for industry partnerships focused on decarbonizing ground vehicle technologies. All models and datasets will be made available to the academic community to accelerate collaborative innovation in vehicular systems integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in veterinary clinic workflow dynamics through the development of a computational model to optimize client-patient intake and administrative decision-making. Veterinary receptionists operate in high-stress, high-volume environments where manual scheduling, triage prioritization, and client communication bottlenecks frequently compromise service quality. Existing software solutions lack adaptive capabilities to account for variable factors such as emergent case urgency, staff availability fluctuations, and client behavioral patterns. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing resources to process multi-modal datasets—including historical appointment logs, client interaction transcripts, and real-time clinic operational metrics—to simulate and iteratively refine workflow protocols. A hybrid machine learning framework will integrate natural language processing for sentiment analysis of client communications, agent-based modeling to represent staff-client interactions, and reinforcement learning to dynamically allocate resources under constrained conditions. Key computational challenges include handling sparse or unstructured data from legacy record-keeping systems and maintaining interpretability in decision-support outputs for non-technical users. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predicting appointment no-show probabilities, optimizing triage prioritization in emergency scenarios, and generating personalized client education materials through automated dialogue systems. By computationally modeling the interplay between administrative efficiency and client satisfaction metrics, this work aims to establish evidence-based best practices for veterinary reception training programs while advancing methodological approaches to service-sector workflow optimization in non-traditional HPC domains. The project’s interdisciplinary nature bridges veterinary practice management, human-computer interaction, and computational social science, occupying a specialized niche at the intersection of animal healthcare administration and adaptive resource allocation systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, veterinary technicians, or veterinarians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in veterinary office and animal care facility procedures, veterinary terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing horticultural production systems through advanced computational modeling of plant-environment interactions. Current horticultural practices often rely on generalized protocols for irrigation, nutrient delivery, and pest management, leading to suboptimal resource use and reduced economic viability for growers. The research problem centers on developing precision horticulture frameworks that account for micro-scale variability in plant phenotypes, soil conditions, and microenvironmental factors—a task requiring analysis of multidimensional datasets spanning genomic, phenotypic, and geospatial domains. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement machine learning models trained on heterogeneous data streams, including hyperspectral imaging of plant stress responses, IoT sensor networks capturing real-time soil moisture/temperature gradients, and historical yield records from commercial nurseries. Computational methods will integrate convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image-based plant phenotyping with reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate adaptive management strategies under dynamic climate conditions. Key deliverables include predictive models for water-use efficiency in containerized ornamental crops and decision-support tools for site-specific nutrient application schedules. By enabling granular analysis of plant performance across spatial and temporal scales, this work aims to reduce fertilizer waste by 15-20% and water consumption by 25-30% in trial systems while maintaining crop quality benchmarks. The resulting computational pipelines will be shared as open-source resources to support replication studies in diverse horticultural contexts, advancing both academic understanding of plant-environment feedback loops and practical applications for horticultural businesses. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities to process terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize training of deep learning architectures, and run iterative simulations of management scenarios across heterogeneous growing environments.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Applied Horticulture/ Horticultural Business Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in horticultural service operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design, fault diagnosis, and performance validation of integrated security systems through high-fidelity simulations, addressing critical gaps in current installation and inspection practices. Modern security systems combine heterogeneous components—including motion sensors, biometric access controls, network-connected surveillance cameras, and AI-driven intrusion detection algorithms—whose interactions create complex failure modes that are difficult to diagnose empirically. Current industry methods rely on manual testing and heuristic configurations, leading to vulnerabilities from component interoperability issues, environmental interference, and evolving cyber-physical threats. To overcome these limitations, we propose creating a modular simulation environment using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-sensor security networks across diverse building architectures and threat scenarios. The computational approach will integrate multi-physics models (e.g., electromagnetic interference patterns, thermal signatures), machine learning classifiers for anomaly detection, and discrete-event simulations of intrusion sequences. HPC capabilities will enable parallelized testing of 10,000+ system configurations under variable conditions (e.g., weather, network latency, tampering attempts), generating datasets to train predictive maintenance models and resilience benchmarks. Key outcomes include: (1) a validated library of optimized security system templates for residential, commercial, and industrial use cases, reducing installation errors by simulating structural and electronic constraints; (2) an automated diagnostic tool that correlates sensor data streams with simulated failure trees to accelerate repair workflows; and (3) probabilistic risk assessments for emerging threats like drone incursions or adversarial AI attacks. By enabling data-driven system design and proactive vulnerability testing at scale, this research will directly enhance the technical precision of security technicians while lowering costs associated with iterative physical prototyping. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated through an open-access portal to advance industry standards in security technology education and certification.
cip_title: Security System Installation, Repair, and Inspection Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair household, business, and industrial security alarms, sensors, video and sound recording devices, identification systems, protective barriers, and related technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to analyze the dynamic impacts of multinational trade agreements and financial market integration on global economic stability using advanced computational econometric methods. Current empirical models struggle to capture the nonlinear, high-dimensional interactions between heterogeneous national policies, cross-border capital flows, and exchange rate volatility, particularly during systemic shocks. Our research will develop and estimate a multi-country dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) model incorporating 40+ national economies with sector-specific production networks, strategic trade policies, and interconnected financial markets. The computational implementation requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to solve the model’s equilibrium conditions across nested Monte Carlo simulations that vary tariff schedules, environmental regulations, and digital trade barriers under different geopolitical scenarios. Parallelized Bayesian estimation will be applied to terabytes of historical trade data (UN Comtrade, BIS banking statistics) and real-time financial market feeds. Key innovations include machine learning techniques for dimension reduction in policy parameter space and GPU-accelerated computation of forward-looking rational expectations. Expected outcomes include quantitative assessments of how regional trade pacts affect third-country welfare through production relocation effects, estimates of optimal currency basket weights for emerging markets facing capital flow reversals, and stress-test frameworks for global value chain resilience. Results will inform multilateral institutions on designing cooperative mechanisms to mitigate trade policy spillovers. The project requires sustained access to HPC clusters with multi-node MPI capabilities, large-memory nodes for sparse matrix operations in equilibrium solvers, and GPU arrays for deep learning components.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study and analysis of international commercial behavior and trade policy. Includes instruction in international trade theory, tariffs and quotas, commercial policy, trade factor flows, international finance and investment, currency regulation and trade exchange rates and markets, international trade negotiation, and international payments and accounting policy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-cultural dynamics of 19th-century Protestant missionary networks in the Pacific Islands through the computational analysis of historical correspondence, ethnographic records, and mission society archives. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how missionary activities—shaped by localized interactions, language adaptation, and cross-cultural negotiation—contributed to long-term shifts in Indigenous social structures and regional connectivity. While traditional historiography has relied on qualitative close readings, this study employs high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze over 150,000 digitized pages of multilingual texts (letters, journals, reports) and relational metadata spanning 1820–1900. Natural language processing (NLP) models, adapted for historical dialects and non-Latin scripts, will identify patterns in missionary discourse related to resource allocation, conflict resolution, and knowledge transmission. Concurrently, network analysis will map the evolution of mission stations, supply routes, and interpersonal alliances, integrating GIS data on environmental constraints and preexisting Indigenous trade pathways. The computational workflow requires iterative training of custom transformer-based NLP architectures to handle code-switching in missionary texts (e.g., English-Tongan-Rarotongan mixes) and probabilistic graph modeling to reconstruct fragmented or anonymized correspondences. HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive tasks, including large-scale named entity recognition across heterogeneous documents and dynamic network visualizations of multi-decadal interactions. Expected outcomes include an open-access database linking missionary operations to demographic and ecological datasets, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural brokerage roles in colonial contact zones, and methodological innovations in computational humanities for under-resourced languages. By revealing how mission infrastructures both disrupted and catalyzed Indigenous transnational networks, this research aims to reframe scholarly debates on religious globalization while providing actionable models for heritage communities documenting complex colonial legacies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of religious outreach, social service and proselytization, and that prepares individuals for mission vocations. Includes instruction in theology, evangelism, preaching, medical and social mission work, missionary education, missionary aviation, emergency services, legal and political aspects of working in other countries, and preparation for ordination as missionaries.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of large-scale digital communication networks and their role in shaping contemporary public discourse, with a focus on polarization and misinformation diffusion. As digital platforms generate unprecedented volumes of multimodal data—including text, image, and network interaction patterns—traditional analytical tools struggle to capture the complexity of these systems. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to model how communication theories of agenda-setting, framing, and cultivation manifest in algorithmically mediated environments, particularly examining emergent patterns that diverge from legacy media contexts. The proposed methodology combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques with dynamic network analysis to process terabyte-scale datasets from social media platforms, news archives, and collaborative fact-checking databases. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models to detect rhetorical strategies across linguistic and visual modalities, while parallelized graph algorithms will map temporal shifts in information cascades and community formation. Agent-based modeling will simulate how platform affordances interact with human communication behaviors under different theoretical assumptions. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel taxonomy of digital persuasion tactics grounded in communication theory, (2) quantifiable metrics for assessing the entrenchment of polarized belief systems through machine learning-derived latent variables, and (3) open-source tools enabling researchers to analyze cross-platform communication flows at scale. By bridging computational social science with critical media theory, this work aims to advance methodological paradigms for studying 21st-century communication ecosystems while providing empirically grounded insights into the systemic risks and democratic potentials of networked public spheres. The requested computing resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous media corpora, and real-time visualization of multidimensional communication networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on theories of communication. Includes instruction in theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address a critical gap in culinary arts research: the systematic optimization of multi-scale interactions between cooking techniques, ingredient behaviors, and sensory outcomes. While traditional culinary training emphasizes hands-on experimentation, the complexity of dynamic processes—such as heat transfer in heterogeneous foods, enzymatic reactions during fermentation, or flavor compound interactions—remains underexplored at a predictive, quantitative level. The research will develop computational models to simulate these processes across spatial and temporal scales, enabling data-driven insights into how variables like temperature gradients, ingredient composition, and mechanical stress (e.g., kneading, emulsification) influence textural, nutritional, and aesthetic qualities of dishes. Computational methods will integrate molecular dynamics simulations for micro-scale ingredient interactions, finite element analysis for macro-scale heat and mass transfer, and machine learning to correlate simulated data with sensory evaluation metrics from chef collaborators. By creating a digital twin framework for culinary processes, the project aims to establish predictive tools for recipe optimization, waste reduction, and adaptive menu design under resource constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of validated models for specific techniques (e.g., sous-vide, pastry lamination) and a decision-support system to assist chefs in balancing creativity with operational efficiency. This work bridges culinary arts with computational science, offering a novel paradigm for innovation in professional kitchens while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for non-STEM domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide professional chef and related cooking services in restaurants and other commercial food establishments.  Includes instruction in recipe and menu planning, preparing and cooking of foods, supervising and training kitchen assistants, the management of food supplies and kitchen resources, aesthetics of food presentation, and familiarity or mastery of a wide variety of cuisines and culinary techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of multisensory worship environments through computational modeling of acoustic, visual, and congregational response data. Contemporary worship spaces increasingly integrate live music, digital projection, immersive lighting, and architectural acoustics, yet current design practices lack rigorous methodologies to holistically balance these elements in real time. The research addresses this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate and analyze the dynamic interplay between sensory stimuli, spatial configurations, and participant engagement in Christian worship contexts. Using anonymized biometric datasets (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate variability) collected during worship services alongside acoustic measurements and 3D visual renderings, the project will employ parallelized agent-based models to simulate congregation-wide responses to varying artistic and technological inputs. Machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in how specific combinations of musical key signatures, projection timing, and reverberation profiles correlate with self-reported spiritual experiences. A second computational strand will focus on real-time optimization challenges, using GPU-accelerated finite element analysis to model sanctuary acoustics under different hardware configurations and neural networks to predict ideal lighting transitions during liturgical sequences. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for worship ministry teams to prototype sensory designs virtually before implementation, reducing technical trial-and-error in live settings. By bridging computational science with worship theology, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for creating accessible, theologically coherent multimedia worship experiences while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for studying ritual-artistic convergence. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling high-resolution spatial audio simulations, training deep learning models on multimodal datasets, and running large-scale comparative analyses of historical worship service archives.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the use of musical and theatrical arts in Christian worship. Includes instruction in digital media, electronic hardware design and installation, music, theater, and worship theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of dialectal variation and historical language change in Indonesian and Malay languages. Despite their widespread use across Southeast Asia, comprehensive studies of regional linguistic diversity—particularly in underdocumented dialects—remain limited due to the scale of data and complexity of phonological, morphological, and syntactic patterns involved. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) modeling phonetic and lexical shifts across 20+ regional Malay variants using parallel corpora, and (2) reconstructing proto-forms through automated phylogenetic algorithms. Computational methods will include neural sequence-to-sequence models for dialect alignment, transformer-based embeddings to detect semantic drift in historical texts, and Bayesian inference for phylogenetic tree estimation. A custom pipeline will process multilingual datasets comprising digitized manuscripts, modern speech transcripts, and field recordings (totaling ~5 TB), requiring distributed storage and GPU-accelerated training. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as training dialect classifiers on heterogeneous text sources and running Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) simulations for language divergence dating. Expected outcomes include the first computational reconstruction of proto-Malayic phonology, a publicly accessible dialect atlas with interactive visualization tools, and a framework for automating philological analysis of non-standardized texts. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philology, this work will provide new insights into language contact dynamics in maritime Southeast Asia while developing scalable methods for preserving endangered linguistic heritage. The resources will directly support graduate training in digital humanities applications for regional languages, bridging gaps between linguistic theory and data-driven approaches.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Malay and Indonesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of enforcing environmental regulations across vast and ecologically sensitive regions through the development of advanced computational models. Current methods for monitoring illegal activities such as poaching, illegal logging, and hazardous waste dumping often rely on reactive, resource-intensive patrols, which are insufficient for real-time intervention. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes an integrated approach combining high-resolution satellite imagery, IoT sensor networks, and historical enforcement data to predict environmental crime hotspots and optimize emergency response strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte geospatial datasets, training machine learning algorithms to recognize patterns of illicit activity, and simulating dynamic scenarios such as wildfire spread or pollutant dispersion in near-real time. Agent-based modeling will further assess the efficacy of various patrol routes and resource allocation strategies under different environmental conditions. The expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for proactive enforcement, optimized deployment algorithms for field personnel, and decision-support tools for rapid crisis management. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to transform environmental law enforcement from a reactive to a predictive paradigm, significantly enhancing the capacity to prevent ecological damage, protect public safety, and ensure compliance with natural resource legislation. The tools developed will provide agencies with scalable, data-driven solutions to safeguard ecosystems while efficiently utilizing limited personnel and logistical resources.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Law Enforcement and Protective Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to enforce natural resource and environmental protection regulations and laws; and to perform emergency duties to protect human life, property and natural resources, including fire prevention and control measures, and emergency and rescue procedures. Includes instruction in natural and physical sciences, natural resource management, outdoor field skills, firearms and outdoor equipment and vehicle operation, evidence collection and environmental sampling and monitoring, natural resource legislation, environmental compliance techniques, patrol procedures, investigation and report writing, interpersonal skills and crisis intervention, community liaison, public safety, public education, and public relations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 03.0203.

abstract: The increasing complexity of managing acute, life-threatening conditions in veterinary patients—such as sepsis, trauma, or multi-organ failure—demands advanced tools to optimize time-sensitive clinical decisions. Current protocols for emergency and critical care rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for the dynamic interplay of physiological variables, comorbidities, and treatment responses in individual animals. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive modeling framework to analyze real-time and retrospective clinical data from veterinary intensive care units (ICUs). Leveraging electronic health records, continuous vital sign monitoring, and biomarker data from dogs and cats admitted to tertiary care facilities, we will train machine learning models to predict patient-specific risks of decompensation, treatment efficacy, and long-term outcomes. Computational workflows will integrate multi-modal datasets, including time-series hemodynamic parameters, laboratory results, and imaging findings, to simulate disease trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. The models will employ ensemble learning and mechanistic modeling to address data sparsity and physiological heterogeneity inherent in veterinary critical care. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional data and enable real-time decision support during emergencies. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for early detection of sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, optimized fluid resuscitation strategies, and personalized prognostic scoring systems. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven critical care protocols, directly improving survival rates and resource allocation in veterinary ICUs while advancing translational insights into human-animal comparative medicine. The requested computing resources are essential for scaling complex simulations, hyperparameter optimization, and validation across diverse patient cohorts.
cip_title: Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Medicine
cip_definition: Research focused on the emergency treatment and management of care for animals with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. May included related research in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures, and long-term care of critically diseased animals.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the computational mechanisms underlying dynamic decision-making in uncertain environments using large-scale cognitive modeling. Traditional models of decision-making often rely on simplified assumptions that fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between memory retrieval, attentional shifts, and reward valuation observed in human behavior. To address this gap, we propose developing a parallelized neural network architecture that integrates reinforcement learning, episodic memory sampling, and drift-diffusion processes within a unified framework. The model will be trained and validated against behavioral datasets from multi-armed bandit tasks and sequential prediction experiments, requiring iterative simulations across thousands of parameter combinations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the combinatorial complexity of these simulations, which involve real-time interactions between millions of artificial neurons and synaptic weight updates across hierarchical layers. We will employ GPU-accelerated tensor operations via PyTorch for core computations, coupled with Bayesian optimization for parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical network architectures that reproduce human-like exploration-exploitation tradeoffs, (2) quantitative predictions about individual differences in uncertainty tolerance based on model parameters, and (3) open-source release of modular code for simulating hybrid cognitive-neural systems. This work will advance theoretical understanding of how distributed neural systems balance stability and flexibility in complex tasks while establishing scalable methods for cognitive modeling. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across 100+ GPU nodes, reducing wall-clock time for convergence testing from months to days. Results will directly inform the design of subsequent neuroimaging experiments and contribute foundational insights to computational psychiatry research frameworks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in research and experimental psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in Tibetan language and literature research, particularly the computational analysis of under-resourced textual corpora and dialectal variation. Despite the rich literary and linguistic heritage of Tibetan, large-scale studies remain constrained by fragmented digitization efforts, non-standard orthographies across historical periods, and the complexity of processing agglutinative morphology. Current tools for Tibetan natural language processing (NLP) are limited in scalability and accuracy, hindering efforts to analyze secular and religious texts, trace linguistic evolution, or map dialect features. This project proposes a computational workflow integrating NLP, machine learning, and corpus linguistics to process and analyze diverse Tibetan language data. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for automated text segmentation and parsing of classical Tibetan, developing dialect classification algorithms using phonetic and syntactic features, and enhancing optical character recognition (OCR) accuracy for digitized manuscripts through neural networks. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale text corpora, distributed training of deep learning models on GPU clusters, and high-throughput analysis of audio recordings from understudied Tibetan dialects. Expected outcomes include an open-access, annotated digital corpus of premodern Tibetan texts; a dialect atlas visualizing phonological and lexical variation; and reproducible pipelines for Tibetan NLP. These resources will advance philological research, support preservation initiatives, and facilitate applications in lexicography, language education, and cross-disciplinary studies. By leveraging computational scalability, this project aims to bridge gaps in Tibetan linguistic scholarship while providing infrastructure for future research in low-resource language contexts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Tibetan language. Includes instruction in philology; secular and religious Tibetan; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, Buddhist studies, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between urban environmental design and dynamic criminal activity patterns, leveraging computational modeling to inform crime prevention strategies. While prior research has established correlations between built environments and crime rates, gaps persist in understanding how real-time spatial, temporal, and social variables interact to create emergent criminal opportunities. The study will develop a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) simulating pedestrian movement, environmental affordances, and offender decision-making within a 3D-rendered urban landscape. The model integrates heterogeneous datasets, including crime incident reports, traffic flow sensors, public transit schedules, LiDAR-scanned topography, and anonymized mobile device density metrics. Deep learning architectures (e.g., graph convolutional networks) will analyze historical crime data to parameterize agent behaviors, while Monte Carlo methods will test the crime prevention efficacy of proposed infrastructure modifications under varying demographic and policy conditions. High-performance computing resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations across multiple urban configurations and scaling neural network training on terabyte-scale geospatial datasets. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework identifying high-risk environmental configurations, validated through retrospective analysis of crime displacement following documented urban redesign projects. This computational approach advances criminal justice research by enabling scenario testing without real-world intervention risks, providing evidence-based recommendations for situational crime prevention through architectural planning. The tools developed will be shared via a cloud-based platform for law enforcement analysts and urban policymakers, bridging computational social science with practical criminal justice applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the criminal justice system, its organizational components and processes, and its legal and public policy contexts. Includes instruction in criminal law and policy, police and correctional systems organization, the administration of justice and the judiciary, and public attitudes regarding criminal justice issues.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and sociolinguistic impacts of neural language model (NLM)-generated feedback on second language (L2) writing development, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between learner behavior, linguistic output, and automated feedback systems. While NLMs like GPT-4 are increasingly integrated into language learning tools, their influence on learners’ metalinguistic awareness, error correction patterns, and long-term linguistic development remains understudied. The research addresses this gap by analyzing longitudinal datasets of L2 writers (N=1,200+) engaging with NLM-powered writing assistants, focusing on how feedback personalization strategies affect syntactic complexity, pragmatic competence, and identity negotiation in multilingual contexts. Computational methods include (1) transformer-based fine-tuning of feedback generation models using domain-specific corpora, (2) multilevel Bayesian regression to quantify learning trajectories across proficiency levels, and (3) agent-based modeling of classroom-scale feedback adoption dynamics. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of multimodal interaction logs (text, edit histories, eye-tracking) and for training custom embeddings that capture cross-linguistic transfer patterns among typologically diverse L1-L2 pairs (e.g., Mandarin-English vs. Arabic-German). Expected outcomes include (a) a framework for optimizing NLM feedback architectures to balance error correction efficacy with cognitive load management, (b) identification of threshold effects in model-driven language development, and (c) open-source tools for simulating feedback scenarios in low-resource pedagogical contexts. The project advances applied linguistics research by providing empirical foundations for ethical AI integration in language education while contributing novel methods for large-scale analysis of human-AI interaction patterns. Resulting datasets and computational models will be made available through an interactive repository designed to support research in adaptive educational technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language-related concerns in the everyday world, including language education, acquisition of first and additional languages, discourse analysis, language assessment, literacy, and language policy and planning. Includes instruction in linguistic theory; language teaching and learning; discourse analysis; language and cognition; and language, culture, and identity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-institutional datasets on college student mental health and counseling outcomes. While student counseling services are critical for academic success and well-being, resource allocation decisions often rely on fragmented or localized data, limiting the generalizability of insights. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in intervention efficacy, demographic disparities in service utilization, and longitudinal outcomes across diverse student populations. Current approaches, constrained by conventional computing, struggle to process complex, high-dimensional datasets (e.g., multi-year counseling records, linked academic performance metrics, and demographic variables) at scale. This project will employ machine learning techniques, including deep learning and ensemble methods, to model student outcomes and simulate the impact of hypothetical counseling strategies. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) of anonymized counselor notes, clustering algorithms to subgroup students by risk profiles, and agent-based modeling to test intervention scenarios. HPC resources are essential for training predictive models on terabytes of heterogeneous data, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized grid searches, and running computationally intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predicting at-risk student populations, validating equity-centered counseling practices, and informing data-driven resource distribution (e.g., staffing, program types). Results will be disseminated through open-access predictive tools and visualizations to support evidence-based decision-making in student affairs. By bridging computational advances with counseling research, this work aims to enhance institutional capacity to address mental health crises and reduce attrition among marginalized students.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of U.S. constitutional jurisprudence through large-scale computational legal analytics. The core problem addressed is the lack of systematic, data-driven methodologies for mapping how doctrinal shifts in constitutional law emerge and propagate across judicial hierarchies and temporal scales. Traditional legal scholarship relies on manual case analysis, limiting the scope and granularity of insights into complex, system-wide patterns. This project proposes a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and temporal graph modeling to process over 250,000 federal and state court decisions spanning 1789–2023. Custom transformer-based models will be developed to classify legal reasoning patterns, detect citation network dynamics, and quantify semantic drift in key constitutional concepts (e.g., "due process," "equal protection"). The HPC environment is critical for training domain-specific legal language models, executing parallelized network simulations, and storing multidimensional embeddings of judicial discourse. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for identifying latent dependencies between Supreme Court doctrine and lower court adoption rates, 2) predictive models of jurisprudential change under varying sociolegal conditions, and 3) interactive visualizations of constitutional law’s conceptual topology. By bridging computational social science and legal theory, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying law as a complex adaptive system, with implications for judicial education, policymaking, and public understanding of constitutional governance. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale legal text corpora, GPU-accelerated model training, and real-time simulation of hypothetical doctrinal scenarios—capabilities unfeasible without HPC infrastructure.
cip_title: American/ US Law/ Legal Studies/ Jurisprudence
cip_definition: An advanced, professional program of the U.S. legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dynamic stochastic equilibrium models with heterogeneous agents and adaptive learning mechanisms, a class of problems central to understanding economic resilience under recurrent systemic shocks. Traditional solution methods for such models rely on restrictive homogeneity assumptions or simplified learning dynamics due to computational constraints, limiting their capacity to capture real-world complexity. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these limitations by enabling large-scale parallelization of agent-based simulations, coupled with machine learning techniques for dimensionality reduction in strategy spaces. The research will focus on modeling economies where agents with heterogeneous risk preferences and incomplete information iteratively update their consumption, savings, and investment strategies in response to climate-related productivity shocks and policy interventions. Computational challenges include solving high-dimensional fixed-point problems across networked agent interactions, tracking evolving belief distributions, and quantifying path-dependent systemic risk. The project will implement a hybrid architecture combining Monte Carlo Markov Chain methods for Bayesian belief updating, distributed optimization algorithms for equilibrium computation, and graph neural networks to model spillover effects in agent networks. Expected outcomes include (1) novel metrics for assessing policy effectiveness in multi-agent adaptive systems, (2) open-source computational tools for high-dimensional economic dynamics, and (3) quantitative insights into the relationship between information diffusion patterns and macroeconomic stability. This work bridges mathematical economics, complex systems theory, and computational statistics, requiring resources for massive parallel processing of agent populations (>10^5 nodes), storage of high-frequency simulation data, and real-time visualization of emergent network structures. Results will advance both methodological capabilities in economic modeling and substantive understanding of adaptation mechanisms in coupled human-environment systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical methods to the development of economic theory, models, and quantitative analysis. Includes instruction in data analysis, applied business economics, calculus, econometrics, linear algebra, microeconomic theory, probability, and statistical methods.

abstract: Family practice nurses address complex health challenges shaped by multifaceted interactions between biological, environmental, and socioeconomic factors. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to model these dynamic, nonlinear relationships at the population scale, limiting the ability to predict health outcomes or optimize interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that identify high-risk patient subgroups and evaluate targeted care strategies for chronic disease management in family nursing contexts. Using de-identified electronic health records, demographic data, and environmental exposure metrics from diverse patient populations, we will train ensemble machine learning algorithms to quantify how individual and community-level variables jointly influence risks for conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and maternal health complications. Computational workflows will integrate feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, and sensitivity analyses to improve model interpretability while maintaining predictive accuracy. Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations will then project long-term health outcomes under varying intervention scenarios, including nurse-led preventive care models and telehealth integration. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, we aim to overcome memory and processing constraints inherent to single-machine analyses of high-dimensional healthcare data. The resulting framework will provide actionable insights into modifiable risk factors and resource-efficient care pathways tailored to family practice settings. Anticipated outcomes include validated decision-support tools for risk stratification, evidence to guide community health investments, and scalable methods for evaluating health equity impacts of nursing interventions. This work bridges computational innovation with frontline nursing practice, advancing data-driven strategies to reduce care disparities and improve preventive health outcomes in underserved populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide independent general care for family groups and individuals in the context of family living. Includes instruction in family theory and intervention, role synthesis, family primary care, nursing practice and health care policy, holistic practice, pediatric practice, gerontological practice, health assessment, clinical pharmacotherapeutics, clinical techniques, and pathopsychology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the performance, efficiency, and reliability of alternative fuel vehicle (AFV) systems, particularly in hybrid and converted vehicle platforms. The integration of diverse fuel technologies—such as compressed natural gas (CNG), liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and hybrid electric systems—into existing automotive frameworks introduces complex interactions between mechanical, electrical, and thermal subsystems. Current diagnostic and conversion methodologies often rely on iterative physical testing, which is time-intensive, costly, and limited in exploring the full parameter space of multi-fuel systems. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate and optimize AFV subsystems at unprecedented resolution. The project will develop multi-physics models to analyze combustion dynamics in CNG/LPG engines, battery degradation in hybrid systems under variable load conditions, and thermal management in retrofitted electric vehicle drivetrains. These models will integrate machine learning algorithms to predict failure modes and identify optimal conversion configurations. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, the team will evaluate thousands of design permutations, correlating results with experimental data from industry partners to validate predictive accuracy. Anticipated outcomes include a computational toolkit for diagnosing AFV performance bottlenecks, data-driven guidelines for efficient vehicle conversions, and predictive models to extend component lifespans in hybrid systems. This work will directly support technician training programs by providing scalable, interactive simulation modules for AFV maintenance scenarios. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter spaces and real-time data assimilation required for these analyses, which cannot feasibly be executed on local hardware. By bridging computational innovation with applied automotive technology, this project aims to accelerate the adoption of sustainable transportation solutions while reducing costs for AFV retrofitting and repair.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the maintenance of alternative fuel vehicles and the conversion of standard vehicles to AFV status. Includes instruction in electrical vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles, hybrid fuel technology, electrical and electronic systems, engine performance, diagnosis and repair, and conversion/installation.

abstract: Plant productivity and resilience are critical for sustainable agriculture, yet climate variability and emerging pathogens threaten global crop yields. Traditional breeding and experimental approaches are limited by the complexity of plant-environment interactions and the vast genomic datasets required to identify stress-adaptive traits. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework integrating multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) with environmental variables to model crop responses under abiotic and biotic stressors. Using machine learning algorithms and mechanistic simulations, we will analyze terabyte-scale datasets from 15 key crop species, including maize, soybean, and wheat, to identify genetic markers associated with drought tolerance, disease resistance, and nutrient-use efficiency. Parallelized genomic selection models will optimize breeding strategies by simulating trait inheritance across 10^6 potential crosses, while agent-based modeling will predict pest-pathogen spread under projected climate scenarios. Computational workflows will leverage containerized pipelines on GPU-accelerated nodes to reduce runtime for deep learning architectures analyzing hyperspectral plant phenotyping imagery. The proposed work addresses three critical gaps: (1) scalable integration of heterogeneous agricultural datasets, (2) predictive modeling of genotype-environment-phenotype interactions at landscape scales, and (3) optimization of crop improvement timelines through in silico breeding simulations. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for genomic prediction, a curated database of stress-responsive molecular pathways, and validated trait candidates for field trials. By enabling rapid analysis of complex biological networks and environmental variables, this HPC-driven approach will accelerate the development of climate-resilient crops, directly supporting food security goals in the face of global change. Resource allocation will prioritize memory-intensive genome assemblies (>512 GB/node) and multi-node MPI configurations for population-scale simulations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific principles that underlie the breeding, cultivation, and production of agricultural plants, and the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural plant products. Includes instruction in the plant sciences, crop cultivation and production, and agricultural and food products processing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing resource allocation and risk mitigation in large-scale, multi-stakeholder projects under uncertainty. Traditional project management tools often struggle to handle the dynamic interdependencies, nonlinear cost-time trade-offs, and probabilistic risk profiles inherent in complex initiatives such as infrastructure development or enterprise digital transformation. The research will employ agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations to capture emergent behaviors in project networks, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify adaptive resource allocation strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process heterogeneous datasets spanning project schedules, workforce capacities, supplier reliability metrics, and environmental variables, while maintaining computational feasibility for real-time scenario testing. The computational architecture will leverage parallel processing to simultaneously evaluate thousands of project pathways, incorporating stochastic demand fluctuations and constraint variations. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system that quantifies the cascading impacts of resource allocation choices across temporal and organizational boundaries. This work will advance project management practice by enabling data-driven negotiation of competing stakeholder priorities, proactive identification of critical path vulnerabilities, and dynamic rebalancing of human capital investments. The resulting models will be validated against historical project failure cases and industry partner datasets, with particular attention to improving success rates for projects exceeding $100M in budget. By integrating computational social science methods with operations research principles, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for predictive analytics in complex project governance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply quantitative and qualitative knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage projects in a wide range of fields and occupations. Includes instruction in project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of turbulence and magnetic fields in shaping star-forming regions within molecular clouds, a critical unsolved problem in galactic evolution. Current observational data from facilities such as ALMA and JWST reveal complex filamentary structures and velocity gradients in these clouds, but the interplay between supersonic turbulence, magnetic pressure, and gravitational collapse remains poorly quantified. To address this, we propose a series of high-resolution, three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations incorporating self-gravity, radiative cooling, and interstellar chemistry networks. These simulations will model parsec-scale molecular cloud environments at sub-0.01 pc resolution, spanning parameter spaces for magnetic field strengths (5–50 μG), turbulent Mach numbers (2–20), and metallicities representative of varying galactic environments. The computational workflow will utilize adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) via the FLASH code to prioritize resolving shock interfaces and collapsing cores, paired with post-processing radiative transfer calculations to generate synthetic observables for direct comparison with multiwavelength surveys. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce dimensionality in the simulation output and identify diagnostic signatures of dominant feedback mechanisms. Successful execution requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for MHD solvers and large-memory nodes for spectral synthesis, with an estimated 1.2 million core-hours to achieve statistically robust sampling across initial conditions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive scaling relations between cloud-scale turbulence and core mass functions, constraints on magnetic braking efficiency in diverse environments, and publicly released simulation datasets to inform interpretations of upcoming JWST and SKA observations. This work will advance first-principles understanding of star formation efficiency, with implications for galactic-scale models of stellar feedback and chemical evolution.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the planetary, galactic, and stellar phenomena occurring in outer space. Includes instruction in celestial mechanics, cosmology, stellar physics, galactic evolution, quasars, stellar distribution and motion, interstellar medium, atomic and molecular constituents of astronomical phenomena, planetary science, solar system evolution, and specific methodologies such as optical astronomy, radioastronomy, and theoretical astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural theological debates and their impact on the evolution of ethical frameworks using computational text analysis and network modeling. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of argumentation, conceptual borrowing, and doctrinal adaptation across historically significant religious texts from diverse traditions (e.g., Abrahamic, Dharmic, and Indigenous systems), which remain underexplored due to the scale and linguistic complexity of primary sources. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic similarity analysis and topic modeling, with dynamic network analysis to map the flow of ideas and ethical propositions across temporal and cultural boundaries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multilingual corpora spanning over 10 million words, train custom embeddings for archaic theological vocabulary, and simulate large-scale interaction networks representing doctrinal exchanges. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational pipeline for analyzing comparative religious texts, (2) quantitative evidence of previously hypothesized syncretic relationships between ethical systems, and (3) interactive visualizations of idea diffusion patterns across simulated debate environments. The project will advance digital humanities methodologies by developing transferable tools for philosophical content analysis while offering empirical insights into how moral reasoning evolves through intercultural dialogue. Results will be disseminated through open-access datasets, a public code repository, and interdisciplinary workshops bridging computational science and religious studies. This work addresses a critical gap in understanding the structural commonalities of ethical discourse, with potential applications in interfaith education and culturally informed AI ethics frameworks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in philosophy and religion, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the formation and evolution of shared cultural identities across the British Commonwealth through computational analysis of multilingual textual and visual archives. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance in postcolonial societies, using materials ranging from 20th-century newspapers and pamphlets to digital community archives. While traditional scholarship has relied on manual analysis of selective sources, the scale and linguistic diversity of available materials—spanning over 50 countries and 30+ languages—require advanced computational methods to systematically trace transnational narratives. The project will develop machine learning pipelines for semantic analysis of digitized texts, multimodal embeddings linking visual motifs (e.g., protest art, architectural styles) to textual discourse, and network models mapping the circulation of cultural concepts across regions. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on low-resource languages prevalent in Commonwealth diasporic communities, processing high-resolution image datasets, and running large-scale comparative simulations. Expected outcomes include a novel cross-lingual framework for analyzing cultural hybridity in postcolonial contexts, an open-access repository of annotated multilingual corpora, and visualizations of how key identity markers (e.g., religious syncretism, vernacular literatures) propagated through Commonwealth migration networks. By computationally bridging dispersed archival sources, this work aims to reveal understudied connections between cultural preservation and globalization pressures, offering methodological innovations for digital humanities in area studies while informing contemporary debates about heritage stewardship in pluralistic societies. The requested allocation will support GPU-intensive model training, distributed storage for petabyte-scale archival data, and parallelized network analysis across temporal and geographic dimensions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries comprising components of the historical British Empire and modern British Commonwealth, including migration patterns, shared sociocultural and political features and problems, and contemporary relations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the acoustics and compositional patterns of pre-modern sacred music within understudied liturgical traditions, focusing on the interplay between ritual context, sonic environments, and spiritual cognition. While computational musicology has advanced significantly in analyzing Western sacred repertoires, non-European traditions—particularly oral or semi-oral practices from marginalized communities—remain underrepresented in digital humanities research due to the technical challenges of processing complex ritual audio data. Our team will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze a corpus of 15,000+ field recordings spanning eight traditions, including Ethiopian mezmur chant, Alevi semah liturgies, and Khmer Buddhist ceremonial music. Machine learning models will be trained to disentangle multimodal features (vocal timbre, microtonal pitch contours, rhythmic cycles) while accounting for environmental variables like architectural resonance and ritual movement patterns captured via 3D spatial audio metadata. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate how acoustic properties of sacred spaces (e.g., reverberation times in rock-hewn churches vs. timber shrines) influenced compositional choices across traditions. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of high-resolution audio spectrograms, large-language model analysis of liturgical texts for semantic-sonic correlations, and GPU-accelerated physical simulations of historical worship spaces.
