Expected outcomes include the first cross-cultural taxonomy of sacred music acoustics tied to ritual function, open-source tools for analyzing vulnerable musical heritage, and a framework for reconstructing lost compositional practices through psychoacoustic modeling. By bridging ethnomusicology, archaeoacoustics, and auditory cognition studies, this research will advance understanding of how sacred music operates as embodied spiritual technology while preserving endangered traditions through computationally robust documentation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, theory, composition, and performance of music for religious or sacred purposes, and that prepares individuals for religious musical vocations such as choir directors, cantors, organists, and chanters.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing turfgrass health and playability on golf courses while minimizing environmental impact and operational costs through advanced computational modeling. Traditional grounds management relies on generalized agronomic practices, which often lead to over-application of water, fertilizers, and pesticides, contributing to ecological strain and financial inefficiency. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-resolution, multi-scale simulation framework integrating site-specific variables such as microclimate data, soil hydrology, turfgrass genetics, and pest dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled irrigation systems, drones, and soil probes, enabling dynamic modeling of turf responses under diverse scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and synthetic datasets to predict localized stress factors (e.g., drought, disease outbreaks) and recommend precision interventions. By parallelizing complex agent-based models of root-zone microbial communities and nutrient cycling, the simulations will quantify trade-offs between turf quality, resource use, and ecosystem health at unprecedented spatial granularity. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool for groundskeepers, optimized irrigation and pest management protocols, and a validated sustainability index for golf course certification programs. The computational framework will advance the integration of precision agriculture techniques into recreational land management, offering scalable solutions for an industry under increasing pressure to adopt environmentally responsible practices. This work bridges agronomy, data science, and environmental management, establishing a novel interdisciplinary niche within golf course operations research.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Golf Course Operation and Grounds Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operation of golf courses. Includes instruction in turf grass science and management, golf course design and construction, grounds equipment and operation, pest control, and grounds management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing injury prevention and rehabilitation strategies in athletic training through advanced computational modeling of biomechanical and physiological data. Despite advances in sports medicine, injury mechanisms—particularly those involving repetitive stress or complex movement patterns—remain poorly understood due to the dynamic interplay of anatomical, neuromuscular, and environmental factors. Current clinical tools often lack the resolution to model these interactions at the individual athlete level, limiting personalized interventions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity computational framework integrating motion capture data, musculoskeletal modeling, and machine learning to simulate injury risks and rehabilitation outcomes under diverse physiological conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of kinematic, kinetic, and electromyographic data from collegiate athletes, run finite element analyses of tissue stress distributions, and train deep neural networks to predict injury susceptibility based on individualized biomechanical profiles. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated workflows to simulate real-world scenarios, such as the effects of altered gait mechanics on knee ligament loading or the efficacy of proprioceptive training in reducing ankle sprain recurrence. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for quantifying injury risk thresholds, validating biomechanical interventions, and generating athlete-specific recovery protocols. By elucidating the multifactorial drivers of sports injuries, this work will advance evidence-based practices in athletic training, directly impacting clinical decision-making and athlete health outcomes. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as a template for future studies exploring neuromuscular adaptations across populations, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between sports medicine and computational science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work in consultation with, and under the supervision of physicians to prevent and treat sports injuries and associated conditions. Includes instruction in the identification, evaluation, and treatment of athletic injuries and illnesses; first aid and emergency care; therapeutic exercise; anatomy and physiology; exercise physiology; kinesiology and biomechanics; nutrition; sports psychology; personal and community health; knowledge of various sports and their biomechanical and physiological demands; and applicable professional standards and regulations.

abstract: Theatre arts management faces complex challenges in optimizing resource allocation, production scheduling, and financial planning due to the dynamic interplay of artistic goals, operational constraints, and market variables. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for the nonlinear relationships and stochastic factors inherent in theatrical productions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing computational models to simulate theatre management scenarios and generate data-driven decision-support tools. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling to map interactions among stakeholders (artists, administrators, audiences), Monte Carlo simulations to assess financial risks under variable attendance and sponsorship conditions, and machine learning algorithms to analyze historical box office data for predictive audience engagement analytics. Key applications include dynamic pricing strategies, optimized rehearsal/performance schedules under resource constraints, and risk-aware investment frameworks for production portfolios. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of large-scale scenario trees in financial modeling and real-time parameter adjustments in scheduling algorithms—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include open-source optimization toolkits tailored for regional theatres, empirical insights into effective fund-raising strategies under economic uncertainty, and visualizations of design-to-production workflows that balance creative aspirations with budgetary realities. By integrating computational social science methods with arts management praxis, this research aims to establish new methodologies for sustainable theatre operations while advancing academic discourse at the intersection of cultural economics and computational modeling.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business management principles to the management of theatres and production corporations. Includes instruction in theatrical production, theatre design and planning, fund-raising and promotion, investment strategies, human resources management, theatre operations management, marketing, public relations, financial management and insurance, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Bulgarian language studies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale linguistic and literary datasets. While Bulgarian’s complex morphology, syntactic structures, and rich literary traditions offer fertile ground for computational inquiry, existing tools for corpus-based analysis, dialect modeling, and historical text processing remain underdeveloped compared to those for widely spoken languages. The project will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) developing machine learning models to automate the morphological and syntactic annotation of premodern and modern Bulgarian texts, including underrepresented dialects, and (2) applying graph-based network analysis to trace stylistic and thematic evolution across 19th- and 20th-century Bulgarian literature. Computational workflows will integrate transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT variants) fine-tuned on curated corpora spanning 10 million tokens, alongside graph neural networks to model intertextual relationships in literary works. The HPC infrastructure is essential for training these models, given the need for parallel processing of heterogeneous data (manuscript scans, normalized texts, metadata) and iterative optimization of hyperparameters in deep learning pipelines. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, computationally annotated corpus of Bulgarian historical texts, a suite of NLP tools tailored for Bulgarian philological research, and quantitative frameworks for mapping literary influence across periods. These resources will empower scholars to investigate previously intractable questions about language change, dialect convergence, and literary innovation while establishing methodological precedents for computational Slavic studies. By bridging traditional humanities scholarship with advanced computational methods, the project aims to enhance global access to Bulgarian linguistic heritage and stimulate interdisciplinary collaboration in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bulgarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and molecular drivers of repetitive stress injuries in specialized occupational populations (e.g., musicians, surgeons, athletes) using multiscale computational modeling. Despite extensive clinical studies on acute trauma, the mechanisms underlying chronic microtrauma accumulation in high-precision, repetitive tasks remain poorly understood, partly due to the inability to dynamically model tissue-scale strain patterns alongside cellular-level mechanobiological responses. We propose an integrated computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) of soft tissue deformation with agent-based modeling of inflammatory cascades triggered by mechanical stress. High-resolution motion capture data from ergonomic studies of surgical trainees will inform FEA simulations of tendon and connective tissue loading during prolonged instrument manipulation. These outputs will feed into stochastic models of macrophage activation and cytokine diffusion, calibrated against single-cell RNA sequencing data from biopsy samples. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the iterative coupling of macroscopic biomechanical simulations (10^6-10^7 elements) with fine-grained cellular models (10^4-10^5 agents per time step) across biologically relevant timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of injury risk thresholds for specific task profiles and identification of mechanosensitive molecular targets for early intervention. This work bridges gaps between occupational medicine, computational biomechanics, and systems biology, offering a novel paradigm for preventing work-related musculoskeletal disorders through simulation-guided ergonomic design and personalized activity monitoring. Successful implementation could redefine standards in procedural training programs and high-risk professions where traditional epidemiological approaches lack the resolution to address individualized physiological responses to repetitive strain.
cip_title: Health Professions and Related Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health professions and related clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of morphosyntactic features in regional Spanish and Portuguese dialects across Latin America, with a focus on understudied rural and Indigenous contact varieties. The research addresses a critical gap in Hispanic and Lusophone linguistics: large-scale, comparative studies of grammatical variation often lack computational rigor due to the complexity of modeling non-standardized linguistic data. We propose a mixed-methods approach combining corpus linguistics, rule-based morphological parsing, and machine learning classifiers to process multilingual text corpora spanning four centuries, including colonial manuscripts, oral histories, and modern social media. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of heterogeneous data (historical spellings, code-switching, and dialectal orthographies) and training transformer-based models to detect syntactic shifts influenced by Indigenous substrate languages. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for corpus alignment across temporal and geographic axes. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access database documenting morphosyntactic trajectories in 12+ dialect zones, (2) probabilistic maps of grammatical convergence/divergence patterns, and (3) a computational framework adaptable to other low-resource language contact scenarios. By quantifying how sociohistorical factors (e.g., migration, language policies) correlate with structural changes, this work will advance theoretical debates about language variation in postcolonial contexts while providing pedagogical tools for heritage language preservation. The requested HPC resources are essential given the project’s scope: initial pilot studies required 8TB of annotated text and 900+ GPU hours to achieve baseline accuracy, with final models anticipated to process 50TB+ of multi-modal linguistic data.
detailed_field: Hispanic/ Latin American languages, literatures, and linguistics
cip_title: Hispanic and Latin American Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages and literatures of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking areas of the world, including the Iberian, Latin American, and Lusophone worlds. Includes instruction in Spanish and Portuguese language and linguistics; regional and Latin American dialects; and Spanish, Portuguese, Spanish American, Luso-Brazilian, and Chicano literature.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis and simulation of theatrical performance dynamics. While traditional theater research relies on qualitative, small-scale observations of actor-audience interactions, set design efficacy, and script structure, the lack of scalable quantitative methods limits the ability to model complex, large-scale performance systems or analyze historical datasets for cross-cultural patterns. This research proposes the development of a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), natural language processing (NLP), and 3D spatial simulations to study how variables such as dialogue pacing, stage geometry, and audience demographics collectively influence perceived dramatic tension. The ABM component will simulate audience response dynamics using behavioral data from motion-captured performances, while NLP algorithms will analyze semantic and prosodic features in a corpus of 20th-century experimental plays to identify structural correlates of emotional engagement. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated rendering will model sightline and acoustics trade-offs in historically significant theater architectures. HPC resources are essential to process multimodal datasets (e.g., motion capture, archival scripts, architectural blueprints) and run iterative simulations at scales exceeding 10,000 agent-interactions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible toolkit for quantifying narrative rhythm and spatial performance parameters, (2) predictive models linking script structures to audience engagement metrics, and (3) evidence-based reconstructions of acoustics in demolished theaters. By establishing computational methods tailored to theater studies, this work aims to bridge gaps between artistic practice and data-driven humanities research, offering new methodologies for preserving intangible cultural heritage and optimizing contemporary performance spaces. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale performance datasets and real-time rendering of complex spatial models, capabilities unattainable with standard departmental computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Drama and Dramatics/ Theatre Arts, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of dramatic works and their performance. Includes instruction in major works of dramatic literature, dramatic styles and types, and the principles of organizing and producing full live or filmed productions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address the challenge of analyzing high-dimensional, longitudinal biomedical data with complex missingness patterns, a pervasive issue in clinical and public health studies. Traditional statistical approaches often rely on restrictive assumptions about missing data mechanisms, leading to biased estimates and reduced power in identifying dynamic risk factors or treatment effects. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel Bayesian joint modeling framework that integrates longitudinal outcomes, time-to-event data, and covariate processes while explicitly accounting for non-ignorable missingness through shared latent structures. The computational burden of estimating high-dimensional parameters and latent variables necessitates advanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms, which will be optimized for parallelization across high-performance computing (HPC) nodes. We will implement adaptive Metropolis-Hastings samplers with gradient-based proposals and develop distributed computing strategies to handle large-scale datasets from multi-center cohort studies. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid evaluation of model performance through simulations spanning diverse missingness scenarios, as well as applications to real-world studies on chronic disease progression. Expected outcomes include open-source software for reproducible analysis pipelines, rigorous quantification of biases under model misspecification, and clinically actionable insights into time-varying predictors of patient outcomes. By providing robust tools for complex biomedical data, this work will enhance the reliability of evidence guiding personalized intervention strategies and public health policy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of descriptive and inferential statistics to biomedical research and clinical, public health, and industrial issues related to human populations. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, modeling, clinical trials methodology, disease and survival analysis, longitudinal analysis, missing data analysis, spatial analysis, computer tomography, biostatistics consulting, and applications to such topics as genetics, oncology, pharmacokinetics, physiology, neurobiology, and biophysics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the multi-dimensional impacts of transnational policy frameworks on human security outcomes in fragile and conflict-affected regions. The research addresses a critical gap in public policy analysis: the lack of scalable, data-driven methodologies to evaluate how overlapping international agreements—ranging from climate adaptation pledges to arms control treaties—interact dynamically to influence displacement risks, resource access, and governance stability. Traditional policy evaluation tools struggle to account for the non-linear feedback loops, time-lagged effects, and spatial interdependencies inherent in these systems. To overcome these limitations, the project will develop an adaptive computational framework integrating three components: (1) natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to systematically codify treaty obligations and compliance reports from 150+ multilateral agreements; (2) agent-based models simulating how policy-induced resource allocation changes propagate through local socioeconomic networks; and (3) geospatial-temporal analyses linking satellite-derived conflict indicators with policy implementation timelines. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing unstructured multilingual policy documents at scale, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across diverse conflict scenarios, and maintaining high-resolution spatial datasets spanning 40+ at-risk regions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible policy interaction matrix identifying leverage points for reducing unintended consequences, along with machine learning models capable of forecasting second-order governance impacts when novel agreements are proposed. By quantifying how discrete policy instruments collectively shape human security trajectories, this work aims to advance evidence-based frameworks for designing coherent international policy portfolios while mitigating fragmentation risks in multilateral systems. The computational tools developed will be shared with UN policy coordination units to strengthen scenario-testing capacities in crisis response planning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to relationships among nations and among governments and non-governmental entities. Includes instruction in international politics, governance, financial policy, and security affairs; globalization; economic and social policies of developing nations; and applications to specific public policy topics such as labor and employment, immigration, and human rights.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the historical and cultural dynamics of Ural-Altaic and Central Asian societies, with a focus on reconstructing and analyzing the evolution of multilingual textual traditions along the Silk Road. The research problem centers on the fragmented and heterogeneous nature of surviving manuscripts, inscriptions, and epigraphic materials, which span Turkic, Mongolian, and other regional languages across diverse scripts (e.g., Old Uyghur, Classical Mongolian, Brahmi-derived systems). Current scholarship lacks systematic tools to analyze these materials at scale, particularly for identifying cross-cultural linguistic influences, scribal practices, and semantic shifts over time. To address this gap, the project will employ computational linguistics, machine learning, and geospatial modeling techniques. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for low-resource historical languages to automate text recognition and translation, applying network analysis to trace the diffusion of literary motifs, and simulating trade route interactions using agent-based models to correlate cultural exchange with textual production patterns. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of digitized manuscripts, running large-scale parallel simulations, and optimizing deep learning architectures requiring GPU-accelerated workloads. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated texts, interactive maps visualizing cultural-linguistic contact zones, and novel methodologies for integrating computational analysis into philological and historical studies. By bridging area studies with advanced computing, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of Central Asia’s role in premodern Eurasia, while preserving endangered cultural heritage through digitally sustainable frameworks.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries of Inner/Central Asia, including the Turkic and Mongolian inhabitants of the Caspian, Amur, Tien Shan, Baikal, Gobi, Siberian, and Manchurian areas and the historical Silk Road, in terms of their past and present development.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurocognitive dynamics of real-time language comprehension through computational modeling of large-scale behavioral and neural datasets. A critical gap in psycholinguistic theory lies in explaining how hierarchical syntactic structures and semantic ambiguities are resolved incrementally during rapid speech processing, given the brain’s parallel-interactive processing constraints. Current models struggle to integrate multi-level linguistic features (phonological, syntactic, contextual) with empirically observed reaction times and neural activation patterns from EEG/fMRI studies. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid computational architecture combining parallelized neural networks with probabilistic Bayesian inference systems. The model will simulate cascaded activation across lexical, syntactic, and discourse representation layers while incorporating individual differences in working memory capacity—a key cognitive constraint. High-performance computing resources are essential for three components: (1) training deep neural networks on corpus-derived speech streams (5TB of annotated multilingual data), (2) running Monte Carlo simulations of probabilistic parsing pathways under noise perturbation, and (3) optimizing model parameters against 12 experimental datasets (N=800 participants) through distributed genetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for testing competing theories of sentence processing architecture, novel predictions about neural oscillation patterns during ambiguity resolution, and open-source tools for simulating individual differences in language comprehension. By leveraging GPU-accelerated parameter space exploration and large-scale model comparison, this work will advance mechanistic accounts of how biological constraints shape linguistic computation, with implications for cognitive models of learning and adaptive processing. The requested resources will enable computationally intensive simulations that directly connect micro-level neural dynamics to macro-level behavioral phenomena in human language.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the mechanisms and processes of learning and thinking, and associated information encoding, decoding, processing and transmitting systems. Includes instruction in theories of cognition and intelligence; studies of cognitive processes such as memory, sensation, perception, pattern recognition, problem solving, and conceptual thinking; cybernetics; psycholinguistics; and the study of biological and social communications mechanisms and processes.

abstract: Liver transplantation remains a life-saving intervention for end-stage liver disease, yet significant challenges persist in predicting graft survival, optimizing immunosuppression regimens, and managing post-transplant complications. Current clinical models often rely on static, single-modality data, limiting their ability to account for dynamic interactions between donor-recipient immune compatibility, multi-omics profiles, and evolving clinical variables. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive framework to integrate longitudinal multi-modal data—including genomics, proteomics, radiomics, and electronic health records—from a multicenter cohort of 2,500 liver transplant recipients. Using machine learning approaches such as transformer-based neural networks and ensemble models, we will simulate immune-mediated graft injury pathways, predict early and late rejection events, and identify biomarkers of tolerance. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale parallel simulations to analyze spatial transcriptomic data from graft biopsies, coupled with time-series clinical variables. Validation will involve retrospective prediction of known outcomes and prospective correlation with real-world transplant registry data. This resource-intensive approach is necessary due to the high dimensionality of multi-omics datasets, the temporal complexity of post-transplant immune responses, and the need for real-time adaptive modeling in clinical decision support tools. Expected outcomes include the creation of a validated predictive model for graft survival with superior accuracy to existing clinical scores, a computational platform for personalized immunosuppression dosing, and open-source tools for dynamic risk stratification. The project directly addresses unmet needs in transplant hepatology by enabling data-driven precision in pre- and post-transplant care, with potential to reduce rejection rates, improve long-term patient outcomes, and lower healthcare costs through optimized resource allocation.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge and the skill required of a gastroenterologist to care for patients prior to and following hepatic transplantation that spans all phases of liver transplantation.

abstract: The development of next-generation nuclear fusion reactors demands high-fidelity computational tools to address the complex multiphysics phenomena governing plasma stability, neutron transport, and materials performance under extreme conditions. Current simulations often rely on decoupled or reduced-order models due to computational limitations, leading to gaps in understanding the nonlinear interactions between magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities, neutron-induced material damage, and heat transfer in plasma-facing components. This project seeks to advance integrated, high-resolution simulations of fusion reactor systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve coupled plasma-material dynamics at unprecedented scales. The research will employ a hybrid computational framework combining finite-element MHD solvers, Monte Carlo neutron transport codes, and molecular dynamics models to capture cross-scale interactions—from macroscopic plasma behavior to atomic-scale defect evolution in tungsten-based divertors. Key challenges include optimizing parallel scalability for heterogeneous architectures, managing data-intensive workflows between physics modules, and validating simulations against experimental datasets from tokamak facilities. The HPC resources requested will enable parametric studies of reactor configurations under varying magnetic confinement scenarios, neutron flux intensities, and transient thermal loads. Expected outcomes include predictive insights into plasma edge-localized mode (ELM) suppression mechanisms, quantitative estimates of structural degradation in irradiated materials, and optimized divertor geometries to mitigate heat flux asymmetries. By bridging gaps between plasma physics and materials engineering, this work aims to accelerate the design of robust fusion systems with enhanced operational lifetimes, directly supporting global efforts to achieve sustainable fusion energy. The developed computational workflows will also be disseminated as open-source tools to foster collaboration within the fusion research community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling and manipulating nuclear energy, including nuclear power plant design, fission reactor design, fusion reactor design, reactor control and safety systems design, power transfer systems, containment vessels and structures design; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as fission and fusion processes, human and environmental factors, construction, and operational considerations.

abstract: Soil microbiomes play a critical role in mediating biogeochemical cycles, plant health, and agricultural productivity. However, the dynamic interactions between microbial communities, soil physicochemical properties, and crop management practices remain poorly resolved at scales relevant to agricultural systems. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in their ability to disentangle these complex, nonlinear interactions or predict emergent behaviors under varying environmental conditions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that integrate microbial genomic data, soil chemistry, and crop phenology to predict how soil management strategies influence microbiome stability and function. We will employ agent-based modeling to simulate microbial community dynamics at the micrometer scale, coupled with genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions to predict nutrient fluxes. These fine-grained simulations will be nested within larger-scale biogeochemical models parameterized using field data from long-term agricultural trials. Machine learning approaches will further identify key microbial taxa and functional genes associated with soil carbon sequestration and nitrogen-use efficiency. The computational workload necessitates parallelized simulations across thousands of cores due to the high dimensionality of genomic datasets and stochasticity in microbial interactions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to optimize crop rotation, tillage, and amendment strategies for enhanced soil health. By elucidating the mechanistic links between microbial community structure and agronomically relevant soil functions, this work will provide actionable insights for sustainable intensification of agricultural systems. The developed models will be made available to the broader research community through open-source platforms, enabling future investigations into microbiome-driven soil management solutions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on application of microbiological theory and methods to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions, and the biological components and effects of soil management strategies. Includes instruction in microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, soil chemistry and physics as related to biological characteristics, and environmental science.

abstract: Infectious diseases in livestock pose significant threats to global food security and agricultural economies, with pathogens such as *Mycobacterium avium* subsp. *paratuberculosis*, influenza A viruses, and antimicrobial-resistant bacteria presenting persistent challenges. Current gaps in understanding host-pathogen dynamics and immune evasion mechanisms hinder the development of targeted interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genomic, transcriptomic, and structural determinants of microbial virulence and host immune responses in agriculturally relevant species. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating bacterial and viral whole-genome sequencing data from clinical isolates, RNA-seq datasets from infected host tissues, and molecular dynamics simulations of pathogen-host protein interactions. Machine learning models will identify genetic markers associated with pathogenicity and antimicrobial resistance, while agent-based models will simulate intra-herd transmission dynamics under varying immune conditions. Phylogenetic analyses will trace the evolution of zoonotic viruses across species barriers, and epitope mapping tools will predict conserved antigenic regions for vaccine design. The scale of these datasets—encompassing terabytes of sequencing data and millisecond-scale molecular simulations—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated workflows only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of immune evasion strategies employed by priority pathogens, (2) predictive models for emergent antimicrobial resistance in veterinary settings, and (3) structural characterization of host receptor-pathogen protein interfaces to guide therapeutic development. By bridging computational immunobiology with veterinary microbiology, this work will directly inform vaccine strategies, biosecurity protocols, and precision antimicrobial use policies, advancing the agricultural sciences’ capacity to mitigate infectious disease burdens in livestock systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microbial causation and immunologic processes related to animal disease, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in bacteriology, mycology, virology, immune response mechanisms, humoral and cell function, cancer defenses, immune system dysfunction, immunologic diseases, parasitology, pathogenesis, and disease vectors.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing decentralized resource networks for small businesses engaged in circular economy practices—a critical gap in entrepreneurial operations where dynamic resource flows, regulatory constraints, and sustainability goals intersect. Small enterprises often lack the computational tools to model complex, multi-stakeholder systems required for efficient material reuse, energy recovery, and waste valorization. Traditional linear optimization models fail to capture the nonlinear interdependencies and real-time variability inherent in these networks, particularly when integrating IoT-generated supply chain data with ecological impact metrics. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a graph-based reinforcement learning framework to simulate and optimize decentralized resource exchanges across spatially distributed small businesses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training multi-agent models that account for heterogeneous business objectives, time-varying resource availability, and regulatory scenarios. The computational architecture will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing supplier geolocation, material composition analytics, and carbon accounting records. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system that enables small businesses to dynamically reconfigure resource partnerships while maximizing circularity metrics. This work advances computational entrepreneurship by introducing scalable methods for ethical AI in resource allocation, directly addressing the operational bottlenecks faced by sustainability-driven small enterprises. The project’s significance lies in its potential to democratize access to advanced predictive tools for circular economy adoption, fostering resilience in entrepreneurial ecosystems without requiring proprietary software investments. Results will be validated against case studies from urban manufacturing cooperatives and rural agro-industrial networks, establishing performance benchmarks for decentralized circularity optimization.
cip_title: Entrepreneurial and Small Business Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in enterprise management and entrepreneurship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance comparative analyses of cultural and group identity formation across intersecting axes of race, gender, sexuality, and geography. The research problem centers on the limitations of current methodological frameworks in capturing multidimensional, dynamic interactions within and between groups, particularly when analyzing large-scale digital archives, multimedia cultural artifacts, and transnational discourse networks. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to process the volume and heterogeneity of data required for robust comparative studies, while existing computational tools often lack the flexibility to model intersectional identities or trace evolving cultural narratives across temporal and spatial scales. To address this, the project will develop and deploy scalable computational workflows integrating natural language processing (NLP), multimodal data fusion, and network analysis techniques. These methods will be applied to curated datasets spanning 20th-century diasporic literature, social media discourse from transnational LGBTQ+ communities, and visual culture archives reflecting decolonial movements. Key computational challenges include training custom transformer-based models to detect nuanced identity markers in multilingual texts, optimizing graph algorithms to map cross-cultural influence networks, and implementing GPU-accelerated pipelines for analyzing image-text relationships in multimedia artifacts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, iterative model training with hyperparameter optimization, and real-time visualization of complex relational dynamics. Expected outcomes include new open-source tools for intersectional cultural analytics, a publicly accessible repository of annotated datasets, and theoretical insights into how marginalized groups negotiate identity in transnational contexts. By bridging computational scalability with critical cultural theory, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-intensive comparative studies while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue between digital humanities and social science approaches to group identity.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comparative study of the history, literature, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of different groups such as racial, gender, sexual, class, ethnic, geographical, and national. Includes instruction in comparative studies, comparative literature, critical race theory, cultural anthropology, cultural studies, religious studies, science studies, social and cultural theory, urban studies, and visual culture.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of quantum many-body dynamics in ultracold molecular systems, a critical challenge in atomic and molecular physics. Ultracold molecules exhibit complex interactions governed by highly correlated electronic, vibrational, and rotational states, which are difficult to model analytically or probe experimentally with sufficient resolution. The research aims to develop and apply high-performance computing (HPC) simulations to unravel these dynamics, focusing on systems of dipolar molecules in optical lattices. Key objectives include mapping the interplay of long-range dipole-dipole interactions, external field effects, and quantum degeneracy, which dictate phenomena such as phase transitions and entanglement propagation in these systems. The computational approach combines tensor network methods with large-scale exact diagonalization to handle the exponential scaling of Hilbert space, while machine learning techniques will optimize basis sets and reduce computational costs. Time-dependent simulations will model non-equilibrium dynamics under realistic experimental parameters, including trap geometries and decoherence effects. The HPC resources requested will enable simulations at unprecedented scales, targeting systems of 50-100 interacting molecules—far beyond current capabilities—while maintaining quantum-state resolution. Expected outcomes include predictive models for controlling molecular quantum states, insights into entanglement generation in driven-dissipative environments, and benchmarks for emerging experimental platforms. This work will directly contribute to the development of quantum simulators and precision measurement technologies, while addressing foundational questions in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics. By bridging gaps between theory and experiment, the project aims to establish computational protocols that enhance the design and interpretation of ultracold molecular experiments, fostering advances in quantum information science and fundamental physics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between neural population dynamics and high-level cognitive decision-making under uncertainty, integrating computational neuroscience, behavioral psychology, and machine learning. The core research problem addresses a gap in understanding how distributed neural circuits collectively encode uncertainty across hierarchical temporal scales—from rapid sensory processing to slower deliberative choices—and how these mechanisms fail in neuropsychiatric conditions characterized by impaired risk assessment, such as anxiety disorders. Current models either oversimplify biological detail or lack the scalability to capture multi-regional brain interactions during complex tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel computational framework combining biophysically detailed spiking neural network models of prefrontal-amygdala interactions with hierarchical Bayesian inference processes. The approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate networks of >500,000 neurons with biologically realistic connectivity, incorporating real-world behavioral data from human participants performing a sequential risk-taking task. Machine learning pipelines will analyze trial-by-trial decision patterns and neural activity signatures, enabling cross-validation between simulated and empirical datasets. Key computational challenges requiring HPC resources include parallelized parameter space exploration for circuit models, large-scale neural population state tracking, and optimization of hybrid neural-Bayesian architectures through evolutionary algorithms. Expected outcomes include 1) a mechanistic explanation of how metastable neural states gate uncertainty representations across timescales, 2) predictive models linking specific circuit dysfunction to maladaptive risk perception, and 3) an open-source toolbox for simulating multiscale decision architectures. This work will advance cognitive science by unifying neurobiological and computational perspectives on uncertainty processing, with translational implications for developing biologically grounded AI decision systems and personalized neuromodulation therapies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the mind and the nature of intelligence from the interdisciplinary perspectives of computer science, philosophy, mathematics, psychology, neuroscience, and other disciplines. Includes instruction in mathematics and logic, cognitive process modeling, dynamic systems, learning theories, brain and cognition, neural networking, programming, and applications to topics such as language acquisition, computer systems, and perception and behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in the analysis of large-scale legal document corpora, a critical challenge for legal support services operating in complex litigation and regulatory environments. Traditional manual review processes for case law, contracts, and regulatory filings are time-intensive, error-prone, and ill-suited to identifying subtle patterns across jurisdictions or temporal shifts in legal reasoning. Our research focuses on developing a computational framework to automate the extraction of semantically meaningful features from unstructured legal texts, map citation networks, and detect latent correlations between legal outcomes and contextual variables (e.g., judicial appointments, socio-political trends). The proposed methodology combines transformer-based natural language processing models, graph neural networks, and temporal clustering algorithms to process multilingual legal datasets spanning 50 million pages of case law, statutes, and administrative rulings. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific language models, optimizing hyperparameters at scale, and simulating the cascading impacts of precedent alterations in hypothetical litigation scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for legal analytics, validated against manual annotations from practicing attorneys, and a novel metric for quantifying jurisdictional divergence in statutory interpretation. By enabling rapid, reproducible analysis of legal texts, this work aims to reduce operational bottlenecks in legal support workflows, enhance predictive capabilities for case strategy development, and provide empirical insights into systemic biases or inconsistencies within judicial decision-making. The project bridges computational linguistics, network science, and legal informatics, advancing a specialized niche in legal support services that remains underserved by existing interdisciplinary research infrastructures.
cip_definition: Any program in legal support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Fisheries management faces critical challenges in balancing sustainable resource use with economic and ecological demands, particularly under climate change and increasing anthropogenic pressures. Current stock assessment models often lack the spatial and temporal resolution needed to capture complex population dynamics, migratory behaviors, and ecosystem interactions, leading to uncertainties in harvest quotas and conservation strategies. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework to simulate fish population dynamics, habitat shifts, and fishing effort distributions across marine and freshwater ecosystems. The framework will integrate environmental data (e.g., temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen), species-specific life history traits, and spatially explicit fishing activity datasets to predict stock responses under varying management scenarios and climate projections. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of simulating millions of individual agents across decadal timescales, coupled with real-world hydrodynamic and biogeochemical datasets. Parallelized algorithms will optimize model runtime, while machine learning techniques will be applied to calibrate parameters and reduce uncertainty in population trajectories. Expected outcomes include improved predictions of stock resilience, identification of critical habitat thresholds for endangered species, and evaluation of adaptive management policies such as dynamic marine protected areas or seasonal closures. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to provide fisheries managers with scalable, decision-support tools that enhance the precision of stock assessments and promote ecosystem-based management. The results will directly inform regional and federal policy discussions on sustainable fishing practices, addressing gaps in current conservation frameworks while supporting the socioeconomic stability of fishing-dependent communities.
cip_title: Fishing and Fisheries Sciences and Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the husbandry and production of non-domesticated fish and shellfish populations for recreational and commercial purposes and the management of fishing and marine/aquatic product processing to ensure adequate conservation and efficient utilization. Includes instruction in the principles of marine/aquatic biology, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, water resources, fishing production operations and management, fishing policy and regulation, and the management of recreational and commercial fishing activities.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between urban spatial configurations and emergent pedestrian movement patterns to model how micro-scale human behaviors influence macro-scale accessibility and equity in cities. While urban mobility is often studied through transportation networks or economic frameworks, this research adopts a novel computational social science lens, focusing on pedestrian decision-making as a driver of spatial segregation, resource access, and neighborhood vitality. The core challenge lies in simulating millions of individual agents with heterogeneous preferences (e.g., safety, convenience, social ties) across high-resolution urban environments while capturing feedback loops between mobility choices and evolving neighborhood conditions. We propose an adaptive agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrating real-time geospatial data streams (street-view imagery, pedestrian sensors, crowdsourced place perceptions) with machine learning to calibrate agent behavior rules. High-performance computing resources are essential to parallelize simulations across 20+ urban case studies, each requiring 10^5-10^6 agents interacting over dynamic graph representations of street networks and land use. The computational workflow leverages GPU-accelerated spatial kernels for pathfinding and graph updates, paired with Bayesian optimization to iteratively refine parameters against ground-truth mobility datasets. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) identification of critical inflection points where pedestrian behavior amplifies or mitigates spatial inequalities, (2) a scalable urban simulation toolkit for testing equity-focused interventions (e.g., pedestrian infrastructure investments), and (3) synthetic population mobility datasets to support policymaking in underserved cities lacking traditional survey infrastructure. By bridging computational scalability with behavioral realism, this work advances methodological frontiers in urban social science while providing actionable insights for designing cities that prioritize human-centered accessibility over purely efficiency-driven models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of social science principles to the study of urban institutions and the forces influencing urban social and political life. Includes instruction in urban theory, the development and evolution of urban areas, urban sociology, principles of urban and social planning, and the politics and economics of urban government and services.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in designing next-generation antenna systems for emerging terahertz (THz) wireless communication networks, such as 6G. Current electromagnetic simulation tools struggle with the scale and complexity of optimizing high-frequency, ultra-wideband antenna arrays, which require nanoscale geometric precision and multi-physics modeling of radiative coupling, thermal effects, and material nonlinearities. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework combining parallelized finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations with machine learning (ML)-guided optimization. The FDTD simulations will leverage distributed-memory parallelism via MPI to model antenna performance across 3D multi-scale geometries with sub-micron resolution, while ML surrogates will iteratively refine designs to maximize gain, bandwidth, and energy efficiency. The computational workload necessitates large-scale HPC resources due to the memory-intensive nature of high-resolution THz wave propagation models and the need for thousands of parameterized simulations during optimization cycles. Expected outcomes include novel antenna architectures capable of operating efficiently in the 0.1–1 THz range, validated through experimental prototypes. This work will also yield open-source software modules for GPU-accelerated FDTD-ML co-design, enabling broader adoption of HPC in electromagnetic device research. Successful implementation will directly advance the development of compact, high-throughput wireless systems critical for 6G infrastructure, biomedical imaging, and space communications, while establishing scalable computational workflows for future electronic engineering challenges at the intersection of photonics and radio frequency (RF) technologies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronic engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic topology and geometric combinatorics by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address computational challenges in homotopy theory and transformation group actions. The central research problem involves characterizing higher-dimensional homotopy invariants of non-simply connected spaces and analyzing the dynamics of group actions on continua—problems that are theoretically intricate and computationally intractable with conventional methods. Key obstacles include the exponential growth of combinatorial configurations in cell complex decompositions, the memory-intensive nature of persistent homology calculations over large simplicial complexes, and the need for parallelized algorithms to explore transformation orbits in high-dimensional representation spaces. The proposed computational approach combines novel algorithmic frameworks for distributed computation of spectral sequences, optimized parallel processing of chain complex data structures, and GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods to sample group action dynamics. These methods will be implemented via a hybrid MPI-CUDA architecture to efficiently distribute computational tasks across nodes, minimize inter-process communication overhead, and optimize memory utilization during large-scale homology computations. Expected outcomes include the first systematic classification of homotopy types for certain families of 6-dimensional CW-complexes, quantitative bounds on stabilizer dimensions in profinite group actions, and open-source software tools for computational topology. The results will directly contribute to open conjectures in shape theory and transformation group topology while establishing new benchmarks for applying HPC to pure mathematical research. By addressing these computationally prohibitive problems, the project aims to bridge theoretical advances in foundational topology with cutting-edge computational techniques, creating infrastructure that will benefit multiple subfields within pure mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of unaltered geometric configurations under conditions of continuous, multi-directional transformations. Includes instruction in mathematical logic, proof theory, model theory, set theory, combinatorics, continua, homotopy, homology, links, and transformation actions.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable livestock production necessitates advanced genetic strategies to improve disease resistance, productivity, and environmental adaptability in agricultural animals. Current genomic selection models struggle to account for the complexity of polygenic traits, genotype-by-environment interactions, and the integration of multi-omics data, limiting their predictive accuracy and applicability across diverse populations. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing scalable computational frameworks for optimizing breeding programs using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to analyze whole-genome sequencing data from cattle, poultry, and swine populations (n ≈ 50,000 animals) alongside longitudinal environmental and phenotypic records to identify causal variants, epigenetic modifiers, and adaptive gene networks. Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and gradient-boosted trees, will be implemented to model non-linear genetic effects and predict trait expression under varying management and climate scenarios. Bayesian hierarchical models will concurrently estimate population parameters while accounting for pedigree structure and spatial-temporal covariates. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized genomic prediction tools, Markov chain Monte Carlo samplers, and distributed tensor operations to process terabytes of genomic data. Expected outcomes include novel breeding value estimation methods with improved generalizability, open-source software for genomic selection under environmental constraints, and actionable insights into pleiotropic loci affecting multiple production traits. By enabling rapid analysis of complex genotype-phenotype-environment relationships at unprecedented scale, this research will directly inform breeding strategies to enhance animal welfare, reduce agricultural emissions, and secure food systems against climate variability. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive computations, iterative model training, and large-scale simulations of breeding program outcomes over generational timescales.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural animal health, the development of new animal breeds, and the selective improvement of agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, animal health, animal husbandry, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct a large-scale computational analysis of African-American/Black literary texts across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. The research addresses a critical gap in literary studies: the systematic examination of thematic, stylistic, and intertextual patterns within the expansive and diverse corpus of Black diasporic literature. Traditional close-reading methods, while foundational, struggle to synthesize connections across centuries, genres, and geographic regions, limiting scholars’ ability to trace the evolution of cultural motifs, narrative strategies, and collective memory in response to socio-historical forces. To overcome these limitations, this project will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyze a curated digital corpus of over 10,000 texts, including novels, poetry, essays, and transcribed oral narratives from the 19th century to the present. Topic modeling will identify latent thematic clusters, while sentiment analysis and semantic network mapping will quantify shifts in emotional tonality and conceptual relationships correlated with key historical events, such as the Harlem Renaissance or the Civil Rights Movement. Custom transformer-based models will detect intertextual references and stylistic innovations, enabling a granular study of influence and adaptation among authors. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized text ingestion, distributed training of deep learning architectures, and high-memory network analysis—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access interactive database visualizing literary trends, a series of computational workflows tailored to diasporic textual analysis, and peer-reviewed findings on understudied transnational connections in Black literary expression. By integrating computational rigor with literary scholarship, this project aims to advance both methodological innovation in the humanities and substantive insights into the dynamic traditions of African-American/Black literature, ultimately enriching pedagogical and public understandings of this cultural legacy.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ethical decision-making in complex, large-scale social systems. Traditional ethical analysis often relies on hypothetical or small-scale case studies, limiting its capacity to model dynamic interactions between diverse moral frameworks or predict emergent outcomes in real-world scenarios. To address this gap, we propose developing computational models that simulate ethical reasoning across heterogeneous populations, integrating normative theories (e.g., deontology, consequentialism, virtue ethics) with empirical data on cultural and contextual variables. Agent-based modeling will be employed to represent individuals and institutions as autonomous agents governed by distinct ethical principles, enabling the study of moral conflicts, cooperation, and systemic shifts under varying conditions. These simulations will incorporate multi-layered networks to capture the influence of social structures, power dynamics, and historical precedents on collective ethical behavior. Additionally, natural language processing techniques will be applied to analyze ethical discourse in philosophical texts, policy documents, and interdisciplinary research, identifying patterns in moral argumentation and value prioritization. The scale and complexity of these tasks—requiring millions of parallelized simulations, high-dimensional parameter spaces, and large textual corpora—necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for testing the robustness of ethical theories in sociotechnical systems, (2) data-driven insights into how moral norms evolve under technological or environmental pressures, and (3) open-source tools to support ethicists in evaluating policy interventions or AI systems. By bridging formal ethical analysis with computational social science, this work aims to enhance the predictive and prescriptive capacities of moral philosophy while maintaining rigorous engagement with normative theory.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the theory of moral good and its application to various theoretical and practical problems. Includes instruction in ethical theory, history of ethics, belief and value systems, ethical constructs, and applications to specific topics, issues and problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and fabrication of structural and ornamental ironwork, addressing critical challenges in load distribution, thermal stress management, and material efficiency. While traditional ironworking relies on empirical methods and standardized codes, increasingly complex architectural demands and sustainability requirements necessitate data-driven approaches to predict structural behavior under dynamic conditions. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in large-scale metal structures, including stress-strain dynamics during welding, thermal deformation in ornamental components, and fatigue resistance in high-load environments. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify optimal beam configurations, welding parameters, and reinforcement patterns. Simulations will integrate real-world data from strain gauges and thermal sensors to validate models against physical prototypes. The computational workload requires parallel processing to manage iterative optimizations across millions of mesh elements and time steps, which is infeasible with local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing material waste in fabrication, enhancing the safety margins of custom architectural designs, and reducing reliance on physical prototyping. These tools will be disseminated as open-source modules for educational use in ironworking programs, bridging gaps between traditional trade skills and computational literacy. By advancing the precision of structural simulations, this work aims to set new benchmarks for energy-efficient metal construction and support the development of next-generation building codes. The project aligns with national priorities for sustainable infrastructure and workforce development in technical fields, offering a template for integrating HPC-driven innovation into trade education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to make and install structural, ornamental, and reinforcing metal structures and supports. Includes instruction in drafting, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, welding, riveting, beam placement, ornamental design, structural reinforcement, crane operation, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Bulgarian linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in scalable text processing and data-driven inquiry for under-resourced languages. The primary research problem centers on the challenges of analyzing large-scale Bulgarian textual corpora—spanning medieval manuscripts, modern literature, and dialectal variations—using traditional methods, which lack the capacity to efficiently process complex linguistic patterns or map diachronic language evolution. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, machine learning models, and philological analysis to investigate three core areas: (1) automated morphological and syntactic parsing of pre-modern Bulgarian texts to trace grammatical shifts; (2) dialect classification using phonetic and lexical features extracted from regional speech corpora; and (3) semantic network analysis of literary works to identify thematic and stylistic trends across periods. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on heterogeneous datasets, optimizing parallel processing for corpus annotation, and managing storage demands for digitized manuscripts. Expected outcomes include the development of open-access tools for Bulgarian NLP tasks, a georeferenced dialect atlas, and quantitative frameworks for literary periodization. These results will directly contribute to preserving linguistic heritage, enhancing pedagogical resources, and enabling cross-disciplinary applications in fields such as digital humanities and computational social science. By addressing the computational limitations of existing Bulgarian language research, this project aims to establish a foundation for large-scale, reproducible studies while fostering collaboration between linguists, literary scholars, and data scientists. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, high-memory nodes for corpus management, and scalable storage solutions for shared datasets, ensuring rigorous and innovative scholarship in a field traditionally constrained by manual methodologies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bulgarian language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and semantic patterns underlying ethical symbolism across religious and philosophical traditions using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing large, multilingual corpora of primary texts (e.g., scriptural exegeses, philosophical treatises) to identify how ethical concepts are symbolically encoded and evolve within and between traditions. Current manual approaches struggle to scale across diverse texts, limiting comparative studies of shared ethical frameworks. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), semantic network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM). NLP pipelines will process digitized texts in Sanskrit, Arabic, Classical Chinese, and Greek, leveraging transformer-based models for cross-lingual concept extraction. Dynamic semantic networks will map relationships between ethical symbols (e.g., "justice," "compassion") and their contextual associations, while ABM simulations will test hypotheses about how these symbolic systems influence decision-making paradigms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training multilingual NLP models, analyzing terabyte-scale text datasets, and running complex simulations of symbolic interaction across thousands of cultural-historical scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel computational framework for comparative ethics research, 2) a publicly accessible database of annotated ethical symbols spanning six religious-philosophical traditions, and 3) peer-reviewed insights into cross-cultural convergences in symbolic moral reasoning. This work will provide humanities researchers with scalable tools to study ethical systems as dynamic, interconnected phenomena, bridging gaps between philosophical analysis, religious studies, and computational social science.
cip_definition: A general program that combines the study of philosophy and religious studies. Includes instruction in logic; ethics; epistemology; symbolism; phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature, and art of religion; and world religions.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of personalized employee development pathways using computational modeling to enhance workforce adaptability in dynamic organizational environments. The research addresses a critical gap in Human Resources Development: the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to design individualized training interventions that balance employee skill growth, job role evolution, and organizational objectives amid rapidly changing market conditions. Current approaches often rely on static competency models that fail to account for complex interdependencies between learning patterns, team dynamics, and emergent organizational needs. We propose developing an adaptive simulation platform leveraging agent-based modeling and reinforcement learning to simulate workforce ecosystems at enterprise scale. The computational approach will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including skill assessments, collaboration networks, and performance metrics—to model how micro-level learning decisions propagate through organizational hierarchies. High-performance computing resources are essential to process longitudinal employee data (simulated and anonymized real-world datasets) while running parallelized simulations of alternative training policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel metric framework for quantifying "adaptive capacity" at individual and team levels, plus evidence-based recommendations for aligning personalized learning architectures with strategic workforce planning. The research will provide organizations with predictive tools to optimize human capital investments, reduce skill obsolescence risks, and improve retention through computationally designed career pathways. By bridging cognitive science, network theory, and operations research within an HR context, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for next-generation organizational development strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply integrated training, organizational development, and career planning and counseling skills to the design, management, and evaluation of programs to improve individual productivity, employability, and job satisfaction and organizational effectiveness. Includes instruction in psychology; organizational behavior; principles of adult education; occupational counseling; skill testing and evaluation; program design; consulting practice; organizational development; and applications to issues such as training, management development, customer service, and total quality management.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate diachronic and synchronic variations in understudied premodern East Asian textual corpora through advanced computational linguistics methods, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale multilingual datasets. Despite growing digitization efforts, significant gaps persist in understanding linguistic evolution and cross-regional literary influences in classical Chinese, early Japanese kanbun, and vernacular Korean texts due to the computational complexity of parsing non-Latin scripts, structural ambiguities in historical grammar, and the need for cross-referencing heterogeneous metadata (e.g., temporal, geographic, and authorial contexts). Our research will employ transformer-based language models fine-tuned for classical Sinographic scripts, combined with graph-based algorithms to map syntactic shifts and lexical borrowing patterns across 10th–17th century texts from China, Japan, and Korea. The computational workflow involves three phases: (1) preprocessing and aligning approximately 15 TB of digitized manuscripts and printed materials using OCR correction pipelines optimized for seal scripts and semi-cursive calligraphy; (2) training multilingual embeddings to detect semantic and stylistic divergences in parallel corpora (e.g., Buddhist sutras vs. secular administrative documents); and (3) applying dynamic network analysis to trace the diffusion of literary tropes across regions. HPC resources are critical for managing GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage of annotated texts, and parallelized comparative analyses across temporal slices. Anticipated outcomes include the first unified computational framework for cross-regional East Asian philology, a publicly accessible database of annotated texts with diachronic linguistic features, and quantitative insights into how maritime trade routes influenced literary hybridization. This work will establish scalable methodologies for analyzing non-Western historical languages while addressing infrastructure gaps in underrepresented humanities computing domains.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: East Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
