cip_definition: Any instructional program in East Asian languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Geriatric patients often present with complex, overlapping health conditions requiring personalized care strategies. Current clinical decision-making tools struggle to integrate multidimensional data—including polypharmacy interactions, comorbidities, and social determinants of health—to predict outcomes or optimize care plans. This project proposes developing a computational framework to model geriatric health trajectories using machine learning (ML) and simulation approaches, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will leverage structured electronic health records (EHRs) and unstructured clinical notes from geriatric populations to train predictive models for adverse events (e.g., falls, readmissions) and treatment responses. A hybrid ML architecture combining graph neural networks (to model disease-drug-diet interactions) and time-series analysis (to track longitudinal health states) will be implemented. Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations will further evaluate drug efficacy and toxicity risks under age-related physiological changes. HPC resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters across thousands of parallel trials, and running computationally intensive molecular dynamics simulations to assess protein-drug binding affinities in aging-related metabolic pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive tool for geriatric care prioritization, (2) evidence-based polypharmacy adjustment guidelines accounting for renal/hepatic decline, and (3) simulated datasets validating intervention strategies for frailty syndromes. By integrating population-level patterns with individual-level biomarkers, this work aims to advance precision gerontological nursing practices while establishing scalable computational methods for aging research. The requested computing infrastructure will enable training models on diverse patient cohorts, ensuring robustness across racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic groups underrepresented in existing geriatric studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation diffusion across social media platforms, with a focus on identifying patterns tied to user demographics, platform-specific affordances, and cultural contexts. As digital communication environments grow increasingly complex, traditional computational tools struggle to process the scale and heterogeneity of multimodal data (text, images, video) required to model these dynamics accurately. The research problem centers on addressing methodological gaps in analyzing cross-platform communication behaviors at scale, particularly in multilingual and intercultural contexts. To achieve this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to support three computational workflows: (1) large-scale natural language processing (NLP) for semantic and sentiment analysis of multilingual social media corpora, (2) network analysis of user interactions to map cascading misinformation pathways, and (3) machine learning models trained to detect contextual shifts in misinformation narratives across demographic groups. These methods require parallelized processing of terabytes of unstructured data, including real-time social media streams and historical archives, to identify latent variables influencing misinformation resilience. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for modeling communication ecologies in crisis scenarios, validated through case studies on climate change discourse and public health advocacy. The computational outputs will advance communication theory by quantifying how platform architectures mediate intercultural information flows, while practical applications will inform stakeholder strategies for mitigating misinformation. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to bridge qualitative communication research with data-driven approaches, fostering new interdisciplinary methodologies for media effects research.
cip_definition: An program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, research and research methods, and theories of communication, and that spans specialties within the field of communications. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods to address challenges in analyzing high-dimensional, sparse, and unbalanced biometric datasets common in agricultural and natural resource studies. Traditional statistical models often fail to accommodate the complex error structures, temporal dependencies, and missing data patterns inherent in field experiments, longitudinal trials, and observational ecological datasets. We propose a hybrid computational framework integrating Bayesian hierarchical modeling, stochastic optimization, and parallelized Monte Carlo sampling to improve parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification in such scenarios. The research will focus on two key applications: (1) optimizing multi-trait selection in plant breeding programs with unbalanced phenotypic records and genotype-environment interactions, and (2) modeling spatiotemporal variation in wildlife population dynamics using incomplete survey data. The computational workflow will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources for intensive matrix operations in mixed-effects model fitting, large-scale Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations, and bootstrap resampling for model validation. Specific HPC demands include distributed memory architectures for parallel processing of independent experimental replicates, GPU acceleration for tensor operations in multi-dimensional spline fitting, and high-throughput job scheduling for sensitivity analyses across biological parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for robust variance component estimation in unbalanced designs, improved convergence criteria for high-dimensional optimization problems, and adaptive sampling algorithms for missing data imputation in longitudinal studies. These computational advances will enhance the statistical rigor of biometric analyses in precision agriculture and conservation management while providing a template for handling complex error structures in biological systems. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from ongoing collaborations with agricultural research stations and wildlife monitoring networks, directly supporting methodological innovation in biostatistical applications for sustainable resource management.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics and other computational methods to the study of problems in the biological sciences and related fields in agriculture and natural resources. Includes instruction in computational biology, mathematical statistics, matrix algebra, applied calculus, experimental design, linear modeling, sampling theory, stochastic processes, spatial and temporal analysis, longitudinal analysis, sparse/unbalanced data and complex error, and applications to such topics as population genetics, animal breeding, forest genetics, population dynamics, wildlife biometry, ecology, and agricultural and natural resource management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on workplace team dynamics and resilience under rapidly changing organizational conditions. Industrial and organizational (I-O) psychology faces a critical challenge in modeling complex, multilevel interactions—such as communication patterns, stress cascades, and adaptive decision-making—that influence team performance in high-stakes environments. Traditional statistical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, time-dependent relationships inherent in these processes, particularly when analyzing large-scale, multimodal datasets (e.g., longitudinal surveys, communication logs, biometric sensor data). To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) integrated with machine learning to simulate team behavior under varying stress and resource constraints. The ABMs will incorporate empirically derived parameters from existing organizational datasets (N ≈ 15,000 employees across 12 industries) to replicate real-world decision hierarchies and reward structures. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze unstructured team communication data (≈10 TB of meeting transcripts and messaging logs) to identify resilience markers. HPC resources are essential for scaling Monte Carlo simulations to test intervention scenarios (e.g., modified feedback protocols, dynamic task reallocation) and for training transformer-based NLP models on heterogeneous text corpora. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks linking specific leadership behaviors and communication styles to team adaptability, as well as open-source tools for simulating organizational change impacts. This work directly supports evidence-based strategies for mitigating employee burnout and optimizing resource allocation in crisis-response teams, advancing I-O psychology’s capacity to address emergent workforce challenges. The computational workflows will be disseminated via partnerships with industry consortia to ensure translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and group behavior in institutional settings, applications to related problems of organization and industry, and that may prepare individuals to apply such principles in industrial and organizational settings. Includes instruction in group behavior theory, organizational theory, reward/punishment structures, human-machine and human-computer interactions, motivation dynamics, human stress studies, environmental and organizational influences on behavior, alienation and satisfaction, and job testing and assessment.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and reliable solar energy systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize installation designs, predict system performance, and streamline maintenance protocols. This project seeks to address critical gaps in current solar energy system modeling by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex interactions between photovoltaic (PV) components, environmental variables, and grid integration dynamics. Traditional methods for system design and fault diagnosis often rely on static models or localized datasets, which fail to account for real-time environmental variability, long-term degradation patterns, and the heterogeneous performance of PV arrays under diverse operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and finite element analysis (FEA). The ML component will train on historical and synthetic datasets—generated via HPC-driven simulations—to predict energy output fluctuations caused by shading, temperature changes, and panel degradation. Concurrently, CFD and FEA simulations will model thermal stress distributions and structural wear in PV modules under extreme weather conditions, enabling proactive maintenance strategies. By scaling these simulations across thousands of scenarios, the HPC environment will allow us to identify optimal installation configurations, validate repair protocols, and develop predictive maintenance tools tailored to regional climatic challenges. The outcomes of this research will directly inform curriculum updates in solar technician training programs, ensuring alignment with data-driven industry practices. Additionally, the open-source models and datasets produced will serve as a foundation for future innovations in solar energy system resilience, reducing downtime and operational costs for residential and commercial installations. This project underscores the critical role of HPC in advancing solar technology education and practice, bridging the gap between theoretical models and real-world system deployment.
cip_title: Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair solar energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Latin textual corpora spanning classical, medieval, and ecclesiastical periods. A central challenge in Latin philology lies in systematically tracing linguistic evolution, syntactic variation, and lexical shifts across eras, dialects, and genres—tasks complicated by the scale and diversity of surviving texts. Traditional manual methods struggle to process the growing digitized corpus, which includes inscriptions, classical literature, medieval manuscripts, and liturgical documents, often with fragmentary or contested authorship. This research proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with historical linguistic frameworks to model diachronic and synchronic patterns in Latin usage. Key objectives include training domain-specific language models on curated datasets of classical and post-classical Latin; developing algorithms to detect stylistic and grammatical features indicative of period, genre, or regional influence; and applying graph-based methods to analyze intertextual networks in medieval theological works. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of multilingual manuscripts (e.g., Latin-Greek comparative analysis), high-dimensional clustering of syntactic structures, and simulation of dialectal convergence in Italic languages. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital toolkit for Latin philological analysis, quantitative maps of linguistic change across transitional periods (e.g., Late Antiquity to Carolingian Latin), and improved attribution models for anonymous ecclesiastical texts. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic scholarship, this project aims to deepen understanding of Latin’s sociolinguistic dynamics while establishing scalable methods for interdisciplinary textual research. The requested resources are critical to handling memory-intensive tasks, such as training transformer models on non-standard orthographies and optimizing optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines for digitized pre-modern manuscripts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Latin language and literature from its origins through its decline and its current ecclesiastical usage, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, related Italic dialects, Late Roman and Medieval Latin, and modern Church Latin.

abstract: Behavioral neuroscience research increasingly relies on advanced computational methods to address the complexity of neural systems and their role in behavior. This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interactions between neuromodulatory systems (e.g., dopaminergic and serotonergic pathways) and large-scale neural networks underlying decision-making and reward processing. A key challenge lies in modeling these multiscale processes, which span molecular signaling, synaptic plasticity, and network-level oscillations, while integrating empirical data from rodent electrophysiology and calcium imaging. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining biophysically detailed neural network simulations with machine learning-driven analysis of high-dimensional neural datasets. The simulations will incorporate spiking neuron models with modulatory dynamics, calibrated using in vivo recordings, to predict how pharmacological perturbations alter network states and behavioral outcomes. Concurrently, deep learning architectures will be trained to identify latent patterns in neural population activity associated with specific behavioral states. These computationally intensive tasks require high-performance computing (HPC) resources for parallelized parameter optimization, large-scale numerical integration of differential equations, and processing of terabyte-scale imaging datasets. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed memory processing for ensemble modeling, and high-throughput data pipelines. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how neuromodulatory systems reconfigure network dynamics to adaptively regulate behavior, with implications for understanding maladaptive decision-making in addiction and compulsive disorders. The developed computational framework will also provide an open-source toolkit for simulating neuromodulation effects, enabling the broader neuroscience community to test hypotheses about system-level interactions that are experimentally intractable. By bridging molecular, cellular, and systems-level perspectives through computational integration, this work aims to advance mechanistic models of brain-behavior relationships while demonstrating the critical role of HPC in modern neurobiological research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biological bases of behavior and psychological functioning, and their application to experimental and therapeutic research problems. Includes instruction in functional neuroanatomy, neural system development, biochemical neural regulatory mechanisms, neurological biophysics, memory storage and retrieval, physiology of cognition and perception, physiological bases of psychopathology and behavioral disorders, psychopharmacology, comparative psychobiology, molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, and specialized experimental design and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive decision-making in contested logistics environments, a critical challenge in modern military operations. Traditional logistics models struggle to account for dynamic, multi-domain threats—such as cyberattacks, electronic warfare, and autonomous systems—that disrupt supply chains and resource distribution in real time. To address this gap, the research proposes an integrated approach combining agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, and real-time threat simulation to create resilient logistics networks capable of autonomous recalibration under adversarial conditions. The core computational challenge lies in scaling these models to handle the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent interactions across heterogeneous domains (e.g., physical transport, cyber networks, sensor grids) while maintaining operational security constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parallelize scenario testing across thousands of simulated environments, train deep reinforcement learning agents on high-dimensional state spaces, and validate system performance against historically derived conflict datasets. Expected outcomes include a modular simulation platform for evaluating hybrid threat impacts on logistics architectures and actionable metrics for balancing resource efficiency with operational survivability. This work bridges gaps between military strategy, distributed systems optimization, and adversarial machine learning, offering dual-use applications in disaster response and critical infrastructure management. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to advance computational methods for uncertainty-aware decision-making in domains where traditional operations research approaches fail to capture emerging asymmetric threats. Results will inform both tactical planning tools and broader policy frameworks for integrating AI-driven logistics into next-generation command-and-control systems.
cip_title: Military Technology and Applied Sciences Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on applied military science, military operations, intelligence gathering, military technology, and national security. Includes instruction in computer science, engineering, ethics, field training, leadership, military strategy, logistics, management skills, and politics.

abstract: Mammography remains pivotal in early breast cancer detection, yet challenges persist in diagnostic accuracy, variability in image interpretation, and optimization of imaging protocols across diverse patient anatomies. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational tools that enhance mammographic image analysis, quality assurance, and technologist training. The research will address two interconnected problems: (1) the need for robust, AI-driven systems to detect subtle malignancies in mammograms, particularly in dense breast tissue, and (2) the development of virtual simulation environments to improve positioning techniques and equipment calibration. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining deep learning architectures—including 3D convolutional neural networks and vision transformers—with physics-based simulations of X-ray interactions in breast tissue. Training and validation will utilize de-identified mammography datasets comprising over 100,000 annotated images, requiring distributed GPU computing for model optimization. Concurrently, Monte Carlo simulations modeling X-ray scattering and absorption across heterogeneous breast compositions will be parallelized using HPC clusters to generate synthetic data for rare cases and equipment scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source AI toolkit for lesion detection with explainability features tailored for mammographer training, and evidence-based guidelines for personalized imaging parameter selection. By integrating large-scale data analytics with biomechanical modeling, this work aims to reduce diagnostic false-negative rates by an estimated 15-20% in simulated trials while advancing competency-based education in mammography technology. The computational frameworks developed will directly inform curriculum enhancements in mammography positioning and quality control, bridging the gap between radiologic science and precision oncology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered radiographers to become registered mammographers. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology, mammography instrumentation, mammography positioning, principles and procedures of mammography, and quality assurance.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the documentation and analysis of understudied Indigenous languages across the Pacific region, particularly focusing on endangered Papuan and Polynesian languages with limited digital resources. The rapid decline of speaker populations and the scarcity of accessible linguistic data threaten both cultural heritage and scholarly understanding of language evolution in Oceania. Traditional methods of manual analysis are insufficient to handle the complexity and volume of multimodal data—including transcribed oral histories, legacy recordings, and contemporary speech samples—that require large-scale computational processing. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable pipeline for automated phonetic alignment, syntactic parsing, and cross-dialectal comparison. Machine learning models will be trained on existing annotated corpora of related languages (e.g., Māori, Samoan, and Tolai) to predict morphological structures and semantic patterns in lesser-documented languages like Rotokas (Papua New Guinea) and Niuatoputapu (Tonga). Additionally, phylogenetic algorithms will reconstruct historical language relationships across Micronesia and Melanesia, testing hypotheses about prehistoric migration routes. The computational workflow will integrate speech recognition tools adapted to non-European phonologies and GPU-accelerated simulations of language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access digital lexicons, annotated text corpora, and interactive maps visualizing dialectal variation, which will directly support Indigenous communities in language revitalization efforts. By enabling rapid analysis of terabyte-scale audio datasets and complex network modeling of language families, this project aims to advance both computational linguistics methodologies and typological knowledge of Pacific languages, while addressing urgent preservation needs. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive natural language processing tasks and iterative model training across distributed datasets that cannot feasibly be processed on local infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Australian/ Oceanic/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages native to Papua/New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and the island groups of the Pacific Ocean, including, but not limited to, the Papuan languages, the Australian languages, the Micronesian languages, and the Polynesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the detection and analysis of fraud patterns in government contracting and grant systems, a critical component of suspension and debarment investigations. Current investigative workflows rely on manual audits and fragmented data analysis tools, which struggle to scale with the volume and complexity of modern procurement networks. The research problem centers on developing computational methods to identify subtle, systemic fraud indicators across large-scale transactional datasets, interagency records, and unstructured legal documents. By integrating natural language processing (NLP) for contract text analysis, graph-based anomaly detection to map relationships between entities, and machine learning models trained on historical debarment cases, this project aims to automate the identification of high-risk actors and collusive behaviors. The computational approach will involve constructing a federated data architecture to securely process sensitive procurement records, followed by parallelized simulations of fraud scenarios to refine detection algorithms. Key challenges include preserving evidentiary chain-of-custody in computational workflows and addressing jurisdictional variability in legal frameworks through adaptive modeling. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for investigators to prioritize cases, predict emerging fraud typologies, and visualize multi-agency risk networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration across terabyte-scale datasets, reducing the time from initial suspicion to actionable findings. By bridging computational criminology, forensic accounting, and administrative law, this work will establish a framework for data-driven suspension and debarment processes, enhancing public trust in government procurement systems. The project’s open-source algorithms and validation datasets will provide a foundation for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of regulatory enforcement and advanced analytics.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for investigating criminal behavior among government contractors and grantees at different levels. Includes instruction in financial fraud and money-laundering, auditing, computer investigations, legal concepts and applications, procurement law, non-procurement debarment, jurisdiction and lead agency, analytical methods, suspension, parallel proceedings, evidence protection, equitable considerations, investigative techniques, administrative and global solutions, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation diffusion in digital public communication networks and evaluate the efficacy of real-time counter-messaging strategies. As digital platforms become central to public discourse, organizations face unprecedented challenges in mitigating the rapid spread of false narratives while maintaining audience trust. Traditional methods of analyzing communication patterns struggle to account for the scale, velocity, and nonlinear interactions inherent in modern social media ecosystems. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining network analysis, agent-based modeling, and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate misinformation propagation across heterogeneous user communities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale social media datasets, training transformer-based NLP models to detect emerging narratives, and running parallelized simulations of intervention scenarios across diverse demographic parameters. The computational workflow will map temporal network structures using dynamic graph algorithms, quantify sentiment shifts through deep learning classifiers, and test adaptive response strategies through Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying key leverage points for effective message correction, (2) benchmarks for organizational response timelines under varying crisis conditions, and (3) open-source tools enabling communication practitioners to stress-test campaign strategies in simulated misinformation environments. By bridging computational social science with applied communication theory, this research will advance evidence-based frameworks for maintaining informational integrity in complex digital publics. The requested resources directly enable large-scale parallelism for network simulations and GPU-accelerated NLP training that cannot be feasibly conducted through institutional computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in organizational communication, public relations, and advertising, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing sustainable urban design through the integration of dynamic environmental, social, and economic data. Traditional urban planning tools often rely on static models that inadequately capture the complex, interdependent systems shaping cities, such as fluctuating energy demands, evolving material performance under climate stressors, and socio-spatial equity dynamics. Our research addresses this gap by creating a multi-scale simulation platform that models urban systems as adaptive networks, enabling real-time analysis of design interventions across temporal and spatial dimensions. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate pedestrian and vehicular movement, finite element analysis to assess structural and thermal behavior of sustainable materials, and machine learning algorithms to predict long-term environmental impacts under varying climate scenarios. These components will be integrated using a modular architecture, allowing iterative feedback between urban morphology, resource efficiency, and community well-being metrics. HPC resources are critical to manage the high-resolution datasets (e.g., LiDAR-derived 3D city models, IoT-sourced environmental data) and to parallelize simulations evaluating thousands of design permutations. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for urban planners to visualize trade-offs between carbon neutrality goals, construction costs, and social equity indicators in specific neighborhoods. The project also aims to identify design principles that balance adaptive reuse of existing infrastructure with innovative material systems, reducing embodied energy by 15-20% in simulated urban blocks. By bridging computational engineering with participatory design ethics, this work advances a data-driven paradigm for equitable, resilient cities while establishing scalable methodologies for interdisciplinary sustainability research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, physical, and social science in the design of sustainable cities and metropolitan regions. Includes instruction in community revitalization, community economic development, construction technology, design innovation, environmental economics, ethics, justice and politics, sustainable materials, sustainability theory, structural materials, and urbanism.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of the dynamic interplay between cognitive, emotional, and environmental factors in early childhood development through computational modeling of longitudinal behavioral and neuroimaging datasets. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear, time-dependent interactions that characterize developmental trajectories, particularly when analyzing high-dimensional data spanning multiple domains (e.g., attention, memory, social responsiveness) and environmental contexts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multilevel neural network models and agent-based simulations that integrate behavioral, physiological, and caregiver-report data from a 5-year longitudinal cohort (N=1,200 children aged 2–7). The computational framework will model developmental cascades—where small variations in early cognitive or emotional functioning amplify over time through complex interactions with environmental stimuli. Key challenges include optimizing parallelized parameter estimation for stochastic differential equation systems modeling brain-behavior relationships, and conducting large-scale sensitivity analyses across simulated developmental pathways. HPC resources will enable 1) Bayesian inference on hierarchical models with >10⁵ parameters, 2) real-time adaptation of virtual child agents in simulated learning environments, and 3) comparative analysis of 50+ competing developmental theories through pattern matching in neural activation trajectories derived from fMRI datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying critical inflection points in typical and atypical developmental sequences, quantifying resilience thresholds under varying environmental conditions, and generating testable hypotheses about compensatory mechanisms in neurocognitive development. The resulting computational toolkit will be disseminated as open-source software to support replication studies and large-scale collaborative research in developmental science, while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of developmental psychology and computational neuroscience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from infancy through childhood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying stress-induced decision-making deficits through computational modeling of cortico-limbic circuit dynamics. While acute stress is known to impair prefrontal cortex (PFC) function and amplify amygdala activity, the precise spatiotemporal interactions between these regions during value-based decision tasks remain poorly quantified. We propose to develop biophysically detailed neural network models incorporating stress hormone dynamics, synaptic plasticity rules, and region-specific connectivity derived from primate and rodent tract-tracing studies. These models will simulate population-level activity across PFC subregions (e.g., dorsolateral vs. orbitofrontal cortex) and amygdala nuclei under varying stress intensities, using experimentally validated parameters from published electrophysiological and behavioral datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and run large-scale simulations capturing 1) millisecond-scale neural dynamics across >100,000 conductance-based neurons, 2) stochastic neurotransmitter release effects, and 3) long-term potentiation/depression processes over decision-making timescales. Parallelized parameter optimization will employ evolutionary algorithms to identify circuit configurations that reproduce empirical patterns of stress-induced choice biases. Resulting models will be analyzed through dimensionality reduction techniques to extract phase-space representations of decision trajectories. Expected outcomes include a computational taxonomy of stress effects on decision circuits, predictive models of behavioral vulnerability phenotypes, and openly shared simulation libraries for testing pharmacological interventions. This work addresses critical gaps in psychobiological theories of stress cognition while demonstrating how HPC-enabled neurocomputational approaches can advance mechanistic understanding of adaptive behavior. The requested resources will support 15,000+ core-hours for model exploration and 50TB of storage for raw simulation outputs and processed network analysis files.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the biological bases of behavior.

abstract: Microplastic pollution and synthetic polymer waste present critical environmental challenges, yet the mechanisms by which microbial communities interact with these materials across different ecosystems remain poorly understood. This project integrates environmental microbiology, materials science, and computational modeling to investigate biofilm-polymer dynamics in marine and soil environments. We propose a multi-scale computational framework combining molecular dynamics simulations of enzymatic degradation pathways, genome-scale metabolic network models of microbial consortia, and machine learning algorithms trained on environmental metagenomic data. High-performance computing resources will enable the integration of atomistic-scale polymer degradation processes with ecosystem-level biogeochemical fluxes, addressing a critical gap in predicting biodegradation timelines and engineering functional microbial communities. The expected outcomes include predictive models linking polymer chemistry to microbial metabolic functions under varying environmental conditions, validated through collaboration with experimental laboratories. By bridging molecular-scale mechanisms with ecosystem dynamics, this research will advance strategies for targeted bioremediation and inform the design of environmentally responsive materials. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other interdisciplinary challenges at the interface of microbial ecology and materials sustainability. This work addresses a niche not fully captured by traditional disciplines, leveraging HPC to resolve cross-scale interactions critical for mitigating polymer pollution and advancing sustainable materials science.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to model emergent dynamics in urban heat resilience, combining climate science, social vulnerability metrics, and infrastructure systems analysis. Urban heat islands (UHIs) disproportionately impact marginalized communities during extreme heat events, yet existing models inadequately capture the feedback loops between microclimatic conditions, human behavioral adaptation, and aging energy grids. Our research addresses this gap by constructing a multi-layered agent-based model (ABM) coupled with high-resolution atmospheric simulations and real-time socioeconomic datasets. The ABM will simulate individual and institutional decision-making under thermal stress, while nested weather research and forecasting (WRF) models parameterize localized heat flux dynamics at street-canyon scales. Machine learning surrogates will bridge these components, enabling sensitivity analyses of policy interventions such as green infrastructure deployment or emergency cooling center allocation. The computational demands are substantial: ensemble simulations across diverse climate scenarios (RCP 4.5/8.5) require parallelized execution of 10^5 agent interactions per km² at hourly temporal resolution over decadal horizons. We request GPU-accelerated nodes for WRF downscaling and CPU clusters for ABM calibration using Bayesian optimization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital twin platform for cities to stress-test heat mitigation strategies through virtual experimentation. This work advances systems science methodology by formalizing cross-domain couplings between biophysical processes and social inequity drivers, while delivering actionable insights for climate adaptation planning. Successful implementation will demonstrate how computationally intensive, multidisciplinary integration can address pressing societal challenges at the human-environment-technology interface.
cip_definition: A program with a multidisciplinary approach to the analysis and solution of complex problems, requiring a combined approach using data and models from the natural, social, technological, behavioral and life sciences, and other specialized fields.

abstract: The growing complexity of managing geriatric patients with multiple chronic conditions (multimorbidity) presents a critical challenge in clinical care. Current treatment guidelines, often designed for single-disease contexts, fail to account for interactions between comorbidities, polypharmacy risks, and age-related physiological changes, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model disease interactions, predict treatment responses, and optimize personalized care strategies for elderly populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze multi-modal datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), genomic repositories, and longitudinal geriatric studies encompassing over 500,000 patients across acute, ambulatory, and long-term care settings. Machine learning models (ensemble methods, graph neural networks) will identify patterns in multimorbidity progression, while pharmacodynamic simulations will quantify drug-disease and drug-drug interaction risks specific to aging metabolisms. Agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of social determinants and care-setting transitions on health outcomes. The computational scale requires HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale data integration, parallelize millions of treatment scenario simulations, and train complex models with cross-institutional validation. Expected outcomes include: (1) a predictive tool for adverse event risk stratification in elderly patients with ≥3 chronic conditions, (2) optimized treatment algorithms balancing efficacy and safety in polypharmacy contexts, and (3) care-pathway simulations quantifying resource allocation impacts across healthcare settings. By enabling granular analysis of geriatric care dynamics at unprecedented scale, this HPC-driven approach will advance personalized intervention strategies while informing health system planning for aging populations. All workflows will adhere to HIPAA-compliance standards through secure data enclaves and federated learning architectures. The resource request directly supports the program’s mandate to integrate socioeconomic, ethical, and clinical dimensions in aging-related research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the care and management of elderly patients in acute, ambulatory, community and long-term care settings, and the treatment of diseases and conditions associated with the aging process. Includes instruction in ethical and legal issues, behavioral aspects of illness, socioeconomic factors in care and rehabilitation therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the effectiveness of technical teacher training by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize pedagogical strategies for vocational education. Technical educators must adapt to rapidly evolving industries, yet existing training frameworks often lack empirically validated methods for integrating emerging technologies (e.g., AI, advanced manufacturing) into curricula. A critical challenge lies in understanding how different instructional approaches impact student skill acquisition and workforce readiness. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates classroom dynamics and evaluates the efficacy of pedagogical interventions under varied conditions. The project will utilize agent-based modeling (ABM) to represent interactions between instructors, students, and technical tools, incorporating real-world data from partner vocational schools. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in skill development trajectories and predict outcomes of hypothetical teaching strategies. HPC resources are essential to manage the scale and complexity of these simulations, which involve thousands of parallel runs to account for diverse learner profiles, technical domains, and institutional contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model linking instructional methods to student competency gains, (2) actionable insights for tailoring professional development programs to specific technical disciplines, and (3) an open-access toolkit for simulating classroom scenarios in vocational education settings. By enabling data-driven refinements to teacher training paradigms, this work aims to improve the scalability and relevance of technical education, directly supporting workforce demands in high-tech industries. The computational infrastructure requested will support both the ABM simulations and the deep learning analyses required to process multimodal educational data (e.g., assessment scores, sensor data from technical labs, and longitudinal employment metrics).
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational technical education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in high-volume data entry workflows by developing and testing scalable, AI-enhanced microcomputer applications optimized for accuracy and speed. Traditional data entry processes remain labor-intensive and error-prone, particularly when handling unstructured or semi-structured inputs such as scanned documents, audio transcripts, or multi-format spreadsheets. While existing software tools offer basic automation, they lack adaptive learning capabilities to handle diverse data types or dynamic user environments efficiently. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and evaluate machine learning models for context-aware data parsing, error correction, and workflow automation. The research will utilize transformer-based architectures to process text and tabular data, coupled with computer vision models for image-to-text conversion, all integrated within a modular software framework compatible with standard office suites. HPC resources are critical for processing large-scale synthetic and real-world datasets (≥10 TB), including heterogeneous documents and voice recordings, to simulate operational complexity. Parallelized training will optimize hyperparameters for latency-sensitive applications, ensuring usability on standard office hardware after deployment. Expected outcomes include open-source software plugins for popular microcomputer platforms, validated to reduce manual correction time by ≥40% in pilot tests with regional healthcare and logistics partners. The project will also produce benchmarking datasets and performance guidelines for AI-driven data entry tools in resource-constrained environments. By enhancing the interoperability of advanced computational methods with everyday office software, this work aims to democratize access to efficient data management solutions for small businesses and educational institutions.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform basic data and text entry using standard and customized software products. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, personal computer and work station operation, reading draft texts and raw data forms, audio and tape dictation, and various interactive software programs used for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in art historical analysis and conservation through advanced computational methods. The research focuses on two interconnected problems: (1) the large-scale analysis of stylistic and material patterns in understudied medieval manuscript collections, and (2) modeling environmental degradation effects on organic pigments in pre-modern paintings. Current manual methods for comparative stylistic analysis and conservation risk assessment are time-intensive, lack scalability, and struggle to account for multivariate degradation factors. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a hybrid computational workflow. First, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will be trained on multi-spectral imaging data from digitized manuscripts to detect subtle stylistic variations and workshop attributions across 15,000 folios from dispersed collections. Parallelly, molecular dynamics simulations will model the interaction of temperature, humidity, and light exposure on nine organic pigment binders, using density functional theory (DFT) calculations to predict degradation pathways. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabyte-scale cultural heritage datasets, running ensemble simulation models across multiple parameter combinations, and training deep learning architectures with sufficient granularity to capture micro-features in high-resolution conservation imaging. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible attribution framework for manuscript studies, predictive risk matrices for pigment conservation, and open-source tools for material culture analysis. By integrating computational science with art historical expertise, this work aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing cultural heritage at scale while advancing preventive conservation strategies for fragile collections. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impossible on local clusters, particularly for the DFT simulations requiring weeks of sustained computation across multiple nodes.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical development of art as social and intellectual phenomenon, the analysis of works of art, and art conservation. Includes instruction in the theory of art, art history research methods, connoisseurship, the preservation and conservation of works of art, and the study of specific periods, cultures, styles, and themes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of microbial community resilience under host immune pressure, with a focus on pathogenic bacteria in chronic infection contexts. A critical gap in microbiology lies in understanding how polymicrobial interactions and host immunomodulatory signals jointly shape microbial survival strategies, particularly in environments such as chronic wound biofilms or mucosal interfaces. Current experimental models struggle to disentangle the spatial, temporal, and molecular complexity of these systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational-experimental framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with multi-omics datasets. The ABM platform will simulate microbial population dynamics, incorporating parameters for quorum sensing, metabolic cross-feeding, and immune cell chemotaxis derived from in vitro transcriptomic and proteomic profiles of Staphylococcus aureus-Pseudomonas aeruginosa co-cultures exposed to macrophage-secreted cytokines. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across parameter spaces representing varying host immune states (e.g., pro-inflammatory vs. immunosuppressive conditions) and spatial biofilm architectures. Machine learning pipelines will identify emergent interaction patterns predictive of microbial survival, which will be experimentally validated using CRISPR-interference knockdowns of prioritized bacterial genes in flow cell biofilm models. Expected outcomes include a predictive map of host-microbe-microbe interaction nodes that drive chronic infection persistence, with translational potential for precision immunomodulatory therapies. This work directly advances microbial ecology research by bridging population-scale behavior with host interface biology, a task infeasible without large-scale computational modeling. By elucidating how immune pressures select for cooperative microbial traits, the project will provide foundational insights into infection recurrence mechanisms and antimicrobial resistance evolution in complex host environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of unicellular organisms and colonies, and subcellular genetic matter and their ecological interactions with human beings and other life. Includes instruction in microbial genetics, cell biology, cell physiology, virology, pathogenic microbiology, environmental microbiology, immunology, biostatistics, bioinformatics, and laboratory methods including microscopy.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive maintenance strategies for complex mechanical systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiphysics simulations and machine learning (ML) integration. Modern industrial machinery and transportation systems increasingly rely on interconnected mechanical, hydraulic, and electronic components, yet current diagnostic methods struggle to predict cascading failures arising from multiparameter interactions. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to model wear patterns, thermal stresses, and vibration-induced failures in heterogeneous mechanical assemblies under dynamic operational conditions. The proposed approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) for localized stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for lubrication and thermal analysis, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to map component interdependencies. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulation of multiyear operational timelines across diverse environmental and load scenarios, generating training data for ML models that predict failure probabilities at subassembly and system levels. The computational workflow will integrate real-world sensor data from industrial partners, including vibration spectra, thermal imaging, and maintenance records, to validate models against empirical failure modes. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive maintenance toolkit capable of identifying critical failure pathways in electromechanical systems with 85% accuracy or greater, reducing unplanned downtime by an estimated 30-50% in target applications. The resource-intensive nature of multiphysics simulations and the need for hyperparameter optimization across terascale datasets necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Successful implementation will provide a template for integrating HPC-driven simulations into repair technician training programs, bridging the gap between traditional diagnostic practices and data-driven maintenance paradigms. This work directly supports workforce development in emerging smart manufacturing and transportation sectors where predictive repair capabilities are becoming essential.
cip_title: Mechanic and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanic and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Korean linguistic and literary corpora, with a focus on dialectal variation and syntactic evolution. While Korean exhibits rich dialect diversity and complex morphosyntactic structures, large-scale quantitative studies remain limited due to the computational demands of processing heterogeneous textual data spanning historical, regional, and sociolinguistic dimensions. The project will compile and analyze a multi-register corpus comprising 20th–21st century written and transcribed spoken Korean, including understudied regional dialects (e.g., Jeju, Gyeongsang) and web-based communication. Computational workflows will integrate NLP pipelines for automated tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and syntactic parsing optimized for non-standard Korean variants, supplemented by neural architectures (e.g., transformer-based models) to detect diachronic shifts in grammatical patterns and lexical semantics. A key objective is to model dialect convergence/divergence through high-dimensional feature analysis, requiring iterative simulations of language contact scenarios. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC nodes, the project aims to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks inherent in traditional single-threaded approaches. Expected outcomes include the first open-access repository of computationally annotated Korean dialect data, predictive models of syntactic change, and visualization tools mapping dialect boundaries. These resources will advance philological research, inform language preservation efforts, and support applications in NLP systems tailored to regional Korean varieties. The computational framework developed will establish scalable methodologies for linguistic inquiry, bridging humanities scholarship with data-intensive techniques while prioritizing the unique challenges of Korean language analysis.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in autonomous material handling systems within large-scale logistics hubs, such as ports and warehouses, where dynamic environments and scalability challenges limit operational throughput and energy efficiency. Current systems often rely on static algorithms that struggle to adapt to real-time disruptions, variable demand, or complex coordination between robotic agents. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the development of a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The framework will simulate heterogeneous fleets of autonomous vehicles (e.g., drones, forklifts) operating under constraints such as collision avoidance, energy consumption, and task prioritization. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of thousands of agents across diverse scenarios, leveraging GPU-accelerated neural networks to optimize decentralized decision-making policies. Large-scale simulations will integrate real-world data streams from IoT sensors and digital twins of logistics infrastructure to validate model robustness. Key outcomes include a scalable coordination algorithm capable of reducing task completion times by 15–20% under peak demand and cutting energy use by 10–15% through adaptive pathfinding. The computational methodology will also produce a benchmark dataset for multi-agent logistics systems, fostering reproducibility in the field. By advancing the integration of HPC-driven AI in transportation and materials moving, this work aims to set new standards for automation resilience, directly supporting the transition to smart, sustainable supply chains. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source software, enabling industry and academic partners to adapt the framework to diverse operational contexts, from e-commerce distribution centers to emergency resource deployment networks.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in transportation and materials moving, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing multimedia content delivery across heterogeneous digital networks, a critical issue in an era dominated by bandwidth-intensive applications such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and ultra-high-definition streaming. While existing compression algorithms and adaptive bitrate streaming techniques mitigate some latency and quality concerns, their performance degrades under dynamic network conditions and diverse user device capabilities. This research proposes the development of a machine learning-driven framework to model real-time user Quality of Experience (QoE) and dynamically optimize multimedia encoding parameters, network resource allocation, and content prioritization. The computational approach involves training deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models on large-scale datasets of user interaction logs, network telemetry, and perceptual quality metrics. These models will simulate multi-agent environments where competing data streams (e.g., 4K video, interactive 3D assets) must share constrained network resources while maintaining strict QoE thresholds. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized training of DRL agents across thousands of simulated network topologies, (2) real-time inference across distributed edge computing nodes during model validation, and (3) large-scale sentiment analysis of user feedback datasets to refine QoE metrics. Expected outcomes include novel adaptive encoding heuristics, a predictive model for bandwidth allocation in 5G/6G edge networks, and an open-source toolkit for evaluating multimedia delivery systems under constrained conditions. The research directly advances the field of digital communication by providing empirically grounded strategies for managing the computational-intensity of next-generation media formats while informing policy discussions about equitable bandwidth distribution in public infrastructure. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural architecture search and distributed memory clusters for simulating global-scale content delivery networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, critical evaluation, and regulation of new electronic communication technologies using computer applications; and that prepares individuals to function as developers and managers of digital communications media. Includes instruction in computer and telecommunications technologies and processes; design and development of digital communications; marketing and distribution; digital communications regulation, law, and policy; the study of human interaction with, and use of, digital media; and emerging trends and issues.

abstract: This project seeks to address disparities in educational outcomes for culturally and linguistically diverse learners by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop adaptive, data-driven instructional strategies. Current approaches to multicultural education often rely on generalized frameworks that struggle to account for the intersectional identities of students, including language proficiency, cultural background, and socioeconomic factors. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study analyzing large-scale, multilingual datasets from K-12 and adult education programs to identify patterns in student engagement, content accessibility, and learning outcomes across diverse populations. The research will employ machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures, to process natural language data from student-teacher interactions, multilingual assignments, and community feedback. These models will be trained to predict instructional interventions that align with culturally responsive pedagogy, such as personalized resource recommendations and dynamic curriculum adjustments. Agent-based simulations will further model classroom ecosystems under varying pedagogical strategies, enabling the testing of hypothetical scenarios without real-world risks. By integrating these computational approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights into optimizing instructional design for underrepresented groups, particularly emergent multilingual students and learners from non-dominant cultural backgrounds. The outcomes will include open-access predictive tools for educators, a repository of simulated teaching strategies, and evidence-based guidelines for deploying adaptive educational technologies in multicultural settings. This work directly supports the advancement of equitable, scalable solutions in teacher education by translating complex sociocultural dynamics into computationally tractable models, thereby empowering educators to address systemic barriers with precision.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, and implementation of instructional and advising services for culturally diverse learning populations. Includes instruction in cultural diversity, at-risk populations, multilingual and ESL education, program and curriculum design, instructional technology, information resources, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling and communicating with multicultural populations, law and regulations, and applications to specific cultural groups, educational services, and research issues.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize IT support workflows in large-scale organizational environments through advanced computational modeling of help desk ticket resolution patterns. The research addresses inefficiencies in current technical support systems, where manual triage processes and reactive problem-solving often lead to delayed response times and resource misallocation. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop a dynamic simulation framework that analyzes historical support ticket data, real-time system telemetry, and user interaction logs to predict and prioritize emerging technical issues. The computational approach combines natural language processing for ticket classification, graph-based anomaly detection in networked support systems, and reinforcement learning models to simulate optimal technician-task pairing strategies. A novel agent-based model will simulate multi-tier support environments, incorporating variables such as technician expertise, hardware/software failure rates, and user skill levels. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms capable of identifying latent systemic issues (e.g., correlated software crashes across user groups) before they generate support requests, as well as optimized resource allocation templates for common crisis scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for processing petabyte-scale log datasets from partner institutions and running parallel simulations of support infrastructure under varying stress conditions. Results will be validated against live support metrics from three university IT departments, with potential applications in enterprise technical support, educational technology management, and emergency response systems. This interdisciplinary work bridges information systems management, human-computer interaction, and operational logistics, advancing computational methods for service-oriented computing domains while maintaining direct relevance to computer support specialist training and practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical assistance, support, and advice to computer users to help troubleshoot software and hardware problems. Includes instruction in computer concepts, information systems, networking, operating systems, computer hardware, the Internet, software applications, help desk concepts and problem solving, and principles of customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision and efficiency in machining processes by developing computational models for optimizing toolpath planning, material deformation prediction, and thermal management in metal fabrication. Traditional machining workflows often rely on iterative trial-and-error methods to address challenges such as tool wear, workpiece distortion, and heat-induced material degradation, leading to increased costs, material waste, and energy consumption. To overcome these limitations, this research will integrate physics-based simulations with machine learning (ML) to create predictive frameworks for machining parameter optimization. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution and thermal profiles during cutting operations, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate coolant flow and heat dissipation. These simulations will generate datasets to train ML models that correlate machining parameters (e.g., spindle speed, feed rate, tool geometry) with outcomes such as surface finish quality and tool longevity. HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations across diverse materials (e.g., steel, aluminum, titanium) and machining configurations, enabling the exploration of complex parameter spaces impractical for physical testing. The resulting hybrid computational toolkit will be validated against experimental data from CNC milling and turning operations. Anticipated outcomes include open-access predictive models to guide toolpath programming, reduce scrap rates, and minimize energy use in industrial and educational machine shops. By bridging computational modeling with hands-on machining, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of data-driven practices in vocational training programs, equipping future technicians with skills to optimize digital and physical workflows. The project will also contribute benchmarks for integrating HPC-driven analytics into small-scale manufacturing, supporting sustainability goals in technology-driven trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and modify metal parts in support of other manufacturing, repair or design activities, or as an independent business.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced commercial photography workflows, particularly in processing high-resolution imagery, simulating complex lighting environments, and integrating machine learning (ML) for artistic enhancement. As commercial photographers increasingly adopt 8K-resolution imaging, multi-sensor capture systems, and AI-driven post-processing tools, existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to manage the scale, speed, and precision required for iterative creative exploration. The research problem centers on bridging this technical gap to enable novel artistic methodologies while maintaining practical production timelines. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize pipelines for three core applications: (1) parallel rendering of photorealistic 3D product visualizations using physics-based light transport simulations, (2) training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on terabyte-scale image datasets to automate context-aware retouching and style transfer, and (3) real-time fusion of multi-spectral imaging data for augmented reality (AR) previsualization systems. Computational methods will include distributed rendering via ray-tracing engines, GPU-accelerated ML model training with PyTorch, and OpenCL-based image stacking algorithms. Expected outcomes include a framework for scalable hybrid photography (combining physical captures with synthetic elements), quantifiable reductions in processing latency for high-bit-depth composites, and open-source tools to democratize HPC access in photography education. By enabling complex computational workflows previously inaccessible to individual artists and small studios, this research aims to expand the creative possibilities of commercial photography while contributing new benchmarks for computational efficiency in visual arts applications. The project will directly support curriculum development in computational photography and provide case studies for integrating HPC resources into media production pipelines.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for enhancing the protection of cultural and archaeological sites from illicit activities such as looting, vandalism, and unauthorized excavation. Despite advances in remote sensing and site monitoring, law enforcement and heritage professionals lack robust computational tools to dynamically assess site vulnerability, simulate threat scenarios, and prioritize resource allocation across large, geographically dispersed regions. The project addresses this gap by integrating geospatial data, historical crime patterns, environmental variables, and real-time sensor inputs into a machine learning-driven platform capable of forecasting risks to cultural resources. Computational workflows will process multispectral satellite imagery, LiDAR datasets, and anonymized crime reports to train spatial-temporal models that identify high-risk zones and optimize patrol routes. Agent-based modeling will simulate looting networks and site intrusion dynamics under varying enforcement strategies, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will mine textual records from antiquities markets and dark web forums to detect emerging trafficking trends. The HPC environment is critical for handling the scale and complexity of these heterogeneous datasets, enabling parallelized simulations and rapid retraining of deep learning architectures as new data streams become available. Expected outcomes include an open-source risk assessment toolkit for cultural resource managers, validated predictive metrics for site vulnerability, and evidence-based protocols for deploying surveillance technologies in resource-constrained contexts. By bridging computational criminology and heritage conservation, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for proactive cultural resource protection, ultimately reducing response times to threats and preserving irreplaceable archaeological assets for future generations.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement principles and techniques to the protection of cultural resources and the investigation of related crimes. Includes instruction in cultural resources law, archaeological standards of value, site damage assessment, evidence collection, surveillance techniques, investigative techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interplay between cultural identity and intergenerational knowledge transmission among Indigenous communities in the Pacific Rim, with a focus on Polynesia and Micronesia. Current research on cultural resilience in these regions faces challenges in synthesizing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized oral histories, colonial-era archival texts, and contemporary Indigenous language corpora—while adhering to community-driven research protocols. The computational limitations of traditional methods hinder the ability to identify patterns in cultural adaptation, language revitalization, and gendered knowledge systems across temporal and spatial scales. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods framework combining natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of Indigenous narratives, network modeling to map knowledge-sharing pathways, and agent-based simulations to explore hypothetical scenarios of cultural transmission under demographic and environmental pressures. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual textual data (spanning 15+ Pacific languages), running parallelized simulations of social networks, and applying deep learning architectures to detect subtle linguistic markers of cultural hybridity in historical records. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for ethically engaged Pacific Studies scholarship, co-designed with community partners to prioritize data sovereignty. This work aims to advance methodological innovation in digital humanities within area studies by demonstrating how HPC can facilitate non-extractive analysis of cultural datasets, ultimately contributing to Indigenous-led efforts to document and sustain intangible heritage. Results will be disseminated through open-access repositories with restricted cultural sensitivity protocols, peer-reviewed publications, and multimedia resources for Pacific educational institutions.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Australasia and the Pacific Ocean, related island groups and bordering coastal regions, and including pre- and post-colonial migration patterns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of modeling and optimizing real-time multimedia communication networks in dynamic, large-scale digital environments.
