As multimedia platforms evolve, the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of user-generated content—spanning video, audio, and interactive media—exceed the analytical capacity of conventional computational tools. This gap impedes the development of adaptive systems capable of sustaining engagement, ensuring equitable content dissemination, and mitigating misinformation across global platforms. The research problem centers on designing a computational framework to simulate user interactions, content diffusion patterns, and network latency under varying conditions, enabling predictive insights into platform scalability and resilience. The proposed approach integrates agent-based modeling, graph neural networks (GNNs), and real-time data stream processing to analyze multi-modal communication behaviors. Agent-based simulations will replicate diverse user demographics and interaction scenarios, while GNNs will map emergent information cascades and network vulnerabilities. Parallelized processing on HPC clusters will enable the handling of terabyte-scale datasets from social media APIs and streaming services, with iterative model training optimized via GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable toolkit for simulating multimedia platform dynamics under stress scenarios (e.g., viral misinformation spikes), (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing content delivery algorithms to reduce latency and bias, and (3) actionable metrics for policymakers to evaluate platform accountability in content moderation. By advancing computational methods tailored to digital communication research, this project aims to bridge technical and sociotechnical gaps in multimedia system design, fostering more ethical and efficient digital ecosystems. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the necessary scale, speed, and complexity for these simulations, which cannot be replicated on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, critical evaluation, and regulation of new electronic communication technologies using computer applications; and that prepares individuals to function as developers and managers of digital communications media. Includes instruction in computer and telecommunications technologies and processes; design and development of digital communications; marketing and distribution; digital communications regulation, law, and policy; the study of human interaction with, and use of, digital media; and emerging trends and issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research in Chinese dialectology and classical text analysis, addressing critical gaps in scalable methods for processing understudied regional dialects and premodern literary corpora. The research problem centers on the computational complexity of analyzing morphosyntactic and phonological patterns across vast, heterogeneous datasets of spoken and written Chinese, including digitized historical texts (e.g., Tang dynasty poetry, Ming-Qing vernacular novels) and contemporary dialect recordings. Traditional methods struggle to efficiently parse non-standardized orthographies, dialectal variations, and classical grammar structures at scale, limiting insights into language evolution and regional linguistic diversity. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining transformer-based neural language models fine-tuned on classical Chinese corpora with dialectometric algorithms optimized for parallel processing. Key tasks include training bidirectional encoder models on a curated corpus of 10,000+ classical and dialect texts, implementing distributed computing pipelines for phonetic alignment of oral dialect data, and developing graph-based visualization tools to map diachronic syntactic shifts. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of large-scale embeddings, reduce runtime for dialect comparison workflows by 80% compared to local clusters, and support memory-intensive analyses of multi-register texts (e.g., ritual bronzes, woodblock prints). Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for classical Chinese-dialect cross-comparison, a phonologically annotated database of Jiang-Huai Mandarin variants, and quantitative models tracing lexical borrowing between literary and vernacular traditions. This work will directly benefit philological research, inform language preservation initiatives, and provide methodological frameworks for applying HPC resources to under-resourced non-Western languages. Results will be disseminated through the Journal of Chinese Linguistics and an open-source platform for digital humanities scholars.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of China and associated dialects and literature. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing reliance on space-based systems for military operations necessitates advanced strategies to ensure resilience in contested environments. Current satellite constellations, designed for stable orbital regimes, face vulnerabilities from emerging anti-satellite technologies and dynamic threat profiles. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing next-generation space architectures that balance operational capability, survivability, and rapid reconstitution. The research employs high-fidelity simulations integrating orbital mechanics, threat modeling, and network resilience metrics to evaluate constellation configurations under multiple contested scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the team will implement parallelized agent-based models to simulate kinetic and non-kinetic engagement scenarios across diverse orbital regimes, coupled with machine learning techniques to identify optimal reconfiguration patterns and failure mitigation protocols. The computational approach addresses the combinatorial complexity of multi-domain space operations through adaptive mesh refinement for debris field propagation and GPU-accelerated analysis of electromagnetic interference patterns in multi-spectral environments. Expected outcomes include predictive models for constellation degradation thresholds, automated decision-support tools for orbital slot allocation, and novel metrics for quantifying system-level resilience in hybrid warfare contexts. This work will provide foundational insights for designing agile space systems capable of maintaining critical functions during extended conflicts while informing the development of standardized testing protocols for military space asset certification. The resulting framework aims to bridge gaps between traditional aerospace engineering paradigms and modern computational warfare requirements, offering tangible advancements for national security infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and operation of missiles, satellites and other space-based systems for military purposes. Includes instruction in the military applications of space, space technology, aerospace engineering, systems architecture, orbital mechanics, launch and retrieval systems, ground support systems, satellite communications, and space-based sensor systems.

abstract: Climate variability and soil nutrient heterogeneity present significant challenges to optimizing crop productivity and sustainability. Current agronomic models often lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between root architectures, soil biogeochemistry, and microbial communities under spatially variable field conditions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to predict crop responses to nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium (NPK) fertilization strategies across diverse soil types and hydrological regimes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate mechanistic models of root growth and nutrient uptake with machine learning algorithms trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles) from experimental wheat and soybean trials. The computational pipeline will couple 3D soil-plant hydrology simulations with Bayesian optimization to identify nutrient management plans that maximize yield stability while minimizing environmental losses. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of rhizosphere microbial communities to quantify their role in mediating plant stress responses to drought and nutrient limitations. The research will utilize existing field data from 14 USDA-ARS sites while generating new validation datasets through sensor-equipped lysimeters. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of optimal fertilizer regimes for key US cropping systems under projected climate scenarios, (2) identification of root phenotype-microbiome synergies that enhance nutrient use efficiency, and (3) open-source tools for real-time adjustment of precision agriculture recommendations. By resolving submillimeter-scale processes across hectare-scale simulations, this work will advance fundamental understanding of plant-soil feedbacks while directly addressing the urgent need for climate-resilient nutrient management strategies. The requested computing resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale environmental sensor data, running ensemble climate simulations, and training deep neural networks on hyperspectral plant phenotyping imagery. Results will be disseminated through the CyVerse platform to support evidence-based decision-making for farmers and extension specialists.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the chemical, physical, and biological relationships of crops and the soils nurturing them. Includes instruction in the growth and behavior of agricultural crops, the development of new plant varieties, and the scientific management of soils and nutrients for maximum plant nutrition, health, and productivity.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in public resource allocation during large-scale emergencies by developing computational models to simulate and optimize decision-making processes under uncertainty. Municipal governments often face challenges in dynamically distributing limited personnel, equipment, and funding during crises such as natural disasters or public health emergencies, with existing strategies frequently relying on static protocols ill-suited for rapidly evolving conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct agent-based simulations of multi-jurisdictional disaster response scenarios, incorporating real-world variables such as infrastructure damage, population mobility patterns, and interagency coordination constraints. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to historical emergency management datasets to identify critical decision thresholds and predict cascading resource demands across interdependent systems. A key innovation involves integrating game-theoretic frameworks to model competing stakeholder priorities within constitutional and ethical boundaries of public administration. The computational intensity of simultaneously processing geospatial data, running parallelized scenario analyses, and training predictive models necessitates access to advanced GPU clusters and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive resource allocation strategies that balance equity, efficiency, and regulatory compliance. This work directly contributes to public administration scholarship by providing quantitative methods to evaluate policy implementation in complex emergency contexts while advancing computational social science capabilities. Results will be disseminated to state emergency management agencies and incorporated into graduate-level public service curricula, bridging technical innovation with practical governance challenges. The requested computing resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale municipal datasets and real-time simulation of city-scale emergency scenarios previously infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as managers in the executive arm of local, state, and federal government and that focuses on the systematic study of executive organization and management. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing complex industrial systems under uncertainty, with applications in supply chain resilience, production scheduling, and human-in-the-loop decision-making. Industrial and systems engineering problems increasingly involve high-dimensional stochastic optimization, multi-agent interactions, and nonlinear dynamics that challenge conventional solvers. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized simulation-optimization methods combining discrete-event simulation, deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and distributed mixed-integer programming. The computational workflow will integrate stochastic models of system disruptions (e.g., material delays, demand fluctuations) with adaptive control policies trained through GPU-accelerated DRL agents. Key innovations include hybrid CPU-GPU architectures for simultaneous scenario generation and policy evaluation, along with decomposition algorithms to distribute large-scale optimization tasks across multiple nodes. Initial pilot studies on single-node systems demonstrate promising results for mid-sized supply networks but face memory constraints when scaling to enterprise-level systems with >10^5 decision variables. The requested resources will enable systematic benchmarking of distributed optimization strategies against industrial case studies in semiconductor manufacturing and healthcare logistics. Expected outcomes include 1) open-source tools for stochastic industrial system optimization, 2) performance comparisons of HPC-enabled algorithms versus commercial solvers, and 3) generalized insights about compute-time tradeoffs in approximating solutions for NP-hard systems engineering problems. This work directly addresses the growing need for computationally efficient methods to manage interconnected systems in volatile environments, with potential applications ranging from smart factory scheduling to emergency resource allocation. By coupling industrial engineering principles with advanced computing architectures, the project aims to establish new best practices for data-driven systems design under uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Combines instruction in industrial and systems engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing disease resistance and productivity in agricultural and veterinary systems through advanced genomic and computational modeling. Current limitations in analyzing large-scale genomic datasets for plant, livestock, and zoonotic pathogens hinder the identification of genetic markers linked to disease resilience and adaptive traits. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-omics data (genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics) from crops, livestock, and pathogens, integrating machine learning models to predict host-pathogen interactions. The computational workflow will include genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for identifying candidate resistance genes, molecular dynamics simulations to study protein-ligand interactions in veterinary drug development, and agent-based modeling of disease spread in agricultural ecosystems. These methods require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative simulations that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) to train convolutional neural networks on hyperspectral imaging data of plant stress responses, alongside CPU-intensive phylogenetic analyses of pathogen evolution. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel genetic targets for breeding disease-resistant crops, predictive models for emerging livestock pathogens, and optimized antiviral compounds for veterinary applications. By accelerating computational workflows, this research will directly support preparatory programs in agriculture and veterinary sciences by generating open-access datasets and scalable analytical pipelines. The requested HPC allocation will enable processing times reduced by 60-80% compared to current benchmarks, facilitating rapid translation of findings into educational modules and pre-professional training tools. This work aligns with national priorities in food security and sustainable agriculture while avoiding overlap with natural resources conservation-focused initiatives.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in agriculture or veterinary medicine or science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interconnected cultural and linguistic dynamics of Caribbean diasporic communities through large-scale textual and multimedia datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in Caribbean Studies: the lack of computational methodologies to systematically trace how cultural identities—particularly those shaped by gender, ethnicity, and hybrid linguistic practices—are negotiated and preserved across geographically dispersed populations. Current scholarship often relies on qualitative or localized case studies, limiting the capacity to identify transnational patterns in cultural production, such as folklore, oral histories, digital media, and intergenerational storytelling. To address this, the project will employ machine learning (ML) techniques, including multilingual natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal network analysis, to process over 10,000 digitized records from public archives, community-sourced oral histories, and social media spanning English-, French-, Spanish-, and Creole-language contexts. HPC resources will enable the training of custom transformer models to detect semantic and syntactic shifts in Creole languages, map thematic networks in diaspora-centric narratives, and visualize the diffusion of cultural motifs across time and space. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational framework for analyzing Caribbean cultural data, new insights into how digital platforms reshape identity formation in diasporas, and methodological advancements in ethically engaging multilingual, community-generated materials. By integrating computational rigor with cultural theory, this work aims to establish scalable tools for preserving marginalized narratives and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in Caribbean Studies, while adhering to data sovereignty principles prioritized by the region’s communities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the major islands and archipelagoes of the Caribbean Sea and related coastal borderlands, including immigration patterns and Pre-Columbian, colonial, and modern societies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the operational dynamics and scalability challenges of decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) using computational modeling and large-scale data analytics. DAOs represent an emerging organizational paradigm in business, leveraging blockchain technology to enable decentralized decision-making and resource allocation. However, their lack of traditional hierarchical structures introduces unique risks, including governance fragmentation, incentive misalignment, and inefficiencies in collective action. Current research lacks robust quantitative frameworks to analyze these dynamics at scale. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating DAO member interactions, voting mechanisms, and token-based incentive systems. The ABM will integrate real-world blockchain transaction data to parameterize agent behaviors, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of thousands of autonomous agents operating in parallel. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to process on-chain governance data, identifying patterns in proposal success rates and conflict resolution. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated optimization algorithms to iteratively refine governance parameters, testing hypotheses about stability under varying network sizes and incentive structures. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for DAO resilience, a taxonomy of failure modes in decentralized governance, and scalable benchmarks for tokenomic design. This research will contribute to the quantitative study of emergent organizational forms in business, offering methodological advances in modeling decentralized systems. Results will inform the design of DAO frameworks, enhancing their viability as alternatives to traditional corporate structures. The project aligns with the Management Sciences and Quantitative Methods domain by pioneering computational approaches to analyze nontraditional business architectures, bridging gaps between blockchain research, game theory, and organizational theory.
cip_title: Management Sciences and Quantitative Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business quantitative methods and management science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing personalized language learning in under-resourced foreign language classrooms (e.g., Mandarin, Arabic, or Indigenous languages) through the development of AI-driven adaptive instructional tools. Despite growing demand for proficiency in these languages, educators often lack the capacity to tailor instruction to individual learner needs due to limited pedagogical resources and heterogeneous classroom dynamics. The research problem centers on modeling the interplay between learner-specific error patterns, cross-linguistic transfer effects, and instructional intervention efficacy—a task requiring analysis of high-dimensional linguistic and behavioral datasets. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on multimodal data (speech, text, and interaction logs) from diverse language learners, simulating longitudinal proficiency trajectories under varying instructional conditions. Computational methods include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for error annotation, graph neural networks to map interlanguage development patterns, and reinforcement learning frameworks to optimize feedback strategies. By parallelizing model training across multiple GPU nodes, HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of virtual classroom simulations at scales replicating real-world educational contexts. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive models identifying critical intervention windows for specific error types, (2) a framework for generating adaptive curricular materials aligned with learner profiles, and (3) open-source tools to help instructors visualize class-wide learning patterns. This work will directly enhance teacher preparation programs by providing evidence-based strategies for differentiated instruction in low-resource language settings, while advancing computational methodologies for educational applications. The requested resources are essential for handling the project's large-scale data processing needs, which exceed the capacity of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach foreign languages programs at various educational levels, other than French, German or Spanish.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of culinary arts through the development of a predictive modeling framework for optimizing multi-sensory dining experiences. While traditional culinary training emphasizes hands-on experimentation, the integration of computational methods remains underexplored despite its potential to enhance precision, creativity, and sustainability in food preparation. The research problem centers on the lack of systematic tools to analyze complex interactions between ingredient composition, cooking techniques, and sensory perception—variables that are inherently multivariate, nonlinear, and culturally contextual. By employing agent-based modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), this project will simulate heat transfer dynamics in diverse cooking environments, model molecular interactions during ingredient transformations, and correlate these processes with sensory evaluation datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on global culinary databases spanning historical recipes, regional flavor pairings, and nutritional profiles to identify novel gastronomic patterns. The computational workflow will integrate heterogeneous data types, including spectroscopic analyses of ingredient matrices, thermal imaging from cooking processes, and psychometric evaluations of taste perception. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for virtual recipe testing, reducing material waste in culinary experimentation by 30–50%, and a predictive tool for designing allergen-free or nutritionally optimized dishes without compromising sensory quality. This work bridges culinary practice with computational science, establishing a foundation for data-driven gastronomy while addressing gaps in culinary education through simulation-augmented training modules. The requested HPC resources are critical to manage the high-throughput simulations and large-scale data fusion required, enabling real-time parameter optimization across spatially resolved thermal models and multi-modal sensory datasets. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools for culinary institutions, fostering innovation in a field historically reliant on analog methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide professional chef and related cooking services in restaurants and other commercial food establishments.  Includes instruction in recipe and menu planning, preparing and cooking of foods, supervising and training kitchen assistants, the management of food supplies and kitchen resources, aesthetics of food presentation, and familiarity or mastery of a wide variety of cuisines and culinary techniques.

abstract: Histologic processing is foundational to accurate diagnostic and research outcomes, yet protocol optimization remains labor-intensive and variable across tissue types. Current approaches rely heavily on empirical trial-and-error, leading to inefficiencies in reagent use, time, and personnel effort. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model and predict optimal tissue processing protocols using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on identifying quantifiable relationships between tissue characteristics (e.g., lipid content, cellular density), processing parameters (e.g., fixation duration, embedding temperatures), and histologic outcomes (e.g., sectioning artifacts, staining quality). A multi-scale computational approach will integrate machine learning with finite element analysis (FEA) simulations. Tissue-specific datasets, including digitized histology slides and metadata from diverse specimen types, will train neural networks to classify tissue degradation risks and recommend processing adjustments. Concurrently, FEA models will simulate chemical diffusion dynamics during fixation and dehydration phases, optimizing time intervals for heterogeneous tissues. HPC resources are critical to manage the high dimensionality of parameter space (e.g., temperature gradients, pH variability) and the computational intensity of 3D tissue microstructure simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to automate protocol adjustments, reducing processing time by an estimated 20–35% while minimizing artifacts that compromise diagnostic accuracy. The project will also generate open-source algorithms for artifact detection in whole-slide images, enabling real-time quality control. By bridging computational science with histotechnique, this work aims to standardize best practices, enhance training resources for histologic technicians, and improve reproducibility in preclinical and clinical tissue analysis. Successful implementation could extend to developing adaptive protocols for rare or challenging specimens, advancing precision in histopathology workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical components of renewable energy infrastructure, yet optimizing their performance under variable environmental and operational conditions remains a significant challenge. This project seeks to address gaps in predictive modeling of hydroelectric turbine efficiency, sediment transport impacts on infrastructure longevity, and dynamic grid integration strategies. Current models often rely on simplified assumptions that fail to capture the complex fluid-structure interactions, multiphase flow dynamics, and real-time demand-response scenarios inherent to hydroelectric systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable high-fidelity simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven optimization, and large-scale scenario analysis. Key components include three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of turbine arrays under varying flow regimes, coupled with discrete element modeling (DEM) to assess sediment abrasion effects on turbine blades and reservoir structures. Parallelized ML algorithms will integrate historical operational data, weather forecasts, and grid demand patterns to optimize power generation schedules and maintenance cycles. Additionally, agent-based models will evaluate the resilience of hydroelectric systems within hybrid renewable energy networks. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the coupled CFD-DEM simulations and ensemble ML training—necessitate access to HPC resources for memory-intensive workloads and scalable processing. Expected outcomes include validated models for turbine efficiency prediction under sediment-laden flows, adaptive control strategies for grid stability, and a decision-support tool for infrastructure lifecycle management. These results will directly inform hydroelectric plant retrofitting efforts, support the design of next-generation turbines, and enhance the role of hydroelectricity in achieving grid decarbonization targets. By integrating advanced computational methods, this work bridges critical gaps between theoretical hydrodynamics and real-world operational challenges, advancing the engineering technologies underpinning sustainable hydroelectric energy systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in hydroelectric energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning models that enhance personalized educational interventions for students with developmental delays. A critical challenge in special education is designing individualized learning plans that adapt to the heterogeneous cognitive, social, and emotional profiles of these students. Traditional methods for creating such plans often rely on manual, time-intensive assessments and static curricula, which struggle to integrate real-time behavioral data, longitudinal performance metrics, and multimodal inputs (e.g., sensor-based engagement tracking, speech patterns, or fine motor skill evaluations). To address this, we propose a computational approach using deep reinforcement learning and ensemble models to dynamically predict student needs and recommend tailored instructional strategies. The project will train these models on aggregated, de-identified datasets spanning video-recorded classroom interactions, standardized assessment scores, and individualized education program (IEP) outcomes. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these datasets, which include high-dimensional temporal sequences and require parallel processing for hyperparameter optimization and cross-validation. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom scenarios to test intervention efficacy under varying constraints. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for generating adaptive lesson plans and a framework for integrating predictive analytics into teacher training programs. By enabling rapid iteration of data-driven strategies, this work aims to reduce educators’ administrative burdens while improving the precision of interventions for developmentally delayed learners, ultimately advancing equity in special education. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with local school districts and workshops for special education teachers.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals Who are Developmentally Delayed
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who exhibit slow social, physical, cognitive, or emotional growth patterns related to age, or a combination of such factors that affect learning, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identification of developmental delay patterns, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising developmentally delayed students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the scalable manufacturing of gene therapy vectors, a cornerstone of modern biopharmaceutical production. Current limitations in bioreactor efficiency and vector stability hinder the consistent production of high-quality viral vectors, which are essential for gene delivery in therapeutic applications. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to optimize both vector design and bioreactor operation. At the molecular level, coarse-grained MD simulations will elucidate the structural stability of viral capsids under varying physicochemical conditions, identifying key residues for mutagenesis to enhance resilience. Concurrently, CFD models will resolve multiphase transport phenomena within bioreactors, linking shear stress, nutrient gradients, and oxygen transfer to cell viability and vector yield. These molecular and reactor-scale models will inform ML-driven optimization to propose design rules for robust capsid variants and bioreactor operating parameters. The project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the computational load of iterative MD sampling (10⁶–10⁷ atom systems), multiphysics CFD simulations (10⁸ grid cells), and ML training on heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating capsid sequence modifications with stability metrics, validated against experimental collaborator data, and bioreactor design guidelines to maximize volumetric productivity. Success will advance the translation of gene therapies by reducing process development timelines and improving manufacturing reliability, directly addressing unmet needs in personalized medicine and large-scale bioproduction. This work aligns with the chemical engineering principles of transport phenomena, reactor design, and molecular-scale process optimization, while avoiding overlap with excluded engineering disciplines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems at the interface of chemical engineering and biology, with an emphasis at the molecular level, such as biopharmaceutical processes, protein engineering, metabolic engineering, gene therapy, biomaterials, cell and tissue engineering, and drug delivery. Includes instruction in chemical engineering, thermodynamics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, momentum and heat transfer, cellular and molecular biotechnology, process design, and chemical reactor design.

abstract: The study of plant structural adaptations to mechanical stress has remained underexplored due to the lack of integrative computational frameworks bridging cellular architecture, tissue-level mechanics, and environmental interactions. This project seeks to resolve how specialized cell wall compositions in mechanically stressed plants (e.g., wind-prone coastal species) enable energy dissipation and structural resilience, a question unaddressed by traditional biomechanical or physiological approaches. We propose a multiscale computational model integrating molecular dynamics simulations of cellulose-microfibril networks, finite element analysis of tissue deformation under dynamic loads, and machine learning-driven optimization of hypothetical cell wall architectures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to parameterize these models using empirical data from atomic force microscopy, tensile testing, and live-cell imaging of stress-responsive lignocellulosic reconfiguration in *Calystegia soldanella*, a model species exhibiting extreme dune habitat adaptation. Simulations will iteratively predict optimal wall compositions under stochastic wind regimes, validated via 4D X-ray tomography of living shoots under controlled turbulence. The project’s computational workflow—leveraging GPU-accelerated molecular modeling and distributed finite element solvers—requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets to resolve nanoscale-to-macroscale mechanical feedback loops. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identification of evolutionary design principles governing plant mechanical resilience, (2) predictive algorithms for cell wall engineering in bioinspired materials, and (3) open-source tools for simulating plant-environment mechanical interactions. This work establishes a novel paradigm for studying plant adaptation through computational mechanics, advancing both fundamental knowledge and applications in sustainable material design, while circumventing traditional disciplinary boundaries in plant biology research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in botany/plant biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize operational workflows in veterinary offices through advanced simulation and predictive analytics, addressing inefficiencies in resource allocation, staff scheduling, and client-pet service coordination. Veterinary practices face unique challenges due to fluctuating caseloads, emergency interruptions, and the need to balance clinical care with administrative tasks such as compliance tracking, inventory management, and client communication. Traditional management approaches often rely on static protocols ill-suited to dynamic environments, leading to staff burnout, financial waste, and reduced quality of care. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) system simulating clinic operations under variable conditions, integrating real-world data on appointment patterns, staff roles, equipment usage, and regulatory constraints. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run large-scale, parallelized simulations that account for multivariate interactions—such as the cascading effects of emergency cases on routine appointments or supply chain delays on surgical scheduling—while maintaining granular temporal resolution. Machine learning components will analyze historical clinic data to predict demand surges and optimize shift rotations, inventory orders, and equipment maintenance cycles. The simulations will also test hypothetical policy changes, such as revised telehealth integration or fee structures, to evaluate their operational impacts before implementation. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for veterinary administrators to model clinic-specific scenarios, alongside evidence-based guidelines for dynamic resource allocation. By translating computational power into actionable management strategies, this work aims to reduce overhead costs, improve staff well-being, and enhance service capacity in veterinary care—a critical sector underrepresented in computational resource allocation research. The project bridges a gap in non-STEM HPC applications, demonstrating how advanced computing can address niche administrative challenges in specialized professional settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a veterinary office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, veterinary care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of anthropogenic impacts on terrestrial hydrological and biogeochemical cycles through high-resolution, process-based modeling of coupled land surface systems. Rapid land-use changes, including urbanization and intensive agriculture, are altering water quality, sediment transport, and carbon-nitrogen dynamics at watershed scales, but current models lack the spatial granularity and cross-system integration required to predict emergent behaviors. We propose to develop a novel computational framework that couples a hydrologic model (ParFlow-CLM) with a reactive transport biogeochemistry module (PFLOTRAN), informed by satellite remote sensing data (Sentinel-2, Landsat) and geospatial anthropogenic datasets. The integrated model will resolve sub-kilometer heterogeneities in soil properties, vegetation patterns, and human infrastructure across multi-watershed domains in intensively managed landscapes. High-performance computing resources are essential to address the computational demands of (1) parallelized transient simulations across 10^4–10^5 grid cells with daily meteorological forcing over decadal timescales, (2) assimilation of high-dimensional remote sensing products via machine learning-based parameter optimization, and (3) uncertainty quantification through ensemble runs assessing land management scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include the first open-source toolset capable of simulating feedbacks between engineered water systems, contaminant transport (e.g., nitrate, microplastics), and carbon sequestration potential under dynamic land-use pressures. Results will directly inform regional-scale pollution mitigation strategies and sustainable soil management policies. The computational infrastructure will enable scaling to continental domains in future work, addressing critical gaps in predicting how human-modified landscapes respond to climatic and socioeconomic stressors. This work requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning workflows and large-memory nodes to handle geospatial datasets exceeding 50 TB. By integrating cutting-edge computational hydrology with anthropogenic disturbance modeling, the project bridges a critical gap between environmental processes and human system dynamics.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: Aquaculture systems face complex challenges in optimizing production efficiency while minimizing environmental impact, particularly in managing disease outbreaks, feed utilization, and hydrodynamic interactions in dense aquatic farming environments. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model multi-scale interactions between farmed species, pathogens, and environmental conditions in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve spatially explicit agent-based models simulating fish behavior, pathogen transmission dynamics, and water quality parameters at individual and population levels. Coupled hydrodynamic models will assess flow patterns and waste dispersion in tank designs, while machine learning approaches will integrate sensor data to predict optimal feeding schedules under variable temperature and oxygen conditions. The computational workflow requires parallelized simulations across thousands of cores to capture stochastic biological variability and system nonlinearities at operational timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for disease risk mitigation, improved feed conversion ratios, and validated tank design templates that reduce energy use by 15-20% in RAS facilities. By enabling high-resolution modeling of coupled biological-physical processes, this work will advance precision aquaculture strategies that align production goals with environmental sustainability. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will provide the aquaculture industry with evidence-based protocols to address critical bottlenecks in scaling sustainable marine protein production, directly supporting food security priorities. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated neural network training on water quality datasets and large-scale parameter sweeps to optimize intervention thresholds under climate variability scenarios.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to select, culture, propagate, harvest, and market domesticated fish, shellfish, and marine plants, both freshwater and saltwater. Includes instruction in the basic principles of aquatic and marine biology; health and nutrition of aquatic and marine life; design and operation of fish farms, breeding facilities, culture beds, and related enterprises; and related issues of safety, applicable regulations, logistics, and supply.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of personalized hearing rehabilitation strategies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex auditory processing in individuals with hearing loss. Current hearing aid algorithms often struggle to adapt to dynamic acoustic environments, particularly in noisy settings, due to limited computational capacity to simulate real-world auditory scenes and individual neurophysiological variability. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale simulations of auditory pathway responses with machine learning techniques. The research will utilize anatomically detailed cochlear models, cortical auditory processing networks, and patient-specific audiometric data to generate synthetic neural responses to diverse acoustic stimuli. HPC resources are essential to parallelize simulations across thousands of soundscape scenarios (e.g., speech-in-noise, music perception) while accounting for heterogeneous hearing loss profiles. Deep neural networks will be trained on these simulations to predict optimal hearing aid parameter combinations for individual users, with iterative refinement using electroencephalography (EEG) data from human subjects performing auditory tasks. Expected outcomes include a validated computational pipeline for hearing aid personalization, novel biomarkers for auditory processing efficiency, and open-source tools for simulating hearing loss compensation strategies. This work will directly address critical gaps in audiological rehabilitation by enabling data-driven optimization of assistive devices, reducing the trial-and-error approach currently dominating clinical practice. The computational models will also provide foundational insights into neural plasticity following hearing loss, informing future interventions. By utilizing HPC capabilities to bridge biophysical modeling and clinical audiology, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for precision hearing healthcare.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to diagnose and treat hearing loss and other disorders involving the ear, advise patients on means to use their remaining hearing, and select and fit hearing aids and other devices. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of hearing, hearing measurement, auditory pathology, middle and inner ear analysis, rehabilitation therapies and assistive technologies, and pediatric and other special applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Latin textual evolution across historical periods, with a focus on syntactic, morphological, and stylistic shifts from Classical to Medieval and Ecclesiastical Latin. A central challenge in Latin philology is the manual analysis of large, heterogeneous corpora spanning millennia, which limits the scale and reproducibility of studies on linguistic change, textual transmission, and authorial attribution. To address this, we propose developing a scalable computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with domain-specific philological databases. The research will utilize parallelized text processing pipelines to analyze syntax (e.g., ablative absolute usage trends), morphological variation (e.g., verb conjugation regularization), and lexical borrowing across approximately 50,000 Latin texts from the Classical, Late Antique, and Medieval periods. Custom transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to detect stylistic features in understudied ecclesiastical texts, while graph-based algorithms will map intertextual networks in patristic literature. Computational demands include training multilingual embeddings for Latin-Greek comparative analysis, processing high-resolution manuscript images via OCR post-correction, and running iterative simulations of dialectal contact scenarios. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as aligning fragmented manuscript witnesses and optimizing hyperparameters for low-resource Latin NLP models. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for diachronic Latin analysis, a curated dataset of annotated transitional texts, and quantitative insights into the sociolinguistic factors driving Late Latin variability. This work will establish a methodological bridge between computational linguistics and traditional philology, offering scalable solutions to longstanding debates in Latin literary chronology, textual criticism, and the evolution of liturgical Latin.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Latin language and literature from its origins through its decline and its current ecclesiastical usage, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, related Italic dialects, Late Roman and Medieval Latin, and modern Church Latin.

abstract: Global food security is increasingly challenged by climate variability, population growth, and the need for sustainable intensification of agricultural systems. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting region-specific crop performance and optimizing agricultural management strategies across diverse international contexts. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution climate projections, soil health metrics, genomic data for staple crops, and socio-economic indicators—into a unified modeling framework. The computational approach combines mechanistic crop growth simulations, machine learning-driven yield prediction, and agent-based modeling to evaluate interactions between biophysical constraints, policy scenarios, and farmer decision-making. Key objectives include (1) simulating climate adaptation pathways for maize and wheat systems in South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Latin America under multiple emission scenarios; (2) identifying genomic markers associated with drought tolerance through whole-genome sequencing analysis of 10,000+ crop accessions; and (3) optimizing irrigation and fertilizer allocation strategies using spatially explicit optimization algorithms. The scale of genomic data processing, the complexity of multi-model coupling, and the need for real-time parameter calibration across terabyte-scale geospatial datasets necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized computation, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-memory node utilization. Expected outcomes include open-access predictive tools for climate-resilient crop selection, evidence-based policy briefs on input-use efficiency, and a global database linking genotype-environment-management interactions. This work directly supports the International Agriculture program’s mission by advancing computational methods to decode cross-regional agricultural challenges, thereby informing equitable strategies for food production and resource allocation in low- and middle-income countries.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of agricultural management and scientific principles to the problems of global food production and distribution, and to the study of the agricultural systems of other countries. Includes instruction in agricultural economics; comparative agricultural systems; international agribusiness and law; third-world development studies and economic development; and global applications of climate, soil, water resources, ecological and environmental studies, and animal and plant sciences.

abstract: The rapid evolution of wireless communication systems demands advanced computational methods to address the complexity of next-generation networks. Current challenges include optimizing spectral efficiency, mitigating interference in dense deployments, and ensuring ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) for emerging applications like IoT and smart infrastructure. This project seeks to develop scalable algorithms for dynamic resource allocation and interference management in heterogeneous 5G/6G networks, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale scenarios with thousands of nodes. Traditional simulations fail to capture real-time network dynamics at this scale, necessitating parallelized frameworks to evaluate adaptive beamforming, multi-user MIMO configurations, and distributed edge computing architectures. The computational approach integrates machine learning models trained on synthetic channel data—generated via ray-tracing simulations—to predict optimal power allocation and scheduling strategies under varying traffic loads. Key methods include GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for statistical network analysis, distributed optimization solvers for non-convex interference minimization problems, and graph neural networks to model spatial-temporal correlations in user mobility patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid prototyping of hybrid digital-analog precoding schemes and federated learning protocols for privacy-aware network optimization. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms to enhance network capacity by 20-30% in high-density urban environments, validated through emulation frameworks that replicate 3GPP compliance tests. This work will provide open-source tools for channel modeling and resource management, directly contributing to industry standards for 6G coexistence mechanisms. By addressing computational bottlenecks in network design, the project aims to bridge gaps between theoretical performance bounds and practical deployment constraints, offering actionable insights for telecom stakeholders and academic researchers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of communications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in communications networks and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for next-generation wireless communication networks, addressing the challenge of dynamically balancing spectral efficiency, energy consumption, and latency in dense urban environments. Existing resource allocation models struggle to adapt to real-time network conditions, particularly in scenarios with high user mobility, interference, and heterogeneous device requirements. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to model network topologies and optimize resource distribution. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning architectures on large-scale network simulations generated via stochastic geometry and ray-tracing propagation models. Key computational tasks include parallel Monte Carlo simulations of 5G/6G channel access protocols, distributed training of GNNs across multiple GPU nodes, and real-time optimization benchmarking under varying traffic loads. The proposed methods will be validated against standardized 3GPP scenarios and open-source network datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel MORL framework for adaptive subchannel/power allocation in non-stationary environments, (2) quantitative comparisons of computational efficiency between conventional optimization and machine learning-driven approaches, and (3) open-source simulation tools for massive MIMO network prototyping. This work directly supports communications engineering research by enabling complex trade-off analyses that exceed the capabilities of single-node computing environments, particularly in parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 dimensions. Successful implementation will provide methodological advances for network optimization under uncertainty while informing practical deployments of energy-aware communication systems. The requested computing resources are essential for handling memory-intensive network graph operations and achieving statistically significant results across diverse urban configurations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of communications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in communications networks and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive, AI-driven cyber deception frameworks for military electronic warfare operations. Modern cyber-physical battlefields require dynamic, real-time responses to adversarial tactics that exploit vulnerabilities in networked command-and-control systems. However, existing static defense architectures struggle to counter machine learning (ML)-enhanced cyber attacks that evolve during multi-domain operations. The research problem centers on creating computationally intensive simulations of adversarial ML scenarios to train deception-based defense systems capable of anticipating and misdirecting adaptive threats. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale cyber terrain environments, simulate attack vectors across wireless and satellite networks, and optimize reinforcement learning agents for automated response generation. Key computational methods include parallelized Monte Carlo Tree Search for threat path prediction, GPU-accelerated neural network ensembles to emulate red-team tactics, and evolutionary algorithms to stress-test defense protocols under resource constraints. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated library of synthetic adversarial behaviors reflecting nation-state cyber warfare capabilities, (2) quantifiable performance metrics for deception efficacy in contested electromagnetic spectra, and (3) open-source tools for evaluating system resilience against coordinated electronic and cyber-kinetic attacks. This work directly addresses the DoD's priority on maintaining decision superiority in degraded electronic environments while avoiding vendor-locked solutions. The HPC-enabled scale of simulations—encompassing >10^6 node networks with embedded physics-based RF interference models—provides unprecedented fidelity for testing acquisition strategies targeting next-generation cyber warfare systems. Results will inform joint all-domain command system requirements and ethical AI deployment guidelines for autonomous electronic countermeasures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cognitive processing constraints and the structural evolution of morphosyntactic systems across diverse languages, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model diachronic language change at scale. While historical linguistics has traditionally relied on comparative methods and philological data, computational limitations have hindered systematic exploration of how cognitive biases—such as memory limitations, parsing efficiency, and analogical generalization—interact with sociocommunicative pressures to shape grammatical complexity over centuries. The research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models that simulate language transmission across generations under varying cognitive and social parameters. Using parallelized simulations on HPC clusters, we will quantify the emergence and stabilization of morphological paradigms, argument marking systems, and syntactic alignment patterns in artificial language populations. Neural networks trained on simulation outputs will identify critical thresholds in processing load that predict typological shifts, while graph-theoretic analyses will map pathways of change in feature space. The computational framework integrates psycholinguistic experimental data on human pattern generalization with cross-linguistic typological databases, enabling validation against attested historical developments. Expected outcomes include a probabilistic model of structural convergence/divergence in language families, identification of universal versus contact-driven change mechanisms, and methodological innovations for scaling cognitive-evolutionary linguistics beyond isolated case studies. By bridging computational neuroscience, complex systems theory, and linguistic typology, this work aims to advance predictive theories of language change while providing open-source tools for simulating cultural evolution processes. The HPC resources requested are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of multidimensional parameter spaces, enabling simulations across >10^6 agent generations with real-world population dynamics—a computational load infeasible on standard infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language, language development, and relationships among languages and language groups from a humanistic and/or scientific perspective. Includes instruction in subjects such as psycholinguistics, behavioral linguistics, language acquisition, sociolinguistics, mathematical and computational linguistics, grammatical theory and theoretical linguistics, philosophical linguistics, philology and historical linguistics, comparative linguistics, phonetics, phonemics, dialectology, semantics, functional grammar and linguistics, language typology, lexicography, morphology and syntax, orthography, stylistics, structuralism, rhetoric, and applications to artificial intelligence.

abstract: The increasing complexity of neuromuscular rehabilitation necessitates advanced tools to optimize patient-specific interventions, particularly for post-stroke motor recovery. Current clinical practices rely on generalized therapeutic protocols, which often fail to account for individual variability in neural plasticity, biomechanical constraints, and physiological adaptation. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework integrating neuromuscular dynamics, biomechanical simulations, and machine learning to predict personalized rehabilitation outcomes. The research aims to address the critical gap in dynamically modeling how patient-specific factors—such as corticospinal tract integrity, muscle synergies, and joint kinematics—interact to influence functional recovery. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization across heterogeneous datasets, including motion capture, electromyography, diffusion tensor imaging, and clinical assessments. Multiscale simulations will couple finite element models of musculoskeletal systems with reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine therapeutic exercise parameters (e.g., resistance, range-of-motion targets) in silico. Concurrently, graph neural networks will analyze longitudinal patient data to identify predictive biomarkers of recovery trajectories. The computational pipeline will be validated against a longitudinal cohort of 200 stroke survivors undergoing physical therapy. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source platform for simulating rehabilitation scenarios, actionable biomarkers to guide clinical decision-making, and optimized exercise prescriptions tailored to individual neuro-mechanical profiles. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation science, offering a paradigm shift from trial-and-error therapeutic design to mechanistically informed precision physical therapy. The project’s computational demands—including parallelized Monte Carlo simulations, real-time optimization of high-dimensional models, and terabyte-scale multimodal data integration—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically relevant throughput and accuracy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate, examine, diagnose, and alleviate physical functional impairments and limitations caused by injury or disease through the design and implementation of therapeutic interventions to promote fitness and health. Includes instruction in anatomy, behavioral sciences, biology, biomechanics, biophysical agents, care plan development and documentation, cellular histology, clinical evaluation and measurement, clinical reasoning, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, professional standards and ethics, rehabilitation psychology, and therapeutic exercise.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analysis of Sanskrit and Classical Indo-Aryan language corpora, addressing challenges in processing complex morphological structures and tracing diachronic linguistic developments. Traditional methods for analyzing these texts are hindered by the vast volume of sources and the intricate grammatical rules governing Sanskrit and its related languages, such as Pali and Prakrits. The research will employ parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored to ancient Indo-Aryan languages, including tokenization of sandhi compounds, morphological parsing using finite-state transducers, and probabilistic modeling of syntactic constructions. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to process multi-gigabyte text corpora spanning Vedic to post-classical Sanskrit, enabling comparative analysis of lexical, phonological, and grammatical features across historical periods and related dialects. Key outputs will include an open-access annotated corpus with machine-readable linguistic annotations, quantitative models of language change in the Indo-Aryan family, and optimized NLP tools for classical South Asian languages. The computational resources will facilitate previously intractable analyses, such as network modeling of intertextual relationships in commentarial traditions and phylogenetic analysis of Prakrit dialect variation. These outcomes will provide novel methodologies for digital philology in Indology while offering substantive contributions to historical linguistics through data-driven perspectives on Sanskrit's linguistic ecology and its development within the broader Indo-European context.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Sanskrit and Classical Indian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Sanskrit and related ancient and classical Indo-Aryan languages. Includes instruction in Vedic and Classical Sanskrit, Pali and other Prakrits, and the historical development of Indo-Aryan languages and their relation to Indo-European languages such as Greek, Latin and the Baltic languages.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in student counseling interventions by analyzing complex, multi-modal datasets to identify patterns in student mental health outcomes. Student counseling services face growing demand due to escalating mental health challenges among diverse student populations, yet evidence-based frameworks for personalizing interventions remain underdeveloped. Traditional statistical methods struggle to integrate heterogeneous data sources—such as anonymized session transcripts, longitudinal well-being surveys, and behavioral engagement metrics—while preserving privacy and scalability. This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model dynamic interactions between counseling strategies, student characteristics, and institutional support systems. Computational workflows will be optimized to process sensitive text data securely, extract latent psychosocial features, and simulate intervention pathways across hypothetical student cohorts. By parallelizing model training on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks associated with high-dimensional datasets spanning multiple universities. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating counseling intervention efficacy under varying demographic and resource constraints, as well as actionable insights into how institutional policies and counselor training programs can adapt to systemic stressors. This work bridges gaps in education research by providing computational methods to study counseling processes at scale, with potential applications in developing adaptive support systems that reduce disparities in student mental health outcomes. Results will be disseminated through counseling education networks to inform data-driven practices in student personnel services.
cip_title: Student Counseling and Personnel Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in student counseling and personnel services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the role of genetic and biomechanical factors in cellular mechanotransduction anomalies linked to idiopathic vascular malformations—a poorly understood class of congenital disorders affecting blood vessel development. Despite clinical recognition of these conditions, their molecular etiology and biomechanical drivers remain elusive, limiting diagnostic precision and therapeutic innovation. We propose an integrative computational framework combining multi-omics data analysis with fluid-structure interaction (FSI) modeling to decode how specific somatic mutations disrupt endothelial cell signaling under hemodynamic forces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable three synergistic aims: (1) large-scale comparative genomics to identify mutation clusters in mechanosensitive pathways using whole-exome sequencing data from patient cohorts; (2) GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulations of mutated shear stress sensors (e.g., PIEZO1, VE-cadherin complexes); and (3) multiscale FSI models simulating hemodynamic microenvironments in malformed vasculature, incorporating patient-derived endothelial cell mechanical properties. The computational pipeline will integrate machine learning to predict genotype-biomechanical phenotype relationships across spatial scales. This interdisciplinary approach bridges developmental biology, clinical genetics, and computational mechanics—a niche not systematically explored in existing literature. Expected outcomes include a predictive atlas linking genetic variants to endothelial mechanoresponse aberrations, validated against in vitro microfluidic assays. By elucidating how somatic mutations interact with local hemodynamics to drive malformation pathogenesis, this work could inform personalized risk assessment tools and mechanotherapy strategies. The project directly aligns with pre-medical training objectives by exemplifying translational applications of computational modeling in solving clinically relevant biomedical problems while requiring HPC capabilities for handling terabyte-scale datasets and complex multiphysics simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in medicine, osteopathic medicine, or podiatric medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of host-microbe-environment interactions in chronic inflammatory diseases, integrating organismal physiology, environmental exposure data, and microbial community behavior. Chronic inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) involve complex, nonlinear feedback between host immune responses, spatially structured microbial ecosystems, and environmental triggers, yet most models oversimplify these interactions as isolated systems. We propose a multi-scale computational framework to simulate how microenvironmental gradients (e.g., oxygen, pH), host tissue remodeling, and microbial metabolic networks collectively drive disease progression or resolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatially explicit agent-based models of mucosal microhabitats, coupled with dynamical systems modeling of host immune signaling. The agent-based component will simulate 3D microbial biogeography and metabolite diffusion at micrometer resolution across clinically derived gut tissue geometries, while ordinary differential equation networks will capture immune cell recruitment and cytokine cascades. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in microenvironmental parameters that predict microbial community destabilization and characterizing compensatory mechanisms between epithelial repair pathways and dysbiosis. This work will advance integrative disease models by bridging tissue-scale biophysical constraints with population-level microbiome ecology, providing a platform to test hypotheses about dietary, probiotic, or pharmacological interventions. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations for parameter space exploration, requiring ~50,000 core-hours to achieve statistical robustness across biologically variable scenarios. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and collaborations with experimental labs validating predicted interaction motifs in murine IBD models. By unifying disparate scales of biological organization, this project aims to redefine therapeutic strategies for complex inflammatory disorders through computationally driven mechanistic insight.
cip_title: Integrative/ Interdisciplinary Biology, Biosciences, and Biomedical Sciences
cip_definition: A program that crosses multiple specializations within the biological and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in general biological research and variety of specializations.

abstract: Ambulatory care faces increasing demands to optimize patient outcomes while managing complex, heterogeneous populations outside traditional hospital settings. A critical challenge lies in predicting adverse events and personalizing interventions using high-dimensional clinical, behavioral, and multi-omics data. This project proposes to develop machine learning models that integrate electronic health records (EHR), wearable device metrics, and genomic data to forecast hospitalization risk and treatment response in ambulatory patients with chronic cardiometabolic conditions. The research addresses a key gap in scalable predictive analytics for decentralized care settings, where dynamic risk stratification is limited by computational constraints in processing temporally dense, multimodal datasets. We will employ federated learning frameworks to preserve data privacy across institutions while training deep neural networks and gradient-boosted ensemble models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for distributed model training across 200,000+ patient records, genomic variant analysis, and real-time simulation of intervention scenarios. Computational workflows will include NLP processing of clinical notes, time-series analysis of continuous biosensor data, and Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning.
