The project will validate models using retrospective data from three health systems, assessing performance metrics (AUC-ROC, calibration) against existing clinical risk scores. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive framework for ambulatory risk stratification and evidence-based thresholds for deploying targeted interventions. By enabling rapid analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, HPC resources will directly support translational objectives: identifying high-risk subgroups for care pathway adjustments, reducing unnecessary hospitalizations, and informing resource allocation in value-based care models. This work aims to establish computational infrastructure for learning health systems in ambulatory medicine, with preliminary models demonstrating potential to reduce 30-day readmission rates by 15-20% in validation cohorts.
cip_definition: Research focused on Ambulatory Care

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and the urgent need for personalized therapeutic strategies demand advanced computational tools to overcome limitations in traditional experimental approaches. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the development of precision pharmaceuticals by investigating drug-target interactions, pharmacokinetic properties, and genetic factors influencing drug efficacy and toxicity. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) employing large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model atomic-level interactions between candidate drug molecules and dynamic protein targets, including those associated with antimicrobial resistance and cancer, and (2) developing machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-omics datasets to predict patient-specific drug responses and adverse reactions. The MD simulations will utilize enhanced sampling techniques to capture rare conformational changes in target proteins, while the ML framework will integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and pharmacogenomic data to identify biomarkers of therapeutic success. Additionally, virtual screening of compound libraries against dynamically refined protein structures will prioritize novel drug candidates for experimental validation. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized simulation tasks and distributed memory systems for processing high-dimensional biological data. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimized lead compounds with improved binding kinetics, predictive models for personalized dosing regimens, and mechanistic insights into drug resistance pathways. By reducing reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, this research will lower development costs and timelines while advancing precision pharmacy practices. The proposed work directly addresses critical challenges in pharmaceutical care, including treatment individualization and antimicrobial stewardship, with potential translational impacts on patient outcomes and public health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent or employed practice of preparing and dispensing drugs and medications in consultation with prescribing physicians and other health care professionals, and for managing pharmacy practices and counseling patients. Includes instruction in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmacy practice, pharmacy administration, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing mineral extraction and processing systems through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations of traditional empirical methods. The research focuses on developing multiscale, multiphysics simulations to model complex interactions in ore fragmentation, mineral liberation, and slurry transport—processes central to efficient resource recovery. Current methods struggle to integrate micro-scale mineralogical heterogeneity with macro-scale operational parameters, leading to inefficiencies in energy use, material recovery, and waste management. By implementing coupled discrete element method (DEM) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) frameworks, we aim to resolve particle-scale breakage dynamics and fluid-particle interactions in processing equipment such as crushers, mills, and flotation cells. These simulations will be validated against experimental data from sensor-equipped pilot-scale systems. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained on HPC-processed geospatial and operational datasets to predict ore variability and optimize real-time decision-making in mine planning. The computational demands of these tasks—including high-resolution 3D meshing, parallelized solver algorithms, and large-scale parameter space exploration—necessitate access to HPC resources for feasible execution. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing energy consumption in comminution, improving mineral recovery rates by 10–15%, and reducing tailings waste through optimized separation thresholds. The project will provide open-source simulation modules to advance collaborative research in sustainable mining practices, directly supporting industry priorities in decarbonization and circular resource economies. By bridging computational innovation with mineral engineering fundamentals, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven, environmentally conscious mineral resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of mineral extraction, processing and refining systems, including open pit and shaft mines, prospecting and site analysis equipment and instruments, environmental and safety systems, mine equipment and facilities, mineral processing and refining methods and systems, and logistics and communications systems.

abstract: The increasing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) presents a critical challenge to global health, particularly in treating bacterial infections such as tuberculosis and hospital-acquired pathogens. Current clinical strategies often rely on generalized treatment guidelines, which fail to account for rapidly evolving resistance patterns and region-specific pathogen genomics. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale bacterial genomic datasets and predict context-specific resistance mechanisms. The research will integrate whole-genome sequencing data from clinical isolates across sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia with regional epidemiological metadata, including antibiotic usage rates and healthcare infrastructure variables. Using phylogenetic inference, machine learning models, and agent-based simulations, we will identify genetic markers associated with emerging resistance, model transmission dynamics, and optimize treatment protocols under resource-constrained scenarios. Computational workflows will employ containerized pipelines for reproducibility, with iterative model training on GPU clusters to handle high-dimensional data (e.g., 100,000+ genomes paired with clinical outcomes). Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to guide antibiotic selection based on local resistance trends, (2) dynamic maps of AMR risk stratified by pathogen lineage and geographic location, and (3) open-access tools for real-time genomic surveillance in LMIC clinical settings. By enabling data-driven treatment decisions, this work aims to reduce AMR-related morbidity and mortality while preserving the efficacy of existing antibiotics. The scale of genomic and epidemiological data integration necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory simulations, and efficient storage of multi-terabyte datasets—requirements unmet by local institutional infrastructure. Successful implementation will provide a template for translating computational genomics into actionable clinical strategies for global health equity.
cip_definition: Research focused on Global Health

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in optimizing microbial cell factories for sustainable bioproduction. Despite advances in synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, inefficiencies in pathway regulation, substrate utilization, and product toxicity often limit the yield and scalability of engineered microbial systems. Traditional experimental approaches to troubleshoot these bottlenecks are time-intensive and costly, particularly when exploring complex genotype-phenotype relationships or screening vast combinatorial libraries of genetic modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated computational pipeline combining genome-scale metabolic modeling (GEM), machine learning (ML)-guided strain optimization, and atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. GEMs of target organisms (e.g., Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae) will be refined using constraint-based algorithms (e.g., flux balance analysis) to predict metabolic fluxes under varying genetic and environmental conditions. Parallelized ML models will iteratively identify optimal gene knockout/overexpression candidates and regulatory circuit designs by training on multi-omics datasets and prior experimental results. For critical enzymatic bottlenecks, MD simulations will probe structural dynamics and substrate-binding mechanisms to inform rational enzyme engineering. The computational workflow demands HPC capabilities to manage large-scale parameter sweeps, stochastic simulations of genetic circuits, and energy calculations for protein-ligand interactions. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-efficiency strain designs for producing biofuels, therapeutic proteins, and platform chemicals, validated through subsequent wet-lab experiments. This work will establish a scalable framework for in silico bioprocess optimization, reducing experimental trial-and-error while advancing fundamental understanding of microbial metabolism. The requested resources will directly support the development of open-source tools for the biotechnology community, enabling faster translation of lab-scale discoveries to industrial applications in renewable energy and biomanufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of biologists and biotechnologists in research, industrial, and government settings. Includes instruction in fermentation technology, cell culturing, protein purification, biologic synthesis, assaying and testing, quality control, industrial microbiology, bioprocessing, chromatography and bioseparation, genetic technology, laboratory and hazardous materials safety, and computer applications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive computational framework to optimize dynamic facility management in hybrid work environments, integrating real-time spatial, occupancy, and environmental data with organizational behavioral models. Traditional facility planning relies on static spatial metrics and historical trends, but post-pandemic workplace dynamics require granular, responsive strategies to balance fluctuating occupancy patterns, resource allocation, and employee well-being. The research addresses this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate complex interactions between physical workspace configurations, IoT-derived sensor data, and human behavioral parameters. Agent-based modeling will simulate occupancy flows under variable hybrid schedules, while machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized sensor data (motion, air quality, noise) will predict space utilization inefficiencies. Concurrently, graph-based network analysis will map interpersonal collaboration patterns to inform workspace zoning. The computational pipeline will synthesize these datasets through iterative optimization cycles, proposing spatially adaptive layouts that minimize energy use and maximize ergonomic outcomes. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to enterprise-level facilities, processing high-frequency IoT streams, and training predictive models with sufficient temporal resolution to capture emergent workplace dynamics. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for facility managers to evaluate design interventions in silico, reducing the trial-and-error costs of reconfiguring physical spaces. By bridging computational modeling with human-centric design principles, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for responsive facility management that aligns operational efficiency with evolving organizational needs. The project will also contribute methodological insights into applying HPC to non-traditional domains, demonstrating how facility planning can serve as a testbed for interdisciplinary computational research at the intersection of environmental design, behavioral analytics, and operational logistics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational framework to optimize the design of advanced composite materials for high-performance manufacturing applications. A critical challenge in materials engineering lies in predicting how atomic-scale interactions and microstructural features collectively influence the macroscopic mechanical and thermal properties of composite systems, particularly those involving novel bonding interfaces or hybrid material phases. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and struggle to capture the coupled effects of processing variables, defect dynamics, and interfacial phenomena across spatial and temporal scales. We propose an integrated computational strategy combining density functional theory (DFT) simulations, phase-field modeling, and finite element analysis (FEA) to establish structure-property relationships in metal-ceramic and polymer-matrix composites. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of interfacial adhesion mechanisms, parallelized phase-field computations of microstructure evolution during processing, and stochastic FEA simulations assessing mechanical performance under operational loads. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify optimal processing parameters and material combinations from the multi-terabyte simulation datasets generated. This approach addresses critical gaps in predicting failure initiation at bonded interfaces and quantifying the effects of residual stresses from manufacturing. Successful implementation will yield validated predictive models for designing composites with tailored strength-to-weight ratios, thermal stability, and damage tolerance, directly supporting applications in sustainable infrastructure and energy-efficient manufacturing systems. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the memory-intensive quantum mechanical calculations, multi-physics coupling across scales, and data-driven optimization workflows inherent to this research. Outcomes will advance computational materials design methodologies while providing open-access datasets to accelerate innovation in industrial materials development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and materials science principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and related processes used in manufacturing in a wide variety of settings; the synthesis of new industrial materials, including marrying and bonding composites; analysis of materials requirements and specifications; and related problems of system design dependent on materials factors.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing maintenance and safety protocols for aging missile and space systems infrastructure through advanced computational modeling. While traditional engineering approaches focus on hardware performance, this research targets operational frameworks governing inspection, repair, and lifecycle management—a critical but understudied domain intersecting systems engineering, logistics, and risk analysis. The central problem lies in the lack of adaptive decision-support tools capable of processing multi-dimensional data (equipment telemetry, maintenance histories, environmental factors) to predict failure cascades in complex, interdependent systems. To overcome this, we propose developing a high-fidelity digital twin environment leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) and discrete-event simulation. The computational approach will integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning decades of operational records with real-time sensor inputs, modeling system degradation patterns and human-process interactions at unprecedented scale. Key innovations include hybrid agent-based models that capture both technical subsystem behaviors and organizational decision-making workflows, enabling scenario testing for rare-event risks in nuclear-capable systems. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: 1) training GNNs on petabyte-scale historical maintenance logs, 2) running massively parallel simulations of alternative maintenance strategies under 10,000+ parameter combinations, and 3) real-time optimization of inspection schedules across global infrastructure networks via quantum-inspired annealing algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predictive maintenance prioritization that reduces unplanned downtime by ≥30% in modeled scenarios, along with novel metrics for quantifying systemic risk propagation in aging ordnance systems. This work will establish computational foundations for next-generation sustainment protocols in national security infrastructure while advancing methodological integration of operations research and AI in safety-critical domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of rocket systems, guided missiles, and space vehicles as well as related systems. Includes instruction in engineering mechanics, engineering graphics, materials and processes, electronics, propellant and guidance systems, control systems, fluid power, nuclear and conventional weapons systems, hazardous materials, non-destructive inspection and testing, quality assurance, safety procedures and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of simulating and optimizing civil infrastructure designs in complex geological environments, a critical challenge in civil drafting and engineering CAD/CADD workflows. Current software tools struggle to efficiently model large-scale infrastructure systems—such as water distribution networks or transportation corridors—while integrating high-resolution geological, hydrological, and seismic data. These limitations hinder the ability to predict system resilience under dynamic stressors like earthquakes or climate-induced soil instability. To overcome this, we propose developing a scalable computational framework using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multi-physics simulations that couple finite element analysis, geospatial data processing, and automated drafting parameter optimization. The project will leverage parallelized algorithms to distribute tasks across HPC nodes, accelerating iterative design testing and sensitivity analyses. Key computational components include GPU-accelerated rendering for 3D geological mapping, machine learning models to predict material stress thresholds from historical survey data, and parametric scripting to automate CADD blueprint revisions. By integrating these methods, the framework will reduce simulation runtime for large infrastructure projects from weeks to days while improving precision in risk assessment. Outcomes will include open-source CADD workflow modules tailored for academic training and a case study validating the approach on a regional stormwater management system with variable soil composition. This work will advance computational drafting methodologies, support climate-resilient infrastructure design, and provide students with hands-on experience in HPC-aided civil engineering workflows, bridging gaps between traditional drafting techniques and modern computational geotechnics.
cip_title: Civil Drafting and Civil Engineering CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawing and electronic simulations in support of civil engineers, geological engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic civil engineering principles, geological and seismographic mapping, machine drafting, computer-aided drafting (CAD), pipe drafting, survey interpretation, and blueprint reading.

abstract: The increasing demand for home-based healthcare services necessitates innovative approaches to optimize care delivery and improve outcomes for homebound patients. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulation frameworks that enhance decision-making for home health aides (HHAs) and caregivers. The research problem centers on the complexity of managing dynamic patient needs—such as fluctuating vital signs, infection risks, and emergency events—within decentralized home environments, where real-time clinical oversight is limited. Current protocols rely heavily on manual documentation and static care plans, which may fail to account for rapidly evolving patient conditions or environmental factors. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze multimodal datasets, including electronic health records, in-home sensor data, and caregiver-reported observations. HPC resources will enable large-scale training of ML models to predict patient deterioration (e.g., sepsis, falls) and simulate the impact of varying care strategies under diverse home conditions. Key computational challenges include processing high-frequency sensor data, managing spatiotemporal variability in home environments, and optimizing model generalizability across patient subgroups. The expected outcomes include (1) a predictive analytics toolkit to alert HHAs to emerging risks, prioritized by severity, and (2) evidence-based recommendations for personalized care workflows that adapt to patient needs. By integrating HPC-driven insights into home health training programs, this work aims to reduce preventable hospitalizations, improve resource allocation for home care agencies, and empower HHAs with data-driven tools to enhance care quality. The project aligns with national priorities to scale home-based care while addressing health disparities among aging and disabled populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and support services for homebound disabled, recovering, or elderly people. Includes instruction in basic nutrition, home sanitation, infection control, first aid, taking vital signs, personal hygiene, interpersonal communication skills, supervised home management, emergency recognition and referral, geriatric care, and legal and ethical responsibilities.

abstract: Financial crime networks increasingly exploit advanced technologies and global financial systems, necessitating innovative computational approaches to uncover and analyze complex fraud schemes. Traditional forensic methods struggle with the scale and sophistication of modern financial data, particularly in cases involving cross-jurisdictional transactions, cryptocurrency obfuscation, or layered money laundering networks. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy scalable algorithms for detecting and mapping illicit financial activities across heterogeneous datasets. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating machine learning models to identify anomalous transaction patterns in multi-terabyte accounting datasets, (2) applying graph-theoretic analysis to trace hidden relationships in transnational financial networks, and (3) simulating money laundering behaviors to refine predictive analytics under varying regulatory conditions. Computational workflows will integrate structured accounting data, unstructured documents, and blockchain ledgers using parallelized data ingestion pipelines and GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks. The scale of analysis—encompassing billions of nodes for cross-border transaction graphs—requires distributed memory architectures and optimized sparse matrix operations only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for forensic accountants and law enforcement, validated against active Interpol cases involving trade-based money laundering. By enabling real-time analysis of previously intractable datasets, this work aims to establish new standards for fraud detection latency and accuracy while providing empirical insights into evolving financial crime methodologies. The project bridges computational social science and forensic accounting, advancing technical capabilities for public-private anti-fraud initiatives without direct alignment to traditional STEM or listed non-STEM disciplines.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of conducting investigations into financial crime, terrorist activity, and the analysis and use of accounting data as evidence. Includes instruction in the principles of accounting, investigative auditing, computer investigations, accounting system documents and software, business corruption, criminal and terrorist financial networks, international money markets and movement, net worth analysis, financial fraud, exposing concealed assets, records seizure, fraud and money laundering statutes, fraud case initiation, case management, and case presentation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance adaptive interface design for immersive augmented reality (AR) environments by integrating real-time cognitive-affective modeling with user behavior analytics. While current AR systems adapt layouts based on basic gaze or gesture inputs, they often fail to account for dynamic cognitive load, perceptual biases, or emotional states, limiting accessibility and exacerbating user fatigue. Our research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that synthesizes multi-modal data streams—including eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and physiological signals—to predict and respond to nuanced user states. The core challenge lies in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive data at low latency while maintaining robust model accuracy across diverse user populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (sampled at 1kHz from 120+ participants) and for simulating interface adaptations through agent-based modeling. The computational pipeline involves three phases: 1) real-time feature extraction from biometric sensors using parallelized signal processing, 2) ensemble learning to classify cognitive load and emotional valence via federated learning architectures, and 3) probabilistic reasoning to optimize interface parameters through differentiable user simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source library for adaptive interface prototyping and empirical validation showing ≥30% reductions in task completion errors and cognitive strain metrics across neurodiverse user groups. This work bridges human-computer interaction, cognitive neuroscience, and machine learning, offering novel methodologies for personalized human-technology collaboration. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to establish scalable design principles for AR systems that dynamically align with users' biological and perceptual needs, particularly benefiting high-stakes domains like medical visualization and industrial training.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: Habitat fragmentation and biodiversity loss pose critical challenges for global ecosystems, yet predicting long-term ecological outcomes under dynamic human pressures remains computationally intractable with conventional methods. This project seeks to advance conservation planning by developing spatially explicit, multi-scale models that integrate landscape genomics, species interaction networks, and anthropogenic disturbance regimes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to analyze continental-scale habitat connectivity patterns across 27 threatened vertebrate species in Southeast Asia's Sundaland biodiversity hotspot, where accelerating deforestation and infrastructure development require urgent predictive frameworks. The computational workflow combines maximum entropy species distribution models with circuit theory connectivity analyses across 1km² resolution grids, incorporating temporal land-use change projections from satellite-derived datasets (2000-2030). A novel agent-based modeling component will simulate meta-population dynamics under alternative conservation scenarios, requiring parallel processing of >10⁶ individual agents with genetically informed dispersal behaviors. Machine learning approaches will identify critical habitat corridors and evolutionary significant units most vulnerable to fragmentation effects. Expected outcomes include: 1) predictive maps of genetic diversity loss under proposed development plans, 2) optimized corridor networks maintaining >90% of current connectivity, and 3) open-source computational tools for integrating genomic resilience into protected area design. These resources will directly inform multinational conservation policies under the ASEAN Wildlife Enforcement Network, while advancing theoretical understanding of extinction thresholds in fragmented landscapes. The requested computing allocation enables processing of 850TB of multispectral imagery, genomic datasets from 15,000 individual samples, and stochastic simulations across 10⁴ possible landscape configurations – a computational scale essential for addressing real-world conservation challenges at the interface of ecological complexity and human development needs.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences to the specific problems of biodiversity, species preservation, ecological sustainability, and habitat fragmentation in the face of advancing human social, economic, and industrial pressures. Includes instruction in ecology, environmental science, biological systems, extinction theory, human-animal and human-plant interaction, ecosystem science and management, wetland conservation, field biology, forest and wildlife biology, and natural history.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of high-impact mesoscale atmospheric processes, particularly those driving extreme precipitation and convective storm systems, which are critical yet poorly resolved in current regional climate models. Despite progress in meteorological modeling, persistent gaps exist in simulating fine-scale interactions between atmospheric dynamics, microphysics, and boundary layer processes—a limitation exacerbated by computational constraints on spatial resolution and ensemble size. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled investigation using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model configured at cloud-resolving resolutions (≤1 km grid spacing) across nested domains. The study will focus on historically under-simulated regions prone to rapidly intensifying storms, leveraging multi-source observational data (radar, satellite, and ground-based sensors) for validation and data assimilation. Computational workflows will integrate ensemble-based sensitivity analysis to quantify uncertainties in microphysical parameterizations and boundary conditions, while machine learning techniques will be tested to optimize subgrid-scale process representation. The required HPC resources will support large-domain, high-frequency output simulations over decadal climatological periods, with parallelized workflows managing ~10⁴ core-hours per ensemble member. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of resolution thresholds necessary to capture critical storm-scale feedbacks, (2) improved parameterization schemes for convective initiation in regional models, and (3) open-access datasets of high-resolution hindcasts for community benchmarking. By elucidating processes central to extreme weather predictability, this work will directly inform climate adaptation strategies and severe weather forecasting frameworks. The computational demands inherent to these objectives—particularly the need for sustained petascale storage, low-latency I/O, and scalable MPI-based parallelism—necessitate dedicated allocation within a tier-2 or tier-3 HPC environment to achieve scientifically robust results within project timelines.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in atmospheric sciences and meteorology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance and fault diagnosis for complex electrical and electronic systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current diagnostic protocols in electrical/electronics repair often rely on reactive or rule-based strategies, which struggle to adapt to dynamic operating conditions, leading to unplanned downtime, costly repairs, and safety risks. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and multiphysics simulations to model equipment degradation, predict failure modes, and optimize repair workflows. HPC resources will enable the training of deep neural networks on large-scale datasets of sensor telemetry, historical maintenance records, and synthetic fault scenarios generated via finite element analysis (FEA). These models will simulate thermal, mechanical, and electrical stress interactions in critical components such as power converters, motor drives, and embedded control systems. Parallelized computation will facilitate parameter sweeps across diverse operating environments and accelerated testing of hypothetical failure cascades. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance toolkit that identifies emerging faults with >90% accuracy 48–72 hours prior to failure, validated through case studies on industrial automation systems and renewable energy infrastructure. The project will also produce open-source simulation templates to help technicians visualize failure mechanisms and test repair strategies in silico. By bridging computational modeling with hands-on repair practices, this work aims to advance adaptive maintenance paradigms, reduce lifecycle costs of electrical systems, and inform curriculum updates for technician training programs. The requested HPC allocation is critical to handling the project’s computational demands, including GPU-accelerated ML training, distributed FEA jobs, and real-time digital twin simulations requiring low-latency data processing.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronics equipment installation and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Dairy production systems face complex challenges in optimizing animal health, milk yield, and environmental sustainability while balancing economic constraints. Current empirical models struggle to integrate multi-scale data—from microbial interactions in rumen ecosystems to herd-level management dynamics—limiting predictive capacity for precision dairy farming. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model nutrient utilization, methane emission dynamics, and disease susceptibility in dairy cattle. The research will integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic profiles) with real-time sensor data from wearable health monitors and automated milking systems. Machine learning models will be trained on these heterogeneous datasets to identify biomarkers for subclinical mastitis and metabolic disorders, while agent-based simulations will evaluate the systemic impacts of alternative feed formulations and housing configurations. A parallelized optimization pipeline will iteratively refine management strategies to maximize feed efficiency and milk solids yield while minimizing greenhouse gas emissions. The computational workflow requires HPC resources to manage large-scale genomic datasets (>10 TB), perform parameter sweeps across 10,000+ simulated herd scenarios, and execute ensemble modeling of rumen microbiome interactions at hourly resolution. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for early disease detection, validated protocols for methane mitigation through dietary interventions, and decision-support systems for facility design adaptations under climate variability. This work directly addresses critical gaps in translational dairy science by bridging molecular-scale insights with operational-scale management, ultimately advancing the resilience and sustainability of modern dairy production systems. The requested computing allocation will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling biological and operational trade-offs, providing actionable strategies for producers and policymakers.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the selection and care of dairy animals and associated dairy farm and processing facilities and operations. Includes instruction in basic animal and dairy science; dairy animal nutrition and health; design and operation of dairy housing, feeding, and processing facilities and equipment; and related issues of safety, sanitation, shipping and handling, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in administrative workflow optimization through the development of predictive computational models tailored to dynamic office environments. Administrative professionals increasingly manage complex, data-dense tasks—such as scheduling, document prioritization, and cross-departmental coordination—amidst variable workloads and shifting organizational priorities. Traditional heuristic approaches to task management struggle to adapt to real-time constraints, leading to bottlenecks, resource misallocation, and reduced responsiveness. To bridge this gap, the study proposes a hybrid computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate office ecosystems, predict task-critical paths, and recommend adaptive resource allocation strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets of historical workflow patterns, simulate multi-agent interactions under diverse operational scenarios, and train ML algorithms to identify latent dependencies between tasks, personnel availability, and organizational objectives. The ABM component will model administrative staff as autonomous agents with skill-specific attributes, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will analyze temporal task sequences to forecast priority conflicts. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for testing workflow configurations, predictive metrics for proactive task delegation, and empirically derived thresholds for workload balancing. This work contributes to the emerging interdisciplinary niche of computational organizational efficiency, offering scalable solutions to enhance decision-making in administrative roles. By integrating operations research with secretarial science, the project aims to establish data-driven frameworks that reduce operational latency in business environments while providing foundational insights into the computational reskilling needs of administrative professionals in the AI-augmented workplace.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for commercial and industrial vehicle systems using high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize repair workflows and reduce operational downtime. Current maintenance practices rely heavily on reactive or scheduled interventions, which often lead to inefficiencies, unexpected failures, and inflated costs. To address this, the research will integrate real-time sensor data from vehicle telemetry systems—including engine performance, brake wear, and transmission metrics—with machine learning (ML) models to predict component failures and prescribe targeted maintenance actions. The computational approach involves training deep neural networks on historical failure datasets and simulating wear patterns under diverse operating conditions using multiphysics modeling. HPC resources are critical to process terabytes of telemetry data, run parallelized simulations of mechanical stress and thermal degradation, and iteratively refine ML architectures for accuracy and generalizability. Expected outcomes include a scalable software toolkit that identifies high-risk components with 85–90% prediction accuracy, recommends cost-effective repair sequences, and dynamically adapts to evolving vehicle usage patterns. This framework will be validated against field data from fleet operators, with results disseminated to regional technical colleges to modernize vehicle repair curricula. By transitioning maintenance strategies from heuristic-based to data-driven paradigms, the project aims to extend vehicle lifespans, lower repair costs for small-to-medium enterprises, and reduce environmental waste from premature part replacements. The proposed HPC allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale finite element analyses, and cloud-based deployment prototypes, enabling advancements in both computational mechanics and applied automotive technology.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of vehicles and mobile equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the cognitive and motor skill development processes in music education, with the goal of optimizing pedagogical strategies for music teachers. While music learning involves complex interactions between auditory processing, motor coordination, and theoretical understanding, existing research has yet to fully model these dynamics at scale due to computational limitations. Our study addresses this gap by developing agent-based simulations of student ensembles and solo performers, integrating real-world data from motion-captured instrumental techniques, EEG recordings of neural responses during sight-reading, and longitudinal assessments of music theory comprehension. These multi-modal datasets will be analyzed using machine learning pipelines to identify patterns in skill acquisition, error correction, and the efficacy of instructional interventions. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-resolution sensor data, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and training deep learning models to predict student outcomes under varying teaching methods. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for mapping the interplay between cognitive load, motor skill development, and music literacy, enabling the design of adaptive curricula that balance technical rigor with creative expression. Results will directly inform music teacher education programs by quantifying the impact of different instructional sequencing strategies, from foundational technique building to ensemble collaboration. By bridging computational modeling with music pedagogy, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for training educators to address diverse learner needs while maintaining the artistic integrity of music instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach music and music appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to enhance the accuracy and accessibility of real-time captioning systems in legal settings, with a focus on addressing the unique challenges of courtroom environments. While court reporting traditionally relies on stenographic expertise, emerging demands for multilingual support, rapid transcription of overlapping speech, and real-time error correction necessitate innovative computational solutions. The research problem centers on the limitations of existing automated systems in handling complex acoustic environments, specialized legal terminology, and dialectal variability—issues that disproportionately affect equitable access to justice. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this project will train and deploy machine learning models to analyze vast datasets of courtroom audio recordings, annotated transcripts, and stenographic outputs. Computational methods will include the development of domain-specific speech recognition architectures optimized for low-latency processing, adversarial training to mitigate bias in dialect recognition, and hybrid models that integrate semantic context from legal corpora. The project will also simulate real-time captioning workflows under varied acoustic conditions to optimize resource allocation for edge computing in courtrooms. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive captioning, benchmarks for evaluating legal transcription systems, and a novel dataset linking prosodic features (e.g., stress, pause patterns) to contextual ambiguity in judicial proceedings. By bridging computational linguistics, acoustical engineering, and legal pedagogy, this work aims to establish scalable protocols for maintaining procedural integrity in increasingly digital court systems while preserving the irreplaceable role of human court reporters through augmented intelligence tools. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of audio-visual data, iterating deep learning architectures, and validating system robustness across diverse demographic and linguistic cohorts.
cip_title: Court Reporting and Captioning/ Court Reporter
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to record and transcribe examinations, testimony, judicial orders and instructions, legal opinions, and other formal proceedings via print or electronic methods. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcription, shorthand, verbatim recording, equipment operation and procedures, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop personalized, adaptive teaching frameworks for students recovering from traumatic brain injuries (TBI) by leveraging computational modeling to predict individualized learning trajectories. TBI survivors exhibit highly variable cognitive, sensory, and motor deficits, complicating the design of effective educational interventions. Current approaches rely on manual, trial-and-error adjustments to individualized education programs (IEPs), which are time-intensive and lack predictive precision. To address this, we propose integrating neurocognitive assessment data, behavioral observations, and longitudinal academic performance metrics into machine learning models to simulate how differing instructional strategies may affect recovery and learning outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training multi-modal neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (including neuroimaging-derived connectivity patterns and real-time classroom interaction logs) and for running large-scale simulations of intervention scenarios. The computational pipeline will (1) identify latent patterns in TBI-related functional impairments using unsupervised clustering, (2) map these clusters to optimized teaching strategies via reinforcement learning, and (3) validate predictions through in silico trials that model neuroplasticity-driven recovery processes. Outcomes will include a scalable tool for generating dynamic IEP recommendations, reducing the planning burden on educators while improving the specificity of interventions. By simulating neurocognitive recovery timelines under varying educational conditions, this work aims to bridge gaps between clinical rehabilitation and classroom practice, offering empirically grounded strategies to support TBI-affected learners. The project’s computational demands—particularly in processing high-dimensional neurobehavioral data and iterating complex, time-dependent models—necessitate GPU-accelerated clusters and large-memory nodes to achieve practical training times and enable real-world applicability in teacher preparation programs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Traumatic Brain Injuries
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who are surviving and recovering from brain and brain stem injuries affecting their cognitive, perceptive, and motor functions. Includes instruction in neurophysiology and neuropathology; speech, other sensory, and motor pathologies; emotional and cognitive disabilities; physical and occupational rehabilitation techniques; developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising brain-injured students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform misinformation dissemination in fragmented media ecosystems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets. Contemporary communication research faces challenges in tracking misinformation across rapidly evolving digital platforms—including social media, podcasts, and decentralized networks—due to the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of data. Current methods, often limited to single-platform or text-centric analyses, fail to capture the interdependencies between media formats and their collective impact on public discourse. This study proposes a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and temporal modeling to map misinformation diffusion patterns across audio, video, and text-based platforms. The research will employ transformer-based models fine-tuned for multimodal content classification, paired with dynamic network algorithms to identify cross-platform amplification nodes. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training domain-specific language models, and simulating information cascades at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel dataset annotating misinformation trajectories across three media types, 2) computational models quantifying platform-specific vulnerabilities to coordinated disinformation campaigns, and 3) evidence-based frameworks for platform-agnostic intervention strategies. By revealing how multimedia ecosystems amplify misinformation, this work aims to advance communication theory on digital discourse while providing actionable tools for journalists and fact-checking organizations. The requested computing allocation will enable processing of real-time data streams from 15+ platforms, reduce model training times from weeks to days, and support the first longitudinal analysis of cross-media misinformation networks at this granularity. Findings will be disseminated through open-access tools for communication researchers and partnerships with journalism ethics consortia.
cip_title: Communication, Journalism, and Related Programs, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication, journalism, and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the operational reliability and tactical effectiveness of next-generation aircraft armament systems through advanced predictive modeling and real-time simulation. Modern military platforms integrate complex, interdependent subsystems—such as targeting sensors, munitions deployment mechanisms, and countermeasure interfaces—that require precise coordination under dynamic environmental and combat conditions. Current maintenance protocols and failure prediction models lack the granularity to address emergent vulnerabilities arising from hardware-software interactions, material fatigue in extreme climates, and electromagnetic interference patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute multi-physics simulations combining computational fluid dynamics, structural stress analysis, and machine learning-driven anomaly detection. These simulations will synthesize terabyte-scale datasets from operational flight recorders, component wear analytics, and synthetic threat scenarios to model system degradation pathways and failure thresholds. A parallelized Monte Carlo approach will assess probabilistic outcomes across diverse mission profiles, while neural networks trained on historical maintenance logs will identify latent risk factors in subsystem interoperability. The resulting framework aims to reduce unplanned maintenance downtime by 25–40% and improve threat response accuracy through adaptive decision-support algorithms. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing of novel armament configurations, this work will directly inform lifecycle management protocols and enhance the operational readiness of legacy and next-generation platforms. The computational outputs will be validated against live-fire exercise data and integrated into a classified predictive maintenance toolkit for joint service use, addressing a critical capability gap in sustainment logistics for modern aerial warfare systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of aircraft weapons systems and associated peripherals. Includes instruction in basic science and quantitative methods, computer science, electronics, engineering graphics, fluid power, heavy equipment operation, armament systems, weapon materials and processes, weapon safety, corrosion control, aircraft systems maintenance, and maintenance management.

abstract: The development of multicellular organisms relies on precise spatiotemporal coordination of cellular behaviors to generate functional tissues and organs. A critical challenge in developmental biology lies in understanding how collective cell dynamics—such as migration, adhesion, and mechanical force generation—are integrated across scales to drive morphogenesis and anatomical patterning. Traditional experimental approaches provide limited resolution for quantifying emergent properties of cell populations or predicting outcomes of perturbed developmental processes. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled, multiscale modeling framework to simulate cellular self-organization during key embryological events, including somitogenesis and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. Leveraging agent-based modeling, we will construct 3D simulations in which individual cells are encoded with experimentally derived biophysical parameters (e.g., cortical tension, adhesion kinetics) and responsiveness to microenvironmental cues. The models will integrate live-imaging data from vertebrate model systems to validate predicted cell trajectories and tissue remodeling patterns. HPC resources are essential to resolve the nonlinear interactions of >10^5 simulated cells over developmental timescales, requiring parallelized computation and optimized memory allocation. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how local cell-cell signaling errors propagate to structural birth defects, such as neural tube closure failures. By bridging cell-level dynamics with tissue-scale phenotypes, this work will establish a computational platform for testing hypotheses about developmental robustness and vulnerability. The resource request directly supports the program’s focus on cell differentiation and morphogenesis while advancing computational methodologies in cellular anatomy. Results will be disseminated through open-source model sharing and collaborations with experimental developmental biologists, offering new strategies to interrogate embryological processes that are inaccessible to purely empirical approaches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of embryology, development, and growth of animals and human beings. Includes instruction in fertilization, oogenesis, histogenesis, gastrulation, and cell differentiation; embryological development including organ and pattern formation, morphogenesis, gene regulation, cell lineage, and fate maps; disease and defect studies; transgenic and evolutionary models of growth and development; and applications to specific organisms and phyla.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of preparing secondary educators to design adaptive, evidence-based instructional strategies for diverse classrooms through the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulation platform. While teacher education programs emphasize differentiated instruction, pre-service teachers often lack opportunities to practice responding to dynamic, multifaceted classroom scenarios that involve varying student abilities, cultural backgrounds, and engagement levels. To bridge this gap, we propose creating a virtual classroom environment using agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate student interactions, learning trajectories, and real-time feedback mechanisms. The computational model will integrate empirical datasets from student assessments, demographic records, and behavioral observations to generate synthetic cohorts reflecting the heterogeneity of secondary classrooms. Machine learning algorithms will train adaptive "student agents" to exhibit realistic responses to pedagogical interventions, enabling pre-service teachers to test instructional strategies in a risk-free setting. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to accommodate complex variables (e.g., individual learning styles, peer dynamics, resource constraints) and for enabling concurrent user interactions during training modules. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for quantifying the impact of teaching practices on simulated learning outcomes and a repository of scenario-based training modules. This work will provide teacher education programs with a tool to enhance pedagogical adaptability, directly aligning with the program’s focus on equipping educators to address secondary students’ evolving needs. The open-source platform will be designed for integration into existing curricula, offering a scalable solution to improve instructional readiness in STEM and humanities disciplines alike.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the secondary grades, which may include grades seven through twelve, depending on the school system or state regulations. May include preparation to teach a comprehensive curriculum or specific subject matter.

abstract: The project aims to advance understanding of mesoscale ocean eddy impacts on biogeochemical cycles in the subtropical oceans, where these dynamic features drive nutrient supply and carbon export but remain poorly resolved in global models. Current limitations in computational resources restrict simulations to resolutions too coarse to capture eddy-driven vertical transport, leading to persistent underestimation of primary productivity in oligotrophic regions. This work proposes a high-resolution coupled physical-biogeochemical modeling study using the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) configured at 1.5 km horizontal resolution, nested within a broader 4 km domain spanning the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre. The configuration will integrate advanced turbulence closure schemes and a 12-component biogeochemical module tracking carbon, nitrogen, and iron cycling. Multi-year simulations will be forced with high-frequency atmospheric reanalysis data and boundary conditions from CMIP6 Earth system models to assess climate change impacts on eddy-mediated nutrient fluxes. Computational demands necessitate high-performance computing resources for parallelized model integration, with an estimated 2.5 million core-hours required to complete decadal-scale runs across multiple emission scenarios. Outputs will be validated against autonomous float measurements, satellite ocean color products, and Lagrangian drifter trajectories. The results will quantify eddy-driven lateral and vertical nutrient fluxes at unprecedented resolution, reducing uncertainties in marine carbon cycle projections. By resolving submesoscale biophysical interactions, this work will provide critical parameterizations for improving ecosystem dynamics in next-generation climate models while informing marine resource management strategies in rapidly changing subtropical ecosystems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the ocean/marine sciences, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Punjabi language dynamics and literary heritage. Despite Punjabi’s status as a major global language with rich dialectal diversity and a vast literary corpus, systematic large-scale studies of its linguistic evolution, regional variations, and sociocultural influences remain limited due to computational constraints. The research problem centers on the need to model phonetic, syntactic, and lexical patterns across Punjabi dialects and historical texts, which require processing terabytes of unstructured data, including digitized manuscripts, oral recordings, and modern digital content. The project proposes a multi-phase computational approach. First, parallelized text processing and phonetic alignment algorithms will be deployed to analyze dialectal variations in spoken and written corpora, spanning major Punjabi dialects (e.g., Majhi, Doabi, Malwai). Second, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to automate the semantic and stylistic analysis of pre-modern and modern Punjabi literature, identifying temporal shifts in thematic focus and linguistic innovation. Third, graph-based network analyses will map the diffusion of loanwords and syntactic structures across contact languages (e.g., Urdu, Hindi) in urban and rural contexts. These methods demand significant GPU-accelerated computing power for training deep learning architectures and processing high-resolution scans of aging manuscripts via optical character recognition (OCR) optimized for Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi scripts. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access computational repository for Punjabi linguistics, comprising dialect atlases, annotated literary corpora, and tools for low-resource language NLP applications. The project will directly contribute to preserving endangered dialectal forms, enhancing pedagogical resources for Punjabi instruction, and informing policy frameworks for language technology development in South Asia. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to establish a paradigm for interdisciplinary research in less-resourced languages within digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Punjabi language (Punjabi) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to model and optimize law enforcement resource allocation in dynamic urban environments, addressing the critical challenge of balancing proactive crime prevention with community trust-building initiatives. The research problem centers on the inherent tension between deploying predictive policing algorithms—which often rely on historical crime data and risk perpetuating biases—and implementing community-oriented strategies that prioritize transparency and equity. Current approaches lack the computational granularity to simulate real-time interactions between policing tactics, socio-demographic variables, and emergent public sentiment. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-agent simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model urban ecosystems at unprecedented resolution. The framework will integrate heterogeneous data streams, including anonymized crime reports, demographic data, body-worn camera metadata, and social media sentiment analysis, processed through hybrid machine learning architectures (graph neural networks coupled with reinforcement learning). Agent-based models will represent diverse stakeholders—officers, residents, local businesses—operating under configurable policy regimes. Computational experiments will quantify how different resource allocation strategies affect both crime displacement patterns and community cooperation metrics across temporal and spatial scales. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for police departments to stress-test proposed operational strategies in silico before implementation, reducing the risks of unintended consequences. The HPC environment is essential for executing parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations while maintaining the fine-grained spatial resolution (block-level) and temporal fidelity (minute-scale event sequencing) required for practical insights. By creating a virtual proving ground for equity-focused policing strategies, this work aims to advance evidence-based policy-making in law enforcement while maintaining computational rigor typically reserved for physical sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: Architectural conservation faces a critical challenge in predicting and mitigating the degradation of historic building materials under evolving environmental stressors. Traditional analysis methods, reliant on physical sampling and laboratory testing, are often slow, destructive, and limited in scalability. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model the long-term behavior of historic materials—such as lime mortar, timber, and stone—using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-decadal environmental interactions. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including climate projections, material property databases, and 3D structural scans, to create predictive models of decay mechanisms like salt crystallization, freeze-thaw cycles, and microbial colonization. Computational methods will employ finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for microscale material interactions, and machine learning (ML) to identify degradation patterns across diverse architectural contexts. By leveraging parallelized workflows on HPC clusters, the project aims to resolve time-dependent processes at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, enabling scenario testing for adaptive conservation strategies. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital toolkit for prioritizing at-risk structures, optimizing repair material compatibility, and informing climate-resilient preservation policies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges heritage science, computational mechanics, and environmental data analytics, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to proactive conservation practices. The project’s computational demands center on large-scale parameter sweeps for probabilistic degradation forecasts and GPU-accelerated ML training using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to analyze terabyte-scale LiDAR and hyperspectral imaging datasets. Results will advance the sustainable reuse of historic buildings while establishing scalable methodologies for integrating HPC into cultural heritage research, a domain traditionally underrepresented in computational resource allocation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the architectural design principles and building techniques used in historic structures and environments, and the process of saving and restoring old buildings and districts for contemporary use and enjoyment. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation techniques, and material conservation.

abstract: The development of advanced materials with tailored functional properties requires a fundamental understanding of complex microstructure-property relationships that are difficult to probe experimentally. This project seeks to address critical gaps in predicting the emergence of defect-mediated phenomena in next-generation nanostructured alloys under extreme thermomechanical conditions. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we aim to establish multiscale models that bridge quantum-accurate atomistic simulations with mesoscale phase-field methods to capture dislocation dynamics, grain boundary interactions, and solute segregation effects. The computational framework will integrate density functional theory (DFT) calculations for interfacial energetics, molecular dynamics (MD) for defect propagation, and machine learning potentials trained on ab initio datasets to extend accessible timescales. A key innovation involves coupling these approaches within an adaptive sampling workflow to identify dominant deformation mechanisms in refractory high-entropy alloys proposed for fusion reactor components. The HPC resources will enable large-scale parametric studies across compositionally complex systems, which exhibit computationally demanding configurational disorder. Expected outcomes include predictive models for microstructure evolution under irradiation and high-stress loading, validated against synchrotron characterization data. This work will directly inform the design of radiation-tolerant materials for extreme environments, with applications in nuclear energy and aerospace engineering. The requested allocations—spanning CPU/GPU nodes for hybrid DFT-MD workflows, high-memory nodes for phase-field ensembles, and parallel storage for petascale microstructure datasets—are essential to achieve the necessary statistical sampling and spatial resolution. By elucidating how atomic-scale defects govern macroscopic failure, this research will advance computational materials discovery paradigms while addressing a critical bottleneck in alloy development for national infrastructure priorities.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in materials sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing decentralized, self-organizing networks for dynamic environmental monitoring in underserved rural regions. Traditional network protocols struggle to maintain reliability and low latency in such environments due to rapidly changing physical conditions, intermittent power availability, and heterogeneous device capabilities. The research proposes a novel computational framework inspired by adaptive biological systems, integrating swarm intelligence algorithms with lightweight machine learning models to enable networks to autonomously reconfigure topology, routing paths, and resource allocation in response to environmental perturbations. The core innovation lies in developing multi-agent simulations that model network nodes as autonomous entities capable of collective decision-making through localized data exchange, prioritizing energy efficiency and fault tolerance without centralized coordination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for simulating large-scale networks (10,000+ nodes) under diverse environmental stress scenarios, including stochastic weather patterns, electromagnetic interference, and partial node failures. Computational methods will combine discrete-event network simulations with evolutionary optimization techniques, requiring parallel processing to evaluate millions of configuration permutations. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available benchmark dataset quantifying network resilience metrics under real-world constraints, 2) adaptive protocol designs that reduce energy consumption by 30-50% compared to existing mesh networking standards, and 3) predictive models for optimal node placement in terrain-aware deployments. This work bridges gaps between distributed computing, environmental sensing, and complex systems theory, with potential applications in disaster response networks, precision agriculture telemetry, and IoT infrastructure for climate-vulnerable regions. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits to support replicable research in emerging fields of ecological networking.
cip_title: Computer Systems Networking and Telecommunications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer systems networking and telecommunications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The preservation and restoration of human remains through embalming involve complex biochemical and physical processes that remain poorly understood at a mechanistic level. Current practices rely on empirical protocols, which may not account for individual variability in tissue composition, decomposition states, or environmental factors. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamics of embalming fluid diffusion, tissue interaction, and microbial suppression in human remains, with the goal of optimizing embalming protocols for diverse scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to simulate multi-scale, multi-physics processes, including fluid transport through heterogeneous tissues, chemical reaction kinetics of preservative agents, and the biomechanical effects of restorative interventions. A combination of finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, and machine learning will be employed to integrate anatomical data from 3D scans, histochemical profiles, and real-world case studies. The models will be validated against experimental data collected from controlled embalming trials, incorporating variables such as pH, temperature, and tissue hydration. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for tailoring embalming solutions to specific decomposition patterns, improving restorative outcomes in traumatic death cases, and reducing environmental impacts through minimized chemical use. The research will also explore the computational modeling of pathogen inactivation kinetics in remains, addressing public health concerns in mortality management. By bridging mortuary science with advanced computational methodologies, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based practice in the field, while generating open-access datasets to support education and regulatory innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for licensure as embalmers and morticians.  Includes instruction in pathogenic microbiology, systematic pathology, thanatochemistry, gross anatomy, clinical mortuary science, embalming, restorative art, applicable laws and regulations, and special services such as cremation and preparations required by specific religious communities.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize real-time adaptive decision-making in customer service support systems, with a focus on call center and teleservice operations. The core problem lies in the inefficiency of current customer interaction models, which struggle to dynamically balance service quality, agent workload, and operational costs under fluctuating demand and heterogeneous customer behavior. Traditional rule-based or static queue management systems often fail to account for the nonlinear interplay of variables such as caller intent, agent skill proficiency, emotional tone analysis, and cross-channel interaction histories. To address this, the project proposes a computational framework combining agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and reinforcement learning to simulate and optimize multi-dimensional service scenarios. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large-scale interaction datasets—including voice, text, and behavioral metadata—while training deep neural networks to predict optimal response pathways. The methodology includes three phases: 1) Developing a high-fidelity simulation environment mirroring real-world call center dynamics, 2) Implementing hybrid clustering algorithms to categorize emergent customer interaction patterns, and 3) Testing adaptive allocation strategies through multi-objective optimization constrained by service-level agreements and workforce capacity. Expected outcomes include a predictive model capable of reducing average handle time by 15-20% while maintaining satisfaction metrics, alongside operational guidelines for resource allocation under uncertainty. This work bridges computational social science, behavioral economics, and operations research, offering novel insights into human-AI collaboration in service ecosystems.
