Includes instruction in aromatherapy history and theory, basic physiology of absorption, aromachemistry, organic chemistry, botanical taxonomy, carrier oils, essential oils, extraction methods, blending techniques, application methods, safety, client consultation and treatment planning, business management, professional standards and ethics, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing multi-modal urban transportation networks under dynamic demand and sustainability constraints, a critical issue in public transportation management. Current decision-making frameworks often rely on static models that inadequately capture real-time interactions between transit modes, fluctuating commuter behavior, and environmental impacts. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an agent-based simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale urban mobility systems. The computational approach integrates machine learning for demand forecasting, discrete-event simulation for logistics operations, and graph theory for network optimization. By incorporating real-time data streams—such as traffic sensors, transit ridership, and environmental sensors—the model will dynamically evaluate trade-offs between operational efficiency, equity of access, and carbon emissions. HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating millions of individual agent decisions across diverse transportation modes (e.g., buses, ride-sharing, micro-mobility) while iteratively testing policy interventions. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for transit agencies to (1) predict the systemic impacts of infrastructure investments, (2) optimize service allocation during disruptions, and (3) quantify emission reductions from mode-shift incentives. The project aligns with transportation policy priorities by enabling evidence-based strategies to reduce congestion and advance climate goals. Computational outputs will be validated against historical data from three metropolitan case studies, with model code and aggregated datasets made publicly available to support reproducibility. This work directly contributes to the Business Administration field’s focus on operational efficiency and resource management in public-sector contexts, offering transferable methodologies for large-scale infrastructure project evaluation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, policy, law, and practices required to administrate and operate public transportation facilities, networks, services, and systems. Includes instruction in demand analysis and forecasting, environmental planning, facilities design and construction, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, multi- and intermodal transportation systems, project management, public administration, public policy, transportation economics, transportation law, transportation operations, transportation systems, and transportation technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling electromagnetic interference (EMI) within high-frequency integrated circuits (ICs), a critical bottleneck in advancing next-generation electronic systems. As ICs scale to nanometer dimensions and operate at gigahertz frequencies, traditional simulation tools fail to capture the complex electromagnetic coupling effects that degrade signal integrity and power efficiency. The research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework combining full-wave electromagnetic solvers with machine learning (ML) to predict and mitigate EMI in multi-layer circuit architectures. The computational approach will leverage finite-element method (FEM) simulations to model near-field coupling across 3D IC stacks, generating terabyte-scale datasets of spatial field distributions under varying frequency and material conditions. These datasets will train graph neural networks (GNNs) to identify EMI hotspots and recommend layout optimizations, enabling real-time design feedback. The HPC resources will facilitate parallel execution of thousands of parameterized FEM simulations on GPU clusters, reducing computation time from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include validated ML models for EMI prediction with >90% accuracy compared to experimental measurements, open-source simulation workflows, and design guidelines for reducing cross-talk in 5G/6G communication chips. This work will directly benefit semiconductor manufacturers and IoT device developers by accelerating the design of interference-resistant electronics while maintaining compliance with international EMI standards. The proposed computational pipeline also establishes a template for integrating physics-based modeling with AI/ML in electromagnetic compatibility research, addressing a critical gap in electrical engineering education and industry practice.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronic engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of efficient catalysts for sustainable chemical manufacturing processes. Industrial catalysts are critical for optimizing reaction yields, reducing energy consumption, and minimizing waste, yet their design remains constrained by the complexity of modeling dynamic reaction pathways and interfacial behaviors at scale. Traditional experimental approaches are costly and time-intensive, while existing computational methods often oversimplify multi-component systems or lack the resolution to capture transient catalytic states. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating quantum mechanical density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML)-driven reaction network analysis. The HPC environment will enable large-scale DFT calculations to screen transition metal alloy catalysts for CO₂ hydrogenation—a priority reaction for carbon utilization—while MD simulations will model solvent-catalyst interactions under industrial operating conditions. Concurrently, graph neural networks will predict optimal active site configurations and side reaction pathways using datasets generated from these simulations. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental catalysis studies conducted by our collaborators, ensuring alignment with real-world performance metrics. Successful execution of this project will yield (1) a validated protocol for rapid, high-accuracy catalyst screening, (2) atomistic insights into degradation mechanisms affecting catalyst longevity, and (3) open-access datasets linking computational descriptors to experimental catalytic efficiency. Outcomes will directly inform the design of next-generation catalysts for green chemistry applications, with potential impacts on renewable fuel production and circular manufacturing systems. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the ∼500,000 core-hours required for parallelized simulations, ML training on >10^6 configurational snapshots, and iterative model refinement. This work bridges computational innovation with applied chemical technology, advancing both fundamental understanding and industrial scalability in sustainable catalysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of chemical and biochemical research and industrial operations. Includes instruction in principles of chemistry and biochemistry, technical mathematics, computer applications, radiochemistry, industrial biochemistry, chemical instrumentation, physical chemistry, laboratory research methods, industrial processing methods and equipment, and test equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: The increasing complexity of toxicological exposures—including novel synthetic drugs, environmental contaminants, and chemical warfare agents—demands advanced computational approaches to predict toxicity mechanisms, optimize treatments, and inform public health responses. Current clinical methods for assessing dynamic exposure outcomes rely heavily on observational data and limited experimental models, which struggle to account for multifactorial interactions between xenobiotics, biological systems, and patient-specific variables. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of toxin pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) and multi-organ injury, integrating genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data with real-world clinical datasets from poison control centers and electronic health records. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we will characterize binding affinities and off-target interactions of emerging synthetic opioids and hallucinogens with neuronal receptors, enabling mechanistic toxicity predictions. Concurrently, machine learning frameworks will analyze population-level exposure data to identify risk clusters and biomarkers of acute organ damage (e.g., hepatorenal toxicity from heavy metals). HPC resources will be critical for scaling ensemble docking simulations across thousands of toxin-receptor permutations and training neural networks on high-dimensional toxicogenomic datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for rapid clinical decision support, a computational pipeline for real-time toxicity risk stratification during mass exposure events, and mechanistic insights into toxin-induced cellular injury pathways. These tools will directly address gaps in personalized antidote dosing, chronic exposure monitoring, and preparedness for novel toxic threats, ultimately reducing morbidity and mortality from acute and chronic poisonings. By bridging computational toxicology and clinical practice, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for evidence-based medical toxicology in an era of rapidly evolving chemical risks.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians who specialize in the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and monitoring of injury and illness from exposures to drugs and chemicals, as well as exposures to biological and radiological agents. Important areas include acute drug poisoning; adverse drug events; drug abuse, addiction, and withdrawal; chemicals and hazardous materials; terrorism preparedness; venomous bites and stings; and environmental and workplace exposures.

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision in perioperative anesthesia care by developing predictive models for individualized anesthetic dosing and real-time hemodynamic optimization, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current protocols for anesthesia administration rely on population-based guidelines and intermittent monitoring, which inadequately address dynamic patient-specific factors such as comorbidities, drug interactions, and intraoperative physiological fluctuations. These limitations contribute to preventable complications, including hypotension, delayed emergence, and postoperative delirium. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) with multiphysics simulations to model patient responses to anesthesia under diverse clinical scenarios. Large-scale retrospective data from electronic health records (n≈50,000 surgical cases) will be used to train ensemble ML models predicting hemodynamic responses to common anesthetic agents, incorporating time-series vital signs, preoperative risk factors, and surgical context. Concurrently, finite element modeling will simulate drug distribution and cardiovascular dynamics at tissue and organ levels, parameterized by patient-specific imaging and biomarker data. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (≥100 features/case), optimizing hyperparameters across distributed nodes, and executing parallelized simulations of drug-receptor interactions at scale. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for real-time anesthetic dosing recommendations, (2) mechanistic insights into interpatient variability in drug sensitivity, and (3) open-source tools for intraoperative decision support. The computational workflows will directly inform a prospective trial evaluating model-guided anesthesia in 200 patients undergoing major abdominal surgery. By enabling rapid analysis of complex physiological interactions and heterogeneous clinical data, this work aims to establish a paradigm for adaptive anesthesia care, reducing adverse events and improving recovery trajectories in surgical populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of anesthesia for general and specialized surgery and obstetrics, critical patient care, and the care of pain problems. Includes instruction in surgical procedures, current monitoring procedures, fluid therapy, pain management, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures outside the operating room, and operating room safety.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modular construction workflows through advanced simulation and optimization of off-site manufacturing and on-site assembly processes. Modular construction offers significant potential to reduce costs, timelines, and material waste in building projects, but its adoption is hindered by unpredictable delays arising from design-modeling mismatches, supply chain variability, and logistical bottlenecks. Current industry tools lack the capacity to integrate multi-scale data from building information modeling (BIM), real-time sensor networks, and supplier databases into actionable decision-support systems. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for dynamic process optimization. The computational approach will combine discrete-event simulation of construction sequences with machine learning-driven anomaly detection to predict delays, coupled with multi-objective genetic algorithms to iteratively refine assembly schedules and material delivery plans. Finite element analysis will be parallelized to assess structural integrity across modular unit configurations during iterative design adjustments. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale parametric analyses of 3D BIM geometries, stochastic supply chain scenarios, and real-time synchronization of IoT-enabled job site data. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital twin system capable of reducing idle time in modular assembly workflows by 15–25% while maintaining compliance with ASTM and ISO standards for construction quality. The resource allocation will directly support graduate student researchers in Construction Engineering Technology by enabling cloud-based collaboration with industry partners testing the system on active multifamily housing projects. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for construction simulation, advancing workforce training in next-generation project planning methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing dynamic decision-making in casino operations through high-fidelity simulations of customer behavior and resource allocation under uncertainty. The research addresses a critical gap in casino management: the lack of predictive tools to model complex, real-time interactions between customer preferences, gaming floor layouts, staffing patterns, and regulatory constraints. Traditional operational strategies rely on static heuristics or aggregated historical data, which fail to capture emergent behaviors in evolving environments—such as shifting player demographics, adaptive game design trends, or the integration of mixed-reality gaming platforms. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) paired with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate millions of player-path scenarios across parameterized casino ecosystems. The ABM component will incorporate heterogeneous agent profiles derived from anonymized player tracking data, psychometric surveys, and real-time biometric inputs (e.g., gaze tracking, dwell times), while DRL frameworks will train adaptive policies for staff deployment, promotional targeting, and spatial resource allocation. Computational challenges include managing high-dimensional state-action spaces for multi-agent systems and optimizing parallelized simulations across GPU clusters to achieve real-time decision latency thresholds. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support system capable of prescriptive adjustments to floor layouts, game mixes, and service protocols under probabilistic regulatory and revenue targets. The project will advance computational methods for service industry optimization while providing novel insights into behavioral economics within constrained entertainment environments. Results will be disseminated through gaming industry partnerships and adaptive AI licensing frameworks, with potential applications extending to hospitality and experiential retail sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage casinos and gaming establishments. Includes instruction in business and financial management; casino operations; casino security and surveillance; hospitality, facilities, and personnel management; and principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing multi-modal transportation networks in rapidly urbanizing regions, where competing priorities of environmental sustainability, economic efficiency, and social equity complicate infrastructure planning. Traditional analytical tools often fail to account for dynamic interactions between land use patterns, travel behavior, and climate resilience at metropolitan scales. To overcome these limitations, this research will develop an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and high-resolution geospatial analytics. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate millions of individual travel decisions under diverse policy scenarios, incorporating real-world data on population growth, emissions thresholds, and infrastructure decay. Key computational tasks include parallelized traffic microsimulations, GPU-accelerated deep learning for demand forecasting, and Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic risk assessment of flood impacts on transport corridors. By coupling these approaches, the model will evaluate trade-offs between interventions such as congestion pricing, electric vehicle adoption incentives, and green infrastructure investments. The outcomes will provide evidence-based guidance for equitable resource allocation in transportation planning, particularly for communities disproportionately affected by mobility gaps or environmental hazards. The scalable computational architecture will be designed for open-source release, enabling municipal agencies to adapt the tool for localized decision-making. This work directly supports public administration goals by advancing data-driven strategies to balance decarbonization targets, fiscal constraints, and accessibility needs in infrastructure development. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the petabyte-scale urban datasets and computationally intensive multi-objective optimizations required to generate policy-relevant insights within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the economic, social, spatial, and environmental aspects of transportation and infrastructure planning. Includes instruction in economics, environmental analysis, geographic information systems (GIS), logistics, risk analysis, transportation economics, transportation evaluation, transportation planning, transportation policy, and urban transportation planning.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling and analyzing complex ballet movement patterns to advance research in choreographic preservation, pedagogical innovation, and biomechanical efficiency. While ballet relies on embodied knowledge transmission, current methods for documenting choreography (e.g., Labanotation, video) lack the granularity to capture nuanced physiological and spatial relationships critical for technical training and archival fidelity. We propose developing a computational framework to process high-resolution motion capture data from professional dancers performing canonical ballet repertoire, integrating biomechanical metrics with stylistic annotations. The research will employ graph neural networks to model dynamic interactions between body segments during jumps, turns, and port de bras, while reinforcement learning algorithms will simulate adaptive coaching strategies for technique optimization. A parallelized pipeline will process terabytes of 3D kinematic data, requiring GPU-accelerated computing to train models on heterogeneous movement vocabularies across ballet styles (e.g., Vaganova vs. Bournonville). Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access repository of computationally annotated ballet sequences, linking motion data to historical stylistic descriptors; (2) predictive models identifying injury-risk movement signatures in training regimens; and (3) tools for generating augmented feedback interfaces for dance education. By leveraging high-performance computing to bridge qualitative artistic traditions with quantitative movement analysis, this work aims to establish new methodologies for preserving choreographic heritage while advancing evidence-based approaches to dancer training. The computational infrastructure requested will enable large-scale ensemble simulations and real-time processing of multi-modal data streams (motion, force plates, electromyography), which are intractable on local workstations. This resource will directly support the first systematic effort to computationally codify ballet’s physical and aesthetic complexities, with implications for dance science, digital humanities, and augmented performance technologies.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to express ideals and feelings through interpretation of classical dance choreography. Includes instruction in ballet exercise, solo and ensemble dance, history of ballet, ballet choreography, Laban notation, ballet technique, and interpretations of specific styles and schools.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation propagation in decentralized communication networks, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale interactions across hybrid digital platforms. As emerging communication technologies—such as federated social networks, encrypted messaging systems, and AI-mediated content tools—reshape information ecosystems, traditional analytical frameworks struggle to capture the nonlinear, cross-platform behaviors driving misinformation spread. The research problem centers on identifying critical thresholds at which localized misinformation events escalate into systemic crises, particularly in contexts where algorithmic moderation and human intervention interact unpredictably. Using a mixed-methods approach, we will integrate network science simulations with natural language processing (NLP) of multi-platform communication traces (e.g., social media posts, encrypted chat metadata, and synthetic media shares). Computational workflows will employ graph neural networks to model cross-platform influence cascades, coupled with agent-based simulations of user communities adapting to evolving content policies. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning six communication platforms, training transformer-based NLP models on multilingual misinformation corpora, and running Monte Carlo iterations of crisis escalation scenarios with over 10^6 simulated agents. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for assessing platform-interconnected risks, quantitative metrics for resilience benchmarking, and visual analytics tools to support policymakers in designing adaptive content governance strategies. By mapping the computational affordances of modern communication technologies to their societal impacts, this work aims to advance both scholarly understanding of decentralized information systems and practical interventions for maintaining epistemic security in journalism-adjacent digital spaces.
cip_title: Communications Technologies and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications technologies and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time computational modeling of American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current machine translation systems for signed languages struggle to process the multimodal, continuous, and context-dependent nature of ASL, particularly its non-manual markers (e.g., facial expressions, body movements) and spatial grammar. These limitations hinder the development of assistive technologies for the Deaf community and tools to support human interpreters. The research problem centers on optimizing neural architectures to model ASL’s visual-kinetic structure at scale while maintaining real-time inference speeds. The computational approach integrates 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatiotemporal feature extraction from video data with transformer-based models to capture syntactic and discourse-level dependencies. Training will utilize a novel multimodal dataset of annotated ASL dialogues, including motion-capture data and gloss transcriptions, to align linguistic features with visual signals. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution video inputs, parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across model variants, and deploying large-scale transformer fine-tuning. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for ASL machine interpretation with sub-second latency and improved accuracy relative to existing methods, measured by human interpreter validation. The project also aims to release open-source tools for preprocessing ASL video data and a curated dataset to advance research in low-resource signed languages. By addressing computational bottlenecks in processing ASL’s unique morphology and syntax, this work will directly support the development of next-generation interpretation technologies, reducing communication barriers and enhancing educational and professional accessibility for Deaf individuals. The interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational linguistics and sign language studies, offering new pathways for research in under-resourced language technologies within the Humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as simultaneous interpreters of American Sign Language

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of processing ultra-high-resolution video and complex digital film simulations in real time, which are critical for advancing workflows in photographic and film/video production. Current consumer-grade hardware struggles to manage the latency, storage, and rendering demands of 4K/8K video editing, AI-driven post-production tasks, and dynamic lighting simulations, particularly in collaborative environments. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize scalable pipelines for three core applications: (1) machine learning-enhanced frame interpolation and noise reduction for low-light cinematography, (2) GPU-accelerated ray tracing to simulate real-world lighting interactions in virtual production environments, and (3) distributed processing of multi-camera footage for live event streaming and volumetric video capture. Using containerized workflows on HPC clusters, we will parallelize computationally intensive tasks such as neural network training on high-frame-rate video datasets, real-time color grading across terabyte-scale projects, and photorealistic renderings of hybrid physical-digital sets. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in processing times for 8K footage, a framework for predictive lighting adjustments during live shoots via on-the-fly simulation, and open-source tools to democratize HPC access for small-scale filmmakers. By integrating these workflows into our curriculum, the project will also train students in cutting-edge computational production techniques, bridging gaps between artistic vision and technical execution. The resource allocation will directly support innovation in film technology education while enabling research into sustainable, scalable solutions for next-generation media workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation and maintenance of camera and lighting equipment and the production of finished still, video, and film products under the supervision of photographers, directors, and editors. Includes instruction in equipment setup and maintenance; lighting; power supplies; studio and film set tasks such as camera operator, grip, and best boy; plate and negative handling and development; laboratory procedures; and digital software applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance equestrian science through the development of a computational framework for analyzing equine biomechanics and rider-horse interaction dynamics. Despite the critical role of biomechanical efficiency in equine performance and welfare, existing studies often rely on limited datasets or simplified models, failing to capture the complexity of real-world riding scenarios. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating high-resolution motion capture data, inertial measurement unit (IMU) outputs, and physiological metrics from both horse and rider into a multi-scale computational model. This model will simulate load distribution, gait anomalies, and musculoskeletal stress under varying conditions, such as different riding styles, terrains, and equipment configurations. The computational approach employs finite element analysis (FEA) to evaluate tissue-level stresses in equine limbs, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify patterns predictive of injury or performance decline. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of synchronized sensor data, running iterative simulations, and training deep neural networks to optimize predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated equine movement datasets, predictive tools for injury risk assessment, and evidence-based guidelines for optimizing saddle fit and training regimens. By addressing the interplay between physiological limits and training practices, this work aims to reduce sport-related equine injuries while enhancing competitive outcomes. The project’s interdisciplinary nature—spanning computational biology, sports science, and veterinary medicine—exemplifies an emerging niche within equestrian studies, offering methodological innovations applicable to other animal-athlete research domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the horse, horsemanship, and related subjects and prepares individuals to care for horses and horse equipment; ride and drive horses for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes; and manage the training of horses and riders. Includes instruction in horse breeding, nutrition, health, and safety; history of the horse and horsemanship; horse development and training; riding and equestrian technique; stable, paddock, and track management; and equipment maintenance and repair.

abstract: The management of acute medical conditions in aging populations presents complex challenges due to heterogeneous patient responses, comorbidities, and polypharmacy. Current clinical decision-making tools often lack the granularity to predict individualized outcomes or optimize interventions in real time. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating multi-modal data—including electronic health records (EHRs), biomarker trajectories, and imaging data—to model dynamic treatment responses in critically ill older adults. A key barrier is the computational demand of processing high-dimensional, temporally resolved datasets while accounting for interactions between clinical variables, which existing statistical methods cannot efficiently resolve. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble machine learning models that identify patterns in treatment efficacy and adverse event risks across diverse geriatric cohorts. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing and harmonizing EHR data (structured and unstructured) using natural language processing, followed by feature selection and time-series analysis to extract predictive signatures. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models and recurrent neural networks, will be optimized to simulate patient trajectories under varying intervention strategies. Validation will employ synthetic datasets generated via agent-based modeling to test clinical scenarios while adhering to privacy constraints. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms capable of stratifying patients by likelihood of clinical deterioration, renal/cardiac complications, or delirium during acute care episodes. These tools aim to enable proactive, personalized intervention adjustments, reducing ICU lengths of stay and iatrogenic risks. The scalability of this approach relies on parallelized computing for model training and hyperparameter optimization, which necessitates access to GPU clusters and large-memory nodes. By integrating computational precision with geriatric acute care principles, this work has the potential to redefine clinical benchmarks for aging populations in critical settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Acute Care

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systemic mechanisms underlying cancer-related skeletal muscle dysfunction, a critical factor in physical disability and reduced quality of life among oncology patients. Cancer cachexia, characterized by severe muscle wasting and metabolic dysregulation, remains poorly understood, particularly in how tumor-derived factors disrupt skeletal muscle anabolic-catabolic signaling. Current experimental models lack the capacity to integrate multi-omics data (e.g., proteomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic profiles) with systemic physiological responses during disease progression. To address this gap, we propose a computational physiology framework combining dynamic network modeling and machine learning to simulate muscle-tumor crosstalk under varying exercise and therapeutic interventions. HPC resources will enable the construction of multi-scale models incorporating (1) mechanistic ordinary differential equation systems representing intracellular signaling (e.g., mTOR, ubiquitin-proteasome pathways), (2) agent-based simulations of muscle fiber heterogeneity, and (3) whole-body physiological parameters (oxygen consumption, circulatory cytokine dynamics). Datasets from ongoing murine cancer cachexia studies—including longitudinal muscle transcriptomics and in vivo force production measurements—will parameterize and validate these models. Expected outcomes include identification of exercise-responsive signaling nodes that mitigate muscle atrophy and predictive biomarkers of treatment response. This work will advance precision exercise prescriptions for cancer patients while elucidating fundamental principles of stress adaptation in skeletal muscle. The computational infrastructure developed will be scalable to other pathologies involving exercise intolerance, such as post-ICU syndrome or chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity. By bridging exercise physiology and oncology through systems-level modeling, this project addresses an urgent need for mechanistic, data-driven strategies to preserve physical function in cancer populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in physical or motor activity, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in muscular and skeletal anatomy; molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction; fuel utilization; neurophysiology of motor mechanics; systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others); fatigue and exhaustion; muscle and body training; physiology of specific exercises and activities; physiology of injury; and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal dynamics of cultural narratives within the Southwestern United States, a region shaped by overlapping Indigenous, Hispanic, and Anglo influences. The research problem centers on understanding how historical and contemporary narratives—preserved in multilingual texts, oral histories, and community archives—reflect and reinforce regional identity amid environmental and demographic shifts. Current methodologies in regional studies lack scalable tools to process heterogeneous, unstructured data (e.g., digitized folklore collections, ethnographic field notes, and georeferenced oral histories) while preserving contextual nuance. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), geospatial analysis, and network modeling. NLP pipelines will be developed to identify thematic patterns and sentiment trajectories across English, Spanish, and Indigenous language corpora, accounting for dialectal variations and historical semantic shifts. Geospatial clustering algorithms will map narrative diffusion pathways against environmental data (e.g., drought records, land-use changes) to assess how ecological pressures influence cultural storytelling. Network models will trace the evolution of narrative hubs within and across communities, using temporal graph embeddings to quantify intercultural exchange. The HPC environment is critical for training transformer-based language models on region-specific texts, parallelizing geospatial computations across high-resolution datasets, and simulating large-scale narrative networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database linking cultural narratives to socioecological contexts in the Southwest, (2) open-source tools for interdisciplinary regional analysis, and (3) new theoretical insights into how subregions negotiate identity through storytelling during periods of rapid change. This work will provide a scalable template for computational regional studies, emphasizing ethically grounded, community-engaged approaches to cultural data.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the defined geographic subregions and subcultures within modern and historical countries and societies. Includes such topics as Acadian Studies, French Canadian and Quebec Studies, Southern (U.S.) Studies, New England Studies, Southwestern Studies, Northern Studies, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational legal studies inquiry into the evolution of judicial decision-making patterns within decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). As blockchain-based entities governed by smart contracts and distributed consensus mechanisms, DAOs present novel challenges to traditional legal frameworks, particularly in resolving disputes and interpreting governance protocols. The research problem centers on identifying emergent legal norms in DAO governance through large-scale analysis of on-chain dispute resolution data and off-chain community deliberations. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for smart contract bytecode and forum discourse, the project will construct temporal network models to trace how quasi-legal principles develop across 50,000+ DAO transactions and associated social metadata. Computational demands arise from processing heterogeneous blockchain data (Ethereum, Solana) while maintaining cryptographic integrity, analyzing multilingual forum interactions, and simulating governance scenarios through agent-based modeling. The HPC environment is critical for training transformer-based architectures on limited annotated legal texts specific to decentralized governance, as well as for running parallelized simulations of hypothetical disputes under varying regulatory assumptions. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel taxonomy of algorithmic legal reasoning in decentralized organizations, 2) probabilistic models predicting conflict escalation paths based on smart contract design features, and 3) an open-source toolkit for auditing governance protocols against emergent jurisprudential patterns. By bridging computational social science with legal informatics, this work aims to establish methodological foundations for studying law in algorithmically mediated environments while providing actionable insights for policymakers grappling with the juridical status of Web3 institutions.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on law and legal issues from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the accuracy and scalability of forensic anthropological methods for skeletal trauma and decomposition analysis through advanced computational modeling. The primary research challenge lies in the complex, multivariate nature of taphonomic processes, where environmental variables (e.g., temperature, soil chemistry, scavenger activity) interact dynamically with skeletal remains, complicating time-since-death estimates and trauma interpretation. Traditional analytical approaches struggle to account for these nonlinear interactions at scale, particularly when analyzing large or fragmented skeletal assemblages. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), agent-based modeling (ABM), and machine learning (ML) to simulate decomposition dynamics and biomechanical responses to perimortem trauma. FEA will model stress distributions in bone under simulated blunt or sharp force impacts, while ABM will recreate scavenger behavior and environmental interactions affecting soft tissue degradation. ML algorithms trained on existing forensic case databases will identify patterns linking skeletal markers to environmental contexts. This computationally intensive workflow requires parallel processing to manage large-scale simulations across diverse climate scenarios and skeletal morphologies. Anticipated outcomes include (1) probabilistic models for postmortem interval (PMI) estimation with quantified uncertainty in variable environments, (2) a reference database of simulated trauma signatures correlated with weapon types and biomechanical forces, and (3) open-source tools for automated fracture pattern classification. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to advance forensic anthropology’s capacity to resolve ambiguities in mass disaster scenarios and prolonged PMI cases, while establishing reproducible computational standards for the discipline. The resulting methodologies will be validated against casework data from collaborating medical examiners, ensuring translational impact for both academic research and forensic practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and skeletal anthropology in medicolegal death investigations. Includes instruction in biological anthropology theory, crime scene investigation, forensic anthropology field methods, forensic anthropological techniques and procedures, human anatomy, methods of human identification, mortuary archaeology, osteology, and taphonomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize quality control (QC) processes in manufacturing systems through advanced simulations and predictive analytics. Current QC methodologies often rely on static sampling protocols and retrospective defect analysis, leading to inefficiencies in detecting process deviations and addressing root causes in real time. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating high-performance computing (HPC) to enable dynamic, data-driven QC systems capable of adapting to complex production environments. The proposed work will focus on two computational approaches: (1) large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to model variability in manufacturing processes and predict defect probabilities under diverse operating conditions, and (2) machine learning algorithms trained on multi-modal sensor data (e.g., vibration, thermal, and dimensional measurements) to identify early-stage anomalies in production lines. These methods will leverage parallel computing architectures to process terabytes of operational data, enabling real-time feedback loops for process adjustments. The project will also employ finite element analysis (FEA) to virtually test material stress thresholds and component tolerances, reducing reliance on physical prototyping for QC validation. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for simulating QC protocols, predictive models for defect prevention, and optimized inspection schedules that minimize downtime. By enhancing the precision and responsiveness of quality assurance systems, this work aims to reduce waste, improve compliance with ISO standards, and lower lifecycle costs for manufacturers. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the computational demands of iterative simulations, hyperparameter tuning for machine learning models, and large-scale data fusion tasks. Successful implementation will provide a template for integrating computational engineering technologies into QC education and industry practices, aligning with workforce development goals in advanced manufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining consistent manufacturing and construction standards. Includes instruction in quality control systems management principles, technical standards applicable to specific engineering and manufacturing projects, testing procedures, inspection procedures, related instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance strategies for legacy military hardware systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the unique challenges of aging infrastructure in defense contexts. Military maintenance programs increasingly face operational inefficiencies due to incompatibilities between legacy systems and modern diagnostic tools, compounded by sparse historical performance data and heterogeneous environmental stressors. Traditional condition-based maintenance models struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between mechanical wear, supply chain variability, and mission-critical operational timelines. To bridge this gap, the proposed research will integrate physics-informed machine learning (ML) with discrete-event simulation to model degradation pathways under multi-domain constraints. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to simulate equipment failure modes across diverse operational scenarios, including extreme climates and intermittent supply conditions. Custom ML architectures will be trained on hybrid datasets—combining sparse sensor data, maintenance logs, and synthetic failure scenarios—to predict component lifespans while quantifying uncertainty. The computational pipeline will prioritize interoperability with legacy diagnostic protocols to ensure practical deployment. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for generating adaptive maintenance schedules that balance cost, risk, and readiness metrics. This work fills a critical gap in military maintenance technology by providing data-driven strategies tailored to systems excluded from modern digital twin ecosystems. By focusing on computational resilience rather than hardware modernization, the project aligns with DoD priorities for extending service life of existing assets while reducing unplanned downtime. Results will be validated against historical maintenance records from armored vehicle fleets, with methodologies designed for transferability to naval and aviation systems.
cip_title: Military Systems and Maintenance Technology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military systems and maintenance technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for social enterprises operating in dynamic, resource-constrained environments. Social entrepreneurship often involves balancing mission-driven objectives with financial sustainability, yet existing decision-making models fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between stakeholder networks, fluctuating resource availability, and evolving social impact metrics. The study addresses this gap by creating a multi-agent simulation platform that models complex trade-offs in real time, integrating heterogeneous data streams such as donor behavior, community needs assessments, and environmental volatility. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to execute large-scale parameter sweeps across thousands of simulated scenarios, enabling the identification of robust allocation policies resilient to systemic shocks. Computational methods include stochastic optimization algorithms adapted for multi-objective social impact goals, network analysis of stakeholder influence patterns, and machine learning techniques to predict emergent outcomes from intervention cascades. The platform will be validated using case studies from partner organizations in renewable energy cooperatives and equitable healthcare access initiatives, incorporating both historical performance data and forward-looking stress tests. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive resource prioritization in social ventures, quantitative benchmarks for impact-finance equilibrium points, and predictive insights into how policy interventions alter systemic behavior across socioeconomic strata. By bridging computational social science with entrepreneurial strategy, this work aims to establish new methodologies for scaling social innovation while maintaining fidelity to grassroots stakeholder needs. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling the high-dimensional, time-sensitive computations inherent in modeling decentralized social systems at regional and global scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on blending entrepreneurial ideas and management skills for issue advocacy and social change. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, design, entrepreneurship, finance, investing, resource management, project management, prototype development, and marketing.

abstract: The safe and efficient execution of underwater operations in professional diving depends critically on accurate decompression modeling and real-time environmental adaptability. Existing decompression schedules often rely on simplified physiological assumptions, leading to inherent risks of decompression sickness (DCS) in dynamic or unpredictable conditions. This project seeks to advance diver safety by developing high-resolution computational models of inert gas exchange across heterogeneous tissue compartments under variable depth, temperature, and exertion scenarios. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement parallelized finite element simulations to solve coupled partial differential equations governing gas diffusion and perfusion, integrating real-world dive profiles from wearable sensor datasets. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize decompression strategies under constrained timeframes. The computational demands of resolving micron-scale tissue gradients and iterating across millions of parameter combinations necessitate cluster-scale processing capabilities. Expected outcomes include validated decompression algorithms that reduce DCS incidence by ≥30% in test cohorts, probabilistic risk assessment frameworks for dive planning systems, and open-source tools for adaptive decompression table generation. This research directly supports the program’s mission to enhance diving safety protocols while providing trainees with data-driven insights into human physiology under hyperbaric conditions. The proposed models will furthermore serve as foundational components for future work in emergency ascent planning and equipment design validation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as professional deep-water or scuba divers, diving instructors, or diving support personnel. Includes instruction in the use of diving equipment and related specialized gear; diving safety procedures; operation and maintenance of underwater life-support systems; underwater communication systems; decompression systems; underwater salvage; exploration, rescue, and photography; and installation and fitting of underwater mechanical systems and their maintenance, repair or demolition.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing school-based counseling interventions for improving academic engagement and socio-emotional outcomes in adolescents. A critical challenge in educational psychology is understanding how multi-level factors—such as individual cognitive-behavioral traits, peer networks, and school climate—interact to mediate the efficacy of counseling strategies. Traditional statistical methods struggle to model these dynamic, nonlinear relationships within large, longitudinal datasets. We propose a computational approach integrating (1) multilevel agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate student interactions within virtual learning environments and (2) machine learning analysis of real-world data from 15 K-12 schools, including academic records, counseling session logs, and ecological momentary assessments. The ABM component will require parallelized simulations to test how variations in counseling delivery modes (e.g., group vs. individual sessions) and timing affect emergent outcomes across diverse student populations. Concurrently, transformer-based NLP models will process qualitative data from counselor notes to identify linguistic markers predictive of intervention success. HPC resources are essential for managing the computational load of these large-scale simulations and deep learning workflows, which involve high-dimensional data (n > 10,000 students) and iterative parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for personalizing counseling approaches based on student profiles and contextual factors, as well as actionable insights into resource allocation for school mental health programs. This work aligns with educational psychology’s focus on evidence-based practice by bridging computational social science with applied counseling research, offering scalable tools to enhance student support systems without clinical intervention. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and partnerships with school districts to promote equitable access to adaptive counseling resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the evolutionary and ecological dynamics of ancient ecosystems through computational paleontology. A central challenge in paleobiological research lies in integrating large, heterogeneous datasets—including fossil occurrence records, geochemical proxies, and stratigraphic data—to model species interactions, biogeographic patterns, and responses to environmental perturbations across deep time. Current computational limitations restrict the scalability of probabilistic models and simulations, particularly when analyzing high-resolution, continent-scale datasets spanning millions of years. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-tiered computational approach. First, Bayesian hierarchical models will be implemented to quantify uncertainties in fossil preservation biases and temporal correlations among extinction events. Second, agent-based simulations will reconstruct paleocommunity dynamics under varying climatic and tectonic scenarios, parameterized by geochemical and lithostratigraphic data. These simulations will integrate GPU-accelerated algorithms to handle complex spatial interactions among species and abiotic factors. Third, machine learning workflows will classify microfossil assemblages from 3D µCT scan datasets, automating taxonomic identifications while accounting for taphonomic distortion. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce runtime for iterative model testing, and support high-dimensional visualization of paleoecological networks. Anticipated outcomes include novel frameworks for quantifying extinction selectivity in mass extinction intervals, spatially explicit models of Mesozoic vertebrate dispersal, and open-source tools for microfossil data processing. By resolving computational bottlenecks, this work will advance predictive capacity for ecosystem resilience under anthropogenic climate change while establishing scalable methods for synthesizing paleontological and geological data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of extinct life forms and associated fossil remains, and the reconstruction and analysis of ancient life forms, ecosystems, and geologic processes. Includes instruction in sedimentation and fossilization processes, fossil chemistry, evolutionary biology, paleoecology, paleoclimatology, trace fossils, micropaleontology, invertebrate paleontology, vertebrate paleontology, paleobotany, field research methods, and laboratory research and conservation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in high-resolution digital platemaking workflows, which face growing computational demands as imaging resolutions increase and production timelines shorten. Current workflows in graphic arts and print media—critical to communication and journalism industries—struggle to balance processing speed, color accuracy, and material waste reduction, particularly when scaling to large-format outputs. To resolve these challenges, this research proposes the development of an adaptive, machine learning-driven optimization framework for platemaking and direct-to-plate imaging processes. The framework will integrate high-fidelity simulations of ink dispersion, substrate interactions, and raster image processor (RIP) algorithms to predict and correct imaging artifacts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (historical print jobs, material test results, and sensor data from imaging hardware) and to run Monte Carlo simulations assessing probabilistic outcomes under variable press conditions. Parallelized workflows will be designed to reduce latency in preprocessing steps, such as trapping and imposition, while GPU-accelerated rendering will optimize high-bit-depth image conversion. Expected outcomes include a 30–50% reduction in computational bottlenecks during plate rasterization, improved dynamic color calibration models for diverse substrates, and predictive tools to minimize ink overuse. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish scalable, sustainable workflows for next-generation digital platemaking, directly benefiting academic programs training professionals in communication technologies and journalism production. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for educational use and partnerships with industry stakeholders to bridge gaps between academic research and real-world graphic arts applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare film, digital data, and surfaces to reproduce printed or graphic images. Includes instruction in platemaking, stripping, camerawork, imposition, digital imaging, computer direct-to-plate and direct-to-press, and related processes.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between cultural narratives, collective memory, and the evolution of sports fandom through advanced computational modeling. The central problem lies in understanding how large-scale sociocultural dynamics—such as shifting gender norms, regional identity formation, and transgenerational storytelling—shape fan engagement patterns across different sports ecosystems. While qualitative studies have explored isolated aspects of sports culture, there remains a critical gap in quantitatively modeling these multidimensional interactions at population scales over decadal timeframes. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) frameworks enhanced with natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze historical sports media archives (1940-present), fan-generated content, and demographic datasets. High-performance computing resources are essential for constructing parallelized simulations that incorporate 1) neural language models trained on 80+ years of sports journalism, 2) spatial-temporal analyses of regional affiliation networks, and 3) dynamic belief systems reflecting evolving cultural values. The computational architecture will enable parameter sweeps across diverse historical contexts while maintaining fine-grained representations of individual and community-level decision-making processes. Expected outcomes include the development of novel metrics for measuring cultural inertia in sports traditions, predictive models of fandom migration during societal upheavals, and visualizations of narrative propagation pathways through fan communities. By creating the first computational framework that bridges historical sociology with sports studies, this work aims to provide athletic organizations and cultural institutions with evidence-based strategies for navigating rapidly changing landscapes of community engagement. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale text corpus analysis, and multi-agent simulation environments requiring petascale storage and high-memory nodes.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological, sociological, and historical aspects of sport and physical activity. Includes instruction in theory of sport, sport psychology, sport in American society, gender and race/ethnicity and sport, and sports history.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze diachronic and synchronic linguistic variations across Portuguese dialects, with a focus on the divergence between Metropolitan Portuguese and Luso-Brazilian Portuguese. While prior studies have cataloged phonological, morphological, and syntactic differences, the computational demands of processing large-scale textual corpora—spanning historical manuscripts, modern literature, and digital communication—have limited comprehensive modeling of language evolution and regional differentiation. Our interdisciplinary approach combines corpus linguistics, machine learning, and phylogenetic methods to reconstruct linguistic change across time and geography. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models on heterogenous textual data (15th–21st centuries), implementing parallelized alignment algorithms for dialect comparison, and simulating language contact scenarios through agent-based models. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including digitized colonial archives, sociolinguistic interviews, and web-scraped contemporary texts, while mitigating memory constraints in gradient boosting classifiers for dialect identification. Expected outcomes include a dynamically annotated corpus with diachronic metadata, probabilistic maps of dialectal boundaries, and open-source tools for Portuguese philological analysis. These resources will advance understanding of Lusophone language diversification, particularly the role of sociopolitical factors in shaping Luso-Brazilian innovations, while providing methodological frameworks applicable to under-resourced languages. The project directly supports pedagogical initiatives in Portuguese linguistics and enhances computational humanities capacity within Lusophone studies, with potential applications in NLP tool development for regional dialects. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with traditional philological expertise, this work bridges gaps between linguistic theory and data science, offering novel insights into the adaptive trajectories of Portuguese in global contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Portuguese language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Metropolitan Portuguese; Luso-Brazilian Portuguese; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Hindi linguistics, with a focus on analyzing dialectal variations, historical text corpora, and sociolinguistic patterns across Hindi and its related dialects. A key challenge in Hindi language studies is the lack of scalable computational tools to process large, heterogeneous datasets—including digitized manuscripts, modern speech corpora, and multilingual code-switched texts—which are critical for understanding linguistic evolution and regional language use. Current methods, limited by conventional computing capacities, struggle to handle the computational complexity of phonetic alignment, syntactic parsing, and semantic modeling across diverse Hindi dialects such as Braj, Awadhi, and Hindustani. This project proposes a multi-stage computational approach combining corpus linguistics, machine learning, and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. First, HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of over 10 terabytes of digitized historical texts and contemporary speech data, using optical character recognition (OCR) refinement and dialect classification models. Second, transformer-based architectures will be trained to detect syntactic and semantic shifts between early modern Hindi (e.g., Bhakti-era literature) and present-day formal/informal registers, with attention to code-switching phenomena in urban contexts. Third, geospatial modeling of dialect features will be conducted to map linguistic convergence zones and sociolinguistic influences. The computational workflows will utilize frameworks like Apache Spark for distributed text processing and PyTorch for deep learning tasks. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, computationally annotated corpus of cross-dialectal Hindi texts, a suite of NLP tools optimized for under-resourced Indian languages, and empirical insights into the impact of technological adoption on Hindi’s lexical modernization. These resources will directly support pedagogical innovations in Hindi language programs and provide foundational data for policy-making in language preservation. The project underscores the transformative role of HPC in addressing methodological gaps in non-English linguistic research, with implications for computational humanities scholarship broadly.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hindi language, antecessors, and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Hindi; Hindustani; related dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Construction projects are complex systems influenced by dynamic variables such as weather patterns, supply chain disruptions, labor availability, and regulatory constraints. Traditional project management tools often fail to account for the interdependencies and stochastic nature of these factors, leading to cost overruns, delays, and suboptimal resource allocation. This research proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to model construction project workflows under uncertainty, integrating real-time data streams with predictive analytics to optimize scheduling, risk mitigation, and sustainability outcomes. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute agent-based simulations of construction site operations, machine learning algorithms for delay prediction, and multi-objective optimization techniques to balance competing priorities across cost, time, and environmental impact. Key computational challenges include processing heterogeneous datasets from IoT sensors, historical project records, and climate models while maintaining the temporal granularity required for actionable insights. The research will implement parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify systemic risks and evaluate mitigation strategies across thousands of simulated project scenarios. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that dynamically updates resource allocation plans based on evolving site conditions, probabilistic completion timelines, and carbon footprint projections. By bridging computational science with construction management practices, this work aims to establish new methodologies for adaptive project governance in the context of climate change and global supply chain volatility. The HPC infrastructure is critical for achieving the necessary scale and speed to model multi-year projects with hourly resolution, enabling practitioners to test interventions in silico before implementation. This interdisciplinary approach advances both computational capabilities in business operations and the practical application of digital twin technologies in construction ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: The integration of variable renewable energy sources into modern power grids presents a critical challenge for achieving decarbonization targets while maintaining grid stability. Existing energy system models often lack the granularity to capture real-time interactions between distributed generation, storage technologies, and demand-side flexibility across multiple temporal and spatial scales. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize hybrid energy systems under uncertainty, focusing on the dynamic co-design of grid architectures and distributed control strategies. The research will employ multi-physics simulations combining power flow analysis, electrochemical storage degradation models, and stochastic weather-driven generation profiles at unprecedented resolution. Machine learning techniques will be embedded within traditional optimization paradigms to create adaptive decision-making algorithms capable of handling nonlinear system responses and partial observability conditions. The computational workflow leverages parallelized Monte Carlo methods for robustness testing across thousands of scenario permutations, requiring access to high-performance computing resources for both training surrogate models and executing large-scale sensitivity analyses. Key innovations include a novel graph neural network architecture for predicting cascading failure risks in meshed microgrid topologies and a hybrid quantum-classical optimization approach for storage dispatch scheduling. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for designing resilient multi-energy networks, validated against real-world data from partner utilities. The resulting open-source computational tools will directly support the transition to renewable-dominant grids by enabling system operators to evaluate complex tradeoffs between infrastructure investments, operational costs, and reliability metrics. This work bridges critical gaps in energy systems engineering through its unique combination of artificial intelligence, quantum-inspired algorithms, and high-resolution physical modeling at the grid edge.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of energy generation, storage, conversion, and distribution systems. Includes instruction in conventional and alternative/renewable energy systems, electrical power systems, and electrical system design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance three-dimensional modeling and simulation of complex anatomical structures in domestic and livestock species, with a focus on bridging structural analysis to functional and pathological insights. A critical challenge in veterinary anatomy is the integration of multiscale imaging data—from electron microscopy and micro-CT scans to histology and molecular imaging—into dynamic, predictive models that account for interspecies variability. Existing tools struggle to process these heterogeneous, high-resolution datasets efficiently, limiting the ability to simulate physiological behaviors or disease progression in silico. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining image segmentation, finite element analysis, and machine learning to model tissue biomechanics, neural pathways, and vascular networks in species such as equine and bovine. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, GPU-accelerated rendering of organ systems, and large-parameter-space simulations of biomechanical stress, electrophysiological activity, and fluid dynamics under pathological conditions (e.g., osteoarthritis, neuromuscular disorders). Key outcomes include species-specific digital twins of musculoskeletal and nervous systems, validated against experimental data from cadaveric studies and clinical cases. These models will provide a platform for testing hypotheses about structural adaptations, optimizing surgical interventions, and predicting therapeutic responses. The resource allocation will directly support training in computational anatomy for veterinary researchers, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between anatomists, data scientists, and clinicians. By enhancing the resolution and predictive power of anatomical models, this work aims to transform diagnostic and educational tools in veterinary medicine while advancing foundational knowledge of interspecies morphological diversity.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of small and large animal cellular, organ, tissue, and body systems and their relation to physiologic function, disease, and therapeutic treatment. Includes instruction in histology, ultrastructure, molecular biology, biochemistry, developmental biology, neuroscience, electrophysiology, electron microscopy, computer imaging, and applications to specific species.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational modeling of American Sign Language (ASL) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the language’s complex spatial, temporal, and grammatical structures. While ASL is a fully realized natural language with distinct syntax and morphology, computational tools for processing it remain underdeveloped compared to those for spoken languages. Existing methods struggle to capture the simultaneous integration of manual parameters (handshape, movement, location) and non-manual markers (facial expressions, body posture) that define ASL linguistics. This limitation hinders advancements in machine translation, educational technologies, and automated linguistic analysis for ASL. To bridge this gap, our research employs deep learning architectures, including 3D convolutional neural networks (3D-CNNs) and transformer-based models, to process video datasets of native ASL discourse. These models will be trained to segment and classify phonological, morphological, and syntactic features while preserving the temporal coherence of signing sequences. HPC resources are essential for handling the computational intensity of processing high-resolution video data (at 60+ fps) and optimizing models through hyperparameter tuning across multi-GPU environments. Additionally, we will implement parallelized pipelines for large-scale corpus analysis, leveraging annotated ASL datasets from collaborative partnerships with Deaf community organizations. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for granular ASL feature extraction, benchmarks for evaluating sign language processing models, and open-source tools to support future research in ASL computational linguistics. This work will directly contribute to equitable language technologies for Deaf users and advance theoretical understanding of visuo-gestural language structures through data-driven methodologies. By aligning computational approaches with ASL’s unique linguistic properties, the project aims to set new standards for interdisciplinary sign language research in the digital humanities.
