detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on American Sign Language as a communication medium or language skill that is, not elsewhere classified

abstract: School psychologists face increasing demands to address complex, multidimensional student behavioral challenges through evidence-based interventions. However, the dynamic interplay of individual, classroom, and systemic factors influencing intervention efficacy remains poorly understood due to limitations in analyzing high-dimensional, longitudinal datasets with traditional statistical methods. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that identify predictors of successful behavioral interventions in K–12 settings. We will analyze integrated datasets spanning 10 years of anonymized student records (n ≈ 50,000), including behavioral incident reports, academic progress metrics, individualized education program (IEP) outcomes, and community risk factors. Machine learning techniques (e.g., ensemble classifiers, temporal network analysis) will be applied to model how developmental trajectories, classroom climate variables, and intervention timing interact to predict intervention success. Computational demands necessitate parallelized processing for 1) feature selection across 800+ variables, 2) multilevel survival analysis of intervention durability, and 3) agent-based simulations of school-wide behavioral support strategies. The HPC environment is critical for handling memory-intensive operations involving sparse data imputation, cross-validation of complex models, and real-time sensitivity analyses across hypothetical scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework to guide resource allocation for at-risk students, optimized timelines for deploying tiered behavioral supports, and actionable insights into systemic barriers affecting intervention scalability. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for school psychologists to simulate intervention impacts within local contexts. This work advances data-driven decision-making in educational settings while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for student privacy. By clarifying mechanisms underlying effective supports, the project aims to reduce disparities in behavioral health service access and improve scalability of evidence-based practices in under-resourced schools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and synthesizing immersive, large-scale soundscapes that integrate real-time audience interaction and adaptive algorithmic composition. The core research problem lies in the limitations of conventional computing systems to process high-dimensional acoustic data and machine learning models simultaneously, which restricts the complexity and responsiveness of interactive sound art installations. Current tools struggle to manage multichannel spatial audio rendering, dynamic timbral manipulation, and low-latency feedback loops required for participatory performances. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized neural networks for real-time sound synthesis and analysis, coupled with distributed acoustic simulation engines. The computational approach will involve training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on culturally diverse sound archives to produce adaptive sonic material, while graph-based algorithms will map audience biometric inputs (e.g., motion tracking, physiological sensors) to parametric composition systems. Containerized workflows will enable scalable deployment across HPC nodes, with Kubernetes orchestration managing real-time audio processing pipelines. Expected outcomes include a novel software toolkit for spatial sound design, validated through public installations at three international festivals, and a corpus of computational models that reveal new relationships between cultural sound practices and emergent AI-generated music structures. The research will advance methodologies for distributed computing in live performance contexts while establishing benchmarks for latency-sensitive audio processing in artistic applications. By overcoming current technical barriers, this project aims to expand the scope of sound art as a participatory, culturally reflexive medium and provide performative frameworks that bridge algorithmic composition with embodied listening experiences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on sound as a form of cultural expression, and its relationship to other disciplines such as computer programming, performance, and video. Includes instruction in acoustics; arranging, composing, and editing music; music theory; musicology; orchestration and scoring; and sound design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets commonly encountered in applied settings such as public health monitoring, environmental risk assessment, and precision medicine. The research problem centers on addressing computational bottlenecks in Bayesian hierarchical modeling and non-parametric regression when applied to massive datasets with complex spatial-temporal dependencies. Traditional implementations of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling and Gaussian process regression become computationally intractable at scale due to O(n³) time complexity, limiting their utility for modern applied statistics challenges. To overcome these barriers, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining (1) stochastic variational inference algorithms optimized for distributed-memory architectures, (2) low-rank covariance approximations implemented via parallelized linear algebra routines, and (3) multi-stage subsampling techniques validated through empirical process theory. The implementation will leverage MPI-based parallelism for large-scale parameter space exploration and GPU acceleration for core linear algebra operations. Our methodology will be tested on three applied case studies: modeling multi-city air pollution-health outcome relationships (n ≈ 10⁸ observations), genomic variant effect estimation with electronic health record data (p ≈ 10⁶ features), and real-time anomaly detection in smart grid sensor networks. Successful completion will produce open-source R/Python packages implementing the optimized algorithms, along with rigorous theoretical guarantees on approximation-error bounds. The requested high-performance computing resources are essential for benchmarking scaling performance across 100-10,000 CPU cores, validating statistical properties through large-scale simulation studies (>1M Monte Carlo replicates), and maintaining reproducible workflows for petabyte-scale applied analyses. Outcomes will directly enhance the capacity of applied statisticians to implement sophisticated models on real-world data while maintaining computational feasibility, particularly in resource-constrained domains such as local public health agencies and environmental monitoring programs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding and treatment of acquired communication disorders resulting from neurodegenerative conditions, with a focus on primary progressive aphasia (PPA). PPA is characterized by the gradual deterioration of language networks, yet the neurocomputational mechanisms driving its heterogeneous subtypes remain poorly quantified. Current clinical assessments lack the granularity to capture subtle, dynamic changes in neural-linguistic interactions, limiting personalized intervention strategies. To address this, we propose a multimodal computational framework integrating high-resolution functional MRI (fMRI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and real-time speech acoustics data from PPA patients. The core innovation lies in developing biophysically grounded neural network models that simulate cortico-subcortical interactions during language tasks, calibrated against patient-specific neuroimaging and behavioral data. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale parameter sweeps across these models, optimizing them via genetic algorithms, and performing probabilistic tractography on terabyte-scale DTI datasets. Machine learning pipelines will then identify subtype-specific biomarkers predictive of disease trajectory and treatment responsiveness. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible computational atlas mapping language network degradation patterns across PPA subtypes, (2) an open-source toolkit for simulating intervention effects on neural dynamics, and (3) clinically actionable metrics for tailoring neuromodulation protocols. By bridging computational neuroscience with speech-language pathology, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift from symptom management to mechanism-targeted therapies in neurodegenerative communication disorders. The scale of data integration and model complexity necessitates the parallel processing capabilities, GPU acceleration, and large-memory nodes uniquely afforded by HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate the speaking, language interpretation, and related physiological and cognitive capabilities of children and/or adults and develop treatment and rehabilitative solutions in consultation with clinicians and educators. Includes instruction in the anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing, biomechanics of swallowing and vocal articulation, communications disorders, psychology of auditory function and cognitive communication, language assessment and diagnostic techniques, and rehabilitative and management therapies.

abstract: Periodontal diseases, including gingivitis and periodontitis, represent a major global health burden with complex etiologies involving microbial, immune, and genetic interactions. Current clinical approaches to diagnosis, risk stratification, and implant integration lack precision due to incomplete understanding of these multifactorial dynamics. This project proposes to develop multiscale computational models to unravel the systems-level mechanisms driving periodontal disease progression and implant failure. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to simulate microbial biofilm-host immune interactions at cellular resolution, model biomechanical stress distributions in peri-implant bone under diverse occlusal loads, and analyze multi-omics datasets from longitudinal patient cohorts. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling of polymicrobial communities, finite element analysis of bone-implant interfaces, and machine learning integration of genomic, proteomic, and clinical data. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated architectures to achieve biologically relevant timescales for biofilm development and immune response cascades. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk biofilm compositions, optimized implant design parameters to minimize microfracture risk, and machine learning classifiers for early detection of progressive bone loss. These results will advance personalized treatment strategies and inform next-generation implant materials. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source tools for the dental research community. By bridging clinical observations with mechanistic simulations, this work addresses critical gaps in translating basic periodontal research into precision clinical interventions, with potential to improve long-term outcomes for 500 million patients affected by severe periodontitis worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, and in the placement and maintenance of dental implants.

abstract: The development of programmable nanoscale metamaterials with dynamically reconfigurable electromagnetic properties presents a critical challenge in next-generation photonic engineering. Current design paradigms struggle to reconcile real-time tunability with the quantum-confinement effects dominant at sub-100nm feature sizes, particularly under operational thermal and mechanical stresses. This project proposes a multiscale computational strategy to optimize transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures integrated with phase-change alloys, targeting actively controllable optical responses in the near-infrared spectrum. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will couple time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations for electron-phonon interactions with macroscopic finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations, creating a bidirectional feedback loop between atomic-scale phenomena and device-level performance. Machine learning surrogates trained on these multiscale datasets will accelerate the exploration of 10^5+ geometric and compositional permutations while maintaining quantum mechanical accuracy. Key innovations include the development of strain-aware pseudopotentials for deformed monolayer systems and probabilistic models predicting metastable phase distributions in confined geometries. Success metrics will focus on achieving >90% correlation between simulated and experimental extinction spectra for prototype devices, alongside the identification of three novel material combinations demonstrating >40% optical modulation depth at telecommunications wavelengths. The resulting computational framework will establish fundamental principles for engineering light-matter interactions in dynamically reconfigurable nanoarchitectures, with applications ranging from adaptive optical coatings to ultracompact beam steering components. By open-sourcing optimized simulation workflows and curated training datasets, this work aims to catalyze cross-disciplinary advances in nanophotonic system design while addressing critical gaps in predictive modeling capabilities for quantum-scale metamaterial engineering.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the engineering of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across engineering disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Medical Family Therapy (MFT) by modeling complex interactions between chronic illness, family dynamics, and therapeutic outcomes. Current research in MFT faces limitations in analyzing large-scale, multi-level datasets that capture biological, psychological, relational, and sociocultural variables. Traditional statistical tools struggle to account for the nonlinear, interdependent nature of these systems, hindering efforts to predict long-term health outcomes or optimize family-centered interventions. This study proposes a computational approach integrating systems science, machine learning (ML), and multilevel modeling to address these gaps. Using anonymized electronic health records, longitudinal patient-reported outcomes, and coded therapy session data, we will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate family-illness interactions under varying therapeutic scenarios. ML algorithms will identify predictive patterns in treatment adherence, emotional distress, and relational resilience, while Bayesian network analysis will map causal pathways linking systemic factors to health outcomes. HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets, training ML models with cross-validation, and running large-scale ABM simulations to test intervention efficacy. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for modeling family-illness systems, (2) predictive tools to personalize therapy plans based on family dynamics, and (3) actionable insights into how cultural, spiritual, and relational variables mediate chronic disease management. This work will directly inform clinical training programs and enhance the precision of systemic interventions for families navigating complex health challenges. By bridging computational methods with MFT’s humanistic focus, the project aims to establish scalable, evidence-based strategies that improve holistic care for medically vulnerable populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with patients and their families who are experiencing emotional, physical, relational and spiritual difficulties related to acute and chronic illnesses. Includes instruction in cultural context, ethics, family dynamics, family therapy, gender, human development, marriage counseling, psychopathology, research design and methods, sexuality, and systems thinking.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Danish dialectology and philology, addressing critical gaps in the digital analysis of regional language variation and historical linguistic change. While Danish has a rich dialectal diversity documented across centuries, large-scale computational studies remain limited due to fragmented textual corpora, the complexity of phonological and syntactic patterns, and the lack of interoperable tools tailored to Danish. The research problem centers on the need for scalable methods to process, annotate, and model multi-register texts (e.g., historical manuscripts, modern speech transcripts, and sociolectal data) to trace linguistic evolution and dialect boundaries. The project will employ NLP techniques, including transformer-based models for syntactic parsing and dialect classification, alongside phonetic alignment algorithms to map sound shifts across time and space. Computational philology methods will be applied to digitized archival materials, using OCR correction pipelines optimized for older Danish orthography. A key innovation involves training a language model on diachronic and dialectal corpora to simulate syntactic change and contact influences. HPC resources are essential for handling the volume of data (20+ terabytes of text and audio), parallelizing computationally intensive tasks like neural machine translation of historical texts, and enabling high-resolution geospatial modeling of dialect features. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible, annotated corpus of Danish dialects spanning 1600–present; (2) probabilistic maps of dialect convergence zones; (3) open-source tools for philological analysis of Nordic languages; and (4) novel insights into language standardization processes. The results will directly benefit language preservation initiatives, inform policy on minority dialects, and provide a framework for computational humanities research in under-resourced languages. By integrating advanced computing with Danish linguistics, this project aims to redefine methodological paradigms in Scandinavian studies while strengthening Denmark’s digital cultural heritage infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Danish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic stressors, including nutrient pollution, climate change, and invasive species, yet predicting their ecological responses remains a critical challenge in limnology. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to simulate multi-trophic interactions and emergent ecosystem dynamics in temperate lakes under varying disturbance regimes. The research combines long-term limnological datasets (water chemistry, plankton communities, fish populations) with spatially explicit environmental data to parameterize agent-based models (ABMs) and hydrodynamic-biogeochemical models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex feedbacks among physical lake processes (e.g., stratification, nutrient mixing), species behavior (e.g., predator-prey dynamics, algal bloom formation), and stochastic disturbance events (e.g., heatwaves, pollutant pulses). Parallelized simulations will assess how biodiversity loss and shifting thermal regimes alter ecosystem stability across gradients of lake depth, trophic status, and connectivity. Machine learning workflows will further identify early warning signals of regime shifts from multidimensional output data. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into resilience thresholds for keystone aquatic species, spatially resolved projections of habitat suitability under climate scenarios, and scalable methods to prioritize lakes for conservation interventions. By bridging ecological theory with computational scalability, this work will advance predictive capacity for freshwater resource management while addressing fundamental questions in aquatic community ecology. The requested allocation supports iterative model calibration, large ensemble simulations (>10,000 core-hours), and high-dimensional data synthesis, enabling novel analyses of cross-scale interactions that cannot be feasibly studied through empirical approaches alone.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the diagnosis and mechanistic understanding of complex neurological disorders, including epilepsy, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and peripheral neuropathies, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal electrophysiological datasets. Current clinical neurophysiology workflows face challenges in integrating high-density electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and nerve conduction study (NCS) data at scale, particularly when correlating time-sensitive signals with clinical outcomes or identifying subtle, spatially distributed biomarkers. The proposed research will develop computational pipelines to process and model these high-dimensional datasets, enabling the detection of latent patterns indicative of disease progression or treatment response. Key computational methods include adaptive signal processing algorithms to denoise recordings, graph-theoretical network analysis to quantify connectivity aberrations in EEG-derived brain networks, and machine learning models trained on federated datasets to classify neuromuscular dysfunction subtypes from EMG/NCS features. HPC resources will be critical for optimizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer architectures for real-time signal interpretation, conducting large-scale simulations of neurophysiological signal propagation under pathological conditions, and performing Bayesian inference on heterogeneous patient data to predict therapeutic outcomes. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers for early seizure focus localization, a predictive model of motor neuron degeneration kinetics in ALS, and an open-source toolkit for automated, integrative analysis of clinical neurophysiology data. By addressing computational bottlenecks in signal processing and multimodal integration, this work will enhance the translational utility of electrophysiological testing, support personalized therapeutic strategies, and provide a scalable framework for future studies in neurodiagnostics. The requested resources will directly enable the handling of petabyte-scale datasets and the development of clinically actionable tools to improve patient outcomes in refractory neurological disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous system disorders using a combination of clinical evaluation and electrophysiologic testing such as electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and nerve conduction studies (NCS).

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to optimize quality control processes in advanced manufacturing systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive analytics. Current quality assurance methods face challenges in efficiently analyzing high-dimensional, real-time data from multi-sensor production environments, particularly when detecting subtle defect patterns or predicting process deviations in complex materials and components. The research will integrate machine learning (ML) models with physics-based simulations to create a hybrid quality prediction system. Computational workflows will process heterogeneous data streams—including thermal imaging, vibrational spectra, and in-line metrology—using parallelized feature extraction algorithms. Finite element analysis simulations of stress distributions and microstructural evolution will be scaled across HPC nodes to correlate material behaviors with sensor-derived quality metrics. A reinforcement learning architecture will then iteratively optimize inspection protocols by balancing computational costs, measurement accuracy, and production throughput constraints. The HPC infrastructure will enable training of ensemble ML models on terabyte-scale historical defect datasets while maintaining low-latency inference for real-time process adjustments. Expected outcomes include a 30–50% reduction in computational overhead for multivariate statistical process control compared to conventional methods, along with improved early detection rates (>15% sensitivity gain) for submicron-scale defects in additive manufacturing applications. The resulting open-source framework will provide manufacturers with adaptive quality control templates that automatically adjust to evolving production parameters, material properties, and tolerance requirements. By bridging data-intensive quality metrics with HPC-driven analytics, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for precision manufacturing while reducing waste in high-value component production.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in maintaining consistent manufacturing and construction standards. Includes instruction in quality control systems management principles, technical standards applicable to specific engineering and manufacturing projects, testing procedures, inspection procedures, related instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the integration of generative design algorithms with high-fidelity simulation tools in drafting and design applications. A critical challenge in computer-aided design (CAD) and simulation lies in efficiently balancing computational accuracy with real-time iterative capabilities, particularly for complex systems such as multi-material structures or fluid-structure interaction models. Current workflows often face bottlenecks in processing large-scale parametric datasets, limiting their ability to support adaptive design optimization in resource-constrained environments. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations within an automated design loop. The computational approach will combine distributed-memory parallelism using MPI for macro-scale task distribution with GPU-accelerated solvers for micro-scale simulation components. Machine learning models will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to predict optimal mesh configurations and material properties, reducing redundant computations. Validation will occur through case studies involving aerospace component design and sustainable architectural systems, comparing HPC-optimized results against traditional workstation-based workflows. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in simulation time for high-resolution models, enabling rapid prototyping of designs that meet strict safety and efficiency standards. The project will also produce open-source templates for scalable simulation pipelines tailored to drafting and design education, allowing students to engage with industrial-scale problems. By demonstrating the feasibility of HPC-driven generative design, this work aims to bridge gaps between academic training and industry demands, fostering innovation in applications ranging from energy-efficient manufacturing to resilient infrastructure planning. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the memory-intensive nature of multi-physics simulations and to train predictive models on diverse geometric datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling of complex population dynamics under intersecting social and environmental stressors. Contemporary demographic research faces challenges in simulating large-scale, heterogeneous populations with interdependent behaviors—such as migration responses to climate variability, shifts in fertility patterns amid urbanization, or mortality disparities under healthcare inequities. Existing models often oversimplify spatial, temporal, or social granularity due to computational constraints, limiting their capacity to capture nonlinear feedback loops or policy impacts. This research will develop and calibrate an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrating individual-level decision-making algorithms with spatially explicit environmental and socioeconomic data. The computational approach combines Bayesian inference for parameter estimation, machine learning techniques to harmonize disparate demographic datasets (e.g., satellite-derived migration proxies, health surveys, and census microdata), and parallelized simulations to explore scenario-based outcomes across multiple decades. Key innovations include adaptive network structures to model social influence and a scalable architecture to resolve subnational heterogeneity in low-data regions. By deploying this framework on HPC infrastructure, the project will simulate population trajectories under varying policy interventions (e.g., healthcare access expansions, climate adaptation programs) while accounting for uncertainties in demographic rates and behavioral responses. Anticipated outcomes include high-resolution projections of demographic resilience for vulnerable populations, open-source tools for dynamic population modeling, and evidence to optimize resource allocation in public planning. The work addresses critical gaps in demography’s capacity to forecast interconnected social-environmental risks, offering methodological advances for reproducibility and scalability in population studies. Results will directly inform interdisciplinary policy dialogues on equitable adaptation strategies, with applications to national statistical agencies and international development organizations.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of population models and population phenomena, and related problems of social structure and behavior. Includes instruction in population growth, spatial distribution, mortality and fertility factors, migration, dynamic population modeling, population estimation and projection, mathematical and statistical analysis of population data, population policy studies, and applications to problems in economics and government planning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model multi-scale biological systems with dynamic, non-linear interactions that are intractable with conventional methods. The research problem centers on understanding how cross-scale feedback—from molecular networks to cellular populations—drives emergent behaviors in microbial communities and host-microbiome systems. Current approaches often isolate biological scales or rely on oversimplified differential equations, limiting their ability to predict system-level outcomes under perturbation. To address this, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, and graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture spatial, temporal, and functional dependencies across scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parallelize ABM simulations across thousands of microbial agents, solve partial differential equations governing metabolite diffusion, and train GNNs on heterogeneous data streams. The computational workflow will leverage MPI for distributed ABM execution, GPU-accelerated solvers for reaction-diffusion equations, and PyTorch for GNN optimization. Validation will utilize published datasets on gut microbiome metabolite exchange and synthetic microbial consortia, with model outputs compared to experimental time-series and spatial distribution data. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in cross-scale coupling that trigger phase transitions in community stability, (2) open-source software for scalable multi-scale integration in biological systems, and (3) predictive models of microbiome dysbiosis mechanisms relevant to chronic inflammatory diseases. By enabling efficient simulation of biological complexity beyond single-scale analyses, this work will advance computational tools for systems biology and provide a template for studying other hierarchically organized biological systems. The requested allocation of 500,000 node-hours on an HPC cluster will support intensive parameter space exploration, sensitivity analyses, and benchmarking against reduced-order models, which are computationally prohibitive on local resources.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_title: Biomathematics, Bioinformatics, and Computational Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biomathematics, bioinformatics, and computational biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into radiologic physics research is critical to addressing challenges in precision radiation therapy and advanced medical imaging. Current limitations in modeling complex radiation interactions with biological tissues and optimizing patient-specific treatment plans hinder the accuracy of dose delivery in radiotherapy and the resolution of diagnostic imaging. This project seeks to leverage HPC resources to develop computational frameworks that enhance the predictive accuracy of radiation transport models, refine image reconstruction algorithms, and enable real-time adaptive treatment planning. The research will focus on two subspecialties: therapeutic radiological physics, through Monte Carlo simulations of photon and particle beam interactions in heterogeneous tissues, and diagnostic radiological physics, via iterative reconstruction of clinical CT and MRI datasets using machine learning (ML)-augmented algorithms. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo dose calculations (using tools like Geant4 and GATE) with deep learning models trained on retrospective patient data to predict optimal beam configurations and mitigate organ-at-risk exposure. For diagnostic imaging, neural networks will be integrated into statistical iterative reconstruction pipelines to reduce noise and artifacts while preserving anatomical detail. The project will validate these models against experimental phantom measurements and clinical outcomes data. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for personalized radiotherapy planning, improved image quality in low-dose protocols, and scalable workflows for adaptive therapy. By addressing computational bottlenecks in stochastic simulations and large-scale image processing, this work aims to advance precision in radiation oncology and diagnostic radiology, directly contributing to reduced treatment toxicity, enhanced early disease detection, and optimized resource utilization in clinical workflows. The requested HPC resources will enable the processing of multi-terabyte imaging datasets and millions of simulated particle histories, which are infeasible with standard laboratory computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on that branch of physics which includes the physical aspects of radiation therapy, radiologic diagnosis, and/or nuclear medicine. Radiologic physicists must specialize in at least one of the three subspecialty areas: therapeutic radiological physics, diagnostic radiological physics, and/or medical nuclear physics.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern graphic communications workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize complex, multi-stage production processes. Traditional methods for managing prepress, press, and postpress operations—such as color calibration, substrate behavior prediction, and workflow scheduling—often rely on iterative physical trials, leading to material waste, energy overuse, and time delays. As digital and hybrid printing technologies expand, the need for predictive computational tools to simulate interactions between inks, substrates, and dynamic press conditions has grown. This research will develop physics-informed machine learning models to predict outcomes across diverse printing methods, including offset lithography, flexography, and digital inkjet systems. High-fidelity fluid dynamics simulations will analyze ink dispersion and drying behaviors under variable environmental conditions, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize job scheduling in multi-device production environments. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of high-resolution image data (e.g., spectral reflectance maps, 3D substrate textures) and real-time parameter adjustments across millions of iterative scenarios. Access to HPC resources will enable the training of neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of historical print job logs, material specifications, and sensor-derived press telemetry. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce substrate waste by 15–25% in trial phases, dynamic calibration protocols for cross-media color consistency, and generative models for automating prepress adjustments in variable-data printing. The project will also produce open-source computational workflows tailored to graphic communications education, allowing students to virtually explore press mechanics and material science principles. By integrating HPC-driven insights into production pipelines, this work aims to advance sustainable practices in the industry while bridging gaps between traditional print methodologies and computationally enabled design-to-production systems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the manufacture and distribution or transmission of graphic communications products. Includes instruction in the prepress, press, and postpress phases of production operations and processes such as offset lithography, flexography, gravure, letterpress, screen printing, foil stamping, digital imaging, and other reproduction methods.

abstract: Osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) is a cornerstone of osteopathic medicine, yet the biomechanical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects remain incompletely characterized. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to simulate the biomechanical interactions of OMT techniques on human tissues and their downstream effects on physiological systems. A key challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous clinical data—including patient-specific imaging, motion capture, electromyography, and electronic health records—into predictive models that account for anatomical variability, tissue viscoelasticity, and neural feedback loops. To achieve this, we propose a two-phase computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, finite element modeling will simulate the three-dimensional mechanical deformation of musculoskeletal structures during representative OMT protocols, incorporating anisotropic material properties derived from diffusion tensor imaging and ultrasound elastography. Second, machine learning algorithms will analyze longitudinal clinical outcomes data to identify patterns linking specific mechanical inputs to neuroinflammatory modulation and autonomic nervous system responses. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities for iterative parameter optimization in finite element simulations (estimated at 10⁶ core-hours) and GPU acceleration for training deep neural networks on multimodal datasets (>50 TB). Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models quantifying force transmission pathways during OMT, (2) mechanistic insights into how manual interventions influence systemic biomarkers such as cytokine profiles and heart rate variability, and (3) a computational framework for optimizing OMT protocols based on individual patient characteristics. This research will advance evidence-based practice in osteopathic medicine by establishing quantitative relationships between manual interventions and their clinical effects while demonstrating how HPC resources can catalyze innovation in hands-on therapeutic disciplines. The resulting models and datasets will be made available to the research community through an open-access portal, fostering collaborative investigations into osteopathic principles.
cip_definition: Research focused on Osteopathic Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the structural and logical patterns in cross-cultural ethical frameworks using computational text analysis and network modeling. While comparative ethics has traditionally relied on qualitative hermeneutic methods, the scale and complexity of analyzing global philosophical texts—spanning classical Western, Asian, African, and Indigenous traditions—exceeds manual interpretive capacities. Our research problem centers on identifying latent conceptual convergences and divergences in ethical reasoning across these traditions, with a focus on how foundational axioms (e.g., duty, virtue, reciprocity) are contextually operationalized. We propose a two-phase computational approach: first, deploying natural language processing (NLP) tools to parse and annotate a curated corpus of primary texts (n ≈ 10,000 documents across 15 linguistic traditions, machine-translated and manually validated), extracting argumentative structures and semantic relations. Second, we will construct probabilistic graph networks to model how ethical concepts cluster and interact within and between traditions, using Bayesian inference and community detection algorithms. High-performance computing resources are critical for training transformer-based NLP models on low-resource languages present in our corpus and for running large-scale network simulations with adaptive sampling. Expected outcomes include (1) a quantitative typology of ethical systems based on inferential connectivity rather than geographic or historical proximity, (2) open-access tools for computational philosophical analysis, and (3) methodological frameworks for scaling hermeneutic inquiry through human-AI collaboration. By revealing previously underexamined epistemic bridges between traditions, this work aims to reshape debates in global ethics while demonstrating how computational methods can expand the scope of humanistic research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Philosophy, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive decision-support framework for optimizing undersea sensor network configurations in contested maritime environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address dynamic operational constraints. Modern undersea warfare requires rapid integration of heterogeneous data streams—acoustic, environmental, and tactical—to inform sensor deployment, signal processing, and threat-response protocols. However, existing approaches struggle with real-time recalibration under variable oceanographic conditions, adversarial counter-detection tactics, and resource limitations. The proposed research combines agent-based modeling, adversarial machine learning, and multi-objective optimization to simulate contested undersea domains, prioritizing stealth, coverage, and operational endurance. Computational workflows will integrate oceanographic datasets, probabilistic threat models, and mission-specific constraints to generate resilient network topologies. HPC resources are critical for scaling Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of scenario permutations, training neural networks to predict optimal sensor repositioning strategies, and testing counter-adversarial algorithms under high-uncertainty conditions. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for simulating sensor network performance across diverse undersea theaters, validated against historical operational data. This framework aims to reduce decision latency during mission planning by 40-60% compared to manual methods while improving detection avoidance metrics by 25%. By bridging computational game theory, distributed systems design, and maritime operational art, the project addresses a gap in adaptive resource allocation for undersea platforms operating in denied areas. Results will inform next-generation autonomy protocols for unmanned underwater vehicles and contribute to open-source tactical simulation libraries, subject to security review.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, engineering design and military concepts that govern the operational employment of underwater sensors and weapons systems. Includes instruction in acoustics, electrical, and mechanical engineering; mathematics; meteorology; oceanography; physics; operations analysis; human factors; computer science; and robotics.

abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of healthcare data present significant challenges in efficiently managing, analyzing, and securing medical records while adhering to evolving regulatory standards. This project seeks to address the computational limitations hindering the development of advanced predictive models and real-time analytics for large-scale, heterogeneous health datasets. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to design and validate scalable algorithms for integrating structured and unstructured clinical data—including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging data, and genomic information—into unified, privacy-preserving frameworks. The computational approach will involve distributed machine learning techniques optimized for parallel processing, enabling the training of multimodal models to identify patterns in disease progression, treatment efficacy, and population health trends. A key focus will be on implementing federated learning architectures to maintain data security and compliance with HIPAA and GDPR requirements while facilitating cross-institutional collaboration. Additionally, we will develop automated tools for anomaly detection in medical records to improve data quality and reduce errors in clinical decision support systems. The use of GPU-accelerated computing will allow rapid processing of high-dimensional datasets, such as radiomics features and longitudinal patient data, which are infeasible to analyze using conventional infrastructure. Expected outcomes include novel methodologies for real-time data harmonization, enhanced predictive analytics for chronic disease management, and open-source frameworks for secure, interoperable health information systems. This work will directly contribute to improving the scalability and accuracy of medical record technologies, supporting healthcare providers in delivering personalized care and public health agencies in resource allocation. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming memory and processing bottlenecks, enabling iterative model refinement, and validating results across diverse simulated and real-world datasets. Success in this project will advance both academic understanding of health data science and practical applications in clinical settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in creating large-scale, immersive digital artworks that integrate real-time interactivity and dynamic generative systems. The core research problem lies in overcoming the limitations of conventional computing infrastructure, which struggles to process high-resolution visual data, multi-sensor inputs, and machine learning models simultaneously at the scale required for public installations. Current tools for interactive media art often sacrifice complexity or latency, restricting artists’ capacity to explore nuanced audience engagement or intricate algorithmic aesthetics. To bridge this gap, the project proposes a computational workflow combining real-time neural style transfer, physics-based simulations of virtual materials, and distributed rendering across multiple output channels. Custom code will integrate GPU-accelerated inference for vision-based audience tracking (using pose estimation and gesture recognition models) with procedural generation algorithms that adapt visual outputs to participant behavior. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of high-dimensional data streams, reducing latency during multi-user interactions while maintaining 4K-resolution outputs across projection-mapped surfaces. Expected outcomes include a publicly exhibited installation exploring emergent narratives in human-AI collaboration, alongside an open-source framework for scalable interactive art production. This work advances methodological intersections between computational design and media theory, offering new models for resource-intensive creative practices. By demonstrating how HPC can expand the technical and conceptual boundaries of digital art, the project aims to influence both artistic methodologies and interdisciplinary discourse on computational aesthetics, fostering innovation in visual storytelling and participatory media environments.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Fine Arts and Art Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fine arts and art studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for personalized ophthalmic lenses requires advancements in computational modeling to optimize lens design, material performance, and fabrication workflows. Current challenges include simulating complex optical aberrations across diverse patient anatomies, predicting stress distributions in high-index and progressive lenses during surfacing, and optimizing coating durability under real-world conditions. Existing software tools lack the resolution and scalability to model these multi-physics interactions efficiently, particularly when accounting for variable edge thicknesses, material fatigue, or environmental stressors. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to address these limitations through parallelized finite element analysis (FEA), ray-tracing optimization, and machine learning-driven material simulations. The computational workflow will integrate patient-specific corneal topography data, lens material properties, and grinding tool kinematics to predict surface roughness, residual stresses, and optical performance metrics prior to physical fabrication. GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods will simulate light scatter in tinted or coated lenses, while molecular dynamics simulations will evaluate adhesion failure risks in anti-reflective layers. By leveraging HPC resources, the project aims to reduce iterative prototyping cycles by 40–60% and improve lens accuracy to sub-micron tolerances. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for lens durability under impact testing, a parameter optimization library for edge-finishing tools, and open-source computational templates for refractive error correction in irregular corneas. These results will directly enhance the precision of ophthalmic laboratory workflows, reduce material waste, and support the development of next-generation adaptive lenses. The resource allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across 10,000+ anatomical datasets and real-time feedback integration with digital surfacing equipment, establishing a foundation for AI-driven manufacturing in optometric care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of computational imaging, generative artificial intelligence (AI), and large-scale visual data analysis within the visual arts and media studies. A critical challenge in contemporary digital art and design lies in processing and synthesizing ultra-high-resolution visual datasets—such as 3D-scanned cultural artifacts, multi-spectral imaging of historical artworks, or dynamic simulations of material behaviors—which exceed the capabilities of standard computing infrastructure. Additionally, the development of generative AI models for creating ethically informed, culturally responsive digital art requires iterative training on distributed systems to address computational bottlenecks and ensure reproducibility. This project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining physics-based simulations, neural radiance fields (NeRF) for 3D scene reconstruction, and diffusion-based generative models to explore three interconnected objectives: (1) reconstructing degraded or fragmented visual artworks via inverse rendering techniques, (2) simulating environmentally responsive digital installations in real-time virtual spaces, and (3) training customizable generative models that incorporate artist-driven constraints to mitigate dataset biases. The use of GPU-accelerated nodes and parallelized workflows will enable rapid iteration on terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining fidelity to artistic intent. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for artists working with AI-generated media, novel methodologies for preserving ephemeral digital artworks, and a framework for ethical computational creativity. By integrating HPC into visual arts research, this project aims to bridge technical and creative domains, fostering interdisciplinary collaborations that redefine the role of computation in artistic practice and cultural preservation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the visual and performing arts and that may prepare individuals in any of the visual artistic media or performing disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance Latin language pedagogy by developing a computational framework to analyze and optimize instructional strategies for diverse learning contexts. Despite Latin’s structural complexity and its role in fostering critical linguistic and cultural competencies, many educators lack tools to systematically evaluate the efficacy of curricular materials or student engagement with authentic texts. Traditional manual analysis of student work, such as translations or compositional exercises, is time-intensive and limits scalability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train natural language processing (NLP) models on a corpus of student-generated Latin texts, pedagogical materials, and classical literature. The models will identify patterns in grammatical errors, stylistic development, and contextual comprehension gaps across proficiency levels. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom interactions to test the impact of differentiated instructional approaches on learning outcomes. The computational pipeline will integrate syntactic parsing, semantic analysis, and machine learning classifiers optimized for Latin’s inflectional morphology and limited modern speech data. By automating the detection of pedagogical challenges and simulating intervention strategies, this project aims to generate actionable insights for curriculum design and teacher training. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access toolkit for Latin instructors to analyze student work, predict learning trajectories, and adapt teaching methods. This work bridges computational linguistics and classical language education, offering a scalable method to preserve Latin’s pedagogical relevance while empowering educators with data-driven strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing large textual datasets, training domain-specific models, and iterating simulations efficiently, enabling advancements in both teacher education and classical language pedagogy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach Latin at various grade levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of host-microbe interactions in mucosal immunity using high-performance computing (HPC) to model microbial community behavior and immune response networks. Current experimental approaches struggle to capture the spatial, temporal, and functional complexity of microbial populations in mucosal environments, particularly their bidirectional signaling with host immune cells. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and stochastic simulations to resolve how localized microbial metabolite gradients influence immune cell differentiation and barrier function. Metagenomic and proteomic datasets from murine gut and respiratory tract models will parameterize microbial community structures, while immune receptor-ligand binding kinetics and cytokine diffusion parameters will be derived from time-resolved microscopy and flow cytometry. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 3D mucosal environments at physiologically relevant scales (>10^6 interacting agents), incorporating dynamic host-microbe feedback loops. Key outcomes include predictive models of dysbiosis-induced immune dysregulation and identification of critical microbial taxa or metabolic pathways that stabilize mucosal homeostasis. This work addresses a fundamental gap in understanding how polymicrobial communities collectively modulate immune tolerance or inflammation—a question inaccessible to reductionist experimental systems. By bridging microbial ecology and immunology through scalable computational methods, the project will provide mechanistic insights into diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and asthma, while establishing an open-source simulation platform for hypothesis-driven microbial immunology research. The requested resources are essential to manage memory-intensive simulations and optimize machine learning pipelines for pattern recognition in high-dimensional host-microbe interaction datasets.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the microbiological sciences and immunology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing project efficiency, cost management, and risk mitigation, particularly as projects grow in scale and complexity. Traditional methods for planning and managing multi-phase construction processes—such as structural analysis, material logistics, and labor allocation—often rely on static models that fail to account for dynamic variables like weather disruptions, supply chain variability, and real-time structural performance data. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework for simulating and optimizing construction workflows through high-performance computing (HPC). The research will focus on integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessment, discrete-event simulation for supply chain and labor scheduling, and machine learning models to predict and adapt to real-time project risks. By leveraging HPC resources, the team will execute large-scale parametric studies to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations, including material substitutions, equipment configurations, and regulatory constraints, under varying environmental and operational conditions. Key outcomes will include a validated digital twin platform capable of simulating construction processes at high fidelity, predictive tools for identifying cost and schedule risks, and data-driven recommendations for resilient project designs. The computational demands of this work—particularly the parallel processing requirements for FEA-coupled simulations and the training of deep reinforcement learning models on heterogeneous datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. This research will advance the integration of computational modeling into construction engineering practice, offering a pathway to reduce material waste, improve compliance with safety standards, and enhance the adaptability of construction projects in response to unforeseen disruptions. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools and case studies, providing actionable insights for industry stakeholders and academic researchers focused on smart construction technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools for modeling and synthesizing immersive 3D sound environments, addressing the challenge of creating spatially dynamic audio experiences for interactive media and live performance. While spatial audio technologies have grown in prominence, existing methods for real-time sound propagation modeling and adaptive synthesis remain computationally prohibitive, limiting their accessibility and scalability in artistic applications. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) acoustic simulations, enabling efficient modeling of complex virtual environments with frequency-dependent material absorption and diffraction effects. Concurrently, machine learning frameworks will be implemented to train neural networks on spectral and spatial audio features, optimizing adaptive synthesis algorithms for dynamic listener interactions. The computational workflow will integrate these components into a GPU-accelerated pipeline, validated through case studies in augmented-reality music performance and interactive sound installations. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to overcome latency and fidelity barriers in real-time spatial audio processing, facilitating novel creative workflows for composers and sound designers. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for parametric spatial audio rendering, a dataset of annotated 3D acoustic environments, and performance benchmarks for music-oriented HPC applications. This work bridges computational acoustics and artistic practice, offering scalable solutions for emerging domains such as VR/AR-enhanced performances and AI-driven interactive composition. The resource allocation will directly support graduate student researchers in music technology while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations between performing arts and computational science communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creative aspects of the blending of music and technology; and that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the composition, recording, synthesis, and performance of music; audio-visual production; scoring for film and multimedia; and software and multimedia development. Includes instruction in music theory, music history, composition, acoustics, recording technology, computer composition, electronic music synthesis, technology-based performance, 3D sound and spatial audio, and music business and law.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment outcomes are influenced by complex biomechanical interactions between teeth, periodontal ligaments, and alveolar bone, yet current predictive models lack the resolution to account for individual patient variability. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate orthodontic tooth movement and optimize treatment planning using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on the inability of conventional clinical methods to predict tissue-level biomechanical responses to orthodontic forces, leading to suboptimal treatment timelines and occasional complications such as root resorption. To address this, we will construct patient-specific finite element models derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans, incorporating heterogeneous material properties of dental and periodontal tissues. Multiscale simulations will resolve force distribution at the enamel-dentin interface, ligament deformation, and bone remodeling dynamics under varying orthodontic load scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and retrospective clinical data to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment efficacy. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational burden of 3D biomechanical modeling at micron-scale resolutions, iterative parameter optimization for personalized simulations, and large-scale data integration across 500+ patient cases. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational platform for simulating orthodontic interventions, (2) clinically actionable metrics to customize force application protocols, and (3) predictive models linking anatomical features to treatment duration estimates. This work will advance precision orthodontics by reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice and providing mechanistic insights into tissue adaptation processes. All models and datasets will be made available to the research community through an open-access portal, fostering collaboration in computational dentistry.
cip_definition: Research focused on the principles and techniques involved in the prevention and correction of dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit computational framework to model the impacts of climate change and anthropogenic disturbances on migratory wildlife populations and their habitats in fragmented ecosystems. The research addresses critical gaps in predicting species resilience under dynamic environmental stressors, particularly for wide-ranging ungulates and aquatic species in western North America. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale ecological datasets—including remote sensing imagery, GPS telemetry, climate projections, and land-use change maps—to parameterize agent-based models (ABMs) simulating population dynamics, habitat selection, and connectivity. The computational approach leverages machine learning algorithms to identify nonlinear relationships between environmental covariates and species distributions, coupled with parallelized simulations to explore scenario-based outcomes under varying climate and management regimes. Key challenges requiring HPC include processing terabytes of LiDAR and satellite data, running ensemble projections across heterogeneous landscapes, and optimizing habitat corridor designs via genetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of habitat suitability shifts, vulnerability assessments for priority species like mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and native cutthroat trout (Oncorhynchus clarkii), and evidence-based recommendations for adaptive management of migratory corridors. The project directly supports regional conservation initiatives by state and federal agencies, while advancing computational methods for ecological forecasting. By quantifying trade-offs between development pressures and ecosystem integrity, this work will inform policy decisions under the Endangered Species Act and state wildlife action plans, ultimately enhancing the capacity of natural resource managers to balance biodiversity preservation with human land-use needs in rapidly changing environments.
cip_title: Wildlife, Fish and Wildlands Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conserve and manage wilderness areas and the flora, marine and aquatic life therein, and manage wildlife reservations and zoological/aquarium facilities for recreational, commercial, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in wildlife biology, marine/aquatic biology, environmental science, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, natural resources management and policy, outdoor recreation and parks management, the design and operation of natural and artificial wildlife habitats, applicable law and regulations, and related administrative and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of political communication in digital media ecosystems, with a focus on large-scale social media data and news content. The research problem centers on understanding how algorithmic curation, misinformation propagation, and real-time public opinion shifts interact during electoral campaigns. Traditional methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and complexity of multilingual text, image, and network data generated by platforms like X (Twitter), Facebook, and TikTok, particularly during high-stakes political events. We propose a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling to study (1) the spread of coordinated political narratives across platforms, (2) the relationship between media framing in traditional news outlets and viral social media content, and (3) emergent polarization patterns in electorate engagement. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets spanning 2020-2024 election cycles in three democracies, utilizing transformer-based models fine-tuned for political discourse analysis, dynamic network inference at hourly resolution, and parallelized simulations of information diffusion under varying platform moderation scenarios. Expected outcomes include new computational frameworks for detecting AI-generated political content, quantifying cross-platform narrative alignment, and modeling the temporal cascade of misinformation events. The research will produce open-source tools for political communication scholars and evidence-based insights for policymakers addressing electoral integrity challenges. By enabling analysis at unprecedented scale and speed, HPC resources are critical to capturing the sociotechnical complexity of modern political communication, directly advancing the program’s mission to prepare professionals for evolving media-political landscapes.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human and media communication in the political process and that prepares individuals to function as members of political and public affairs organizations, political campaign staffs, and related government and media entities. Includes instruction in media effects, political speaking and debating, political advertising and marketing, image management, political journalism, opinion polling, and aspects of print and broadcast media related to the production and distribution of media messages in political settings.

abstract: Microbial communities exhibit complex interactions with host immune systems, yet the mechanisms driving pathogen resilience and immune evasion in polymicrobial infections remain poorly understood. This project seeks to investigate how interspecies microbial dynamics influence immune response modulation and contribute to chronic infections, with a focus on Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa co-infections in mucosal environments. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of microbial population dynamics with stochastic simulations of host-pathogen molecular interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model spatial heterogeneity in infection sites, track ligand-receptor binding events across immune cell surfaces, and simulate emergent community behaviors over biologically relevant timescales (days to weeks). The ABM will incorporate experimental data on microbial growth rates, metabolite exchange, and cytokine secretion profiles obtained from in vitro co-culture systems. Parallelized parameter sweeps will evaluate how variations in host neutrophil recruitment efficiency and microbial quorum-sensing cross-talk affect infection outcomes. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in immune cell density required for pathogen clearance, characterizing metabolic cooperation strategies that enhance microbial survival under immune pressure, and predicting temporal windows for effective therapeutic intervention. These computational insights will guide subsequent validation experiments using synthetic microbial consortia and air-liquid interface epithelial cell models. The resource request supports 18 months of large-scale simulations requiring 200,000+ CPU hours for multi-scale parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses. Results will advance fundamental understanding of immune evasion in polymicrobial contexts while providing a predictive framework to optimize antimicrobial stewardship strategies in clinical settings facing rising antibiotic resistance challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the microbiological sciences and immunology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Gerontology research has yet to fully explore how dynamic, multi-sensory environmental stimuli—such as ambient noise, visual complexity, and tactile accessibility—interact with cognitive resilience in older adults, particularly in urban settings. While environmental gerontology emphasizes static features like walkability, the real-time cognitive load imposed by sensory-rich environments remains poorly understood. This project employs high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate real-world sensor data, neuropsychological assessments, and immersive virtual reality (VR) experiments, creating a computational model of environmental cognitive demand. Using federated learning architectures, we will harmonize heterogeneous datasets from wearable devices (measuring physiological stress responses) and VR headset logs (tracking navigational behavior in simulated environments) to train neural networks predicting cognitive fatigue thresholds. Agent-based modeling will simulate population-level interactions between sensory environmental features and individual neurodiversity, accounting for variables like mild cognitive impairment and sensory attenuation. The computational pipeline requires distributed memory parallelism to process high-frequency sensor data (1000+ Hz sampling rates) and GPU-accelerated rendering of VR-derived spatial networks. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of "cognitive load hotspots" in urban infrastructure and personalized thresholds for environmental adaptability, advancing tools for dementia-inclusive urban design. By quantifying the temporal dynamics of environmental interactions, this work pioneers a sensory-informed framework for aging-in-place initiatives, addressing a critical gap in gerontological research. The models will be validated against longitudinal mobility data from community-dwelling older adults, with open-source tools developed to aid policymakers in optimizing public spaces for cognitive diversity. This project establishes a novel intersection of computational neuroscience, environmental psychology, and gerontology, requiring HPC resources to manage its data intensity and model complexity.
