cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences and psychology.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize culinary operations and resource efficiency in commercial kitchens through advanced computational modeling, addressing the challenge of minimizing food waste while maintaining service quality in dynamic hospitality environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), the research will develop predictive models to simulate ingredient utilization patterns, equipment energy consumption, and workforce scheduling under variable demand scenarios. Current industry practices rely on heuristic decision-making, which often leads to inefficiencies in perishable inventory management, inconsistent meal preparation times, and suboptimal labor allocation. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling to replicate kitchen workflows, Monte Carlo simulations to assess supply chain risks, and machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized operational data from partner restaurants. Key objectives include quantifying the impact of menu complexity on waste generation, identifying energy-saving opportunities in multi-oven systems, and creating adaptive staffing models that account for seasonal demand fluctuations. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across heterogeneous datasets encompassing ingredient shelf life, equipment specifications, and customer traffic patterns. Expected outcomes include a decision-support framework capable of recommending real-time adjustments to purchasing orders, equipment usage schedules, and task prioritization during peak service periods. This interdisciplinary work bridges culinary arts, operations research, and computational sustainability, offering novel methodologies for an industry transitioning toward data-driven management. Successful implementation could reduce food waste by 15-25% in test environments while maintaining profitability margins, providing actionable insights for culinary education programs and small-to-medium enterprise restaurant operators. The project establishes a precedent for applying HPC resources to non-traditional domains in hospitality management, demonstrating how computational intensity can address persistent challenges in service-oriented fields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage food and beverage preparation and service operations, restaurant facilities, and catering services.  Includes instruction in food/beverage industry operations, cost control, purchasing and storage, business administration, logistics, personnel management, culinary arts, restaurant and menu planning, executive chef functions, event planning and management, health and safety, insurance, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, cross-channel consumer engagement in digital marketing environments. While businesses increasingly rely on omnichannel strategies to integrate customer interactions across platforms, the computational demands of modeling dynamic, high-dimensional consumer behavior—spanning social media, e-commerce, mobile apps, and IoT touchpoints—exceed the capabilities of conventional systems. Current approaches often rely on siloed analytics or simplified heuristics, limiting their ability to capture nonlinear interactions, temporal dependencies, and context-aware personalization at scale. The proposed work will develop a computational framework combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with large-scale graph neural networks (GNNs) to simulate multi-agent consumer journeys in real time. The model will ingest heterogeneous data streams—including clickstreams, sentiment analysis from natural language processing (NLP), geospatial patterns, and probabilistic attribution data—to predict and optimize micro-moments in customer decision pathways. HPC resources are critical for training ensemble models on terabyte-scale datasets, enabling parallelized hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simulated marketing scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel algorithm for adaptive budget allocation across digital channels, empirically validated against anonymized corporate partner datasets spanning 10M+ user profiles. The research will advance computational marketing by addressing latency and scalability barriers in dynamic campaign orchestration, with potential applications in churn prediction, hyper-personalized content delivery, and ethical AI-driven targeting. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for marketing analytics, reducing barriers to entry for SMEs lacking proprietary HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop a digital marketing plan and integrate marketing, advertising, sales, and logistics across physical and digital channels. Includes instruction in digital marketing, e-commerce, online consumer psychology, search engine optimization, social media marketing, and web analytics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for real-time, high-fidelity media production in radio and television broadcasting by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize workflows and enhance computational efficiency. Current broadcasting workflows struggle with processing large-scale multimedia datasets—such as 4K/8K video, spatial audio, and interactive live-streaming feeds—in real time, particularly when integrating AI-driven tools for automated editing, dynamic content personalization, or immersive augmented reality (AR) overlays. These challenges are compounded by the need to maintain low-latency performance across distributed production teams and heterogeneous devices. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a computational framework that employs parallelized encoding/decoding algorithms, GPU-accelerated machine learning models for content analysis, and distributed network simulations to model broadcast environments. HPC resources will enable large-scale testing of hybrid cloud-edge architectures for live production, simulating variable bandwidth conditions and multi-camera synchronization scenarios. Additionally, the project will develop predictive models to automate resource allocation for rendering and streaming tasks, reducing manual intervention in time-sensitive workflows. Outcomes will include open-source software tools tailored for broadcast engineers, benchmarking data on latency reduction in live productions, and scalable protocols for integrating AI-enhanced post-production tools into existing studio systems. By advancing computational methods for media processing, this work aims to democratize access to high-quality broadcasting technologies for smaller studios and educational institutions, while preparing students to innovate within evolving industry standards for 5G-enabled and AI-augmented media ecosystems. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s terabyte-scale datasets and complex, concurrent simulations of broadcast networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of radio and television programs, and related operations, under the supervision of broadcast and studio managers, directors, editors, and producers. Includes instruction in sound, lighting, and camera operation and maintenance; power and feed control; studio operations; production preparation; broadcast engineering; related computer applications; and specialized applications such as news, entertainment, live talk, sports, commercials, and taping.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of radiation-magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) processes in turbulent, star-forming molecular clouds through high-resolution numerical simulations. Star formation efficiency in galaxies remains poorly constrained by observations and theory, with computational limitations preventing realistic 3D treatments of non-equilibrium radiation transfer, magnetic fields, and supersonic turbulence simultaneously. Current models either simplify radiative processes or neglect magnetic fields, leading to uncertainties in predicted stellar initial mass functions and feedback mechanisms. To address this, we propose to employ the GPU-accelerated code CHOLLA-astro, extended to include implicit radiation transport and anisotropic magnetized turbulence, on high-performance computing systems. The simulations will resolve scales from 0.1 pc down to 0.001 pc across domains spanning 10 pc, capturing the interplay between ionizing UV radiation, magnetic pressure, and compressive turbulence during protostellar collapse. A key innovation involves coupling adaptive ray tracing for radiation sources with a Monte Carlo dust photon transport solver, enabling self-consistent modeling of radiative heating/ionization fronts in magnetized media. Each simulation will require ~2 million node-hours across 3,000+ GPUs to achieve the necessary spatiotemporal resolution over 10^6 timesteps. The resulting datasets will quantify how magnetic resistivity and radiation pressure regulate gas accretion onto protostars—a critical open question in galactic-scale star formation models. Data products will include synthetic ALMA- and JWST-like observations to facilitate direct comparisons with recent surveys of nearby star-forming regions. By establishing scalable workflows for exascale RMHD simulations, this work will enable future studies of galaxy evolution with unprecedented physical fidelity, directly supporting interpretation of multi-messenger astrophysics data from next-generation observatories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and observational study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena. Includes instruction in cosmology, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex legal, economic, and spatial dynamics of real estate and land development regulation. While land use law is a well-established domain, its interaction with rapidly evolving urban growth patterns, climate resilience frameworks, and algorithmic decision-making tools in municipal governance remains understudied from a computational perspective. The core research problem centers on modeling how multi-layered regulatory constraints—including zoning ordinances, environmental impact assessments, and public-private partnership agreements—shape development outcomes in heterogeneous urban landscapes. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between stakeholders (developers, municipal entities, community groups) under varying legal regimes, integrating spatial data layers for parcel-specific restrictions, infrastructure capacity, and environmental risk factors. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze historical permitting decisions and predict bottlenecks in approval workflows, while graph databases will map interdependencies between overlapping regulatory frameworks. Computational legal analytics methods will be developed to parse unstructured text from case law, municipal codes, and environmental review documents, enabling systematic identification of conflicts or ambiguities in policy implementation. Expected outcomes include a scalable simulation framework to evaluate proposed land use reforms, predictive tools for assessing development feasibility under climate adaptation scenarios, and visual analytics dashboards to support equitable policy design. By quantifying the systemic effects of legal structures on urban form, this work aims to advance evidence-based approaches to land governance while establishing computational social science methodologies tailored to legal-technical interfaces in real estate. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing large-scale geospatial datasets, running parallelized policy simulations, and training domain-specific language models to process legal texts at metropolitan scales.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance and failure diagnosis for electromechanical business machines by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced simulation and machine learning models. Current repair methodologies rely heavily on reactive approaches, leading to prolonged machine downtime and high operational costs. To overcome these limitations, this research will integrate multi-physics simulations with sensor data analytics to model wear patterns, component stress, and electrical anomalies in devices such as multifunction printers, mailing systems, and data processing equipment. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate mechanical degradation under operational loads, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model thermal behavior in high-use components. Parallelized machine learning pipelines will process historical repair datasets and real-time telemetry to identify failure precursors, optimizing maintenance schedules. The computational demands of these tasks—including large-scale parameter sweeps for scenario testing and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous sensor data—necessitate HPC infrastructure for efficient execution. Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance frameworks that reduce unplanned downtime by 30–50%, digital twin prototypes for common business machine categories, and open-source diagnostic tools that correlate simulation outputs with empirical repair data. These results will advance technical education in business machine repair by introducing data-driven decision-making into curricula, while providing industry partners with scalable models to extend equipment lifespans. The project’s computational workflows will also serve as a template for integrating HPC resources into vocational technology programs, bridging gaps between traditional hands-on training and modern computational diagnostics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain and repair a variety of office machines, such as typewriters, word processing and dictation machines, calculators, data processing equipment, duplicating machines, and mailing machines. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment, and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of business machines.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct a large-scale computational analysis of thematic and structural patterns in children’s and adolescent literature across historical periods and genres. While scholarship in this field has traditionally relied on qualitative close reading, the growing availability of digitized texts—including novels, picture books, and serialized fiction—enables transformative quantitative approaches. However, the scale and complexity of these datasets, which span centuries and diverse cultural contexts, demand advanced computational tools to identify latent trends, track narrative evolution, and interrogate representations of identity, agency, and societal norms. This research addresses gaps in understanding how children’s literature reflects and shapes cultural values over time, particularly regarding marginalized voices and intersectional perspectives. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic analysis, sentiment detection, and topic modeling, alongside network analysis to map character interactions and plot dynamics. Custom algorithms will be developed to account for multimodal elements in illustrated texts and adapt NLP pipelines to the unique linguistic features of children’s literature, such as simplified syntax and didactic framing. By analyzing a corpus of 50,000+ texts from the 18th century to the present—drawn from open-access repositories and ethically sourced publisher archives—this study will quantify shifts in narrative priorities, genre conventions, and representational equity. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive visualization platform for exploring textual trends, a methodological framework for computational children’s literature studies, and evidence-based insights to inform pedagogical practices, publishing diversity initiatives, and library collection policies. The computational intensity of training domain-specific language models and processing high-resolution image-text pairs necessitates HPC resources for parallelized workloads, large-scale data storage, and GPU-accelerated deep learning. This project bridges humanistic inquiry and computational innovation, advancing both scholarly discourse and professional applications in children’s literary studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scholarly study of children's and adolescent literature and that may enhance the professional work of teachers, librarians, publishers, booksellers, and creative writers. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, studies of various types of literary text, book artists, and children's films.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate fundamental principles governing the coordination of complex biological systems across scales, from molecular interactions to organism-level behaviors, without focusing on specialized subfields. A central challenge in general biology lies in understanding how decentralized processes—such as nutrient distribution in multicellular organisms or collective decision-making in social species—emerge from localized interactions without centralized control. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and network theory simulations to analyze how simple rules at the micro-level give rise to macro-level biological organization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of interacting agents in dynamic environments, parameterize models with empirical data from diverse species, and perform sensitivity analyses across ecological and physiological contexts. The computational framework will integrate stochastic optimization algorithms to identify rule sets that maximize system robustness under environmental perturbations. Expected outcomes include predictive models of self-organization in biological systems, validated against observational datasets on resource allocation in plant colonies and collective motion in invertebrate groups. These insights will advance generalized theories of biological coordination, bridging gaps between organismal and systemic perspectives. The project’s scalable computational tools will be shared as open-source resources to support broader investigations into emergent phenomena across underexplored biological systems, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in basic biological research.
cip_definition: A general program of biology at the introductory, basic level or a program in biology or the biological sciences that is undifferentiated as to title or content. Includes instruction in general biology and programs covering a variety of biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in human sciences communication, focusing on the intersection of family and consumer sciences (FCS) content delivery, digital media dynamics, and audience behavior modeling. The research problem centers on the challenge of optimizing tailored communication strategies for diverse populations in rapidly evolving digital environments. Traditional methods for analyzing audience engagement, content efficacy, and cross-platform information dissemination in FCS contexts lack the computational power to process large-scale multimedia datasets, simulate complex user interaction patterns, or model emergent communication phenomena in real time. The proposed work employs machine learning architectures, natural language processing (NLP), and agent-based modeling to analyze multi-modal communication channels (e.g., interactive educational platforms, social media, and augmented reality tools) used in FCS outreach. Computational workflows will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including textual, visual, and behavioral metrics—to identify patterns in information retention, ethical concerns in persuasive messaging, and cultural variables affecting consumer decision-making. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on curated FCS corpora, running parallelized simulations of community-scale information diffusion, and conducting sensitivity analyses on intervention strategies under varying socioeconomic scenarios. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for adaptive message personalization, predictive models of audience segmentation efficacy, and evidence-based guidelines for mitigating misinformation in human sciences contexts. This work addresses a gap in computationally intensive social systems research while maintaining direct relevance to FCS priorities such as household resource literacy, intergenerational knowledge transfer, and equitable access to consumer education. The results will inform both academic understanding of human sciences communication ecosystems and practical tools for public-facing institutions.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Communication
cip_definition: A program that focuses on communication of human sciences subject matter and related consumer information to a variety of audiences through print and non-print media.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven, computational framework to analyze the efficacy of adaptive language learning tools for English as a Second Language (ESL) learners, with a focus on personalized instruction strategies. A critical challenge in ESL education is optimizing pedagogical interventions for diverse learner populations, particularly in identifying patterns in language acquisition difficulties (e.g., syntactic complexity, phonemic awareness) across varying linguistic backgrounds. Traditional methods lack scalability for large, heterogeneous datasets, limiting insights into individualized learning trajectories. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including speech recordings, written assignments, and interaction logs from digital learning platforms—using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques. Computational models will be trained to classify error types, predict learning bottlenecks, and simulate language development pathways under different instructional conditions. This requires parallelized processing of terabytes of unstructured text and audio data, fine-tuning transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT, Whisper) for ESL-specific tasks, and running iterative simulations to evaluate hypothetical teaching strategies. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for diagnosing learner-specific challenges in real time, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive curriculum design, and (3) open-source tools to help instructors integrate computational analytics into classroom practices. By enabling rapid analysis of cross-cultural and cross-linguistic variables, this work aims to advance precision in ESL pedagogy while reducing instructor workload. The project directly aligns with the program’s mission to innovate teacher training through empirical, technology-enhanced methodologies, with broader implications for equity in language education.
cip_title: Teaching English as a Second or Foreign Language/ ESL Language Instructor
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching English to students who are not proficient in English or who do not speak, read or write English, and that may prepare individuals to function as teachers and administrators in such programs.

abstract: Insect navigation under complex environmental conditions represents a critical yet underexplored area in entomology with implications for pest management, pollination ecology, and bio-inspired robotics. Current models of insect movement lack resolution to predict behaviors in dynamic, multi-stimulus environments, particularly for species exhibiting rapid adaptation to anthropogenic disturbances. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, multi-agent simulation framework to resolve how sensory integration, memory, and environmental heterogeneity collectively shape navigation strategies in flying pollinators and invasive pests. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will parameterize individual-based models with empirical data from field-recorded trajectories, wind tunnel experiments, and neurophysiological studies. Each agent’s decision-making algorithm will integrate real-world geospatial layers (topography, vegetation, urban structures) and stochastic meteorological inputs to simulate population-level movement patterns at landscape scales. Computational challenges include parallelizing agent-environment interactions across 10⁵–10⁶ individuals, optimizing fluid dynamics calculations for low-Reynolds-number flight in turbulent airflow, and implementing machine learning modules to emulate plasticity in odor-guided navigation. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of pest colonization risks under climate variability, identification of sensory bottlenecks in pollinator foraging efficiency, and generalized principles for resilient navigation systems. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—requiring GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time sensory processing tasks and large-memory allocations for 3D environmental matrices—necessitates scalable computing infrastructure. By bridging entomology, complex systems theory, and computational engineering, this work will establish a platform for testing ecological hypotheses inaccessible through traditional experimentation while informing sustainable agricultural practices and conservation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of insect species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of heterogeneous computing architectures—integrating CPUs, GPUs, and emerging accelerators—demands advanced resource allocation strategies to optimize performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. Current approaches often rely on static heuristics or oversimplified models, which fail to adapt to dynamic workloads or exploit hardware diversity effectively. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing adaptive, machine learning-driven resource management frameworks tailored for heterogeneous systems. The research will focus on optimizing task scheduling, memory allocation, and power distribution under varying computational demands, with an emphasis on real-time adaptability and cross-layer hardware-software coordination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate large-scale heterogeneous architectures, train neural network models for predictive allocation, and evaluate performance across diverse benchmarks. Computational methods will include discrete-event simulations, reinforcement learning algorithms, and parallelized Monte Carlo sampling to explore optimization spaces efficiently. The project will also leverage distributed computing frameworks to model multi-node interactions and scalability challenges. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for dynamic workload balancing, energy-aware scheduling policies, and open-source tools to aid hardware-software co-design. These contributions will advance the design of next-generation computing systems, particularly for latency-sensitive applications like autonomous systems and edge computing. By quantifying trade-offs between performance, energy, and thermal constraints, this work aims to establish generalizable principles for resource allocation in heterogeneous environments, bridging gaps between theoretical models and practical implementation. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid prototyping, validation at scale, and reproducibility of results, ensuring robust solutions that align with industry trends toward modular, reconfigurable computing platforms.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer hardware and software systems and related equipment and facilities; and the analysis of specific problems of computer applications to various tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of coupled surface-subsurface hydrological processes in heterogeneous watersheds, with a focus on quantifying groundwater contamination risks under climate variability. Current models often simplify the integration of surface water flow, unsaturated zone dynamics, and groundwater transport, limiting their ability to resolve fine-scale contaminant pathways or transient climate interactions. We propose a high-resolution, three-dimensional modeling framework using parallelized Hydrus-MODFLOW and PFLOTRAN codes to simulate reactive solute transport across soil and aquifer systems. The computational workflow integrates stochastic parameterization of hydraulic conductivity fields, ensemble climate forcing from regional CMIP6 projections, and probabilistic uncertainty analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute the 10⁴–10⁵ core-hour simulations required for meter-scale discretization of 500 km² domains over decadal timescales. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive Monte Carlo ensembles and optimizing coupled solver performance across multi-physics kernels. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) identification of high-risk zones for nitrate and heavy metal mobilization in agricultural-alluvial aquifers under drought-flood cycles, 2) quantification of model sensitivity to bedrock topography and preferential flow features at sub-watershed scales, and 3) open-source release of optimized GPU-accelerated transport modules. Results will directly inform managed aquifer recharge strategies in the study region while advancing numerical methods for reactive transport in fractured media. By resolving previously intractable spatiotemporal couplings between infiltration events and contaminant breakthrough curves, this work addresses critical gaps in process-based understanding of water quality resilience—a prerequisite for sustainable groundwater management in climate-stressed basins.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the occurrence, circulation, distribution, chemical and physical properties, and environmental interaction of surface and subsurface waters, including groundwater. Includes instruction in geophysics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, chemical physics, geomorphology, mathematical modeling, hydrologic analysis, continental water processes, global water balance, and environmental science.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic resource allocation for next-generation communication networks, particularly as demand surges for high-bandwidth applications such as augmented reality, ultra-high-definition streaming, and distributed teleconferencing. Current protocols struggle to adapt to fluctuating user densities, heterogeneous device capabilities, and variable latency thresholds, resulting in suboptimal bandwidth distribution and service degradation. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to develop adaptive algorithms that optimize real-time resource allocation across large-scale, decentralized networks. Using simulated environments replicating 5G/6G edge networks, the project will model traffic patterns, device interactions, and QoS requirements under diverse scenarios. Machine learning techniques—including graph neural networks and reinforcement learning—will be trained on these simulations to predict congestion points and preemptively allocate computational and spectral resources. Additionally, the project will prototype hybrid protocols that integrate centralized orchestration with decentralized decision-making, balancing scalability and responsiveness. By leveraging parallel computing architectures, the team will iteratively test algorithmic performance across millions of simulated network states, varying parameters such as node density, data payload size, and mobility patterns. Anticipated outcomes include a framework for intelligent resource distribution that reduces median latency by 30-50% in high-density scenarios compared to existing standards, alongside benchmarks for protocol adaptability in underprovisioned environments. This work directly supports the development of robust communication infrastructures capable of sustaining emerging immersive technologies, offering actionable insights for network operators and standards bodies. The computational scale required—processing terabyte-scale network logs, training deep learning models on heterogeneous data streams, and running real-time simulations—necessitates access to HPC resources with GPU acceleration and distributed memory architectures.
cip_title: Communications Technologies and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications technologies and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between neurocognitive development and environmental influences during adolescence using advanced computational modeling and large-scale longitudinal data analysis. The research problem centers on identifying dynamic, age-specific patterns in decision-making and emotional regulation, which are poorly understood due to the multidimensional nature of developmental data (e.g., neuroimaging, behavioral assessments, ecological momentary assessments) and nonlinear interactions between biological maturation and social context. Current analytical approaches often oversimplify these temporal and hierarchical relationships, limiting predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework integrating recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with multilevel Bayesian models. This approach will process high-frequency longitudinal data from three cohorts (N=1,200, ages 12-25) tracking neural connectivity changes via resting-state fMRI, real-world behavioral data from mobile sensing platforms, and cognitive task performance metrics. The HPC resources are critical for three components: 1) Training RNNs on temporal sequences of multimodal data to detect latent developmental trajectories, 2) Running parallelized Bayesian parameter estimation for individualized growth curves across 50+ cognitive and emotional domains, and 3) Simulating system-level neurodevelopmental cascades under varying environmental conditions using agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include a publicly available computational toolkit for developmental pattern discovery, novel biomarkers of adaptive vs. maladaptive developmental pathways, and evidence-based theoretical refinements to dual-systems models of adolescent cognition. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle complex temporal dependencies and high-dimensional interactions, this work aims to advance precision in characterizing normative and atypical development while establishing computational methods tailored for developmental psychology's unique data challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from adolescence to adulthood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, hyper-personalized marketing strategies in decentralized financial service ecosystems. As digital banking, insurtech, and blockchain-based financial platforms proliferate, traditional customer segmentation models struggle to account for dynamic behavioral patterns, cross-platform interactions, and the ethical constraints of data usage across jurisdictions. The study focuses on developing an adaptive computational framework that integrates federated learning with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to balance personalization efficacy, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency. The proposed system will process heterogeneous data streams—including transaction metadata, cross-platform engagement signals, and evolving privacy preferences—while maintaining localized data governance. Computational experiments will simulate decentralized financial service networks using synthetic datasets mirroring real-world complexity in scale (10^8+ user agents) and temporal resolution (millisecond-level event streams). Key challenges include optimizing MARL credit assignment across competing service providers, preventing collusion in decentralized incentive structures, and quantifying the trade-offs between model explainability and predictive accuracy under varying regulatory scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel metrics framework for evaluating cross-institutional personalization performance, open-source algorithms for privacy-preserving collaborative learning in financial marketing, and operational benchmarks for latency-sensitive decision-making in distributed service environments. By advancing computational methods tailored to emerging decentralized finance (DeFi) marketing challenges, this research aims to provide actionable insights for institutions navigating the convergence of personalization technologies, regulatory fragmentation, and consumer demands for data sovereignty. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training large-scale MARL architectures, conducting parallelized scenario testing across regulatory regimes, and validating system robustness under extreme data throughput conditions.
cip_title: Business and Personal/ Financial Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and operational tasks associated with the provision of personal and financial services. Includes instruction in banking, marketing research, advertising, promotional campaign organization, insurance, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: Otolaryngologic disorders, particularly those involving the head and neck, present complex clinical challenges due to anatomical intricacy, disease heterogeneity, and the need for precision in diagnosis and treatment. This project seeks to advance computational modeling of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) to identify molecular biomarkers predictive of treatment resistance and metastasis. A critical barrier in current research is the integration of multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic) with high-resolution imaging and clinical outcomes at scale, which is computationally prohibitive for standard infrastructure. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models that synthesize these multimodal datasets. The computational workflow will include preprocessing of raw sequencing data, 3D reconstruction of tumor volumes from imaging, and federated learning frameworks to preserve patient privacy while training predictive models across institutions. Parallelized algorithms will be employed for feature selection, dimensionality reduction, and survival analysis to map tumor subtypes to therapeutic responses. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers associated with locoregional recurrence and the creation of open-source tools for HNSCC subtyping. These results will directly inform clinical trial designs for targeted therapies and adaptive radiotherapy planning. The scale of data—expected to exceed 500 TB across 2,000 patients—necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies. By addressing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to bridge translational gaps in otolaryngology, enabling data-driven precision medicine for improved patient survival and quality of life.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians to diagnose and provide medical and/or surgical therapy or prevention of diseases, allergies, neoplasms, deformities, disorders, and injuries of the ears, nose, sinuses, throat, respiratory and upper alimentary systems, face, jaws, and the other head and neck systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of cross-platform consumer sentiment dynamics in fragmented digital markets. Traditional marketing research tools struggle to process real-time, unstructured data from heterogeneous sources—including social media, e-commerce reviews, and IoT-enabled behavioral feeds—at scales necessary to capture rapidly evolving consumer preferences. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to integrate multimodal data streams, identify latent demand signals, and simulate emergent market behaviors under dynamic competitive conditions. Using a hybrid approach combining transformer-based natural language processing, graph neural networks for cross-platform influence mapping, and agent-based market simulations, the project will model how micro-level consumer interactions generate macro-level trend adoption patterns. Computational challenges include processing petabyte-scale historical datasets, training attention mechanisms on sparse multimodal inputs, and running parallelized market scenario simulations with 10^6+ agent interactions per trial. The HPC infrastructure will enable distributed training of deep learning models across GPU clusters, in-memory processing of temporal graph networks, and Monte Carlo sampling of stochastic simulation parameters. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source toolkit for real-time sentiment convergence forecasting, (2) quantitative metrics for platform-specific marketing elasticity, and (3) evidence-based strategies for allocating digital ad spend across attention-competitive environments. By addressing the computational bottlenecks in large-scale behavioral synthesis, this work aims to establish new methodologies for adaptive marketing mix optimization in hyperconnected markets while contributing foundational techniques for HPC applications in computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide analytical descriptions of consumer behavior patterns and market environments to marketing managers and other business decision-makers. Includes instruction in survey research methods, research design, new product test marketing, exploratory marketing, consumer needs and preferences analysis, geographic analysis, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of decision-making under uncertainty using large-scale computational models of cognitive processes. Traditional experimental approaches in psychology often struggle to disentangle the contributions of individual cognitive mechanisms—such as memory retrieval, attention allocation, and probabilistic reasoning—in complex, real-world decision tasks. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework integrating neural network models with Bayesian inference algorithms. This framework will simulate how agents adaptively balance exploration and exploitation in dynamic environments with incomplete information. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for systematically varying parameters across thousands of simulated agents, iterating through environmental stochasticity, and analyzing high-dimensional behavioral trajectories. The computational workflow will involve parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore parameter spaces, coupled with machine learning techniques to identify emergent patterns in decision strategies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated model architecture capturing interactions between memory constraints and uncertainty resolution, (2) quantitative predictions about behavioral trade-offs in human decision-making under resource-limited conditions, and (3) open-source tools for scalable cognitive modeling. Results will advance theoretical frameworks in experimental psychology by linking micro-level cognitive processes to macro-level behavioral phenomena, while providing methodological innovations for simulating complex psychological systems. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across biologically plausible neural scales (10^4–10^6 simulated units) and longitudinal task environments that exceed the temporal resolution of laboratory experiments. This work bridges computational neuroscience and experimental psychology, offering new pathways to test mechanistic hypotheses about cognition that are infeasible with conventional experimental designs alone.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in research and experimental psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of decentralized digital communication networks and their emergent effects on collective identity formation, using computational methods to analyze patterns of interaction at scale. While traditional studies of social cohesion have focused on geographically bounded communities or institutional frameworks, the rise of ephemeral, algorithmically mediated spaces—such as encrypted messaging groups, decentralized social platforms, and peer-to-peer content-sharing networks—presents novel challenges for understanding how trust, norms, and shared meaning develop in fragmented digital environments. The research addresses this gap by employing a mixed-methods framework that combines large-scale network analysis, natural language processing (NLP), and agent-based modeling (ABM) to map how decentralized architectures influence the propagation of cultural narratives and the stabilization of group boundaries. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets of timestamped interactions across multiple platforms, training transformer-based models on multilingual, code-mixed communications, and simulating emergent coordination behaviors under varying network topologies. Expected outcomes include a computational typology of trust-building mechanisms in non-hierarchical digital spaces, quantitative models linking platform affordances to polarization thresholds, and open-source tools for real-time detection of latent identity fractures in decentralized communities. By bridging computational social science with digital ethnography, this work aims to advance theoretical frameworks for studying post-institutional social organization while providing actionable insights for developers and policymakers seeking to mitigate systemic risks in next-generation communication ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that combines sociology and anthropology to study how society is organized, the origins and development of social institutions, social change, social organizations, race, class, gender and culture.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational tools for analyzing the spatial, dynamic, and sociolinguistic features of American Sign Language (ASL), a visual-gestural language central to Deaf communities. Current linguistic software and analytical frameworks are predominantly designed for spoken or written languages, lacking the capacity to model ASL’s simultaneous use of manual signs, non-manual markers (e.g., facial expressions, body shifts), and three-dimensional signing space. This limitation hinders large-scale empirical research on ASL structure, variation, and evolution, as well as the development of technologies to support ASL education, translation, and preservation. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-phase computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multimodal ASL datasets. The first phase involves training deep neural networks on a corpus of 500+ hours of annotated ASL video data to automate the identification of phonological, morphological, and syntactic patterns, with a focus on classifier predicates and constructed dialogue. The second phase employs agent-based modeling to simulate the emergence of regional ASL variations under different social and demographic conditions. These simulations will integrate historical linguistic data and sociocultural variables to test hypotheses about language change in Deaf communities. The third phase develops a real-time ASL processing pipeline using GPU-accelerated motion capture and 3D spatial analysis to map signing kinematics. By combining these approaches, the project aims to produce open-source tools for ASL transcription, machine-assisted translation, and dialect modeling. Outcomes will advance theoretical understanding of visual-spatial grammar systems, inform ASL pedagogy, and enable scalable preservation of endangered ASL varieties. The computational demands—including parallel processing of high-resolution video, large-language model fine-tuning, and complex spatial simulations—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve practical runtime and accuracy thresholds. This work bridges computational linguistics and disability studies, centering ASL as a vital human language deserving of equitable research investment.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on American Sign Language as a visual and motor medium of communication and discourse for deaf individuals and deaf culture. Includes instruction in the development of ASL, ASL morphology and syntax, signing technique, English translation of ASL, formal and colloquial ASL, and ASL transcription.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how dynamic neural circuit interactions underlie decision-making deficits in stress-related neuropsychiatric disorders. While rodent studies have identified prefrontal-amygdala-hippocampal circuits as critical for adaptive behavior under threat, the mechanisms by which chronic stress disrupts their coordination during decision processes remain poorly understood. Existing models lack the spatiotemporal resolution to capture millisecond-scale network dynamics across distributed regions during complex behavioral tasks. To address this, we propose a computational neuroscience approach combining biophysically detailed spiking neural network models with behavioral reinforcement learning frameworks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of >100,000 neurons with region-specific connectivity derived from tract tracing data, incorporating synaptic plasticity rules modulated by stress hormones. The models will be constrained by in vivo electrophysiology recordings from mice performing threat-conditioned probabilistic foraging tasks. Parallelized parameter optimization will identify circuit configurations that reproduce stress-induced behavioral rigidity observed experimentally. Memory-intensive GPU-accelerated simulations will resolve subcellular signaling cascades influencing synaptic efficacy during task epochs. Expected outcomes include: 1) A mechanistic explanation for how stress disrupts phase-locked oscillations between prefrontal and amygdala populations during conflict resolution 2) Predictive models of optogenetic intervention strategies to restore adaptive network dynamics 3) Open-source simulation tools for multiscale neural circuit analysis. This work directly addresses NIH priorities in computational neurobiology by bridging molecular neurophysiology with behavioral phenotypes of mental health disorders. The requested 200,000 CPU-hr allocation and 64TB scratch storage will support 18 months of large-scale simulations, enabling unprecedented resolution of stress pathophysiology mechanisms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates as it relates to control of behavior. Includes instruction in neuronal systems and circuits, higher level studies of behavior and cognition, computational neurobiology, and behavioral manifestations of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the socio-computational dynamics of digital communication platforms as emergent spaces for decentralized collective decision-making, focusing on how non-hierarchical information ecosystems influence public reasoning and consensus formation. The research problem centers on understanding how algorithmic affordances, network topology, and user-generated content interact to shape epistemic outcomes in contexts where traditional institutional authority is absent. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose to analyze multi-platform interaction data (spanning federated social networks, collaborative knowledge bases, and participatory governance forums) using a novel hybrid methodology combining agent-based modeling, dynamic network analysis, and transformer-based natural language processing. Computational experiments will simulate alternative information diffusion scenarios under varying platform architectures, while large-scale linguistic analysis of 50+ million user contributions will identify patterns of argumentation, epistemic vigilance, and belief updating. The project will develop an open-source framework for simulating socio-technical systems that bridges micro-level cognitive processes with macro-level network effects. Expected outcomes include (1) computational evidence characterizing how specific platform features amplify or mitigate polarization in decentralized communities, (2) predictive models of consensus emergence in leaderless deliberation environments, and (3) actionable insights for designing communication infrastructures that balance autonomy and epistemic resilience. By advancing methodological integration between complex systems science and social epistemology, this work addresses critical gaps in understanding collective intelligence phenomena that transcend traditional disciplinary boundaries, with implications for digital governance, online community design, and crisis response coordination in increasingly decentralized media landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of human social behavior and social institutions using any of the methodologies common to the social sciences and/or history, or an undifferentiated program of study in the social sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of structure-function relationships in the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), with a focus on resolving the anatomical basis of synaptic connectivity anomalies in neurodegenerative disorders. A critical challenge in neuroanatomy is integrating multiscale imaging datasets—ranging from electron microscopy reconstructions of neuronal ultrastructure to mesoscale circuit mapping—to model how discrete anatomical disruptions contribute to pathologies such as Alzheimer’s disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Current limitations stem from the computational complexity of aligning terabyte-scale 3D imaging datasets, segmenting densely packed neurites, and simulating signal propagation in disease-affected circuits. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining machine learning-driven image analysis, graph-theoretical network modeling, and biophysically constrained simulations of neural activity. The HPC environment is essential for training deep neural networks to automate the identification of synaptic contacts and pathological features (e.g., amyloid plaques) in high-resolution imaging data, as well as for constructing large-scale connectomes from these annotated datasets. Additionally, parallelized simulations will model how specific anatomical alterations—such as axon degeneration or dendritic spine loss—impact network dynamics. This approach will enable the first integrative analysis of structural degeneration patterns and their functional consequences across spatial scales. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible atlas of disease-specific neuronal connectivity changes, (2) predictive models linking subcellular anatomical disruptions to circuit-level dysfunction, and (3) new criteria for evaluating the neuroanatomical specificity of emerging therapeutic strategies. By bridging advanced imaging and computational neuroscience, this work will provide foundational insights into the anatomical drivers of CNS disorders, directly supporting the development of targeted neurorestorative interventions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates or the nervous system of invertebrates. Includes instruction in cellular and circuit anatomy, mapping of neuronal pathways, anatomical distribution and mapping of neuronal signaling molecules and their receptors, and the anatomical basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the systemic risk dynamics of decentralized cryptocurrency markets, focusing on the emergent behavior of liquidity protocols and automated market makers (AMMs) in decentralized exchanges (DEXs). While traditional financial systemic risk models emphasize centralized intermediaries, decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems operate via algorithmic coordination, creating unique vulnerabilities that remain understudied. The core research problem lies in quantifying how network effects, protocol interdependencies, and liquidity fragmentation across blockchain-based DEXs propagate instability during market shocks. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with real-time blockchain data ingestion. The ABM will simulate heterogeneous agents (e.g., liquidity providers, arbitrageurs, leveraged traders) interacting across multiple DEX protocols under varying market conditions, while on-chain transaction data will parameterize and validate model assumptions. Computational challenges include scaling simulations to replicate the Ethereum and Solana ecosystems’ transaction throughput (>1,000 TPS), modeling cross-chain liquidity flows, and analyzing high-dimensional time-series data to detect latent risk cascades. GPU-accelerated graph neural networks will be employed to map liquidity network topologies and stress-test protocol resilience. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel risk metric for DeFi liquidity fragmentation, (2) protocol design recommendations to mitigate reflexivity in AMM pricing, and (3) a publicly accessible dataset linking on-chain activity to systemic vulnerability indicators. This work bridges financial economics, distributed systems, and computational social science, offering policymakers and protocol developers tools to address stability challenges in algorithmically mediated markets. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of multi-chain simulations and achieving sub-second latency in real-time risk monitoring applications.
cip_title: Finance and Financial Management Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in financial management and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The rapid proliferation of decentralized autonomous systems (DAS) in critical infrastructure—such as smart grids, distributed sensor networks, and robotic swarms—has exposed gaps in existing frameworks for real-time, trustless coordination under dynamic constraints. This project seeks to develop a novel computational architecture for DAS that integrates cryptographic verification, game-theoretic incentive alignment, and adaptive resource scheduling without relying on centralized authorities. The core challenge lies in balancing Byzantine fault tolerance with sub-second latency requirements while operating in environments with intermittent connectivity and adversarial actors. To address this, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling framework coupled with a lightweight consensus protocol optimized for heterogeneous computing clusters. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of urban-scale DAS deployments, stress-testing scenarios involving up to 10^6 autonomous agents under varying network topologies and threat models. Key computational components include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for protocol robustness analysis, GPU-accelerated lattice-based cryptographic primitives, and evolutionary algorithms for optimizing incentive parameters. The resulting toolkit will provide quantifiable metrics for resilience-efficiency tradeoffs in trustless coordination systems, with direct applications to next-generation industrial IoT and disaster response networks. Successful validation of our architecture could reduce synchronization overhead by 40-60% compared to existing blockchain-inspired approaches while maintaining provable security guarantees. This work bridges gaps between distributed systems theory, cryptographic engineering, and multi-agent AI—a critical intersection not fully addressed by conventional computer science subfields. Resource allocation will specifically support the development of custom MPI-based communication layers and the curation of synthetic training datasets capturing rare but catastrophic failure modes in decentralized systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that simulate the impact of personalized instructional strategies on middle school student learning outcomes. A critical challenge in middle-grade education is tailoring pedagogy to address diverse student needs—spanning cognitive development, engagement, and socioemotional factors—within constrained classroom time. Traditional methods for evaluating instructional efficacy rely on small-scale trials or observational studies, which are time-intensive and lack the granularity to model dynamic interactions between teaching methods, student behaviors, and academic progress. This project addresses this gap by constructing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate classroom environments, incorporating variables such as individualized learning trajectories, teacher-student interaction patterns, and real-time feedback mechanisms. The ABMs will integrate empirical datasets, including anonymized student performance records, engagement metrics, and teacher intervention logs, to parameterize and validate simulations. Computational demands arise from the need to run thousands of parallel simulations across diverse demographic and pedagogical scenarios, requiring scalable processing power to optimize model accuracy. Machine learning techniques will then analyze simulation outputs to identify high-impact teaching strategies that maximize learning equity and efficiency. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting the efficacy of differentiated instruction in middle school contexts, with potential applications in teacher training programs and adaptive curricular design. By quantifying how specific interventions affect heterogeneous student populations, this work aims to provide educators with data-driven tools to refine instructional practices. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the complexity of multi-agent interactions and large parameter spaces inherent in this research, enabling insights that could directly inform classroom practice and policy in middle school education.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Junior High/ Intermediate/ Middle School Education and Teaching
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the middle, intermediate or junior high grades, which may include grades four through nine by regulation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address unresolved questions about the socio-environmental dynamics of ancient civilizations through large-scale, integrative data analysis. While interdisciplinary studies of antiquity have long relied on qualitative methods, recent advances in digitized archaeological records, remote sensing datasets, and textual corpora present opportunities—and challenges—for quantitative modeling of complex interactions between human societies and their environments. The research problem centers on how climatic shifts, resource availability, and cultural exchange networks influenced the resilience or fragmentation of Bronze Age Mediterranean and Mesopotamian societies (ca. 3000–1200 BCE). Current gaps persist in synthesizing high-resolution paleoclimate proxies, settlement patterns, and multilingual textual data at regional scales, limiting systemic analyses of adaptive strategies. To overcome this, the project will deploy computational workflows integrating agent-based modeling, geospatial network analysis, and machine learning-assisted corpus linguistics. Agent-based simulations will reconstruct subsistence decision-making under variable climate scenarios, while graph-based network models will map trade and cultural connections using archaeological site distributions and cuneiform tablet metadata. Concurrently, transformer-based NLP models, trained on transliterated Akkadian, Hittite, and Linear B texts, will identify semantic patterns related to resource management and crisis response. These parallel pipelines require HPC resources to manage iterative simulations across parameter spaces, process multi-terabyte geospatial datasets, and fine-tune language models. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of linked climate-cultural datasets, validated frameworks for simulating ancient socio-ecological systems, and peer-reviewed insights into how multi-scalar stressors affected institutional longevity. By enabling computationally intensive synthesis of disparate data types, this work aims to establish new methodologies for interdisciplinary ancient studies while contributing to broader discourses on societal resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Western and Non-Western cultures and related topics in the periods of Pre-history and Antiquity. Includes such disciplines as ancient languages, archeology, history, art history, geography, population studies, environmental studies, religious studies, and the social sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic feedbacks between urban land-use patterns, microclimate variability, and socioeconomic vulnerability under climate change scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate heterogeneous datasets spanning spatial, temporal, and disciplinary scales. Rapid urbanization alters local climates through heat island effects and modified hydrological cycles, while climate extremes disproportionately impact marginalized communities—a complex coupling requiring analysis of high-resolution geospatial data, climate models, and demographic indicators. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the simultaneous integration of multi-terabyte remote sensing datasets (e.g., Sentinel-2, LiDAR), granular census data, and ensemble climate projections at city-to-neighborhood scales. We propose a computational workflow combining graph-based spatial analytics, machine learning-driven downscaling of regional climate models, and agent-based simulations of adaptive infrastructure planning. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of 10+ years of hourly urban meteorological data, automated feature extraction from satellite imagery using convolutional neural networks, and Monte Carlo simulations evaluating 10,000+ policy intervention scenarios. Key innovations include a coupled modeling framework bridging hydrodynamic urban microclimate simulations with social vulnerability indices, validated against ground sensor networks in three case-study cities (Toronto, Mumbai, Lagos). Anticipated outcomes include predictive maps of heat exposure risk under shared socioeconomic pathways, open-source tools for equitable climate adaptation planning, and scalable methods to prioritize green infrastructure investments. This work advances interdisciplinary scholarship by fusing physical geography, environmental justice, and computational social science, directly informing municipal policy while developing transferable cyberinfrastructure for integrative human-environment systems research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on interactions between people and the natural and built environments. Includes instruction in climate science, sustainability, environmental science and policy, research methods, geographic information systems (GIS), human geography, physical geography, remote sensing, and public policy.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis of large-scale visual media datasets, enabling new methodologies for studying cultural and aesthetic patterns in digital art and design. The exponential growth of digitized art collections, photography archives, and user-generated visual content presents a critical challenge: traditional analytical tools are insufficient for identifying nuanced trends across spatially and temporally diverse datasets. This work addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to systematically interrogate visual media at scale, with a focus on uncovering latent relationships between artistic techniques, sociocultural contexts, and audience engagement metrics. Proposed methods combine computer vision algorithms for feature extraction (e.g., color topology, compositional balance, texture mapping) with machine learning models trained to classify stylistic evolution across decentralized art repositories. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale image datasets, iterative refinement of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for simulating historical design paradigms, and 3D rendering of complex multimedia installations. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for art historians and curators to analyze cross-cultural visual trends, as well as novel visualizations of how digital-native artworks reflect contemporary societal values. The computational demands of training multimodal transformers on high-resolution imagery and simulating dynamic viewer interactions with virtual gallery spaces necessitate dedicated GPU clusters and distributed storage systems. By bridging computational scalability with art historical inquiry, this project aims to establish new standards for data-driven scholarship in visual culture while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between artistic practice and computational innovation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of the visual arts. Includes instruction in art, photography, and other visual communications media.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and real-time customer engagement strategies in hospitality and recreation marketing operations through advanced computational modeling. Traditional approaches to demand forecasting and personalized marketing in this sector often rely on static segmentation or simplified heuristic models, which struggle to adapt to rapidly shifting consumer preferences, seasonal volatility, and hyperlocal competitive dynamics. The research problem centers on developing a high-fidelity simulation environment capable of integrating heterogeneous data streams—including IoT-enabled facility usage patterns, real-time sentiment analysis from social platforms, and transactional histories—to model customer decision pathways under variable pricing and promotional conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will implement agent-based modeling frameworks combined with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms to simulate millions of concurrent customer agents interacting with evolving marketing stimuli. Computational workflows will prioritize parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing across diverse market conditions, coupled with distributed training of DRL policies to optimize multi-objective outcomes balancing revenue, customer satisfaction, and operational capacity constraints. Expected outcomes include the development of adaptive pricing architectures capable of adjusting offers at sub-hourly intervals, predictive models for identifying high-value experience customization opportunities, and operational benchmarks for technology ROI in recreation marketing ecosystems. The research will contribute novel methodologies for synthesizing behavioral economics principles with large-scale computational marketing optimizations, addressing a critical gap in data-driven decision support systems for hospitality operators. Successful implementation requires HPC resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of real-time data integration, multi-agent interactions, and iterative policy refinement, with particular emphasis on GPU-accelerated neural network training and distributed memory architectures for concurrent scenario evaluation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide marketing services in the hospitality and leisure fields. Includes instruction in hospitality operations, customer sales and assistance operations and techniques, telephone operations, basic office management, retail sports, recreation equipment, food and beverage.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to predict biomechanical and microbiological interactions influencing osseointegration failure in dental implants, a critical yet understudied driver of implant complications. While current clinical guidelines rely on generalized risk factors, emerging evidence suggests that patient-specific variations in jawbone microarchitecture, occlusal force dynamics, and oral microbiome composition interact nonlinearly to determine long-term implant success. We propose an integrative modeling approach combining 1) finite element analysis of bone-implant stress distributions derived from clinical CT scans, 2) machine learning analysis of metagenomic sequencing data from peri-implant sulcular fluid, and 3) dynamic simulations of microbial biofilm growth under mechanically stressed conditions. High-performance computing resources will enable multiscale integration of these typically siloed data types through coupled biomechanical-microbial agent-based models operating at 10^6+ computational agents. The project will leverage existing retrospective data from 450 implant cases (imaging, microbiome samples, and 5-year outcome records) while prospectively collecting multimodal data from 30 new patients undergoing implant therapy. Computational workflows will be validated against clinical outcomes using time-to-event analyses and microbial culture experiments. Expected outcomes include a predictive model identifying high-risk implant scenarios through patient-specific simulations, novel biomarkers of early osseointegration failure, and an open-source toolkit for simulating bone-microbiome-implant interactions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges dental biomechanics, computational microbiology, and clinical decision science, addressing a critical gap in personalized implantology while establishing computational methods adaptable to other device-associated infections in healthcare.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program that generally prepares dentists in one or more of the oral sciences and advanced/graduate dentistry specialties.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of intergenerational decision-making in household resource allocation under economic uncertainty, a topic situated at the intersection of human development, behavioral economics, and computational social science. While existing studies in Family and Consumer Sciences often rely on survey-based or qualitative methods, this research addresses a critical gap by modeling complex, nonlinear interactions between cultural norms, cognitive biases, and financial stressors that influence family systems. The computational challenge arises from simulating millions of agent-based household scenarios with heterogeneous parameters, including varying income volatility, multi-generational cohabitation patterns, and culturally embedded risk perceptions. A hybrid modeling approach will integrate adaptive network architectures (to capture evolving family structures) with reinforcement learning frameworks (to simulate decision-making heuristics), validated against longitudinal datasets from transnational demographic surveys. The HPC environment is essential for parallel processing of stochastic simulations across parameter spaces and for training deep learning models to identify latent patterns in high-dimensional behavioral data. Expected outcomes include predictive models of resilience strategies adopted by households facing economic shocks, visualized through interactive decision trees accessible to policymakers and financial literacy educators. This work will establish a novel computational methodology for human sciences research, enabling granular analysis of socio-economic behaviors while preserving the contextual complexity often lost in traditional disciplinary approaches. By bridging agent-based modeling with family systems theory, the project contributes to evidence-based interventions aimed at improving household financial stability in demographically diverse communities.
