cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing resilient urban infrastructure systems under climate-driven stressors, with a focus on integrated transportation networks and water resource management. Aging civil infrastructure, increasing flood risks, and evolving traffic demands necessitate computationally intensive modeling to evaluate system-wide vulnerabilities and adaptive solutions. Current approaches often rely on simplified assumptions or decoupled analyses, limiting their ability to capture complex interdependencies between structural components, hydrological processes, and human mobility patterns. This project will develop a high-resolution computational framework combining finite element analysis, hydrodynamic simulations, and agent-based transportation modeling to assess multi-hazard scenarios across spatial and temporal scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for real-time flood prediction using 2D shallow water equations, coupled with parallelized structural reliability assessments of bridges and drainage systems under dynamic loading conditions. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC clusters to reduce the cost of probabilistic risk assessments involving 10^4–10^5 parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting infrastructure failure cascades during compound flooding and traffic disruption events, with sensitivity analyses informing climate-adaptive design standards. The computational tools will enable municipalities to prioritize retrofitting strategies for at-risk assets while balancing economic and safety constraints. By integrating terabyte-scale LiDAR datasets with real-time sensor inputs, this work will advance predictive capabilities for infrastructure resilience planning in coastal and urbanized regions. Resource allocation will support large-scale parametric studies, validation against case studies from collaborating agencies, and the development of open-source simulation modules for broader academic and industry use.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of structural, load-bearing, material moving, transportation, water resource, and material control systems; and environmental safety measures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing complexity of media content analysis and production workflows in the evolving landscape of broadcast and streaming platforms. As audience consumption patterns fragment across traditional and digital formats, radio and television professionals face challenges in efficiently analyzing large-scale audiovisual datasets, optimizing real-time production pipelines, and simulating audience engagement scenarios. Current consumer-grade computational tools are insufficient for processing high-resolution video feeds, applying machine learning models to content metadata, or modeling distribution network performance at scale. The proposed research will employ parallelized computing architectures to develop a framework for automated media asset tagging, dynamic bandwidth allocation simulations, and AI-assisted editing workflows. Key computational tasks include training neural networks to identify narrative structures in archival television content, rendering multi-camera virtual production environments, and stress-testing broadcast infrastructure models under varying load conditions. By integrating these workflows into a unified HPC environment, the project aims to reduce post-production processing times by 40–60% for 4K/8K content, enable predictive analytics for audience retention, and generate actionable insights for adaptive bitrate streaming configurations. Outcomes will directly inform curriculum development in media technology courses while providing open-source optimization templates for small-to-midsize production studios. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated video encoding experiments, distributed storage solutions for petabyte-scale media libraries, and real-time rendering benchmarks critical to advancing broadcast education and industry practices. This work bridges theoretical media studies with applied computational research, addressing pressing needs in content lifecycle management and next-generation storytelling infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, methods, and techniques used to plan, produce, and distribute audio and video programs and messages, and that prepares individuals to function as staff, producers, directors, and managers of radio and television shows and media organizations. Includes instruction in media aesthetics; planning, scheduling, and production; writing and editing; performing and directing; personnel and facilities management; marketing and distribution; media regulations, law, and policy; and principles of broadcast technology.

abstract: This project seeks to understand how rapid environmental change disrupts co-evolutionary dynamics between mutualistic species, with implications for ecosystem resilience and biodiversity conservation. A critical gap exists in predicting how shifts in phenology, range distributions, and interaction networks under climate warming alter reciprocal selection pressures between plants and their pollinators. To address this, we propose developing spatially explicit, individual-based models that integrate empirical data on species traits, interaction networks, and environmental gradients. These models will simulate multi-generational feedbacks between ecological interactions (e.g., pollinator foraging behavior, plant reproductive success) and evolutionary processes (e.g., selection on floral morphology and pollinator sensory adaptations) across heterogeneous landscapes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the stochastic, high-dimensional simulations required for capturing complex eco-evolutionary dynamics at regional scales. Each simulation will track >10^6 individual organisms across dynamically changing environments, incorporating real-world climate projections and habitat fragmentation scenarios. Parallelized parameter sweeps will assess how varying rates of environmental change and dispersal limitations modulate evolutionary rescue potential. Outcomes will identify thresholds beyond which co-evolutionary relationships collapse, quantify the role of genetic diversity in buffering interactions, and predict spatial hotspots of network destabilization under future climates. This work bridges ecological and evolutionary timescales, providing a framework to prioritize conservation efforts for mutualisms critical to ecosystem function. By leveraging HPC capabilities, we aim to overcome computational bottlenecks that have previously limited the integration of adaptive evolution into large-scale ecological forecasts, advancing predictive capacity for biodiversity responses to anthropogenic change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how evolution shapes biodiversity, and how organisms interact with each other and their environments. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance speech pedagogy by developing computational models to analyze and predict the efficacy of instructional strategies for students with diverse speech and language learning needs. A critical challenge in speech teacher education is the lack of data-driven frameworks to personalize instruction for learners with varying linguistic backgrounds, communication disorders, or socio-cultural contexts. Existing methods often rely on generalized approaches, which may not account for the complex interplay of phonetic, syntactic, and pragmatic factors influencing individual learning trajectories. To address this gap, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale speech datasets from classroom interactions, therapy sessions, and standardized assessments. These datasets include audio recordings, transcribed dialogues, and longitudinal performance metrics from K–12 and adult learners. Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures and temporal convolutional networks, will be trained to identify patterns in speech development, correlate instructional interventions with learner outcomes, and simulate the impact of pedagogical adjustments. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of high-dimensional audio data, hyperparameter optimization across multiple model configurations, and real-time simulations of classroom scenarios. The computational outputs will inform the design of adaptive teaching toolkits that recommend evidence-based strategies for articulation, fluency, and pragmatic language instruction. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of annotated speech datasets, predictive models validated against clinical and educational benchmarks, and a framework for integrating computational analytics into teacher training curricula. By bridging speech science, educational practice, and computational modeling, this work aims to empower educators with scalable tools to address inequities in speech and language education while advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of linguistics and teacher preparation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach speech and language arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the efficacy of adaptive learning systems in K-12 science curricula, with the goal of optimizing personalized instructional material design. Despite advances in educational technology, a critical gap persists in understanding how dynamic, multimodal learner data—including interaction logs, formative assessments, and biometric feedback—can be systematically integrated to refine curriculum sequencing in real time. Current methods for evaluating adaptive systems rely on small-scale trials or simplified models, limiting their scalability and generalizability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and network analysis to model student learning pathways across heterogeneous datasets. The computational workflow will involve training multi-agent DRL models on anonymized student interaction data (spanning 50,000+ learners) to simulate decision-making processes in curriculum adaptation, coupled with temporal graph networks to identify latent patterns in concept mastery trajectories. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabytes of multimodal educational data, parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simulated classroom environments, and running evolutionary algorithms to stress-test curriculum designs under diverse pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive model for mapping learner behaviors to optimal instructional sequences, 2) an open-source toolkit for evaluating curriculum robustness against demographic and cognitive variability, and 3) evidence-based guidelines for embedding real-time analytics into adaptive learning platforms. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work aims to advance computational curriculum theory while providing scalable methods for evaluating educational interventions—a critical need in post-pandemic learning environments where hybrid and personalized instruction have become ubiquitous. Results will be disseminated through an interactive web portal for educators and peer-reviewed publications on data-driven curriculum design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the curriculum and related instructional processes and tools, and that may prepare individuals to serve as professional curriculum specialists. Includes instruction in curriculum theory, curriculum design and planning, instructional material design and evaluation, curriculum evaluation, and applications to specific subject matter, programs or educational levels.

abstract: Musicological research has traditionally relied on manual analysis of scores and historical texts, limiting the scope and scale of inquiries into the evolution of musical practices. This project addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing vast corpora of digitized musical scores and archival recordings to uncover patterns in harmonic development, stylistic shifts, and cross-cultural influences across seven centuries. The research requires high-performance computing resources to process and analyze over 100,000 score files (in MEI and MusicXML formats) and 15,000 hours of audio recordings through machine learning models optimized for music information retrieval. Computational methods will include transformer-based architectures for symbolic music analysis, graph neural networks to model influence networks among composers, and spectral clustering techniques to identify latent stylistic groupings. These approaches will be augmented by agent-based simulations of theoretical frameworks from historical treatises, testing hypotheses about the transmission of compositional practices. The integration of heterogeneous data sources—including non-Western notation systems—demands parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated feature extraction to maintain project timelines. Expected outcomes include the first longitudinal dataset mapping harmonic complexity indices from medieval polyphony to modern experimental works, computational tools for cross-epochal style comparison, and evidence-based revisions to existing narratives about the globalization of musical techniques. By enabling the processing of culturally diverse materials at unprecedented scales, this work will establish new methodologies for data-driven musicology while providing open-access resources for interdisciplinary scholarship in historical acoustics and performance practice reconstruction.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical evolution of music as a social and intellectual phenomenon, the development of musical instruments and techniques, and the analysis and criticism of musical literature. Includes instruction in music history research methods, aesthetic analysis of musical compositions, history of musical writing and notation, the development of musical instruments, the development of music theory, and the study of specific periods, cultural traditions, styles, and themes.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated systems through large-scale numerical simulations, with a focus on non-perturbative regimes where conventional analytical methods fail. The central problem involves resolving the interplay between quantum coherence and collective excitations in low-dimensional spin systems and topological field theories, which are poorly understood beyond small-scale or mean-field approximations. These systems are critical for advancing foundational theories of quantum matter, particularly in contexts where entanglement dynamics and non-equilibrium behavior dominate. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining tensor network methods, stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), and spectral discretization of continuum field equations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for handling the exponential scaling of Hilbert spaces in tensor network optimizations, mitigating the sign problem in frustrated spin systems via QMC parallelism, and solving high-dimensional partial differential equations governing topological defects. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for matrix product state evolution and distributed memory architectures for thermodynamic limit extrapolations. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative predictions for entanglement entropy growth in dynamically driven spin chains, (2) classification of phase transitions in 2D quantum spin liquids beyond current symmetry-based paradigms, and (3) first-principles characterization of soliton stability in non-integrable quantum field theories. These results will provide benchmarks for experimental collaborations studying quantum simulators and inform the development of error-resilient quantum memory architectures. The computational workflows and open-source solver libraries developed during this project will enhance the broader theoretical physics community’s capacity to model strongly correlated systems, bridging gaps between abstract mathematical formulations and observable physical behavior. Resource allocation is requested to support sustained multi-node calculations, including 200,000 core-hours for finite-temperature QMC sampling and dedicated GPU partitions for real-time evolution studies exceeding 50 qubits.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and mathematical formulation and evaluation of the physical laws governing, and models describing, matter-energy phenomena, and the analysis of related experimental designs and results. Includes instruction in classical and quantum theory, relativity theory, field theory, mathematics of infinite series, vector and coordinate analysis, wave and particle theory, advanced applied calculus and geometry, analyses of continuum, cosmology, and statistical theory and analysis.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation aims to optimize functional outcomes for children with disabilities, but clinical decision-making remains constrained by heterogeneous data sources and complex interactions between biological, biomechanical, and environmental factors. Current analytical approaches struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets—including genomic, neuroimaging, wearable sensor data, and electronic health records—while accounting for individual variability in treatment response. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient-specific recovery trajectories and predict optimal rehabilitation strategies using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will develop machine learning pipelines to harmonize multimodal datasets from a retrospective cohort of 2,500 children with cerebral palsy, traumatic brain injury, and spinal cord injuries. Predictive models will identify biomarkers of motor and cognitive recovery, while biomechanical simulations of musculoskeletal dynamics will evaluate the efficacy of assistive devices and therapeutic exercises under varying physiological constraints. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning architectures on large-scale neuroimaging data, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in treatment outcomes, and optimizing hyperparameters across diverse patient subgroups. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for personalizing rehabilitation protocols, validated against a prospective cohort of 200 patients. This work will advance precision medicine in pediatric rehabilitation by linking computational phenotyping to evidence-based interventions, ultimately reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice. The tools and datasets generated will be shared openly to accelerate innovation in rehabilitation science, with direct implications for improving functional independence and quality of life in children with disabilities.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Rehabilitation

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic organization of cellular compartments and their role in maintaining structural integrity during stress responses, a fundamental question in cell biology with implications for understanding disease mechanisms. A major gap exists in mapping how organelles such as lysosomes, endosomes, and the cytoskeleton coordinate spatial reorganization under metabolic or mechanical stress, particularly in human epithelial cells. Traditional imaging and biochemical approaches lack the resolution to model these interactions at subcellular scales across time. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations to reconstruct 3D organelle dynamics within realistic cell geometries. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and run spatially resolved models that integrate live-cell imaging data, simulating millions of interacting agents (e.g., vesicles, cytoskeletal filaments) over biologically relevant timescales (hours to days). The ABM will encode rules for organelle motility, tethering, and membrane remodeling, while LBM will simulate cytoplasmic fluid dynamics and diffusion gradients. Validation will leverage experimental datasets from collaborating labs, including light-sheet microscopy and traction force microscopy of stressed epithelial monolayers. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of stress-induced organelle redistribution, (2) identification of critical thresholds in cytoskeletal strain that trigger loss of compartmentalization, and (3) open-source simulation tools for visualizing multiscale cell architecture changes. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of how spatial organization failures contribute to pathologies such as epithelial barrier dysfunction, directly supporting the program’s focus on cell structure-function relationships. The requested resources—200,000 CPU-hours and GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized LBM—will enable parameter sweeps across physiologically relevant conditions currently inaccessible to local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cells, cellular systems, and the molecular basis of cell structure and function. Includes instruction in cell biology, cell chemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, and structural biology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding mesoscale ocean-atmosphere interactions and their influence on global climate variability, utilizing advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current modeling limitations. While modern Earth system models (ESMs) simulate large-scale climate dynamics, their coarse resolution fails to resolve fine-scale oceanic processes—such as eddy-driven upwelling, submesoscale turbulence, and air-sea feedbacks during extreme events—that modulate heat, carbon, and moisture fluxes. These unresolved processes contribute to uncertainties in projections of regional climate extremes, ocean heat uptake, and biogeochemical cycles. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel, high-resolution coupled modeling framework integrating the Community Earth System Model (CESM) with a regional ocean model (ROMS) configured at sub-10km horizontal resolution, explicitly resolving eddies and boundary layer dynamics. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated simulations to conduct decade-scale ensemble experiments under IPCC SSP scenarios, isolating how small-scale ocean processes amplify or dampen large-scale climate feedbacks. Concurrently, machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize parameterizations of unresolved vertical mixing and aerosol-cloud interactions in turbulent marine boundary layers. The project will utilize HPC resources for model integration, petascale data storage, and statistical analysis of multi-terabyte output. Expected outcomes include quantifiable reductions in uncertainty for projections of marine heatwaves, tropical cyclone intensification, and ocean carbon sequestration rates. Results will be synthesized into publicly accessible datasets and policy-relevant metrics to guide coastal adaptation planning. By advancing the fidelity of coupled climate-ocean dynamics, this work will directly inform the next generation of IPCC assessments and mitigation strategies for vulnerable marine ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the climate system of the earth with emphasis on the physical, dynamical, and chemical interactions of the atmosphere, ocean, land, ice, and the terrestrial and marine biospheres. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, climate analysis, climate change adaptation/mitigation, climate policy, ecology, energy development, environmental impacts, marine chemistry, meteorology, and oceanography.

abstract: Language attrition—the gradual loss of linguistic competence in multilingual speakers—is an understudied phenomenon with profound implications for education, identity, and cross-cultural communication. This project seeks to model the cognitive and sociocultural mechanisms driving attrition in diaspora communities, where reduced exposure to heritage languages intersects with social network dynamics. Current theories lack empirical validation due to the complexity of longitudinal, multi-scale data integration. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with natural language processing (NLP) to simulate language use and attrition patterns across virtual communities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle large-scale simulations that incorporate individual cognitive parameters (e.g., memory decay rates), sociolinguistic interaction networks, and macro-level language policy effects. Parallelized ABM simulations will model diverse diaspora scenarios, while transformer-based NLP pipelines will analyze longitudinal speech and text corpora from multilingual speakers to validate model outputs against real-world attrition markers. Machine learning classifiers will identify predictive features of attrition risk, such as syntactic simplification or lexical diversity loss. By integrating these methods, the project aims to quantify how social cohesion, language contact intensity, and policy interventions modulate attrition trajectories. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible attrition prediction toolkit for educators and policymakers, and novel computational methods for analyzing multilingual interaction data. This work bridges gaps between psycholinguistics, computational social science, and language policy research, offering scalable tools to address language preservation challenges in globalizing societies. The requested HPC resources will enable simulations at unprecedented granularity, with an estimated 50,000 agent-hours per experimental condition and real-time processing of terabyte-scale multilingual corpora.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language-related concerns in the everyday world, including language education, acquisition of first and additional languages, discourse analysis, language assessment, literacy, and language policy and planning. Includes instruction in linguistic theory; language teaching and learning; discourse analysis; language and cognition; and language, culture, and identity.

abstract: This proposal seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the role of non-coding structural genome variations in modulating gene regulatory networks associated with complex polygenic traits. Despite advances in sequencing, the functional impact of large-scale genomic rearrangements—including inversions, duplications, and translocations—on spatiotemporal gene expression remains poorly characterized, particularly in non-model eukaryotes. Current limitations stem from the computational complexity of resolving structural variants (SVs) in repetitive regions and linking them to expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) across diverse cell types. Our project will analyze whole-genome sequencing data from 10,000 individuals, integrating long-read sequencing to resolve SVs with matched single-cell RNA-seq datasets from 15 tissue types. Custom computational pipelines will deploy graph-based genome representations and machine learning models to associate SV architectures with chromatin conformation changes and cascading transcriptional effects. Resource-intensive tasks include de novo assembly of unresolved genomic regions (requiring >50 TB RAM/node), population-scale haplotype phasing, and 3D genome simulations to predict enhancer-promoter rewiring. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a comprehensive atlas of pleiotropic SVs influencing co-regulated gene clusters, (2) mechanistic insights into how structural variants alter regulatory topologies in developmental pathways, and (3) open-source tools for multi-omics integration of SV impacts. The HPC environment is critical for managing petabytes of heterogeneous data, executing parallelized comparative genomics workflows, and training interpretable neural networks on tensor-based genomic inputs. Results will advance functional genomics by elucidating the structural basis of gene expression plasticity, with direct applications for interpreting pathogenicity of variants of uncertain significance in Mendelian disorders. This work will establish computational frameworks to bridge genome structure and function at unprecedented resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of whole genome sequences and patterns of gene expression. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular biology, genetics, protein technologies, genomic sciences and techniques, bioinformatics, and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize culinary workflows in commercial kitchens, addressing inefficiencies in food preparation, equipment utilization, and staff coordination that contribute to energy waste, operational delays, and inconsistent output. While culinary arts training emphasizes manual skill development and theoretical knowledge, the integration of computational modeling to analyze dynamic kitchen systems remains underexplored. The research problem centers on the lack of data-driven frameworks for simulating real-time kitchen operations under variable constraints, such as fluctuating order volumes, equipment failures, or staff availability. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and discrete-event simulation (DES), this project will construct a virtual kitchen environment parameterized by empirical data—including task durations, equipment energy consumption, and spatial layouts—collected from partner restaurants. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations to test scenarios ranging from routine service to high-demand events, optimizing variables like workstation placement, staff-task assignments, and equipment scheduling. Machine learning techniques will further identify patterns in simulation outputs to recommend adaptive workflow adjustments. Expected outcomes include predictive models that reduce energy use by 15–20% in test kitchens, decrease food waste through improved task synchronization, and generate training modules for culinary students focused on systemic efficiency. By bridging culinary practice with computational systems analysis, this work aims to establish a novel interdisciplinary niche within gastronomic education and food service management, advancing sustainability and operational resilience in a critical, yet computationally underserved, sector.
cip_title: Cooking and Related Culinary Arts, General.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of the cooking and related culinary arts, and that may prepare individuals for a variety of jobs within the food service industry.  Includes instruction in food preparation, cooking techniques, equipment operation and maintenance, sanitation and safety, communication skills, applicable regulations, and principles of food service management.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in social service delivery systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize resource allocation strategies for vulnerable populations. Current approaches to social welfare administration often rely on static, siloed datasets and heuristic decision-making, which can perpetuate disparities in access to services such as disability counseling, child welfare interventions, and employment support. The research problem centers on developing dynamic, evidence-based frameworks to simulate the cascading effects of policy changes, funding shifts, and demographic trends across interconnected social service networks. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning techniques to analyze multi-source datasets, including anonymized case records, regional economic indicators, and service provider capacity metrics. By simulating millions of service interaction scenarios under varying constraints, the HPC environment will enable parameter optimization for equitable resource distribution while accounting for real-world complexities like geographic barriers, cultural competencies, and staff turnover rates. The models will be validated against historical outcomes from child protective services and homeless assistance programs to ensure translational relevance. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify the long-term impacts of allocation decisions on client well-being metrics, as well as policy-sensitive dashboards for administrators to stress-test budget proposals. This work holds significance for advancing data-driven public administration in social work, particularly in identifying leverage points to reduce service gaps for marginalized communities. The computational outputs will be disseminated through open-access platforms to support evidence-based policymaking in municipal and nonprofit agencies, with potential applications in disaster response planning and cross-sector service integration. By scaling traditionally qualitative social work decision-making processes through HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for optimizing limited resources in human service systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional practice of social welfare administration and counseling, and that focus on the study of organized means of providing basic support services for vulnerable individuals and groups. Includes instruction in social welfare policy; case work planning; social counseling and intervention strategies; administrative procedures and regulations; and specific applications in areas such as child welfare and family services, probation, employment services, and disability counseling.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex decision-making dynamics within household systems under socio-economic stressors, a critical yet underexplored area in Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Traditional studies in FCS rely on survey-based or qualitative methods, which struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between economic constraints, interpersonal relationships, and adaptive consumer behaviors. The research problem centers on understanding how households negotiate competing priorities—such as budgeting, childcare, and health management—amidst external shocks like inflation or policy shifts. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that integrates real-world demographic, financial, and psychosocial data to simulate decision pathways across diverse family structures. The computational approach will involve parameterizing agents with behavioral traits derived from longitudinal FCS datasets, then simulating scenarios that test resilience strategies under variable resource allocations. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify emergent patterns in adaptive behaviors, while network analysis will map interdependencies between household members’ roles. HPC resources are essential to manage the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize simulations across thousands of virtual households, and process real-time feedback loops inherent to dynamic systems. Expected outcomes include predictive models of household resilience, identifying thresholds at which specific interventions (e.g., financial literacy programs, childcare subsidies) yield optimal outcomes. This work will advance FCS by providing a scalable, evidence-based tool for policymakers and educators, bridging gaps between micro-level family dynamics and macro-level socio-economic trends. The computational framework will also establish a replicable methodology for transdisciplinary research at the intersection of consumer behavior, resource management, and human development.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on family and consumer sciences, including how individuals develop and function in family, work, and community settings and how they relate to their physical, social, emotional, and intellectual environments.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in real-time court interpretation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models for improving the accuracy, latency, and contextual adaptability of machine-assisted legal interpretation. Court interpreters face unique demands, including rapid processing of specialized legal terminology, adherence to strict procedural norms, and management of complex linguistic phenomena (e.g., code-switching, regional dialects) under time-sensitive conditions. While human interpreters remain essential, existing translation technologies lack the domain-specific optimization required for courtroom environments. This project proposes a novel computational framework combining neural machine translation (NMT) with real-time acoustic and semantic analysis, trained on a curated multilingual corpus of legal proceedings, court documents, and interpreter training materials. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing for three core tasks: (1) training transformer-based models on legal discourse patterns and jurisdictional terminology variations; (2) simulating high-stress interpretation scenarios through generative adversarial networks (GANs) to stress-test system robustness; and (3) optimizing latency thresholds for simultaneous interpretation using distributed GPU-accelerated inference pipelines. The computational architecture will integrate speech recognition, domain-constrained translation, and prosody preservation modules, with validation against certified court interpreter benchmarks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for interpreter training, prototype systems for real-time decision support, and quantitative models of interpretation quality under varying courtroom conditions. By bridging computational linguistics with legal procedural requirements, this work aims to establish new standards for human-AI collaboration in justice systems while addressing equity gaps in language access. The requested HPC allocation will specifically support distributed training of multi-modal models across 10+ languages and runtime optimization for sub-500ms latency thresholds at 95%+ BLEU scores on legal text.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to provide accurate translation and interpretation between two or more languages for parties involved in a legal proceeding. Includes instruction in courtroom standards and procedures, court interpreting, legal terminology, consecutive interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, and sight translation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the acoustic and biomechanical dynamics of advanced performance techniques in stringed instruments, with a focus on violin and cello. While traditional pedagogical methods emphasize empirical mastery of technique, the relationship between nuanced bowing strategies, fingerboard articulation, and resultant acoustic signatures remains understudied. Current analytical tools lack the resolution to model real-time interactions between performer biomechanics, instrument resonance, and environmental acoustics at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) of string vibrations, machine learning-driven motion capture analysis of bow kinematics, and high-fidelity wave propagation simulations. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multimodal datasets, including 3D motion trajectories from professional performers, high-sample-rate audio recordings, and material stress models of instrument components. By simulating how microvariations in bow pressure, speed, and contact point influence harmonic spectra and transient responses, this study aims to quantify previously qualitative aspects of expressive performance, such as timbral warmth and dynamic articulation. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive model correlating biomechanical inputs with perceptual acoustic features, which could inform pedagogical tools for technique optimization. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets of simulated and empirical performance data, fostering interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computational acoustics and performing arts. The scalability of this approach will also permit future exploration of ensemble synchronization phenomena and stage acoustics adaptation, advancing the scientific understanding of artistry in string performance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individual to master a stringed instrument and performing arts as solo, ensemble and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the study of non-classical logical systems, particularly those addressing reasoning under uncertainty, inconsistency, and dynamic contexts, which are critical to philosophical debates about the foundations of rational argumentation. Traditional analytical methods struggle to manage the combinatorial complexity inherent in these systems—such as paraconsistent, modal, and relevance logics—limiting their scalability and practical applicability. To address this, the project proposes a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and analyze large-scale logical structures. Key objectives include automating proof verification in multi-valued logics, optimizing theorem-proving algorithms for parallel execution, and evaluating the decidability boundaries of non-classical systems through exhaustive search strategies. Computational methods will involve developing custom SAT solvers tailored to paraconsistent frameworks, implementing distributed model-checking algorithms for temporal and epistemic logics, and applying machine learning techniques to identify patterns in proof complexity across varying logical semantics. The use of HPC is essential to handle the exponential growth of possible states in dynamic reasoning scenarios and to enable rapid iteration over parameterized logical models. Expected outcomes include new insights into the computational trade-offs between logical expressivity and tractability, publicly accessible tools for automating complex philosophical analyses, and frameworks for applying non-classical logics to interdisciplinary challenges in artificial intelligence and formal ethics. By bridging formal logic with advanced computational techniques, this research aims to expand the methodological toolkit available to philosophers while demonstrating the practical relevance of logical theory to problems in knowledge representation and automated reasoning.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of valid inference, argument, and sound reasoning. Includes instruction in Classical logic, properties of argument, validity, proof, fallacies, formal and material logic, symbolic and mathematical logic, analysis, specific schools of logic, and applications to problems in other academic disciplines and professional fields.

abstract: Cardiovascular interventions require precise characterization of coronary hemodynamics to optimize clinical outcomes, yet current methods for evaluating blood flow and pressure gradients in stenotic vessels remain limited by static anatomical assessments and simplified computational models. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing patient-specific, dynamic simulations of coronary blood flow and pressure under varying physiological and procedural conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate high-resolution intravascular imaging data (e.g., optical coherence tomography) with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models to simulate transient flow patterns, shear stress distributions, and pressure gradients across stenoses before and after percutaneous coronary interventions. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify predictive hemodynamic signatures associated with procedural complications, such as stent thrombosis or edge dissection. The computational workflow will require processing multi-terabyte imaging datasets, running parallelized CFD simulations with adaptive meshing for complex geometries, and training deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data. HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative modeling demands, particularly for simulating time-resolved, three-dimensional flow dynamics in anatomically accurate coronary trees. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for post-interventional hemodynamic performance and a framework for real-time procedural decision support. This work aims to advance the personalization of interventional strategies by quantifying how anatomical and physiological variables interact to influence procedural success, potentially reducing adverse events and improving long-term patient outcomes. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source resources to foster collaboration in hemodynamics research, bridging gaps between imaging innovation, computational modeling, and clinical translation in interventional cardiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of specialized imaging and other diagnostic techniques to evaluate blood flow and pressure in the coronary arteries and chambers of the heart, and in the use of technical procedures and medications to treat abnormalities that impair the function of the cardiovascular system.

abstract: Urban landscapes present dynamic, heterogeneous ecosystems where wildlife must navigate complex sensory environments shaped by anthropogenic activity. However, the physiological and behavioral mechanisms enabling vertebrate species to adapt to urban acoustic and thermal stressors remain poorly understood, particularly for understudied taxa such as urban-adapted reptiles and amphibians. This project seeks to model the real-time interplay between environmental stressors, species-specific sensory biology, and adaptive decision-making in human-dominated habitats using high-performance computing (HPC). We will integrate biophysical data from field sensors (acoustic arrays, thermal imagers) with species-specific physiological thresholds and movement data from GPS/accelerometer-tagged animals to construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating individual and population-level responses to urban microenvironments. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized processing for 1) high-resolution spatiotemporal analysis of urban heat island dynamics and noise pollution gradients, 2) Bayesian inference of stressor impact thresholds across species, and 3) ensemble forecasting of habitat selection under future urban development scenarios. Machine learning architectures will be employed to classify behavioral modes from high-frequency movement data and predict evasion strategies across sensory modalities. The HPC environment is critical for handling the project's multi-terabyte datasets, running computationally intensive parameter sweeps for ABM validation, and executing 3D acoustic propagation models in complex urban topography. Outcomes will establish a novel framework for quantifying sensory-driven habitat suitability in anthropogenic landscapes while providing municipal planners with predictive tools to mitigate human-wildlife conflict through noise/thermal buffer design. This work bridges comparative sensory physiology, urban climatology, and computational ethology—advancing wildlife management in emerging Anthropocene ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological principles to the study of vertebrate wildlife, wildlife habitats, and related ecosystems in remote and urban areas. Includes instruction in animal ecology; adaptational biology; urban ecosystems; natural and artificial habitat management; limnology; wildlife pathology; and vertebrate zoological specializations such as mammalogy, herpetology, ichthyology, ornithology, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for analyzing underdocumented Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, many of which lack digitized corpora or tools for large-scale linguistic analysis. The research focuses on three languages from the region—Tagalog (Philippines), Māori (Aotearoa/New Zealand), and Javanese (Indonesia)—to investigate syntactic and morphological patterns that challenge existing typological frameworks. A key problem is the limited scalability of traditional manual methods for parsing complex agglutinative structures and tracking dialectal variations across historical texts. To overcome this, the project proposes deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on newly assembled multilingual datasets, including transcribed oral narratives, pre-colonial epigraphic materials, and modern literary works. Computational workflows will integrate NLP pipelines for morpheme segmentation, dependency parsing, and semantic role labeling, optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters. Phonetic modeling of tonal shifts in Māori dialects will further leverage parallel processing to analyze terabyte-scale audio recordings. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational grammars for these languages, datasets annotated with cross-linguistic metadata standards, and a containerized toolset for low-resource language analysis. Results will advance theoretical understanding of argument marking systems in Austronesian languages while providing practical resources for endangered language revitalization initiatives. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the need for distributed training of deep learning architectures, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and comparative analyses across 50+ related languages—tasks infeasible on local computing resources. This work bridges computational linguistics and area studies, offering methodological innovations applicable to understudied languages globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian and Australasian/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Geriatric patients often present with complex multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and heterogeneous responses to treatment, creating challenges in optimizing care pathways across clinical settings. This project seeks to develop computational models that predict treatment outcomes and adverse event risks in elderly populations by integrating multi-modal health data. We propose to create a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, medication adherence patterns, and socioeconomic determinants from 85,000+ geriatric patients treated at our academic health network. The computational approach will employ multiscale modeling techniques, including ensemble machine learning to identify risk trajectories, agent-based simulations of care transitions, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic models adjusted for age-related physiological changes. A key innovation involves natural language processing of unstructured clinical notes to quantify functional status and behavioral factors influencing recovery. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of petascale datasets, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification in comorbidity management, and real-time optimization of personalized treatment plans through reinforcement learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for hospital-acquired delirium risk stratification, polypharmacy interaction networks specific to aging metabolisms, and decision support systems for post-acute care placement. This work addresses critical gaps in geriatric clinical research by enabling systems-level analysis of care interactions across acute, ambulatory, and long-term settings while accounting for ethical, legal, and socioeconomic dimensions of aging populations. The computational infrastructure developed will provide a template for data-driven geriatric research that respects patient complexity while advancing precision medicine approaches tailored to older adults.
cip_definition: Research focused on the care and management of elderly patients in acute, ambulatory, community and long-term care settings, and the treatment of diseases and conditions associated with the aging process. Includes instruction in ethical and legal issues, behavioral aspects of illness, socioeconomic factors in care and rehabilitation therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in industrial process optimization, a critical challenge in applied engineering. Traditional methods for improving manufacturing systems often rely on iterative physical testing or simplified simulations, which struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between variables such as material behavior, equipment dynamics, and environmental factors. These limitations result in suboptimal resource use, energy waste, and prolonged development cycles. To overcome these barriers, this research proposes a computational framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning (ML), and real-time data assimilation to model and optimize complex manufacturing processes at scale. High-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will be coupled with ML-driven surrogate models to predict system responses under diverse operational scenarios. These models will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to capture interdependencies between process parameters, material properties, and quality metrics. The computational workflow will employ parallelized solvers and distributed training algorithms to reduce time-to-solution while maintaining accuracy. Key outcomes include the development of adaptive control strategies for minimizing energy consumption in additive manufacturing systems, predictive tools for reducing material waste in composite forming processes, and a scalable digital twin framework for real-time process monitoring. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations, enabling rapid iteration of ML models, and validating results against experimental data from collaborating industry partners. By advancing data-driven optimization capabilities, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical process models and practical industrial applications, directly supporting the program’s focus on enhancing manufacturing efficiency and systems integration. The resulting methodologies will be disseminated through open-source toolkits designed for adoption by small-to-medium enterprises, promoting broader access to advanced computational resources in applied engineering contexts.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dance as a dynamic cultural and biomechanical phenomenon through computational analysis of movement patterns and choreographic structures. While dance has historically been examined through qualitative frameworks, the growing availability of motion-capture data and digitized Labanotation archives presents an opportunity to quantitatively analyze large-scale movement datasets. However, processing these datasets—spanning diverse dance traditions, temporal scales, and cultural contexts—requires significant computational power beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying cross-cultural movement signatures and choreographic evolution patterns, which are obscured in smaller datasets or manual analysis. Using motion-capture data from global dance archives and Labanotation transcriptions, the project will apply machine learning algorithms to classify movement sequences, simulate kinematic variations, and model choreographic decision-making processes. Computational methods will include time-series analysis of joint kinematics, graph-based representations of choreographic networks, and probabilistic modeling of improvisational structures in jazz and contemporary dance. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the team aims to process over 10,000 hours of annotated dance data, enabling comparative studies of biomechanical efficiency in classical ballet versus folk traditions, as well as the cultural transmission of gestural motifs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of computationally tagged movement elements, tools for automated Labanotation generation, and new theoretical frameworks linking choreographic complexity to cultural narratives. This work will provide dance scholars with unprecedented scalability in analyzing movement as data, while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations between performing arts and computational sciences. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations and training deep learning models on heterogeneous movement corpora, tasks that are infeasible without distributed computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to express ideas, feelings, and/or inner visions through the performance of one or more of the dance disciplines, including but not limited to ballet, modern, jazz, ethnic, and folk dance, and that focuses on the study and analysis of dance as a cultural phenomenon. Includes instruction in technique, choreography, Laban notation, dance history and criticism, and dance production.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize cross-cultural consumer decision-making processes in digitally fragmented global markets. The central problem lies in the inadequacy of traditional consumer behavior models to account for real-time, nonlinear interactions between cultural variables (e.g., values, communication norms) and digital platform dynamics (e.g., social media algorithms, localized e-commerce interfaces) in international marketing contexts. Current approaches often rely on static, country-level cultural dimensions or simplified A/B testing frameworks, which fail to capture emergent patterns in hyper-localized, multi-platform consumer journeys. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that simulates cross-cultural consumer interactions at scale, integrating natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual sentiment analysis, reinforcement learning to model adaptive purchasing behaviors, and network analysis to map information diffusion across hybrid online-offline ecosystems. The computational model will ingest heterogeneous datasets—including geotagged social media activity, cross-border e-commerce transaction logs, and cultural context embeddings from large language models—to simulate decision pathways under varying cultural and technological constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) predictive insights into how micro-cultural variables interact with platform-specific features to drive conversion rates, 2) an open-source toolkit for optimizing global marketing campaigns across digital fragmentation boundaries, and 3) quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural adaptation costs in market entry strategies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for running parallel simulations across 50+ cultural configurations while maintaining sub-second latency for real-time parameter adjustments, enabling unprecedented granularity in modeling emergent international consumer behaviors. This work aims to establish computational cultural analytics as a distinct interdisciplinary domain within international marketing research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing activities in enterprises primarily engaged in exporting or importing goods and services in world markets. Includes instruction in international trade controls, foreign trade operations, locating markets, negotiation practices, monetary issues, and international public relations.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the computational modeling of entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation strategies for early-stage ventures operating in highly dynamic markets. The core problem lies in the absence of scalable frameworks that integrate real-time market volatility, cognitive biases, and heterogeneous stakeholder inputs—factors critical to entrepreneurial success but traditionally analyzed through qualitative or static quantitative models. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop an adaptive simulation environment that captures multi-agent interactions, stochastic market events, and iterative decision pathways. The computational approach will combine agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate thousands of entrepreneurial scenarios, varying parameters such as funding cycles, competitive responses, and regulatory shocks. Large-scale datasets from crowdfunding platforms, pitch competitions, and startup accelerators will be processed to train and validate models, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will analyze unstructured feedback from investors and customers to refine decision heuristics. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to quantify risk-reward tradeoffs in resource allocation, identify resilience patterns across venture typologies, and generate prescriptive insights for adaptive pivoting strategies. This work bridges behavioral economics, computational social science, and entrepreneurial practice, offering a novel toolkit for mitigating systemic failures in early-stage ventures. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the parallelized simulations, high-dimensional optimization tasks, and real-time data integration required to model complex entrepreneurial ecosystems at fidelity impractical on conventional systems. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation platforms and interdisciplinary partnerships with incubators, advancing both academic research and applied entrepreneurial education.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform development, marketing and management functions associated with owning and operating a business.

abstract: This project seeks to advance computational photography techniques for commercial applications by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in processing ultra-high-resolution visual data. Commercial photography increasingly relies on workflows involving 4K/8K video, gigapixel image composites, and AI-driven post-processing, which demand intensive computational resources. Current consumer-grade systems struggle with processing latency, memory constraints, and scalability when handling multi-layered projects common in advertising, product visualization, and archival documentation. The research will develop optimized pipelines for neural rendering, real-time HDR fusion, and AI-assisted color grading using distributed computing frameworks. Key methodologies include parallelized processing of image stacks across GPU clusters, training domain-specific generative models for texture synthesis, and implementing physics-based light transport simulations to enhance digital scene reconstruction accuracy. The project will utilize containerized environments to standardize workflows while maintaining compatibility with industry-standard software suites. Outcomes aim to reduce render times for complex composites by 60-80%, enable interactive editing of 100+ layer projects, and improve fidelity in virtual product photography simulations. This work will directly benefit commercial photography education by creating open-source tools for managing computational workflows, while advancing research at the intersection of artistic practice and computational imaging. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC resources can democratize access to advanced digital production techniques typically limited to large studios, fostering innovation in visual storytelling for small-to-medium enterprises. The computational frameworks developed will be validated through case studies in automotive advertising photography and cultural heritage digitization, with performance benchmarks published to guide future resource allocation in arts computing initiatives.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: Soil health and nutrient dynamics are critical determinants of agricultural productivity, yet predicting their spatial-temporal variability at field scales remains a persistent challenge due to complex interactions between soil physicochemical properties, microbial activity, and crop-root processes. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, process-based modeling framework to simulate soil-crop systems under diverse management practices, with a focus on optimizing nitrogen and phosphorus use efficiency. The research integrates soil hydrology, biogeochemistry, and plant physiology models into a coupled computational system, parameterized using field data from long-term agronomic trials across contrasting soil types. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-scale interactions, including meter-scale heterogeneity in soil organic matter, pore-scale nutrient transport, and hourly microbial metabolic processes across growing seasons. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to assimilate remote sensing data (hyperspectral and thermal imagery) and sensor-network measurements into the model, enabling dynamic calibration. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of soil nutrient availability at sub-field resolution, (2) quantification of management-induced trade-offs between short-term crop yields and long-term soil carbon stocks, and (3) open-source tools for simulating cover crop impacts on nitrogen leaching risks. By leveraging HPC capabilities to parallelize ensemble simulations across thousands of soil-crop-management combinations, this work will provide actionable insights for precision nutrient management, directly addressing the urgent need to reduce agricultural greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining food security. The computational framework will be designed for transferability to other cropping systems, establishing a foundation for scalable soil health analytics in sustainable agronomy.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that generally focuses on the scientific classification of soils, soil properties, and their relationship to agricultural crops. Includes instruction in soil chemistry, soil physics, soil biology, soil fertility, morphogenesis, mineralogy, hydrology, agronomy, and soil conservation and management.

abstract: Radiation therapy relies on precise dose delivery to maximize tumor control while minimizing damage to healthy tissues. Current treatment planning systems face challenges in accurately modeling complex scenarios involving tissue heterogeneity, dynamic anatomical changes, and emerging modalities such as ultra-high-dose-rate (FLASH) radiotherapy. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport coupled with machine learning-driven optimization frameworks. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating patient-specific phantoms incorporating 4D CT and functional imaging data to model anatomical motion and tissue response variability, (2) implementing GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo dose calculations for charged particle beams in heterogeneous media, and (3) training neural networks to predict optimal beam configurations under biological uncertainty constraints. The computational workflows will leverage high-performance computing resources to manage the substantial processing demands of iterative simulation-optimization cycles, which require ~10^6 core-hours for comprehensive parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include validated models for FLASH proton therapy normal tissue sparing effects (±2% accuracy) and an open-source framework for adaptive radiotherapy planning that accounts for interfractional anatomical changes. By improving the physical accuracy of dose deposition predictions in moving targets near critical structures, this work directly supports the program's mission to advance therapeutic radiologic physics through computational innovation. The resulting tools will enable clinical researchers to test novel fractionation schemes and beam modalities while maintaining compliance with radiation safety protocols through enhanced secondary dose calculations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physical aspects of the therapeutic applications of x-rays, gamma rays, electron, and other charged particle beams, neutrons, and radiations from sealed radionuclide sources; and with the equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to detect and analyze complex financial fraud and money laundering networks, which increasingly exploit decentralized financial systems and encrypted transaction channels. The rise of cryptocurrency, cross-border digital payments, and AI-driven obfuscation techniques has outpaced traditional forensic accounting tools, creating critical gaps in identifying illicit financial flows tied to organized crime and terrorism. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets of transactional records, blockchain ledgers, and unstructured data (e.g., invoices, communications) across global jurisdictions. Machine learning models—including graph neural networks (GNNs) and transformer-based anomaly detection—will be trained to recognize evolving fraud patterns, such as layered transaction networks, shell company linkages, and behavioral anomalies in accounting metadata. Parallelized algorithms will reconstruct temporal financial networks, tracing asset concealment strategies while adhering to legal constraints (e.g., privacy laws, chain-of-custody requirements). Computational experiments will validate the framework against historical cases of terrorist financing and corporate fraud, with iterative refinement using adversarial simulations to counter evasion tactics. Outcomes will include an open-source toolset for forensic analysts, optimized for GPU-accelerated environments, to prioritize high-risk transactions and visualize concealed financial relationships. This work directly supports homeland security priorities by enhancing the speed and precision of financial evidence analysis, reducing the manual burden on investigators, and providing actionable intelligence for disrupting illicit networks. The scalability of the proposed methods will also inform policy discussions on regulating emergent financial technologies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of conducting investigations into financial crime, terrorist activity, and the analysis and use of accounting data as evidence. Includes instruction in the principles of accounting, investigative auditing, computer investigations, accounting system documents and software, business corruption, criminal and terrorist financial networks, international money markets and movement, net worth analysis, financial fraud, exposing concealed assets, records seizure, fraud and money laundering statutes, fraud case initiation, case management, and case presentation.

abstract: Occupational and environmental health nursing faces critical challenges in understanding multifactorial interactions between workplace hazards, environmental exposures, and population health outcomes. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to integrate large-scale, heterogeneous datasets—such as electronic health records, environmental sensor data, occupational injury reports, and geospatial information—limiting the ability to predict risks or design targeted interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that identify high-risk scenarios and optimize prevention strategies for workers in industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and construction. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) analyzing longitudinal patterns of occupational exposures and their association with chronic health conditions using machine learning techniques, and (2) simulating workplace-specific intervention scenarios through agent-based modeling to evaluate their potential impact on reducing injuries and illnesses. Computational methods will include ensemble learning algorithms to handle imbalanced health outcome data, graph-based analytics to map exposure networks across job roles, and geospatial clustering to identify regional risk hotspots. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of multimodal data, training complex neural networks, and running parallelized simulations across diverse workplace configurations. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized exposure thresholds linked to respiratory and musculoskeletal disorders, predictive tools for early intervention in high-risk populations, and scalable models for simulating safety protocols under dynamic occupational conditions. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making in occupational health settings, enhance regulatory guidelines for exposure monitoring, and contribute to the development of precision health strategies tailored to worker populations. By integrating computational advances with nursing expertise, the project aims to bridge critical gaps in workplace health surveillance and prevention.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver nursing health care services to workers and worker populations in clinical settings and at job sites. Includes instruction in public and community health, occupational safety and health, occupational health surveillance, case management, fitness for duty testing, medication, allergies and immunization, emergency and ambulatory care, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of psychosocial resilience in aging populations by analyzing complex longitudinal datasets to identify predictors of adaptive cognitive and emotional functioning in older adults. With global populations aging rapidly, there is an urgent need to develop scalable, data-driven insights that inform counseling interventions to support mental health and well-being in later life. The research integrates heterogeneous data sources—including cognitive assessments, biomarker profiles, psychosocial surveys, and electronic health records—to model trajectories of resilience and risk across diverse geropsychological domains. A key challenge lies in disentangling dynamic interactions between biological aging processes, social determinants, and psychological outcomes, which require computationally intensive methods. The proposed work employs multilevel machine learning models (e.g., ensemble algorithms, recurrent neural networks) to analyze temporal patterns in high-dimensional datasets from three longitudinal aging studies (N > 15,000 participants). High-performance computing resources are essential for training these models on clustered data with nested covariates, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized grid searches, and conducting large-scale simulations to test intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of modifiable psychosocial factors that buffer against age-related cognitive decline, 2) predictive tools to personalize counseling strategies for older adults at risk of isolation or depressive symptoms, and 3) open-source computational frameworks for analyzing aging-related psychological data. By leveraging advanced analytics, this work aims to bridge gaps between geropsychological research and applied counseling practice, ultimately informing preventive approaches to enhance quality of life in aging populations. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale datasets and running iterative model validations necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve these objectives within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychology of aging and of elderly individuals and populations, with reference to growth and decline across the life span.
