Deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models) will be trained to classify SLI subtypes and predict responsiveness to specific interventions, while generative models will simulate individualized language exercises tailored to students’ evolving needs. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of processing high-dimensional speech data, optimizing hyperparameters for diverse learner profiles, and validating models across multi-site datasets. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated progress monitoring, a validated taxonomy of SLI subtypes linked to intervention efficacy, and scalable frameworks for generating adaptive lesson plans. By bridging computational advances with special education pedagogy, this work aims to empower educators with evidence-based, real-time decision-support systems, ultimately improving academic and communicative outcomes for students with SLI. The project aligns with federal mandates for data-informed individualized education programs (IEPs) and addresses urgent gaps in equitable access to specialized instructional resources.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Speech or Language Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study and design of educational services for children or adults with speech and language impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with speech and language impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with speech disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Women’s health research faces unique challenges due to the biological, social, and environmental complexity underlying sex-specific conditions. This project addresses critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms of understudied women’s health conditions, including endometriosis, preeclampsia, and hormone-responsive cancers, through integrative computational modeling. A key barrier to progress is the limited ability to analyze high-dimensional datasets—spanning genomics, proteomics, electronic health records, and imaging—while accounting for dynamic hormonal interactions and population-level heterogeneity. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining machine learning, multiscale simulations, and genome-wide association studies (GWAS). The computational workflow will integrate multi-omics data from clinical cohorts (n > 50,000) to identify subtype-specific biomarkers and predictive signatures for disease risk, progression, and therapeutic response. Deep learning models will map hormone receptor interactions across tissues, while agent-based simulations will model cellular microenvironment dynamics in conditions like uterine fibroid growth. Large-scale parallelization will enable iterative optimization of these models across parameter spaces and validation against independent clinical datasets. Anticipated outcomes include the discovery of novel therapeutic targets for endometriosis, risk stratification tools for preeclampsia, and mechanistic insights into racial disparities in gynecologic cancer outcomes. By leveraging HPC resources, this project will overcome current limitations in data processing speed, model complexity, and reproducibility, enabling transformative insights into conditions that disproportionately affect women. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for gender-aware health analytics, fostering collaboration in women’s health research. This work directly aligns with national priorities to reduce health inequities and advance precision medicine for underrepresented populations in clinical research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Women's Health

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dramatic performance dynamics through large-scale simulation and analysis of theatrical interactions. The central research problem lies in understanding how complex variables—such as actor positioning, vocal modulation, audience sightlines, and real-time emotional feedback—collectively influence the efficacy of live performances. Traditional methods of analyzing these dynamics rely on manual observation, limited-scale experiments, or post-hoc surveys, which struggle to capture the multivariate, nonlinear relationships inherent in theatrical spaces. To address this, we propose a computational framework that integrates agent-based modeling, real-time motion capture datasets, and machine learning to simulate audience-performer interactions within virtualized theater environments. Using HPC resources, we will model diverse performance scenarios across historical and contemporary theater architectures (e.g., proscenium, thrust, arena stages) and populate them with AI-driven audience agents trained on behavioral datasets from prior productions. The simulations will quantify how adjustments to blocking, acoustics, or lighting affect collective audience engagement metrics, derived from gaze-tracking and physiological response proxies. Additionally, NLP-driven analysis of dramatic texts will correlate linguistic patterns with optimal emotional pacing in simulated performances. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for directors and dramaturgs to pre-visualize production choices, a repository of performance optimization strategies tied to specific theatrical forms, and new insights into the relationship between spatial design and narrative impact. By bridging computational methods with performance theory, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-informed theatrical practice while preserving the artistic integrity of live drama. The project’s scale—requiring parallel processing of high-fidelity simulations across thousands of agent interactions—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve timely results and enable iterative, hypothesis-driven experimentation.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Drama and Dramatics/ Theatre Arts, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of dramatic works and their performance. Includes instruction in major works of dramatic literature, dramatic styles and types, and the principles of organizing and producing full live or filmed productions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate complex driver behavior dynamics for improving instructional strategies in driver and safety education. Traditional driver education curricula rely on static scenarios and anecdotal evidence, which often fail to account for the interplay of cognitive, environmental, and situational variables affecting real-world decision-making. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create large-scale, agent-based simulations that integrate heterogeneous data streams, including driver telemetry, traffic patterns, and physiological stress indicators. These simulations will model high-risk scenarios (e.g., distracted driving, adverse weather responses) with parametric variations to assess how different instructional methods influence trainee outcomes. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to analyze simulation outputs, identifying critical thresholds for skill retention and risk mitigation. The computational workflow requires parallel processing to handle millions of agent interactions and real-time data assimilation from existing driver education datasets. Expected outcomes include evidence-based frameworks for optimizing lesson plans, adaptive training modules tailored to individual learner profiles, and predictive tools for evaluating instructor interventions. By quantifying the efficacy of pedagogical approaches under dynamically variable conditions, this research will directly enhance the precision and scalability of driver and safety teacher education programs. The resulting models and datasets will be made available to educational institutions, enabling data-driven revisions to certification standards and curricular guidelines. This work underscores the transformative potential of computational modeling in teacher education, bridging the gap between theoretical instruction and practical competency in safety-critical domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach driver and safety education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Museums face growing challenges in managing complex, heterogeneous collections while balancing preservation, accessibility, and public engagement. This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational approaches for artifact conservation risk assessment and immersive exhibit design by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current methods for evaluating environmental degradation risks (e.g., humidity, light exposure) rely on localized datasets and static models, limiting predictive accuracy across diverse collection types and global climate scenarios. Simultaneously, the increasing demand for interactive digital exhibits requires real-time rendering capabilities that exceed conventional computational resources. Our research proposes a dual computational framework: (1) developing machine learning models trained on aggregated conservation metadata from 50+ institutions to predict material-specific deterioration patterns under variable conditions, and (2) creating GPU-accelerated simulations for testing virtual exhibit layouts through crowd dynamics modeling and ray-traced lighting analysis. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale conservation records, parallelized climate scenario modeling, and AI-driven optimization of 3D artifact reconstructions. Expected outcomes include an open-source risk assessment toolkit for preventive conservation and a procedural generation system for designing accessible virtual exhibits that adapt to visitor interaction patterns. This work bridges computational science with museological practice, offering scalable solutions for collection stewardship while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in digital heritage. By integrating large-scale data analytics with real-time visualization capabilities, the project aims to establish new standards for evidence-based conservation planning and democratized access to cultural collections through computationally enhanced museum experiences.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the attitudes, knowledge, and skills required to develop, prepare, organize, administer, conserve, store and retrieve artifacts, exhibits and entire collections in museums and galleries, and that prepares individuals to assume curatorial, technical and managerial positions in museums. Includes instruction in institutional management, acquisition, exhibit design, conservation, packing techniques, and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in diagnosing and resolving hardware-level failures in complex computing systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate fault scenarios. Current diagnostic protocols in computer installation and repair rely heavily on manual testing and static decision trees, which struggle to adapt to the growing diversity of modern hardware architectures, including heterogeneous systems integrating CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators. The research problem centers on the lack of dynamic, predictive tools capable of mapping failure modes across evolving hardware configurations. To overcome this, the project will employ parallelized computational workflows to simulate hardware malfunctions under controlled conditions. Using HPC clusters, we will generate synthetic datasets representing failures in power delivery systems, memory hierarchies, and thermal management components, correlating these with performance degradation metrics. Machine learning models, trained on these datasets, will be optimized to identify failure precursors in real-time telemetry data from instrumented systems. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulations will assess the reliability of repair protocols under variable environmental and workload stresses. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for rapid iteration across thousands of simulated hardware configurations—necessitate access to scalable HPC resources with GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and large-scale parameter sweeps. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic framework that dynamically prioritizes repair actions based on probabilistic fault localization, reducing mean time-to-repair (MTTR) by an estimated 30-50% in benchmark cases. The project will also produce annotated simulation datasets for educational use, enhancing training modules in hardware troubleshooting curricula. By bridging computational modeling with applied repair techniques, this work aims to advance adaptive maintenance strategies for next-generation computing infrastructure while providing hands-on HPC exposure to technicians-in-training.
cip_title: Computer Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair computers and related instruments. Includes instruction in power supplies, number systems, memory structure, buffers and registers, microprocessor design, peripheral equipment, programming, and networking.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing environmental and economic challenges posed by textile overproduction and waste in the apparel industry, driven by inaccurate demand forecasting and shifting consumer preferences. Traditional methods for trend prediction rely on historical sales data and static demographic analyses, which fail to capture the dynamic interplay of socio-cultural, economic, and psychological factors influencing modern consumption patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale social media analytics, real-time retail data, and agent-based modeling to simulate consumer decision-making processes and predict regionalized demand for textile products. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process terabytes of unstructured data—including image-based trend content from platforms like Instagram and TikTok, sentiment analysis of user-generated reviews, and macroeconomic indicators—while training machine learning models to identify emergent patterns. Agent-based simulations will further model how peer influence, sustainability awareness, and pricing strategies interact to shape purchasing behavior across diverse consumer segments. The resulting predictive tools will enable apparel producers to optimize production schedules, reduce material waste, and align inventory with localized demand, fostering resource-efficient practices. By situating computational social science within textile and apparel research, this project advances interdisciplinary methodologies for sustainable fashion systems while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional domains. Outcomes will include open-source predictive models, a dataset linking digital behavior to textile consumption, and actionable guidelines for industry stakeholders to mitigate overproduction.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the development of textile products and their distribution and use in terms of the psychological, social, economic, and physical needs of consumers. Includes instruction in the production, distribution, marketing, and end use of various apparel and textile products.

abstract: Agricultural productivity and veterinary health face escalating challenges from emerging pathogens, climate variability, and the need for sustainable practices. A critical bottleneck in addressing these challenges lies in the computational limitations of analyzing complex biological systems, particularly when integrating multi-omics data (genomics, proteomics, metabolomics) to unravel disease mechanisms or optimize traits in crops and livestock. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale simulations and data-driven modeling of plant-pathogen interactions, host immune responses in livestock, and genome-to-phenome predictions in agriculturally relevant species. The research will employ machine learning frameworks to analyze terabyte-scale datasets from RNA sequencing, hyperspectral imaging, and sensor-derived phenotypic data, alongside molecular dynamics simulations to study protein-ligand interactions for novel veterinary drug discovery. Key computational workflows include genome-wide association studies (GWAS) accelerated via parallelized algorithms, agent-based modeling of disease transmission in livestock populations, and neural networks trained to predict stress-tolerant crop phenotypes under varying environmental conditions. The allocation of HPC resources will facilitate the processing of heterogeneous datasets at unprecedented resolution, reducing analysis times from months to days. Anticipated outcomes include identifying genetic markers for drought-resistant sorghum cultivars, optimizing vaccine targets for avian influenza strains, and validating predictive models for mastitis resistance in dairy cattle. These advances will directly inform translational breeding programs and precision veterinary interventions, enhancing resilience in agricultural systems. By bridging computational scalability with biological complexity, this work underscores the critical role of HPC infrastructure in accelerating innovation for food security and animal health.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in agriculture or veterinary medicine or science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social interaction patterns among older adults in digitally connected communities, leveraging computational modeling to explore how emergent technologies influence psychosocial well-being in aging populations. While gerontology is traditionally situated within health sciences, this study adopts a social science lens to analyze how older adults navigate, adapt to, and reshape virtual social ecosystems—a niche intersecting aging studies, digital sociology, and human-computer interaction. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable frameworks to quantify the bidirectional relationship between technology-mediated communication and age-related shifts in social needs, particularly in heterogeneous populations with varying digital literacies. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating longitudinal social network evolution among older adults, integrating empirical data from wearable sensors, social media engagement metrics, and demographic surveys. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale parameter sweeps to test hypotheses about how algorithmic personalization, platform accessibility features, and cohort-specific cultural norms modulate outcomes such as loneliness, social capital accumulation, and intergenerational connectivity. The ABM will incorporate machine learning submodules trained on real-world interaction datasets to refine decision rules for agent behaviors, requiring GPU-accelerated workloads for both model calibration and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for predicting technology adoption barriers in aging populations and evidence-based insights into designing inclusive digital spaces that align with psychosocial aging trajectories. By bridging gerontological health research with computational social science methodologies, this work aims to inform policy and industry strategies that prioritize equitable social participation in an increasingly digitized aging society.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the integration of bio-informed adaptive systems into building envelope design, addressing the gap between static architectural solutions and dynamic environmental demands. Current building systems often rely on fixed parameters for thermal regulation, acoustics, and daylighting, leading to energy inefficiencies and occupant discomfort in fluctuating conditions. By leveraging biologically inspired models—such as plant stomatal response to light and humidity or animal skin pore dynamics—we aim to simulate and prototype building skins capable of real-time, climate-responsive adaptation. The research employs high-fidelity fluid dynamics (CFD) and agent-based modeling to simulate multi-scale interactions between adaptive materials, environmental variables, and occupant behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for resolving the nonlinear, time-dependent feedback loops inherent in these systems, particularly when scaling from component-level simulations (e.g., phase-change material panels) to whole-building performance analysis. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs by training surrogate models on HPC-generated datasets, enabling rapid exploration of design permutations. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for bio-responsive architectural design, quantitative benchmarks for adaptive envelope efficiency across climate zones, and novel metrics for evaluating resilience under extreme weather scenarios. This work bridges computational biology, material science, and architectural practice, offering a pathway to reduce building-sector energy consumption by 15–30% in retrofitted structures while maintaining occupant-centric performance. The requested resources will support parametric optimization runs, sensitivity analyses, and large-scale validation against experimental data from partner institutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of advanced technology to building design and construction, retrofitting existing buildings, and efficient operation of buildings, including lighting and daylight design, acoustics, solar design, building conservation, and energy-conscious design. Includes instruction in architecture, building technology, civil and structural engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental control systems, sustainability, and computer tools and applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex dynamics of intergenerational resource allocation within families, a critical yet underexplored area in Work and Family Studies. While traditional research in this field relies on qualitative surveys or small-scale quantitative studies, the proposed work addresses a gap in scalable, data-driven simulations of how families navigate competing demands—such as childcare, eldercare, financial planning, and time management—under varying socioeconomic conditions. The research problem centers on understanding how systemic stressors (e.g., inflation, healthcare access disparities) disrupt decision-making patterns in households, particularly in marginalized communities where resource constraints amplify trade-offs. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate household behavior across diverse demographic profiles, integrating real-world datasets on income, health outcomes, and policy landscapes. Computational workflows will parallelize thousands of scenario iterations to capture nonlinear interactions between individual choices, institutional policies, and macroeconomic trends. Machine learning techniques will then identify emergent patterns in caregiving strategies and resilience mechanisms. By quantifying the cascading effects of policy interventions (e.g., subsidized childcare, flexible work mandates) on family well-being, this research aims to generate actionable frameworks for policymakers and educators. The use of HPC is critical to managing the high dimensionality of variables (e.g., cultural norms, geographic disparities) and enabling probabilistic forecasts at population scales. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for family resource educators and validated metrics for assessing the equity of caregiving support systems. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, economics, and human development, advancing Work and Family Studies into data-intensive domains while preserving its focus on applied, human-centered outcomes.
cip_definition: An introductory program that focuses on family and consumer science concepts and principles at the basic and vocational levels, and the various potential career paths open to interested students. Includes instruction in career, community, and family connections; family and family/consumer resources; human development; interpersonal relationships; nutrition and wellness; parenting; and career possibilities in various related areas.

abstract: Plant diseases caused by airborne fungal pathogens pose significant risks to global food security, yet the interplay between localized microclimatic dynamics and spore dispersal mechanisms remains poorly quantified. This project seeks to model the multiscale environmental drivers of *Puccinia graminis* (stem rust) epidemics in wheat agroecosystems, integrating high-resolution atmospheric data, host phenology, and pathogen life cycle traits to predict outbreak trajectories. Current limitations in forecasting stem rust spread stem from an inability to resolve fine-scale turbulence, moisture gradients, and thermal fluctuations that govern spore viability and deposition patterns. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for 3D wind field reconstruction, agent-based modeling of spore cloud dynamics, and probabilistic machine learning to link microclimate heterogeneity with infection risk. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel execution of ensemble simulations across diverse agro-meteorological scenarios, processing terabytes of remote sensing data and in-field sensor inputs to parameterize boundary conditions. Key innovations include the coupling of Lagrangian particle tracking for spore transport with reaction-diffusion models of leaf surface infection processes, scaled across canopy architectures. Expected outcomes include the first spatially explicit risk maps of stem rust propagation under shifting precipitation regimes, validated against experimental plot trials in collaboration with the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT). By quantifying threshold conditions for epidemic emergence, this work will inform real-time decision support systems for precision fungicide deployment and climate-resilient crop placement. The computational pipelines developed will establish a template for analyzing aerially transmitted plant pathogens, bridging gaps between micrometeorology, fluid dynamics, and disease ecology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: The clinical management of hematologic malignancies remains challenged by interpatient heterogeneity in treatment response and the dynamic evolution of resistance mechanisms. While multi-omics profiling has generated vast datasets linking genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic features to clinical outcomes, integrating these high-dimensional data streams into predictive models for precision oncology requires computational resources beyond conventional infrastructure. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop and validate machine learning frameworks that unify multi-omics data from large-scale clinical cohorts of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) patients. The computational approach will focus on three pillars: (1) scalable preprocessing of whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq, and chromatin accessibility data using parallelized workflows; (2) training of ensemble neural networks to predict therapeutic response by harmonizing multimodal inputs; and (3) Bayesian inference modeling to map clonal evolutionary trajectories underlying relapse. The HPC environment is critical for managing datasets exceeding 500 TB, optimizing hyperparameters across >10,000 GPU hours, and simulating tumor-immune interactions at single-cell resolution. Expected outcomes include clinically validated algorithms for early prediction of venetoclax resistance in AML and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell failure in DLBCL, accompanied by open-source tools for real-time genomic risk stratification. By enabling complex pattern recognition across evolving tumor ecosystems, this work aims to establish a computational pipeline for translating multi-omics discoveries into adaptive therapeutic strategies, directly addressing the National Cancer Institute’s priority of bridging computational biology with interventional trial design. The requested resources will accelerate the development of AI-driven decision support systems capable of guiding risk-adapted therapy in hematologic malignancies.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hematology-Oncology

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic spatial organization of cellular components during tissue morphogenesis, a fundamental yet poorly understood process in developmental anatomy. A critical gap persists in modeling how mechanical forces and intracellular signaling pathways collectively drive the emergence of three-dimensional tissue architecture. To address this, we propose an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with continuum mechanics to simulate multicellular systems at subcellular resolution. The ABM component will represent individual cells as discrete entities with rule-based behaviors, while finite element methods will model stress propagation across extracellular matrices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the scale of these simulations, which require tracking >10^5 interacting cellular agents with micrometer-level spatial precision over developmental timescales (48-72 simulated hours). Parallelized code will leverage GPU acceleration to optimize force calculations and matrix solvers. Experimental validation will utilize time-lapse microscopy datasets of avian limb bud development, with machine learning pipelines (deployed on HPC clusters) quantifying cytoskeletal dynamics and strain patterns from 4D imaging data. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of critical force thresholds regulating epithelial folding patterns, 2) predictive models of tissue buckling under genetic perturbation scenarios, and 3) open-source simulation tools for visualizing mechanochemical coupling in developing tissues. This work will advance our mechanistic understanding of how cellular-scale processes generate anatomical form, with implications for congenital defect research and bioengineered tissue design. The requested computing allocation (500,000 CPU-core hours, 2 TB RAM allocation, and GPU node access) will enable parameter space exploration across physiologically relevant mechanical regimes currently inaccessible through conventional computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_title: Cell/ Cellular Biology and Anatomical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cell/cellular biology and anatomical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven framework to model and optimize pedagogical strategies in STEM teacher training programs using high-performance computing (HPC). Despite advancements in educational theory, teacher professional development often relies on qualitative assessments and small-scale studies, limiting the scalability of evidence-based practices. This work addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing large, multimodal datasets—including classroom video recordings, student performance metrics, and teacher reflections—to identify patterns in effective instructional techniques. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) to evaluate teacher-student discourse, computer vision algorithms to assess classroom engagement dynamics, and agent-based modeling to simulate the impact of pedagogical interventions across diverse educational contexts. These methods require HPC resources due to the scale of data (10,000+ hours of video from 200 classrooms) and the complexity of training deep learning models for real-time feedback systems. By parallelizing tasks such as feature extraction from video streams and optimizing hyperparameters for ensemble models, HPC will enable rapid iteration of simulations testing how variations in lesson pacing, questioning strategies, and differentiation practices affect student outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for quantifying teaching effectiveness, personalized recommendations for teacher professional development, and generative models that propose context-aware instructional adaptations. This work will directly inform the design of competency-based training modules for pre-service and in-service STEM teachers, with broader implications for reducing disparities in subject-specific pedagogical training. The resource request prioritizes GPU nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale simulations of classroom interaction networks.
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Subject Areas, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education, specific academic and vocational programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Vietnamese linguistic and literary structures. Vietnamese, a tonal language with significant dialectal diversity and a rich literary tradition, presents unique challenges for large-scale linguistic modeling, particularly in parsing syntactic patterns, mapping dialectal variations, and analyzing historical textual evolution. Traditional methods, constrained by limited computational power, struggle to process the volume and complexity of data required for comprehensive studies. This research aims to develop a scalable computational framework to analyze multi-regional Vietnamese corpora, including digitized classical literature, modern texts, and oral narratives, to uncover patterns in tonal shifts, lexical borrowing, and dialect convergence. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic and syntactic parsing, coupled with phonetic alignment algorithms to map tonal variations across dialects. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabytes of text and audio data, training deep learning models to identify diachronic changes in literary styles and regional speech patterns. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access datasets annotated for tonal, syntactic, and dialectal features, as well as tools for automated analysis of Vietnamese historical texts and contemporary media. These resources will support advancements in Vietnamese NLP applications—such as speech recognition systems tailored to regional accents—and provide scholars with new methodologies for studying linguistic evolution and literary trends. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this project bridges a critical gap in Vietnamese studies, offering scalable solutions for preserving linguistic heritage and enhancing cross-disciplinary research in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Vietnamese language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The development of predictive models for molecular interaction networks remains a critical challenge in cheminformatics, particularly in the context of drug discovery and chemical property optimization. Current approaches often rely on simplified approximations or small-scale datasets, limiting their accuracy and generalizability. This project seeks to address these limitations by integrating large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with graph-based machine learning (ML) to model complex molecular interactions at an unprecedented scale. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform ensemble MD simulations of diverse ligand-protein systems, generating terabytes of trajectory data to capture dynamic binding behaviors. Concurrently, graph neural networks (GNNs) will be trained on curated chemical databases containing millions of annotated small molecules, with explicit encoding of 3D conformational flexibility and quantum-mechanical descriptors. The computational workflow requires distributed GPU-accelerated nodes for parallel MD sampling and specialized hardware for optimizing memory-intensive GNN architectures. Key outcomes include: (1) a publicly available dataset of simulated ligand-protein interaction pathways, (2) open-source software for coupling MD-derived features with ML-based activity prediction, and (3) validated models for prioritizing drug candidates with multi-target polypharmacology profiles. By bridging physics-based simulations with data-driven learning, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for predicting off-target effects and binding affinity landscapes, directly addressing reproducibility challenges in virtual screening. The requested HPC allocation is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of molecular conformations and interaction networks, enabling calculations that exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters. Successful implementation will provide the cheminformatics community with scalable tools for rational molecular design while advancing fundamental understanding of structure-dynamics-activity relationships.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on applying computer science approaches in the representation, analysis, design, and modeling of chemical structures and associated metadata, such as biological activity endpoints and physicochemical properties. Includes instruction in chemical information technology, computational chemistry, computer science, database design, molecular modeling, scientific computing, and statistics.

abstract: Current disaster response frameworks often struggle to adapt to the complex, dynamic nature of modern crises, particularly when integrating real-time data streams and coordinating multi-jurisdictional efforts. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing an artificial intelligence-enhanced incident command system (ICS) optimization platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will employ a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling to simulate population movements and responder behaviors with reinforcement learning algorithms trained on historical disaster datasets. HPC capabilities will enable large-scale parallelization of scenario testing across diverse hazard contexts, including cascading disasters where natural and anthropogenic risks intersect. Key technical challenges involve real-time assimilation of heterogeneous data sources—such as social media feeds, IoT sensor networks, and satellite imagery—into decision support modules while maintaining ICS protocol compliance. The computational framework will incorporate ethical constraints through multi-objective optimization techniques that balance operational efficiency with equity considerations in resource allocation. Expected outcomes include an open-source ICS simulation toolkit capable of stress-testing contingency plans at unprecedented scale, predictive models for casualty reduction through optimized evacuation routing, and evidence-based policy recommendations for interoperability standards in cross-sector emergency response. By creating a virtual proving ground for crisis management strategies under computationally intensive conditions, this project aims to advance adaptive resilience capabilities for increasingly frequent and severe disaster scenarios.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of the incident command system model to formulating and implementing effective response to natural and man-made disasters. Includes instruction in contingency planning, hazard and risk assessment, joint operations, law and ethics, emergency response and recovery, event mitigation, emergency rescue and medical operations, incident command, terrorism and national security issues, law enforcement, relief administration, volunteer and citizen coordination, public relations and applications to specific types of incidents.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding mesoscale atmospheric processes that govern extreme precipitation events in midlatitude coastal regions, which are poorly resolved in current global climate models. The research problem centers on improving the predictability of high-impact weather systems under varying climate scenarios, particularly as warming oceans and shifting atmospheric circulations alter moisture transport and storm dynamics. Current model parameterizations struggle to capture fine-scale interactions between ocean surfaces, boundary layer processes, and convective initiation, leading to uncertainties in projections of flood risks and hydrological extremes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-resolution numerical modeling campaign using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with an advanced ocean mixed-layer scheme. The computational approach will employ ensemble-based simulations at 3-km horizontal resolution across multiple decades of historical and SSP5-8.5 scenario data, explicitly resolving convective processes and land-ocean thermal gradients. This requires substantial high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage the petabyte-scale data output, complex matrix operations for ensemble Kalman filter assimilation of radar and satellite observations, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses of parameterization suites. Expected outcomes include 1) new insights into ocean-atmosphere feedback mechanisms that amplify precipitation extremes, 2) optimized parameterizations for coastal convection in climate models, and 3) probabilistic frameworks for extreme rainfall forecasting that integrate dynamic and statistical downscaling. The generated datasets will be made available through a community repository to support regional climate adaptation planning. By leveraging HPC capabilities to bridge scale disparities in atmospheric modeling, this work aims to directly inform resilience strategies for vulnerable coastal populations while advancing the computational methodologies required for next-generation Earth system prediction.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the prediction of atmospheric motion and climate change. Includes instruction in general circulation patterns, weather phenomena, atmospheric predictability, parameterization, numerical and statistical analysis, large- and mesoscale phenomena, kinematic structures, precipitation processes, and forecasting techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in professional and technical communication through large-scale analysis of digital writing practices and document usability. A critical challenge in the field lies in understanding how complex, multimodal documents—such as web-based technical manuals, interactive scientific reports, and AI-generated business communications—are navigated and interpreted by diverse audiences. Traditional qualitative methods, while valuable, struggle to account for the scale and variability of user interactions with digital texts. This study proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and agent-based modeling to simulate user engagement patterns, evaluate document effectiveness, and optimize design choices. The research will process terabytes of anonymized user interaction data (e.g., clickstreams, eye-tracking datasets, and revision histories) from institutional partners, alongside publicly available corpora of technical documents. NLP pipelines will classify semantic structures and rhetorical moves, while reinforcement learning models will predict how document design features influence comprehension and task success. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will stress-test proposed content strategies under variable user scenarios. Outcomes will include a framework for data-driven document design, open-source tools for usability prediction, and evidence-based recommendations for integrating generative AI into writing workflows. By quantifying relationships between compositional choices and user outcomes at unprecedented scale, this work aims to redefine best practices in professional writing education and industry standards. The requested HPC resources are essential for training deep learning models on heterogeneous text-visual datasets and running parallelized simulations, tasks that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. This interdisciplinary effort bridges humanities-based writing research with computational methodologies, positioning technical communication studies to address emerging challenges in digital literacy and AI-mediated communication.
cip_title: Professional, Technical, Business, and Scientific Writing
cip_definition: A program that focuses on professional, technical, business, and scientific writing; and that prepares individuals for academic positions or for professional careers as writers, editors, researchers, and related careers in business, government, non-profits, and the professions. Includes instruction in theories of rhetoric, writing, and digital literacy; document design, production, and management; visual rhetoric and multimedia composition; documentation development; usability testing; web writing; and publishing in print and electronic media.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform media influence on public opinion formation during complex sociopolitical events, with a focus on the interplay between legacy news outlets, social media networks, and emerging decentralized communication platforms. Traditional methods for analyzing media ecosystems struggle to process the scale and heterogeneity of modern communication data, particularly when examining temporal patterns, sentiment diffusion, and network-level information cascades across multiple modalities (text, video, audio). Our research will employ high-performance computing resources to implement a multimodal computational framework combining natural language processing, dynamic network analysis, and agent-based modeling. The proposed approach will process terabytes of timestamped media content from curated datasets spanning broadcast transcripts, social media posts, and podcast episodes, while simulating audience engagement patterns through parallelized discrete-event simulations. Computational tasks include transformer-based sentiment propagation models, community detection in temporal interaction networks, and large-scale topic alignment across heterogeneous media sources. Expected outcomes include new theoretical insights about attention economies in fragmented media environments, methodological advances in cross-platform communication analysis, and open-source tools for modeling information diffusion at societal scales. By leveraging GPU-accelerated machine learning and distributed memory architectures, this work will enable unprecedented granularity in examining how competing narratives emerge and stabilize across communication channels – a critical capability for addressing contemporary challenges in misinformation research, intercultural communication, and media effects scholarship. The requested resources directly support the development of computational social science capacity within communication studies while maintaining strict ethical protocols for large-scale media analysis.
cip_definition: An program that focuses on the comprehensive study of communication, research and research methods, and theories of communication, and that spans specialties within the field of communications. Includes instruction in interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: Hematologic malignancies and solid tumors exhibit complex molecular heterogeneity, driving variable treatment responses and resistance mechanisms. While advances in multi-omics profiling have generated vast genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets, integrating these data to identify predictive biomarkers and therapeutic vulnerabilities remains computationally prohibitive for standard clinical research infrastructure. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analysis of multi-omics data from 5,000 patients across 15 cancer subtypes treated at our institution. We will develop a machine learning framework integrating genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment signatures, and longitudinal clinical outcomes to model treatment resistance. Key computational steps include dimensionality reduction of single-cell RNA-seq data, Bayesian network inference of signaling pathways, and ensemble learning to predict drug response. A second aim involves molecular dynamics simulations of recurrent mutation hotspots in hematologic drivers (e.g., FLT3, JAK2) to prioritize neomorphic binding sites for targeted therapy. These simulations require GPU-accelerated sampling of protein conformational states across microsecond timescales. The HPC environment is critical for managing petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing workflows, and executing resource-intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models of therapy resistance deployable via clinical decision support tools, (2) structural blueprints for designing inhibitors against previously undruggable oncoproteins, and (3) an open-source computational pipeline for adaptive oncology trial design. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work bridges the gap between high-throughput omics data and clinically actionable insights, directly addressing the National Cancer Institute’s priority of computationally-driven precision oncology. Resource allocation will support urgent analyses for three active clinical trials investigating resistance mechanisms in AML and NSCLC while establishing a scalable infrastructure for real-time genomic data interpretation in our molecular tumor board.
cip_definition: Research focused on Hematology-Oncology

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and long-term performance of geosynthetic-lined waste containment systems under dynamic environmental and mechanical loads. Current geoenvironmental engineering practices rely on simplified analytical models that inadequately capture coupled hydro-mechanical processes, soil-geosynthetic interactions, and contaminant transport in heterogeneous subsurface environments. These limitations hinder the prediction of critical failures, such as liner leakage or slope instability in landfills, particularly under extreme climatic events or seismic activity. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating three-dimensional finite element modeling (FEM) with machine learning techniques. The FEM simulations will resolve multiphase flow, non-linear soil behavior, and geosynthetic creep at high spatial-temporal resolution, calibrated using experimental data from triaxial tests and hydraulic conductivity studies. Machine learning models will then identify patterns in simulated failure mechanisms to generate predictive tools for system vulnerability assessment. The computational workflow will leverage parallel processing to handle large-scale parametric studies evaluating liner configurations, material properties, and site-specific geostratigraphic conditions. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting interface shear strength degradation in composite liners, contaminant breakthrough times under cyclic wet-dry conditions, and probabilistic slope stability assessments for landfill embankments. This work will directly inform the development of next-generation design guidelines for geosynthetic barrier systems, enhancing their resilience to climate-induced stressors and reducing environmental contamination risks. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory-intensive simulations of multiphysics interactions across relevant engineering timescales, enabling transformative insights into sustainable waste containment strategies at the intersection of geotechnical engineering and environmental protection.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply geotechnical engineering methods, which deal with the analysis, design and construction of earth and earth supported structures, to the application of environmental problems, such as waste containment, waste disposal, construction of land fills, soil permeation, soil analysis, and soil improvement. Includes instruction in soil mechanics, soil dynamics, soil behavior, waste management and containment systems, geosynthetics, geochemistry, earth structures, geoenvironmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, and foundation engineering

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methodologies for analyzing high-dimensional, complex datasets using Bayesian hierarchical models, with a focus on addressing computational bottlenecks in inference tasks. Modern applications in epidemiology, environmental monitoring, and social sciences increasingly involve datasets with millions of observations, intricate dependency structures, and latent processes, rendering conventional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods computationally infeasible. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining parallelized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) samplers, variational inference techniques, and distributed computing strategies. The core innovation lies in partitioning high-dimensional parameter spaces into conditionally independent subsets, enabling asynchronous gradient calculations across multi-node high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. This approach will be implemented through a custom integration of Stan and PyTorch, optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures, with adaptive load-balancing mechanisms to handle heterogeneous data structures. Key challenges include ensuring numerical stability in large-scale sparse matrix operations, minimizing communication overhead in distributed memory systems, and validating approximation fidelity through theoretical error bounds. The requested HPC resources—specifically, access to GPU nodes with high memory bandwidth and multi-terabyte distributed storage—are critical for benchmarking against existing methods using synthetic and real-world datasets, including a 10-million-record climate sensor network dataset and genomic variant-phenotype association data. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for scalable Bayesian inference, (2) novel convergence criteria for partitioned MCMC workflows, and (3) applications to real-time pandemic risk modeling with spatially varying transmission parameters. This work will advance statistical computing by bridging theoretical rigor with practical scalability, directly supporting reproducible research in public health and environmental statistics. The computational infrastructure will also facilitate training graduate students in cutting-edge statistical computing techniques, strengthening institutional capacity in data-intensive statistics.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and statistics or a specialization which draws from mathematics and statistics. Includes instruction in calculus, linear algebra, numerical analysis and partial differential equations, discrete mathematics, probability theory, statistics, computing, and other related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework to model emergent dynamics in coupled socio-technical-ecological systems (STES), with a focus on resilience thresholds in urban food-energy-water (FEW) networks under climate volatility. While existing approaches often isolate technical or ecological subsystems, our work integrates granular behavioral data, infrastructure interdependencies, and stochastic environmental stressors into a unified agent-based and system dynamics model. The research addresses a critical gap in predicting cascading failures when human adaptive behaviors, such as shifting resource consumption patterns, interact with engineered systems and biophysical constraints during prolonged droughts or heatwaves. The computational methodology combines three elements: (1) high-resolution network analysis of FEW flows across urban and peri-urban regions, (2) bounded-rationality decision algorithms for households and institutional actors calibrated to survey data, and (3) climate ensembles projecting compound extreme events at city-region scales. By implementing hybrid parallelization strategies across GPU and CPU architectures, the framework will simulate decade-scale trajectories at 12-hour temporal resolution for systems comprising >10^6 interdependent agents and infrastructure nodes. Key innovations include adaptive meshing techniques to handle multi-physics interactions between discrete behavioral choices and continuous material flows, along with uncertainty quantification through iterative Latin hypercube sampling. Expected outcomes include identification of leverage points for preventing systemic collapse, validated against historical crisis events in three climate-vulnerable megacities. The resulting open-source toolkit will enable policymakers to stress-test intervention portfolios across social, technical, and ecological domains simultaneously—a capability critical for achieving climate adaptation goals under deep uncertainty. This work advances systems science by creating the first scalable platform to observe phase transitions in STES through the lens of distributed human-environment coupling rather than traditional sectoral boundaries.
cip_definition: A program with a multidisciplinary approach to the analysis and solution of complex problems, requiring a combined approach using data and models from the natural, social, technological, behavioral and life sciences, and other specialized fields.

abstract: Forest operations face critical challenges in balancing economic efficiency, ecological sustainability, and worker safety, particularly in steep and complex terrains. Current harvesting and transportation planning methods rely on simplified empirical models that inadequately capture the dynamic interactions between equipment, environmental variables, and forest structure. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to optimize forest operations through agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML)-driven adaptive control systems. The research will focus on simulating heterogeneous forest stands, terrain variability, and equipment behavior at scales previously unachievable due to computational limitations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of multi-agent systems representing harvesting machinery, soil dynamics, treefall mechanics, and biomass transport logistics under stochastic environmental conditions. A hybrid approach combining physics-based models (discrete element method for soil-vehicle interactions, finite element analysis for tree mechanics) and deep reinforcement learning will be implemented to identify optimal operational strategies that minimize soil disturbance, carbon footprint, and costs while maintaining productivity. The computational workflow will integrate LiDAR-derived forest structure data, real-world equipment telemetry, and environmental sensor networks to validate models against field observations. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of predicting site-specific operational thresholds, recommending adaptive equipment configurations, and quantifying trade-offs between extraction methods. This work will advance precision forestry by establishing a computational foundation for next-generation forest engineering that addresses climate resilience and circular bioeconomy goals. The requested HPC allocation will support intensive parameter space exploration, sensitivity analyses across diverse biomes, and the training of graph neural networks for real-time operational optimization. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and partnerships with forest industry stakeholders to accelerate adoption of data-driven sustainable practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and forestry principles to the design of mechanical devices and processes for efficient forest management, timber production and related forest logistics systems. Includes instruction in forest products processing, forest management, forest harvesting, timber structure design, production analysis, road and bridge construction, vehicle adaptation and design, and harvesting equipment design.

abstract: Large-scale graph analysis is fundamental to advancing computational solutions in social network dynamics, infrastructure resilience, and genomic interactions, yet remains hindered by the inherent complexity of billion-edge datasets. Current algorithms for critical tasks such as community detection, dynamic shortest-path computation, and temporal anomaly detection exhibit prohibitive time complexity when applied to real-world graphs, limiting their utility in time-sensitive applications. This project proposes the development of adaptive parallel algorithms optimized for heterogeneous high-performance computing (HPC) architectures to address these scalability barriers. We will implement a multi-tiered computational strategy combining distributed-memory parallelism (via MPI) for coarse-grained graph partitioning, shared-memory multicore optimization (using OpenMP) for local subgraph analysis, and GPU acceleration for regular subroutines like similarity scoring. Key innovations include a dynamic load-balancing framework that adjusts work distribution based on real-time vertex centrality metrics and a communication-reduction protocol leveraging probabilistic data structures. The research will validate these methods on web-scale crawls (Common Crawl), urban mobility networks (OpenStreetMap), and biomedical interaction graphs (STRING DB), requiring access to HPC resources with multi-terabyte memory capacity and support for hybrid CPU-GPU workflows. Anticipated outcomes include (1) open-source implementations demonstrating ≥50% speedup over state-of-the-art frameworks (Dask, CuGraph) on 10^9-edge graphs, (2) theoretical advances in complexity analysis of asynchronous graph traversal models, and (3) applied breakthroughs in pandemic spread prediction through mobility graph analysis. By establishing scalable computational patterns for massive graph processing, this work will enable new research capabilities across computational social science, infrastructure planning, and systems biology while advancing foundational knowledge in parallel algorithm design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer theory, computing problems and solutions, and the design of computer systems and user interfaces from a scientific perspective. Includes instruction in the principles of computational science, computer development and programming, and applications to a variety of end-use situations.

abstract: Aerospace medicine faces critical challenges in safeguarding human health under the extreme and dynamic conditions of air and space travel, where crews and passengers are exposed to unique stressors such as microgravity, radiation, prolonged confinement, and rapid shifts in atmospheric pressure. Current clinical models for predicting and mitigating health risks in these environments lack the resolution to account for complex, interacting physiological and psychological variables. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating cardiovascular, neurocognitive, and immune system responses to simulate human adaptability and resilience during long-duration space missions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these dynamics at scale, coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of hemodynamic changes in microgravity with agent-based simulations of stress-induced cognitive performance decline. Machine learning algorithms will analyze multimodal datasets from astronaut biometrics, environmental sensors, and ground-based analogs to identify early biomarkers of decompensation. Additionally, the project will simulate emergency medical scenarios—such as trauma management in partial gravity or pharmacological interventions under altered pharmacokinetics—to optimize protocols for autonomous healthcare delivery. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated workflows for real-time parameter optimization and probabilistic risk assessment. Expected outcomes include predictive models of crew health degradation, validated countermeasures for mission-critical tasks, and adaptive guidelines for medical system design in next-generation spacecraft. By quantifying interactions between physiological thresholds and environmental variables, this work will advance clinical strategies to enhance crew safety, mission success, and passenger well-being in commercial spaceflight. The HPC infrastructure will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling human-environment interactions, with translational applications for terrestrial aviation medicine and extreme-environment healthcare.
cip_definition: Research focused on the health care of operating crews, support personnel, and passengers of air and space vehicles. Includes instruction in special conditions of physical and psychological stress, emergency medical procedures, adaptive systems and artificial environments. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods in architectural design, specifically targeting the optimization of adaptive urban microclimates through real-time, multi-physics simulations. Traditional design workflows struggle to integrate dynamic environmental factors—such as wind patterns, solar exposure, and thermal flux—into iterative design processes, particularly at the scale of dense urban neighborhoods. Current software tools are limited by simplified models or long computation times, hindering architects’ ability to explore complex, data-driven solutions for climate resilience. This project addresses this gap by developing a parametric framework that couples generative design algorithms with high-fidelity fluid dynamics and energy modeling, enabled by HPC parallelization. The computational approach will involve deploying finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations across distributed GPU clusters to evaluate thousands of design variants under varying climate scenarios. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on simulation outputs to accelerate feedback loops between design iteration and performance analysis. Key outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating microclimate interactions within architectural and urban design workflows, validated against physical-scale wind tunnel and thermal data. The research aims to establish scalable methodologies for embedding real-time environmental feedback into design processes, with implications for reducing urban heat island effects, improving energy efficiency, and enhancing pedestrian comfort. By bridging architectural design with advanced computational modeling, this work advances the integration of sustainability metrics into early-stage design decisions, offering a template for resource-efficient, climate-responsive urban development.
cip_definition: An advanced program of study for architects and related professionals that focuses on theoretical and practical issues in architecture and integrates digital technologies into architectural design, fabrication, and construction. Includes instruction in architectural history and urban theory, 3-D digital technologies, construction, design and fabrication methods, and sustainable practices in architecture.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform misinformation dissemination in fragmented digital media ecosystems, a pressing challenge in contemporary communication and journalism studies. The research problem centers on understanding how unverified or misleading content propagates differently across social media, news aggregators, and emerging decentralized platforms, particularly during breaking news events. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the scale, velocity, and multimodal nature of modern information flows, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to process multilingual text, images, and video metadata from real-time API streams and historical archives (totaling ~800 TB of raw data). The computational methodology combines transformer-based natural language processing for cross-lingual claim matching, computer vision techniques for meme template tracking, and temporal network analysis to model information cascades. These methods require parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows to handle complex graph computations (projected 12M+ nodes) and multimodal embeddings. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for identifying platform-specific amplification patterns and vulnerable demographic segments based on interaction networks. The research will produce open-source tools for journalists and fact-checkers to prioritize debunking efforts during crises, along with theoretical insights about attention economies in hybrid media systems. By leveraging HPC resources for large-scale simulation of information diffusion scenarios (agent-based modeling projected at 10⁶ concurrent actors), this work addresses critical gaps in computational communication research while maintaining human-centered ethical analysis through iterative collaboration with journalism practitioners. Results will advance both academic understanding of digital misinformation ecosystems and applied strategies for preserving information integrity in next-generation media environments.
cip_title: Communication, Journalism, and Related Programs, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication, journalism, and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the efficacy of immersive language acquisition strategies in Spanish teacher education, with a focus on identifying pedagogical approaches that optimize learner proficiency in real-world communication contexts. A persistent challenge in Spanish language instruction lies in addressing gaps between theoretical grammar instruction and the dynamic, context-sensitive nature of spoken and written Spanish, particularly in dialectally diverse settings. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model large-scale datasets of learner interactions, linguistic corpora, and instructor feedback. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be implemented to analyze syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic features in learner outputs, while neural network models will simulate language acquisition patterns under varying instructional conditions. The computational workflow will integrate transformer-based architectures for fine-grained error detection in learner Spanish, coupled with agent-based simulations of classroom discourse dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative metrics correlating specific teaching methods with linguistic competency gains across proficiency levels, (2) predictive models for common interference points between English and Spanish grammatical structures, and (3) an open-access repository of annotated training data for Spanish pedagogical applications. By enabling parallel processing of multimodal educational data—including speech recordings, written assignments, and behavioral engagement metrics—the requested HPC resources will facilitate research scalability beyond the limitations of traditional classroom studies. The results aim to directly inform the design of adaptive teaching curricula and diagnostic tools for Spanish language educators, ultimately strengthening evidence-based practices in teacher preparation programs. This work bridges computational linguistics with applied language pedagogy, offering novel methodologies for addressing persistent challenges in heritage language maintenance and second language acquisition.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach Spanish language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Patients in hospice and palliative care face multidimensional challenges due to the heterogeneous nature of advanced illnesses, requiring care plans that balance symptom management, patient preferences, and prognostic uncertainty. Current approaches to predicting symptom trajectories or optimizing interventions remain limited by the complexity of integrating biological, psychosocial, and environmental data at scale. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model patient-specific outcomes and care pathways using high-dimensional datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes, and caregiver narratives. The research will employ machine learning techniques—such as federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-institutional data integration and transformer-based models to analyze unstructured clinical notes—coupled with mechanistic simulations of pain and symptom propagation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train these models on distributed datasets, perform hyperparameter optimization, and run Monte Carlo simulations evaluating the probabilistic impact of palliative interventions (e.g., opioid titration, psychosocial support timing) on quality-adjusted survival. By identifying latent patterns in symptom clusters and treatment responses, this work aims to generate predictive tools for clinicians to personalize care plans while respecting ethical and cultural preferences. Anticipated outcomes include open-source algorithms for dynamic risk stratification, a simulation platform for testing hypothetical care scenarios, and evidence-based guidelines for intervention sequencing in diverse populations. This computationally intensive approach addresses a critical gap in palliative care research by enabling data-driven, patient-centered decision-making at the intersection of biological complexity and humanistic care.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: The increasing adoption of solar energy systems demands advanced tools to optimize installation efficiency, predict long-term performance, and address site-specific challenges such as shading, weather variability, and component degradation. Current industry practices rely on static models and empirical guidelines, which often fail to account for dynamic environmental interactions or emerging material technologies. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model solar energy systems under diverse real-world conditions, enabling data-driven decision-making for installers and technicians. The research will integrate multi-physics simulations—including photovoltaic (PV) cell performance, thermal dynamics, and structural stress analysis—with machine learning algorithms trained on historical weather patterns, material degradation datasets, and energy output records. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between solar arrays, environmental factors, and adjacent infrastructure to optimize panel placement and maintenance schedules. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will assess airflow impacts on system cooling, while Monte Carlo methods will evaluate probabilistic risks of component failures. By leveraging GPU-accelerated parallel processing, the framework will generate high-resolution, site-specific installation guidelines and predictive maintenance protocols. Expected outcomes include validated models for estimating energy yield loss due to micro-shading, a decision-support tool for prioritizing repair tasks based on real-time sensor data, and open-access datasets correlating installation parameters with long-term performance metrics. These resources will directly enhance technician training programs by integrating computational literacy into solar system design and troubleshooting curricula. The project’s scalable computational approach addresses critical gaps in solar workforce readiness, supporting the transition to resilient, adaptive renewable energy infrastructure.
cip_title: Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair solar energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in evaluating the cost-effectiveness and policy impacts of novel pharmaceutical interventions using advanced computational modeling.
